Will he go back to sleep? Meera walked and walked. Suddenly night became daylight. She was in the magical part of the jungle. She saw a violet beak and long neck behind a tree. She stumbled on a stone and fell into the stream. Will Meera drown? The violet colored bird jumped into the cold waters of the stream to save Meera. Meera was wet and shivering. She was scared of the bird. Was it a dream? 'Don't get scared. I am Lilac.' Meera was amused when the bird spoke in a human tone. Meera invited Lilac to the village. She wanted the villagers to see her new friend. Whenever the villagers had a problem, they went to the old Haji. The village headman met the Haji and asked his advice. Haji told him about the huge violet colored bird with elephant feet and human voice. Will the headman believe the Haji? Sonu met the tinkling fire fly that flew all over the jungle. The fire fly told about Lilac and how she liked to eat red berries. Did Sonu believe her? After a hearty meal of red berries, Lilac rested under the trees. The villagers and headman came with bamboo sticks. Will they beat the bird? Meera stood in front of the bird and pleaded with the men, 'Lilac is harmless, she comes here for the red berries. Don't harm her.' Will the villagers listen to a little girl? There were plenty of red berry trees in the village. The men talked with each other and agreed to share the berries, as long as their fields were not trampled. Was Meera happy? Meera's father lifted her on his shoulders. Lilac smiled looking at the happiness in their faces. Are you smiling too?
author: Annapurna Sharma
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: What is IT?
text: "It's a he" shouted Zayan. "No, a she, I saw her wearing a blue sari last week" said Zara, her face red with anger. " A he! A he! A he! and I have seen him wearing boy's clothes" Zayan said. "Can't you both just go play something else, I told you not to talk about this" their mom shouted at them. Zayan and Zara could not understand why the it living in flat number B-5 wore men's clothes some days and women's clothes some other days. Well, they could find out. But what was even stranger was that their mom and dad never answered the questions and even asked them to stop thinking about who ever lived in flat B-5. "But mom, is it a he or a she?" asked Zara. "I don't want to hear anything about it - go out and play" said mom. Hmmm sometimes grown ups just don't get it right. Out in the courtyard dear old Ruhi aunty was walking slowly holding her white stick. "Hello Zara and Zayan. What was all that shouting about?" she asked. "Hello Ruhi aunty, but how did you know it was us? You can't see anything!"Zara was astonished. "Ha ha, my dear child, what do you know about seeing?"she smiled. "We were arguing about the man in B-5" said Zayan. "No, it's a woman" Zara squealed, "It's a woman, right Ruhi aunty?" she turned to the blind old woman for support. "How do I Know, I am a blind woman" Ruhi aunty's face beamed with suppressed laughter. Ahhhh sometimes these grown ups are just too much. " It's a SHE " " No, it's a HE " their voices flared up. "Hush hush my dear children! All I can see is that the IT you are talking about is a human. Some are born girls and grow up to be women. Some are born boys and grow up to be men. But some girls feel like boys, and some boys feel like girls." "How come? That's strange!" The old lady smiled."What matters is not what one is born as or looks like, but what one truly feels within. Now why don't you go up to B-5 and ask her or him directly?" "But how?" "Why is that?" "What happens to them?" "How can a girl be a boy or a boy a girl?" A flurry of questions flew to the smiling old woman. " Just look at the flowers around you in the garden, are they all alike?" she asked them. "Well, no. They are all different" said Zara. "But they are all flowers, right?" the gentle old face turned lovingly towards them. "I think I can see what you are trying to show us Ruhi aunty" said Zayan. "And I thought you were the blind one!" Zara hugged Ruhi aunty.
author: Reshma Jannath

title: HAPPY MAKES FRIENDS
text: Happy the puppy lived on a farm. His parents Moti and Tara were watchdogs. Happy scampered along with them. He practiced his Woofs and Wuffs. He made rounds of the farm. He played with Gora the calf, Puff the piglet and Tack the chicken. Sometimes he chased Inku and Minku the mice duo. But he wished he had more friends. He looked beyond the fence. He could see the woods. He knew that some animals lived there. He would ask them to be friends with him. One night Tara was putting Happy to sleep. It was a full moon night and the Big Moon shone brightly. Happy asked Tara, “Mama dear, I wish I had more friends. Can I ask Big Moon to be my friend?” Tara kissed him lovingly and said, “Big Moon has to show light at night. He cannot be friends with you.” “Mama may I go to the woods to make friends?” “No dear. The woods are not safe. Now sleep like a good puppy.” Happy was a curious puppy. He asked, “Mama dear, why aren’t the woods safe?” “The woods are dark and creepy. There are wild animals in the wood. You shall not venture into the woods. Now go to sleep dear.” Tara mumbled as she fell asleep. But Happy was wide awake. He had made up his mind to go to the woods. ‘Animals means friends. I want to make more friends. I shall go to the woods,’ Happy said to himself. He wiggled out of the bed. He crept out of the fence. He saw the Big Moon smile at him. “Hello Big Moon, I am off to find friends. Your light has lit up the woods. Now they don’t seem creepy. “ The Big Moon smiled and shone even more brightly. Happy darted into the woods. Suddenly he heard a cry,” Hark, who enters the woods? And why?" Happy halted. He saw Mr. Owl sitting in the tree. He had big round eyes, a round face and a hook-like beak. Happy said, “Good evening Mr. Owl, I am Happy the puppy.I have come here to find friends. Please help me.” “Hmm, go straight till you find the Big Tree. Every Full moon night baby-animals desirous of making friends gather beneath the tree. Now Hurry! " Happy ran ahead. Suddenly he saw a spark. It was moving! A flying insect was carrying a spark in his tail! “Hello! Who are you? And you have your own light!” Happy asked. “I am Fify the firefly. " “ I am Happy the farm-puppy. I am going to the Big Tree to find friends.” “Oh! May I join you?” “Why not? The more the merrier!” Happy said with a smile. “Please feel free to go ahead. You can fly and reach earlier.” Happy ran further. He heard a strange sound. He glanced up and saw a strange thing hanging from the branch. Was it a huge leaf? Was it an animal? Suddenly the thing opened its eyes. Happy was frightened. He gathered his wits and said, “Hello! I am Happy the puppy.” “Hi there! I am Batsy-watsy the bat. Are you going to the Big Tree to make friends?” “Yes Batsy-watsy. I am indeed going there!” “I too shall go then. See you under the Big Tree!” Batsy–watsy spread his wings and took flight. Happy continued his pursuit. Suddenly he heard a strange sound ‘Cric-Cric’. He saw a small green insect. It was a cricket! “Hello, I am Happy the puppy. Hello, little cricket." “The name is Hoppity. I have friends on the farm. You are the farm-pup right? Welcome to the woods!” “I am going to the Big Tree to find friends.” “Oh wow! I too am going there. The Big Moon night is the best time to find friends under the Big Tree. Let us hurry. I’ll jump and go ahead.” Finally Happy reached the Big Tree. He saw Fify, Hoppity and Batsy-watsy. He also spotted an owlet and a fox cub. "Welcome Happy!" They chorused. Batsy-watsy introduced Foxy the fox-cub and Owly the owlet. “Will you be friends with me?” Happy asked. “Yes. Let us become friends,” the five chorused. They played, sang and danced. They had a merry time! The Five friends took a Friendship oath very solemnly. They decided to meet under the Big Tree every Big Moon night. The five friends departed on a merry note. Furry decided to guide Happy to the farm. The Big Moon lit up the path to the farm. Soon they reached the farm. “Bye Furry.” “Bye Happy. Good night, sleep tight.” Furry waved his paw. Happy waved back. Then he crawled under the fence and entered the farm. He glanced up and saw the Big Moon. He smiled and said, “Thanks Big Moon!” He glanced around. Everybody was sleeping. Moo and Gora were sleeping; Rinku the piglet was sleeping; Inku-Minku were sleeping;Tack the chicken was sleeping; even his mother was sleeping. Happy snuggled inside the blanket next to his mother. Happy recalled the happy moments in the forest. He soon fell asleep. What an adventure!
author: Malvika Dekhane

title: Are You Happy?
text: A small black puppy lived with his mother. A parrot from a nearby tree used to make fun of his black colour. He used to say," Look at me Puppy dog. How beautiful Iam with green wings and pretty red lips! Look at yourself. You are dark as night." Puppy looked around. He saw the beautiful and colourful rooster, little brown rats and white pigs..... Puppy thought that everyone around him were beautiful and colourful and so they were happy. Puppy asked his mom," Mom, why am I black? That makes me sad." His mom replied," Yes. You are black. So what? There is nothing wrong in being black. We dogs are known for faithfulness. You should be proud of that." But the puppy was not satisfied at that. That night he did not get sleep. He came out of the kennel and was running here and there.. Suddenly, he saw himself in a forest There he saw a big owl sitting on a tree and h...o...o...t...ing. The noise frightened the puppy. But he gathered all the courage and asked the owl,"Owl! Are you happy?" The owl said,"Yes Iam happy. What is your problem?" "But you have two big round eyes which are very scary. Also a horrible voice which shakes the forest.. Is it ok for you?" asked the puppy. The owl said," So what? Iam the nightwatchman of the forest. All animals sleep in peace, because I take care. Also we owls are wise. Iam proud of all that. " The puppy ran further. He came across a fox. He stopped the fox and asked," Oh Fox! Are you happy? " The fox said, " Yes Iam. But what is your problem?" " No. They say that you are short and very cunning." said the puppy. The fox replied," I am not worried about my height. I am shrewd and if others say it is cunningness, I don't care. I can help my friends with my tricks. I am proud of that and so I am happy." Saying this the fox with its bushy tail ran away. As the puppy was about to turn, something glittered in the dark. It was a firefly. Now the puppy asked," Firefly Are you happy? " Fire fly answered," Yes. Iam. What is your problem? " "You glitter like a star in the night. But in the morning you don't. Are you not worried about that.?" asked the puppy. The firefly replied," Why should I? When it is dark, I spread light around me. I am proud of that. And so Iam happy." Saying this, the firefly made a buzz sound and flew away flattering its wings. When he was about to return something caught his attention. That was a bat hanging upside down in a tree. The puppy asked the bat," You ugly bat!When everyone walk and fly straight, you hang upside down.Are you happy over that? " Immediately the bat gave a hearty laugh and said," Iam not worried about my looks..Do you know that I am the friend of the farmer? I am proud of that and so Iam happy.... The puppy ran home. His mother was waiting for him. She asked," Pup. Where did you go? Puppy said what other animals told him and added," Mom, now even I am not worried about my colour or looks. I shall do what I am good at and be proud of that.. "On hearing this, his mom felt very happy. His mom hugged him and both of them went to sleep. Dear friends,"The puppy is right. Isn't he?"Our behaviour and attitude are more important than our looks.
author: Rajalakshmi Paramasivam

title: Hide and Seek
text: Pig,cock,dog,mice Sleeping The moon is smiling. The big moon looks at Sheru,the dog. Sheru wants to play with the moon. The moon wants to play with Sheru. Sheru cannot see the moon. Sheru asks the bee. Have you seen the moon? Sheru also asks the grasshopper. He did not find the moon.
author: anshu

title: Come Home, Papa
text: "Happy Birthday, Vishakha!" "This party is awesome, aunty.” said Rohit. Vishakha was happy because many of her friends had come for her birthday party. ﻿ Vishakha's mother hugged Rohit in response. That is what everybody loved about her. She was affectionate and she loved all the kids like her own. The parents and their kids loved her back. They were always there in her time of need. And so was she. ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿ "This is the best birthday ever!" exclaimed Vishakha excitedly as all her friends settled down to watch a movie. The movie was about a tiger and his cub that were playing and having fun in the jungle. This movie made Vishakha a bit sad. Why? She didn't know. All of Vishakha's friends left soon after the movie, Rohit was the last one to go. "That was a really nice movie, wasn't it Vish?" asked Rohit. "Oh! I loved it." said Vishakha happily. "But where is your father? I have never seen him." Questioned Rohit. "Father? Daddy? Dad? Yeah, where is my father? Maa, where is he?" Her mother yawned and said "time for bed, come on kiddo." "But, but... but I want a father too, just like that cub!" "Come on now Vishakha, mommy is tired. Come here and give mommy a goodnight kiss." "But MAAAAAA!!!" "VISHAKHA!" shouted her mother. "Okay Maa." said Vishakha sadly. The next day school was off. Hence, Vishakha and Rohit sat down and read together. "Where should I look for him, Rohit? Where do you usually look when your father is missing?" "The washroom, that's his favourite hiding spot. That's where I look for my dad." "I checked but he wasn’t there. Do you know where my father is?" "Umm, I don't know. But this book says that parrots speak and they know-it-all." "But, I don't have a parrot." "Oh! I do. Let's go!" "Mirchi, look who is here." called out Rohit to his parrot. "Ki-Ki-Vishakha" chirped the parrot. "O, Mirchi! Dear Mirchi. Do you know who my father is? Or where is he" "NO!!! Is he cute like I am?" "That's what I am asking you." "Ki-Ki-ka-ka" "Rohit, what does he mean?" "Hello, Vishakha. How are you darling?" said Rohit's mother. "Aunty, aunty do you know where my father is? I was just asking Mirchi about it, but he won't say." "Haha! Mirchi is a nutcase. You should ask your mother, she will know." "I tried auntyyyy! But Maa has no idea either." "Hmm. It is getting late. You should go home." "Yes I should. Bye aunty." That evening Vishakha wasn't able to stop thinking about her father. What he looked like, what was his profession and most of all where was he, questions like these kept propping up in her mind. She decided she will talk to her mother. Her mother looked quite different, she couldn't understand why! "Hey Maa! Are you alright?" asked Vishakha softly. "Come here Vish, look at these stars! Look how they shine." "They are adorable Maa. I wish I was a star." "One day, you will be. Just like your father." "My father is a star?" asked Vishakha excitedly. "Yes darling, he is. Can you see that star? The one which is the brightest!" "Aah haan." "Well, that is your father, smiling at you." "Hello Papa! Maa, can he hear me?" "A little louder will do, Vish." She smiled at the star, closed her eyes, tried counting the distance and then yelled at the top of her voice, "Come home, Papa."
author: Apoorva Mathur
illustrator: Hari Kumar Nair; Kabini  Amin; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Soumya Menon; Vartika  Sharma; Vishnu  M Nair

title: Birds Of A Feather
text: Lali looked pretty much like the other girls in Susheelpur. But in fact, she was unlike any girl the villagers had ever seen! All the girls in Susheelpur were demure and docile - but not Lali. She climbed trees instead of sitting quietly under them. She ran faster than any boy for miles around. And every time Ma called her into the kitchen, Lali sneaked away into the forest nearby. Instead of doing whatever it was that girls were supposed to do Lali would skip to the forest to meet her best friend, a strange creature she had named Kala Khatta. Kala Khatta was a gigantic beast who was part-animal, part-bird and entirely unusual. Lali had never seen or even heard of anything as wondrous as him. Lali loved Kala Khatta with all her heart. For he understood her like nobody else did. He knew only too well what it was to not conform, to be different. Kala Khatta delighted in his uniqueness. Why be like everybody else when you were born to be just you? Isn't it best to be original? He did not expect Lali to be like other girls. In fact, Kala Khatta helped her try out new things! He taught her to nestle among the highest branches of trees to watch baby birds emerge from their eggs. He helped her understand the language of the forest. And he showed her how delightful it was to frolick in streams. Kala Khatta and Lali spent their days romping in the forest and rollicking in rivers. And Lali blossomed into a fearless, peerless child. Every evening, after a whole day of fun, she bade him farewell and promised to return the next morning. But one morning, Lali's world turned on its head. It all began when Tongewalla Taufeeq saw Lali slinking out of her home and running to the forest. Tongewalla Taufeeq was horrified! What business did a girl have in the forest? And why did she have to run so fast, anyway? So Tongewalla Taufeeq galloped to the Sarpach, who too was aghast at the news. "What?" he cried. "A girl who wants to play in the forest instead of cooking and cleaning like girls are meant to do? Gasp!" Soon, word spread about Lali's trips to the forest. And Lali's Papa was furious! "But Papa,"pleaded Lali. "I was only playing with my best friend. Kala Khatta is the only one who understands me!" "Eh? Your gola is the only thing that understands you?" Papa was completely confused. "No!! Kala Khatta is the most wonderful creature in the world! He is half-animal and half-bird. And he is the colour of juicy jamuns glinting in the sun! He is one of a kind and cannot really be compared to anything else. He is like me, you see - just bigger... and purple!" But this only made matters worse. "Half-animal half-bird? Have you begun lying to me now, Lali?" roared Papa. Before long, the Sarpanch called an emergency meeting to deal with this crisis. "We simply cannot allow girls to run about as they please," said the Sarpanch, shaking his head somberly. "Yes, yes," agreed the rest of the council. "Girls must do what girls are supposed to, and boys must do what boys are supposed to." "But why can't girls play like boys? Why do they say that is wrong?" wondered Lali sadly. She turned and fled to the forest, back to the only being who understood what she was feeling. Kala Khatta was waiting for her. He always knew when Lali was in need of comforting. As soon as she saw her friend, Lali burst into tears. "They think I am unnatural, Kalu!"she sobbed. "My Papa is furious, my Ma is probably ashamed of me. All because I don't want to act like other girls. But is it such a bad thing to be just me?" But unknown to Lali, all the men of the council had followed her into the forest. Kala Khatta stiffened, and every hair on his long tail trembled and stood up in alarm. What was that crackling he had heard? And what was that strange scent in the air? He whipped his head about, his heart racing in panic.Oh No! A large group of armed men were rushing towards them! The villagers stopped in their tracks when they saw the huge creature confronting them. Their jaws dropped and their eyes popped! "What is this?" they cried. "Is it an animal or a bird? And why is it such a peculiar colour? Such a strange creature should never live in our forest.. let it go back to where it came from. Let's chase it away!" "NO!! " shouted Lali, jumping in front of her friend. "I will NOT let you hurt him! Kalu has never harmed anybody in his life! So what if he does not look like the other creatures of the forest? He is gentle and wise and loving. Doesn't that count?" Lali paused, and sighed sadly. "Shouldn't who we are matter more than what we look like?" Nobody said anything. But as Lali's words slowly sunk in, everybody lowered their weapons. "Perhaps there is something in what the little one says," muttered the Sarpanch. "It is true that Lali does not act the way we expect girls to. Yet she is fearless, loyal and truthful... and surely those values are far more important than anything else." Papa picked Lali up and hugged her tight. "You're right, Lali! Children should be allowed to be children... so what if a boy wants to cook and a girl wants to play in the jungle? What matters is who they are at heart!" Everybody cheered as Papa hoisted a delighted Lali onto his shoulders. A little girl and a strange creature had changed Susheelpur forever!
author: Sreedevi Gopakumar
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Time Teller
text: O nce upon a time, in a kingdom far away, Lived a King, ruling, night and day. An old Minister, helped him rule, He was very wise, unlike any other fool. The King had a son, the Prince, the heir. Oh, all the time, he'd put on such airs! Then, one day, the King got sick. His time was near, the clocks went tick! The old Minister said, "The Time Teller's prophecy was right! Upon us, is the dark night!" "The Prince will now rule!", declared the Minister. Oh, little did he know that the Prince was so sinister! Days went by and so did night. But everything was just not right. The Prince still put on airs, As a ruler, he was not fair. The Time Teller, the old woman, so wise, Was called to the court to prophesize. She said, "Someday, oh son! Good luck will come to you through someone." One day the Prince met the blacksmith's daughter. In the Kingdom, she was extremely sought after. Her hair was golden, like her heart. She was kind and sweet, And she loved art. They became friends,really soon. To the Prince, she had come as a boon! While cleaning her father's workshop, She found a lovely pocket watch! She went to the Prince with it, With happiness, her face lit! The Prince did not like the watch. He wouldn't take it, won't even touch. Blacksmith's daughter became very sad. The Prince now seemed to be so bad. She cried and cried with the pocket watch in her hand. She decided to give it away, or bury it in the sand. Another day, the sun had set. But the Prince's good luck hadn't come to him yet! He went to the Time Teller to ask where it was! She told him that it was now a lost cause. The pocket watch was his good luck. He rejected it, now causing a ruck! The Prince went back to the blacksmith's daughter, Now, it was the pocket watch he was after! She told him that she had given it away. He shouted, "How could you? Say?!" When the blacksmith's daughter was taking the watch to bury, She came across a young man, running in a hurry! She stopped him and asked, "What happened? Why are you running?" "I am going to fight the Prince, defeat that man, selfish and cunning!" He saw the pocket watch in her hand and let out a sigh. He said, "Oh what a lovely watch. May I?" She gave him the pocket watch, because he asked. In his admiration for it, she simply basked! The young man defeated the Prince with the luck so good. And he became the ruler, like a King would. The Prince cried over the good luck he lost! His kingdom was now gone too! *sob* *sob*
author: Sonali Sharma
illustrator: Greystroke; Helga Parekh; Sonakshi Verma; Sonali Sharma

title: Finding a New Friend
text: I live in a big big home with mummy, papa and my dog. My dog’s name is Scooby. My cousins also live nearby. You know I have six cousins. See, these are my cousins. I love all of them but my favorite is Rima. She lives with me in my home. She is my best friend. Rima, Scooby and I play together in the streets and everywhere else. We love to play hide and seek. Yesterday, I suddenly heard mummy and papa talking that we will have to shift to another city!! But “I don’t want to go”, I said with tears in my eyes. Papa took me in his arms and said, “Even I do not want to go sweetie but I do not have another option”. I ran and told Rima about it. She too had tears in her eyes. Papa even told us that we will have to leave in another twenty days. I got even sadder. I did not want those twenty days to get over, ever!! But time just flew away. Just the day before, when we had to leave, I suddenly had an idea. “Papa, papa, we can take Rima along with us, please, please say yes. I do not want to leave her.” He hugged me tightly and sadly said, “How can she leave her parents behind?” I had no reply. Finally the day when we had to leave arrived. Both of us started crying. Papa promised to take me back to my home during every summer vacations. And then we left. My train journey to the new city was filled with memories. How we used to share all our secrets, how we used to do mischief together, everything!! The only relief that I had was Scooby. I missed everything back there. We finally reached our new house. I had already started missing Rima and my old home. “Why did we come here?? I do not like this house and even this city is bad”, I sighed. “I want to go back. I have no friends here.” On seeing the new house I ran to see inside, if I could find something interesting. For the next few days, I had almost forgotten everything as I had got a room of my own and wanted to decorate it with my drawings. On seeing one of them, I remembered how both Rima and I made it. One day while returning from the grocery shop, we met Khanna aunty and her daughter Neha. While mommy and aunty were talking, Neha said "Hii" and we started talking. We became friends. I was happy as I had one now. I got to know that we went to the same school and also were in the same class. In my class, I made many friends but had no best friend, nobody like Rima. One day Khanna aunty asked us for picnic. I was pretty thrilled as this was our first outing after coming here. We went to the zoo. I was so thrilled to see so many different animals together. It was so beautiful that I did not want to come back. But we had to. Slowly, our friendship started growing. We often went out together and Neha showed me so many new places in the city. We even used to do our homework together. We also played with each other just like Rima and I used to. Soon we became as good friends as Rima and I were. She became my new best friend. When I went back to my old home, I told Rima about her and even showed her Neha's pictures. And that’s how I found a new friend.
author: jinia dasgupta
illustrator: Henu; Ketan Raut; Mayur Mistry; Padmanabh; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Rijuta Ghate; Ruchi Shah; Santosh Pujari; Sonal Goyal; Soumya Menon; Sumit Sakhuja; Sunaina  Coelho; Suvidha Mistry

title: Maya's Flying Adventure
text: "Who are you and why are you siting under our tree?" "I'm Story Hari, And this will be a story tree. Do you all want to listen to a story?" "Do your stories come true?" "Of course they come true! I'm story Hari and my stories always come true." "Can you tell us the story of the flying Elephant Bird and the little girl?" "Sure! Gather around and keep your ears wide open." "Who are you little girl and why are you here alone?" "I'm Maya and I want to have an adventure, a flying adventure. Who are you?" "I am Elbert, an elephant bird and I can fly." "No Way! Elephants don't fly!!" "Aha but I'm a bird also so I can!" "Oh please, will you take me on your back?" "Sure but it'll have to be in the night. Can you bring me something to eat"" "Of course! Do you like rotis? "I love rotis.. Bring them and come tonight." "Amma can I have a few extra rotis tonight?" "Why Maya, are you hungry?" "Yes amma I'm so hungry that I think I can eat a hundred rotis." "That's a lot!! How about I give you ten?" "Sure. Thank you amma." When amma gave her the rotis, Maya ate just one and saved the rest for Elbert in her pocket. The sun set and it grew dark. Maya waited for the moon to rise in the sky. She left home to meet her new friend Elbert. Elbert was waiting and watching. He was hungry. His stomach went "GROWL! GROWL!" I want my rotis he cried. Elbert smiled happily when he saw Maya coming. When Elbert finished his rotis, he let out a huge BURRRP!! The Burp was so loud it scared Maya and she fell into a lake with a BIG SPLASH!! As Elbert just looked on, Maya cried, HELP! HELP!! When Elbert saw Maya was scared he jumped into the water making a bigger SPLASH and Maya found herself on the bank. Maya was wet and angry. She shouted at Elbert. "Look what you've done!" A group of men heard Maya shout and came to beat up Elbert. Maya saw that a group of men had come with sticks to beat up Elbert. She felt sorry for her friend and held out her hands to try and protect the elephant bird. "Why did you leave home without telling us, Maya? We were so worried." said appa. "I'm so sorry appa, I just wanted an adventure with my new Magic Flying elephant Bird friend." "That's OK! You're safe now. Why don't you go for a quick ride on your friend's back and see the whole forest?" smiled appa. And that is how Maya had her Flying Adventure, said Story Hari.
author: Mala Ashok

title: Where do these ants go?
text: Troy " I want to know where do these ants go". They go up the shelf to eat biscuits. And up the dining table for the cake. Haha! This one even uses my roller skater. Look at them, how happily they are enjoying the sweets. Crunching and Munching... They can smell danger. So many! So this is where they live. Umm... Where are they going now? Oh, No! My lollipop. Draw An Ant And Colour It
author: Anushruti Ganguly

title: My Mean Brothers
text: I have a younger brother. I don't like him. He is very mean. He never lets me sleep near Mummy! He never lets me play on the iPad! He always gets more chocolates and he never shares them! He always gets the better gifts. This year, on his birthday he got a bicycle, while I got a stuffed monkey. Mummy loves him more. I just know it! He always pulls my hair. He never gives me the TV remote. Once, he almost cut off my Barbie's hair! Oh, and I also have an elder brother but I don't like him either. He always tries to take the remote. He always complains that Daddy loves me more. And he never lets me play with any of his stuff! But the thing I dislike the most is that he never lets me go to the bathroom in peace!
author: Rimsha Falak

title: No work, just fun
text: Grrrrr..... Those pesky animals! I have already told them about hundred times not to play in the night but see what disrespect they give to my sayings. I am telling them for their good but they simply won't listen. What shall I do? Sometimes they play 'Who - will- reach - the - moon?', Sometimes they play ' Catch - me - if - you can!' What shall I do? Well, I prefer going inside my hut painted with wavy design and circles and doze off. You expected a new, fresh day to be helter skelter but no! They run and jump all night and laze around in the sun. My, my we're running out of time, let me narrate to you the story of all Lazy Farm Folks. Once upon a time all the farm folks were very lazy, They didn't move a muscle to help in the farms just running and jumping all night but no work in the day. One day the headman introduced us to the' All Farm Folk will work hard year.' The cow's ears perked up, the hen's wings jumped up, the pigs tail's curled up and the dog's tongue dried up. WHAT! That shocking faces pulled up a great smile on my face. Finally, at least for a year they'll move their fat stomachs and do some work. The animals pulled up their hind limbs and dragged themselves towards the storage where all the tools which we use in the fields were kept. The bulls and cows put on their harness, the dog carried the sickle and basket of dry grass and also the plough. The pigs came along with heaps of packets with seeds and finally the hens came with water. All the tools they had brought but how do we use them? Do you have any idea? Lazy they had been so why would they ever care to learn. The farm folk mixed everything up. They sowed the sickle and the plough, they showered seeds on top of the sickle and plough, they drank up all the water and sat there idly without doing anything else but one thing I appreciate, they sleep at night! One night my friend made her way to the barn to see if the all the farm folks were doing well. Hoinkkkkkk...... Mooooooo....... bow bow........... cackle cackle........... THEY WERE ALL PLAYING AT NIGHT! Grrrrrr............. I knew their good behavior wouldn't last for long! Help me! What do I do? Waaaah..... They'll never listen to me! Hmmph!
author: Pahi Shrivastava
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Playful Punda Doesn't Sleep!
text: Punda was a playful puppy. He was also a brave little dog. Every night, Punda would wait for his mother to fall asleep, and then run out to play in the darkness of the night. With a hop and a skip, he would run out the farm and into the little forest across the bridge. He would meet some friends on the way; he would prance and dance, and play and sway. Until he was all too tired. One night, the beaming moon asked him why he did not sleep when he should. Punda replied, "I go to see my friends who stay awake, just like me." "But do you know why they do not sleep at night?" asked the moon, with a smile. Punda did not know. He decided he would ask them when he met them that night. First, Punda met Bijli, the firefly. Curious, he asked, "Bijli, you shine so bright! Don't you tire of shining all day, all night? Why don't you ever rest?" Bijli glowed brighter with her warm smile and replied, "Oh Punda, don't you know? I shine and light up the bug world at night. By day, I rest under the warm blades of grass." Now that Punda knew why Bijli stayed awake, he asked Ulloo, the owl. "Ulloo, dear friend, what keeps you awake? Why don't you sleep in the dark of the night?" "Ah, that's because my big, round eyes see better at night. It's when I can hunt my prey, when they are slow and sleepy," said Ulloo, holding on tight to his dinner - a struggling little mouse. Punda found Kirki, the cricket, wide awake and busy making music by rubbing his legs. "You chirp all night long, Kirki! Get some rest, won't you?" he suggested. Kirki explained that chirping helps cricket friends find each other. "During the day, we sleep in cozy crevices after our night-long merriment," he said with glee. "Chamgu!" Punda called out, as he reached the big bat's tree. Chamgu was hanging upside down, just back from a long flight. He told Punda about his strong lungs and webbed fingers that help him fly far and high at night. "I can't see all too well in daylight, so I rest by day and hunt by night," he panted to catch his breath. Punda was lost in thought about his nocturnal friends, as he headed back to the farm, when he was frightened by the cunning fox. Lomdi was waiting for Punda behind the bushes! Poor Punda was so afraid that he ran back to Chamgu's tree as fast as he could. Punda screamed for help, "Lombdi is after me! Do something, Chamgu!" Just then, all his friends sprang out from behind the tree. "It was just a prank," they laughed. "I would never eat you, little one," reassured Lomdi. "But a puppy must not wander about at night like this," he cautioned. Playful Punda had learned his lesson: never to stray away by himself. And definitely not at night! He bade goodbye to his night-time friends, and returned to the farm, where all the animals were fast asleep. Punda's mother woke up as he settled down to rest beside her. "What's the matter, dear?" she asked sleepily. "Just very sleepy, mamma," yawned a tired Punda. His mother gave him a hug, and covered him warm. Under the light of the beaming moon, Punda was now fast asleep. Peacefully and safe.
author: Vidya Shanbhag

title: When Pilloo Grows Up
text: It was the end of a long day. At Mangal Farm, the animals were fast asleep. All except one. Pilloo the Puppy was wide awake near his mother, Daya. Inside his little head, Pilloo had a big question. "What will I be when I grow up?" Pilloo wanted to find an answer that night. He rushed out of the farm gate, wondering who would be awake at that time. First, Pilloo met Billa the Bat. Pilloo said, "When I grow up, I want to be a Bat." Billa said, "Great idea! Together, we can fly at night and eat many insects." Next, Pilloo saw Coru the Cricket. Pilloo said, "When I grow up, I want to be a Cricket." Coru whispered, "Good idea! Let's chirp all night and taste yummy plants." Then, Pilloo spotted Fafa the Firefly. Pilloo said, "When I grow up, I want to be a Firefly." Fafa smiled and said, "Nice idea! You and I can glow at night and drink tasty nectar." Soon, Pilloo met Fili the Fox. Pilloo said, "When I grow up, I want to be a Fox." Fili grinned and said, "Fun idea! Every night, we can run together and hunt for food." Moving on, Pilloo saw Ola the Owl. Pilloo said, "When I grow up, I want to be an Owl." Ola said, "Very good idea! Let's fly quietly at night and catch many mice." Pilloo pretended to be a Bat, a Cricket, a Firefly, a Fox, and an Owl. And all the animals had fun watching his actions. Pilloo hurried back to the farm before his mother woke up. But Daya was already awake and looked worried. Pilloo told his mother about his adventure. Then, he shouted out loudly, "I have decided. When I grow up, I shall be a Dog." Pilloo and Daya laughed out loud and hugged each other. Little Pilloo was tired after his night adventure. He fell asleep quickly, dreaming about all that he would do when he became a Dog.
author: Anita Nagarajan

title: Golu and the Moon
text: G olu, the dog was always looking for answers. While all his friends slept, he was wide awake wondering about everything. One such night, Golu was watching the stars and the moon and wondered whether they were playing hide and peek with the sun. To his surprise, that night, the moon spoke to him. He said "Come, visit me tomorrow when you see the cows going back to their shed. I will give you the answer". Golu was super excited to hear this and went running to tell his friends. First he went and told the firefly.... Then he told the grasshopper.... Next he told the fox.... Then he told the bat.... And the owl.... That night, all his friends were awake and they all jumped with so much of joy they could not stop their excitement. Golu was very snoopy the next day and was following what the cows were doing all day. 'Ah! there they go', he said. All the cows one by one started entering their shed. Golu waited and watched them all go and then started to see where the moon was. But the moon was nowhere to be seen.... All that Golu could see was the sun moving away behind the clouds and the clouds getting together. He was staring looking at the clouds getting close to each other and the colours of the sky change. Golu had been staring at the sky for so long and when he looked down, he saw that everyone around him had gone to sleep.... Golu was disappointed that the moon did not come to talk to him, as promised. Golu went and laid down beside the cow shed and dozed off. He had a long tiring day. He woke up with a start and saw something shining at him.There, he saw the stars had come and the moon was smiling at him. Golu and the moon spoke for a very long time and Golu was very happy to get the magical answers. Good Night Moon! he said.
author: Shruthi swaminathan

title: Rain is falling chamma, cham......
text: I think rainy season is liked by everyone.It is the best season among all four season,it just comes after hot summer season.Sometimes with rain there are storms,thunder and lightning too. Suddenly a drop of rain falls into my head when i look into the sky.Drop turn into showers and showers. During rainy season children play with mud,dance enjoy,eat sweet mangoes,and make small boats with paper. New leaves are coming to the plants and trees as they get natural water after long time...... Rainy season is very important for farmers,as they really need more water for crop cultivation. Birds and animals they enjoy rainy season as they get lot of water to drink and grow....
author: shilpa

title: Sharbani and the Elephant bird
text: In a beautiful village in the interiors of India lived Sharbani. Sharbani was a chirpy young girl. She was always full of life. The village was near a dense forest. Now, the green forest lay beside a lake. Sharbani loved to wander into the forest. She loved to explore the fauna and flora in the forest. Occasionally she used to come across some small forest animals too. Since the village lay at the edge of the forest, no wild animals were spotted close to the village. She loved to watch the fish in the lake. She was delighted to watch the birds chirp away. She loved her mother and occasionally gave her a helping hand. Sharbani used to collect twigs and broken branches for her mother from the forest. In return, mother used to give Sharbani grains to feed the birds in the courtyard. > V D Everyday Sharbani used to play with her ball beside the lake near the edge of the forest. One day, as she was playing she came face to face with a huge bird. The bird was as big as an elephant. Sharbani stood aghast with fright. She started sweating profusely. The huge elephant bird had a beak and a small feathered tail. Sharbani was clueless. She expected the huge bird to pounce on her anytime now. But as she stood and watched, she was caught by surprise.The huge elephant bird started playing with the ball. Sharbani started to step back slowly. The elephant bird began to move towards her. It startled her so much that she didn’t realise that she was nearly at the edge of the lake. Sharbani lost her balance and fell into the lake with a splash! Sharbani swam across to the village and ran back home as soon as she could. She told father about the huge elephant bird. Her father was annoyed that she had again strolled into the forest. He thought that Sharbani had just imagined the bird. How can a bird be as huge as an elephant? Sharbani could not sleep that night. Had she really imagined that bird? No! she had actually seen it. She had to find an answer. Finally, curiosity got the better of her and she took a lamp and ventured out into the night. She headed to the forest. She started to look around everywhere for the huge bird. She rummaged behind the bushes, trees and plants. She had foraged the forest area near the lake, but she still did not encounter the bird. She went to bed sad and disappointed. Early next morning, Sharbani scurried out again to the forest. It was then that she saw it. Creeping out from the trees, the huge elephant bird was standing near the lake! Sharbani wasn’t afraid now. She knew that the bird meant no harm to her. She got a new friend! Sharbani was so happy that she could not contain her excitement. She hurried home to tell her mother the news. She also informed her neighbours in the village about the bird. She also informed Uncle Bhidukaka about the bird. Now Bhidukaka got disturbed hearing the news. Sharbani was a sweet young girl. There was no way she would weave a false story! He would need to alert the Sarpanch, he thought. Bhidukaka narrated the event to Sarpanch. The Sarpanch was concerned about the safety of the villagers. He called for a meeting of the villagers. The villagers became anxious on hearing the news. Will they have to leave the village? Where will they go now? Sharbani narrated the entire chain of events to the villagers. She could not fathom why the villagers were so worried. She clarified that the bird was very friendly to her. It did not harm her in any way. She also informed them that the bird fed on the fruits and leaves of the trees.It did not hunt the other animals from the forest. Sharbani was engulfed in a volley of questions. “When did you see the animal first?” “Where did you see it?” “How many of them were there?” “Why didn’t you alert the villagers immediately?” "Are you sure you are not making up this story?" The Sarpanch finally asked Sharbani to escort the entire village to the elephant bird. Sharbani ushered them to the edge of the forest near the lake. There near the lake, sat the huge bird.The villagers were dumbstruck. They had never seen such a huge bird ever in their life. Sharbani was actually telling the truth. The bird actually existed. It was indeed a docile creature! The villagers now heaved a sigh of relief. They felt assured that the bird would not hurt them or ruin their village in any manner. The one person who was too happy to hear the news was Sharbani. She loved the elephant bird and now she felt assured that she would be loved too!
author: Sheeba Lekhak
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Stooey The Playful Pet
text: Stooey lives with Sarsa Mami, Kitcha Uncle, and Meghana in a flat, in Chennai. Stooey is a very friendly dog. He is also very smart. He knows how to get his way, even when his family has other ideas. Sarsa Mami decides to take her daily walk. “Down, Stu! Sit!” she says, as she walks out of the gate and carefully closes it behind her. Stu pretends to obey, but his eyes twinkle with disobedience and he cocks his head as if to say, wait, you can’t leave me behind so easily, you’ll see! Sure enough, just as she reaches the corner of the street, she sees a familiar golden brown figure, following, tongue hanging out and laughing. He’s, free to roam, following up interesting scents, sniffing at pretty girls, nosing interesting bags dangling from people’s arms, just staring at people and trying to be friendly. Stu is a street breed, but he imagines himself to be a Labrador, for he’s barrel chested and well muscled. So even if he wants to be friendly, strangers look at him warily and quickly walk off. Stu looks disappointed. He can never understand this. One day, he followed Sarsa Mami to the local roadside temple. The priest taking pity on her, let him stay, for Stu, would not budge and would simply pretend to be deaf, when faced with a direct command to go home. So there he sat, next to the flower vendor, grinning and frightening the life out of all her customers and even, facing the deity and the arathi at the right time. Stu is the leader of a pack of dogs and he assembled the pack himself. Blackie, a beautiful, sleek black dog was his partner in crime and they used to have a fine time barking at other dogs and sliding down the sand piles at a local construction site. Soon, Blackie followed him into the apartment compound. Next came Alli [ Alice] a poor, starved little Alsatian cross breed, thin as a skeleton and starved in many ways. She followed Kitcha Uncle home, was kidnapped by rag pickers, found by a neighbor and adopted by Stu who taught her to be street smart. The last is Valli. She’s a nick-eared dog, black and white and loves rats. Diwali crackers scare Valli. “How frighteningly noisy they are! Why do people have to burst crackers?” she thinks. She went running away, nearly four kilometers at Diwali time, to escape the crackers. They follow Stu’s lead, and run barking, in a pack, when they see intruders. They have a lot of fun. found by a neighbor and adopted by Stu who taught her to be street smart. The last is Valli. She’s a nick-eared dog, black and white and loves rats. Diwali crackers scare Valli. “How frighteningly noisy they are! Why do people have to burst crackers?” she thinks. She went running away, nearly four kilometers at Diwali time, to escape the crackers. They follow Stu’s lead, and run barking, in a pack, when they see intruders. They have a lot of fun.
author: Preethi Krishnan

title: A TALE OF A BIRD AND HER FRIEND
text: This is a tale of a girl named Chunmun and a bird named Frannie. Frannie worked in a circus. Chunmun went to the circus, she enjoyed the show. When the show was over she went to meet Frannie as she enjoyed the show very much. Frannie was pleased but somehow seemed sad. Frannie shared her problem. Chunmun promised to help her escape from the circus that night. She took the lantern and set off to help her escape. This was the toughfest thing. She reached the circus and saw that Frannie was locked in a cage. An idea striked in her mind and she somehow managed to escape Frannie. Chunmun took her to the village. When they reached the village she told Frannie to take rest as it was very late. Next morning, when she went to meet Frannie she saw the villagers gathered around her. Chunmun told everything to them about Frannie and how she managed to escape her. Everyone appreciated her and applauded her. Frannie was free and was thankful to Chunmun. They remained friends forever.
author: ananya khetan
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Change-o-saurus
text: Once apon a time, in a jungle, there lived six animal friends. A wise owl, a dreaming dog, a curious firefly, a funny fox, a jumpy grasshopper and an alert bat. One day the wise Owl suggested that they should travel in time. All the animals laughed except the dog. He told that they could. Then one by one each of the animals tried to make a time machine. Unfortunately, each of them failed. The fox tried first and the dog tried in the end. The dog told the fox the story of The Hunter and the birds and that the story gives a message that " Unity is strength " and told the same thing to all the other animals also. Then all the animals including the owl went to their workshed and this time they all worked together and succeeded in making the time machine. After they finished working on their project they took it out of the work shed and one by one entered the time machine. The dog again was the last one to enter the time machine. Once all were in the grasshopper switched on the time machine. When time machine started the bat switched on a button which turned them all into humans. The owl explained that they made this time machine to find out about the dinosaurs that humans have not found out yet. The wise owl being the leader was very curious. The animals seeing him, also became very curious and wanted to learn more. Then the firefly (who was actually a human now) asked, " How do we know which time in history to go to?" The owl said we can't go back to modern times back to our forest unless the mission gets completed and the button which turned us into humans has only given us little more brains so that we could steer the time machine. We need to keep looking out for which time to land in. They didn't know that if you go close to a time you get sucked in to it. The bat who was in charge of looking which time they were above didn't know that either. So the bat told that they were way too close Neanderthal times and unfortunately got sucked into it. They were all so sad, now they didn't know a way out. Suddenly, a Neanderthal came close to their time machine and enquired who they were and how did they come here. The owl explained everything to the Neanderthal and asked for help. Luckily for them Neanderthal had magic powers and could transport them to Dinosaur times. In a flash they were in the Jurassic era. Next thing that they saw made their eyes pop out. They had never seen such a thing before in their lives. They all gasped for breath and in chorus said " WWWWWOOOOOWWWW". The owl said it was a new species of dinosaur but didn't know which one. The dinosaur also hadn't seen anything like humans (animals turned to humans) before and opened its mouth in surprise. They saw it didn't have sharp teeth so were relieved to know that it was possibly a herbivore. Now they went close to it without fear and asked who that dinosaur was and what was its name? The dinosaur said that it came from a group called Changus and its name was Changeosaurus. It said it was a special dinosaur because it could change colour and form and it had lots of knowledge. The humans(animals) got excited and asked him if it could come with them to their jungle and teach them. Changeosaurus asked them why in jungle? They said they were animals in human disguise and told Changeosaurus the whole story of the time travel. Changeosaurus agreed to come with them but he thought all the animals in modern times might get frightened of him so he decided to turn himself into his favourite animal the dog to come along. All the humans (animals) were so glad to hear that. Now they all got into the time machine, changed back into animals and started their journey back home. They were so happy to have a new friend who was wise and curious just like the owl and from whom they could learn. Every weekday they came to him to learn and on weekends they played happily together. This whole time travel thing was the dreamy dog's dream. When he told it to his other friends all of them laughed so hard and from that day they named him Changeosaurus.
author: Aahan Sarin
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Night Trouble
text: It was a bright night. All the farm animals were asleep. The pigs were in their pen, snoring loudly. The horses stood in their stables, snorting as they were breathing. Cows were sprawled on the lawn, lying in the shiny moonlight. But there was only one animal who was still awake....... the dog and her puppy Rover. The dog curled up in a ball under the tattered shed. The dog immediately fell asleep but little Rover was still staring at the sky. He couldn't sleep. He just wasn't sleepy. So Rover got up and ran across the grass. He decided to ask some of his friends for advice. Then off he ran into the night. Along he went into the dark and stopped at an old tree stump where a wise owl was sitting. "Wise Owl! Wise Owl! I am pretty sure you know what's right. But how do you go to sleep at night?" he asked. "Oh! You cannot sleep at night. You can only sleep in the morning." replied the Owl. Now the puppy was very confused. But why is my mother sleeping, he wondered. He toddled off asking for more advice. Along the way, the little puppy saw a fox staring at him. "Foxy! Foxy! It is very hard for me to go to sleep comfortably," he said. "Oh, that's very easy. Just put your tail around your head. It has been always comfortable for me," he replied. The puppy started chasing his tail, but his tail wouldn't reach his head. In fact, the tail was a stump. So Rover walked off to look for more advice. While Rover was walking, he came upon a bat who was high in the tree. He said, "Black Bat! Black Bat! I try with all my might. But I can't sleep right." "Turn upside down and sleep then. I am sure it will work, " the Bat replied. So the puppy began climbing up the tree, but he slipped and fell on the ground. Rover was not asleep but was hurt. Anyway, he went away in the night looking for more advice. As the puppy walked in the night, he came upon a firefly who was happily buzzing and so he asked, "Firefly! Firefly! In the middle of the night How can you sleep with all that light?" "Just switch your light off. I can always fall asleep after that." the Firefly replied simply. The puppy looked around. he couldn't find the light. He could only see his tail. He closed his eyes and concentrated. However, all he managed was a headache. Off he went into the night looking for more advice. Rover headed along fields and pastures, where crickets were hopping round. He asked the cricket. "Cricket! Cricket! As you can see It is very hard to go to sleep since it is so noisy." "Oh I have the same problem, You can try not to make any noise for me. That always work for me," answered the cricket. So the puppy held his breath and tries not to speak. He didn't feel sleepy, though. He felt strained. He sighed and started going back home. The puppy was still not sure how to fall asleep. He ran back to his shed cutting across the fields. He felt exhausted and quietly crept under the covers. "Oh! Hello, Rover," his mother got up sleepily. "Close your eyes now and try to fall asleep." Rover closed his eyes, curled up in a ball and fell asleep. Finally, all the farm animals were asleep.
author: Shristuti Srirapu

title: Puppy's Friend
text: Well past midnight, the puppy ran out. He seemed to be in a hurry, without a doubt. With the moon shining bright in the sky "Where are you going?", asked the firefly. "To see off my buddy " Said the puppy. "What's up?", asked the bat looking for someone to have a good chat. "I need to go and see-off my buddy" hurriedly said the puppy. The fox jumped from behind the bush, to ask the puppy, "What's the rush?" "Going to wave a goodbye to my friend as his vacation comes to an end". Wonder who puppy's new friend is? A big purple bird and not a liz. Oh beauty! do you've a clue of her home and where is she headed to? She flew all the way from a far away land where it is cold that she cannot stand. She liked it here and said she will be back As soon as it is time to leave her cosy shack.
author: Prajakta Kashalkar-Joshi
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Tigu's Nocturnal Jaunt
text: “Please come with me for a walk through the woods at night, Chirpy sparrow,” pleaded Tigu, the little doggie. “NO!” said Chirpy. “I’m a day bird and NOT a nocturnal bird.” “Noc…non….nocnal? What does that mean?” “Nocturnal!” retorted Chirpy. “It means being wide awake after the sun sets. We do work when the sun is in the sky. Nocturnal folks hunt for food at night!” “Do you know any nocturnal bird?” asked little Tigu. “Even if I did, I will not say its name.” “Why?” persisted Tigu. “They are bigger than me and very scary. And don’t again say, ‘Why?’ They can EAT me up! “ Tigu, however, was now very keen to meet a nocturnal animal or bird. That night, the little doggie ran into the woods. He found a little creature sitting on a branch in a bush. The creature had four long legs and wings. It looked like a grasshopper as well as like a Katydid. It was chirping loudly. “Who are you?” asked Tigu. “I am Cricky, a cricket. Am a distant relative of the grasshoppers.” “Are you singing?” “No! I’m playing a tune by rubbing my forewings together. Only boy crickets can do this!” said Cricky, proudly. “Do people like you?” asked Tigu. “Some people do think crickets bring them prosperity!” “What do you eat?” asked a curious Tigu. Cricky was very small. He certainly could not munch on a crispy biscuit or a raw carrot which Tigu loved to eat! “Forget what I eat!” said Cricky. “Animals and birds eat me. Did you know that human folk too eat me? They fry us or grind us into cricket flour to make protein bars. Cricket farmers grow us to sell us as food for humans and pets. I live in a very scary world!” Tigu was shocked. “Little doggie! There are folks who relish dog meat!” “Grrrrrrrrrr!” growled a frightened Tigu. “How do you know all this?” “Migratory birds get us news from all over the world!” Cricky again started chirping. “May I sing along with you?” asked Tigu. “ NO! Your barking melody will announce that you are up and about at night. A very dangerous thing to do. A hungry fox could catch you! Run away little doggie. Go home!” Tigu ran away further into the dark woods! He sat down under a tree after a while. He felt very uncomfortable. He was sure someone was staring at him! He looked up. From a crevice in the tree, just above his head, two eyes were unblinkingly glaring at him! “G rrrrrrrrr!” growled Tigu. “SHHHHHH! Haven’t you ever seen an owl, you silly dog?” Tigu saw a strange bird glaring at him. “Your…your eyes scared me!” whimpered Tigu. “Who are you?” “I’m Owly, a barn owl. My eyes are fixed in their sockets. So I cannot move them. Yet I have binocular vision. THAT, little doggie, means I can see far off things very clearly.” "What do you do, Sir, if you want to look to the left or right?” asked Tigu, politely. “My head and neck are very flexible. All I have to do is turn my head and neck 270 degrees to the left or right! Excuse me!” said Owly. Tigu saw Owly swoop down and catch a hapless little mouse in its sharp talons. Owly gulped down mouse whole! “Mama says food should be chewed properly!” adviced Tigu. “We are able to digest it better!” ”Gulping down small food saves me time!” retorted Owly. “I regurgitate all the indigestible stuff, such as bones, scales, skin and fur, in the form of hard pellets.” “Re…re…re what?” “Regurgitate. This means I throw out the undigested food through from my beaky mouth! Anyway, WHY are you up and about at night? Run home, foolish little one. A fox could catch you!” Tigu ran away. He did not go home. Moon was in the sky. He wanted to meet more nocturnal folks! He found a strange creature hanging upside on the branch of a tree. It looked like a rat but it had wings! “I can sense you are there,” said the strange creature. “Who are you? My eyesight is not good. I cannot see you!” “I’m Tigu, a little doggie. What is your name? How do you know I am here if you cannot see me?” “I’m a fruit bat. My name is Batty. My vision is not good. So I emit a sound that hits you and echoes back to me. I then know where you are! This technique of ‘seeing’ with sound is called echolocation. Dolphins too can detect their prey’s location by doing this. Did you know that?” “No,” said Tigu, sadly. “I have not met a dolphin. Are they nocturnal creatures too?” “They live in the sea with the fish and whales!” Tigu had eaten fish. However, he had never heard about or seen a sea. He did not want Batty to know this. So he did NOT ask the bat, “What is sea?” Instead he declared, “You look like a mouse!” “Am better than a mouse. I can fly!” said Batty proudly. “I have a cousin called flying fox!” “grrrrr!” whimpered a very frightened Tigu. “Bats are not foxes, silly doggie! Anyway, WHY are you up and about at night? Run home before a nasty fox catches you!” Tigu did not go home. He followed a light glowing in front of him. It looked like an insect! “Hello!” said the insect creature. “I’m Glowy, the firefly!” “You must be feeling very hot,” said Tigu. “Fire makes me feel hot!” “I have light organs under my abdomen. When oxygen touches these, a chemical in my body turns it into cold light. THAT is the secret of my lovely glow! Why are you in the woods, little doggie? Run home! Bad fox will catch you!” Tigu ran on. Then it happened. Tigu bumped into a fox! “Hey! Look when you run!” said Foxy, in a sharp, nasty voice. “Sorry, Sir!” growled Tigu. “Who are you?” “I’m Foxy, the brown fox! How come you have never heard of clever me?” Tigu knew it was now time to go back home. Otherwise Foxy would invite him home! Then either he, little Tigu, would be served dinner by Foxy or become dinner for Foxy! Tigu wished he had listened to the wise advice of Cricky, Owly, Glowy and Batty to go back home. Now he had to find a way to escape from nasty Foxy. It was not going to be easy. Foxy was definitely bigger and stronger than him! Tigu turned around. “Where are you going?” asked Foxy. “I’m bored. Moon is in the sky. We have light. Come, play with me!” Tigu slowly ran ahead. “Where are you going?” asked Foxy. “Back to a dear farmer friend of mine. Can’t you hear him? He is calling out to me!” said Tigu, as he ran a little faster. “Why did you run away from him?” asked Foxy. “He asked me to go ahead to find a fox and bring it back to him. I’m so glad you yourself came to me. Now I can take you to him. He will be very happy! He wants to meet you. He says YOU, Mr Fox, are very, very clever. You always succeed in stealing a chicken from his chicken coop. My friend wants to congratulate clever YOU!” Foxy stopped in his path. “Good God! I just remembered I have some urgent work to do!” said Foxy. “I’ll come later to meet your friend.” " NO! " barked Tigu, loudly. “ COME WITH ME! MY FRIEND WANTS TO SHAKE HANDS WITH YOU! " “Hush, little one!” said Foxy, scared that Tigu’s man friend would find them. “I will follow your scent and come to meet you!” “ PROMISE? ” “Yup!” said Foxy. “Run along, little doggie. I will come to meet your friend!” Tigu ran home as fast as he could! He did not stop to talk to Batty, Owly, Glowy or Cricky. Tigu has decided that his next nocturnal jaunt will be with a strong, fierce friend. After meeting nasty Foxy, he now knows that it is NOT safe to run about alone in the woods at night!
author: Hema Rao

title: Saru, your milk!!
text: Scene 1 (At Khulipuri village) (Crowing of a cock) Cock - aka - doodle - doo....... Amma: Saru......! Where are you? You haven't finished your milk! Come back straight away....... (Saru enters the hut) Saru: Amma, I have already told you not to mix turmeric but you always do. Uh huh! I won't have this milk. Esha is calling me..... Amma: Saru............. Narrator: But Saru was already out of sight... Scene 2 (At Ram Rangan Forest) Narrator: Saru and Esha crossed Ramratna fields and made their way to the Sharatnami river to cool off in the scorching sun. (Esha whispers) Esha: Ummmmm...... Saru I hear some rumbling down there in the bushes beside Samprada Orchards........ Can you hear them? (Saru speaks loudly) Saru: What is it Esha? You must be hearing some silly noise. Now co -................ (Saru is interrupted with a screech.) Narrator: The terrified girls got out of that site and raced towards Sharatnami river. Scene 3 (At Ram Rangan forest again) Narrator: The girls made up their mind to check the bushes, and find out what the noise was......... Saru: Esha, we hear these noises seldom. The Ram Rangan forest is a secret and magical forest. How could someone possibly enter? Esha: Anything can happen Saru. This is how life is..... Narrator: The girls slowly move towards the bushes and peek inside on the count of three Saru: Awwww! A dinosaur. One with a purple shade, jet black eyebrows, blue eyes and a grinning mouth. Narrator: Word spread like wildfire in the forest. Damru: Mr. Bat, Have you heard, the two girls of Khulipuri village were walking to Sharatna- (Damru is interrupted by Mr. Bat) Mr.Bat: Now don't tell me a tall story... Just get to the final topic! Damru: Fine, Fine! The two girls found a dino in the forest..... Mr.Bat: Let me give a big hand for that. Huh! Oh really? Damru: It is true believe me.......... Scene 4 (At Khulipuri village.) Narrator: The girls sure did find something but dino was in for trouble.... Saru: Welcome dino, to our splendid village with merry people. You are free to roam. Esha: But Saru don't you think that dino will be unsafe. Shravan, our hunter might hurt him. In my opinion, I say that let the bird stay in the outskirts and enter no village. (Saru motions to dino) Saru: Don't go! There is threat. Let us explore more of the outskirts. Come Esha. Narrator: They avoid the village and move towards the outskirts to explore. Narrator: They were just moving away when worried Esha says....... Esha: Saru we haven't been at home from morning. Amma might be searching for you and me! Come on! Saru: But what about dino? What can we do about him?...................... I know! We can let him sleep under the Chaturbhuja Tree. I will show him the way while you go to Amma and tell her that I am coming. Narrator: Saru dropped dino at the Chaturbhuja tree and raced back home. Scene 5 (Near the Chaturbhuja tree.) Narrator: Saru couldn't stick to her bed for too long. All kinds of strange things happening to dino were circling in her mind. She got up and shuffled towards the tree in the cold night. Saru: Dino, Dino! Where are you? Dino....... It's Saru here. Please don't tell me you are not there. Dino....... Narrator: Saru didn't hear any reply. The forest was silent and calm.She hurriedly started to search every corner, every nook of the forest. Dino? Dino? Dino? No! She searched everywhere but there was no trace of Dino.............. Scene 6 (At Khulipuri village) (Everyone wakes up due to the crowing of the cock.) Narrator: Saru quickly rushes to Esha and recites her encounter in the night. Flabbergasted Esha instructs Saru to take her to the tree. Scene 7 (At the forest where the tree was located.) Esha (Looking at the tree): You're right. Dino's missing. I am sure he has been hunted by someone but I don't know who that someone is. Saru: Hmmmmm... Esha, don't you have the feeling that Dino must have run away to Lalnagar village cause I see some foot marks towards the path which leads to Lalnagar village. Esha: Your right. Silly! If you had noticed those earlier then we would have reached more quickly. Now leave that and lets move on. Saru: I agree. Let's go! Narrator: The girls walked real fast to reach Lalnagar and finally seeing their red,out of breath bodies Shyam offered a lift till the village. They reach the village in no time. Scene 8 (At Lalnagar) Saru: Maybe Chandlal babu, the headman might have seen Dino. Let's hope that he might have. Narrator: They went in the hot sun, with a piece of warm bun, They were almost there, but any trace they couldn't share. Scene 9 (They keep on walking and searching.) Saru: I think- AAAAAAAAAH! Narrator: And there stood Dino with his grinning face. What a trick Dino had played!Saru tripped and fell in the water! Esha: Oh! Saru. But I must say it was a fine trick. Hahaha! Saru: Pesky! Where were you? We were searching for you everywhere! Cool trick by the way............. Narrator: Saru and her friends walked back to Khulipuri village. Scene 10 (Back at Khulipuri Village) Narrator: Saru was imagining herself being laden with flowers of all colours and being said that she found a dino an behaved well with it.But all she heard was........ (Lots of people talking together) Villagers: Saru, Your milk!,Your Milk! You didn't drink it! Saru you forgot! Saru, Saru,Saru, Saru!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Saru: But....... Waaaaaaah! And that is the tall, Funny, adventurous, Curious story of Saru and her Mates................

title: Rinku-The Savior
text: There was a village named Rampur located at the bank of the river Sarada, which is only source of water for the villagers. The atmosphere in the village was always pleasant and people enjoyed their neighborhood. No quarrels and ill treatment There was always a evening session of stories held by Mukhiya of the village under a huge Banyan tree and all the children gather to hear his fascinated stories. But that day Mukhiya didnt attend to narrate his story.He went to meet his old friend. And came back with a news that there was a strange animal found moving near the river and warned the villagers to not to visit river until the animal is caged.Everyone worried about what harm could the animal do to them. But little girl named Chitra,was excited to see the animal as she was hearing more stories about it.One evening Chitra informed mother that she is going out to play with her friends and took her ball. But she has some other thing to do.She slowly went to the river without getting caught by the villlagers. She started playing with the ball,but secretly waiting for the animal to come.Her ball ran into the bushes and suddenly she heard a strange noise behind the trees she was standing and there appeared a huge animal with a beak and claws and a huge tail. With the sudden appearance of the strange animal chitra shivered with fear and took two steps back, unaware of the river. She slipped into the river and started shouting for help. Then the animal Jumped into the river and helped chitra to get back Chitra is safe now. She thanked the animal and gave him some fruits to eat.She also made her mind clear that this animal is no way a harm to the village. So she immediately rushed to the village and narrated the story to her father and the villagers.There was a long argument from both the sides.No one are ready to believe her words so she asked them to visit the river and see what kind of animal it is. Everyone agreed and walked to the river along with Chitra. There they found the animal bathing in river and then came out and had some fruits from the tree near by.The animal overjoyed on seeing Chitra and rubbed its beak smoothly to her head Now villagers believed that it is of no harm and moved near. Some patted its back and some fed the animal with fruits. Finally Chitra was happy as she can visit the animal without fear and take a ride on it. Everyone called the animal Rinku-The savior.
author: Ghousia Begum
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Core Act of the Magic of Friendship
text: Dandi the violet bird wanted some friends. She believed that to get a friend, you must wait till they come and be your best friend. So, Dandi went inside a lush forest and waited till someone came by and asked to be a friend of hers. She waited days and months for one, but no one came. Dandi couldn't bare looking at the insulting sight of birds Tick and Tock playing joyfully and mice Vinegar and Cheesey. playing Toss the Laddu together. She felt sad for she did not have even one friend whom she could play with. One day she decided to find out why she did not have a friend and set out on an unexpectedly amazing tour of the rainforest. A warm feeling crept over her when the water from the trees dripped and dropped droplet by droplet over her. She loved taking an elephant ride and especially had fun when the friendly elephant splashed water from a nearby stream drenching her wet. When Dandi came upon a small village beyond the rainforest, something caught the corner of her eye. She saw a hut which seemed a little different from the other huts in the village. In the garden of that hut, she could see children playing joyfully, Grandpa gently swinging on the swing reading a newspaper. Dandi could not help but wonder," Is this house magical in some way? How come there is such happiness and joyfulness in the house that it just stood out from the others?" That day Dandi's curiosity bet her fear of making friends. She was confident that today she will surely make a friend. She had never felt this brave before. 'This is my first time this close to humans.' She thought. Back from where she came from, there weren't many options to make friends with. Then, an idea struck her. She ran towards that hut like a lightening bolt would, to strike a tree. She waited at the gate for someone to come forward to make friends with her but no one did. She felt as disheartened as a parched ground waiting for the rain. She felt bitter from inside. Then suddenly, she saw a little girl walking around every house. She seemed to be looking for something. It somehow seemed important to the girl. Finally, as if she hit a jackpot, she ran out of a hut squealing with a jolly good expression dancing all over her face. She was beaming with happiness. The girl was holding someone's hand. "Oh! my new friend! we are going to have a wonderful time together. I am so glad that you accepted my friendship." She said. That was when it hit Dandi. She realized, that to have a friend, she needed to make an improvement in herself. She thought that if I keep waiting for someone to come and make friends with me, the people may not even know that I exist. To get a friend and enjoy the world of friendship, I must go forward and offer myself to make friends. Dandi took the most important step of entering the door to the magic of friendship. This was the last stair on the staircase of making friends and she did it alright! She moved forward and asked the girls nervously. "Hi, I am Dandi Violets. I am looking for friends. Would you like to be my friend?" The girls looked at each other and took a quick glance of Dandi. A shy feeling crept over them. They looked at each other as if asking for their consent. "YES!!!" They exclaimed joyously and gave Dandi the biggest hug she had ever received from anyone she'd ever known! MORAL: Ask if you want a friend, do not wait for them to come forward. THE END
author: Aanvi Mathur

title: Educate the girls, save the world
text: 'Tring, Tring!', rang the school bell.All the students went running to the huge Chaturbhuja tree where they would sit under it's shade. A big, shady,leafy, green tree it sure was. But what is this I see! Only the male gender is present. Since I am a girl I must flee. But why is the female gender not being educated? Here is where my story starts. People in this world don't want the female to be educated but somehow few countries manage to educate their girls. Story Time! Have fun! 4 year old Lakshmi asked her mom," Amma, I want to go to school. I want to be educated like Bapu." Before Amma could answer Bapu came inside and said in a stern voice," Lakshmi, Don't talk about these things. Girls don't go to school! Now be quiet and silently sweep my room." Without saying anything even Amma got on with her work. Lakshmi, looked at her mom, perhaps that meant bye, and walked out of the house to meet her friends Anu, Swara and Sresta. This is what she said," If we are stranded in the jungle and we are not able to find our way and we very much wish to calculate how far the village is, for that we need to study and for that we need a school. We will collect money from each house to build a school exclusively for girls to study. Lets get to work." They went to every house and pleaded for some donation for money. Soon the day passed and they had collected a lot by going to 15 different villages. They gave the money to the headman and the builders started the construction. Almost lots of girls from about 21 villages used to come to that school everyday. Looks like Lakshmi and her friends created a living and made way for future. Bonus: She became a school principal when she grew up and won a big lot of awards. Note: This is not based on a true life story. Educate the girls, Save the girls!
author: Pahi Shrivastava
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Mr.Paper...
text: Hi,I am Mr.Paper,as i have become very useful article in our day to day life. You can see me everywhere at home, school,shops, factory etc..... I am manufactured in the factory from grass,straws and bamboos.... Now a days it is difficult to imagine the life without news paper.It is the first thing people look in morning.It is good habit to read news paper on daily basis.
