title: Tukkee and Her Parrot
text: Tukkee was a little girl who lived with her parents in a village near the jungle. She was a very happy child and was loved by her family and friends. Her parents were farmers and earned their living by growing vegetables and grains in a small piece of land owned by them. Her family was not rich but they managed to save enough for the year. One year the summers became too hot and no rains followed. Everyone in the village was worried and hoped it would rain soon. An year passed and then another but the village and the forest had no respite from the scorching sun. Water became scarce and the farmers in the village were not able to grow either vegetables or grains. Tukkee's father sold of his cattle to arrange for money to buy food for his family. Tukkee was sad because she loved the cow and other animals. She had often taken them for grazing in the nearby forest when her parents were busy in the fields. But she understood her father's plight and did not cry. The water in the river had dried up and even the well in the village was left with just a puddle. Animals from the nearby forest started coming towards the village in search of water. Till now the villagers and the wild animals had lived in complete harmony but with the onset of drought both man and animal had started encroaching each other's territory. Many villagers afraid that the wild animals would attack them and their children started leaving the village. With the rain no where in sight they even moved to bigger cities in search of work. Tukkee's father could not afford to leave his piece of land and go. Tukkee bid farewell to many friends who left along with their parents. She soon felt lonely and sad. To cheer her up, Tukkee's father got her a parrot. "You can teach him how to talk." said her father. Tukkee was delighted. She took care of the parrot and even shared whatever little food she had with it. Many days passed but even though Tukkee tried a lot, the parrot did not speak. "Say my name, Tukkee. Say Toookkeeee." But the parrot just chirped and did not say a word. Tukkee loved her parrot. She even set it free from its cage. The parrot would fly around the village and Tukkee would follow it everywhere feeding it chillies and a few grains that her mother would give. "Don't go to far." her mother would say, "There is a tiger on the prowl."Tukkee obeyed her mother and always played close to home. "When will my parrot talk, Mother?" she asked. "Soon my child." replied Mother. One night when Tukkee was fast asleep and the entire village lay still, slowly from the jungle a big yellow cat with a shiny coat moved towards the village. It was the tiger, hungry and thirsty. Not a dog barked as they hid with fear as the tiger prowled around the village in search of food and water. It headed towards Tukkee's house where her father was sleeping in the verandah. The parrot saw the tiger and started fluttering and screaming, "Toooookie." he chirped, "Tooookie," loud and clear. Tukkee woke with start surprised at the parrot's call. But on seeing the parrot frantically flutter she knew something was wrong and woke her father who called out their neighbours for help. The tiger was shocked at the commotion
author: Vibha Lohani
illustrator: Bulbul Sharma; Greystroke; Helga Parekh; Reshma Barve; Sanjay Sarkar; Saurabh Pandey; Soumya Menon; Vinayak Varma

title: Meena and her bird
text: It was a very peaceful atmosphere in Meena's house. Meena's mother was making rotis. Meena's father was chanting the Vedas while Meena's siblings played around him. Meena herself was squatting next to her mother, ready to run small errands for her. But in the barn there was confusion. Clancy, the colt, was running in circles around the barn knocking over everything in his way. Florence Negrestor Colster, the pig, was in hysterics because Fanny, the calf, had teased her saying that her name was far too fancy and long for a pig. Everyone was shouting and screaming, the older ones because the younger ones were shouting and screaming. The younger ones because grandma pig who used to tell them a story every night had just died. And they couldn't sleep without a story. Finally Ma pig, sleepy as she was, rose up and said wearily " I will tell you a story", her voice was drowned in the cheers that followed. When the noise died down Ma pig cleared her throat and started the story....... Once Meena had a ever so tiny pet bird. She really loved it a lot. She spent all her free time with it. But it was quite obvious that the bird didn't love her as much as she loved it. It kept trying to run off into the forest. Meena was quite afraid that it would get trampled upon. So, when a great magician came to the town she was quite happy. She went straight to the magician and begged him to enlarge the bird. The magician agreed to do it for ten rupees. When the bird was enlarged it was too big to sleep in the house. So they put it to sleep outside the house (they had to drive it there with sticks). The next morning a cry from the early rising Meena woke her parents. The bird had disappeared. Meena was inconsolable. She cried the whole day. But when the house was dark and silent she slipped out of the house w ith a lantern to light the way. She went straight to the forest and lo! There to greet her stood the bird. Meena played with the bird all night long. At the crack of dawn she tried to lead it home. But as soon as it saw that she was taking it home it bolted. But the next night it was there at the edge of the forest waiting for Meena. But when she tried to take it home it bolted again. And so it happened. Every night, when everyone was asleep Meena would creep out to play with the bird. Every morning at the crack of dawn she comes back home. THE END. "You like it?", asked Ma pig. No one answered. Everyone was fast asleep. "Well that certainly was a not-so-bad good night story", thought Ma pig as cuddled up in the straw. Suddenly she spotted a tiny light. She looked out of the barn window. There was Meena holding the lantern and tip-toeing out of the house. "Well, that's none of my business if it is what I think it is", thought Ma pig as she went back to the straw. THE END
author: Vakula  Surendar
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Mr Moon's New Friends
text: The Moon shined bright, as it looked down. It was so lonely up there, he almost carried a frown. Everyone was fast asleep, he could hear them snore. He smiled, it was time for his night stroll. He would peek through windows and glance through doors. He would pass through the barn and hear animals snore. But today was different, some one was awake. Lola the bitch and her puppy Jake. The naughty puppy, closed his eyes for a while and just as his mother slept, he smiled. Jake saw the big shy orb hiding behind the tree. He smiled and asked the Moon, "Will you play with me?" The moon nodded in delight, and shone very bright. The little puppy asked, "How many friends do you have Mr. Moon, five, six or ten?" The Moon frowned and said, "Alas, I have none. Everyone sleeps at night, when I come out. I can't even whisper, let alone shout." Jake smiled and said, "Not everyone sleeps at night. Some doze off, when the day is bright." "Come along," said Jake and started to run. The Moon followed him, looking for some more fun. They came to a tree, with leaves red and brown. A funny sort of creature, hung upside down. "Mr. Moon," said Jake, "Meet Mr. Bat. He stays up all night and loves to chat." They tiptoed carefully, on the grass they tread, when Jake saw someone pointy ahead. "Oh Look Mr Moon," cried Jake, "This is Mr. Cricket. You can listen to him sing, without buying a ticket!" They moved ahead to a glowing hedge. Jake called out softly, "Mrs. Glow Worm, come out, please don't dread." Mrs. Glow Worm sparkled a little more, as with a warm smile, she said, "Hello!" The Moon smiled to see this tiny speck of light. He thought the worm was a pretty treat to the sight. They moved ahead and took a long stroll, until they reached the big tree with a hole. An owl sat atop with big round eyes, Jake called out to him, "Mr. Owl, I have a surprise!" "Meet Mr. Moon, he comes out every night. He is big and round and spreads a lot of light." Mr. Owl hooted out aloud, almost scaring off the cloud. "Hello Mr. Owl," said the Moon, "How do you do?" "I am good," hooted Mr. Owl, "And I hope you are too!" As the Moon and Jake moved ahead from the Owl, they came across a furry Fox, on the prowl. "Oh Mr. Fox, you scared me today. Meet Mr. Moon he has come out to play." The Moon was happy, so many friends he had made. They laughed and danced and all night they played.
author: Vibha Lohani

title: GUBBI & HER GUMMA
text: Meet Gubbi, the naughtiest girl in the village. She was the most adorable child anyone had ever met. She loved playing pranks, especially on her parents. One fine day, Gubbi decided to go to the woods, all alone. So she sneaked away when her amma was busy making rotis. Gubbi was so engrossed running here and there in the woods that she did not notice where she was going! She slipped, fell and went tumbling down all the way to the river. Before she knew what had happened, she was drowning! She screamed for help. But no one heard her. Wait... someone did hear her! When Gubbi opened her eyes, she was no longer in the water. In fact, someone had fished her out. She turned to see who was around. To her shock, she saw a huge strange looking creature smiling at her! It had a beak, but no wings! It had a feathery tail and bird-like claws too. However, it wasn't a bird because it couldn't fly! Gubbi was shivering with fear. Gubbi ran back to the village as fast as her tiny feet could carry her. She told her parents, her neighbours and everyone what she saw. According to Gubbi, the creature was a "Gumma". A trader from a faraway land passing by happened to hear her story. He wondered what the Gumma looked like. The villagers did not believe Gubbi. Some said that she was dreaming. Some said she had mistaken a huge tree for a "Gumma". The rest said that Gubbi was cooking up a story to scare other children of the village. Gubbi was sad and felt helpless. Gubbi decided to find out on her own if it was a dream that she saw. So, holding a lantern in hand, Gubbi set out to the woods that very night, without telling anyone... Gubbi roamed the woods searching for her Gumma, but it was nowhere to be seen. She looked here, she looked there. She looked for it everywhere. The sun was rising and a disheartened Gubbi decided to go back. Just when she was leaving, Gubbi heard a rustle from behind a bush. She turned to see the magnificent creature standing right there! But this time, Gubbi wasn't scared to see her Gumma. In fact, she wanted to thank it for saving her life. She smiled at her Gumma and the Gumma smiled back... Gubbi completely forgot that she had to go home before her parents woke up. She spent the day with her Gumma. She saw the Gumma bathing in the river. The Gumma ate fruits from tall trees as it was tall too! After playing with the Gumma, Gubbi went back to her worried parents and narrated the whole story. Her appa scolded her. But after thinking for sometime, her appa decided to talk to the village head about this "Gumma". Yes, Gubbi's appa believed her. Gubbi and her appa spoke to the village head in the presence of villagers. They decided to search the creature. They wanted to make sure that the strange creature would not cause harm to them or their crops. Gubbi then told them where they could find her Gumma. She suggested that she go first and the villagers follow her. She felt that the creature wouldn't come forward if it saw so many men approaching it. The villagers thought it was a good idea. After walking for a long time, they finally spotted it! The Gumma wasn't expecting the villagers at all! The villagers were awestruck on seeing the strange creature. Soon the word spread and the trader from a faraway land came to know about the Gumma. He met the village head and asked him if he could buy the creature. He promised ten bags of gold coins in exchange. The villagers liked the deal and decided to sell the creature to the trader. So much gold could do much good to the village, they said. But Gubbi didn't want her Gumma to be sold. Sensing danger, the creature ran deep into the woods, never to be seen again by any villager. Gubbi was happy that the villagers couldn't sell her Gumma to the trader. She was happy that her Gumma was safe. To this day Gubbi doesn't know that her friend stealthily moves near her house every night to make sure that Gubbi is safe.
author: Adithimanasa T S
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Bheera's friendship
text: Dr.Sharmista takes her dog whom she fondly calls as Bheera for outing to the nearby jungle.And then Bheera runs to something that shines brightly.On Reaching the place, he sees a firefly know as 'Titli '.Slowly the firefly know as 'Titli' be friends Bheera and soon after that their friendship blossoms. One day Bheera -the dog travels alone in jungle to meet Titli as he is fascinated by her glowing nature. Bheera says "AhTitli! what a fascinating creature are you, you are only one who is the cause ofmy being so happy".To this Firefly Titli says "Dear Bheera you are only one who has admired me the most"
author: Mitthi(Mohini)

title: Getting Your Way
text: Meera was an average eight year old in her village. Well, perhaps not the most average one! Because after all, how many eight year olds possess a large, purple-coloured elephant bird? None at all! Meera loved her elephant bird! She didn't know how she lived before she found him! There was, however, one little snag in keeping the elephant bird- no one else knew. You see, Meera was rather a naughty little girl, and she felt certain that no one would encourage her in the looking after of her bird, (this was correct) on account of all the tricks she had played on them. Living in a joint family had its advantages- more people to trick! Her mother would definitely not let her keep the bird, especially since Meera stole all the chapattis one day and fed it to the bird itself! And her father-well, if we continue like this, we'd be going all day! But how long can things be kept a secret? Not very long!-especially not in large families! There came the day when Meera's elder brother Shyam found the elephant bird hiding in the abandoned cowshed. "Ammaaaaaaaaaaa!" he shouted after a dumbstruck pause, "AMMA! THERE'S SOME-SOME THING IN THE SHED!" Amma came hurrying out, and she in turn called her husband, 'Appa'. This went on for a few minutes until the entire family was standing around the frightened elephant bird. Well, the entire family except for Meera! Poor Meera! When she saw the crowd near the shed, she came running up as fast as her short legs could carry her! "MEERA" shouted the whole family, because by now, they had put two and two, and figured out that no one else but Meera would keep such a bird in the cowshed! "DON'T HURT MY ELEPHANT BIRD!" yelled Meera as she reached the shed. She stroked the lovely bird's long neck lovingly as she glared at her family-who glared right back at her! "How dare you keep such a creature here?" they demanded angrily. "Leave the creature in the forest right now!" shouted her father, coming up to her, "It could be dangerous-" "It is NOT!" interrupted Meera, but this just made everyone angrier than before! "IT COULD BE DANGEROUS," continued her father, increasing the volume of his voice, "And it should be gone in half an hour." Saying so, he walked off dramatically, and slowly the rest of the family also joined him, occasionally turning to shake their heads at the unfortunate Meera and her elephant bird. Meera felt tears fill her eyes as she looked at the elephant bird. "Sorry," she whispered, "You have to go." Fifteen minutes later, Meera was walking in the forest with the elephant bird by her side. Well, not exactly by her side! He was making things very difficult indeed for Meera, since it kept stopping, pawing the ground, eating fruits and splashing the river water on her. "Okay-That's IT!" shouted Meera after about twenty minutes of this, "I'm just going to leave you HERE! Good bye elephant bird!" She stormed back in the other direction, but the elephant bird slyly pushed an apple in her direction. "Now you're throwing things at me!" said Meera irritably, and then she tripped over the apple. With a scream, Meera fell into the river headfirst, toppling into the strong current. The elephant bird dived in after her, and pulled her out in one powerful movement. Meera lay on the ground gasping with sobs and with the icy coldness of the water. "Oh-elephant-bird!" she managed to say, "You-you saved my life!" The elephant bird inclined his head modestly as if to say- "Oh well, that was nothing." A grasshopper who had seen all this, hopped all the way back to the farm, and told Paachu the farm dog what happened. "So you're saying," Paachu barked slowly, "You're saying that the elephant bird saved Meera's life?" "That's right!" chirruped the grasshopper excitedly, "That's right! He was a good old thing, I knew! He wouldn't hurt anybody! Though Meera was going to leave him, he saved her life!" "Wow!" barked Paachu, "That's some nice bird she has! I'd better tell everyone!" But the moon smiled at the pair of animals. She had seen it all. She knew what had happened-do you? The clever old elephant bird had purposely and indirectly pushed Meera into the river so that he could save her himself! Then what would the family say? Why, they would say- "You good old bird! You can stay with us forever! You saved our darling Meera's life!" And what do you think did happen? Just that! Paachu passed on the message until the whole family knew, and they rushed to the forest at once, congratulating the bird and hugging Meera. Meera never quite knew what happened, though she did have a faint idea that the elephant bird had got his way through her falling into the river. Even though six years have passed now, and Meera lives happily with her elephant bird all grown up, the moon never forgot the story of the elephant bird. And how do I know this story? Well, the moon told me, of course! THE END
author: Gayatri Allamsetty
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Bonding .
text: Darn!!!My parents are too much,Rita thinks and steps out of house in the night with a lamp in her hands.Chanting "I am not all alone Krishna is with me " she surpasses the jungle and goes to the local market place to buy medicines for her little brother Raj. Raj who has a speech defect. Rita parents knowing her nature let her go, but eventually one day Raj shouts at her with difficult and run away from his house without giving Rita a proper explanation.Rita shrugs her shoulders and cries a lot for him. 'Raj' 'Raj' saying this she sleeps with swollen eyes. Next day morning when Rita wakes up she finds Raj holding two cups of flavoured milk for hher which he had got from the local market that day in mark for the love she showers on him.. Though he did shout at her but for a good reason because of his shouting his vocal cord started to work in rhythmic way. Seeing Raj's love towards Rita --- his sister, their parents i.e. Rita's parents feel delighted with joy in their eyes they hug Raj with all their love.
author: Mitthi(Mohini)

title: Chanda Mama says 'Good Night'
text: It was night. All the animals were still awake. They were busy talking about how their day went. Lucy was cracking good jokes and all animals were laughing. Lucy came back home to sleep. Chanda Mama smiled at him and said, 'Lucy, did you say Good Night to your friends?' Chanda Mama said, 'Lucy, you should always say good night to everyone before you go to sleep. It is a good habit.' Lucy understood. He ran towards his friends' home. 'Hey Baty, you sleep hanging upside-down?' 'Yes, Lucy!' 'Good Night Baty, Sweet Dreams!' 'Good Night Lucy' 'Hi Mr. Hopper. You are not asleep yet?' 'Hey Lucy. Going for a walk after my dinner.' 'Good Night Mr. Hopper. See you tomorrow.' 'Hello baby Bee, do not go far away alone in the night. Where is your mother, Lady Bee?' 'She will be back in a minute.' 'Okay. Good night baby Bee!' 'Mr. Smart Fox, hello.' 'Hello kid' 'Before you go to bed, I wanted to say you Good Night!' 'Wonderful Lucy. Good Night to you too. You are a very good kid.' 'Uncle Owl, I always see you sleeping during day, but not in the night!' 'Yes Lucy. I sleep during the daytime. Do not worry, you can still wish me 'Good Night' kid.' 'Good Night Uncle Owl!' Lastly, Lucy came to his best friend Big Piglet. The Piglet hugged Lucy and both wished each other 'Good Night'. Chanda Mama was happy to see Lucy wishing Good Night to everyone. Lucy wished Chanda Mama Good Night and went to sleep.He was very tired. He felt happy that he wished all his friends Good Night. Chanda Mama said, 'Good Night my dear Lucy'. Good Night to all of you. May you all have sweet dreams and a wonderful day tomorrow. Good Night readers.
author: Ankit Kumar

title: Munni and the Big Sea Bird
text: A Big Sea Bird lived in the Pundy village near river Kaveri. The Big Sea Bird loved to play football. One evening, while playing with her friends, Munni saw the Big Purple sea Bird. She went to the Big Sea Bird and said, "Will you be my friend? Will you play with me?" The Big Sea Bird smiled happily. She said, "Yes. You are my first friend!" Munni was very happy. She never had a Big Sea Bird as a friend. She started playing football with her new friend. BUT the villagers did not like the Big Sea Bird! They thought that it was big and ugly. Munni's father, Pappu was very angry at her. He stopped her from playing with the Big Sea Bird. He told Munni to go back to their hut. Munni was very sad. She was still dreaming of playing with her the Big Sea Bird. Munni saw that her amma was busy cooking food. She escaped from home and ran to play with Big Sea Bird. Munni was playing football near the river with her new friend. The Sea Bird loved playing with Munni. She took some water in her mouth and poured over Munni. Munni said, "Wait Big Sea Bird, you poured water on me. I will also do the same thing with you." She ran towards the river to get some water. BUT her leg slipped. Munni fell in the river. She did not knew swimming. She was going down and down in the river! The Big Sea Bird came to her rescue. She pulled Munni out of the river and saved her life. She was Munni's best friend ever. Munni's father saw how the Big Sea Bird saved Munni's life. He hugged her. He said, "Munni, you can play with the Big Sea Bird. She saved your life. She will always take care of you."
author: Ankit Kumar
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Lost Football
text: It was a quiet and cool night. The whole village of Kohlrampur was asleep. All men, women, kids and animals were in deep sleep. Every morning the Village Mukhiya used to play football with his grandson. BUT that morning he was not able to find the football. The Village Mukhiya was angry at the villagers. The Village Mukhiya stopped an old man. 'Sirji, have you seen a red football?' 'No Mukhiya Ji. I am a traveller. I was just passing by this village. I have not seen your football.' Mukhiya thought that Golki would have stolen the football. Golki was the most mischievous girl in the whole village. She was very naughty. Mukhiya told her, 'Golki, enough of your playful behaviour. Give my football back to me!' 'I do not have it Mukhiya Ji', said Golki. But no one in the village believed Golki. They all started scolding Golki. They said that she was a thief and a very bad girl. Golki did not like that the villagers called her a bad girl. During night, when her mother and father went to sleep she went out. She took a lamp with her. She started searching for the football. Golki started searching behind the bushes and the trees. She searched in the village garden. She checked everywhere in the village, but she could not find the football anywhere! Next Day Morning, she started searching again. Golki went from one house to another and then another. But alas! She could not find the football anywhere. Golki was very sad that she could not find the football. She decided to go near the river. She would sit there and think on how to find the football. Near the river, Golki saw a Big Purple Elephant Bird. The Big Bird was playing with the football. Golki went to take the football from the Big Bird. BUT the Big Bird did not give the football back to Golki. Instead the Big Bird hit Golki with football. Golki ran towards the village. The Villagers came with stick in their hands. They fought with the Big Bird and took the football. Golki went home happily. Everyone loved Golki for finding the football. She even played football with the Village Mukhiya and his grandson.
author: Ankit Kumar
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Chakora , The Brave Dog
text: Chakora, the stray dog with big eyes and black skin was roaming around in the village. He liked jumping over the fences, running on the soft green grasses, playing around with small insects, trying to catch flies with his claws. As the moon was shining very brightly, sleep stayed away from him that night. Chakora did not feel anything when he was having the time of his life that night. But soon afterwards, tiredness crept inside him, he started feeling thirsty and hungry. He scanned his gaze through the village but there was not a soul awake at that hour. The doors were closed. The lanterns were not lit. While roaming around to find some water and food, Chakora came across the banyan tree where Kallu, the bat was hanging on its branch. Chakora looked at Kallu and saw that Kallu was meditating. Chakora was amused when he saw the asana in which Kallu was meditating. Chakora thought that the humans need to learn from him and pay him royalty for using his trademark asana position. While thinking about it, suddenly his thought met thirst and hunger. With a very sorry face and a tragic expression, Chakora asked Kallu if he had any left over food to spare. Kallu, still holding his ground in his

title: Raven and the magical guitar
text: Once upon a time there lived a witch named Raven Feather.Raven looked as pretty as a newly made doll,had perfectly straightened dark black hair and was kind but strict.She used to teach Tella, Gold, Tigar and few other girls,but now she works in a company called Google. Tella looked as pretty as a lemon, had lovely brown hair and was very kind.Gold was as pretty as snow and had beautiful golden hair like her name and was kind sometimes was also mean. Tigar looked as pretty as a tomato, had nice hair the color of a blueberry and was mean most of the times. Raven,Tella, Gold, Tigar, and Lima were B.F.F’s and always hung out when they were free. Lima was Raven’s best buddy sense kindergarten and was kind and strict also like Raven. One day, Raven and her friends planned to meet in a park called Lily Gardens on Saturday. This Saturday Raven and her friends packed their lunch and met in Lily Gardens. They had lots of fun and it was story time, Raven kindly offered to go first. She chose a story that took place in many places and was about five of them. Last saved on 4:32 PM The whole story started with Raven becoming angry at Tella, Gold and Tigar for not playing correctly and gave them extra homework. All the girls that got extra homework were so mad they looked as red as tomatoes. Tigar was the angriest person on the entire planet.So, Tigar made a plan of stealing Raven’s guitar as she was mean most of the times. Raven had a magical guitar. This guitar was magical for it’s power of never going out of tune.That night Tigar sneaked into Raven’s house and grabbed the guitar and went back to her house. The next morning was a total disaster for Raven, she couldn’t find her magical guitar. So,Raven called Lima for help. Lima turned up in a minute and Raven to calm down. Raven did as she was told. Lima asked a lot of questions like the detectives do. Raven had time to answer one question before the other question. After all the questions Lima wanted Raven and herself to visit the girls. They visited Tella first. They asked her if she stole the magical guitar? But her answer was no. Because she had a sleepover with Gold and Gold’s answer was the same too. Then they visited Tigar and asked her the same question...but her answer was a bit weird… Her answer was hmm...hmm oh I...I...didn’t steal anything fr...fr...from any one. I was at...at...my mom’s house. Ya...ya that is it. Raven and Lima searched everyone's house and got their answer. Tigar had stolen the guitar. Tigar was very sorry for Raven. And said sorry like a gazillion times. Then Raven forgive Tigar. Tigar gave Raven’s guitar back to her. Then all the girls were happy and lived together. Raven and her friends lived happily ever after.
author: Vaishnavi guttikonda

title: Spotty's nighttime adventure
text: It's a quiet night, Everyone is tired and sleeping... Everyone but Spotty Spotty just can't sleep! So spotty decided to go on an adventure! "But who will play with me?" he thought, "Everybody is asleep..." The moon smiled at him and said, "Well, we will see about that..." So Spotty jumped and skipped his way to the deep dark forest. But the forest wasn't silent. It was filled with buzzes and new sounds. "I wonder who is chirping?" thought Spotty. Well it was Mr. Jiminy, the cricket. "Hello there!" chirped the cricket, But poor Spotty was too scared, he ran away. He almost ran all the way back home, Till he saw a light, floating near him. He stopped to see, it had a tiny face! "You shine just like the moon" he said "Thank you! I am Glow, the firefly" she said as she flew away with her friends... Spotty was too excited to go back now... As Spotty explored some more He was surprised with another voice. A face popped down from the tree It was Mr. Fang "Why are you upside down?" asked Spotty "Maybe I am straight and everybody else is upside down" laughed Mr. Fang It left Spotty wondering as he went round the tree... Behind the tree he saw two bright red eyes, he went closer and it was Mr. Hoot, the owl. "What are you doing up so late?" asked the wise owl. "I'm exploring the night" replied Spotty "You should go back, it is time for bed, come back tomorrow, and I promise you fun and adventure." said the owl. And so Spotty went home. When he reached back, he was very tired. "Are you alright?" asked his mother as he snuggled against her. "Mmm" he mumbled, he was already asleep. He was already dreaming of more adventures for the next morning...
author: Jaya Modi

title: Mythili and Mystery, the purple elephant
text: Once upon a time in a little forest of Jataka lived a purple elephant bird, Mystery. As humans converted forest area into industries, he and his family had to travel from one place to another for their daily existence. As they moved continuously, they reached a drought effected place. Being very tired from the journey, all of them decided to rest. However, Mystery decided to discover the place. When he returned, he was dumbstruck. The place where he had left his family, was now reduced to ashes and smoke. There had been a forest fire. He had lost his family. He was plunged into deepest regret and grief. If only, if only he had not left his family to wander away, he would not be alone now. He felt abandoned. He didn't know what to do. Mystery began to roam aimlessly. While he was sitting and crying silently in a forest, a red ball rolled up to him. Astonished by the object, Mystery immediately started to examine it. A little girl had come running behind the ball. She stood staring in fear, at the creature who had her ball. As Mystery moved towards her to return the ball, she ran for her life, untiringly. Thrilled that he had got a playmate, he began to run after her. When the girl neared a turn, she slipped on a puddle of water and went headlong into the stream. Mystery was surprised!He saw the girl struggling for life, immediately, he jumped in and saved her. Then he left, walking back alone. He was sad. The little girl had been afraid of him, while all he wanted was a friend. She would have even died if he had not pulled her out of the stream. The villagers had come running, hearing the girl scream. Seeing her lying wet on the riverside, they took her home and revived her. Coming back to senses, Mythili narrated what had happened. Secretly, she felt bad for having runaway, now that she knew it had saved her life. But the villagers were hunting it! What was she going to do? It, after all, seemed like a baby animal. No, she was not going to be a murderer. The animal must be warned and sent away. And that is exactly what she would do! The very next morning she left in search of the animal. How scared it must be! Poor little thing, she wondered. However, even after searching for the whole day, she couldn't find it and returned home late. She was tired and weak, yet her thoughts never left the animal who saved her life. Mythili, had her dinner, and went to sleep. She was off to dreamland soon because of the tiring day she had had. Suddenly at night, she was woken up by a strange noise. Immediately, the thoughts about the animal came back to her. Was the animal hurt? Was it in any trouble? Had the villagers caught it? She snatched the lamp beside her bed and headed out to find what had happened. She searched through out the village and went into the forest. She was alone and scared. What if some dangerous creature attacked her? What if she was killed? Was it really the strange animal which had made that sound or were they robbers? Her small heart pumped with fear and excitement. But her will power remained strong. She knew what she had to do, and she would do it, irrespective of whether she was scared or not. She owed it to that animal. She searched the whole night. Walking here and there, searching in the trees and in bushes. However hard she searched, the animal was not to be found. She became worried. The next day dawned and she went back home, tired yet anxious. In the morning when she returned home, she received the news that the animal was found on the outskirts of the village. All the brave men had set out to kill the animal. Mythili was terrified!" Oh my God! What will I do now!",she exclaimed. Her will was not to be undermined. She ran fast on her little feet. As soon as she inquired and made sure where she could find the animal, she stepped away from the main road. Speeding through fields and mountains, she finally reached the site before the villagers. To her horror the animal was hurt and crying. She decided she would defend it from being killed. When the villagers reached the site, they were astonished to see Mythili sitting along with it. Her father strode out of the group and went to bring back his daughter to her senses. But no she was too sure to be convinced. She begged her father to understand the plight of the animal. It was hurt. All it needed was some care. She would take care of it and send it away when it was alright. There was no need to kill it. It was of no harm and in fact it had saved her life. Mystery, was surprised. He was under the impression that he was either going to be killed or locked up. Never had he expected such a turn of events. Well, now he realised good begetted good! He hoped he would be allowed to stay and play with the little girl, whom he had grown to like. Her father thought about it for a while and spoke to the other villagers. He knew his little one, though she was often naughty, she had never been wrong! "I know my little girl. We have grown her to be a sensible and understanding person. I know she will not say anything unless she is sure about it and I am going to be by her side", he declared. Her father being one of the important people of the village, no one argued. Mythili ran home to tell her mom the good news! At first shocked but then convinced to be happy, her mom also agreed to taking care of the animal. She was so overjoyed!! With great hesitation, the villagers brought home the animal. Mystery was terrified. He didn't know what was going to happen to him. The girl was no where to be seen. Had they convinced her against defending him? Then, he was welcomed home, by the mother and the little girl. Mystery was taken to a grove near the stream and tied safely to a tree. That way,he couldn't harm anyone, the father assured. As days passed by, Mystery felt at home and got better quickly. Many of the other little children also had come to play with him and now he had so many friends. He had a family! The very humans who had destroyed his family, had became his own family now. He was nostalgic and yet happy. He missed his family but felt content to belong somewhere now. But as he got better, he got sadder. He would have to leave once he was alright, Mythili had told him! Again he would roam aimlessly and be alone. He didn't want that. Lucky for Mystery, during his stay in the village, the people were convinced he was of no harm and allowed him stay as long as he liked! Oh! How Mystery and Mythili celebrated! The villagers were also happy and so were their children. And so the little village on the river side was happy and content once again! And this time so was Mystery, he would never stray away again, he promised himself!
author: Sruthi Suresh
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: MONU AND HIS PINK CHEEKS
text: "Monu, what's on your cheek?" asked Cricky, the cricket. "Is it allergy?" She widened her eyes and ran away. Monu ran into the farm to ask his friends about the allergy. But all the animals were fast asleep. He was worried and ran into the woods to ask his other friends. He looked at the moon with a sad face. The moon beamed at him. Bunny, the bat got frightened on seeing Monu's cheeks and slipped from the Peepal branch and fell down. He flew away into the darkness. Everyday Jacky, the jackal used to chase Monu around the woods and play with him. But today he too slipped away into the dark woods on seeing Monu's cheeks. Barny, the owl was about to have his meal. He stared at Monu and the rat under his feet slipped away. "Go away!" he screamed. "Monu, don't come near me!" Jinny, the fire fly yelled and fluttered away. Monu felt like crying. Feeling sad, Monu came back to the farm to sleep beside his mother. But he couldn't sleep. He thought - "All his friends ran away from him. What if his mother and the other farm animals contacted the allergy from him?" He felt sad and decided to leave the farm. He slowly walked into the woods. He wished he had a mirror, so that he could see his face. He heard laughter from behind the Banyan tree. All his friends were laughing and having fun. They played a trick on him. It was a mole on his cheek. He was angry with them. But later he too joined in their laughter. He came back home and slept peacefully beside his mother.
author: Annapurna Sharma

title: THE WISHING DOG AND THE MAGICAL MOON
text: There lived a dog named Wiffy. It always have a wish to talk with the moon.One night, he is talking with him self that he has no friends.Then he looked up and said"Oh moon, please come now." Then someone said 'Hi my dear friend'.The dog looked around.Then he looked up and said'Are you talking to me.The moon said'Yes, with you only.He thought that he was seeing a dream.He had lost his hope. The moon said its not your dream. Its real.The moon knows magic.So he brought many animals to the village where the dog lives and said to the dog'You said that there are no animals in this village. friends in this village There are many animals in this village and all are your friends.The dog said 'really' and went around the village to see the other animals.He found many animals and seemed to be very happy.He talked to the animals. He maid funny jokes and spent all night happily.He was thankful to moon.
author: murali k

title: Rani learns to swim
text: 'Rani stared down at the water. No, she could not go in there. It was so cold and scary. "Well, go in", said the swimming master, pushing Rani roughly into the water. "NOOOOOO.....", Rani screamed as she fell towards the water, her fingers searching desperately for a hold in the smooth swimming pool wall. She found a tiny crack. Holding on tightly to it she hauled herself up. Amidst the merciless laughter of the other children she turned and ran towards the forest. ' Rani lived this moment over and over again. Two big tears dropped onto her nose. Three, four.......no, she couldn't count. They were coming in a flood now. "Why are you crying, little one?", asked a soft voice. Rani spun around, startled. In front of her was a big purple bird. "It must be my imagination", she thought aloud. "Well that is kind of right, I am called imagination, though not yours", said the purple bird. "Did you just speak?" "Yes, why?" "Wow" 'Why,wow?' "Because I haven't heard a bird talking before. " "Oh". The bird put a wing across her shoulder. "Tell me why you were crying". "Well, I am a klutz at swimming...",began Rani and the whole story poured out. "An imagination can help you here, I think", said the bird. "How?", asked Rani. "Come with me and I will tell you", said the bird. Rani trotted alongside the bird."Since I am the bird of imagination, I can make all I imagine come true. Look at what imagination can do." And then it was pure entertainment for Rani. It made strawberries appear though it was winter. It ate the strawberries coolly. Then the next second was dancing in the moonlight for the moon had suddenly risen. The next minute Rani felt like she was being dragged into the desert. A few moments later she was in an ice cold lake. Before she could say 'Brrr...', she was whisked into the air and came down again with a 'plop' on a cushion. The cushion burst and the feathers flew up into the air. "Wow, what a ride", exclaimed Rani beside herself with excitement. The purple bird smiled. "You have only seen the pleasurable half of imagination. Here is the useful part. watch!" The sky burst into light. Two men came into view. One was chipping away at a piece of wood. Another was drawing a model. "Do you recognize them?", asked the purple bird. A puzzled expression crossed Rani's face. "No..., wait, could it be....yes it is! They are the Wright brothers! I have seen them in my science book!" "Exactly", said the purple bird. "The Wright brothers had strong imaginations which enabled them to build the first flying machine. And, come now, it is time for us to go back to the river ". As the purple bird was taking her back, Rani said "The trouble is I dont have any imagination at all" The purple bird laughed. It was a deep throaty laugh. "Everyone has an imagination Rani", it said. "Not me", sighed Rani. "Oh well, I suppose I have to imagine I have an imagination!" "If you can imagine you have an imagination, you must have an imagination", said the purple bird. "This is all very confusing", said Rani. "I agree", said purple bird. "Well, if you are so convinced that you dont have an imagination, then I must give you some." They had reached the river by now. The bird dipped a pitcher in and tried to fill some water. But, unfortunately, it had very clumsy wings and it lost two pitchers before it managed to fill a pitcher at last. Then it said something that sounded like mantras and it gave the pitcher to Rani saying,"This will give you some imagination." Rani gulped the water down. When she finished she said," I feel full of imagination." The purple bird laughed. "Actually that was just plain water. But with a little help you managed to imagine that it was special." Rani smiled. Suddenly she saw visions of herself as a great swimmer winning thousands of races. She turned to the river, held her breath and turned back. The bird winked reassurance. She turned back to the river, held her breath and plunged in. In just 20 minutes, she was swimming back and forth across the river comfortably. But, when she turned to cast a proud look at the bird, it had disappeared.
author: Vakula  Surendar
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Baingani
text: This is the story of a little girl who lived in a village called Ghariya. The people of ghariya were peaceful and loving people. The animals and the village people lived happily together with each doing what they were best at doing. In this village, lived a little girl Ragini. She was a lovely and happy girl. There were two things that she loved the most - going to school and playing with her friends. She had many friends in the village. She would eagerly get up in the morning to go to school and rush back home to play with her friends. One day, there was a creature who arrived at the edge of the village. His name was Baingani. He was bright as a brinjal and looked at nothing else that you have seen! Bangani had travelled far and wide and had just flown in after a long journey. All he wanted to do was rest for a while before moving on to his destination. As he was resting under a tree, he heard a big splash! Who was that? It was Ragini who was playing by the river bank. She had just returned from school and was waiting for her friends to join her. Slowly Baingani inched forward to take a look at her. He had never spoken to a human before! Ragini was taken aback at first when she saw the bird, but she bravely spoke first. "Hello". " I am Ragini, who might you be? ". The bird was startled, he had never spoken to a person before. He didn't think that they were very friendly. "I am baingani, i come from far away land. I usually stay away from people". "Why"? Ragini asked. "Because they do not seem friendly". "Hmm.. maybe because they have not seen anything like you before". Ragini and the bird chatted for some time before she had to leave. Soon the sighting of a strange bird reached the ears of the villagers, who did not hesitate to drive it away. They came to the river bank with sticks and shrill cries, hoping to scare it. Baingani was in a dilema now. He wanted to leave, he knew that it was not a good idea to talk to humans. But he also wanted to see Ragini one last time. As soon as Ragini heard about the bird being driven away, she went to speak with the elders of the village. Each house that she went to, she was told the same thing. "We don't know what kind of a creature this is and who knows what it was do to us". She finally decided to meet with the eldest Daadi in the village. "Daadi, we are all different from each other too. But we are not scared of each other, why are then we scared of something that is different from us? Baingani has done nothing to deserve this". Daadi saw the truth in Ragini's words and she let the villagers know that they will not be hunting the bird. The villagers realized their mistake and let the bird be. The villagers finally understood that just because something was different from us, does not mean that it is bad or scary. Each living creature is different and we all have own strengths. Just because we are different from others doesn't mean we deserve any less. Soon Baingani found a loving shelter by the river in the village and guess who his best friend was? Ragini of course.
author: Vivaan M
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Dugdug and the Rasgulla
text: Late one night as the village of Bholapur slept and snored, the Moon opened his eyes with a POP and scanned the land below him. The cats and rats, dogs and hogs, cows and sows and all other animals on Munni's farm had slipped into the land of dreams. All, except for Dugdug. Dugdug was hungry. Sneaking out of the kennel, his eyes fell on the Moon and the rumble in his tummy got louder. 'Mmmm...' he drooled, 'a nice juicy Rasgulla is just what I want for dessert!’ But how would he reach the delicious dessert floating in the faraway sky? He ran into the forest to consult with his friends, who immediately convened a meeting to help stop the grumble in Dugdug’s belly. “Climb up the grand old Oak and pounce on the Rasgulla once you reach the top!” they chorused. And so Dugdug started to climb the oak. His paws slipped at first and his soft skin scraped against the bark of the Oak, but he did not give up. He had made up his mind to eat the Rasgulla, come what may. Unknown to him, the Moon was following his every move. 'Mmmm...' thought the Moon, smacking his lips. 'A plump pup for breakfast is just what I want! I shall gobble him up the moment he pounces on me!' He patiently waited for his breakfast as it slowly but surely climbed the tree. Right at that moment, Munni was out looking for Dugdug, shining her lantern into the dark, silent forest. 'Where has the little mischief-maker disappeared in the middle of the night? Kaka, Baba, Tauji, Bhaiyya... they're all going to scold me for forgetting to tie Dugdug to the kennel post!' she worried. Just then, she heard a light rustling of leaves above her and a 'Woof' that was unmistakably Dugdug's. "Dugdug! Come down right now!" Munni commanded, anxiety written all over her face. But Dugdug wanted nothing else than to sink his teeth into the Rasgulla. Balancing himself on the topmost branch, he pounced towards his dessert with all his might. The delighted Moon opened his mouth wide and waited for Dugdug to fall right in. Munni had only heard in stories that when the Moon was at his roundest, he got greedy and gobbled up anything and everything he fancied. Now, staring at the Moon's open mouth waiting for Dugdug, she realized that those weren’t merely stories... Worried about her favorite pup, she swung into action letting out a series of sharp whistles in what seemed to be a secret code. Almost immediately a giant bird with bright purple feathers and large blue eyes appeared out of nowhere. She was taller than the tallest Giraffe that ever was! Not long ago, Munni had saved the bird from being trapped by hunters and sold to the zoo in a faraway city. The bird had promised to repay the debt and they had become good friends, meeting in secret and frolicking in the forest every now and then. "We have to save Dugdug!"Munni whispered into the bird's ears, jumping on to her back and scaling her neck like an expert mountaineer. The bird soared into the night sky and intercepted Dugdug just as he was entering the Moon's mouth. With arms extended, Munni caught Dugdug by his tail, pulling him out of trouble in the nick of time. 'Hey, get out of the way of my dessert!' a perplexed Dugdug wanted to scream, but all he could do was let out a tired whimper. The superman stunt he tried to pull off had drained him of all his energy. Soon, poor Dugdug was back in the kennel, tied securely next to his Mom, his tongue still dangling out in the hope of tasting that wonderful Rasgulla. And the Moon? Well, all I know is that the next time I looked at him, I could spot a vague outline of a rabbit in his tummy.
author: Priya Narayanan
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: RONNIE THE HERO
text: RONNIE MY HERO This was the day when I met my new friend Ronnie..He was a small pup just some days old...I was really happy that day.After some days he started growing and he was as big as when I was 5 yrs old, we both understand each other. My aunt had given me this life. I take him walk everyday. Once when I went to play with friends I saw many plants with pink flowers. I decided to take home and give it to my parents, so I started to collect.I had many with me so it was not fitting in my palm so everything fell. I felt so bad that I started to cry. My mom was so worried about me that she said to ronnie to find me. He sniffed the roads and parks and he managed to find me. My mom scolded me a lot but I was happy that ronnie could find me. Sometimes I hide ronnie's things in mud but I am glad that he finds it easily. He is brown in color and his ears are dark brown. Dear readers you may think why did i keep his name ronnie instead of brownie, because my mom and I dont like the name much and it is a bit common too. I have much more to tell about ronnie, but i find this much is enough I could write a whole book about him but now my hands are hurting.. I hope you liked my story and had nice a fun!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! THE END
author: Ajara Alesar

title: Bhulu the party planner
text: Moon smiled and wished goodnight to all the firm animals.They were sleepy after a long tiring day and within seconds started snoring zzzzz. Doggi Bhulu hugged his baby sister Poli and wished her goodnight.Moon beamed over their cozy shade. Bhulu pretended to sleep until poly was fast asleep.But he was not a bit sleepy.How would he.he slept all day long.He was getting bored by every passing moment. He thought of going out and party.So he tiptoed and sneaked out of the shade and stared running. After few meters he saw red eyed owlie the owl,sitting on a tree top and eating her dinner. Hey owlie, I am so bored.can we two party?Owlie said not a bad idea at all. But two in a party is even more boring.why don't you ask some more friends to join us. So bhulu ran and ran to invite some more friends.after few kilometers he met Foxie the fox behind a bush. Bhulu said 'Foxie my friend' we are partying tonight at owlie's place.Why don't you head there till the time I invite some more friends. Bhulu started again.After roaming here and there he saw batty the bat doing her night time yoga by hanging upside down from a tree.He asked her as well to go straight to owlie's house and he headed to find some more folks. This time he met Kitkit the cricket sitting on a leaf,half asleep. Bhulu woke him up. Kitkit said 'hey bhulu, you startled me." Sorry for that kitkit.But we are going to have a blast at owlies place tonight.I came all the way to invite you.Please go there.I ll join you in sometime. After few more miles of walk Bhulu saw something blinking nearby.It was none other than his friend fiery the firefly. Hey fiery it's good that we met.Please Join us at the grand party we are having at owlies house.Fiery was more than happy.Bhulu thought now this is a nice crowd for a party and they both headed to the venue. Bhulu along with fiery reached at Owlie's place.All were already having a great time. But after running and walking so much Bhulu was damn tired.His legs were paining badly. With shaky legs and sleepy eyes he yawned big and simply dozed off.
author: Sudipa Das

title: Of Karuvadams and summer vacations
text: Raji, a brilliant young woman in her 20's dreamt of persuing her higher studies from the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru after her graduation. But like,most girls raised in the 60's, she was married off to a young man who worked in a small town in Tamil Nadu as an engineer. Unlike Bangalore which was a big city, living in the small town was a very different experience for Raji. The town was small and all she spotted were cashew forests at a distance. On some days, she longed to get back home to her city. Little did she know that this small town would soon be home for next 40 years of her life. She was soon mother to a charming boy and a pretty girl. Raji also went on to become a mother to twin daughters. With no sophisticated medical advancements in the late 70's, Raji knew that she was carrying twins only by the fifth month of her pregnancy. Her twin daughters were a delight and became a talk of the town! - after all no other family in the small town had twins. The twins played together,grew up together and even shared the same desk at school. In an era where summer camps were unheard of, Raji went on to curate the best summer activities for her twin daughters. From knitting and learning to make plastic bags and purses, to drawing colorful kolams aka rangolis, Raji patiently engaged her twins. However the best activity the twins engaged in was setting up a golu aka dolls during Dusshera, and making paper packets of sundal (a snack prepared using various dals) and distributing to neighbours! Summer vacations were the best because Raji, a master chef delighted her kids with Neer Moru (chilled butter milk), Paanagam (a sweet drink prepared using jaggery), fruit salads, and glasses of chilled Rasna from her kitchen! and not to forget a delightful mix of musk melon and sugar syrup that was allowed to set in the fridge, before the kids devoured them There was also nungu (palm fruit), a local summer fruit that the family indulged in.... and how could they forget Pazhapayam, a.k.a jack fruit that grew in abundance in their small town! Dining in restaurants was unheard of and neither could the family of six afford it in their small town. So there was Pazhakottai sambar, Pazhaapayam payasam.. all of which was churned out from the home kitchen. In the mid 80's, Raji was highly influenced by the TV serial Rajni, that took on corrupt government officials. Raji believed in being honest, and straight forward. Raji never minced words come what may - even if it meant earning enemies. Sometimes this landed her kids in trouble- after all who wants to be friends with kids whose mom always gave lectures and stern glances. With her diction in English and graduation in science from a prestigious college in Bengaluru, Raji could have easily landed a job in a bank or school in the small town but she chose to be a home maker. Raji put to use the summer heat in the best possible way by slogging it out in her kitchen and indulged in making Karuvadams (Rice Fryums). Making Karuvadams was a family activity. The entire family helped in laying out the vadams out to dry, the children taking charge of shooing away the crows that eagerly waited to get a taste of the vadams. Standing guard at the terrace with a black umbrella was a favorite activity for her kids because it meant getting a chance to peel of half cooked vadams and popping them into their mouths.. yummmmm! How yummy and mouth watering the vadams were! At night, Raji went on to fry the vadams and the entire family indulged in judging the vadams- too spicy! too salty came the feedback from across the dining table. From tomato vadams to garlic vadams from rice vadams to ural dal vadams - there were vadams of all varieties! Raji believed in beginning every month on a sweet note. Every month,she got home a Cadburys chocolate for the twins and their favourite Chandamaama from a local book store in the town centre...and that was not all, the twins got to read about farther towns and cities from a magazine called Target - something they looked forward to every month eagerly. From stories of school bullies to stories of teachers and homework, her children loved sharing their school stories with Raji. In an era where cake designers and birthday party organisers was unheard of, Raji went on to learn baking from a local women's group. The twins went on to enjoy double decker cakes and donned frilled frocks and skirts - all of which Raji created on her own. At 70, Raji now enjoys solving sudokus in the daily newspaper! She continues to take interest in watching cookery shows on Kannada and Andhra cable channels and she can whip up a spicy Gongura pickle or a Mangalorian Sambar in a jiffy. Wouldn't you ask me who Raji is? I call her AMMA!! Thank you amma! you are the world's best super hero!
author: Vani B
illustrator: Ad Sarin; Ajanta Guhathakurta; Angie & Upesh; Priya Kuriyan; Rijuta Ghate; Rupa Prakash; Santosh Pujari; Soumya Menon; Suvidha Mistry; Tanaya Vyas; Tanvi Bhat; Ujwala Waghmare

title: Nothing!
text: Let's do SOMETHING today. Let's do NOTHING today. How do you do 'NOTHING'? By lying on the green grass and looking at the blue sky. But that is doing something... How do you do 'NOTHING'? By closing your eyes, and breathing in and out. But that is doing something... How do you do 'NOTHING'? By feeling the softness of the leaves against your cheeks. But that is doing something... How do you do 'NOTHING'? By staring at the stars on a dark, dark night. But that is doing something... How do you do 'NOTHING'? Hmmmmm...... I know, let's draw a zero and then we would have done NOTHING!
author: Purvi Shah
illustrator: Aditi Dilip; Deepa Balsavar; Kabini  Amin; Muniza Shariq; Vartika  Sharma; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Chinnu
text: The moon smiled down upon the village of Chavvi, located beside the river, Jhelum. The whole village was asleep. Munni, Chinnu's dog slept peacefully in the shed, under the night sky. When the whole village slept, little Chinnu woke up. She had decided to run away from home. She took a lantern and slowly moved out of the house and ran away into the darkness. She felt that nobody loved her. She was tired of the scoldings she received from her father and mother. "Bad Chinnu. Won't obey when I ask her to get me a glass of water. What do you do the whole day other than fool around. Sad that I had a daughter and not a son", her father had shouted at her the other day and given her a tight slap. "Chinnu, help me around with the pots and pans. The only thing that you do whole day is play around. At least try to be a nice girl for god's sake", her mother had screamed as she was just about to run out to Tanu's house for playing. Munni heard the sound of his mistress footsteps and was alarmed to see her run away in the dark. She decided to follow her but soon lost scent of Chinnu. Munni asked the firefly, Kochu, "Kochu, did you see Chinnu run this way." Kochu, the firefly, replied, "No Munni, I didn't see her." Next Munni saw the grasshopper, Thambi, and asked him, "Thambi, did you see my mistress run this way." "No, Munni, I didn't see Chinnu. Why would she be out in the night", Thambi, the grasshopper, replied. Then she saw Mooga, the owl and asked him hopefully, "Did you see Chinnu run off this way?" "No Munni. I didn't Chinnu run this way", Mooga, the owl, replied. Meanwhile, Chinnu was running the whole night. And slowly the day dawned and morning light shone over the whole area. Tired with all the running, Chinnu tripped over a rock and fell into the river. The only one who saw it was Cheeta. Cheeta was a new kind of animal that nobody had seen in the area before. He had a huge body, a small tail like that of hen and a beak like that of parrot. His body was violet in color. Since he was a new animal and looked huge and harmful, the villagers had banished him from their village and forced him to live in the outskirts. Seeing Chinnu fall into the river, Cheeta jumped in and saved her. Once out of the water, Chinnu started crying. She was sad that nobody loved her, scared that Cheeta was standing next to her and angry that she was saved by Cheeta from drowning and dying. Cheeta listened to all of Chinnu's compliants patiently and then told his own story to her. He told her how his parents had abandoned him, how his own tribe had disowned him because he was ugly and different and how bad he felt when in this village too he was banished. Chinnu felt sorry for him and soon both of them became friends. Cheeta asked Chinnu to go back to her parent's house and live there as a good girl. He carried her on his back and dropped her back at her house. Soon, the story about how Cheeta saved Chinnu from the currents of the river spread in the village. Everyone who heard it was surprised to know that Cheeta didn't harm humans, but instead helped them. Chinnu came back home and lived obediently and happily with her parents. She never again thought of running away from her home. Cheeta was welcomed back to the village. Chinnu, Munni, Cheeta and the other children of the village, all, became good friends. Years later too, the story of Chinnu and Cheeta was recited in the village. The village leader told the story of how an ugly animal that was mistreated and banished from the village had saved a hapless girl who once thought nobody cared about her. The girl was proved wrong, the creature saved her and they became good friends forever.
author: Gitanjali Maria
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Artist
text: Mom... Her hugs always smoothed your worries away.. She woke up before you did, and ensured your tiffin box had colorful food for school...and when you fell sick, she prayed to all known gods on the planet! She indulged you in your hobbies patiently. She lend you an ear for all your stories - some real, some fabricated. She knew how to pacify you when you threw a tantrum.....and when she fell sick - all hell broke loose, because none knew how to run a home smoothly like she did! Sometimes she screamed and yelled and behaved like a woman possessed...May be we drove her crazy with our silly tantrums.. She sacrificed her dreams, so you could have a happy childhood.. She wished and prayed that all our dreams came true. Around the world, people use different names to call her - Amma, Maa, Mom, Aayi, Ammee, Mummy, Maataji... I would say she is a juggler and an ARTIST!...... because artists create masterpieces... mothers craft a home.. with their love, dedication and sacrifice...
author: Vani B
illustrator: Greystroke; Henu; Kabini  Amin; Madhuri Purandare; Niloufer Wadia; Priya Kuriyan; Rijuta Ghate; Ruchi Shah; Rupa Prakash; Soumya Menon; Suvidha Mistry; Swati Priyanka; Tanaya Vyas

title: Help !!!! The Sky is Falling !
text: It was a hot summer night. Not a leaf stirred. Minky, the new born puppy had just drifted off to sleep. But he woke up startled.. It first started as a prick, then a drip, then another drip... Drip Drip Drip.. Trip Trip Trip.... First it was one drop.. then another... then another... now the drip drip, trip trip was fatter and it was falling faster. Minky sprung out of bed. "What could the drip drip trip trip be?", he wondered... And as he ran, it fell on to his eyes, his nose and on to his fleece and made him wet. "Oh my God! I think the sky is falling ", muttered Minky. He first ran to his friend, the bat. "Didn't you notice, the sky is falling ", he muttered in one breath, and ran even before the bat could respond. He then ran to the grasshopper and muttered in one breath, "The sky is falling", "Run! save yourselves"! The trip trip, drip drip only got louder. There was a flash of light in the sky, followed by a loud KaboooooooooOOOOOooom!!!. Minky shivered hearing the drip drip..trip trip and the loud KaboooooooooOOOOOooom.. He then ran to the wise old grand ma owl and exclaimed " Grandma Owl, the sky is falling ", don't you hear the trip trip drip drip...and the loud KaboooooooooOOOOOooom?? The wise Grand ma owl let out a laugh and said " The trip trip drip drip is Rain and the loud KaboooooooooOOOOOooom is Thunder!" "and the sky isn't falling. So don't panic". Minky let out a huge sigh of relief. All the animals let out a loud laugh! Thankfully the sky wasn't falling down on them! They enjoyed soaking in the rain.
author: Vani B

title: The Rhythm of Friendship
text: On one fine Sunday morning Dhara asked her mother: "Ma!Ma! What a beautiful morning it is! With the Sun glowing and birds chirping in it. A morning so fine, I feel so divine. Allow me Ma to go outside I want to see my friends in sky." So she jumped outside the hut she loved To see the birds chirping much: "Chieee! Chieee!" they say, And so glee glee she get. And on her way to the pond, She heard a very beautiful song. Dholak Ji was singing it, While on his way to the town. She paused and said, "Dholak Ji,Bring me a set of bangle please" "The best one I can find,I will", tuned he with me. Then she went to Rani 's house hoping to see her in the grounds But she met her mother instead who told her she went to the pond indeed. Hoping to find Peru around, The little puppy she was very fond She went to the F armer in the fields To ask him if he had seen him Then he got very angry and said, "I have lots to do madame! Don't bother me I'm a Farmer man I have in the fields men so few And with this I bid you adieu." Knowing his temper really well, Dhara never minded his yell. And off she went with a run, In the shining morning Sun. Reaching to the pond she saw fishes and weeds and the boat, huts and trees and the goat. But to her utter surprise, Rani was nowhere to find. "Rani! Rani!", she yelled Looked here and there, again and again. "Now Now,Where would she actually be? I wonder if she's in the trees?" There was rustling in the trees, And when she turned around to see Hoping to find Rani there Instead a giant shadow appeared. "Oh my!my!" What is she seeing she wondered Is it an elephant or a bird!! Or is it a monster that thundered!! And at that instant, When she backed off She slipped her feet And rolled down "Splash" was the sound Oh! She fell into the pond. Dhara swimmed to the bank And came out all dripping wet And for the giant bird in front, “Who are you?!!”, were her words!! Seeing the courage of this girl, “I am the Elephant bird”, it tells. Our brave Dhara talked it out, He was the only one left she found. I always come out at night, No one can see me in moonlight. My name is Big But I am very shy. You are little But really brave. Let's be friends from now on, and meet at every night on. Don't let anyone know, Except you and Peru and S now." "HOOOOT!!!",replied Snow, the owl. Who was dreaming of the clouds. I don't know if I am pretty, And will the villagers love me. So I live in this forest by the pond, and come out only when no one's 'round. So every Sunday night, with Peru by her side, Dhara goes to the pond To meet her lovely friend around. “I have this ball! Well it’s not my fault, It fell from over that hill top” “Let’s play fetch,You throw I’ll catch!!” Many Sundays passed by, Big was now not shy Laughing and prancing in the jungle, Everyone dancing in the rain, Big was happy evermore, What could a lonely bird get more? It was one night, Dhara find and find, But it seemed like Big had vanished from sight, She was concerned extremely Where would such a big bird be!! Then came Peru to her rescue He told her "Not to worry" and, "I'll find Big for you Dhara as you're my dearest friend". He ran to snow asked where did Big go? "He was sad and looked so mad And headed to the fields", snow said. But on his way to the fields, He saw Bat hanging with his feet "If you are looking for Big, He is in a FIGHT indeed!!" Then Peru saw the light shine, It was Firefly in the night "Big always protects the cattle, But today it seems there'll be a battle!!" Peru asked the Fox sly If he had seen the shaken sky "A fearful battle was fought, and the wolves were nearly caught!!" When he finally reached the fields, All was done and finished. The Cricket told him, "What a fight!!" "It was such a tremendous sight!!" "Big was bold and so strong, the wolves could not last long!!" All the villagers were in rage, Let's hunt him down they say!! "He must have destroyed the farmer's fields 'Coz he is the only one so fit." "NO!!", screamed Dhara "It's not his fault, Please don't be harsh!!" "His name is Big, He's just a baby bird." "And you might get surprised, 'Coz he is the only one left alive!!" "He destroyed the poor farmer's field, What if he would have his animals killed?!" "He is a beast!! Why you take his side? Let's take him to the elderly wise." All were discussing the matter, Everyone criticizing in manner, And then came the farmer from his fields,"Don't take the decision hurriedly!" "Dhara is a good girl and, her friendship is stronger than any of us" "Before coming to any conclusion, ask Dholak Ji for all the clarification. " "I am the merchant of this place I need to visit the town each day. Last night when I was coming back, saw hungry wolves in the black!!" "They wish to attack all the cattle But with the giant bird they had to battle!! As the bird was cattle's friend, and so they rely on its mightiness. "Thus the battle started out, All the field was upside down But when it came to an end All the cattle were safe, Amen!!" "Like all of you, I was first astonished too. But what I came to know is that, This was going on from the start, and, Big was always in our part, Yes!!" "This is not what I had always known but, Thanks to little Peru our own!! He searched for truth all night long with all his strange jungle friends he came to know the actual fact." "Those wolves used to come every night, But this time it was more than fright, My field was destroyed in their fight Now everyone knows the truth that lie." The villagers one-by-one, Start clapping and they sung: "Praise to Big, the Elephant Bird Shy was he but not so dumb, His friendship with Dhara is there that led his mightiness our cattle spared!!" "Thanks to Peru for the truth You're little but so cute, You helped resolved the problem by Letting us know how it caused. Boy!!" "Good is Dhara and so brave She is small but strong in state, You stood with the truth when needed You believed in Big when he was discredited!! " Now everyone was happy again, The Sun was shining bright again The villagers are now not afraid To see Big playing with his friends They feel so proud with such a creature Who is the best in all its features!! This is what a friendship is You help the one who is in need. One can be big, One can be small One can be rich, One can be not But if you have your friends around, No one can make you touch the ground!! Thanks to Peru,Big and Dhara once again there is peace in ' Vasundhara '
author: Purva  Moon
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: What happens at night?
text: The moon as usual was shining bright. The dog and the goat were sleeping tight. The moon smiled as the dog's and the goat's snores reached him. He was happy because it was night. Because, this is what happens at night. The cow, the calf and the little cat. The smiling pig and the grumpy one at that. The rooster, the rats, the goat and the dog and even the tiny spider have closed their eyes. The moon smiled as the animals rested. He was happy because it was night!
author: Sushma Bijoor

title: A story about Tiku and Pari
text: Tiku, a large purple bird was sad and grumpy. People wanted to run him out of the village. They thought that Tiku had no wings and was ugly. Infact they thought he was giant, scary and might scare the kids in the village. Tiku started to believe that he was ugly because he was giant and had no wings. He felt asleep under his favorite tree. Next morning, he heard a cry of a child. He rushed to check on her. By the tree, he saw a little girl. As he got near her, she started to get angry. Don't get scared of me, I am here to help you. "What is your name?" asked Tiku. "Pari," replied the girl. "That's a pretty name, I heard you cry so I came to check if everything was okay. Why were you crying?" said Tiku. "Because today my father scolded me very badly," replied Pari. "But why, did you make any mistake?" asked Tiku. "Yes, I sneaked out of house without telling my mom," said Pari. "But why?" asked Tiku. "I wanted to play with my friend Lila, if I would have asked my mother she would not have allowed me to go out," explained Pari. "That was not right! What happened after that?" asked Tiku. " " On the way, I met my aunt Reema, she had lost her kitten. I offered to help her." "I looked all around the forest for a very long time, but could not find the kitten." "I informed my aunt that I could not find her kitten and then left back for home." "It was very late, my parents were very worried, when they found me missing." "My parents were unhappy that I went out without informing them. And hence my father scolded me very badly the next day. " "So, I was crying because he did not listen to me. And shouted. This is the first time he had got so angry with me." "Don't be sad, you're father was worried about you, he loves you for sure," said Tiku. "I will show you what I can do with my tail," said Tiku. He wiggled his tail, up and down, up and down, side to side, Pari smiled and then laughed. "I like what you do with your tail!" "I can show you something more," said Tiku. Tiku jumped inside the river. He would held out his head and then go back again inside the water. He would go in and out, in and out. He did it many times. Pari enjoyed his acts. "You must be hungry!" said Tiku. "Yes, but I cannot reach up there." "No worries," said Tiku. He jumped out, plucked fruits from the tree and shared with Pari. "Being giant, has so many advantages," said Pari. "Not everyone thinks so! Some people think I am giant, have no wings hence I am ugly. Anyways lets go home," said Tiku. On the way back home, they met the villagers, who wanted Tiku to be out of the village. "You again came back Tiku, didn't we tell you to leave this village never to come back again" said villagers. "You giant, ugly, scary, wingless bird cannot stay here. "Nooooooo..." cried Pari. "I don't think so! It doesn't matter how we look, what matters is what we do. Today, he made laugh. He played and showed his love and care for me. I will not let him go anywhere." All the villagers shouted, screamed, forced Pari to push Tiku away. But Pari, would not listen. She found Tiku most helpful, loving and caring. Atlast, villagers gave up and agreed with Pari and allowed Tiku to stay back. From a distance, Pari's father saw how she fought for the right and compelled villagers to give justice to Tiku. He came near Pari and picked her in his arms. Pari was excited to see his father. And was happy to find out that he was no longer angry with her. While, Tiku stayed back in the village. Never again anyone thought that he was ugly.
author: Namrata Agarwal
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Kuttu and His Night Friends
text: Kuttu was a happy-go-lucky pup. He lived on a farm that was close to a forest. Kuttu spent his day playing and jumping around in the farm. He tickled the piglet with his tail. Splash! Kuttu leaped in the pond to float with the ducklings. He chased the rabbits till they rushed into their holes. But when night fell, Kuttu felt scared. Tonight, the farm was filled with darkness except for a lantern that flickered in a close distance. The birds chirped no more. The piglets retired to their cosy little bed made of hay. The chicks cuddled in their mother’s wings and slept in peace. But Kuttu could not close his eyes. His mother slept close to him. But Kuttu lay wide awake. The darkness and the quietness of the night scared him. Kuttu looked at the lantern that hung in a shed. 'There's light in that shed', he thought to himself, 'Perhaps that place will make me feel better.' Kuttu walked towards the shed. Kuttu had barely taken a few steps towards the lantern when he noticed a pair of shining eyes on the tree. 'Who are you?' asked Kuttu. 'I am Oola, the Owl.' 'Isn't it so dark here?' asked Kuttu. 'I don't think so. I love the night. It is in the darkness of the night that I can keep my eyes wide-open and hunt for food for myself,' hooted Oola. 'But I am too scared of the darkness,' Kuttu whined. 'Oh! Why? The darkness is so delightful. It is in the darkness that the moon shines like a big white ball and the stars twinkle in the night sky.' ‘ WHOOOOO —’ Oola hooted looking at the dazzling sky. Kuttu sighed and walked away. As he moved closer to the lantern, a black creature flew past Kuttu, flapping its giant wings. 'Who are you?' asked Kuttu. 'I am Baawra, the Bat.' 'Isn't it so dark here?' asked Kuttu. 'I don't think so. I love the night. It is in the darkness of the night that I can zip back and forth across the lake.' 'But I am too scared of the darkness,' whined Kuttu. 'Oh! Why?
