The darkness is so delightful. It is in the darkness that you can reach the stars!' SWOOOOP! Baawra zipped off to a tree and hung upside down. Kuttu sighed and walked away. Suddenly he felt the bushes moving. Kuttu was about to scream and run back when he noticed a fox emerging from the bushes. 'Who are you?' asked Kuttu. 'I am Fankar, the Fox.' 'Isn't it so quiet here?' asked Kuttu. 'I don't think so. I love the night. It is in the quietness of the night that I can howl at the moon!' said Fankar, smiling and looking up at the moon. 'But I am too scared of the quietness of the night,' Kuttu whined. 'Oh! Why? The quietness is so delightful. It is in the quietness of the night that you can make a silent wish upon a star. And you know what, these wishes come true!’ ' AH-WHOOOOOO, ' Fankar howled. Kuttu sighed and walked away. Chirr-Chirr-Chirr— 'What is that sound?’ Kuttu looked here and there. 'Who are you?' asked Kuttu. 'I am Kirr-Kirr, the Cricket.' A tiny insect hopped around Kuttu. ‘Isn’t it so quiet here?’ asked Kuttu. 'I don't think so? It is in the quietness of the night that I can sing songs with my friends.' Chirr-chirr-chirr —Kirr-Kirr went on. ‘But I am too scared of the quietness of the night,’ whined Kuttu. ‘Oh! Why? The quietness of the night is so delightful. It is in the quietness of the night that you can hear the sound of the soft breeze blowing! HUSHHHHHHHH —the wind whispered. Kuttu sighed and walked away. Kuttu thought about what Oola, Baawra, Fankar and Kirr-Kirr said about the night. By now, he had completely forgotten about the lantern and had walked out of the farm, into the forest. Still deep in his thoughts, Kuttu walked on and on till he saw something magical! A tall tree stood in the middle of the forest. It was no ordinary tree. It was lit up, with dancing dots all around it. ‘Oooooh! What’s that?’ Kuttu stopped and looked at the tree in wonder! One of the tiny dots moved closer to Kuttu. It went past his eyes, behind his ears, below his stomach and landed on his nose. He watched the shimmering light with eyes wide-open. ‘Who are you?’ asked Kuttu, still in awe. ‘I am Fifi, the Firefly. I weave dreams in the night on that tree.’ Kuttu looked at the tree and noticed thousands of fireflies dancing around the tree. ‘And how do you do that?’asked Kuttu. ‘I weave dreams with a song,’ said Fifi. ‘A song! Can you sing it for me too, please?’ Kuttu woofed in excitement. ‘Sure!’ said Fifi and started to sing— ‘When the sun sets and the moon shines, When the darkness falls on every kind, I spread my golden wings and dance Weaving dreams of a happy kind. I skip and hop around little ones like you, Slipping a dream or two in… No! No! Not in your shoe! I slip a dream or two in your eyes, So that you have a happy night, And welcome the day with a smile so bright!’ Kuttu danced to the song. By now, Kuttu was tired and wanted to sleep. But where was he? He was in the woods! But this time Kuttu was not scared. His night friends—Oola, Baawra, Fankar and Fifi helped him find his way back to the farm. Kuttu snuggled close to his mother. As he lay in his bed, he looked up at the big white ball. He heard the wind whispering in his ears. He remembered the song that Fifi sang to him. Kuttu shut his eyes, tightly. This time he was not scared of the darkness and the quietness of the night. And when Kuttu was fast asleep, guess who came by? Fifi skipped and hopped around Kuttu and slipped a beautiful dream in his eyes. Kuttu smiled in his sleep. It must have been a happy dream!
author: Roohi  Saluja Sehgal
illustrator: Samidha Gunjal; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Stop Child Labour!!!
text: "Please listen to me! This won't do! There can't be usage of child labour around here! What is the point of using us for doing all kinds of odd jobs? Do you know?", Muniya asked the village council. "Fine! Your request is accepted. There shall be no child labour in the village anymore!",said the Headman to me. But the villagers didn't agree, " The house is poor. There is not a single penny in the house. Child labour has to continue!" Muniya pleaded, "Everyone of you just don't understand. In this village there are 200 unemployed adults and their salary is 500 rupees per day, there are 150 kids in this village and their salary is 80 rupees per day. So what do you think dear reader. In which way will the village make more money? Child labour is due to poverty is a wrong assumption". They discussed and discussed and discussed. In the end everyone agreed that people employ child labour because their salaries are low. Instead if an adult is employed the income of families will go up. It was decided to stop child labour in village. And if someone uses child labour, nobody will use their services and will report it to government authorities like police, sarpanch and labour commissioner. The headman brought some news for the kids. "From now on, no kid should be seen doing labour. All of the kids should be sent to Chord Bridge school which educates and rehabilitates child labourers." Now every child in the village goes to school. Every child dreams of their future and what they want to become. All the kids were very happy that they will go to school. The purple giant bird also wants to go to school. Muniya is angry that bird has made her wet on the way to school. Muniya explained the giant purple bird that birds don't go to school. The giant purple bird played in the village while kids went to school. They went door to door for awareness campaign against child labour. They explained everyone that poverty is not cause of child labour and every child deserves pen and book in their hand. Headman himself made rounds around the village to check, if there are any child labour employed. Everyone in village made sure there is no child labour in village. You don't know what we became when we grew up! A choreographer, A famous doctor and what else! Everyone in village is so proud of us. Do you want a book in child's hand or a shovel or a hammer or utensils?
author: Pahi Shrivastava

title: A Helping Hand
text: Romu lay awake in his shed outside the barn besides his sleeping pup..Kola. He gazed worriedly at his growing offspring. The child was becoming stronger and naughtier day by day and without a mother he was getting out of hand. Finally he dozed off when he was woken up by the snort of the resident pigs. He found his Kola had disappeared. The pig helpfully informed him that Kola had woken up and decided to follow the cute firefly to her abode. Romu was livid with fear and anger at the audacity of the pup. He rushed out in the moonlit night looking frantically. He soon came upon the GrassHopper. He narrated his tale of woes and asked the GrassHopper how to control an errant child. The GrassHopper just smiled and sang "How do I know, you reap what you sow! Your answers lie in the lake. By the way, the firefly lives on the Blue Mountain. Now move on" Romu felt a stab of apprehension. He had heard about the Blue Mountain and how inhospitable its terrain was. But how could he go alone there. Soon he met the Fox. Just being around the sly fellow made his skin crawl. But he had no choice. Maybe he would accompany him with his sharp teeth and wicked mind? In a shaky voice he asked him if he had seen his little pup. The fox replied "I don't have the time, I am out for a hunt. Your answers lie in the lake." Romu was dejected and lonely. However, he had to think of his baby Kola first. He gathered his wits and tread along towards the lake. Thats where all the answers are! Next he found the Bat relaxing upside down on a tree. Hmm...maybe he will help...he seems kind... Romu asked in a beseeching voice.."Will you help me find my little Pup Kola...he has gone after the firefly." The Bat did not like anyone disturbing his comfortable upside down perch on the branch. He muttered crossly "Don't disturb me, your answer lies in the lake." Next he came upon the King of Night, the Owl. Knowing how wise he is, it would be good to take him along. "Oh Night King, I humbly request your presence alongwith me to be my guide and help to the Blue Mountain. How to get there and search for my son?" The wise Owl opened his big tired eyes and looked at Romu for a second and then he shut them again. Then he muttered "Um..Um..Look in the lake...lake!" Romu was perplexed but he trudged along. How do I do it all alone? He wondered. Soon he reached the Lake. So here I will find someone to help me look for my Kola. He looked around and saw no one.Then he peered in the Lake. He thought he saw someone. He looked again and yes there was a mean Dog in the Lake."Help Me!" He waited for answers. The Dog in the Lake shouted back "Help Me!" " How can I help you, You are so strong!". The Dog in the Lake repeated.. " How can I help you, You are so strong!!" Romu soon realized it was his Reflection he was talking. Was he strong like the Reflection said? He had never felt that way. He was always the barn dog barking at the straying goat. But now he realized maybe he had some skills. The Barn animals did get in line whenever he came barking. Well even the cows! He didn't need others to help him find his son. He knew he had to go to the Blue Mountain. Quickly he ran about collecting vines from the trees around the lake and made it in a strong sturdy rope. Using that he climbed the nearby Blue Mountain. Little Kola was there playing with the Firefly family. When he saw his Father, Kola rushed to him and hugged him tight. " Dad I missed you but how did you find me?" "Well I had a helping hand." said Romu "Remember, if you ever need a Helping Hand, its at the end of your Arm!"
author: Alka Agarwal

title: A cute puppy
text: Ranjan Goswami Sumi was fond of puppies.She wanted to keep a pet puppy.She wanted to play with it. She said to her mama,"Mom, I want a puppy.Please bring a puppy for me.I want to play with a puppy." Mama said,"Ask your dad." When Sumi's dad came from office Sumi said to him,"Dad, I want a puppy.Will you please bring a puppy for me?" Dad replied,"I will bring a puppy for you but you will have to take its proper care and you will not neglect your study." Sumi said happily."Yes, dad,I will take its care and study well." That night Sumi saw a cute puppy in her dream. The next day dad bought a cute puppy from a pet shop and gave it to Sumi. Sumi was very happy.Soon Sumi and the puppy became friends and started playing together.
author: Ravi Ranjan  Goswami
illustrator: Madhuri Purandare; Santosh Pujari; Sonal Goyal; Soumya Menon; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Didi's Bag of Colorful Treasures
text: There was a big ground near their home. This ground was quite unusual. There were no trees and no plants, only piles of garbage. The waste and filth of the entire city was dumped into the ground. These children didn't go to school. They used to spend their days in the ground. They would search for plastic bottles, and fish out patches of cloth... They knew a lot about garbage. One day, didi visited the garbage ground. She was wearing a red chunni (scarf). As she wandered around, she kept looking at the kids and then finally, sat down in one place. She took something out of her bag and looked at it. At first, the kids stared at her from afar. Then, they inched closer to look at her. Didi had a lot of books. Thick, thin and colorful books full of stories! The children kept coming closer to her now. Didi started visiting them every day. The kids too became close to her. They loved to hear stories from their didi. In a few days, they learnt how to read alphabets and words. Slowly, they even started telling stories. "Let's make Didi's place beautiful!" The little kids found a chair and a table from the garbage. One kid brought a mat, and the other a curtain. Some item from here, other pieces from there were found, whatever they could find in this garbage ground. One day, didi did not come. She didn't turn up the next day too. The anxious children kept waiting. As they chatted with each other, they began to read those books. As they read those books, they began to teach others how to read. One day, they found didi 's address in a book. They immediately set out to look for her. They didn't forget to take their bag of books along with them! As they were searching for didi, they read a bus number. As they walked, they were able to understand the name of a street. Didi had already taught them these things. " Where does didi live? Here or there?" After searching and searching for their didi, the little children grew upset. The tired kids were about to return home when one of them saw a red chunni (scarf). Didi was lying in a bed. She looked sick and sad. Her face was without a smile or glow. The doctor had given her med ﻿ icines. But didi was still not feeling better. The kids ran towards her and hugged her tight. They showed her the bag of books. The kids read some stories to their didi. She began to smile again. Even her eyes were shining now! Didi visits them regularly now. All the kids gather around her. They meet every evening. They laugh so much and study too! See how much fun they have together! The children, their didi and their books!
author: Sherein Bansal

title: A Monkey called Manki
text: One of them was 'Manki'. He was named by Pappu. Pappu was the son of the master of that house and studied in a nearby primary school. Whenever he bumped into this monkey, Pappu would call him 'Manki'. The elders of Pappu's home were enemies of the monkeys. Whenever they saw monkeys up on the roof, or in the vicinity of the house, they would throw stones or threaten them with a stick to make the monkeys flee. But the elders were not the only ones at fault here. The monkeys were used to taking away any object kept out in the open, like utensils, clothes, etc. Then the people had to chase the monkeys to get their things back! To get back their things, people used pieces of roti (bread), gram seeds, or any kind of food. People threw these things at the monkeys so that they could drop their things and leap at the food instead. Then everyone would take back their things. This happened often. These monkeys could find food anywhere- nearby parks, gardens, farms, etc. but this particular hide and seek game with the people added to their fun! They enjoyed scaring, teasing and even playing with the kids. Even though the kids were supposed to stay away from the monkeys, some of them would chase the monkeys and throw stones at them for no reason. In spite of all this, those days were fun. Televisions had not reached that village yet. One day, word spread that there's a new TV in the village. The next day, the village head received a TV at home. A TV antenna was installed on the roof of his house. For the monkeys, this object was new and exciting. As soon as the roof emptied, Manki and other young and old monkeys from his troop reached there. Everyone was curious and excited to see the antenna. The kids were scolded into staying away from it. Manki's uncle, the smartest monkey of the troop, came forward. At first, he touched it with his paw and then bit with his teeth. When nothing happened, he grew more confident, and true to his nature, the Manki's uncle shook the antenna and then swung from it. Suddenly, the village head's son climbed up on the roof with a stick and rushed into the troop of monkeys to attack them with it. The monkeys fled. Some leaped onto the neighbor's roof and some climbed up a nearby tree. The boy corrected the bent antenna and went away. In just a few more days, every house in the village got a TV. Antennas were installed on the roofs and tiles. But there was a change in the atmosphere of the village. Manki and his friends could feel that something strange was happening. As soon as dusk fell, the lively streets and markets were deserted. People began to hole up inside their homes. The kids were no longer playing or creating a chaos out in the streets. They were not chasing the monkeys either. Even Manki's friend, Pappu, no longer came to meet him on the roof with roti. Manki was feeling restless. He went to sit alone on Pappu's roof. He was completely bored. Then he remembered something! When Manki's uncle had shaken the TV antenna, the village head's son had rushed to the roof. Manki had an idea. He called all his friends and made a plan with them. The next evening, Manki and many of his friends climbed up the roofs of the houses of that street where antennas were installed. All the people were busy watching TV inside their homes. Manki was on Pappu's roof. He let out a scream. He climbed up the antenna and shook it wildly. This was a signal for all the monkeys. Every one climbed the antennas and began to swing from them. After some time, they ran to climb onto the nearby trees. From there, they saw the drama on the street unfold. They saw that some people came out of their homes. Some went up on the roof to correct their antennas. Some came out to talk to others. Some kids started playing in the street. A few of them saw the monkeys in the trees and started shouting at them, "Monkey! Monkey!" Even if for a short time, there was excitement and liveliness back on the streets. Manki and his friends enjoyed this changed atmosphere a lot. Now whenever they felt bored, they would shake the antennas and flee. They had found a new way to tease the humans.
author: Sherein Bansal
illustrator: Aishwarya Jaitly; Delwyn Remedios; Priya Kuriyan; Ruchi Shah; Rupa Prakash; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya; Vibhash Pandey; Vishnu  M Nair

title: Bunty's Vacation with Grandma
text: He is very friendly. The bell goes off, the school is over! Bunty and his friends rush home together. One day, when he came home, he said to his parents, "I'll go visit grandma in my summer vacations!" He helps her in all her chores, whenever Bunty to his grandma goes. He picks out vegetables from the garden's natural stock. And even takes Sheru along for a walk. One day, he was shocked when he found, the garden's plants broken and strewn around. He rushed to grandma and described her the garden. She had a plan! She knew what needed to be done. Grandma said, "Go there early tomorrow. Keep alert. Hide carefully! I'll come as soon as you see the culprit, and scream for me!" Next day, Bunty peeped out to see who he heard, He saw the loyal garden troublemaker standing alert! He approached Sheru, and saw potatoes growing out of the mud. Happy to see the potatoes, Bunty thought, "I'll give these to grandma right away." He went home with the garden troublemaker, basket of potatoes and a great tale!
author: Sherein Bansal

title: The Guests of Orissa
text: It is a small village in Orissa, at the Bay of Bengal. It is home to turtles. Each year, thousands of turtles come at the coast and lay eggs on the sand. Then they go back into the water. After some days, baby turtles break out of the eggs and start running towards the water. But it is summer now. There are no turtles. Sutapa goes to the sea coast daily with her grandpa and sees the fishing boats bobbing along the waves for a long time. She enjoys talking with her grandpa while walking on wet sand. Sutapa was asking her grandpa endless questions about turtles. "Have you ever seen turtles? What do they eat? Have you ever touched them?" Grandpa was just answering 'yes' or 'no'. Sutapa was not satisfied at all. She was coaxing again and again. "When did you last see the turtles? How old were you then?" She was unstoppable. Sutapa was curious about turtles. Her grandpa said to her, "When I was of your age, I used to come with my friends at the sea coast to steal turtle eggs. We used to eat some and sell a few." Sutapa disliked the idea and said,"Yuck! Who can eat turtle eggs?" Grandpa just smiled and said, "We see turtles as an incarnation of Lord Jagannath and so, don't eat its flesh. I remember that once many turtles were thrown onto the sea coast after a storm. Nobody took notice of them. Even God's incarnation could not move us. Sometimes baby turtles buried under the sand become morsels for dogs and crows. The villagers acted as silent witnesses and failed to protect them." Sutapa realized that her grandpa was full of regret. Sutapa was keen to know more about turtles. She said, "Oh! So have all the turtles of this village died by now?" "No, no." Grandpa continued, "One day, one scholar gentleman came to our village. He was doing some research work on turtles. He made us aware about turtles in our region. He made us understand that these turtles are special species. And we should protect them. Research scholars lived with us and taught us various ways of their survival. We all co-operated with them. Now Orissa is known for these turtles, even throughout the world. They are named as Olive Ridley." "Wow! I will also meet Olive Ridley!", said Sutapa excitedly. Grandpa smiled as usual. Sutapa's grandpa disclosed many more facts about turtles. Do you know all these? * Olive Ridley is one of the seven species of turtles. It is on the verge of extinction. * Orissa is the home of Olive Ridley. This is their favorite place. They are also found in Mexico and Costa Rica. Besides it, Olive Ridley are also seen at Velas village in Ratangiri district of Maharashtra. * The turtles cover thousands miles to reach the sea coast to lay eggs. * The female turtles returns to sea water by the end of March month after laying eggs beneath the coastal sand. * The baby turtles emerge from the eggs after 40-60 days. The mother is not present to look after them. They struggle to survive right from birth. * It takes 30 years for a turtle to reach adulthood and he lives for 50 years. * May 23 is celebrated as World Turtle Day. Source: Brunch, Hindustan Times
author: Rita Bansal
illustrator: Muniza Shariq; Rajiv Eipe; samyak jain

title: A Lovely Puppy
text: She also wanted to have a pet. Wherever and whenever she comes across any pet, she stops to play with them. She said to her Mom one day," I want a puppy. Please bring one for me. I will look after him and play with him." Mom said,"Ask your Papa." In the evening when Papa came back from office, Summi said to her papa,"Papa, I want a puppy. Will you bring one for me?" Papa said,"Of course dear. But you have to take care of it nicely. You should also study well. Don't play with it the whole day." Summi was very happy. She said,"I will take care of it, play with it and complete my studies too." That night Summi dreamt of a beautiful puppy. Next day, papa brought a lovely pup from a pet shop and gave it to Summi. Summi was very happy! Soon she was friendly with it and both played happily.
author: Rita Bansal
illustrator: Madhuri Purandare; Santosh Pujari; Sonal Goyal; Soumya Menon; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Way We Think
text: She sweeps the roads and streets, and picks garbage from many houses. This was her livelihood. Through this work, she was able to take care of her three daughters. She had already arranged marriage for her eldest daughter. Her second daughter, Kusum, and the youngest one are still studying. Kusum's college result will be out today. Chanda has been worried lately. Will she be able to enroll Kusum for further studies? She doesn't have enough money to marry off her eldest daughter as well as send Kusum to a university. She has to think of her youngest one's future too! How will she manage so much? She carried these worries to her work every morning. Whenever she raised her eyes to see well-educated and wealthy children going for work, she would think, 'I'll make sure my Kusum's future is just as promising.' But for that, she must fund Kusum's further education! Her dear child is smart and hard working. She'll find a great job if she gets the right opportunity. The daughter of a sweeper working in a big office... Is it possible? She didn't know the answer to that, but she knew that making efforts is definitely possible and that at least, she will do! May God help Kusum pass her exams with a good score! During all this deep introspection, her boss came for a work inspection. Standing afar, he said, "The boss's wife has called for Kusum, because their maid has gone to her village." He simply delivered his message and walked away, but Chanda's heart grew sad. My daughter is so bright, and she is reduced to cleaning someone's house! She felt bad. But there was nothing in that message to feel so bad about! It was because of her masters' kindness from time to time that her daughters had succeeded in being educated so far. If they ask Chanda and her daughters to do something in turn, then it's fair. She reasoned that a person doing a job which is considered menial is not a small person at all. This is again the kind of thinking that human beings have created for themselves. But for God, jobs and people do not have a status. Any job done with heart and honesty is superior to all, whether it is cleaning houses or simply studying! With that thought, Chanda resumed sweeping the floors swiftly.
author: Sherein Bansal

title: A Street, or a Zoo?
text: Sonu, Monu and Rina set out to play. They saw a kitten. She was looking at a big rat. "Oh look!" shouted Sonu. Rina saw a tiny ant going towards the big rat. Suddenly, a very big shadow fell upon them all. A very big eagle came down to the wall. A tiny ant, a small kitten, a big rat and a very big eagle in the same long street! What would the three clever children do now? They clapped their little hands! The eagle spread its big wings and flew away. Rina made the ant climb onto a leaf. She left the leaf on the wall. The ant saw a grain of sugar. She picked it up and ran home. The big rat picked up a half-eaten pakoda and went back into the drain. The small kitten said 'miaaww' and started licking her paw. Monu got her some milk in a cup. The three kids played with her. The very big eagle sitting on the tree blinked and flew far away.
author: Mala Kumar; Manisha Chaudhry

title: I am Tashi
text: Hello I am Tashi. I am a Tibetan boy. I am 9 years old. I live on a mountain with my family. I want to introduce Tibetan daily life. My family consists of my grandfather, my parents and my brother and me. I wake up in the morning and and go to the river to wash my face. My dog always chases me. In summer time, there are lots of flowers near the river. My brother and I like apples.We eat apples in the morning. My mom makes milk tea everyday. My mom waters and feeds the sheep and the yaks. Today my father bridles the horse and rides. We went to the restaurant in town and we ate food including mushrooms. We drank tea in a tea shop. I like vegetable momo. My brother likes mutton. When we came back, we met some Buddhist pilgrims. They made offering of lotus and orange in the temple. I saw a fox chasing a cat near my family's tent. In the evening, we read from a book with my grandfather. He wears glasses; he shows us a map of the world. We live near the Tibetan Himalayas with our friends. You are welcome anytime.
author: ROGPA NGO, Dhasa

title: A girl with a lantern
text: One night due to power cut the village was immersed in the darkness. Neelima's father had not come home from his farm.Neelima waited for him outside her house with a lantern. She heard a dim noise at a little distance so she moved a few steps forward to know what it was. Her pet pup Blacky also came out there. Suddenly Blacky charged toward a tree. An owl was sitting on that tree holding his prey,a mouse, by its tail. Blacky barked at the owl. In the meantime, Neelima's father arrived there. Neelima, her father, and her pet Blacky came home together. By this time electric supply of the village had also been restored.Neelima's mother cooked tasty food. All had dinner and went to bed.
author: Ravi Ranjan  Goswami
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: A Lesson
text: He was very fond of reading comic books. His annual exams were over and it was his summer vacation. Deepu used to procure comics from his dad or friends, and read them all day. He even brought them along in the car when he went anywhere with his dad. He would sit inside the car and read his comics. A few days ago, he found a new hobby. He liked listening to songs on the mobile through his earphones. Deepu didn't have a phone so he used to ask for it from his mother or his father. One day, he visited a mall in the city with his parents. He saw an iPod in a shop there. He had seen it with a didi in the neighborhood. She often listened to songs on her iPod. She had once let him listen to music on it. He was stubborn and finally got his father to buy him an iPod. Now he read his comics at times, and at other times, listened to music on the iPod with his headphones. Since he got his iPod, wherever he went, the iPod went with him. Even when he was walking on the road, he would be listening to music through his headphones. His parents advised him not to have his ears closed to the world. He shouldn't use his ears only for music. He would obey them for some time, and then go back to his old habits. One day, Deepu's mom asked him to buy tea leaves from the nearby market. As per his habit, he was walking on the road with his iPod, listening to songs through his headphones. At one point, he was supposed to cross the road to the other side. As soon as he turned, an auto appeared from behind. The auto driver honked the horn but Deepu couldn't hear a thing! The auto probably went out of balance. Even though the driver applied brakes, the auto still managed to have a slight impact with Deepu. Deepu fell on the road, and his knees got hurt. Luckily, the injury was minor. He was limping but was able to return home. He learnt an important lesson. One should be careful while walking on the road, especially when crossing it. Also, one should never listen to songs through headphones or earphones on the road. He determined to learn from his mistakes and never to repeat them.
author: Sherein Bansal
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Vinayak Varma

title: Suman Didi
text: Suman goes to college. Suman loves her younger sister Kusum very much and plays with her. Sometimes Suman tells Kusum interesting stories,which she likes very much. On Sundays, she takes Kusum and her friends to a nearby park and tells them interesting and educational stories. Kusum and her friends address Suman as Suman Didi. Suman Didi is quite popular among the neighbourhood children. Suman Didi loves children and the children love Suman Didi.
author: Ravi Ranjan  Goswami

title: Awake at night
text: Dan lived on a farm with his mum, He was a friendly dog, He wasn't able to sleep that night, Whilst his mom slept like a log. He crept away to meet his friends, those who were awake at night. He bounded towards the meadow first, As the moon shone full and bright. Dan first ran to meet his pal, the firefly, He glowed and so, he was called shiny, Dan said, "Meet me soon, on the sly, Under our old, loved, Banyan tree." On the edge of the forest, Dan met Fred fox, He had a strong nose and a bushy tail, Dan told him the same message, And he quickly returned to his search trail. Next, Dan met Flutter, the black bat, She was hanging upside down on a tree, Dan told her to fly to the old Banyan. She said, "Sure. Thanks for thinking of me." Dan went on and met one more friend, Brie with her owl's claws and beak, Dan said, "Fly quick, to the old Banyan tree. Forget the poor mouse. He can't even squeak." Dan's last stop was to meet Hoppy, The Cricket green and bright, He sang all the way to the Banyan tree, Under the full moon's light. All the friends met under the Banyan, hoots and cackles and woofs to greet, They chatted, joked, giggled and laughed, Just like we do when good friends meet, A tired Dan rushed home late in the night, Into his mum's blanket he stealthily crept, With a smile on his face and a happy heart, He hugged his mum close and soon he slept.
author: Poornima Kulkarni

title: The Moon's Face
text: There was once a peaceful little village hundreds of kilometers away from the city. In this peaceful little village was a tiny little farm. And on this little farm was a cat to kill the mice. There were chickens who laid eggs. There was a cow and her little calf to give milk to the farmer. There were pigs who did- well, nothing but roll around in the mud and squeal and oink. These were the jobs of the animals on the farm, which they performed dutifully day after day, week after week, month after month, year after year without any questions. None of the animals wondered why on earth they couldn't do anything different once in a while. Ah, but there is one animal that I haven't mentioned yet. On the farm was a young dog named Tinku, and his job was to bark and keep the others in line. He was the only one who ever wanted to do something different, something special... Tinku had an old mother, frail and weak, but she cared for Tinku more than any dog has ever been cared for. One night he asked her, "Mother, why do we never do anything but bark and keep the others in line? We don't do anything different than we ever do." There was a silence as Tinku's mother thought about the answer to the question that nobody had ever asked on this little farm before. "It's the way of things, Tinku," she simply said, as she had no answer to this intriguing question. "It is and has always been, and it will always be. Besides, don't you like barking and keeping the others in line? What could possibly be more joyful? Perhaps only talking to the moon could be more satisfying." This was, of course, just a passing sentence, but little Tinku didn't know that. "The moon? But the moon is just a giant white face with no features. It has no nose, no eyes, no mouth and no little pink tongue like mine. Surely it can't talk without a little pink tongue?" he wondered curiously. "Oh, but it does. It has big eyes like the cow, a small wet nose like mine, a smiling mouth like the pig's and a little pink tongue just like yours," Tinku's mother exclaimed. "If you look carefully you'll be able to see its face and once you do, you'll be able to talk to it. Now go to sleep, Tinku." With that, she closed her eyes and slept. But Tinku couldn't go to sleep. He stared up at the moon curiously and tried to imagine big eyes like the cow, a small wet nose like his mother's, a smiling mouth like the pig's and a little pink tongue very like his own. Try as he might, he couldn't. He didn't give up, though. For weeks afterwards he looked up at the moon and tried to imagine the moon's face. Life continued as usual at the little farm. The cat killed the mice. The cow gave milk. The chickens laid eggs. The pigs rolled in the mud and squealed and oinked. And Tinku barked and kept all the others in line. However, a few months later, after a normal day, he trotted back home to his little shed. To his surprise, his mother was not there. He searched the entire farm but his mother was nowhere to be seen. He went to the pigs and asked them whether they had seen his mother. They hadn't. Neither did the chickens and the cat. When he asked the cow, she stared pitifully at him with her big brown eyes. "Do you not know, little Tinku? The farmer said that your mother has become useless and so he sold her," she gently told him. Tinku went back to his little shed in tears and cried and cried himself to sleep. Nobody was there now to cuddle and comfort him anymore. He was all alone in this big dark world. When he woke up, Tinku said sadly to himself, "There is nothing here for me anymore. I'm going to find my own fortune in the world." Saying so, he trotted past the snoozing farm animals, past the big house and through the field of grass. "Where are you going, little dog?" a teensy-tiny voice asked him. "Who's that?" Tinku demanded, alarmed, as he looked around him for the source of the sound. "It's me, the Green Grasshopper," a little grasshopper said as it hopped onto a a tall blade of grass. "I'm hoping to find my own fortune. Say, have you seen the face of the moon? My mother said that if you could, you would be able to talk to it," Tinku asked him. The Green Grasshopper thought deeply for a while and answered, "I can see its eyes. See? There are its big eyes." Tinku looked up at the moon and he, too could see the moon's eyes. They did look like the cow's eyes! Joyfully, Tinku thanked the Green Grasshopper and went on his way. As Tinku neared the bushes that were the border between the field and the forest, he saw a pair of bright black eyes staring at him from between them. "Where are you going, little dog?" the owner of the pair of eyes asked curiously. "Who are you?" Tinku questioned. A red fox hopped out from behind the bushes. "It's me, Red Fox," it said in greeting. "I'm going to seek my fortune. Tell me, have you seen the moon's face? If you have, maybe you could help me talk to it," Tinku asked. Red Fox thought about the question and replied, "Well, not the whole face, but I have seen its nose. Look, there it is." Tinku looked up to where the fox was pointing. And he saw the moon's eyes and nose! The nose was just like his mother's little wet nose. Delighted, Tinku thanked Red Fox and entered the forest near the little farm. Tinku wandered past the trees and bushes, following the path. He was just listening to the crickets chirping when he heard hooting and a flutter of wings above him. "Where are you going little dog?" the hooting voice asked him. "Who are you?" Tinku asked, looking above him. An owl flew past him and landed on a tree near Tinku, saying, "It's me, Brown Owl." "I'm seeking my fortune in this world. By the way, have you seen the moon's face? Maybe then I can finally talk to it," Tinku eagerly replied. Brown Owl then responded, "Since I live beneath the trees, I haven't been able to see its entire face, but I always see its mouth. There it is, smiling." Tinku looked at the moon and nearly jumped with joy at seeing a smiling mouth, a nose and two eyes staring down at him. He happily thanked the owl and trotted down the path. But try as he might, he couldn't find anybody who had seen the moon's little pink tongue. Days later, he approached a big red house in the middle of the forest. It was night so nobody seemed to be awake. Outside the house, by the front door was a little shed where another larger dog was sleeping. Tinku decided to ask the dog whether he could share the shed. "Excuse me?" he asked the dog. He couldn't see the dog properly because it was so dark, but nobody answered. Tinku sighed and decided to go sleep under a tree when he heard the dog say, "Hello? Is anybody there?" "Yes, it is another dog. My name is Tinku. I was wondering whether I could share your shed," Tinku answered. "Tinku?" the dog asked in a strange voice. "Mother?" Tinku cried, suddenly recognizing her. Tinku's mother jumped up and hugged him. "What happened?" she asked. Tinku narrated his entire story to his mother and she listened attentively. Tinku's mother sighed and said, "Tinku, you were right. There is so much more to life than barking and keeping the others in line, and only you realized that. See, you took a risk by going away and look how happy you are. Risks are just a part of life and I didn't realize that until I came here. Here we do so many other things and life in this house is so much more better." "But I still didn't find the moon's little pink tongue," Tinku cried. Tinku's mother laughed and said, "I can see it. It is right there, see?" She pointed to the moon and Tinku saw the moon's little pink tongue- and it was exactly like his very own tongue. "But mother, how come nobody else could spot its tongue? Even I couldn't and it is just like my own!" Tinku exclaimed in wonder. His mother cuddled him and thoughtfully smiled. "That is because I love you so much that I can recognize your little pink tongue immediately. I love you no matter what," she explained. "How can I talk to the moon, then?" Tinku asked. "Just talk to it with your heart and it will listen," his mother told him. And that was exactly what little Tinku did. He didn't need his little pink tongue to speak after all. From then on, he stayed at the red house with his mother and talked to the moon every night before going to sleep. He made sure that no day was like the other and occasionally they ventured into the forest and farm to meet the farm animals, the grasshopper, the fox and the owl. THE END
author: Shreya  Challa

title: Night Friends
text: It's night time. Everyone is asleep except Spotty. Spotty is awake. Spotty has an idea. He will meet his "Night" friends. He meets Owl. Spotty woofs. Owl hoots. Then he meets Firefly. Spotty woofs. Firefly glows. Next he meets Bat, hanging upside down from a tree. Spotty woofs. Bat flaps his wings. Next Spotty meets Cricket. Spotty woofs. Cricket chirps. Fox is just around. Spotty woofs. Fox smiles. All the friends meet. They chat and laugh, long into the night. Spotty is tired. He goes back to mum and sleeps. Z
author: Poornima Kulkarni

title: Saathi
text: Gopalpur was the busiest little town you had ever seen. Everybody was always busy, including little Sita. All day she did what her mother told her to do. She helped cook. She fetched water from the well. She went to pick mangoes in the family's mango grove. She collected the eggs from the hen-house. She cleaned the house. She washed the cow. All this and she was only five years old! One day her mother told her to pick five mangoes from the best mango tree and give them to the new neighbor as a greeting. She did exactly that and the person who opened the door was the merriest old man you had ever seen. "Thank you for the mangoes. Tell me, what do you play here?" he asked her. Play? Little Sita was confused. She had never played in all her life. "I clean the floors," she said. The old man shook his head in confusion as Sita walked back home. Back home, Sita was making the rotis with her mother when they ran out of firewood. "Go collect some firewood from the woods, Sita. Remember to stay on the path no matter what," her mother instructed. "Yes, Ma," Sita obediently said, still wondering what the old man had been talking about. By this time it was dark so Sita grabbed a lamp and hurried to the woods. She followed the path like her mother always told her to. Today, however, there was no dry wood by the path. Sita started wondering what she should do. Now, we all know that we are not supposed to wander off the path, especially at night, but even the most obedient of us forget. So when Sita spotted a pile of dry wood off the path she couldn't resist. She hurried to collect some wood but a few minutes later she realized she was lost. Panicked, Sita started looking everywhere for the path but alas! It was nowhere to be seen. Shivering, Sita curled up by a small pond and started to cry. Night slowly became day and Sita was still lost. She had absolutely no idea what to do. Suddenly Sita saw a giant purple monster in the corner of her eye. She tried to get up to run away from the monster but fell into the pond instead! Sita sobbed as she attempted to get out of the pond. Once she was on shore she noticed that the monster was following her. "Get away from me!" Sita cried, tears streaming from her eyes. "Leave me alone!" Still the monster followed her. Sita finally noticed that it was not a monster, but a giant purple bird. It nudged a red ball towards her. "You want to throw that ball around? Well, I don't have time. I still have to collect firewood and go home," Sita frowned. The bird didn't move. "All right," she sighed and threw the ball into the water. The big purple bird immediately jumped in and threw it back to her. They threw the ball back and forth and afterwards the purple bird plucked fresh ripe mangoes off a tree for her. For the rest of the day, Sita played with the bird. For the first time in her life she was having fun. She hugged the purple bird and said to it, "You are my new best friend. I will call you Saathi. It means 'friend.'" Sita played all day and she didn't even worry about cooking or collecting firewood even once. While Sita and Saathi lay basking in the sun in the afternoon, Sita heard her name being called by someone. "That's Ram Uncle who is the policeman!" she gasped. "I have to go, Saathi. I'll see you soon!" She jumped up and ran to the voice. "Ram Uncle!" she exclaimed as she saw him. "Sita! What happened?" he said in shock as he saw her. She explained about how she had gotten lost and about her new friend as they walked back towards the village. Once they reached the village, Ram Uncle told the villagers what had happened. "That purple bird must have kidnapped her!" "The hideous beast was going to eat her!" Upset cries arose from the villagers. "No, no!" Rani exclaimed, shocked. "Saathi is my friend!" "What do you know, Rani?" a villager snapped. "We are going hunt down this monster tomorrow!" The next day, as Sita plucked mangoes from a tree, she noticed a group of villagers including the village headman heading towards the forests carrying large heavy sticks. They were going to hurt Saathi! Sita ran into the forest and saw Saathi sitting on the ground, eating fruits. "Saathi, Saathi! The villagers are coming to hurt you,"she cried. Just then, the villagers arrived at that very spot and noticed the big purple bird. As the group of villagers ran towards Saathi, Sita blocked her friend. "Don't hurt my Saathi! She's my best friend!" Sita cried. "Sita, this monster tried to eat you!" the village headman snarled. "No, no! She's my friend. It's all my fault that I got lost in the forest! She didn't do anything!" Sita said. "I never got to have any friends and I have never played and had fun! It is only because of Saathi that I know what fun is!" The villagers looked at each other. "This is true. All of us are always busy. We never get to relax. I don't remember the last time I did anything but work," one villager muttered. All the others agreed. "All right, Sita. We won't hurt Saathi. You can play with her whenever you want," the headman told Sita. Sita had never been happier! From then on, Gopalpur was not only a busy town, but a relaxing town. Everybody was happy to get a break from work. But Sita and Saathi were the happiest. THE END
author: Shreya  Challa
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Kanu's Violet Friend
text: Kanu lived in a world that she loved all her life. That world was her peaceful village. And her whole life had exactly 7 years so far. Even the cows, the pigs and the cats lived together in peace. When the day ended, everyone went to sleep after a long long day of honest work. There were no worries, no fights that kept them awake at night. You could hear the crickets, it was that quiet. Kanu was friends with all the animals. She shared everything with them. They loved her back unconditionally. One day, Kanu was walking through her fragrant village. Her village had all the colours she loved. Red, blue, pink, yellow, purple, and most of all, green. It was Spring and every where she looked, she found one of her favorite colors looking back at her! Suddenly.. She heard something. And then saw one of her favorite colors, purple, behind a tree. She approached excitedly thinking it might be a bird. But imagine her surprise when she saw it wasn't a small purple bird, but a big tall purple animal! Strangely, he looked happy to see her! Kanu had seen all kinds of birds and animals in her little village. She fed breads and other little things to crows, parrots, koels, owls, sparrows, ducks, swans, swallows, hens, nightingales, peacocks, mynah and the strange woodpeckers. She talked to cows, rabbits, dogs, cats, pigs, squirrels, goats, horses and the furry sheep. But she had never seen this big animal before. She stepped back in fear, and fell into the village pond! Kanu wasn't afraid of the water, but she was afraid of the purple animal who looked like a dinosaur. The Violet dino bowed his head towards the pond, stretched out his long neck to help Kanu climb back to land. But Kanu ignored this and got out of the water herself. She was very wet! And very very angry! Because of this unwanted purple guest in their village, she had fallen into the water and ruined her blue frock! She waved her hands furiously at him, and shouted at him to go away! The poor animal bowed his head again, this time in sadness. He did what she asked him to. He went away. He kept walking until he found a place where there was no villager. He did not want to trouble anyone. He sat down and soon, started to doze off. He suddenly woke up with loud noises coming from behind him. A crowd of villagers had gathered! Some looked scared, some looked angry. Or maybe they were angry because they were scared. They rushed towards him with sticks and stones. The Violet animal ran away as fast as his big strong legs could carry him! He loved the villagers. But the villagers did not love him. He realized he must disappear for some time. When Kanu got home that day, her father called her to his room. Kanu was already upset at what happened to her near the village pond. She hoped that her father would give her a little gift to cheer her up. But he had no gift. In fact, he was angry. But not at her. He was angry at the Violet animal. Her father, and the whole village, had now met him. She had never seen her father so upset. He asked her not to go out because there was a dangerous beast in the village. The elders had decided to capture the beast! Kanu was a sweet girl. She could not be angry with anyone for too long. So when her father told her that the beast might get captured because everyone wanted to get rid of it, she grew sad. She was surprised to see a strange animal that she had never seen before. But she did not want him harmed in any way. She tried to convince the village elders to leave him, but the entire village was against her. What should she do? Kanu knew that this is the first time the whole village was worried and scared about something. This was new for all of them. She slipped out of her home late at night to search for the Violet creature. She wanted to warn him about the angry villagers. But she could not find him anywhere! Where could he go? Where could he hide? She wondered. Did he leave? That made her sad. She suddenly realized that she had wanted to know him better. But now he had gone. Kanu returned home with a heavy heart. As soon as the sun came up, Kanu had an idea. The whole village might be against her. But there was one person who would always support her... Her mother! So, she looked for her mother everywhere, in the storage room, on the bullock carts, at the neighbor's house, and finally found her! She knew her mother will help her convince everyone to stop looking for the animal. Her mother was a wise, sensible woman who was well-respected in their village. All the villagers came to her for advice. And now, Kanu needed some advice too. So, Kanu told her mother everything. How she met the animal, how she got scared, then angry and then made him leave. She also told her that he smiled strangely when he looked at her and that he came in the way when she was trying to get out of the village pond. Kanu's mother was a good listener. She understood everything, and then gently corrected her sweet daughter. "Kanu, do you think that the animal was smiling because he was happy to see you? And do you think that maybe he was trying to help you out of the pond?" Kanu was silent. She hadn't thought like that. Kanu felt guilty. Her fear had made her blind to the animal's kindness. She asked her mother, "What should i do now?" Her mother said, "Go to your animal friends. This village worships all the animals. If the elders are not listening to you, they will certainly listen to them. Tell your friends to spread the word and find this sweet Violet creature!" Kanu was relaxed. Now she could DO something. So she left her home happily and went in search of her best friend, Khabbu. Khabbu was her dog. They both had grown together, played together and eaten their meals together. Khabbu was a happy dog and loved to help Kanu in everything. Kanu asked Khabbu to tell all the animals and birds of the village about this kind Violet creature. She told Khabbu that they all must unite to save him! Khabbu happily took off to meet all his other friends from the village. He first met the wisest of all his friends, Flacko the fox. Years ago, Khabbu was scared of him, but then soon saw that Flacko was a gentle animal with many many stories and lots of wisdom. Flacko knew about the animal. He said, "That creature is the Violet Boon. He is a gift of Gods. He must have come to bless this village but the villagers scared him away." Khabbu could not believe it! This was a great luck for the village. He decided he will do everything he can to find the Violet Boon for the village. So Khabbu ad Flacko went from animal to animal, telling them the great news! Everyone was overjoyed. The animals celebrated wherever Khabbu went to spread the word. "We will find him! "Don't worry! We have the whole night!" "We'll talk to the villagers in the morning!" All the animals and Kanu joined hands in looking for the Violet Boon. They looked for him everywhere in the village. Even their small village seemed huge to them now. "Where could he be?" Kanu kept asking herself. There was only one place left now...The village pond. The place she had met him first. Kanu decided to go there. There he was! At the village pond! Bright, beautiful, violet and divine. How could Kanu not see him like this before? But she also saw that he was sad. She went towards him to comfort him. He smiled when he saw her coming. This time, Kanu smiled back. "I'm very sorry for my behavior. I've been looking for you since days. Will you please forgive me? Today, the animals told me who you are. Please don't leave our village. The animals and I will explain everything to the village elders..." Kanu was sincere, and the Violet Boon saw that. He silently nodded and touched Kanu's head with his beak. The next day, a stableman went with his horses to the Village S arpanch (Village head). He told the sarpanch that his horses were chosen by all the village animals to deliver an important message to him. He told the sarpanch the truth about the he truth about the Violet Boon. The sarpanch was shocked. He was a sensible man who felt sad for the anger, hate and fear within the village. He immediately decided to take action, and hold a panchayat. Every villager attended the panchayat. They talked among themselves. "This must be for that beast." "Let's see what the sarpanch will do about it!" But the sarpanch surprised all the villagers with the amazing truth. Everyone rejoiced and hugged Kanu for her bravery and honesty! They set out to rectify their huge mistake. Kanu and all the animals led them to the village pond where they found the Violet Boon. Everyone apologized to him, asked him to stay and bless the village with his beautiful presence. Kanu's father was extremely proud of his little daughter. He took her in his arms and then put her up on his shoulders so that everyone could see the little star of the village! The Violet Boon blessed Kanu, her family, her kind animal friends and the whole village. He promised to come again soon. Joy, peace and understanding were back in the village. Kanu accompanied the Violet Boon when he finally got ready to leave the village. They had become good friends! She waved him goodbye as the Violet Boon slowly went inside the pond water and then, disappeared. 'Maybe he will go to a different village now', Kanu thought. 'I hope they are kind to him and get to know him first before asking him to leave!" She had, after all, learnt an important lesson in acceptance and friendship.
author: Sherein Bansal
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: JHYAN VRIKSHA WITH SADAR CHACHA
text: There was a village near a town. In other villages, people where poor but not here. People where rich and hard working. Half of the population used to work in the companies of the town. People had facilities like parks, schools, hospitals, malls in the town. Children were taught good manners but still they ate junk food frequently! They didn't know the value of money, good food. After all this they didn't even exercise! They took a auto to and from school. The villagers where tired of the habits of children. They scolded them, told them, explained them but still they didn't listen. One day, they held a meeting. They all where very confused. One said leave the village and the other said ban junk food. They thought it will be to strict. At the end, they all went to Sadar Chacha. Sadar Chacha was a elder man near the edges of the village. His son and daughter where in another town near by. He was wiser and elder than all. When the villagers explained to Sadar Chacha, he thought and thought. Finally, he smiled. "Call all children and villagers below the Mango tree today evening 6 to 7. I know how to handle all this. " instructed Sadar Chacha. At six, everyone gathered around the tree. Sadar Chacha was happy to see all those happy faces. They reminded him of his little grand children whose grand children came in their winter vacations to visit him. " Children, today I am going to tell you a story. " told Sadar Chacha. " What story Chacha Dada? " asked a boy. " It is a story about a girl................................................................... " started Sadar Chacha. " Once upon a time, there lived a girl.Her name was Meena. Meena lived in a village to a walking distance to a town. Her father worked in the town. She was very nice and kind but there was only one bad thing about her.... she always ate junk food. She never exercised, ate home food. Day by day she became plump. People used to scold her, told her and explain her that it is not good for her and she is becoming fat but she never listen to anyone. Being the only daughter, her father never scolded her. He bought whatever she asked. It was a dark night. All misty. Meena had gone to her friend's birthday party. Meena was returning all alone. There was no auto or taxi. She was sleepy and heavy as she ate a whole pizza after winning the ' eating competition for Pani Puri '. She was crossing the bridge while she slipped and fell down. She managed to hold a little part of the road but the road couldn't take her weight. She fell down in the water. She knew swimming but was so fat that she couldn't swim. She screamed for help but no one could listen. She was depressed. The next moment she was unconscious. Luckily for her, that river passes through that village. Her neighbour 's friend's nephew saw her and called others to help her. When she woke up, she found herself home. Her mother was looking worried just like other villagers. " We where so worried for you " told the villagers. " I am sorry. It is my mistake. I promise to eat less junk, exercise. " told Meena tearfully. " It is good that you understood. Now you must rest. " told the villagers. The wished goodnight and went to their homes. She started eating good food. She started walking and exercising. No sooner she was a fit girl. When she grew up, she became an Olympic gold medallist in diving and racing. She also learnt the value of money So you understand kids? Do you want to be the young Meena or the elder Meena " finished Sadar Chacha. " WE PROMISE TO EAT LESS JUNK FOOD AND EXERCISE DAILY " Cried all the Kids. Who do you want to be????????????????????
author: Meesha Maheshwari

title: A beautiful day
text: "Amar chacha, Amar chacha"...the kids come running to the banyan tree, under whose caring shade, the old wise Amar chacha was perched comfortable. "Hello kids, so good to see all of you here today. Who is going to share a story with us today" asked Amar chacha. "Me..meee..me... Chutki was all excited. "Okay, dear girl, let us hear it..." My mum and I were preparing chapatis on the fire in our veranda, when the naughty birds came pecking at the grains... I shooed them and followed along the way... Golu our dog was so excited, he merrily followed me through the village as I played with my friends. As night fell, the moon came out smiling down upon us and smiling at little Golu, was merrily jumping around. Golu spots an owl in the hallow of a tree and asks the owl, "excuse me, miss, you have such big and beautiful eyes. Have you spotted my little Chutki passing through here?" The old owl hooted, and said, "hello little doggy, I have seen Chutki, she was singing a song and walking along, admiring the flowers and the trees. She seems to be headed to the old farm." "woof woof, thank you owl", said Golu as he wagged his tail and merrily walked on. "woof woof, hello Mr. Bat, have you seen my Chutki? I am looking for her..." said Golu. "Hello Golu, the night is young and I have only just opened my eyes and stretched my wings" said the bat. "I haven't seen Chutki today, although she likes to meet the piggies at the farm, maybe she may have gone there...", said the bat. "Thank you my friend", said Golu as he moved on... "Hello missy, have you seen my Chutki today?" asked Golu as he was still panting from his long walk. "Golu, so good to see you. Little mouse Tinu was hurt, so Chutki took her to the farm to reunite her with her mother. She just passed through here a few moments ago..."said the grasshopper. "woof woof, thank you.." It was late evening by the time Chutki reached the farm and all the farm animals were tucked in next to their mothers, almost magical as the moon watched over them, gently lighting the path and keeping them warm. The baby cow tucked next to her mother, baby piggy sleeping on his back with his feet in the air next to mummy piggy and baby kitty on mummy cow's back cuddly and comfortable. Ah, what a beautiful sight, when nature is calm, serene and beautiful. Finally Golu reached the farm and was reunited with his mummy, and he wagged his tailed and barked with excitement "woof woof, mummy I am back"... so happy to see his mummy. His mother was delighted too, and she hugged and kissed Golu and cuddled him as they prepared to go to sleep. As Golu lay on his back, he was happy to be home, but he missed his friend Chutki and was wondering if she was already asleep or awake.... Finally Golu closed his eyes and went into a beautiful world of dreams..Zzzz He will swim the deepest oceans and climb the highest mountain and soar the skies in his beautiful dream... a wonderful world where anything is possible. Good night my lovelies... dream a beautiful dream.
author: Khushrav Kumana
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: My Grandma!
text: My favorite person in my family is my Grandma. She makes yummy laddoos for me! Her laddoos are big and soft with a tiny cashew nut on top! My Grandma also helps me read new books. Grandma is also very brave! She is not afraid of spiders. She shoos them away with a newspaper in hand. I like to help my Grandma. She tells me interesting tales from her childhood, while I help her peel the peas. The yellow sweater that she knitted for me is my favorite! I love my Grandma. She really is the best!
author: Payoshni Saraf
illustrator: Aman Randhawa; Priya Kuriyan; Rajiv Eipe; Reshma Barve; Ruchi Shah; Tanaya Vyas

title: Mothers  love
text: I am always hungry. I love to eat with my mother. But my mom is not at home. she goes for work early in the mornining. I am waiting for her eagarly. When she comes home she feed us with love. I am very happy. I sleep with my mother happily.
author: sonali pimpalkar
illustrator: Madhuri Purandare; Rijuta Ghate; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: True friends
text: Once there was a dog named Moti. He had a friend name d Raju. They were sitting in an umbrella and playing in the river.It started raining. They enjoyed the ride together. Suddenly, The dog fell in the river. Raju went out of the river. He saw a fishing rope on the bank.He threw the rope towards Moti and saved his life. After that they caught many fishes and went home happily.
author: Giridhar Panghate

title: My School
text: It was my first day to school.No one was familiar.everything was new. No one was in the class.No one let me sit beside.I didn't understand why they behave like that. Teacher entered in the class and just smiled at me.I smiled in reply.Teacher introduced me to the class. Days passed. Some boys and girls became my friends. I was different. I found my teacher close to me as he always talked with me like a friend. A year passed and I changed totally.Now everyone called me Rita,not mad girl.
author: Giridhar Panghate
illustrator: Mayur Mistry; Nina Sabnani; Priya Kuriyan; Sanjay Sarkar; Saurabh Pandey

title: Brave girl LATA
text: There was a little girl named Lata. She was very brilliant and a perfect nature lover. Lata and her friends usually played various games in the evening. One evening they were playing hide and seek. All of the friends founded a broken house and decided to hide in it. While playing one of the friend fall in the water tank which was about 10 feet deep. lata noticed a sound near water tank. She quickly ran towards that tank. she silently thought what can be done to save him. She saw a rope hanging on the wall. Without wasting a second she dropped that rope in the tank which was tied somewhere tightly. Through that rope he climbed up and reached the floor successfully. For her wonderful and brave job. She was awarded. she had saved her friend. she was very happy for this wonderful job.
author: zpup DIGHORI
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Greystroke; Henu; Lavanya Karthik; Maya  Ramaswamy; Phidi Pulu; Sanjay Sarkar; Suvidha Mistry

title: The little Painters
text: It was holiday time. Veena and Vinay were i the garden with strewn color boxes. All the possible colors were there; white, red,green and yellow and not to miss blue also. The painter men were busy in their work. One was on the ladder and the other one was hanging by the wall. Veena curiously asked " Is there anything we can do to help you? " The painter man handed over the brushes to both of them " you paint the gate from inside " he said to Veena, and "you paint it from outside" he said to Vinay. Veena and Vinay picked up two boxes of color and got ready to paint. Veena started painting the gate from one side and Vinay started from the other side. Some color fell on the floor, some on the wall, but more color fell on both of them. Somehow they finished the work. They wiped the color which fell on the floor and wall. And in the last they have cleaned themselves. " My red gate is so nice" said Veena. " My green gate is so nice" said Vinay. "Oho you guys have painted the gate in two different color " the painter man said in a displeased tone. " Ok let it be like this " their mother said.
author: Kausor Khan

title: Enjoy rain.
text: There was a cute little girl named Veena. She loved playing in the garden, with birds,and animals. She went to school,but did not want to study,There she saw dark clouds in the sky, and heard a loud thunder sound, dhannn, dhannnn, dhanannnn,and lighting also started to flash, thrrr, thrrrrr, thrrrrrrrr. Oh my god! it was about to rain. Suddenly it started raining heavily. All the children left the school and ran out in rain to play. They splashed the water,and played with paper boats. Veena also came to play in the rain. There she saw lovely peacock dancing. Veena and her friends enjoyed the rain.
author: sakina vora
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Manjari Chakravarti; Priya Kuriyan; Sanjay Sarkar

title: The Fruit of Joy
text: Despite Nanni warning me, I tiptoed to her mango tree. The fruit was green but I was keen, to pluck one or two quietly. First I jumped for the lowest fruit, then I shook the tree from its roots. A stone was flung, on branches I swung, but all my efforts went in vain. So I gave up and turned around, when thud a mango fell to the ground. It was really kind that the tree didn’t mind, but Naani saw it in my hand and frowned.
author: Dharani Isser

title: Greeny and Hoppers Become Friends
text: One morning Greeny the dinosaur decided to go on a little adventure. "Bye Mom! I will be back in the afternoon! I am going to sail down the river to explore," he said. His mom replied, "Make sure to pack some lunch and stay safe! Have fun!" So Greeny set off in his little red boat down the river. "Here is a nice spot to stop. I will pick some flowers for Mom first," said Greeny. As he was about to pick a nice purple flower he saw a small grasshopper sitting on a leaf. "Hello! My name is Greeny," Greeny said, "What is your name?" "I am Hoppers. Let's be friends!" replied the grasshopper. "Ok!" replied Greeny. The two friends decided that they would spend the entire day together. "The day is so nice. It makes me want to dance!!" exclaimed Hoppers. "Let's dance together!" replied Greeny. The two then pranced around the flower fields until they were too tired to move. "Thanks for playing with me today Hoppers! I had so much fun! But Mom is waiting for me at home. I have to go back now," said Greeny. "I had so much fun today too! Maybe we can meet sometime next week! Bye until next time!" replied Hoppers.
author: Jeon Wonwoo

title: Sam Uncle
text: Sam Uncle is an auto driver who lives in Saket area of new Delhi. He is very kind & generous in person. Sam Uncle drops me everyday to my school which is in Mehrauli,New Delhi.He comes to my home at 7 AM. He drives very well and always follow the traffic rules. My parents also rely on Sam Uncle as he takes care of me very well.
author: abhishek khanna
illustrator: Ajanta Guhathakurta; Priya Kuriyan; Rupa Prakash

title: My sister – My hero!
text: This is my sister. She studies in a college. Her name is Seema. We like to take walks. We like to see things. My sister and I like to talk. My sister tells me stories. I like to listen to them. She is very smart. I love my sister very much. She makes me very happy. My sister is my hero.
author: Ameya Date

title: FLY IN SPACE
text: One night in Lalaland Mr. Fly was gazing up at the night sky. Then there was a flash of lightning and there it showed a weird constellation like a streak of lightning in the sky. Then Mr. Fly looked left to right 10 times. He built a machine he pressed the on switch and cazzam! He went flying to space and never came back. Some people think he died and some think he went to earth, but no one knows for sure except for lucky astronauts! THE END
author: YoMik

title: Friendship Land
text: This is Dino, a sad and lonely dinosaur who had no friends. One day, he asked the beautiful river by his cave, if she had friends. "Yes, of course", she said. "The rain and the rainbow are my best friends", she added. "Colorful fish also pay me a visit sometimes. They too are my friends." Looking at Dino's grief-stricken face, the river understood that he had no friends. Suddenly a boat magically appeared in front of Dino. The river said, "this boat is my gift to you Dino, it will take you to Friendship Land, a land full of new friends". Dino thanked the river and sat on the magical boat. The boat slowly sailed him far, far away from his home. Dino soon arrived at Friendship Land, the most beautiful place on the planet. He had never seen such colorful flowers, nor had he seen a grasshopper before! The grasshopper welcomed Dino and asked him if he would want to be friends? "Oh yes, yes, yes!" exclaimed Dino, with excitement. Soon, Dino made friends with the birds, bees, butterflies and flowers of Friendship Land. He was never ever sad and lonely again because he had a land full of friends!
author: Janani Ganapathi
illustrator: Shailja Jain Chougule; Sweta  Roy Choudhury

title: The Little Fish
text: Once upon a time, there lived a little fish called Hilly. Hilly used to stay with her parents and three sisters, Tilly, Milly and Tes. They used to live in a small house in the deep seas of the Indian Ocean. Hilly used to enjoy playing with her three sisters. One day, while she was reading close to a coral, she saw 2 big fish going inside a secret door. She went and asked them, “What are you doing here?” So, the big fish said, "There is a secret treasure behind this door and the fish guard only allows the big fish in". Hilly found it very amusing and wished in her mind, “How I wish I was big then I could also see the secret treasure!” Suddenly, an idea struck her. She thought, “Let me go to the Sea wizard. May be he can help me become big.” So, off she went to the Sea wizard. When she got into the Sea wizard’s cottage inside the sea, she knocked at the door and said, “Hey Sea wizard, it’s me Hilly.” The Sea wizard opened the door and said, “Come in Hilly, what brings you here.” Hilly said, “Oh! Sea wizard, I have a big problem, you see! I want to become big like the big fish. They’re so big, they can dance in the seas beautifully.” (She didn’t want to tell him about the secret treasure). He said, “Oh, little Hilly, if that’s what you want, so be it. But let me warn you that once I help make you big, I may not be able to undo it.” Hilly said, “I’m sure that’s what I really really want. I want to be big.” The Sea wizard said with a sigh, “Alright, here you go and whoof in a cloud of purple dust, Hilly became big.” She thanked the wizard and set sail towards the seas. But as soon as she reached home, she called out “Mother, I’m here”. Mother opened the door and asked, “Who are you?” Poor Hilly! She tried to tell her who she was but she wasn’t able to convince her. On the contrary, her mother started worrying why Hilly wasn’t home yet. Hilly was sad. She went to her favourite garden hoping that she’ll find her old friends or her sisters. But, they refused to recognize her. Moreover, they were too scared of her thinking the big fish will eat them up. After they left, Hilly was reminded of her favourite rocking sea horse. She tried to sit on it but she couldn’t. She realised that now she was too big to sit on her favourite horse. She felt even more sad now. She sat down and started thinking. She remembered all her joyous fun moments were with her mother, her 3 sisters and her friends and sadly, now she was distanced from all of them. She thought to herself, “If I want to return to my family, I need to go to the wizard and request him to make me small again.” She went to the wizard with lots of hopes. The wizard opened the door and saw the teary-eyed Hilly. He felt sad for her after hearing her tale. He assured her that he will help her become small again. At the same time, he reminded her that being greedy never helps. We should be thankful to God for the way He has made us. Finally, Hilly became small again and she rushed home to be with her family. This taught her a big lesson and she never ever became greedy again. Moral of the story: Be happy for who you are. Love yourself as you’re one-of-a-kind and unique!
author: Rhea Dharamshi
illustrator: Muniza Shariq; Rajiv Eipe; Sangeeta Das; Srikrishna Kedilaya

title: Friendship Land
text: This is Dino, a sad and lonely dinosaur who had no friends. He lived on his own in a little cave by a beautiful river. One day, he walked up to the beautiful river to drink water, after which he asked her if she had any friends. "Yes, of course. Everyone has friends!", she exclaimed. "The rain and the colorful rainbow are my best friends", she added. "Multicolored fish also pay me a visit sometimes. Red, purple, yellow... They all are my friends too." Hearing that, Dino's face faded. Looking at Dino's grief-stricken face, the river understood that he had no friends. Suddenly a boat magically appeared in front of Dino. It was a very attractive shiny wooden boat. The river said, "this boat is my gift to you Dino, it will take you to Friendship Land, a land full of new friends". Dino thanked the river, promising that he would never forget her and sat on the magical boat. He waved his cave goodbye and the boat slowly sailed him far, far away from his home. Dino soon arrived at Friendship Land, the most beautiful place on the planet. He was so happy that he almost forget to thank the magical boat. He stepped out on the new land and kissed the boat goodbye. His eyes had never seen such colorful flowers, nor had they seen a grasshopper before! The grasshopper welcomed Dino and shook hands with him saying "I am Greeny, the grasshopper. Would you want to be friends with me?" "Oh yes, yes, yes! I would love to be your friend Greeny!" exclaimed Dino, with excitement. Soon, Dino made friends with the birds, bees, butterflies and flowers of Friendship Land. They would dance, sing and play together every single day and then sleep together on the flower bed at night. Dino was never ever sad and lonely again because he had a land full of friends!
author: Janani Ganapathi
illustrator: Shailja Jain Chougule; Sweta  Roy Choudhury

title: The Scarecrows on Parade
text: Ma make scarecrows for their field. She picked her new red frock and red ribbons to make a lovely looking scarecrow. "But scarecrows have to be scary, not pretty", said Ma. She tried to make scary face. But Gauri found it funny! he he he Both Ma and Gauri fixed the scary scarecrows in the field. Scarecrows can shoo the birds away. At night lying on her cot, Gauri looked out from her window. She saw a scarecrow look down at it's clothes! "I wish we had something pretty to wear!" sighed the scarecrow. It did not like old clothes. Others also wanted to change their clothes to new and neat ones. They found Gauri's clothes on the clothesline. One scarecrow put on her lovely red frock and tied the red ribbons on her straw hair. She felt pretty and showed off. Soon, all the scarecrows began dressing up! walking! turning! twisting! and twirling! They were having fun! But what's that? Birds here, birds there, birds everywhere. Munching and chomping the delicious grains in the field. They were happy. Scarecrows were busy having fun and not shooing them away. The scarecrows heard all the munching and chomping of the birds. They were horrified! "Shoo! Be gone!!" The scarecrows waved their straw hands at the birds. Gauri saw the birds coming towards her. She screamed. Ma held her tight. She had come to wake Gauri up. Oh! It is morning now. Gauri looked out. The fields are safe. The scarecrows are at the same place as the night before. Phew! it must have been a bad dream. Or was it? Were the scarecrows waving to her? She saw the red ribbon on a scarecrow's straw hair. She blinked! Did the scarecrow just wink at her?
author: Divya Gogoi

title: Lost in the Night
text: One night Mama dog and Pup were sleeping. Pup woke up. He went outside without Mama's permission. " Meow, meow "... It was the kitten! She was lost! Pup wanted to help her. Pup took the kitten to her mom, to their home. "Hoot hoot..." It was the Owl. He was lost too! Pup wanted to help. So he took the Owl to his home. He again was walking when he saw the cub. Now, he was lost too. Pup wanted to help again. So he took the cub to the Lion. Lion said "I have heard that you helped everybody today.""Um,Yes I did, my Lord." said the Pup. "Anyway, it is getting dark. I should help you" said the Lion. Lion and the cub took the Pup to his home. Mama dog was surprised when the King of the Jungle was there. So they all together had a yummy feast together.
author: Janaki Latha
illustrator: Aditi Dilip; Bindia  Thapar; Deepa Balsavar; Rupa Prakash; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Atoms, Molecules, Elements, Compounds
text: Dalton called it 'an atom' thinking it was indivisible, But its positive nucleus and negative electrons make its charge neutral. Elements form when atoms of only one family gather, Compounds form when atoms of different families get together.
