title: Buddy and I
text: March 25, 2017, Saturday night, I met 'Buddy'. He had occur colored patches on his white body. He had a tiny open wound right in the middle of his neck, which you would notice only when he sat upright on his two legs. He had dark brown beady eyes that looked straight, without a blink, into my eyes. He had very soft pads under his paws, which can be felt only when he put his paw on your hand for a handshake. He was a 'Hand-shake' friendly dog. For some reasons, he kept sitting on his two hind legs to offer his paw-shake to people. His name was 'Buddy'.... my daughter called him so! The place where I met him was quite far from the city lights.... a remote village, where we had gone for a 'star-gazing' weekend expedition. There were hundreds of people, like us who had come to show stars and planets to their children. The event was organised by a star-gazing club called 'Khagol-Mandal' near Mumbai. We were very excited for this dark night adventure. Especially my daughter, as we were to see stars and planets through their telescopes. We had nothing but the stars and planets and camping on our minds. And suddenly at dinner break, we spotted a huge Dalmatian with two other dogs. They were very friendly. Since my daughter loves dogs, my husband took her to the Dalmatian, just for a little petting. I stayed back, as I am not too much of a dog lover. They came back to me to tell how friendly the dogs were, and said I must pat them as they had become our pets. They showed 'Buddy' to me, the occur patched dog! I smiled.. yes! he indeed was very friendly, to be precise Hand-shake friendly! My husband and my daughter wanted to me give my hand for his paw-shake, I tried.. but I was scared. Buddy scuttled away. The dinner-break was about to get over. I was sitting on my mat waiting for my husband and daughter to come back from dog-patting and join me. It was then, Buddy came to me and sat on his hind legs offering his paw-shake. I gave my hand, he placed his paw and touched my palm and then wrist and then little up on my hand. Three times. Then he gave his another paw, I gave my another hand, again same way he touched my hand three times, palm, wrist and up on hand. His paws were very soft and paddy. I wasn't scared anymore. I was smiling and giggling! My daughter and others came there to watch. He kept giving me his paw one after another. And kept looking straight into my eyes all the while. He wasn't ready to move away or give paw-shake to anybody else. My daughter commented, 'Mumma, he likes you very much!' Yeah! It was obvious! He was nearing inches by inches with every paw-shake...and I was worried. He was going on and on with his paw-shakes.. i was getting tired and worried. Worried that he might come and sit in my lap, he was so near me by now! His gaze never leaving me! Who was he? I got up and moved away. He followed me. I moved quite away pretending to go somewhere and Buddy got busy with others. Thank goodness! I felt.. The break got over and event continued.. and once more, we got busy star gazing.... when buddy came to me again! He sat near me and offered his paw. I got up and moved away. I didn't want the long paw-hand-shakes again. After all, he was a stray dog, with muddy paws and a wound! Hygiene kept playing on my mind and after every paw-shake with me or my daughter, I kept pouring down chunks of hand-sanitizer in both our palms. I was worried for germs and all. There was a dust-bin near our mat. Throughout the star-gazing event, Buddy kept coming to that bin, peering into it to get some left-overs for his meal. He with the other dogs was mouthing every packet of food thrown into the Bin. It was such a typical siting of stay dogs. Wasn't it? But I felt pinch.. I felt sad! I don't know why? Did I know him? Why was I feeling bad about his fate, his life near the left-over bin? The event got over early Sunday morning and we returned to our city homes. Now, far away from 'Buddy'.. But No! I was not able to go far.... I was not able to push away 'Buddy' from my mind. I don't know why! There was something special about him and me. There was a connection. Some cosmic connection! I am sure we must have known each other in someway, in some world, on some earth, in some galaxy! Maybe! I can never forget his gaze! His touch! He knew me! I am sure! But, he didn't even woof! So I would never know!
author: Shital Choudhary
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Bindia  Thapar; Deepa Balsavar; Hari Kumar Nair; Henu; Kunea Madigibuli; Preethi Krishnan; Santosh Pujari; Shikha Nambiar; Sonali Sharma; Sorit Gupto; Suvidha Mistry; Zainab Tambawalla

title: What happened to the shawl?
text: One day, the great Buddha was taking a walk around the monastery. He was approached by a monk who wanted a new woolen shawl. The Buddha asked him, "What has happened to your old shawl?" "It had become very old and worn out. So I am using it as a bedsheet," replied the monk. The Buddha asked again, "But what happened to your old bedsheet?" "Master, that bed sheet got old with use. It was worn and torn. So I cut it up and made a pillow cover out of it," replied the monk. "But there certainly was a pillow cover before you made a new one. What did you do to your old pillow cover?" asked the Buddha. "My head had rubbed a million times against the old pillow cover and had made a big hole in it. So I made a doormat out of it," replied the monk, in earnest. Gautama Buddha was not satisfied by this answer. He always delved deep into every issue. He asked the monk, "Tell me, what did you do with your old doormat?" The monk replied with folded hands, "Master, the old doormat had got totally worn out. After being used for so long, the warp and the weft had come out. So I took the cotton fibres and braided a wick out of them. Later, I burned the cotton wick in the oil lamp." The Buddha smiled after listening to the monk. The monk got a new shawl! Make your own cloth ball 1. Choose old clothes at home that you can reuse. You will need to cut out two pentagon shapes and five petal shapes like this. 2. Hand-stitch the pieces. Or get an adult to machine stitch them. Leave a small hole in one pentagon. 3. Turn it inside out. 4. Insert a strong balloon and blow it. 5. Twist the mouth of the balloon, tie a knot, and push it in through the button-hole. 6. Yippee! Your colourful cloth ball is ready. Fun with threads! Here is an easy way to have hours of fun with small bits of thread or wool. 1. Find an empty matchbox. 2. Thread a length of wool about 70cm long diagonally through the box. 3. Thread a length of wool in another colour through the other diagonal. Tie the ends together. 4. Ask a friend to hold both the ends of the wool. And you can slide the box gently across. Surprise, surprise! The wool seems to change colour as it comes out of the box! Find more such free-to-download projects at ww.arvindguptatoys.com Recycle! Reuse! Reduce! We buy, use and throw away things without thinking much about them. We buy much more than we need. Our mantra seems to be, "Buy more! Throw more!" We misuse Earth’s resources like water, trees, sand and soil and produce tonnes of junk that become mountains of garbage. But has it always been like this? Have we Indians always been wasteful? No! History tells us that Indians have been very frugal and sensible. We believe that every object has several uses - not one, but many lives. The concept of reuse and recycle has very deep roots in the Indian culture. This story is 2,500 years old, set in the times when the great sage and teacher Gautama Buddha lived. It shows a deep respect and sensitivity for the material world. It has many lessons for us.
author: Arvind Gupta

title: April fool.... have fun!
text: Ashu: Today morning a little penguin came and perched on our window grill. Bittu: Really? Why didn't you show me? Ashu: Ullu Banaya.... Bada Maza Aaya! Ullu Banaya.... Bada Maza Aaya! (Ashu Sang) (in Hindi) Bittu: Youuuuuu! Ashu: Oh common! I thought you would get it. You know very well that: 1) Penguins can't fly.... then how can they fly up the window and perch huh? 2) Penguins live in Southern Hemispher.... how can one come here in our hot city huh? Bittu: Huh! Bittu: Hey! I just saw a Gorilla up on that big mountain! Ashu: where.. where? show me. Bittu: Ullu Banaya.... Bada Maza Aaya! Ullu Banaya.... Bada Maza Aaya! Ashu: Youuuuuu! Bittu: Oh! title: Bed-Time Stories
text: My Amma tells me a story every night. There is one story about a frog which talks. There is another story about a king with a long beard. Sometimes it is about a flying elephant. In one story a fox and a tiger are friends. The tiger falls into a hole. How will the tiger get out? Then the clever fox saves the tiger. This is the best story. I listen to the story and then fall asleep.

title: How cats can see in dark ?
text: Colby, the owl was sad because she had no friends. She was awake when everyone slept and slept when everyone was awake. All the animals teased her. Though she tried to stay awake during the day she couldn't. Then one day when Colby was sleeping a tired cat came and asked for shelter, but Colby was in deep sleep, so the cat purred. Colby woke up, and asked why she was here. She told that she had traveled a long distance from the forest in search of food and lost her way and that she was tired and that if she got shelter she would be very grateful to Colby. Colby told that she could stay with her as long as she wanted. They shared their meals. The cat realized that Colby was awake in night and slept during the day, so she started staying awake in the night. At the beginning it was difficult but later she got used to it. And that's how cats have a good vision in the dark.
author: Kshirin Shetty
illustrator: Jagdish Joshi; Priya Kuriyan; Sanjay Sarkar; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Seetha's prize
text: Seetha was a girl who used to love helping others. She was a responsible girl and really helpful. After school she used to feed her brother, help her mother with the housework, and used to help her father iron his clothes for his office. After helping her family she used to go to Ranjhana aunty and help her by drying clothes. Her parents were proud of her. One day when she was on her way to school, she saw an old woman who had fallen down. Nobody was willing to help her. Seetha ran and helped the old woman by taking her to the nearest hospital. She rushed to school and that day was the award giving ceremony, the principal announced Seetha's name and told the school about the incident and that she was her mother and she didn't know about the accident until her mother called her from the hospital. Seetha recieved a chocolate and a book. Seetha was very happy. MORAL: The good you do comes back to you.
author: Kshirin Shetty

title: Two stories
text: Story No. 1 Mr. Goat and Magic Once a goat climbed up a hill. It was surprised to find everything so very small from up there. The houses, the roads, the farms, even the other goats.. so small! The goat climbed down to check what the matter was. When it reached down, everything came back to its normal size. How? Goat thinks it was magic! was it? Mr. Goat.. there is no magic! Just physics! See these building.. they appear so tiny.. but there are big and tall.. They appear small because they are far. Our eyes create a triangle to see objects. Triangle becomes acute when objects are far so we find them smaller. And Triangle shrinks as objects come near, so we can see its normal size. Story No. 2 An Ant and a Girl Once there was a girl. She went to a park and noticed a tiny ant carrying a big green fruit. The girl thought if an ant can carry things bigger than her size, why can't she? So off she went, back to her house, and tried carrying her Grandpa!! Oh! but she could not!! But Why?....she wonders aloud! Oh little girl! Ants and humans have different body structure. Ants have thick muscles with a greater cross-sectional area relative to their body size compared to other bigger animals. And so ants can carry up to 50 times their body weight because their muscles can bear! but ours can't!!
author: Shital Choudhary
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Alison Byrnes; Anushruti Ganguly; Deepa Balsavar; Henu; Maya  Ramaswamy

title: The Jhula Park
text: Mamma, can I go to the Jhula Park? Jhula Park, I asked? Where is that Chiara? Oh mamma, where I go and play with the sand, hop on the see saws and slide down from the BIG slide. Oh, are you talking about the big park behind our home? No, no, mamma, it is not big park, it is Jhula Park. But, why do you call it the Jhula Park, Chiara? Because, mamma, the Jhula Park has one BIG 'JHULA FRIEND'. Come, come, I will show you from the window. Can you see there, mamma? So many friends play and sit together on the Jhula and have fun. You can make new friends on the Jhula Friend too. Wow!! Is that so? Yes!!! Eera and I sit on the Friend Jhula together. We spend so many hours on the Jhula. We share our snacks, we sing songs, we tell each other our school stories and we share our dolls too. We hold each other’s hand so that we do not fall off. We fight sometimes but we always say sorry and hug each other and become friends again. That is why we call it the JHULA PARK because it gives us new friends to love and care for and share with. We love our JHULA PARK. That is so nice! I also love your JHULA PARK, Chiara. Mamma, you are my best friend too. Come, we will go together and have fun with our Jhula Friend!
author: Charisma Hiranandani
illustrator: Bindia  Thapar; Jisha Unnikrishnan; Saloni Chopra; Suvidha Mistry; Zainab Tambawalla

title: 'A Memorable Party Last Night'
text: Jimmy was an adventurous dog. One night he did not feel sleepy. He started roaming around the village. Suddenly he saw a light coming from between the leaves from the forest. Jimmy follows the light and runs towards the forest. While he was walking in the forest searching for the light, Jimmy saw a round creature hiding behind the clouds giving out the light. The creature was starring at him. Jimmy got scared and asked "Who are you?Are you going to shoo me away?". The creature said "No, not at all, Don't be scared". They introduced themselves to each other, then the moon said "Jimmy, would you like to play with me?" Jimmy said sadly "But if I play with you, I won't be able to sleep and tomorrow I will not be able to play with my other friends" "That will not be a problem, you can sleep later" requested the moon." That is a good idea, I will play for a little while" thought Jimmy and agreed to play with the moon. "Come with me " said the moon. While they were walking through the forest, Jimmy spotted a very funny looking creature. "Who are you?" asked Jimmy. "Hoot Hoot" said the creature "I am Jolly the Owl, may I know who you are?". "I am Jimmy, I am moon's friend". '"Oh, that is nice" said Jolly They introduced themselves to each other. Now Jimmy had two friends Jolly and the moon. Suddenly he heard a sound. "Who was it?" thought Jimmy...... The creature hopped in front of them. Jimmy asked"Who are you?". The creature said"I am Tina the cricket, may I know who you are?". "I am Jimmy" said the dog. They introduced themselves to each other. Then suddenly Jimmy said, "Hey Tina, your voice is so sweet..... can you sing a song for me?". Tina said "Yes, why not". Tina started singing, it was a very melodious tune. Suddenly they were interrupted by a funny looking creature. "Who are you and what are you doing here?"asked Jimmy curiously. "I am Bobby the fox, may I know who you are?" said the creature. " I am Jimmy"said the dog. They introduced themselves to each other. Just then two more friends came. "Hello Vicky the bat and Shiny the glow worm" said Jimmy. "Hello my dear friends" said Vicky. Bobby said surprised "You know them already, Jimmy?". "Yes, of course" said Jimmy. "As everyone have come here, Let's party". said Jimmy. They were all dancing, singing songs and enjoying the party. "Oh, I'm very late and what if mamm saw me out?" thought Jimmy." Bye friends, meet you next time" said Jimmy "Farewell"said the friends and Jimmy ran through the forests and reached his house. He yawned and snuggled close to his mamma and went into a deep sleep......
author: shreya sreerekha
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Ant and the Green Mung Bean
text: One day, an ant went looking for food. She found a sprouted green mung bean in the kitchen. The ant tried to pick up the green mung bean. It was very heavy. The ant then started to pull it to take it home. Her home was far away. On her way home, someone had left a tap open. Water was flowing from it. The tiny ant thought it was a river! Somehow, she crossed it. Her home was very far away. Then the ant saw a bucket. She held on to the green mung bean and tried to climb it. She tried hard but she kept slipping down. Soon another ant came up to her. They talked to each other. Now, they both went around the bucket while pulling the green mung bean. Further ahead, a woman was cleaning her house. Swoof! The ant fell to one side and the green mung bean fell on the other. The ant ran to get her green mung bean. Her home was still very far away. Next, the ant came close to a sleeping dog. The dog sneezed loudly! The green mung bean rolled off near the dog’s mouth. The ant carefully went near the dog. The dog opened one eye and looked at the ant. The ant took the green mung bean and began walking. Her home was very far away. Close by, a chick was pecking on some grains. It saw the green mung bean and tried to peck on it. Ah, now my green mung bean is gone, thought the ant sadly. Just then, the chick’s mother called out from under the papaya tree. Cluck! Cluck! Cluck! The chick left the green mung bean behind, and ran towards its mother. Once again, the ant picked up the green mung bean and started walking home. Her home was still... Oh, it was right in front of her now! Do you know your beans? The ant in this book found a green mung bean with a sprout. Sprouted beans are very good for our health. We can make sprouts with pulses like rajma, chickpea, black gram and horse gram. Bean Games Get to know the different kinds of pulses by playing this game with your friends. Ask an adult to give you different kinds of pulses from your kitchen, like chickpea, rajma, toor dal, soy bean, mung bean and peas and learn their names. Put them all in one bowl. Blind-fold one person. She has to feel the pulses and guess the name. See how many she gets right. Another way to play this game is to make all the players close their eyes. Then, everyone tries to separate the different kinds of pulses into different groups.
author: Aditi Sarawagi

title: Angry Akku
text: When the last school bell rang, all the children laughed and screamed with joy. All, except Akku. Akku was ANGRY! "Akku! Akku! Look at the pretty sunflowers!" said Appa, as they rode through a field. "GRRMPH! They’re TOO YELLOW! They’re making my eyes hurt!" said Akku. "Akku! Akku! Look! Look at all the monkeys!" said Appa, pointing at the roof of their house. "CHEEE!" said Akku. "SHOOO! Go AWAY! SHOOO!" "Here, drink some buttermilk," said Appa. "It’ll cool you down." "HRRRM!" said Akku. "I DON’T WANT ANY!" "Try a sip, at least?" "OKAY! FINE!" said Akku, and tried a sip. It wasn’t all that bad. She had another sip. And another. In no time, the glass was empty. "Would you like a vada?" asked Appa. "FFEHH!" said Akku. "Just one little bite?" "Okay, FINE!" said Akku, and took a bite. It was quite good. She took another bite. And another. In no time, the plate was empty. "Good girl," said Appa. "Now will you tell me why you’re so angry?" "NO!" said Akku. "Was it something I did?" "NO!" "Was it something Amma did?" "NO!" "Did something bad happen in school today?" "MAYBE!" "Oho." "Would you like to draw it?" asked Appa. "Here’s a nice sheet of paper and some crayons." "Okay, FINE!" said Akku. Akku drew a brick… "This is the STUPID BRICK that I tripped over this morning," said Akku. "You’re right. That IS a VERY STUPID brick!" said Appa. And Akku drew a boy… "This is Bikku, a VERY BAD BOY! He laughed when I fell down!" said Akku. "You’re right," said Appa. "He shouldn’t have laughed at you." And Akku drew an idli… "This is my idli," said Akku. "It fell out of my lunch box when I tripped over the STUPID BRICK!" And Akku drew a crow… "This is the VERY BAD CROW that flew off with my idli," said Akku. "The crow must have been very hungry," said Appa. And Akku drew her teacher… "This is my teacher, Amala Miss," said Akku."She helped me up when I fell down. And then she hugged me." "That’s nice of her," said Appa. "And then she pinched my cheeks. I DON’T LIKE IT when my cheeks are pinched." "Oho! That must have HURT, no?" "A little bit. But I’m okay now." "That’s good." "See how well you draw, Akku?" said Appa. "You’re a real artist! Will you draw something for Amma too?" "OH-kay!" said Akku, and started drawing some more. "This is a little white mouse… and this is a boat… and this is a coconut tree…" "And this is a sunflower… and this is your cycle, Appa… and this is a dog… and this is a frog…" In no time, Akku had forgotten all about the STUPID BRICK that made her trip and fall. And about the BAD BOY who laughed at her. And about the IDLI-STEALING CROW. And Akku even forgot about being ANGRY. 10 Things to Do If You Feel ANGRY like Akku: 1. Laugh loudly and jump around with your arms in the air! 2. Slowly – very, very slowly – breathe in, and breathe out! 3. Drink some water! Or buttermilk! 4. Eat a piece of fruit! Or a vada! 5. Tell a grown-up about how you’re feeling! 6. Write about how you’re feeling! 7. Draw it out! Paint it! 8. Play with a pile of clay! 9. Make up a song about your anger! Sing it aloud! 10. Dance like a monkey!
author: Vinayak Varma

title: happy family.

title: Kalu becomes White.
text: Tina had a friend. It was a small black ant. His mother called him Kalu because he was so black. They lived under a big jamun tree in Tina's garden. But Kalu was sad because he was black. So one day he stole a cake of white paint from Tina's colour box. He rubbed it all over his body and turned white. When Kalu returned home and knocked on the door. His mother opened the door but thought Kalu was some one else."Who are you? You are not my Kalu?"she said. "Yes mom! It is me Kalu!" he cried. His mother looked at him for a long time and then dragged him under the shower. Poor Kalu! He changed into black again. He cried and cried and cried. His mother hugged him,kissed him and gave him a lump of sugar. Kalu came out to play with his friends Tina and Ratty and was happy and forgot about his dark skin.
author: Joysree Das

title: Friends
text: Munni and Sheela lived in their small village. Their village was very beautiful. They spent most of the time together playing games, enjoying each others company. They sang melodious songs and use to call their friends. And their best friends were birds and animals in their village. Singing use to make them feel very happy and energetic. All of their friends also enjoyed their songs and friendship. One day sheela got to know that Munni was going with her parents away from their village. She cried for many days. Sheela missed munni and their songs a lot looking through their picture. One day Sheela sat on her favourite tree singing her friends song. To her surprise munni sat with her on the tree and both of them sang together once again. Their joy came back to light and again their friends enjoed their friendship

title: The caterpillar who wanted to fly
text: There was a leaf and on that leaf was a tiny egg. A caterpillar cracked out of the egg. He was a tiny little caterpillar. He wiggled its body this way and then that way. He looked down. The ground was way, way down. Then he looked up. The sky was way, way up. He fell in love with the bright blue sky. He gazed up at the sky. He wanted to fly in the sky.. He longingly looked at the clouds floating up in the sky. He wanted to be like the clouds. He longingly looked at the birds flying up in the sky. He wanted to be like the birds. One, Two, Three. He leaped off from the leaf. Zoom and then splat, he plummeted straight to the ground. He was not hurt but he became sad that he couldn’t fly. And when he was sad, he ate a lot. Munch and crunch. Munch and crunch. He kept eating. A bright pink balloon with a long string attached at its end came floating by. One, Two, Three. The caterpillar leaped off and caught the balloon’s string. Zoom, Zoom he floated like the clouds in the sky. The caterpillar was happy. A bright pink balloon with a long string attached at its end came floating by. One, Two, Three. The caterpillar leaped off and caught the balloon’s string. Zoom, Zoom he floated like the clouds in the sky. The caterpillar was happy. Suddenly the balloon got caught in a rose bush. POP, the balloon burst. Zoom and then splat, the caterpillar plummeted straight to the ground. He was not hurt but he became sad that he couldn’t fly. And when he was sad, he ate a lot. Munch and crunch. Munch and crunch. He kept eating. A little boy was playing with paper planes. Vroom, Vroom went the paper planes. One, Two, Three The caterpillar leaped off and landed on the paper plane. Vroom Vroom, he glided in the sky. The caterpillar was happy. Suddenly the paper plane landed in a puddle. The paper plane got soaked. Splashed and drenched, the caterpillar made it back to the dry ground. He was not hurt but he became sad that he couldn’t fly anymore. And when he was sad, he ate a lot. Munch and crunch. Munch and crunch. He kept eating. A little girl with her father was flying a bright red kite. Whoosh, Whoosh flew the kite. One, Two, Three. The caterpillar leaped off and landed on the red kite. Whoosh, Whoosh.. he glided in the sky. The caterpillar was happy. Suddenly a strong wind blew and the kite got stuck in a tree. The kite was torn and was abandoned there. The caterpillar got tangled in the kite’s thread. A jingle here and a jangle there, he freed himself from the tangle. He was not hurt, but he became sad that he couldn’t fly anymore. And when he was sad, he ate a lot. Munch and crunch. Munch and crunch. He kept eating. The little caterpillar was not little anymore. He was a cute and fat caterpillar. But he was a sad caterpillar. He longingly looked at the clouds floating up in the sky. He longingly looked at the birds flying up in the sky. But now he wanted to hide from the clouds and the birds. So he built a thick cocoon around him and went to sleep. He dreamed about floating like the clouds. He dreamed of flying like the birds. He dreamed and dreamed and he lost track of time. A snooze here and a yawn there, he slept for a long, long time. One day the caterpillar cracked out of its thick cocoon. He wiggled his body this way and that way. POP and whirl Something had popped out of his body. He waited and waited to find out what it was. While he was waiting, He gazed up at the sky. He still wanted to fly in the sky. One Two Three Four little yellow wings had stretched out. He leaped off from his cage. A flip and a flap, he fluttered in the sky. The little boy said, “Ah, look at this magnificent butterfly”. The little girl said, “Ah, look at how high the butterfly flies”. The caterpillar realized he had turned into a butterfly. He was happy for he could now fly in the sky. And he mumbled to himself “The wait was not bad after-all”.
author: Gowri Nagarajan
illustrator: Bulbul Sharma; Gita V. Reddy; Gowri Nagarajan; Greystroke; Jeyanthi Manokaran; Muniza Shariq; Niloufer Wadia; Nina Sabnani; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Priya Kuriyan; ramesh s; Rijuta Ghate; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Tanvee Nabar; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Bee-Not-So-Busy
text: All day long the Busy-Bees flew from hive to flower and back to hive, gathering pollen and nectar. Their wings beat so fast that they caused a buzz! “Look at us! We’re humming with activity!” they sang. Bee-Not-So-Busy was different from the other bees. “Why don’t bees enjoy the garden like the other insects?” she wondered. “I’ll leave the hive and live like the beetles and the butterflies, the ants and the grasshoppers!” she said. She saw a beetle on a leaf. She thought beetles were smart. Instead of gathering nectar and making honey, they ate the leaves on the plant. After dressing up in a beetle suit, she flew down beside the beetle. Bee-Not-So-Busy took a big bite and almost vomited. “Yuck! This leaf tastes horrible!” She flew to a flower and sipped some nectar and felt better. “I’ll live like a butterfly. They sip nectar but don’t work like bees.” “They fly over flowers before choosing one. They don’t rush at all. And they don’t hum.” “They have so much fun!” Bee-Not-So-Busy found a bright and colorful butterfly costume. She had a nice day sipping nectar and flying among the flowers. By evening, she was tired. Like the other butterflies, she folded her wings and went to sleep under a leaf. Suddenly there was thunder and lightning. Thick drops of rain fell hard and fast. Bee-Not-So-Busy took shelter under a bunch of flowers. The flowers grew heavy with the rainwater. Bee-Not-So-Busy was scared she would drop into the puddle that had formed around the plant. The rain stopped after sometime. Bee-Not-So-Busy threw away the wet butterfly coat and rested on a stem. She saw ants rushing out of an anthill. “Our food is all gone! Our home is all wet!” they cried. Moths, beetles, butterflies, grasshoppers were all wet. They would have no food until the sun shone tomorrow. Bee-Not-So-Busy missed her dry, warm, and safe beehive. She was also hungry and longed for the food stored in the hive. There was honey and nectar and pollen in there. She shook herself dry and flew back to the hive. Bee-Not-So-Busy had a tasty meal. Happy to be back in her safe, warm, and dry home, she fell asleep. Early the next morning, she flew from flower to hive and back to flower. She worked all day long. Bee-Not-So-Busy had became a Busy-Bee.
author: Gita V. Reddy

title: ADVENTURES EVERYWHERE!
text: Zainab Tambawalla Adventures are fairytales They are not true, This is what people say today Because they have no clue! But adventures are magical, Every moment you might discover something new! After all, life is a fairytale too! An adventure can be anything new… Maybe a new book … A new school … Or a new chapter too! Every moment is an adventure if you want it to be Every thing can be done adventurously if seen from another angle Not every thing is discovered somethings we need to discover ourselves anew! And that is where the adventure starts! It might never last After all, adventures are not just about discovery But to quench the thirst of curious little hearts!

title: Animal Symphony
text: "Tweet-tweet,"sparrow chirps a happy song, even before the break of dawn. "Wake up, wake up, and sing your song; there is no way you can go wrong". "Eee Eee Eee", screeches monkey excitedly, swinging from tree to tree. "I love a good harmony-ee-eee; who will sing with me-ee-eee?" "Glug, glug, glug", bubble the fish in the sea, swishing their fins merrily, "we'll add depth to your melody". "Ribbit-ribbit," croaks frog from the field, catching his breath between leaps, "Give me a minute; and I shall sing my bit, ribbit-ribbit." "Sssssss," hisses snake, slithering past, making an s-shaped path in the grass, "If I could do only one thing, I would choose to sss-sss-sss-sing". "Mooooooo-ve!," low the cows in the street, the traffic jam is giving them restless feet, "We would love to get with the beat; music is a treat, even in the mid-day heat." "Cluck, cluck," tuts hen, picking up a pen, "I will get back to work on my lyrics then. I have been counting chickens, since goodness knows when." "Quack, Quack," grumbles duck, "I haven't had much luck, catching any fish today; I wonder where they play." 'Bzzzz-Bzzzz!' hums busy bumblebee, who has pollen stuck to his knee. "Don't you see, buzzing is my thing; I won't sting, unless you bother me." "Bow, wow, wow!," barks dog in glee; he is always game for company. "There's that sad cat in the tree; I wonder if she will sing with me?" "Meow-oow-oow", yowls cat in fright, she likes to get things just right, And dog's loud barks are way off-key, so she decides to flee. "Baa-ah", bleat the tired sheep, "We really need our beauty sleep. While half the world is counting sheep; how can we fall asleep?" "Who, who, whooo?", hoots owl, once the sun is fast asleep, and half the world is counting sheep. "Who-oo's awake to sing with me?" "Aaaaa-ooooooooo", deep in the woods, a lonely wolf howls back in tune, "I'll sing with you, from June to June, an ode to the beautiful moon." "Cheep-cheep, cheep-cheep," crickets chirp songs of peace, "as the night grows dark and deep, we'll lull the world to sleep-cheep-cheep". But though the night grows dark and deep, baby bear just won't sleep. So mama bear grrrr-rrrr-growls a lullaby, till he's snoring by her side. And so, from dawn to dusk and beyond, the animals practise their songs. And all you have to do is listen to hear the animal symphony loud and clear... Tweet Tweet Ee Eee glug glug mooo moooo ribbit ribbit sss sss bzzz bzzz cluck cluck quack quack bow wow meow meow cheep cheep baa baa hoo hoo aaaa ooooooo grrrrrr
author: Averil Nunes
illustrator: Amar Soni; Angie & Upesh; Archana Sreenivasan; Bindia  Thapar; Bulbul Sharma; Jagdish Joshi; Maya  Ramaswamy; Olivia Fraser; Ruchi Shah; Sangeetha Kadur; Sanjay Sarkar; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Suvidha Mistry; Zainab Tambawalla

title: A LITTLE ADVENTURE
text: M ini sat beside Bella her cow. "I feel bored,I want an adventure", she said. Then Bella spoke,"why don't you come with me and I will show you my friends!" First, Bella took Mini to her friend Lili the deer. "Hi" said the deer, "shall I show you a trick?" "Okay", said Mini, and so the deer jumped high over Mini's head and landed on the other side! "Wow, what a wonderful trick!", said Mini and she went off with Bella. Next, Bella took Mini to Rip the frog. "Hi", said Rip, "want to see a trick?" "Okay", said Mini, so the frog let out his long tongue and caught a fly with it, then went the tongue back into the frog's mouth. "That was not a very good trick", said Mini, "but it's nice" and she went off with Bella. It was getting hot, so Bella took Mini to a pond for a swim. In the pond there was a fish. "Watch me it said and blew a big bubble in the water. "Wow!", said Mini, then she heard Bella calling her. "Bye bye" she called and went off. "We have one last friend to meet", said Bella, "and that is Don the monkey" They soon reached. "where is he?", asked Mini, "i'm here", said a voice. Mini looked up and there was a monkey hanging upside down from one of the branches of a tree. Then she too climbed up and hung upside down. "This is fun! ", she said. "It's time to go now" said Bella after sometime. "Bye" said Mini as she walked with Bella home. "Did you enjoy today?" asked Bella. "Yes I did ", said Mini. "And I really liked the part when I hung from the tree with Don the monkey! " THE END!!!
author: Naomi Kamath

title: Kuki's Birthday Gift
text: It was Kuki’s birthday and she wanted a perfect gift. When a cat she wished to get, Grandma said, ‘No, Kuki, not a pet!’ When a doll she wanted to buy, Mother said, ‘You have too many already.’ Sigh! Not knowing what to do then, She went out into the garden. ‘What brings you here, Kuki?’ Gardener Uncle asked, Even as a squirrel and a cat scurried past. ‘It’s my birthday,’ she said, ‘I want a perfect gift, But I don’t have any.’ ‘Oh Kuki, you could get a sapling, And watch it grow into a tree.’ ‘Oh no, trees are so boring, They stand in one place all the time.’ ‘But trees are wonderful,’ Gardener Uncle said, ‘They’ll play with you and let you climb.’ ‘They change colours, if you know what I mean, Red and yellow, pink and purple...’ ‘Under the sun, they are golden green...’ ‘In the night, they are hardly seen.’ ‘Some are tall, some so small, Laden with fruits and flowers that fall.’ ‘Birds love them and you will too, Trees are better than the world’s best doll.’ And so, in the evening, Kuki’s mother brought home many saplings. One for Kuki, and the rest for her friends. While giving them the saplings, Kuki told her friends, ‘They help you breathe and leave you never, These are the only gifts that can stay forever!’ ‘Oh, trees are such magical living things!’
author: Nalini Ramachandran
illustrator: Archana Sreenivasan; Greystroke; Kruttika Susarla; Nimret Handa; Priya Kuriyan; Vinayak Varma

title: Everyone has a right to a bath
text: Krishnan Mrs Earthworm is angry. She is fed up of being covered in mud and never being able to have a proper bath. She insists that her husband install a bathtub with running water. The bathtub is easy to make. Mr Earthworm finds an old flower pot lying in the kitchen garden. He patches up the few holes and some gaps. And it’s done! The installation of running water at their home was quite another thing. The first attempt was with straws connected to the surface. But the flow was too weak and during heavy rains the mud rose obstructing the mouth of the pipes. He improved his device by connecting a garden hose directly onto a drainpipe. The flow was absolutely satisfactory. But this water was not suitable for Mrs Earthworm. She finds that it had too much residue, is not clear enough and does not smell good. There was another more important problem that dampened Mrs Earthworm's craving for a bath - the temperature. The water is too cold! Mr Earthworm got back to work and added a filter and a handmade water heater. Now it’s perfect. Mrs Earthworm can finally relax in the bath that she so wanted.
author: Pallavi  Krishnan

title: A little pet for Chitti and Chinni
text: Chitti and Chinni were twins. It was their sixth birthday. They were happy and excited because amma and appa had promised to buy a pet for them. "Will it be a parrot?" wondered Chitti. "But parrots are meant to fly Chitti," replied Chinni. "A rabbit?" Chinni said with sparkling eyes. "How about a dog?" said Chitti. The twins danced round and round thinking of their pets. They kept singing whatever came out of their mouth. " Our dear little friend is coming Is coming from the pet shop" Amma was cooking delicacies for the special day. She too seemed to be excited about the pets and sang along. " Our dear little friend is..la la la" In the evening, appa came home with a big box. When he opened, there was no parrot or rabbit or a dog but a fish bowl with three beautiful fish. Chitti held amma's sari tightly and stood with her mouth wide open. 'Amma knew what was going to come. Why didn't she tell us?' she thought. But did Chinni keep quiet? No. Not at all. She cried and cried. A little later, appa said, "Chitti, Chinni, you are too little to take care of big pets. On your next birthday, you will get a bigger pet. I promise. Now you take care of these fish. See to it that they don't cry and change the water every three days." The twins looked at amma who lovingly said, "They are great pets. I'm sure you'll like them girls." They thought amma was happy that she didn't have to invest time in taking care of big pets. For three days, Chitti and Chinni didn't go near the fish bowl. Finally, on the fourth day, they stood near the fish bowl and looked at each other. It was time to change the water. But the gold fish was trying to say something. It swam around and came back peering at the girls. It seemed like it was trying to talk to the twins. Chitti and Chinni looked into the glass bowl. What they saw was amazing! There was a tiny little baby fish, 'the fry' inside. They would have cleaned the bowl without noticing. They had saved a baby fish. They were so glad. When amma and appa came to know, they too were happy. Since then, Chitti and Chinni took care of the fishes and loved them.
author: Leena Satuluri

title: Pintu's new buddy
text: Pintu has found a new buddy for his lunch time. Is he Chintu??.. No!! Tinku??.. No!! Pinku??.. No!! Is his new buddy his Teddy??.. No!! Then who is this new buddy? It’s his Mumma’s phone. OFF or ON. It’s always in his hands. He plays games or watches video takes photos and listens to the radio. BUT!! Why is he not holding the phone today? Is it broken? or Mumma has taken? What happened? Aha!! The phone is charging!! Phone battery had come to margine. Ammm!! Huhhh!! Awww!! What can be done without phone? Mumma is busy. Pappa is snoring. Friends went for fizzy. It’s very boring. Wait!! Mumma is getting something That looks great!! Mumma takes out a story book from a box. Pintu takes a look at the story of GRAPES and A FOX. There is also a story of A MOUSE and THE LION KING, Pintu finds the book very interesting. Pintu loves his new buddy, the Book. It will never leave him for fizzy nor will ever go dizzy. Pintu wants to read. Now, mumma’s phone is of no need. Pintu asks mumma to give more, mumma gives him BOOK of animals which roar. Pintu is very happy, asking for still more. Mumma gives him many books. BOOKS of flowers, BOOKS on plants, BOOKS about birds and BOOKS of daily chores. Pintu forgot the phone. Now, he just reads on and on. Colour the picture and enjoy the story.
author: Riddhi Nath
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Angie & Upesh; Delwyn Remedios; Kavya Singh; Lavanya Karthik; Natasha  Mehra; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Riddhi Nath; Santosh Pujari; Suvidha Mistry

title: Balakhani-imitated mumu
text: Prakash' There was a mumu. He went on the pond There a girl was running a boat. Two ducks were floating. Only then did his mother come to the shore. "I can also swim in the water," Mumu asked. "If you come swimming you can swim. The duck's mother said. Mumu ran and jumped into the water. She did not swim. He started drowning in water. '' Help! Save! '' He started shouting loudly. All the ducks ran into the water. Having left Mumu with water, came out. Since then Mumu has stopped copying. Now do it - Fill the color you want in the picture of Mumu. Then show to the teacher and the teacher.
author: Omprakash Kshatriya  'prakash'  ओमप्रकाश  क्षत्रिय 'प्रकाश'

title: A (Eeek) Visitor
text: “Eek- eek-” the sound came again. But, mother continued to sing a lullaby to get Pinky to go to sleep. Pinky lied quietly in mother’s lap with her sleepy- half shut eyes and smile on her face. House was all at peace, so Pinky could have her nap. “ Tip-tap, Tip-tap ” a sound of quiet footsteps was heard. Mother got scared. Who could be there? Pinky’s father went to scout. The maid also left the house. “Khannn- khatt”, now came the sound of plate. Pinky was now fast asleep. Mother feared even to flip. “Let me go and see!” Mother thought once. “What if there is a thief and give my head a hit?” Mother’s mind was full of thoughts. She made Pinky sleep on the bed carefully, and rose silently to see outside the room. Mother, quietly, closed the bedroom door and peeped outside. Nothing was seen. Slowly, she came out of the door and guess, what was on the floor?? Half eaten mangoes and lentil sprouts lied all over the floor!!! Mother ran into the kitchen. “huff! No thief, no kitten!” She sighed and came out to the hall. Her eyes fixed at the balcony. Whom did she see there? It had a large sized, hairy grey body and a tail. It had a black Hanuman like face and ears. It had long black paws. It was sitting there with all his comfort with very innocent but naughty eyes. What was it? A MONKEY!! It was sitting on the balcony railing holding its dark grey tail. “ Eek-eek ” the monkey made the sound once more while jumping into the neighbour’s open door.

title: Ants' Defence
text: The Ants' Defence Written & Illustrated By: Anam Fathima Produced By: Al Qamar Academy Contact: Al Qamar Academy 14, Kalyani Nagar, Opposite Journalists’ Colony Kottivakkam, Chennai 600041 Ph: 044 24511226/ 9677019226 info@alqamaracademy.in An Al Qamar Trust publication. Al Qamar Academy is a micro school in Chennai, India. As an alternative school, Al Qamar focusses on inculcating curiosity, enabling real learning and developing a social conscience in children. The school constantly innovates in its pedagogical delivery. The school was founded by IIT’ian Hauroon Jamal and Aneesa Jamal. This book is an outcome of a bookmaking workshop at Al Qamar Academy followed by three one-to-one mentoring sessions for the young authors conducted by renowned conservation educator and nature photographer K. Ramnath Chandrasekhar. The storytelling module used by him during the sessions were designed for Karthavyam, an initiative on public-problem solving. DEDICATION For my family, friends and teachers. Hi! I’m Meela and I’m the Queen’s helper. I'm so lucky to be one! I love the Queen very much. And I couldn't let anybody hurt her. Now, I’ll show you around the house and its dangers. Our house is on top, or rather inside a hill called the Anthill. No wonder we ants live there. We have four rooms. One is the Baby Room. The other – the Queen’s Room. The third is the Working Room. The last is the Seed Room. We used to do gardening too in our Anthill!! Sometimes the plants used to grow bigger than us. But lately no plants are growing due to something called “Pollution” caused by our unfriendly neighbours – the Evil Scientists. They had dumped some smelly stuff called trash in front of our house for us to starve. Now we are trapped unless somebody can float through that trash… Meanwhile, unknown to the other ants, the evil scientists had found a hidey hole and had come to capture Queen Anty, who had been left unguarded. We ants were still discussing the Problem about being trapped and no plants growing business. “Who can float through trash?” “I bet I know the answer who! Queen Anty of course!” “How come we never thought of it?” said Golu, one of the ants. We went to Queen Anty’s chamber (room). We sighed with relief for there had been no one to guard Queen Anty as they usually did. At first, everything looked perfect. Or so we thought! Then a wise Ant said: “Be careful O youngsters! You will indeed not be satisfied by just guessing, O young Ants! There are drops of blue blood. I foretell you the humans have come!” And with that he went off. Queen Anty was missing! We panicked. “Maybe the Evil Scientists kidnapped her!” “Oh dear! Maybe we can follow the men” suggested Artilla, a young ant. “But how will we? Have you forgotten about us being stuck in the trash?” someone asked. "Oh, I haven’t thought of that!” said Artilla. “Well, what about digging?” she asked. “We can call the gardener ants to help us. They’re good diggers.” And at last when the gardener ants were finished digging, we went out. Aaah! How fresh the air felt. But the soldiers made us march on. We were following the evil men. We continued following the men. We enjoyed the beautiful scene. But we couldn’t see properly because the soldiers urged us on if we stopped. At last we reached there – by sliding on rainbows and floating on clouds. We reached the scientists’ lab and searched everywhere for Queen Anty and found her behind a trapdoor with many other animals. When we were at the doorway the men appeared. The soldiers and the Queen fought with the Evil Scientists and captured them. But there was only one problem – we had followed the men. Thus we did not know the way back. Luckily for us, we had an ant known as Hashrim, who wrote everything down. Normally we would have called him foolish, but now we didn’t. We followed the instructions and came back home. And fixed our home and lived happily ever after. MESSAGE TO THE READER People who dump garbage should realise that they are harming the environment – including ants, earthworms and other insects. AFBN stands Anam Fathima Binte Naveeth Ahmed. Anam studies in Grade 4 in Al Qamar Academy. She likes reading, writing, craft work and taking care of pets. She loves her two pet parrots very much.
author: Anam Fathima

title: Pure Happiness
text: Buzzzzz......Buzzzzz......Grrrmmmppp.....Grrrmmmppp. "Oh this old fridge is yet again making these funny and irritating sounds. It is getting so difficult to concentrate on my homework." said eight-year old Munira covering her ears with her hands. The fridge in their house was almost twice as old as her, but mother was not ready to discard it even though it made loud sounds all day and night long. Munira went out to find her mother. She saw her mother outside the house buying vegetables from Kamal Uncle, the vegetable vendor who came every evening to their colony. He was a very friendly man. On seeing Munira, he called her, "Hello Munira bitiya. How are you?" "I am fine uncle. How are you and your daughter Shyama?" "All fine bitiya. I will come tomorrow morning with Shyama. You can meet her then." At night Munira was having dinner with her parents with the buzzing sound from the fridge in the background. Munira complained yet another time about the noisy fridge. But this time instead of getting upset about the fridge, mother announced that she had decided to discard the fridge and buy a new one. Munira's happiness knew no bounds. She was already planning which brand to buy. Ding Dong...Ding Dong... In the morning, at around ten, the doorbell rang. Munira, as usual, ran to open the door. It was Kamal Uncle, the vegetable vendor, along with his daughter Shyama. Behind them, just outside the house, Munira saw Kamal Uncle's hand cart. But it did not have any vegetables on it. It was empty. She noticed that Shyama appeared extremely excited as if looking for something. She welcomed them inside the house. "Hello Kamal ji and Shyama. Please come inside. I have already cleaned and kept the fridge ready for you to take it. We shall be going to the market today to order a new one." Shyama came inside and touched mother's feet and thanked her for the fridge. She then came near the squeaking fridge, which seemed excited too. The fridge made rat-like noises as if welcoming its new owners. Shyama then ran to have a look at the fridge. She examined the fridge inside out and looked happily at her father. Kamal ji patted her head with a smile on his face. Surprisingly, both Kamal ji and Shyama did not mention the sounds coming from the fridge but kept thanking mother for it. Mother unplugged it and asked them to load it on the empty cart. Shyama helped Kamal ji to carry the frigde outside the house. With a little help from father, they loaded it onto the cart. Shyama too climbed on the cart and sat near the fridge holding it tightly. With a delightful smile on her face they left. Munira kept looking at them from the window till they reached the other end of the street. Suddenly mother came and stood besides her. "Mummy, How come shyama was so happy with the noisy fridge?" Mother smiled at her innocence and said,"Munira beta, for her having the fridge was a luxury and was equal to happiness. She did not notice the noise because she thought of keeping her father's unsold vegetables in it so that they remained fresh. Or may be she noticed but decided to ignore it because of the utility for them." Munira had a puzzled look on her face. Mother stroked her hand lovingly on Munira's head and said,"Always remember my dear that happiness lies in our thoughts and not in the material possessions. While I was buying vegetables, Kamal ji told me about Shyama's thoughts and that was when I decided to give away the fridge to them. For us it had become a noisy old machine but for them it was pure happiness."
author: Neha Modi

title: TRUE FRIENDS
text: TRUE FRIENDS Written & Illustrated By: Author Name Produced By: Al Qamar Academy Contact: Al Qamar Academy 14, Kalyani Nagar, Opposite Journalists’ Colony Kottivakkam, Chennai 600041 Ph: 044 24511226/ 9677019226 info@alqamaracademy.in An Al Qamar Trust publication Al Qamar Academy is a micro school in Chennai, India. As an alternative school, Al Qamar focusses on inculcating curiosity, enabling real learning and developing a social conscience in children. The school constantly innovates in its pedagogical delivery. The school was founded by IIT’ian Hauroon Jamal and Aneesa Jamal. This book is an outcome of a bookmaking workshop at Al Qamar Academy followed by three one-to-one mentoring sessions for the young authors conducted by renowned conservation educator and nature photographer K. Ramnath Chandrasekhar. The storytelling module used by him during the sessions were designed for Karthavyam, an initiative on public-problem solving. FOR MY DEAR FAMILY Tuesday 2nd June “I'm late for my art class,” Divya shouted. She rushed down and took her paint and colours. She reached but class had already started. After two hours of class she came back home. Divya quickly ate dinner and went off to sleep, so that she could wake up for school early the next day. Wednesday 3rd June Divya was early to school. She reached before everyone. She saw a new girl in class. Divya was surprised. She asked the new girl her name. “I'm Afra. Who are you?” she asked “I’m Divya.” They both shook hands. The first class started. It was English. They got their exam papers back. Divya had scored the highest marks. Thursday 4th June At lunch break, Afra saw she had lemon rice which she had not eaten for breakfast. When she opened it there was a foul smell. Afra knew it was rotten, but she ate it, because she was afraid her mom would scold her if she didn’t finish her lunch. In class Afra felt hot, dizzy and sick. The teachers took her to the doctor. The doctor said she had eaten rotten food and was sick. She’d better go home. Mom was very sad when Afra reached home. Friday 5th June The next day Divya saw that Afra hadn’t come to school and she got worried. She called Afra after school and asked, “Afra why didn’t you come to school today?” Afra replied “Oh! it was because I had high fever.” “Are you better now?” “Yeah! I'm fine.” They talked for about half an hour. Saturday 6th June Divya was bored at school, because all her best friends - Anjali, Rasha and Afra were absent. After going home, she put on her favorite shirt and track pants. Then she went to Afra’s house. Afra was there lying on the bed. Her mom was very worried, because she had high fever and was very sick. Monday 8th June Afra got sicker. Her family took her to the hospital. The doctor was in a hurry. The hospital put her in the ICU and took many tests. After two hours the Doctor came out “We can’t do any thing.” Afra was unconscious. Her family took her home. Tuesday 9th June Doctors in other hospitals saw Afra. They said the same thing. One doctor finally diagnosed her disease as “Doonfur”. Now Afra’s Mom was very worried wondering if Afra’s life was at risk. Divya said, “Why don’t we ask for help?” “What kind of help?” Suddenly there was a knock at the door. It was Rasha! “Why don’t we get help from the government?” Divya said, “Ok we can do that.” “We will write a letter to the government.” Wednesday 10th June To, The Health Department, Government of Tamil Nadu,, 2nd Main Road, Nugambakam, Chennai 600034 10th June 2016 Dear Sir, Our friend is sick. She has fever and a new disease called ‘ DOONFUR’. Please help in any way you can. Yours sincerely, Divya AFTER A WEEK........ Thursday 17th June There was a reply letter from the Government. Everyone gathered in Afra’s house to look what reply was. Divya read it aloud to everyone. Dear Divya and friends, We will try to help you. Come to this address and then I will tell you something which will be a little bit relief for your friend. Sincerely, Krishna Kumar Health officer Friday 18th June Rasha and Divya checked the address and went to the Health Office. They went in and met the officer. He introduced himself to them, “Hi, I'm Krishna Kumar. This is Dr. Rafi. He will help you.” Saturday 19th June Dr. Rafi said “Please consult my friend, Dr. Shah in Maharashtra. He has the medicine for the disease your friend has. He works in a health clinic. If you need help call him at this number.” Sunday 20th June Divya and her friends reached Maharashtra. They went to the health clinic. It was huge. They met Dr. Shah. He had a big can with red liquid medicine. The doctor took a small bottle, poured in the red liquid medicine and gave it to them. He said “This is the medicine for Doonfur. It may take your friend more than a week to get well.” Monday 21st June Back again in Chennai, Divya and Rasha went straight to Afra’s house to give her the medicine. Afra’s mom felt hopeful and thought her daughter would get well. After a week… Monday 28th June Afra woke up and blankly asked, “ Why am I not going to school?” Her mom told her everything she had gone through in the past few days. Divya and Rasha told the hospitals and clinics that Afra got well because of they got the new medicine. They gave them the contact number of Dr. Rafi and Mr. Krishna Kumar. Afra went back to school again. She looked as if she had not gone to school for a year. Everyone thanked Dr. Rafi and Mr. Kumar. ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS I thank Ram Uncle for helping and inspiring me to write a wonderful story. I thank Mrs. Nazreen Sheriff for helping me correct my errors and guiding me through the whole story. I thank Mrs. Aneesa Jamal for encouraging me to join the class and finish my work in time. I thank my friends Zaynab and Safaa for helping me finish my story. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Aayshah Maseerah studies in Grade 6 at Al Qamar Academy. She lives in Chennai with her mother, father and brother.
author: Aayshah Maseerah

title: A Special Journey
text: Deepu loves to play with his toy engine. It is blue and yellow, and has eight wheels. Last year, Deepu went to Chennai by a fast train. The engine went BAAAAM, the coaches went THUD THUD, the people went CHATTER CHATTER... It was so much fun! Ah! Deepu was waiting for his next trip by train. He wanted to sit in a real train again. It was Saturday. Amma had gone out to meet a friend. Appa and Deepu were at home. Deepu was playing with his toy engine. Appa was reading the newspaper. Suddenly, Appa had an idea. He asked, "Deepu, shall we go to the railway station?" "YES!" answered Deepu, jumping up and down happily. Appa and Deepu went to the small railway station nearby. On the platform, a red train zoomed past them. SWISSSSH... Deepu shouted with joy, "Train, train!" It was the fast train from Delhi. It did not stop at the station. Then a blue train chugged into the platform. PHISSSSH... It stopped. A few people got off the train. The guard waved a green flag. BAAAAM... shouted the engine. And PHISSSSH... the train started moving. "Bye-bye train!" shouted Deepu. Appa had another idea. He held Deepu's hand and went to the ticket counter. "Where are we going?" asked Deepu. "Shhh..." whispered Appa. "I have a surprise for you." At the ticket counter, Appa bought tickets for City railway station. Appa and Deepu walked back to the platform and waited. Soon a blue train stopped at the station. PHISSSSH... Appa said, "Come, Deepu. Let's get in." Deepu's eyes were wide open now. "Really, Appa? Where are we going?" he asked. "On a train ride," said Appa. "But we don't have any luggage. We have not told Amma," said Deepu. Appa laughed. "It is a short journey, Deepu. A special one, just for you. We will be back soon." "YIPPEEE!!!" shouted Deepu. He was so excited. He was going on a real train journey again. He had waited for a long time. They entered the train and found two empty seats. Deepu sat near the window. He was very happy. BAAAAM... shouted the engine. PHISSSSH... the train started. THUD THUD... the coaches moved along the tracks. CHATTER CHATTER... the people in the train spoke loudly. Deepu looked out at the green fields, pink houses and tall trees. Black smoke rose from a factory. A cow was munching on some grass. "MOOOO...", shouted Deepu. Another train passed them. ZOOOOM... Deepu waved to the people in the other train. The sun shone brightly in the blue sky. Birds were flying in search of food. "I am flying," thought Deepu, as the train moved fast. THUDTHUD THUDTHUD THUDTHUD... the train crossed a bridge over a river. After some time, the train started slowing down. It was entering City railway station. PHISSSSH... it stopped at the platform. Deepu and Appa got off the train. "Thank you for the surprise, Appa. It was so much fun!" said Deepu. City railway station was crowded. Deepu held Appa's hand tightly. Many trains were waiting at the station. Trains to Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Goa... Travellers were in a hurry. " Kaapi, kaapi... chai, chai..." cried the vendors. Appa and Deepu returned home by auto. At home, Amma hugged Deepu and asked, "Where did you go?" "On a special journey," said Appa. "Very special," said Deepu, with a big smile. "Wow! You must tell me all about it," said Amma.
author: Anita Nagarajan
illustrator: Preeti Krishnamurthy; Priya Kuriyan; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Santosh Pujari

title: My Grandma has a tail.
text: MY GRANDMA HAS A TAIL. Have you met my Grandma? Everybody says my Grandma has a tail. The tail follows her all day long Mumma says it even does a pirouette when Grandma sings a song. I wonder, why haven't I seen it yet? Papa says the tail is growing long and tall, and it even answers Grandma's phone whenever she gets a call. What?! Why haven't I seen it yet? My teacher says the tail helps my Grandma a lot, it even helps her to water the plants in the pots. Sigh, I haven't seen it yet. Now I know why everybody says that my Grandma has a tail Because it was always ME following her on all her big, small trails. The bus driver told me the tail sits next to Grandma in the bus, and imitates everything that my Grandma does. I really wonder why haven't I seen it yet. So one day I asked Grandma, "Everybody says that you have tail But I always wonder why haven't I seen it yet?" Grandma laughed out loud and pulled out her phone, then she showed me pictures of her tail as we ate a bowlful of crunchy kale. Look! It's me in the pictures following her all day long and doing a pirouette when she sang my favourite song. It's me in the pictures growing all tall and answering her phone when she got a call. Now I know why everybody says that my Grandma has a tail, because it was always ME following her on all her big, small trails.
author: Gauri Dalvi

title: Everybody needs a hug.
text: EVERYBODY NEEDS A HUG. Last summer Eya brought Basil home from the farmer's market. This happy plant danced in the rain and smiled in sunshine. Eya remembered to water it every day. She sat next to it and read books. She sang to it. She hugged it. Basil gave Eya and her family many fresh pestos, a delicious crunch on their pizza and a distinct aroma around their little home. Eya grew taller and so did Basil. Soon, Eya got busier with school, her friends, the TV, her homework. But she never forgot to water Basil. One morning, the happy plant wasn't looking so happy anymore. It had started to droop. It looked sad. And that made Eya wonder. Mumma was noticing that Eya had started to water Basil a little extra every day but she had clearly forgotten something else. She had stopped reading to it. She had stopped hugging it. Basil was withering. It had stopped dancing in the rain. It had stopped smiling in the sunshine. That made Eya sad. There were no fresh pestos, no crunchy leaves on her pizza, no aroma around the house. So she asked Mumma. "Why is Basil not looking happy anymore?" "Aren't you forgetting something Eya?" Mumma asked. And gave her a tight hug. Eya remembered what she had been forgetting. She ran to Basil and gave it a mighty hug and sang to it really loud. Next day, Basil sprouted some tiny new leaves and once again danced in the rain, as Eya read her favourite story for the tenth time. That day Eya realised that some things are important and they must be done but there are some other things that are essential and cannot be forgotten, just like the hug.
author: Gauri Dalvi

title: DeeSy short stories 1: On a demonetized day...
text: As he approached the bank, he took out the notes of Rs. 1000 from his pocket, counted them and stuffed them in. Worried about his knee pain, he joined the long queue. Just then he saw a young man approaching him with a folding chair. “Many of the retired employees of our bank have come to help us with the demonetization work. We thought we would also do our bit to help the elderly”, he said. Sitting on the chair, he noticed the lady ahead of him in the queue struggling to hold her sleeping baby and his toys. He offered to hold the toys. After handing over the toys, she took out a banana and offered it to the small child holding hand of a man standing in ahead of her in the queue. While the child was happily eating the banana, his father had lent his power bank to a youngster ahead of him. As the battery of his discharged mobile phone started charging, the youngster explained to the aunty standing in front how to fill the demonetization form. Meanwhile, aunty lent her mobile phone to a young girl in front who was telling her parents that she couldn’t call as her phone had zero balance. After her call, she got to know that an elderly lady standing ahead of her wanted to go to the restaurant outside to take her medicines with food but feared that she would lose her place in the queue. The girl assured the lady that she would guard her place. The elderly lady nodded gratefully and stepped out. Outside the restaurant, a shabby child was explaining to his younger sister that he had only one note of Rs. 500 –his father’s daily wages. The elderly lady signalled to the restaurant manager that she would pay for the childrens’ food. The restaurant manager was approached by a tourist whose old notes of Rs. 500 he accepted. When the tourist rang up his home, his mother told him that she was going to the bank she retired from to help her younger colleagues with the demonetization work…
author: Dr. Deepti S.

title: Eyes to see, Teeth to bite, Lips to Kiss!!
text: Papa! Papa! My Kamali Mam told me to read the parts of the body and its functions...This is my book, papa! It's not very hard my child to read from the book. title: Ki-Ki ? - Parrot!
text: It was Sunday, Akil and Vardhan were playing on the ground. "My school friend taught me a new game", said Akil. Vardhan asked, "What's that?" title: Tina loves Laddoos
text: Once upon a time, there lived a girl called Tina. Tina was a very obedient and honest girl. She always told truth and never lied. Tina loved laddoos. Tina's maa made world's yummiest laddoos. Whenever Tina got good marks in tests at school or helped a person, Tina's maa would make laddoos for Tina. One day, Tina had a test at school. When leaving home for school in the morning, Tina's maa said- "All the best, Tina. Do well in your test. I will make laddoos for you because I know you will get good marks in the school test." Tina replied. "Thanks, maa. Yes, I will get good marks and then, come home and eat laddoos." After that, Tina goes to school and gives her test. When teacher gives back the checked papers, Tina finds that she did not get good marks. Tina becomes sad and goes home. She thinks, "Today, I will not get laddoos. Maa will become sad too because I did not get good marks." Now, Tina arrives home. Maa says, "Wash your hands, Tina and come, sit. I will bring laddoos." To which Tina replies, " No, maa. I will not eat laddoos because I got bad marks in the school test." Tina's maa smiles and gives Tina a laddoo to eat. Tina looks at her maa and maa says, "So what, if you got bad marks, at least you are honest. This laddoo is for your honesty."
author: Manpreet Kaur

title: The Tale of the Toilet
text: It’s a big job, it’s number one priority and number two is pretty important too, because you can never ignore nature’s call. So when you gotta go, you gotta go! Some people can do this business inside their houses, some have to go outside. Some pour water after it’s done, others need not. It’s different in different parts of the world, just as it was different at different times in history. Toilets of the past A very long time ago, more than 3,000 years ago, the people of Indus Valley had beautiful houses with toilets built inside them. People could finish their business in privacy and pour a bucket of water which would flush the waste down a drain. This way, they managed to keep their houses and streets clean. The Indus Valley, situated in present day Pakistan and India, is one of the three oldest civilizations that we know of, the other two being Ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. From what we can see of the ruins today, the people of Indus Valley had great building skills, were good at making metal and ceramic products, and planned their city-wide drainage systems very elaborately. Around the same time, similar toilet arrangements were present in other parts of the world. Homes in Egypt and Babylonia had toilets built in, and the ruins in Skara Brae in Scotland and the Minoan Crete in the Mediterranean show plenty of pipes leading out of what definitely seems like a toilet inside a house. A little later, about 2,000 years ago in Rome, people used public toilets. A long slab of stone had keyhole-shaped cuts at intervals. People would sit on these openings and do their toilet business while having a friendly chat with the person next to them. I told you it was a “public” toilet! How did they clean themselves, do you wonder? After I tell you, you might wish you had never wondered. They took a long stick that had a sponge attached to one end and dipped the sponge into water, and then used it to wipe their backsides. After they felt clean, they simply handed the stick over to their neighbour, who dipped it in water and used it again. Let me give you a friendly tip here – if you ever find yourself in this place, make sure you pick the very first seat! Not everyone had to poop in public in Rome. If you were super-rich, you would have a chamber pot at home into which you would do your business. Once done, you would simply empty the contents onto the street outside. And if someone happened to walk by at the time, well, too bad for them! About 500 years ago, Queen Elizabeth of England had a toilet constructed inside her house. It had a pipe leading out into a sewage pit outside. But she never used it much because the stench from the sewer filled the toilet and she could not even breathe. So back to the chamber pot she went. Toilets of the present Toilets these days don’t stink. How did they achieve that? In 1775, the English inventor Alexander Cumming figured out a way. Instead of using a straight pipe to connect the toilet to the sewage line, he made it S-shaped. This made sure that while poop and pee and water can go down the drain, no smell can come back up. Have you noticed that a little water always stays in the toilet even after flushing? This is what creates the "seal" and prevents the foul smell from entering the room through the drain. Just like olden times, different parts of the world today have different kinds of toilets. Some places don’t have toilets at all. Some toilets are made for sitting, some are made for squatting. Some have a bucket with water for flushing, others have a tank filled with water and a handle that releases the water. Some toilets have paper to wipe the backside, some have a tap or a bucket of water to wash up. There are some toilets that don’t use water at all. Like the ones on a plane. With all the turbulence, you certainly don’t want any water in the toilet bowl! The waste is removed by a powerful vacuum and stored in a tank below. After the plane lands, the waste is disposed of. There are also waterless toilets on the ground. They were designed and built for places without easy access to water, such as remote villages in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra. They have been working well, so wouldn’t it be a good idea to have such toilets everywhere? Because the less water we use, and the less sewage we create, the better for the planet, right? Toilets of the future How do you make a waterless toilet? The first step is to make sure that you don’t let the urine and the faeces mix. No it’s not as gross as it sounds – it just needs the pot to be designed in a clever way. Like having a sloping bamboo mat act as a sieve that will allow the waste water to pass through, but can hold the poop and send it to a different pit. Since urine by itself is not harmful (it’s only the bacteria that collect on open urine that cause the smell and the hazard), it can be safely let into the ground or put to use. Here’s how: Hydrogen can be separated from the urine and used to fuel a generator. Urine also has nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium that are great ingredients for fertilizers. Now that urine is taken care of, what do we do with the solid waste? Well, if it is properly mixed with ash and grass, and allowed to rest in a pit, millions of bacteria will break it down into perfectly useful compost for agriculture. These toilets will help us build a world where there is no "waste." Instead it is turned into something of use. If all houses in a city have such toilets, no sewage comes out of them, no expensive sewage treatment plants are necessary and no sewage will flow through the drains into lakes and rivers! What a great future for everyone! On pg 18 is a board game. You’ll need a few friends to play with and a die. Below are instructions on what to do if you land here: At 3 Queen’s chamber pot: Illegal use of Queen’s chamber pot. Punishment: Banished into her toilet for 2 turns. At 6 Roman toilet first seat: Good for you! First use of sponge! Move ahead 7 spaces. At 9 Stuck in the toilet queue! Move only if you roll a 2 or a 4. At 12 Roman toilet last seat: Yuck. Don’t want to use that sponge? Okay, we'll let you kill the time. Lose a turn. At 15 Mohenjo-daro: Congratulations! You have entered one of the best toilets of all time! So you get to roll the die again. If you roll 2,4,6 move that many spaces forward. If you roll 1,3,5 you can pick any pawn on the board (other than yours) and move it that many spaces back. At 19 Oops. Left the toilet dirty. Move back 3 spaces. At 21 Waterless toilet: Congratulations! You just used a waterless toilet! Take the short-cut! At 23 Flying waste! Oh dear! You got hit by flying waste! Move only if you roll a 1 or 6.

title: A Bigger and a Better Picture through my Grandma's spectacles
text: “Tinu, have you seen my spectacles?” asked my Grandma. “Grandma, your spectacles are on the table”, I replied. “Shhh....I’m going to wear them. Don’t tell her”, I whispered to Pupu*. I ran to my room to see how I looked in them. I see my Papa in the mirror. Grandma, do your spectacles make people big? I see a rainbow on my table with more than seven colors. Grandma, are your spectacles making me dream? I see Rumi and Satya come out from my story book to play with me. Grandma, do your spectacles do magic? I see my handwriting in my note book changing from small to big. Grandma, are your spectacles making things bigger? I see my car going as fast as other cars on the road. Grandma, do your spectacles make my things go fast? I see my little sister Anya laughing at me. Grandma, do your spectacles make others happy? I see bigger apples in my basket being given to some children on the street. Grandma, do your spectacles make us give big? I see Papa, Ma, Anya, Pupu and you so near to me. Grandma, do your spectacles make people closer to one another? “Grandma, can I wear your spectacles everyday?” I asked. "Why?" asked Grandma "Because I see a bigger and a better picture of everything", replied Tinu.
author: Toral Mehta

title: Snake and Sparrow
text: Tweety is a sparrow. She's a warm and loving soul. Everyone one calls her Sweety Tweety and loves playing with her. However, her best friend is a snake. His name is Vincent. This morning, Tweety's mom prepared her lunch seeds. There's bread beans. There's barley. there's sunflower seeds. There's sesame. Not to mention Tweety's favorite: corn and dry peas. "Tweety, remember, you can play with Teddy, you can play with Steed, you can play with Stripes, and you can play with Trunks." Tweet's Mommy pointed out. "But I don't want to see you playing with Vincent. He's a snake and snakes are very dangerous." Mommy reaffirms. "But Mommy, Vincent is my best friend. He always plays with me when all the other kids wouldn't," complained Tweety Tweety also added, "the other kids wouldn't play with me because they think i'm too small." "Vincent is nice Mommy. Why can I not play with him?" "Young Lady, there's a lot of things in life you don't understand yet." Mommy replies strongly. "Mommy knows what's the best for you so stop complaining, or I won't prepare corn and dry peas for you." Tweety tries to convince Mommy, "I don't want corn or dry seeds if I can't play with Vincent." "No, means NO!" Said Mommy. "But Dad~!" cried Vincent. Vincent's Daddy strongly rejected, "No But's!" "I don't want you to play with Tweety. You can play with Teddy, you can play with Steed, you can play with Stripes, and you can play with Trunks. But I don't want you to ever play with Tweety." "But Dad, Tweety is my best friend." Vincent argues. "What did I just say? No But's, Tweety is too differnt" and that was the end of the conversation. "My Mommy is still as stubborn as always." At the play ground. Tweety explained what happened earlier today to Vincent. "She thinks you are dangerous, but i know would never do anything to hurt me." Vincent agrees, "my said we're different as well, but I don't think there's that much of a difference." "Yeah, that's what I think," Mr. E said as he overheard their conversation. Vincent thought to himself, "Daddy never listens to me. What can I do to convince him that Tweety is a Sweety." "I know Daddy wants me to be strong and vicious, but if being like Daddy means that I can't play with Tweety, then I don't want to be like Daddy." This has gone on for some time now. Vincent's Daddy and Tweety's Mommy never liked each other, but Vincent and Tweety are friends for life. If only there's a way to convince them. Mr. E is incredibly good with remembering and that's why he's their Math teacher. "I think you guys should make a pie chart." "I love pie!" Tweety exclaimed excitedly. "But I don't know how that will help." "No, no, a pie 'chart'. This is what a pie chart looks like." Mr E. then drew a chart with some crayons on the floor. "Now, you guys look differently, you guys walk differently,, and you guys eat differently." Mr. E. explained as he drew on the paper. "I guess we really are different." Vincent whimpers with a teary eye. "But, but you're not dangerous right, Vincent?" Tweety cries. "We're not done yet children." Mr. E. reassures. "There. Now. it's done" Mr. E. concluded his drawing and showed the children. "You both love playing, you both love talking to each other, you both have the same problems, AND, most importantly, you both love each other." Mr. E. then passes the drawing back to the children, "Now, how about you guys make your own drawings and color them in? After you are done. I can show them to your parents. Does that sound fair?" "Thank you Mr. E.!!" Vincent and Tweety replied happily. Vincent and Tweety went home later today and found that their parents were incredibly proud. Daddy said that she never knew Vincent really cared about Tweety that much. Mommy made some pie for Tweety to share with Vincent tomorrow. She said it's to celebrate a new friendship. From then on, Tweety and Vincent were best friends until the very end.

title: Once upon a Father's Birthday
text: Once upon a Father's Birthday. Daddy's birthday is coming soon, should I gift him a new princess crown? or should I just gift wrap the moon?
