She put on her best clothes and went out of her room........ where a surprise party awaited her! All her friends were also there! Meena played with her friends all day. She even went to the water park with them to play! After the party, Meena opened all her gifts. Inside were many things, somebody had given her a camera, somebody clothes or toys. Meena had enjoyed herself a lot. She went to her parents to thank them. She went to her parents and said," Thank You mom and dad, for making my birthday so wonderful!". Her parents were very overwhelmed by the way she had thanked them. " Your welcome, my angel!", replied her father and hugged her. Her mother looked close to tears. " And happy birthday", they said.
author: Saachi Singh
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Greystroke; Kavitha Mandana; Megha Vishwanath; Sandhya Prabhat; Shailja Jain Chougule; Soumya Menon; Tanvi Bhat; Taposhi Ghoshal

title: The lost and found boy
text: Ravi missed his home. He ran away from his home in his childhood.He is very poor now. He ran away from his home without bringing his debit card or phone. He is a young man now without any home, money or work. He was very hungry but he didn't have money so he went to a hotel and said, ''Please give me some work, so that I can buy food and eat." The hotel manager said, 'Yes,you can serve our customers,and in return I will give you some money." That day Ravi was very happy to get a job. Next morning, some customers arrived in the hotel. Ravi was in-charge of the new customers, he didn't know it was his family.His family also didn't know that his son was working in this hotel. Then he went to the room where his parents were living. The parents talked to him normally as they would to a hotel attendant. In the midst of the conversation, Ravi mentioned about his childhood days and hometown. The parents started connecting it with their missing son. They showed Ravi his childhood photographs with the family. This picture was clear in Ravi's mind. He started crying and asking for forgiveness. The family was overjoyed to find their missing son after a long time.
author: Mussarat begum

title: meena's cat
text: Meena loved cats.She used to play with cats that roamed around in her apartment all the time. One day she said to her father, "father cats are so cute, right?".Her father who was talking to her mother said "yes, they are". Then the girl asked "So can I have one?".Her father replied "fine,but you will have to take the responsibilities for it. The girl replied "fine". Soon the cat gave babies.Within months the number of cats increased. One day she said "I am tired of taking care of somany cats. She started gifting her friends cats as soon as she got to know that her friends like cats she even started selling cats in her apartment.One day person who took care of cats came to her and said"I heard that you like cats and I like them too. I wanted to buy a cat from you.how much would you sell it to me for?".The girl replied"you can take it for free,you don't have to pay me for this".The person was happy and gave her a chance to take care of cats with him. After some months she started working and taking care of cats with him.he started telling lot of about cats that she didn't know like what they eat,what they like,etc, so she gave the cat jallebies to eat.When her parents got to know this,they scolded her badly and gave the cat to their neighbour.
author: Anika Chatterjee
illustrator: Bindia  Thapar; JP Brouard; Kalynne Vorster; Rijuta Ghate; Ruchi Shah

title: Why is There a Hole in the Wall?
text: Lungisa lived in a village called esiKhaleni or Place of Noise. Some people also called it Hole-in-the-Wall. “Why is there a hole in the wall?” Lungisa asked his mother. “Because one of the sea-people used a giant fish-head to break through the wall so that he could get to the woman he loved.” “Interesting,” said Lungisa. “Why is there a hole in the wall?” Lungisa asked his teacher. “Because waves crashed against the rocks for millions of years, and made a hole in the sandstone,” said his teacher. “Interesting,” said Lungisa. “Why is there a hole in the wall?” Lungisa asked his granny. “So that our ancestors will have a gateway to us.” “Interesting,” said Lungisa. “Why is there a hole in the wall?” Lungisa asked his aunty. “It is a window to god.” “Interesting,” said Lungisa. “Why is there a hole in the wall?” Lungisa asked his friend. “Because a ship crashed into the wall.” “Interesting,” said Lungisa. “Why is there a hole in the wall?” Lungisa asked his little sister. “So that my brother can keep asking questions,” she said. And Lungisa laughed. But he kept on asking.
author: Kirsty  Paxton

title: The Boy Who Saved the Village (With Help From a Squirrel)
text: If you do things for other people, they will reward you with kindness. On a cloudy day, Pradesh was walking in the forest. He was on his way back from the well. It had been an eventful morning. Since the water was broken, his mother sent him to fetch water. The well water was extremely heavy, so Pradesh decided to take a break under a wide oak tree. Soon enough Pradesh met a squirrel. The squirrel said," Pradesh, the village is in distress. There is no water. You need to help them." Pradesh silently agreed, remembering his mother's and father's late night conversation. The squirrel said that he needs to go to the city, which was about 2 miles east. The squirrel also said that the village would start to become thirsty soon. The squirrel lead the boy to the city. Of course, the city was filled with people. This was Pradesh's first time in the big city. The squirrel knew exactly where to go. He was led to a building with a board that read "Board for Rural Services." Pradesh walked in and told the man his problem. The man said he would give the village five truck loads of water and a water pipeline that would be built in a year. Pradesh went back to his village in one of the trucks with water and the squirrel rode on top. The village was so proud of Pradesh when he returned with the water. His mother drank from her canteen with a smile on her face. The entire village was happy and Pradesh was honored. The pipeline was soon built and the villagers had access to water. Pradesh set a goal and worked for it. In the end, he was rewarded.
author: Arnav Dharmagadda
illustrator: Sanjay Sarkar; Sugandhini, Sunita,Thejaswini TVS School, Tumakuru; Vinayak Varma; Zara Asgher

title: My granny's birthday
text: I am " Meenu". i am in grannies farm. She is my granny. Today is her birthday. She is getting ready for go to temple. I want to give a surprise for my granny. Now i am making flowers bouquet. Yummy! Now granny cut the cake. Me and my friends are enjoying my grannies birthday.
author: minal kharat
illustrator: Kavitha Mandana; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Ruchi Shah; Sandhya Prabhat; Sanjay Sarkar

title: SHAMU THE BRAVE DOG
text: Gopal is a farmer. He has a big farm. many animals like cows sheep, pigs,hens are lived in the farm. Shamu is Gopal's pet dog. He loves his dog very much. And Shamu also love him too. He takes care of his farm. One night when he was resting under the tree he saw some unusual things happens around the farm. He saw that a person wanted to enter in to the farm by climbing the gate. Immediately shamu started barking and ran towards the gate and bite him and the man ran away Shamu contentiously barking and Gopal heard his barking and he ran towards to the gate and he patted on his back for his saving his farm and animals.
author: Shubhangi Rai
illustrator: Kavitha Mandana; Lavanya Nagappan; Natasha  Mehra; Preeti Krishnamurthy

title: My Buddies....
text: Hey, meet my buddy Sonu.... She is sweet like ice-cream. He is Montu... My naughty & very sweet buddy... This is me.... Moms called me Pinky.... and dada called me Laddu.... Ha Ha Ha!!! Isn't it funny.... Sonu, Montu and Me play together and have fun. Mom cooks yummy.... food for us.... We enjoy eating together... And now.... meet my best buddy.... My Mom and My Dada....
author: Geetmala Sabbani
illustrator: Dhriti Nut; Rijuta Ghate; Sandhya Prabhat; Sukhada Rahalkar; Zainab Tambawalla

title: THE STORY OF BRAVE RITY
text: Once there was a very happy family.There was a girl named Rity and a boy named Rahul. They lived in a happy town. Rity was very smart and Rahul was small so he did not go to school. Rity worked very hard.She always completed her work and always scored good marks. But one day, all the happiness went away because a very big storm came and everyone was unhappy in the town. Rity started to help everyone. Then, everyone was saved. Everyone lived happily ever after in the town. THE END
author: Samaira Singh
illustrator: Henu; Jeyanthi Manokaran; Mayur Mistry; Priya Kuriyan; Sharanya Singh; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Tell me now! - 'Good For You'
text: Why should I go to school every day? It is good for you. Why should I have a bath every day? It is good for you. Why should I not play in the sun? It is not good for you. Why should I not stay up late? It is not good for you. Why should I sleep every day? Your body needs rest. Why should I listen to you? You know why.
author: Madhav Chavan

title: Round and Round (Tell me now series)
text: Why are wheels round? This bus does not move. Why are bangles round? I will not buy square bangles. Why is a chapati round? It is not round when I try to roll it. Why is your bindi round? Do you think this bindi looks nice? Why are eyes round? They are round and they are BIG! Why is zero round? I don’t know.
author: Madhav Chavan

title: Sweet and Sour (Tell me now series)
text: Why is sea water salty? It tastes salty because there is salt in the sea. Why is the chocolate sweet? It tastes sweet because there is sugar in it. Why is a lime sour? The acid in the lime makes it sour. Is there salt in tears? Yes, there is. Is there sugar in a mango? Yes, there is sugar in ripe mangoes. Is there acid in curds? Yes, there is some acid in curds.
author: Madhav Chavan

title: Kato Clever and the Big Trouble
text: In a small garden in the city, there was a big pipal tree. Many small animals lived together on the pipal tree. There also lived a family of squirrels. Vikki was one little squirrel among them who liked to talk big. His cousin, Kato from Far Forest, had come to visit him. One evening, as all the animals who lived in the little garden were just going to sleep, they heard loud sounds from the park, next to the little garden. Kato and the other squirrels saw big yellow machines, and men in hard yellow hats, pointing to the little garden and other houses on the street. They were going to pull them all down and build a parking lot. The people who lived there would move to other houses; but no one gave a thought to the animals, birds and insects who lived in the little garden. The machines were first spotted by the mole family. To be more exact, by Mister Popples, the eldest who told Master Mopples, who in turn told the youngest, Little Popples. When they were young they were called Pop, Mo p and Pip. Mister Popples told the squirrels, the squirrels told the birds, caterpillars, butterflies, tiny spiders and all those who lived in the little garden. There was total panic, a lot of running, flying, scurrying and hopping, with no one knowing what to do? Where to go? The caterpillars said, “Let us look for leaves.” The butterflies said, “We want flowers.” The mice wanted holes. The moles wanted to dig their own holes. The squirrels, birds, insects wanted trees, bushes and grass. All the animals wanted the soft earth, not cement or concrete. “Where will we find all this?” they cried. “We will surely die,” they said and wept. Kato’s uncle and aunt were very quiet and all the little squirrels crept close to their mom. Kato cleared his throat and spoke shyly, “I live in the Far Forest, may be we can all go there?” There was a buzz of excitement and someone said, “How?” Kato scratched his head and thought hard, “Well, the Squirrel Express can take the squirrels and the butterflies, spiders, caterpillar and all the insects. The birds can either fly or come with us. The moles, mice and the grass snake family can go by the underground Mole Express.” Everyone thought it was a splendid idea. Mister Popples rushed to ask Mister Grumbles, the driver of the underground express train if he could take them all to the Far Forest. Mister Grumbles fumbled, stumbled, bumbled before he finally mumbled, “Alright.” Now it was Mister Popples’ turn to be grand. “Friends, you need not worry, my grandfather’s grandson’s... third nephew’s.....second niece’s family live in the Far Forest.” So, in the early hours of the morning the Squirrel Express and the Mole underground train with all its passengers, chugged their way to the Far Forest with its trees, flowers, ponds and soft earth.
author: Herminder Ohri

title: Mohar's Adventures
text: Chanda Little Mohar is very happy! She was the first one to get out of bed in the morning today. And guess why? For she has a dinner invitation today......that too at Kutu Aunty's place! And where there is Kutu Aunty, there is yum yum food! Fried rice, chilly chicken, sweets and lots and lots of ice-cream. That is why, Mohar has decided that today she will not eat anything all day! When Maa came and asked her, "Mohar, eat something?" - Mohar shook her head and sternly replied, "Nuh-uh!" Maa tried again. "A little bit at least?" Mohar felt bad for Maa. She said, "Okay! But remember, only a little bit!" In the afternoon, Ma said, "Mohar, my dear little one, take a small nap? Or else you will look all dull at the party tonight!" But sleep was the last thing on Mohar's mind! Although she went to bed, she tossed and turned, and then......tossed and turned some more. When she finally fell asleep, she dreamed of food and lots of ice-cream! As soon as the clock struck six, Mohar was out of her bed. Off she went to her Maa and requested, "Maa, get me ready for the party please?" Ma made Mohar wear her favourite frock. She combed her hair. She even put a little lipstick on her lips. Then she asked Mohar, "Now go and play outside while I get ready? But remember, don't be too naughty!" The house Mohar lived in was like those old-fashioned ones. She lived in a joint family. Her grandma, grandpa, uncle, aunty - all of them lived together. They all had their own different rooms. But the rooms were all joined by a single U-shaped verandah made out of red sandstone. A set of stairs from the verandah led down to the kutcha courtyard. Mohar thought, why not play a new game while Maa gets ready? She would close her eyes and see if she can walk from one end of the verandah to the other. So Mohar closed her eyes and spread out her hands right in front of her for balance. Then she started counting "One, Two..." as she took one step after the other. But right as she counted ten - Thump-Thud-Thwack! She had completely forgotten to take the left turn......and down in the courtyard she fell! Ma-Baba heard the loud noise and came running outside. There they saw that Mohar was sitting on the ground, all muddy and dirty! They laughed and laughed and laughed, till tears rolled down their cheeks! Mohar felt really bad. Here she was sitting on the ground, all hurt. And Ma-Baba were laughing? "Whaa!!" she started crying. Then Maa picked her up fondly. She wiped her arms and legs clean. She gently put medicine on her wounds. She even gave her a sweet little kiss on her cheek. Then Mohar saw Baba standing on the side, with a big ice-cream in his hand. Mohar almost jumped with joy! She surely could not go for the party in this state. But so what? The sweet kiss and the big fat ice-cream had already filled up her little tummy!
author: Anurima Chanda

title: The battle between giraffe and a lion
text: One day a lion was trying to find an animal to eat. In the other side there was a giraffe who was eating leaves. Then the giraffe heard a sound,it thought it was the lion by hearing the sound. Then the both of them saw each other. Then the lion said I want to fight you. The giraffe asked why?. Then lion said, because I want to eat someone. The giraffe said, I'm not easy. Then the battle begins the lion makes the first move, but the giraffe outsmarts and hit it with It's iron like legs. the match is decided, the lion doesn't know what hit it. The giraffe has WON!!!!!!!
author: Nitishaan Goswami

title: The value of friendship
text: One day deer wanted to see how much everyone loved her. She went to the monkey and told him that she was racing with rabbit and got hurt badly. The monkey felt bad for her. She told the same thing to bear,the bear felt bad for her too. Deer told the same thing to the elephant. He also felt bad for her too. Deer felt terribly bad. She shouldn't have. lied or have thought of judging her friends. Deer went to her mother and told her what she did. her mother told her yo go and say sorry to rabbit. deer went to rabbit and said sorry for what she had done. rabbit forgave her and they became friends again Mo ral: Never judge friend ship.
author: Tishya Suri

title: My Mum and I
text: Hello there! I am Kavitha and that is my mother Geetha. She is the world's best woman, mother, doctor, cook and teacher that I had met. In this story you will know about my life with my mum. I am very sure that Amma loved me ever since I was there in her tummy. She made sure I got all the nutrients that I needed and all the love necessary. She always had lots of food and thats why I was so bubbly and healthy when I was born. Amma never ever let me get hurt when I was a baby. She always cradled me in her arms like she does now. I too adored my mother since I was born. Every year she would throw me the most amazing birthday parties. My friends and I always had the best time. Till I was 10 Amma and Appa made sure that everyone I loved was there at my party. Though they were both very busy doctors, they always made time for me and were at home on my birthday. I dont think that I could have had fun in my childhood without these two amazing parents. She always comforted me when I cried. I was never left alone in sorrow. Even if it was because she scolded me that I cried she would immediately apologised and hug me till I stopped crying. Soon Amma was due another baby with whom I had to share my love with. I wasnt happy at first but Amma promised me that no matter what I would always be her girl and I knew that Amma never broke a promise. But, once the baby came, little Karthika, I was completely ignored in the house. I felt terrible and would cry every night. One night Amma caught me wailing into my pillow and cuddled me like she used to and said,"No matter what happens you will always be my darling Kavi!" From that night I cheered up and knew that my mother would always be mine. Soon enough I began to adore Karthika and we became the best of friends. Amma told me that I was Karthi's second mother and that we should always be very close. Soon many years went by and I was married. I feared that my relationship with my parents would drift apart, so I made sure that though I was going to live abroad like my parents always wanted, they would visit me all the time. I enjoyed living with my husband so much but missed the company of parents and sister badly. Soon, I was due a baby and that minute I made my parents live with me. Amma and Appa seemed more excited than I was. So, after nine months of waiting I had my beautiful daughter Vennila. The first person to hold her was not me, not her father, but her grandmother Geetha who loved her as much as she loved me when I was born. My father and sister too held her as my husband and I cried happy tears and when Vennila was given to her father you should have seen the cheeky yet adorable look she had on her face. So there my parents at the age of 68 winning the golf games at their hospital, which they now own, happily enjoying the years to come visiting us now and then. And each time they visit Vennila hugs them tight and shows them all the new things she learns and I tell my Amma and Appa how much they mean to me.
author: Mekala Gopal
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Bindia  Thapar; Niloufer Wadia; Sahitya Rani; Saloni Chopra; Sandhya Prabhat; Soumya Menon; Suvidha Mistry

title: A Miaow and A Roar
text: Vedika and Karan loved to huddle and read together on their grandfather’s rocking chair. “Look at the lion,” pointed Vedika. “It’s a very small picture. Fetch me Grandpa’s big looking glass,” said Karan. Karan moved the magnifying glass forward and back till he saw the lion look really huge. “Vedika! This lion is getting bigger and bigger!” “The lion is moving, Karan!” screamed Vedika. Just then, Karan and Vedika put down the looking glass and found themselves standing in front of a huge, big lion. The lion opened its wide mouth and let out a, “Miiaaooww!” “What’s wrong Mr. Lion? Why do you sound like a cat?” asked Vedika. “My cousin, the cat and I met at the lake yesterday and when we drank water from the lake, I got her miaow and she got my roar,” said the lion. “This is terrible, Mr. Lion. Where can we find your cousin, the cat?” asked Karan. “Sitting on some tree and scaring the birds I think,” replied the lion. “Vedika, let’s help the lion get his roar back,” said Karan. “Come with us Mr. Lion,” said Vedika. Just then they heard the roar they were looking for. They searched and searched till they found the cat sitting high up on a tree. “Miss Cat, you have a loud roar,” said Vedika. “Yes, I do. And, the lion has my tiny miaow,” replied the cat. “Now I can scare all the birds and animals.” “Mr. Lion needs his roar back. Please give it back to him,” begged Karan. Just as he said that Karan let out an, “Aaaachooooo!” Then, one more followed and another and then many more. “Stop that Karan, you are making me want to, to, too…Aaaaachoooo!” sneezed Vedika. Then, one more followed and another and then many more. Before anyone could say anything, the cat and the lion sniffed, opened their mouths wide and let out an Aaaaachoooo! One sounded like a iaowchooooo and the other a roarchooooo. Then, one more followed, and another and then many more. Everyone looked at each other and sniffed. The lion tried to miaow but out came a Roaaarrrrr! The cat tried to roar but out came a Miiaaow! Vedika clapped her hands and giggled. “Mr. Lion, you have your roar back.” “I do, I do, and thank you,” he replied. The cat didn’t look very happy. “Miss Cat, you sound very sweet with your miaow,” said Karan. “Do I? Well, then thank you,” said Miss Cat. Vedika and Karan held their looking glass to get a closer look at the cat and as they moved it forward and back, the cat became smaller and smaller. Just then Karan and Vedika found themselves rocking back and forth on their grandfather’s rocking chair.
author: Tanya Luther Agarwal

title: The Fire Birds of Mumbai
text: The island city of Mumbai has a well-kept secret. Every year, the dusty, smoky city becomes pink in colour. Just like tens of thousands of people come to Mumbai to make it their home. Tens of thousands of flamingos visit the Sewri Mudflats between November to March to make it their home for a few months. The flamingo is also called the fire bird, because their wings look like pink fire. Their necks are shaped like the letter "S". When they are looking for food, they put their head in water, turn it upside down and WHOOSH, they shovel in a fish. MMMMM! Don't they look like they are running on water? Just like different people make a city special... These birds make Mumbai special.
author: Bijal Vachharajani
illustrator: Anita Mani; Bindia  Thapar; Santosh Pujari; Vijay Kumar Sethi; Vivek Vegda

title: A Day with Colours
text: I'm in the mood to draw today. But I have only four colours with me. Oh no! What can I draw with these? I have red. What can I draw with RED? Maybe I can draw... chillies. But that's SO boring! I know! I know! I can draw... a woodpecker with a RED head! Then I have yellow. What can I draw with YELLOW? I guess I can draw... bananas. But that's SO boring! Oh I have another idea! I can draw... the YELLOW beak of a hornbill! And then there's blue! What can I draw with BLUE? Maybe... a blue train? But a train can also be red. Or yellow. Or black. Or white. Or... So maybe I should draw something else instead. Like the deep BLUE sea. If only I could draw a turtle in it too. How I wish had GREEN with me! But wait... GUESS WHAT? I just mixed BLUE and YELLOW and you'll never guess what I got! GREEN! GREEN! GREEN! So guess what I drew? Maybe I should try mixing something else now. Any ideas? Mmm... BLUE and RED? Let's see. Wow! I got PURPLE from BLUE and RED. Isn't that amazing? But I can't think of anything with purple. Can you? Here is a kingfisher with bits of purple in it. Can you see? My friend says he can only see blue. Okay, so I cheated a little. So what?!? Anyway, forget purple! Maybe I should mix something else. RED AND YELLOW? My friend says mixing RED and YELLOW will give me WHITE. Well, he is wrong! Because... I got ORANGE! What a silly boy. There are SO many things I can draw with ORANGE. So many, many things! Like mangoes. The setting sun. And mangoes and the sunset together, of course! And not to forget, my favourite creatures. Clownfish! It's been such a busy day! I'm tired. Look at all these things I've drawn with just four colours! You never asked about the fourth colour! But I'll give you a clue.
author: Yamini Vijayan
illustrator: Abhilash Kar; Aman Randhawa; Anant Shahane; Bulbul Sharma; Chetana Purushotham; Greystroke; Mary Marble; Maya  Ramaswamy; Michael Tymbios; Nimret Handa; Nirmal Kulkarni; Pooja Rathod; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Priya Kuriyan; Rohit Kelkar; Sanatan Juanga; Soumyabrata Roy; Vinayak Varma

title: Ah! Football!
text: I like playing with my friend Chuma. We are good friends. When either one of us is sent somewhere, we go together. One day, my grandmother sent me to the shop to buy salt and cooking oil. I went with Chuma. On the way, we saw our friends playing football. "Ah! Football!" I said. I wanted to play too. I said to Chuma, "Let's ask if we can play with them. I like playing football very much." Chuma replied, "Let us go to the shop first, then we can come to play." But I replied, "Let us play first!" "Grandmother will not allow us to return." We joined our friends to play. I was the goal keeper. The goal posts were made of two big stones. I worked hard to catch the ball. My friends were not able to score any goals. We played until the field was full of sand. Then we went to the shop. Grandmother's money was gone! I started to cry. Chuma shouted, "Stop crying. You wanted to play first." We returned home without salt or cooking oil. We were very dirty and worried. Grandmother was annoyed when we got home. The first question she asked us was, "Where were you all this time?" We had to tell her the truth. She forgave us but warned, "Never again go to play without permission." We went to feed the ducks. Later on, we cleaned ourselves.
author: Stella   Kihweo

title: Counting Animals
text: One elephant is going to drink water. Two giraffes are going to drink water. Three buffaloes and four birds are also going to drink water. Five antelopes and warthogs are walking to the water. Seven zebras are running to the water. Eight frogs and nine fish are swimming in the water. One lion roars. He also wants to drink. Who is afraid of the lion? One elephant is drinking water with the lion.
author: Clare Verbeek; Thembani  Dladla; Zanele Buthelezi

title: Beloved Daughter
text: This is Natabo. She has six brothers. Her parents give her a small pot. She loves it. One day her brothers break the pot. Natabo cannot find her pot. She cries and cries. Natabo runs away. She climbs a tall tree. Her parents find her. "Please come down," they ask. Her brothers sing, "Please come down." Natabo makes fun of their song. Then Natabo's friend comes. "Please come down," she sings. Natabo's friend sings until she comes down from the tree. The friends walk home together. Everyone celebrates that Natabo is home. Natabo gets a new pot!
author: Mulongo  Bukheye; Ritah  Katetemera

title: Friends
text: My name is Simo. I have four friends. Their names are Zizo, Lele, Sisa and Ayanda. My friend Zizo likes to play soccer. My friend Lele likes to swim. My friend Sisa likes to play hide-and-seek. My friend Ayanda likes to read. Me? I like to do the things they like to do. I play soccer with Zizo. I swim with Lele. I play hide-and-seek with Sisa. Come, friend, what do you like? Come, play soccer with us. Come, swim with us. Come, play hide-and-seek with us. Come, read with us!
author: Hlengiwe  Zondi; Zimbili  Dlamini

title: Ready, Steady, Go!
text: Most of Nisha’s classmates came to school by the school bus, on rickshaws or cycles. Nisha was a little different. She came to school on her wheelchair. She lived quite close to the school. Sometimes she would meet her friends, Rajat, Piu and Soham on the way and they would race each other. Nisha would be overjoyed whenever she won. Most parents would not allow children to race down the streets. But Chanchalpur was a small town and school started very early in the morning when there was hardly any traffic at all, so their parents did not worry much. Nisha loved school. She had some trouble in the beginning. The singing lessons were held on the third floor and she was unable to climb stairs in her wheelchair. The Principal, Sarita ma’am, and other teachers soon took note of this, however, and had ramps built in the school. Now, Nisha had no trouble at all going from one part of the school to another. Before Nisha, this school in the little town of Chanchalpur had never had a student who used a wheelchair. When Nisha came, the teachers unanimously decided that every child should be included in all activities of the school and took adequate measures. Nisha did her lessons well. She loved the huge school library and was a regular visitor there. She was also quite a good singer and was an obvious choice whenever the school participated in any singing competition. What made Nisha very sad, however, was that she could hardly participate in anything at all in the annual sports day at school. She was part of the school band and the teachers arranged the school drill in such a way that Nisha would always be a part of it, but Nisha wanted to participate in the competitions. This year too, she felt miserable as she saw her friends preparing for relays, high jumps, hurdles and races. “I wish I could participate in at least one event,” she told Soham sadly. Nisha’s class teacher, Munira Ma’am also noticed her gloom and discussed the matter in the staffroom. But nobody could come up with any solution. The teachers were very sad for Nisha. Then suddenly, while preparing for the cycle race, Piu had an idea. She called all the other participants in the race together and discussed her plan. “That’s a brilliant idea, Piu!” they all agreed. “Let us talk to Munira ma’am at once!” The excited children rushed to their teacher. “What is it?” ma’am asked. “Piu has an idea—” started Soham, “About Nisha—” continued Ritam excitedly, “Tell ma’am it’s about sports day,” said an impatient Jenny. “Children, please calm down,” said Munira ma’am amusedly, “since I heard it’s Piu’s idea, let her speak. I will never understand what you’re trying to tell me if all of you talk at once. So, Piu, what is it?” “Ma’am,” said Piu, “you know how much Nisha wants to participate in at least one competition on sports day? I think she can be part of one.” Now Munira ma’am was really interested. “Really Piu? Which one and how?” she asked. “The cycle race ma’am!” replied Piu excitedly. “We often race each other to school on our cycles in the morning. Nisha also races on her wheelchair along with us. Why not include her in the cycle race then?” Munira ma’am’s eyes shone with pride. “What a wonderful idea, Piu! Let me discuss this with the other teachers in the staffroom and then we can let Nisha know in a day or two.” All the students went away happily. Principal ma’am and the teachers were thrilled when they heard Piu’s plan. Sarita ma’am immediately called up Nisha’s parents to ask if they would grant permission for her to take part in such a race. They were very happy and agreed. So Munira ma’am went back to class and said, “Nisha, how would you like to participate in a race on sports day this year?” Nisha looked at ma’am in disbelief and hope. Smiling, Munira ma’am said, “Piu, would you please tell Nisha about your idea?” Nisha could not believe her ears as Piu excitedly explained her idea. After she had listened, Nisha spun around in her wheelchair in Joy and hugged Piu. She was overjoyed! So were Nisha’s parents and all the teachers of the school as they saw Nisha in line with the other participants in the cycle race on sports day. The P.T. teacher announced on the microphone: Ready, Steady, Go! and a beaming Nisha zoomed ahead in her wheelchair.
author: Rimjhim Bhattacherjee

title: LION KING
text: The LION is one of the big cats in jungle. The LION is king of forest, the LION holds both beauty & strength. The LIONS are truly social cats. The LION is a wild animal, it has very large head and neck covered with hairs. We can also see this wonderful animal in national parks. The average speed of the LION is 40km per hour. In india maximum no of LION can be found in Gujrat Gir Abhiyaran, India Prime Minister NARENDER MODI is from lion territory - GUJRAT.
author: vijay tanwar

title: Elly and Ex
text: Once upon a time there were two flamingos. Their names were Elly and Ex. They had backward bending knees which were very funny and people laughed at them. They lived in South America in Brazil around a large salt lake. They had beautiful pink feathers, tall majestic legs and could swing their head upside down with their long necks. Once they were in their pond they saw two children playing soccer together nearby but not enjoying themselves. So Elly and Ex decided to join the boys. They thought the two boys playing with the round ball were so fascinating but looked lonely and so they walked up to the boys and said, “would you like to play with us? can we play with you? “ha! ha ha ha! you can’t play soccer you silly flamingos. Your knees are bending backwards.” “ Oh, you should not laugh at us, if our knees bend backwards, it doesn’t mean we can’t play soccer. We can learn how to play soccer. Just give us some instructions and we will follow them.” The boys started teaching some rules to the flamingos and soon they were having a match between the two boys and the two flamingos and guess who won? No one had won the match because they had a draw and the boys were so happy to play with the flamingos, that they gave their soccer ball to the flamingos and said,” here, take this ball and teach the other flamingos how to play soccer.” Elly and Ex were very thankful to the boys and went back and taught all the other flamingos to play soccer. One day the two boys came to the flamingos and said,” Elly, Ex please help us. Brazil team with Neymar and Marseilles have challenged us to play game and we want you in our team too.” The flamingos happily agreed, “of course! You gave us a ball as a present and we shall give you a ‘helping leg’ in your game. It will be a tough match with a toughest team in the world.” In 2 weeks the game was scheduled at the stadium in Brasilia city. The stadium was full of spectators. Everyone was very eager to watch the match between the national team and the team of flamingos and the young boys. The people whispered in the stands,” how will this flamingo team play against our stars, they have funny legs bent backwards.” “They won’t be able to dribble the ball either”. “Let’s wait and see. The national team boys will give the flamingos team a royal defeat.” Soon the umpire blew his whistle and the game began. Neymar scored a goal in the first 2 minutes and then another one in the next 5. The flamingo team was down 2-0 and the end of the first ten minutes. Elly and ex got angry, they dribbled and passed and ran as fast as their legs could carry them and Elly scored ten goals. What a cracker of a game! The flamingo team had defeated the Brazil team by 10-2. And there was a new football star in the world. It was Elly the pink flamingo.
author: Ananya Verma
illustrator: Anita Mani; Muniza Shariq; Sunando C

title: Little Sona and Her Quick Mind
text: I want to make one like that too," said Sona. Sona's father began slitting the wood. "I also want to slit wood like that," said Sona. "Yes, you will, but first you must watch and learn," said her father. Then Sona's father began to attach wheels to it. "I want to beat a nail too!" saying that Sona took the hammer. The cart was finished. Sona's father would now tie a rope to the cart to help pull it. "But where have I kept the rope and my pencils?" Sona's father began searching for them. Sona's father felt defeated. Seeing her father's condition Sona started to laugh hysterically. "Should I search them for you Baba?" asked Sona. Sona pulled out the pencil from behind one ear of her father and the rope from behind his other ear. "I really was watching you closely Baba," Sona told her father. "You really have been helpful Sona," said her father petting her head.
author: Tanurima Chanda

title: The race
text: Once a upon a time, the turtle and rabbit met each other. They said'Hello I am turtle, other one said'Hello I am rabbit. Will you be friends with me'? Then the turtle said 'Of course, why not'. So that time rabbit and turtle decided to do a race. So before going to race they decided to soak them self into the water. Then the rabbit decided and said in in her on mind that'If I soak the water properly then I will win this race. So the rabbit said that'now lets start he race'. So the turtle said 'okay'. So the rabbit said'lets get started. So the turtle said 'Ready steady go'. So the they both started running and doing the race. So they started. The rabbit yawned and said'I am feeling sleepy'. So the turtle said'okay'. Then went in a deep sleep So she decided to sleep in the top of the roof for a while.So she climbed up in the top of the roof and then began to sleep. That time the turtle already reached at the finishing line. Then he stopped and ran to the rabbit, when he reached he saw and said'wake rabbit' so she woke up and said'Rabbit I reached in the finishing line, but I came to wake you up. Then the rabbit rushed towards his back and started running. So they both finished reached to the finishing line and said to the turtle 'congratulations turtle for becoming 1st position in the race. So the rabbit also got the prize in the 2nd position. So they both kept the prize and enjoyed the beautiful nature.
author: Ayanna Kullu

title: Feelings
text: My heart feels a lot of things. I feel happy when my granny tells us stories in the evening. I feel silly when I play with my friend. I feel bad when my dad says he does not have money. I feel loved when my mom gives me a hug.
author: Clare Verbeek; Thembani  Dladla; Zanele Buthelezi

title: How Many?
text: How many legs do two ladybirds have? How many wings do four birds have? How many horns do three rhinos have? How many trunks do five elephants have? How many ears do seven dogs have? How many tails do three monkeys have? How many eyes do six cats have? How many legs does one worm have?
author: Clare Verbeek; Thembani  Dladla; Zanele Buthelezi

title: Kintsugi - The Japanese Art of Mending
text: Craaash...!! "Tina, what have you done? It was a very costly pot!" "Ameena, how was your day at school?" Abba asked. "Not so good, Abba. My best friend Tina was upset. She broke a very costly pot in her father's shop by mistake. " "Oh! Can't it be mended?" "How can anyone mend a broken pot, Abba?" Ameena was curious. "Well, it is an art my child. An ancient art." said Abba. "Ancient art!" exclaimed Ameena. "Please,tell me more about it, Abba." "Kintsugi is an ancient Japanese art of mending broken pottery. Folktales say it originated in the 15th century after a Japanese king sent a tea bowl for repair to China but the result was ugly." Abba narrated the story. "So did he throw away the bowl?" asked Ameena. "No my child. The Japanese artisans worked on it and found a unique way to mend the pot." "Really, how Abba?" "They used lacquer mixed with gold powder. Not only was the pot repaired it looked beautiful too." replied Abba. "This Japanese art is mostly used on ceramic ware. The philosophy is to encourage mending and now artisans use different techniques and colours to do the same." "Thank You Abba!" said Ameena. "Tomorrow, I will tell Tina about Kintsugi. I am sure she will be happy to know that broken pots can be repaired." "Oh, but don't go around breaking pots to repair them later." said Abba with a hearty laugh.
author: Vibha Lohani
illustrator: Aman Randhawa; P.G. Dinesh; Suvidha Mistry; Vibha Lohani

title: Cooking for Upupi
text: Upupi the Hoopoe was the new bird in town She had travelled very far, oh really far from home And now out for a lunch break on her first day at work She craved something special, scrumptious, and... and... Oh she did not quite know! She had asked around and chosen the best restaurant in town - The famous Chef Roller's 'Slurpattackapackawow' - it was world-renown. She had ordered four dishes and all four she had sent back For Upupi was sure each something did lack. Chef Roller in the kitchen was puzzled by this new guest "What stops this picky bird from licking her feathers like the rest?" Chef cooked with love and every dish was his pride He scratched his blue head - "How could the hoopoe be satisfied?" He had served her a bowl of fresh snails cooked in dew Salted and peppered - the best he could stew. She had tasted a spoonful and said rolling her eyes, "This simply does not taste very nice." Then within a hole in a rock chef had fried some mango seeds And sprinkled them with curried twigs, two nuts, and centipedes. When this crunchy meal had been served in a coconut shell Upupi caught one whiff of it and said, "What a horrible smell!" Hmm.. perhaps something really sweet? But no! Not even this third delight was Upupi ready to eat! Even though Chef had whipped her a fresh blueberry treat Spread on a bed of the purest pink marshmallows Decorated with colourful confetti - parrot greens and canary yellows. And his famous 'Cloud Bites'? “This cloud tastes of smoke”, said Upupi, adjusting her crown. “Wring me some rain to wash it down.” A server ran to fetch a cup, another to the chef A third conveniently pretended that he was deaf! Chef Roller was tired, but was not ready to throw in his hat So he sat down with Upupi and decided to have a friendly chat The servers crowded in the kitchen and watched from a distance Five minutes, then fifteen - wow! they admired their boss’s persistence. At last they saw Chef get up and after asking Upupi to wait Fly into the kitchen with a big smile on his face “The hoopoe’s simply homesick and does not know it yet!” “She misses food from home, I’m willing to bet!” He then looked through his book of recipes from every place in the country And brought down some ingredients stored on high shelves in his pantry Chef had found the perfect dish from Upupi’s hometown Just a simple meal - spiced beetles fried until they were brown. Chef served Upupi the beetles and saw her face brighten “Oh Chef!”, said Upupi, “this smells exactly like my grandmama’s kitchen!” “It tastes like the evening air on walks with my Pappy, It is special and scrumptious and makes my heart truly happy.” She finished every bit of her lunch and he personally cleared her plate They shared a warm wing-shake and they both felt great. Upupi the hoopoe who was the new bird in town And Chef Roller the pride of 'Slurpattackapackawow' - it truly was world-renown!
author: Sumithra Surendralal

title: Two Hungry Boys
text: Ben and Thabo are two hungry boys. Granny is making ten cupcakes. She puts them on a plate. Ben takes one cupcake. Thabo takes two cupcakes. Ben takes four cupcakes. Thabo takes two cupcakes. How many cupcakes did Ben eat? How many cupcakes did Thabo eat? How many cupcakes are left for granny?
author: Clare Verbeek; Thembani  Dladla; Zanele Buthelezi

title: Is There Anyone Like Me?
text: I wonder if there's another me somewhere in the world. Who looks the same. And talks the same. And even has my curls. Someone with my eyes my ears. Who even has my laugh. Who can do what I can do. And can't do what I can't. I've looked and looked everywhere to find another me. I went down to the park and looked behind the trees. I looked around, up and down. At every single face. I couldn't find another me in any single place. There's only one me in the world! I'm special, oh it's true! But not just me, don't you see? There's only one of you!
author: Fred Strydom

title: Monkey and the Drought
text: The rains did not come. The land was very dry. This monkey left home to look for water and food. She walked over hills and valleys. She came to a place named Tirkol. Monkey was very happy in this place. She ate fruit and got fat. But she missed her friends. So Monkey made the long journey home. The other monkeys were joyful to see her. "Where is this wonderful place with fruit?" they asked her. "I will take you there," said Monkey. The other monkeys loved Tirkol. They decided to stay there forever. But the monkeys from Tirkol were worried. "These new monkeys will eat all our fruit," they said. The Tirkol monkeys went to attack the new monkeys. "Why fight?" asked an elder. "There is enough fruit for all!" This was true. So the monkeys decided to live together peacefully.
author: Alice Edui

title: Learning to read
text: Once upon a time, was a little girl that did't know to read, she always was sad for that reason, she always search consolation in the tree and one day her dad see her so sad, and ask her: "Why are you sad baby?" and the girl answer he "Nothing dad, is just that I don't know to read, and I haven't anybody to teach me"... The next week her dad take her at the school, she was so happy to have friends and learn to read, in the first day of school, the childrens there received her with enthusiasm, and she explain them the reason why she was there, all the class understand her situation and start to help her for learn to read, and all the week pass... On friday, next to school, her dad ask her: "How do you feel?" and she answer he " Good dad, now with help of all my friends I know to read!!"...
author: Jime CH
illustrator: Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Mayur Mistry; Nina Sabnani; Shailja Jain Chougule

title: The little rabbit
text: Once upon a time a little rabbit steal carrots to give food to other animals than can't get food The little rabbit steal the carrots from the farm of the family Watson He make that other animal be happy But the family be sad because your carrots are lost One night when the little rabbit break into the farm the family Watson break down the act And the little rabbit never steal again because is bad but the family get the carrots to him and the other animals
author: Adair Rosas
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Ketan Raut; Namrata  Gosavi; Padmanabh; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Sonakshi Verma

title: The little Hugo
text: Once upon a time was a little elephant named Hugo, and he live in a zoo, Hugo not have a dad, he only had his mom. One day the mother of Hugo disappeared for no reason, Hugo was too scared and he decide to go and find her, because she was the only person in the life of Hugo... On the way to find his mother Hugo meet a small chicken crying. Hugo asked his name to the chicken and he told her that his name was Carlitos and he also was looking his mother. Hugo and Carlitos decided to look for their moms together and little by little they became more friends. When the two finally found their moms the two live very happily. This friendship will be rare, because they are so differents, but the two supported each other when they needed someone. This two did a lot of pranks together... Carlitos never imagine having a friend as good as Hugo and now practically are brothers by choice Actually Hugo and Carlitos with their moms live very happily.
author: Nohemi Vazquez
illustrator: Harshvardhan Gantha; Niloufer Wadia; Ruchi Shah; Sanjay Sarkar; Shubhshree  Mathur

title: The Man in the Hat
text: This book is about That man in the hat. Come see what he saw In the Western Ghats! When he was a boy, He liked to read books, All books about animals. His friends gave him looks! But the man grew up. The man in the hat. He got a nice camera. To look for a cat. He wanted to see Turtles and snakes. He wanted to see Crocodiles in lakes. But on his first trip to the Western Ghats, What did he see? A secret grey cat! The cat was too fast For the man in the hat! The cat ran away! It hid in the Ghat. "I will find it again." Said the man in the hat. "Its color was grey, Just like my hat." The man walked on in the Western Ghats. The sun was so hot, He needed his hat. "I'll look for water," He said at last. "All animals need water. Maybe the cat went past!" "Oh, Tiger!" he said, "Have you seen a cat? One big and fast, And grey, like my hat?" If the tiger knew, she did not say. She gave a big roar And ran away! "Well," the man said, "I must try again." But as he went on, It started to rain. Out came the termites. Out came the ants. Soon all of the termites Were food for the ants. Rain fell on his hat, That rain in the Ghat. It became waterfalls. And it filled all the rivers. We all must have water. Ants, men and cats. If we will have water, We must save the Ghats! The rain was good for Deer and elephants too. The man in the hat Went to ask them, too. "Excuse me, my friends," Said the man in the hat, "Has anyone here seen A big grey cat?" "No," said the elephants and the barking deer. "We've not seen a cat Like that around here." So on up to the rainforest went the man in the hat. In the next-up level of the Western Ghats. There in a tree, What did he see? A Lion-tailed Macaque Then two, then three! "Good day, Macaques," said the man in the hat. "Can you help me find The secret grey cat?" "Look in the trees for a hive of bees. Under that tree, Is a frog hard to see." "He lives underground. But has friends all around. Go and ask him about your cat. Go and ask him, man in the hat!" Left, right, left right Went the man in the hat He went to find The big grey cat. At last he came To a tree so tall, It had a bee hive About to fall. A frog said to him From underground, "Are you the man Who walks around?" "My friend the bat Says you look for a cat." "Yes," said the man, "The cat in the ghat." The frog came up From underground. A purple frog! It made a big sound. The purple frog Told the man in the hat To find a guide Who had seen the cat. The man went up Past forests thick. The trees grew thinner Very quick. When people cut trees, To make things cheap, The animals Have nowhere to sleep. "Dear God," the man prayed, "Please, please, please, For the animals here, Please save these trees!" And on he went to the tip-top grass. Up, up he went, the man in the hat. Will he find the cat at last? Will he find the cat in the ghat? So far inside the Western Ghats In grass so green Sat the man in the hat. He rested a bit There in that place. He turned to see A human face. "Good day, Sir!" Said the man in the hat "Can you guide me to the big grey cat?" "This cat I have seen But once before! Please help me find What I came here for." " Pogeyan is your cat," Said the kind guide. "Far up in the ghats Is where she hides." "Where she is now, Nobody knows. But up in this ghat She comes and goes." So happy he was! The man in the hat. He turned a flip, Just like that. "Then up I will go!" Said the man in the hat. Like a Nilgiri Tahr, The goat of the ghat. It was time to sleep So the man in the hat Set a camera trap For the cat in the ghat. He slept. He woke. He looked in the trap. It was good! He saw it! The secret grey cat! Then a snake woke him up. And that's when he knew. It all was a dream. Let's hope it comes true! The Man in the Hat He looks for a cat. He looks for the cat way up in the ghat! This tale is based on the real-life trek of Sandesh Kadur, a nature film maker and explorer. The Western Ghats are the oldest mountains in India and home to many rare animals.
author: Lea Shaver

title: The Mango Tree
text: I like to go to her village. I like to play with the girls and boys. I am always happy to see my grandma! She is always happy to see me. She makes special foods for me. She sits with me and braids my hair. We love each other very much. When I am with her, I never want to leave! Grandma's house has a big mango tree. I love to climb so high in this tree. It is tall and wide, with big green leaves. You cannot count all the mangos up there! Grandma's mangos taste so sweet. I want to eat 100 mangos! Now it is time to go back to the city. I do not want to leave Grandma's house! I hide in the tree so no one can see me. I do not want my parents to take me away. I want to stay longer with my grandma. My parents can take the baby home! My father looks for me left and right. My mother looks for me too. But they cannot find me. They do not look for me in the tree. They think only boys can climb trees. They will never find me up here! Oh no! Who is this? Grandma's dog sees me in the tree! Go away, dog! Go away! The dog tells my secret. They see me. Now I have to climb down. Grandma gives me a big hug. I tell her that I am sad to leave. She says that I will come again. And she is proud I can climb so high. I say, "Next time I will eat 100 mangos!"
author: Lea Shaver

title: Devi and Bonda
text: I want to knock it down again! Bonda does it. He makes a box tower. He does a good job. He does not smile. He does not frown. Devi Vroom! Vroom! BAM! And she knocks it down again!!! Bonda laughs and claps. He does this every time. Bonda is my best friend. A perfect friend for a girl in a wheelchair! Devi Hi! I'm Devi. I'm from the future! The year 2085. So much has changed since your time. Today, technology makes life wonderful! Devi Meet Bonda. My best friend. A ROBOT. Did you guess that? Who else would build a tower 50 times? Bonda never gets bored! Devi Bonda can do many things. He can get my secret box from the top shelf. He can lift Baba's desk to find my earring. Things like that. Bonda Humans are useless! Your legs and arms cannot grow taller. My arms have cameras and telescopes! Devi I have to train Bonda. I "program" him. I show him how to do things. Like on Sunday, I wanted my box. First, I sent Bonda to the shelf. Bonda's screen has a map of my house. I drew the path to the shelf with my finger on the map. Next, I told him to reach up and scan the top shelf. His camera finger took pictures. Devi Bonda showed me the pictures he took. I touched the picture of the box I wanted. "That is my secret box, Bonda," I said. Can you bring it to me? Now, I only have to say, "Secret box!" And off he goes. Once Bonda learns, he never forgets. Not like humans! Devi So, that is my best friend. I have human friends too. We play and fight and go to school. But I love Bonda best. He never gets mad at me! Devi Robots do not have feelings. But, shhh! Don't tell Bonda I said that! It might make him feel bad! Bonda That is not logical, Devi! If I do not have feelings, how can I feel bad? Silly humans. Pah! Devi The best part is, I have Bonda all to myself! I never get jealous. Because I am his only friend! Bonda That is not true. I have other robot friends! Wait! Does Devi only like me BECAUSE she thinks I have no friends? And no feelings? Oh no! I feel mad, and sad, and... Devi Bonda, are you okay? You are getting hot! You are not working! I will take care of you now. I will shut you down. It will be like going to sleep. Then I will start you again. Bonda Devi's eyes are wet. She is sad. I feel sad. But, wet eyes mean she cares about me. So I also feel happy! I feel happy-sad. Whirr! Hum! Bonda reboots. Devi Bonda? Bonda, do you hear me? Is your memory gone? I want you to remember our fun! Our love... Bonda Aha! Love. That sad-happy feeling is love! Bonda Hi, Devi! What can I do? Do you want me to stack the boxes? Do you want me to get your secret box? Devi Oh, Bonda! You're all right! I am so glad! Bonda I do something very odd. No one programmed me to do it. I wrap my arms around my friend, Devi. This is not logical! Who or what is a robot? A robot is “any electro-mechanical machine guided by a computer program or electronic circuits." It doesn't have to look like a human. T here are robots all around us, already! Really? Where? Well, they are in factories, warehouses, orchards, hospitals and even homes. They may look like large mechanical arms. Car factories use these for welding, gluing and painting car parts. Or they may look like tiny cameras, attached to thin hair-like tubes,. Hospitals use these to entering our intestines and arteries to check them out. Some robots look like flat round discs, buzzing around. Homes and offices use these to clean floors at night when everyone is asleep. Some look like small wheeled vehicles, going into war zones. Soldiers use these to find dangerous landmines. Other robots roll across the surfaces of the moon or Mars. They take pictures and sendsamples to send to scientists back on Earth. Will there be a Bonda for every Devi by the year 2085? We'll have to wait and see! Have you ever seen a robot? If you have ever used, or even seen, a computer or a smartphone, you have 'seen' a robot! Yes, they are in those devices as well. Some of them even have names, like Siri and Cortana. They can help us find useful information for school projects, traffic reports and more. They can book our bus and train tickets, and order our groceries. They can even tell us exactly how many calories we have burnt after a game of football! What does the future of robots look like? We may not have robots walking our streets in India by 2040. But we will definitely be surrounded by robots of one kind or another without knowing it. It is quite likely that there will be driverless “robot” cars on our streets. We may have microscopic robots in our contact lenses that help us take pictures. We won't even have to hold our phones or cameras up to take them. But how will we take selfies?? And little airborne robots called drones will be flying all around. They will deliver letters, packages and kababs, putting delivery boys out of business! As for 2085, 45 years AFTER that, who knows what robots will be up to?
author: Lea Shaver

title: New Pussy Cat
text: Prosy wanted a pussy cat. Prosy's family went to visit the pussy cats. Prosy wanted this cat. It was too big for her. Tim wanted this kitten. It was too small for him. Mum wanted this kitten. It was too quick for her. Everyone liked this kitten. They took the kitten. Everyone is happy with the new pussy cat.
author: Ritah  Katetemera

title: Palm Tree
text: Let me tell you about the palm tree. This tree lives when everything else is dry. The shade from a palm tree is always cool. We eat fruit from the palm tree. We use palm leaves to thatch our houses. We make brooms and mats from palm leaves. We use palm tree seeds for fuel. Do you see why the palm tree is important?
author: Simon Ipoo

title: A problem with the breakfast
text: Tom Tower usually has only 15 minutes to eat lunch so he bolts it down. This does not mean he eats much for lunch since he only has a sandwich and a coffee. However, his wife Susan loves cooking and she always break up a wonderful dinner. This explains why Tom is not so thin. He pigs out every evening on a full course dinner with vegetables and a pasta side and to top it break off, a big dessert which Susan picks up on the way home from school where she is a teacher. Susan is quite girl, so it is not surprising she only picks all the food she prepares and just gnaws a carrot or some other vegetable while she listens Tom speak his day. For breakfast, Tom sometimes warms up Susan's left-overs and then he runs off for another day of work. This is against the doctor's advice so Tom should think about cutting back on meat and eggs to bring down his cholesterol.
author: gaby mila
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Henu; Niloufer Wadia; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'

title: JUST LIKE YOU, BEAUTY
text: Some time ago there was a caterpillar, which is always slow and one step, meets the desire to reach the sun to shine like the moon. She longed to be a beautiful red butterfly with long wings like sparkling newborn baby eyelashes, with flashes that when you look, you know that it was something that made you calm, fragile as a porcelain doll. In a less expressive way, she only wanted to be a free and scattered light that moved in directions that although she would be afraid to face, she would always be able to handle the view from the sky. She was always waiting with her friends for caterpillars, her encounter with the butterflies, they connected, and every night was a new anecdote. Caterpillar: butterfly, butterfly, tell me what you've done today you come so cool? Butterfly: it is nectar and wind, I am relieved, the nectar fills me with energy is as sweet as human singing of opera with rhythm and high notes Caterpillar: What I need to do to be someone as beautiful and free as you, to stay and go whenever you need to feel at home and run away from home Butterfly: you just have to wait, beautiful Caterpillar: BEAUTIFUL? Maybe not the fat, ugly and creepy I am! Every day I dream of having my own shape and color that when I pass they recognize me and they do not run away, because as I am, only... and I got them to fear me, I'm harmless, but nobody knows me Butterfly: YOU ARE BEAUTIFUL! Because I go through that, and I know that you can be even better, you will go higher, you will have more colors, and more anecdotes, take it easy Caterpillar: I want more butterflies like you that make me feel lights, rainbows and things that I still believed I could not feel Butterfly: you take the time, handle it your correct address

title: Emily, Monsoon and Frogs
text: Monsoon was in full swing. Rain stopped only sometime back, still trees were filled with water diamonds and leaves showered water if branches were moved to and fro. Puddles were formed every here and there. Few of the puddles were still with the reflections of sky, the trees and other surroundings, while the other puddles were filled with small-small circular waves with some wriggling creatures. Emily was waiting for her school bus with her mom. But, her eyes were watching the small fishes with wriggling tails in a puddle. She wondered what kind of fishes they are. Emily was studying in third grade. As her name meant, she was very eager/ striving girl. “P-eeeep-eeeep, P-eeeee-p!!” sound of the bus horn came and she sat in the bus waving bye to her mom. At evening, she went for a walk with her father like every day. She observed the same kind of fishes in the other puddles like she did in the morning. Her eagerness spurred. “What are those, papa?” Emily asked her father. “Those are tadpoles, Emily.” her father replied gently. “What are tadpoles?” asked avid Emily. “Tadpole is one of the stages of frog when it grows from an egg to an adult frog. It is called life cycle of frog.” Her father answered. “Oh!! I thought these are some kind of fishes..So, how does a tadpole grow into frog? What are the other stages of frog’s life cycle?” Emily asked enthusiastically. “Tadpoles find their food from water and they grow into froglets and then, to the adult frogs.” said Emily’s father. “Papa, where do the tadpoles come from? What are froglets?” Emily strived for more information. “A female frog lays hundreds of eggs covered in a jelly like material and releases them in water. This is called frogspawn. These eggs hatch into tadpoles after few days. Fishlike tadpoles have big head and a long tail.” Her father started explaining her about the stages of frog development. “After few weeks, tadpoles develop back legs and front legs. This stage is called froglet. Then, the tail disappears slowly and froglet transforms to an adult frog. ” Emily’s father told. “Papa, where do the tadpoles come from? What are froglets?” Emily strived for more information. “A female frog lays hundreds of eggs covered in a jelly like material and releases them in water. This is called frogspawn. These eggs hatch into tadpoles after few days. Fishlike tadpoles have big head and a long tail.” Her father started explaining her about the stages of frog development. “After few weeks, tadpoles develop back legs and front legs. This stage is called froglet. Then, the tail disappears slowly and froglet transforms to an adult frog. ” Emily’s father told. “Wow!! But papa, how do the eggs and tadpoles grow into frog? What do they eat?” little Emily’s curiosity roused. “The eggs get their food from the egg yolk itself. Tadpoles eat algae, small plants and even tiny bugs to grow. Froglets don’t eat other food, they use up their own tail as their food to grow into an adult frog.” Emily’s father said. “How interesting!! Papa, can we take few tadpoles to our home and grow them to frogs at home?” Emily found the little creatures interesting. “Yes, of course!! We need to grow them in clean water and feed them as per their requirement. While rearing tadpoles at home, you can also observe the development of frog through different stages of growth. It would be a very fascinating experience for us to rear and study them.” Her father said joyfully. “Really?? Please let us take some tadpoles home, papa.” Emily requested her father. “Sure, dear!!” said her father collecting few tadpoles from a puddle in a water bottle. “Yayyy!! How fun!!” Emily said jumping. Happy and thrilled about her new friends, Emily went back her home with her father. Activity Write the names of different stages of life cycle of frog.
author: Riddhi Nath

Because it was a bud, not a fruit, silly! Now Flippy was tiny but she was really very smart To sip nectar she could use her beak like a dart But oh no! She went overboard... and she poked and she poked.... Until the bud burst open and gave her a start! Flowerpeckers are among the tiniest birds in India, measuring only around 8cm from beak to tail! The Pale-billed Flowerpecker is one of this family, and is heard more often than seen, with its 'tik-tik-tik-tik' calls. Common in South India, it loves the fruit of the Singapore Cherry tree! title: Andrew Brutus & the canary!
text: Andrew grinned at the bird. It just stared at his face. A cat was crouched behind the wall, ready to spring at the canary. Andrew gripped his Beretta 92FS. The cat sprung. The Coke can flew out of his hand. He fell back with a thud, and the canary screeched in a sudden panic, and flew up. His dad was just driving into the garage. Andrew fired the handgun at the cat., but the barrel was empty. He dashed to the attic, before the cat could kill his bird. “Where’s my Ammo gone?” he muttered. Dad walked in. “Dad! My bullets are missing?!” Dad ignored him. The cat was jumping up. He ran where the attack was happening, past the kennel... THE KENNEL! He opened it, and his dog was wagging his tail. “Save my pet bird, Brutus!” the dog chased the cat away, and came back to Andrew, and he smiled. The bird wasn't too badly off. “What happened with Brutus?” asked dad. Andrew stared. “Just joking, I know what happened. I confiscated your ammo, I didn’t want you using a gun. Who gave it to you, anyway?” “Marcus, our neighbor.” “Put Brutus back,” said dad. “Ok dad,” Andrew said. The bird was set free so cats couldn’t harm it, and Brutus stayed inside the house, and they lived happily ever after.
