She knew that if anyone found out that she was Dr. James Barry she would no longer be allowed to be a doctor. Everyone had to believe Dr. James Barry was a man. Dr. James Barry fought when he thought something was wrong. In Cape Town, people with leprosy were banished to Robben Island. The lepers were put on the island because people believed they could catch the disease from them very easily. Dirty houses and bad food made the lepers much sicker. Dr. James Barry asked the leaders in Cape Town for cleaner living conditions and healthier food for the sick people on Robben Island. Many years later, Dr. James Barry worked in a war hospital. Here he met Florence Nightingale, a nurse. Florence Nightingale was also known as The Lady with the Lamp, because she would check on wounded soldiers at night. She became famous during the war because she asked the army leaders for cleaner living conditions and healthier food for the soldiers. Dr. James Barry had been asking for the same things for many years. Dr. James Barry traveled all over the world. He worked in South Africa, St. Helena, Barbados, Mauritius, Trinidad and Tobago, Malta, Corfu, Jamaica, Crimea, West Indies, Canada… 11 places in all. What exciting adventures he had! People only found out that Dr. James Barry was a woman when she died in 1865. In the same year, Dr. Elizabeth Garret Andersen became the first woman to become a doctor in Great Britain. Dr. James Barry has shown us that girls can do anything they want.
author: Michelle   Matthews

title: Miss Tiny Chef
text: Kasini is eight years old. She loves to cook. She reads a cook book on the school bus every morning and before bedtime. Nobody knows her secret, that she sleeps with a wooden mingling stick every night. When she sleeps, she dreams that she is smiling, wearing a chef’s hat and holding her mingling stick high up in the air. Kasini loves to sing as she cooks. She sings to the carrots and dances with the flour. She slices the cucumber and places two on top of her eyes. She bangs the saucepans loudly as she jumps up and down. “GET BACK TO WORK.” the stick scolds. “Cooking is not work, it’s fun,” Kasini laughs. The stick tells her if the soup needs more salt, if the chicken needs more heat and when the Ugali is ready to eat. Sometimes Kasini doesn’t listen to the stick. “I will use my palm to taste the soup,” she says. “I will use my mouth to taste the chicken,” she decides. The stick laughs for she is young and it is old. Older than the cutlery in the house, older than Kasini’s older brother. So old it knows all the great recipes by heart. Kasini adds more salt, pepper and curry powder to the soup. This is wrong and she knows it but she is only being stubborn. The stick doesn’t like being disrespected, it changes colour from brown to red to show Kasini that it is angry. “The soup will burn without the mingling stick!” moans Kasini. She sings for the stick, but there is no change. “I am sorry,” she says. The stick turns back to brown just in time and Kasini hugs it in joy. “Now I can serve mummy the food I made,” Kasini says excitedly. “The food we made,” she giggles, as she tucks the stick away.
author: Linda Nabasa

title: The Three Doof-Doofs
text: What is that? What is that doof-doof-doof noise? A cat? A mouse? A visitor in the house? No, it’s something even furrier than a cat, even cuter than a mouse, and much tinier than you and me. It’s the three Doof-Doofs. These sweet creatures have only one foot each to hop on. And each hop makes a thumping doof-doof on the floor. AHHHH UHHH! Here is Solly Doof, the smart one, who is always thinking looooong and loud. He uhhs and ahhs and doof-doofs all night long. He reads daytime stories to the other Doof-Doofs, because unlike you and me, that is when they sleep. Thinky, stinky Solly Doof prefers reading over bathing any time. And here is Sally Doof, the smallest and sweetest Doof-Doof of the three. In a little quiet voice, she sings doobee-doobee Doof-Doof songs, when it gets a bit too quiet in the night. She likes finding shiny things and cuddles. Snuggly, huggly Sally Doof who loves to sing. Clink C lank Clunk! Don’t forget Silly Doof, the funniest Doof-Doof in the house. He is always joking. Hahahahaha! Wiggly, giggly Silly Doof will make you laugh until your tummy hurts. He cheers up the other Doof-Doofs whenever they feel sad. He loves to dance on his big silly foot, to the songs that Sally Doof sings. So, if at night you ever hear a strange doof-doof noise again, remember, it’s just the three Doof-Doofs, reading, singing and dancing on their one doof-doof foot. So sleep well, little one. Or keep one eye open... Because maybe, just maybe, you’ll see three cute little creatures hopping past on one foot, going doof-doof-doof.
author: Claudi  Potter; Wynand Botha

title: The Three Friends
text: Anna and Stacy were the best of friends and were enjoying the last few summer holidays at Anna's home. It was nice sunny day and they were busy running around the yard and making sand castles. Suddenly Stacy heard a low mew.She ran after the noise. There it was, a small brown and white kitten hidden in the bushes and mewing. It looked hurt. Anna and Stacy picked it up and saw that it was hurt near the leg and ants were around the wound. Anna called her mother and she came with a small shoe box. Her mother picked it up carefully and put Kitty on a soft cloth. They went inside home, mother cleaned the wound and put some cream on the kitten’s leg. She must be hungry Anna said.She filled a bowl of milk and put in front of kitten.But it could not get up and lap up the milk. Why don’t we use a small dropper? Stacy said.Mother fetched a dropper and together Anna and Stacy fed her. They named the kitten Caramel because it was brown in color.Anna and Stacy took turns taking care of Caramel and in a few days it was fine and was playing with them.They taught it tricks to play with wool and to catch a ball.They spent their evenings running with Caramel and tickling its neck. Caramel loved the attention. One day a big brown cat came near their home.She was purring and mewing.Caramel was also mewing and trying to jump the fence. ”Looks like that is Caramel’ s mother and it has come looking for it. We should let Caramel go “ said mother. “No!” Anna and Stacy shouted.She is our pet, we love her.We cannot let it go anywhere. ”But darling listen, imagine if someone kept you away from me.Will you like that?” Mom said. “No, I don’t want to be away from mom”. Anna and Stacy said together."Then you need to let Caramel go." Anna and Stacy moved ahead to let Caramel out of the basket and to its mother. mother. The cats started licking each other and nuzzling. Anna and Stacy were sad to leave their new friend and went inside home.Mom made a nice cake to cheer them up. The girls were a bit sad the next morning when they were getting ready for school.But they were happy that Caramel found its mother. When they were walking to school, they heard a mew, they looked back and found Caramel walking behind them to school! They were so excited.They played with her till they reached school.Caramel stopped near school and walked back to its mother. From then on, every morning Caramel accompanied Anna and Stacy till school gate and they remained the best of friends!
author: Madhavi Agnihotri

title: Small Bird's Big Adventure
text: Small Bird was a small bird. He was very small and very birdy. Small Bird lived in a beautiful house with the Giant. Small Bird loved the Giant very much. She was a kind Giant. She gave Small Bird lots of toys. Small Bird was sad when the Giant wasn’t around. So one day Small Bird went to go find the Giant. Small Bird flew up and up until he could see the whole world. He wanted to find the Giant. Where would he land? Small Bird landed in a huge forest, filled with trees and flowers and treasure. Small Bird loved playing with the shiny jewels! But where was the Giant? Small Bird walked into a vast field of snow. The snow was white and soft. Small Bird loved rolling around on the cool ground. But where was the Giant? This time, Small Bird flew even higher into the sky. He flew among the stars and galaxies! He saw the moon! He saw a comet! But where was the Giant? From way up high, with his sharp birdy eyes, Small Bird saw something! What could it be? Small Bird dived down, down, down. Where would he land? Small Bird landed right in the Giant’s hands! He was so happy to see her. “I love you, Giant!” he shrieked. The Giant held Small Bird close to her. “I love you too,” the Giant said.
author: Nick  Mulgrew

title: A Joyful School
text: One fine morning all baby animals went to school. But in the school, they found the teacher fox was not present. They felt very happy and began to dance in the classroom. Suddenly the head teacher elephant entered in the classroom. The baby animals got afraid. They stop dancing. But the head teacher said" No no don't stop. I came here to dance with you all."
author: Saiparna  Bera
illustrator: Aliya Shetty Oza; Ketan Raut; Namrata  Gosavi; Niloufer Wadia; Rob Owen

title: Where is Thabo?
text: It’s Monday morning and Thabo’s family is getting ready for the day. Mama is in a hurry. She sloshes her tea across the counter. But where is Thabo? Slow down, Mama. Baba is in a hurry. His clothes are all wrong. But where is Thabo? Slow down, Baba. Zinzi is in a hurry. She gobbles up her cereal. Has anyone seen Thabo? Slow down Zinzi. Thabo! Where is Thabo? Thabo is not in a hurry. Hurry up, Thabo! You will be late for school and remember, it’s soccer practice today. Thabo is in a hurry. Hurry up, everyone. It’s soccer practice today.
author: Melissa  Fagan

title: Clever Pig
text: Come Pig! Let’s play. Can you find the carrot? No, it’s not under there. No, it’s not inside. Clever Pig! Wake up, Pig! Come out and play. Where is she? Pig is gone. The sun came up. And the sun went down. But, no Pig. I miss my friend. My Pig! Clever Pig. And one, two, three new friends! Come, pigs! Let’s play. Time for bed! Goodnight, pigs.
author: Nathalie  Koenig

title: Nurture the Seeds
text: Neha was given a new class assignment. On reaching home she said to her mom, "please give me some dry peas. Teacher has told us to sow them, keep them in sunlight and water them daily. We have to show the plants to her after a week." Her mom replied, "Neha since it is your assignment, it is your responsibility. I will guide you if you need any help. Neha agreed and sowed the dry peas in a pot and watered it. Next day, Neha forgot about the peas. After a week, her teacher reminded them to get their assignment to school the next day. Neha panicked for a moment, but then remembered sowing the peas and was sure that they would have grown into plants. On reaching home, Neha went to check on the peas. But she was shocked to see that there were no plants in the pot. She screamed, "Oh Mamma, see this! The peas which I had planted have not grown. I must tell the teacher that peas don't grow like this." Her mom asked her, "Neha, why don't you check with your classmates if their seeds too didn’t grow?" So Neha visited her friend Poonam's house in her neighbourhood to check her seeds. Poonam's seeds had grown into plants. Poonam explained to her that she had watered them daily and now they had grown into beautiful little plants. Neha realised that she had forgotten the teacher’s instructions to water the seeds daily. She returned home and told her mom, "Mom, we forgot to water the plants." Her mom smiled. She said, "Neha, I did remember, but I wanted you to learn to take responsibility for your own assignment. Neha could not submit her assignment the next day but learnt a valuable lesson about taking responsibility for one's assignments. She re-planted some peas and watered them daily and this time they grew into beautiful plants. About the Author Dr. Jyoti Hegde is a Corporate Behavioral Trainer and a Life Skills Trainer for Kids based in Goa. Jyoti has a degree in Ayurvedic Medicine. She has over thirteen years of work experience in the medical field and has worked in various hospitals/medical centres in Bangalore and Goa. Jyoti has been personally trained and mentored in the field of behavioral training by Corporate Behavioral Trainer, Amey Hegde. Jyoti has also been trained by various master trainers to practice and implement international concepts of Positive Psychology, Facilitation Skills, and Neuro Linguistic Programming (NLP) in developing and conducting training programs. Jyoti is a co-creator of the Life Skills Diamond Model, a framework for holistic development of children. She has created an ebook “Polishing Real Diamonds” containing quotes about child development. Jyoti also writes articles and stories related to child development and shares them on her blog Jyoti has co-conducted training sessions on various aspects of behavioral training for employees from reputed organizations like Sanofi, Vedanta, Dona Sylvia, Funskool, The Leela Goa etc. She has recently started CHAMPS a year long programme on Life Skills and Personality Development for kids. She also conducts open-to-public Personality Development and Public Speaking Workshops for students. Jyoti is an active member of Toastmasters International, an educational organization that is a world leader in communication and leadership development. Jyoti's passion is to make a positive difference by conducting impactful sessions for kids on the values, habits, and life skills needed for health, happiness and success.. Please send your feedback to jyotiheg@gmail.com Read her other stories for kids at
author: Jyoti Hegde
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Debasmita Dasgupta; Ketan Raut

title: My fish,no my fish!
text: Sita thought for a moment and said "don't do this,fishes will die when separated by water" They didn't paid attention to her and continued on their way to the pond. Raja and Ram sat near the pond and saw to fishes jumping in water,one was a thin and second a fat one. There came a third fish. They didn't saw any fish bigger than this! Sita said" This fish is even bigger than my father's foot!" Raja and Ram took their fishing rods with and struggled for the fish. Ram said"its mine!" Raja said"no,its mine!" Raja pulled the rod, Ram pulled stronger. BOOM! They fell down as their rods broke. Do you know why? Any guesses? fished tied their strings together!
author: hyder  abbas

title: The Sea
text: On a very hot day, on a holiday day, we go to the beach. To the sea. We go to the sea, my family and me. On the edge of the sand is the water. That’s where my toes touch the sea. The waves play a game. They say yes, I say no. They run up to meet me, and I run from the sea. They say no, I say yes. I run back to the edge. I chase the waves home to the sea. They say yes, I say no. They say no, I say yes. The sea chases me, and I chase the sea. There is blue. There is sea spray. In the game, I can’t be still. A chasing wave brings me a shell. It leaves it for me on the wet sand. I find a feather in the dry sand, and I send it on a wave to the sea. Then the waves say yes, and I say yes too. I have sea and sand in my toes. Oh, I love the sea.
author: Nicola  Rijsdijk

title: Chapati Lost, Chapati Found
text: There was a dog at Kamal's home. His name was Bhaunku. One day, Kamal went to give his dog Bhaunka a Chapati. Suddenly, a monkey stole the chapati and ran. He ran and sat on top of the terrace wall. A bird saw the chapati. She then stole it from the monkey. She then flew to the Pipal tree in the yard, and sat on it. There was a peacock sitting on the tree. She saw the chapati. The bird realized and immediately flew to save the chapati from the peacock. Bhaunku started barking from down, "bhaw-bhaw-bhaw-bhaw!" The bird got scared. She started saying, "kaav-kaav!" She dropped the chapati from her beak. The chapati fell into the yard. Bhaunku quickly picked up the fallen Chapati. The chapati was finally with the rightful owner.
author: Harshit Didwania

title: My Fingers, My Hands
text: How will it be fixed? but look! hands did a wonderful job in rounding papers, collecting pens, sweeping flour, hanging spoons, picking brushes, pens and books! My fingers, my hands... flip the pages, touch the books. See the pictures, with the eyes read the stories... whenever they are tired or have some spare time!
author: Ruby Gaylong

title: The adventures of Bhaunku
text: One day, Kamal went to Bhaunku to give him some bread. Suddenly a monkey snatched the bread and ran away. The monkey went and sat on the wall of the terrace. A crow flying past saw the bread. The crow snatched the bread from the monkey. He flew to a tall tree in the courtyard. He sat down at the top. There was a peacock sitting on the same tree. He saw the bread. The crow quickly flew away to try and save his bread. Bhaunku made a noise from down below, "Woof woof!" The crow got scared. He said, "Caw-caw!" The bread slipped out of his beak and fell in the courtyard below. Bhaunku jumped and picked up the bread right away. The bread was returned to its rightful owner.
author: Charvi Singh

title: Where is my bat?
text: I lost my bat. I cannot find it anywhere. I looked behind the door. It wasn't there. I climbed and looked up. I couldn't find it there too. I looked under the bed. But it wasn't there either. I searched in the suitcase. But I couldn't find it there too. I looked up, I looked down. I looked here, I looked there. Not here. Not there. Not anywhere. Nowhere.
author: Harshit Didwania

title: Tap-Tap-Tap
text: There was a forest. Very dense. One day, it started raining heavily. Next day, the sun came out. All animals came out. There was a sudden noise - Tap-Tap-Tap. Everyone got scared. The lion thought. The Leopard thought. The elephant thought. The bear thought. What is this sound? The bear got scared. He went and hid behind the bushes. The deer started shivering. He ran away. The leopard also didn't stay there. Lion said, "I am not scared." But he also slyly left. Large animals ran away quickly. The ant said, "Let's go friends, let's find the Tap-Tap-Tap." Let's see who that is. There is nothing to be afraid when we all are together. The rat said, "Good Job, Ant brother" Everyone left to look for Tap-Tap-Tap. Then everyone saw, that rain water was dripping on the leaves - Tap-Tap-Tap. The ant said, "Look!", proudly. Everyone shook their heads in agreement and smiled.
author: Harshit Didwania

title: Bablu's Peacock Dance
text: Hindustani Devi This is Bablu's school! Raju said, "The festival is next Sunday. It will be fun!" "Oh, it will be fun to watch Bablu dance. That little boy can dance like a peacock." said Nandu. Two teachers were talking about the same thing. "Bablu can perform the peacock dance really well now. It should be fun to watch him." Bablu's mom and dad too were talking about Bablu's dance. "We'll get to see Bablu perform his peacock dance on Sunday." It was Sunday, the day of the festival. The stage had been decorated. The audience was seated, ready to watch the show. Bablu was wearing a costume decorated with real peacock feathers that he looked like a real peacock. His teacher gave him the cue to dance. Bablu said, "I am not going to dance. My friends, uncles, aunties, Mom, Dad, all are here to watch Bablu dance. I will not dance. I am going to sit with them to watch Bablu dancing." The teacher said, "You are Bablu! Everyone is here to watch your dance performance! If you don't dance, what will anyone watch? You can watch the video of the dance afterwards." "I don't care. I am going to watch the performance with everyone else." said Bablu. One of the teachers got a huge mirror and placed it at one end of the stage. "Bablu, why don't you dance and watch yourself dancing in the mirror? That way, you will be able to watch the performance with everyone else." Bablu loved the idea. He watched himself dancing in the mirror and he performed the peacock dance very well. Everybody clapped their hands for him, delighted with his performance.
author: Thangjam Hindustani Devi

title: Ice Cream made of Clouds
text: She kept changing colors! When Sarala laughed, the kite turned pink. When Sarala was angry, the kite turned red. When Sarala was sad, the kite turned blue sometimes, and yellow sometimes. And when Sarala was chirpy, the kite turned green. One day, the kite was flying high in the sky. Down below, Sarala was holding the string and giggling. She said, "fly higher kite! Fly higher!" The kite flew higher and higher and reached the clouds. In the clouds, the kite found a little fairy. Seeing the kite, the fairy also got very happy. Both of them spoke sweetly. They even flew together! Seeing it was getting late, Sarala tugged at the kite's string. The kite told the fairy, "Now I need to leave. My friend is calling me." As a gift, the fairy gave the kite an ice cream made of clouds. It was soft and fluffy like cotton! The kite told the fairy, "we will meet again." The fairy said, "I'm coming too." The kite gave Sarala the fairy's present, ice cream made of clouds! Sarala said to the kite, "You are so dear to me."
author: Charvi Singh

title: The Clever Chicken
text: Once upon a time, a hen and her 8 chickens were searching for food here and there. Suddenly, a jackal came around. Looking at the fat, healthy chickens, his mouth started watering. He then decided to eat them all. He said to the mother hen,"You look unwell, I will take you to see a doctor." He quickly took the mother hen to the bushes nearby and ate her. Now he wanted to eat the chickens too. The jackal went near the chickens. He was unaware that the hen's feathers were stuck on his long mustache. Seeing the feathers, the chickens got scared and fled. But the youngest chicken could not run. She went and hid inside a hollow pumpkin. The jackal growled, "Oh kid, now I am going to eat you." And just then, the jackal smashed the pumpkin on the stone. But the young chicken flew and sat on the bark of a nearby tree. "How should I eat you now?", asked the Jackal. "Open your big, wide mouth and I will jump into it", said the tiny chicken. The jackal opened his big mouth and stood under the tree. The chicken dropped a big fruit in it and the jackal choked and died. And the young chicken flew away happily.
author: Ruby Gaylong

title: Mom, Hurry Up!
text: I woke up in the morning. I rubbed my eyes. I could not see mom. "Mom! Mom! Come fast." Mom responded from the other side, "Yes son, wake up! Wash your hands and face." I quickly take a bath. Put on my shirt. I have to leave early. "Mom, listen to me!" "Yes, yes! I am coming", says mom. "I have to boil the milk. I will come after that." I combed my hair. Buttoned up my shirt. I am completely ready. "Mom, be quick." Mom hands over the clothes to my sister. Dresses her up. She has so many things to do in the morning. But, I have to rush. "Mom, I am getting late." I pick up my bag and bottle, wear my shoes too. "Lets go Mom, hurry!" "Yes, I am coming. First, let me comb your sister's hair. I need 5 more minutes. Then we will leave" "I want to go now. I am not going to wait." I feel like crying. My sister left for school, and I am still here. "Almost done! Just have to fill the water." Mom always has something or the other to do. "Mom, hurry up. I will not wait now." "Mom, lets leave. Now!" I pull my mom, holding her hands. "Oh, but let me first turn off the lights." Now we are outside the house. Mom locks the door. "Lets go son!" Now I am happy. Mom is with me. She calls me with love and I am going to the school.
author: Ruby Gaylong

title: It's just a game!
text: Hindustani Devi There was a baby elephant called Golu, round as a drum. There was a baby rabbit called Chotu, fluffy as a cotton-ball. They used to play together. One day, Golu said, "Let's play something new." Chotu said, "Kneel down, and I will jump on your back in one hop. Golu knelt down. Chotu jumped up. Chotu landed on Golu's back. "Wonderful!" said Golu, laughing, "Now you kneel down and I will jump on your back!" "You?" "Yes, me!" "How can you jump?" said Chotu, trembling. "Like this!" said Golu, jumping up in the air. Thud! Thud! Thud! Coconuts rained down Golu's back. Startled, Golu ran off. One tiny coconut too landed on Chotu. "Phew! Better this coconut on my back instead of the elephant!" thought Chotu, thanking his luck.
author: Thangjam Hindustani Devi

title: My Aaji has a tail
text: Have you met my Aaji? Everyone says that my Aaji has a tail. Aaji’s tail follows her all day long, Mumma says it even does a pirouette when Aaji sings my favourite song. I wonder, why haven't I seen it yet? Papa says the tail is growing long and strong. It even answers Aaji's phone when she gets a call. What! Why haven't I seen the tail yet? My teacher says the tail helps my Aaji a lot. It even helps water the plants in the pots. Sigh! I haven't seen it yet. The bus driver told me the tail sits next to Aaji in the bus. And imitates everything that she does. Someone please tell me, why haven't I seen the tail yet? One day I asked Aaji, "Everybody says that you have a tail. But why haven't I seen the tail yet?" Aaji laughed out loud, and pulled out her phone. Look! It's me. And that's me, it's me again. It's me everywhere! Now I know why everyone says that my Aaji has a tail. Because it was always ME following Aaji on her small and big trails.
author: Gauri Dalvi

title: And Bablu danced
text: This is Bablu's school. Raju said, "There is a fair next sunday. We will enjoy it." Nandu said, "We will enjoy seeing Bablu's dance. He'll dance like a peacock." The teacher was saying, "Bablu has learnt the peacock dance well. We will enjoy seeing his dance." Bablu's parents were talking to each other. "We will see Bablu's peacock dance on Sunday at the school." It was the day of the fair. The stage was set up. People were sitting on the chairs. Bablu was decorated with feathers and turned into a peacock. The teacher asked him to dance. Bablu said, " I will not dance. My friends, uncle, aunt and parents will all see Bablu's dance. I won't dance. I will see Bablu's dance with him. The teacher explained to him, "You are Bablu! If you do not dance then what will we see? You see the dance on the video later." "No. I'll see it with everyone now", said Bablu as he started to cry. The teacher put up a big mirror in front of the stage. "Bablu you dance and see yourself in the mirror. That way, you and everyone will see your dance at the same time" Bablu, without any worries, danced like a peacock. Everyone clapped.
author: Harsh Thakar

title: Aksha and Sasha: The Story of Friendship
text: One day, a girl and her friend came into class. One girl named Sasha did not like school,but the other girl named Aksha loved school. They were best friends. Aksha enjoyed going to school. She was the teachers pet. Aksha got all A's. Aksha's dream was to become a teacher. Her teacher always said, "Aksha, you will become a great teacher. Maybe even better one than me." But Aksha always got teased and bulli ed at schools. Everyone thought she was weird. Aksha didn't like this. Even though people judged her, she kept studying. She did not give up on her dreams. Sasha was very good in sports like soccer. But again she was very bad at school. Her grades were horrible, mostly all below C's. No one cared about grades though. That's why Sasha had a lot of friends. They called themselves the squad. Sasha bullied kids all the time. She thought it was funny, but Aksha didn't appreciate that. Nobody fought back because they knew that was not the right thing to do. One day, Aksha got tired of Sasha bullying kids and didn't want to be friends. Sasha missed Aksha. She thought about her every day after school. Finally, the girls decided to work thing out. The girls me t and talked to each other. Aksha made Sasha promise that she would be nice to everyone. The two girls danced and played around for hours. Sasha started being nice and apologized to everyone she hurt. That night, all was well.
author: valliyappan swamynathan
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Nilesh Gehlot; Soumya Menon; Sunando C; Suvidha Mistry

title: Babloo's Dance
text: This is Babloo's school. Raju said, "We have the school programme next Sunday. It will be fun." Nandu said, "The fun will be in watching Raju dance. The small boy will dance like a peacock." Two teachers were talking among themselves. "Babloo has learnt the peacock dance very well. It will be fun to watch his performance." Babloo's parents were talking among themselves. "On Sunday, we will get to watch Babloo's peacock dance at his school." It was finally the day of the meeting. The stage was set. People sat down in the chairs to watch. Babloo was wearing a costume decorated with peacock feathers. The teacher gave him the signal to dance. But Babloo said, "I will not dance. My friends, aunts and uncles, mother and father - they will all watch Babloo dance. I will not dance. I will only watch the dance with them." The teacher said,"You are Babloo. If you do not dance, how will they see the dance? You can see the dance on video later." Babloo replied, "Whatever happens, I will watch the dance only with them." So one teacher put a big mirror on one side of the stage. "Here Babloo, you dance and watch yourself in this mirror. This way, we all will be able to watch the dance together." Babloo danced like a peacock with lots of energy and vigour. Everyone clapped for him.
author: Vrinda Singh

title: How the lynx got it's big teeth
text: A long time ago in a jungle there lived a lynx, a cow, a deer, a bear and a ibex. Lynx was sitting in a tree and Deer and Bear came up to Lynx. “ Hi “ said Bear. “ What are you doing Lynx? “ asked Deer “ Nothing “ replied Lynx. When out the corner of Lynxes eye he saw Ibex chasing cow. “Go away!” Cow mooed. Lynx leaped down the tree to try help cow, after Ibex ran away. After that, all the animals huddled up to discuss about Ibex. “It needs to stop” Bear exclaimed “he's annoying everyone.” “Who wants to go in” asked deer. Lynx raised his paw and said “I'll do it." The next day Lynx was watching Ibex chase Cow and Lynx jumped out of a bush and scared Ibex. Ibex got scared and ran away Lynx chased Ibex and caught him. His gums got caught on Ibex’s horns and the horns snapped off. After Lynx got the teeth off Ibex’s horns Lynx showed it's big teeth and glared at Ibex. Ibex ran away and never bothered anyone ever again. And that's how the lynx got it's big teeth.
author: Enrico
illustrator: Clay Jakobi; Enrico; Ketan Raut; Muniza Shariq; Preeti Krishnamurthy

title: The Biscuit Jar Must Fall
text: Micki and her friends Lolo and Unathi were reading their favourite books. “If you help Micki clean her room, ”Prudence said, “you can all have biscuits afterwards.” “YAY!” But they carried on and read and read and read. Then they stopped reading and cleaned Micki’s room. “My room is tidy now,” Micki said. “Let’s go and get biscuits.” But they could not find Prudence anywhere. Micki, Lolo and Unathi stared at the biscuit jar on the top shelf wondering how to reach it. So they found a chair and took turns to climb on it. But none of them could reach the biscuit jar. “My mama would say this is dangerous and we could fall and hurt ourselves,” Lolo said. So Lolo sat on Unathi’s shoulders and stretched out his arms but could not reach the biscuit jar. “My father would say this is dangerous and we could fall and hurt ourselves,” Unathi said. So they found a rope to throw around the biscuit jar and pull it down. But they could still not reach the biscuit jar. “My mummy would say this is dangerous and the jar could fall on us and hurt us,” Micki said. “What are you doing?” Jonathan and Sakhi asked. “We are trying to reach the biscuit jar,” Micki said. “We can help you,” they said. “Let’s push the table close to the shelf and climb on that instead,” Jonathan said. But still, none of them could reach the biscuit jar. “Let’s throw a ball at the jar and knock it down so that the biscuits fall out,” Sakhi said. “Yes!” Lolo and Jonathan said. “No!” Unathi and Micki said. Finally, Micki had an idea… And that is how, together, they reached the biscuit jar!
author: Nozizwe  Herero

title: Watch and learn
text: I want to help, Father!", said Sona Father begun to saw through the wood. "I want to use the saw as well, Father!", said Sona while extending her arm. "Yes for sure, but be careful!", said Father. Father started to add the wheels. "I also want to put the nails", said Sona whilst picking up a hammer. "Yes my dear, but you need to watch carefully first.", said Father. The car was finished. Father started putting threads. "Where did I leave the pencil and thread?", wondered Father while looking everywhere. He became worried. Sona laughed and said, "Should I look for it?" Sona pulls the pencil from behind her father's left ear and thread from his right. "I was watching very carefully, Father", said Sona. "Oh Sona, you were such a big help today!", Father said with love for his daughter.
author: Anam Akhtar

title: Zanele Sees Numbers
text: Everyone tells Zanele that numbers are all around her. But no matter how hard she tries, she can’t see them. Zanele asks Gogo to help her see some numbers. Gogo points to the jars on the shelf and counts, “one, two, three, four.” But Zanele is unhappy. “Those aren’t numbers. Those are jars!” Zanele asks Mom to help her see some numbers. Mom points to the carrots in the garden and counts, “one, two, three, four.” But Zanele is unhappy. “Those aren’t numbers. Those are carrots!” Zanele sees Linda counting the chickens, to see if they have all come back home. But Zanele is unhappy. “Those aren’t numbers. Those are chickens!” Zanele sees Auntie counting the hours until supper. But Zanele is unhappy. “Those aren’t numbers. Those are hours!” Zanele can’t see the numbers in the world. She goes to speak to her sister, Gugu, who is eight years old and knows everything. “If you look at anything in the right way, you can see a number in it,” says Gugu. Gugu gives Zanele a pair of magic glasses and tells her to go look for numbers in the world.
author: Laura  de Lange

title: The Big Bad Wolf and the Clever Jackal
text: Once upon a time there was a jackal. He went to search food in the jungle far an far. In the forest lived a big bad wolf. He wanted to eat the jackal. He went to the jackal and said, "I will eat you." The jackal had an idea. He said to the wolf, "I am stronger than you. Come I'll show you." And he took him to the animals. All the animals got scared of the wolf and ran away. But the wolf thought that they got scared of the jackal. So the wolf said sorry to the jackal. Moral of the story: When we are in trouble, we should always use our mind and find an idea.
author: Jyoti Hegde

title: My Puppy, Samson
text: This is my puppy, Samson. He is 2 years old. We like to play a lot of games. Samson lets me know he's ready to play when he looks at me and wags his tail. Samson loves to use his nose to find treats. I hide his favorite treats around the house and ask him to "Find it!" Samson sniffs all around the house until he finds his treats. He is really good at this! Sometimes, when he is busy finding his treats, I like to find a hiding spot so that he'll need to find me next. He found me! We love this game. We play it again and again. After playing "Find it" and "Hide and Seek", we like to play music and dance. Samson has some smooth moves. Samson brings me so much joy every day. I love my puppy.
author: Vanessa Sadueste

title: Louise the Chef
text: This is Louise. She loves to try new things! One day, Louise's mother said, "Louise, come help me make bread." "Ok!" said Louise. She wanted to learn how to make bread. The first thing Louise and her mother needed was flour. Flour is made from wheat. Louise helped her mother create dough using the flour and oil. After Louise made the dough, her mother helped her put it in the oven to rise. After several minutes, her mother took the bread out of the oven. The bread looked delicious! Good job, Louise!
author: Jacquelyn Wong
illustrator: Miza Magalhães; Rob Owen; Sonal Gupta Vaswani

title: Where is my toy?
text: Its not here, its not there Where is it? Its not on the couch Its not under the bed Its not in the box Its not under my sister's dress Its not under the desk Its not in my bag What what....where did it go? I looked everywhere in my room, and under most of my books I have looked under the chair, I have looked under the seat Where did it go? My grandma came back from her walk. "Look what I found in the park!" It can come back, it can go forward It can turn, it can lean "Haha" said my grandma as she laughed Oh my grandma! Thank you so much! You have found my toy (yoyo) Yoyo? What an interesting name! It is an enjoyable toy! I want to play with it, it fills me with joy and happiness My grandma laughed as she played with my yoyo for the rest of the day
author: Menna Ehab

title: Music Down the Hill
text: There was once a fox, a raccoon, and a deer in the forest. They were best friends and lived at the top of the hill. One day they heard music coming from the bottom of the hill. They did not know where it was coming from. They had never been down the hill before and were scared to go. They decided to overcome their fear and go down the hill. They made it down safely and were glad they did. The music was loud and happy. They loved the music! They listened and danced all day. Later they had to go back home up the hill. But now they were not afraid anymore of going down the hill. The happy music was stuck in their heads all day. They told all their friends about the music. They were excited and decided to all have a dance party. Now no one on the hill was afraid to go down the hill.
author: Samantha Tse

title: My Hands and My Fingers
text: Hands can.. knock and clap and snap! My hands can pull and push, and pick paper, shoes, pen, spoons and even a big car! My hands can touch the softness of dough, wetness of soap, a brush that's rough, a pointy pin and icy cold water all with great pleasure! My hands are very strong... They can pick up a heavy box even if it is out of my reach! But oh gosh, they also make so many mistakes sometimes! The heavy box slipped out of my hands! They all fell down.. The papers, shoes, pens, spoons, dough, soap, brush, pin and all the colourful books! All the things have fallen...there is mess everywhere! How to fix this? But look! My hands did a miracle- collected paper, pen and dough, hung the spoons, kept the brush, picked the pins, and books? My fingers and hands... turn the pages, feel the books, see the pictures with my eyes Read stories, whenever they get tired or when... ever I get free time!
author: Garima Gupta

title: My Family
text: I am Tuktuk. I have a big family. Let's meet them... This is my mother, and this is my father. Here is my brother Neetu and my sister Meetu. Oh look... Now, my paternal and maternal grandparents are also here. My mother has three sisters. I call them all Aunties. And look... My father has four brothers. Two elder and two younger. Along with them... are their wives, two elder aunties, and two younger aunties. Look, look, look... My family also has five small kids. We all have a lot of fun together. Look! How big my family is. Wait, wait!! I forgot about Buzo, who wags his tail and barks all day... Woof!! Woof!! Woof!!
author: Garima Gupta

title: Grandpa's Garden
text: This summer, Beth is visiting her Grandpa. They have lots of fun together! They ride bikes. They go for walks along the water. They play games. Beth's favorite activity is helping Grandpa with his garden. She gets to dig a hole in the dirt and plant a seed. Every day she and Grandpa water the plants and watch them grow. At the end of the summer, the best part is that Grandpa and Beth get to eat all the yummy food they grew!
author: Kristin Kahlich
illustrator: Lavanya Karthik; Niloufer Wadia; Priya Kuriyan; Samidha Gunjal

title: Willy the Willow Tree
text: My name is Willy the willow tree. I am tall with green leaves. I have lots of friends who like to climb my trunk and branches. Sometimes they hide too well and their friends can't see them. The dog barks. Who do you think he sees? It is a red bird! Now I have even more friends! Two children, a dog, and a bird. I am a happy tree.
author: Hannah Peter

title: Eyad's Pigeons
text: My name is Eyad. Every morning, dada takes me to the balcony to listen to the birds. Pigeons are my favourite! T here are always so many in the sky. Dada says they can carry messages and recognise our faces. Some are white, like my dada’s beard. Some are grey, like my dadi’s hair. Some have shades on their neck. I hope to find out more about them, when I grow up. The pigeons coo when they hear me hum. When I come too close, they fly away in a flock. They flap their wings so hard that some of their feathers fall off. The pigeons do backflips in the air. Does that mean they are happy? I wish I could do backflips too! They poop all over the balcony. That’s why dada hates them! But I do not want the pigeons to leave, I ask dada if I could keep one. “We cannot force them to stay,” dada says. “Birds are meant to fly wherever they want.” “Why can’t I fly?” I ask dada. “We all have special powers,” he says. “Pigeons can fly and see colours that are invisible to us.” “Do I have a special power?” I ask. “Yes,” dada says. “One day you will find it.” “I cannot wait,” I say. “Neither can I,” dada says. Did you know? Historically, pigeons were used to deliver important messages. That is because they have the amazing ability to return to their homes even when they are thousands of kilometres away in an unknown location. One of the greatest examples is a pigeon named Cher Ami. She was awarded a bravery medal from the French Army for saving 200 people in World War I by delivering a message even though she was injured. A note about pigeons Do not feed pigeons, they can manage by themselves! And like Eyad’s dada says, do not keep birds in cages. They are meant to fly in the sky.
author: Sadia Tabassum

title: You Can't Find Me!
text: My name is Mia. I am going to the market with my Ma. I am the best at hide-and-seek in the world! You will never find me in the market. And I will find the things on my Ma’s shopping list before you. Find: (1) 10 red chillies (2) 2 green tomatoes (3) 1 potato (4) 1 fat pumpkin Oh no! How did you find me? Find: (1) 6 yellow bananas (2) 3 oranges (3) 1 red apple (4) 1 green papaya with stem You found me and the fruits on my Ma’s list! It won’t happen again. Find: (1) 5 roses (2) 1 purple garland (3) Jasmine flowers (4) Flowery shorts This is not fair! I am the best at hiding in the world! Find: (1) 1 lungi with dots (2) 1 sari with green stripes (3) 1 school uniform with squares (4) 1 plain black T-shirt Did Ma tell you where I was hiding? Let me see how you find me now. Find: (1) 3 pinching crabs (2) 1 angry squid (3) 7 prawns (4) 2 fish on ice You got lucky so far. But you will never find me in my own house! Find: (1) 1 big pot (2) 1 wooden spoon (3) 1 box of matches (4) 1 bottle of water You found me AG AIN! Okay, I cannot play anymore. I have to go eat lunch. I would have won if Ma had not asked me to stop playing. I am the best at hide-and-seek in the world! Answer key: (1) 10 red chillies (2) 2 green tomatoes (3) 1 potato (4) 1 fat pumpkin Answer key: (1) 6 yellow bananas (2) 3 oranges (3) 1 red apple (4) 1 green papaya with stem Answer key: (1) 5 roses (2) 1 purple garland (3) Jasmine flowers (4) Flowery shorts Answer key: (1) 1 lungi with dots (2) 1 sari with green stripes (3) 1 school uniform with squares (4) 1 plain black T-shirt Answer key: (1) 3 pinching crabs (2) 1 angry squid (3) 7 prawns (4) 2 fish on ice Answer key: (1) 1 big pot (2) 1 wooden spoon (3) 1 box of matches (4) 1 bottle of water
author: Jemma Jose

title: Foxy Joxy Plays a Trick
text: Foxy Joxy was a sly fox. He sold big, fresh watermelons. Watermelons for sale! “Your price is too high,” said Rabbit Jabbit. “You are asking too much,” said Gia Giraffe. Foxy Joxy had a clever idea. He slit open a big watermelon, scooped out the fruit, and gobbled it up. Then he filled it with water! He took a needle and thread and sewed the watermelon back together. He sold his water melons for a cheap price. Many animals bought from Foxy Joxy. “This watermelon has only water in it,” complained Funky Monkey. “Well, you got what you paid for,” said Foxy Joxy. “We need to teach Foxy Joxy a lesson,” said Ellie Elephant. The animals gathered around and came up with a plan. “I have an idea,” said Oliver Owl. They took an empty watermelon, stuffed Foxy Joxy into it... and played a game of football with it. Foxy Joxy was dizzy! He learnt his lesson and never cheated again.
author: Nahida  Esmail

title: Miss Bandicota Bengalensis Digs Up the Seashore
text: Meet Miss Bandicota Miss Bandicota Bengalensis was a little Indian mole rat who grew up in a maze of burrows with her mother, seven sisters and ten brothers. They were terrific pests, the nineteen of them, always out on a rampage. One night she was out foraging as usual, when suddenly, she heard an angry human voice. Quick and nimble, she just managed to escape from the farmer's scary grasp. As she was fleeing, she looked into the eyes of a mole rat stuck in a trap. Those were the saddest eyes she had ever seen. She was so terrified that she huddled in her mother's burrow all night, her eyes tight shut. In the early hours of twilight she announced to everybody's dismay that she would never attack a farm again. All her brothers and sisters tried to change her mind, but she would not budge. She soon became bored and restless and realised that she couldn't sit in that same old burrow any longer. She quietly packed her explorer's kit with her sunglasses, binoculars, magnifying glass and, of course, her favourite - a strip of sticker bandages. Her mother was worried. "Whatever will you do? Whatever else can you do?" Miss Bandicota Bengalensis smiled and said simply, "I can burrow." So she burrowed and burrowed and burrowed and burrowed. But there was never a dull moment, for every burrow she dug went to some place new. And she would never need to attack a farm again. On the Seashore Somebody raised her tiny nose out of a hole in the sand. Who was that? Miss Bandicota Bengalensis! She had just emerged from a new burrow after a long night of digging through sand and clay. The sun was going to rise. Just as she was about to set her sunglasses on top of her nose, she caught a glimpse of the world above. In a flash she was washed back into her burrow. As she struggled to find solid ground, she yelled frantically, "Help, help! The river has burst it's banks!" "There's no need to panic. This is the Arabian Sea," said a calm and reassuring voice drifting nearby. A baffled Miss Bandicota Bengalensis scrambled out on to the soggy sand. As she shook her dripping tail, she felt the soft, wet ground sinking slowly beneath her. She was looking down at her toes uneasily, when she noticed something bright and blue floating between her feet! "You've reached the beach of Bordi, seventeen kilometres of fabulous sticky sand!" it said. In a fraction of a second, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis had grabbed the magnifying glass from her kit. The very next moment, she was keenly examining the fascinating little creature, as it lingered on, quite unperturbed by this sudden intrusion. It was a strange-looking animal; a round body, silvery grey in the middle, surrounded by a turquoise-coloured ring and numerous translucent tentacles branching out radially. "Who are you?" asked Miss Bandicota Bengalensis inquisitively. "You can call us Porpita. We are a colony of polyps," it said, swimming by lazily. "I'm Miss Bandicota Bengalensis. Whatever is... er... are polyps?" As you might already know, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis could never resist asking a question. "Sort of like a family," it answered. "We live together and work in unison. Some of us breathe, eat; some of us taste or feel and some of us make little new polyps." Miss Bandicota Bengalensis was most intrigued. "That doesn't sound like my family at all. We all live in our own burrows, collect our own food and make our own baby mole rats." "How quaint!" remarked Porpita, "It must be quite tiring to be a mole rat." "Not at all, we... glug glug glug... glug... glug..." Poor Miss Bandicota Bengalensis swallowed a mouthful of sea water as she was knocked over by a large wave. "Thoo... thoo... thoo," she spat out, wincing at the horrid taste of salt water. Almost immediately, she leapt towards the shore, dodging another quick wave. As the waves subsided, she turned around to ask Porpita yet another question. And stopped in wonder. Scores of sparkling polyps, just like Porpita, were gliding leisurely over the rolling waves. It was as if t he night sky had gently dropped countless twinkling stars into a magical sea. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis stood mesmerised by the polyps that dipped and rose gently with the waves of Bordi. She bid them a silent farewell as they faded into the tranquil waters. "Deeper! Deeper!" An eager voice shook Miss Bandicota Bengalensis out of her daydream. Her drowsy eyes fell upon a couple of human kids digging the sands of Bordi with funny-looking tools. From her last trip to Kaas Pathar, the plateau of flowers, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis had learned that not every human was a danger to mole rats. So she rushed in to play. "Can I dig too?" she pleaded anxiously, "I love to burrow!" The kids shrieked and bolted, flinging their beach toys away. Miss Bengalensis looked baffled. She had grown up running away from humans. This was the first time she had seen humans run away from mole rats! "We're not all out to catch you, you know?" she hollered after them. But the kids had long disappeared. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis looked at a bright green toy lying next to her feet. She picked it up and made a futile attempt to dig with it. 'No wonder humans can't burrow!' she thought to herself. She dropped it and began to stroll down the lonely shore. Further down the beach, she came upon a peculiar sight. Tiny balls of sand were scattered around in puzzling patterns. It was as if the seashore was dotted with constellations. 'The mystery of the curious sand balls!' thought Miss Bandicota Bengalensis. Her face lit up. Holding up her magnifying glass, she was lost in her investigation. Suddenly, she felt a small pinch at the tip of her tail. Swinging around, she spotted a crab looking up at her. "No need to be nasty! I was just looking," Miss Bandicota Bengalensis said reproachfully, tucking her tail between her legs. "Sorry about that! I was just going about breakfast when your tail came in the way," said the crab apologetically. "Oh, never mind! Mole rats nibble all day too. I know what you mean," replied Miss Bandicota Bengalensis, for she happened to be a very forgiving mole rat. "I'm Mrs. Scopimera," said the crab. "I'm Miss Bandicota Bengalensis. Do you know where these tiny balls of sand came from?" "Oh, those are just sand bubbles! We make sand balls like that when we suck our food in." "And do you make them yourself or do you also have a family to help you, like Porpita?" asked Miss Bandicota Bengalensis. "Oh! You mean the polyps? I've seen them stick together in rings, bobbing in the water all day. We sand bubblers are nothing like them," she said proudly. "We wander the beach sands, sometimes in pairs, sometimes alone." "We do have large families though," she continued. "My children must be down there, up to some mischief or the other. Would you like to play with them?" she said in a friendly voice. A little Scopimera peeped out of a hole and called, "Come on, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis. We're building a maze! Will you help us with the burrows?" "Burrows? I love burrows!" Miss Bandicota Bengalensis sprang into the nearest hole, head first. Immediately, she was stuck! She was upside down in the sticky sand, her head in a hole and her legs sticking out in the air. Not one to lose heart easily, she threw her kit into the hole and promptly started burrowing to make a tunnel. The little sand bubbler crabs were thrilled. They had never seen anyone burrow so fast! They all began digging industriously, some sideways, some backwards, some upside down and some all around. In no time the seashore of Bordi was dug up into a secret maze. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis wanted to try out every new tunnel in it! Can you help Miss Bandicota Bengalensis get back to her travel kit through the secret maze? Miss Bandicota Bengalensis scurried excitedly through the underground maze at lightning speed. She finally reached her travel kit with shining eyes and a triumphant smile. She had never crossed so many new burrows in such little time! As she climbed out of the hole, she gasped in horror, "The sea has vanished!" She scampered around in circles, only to turn back again and again, "Gone! Disappeared!" As her eyes grew bigger and rounder in shock, more and more Scopimera kids clutched at their tummies and rolled in laughter. Poor Miss Bandicota Bengalensis! "There! There! It's just low tide," said Mrs. Scopimera kindly, coming to her rescue. "It's just low what?" asked a puzzled Miss Bandicota Bengalensis. "Low tide. The sea water recedes during low tide and returns when the tide is high. Nothing to worry about, you know, it happens twice a day. That's when we sand bubblers get to eat. We have to rush into our holes again when the waves return." "But where does the sea go?" "Just far, far behind. The water only seems to disappear over the flat and gentle Bordi sands. If you look hard enough, you will see a foamy white line. That's where the shore is now. " Miss Bandicota Bengalensis fished out her binoculars hastily. Sure enough, she could see the waves of the Arabian Sea in the distant horizon. She heaved sigh of relief and collapsed on the sand. All that running around had made her very hungry and very thirsty. So she she began yet another journey, this time in search of food and water. Mrs. Scopimera accompanied her down the beach, up to the rows of casuarina trees. There, she wished Miss Bandicota Bengalensis luck and returned to her children. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis trotted ahead, along the edge of the beach. Her legs began to hurt. The tip of her tail, where Mrs. Scopimera had pinched it, was smarting. Always prepared, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis stuck her sticker bandage around her tail. The strong little mole rat walked steadily on, even as the rays of the sun beat down upon her. After what seemed like a zillion steps, she reached a sharp bend in the road. As the coast turned inwards, to her joy, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis discovered a charming grove of chickoo trees. The branches, laden with soft brown fruit, swung low. The orchard grounds were strewn sweet ripe chickoos. A farm pond lay nestled in the shadows of a hundred trees. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis first rushed to the edge of the pond and drank to her heart's content. Now refreshed, she dashed around the trees, madly gathering a heap of chickoos. She made a heap any self-respecting mole rat would be proud of! Pleased with the morning's work, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis leaned back to admire the most alluring pile of fruit she had ever seen. Her greedy fingers couldn't wait to poke into the soft ripe skin. Her greedy toes couldn't wait to jump on the pile. Nobody saw the very hungry mole rat pounce on the chickoos. But before long... A busy honey bee was foraging around in the afternoon, when she came upon an enormous pile of black and beady chickoo seeds. A happy mole rat lay curled in a hole beneath it. "A good worker works all day and sleeps only at night," muttered the honey bee. A very sleepy Miss Bandicota Bengalensis turned over and murmured, "Sleep at night? No, no, no, not at all. Tonight, I must dig a new burrow..." Bandicota bengalensis, also known as the Indian mole rat, is a giant rat of South Asia. It is not related to the true bandicoot. They can be up to 40 cm long, including the tail. They are seen as pests because they damage cereal crops and gardens. They make pig-like grunts when attacking. The name 'bandicoot' is derived from the Telugu word pandikokku, which translates to 'pig-rat'. Did you know that Porpita porpita is also called the 'blue button jellyfish'? But it is actually not a jellyfish at all! As you now know, it is a colony of many tentacle-shaped animals. They all float together and eat through a single mouth in the centre of the button! Can you believe that the chickoo (scientific name: Manilkara zapota) is not from India? It came from faraway Central American countries like Mexico. The chickoo travelled across the oceans with adventurers just like Miss Bandicota to reach the shores of India, maybe about 200 years ago. The sand bubbler crab does not have lungs. So how does it breathe? It has 'gas windows' on its legs, through which it takes in oxygen. At high tide, the land crab depends on the air trapped in its burrows. At low tide, it emerges, to feed and make sand bubbles.
author: Aditi Ghosh

title: Hello Friend!
text: When I went for my First Day of School I saw A lot of people everywhere and Shaking hands with Teachers and other Staff I saw Teachers Greeting them and they Greeted Back "I wonder why they always greet them, because they always come tomorrow" I wondered When I went Inside, there were a lot of Students in The School and the staff room for helping them, I saw 2 Girls Giggling... "No Students were supposed to go to the Staff Room" I Thought I saw a few Mad teachers, at First I didn't know why, but I think They were mad for Children for Coming in and Helping. When Me and My Dad went in my Classroom I saw A family. I talked to the student and Played while my Dad and My friend's family waited "Hi, what is your name?" I Asked. "My name is Shelli. What is your name?" Shelli asked. "My name is Kurti. Can you tell me about this school?" I asked to Shelli. "So when last year I came there were a lot of people in the staff room and the teachers were mad. I asked them about this School. They Agreed to tell it to me" Shelli said "What did they say?" I asked "They said that your Friends will be Enjoying new students and they get chocolate and Lolipops for you and the Year goes exiting every day for you until next year... They pick a person if a new student doesn't come" Shelli Said "Thanks For letting me learn about this school." I Said "Where do you get picked?" I asked "They vote each other" Shelli said Whoa, I don't like to vote. So I told him "Why can't we do Elimination" I asked. "Nah. We don't do elimination" Shelli said I like Shelli so much that I asked him to be friends and he said 'Yes'.
author: Sri Niranjan G Shivakkumar

title: Senzo and the Sun
text: The morning sun creeps over the horizon and peeps through the leaves, waking Senzo. Gogo’s rooster shakes his wings, stretches his neck and crows. Koek-a-loek-a-loo! Senzo can crow too. Koek-a-loek-a-loo! Can you? The sun is bright and warm. Senzo is ready for school. He takes Gogo’s hand. The road is busy. Taxis zip past and toot their horns. Beep-beep! Beep-beep! Senzo can toot too. Beep-beep! Beep-beep! Can you? The sun is high in the sky. School is over and Senzo’s friends play on the grass. They stretch out their arms and run down the hill. Weeeeeee! Weeeee! Senzo can run too. Weeeeeee! Weeeee! Can you? The sun is low on the horizon, the sky is full of colour. The long day is nearly over and supper is finished. Gogo and Mama wash the dishes. Splish -splash! Splish -splash! Senzo can wash dishes too. Splish-splash! Splish-splash! Can you? The sun is dipping under the horizon, casting long shadows. Senzo is washed and full and tired. “It’s time to sleep,” says Mama. She holds Senzo close and rocks. She hushes him. Shhhhhhhhh, shhhhhhhhhh. Senzo can hush too. Shhhhhhhhh, shhhhhhhhh. Can you? The sun has done her work for the day and she’s going to sleep. She pulls a blanket of darkness over herself to keep warm. The sun dreams. Senzo can dream too. Can you?
author: Sarah  McGregor

title: The Lion Who Wouldn't Try
text: It was a sunny day in the jungle. All the animals were out playing. “Come play with me, Lion,” said Cheetah. “Catch me if you can!” ZOOM-ZOOM! went Cheetah. “I don’t want to play,” said Lion. “I’ll lose.” “Come play with me, Lion,” said Elephant. “We can throw rocks! ”KA-POW! KA-POW! went Elephant. “I don’t want to play,” said Lion. “I’ll lose.” “Come play with us, Lion!” said the monkeys. “Who can eat the most bananas?” POP! POP! POP! went the monkeys. “I don’t want to play,” said Lion. “I’ll lose.” “Come play with me, Lion," said Springbok. “Let’s jump high!” ZOOP! ZOOP! ZOOP! went Springbok. “I don’t want to play,” said Lion. “I’ll lose.” “Come play with me, Lion,” said Crocodile. “It’s a swimming competition!” SPLASH! SPLASH! went Crocodile. “I don’t want to play,” said Lion. “I’ll lose.” Elephant and Crocodile had the swimming competition without Lion. Crocodile was quicker than Elephant, but each time Crocodile got ahead, Elephant tickled him! TEE-HEE-HEE! went Elephant and Crocodile. Lion sat sadly by himself, watching Crocodile and Elephant swim. “Why are you sad, Lion?” asked Mouse. “Because I don't want to play,” said Lion. “I'll lose." Lion slipped on a banana peel! WHEEEEEE! went Lion. “That looks like fun!” said all the other animals. Lion played, and he was happy.
author: Liza  Esterhuyse

title: Angela, the village girl
text: once upon a time, in a mountain village on the alps lived a girl named Angela. Angela had lost parents when she was 3 years old and lived in a small hut with her aunt Tanvi. She loved to spend time just watching and observing the wonderful nature around her. one day she noticed something fascinating in the prairies around her hut. A beautiful pink butterfly had fallen unconscious on the grass. Another blue butterfly which was fluttering nearby stopped by and seemed to mutter something and disappeared quickly. As Angela was watching with her wide eyes, the blue butterfly reappeared from somewhere with some fresh herbs. The blue butterfly vigorously rubbed the herbs on the pink butterfly. To Angela’s amazement, the pink butterfly woke up and started fluttering around. Both the butterflies flew away happily. A few days later, Angela heard that a small girl in a nearby village had fainted. Hearing this news, Angela quickly went looking for the very same herbs and brought it to the little girl. SHE vigorously rubbed the herbs on the little girl. Lo and behold! the little girl gained consciousness. Everybody in the village thanked angela for her quick thinking and kind gesture. Angela was also very happy and went back to observing the wonderful nature around her. NATURE HAS A LESSON FOR EVERYONE
author: Smitha HS
illustrator: Jeyanthi Manokaran; Rajiv Eipe; Sanjay Sarkar; Smitha HS

title: My Family
text: I have a BIG Family....let's go and meet them This is my mother and this is my father! Meet Nitu..my big brother and Mitu..my big sister And here are my both maternal and paternal grandparents! My mother has three sisters..and I call them "Mavshi "* (*Maternal aunts in Marathi are called "Mavshi ") My father has three brothers...two elder brothers and two younger brothers..I call all of them "Kaka "* (Kaka =paternal uncle in Marathi) and meet my aunts....two elder and two younger..I call them "Kaku"* (*Kaku =paternal aunt is called Kaku in Marathi) And my family also has five small kids!!!! And we play together and have fun together! see..I have a big and lovely family!!! oops!! How can I forget this important family member!! Meet my pet:Bujo!He loves to roam around me and does "woof..woof " all the times!!!
author: चिन्मय (Chinmay ) गवाणकर ( Gavankar )

title: Tanvi,The Cute Girl
text: In the village of alps, there lived a cute little girl named Tanvi. She used to walk in the garden of her house and liked to look at the trees. One day, she got bored of looking at the same trees in her garden everyday. As she was sitting in front of her garden, she saw an elephant and a parrot coming to her. As Tanvi was watching the elephant and the parrot, she had got one idea.Her idea was to go with the elephant and the parrot to the forest. Tanvi sat on top of the elephant and went to the forest. As she went, she looked at many things- how butterflies fly,how frogs jump and more. After Tanvi came to the forest, she picked many fruits for the parrot,elephant and herself. After she spent a lot of time in the forest, she was taken to her home by the elephant and the parrot. After she came back to her home, she was very tired and went to sleep.
author: Meghna Nair

title: Incy, The Milk Tooth!
text: Incy, the milk tooth was a brave and bold incisor. For five years he had faced challenges with a sparkling smile! But more recently, he had been wobbling for days. He knew he had to pack up his belongings because soon it would be time for a change. On Monday, Incy faced a red, juicy apple head-on. But nothing happened to Incy. On Tuesday, he chewed on a cool, green cucumber. But nothing happened to Incy. On Wednesday, he chomped his way through a long, crunchy carrot. But nothing happened to Incy. On Thursday, he gobbled up cookies and cupcakes, fresh from the oven. But nothing happened to Incy. On Friday, he bit on hard almonds and walnuts. But nothing happened to Incy. On Saturday, he feasted on chocolates and candies. But nothing happened to Incy. Finally, on Sunday, Incy got stuck to a chewing gum! Ouch! I t was a sad day for him. He said to himself, "Today is the day when I must leave home and be by myself, all alone!" "But I love my home. It has been so cosy inside this d ome with my milk teeth buddies," Incy sighed. "In the past when I peeped out of the gums for the first time," he said, "I was welcomed with a party. All through these five years I was treated like royalty and brushed twice daily." "Pampered with sweets galore; in a lifetime could a milk tooth ask for more?", he recalled. "Alas! I have been shown the way out; to make place for someone else no doubt," he wept. "A keepsake tin box is my new home from where I will go nowhere to roam", Incy realized. But oh! What do I see? My old friends are here, waiting for me! Yippee!
author: Gitanjali Mehra

title: The Lion King and his Canopy
text: One day the king of the city went to the jungle. He rode his elephant. The king was sitting on a soft mattress. The mattress was kept inside a decorated canopy, tied to the elephant's back. The canopy was providing shade to the King. He looked so proud and happy enjoying the ride. Now, our Lion king saw this. He said to himself: I am king too. I will also ride the elephant. He immediately summoned the wild elephant. The Lion told him, that his mind is full with the idea of the elephant ride. Because that is what Kings from the cities do. The poor wild elephant got scared. He pleaded, " Oh King, we live in jungle. It is not right to copy the King from the city" But, the Lion king was in no mood to listen to the poor elephant. In a single leap, he mounted on the elephant's back. But, how could he have the style and show of the king from the city! The monkey was just there. He was curiously observing this. He commented, "Oh King, the King from city rides the elephant in a canopy. Not like the way you are riding". The Lion king pondered for a minute. He ordered the monkey. "Go right now and bring the canopy maker here" What could the poor carpenter do? He was scared for his life. As the Lion king roared, the carpenter made a beautiful canopy for the Lion king. The Lion king was happy. He ordered the carpenter, to tie the canopy neatly on the elephant's back. Once all was set, the Lion King leaped again and this time seated himself in the canopy. The carpenter immediately ran away. So scared he was, that he had forgotten to tighten the ropes of the canopy. Here, the Lion king ordered the elephant to march. As the elephant started moving, the canopy started swinging right to left and left to right. Finally, the canopy, hit a tree and tilted on a side. Then what? There was a big sound "" Dhadaam dhoom "" And the Lion king found himself lying on the ground. The monkey was barely able to hide his laugh. The elephant had run away in fear. Slowly, the Lion king gathered himself and was back on his feet. While rubbing his bruises, he declared "Never again an elephant ride. Animals must walk on their own feet. That's my order."
author: Abhay Kale

title: We went to the market
text: There are many shops. There are many people. Some people do shopping. Some people just watch. What will my mother do? First we went to the grocery store. Mother bought wheat, sugar, and pulses. We had not taken a bag with us for the grocery. The store will send the grocery home. After that mother went to the vegetable store. I asked, "Will you buy vegetables, mother?" Mother said, "No." The vegetables vendor screams, "Come, come, buy, the vegetables are fresh!" Why did mother stop here? Oh, this is the oil store. The store smells of oil. Mother complains to the shopkeeper, "The oil is very expensive." The shopkeeper doesn't like it. Then we went to the fish market. Some people don't like the smell of fish. I like fish a lot. See! How the fisherwomen dress! Can you spot the fat cat? It only rests there, and is getting fat eating fish all the time. We stopped at the dairy. Mother bought some butter and cottage cheese. Why do they not stock ice cream? I like ice cream a lot. What do you think, my mother will buy me ice cream? "Will you buy some utensils?" I asked my mother. There was nobody in the utensils store. When there are weddings or festivals, then people buy utensils. Wait, "Oh mother! Don't go into this store!" I shouted. My mother likes the clothes store. The storekeeper shows her a lot of sarees. But she doesn't buy even one. I wanted just this! The toys store! The teddy bear i so big! I want this scooter, and this toy truck...! I promised my mother, "I will only touch and see the toys but I won't ask for any today. I will only take one on my birthday."
author: Lalita Dhanvada

title: Can I do something too?
text: I too, do something? Shall I throw a ball? Shall I carry my baby brother? Or shall I play the Tabla? Or maybe I can ride the bi-cycle! Shall I put on my new dress? Or let me rectify the ball of wool! Shall I water the plants? Shall I feed the baby goat some grass! or shall i draw a picture! Let me go fly a kite? Or shall I just laugh out loud!!!! Ha ha ha!
author: radhika ponnala

title: Teacher Ledibadi
text: Ladybird is our new class teacher. She loves singing and dancing. She says she was never meant to be a teacher. Her parents forced her into teaching. Her father even changed her name from Lendebadi to Lady Bird saying, "that is trendy. Everyone will call you Lady, you hear?" I did not hear and I do not like to be called Lady Bird. I call myself Lendebadi because I love it that way. Besides, it means loving and caring. this is what I am. A loving and caring person. "Come and I will tell you another story class. I would rather tell stories that stand here in a heap than teaching what does not make sense to me." She says, as she gathers us into a circle to hear her childhood stories. Whenever she did this, her face turned bright and clear. Her wings changed to yellow. Other moments, her face was gloomy and full of tears. And so the story goes. Many years ago, when my mother was a young girl. She had many friends. They all dressed alike. Then one day, something strange happened. The court of one of her friends turned yellow. They didn't know what to think, say or do. "Should we be sad?" They wondered. That day, it rained heavily. No one knew why it had rained so much like that. They could not even trace their way back home. Then they started looking for their friend. Where is she that had a yellow coat? She was no where to be seen. But the running water was yellow. "See, she has drowned in the rain." One of them shouted out. No! Shouted another. "She is washed up." "Her real coat is not yellow. That is the colour of paint." They chorused. But still, they could not see their friend. "I am here, shouted Ledibadi." Smiling. I like to be me. No painting. No colouring. "Yes!" they all shouted. "I will be me!" And, that is when spider came. He snatched one. Then snatched another. Until all the friends were gone. Mother remained sad and lonely. That is why she changed her name too.
author: Cornelius Wambi Gulere

title: Excursion
text: There were five friends - A monkey, mouse, rabbit, squirrel and bear. There was a tiger in the jungle. One day they went for a picnic. They played I-spy and Catch the Thief. They also ran a lot and played for quite late. The monkey said "We should eat something now, Please bring something". Everyone brought something. The rabbit brought a carrot. The bear brought a cabbage, the squirrel brought a tomato, the mouse brought a radish. Everyone washed the fruits, cut them and mixed them up. Then came the time to eat. The bear said "Wow!, this is unique. Tell the name of this dish". The mouse said - "This is called Chaat". The squirrel said, "This is Mixed fruit". The monkey said, "This is called Salad. Eat a lot, build your strength". The mouse said, "I will eat this from now on. I have to become a tiger when I grow up". Everyone started laughing.
author: Anurag

title: Should I do something too
text: I do something too? Should i play with the ball Should I take my little brother in my lap Should I play drums Should I ride a bicycle Should I wear a new frock Should I fix the entangled wool shell ﻿ Should I water the plants Should I feed the baby goat, Or make a drawing Should I fly a kite Or should I laugh out loud.
author: Aditi Singh

title: Drip-Drip-Drip
text: There was a dense jungle. One day it rained heavily. There was a bright sunshine the next day. All the animals came out. Suddenly, there was a dripping sound. Everybody got frightened. The lion, cheetah, elephant and bear wondered! "What kind of sound is this?" The bear got frightened. He hid behind the bushes. The deer started shivering. He ran away. The cheetah also didn't stay there. The lion said, "I am not frightened". But, he also ran away. All the big animals ran away quickly. The ant said, "Friends, lets go and search for this dripping sound. Lets see who is it. If we are together, why to fear?" The mouse said, "Well done, Brother Ant!" Everyone started to search for the dripping sound. Then they saw that the rain water was dripping on the plant leaves and was making this sound. The ant proudly said, "See!". Everybody nodded in agreement and smiled.
author: Anurag

title: Drip-drip-drip
text: There was a jungle. Very dense. One day it rained heavy. Next day it was sunny. All the animals came out. Then there was a sound- drip, drip, drip. All got scared. The tiger thought. The cheetah thought. The elephant thought. The bear thought. What is this sound? The bear got scared. He hid in the bushes. The deer started shivering. It ran away. The cheetah also did not stay. The tiger said, "I am not scared." But he also slid away. The big animals all ran away. The ant said, "Friends, lets go and find drip-drip-drip. See who it is. If we are all together, what is there to be scared!" The mouse said, "Bravo, brother ant!" Everyone went to find drip-drip-drip. Then everyone saw, the raindrops were falling on the leaves - drip-drip-drip. The ant said proudly, "See?" Everyone nodded their head and smiled.
author: Lalita Dhanvada

title: The tale of Kake
text: Kake is a crow! He cleared his throat and cawed a few times. Suddenly, he could hear the beautiful song of the cuckoo. Kake enjoyed the song for sometime, but then, he got angry. This is not fair! When the cuckoo bird was just an egg, it was a crow that incubated and hatched her but she has such a beautiful voice! "I shouldn't feel jealous" Kake thought to himself! I should learn how to sing beautifully from her, decided Kake. Kake searched and found the cuckoo, but she was suspicious. Courteously, Kake asked the cuckoo, "Will you teach me how to sing beautifully, like you"? The cuckoo replied, "Yes, I can teach you on one condition. You should come here everyday at sunrise." Kake agreed. "Then we can start the training tomorrow" cuckoo said and got back to her work. Kake likes sleeping very much. He hasn't woken up before sunrise till now. But he has singing practice tomorrow! And so, he set an alarm in his clock. The next morning, he woke up to the alarm energetically and went to his singing class. The cuckoo bird was waiting impatiently and started the class as soon as Kake sat on a nearby branch. "Please sing this first" she said and sang "Coo... Coo...". Kake also tried singing but no matter what he did, he was only able to sing 'Caw... Caw...'. The cuckoo waited for sometime, but lost her patience. "You can't do it" she said, "Please find someone else" and flew off. Kake was very disappointed. He returned to his nest, dejected. "Hey peacock! Can you teach me to dance?" Kake asked the Peacock. "Of course! Watch me and do the same" the peacock said. Kake spread his tail feathers and jumped to the beat. "This is not right" said the peacock. "Look at me carefully" he said. Kake tried again and again but he couldn't dance like the peacock. The peacock was angry, "You can't dance at all" he cried and flew away. Kake became very sad. He can't sing or dance! At least let me learn how to build a good nest, he thought and went to a sparrow. After the sparrow heard Kake's request, he proudly said, "You can never build a nest like me" and sent him back. Kake was very disappointed. How can I master at least one thing? He looked down from his nest and saw that there were some rice grains in the backyard of the house below. He then cawed loudly "Caw...Caw..."calling all his friends and family. All of them had a nice meal. Then, he understood. He can't sing or dance beautifully, or build a nest well. But who else shares their meals with others? Not a cuckoo, not a peacock and definitely not a sparrow. No one except him and other crows. Kake was very happy after he understood this about himself. He was very proud to be a part of this generous family. The other crows saw that Kake was happy and asked playfully"Kake! you look happy, are you getting married?" Kake blushed. Color it as you wish.
author: Akila Muthukrishnan

title: Ice-cream from the clouds!
text: Sarala loves to fly kites. Kites also love to spend time with Sarala. Sarala's favourite kite always tries to keep Sarala happy. The kite even changes colors to keep Sarala entertained. Whenever Sarala laughs, the kite turns pink, and red when Sarala gets angry. If Sarala is lost in thought, the kite turns blue or yellow. One day, the kite began to fly really high. Sarala laughing said to the kite "fly even higher". The kite flew higher and higher and even crossed the clouds. Beyond the clouds, the kite met a little angel. The angel was also happy to see the kite. As Sarala was getting late, she pulled at the thread. The kite realizing that Sarala had to go, said to the angel "My friend is calling me. I need to go". "See you later!" said the kite to the angel. "Bye bye', said the angel. On the way back, the kite brought some ice-cream made from the cool clouds and gifted it to Sarala. Sarala was very happy and said, "You are my favourite kite!".
author: radhika ponnala

title: Mom, hurry up!
