text: I woke up early I rubbed my eyes I Couldn't see mom Mom, mom, please come soon! Mom says from there, "Yes dear son, get up! Freshen up, wash your face and hands!" Let me take a bath quickly Then wear my shirt I need to go early. "Mom, listen to me!" "Yes, I am coming," Mom explains. "I need to boil milk, I will come after that!" Let me comb my hair, button up my shirt! I am ready now! "Mom, please hurry" Mom gives cloths to my sister She gets her ready. There is so much work every morning. But I am in a hurry! "Mom, I am getting late" Let me pick my bottle and my bag. Let me also put on my slippers! "Now I am going mom! Please hurry!" "Yes, Yes, I am coming! Allow me to comb your sister's hair, I need five more minutes. Then we will go. " I need to go now. I am not going to stop. I am about to cry. My sister has already left for school, and I am still here. "Its almost done! Just need to fill water!" Mom always have some or the other work. "Mom, please hurry, I won't stop now" "Lets go now. Right now!" I begin to pull my mom by het hand. "Oh, at least let me switch off the lights" Now we came out on the road. Mom locks the door.
author: karan bansal

title: Cloud ice cream
text: It kept Sarala happy every step. When Sarala laughed it became pink. When she would be angry it would become red. When she would be sad it would become blue or yellow. When Sarala would be chirpy it would be green! One day the kit was flying high. Sarala was laughing and holding the thread below. She way saying fly higher! Flying high the kite crossed the clouds. There it met a little fairy. The fairy was happy to find a kite. Realizing that it was getting late, Sarala tugged the the thread. The kite said, "I will leave now. My friend is calling me." The kite said, "We'll meet again." The fairy said, "I'll also come." The kite gave Sarala the fairy's gift, cloud ice cream! Sarala said, "You are so dear to me kite!"
author: Lalita Dhanvada

title: The lion's howdah
text: One day he saw the city's king. The king was sitting arrogantly on an elephant. The lion called the jungle's elephant and told him the voice of his heart. The elephant got frightened. The lion did not agree. He sat on the elephant, but it did not had the charm of a king. The monkey said, "My lord, Kings sit on a howdah, not like this" The lion ordered, "Go and make a howdah". The howdah also came. A howdah similar to city's king got prepared. The howdah got placed on the elephant's back. The lion jumped and sat in it. But as soon as the elephant walked, the howdah started shaking. It wasn't tied properly. It struck a branch of the tree and got turned upside down. The lion fell down. The lion never sat on an elephant ever again. He said "Walking on foot is the best".
author: Anurag

title: The cat's feast
text: There used to lived few fat cats in a far-off village. Few rats also used to live in the very same village. One day, the fat cats thought of having a feast. The called the chef. He lit up a fire and then cooked rice, pancakes and several other dishes. The rats were smelling the food and hence were getting very happy. They asked their chief for a permission to attend the feast. The rats went to the feast. There was music playing and both cats and rats were dancing together. Several musical instruments were being played. The rats knew the meaning of this. While dancing, they ran through their holes. The fat cats had to accept their defeat. Because what is a feast without tasty rats!
author: Anurag

title: An Ice-cream of clouds.
text: Sarla was cheerful, she would be green. One day the kite was flying high in the sky. Sarla was holding the kite by its thread, laughing and urging the kite to fly higher! The kite flew so high that it crossed the clouds. There the kite met a tiny angel. The angel was delighted to find the kite. Realising that it's getting late, Sarla pulled at the kite's cord. The kite said to the angel, "I'll have to leave now. My friend is calling me" The kite then said, "We'll meet again". Angel replied, "I want to come with you too". When the kite reached Sarla, it presented her with a gift - An ice-cream made of clouds! Sarla thanked the kite and said. "You're so dear to me, Kite".
author: Anchal Vaish

title: Mom ! Come On
text: I got up in the morning and rubbed my eyes. I wasn't able to see mother and hence I shouted "Mom, Mom! Come Fast" Mom responded saying, "Yes son, get up, wash your face and get refreshed" I then took a bath quickly, wore my shirt and told mom that I have to leave quickly. "Yes, Yes I'm coming" said Mom. "I have to boil milk, will do that and come", she said. Ok, I'll comb my hair and button my shirt. I'm ready, Hurry Up Mom! Mom also prepares sister's clothes and gets her ready. There is so much of work every morning, but I'm in a rush. Mom, I'm getting late. By now, I pick my school bag and water bottle too. Also, I have worn my slippers. Let's go! Mom, come fast. "Yes, Yes, I'm coming. Let me comb your sister's hair. I need five more minutes, we'll leave then" I have to leave now. I am not going to wait any longer. I feel like crying. Sister has gone to school and I am still here. "Its almost done son, I just have to fill water". Mom always has some work or the other. "Come on Mom, I will not wait now". "Lets go now, now!", said I as I dragged her by holding her hand. "Yes dear, let me switch of the lights", she said. We've come out now. Mom is locking the door.
author: Anurag

title: We went to market
text: There are lot of shops and people. Few of the people are purchasing things and few are just looking around. We first went to the grocery store. Mom purchased wheat, rice, sugar and pulses. We did not bring the items with us as the shopkeeper will send them home. After this, Mom stops at the vegetable shop. I asked, "Will you buy vegetables?" Mom said No. The vegetable hawker shouts, "Come and buy fresh vegetables". Why did Mom stop here? Oh, this is the oil shop. There is smell of oil everywhere. Mom complains to the shopkeeper, "Oil is very expensive". The shopkeeper doesn't likes this. Now we reached the fish market. See, the kind of clothes fisherwomen wear. "Are you able to see fat cats"? - They only rest here and get fat by eating fishes. We stopped at the dairy. Mom purchased some Ghee and Cottage Cheese. Why don't they have ice-cream? I like it very much. What do you think, will my mom buy me ice-cream? "Will you buy some utensils?", I asked Mom. There is no one in the utensil shop. People normally buy utensils when there is a marriage or a festival. "Wait, Mom!!! Don't go to this shop", I shouted. My mom likes the cloth shop. The shopkeeper shows her many sarees but she doesn't buy even a single one. I just wanted this! The Toys shop! The bear is so big! I want this scooter and this toy truck...! I promised Mom, "I'll only touch the toys, I will not demand the toys today". I will only ask for a toy on my birthday.
author: Anurag

title: Sweet talk
text: Life was good for Gundu. He lived in a beautiful forest and all the animals were his friends. But, he was bored. Everyday was the same... He met his friends, played around, ate and slept. He wanted some excitement! One day, by the edge of pool he met his friends. "Hey ho!" said Kaka. "How's life?" "Same ole' same ole'" said Gundu, cheerlessly. "Why so?" asked Titli Turtle as she crawled out of the pool. "Ah well..." said Gundu. "I think he is bored," said Pinky Flamingo. "Why don't you take a walk down that road and check out the city?" "Hahaha...yes you should," said Kaka. "That will be give you something to talk about!" Gundu thought, "Will this journey bring me the excitement I am looking for?" "Yes, I am sure this will be the making of me. I will explore the big city." As he set out he was a bit nervous, so he said, "Kaka would you like to come with me?" "I will catch up with you. Carry on!" she said, encouragingly. So off Gundu went. He saw cars and buses and millions of eyes following him as he walked by. He felt self conscious. But his heart thumped with joy. He noticed a little girl in a car jumping up and and down and pointing to a long moving thing that belched smoke. "Ah! This is the life," he thought. "So much to see and do...and there I was stuck in that small forest. But, what is the crawling thing belching smoke? There so much I know nothing about. This is the time to find out!" All kinds of vehicles went by. When they passed Gundu, the people in the vehicles became excited...pointing their fingers and shouting out. A vehicle on three wheels whizzed past. Gundu moved hastily to the side. The people in that strange vehicle were drinking water. When they saw him they put their heads out and peered at him. Suddenly, Gundu felt very thirsty. And, now he was hungry too. His stomach growled. Just then he spotted a green field... it was tempting. He strolled across and began to feast. He was half way through his meal when he heard a gasp and the sound of little feet running away. He looked up to see a flash of blue and a little girl running as if her life depended on it. He shrugged and continued his meal. Meal over, he was dozing off when he heard a ruckus. He saw people running towards him. They carried sticks and stones and then began to throw something that had smoke coming out of it. The minute the smoky thing touched the ground it went off...TUP TUP TUP TUP... loud, smelly and making the air smoggy. Gundu was a shocked. "What are they doing?" he wondered. The noise grew louder and Gundu began to feel afraid. He had no clue what was happening. "Why are they shouting and waving sticks? I was having such a good time out here," he thought. Just then he heard a cheerful "HEEELLLLLOOOOO!" It was a jumbo and he seemed to be laughing at Gundu. "Uh! Hi!" said Gundu, hesitantly. "Wassup?" "You man!" said the Jumbo, now guffawing with laughter. "Me?" "Yeah man! See these people? They are all scared of you!" Now it was Gundu's turn to laugh. "I guess you should be moving out man..." "Why? I was just beginning to have a good time," whined Gundu. "It's my advice pal." Just then Kaka flew in and settled on Gundu. Hearing Jumbo's talk Kaka added, "Yeah...you better move it. Or, you could well end up like Jumbo here... ferrying people about during the festival!" Kaka went on to describe the procession and Gundu realized it was not a joke. When Kaka finished Gundu said, "I better get going." And with one final trumpet he was off!
author: Nimi Kurian
illustrator: Ajanta Guhathakurta; Ajit Narayan; Greystroke; Lavanya Karthik; Rohit Bhasi; Sanjay Sarkar; Shilpa T; Tapas Guha; Vinayak Varma

title: Thuli's Special Secret
text: Thuli stays with her grandmother and their cow, Special, in the village. Her parents work in the city. Every morning her grandmother wakes Thuli up early to go to watch the sunrise. When the sun is up in the sky, Grandmother bathes Thuli. She brushes Thuli’s teeth, washes her face, and brushes her hair. When Thuli is nice and clean, Grandmother gives Thuli some porridge. Thuli loves the porridge. But she loves the milk more, because it comes from their cow, Special. The milk is fresh and creamy. After eating, Thuli and Grandmother sit under the tree, and Grandmother tells Thuli stories. When the stories are finished, Grandmother gives Thuli some cookies and a glass of milk, fresh and creamy. Thuli’s parents bring the cookies with them when they visit. Chocolate chip cookies are Thuli’s favourite. Special always looks at Thuli as she eats her cookies. Thuli wants to share her cookies with Special, but Grandmother gives her only enough for herself. That day, after listening to the stories, Thuli follows Grandmother into the house, tiptoeing so that Grandmother doesn’t hear. Thuli sees Grandmother take the cookies out of a cake tin inside the oven. Thuli runs back outside and tells Special that soon she will share her cookies with her. Later in the afternoon, Grandmother and Thuli take a nap, then wake up to watch the sunset. When the sun sets, Thuli sneaks off into the kitchen. She opens the oven, and takes out cookies for Special. Special licks Thuli when she gives her the cookies. Special smiles. Thuli smiles. “ It’s our little secret,” she says.
author: Baeletsi  Tsatsi

title: Nomvundla and the Chilli-Eating Contest
text: Nomvundla the hare and Soko the monkey are buddies. “Hurry, Soko! We don’t want to be late for the Chilli-Eating Contest,” says Nomvundla. “Nomvundla, if you win, who will you take to the Hamba-Hamba Funfair?” asks Soko. “That’s easy,” says Nomvundla. “I’ll take my best friend!” “Hmm, I wonder who Nomvundla’s best friend is?” Who do you think Nomvundla’s best friend is? Nomvundla and Soko are the last to arrive. “Soko, you go first,” says Nomvundla. CHILLI-EATING CONTEST RULES 1. DON'T SAY HOW HOT IT FEELS 2. FINISH ALL YOUR CHILLIES “Nomvundla, I’m scared,” says Soko. “I’m not!” says Nomvundla. How many chillies would you be able to eat? EEE! HOT! MAIWE! EISH! HHLLLIIIII! EISH! It’s Nomvundla’s turn. She has a plan. Nomvundla starts to sing: “You say it’s HOT. I say it’s NOT!” The judges are surprised and ask her what she is saying. She carries on singing her song until her chillies are finished. Can you help Nomvundla sing her song? Hooray! Nomvundla is the winner! “YOU are my best friend, Soko!” WHEEEEEEEE!
author: Fortune  Tazvivinga

title: What's in the Pot?
text: “What’s for supper?” asked Sam. “It’s a surprise ”, said Mama, putting a big pot on the stove. She added a jug of water. Sam was worried. “Are we having water for supper?” he wailed. “It’s a surprise. Wait and see.” replied Mama. “Can I help?” asked Sam. “I could stir.” “You are still a bit short,” said Mama. “The pot might fall over. But you can help me by fetching things.” “Can you bring me an onion, please.” “This doesn’t smell very nice.” “They will taste nice once they are cooked.” “Now I need some tomatoes. No, that is an apple. The tomatoes are also round and red, but you will find them in the fridge.” “Can you bring me potatoes. They are round and brown.” “Is supper ready yet?” “If you are hungry you can eat the apple while you wait.” “What about these?” “No, we won’t need biscuits. We can save those for after supper.” “What’s in the pot?” “It’s a surprise. Wait and see.” “What about this?” “That is a watermelon. It will be too big for the pot.” “See if you can find some spinach. It is also green.” “Please get some bread. No, it won’t go into the pot but on the table.” Mama carried the pot to the table and started to dish up. “What’s in the pot?” asked Sam. “Soup!” My favourite!
author: Crystal  Warren

title: Maybelle the Mule
text: Maybelle the Mule spent a lot of time hanging out on her own. She just felt a little bit different. After all, her mother is a horse and her father a donkey But Maybelle wasn't a sad mule, she still had loads of fun! Often times when the other animals were playing in large herds, she felt more comfortable making up some of her own games, and chasing her tail But sometimes at the water hole, she wondered what the other animals were talking about, and what they were up to. They always seemed to be having so much fun...Maybelle wanted to go and talk to them, but was afraid because she was different to them With two different parents she thought they would make fun of the way she looked. Her face was part Horse and part Donkey She was shy about her curly hair. Her parents always said it was "cute", but Maybelle thought the other horses might make fun of her Donkey curls Maybelle started to think her only friend was her own shadow, and she was starting to not like her too much either Then one day at the watering hole, Maybelle met Henrietta the Hippo, who asked to be her friend. Maybelle was surprised and said, "why do you want to be my friend? You're the funniest animal on the plains, and I'm just a shy mule". Henrietta said, "I used to be just like you, I thought no one would like me because I am big and slow" Then Maybelle met Hulk the Hedgehog who said, "before I thought everyone wouldn't want to play with me because of my scary spikes"...and Pierre the Parrot said, "I never thought I would have friends because I am the only one with wings, and my house is all the way up in the trees" Maybelle let out a loud HUFF, and said, "enough is enough! It is great that you are all different, it's what make you all so special". She then quickly realised, she had not been feeling the same way about herself this whole time Maybelle decided she was going to be happy she was a Mule! After all, all of the other animals on the plains had things about themselves different from all the other animals Now Maybelle has made friends all over. From Gina the Giraffe, to Eleanor the Elephant, Maybelle is happier than ever Sometimes she still needs some time alone, but now, she gets to decide when!
author: Harvey Abitbol

title: My Sisters Wedding
text: There once were two girls called Maya and Anika. Maya was 6 years younger than Anika, and while they didn’t get along when they were younger, as they grew up, they became best friends. One day, Anika met her future husband, Rohit while working overseas. Over a few years they got to know each other and decided they wanted to spend their lives with each other. One lovely evening in Paris, Rohit proposed to Anika, and she said YES to the great delight of their family and friends! Anika wanted her grandma to be at her wedding, so they decided to have a big Indian wedding with hundreds of guests in Bangalore in India. After months and months of planning, the three day wedding extravaganza went off without a hitch. Anika looked beautiful and all the guests at the wedding had the time of their lives. After the wedding, Anika and Rohit decided to travel the world on their honeymoon and lived happily ever after! The End.
author: Uttara Nataraj
illustrator: Henu; Sahitya Rani; Saloni Chopra; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: A Pig's Personality
text: Two fuzzy pigs lived in a sty. It had wooden walls with long open spaces. There was a dusty dirt floor and a wet water trough. At night, their farmer brought buckets of slop. Their favorite nights were when she threw heads of lettuce and corns on the cob to them. Sometimes she leaned over the wooden walls and scratched them between the ears first. That was the best part. They liked their life in the sty with the farmer and the scritchy scratchy corn cobs. But sometimes the pigs wanted...... more. They dreamed of what the world might be like outside the farm. But more importantly -- what would they be like? Does a pig's personality change depending on where he or she lives? The two pigs did not know. What makes a pig a pig? Would a pig be a pig if a pig was a shark? The two pigs did not know. What would happen if they experienced somewhere new and something different? Bad things could happen. Someone might be mean to them. They might catch a cold. There might not be farmers or heads of lettuce or even corns on the cob. The two pigs just did not know. They considered these questions. The afternoon light came through the long spaces in the wooden walls. It made stripes across their bellies. They watched the stripes move as the day passed. That night, after their bucket of slop, they decided. The two pigs left the sty. T hey did not know what would happen. But it was important to find out.
author: Molly Seltzer
illustrator: Ella Clark; Nidhi Jha; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: Mom! Hurry up.
text: I woke up in morning. I rubbed my eyes. Mother was not there. I shouted, "Mom! Please come fast". Mother said,"Dear son, please wake up and wash your hands and mouth". I bath quickly. Wear my clothes as I have to go quickly. I again shouted, "Mom, please listen". Mom said,"Yes my son I am coming. I have to prepare milk and then I will come". I comb my hair. Buttons my shirt. I am ready. I again shouted, "Mom, hurry up!". Mother gives clothes to my sister. She makes her ready. There is too much work in morning but I am also in hurry. "Mom, I am getting late". I pick my school bag and water bottle. I wear my shoes also. I again says,"Mom come now, I am getting late". Mom says," Just coming. Let me comb your sister's hair. I will come in 5 minutes and then we will leave". I have to leave and now I will not stop. I feel like crying. Sister left for school and I am still here. Mom: "It's almost done. I just have to fill water." Mom always has some work. I said,"Mom, hurry up as I will not wait now". I pulls my mom's hand and said,"Now move". Mom says,"Ok my son but let me switch off the lights". Now we come outside of our house. Mom locks the door.
author: Akesh Khandelwal

title: A fun picnic
text: One upon a time, a monkey, mouse, rabbit and a bear were good friends. They played hide and seek, thief and police. They played together for long time. Monkey said, "I am hungry, can you all please bring something to eat?". Everyone got something to eat for him. Rabbit bought some carrots. The bear got some cabbage. Squirrel got some tomatoes. Mouse bought some radish. He washed all the vegetables, cut them and mixed all of them together. Now it was time for them to eat. Bear said, "Wow this is tasty, what is this called?". Mouse replied, "Snack mixture". Rabbit said, "mixed veggies". Squirrel said, "This is a pickle". Monkey said, "This is salad, eat generously, it makes you stronger." Mouse said, "I am going to eat this everyday now, I will be a lion when I grow up". Everyone started laughing.
author: Jayanti Dabhere

title: What's in the water?
text: The world has millions of buckets of water. Water is in our oceans! Water is in our drinking glasses. Many different types of animals live in water. Some are colorful like this fish. Some are rectangular like this whale. Some animals that live in water are so big that you can see them from far away. Some animals that live in water are so small that they live in a tank. Water is home to many different animals! What's your favorite?
author: Hannah Peter
illustrator: Gracie; Greystroke; Lily Banerjee; Marleen  Visser; Maya  Ramaswamy; Monappa; Priya Kuriyan; Soumya Menon

title: Roam and ramble
text: There were five friends - a monkey, a mouse, a rabbit, a squirrel and a bear! In the jungle, there was a tiger! One day, everyone went for a picnic! They played hide and seek, and they played cops and robbers. They all ran around a lot. Playing until it was very late! The monkey said, "let's eat something now, please bring some food." All friends went to get something or the other. The rabbit got some carrots. Bear got some cabbage. Squirrel some tomatoes. Mouse some radish. Everyone washed, cut and mixed the food. Bear said, ah! this is exceptional. What is this called? The mouse said, its a snack called "chaat"! Squirrel said, "its called mixed." Monkey said, "its a salad." Eat more, Become stronger. The mouse said, "I'll only eat this from now onwards." I'll become a tiger when I'm older! Everyone started laughing.
author: Aparna S.

title: The cats dilemma
text: Once upon a time, in an apartment, there was a little girl. She loved animals. All of them. Especially cats. And dogs. And cows. And elephants. And mongoose. In this apartment, there was a cat. The little girl, would often give milk to the cat. Each day the cat waited for the milk and the girl waited to give milk to the cat. The cat, however, was an intelligent cat. More intelligent than other cats. She followed the milk man each day. She saw the milk man placed the milk into a bag. And the girls mother took the milk and poured it into a bowl for the cat to drink. The cat thought about it. She felt so much trouble was not necessary. She could help herself to the milk straight from the bag. Why did the girl have to go through so much trouble? So, each day, she would follow the milkman. The moment he left, she would jump and poke the bag with her claws. The milk would spill down and she would drink the milk. There was no trouble at all...or so she thought... The girls mother was not happy. Each day the milk spilt and she had to clean up the floor. She told the little girl that the cat was not doing the right thing. The girl told the cat, but the cat did not understand the fuss. They tried many things, but the cat kept trying to drink the milk herself. Thus, each day, it was a competition as to who reaches the bag first. Sometimes the mother won, sometimes the cat. They tried to keep the bag higher, but the cat was able to reach it. They told the milk man to ring the bell, but he forgot. The girl was not happy because mother was not happy with the spilt milk and she was not able to give milk to the cat... Finally, the mother won, because she put a stronger bag with a steel bowl inside it... With the steel bowl, the cat realised that she could not reach the milk bowl. The cat was unhappy, but the girl continued to give milk regularly to the cat. To this day the cat cannot understand, why do humans insist her on giving her milk than allowing to take the milk herself...
author: Neel
illustrator: Anurima Chanda; Dhaanya  Arora; Ruchi Shah; srid har

title: the thursty crow
text: theair was a crow who was very thursty one day he was flying over the sky suddenly he saw a pot then he whent to words the pot he saw water in it so he plased his mought in the pot it was lo so he plased 4 and 5 pebles in it the water came up then he drank water and flue avay the end

title: My School called ' Balavadi '
text: This is my school, it's called ' Balavadi '. My brother Chinnu and I go to Balavadi school. This is a small school, there are many children in this school. We keep our flip flops near the door and go inside. All footwear are kept in a straight line. When you keep them in a straight line, it looks pretty. We keep our lunch boxes near the wall. Some are big lunch boxes, some are small. We hang our water bottles on the wall. Each water bottle has a different color. Red, blue, green, yellow......... Math is my favorite subject. Chinnu likes to join different pieces. He likes to play with beads. I like playing with cards. Teacher says when you play different games, you become smart. This is story telling time. There's a puppet in teacher's hand. Teacher tells a story using the puppet in her hand. Teacher changes her voice and you feel as if the puppet is talking. We read books. Some books have pictures in them. Teacher teaches how to recognize different letters in alphabet. Because I already know the alphabet, teacher says I will be a fast learner. Teacher does not know I know numbers too. My friends think it is the puppet talking. They are surprised. I am not surprised because I know the puppet cannot talk. Teacher is the one who talks like the puppet. Now it is play time. There is a big tray with clay in it. Chinnu likes to play with clay and make different figures. I like to make fruits using clay. Bell rings at 4 in the afternoon.
author: Paul Pai

title: Watch Out! The Tiger is Here!
text: It's not easy being a tiger. Yes, tigers are beautiful and fierce. But tigers are also big and heavy. This makes it difficult for them to hunt for food. Out of every twenty times a tiger hunts, it eats only once. When a tiger moves through the forest, KHAU! KHAU! KHAK! The langur calls, just like an old man coughing! KHAU! KHAU! KHAK! AWOOOO! HAWOOOO! The barking deer calls, like a scared dog! AWOOOO! HAWOOOO! OOW! OOW! OOW! The spotted deer calls, like a little bird! OOW! OOW! OOW! The whole forest knows the tiger is here! AHUUUN? AHUUUN? The tiger wonders, where has everyone gone?
author: Sejal Mehta

title: Who Ate All That Up?
text: Nothing goes to waste in a forest. Nothing at all! Everything gets cleaned up. Absolutely everything! When leopards don’t finish their food, Who eats the rest? The vultures and the hyenas! And the hungry wild boar. GRUNT! GRUNT! When the vultures and the hyenas waste their food, Who gobbles it up? The flies and the maggots! And the hungry wild boar. GRUNT! GRUNT! When elephants poop in the forest, Who snacks on that? The dung beetles! And the hungry wild boar. GRUNT! GRUNT! When branches, leaves, and rain fall on the ground, Who feasts on it all? The termites and the fungi! And the hungry wild boar. GRUNT! GRUNT! When the air gets dirty with smoke, Who sucks it all in? The trees! Ummm, but not the hungry wild boar. GRUNT! GRUNT!
author: Sejal Mehta

title: Wild Cat! Wild Cat!
text: Some wild cats have stripes. Like the tiger! Some wild cats have manes. Like the lion! Some wild cats have spots. Like the leopard and the leopard cat! Some wild cats are the best climbers. Like the clouded leopard and the marbled cat! Some wild cats live high up in the mountains. Like the snow leopard and the Pallas's cat! Some wild cats live in the desert. Like the desert cat! Some wild cats have hairy ears. Like the caracal and the lynx! Some wild cats love to fish. Like the fishing cat! Some wild cats are the smallest wild cats in the world. Like the rusty-spotted cat! Some wild cats look like house cats. Like the jungle cat and the golden cat! But they are all wild cats!
author: Sejal Mehta

title: Kajol, a young and vibrant girl
text: If anyone asks me to make a wish, I would ask for Teach For India till grade 12.” Kajol, a young and vibrant girl hailing from a small village in Bihar, defined the importance of education in the above line. The essence of education in people’s life is increasingly being recognized in the globalized world. The fact that we are about to enter in an era where we need to prepare children for democratic citizenship and responsibilities for the future. There are many like Kajol in the country. “My father, a metric pass and mother, a housewife, have always emphasized on the importance of education. Not just at the face of it, but they want us to get what was kept away from us ” The father being the sole bread earner decided to shift to Delhi for better job prospects and in a hope to live a better life. Kajol was just in grade 3 at the time and packed her bag of clothes and innocence to follow the father. As she recollects those days, Kajol think about that how Delhi has given her wings and how Teach For India has taught her to fly. I have an aim to live.” I am a fan of Sciences and wants to pursue a career in the field, whereas, my father wants me to complete BA and become a teacher to which I shrugs and resists. “I want to do something for my country". There are many girls like Kajol in the country.And we "fellows" are helping them to bring them closer to their dreams.
author: Sumit Bidla
illustrator: Anupama Ajinkya Apte; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Sahitya Rani; Sheetal Thapa; Sreevidya Gowda; Thea   Nicole de Klerk; Zara Asgher

title: What is Great Grandma's age ?
text: It was their Great Grandma's birthday. To take part in the celebration, they had to catch an early train. Grandma is their mother's mother's mother. Along with the children's grandma, Great Grandma lived in Mysore. Nobody knew exactly when she was born. But they celebrated her birthday during a festival called "Sankranti". Putti asked " Would Great Grandma like a cake as soft as a flower with creme on top that looks like roses?" When Putta, Putti reached Grandma's house, they ran to Great Grandma's room. "Happy Birthday, Great Grandma! How old are you today?" asked the kids. "I don't know my age. Who knows? What does it have to do with anything?" said Great Grandma. With a smile on her face, Great Grandma said " 5 years before I was born, India's King and Queen threw a huge function in Delhi. Our Mysore King too was there at that function and he was presented with a gold medal. Putti, hearing that, said " Oh, if it was a big function, there must have been lots of cakes there!?" " Oh, Yes!" said Great Grandma. Then she remembered another subject. " When I was your age, around 9 or 10 old, my uncle came from Mumbai in a clean train ". " Clean train?" asked Putta, Putti. "Oh, Yes!" Then Great Grandma remembered another topic. " When I was your age, around 9 or 10 old, my uncle came from Mumbai in a clean train ". " Clean train?" asked Putta, Putti. Great grandma continued. " After a few years, I got married. At that time, girls 15 yrs or older could get married. My father had a lot of respect for law and order. So when I became 16, I got married. Within a few days, my husband, your great grandfather got a job in Mumbai. We had to leave Mysore" said Great Grandma. Putta asked Great Grandma " Do you remember any important event the year you got married?" Great Grandma laughingly said " There was a lot of water in Cauvery River.Because of the Dam over the river, and reservoir there were no floods. During summer, because of the reservoir all the rice and wheat fields got plenty of water." Grandma, who was behind the door, asked Great Grandma " Are you talking about the K.S.R.?" Great Grandma laughingly said " There was a lot of water in Cauvery River.Because of the Dam over the river, and reservoir there were no floods. During summer, because of the reservoir all the rice and wheat fields got plenty of water." Grandma, who was behind the door, asked Great Grandma " Are you talking about the K.S.R.?" Get out of India!" Putti's eyes got wide. " Putta, we have read it in History. Revolution started in 1942. Which means in 1942.........." "......Grandma was born, not Great Grandma " said Putta. " Yes, but can we get a hint from it?" Putta said " Grandma is Great Grandma's 5th child. All children were born with 2 years difference between each of them. So Grandma was born in 1942......" "......Great Grandma's 4th child was born in 1942 - 2 = 1940. 3rd was born in 1940 - 2 = 1938. 2nd was born in 1938 - 2 = 1936. And the 1st 1936 - 2 = 1934. Grandma got some sweets for Great Grandma. " Kids, what I am about to tell you might help you. KRS means Krishna Raj Sagar Dam - next to it is Brindavan Garden. Last year we went to see the water fountains there, do you remember?" Putta, Putti nodded their heads to say yes. In the library, Putti found a book about Mysore history. " Here, the popular KRS Dam and Brindavan gardens was inaugurated in 1932" she had a big smile on her face. " So, Great Grandma got married in 1932. 84 yrs ago!" Putti said " Great Grandma said she must have been 16 at the time of her marriage. But, she could have been 15, 17 or 18." " When her uncle came from Mumbai in a 'clean' train, her age might have been 9 or 10. Let's ask Grandpa about it, he might know" said Putta. He took out a book on Indian Railways." India's first electric train came to Mumbai in the year 1925 " says here in this book. Great Grandma was 9 years old at that time. That means she was born in the year 1916, said Putti. " Grandpa, in the year 1911 did any foreign King visit India? Was there a big function during his visit?" Grandpa said " Oh, yes. 1911? King George V of England visited India. Gateway of India was built during that year in his honor. Not one, but there were many functions >" Then he said" Although I am getting old, my memory is still good! Isn't it?" He was proud of his memory. After 5 minutes, kids came running through Great Grandma's room. " Mysore King got his Gold medal from King George V, right?" Great Grandma, smilingly said " Yes, it was King George! You kids are so smart!" Then she patted their backs! Mother said " You kids did some detective work! For this you and Great Grandma are going to receive a Prize - it's a big cake, soft as a flower with creme on top shaped like pink roses." Kids started dancing with joy. In this story, do you remember all that was said by Great Grandma? Those things really happened. There is more information about them. King and Queen visit India in 1911. British King George V and his wife Queen Mary - when they visited India for the 1st time, there were over 400 kings and queens in India - who were all at the function for Georgr V. They called it Delhi Durbar. Total attendance was over 200,000. Every day 20,000 breads. Every lunch, dinner over 1000 cows and goats were slaughtered. Mysore King Krishna Raj IV Vodeyar received the Gold medal from George V, along with other Kings. Clean Train (1925) - 1925 February 3 - India's 1st electric train started from Mumbais' Victoria Railway station to Kurla station. Which meant, India became Asia's 3rd, World's 24 th electric train country. Cauvery Dam (1932) - River Cauvery runs from Karnataka State to Tamil nadu State. Before the Dam and Reservoir were built, there was not enough water during summer time for the fields. But now there is plenty of drinking water for the city of Bengaluru. Gandhi's speech in 1942. " Get out of India - said Gandhiji on August 8, 1942 in Mumbai. He asked all the people of India to revolt against the British. He said, not with violence but without! After 5 years, on August 15, 1947 India got its independence from the British. That Maidan where he gave the speech is still called " August Revolutionary Maidan ".
author: Paul Pai

title: The Punctuation Marks' Journey
text: This is Exclamation Mark, Full Stop, Question Mark and Comma. They are punctuation marks who need a job in this book, but they aren't sure where to go. Letters and words are zooming about, trying to form sentences. Where do the punctuation marks fit in? What should they do? “Well, I know where I belong,” says Full Stop. “I always stand at the end of a sentence.” “No, I go at the end of a sentence!” says Question Mark. “No way!” yells Exclamation Mark. “I'm the one who belongs at the end of a sentence!” Nobody can agree, and the letters and words just keep zooming around in confusion. “What will we do?” asks Comma. Comma stands in the middle of bickering punctuation marks and tries to separate them. “There is room for all of us among these words and letters,” says Comma. “Let me show you.” “You're right, Comma,” everyone says, “we're tired of arguing. Show us what to do!” Comma shows the other punctuation marks how he does his job. Comma organises all the words into a list, and stands between each word, separating them to make the list easier to read. What do you see in Comma's list? Now that Comma has found where he belongs, can Question Mark, Exclamation Mark and Full Stop figure out what kind of sentences they should make? The full stop is placed at the end of declarative sentences, like this one. The exclamation mark is used to express emotions, like happiness, anger or excitement! And do you know what kind of sentence ends with a question mark? Don't forget: the word that comes after Question Mark, Exclamation Mark and Full Stop should start with a capital letter, because it will be the beginning of a new sentence. While the punctuation marks were talking, they remembered the letters and words zooming around in confusion. “W e have an important job,” the punctuation marks say. “Look how confused the letters and words are without us!” Now the punctuation marks know what they need to do.
author: Shannon David

title: All The Way Home
text: Because they were rejected by their mother, piglets Wolver and Hampton were being hand-raised by students at the Dean Hall School in New Zealand. When they disappeared from the school grounds on different days, no one thought the newborns could survive on their own. Amazingly, the two very skinny pigs found each other and returned to the school after 10 days of fending for themselves.
author: SHAPATH MANDAL
illustrator: Ella Clark; Rohit Bhasi; Sheetal Thapa

title: THE BELOVED MOTHER
text: Sweet sweet sweet mother, Gentle and caring and kind Lovely, always there in times of need courageous in times of hard situations, Radiant beams from thy face, Jolly and always advising me when ever i go astray Sweet sweet sweet mother. Sweet sweet sweet mother, A hardworking woman, She has managed to raise me, Alone in the house, Always careful in her tongue when speaking to people, Strong as a lion, she does not fear anything, She is social to everyone thus has made many friends, Sweet sweet sweet mother.

title: HUNTING FOR FOOD
text: When a crow feels hungry, it flies all around, Searching hard to see if there’s any food to be found. It tries to catch insects, lizards, or small mice; It hunts for fresh fruits, or a few grains of rice. When a squirrel feels hungry, it scampers with ease, Through the branches of leafy green trees. It hunts for fresh fruit and nuts, or tries to steal, Eggs from a bird’s nest, to have a tasty meal. When a lizard feels hungry, it’ll hunt for insects that are small; Crickets, spiders, cockroaches and worms – lizards relish them all! A lizard will hunt scorpions, grasshoppers, and even centipedes – Crunchy creepy crawlies are just the food that a lizard needs! When a frog feels hungry, it sits motionless and still, And waits for a fly or a mosquito to come by, to make a kill. A frog snares flying insects with its long, sticky tongue – And then gulps them down, one by one! When a snake feels hungry, it slithers here and there, To see if there’s a meal to be found anywhere. When a snake catches a frog, a rat, or a bird, it swallows it whole; Because a snake never chews its food, or eats it from a bowl! When a monkey feels hungry, it leaps through the trees, Searching for ripe fruits hidden among branches and leaves. Green vegetables, seeds, and honey are things a monkey likes to eat, And sometimes, a monkey will hunt a small animal for meat. When I feel hungry, I never have to worry – Straight to our kitchen do I hurry. In our kitchen there’s always food galore – Rice, chapattis, fruit, lentils, and more! The only thing I have to hunt for are chocolates and sweets, ‘Cos mama hides the jars filled with these delicious treats. Sometimes, when I find the jars there’s nothing inside them – Mama has cleverly outwitted me AGAIN!
author: Santhini  Govindan
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Maya  Ramaswamy; Prabha  Mallya; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Priya Kuriyan; Rijuta Ghate; Salim  Kasamba; Sanjay Sarkar
