title: Birthday Gift
text: “Appa, read out this book for me”, said Samyu running towards her Appa. Once she was near Appa, she had the reverse gear on, sat on Appa’s lap and gave the “My little Puppy” book to Appa. “Samyu we have read this book over 10 times today alone” grumbled Appa, but Samyu was very clear she wanted to read that book only. So Appa started reading the book - “Mojo was a cute brown puppy!”. Samyu enjoyed the story so much that she continued to smile the entire time Appa was telling her the story. The moment she realized the story was going to get over, she sprung from Appa’s lap and sprinted towards her book shelf to get one more book. One after the other, Samyu and Appa continued to read so many stories! All of a sudden, Samyu decided to read a book by herself, well it was the Children’s Encyclopedia that she loved to browse everyday. She enjoyed looking at the colourful pictures in the book. She swam with the dolphins, flew with the honeybees, danced with skeletons, explored the submarines, enjoyed eclipses and zoomed on in the rockets! Samyu closed the Encyclopaedia book, took “My little Puppy” and started running towards Appa, when she heard the doorbell ringing. She rushed to the door to find Varun Mama holding a brown puppy in his hand wishing her “Happy Birthday”!
author: Deepika Arun
illustrator: Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lavanya Karthik; Rijuta Ghate; Sandhya Prabhat; Soumya Menon; Thea   Nicole de Klerk; Vinayak Varma

title: Dev's day at the zoo!
text: Dev was very happy! His parents were taking him to the zoo. "Zzzooooo!", he shouted! They took a long and bumpy ride in an auto! "Brrrrrrr", Dev said. Finally they reached the zoo! It was a Sunday, so there was a huge crowd! Dev's father went to take the tickets. "Dada Dada", Dev screamed, worried that his father was leaving. Dada quickly came back with the tickets. They were going on a Safari! After a long wait, the Safari began! Dev was so excited to see the animals in the open rather than in the cages! First they saw many deer drinking water! "Deedar, Deedar", Dev screamed! "Its not Deedar, it is deer, my sweetheart" said Mama. The driver said "Dont make any noise or you will scare the animals!" As they drove on, they saw a baby bear! "Beel! Beel!", yelled Dev. "It bear, my little baby!", said Dada. Dev was very excited to see the little bear waving its head left and right! They went on to see an elephant. "Aana! Aana"! Dev shouted It was taking bath! Dev's mama said "Look Dev! Can you see the elephant taking water in its trunk and spraying it on itself? It is trying to stay cool in this hot weather." Dev also started waving his tiny arms! As they went on, Dev gasped. There was a lion sleeping in the forest. "Lanan! Lanan!" His mama smiled. "Yes Dev, it is a lion." The lion did not even turn to look at their bus! It was fast asleep. As they went on, they saw a tiger lying down in the water! Dev thought to himself, "I think this is the animals' nap time". "Taagal Shleeeep." His Dada said, "Yes Dev, the tiger is sleeping." As they went on, people started shouting! Dev reached over to see what the excitement was. There was a peacock walking around opening out all its feathers! It was so beautiful! He also started to dance like the peacock. His parents laughed. Dev was jumping up and down on his seat when he saw two crocodiles lying on the ground with their mouth open. Their teeth were so sharp! Dev cuddled up to his mother, scared! "Cacadil!" His Mama laughed and held him tight. He was still scared, when he saw many monkeys jumping around in the trees saying "Oo oo". They were so funny that Dev started to laugh. "Manki. Oo Oo!" He saw a baby monkey clinging to its mother just like him. "Baaaby!" Dev did not want this day to end, but the Safari was over and he thought to himself. "This is the happiest day of my life!" He shouted "Dev happy happy!", clapping his hands as his father bought him an ice cream.
author: Anamika Radhakrishnan
illustrator: Ajanta Guhathakurta; Alicia Souza; Bijal Vachharajani; Herminder Ohri; Jithin Jacob; Ketan Raut; Maya Marshak; Rob Owen; Saurabh Sawant; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Titus Ndhokero; Vijay Ramanathan

title: Behind the Lie
text: As soon as their father left for work, Ramesh swept up the broken glass while Valli made tea. Though she was only eight years old, she had already learnt how to make the strong, sweet tea that their mother liked. In between sips, Amma held the warm glass to her throbbing forehead. And to her swollen cheek. I fell. I tripped. The glass shattered when I dropped it. These were Amma’s usual excuses. And no one looked beyond what she said. Not even when the children started repeating the lies. “Buying bread for the third day in a row?” asked Murugan, the owner of the neighbourhood store. There weren’t many customers at his store that morning so he chatted with Valli as he entered her purchases into his account book. “If your Amma is still not well enough to cook, don’t you think you should take her to the doctor?” “It’s not that kind of illness, Murugan anna,” Valli sighed. “What kind of illness is it, then?” Murugan persisted. “Just that her arm is hurting very badly. Because she tripped on the road and fell straight on her shoulder,” Valli repeated her mother’s lie. But her eyes told another story. And though she avoided Murugan’s eyes, he felt very uneasy. Something was not right. He discussed it with his wife, Sarasa, later that evening and was shocked to hear the truth about Valli’s mother, Meenakshi. “It’s not tripping or falling. It’s her monster of a husband. Looks like he wouldn’t hurt a fly! But that’s just a mask. Poor Meenakshi — she puts up with all his blows and beatings to protect the children.” Murugan was very upset. “I didn’t know this. Why didn’t you tell me earlier? We should have done something.” After all, both families had lived on the same street for years. It wasn’t right that Meenakshi and her children should suffer like this. “You mean you’ve never noticed?” Sarasa was surprised, “Meenakshi’s bruises? The cut lip some weeks ago? It breaks my heart,” she sighed. “But what can we do? Interfering might only make things worse.” Murugan wondered how he could help without making things worse for Meenakshi and her children. He thought about it deeply before coming up with a plan. The help Murugan arranged arrived at Valli’s door some days later. It came wearing a wide smile a khaki police uniform. “I’m Sub Inspector Jaya,” the young policewoman introduced herself. “My uncle, Murugan maama, asked me to visit you. I got off duty early today, so I stopped here on my way home.” Luckily for Valli and her family, Appa was travelling on work. When their father was at home, the three of them lived under a cloud of fear, always scared about doing something that could set off his violent temper. “Don’t make Appa angry,” Meenakshi would beg her children every day. “No singing, Ramesh. Please! Don’t bounce that ball, Valli.” SI Jaya listened patiently when the children told her all of this. Then she and Amma spoke in low voices for a long time while the children did their homework. When it was time to leave, Jaya insisted that they note down her mobile number. “You can call me any time. Day or night. And if I can’t come myself, I’ll have the beat policeman at your door in minutes,” she promised. “But I don’t have a phone,” Amma pointed out, “My husband refuses to let me have one.” Jaya made Amma write down her number anyway. “This terrible situation is not your fault,” were her parting words to them as she got onto her bike. “This violence is not okay. And the three of you should never suffer in silence thinking it is normal. Meenakshi, you must think about what we’ve discussed and do some of the things I’ve suggested.” After she left, Valli asked Amma what Jaya meant. “The SI wants me to write to someone in our family telling them how things are. She says we should not keep hiding our problem. That we should share our problem with people who care for us. She also said I could file a complaint at our Police Station if I wanted. But I don’t know what to do. Will any of this really help us?” Ramesh nodded gloomily. He was moody, and suspicious of everyone these days. More so ever since he too had become the target of Appa’s anger whenever he rushed to help Amma. “The SI wouldn’t have given us her personal number anyway. Try calling that number,” he challenged his mother and sister bitterly. “I bet you a full bar of chocolate that you’ll just get a recorded message. Or no one will answer.” “Let’s write to someone first then. Why not write to Paati?” Valli knew Appa was a little scared of his mother. It took a few days, but Amma did finally write to Paati. Then, they all waited eagerly for a reply. A visit from Paati would be nice. She was strict with them but what fun they had when she visited, bringing tins of home-made snacks with her. She would braid Valli’s hair in a new way each day and play cricket with them in the tiny lane. Amma would join them sometimes. Paati and Ramesh would sing together at home, and though Appa would look very irritated, he would control his temper while Paati was there. Yes, their grandmother would tell Appa that his violence was not acceptable. But when two weeks passed with no answer from Paati, all three grew downcast. What could they do next, they wondered sadly. Appa had been travelling and when he returned, he had some news for them. “My mother called me a few days ago,” he said gruffly. “She’s arriving here tomorrow. She wants to stay a few months. Months! I can’t understand why. Here…” he flung some money on the kitchen counter. “Pay the bill at the store and don’t forget to buy my mother’s special brand of coffee when you buy provisions for the month.” As soon as he left, slamming the door angrily behind him, the children jumped with excitement. “Give us a little of that money to buy sweets, Amma!” Ramesh pleaded. Amma agreed. More rare than the money she gave each of them was the half-smile on her face. On their way to school, Valli made Ramesh stop at Murugan’s store. After SI Jaya’s visit to their home, Murugan made it a point to talk to the children whenever he could. He was busy when they entered the store, so Valli prodded Ramesh to the place where the sweets were displayed. “You had better buy me that full bar of chocolate before you spend your money on anything else,” she demanded, “because I am surely going to win the bet.” It took Ramesh a minute to remember the bet he had made the day SI Jaya had visited. He laughed and told his sister to hurry up. When Valli had chosen what she wanted, she went up to Murugan and asked whether she could make a call from his phone. She dialed Jaya’s number. “Yes, Murugan maama,” answered a familiar voice at the other end. Valli wiggled her thumb at Ramesh. So much for him thinking that the policewoman wouldn’t answer their call. "Jaya akka, it’s me. Valli." “Is everything alright, Valli? Do you need help?” Jaya sounded concerned. “We’re fine, akka. I just called to tell you that my Paati is coming to stay with us for a few months because Amma wrote telling her about Appa. And… how bad things were.” “That’s such good news! And now you also know how to reach me, right? You can call me any time for help.” The call over and Murugan’s many questions answered, the children started unwrapping their chocolate as they left the store. Valli’s heart felt lighter. Not just because of the chocolate they were sharing. Not even because of the whole extra bar she had won from her brother. But because, for the first time in months, she could hear Ramesh singing softly to himself as they walked to school. How children can cope with violence in the home Children who live with an abusive or violent parent often feel scared or angry or ashamed. This is only natural. If you know anyone in this situation, let them know that: No one should suffer violence in silence. All children and adults have the right to live in safety, especially within their home. The violence is never the child’s fault. The child’s actions or behaviour does not cause the violence. Violence in the home is a crime. In India, the law provides protection to children and women once the crime is reported. Those found guilty of the crime will be punished. When children cannot act on their own to report abuse, their friends and classmates can help by: Suggesting they share the problem with trusted people and following up until they do. Trusted adults could be grandparents, aunts, uncles, neighbours, school principal. Discussing the problem with their own parents and seeking their help. Calling for help on their behalf if required. Call 1098. This is CHILDLINE, the 24-hour helpline which can be dialled from any part of India by any child or adult. It provides immediate help to children seeking protection from child abuse, violence against a parent at home or any crime against children.
author: Asha Nehemiah

title: How Camel got his hump
text: Long ago camels did not have humps. Their backs were flat, just like dogs and cats. As you all know, Camels live in deserts, and so do Lizards. It all began with a newly formed friendship between a Camel and a Lizard. They were neighbors. Once they were old enough, they started their schooling. Every morning, both would leave together to go to school... waving their mothers bye-bye! And this is how they walked on sand: - Camel left behind his hooves mark in the sand, - Lizard slithered leaving a wavy trail in the sand. Their mothers used to keep a watch on these trail to make sure their children were on correct path. However, Lizard was much slower than the Camel and so Camel had to walk unusually slow to match her speed. One day, Camel suggested, "Hey! why don't you ride on my back and we can reach much faster?" Lizard loved the idea and hopped on Camel's back. Off they went to their school. But that day, Lizard's mother got very worried about the whereabouts of her daughter. As, she could neither see her trail nor could she see her on Camel's back, once they were out of sight. When they returned from school, the Lizard's mother raised her concern. Camel, thought for a while... and then he came up with a brilliant suggestion. Camel said, "I know how to hunch... when I lift my shoulders my back raises a bit; Lizard can sit on my hunch and you will be able to see her!" Lizard's mother liked the idea. So, the next day Lizard sat on Camel's hunched back. However, that was just a small hunch and after a distance Lizard's mother was not able to see her again. So, Camel strained his muscles and tried harder to raise his hunch-back further up. He did this everyday after that, straining and raising his hunch-back a little further up. For the love of his friend Lizard, he kept practicing walking with raised bump everyday. Days went by, and now the Camel had become an expert in hunch backing. Walking with a raised bump on his back became quite normal to him. Camel loved his hunched back bump or 'hump' and kept it on all the time. People of desert started admiring the Camel for his 'hump' which became a symbol of 'Friendship'! Generation after generations, Camels took pride in keeping hump as mark of friendship. And slowly the evolution took its pace and Camels were born with humps. And this is how Camel got his hump! Did you know? 1) There are two types of camels: dromedary camels, which have one hump, and Bactrian camels, which have two humps. 2) The camel's hump is like a storage box. When camels don't get enough food and water in the desert, they use their stored fat.. this will cause their hump to go down. When they eat and drink again the hump will refill with fat and go up again. 3) Camels can survive up to six months without food or water.
author: Shital Choudhary
illustrator: Dinaz Irani; Juhi  Agarwal; Karthikeyan S.; Muniza Shariq; Priya Kuriyan; Sangeetha Kadur; Siraj Saxena; Smitha Tumuluru; Swetha g; Titus Ndhokero

title: When McQueen and Mater go to Aleppo
text: McQueen was rather sad and he was not racing, but was just parked outside the Sheriff’s office. Mater, asked, “hey McQueen what happened?”. McQueen said, “I’m not sure what to do Mater. There is this kid, who has been sending messages to me, asking she wants to meet both you and me. But I’m not sure why and even how to go there.?” Mater asked, “Which place McQueen?”. “Aleppo”, said McQueen. Mater:Aleppo! McQueen: “Oh, do you know where that place is?”. Mater: No, I don’t, but i just liked the name. McQueen: Hmm.. We have to find a way to go there Mater: May be can ask the road checker (my son calls the GPS as the road checker) McQueen: Good idea. Oh, this is in another continent (At this point my son started guessing the continents – when he said Asia, I said, that’s where Aleppo is and thats where they need to go) Mater: Alright, then lets go. (After about hundred days, after crossing the rivers, the mountains, the deserts, the long winding roads, they eventually made it to Aleppo. But as soon as they entered Aleppo…) McQueen: What’s going here? Why are there so many dusty’s (Disney airplane character, my son relates to) flying around? And why are they dropping bombs all over? Mater: McQueen, I’m really scared to go in there. I don’t see any in the streets. I see no kids. I see no playgrounds, parks and I don’t see any houses. Everything seems to be destroyed and the whole place if filled with gray colored smoke. McQueen: Yes. I don’t understand how the kid even sent me so many letters. But we can’t go back now, we came this far and we still need to meet the kid. Lets enter the city. (McQueen and Mater, changed their body colors to gray and they tiptoed – drove very slowly. Every 5 minutes there is a whistle like sound, which was the sound of dusty passing by. There are McQueen/Mater car toys that can change colors. My son, added – oh they are trying to camouflage) Mater: Is this what is called a war? McQueen: Looks like it. But if there is no one around, what are they fighting for? Mater: McQueen, how far, should we tiptoe? How do we find the kids house? McQueen: Well, i do have a landmark, the kid wrote to me in one of the letters. The kids house is in front of a big golden building (shrine). (After about 30 long minutes) Mater: McQueen, I don’t see the shrine. Its getting dark, should we go back now? McQueen: No we can’t. We have to keep looking. Oh, there it is. But wait, its not golden. Its gray color and looks like only half the building is there. May be this is it. Lets wait and see if Mater: But McQueen, we changed our colors, how would the kid recognize us? McQueen: That’s right, Mater. Lets change our colors. (With in a few minutes, someone knocked on the car and it was a bunch of kids) McQueen: Are you the one who wrote me the letters? Kid: Yes, we all wrote to you, because we heard about you and your friendship and we wanted to see you and Mater race. McQueen: With a proud smile, yeah, we both are wonderful friends and good racers. Kid: Can we all go racing now? McQueen: No, i don’t think its a good idea. Kid: No, we all want to go, even my parents would like to go see the place. (The entire place was dark now. McQueen and Mater changed their colors and they started a race, but it was a slow race. The entire place was destroyed. There were no buildings anymore, everything was crushed) Mater: But why is this place like this? Kid: We don’t know. One day we were in the school and all of a sudden, the teacher came and said, “Everyone go home now. Your parents are waiting outside. Tomorrow is also a holiday”. We were all very happy we got holidays. And ever since we came back home, we never went to our school. Our school is also not there anymore. Mater: Don’t you at least go to the park? Kid: No, there are no parks anymore. We stay home all day. Sometimes, we are just lying under the beds, the whole time and we have to turn off the lights in the night and just have a tiny little candle. McQueen: Why? Why do you do that? Won’t you get scared? Kid: We do it so that the jets cannot see us. The bombs are more scarier than living in the dark. Mater: And what about food? You don’t go anywhere, so how do you buy stuff? Kid: Sometimes, someone just drops some bread at our door and we just that for days. McQueen: Oh, I’ve lot of toys and lot of food. You can take all of those. Mater: And when we go back, we will tell everyone about Aleppo, so they can bring more toys and more food for you guys. McQueen: Also, we all ask other kids to write to you and wish the jets stop flying and scaring you. (It was going to be sunrise soon, so McQueen, Mater dropped the kids back at their home. The kids gave a tight hug to McQueen and Mater and kissed them goodbye. McQueen and Mater safely made it out of the city.
author: suresh ediga

title: A walk in the neighborhood
text: I love my neighborhood. Every Saturday my Mom and I take a walk to buy our food. Our first stop is at Mr Feb's fruit stall. I love watermelons. Mom always buy a watermelon for me. Our next stop is the food stall. Mom and I order fish. The people at the market are so friendly.
author: Tersia Haussamer
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Jemma Jose; Rijuta Ghate; Santosh Pujari

title: THE BIGGEST WIN
text: There was a strong Big Brother and small brother.The big brother always used to help his brother in school and other public areas.But when in home,he beat his brother violently.This created a bad impression in small brother about his elder brother. The Big Brother was always lazy to do any work,instead he made his work done by his younger brother. One day, younger brother was out to his friends house,because of fighting with his elder brother.He called him to play football but his brother refused. This made him angry.The elder thought that he had won his younger brother and he can do his job on his own.He said"I don't want your help anymore,I had won You.... HAAAAAAAAAA!!!! " But in few minutes,He felt his loneliness. He was exhausted.He went out and searched his brother for all day. But he failed,meanwhile younger brother came home and searched for His elder brother.He asked his parents,neighbours.But no answer. He waited till night out side waiting for his brother. there was a boy walking in street alone and sad. It was none other than his brother. They both came running to each other,and hugged. They went home happily. The next day, elder brother gave him a letter of peace. The both brothers thought that this was The biggest win in their life.:-)
author: Anitha Jaganathan
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Mohit Suneja; Ouk  Ratha; Sunando C

title: The Best Place To Nap
text: “I’m so tired!” yawned Eli as he stretched to the skies “I need a nap!” he said, rubbing his eyes “Somewhere snuggly to curl up in a ball…” He looked all around, and then began to crawl Out into the garden where he found a leaf pile. He nestled down with a happy smile. But just as he closed his sleepy little eyes... Around him buzzed a swarm of flies “Go away! Stop buzzing, I’m trying to nap!” But no they didn’t stop, they went Flap flap flap… Sleepy little Eli crawled back inside, In a dappled corner, a stack of books he spied He climbed on top and rested his head “This is rough. And hard..” he sleepily said. “Books are only meant to be read... They’re just not soft enough to make a bed” Shhh…ever so quietly, Eli nuzzled his fur And Toby the dog, didn’t even stir. But… “Ahh-ahhh- Aaaachooo”, Toby woke with a jolt Off darted the furry pillow, quick as a bolt Where oh where is the best place to doze? Eli thought and thought as he twiddled his toes Somewhere dark and warm, is there such a place? Hmmm, maybe inside Dad’s guitar case… The shape was all wrong, the case way too small “Oh gosh, I really am tired now…” Eli started to bawl Eli was lifted from the floor so high, By a warm pair of hands and a lullaby Three hours later Eli’s eyes open wide. He had fallen asleep, and he hadn’t even tried! He stretched and yawned and he started to clap “I found it! It’s true!" "Grandpa's lap is the best place to nap!”
author: Simone Patrick
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Harshvardhan Gantha; Jithin Jacob; Kavya  Bagga; Prashant Miranda; Shubhshree  Mathur; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Kallu's Mud Bath
text: It was a hot sultry afternoon. The animals on Tinku’s farm were resting. The horses with their baby colts were slowly munching the grass in the stable. The sheep and lambs were taking a nap in their pen. The hens and chickens were clucking about pecking on grains in their coop. The dogs and their puppies were resting in their kennels. In fact farmer Tinku too was resting in his farmhouse. Kallu the piglet was getting rather bored. He looked at papa pig and mummy pig sound asleep in the pigsty. His brothers and sisters too were asleep. Kallu just couldn’t nap. He didn’t like napping in the afternoons. In fact Kallu loved playing all day long... and his favourite game was rolling in the mud. So Kallu set out to look for a playmate. He called out to Chilu the colt but when Chilu heard about rolling in the mud, he said, ‘Neigh. That sounds yucky. In fact you pigs are pretty yucky. I even heard you eat rubbish. Yikes!’ Kallu moved on and asked Noni the lamb. ‘Ba-ba-ba My beautiful white coat will get dirty in the mud.’, said Noni Sadly he moved on and asked the chickens. ‘Cluck Cluck scolded mummy hen. Filthy pig go away I won’t allow my chickens to get filthy with you’, she scolded. Kallu felt hurt, sad and alone Just then he heard ‘Woof! Woof!’. It was Pinky the puppy. She had been following Kallu all along. Kallu wanted to ask Pinky but then he thought she too would call him dirty so he decided not to. Kallu went alone to the mud and sat there. He really wanted to take a dip but he thought everyone will call him dirty. ‘What happened Kallu, why do you look so sad?’, asked Pinky who was still following Kallu. ‘Go ahead and roll in the mud Kallu. I think you really want to do it.’, encouraged Pinky ‘Yes I do but then everybody will call me a filthy pig.’, said Kallu sadly. Pinky smiled and placed her paw on the piglet’s shoulder. ‘My mummy always says, Be who you are and not who the world wants you to be. And also Kallu my mummy says, you pigs roll in the mud to stay cool on a hot day.’ ‘Really Pinky? That’s why I so want to do it.’ grunted Kallu ‘Yes it is very hot today.’, Barked Pinky cheerfully Saying that Pinky ran towards the mud pool and dived straight into it. ‘ Woof! Woof! Come now Kallu, won’t you join me?’, Barked Pinky Kallu ran in happily. The cool mud made him feel so lovely. He rolled and rolled and covered himself completely in the mud. Just then he saw Pinky too rolling happily. ‘Hey Pinky! This is so much fun but hey you are not a pig Pinky, you are a puppy. Why are you rolling in the mud?’, he asked ‘That’s what friends do for friends.’, said Pinky affectionately.
author: Rohini  Vij
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Greystroke; Lavanya Nagappan; Olivia Fraser; Partho Sengupta; Priya Kuriyan; Ruri Irawati; Sanjay Sarkar; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Who Eats What ?
text: Carrion is the rotting flesh of a dead animal. Whales eat small fish and squid. Penguins also eat small fish, squid and krill*. *krill- a very small shrimp-like fish. Monkeys eat all kinds of fruits, bugs, and leaves. Tigers eat large or medium sized animals. Pandas love to eat bamboo stems and leaves. Vultures and hyenas eat the remaining food that is left over by other animals, like lion, cheetah, and leopard. Vultures and hyena are called scavengers.
author: Sharmila Pal
illustrator: Alison Byrnes; Greystroke; Herminder Ohri; Malvika Tewari; Partho Sengupta; Rohan Chakravarty; ROSH; Salim  Kasamba; Sharmila Pal; Shreya Shruti; Suvidha Mistry

title: Foodeometry!!
text: I am Foodie. I love food. I love shapes, too. Come, let's learn shapes with foods. Poori is round. when I eat it, I gain pounds!! Sandwich is square. And, I love to share. What is the shape with three angles? It is called triangle. Pizza is a triangle. French fries are rectangles. They have four angles. This is heart shaped cake. On my birthday, my mother did bake. In the school breaks, This is my favourite papad with star shape!! Eggs are oval. But, many are not good for your bowel!! Hexagon is the Pomfret. My mother cooks it just perfect, for which I am always set!!! Dosas are cylinder. They are good at any time!! which shape is this? can you guess? It is Jalebi, in spiral shape. I love these shapes and the food. They make me strong and cheer up my mood.

title: WHAT DID I CATCH IN THE GARDEN?
text: On a bright, sunny, summer’s day, I went out into the garden to play. I saw a little yellow butterfly flying around, Fluttering its tiny wings, without making a sound. I tried to catch it, but the butterfly flew away. Then I saw a tiny, red ladybird going on its way. The black spots on the ladybird’s red body caught my eye, But I could not catch the ladybird, though I did try. When I saw a squirrel with a bushy tail, leaping off a tree, I knew I couldn’t catch him – he was far too quick for me! A chameleon, sitting on a wall, seemed to be having so much fun, As he changed his colour, while basking in the sun. But as soon as I went near him, the chameleon scurried away, I didn’t catch him, or see him again that day. I saw a parrot on a bush in the garden – its feathers were green, Its red beak was curved, and its claws were the sharpest I’d ever seen. How I wanted to catch that lovely parrot! I stretched my arms out wide, But the parrot flew away, even before I got to its side! I did not notice a grasshopper, perched on a tree stump, Till it hopped away, with one mighty jump. I scampered after that grasshopper, running with all my might, But I couldn’t nab it before it hopped out of sight. A sunbird flew into the garden – it was bright red and yellow. That tiny bird was such a charming little fellow. Should I try to catch him? Before I could make up my mind, The tiny bird vanished, and was impossible to find. I sat under a tree, and felt disappointed indeed – I had tried to catch so many creatures, running behind them at top speed. But I had not caught even one, though I had tried my best, I lay down in the grass, closed my eyes, and decided to rest. And then I realised, that though all the garden creatures had fled; I had actually caught something - a POEM, straight from my head!
author: Santhini  Govindan
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Herminder Ohri; Lauren Holliday; Madhuri Purandare; Muniza Shariq; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Sachit Nandan Anand; Sanjay Sarkar

title: The Haunted Book
text: It was odd. Suren had never noticed that book on the shelf before. Was it possible? He had read practically every book in his father's bookshelf. He picked the book to read. little did he know about the book, he got lost in the world of the dead. Suddenly, a colony of bats fly above him. Frightened out of his wits, he falls down and breaks a twig. The sound of the twig snap woke all the ghosts and spirits. zombies arose from their coffins. In less than a minute, thousands of dead people covered him. They licked him.He woke up shouting and saw his dog licking his face. Next minute, he was running towards his father's bookshelf. He searched every corner of the bookshelf and found the book. He flipped the pages and saw it filled with his father's childhood photos. For next half an hour, he enjoyed his father's photos.
author: Gunika Beriwal

title: Families are Special
text: “Didi Didi, what are you writing?” Riya asked her older sister, Vanya. “Riyu can you please let me finish my homework. I’ll tell you everything later. ” “Didi no no please, I want to help you.” Vanya put her neatly wrapped and labelled notebook away and asked, “Okay tell me Riyu, what is a family?” “Family is us Didi.” Vanya laughs and says “Aww, you are right. Maybe that’s what you feel in your heart. Family is about what we feel in our heart. Do you want to know what I feel Riyu?” Riyu’s innocence always made Vanya’s heart melt and she indulged her little sister’s curiosity. “Yes yes Didi, tell me.” “In this big big world, there are many many families You and I have a family, everyone has a family, Different and special in its own way, Some that we are born into, some that we create or become part of, along the way too Families love and families care, Families work and families share. Caring each day and in every way, Sharing food and fun, smiles and tears, journeys and stories, Every single day. We grow, our family grows, Sometimes together, sometimes apart, but always in our heart. Families are special like the yummy icing on the cake, they only take oodles of love and hugs to make.” “Didi I understand. Now my dear Didi, can I give you a hug for goodness sake?” Vanya laughed every time Riya used some big words like that and this time too. Riya jumped on her Vanya Didi’s lap and the sisters broke into a warm and tight hug!
author: Ramya Iyer

title: PREENY THE PEACOCK
text: Preeny was very proud of his beautiful feathers. He walked around, with his head held high. He never greeted the other birds of the forest. He would not talk to the animals. One day he was dancing in the rain. His feathers were spread like a fan. He did not see a puddle of water. He fell into it. When he came out of the puddle, his feathers were a dirty brown! The other birds came running to help him. Golu, the elephant poured water on him. And Preeny became beautiful once more!
author: usha aswath iyer

title: Who Drives the Driverless Car?
text: “Story time!” Suvi rushed into her grandmother’s arms. It was a warm night and the stars lit up a cloudless sky. Paati was visiting Suvi this summer. “Shall we continue with the Ramayana?” asked Paati. “Yes!” said Suvi. Paati had already told her about the war where Rama defeated Ravana, the king of Lanka. Now Paati picked up from where she had left off. “After Ravana was killed, Rama had to return to Ayodhya, his kingdom far, far away. So Vibhishana, the new king of Lanka, gave him a magic chariot. It was called Pushpaka Vimana and could fly on its own.” “How did it know where to go?” asked Suvi. “Oh, the traveller just had to give it a command,” said Paati. “That’s just like a driverless car!” said Suvi. Paati’s eyes grew round. She said, “A car without a driver! What is this amazing thing?” “A car that can drive on its own,” sang Suvi. “I don’t believe it!” said Paati. “How can a car drive by itself? By magic?” “Not magic, Paati,” said Suvi. “Science!” “Then tell me,” asked Paati, “how does this driverless car work?” Suvi wasn’t sure. She turned on the computer to look it up. While she was trying to connect to the internet, Suvi asked, “Do you drive, Paati?” “I used to ride a scooter many years ago,” she replied. “But now I’m scared to even walk on the streets. I’m afraid I will bump into somebody or get hit!” Suvi and Paati were looking at the screen. One website said driverless cars were also called self-driving cars. “And there’s a computer, just like this one, inside each car,” said Suvi, patting the desktop. “And cameras and sensors. The computer uses these to make a picture of the road around the car.” “This picture,” she went on, “tells the car how far away other objects are. Like a tree or a road divider. That way, the car can avoid crashing into them. The same sensors also show the car where and how to park.” “But how does the car know where it is and where to go?” Paati wondered. “The car’s computer has maps in it, which tell it where it is. When we give it an address, these maps can figure out how to get us there,” Suvi explained. Just then, Appa came in. He looked very tired. “What’s the matter?” asked Paati. “Traffic is a nightmare!” Appa grumbled. “Everybody is in a hurry, nobody follows the rules.” “If everyone was in a driverless car, this wouldn’t be a problem!” Suvi said. Paati turned to her in surprise. Suvi continued, “The engineers who build the car’s computer put all the traffic rules in it. So when the computer makes a decision, it checks to see if the car is following the rules.” “Hmm…” said Paati. “Let’s say the car starts moving when the traffic light turns green but someone crosses the street suddenly. Wouldn’t the car hit them? A human driver might be able to stop the car.” “I had to do that today!” said Appa. “A man speaking on his phone wandered across when the pedestrian light was red. I stopped just in time. Phew!” “My goodness!” said Paati, looking worried. “The self-driving car’s first rule,” said Suvi, reading from the screen, “is not to hit anything or anybody. So even if the traffic rule says the car can go, its sensors will stop it if there’s something in front.” “Are you saying the computer understands that not hitting anything is more important?” asked Paati. “Exactly!” replied Suvi. “But can a computer make the car stop faster than a driver can?” “Oh yes, Paati,” said Suvi. “It can make decisions much faster than a human being can. And it never gets tired or sleepy.” “And I am sure computer-controlled cars would never try to break the rules to get ahead like many drivers do,” said Appa. “Did you know drivers’ mistakes are responsible for almost 90% of car accidents?” Then he added cheerfully, “In a driverless car, I could work or push my seat back and relax while the car does its job.” “Safer roads and fewer accidents mean less worry,” said Paati, looking at Appa fondly. “I don’t know if our Pushpaka Vimana stories are fact or fiction, but science is truly magical!” Did you know? 1. The earliest idea for the driverless car can be traced to Leonardo Da Vinci, the famous Italian painter, sculptor, and inventor. In the 15th century, he sketched a blueprint of a cart that could move on its own. In 1925, a car was guided through traffic in New York City via radio signals sent from another car following close behind. 2. Self-driving cars are still being tested by computer and car companies. Some such cars can be found on the roads of Western countries. But someone is always in the driver’s seat to make sure there are no accidents. 3. In India, plans are underway to allow similar testing of driverless cars. But with so many people and so much traffic on our roads, this is going to be a challenge! 4. Over one million people in the world die in car crashes every year. Imagine how many lives driverless cars could save. 5. Driverless cars can ‘see’ and drive in complete darkness, thanks to their maps and sensors. 6. Some existing cars already have features like automatic braking, lane keeping and cruise control.
author: Vidya Pradhan

title: Meet my Family!
text: Meet my family, We all live so happily, I love my family. I have a little sister, Her name is a tongue-twister, We call her Chinmayi. Do you know, We are a terrific duo. We love each other, We play together, We share our toys, And make so much noise! Our Grandma gets jittery, She says do not get any injury! My Grandma is so nice, She is healthy and wise. She loves us so much, That you can never judge. She tells us stories, Of Kings and Queens of some other territories. Meet my family, We all live so happily, I love my family. Papa and Grandpa go to office, In their work, they are so flawless. On Sundays, they take us to gardens and parks, So that we can have fun before it gets dark! Meet my family, We all live so happily, I love my family. Mummy I love you, Papa I love you, Grandma and Grandpa I love you, But above all, I love my little sister. Her name is a tongue-twister, We call her Chinmayi. All day along, we have fun, In night onto the bed we run. It is the time when mummy's work is done. It is bed-time and It is story-time. We love stories, Loads and loads of them, And especially when from mummy it comes! We all live so happily, I love my family.
author: Anisha  Bajaj
illustrator: Lavanya Karthik; Nikhila Anil; Nikita Modi; Ramya Iyer; Reshma Barve; Ruchi Shah; Saloni Chopra; Suvidha Mistry

title: My Heroes
text: Twelve writers gathered together one day, They each spoke a language too many, One to two they told and weaved, Stories grew from ten to many, At Uganda Christian University. These and many more heroes have come to mind, Gathering to read and write with zeal of a kind, The presidential jet came on time to flip the pages, Completing our story about the flight of the bright, At Bishop Willis Core Primary Teacher's College. Children's story illustrators and writers rejoiced, Children and mother smiled and jumped, Neighbours and families overjoyed danced, We all knew it was the time to dance as we smiled, Happy indeed that Kampala and Hoima sighed. We ate our meals to celebrate the festive days, On achieving of reading and writing skills, That we ourselves thought, taught and wrote, After a few tips from one and all together, Making us the winners among them always. Born and bred in this wonderful village, We now have gone out far and wide, In sky scrapers were many now live, At least in our reading, transported, Housed in the sky as the limit. No more reading old brown notes, We refuse to read notes and notes, We shall write and read as we like, No more reading without writing, We are the new generation of bookers. See how we swim in books and books, Written and illustrated by us and ours, Read and liked by us and not force on us, You and I worming through piles and piles, And making book worms where none were before.
author: Cornelius Wambi Gulere

title: SLURP & BURP
text: Jiffy, the giraffe likes you. He's going to lick you! SLURP SLURP SLURP! "Oh, I've had too much of you! " BURP BURP BURP! "I better go back to leaves, That's my kind of treat!" Kitty, the cat likes you. She's going to lick you! SLURP SLURP SLURP! "Oh, I've had too much of you! " BURP BURP BURP! "I better stick to fish, That's my favourite dish!" Ben, the doggy likes you. He's going to lick you! SLURP SLURP SLURP! "Oh, I've had too much of you! " BURP BURP BURP! "I think I'll chew on a bone, And leave you alone!"
author: Kaanchan Prashanth

title: Baby Talk
text: They smile and pinch my cheek. I'm not sure I like it much, Not everyone has Amma's soft touch. When Appa carries me He trembles like a leaf. Something about a teeny baby Makes a big man so wobbly! Guddu Annaa is not sure yet, If he wants me in his bed. He's not sure about sharing, Appa and Amma's sweet caring. Ammama is my grandma A mighty Queen of drama! I have one Paatima too, Who creates equal hullabaloo! They cuddle and kiss me all the time And I can't help but smile! Amma tells them not to pamper me so, But they won't hear of it, Oh No! Grandpa 1 has a toothless grin, Grandpa 2 has a dimple chin! Mittu mama has prickly hair, Always standing up, poking the air! He doesn't speak a lot, I think he tries to talk in thought! Geetha Maami cannot be stopped, She talks and talks, and talks and talks! Even in her sleep she can't keep quiet, Her loud snores are quite a riot! Then there's Kanaga-ma who cleans the house, And looks at me like I'm a dirty mouse! She keeps saying I'm dark as the night, And suggests remedies to make my skin light! Amma ignores her rude remarks, And holds me closer to her heart. Das Anna brings the groceries And all the gossip from down the street. Some aunty had a haircut, Some Uncle didn't approve of that! Some naughty kids had broken a light, Somebody's dog barked all night! Some boy spoke on the phone to long Some girl slept right through the morn! With Amma, his news goes unheard, But my grandmas gobble up every word! Everyday I grow a little more, Longer and stronger from head to toe. I can't wait to run around and play, And make these people do as I say! For now, from someone's arms I listen and see, Everything that happens around me. I may not understand why they laugh or sigh, But I know it's love in their smile.
author: Kaanchan Prashanth
illustrator: deepthi damodar; Greystroke; Jeyanthi Manokaran; Kavitha Mandana; Louwrisa Blaauw; Madhumita Srivastava; Madhuri Purandare; Rajiv Eipe; Sahitya Rani; Shambhavi Singh; Shrujana Shridhar; Suvidha Mistry; Vinayak Varma; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Louse's New House
text: There was once a jolly louse which lived in the hair of a girl. Every day, it sipped blood from her head. The poor girl! She scratched and scratched! With its stomach full, the louse was happy. One day, the louse heard about a bed bug. This bed bug lived in the royal mattress of the King himself. “How marvellous to live in such a grand home!” thought the louse. The louse dreamt about the King’s head all day and all night. “His hair must be so soft and thick, not sweaty and smelly like this little girl’s head.” The next day, the louse decided, “I am moving to a new home!” So while the little girl was playing in the park, the louse hopped out of her head and landed on...... the head of a little boy! This boy’s mother was the King’s chariot driver. As the boy kissed his mother goodnight, the clever louse leapt into the woman’s hair. There it waited quietly, until the next day when the chariot driver set off for the palace. The louse was careful not to give her an itch. If she scratched, it may fall off. The louse did not want that! Not when it was so close to the King's royal hair. At the palace gates, the King was waiting to go for his morning ride. As soon as he sat down, the louse bit into the driver’s scalp. “Ouch!” said the lady, and scratched her head. The louse flew off her hair and landed on...... the King's freshly-bathed shoulder. Mmmm. He smelt good! After a breezy chariot ride, the King returned to the palace. As he sat down to rest, the louse looked around his room. It was thrilled. No dirt! No heat! And such a lovely smell! But soon, the louse got hungry. The King was asleep so this was the perfect time for a royal feast! The louse ran up the sleeping King’s neck. It crawled higher and higher, stomach rumbling with hunger. Finally, on top of the King’s head, the louse was shocked. The old King barely had any hair! What a terrible mistake!
author: Nandita Jayaraj

title: No, I Shan't Eat!
text: Eat your food darling. Amma has made hot rice with sambar, full of lentils and vegetables for you my love. Put some ghee on top and eat. Shan't. Won't. Not now. Not Ever. Eat your food darling. Today I have fried fish for you. The apples are red, and the grapes juicy. Eat them pleease. Shan't. Won't. Not now. Not ever. Good, you are back from school. Have the unniappam and the payasam. I grated the coconut, added the jaggery, mashed the banana - all for you darling, all for you. Eat my sweetheart. Eat. Shan't. Won't. Not now. Not ever. Oh Doctor, I don't know what to do. I try so much I do, but my daughter simply won't eat, tell me, please do. Hmm...let me see..yes, it's quite serious this disease. There's only one thing to do. Feed her nothing but gruel rice for a week. Huff! I don't care. Amma fried the pooris and potatoes and added a dash of spice. Amma added coriander making it even nicer. Amma I think I'll have the potatoes and pooris not this sad bowl of gruel rice. You can't. You mustn't. Not now. Not ever. The biriyani looked so good. The cauliflower curry so very yum. Amma please let me have a bite. This soupy rice with not a spice in sight is no good. No dear, you can't. You mustn't. Not now. Not ever. Achhan munched on the fried beans and crunched on the peanuts. Followed it up with hot rotis and even hotter brinjals. Amma, oh amma, I can't take it anymore. I'm alright I tell you. I shan't throw a fit. Not today. Not ever. Amma and doctor with me in the middle. She seems alright. I think her problem is gone. Her stomach seems fit and fine. But should she ever refuse her food again, it will be back to rice gruel evermore. No never. Not ever. I'll eat up every last morsel, whatever amma makes. The rice and the curry, the poriyals and paysams. Doctor and Amma burst out laughing. I wonder. I wonder. I wonder why.
author: Sheeba Manish

text: A lion was sleeping under the tree in the forest.While it was resting so nicely a mouse disturbed it in its sleep.The lion was very angry and wanted to eat the mouse.Poor mouse was apologising asking the lion not eat her one day she will be able to help the lion.The lion laughed at the mouse not knowing how can a little mouse help him. One day the lion was trapped by the hunters with a net.It was roaring making a loud noise cannot get out of the net. The mouse heard this noise and came to side of the noise.There is a mouse trapped,she said "dont worry I will keep my promise and help you".The mouse chopped the net with its little teeth up until there was a big hole.The lion was able to get out. title: Johnny Escape
text: One day Johnny the dog was bored at home. He wanted to go on an adventure. He sat outside his house thinking what he could do. Johnny decided to go for a walk and saw a peacock. He got really happy but it still was not enough. He decided to carry on walking to see what else he would find. Just as he thought that seeing a peacock was not that adventurous a cookie rolled passed him. Johnny thought he needed to follow the cookie. He thought that he had to get the cookie, so he decide to run after it. Just when he grabbed the cookie a monkey came and said that was his cookie. Johnny thought that he would not let go of his cookie that he found, so Johnny decided to run with the cookie. Johnny did not want to give Monkey his cookie back so he ran away with the cookie and Monkey could not get to him. Johnny managed to get away from Monkey with the cookie. Johnny got away with the cookie. That day Johnny went home to think about his next adventure. The End.

title: My family
text: This my family photo. All the members of my family are here and looking very happy. My grandmother and my grandfather are sitting on a sofa with other grand children. Today my family is going for a day out.We are going to the nearest beach at Strand. We are going to sail with a small boat.
