title: Whoopee... Hyperloop!
text: Little Vishnu was a dreamer. He loved to read. He also loved to travel. But he hated waiting at airports and train stations, taxi stands and bus terminals. Travel always seemed to take so much time! ‘How I wish I had a magic carpet,’ he thought. ‘I would whizz from place to place in no time like Aladdin.’ How did human beings first go from one place to another? They walked. Once they learnt to tame animals, they rode donkeys, horses, camels, and elephants. Hundreds of years passed. The wheel was invented, and bullock carts and other carriages took people everywhere. A few centuries ago, the steam engine was perfected and trains were built. Next came the motor car, and people got to places faster. Cars ran on internal combustion engines. The Wright brothers took this engine and worked on it so that it could power a plane. Engineers took this a step further. They designed rockets to fly humans to outer space and to the moon. ‘But why are we still slower than a magic carpet?’ Vishnu wondered. He asked his mother. He asked his father. He even asked his teacher. Nobody could give him a satisfactory answer. His father said, “We are faster than we ever were. We can go from Chennai to Bengaluru in five or six hours by rail or road. And it takes less than 40 minutes by air. Why, you can even fly from Delhi to Washington in just 16 hours! The Japanese bullet trains take people from one island to another in just a few hours. How much faster do you want to go, Vishnu?” How far in 40 minutes? 4 km 40 km 60 km 600 km ‘They don’t understand,’ thought Vishnu. Every time he travelled, he wished he had magical powers that would take him anywhere in an instant. He grumbled about it to Rahul, his best friend. One day, Vishnu saw a newspaper headline that sent his little world into a spin. It said: ‘Hyperloop: the modern day magic carpet’. He ran to his friend’s house. “Rahul, the Hyperloop is coming! It is going to be faster than any train or plane,” he said. “What is that?” asked Rahul’s sister Anuradha, joining them. “Hyperloop is a super, super, SUPER fast mode of transport. I just read about it in the newspaper. It’s a system with small vehicles called pods that will carry people through long, massive vacuum tubes. These tubes will rest on columns or be constructed underground.” The more Vishnu told Rahul and Anuradha about the hyperloop, the more excited he became. “We would be able to go from Chennai to Bengaluru at the speed of a plane — in less than 40 minutes! Isn’t it great? It takes five to six hours when we go by bus or train.” The more Vishnu told Rahul and Anuradha about the hyperloop, the more excited he became. “We would be able to go from Chennai to Bengaluru at the speed of a plane — in less than 40 minutes! Isn’t it great? It takes five to six hours when we go by bus or train.” Anuradha was full of questions. “How will it move? Is it safe?” “The pods will go whoosh! Through the tubes... levitating all the while. Safety tests for the hyperloop are being carried out right now,” Vishnu said. “They will be faster than bullet trains!” said Rahul. “Really?” asked Anuradha. “The idea is to work towards the speed of sound, about 1,235 kilometres per hour,” said Vishnu. “But how?” asked a puzzled Rahul. “With hardly any air resistance or friction to slow them down in vacuum, the pods can whizz through the tubes. Imagine zipping from Chennai to Bengaluru in a matter of minutes! How awesome is that?” They laughed, thrilled with the idea. “But tomorrow I have to take a bus to Bengaluru!” groaned Vishnu. That night Vishnu dreamt of travelling in the hyperloop... Hyperloop, the dream transport The hyperloop is a futuristic transport system. It is expected to be environment-friendly since the tubes can have solar panels on the roof, allowing for a clean and self-powering system. India is already working on a hyperloop project. It will run from Mumbai to Pune. But the world has seen great inventions because of people’s dreams and imagination. Vishnu dreams a lot. What do you dream about?
author: Sreelata Menon

title: The Case of the Missing Water
text: The tank in Ranj’s village was almost dry. Ajji began to pray for rain. Amma collected all the buckets and pots and vessels in the house and filled them up. “We need to store as much water as we can,” she said. Appa collected tools to dig a little deeper. “We just need enough until the rains arrive,” he said. Ranj got out her notebook and pencil. She put on her thinking cap, and followed her parents to the tank. She examined the tank bed closely. It was cracked and dusty. Ranj wondered, “Where did the water in the tank go? Did it run away? Was it stolen? This is a mystery!” Ranj loved solving mysteries: Like the time Ajji couldn’t find her reading glasses. Ranj had found them in her book, marking the page she was reading. Then the other time — Why were elephants visiting the ragi fields? Turns out it was because their long, long trunks could smell the ripening grains, all ready to eat. “I’ll find that water,” Ranj muttered to herself. Ranj walked to the other side of the tank, past dead fish and dried reeds. “Do you know where the water could have gone?” Ranj asked a fisherman. “Downstream?” the fisherman suggested. Ranj followed the dry stream bed down the hill. At the bottom was another tank. It had lots of goats, but no water. Ranj asked the goatherd, “Do you know where the water might be?” “Upstream,” the goatherd suggested. “That’s where I came from,” Ranj said. “No water there.” “Further up, then?” the goatherd said. “That’s where your water comes from.” Ranj climbed up to the tank. Then she climbed up some more to a tank further up the hill. There was no water, no birds. There was only one person there. “Sapna, I can’t find any water. Any idea where it’s gone?” Ranj called to her. She knew Sapna from school. “Downstream,” Sapna called back. Ranj was suddenly angry. She stomped her foot. “NO!” she shouted. “It’s not. I have searched and searched. It’s not upstream or downstream. Got it?” “How about up there?” Sapna suggested. Ranj and Sapna looked up at the sky. The sun glared back at them. Everything was white-hot and dusty. “No,” they agreed together. “No water there.” Ranj collapsed into the boat with Sapna and gnawed on a lotus stem. She was hot and tired. “Manju’s parents left the village,” Ranj said. “They went to the city where they have water. Maybe we should all go.” “You go,” Sapna snapped. “No one asked you to be here.” “Fine,” Ranj said. And she stomped back home. But it wasn’t fine! There was still no water, still no rain. The next day, Ranj brushed her teeth with muddy tank water in a tiny glass. “Thooo!” she spat. In school, the class was half-empty. More families had left the area. Ranj just couldn’t bear it. She missed all her friends! In the middle of Environmental Studies class, she turned and ran out of school. She ran and ran until she was panting. She finally sat at the side of the road. “I have to find the water!” she huffed. “Can I help?” said a voice. It was Sapna who had seen Ranj running away from school. Ranj beamed. “Yes!” “We have to do this properly,” Sapna said. “Like real Sanitary Engineers.” “Like who…?” Ranj asked. “Sanitary Engineers build pipes and tanks and drains. I am going to be one when I grow up,” Sapna said. Ranj and Sapna decided to draw a map of their village and all its tanks and streams, showing all the places where the water might have flowed. Where could the water possibly have gone? Finally, they sat back and pored over the map. “We haven’t seen that tank yet,” Ranj pointed to one of the tanks they had drawn. “Let’s go,” Sapna agreed. Ranj and Sapna began climbing up the hill. The stream here was dry as well. “Maybe we shouldn’t have missed school. This tank is probably dry as well,” Sapna said sadly. When they reached the tank, Ranj and Sapna realised they were wrong. This tank was full! Sapna pointed at a small pump at the end of the lake. There was a tanker just below the bund, collecting water as it flowed. A man stood by, guiding the tanker. “Mystery solved,” Ranj spat. She had never felt so angry after solving a mystery. “Where are you taking our water?” Ranj wanted to know. “The city,” the man said. “They have more people, so they need more water.” “That’s not fair!” Sapna said. The man shrugged, “That’s how it is.” “My friend is a Sanitary Engineer,” Ranj yelled. “She knows what’s fair.” The man laughed. “Sanitary Engineer it seems! You’re just children!” Sapna said quietly, “Yes, but I know you can’t just take our water away.” “Go home,” the man said. “You can’t change anything!” “We’ll break your pump!” Ranj shouted, running at the pump with a stick. “Oho!” said the man. “Shouldn’t Sanitary Engineers be building pumps, not breaking them?” “Yes… no… not like this…” Sapna said, unhappily. But Ranj said, “I’m a detective! I can do what I want.” Ranj had a better idea. She hugged the pump. “You can’t turn it on now!” Sapna ran up to hug the pump too. “Hey!” said the man. Now he was really angry. “Just go home,” he said. That was when the clouds broke. Thunder roared, lightning slashed, rain poured. Sapna started to laugh. “The monsoon is here!” Ranj shouted. “I’m going home, even if you aren’t,” the tanker man said. It rained and rained. WOOSH, the bund overflowed, and the stream rushed down, splashing them. “The water has been found! Mystery solved!” Ranj said. “WOOOOOO! ” They yowled with joy. Water Words Tank: A name for a man-made place to collect water. Tank sizes can vary from small pools to large lakes. Bund: A small wall – usually made of mud or stones – to stop and hold water in a tank. Stream: A small channel through which water flows. Spring: A place where underground water comes up to the surface. Water table: Level of water under the ground. Wells have to be dug deep enough to hit the water table to get water.
author: Shalini  Srinivasan

title: Antonio's Messy Room
text: One day there was a boy named Antonio. His room was very messy. Every time his mom told him to clean it, he didn't. Everyday his room got more messy and he couldn't find anything. One day his friends wanted to come over and hang out with him. Antonio didn't want them to see his room looking like a mess so he decided to hide everything in the closet. Antonio believed that he did a great job at hiding his stuff. When he began walking away, everything fell back out. He was stuck with clothes, shoes, and toys to put away. After that, Antonio began to think. What if he cleans his room instead of throwing things everywhere? Maybe his job wouldn't be that hard. Just then the door bell rang. "Oh no, my friends are here!", thought Antonio as he peeked outside. Antonio, what a mess! You need to clean this room right now! Looks like Antonio is going to need some help tidying his room. Can you find: 1) A trophy cup 2) a playing card 3) A black and white feather 4) A red sock 5) A golden key 6) A comb 7) An apple 8) A flashlight Antonio told his mom to stall his friends while he cleans up. His mom was reluctant, but finally gave in. Antonio then began to put everything where it goes. For the first time in years he finally saw his floor. After 30 minutes, Antonio came out to play with his friends. When he invited them to his room they complimented his room and stuff. They played, watched a movie, ate pizza, and talked all day. From that day on, Antonio learned that being dirty is not cool. He should clean up when things get messed up or else the mess will just get bigger and bigger.
author: Diane C
illustrator: Catherine Groenewald; Diane C; Jisha Unnikrishnan; Rijuta Ghate; Suvidha Mistry

title: The Girl who Met a Tiger
text: A girl named Cloe went on an adventure to a forest. It was dark and spooky. But, Cloe was a brave girl. She was a bit sleepy. So, she slept under a tree. When she woke up she saw a small and cute little tiger cub on her lap! She picked it up and kept it in her bag and kept walking. But the cub, which she had was a magical tiger! Cloe, had to cross a big river. She said to herself, "I can't swim. I wish I had a boat." The magical tiger waged its tail. Suddenly a boat appeard!! Cloe was surprised and hopped on the boat. The boat went to the end of a RAINBOW! Cloe and the tiger got off from the boat and played on the rainbow. Cloe wanted to live on the rainbow forever. So, she wished it and it came true. Cloe and the tiger lived happily! THE END.
author: Amudhini Siddharth
illustrator: Helga Parekh; JP Brouard; Kalynne Vorster; Manjari Chakravarti; Muhammed Shafi; Namrata  Gosavi; Rayika Sen; Ruchi Shah; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Taposhi Ghoshal; Vidula Nene

title: Under the Invisibility Cloak
text: Arnav and Tanisha loved to play hide-and-seek. Every evening, this is what they did with their friends. One day, Arnav said to Tanisha, “What fun hide-and-seek would be if I could disappear and no one could see me!” They decided to ask Mamma and Papa if it was possible to become invisible. Papa smiled and said, “That sounds like science fiction.” Mamma designed curtains and cushion covers for people’s homes and knew a lot about different kinds of cloth. She said, “I think scientists are working on fabrics that could make the wearer invisible.” “Ooh, you mean like a real invisibility cloak?” asked Tanisha. The children decided to visit the library to find out more about these new-age fabrics. Arnav and Tanisha browsed through shelves and shelves of books to trace the history of fabrics. The oldest fibre that makes up fabric, they found out, is linen. This is made from the stalk of a plant called flax. Cotton is an old fabric too. Like linen, this also comes from a plant. They borrowed some books and left. Cotton Flax At home, Arnav looked at his clothes and said, “Mamma, my shorts are thick and my shirt is thin. But aren’t they both made of the same fabric, cotton?” “Good question, Arnav,” said Mamma. “How thick a fabric is depends on the quality of the fibre it’s made from...” “...and the way the fabric is woven,” Papa chipped in. “Are there other plant fibres?” asked Tanisha. “Yes, coconut, bamboo, jute are some of them,” Mamma replied. “There are insect and animal fibres too,” added Arnav. “Like silk from silkworms and wool from sheep.” Tanisha asked, “Mamma, I know you are wearing a silk sari and Papa’s shirt is made of linen and my muffler is made of wool. But what is my frock made of?” “It’s polyester, an artificial fibre. It doesn’t come from a plant or an animal and is made in a laboratory,” said Mamma. The siblings were very excited to learn that fabrics could be made in laboratories. They began looking through chapters on artificial fibres. They knew that some fibres were elastic. Like spandex, which track pants are made of. They read about how scientists developed high-performance fibres. These could resist heat, electricity and chemicals. “Some new fibres are shock-absorbent; they are useful to the police and soldiers. Some don’t catch fire easily; these are great for the fire brigade,” read aloud Tanisha. Just then, Mamma said, “Arnav, Tanisha, look what I have found in one of the library books you brought home.” It was a book on high-tech fibres! She read aloud an interesting bit that said nanofibres made from carbon were called smart fibres. And smart fibres could sense temperature, pressure and radiation. “Nanofibres...why are they called that?” asked Arnav. “Nanofibres are really thin fibres. When you divide one metre by a hundred crore, you get one nanometre. Nanofibres have a diameter of just a few nanometres,” said Papa. 1 metre 1,00,00,00,000 =1 nanometre As Arnav and Tanisha browsed through the pile of books, they also found out that cloth made from smart fibres is called intelligent material or e-textile. This is used in health wear. Such materials have tiny sensors in the fabric, which can pick up a patient’s breathing, heart rate and body temperature. This information can be sent to the doctor and the patient can stay at home. “Now to return to your first question – is it possible to become invisible?” said Mamma. She had just read an article in a science magazine, which explained that scientists in a university had made a cloak that would make the wearer invisible. The fabric was made of fibres with a diameter of 80 nanometres. She pointed to an illustration and added, “We can see any object – say, a pair of red glasses or a blackboard – because it reflects some of the light falling on it. But this cloak does not reflect light. Instead, the fabric bends the light a little so that it goes around it. So you can’t see the cloak, or anyone under it.” “Can I get a shirt made with that material?” asked Arnav, excited. He’d laugh so much at his friends’ expressions when they saw just his head and legs moving about, with nothing connecting them. “Newspaper reports tell us that scientists and manufacturers are working on the idea. Such fabrics are being developed in some countries. But they are not available yet,” said Mamma. “Playing hide-and-seek wearing an invisibility cloak would be such fun...” said Tanisha. “Can this smart fabric be used by grown-ups for anything important?” “Yes, soldiers can wear this when they’re out fighting the enemy,” Papa said. “And when I need to work and you want me to play with you, I can play hide-and-seek by slipping under the invisibility cloak,” he joked. At school, Arnav and Tanisha told their friends all about smart fabrics. “I have an idea. Since Kelkar Sir hasn’t come to class yet, why don’t we go to the laboratory and do some exciting experiments,” said Tanisha with a twinkle in her eye. “Wait,” whispered Arnav, “what if he is actually hiding under an invisibility cloak to find out what mischief we might be up to?” Smart fabric facts Some smart fibres are used to make cloth to clean lenses of spectacles, mirrors and jewellery. Clothes made from heat resistant fibres are used by people working in factories manufacturing explosives. Some fibres are hollow and can store perfumed liquid in them. These are used to make mattress and pillow covers. What would you do if you had an invisibility cloak? Let’s see what Arnav and Tanisha plan to do! 1. When someone throws a plastic bottle, get under the cloak, pick up the bottle, and walk in front of the person. Imagine his horror when he sees the bottle moving in front of his eyes! 2. See Teacher’s glasses on the table? Cover it with the cloak. Teacher will never find his glasses. So no class! 3. Ring the recess bell early – TAN-TAN-TAN!
author: Varsha  Joshi

title: It's a Laddoo Party!
text: DING-DONG! “Peter Uncle has sent us laddoos!” says Mira. “Let’s count them – 1, 2, 3…12!” says Mihir, her brother. “Twelve laddoos for two of us to share. That makes six for each of us!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It’s Riya, Mihir’s friend. “So many laddoos!” says Riya. “Twelve laddoos for three of us to share. That makes four for each of us!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Riya and Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It’s Mira’s friend, Prisha! “WOW! Laddoos!” says Prisha. “Twelve laddoos for four of us to share. That makes three for each of us!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Prisha, Riya and Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It’s Ananya and Dhruv, Mira and Mihir’s cousins! “Aha, yummy laddoos!” say Ananya and Dhruv. “Twelve laddoos for six of us to share. That makes two for each of us!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Ananya and Dhruv, Prisha and Riya and Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It’s Ravi Mama and Rita Mami! “So many laddoos and so many people!” says Ravi Mama. “Twelve laddoos for eight of us to share. That makes one for each of us and four remaining!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Ravi Mama and Rita Mami, Ananya and Dhruv, Prisha and Riya and Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It’s Papa! “May I join you?” says Papa. “Don’t forget me!” says Mummy, from the garden. “Twelve laddoos for ten of us to share. That makes one for each of us and two remaining!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Papa and Mummy, Ravi Mama and Rita Mami, Ananya and Dhruv, Prisha and Riya and Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It’s Dada and Dadi! “It’s a party!” says Dada. “No, no…It’s a laddoo party!” corrects Dadi. “Twelve laddoos for twelve of us to share. That makes one for each of us!” says Mira. “Let’s eat!” says Mihir. Dada and Dadi, Papa and Mummy, Ravi Mama and Rita Mami, Ananya and Dhruv, Prisha and Riya and Mira can’t wait to bite into the laddoos. “YES!” says Mira. “At last…!” says Riya. “Yum…mmm…mmm…” says Dhruv. CHEW-CHEW! CHOMP-CHOMP! “May I have another?” asks Prisha. “But they’re all gone!” says Ananya. DING-DONG! Uh-oh! Who’s at the door? It is Neeta Aunty and Peter Uncle and their little niece Alice. “SURPRISE!” says Alice. “Thanks!” says Mihir. “More laddoos for us to share. Happy Laddoo Party everyone!” There are thirty laddoos in the box. If there were fifteen people at home, how many laddoos would each get? If there are eight big laddoos and four of you, how would you share them equally?
author: Srividhya Venkat

title: Bhabho the Buffalo
text: It got stuck on Bhabho’s horns. Bhabho hardly noticed this little seed. Slowly, the seed began blooming into a tiny sapling. Leaves began sprouting. Eventually, that little sapling began to grow into a plant. Branches began spreading their arms. Everyone was worried for Bhabho. But Bhabho was indifferent. She would roam and sit anywhere she liked, just like before. When the sun shone fiercely, other buffaloes would get hot and bothered searching for shade. But Bhabho didn’t have to lift a leg. She’d giggle and say, “Look, I have my own umbrella!” They couldn’t help but agree with her. After all, Bhabho now had a splendid tree growing on her horns. One day, a bird decided to make her nest on Bhabho’s tree. “Don’t shake the tree, Bhabho,” she warned the buffalo. “I’ve kept my eggs on it.” Bhabho felt irritated. “But I will need to search for food, won’t I?” she asked. The bird thought to herself, “Bhabho is right.” She gathered all her bird-friends and told them, “We will need to bring Bhabho her food so she doesn't move our babies!” Bhabho would happily chomp the food brought to her by the birds and relax in the shade of her tree. What else could a buffalo want in life? A tree on Bhabho’s horns, leaves on the tree, a nest among the leaves and two little eggs in the nest. What a quirky sight! People would remark to Bhabho that she was being far too lazy. But Bhabho remained unconcerned. “Is there any other buffalo around who is doing what I’m doing?” she’d ask. Nobody had an answer to Bhabho’s question. But they all knew that one day, the eggs would hatch, the little birds would grow up and eventually fly away. Bhabho would finally have to get up and roam around for shade and food just like the other buffaloes. But Bhabho had made a secret decision. She would continue sitting at her spot forever. Because Bhabho was like no other buffalo.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Vegetables, Anybody?
text: Mother was fed up with Geetu. Geetu would make a fuss whenever she had a meal. She would eat puris or parathas sometimes. But vegetables were a big ‘no-no’. Geetu would finish her meal when her mother was not present. Or she would empty her vegetable bowl back into the pot when her mother was not looking. She relished sweets and ice creams, pastries and cookies. She could gorge on pizzas and burgers and guzzle soft drinks. But vegetables, NO Mother had tried many methods to make Geetu at least taste the vegetables that she made but Geetu slipped away every time. And finally Mother decided that Geetu’s grand parents would be the best choice to make Geetu eat vegetables. That summer saw Geetu and her Mother set out for the little village of Kumarkonam. Unfortunately, Geetu’s grandparents were too fond of their granddaughter to force her to eat the hated vegetables or even to make her do anything against her wish. The first few days went by in Mother trying to convince her parents to teach Geetu to eat. One week later, Geetu’s grandfather took her to the fields nearby. ‘Do you know that your grandmother used to work in the fields when she was young?’ asked her grandfather. ‘She loved the plants and shrubs and the crops.’ ‘What plants did she like?’ Asked Geetu curiously. She couldn’t imagine her grandmother as a young girl. ‘Well she loved all the colourful ones- green peas, red tomatoes, orange carrots, white radish, red beet, and yellow pumpkin…’ ‘Was it hard work?’ Geetu asked hesitantly. ‘Yes, of course. But she was proud of the fact that she could grow the plants she loved to eat,’ said Grandfather. The next day, early in the morning, Geetu and her grandfather set out for the fields. There, Dhondu, the field worker had cleared a small piece of land. Geetu excitedly placed some seeds her grandfather had given her in little holes. She covered up the holes and watered them. Day after day, both followed the same routine. It was difficult to drag Geetu away from the piece of land. She even suggested that they spend the night there, so that they could watch the plants growing. In a week’s time the plants started showing wisps of green. Then came small tendrils, followed by little signs of the fruit. Of course some of the plants withered away. Geetu mourned them as if they had been her friends. As her summer vacations were nearing their end, Geetu managed to bring home her harvest- six brinjals, ten tomatoes and a few green chilies. Geetu laid the vegetables out on the table- proudly showing off her produce. She told her mother, ‘Make the brinjals for me, Mother. And don’t forget to add the tomatoes.’ Mother stared at her open-mouthed. But grandfather secretly smiled into his beard. He remembered a similar trick played on another nine year old, many years ago, before she became his wife.
author: usha aswath iyer
illustrator: Alankrita Amaya; Antra Khurana; Diana James; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Ninoshka Dias; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Priya Kuriyan; Samidha Gunjal; Santosh Pujari; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Srirupa Gupta; Tanaya Vyas

title: Summer Trip of Animal Kingdom
text: It was summer season and it was very hot. The animal kingdom felt tired and bored. They decided to take a summer holiday trip to the newly opened “Human World Theme Park”. They felt very excited as they would get to see different types of humans and understand their behaviour. The animals boarded a train and off they went to the theme park. All the animals danced and sang songs as the train chugged away to the theme park. The Human World Theme Park was something that seemed totally new to them. There were several buildings of different shapes and sizes. There were very few trees and plants. There were some strange moving objects that seemed to carry the humans from one place to another. Inside the theme park, the animals first met Srinivas, an animal bully. He liked to scare animals and harm them. He felt happy doing it. As the animals passed by, they saw him scaring and chasing away a monkey. The dolphins saw this and said to Srinivas,”Why can’t you be like us? We are very kind to other animals and humans as well. We have saved many animals and humans from danger. We are friendly and care for other living things” Next, the animals met Raju and his mother buying vegetables and fruits from a shop. They asked the shopkeeper to put all the vegetables they bought in a bag as they did not bring one. The shopkeeper put the vegetables in a plastic bag and gave it to them. The birds and Octopus saw this and said,” Why can’t you be like us and protect the environment by reusing and recycling materials instead of using new plastic bags everytime”. The octopus said,” I use discarded coconut shells as shelter”. The birds said, “We use any waste items like broken twigs, and other discarded items to build our nests” Next, the animals met Ramu,a school student. His mother said to him,” Ramu, you have to work hard if you have to succeed in life. Iam only asking you to sit and study for couple of hours every day. Can’t you do that?”. Ramu replied,” Amma, two hours is too much.” The bees saw this and said to Ramu, “Why can’t you be like us and work hard? We travel several thousands of miles and visit huge number of flowers just to collect a small teaspoon of nectar. If we had not worked hard like this, the world would not have had honey” Next the animals met a group of school students who lost a football match in a tournament. They were complaining about each other about the reason for the loss. One boy said, "It is because of Sanjay we lost. He missed such an easy goal". Another boy said, "Ram did not defend the ball properly. That is why they were able to score easily". Likewise many names cropped up as reasons for the loss The ants saw this and told the boys," Why can’t you be like us and work as an organized team. You will surely succeed. We are able to carry loads of food several hundred times our weight because we work as a team. We are able to build giant ant hills because of proper teamwork. We never complain about one another and only focus on achieving the goal as a team". The trip finally ended. The animals went back to their habitat thinking that the humans can learn a lot from them.
author: Aru
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Bindia  Thapar; Deepa Balsavar; Herminder Ohri; Muniza Shariq; Priya Kuriyan; Rajiv Eipe; Sanjay Sarkar; Sou  Kimsan; Soumya Menon; Sunando C

title: Sharing
text: She calls out, “Ma, I'm hungry! Please give me something to eat.” Next door, Bala feels hungry. She calls out, “Aunty, I'm hungry! Please give me something to eat.” Ma makes khichdi from rice and lentils for Rani. “But I don’t like khichdi!” Rani sighs. Ma says,“Khichdi is good for you, Rani." “ Go on, eat it." Rani walks outside with her bowl of khichdi still feeling hungry. Next door, Aunty prepares noodles for Bala. “But I don’t like noodles!” Bala sighs. Aunty says, “Noodles are good for you, Bala." “ Go on, eat.” Bala walks outside with her bowl of noodles still feeling hungry. Rani notices Bala's bowl of noodles and says, “Oh! I love noodles!” Bala replies, “And I love khichdi!” Rani happily gives her khichdi to Bala. And Bala happily gives her noodles to Rani. “YUM! These noodles are delicious!” “YUM! This khichdi is so good! ” Ma walks out and sees Rani eating noodles. Aunty comes out and sees Bala eating khichdi. Ma and Aunty look at each other and smile. Aunty says, “The girls are so happy to share their food!"
author: Erica Cuellar

title: Froggy Finds His Smile
text: Little Froggy was very sad. He tried hard to smile, but he couldn't. He thought to himself, Alas! I lost my smile. He decided to look around for his smile. On the dewy grass, he saw a big black snake. "Hey there! Have you seen my smile?", asked Froggy The snake hissed and said, "Nope, try else where". Froggy looked up and saw an owl sitting on the branch of a woody tree. "Have you seen my smile?", asked Froggy. The owl hooted Hoo-ah-hoo...Hooo...Hoooo...Hoooooooo and said, "Nope, try else where". Froggy moved on and saw a lizard sitting on a rock. "Have you seen my smile?", asked Froggy. The lizard squeaked and said, "Nope, try else where". Moving on, Froggy saw a shrew sitting on a tree branch. "Have you seen my smile?", asked Froggy. The shrew twittered and said, "Nope, try else where". Froggy was disappointed. He kept walking. He saw a horn bill sitting on the farthest branch. "Have you seen my smile?", asked Froggy. The hornbill gave a reverberating kok and said, "Nope, try else where". Froggy sighed and in the adjacent branch, saw a black langur. "Have you seen my smile?", asked Froggy. The langur squawked loudly and said, "Nope, try else where". Froggy felt depressed and dejected. He must have really lost his smile somewhere. Then, he saw an orange bird. "Birdy, you fly far and wide. Have you seen my smile"? asked Froggy. The bird chirped and flew away without giving Froggy a look, "Nope, try else where". After all this, Froggy was totally hungry and exhausted. He decided to head home. He saw her mother sitting on their favorite rock, surrounded by beautiful violet flowers. "Mama, Have you seen my smile"? asked Froggy. Mother croaked and said, "Indeed I have, dear." "Mama, where's it? I have been searching for it every where.", Froggy asked impatiently. "The smile is in your eyes, sweetie." "Ugh! In my eyes?" "Yes, It is within you, me, and all of us. Don't look for reasons to smile. Pass the smile and joy around. It's infectious and spreads fast.", Mama frog explained. "Ha ha. Sure, Mama". Froggy hugged his mom. Froggy found his lost smile. By the way, have you?
author: Lakshmi Venkat

title: THE MAGICAL ELEPHANT
text: There once lived a magical elephant in the banks of the river Nandhini.One day a farmer who lived in the jungle had come to take water to his home. He saw the elephants bathing at the other side of the river.He tought to himself that the 3rd biggest elephant was a magical elephant.It had a design like a magician.But still,he wanted to test it if it was a real magical elephant. Suddenly, because of the heavy rain and wind a small humming bird had fallen in the river and with his magical powers lifted the drenched humming bird and laid him on a tree. Ramu was shocked, and he wanted the elephant so he climbed a tree and took many bananas and cleverly laid them in the ground. He set the bananas till his home and went back to his house. The next morning he saw the elephant at his his doorstep. Years passed, both of them became very good friends.The farmer treated him very well.He gave good food, water and shelter. The elephant also gave him a lot of things back.One day the farmers 3 cruel friends Ramu, Harish and Viram was crossing the farmers house and saw the farmer had become very rich. Is he a farmer or a lawyer? Asked Viram.He is definitely a farmer. Said Harish. No, he is definitely a lawyer.Stop fighting you idiots, this is not the time to fight. He has started a fair over there.Said Viram.We need to find how he has become rich.Today night we are Stepping in his home and find the reason behind how the farmer got rich.Said Ramu.It's time to rob.Said Harish. That night, all three of them went to his house sneaking through the forest. Harish who was not scared of anything went first to see if there was some danger coming. Viram followed Harish. Ramu the scariest guy went at the last.his legs was shivering and when the owls start howling he use to hide behind Viram.Viram got annoyed at what Ramu was doing, but he didn't want to yell so he whispered, don't do that Ramu stop hiding behind me.They started walking,they walked and walked untill the farmers house came. Finally they reached the farmers house. They climbed the wall and slowly jumped inside the house. They knew that the doors was closed, so they had to sneak through the window. They searched through all the windows but they could not find anyone. Finally, the last window at the back of the house they saw a big room and a big thing inside. Go get the truck Viram, said Harish. Viram ran and got the truck. HARISH USED HIS BRAIN and kept so many bananas on the carrier of the truck. The elephant smelled the bananas and went and sat on the carrier and started eating the bananas. Meanwhile the others closed the carrier and drove the truck to their home.Months passed, at one said Ramu, Viram and Harish were treating the elephant very badly that it was losing it's power and energy. The three people was acting more harshly than a britisher. The elephant gave everything to them. He gave lots and lots of money, he gave money more than the richest person in the world. They asked him more than 100 bungalows but did not give anything in return. At the other side the farmer was very sad for losing his dear friend.He searched everywhere but could not find him. One day when the farmer was leaning at his window he was seeing the back part of his house, he saw huge footprints in the size of an elephants leg.He went down and saw some truck tire marks.He followed them and went to a big bungalow.There he sneaked through a window and saw all his three friends over there treating the elephant very harshly. He got very angry. He took a stone, broke the window glass and went inside. The 3 friends knew that the farmer, so they had made a weapon, a robot weapon! He fought with the robot but lost. He fought 10 times but all the times he use to lose, he used to get new plans everyday day but still he used to lose. on the 11th day he had a plan he knew that his friends was greedy and robot could be defeated by water so he bravely went to the fight hoping for a win. When he entered there house the robot came to attack, he told wait, he told his ex-friends that there is a well near the banyan tree, inside the well there is a treasure. The 3 friends believed it and went and dived in the well. They swam but could not find the treasure, after sometime they came to recognize that the farmer had fulled them, they started shouting for help but no one came. Meanwhile, the robot was guarding the elephant. The farmer ran and got a bucket of water and poured it on the robot. The robot's engine got spoiled and the robot fell down. the farmer took the elephant to his home and gave it a lot's of food. The next day, the farmer put on the T.V, a newscaster was telling that an elephant was destroying the market he saw the elephant's picture. When he saw the picture he came to know that it was the mother of the elephant because it had a flower design just like his elephant. He knew he had to let go the elephant for his village, he was sad but still he had to give him back. So he went to the market and saw the elephant destroying the market. He threw an apple on the elephant to distract it's attraction on others. The elephant got very angry and started attacking him that time the farmer got his elephant in front of him. The elephant stopped attacking the both stood happy, small tears came from there eyes. The mother elephant was showing it's love with it's trunk. The farmer was happy to see both of them happy.All it's family members came and started showing it's love. The elephants started going to their home. Take care of you little elephant, live happy with your family happily. I will never forget you. The elephant waved a bye with it's trunk. and went home. I will never forget you little elephant. bye, bye.

title: Diu Reads Books
text: Meet Diu, the perpetual bookworm. She is always with a book. Yes, always! Diu reads a book when in bed. Is she doing the right thing? Diu reads a book when in the bathroom washing up. Is she doing the right thing? Diu reads a book when having her breakfast. Is she doing the right thing? Diu reads a book when she steps out to go to school. Is she doing the right thing? Diu reads a book when playing in the swing. Is she doing the right thing? Diu reads a book even when she sits in the garden. Is she doing the right thing? Is Diu doing the right thing? Partly Yes and partly No. Is Diu doing the right thing? Yes, because it's good to read books. Books inspire creativity. Books answer questions that you have. Books also contain questions for you. Is Diu doing the right thing? No, because you should not read a book when bathing, eating, playing or when stepping outside. What's a bookworm? Scientifically, a bookworm refers to any insect that bores through and damages the books. They gnaw the binding and make small holes on the books. You can see them in old books that you borrow from the lending library. Who's a bookworm? Someone who reads a lot. Someone who loves to read. How to select good books? Think about what you like. Think about what you don't like. Visit a good library. Ask the librarian for suggestions. Always sit at your desk to read a book. Sitting posture matters. Ensure there's plenty of natural light. Keep the book at a comfortable distance from the eye. Use bookmarks to keep tab of your reading progress. Don't read for a really really long time. Take breaks often. Don't read on a moving vehicle or while having food like Diu did. Wow, is there so much to do when reading a book? Surely, I will follow these pointers. Diu thought to herself. Gleefully, she resumes reading her favorite book. So, what's your excuse? Your book is up for grabs. Happy reading!
author: Lakshmi Venkat

title: Gulmohar
text: Ambika is Sad. She has to move to new town. Her father is transferred again She is not able to make new friends. Her parents are worried. Ambika thanks her mother for putting the swing on the tree..
