title: Simba's Cosy Corner
text: Simba was now nine months old. And he had decided it was time for him to be a real watch dog. He would stay awake all night and guard his family. But then he needed to sleep during the day. Where could he sleep without being disturbed? His first thought was the kitchen. Mother was tolerant and she whipped wonderful smells. But the thought of the shrill pressure cooker, the grinding of teeth of the mixer and the sputtering of mustard seeds- who could sleep through these sounds? Father’s room was out of the question- Father was strict about rules and he kept the door to his room shut. Father did not trust Simba! One day he slipped into the laundry basket- it was wonderful. Full of the smells of his family. He secretly wondered why humans shed their skin so quickly, every day practically. But Bina, the maid upset his cosy plans when she picked up the basket and up-ended the contents on to the floor. His attempts to sleep peacefully were all in vain. How could a house of four members, of whom two left every morning, be so noisy and unsafe for a poor dog? The drawing room was frequently disturbed by the calling bell; the bathroom was no place for a decent dog. And the bedrooms were not kept open for Simba. A week after this futile search for a cosy corner, Mother kept calling Simba. She couldn’t find him anywhere. He had not gone out, so where could he be? It was only by mid-morning she realized where the cunning little pup was. He was curled up on an old, empty sack, in a corner of the storeroom! ﻿ Mother gently closed the store room door, remembering to leave it a little ajar for the poor tired mite who took his guard duties so seriously.
author: usha aswath iyer
illustrator: Audrey Agnier; Niloufer Wadia; Preethi Krishnan; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Rijuta Ghate; Sheetal Thapa; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sunaina  Coelho

title: Fishing in My Village
text: Last night, it rained so hard that water overflowed the river banks. The villagers got excited and started fishing! Thao Thong fished with a hook and line, and caught a big striped snakehead fish. Nang Khambai fished with a fishing cage and caught a silver barb. Nang Bouakhao’s fishing net caught shrimp. Grandfather Boun used a cast net to catch an Asian red-tailed catfish. Thao Kood fished with gillnets and caught mud crabs. Grandmother Pheng fished with lift nets and caught river carp. Uncle Khampiew used a trap and caught catfish. Aunt Khamsouk went spin fishing and caught a broadhead walking catfish. Thao So fished with a pole and line and caught a basa fish. At noon, the villagers enjoyed their catch. They cooked all the fish and had lunch together by the river.
author: Sanjana  Khoobchandani

title: Meow!
text: Plop! Bham! Dhap! Hearing these sounds, Rimi rushed to the kitchen. Four tiny paws and two curious eyes stared back at Rimi in fear. "Meow!" said Rimi with a smile on her face. She stretched out her hands towards the tiny kitten. "Meow!" responded the four hearty paws, staring back at Rimi. The kitten came to see Rimi's hand. It was looking for food. "Mom, can we give her some food?", Rimi asked mom. A bowl full of milk and crushed biscuits were served. The kitty looked happy and smiled at Rimi. Rimi wanted to play with the kitty the entire day. But, the kitty drank all the milk and jumped out of the window. Rimi became sad and almost started crying. Mom came to console her but she was still sad. She went to her bed and sunk her face into the pillow. After sometime, she heard "Meow". Rimi jumped up to see if the kitty was back. Her mom stood at the door, with a glass of milk in her hand. Rimi ran to her and hugged her tight. "My meow is back", said Mom.
author: Aditya Sen
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Deepa Balsavar; Gwendolene van der Merwe; JP Brouard; Kalynne Vorster; Madhavi Agnihotri; Madhuri Purandare; Ruchi Shah; Suvidha Mistry

title: My Cousin Visits My Village
text: This is my village. Today Ek comes to visit. Ek is my cousin from the city. I show Ek my family. “Here is my mother and my father.” “Here is my grandma and my grandpa.” I show Ek our river. “Look! A villager is fishing!” I show Ek our big rice field. It is filled with yellow rice! “And this is where we keep rice. ” “ Rice must stay dry!” “This is our village temple. ” “The monks keep the yard tidy.” “This is our mango grove.” “The mangoes are ripe and juicy.” Ek, be careful! “Don't worry, Ek! We can rest here.” “It's our house.” “This is our market.” “Aunty makes delicious treats!” “Ek, don't eat them all!” “I love my village,” Nouy says. “I love your village too!” Ek agrees.What else can we see tomorrow?
author: Silima Keopaseuth

title: Radha's Scarecrow
text: Radha was a nine year old girl who lived with her parents in a small house near their fields in Rampur village. She helped her mother at home and her father in the field. She loved to sit by the window in her room and look at the field. This year they were working very hard in the field because they did not have a good crop for the last two years. Her father was thinking of new methods to have a good crop this year. He heard the villagers talking about making a scarecrow to protect the crop from being eaten by the birds. He decided to make one for his field too because last year the birds had destroyed the entire crop. He went home and called Radha and told her about his plan to make a scarecrow. Radha gladly offered to help. He asked her to bring some hay and rope from the backyard. In the meantime, he tied a few sticks together to make the structure of a scarecrow. He then painted a round earthen pot and made eyes, nose and a smiling mouth for the scarecrow. He then asked Radha to bring one of her old dress for the scarecrow to wear. Radha asked angrily, "Why should I give my dress for the scarecrow? You have not bought me any dress for the past two years and now you want me to give one dress to this scarecrow." Her father rolled his eyes and said sternly,"Go and bring an old dress quickly. I have to fix the scarecrow in the field today itself." Radha went to her room stomping her feet. She chose a very old tattered red dress for the scarecrow and gave it to father. The scraecrow was ready to be put in the field with its smiling face. But Radha was sad. She had to part with a dress of hers. That night she cried to sleep. The next day when she woke up, she looked outside her window and saw the smiling scarecrow standing in the field. She grumbled looking at the sacrecrow, "Stop smiling. You took my red dress so I am never going to talk to you." Everyday Radha would look at the scarecrow from her window and cry about the red dress. She was very upset with the scraecrow. A few months had passed but Radha was still angry with the scarecrow. She could only see her red dress on the scarecrow and its smiling face. One morning, while she was still sleeping, father came to wake her up. He was very excited. "Radha wake up. Wake up you lazy bones. I have to show you something. I am so happy it worked. Wake up fast." Rubbing her eyes, Radha woke up. Her father was standing near the window and pointing towards the field. She got up and saw what her father was pointing. To her surprise the field was lush green with beautiful crop swaying with the morning breeze. She rubbed her eyes again and again. She could not believe her eyes. Father and Mother were very happy. They were talking about a bumper crop this year. Father came close to Radha and said, "Its good we made the scraecrow. The birds did not spoil the crop this year. I will buy you a new dress and toys with the money we will get by selling the crop." Radha was also very happy but she was surprised too. She thought, "I looked from the window everyday but I never noticed the crop. I only saw the scarecrow wearing my red dress. It made me very sad and angry." Since Radha was so angry at the scarecrow she never noticed the beautiful crop growing around it. But now Radha was very happy because father had promised her a new dress and toys. She was no longer angry at the scarecrow and was glad that together they made the scraecrow and she gave her red dress to the scarecrow.
author: Neha Modi
illustrator: Priya Kuriyan; Ruchi Mittal; Sanjay Sarkar; Tanaya Vyas

title: Bounthy's Singing Birds
text: There are birds all around that sing beautiful songs. "Coo-oo, coo-oo," sing the birds. Bounthy sits and listens to the birds sing with joy. Every day, his father takes one bird to the forest to help catch other birds. He catches the birds one by one and brings them all home. Bounthy’s home is filled with birds. But after some time, instead of singing, they sigh sadly. One day, Bounthy wakes up to see that none of his birds is singing. He tries to find ways to make them happy and sing again. He feeds them rice, but they don't eat any of it. “What happened to you, my birds?” he asks them. “Do you want to go back to the forest?” Bounthy decides to talk to his father. Bounthy and his father take the birds back to the forest and set them free. As the birds fly away, they look back at Bounthy with a smile. The next morning, Bounthy hears all of the birds singing happily on a tree next to his home. “Coo-oo! Coo-oooo!”
author: Sanjana  Khoobchandani

title: Nin Wants to Get Dressed
text: Today is Nin's first day of school. But Nin can't put on her uniform by herself! She runs to her mother for help. “Mama, will you help me put on my uniform?” asks Nin. “I will help you when I finish cooking,” says Ma. Nin runs outside to find someone else who can help. “Papa, will you help me put on my uniform?” asks Nin. “I will help you when I finish feeding the ducks,” says Papa. “Grandpa, will you help me put on my uniform?” asks Nin. “I am taking the cattle to the field. I’ll help you when I come back,” says Grandpa. “Grandma, will you help me put on my uniform?” asks Nin. “I will help you once I finish sweeping leaves from the yard,” says Grandma. “Brother Lah! Will you help me put on my uniform?” asks Nin. “I'll help you when I finish drawing water from the well,” says Brother Lah. No one can help me, thinks Nin sadly. Everyone is so busy! Nin decides to put on her uniform herself. First, it's inside-out. Then, the back is in the front! And then, Nin tries to put on her shoes. Nin looks in the mirror. Oh no! Her uniform is all wrong! Her family looks at her and giggles. “I will help you,” says Ma. “We will also help you!” say Brother Lah and Papa. Now, Nin is finally ready for school. Have a great first day, Nin!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Bountong's New Hat
text: He made it himself. It is brown with a long tail. It has horns and big eyes. It looks like Buk-Le, his water buffalo. When the wind blows Whooosh! Whooosh! the hat's tail flies high. Bountong is happy with his new hat. He puts it on and runs to visit Buk-Le. Now they can play like two buffaloes! They ride across the fields and run with the wind. Wooooooo! shouts Bountong. Mooooooo! moos Buk-Le. Wooooshh! blows the wind. Wheeee! says the hat. Suddenly, the wind blows hard. The hat's tail tugs and flutters. Bountong gets tangled in the hat's long tail! He tumbles down from Buk-Le. Buk-Le feels bad for his friend. The wind is worried. Bountong's new hat feels sorry. “Go away!” shouts Bountong. He throws the hat away. The wind blows the hat up, up, up! Go! Go! Go! says the wind to the hat. The hat says good-bye sadly. The hat flies into the air. It disappears. But now the wind begins to blow. The rain begins to fall. Bountong wishes he had his hat. Bountong and Buk-Le walk back across the fields. The rain falls like needles on their backs. Bountong and Buk-Le shiver in the cold. Bountong starts to cry. He misses his hat. “Where are you, hat?” When the wind hears Bountong crying, it searches for his hat. Found it! The wind blows and blows. Bountong and Buk-Le slowly trudge homewards. When Bountong arrives home, what does he find? Now they can play like two buffaloes again. Bountong, Buk-Le and Bountong's hat. The wonderful brown hat with a long tail, horns and big eyes.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Douangkeo Wants to Be a Magician
text: Khamla wants to be a teacher because she likes to help people learn. Duoangta wants to be a doctor because she wants to help sick people. Khonesavan wants to be a novice monk because he wants to show his community how to be a good person. As for Douangkeo, she wants to be a magician because she loves magic shows! But she doesn't know what to do! She doesn't have the tools that a magician needs. There’s not even a school for magicians in her neighbourhood. Douangkeo loves her dog. He is her best helper. He is great at tricks. All his tricks give Douangkeo an idea! She will teach herself how to be a magician! And her trusty dog will help. First, Douangkeo turns the rice basket into a magic hat. Then she turns a curtain into her magician’s cape. The sticky rice container turns into her magic box. A chopstick becomes her wand. Douangkeo is finally a good magician! She and her dog can now perform magic shows for all her friends. And that's exactly what they do.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Xay Goes Fishing
text: I go with you?” asked Buffalo, as he jumped onto the boat. Xay's boat sank. “Oh no, you can't come with me!” Xay said. “May I go with you?” asked Horse, as he climbed aboard the boat. Once again, Xay's boat sank. “Oh no, you can't come with me either!” Xay said. “May I go with you?” asked Goat, as she stepped onto the boat. Xay's boat sank. “Oh no, you can't come with me either!” Xay said. “May I go with you?” asked Pig, as she walked right onto the boat. Xay's boat sank. “Oh no, you can't come with me either!” Xay said. “May I go with you?” asked Dog, as she stepped onto the boat. Xay's boat sank. “Oh no, you can't come with me either!” “May I go with you?” asked Cat, as he nimbly leapt onto the boat. Xay's boat didn't sink! "Yes! You can come with me.” Xay said. Xay and Cat went out to fish in the middle of the river. They fished happily and caught a lot of fish. After a while, Xay and Cat began to miss the the friends they had left behind on the shore. They rowed back to their friends on the shore. They all fished happily by the river bank.
author: Brian Kavanagh

title: Colouring Pencils
text: He is very happy. “Thank you, Ma!” he says. The pencils in the box are scared. “I don’t want to get out of the box,” says the yellow pencil. “I'm afraid To To might wear me out!” the red pencil exclaims. “Yes, I’m afraid, too,” says the blue pencil. “But let’s get out and explore.” Outside the box, the colouring pencils spot a colouring book on the table. “Hey, these pictures are so creative!” says the red pencil. “I like these pictures,” cries the yellow pencil. “I like them too,” agrees the blue pencil. “But why are these pictures not coloured?” asks the blue pencil. “I don’t know,” says the yellow pencil. “I don’t know either,” says the red pencil. “Well, without coloured pencils like you, these pictures will never have colours,” says the colouring book. “I’m worried that To To might use us too roughly. That will hurt!” says the red pencil. “But I also want these pictures to look beautiful.” “Well, what can we do?” asks the blue pencil. “Let’s get back into the box,” says the yellow pencil. Soon, To To takes out the pencils. “I will colour all my pictures!” he says happily. He uses the pencils gently to colour the pictures in his colouring book. When he's gone, the colouring pencils look at the pictures that To To has coloured. “These pictures look beautiful!” says the red pencil. “I love them!” says the yellow pencil. “Me too!” cries the blue pencil. All the colouring pencils make a decision together. “We want all the pictures in the world to have beautiful colours like this!” they say.
author: Gouri Srinidhi

title: Busy Mother Hen
text: She waits and waits for her eggs to hatch. Mother Goat passes by. “Will you go to the fair with me?” she asks Mother Hen. “I'm busy with my eggs, ” Mother Hen answers. One, two, three, four, five, six. Six round eggs! Mother Pig passes by. “Will you go to the fair with me?” she asks. “I'm busy with my eggs,” answers Mother Hen. One, two, three, four, five, six. Six round eggs! Mother Cow passes by. “Will you go to the fair with me?” she asks Mother Hen. “I'm busy with my eggs,” answers Mother Hen. Mother Hen waits and waits. “When will I see my chicks?” she wonders. Mother Hen feels something. What's happening? One, two, three, four, five, six. Crack! Crack! Crack! Crack! Crack! Crack! Six chicks have hatched. Mother Hen is happy with her lovely chicks. Then she remembers. There is a fair today! Mother Goat, Mother Pig and Mother Cow have already left. Mother Hen is ready now. She will take her chicks to the fair. One, two, three, four, five, six! Mother Hen and her six chicks have a fantastic time at the fair. What fun! Her chicks were worth the wait.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Kolam fun!
text: Priya loved kolams. She would sit for hours in her verandah looking at the stars and trying to make kolam patterns out of them. Priya's mother was an expert Indian classical musician who loved singing and playing the veena. Priya used to listen to her mother with fascination. Priya's mother was also an expert kolam artist. However, Priya could never use her mother's kolam powders because her mother forbade her from doing so. Deepavali was arriving and Priya's mother was making sweets. Priya thought of giving her mother a colourful surprise. She first went to Ahmed chacha's kurta dukan, to see if she could buy her darling mother a lovely kurta. Mom's kurtas looked so faded. She eagerly asked Ahmed chacha, "Chacha, how much for this purple kurta?" Ahmed chacha smiled, "Dear, that kurta is costly. It is 1200 rupees." Priya looked sadly at the kurta and walked away from Ahmed chacha's kurta dukan. Then, she saw a mango tree. "Mm," she said," I shall get mummy some mangoes." She climbed the first branch then the next and stretched her hand out. She stretched as far as she could but no mango came in her hands. Felling sad, she walked away from the mango tree. It was finally deepavali day and Priya still hadn't got her mother anything. Her elder brother Rahul told Priya proudly," See. I got mummy a saree from Kashmir when I went with my friends." Priya felt even more sad looking at the beautiful saree in front of her. Priya suddenly got a big idea! Lots of flowers had fallen in her garden. She gathered all her flowers and. with the help of her aunt, made a huge kolam! "Mummy! Mummy!" she cried, "Come fast!" her mother came to see what she was making so much noise about. When she saw the kolam, she hugged Priya with tears in her eyes. "Dear," she told Priya," I am giving you permission to use any of my kolam powders from now onwards!" Priya couldn't stop smiling. Excited, Priya wore her new dress and lit the Deepavali lamps. Mummy was wearing the new saree her brother had gifted her and was looking happily at the kolam. Priya yelled, "Happy Diwali!"
author: Sanjana

title: Kham's Precious Little Lamp
text: Every night, he reads a book by the light of his little lamp. Before he goes to bed, he puts out the lamp. Kham likes his little lamp. It is precious to him. One day, electricity reaches Kham's village. Electricity turns night into day. Kham's little lamp lies forgotten in the corner. The little lamp misses the nights when Kham would light her and she'd help him do his work. She remembers the happy nights when Kham and she used to catch frogs, go fishing and read books together. One night, Kham's village is caught in a thunderstorm with heavy rain. The power goes out. Kham begins to look for his little lamp. When he finds her, Kham smiles and whispers, “You are my bright light.” He sits down to read his book by the light of his little lamp, just like old times. When it's time for Kham to go to bed, he puts out the lamp......and sleeps peacefully. The little lamp is happy to be needed again. She sleeps peacefully too, smiling in the darkness.
author: Shannon David

title: I Love My Mom
text: She works hard all the time. And I learn so much from her! When my mom cooks, I learn to cook too. When she waters the flowers, I learn to water the flowers too. When she washes our clothes, I learn to wash our clothes too. When she dries our clothes, I learn to dry our clothes too. My mom also bought me a bicycle and she taught me how to ride it. As I ride my bicycle, my mom smiles when I go “WHEEEEEEE!” At night, my mom makes the bed. I learn how to make the bed too. Before bedtime, my mom tells me stories. When I'm sleepy, my mom sings me a lullaby. I love my mom so much!
author: Stephanie  Wei

title: 2 Problems that was solved by Lions and Tigers
text: There once was a forest which was filled with trees. Men came to cut trees in this forest. The animals were quite unhappy. They were afraid to fight with these men. They decided to tell a tiger about this because there were no lions in that forest. They went to the tiger and said “O Great Tiger, have you been noticing that men are cutting trees?.” “Yes, said the tiger but today only, when I woke up this morning, I saw a man cutting a tree. I was sleepy, so I didn’t kill him.” A group of woodcutters were passing that way. They heard the conversation that was going on between the Tiger and the animals. They went to the tiger and said “O great tiger please forgive us.” The Tiger forgave them and said “If you again come to this forest to cut trees, you all will be killed”. They hurried to the little band of Woodcutters “Listen everybody, we should no longer go to the forest to cut trees, We saw a tiger and all the animals of the forest, they were having a meeting, When we heard their conversation, we heard the animals complaining about us, they were saying that they were unhappy because the trees were cut off, we apologized to the tiger and the tiger said If you again come to this forest to cut trees, you all will be killed” “Oh no” said the team’s leader “What shall we do now? Our families will starve with hunger”. The Leader was crying. Some of the woodcutters said “There is another forest 4 kilometers away from the forest which is 2 kilometers away from us. Why not we go and cut trees from there. From that day onwards the group of woodcutter went to another forest to cut trees. The animals were living peacefully for a month, until another error began. Men came with guns and shot at the animals and took the dead bodies. One day, a man shot the tiger too. Now they were many of the animals who lost their children, and animals that lost their mothers. They were very unhappy. It happened that a lion came into the forest. He was kind and gentle. The animals went to him “O Great Lion, will you be our king?” The lion said “Yes, why not”. The animals made him the king. One day, the Lion heard a very loud voice. He ran and ran till he came to a truck. The hunters on seeing the lion hid among the bushes. They whispered “Let’s go away. From tomorrow we will go to a nearby forest. So the hunter from that day on went to the forest where the woodcutters came to cut trees. There were only 31 animals left in the jungle, all the others were shot. A monkey which was the Lion’s minister also was shot. Now a giraffe was the minister of the lion. The animals were living peacefully. The lion was old. He was at least 63 years old. He couldn’t go and get his prey. The day he became 64, a bull came to the forest by mistake. The animals all killed the bull and presented it to the lion. The lion was sad. Yet he ate it. The forest was becoming as before. Many trees grew and the number of animals also increased. The animals lived peacefully in the reign of the gentle and loving lion. Moral: Love solves all problems
author: John Mathew

title: The Three Little Kittens
text: One day three little kittens meet a big dog. The kittens are scared of the dog. The little kittens run......and the dog follows them. The little kittens run faster and faster! The little kittens run into a little bird. But the little kittens keep on running. The little kittens run into a little boy. But the little kittens keep on running. They run towards a long piece of wood. “Uh oh! We're in trouble now.” “Help! Help!” they cry. The smiling dog runs up to them. “I'm so happy to run with all of you!” he says. What a surprise! Now, the little kittens have a new friend.
author: Magdalena  Cooper

title: Rat and Goat
text: Today he wants to play Moek (hopscotch), but there is nobody to play with. “ I have an idea, ” he thinks. “ I'll invite Goat, my neighbour. ” Goat likes to spend time alone, fishing and napping. Rat goes to Goat's house and knocks on the door. Tok Tok! “Brother Goat!” Rat exclaims. “Come play with me!” “No, no!” Goat says. “I need to sleep. I don't want to play.” “Please, Goat,” Rat replies. “Play with me. We will have fun together.” Finally, Goat agrees. “Okay, okay,“ Goat says. “I will play with you.” Goat and Rat play hopscotch together. Goat has lots of fun playing with Rat. He decides that next time, he will jump out of bed to play.
author: Sanjana  Khoobchandani

title: Puppy's Birthday Party
text: I want to give puppy a birthday party!” Xongyee said to her mother. The puppy overhead. He was so happy! Xongyee and her mother went to the market. They bought a birthday cake. Meanwhile, the puppy left the house. She invited her friends to the party. “Hello, my bird-friends! Please come to my birthday party.” “Hello, my rabbit-friends! Please come to my birthday party.” Everyone went to find the cats. “Hello, cat-friends! Please come to puppy's birthday party!” Everyone went to find the turtles. “Hello turtle-friends! Please come to puppy's birthday party.” Everyone went home to puppy's house. Xongyee was going to open the door. She thought the party was a surprise! Instead, Xongyee was surprised! Everyone had come to puppy's birthday party. Everyone loved the party! "Happy Birthday, puppy!" they sang.
author: Alisha Berger

title: An Adventure with a Water-Snake
text: One day, Khan fell asleep while fishing. He was waiting for the fish to eat the rice he used as bait. Suddenly, Khan's fishing rod began to shake! He woke up immediately. What could it be? A creature was struggling to free itself from the fishing rod! The creature tugged and pulled on the rod with such great force that Khan fell into the water. The creature pulled him deep into the the sea. Khan realized the creature was actually a massive water snake! Khan saw all kinds of animals living in the sea. Khan and the water snake swam in the sea together. The water snake took Khan to a rock, and spoke to Khan. “My egg is stuck below this huge rock!” she said. Khan pushed and pushed, but the rock was too heavy to move! Khan had an idea. He opened the bag of rice that was on his shoulder. The nearby sea animals swam up to Khan, and wanted to eat the rice. Khan requested all the animals that wanted the rice to help him free the egg from the rock. All the sea animals agreed to help. They began their journey to the rock. When they reached the rock, they pushed and pushed with all their might. After a lot of effort, the rock finally moved. Khan saw the water snake's precious egg! Khan stretched his hand out and carefully pulled out the egg. It began to rattle and shake! What was happening? Out of the egg came a tiny water snake. It was safe! The water snake was overjoyed. So were Khan and the other sea animals. Khan finally fell asleep, exhausted with all the excitement. The water snake carried him safely on its back. Khan woke up at the riverbank again. He saw his empty bucket filled with fish. Was it all a dream?
author: Gouri Srinidhi

title: STICKY HAS A PROBLEM
text: Sticky loved his mother. And today was her birthday. What could he get her? What should Sticky do? After all he loved his mother so much. What could he get her? What should Sticky do? After all he loved his mother so much. He would not be allowed to go out to the market. He had no money to buy her a gift. But a birthday was a special day. Couldn’t Sticky get his mother a teeny-weeny gift at least? He asked Buzz for some honey, but the bee had finished all his stock. He begged Sheena for some nuts, but Sheena had been greedy and had eaten all her store of nuts. Buffly came flitting by. ‘What is the matter, Sticky dear? Why are you sad?’ Sticky told her his problem. ‘I have an idea,’ said Buffly. ‘And it will not cost you a penny!’ she added. ‘Yes, let’s collect all the wild flowers around us. We can make a bouquet for your mother!’ Sticky smiled with happiness. Buffly directed Sticky towards all the choicest flowers, colourful, fragrant and beautiful. Sticky had a large enough bouquet now. Sticky presented his mother with the flowers. He had another gift for her. Mother was always busy. He made her sit down for a while. Koel, the cuckoo, sang the sweetest songs for Mother. Mother smiled from one end to the other. 'Thank you for a beautiful birthday and wonderful presents, Sticky. Today, you brought music to me.’ Sticky felt so proud. He asked, ‘Which present did you like the best, Mama?’ Mother hugged Sticky and said, ‘Your gifts are wonderful, Sticky. But the best gift of my life? It is you!’
author: usha aswath iyer
illustrator: Anuradha  Dhyani; Deepa Balsavar; Greystroke; Hari Kumar Nair; Joanna  Mendes; Lauren SantaCruz; Manjari Chakravarti; Partho Sengupta; Pia Meenakshi; Priya Kuriyan; Promina Shreshtha; Rishi Goyal; Sanjay Sarkar; Sara Verlekar; Vishnu  M Nair

title: How was the dog Laika allowded to go in space
text: Laika. In 1957, Laika became the first animal launched into orbit, paving the way for human spaceflight.... Laika, a stray dog from the streets of Moscow, was selected to be the occupant of the Soviet spacecraft Sputnik 2 that was launched into outer space on 3 November 1957 This dog was the first animal to go in the space she was the trained to fly the spaceship and the food that they eat a nutritious gel in space. Laika Died within the hours because the spaceship had burst. I was feeling sad for her but she was the the first dog and animal to go in space.
author: Himanshu Rathore

title: A little cat
text: Once upon a time there was a little cat named Creamy. She liked to jump up, down and around! When Creamy's owner Khowhom went to school Creamy kept jumping up, down and around. PRINGGG!! Oops! Creamy broke a vase. When Khowhom came back she laughed and said.. "Oh Creamy you broke my vase." Creamy looked very sad, so Khowhom felt bad and said "Creamy do not cry, I'm sorry." Then Creamy jumped up down and around again!
author: Pawnee Maiden

title: All Aboard
text: Nina is going on her first train ride! But she is not happy at all. Her family is moving from Kolkata to New Delhi. “Do we really have to move?” Nina asks. “All my friends and Nani-Nana are going to miss me. Where will I find the perfect puchkas? Why can’t you find another job in Kolkata, Baba?” “Don’t be sad, Nina,” says Baba. “You will make new friends, and find a new puchkawalla.” But Nina doesn't want to listen. Ma and Baba try to cheer her up. “Would you like some ice cream in a cup?” “Ice cream in a cone?” “Ice cream on a stick?” “Cucumbers?” “Toffees?” “No! I said no!” Nina shakes her head. Ma and Baba do not know what else to do. Then Baba smiles. “I see a...” begins Baba. “Oooh! My favourite game,” says Ma. “I see something that is brown,” says Baba. “My shoes? The hills? The suitcase?” asks Ma. “Suitcase is correct!” Baba says, clapping. Nina puts down her book and starts listening. “My turn,” says Ma. “I see something that is yellow.” “Mustard field!” says Baba. “My hairband!” says Nina. “Correct,” Ma claps for Nina. Nina laughs and joins in. “I see something blue.” “The sky!” says Ma. “I see something brown,” says Ma. “That hill!” says Baba. “I see something white,” says Baba. “A cow!” says Nina. “I see something green,” says Nina “Grass!” reply Ma and Baba. “I see something black,” says Ma. “A crow!” says Nina. “I see a tall animal with brown spots,” says Baba. “Huh! You saw a leopard?” asks Ma. “No, a giraffe!” says Baba. Nina looks out of the window and yells, “Giraffes do not live in India! You cheated, Baba.” Everyone starts laughing. Baba and Ma spread a blanket on their seat. They fluff up a pillow for Nina. “Can we play this game again when we reach Delhi?” Nina smiles. “I am sure it will be even more fun to play this game in a new place!”
author: Rohini Kejriwal

title: STICKY GETS STUCK
text: Snail was in a big hurry. He wanted to go to see the edge of the rainbow. He moved as fast as he could. He met his neighbor, Buffly flitting about the flowers. He did not stop to talk. He saw Artie the ant eating a drop of honey. But Sticky did not stop to share. He heard Koel singing sweetly. But today Sticky would not stop and listen. In his hurry Sticky did not notice two big stones on the way. He moved between the two stones and got stuck! His big shell would not allow him to pass through. Sticky wriggled and struggled, pushed and huffed- but it was of no use. How would Sticky see the rainbow’s edge? Suddenly Sheena, the squirrel popped out of a tree. ‘Hello, Sticky. What are you doing?’ Sticky was too busy to answer. ‘You will break your shell,’ warned Sheena. But Sticky continued to push and push. Suddenly Sheena came near Sticky’s head and said, ‘Why don’t you crawl backwards? Then you can choose another path and your shell will not break.’ Sticky realized Sheena was correct. He crawled backwards and heaved a sigh of relief. Now he would be able to see the edge of the rainbow!
author: usha aswath iyer
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Cornelius Wambi Gulere; Hari Kumar Nair; Manish Mutalik; Musonda  Kabwe; Preeti Krishnamurthy; ROSH; Sanjay Sarkar; sarmistha hota; Shreya  Sen

title: Granny on Wheels
text: ‘Ah, those were the days’, sighed Ammu Amma, sitting on her wheelchair looking out of her window, remembering her younger days. ‘I wish I could get out and see the new world’. She slowly dozed off. Suddenly a crow perched itself on the window sill. ‘Ammu Amma, Ammu Amma!’ cried the crow. ‘To see the new world, you have to circle a tree first...’, Ammu Amma woke up with a jerk. The crow flew away. ‘It must’ve been a dream …’, thought Ammu Amma and she went back to her siesta. Soon a squirrel knocked on her window and whispered, ‘Ammu Amma, Ammu, Amma! You only have to go around a tree...’ Ammu Amma was now wide awake. The squirrel ran back into a shoe flower bush. Now Ammu Amma was scared but also curious. She rang the buzzer which she carried with her to use anytime when she needed help. Uma, a girl of twenty who was her nurse and companion came immediately. Both of them were very fond of each other. ‘Uma, dear, can you to take me to that mango tree outside, please?’, asked Ammu Amma. ‘I think I need some fresh air’. ‘Sure, Ammooma’, replied Uma. Uma headed to the garden pushing Ammu Amma’s wheelchair. Shangu the dog followed them. He then jumped up and sat on Ammu Amma’s lap. Ammu Amma looked around. Komukka the gardener was watering the vegetable patch nearby. Nobody else was around. ‘Now, take me around the mango tree’, instructed Ammu Amma to Uma. Uma was puzzled but did as she was told. As they went half-way around the tree, a strange thing happened. Ammu Amma’s wheelchair started to levitate off the ground, lifting everyone with it. Unable to believe what was happening, Uma held tightly onto the handles of the wheelchair she was pushing. Ammu Amma clutched onto the hand rest with one hand and held on to her dog with the other. They were all so frightened that none of them could speak. Except Shangu, who started to bark. Komukka looked towards the mango tree and saw what looked like a metal chair in the air, with two people and a dog hanging on to it. It was going up in spirals. He dropped what he was doing and rushed to help. He caught hold of a wheel of the wheelchair, tried to yank it down, but instead he seemed to lift with it! That was really surprising, because he was a strong man who could actually lift ten wheelchairs, but now he was at the mercy of one! Soon they stopped circling over the tree and went up into the clouds. Ammu Amma, Komukka and Uma shut their eyes in horror, still tongue-tied. But Shangu stopped barking and slowly settled down. He actually liked the cool wind blowing in his face… it was rather like going for a drive in a car. Except, this was more exciting … he could chase birds from the sky now! And the cars below looked like mere ants. But he was worried about the rest. Why were they so tense? Ammooma did not have to hold him so tight, he knew he could manage by himself. They passed a flock of cranes. ‘Look ma’, said a little crane, ‘these humans really look miserable, they all have their eyes shut tight.’ ‘I know, dear’, said the ma crane. ‘I guess they don’t like change much … they cling onto too many things! Maybe only their dogs can be happy!’ Hearing that, Ammu Amma, slowly opened one eye … and saw Shangu was actually enjoying the ride. She mustered the courage to open the other. She was horrified to see Komukka hanging below the wheels and Uma floating like a cape behind. But she had no clue how to help them. Finally, she consoled herself. ‘This must be a special wheelchair, if it can carry all of us and still keep us safe’, she reasoned. ‘Maybe I just need to relax’. She eased her hands and stretched her legs. She looked ahead and saw how beautiful the setting sun was. A flock of parrots were heading towards their home. ‘Look pa’, said a baby parrot. ‘You told me humans are always talking, but why is this bunch so silent and scared?’ ‘Maybe the girl told them to shut up’, explained the pa parrot. ‘They always do what the others do! What’s worse, when they talk, they try to make us repeat the same thing. We just humor them just to keep them quiet for a while!’. Uma was startled to hear this and opened her eyes. She had a pet parrot at home to whom she was always teaching new words. ‘I’m so sorry’, she apologized to the parrots. ‘I did not know how you felt, I feel so terrible!’. If at all she managed to get back home, she would let her bird out of the cage. She looked down and realized how beautiful the fields down below were. She eased her grip and realized she could actually fly! Uma then saw Komukka dangling from the wheel. ‘Komukka, Komukka, it’s okay … just let go … the laws of motion don’t seem to apply here …’, she cried out to him. ‘What do you know about anything, girl’, shouted back Komukka, his eyes still tightly shut. ‘I’m like a rat trapped tightly under an eagle’s claw!’ ‘No, no, Komu, you won’t fall’, cried Ammu Amma, ‘The girl is right … just open your eyes and feast on the sights…’ But no amount of coaxing nor cajoling could get Komukka to let go nor open his eyes. He looked so blue! Just then the wind blew a large ball of cloud towards him. It was so soft, like ball of fur. The cloud continued to roll all over Komukka, tickling him everywhere. He was starting to loosen his grip. ‘Oh, god’, he cried out loud, ‘please look after my family after I’m gone’. Suddenly a blowball (dandelion) carried by the cloud floated up into his nose. ‘ACHCHoooHooooooo’, Komukka gave an enormous sneeze. This forced him to let go and open his eyes. But he didn’t go spiraling downwards! Instead he felt so agile and light. He was floating! ‘The ladies were right!’, admitted Komukka. He did yoga poses in mid-air. Shangu tried to imitate him. Everyone laughed. Ammu Amma tried to get up from the wheelchair to try some stunts. But she could not. After all, she was ninety-three. So, she started to sing. Uma started to dance. The sky turned orange. The moon was just starting to take over… some stars started to appear, making odd patterns in the sky. To Uma, it looked like they were guiding the wheelchair, but she wasn’t absolutely sure. The most important thing was that no one worried how they were going to get back home. But all of them knew deep inside their hearts they eventually would … even Shangu.
author: Deepthy Menon
illustrator: Ajanta Guhathakurta; Archana Sreenivasan; Henu; Kanika  Nair; Kavya  Bagga; Lavanya Karthik; Niloufer Wadia; Sanjay Sarkar; Shailja Jain Chougule; Sou  Kimsan; Soumya Menon; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Subhasish Das; Suvidha Mistry; Tanaya Vyas; Tapas Guha

title: Diu's Dressing Dilemma
text: Diu is super excited and happy. Woo-hoo! I am going to Rohan's birthday party this afternoon. Let me take a shower first. Later I will figure out what to wear for the party. Yay! Oh well, I will wear one of my nicest clothes. After a quick shower, she went to gather clothes from the clothesline. Gosh! I can't reach my dresses and then she jumped up. Diu sat on her clothes pile looking terribly confused. Huh! What should I wear? She decided to try on her favorite red and green salwar-kameez. Oops! This is too loose. Next, Diu tried the green button-down shirt and red pants. Aargh! Both are so tight and bursting at the seams. Then, she tried her pink leggings. Dang! I can't put my legs in. How about the blue frock or the blue striped Tee? Huh! They don't look pretty. On second thoughts, she fished out the yellow lehenga. Dang! The choli is very tight and hurts. Finally, Diu wore the green kurti and the yellow palazzo. She tied her blue shawl to complete the effect. She looked at the mirror and smiled. Yippe! This looks perfect. And that is what Diu wore for the party. Woo-hoo!, Yay!, Oh well, Gosh!, Huh!, Oops!, Aargh!, Dang!, Huh!, Dang!, Yippe! What are these words? Hurray! You are correct. These are called Interjections. Interjections add an emotion or a sentiment to a sentence. For example, Joy, Surprise, Enthusiasm, Disgust. An interjection can be followed by either a comma or an exclamation mark. Phew! That was quite a mouthful, wasn't it? Recollect that when trying on the yellow lehenga, Diu had said this: Dang! The choli is very tight and hurts. What are the other interjections that you can use instead of Dang? How about? Ouch! That hurts. Darn! That hurts. Gee! That hurts.
author: Lakshmi Venkat

title: The Tino, the Rhear and the Biger
text: Tingu Tiger is not happy with his skin. “It’s furry and orange with black stripes. I wish my skin was rough and grey,” says Tingu. Tingu Tiger likes Ranga Rhino’s skin very much. “Will you change skins with me, Ranga?” asks Tingu. “What fun!” says Ranga. “Let’s do that!” Tingu gives Ranga his furry skin. Ranga gives Tingu her rough skin. “Thank you, Ranga Rhino! I really love my new skin.” “No, no, I am Ranga Rhiger now. And you are not a tiger anymore.” “Right, I am a tino now!” says Tingu. Tingu Tino jumps, dances, swims, runs, and marches happily in his new grey skin. After a while, the skin becomes itchy, scratchy and boring. “I think I will get my old skin back. It was softer, smoother and more fun,” thinks Tingu. “Ranga Rhiger! Where are you?” “Ah, there you are Ranga Rhiger!” Tingu calls out. “No, no! I am not a rhiger now,” says Ranga. “I changed skins with Bubbloo Bear. I am now Ranga Rhear!” “I want my nice old skin back,” sighs Tingu. “Where is Bubbloo Bear?” “There by the pond,” Ranga Rhear points. “But Bubbloo is now a biger!” Bubbloo Biger says “No!” to Tingu. “I don’t want that rough, grey skin and be a bino!” Bubbloo says angrily. “But I don’t want to remain a tino!” cries poor Tingu. Bubbloo Biger has a great idea. “Let’s ask Rani Simmy what to do.” Rani Simmy roars and growls at them. “What nonsense, you silly animals! Change back to your skins right now.” “Ranga, give that skin back to Bubbloo! Bubbloo, give that skin back to Tingu! Tingu, give that skin back to Ranga!” The rhear, the biger and the tino do as they are told. They are back to being a rhino, a bear and a tiger. When Tingu, Ranga and Bubbloo go away, Rani Simmy grins to herself. “That was fun! Hey, Crocodile, let’s become a locodile and a crion!”
author: Ashok Rajagopalan

title: Life in Fishyork
text: Deep in the ocean far from the humans is a beautiful underwater world called Fishyork. In Fishyork everybody are friends except for one creature. This creature is called The big trouble, but his real name is Jayden. Jayden is a giant gray shark, which lives in an old drowned wreck away from all the others. Nobody knows why he does not want to be friendly. He is mean and rude. In his wreck with him lives also 3 evil barracudas who help him with his bad intentions; their names are Jill, Bill and Fill. While Jayden is dedicating on his plans, the entire Fishyork is developing very quickly! There are hospitals, underwater train stations, schools, cars, buildings and shopping centers. Fish are happy and peace is everywhere! In a rough neighborhood in the suburb of the city lives a little fish that is unique because he is long and he has the right fin pink and the left one blue and the rest of his body is white with some black spots; his name is Lexi. When he walkes on the streets everybody looks at him disgusted and try to avoid the little fish. He lives alone because his parents had been killed when he was a baby so he doesn’t remember them. In Fishyork lives also Lexis friend the octopus. His name is Jerry, he is very special because he has only seven tentacles. When Jerry came to school for the first time, he felt very nervous. He was afraid of his new classmates because they could laugh at him. He entered the class and saw a seahorse smiling at him. “He looks nice,” thought Jerry. But he was wrong. The seahorse just wanted to embarrasse him. Jerry was really disappointed. After that a little fish came to him. He never saw a fish like this before; her name is Lexi and she is as unique as Jerry. And the big friendship begins. They have a lot of experiences together and always help each other. They always try to find out what happened with Lexis parents. One day, Lexi and Jerry went to Lexis' house after having been for a ride in Fishyork and they decided to play with the playstation, they went to the cellar where there were all the playstation games but they didn't find them so they searched all over. In the corner they found a box on which was written “memories”. They opened it for curiosity and they found some photos of when they were young with their parents, behind every photo there was the date and the place where it was made, so they decided to visit these places. During their trip through all the places which were written in the photos, they found out a little bit more about her past. They discovered that Lexi’s parents were doctors, and they had saved many lifes. Furthermore, they found out that Lexi had an older brother, too. But, nobody in FishYork knew where he was.Their investigation continued, she was not going to give up, he was the only thing she had. That is why, they interviewed everyone in the town. Finally, they found a clue that led them to an old drowned wreck far away. “Who is there?” Said a hidden creature with a strong voice. “We are Lexi and Jerry, we want to meet you.” “Do you want to meet me, really?” “Yes we do, you are my brother.” Said Lexi. Then the creature came out of the shadows, and the two friends discovered that Lexi’s brother was The big Trouble. At the beginning they were scared, because they thought that he was bad, as his name said. But, then they realized that he was like that because he lost his parents when he was a child. Lexi’s parents decided to adopt a shark, before Lexi was born, and they loved both equally.
author: Veronika Mojik

title: Tall and Short
text: Pa is getting my hat. Pa is tall. Ma is getting my shirt. Pa is taller than Ma. My sister is getting my book. Ma is taller than my sister. My brother is getting my bag. My sister is taller than my brother. And my brother is taller than me. I’m the shortest in the family. Oh wait! There is our puppy, JoJo. Jojo is getting my slippers. Ha ha! JoJo is the shortest. Yes! JoJo is shorter than me. I’m shorter than my brother. My brother is shorter than my sister. My sister is shorter than Ma. Ma is shorter than Pa. Wow! Pa is the tallest, and JoJo is the shortest.
author: Celia  Bolam

title: The Bee and the Elephant
text: I am lost," said Little Bee. "I cannot find my home!" "Can you please help me, Mr. Elephant?" "Is this nest your home, Little Bee?" the elephant asked. "Oh no!" cried Little Bee. "This is a bird’s home." "Is this cave your home?" asked the elephant. "Oh no! This is a bat’s home." "Is this hive your home, Little Bee?" "Oh yes!" said Little Bee happily. "This is my home. " "Thank you for helping me, Mr. Elephant."
author: Celia  Bolam

title: Piggy Wants to Fly
text: I want to fly like the butterfly does." "Follow me!" said the butterfly. "But I do not have wings, I cannot fly." "I know, I’ll use palm leaves to make wings!" "Flap your wings hard to fly!" cried the butterfly. "I cannot seem to fly," said Piggy. "Let me try one more time." "Look! I can fly!" Piggy said leaping off the branch. "Oh no! Why did I fall? I do not have wings like you, so I will have to be okay with not flying."
author: Stephanie  Wei

title: The Bees
text: We poked the beehive! Run fast! Now we need to hide from the bees! Let's hide under this scarf. Oh no! The bees have found us. Where should we hide next? Let’s go into the stream. Oh no! The water will not help us. The bees have found us again. Where should we hide now? Wait! I know! Look at the smoke. We will go towards the fire. I remember something my grandmother told me. She said that bees are scared of smoke. I think she was right! I think the bees are going away. Goodbye bees! Go back home. We're sorry we poked your house. Yay! The bees found their way back to the beehive. Now everyone is safe!
author: Celia  Bolam

title: Little Monkey's Lost Bananas
text: He never puts his things in order, so his house is very messy. One morning, Little Monkey could be heard shouting from his tree house. “Where are they? They are gone! My bunch of bananas! Where have they gone?” Little Monkey asked the bee. “Bee! Bee! Did you eat my bananas?” “Buzz! Buzz! Buzz!" responded the bee. "I eat nectar and pollen. I don’t eat bananas.” Little Monkey asked the snake. “Snake! Snake! Did you eat my bananas?” “Hiss! Hiss! Hiss!" responded the snake. "I don’t know anything about your bananas. Don’t disturb me!” Little Monkey was hungry! “I have searched everywhere! Inside and outside... but my bananas are gone!" He kept searching, looking on the table and under the bed. “I still can’t find them! I can’t find my bananas!” Little Monkey became very angry. He stomped his feet, crying, "I'm so hungry! My bananas are gone, and I have nothing to eat!" Little Monkey looked sadly out from his balcony. "Ah! Wait..." he said. "Those are banana peels! 1...2…3…4… so many!” “Oh! There's the rabbit! So he’s the one who ate my bananas!” “Rabbit! You’re eating my bananas!” shouted Little Monkey. “No, Little Monkey. I’m not eating your bananas," responded the rabbit. "Look over there. I grow bananas!” The rabbit came over to the base of Little Monkey's tree. “You sound very hungry," Rabbit said. "Here - take a bunch of my bananas.” Little Monkey was happy. “Thank you! Thank you, Rabbit! But…” “Who… Who…Who took MY bananas?” Suddenly, Little Monkey remembered. “Oh… Now I recall! I was very hungry last night. I ate all the bananas!”
author: Rose Larsen

title: Cicada's Song
text: She wanted to learn a new song! So she decided to visit Kingfisher to learn to sing his song. “Doo-oo-oo! Doo-oo-oo!” sang Kingfisher. But Little Cicada could not sing his song. She then visited Mynah. Maybe she could learn to sing Mynah's song. “Keak! Kaek! Kaek!” sang Mynah. But Cicada could not sing Mynah's song. She then visited Cricket. Cicada was determined to learn a new song! “Krik krik krik! Krik krik krik!” sang Cricket. But Cicada could not sing Cricket's song, either. Then it started to rain. The ducks sang, “Quack! Quack! Quack!” Frog came out and croaked, “Ribbit! Ribbit! Ribbit!” All the animals came out. And they all sang their songs. “Doo-oo-oo! Doo-oo-oo!” “Keak! Kaek! Kaek!” “Krik krik krik! Krik krik krik!” “Quack! Quack! Quack!” “Ribbit! Ribbit! Ribbit!” Cicada listened to all the songs. None of the other songs sounded like hers. So she started to sing. “Yaeng! Yaeng! Yaeng!” All the animals sang together! “Doo-oo-oo! Doo-oo-oo!” “Keak! Kaek! Kaek!” “Krik krik krik! Krik krik krik!” “Quack! Quack! Quack!” “Ribbit! Ribbit! Ribbit!” “Yaeng! Yaeng! Yaeng!” Since then, Cicada has enjoyed her song. Sometimes she even makes up new songs, songs that only she can sing.
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Walking Mountain
text: Once upon a time, there was a camel. He was very large. All the other camels had only one hump, but he had two. The camel was very proud of this. He kept his distance from the other camels. One day, a sandstorm whirled around the desert. There was dust and sand everywhere! The camel was sleeping. He had no friends to wake him up so he slept through the storm. Sand gathered around him till only his two humps could be seen. Soon after, two desert tortoises came by. They began to climb up and down the humps, racing each other. All of a sudden, the camel woke up. He heaved himself up and rose from the ground. The tortoises were terrified. “Run!” they screamed. “It's a walking mountain!” The next day, the sun was very hot. The camel went to a nearby lake to cool off. He stepped into the water and waded deep inside the lake. Only his humps could be seen. Two frogs came by and climbed on top. They had a little picnic. As the sun began to set, the camel heaved himself up and rose from the lake. The frogs leapt off the camel in fright. “Run!” they screamed. “It's a walking mountain!” The camel was puzzled. “Why is everyone calling me a mountain?” He decided to search for a mountain to see what it was. He crossed forests. He waded through rivers. He walked over plains. It soon grew dark. Tired, the camel curled up on the ground and fell asleep. That night it snowed heavily. In the morning there was snow everywhere. Only the camel's humps could be seen. Two mice came by. They began chasing each other up and down the camel's humps. This tickled the camel, and he woke up. He heaved himself up and rose from the ground. The mice sprang away in fright. “Run!” they screamed. “It's a walking mountain!” At that moment, the camel happened to see a snow-capped mountain in front of him. “Oh my goodness!” he cried. “What an enormous camel!”
author: Gouri Srinidhi

title: Socks
text: Ma needs to use them. Ma uses the socks to make mops. Anu doesn't like that her socks are used as mops. Anu loves her socks because socks can change the colour of your feet! If you want red feet, wear red socks. If you want blue feet, wear blue socks. If you want colourful feet, wear colourful socks. There are so many colours to choose from! One day, Anu has an idea. She puts colourful socks on her cup, her bat and her ball. “Ma, look! ” Anu says. “I made three new, colourful friends!” The next day, Anu gets a surprise. One of her socks has turned into an elephant! And another sock has turned into a cat! Anu runs to show Ma the elephant and cat. “My socks are my friends,” Anu says. “You won't make my socks into mops now, will you?” Ma laughs and gives Anu a great, big hug.
author: Shannon David

title: The Dog's Eggs
text: Every day, she sat on the eggs for hours. She left only to feed herself. Many days passed like this. She was waiting for her baby pewits to hatch. One day, she was very hungry. She covered the eggs and went in search of food. But when she returned... What? A dog was lying on the warm eggs. The pewit waited and waited for the dog to leave. Morning turned to noon. Noon turned to evening. But the dog didn't move an inch! The warm eggs made a nice place to rest. Suddenly, one by one, four baby pewits hatched. The dog woke up, too. He started to walk away. The baby pewits started crying. “Mama! Mama!” they called to the dog. “Mama! Mama!” The dog was confused. “Mama! Mama! Mama!” But he was not their mother! He had only been taking a cosy nap. He needed to get away! The dog ran off as fast as he could. The baby pewits soon got tired. Mother Pewit said, “Those eggs were mine! You are my children.” Hooray! The babies ran to their mother. “Mama! Mama! Mama!” “M y babies! I love you,” Mama said.
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Bubble Mystery
text: She was going to the pond for the first time. Bath time! At first, Toot-Toot was scared of the water. But when she saw all the other goats splashing around, she jumped in! Everyone laughed. Everyone splashed. Everyone played and played! Toot-Toot soon found bubbles all around her. They were going blop blop blop! She was a little afraid. But she soon got over it. Toot-Toot began to jump, dance and twirl through the bubbles. After that fun day, Toot-Toot began to wonder, ”How are bubbles made?” She asked her Baba. Baba said he didn't know. Toot-Toot asked her Ma. Ma said she didn't know, either. So Toot-Toot decided to solve the bubble mystery all by herself. She flapped her tail in the water... She blew into the water with all her might... But she didn't make a bubble! One day, Toot-Toot's tummy was hurting. She wondered what to do. She decided to bathe in the pond's cool water. There was a deep rumbling in her tummy. Suddenly, gas escaped from Toot-Toot! Pssshhhhhtttt! As the gas shot through the water, bubbles popped up to the water’s surface. Blop blop blop! Finally, Toot-Toot had solved the bubble mystery! Now, whenever it's bath day, Toot-Toot makes the most magnificent bubbles of all. After her first bath day, Toot-Toot's sister asked her how bubbles were made. And what did Toot-Toot say? Why, she told her sister she didn't know!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Frog's Bright Idea
text: One day Frog was very hungry. So he went to search for food. Behind the leaves, he saw a lot of insects flying around. “Today, I’ll eat until I’m full!” he thought. Frog jumped here. Frog jumped there. Frog jumped up. Frog jumped down. But he couldn't catch anything! After all that jumping he was starving! “They’re all so fast!” he panted. “I can’t catch a single one.” “If this goes on, I will die of hunger!” Suddenly he saw a light shining far away. He went towards it. “Wow!” said frog. There was a candle with bugs and moths flying all around. Frog ate and ate until he couldn’t eat anymore. The next evening Frog came down to the pond with a candle of his own. He put it right at the edge of the pond and lit it. Soon, his candle was surrounded by insects and frog ate and ate. Frog ate until he couldn't eat anymore! A few days later the pond looked very different. Now every night the frogs feast in the light of the candles.
author: Magdalena  Cooper

title: What Am I?
text: I am? I clean your face. I wash your hands and your body. I clean your clothes. When you are tired and hot, you need me. I will help you when you are thirsty. After playing in the sun, you need me. Sometimes I make you feel cold. I can make things float. I can make you swim. I help flowers and plants grow. Sometimes you play with me. You always need me around. Without me, the land will be dry. Without me, the flowers and the plants will fall. What am I? I am water!
author: Erica Cuellar

title: A Little Monkey and a Fish
text: One morning, a little baby monkey was playing in a tree while his mother picked fruit. The little baby monkey was picking leaves. He was happy. He picked all the leaves off one branch, so he jumped to another branch. Crrraaaackkk! The branch broke! As the little monkey fell, a big fish jumped out of the water. But a strong hand reached out just in time and saved the little monkey. The next morning the little monkey went back to picking leaves. The little monkey threw some more leaves into the water. Then, all of a sudden... Aha! Smart little monkey! He learned how to keep himself safe in the tree.
author: Shannon David

title: Drivers in a Hurry
text: I am in a hurry. Get out of the way! Get out of the way!” Bugudam Bugudam! A bus starts its journey. “I am in a hurry. Get out of the way! Get out of the way!” Bugudam Bugudam! A train is also in a hurry. Pappak Pappak! Get out of the way! Get out of the way! Pappak Pappak! Watch out! Watch out! CRASH! The drivers start to cry. They realize that they had forgotten something important. We need to install traffic lights. Let’s do it together. Our traffic lights are ready! When we see the red light, we must stop. When we see the yellow light, we must slow down. When we see the green light, then we can go on. We must obey the traffic laws.
author: Alisha Berger
illustrator: Keo  Phunphalla; Sao Sreymao; So  Chakrya; Soeurm  Kakada; Youm Kosal

title: A Day at the Carnival
text: They plan to ride every ride! “But don't lose me! ” Tiny Mouse tells his brothers. They race each other on toy cars. They go up and down on the merry-go-round. They ride the winding caterpillar coaster. They take a spin on the Ferris wheel. The brothers walk to the balloon cart......and they each buy a balloon. One balloon, two balloons... “ Wait, where is Tiny Mouse? ” Little Mouse and Littler Mouse run to the toy cars. Tiny Mouse isn't there. They run to the merry-go-round. Tiny Mouse isn't there. They run to the caterpillar coaster. Tiny Mouse isn't there, either. They run to the Ferris wheel. Thank goodness! There is Tiny Mouse! The Little Mice each buy a glass of sugarcane juice. One glass, two glasses, three glasses! What a fantastic day at the carnival. Hooray, Hooray, Hooray!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Tin Trong, the Little Bus
text: There is a little bus called Tin Trong. He drives a long way every day! Tin Trong drives uphill and downhill. He drives in sun and rain, dust and mud. One day, Tin Trong is exhausted. He reaches his parking space late. Tin Trong coughs. Khoo, Khoo, Khong, Khong! He is too sick to drive tomorrow. The next day, Tin Trong calls in sick. He knows how to feel better. He needs a rest and a good tune up! Ngeet Ngeet! Cheet, Cheet! Bang Bang! Bang Bang! Ngeet Ngeet! Cheet, Cheet! Bang Bang! Bang Bang! Now, Tin Trong feels better. Actually, he feels great! Tin Trong asks for one more thing. He asks for a bath. Then he takes a nap. He has to wake up early tomorrow! The next day, Tin Trong is strong again. He travels straight ahead. He travels back and forth, left and right. Tin Tin… Tet Tet… Tin Tin… Tin Trong takes the bus riders home one by one. They are happy. "We missed you yesterday," they say. "But everyone needs a rest sometimes!"
author: Alisha Berger

title: Drawing My Cat
text: Lida loves to draw pictures, so she decides to draw all the vegetables her father brought. First, she starts with the limes and the tomatoes. After that, she draws the cucumbers and the string beans. Last, she draws the squash. Meow-Meow the cat walks by while Lida is drawing. “Ah, I want to draw Meow-Meow too!" says Lida. "Where should I start?” “Oh, I know!" Snip, snip, snip.... Lida takes out her glue, and starts pasting things together. “This is my picture of Meow-meow the cat!” says Lida happily.
author: Gouri Srinidhi

title: Preeny Refuses to Share
text: Preeny, the Peacock also joined the nearby school. He was happy with his teachers and his friends. He especially enjoyed the Environmental Studies class. His teacher made it very interesting. One day, Miss Dolly, his teacher decided to take them to the nearby park for their lesson. The lesson was ‘Naming the Trees’. She also declared that they could bring their lunch boxes. The class was going to have a picnic lunch! In the park! All the students were excited. The lesson was fun too. They counted the trees, identified some and even hugged the trees. In fact, Bulbul and Koel even talked to the trees! When it was time to eat their lunch, Miss Dolly asked all to sit in a circle and share their food. She gave each one of the students a lollipop to suck after eating their lunch. All the students opened their boxes and shared with their friends. Preeny however sat a little far away, and silently ate his food. He neither offered his food nor took theirs. The other students nudged each other and whispered. Finally some of the students went and reported the whole thing to Miss Dolly. Miss Dolly was surprised. Preeny was quiet and a little withdrawn, but he was friendly and co-operative. And he obeyed Miss Dolly whenever she gave any instructions. What was the matter today? Miss Dolly waited for all the students to walk back to school. She quietly walked back with Preeny. She asked him, ‘Why didn’t you share your food Preeny? Are you upset or angry? ’ Preeny quietly whispered, ‘Miss, I had brought yesterday’s leftovers for lunch. My mother is ill so she could not make fresh food. How can I give my friends stale food?’ Miss Dolly hugged Preeny and praised him for his thoughtfulness. She made a mental note to talk to the class too! Preeny’s face lit up with a slow smile.
author: usha aswath iyer
illustrator: Abhishek Choudhury; Ajit Narayan; Herminder Ohri; Kavita Singh Kale; Ketan Raut; Lavanya  Naidu; Padmanabh; Partho Sengupta; usha aswath iyer

title: Jerome Wants Bananas
text: Jerome was a very hungry monkey.One day he heard a noise,but it was only Jerome's tummy!Now,he made up his mind to find a bunch of bananas. But,he didn't live anywhere near a banana plantation! So,he walked and walked until he saw a lake,then he swam and swam but poor Jerome still couldn't see any bananas! So,he walked for hours until his legs ached,then suddenly out of the corner of his eye he spotted a bunch of bananas!His joy knew no bounds, he climbed the tree and took the bananas. And there he is,enjoying his bananas.Well,I'll say he deserves it.What about you?
author: Shruthi Sridharan

title: Save planet earth from pollution demon !!
text: Few years ago, all the planets Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were living happily, revolving around the Sun. The happiest of all was the mother planet Earth, it was the only known planet were LIFE was possible because -It was neither too H OT nor too COLD like other planets, -It has water for life to exist, and -It is protected by blanket of atmosphere. Sometime later as population on earth increases, people started cutting trees to build houses.The air gets polluted because of vehicles and factories smoke. People started wasting water. Use of plastic increases and living on earth became miserable. Days went by, more and more trees were cut on earth. One day it gave birth to a demon named "Pradushana". The demon was very powerful and deadly, it started troubling all living beings on earth. P eople on earth started suffering from diseases like Asthma, typhoid, malaria, dengue, deafness etc. Diseases caused by "Pradushana", lead to the deaths of many living beings on earth. The mother earth was in real DANGER! One day all the kids on earth gathered and prayed to the mother earth. "Help us mother!", they all said. Tell us some way, to fight this deadly demon who is killing many people. After listening prayer of children Mother Earth broke into tears and said, "When your own life is in danger, then you realized my value and came to seek my help". This demon is very powerful and you have made it so, by feeding him with your greed! But I am your mother and will tell you some solution for sure... "Here are some of the ways to kill the demon, if you follow them regularly you may win over! ",Mother said. 1. Walk or ride your bicycle whenever possible for short trips, save fuel. 2. Carpool to school or work. 3. Choose organically grown fruits and vegetables. 4. Grow your own fruits and vegetables. 5. Turn off lights and electronics when you are not in the room. 6.Reducing, Reusing, and Recycling, remember 3R's. 7. Use fewer and environmentally friendly chemicals. 8. Don't use pesticides and herbicides. 9. Don't flush medication. 10. Dispose of toxic waste properly. 11. Conserve water, every drop counts! 12. Always bring a cloth or jute bag when you shop. 13. Plant more trees. They clean the air, provide oxygen, and beautify your surroundings. 14. Avoid plastic. 15. Don't burn crackers. The kids were delighted to hear the solution. They all thanked mother earth and started following the instructions given by mother earth from that day on wards. They promised to keep the earth clean and green always. They have -planted many trees, -stopped wasting water, -started using reusable things, -started pooling and -started keeping their home and surrounding clean and green. -started using jute bags for shopping. The kids also started educating others around them,about how to make planet earth happy again. With time more and more people realized the fact and they also joined, "the Go Green and Clean" revolution with the kids. The demon was getting weak day by day.The efforts made by the kids and others, to keep the environment clean and pollution free has kicked that demon far away. Now, the people on earth are more healthy and happy once again.
author: Chaitanya Verma

title: Sally Saves the Day
text: One day,Sally was really,really bored,so she tried pretending she was a superhero.Seeing this,her dad asked if she wanted to have a dive.As her dad was an inventor,he had created a magnificent submarine.Sally nodded, she loves a dive.She brought her two best friends along,Cat and Fish. They were all having a great time,Sally asked her dad if she could go for a swim,he said "yes".All was great until some thing terrible happened, Fish got caught in a clamshell! Without panicking Sally went back to the submarine and got a stick,she swam back to the clamshell and tried to open the shell with all her might,at last it opened!Fish was free!"YAAY' shouted Sally.Fish thanked Sally.Then they all went back to the surface in her dad's submarine. Back home,Sally was enjoying cake and was given a present to honor her bravery.All this was planned by her dad.Well,Sally's day ended up great didn't it?
