title: Meet My Family
text: Hey, I'm Neha. I have an interesting family. Do you want to meet them? These are my parents. Both my mother and my father work in the post office. This is my older brother, Raj and my older sister, Rohini. We play games together, especially during the holidays! These are my paternal and maternal grandparents. I like it when they come to visit me. These are my father's brothers. They are my uncles. My father is the oldest of them all! These are my father's sisters. They are my aunts, Shanta and Susheela. The girl in the pink clothes is my cousin Latha. She is Susheela aunty's daughter. Oh, and I almost forgot. This is my dog, Neelu. She's almost two years old and everybody loves her! So, this is my family. Now you can tell me about yours!
author: Gopika Kumaran

title: The Night the Moon Went Missing
text: Late one night, when her Amma and Achan are fast asleep, Maisha grabs her goggles and sneaks out of the house. Maisha loves the beach at night. And one of her best friends lives in the sea. Maisha goes to their usual meeting place on the beach and calls out. “Uchli! Are you here?” She can sit here for hours, watching Uchli fly in and out of the water. Uchli is a flying fish who loves to show off his tricks. But today, Uchli looks worried. “What’s the matter?” Maisha asks. “Why do you look so upset?” “Can’t you see?” he says. “The moon is missing!” The moon! Uchli is right—their friend is not in the sky tonight. In fact, there’s a big hole where the moon should be. “But we saw her just last night,” Maisha exclaims. “She rose from the sea right here in front of us... Do you think she’s lost underwater?” “We have to find her!” Uchli says. “But how will we see anything without the moonlight?” Maisha asks. Just then, Uchli notices something in the water. Every time a wave breaks in the distance, little sparks of light glow and fade and glow again. “Maisha!” he shouts, excited. “I have an idea! Get on my back, let’s go to those waves over there.” When they r each the lights, Maisha takes a deep breath, holds Uchli tightly and... Maisha gasps. She feels like she’s floating in a sky full of stars! There are tiny creatures glowing all around her. “Wow, who are they?” she whispers to Uchli. “They’re plankton. Maybe they can help light our way in the sea!” Uchli says. “Will you share your light with us?” Maisha asks one of them. “The moon is missing, and we need some light to find her.” “You will need more than just my light,” the plankter says. “Let me ask my friends if they can help too!” Soon, Maisha and Uchli are joined by an army of little creatures, with their flickering lights. “Now where can the moon be?” Maisha wonders. “I can help you,” a deep, booming voice says, near Maisha's ear. She spins around. The eight arms of a firefly squid glimmer back at her. His body is covered in neon-blue lights. “I saw the moon go this way just a little while ago.” At first, Maisha is scared of the long tentacles. But she knows the firefly squid’s light can help them see better underwater. “Lead the way,” she says. The squid wraps a tentacle around Maisha's finger. “Hold on tight!” Then Maisha, Uchli, the glowing plankton and the firefly squid all swim down together. Down, down, down they go where to the water is very dark. But the plankton glow brighter, and the squid flashes his light. There is still no moon in sight. Then they meet an anglerfish, out on a hunt. She has sharp teeth, but Maisha is not scared any more. “Hello,” she says. “We’re looking for the moon. Have you seen her around?” “Yes,” says the anglerfish. “I saw her swimming with some moonfish a few hours ago. Follow me!” Maisha, Uchli, the squid and the plankton follow the green lure of the anglerfish. The light from the glowing animals falls like a spotlight on the dark ocean floor. Suddenly, Maisha sees something bright under a rock. It’s the moon! “Help,” squeaks the moon. “I’m stuck!” The squid lifts the rock with his tentacles. “Hurrah!” everyone shouts, as the pale moon slips out. “What happened?” Uchli asks. “I came here to meet my cousins, the moonfish,” says the moon. “I got lost on my way back when my light began to fade. And then I got stuck under this rock. Thank you for coming to find me.” “So this is where you are when you’re not in the sky!” Maisha says. The moon smiles and begins to float up towards the surface. Finally, she jumps into the sky. Uchli and Maisha wave goodbye to their new friends and swim back to the beach in the moonlight. The stars under the sea continue to shine deep into the night. MEET THE LIGHT-MAKERS Did you know that many animals, both above and under water, are able to make their own light? The tiny plankton that Maisha and Uchli meet glow to scare away the animals that might eat them. When they sense movement in the water, the plankton let out bright sparks as a warning. Sometimes, waves and boat traffic also trigger this light. While plankton animals have a chemical in them that helps them glow, the firefly squid has special organs called photophores that produce its light. Thousands of these light-producing photophores on the squid’s body flash to attract food, impress a mate or confuse predators. The lures of anglerfish get their light from the glowing bacteria that live inside them. Many plants and animals glow above the water too. Fireflies, some mushrooms, and even you emit a tiny amount of light every day!
author: Shreya Yadav

title: Save River Save Water
text: INTRODUCTION Someone has truthfully said that a child’s love for books never dies. Children are the future of the country. Parents always bring up their children with the abilities and education so that they can look after their family and serve their country at their best. Representing this here is a story based on children’s idea and satisfaction for conservation of water a major problem in today’s life. It’ll be my honor if readers will read my book and also do something for the problem of water pollution. I hope that you will enjoy my story and it will make you aware and alert. So, readers have fun!!!!! Ahaa!! That’s a goal, my team will surely win. What do you think readers?? Is that right?? Oh!! Sorry, I have not told anything about myself. I am Gopal and I live with my parents in Delhi. So, basically I was playing with my friends in a big park which was full of grasses and flowers. And it was a goal for my team. After an hour or two of play, we found that our water bottles were empty. So one of my friends, Jerry, said that we should fill our bottles from river Yamuna which was flowing nearby. Everyone agreed. So we all went to river Yamuna. When we reached, we found that the water was full of floating plastic bottles, sewage and foam. It was in pathetic condition. We didn’t have any other option than going back home to fetch water. When I reached home, I asked my mother about the river and its condition. She told me about the sewage system and industrial waste disposal system of the city. She explained me that there is a network of pipelines below the ground. It carries all the waste from every house and finally drains it in the river. Also, many industries in the city also dispose of their liquid and solid waste into the river. More curiously I asked that how this is connected with the tragic condition of river banks??? She further told me that the river water carries the waste and leaves it on the banks. She explained that uncivilized habits of people are also responsible for all this. They throw lots of plastic and hazardous material in the river. I asked her that why don’t they clean it?? She said that if they would have that much sense why they would even throw the garbage. I again asked that who will clean it? She smiled and said that you all should think and do something, collectively, to clean it. From that day only, I decided to clean the river Yamuna and its banks. Next day, I called my friends and told them about all this. They also showed determination to clean the river and were ready to support me. Now, we all needed various things required to clean the river. But none of us had any material needed. So we all went to a waste picker and asked for the materials. He managed to bring the materials required for all of us for cleaning the river banks. We paid him for that from our pocket money. We all reached the river and start picking up the various plastic wastes like bottles, bags, packets and other garbage etc. On seeing our hard work some people also joined us. Then we continued the process till one week. After that the banks were very much cleaner. To prevent people from throwing the garbage again we made them aware and understand that how the river is important for the human life. My mother had said one day " child is the father of the man ". That time I couldn’t understand its meaning. But now, I have understood that how the child is the father of man. By seeing the improvement in the cleanliness of the river and the banks, we went back home not because we were thirsty again, but because we have proven that the children can bring any change in the society whether it is the water issue or anything else.
author: atharvsantosh gupta
illustrator: Ameyy & Jhari C; Harshvardhan Gantha; Jean de Wet; Monappa; Onesmus   Kakungi; Rajesh Khar; Tapas Guha

title: Dad! You are the Best!
text: I love that you are always there for me and mum! I love it when you carry me on your shoulders, so I can look at the world better! I love the time we spend in the kitchen and the yummy food you cook for me! I love it when you convince me to drink water! I love it when you gently admonish me while making commotion! I love to push your laptop away and make you play with me! I love to imitate your exercise sessions! I love your struggle trying to comb my hair! I love our cycling timing together! I love our play time at the park! I love our visits to the zoo! I love your storytelling at bedtime! I love that you are always there watching me grow up! One day I will grow up, aspiring to lead an independent life like you! But I will always be your sweet little bundle of joy!

text: Hello, my name is Shreyashri I stay in ANUBHAV learning centre for almost 9 hours each day. title: Jolly, Jumpy, Round and Red
text: Four little lousy lice Jolly, Jumpy, Round and Red, Dancing and frolicking on my distressed head, "Catch us if you can!" they willfully said, As they had a satisfying fill of my blood, With every wickedly greedy gulp, Growing more bold, nasty and plump, Causing a scalp itchy, twitchy, scratchy and sore... The icky, yucky, beastly four! Several sweeps of my comb I did dare, Through marked sections of my frizzy hair, In a frenzy they fled to the untouched end, Unaware of what I truly did intend, Still feasting on me without a thought or care! Making my anger quickly flare, With a scalp itchy, twitchy, scratchy and sore The icky, yucky, beastly four... More calculated and frantic brushing... To keep up with my adrenaline rushing, I forced them to go scurrying! My focused attack surely had them worrying. They rushed to huddle in a corner panting, Yet they continued to feed as if taunting, Making my scalp itchy, twitchy, scratchy even more! The icky, yucky, beastly four... Even as the itching got intense, I searched for them with a mirror and magnifying lens, And I had stumbled on their hideout...I could sense, My fingers clutched the comb rather tense... For a swift and strong slide down my long mane. Finally got them all simple and plain! Soothing my scalp itchy, twitchy, scratchy and so sore The icky, yucky, beastly four... Then a firm and fatal click of my nails, It is a neat trick that never fails... The irksome quartet of many a quirky tales, Now lie flattened and still on the shiny floor, They can cause mischief and trouble, no more! Or a scalp itchy, twitchy, scratchy and sore, Bringing a fitting end to this lousy lore, Of Jolly, Jumpy, Round and Red, the icky, yucky, beastly four...

title: Helping Friend

Sonu "T for tree", "C" for Clouds... Monu claps..clap...clap...clap Trees are Green!!! Grass is green too..!!!!!! "B" for Bridge.... "R" for River....... Monu and Sonu are hungry. title: Molly & Meena
text: Molly is always bored. ‘It’s too hot and sunny’, she says. Meena is chasing butterflies outside. Suddenly it starts to rain. ‘It’s too dark and cold’, cribs Molly. Meena is now dancing with peacocks. The sun comes back again. ‘I’m bored’, says Molly. Outside, the peacocks and butterflies lift Meena and put her on a rainbow.

title: The Two Drops Of Water
text: Once upon a time there were two drops of water. They were really very happy because they had came to know that they were landing on the earth. They were very excited because they have to see how earth looks from land. Then they were finally landed on the land from the clouds. They were very excited, happy, thrilled, delighted seeing the beautiful nature around them. After few hours they went to the home of very naughty girl who never respects water. This is Ria. She was the naughty girl, never respects water. Those two drops had came to her home. But till now never used in anything. In Ria there was one bad thing but there was a good thing too. She loves to read book and if something is written in the book then she do the same. Once she was reading a book on water. There she found about scarcity of water. She found how we have to respect water, how we have to be friendly with water, how we have to conserve water. And then she got a nice idea. She thought about the water cycle. She thought that how about to take the water in the container and keep it in the sun. The sun would absorb the water and the water can go back to the sky, to there friends. Then she take the the water in a container and kept it in the sun. Unfortunately the two drops come in the container. They were really very sad that they do not had any respect on earth and wanted to go back in the sky. After sometime the water was absorbed. The two drops gone back to there home and lived happily. Here Ria start respecting water and became a loved one to everyone.
author: manu chandra
