text: two boys fought in the school playground they were ready to fight. they were mad at each other because they bumped into each other 3 minutes ago, ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ the tall kid got the small kid and threw him in the air and the tall kid stopped fighting. and they forgave each other and they became the best friend in the whole entire universe.
author: 양현서

title: Velu and the Vegetable Vendor
text: Velu is a naughty and curious ten year old. He is quite famous in his neighbourhood. “No one can beat him in kitti ” his best friend Rajesh would boast. “That brat broke my scooter’s rear view mirror with his sixer” Natarajan uncle would complain. “He always helps his friends study” Rekha madam would appreciate. “Onions, potatoes and ripe tomatoes,! Carrot, beans and spinach too! Fresh from the farm!! ” It was Velu's favourite time of the day. “Fresh vegetables for a reasonable price!” the vegetable vendor announced to the whole street manoeuvring his pushcart. Velu was amused by the rhythm and rhyme of the vendor’s call. He used to mimic it at school “Fresh from the farm!” It was Velu's daily routine to watch the vendor pass by. Amma would bargain and complain about the price of the vegetables. “Oh madam! What can a poor man like me do? Everything is so expensive these days” the vendor would reply smiling. “I wonder if this guy is selling gold or vegetables!” amma would mumble as appa would sit unaffected with his face buried in the day’s newspaper. It was summer vacation and street cricket had begun early in the morning. “Oye Velu! What are you staring at?” the vendor called Velu wanted to run away. But he mustered the courage and asked “Can I walk with you for some distance?” “Oh sure!” said the vendor busily counting the coins an old lady had given him for the potatoes. Velu signalled to Rajesh that he was going for a walk. Munching on a crunchy cucumber, Velu asked “Where is your farm? I’m sure it must be acres and acres” “Oh son! We poor folks don’t own farms. I just sell these vegetables for my master and get paid for my labour” Velu went on and on. “How big was the largest pumpkin you have ever sold?” “I hate carrots. Do you really think they will help my eye sight?” “What will you do with the left over vegetables at the end of the day?” Velu stopped to stare at a wall poster about the circus coming to town. When he turned around, the vendor was long gone. He realised he was very far from his home and began to tremble in fear. As tears were brimming in his eyes, he heard amma calling “Velu! Velu!” “Where did you vanish? Appa and I were looking for you everywhere.” Amma was sweating all over and panting. She had been running frantically through the streets looking for him. Appa was reprimanding the vendor ”He is just a little boy. Why did you take him with you?” Velu went to the rescue of the hapless vendor shivering at Appa’s rage. “ Appa it is my mistake. I am responsible. I wandered away without your knowledge.” Appa and amma hugged Velu tightly. “I promise to be more responsible in future” said Velu, happy to be in their arms again.
author: Jeyashree Kathiresan

title: Mission of the Fish
text: Puti are playing in the river. All of a sudden, Tengra bumps his head on something hard. "Ouch! What is that?” Tengra says angrily. It is a coconut shell. “Have rivers become dumping grounds for trash?" Puti asks. The river used to be so beautiful! Tengra thinks. He swims around and notices more garbage. The water is dirty and full of people's trash. Tengra becomes more and more angry. Tengra gathers his friends Puti, Rui, Katla, Chingri and Koi and asks for their help. How can they make the place where they live cleaner? The fish decide to speak directly with the humans. The next day, Tengra and his friends visit the river bank and spot a boy throwing trash into the water. They tell him gently, “You are polluting our home. Why are you throwing your garbage into the river?" The boy is surprised. “I’m so sorry,” he says in a small voice. “I never thought about what I was doing.” The boy begins spreading the message of the fish to all his friends. Everyone listens. All the fish dance with joy. The next day, Tengra and his friends swim excitedly to school. They know that their home will become beautiful again.
author: Celia  Bolam

title: What is your name?
text: Hello! This little boy's name is KIYAN. But he has many other names. Mama calls him LADDOO. She says he is super sweet. Daddy calls him VEDOO. Daddy says he is funny. Dadi calls him MEAOW MANI. She says his skin is soft like a cat's. Dadu calls him BUNNY. He says he can only see two teeth. Ira didi calls him GUNDRU. She says Kiyan is a little rascal. Sahil bhaiya calls him CINDRU... don't know why! But he says Kiyan throws tantrums! But when Kiyan plays a prank and hides somewhere, they are ALL angry with him. And shout... KIYAAAAAAAAAN! WHAT ARE YOUR PET NAMES?
author: Neha Taksale

title: What did Priya eat?
text: Priya was a beautiful, sleek, shiny, brown cow. All the children loved her. She gave a lot of milk. The children drank milk every day. One morning, Priya did not get up. “Wake up, Priya! We want milk!” called the children. “I can’t,” moaned Priya. “My tummy hurts so much.” “Poor Priya! Don’t be sad. We will call the vet,” they said. The vet gave Priya a check-up. She had come with her portable X-ray machine. She took an X-Ray of Priya’s stomach. She looked at the X-Ray and shook her head. “Priya, you have eaten too much plastic!” she said. “I will give you an injection for the pain. You must rest for a day and then you will feel better.” The vet left and the children sat around Priya. “PLASTIC! Why do you eat plastic? Cows eat green grass!” they said. “Green grass? There is no green grass anywhere, except in the park. But outside the park there is a sign that says NO COWS ALLOWED,” said Priya. “We get our food from the garbage dump. Do you know what is in the garbage dump? Sweet wrappers, wafer packets, biscuit wrappers and plastic bags! The dump is also full of tasty vegetable skins and fruit peels. So our food is mixed up with the plastic waste and other waste,” said Priya. “We do not have fingers like you do. We cannot separate the plastic from the food, so we just eat the plastic along with the vegetable peels and other yummy treats like carrot-tops and corn cobs. That’s how we get plastic into our stomachs.” The children were upset. “We must do something,” said Ravi, the oldest. “What can we do?” asked Tina. Situ knew a lot – she liked to watch nature shows on television. “In some cities, people put their garbage into different-coloured bins. They put food waste into a green bin, plastic in a red bin and other rubbish in a blue bin.” Nitesh loved action. “Let’s tell everyone in our area to do the same. Then Priya and her friends will not have to eat plastic,” he said. “Wonderful idea!” all the children chorused. “Let’s start today.” Soon the children were teaching all the grown-ups how to separate the waste. They asked every family to have three different bins in each house. They made posters to help everyone remember how to separate their garbage: paper waste to be put into the blue bin, plastic waste into the red bin, and food waste into the green bin. * FOOD *PLASTIC *PAPER Now the garbage dump is neat and clean, and Priya will not get sick again. Everyone is happy. And most of all - our wonderful planet Earth. The Three R's Look, here is a doctor throwing a plastic bag into the green bin. Correct her please. Here is teacher - he is throwing his paper waste in the green bin. Which bin should paper be thrown into? To help Priya, make sure you follow the three R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.
author: Anna D

title: Bravo Burli!
text: An old woman sat in the veranda of her thatched hut with her granddaughter by her side. “Please tell me a story,” pleaded the little girl tugging at the old woman’s arms. “A story?” exclaimed the lady. “Hmmm… let me see. Would you like to hear the story of a brave little girl?” The little girl nodded enthusiastically. “Then listen,” said the grandmother. “Deep inside a jungle..." Deep inside a jungle was a small village. Deep inside the village was a cluster of low huts. Inside the hut lived a family of Kondh tribals who knew the jungle like the back of their hands. Each zigzag path, each large sal and mohua tree, each pug mark of the mongoose and the tiger, oh yes! They knew it all and much, much more! Burlimundi was a little tribal girl who woke up early every morning. She took her bath in the stream close to her hut and helped her mother cook mandya jau, a porridge made of ragi and rice. Yummy! Burlimundi would lick her bowl clean and then help her mother wash the dishes in the stream. The doors would then be bolted and all the women would gather and climb￹up a hill near the jungle to collect firewood, roots and fruits for their supper. The path was steep and long but Burlimundi was a strong girl, agile as a monkey and swift as a hare. Meanwhile, a few young men of the village along with Burlimundi’s father and two elder brothers would go into the jungle to hunt. The others would make their way to the fields to plough. 'When will I have my nose and ears pierced like yours and apply black paint on my face?' Burlimundi asked her mother one day, staring at her tattoos and her ornaments made of beads. 'Oh, Burli,' sighed her mother, 'it’s a long way off. You’ll wear ornaments when you are much older, not before that! And I will not let you pierce your face with needles to make black lines on your cheeks!' Burlimundi sulked. Growing up seemed very far away but now it was time to play. Little Burli looked around. It was summer. The streams were drying up but the mango trees were heavy with fruits – green, yellowish-orange and red. The little girl climbed up a tree and quickly hid herself in the foliage. 'Aya, guess where I am?' she cried out to her mother. Premsila Majhi, Burlimundi’s mother pretended to look for her daughter and shouted, 'Oh no! I cannot find my daughter. Maybe a tree spirit has carried her away. I’ll have to call Jani, the medicine man to get her back!' Spirits who whisked children away and spread misfortune were feared by all adivasis. 'Here I am, Aya!' cried Burlimundi nervously and she quickly jumped down from the tree with a mango in her hand. The women laughed. 'Oh Burli, go pluck some more mangoes, we were just trying to scare you,' said Premsila. Burli was angry. She ran deeper into the forest and decided to stay far away from her mother. 'Aya always scares me with stories of spirits,' she muttered to herself with a frown. The jungle was dark and dense. The chirping of birds and the screech of monkeys echoed all around. Burli walked bravely alone. This is where my Abba comes everyday to hunt, she thought, But why does he tell me that a jungle is not a playground for little girls? Suddenly the jungle resounded with eerie sounds. Birds nervously twittered when a fearful breeze blew through the mohua leaves. Squirrels squeaked in fright and monkeys chattered and hid themselves in the hollows of trees. 'What’s the matter?' asked Burli turning around in bewilderment. A rumble sounded and the little girl looked up at the sky thinking it to be thunder. But it was not! What can it be? thought the girl and then she heard a growl. There was no mistaking it this time. It was loud and clear like the grunt of the devil and even the sal trees trembled. Burlimundi froze, her legs became numb for she realized that it was none other than a tiger on the prowl! 'What am I going to do?' whispered Burli. She was all alone and felt very scared. The bushes rustled and suddenly without any noise, a black-and-yellow striped coat glistened behind the trees, and then a large beast with flaming eyes and pointed teeth snarled and appeared before Burlimundi. His whiskers twitched and he gnashed his teeth noisily as if he were sharpening knives on a stone. Burlimundi was about to scream when her Abba’s voice seemed to echo through the jungle. 'When you see a tiger do not run, Burli. Tigers sense fear and they pounce on you. If you have fire, wave it around. Tigers hate flames.' Burlimundi did not move. She was a brave little girl and stood rooted to the soil like a little sal tree. She suddenly remembered she had slipped in a matchbox into her pocket while her mother cooked this morning. Why had she done that? She was not sure. But now she knew. It was destiny. The matchbox would save her life! The tiger stared at her and their eyes met, flaming yellow with jet black. Burli did not budge. She was a brave girl and her mother’s favourite child. Quick as lightning, she dug in her palms into her pockets, took out the matchbox and with one swift strike lit a matchstick. The tiger’s gaze wavered for a moment and that was enough for Burli to pick up a dry branch and light it. The fire caught on instantaneously like yellow flaming tongues of a monster and the tiger leapt back in fear. He glanced at the little girl holding the flame. Should I eat her up? he seemed to think, and then realised he was not hungry. Maybe he had devoured a monkey just a while back and his stomach felt queasy? Why risk my life and eat a skinny girl? he thought and then with one swipe of his tail and a grunt, he nervously turned around and walked away. That was close! Burli heaved a sigh and ran as fast as she could to where her mother was. 'Oh Aya, I just met a tiger and he did not eat me up!' panted the little girl. The women looked at one another and burst out laughing. 'You are such a sweet little girl, Burli. Why would a tiger not eat you up?' one of them jokingly remarked. Burli scratched her head. 'I don’t know…' she murmured, 'maybe because I knew how to light a fire?' 'Light a fire?' chorused the woman. 'That’s not possible!' 'But I did!' protested Burlimundi with tears blinding her eyes and thankfully her mother stepped in. 'Hush. Don’t you dare make fun of my daughter. She is a brave girl who can certainly scare a tiger away. I am so proud of her!' said Premsila and she hugged her Burli warmly. Burlimundi clasped her mother’s hand and smiled. Ooh! It was a radiant smile that lit up the dark summer night." “Where is Burlimundi now?” asked the little girl after hearing her grandmother’s story. The old woman smiled and then chuckled, “Burlimundi is no other than your grandmother, my child, and she’s sitting right in front of you!” The little girl’s eyes lit up. “You are surely the bravest grandmother in the whole wide world and I want to be as strong as you!” said the little girl proudly, and putting her head gently on the old lady’s lap, she gradually drifted into sleep.
author: Nabanita Deshmukh

title: Look Again!
text: It was evening. The birds were chirping and flying back to their nests. Putti and Akka were walking back from the park. "Look, Akka! There's a butterfly on the bush!" said Putti. "A butterfly? Look again! " said Akka. "Huh?" said Putti. They passed by Parvati's house. "Akka, look, Parvati's dog is wearing ponytails today!" said Putti. Akka giggled. "You funny girl! Look again! " she said. "Huh?" said Putti. They walked past the big old Gulmohar tree. "Akka! A snake!" screamed Putti and clung to Akka. "Oh Putti, look again! " said Akka. "Haaaa!" said Putti, and relaxed. They passed by Raghav's house. "Akka, how did Raghav's mother's hair grow long so quickly? I saw her yesterday and she had short hair!" said Putti. Akka laughed. "Putti, Putti, look again! " "Aha!" said Putti. They went past the old library. "Ooooh Akka!" said Putti. "Have you ever seen such a big fruit on such a small plant?" "You're seeing things today, Putti!" Akka said, laughing and ruffling Putti's hair. " Look again! " "Aaaah!" said Putti. "Walk faster, Putti, it's getting dark!" said Akka. "Look, the streetlights have been turned on!" "Eeeeeeeee! A monster!" shouted Putti. "Aw, look again, Putti!" said Akka. "Phhshhhhh!" sighed Putti, relieved. Putti and Akka reached home. "Look, Putti! Aren't these Ajji's slippers?" asked Akka. *Ajji: Kannada for grandmother They peered in through the window. "Yes, Putti! Ajji is here! She said she would bring chakli!" said Akka. *Chakli: a fried, crunchy snack made with rice flour and gram flour. "Better look again, Akka," said Putti. "What if that is not Ajji? What if it's someone else wearing a saree? What if it's just a saree draped over a chair? What if it's just a bundle of clothes. What if..." "Look again, Putti!" said Akka. It WAS Ajji! And she had brought chakli!
author: Shruthi  Rao

title: Puppy Hears a Noise
text: Where is that sound coming from?" asks Puppy. “Baby Elephant, Baby Elephant, you're screeching so loud!” says Puppy. “It’s not me. I don’t screech,” answers Baby Elephant. “Porcupine, Porcupine, you're screeching so loud!” says Puppy. “It’s not me. I can’t screech,” answers Porcupine. “Woodpecker, Woodpecker, you're screeching so loud!” says Puppy. “It’s not me. I can’t screech,” answers Woodpecker. “Hornbills, Hornbills, you're screeching so loud!” “It’s not us. We can’t screech,” answer the Hornbills. “Hummingbirds, hummingbirds, you're screeching so loud!” “It’s not us. We can’t screech,” answer the Hummingbirds. “Baby Monkeys, Baby Monkeys, you're screeching so loud!” says Puppy. “It’s not us. Who is it? Let’s find out!” answer the Baby Monkeys. “We are Crickets, we are Crickets, we chirp-screech! We rub our wings together to make the chirp-screech noise at night.” Oh! It's the crickets!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Saru and her Little Secret
text: At the far edge of the forest near a large muddy pond is a wooden fence. Inside the fence stands a big brick building surrounded by small cottages and sheds. A large number of people live here and do a lot of good work. The big building has a student hostel, a school and a hospital. In the hostel lives a little girl called Saru. Saru is playful and ready to run, skip and jump, ever so often. A boy called Mangu lives at the hostel too. Mangu is Saru’s best friend but unlike her he is timid and does not run about as much. Saru has three more friends who live in the cottages nearby. They are Hari, Manik and Ketki. Hari’s father works as a driver, Manik’s parents work at the hospital and Ketki’s mother is a teacher at the school. Then, there is Mai; she is the caretaker of the children. Mai has eyebrows, which are always crossed over each other, and she has a booming voice whenever she calls out to Saru. If you were to pass by the hostel you would be sure to hear Mai calling out to Saru at any time of the day. This is because Saru was never where she was meant to be. She was always away in the woods or near the pond. Now that we know all about the people in the story, let us begin, not at the very beginning but on a bright sunny morning in the month of May. Saru pulled down the yellow sheet from her eyes as she heard the sounds of the pots and pans in the kitchen. She jumped out from her bed. Soon, Saru ate her rice gruel and got ready for the day. It was a school holiday. The day was definitely going to be a very good one, Saru knew. Whenever there was no school Saru was sure to have plenty of fun. She called out to Mangu. But Mangu was not in the mood to go to the pond with her. Mangu liked school and would have liked to be there instead of running off with Saru. Saru decided to ask her other friends to join her. But all of them seemed to have something to do that morning and Saru was left to herself. Not being too upset about it, she raced towards the fence of the building and slipped out from an opening between the wooden planks. She knew she shouldn’t be doing that, but Saru was too excited and didn’t stop to think. Off she went down the hill, tip-toed over pebbles on the slush and the puddles and then ran further downhill to the pond by the large pipal tree. There were times when a passerby would sit under the shady tree or take a nap. But there was no one around this morning. Saru was glad she was alone; she knew that if anyone from the hostel saw her she would have to answer a dozen questions and she was sure that there would be a good scolding in store for her. Saru’s favourite pastime by the pond was to catch dragonflies. The long winged insects looked just like helicopters that she had seen in pictures before, and catching them by their delicate wings was just the right kind of fun she was looking for. “One down, two down, and many more down!” Saru would carefully hold her fingers towards the dragonfly as it hovered over the reeds and snap her fingers at great speed to catch the buzzing insect. Then she would sit it down on the sticky leaves of the bushes nearby. The dragonfly would be stuck to the leaf for a few minutes and then fly away. While Saru was busy snapping up the dragonflies she heard a scratching sound in the bushes nearby. In a moment the sound grew louder and Saru could see the bushes moving. A curious girl by nature, Saru peered through the bushes to see, what the sound was about. As she moved the branches out of the way, Saru came face-to-face with a tiny creature with the biggest eyes and the funniest shape ever. It looked like a little baby deer with the body of a large mouse. The little animal was startled to see Saru and tried to scamper away but couldn’t do so. Its leg seemed to be caught in something below. As Saru stared at it in amazement, she could see the poor animal frightened and trying hard to get free and escape. The more it tried to do so, the more it seemed to be trapped. It pulled and pulled till it could do no more and sank down into the bushes. She pushed the bushes away some more and looked below at the tired animal lying in a heap. The little strange animal had got its hind leg trapped in a long vine from the tree above. Saru carefully unwound the vine from its leg and freed it. But the poor deer was wounded and didn’t move. Feeling sorry for the animal, she decided to carry it home and nurse it back to health. As Saru walked back to the building with the mouse-like animal in her arms, she spotted Mai standing in the verandah, looking out for her. Sensing trouble, Saru made a dash for the tractor shed nearby. She knew that one look at the little animal in her hands and Mai would tell her to leave it in the woods. Mai didn’t like anything little, people or animals! After Mai had grown tired of calling to Saru and had returned inside, Saru gingerly stepped around the building and carried the frightened creature inside the shed adjoining it. This shed housed the large pots, pans, ladles, and vessels that were needed for cooking large and special meals on festival days. Saru looked around the dark room and decided that she would keep the little animal there and nurse it back to health. Though Saru was barely a few years old herself, she knew that the animal wouldn’t survive outside as it probably had a broken leg. After a hasty glance around the room, she made up her mind and placed the animal in a large pot, which was the largest vessel there and was used only on special occasions. She spread a jute bag at the bottom and laid the animal very carefully on it. First, Saru made a quick trip to her friends giving them the delightful news. Then, she ran to get some milk from the kitchen. Within minutes, they were all peering at the quaint little animal. Hari was the oldest of the lot and as soon as he saw the animal he proclaimed that it was a baby deer. Ketki, who loved to read and was the most poetic, decided that they should call it ‘Pillu’. Since Mangu was the gentlest in the group, he was chosen to feed milk to Pillu. Pillu was a little hesitant at first but as he was hungry he soon drank the milk that Mangu offered in spoonfuls. They decided that Pillu should be kept in the shed as no one went there much. Mangu agreed to feed it and the others promised to bring it some food whenever they could. Pillu looked a great deal sturdier later in the evening. He had been fed another round of milk after he had nibbled at the bhakri that Manik had sneaked in. As night fell, the friends tucked Pillu under the folds of a jute bag and headed to their beds. The children spent a restless night, while Pillu slept peacefully in his new home. Before long it was morning and the excited children went straight to the shed. Pillu was sitting up, his head bobbing over the rim of the large pot. The children sat down for some important discussions. They whispered to each other. They argued. Mai had glared at them when she had passed by and wondered what they were up to. Seeing nothing amiss, she had continued on her way. As the children stroked the soft fur on Pillu’s tiny body and cuddled him, he seemed warm and calm. They wanted to keep him forever. However, they knew that once he grew up into a large deer, they wouldn’t be able to hide him in the small room. Every time they heard footsteps close by they would hide Pillu in the pot. None of them wanted to leave Pillu’s side. Pillu was their little secret. The next day was the same. In the morning they rushed to the shed before school. They had each managed to get some food for Pillu. They fed him with care and headed for school. No sooner was school over than they hurried back to the shed to be with Pillu. Pillu had been good and had managed to stay in his pot and out of trouble. They spent the evening playing with Pillu who was strong enough to stand up now. His leg seemed to be healing well. Days passed by and each day Pillu grew fatter and healthier. Soon Pillu grew friskier too. He seemed to want to be out of his pot more and the children began to panic. They were certain that if someone spotted Pillu, that would be the end of their secret. They were also worried about Pillu's strange growth; they wondered why Pillu continued to look like a large mouse and hadn’t grown into a deer as yet. It was probably because they had kept him for so long in the pot, they fretted sadly. A few days later there was chaos. It was late in the night and everybody was asleep when, suddenly, there was a loud clanking sound. The sound rang out from Pillu’s shed and it woke up all the people. Everyone ran towards the shed. And there he was! Little Pillu stood in the centre of the shed looking around with his large loopy eyes. He had probably tried to get out of the pot and had overturned a lot of other pots and pans. The room looked a real mess. They were shocked to see Pillu. Everyone seemed to be talking at once. All through the commotion, little Pillu stood looking as sweet as ever. Soon, a gentleman with a kind voice came forward. He calmed the people down by asking them not to be afraid as the animal was harmless and had probably strayed in from the wild. Still it was Mai who seemed to have all the answers. She raved and ranted. She said she knew the mess had been caused by Saru and her friends who were up to mischief all the time. T he person with the gentle voice picked up little Pillu and beckoned to Saru and her friends. He was smiling and asked the children if they had taken care of Pillu. Comforted by his gentleness, the children told him how they had found Pillu and how they had taken care of him. They also said they were worried about how tiny their little deer was. Could it be because they had kept him in the pot, they asked. He laughed gently when he heard this. The kind man told the children that the little animal that they had looked after so well was actually a mouse-deer and not a deer. The children were most surprised to learn that their Pillu was in fact not a baby deer and was always going to look as he did – a bit like a mouse, a bit like a pig, a bit like a deer! The elders decided to let the children keep Pillu at the hostel. The kind man announced that an animal shelter would be built there. There were squeals of delight from the happy children. A month later, an animal shelter was built for sick and needy animals from the forest. Little Pillu began to live there forever! If you go up to the hostel one day you just may see Pillu playing with Saru and her friends! This story is inspired by the the work of Dr Prakash Amte, son of the late social worker, Baba Amte. Started by Baba Amte, the Lok Biradari Prakalp works for the welfare and development of Madia Gond tribals in the remote regions of central India. The organization runs a free hospital, a school and an animal shelter called Amte’s Animal Ark, an orphanage-cum-rescue centre, at Hemalkasa. Visitors are welcome at the shelter. To learn more about Lok Biradari Prakalp do visit
author: Sunita Lad Bhamray

title: The Lost Duckling
text: He was hurt. Tharul cleaned and fed him, and named him Ducky. The cat saw Ducky. Ducky ran away! But, he was hurt again. Tharul and his friends looked after Ducky. One day, the mother found her little duckling. They went back home. Tharul and his friends said goodbye to their friend.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Secret Owner
text: One day, Abaron stole a bag. It had a rooster inside it. He hid the bag in a tree and went into the forest. Aaron and Baaron saw Abaron stealing the bag. They wanted to teach him a lesson. They took the bag from the tree. Abaran saw Aaron and Baaron taking the bag he had hidden in the tree. He went up to them, but he was scared to ask for the bag. Aaron and Baaron began walking away from the forest. Abaron followed them. The three of them came near a stream. “I will take the bag across,” said Aaron. “No! The bag might fall into the stream,” said Abaron. “Yes, the bag is quite heavy,” agreed Aaron. He winked at Baaron. "It might sink." “Let’s cut the bag into two parts,” said Baaron. “No!” shouted Abaron. “Don’t cut the bag.” “Go where you have to go,” said Baaron. “We will certainly cut the bag in two.” Abaron was worried about the rooster. He began shouting, “Thieves! Thieves! They stole my bag. Catch them!” Hearing Abaron’s cry, the Arachchi* came running with his assistant. *An important official native to Sri Lanka “Whose bag is this?” he asked them. Aaron and Baaron winked at the Arachchi. He understood. They all said, “It’s not ours.” “Is that so? Then throw the bag into the stream,” ordered the Arachchi. His assistant threw the bag into the stream. “Oh no!” shouted Abaron, and jumped into the stream. The rooster came tumbling out. Abaron had fallen for the Arachchi’s trick.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Lucky Time
text: One hot afternoon, everyone had fallen asleep except two sneaky mice. They were hungry for some of uncle's jaggery. Just as they were about to reach for the jaggery, aunty came back from fetching water. "Run!" cried the mice as they scurried away. Again, they reached for the the jaggery, but just as they grabbed it the cat spied them. “Run!” “HIDE!” What a narrow escape! Finally, all was quite. “Let’s get the jaggery now,”squeaked the mice. Clang! BANG! Down came the jaggery! Down came the mice! “Bow-wow! Bow-wow!” The dog ran past. “This dog is so naughty!” cried aunty, as she chased the dog. “What a mess!” said aunty, as she picked up the jaggery from the floor. The mice ran to the kitchen to hide. Aunty opened a basket and put the jaggery away. "What luck! Jaggery all to ourselves" The jaggery was finally theirs to eat. They couldn't believe it! They ate and ate until their stomachs were full. "Such good Jaggery!" After they were finished, the sneaky mice took as much as they could carry and went home.
author: Magdalena  Cooper

title: I Need a Violin
text: Dragonfly is sad because he wants to join, but he lost his violin. “I have an idea!" says Butterfly. Butterfly and Dragonfly fly to Ladybird's house. Ladybird is shelling peanuts. Butterfly and Dragonfly offer to help. In return, he gifts them a beautiful peanut shell. Next, they help Grasshopper mow her lawn. In return, she gifts them a few straws of hay and some grass from her lawn. Finally, they help the bees to find their honey. "Thanks!" say the bees as they hand Butterfly a ball of wax. Then, Butterfly begins to look for a cobweb. "What are doing now?" whines Dragonfly. Dragonfly is tired of helping. He goes to sleep. Suddenly, he wakes up to a beautiful sound! What's this? Butterfly has made a violin using the gifts they received! "Here," says butterfly. "Now you can play with me while I sing." Now, whenever Butterfly sings, Dragonfly plays the violin.
author: Magdalena  Cooper

title: Colourful Birds
text: Once upon a time, all birds were white. “Make me beautiful, Grandfather Magic,” said Woodpecker. “Come, I will paint you a beautiful colour,” said Grandfather Magic. Woodpecker was now red. A little bird looked at Woodpecker. She wanted to look beautiful, too. “This is my favourite flower,” said the little bird to Grandfather Magic. “Will you paint me the same colour as this flower?” Grandfather Magic painted the little bird a beautiful yellow. The yellow bird went to Woodpecker. “Look how beautiful I am, Woodpecker!” said the yellow bird. “No, no, I am more beautiful than you,” argued Woodpecker. Oriole tried to calm them down by holding them apart. During the fight, the yellow colour of the little bird mixed with the red colour of Woodpecker. Oriole became… orange! “O-o-range, o-o-riole! O-o-range, o-o-riole!” The parrots teased Oriole. Oriole chased after them angrily. “Oh, Grandfather Magic!” cried the parrots. “Please save us!” “Come, let me paint you all green,” he offered. The green parrots showed off their colour to Kingfisher. “Where did you get this beautiful colour, dear parrots?” “Go to Grandfather Magic!” they chirped. Kingfisher liked the colour of the sky. So Grandfather Magic turned her blue. Kingfisher went to meet Woodpecker. As they were talking, Pigeon crashed into them. “Oh no!” A little bit of red from Woodpecker mixed with a little bit of blue from Kingfisher. Pigeon looked at the smudge of purple on her. "Purple looks good on me," she thought. While Grandfather Magic painted Pigeon purple, all the birds joined them. What a wonderful rainbow of colours!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Who Will Win?
text: This is the Shapes Family. Today, the Lantern Competition was announced in their town. The Shapes get ready for the competition. Circle got to work. But, he wouldn’t let his little sister Triangle help him. Ms. Rectangle said to her, “Make a lantern with triangles!” Circle made a lantern with circles. He showed it to Mr. Square. Triangle made a lantern with triangles. “Don’t you think we are using the same old shapes?” asked Circle. Triangle agreed. Together, they made a new lantern with circles and triangles. Mr. Square made a lantern with squares. The Shapes finished making their lanterns. The winning lantern design was announced. It was the circle-triangle lantern!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Miss Goat's House
text: One morning, Miss Goat was grazing in the field. “Why is it is so hot this early in the year?” thought Miss Goat. “I must find some shade, away from this blazing heat,” thought Miss Goat. She bit off a lotus leaf and took shelter under it. But soon, the lotus leaf withered in the heat. Miss Goat tried to take shelter under a banana leaf, but the afternoon sun was so strong that the banana leaf withered too. Miss Goat ran to the jungle to make a shelter of tree branches. But, a hot wind blew away all the leaves! Miss Goat saw some villagers building a house. “I must learn how to build a strong house like that one,” she thought. After watching the villagers for a while, Miss Goat knew what she had to do. She gathered tree branches. She gathered banana leaves. Miss Goat dug holes for the tree branches. Then she spread the banana leaves over the tree branches and tied them tightly together. She worked so hard, she was now hotter than ever! Just as she finished, the hot wind began to blow. But this time, the wind could not blow the banana leaves away! Miss Goat settled inside her home. “I'm not hot any more!” she thought happily. "Now, I just need a nap."
author: Alisha Berger

title: Where is my Pet?
text: It likes hiding itself. Nia has a difficult time finding it. “What shall I do?” Oh! Nia has an idea! On Monday, she decides to paint it red. This will help her find it easily. “Where are you?” Nia wonders. “I’m here, resting among the red apples.” On Tuesday, she paints it orange. This will help her spot it easily. Her pet hides itself among the oranges. On Wednesday, she paints it yellow. “When I paint it a bright colour,” thinks Nia, “I will find it easily.” “Look, I’m here!” On Thursday, she decides to paint it green. Can you see where Nia’s pet has hidden itself? On Friday, she paints it blue. Nia’s pet hides itself on a painting hanging on the wall. On Saturday, she paints it purple. Her pet hides itself on a plate of grapes. On Sunday, Nia decides to paint her pet with all the colours of the rainbow. Ooh! Now Nia’s pet has nowhere to hide.
author: Brian Kavanagh

title: Ledile's Red Balloon
text: One day, the balloon floated across the river. Ledile couldn’t swim. What could she do? Ledile broke a branch from a tree......but the branch was too short to reach the balloon. A tall man came to the river. Ledile asked for his help. “I cannot swim, either,” said the man. Ledile decided to wade into the river up to her waist. Maybe then the stick would reach the balloon! She took off her shoes. She stepped into the river. The water was soon up to her knees. She waded further into the river. The water reached her waist. She was scared--and she still could not reach the balloon! Ledile hurried out of the water. She was about to give up when she saw a small fish. “Please help me!” she called to the fish. "I will try," said the fish. The fish blew and blew, but the balloon did not budge. Then a bigger fish came along. “Please help me!” Ledile asked again. “I will take you to your balloon,” said the big fish. Ledile hopped onto the fish. She reached her balloon! Hooray!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Billy to the Rescue
text: But Billy loves being clean and shiny. “I don’t want to get dirty,” he says. “Billy, the animals need you,” say the firefighters. “Billy, the plants need you!” “Billy, the people need you!” “Please, Billy, we all need you.” “Am I that important?” Billy asks. “Yes, you are! Let’s go then!” “Thank you, Billy,” everyone shouts.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Botse-Botse Wants to Get Married
text: She wants to get married, too. She considers what she will need. I need a ring! There, now I have a ring. I need a wedding dress! There. Now I have a wedding dress. I need a bride’s tiara. There, now I have a tiara! But where is my groom? Oh! Maybe I am too young to get married yet. I want to go to school! I will learn to read at school. I will learn to write at school. I will write stories about girls like me. Girls who can do anything!
author: Alisha Berger
illustrator: So  Chakrya; Soeurm  Kakada; Ven Che; Yuom  Kosal

title: The Green Apple
text: Green Apple wants to be red, too. That night, Green Apple couldn't sleep. She tried to think of a plan. She tiptoed up to Red Tomato. She took his jacket! The next morning, Red Tomato was furious when he realized that his jacket was gone. Green Apple was putting on the jacket. “Take it off!” shouted Red Tomato. Green Apple took off the jacket. She gave it back. But Green Apple did not give up! She befriended Strawberry. That night, Green Apple sneaked up to Strawberry. Strawberry opened one eye and asked, “What are you up to?” Green Apple began to run. The tomatoes, strawberries and red peppers all chased her away! Green Apple soon reached the forest. She got another idea. She came across Chameleon. “Sir Chameleon, I know you can change colours," Green Apple said. "Can you please make me red?” Chameleon told her, "Go to the mountain, and collect long leaves." Green Apple went to the mountain. But it was so high! She collected leaves from the bottom of the mountain instead. She took them back to Chameleon. Chameleon ate up the leaves. He touched Green Apple with the tip of his tail. Green Apple turned purple! “You gave me the wrong leaves,” Chameleon sighed. “I am sorry,” said Green Apple. “Oh, shame,” said Chameleon. “Who has heard of a purple apple?” Green Apple looked at her hands. I liked it better when I was green, she thought. "All right," Chameleon said. "Now run away from the forest, and do not look back." Green Apple met a boy. “Apple, apple, please be my friend, he said. "I love your green colour.” Green Apple looked at herself. She was green! Green Apple was happy to have found a friend. She was happy to feel like herself again.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Lost in the Dark
text: Rebone were friends. One day, they went to the forest to fetch firewood. On the way home, they came across a river. They played and played until the forest turned dark. It was so dark that they could not find their way back home. Suddenly, they heard a loud howling from somewhere in the forest. Lebo screamed and ran. The others followed. Then Bonolo shouted, “Hey, look! I see a cave. Let’s hide here.” “No,” said Lebo, “There might be wild animals inside.” All three girls kept running. “Look over there,” pointed Rebone. “I can see lights. Maybe that’s where our home is.” The three girls followed the lights, but soon realised that they had been chasing fireflies. By now the girls were tired and hungry. They decided to rest under a tree. “Come on,” said Lebo. “Let’s climb the tree. We’ll be safer there.” All at once they heard voices and a dog barking. People were calling out their names. Their parents and people from the village had come looking for them. “Here we are!” shouted the girls. The girls were happy to be reunited with their family. They promised never to lose track of time again.
author: Alisha Berger

title: A New Visitor
text: We have a visitor!” “Let's run to see the visitor!” “Will the visitor be friends with us?” “Should we give the visitor a gift?” “Let’s find out who it is first!” All the animals rush and push and knock each other down. “Let’s go higher to see the visitor.” All the animals gather in the middle of the jungle. The monkeys point at the new visitor. “Look! Look!” They all look at the new visitor and laugh loudly. Cuddled up next to mother, the new visitor is drinking milk!
author: Brian Kavanagh

title: A Dress for Porcupine
text: The New Year is just around the corner. Gethum, the spider has a lot of work to do. “How do I make a dress for Kooru?” Gethum wonders. The first dress Gethum made was too thin. The second dress was too tight. Kooru couldn’t even walk in it. Maybe I should just stay home on the new year, thought Kooru. I will somehow make a dress for Kooru, thought Gethum. But the next dress didn't suit her either. It only covered her front! “No dress suits me because of my spikes,” Kooru cried to Gethum. Now it was the New Year's eve. Gethum worked all night. She didn't sleep at all. She wove a beautiful design around Kooru’s spikes. Everyone wore beautiful clothes on New Year's day! There were many competitions and lots of gifts and awards. Of course, Kooru won for Best Dress. But, the most prestigious prize was for the year's Hardest Worker. And you know who won that prize!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Paatti's Glasses
text: Patti had lost her glasses and little Muni was determined to find them. But,where should she look? Muni pondered over this question for a while.Then she knew it, in Patti's room! Muni had searched everywhere,in Patti's cupboard, under her chair, and even inside the sink! But no glasses were to be found.There was only one place where she didn't look.... Yes! It was in Patti's messy table. Muni ran to Patti and gave her the glasses. And to celebrate, they had Patti's home-made laddoos! Mmmm... tasty,lovely,delicious.
author: Shruthi Sridharan

title: Tiny Squeaks
text: Amit was walking through the forest.The only light he got was from his trusty flashlight. Then,"SQUEAK". Amit was startled.He stood petrified for a second and then walked towards the sound. Then,"SQUEAK", but this time it was louder. Amit almost jumped out of his skin.He looked around there was nobody not even a mouse.There were only few mushrooms. That's when,"SQUEAK", Amit spun towards the mushrooms.And there, he saw a tiny girl,sitting under an umbrella.She was scared stiff at seeing such a huge boy. Amit,seeing this introduced himself and said that he meant no harm. After she settled down, she told Amit that her name was Tiny. She told Amit many fascinating tales.Tiny and Amit became strong friends forever.
author: Shruthi Sridharan

title: The Confused Dragonfly
text: On a happy evening there were group of dragonflies playing over nests and webs. Suddenly rain started falling all the dragonflies flew away to their shelters. Except one dragon fly which was confused and searching for shelter. Dragonfly was in search of it's shelter. Meanwhile rain started to become heavy and the dragonfly was more confused. Dragonfly found a frog and asked for it's help but frog was enjoying the rain and din't even care for dragonfly. It went on searching for it's shelter. But couldn't still find any. At last it found a leaf and it was sitting under the leaf happily watching the rainfall.
author: Madhuri Srinivas

title: Little parrot and Mona
text: "Yayy cute little parrot", shouted Mona after seeing it in her father's hand. "Yes, it's for you",said her father and gave it to her hand. "it's so cute daddy",replied Mona. Mona took her parrot in to her room and kept it near a window. she thought of giving that parrot a name.Then she suddenly remembered about her friend's birthday party and left in hurry. Mona went to her friend's birthday party and she bought a piece of cake for her little parrot while coming back home. When Mona was about to give a piece of cake to her parrot her father warned her not to feed it with such foods.He also told that,"parrot's usually eat guava's,sunflower seed's,canary seeds". Mona was surprised. As soon as Mona entered in to her parrot started shouting at her," I don't want to be in this cage. I want to fly freely like my friend's." And again parrot told,"you can freely play whenever you want because you are not caged like me.I too want to play like that without being caged like this". Mona watched her parrot trying to escape and felt bad about it. Mona went to her little parrot and said that"i will release you from this cage so that you can freely fly and play with your friends". Mona released her parrot saying that to her. Parrot flew away with happiness and thanked Mona for her help. HAPPY ENDING:)
author: Madhuri Srinivas

title: Chris the Crying Crocodile
text: Chris the crocodile sat crying by the lake. All of the other animals came to ask why he was sad. "Why are you crying?" asked Fred the fat frog. "Yes, why are you crying?" asked Fran the fancy fish. "I'm very lonely," said Chris the crying crocodile. "I have no friends at all." "I tried to make friends with the men with nets," he said. "But when I tried to say hello, they ran away!" "And they came back with guns!" "It's ok," said Betty the butterfly. "You can be my friend. Just promise not to eat me." "I promise!" said Chris the crocodile. But Betty the butterfly flew away. So Chris the crying crocodile was even sadder than before. But Betty the beautiful butterfly came back with all of her butterfly friends. Now Chris the crying crocodile cried tears of happiness. He wasn't lonely anymore.
author: Jessica Wright

title: Anna the Famous Pop Star
text: Anna wanted to be a grown up. She didn't want to be a little girl any more. She wanted to be famous. Instead of making the bed, she dreamed of making beautiful music. Instead of carrying the newspapers, she dreamed of being on the front page of every newspaper in the world. Instead of carrying the buckets of water, she dreamed of carrying buckets of gold. She would be famous! She wanted to travel the world and meet important people, just like her mummy did. She wanted to dress in colourful clothes. She wanted to visit exciting places like the postcards in the wardrobe. While she is reading her books every day, she dreams of the amazing places she will go and people she will meet when she is famous. So she puts on her mummy's slippers and she dreams. She dreams of far away places instead of setting the table for dinner. She dreams of being a famous pop star and her little brother is her drummer. So into the room they go and the performance begins. They are FAMOUS! She dreams that the banana is a golden microphone and the apple is a shaker. Their music is amazing. Their picture will be in every newspaper and they will be famous throughout the world. They sing and dance all day long. The door opens with a CRASH! Mummy is not happy. She did not hear Anna's beautiful singing. She did not hear Jack's perfect drumming. All she could see was a MESS! So Anna goes into the bathroom. She shuts the door. She stands on the stool and sings. She sings as loud as she can. She sings herself happy. "I can still be famous!" she decides. And she is.
author: Jessica Wright

title: story of a teeny tiny ant.
text: There was a teeny tiny ant, living alone away from his home in a hostel. He left his home to study at an ant university. He didn't had any friends. The teeny tiny ant, once came across a strange looking white big ant in the ant cafeteria at the university. The big white ant seemed to have come from far far away. he could speak strange languages. the big white ant seemed to be having trouble with his 'ant mobile phone'. The teeny tiny ant helped the big white ant to fix up his mobile phone. And, thus they became friends. The big white ant started teaching the teeny tiny ant about the languages he knew and he taught the teeny tiny ant about his home town and his life in the country where there were all big white ants roaming around. The big white ant, took the teeny tiny ant around small to medium sized mountains for fun. every weekend the ants use to have fun, they use to drive around the ant university, eat at cool places, meet new people through ant couchsurfing. It was such a fun time. The big white ant also introduced the teeny tiny ant to another strange looking big white ant. This was a female white ant. she was skinny, had red hairs and smiled in a fun way. the female white ant use to wear spectacles sometimes. Use to look like the picture above. The female white ant made mint tea for all the three ants and all the three ants played around a lot. But, one day both the big white ants decided to go back to there homeland. They said 'bub-bye' to the teeny tiny ant, and they left. The teeny tiny ant, now sits alone, looks outside his office window and thinks about what the big white ants must be doing at this moment. Also, sometimes the teeny tiny ant writes stories during his office time, wasting his company resources. The teeny tiny ant misses his big white ant friends. Buhuhuhuhu (ant crying).....
author: siddharth ingle
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Gita V. Reddy; Joysree Das; Partho Sengupta; Tanvi Bhat

title: Leah's perfect kitty cat.
text: It is Saturday morning in the Jones house, the day Leah's parents promised her a kitty cat. Immediately when Leah got to the pet store she fell in love with a brown soft furred kitty cat. But her parents said "Why don't you take the ginger cat instead." Leah smiled but she was not happy and she walked on. Leah put the brown furred cat down. She picked up the white cat with stripes and spots. "Why don't you take this black rough cat instead.", her father said. Leah smiled but she was not happy and she walked on. Leah picked up a few more kitty cats. Her parents nodded their heads. The cats she picked up weren't perfect enough. So she walked on. "Take this one instead.", said her father. Leah looked down and walked on. Then, Leah picked up a yellow cat. She loved this kitty cat. This kitty cat loved her too. The kitty cat even licked her. Her parents said, " We think she is perfect for you!" Leah was very happy with her choice. Her kitty cat was perfect for her and that's why she called her kitty cat Miss Perfect.
author: Aneeqah Baker
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Gwendolene van der Merwe; JP Brouard; Kalynne Vorster; Padmanabh; Partho Sengupta

title: Bheema's problem
text: One day, Gauri, the cow, asked him, “Bheema, why are you so sad?” Bheema said, “I cannot get up early and Ramu shouts at me every day. Will you wake me up every morning, please?” “Yes, I will,” said Gauri. Early next morning, Gauri mooed loudly, but Bheema did not wake up. Coming back from the river in the evening, Bheema met Moti, the dog. “I can never get up in the morning on time. Will you wake me up?” Bheema asked Moti. “Yes, I will,” said Moti and the next morning he barked and barked but did Bheema did not wake up. That evening Bheema met Cheenu, the rooster. He said to Cheenu, “You crow in the morning and everybody wakes up. Will you wake me up too?” Cheenu agreed. The next morning, Cheenu crowed long and loud, but Bheema did not wake up. The next evening, Bheema saw Kalu, the crow, cawing away happily. “Kalu, will you wake me up in the morning, please?” he asked. Kalu said, “Why not? I will caw and wake you up.” The next morning Kalu cawed all he could but Bheema did not wake up. Bheema was sad. The next morning, a fly came and sat on his nose. “Aaah…chhoooo… ahchhoo!” Bheema got up with a big sneeze. “Wow! I woke up. How did I wake up?” he asked in wonder. “I woke you up,” said the fly.“Will you wake me up like this early every morning?” “Sure,” said the fly. Bheema was happy. Now he would have no problem getting up early every morning!
author: Paridhi Gupta

title: Asila...Basila...Uthila...Jaucha
text: He would go to the town sometimes. He became friends with Sudhir. They did not speak the same language but they talked to each other in sign language. One day Samu’s wife said to him, “You have made a new friend. But we don’t know his language. How will we talk to him? Why don’t you go to him and learn his language?” Samu agreed with his wife and went to Sudhir’s house. As Sudhir saw him coming he said, “Asila?” (In Odia this means, ‘You have come?’) Samu did not understand but he came inside and sat down. Sudhir said, “Basila?”(In Odia this means, ‘You sat down?’) Samu did not understand so he got up somewhat angry. Sudhir said, “Uthila?”(In Odia this means, ‘Standing up?’) He turned to leave and his friend said, “Jaucha?” (In Odia this means, 'You are leaving?') Samu left but he kept saying these four words to himself. It was almost night by the time he reached home. Just then some thieves from the town entered his field of maize. Samu’s wife wanted to know what he had learnt from his friend. He repeated the first word that he had heard. Since his wife could not hear too well, he said loudly, "Asila?" The thieves outside heard him. They thought they must have been spotted! So they quickly sat down in the field. Samu’s wife asked him what else he had learned. He said, "Basila?" His wife liked the sound of these new words. She said, "Say it again, please." He said, "Basila?" The thieves were certain he had seen them. So they stood up quickly. His wife clapped her hands in delight and said, "And what else?" He said, "Uthila?" The thieves thought they should turn and leave before they got caught. His wife said, "Anything else?" He said, "Jaucha?" Now the thieves felt they were in real danger! Surely the man was talking to them after seeing them They slipped away as fast as they could and never came back! The Concept India’s diverse linguistic landscape has a rich seam of stories for children. Unfortunately, many tribal languages do not have literature for children in book form or books for reading pleasure. As increasing numbers of tribal children go to school, it is now more necessary than ever to create a body of children’s literature in their languages. Literature that reflects their own world and opens up the world beyond because books are magical, powerful things that inform, amuse, educate and entertain in the most interactive way. Books make every child an independent and life-long seeker of knowledge in her own unique way. For education to be truly meaningful to every child, she must get good books to read in her own language. The Project Pratham Books and IgnusERG, with the support of Bernard van Leer Foundation have created the first ten books for children’s reading pleasure in Munda, Kui, Saura and Juanga languages from Odisha. The stories were written and illustrated by authors and illustrators belonging to these tribes in a series of workshops. This series of books is called Adikahani. It is a significant first step towards giving a voice to cultures that do not find adequate representation in mainstream discourses. The Partners IgnusERG is a guild of resource persons working to support teachers and enhancing the quality of education, particularly in government schools. They focus their efforts on bringing equity in education and addressing the needs of marginalized children. Bernard van Leer Foundation is an international grant-making foundation based in The Hague. Its mission is to improve opportunities for young children growing up in socially and economically difficult circumstances. It has a particular interest in supporting mother-tongue based education. This story was written by the Kui Writers’ Group consisting of Buna Kanhar, Filiman Pradhan and Pramod Digal. With a background in ECCE, they all interact with children regularly. It has been illustrated by Sugrib Kumar Juanga, using the Saura mural style as a base. The Kui language is spoken by more than 1 lakh people in Khondhamal, Gajapati and Rayagada districts of Odisha. It is related to the Gondi language. The spellings of the language in Odia script are not definitive as many new sounds are being rendered in print for the first time.
author: Paridhi Gupta

title: Manners in the Park - Spot the Difference
text: 1a. The children in this park are playing happily. 1b. The children in this park are not playing happily. Can you spot why? 2a. The children are playing as a team. 2b. The children are not playing as a team. Can you spot why? 3a. The people are walking in a spotless park. 3b. The people are walking in a messy park. Can you spot why? 4a. The children are having fun together. 4b. T he children are not having fun at all. Can you spot why? 5a. The water in this park is clean. 5b. The water in this park is polluted. Can you spot why? SPOT THE DIFFERENCES In one park, the children are playing happily and making friends. In the other park, the children are neither kind nor considerate. Who could spot the most differences – your friends, teachers, parents or you? 1a, 1b 1. Two children are trying to get on the swing at the same time. 2. A child is pulling another child’s leg while he is on the monkey bar. 3. A child is throwing sand at anyone who tries to enter the sandbox. 4. The monkey bar is missing two rods. 5. A red swing seat has turned blue. 6. The shovel in the sand box is missing. 2a, 2b 1. A girl is arguing with the referee. 2. Two children are about to punch each other while tackling the ball. 3. A player from one team is tripping the runner from the other team. 4. All the blue checks on a white shirt become blue stripes on a white shirt. 5. A girl’s hairstyle is different. 6. The referee has a blue whistle around his neck. 3a, 3b 1. A man is seen throwing a toffee wrapper on the ground. 2. A tea seller has a clutter of plastic cups around him. 3. A child has thrown some trash into the bin and missed. 4. There is a blue plastic packet in the bushes. 5. The walls along the boundary of the park have old posters. 6. There is a pile of rubbish under the lamp. 4a, 4b 1. A girl in the green top is angry with the boy who wants to skip with them. 2. A few younger kids are seen seated with their roller skates on, the older girl is not letting them skate with her. 3. One roller skater is elbowing another. 4. One of the shoelaces on the roller skates is untied. 5. The hopscotch area has an extra box. 6. One skipping rope is blue. 5a, 5b 1. The child in a red shirt, standing next to the gardener, has plucked a flower. 2. One child is twisting a dog’s tail, the dog looks distressed. 3. A jogger is spitting into the water. 4. One of the flowers in the garden is yellow. 5. The water is foaming. 6. The goose leaving the pond has a film of black liquid on its wing.
author: C G Salamander

title: The princess and the lion
text: Krishnamoorthy, Sithiravelu Karunanandarajah, Uma Balamurali, shyrus joseph the princess and the lion once there was a lion the lion had two cubs one day the cubs got lost in the forest the lion went to search for his cubs the lion saw a princess.he asked her to help him they found the cubs from that day the princess and the lion became friends.
author: Tanya lemos
illustrator: Jai Bhagwan Gupta; Jayaprakash Bojan; Santhosh Krishnamoorthy; shyrus joseph; Sithiravelu Karunanandarajah; Uma Balamurali

title: my family
text: Neha lived with her mom dad and brother in a small village, One fine day Neha's father was not feeling well, But he had to complete his office work on time, so neha and her brother were worried and wanted to help him. Neha's Father was having fever but then also he had to work so Neha's mother and the children brought a shawl for him and helped him so he gets alright fast. Neha and her family were happy that thier father became alright by helping each other. Moral; We should help each other
author: Venita  Hendriques

title: Peanut Butter & Jelly Sandwhich
text: Hi! I'm Peanut Butter and I'm new to this town. I have no friends. Ma came by this morning and said - "Don't just wait and watch sweetie! if you're bored, go out and find yourself some friends to play with". Will you help me look for friends? Great! Let's go! First, I came upon Cupcake. I saw her putting sprinkles on herself from a sprinkle machine, while playing with a friend. I asked her if I could play with her. "I'm sorry, but this is only a two-person game", said Cupcake. Then I found Jelly! I said to Jelly, "Can I play with you?" And guess what! Jelly said "YES". Yessss!! I was so happy. I had finally found a friend.
author: Shuchi Pannala

title: Pigeon power!
text: Hamdan was a young boy with a fascination for pigeons. He loved it when the pigeons used to fly around his balcony. He lived in a small apartment with his uncle. The apartment was in a big city. So, pigeons did not come there often for the fear of black smoke and shiny colourful things known as cars. Hamdan used to keep a small bowl, in which eh used to put little rice for the birds. Hamdan's old uncle hated pigeons. He thought they were a nuisance. Uncle's cat also didn't like pigeons. So, Hamdan could only play with the pigeons in the early mornings when his old, angry uncle was fast asleep and snoring. One day, Hamdan asked his uncle, "Daadu, why don't you like pigeons?" Daddu replied very angrily, "Chee! Pigeons only dirty our balcony. they are of no use." But Hamdan said, "But daadu, aren't they such beautiful creatures?" "When they flap their wings, they look like dancers. Their pretty blue necks add a pop of colour on their grey bodies. After all, this building was once their home. All this land was once a beautiful forest. Maybe there was a tree which was chopped down to make this building. That tree must have been their home, daadu." Daadu replied," Hamdan, you are right. This ploace must have been their home. Remember how much you hated shifting from our big house in Chennai? Maybe, even these poor birds had to shift from their tree. You are a very clever boy, Hamdan!" From that day onwards, the pigeons flew everyday to Hamdan's balcony where his uncle had kept some rice and water. It was a ritual to wake up every morning and sing with the pigeons for a while. Hamdan finally could be with the creatures he loved the most!
author: Sanjana

title: The fish who couldn't eat worms
text: There once was a fish who could not eat worms. His classmates made fun of him so much that he felt like a person. One day, there was a group quiz. Every group failed except the little fish's group. The little fish was very smart! Nobody had seen his brilliance because all of them were busy teasing him. Nobody ever teased him any more. The little fish was so happy that he started eating worms! All the little fish became his friends.
author: Srinwanti Mitra
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Monappa; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Thea   Nicole de Klerk; Yulianto  Qin

title: Now I've Got You!
text: Look behind you,” said the Wasp “Now I've got you!” said the Snake. “Too bad for you,” said the Frog. “Why?” asked the Snake. “Look behind you,” said the Frog. “Now I've got you!” said the Mongoose. “Too bad for you,” said the Snake. “Why?” asked the Mongoose. “Look behind you,” said the Mongoose. “Now I've got you!” said the Eagle. "Frog, let me go and I will save us all!" yelled the Wasp. The Frog let go of the Wasp. The Wasp flew up and stung the Eagle hard on her neck. The Eagle let go of the Mongoose. The Mongoose let go of the Snake. The Snake let go of the Frog. KER-SPLASH! Everyone said, "Thank you, Wasp!" And the Alligator thought, "Now I've got you..."
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Lost Doll
text: This is Abi. Abi has a doll. Abi loves her doll. But today, her doll is missing. She goes to look inside the house. She looks inside the kitchen. She looks in the dining room. She looks in the bedroom. She looks outside. “Where is my doll?” she asks the cat. “Meow,” says the cat. “Where is my doll?” she asks the chicken. “Ku-ku-ku,” says the chicken. “Where is my doll?” she asks the dog. “Bow wow wow,” says the dog.
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Snail's Wonderful Journey
text: Snail wants to take a trip on the highway. He sees a bus coming quickly towards him. The bus stops nearby. Oh! There is a gecko on the bus. The bus slows down to let passengers on and off. When Gecko sees Cheta, he isn't happy. “This bus is mine!” he says. “Well, the road is mine!” says Cheta. They both laugh. “I want to ride on the bus like you," says Cheta. “Then come to this stop early tomorrow morning,” says Gecko. Cheta arrives early the next morning. But not early enough! He misses the bus. "Oh, why haven't they made a watch for a snail?" Cheta moans. Cheta tries again the next morning. But, this bus never comes. "Oh, the bus must have broken down!" moans Cheta. "How unlucky I am!" I am not going home tonight, Cheta thinks to himself. I will stay right here and wait for the bus. The next morning, there is a long queue of people waiting for the bus. Cheta the Snail manages to get on! But, he is so small compared to all the people's feet that Gecko cannot see him. “Oh! Cheta still hasn't come,” thinks Gecko sadly. Cheta crawls to the windowsill. He is thrilled to see trees, houses, and mountains passing speedily by. The bus is so FAST! Riding a bus is like floating through the sky, thinks Cheta happily. “I never imagined an experience like this,” sighs Cheta. This time, Gecko hears him. Gecko is so happy to see his fellow traveler. In the evening, the bus returns to Cheta's stop. Gecko gets off with his new friend. "What a wonderful journey we had today!" says Cheta. "I want to fly like that again." "My friend, there are so many different buses!" says Gecko. "Our adventures will be endless."
author: Alisha Berger

title: Thembi and the Singing Tree
text: Here lives Thembi, her brother, Bongani, and their Gogo. Gogo is in the kitchen, cooking dinner. From the window she can see Bongani and the other children playing. But where is Thembi? Gogo decides to find Thembi. She takes off her apron and goes to find her granddaughter. Gogo finds Thembi sitting under the big tree, playing with her favourite doll. Gogo asks Thembi, “Why are you sitting here, all alone?” “Oh,” replies Thembi, “the other children don’t want to play with me.” “What about playing with your friend Sizani?” asks Gogo. “Sizani is mad at me,” replies Thembi. “She said that I just ignored her last week. “Gogo, I really didn’t see her.” “And what about playing with your brother?” asks Gogo. “Bongani doesn’t like to play with me,” sighs Thembi. “He says that I miss every time he kicks the ball to me.” “But aren’t you lonely?” asks Gogo. “Oh no,” replies Thembi. “I love sitting here, listening to the tree sing its beautiful song. “Listen, can’t you hear it?” Gogo listens and then looks up into the tree to see a beautiful Kingfisher, a Cuckoo, and a Robin, all singing their songs. Gogo remembers Thembi’s teacher once telling her that Thembi struggled to see things on the board. So, early the next morning, Gogo and Thembi walk to the local clinic. At the clinic, they meet Mr Ntuli. He asks Thembi to cover one eye with her hand and to look at the wall in front of her and tell him what she can see. Thembi looks carefully at the wall and says, “I can see something, but I am not sure what it is.” Mr Ntuli puts a metal frame on Thembi’s nose. Then, he slides a round glass into the frame and again asks Thembi, “Now, what can you see?” “I can see everything!” shouts Thembi. “I can see the letter E and F and P, and even the little letters, P, Z and D.” “That’s perfect,” says Mr Ntuli. “All you need are glasses and you will see just fine.” The nurse takes Thembi and Gogo to another room where there are many shelves filled with different kinds of spectacle frames. Thembi chooses a pair of bright red frames. “A good choice,” says Gogo. After one week, Thembi and Gogo return to Mr. Ntuli’s office. Thembi tries on her new glasses. Mr. Ntuli asks Thembi to look out the window and tell him what she sees. “Oh, I see people and there is a small dog and there is a black bird on top of that house,” says Thembi excitedly. “Thembi,” says Mr. Ntuli, “I want you to promise me that you will wear your glasses every day.” “Oh, yes,” replied Thembi. “I promise. I love my new glasses. I love all the wonderful things I can see.” As Gogo and Thembi walk home, Thembi sees Sizani on the other side of the road. “Hi Sizani!” Thembi shouts. She waves at Sizani. Sizani smiles and waves back. Just before Gogo and Thembi reach their house, they meet some of Thembi’s school friends. “Oh Thembi, I love your new glasses,” says one girl. “They make you look really smart,” comments one of the boys. All of a sudden, a ball comes rolling towards Thembi. It is Bongani. Thembi quickly kicks the ball back. “Do you want to play?” asks Bongani. “Yes,” Thembi replies, “but first I have something very impotant to do.” Thembi walks behind the house and sits under the large tree. As she looks up, she can see the Kingfisher, the Cuckoo, and the Robin. “ Thank you, tree. Thank you for always singing to me.”
author: Alisha Berger

title: Save water
text: STORY ON "SAVING WATER" Santosh was a student of class 7. He was staying a village of Uttarakhand. In his village, there was a big pond. People of this village used the water of this pond for daily purposes. Almost all the houses took water/tap connection from the pond. The pond was big, so people used to use water carelessly. Santosh was very cleaver. He always said “water is very important”. He saved lots of water when he was using it. He tried to tell everyone to take care of water, but they didn’t care. Few months later, summer season came. People of the village started facing the problem of water scarcity. They had little water to drink, to prepare food, to wash with or even to use when they went to toilet. It was a big problem for them. During this time the villagers realised their mistake of ignoring the advice of Santosh. As the villagers were illiterate they approached him again. Santosh, said it is because of your ignorance you are facing this problem. Now you need to request the government for help and remember not to waste water again in life as it is very precious.
author: OMDEEP DAS

title: Clever Rabbit
text: It was evening. Cows, goats and sheep were returning to their sheds. The farmer made sure they all returned home safely. The clever Rabbit was awake inside his hutch. He was thinking, “I want to explore the outside world.” The other rabbits were dozing. The door to their hutch opened. The farmer came in. It was meal time for the rabbits. The food smelled nice. All the other rabbits were awake now. They hopped closer to the farmer. The clever Rabbit watched the farmer walk out the hutch. “Aha! Now I know how I can sneak out. Tomorrow I must get out of here.” “I’ll hop into the basket when the farmer brings in food,” the clever Rabbit thought. The other rabbits quickly finished their meal and fell asleep. In the morning, the farmer brought in food for the rabbits. “Today is the day,” the clever Rabbit thought to himself. “I must get out of this hutch.” As soon as the farmer put the basket down, the clever Rabbit quickly jumped in. No one saw him. After the farmer had fed the other rabbits, he carried the basket outside. The clever Rabbit was finally free! He sang to himself. He walked around like a king. Suddenly, a dog came up to the clever Rabbit and started barking at him. The clever Rabbit hadn’t thought of this danger. T he dog chased the clever Rabbit, who ran and ran and ran. The clever Rabbit just managed to outrun the dog. The clever Rabbit was now in the forest. He found some tender, sweet grass to eat. Food had never tasted so good back in the hutch. Full, he dozed off. The clever Rabbit was awakened by the loud roaring of a lion. “Ngrrrrr! Ngrrrr!” The sound was terribly scary. The lion was hungry. He chased the clever Rabbit. The c lever Rabbit ran for his life. “Will I escape alive?” he wondered. The clever Rabbit ran all night long. When it was daybreak, the clever Rabbit couldn't believe his eyes. He was back at the farmer's house! The door to the hutch was open. He saw the farmer feeding the other rabbits. The clever Rabbit snuck in behind the farmer. He was starving. He ate till he was full again. “I know better now. The outside world is sweet, but also bitter,” he told himself. From that day on, the clever Rabbit learned more and more about his world inside the farm. He even advised other rabbits on their issues!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Black Ant
text: This is Black Ant. Black Ant plays in the mud. Black Ant plays football. Black Ant wears shoes. Black Ant eats tomatoes. Black Ant meets Yellow Cat and they look at each other. Black Ant and Yellow Cat climb a tree. Yellow Cat falls down from the tree! Yellow Cat runs away. Black Ant climbs down the tree. Black Ant looks around the bush. The bush is on fire! Black Ant puts out the fire. Black Ant builds a house. Blue Elephant comes over to the house. Black Ant bites Blue Elephant. Blue Elephant falls down! Black Ant rests in the house.
author: Brian Kavanagh

title: The Peacock Who Wished to Fly
text: Peacock was a kind and gentle bird. He lived in peace with all the other birds. But Tausi had a dream. Instead of pecking at the ground, he wanted to fly to faraway lands. He wished he could see the all the beauty of nature for himself. But Tausi, the Peacock couldn’t even travel far in search for food. Some naughty birds mocked him. They left him alone whenever they went in search of food. Tausi the Peacock thought to himself, If I am a bird, then I should be able fly. Why don't I have wings like other birds? Tausi the Peacock thought hard. He decided that he would try to collect feathers from other birds. He crept up behind the Owl. He plucked a few feathers from her back without being noticed. The feathers were beautiful, long and dark. He did the same with the Parrot. He got beautiful green and yellow feathers. He stole feathers from many different birds. He even plucked feathers from Geese who were swimming in the river. The feathers were pretty and white. Tausi kept his feather-gathering a secret. Tausi, the Peacock even stole feathers from two Eagles while they were busy eating! By now he had collected a lot of beautiful feathers. He cleverly wove them together. He carefully fixed the feathers to his tail. When he stretched his tail, the feathers spread out like a fan. It was beautiful. The different colours made him look even more attractive. Now Tausi the Peacock was the most attractive bird in the village. None of the other birds had feathers as beautiful as Tausi, the Peacock. Tausi the Peacock was happy. As the most beautiful bird in the jungle, he no longer wanted to fly. Other birds didn’t mock or tease him any more. They were too busy admiring his beauty!
author: Alisha Berger

title: How the Tortoise Built Her House
text: Once upon a time, the tortoise had no shell. It was very difficult for her on hot, rainy, and cold days! She wished she could build herself a house. So, she started collecting materials. The tortoise moved quite slowly. She was never be able to collect enough tree branches to build a proper house. She sat down and thought about what to do. After thinking for a long time, she decided to go in search of a house that was already built. One day, she saw a cave. She peered inside. It looked warm and dry! But the cave belonged to a rabbit and her children. She climbed up a tree. But, she was chased away by birds chirping and cawing noisily in their nests. The tortoise walked away sadly, sweating in the heat of the sun. One day, as the tortoise was wandering about, she found a cow in its pen. She was with her calves. "Can I join you, please?" asked Tortoise. “I’m sorry,” said the cow, “but we can’t help you. It's full in here already.” As the tortoise left the pen, she passed under a tree. Drops of gum from the tree fell on her. The tortoise loved the cool feeling of gum sliding all over her back. Since it was quite hot, she stopped there for a while to rest. Her back got soaked with gum. As she walked away, she noticed a piece of tree-bark stuck to her back. It was stuck firmly in place. The tortoise picked up another piece of bark and placed it on her back. Then another piece, and another. She flipped on her back to press them firmly into place. When she walked in the hot sun, none of the pieces came off. She jumped into water and splashed around, cool at last. Best of all, the pieces remained firmly stuck to her back! Tortoise played in the sand. The pieces of bark remained stuck to her back. Now the tortoise felt comfortable, no matter what the weather. She was no longer afraid of the heat, rain, or cold. The pieces of bark remained stuck on her back forever. Finally, the tortoise had built her home. She carries it around proudly to this day!
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Adventures of Mboza and her Rooster
text: She traveled with her family to her grandma’s village. Mboza was quite excited about the trip. During each visit, her grandma would give her a special gift. She wondered what gift her grandma would give her this time! Mboza’s grandma was at the bus station to receive them. She welcomed them warmly. “Grandma, what gift are you giving me this time?” Mboza asked eagerly. Her grandma chuckled and said, “Be patient, Mboza. Wait until we get home.” When they got home her grandma smiled and said, “This time, I’ve not prepared a gift for you myself. You’ll have to get it on your own. See that rooster?” She pointed to a large, colourful rooster. “Mboza, if you catch it, it’s yours!" Grandma said. So, Mboza started to chase the rooster. She dived this way and that way, but the rooster kept outsmarting her. Mboza fell down with a CRASH! Everyone laughed at Mboza. Now, the rooster ran around even faster! Mboza got up. She wouldn't give up the chase! Next, the rooster ran straight into a thorny bush. Mboza found a long stick. “Kho! Kho! Kho!” cried the rooster as it buried into the bush. “Shiiih! Shiih!
