On days when she felt cross, her stinging tentacles kept the other creatures away. But today her rock felt lonely. “I have no fins. I have no feet. I am different to every other creature.” “Even that hermit crab is off having adventures!” “Save me! That fish wants to pluck me out of my shell!” Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee whipped up her stinging tentacles and hid the hermit underneath them. “Go away, you big bully!” The big fish bared his teeth, but was afraid of being stung. He gave up and swam away with a cheeky flick of his tail. “That was close!” said the crab. “Is it safe now?” “You can come out, Crab. What’s your name?” “Herman. I’m a hermit, but I think I need a bodyguard. I wish I was as brave as you!” “I’m Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee. I wish I had amazing adventures like you.” “But why don’t you?” He asked. “I’m stuck to my rock. And I don’t have legs!” She replied. “Well, I don’t have stings, but I do have an idea!” Herman took Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee by the tentacle and danced around her, pulling silly faces. First Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee snorted, and then she giggled — and then she laughed so hard she popped right off her rock. Herman gently picked her up and settled her on his shell. “Are you ready? I feel an adventure coming on.” He said. Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee adventures all over the ocean, catching tasty treats. Now she only uses her stinging tentacles to keep the nasty fish away from Herman. And she never, ever feels lonely. Photo credit: Prof. C.L. Griffiths
author: Matthew  Griffiths

title: The Conical Hat
text: I protect you from the sun. I protect you from the rain. I protect you from the wind. I am smaller than an umbrella. But I am bigger than a cap. People make me from cane. People make me from leaves. People don't make me too big, nor too small. I have a cone in the middle to help me stay on top of your head. If you rise, I rise. If you stoop, I stoop. I am the farmers’ hat. You can wear me as you tend the crops. You can wear me as you cross the stream. You can wear me when you play outside your home. But please do not run too fast or I might fall! Pleasant is my shade. Pleasant is my love. Always care for me and I will always love you.
author: Erica Cuellar

title: Meera and Ameera
text: Meera and I are a team. She’s my most favourite person in the world. Do you know why? She’s the only one who can see me! Everything she likes, I like. Everything I like, she likes. Our names also sound the same. Meera and Ameera! Things that happen to her happen to me too. “I lost another tooth,” Meera says. While I lost another quill. Sometimes, we can be a little different. Meera makes up problems. I make them go away. Like the other day when it was raining— “Oh no, now we can’t go out to play,” Meera cried. But I had an idea! Off we sailed on a paper boat. Or the time when she started school. “What if I don’t make any friends?” Meera was worried. “You made friends with me. Now go make one more friend,” I told her. It’s my turn to tell the story now. Ameera is my most favourite person in the world. Do you know why? She turns stuff upside down, just so I have a different view. Ameera never lets me walk into a fight alone. Even though she doesn’t help much. She makes every day a BIG adventure. Like the time we had to get out of a murukku maze. “I know! Let’s eat our way out,” Ameera said. Like Ameera said, we’re a team.
author: Nimmy Chacko

title: Whose House is This?
text: This house is mine.” Isn’t this also the house of the sparrow inside the terrace hole? Mother says, “This house is mine.” Isn’t this also the house of the common mynah on the roof? Grandma says, “This house is mine.” Isn't this also the house of the chicken in the coop? Grandpa says, “This house is mine.” Isn’t this also the house of the swallow on the top of the door? Uncle says, “This house is mine.” Isn’t this also the house of the pigeon on the branch? Aunty says, “This house is mine.” Isn’t this also the house of the bees in the hives? Brother says, “This house is mine.” Isn’t this also the house of the cat that chases the mouse? Sister says, “This house is mine.” Isn't this also the house of the cows in the shed? Everybody says, “This house is mine.” It is not only mine, but also ours! I say, “This house is mine, but also everybody else’s!”
author: Rose Larsen

title: Kuppu
text: Kuppu loved picking up little things from the floor. He would pick up the shiny red button from the garden. The piece of bright orange string under the staircase. The coin that had rolled behind the T.V stand. He would turn them in his hand and admire their beauty, before the black pebble lying on the floor caught his attention. But lately, Kuppu had started putting things into his mouth! One day he found a piece of biscuit on the floor and popped it into his mouth. “Hmmm....tasty and chewy” The next day, it was the Neem fruit that had fallen down inside the balcony. “Thoooo...bitter” It was immediately spit out. He was about to put a pebble into his mouth. “Nooooo...” cried Amma. “You should not put everything into your mouth Kuppu!” “Why not, Amma?” Kuppu loved asking questions. “Do you know what happened to Anjaneya when he tried putting everything into his mouth?” Kuppu loved Anjaneya. He wanted to know. He climbed on to his mother’s lap to hear the story. Anjaneya was a naughty child. He loved putting things into his mouth too! He would never listen to his mother when she told him not to do so. One day he saw the bright red sun in the sky. “Must be a tasty fruit, let me swallow it” thought Anjaneya. He started flying towards the sun. First like a kite, slowly and gracefully rising up. Then like the birds that came every evening and purposefully move in one direction. Finally fast and loud like the aeroplane that flies past the buildings everyday at great speed. He flew higher and higher, with his mouth open, all set to swallow the sun.. “Help....!” cried the Sun, who of course, did not want to be swallowed! “You cannot swallow everything, Baby Anjaneya” shouted Indra, who came to help the Sun. Indra was the king of the Devas. “Ha-ha...” laughed Anjaneya, as he moved closer to the Sun. Indra got very angry and threw the Vajrayudh in his hand at Anjaneya. It hit poor Baby Anjaneya in his face and Dhoooom, he fell down from the sky onto the ground, much like the mango fruit falling from the tree. His cheeks turned red and started growing bigger and bigger. Anjaneya‘s dad, Vayu rushed to his side and lifted the tiny Anjaneya in his arms. He was very angry at Indra for hurting the tiny child and started scolding him. Indra realized his mistake and used his powers to wake up Baby Anjaneya. But his cheeks remained swollen. “Look what happens when you try to put everything into your mouth, Anjaneya!” scolded his mother, while giving him a tight hug and a kiss.
author: Deepa Sundararajan

title: Rolly Olly - Brother and Sister short stories
text: Introduction Rolly is a brother bug. He likes to spin. Olly is a sister bug, and she likes to dance. They both like to play with blocks. They both like to eat pizza. Olly cries a lot. She cries when she cannot stack her blocks. Her brother, Rolly, helps and teaches her to slowly stack her blocks. Olly cries when her pizza is hot. Rolly cools his pizza and gives it to her. Olly finishes her pizza and says, “Thank you. I love you.” Rolly smiles and says, “You are the best”. Rolly Olly - School Story Rolly and Olly are standing at the bus stop to go to school. It is Olly’s first day of Kindergarten. Olly is too scared to go to school. Rolly comforts Olly, “School is fun. You will enjoy, learn and play.” Olly is sad and misses her toys. Rolly says, “You will make new friends and they will play with you. Besides, you will have me, your brother at school. We can meet during recess.” Olly shouts “Yay!” She looks smiles and says, “I am ready to go to school.” ”Happy School Time.” Rolly Olly - Bedtime story It is time for bed and Rolly wants to read a book. Rolly's sister, Olly, cannot sleep alone. She wants Rolly to help her go to sleep. Rolly narrates her a bug book. Olly enjoys the story, but she cannot sleep. Rolly makes a puppet story with Olly's toys. Olly smiles, but she cannot close her eyes. Rolly even dances wearing Olly's ballet dress! Olly laughs and claps but, she never yawns. Rolly is now too tired to even speak. Rolly crashes down and goes to sleep in Olly's bed. Olly is happy to have company. Olly looks at Rolly, smiles, and happily goes to sleep. ”Happy Sleeping.” Rolly Olly - Marching Game Rolly is busy reading a book in his room. His sister, Olly, is bored. She wants Rolly to play with her. Rolly puts his book aside and says, “Let’s play, Roaches Go Marching.” Olly is excited and shouts, “Yay!” Rolly says, “Roaches go marching one by one and suddenly stop to pick up a book.” Olly lifts the book and puts it on the shelf. Rolly says, “Roaches go marching one by one and suddenly stop to tie their shoes”. They bend down to tie their shoes. Rolly says,” Roaches go marching one by one and suddenly stop to exercise.” They exercise till their arms and legs ache. Rolly says, “Roaches go marching one by one and suddenly stop to take a rest.” They sit down and chat. They are tired. They look, smile and doze off. “Happy Sleeping.” Rolly Olly - Olly’s Tooth Rolly and his sister Olly, are sitting at a table eating breakfast. Suddenly, Olly yells in pain. “What is the matter?” asks Rolly. “It is my tooth. It hurts when I chew food and it is also wiggly,” says Olly. “I can help you by removing the bad tooth,” says Rolly. Olly is scared. Rolly promises Olly that he will be gentle, and will remove her tooth slowly. Rolly asks Olly to get a thread. He ties one end of the thread on Olly's wiggly tooth. Olly is scared, but she trusts Rolly. Holding one end of the thread, Rolly asks, “Are you ready?” Before Olly can ask a question, Rolly pulls the thread with all his might. Olly screams. She is angry. She then sees the wiggly tooth hanging on the thread. She feels much better. She looks, smiles, and says, “You are the best.” Rolly Olly - Pajama Party Rolly and Olly have friends at home for a pajama party. Olly had laid a new bed for her friends to sleep. She had her whole night planned. Olly’s two best friends are in her room dancing, eating and talking. Olly is too excited. Rolly and his friends are in his room talking. There are a few white clothes on top of Rolly’s bed. Suddenly the lights in Olly’s room go out. It is pitch dark. Olly yells, “Rolly, candles please.” Olly and her friends call for Rolly again. There is no response from Rolly. Olly yells, “Rolly, where are you?” Olly and her friends spot three scary figures through the windows in her room. They all shout,“Aahhhhh!”. Suddenly the lights in Olly’s room are on. Olly and her friends hear laughter sound from their room window. The scary figures remove their masks. They are none other than Rolly and his friends.Olly and her friends look and rush towards the window screaming, “We are going to get you.” “Happy Pajama Party.” Rolly Olly - Tik Tok, Tik Tok Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 6 O’Clock. Olly is awake. She brushes her teeth and showers. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 7 O’Clock. Olly is fixing her bed and setting her toys. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 8 O’Clock. Olly eats her breakfast and is ready to go to school. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 9 O’Clock. Olly is at school reading, writing and playing ball. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 3 O’Clock. Olly is home and is hungry for a snack. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 4 O’Clock. Olly is doing her homework and later reads her favorite book. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 7 O’Clock. Olly is eating her dinner and spending time with her family. Tik Tok, Tik Tok, it’s 9 O’Clock. Olly is in her bed, ready to sleep and dream pleasant dreams. Rolly Olly - Olly’s Fundraiser at School Olly is in second grade. She has a problem. She hiccups (ikk’s and ikk’s) like a sparrow. Olly, usually ikk’s when she is sad or mad. Olly is now in her classroom. She has hiccups. At first, her ikk’s are quiet, until it increases and the whole class hears it. Olly’s friends, sitting near her, close their ears. Everyday, Olly and her friends play games in the gym. Their school has limited school items to play during recess. Sometimes, a kid had to wait their turn to play. Olly suggests an idea, we can “Fundraise to buy more play items.” She explains to her friends that the word, “Fundraise” is to “raise money for a cause.” Olly, her friends, and their teacher speak with their school’s principal on their idea to fundraise for play items. They talk about planning and selling lemonade and candles as a means to fundraise. The Principal agrees. Lots of adults have come to support and buy their products. Together they collect enough money. Now they have play items for every kid to play and have fun. Olly realizes that her hiccups have stopped. She is now not too sad or mad. “Happy Playing.” Rolly Olly - Happy Thanksgiving It is Thanksgiving. Rolly and Olly are ready to spend the day celebrating. They make two beautiful cards, thanking Mommy and Daddy. They plant daffodil seedlings, thanking Mother Earth. Family time with mom and dad. They help mom and dad by making cranberry sauce to go with the feast. They say special thanks to Grandma and Grandpa. Rolly and Olly look at each other and say, “Thank you and Happy Thanksgiving!”. Rolly Olly - Mother’s Day Rolly wakes up early in the morning. It is “Mother’s Day.” Rolly goes to Olly’s room. He says, “Wake up. Its Mother’s Day.” They decide on the presents they will make together. “I will make a card,” says Olly. “I will make some breakfast,” says Rolly. Olly starts making a beautiful card with stickers and colors. Rolly toasts some bread. He spreads some peanut butter and jelly on the toast. He also warms some milk and places it on top of the tray.Olly places the card on the tray. Suddenly she realizes that something is amiss. Rolly sees Olly rush to her room. Olly places some colorful flowers on the tray. They themselves are a bit messy, but they are happy. They look, smile and greet each other, “Happy Mother’s Day.” Rolly Olly - Happy Christmas It is Christmas Eve. Olly is excited thinking about the snow, candy canes, presents, and parade. She thinks about Santa and ways to welcome him. Olly’s older brother, Rolly says, “Santa doesn’t give you presents, parents do.” Does Olly believe Rolly? Olly shouts, “No Way”. Olly had written a letter to Santa. She is sure that Santa will bring her the gift she had asked for in the letter. She makes her bed close to the Christmas tree and waits for Santa. She soon falls asleep. Rolly and Olly wake up early on Christmas morning. They look for their presents under the tree. Rolly and Olly are happy with their gifts. Olly gets exactly what she wants - A Pegasus toy. Olly goes for a Christmas parade with Rolly. She gets to sit with Santa and ride along with him. Olly looks and smiles thinking about the day’s events. “Happy Christmas.”
author: Gomathy S

title: Chintu and Milo
text: One day a sad dog was crying on the road. "Kuinnn Kuinnn", he cried. He had no home or friends. Chintu loved animals and felt bad for the dog. So, she brought him home. She named him M ilo and took care of him. Chintu's brother also played with him. Milo was very happy to have a home and kind friends. When Chintu and her brother went to school, Milo played on his own around the house. Living with them, Milo was very happy. "BOW BOW!!" he barked in joy. When all the other animals slept during the night, Milo stayed awake and guarded the house. He always protected his friends.
author: Surabhi Chatrapathy
illustrator: Alankrita Amaya; Deepa Balsavar; Henu; Jayesh Sivan; Santosh Pujari; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Forest Animals
text: Wow! Look at the giraffe,it's neck is veeeeeeeeeeeeeeery long. Hey, look hear the rabbit.How beautiful it is! Shhhhhhhhhhhhhhh! Don't make noise,There is a dangerous tiger coming towards us.Come let's run. Thank god! we escaped from the tiger. yeh! see here how the monkeys are jumping from tree to tree. There's coming an elephant it would have been good if we had a ride on it............awwwwnnnn Come on let's capture this moment. ohhhhhh no! but i forgot my camera Alarm................. trrrrrriiiiinnnnnngggggggg. oh no!it was only dream
author: Ash Rani
illustrator: Aliya Shetty Oza; Anant Shahane; Lakshmi Mitter; Olivia; Sanjay Sarkar; Santosh Pujari; Sorit Gupto

title: The Brave Rooster
text: There was a village long ago, where people smiled with a happy glow. In the village lived a boy and he had a pet Rooster. He was a good pet and his name was Booster. A giant monster scary and vicious, raided the village and acted pernicious. People screamed and ran hither-thither, the monster howled and growled with blither. The little boy and his pet Rooster tried to be brave, picked up his sword with vigor and rave. The giant growled and the little boy quivered. The monster crushed his sword and then the boy shivered. The pet with a pointy beak, flew with all his might. He pecked the monster’s eyes and was ready to fight. The monster ran screaming in pain, to never return to that village again. The entire village praised the Rooster, called him brave. They cheered and crowned him “Sir Booster” the great.
author: Gomathy S

title: Today, I went to the zoo
text: Today, I went to the Zoo and I saw Elephants. Elephants are Grey. Today, I went to the Zoo and I saw lions. Lions are orange. Today, I went to the Zoo and I saw Giraffes. Giraffes are yellow and brown. Today, I went to the Zoo and I saw Zebras. Zebras are black and white.
author: layna oliver

title: Richard's Bad Day
text: He had a shower but the water was cold so he came out of the shower straight away. He got dressed and had some breakfast but the breakfast was old and yuck. He got dressed and had some breakfast but the breakfast was old and yuck. Richard wanted to play with his toys but his sister Amy was taking all the toys and not sharing them so he told his mum that Amy was not sharing, but all she said was ''HUH'' Then at that moment he smelled something good and he saw his mum had made a very yummy cake. They really enjoyed it!
author: Amna  Singh
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Deepa Balsavar; Lavanya Karthik; Rijuta Ghate

title: Susheela loves to draw Rangolis
text: She is learning to put Rangoli from her mother. Every Pongal festival, susheela has permision to draw one Rangoli Susheela loves to draw Rangoli. She drew Rangoli on the floor, steps and walls. She also drew Rangoli on trains and tall buildings. She also drew Rangoli on flying kites. Anyone and Everyone who saw her Rangoli enjoyed viewing it. That night Susheela stood in her house terrace and saw the sky. Stars saw her and shone. Susheela then started thinking where to draw the next Rangoli. Every new day is welcomed by drawing a Rangoli in front of the house. Rangoli's bring good luck. Traditionally Rice Flour is used to put Rangoli.
author: Amna  Singh

title: Where has Neelima's father gone?
text: One night due to power cut the village was immersed in the darkness. Neelima's father had not come home from his farm.Neelima waited for him outside her house with a lantern. She heard a dim noise at a little distance so she moved a few steps forward to know what it was. Her pet pup Blacky also came out there. S uddenly Blacky charged toward a tree. In the meantime, Neelima's father arrived there. Neelima, her father, and her pet Blacky came home together. By this time electric supply of the village had also been restored.Neelima's mother cooked tasty food. All had dinner and went to bed.
author: Amna  Singh
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Gagan Visits Kamal
text: He walks through the streets with long strides. The city is crowded and very noisy. So much confusion, Kamal. Do not get into trouble. Kamal looks around before crossing the street. Once it's clear, Kamal goes ahead. Motorcycles rush by! Vroom! Vroom! Kamal sees a horse pulling a buggy. Thundering hooves! Kamal sees his friend Gagan through the crowd. Wow, Gagan! Hello, Gagan! Now, Kamal and Gagan walk home together.
author: Rose Larsen

title: The Soil
text: Look at the soil, my friend. The grass is so green here! This is where flowers bloom. They smell so sweet! This is where rice and wheat grow. This is where the potatoes and sweet potatoes grow! The soil is where the mud dauber builds its nest. A mud dauber is a type of wasp that makes nests out of mud. The swallow makes her nest out of soil too! She carries it in her beak. This is where the crocodile lays her eggs. And where the chameleon gives birth to her young. Look, my friend. This is where the horses and the elephants live. This is where the day breaks. This is where we play and dance. The soil is our life.
author: Shannon David

title: Miss Bandicota Bengalensis Enters  a Deep Dark Jungle
text: Meet Miss Bandicota Miss Bandicota Bengalensis was a little Indian mole rat who grew up in a maze of burrows with her mother, seven sisters and ten brothers. They were terrific pests, the nineteen of them, always out on a rampage. One night she was out foraging as usual, when managed to escape ever so barely from a farmer's dark and scary grasp. As she was fleeing, she glanced into the eyes of another mole-rat stuck in a rat-trap. Those were the saddest eyes she had ever seen. In the early hours of dawn she announced to everybody's dismay that she would never ever attack a farm again. “Whatever else can you do?” her mother had asked. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis had smiled simply and said, “I can burrow.” So once again she started digging anew – Every evening she woke up after the sun was down and packed her burrowing kit: her sunglasses, binoculars, magnifying glass and of course her favourite – a strip of sticker bandages. “An explorer is always prepared,” she said. And she burrowed and burrowed and burrowed and burrowed... But it was never a dull moment for her, for every burrow she dug, went to some place new. She had just emerged from a new burrow after a long night of digging through loads of crumbly rock and gravel. She was about to set her sunglasses in perfect balance, on top of her nose, just before the sun appeared, when it donned upon her that the world outside was pitch black. “ This can't be right, it must be morning by now,” she thought to herself, most bewildered by the strange dark world she had entered. It seemed to be a soft burrow of some sort, long and narrow, and it seemed to be squirming about itself! Miss Bandicota Bengalensis was beginning to get a bit alarmed as she couldn't seem to find her way out. She started wriggling in panick, when suddenly, “Aaaaachhoooooo!” A swift gust of moist air blew Miss Bandicota Bengalensis out into the morning light. As she struggled to get back on her feet she looked up in sheer astonishment – An elephant! “Whatever were you doing inside my trunk?” he asked, crouching back, a little annoyed. “I am quite sorry, Mr.... er... Mr....?” “Mr. Elephas Maximus Indicus,” the young elephant answered importantly. “Well, you see Mr. Elephas, I was just coming out of my burrow and surprisingly it seemed to go straight up your long long... Is that your nose?” “You mean my trunk, don't you? Well, I must apologise too, then. I was fiddling around with the dry leaves and didn't notice when I covered your hole. Are you new to the Jim Corbett jungles, Miss...?” “Miss Bandicota Bengalensis, I just arrived today. Did you say... jungles?” “Indeed, I did,” said Mr. Elephas theatrically. “Welcome to the most famous jungles of Uttarakhand, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis!” “Thank you,” replied Miss Bandicota Bengalensis excitedly. “Nothing like a new jungle to explore!” “Well, no visitor roams the Corbett jungles alone,” advised Mr. Elephas. “It is home to several tigers and ferocious leopards. You will most certainly need a guide,” he said seriously. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis looked back anxiously, “Do you know a guide, Mr. Elephas?” Mr. Elephas now, seemed mighty pleased. “But of course, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis! I'm the best guide you could find in the whole of Ramnagar,” he said, quite pompously. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis looked a bit uncertain. “Well, what are you waiting for? Hop on! And off we go!” announced Mr. Elephas, lowering his trunk to the ground. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis imagined for a brief moment an encounter with a ferocious leopard. She then looked back at Mr. Elephas again. He did look tough and strong, and above all tall, a safe bet in a wild jungle full of big cats. And so, she jumped onto Mr. Elephas, scurried up his trunk, over the top of his forehead, onto his wide, grey, leathery back, that towered over all. And what a grand ride it was! Mr. Elephas marched into the wilderness majestically, with a soft, rhythmic sway in his gait. A stony path led them through the early summer forest, dotted with oranges, reds and vermillion of flowering Palash trees. Seasonal streams crossed through the dry grasslands, some parched and some still flowing. A family of deers waded through the shallow waters for an early morning drink. A black-necked stork stood quietly in his pool of water. Through her binoculars, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis soaked in the everyday scene of a jungle sunrise. Down the road, she spotted the most peculiar looking mud castles, scattered here and there. They had strange pointy peaks, some even higher than the grasses. “Whose house is that?” she asked, pointing inquisitively, to the closest mud hill. For as you might already know, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis could never resist asking a question! “That's a termite hill. I've seen some that are even taller than the trees,” replied Mr. Elephas. “Do you know how they build them?” asked Miss Bandicota Bengalensis yet again. And Mr. Elephas, the very wise guide, rambled on knowledgably, happy to answer Miss Bandicota Bengalensis question after question... Soon they found themselves surrounded by dense rows of Sal trees, standing tall and firm, holding on to the last leaves of the season. The rays of the sun sparkled brightly through the yellows, browns and greens of the sal leaves. Sun beams shone in and out through the tree trunks, playing a magical game of hide and seek. Mr. Elephas slowed down to marvel at the enticing play of sunlit colours. “Sunny leaves make me happy,” he remarked simply. For once, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis didn't ask any question. And they moved on quietly, through the enchanted jungle of sal trees. As the sun grew hotter, Mr. Elephas wandered out of the official Corbett boundries, round a tiny village and approached the banks of the mighty Kosi River. “Hold on tight, now!” he said and slowly but steadily, he walked into the river waters. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis watched in awe as Mr. Elephas treaded firmly over the river bed. The watercourse had dropped low with the summer heat but the currents were still strong. A school of shining golden Mahseer fish swam swiftly by them. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis looked down into the Kosi waters longingly “If only I could swim,” she sighed. “Whoooooooooosh!” a sudden splash of cold water drenched Miss Bandicota Bengalensis from head to toe. She looked up at the clouds puzzled and then down at Mr. Elephas. There he was, drawing from the river into his trunk and spraying fountains of water in the air, as he crossed the Kosi. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis drank in some of the fresh water as Mr. Elephas playfully sprinkled her with more. Pleased with their cool showers, Mr. Elephas then ambled into a leafy cluster of bamboos. The afternoon was hot and lazy and Miss Bandicota Bengalensis lolled into a gentle snooze. Mr. Elephas went about with the day's meal, plucking through grasses, shrubs and trees. A soft nudge shook Miss Bandicota Bengalensis out of her long nap. “Come along now, it's time for the tigers to go on hunt. Remember, you must be as quiet as you can.” Miss Bandicota Bengalensis wasn't really sure she wanted to meet a tiger, but she climbed on to Mr. Elephas respectfully. The sun had begun to set and the dusky sky cast long dark shadows on the ground. Bones of a deer from a previous hunt lay abandoned by the river banks. Mr. Elephas entered into a thicket of tall shrubs, so dense that Miss Bandicota Bengalensis could no longer see the ground. She had to clear away the branches that grew higher up to guard her eyes. As sheaves of wild curry leaves fell upon her, a fresh forest aroma began to make her mouth water. To her delight, a clump of Ber trees spread its thorny branches before her, loaded, with hundreds of the little round fruit, deep orange in colour, ripe and beckoning. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis picked carefully, so that she didn't scratch herself. As she was greedily gobbling the sweet and sour ber, without warning a large herd of Sambar deer appeared silently from inside the bushes. There was a moment of quiet unease. Mr. Elephas stopped in his tracks. The Sambars looked towards their left all at once, and froze. A waft of pungent odour floated by. In a single breath, the Sambars had vanished into the dark jungle again. “Do you smell the tiger?” asked Mr. Elephas in a hushed tone. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis clutched on hard to Mr. Elephas, as he turned to follow the scent. A few steps ahead, surely enough, they had reached a tiger track. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis stared in disbelief as Mr. Elephas joined the tiger trail, winding through the deep woods, near and around the water hole. As the woods began to clear, Mr. Elephas stopped to examine the track which seemed to get more jumbled. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis peered down to help. The both of them gasped, as they began to realise that it was not one but two tiger tracks they were following. Down below in the soft white sand, they could now see pugmarks more conspicuously. Some were big and some were much smaller, as if walking close together. “I must have a look through my magnifying glass” pleaded Miss Bandicota Bengalensis in a low whisper. But Mr. Elephas would not allow it. “It seems to be a mother and her cub. It's much too dangerous to stop here” As he walked ahead a loud and resounding growl filled the jungle air with fear. An eerie silence followed. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis felt a sharp chill down her spine. Mr. Elephas marched on undaunted, till the tiger trail disappeared, the tree cover cleared completely and they were back to safety on the river banks. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis heaved a sigh of relief and thanked Mr. Elephas for his courage. “Oh! You don't need to thank me,” replied Mr. Elephas. “No one messes with a tigress protecting her little one, not even a brave elephant like me.” Even as she was glad to have escaped from the tigress, Miss Bandicota Bengalensis regretted not having been able to inspect the jungle a little more closely. If you went for a walk in Himalayan jungles could you spot some of the animals that Miss Bandicota Bengalensis may have missed out on her adventure? The night sky had now descended upon the Kosi river valley. As they returned from their adventure in the deep dark jungle, Mr. Elephas called up to Miss Bandicota Bengalensis affectionately. “My friend, I must get back to my mother and sisters now. Would you like to meet them?” he invited. Miss Bandicota Bengalensis would have loved another ride atop her new friend, but there was simply no time left... “Tonight, I must dig a new burrow...”
author: Aditi Ghosh
illustrator: Barkha Lohia; Deepa Balsavar; Greystroke; Kavita Singh Kale; Muhammed Shafi; Niloufer Wadia; Nimret Handa; Rohan Chakravarty; Ruchi Shah; Sangeetha Kadur; Sanjay Sarkar; Sunaina  Coelho; Thummarat Phromphing; Vallabhi   Shegaonkar; Vinayak Varma; Vishnu  M Nair

title: Rabbit Goes on a Quest
text: I am safe,” said Rabbit. “Someone has attacked the forest! I must tell the king!” said Rabbit. “Are you the king?” asked Rabbit. “No, I am not the king,” said Rooster. “Someone has attacked us! I must tell the king,” said Rabbit. “Well then, I will go with you,” said Rooster. “Are you the king?” asked Rabbit and Rooster. “No, I am not the king,” said Emu. “Someone has attacked us! We are going to tell the king,” said Rabbit. “Well then, I will go with you,” said Emu. “Are you the king?” asked Rabbit and Rooster and Emu. “No, I am not the king,” said Hippo. “Someone has attacked us. We are going to tell the king,” said Rabbit. “Well then, I will go with you,” said Hippo. “Are you the king?” asked Rabbit and Rooster and Emu and Hippo. “No, I am not the king,” said Gorilla. “The king is inside.” “Wait! So… this was not an attack?” Rabbit asked. “Some of my arrows missed their mark,” the king said. “Oops!”
author: Brian Kavanagh

title: My First Day at School
text: I am six years old. I am a new student at Manyinga Primary School. My first day at school was exciting. I got up early in the morning. My father took me to school. On the way there were many other students. Some were with their parents. I heard the bell ringing, “Gong! Gong! Gong!” Other students started running. Each student took his or her place in a line. I ran and joined the others. When I looked at the other students, I felt very small. They seemed much older than me. An older girl took me by the hand to where students of my age were gathered. I was with the wrong class! As I stood in line with the students my age, I heard someone yell, “Madam, this boy has wet his shorts!” We all turned back. I saw a little boy holding his shorts, looking sad. Both his legs were wet. His eyes were wet with tears. An older boy came and took him by the hand to get help. Then a teacher showed us our classroom. It was large and clean. One student came in late. He was holding his shoes. The teacher asked why. He said that his mother had taught him to always take off his shoes before stepping into a room. We all laughed. The bell rang again, “Gong! Gong! Gong!” We rushed outside and stood in lines. A teacher came to us and told us that it was break time. There was no need to stand in lines. It was time to play! After a short while, the bell rang again. All other students were rushing into their classrooms. I was confused, I did not know where to go. I had forgotten my classroom! I saw a classroom in front of me and stepped inside. Two other students followed me. None of us knew where to go. One of the students who was with me started crying. An older girl asked him what was wrong. He replied that he wanted to see his mother. Some of the other students laughed, but some wanted to help. One of the older girls took us to our classroom. Our teacher told us that soon it would be time to go home, and we should wait for our parents to pick us up from the classroom. The bell rang again, “Gong! Gong! Gong!” We were happy to see our parents waiting for us outside. After dinner, my father and mother asked me what my day at school had been like. I told them about how we lost our classroom. They laughed and said I should listen carefully to the teachers. That night, I couldn't sleep. The night was long and I was eager to start my second day of school.
author: Shannon David

title: Oh! My Creator!
text: DO YOU KNOW WHO AM I? MY DEAR CHELLAMS! Yes, your guess is correct. How many times have you tried to catch me? we are about 15000 and 20000 different species. can you believe this? Our CREATOR created us in an unique way. I am the" symbol of resurrection!". Do you know this? I love nectar of the flowers because I want to be so sweet like my CREATOR! you can see me and my friends during daytime, in gardens and forests. our brothers MOTHS are brown and some times colorless. But very active in night time. Flowers are fond of my kisses. I never give up my tries. I am in the hands of my CREATOR,who feeds me,cares me,engraves me in HIS PALM! I am not afraid,because I know there is a purpose in my life. ARE YOU AFRAID? MY CHELLAMS! DO YOU FEEL HOPELESS? CAN'T YOU STUDY WELL? ARE YOU A FAILURE IN ALL OF YOUR WORKS? MY ANSWER IS NEVER GIVE UP LIKE ME....TRY TO BREAK YOUR COCOONS FIRST! I always sing a song while i fly......can you sing with me?? THOUGH I am small and frail MY CREATOR IS ALMIGHTY!!!!!! May be i am helpless, He is always helpful..... so Nothing is impossible to me, Nothing is impossible to YOU! work hard every day, thank God every body! Nothing is impossible to You! oh! it's time for me to touch the sky and bring the wishes from heaven to the Earth. So many flowers will be waiting for my smile in their garden. This life is too short but make every moments a beautiful start to make, the hopeless to get HOPE! the helpless to get the HELP, the coward to be the BRAVE, the cruel to give LOVE........ because life is short..... but YOU ARE THE SMARTEST IN MY CREATOR'S CREATION!!!!!!! LOVE, LIVE,AND ALWAYS GIVE....... Don't forget this...... " you too have a unique purpose in GOD's plan". WITH LOVE, your butterfly.
author: KARPAGA LAKSHMI MOHAN

title: The Fish that Couldn't Swim
text: There once was a boy who could run and jump and climb. He could even make a noise like a seagull. But he couldn’t swim. And oh, how he wanted to. Then one day...... he noticed a fish that couldn't swim either. He wanted to help the fish. So he put it in the water...... and the fish came alive! But the boy also wanted to learn to swim. So the fish showed the boy how to put his mouth in the water and blow. What fun they had! The next day, the boy remembered what the fish had taught him. And so the boy who could run and jump and climb, and even make a noise like a seagull, learned to swim like a fish.
author: Sarah  Gaylard

title: Sakadang Hileud Loba Gaya
text: Beja pabeja-beja. Cenah, Sakadang Papatong ngayakeun pesta di kebon. "Hayu urang indit ka ditu!" ceuk Sakadang Sireum ka baladna, nyaeta Sakadang Hileud jeung Sakadang Bangbung. "Hayu!" ceuk Sakadang Bangbung sumanget pisan. "Kela," ceuk Sakadang Hileud. "Maenya indit ka pesta teu dangdan heula? Tingali, kuring ukur make sapatu nu pulasna kulawu butut." "Teu nanaon atuh. Tempo, kuring mah teu disapatu-disapatu acan!" ceuk Sakadang Sireum. "Nu penting mah urang datang ka pesta, pikeun ngahurmat babaturan urang Sakadang Papatong!" Tapi Sakadang Hileud teu ngadenge omongan Sakadang Sireum. Manehna hayang kapuji minangka sato nu panggayana. Sakadang Hileud gagancangan balik ka imah, tuluy muka lomari. Bray. Ambuing... Sanggeus sakabeh sapatuna dipake, Sakadang Hileud balik deui ka tempat tadi. Kedepruk. Kedepruk. Ti kajauhan keneh sora sapatuna geus kadenge. "Tenjo. Hade, pan? Kuring tea, sato panggayana di kebon!" ceuk Sakadang Hileud ka Sakadang Bangbung, agul pisan. Kedepruk. Kedepruk. Kedepruk. Sora sapatu minuhan kebon. "Sora naon eta?" tanya Sakadang Congcorang. "Teuing atuh," tembal Sakadang Lancah. "Wah, bahaya..." "Aduh! Naha bet make sapatu nu kekedeprukan kitu?" ceuk Sakadang Papatong bangun reuwas nempo Sakadang Hileud. "Naha ulah kitu?" tanya Sakadang Hileud. "Kumaha mun sora sapatu anjeun kanyahoan ku Sakadang Manuk?" "Lamun Sakadang Manuk nyahoeun urang keur ngarumpul di dieu, tangtu cilaka. Urang sarerea bisa dihakan!" Sakadang Hileud colohok. Manehna teu nyangka yen kalakuan loba gaya jeung hayang katangar teh bisa nyilakakeun babaturanana. Pesta kebon dibolaykeun. Sakadang Hileud balik ka imahna bari kaduhung. Ti harita, manehna teu hayang katangar, tara loba gaya deui.
author: ED Jenura

title: Where is Lulu?
text: “Oh, no!” “Lulu! It’s time to go,” calls Ma. Where is Lulu? Is she under the sofa? Is she behind the curtain? Where is Lulu? Is she next to the stove? Is she in the cupboard? “Lulu! It’s time to go. Where are you?” calls Ma. “There you are!” “I don’t want to gooo!” “We have to go,” says Ma. “But I really like this one!” “I really like this one!” “And this one.” “And this one.” “And this one.” “See? You return books and borrow more.” “YAY!” Where is Lulu now?
author: Clyde   Beech; Mohale  Mashigo; Nkosingiphile  Mazibuko

title: Tina and the Stars
text: One evening, Tina was sitting outside with her father. She looked at the sky. She could see the bright stars twinkling. “Dad, the stars look like sparkling butterflies. How lovely they are!" Tina sighed. “Dad, I want the stars. Will you buy me some?” Tina's father laughed. “Ooh! Tina. The stars are not for sale. They can only be found up there in the sky,” her father told her. “So, will you go up there someday to get them for me?” Tina asked. “Wait patiently, Tina. I’ll find you the stars.” “Ooh! Okay." Tina paused. " Friday is close to Saturday, isn’t it?” “Yes,” Tina’s father responded. “Friday is close to Saturday. These days come one after the other.” "Can you look for the stars on Saturday, Dad?" Tina asked. Tina's father was quiet. So was Tina. Then she said, “When I grow up, I’ll go and get the stars.” The two laughed and went back in the house. Tina was playing. Suddenly, an angel appeared. The angel was shining brightly. He shone like the stars. Tina smiled and asked, “Can I become an angel too?” The angel just laughed, lightly. “Tina, you’re very curious girl. Why do you ask?” “I love the stars. They amaze me. I wish I could fly up close to them. They twinkle and I’m happy when I look at them,” said Tina. “I’ll give you wings,” the angel said. Then the angel touched Tina on her back. Wings sprouted from her shoulders! “Thank you very much!" Tina called. The angel had disappeared. Tina raised her head. I can’t go on my own to pluck the stars from the sky, she thought. She then shouted to the stars, “Hey, dear Stars, I’m coming to get you.” The stars showed that they had heard her. They shone even brighter. A pigeon was passing by, she heard Tina calling out to the stars. She followed Tina. “Are you talking to the stars?” she asked her. “Yes! And I’m looking for a friend to accompany me into the sky.” “I will go with you,” the Pigeon said. Then, together they flew up, up, and up. They flapped their wings. They traveled until they reached the gates of heaven. They found an old guard. "Can we come inside?" they asked. The old guard said, “Whoever manages to answer my question will have permission to step inside. Okay?” “Okay,” Tina and the pigeon responded. “If you add one star to four other stars, how many do you get?” the guard asked. “The answer is five stars,” Tina responded quickly. Tina worked hard at school. She liked all the subjects. But she loved maths best. The guard was impressed. He told her, “That's right! Go inside, but take no more than five stars each.” Tina and her friend the pigeon selected five big stars each. Tina wanted to give one to her dad, another to her mom, another to her brother, and another to her friend, Fatuma. Her fifth star, she would keep for herself. Was it all a dream? It felt real to Tina. As she slept, her face shone with a smile. One hand was closed in a tight fist, as if she was holding stars. Tina laughed a bit in her sleep. Her parents went into the room to make sure she was OK. Tina's mother kissed her on the forehead. A week later, Tina's father father brought her a surprise. Two toy stars! Inside the stars were miniature lights. They shone and twinkled. They gave out very beautiful light. Tina loved them! She placed two stars in her room. She couldn't wait to fall asleep and share them with her friend pigeon.
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Crown
text: Where is my crown?" I asked the rooster for his crown. Shaking his head the rooster said, “No, I will not give you my red crown.” The multi-colored peacock has a blue crown. "Where is my crown?" I asked the peacock for his crown. Shaking his head the peacock said, “No, I will not give you my blue crown.” The white crane has a white crown. "Where is my crown?" I asked the crane for her crown. Shaking her head the crane said, “No, I will not give you my white crown.” “Enough, rooster, enough!” “Enough, peacock, enough!” “Enough, crane, enough! I will not take your crowns.” “I don’t need anyone else’s crown. I will wear my own crown!”
author: Brian Kavanagh

title: The Story Of Beluga Whales
text: Contents What Do Belugas Do Why Are Belugas Different Why Do Belugas Use Ecolocation FAQ Index Thank You/Sources Websites What Do Belugas Do Beluga whales are opportunistic feeders. They prey on about 100 different kinds of primarily bottom-dwelling animals. They eat octopus; squid; crabs; snails; sandworms; and fishes such as capelin, cod, herring, smelt, and flounder. How Are Other Whales Different From Belugas Part I •Other whales are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals. They are an informal grouping within the infraorder Cetacea, usually excluding dolphins and porpoises. Whales, dolphins and porpoises belong to the order Cetartiodactyla with even-toed ungulates and their closest living relatives are the hippopotamuses, having diverged about 40 million years ago. The two parvorders of whales, baleen whales (Mysticeti) and toothed whales (Odontoceti), are thought to have split apart around 34 million years ago. The whales comprise eight extant families: Balaenopteridae (the rorquals), Balaenidae (right whales), Cetotheriidae (the pygmy right whale), Eschrichtiidae (the grey whale), Monodontidae (belugas and narwhals), Physeteridae (the sperm whale), Kogiidae(the dwarf and pygmy sperm whale), and Ziphiidae (the beaked whales). How Are Belugas Different From Other Whales Part II Belugas have thick, muscular bodies that taper at both ends. Their round heads have a small beak, and their necks are narrower than other whales. Unlike otherwhales, their neck vertebrae are not fused, allowing them to move their heads up and down and from side to side, according to the American Cetacean Society Why Do Belugas Use Echolocation "Sound to them is like eyes to us," says Vergara. Like other toothed whales and many bats, they use echolocation: they make a rapid string of clicks that bounce back from the environment, and interpret the echoes to identify objects such as food. Belugasmake all these sounds despite having no vocal cords. title: Mother Hen
text: This is Mother Hen. She wants to throw a party for her chicks. Mother Hen wants to go to the market to buy bread and fruits for the party. However, she is scared to go alone. Mother Hen asks Duck to go with her, but she refuses. Mother Hen asks Cat if she wants to go to the market. Cat is too lazy and will not go. Mother Hen asks Goat if she can go to the market. Goat also refuses. Mother Hen asks Rooster to look after her chicks. Mother Hen decides to go to the market alone. On the way, she sees Wild Dogs. The Wild Dogs chase Mother Hen. title: Tine and the Faraway Mountain
text: “I completely let go of fear. Fear of norms and fear of society. I was neither afraid of failure, nor dying. I believed in my own strengths and nurtured my natural talent. I improved my weaknesses. And above all, I always followed my heart” —Tine Mena, mountaineer Today is a big day for Tine Mena. At the age of 25, she has become the first woman from Northeast India to climb Everest. At 8,848 metres, Everest is the highest mountain in the world. It’s as high as five thousand men (who are six feet tall) standing on top of each other! This is the story of Tine’s journey, a girl who loves to climb mountains. Whooshoo! Whooshoo! In the Mishmi hills of Arunachal Pradesh, Tine heard a wondrous call from the distant mountains. She was drawn to it, a sound only she could hear. Tine loved to climb. She climbed trees, ran through the jungle and went fishing in the river. She was as fearless and strong as Naaya, her grandmother. If Tine fell down, Naaba, her father, would tell her to get up and carry on. Tine and her younger sister Sony loved eating apples, oranges, and berries from the forest. They spent long days lying under the sun. Ah, Tine would smile, what a wonderful life! But one day, Tine’s world turned upside down. There was no school in Echali, so her family moved to the closest big town, Roing. There, the ‘Whooshoo’ became a faint whisper. All she wanted was to be in the mountains. Ten years later, Tine finished school. The mountain call was strong again - whoshooo, whoshooo. To be close to her mountains, Tine applied to be a porter for an army expedition. She could carry heavy loads and march for days, shoulder to shoulder with others. But there was one small problem—women were not allowed to be porters. But did that stop her? Of course it didn’t! Tine dressed as a boy and began working. She’d carry nearly 25 kilos every day. It took a week for everyone to realise that she was a girl disguised as a boy! Tine was scolded for breaking the rules. But she could work as much as the boys and knew the route better than anyone. So the officers agreed to let her continue working. Her act would later help lift the ban on female porters. Tine worked hard and became a coordinator, someone who plans mountain trips. That’s when she met Dr. Romeo Meitei, the leader of an expedition. “I must say that you have all the makings of a naturally gifted climber,” he said. “You have the build, the strength, and the determination. Now all you need, is technique.” Dr. Meitei became her mentor and Tine began her training. But it was when Tine saw The Race for Everest, a film about the first climb of Mount Everest, that she heard about her dream mountain. The Whooshoo became a roar. Climbing Mount Everest became Tine’s dream. Finally, Tine left for Nepal. She was anxious, but determined. At the Everest base camp, it was cold and the air, thin. After her training, Tine began her climb with Cherring Sherpa*. The climb was divided into four sections so climbers could rest at different camping points and continue to the top over a few days. By the time Tine and Cherring Sherpa reached the second camp, the weather had worsened. *Sherpas are a Tibetan ethnic group living in high Himalayan regions who are known for their climbing skills. But the musical Whooooshooing was also growing louder and hypnotic! “Do you want to go ahead?” Cherring asked. “I don’t think I will get another chance to do this,” Tine said. Somehow, they reached their final camp. But the wind blew their tent and supplies away. They found another tent in which they took shelter. No walkie-talkies, no medicines, all Tine and Cherring had was a packet of noodles. “Let’s share half of it,” Cherring suggested. “If we make it alive, we will eat the other half,” Tine said with a determined smile. For every two steps they took, the wind sent them reeling back a step. The stormy winds howled, “Go awayyyyy”. But Tine could only hear “Whoooshoooo”. With new resolve, they fearlessly began the last push to reach the top. At 10.45 am on May 9, 2011, Tine summited the highest mountain in the world. The young girl who loved to climb trees had climbed to the top of the world. She had found her faraway mountain, and was one with the sound that had called her all her life. Whoooshoo, she dances with her beloved mountain. Tine Mena, the mountaineer Tine Mena is an adventurer who holds the distinction of being the first female Everester from Northeast India. At Dr. Romeo Meitei’s suggestion, Tine enrolled at the Manipur Mountaineering and Training Association in Imphal. She won a gold medal at the course and another for best student of the basic mountaineering course at the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute in Darjeeling. Tine turned down a well-paid job as a mountaineering instructor to chase her Everest dream. She raised private sponsorship for her expedition. Tine has inspired many youngsters in the northeast, starting with her cousin Ruby Lombo, a cycling athlete. Tine continues to be a role model for adventurous children.
author: Shikha Tripathi

title: Little Sisters

title: Come back my babies.
text: Once upon a time,in Dalhousie,Himachal Pradesh, there lived three little girls named Meenu,Neetu and Raja.They used to play and had a lot of fun together. They used to play in the snow. They had fun climbing trees........ They enjoyed eating fresh fruits plucked from the trees...... Admiring nature,enjoying running around and exploring new things in the jungle. Playing hide and seek......... Sliding down the mountain and tearing off their clothes......... One fine morning, the weather was pleasant for playing.So they decided not to go to school that day. Meenu said-‘’Mom, I am not feeling well. I think I have fever.’’ Mom replied touching her forehead-‘’No, my dear. Just go to school. You don’t have any fever.’’ Now it was Neetu’s turn to make an excuse-‘’Mom, I fell from my bicycle and got hurt.So I don’t feel like going to school.’’ Raja added-‘’ If they both are not going,how can I go alone!’’ Mom yelled-‘’Don’t make excuses. Just get ready for school.The school bus must be coming. ‘’ With a sad face,three of them got ready and headed slowly towards the bus stop. They deliberately left the bus but in their back of mind they had a fear of their mom. So they ran away from there and reached on the top of a hill and started playing with mud. They got so engrossed in their play that they forgot to go home. Meanwhile at home,Mom got worried when her daughters did not return home after school. She called her husband and he called the Police.They started searching for the girls. Everyone in the town started searching for them, but could not find. Worried mother kept searching for her daughters-‘’Meenu.........., Neetu........Raja...........,where are you?Come back my babies........” At last they came running home and found their mom in tears.They got scolded by everyone in their house and school too. And they promised their parents that they will not go anywhere alone without them.
author: Vasudha Sharma

title: Oompalini -  The Sneaky Little Lizard
text: It was night. And there was an orange glow in the dark... It was spinning around in different directions! There lived in Mrs Maisie's Garden, besides her dog and cat and the busy birds and butterflies, a very sneaky little lizard called Oompalini. Yes, the orange glow was from Oompalini's back! He was sleek,slender, stealthy and charismatic, often a loner and a show off! At night, he would often curl himself up into a ball and roll around the garden on his spine like a yo-yo. Buster, the dog and Petrissia,the cat often got tricked and mistook him for a rolling ball that disappeared and reappeared.It caught their attention most of the time and was a source of playful distraction. Oompalini's resting place was a bed of damp soil on a barren pot in Mrs Maisie's garden. He would often hide behind the pot and watch the ongoing's in the garden The garden was a beautiful one. Mrs Maisie attended to it with love and care and a lot of hard work. She would often be seen working with a pair of gloves, garden scissors and a hat, clipping upon the cluster roses or shaping the golden leaved bushes. Frogs plopped in and out of the miniature lotus pond, sticking their tongue out at the sight of a fly. Dragonflies whizzed in the air in circles and a number of birds and butterflies flew about from flower to flower often feeding upon the fresh morning dew and flower-honey. By noon however, all the garden beings sheltered from the sun in the bushes and potted plants or went for a swim in the pond. One afternoon, Oompalini chanced upon Mrs Maisie carrying what appeared to be two large food bowls. Of-course, it was for Buster and Petrissia whom she pampered very much. The waft of freshly baked butter filled mini-buns and parsley-pumpkin soup filled the air. Oompa was tired of having to hunt flies and insects everyday. He wanted a different taste too and food to be given on his platter. The aroma from the food bowl kindled his lizardy senses and he craved this new delicacy. Mrs Maisie placed the food in front of Busters kennel and Petrissias basket. She called out to them with a swift but long whistle, hoping they would come soon finishing off their daily snooping abouts! Seeing no sign of them returning, she walked back into her house relieved to finish off her morning duties. Oompa stealthily made his way to the food-bowls propelled by his taste buds, his slimy mouth dripping with saliva. He sniffed about the food bowls for a good while, allowing the aroma to transport him into lizardy dreams, one that involved feasting with the most beautiful lizardly queen. Soon though, he came back to his senses. Petrissia's bowl had fish and chips. And he thought 'OOh yummy!' He plunged into the pumpkin soup, the bowl being the size of a round swimming pool and loudly slurped up the liquid, coming up to the surface in-between intervals of drinking to have a breath of fresh air.He then moved on to the mini buns which he rode on thinking smugly to himself 'Im a rider on this wild Mexican bull. Giddy up Bunny Bun!' Once he finished riding it, he dug into the buns with big chunky bites and chipped off their edges for most of its parts. Oompa ate to his hearts content and then when he was half full, he quickly jumped out and made his way to Petrissia's bowl. Fish and chips!! He crunched and munched and chomp, chomp, chomped it all up! He ate the fish, a sea creature that was obviously larger than him, by making his way up from the tail until the middle, leaving the spine exposed. He was so stuffed that his belly bloated up like a balloon and his cheeks bulged out exposing their rosy red color. He found it hard to scuttle back to his bed over the pot. He dragged himself little by little all the while burping out strange gases and making funny grunting sounds until he collapsed on his damp but cozy soil bed. Elated and and over the moon, Oompa fell into a deep slumber. He slept for three days and nights not knowing when the Sun arose or set. Unable to sleep on his belly, he dozed upon his back. Luckily, he escaped notice by Buster or Petrissia or the garden beings. The color of his skin camouflaged him to the pots mud. Meanwhile, Buster and Petrissia had gone on a long walk to the lake with Mr Williams. They returned excited to have steaming hot food prepared by Mrs Maisie, but were met with dismay at the sight of half eaten and left over food bowls. Anger, a sense of betrayal and revenge coursed through Buster's face along with a sense of animate curiosity as to who could be the perpetrator that stole their food. Petrissia was more complacent and had a look of surprise intermixed with dumb wonder. A theft had never before occurred in their garden! Buster immediately began the hunt for the thief. Bits and pieces of chips were strewn around the bowls. They began to search by following the trail of smell. Sniffing and snooping high and low, hither and thither, East and West, North and south, Buster busied himself like a poacher out to hunt in search of his target. Petrissia was softer, she often purred in discontent and cried tears quietly when she was tired of looking for the notorious thief. She had looked inside of Mrs Maisie's house where she could easily slip in and out. In she went through the pet door, into the kitchen, inside the drawers, under the bed, over the table, out through the fence, over the roof and trees, striding upon the pipeline, down through the chimney hole, and so on and so forth. She would often come back to the food bowl and nibble upon the left overs in hunger and disappointment. Buster was different and he hadn't touched the food once it was eaten, nor had he eaten food that was given to him by Mrs Maisie until he had found the trespasser. Angrily he looked in the corners of the garden, under the bushes, among the leaves, huffing and puffing, panting and barking. Occasionally he would lap up water from the pond when he was thirsty, tired from all his searching, but he would continue to keep one eye out cautiously for the thief incase he was inside the water too. This went on for 3 and a half days They inquired about the theft with the garden Squirrels, humming birds, Mr grasshopper and Ladybug, and of-course the butterflies. But every single one of them claimed to be innocent or not having seen the gluttony food thief. On the afternoon of the fourth day, Mrs Maisie now refilled their bowls with fresh food, warm rosemary potato wedges, herby cheese bruschettas and some cooling lemon juice. This time they made it a point to be right there when Mrs Maisie was serving them. Busters eye's were wide open and bulging, if by chance the thief would steal again, as he was speedily gobbling up his food and gulping his lemon juice. Oompalini woke up on the afternoon of the 4th day. His belly was back in shape and he rolled over pleased to feel the damp soil. He strolled about for sometime and took a swim in the pond and enjoyed the afternoon rain showers as it poured over him. The smell of rain on the earth reminded him of his childhood and moments that seem to be so quickly passing by. He later lay at the edge of the pond under a mushroom to shelter from the rain. His webbed hands interlocked behind his head, slender body leaning against the stalk while his right leg folded over the left, his body assuming a relaxed position until the sun set. He remain undisturbed until Buster and Petrissia arose at Dusk. Unassuming of the danger ahead of him, he began to curl himself into a ball and roll on his back. The glow on his back was a mild orange fade. He rolled and rolled and rolled, Upon moss, and stone, Over gravel and dead bone. Around tree trunks and leaves In Mrs Maisie's splendid garden of Eve His blood rushed, thrilled he gushed In circles he rolled, a ball he bowled Topsy turvy and moving His senses heady 'n'grooving Until The Moon shone a shiny silver bright The dark night was turned white The yo-yo turned orange bright He was sure to be caught in plain sight!!! The faint glow on Oompa's back became a loud orange and drew the attention of all the garden beings who arose at midnight frightened by his strange grunts and rolling movement. Buster awoke with eyes wide open and silently approached the rolling mystery. He gave a whack with his right paw and set the rolling lizard to a standstill. Petrissia came purring behind to see what the commotion was about and she immediately identified the stench of fish and chips from Oompa's body.So had Buster... Without a pause, Buster ran to the spot where the dazed lizard lay, he tore him to pieces with his teeth while muffling the lizards screams to gory silence. Out burst all the food that he had greedily stolen and eaten and the orange glow of his back faded to a dark black in the night. 'Serves him right!' thought Buster 'for stealing' He went back to his kennel triumphant and contented at last and proceeded to have a sound nights sleep! The garden was quiet once again, peace returned at night but a murderous silence prevailed. We all, as children are told time and again that we ought not to steal. But lured by temptations and a sense of lack, we make our way into our friends pencil box when they are not looking to use their eraser or take away the new doll pen. We often fail to ask permission to use another's items. Sometimes, we don't ask because of fear or simple because of shyness. Its important to build healthy sharing habits and look after our friends when they need something. Its also important to ensure they do the same for you when you need their help Its always lovely, ask for what you want with kindness and politeness. Understand, that if you did not get what you wanted, it is for the best! Would you like to end up like Oompalini who stole food? or like Buster and Petrissia, two known enemies of the animal world who both worked together to search for the thief? Sometimes, its better to surrender to what is given to us than to ask for more and trust that all will be taken care of.
author: Beatrice Clearwater

title: World of Music
text: I want to show you something." They all went in, and followed Masi to a room. Vivaan looked inside. Musical instruments everywhere! "What are all these?" Vivaan was curious. Masi said, "A musical instrument is a device used to make music. Let me introduce you to each of them." "Look at that big box!" Vivaan said. Ma smiled. Masi sang, "Harmonium sure looks like a box, a musical instrument with bellows, keys and stops. You can create melodies with it and sing along, sit on the floor and play your favourite song." " Tabla always comes in pairs, and brings its own cushion-chairs. It makes beautiful, rhythmic sounds, when you tap your fingers on those rounds." "Now let's have a look at Sitar, it's popular worldwide, an all-star. Shaped round at bottom with a tall neck, a Sitar has many strings and frets." Made of bamboo and hollow inside, Bansuri is always by Krishna's side. Blow air to make sound, use fingers to play, You can take a Bansuri anywhere. Masi said, “The sound of this one brings back memories, Remember where you heard its melodies?" Vivaan said, "I heard Shehnai during your wedding celebrations, where everyone kept going, Congratulations! Congratulations!" Ma and Masi burst into laughter. "The concert is about to start. Let's head to the hall," said Masi. The musicians took the stage. The audience took their places. And the notes from the instruments filled the huge hall. Classical musicians who made an appearance Sitar - Pandit Ravi Shankar, Anoushka Shankar, George Harrison Harmonium - R.K. Bijapure Flute - Debopriya and Suchismita Chatterjee, aka Flute Sisters Shehnai - Ustad Bismillah Khan Tabla - Zakir Hussain
author: Shivika Nayyar

title: Little Girls Who Dream
text: There was once a little girl who dreamt a lot. She dreamt of seas and forests, of fields and valleys, of mountains and rivers; she sometimes dreamt she flew high into the sky and at other times she saw herself diving into the ocean; but best of all, she dreamt of the school bell ringing to announce the end of the school day and of all the children running out with their bags in glee. Sometimes upon waking up, she would discover she was not at home under the blankets but had dozed off in class and the bell had really rung! Vijaya - that was the little girl's name - loved the lunch break and the end of school hours for then she could play with Ammu, her best friend, and talk ten to the dozen while cycling on their way back home. Viji, as she was called by her friends, loved to talk about her dreams to Ammu who would listen with wonder and wish she could have such amazing dreams too. Ammu was a patient listener and a warm-hearted girl. She cried easily if the others bothered her but Viji was her protectress. The mean kids did not dare make Ammu cry when Viji was around because she would make her eyes very large and scary and glare at them. She would give those girls a good scolding in a stern, high voice that they feared would catch the attention of the teachers if it were allowed to continue. Viji loved looking after Ammu and together the two of them discussed the beautiful lands that they sometimes dreamt of and wondered where those places could be. Perhaps it was in America? Ammu had ventured. Viji didn't like the sound of America and said she would find out the name of the place from somebody when she dreamt next. One day, Viji didn't come to school and Ammu had to spend a whole day without anyone to talk to. She waited eagerly for her best friend to show up on the next day but Viji was absent again. This went on for the whole week. She found out that Viji's maternal grandmother was very sick in bed and that Viji and her parents had had to rush to her aid to her mother's village in Andhra Pradesh. When the weekend came, there was still no news of Viji. On Sunday night, Ammu prayed hard before going to bed that Vijaya should return to town and attend school the next day. She put in an additional prayer asking for her grandmother to be healed soon, recalling how much Viji loved her. That night, Ammu had a vivid dream. She saw that she was travelling though a dark forest with Viji. They were small and the trees were big and tall. As they walked, leaves fallen on the ground crumpled under their feet. At long last they came upon a bright green field at the end of the woods. The sun shone merrily on a cottage in the distance. She could spot a cow and two country fowls near it. Someone waved at them from within the fence. The two of them ran to greet her. It was an old woman, quite tall and healthy, with long graying hair tied in a plait behind her, a big beaming smile and deep, peaceful, beautiful eyes. She bowed down and scooped the two of them up, one on each arm and Viji screamed, " Ammamma! " It was her grandmother, whole and well. Of course she was pleased to see her! The next moment Ammu found herself being shaken firmly by her mother, trying to wake her up. "What are you smiling at, my dear?" she asked. "If you sleep a moment longer you will be late for school today! Come on, we have to get you ready." Ammu was still half asleep. Her mother continued. "Oh, and Vijaya's mother called up saying you are to take your cycle by their house today. Vijaya is going to school. They returned late last night with her grandmother." Ammu jumped up from her bed at this. All her drowsiness was gone. She knew it! Hadn't she just dreamt of it all? Wait till she could tell Viji all about it! This was going to be the best Monday of her life.
author: Dona Wording

title: Nani's Walk to the Park
text: Once a week, Nani* goes to the park. Today, Venki wants to go with her. “I walk slowly,” says Nani. “And I take my time getting there.” “I don’t mind,” says Venki. So Nani picks up her shopping bag and starts to cross the road. “But Nani,” says Venki, “the park is that way!” *Nani means grandmother. “We’ll go this way,” says Nani, “through the Lane of Treasures.” The Lane of Treasures? What a wonderful name for the market. The shops here sell everything! When Nani finishes shopping, Venki points to a gate and asks, “Shall we take a shortcut, Nani? We’ll be at the park in no time.” “No,” says Nani. “We’ll go through the Lane of Beauty.” In the Lane of Beauty, the people stitch amazing goddhis.* A lady gives Nani a goddhi in which Venki sees a piece of her favourite saree and a bit of his Ma’s kurta. “Shall we go to the park now?” asks Venki. *A goddhi (pronounced go-the-dee) is a traditional hand-stitched quilt made of recycled material, usually soft, old cotton sarees. “Yes,” says Nani. “We’ll take the Lane of Happiness.” “Come, come,” Nani calls softly and Venki laughs as dogs and cats tumble out from everywhere! Nani pours the milk she bought at the market and they watch as the animals lick their bowls clean. Venki doesn’t want to leave the Lane of Happiness but Nani reminds him that they are on their way to the park. Next, Nani and Venki walk through a lane behind a little school. The children are playing langdi, lagori and sakhli.* “Is this the Lane of Noise?” asks Venki. “No, it’s the Lane of Mischief. It reminds me of you and your friends!” laughs Nani. “Have you named all the lanes in the city?” asks Venki. “Not all,” smiles Nani, “only the ones that are important to me!” *These are some traditional games played in India. “The park is not far now, but you will have to be a little patient. I want to stop at the Lane of Friendship.” In the Lane of Friendship, Nani visits her dear friend. They were girls together and they have grown old together. They whisper and they giggle. Then, Nani gives her friend a hug and says, “It is time to leave. We will now walk through the Lane of Dreams.” The Lane of Dreams has more books than Venki’s school library! The bookseller sells old books for very little money and buys the ones people have finished reading. And they walk down the Lane of Magic. Nani chooses a book and says, “Let’s go, we are almost at the park now.” And they walk down the Lane of Magic. Venki looks up at the big trees that offer shade, and feels a cool breeze. Nani shows him Gulmohar, Amaltas and Jarul trees. The flowers on the road look like a magic carpet. At last they are at the park. It has been a long time since they left home. Venki looks around and thinks of all the people and places he has seen that morning. “I like your lanes, Nani,” he says. “May I come with you next week too?”
author: Deepa Balsavar

title: What is this?
text: My mother is Japanese. and My father is Korean. One day, my mom cooked me a meal. " what is this?" I asked. "This is sushi." Mom answered. Next day, my dad prepared me a meal. "what is this?" I asked. "This is bulgogi." Father answered. A few days later, my father's birthday was came up. ﻿"what is this?" I asked. "This is pizza noodles!" my father answered. ﻿Joe was happy to taste the foods of various countries.
author: chaeeun lee
illustrator: Aayshah Maseerah; Ajit Narayan; Greystroke; Kruttika Susarla; Meenal Singh; Rijuta Ghate; Rupa Prakash; Sandhya Prabhat; Vibha Surya

title: Chunu & Munu: Our School
text: Look Munu, this is our school. Isn't it a nice school?" "At school we have a ground to play in and a garden to dance in. Our school is so much fun!" "When we dance there, our feet don’t tire. When we sing there, our voices don’t tire." "We are all children of our mother, and every year we grow up." "Everybody goes to the next class at school." "Reading is so much fun It’s almost like singing and dancing." "The classrooms are so clean, and our friends look so neat." "Look how our teachers speak lovingly to all of us." "Look at this library! From your heart, Munu, how do you feel?" "Everyone is sitting together nicely in the library reading." "All the books are our good friends who never say no to us." "Wherever we go, we can borrow the books from the library, and they come with us." "The books never get tired of being with us. They are good friends." "Is there another school like ours?"
author: Stephanie  Wei

title: Living with birds
text: "cuckoo~" At 8:00 o'clock l get up. "There is a Chicken." "Hi~ chicken! Do you know? Our morning begins with your cry" "Tweet~Tweet~" "There's a sparrow sitting there." "Do you know? Your cheerful song makes us feel better." "Caw~Caw~" I hear crows somewhere. "There the crow flies." "The crow's crying is something unlucky." "hoot-hoot" "The owl is crying." "It's already 9 o'clock." "Hi~ Owl~ Do you know? With your lullaby we sleep." I fell asleep and thought. 'I hope Tomorrow will also be with the birds.'
author: 아리 김

title: Katya and Kaboo
text: Hello, this is me Katya. I live in the village with Kaboo and Maama and Paapa. Kaboo and me have fun times together. Kaboo is no ordinary cat, He has a long tail that can do magic! But Kaboo’s magic sometimes goes wrong. Like the time we went on a slide and his tail turned the slide into a big broom. Sweep – sweep – sweep, we tumbled and tossed about. When Kaboo thinks no one is looking, he makes his tail bring him a nice saucer of milk. But I know it! Slop – slop – slop, he licks all the milk up. Kaboo’s tail gives out shiny sparks when he is suddenly surprised. I try to surprise him by hiding behind Paapa’s chair. Snore – snore – snore, goes Kaboo softly, in front of the chair and Oh! He knows I am there! After a hard day of playing, Kaboo snuggles in bed with me and we go on trips to faraway places and have all the lovely things to eat. Dream – dream – dream, of chocolate, cakes and ice-cream.
author: Sherline Pimenta K.

title: What is she doing?
text: wow, She looks very busy! Let's take a look at what she does at home. What is she doing? She's eating beans with her grandmother. What is she doing? She is reading a book. There is a spider in the book! What is she doing? She is hanging the laundry. What is she doing? She gives dad a washing dish. What is she doing? She is eating an apple and giving brother a banana. What is she doing? She is doing her brother's bowl. ﻿ ﻿What is she doing? She is giving her shoes to her mom. She had a busy day and became night. What did you do at home today?
author: sujin choi
illustrator: Aman Randhawa; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: The Tall Dwarf
text: Once upon a time in a far off land there was a small village of dwarfs. They were all a happy bunch and would help each other in need. They lived in small huts which had fenced garden. The mama dwarfs would take good care of their children and the daddy dwarfs would march everyday to work to the nearby forest. The daddy dwarfs would chop trees from the nearby forest. They would keep some of the chopped wood for cooking in their garden and the rest they would stock in their mini carriages and take them to grandpa dwarf house. Grandpa dwarf was the oldest member of the family and a very good friend of the carpenter, Jerry. Jerry belonged to the town side village and knew each of the dwarfs personally. He would visit them every four days and would load the logs of wood in his cart and take them to his workshop. For all the logs of wood taken, he would give the dwarfs a cart full of fruits, vegetables and grains. It was a happy life of the little hard working men and they were happy with their carpenter friend. Among the kid dwarfs, there was one named Rex. Rex was a very naughty kid of his parents and would always want to try something new. He was always a head full of questions and would keep asking them till he was convinced. He would sometimes accompany his father to grandpa dwarf house. Grandpa was Rex’s best friend and would pamper him with fruits and sweets. Rex had seen Jerry come to grandpa dwarf's house and would have loads of fun with him. Jerry would pick up Rex, mount him on his shoulder, twist him up and down till he would giggle and chuckle. Rex seemed to be getting naughtier by the day and his curiosity was growing each day. It was getting difficult to control the naughty and adamant Rex. One fine day, Rex threw a tantrum and shouted out loud saying,"I hate being a dwarf kid. I am so short and insignificant. When I grow up like both of you, I will just grow a bit in height. How disgusting!! I want to become like Jerry. A tall and handsome man is what I want to be in my adulthood and not a dwarf." Rex's father was shaken with his irrelevant protest and arrogance. Both the parents and grandpa made him understand but all in vain. There was a lot of unrest in Rex’s house, he refused to eat and play. The other kids too were getting influenced and every dwarf house was found battling with the issue which Rex had raised. Grandpa dwarf decided to nail this issue. He decided to take Jerry’s help. One fine day,Grandpa and Jerry,decided to take all the kids to Jerry’s village. The kids were excited as they also were somehow getting tired of being too pushy with their demands and needed a break. When they reached the village, Jerry took all of them to his workshop. It was a big space where logs of wood were piled upon each other. There was also a section which had a display of all Jerry’s creations which he had done with the help of wood bought from the dwarf village. Some were big. Some were small. He then took them to his friend John, the ironsmith’s shop. He showed them how each piece of iron is molded as per purpose. A big piece can be molded to make an axe and a very small piece can be molded to make a nail too. The kids were awestruck and found the tour to village very enjoyable. After all the guided tours Jerry took them to his home where his mother had made delicious meal for everyone. The kids, all hungry and tired, ate their fill and were excited to see more. But Jerry, seizing the moment decided to put forth his thought process of “being what you are“. He asked each of them if they liked the visit to both the workshops and asked about what was the best thing that they noticed in both the work places. Rex, sharp as he was immediately replied, " I saw the huge workshop, huge stack of logs of wood and the huge cupboard."
