The other kids very politely said, the small shoe rack made out of small planks of wood, the big iron molded to an axe and the small iron piece molded to a nail was very impressive. So Jerry, summed it up quickly and said, “Guess you kids have got your answers for your demands from your parents. Like the big logs of wood which were piled up were all chopped by your parents and not by me. Your parents even if short in height have made an effort to chop huge logs of woods. They did not get perturbed with their heights instead with combined effort they ensured they would meet my demand of giving me those big logs. Similarly, with that wood I could make the big wardrobe. With that left over wood I made the shoe rack. Is that not commendable? John takes an iron piece and decides to make an axe and a nail. It’s all as per need or purpose. The axe is used to chop the wood and a nail to fix the wood. Similarly kiddos, love the way you are. Show your parents that like them, you all also can handle difficult things and easier things too. Like for Rex, you are good at archery, why don’t you try becoming an expert in it and participate in inter-village championships? Scott, you got very fine hands. Why don’t you attain an expertise to become a great sculptor and give the world a masterpiece? Make use of this life kids. You see the tool box? Every tool has a purpose and a special task to perform. So are you all my friends, you all are special and ensure you prove yourself to be special.” Grandpa was quietly watching all of them muttering and regretting of being so unreasonable. He stood up and said” So, shall we go back to our home and start working towards our purpose of life? “The kids shouted out a big “Yes” and then hugged grandpa and Jerry and apologized for being so rude to the elders. On returning to the village, the kids individually narrated the entire day to their parents and apologized for their unreasonable behavior. The dwarf village was no more just a happy place but it turned out to be a happy and a special place. Jerry and grandpa dwarf saw the children grow in their abilities and were happy that they paved a way for the disturbed little minds.
author: Moushumi Ananthakrishnan

title: Bhujar
text: Today Rini's class shared interesting stories. Their teacher wanted to know who had a pet at home! Mithu said he had a pet cat named Tuni. Rupa had a pet sheep named Tusi. And Ratan had a pet owl named Tuli. The whole class burst out laughing: Tuni, Tusi, Tuli! They sounded like fun. But Rini did not say anything. She didn't have a pet. That evening, Rini couldn't wait to talk to her father. “Daddy, can I have a pet like my classmates?” she asked. “Yes, I suppose so. You can have a cat or a dog," he said. "Hooray!" said Rini. “I want a dog, please. Oh, please please bring me a dog.” “Okay, I will bring you a puppy," Rini's dad told her. "Thieves don't come to steal from your house when you have a dog!” Soon, Rini’s father brought her a puppy. It was a white puppy with really soft fur. Rini named her Bhujar. Bhujar was full of energy! Her Dad taught Rini how to take care of a puppy. He said, “You must feed her and clean her regularly. Then she will know to be faithful.” Rini looked after Bhujar everyday. Rini gave Bhujar baths, and took her for walks and on adventures. Bhujar adored Rini, and Rini adored Bhujar. Wherever Rini went, Bhujar went with her. But Bhujar was not allowed to go to school with Rini. When Rini went to school, Bhujar had to stay at home alone. One day, Bhujar followed Rini to school. She moved around Rini, barking and jumping. “Bhujar, why are you coming with me?" Rini scolded. "You can't come to school. If you do, boys and girls will tease you. And the teacher won't be happy!” So Bhujar went home. A man was roaming to and fro near the school. Rini had been seeing the man for several days. She knew was not from her village. He comes here very often riding a motorcycle, thought Rini. He always wears a black cap. The man asked, “How are you, Rini? You look so beautiful today. Do you like peanuts? I’d love to buy some peanuts for you.” “I do not know you," answered Rini. "Why are you speaking to me?” The man said, “Everyone knows me. My name is Basu. All children call me Uncle Basu. Let’s go, I’ll buy some peanuts for you.” “No, I don’t need peanuts. Please leave me alone!” Rini went to the class and told her friends about the man. She was surprised that everybody in the class knew about him! He was good friends with all children. Mithu said, “Uncle Basu is very good. A few days ago, he bought delicious peanuts for Ratan and me.” Rupa said, “Don’t you know about Uncle Basu? He brings so many things for us to eat. Yesterday, Uncle Basu bought us mango-pickles. Uncle Basu is a very good man.” Rini said, “He doesn't seem very good. You are greedy to eat his mango-pickles!” On her way home, Rini ran into Uncle Basu again. With him were four other men Rini didn't recognize. Uncle Basu blocked her way. “Let’s go, Rini," he said. "I will take you somewhere for a nice outing. Come along with us now.” “No no, I will not go anywhere," said Rini. "I have lot of work to do. I have lot of lessons to learn today.” She was terrified. The man said, “Come on, Rini. Let’s go to the park. The park is very beautiful.” Rini said, “Please, please leave me alone. I don't want to go to the park.” But then men forced her to get on the minibus. And then, Bhujar arrived. She came running, barking, furious! She bit Uncle Basu and yanked him from the minibus. He began to yell in pain. The village people came running when they heard the screams and noise. The four strange men drove away in fear. But the man—Uncle Basu—could not get rid of Bhujar. He was caught and confessed his guilt to the people. He said, “We kidnap children and sell them. We get lot of money in return.” Weeping, Rini hugged Bhujar. She said, “Bhujar, you saved me from that man!” People began to praise Bhujar. From then on, Bhujar does not stay at home. She is welcome at school with Rini. When Rini is in class, Bhujar sits under the nearby banyan-tree. Under this banyan tree the wicked man used to come and roam. Now Bhujar barks whenever she sees a stranger. Now all the children know Rini's pet. And they all love her... almost as much as Rini does.
author: Alisha Berger

title: My lover
text: Hi, this is my house. Now, let me introduce my family. My name is sandy. This is my room. First, fredy is my best friend. We're always together. Fredy and I are two. Second, there is always kitty in the livingroom. Fredy, kitty and I are three. Third, there are always birds in the tree. Today is two birds. We're all four. Fourth, there are fish in the stream. We're all five. ring ring ring... "Hello? umm.. ok." Let's go home now. Lastly, this is my family. We're all six. Bye Bye~!!
author: lee ye jin

title: Are You an Insect?
text: EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEKKK! Do you run when you see a cockroach? Or scream when you see a bee? Look closely instead. Insects are amazing. They help scientists make machines. Grasshopper Robots are tiny. But they leap very high. Just like real grasshoppers. One day, they may explore places that no one has ever been. RoachBots run around and squeeze through tiny cracks. Just like real cockroaches. One day, they could help find people who are lost or trapped. RoboBees can fly and perch on plants. Just like real bees. One day, RoboBees might travel to Mars in a spaceship, collect mud and gas and bring it back to us. Water Strider Microbots can walk on water. Just like real water striders. One day, they could clean our lakes and oceans. The next time something crawls or buzzes around, look carefully. It might be a RoachBot or a RoboBee. You never know. A bot is a computer program or little machine that can perform simple, repetitive tasks. RoachBots Grasshopper Robots RoboBees Water Strider Microbots
author: Shabnam  Minwalla

title: Where is My Mother?
text: She cannot fly yet. “Are you my mother?” Baby asks the crow. “ Kaa! Kaa! Not me!” the crow says. “Are you my mother?” Baby asks the hen. “ Cukuruk-koo! Not me!” the hen says. “Are you my mother?” Baby asks duck. “ Quack! Quack! Not me!" the duck says. Maybe if I call for my mother loudly, she will hear me, Baby thinks. “Cheep! Cheep! Cheep-cheep!” Mother hears Baby and comes flying. They fly happily together into the sky. Hooray!
author: Alisha Berger

title: Cuckoo Wants To Sing
text: Once there was a black cuckoo. He sung beautiful songs of the seasons in Bangladesh. Then, in Baishakh, the first month of the year, the cuckoo got very sick. Suddenly, he could not sing anymore! He felt very sad. In the month of Jaishtha, the mangoes and jackfruits became ripe. Cuckoo wanted to sing of their tastiness! He flew from tree to tree, trying and trying to sing his delicious song. But, not a noise came from his throat. Summer came. Shimul Tree saw cuckoo was sad. The tree said: "Now the weather is very hot. Surely that is the reason you cannot sing. Just wait for Monsoon! Heavy rain will start then, and the drip-drop song of rain will help you sing, too." Monsoon came. The rain fell in heavy sheets throughout the months of Ashar and Shrabon. Rivers, canals, lakes and fields all filled with water. The kadam tree bloomed its round yellow bunches. The cuckoo flew in the rain from tree to tree, searching for his voice. But, he still could not sing. Monsoon finished. Autumn arrived in the months of Bhadra and Ashwin. White Kash flowers bloomed. The ground was soon covered in petals. Ripened palm fruits hung heavily from the tree. The cuckoo tried to sing of their beauty. But still, he could not. Then came the late autumn. Farmers harvested new rice in the months of Kartik and Agryahayan. But, the cuckoo still could not sing of the bountiful harvest for the Nabonno festival. He was near-bursting with frustration! The winter season arrived in the months of Poush and Magh. The weather turned very cold. People tried to warm themselves in the sun. Women made jaggery from hot date juice. They made sweet cakes. Leaves fell from the trees. Fields were covered in yellow mustard flowers. The year had almost come to an end. And still, the cuckoo could not sing. He began to cry. What did it mean if his song was forever lost? At last, the spring came. It was the final two months of the year, Falgun and Chaitra. New leaves sprouted in the trees. New buds grew in the mango trees. Honey-bees started flying and singing. The honey-bee buzz stayed in cuckoo's ears. Cuckoo tried again to sing, to no avail. But the honey-bees' song did not stop. They buzzed and buzzed. So cuckoo kept trying to sing, too. At last, he found a squeak. Then a squawk! And finally, the cuckoo sung a short song. His year of effort had not gone in vain! And now, the cuckoo is known as the bird of spring. When the people of Bangladesh hear his melodious song, they know spring has arrived.
author: Alisha Berger

title: Goat and Hyena's knife
text: Once upon a time, there was a long dry spell. The animals ate all the grass in the country. Only the imbowa plants on the big trees survived. One day Goat saw Hyena pass by with a knife. Goat asked for the knife so that she could cut imbowa plants to eat. Hyena gave the knife to Goat. She cut down the climbing plant, and ate until she was full. Goat forgot all about the knife she had used. When Hyena returned to ask for the knife, Goat was at a loss. She could not remember where she had dropped it. Goat scratched here and there in search of the knife. Up to today Goat is still looking for that knife. Hyena told Goat, "Since you have lost my knife, which was the source of my livelihood, I will eat you. Then I will eat your offspring!" From that time, Hyena has never spared Goat. Meanwhile, Goat continues to search for Hyena's knife.
author: Wekunya   Cornelius

title: Baboon chief
text: Don was a big baboon. He was a bully. He was the baboon chief. His followers gave him a special cloth. “I will wear this on my head,” said Don. “Everyone follow my orders. Do not question me!” shouted Don. So, the followers followed their chief. If Don jumped, everyone jumped. But the band on Don's head was too tight. He touched his sore head. The baboons all touched their heads. “This hurts,” said Don. “This hurts,” they copied. “This is too tight!” “This is too tight,” they copied. Don fell down, over a cliff. They all copied him. The baboon chief died. His followers were hurt, but they lived.
author: Bonsamo   Miesso; Elizabeth Laird

title: Book of Reflections
text: "Where did Grandma keep the laddoos …?", Lavanya wondered as she searched her Grandparents’s room. "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!", screamed Lavanya as the lights went off. All she could see was a pair of eyes. "Don't be scared, Lavanya", Grandpa tells her. “But, I can’t see anything!” Lavanya retorts. “Have you ever wondered why?”, Grandpa says with a chuckle. His question takes Lavanya by surprise. “It is because there is no light!” Lavanya answers brightly as the lights come on. "That is correct. Light helps us see things around us". "Look over there," Grandpa says pointing at the mirror. Light also helps us to see ourselves in the mirror! Isn't it so special?" Lavanya is fascinated and remembers that she has seen this in many other places. She decides to go on a adventure to look for places where she can see herself. The first time she sees it is when she is about to eat Grandma’s delicious rasam rice. She spots herself in the spoon. But the image does not look exactly the same as the mirror, in fact it is is upside down! Curiously, she flips the spoon and...aha! She finds a bigger herself on the other side. Grandpa and Lavanya go for their evening walks in a big park at the center of their small city. As Grandpa is driving, Lavanya spots herself in the scooter mirror with her hair flying everywhere and giggles to herself. She decides to do a little more exploration in the park. As they take their walk in a nearby lake, she she sees the image of the trees in the water. “You can see the grass and the trees too!”, she tells Grandpa. Once they had driven back home, Lavanya sees her grandma walk to the kitchen with a packet of laddoos. She quietly follows her with a small mirror in hand. When Grandma is hiding the packet of laddoos in one of the shelves, she slides the mirror inside the room by opening the door a bit. Lavanya is now able to see where laddoos the are being hidden. That night at the dinner table, she smiles and places a laddoo on her Grandpa’s plate.
author: Najiba Yasmin, Sanjana Thandaveswaran,  Akshara Raje
illustrator: Najiba Yasmin, Sanjana Thandaveswaran,  Akshara Raje

title: Plants live and eat?
text: It was night time when Raju's mother was tucking him into bed. Raju- maa, today's class was weird. my teacher told me that plants can also eat food. Mother- (she chuckled) yes raju they can eat food but like us. Raju: but how? they dont even move. Mother: no but they get food from the sun, water and air. Raju: I dont understand. (confused look) Mother: dont worry. tomorrow your teacher will tell you everything. With this thought he drifted off to sleep. H e woke in a different world. everything was green here. He was in a round black boat surrounded by water. Suddenly from behind him a voice came. DNA: Hola, I'm DNA your new friend. what is your name kid? Raju: Hello, im raju. can you tell me where we are? DNA: ofcourse. We are inside of a mango leaf cell. and I am the president of this cell. Raju: What is a cell? DNA: Cells are like little cities of islands in the leaf that helps it make food and i tell them how to. there are millions of these little cities in the leaf. let me show you around my friend. He rowed the boat until they reached an oval island where there were a lot of round little men getting on an off. Raju: What is this place? DNA: This is called the island of mitochondria where a lot of these little round men are made who can then go off to work at different islands in this cell. Their name is energy. They moved towards another island which was very green and there was light falling on it. Raju could see the little round men called energy landing on the island. DNA: here, my friend is where most of our food is made. Raju: how do they make it? DNA: they use this light and them mix it with some spices called enzymes to make it tasty. They again moved to a different place but this time it was a big island, the biggest he had seen. Raju: woah DNA: yeah i know it is big. this is the vacuole. This island keeps our cell in shape. Raju: Ive done a lot of sightseeing and i am thirsty. can i drink water from this river? DNA: (laughs) This is not just water my friend this is healthy water we call cytoplasm. it has all the nutrients and salts we need. go on drink. T hey had finally reached the boundary of this cell city. DNA: I must say good bye to you my friend as my city limit ends here. This is our city wall. you can go ahead and search for a place called the stoma. the way out of this leaf is from there. Raju nodded and bid his friend farewell. He walked and walked and walked and after some time he reached a bunch of small rivers. some of them seemed to have water other were almost like the cytoplasm in that cell city, full of nutrients. Raju: oh so this is where they get water and nutrients from. He finally reached the cloud like city. it was squishy and fun to walk on. he say little spaces where we could see different little round men going up and down. Raju: Hello, could you tell me who are you? Air: Hello there friend, im Carbon dioxide but you can call me CO2. what are you doing on the spongy city this is a place for air only? Raju: nothing I am just finding my way out of this leaf. AIR: Oh goodie, I am on my way out too. you can come with me. Raju: (smiled) awesome They walked towards a huge gate with guards standing on either side. Air: I must say good bye as i have work else where Raju bid his friend co2 farewell and then tried to step out of the gate but to his horror he fell. Raju woke up with a start. it was 7 in the morning and he had to get ready for school. He sat up and remembered his dream. It was very interesting and he was delighted because now he would know every answer to his teacher's question Photosynthesis is an essential process for plants and some bacteria to use energy from sunlight with water and CO2 to produce their food which is glucose. This work is done by the leaves of a plant. There are a lot of different kinds of layers in the leaf which are shown in the image below. all these layers have different cells with different functions guided by the DNA. The by product of this process is oxygen that we all breathe in so SAVE PLANTSSSS!!
author: Avnie  Agnihotri
illustrator: Avnie  Agnihotri; Harshvardhan Gantha; Rijuta Ghate

title: Neha, Mia and Martians in Jars
text: “A post-Apocalyptic world, that’s hard to imagine isn’t it?” Neha wondered. “What would we do? Where would we go? Will have to grow our own grain and sow?” “If the world was going to end tomorrow”, replied Mia. “We could just go live on Mars take over the planet, capture the Martians and put them in giant jars” “Mars has no Oxygen” said Neha “We’ll take our own trees!” quipped Mia. “Mars has no water.” grunted Neha. “Oh, the Martians will share.” dismissed Mia. “Science forbids it, especially chemistry and Biology. All those years of research, they might just throw a fit!” A breathless Neha glared. With an eye roll Mia grumbled,” Earth isn’t all that special. I’m sure there’s something out there that’s residential.” “Fine you’ll see for you rself. Bring out the telescope.” Neha declared. “But we’re not allowed to use THE telescope.” Said an exasperated Mia. With an air of finality and gumption Neha decides, “To prove a point I am willing to risk it. In the name of science and all things good, I’ll make sure to clear up all that is misunderstood." “The telescope is no ordinary one. It allows for the viewer to be transported to any place their heart desires. All that it demands, is that you give it a sound command.” “Grab your spacesuit Mia.” Neha and Mia hold each other’s hands tight, their hearts beating a mile a minute and chant, “I wish I may, I wish I might for the telescope to take me to the wondrous terrains of Mars deep into the night.” A zoom and a swirl later they find themselves on red rocky roads. “This is free-ee-zing. My fingers and toes have lost all feeling.” Cried Mia. “Well you see the first problem don’t you. The sun’s too far away.” Replied Neha, all matter of fact like. Mia’s stare was a blank one, “Your point being?” Neha’s eyes lit up, “Think of it as a witch’s potion, for life to occur as we know it you throw in a dash of CHONPS….” “CHOMP?!?” a confused Mia shrieked. “No CHONPS. As I was saying, a sprinkle of that, some water or an equivalent solvent and a source of energy for chemical reactions to happen. Well now that I think about it, eruptions from Mars’s volcanos could work as energy…” Neha’s voice trailed. Mia was quick to add “CHONPS sounds like the sound a zombie makes while biting into a human hand. Do you think their brains disintegrate into sand?” “CHONPS. The C stands for carbon, the building blocks. H for Hydrogen, recognizable in the periodic table as the first box. O meaning oxygen the thing that trees make and N for nitrogen, the thing that lighting strikes bake. P as in phosphorous, grind up a few bones and you’ll find plenty of it in there and finally S. The smell of rotten eggs announces its arrival a lot before I can, Sulphur!” recited Neha “Well I think I get it now. So, energy like the sun to help with getting things started, like a fire for food.” Water to make it a curry and CHONPS as vegetables and flavours?” asked Mia. “That’s exactly it!” Now let’s get out of here, unless you want to become more than a sightseer?” twinkled Neha.
author: Tanvi Sawant, Mahika Arora

title: Baby Gets A Name
text: Nimmi's little sister was born some time before the sun rose in the sky. Nimmi knew that the time after night when there was light in the sky but the sun had not yet risen was called dawn. She had been taught that at school. It had rained heavily all through the night but just before the baby's first cry could be heard from the room Mrs. Sen was in, the downpour suddenly stopped and the first signs of light appeared on the perfectly clear sky. "The baby is here, the baby is here!" Nimmi jumped up and down and tried to drag her grandfather by the arm to go look inside her mother's room. Grandpa had fallen asleep on the chair waiting for the delivery to happen. Little Nimmi, however, had been very excited and alert. She had sat all along with ears pricked, trying to make sense of every muffled voice from inside the room, not wanting to miss the moment the baby came out. Grandpa awoke and taking 5 year old Nimmi in his arms, stood beside the door. Shortly a nurse came out smiling broadly and said, "It's a girl! You may go in." "Where is baby, Mumma?" asked Nimmi, looking around. "Baby is having a bath, honey", Mrs. Sen replied. "Oh!" said Nimmi. It seemed strange to her that Baby should bath so early. She must feel so cold! Nimmi didn't approve of this hospital at all. They should know better than to make her little sister bath at this hour. What if she caught a cold? "What time is it?" Mrs. Sen asked grandpa. The clock was behind her bed and she couldn't see the time on it. "Let me see, umm, it's five in the morning", said grandpa, peering through his glasses to look at the time. "Yes and it's dawn", quipped in Nimmi eagerly, "and it's not raining anymore either!" "Oh!" Mrs. Sen said. "I had thought I would name the baby Varsha because of the rain. Did the rain stop before she was born? Did anyone notice?" "No Mumma grandpa was sleeping!" Grandpa nodded in agreement to these words of Nimmi. "But don't worry, I saw the rain stop moments ago. And there was light outside too. It was DAWN, Mumma," Nimmi stressed again. "Isn't that right, grandpa?" "Yes, yes, if Buri says so it must be so." Grandpa smiled. Buri was the name grandpa called her by. Nimmi looked at her mother now that the matter was settled. Mrs. Sen stared at Nimmi for a moment and seemed to make up her mind about something. Nimmi always noticed little details keenly and perhaps her mother decided that her daughter was right about the time. "But what do we name her now?" she asked grandpa. At this moment, Nimmi's father, who had been busy talking to the doctor, came into the room. Grandpa told him what they were discussing. "Mahesh, maybe we should call the baby Usha, because Buri Didi says our new family member was born at dawn!" Nimmi loved the suffix to her name - Didi! Grandpa explained to her that Usha meant dawn in some languages like Sanskrit, Hindi and Bengali. "Hmm.." said Mr. Sen thoughtfully, "I don't like that name so much" he said, looking at his wife. "What do you say?" "I don't like that name either", said Nimmi loudly enough to make sure everyone heard. "It's not so bad, but we could think of some more options", Mrs. Sen said. "But I don't like the name Usha!" said Nimmi, stamping her right foot on the ground. Everyone looked at her. Nimmi crossed her hands in front of her and looking at everyone seriously said, "We will call her Dawn." "But that's not the sort of name we keep, dearie" began her mother, but Mr. Sen stopped her. "I know just the name for the baby. We can call her Dona." Now Dona sounded like Dawn but wasn't an uncommon name among the Bengalis. Nimmi had heard that name before and liked it instantly, but nothing more could be said on the matter because the nurse entered the room with Nimmi's baby sister who was bawling at the top of her voice. Mrs. Sen stretched her arms out to take the baby. "Don't cry, don't cry", she kept saying. "Don't cry Dona!" she said again, and suddenly, as if at the sound of her newly given name, the baby paused her cries. Everyone turned silent for a moment. Nimmi stared at the baby with awe, along with the others. Then the infant started crying again, but now she was "baby" no more. She had a name. Born when the rain stopped and light dawned, she was Dona. THE END
author: Dona Wording

title: The King's Park
text: It was the last game of hide and seek. The children were so engrossed in their game that they did not realize that they had veered away from their usual path. Now, they were in the King's Park. Though called 'King's' park, it did not appear so. The park was neither cared for nor was there much greenery. The only plants that grew there were the knee high wild grasses that would sprout up after the rains. Long ago there would have been many flowering plants. After the water pipes broke they would have withered away without water. The ropes of the swings were frayed and cut and so were wrapped around the posts. There were only two rungs left in the ladder leading to the slide. The slide itself was riddled with holes. If you still wanted to slide down your dress would catch at the holes and you would probably get hurt. The merry-go-round there was rusted and it would be very difficult to make it go round. Even if you manage to do so the groans and creaks from it would frighten away the children! The King's park did not provide joy to the children, rather it frightened them away. When children troubled their fathers to take them out at night, the fathers would retort "Come!Let us go to the King's park." and that would make the children stop throwing a tantrum. The only special thing about the King's Park was a tomb at its center. It walls were all dilapidated and falling down. Even so, the children from the neighbourhood would gather there to play. There would be no one around to stop or scold them. The tomb's roof, doorway, steps were all covered with pigeon's droppings. It was as if the pigeons did not like the colour of the tomb and were trying to paint in a different colour! The long headstone inside the tomb was bent and broken with age and looked like a hunched back. It was said that the king whose tomb it was, had been a cruel dictator. Under his rule it was forbidden to read and write. He believed that if his subjects became more educated than him then they would overthrow him someday. So there were neither schools nor books in his kingdom. If any house had a book, the king would order the house to be set on fire. In that kingdom there lived a wise man who was well known. People from other places used to come to hear him talk. The mean king could not tolerate this wise man. But at the same time, he could not cause trouble to this man as he had many supporters and was loved and respected by all. The king was waiting for the right opportunity to get rid of this wise man. One day, he brought a false complaint of theft against the wise man and had him hanged. The night the wise man was hanged was a full moon night. Even after killing the wise man, the king found no peace. He started getting mysterious pains in his neck. He would grab his own neck often and without reason. On full moon nights he would go mad. He would make a noose for himself with a rope. It was very difficult for the king's guards to save the king from himself. One night when the guards were not around, the king killed himself. That was a full moon night! The people said even after death the king got no peace. On each full moon night, the king would arise from his grave and roam around the tomb. If someone would go there, the king would shout at them "Get me a rope! Get me a rope!"Wayfarers who did not know of this would fall down in a faint. This is the reason why most people do not visit the King's Park. One evening the children were playing. happily. It was now Raghav's turn. He closed his eyes with his palms and counted loudly...One..Two...Three... Behind him other children ran in search of places to hide....Six..Seven...Eight.. Everyone had found places to hide in. Gopi alone could not find a good hiding place...Nine.. There was only one hiding place left...inside the tomb!...Ten..! As Raghav stopped counting, Gopi rushed inside the tomb. But, Raghav saw Gopi running into the tomb to hide. He called out.."Hey!Gopi, do not go in there." The fear in Raghav's voice made Gopi stop and turn back. He looked at Raghav in surprise and asked "What happened? Why did you stop me?" "You must not hide inside the tomb" said Raghav. "Why? What is there inside?" asked Gopi. "Hey! There is a grave! A King's grave!" said Raghav. "So what?" asked Gopi. "Don't you know what happens here on full moon nights?" asked Raghav. Hearing this, Gopi started laughing. Raghav did not understand the humour in the situation. He hung his head down. Seeing this, Gopi started laughing even more loudly. He also called out to everyone... "Hey, Radha...Kasi...Suma..Tharma..Jillu..all of you come out! Who will play with this coward? Everyone come here now!" They did not understand what the issue was all about. "Why are you two fighting?" they asked. "Who will play with him?"said Gopi pointing at Raghav.He started laughing again. "Why?What happened?"asked Kasi. "He is telling me not to go inside the tomb. He says if I go in there someone will catch hold of me!" "Yes. What Raghav is saying is correct!" said Kasi. His words of support gave some confidence to Raghav. "Do you not know what is in there Gopi?" asked Suma supporting Raghav. "Okay! okay! If Gopi wants to hide in the tomb let him hide there! Why do you bother" asked Tharma. "If he hides in there one of us would have to go into the tomb to catch him. Who will do that?" asked Jillu. Before anyone could reply to Jillu's words, Gopi retorted angrily "You are all cowards! I will not play with you!" The children did not like Gopi shouting at them. When Raghav realised that most of the children supported him, he grew bold. He looked into Gopi's eyes and said " You think you are very brave!" Pat came the retort from Gopi "Not just in thought, I am brave in deed!" "Can you enter the tomb at night?" asked Raghav. "Of course!I can!" said Gopi. "Even on a full moon night?" continued Raghav. "Yes. I can go inside the tomb even on a full moon night. I have no fear" said Gopi. "Will you go till the headstone on the grave?" asked Raghav. "Of course! I will go up till the headstone" replied Gopi. "If so, then, on the next full moon night you should go into the tomb and drive a nail on the headstone" challenged Raghav. "Sure. I will do so." replied Gopi. "If you win this challenge, we will buy you a new cricket ball and bat, but if you lose....?" asked Raghav. "That will never happen. I will not lose. So there is no need to think about that" replied Gopi haughtily. The next problem was how to find out the day of the next full moon. Kasi was looking at the skies. Everyone looked up. They saw a full round moon smiling at them. Yes! It was a full moon night today! "Okay! Let us have the challenge tonight!"said Gopi with determination "but who is going to bring the hammer and the nail?" "I will bring them" said Raghav as he did not want to lose this good opportunity. "Well, We shall meet at night....same place....at 10'o clock sharp!" so saying Gopi stomped on the grass and made his way home. The other children also left for their homes. That night the moon shone like a silver jewel on a blue forehead. Gopi kept watching the clock. He was losing his patience. Just then the clock rang ten times. Gopi peered into the drawing room of his home. Everyone in his family had retired to their rooms for the night. His older brother alone sat and watched the television. Gopi's elder brother did not realize what was going on behind his back. He was engrossed watching some comedy show. Gopi closed the door to his room and silently tiptoed out. Once he crossed the outer gate of his home, he started walking fast towards the King's Park. Raghav was waiting near the ruined entrance arch of the park. Holding his breath, Gopi looked around. There was no one either in the park or outside the park. "Did you bring the nail?" asked Gopi releasing his held breath. Raghav silently held out the nail. "Hammer?" asked Gopi Raghav held out a hammer wrapped in newspapers. "You wait here. I will be back in a blink!" Gopi said and unwrapped the hammer from the newspaper. Carrying the hammer in one hand and the nail in the other, Gopi entered the park. The tall grass shone in the moonlight. Swings, merry-go-round, slide were all bathed in the moonlight. It looked as if they had newly arrived from the heavens. Gopi was shocked when he looked at the tomb. He could see only the roof and not the walls. It looked as if the roof was floating on the air. He froze for a moment. He blinked his eyes a few times and then observed the roof closely. Then,he chuckled softly to himself. He realized that it was an illusion
author: Shyamala V

title: Jealous Anansi
text: Anansi and Rabbit were friends. Anansi was jealous of Rabbit's wealth. Anansi took over Rabbit’s farm. He chased away Rabbit. Anansi sold all the crops. He got a lot of money. Anansi went home carrying his basket on his head. Anansi put the basket down. He went to shelter from the rain. The rain caused flooding, so Anansi hid in a hole. Vulture saw the basket and covered it with his wings. “This basket is mine,” said Vulture. “It is mine!” shouted Anansi. Vulture said, “I found money and maize unprotected.” The chief and his elders took time to decide who was right. Finally, they said, “Vulture is right. The basket is his.” Rabbit returned to his farm. Anansi had no money, or friends.
author: Ghanaian  Folktale

title: Akadeli's Lucky day
text: One day Akadeli, Lucy, Acharait and Mary went to the forest far from home to pick wild fruits. They held hands to cross the big river near the forest. They found a tree full of ripe fruits. The girls agreed to climb up the tree and to pick the fruits with their eyes closed. Lucy, Acharait and Mary did not close their eyes. Only Akadeli closed hers as she picked the fruits. When they opened their eyes, only Akadeli had picked unripe fruits. Lucy, Acharait and Mary laughed at Akadeli and left for home. Akadeli threw away the unripe fruits and began picking ripe ones. Soon, Akadeli filled her basket with ripe fruits. She set off alone, crossing the big river. Half way across the river, Akadeli's basket fell and was carried away. She was angry and began to cry. Before Akadeli got out of the water, she saw a big fish and grabbed it. As Akadeli carried the fish home, a hawk snatched it and flew away with it. Akadeli saw that the hawk had left behind a feather from its tail. Although she was disappointed, she picked up the feather and continued walking home. She came across a traditional wedding. People dancing were wearing grass on their heads instead of feathers as was the tradition. They took her feather and gave her a big bull! Akadeli reached home with her bull. Her parents and relatives were so happy. Lucy, Acharait and Mary wished they had not lied to Akadeli. It was a lucky day for Akadeli!
author: Simon Ipoo

title: Animals Run Away
text: An old woman had chickens and an old rooster. Her grandson visited her. She decided to kill the old rooster. The old rooster ran away to the big city. The old rooster met the cat running away from her boss. The old rooster and the cat met the dog running away. They were joined by a horse which was running away too. The animals came to a house. They saw thieves inside! The animals sang loudly to chase away the thieves. They ate the food they found in the house. The thieves returned later. The animals attacked them. The thieves ran away forever. The animals lived together happily in the house.
author: Cissy Kiwanuka  Luyiga

title: The Legend of the Lonely Dragon.
text: There was once a lonely and abandoned egg on the top of mount Fiji(sort of).It was under the peak!And Inside lay a baby dragon;as you shall see just now. When the egg hatched;the dragon craweled out and spred his soon - to - be strong wings.But,he had his ups and downs.Due to his loneliness he grew grumpy and cranky to any traveler or person he saw. But he realized his mistake.And so when a knight came to kill him the dragon,instead of trying to scare him away too;he apologized.The knight reported this unruly behavior to the king.The king himself went to the dragon's lair to confirm with the knight.Sure enough the dragon just stared at the king.....and bowed!His Highness understood w hat the dragon was trying to do.And so he ordered everybody to befriend Gopu;as he was named(The dragon not the knight or the king!).And hence people also started bringing him food.
author: hot dog
illustrator: Hari Kumar Nair; Nishith  Mehta; Priya Kuriyan; Somesh Kumar

title: My cute puppies
text: Once upon a time, there lived two puppies in a small playground.They were brothers and sisters.But one day an evil puppy came and shooed one of them away and the evil puppy was not letting the puppy in the playground again.The puppy inside the playground was now very worried and the puppy outside the playground ran on the road. on which there were many stores and there were many people there.He was lost and couldn't find his way home but at last tired of walking he saw a playground in front of him and guess what,that was his home. and the evil puppy was gone.They ran to each other and licked and hugged each other.and now they were happy to again be together.They never knew that they had parents but that was the moment when they saw two dogs heading towards them and then they got to know that they were there parents!And then they lived happily ever after.
author: pav bhaji

title: Magozwe Finds a Home
text: In a certain city, there lived street boys. The youngest of them was called Magozwe. When Magozwe was five years old, his parents died. He went to live with Uncle Bunu. Uncle Bunu was a bad man. Magozwe ran away and lived on the streets. Life on the street was difficult. The boys begged from people. One day, Magozwe found a storybook from the rubbish container. The book had pictures of a pilot. Magozwe wanted to be the best pilot ever. One day Magozwe met Thomas. Thomas took Magozwe and his friends to get food. Thomas asked Magozwe to read. Magozwe replied, “I do not know how to read.” Magozwe also said to Thomas, “I ran away from Uncle Bunu's home. He was a bad man.” Thomas asked Magozwe, “Do you want to learn to read?” He gave Magozwe a new storybook. Magozwe thought about going to school. He remembered what Uncle Bunu said. “ You are stupid. You do not know anything.” Magozwe was afraid. Thomas said, “Do not be afraid. You will be fine.” Thomas took Magozwe and the other boys to a home for children. They were all very happy. Magozwe went to school. He liked being in school. He worked very hard. One day Magozwe told Thomas, “I will be the best pilot ever!”
author: Ursula Nafula

title: Goat, the false king
text: Once upon a time, there was a goat called Igodhoobe*. Igodhoobe the goat was the king of farm animals and birds. He lived a good life. One day, Igodhoobe the goat called all the animals and birds to a meeting. *pronounced ee-god-who-buhe "My friends, I have called you because I had a dream," said the goat. All the animals and birds kept quiet. They listened to their king carefully. "I dreamed that there was no food or water left in the land. Many of our relatives died!" said the king. When the animals and the birds heard the dream, they were worried. "What shall we do?" asked the cat. The hen and the duck had an idea. They said, "Let each one of us bring food and put it in the king's store." All the animals agreed with this idea. The king made a rule. He said, "Get ropes. Tie up anyone who does not bring food to my store. Then carry him to me." But, soon after this, it was time for a new king to rule over the farm. All the animals and birds met and elected the cat as their new king. But the goat refused to agree that the cat was king. "I'm the king. There is no other king. I can't obey any other animal," said the goat. The animals took food to the new king's store. But the goat did not take anything. "When the goat was king, we all obeyed him. Now he does not want to obey our new king. What shall we do?" asked the cow. All the domestic animals and birds were angry. "He thinks he is different to us," they all muttered. The dog said, "I helped him when he was king. I did not sleep at night. I was always with him, ready to help." The sheep said, "I gave him my wool to cover his children." The pig said, "When he was king, he told his friends that I eat a lot. But I was often in his garden digging and weeding his maize and millet." The sheep asked, "What did he say? That you eat a lot? Did he think that he will be king forever?" Then the sheep added, "Let him understand that he is not king any more. I don't know why he thinks he is so important." All the animals laughed and agreed that the goat must take food to the new king. King Cat ordered the goat to come to him. When the animals went to fetch the goat, he was sitting on a chair with his legs crossed. "I shall not go to the cat. There is no other king except me. When you become a king, you are always a king," said the goat. "We will tie you with ropes and take you to the new king," said the sheep. So the cow tied the goat to her tail. She then pulled him to the king. The sheep, the duck, the dog, the pig, and the cock cheered as the cow pulled the goat. They all shouted, "Take this stubborn goat to our new king!" From that time, every goat refuses to move when it is pulled. It thinks that you are taking it to the king's court.
author: Alice  Nakasango

title: Who is The Next Ruler?
text: King Leopard was getting old. How will he choose the next king? King Leopard called animals to the party. He would announce his plan. After the party, King Leopard spoke. The animals listened. He said, “A contest will decided the next king.” One who counts to ten before the spear falls, will be king. Elephant pushed everyone aside, “I’m the biggest. I should be king.” Elephant only counted up to four. The spear fell. Boar pushed everyone saying, “I’m the strongest. I should be king.” Boar counted up to six and the spear fell. He left. Everyone said, “Big Elephant and strong Boar failed. Who can win?” Ape counted, “One! Two! Three! Four! Five! Six! Seven!” He cried. King Leopard said, “Ape, you only get one chance.” Ape left. Some animals started leaving. Then, Little Antelope said, “Let me try.” King Leopard shouted, “Give Antelope a chance. Let her try.” Antelope said, “Five and five is ten.” The spear fell down. The contest showed the smartest animal. Antelope was queen after leopard.
author: Athieno  Gertrude; Owino  Ogot

title: Under  The  Sea
text: It was past Preethi's bedtime.''5 more minutes maa!even teddy wants to play.''﻿ ﻿''Teddy can wait;Preethi.'' ﻿Slowly,she fell asleep ﻿.And started dreaming a wonderful dream. She felt something cold lapping against her feet and found herself at the beach. She found herself being sucked into the ocean. Surprisingly, she could breathe underwater.Suddenly(again!)the water gently expelled her and dragged her on shore. She saw her mom above her.''Wake up Preethi!''Coming maa.I can't wait to tell you about my dream!''
author: hot dog
illustrator: Clyde   Beech; Dorian  Dutrieux; Muniza Shariq; Rijuta Ghate; Rohit Kelkar; Stephen Wallace; Sunaina  Coelho; Suvidha Mistry

title: Captain Mayuri
text: Today, Manik and I are going home early from school. Amma told us that our aunt Mayuri is visiting. Mayuri is more like an elder sister to us than an aunt. We like her a lot. She tells us many stories. But, the best story she tells us is always about how her dream came true. As a child, she loved playing with paper planes. She would often dream about planes. She wanted to become a pilot. So, she worked hard in school and college. She topped all her classes and studied towards becoming a pilot. Someday, she would fly a plane. Someday, she would become Captain Mayuri. And the day came quite soon! She passed all the tests and donned her pilot's uniform. She was now flying a plane! Mayuri Aunty points out towards the sky. Look, that is the kind of the plane I fly these days. And you know what they all call me there? "Captain Mayuri!" We are so happy hearing this, we all dance together. Believe in your dreams, she tells us.
author: Mamta D
illustrator: Abhishek Choudhury; Lavanya Karthik; Namrata  Gosavi; Pia Meenakshi; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: A Girl Called Norah
text: This is Norah. Norah's doll is called Sellah. Norah loves Sellah very much. She plays and sleeps with Sellah every night. One day, Norah was very worried because she could not find Sellah. Norah's mother had washed Sellah. Norah went to her mother crying, "I can't find Sellah." Before Norah slept, her mother brought Sellah to her. Norah jumped out of bed and danced with Sellah. Norah hugged her mother and thanked her for cleaning Sellah.
author: Annet  Ssebaggala

title: Lion's shoes
text: Long ago, a lion, a fox, an ape and a hyena lived together. The ape and the hyena plotted to harm the fox. They secretly went to meet the lion. "Lion, you are much respected, but why don't you have shoes?" the ape asked the lion. "You are right. Who can make shoes for me?" asked the lion. "The fox can make shoes for you," replied the hyena. "Call the fox," said the lion. The fox came, and the lion told her to make shoes for him. "The best shoes are made from the skins of apes and hyenas," whispered the fox. "I want the finest shoes," said the lion. So he killed the hyena and the ape. He gave their skins to the fox. The fox was worried that the lion would kill her if she did not make the shoes. She put the skins into the river. The lion became impatient. "Where are my shoes?" he growled. Fox replied, "I am still waiting for the skins to soften." The next morning, the fox came running from the river. She told the lion, "Someone just like you is guarding the skins. I can't get them!" The lion rushed to the river. He saw his own reflection in the water, and jumped in to fight! The lion drowned, leaving the fox alone.
author: Angesom  Abadi

title: Dhritiman the Donkey
text: A few months ago I went to meet my friend, Dhritiman. Dhritiman is a donkey. The first time met him, I didn’t know how to say his name. He looked at me kindly and said, Let me make it easier for you.” Say “Dhree” I repeated after him, "Dhree" Say “Tiii” I repeated after him “Tiiii” Say “Munn!” I repeated after him Munn! Now, say them together! I slowly said out each word, Dhree Ti Munn. Then I said the same words faster, Dhritiman! Yes, I got it. What do you do? I asked him. He replied, I carry loads for people. He said, I am a sturdy animal, my back can bear weight. So I carry things for people. What things? I asked. Mostly clothes and such stuff. Sometimes, water. The washermen, dhobis, have many clothes to be carried to the open air laundry. They wash clothes of other people there. And then they bring back the dried clothes. On my back. So I carry the clothes to and fro. But in the mountains, my cousins carry heavy burdens up the slopes. The donkeys there are stronger. Every day they go up and down the mountains, carrying big loads. Dhritiman tells me many such things. He has been to many places. I liked to hear his stories. One day, the washerman moved away to his village and took Dhritiman with him. After that, I never saw Dhritiman again.
author: Mamta D
illustrator: 211 Studio; Bianca de Jong; Janaagraha; Jess  Jardim-Wedepohl; Megan Andrews; Natalie  Edwards; Shanti Devi; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Devil's scarf
text: There was a rich man who looked for a wife for a long time. When he married, he had a big ceremony that was blessed by the elders. After years of marriage, the man and woman began to worry because they did not have a child. The woman prayed for a child again and again. But she still did not become pregnant. One day, tired of waiting, she said, “Devil, if you give me a child, I will make a beautiful scarf for you.” The following month, she became pregnant. She was happy and made the scarf which she had promised. The woman gave birth to a baby boy. Everybody rejoiced with her. She wanted to give the scarf to the devil but realised that she did not know how to find him. So she visited an elder and asked him for advice. The elder said, “To find the devil, go near the church. You will find two men standing before a wise man. These two have been fighting. The one who refuses to reconcile and leaves in anger is the devil! Follow him and give him this scarf.” The woman went near the church. She saw two men standing before a wise man. The wise man said, “Enough! It's time to forgive each other from the heart.” One of the men bent forward to ask for forgiveness. The other one refused and walked away. The woman called after him, “Wait! I have something for you.” She offered him the scarf. The angry man asked, “What is this?” The woman answered, “It is your present.” He replied, “I do not understand why you are giving me this present.” The woman told him the story. She said, “You are the man who refused to apologise. That means you are the devil.” She stretched out her hand to give him the scarf. This man ran back to the church. He knelt down in front of the other man and said to him, “I forgive you. Forgive me too.” The other man also knelt. They hugged each other. The woman continues to search for the devil. Make sure the scarf does not belong to you!
author: Azeb Worku  Sibane

title: Petros and his Dog
text: Once upon a time, there was a boy called Petros. He was a very clever student. He came first in his class and his parents were proud of him. But Petros wished he had a brother, a sister, or a pet to play with. One day he asked his mom, "Can I play outside? I have studied all morning and I want to play with my friends now." His mom replied, "All right! Go, but don't be late!" On the way to the playground, Petros saw something unusual. It was a little dog with white and brown spots. The dog was stuck in a hole and he was scared. "Don't worry, I won't hurt you. I will help you," said Petros. Petros helped the dog out of the hole. He barked with joy, dancing around the boy and licking him. "You are going to be my dog," said Petros happily as they continued to the playground. The dog ran far ahead. When Petros' friends saw the dog running towards them, they said, "This dog might be dangerous. It might bite us." They picked up stones and threw them at the little dog. Petros was running and shouting for his friends to stop. The friends did not hear Petros. The small dog ran as fast as he could to save his life. Then he hid from the boys who were chasing him. They did not find him. Petros' friends went back to the playground and found Petros crying. "What is wrong?" asked one of them. "You chased my dog!" cried Petros. They were shocked and said, "We didn't know it was your dog. We're sorry. Let's find him." "It's no use. We will never find my dog," said Petros in a hopeless voice. "Yes, we will find him. Get up Petros, we will find your dog. We must not lose hope," his friends said, consoling him. Petros and his friends searched for the dog all afternoon until they got tired. Finally, Petros said, "There is one last place where the dog could be. If we don't find him there, I will search no more. Let's go to the river." When the dog saw the boys coming, he was scared. He tried to cross the river but he was scared of the water. He was about to jump into the river, when he heard Petros calling, "Stop, don't jump!" The dog turned around, saw Petros and ran to him. Petros hugged the dog and the dog licked Petros's face. "My friend! I thought you were gone forever!" cried Petros. Back at the playground, Petros gave his friends some advice. "Before you make decisions, think about what could happen as a result. Be careful of hurting others." His friends thought about his words and said, "We are sorry. The dog will be our friend too."
author: Bethelihem  Waltenegus

title: Rani's First Day at School
text: I am Rani. This is my Mummy. Today is my first day at school! Mummy is holding my hand and walking with me. “I am grown up now,” I say. “Leave my hand, let me walk alone” Mummy holds my hand very tight. There are many children near the school. Some come by bus. Some come by car. Some come by rickshaw. Some cycle and some walk like me. We reach the school gate. Mummy lets go of my hand. S he stays at the gate. I have to go inside alone. There are many new faces around me. I take one step. I take another step. I look back. Mummy gets smaller as I walk away. Will she disappear? I run back to Mummy. I do not feel so grown up now. I hold her hand. “Do not go away,” I say. All children are in the school now. I am alone outside. The teacher comes out. She smiles at me. I smile back. Mummy says, "Rani, I will be here when you come out." I let go of her hand. She waves to me. I run inside. Mummy will be there after school!
author: Riya Parikh

title: The Big Book of Rakshasas
text: everywhere! Here, there, and in your hair! Some Rakshasas who have claws and some others, who have furry little paws Some Rakshasas with all their teeth, and some others who have lost their teeth by eating too many sweets! Some Rakshasas who scream and shout and some others who smell very foul Some Rakshasas who loudly sneeze ACH-CHOO, ACH-CHOO! And some others whose noses are left ﻿ full of goo Some Rakshasas whose stomachs wiggle and jiggle, and some others who always giggle! Some Rakshasas who glow in the night, and some others who can't be seen even in the light! Some Rakshasas who love a treat, and some others who feast on your hand and feet! Some Rakshasas who are sneaky and sly, and some others whose behinds are leaky and they lie! Some Rakshasas who fly high, and some others who peep out of the window and pry! Some Rakshasas who are out and roam, and some others who hide inside your home!
author: Riya Parikh
