title: How to Solve a Problem like Himani
text: March 28 It’s so hot here! Golu was very naughty today. She climbed up a slant and would not come down. Silly goat! Seema and Gullu had to help me get her down. March 30 I can see the snow-capped Himalayan peaks–Nandakot, Maiktoli, Panchachuli, Chaukhamba. But Kumaon is dry. Gullu and I help Ija and Baujyu* get water from the pump down the road, or from the stream further down. Ooof! Wish the water could reach us directly from the snowy mountains. Drinking water is difficult to get even in January, when it snows. *Ija and Baujyu: Kumaoni words for ‘mother’ and ‘father’. April 2 Our ten-day summer workshop with Reena didi started today. She has come from Mumbai. She asked us thousands of questions! What do you like about school? What do you not like about school? How do you commute to school? Suddenly she turned to me and asked the meaning of my name. “Himani means snow,” I said. Why does she ask so many questions? April 3 What a fun day it was! We played a game. One of us needed to think of a problem that we might have faced and state it in the form of a question. Then another classmate had to ask a question related to it. It was almost like a chain story. We had so many questions! How can we get clean drinking water in school? Why do we need clean water? Where will the water come from? Why can’t we have a pipe straight from the melting glaciers? Why do you ask such questions? Why don’t we concentrate on our water problem? Why can’t we have a water filter? Where will we get a water filter from? Why can’t we make it? Who knows how to make one? SOLVE ANY PROBLEM, STEP BY STEP > Identify the problem. > Find out everything you can about the problem. > Discuss. > Decide on the most suitable idea. > Try it out. > If you succeed, very good! > If not, try another idea. April 4 We were surfing the Internet when I found this chart: Could we really solve a problem using this method? April 5 At school, we made a list of our problems. How many problems do we have? BIG PROBLEMS Neighbours who get violent after drinking No hospital or clinic near by Leeches in our socks during the rains. No direct water at home or school Landslides Slippery roads to school during the monsoon PROBLEMS WE CAN SOLVE Plastic bottles everywhere Unclean drinking water Heavy school bag Unlit paths at night April 6 Worked with Ija and Baujyu in the cauliflower patch. Then ran to school for problem-solving day! We went out in pairs to the library, and to talk to our teachers and to each other. Then we came back to class. 1. Identify: The problem is unfiltered drinking water at school. Students keep falling sick because of this. 2. Find out: Why is getting clean water a problem here? Many streams around Kumaon are supposed to have pure water. There are no streams near our school. 3. Discuss: We found out that some people use cloth. This only filters bigger sediments, not harmful bacteria. Manorama said they have a small water filter at home. Moringa seeds in water pots help purify water, said a teacher. 4. Decide: Would a water purifier help us? Pebbles Moringa Seeds Coarse Sand Charcoal Fine Sand Cloth Try it out! We all drew water filters! We decided we needed one that could be attached to the nozzle of our water drum. Santosh bhai and Ashish bhai, our seniors, helped us make a water filter based on our drawings. They have taken a few days off from college to make a water catchment system in our school. The filtered water tasted so fresh and clean! April 11 In the last three days, we’ve done a lot of art. We have applied the problem-solving method to come up with more ideas. Cycle Plough Does not require cattle or a tractor to pull it. Good for narrow step farms. Bottle Torch Torch made with recycled parts. Fitted inside a discarded plastic bottle, so that dampness does not spoil it. Dampness spoils battery-operated torches very quickly in this region. Mini-irrigator Drip irrigation for crops like grapes that need soil to stay hydrated. Made with recycled water bottles, attached to plants like IV tubes in hospitals. April 13 Now that the workshop is over, we’re all busy with harvesting and packing apricots, pears, apples and rhododendron flowers. Ija and Baujyu are so nimble and good at picking fruits! Not me. Yesterday, I slipped and twisted my ankle while picking fruit. No fracture, thank God! I wish I had a gadget that could pick fruits for me! Maybe we could train Golu and the other goats to pick fruits, ha, ha. Seriously, how wonderful it would be to have an efficient, safe, eco-friendly apple-picking machine! Satkhol Tales This story was inspired by the work of The Walking School Bus during their Himalayan Expeditions in 2018. TWSB works towards providing safe transport, nutrition, and innovative literacy programmes. Their contest ‘Search for Jugaad’ sought inventive and scalable ideas that could enable people to find local solutions to challenges of education specific to their community. The images in this story were drawn by Divya, Manasa, Pooja, Deepanshu J, Ritesh, Lakshit, Ujwal, Deepanshu N and Pushpa—students of class 3-8 of Himalayan Public School, Uttarakhand. Over 80 students were part of the art classes conducted by TWSB.

title: Tutu and Titu
text: One morning Tutu was moving on the Sand. It looked as if she was searching for something. Puzzled by this unusual behaviour, Titu and his dad followed Tutu. After reaching a point Tutu started digging the sand. Titu wanted to know why his friend Tutu was doing this. He asked “What is happening Papa, Is Tutu alright?”. His dad replied with a smile, “Titu, Tutu is making his nest. Turtles lay their egg in a nest that is dug out of the sand. They will lay eggs and go back to water.” Titu was excited, “Dad, how can a turtle breath out of water?” Dad replied, “That’s the gift of god to the turtles. Only when they have to lay their eggs they come out of the water. They walk all the way to search for a good spot in the shore. They lay their eggs and then go back to water; It is quite tiresome for the turtles” "Amazing!" said Titu and started watching Tutu with his eyes wide open. By then, Tutu had finished digging the nest and started laying eggs. Of course Titu could only see Tutu's big shell and nothing else. He started asking questions again. "But Papa why is Tutu digging a huge pit for just one egg? Are Turtles eggs so big?" Titu was excited, “Dad, how can a turtle breathe out of water?” Dad replied, “That’s the gift of God to the turtles. Only when they have to lay their eggs they come out of the water. They walk all the way to search for a good spot on the shore. They lay their eggs and then go back to water; It is quite tiresome for the turtles” "Amazing!" said Titu and started watching Tutu with his eyes wide open. By then, Tutu had finished digging the nest and started laying eggs. Of course Titu could only see Tutu's big shell and nothing else. He started asking questions again. "But Papa why is Tutu digging a huge pit for just one egg? Are Turtles eggs so big?" “No my son, Tutu will lay around 100 to 200 eggs in the nest.” replied dad. Titu was super excited that he wouldn't stop. He again asked “Dad, how long should I wait to see the tiny turtles?”. "atleast 45 days dear son", said dad. Titu couldn't wait for that long. He wanted to see the baby turtles immediately Meanwhile, Tutu had started moving back to the sea after laying the eggs. Titu understood the difficulty involved in the entire process. Turtles have to move to the land, dig the nest, lay eggs and go back again. While he was busy thinking about how Tutu would be tired and hungry, he saw Tutu heading towards danger. Tutu was about to eat a plastic cover that was littered on the beach. Dad saw this and alarmed, Titu. “Run and pick the plastic cover before Tutu eats it mistaking it for food. Titu was quick to respond. He picked the cover just in time. Also carefully checked the track of Tutu and cleared all the plastic cover on the way. Titu watched Tutu moved safely towards the sea. Titu left the beach thinking about how plastics could turn harmful to turtles like Tutu. While he reached home, he had made a decision. From next day, clearing plastic waste from the beach became his new hobby. As usual Tutu visited the shore everyday and Titu had fun watching her. He was counting the days and could not wait to watch the hatchlings creep towards the ocean. It was the 48 th day. Titu came earlier than usual and was waiting near the nest. Baby turtles came out one by one and Titu's joy knew no bound. He was thrilled while he held the baby turtle in his palm. Titu felt that the young hatchling felt safe in his palm. He went close to the baby turtle and said with a smile, "I will protect you". Suddenly, he heard cawing crows and barking dogs surrounding the nest. They were ready to catch the turtles and gulp them. Titu's heartbeat became faster. He somehow wanted to save the hatchlings. With the help of his dad, he built a fence and laid a net over the fence and extended it to the sea so that the crows and dogs wouldn't reach the hatchlings. The Tiny hatchlings started peeking one by one out of the sand and moved towards the beach. It was the most beautiful parade one could ever witness. Titu felt very happy and accomplished. The tiny turtles reached the water safely. From next morning, when Titu had Tutu and a bale of little turtles to play with him. FACTS: Females turtle come ashore on a sandy beach to nest a few weeks after mating. Females usually nest during the warmest months of the year. Females of most species usually come ashore at night, alone, most often during high tide. A female sea turtle crawls above the high tide line and, using her front flippers, digs out a “body pit.” Then using her hind flippers, she digs an egg cavity. The female covers the nest with sand using her hind flippers. Burying the eggs serves three purposes: it helps protect the eggs from surface predators; it helps keep the soft, porous shells moist, thus protecting them from drying out; and it helps the eggs maintain proper temperature. Between the months of December and April each year, several thousand Olive Ridley turtles come to the sandy beaches along the outskirts of Chennai to lay their eggs. For nearly four decades now, several dozen volunteers meet at various spots along the coast to patrol the beaches at night. When they come across a turtle laying eggs, they mark the nest and collect the eggs for hatching in an incubator. 45 to 60 days later, the hatchlings are brought to the same spot and released close to the water's edge. Volunteers stand in the water with torches to guide the hatchlings towards the sea. This interference with nature is necessary because the beaches are not protected and human habitation has encroached almost up to the waterline.

Because in the spot where it grew was a place were nothing had grown for 34 yrs. Oh! I just forgot to introduce myself... I am Aniket, a flower enthusiast and a bright learner. My family was getting ready for a party. I came out and said, " Why do you need a party when the plant growing there only is a party. ". Everybody said " We are having a party for both........ You are getting a brother or sister. I was amazed by what they said. I rejoiced in the only way I could..... I cleaned the house like never before, everything sparkled. My dog also raised his head like a loyal dog. He felt proud about what was going on around the house. But, the concentration on the flower was gone. It was drying up. Now everybody had diverted attention to the flower that was going to bloom. Now, I started to make a journal on the flower grow. It was day 3 and it had grown very nicely. It was ridiculous to think that it would never grow to be a flower. I drew and wrote about its surroundings and everything. It's right now the 5th month of my mom's pregnancy. The flower was also going to bloom when it was going to be time. It was amazing that it was surviving in an area where there was very little sunlight. Water that was very important for it was being given to it very nicely........... 7 months later....... My mom in the hospital and me waiting for this flower to bloom. I got to know that my mom had got a baby girl. I was pleased but, at the exact same time, my flower bloomed.
author: Amogh Deshpande-
illustrator: Fahad Faizal; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Partho Sengupta

title: Have You Seen Sundari?
text: Have you seen Sundari? Sundari is green and loves to hide. Is Sundari hiding among the water lilies? Or between the skyflowers? Is Sundari hiding with the fishing cat? Or with the mud crabs? Is Sundari hiding in the mangrove? Or in the salty water? Is Sundari hiding inside the weaver bird’s nest? “There you are, Sundari!” “Oh, I missed you so much. Where have you been?”
author: Aindri C

title: Rose and Rocky's War On Insects
text: Rocky bleated when he spotted the ants. Rose danced all over them. BAAAA! Rocky stomped his hooves when he saw the beetles. Rose hopped on them, one by one. Crunch! Crunch! Rocky ran in circles chasing the bees. Rose waved her arms at them. “What are you doing, Rose?” Amma asked. “We are killing all the insects, Amma.” “BUT WHY?” “Insects sting us. They bite us. They make us itch and scratch,” said Rose. Rocky bleated in agreement. BAAAAAA! “Do you like honey, Rose?” Amma asked. “On my bread,” Rose said. “Who do you think makes the honey?” Amma asked, pointing to a bee. “Oh!” said Rose. “And do you like eating vegetables from the garden, Rocky?” Amma asked. Rocky grinned as widely as a goat can grin. “Who do you think keeps the vegetables safe from hungry bugs?” Amma asked. “And the ants,” Amma said. They take away all the rubbish.” “So without insects, we’d have no honey, no vegetables and a lot of dead cockroaches?” Rose asked. “Exactly!” said Amma. “Then what do we do, Amma?”
author: Annie Besant

title: King's Park
text: They were extremely engrossed in the game and did not realize that they had crossed the old road. They were now in King's Park. Although it was called King's Park, there was nothing majestic about it. Instead of a lawn, there was knee high grass which was not removed by the gardener for a long time. Once upon a time flowery bushes grew here. They were now withered, due to lack of water after the last water- tap was damaged. There were some swings which had become so old and worn out, that they had to be wrapped around the poles. The slide was in a bad state too. Only two steps remained of the stair of the slide. Also there were too many dangerous holes in the metal slide. Anyone could tear their clothes and get hurt while sliding on it. And the merry-go-round......was too rusted to rotate smoothly. And if at all it turned around, it creaked and made frightening sounds, scaring the children away. In short, King's Park was no longer an attraction for the children but a place to be avoided. If any child wanted to go for an outing with his father and if the father said, "Let's go to King"s Park?", the child lost interest. The kingdom of King's Park was in a bad state of affairs. In the center of the park was a small graveyard which did not have a proper compound wall. In spite of this, the neighbouring children would come to the park to play. No one prevented them from entering the park. In the graveyard there was a rectangular tomb which, over the period, was reduced to a small mound and looked like a slight hunch on the surface of the earth. It was said that a cruel king lay buried in the tomb. In his kingdom, it was forbidden to read or write. The King thought that if the people were educated, they would revolt against him and snatch away his throne. Thus there were no schools or libraries in the country. If any books were found in a house, the king would burn the whole house down. In the kingdom there lived a wise man, who was famous in the whole world. People from faraway lands came to listen to him. The tyrant King did not like the wise man, but was helpless. The wise man was very popular and no one could go against him. The king waited for an opportunity to trap the wise man and finally one day, he caught him in a false case of robbery and hung him to death. It was a full moon night when the wise man was put to death. The King lost his peace of mind after this incidence. On every full moon night he would go crazy.Whenever he saw a rope, he would make a loop and put it around his neck and try to hang himself. the guards tried their best to save him. But one day, the guards made a mistake. They could not save the King, who choked to death with the rope, on a full moon night. People said that even after his death the King was not at peace. Even inside the grave he would go crazy. On every full moon night the King would come out of his grave and wander all around the graveyard. If he spotted any passerby who happened to be there, the King would catch hold of him and desperately ask for a rope...."I want a rope......I want a rope", he would plead. The poor passerby would faint before he could get the rope. As the days passed, fewer and fewer people visited the park. It was sunset and the children were playing noisily in the park. It was Zulfi's turn to keep the den. He shut his eyes with both hands and started counting..one...two....three..and the children ran hither and thither to find a place to hide. 6....7.......8...... All the children had already hid themselves in some place or the other. Ashahar was the only kid who had not yet found a place to hide.......9 Ashahar had now only the graveyard to hide in......10 Zulfi just finished counting when Ashahar jumped right into the graveyard. But Zulfi had seen him jumping. He stood still and screamed. "No Ashahar! Not there!" There was fear in Zulfi's voice, Ashahar came out and looked surprisingly at him and asked, " What happened? Why did you scream so loudly?" " You should not hide there!" exclaimed Zulfi. " Why? What is there?" "There is a tomb! The King's tomb." "So what?" "Don't you know what happens there on every a full moon night?" On hearing Zulfi, Ashahar laughed aloud. Zulfi could not understand the meaning of this laughter and he looked confused. Ashahar continued laughing at the confused Zulfi. Finally he stopped laughing and started calling all the children. "Pinky....Kasni....Sheelu....Dharma.....Badku.... every one come out. Who wants to play with this cowardly mouse. Everybody come here quickly!" The children did not know what was happening. All of them came out of their hiding places. "Hey! Why are you fighting?" All the kids asked at the same time. " Who will want to play with him," Ashahar said pointing at Zulfi and started laughing again. " Why, what happened?"Kasni asked, coming forward. "He says not to go in the graveyard. Someone will catch you.", said Ashahar. " He is right!", she exclaimed supporting Zulfi. " You don't know what goes on there." Sheelu was on Kasni's side. "Arre, if Ashahar wants to hide there, let him. Why are you jealous?", Badku tried to be fare. h " If Ashahar hides in the graveyard,someone will have to go inside to find him? Tell me who will go inside the graveyard, near the tomb?", asked Sheela. Before anyone could reply, Ashahar blurted out. "All of you are scared......frightened mice....I do not want to play with you." None of the children liked to be challenged this way. Zulfi was emboldened when he saw that most of the children were on his side. He looked into Ashahar's eyes and said, " You think you are very brave?" Ashahar replied smuggly, " I not only think I am brave, I am brave." " Can you enter the graveyard at night?" " Yes I can enter." " On a full moon night too?" "Yes, on a full moon night too!" " Towards the head side of the tomb?" " Yes, towards the head side of the tomb." " So it is decided that, on the next full moon night you will visit the graveyard and pitch a long iron nail in the ground near the head side of tomb." "Agreed, go on." " If you win, all the kids will give you a bat, a cricket bat,and if you lose...." " That will not happen, so it is not necessary to discuss about it," Ashahar said proudly. Everybody kept quiet as they knew he was argumentative. Now the children wanted to know, when it would be full moon night. Kasni pointed out at the sky. Everyone looked up. A big, disc like, moon seems to smile at them. It was full moon night that day. " Okay! Tonight will do." Ashahar agreed confidently, "But who will bring the nail and hammer?" " I will bring them," Zulfi said, as he did not want to lose the opportunity. "Alright we will meet later, at 10 pm sharp!" Ashahar left stomping the grass with his feet. The other children also went away to their respective homes. At 10 pm the full moon was shining lustrously, as if someone had stuck a 'bindi' on the forehead of the blue sky. Ashahar looked at the clock often. He became impatient. At last, the clock struck 10 pm. He looked at the sitting room. All his family members had gone to their rooms except his elder brother. He was engrossed in watching 'Comedy Circus' show on the T.V. and therefore did not notice anything. Ashahar quietly locked his room and tip toed outside. As soon as he was out of the house, he ran towards King's Park. When he reached there, he saw Zulfi already standing at the broken gate. Ashahar looked all around and regained his breath. Nobody was inside the park, nor outside. "Did you bring the nail?", Ashahar was panting. Zulfi slowly handed over the nail to him. "And hammer?" The hammer, wrapped in the newspaper, was also there. "Now you wait here.... I will go and come back soon," Ashahar said, throwing away the newspaper wrapping. With the big nail in one hand and the hammer in the other, Ashahar entered the gate. The tall grass inside, shimmered in the moonlight. The swing, merry-go-round, the slide and everything else was immersed in the milky white moonlight. Each and every object looked strange, as if it came from a magical land. Ashahar stared at the tomb and was shocked to see the dome floating in the air and the base missing. Ashahar was shaken for a second but soon realized that it was the play of light and shadow. He looked carefully at the tomb, and laughed at himself. The base was in it's place.It was a trick of the moonlight, some parts were lit and others remained in a shadow causing such illusions. Ashahar moved forward. Now he was near the tomb. Moonlight seeped through the broken lattice of the small windows and fell on the tomb which looked milky white. Ashahar stepped on the verandah and saw as if the tomb was turning over. His whole body quivered with fear. He gathered some courage to put a foot forward. He could not lift his foot, it was stuck in the soil. He pulled his leg hard and the strap of his slipper broke. He was sure something unusual would happen.For a moment he thought he should not have got into this trouble. He immediately put these thoughts aside and picked up his broken slipper. It was all soggy with wet mud. He shook the slippers off his feet, threw them aside and climbed the verandah. As he looked inside, once again he felt as if he saw the tomb turning from side to side. He shrank with fear. He closed his eyes and muttered to himself. When he regained some courage, he opened his eyes. The tomb was in it's place. It had not moved on either side. His heart was beating very fast. He was no longer the same Ashahar as in the evening. "I should not have have taken this challenge,"......again the same thoughts came to his mind. He took the nail and hammer and quickly went forward. He looked around the tomb. he saw patches of moonlight everywhere. He looked upwards at the roof......what was that? A big, black blob was hanging from the ceiling of the roof. As soon as Ashahar looked up, the blob came towards him with the speed of a missile. One.....two.....three....The blob had multiplied into many. Before Ashahar could even think, the blobs were slapping him several times all over his head,forehead and cheeks.He was startled and he fell to the ground near the head side of the tomb. The flock of bats then flew to another end of the ceiling. Ashahar was terrified. " Now if there is a moment's delay........" Ashahar did not give a second thought,, he placed the nail near the head side of the tomb and hammered it into the ground with force. As his hands were trembling,he could not hit hard. He tried again.....THUD....he was frightened at the sound made by the hammer. The nail was deep and firm in the ground, Ashahar decided to get up and flee. He rose, full of energy and happiness for accomplishing the challenge, but he could not stand. Dhaap! He fell to the ground where he sat. Someone was pulling his shirt. He tried to get up once again with all his might, but he fell so badly that his head was hurt. He tried to get up once more, with the little strength he had, but fell again. " Is the tomb pulling me down?" he thought and his body turned cold. The tomb seems to be turning round and round, the walls were moving in his direction......faster and faster.....Just before he fainted he heard someone whispering...."Rope! Give me the rope." After that Ashahar went blank. When Ashahar woke up, he was in his own home. The whole house was full of people and everyone was looking at him. Zulfi touched his forehead and said, "Nothing happened Buddy! You nailed your shirt t to he ground..... maybe because you were too scared!" Everybody laughed and Ashahar closed his eyes and blushed. "Look, this is for you," he heard Zulfi's voice. He opened his eyes and saw a brand new bat in Zulfi's hands. Ashahar was amazed to see it. "All our friends knew that you would come to the graveyard and win the challenge. There was a small problem though...so what? Come on, hold this bat!" Once again Ashahar closed his eyes, but this time not out of shame, but to thank his friends.
author: Kumudini Kondhalkar

title: BAREFOOT
text: Ravi gets a pair of slippers as a gift from his dad. Ravi wears the slippers to school. Ravi learns numbers at school. Ravi keeps thinking about numbers and trips over a stone. One of his slippers gets broken. He is worried. He tries to mend the slipper at night. After dinner his grandma says it is always good to play barefoot in soil. The next day Ravi happily plays barefoot. It is always good to play barefoot in soil.
author: Sumaiyah Akrami
illustrator: Harshvardhan Gantha; Imile  Wepener; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Prashant Soni; Sanjay Sarkar; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Tapas Guha

title: What are Mammals
text: What are Mammals?Mammals are a warm-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that is distinguished by the possession of hair or fur, females that secrete milk for the nourishment of the young. Mammals like to eat meat.They don't eat leafs.Some live in a group which is called also pack.And some mammals live lonely.There are 5,000 species of mammals. Mammals can be divided into three more groups based on how their babies develop. Mammals hunt by ruining.A ll mammals have fur or hair. Humans are mammals and so are dogs, whales, elephants, and horses etc.Some mammals can fly and not fly. instead of laying eggs like birds.These mammals are called placental mammals. Some mammals are great at ruining and some are great at strength.Some mammals are cats ad not cats.like the lions,cheetahs,leopards,tiger etc.
author: Agastya Reddy kolli
illustrator: Muniza Shariq; Radha Rangarajan; Santhosh Krishnamoorthy; Saurabh Sawant

title: Coral Reef
text: Starfish, sea urchins and crustaceans are the most commonly found invertebrates on coral reefs, and countless species of fish including seahorses and eels can also be spotted with ease. Many species of sea snakes live in coastal waters particularly around southeast Asia, hunting small fish and eels in the coral reefs. Millions of speeches life in and around coral reefs.Coral reefs are home to millions of speeches. Hidden beneath the ocean waters,coral reefs teem with life. Fish,coral, lobsters, clams, seahorses, sponges, and sea turtles are only a few of the thousands of creatures that rely on reefs for their survival. The coral reefs are really colorful habitats in the water.Even sharks live in coral reefs.To lay there eggs too.Some of the fish protect the coral.Like the parrot fish they eat the allege from the coral. A coral reef is made of thin layers of calcium carbonate. Coral polyps form a living mat over a calcium carbonate skeleton. Coral reefs are located in tropical oceans near the equator. The largest coral reef is the Great Barrier Reef in Australia. The second largest coral reef can be found off the coast of Belize, in control America. Other reefs are found in Hawaii, the Red sea, and other areas in tropical oceans. And unlike plants, corals do not make their own food. Corals are in fact animals.
author: Agastya Reddy kolli

title: Fish
text: There are Amphibians and sea animals which are capable for living in water and there body designs help them to live in water.Marine life is incredibly varied, and includes mammal, fish, single-celled organisms, coral, eels, algae, plankton Whales, dolphins, porpoises, walruses, manatees, seals, and sea otters are all mammals that live in the oceans. Some, like seals and sea otters, can also live on land, but they spend most of their time underwater. There are Many Many Many fish in the sea and even rivers.All animals depend on them.They are the most em portent ecosystem in the world.Even trees depend on them.There are a lot of fish.And there are a lot of fish speeches. Some water creatures can be pet's.Humans are distorting their habitat which is water.With plastic.And fish populations are decreasing then other animal speeches can also decreasing. It is true that some fish can spend the winter frozen in ice and come out swimming once the ice melts. Not all fish get caught in the ice, of course. Ponds and lakes freeze from the top down, meaning that beneath the icy surface there is usually a layer of liquid water where fish swim. Few animals in the water die because of under water Tornadoes.U nder Water Tornadoes are very very very Dangerous. The plastic can not fall apart, but in the ocean it breaks up into small particles the size of the plankton that the fish eat. The debris will accumulate over time in the digestive system of the fish, which will no longer be able to feed properly and eventually die.
author: Agastya Reddy kolli
illustrator: Mamun Hossain; Mangkonephet  Sayasane; Salim  Kasamba
