title: MAYA GOES TO SCHOOL!!!!
text: Maya was a very obedient girl. She liked her mother and father so much. She was always busy doing chores at home or playing with her parrot, Paro. She likes her friend very much. Her home was in the centre of a large field. she always helped her parents when it was har vest time. It was a lot of hard work for the 5 year old Maya. Maya had a beautiful flower garden that she had in her backyard. She liked the flowers very much and always watered them on time. She had tulips and gladiolas. She also had many v egetables like cluster beans and tomatoes. Maya also had a older brother, Shyam. He always got up late in the morning and went to school. Their mom would always gi ve him a lot to eat. But, Maya was not allowed. Her parents needed Maya at home to help them with the chores. While her brother went to school, Maya would finish all her work and wait for him to return so that she could listen to the tales he told about school and his friends. She lo ved listening to Shyam. Maya always wondered how the elephant trumpets and how it is so strong. She wanted to learn how the elephant's ears were so big and why it had wrinkles all o v er it. She looked at the sky and wondered how the clouds were white and why they turned black when it was about to rain. She was eager to find out why the sun didn't fall down from the sky. Maya asked her brother but he wouldn't tell her. He says,"Go find out for yourself, Maya.". So, she has decided to ask her parents to take her to school too, like Shyam. Maya begged her parents to let her go to school. they say,"You have a lot to do at home, Maya. Why do you want to go to school?". But Maya insists them to let her go and they agree to take her to school. ﻿Maya soon went to school with her brother. She was extremely happy. Maya foung out why the elephant had wrinkles and the sun didn't fall from the sky. Her teacher was kind to her and taught her a lot of new things. She taught her father many new things about farm animals and told her mother how the sunlight helps the plant in preparing its own food. She learnt a lot!!!! Maya now knows each and every flower in her garden. Maya loves school!!
author: Kotravai Vanavan
illustrator: Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lily Banerjee; Michael  Sagikwa; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Rohit Karandadi; Sanjay Sarkar; Shohei Emura; Soumya Menon; Therson  Boadu

title: Earth Calling Aru
text: “Aaarrrrrrgh!” Earth is angry today. Really, really, angry. Aru is at it again. She is, for the twentieth time, preparing to fly like the superheroes in her comics. And for the twentieth time, she screams, “Aaarrrrrrgh! “ Gravity, I haaaate you!” “Pffff! That’s so unfair,” mutters Earth. “Gravity is an amazing force. Air, plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, houses, cars and schools, Aru and even me–none of us would be where we are if it weren’t for gravity! But how do I get Aru to see this?” Earth hatches a plan. “Hello, Aru. This is Earth. Since you hate gravity so much, I have decided to take it away. Please fly around as much as you want to. “Of course, you will have to catch your cape first!” “Wh a a a a... ” “ A aa a a aa aa a!” “Nooo oo oo!” “ Eee ee eee eee! ” “Whoaahhhhh!” “Please, please, stop! I called gravity silly because I want to fly. But now everything is flying,” says Aru. “ Hm mm pppph! You think all gravity does is stop you from flying?” “Huh? What else does it do apart from keeping me on the ground?” Aru asks. Earth sighs and explains, “Gravity is an invisible force that makes everything, and I mean EVERYTHING, around us pull or attract each other. It keeps all things in order. Without it, all things, even you and I, would just float away and disappear into space. Poof!” Aru is quick to ask, “But where is all this pulling? I don’t see it at all.” “Well observed, Aru! Everything is indeed pulling on each other all the time. You just don’t see or feel it because I am the heaviest object around you. And my pull is the strongest. So I pull everything to myself and keep us all grounded. “And my pull is the strongest around you because I have the most mass. Remember, greater the mass, stronger the pull,” says Earth. Mass is the amount of matter or stuff in an object. “Hmmm…and the moon? It’s pretty big too. And Jupiter?” Aru asks. “Ah, now you’re really beginning to catch on, Aru. The moon is much lighter than me, so it doesn’t pull you as hard as I do. But it is close enough to pull the water in our oceans and create tides. ” “You see, the farther the object, the lesser its pull. “ Now take the planet Jupiter–it’s the largest one we have in our solar system. It does have a much, much larger mass, but because it’s so far away, it makes the pull weaker than that of the moon.” The universe is full of things heavier than Earth. Like the sun. It pulls Earth and the other planets, and makes them move around it. This also creates days, months, years and seasons, summer holidays, and even special days like birthdays. There are many planets and stars that are heavier than Earth but they are so far away that their pull has little effect on our planet. Aru is quiet for a while. Suddenly, she flaps her arms, and says, “But I do want to fly! Fly, fly, fly away!” “And you will. You could learn to pilot a plane when you grow up, or take off to the moon in a rocket.” Aru is thrilled to hear this. “Yes, one day, I WILL fly! Now can you please turn gravity back on again?” “What did you break now, Aru?” “It wasn’t me, Ma. It was gravity!” “Aaaarrrrghhhh!” What do you think would change on Earth if the moon turned into Jupiter? Why does Earth not fall into the sun? What do you think would change on Earth if the moon moved 10 times farther away? Could a bird fly if there was no air?
author: Labanya Ghosh

title: Meng Was Thirsty
text: Meng swallowed in vain. Her paws scorched a gainst the surface of the road. Her fur trapped her like a furnace. Her eyes were too parched even for tears. But Meng wandered on. She was hunting for water. Meng tapped her foot on the hard, cement tunnel. It was once a thriving canal, streaming with birds and playful otters. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She brushed against the towering stone walls. It was once a reservoir, overgrown with lush greenery up till the eyes could see. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She sat on dry, broken land. It was once a lake, with beautiful fish and families of black swans and yellow ducks. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She walked along the never-ending bed of dust. It was once a river with clean, clear waters that glistened magically in the lights of the night. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She swung to the edge of the beach. The deep blue sea waters used to greet the soft, beige sand there. Not anymore. Where was all the water? Had the people used it all up? Had they let it go to waste without a care about the world? Had they let it go to waste without a care about the world? Meng collapsed. She closed her eyes and dreamt about the wonderful, water-filled world that once surrounded her. Pitter. Patter. Pitter. Tiny droplets trickled from the darkening sky. Meng cupped her hands. She watched with a sunken heart as rain and tears filled her palms ever so s lowly. Meng was thirsty. Don't let the tap run when washing the dishes. Fill a bucket with water and use it to rinse off dirty dishes before soaping. You can also use a bucket of clean water to rinse off soapy dishes instead of washing them directly under a running tap! Dishwashers can significantly reduce water usage. You can help conserve water! Use a bucket with a wring-top to fill water before mopping floors. These buckets prevent the need to open the tap every time you want to clean and wring the mop. Removing your shoes and washing your feet before entering the house can help trap less dirt and grime onto the floors! Wipe up spills immediately for an easy clean-up and to prevent stains from drying up. Opt to take a standing shower instead of drawing water into a bath tub. Or fill a bucket with the water you need before taking a bath. Limit your bathing time to under 5 minutes. Sing and dance to your heart's content with the water turned off! Reuse water from washing rice and vegetables to water plants in your garden. You can collect rain water in buckets to water the plants! Do you have more ideas on how you can help conserve and reuse water?
author: Abhi Krish

title: Henry goes to a Zoo
text: Henry is 13 years old. He goes to Gopi birla school. One day they go for a school trip to the Zoo. Henry is excited because,he likes going to a zoo. In the zoo he saw a lion, elephant, monkey, gorilla and snake. He got scared of the lion because he roared loudly. Henry took deep breathes and he felt better. they ate carrots and pumpkin. then they came back to school. The End
author: Risshan Patil
illustrator: Arun Ramkumar; Fahad Faizal; Jacob Kono; Renuka Rajiv; Ruchi Shah; Salim  Kasamba

title: Meng Was Thirsty
text: She tried to look for water. Meng tapped her foot on the hard floor. It was once a canal with playful otters. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She touched the tall, stone walls. It was once a reservoir with many green trees. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She sat on dry, broken land. It was once a lake with beautiful fishes. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. She walked across the dusty pathway. It was once a river with sparkling waters. Not anymore. Meng was thirsty. Meng swung to the beach. It was once clean with clear waters. Not anymore. Where was all the water? Had the people used it all up? Had they wasted it? Meng fell to the ground. She closed her eyes. Pitter. Patter. Pitter. Meng cupped her hands. Rain and tears filled her palms. Meng was thirsty. Don't let the tap run when washing the dishes. Fill a bucket with water and use it to rinse off dirty dishes before soaping. You can also use a bucket of clean water to rinse off soapy dishes instead of washing them directly under a running tap! Dishwashers can significantly reduce water usage. You can help conserve water! Use a bucket with a wring-top to fill water before mopping floors. These buckets prevent the need to open the tap every time you want to clean and wring the mop. Removing your shoes and washing your feet before entering the house can help trap less dirt and grime onto the floors! Wipe up spills immediately for an easy clean-up and to prevent stains from drying up. Opt to take a standing shower instead of drawing water into a bath tub. Or fill a bucket with the water you need before taking a bath. Limit your bathing time to under 5 minutes. Sing and dance to your heart's content with the water turned off! Do you have more ideas on how you can help conserve and reuse water? Reuse water from washing rice and vegetables to water plants in your garden. You can collect rain water in buckets to water the plants!
author: Abhi Krish

title: There's Amma!
text: “Please buy the nails, rope and flowers. I need them in a hurry,” says Amma. So Ashok, Baby and their Appa go shopping. “Amma!” Baby points. “No, Baby,” Appa says. “That’s not Amma. Amma has long, black hair.” “Amma!” Baby claps her hands. “No, Baby,” Appa says. “That’s not Amma. Amma has long, black hair.” “Amma!” Baby points. “No, Baby,” Appa laughs. “That’s not Amma. Amma doesn’t have a beard!” “Amma!” Baby claps. “No, Baby,” Appa says. “That’s not Amma. Amma is much younger.” “Amma!” Baby claps. “No, Baby,” Appa laughs again. “That’s not Amma. Amma is much younger.” Appa and Ashok get everything on the list. Amma takes the nails, rope and flowers. TAK TAK TAPAAK! Look what Amma has made. A cart for Baby! Off to the park they go. “Baby kept thinking she saw you at the market today,” Appa tells Amma. “I don’t know why.” “Because she is a clever baby,” says Ashok. This time, it is Baby’s turn to laugh.
author: Asha Nehemiah

title: Your own beautiful
text: Leela is one happy little girl, who loves to do all things that make her happy. They include going to school and learning new things every day listening to her favourite songs playing with all her toys, and most importantly the smell of food cooked by amma, especially JALEBIS! Leela loves Jalebis with all her heart! Leela is a cheerful girl. She laughs a lot even for the smallest joke But she can never take in bullying. People would always bully Leela for every thing. This made her angry, sometimes made her cry. Seeing her daughter cry, Leela's mom comes over. She tells her daughter to breathe in and breathe out deeply. Leela does the same. Next, her mom asks her to listen to the sound of her heartbeat. She tells her that it is the music that she loves to hear all the time and that she likes it. She tells her to keep smiling and be the lovely little girl she is. Leela does the same. Leela is happy once again, and she is back to being the same, cheerful girl that she once was. She learns an important lesson in loving herself. Leela's mom is happy and so is her pet spider!
author: Lakshmi Supriya

title: Freddy's Birthday
text: Freddy the lion was not happy. It was his birthday. No one had come to visit him. The jungle around him was quiet. " I am the king of the jungle. No Presents, No Chocolates, No People No Party for me", thought Freddy. Freddy went to meet his friend, Jammy. He wanted to be with Jammy that day. However, Jammy, the tiger was busy playing. He did not even look at Freddy jumping across the field. Tubby, the bear was sleeping. He did not wake up even when Freddy called out his name. I will definitely get a ride from Gajju today. Freddy went to find the elephant. Gajju was having a bath in the pond. He waved to Freddy. But, he did not come out of water. " Has everyone forgotten my birthday today? ", thought Freddy. Tacky, the jackal was running after a butterfly. He did not stop to talk to Freddy. None of my friends remember my birthday party", thought Freddy. He started walking back towards his cave. He was upset. His cave was dark. Power cut on my birthday. It is not a good day today. As he entered the cave, lights went on. Surprise!! Surprise!! came the voices. All his friends were there. His favorite chocolate cake with sprinkles and stars sat on the table with lots of presents. There was music and dance. Freddy danced with his friends. He had a lot of fun. He thanked his friends. His surprise birthday party was the best ever.
author: Ankita  Misra
illustrator: Arjun; Maya  Ramaswamy; Nicci  Nathanson; Ruchi Shah; Salim  Kasamba; Saurabh Sawant; Soumya Menon; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Girl in the Tree
text: Story Description Sunita is bored, so she comes up with a plan to get more attention. She finds her friend Denise and tells her she will climb a tall tree to be seen by everyone. But her plan goes wrong. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Popular ﻿pop-ew-lur ﻿She was a well-liked girl because she was ﻿ ﻿ ﻿popular ﻿. Attention ﻿a-ten-shu-n ﻿I want some ﻿ ﻿ ﻿attention ﻿ ﻿ ﻿because I feel ignored. Exhausted ﻿eg-z-or-st-id ﻿Pamela was ﻿ ﻿ ﻿exhausted ﻿ ﻿ ﻿after running for so long. Forgave ﻿for-gey-v ﻿The police officer ﻿forgave ﻿the boy and let him go. It was the village party and Sunita felt very bored. “Mama and Papa, will you play with me?” “Not now, Sunita,” they said. “We are tired from making the food and doing the preparations. Maybe later. Play with the boys.” “But I can’t play football,” said Sunita. “What about Grandma?” said Mama. “She ate some cake and fell asleep.” “Then you'll have to use your imagination,” said Papa. “There is plenty to do here.” As her Mama and Papa looked on, Sunita came up with a plan. “Nobody wants to play with me,” she said. “Perhaps Papa is right. If I use my imagination, then I can get everyone’s attention in a big way! I’ll be really popular!” Sunita found her friend Denise walking in the woods. “I’ll help you get noticed,” said Denise. “Good,” said Sunita. “Because I have a plan!” Sunita began climbing a tall tree. “When I reach the top, tell them to come and see what I’ve done!” said Sunita. “Don’t climb,” said Denise. “It’s too dangerous. You might fall.” “I can get back down,” said Sunita. “I’ll be ok.” Sunita climbed higher and higher. But the top of the tree seemed to get further and further away. When she reached the top, she was exhausted. “Come down now!” shouted Denise. “You are worrying me!” “I’m stuck!” Sunita called down. “If I move, I’m scared that I’ll fall! This was a bad idea.” “I’ll go and get your Papa,” said Denise. Sunita held on to the tree as her Papa, joined by the villagers, called up to her. “You’re going to be fine,” he said. “Don’t move. We will get a ladder and rescue you.” “I should not have done this,” said Sunita, beginning to cry. “I just wanted some attention.” Some boys who were throwing rocks heard Sunita’s crying. They saw her stuck in the tree as the villagers and her Papa went to find a big ladder. “Jump!” the boys said. “We will catch you!” “I’m too high up!” said Sunita. “It’s too dangerous!” “You have to help us, Sunita. Come down half way and we will meet you.” “I’ll try,” said Sunita. The boys discussed who amongst them was the best climber, then they sent the chosen boy up the tree to meet Sunita. Sunita climbed down and met the boy, who helped her the rest of the way to the ground. Sunita was relieved when she reached the bottom. The villagers returned and praised the boys. Sunita ran into her Mama and Papa’s arms. The boys looked on with shock from the event. “I’m sorry,” said Sunita. “I climbed the tree to get your attention. I felt ignored.” The boys offered to teach Sunita how to play football. Mama and Papa said they would spend more time playing with her. “I will never do that again,” said Sunita, and Mama and Papa forgave her. Sunita and Denise played games with the villagers, and they all celebrated into the evening, happy that Sunita was safe and sound and back at home. Sunita felt happy to be with her family and friends, enjoying the celebrations. She learned it was a bad idea to put herself in danger, and to do things that cause worry to others. Post-Reading Questions What motivated Sunita to get more attention? What things did Sunita learn by climbing the tree and getting stuck? Re-read. Ask: What did Sunita tell Denise to do once she had climbed the tree? Re-read. Ask: How did Papa and the villagers respond to Sunita being stuck? Re-read and 16. Ask: Describe the process by which the boys rescued Sunita, and describe what the boys offered to do for Sunita after rescuing her. Describe what you think is the lesson of the story.
author: Hello English

title: The Dancing Animals
text: Story Description As some jungle animals and a boy are relaxing, a girl arrives from the city, moving her body in a strange way to a musical rhythm. She tries to teach the animals how to dance, but they are too nervous to learn. Slowly over time, she encourages the boy and the animals to express themselves. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Rhythm rih-th-um The song had a catchy rhythm that was easy to remember. Occasionally uh-cay-zhun-al-lee I play music occasionally - two times per week. Craziest cr-ay-zee-ist She wasn't just a crazy dancer. Her extreme moves made her the craziest dancer. Enthusiasm en-thoo-zee-az-um The group enjoyed the music so much that they danced with enthusiasm. One day, Jungle Boy and the animal friends were resting on a hill. Suddenly there came the sound of instruments in the distance. They all woke up, except for Lion, to see a girl from the city moving around in a weird way. “What is she doing?” said Jungle Boy. “And what is that big sound?” “I don’t know,” said Rabbit. “But it sure is catchy. I like it.” “I’m dancing to music!” said the girl. “Why...why would anyone move that way?” said Lion, waking up frightened. “She’s clearly sick and crazy,” said Jungle Boy. “It’s magical,” said Tiger. “I can feel it too,” said Elephant. “There’s something about this noise that is making me sick!” “The sound is called music,” said the girl. “It is created with a mixture of instruments. We hear the sound waves. We feel the beat. It makes us want to move, to groove and flow.” “I am not moving,” said Gorilla. “I am moving but not grooving,” said Leopard. “I am flowing, but not moving or grooving,” said Jungle Boy. “Thith ith different,” said Snake. “Thwing me around by the head, pleathe!” “You can’t just come here and impose your groove on us!” said Lion with a growl. “We are smart animals. We do not partake in such insane body movement. We are decent.” “Chill,” said the girl. “I never said you had to dance!” “Don’t mind Lion,” said Bear. “He is very proud and protective of us. He does not like change.” “This is definitely changing me!” said Elephant. “Look at my legs go!” “You just have to relax,” said the girl. “Here, let me show you how it’s done. I’ll use your ears as drums!” “Don’t you dare use me to create sound!” Bear snapped. “Look, I can stick my back all the way out!” said Leopard, enjoying the music. “Run, before she notices,” said Lion. “Bear can handle himself well.” “I’m with you there,” said Jungle Boy. “Oh, calm down,” said the girl. “My people are having a festival. I want you to get involved. I’m just showing you how it’s done.” “Exactly how what is done?” said Lion. “What is she doing now, Elephant?” “Dont’t worry, Lion. She is behaving like a person now.” “How to dance,” said the girl. “Everyone, stand up and start moving on your own. It’s easy!” “Easy, huh?” said Jungle Boy. “Rabbit, if you start dancing, I’ll join in too.” The animals didn’t dance until the girl looked away. Then Jungle Boy climbed on Gorilla’s shoulders as Gorilla sidestepped. Then Elephant started moving his arms and slid his legs. Then Deer galloped on the spot. Then Bear and Rabbit started pulling poses and spinning around. The girl closed her eyes and listened to the festival. Then Jungle Boy and Bear pointed to where the music was coming from. Then Leopard copied and pointed at the music. Then Elephant pointed his toes and tusks with a sly head turn. Then Lion tried to catch on, but pointed at the ground by mistake. “Haha,” said the girl. “I caught you dancing when you thought I wasn’t watching!” “We did no such thing,” said Deer. “I was just stretching my legs,” said Rabbit, pretending to sleep. “We have to stretch out occasionally, you know,” said Jungle Boy. “Put your paw down,” said Bear to Lion, who had fallen asleep pulling his pose. The girl turned around once more and caught the animals dancing. “I knew it!” she said. “You’re embarrassed to dance in front of me!” “Not at all,” said Jungle Boy. “Don’t know what you’re talking about,” said Bear, doing the big fish, little fish move. “You’re imagining things,” said Elephant, caught in the ‘squat and blow the trunk’ move.” “You mean we can do this dancing thing anywhere at any time?” said Leopard. “And in front of people?” said Monkey? “In the craziest way possible?” said Jungle Boy. “And you’re allowed to copy what others are doing?” said Mouse. “And I won't look foolish?” said Lion, and the girl said, “Yes, yes, yes, yes.” “You can move this way, that way, jump, spin, move fast, move slow,” said the girl. “Go where the music goes and let go.” “Don’t let go,” said Leopard. “You will fall.” “She means relax and move,” said Monkey. “And let the music move your body,” said Mouse. The animals all got up and joined in together, dancing to the great music coming from the festival. This time they danced with enthusiasm and excitement, moving in any way they could and forming pairs. “It’s not so bad after all, is it?” said Lion. “I mean...” “Be quiet,” said Rabbit, dancing on Lion’s back. Gorilla, Bear, Deer and the others joined the gang, and they danced until the music stopped. Post-Reading Questions Why don't the animals want to dance? Describe the girl's personality. Re-read pages 4-6. Ask: What kind of emotions do the animals experience when introduced to the idea of dancing? Re-read. Ask: How did Lion give away that he had been secretly dancing? Re-read pages 14-16. Ask: According to the girl, how can you dance? Dancing and singing is a form of expression. How do you express yourself?
author: Hello English

title: Fred my friend
text: I was playing in the garden when I saw something behind a bush. It was a brown pup. The little brown pup wagged his tail. He looked sad. Even his WOOF was sad. I was not sure about what to do. I called my mother. She patted the dog. I gave him water and food. "Let's take him home", I said. My mother said someone might look for it. But he came after me. We go to the park everyday. No one has come to take him. We play. We walk. We run. We stay together. He has become my friend. I take care of him with love. I call him Fred. My friends also like playing with Fred. Fred and I have a wonderful time together.
author: Ankita  Misra
illustrator: Karen  Vermeulen; Natasha  Mehra; Ntembiso  Velemane; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Rishi Anu; Seat Sopheap; Soumya Menon; Suvidha Mistry

title: We Love Our Home
text: Who loves splashing? The Irrawaddy Dolphin loves splashing in Chilika Lake. Who loves dust baths? The Malabar Pied Hornbill loves a dust bath in the forest in Dandeli. Who loves sitting in wet mud? The Indian Rhinoceros loves sitting in wet mud on the river banks of Kaziranga. Who loves making wide dung piles? The Nilgai loves making wide dung piles at the foothills of the Himalayas. Who loves resting in burrows? Who loves resting in burrows? The Thick-tailed Pangolin loves resting in burrows in the dry lands of Gir Forest. Who loves jumping across treetops? The Yellow-throated Marten loves jumping across treetops in Namdapha. Who loves playing hide-and-seek in short grasslands? The Bengal Fox loves playing hide-and-seek in the short grasslands at Jaisalmer. Who loves building nests with their partners? The Spot-billed Pelican loves building nests with their partners at Atapaka. Who loves staying comfortable and snug at home? We all do! 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 1. Nilgais: Himachal Pradesh, near the Himalayan mountains 2. Bengal Fox: Jaisalmer, Rajasthan 3. Indian Rhinoceros: Kaziranga National Park, Assam 4. Yellow-Throated Marten: Namdapha National Park, Arunachal Pradesh 5. Irrawady Dolphin: Chilika Lake, Orissa 6. Spot-Billed Pelican: Atapaka, Andhra Pradesh 7. Malabar Pied Hornbill: Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka 8. Pangolin: Gir Forest, Gujarat Where can we find these animals and birds in India?
author: Karthika G

title: Shunti the Sunshine Cat
text: Shunti loves to sit in sunny patches. Her favourite spot is on the wall by the gate. From here, she can see... Shunti loves to sit in sunny patches. Her favourite spot is on the wall by the gate. From here, she can see... Tapan’s mother drying wool Arka washing her sports shoes Tapan drying his hair Vijay selling fish Today, Shunti can see Arka, Tapan and his grandfather pulling out weeds. “Can you wheel me to that sunny patch, please?” asks Dadaji. “Sunlight is good for my bones. And yours!” Arka and Tapan wheel Dadaji to the warm and bright garden. “Wheeee!” they squeal. “Faster, faster!” says Dadaji. “Careful, careful!” shouts Tapan’s mother. Shunti’s gaze is on Vijay. “Quicker, quicker,” purrs Shunti. She is so hungry! Today, it is raining. “Oh no, my rangoli!” wails Arka. “Yuck, my shirt,” says Tapan. “Oh ho, my pickle!” cries Tapan’s mother. Shunti is also upset. Now how will Vijay bring fish? Hungry Shunti perches near the stove. Papadams, vegetables and spices. Yuck! Murabba, jams and pickles. Tcha! That’s when she sniffs, looks up and sees... Aha! A jar of sun-dried fish! Today, the sun is out! Yoohoo! “Do you want to make some sun art?” asks Dadaji. Arka and Tapan run to get all the things he asks for: a sheet of black chart paper, f lat and heavy things like stones and coins. They arrange some leaves, twigs, stones and coins on the chart paper, making a pattern. “Leav e it in the sun for four hours,” says Dadaji. Shunti wonders what will happen in four hours. “My busy little workers! Like you, the sun has done a lot of work today," says Dadaji. The sun has made Dadaji’s lap warm. Mmmmmm... Shunti loves the sun! Shall we make some hibiscus tea? Here’s what you’ll need: - A glass jar with a lid - Petals from four red hibiscus flowers - One litre of drinking water - Four spoons of sugar Here's what you should do: Fill the jar with clean water. Wash the petals of the flowers and drop them into the water. Close the lid and shake the bottle. Leave it in the sun for three hours. Add sugar and stir. Your hibiscus tea is ready! Drink up! Sunny days are happy days - The sun is a star. It gives us light and heat. - It’s the sun’s light and heat that makes plants grow. - A bit of morning sun on our skin every day is good for our health. - The sun is VERY, VERY far away from the earth, but it still gives us the energy we need! - Scientists ‘catch’ the sun’s energy and use it in many ways. But you and I can use it by just playing in the sun.
author: Mala Kumar

title: Today I Will
text: Today I will... light candles for the festival. Story Description Let's explore all of the things that you can do today. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Chasing ﻿ch-ey-s-ing ﻿Today I will be chasing birds. Freezing ﻿fr-ee-z-ing ﻿Today it is freezing cold outside. Eagle ﻿ee-gu-l ﻿I saw an eagle today. Guava ﻿g-wah-v-a ﻿ ﻿I will eat a guava today. Today I will... read my favourite book. Today I will... chase a cat chasing a squirrel. Today I will... help my sister pick vegetables. Today I will... keep warm because it’s freezing cold. Today I will... eat lunch under the big tree. Today I will... ride a camel in the hot desert. Today I will... buy guavas from the market. Today I will... wear the same colour as my friends. Today I will... watch the eagle fly. Today I will... just look out of the window. Today I will... do a small favour. Today I will... do anything I want. Yay! Post-Reading Questions Explain the difference between today, yesterday and tomorrow. Match the words to the present, past and future tenses. Re-read. Ask: What fruit will you buy from the market? Re-read. Ask: What kind of bird will you see today? Re-read. Ask: How many birds can you find in the tree? Describe three things that you are doing today.
author: Hello English

title: There Is A Goat on the Roof
text: Story Description Maria’s pet goat climbs on to a church roof and gets stuck, and the villagers try various ways of rescuing him. Pre-reading Vocabulary and Phonics Tinkling ﻿t-ing-cl-ing ﻿The goat's bell made a ﻿ ﻿ ﻿tinkling ﻿sound. Steady ﻿st-e-d-ee ﻿They made sure the bridge was ﻿steady ﻿ before they crossed the river. Dangerous ﻿day-n-jur-u-ss ﻿ ﻿It was too ﻿dangerous ﻿to climb on to the roof. Wander ﻿one-d-er ﻿The goat often wander ed away and got lost. Maria has a pet goat. His name is George. George wears a bell that makes a tinkling sound. Maria and George create a lot of fun and mischief together. They enjoy collecting chopped vegetables, plants and fruit skins, and dropping them around the house. Maria likes to dig and George likes to watch. “What are you doing, Maria?” says Mama. “Digging the deepest hole in the world,” says Maria. One day, George wanders away on his own. He finds some tasty rubbish and leaves, eating away until he is full up. Suddenly George sees something more interesting, and he wanders away again. “Papa, have you seen George?” says Maria. “Oh no,” says Papa. “The goat has wandered away again. Let’s go and find him.” Mama, Papa and Maria search for George when they hear a bell tinkling. They see something that shocks them. They pass the neighbours who see it too. “George?” says Maria. “What have you done?” “There is a goat on the roof,” say the neighbours. “On the church roof,” say Mama and Papa. “Waaaa!” cries Maria. “George is stuck on the roof forever. We will never get him back! Waaaa!” “Don’t worry,” says Papa. “We can rescue that goat. I have an idea.” Mama and Maria look on scared as Papa and the neighbours try to climb the church. But it is too high and dangerous for them to reach George, who waits on the roof. “Ikikikik!” says George. “You silly goat!” says Papa. Desperate to help George, Maria digs a deep hole and fills it with water. “What are you doing?” says Mama. “I am digging a deep hole for George to jump into.” “What have you done?” says Mama. “I have made a pile of boxes,” says Papa. “How will that work?” says Maria. “The goat will jump into the top box,” says Papa. “Then we remove the boxes on the ground, one by one, until George reaches the bottom.” After some thought, both the neighbours and Papa agree that the plan is too dangerous, because the boxes will fall. Papa suggests trying a tall tree for George to climb down. So they cut a tree and lean it towards George, but it is too dangerous and unsteady, and George refuses to get on. “Perhaps we need a bigger tree,” says Papa. “I have a better idea,” says a man who is watching. “Let’s build a slide and attach it to my car!” says the man. “Great idea!” says Papa, and they build a strong and steady slide from the car to the roof. George slides all the way down the ramp to safety, and straight into Maria’s arms. “You silly goat,” says Papa. “You are lucky you are not hurt.” “Ikikikik!” says George as a thank you. All the neighbours and onlookers go home. “George!” says Maria. “I am so happy that you are ok. Don’t wander off again. Do you understand?” “Ikikikik!” says George. Post-Reading Questions What did Maria and George enjoy doing together? What would George often do that got him into trouble? Re-read. Ask: What did everyone see? Re-read. Ask: Why was Papa's plan too dangerous? Re-read pages 15 and 16. Ask: How did they get George down from the roof? What is your favourite pet? If you could have any animal, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: Lenin's Guests
text: “POOOOOOOST!” Who could that be from, wonders Lenin. “Ah, from Rajan Maama!” Two of my friends will be passing through Madurai on the 12th of April. They need a place to rest for a while. They should reach your house by 3 o'clock in the afternoon. I know you will look after them well. Love, Maama Dear Lenin, Today is the 12th of April, a hot and muggy day. "Pchaa! Needs more sugar.” Krinnnggg! The doorbell rings loudly. Slurrrp! “ Oh, hello! Hello! Please come inside,” says Lenin. “Please have some lime juice.” “Oh no! I’m so sorry. I’ll be right back,” says Lenin. Clang! Dhadam! Toing! “Oh, what shall I serve the juic e in? Ah, this and this!” “Try this! You must be so thirsty.” “OH NO!” “I’m so sorry. I’ll be right back.” “Please have your juice now!” “Oh no! I’m so sorry. I’ll be right back.” GLUG! GLUG! GLUG! GLUG! If these animals joined Lenin's juice party, what would he serve them juice in? Turn the page for answers. Giraffe Sunbird Cat Toucan 1. 2. 3. 4.
author: Menaka Raman

title: Lacey Looks For Her Cat
text: Story Description Lacey searches around her house and her village for her pet cat, Tabatha, who has gone missing. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Striped s-try-p-d The striped cat was black and white. Grooming gr-ew-ming A boy was grooming his cat with a comb. Lacey had a cat called Tabatha. Every morning, Tabatha would jump into Lacey's arms to say goodbye before she went to school. But this morning, Tabatha did not come. "Tabatha, where are you?" said Lacey, looking in the hallway. But Tabatha was not there. "Perhaps she is under the wardrobe," said Lacey. But Tabatha was not there. "Perhaps she is under the desk," said Lacey. But Tabatha was not there. "I know," said Lacey. "She's out in the back yard." But Tabatha was not there. Lacey walked down some steps. A striped ginger cat met her. "You're not Tabatha," said Lacey. Lacey walked along a street, looking for Tabatha. But Tabatha was not there. Lacey found a cat sitting in some trash. But it wasn't Tabatha. Lacey saw a boy grooming a cat. But it wasn't Tabatha. Lacey saw a cat standing on a wall. But it wasn't Tabatha. Suddenly a cat started following Lacey. "Perhaps you've seen Tabatha?" said Lacey. The cat looked back at Lacey and then ran up some steps. "Perhaps it wants me to follow?" said Lacey. Lacey followed the cat. It led her to a tree. "Tabatha isn't here," she said. Lacey walked and found a smaller cat. "You're about the same size as Tabatha," she said. Lacey saw a cat sitting on a garden wall. "You're the same colour as Tabatha," she said. Lacey found a kitten walking along her path. "You remind me so much of Tabatha," she said. Lacey saw the striped cat again. "I've walked in a circle," she said. "There is nowhere else to look." "I should check the house again," said Lacey. She looked in the study......and then, once again, she looked in her room. "It's no use," said Lacey. "Tabatha has run away! I'll never find her!" She cried into her pillow. But then, hearing Lacey crying, Tabatha came out from under the bed. "There you are!" said Lacey. "I looked all over for you!" After school, Lacey played with Tabatha and gave her a bowl of milk. Lacey learned that cats like to hide in quiet, dark and warm spaces. Post-Reading Questions Which cats reminded Lacey of Tabatha? Lacey followed a striped cat. Where did it take her to? Re-read pages 17-20. Ask: Which cats reminded Lacey of Tabitha's appearance? Re-read. Ask: What kind of places do cats enjoy? If Lacey had checked properly under her bed, do you think she would have found Tabitha? Was Tabitha somewhere else all along?
author: Hello English

title: The Silent Antics of Sammie and Chintu
text: Bal Vihar School is holding a drama competition. Classes 1 to 7 will be putting up plays. Std. 3 is doing a play called, "Homework Hassles." Miss Lily is their class teacher. "Our play is about two students," she tells the class. "One of them always does their homework, and the other one never does." "I'm going to pick two children to act in the play," says Miss Lily. Chintu and Sammie put up their hands right away. "Pick me, pick me," they both say. But Miss Lily chooses Rohit and Faiza to act in the play. Chintu and Sammie are not ready to give up. When class ends, they run after Miss Lily. "Miss, Miss... we want to be in the play too. Please, please..." "Okay," says Miss Lily. "You can be two of the other students in the play." "Yay!" Chintu and Sammie shout as they high-five each other. "Miss Lily, what do Sammie and I have to say on stage?" Chintu asks. "You don't have to say anything," says Miss Lily. "You have to sit on a bench on the stage with your schoolbags. And you have to be very, very quiet." "But why do we have to be very, very quiet?" asks Chatterbox Chintu. "Because if you keep talking, then Rohit and Faiza will forget their lines," says Miss Lily. "I'm going to be on stage for the first time ever," Sammie says to Chintu during recess. He turns a cartwheel. "I'm so excited!" Chintu frowns. "But Miss Lily said we have to be very, very quiet during the play," he says. "That sounds boring." "Maybe being very quiet on stage will be exciting," Sammie tells him. It's the day of the play. It's time for Chintu and Sammie to go on stage. Chintu and Sammie take their schoolbags and sit down on the bench. "Remember, no talking," Miss Lily tells them. The curtain opens. The play begins. "Did you do your homework?" asks Faiza. "No, I did not," says Rohit. Rohit and Faiza talk and talk and talk about homework. The audience yawns. Chintu looks for his parents in the audience. He sees them sitting with Sammie's parents. He raises his hand to wave to them. Suddenly, he feels himself being pushed off the bench. He falls onto the stage with a whump. The audience laughs. " Are they laughing at me?" Chintu wonders. His face grows warm. He stands up quickly. He wants to know how he got pushed off the bench. And then he sees the reason why. Sammie has put his big, overstuffed schoolbag on the bench. There is no space left on the bench for Chintu to sit. Chintu pushes the bag towards Sammie. But there still isn't enough space. "Put your silly bag down..." Chintu is about to tell Sammie. Then he remembers Miss Lily telling them that they cannot speak. But words are not the only way in which Chintu can tell Sammie what he wants him to do. So, Chintu nudges Sammie's arm. Then he points to the bag, and then to the floor. 'Put your bag down on the floor.' Sammie points to the dusty floor of the stage. He makes a face. ' The floor is dirty.' Chintu frowns, then signs: ' Put your bag on your lap.' Sammie crosses his arms and shakes his head. ' I'm not putting my bag on my lap.' Chintu glares at Sammie and pushes his hands forward. ' I'm going to push your bag off the bench.' Sammie stands up. He plants his hands on his hips and glares at Chintu. ' Just try it -' Chintu and Sammie have forgotten about the play and the audience. They are scowling at each other now. Their hands are bunched into fists. Their faces are the color of beetroots. Luckily, just before they can get into a wrestling match, the play ends. The curtain comes down. The audience claps loudly and for a long time. Chintu is surprised. "They liked our boring play!" Chintu and Sammie come off the stage. They are best friends once more. They have already forgotten their quarrel. Miss Lily is waiting in the wings. She does not look happy. "I told you two to be quiet," she says. "I don't know why Miss Lily scolded us," Chintu says to Sammie. "We were very, very quiet," Sammie agrees. "We didn't say a single word. We didn't even whisper." Finally, it's time for the judge to announce the prizes. "The prize for the best play," says the judge, "goes to to Std. 3 for their play: 'Homework Hassles.'" The judge presents Miss Lily with the trophy. "What a terribly clever idea, Miss Lily" he says. "You had your actors acting without actually speaking. Very original." Miss Lily thanks the judge, but she looks confused. "And a special prize," the judge adds, "to our two outstanding young actors: Chintu Ghosh and Sammie Varghese. They got up to the funniest antics without saying a single word." Chintu can't believe his ears. "Am I dreaming?" he asks. "Maybe we're dreaming this together," Sammie replies. Chintu and Sammie go onto the stage. They shake hands with the chief guest. He smiles and says, "Congratulations!" He gives each of them a gold-colored trophy, which has these words inscribed on it: "Best Actor in the Bal Vihar Drama Competition." Chintu and Sammie give the cheering audience their biggest, brightest smile. They see their parents standing and clapping for them. And they raise their trophy cups high, high, high.
author: Gauri  Sirur

title: Mouli's Mango Dreams
text: One day, I asked Thamma if I may please, Go lie down under the thick mango trees. (* Thamma means grandmother in Bengali) She said, “Mouli, you may lie down under the huge mango tree, where all the squirrels run wild and free. The ladies sit with their combs, and untangle their knotty branches around our homes.” I run to lie down thinking about a beautiful world, Drowned in delicious mango curd. Where the fishes and frogs come swim with me, Under the thick giant mango tree. I have Thamma’s packed rice and parathas Soaked in fresh homemade ghee. The yellow sun gleaming above The thick flowing mango sea. “Mouli!!! Come inside it is getting dark. Run before the shadows become long and stark.” I think about the shining moon and stars, How beautiful they’d look on my ice cream bars. Of colours orange, yellow, red and green A world so mellow no one ever has seen. I run to the house with the huge tree lurking over my head. Counting yummy mangoes as I lie in bed. Mangoes come in various shapes, sizes and colours including yellow, orange, red and green. It is a very popular fruit in India, and that is why it is also known as ‘the king of fruits’. Sour, unripe mangoes are used to make chutneys and pickles as side dishes or eaten raw, dipped in salt, black pepper, red chilli, lime, or sugar. A popular thick juice, called ‘Aamras’ is made of mangoes with sugar and milk, and is often consumed with roti or rice. The mango fruit and leaves are ritually used as floral decorations at weddings, public celebrations and religious ceremonies in India.

title: Harshita's Family
text: Harshita lives in Singapore, with her parents and a younger brother, Aryan. She loves her family, but she misses her grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins in India. She is going to India during her school vacations. She is excited because its her brother's first trip to India. Her mother, Nikita has two siblings, elder sister named Namita and younger sister named Nisha. Namita aunty lives in Pune with Rahul uncle and Harshita's eldest cousin, Yoshi. In the same city, Nisha aunty lives with Gaurav uncle and Harshita's youngest cousin, Suhani. Harshita is looking forward to have fun time with her cousins. She will eat lovely food with her family after play time. She loves her family and her family loves her back and takes care of her. Family Harshita feels happy to have so many people in her family to care and to share.

title: The Cheeky Lucky Monkey
text: Story Description A monkey teases a fish and gets into trouble when the fish wants to eat him. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Reflection ﻿re-fle-k-sh-un ﻿ ﻿The monkey saw his reflection on the river's surface. Swam ﻿s-wam ﻿I swam yesterday. Today I will swim again. Devour ﻿de-vow-er ﻿The fish wanted to devour the monkey in one bite. Tease ﻿tee-z-e ﻿The monkey teased the fish by throwing leaves into the river. The cheeky lucky monkey looked down into the roaring, coursing river. Safely perched on a high branch, he watched the fish swimming by in the current. Looking at his reflection, he laughed. As he started reaching down, a great, gigantic fish stuck its horrid head out of the water. It had sharp teeth like giant fangs or a bear trap. It leaped up from the surface and gnashed its terrifying jaw. The monkey looked at the fish and laughed. "Was that supposed to be scary?" said the monkey. "Here, fishy," said the monkey, picking leaves from the tree. "Come and eat these because you'll never eat me!" The fish clenched its jaw and stared at the monkey, waiting for it to move while planning how to attack. "Don't do that," said the sensible purple monkey, the cheeky lucky monkey's best friend. "You're teasing it and now it is getting angry. It will eat you." "Ha," said the cheeky lucky monkey. "That silly fish can eat leaves. It'll never catch me!" The cheeky lucky monkey collected oranges and threw them at the fish. "If you throw oranges at the fish, it will get angrier," said the sensible purple monkey. "I'm too big for the fish," said the cheeky lucky monkey. Then the monkey jumped on the branches and shook more leaves into the river. The fish swam in circles, waiting for the monkey to get lower. "I'm coming for you now," thought the fish. "You don't know what I'm about to do! I see you getting lower and I'm going to grab you in one huge bite! Dinner is served!" "Aah!" squealed the monkey. "What is it doing? How can it jump so high? It's massive!" "You're going to be devoured by my huge teeth!" thought the fish. "Come here!" The monkey gripped the vine and climbed up, spinning himself away from the fish, gathering height and speed. But he kept swinging back to the fish. "You can't get me!" said the monkey, rolling his eyes, teasing the fish and climbing up the vine. "We'll see about that," thought the fish. "You're mine!" The monkey moved the vine and started swinging to and fro, taunting the fish. "Grrr!" thought the fish. "Wait until you slip off that vine. Then you're finished!" "I can even dance!" said the monkey. "Watch me move! Da daa da da! Da daa da da!" Unexpectedly, the monkey slipped and let go of the vine. He tumbled towards the water. "Dinner at last!" thought the fish. "I knew you would make a mistake!" The fish waited with its mouth open to devour the monkey. But then, the sensible purple monkey caught his friend by the tail and pulled him up to safety. The fish gave up, went underwater and chased after food that was easier to catch. "This one won't last very long!" the fish thought while chasing a much smaller fish. The cheeky lucky monkey escaped from the fish and teased the birds by the river shore. "You're lucky I was there to save you!" said the sensible purple monkey. "Next time you might be alone!" Post-Reading Questions Why was the character called the 'cheeky, lucky monkey'? Why was the fish so determined to eat the monkey? Re-read pages 7-8. Ask: What does the purple monkey advise? Re-read. Ask: How did the monkey escape from the fish's jaw? Why was the monkey lucky to have his friend around?
author: Hello English

title: Razia Learns to Swim
text: Razia and her Ummachi live on an island far out in the ocean. Ummachi wants Razia to learn how to swim. But Razia is scared of being in water. The ocean is sooooo large and deep! Today, the waves are small. So Ummachi takes Razia to the lagoon. “Razia, please get in! The lagoon is shallow,” says Ummachi. “Can I learn to swim next time, Ummachi? Pleeeeeease!” “Don’t be scared, mole. See how all the animals swim. Try moving your legs and arms just like them.” Today, the waves are small. So Ummachi takes Razia to the lagoon. “Razia, please get in! The lagoon is shallow,” says Ummachi. “Can I learn to swim next time, Ummachi? Pleeeeeease!” “Don’t be scared, Razia. See how all the animals swim. Try moving your legs and arms just like them.” Razia peers into the water. So many colourful animals are all around her! Thooooo! The water is very salty. Razia takes a deep breath and dips her head in the water. She watches the animals swim. Just as Ummachi had told her to. A baby turtle swims by, kicking her legs and pushing the water aside with her flippers. Razia tries to swim like the turtle. She accidentally gulps some water. “Ummachi, the water stings!” cries Razia. “It will get easier,” says Ummachi. The next day, a baby octopus jets by. He draws water in and pushes his eight arms forward. Razia tries to swim just like the octopus. “Watch me kick my legs, Ummachi!” yells Razia. “Good! Keep trying.” She swallows some water. Ugghh! But she tries again. The next day an eagle ray soars by, flapping her triangular wings. Razia tries to swim like the ray. She swallows some water, and sinks a little — blub-blub-blub. “This is so difficult, Ummachi!” says Razia. “Keep trying, Razia!” Razia tries again. And again. The next day, some plankton float by. They have no flippers or wings. They move with the waves. Razia stretches her arms and legs. She floats like the plankton. “Ummachi, watch me float!” shouts Razia. “That’s great, Razia! The next day, an eel wiggles by. He swings from side to side, like a snake. Razia tries to swim like the eel. “Razia, you are swimming!” says Ummachi. The next day, a flying fish leaps by. She glides through the air. Razia tries to swim like the flying fish. She flails and crashes into the water. “My arms and legs hurt, Ummachi!” says Razia. “Once you remember to breathe while swimming, your arms and legs will move slower. Then it will hurt less.” The next day, a dolphin zips by. He comes to the surface of the water, breathes deeply and then dives. Razia tries to swim like the dolphin. She lifts her head out of water, gulps some air and dives back in. As the days go by, Razia watches more and more animals swim. She learns many new moves. Razia kicks. She floats. She wiggles. She dives. She holds her breath for longer and longer. She swims faster and faster. “ Razia, it's time to go! ” yells Ummachi. “Can I swim just a little bit longer? Pleeease, Ummachi?” Have You Tried Swimming? Different animals have different ways of moving through water. Tuna and dolphins are shaped to shoot through the water with great speed. Tiny plankton drift wherever the water takes them. Squid and octopuses draw water in and expel it very fast. Try some of these moves the next time you step into the water! Eagle rays flap their wings. Crabs and lobsters walk on the seafloor. Flying fish leap out of water to escape predators.
author: Divya Panicker

title: Mangosaurus Rex
text: Story Description T he Bhamra family is on a train travelling to Lahore by the Himalayas. The father tells a story to his wife and daughter about a mysterious forest, wherein lies a fearsome mystical giant called the Mangosaurus Rex. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Fearsome fee-ur-sum The Mangosaurus Rex was a huge fearsome creature who scared the villagers. Trespassing tre-ss-pass-ing The children were trespassing on someone else's land. Celebrations sel-e-b-ray-shun-s The wild and fun celebrations continued into the night. Ancient ey-n-sh-un-t The tradition was so old that it was ancient. The train travelled by the Himalayan mountains on its way to Lahore. It was a long journey for the Bhamra family. They would not arrive at their destination until midnight. While her mother and father chatted, Aadhya read her book over and over again. Aadhya looked out of the window for a long time, seeing the mountains, fields and rivers stretched out across the landscape. After a while, the scenery changed. Aadhya noticed a big cluster of trees getting closer, as the afternoon turned into the evening. "What is that place?" said Aadhya. "That is the mysterious forest," said father, as mother listened in closely. "Why is it mysterious?" said Aadhya. "Because there is an enchanting story about the place," said father. "Many secretive things happen there. Perhaps I can tell you this story." "Let's hear it," said mother. The train passed through the mystical forest. Aadhya saw many different animals and birds. There were luscious, colourful flowers. "Right here is where our story takes place," said father. "It is the story of the mango king." "The what?" said Aadhya, laughing. "The mango king," said father. "The most fearsome creature of the forest." Once upon a time, there was a forest village that sold mangoes as its business. There were two children, Tim and Kate, who worked collecting mangoes. There was a mango festival every year, and the children had to collect as many as they could find. "I don't think we'll make much money this year," said Tim's mother. "We are running out of mangoes. Less of them grow every year. Very soon we will be poor." Tim and Kate went to sit by a flowery pool, thinking about what the villagers were saying. "I'm sure we will find more mangoes next year," said Kate. "We'll be fine." "I'm not sure," said Tim. "I think my mother is right." As the villagers prepared for the festival, Tim and Kate sneaked away from the village, in search of more mangoes, and carrying a picnic with them. "Everyone is too busy," said Tim. "They won't notice that we've gone." After several hours of playing games, Tim and Kate ate their picnic and rested against a fallen tree. A little cat visited Kate and slept on her leg. "Looks like we won't find any mangoes around here," said Kate. "I feel very bored," said Tim. "Let's do something." Tim and Kate walked further and found a cluster of mango trees. The mangoes were too high to take, so they started throwing stones at the branches to knock them down. "Look at all of these!" said Kate, after they had collected several mangoes. "I wouldn't do that," said Kate, when Tim started eating one. "I'm so hungry!" he said. "But you ate all of your picnic. How can you still be hungry?" Just then, Tim felt sick, and he started coughing out mangoes and spitting them on the ground. "Agh!" said Tim after he stopped coughing out mangoes. "How is that even possible?" "What is this weird place?" said Kate. They walked further and encountered a dense forest blocking out the sunlight. They kept walking when they saw something gigantic in the background, and they froze in fear. "What was it?" said Aadhya. "It was a creature with big eyes, a big belly, and big legs and a big stomach..." said father. "Tell us already," said mother. "All right," said father. "But prepare yourselves. It is scary." "Ahar!" came a figure blasting through the forest. "Who are you two little runts who are stealing my mangoes?" "B-b-b-b...." said Tim. "Wh...how..." said Kate. "Well?" said the impatient giant. "Who are you and what are you doing here?" "I'm sorry," said Tim. "I didn't mean to eat that mango. It made me cough up a load more." "That's your punishment for theft!" said the giant. "What are you?" said Kate. "You don't know who I am?" said the giant. "Ahahahahaha! Oh. You really don't know who I am." "I am the dreaded, the feared, the humble, the admired...wait for it...mango king! But I prefer to call myself the Mangosaurus Rex. The wildest, most dreaded beast and the king of the forest! And you are both trespassing on my property! Now you shall get out, before I either eat you both and turn you into giant mangoes, or I simply throw you out." "We're sorry," said Tim. "We were looking for mangoes for our village festival." "Wait," said the Mangosaurus Rex. "You are children from the nearby village?" "Yes," said Kate. "We are running out of mangoes. We need more for our celebrations. We get lots of guests who pay for our fruits and cakes and..." "Yes, yes," said the Mangosaurus Rex. "I know all about your festival." "We're very sorry for trespassing," said Tim. "We should leave now." "Stop," said the Mangosaurus Rex. "I'm not a threat, really. I won't eat you. Unless..." "Unless what?" said Kate. "I am invited to your festival." "Well, all right," said Tim. "But I don't think many people would like you because..." "Because they've never seen a giant ogre, I mean, the mango king, before," said Kate. "They would be scared." "I understand," said the Mangosaurus Rex. "Why don't you two come with me? I have something to show you. If you let me come to the festival, I'll let you both in on a secret." So the children went with him. The Mangosaurus Rex had a gigantic tree house, inside which were carpets, statues, mango trees, food, artwork, and all the foods that anyone could eat. "This is great!" said Tim. "So much fun!" said Kate. "This is wonderful," said the Mangosaurus Rex. "My two new friends. Now, listen. There's an important thing I must tell you. You see all the mangoes and the trees out there? Well, that is all my property. And you have been stealing my mangoes. I saw what your festival was doing. I felt excluded, because your people fell out with me and never invited me again. So I stopped your mangoes from growing. I've been making your village poor. Well, with my magical power, I can make even more mangoes grow than before, and you can all be rich. So, all you have to do is give me an invitation, get your villagers to apologise to me, and you are all forgiven. Do you understand?" "Yes, Mangosaurus," said Tim. "Ok, Mangosaurus," said Kate. "Mangosaurus Rex," he replied. "The strongest, most admired creature in the forest." The Mangosaurus Rex, Tim and Kate partied into the evening, eating all kinds of fruits and foods they had never encountered before. The Mangosaurus Rex sang with his booming voice and played instruments far into the night. He told the children tales of the forest, of how he had defeated wild beasts bigger than himself, of the ancient elders who once owned the forest, and of the history of their own village. They discovered the Mangosaurus Rex was grumpy but very old. "I'm not upset with them anymore," said the Mangosaurus. "Please tell your villagers this." Tim and Kate returned to the village and told their story. The village elders apologised to the Mangosaurus Rex, and gave him an invitation. He joined the party, and provided the village with more mangoes than they'd ever had. There was peace, and Tim and Kate visited him regularly. "Wow, that was great," said Aadhya as the sun sank below the horizon. "So everyone became friends again, and nobody was poor because they had all the mangoes they wanted." "That's right," said father. "Always build bridges, forgive and offer friendship." "Very good story," said mother. "Did you make it up?" "Yes," said father. "But the part about the Mangosaurus Rex, that was real!" They laughed. Post-Reading Questions What caused the father to tell the story? What festival happened every year in the forest village? Re-read. Ask: What did Tim and Kate take with them to the forest? Re-read. Ask: Who was really responsible for the lack of mangoes? Re-read. Ask: What does the Mangosaurus Rex ask for? What festivals or celebrations do you know about?
author: Hello English

title: Puppies Are Smart, too
text: "He is so cute!" Looking at the puppy Nyla said. "A special gift on your birthday." Said, Papa and Mom. Papa hugged Nyla and said. "Your puppy is your responsibility." Then Mom explained. "It's your responsibility to feed, bathe, walk, and teach him." Nyla now knows that the puppy is her responsibility. "Let his name be Monty", said Nyla. It's how the puppy got his name, Monty. Monty goes with Nyla everywhere. But not to her school. "May I take Monty to my school?" She asked. "Honey, pets do not go to the school." Said, Mom. Monty now shares when Nyla eats, play, and sleeps. They are best friends. But Nyla doesn't share her chocolates. She eats her chocolate hiding from Monty. Sometimes behind the door. So Monty wouldn't see her eating chocolate. But a dog sniff smells. Monty could sniff the smell of Nyla's chocolate. Every time Nyla ate chocolate, Monty could sniff the smell. One day Monty was hiding under the bed. Nyla and her parents were surprised. "Monty is eating chocolate there!" Nyla said. "How could you, Monty?" Nyla gets angry. Monty feels ashamed. He covered face with his paw. Mom said. "Puppy learn fast. Monty learned eating chocolate hiding from others." "As you eat chocolate hiding from Monty!" Papa told her. They all laughed. Monty is also laughing.

title: The bee
text: Once there was a bee who fell sick upon a time The mountain monsters growled and the snow crystals tumbled then the wind blew, far the bee flew he found a barn to keep him warm and made some fire of desire then came a giant spider his name is anger he said oh dear! you can't stay here.... without any delay the bee flew away then he heard a sigh, far from the high he looked around and landed on the ground, found a tree of dragon berry then he blushed, to the berries, he rushed he built a hive where he can hide the bee survives and the story ends RHYMING WORDS blew - flew sigh - high fire - desire around - ground spider - anger tree - berry dear - here blushed - rushed delay - away hive - hide
