title: Neelu and the Phenomenal Printer
text: Miru Mashi is visiting Neelu in Calcutta. Neelu is thrilled. Miru Mashi always has the strangest stories to tell. Miru Mashi is visiting Neelu in Kolkata. Neelu is thrilled. Miru Mashi always has the strangest stories to tell. Like that time when she almost got snapped up by a crocodile, or that other time she lost her little finger to sneaky piranhas! Miru Mashi is a wildlife conservationist, and works with two-toed sloths in the Amazon rainforest. The next day, Miru Mashi takes Neelu to explore the city. At the Maidan, they notice a lot of horse-drawn carriages. The horses look skinny and tired. “Miru Mashi, are these horses sick?” Neelu asks. He notices one limping, barely able to pull the carriage. “These horses pull carriages for hours, and don’t always get enough water or food. Many have injuries on their limbs because of the heavy load they pull. They don’t get weekends off like us,” Miru Mashi says. "But what happens when a horse is severely injured?” Neelu asks. Miru Mashi says that an injury often leads to an infection. This could lead to the limb being amputated, which means it is removed. “After amputation, it’s hard for a big animal like a horse to survive on only three limbs. This is where prosthetics can help,” she says. “What is prosthetics?” Neelu asks. Miru Mashi tells him that prosthetics is a branch of surgery concerned with making and fitting artificial body parts. Miru Mashi tells Neelu that these days artificial limbs can be created using three-dimensional printing. In India, this technology has only been used to help humans so far, but in Australia and the USA exciting work is happening with 3D-printed animal prosthetics. Neelu has read about this technology online and is curious to see how it works. Miru Mashi takes him to meet Arzoo and Salil, designers who work with a 3D printer. “A 3D printer doesn’t print on paper. It can print and create objects using different materials,” says Arzoo. “Think of something,” says Salil, “and we can print it!” Arzoo points to a small yellow cup on a screen. “If you print that, what you get is a photo of a cup on paper. It’s flat, and it only has two dimensions, the length of the page and the height. With 3D printing, you add a third dimension–depth.” Neelu looks inside the printer and sees little spools that look like strings. “This is what our cup will be made of,” says Arzoo. “This is bioplastic, but you can use other material. Metals, wood, nylon, even food or human cells! You have to be able to melt it so it can take the shape you want.” Miru Mashi says 3D printing can create almost anything. “Like the shape of a bird’s beak or a dolphin’s tail or...” “A horse’s leg?” Neelu asks. “Yes, maybe for a small horse someday,” Says Miru Mashi. Neelu is thinking about the horses at the Maidan, and three-legged dogs he often spots on the streets. He has a lot of questions about how 3D printing can help injured animals. Arzoo tells Neelu that 3D-printed animal prosthetics is going to be the next big thing. “There are so many animals who are living better lives because of 3D-printed prosthetics.” She tells him how 3D-printed paws were created for a dog with disabled front legs to help him run better. Salil adds that in Northwestern University, in the USA, they created 3D-printed ovaries for a mouse, who then gave birth to baby mice! It’s time for Miru Mashi to leave. Neelu has learnt so much about animals and animal rescue from her. He tells her that he wants to be a veterinary surgeon when he grows up and use 3D printing to recreate limbs for injured animals. Until then, Neelu is happy spending time with animals at the shelter, especially the horses. MAGIC LIMBS Holly the Horse, Australia After three years of suffering from laminitis, Holly was about to lose her ability to walk. To prevent that, she got 3D-printed titanium horseshoes. Fred the Red-footed Tortoise, Brazil Fred lost most of her shell in a forest fire. She had also suffered from pneumonia and had nothing to eat for 45 days. She was rescued by a group of veterinarians and a dental surgeon, who created a 3D-printed shell for her. Grecia the Toucan, Costa Rica The top part of Grecia’s beak broke off after a brutal attack by a group of boys. He couldn’t forage for food, defend himself from predators, or even sing! Now he has a 3D-printed beak. 3D printing is a process of making three-dimensional objects from a digital file. The image is chopped into slices and fed to the printer. Whichever material is chosen for the 3D-printed object, the printer will pull it through a tube at a very high temperature. It comes out of a nozzle at the end in a very thin strand. The strands are deposited layer by layer on the plate and only after all the layers are printed is a 3D-printed object ready. In the future, 3D printers can help us reduce waste and pollution, and treat injuries. LET'S PRINT IN 3D
author: Riddhi Dastidar

title: An Otter's Way
text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description A group of otters learn from their father about the otter's way of living. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Nestled ﻿ne-ss-ul-d ﻿The otters nestled close together and slept. Beware ﻿be-w-air ﻿ Beware of the fisherman's net! Don't get caught! Swarming ﻿s-war-m-ing ﻿The bees were swarming around the hive to protect it. Gather ﻿ga-th-er ﻿Let's all gather around and listen to what's being said. Ok, kids, it's time to play You're all gathered here today To learn about the otter's way Stay close and rest for a while Eat a fish, roll on your belly and smile Sleep closely in a warm nestled pile Help your friends when they get stuck Swim quietly past the croc with luck While he crawls around in messy muck One, two, three, four, off you go! Swim along with the river flow Beware the current and take it slow The sunlight makes the water glow There's way more life here down below Surface when you see oars row The man casts out his net for trout If you get too close, without a doubt That net will get caught 'round your snout The fish will gather and start swarming Usually where the water's warming Dive and snatch without a warning Splash around if you catch dinner Smarter work makes you a winner You're no longer a beginner Watch closely through the grassy gaps We only have our mental maps To find and mark those painful traps Sometimes fishermen leave behind The odd one that they couldn't wind These ones are a lucky find When the night takes over day Going back home, you can say You're living in an otter's way One by one and out we go Safely into our burrow Bid goodbye until tomorrow Post-Reading Questions The word 'today' r_ _ _ _ _ with 'the otter's way'. In order for two words to r_ _ _ _, they must sound the s_ _ _. Re-read. Ask: Otters like to sleep close together in a p _ _ _. Re-read. Ask: Otters must stay away from the fisherman's n _ _. Re-read pages 6, 9 and 12. Ask: Otters spend a lot of their time avoiding d _ _ g _ r. ﻿ ﻿ What other interesting creatures live close to a river?
author: Hello English

title: The Frog and the Stars
text: Story Description A frog dreams of owning one of the stars in the sky. One night he climbs a tree to get closer to them, and discovers something amazing about the stars. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Distant dih-ss-t-unt The distant stars were far away. Valuable val-yew-a-bull The stars were shining like valuable gems. Spectacular sp-ek-tac-you-lur The sight of the moon and the stars in the sky was spectacular. Gigantic j-eye-gan-ti-k The vast, open sky was gigantic in size. The frog stayed awake at night, looking at the sky. He saw the moon and the stars. He wondered how they had got there. He wondered how far away they were. "If only I could reach the stars," said the frog, sitting on a rock to get higher. "They can't be that far away. Can they? What could be so bright yet so distant?" "They're so wonderful and shiny," said the frog. "I bet they are so valuable! I want to keep one for myself so I can show it off to everyone!" He found a tall rock and reached. But standing on a taller rock would not bring him closer to the stars. So he wrapped his long arms and legs around a tree trunk and started climbing, hoping to get closer. He climbed towards the top and reached out. "Surely I'm nearer to the stars," he said, but his hand could only grab the air. The frog reached the top, and looking down, he noticed something. It was a spectacular sight. It was beyond his wildest dreams. "Tell me, what did he see?" said a boy. "Well, let's find out," said the boy's mother, ready to carry on with the story. The sight filled the frog's heart with joy. As he had always suspected, the stars were within reach! There was the pond he lived in, far below, and on the pond's surface were several, beautiful, twinkling stars. The frog wondered if it was just a reflection of the sky. "There's only one way to find out if they are real!" said the frog. He thought about diving in and catching them. "One...two...three..." he said. The frog hopped off the tree and aimed straight for the pool with his hands stretched out. The frog caught something as he went under the surface with a gigantic splash. It was a wonderful, shiny star, and now it belonged to him. "You weren't far away after all!" he said. Post-Reading Questions What did the frog do first to get closer to the stars? Who was telling the story? Re-read. Ask: How did the frog feel? Re-read. Ask: What did the frog see from the tree? Re-read pages 14-16. Ask: What did the frog catch when he dived into the pond? Do you know how far away the stars are?
author: Hello English

title: Suddu Wants to be a Brave Boy!
text: Suddu is 7 years old. He is getting ready for school. He is feeling quite sad today. Everyone he knows is brave. His Amma yells at the big shopkeepers when they charge more money. His Appa walks in the dark to lock the gate at night. His Akka takes the bus all alone for her music class every Wednesday. Baby Laya is always looking for lizards to squish. And even the lunch box thieves are afraid of his best friend Ayesha! But Suddu does not feel brave at all. He is afraid of dogs. Big ones, little ones, short ones, tall ones, he is afraid of them all! “Maybe if I stop being afraid of dogs, I will be brave too?” “Amma! I don't want to be afraid of dogs. I want to be brave. What can I do?” “We can watch movies about dogs? We can even visit the dog shelter when your exams get over,” Amma says while feeding Baby Laya mashed carrots and milk. Suddu shakes his head sadly. He wants a quick quick solution. He wants to become brave today! He runs to the sitting room. Appa is reading the newspaper and sipping filter coffee. “Appa! I don't want to be afraid of dogs. I want to be brave. What can I do?” Appa looks at Suddu thoughtfully, “There is no one who is afraid of nothing. So are there no brave people?” Suddu's Appa never gave simple answers. And it was time to rush to school! At lunch break, he catches his best friend Ayesha. “Ayesha! I don't want to be afraid of dogs. I want to be brave. What can I do?” “There are puppies behind the sports block, let’s go there!" But the four puppies were so excited to see Suddu, that they knock him right off his feet. He did not enjoy that at all. He decides to give it one last try while walking back home. “Akka! I don't want to be afraid of dogs. I want to be brave. What can I do?” “Let’s take the short cut through the park. My friend Robert takes his dog Buddy for a walk every afternoon.” “Robert! Robert! Tell Buddy to say hello to my little brother Suddu!” calls out Akka. But Buddy was a Gre at Dane and so much bigger than Suddu! Suddu feels his insides give away. His feet turn to jelly. Then just as quickly they turn back into regular boy legs. And then turned again into superman legs. And he RANNNN. He finally stops running and leans against a mango tree. “Maybe I will just be that boy who will never be brave,” he tells himself sadly. Something soft and warm rubs against his legs. He pets it distractedly while he continues, “When I become big I will live in a country where there are no dogs.” He hears a quiet whimper. He looks down. It is a dog! An old exhausted grandpa dog who has forgotten how to bark. Just the kind of dog that Suddu can be friends with! All sorts of happiness flow into Suddu. “We can be friends and you can teach me to be not afraid of other dogs. Can I call you Shadow because I found you under a tree?” Suddu went back home and drew this picture in his drawing book. Can you guess who his new friend is?
author: Varsha Varghese
illustrator: Candice  Botha; Deepa Balsavar; Greystroke; Lavanya  Naidu; Natasha  Mehra; Rijuta Ghate; Soumya Menon; Vishnu  M Nair

title: Lion guard
text: Once upon a time there was a lion, who was walking on the road. There was 2 monkeys sitting on a branch and they saw the lion. Monkey's throw the banana peels on the ground. When the animals were walking they slip over on them. The Cheetah was laughing at the lion!! The lion felt so sad, because the cheetah was laughing. On the way, a mouse saw a lion and ask "what happened lion"? The lion tell the mouse sadly " the animals were laughing at me"!! "Oh! could I be your friend" asks the mouse. "Sure" said the lion. One of the deer saw both lion and mouse playing and felt happy.
author: Aarush Chakravarthy

title: Chutki
text: Hello..I am Myra. This is Chutki, a baby sparrow and my pet. Few weeks back, I saw her falling off from her mother's nest. I picked her up, so Tommy- the street dog would not eat it. This is Chutki’s new home. She loves her new home. She chirps “chi-chi” whenever she is hungry or wants to play with me. Mummy feeds her about once an hour when I am not home. I love feeding her after I am back from my school. I gave her biscuit mixed in water once, but then doctor uncle warned me not to feed her with much sugary food but protein rich food. Then I started giving Chutki powdered grain and dry corn powder mixed with water. Chutki loves her eating time. Once I fed her a caterpillar which appeared from a rotten apple and she gobbled it up happily. Since then, bugs, caterpillars and other insects are her favourite food!! Chutki is grown up now and tries to fly flapping her wings. Soon, she learnt flying. She loves flying inside the house. Chutki hardly lives inside her box home anymore. Sometimes, she sits on my shoulder and sometimes she sits in front of the mirror pecking her mirror reflection. She has become an important part of my family. Her chirping fills the home with joy. One day, we took Chutki to our backyard where there are many trees. Chutki loved the place. I let Chutki fly with her friends. Chutki now lives there with her friends. She loves flying high in sky and spending time in our backyard. Chutki still fills our home with joyous melody with her chirping paired with many of her friends'. World Sparrow Day Sparrows are one of the most human friendly birds. Due to different factors like reduction in number of trees, change in weather, the sparrows are close to becoming extinct*. To raise the awareness on the issue and to save the sparrows from being extinct*- World Sparrow Day is celebrated on March 20 every year. *Extinct means Vanished, No longer existing.
author: Riddhi Nath

title: The Little Boy's Animals
text: Story Description A boy says hello to his animal neighbours every day, and one day when he gets home from school, he gets a big surprise! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Elephant ﻿el-e-f-unt ﻿The elephant has a long trunk. Sheep ﻿Sh-ee-p ﻿The sheep 's fur is wool. Barn ﻿B-ar-n ﻿The animals live in the barn. Forward ﻿F-or-wood ﻿ ﻿He was really looking forward to seeing the animals. "Hello, elephant!" said the little boy. "Hello, little boy!" said the elephant. "What are you doing today?" said the little boy. "I'm going to have my bath," said the elephant. "Good morning, peacock!" said the little boy. "Good morning, little boy!" said the peacock. "Where are you going?" "I'm off to school," said the little boy. "Study hard," said the peacock. "Hello, monkey!" said the little boy. "Hello, little boy!" said the monkey. "What are you eating?" said the little boy. "My favourite - a banana!" said the monkey. "Hey there, frog!" said the little boy. "Hey there, little boy!" said the frog. "What are you doing?" said the little boy. "I'm trying to catch this fly," said the frog. "Hi, sheep!" said the little boy. "Hi, little boy!" said the sheep. "You're in a hurry today." "I need to get to school!" said the little boy. "See you later!" "Hello there, cow!" said the little boy. "Hello there, little boy!" said the cow. "Jingle your bell," said the little boy. "All right," said the cow. "Just for you." "Good morning, deer!" said the little boy. "Good morning, little boy!" said the deer. "What are you doing?" said the little boy. "I'm out walking, like you!" said the deer. The little boy went to school, and when he got home, there was a loud banging at the door. "I wonder who that could be?" he said. He opened the door and all of the local animals were standing on the porch. "Mum, can my friends come in to play?" he said. "It depends how many there are," said his mother. "Are they hungry?" "Are you hungry?" he said to the animals. "We're very hungry," said the monkey. "Can you give us something to eat?" said the deer. "I have eight friends at the door!" the little boy said to his mother. "And they all want something to eat." "Take them around to the barn," said the little boy's mother. The animals went to the barn, and the little boy and his mother gave them a big dinner, which they really enjoyed. The animals thanked the little boy and his mother for the food, and the little boy thanked the animals for their visit. The animals went home, and the little boy looked forward to seeing them again the next day. Post-Reading Questions H _ _ _ _ is a greeting word. Do all of the animals reply to the boy? Re-read. Ask: Who was knocking at the door? Re-read. Ask: What did the animals want? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿Where did the animals eat? ﻿What kind of animals live near you?
author: Hello English

title: The Tree Rhyme
text: Story Description A tree rhymes about itself, talking about the kinds of fruits and flowers it grows, and how it turns from a seed into a tree over time. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Evergreen ﻿e-vur-gr-ee-n ﻿The tree that keeps its leaves year round is called an evergreen. Deciduous ﻿The tree that sheds its leaves every autumn is known as a deciduous. ﻿dih-sid-you-uss Sycamore ﻿si-k-a-more ﻿The sycamore tree grows conkers in the autumn, which fall and can be collected. Enduring ﻿en-d-your-ing ﻿The tree lived for over 500 years. It was enduring. Standing tall with glee, I'm an evergreen tree. I keep my leaves to me, Never shedding annually. Call me a hemlock, a fir, A spruce or a pine, I'm there at Christmas time, When jingle bells chime, In your living room, Above the presents, And the mistletoe and wine. Standing proud and free, I'm a fruit tree. My leaves fall free, Each autumn, annually. I'm an apple, a lemon, An orange, a cherry, You'll find me in the heat, And the humidity. In the summer, When my fruits have grown, Pick them with your hands, Or throw a stone. Standing happy to be, I'm a deciduous tree. My fruits, leaves and petals, Fall annually. I'm an acorn, a sycamore, an elm, birch, an oak, I'll shelter you from rain, And a definite soak. I have my blossom powers, Growing pretty pink flowers. Let's see and read, The life cycle of me. First I'm a seed, then a bundle of roots, Then some leaves and a cluster of shoots. A longer branch and bunches of leaves, Thicker branches, roots, then a tree. You can't see them but under my trunk, There's a hidden part of me, a great chunk. It's like very long toes reaching down, Deeper and beneath the ground. My roots! So deep, hidden and protected, To most creatures they go undetected. My roots soak up nutrients and water, Without them I would be much shorter! My fruit's seeds soon fall all around, And they get sewn into the ground. Winter comes, spring, summer and autumn, The changing seasons somehow sort them. Then with the roots and strong foundation, And according to my calculation, It won't be long before they grow, It won't be long before they......show! Suddenly when I look around, I see that they all surround. Feeding off the soil and roots, Spreading with their stronger shoots. Then over hundreds and hundreds of years, Having seen bears, foxes, wolves, cats, birds and deers, We have spread around together Having outlasted all kinds of weather Standing fair and tall, Cleaning the air for all, We're one of the oldest things you'll see, The strong, firm, enduring tree. Post-Reading Questions What kind of tree sheds its leaves every year? What kind of tree keeps its leaves year round? Re-read. Ask: In the beginning of its life, what is a tree? Re-read pages 8-9. Ask: What does a tree have that we cannot see above the ground? Re-read. Ask: What do the trees do to the air? What is your favourite kind of tree?
author: Hello English

title: Rekha Goes Snorkelling
text: Story Description Rekha goes snorkelling at an island with her mother, where she finds all sorts of fascinating underwater creatures. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Warmer w-or-m-ur The cool water felt warmer after a while. Coral c-o-r-ul The sea bed was covered in beautiful coral. Creatures cr-ee-ch-ur-s There were many different creatures in the sea. Stretchy s-tr-e-ch-ee The octopus looked very stretchy with its tentacles. Phew! That's a lot of rowing! Don't worry, Rekha. We're almost at the island. Mama, it feels cold. You will warm up, Rekha. I'll watch you from the shore. Enjoy your snorkling! Whoops! I drank some water. Ugh! At least the sea feels warmer now. Look! There are creatures, plants and coral everywhere! Tiny little turtles! Colourful creatures with weird and cool shapes! It looks like half an orange! Wow! Dolphins swimming past! They're really friendly! A long, stretchy and fast octopus! It has a huge, fat head! This fish thinks it can fly! It splashed me in the face! Bleugh! Let's go underwater! Cool, pretty blue fish in a group! Ooh, a star fish stretched out! Haha! Fish with pointy noses! Yellow and white ones too! That underwater snake thing looks really scary! I'm not swimming anywhere near it! Whoa! The stingray glides like a bird! I can see its mouth under its body. It looks like a talking marshmallow, haha! I saw all kinds of creatures, Mama! It's so much fun! You should come and swim too! Post-Reading Questions How did the water feel when Rekha first stepped into the sea? What creature frightened Rekha? Re-read. Ask: What did Rekha accidentally do? Re-read. Ask: What flew over Rekha? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What creature does the stingray move like? ﻿If you could see any underwater creature, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: Flies & Superheroes
text: Anoop and Sunita sat next to each other in creative writing class. The teacher gave the class the task of creating an original story. To help the students, the teacher put the students into pairs, so that each student could share their ideas and improve their writing with their partner. "What do you have so far, Anoop?" said Sunita. "I have my main character as a boy," said Anoop. "What have you got?" "Mine is a girl," said Sunita. "Let me share my idea first," said Anoop. "You critique my story and tell me how I can improve the characters and the plot." "All right, then after you share yours, you can analyse mine," said Sunita. Anoop shared his story first. "My character is called Ben and he wants to be a superhero." "Ok, that sounds interesting," said Sunita. "Ben's science teacher explains to him that science has not yet discovered how to be a superhero." "So Ben goes to his mother, who is ironing his clothes. He talks about his idea to grow into a super giant by eating a secret substance." "And she laughs at him," said Sunita. "No! She agrees with him! He can be anything he wants to be." "Except a superhero." "Ok," said Anoop. "Fine, so he can't be a superhero normally. Now he has to come up with a better plan to become one. So what's your idea?" Anita is a graduate who is always thinking about how birds can fly. Maybe she can learn to fly! No, Anoop, it has to be more interesting than that. What about outer space? Maybe she can fly beyond the atmosphere? Anoop, stop for a moment. So she loves birds and wonders if they can fly...in outer space? What about flies, Sunita? Birds fly...flies...yes! She adores flies and she wonders if they can hold their breath in space and fly. So then two flies whizz around crazily in the air and meet. One is a boy and one is a girl, and Sunita loves it because the flies are falling in love and... Yeah...Sunita, stop there. You're grossing me out. Sorry, so maybe they are fly friends? Anyway, back to your story, Anoop... So in my story, Ben talks to his friends about transforming into a superhero and saving the world from evil. His friends laugh at him and they go to this drinks stall where there's a stubbly balding man and a movie poster of Khabir Khan in 'Kashmir If You Can'. And while they drink mango juice, Ben tells his friends about wanting to be a superhero and they shiver with laughter. The old man just stares. So nobody believes in Ben. What do you have next, Sunita? There's a mutated strain of fly that can fly in zero gravity, and Anita studies physics and biology, and gets interested in how to become an astronaut. Has India ever had an astronaut? I don't know. Hey Anoop, maybe she can be the youngest female astronaut in the world! Yeah, she has to study real hard and go through rigorous tests like spinning around at two thousand kilometres per hour. That's crazy, Anoop. So then after getting super smart and graduating from astronaut college and getting her degree in everything to do with space, she officially becomes an astronaut, and she is given a date where she will go into space on a mission. But she has to take something with her, right? Yeah...a specimen of two flies! Do they have to be normal flies, Sunita? Why not those ones that buzz around fruit bowls? Eww, Anoop! Yuck! Well, Ben stares out the window. He rarely goes outside to play because he's so engrossed in watching superhero TV shows and studying science. He starts to think about changing his body to become mega strong like a robotronic impregnable human. You mean nobody can beat him? Yeah! And Ben lives in a...a jungle setting! Loads of leaves and trees surround his house, and where he lives is a training compound where he becomes mega strong. There could be a nice pretty path going from his house through the garden. Yeah, there is! And then at the end of the path is a beastly maze that is different every time he encounters it. So he goes out running and climbing trees, and he's super happy because every time he exercises he gets closer to being a superhero. So it's like he's shedding his skin to become super strong. Yeah, underneath he's a mega lord warrior with a five gold badge unbeaten record! And there's a girl he likes? A girl? Mmmm..yeah, why not. But she's more of a training partner. And she chases him around a tree to try and kiss him, and he doesn't like it so he runs faster. Yeah, but that's kind of grim, getting captured by a girl and being forced to kiss. He's a superhero, not a sissy. What about Anita? Anita dreams about space. She does that a lot, this imagining stuff. Why doesn't she just go there? Ok, ok. I'll get to that. So she wonders about the planets in outer space and what she will find on her mission. And so does the mutated super fly. Yes! The fly dreams of space too! The fly wears a helmet, right? It's mutated but it can't breathe in space. Ok, so the fly can't breathe in space, we know that from science. But it can fly. It can bounce and leap around as much as it wants. Your superhero Ben wears a helmet, right? No, he has special goggles that cast out flame bionic laser doom rays that liquify enemies. What kind of enemies? Superheroes that have turned evil. Like who? Like, the horn men who are part mutated rhinos that tried to take over Africa. Ben thinks of flying and frying his opponents. So have you prepared this story before? A little bit. I wrote some. Then I thought about it. Thought some more. Then I watched TV for my ideas. So this is already a TV show? No, no. This is my story. Yours is definitely more...original, Sunita. Yeah, this is very personal because I love space. Anyway so on the day of the mission, Anita looks great. She is dressed in her uniform with her hair tied back in a pony tail. Are astronauts allowed to do that? Anita has a specially designed helmet to allow her to wear a ponytail. So she's ready to enter the rocket with the flies in a jar. And they blast off into space, don't they? ZOOM! In a controlled launch, yes. What happens in space? Are there aliens? Hmm...no. But other astronauts travel in a group with Anita. She lets the flies out into space, and what a surprise, they can fly in zero gravity! Then what? Then everyone takes important notes and Anita is officially declared correct, and she gets acknowledged because it was her idea. Are the flies happy? Yeah, but they feel a bit sick when they return to earth, because they forget that earth has gravity. So they have to learn how to fly again but they keep hitting the ceiling. Well, Ben learns that certain flies are attracted to light, so if he wants to learn to fly, he needs bright light to give him powers. That was the secret substance turning him into a flying superhero? Light? Yeah, I don't want to write a long story, Sunita. So Ben chats to his Dad and the neighbours to prove his theory that light turns people into superheroes. And Dads are always right, aren't they? Yeah, Dads know everything. So Mum and Dad show Ben how light works. That's when Ben discovers how to access the power of light and transform his body. Oh, I forgot something, Anoop. What? There was a malfunction on the space ship and everything got ejected into space. So they had to spend time tidying up space before they returned to earth. What happens to Ben? Does he become superhuman? Not exactly. No?? No, he doesn't need his human shell anymore. He finds the perfect kind of body. Well, what's that? He becomes an awesome, brilliant fly? A glamorous fly! What? No! Not like a girl. He's a super strong boy fly. That's the end. Well, Anita goes to outer space again and she discovers that birds can also fly in zero gravity. And they can breathe too! So they don't need to wear helmets. That's the end? Yeah. What? What about Anita? Doesn't she find a superhero in space or something? No, she goes back to studying birds and watching flies. Or maybe she doesn't. Maybe she studies cats afterwards. What happens to Ben? He thinks the bedroom light is the moon and gets burned. He loses all of his powers. But he keeps trying to become a superhero again, right? Yeah, he finds a secret substance in bones which transforms his body. Into what? A dog.
author: Hello English

title: Naughty Iman
text: Story Description Iman feels bored so he looks for naughty things to do, like toppling over piles of books and sweets at the market. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Stomped st-om-p-d The boy stomped with heavy feet. Pile p-eye-ul There was a big pile of books. Neighbour nay-bur They said hello to their next-door neighbour. Basket bas-kit There was a basket of fruit. Iman felt very angry because he was bored. He felt like doing something naughty. He crossed his arms and stomped his feet while he thought about what to do. "What's wrong you with you, Iman?" said his mother. "You look upset." "Hmph!" said Iman. "Nothing is wrong." Iman and his mother went to the market. At the fruit stall they tried apples. Iman kept reaching for the bottom apples. "Don't do that, it's naughty!" said the market seller. Iman laughed. At the library, Iman reached for the bottom books in a pile. As he was pulling them out, the librarian said, "Don't do that, it's naughty!" Iman laughed. "You seem happier now," said Iman's mother, as Iman pulled her hand. "What are you excited about?" "Look!" said Iman. "Sweets!" At the food stall, Iman reached for the bottom sweets to pull out. "Don't do that, it's naughty!" said the food seller. Iman laughed. At home, Iman got a stall and climbed up. He started pulling the bottom box out from a big pile. "Don't do that!" said Iman's mother. "The boxes will fall on you!" Iman laughed. Iman still felt bored. He went to the neighbour and stared at his feet. He thought about removing the neighbour's flip flops. "It's too tricky," he said. Iman saw his mother's sari. He tried to pull it off her shoulder! "Don't do that, it's naughty!" said his mother, distracted from her book. Iman laughed. "Iman, come here and look at this!" said his mother, pointing at a basket. Iman stopped trying to remove a book from the bottom of a pile. His eyes filled with joy. He went to the basket. Iman saw the puppies sleeping. He took a puppy and cuddled it. The other puppies slept and watched. "I'm not bored anymore," he said. Post-Reading Questions What made Iman feel calm at the end? What things did Iman do that were naughty? Re-read. Ask: What would happen to the books if Iman takes one out from the pile? Re-read. Ask: What does Iman see that makes him feel excited? Re-read. Ask: What does Iman want to take? Describe some things that make you feel bored or excited.
author: Hello English

title: Tessa's Birthday Surprise
text: Story Description Tessa the baby tortoise is late for school and she forgets something important. It is a very special day for her! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Festival fe-st-i-val Everyone would sing and dance at the festival. Giggling gi-gl-ing The class was giggling together. Applause a-p-laws Clapping hands is a round of applause. Bicycle bi-sic-ul She wanted a new bicycle for her birthday. "Good morning, Tessa!" said Benny Bunny. "Morning, Benny!" said Tessa. Tessa was a baby tortoise who could only walk very slowly. Benny was a rabbit who could hop so quickly. Benny always passed Tessa every morning on the way to school. Because Tessa could only walk very slowly, she was always late for school. "Where have you been?" said Mrs. Honk, her school teacher. "I'm sorry, Mrs. Honk," said Tessa. "Come in and sit down, Tessa," said Mrs. Honk. "If you keep on being late, you'll get detention," said Freddy Fox. "Yeah, then you'll have to stay late after school!" said Manny Mouse. "Oh, no," said Tessa. "I don't want that!" Later, Mrs. Honk brought Tessa to the front of the class. "Tessa, tell me the day and the month, and why this month is important," said Mrs. Honk. "Today is the 28th day of the 10th month," said Tessa. "And this month is very special, because it is the annual animal festival." "What happens at the festival?" said Mrs. Honk. "We sing, play games, eat lots of food and have fun," said Tessa." "Are you forgetting something, Tessa?" said Mrs. Honk. "Um...I don't know," said Tessa. "Think of something that is very important to you," said Mrs. Honk. "Well...clothes, my shell, my bag, my classmates. I'm not sure," said Tessa. The school started giggling and singing a song quietly. "Enough of that!" snapped Mrs. Honk. "You'll give away the answer!" "Ooh..." said Tessa. "You're singing Happy Birthday. It's my birthday today!" After school, Tessa invited Mrs. Honk and her school friends around to celebrate her birthday. They sang Happy Birthday to Tessa and gave her applause. There was a special present from her school friends and Mrs. Honk waiting on the table. "Are you going to open it and see what's inside?" said her mother. "I can't wait!" said Tessa. She opened the present......and inside was an amazing pair of roller skates! "They're brilliant!" said Tessa. "Thank you so much," said Tessa, crying with happiness. "You are my best friends." "We love you so much," they said. "Happy birthday, Tessa." When the party was ending, Tessa put on her roller skates to test them out. "Now I"ll beat Benny Bunny to school every morning!" she said. "And I won't be late for school ever again!" "And perhaps for my next birthday, I'll get something even faster," she thought. "Perhaps I'll get...a bicycle!" Post-Reading Questions Why was Tessa always late for school? What did Tessa want for her next birthday? Re-read. Ask: What is the date? Re-read. Ask: What song was the class singing? Re-read. Ask: What was Tessa's birthday present? What is the best birthday present you've had?
author: Hello English

title: My friend Giri
text: The weather was really good that evening. “I am going down for a walk and you are coming with me,” Naani told me. I didn’t have anything better to do and I could see some of my friends in the park, so I readily agreed. But something happened on our way to the park. A little boy on a bicycle hit my naani and she cried out in pain. She glared at him and asked, “can’t you see?” The little boy started crying. Everyone was looking at us. I tried to hush him but that made things worse. He was wailing louder now. His father came running. “What happened”, he asked us. “Is that your son? She asked him. "He doesn’t know how to ride. That’s why I scolded him”, she told him. “I am sorry aunty, Giri is a special child so please forgive him,” he told her with folded hands. “Ohh,” gasped naani. “I am so sorry, I shouldn’t have scolded him,” she said sadly. Giri was still crying when we left. “Am I a special child mumma?” I asked my mother that night. " You are my special child my dear, she told me and messed up my hair. I told her what happened in the evening and she explained to me - W ell, a special child is more fragile and you need need to be gentle with them, she told me. Like the children in the school you go to on Saturdays? I asked her. The children there don’t have money to buy stationery or even story books, which is why she is there most Saturdays with story books. No, my dear, the children at school have everything but money. They are not special children. They don't have any physical disabilities - they can see, talk, hear, run, hold things in their hands. They can think, communicate, read, write, walk properly and frame proper sentences. But some children have physical disabilities and others have mental disabilities. She told me that Giri has Asperger's syndrome. Some of the symptoms include lack of social awareness, lack of interest in making friends, inability to understand the thoughts, feelings, or emotions of others or avoiding eye contact. Ohh that means Giri must have hit naani accidently, I told her. I didn't sleep well that night. I could only think of little Giri. Next day I packed a box of crayons and a coloring book. Giri was riding his bicycle but stopped when he saw me. Will you like to colour with these crayons, I asked him? He nodded and looked at his father. "But first we have to be friends," I said, offering my hand. “Friendddd,” he yelled, grabbed my hand and shook it vigorously. We played for almost an hour that day. Naani said sorry to him and taught Giri how to color his favorite animal – a pink elephant with a green bow on its tail. She also treated him with his favourite dessert – custard with apples, bananas and grapes. He doesn't talk much and sometimes he gets very loud but he is my best friend and we meet every Saturday to play in the park now. Do you want to join us?
author: pallavi srivastava
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Hayley  Alonzo; Onesmus   Kakungi; Rijuta Ghate; Sanjay Sarkar; Suvidha Mistry; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Polly the Pet Parrot
text: Story Description Lisa gets a new pet parrot called Polly. But Polly doesn't like living inside a small cage, and eventually she becomes sad. Can Lisa make Polly feel happy again? Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Overjoyed oe-ver-joy-d She was overjoyed to have a new pet parrot. Saddest sa-d-ist The parrot stuck in the cage was the saddest parrot. Happiest ha-p-ee-ist The parrot set free was the happiest parrot. Unlocked un-lo-k-d She unlocked the cage and the parrot flew out and into the sky. One day Lisa's father came home with a parrot named Polly. Lisa was overjoyed. "Hi!" said Lisa. "Hi!" said Polly. Lisa loved Polly. She was the perfect pet to show off to her friends. Lisa talked to Polly every day and Polly always replied. "Are you hungry?" said Lisa. "Hungry!" Polly would say. "Want something to eat?" said Lisa. "Eat! Eat!" Polly would say. Each day Lisa offered Polly something new to eat. "Seeds! Nuts! Seeds! Nuts!" Polly would shout. "A piece of cake? A tomato? A strawberry?" said Lisa, offering Polly anything she could find. "Seeds! Nuts! Outside! Outside!" "Can you say the word difficult?" said Lisa. "Easy peasy!" Polly would say. "Can you say silly girl, go away?" said Lisa. "I love you! I love you!" Polly would say. Then one day Lisa came home from school and found Polly looking sad. "What's wrong, Polly?" said Lisa. "I miss my family. I was taken from them and put in this cage. I don't belong here." Lisa was shocked that Polly spoke so well. "That's terrible," said Lisa. "I never realised." Lisa looked out of her bedroom window. She saw a cluster of parrots flying around the park trees. They looked beautiful. They spoke to each other and formed patterns in the sky. "They are my family," said Polly. "I'm so sorry you were put in a cage," said Lisa. "If you keep me in this cage," said Polly, "I'll get upset and miserable over time. I will be the saddest pet..." "...but if you set me free, I'll be the happiest parrot that there is." After some thought, Lisa opened the cage door and went to her bedroom window. "Really?" said Polly. "You're letting me out?" "It's not fair to keep you captured," said Lisa. "You belong outside. Will I see you again, Polly?" "I think you will," said Polly. "Thank you, Lisa." Lisa opened the window and unlocked the cage. Polly spread her wings and flew into the sky, following the group of parrots flying around the trees. She was so happy. She turned back to Lisa and waved with her wing. Lisa smiled. For a while Lisa felt upset, but not guilty. She missed Polly, but she had done the right thing by letting her go. Of course her father was disappointed in her, but he soon came around and understood why Lisa had set Polly free. And to Lisa's joy, when she played with her friends, groups of different birds flew around the park. Perhaps she would see Polly perched in one of the trees! And one day, there was Polly, sitting on a high branch, as happy as any parrot could possibly be. Post-Reading Questions Who could Lisa show off her pet parrot? What kind of things did Polly want to eat? Re-read. Ask: Why did Polly feel sad? Re-read. Ask: Why did Lisa set Polly free? Re-read. Ask: How did Lisa feel after she let Polly go home? What is the best gift that you have received?
author: Hello English

title: Finding Seeds!
text: ﻿Story Description A tree tells a story about a boy, a girl and a dog who collect seeds and grow plants, and also look after trees. ﻿ ﻿ Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Branches ﻿br-an-ch-is ﻿A tree has many branches. Tasty ﻿tay-st-ee ﻿ ﻿The tree fruits are very tasty. Tamarind ﻿tam-are-in-d ﻿The tamarind had a strong taste. Regularly ﻿reg-you-lar-lee ﻿They would regularly go looking for seeds - about three times per week. Sanjay, Sita and Ruffles the dog are seed collectors who love to have fun! They search the ground for seeds and bulbs they can plant. After school, they walk by the rivers, valleys and hills, searching for new seeds. "Here, Ruffles!" says Sanjay. "Sniff over here! See what you can find!" "This is a new seed!" says Sita. They walk in the wind, rain and sunshine, searching for fruit, finding trees and looking after them......new trees they can take shelter under from the strong winds and the hot sun......new trees like me! I'm a magical tamarind tree. "What is it, Ruffles?" says Sita. "What can you see, boy?" says Sanjay. Sita finds some fruit. Ruffles finds his butterfly. Sanjay eats some of the fruit from my branches. "Delicious!" he says. "The fruit from this tree is so tasty!" says Sita. "The best tasting fruit we've found!" says Sanjay. "Ruff!" agrees Ruffles. I grew the apples and bananas especially for them to pick! Sanjay, Sita and Ruffles love me, the magical tamarind tree, and hug me regularly. Their care helps me to produce more tasty fruit! "We can take the seed from this tree," says Sita. "And we can grow a new one!" "Great idea!" says Sanjay. "Then we'll have loads of different fruits!" "Ruff!" says Ruffles. They visit me often and eat their lunch underneath my branches. Every time they come I grow something new for them! And over time, their seed collections grow into new plants and trees. Trees just like me - a magical tamarind tree! Post-Reading Questions What do Sanjay, Sita and Raffles the dog enjoy doing? What two things do they search the ground for? Re-read. Ask: Why do Sanjay, Sita and Raffles stay under the trees? Re-read. Ask: Who did the magical tree grow fruits for? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What do the seed collections grow into? ﻿What is your favourite fruit? What is your favourite tree?
author: Hello English

title: The Adventures of Akara and Linio
text: Meet Akara and Linio. They are straight lines. Akara is a standing line. Linio is a sleeping line. Come on, let’s meet some of their other line friends! See these curved lines? They are Archit and Squiggles. This is Slopes! Slopes is a slanting line. What are these friends going to do today? They are going to make animal shapes together. Look at this dog! Can you spot Linio? Wow, look at this elephant! Where is Archit, can you see? ﻿ Hey, it’s a turtle! Can you spot Squiggles? What a lovely snail! And there’s Slopes, can you see? Woohoo, an owl! Where’s Akara? Shhh! The lines are all resting now. Making animal shapes is fun, but tiring!
author: Kuzhali  Manickavel

title: Taking Off
text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description A scientist called Simon and his daughter Sandra design things that can fly. Simon designs a flying hat, and a pair of flying shoes for Sandra! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Fixed Fik-s-d The skilled scientist fixed the flying hat. Improved imp-roo-v-d The shoes were improved and finally they worked. Higher hi-y-ur The shoes could bounce much higher than before. Further fur-th-ur The hat took the scientist further than before. There was once a scientist called Simon. He designed things that could make people fly. One day he invented a flying cap. His daughter Sandra was just as smart as he was. Maybe even smarter. She had an idea for some flying shoes. The shoes didn’t work but Simon took Sandra on his flights with his working hat. Simon fixed Sandra's shoes, and she could bounce higher and higher. Simon made an upgrade for Sandra’s shoes as a birthday present. She was so happy. She was finally ready for the big jump, the biggest test of her shoes. How high could she go? Simon kept flying higher with his improved hat. Sandra kept reaching higher with her better shoes. Even the pet fish found a way to get into the sky. The shoes were so good that Sandra made it into space, flipping and turning and performing flips. And she took her father on a space flight. The goldfish landed safely when the balloons popped. And Sandra and Simon worked on a hat that could fly them even further - to the moon! Post-Reading Questions What does Simon give Sandra for her birthday? How high can Sandra bounce? Re-read. Ask: How did the pet fish fly? Re-read. Ask: What tricks did Sandra perform in space? Re-read. Ask: What is Simon's next project? If you could invent something, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: I Won't Eat That
text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description A little girl looks at various objects and decides whether or not she will eat them. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Insect in-sec-t The insect was crawling on the leaf. Precious pr-eh-sh-uss The butterfly is a precious creature. Lovely lu-v-lee There were some lovely white flowers on the fence. Delicious de-lih-sh-uss The sandwich tasted delicious. I won’t eat that. These seeds are for birds. I won’t eat that. These are insect eggs. I won’t eat that. Ants have touched it. I won’t eat that. It’s a dirty bird with a mouse. I won’t eat that. It’s a precious butterfly. I won’t eat that. They are flowers on a fence. I won’t eat that. These are lovely white flowers. I won’t eat that. These are potato chips. I won’t eat her. She’s a cow. But I will eat that sandwich! It looks delicious! Post-Reading Questions What was the bird about to eat? What did the girl finally eat? Re-read. Ask: Why wouldn't the girl eat the apple slice? Re-read. Ask: What didn't the girl want to eat? Re-read. Ask: What colour is the girls' lunch box? What things don't you like to eat?
author: Hello English

title: Larry the Locomotive
text: Story Description Larry is a locomotive who travels over bridges and through tunnels on his day, and has to be careful of animals in the fields. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Locomotive low-co-mow-tiv The front engine of a train is called a locomotive. Tunnel ﻿tuh-n-ul ﻿The train travels through the dark tunnel. Complete ﻿co-m-pl-eat ﻿The train completes its journey and arrives at the station. Resting ﻿re-st-ing ﻿ ﻿The train stopped because a cow was resting on the track. Larry the locomotive loves to ride the tracks. Watch out for the dog and the cow, Larry! You'll have to use your brakes! Round we go on the short track, Larry! Through the tunnel in the cliff. Lights on! Stop at the sidings and have a chat with Dennis and Kate. How are you, guys? Over the old stone bridge looking at the river below. Over the big suspension bridge. Wow, look at the view of the city! Look out, there’s a cow up ahead. It’s resting on the tracks. Sound the horn, Larry! We scared the cow away. Now we can speed up! That’s one complete circuit. Well done, Larry! Rest your engines for the day. Post-Reading Questions Why did Larry have to slow down? Who did Larry stop and talk to? Re-read. Ask: Why did Larry shine his light? Re-read. Ask: What kind of bridge did Larry travel over? Re-read. Ask: ﻿How did Larry get the cow to move off the track? ﻿ Describe how a train ride works.
author: Hello English

title: Laasya meets Lakdu
text: 'Dum, dum, clang, clang.' The sound of utensils wake up Laasya. Today she has to paste variety of leaves in her scrap book. "Where are the leaves?" she cries out. She could only find bits and pieces of leaves. Instead, a thin, tiny stick lay in the place of leaves. Quietly and Slowly, she tries to hold the stick. But wait! The stick starts walking. "A walking stick?" she asks herself. Laasya is scared but s he touches it. The walking stick is harmless. She wants to show it to Miss Beena, her teacher. "Sshh! We are going to school now," she tells the walking stick. Carefully, she puts it in her pencil holder. "Wow! That is a stick insect." says Miss. Beena. "Show me, show me," the children buzz. Miss Beena tells them, "It has lost its way. It needs grass and leaves right away." Together, they decide to leave it in Laasya's garden. Miss Beena names the stick insect, 'Lakdu'. "Hee-hee-hee-hee," the children cackle. "Bye bye Lakdu," they crackle. Laasya goes back home. She places Lakdu in her garden. “You are my favourite pet, Lakdu,” she says and sets it free. Whenever Laasya goes into her garden, she finds Lakdu munching on leaves. At times, he simply takes rest on branches. Laasya is happy and proud of her pet.
author: Leena Satuluri

And he has make me learn. he always told me what to do and what not to do. and do not speak so loudly. dad also told us that do not touch things like this. it may get dangerous. he also is a helper. when we need him, he is always with us. dad says that our train is going to come. come fast. come on everybody the train is here. look jay and guardianship you grand parents and your mausi are here. look your mausi is going. lets have a picture.

title: Riya's Carrots
text: Story Description Riya cooks some carrots but burns them. She has to start again from the beginning to cook for her friends. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Wandered one-der-d The rabbit wandered across the field. Wondered wun-der-d The rabbit wondered what to cook. Arrived a-r-eye-v-d The rabbit's friends arrived for dinner. Tortoise tore-tu-ss The rabbit used a tortoise shell as a cooking pot. One day, Riya was in the forest wondering what to do. She decided she would make dinner for her friends - the elephant, the hedgehog, the squirrel and the bird. She went vegetable picking and found a gigantic carrot stuck in the ground. She pulled as hard as she could to get it out! Later, Riya had collected two big carrots. She wondered what to do next. "I need to make a fire to cook them!" she thought. So Riya wandered into the forest and collected lots of wood to make her fire. But the fire was too hot! Riya burned the carrots. They were too hard to eat. Riya found some new, smaller carrots. They looked great! "I'm running out of time," she thought. "My friends are coming soon. I had better hurry up and cook!" Riya collected some big rocks to make a stove. They were very heavy and difficult to move. Riya found a pot on a stove by someone's house. "I need something like this to cook in," she realised. Then later, Riya found a tortoise shell by the side of a path. "I can use this as my pot for cooking in!" she thought. Meanwhile, the elephant, the hedgehog, the squirrel and the bird made their way to Riya's house. "I wonder what we'll eat," said the elephant. "I hope it's big." "I hope it's seeds," said the bird. "With nuts," said the squirrel. "I would like to have carrots," said the hedgehog. And so Riya used the tortoise shell to cook the carrots. Very soon, it was ready......and the animals arrived and enjoyed Riya's delicious carrots! Post-Reading Questions What happened to the first carrot that Riya cooked? Why did Riya have to hurry up and cook dinner? Re-read pages 11-13. Ask: What items did Riya collect to cook with? Re-read. Ask: What animals came to have dinner? Re-read. Ask: What did Riya cook the carrots inside? If you could cook, what would you make for dinner?
author: Hello English

title: Rhino Rescue
text: Story Description Abu, a baby Rhino, loses his way through the fields being chased by a snake, and falls into a pit. A group of people help him find his way back to his mother. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿ ﻿ Buzzing ﻿buh-z-ing ﻿The bee made a buzzing sound. Hissing ﻿h-ih-ss-ing ﻿The snake made a hissing sound. Whimper ﻿w-im-pur ﻿The rhino gave a worried whimper. Machine ﻿muh-sh-ee-n ﻿ ﻿The rhino heard the sound of a machine. Abu was a baby rhino. One day out in the fields, his mother warned him about snakes hiding in long grass. "Snakes are very dangerous," she said. "You will be frightened if you see one. Then you will run away and get lost. Stay away from snakes." Abu went to the swamp to swim in the mud. He watched flies buzzing around his head and laughed at them. He was having so much fun. Suddenly a hissing noise came from the grass, and Abu was alert. Abu walked to the long grass and the hissing got louder. Just then, a huge snake jumped up from the grass and chased a deer. Abu pulled away the grass to see. The snake caught the deer and squeezed it. The snake saw Abu and let the deer go. It hissed at Abu, who ran away as fast as he could, far from the snake and the long grass. Abu ran out of breath and stopped running. He was in longer grass now, and he remembered his mother's advice. "Stay away from snakes." Abu wanted to go back, but which direction was home? Abu walked along a path, but he did not recognise anything. He could not see his mother. He could not see his home. He was lost. He walked and walked until sunset, but still he could not find his home. He was exhausted. He called out but his mother would not come. As the day turned into night, Abu felt sad and desperate. He really wanted to go home and see his mother. He cried but nobody would come. He ran through the night, thinking he was close to home, and with the last of his energy, he ran fast through the bushes. But Abu ran straight into a covered pit. He fell all the way inside, deep and down. Abu's whimpers caught the attention of a nearby rhino. "Mother?" he called up. "Abu!" she said. "I thought I had lost you." "Help me out!" "I can't get to you," said his mother. "I will get help." Abu waited through the night until his mother returned. "Put on the ropes," she told him, and he sat on the ground, completely tired. A very powerful machine began lifting Abu. He felt himself being pulled up and out of the pit. Abu saw scores of people surrounding him. They were cheering and taking pictures. Abu felt sad. He did not know who they were, but they were threatening. Suddenly a man started to remove his ropes, and Abu stared at the people, angry that they had could come to take photographs, and look at him in distress. A local ranger removed the last rope from Abu. "There, you are free to go," he said. Abu saw another rhino hiding behind a tree. "Mother!" he said. "Abu, you're safe," said his mother. "Now we can go home together." They walked all the way back home, avoiding the long grass and not seeing a single snake! Post-Reading Questions ﻿How did Abu get lost? How did Abu get rescued? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What happened to the deer? ﻿Re-read pages 16-17. Ask: ﻿For how long was Abu stuck in the hole? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿How did Abu feel about the people watching him? ﻿Do you feel sorry for Abu? Should he have been more careful?
author: Hello English

title: Treasure in the caves
text: One cave here, one cave there, Tunnels of wind and air. Cave one and cave two Take air in and out of you First, stick your finger in there Let it roam everywhere Side to side, let it wiggle Now, give it a little jiggle Dislodge it from that dark jail. Dig deeper. Use your nail. If the treasure is wet, dry it Roll it between your fingers. Try it! Chuck it once the flakes are dry Don't be scared, don't be shy. Old and young. Women and men. Everyone wants to explore this den. It’s after all your nose, so dig, dig, dig it, Why should anyone mind it? But remember, do take care, Don’t let anyone know the treasure's there! And if you are in a hurry, don't you worry here, Just stick it, squish and squash it, anywhere!
author: Swagata Sen Pillai

title: Monkey Hats
text: Story Description While a man sleeps under a tree, a bunch of monkeys steal the man's bag of hats. They have fun trying them on, but when the man wakes up they get something they don't expect! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Mischievously mih-ss-ch-ee-vus-lee The monkeys mischievously reached down and stole the hats. Admired ad-my-ur-d The monkeys admired how they looked while wearing the hats. Tightened ty-tun-d The hats tightened around their heads because of the heat. Annoyed a-n-oy-d The man became annoyed with the monkeys and their behaviour. One day there was a man walking with a very heavy sack, and the sack was filled with hats. The man stopped to rest under the tree. He was exhausted from the heat and from the weight of the bag he was carrying. Very soon the man fell asleep under the tree. Little did he know that a bunch of monkeys were waiting in that tree. They watched the man sleep, and they mischievously looked through his bag. One by one, they emptied the bag and played with the man's hats. They were a perfect fit! The monkeys tried on different hats and admired the colours. The monkeys joined hands and sang songs, swapping hats with each other. Suddenly the man woke up in a daze. He remembered where he was - under the tree. He looked through his bag but it was empty. He wondered who had taken his hats. The man remembered all of the hats he owned, by colour and shape. Just then, he looked into the tree and saw the monkeys wearing his hats. He felt shocked. But the hats tightened with the heat, and they were painful for the monkeys to wear. So the monkeys threw the hats back at the man, who got very annoyed. The man took his own hat off and performed a magic trick on the monkeys. He threw his hat at the tree......and the hats disappeared from the monkey's heads and returned to the man's bag. The man carried on towards the market with all of his hats safe in his bag, while the shocked monkeys looked on. Post-Reading Questions When did the monkeys steal the man's hats? What happened to the hats in the heat? Re-read. Ask: Why did the monkeys suddenly throw the hats at the man? Re-read. Ask: What did the man do during the magic trick? Re-read. Ask: What did the trick do to the hats? Describe the behaviour of the monkeys.
author: Hello English

title: Sam's Bike
text: Story Description Sam falls off his bike and it breaks. He tries to build a new one, but needs extra help from a friend to finish it and make it work. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Adventure ad-ven-ch-uh Riding the bike in the countryside would be an exciting adventure. Realised re-a-lie-z-d Sam realised that there was someone who could help him. Instructing in-str-uct-ing ﻿She showed him how to fix the bike by instructing him. Mistakes mi-ss-tay-k-s ﻿One only learns to perfect something by making mistakes. Sam and Barbara enjoyed playing games outside. Barbara liked skipping, and Sam liked riding his bike. "See you later!" Sam would say to Barbara as he went on an adventure riding his bike. The bike was special to Sam because his grandfather had made it for him. But, one day when Sam was riding his bike, he fell off. The bike came apart and the wooden frame broke. Sam's bike could not be fixed. The children offered to play games with Sam, but he was not interested. He was too upset to play and he really missed his bike. Then Sam had an idea. He wondered if he could make a new bike all by himself. He needed wood and tools. So Sam collected pieces of wood. He checked to see if they would fit together and make a new frame. It was a difficult job. Sam asked his neighbour to help him build the bike, but his neighbour was too busy. However, he did allow Sam to borrow some tools. Armed with a hammer and nails, Sam started to build his new bike. For several days, Sam worked to put pieces together. His bike was slowly taking shape. He was amazed. Many more hours of work later, and Sam had completed his bike! It took a long time, but he remembered the way his grandfather had made his first bike. Unfortunately, when Sam tried to ride his new bike, it would not move. There was something wrong. "Bye, Sam!" said Barbara, going past on her bike. "Bye, Barbara," said Sam. Then he had an idea. He realised Barbara also had a bike. "Wait, Barbara!" he shouted. Sam asked Barbara to help him with the new bike. She took it apart and corrected Sam's mistakes, instructing Sam how to build a bike properly. Then once Barbara had fixed Sam's bike, Sam tested it. Now it was working! Sam could ride again! "You're the best, Barbara," he said. "Thank you." "You're welcome, Sam," said Barbara. And Sam spent every day riding through the countryside, going up and down hills and back to his village, pleased with his new bike. Post-Reading Questions Why could Sam's bike not be fixed? What did Sam need to make his own new bike? Re-read. Ask: What did Sam's neighbour allow him to do? Re-read. Ask: Why couldn't Sam ride his new bike? Re-read pages 16-17. Ask: What Did Barbara do for Sam? Do you have a hobby that you enjoy? Have you made something before?
author: Hello English

title: Crabby's Shelter
text: Story Description A crab searches the beach for somewhere to shelter from the sun, but he encounters problems when he cannot find anything to use as a shelter. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Squashed sk-wo-sh-d Someone stepped on the banana and squashed it. Split sp-lit After hammering the coconut, it split into two pieces. Snapped sn-a-p-d He pulled the twig apart and it snapped in two. Sulked s-ul-k-d T he crab sulked because it could not find a home. Crabby was searching the beach for food when the sun came out. It was getting hot, so he needed a place to hide and keep cool. Crabby found a lump of rock. "Perhaps I can hide under this!" he said. But the rock was too heavy, and Crabby realised it would squash him. "What about this?" said Crabby. "It's a tight fit." Crabby sat in the lemon slice but it was too small for him. "What about this?" said Crabby. He sat inside the empty eggshell and it split apart. "I need to lose weight," he said. "Maybe I'll fit in this," said Crabby, trying to squeeze into a chocolate bar wrapper. But as he went inside, he tore the wrapper. "This will help," said Crabby, placing a bottle cap over his head. But the cap was too heavy and and Crabby had to keep still. "This is too tricky," he said. "What about this?" said Crabby, clearing out empty peanut shells from a newspaper cone. Crabby fit inside the cone, but it was too hot inside. "Ooh, this looks ideal!" said Crabby, seeing a patterned shell. He grabbed hold of it. Then, Crabby saw it was a snail. "Sorry," he said. "Ooh, a cave!" said Crabby. "Perhaps this is the entrance!" He tickled the wall with his claw and realised it was a human foot. Suddenly the entire foot moved! Crabby quickly crawled away. Crabby had one last plan. He covered his head and body in sand, but the sand was very hot. It was too uncomfortable, and he shook off the sand. "It's worth the risk," said Crabby, looking at a crane's mouth. "I'll fit inside." The crane's mouth quickly snapped open and shut as it swallowed a fly. "Perhaps I'll be eaten," said Crabby. Crabby was exhausted. He had looked for shelter everywhere. He thought he would fry in the sun. He sulked and dreamed of being a crab with a shell. Why couldn't he have his own home? Then suddenly, one of his friends passed by. It was the groovy crab, who had found a colourful shell. "Such a cool design, man," said the groovy crab. Just then, Crabby found a shell of his own. As the sun heated the sand and the sea, Crabby crawled into his new home and slept. After the crabs had rested, Crabby and his friends returned to the sea with their new homes. Post-Reading Questions What does Crabby struggle to do? How does Crabby feel after failing so many times? Re-read. Ask: Why did Crabby want to find shelter? Re-read. Ask: Why did Crabby apologise to the snail? Re-read. Ask: Who came along to help Crabby find a home? Why do you think it is important to shelter from the sun?
author: Hello English

title: Wheely Useful
text: Story Description A tyre called Wheely comes off a truck and crashes. After leaving the truck, Wheely struggles to find a job where he is useful, until a boy comes along. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Whizzing wi-z-ing ﻿ ﻿The car went whizzing by so fast. Attached a-ta-ch-d ﻿The wheel was attached to the frame. Impressed im-pr-e-ss-d ﻿The crowd was impressed at the boy balancing on the beam. Purpose per-pu-ss ﻿ ﻿The wheel felt it need a new purpose in life. There was an old blue car whizzing along a road, coughing out black smoke from its exhaust. The front left tyre felt everything. It was alive, and it's name was Wheely. He had had enough of going so fast for so long! Suddenly the car struck a pothole and a cluster of stones in the road. The car lurched downwards and smashed its front bumper, hurting Wheely very badly. The car then leaped off the ground. It somersaulted and landed, hitting a barrier. Wheely loosened and came off, striking a rock. "Ooh, what happened?" he said, resting against a big stone. "Look! A crash!" said some locals. Wheely panicked when he saw the people and ran away. "I don't want them to take me!" he said as he left the crash site. "Can you give me a ride?" said Wheely as he waited by the roadside. "Sure," said the driver. "Get on the back. We have use for you." So Wheely attached himself to the goods carrier......but he was too small for the truck. Its weight crushed him, and Wheely took all of the weight on his head and caused the truck to topple over onto its side. Sensing a crash, Wheely abandoned the truck when it lurched forwards. "Not again!" Wheely cried out, as he overheated and ran to safety. Meanwhile, the truck steadied and rolled to a stop. "Excuse me," said a passing taxi driver. "We need a replacement wheel for the front. Are you available?" "Oh, wow," said Wheely. "A new job! Sure, I'll do it!" Wheely attached himself to the front of the taxi. But Wheely was too big for the taxi and he tilted it backwards. Also, he could not go fast enough with the number of people crammed inside. He felt dissatisfied. "Get off! Get off!" yelled the driver. Wheely walked everywhere searching for a job. He asked about becoming a replacement bicycle tire, but he was too wide. He asked about being a replacement cart wheel, and replacing a horse to pull a cart, but he was too tiny, and nobody took interest in him. After days of searching, Wheely went to the fields and gave up looking for work. He made friends with a squirrel and a dragonfly, who kept him company while he rested. "I'm just no use to anyone," he said. Just then, a boy waved his hand. "Oh, no, he'll steal me," said Wheely. "I had better get out of here." To his surprise, the boy wanted to build a rope swing for himself and his dog to play on. Wheely was delighted to help out. "This is a different ride," he said. "It feels great, and it's fun too!" The boy and the dog played with Wheely, who didn't have to do anything. The boy used Wheely to balance on and perform in front of an audience. Everyone was impressed with the boy, the dog and Wheely. Best of all, the boy played with Wheely on the road, rolling him faster and faster. "I've never had so much fun before," said Wheely. "I'll never go back to being on cars and trucks! The boy and his dog are making me useful! I can just relax and enjoy!" Wheely realised that even though he did not fit cars, he had a more exciting purpose. Post-Reading Questions Why was Wheely afraid of people? True or false - Wheely didn't feel he was useful anywhere. Re-read. Ask: What new use did the boy and his dog find for Wheely? Re-read. Ask: How did Wheely look in his new work compared to before? Re-read. Ask: What did Wheely realise? Discuss how you make yourself useful. Do you help others?
author: Hello English

title: Happy Birthday
text: Yeah!!! Today is my Birthday!! I will get a lot of gifts.Th boy Quickly dressed up and went to school. The boy was very excited. Hey friend do you know what is today? Yes, today is 18 july.
