title: From Pillars to Palaces
text: Dheera loves to look at structures. Tall pillars. Big towers. Wooden buildings. Clay buildings. New buildings. Old buildings. She wants to see them all. She wants to know what they are made of. So Ma and Baba make her a little aeroplane. All she has to do is think of a structure she wants to see, whisper its name and TWAAAANNGGG! And Dheera’s aeroplane takes her there. First Dheera wants to go to... Iron Pillar in Mehrauli, Delhi Dheera sees an enormous iron pillar. 1,600 years old and almost no rust! There are strange curls and loops on it. She wants to hug this big and strong pillar. Now Dheera wants to go to... Golden Fort in Rajasthan Dheera is in the middle of a vast desert. A yellow sandstone fort stands on top of a hill. There are so many homes inside the fort. She blinks. It glitters like gold. Now Dheera wants to go to... Vittala Temple in Karnataka Dheera runs towards a large hall. It is full of stone pillars. There are 56 big pillars and seven small ones around each of them. She taps the pillars. They sing Sa Re Ga Ma Pa… Now Dheera wants to go to... Padmanabhapuram Palace in Tamil Nadu Dheera is in a wooden palace. Doors, balconies, windows, everything is made of wood. Even the King’s bed is made of 64 pieces of wood. She feels like a queen here. Now Dheera wants to go to... Charminar in Telangana Dheera climbs a long twisting staircase. She reaches the roof of a tall granite building. There are four towers around her. She wants to play in the courtyard below. Now Dheera wants to go to... Bishnupur Temples in West Bengal Dheera is in a temple that looks like a cone. So many shades of brick everywhere. There are terracotta* lotuses on some walls. *baked clay She leans against an arch near the shrine. She is tired. She whispers, “Let’s go home.” ACTIVITY Dheera visits structures made of different kinds of materials. Can you match the material to the structure? Wood Resonant Stone Sandstone Terracotta Iron Granite Iron Pillar in Mehrauli, Delhi Padmanabhapuram Palace, Tamil Nadu Bishnupur Temples, West Bengal Vittala Temple, Karnataka Charminar, Telangana Golden Fort, Rajasthan MATERIAL STRUCTURE
author: Amrita Dasgupta; Vittesh Kalambi

title: The Big, Bad Kurattai
text: Can you say Ku-Zha-Kat-Tai Kuzhakattai means Dumpling Can you say Ku-Rat-Tai Kurattai means Snoring "Move like the wind, Raju. You are invisible! You are a NINJA!" Raju whispered to himself as he dashed to the counter. GADANG! "Raju! Don't touch the kuzhakattais! We're having visitors. Those are for everyone to share!" Hollered Amma from the backyard. MADANG! "Shhh…" Raju told himself. "Silent as a mouse... The challenge of the day is to stuff ALL these sweet, juicy, coconut dumplings into my stupendous mouth! WAHAHAHAHA! OM NOM NOM!" " RAJU! " Amma yelled. " If a single kuzhakattai goes missing... Pinju, go check if he's in the kitchen! " BUUU UURR RRRRP! "Oh oh... Here comes the little tattle tale. " Raju looked around......and spotted something scurrying in the corner. "Heh heh. Raju the mastermind has a plan. Come sit in this bowl, fur ball!" "Anna?" Pinju called. "Raju the ninja was never here." POOF! Raju tumbled away, right into the... OOOFFF! "My belly. Silly fridge... Out of my way!" "HeHeHe! Now just watch the fun!" 1 3 4 2 "Anna? Ohhh... What's that!" Pinju spotted a shiny bowl on the table. "Why was Amma shouting about ku… kurattais? Are the kurattais inside the bowl?" She decided to check. SQUEE SQUEE Huff. "The lid is so tight..." PISK! PISK! AHHH! "AMMA! The kurattai is PISK-ing its tail at me!" "What? Who is snoring like a whale? Is it Thatha?" Asked Amma " Was I dreaming?" Pinju wondered. She decided to take another look, just to be sure. KICHU KICHU "AMMA! The kurattai is KICHU KICHU-ing its nose at me!" "Don’t tickle Thatha’s nose, Pinju. He’ll bounce around the walls sneezing! Help him clean his room, please. Glue and paper everywhere… Is this the age to be sending rockets into Aunty Nimmi’s garden?" Amma lamented. "What is Amma talking about? I'm going to take another peek." Thought Pinju. FLAP FLAP EEEEEeeeeeeee BLINK BLINK "What big ears you have, Mr Kurattai!" "And such long, front teeth…" "Wow, Mr Kurattai, your eyes are the size of marbles!" "Wait a minute..." "You’re just like the…" "AMMA! The big, bad WOLF has come!" " Pinju, Thatha can tell you stories later. Has he brushed his teeth yet? No juice for him otherwise. He may have fooled me yesterday, but not today!" Yelled Amma. "Why is Amma so concerned about Thatha at a time like this?" "I'm going to put the kurattai to test." Pinju pried open the lid and found... AMMA! It’s wiggling its BUM at me! "Get Thatha his walking stick. Just last week he hurt his back after sneaking into Aunty Nimmi’s dancercise class!" Instructed Amma. But Pinju ignored Amma's words. pOkey PoKe The kuzhakattai let out a... AMMMA AAAAA AAAA AAA A A! "What is going on, Pinju? I thought you were in Thatha’s room. Where’s Raju?" "Amma! See this! THE BIG, BAD, KURATTAI IS SQUEAKING AT ME!" tee hEE heee... BWAAA HAHA HAHAHA! "Hey kiddos, I woke up with a brilliant idea! Let's fly this plane at Nimmi's..." sssquEeak Oops. Sigh. "No, Pinju. That’s just an innocent peruchali." " THIS is the big, bad, kurattai! "
author: Abhi Krish

title: What to Draw?
text: "I don't know what to draw," said the boy. "Look at the straight lines that I've drawn," the boy said to his cat. "I still don't know what I should draw," said the boy, whose cat gave him some affection. "I can start by drawing some tomatoes and mini limes," said the boy. "Now I can sketch some cucumbers," said the boy. "Cucumbers, beans and tomatoes," said the boy. "They look great," said the boy. "But something is missing. It's not colour." "What do you think is missing?" the boy said to his cat. "I know what it is!" said the boy. "Look," said the boy to his cat. "I made a picture of you out of fruits and vegetables! You were the missing ingredient!"
author: Hello English

title: Are We Related?
text: Story Description A little house cat finds other cats in the wild, and he tries to find out if they are related to him. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Related re-lay-ted The little cat wondered if he was related to the big cats. Pointed poy-n-ted Cats have pointed ears that move. Proud pr-ow-d Cats admire themselves and are very proud animals. Whiskers w-isk-er-s The cat has long whiskers to feel surfaces. "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," replied the two big cats. "We like to climb trees." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the desert cat. "I like to roll around in the sun." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the lynx. "We have pointed ears, and we can move them." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the big cat. "I like to hunt for fish at night." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the jungle cat. "We like to play with balls of string." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the lion. "I am very proud. I am the greatest of all the cats." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the other cat. "I don't get on with other cats." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the tiger. "I am ferocious and I can wag my tail." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the big cats. "We like to stand in the cold weather and watch for birds." "Are we related?" said the little house cat. "I don't think so," said the two cats. "We get distracted easily. Look, a mouse! Get it!" "Curiosity...a tail...nine lives..." said the tiger. "You are related to us after all!" "You forgot to mention whiskers," said the little house cat. Post-Reading Questions Describe how the little cat and the big cats are related. Which cat called itself the ' greatest of all cats '? Re-read. Ask: What is the big cat doing? Re-read. Ask: Describe the weather in the picture. Re-read. Ask: What were the cats playing with? What is your favourite cat from the story and why?
author: Hello English

title: The Goat King
text: Story Description A nasty goat king runs a farm and treats the animals horribly, and the animals plot their revenge against the king. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Disobeying di-so-bay-ing The king said the animals disobeyed his rules. Sympathy sim-path-ee The king felt no sympathy for the animals. Burden bur-d-un The cat said that being a king would be too difficult for him - a burden. Relieved re-lee-v-d The animals were relieved that the nasty king was gone. There was a farm that was run by animals. They were led by their king - a goat. The animals were unhappy because their king never listened to them. They were forced to work too much. "I'm pulling the cart," said the sheep. "This isn't my job. I should be growing my wool for clothing." "I'm so exhausted," said the pig. "I'm ploughing the field. This isn't my job. I should be planting seeds." "I'm picking vegetables," said the cow. "This isn't my job. I should be ploughing the fields." "You're making us work too much," said the cow, complaining to the king. "And you've put us in the wrong jobs!" "You didn't call me your majesty," said the king, ignoring the cow. "Your majesty, please listen to us." "Leave me alone, I'm busy," said the king. The animals came together to talk about the king. "He doesn't listen to anyone," said the dog. "He only cares about himself." "My back is aching," said the duck. "We have to do something." "Back to work, animals!" shouted the king. "I want to see all of you working until the sun goes down!" The sheep felt lost. He loved the farm, but he missed the old king who was friendly. He felt like running away, but he could not leave his fellow animals behind. The king was furious with the farm animals. They were disobeying him. Instead of working more, they slacked because they were tired. But the king had no sympathy for them. "I'm the king," he said. "I am in control of this farm, and the animals do as I say. Whoever disobeys me will leave this farm forever!" The hen and the duck had had enough of the king's behaviour. Together, they came up with a plan. They spoke about it to the cow. "Everyone must obey me," said the king. "Whenever I walk past you, you must stop what you are doing and get on your knees." "I'm tired of this," said the dog. "We have to do something, right now." The animals agreed. Suddenly, the cow made a move, knocking the crown off the king's head. The cow tied a rope around him and dragging him in circles. "Let's see how you feel, being treated like a slave!" said the cow. The king was terrified by the animals, and he ran far, away, as far as he could. The animals were relieved that he was gone. "What do we do now?" said the animals. "Can we carry on without someone in charge?" said the dog. "What about the cat?" said the sheep. "He has been here the longest. He knows how the work is really done." "I don't want to be the king," said the cat. "It is a burden." "But I could get used to this new position," said the cat, enjoying the attention. "Promise you'll be a fair and good king, and you'll treat us well," said the duck. "I'll treat you no differently," said the cat. "I am one of you." The animals were so pleased to have the cat as their new king. Post-Reading Questions How did the goat king treat the animals? Why were the animals unhappy in their work? Re-read. Ask: What did the sheep miss? Re-read. Ask: Who came up with the plan? Re-read. Ask: Why did the animals choose the cat to be king? Would you be a king?
author: Hello English

title: Inku Chomps, Gobbles and Slurps
text: Inku peeps out of a narrow slit in the tree trunk. She is a Great Hornbill, born just a week ago. SWOOSH! SWOOSH! Pa lands softly on their tree. “Are these for me to play with?” asks Inku. “No, these are figs. Eat them up,” says Pa. GMBH, GMBH. NUM, NUM. “So plump and juicy. With crunchy wasps inside!” says Inku. “Pa has grown a tail on his bill!” says Inku. WHAAAA! “Don’t cry, dear Inku,” says Ma. “It’s just a lizard.” CHOMP, CHOMP. “Oh, it’s scaly!” “My food has wings!” laughs Inku. “Bats are my favourite,” says Ma. GOBBLE, GOBBLE. “So chewy! I love its squishy insides.” “ AAAAA! ” Inku opens her bill wide, seeing a big and furry creature. “Here comes a squirrel,” laughs Pa. SHOOP, SHOOP, the squirrel slides in. “It tickles!” “This looks a little like us,” whispers Inku. “Yes, it’s a small bird – a bulbul,” says Pa. GULP, GULP. “Aaaalll gone!” BURP! “So many hands and legs!” yells Inku. “It’s a scorpion. Beat it against the tree to make it soft,” says Ma. DISH! DASH! BAM! "Wow. Ouch. Still so sharp!” "Are these long lizards?" asks Inku. “No, these are snakes. Slurp them up!” says Ma, grinning. OOOSH, OOOSH, OOOOOOSH, the snakes disappear one by one. “What fun! I think snakes are my favourite.” Inku soon grows big and strong, and leaves the nest. HOP, HOP, HOP, from one branch to the next. She is so excited to explore the forest and catch her own food! Shiny berries. Slippery frogs. Jumping grasshoppers. What will Inku find today? Meet the Great Hornbill The Great Hornbill is India’s largest hornbill. Adult Great Hornbills are 3 to 4 feet tall – almost as tall as you are! Inku’s parents found a large hollow in a big, sturdy tree. Ma entered it and shed some feathers because she would not be leaving the nest for almost three months. Ma and Pa then sealed the entrance, leaving only a small slit open. This is where Inku hatched from an egg. She lived in this nest for 10-12 weeks, until she was old enough to come out. Pa hornbills are very busy during nesting, because Ma hornbills cannot leave the nest. Pa hornbills fly far and wide to bring a variety of tasty and nutritious food for the chick and the mother because they are very hungry all the time.
author: Raji Sunderkrishnan

title: My Mother
text: This is my mother. She takes good care of me. She also plays with me. She loves me a lot. And I love her too. When I cry, my mother is very s cared and asks what happened. I answer a paper cut. Then she says naughty boy. Sometimes when I am wrong my mother scolds me. And I go to say sorry! When she is tired I press her legs and feet. After that I also lie down with her. And we discuss my day at school. After that we do our studies. She also cooks great. For festivals she is always ready. She love dogs.
author: Raghav Sharma
illustrator: Herminder Ohri; Kavitha Mandana; Priya Kuriyan; Shivika Nayyar; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Suvidha Mistry

title: The Fun Bus
text: Papa drove a mini bus. He took people to far off places and brought them back home safely. Once, he drove up to the mountains. He brought bangles for Kajal, a toy top for Karan and a beautiful shawl for Mama. Another time, he went to a beach. He brought lots of big and small sea shells. Kajal painted some of them. She made a necklace for herself and a bracelet for Karan. Often, she wondered what it would be like to go on a trip with Papa. One day, Papa asked, “Would you like to go on a picnic?” The answer was a loud and excited ‘ YES ’. “Okay!” he said. “But, I have two conditions!” "We'll do anything you say!" Kajal and Karan said together. A picnic... Yay!!! “ First condition. We are just four people. You need to gather more to fill all the seats in the bus,” he said. “Why?” asked Kajal. “I don’t want to drive an empty bus all the way up to the national park. If it’s just the four of us, we better get on a local bus. It will save fuel. I think some of our neighbours might be interested.” Are we there yet? This trip is boring! “I’ll ask around,” said Kajal. “You are right, Papa. The more the merrier! ﻿ ” “ Second condition,” Papa continued. “Whoever boards the bus has to help.” “I’ll help clean the bus,” said Karan excitedly. “I’ll make aloo ki sabzi and pooris for everyone,” said Mama. Oh dear!!! I need to cook for a bus full of people. Kajal went around the neighbourhood, checking who would like to go on a picnic. Akki and his father offered to bring board games, a cricket bat, balls, rackets, shuttlecocks, mats and trash bags. Binny and her mom offered to make sweet jalebees for everyone.. Cecil and his family would bring chips, biscuits, water and cool sherbet. Irfan’s and Hiba’s mother offered to cook vegetable biryani and spicy shorba. Amarjeet and his family would bring fruits, plates, bowls, spoons and glasses. Ira’s father was a professional photographer. He offered to create a nice photo album. Kajal was thrilled. All her friends were going to be there. Suddenly, it felt like she was part of a big family. She went to the last house on the street. An old woman lived there alone. People called her Mausi. Kajal told Mausi about the picnic. “I want to come. But, how can an old woman like me help?” she asked sadly, and sent her away. May be next time! Kajal rushed back home. She had to tell Papa who would be coming and how they would be helping. She also had to help Mama make aloo ki sabzi and pooris. Akki bat, Binny jalebee, Cecil water... On Sunday morning, the entire neighbourhood was noisy and busy. Grownups were bringing what they had promised. Kids were helping load the bus. Papa was counting heads. When everyone had gathered, he gave common instructions for the trip. The kids listened to him attentively and the adults agreed with him. Finally, Mausi was invited to board the bus first. Kajal was confused. “ Mausi will keep us entertained with her funny stories and pleasant songs. The trip to the park is long. We all could use some songs and stories!” said Papa. Everyone cheered and boarded the fun bus.
author: Harpreet Kaur
illustrator: 211 Studio; Ajanta Guhathakurta; Angie & Upesh; Avishek Sen; Kabini  Amin; Kavya Singh; Nina Sabnani; Ruchi Shah; Sonali Zohra; Soumya Menon; Students of  Himalayan Public School; Sunaina  Coelho; Taposhi Ghoshal

title: Catch a Ride on Raindrops
text: Splash in the puddles, Jump in the rain, Catch a ride on raindrops, Falling from the sky. Rain hits the ground, And seeps far below, Down where the worms live, Past where the termites dig, Snakes slide and ants creep, Down the rain seeps. Trickle between rocks, Squeeze into cracks, Moisture moves, out of sight, Deep underground. Spring from the earth, Rush with the streams, Race with the fishes, Far across the land. Warmed by the sun, Up the water floats, Into skies, far above, Vapour turns to cloud. Thundering in the sky, They bulge and rumble and grow, Till water bursts, in pouring rain, Down to the earth again. How to Ride the Water Cycle Water travels far and takes many forms over the course of the water cycle. It comes to the earth as rain from the sky. It fills rivers and soaks into the ground to join the water table. The water table, like a river underground, emerges into open air in the form of springs and lakes. Water travels up into the sky as vapour when it's warmed by the sun, and comes together as wispy clouds. When clouds grow dark and heavy with water, they open with pouring rain, bringing water back to earth once more.
author: Anjali Vaidya

title: Bubble's Adventure
text: In a vast beautiful green jungle there was an animal kingdom that lived in peace. The king of the jungle the mighty lion named Solomon ruled the jungle. He had his loyal assistants the cheeky monkey Rusty and the funny hyena Poppy. Both Rusty and Poppy usually summoned the rest of the animals for important jungle gatherings. The jungle was a very beautiful place full of tall green trees, colorful flowers and chirping birds. All the animals lived in peace and respected the king. There was one very unhappy animal that kept to oneself and never really felt part of the kingdom. He was always teased by Rusty and Poppy. The animal became the joke of the kingdom. The animal was none other than a humble donkey named Bubble. Everyone teased him about his name and of course his intelligence. One day Bubble had enough and asked the king if he could venture out of the kingdom to find himself. Solomon thought for a while and had hearty laugh. He said you are surely going to lose the way on your own, at least take Rusty with you to guide you. Bubble was sure this trip would do him good. Solomon told Bubble that every animal of this kingdom has always had the freedom to do their own thing and be themselves. Hearing the positive news from Solomon, Bubble never seemed happier. Bubble couldn’t wait to get out of the kingdom where he was ridiculed and find peace somewhere else. The next morning Bubble wished everyone goodbye and went on his little adventure. Bubble did lose his way but managed to make it to a small village close to the jungle. The new place was both fascinating and scary for Bubble. But Bubble took that step and went into the village. Bubble was now tired and thirsty from the trip. He saw some water in a bowl in front of a house in the village and drank some from it. A little while later a man came out from the house and was surprised to see a donkey in the village. The man named Shyam was very fond of animals and birds; he was already having a cow, a chicken and a goat in his house. He saw Bubble and liked him instantly. Shyam fed Bubble some food and water. He made space for Bubble to rest with the other animals. That night when trying to sleep the cow spoke to Bubble and asked where he came from. Bubble told Maalu the cow that he had come from the jungle because the other animals would tease and make fun of him a lot. Maalu said that she understood what he was talking about; we are low on intelligence but are most helpful to mankind. She mentioned how Shyam took good care of them and made them feel like part of his family. She told him that he had come to a great place. Bubble was still scared but Maalu’s words made him feel happy. All the animals decided it was time to take their beauty sleep to feel all refreshed in the morning. The next morning Shyam woke up early and wished all the animals a good morning. He kissed Maalu on the forehead and asked if she was ready to be milked. Maalu nodded her head and Shyam got the sign. After milking Maalu, it was time to milk the goat Shaalu. The goat too seemed happy to oblige. Just after milking the cow and the goat, Shyam treated them with delicious food and drinks. Shyam soon came close to Bubble and fed him with treats like carrots and radishes. Bubble loved the taste of such fresh produce and was more than happy to be part of Shyam’s family. Shyam was treating Bubble like one of his children just like the rest of them. He decided to name the donkey Buddhi. Bubble was curious to know what the name meant and asked Maalu. She told him that the name meant intelligence. Bubble just burst into tears and loved that Shyam didn’t belittle his intelligence but named him intelligence. Shyam was over the moon to add a new member to his loving family. Buddhi was so happy that he soon forgot the kingdom and his tormentors. One day he had a surprise visitor in Rusty-the cheeky monkey who kept asking when he was coming back to the kingdom. Buddhi replied that he had finally found his real family. He asked Rusty to call him Buddhi and not Bubble anymore. Rusty still couldn’t hold back his laughter but now nothing bothered Buddhi anymore, he had found a place where someone loved him for who he was and just let him be himself. Rusty informed Buddhi that he was never welcomed back in the kingdom as per Solomon’s orders and hoped he had the best life in the village. No matter how irritating your family can be, at the end of the day family is the closest you got to anyone who accepts you as you are, whether you are born into the family or adopted. Being a family is the real adventure that just gets interesting every single day of life.
author: Ruby  Thomas
illustrator: Amy  Slatem; Athumani  Saidi; Emily  Berg; Herminder Ohri; Jean  Fullalove; Jess  Jardim-Wedepohl; Karen Lilje Lilje; Shabani  Hamidu

title: The Sunshine Farm
text: Story Description Children and animals stay at the Sunshine farm, where they grow vegetables and play all day. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Riding ry-d-ing The children had fun riding on the donkeys. Friendly fr-end-l-ee The farmyard cat was very affectionate and friendly. Scraps s-cr-a-p-s The birds hunted for scraps of food to bring home. Practice pr-ac-t-i-ss Everyone wanted to practice their dancing skills. The Sunshine Farm is a place where children come together and play, holding hands and dancing in circles. Every day is an eventful day! They pick the vegetables and take them to the house for dinner. They smell the fragrances of the fresh flowers. They practice riding the baby elephants and horses. They play football and play hide and seek in the long grass. They dig the fields and pick vegetables. The friendly crocodiles lay their eggs by the shore and watch over them. The ants collect scraps of food and return to their hills. The lizards wander through the fields, watched by their mother. The scarecrow stands alone in the field and warns off the birds. The birds build their nests in the house and return with food......and when the day is over, the sun says goodbye and the rooster crows! Post-Reading Questions What activities do the children do at the Sunshine farm? What kind of animals and insects are found at the farm? Re-read. Ask: What do the children enjoy practicing? Re-read. Ask: What animal lives by the water shore? Re-read. Ask: What is the job of a scarecrow? If you had a farm, what things would be there?
author: Hello English

title: Grandpa in the Tree
text: Story Description Grandpa climbs into the tree and gets stuck, causing a funny situation between himself and two policemen. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Parade per-ay-d It was the day of the annual town parade. Awkward or-k-w-ur-d﻿ ﻿ ﻿The police said grandpa was being ﻿awkward ﻿by refusing to climb out of the tree. Careful c-air-f-ul The man had to be careful when climbing down the tree. Sprained sp-ray-n-d He fell over and sprained his ankle. The doctor said he would be all right. It was the day of the annual parade and grandpa got up early. He had a plan to get a great view of the parade. He climbed the tree outside and hunched himself against a heavy trunk. The view was great up there. After a while, grandpa realised he was too frail to get down. His legs and arms were tired. He had been sitting for a long time. Grandpa's grandson and the dog saw him sitting in the tree talking to his friends, who encouraged him to get down. But grandpa was too high up. The police came to investigate what was happening. "You must get down," they said. "It is illegal to sit in someone else's tree." "But this tree belongs to me!" said grandpa. "And I can't get down! I'm too old!" "You weren't too old to get up there!" the policeman said. "For your own safety you should get down," said the police officers. "You're just being old and awkward." "Get my friends over here," said grandpa to his grandson. "They can back me up." "They've gone, grandpa," said the grandson. "You'll have to come down, but take it easy." "I can't get down!" said grandpa. "If you come down we'll leave you alone," said the police officer. Everyone heard the parade coming. At the same time, the police officers tried to climb the tree to get grandpa down. The grandson and the dog watched the people go by, as did grandpa in the tree. The police found a ladder and placed it against the tree. Very slowly, grandpa started to climb down the steps. "Be careful!" said the grandson. "Don't worry, I'm fine!" said grandpa. But grandpa slipped, sending the ladder and himself on top of the police officer. "I'm so sorry," said grandpa, getting up. "I'll arrest you for this!" said the policeman, who had sprained his ankle. When the policeman tried to arrest grandpa, the dog growled. "I'll arrest you too!" complained the policeman, as the dog licked his face. Grandpa, his grandson and the dog enjoyed the parade as the two policeman moved on, with one covered in dog licks. "Next time you'll be in big trouble," said the policeman, as grandpa laughed. Post-Reading Questions Why did grandpa climb the tree? Why couldn't grandpa get down? Re-read. Ask: Why did grandpa ask his grandson to get his friends? Re-read. Ask: What did the police say to grandpa? Re-read. Ask: When grandpa slipped, who did he land on? Do you think it was too dangerous to climb the tree?
author: Hello English

title: Flying is the Best
text: Story Description A boy tells a story of how, no matter what he is doing, he wishes he could fly. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Paddle ﻿pa-d-ul ﻿The dog can paddle across the water. ﻿Glider ﻿g-lie-d-ur ﻿The plane turns and dives like a glider. Flapping ﻿fl-a-p-ing ﻿The bird flies by flapping its wings. Soar ﻿ss-or ﻿ ﻿I want to soar fast across the sky. ﻿ ﻿ I look up at the night sky And seeing the moon and the stars up high I wish I could bounce my legs off the ground and fly I could be a snake and slither like a pest Or be a little caterpillar and sneak into a bird's nest But flying really is the best I could sprint fast through the jungle with ease But with flying I could feel the cool breeze I could grow ears and hop like a bunny Or diddle-bounce-bump like a deer with horns and look funny Or crawl and scarper like a gecko up a hill And pull a wheelie with my legs like a cow and stand still I could swim like a duck and paddle to my mum who sings I could swim like a frog underwater and find new things But I'd rather be able to grow a pair of wings I could build a web like a spider Propel myself with my web to get higher But I would rather move around like a glider To flap my arms and take off Keep flapping and flapping and make off Until my wings help me glide away Makes flying the best, I have to say My grandad gets shampoo in my eyes and I'm crying My father gives me a dosa that he's been frying My mother sings me to sleep and I'm sighing But all of the time I have been dreaming of flying And all the while I am trying Eek ook ahh eeh fly Ooh oh aah ah fly Oof uff I've had enough Mum gives me a piggy back All the while we're smiling walking the track Watching the day turn into the night sky It feels a little bit like I want to fly So when I sleep at night and the stars are up there Without a thought and without a care I'll take off and soar like a rocket on a test Because flying is the best Post-Reading Questions What does the boy wish he could do? Complete the sentence: flying is the b _ _ _. Re-read. Ask: What would the boy rather move around like? Re-read. Ask: What could the boy swim underwater as? Re-read. Ask: When the boy is asleep, how can he fly? If you could have any power, then what would it be? Would you fly?
author: Hello English

title: Moti Uncle
text: Gungun and her mom are best friends. They share stories, play, talk and even study together. Like all subjects, they started doing maths together too. Harshita was losing her interest in maths, so they decided to find someone to help her. Gungun thought it was a good idea if her neighbourhood uncle, Moti can help her study maths. Moti Uncle was happy to teach her maths and they had a great time too. Her mother continued spending time with her without worrying about maths.
author: Nikita B
illustrator: Aman Randhawa; Jesse Pietersen; Meghna Pant; Nivong  Sengsakoun; ROSH; Tanvi Bhat; Tawfiq Ahmed  Anwar

title: Paul the Puffer Fish
text: Paul is a puffer fish. When he gets nervous, he puffs up in size! This is to warn off predators! Story Description Paul the puffer fish worries that water is running out, when the tide goes low. Suddenly, the tide comes back in. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Tide ty-d-e The tide goes in and out constantly. Deep d-ee-p When the tide comes in, the water at the shore is deep. Shallow sh-a-low When the tide goes out, the water at the shore is shallow. Gravity gr-a-vi-t-ee The sun and moon's gravity controls the tide. Paul doesn't understand about tides. When the tide comes in, the water at the shore is deeper. When the tide goes out, the water at the shore is shallower. "Something feels strange," said Paul. "I can feel the water's depth going down. I think we are running out of water!" Sensing danger, Paul puffed up to a huge size, then went back to normal again. This pushed out a lot of the water from the pool he was swimming in. He was alone, and the water was barely swimmable. Paul became nervous and puffed up again! He was huge! He floated to the surface and jumped as hard as he could, trying to escape from the little pool. He landed in a smaller pool with a crab and a starfish. Paul felt embarrassed. "Don't worry," said the star fish. "The tide goes out and then comes back in! Later the water will be deeper again, you'll see!" "The moon and the sun's gravity controls the tide," said the crab. "You just have to wait!" "I worry about Paul," said the starfish. "He doesn't get how it works." "He will," said the crab. "What goes out comes in, and what comes in goes out. Hey, these stones are difficult to pick up." Sensing something coming, Paul sank under the surface. A huge level of water rose and crashed against the rocks. "Here comes the tide!" said the starfish. "Let's ride it, Paul!" said the crab. "Tide incoming!" shouted the octopus. "Everyone, hold on!" Wham! A huge wall of water hit the rocks and everyone held on. Paul no longer felt scared. He flew as high as he could, spreading his fins. At low tide, the waters at the shore are shallower. At high tide, the waters at the shore get deeper. Post-Reading Questions What happens to Paul when he gets scared? What did Paul do when the tide came back in? Re-read. Ask: What happened when Paul puffed up in size? Re-read. Ask: What makes the tide come in and go out? Re-read. Ask: What did everyone do when the tide suddenly came in? How do you know when the tide is in or out?
author: Hello English

title: Mark and Shelley
text: Story Description Mark and Shelley help their Grandma collect eggs for the family business. Learn about how the farm works and how the children help with the organisation. ﻿ Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Business ﻿biz-ni-ss ﻿The children knew how to help with the business. Rival ﻿ry-v-al ﻿The rival farm next door wanted to compete. Carefully ﻿c-air-ful-ee ﻿ ﻿The children carefully selected the eggs. Easier ﻿ee-zee-ur ﻿Having the children to help made things easier for grandma. Mark and Shelley collected eggs to help their Grandma with their family business. It wasn't easy for Mark and Shelley. Sometimes the dog would steal eggs or run away with Mark's shoes, and the hens would not move for Shelley to collect the eggs. And the rival neighbour business always sent their son, David, to check on how Mark and Shelley's hens were doing. He would report back to his family. Mark carefully laid the egg baskets in groups so they could count how many eggs came from each pen. And Shelley did the maths, seeing how many eggs they had collected in total. Mark and Shelley counted the money made from the sales, and told their Grandma how much profit they had made. Grandma was very happy with Mark and Shelley. They always calculated correctly and separated the eggs into different groups, making the work easier. Grandma was too weak to do everything by herself. With Mark and Shelley's help, she did not need to walk around finding the eggs. Grandma always left some eggs for Mark and Shelley's breakfast, to say thank you. "One day, when I am too old to work, you and Shelley can take over the business," said Grandma. "I know you will look after the place." Mark and Shelley were so happy with their Grandma's offer. Post-Reading Questions Why was it difficult for Mark and Shelley to collect the eggs? Why did the neighbours send their son David to the farm? Re-read pages 7-9. Ask: What did Mark and Shelley do together? Re-read. Ask: What did Grandma not have to do? Re-read. Ask: What did Grandma say to Mark and Shelley? Do you help others? What things would you help with?
author: Hello English

title: Run, Bablu, Run!
text: Rohan does not understand why the elders are not allowing Bablu to take part in the orange race today. The race is organized by the local sports club. Seema, Harish, Ahana, Savan – all are taking part in the race. Rohan wants to take part as well! Without Bablu, Rohan will have to run alone in the race. But, Rohan never does anything without Bablu. So, he goes home and asks his mother, “Ma, Why are the Uncles not allowing Bablu to take part in the race?” Rohan’s mother pats his head and says, “Rohan, didn’t I tell you before that Bablu is not like the other children? He is not even like you!” Rohan feels annoyed because Ma is going to bring up Bablu’s disease again. Ma has told him before that Bablu is suffering from a rare disease, called Down syndrome. Rohan even searched about it on Youtube from Daddy’s mobile phone. Because of his disease, Bablu cannot speak properly like the other children. When Bablu walks, other children at the park laugh. When Bablu walks, he flails his hands and legs. It looks like he is trying to swim. But, Bablu has the sweetest smile. He is also really smart because he knows exactly when Tuni is hungry. Tuni is the street dog they both love very much. Bablu does not deserve to be left out of the orange race. Rohan says to his mother, “Ma, just because Bablu has a disease does not mean he can’t run! I will make sure he runs.” Next day, all the children gather at the park for the race. Rohan finds Bablu under the big Banyan tree. Rohan knows at once that he is sad. Otherwise, he would smile at him. Bablu asks in his lispy voice, “Why are you here? You’re not running?” Rohan sits down beside Bablu and says, “How can I run without you, Bablu? I never do anything without you.” Bablu now smiles. Then Rohan says, “But I have a plan! While the other children are having their own orange race, we can have our own race here.” He takes out two oranges from his pocket. Bablu’s smile gets so big that you could see two of his big front teeth! Rohan and Bablu take one orange each and place it on the ground. They keep the oranges a little far away from one another. Then, Rohan and Bablu hold each other's hand and start to walk away from the oranges. Rohan says, “There is no one to keep the oranges for us at the finishing line. So, we have to walk a little away and then we can race from there.” “And we will run up to here to get our oranges!”, replies Bablu. Rohan always understands what Bablu says. Bablu does not understand why other children mock him when he speaks. They reach near the Mango tree which is about two hundred meters away from the big Bunyan tree. Their oranges are kept under the Banyan tree. They stand side by side. Bablu shouts, “One! Two! Three!” And they start running to get their oranges!
author: Sushrita Acharjee

title: MY HOME
text: This is my family. the biggest family ever that I have. I have a dog too! he is boy. the great dog ever. And also I have 3 girls and 1 boy. that makes total 4. I have my big brother too! and a small sister. my mom and me are exactly the same. she loves me and love her too! this is the holy day at my home. we play with our house too! every body loves to play holy. this is the way to my home. when I reach back home I feel that my house is welcoming me back. there is a party at my home. every one is visiting my house. this is the day of Diwali at home. this is the day when we fly kite
