illustrator: Brian Wambi; Priya Kuriyan; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Sharanya Singh

title: The Unlikely Friend
text: Story Description Marigold is a bird who has recently given birth to chicks. She protects them until they hatch. Very soon, a dog called Shep takes interest in them, causing Marigold to worry. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Sniffing ﻿sn-if-f-ing ﻿The dog was sniffing at the eggs to see what they were. Pecking ﻿p-ek-ing ﻿The bird felt pecking from inside the eggs. Hatched ﻿ha-ch-d ﻿The chicks hatched from the eggs. Harmless ﻿h-ar-mm-l-uss ﻿ ﻿The dog did not want to hurt others. He was harmless. Marigold was a pretty bird with white and grey wings. She guarded her eggs from predators, and waited for them to hatch. Marigold walked by her tree to make sure her eggs were safe. One day, unknown to Marigold, a dog called Shep saw the eggs and took interest. He wondered what they were. One morning Marigold was flying when she saw Shep sniffing at her eggs. Marigold swooped down to scare off Shep, who jumped away and ran. Luckily her eggs were fine. When Marigold was warming her eggs, she felt some pecking from inside the eggs. Very soon, the eggs hatched! One by one, chicks appeared! When Marigold went to hunt for food, Shep saw that the eggs had hatched! He was shocked, and the chicks wondered what he was. All of the chicks ran after Shep, chasing and following him as he played. They even hid underneath him to shelter. Shep took good care of the chicks. But Marigold didn't trust Shep. What if he was waiting for them to get bigger, so he could eat them? Marigold warned her chicks away from Shep, because he could be dangerous. Shep did as he was told by Marigold, and he ignored the chicks. But the chicks kept following him. "I have to stay away," Shep explained to the chicks. "Your mother doesn't trust me around you. We can't play together." But very soon, Marigold saw that Shep was just a lazy, funny dog who loved to lie down in the sun. She watched him guarding another bird's eggs, dribbling as he slept. She felt differently about Shep. Seeing that he was harmless, eventually Marigold let Shep play with her chicks, and she joined in. She learned to trust Shep, who became an unlikely friend. Post-Reading Questions How did Marigold know that her chicks were hatching? Why did Marigold stop her chicks from playing with Shep? Re-read. Ask: What was Marigold doing when she saw Shep? Re-read. Ask: Why did the chicks sit underneath Shep? Re-read. Ask: Why did Marigold trust Shep in the end? Name something precious that you protect.
author: Hello English

title: Dadu and Indu go to Cubbon Park
text: Saturday morning Amma rides i n a ruk-tuk-bruk-pruk auto With her dog Dadu and her daughter Indu, Brwm-bruwm-zwee-weee to the green green Cubbon park, Where their ears feel cooler and the temperature is lower. Chitter chatter laugh squirrels playing among crows. Whoosh-swoosh! t hey go chasing, sliding along bark roads. Oh wait! they stop mid-jump to ask, Are those magicians in the park? Caw...caw... complain the crows, There are no magicians in this park! Those are joggers, you pottering pups! Dadu finds the pigeons first. G utur, cutur, gutur, cutur Munching on their breakfast. Gutur...cutur...flap...flap The pigeons fly up above them. Gutur...flap...cutur...flap Land back right beside them. Gutur, cutur, gutur, cutur. "Dadu, Indu, illi banro!", shouts Amma from the bandstand. Gutur, flap, cutur, flap the pigeons go up in grey Pooping in fright on their grainy breakfast tray! Gi-aga-ga-gi-aga sings a woman, in a voice like magic Ga-gi-ga-gi-ga-gi-aga t he chorus beside her, the crowd around her Ga-aga-ga-gi-aga Indu, Dadu, squirrels and crows Ga-gi-ga-gi-ga-gi-aga s ing along loudly striking a lively pose. Under the trumpet tree o n a rug of pink, purple and yellow flowers Amma feeds chow chow bones to bow bow dogs. Indu dreams of bubblegum icecream Dadu eats idlis dipped in chutney, a minty green. Heading back, they can't believe their eyes Floating above ground are ladies, gentlemen and flies Walking over thin, elastic rope w ith flailing hands and legs of hope. "Impossible!", Dadu barks, "a fterall, there are magicians in the park!"
author: Anjana Balakrishnan
illustrator: Ajanta Guhathakurta; Jayesh Sivan; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Rajiv Eipe; Reshu Singh; Sanjay Sarkar; Shamim Ahmed; Tanaya Vyas

title: Ajja and Avanti's pizza adventure!
text: Amma was going out to do some chores and Avanti stayed with her ajja till lunchtime. Avanti loved spending time with ajja. He never scolded her and always helped her in her 'adventures'. Avanti was hungry. She went into the kitchen and found pizza dough on the kitchen counter. Amma had promised to make pizza for lunch. Avanti suddenly had an idea! "Ajja, I am sooo hungry! Let's make pizza and surprise amma!", she said. Ajja was worried. He had never made pizza before. "Wh...Why pizza? I'll make yummy uthapams...they are just like pizzas" "Noooooo...Uthapam is boring! We eat it every week! I want to eat pizza today!" protested Avanti. "But how do we make pizza? I have never done it before", said ajja. "I have seen amma make it before. I can help. Pleeeeeeassssse ajja" said Avanti. Ajja gave in. They first rolled out the pizza dough. "Now we add pizza sauce" said Avanti. "What is that?" asked ajja. "It is like tomato sauce ajja, only different! It has garlic in it" said Avanti. Ajja suddenly had an idea. "Why not use amma's leftover tomato garlic chutney? The one we ate for breakfast with dosa?" "That can work!" said Avanti with a twinkle in her eye. Avanti and ajja assembled the pizza. They added chhese and veggies. Ajja put the pizza into the preheated oven. All they had to do was wait. Avanti grew impatient. The clock was ticking verrrry slowly. Suddenly, she was worried. What if the cheese won't melt? What if the pizza burns? Will amma get angry? Avanti and ajja heard a knock on the door. Amma was back! "Hmm...what's that smell?" asked amma. "Is that pizza?". Avanti smiled nervously. They took the pizza out of the oven and amma sliced it. "Yummy! This pizza is so good!" exclaimed amma. Ajja and Avanti beamed at each other. "We make a great team!" they said as they hugged each other.
author: Deepa Rao
illustrator: Alankrita Amaya; Henu; Jemma Jose; Jesse  Breytenbach; Nikhila Anil; Nirja Desai; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Soumya Menon; Vusi  Malindi; Wiehan de Jager

title: One Positive Idea
text: There was a small girl, her name was Pearl. She was different from others. From all her sisters and brothers. She loved to dream, both big and small. She was very brave, always looking for someone to save. One cold day, when she was at home, she saw a homeless dog hiding under a broken log. The dog was old, his hair was like gold. "Woof, Woof" he cried, "Hold on, I will help you!" she replied. She took her blanket, and was outside in a dash. He was stuck! His foot was trapped under a pile of plastic trash. She helped the dog out from the pile of plastic, and had an AMAZING idea! "My Mission is to Heal the World!" she sang while she twirled. She ran inside and started collecting plastic. From plastic bottles to plastic bags, she got everything her little hands could grab. She ran to her Dad and asked for his help. He said "Of course darling" while he itched his scalp. "I need to build a house for the dog outside, I need to make it with plastic, so people do not throw trash outside." "There isn't enough plastic to build"she said. "How about we ask help from the neighbors instead?". One by one, a lot of plastic she collected, to build a house so the dog was protected. Together they gathered all the tools and started to build. The bottles became walls, straws became windowsills. She thanked her Dad, she thanked the neighbors. Brought the stray dog in and showed off her labor. "How many people are in the world dad?" confused she asked "7.6 billion people darling, why might you ask?" She thought about that number, the focus was real. "Why do people throw plastic in the road, why can't they just build!" The dad was happy to see his brave little girl, trying to help both the animal and the world. "From now on we will build baby girl" he promised. "So, dad, there will be no more homeless dogs or trash on the street?" "Yes baby girl, slowly we will get them all off the street!" With that she smiled, and slowly went to sleep. "Dream sweet dreams my child, tomorrow you will have even bigger dreams!" MORAL: Help the World and Everyone in it too One by one we can make a difference too!
author: Asmita Bharati
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Fahad Faizal; Jesse  Breytenbach; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Kruttika Susarla; Lý Minh  Phúc; Mary Anne Hampton; Nicci  Nathanson; Rohit Karandadi; Sandhya Prabhat; Shambhavi Singh; Shamim Ahmed; Shreya  Sen; Suvidha Mistry; Vivekananda Roy Ghatak

title: Liam and the Rainbow
text: Story Description Liam fishes at the shore when he sees a dog that needs help. Suddenly, something magical comes along. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿ ﻿ Desperate ﻿de-ss-pur-ut ﻿The dog was desperate for the boy's help. Umbrella ﻿um-br-el-a ﻿The boy put his umbrella on the water and it floated. Vanished ﻿va-ni-sh-d ﻿The rainbow that had appeared had suddenly vanished. Delicious ﻿de-li-sh-uss ﻿ ﻿The freshly caught fish tasted delicious. There was a thunder storm with strong winds. The river became violent and the flow was unpredictable. Liam was fishing at the shore with his pet cat Loopy, when he heard barking coming from the water. They looked to see a dog crying out with a howl. It was desperate. "Quick, grab the umbrella!" said Loopy, and Liam leaped up, got the umbrella, placed it in the river and jumped inside it. He kicked his feet and paddled for the dog, who was struggling to stay above the water. "Don't worry, I'm almost there!" called Liam, getting closer. Liam pulled the dog into the umbrella. The storm calmed and they both floated for a while. "Thank you so much," said the dog. "You saved my life." Before they could go back to the shore, Liam and the dog noticed something underneath the surface. It was a swarm of fish! "Wow, look at that!" said Liam. "It's amazing!" A gigantic rainbow coursed from the sky to the umbrella, and suddenly all of the fish swarmed and moved in a beautiful, neat formation, following the rainbow. The umbrella followed it towards the shore. Loopy saw the whole thing. The rainbow flew from the sky and gathered the fish into a neat pile. Then the fish turned and dived straight into Liam's basket. As quickly as it had come, the rainbow vanished, leaving nothing but light rain. The river flow slowed and became calm. Liam carried the dog, as Loopy followed them with a delicious fish in his mouth. Liam carried the entire basket of fish and the umbrella on his head, balancing them as they walked home. Liam adopted the dog, whom he named Snowy, and Snowy and Loopy learned to share the fish between them. Post-Reading Questions Describe how the dog felt in the river. How did Liam catch all of the fish? Re-read. Ask: What did the dog say to Liam? Re-read. Ask: What happened to the river after the rainbow disappeared? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Liam do with the dog and what did he name it? ﻿Do you know all the colours of the rainbow?
author: Hello English

title: Foxy and Armadillo
text: Foxy and Armadillo met one day in the fields. They spoke about what they enjoy planting and growing. "My carrots are the best in the region," said Foxy. "They are the tastiest and you cannot compare them to any other carrot!" "My potatoes come out well. They're delicious and big and ripe. They make great mash and chips. You have to taste them!" Story Description Foxy claims he can beat Armadillo at growing good vegetables. Foxy and Armadillo have a vegetable growing competition, and the winner gets a month's wages. ﻿ ﻿Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics "I'll bet you a month's wages that I can grow a better vegetables than you," said Foxy. "You're on," said Armadillo, and with a lot of pride, the two shook hands. Foxy and Armadillo planted their crops and returned to their daily tasks. They didn't speak to each other, and every day they tended to their carrots and the potatoes, hoping they would grow well. "I don't know much about growing potatoes," said Armadillo. "So I'll do the best I can. I understand the ground and the weather, so perhaps this will help me win. Let's see what happens!" "Oh, boy!" said Foxy. "I'm so confident that I'm going to win, I can just feel it! I can't wait to dig up my carrots. Then we'll see who's better! I bet that silly Armadillo can't make a single potato!" The day finally came when Armadillo and Foxy had to reveal what they had. They dug up everything. Armadillo had acquired a big stash of potatoes! He had grown them so well, they had a delicious looking skin, and they were of different shapes and sizes! It was all thanks to his careful planning, humbleness, knowledge of the ground and the weather that Armadillo did great. He walked away with the winnings. But Foxy was unfortunate! His impatience, arrogance and lack of knowledge caused no carrots to grow. He was left with a bunch of roots and weeds! He blamed it on the weather and bad luck, but Foxy's disaster was his own creation. He was overconfident. Post-Reading Questions Why did Armadillo win and why did Foxy lose? Describe Foxy's personality. Re-read. Ask: Why does Armadillo have a good attitude? Re-read. Ask: Why does Foxy have a bad attitude? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Foxy accidentally grow instead? ﻿How do you prepare for a test?
author: Hello English

title: The Little Bear Gets Lost
text: Blizzards of snow blew through the icy north. Story Description A little bear wanders off and gets lost, losing his group of bears. He searches for the bears and looks for a way back home. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Icy ﻿eye-see ﻿The air was icy in the cold weather. Snapped ﻿s-na-p-d ﻿The tree trunk snapped in half. Distance ﻿di-ss-tan-ss ﻿It was a long distance back home. Investigate ﻿in-ve-ste-g-ate ﻿ ﻿The bears went to investigate what caused the noise. The full moon appeared behind the cloud. One of the only animals around saw it. It was a little bear, wandering on its own, having lost its tribe and wondering where they were. Everything looked strange. The little bear jumped from rock to rock, finding small pools with fish coming to the surface. The little bear moved through some fields and found a cluster of trees. As the day went on, he began to worry. There was no sign of the other bears. Soon he felt very hungry and thirsty. But there was no water or food anywhere. There were only plants with no leaves. The little bear was sure he was close to home, and he decided to climb a tree to see where home was. The little bear was heavy, and the tree trunk snapped in two. He fell and fell... Meanwhile the bear tribe, who had been searching for the little bear, heard cries in the distance. One of the bears went to investigate. He found the little bear wailing on the ground after falling out of the tree. He examined the little bear. He had cut his chest, and he was weak. The bears treated the little bear's wound, and very soon he was reunited with his mother. She was relieved to see him. The little bear learned to stay close to his group and not wander away. Post-Reading Questions How did the little bear get lost? How did the tribe know the little bear was injured? Re-read. Ask: Why did the little bear climb the tree? Re-read. Ask: Why did the tree trunk snap? Re-read. Ask: Who comforted the little bear? Why is it important to stay in your group?
author: Hello English

title: The Kids from the Suburbs
text: Story Description A group of kids living outside the city discover a woman who is ill. They help her to get better, and she helps them to read, understand and enjoy books. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Properly pr-o-per-lee The woman helped the children pronounce words properly. Strength s-tr-eng-th The woman needed strength to get out of bed. Improved im-p-roo-v-d The children's reading improved over time. Create cr-ee-ate Very soon, the children could create their own stories. The kids from the suburbs lived in the hills next to a city. They had no house to live in, so they made the hillside their home. Each day, they did the washing, cleaning, dusting and moving things about. They hung clothes to dry in the sun. They worked hard and well. They found scraps of food to eat and valuable items in the trash. They had to walk very far each day. When they made it to the city, which was a very, very long walk from their home, the kids were tired and frustrated. One of the girls wrote about it in her diary. One of their favourite activities was reading picture books. They enjoyed the stories, but they could not read the words properly. There was a woman who was sick. She heard the kids outside but she could barely get up to talk to them. Her pink shawl flew out of the window. The kids caught the pink shawl and returned it to the woman. Fascinated, the woman asked the kids who they were. They told her where they lived. The woman felt a lot of sympathy for them. She gathered strength and helped the kids with their chores so that they could finally get some rest. She taught the kids how to read the words, and day by day, their reading improved. They could now understand the stories much better. Very soon, after the woman read to the kids, the kids themselves began to enjoy the books more, and create with their own stories. With more visits, the woman brought more books for the kids, and they took it in turns to read their adventures. Helping the kids helped the woman to get better from her illness. And when the woman was almost well again, the kids visited her to cheer her up. The woman was very happy to have the children come and visit her, because they enjoyed each other's company so much. Post-Reading Questions What chores did the children perform every day? How did the children find out about the woman? Re-read. Ask: Where did the little girl write everything down? Re-read. Ask: What did the woman do for the children? Re-read. Ask: Why was the woman happy to help the children? Why is it important to help others?
author: Hello English

title: Alana the Baby Crocodile
text: Alana was a baby crocodile. Each night her father would give her a ride on the lake. Alana loved her father very much, and always enjoyed their adventures on the water together. Story Description Alana's father tells her not to swim in the lake alone. She swims anyway and gets frightened, and she encounters some strange creatures. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Object ﻿O-b-jek-t ﻿The were many objects sticking out of the lake. Retreated ﻿r-ee-tree-ti-d ﻿She retreated by swimming all the way home. Confessed ﻿c-un-fess-d ﻿She confessed that she had done something wrong. Smooth ﻿s-moo-th ﻿ ﻿She glided smoothly across the lake. Alana would always ask if she could ride next to him, but her father said the water was still too dangerous for her and her brothers. When her father was sleeping, Alana took to the water for the first time. Staying afloat was effortless! She cruised along the lake. For a while as she moved, she only passed rocks and small trees sticking out of the surface. She wondered what else she would find. Very soon she reached an old otter reading his book. The otter said hello, but Alana was not used to talking to creatures that were not crocodiles! She swam quickly away! Alana was swimming when suddenly a giant object dived out of the water, and performed a big jump in the air! A huge dolphin that had come to greet Alana as she swam past. Alana was amazed. Alana looked for a place to rest but the shore was far away. She came to some little rocks where a tiny snail was waiting. As she got closer, the snail retreated and shrank inside its shell. It scared Alana, who quickly moved on. Alana found some trees and stopped. The shore was close by. She was worried because she had betrayed her father by going for a swim alone. Alana swam as far as she could, all the way back. She saw her home getting close and she climbed onto the bank. She felt guilty for what she had done, but when she returned home, her father was still asleep. She confessed everything to her grandmother, who promised she would not tell her father. Then her grandmother offered her and her brothers a ride across the lake. But there was one thing missing - her youngest brother. He quickly climbed down from a branch, and he joined Alana and the crocodiles on their grandmother's back. The ride was slow because grandmother was old, but it was smooth. The crocodiles climbed off one by one and navigated the shore, looking for new things to find. And very soon, when Alana became fearless of all the other creatures, Alana's father allowed her to play in the lake......with creatures like the otter, the beaver, the fish and the fisherman in his boat! Post-Reading Questions How did Alana disobey her father? What made Alana turn around and swim back home? Re-read. Ask: What was the first thing to scare Alana? Re-read. Ask: What did Alana's grandmother agree to do? Re-read. Ask: When swimming in the lake, what did Alana become? Name some sea creatures or animals that are dangerous.
author: Hello English

title: Laughter
text: Story Description A girl experiences the different kinds of laughter that we have. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Laughter ﻿la-f-t-ur ﻿There are many kinds of laughter. Floating ﻿fl-oh-t-ing ﻿Laughter makes us feel like we are floating away in the sky. Tired ﻿t-eye-ur-d ﻿Lots of laughter can make you feel very tired and sleepy. Stomach ﻿st-um-uch ﻿Laughter tickles your stomach. Laughter makes you feel light, like you're floating away! Laughter makes you feel hungry. Then you realise you're not hungry enough, then you laugh more. Laughter makes you feel tired. Laughter gets you in trouble. Sometimes you laugh in the wrong situation. Laughter makes you want to go outside and play. Laughter makes you want to hang upside down. Laughter makes you want to jump with joy. Laughter makes your stomach tickle, which makes you laugh more. There are many kinds of laughter. Happy laughter, nervous laughter, sarcastic laughter, a big belly laugh, laughing that makes you cry, and laughing that doesn't stop. Post-Reading Questions Looking at, what kinds of laughter are there? Name some times when you should not laugh. What do you think nervous laughter is? What do you think happy laughter is?
author: Hello English

title: The Perfect Companion
text: In a big crowded city, with buildings aplenty, There lived a little girl in house number twenty. With the hot endless summer, just around the corner, The school vacation would surely feel longer. Boredom would set in, sooner or later, A pet for a playmate would make her feel better. On a warm Sunday night, w hen everything was quiet, She dreamt of a furry cat who was ginger and white. As she stroked its soft fur, i t let out a gentle purr, Her prayers were answered s he sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." Early the next morning, she ran to her mother saying, "My perfect companion goes meow-meow-meow-meow." "A cat's home in a high-rise, is dangerous and unwise," Reasoned her mother, "A cat's not for you!" On a hot Monday night, with the moon shining bright, She dreamt of a puppy playing ball with delight. As it wagged its little tail, she broke into a smile, Her prayers were answered s he sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." Early the next morning, she ran to her father panting, "My perfect companion goes bow-wow-wow-wow." "Bathing and grooming, feeding and walking, Oh no" said her father, "that's not for me!" On a cloudy Tuesday night, with no moon in sight, She dreamt of an elephant that rose to a great height. With her siblings astride, she went for a joyride, Their prayers were answered they sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." Again in the morning, she sat on her Granny explaining, "An elephant is perfect to take me to school." "Breaking our front wall to fit a giant in the hall," Consoled her Granny, "is impossible! " On a damp Wednesday night, i t rained with no respite, She dreamt of a monkey, w hat a funny sight! With tongue dangling free, i t was hanging on a tree, Her prayers were answered s he sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." At breakfast next morning, she climbed on Grandpa chatting, "A monkey for a playmate is so charming and cool!" "Three children are a handful, a monkey can be painful," Chuckled her Grandpa, "Just not for me!" On a cool Thursday night, with the moon milky white, She dreamt of a little mouse harmless and quiet. Shrinking to its size, she followed it in a trice, Her prayers were answered s he sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." The very next morning, she told her brother giggling, "My perfect companion goes squeak-squeak-squeak-squeak." "Gnawing and chewing, it goes on destroying...," Exclaimed her brother, "Mice are not nice!" On clear Friday night, with the stars shining bright, She dreamt of a rabbit very fluffy and light. As it sat on her lap cuddling, s he fed carrots for nibbling, Her prayers were answered s he sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." Early the next morning, she dragged her sister saying, "A rabbit with long ears is perfect for us." Later in the morning, they went to mother pleading, "The perfect companion is a rabbit, it's true." "It has babies by the dozen, and cleaning is no fun", Declared her mother, "No pets for us! " On a dull Saturday night, in the gloomy skylight, She wished for no pets in her dreams that night. On a bright Sunday morning, she heard the sound of whining, And spotted a squirrel in pain and struggling. With a thorn pricked on its toe, the blood began to flow, She decided to help it and beckoned, "FWEET-FWEET-FWEET-FWEET…" She pulled out a thorn and gave it some corn, It felt happier and better, and slept, "zzz-zzz-zzz-zzz..." On a glorious Monday morning, as the squirrel sat waiting, She offered it guavas that were tasty and tempting. It reached her palm scampering, she embraced it beaming, Her prayers were answered she sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." It reached her palm scampering, she embraced it beaming, Her prayers were answered she sang, "laa-la-laa-laa..." Children can learn the following from 'The Perfect Companion': 1. Days of the week 2. Members of the family 3. Common animals Rhyme-and-rhythm stories are known to be excellent in improving vocabulary and concentration in children. They are easy to remember and fun to repeat. The rhythm of this story is inspired by the famous nursery rhyme "Molly Malone". Go on, try it!
author: Rajani Muralidhar

title: Lunch time
text: The lunch bell rang. Children open the colourful lunch boxes. Parathas, dhoklas, Pulao, Idlis, potato fries- the tasty lunch items are out. Meera, Raju, Julie, Elena, Arnav, Varun, - everyone in the class started sharing and eating their lunch. But the new girl Koel looks sad. She is missing her old school and lunch time with her friends. In her old school, she used to sit under a tree for lunch with friends. They talked about many things like friend’s birthday party, evening’s play time planning and school homework. They enjoyed eating together. Here at new school, she doesn’t know anyone. She doesn’t like to eat alone. She has no friends. “How will I make new friends?” –Koel is even sadder. Someone comes to Koel. She is Elena. She offers her lunch to Koel. Elena brought vegetable pulao. Koel likes Pulao. She eats some. Raju also comes with his lunchbox. He offers Aloo paratha to Koel. Koel takes a bite. It’s yummy! Now, Julie, Arnav and Varun also join the friends. Everyone shares the lunch with Koel. Koel is happy now. She is not missing her old school anymore. She likes here now. Everyone was so hungry - all the tiffin boxes are empty. They look at each other. It looks they are still hungry. Woohoo!! Koel has a surprise for her new friends- cakes and sandwiches in her tiffin box. “It’s my birthday today!” Koel said to her new friends. “Wow!! Happy birthday Koel!” everyone wished her. Everyone relishes cakes and sandwiches while discussing about their new friend’s birthday party at the evening. Making new friends is so easy.
author: Riddhi Nath

title: The Story after the race
text: We all knew very well that the hare lost the race because of it's laziness and it's over confidence. The turtle won because of it's slow and steady nature. All the animals are well aware of this. But still they respect the both. Indeed the turtle and hare are very good friends, though they competed with each other. Turtle never shows off and hare never envied. Months passed!! One day, the king of the forest has to meet the king of neighbouring forest to discuss few important matters. But the lion couldn't go immediately. So, he decided to send both turtle and hare as delegates. Both turtle and hare meet the king. "One of you must visit the neighbouring jungle" said the lion. "You need to discuss few important matters with their king and let me know what's there in his mind." said the lion and sent them. "Remember!! you should finish this task within a day." said the lion. The way to the other forest is filled with thorny bushes and stones. They need to cross two rivers too. Both of them understood that it is not an easy task and they both should work together to finish it.Decided to travel together!!! According to their idea, hare should carry the turtle in thorny area and turtle should carry the hare when ever they have to cross the rivers!! both liked this idea. The next day, both of them took all the information from the king and started their journey. while traveling, the hare is jumping and running in the thorny area and the turtle is holding the hare tightly with fear. When they reached the river, they exchanged their places and the hare climbed on turtle's back. Turtle crossed the river very quick and carefully. After crossing two rivers, they did not take much time to reach the other forest. They met the other king and discussed with him and returned back. They both knew how to to travel. So, they traveled even more easily. Both the rivals worked together and finished the task in advance. In this way, all the animal kingdom learned the benefits of working together and helping each other.
author: Bhargavi  Nerusu

title: Sonu's Concert Hall
text: Sonu lived in a one-room- leaky house. Its holey roof blocked the sun’s heat, but rain sneaked in drop by tiny drop, falling in pots and pan, making happy sounds: La, La, La. Sonu had grown up hearing the drips and enjoyed their unique sounds. The long metallic cup made a ringing sound. The big clay pot sounded as though someone had stepped on mushy sponge. The round pan made a feverish bullfrog croak. The pan with the long handle amused Sonu the most. He felt that it would start singing and dancing if left alone. This year the rains were heavy and father tried to tarp the holes but somehow ended up making them bigger. Early morning, a squeak woke up Sonu and he found a baby squirrel that had fallen through a hole. The ticket-less squirrel was trying to sneak into their private concert-hall. Sonu’s mother was not amused. “I wish we could live in a house without holes,” she sighed. Sonu wanted to live only in this musical house where the sun enjoyed shining through the holes. Sonu looked at the spot lights they made on the wall and the floor. This was live theater! Sonu imagined himself as a rock star singing across the room as the light shifted. He held the long handled pan as a guitar. He was surprised to find his mother sulking. “I thought you would laugh!” said Sonu. “I wish I could,” She said, “I don’t like draining pots all day and feel tired of the drippy sounds” She muttered, “...I have no pots left for cooking.” Father teased: “You grumble noisily just like your pots.” Mother pretended to be hurt and chased both father and son with the long-handled pan. All three fell in a heap and laughed. The next day, Sonu brought in discarded bottles and placed them under the holes. Now when the rainwater dripped, it made new sounds, a new music. Sonu looked at his mother proudly, “Ma, we no longer have the La-La-La. We have Sol-Me-Do.” Mother hugged Sonu and said, “I’m very happy to have a son who fills our house with sunshine when it is pouring outside.” That evening father brought home a bundle of reeds and an instruction book. Sonu and his mother had puzzled looks on their faces and so the father explained: “Sonu needs music right through the year, not just during rainy season. These reeds could be turned into musical flutes.” “ Yes!” whooped Sonu, “We could make music together.” The whole family sat together making flutes. Father carved the reeds. Mother drilled holes in them. Sonu fine-tune the sounds. Very soon, they had a couple of flutes ready. This kind of hard work made sense to everyone. Sonu’s secret plan was to sell the flutes at the fair and make money to fix the leaks on the roof. Now, looking at the flutes, he felt so happy he sang: I have a musical home. This pan is my trombone, The roof is my drum, This bottle you could strum… Dad happily joined in the silliness and added: La, la-la, ding-ding, This music makes me sing. Mother looked at both of them amused and sang along: My flute is no silly stick. It makes happy music. Mother and father clapped and danced. They had not finished the song when the long handled pan fell from the hook and clanged. It bounced boing…, boing……. Sonu knew this pot could make music. But today, he saw it’s dance too.
author: jaya rangan
illustrator: Alina  Aphayvanh; Greystroke; Herminder Ohri; Kabini  Amin; Kavitha Mandana; Nankusia Shyam; Proiti Roy; Rajiv Eipe; Sahitya Rani; Sheetal Thapa; Shivika Nayyar; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Suvidha Mistry; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Crow and Sparrow
text: Story Description A crow and a sparrow both go on a mission to search for food, when there is barely any left. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Perched ﻿pur-ch-d ﻿ ﻿The crow was perched on a branch Swooping ﻿s-woo-p-ing ﻿The birds came swooping in and dived for food. Pecking ﻿pe-k-ing ﻿The sparrow pecked away at the nut shell. Beautiful ﻿b-yew-tih-f-ful ﻿ ﻿The sparrow had beautiful coloured feathers. Crow's alarm sounded at five in the morning as the sun rose. She was ready to get up and find food. Sparrow had already been up for a while. She was in a panic. "Have you seen any worms?" she said to a mouse. "No," said the mouse. "I don't eat worms." Crow joined her flock of friends and they hunted together, finding food in the park. But very soon crow could not find any food. The birds separated and flew away from each other. Crow felt very confused and upset. Sparrow found a small fruit in the park, but it was very heavy to carry. On the way back to her nest, she dropped it and it landed in someone's garden. Crow caught a little grey bird's attention by singing. "Have you found any food?" said crow. "No," said the grey bird. "I heard nobody can find food today." Sparrow perched on a branch and thought for a while. "Maybe the insects will know where to find food," she imagined. Crow found a farmhouse with scraps of bread and seeds. She called to her friends, who came swooping in the distance to collect the food. "You must know where to find food," said the sparrow. "I eat very small mites," said the insect. "I don't think you'll like them." "I'll take anything," said the sparrow. Crow had her feed and settled back in her nest as her friends flew away. Later she wandered the ground searching for worms because she was still hungry. "Do you have any food?" said the sparrow to a cow. "I don't think you'll like milk," said the cow. "It's not to your taste." "I'll try anything," said the sparrow. Crow returned to her nest while it rained. Out came a beautiful peacock spreading its feathers, searching the ground for insects. "Why is there such little food?" said the crow. "The seasons are changing," said the peacock. "Winter is coming and the ground is harder." Crow took flight and saw the sparrow struggling to carry a fruit. Again, the sparrow dropped some fruit because it was too heavy, and she started to cry. "I haven't had a meal all day!" she said. Crow realised how hungry the sparrow was. In desperation, the sparrow found a man with a net filled with fish. "Please, give me one!" she said, pecking at the net. "Ok, ok," said the man. "Just leave me alone!" Finally the sparrow ate some food. Crow brought her friends along to find the sparrow. They searched far and wide......until crow found her hiding in her nest. "What is it?" said the sparrow. "I saw you drop the fruit earlier, so me and my friends brought you food from the farm," said the crow. Sparrow was so happy, because now she had more than enough to eat! Post-Reading Questions ﻿Why did crow feel upset? What did crow finally bring the sparrow to eat? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the cow offer to the sparrow? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What is special about the peacock? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the sparrow do again? ﻿If you were a bird, what kind of food would you look for?
author: Hello English

title: The Traveller's Jungle
text: Story Description A traveller finds a jungle to take photographs of. But once inside, strange things start happening to him, and a mystery is slowly revealed. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Mysterious ﻿ ﻿mi-ss-tee-er-ee-uss ﻿ ﻿The forest was magical and mysterious. Enchanted ﻿ ﻿in-ch-ant-id ﻿The place felt very enchanted with the strange atmosphere. Splattered ﻿sp-la-t-er-d ﻿The flowers looked like they were splattered with paint. Ordinary ﻿or-de-n-air-ee ﻿ ﻿It had been a normal, ordinary day. There was a traveller who was crossing the countryside, when he encountered a mysterious jungle. He stopped to take pictures of it. There were trees, shrubs, leaves and plants of all kinds and colours. The traveller felt enchanted by the strange shapes of the things he saw. The traveller picked plants and saw they were almost splattered with paint. He had never seen such wonderful colours! He wondered how they grew. As the day went on, the temperature rose and the traveller felt hot and exhausted. "Perhaps I am seeing things because of the heat, and these are just ordinary plants," he wondered. Too tired to continue, the traveller rested against a rock, where he saw a blue spotted bird smiling back at him, turning its head all the way around. That was when something tapped his shoulder. The traveller saw a greyish man with long hair and a bead of flowers around his head. "I am everything in this forest," said the man. "From the bird you were looking at, to the trees you were taking photos of. It is all a reflection of me." "That's not possible," said the traveller, laughing to himself. But the traveller could only see the man's head. The rest of him was nowhere to be seen behind the giant leaf. "That was a clever magic trick," said the traveller. "I'll prove it to you that I am telling the truth," said the man. The traveller was bemused when his legs and arms began stretching, and his body floated by itself around and around. "What's happening?" said the traveller. "This is so strange!" The experience lasted for a while until the traveller came to a rest, and the man vanished. "I'm suffering from the heat," said the traveller. "This is all a hallucination." The traveller continued, trying to forget the experience, and he saw a beautiful bird perched on some leaves. He could not resist taking a picture. Then the traveller saw the bird grin at him. It transformed into the man's face! The traveller then saw a cluster of elephants bathing in a pond. When he saw their faces, they turned into the man's face. The traveller couldn't believe it was real. The plants and the pond also contained the man's smiling face. The traveller promised to keep the mystery of the jungle a secret. He waved goodbye to the elephants. When he checked the photos, the man appeared in all of them! He was everywhere! Post-Reading Questions What was special about the plants that the traveller saw? What did the mystery man say about himself? Re-read. Ask: Why did the traveller think he was seeing things? Re-read. Ask: What did the traveller find strange about the man? Re-read. Ask: What was the secret that the traveller discovered? Think of a place that is magical or mystical and describe it.
author: Hello English

title: Greedy cat
text: Once a cat saw a hole in the wall of a house He entered in through the hole. There he saw tasty food on the table. He ate all the food and was not able to move a little And when he was about to make him out, he came to know that he was really trapped. His large stomach made it difficult for him to get out through the hole...
author: somasekharan govindapanicker
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Rohan Chakravarty; somasekharan govindapanicker; Tanvi Bhat

title: Lika, the superkid
text: Lika looks at the cloud and touches her belly button at the same time. Just then the cloud moves. Lika touches her belly button again. The cloud moves again. Lika runs happily. “I moved the clouds. I am a superwoman. No, I am a superkid.” “Mom, I can move the clouds.” Mom says: “Well, you can do anything you set your mind on. You don’t give up.” “Dad, I helped the clouds move.” Dad says, “Lika, you always help us. I bet you do the same all around.” Lika sees a cat stuck on a branch in the tree. She touches her belly button but the cat does not move. Lika touches her belly button again. Nothing happens. The cat looks away. Lika tries climbing the tree but slips. Lika calls to the cat: “Here kitty-kitty, COME DOWN. Jump. I will catch you.” The cat does not move. Lika has set her mind to save kitty. Lika likes to help. She brings a ladder and rescues the cat. Lika is a superkid.
author: jaya rangan
illustrator: Greystroke; Imile  Wepener; Jesse  Breytenbach; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Krishna Chandran; Nyambura Kariuki; Priya Kuriyan; Shailja Jain Chougule; Shohei Emura; Tanvi Bhat; Vivekananda Roy Ghatak; Yuvaka  Srestha

title: Where's my Amma?
text: My Amma is not at home. Where can she be? Is she at the Bus stop? No, this is my Mummy, but we can help you look for Amma. Is that your Amma in the corn field? No, this is my Ma, but we can help you look for Amma. Is that your Amma in the Market? No, this is my Mama, but we can help you look for Amma. Is that your Amma cooking rotis? No, this is my Mai, but we can help you look for Amma. Is that your Amma in the garden? No, this is my Ammie, but we can help you look for Amma. Wait! This is my Amma. Thank you friends, and your Mummy, Ma, Mama, Mai, and Ammie for helping me look for my Amma.
author: Suchitra Mohan
illustrator: Dixa Barooah; Nirzara Verulkar; Ntembiso  Velemane; Rijuta Ghate; Rob Owen; Shailja Jain Chougule; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Suvidha Mistry

title: The Girl Who Thinks in Numbers: Data Warrior  Prukalpa Sankar
text: Prukalpa loves numbers. She loves them because she knows numbers can solve problems. Numbers help build patterns and stories. Numbers connect people. They also give people power. This is what she does at SocialCops, a company she has started with her friend Varun. Prukalpa’s favourite numbers involve collecting large quantities of information about people. This is called data. These days, people say, data is more valuable than oil or gold. Why is that? How can a few numbers, or even many numbers, be worth more than some of the most valuable things in the world? Let’s take your school, and you, for example. You didn’t go to school twice this week. You had a stomach bug. It made you vomit. It gave you cramps. It doesn’t seem very important information to anybody else. Only your parents, teachers and you care, right? But what if five other children in your class were also sick on the same days? Often what happens to you isn’t just about you. What if their stomach cramps kept them home too? If the principal got this information, she might wonder why six students of a class fell ill in the same way on the same day? Was it the lunch served at school? Could it be the water they drank in school? This is how information about groups can be very useful. When information about your classmates is put together in one place, it becomes community data. Community data is information about a group of people related to each other, like you and your classmates. This data comes from each of you. It is crowdsourced, which means it has been collected from people. This is how Prukalpa uses numbers or data. She collects it to solve problems, and to help manage schools, cities and lives better. 5 crore women 13 states, 640 districts, 50,000 field mechanics, 3 oil companies, 10,000 LPG distribution centres People impacted Areas Other resources CLEAN COOKING FUEL IN 3 YEARS In 11 months, SocialCops helped distribute 2.7 crore LPG connections. INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTERS AND INTERNET 1 crore women 12 states, 1 lakh villages People impacted Areas BETTER HYGIENE AND SANITATION LEVELS BY BRINGING ANTIBACTERIAL SOAP TO VILLAGES Areas Diseases tracked 822 sub-districts 20 diseases tracked for 260 weeks How do Prukalpa and her team get information that government officers and other organisations need to make decisions? The team puts a simple tool called Collect on people’s phones. This makes it possible for the team to gather useful data from people anywhere in the world. When you have so many tiny bits of information from individuals, you end up with a massive heap of data. What Prukalpa’s team does is clean up the information and organise it. It’s similar to the way you arrange your desk so you can find pens, papers and other material when you look for them. How do they do it? They use powerful computer systems and codes to create connections among different kinds of data. These connections would be very difficult to make without computer systems. They also use charts, maps and graphs to show how data can link to each other. The data begins to tell stories. The connections become easy to understand. Prukalpa loves what she does. She loves being an entrepreneur. But it takes relentless hard work to set up a company. To work in small villages that are tough to reach, to work with government departments that might not be ready to try new ideas, and to help people understand why they should value data. In most places in India, information is still recorded in paper registers. It isn’t available in digital form, which means it is difficult to manage. Also, many government agencies collect data but they don’t work with each other to combine this data in one place. Organising data that is already available has been the biggest challenge for Prukalpa and her team. What has also been tough is realising that change is a slow, difficult journey-built data by data, person by person. As an entrepreneur, this is exactly the kind of work Prukalpa wanted to do when she started out. She decided that her love for numbers shouldn’t be used by a large corporate alone. What keeps her going is the satisfaction that comes from making an impact by seeing lives improve and enabling better decisions. PRUKALPA AND HER TEAM HAVE PARTNERED WITH GOVERNMENTS, BUSINESSES, PHILANTHROPIES, AND NONPROFITS FROM ACROSS THE GLOBE Dominican Republic Ireland USA Guatemala Canada Ivory Coast Liberia Spain Germany South Africa Zambia Mozambique Malawi Kenya South Korea Indonesia Philippines Singapore Malaysia Myanmar Vietnam Bangladesh India UAE Papua New Guinea Sri Lanka
author: Shreyasi Singh

title: The Mehendi Boy
text: Rudra's uncle was going to get married in a day. Friends, relatives, and little children started gathering in his house. There was fun and frolic everywhere. But Rudra was not interested in all this. He spent most of his time watching TV or playing video games. He felt the world outside was very boring. "Start getting ready for the function Rudra. Don't just be glued to the TV and video games," said Rudra's mother. "All your cousins and friends are putting Mehendi on their hands. Go out now and put it on your hands as well," said Rudra's mother. "But I don't want it," retorted Rudra. "Just try once dear. It would be a fun experience and you might like it," said Rudra's mother. With a lot of reluctance, Rudra applied Mehendi on his hands. "Remember Rudra, do not use your hands for another 8 hours till it dries up," said Rudra's mother. Rudra was shocked. "What? How can I change TV channels? How can I play video games if I cannot use my hands?" Rudra thought. Rudra felt irritated. He did not know what to do. He wandered outside his home. He saw some children playing in the park. He saw a slide nearby. "Hmm... I guess I do not need my hands for that," thought Rudra. Whoosh... He slid down the slide with his hands up in the air. Rudra loved it. He went up and down the slide a few more times. An hour passed by. Rudra saw some children playing football. As the ball came towards him, he kicked it. He liked it. "Hmm... I guess I do not need my hands for this," thought Rudra. Rudra played football with the kids for some time. After playing football, Rudra was walking towards his home. He saw Malathi akka telling stories to children outside the community library. Rudra decided to sit and listen to her stories for some time. It was a beautiful adventure story about a magical land, lost treasure, wicked witch and lots more. Rudra got so engrossed that he did not notice the time fly by. "Children, let us continue the story in the next session," said Malathi akka as she closed the story session for the day. "Oh no! Was the wicked witch defeated? Where was the treasure? What happens to the fire-spitting dragon guarding the treasure?" asked Rudra to Malathi akka. "Aha, you have to come for the next session to find out that," said Malathi akka with a smile. Rudra's mind was still thinking about how the story will end as he got up and started walking. He felt thirsty after walking for a long distance. He wanted to drink some water. He saw a cow drinking water. He saw a drinking water tap nearby and requested a man walking by to pour the water into a bowl. "Hmm. I may not need my hands for this," thought Rudra as he bent down on his knees and slurped the water with his tongue like the cow. That was fun he thought as he walked back. Slurp! Slurp! Several hours passed by. It was almost evening and it was time to go home. He saw some birds flying. "I wish I could fly back home," thought Rudra. "Whoo... hooo..." Rudra jumped, hopped and flapped his hands hard trying to fly like a bird. Finally, he reached his home. Eight hours had passed. Rudra washed his hands. There was a beautiful imprint on his hand. He showed it to his mother. "Amma, do you know what happened today? I slid and whooshed down the slide. I kicked the ball with my foot. I listened to an adventurous story from Malathi akka. I slurped and drank water like a cow. I flew like a bird," said Rudra as he lay down on his mother's lap and told his story. "Hmm... Looks like the Mehendi has not just left a beautiful imprint on Rudra's hands but also in his heart" thought Rudra's mother as she smiled, patted his back and made him sleep.
author: Aru
illustrator: 211 Studio; Dr. Sushma  Singh; Gaurav Wakankar; Henu; Iddi  Marumba; Kalp Sanghvi; Ram Soni; Rijuta Ghate; Rob Owen; Sanjay Sarkar; Shanti Devi; Soumya Menon

title: Carol and Theo
text: Story Description Carol marries a local man called Theo. Suddenly, Theo has to go away with his tribe and leave Carol behind for a while. Feeling upset, Carol waits for him to return home. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Decided de-s-ai-did The man decided to look for his scarf. Apologise a-poh-lu-j-ai-z He wanted to apologise for his bad behaviour. Forgiveness for-gi-v-n-uss The man sought forgiveness for his actions. Reunited ree-you-n-ai-tid The husband and wife were reunited after being apart. Carol and Theo were part of an African tribe. They decided to get married. The village priest wed them. They were so happy. Very soon Carol gave birth to a baby boy they called Samuel. They were so filled with joy to be parents. But one day Theo had to go away with the men in his tribe. He had to leave Carol behind. Carol was very upset. She didn’t know for how long Theo would be gone. A member of the village council handed a scarf to Carol, after she left baby Samuel with her father. “That belongs to my brother Ismael,” she said. “Where did you find it?” “It was lying on the ground,” said the council member. Carol found Ismael after he’d had an argument with two men. “Ismael,” shouted Carol. “I found your scarf You dropped it in the street!” “I accused those men of stealing it,” said Ismael. “I had better apologise to them.” Ismael got down on his knees and begged the men for forgiveness. “It’s all right, Ismael,” said the men. “We understand how angry you were.” “Thank you so much,” said Ismael. “You must think before you accuse someone,” said Carol. “I know,“ said Ismael. “Next time I will be more careful.” “Carol!” came a voice in the distance. “Theo!” said Carol. “I’m home,” said Theo. At last, they were reunited as a family. Post-Reading Questions Why did Carol and Theo have to be apart? Use a word to describe Carol and Theo coming back together. Re-read. Ask: What did Carol find that belonged to her brother? Re-read. Ask: Why did Carol's brother get on his knees? Re-read. Ask: What advice did Carol give to her brother? When should we forgiv e, and why should we have patience?
author: Hello English

title: Animal Race
text: Story Description Animals jump in front of each other to try and win a race, but they don't always play by the proper rules. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sneaks ﻿s-nee-k-s ﻿The animal sneaks in front. Rascal ﻿ra-ss-cul ﻿The rascal rabbit hops about. Hefty ﻿hef-tee ﻿The hefty elephant snatches a place. Leaps ﻿ lee-p-s ﻿The dog leaps around. At the back of the group is the slow, slow tortoise......the snake sneaks in front of the tortoise, slithering across the ground......then the rascal rat dips in front of the snake......and the snappy lizard crawls in front of the mouse......and the hefty heavy elephant trots in front of the lizard......and the sneaky cat darts in front of the elephant......and the wily fox leaps ahead of the cat......and the jumpy rabbit hops in front of the fox... and the giant horse gallops away from the rabbit......and the cheating cheetah sprints in front of the horse to win the race......and they all pose for their photo at the finish line! Post-Reading Questions Who won the race at the very last moment? Who do you think finished in last place? Name the animals in order from last to first. Which was the largest of the animals to take part? Which was the smallest of the animals to take part?
author: Hello English

title: The Courageous Lion
text: Story Description For most of his life, the lion has been teased and mistreated at the zoo. Tired of living there, the lion plans to escape, a decision that takes him on an adventure through the city. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Torrential ﻿tu-ren-sh-ul ﻿The rain was so heavy it was torrential. Crept ﻿c-rep-t ﻿The lion crept past the man so he wouldn't make a sound. Kindness ﻿k-ai-n-d-nuss ﻿The lion was touched by the boy's kindness. Alive ﻿ a-l-ai-v ﻿For the first time, he felt alive. There was a lion that lived in a zoo. The people would stare at and tease him. The lion was tired of being mistreated. He wanted to leave and find a new home. One day there was torrential rain and everyone ran for cover. Most people went home from the zoo. The lion felt the depth of the water around his enclosure. He could not feel the bottom. He was desperate to escape, but he did not know if he could make it out. The lion jumped in the pool and floated with the current. He paddled with his paws until he found a patch of dry grass. He lifted himself out and climbed the fence, frightening some of the zoo visitors. He ran as fast as he could through the zoo, determined not to be captured. He walked past several enclosures, including the bear's cage. He saw a bear relaxing, and the bear was not surprised to see the lion. "Listen carefully to me," said the bear. " Don't think you'll escape from this zoo. Wherever you go, they'll find you." The lion crept past the visitor centre and saw one of the cleaners asleep. Without hesitating, the lion bounced through the room and sneaked past the man. From there he ran out of the main entrance and into some fields. The lion went from the fields to some streets lined with advertisements and shops. He saw the city. There was a lot of noise which annoyed him, making him want to hide. The lion found a bridge and crawled under it to hide. Once there, he found people sleeping. His presence scared them a little, but once they realised the lion was peaceful, they relaxed. "They treated you very badly in that zoo," said one of the boys. "You deserve a new home. Stay with us anytime." The lion appreciated the affection and the kindness of the strangers. But the lion could not stay for long. He felt hungry and thirsty. He found a nice little house and went inside. In the kitchen, a pot of stew and a drink of water was on the table. He ate it all up, and felt very tired soon afterwards. Upstairs he found a woman asleep in her bed. Underneath the bed, there was a lot of space. He wondered if he kept still and slept, the woman would not notice he was there. So he curled up underneath her bed, and slept like those people under the bridge. The next morning, very early, the lion woke up. He quickly left the house, not disturbing the woman, and he made his way through the fields, looking for a new home. He didn't know what would happen, but for the first time in his life, he felt alive. Post-Reading Questions ﻿Why did the lion want to escape from the zoo? Describe the lion's actions as he swam, climbed the fence and escaped into the city. Re-read. Ask: ﻿What does the bear warn the lion of? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What does the boy offer to the lion? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What is known about the lion's future? ﻿Do you think the lion will not get caught?
author: Hello English

title: The Sun and the Moon
text: Story Description The sun and the moon work together to invite the sea into their house. But the sea brings along its problems and all of its creatures, and could potentially flood the land. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Steered st-ear-d The sea steered the sun where it wanted to go. Invited in-v-ai-t-id The sun had invited the moon to its house. Receded re-see-did The water receded and went away from the land. Despite dis-p-eye-t They always got on well together, despite their differences. The sun was having the moon around as a guest, when the sea wanted to join in their fun. "You're welcome to join in," said the sun to the sea. The sea reached out and took the sun's hand......and steered the sun to the beach, bringing itself further in......but not realising it had completely circled the house, and it would flood the entire land. The sun worried and wondered what to do. "How about building a wall?" suggested the moon. So the sun built a massive wall around the house to guide the sea in. Once completed, the sun invited the sea to come in......and with the moon's help, they guided the sea into the house. The surrounding land remained dry. The sea brought many creatures with it, including an alligator, a frog, a tortoise, snails and snakes. But very soon the house was getting overcrowded. There were too many sea creatures. "We have to stop it," said the moon. "What can we do?" The entire house was flooded, and the sun and the moon had to think quickly to deal with the problem. Then the sun had an idea. It asked the sea to retreat a little. Very soon the water receded and the level went down. The creatures were allowed in the house, but only a few at a time because there was little room. Even a hippo turned up to see the house! The moon watched carefully as creatures went in and out. Soon the sea went out and said goodbye, taking its creatures with it. The sun and the moon worked well together, and despite their differences and the mistakes they often made, they were good friends. Post-Reading Questions Why did the sun build a wall around the house? When the sea came in, what did it bring along? Re-read. Ask: What problem did the sun and the moon face? Re-read. Ask: Why did the water recede (go back) from the shore? Re-read. Ask: Why did the sun and the moon get along so well?
author: Hello English

title: Dave the Charming Donkey
text: Story Description Dave the donkey starts to change over time, from being a young donkey into a grown-up mature donkey. Along the way he encounters fears and changes in his life. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Hee-haw hee-h-or The sound a donkey makes is called a hee-haw. Meadow m-eh-doe There was a beautiful flat meadow by the river. Shadow sh-a-doe The donkey saw its own shadow against the wall. Socialise so-sh-ul-eyes He was calm around friends because he could socialise well. Dave the charming donkey lived by a meadow and a lake. Dave had a strange hee-haw. It was more like see-saw, and on other days it sounded like haw-hee. Dave saw his reflection in the lake. He saw himself for the first time, and he felt terrified. His hee-haw got louder and louder. Now he could shout over long distances. Dave saw his shadow against a wall. For the first time he saw how big he was. Dave met an animal for the first time. It was a little hedgehog, and it was scared of Dave's oddly shaped head. Dave had fruit for the first time. It was a banana, which he ate with a laughing monkey and a confused bird. Dave saw the hair on his head. It was getting longer. And very soon it stretched all the way down his back. Dave felt like a grown up. He could reach around trees and play with the tyre swing. And he could socialise with the other animals that drank from the lake. Dave saw that he was becoming cool! Over time, the animals liked Dave, and so Dave had a number of friends after a while. He ran, jumped, sang and played with them, and they all enjoyed his company. And very soon, Dave realised he was a charming donkey. He had come far from being scared of his own reflection, and all the animals adored him. Post-Reading Questions How does Dave change as he grows up? True or false - Dave gets lots of friends over time. Re-read. Ask: What changes about Dave? Re-read pages 14-16. Ask: What did the animals like about Dave? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What had Dave come far from? ﻿What do you think is a good ﻿quality to have?
author: Hello English

title: Lila's First Day
text: Today was to be Lila’s first day at her new school. Her mother woke her up in the morning, “Lila, little one, wake up, it’s your first day at school!” Lila’s mother lifted her gently off the bed, “Come on, honey, out of bed.” Little Lila opened her eyes, a little scared. “I don’t want to go, Mummy. I know no one there.” ﻿ “Baby, I know. But you must go. You will meet new people, learn things, and you’ll see – your first day won’t be as awful as you think it might be!” Lila dressed and went down to eat her breakfast, still afraid. She ate her buttered toast quietly and thought in dismay, “At least, school will be over at 12, today.” Mrs. Vaz, Lila’s mother, then quickly ushered Lila off her chair, “Time to leave, sweet girl! I’ll drive you there.” As they reached the parking lot of the school, Mrs. Vaz said to Lila, “I know how you’re feeling… This is a new place for the both of us, and I’m scared too. But change always brings with it something special. Something new! Do you remember what Aunty Rose always says?” “Fear is never a fwend, only a wobblyyy crutch,” Lila says with a soft smile. Aunty Rose always loved talking in funny voices. Lila hugs her mother goodbye, carries her backpack out of the car and waves to her mother driving away - for a good while. Then, sighing to herself, walking past the sounds of merry chatter – Lila walks on slowly into the school. Her class teacher introduces her to the rest of the fourth-grade class. “Lila, do you want to say something to your new classmates?” “Hi, my name is Lila. It’s my first day, today.” Her teacher guides her back to her seat, “Welcome, Lila! We hope you enjoy your stay.” The minutes kept on ticking… Soon, it was their first lunch break. Lila carried her backpack out of class, and followed the crowd. The canteen was in a little garden where butterflies flew about. Where do I sit? wondered Lila. Where I can lay? Then, she saw a big, full tree, not too far away. She walked quickly, skipping a little – sat beside the trunk and took out her cheese and ham sandwich to eat it. She began eating quietly, watching the crowd of children. Lost in thought, she didn’t see the other girl until she felt a gentle tap on her shoulder. “Hello. Can I please sit by you?” the girl said. Lila nodded. “Thank you. I don’t know anyone and it’s my first day, today.” Lila smiled and shyly said, “It’s my first day, here, too.” Before they knew it, the girls were chatting and lunch break was over. ﻿ The second set of lessons were done, and soon it was time to go back home. How the time flew for the both of them, they never knew! When they each got back to their own homes, that day… Can you guess what they told their mothers about that very fine day? “Mum, I made a new friend, today!”
author: Roanna Fernandes
illustrator: Amy  Slatem; Clyde   Beech; Godwin  Chipenya; Jupiter  Pradhan; Karmacharya K.K; Lavanya  Naidu; Mary Anne Hampton; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Renuka Rajiv; Sahitya Rani; Tanvee Nabar; Tasneem Amiruddin

title: Little Monkey's flight with the Bats
text: It was a dark, cold, winter night. Little monkey “Dew”, who never listens at school,always wished to visit the town at dusk. The cheeky little monkey started walking and walking down a dark street. As he was walking, he tripped over the roots of a big banyan tree. “Ouch”, he said as he fell, getting his bottom hit. A little while later, two bats got hold of the monkey walking alone. “Hey, monkey what are you doing here”? Asked the younger bat. “Hi Batty!! Came out to visit the town. Well! Did you check out the town's famous super mall? “Na”, he nodded. “Have you guys been there before”. “Ya a couple of times. You know what, we are blind and we can’t see”,yet we can help you reach the mall, the elder batty added. “How come, when you can’t see” chuckled the monkey. “We will show you how”. Both the bats, decided to carry the little monkey as they fly. They picked a stick and got hold of the ends,mean while little monkey hang on to the middle of the stick. Flying was very new to the little monkey, but he happily accepted the offer. “Woo!! That’s quite good, after all the walking, “I’m flying now”, with a bliss he said to himself. “Well let me know how are you flying without sight"? “It’s kind of technical, I guess you shouldn't get bored as you enjoy your flight”. We regularly transmit ultrasonic sounds through our mouths and noses. These sound waves echo (are reflected) back, giving image of the objects around us. This process is called echolocation. Hence, we use echoes (reflected sounds) to determine the surrounding situation. Arae!! Waa!! Haven’t known that before,exclaimed the monkey hanging strong. You know what, people do copied our technology and they came up with something called “Ultrasonic sensor”, Said the elder bat. “But why do they need it Batty, as they can see ”. Well, the visually challenged are privileged by this ultrasonic sensor and the buzzer, which prevents them from hitting on anything. The buzzer alerts the visually challenged person when an obstacle comes front. Oh Batty!! How do you know all these stuff? “I do carefully listen in my class at school dear little monkey” The bats and the little monkey “Dew” landed safely. And thereafter they happily explored the mall. Moral: Even hanging can never stop you from listening when you pay attention.
author: Ancy Jeesa

title: Bear's Day
text: Story Description Bear performs several activities in a day, from getting covered in paint, to looking for bee hives and singing. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Covered cu-v-er-d The bear was covered in paint. Trip tr-i-p The bear nearly trip ped and fell. Lying lie-ing The bear was lying down on the grass looking at the sky. Singing s-ing-ing The bear was so happy that he was singing. Oh no, bear! What's wrong? Are you bored? Where are you going, bear? Are you heading outside? What's that, bear? Have you found something in the tree? Look, bear! You're covered in honey! Oh, what's that flying over your head? Careful, bear! Don't take a step, there's some mud! Oh, no! Look what you're covered in, bear! What's that you're eating, bear? How does it taste? That's a lot of watermelon, bear! Are you going to eat it all? What's the matter, bear? Are you lost? Who is following you? Oh, bear! Look out for the rocks, you might trip! You look happy, bear! You are covered in paint! What are you doing, bear? Why are you lying down? Oh dear, bear! Did you fall in? Why are you singing, bear? Are you happy? What's that on the wall behind you, bear? Did you paint them? Post-Reading Questions Describe bear's personality. What is he like? How did bear get covered in honey? Why does bear eat so much? What did bear paint on the wall? What items are in the paintings in bear's house?
author: Hello English

title: Silly Camel Tukaram
text: Tukaram was a very silly camel. He lived in a great, big, desert with lots and lots of sand. B ut Tukaram did not like sand at all. "Its too grainy." he complained. And Tukaram did not like the sun. "It makes everything too hot." he complained. And Tukaram did not like the desert plants either. "They just don't look good." he complained. "If only I lived in a blue underwater world, I would be so happy." he thought. So Tukaram moved to a place with lots and lots of water. "Now, I will be happy." he thought. He saw a puffer fish and was very thrilled, but the fish swam away and it was boring. Tukaram saw some turtles and a frog swim by. "Wait for me" he called, but no one did. "This is no different from the desert." thought Tukaram "I miss my desert." he wept. So Tukaram went back home. All his friends were very happy to see Tukaram. "Welcome back" they said. Tukaram looked at the same desert and said. "This is beautiful." He looked at the same sun and thought "This sun warms me up so well." He stepped on the same sand and thought "I can run so fast on this sand." Now Tukaram was happy. He knew he was in the best place he could be in.
author: Suchitra Mohan
illustrator: Chaaya Prabhat; Jitendra Thakur; Juhi  Agarwal; Kalp Sanghvi; Muniza Shariq; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Pia Meenakshi; Priya Kuriyan; Rohit Bhasi; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Swetha g

title: Bless You ... Aaachoo!
text: One day while playing in the garden, Amu sneezed, “Aachoo!” Amma immediately said, “Bless you, my little angel!” and gently wiped her nose with a handkerchief. Amu looked at her thoughtfully and then continued to play. Later, while they were visiting her Ammamma 's house, little Amu happened to sneeze again, “Aachoo!” Her Ammamma promptly said in Tamil, " Dheergaayis purnaayis sadayis.” Amu then said, “What was that, Ammamma?" Ammamma hugged her and replied, “It means bless you. Bless you with a long life, my darling." A few days later, Amu sneezed again, “Aachoo!” This time, Salma didi, who was mopping the floor, quickly said, “ ﻿Jeebo, Jeebo!" Amu turned to her Nanna, who was reading the newspaper, and asked him, “What was that, Nanna?" Nanna looked up from the paper and said, “It literally means 'stay alive’ in Bengali.” Seeing her puzzled look, he put down the paper and continued to say, “huh…it means bless you!” tapping her nose playfully. That evening, Amu went to attend a wedding of a relative along with her Thathayya and parents. While watching the wedding, she happened to sneeze, “Aachoo!”. Immediately, her Thathayya placed his hand on her head and said, “ Dheerga ayushmaan bhava ”. “ Thathayya, what was that?” asked little Amu curiously, Thathayya replied in a deep, solemn voice, “It means may you be blessed with long life.” Amu looked confused, so he sat her on his lap and then said softly, “It means bless you, little one." Later, she saw the newly married couple prostrate before her Thathayya to seek his blessing, who then said, “ …God bless you.” And immediately, Amu acted like she was about to sneeze and said “Aaachooo,” loudly. Everyone around looked surprised. Amma asked, “Are you okay, sweetheart?” Amu confidently said, “Why yes, Amma, I’m okay!" A few days later, Amu was on her way to attend her cousin Devan's birthday party along with her Amma and Nanna. They met a padre collecting donations. When her father donated some money, the padre crossed his fingers and said, “May God bless you.” Amu immediately acted like she was about to sneeze and loudly said, “Aaaachoo!” Nanna asked, “Are you okay, Amu?” Amu replied promptly with a satisfied smile, “Why yes, Nanna, I’m okay!" At the birthday party, it was time to cut the cake. Everyone began to sing, “ Happy Birthday to you, Happy Birthday to you, Happy Birthday dear Devan, Happy Birthday to you..” A few people continued to sing, “ May God bless you.” Amu loudly said, “Aachooo!” They continued to sing, “.. May God bless you.. ”, Amu again went, “ Aachoo!” “.. May God bless you, dear Devan.” Amu now did the loudest, “ Aachoo!!!! ”. Taken aback, her parents asked, “Amu, are you alright?” Amu said smugly, “Why yes, I’m perfect!” Amma sat down face to face, placed her hands on Amu's shoulders and asked with a lot of concern, “Then why do you keep saying Aachoo?” Amu then replied very innocently, with her eyes wide open, “Doesn’t my ‘aachoo’ mean bless you?" Everyone laughed. Amma - Mother in Tamil Ammamma - Maternal Grandmother in Tamil Nanna - Father in Telugu Thathayya - Paternal Grandfather in Telugu
author: Rohini Lochan
