title: The Neighbourhood of Animals
text: Story Description Andy and Jasmine live in a neighbourhood filled with different animals they get along with. There are many dogs and cats, cows and fishes. There is even a friendly frog that gives advice. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Obedient ﻿o-bee-dee-unt ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿The dog followed orders and was very obedient. Investigate ﻿in-ves-te-gate ﻿The dog enjoyed sniffing around to investigate. Guidance ﻿guy-dun-ss The frog gave great advice and wise guidance. Accompanies ﻿a-come-pa-nee-s ﻿The dog accompanies the girl everywhere she goes. Andy and Fred live at house number 1. Fred is Andy's dog. Fred brings the newspaper to Andy every morning. Fred is a good, obedient and helpful dog. Sometimes Fred appears over the fence and startles Georgie the mouse! But it's all right, because Fred and Georgie have a conversation every morning. They are very good neighbours who look after each other. Jasper and Dave live at house number 2, next door to Andy and Fred. Jasper is very quiet and calm, whereas Dave is always running around with lots of energy, flapping his long ears and tongue, and chasing mice. That's why Georgie avoids Dave! Jazz and Dingle live at house number 3. Jazz is a very sleepy dog who can get grumpy, especially when younger Dingle is barking and being very active. Dingle yawns a lot because he chases cats and uses up his energy. Jazz prefers to sit down, wait and eat his food. Marigold and Daisy live at house number 4. Marigold is very patient, but Daisy is always searching for something to do, like playing with her ball. Marigold is older and wiser. Daisy has huge eyes and is waiting for something to happen, so she can investigate. Barry and Margaret live at house number 5. Barry adores butterflies and likes to catch them. Margaret likes to copy Barry a lot and follow him everywhere. They cannot be separated! Jasmine lives at house number 6. She has many friends in the neighbourhood and she likes playing outside with them. She enjoys feeding grass to the cows. She adores watching the baby deer leap and trot in the fields. Whenever she goes near them, they escape and run as fast as they can! Jasmine likes talking with the local frogs. They are full of knowledge and guidance. Whenever Jasmine gets the chance, she speaks to a frog about a problem, and the frog helps her with advice. Jasmine enjoys playing with the fish in the pond because they are lovable and energetic. The fish chase Jasmine around and avoid getting caught. Jasmine likes to hear the rat's stories while the elephant rests against the tree below. The elephant always accompanies the rat on its storytelling adventures. And best of all, Jasmine enjoys hanging upside down with the monkey in the tree. The monkey plays with Jasmine's hair as Jasmine tickles and throws apples at the monkey. The pair are very good friends. Jasmine knows it is important to get along with a wide range of beings, because variety brings greater understanding. Post-Reading Questions True or false? Jasmine got along with a wide range of beings. Who did Jasmine receive advice and guidance from? Re-read. Ask: Why does dingle yawn a lot? Re-read. Ask: What number house does Jasmine live at, and who does she feed? Re-read. Ask: What do the fish do to Jasmine? If you could have any animal, what would it be and why?
author: Hello English

title: Pretty Pink Polly
text: "Look, Mum!" said the little girl. "There's a beautiful bird in the tree. What is it?" "It's pretty pink Polly," said the mother. "Can we take her home?" said the little girl. "No," said the mother. "She doesn't belong inside." Story Description A little girl's mother explains to her why birds belong outside, and should not be kept indoors. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Slippers ﻿ ﻿sl-ip-pur-s ﻿ ﻿Birds don't wear slippers because their feet are too small. Migrate ﻿M-eye-gr-ate ﻿Birds migrate from north to south and back each year. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ Indoors ﻿in-d-or-s ﻿Certain creatures are not kept indoors because they belong outside. Snatched ﻿sn-a-ch-d ﻿They tried to snatch and steal the money. "Her wings are incredible, and her tail is so colourful," said the little girl. "Can we take her home, please?" "No," said the mother, laughing. "Polly enjoys flying. She belongs in the sky." "Where is Polly going?" said the little girl. "She's pointing with her wing," said the mother. "She's going to build a nest in the tree." "Can we take her home, please?" said the little girl. "No," said the mother. "Polly's home is in the tree." "Why is Polly taking us to the barn?" said the little girl. "She's built a nest here," said the mother. "But she already has one in the tree," said the little girl. "This is a spare one in case the tree nest falls out," said the mother. "Can we take her home, please?" "No, she has a home in the tree and in the barn." "Perhaps we can give these slippers to Polly," said the little girl. "Her feet must get cold at night." "They won't fit," the mother said, laughing. "And Polly doesn't need slippers. She has feet with claws." "Can we take her home, please?" "No, she wouldn't like living in the house." "Birds like to fly and soar through the air," said the mother. "They are free. They don't like being stuck indoors. Outside is their natural home." "Some birds migrate from north to south and back again. They travel around the world. They have all the space they need. The world is their playground." "Keeping a bird indoors would be like cutting off its wings. It would be bound and unhappy." "So we can't have Polly to keep?" said the little girl. "We should let her be outside?" "Yes," said the mother. "Where she is happy and always singing." "But I can still play with Polly, can't I?" said the little girl. "Of course!" said the mother. "Polly loves playing with you. But don't try to trap her." Because the little girl understood more about birds, Polly was happy to play with the little girl, knowing she would not be captured. The little girl learned that wonderful things should not be snatched and kept. They should be set free. Post-Reading Questions Where did the little girl want Polly to stay? The little girl learned that wonderful creatures must be f _ _ _. Re-read. Ask: Where is a bird's natural home? Re-read. Ask: Where do birds migrate? Re-read. Ask: Would a bird be happy if it was kept indoors? Name something else that doesn't belong indoors.
author: Hello English

title: Camel and Mantis Have Lemonade
text: Story Description After Camel and Mantis drink lemonade too quickly, they run out. A boy shows Camel and Mantis how to drink from glasses made for them, as he makes more lemonade. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Lemonade leh-mon-aid The glass of lemonade was cool and refreshing. Impatient Im-pay-sh-un-t The animals were impatient from waiting for their drinks. Solution sul-ew-sh-un The boy came up with a solution to the animals drinking too much lemonade. Savour say-v-er They drank slowly and savour ed the last of the lemonade. "That's the last of the lemonade gone," said Ram. "You two really need to cut down on how much you drink. I wanted a glass for myself but now we've run out, I'll have to make more." "It's good stuff, Ram," said Camel. "It's better than the shopkeeper's lemonade, because it contains real lemons," said Mantis. "You two have big stomachs," said Ram. "Where do you put all of it?" Ram got to work making fresh lemonade. Once it was ready, he poured some into a bowl. "It's ok to drink now, but go easy this time," said Ram. "Lemons are expensive. After this we'll be having grape juice." But Camel had already made a big mistake. Impatient to drink, he stuck his head into a narrow glass where the rest of the lemonade was being kept. "You've really done it now," said Mantis. "Ram is going to be annoyed." "I'm so thirsty," said Camel. "You have to help me get my head out." "With my arms?" said Mantis. "Oh, no!" said Ram. "What have you done this time, Camel?" "It was Mantis's idea," said Camel. "He told me to try it. I bet him that my head could just about fit inside." "It's my lemonade glass!" said Ram. Ram pulled with all of his strength and the lemonade squirted out, but Camel's head was still stuck inside the glass. Suddenly, his head came out of the glass with a big pop. Camel and Mantis went out. Later when they returned, they saw that Ram had made much more lemonade - enough to last them an entire week! "Should we sneak in?" said Camel. "It's a bit late for that with your big head," said Mantis. "If we behave ourselves, maybe we'll get a glass or two each." "Ugh," said Camel. "What's this?" "Looks like a magic mirror," said Mantis. "It must be a glass because it's so huge." "I don't want to drink from this," said Camel. "I need a trough or a big bowl." "I've come up with a solution," said Ram. "This big bowl is for Camel to drink from, and this tiny cup is for Mantis to drink from." "But it's not big enough for me to have a bath in my favourite drink," said Mantis. "You'll have to make do," said Ram. "I'll try the bowl," said Camel. "At least my head won't get stuck. But Mantis might get trapped in that tiny cup!" "No, I won't," said Mantis as Camel laughed. "Smaller portions from now on, you two," said Ram. "We're running low on lemons. Mantis, you still get a cup full. It's barely anything. Camel, I'm afraid you won't get as much. You're a big drinker. You do realise that you can carry water for months?" "I go to the toilet a lot," said Camel. "I go once a year," said Mantis. "Hurry up with the lemonade, Ram." "Something doesn't feel right," said Camel. "Bad stomach again?" asked Mantis. "No, this glass is too small. Either that or I have grown." "You're right," said Mantis. "I feel like a giant. There's a year's supply of lemonade in here for me." The two swapped cups and Ram watched them enjoying the lemonade. "What do you think, guys?" he said. "Delicious," said Camel, gulping down his bowl. "I'll savour this since I can't have another bowl." "Do you have any more?" said Mantis. "I'm nearly finished here." Camel grunted at Mantis. Post-Reading Questions What is the boy's main complaint about Camel and Mantis? The boy loves making lemonade. This can be described as one of the boy's pa_ _ions. Re-read. Ask: What happened when Camel got his head out of the glass? Re-read. Ask: How did the boy solve the problem of rationing the lemonade? Re-read. Ask: What mistake did Camel and Mantis make? Name something expensive that should not be wasted. (Think cars, trucks, etc.)
author: Hello English

title: The Food Chain
text: Story Description A comedy story of a frog, a snake and a mongoose having an unlucky day by the pond. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sensing sen-s-ing The frog was sensing danger. Capturing cap-ch-er-ing The mongoose was capturing the snake. Approaching a-pro-ch-ing The crocodile was fast approaching the animals. Escaping es-cay-p-ing The wasp was escaping from the frog. One day a frog was sitting on a lily pad planning to catch a wasp. "Got you!" it said, capturing a wasp. "Oh, dear," said the frog, sensing danger. "Bzzz, you're in trouble now," said the wasp. "Got you!" said a big snake, capturing the frog. "Uh oh," said the snake, sensing danger. "You're in trouble now, ribbit," said the frog. "Got you!" said a giant mongoose, capturing the snake. "Oh, man," said the mongoose. "You're in trouble now, thhththth," said the snake. A humongous eagle approached them with its outstretched claws......and it captured them in one big pile. "Whee!" said the wasp, escaping from the frog. The group was too heavy for the eagle to carry, and they slipped from its claws. The eagle let go of the mongoose......the mongoose let go of the snake......and the snake let go of the frog. They all fell and landed with a gigantic splash in the pond. "Hurray! We're saved!" they cried, not seeing the approaching crocodile, and the wasp laughed as it flew away. Post-Reading Questions What is the biggest animal in the chain? What was the first animal in the chain? Re-read pages 5-9. Ask: What happens to the animals as the chain gets longer? Re-read. Ask: What does the eagle do? Re-read. Ask: Where do the animals land? Do you think the crocodile ate the animals, or did the animals escape?
author: Hello English

title: My own soup recipe
text: Aryan was hungry for soup. He said to his mom, " Mom, let's make some soup! " "Oh, but we don't have all the soup ingredients at home", said his mom. Aryan got upset, he really wanted to have soup. Mom got an idea, " Hey, we can try and make soup with whatever we have at home. " " Hurray", Aryan shouted in excitement, " Let's do it!" They began hunting for soup items in fridge. "Mom, I found an egg, can it be put in soup?" he inquired. "Yes, ofcourse", said mum. "Oo Oo, I found some strawberries, can we add that in soup too? ", he asked. " I don't think so", laughed his mother. "I found some spring onion and tomato and carrots, would they be a good ingredient?", he hesitated. " Yes, and with a hint of butter, salt and pepper, I think we are good to go.", mom assured. Aryan's face was beaming happily, thinking that he picked a ingredients for his own soup. He was so proud. He helped his mother prepare the soup and lay down the table. When mom got the soup to the table, Aryan couldn't help sniffing up the aroma of their home made soup. "Ahaaa...! It smells so amazing", he exclaimed, " I wonder how will it taste like. " "Be careful, it's hot!", Mom carefully served them both the aromatic homemade soup. " It's the yummiest soup ever!", announced Aryan in excitement. His mom said, " The credit goes to you, you helped me find the ingredients of the soup." "No mum, it was teamwork, we did it together. " Aryan happily said.

title: Elephant had a wish
text: Once upon a time, there lived a small elephant in the forest. One day, it suddenly had a new wish. The elephant wanted to see shells of the egg it came out of! The elephant believed that, like chicken and other birds, elephants too come out of eggs! Elephant met a deer and asked for its advice. It asked the deer where can he see the egg shells! The deer was confused by elephant's question. So it said 'I don't know' and ran away. The elephant walked sadly and met a rabbit. Elephant told the rabbit about its wish and asked the same question. Rabbit asked the elephant to kneel down. The rabbit said 'I don't know'! Then it jumped past the elephant and hopped away. Elephant asked a puppy dog. The dog also didn't know. Elephant asked the king of the forest. The lion also said he didn't know. Then he asked Mr.Monkey. Mr.Monkey thought for a while. But he too didn't know. At the same time, a little girl called Geetha wandered into that forest. She was playing with her pet parrot. The parrot was flying first and Geetha came chasing it. Geetha was trying to catch the parrot, that was their game. Elephant saw the parrot flying towards it. So, it asked the parrot the same question. Parrot said that 'mammals* cannot lay eggs'. 'Is that so?' wondered the elephant.. *What are mammals? Ask your parents and find out! Elephant heard a laughing sound and turned around. Geetha was standing there. 'Why are you laughing?' asked the elephant. 'I was laughing, as you were wandering around the forest without knowing this. Okay! Now you have learned a new thing. Why don't you take me for a ride?' asked Geetha. The elephant was clear now. It offered Geetha a ride around the forest on its back. Geetha and the elephant went around the forest happily!
author: Vetri | வெற்றி

title: Dance Time
text: The queen bee ordered the worker bees to watch dancer Thain. Thain's dance moves were going to be the secret code for treasure hunt. The treasure was always flowers. Bees loved the nectar hidden deep inside them. This nectar was used to make the yummy-yummy honey. Thain took center stage. Thain turned left. Thain made one small circle. Thain waggled very little. The bees buzzed with good news. Thain had made a small circle and no waggle to her dance. This meant that the flowers were close by. Thain had given them a route to the Mango tree flowers. Soon, the worker bees brought back nectar from the Mango tree. The flowers were tiny but in millions. The next day the queen gave a new order. All eyes were to be on dancer Shehed's dance. Shehed was in the hub. She turned right and waggled. Shehed turned left and waggled. She danced in the shape of number eight. She waggled a lot. More circles and more waggle meant a longer route. Bees flew for a long time and came to a Ragi field. The Ragi flowers were ready for the bees. Bees carried nectar from Ragi flowers to make honey. Thain bee's life was good. Shehed bee's life was good. Sometimes, they danced for others. Sometimes, they watched new dances to grasp the address of new flowers and new fields. Bringing nectar to the hive was dance time for them. Honey making was super sweet for sure.
author: jaya rangan
illustrator: Biplob Chakroborty; Gita V. Reddy; Kishor Joshi; Maya  Ramaswamy; Natasha Sharma; Reshu Singh; Sheena Deviah; Tapas Guha; Try Samphos; Zainab Tambawalla; அகரன்

title: Boris the Vintage Bus
text: Story Description Boris is a very old bus that gives people a ride from the villages to the city. One day on a journey, Boris gets unwell and breaks down. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Struggled ﻿s-tru-gul-d ﻿Boris struggled around the corners and bends. Mechanic ﻿muh-can-ic ﻿When Boris broke down, a mechanic fixed him. Unwell ﻿un-we-l ﻿Boris felt unwell and broke down. Shiny sh-eye-nee ﻿ ﻿Once the mechanic fixed and cleaned Boris, he looked shiny and felt new. Boris was a vintage bus that took people from the villages to the city. Everybody loved riding in Boris, because he was big, clean, fast and smooth. One day Boris was going to the city when he struggled. He coughed out plumes of smoke over the long distance. Boris slowed around bends and got covered in mud. He felt unwell. By the time he reached the city, he was exhausted. He could not find anywhere to park, and when he did find a space, it was many hours later. Boris broke down, tired and drained of fuel. Some people took Boris to a mechanic who opened him up to look inside. His parts were very old. The mechanic replaced the old parts with new parts, and put Boris back together. Boris felt well again. The car wash cleaned Boris very well. He was looking shiny and new again. Soon Boris returned to the village, happy to be picking people up and dropping them off in the city. He felt like a brand new vehicle! Post-Reading Questions What was Boris's main job? When did Boris start having problems? Re-read. Ask: Did Boris find a parking space? Re-read. Ask: Were Boris's parts new? Re-read. Ask: What did the mechanic do for Boris? How old do you think Boris is?
author: Hello English

title: Three Kids and a Rocket
text: Story Description Julianna tells a story about how she, Annette and Gerry go into outer space, and encounter a black hole which they fly away from, leading them somewhere new. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sleepover sl-ee-po-v-ur The two girls were staying up and having a sleepover. Gaining g-ey-ning The black hole was gaining on them, getting very close. Dodged doh-j-d They somehow dodged the black hole and ended up on another world. Blasted b-la-st-id The rocket blasted off into space. Annette and Juliana were having a sleepover when they started telling stories. Juliana began a story about flying into space in a rocket. "We climbed into the rocket and blasted off into space. We travelled far, far away from the solar system." "What happened?" said Annette. "We encountered something big and strange. You and Gerry were terrified!" "What did we see?" said Annette. "There was a massive black hole!" said Juliana. "I decided we had to get to the nearest solar system!" said Juliana. "We raced through space but the black hole kept chasing us!" said Juliana. "Did we get away from it?" said Annette. "It kept gaining on us," said Juliana. "Gerry tried his best to fly the rocket but the black hole was sucking us in." "Gerry increased our speed but it was too late. We slipped towards the black hole." "That's horrible!" said Annette. "I checked the ship and alarms went off everywhere," said Juliana. "There was nothing we could do." "Did we fall into the black hole?" said Annette. "I took the controls and flew the rocket," said Juliana. "With my skills, I weaved and dodged the black hole, and we finally got away!" "You saved us!" said Annette. "And we were tired," said Juliana. "We had to rest. Then Gerry saw something coming close." "What was it?" said Annette. "A new world," said Juliana. "Was it survivable?" said Annette. "The air was clean," said Juliana. "The planet was dark. There were different trees and fields. There were many moons, and the houses looked strange." "Did we stay there?" said Annette. "We walked around and we realised it was Earth," said Juliana. "But somehow we had travelled into the future." "We were stuck there?" said Annette. "Yes, and we had to find our way back to our time. So we got back into the ship and flew away, and we went back the way we came..." Post-Reading Questions What object chased the rocket through space? Who steered the ship and took them away from danger? Re-read. Ask: Where did Juliana decide they should go? Re-read -13. Ask: ﻿Who rescued the ship from falling into the black hole? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What planet did the three realise they had landed on? ﻿Do you think they made it back to their time safely?
author: Hello English

title: THE RED CAR
text: Yesterday was the first time twenty two month old Kriya sat in the car seat facing front. She saw the red car in front and said 'red car venum.' (meaning she wanted that car) Appa asked her how will we get a red car. Little Kriya said 'Auntie money' meaning - We should give money to auntie and she will give us a red car. And, how does she know about the card? Kriya has seen Appa giving auntie a card and then taking the groceries. Another day, Kriya saw a card lying on the table and kept saying 'Money, Money!' At first Amma did not understand. Then, she knew Kriya was talking about the credit card...... Smart Kid, eh! Smart Kid!!

illustrator: Aindri C; Dorian  Dutrieux; Henu; Kabini  Amin; Snigdha Mishra; Tanvi Bhat

title: Monsters Under the Bed
text: Story Description Reggie tries to sleep when he hears monsters talking under his bed. Or are their voices coming from somewhere else? Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Monster moh-n-st-ur There was a monster under the bed. Racing r-ay-sing He had racing thoughts about the monsters eating him. Costume coss-ch-ew-m He put on his tiger costume and scared the monsters away. Thoughts th-or-t-s The monsters were just thoughts and were not real. "Sleep tight," said Reggie's mother, giving him a goodnight kiss. "Goodnight, Mum," said Reggie. Reggie heard voices coming from underneath his bed. "Is he asleep yet?" one said. "I don't think so," said another. "How many monsters are under my bed?" said Reggie. "None," said a voice. "One," said another. "I think we should eat him whole," said a voice. "We should carve him up and feed him to the other monsters," said another. Reggie got out of bed and looked under the mattress, but there was nothing there. He turned to the side and saw a pair of eyes looking at him. He felt terrified. "We'll wait until the kid is asleep," said a voice. "Then we'll gobble him up!" Reggie screamed when he heard the monster's voice. "Help! Monsters!" he cried. Reggie's mother came racing to the door. "What's wrong?" she said. "There are monsters under the bed planning to eat me!" said Reggie. "See?" said Reggie's mother. "There is nothing but your tiger costume. There are no monsters here. Maybe you are hearing things in your head." "Maybe," said Reggie, seeing there were no monsters under the bed. "Why don't you wear your tiger costume to bed?" said Reggie's mother. "That will scare the monsters." "Good idea," said Reggie. "That will keep me safe!" Reggie put on the tiger costume and got into bed. There were no more voices, because Reggie realised they were coming from his head. He was just having scary thoughts of monsters. For the rest of the night, Reggie slept very well. Post-Reading Questions ﻿What could Reggie hear under his bed? What were the monsters planning to do to Reggie? Re-read. Ask: ﻿ How many monsters were under the bed? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿When Reggie cried out, who came to his rescue? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿Where did the monster voices really come from? ﻿What sound does a tiger make? Would it scare monsters away?
author: Hello English

title: The Household Items
text: Story Description A bunch of household items can help you get ready for the day. Let's find out what they are! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Scissors ss-iz-zur-s A pair of scissors cuts your hair. Comb c-oa-m A comb makes your hair tidy. Clippers cli-p-ur A pair of clippers trims your nails. Ready red-ee Now you are dressed and ready. Getting washed and dressed can be very difficult. But don't worry! The household items are here to help! Scissors trims your hair to look tidy. Soap makes sure you are clean. Towel dries you out. Jumper helps you get dressed. Brush helps you clean your teeth. Comb makes your hair neat. Hat keeps your head warm. Bud cleans your ears. Yuck! Clipper cuts your nails short. Boots cover your feet. And when that's done, you're ready to go out! Post-Reading Questions Name as many items as you can remember from the story, that help you to get ready for the day. Which do you think is the most important item in the story? Which item makes your hair look neat and tidy? Which item keeps your head warm? Which item keeps your teeth clean? Which item helps you to walk outside?
author: Hello English

title: Chili Contest
text: Story Description Mrs. Hopper has never eaten a chilli before, but she enters a chilli eating competition to try winning a free ride on a new roller coaster. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Chillies ﻿ch-ill-ees ﻿ ﻿She won the contest by a clear 50 chillies. Competition ﻿com-per-t-ish-un ﻿The competition winner gets a free ride on the new roller coaster. Handle ﻿han-dul ﻿She knew how to handle eating chillies. Flattered ﻿fla-ter-d ﻿The monkey was flattered by her sharing. "I hear there's a chili eating competition at the funfair today," said Monkey. "The big prize is chocolate and a free ride on the new roller coaster!" "That sounds fun," said Mrs. Hopper. "We should enter." "Rather you than me," said Monkey. "I've never eaten chillies before," said Mrs. Hopper. "What are they like?" "They're extremely hot," said Monkey. "They will make your mouth burn." "Sounds like a challenge," said Mrs. Hopper. "Sign me up!" "Are you sure about this?" said Monkey. At the funfair, a group of animals stood around waiting to enter the contest and eat as many chillies as they possibly could. Mrs. Hopper and Monkey arrived, and Mrs. Hopper was eager to try the chillies! A cheetah could only manage to eat one chili before he burned up and tapped out of the contest. The chillies were too spicy and he started crying, sweating and gasping for water. The other animals laughed when they watched. But the animals could not handle more than two chillies. They collapsed into a pile before someone poured a jug of water over them. The elephant, hippo, tortoise and crocodile could not handle the burn or the heat. They too gave up. Next up was Mrs. Hopper to try and eat as many chillies as she could. She didn't stop eating them. The chillies seemed to have no effect. She did not sweat, cry, cough, or ask for water. "Mmm...delicious!" she said. "I should eat more of these." "Mrs. Hopper!" said Monkey in a panic. "What are you doing? Stop! That's too many." The competition judges declared Mrs. Hopper the winner by about 50 chillies. She ended up eating the entire bowl. Mrs. Hopper received her prize and shared it with Monkey, who was flattered. Then the two had a ride on the brand new roller coaster, which was a thrilling and scary experience! Post-Reading Questions Which animal could only handle one chilli before quitting? How many chillies did Mrs. Hopper win by? Re-read. Ask: How many chillies did the other animals eat? Re-read. Ask: What did Mrs. Hopper share with Monkey? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What was the prize that Mrs. Hopper won? What competition would you enter?
author: Hello English

title: The Starlight Adventure
text: Naina and Madhav couldn’t agree on what the moon was made of. “It’s an egg laid by an alien,” said Naina. “It’s a ball made of cheese,” said Madhav. So they decided to find out. “But we better get back in time for dinner,” Madhav said. “We don’t want to find out what Aai’s anger is made of.” It took them exactly eleven minutes to get lost. “Where’s the moon?” They asked a glowing unicorn for directions. “How come you’re so shiny?” “Do you know what the moon is made of?” “What are you made of?” The unicorn didn’t have time for their questions. Chomp! Crrunch! Gulp! “If I stop eating, I'll never turn into a gorgeous rhinoceros,” she said. Before Naina and Madhav could say anything else, they heard loud sobs in the distance. Waaaaaaah! Aiyeeeee! “WOE IS ME!” the new voice wailed. “Will I be trapped in here forever?” “Stop moaning!” growled another voice. “It sounds like somebody needs our help,” said Naina. “We can be heroes of the sky,” said Madhav. “Look out for the swan,” warned the unicorn, before going back to her food. Naina and Madhav found a surprising sight. An angry queen was guarding a locked tower. A weeping dragon peeked through the window. "Why have you kidnapped a dragon?” Naina asked the queen. "Because he is a no-good thief!” the queen snapped. "He stole my hair while I was sleeping and now he won’t give it back.” “I can’t get it back!” the dragon cried. “It’s too dangerous.” Naina’s eyes lit up. “Where there’s danger, there’s adventure.” “And every adventure needs a brave hero!” said Madhav. “Heroes, you mean,” said Naina. “We will rescue your hair!” The dragon agreed to tell them where the hair was. But he refused to go near it. “A giant fire-breathing dragon is afraid of a harmless swan.” Naina shook her head. “The swan probably doesn’t even know that the hair is stolen,” Madhav replied. “We should just ask him to return it,” Naina suggested. Things did not go according to plan. Hiss! Snort! Flap! The swan spread his wings and attacked the spaceship. Then he chased them across the sky. By the time they escaped the swan, Madhav and Naina’s stomachs were growling with hunger. They looked at the clock in the sky and gasped. “We’re late, we’re late!” Madhav said. They revved the engine of their spaceship. vooRRR! vooRRR! The engine sputtered and came to a halt. Vwomp! Pssssh! The siblings panicked. “We’re stuck!” “How do we get back home?” “Aai will be so angry!” “I’m so hungry!” They turned to the stars for help. The dragon had a blocked nose because of all the weeping. They couldn’t ride his flames home. The flying horse had sent his wings to the dry cleaner. He couldn’t fly them home. The strongest man in space had fractured his arm. He couldn’t throw them home. “We’re doomed!” But the dragon had another idea. The two children climbed aboard an arrow. The centaur took careful aim and shot them right to their front door. “ We never did find out what the moon is made of, ” said Madhav. “Who cares about that? I want to know what stars are made of!” said Naina, her eyes full of another adventure. 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 Meet the Star-Creatures 1. Monoceros – the unicorn 2. Draco – the dragon 3. Cassiopeia – the queen 4. Cygnus – the swan 5. Berenices’ Hair – the queen’s hair 6. Horologium – the clock 7. Pegasus – the flying horse 8. Hercules – the strong man 9. Sagittarius – the centaur Shapes in the Sky A constellation is a group of stars which forms an imaginary pattern when you look at the sky. These patterns are formed by the brightest stars in the sky. The patterns can be animals and objects, mythological people, gods and creatures, and scenes from ancient stories. In 1922, astronomers divided the sky into 88 constellations. Constellations are useful because they can help people recognise stars in the sky. In ancient times, people used constellations to help keep track of the calendar so that they knew when to plant and harvest crops. Sailors and travellers also used constellations as guides to help them find their way. If you’re looking for constellations and can’t find the images described in this book, don't worry! The stars don’t look exactly like the image you’re expecting to see. You might need a star map to spot the stars in the constellations.
author: Parinita Shetty

title: Monkey and the Rabbit
text: Story Description A monkey gets an injury and cannot walk around for long. He drops a bunch of bananas, but being injured, he cannot go to the ground and collect them. He asks for help from a rabbit, who helps him get the bananas back. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Injured in-j-er-d The monkey fell and injured himself. Trail tr-ay-ul There was a trail of banana skins. Pulley pu-lee The rabbit designed a pulley so the bananas could be lifted into the tree. Peacefully p-ee-ss-fu-lee The monkey was very tired and he slept peacefully. One day Monkey dropped his bunch of bananas far below on the ground. He had injured himself, and he wasn't able to climb down his tree to get them back. “Can you help me get the bananas?” said Monkey to some bees. “Sorry,” said the bees. “They are too heavy for us to lift.” “Can you help me get the bananas?” said Monkey to a snake. “I am injured and they are too far away for me to get.” “I can’t help a monkey,” said the snake. “You are too mischievous. You’ll play a trick on me.” Monkey tried to reach out for the bananas, but they were too far away. “That’s it!” said Monkey, getting an idea. “I have to find a way to lift them from the ground!” Monkey got to work studying and coming up with a plan, when suddenly a big gust of wind wrecked his home. Monkey’s notes blew away......and the wind damaged his seats. Monkey then saw something in the distance. There was a trail of banana skins. He saw there was a rabbit eating them! “Hey, rabbit!” Monkey called down. “I need your help!” Monkey explained his plan, and the rabbit helped him. They tied several vines together, and created a pulley system. The rabbit placed the bananas securely in a loop. “Now!” he said to Monkey, and Monkey lifted them up. “You’re the best, thank you,” said Monkey to the rabbit. “But I don’t know how to pay you back for this.” “No need,” said the rabbit. “I’m just happy to help you out!” And monkey slept peacefully, tired from his efforts. He clutched his bunch of bananas close, not allowing anyone near them. Soon his injury healed, and he could collect bananas again. Post-Reading Questions Why did Monkey ask for the rabbit's help? How did Monkey get the bananas back? Re-read pages 8-10. Ask: What happens to Monkey's planning? Re-read pages 11-12. Ask: What does Monkey see on the ground? Re-read pages 13-15. Ask: What act of kindness does the rabbit do? What do you think about the rabbit not wanting anything in return?
author: Hello English

title: Oh No! A Big Dog!
text: Story Description Three kittens try to escape from a dog that seems to be chasing after them. But what does the dog really want, and is he dangerous? Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Sniffed ﻿sn-if-d ﻿ ﻿The dog sniffed at the kittens, who felt scared. Chased ﻿ch-ay-s-d ﻿The kittens were being chased through the field. Plank ﻿pl-an-k ﻿The kittens arrived at a plank by the river. Further ﻿fur-th-ur ﻿ ﻿They could not go any further. A yellow, a brown and a white kitten were wandering through the fields, when they found a big dog in front of them. Suddenly the dog sniffed at them and the three kittens panicked! They ran as fast as they could away from the dog......and straight into a little boy holding a balloon! The brown kitten got up again and ran with the other kittens. Meanwhile the dog was very interested in the kittens and he chased them. The kittens looked behind them and saw the dog coming! The yellow kitten ran straight into a low flying bird! The kittens followed a lane and kept running. They were getting tired. They reached a river bank and found a little plank. But the plank was a dead end! They could not run any further! Then the dog arrived, and he carefully sniffed the kittens. They realised he just wanted to play. They calmed down. The dog and the kittens played and chased each other through the fields......and the big friendly dog gave them a lift home on his back. The kittens had nothing to be afraid of! Post-Reading Questions Why couldn't the kittens go further than the plank? What did the kittens realise after the dog sniffed at them? Re-read. Ask: What did the brown kitten crash into? Re-read. Ask: What did the yellow kitten crash into? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Did the kittens have anything to be afraid of? ﻿If you were a kitten, would you run away from a dog?
author: Hello English

title: Grandpa Rabbit's Umbrella
text: Story Description Grandpa Rabbit has lost his umbrella. Without looking properly, he assumes that it is somewhere in the house. Where could it possibly be? Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Washing w-osh-ing The rabbits were washing their clothes. Diving di-v-ing Grandpa was diving around looking for his umbrella. Bookshelf bu-k-sh-elf The rabbits searched the bookshelf and knocked over some books. Umbrella um-br-el-a The umbrella had mysteriously disappeared. There was a storm coming, and Grandpa Rabbit needed his umbrella to collect more carrots. "Where is my umbrella?" he said, going through the rabbit home and searching for it. "I'm sure it can't be far away." "Perhaps it is in the washing pile!" he said, diving into the basket. "Perhaps I put it in the food bag by mistake," he said, turning the bag upside down. "Flopsy," said Grandpa Rabbit. "I'll give you a carrot if you find my umbrella." "Ok!" said Flopsy. Grandpa Rabbit climbed the bookshelves and searched behind every book. The other rabbits looked on worried as Grandpa searched each book individually. "I don't think it's here," said Grandpa Rabbit. "Maybe I left it outside," he said, as Flopsy helped him. "Maybe it is hidden in the carrots or in storage," he said. "Well done, Flopsy!" said Grandpa Rabbit, as she took the umbrella off his back. "You get a carrot for finding it!" Grandpa opened the umbrella and went into the rain, waving the rabbits goodbye as he went in search of more carrots. And Flopsy sneaked along to help Grandpa. "Right, let's get some more carrots!" said Grandpa. "Now, where is my umbrella?" Post-Reading Questions The whole time, where actually was the umbrella? Who found the umbrella for Grandpa? Re-read. Ask: Where did Grandpa look first? Re-read. Ask: What did Grandpa offer to Flopsy if she found the umbrella? Re-read: Ask: Who sneaked along to go with Grandpa? Name something that you've lost and found before.
author: Hello English

title: Cheenti's Ant-Venture
text: Cheenti was a little ant that lived with her parents Keeda and Pipilika in a field full of wheat grains. They used to eat golden grains every day and sing: - “Grains are so good and grains are so yummy, I’ll sleep in the sun with my big fat tummy.” One day, Keeda and Pipilika had to go to visit their relatives in Ant-Hill. Cheenti stayed behind to play hide-and-seek with her friends. Meanwhile, Maindhak sat near a big stone, waiting for a chance to eat the ants with his long sticky tongue. As soon as Cheenti closed her eyes and began to count, Maindhak quietly stuck out his tongue and snapped up Cheenti. Before she could shout, she was sliding down the frog’s throat and fell straight into his tummy! Cheenti tried to climb back up, but could not. It was so dark inside, that she began to cry. Cheenti: Let me out! Let me out! Maindhak: Ants are so good, and ants are so yummy, I’ll sleep in the sun with my big fat tummy. Saying this, Maindhak fell asleep. As soon as he closed his eyes, he didn’t realise that the long snake Naga was waiting to catch him. Naga crawled up to him, opened his mouth wide and grabbed him. Suddenly Maindhak found himself sliding down a long dark tunnel. He was inside Naga’s tummy. He tried to hop out, but couldn’t. Maindhak: Uncle Naga, let me out! Let me out! Naga: Frogs are so good, and frogs are so yummy, I’ll sleep in the sun with my big fat tummy. Naga burped and slurped, then curled up into a ball and soon fell asleep. Meanwhile, Cheenti’s friends who had been hiding began to look for her. Finding her nowhere, they began to call out loudly. Ants: Cheenti, Cheenti, where are you? Cheenti heard their voices and shouted back. Cheenti: I’m here. Maindhak ate me up. Please help me. The ants heard her voice coming from Naga’s tummy. Ants: Surely Naga must have eaten up Maindhak. What shall we do? Quickly they ran to Ant-Hill to call Keeda Uncle, Pipilika Aunty and Makaura Mamu. Ants: Help, help! Maindhak has eaten up Cheenti. Makaura Mamu: Don’t worry. We shall soon free her. The ants led them to Naga. Makaura devised a plan. Makaura: Keeda and Pipilika, we will have to crawl into Naga’s nose and make him sneeze loudly. This would help to let out Maindhak. The same way we shall try to save Cheenti. At once, Makaura and Pipilika crawled into Naga’s nose. Naga felt a little tickle, then a big tickle, and then a very big tickle in his nose. He felt like sneezing a huge sneeze and opened his mouth so wide that the sun shone right inside up to his tummy. Maindhak’s eyes opened wide and he got his chance to escape. AAAAAACCCHHHHHOOOOOOO went Naga, and out popped Maindhak. Out popped Keeda and Pipilika too! He heaved a sigh of relief. Makauda, Keeda and Pipilika quickly crawled into Maindhak’s nose. Maindhak felt a little tickle, then a big tickle, and then a very big tickle in his nose. He felt like sneezing a huge sneeze and opened his mouth so wide that the sun shone right inside up to his tummy. Cheenti’s eyes opened wide and she got her chance to escape. AAAAAACCCHHHHHOOOOOOO went Maindhak, and out popped Cheenti. Out popped Keeda and Pipilika too! Maindhak jumped into the water. Cheenti hugged her mummy, papa, and mamu. All the ants clapped with joy to see Cheenti safe.
author: Arunima Aggarwal
illustrator: Anam Fathima; Gita V. Reddy; Mayukh Gosh; Naina bhardwaj; Partho Sengupta; Steven McKimmie; Vinayak Varma; Vongsavanh Damlongsouk; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: The Butterfly Park
text: Story Description A girl explores a butterfly park and encounters butterflies of different varieties. She learns about how they change from being a caterpillar. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Migrate my-gr-ate Butterflies migrate each year to different places. Cocoon cu-coo-n The butterfly comes out of its cocoon home. Grateful gr-ate-ful Be grateful and appreciate butterflies. Respect ris-pec-t Don't try to capture them. Treat them with respect. "Welcome to the butterfly park," said Mrs. Imran. "Let's see what varieties of butterfly we can find!" "Butterflies migrate from place to place every year." "They travel in groups for protection. Before, a butterfly is a caterpillar. Yes, those little bugs with many legs that eat leaves! It forms a cocoon and stays protected inside as it changes into a butterfly. Then it hatches." "Some butterflies are yellow. Some are speckled or have many colours. This is to warn predators that they are poisonous to eat." "If you keep very still, then butterflies will come close. They are attracted to flowers of bright colours." "Look, there's a rare green one! Don't try to catch it!" "Keep very still, because it's sitting on your head!" "In certain areas, butterfly populations are decreasing. There are less butterflies there. In some places you will find many butterflies." "So when you see a butterfly, and it lands on you, be grateful, and treat it with respect. Don't try to catch it, but let it go." Post-Reading Questions Name two things butterflies should be treated with. What do butterflies do each year? Re-read. Ask: What is a butterfly before? Re-read. Ask: What are butterflies attracted to? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Should you leave rare green butterflies alone? ﻿What is the difference between a caterpillar and a butterfly?
author: Hello English

title: The Cicada's Song
text: Story Description A cicada teaches a catchy tune to some birds and animals, and after the song spreads around, everyone knows the tune! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Wilderness Wil-dur-nu-ss The cicada wandered through the wilderness, singing its song. Tune Ch-ew-n The cicada's song was a catchy tune. Lyrics Lih-ri-k-s Very soon everyone knew the song lyrics and sang the words. Singing S-ing-ing Everyone went to the river singing the song. One day a cicada came up with a catchy song. He started singing and the song sounded great. The cicada wandered through the wilderness singing his song loud enough for everyone to hear. He encountered a bigger cicada who changed the song to make it sound better. The little cicada was amazed. The cicada practiced his tune again. It had improved! "I'm going to teach everyone our song!" said the cicada as he continued on his way. The cicada found a bird with a giant beak. He sang the song and the bird loved it. The bird learned the tune and the lyrics. Very soon the bird and the cicada were both singing the song. The cicada found a bird with a big orange beak. He sang the song to the bird, and the bird joined in. They both stood on a branch singing across the fields. "Thank you, little one," said the bird to the cicada. "You've just made my day fantastic." The birds passed on the song and the lyrics to a frog and a duck. The four sang together. Very soon, the birds, a duck, a frog and the two cicadas wandered along a path, singing the song. They sang all the way to the river. A good song catches on. Post-Reading Questions Who helps the cicada write his song so it sounds better? Who is the first bird that the cicada teaches the song to? Re-read. Ask: Where did the cicada and the bird sing? Re-read. Ask: What did the bird say to the cicada? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Who did the birds pass the song on to? How do you think the cicada's sounded? Do an impression.
author: Hello English

title: Little Hands Make A Big Difference
text: It was the month of October, and Walnut the tree was happy to be laden with ripe walnuts. Brownie, the little squirrel was happy too! He could eat as many walnuts as he wished to. Brownie even made a nest for himself in the tree. He began to live there. Kai-Kai the black crow also loved the walnuts. He too, made a nest in the tree. As the month of October passed, Walnut began to worry that the walnuts would soon be finished and Brownie would not have anything to eat in winters. Walnut: Do you know that I will not be able to make more walnuts until next year? What will you eat in the winters? Brownie: Oh! Dear Walnut, you have been so kind to me. You have given me food and shelter. You are also worried about me for the winters. I shall make a small den in the ground and bury some walnuts in it. I can use them in the winters. Brownie ran down and began to dig the ground. Kai-Kai helped him by throwing some walnuts down. Brownie picked them up and stored them away for the winter. Brownie: Thank you, Kai-Kai, for helping me. Kai-Kai: You are welcome! Soon the winter months set in and there was snow all around. Brownie was safe and happy as he had plenty to eat. Brownie: Dear Walnut, how can I be of some help to you? Walnut: You have already helped me by burying many walnuts in the ground. Some of them will grow into trees when Spring season sets in. This way I will have many more friends next year. The forest will grow thicker each year. Thank you, Brownie, by helping me to spread my seeds. Your tiny hands will make a huge difference. Brownie: Thank you, Walnut! Kai-Kai: Plants help birds and animals by giving them food and shelter. Birds and animals help them by spreading their seeds to grow more plants. Cows eat grass and make the soil rich with their dung. This helps plants to grow healthy and strong. Kai-Kai: Flowers help bees by giving them nectar to drink. Bees help the flowers to make fruits. Birds and animals give out carbon dioxide, which is used by plants. Plants give out oxygen which is used by us. Depending on one another for living and growing is called interdependence.
author: Arunima Aggarwal
illustrator: Herminder Ohri; Prabha  Mallya; Prashant Soni; Sanjay Sarkar; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Red Butterfly
text: There was a beautiful red butterfly who loved to flaunt her lovely wings the whole day. But her beauty made her so arrogant that she ignored all other creatures around her.She did not try to make any friends as she thought nobody is as pretty as her. One day a group of school children came for a picnic to the garden where the red butterfly was living. The children were enjoying the sight of colourful butterflies flying from one flower to another. The red butterfly got a chance to attract the crowd with her beauty. She about to spread her wings suddenly a naughty girl caught her with her wings.She tried to fly but Finally she escaped from the girl's hands but alas! The red butterfly lost her wings. She crawled on the ground helplessly. She looked up in the sky and painfully saw the other butterflies flying beneath the bright blue sky.
author: smitha k
illustrator: Lavanya  Naidu; Mahbubur  Rahman; Sabyasachi Hazra

title: Bubbles!
text: Story Description A boy and a girl see a man blowing bubbles in the street, and they learn how to make bubbles at home with soap and water. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Bubbles bub-ul-s Soap and water mixed together can make bubbles. Popped poh-p-d After a while, the bubbles popped. Surfaces sur-fi-ss-es The surfaces of the bubbles had soap rolling around. Wobble woh-b-ul The bubbles wobbled in the air. Raj and his sister Mara were on the school bus, when they saw a man blowing bubbles out of a cup. They thought it was really fun. Once home from school, Raj and Mara told their neighbour what they saw. "Oh, it's very easy to make bubbles," she said. "Mum, can we make bubbles?" said Mara. "Really big ones?" said Raj. "After dinner, I'll show you how," said their mother. "We have to mix soap and water," said Mara. "I'll make the loops for the bubbles," said Raj. Raj tested the loops he had made, and they worked! He was blowing bubbles! "Hurray!" cried Mara. "Let me have a go!" Raj created different shapes of loops for the bubbles - circles, triangles and squares. They blew different shapes into the air! Raj watched the bubbles rise and wobble. Mara saw the soap move over their surfaces. "Now we can make really big bubbles!" said Raj, moving a gigantic hoop through the air. "Perhaps we can be inside the bubbles?" said Mara. Mara blew a giant bubble and got stuck inside. Then Raj blew a giant bubble and floated upwards. And the dog blew a giant bubble and wondered what he had done. The three floated around until their bubbles popped. "That was great fun!" said Raj. "Let's do it again!" Post-Reading Questions Who made the children want to blow bubbles? Who taught them how to make the bubbles? Re-read. Ask: What shapes did Raj and Mara make? Re-read. Ask: What did Mara notice about the bubbles? Re-read. Ask: ﻿ Who else apart from Raj and Mara made a giant bubble? ﻿ What two ingredients are needed to make bubbles?
author: Hello English

title: The Wind Current
text: Story Description A girl goes on a walk when she encounters an unusual magical wind current that lifts her up into the air. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Breezy br-easy The wind was breezy and strong. Scurrying s-cuh-ree-ying The squirrels were scurrying up the trees. Overlooking oh-vur-luck-ing I found a hill overlooking my house. Windstorm wind-st-orm A sudden windstorm picked me up off the ground. It was a breezy day when I was walking through the forest. It was so windy that the trees were losing their leaves, and they were blowing all around in the air. I could barely stand up as I walked through the wind. Suddenly I felt that I was not alone. There was movement around me. There was scurrying and nibbling. As I walked through the trees, I saw squirrels. Then they were climbing on my shoulders, on my head and through my hair. The wind carried me on a current through the air, and a few of the squirrels travelled with me. We moved up and down and from side to side until the wind settled. The wind dropped us on a high hill overlooking my house. I knew I would be late getting home, because the walk down to the ground would take a long time. Luckily, one of the squirrels stayed with me. The squirrel hid inside my hair as I began the long walk all the way home. Along the way I told stories to the squirrel about the tall trees I had climbed, and the many windstorms I had encountered. After a while I could feel the squirrel snoring in my hair. I stopped when I saw the full moon in the sky, and I realised that I was lost. It took me a long time to find the house. When I got home I knocked on the door. "Hello, mother," I said. "Where have you been and what time do you call this?" she said. She was very angry and upset. She had worried so much about me going missing. "Don't do this again," she said, and I apologised. Just then the wind picked up some leaves and gathered speed. I kept the little squirrel, who stayed in the trees around our garden, collecting leaves and eating nuts. Occasionally it travelled home on a wind current to see its friends, and then it would always return home to me. Post-Reading Questions Where did the squirrels climb? Did any squirrels follow the girl home? Re-read. Ask: Why was the girl worried? Re-read. Ask: Where did the squirrel hide? Re-read. Ask: How did the mother feel about her daughter going missing? Imagine being carried by the wind. Where would you land?
author: Hello English

title: Crow's Partner
text: Story Description Crow loses his partner from the tree and searches for her. But the strange thing is, she might just be a lot closer to home than Crow realises. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics perch pur-ch The crow stood waiting on its perch. waited way-tid The crow waited throughout the day. feathers fe-th-urs He thought of her golden feathers. realised r ee-al-eyes-d The crow's partner realised something. Crow rested on his perch, wondering where his partner was. She had been gone for ages. "I wonder where she could be," he said to the tree. "Maybe she got lost," said the tree. "No, she's not lost," said Crow. He kept waiting for her to turn up. It was getting late, and he was very worried. "Have you seen my partner?" he said to some bees. "No sign of her, Crow," said the bees. "Just be patient." The day moved on and Crow waited and waited......a rainstorm came and went......and Crow lost his patience. He flew out of the tree and decided to search for her. He circled the region, searching for her golden brown feathers, but he saw no other birds except for crows. He saw a happy family working the fields, which reminded him of her......and he saw a family relaxing and eating, which is what he and his partner did each day. Feeling sad, Crow gave up and flew back to the tree......where his partner almost flew into him! "Where have you been?" said Crow. "I've been worried sick!" "I was sitting by the nest waiting for you to come back, then I realised I was in the wrong tree!" Crow was relieved to have his partner back, and whenever she flew away again, he would shout out and give her a signal so she wouldn't get lost. Post-Reading Questions Where did Crow find his partner? What funny mistake did Crow's partner make? Re-read. Ask: What advice do the bees give to Crow? Re-read. Ask: What feature does Crow look for? Re-read pages 12-13. Ask: Why did Crow feel sad? Do you think Crow should have waited longer? Did he do the right thing?
author: Hello English

title: The Scavenger Hunt
text: Lajjo lives in a village on the banks of the River Kosi. She loves the rain. But this year, the rains have been especially heavy. Lajjo is happy when the rain finally stops. Then all of a sudden, the banks of the river break. In just a few minutes, the village is flooded with muddy water from the river. Lajjo is scared. “We have to leave at once!” cries Babu. “Hurry, Lajjo! We need to get to higher ground where we’ll be safer.” Lajjo and her family wade through the water with great difficulty. With the help of some army men, they reach a hill where their neighbours have moved to. “Oh, no! I left Gudiya behind,” cries Lajjo. She never goes anywhere without her doll! But Babu says that they can’t go back until things are better. The next morning, Lajjo asks if she can go find Gudiya. This time, Mai yells at her. “Lajjo, our home is under five feet of water. We are running out of drinking water, and all you care about is a doll.” “Don’t worry, Lajjo. Gudiya will be fine,” says Daadu. “Shall we play a game?” “A game!” says Lajjo, brightening up. “Yes! It’s a scavenger hunt. You have to find all the items on this list. As soon as you do, I will show you something amazing.” Lajjo looks at Daadu’s list. “I’ll start searching right away,” she says, jumping with excitement. 1. 1 bucket 2. 1 cotton cloth 3. Gravel 4. Sand 5. 1 hammer 6. 1 hole punch Lajjo runs first to Mai. “What is it, Lajjo?” asks Mai, sounding tired. “If you are thirsty, I don’t have any drinking water.” “No Mai, Babu gave me a sip of water. I need a cotton cloth. Do you have one?” Mai doesn’t have a spare cloth. So she cuts a piece from her cotton sari. “Here! Take this.” Lajjo gives Mai a big hug. Babu helps Lajjo find a bucket. She fills it with sand. “Yay! Three things off my list!” “Lajjo, I’m thirsty. Do you have some water?” asks her friend Prateek. “Sorry, Prateek. We finished all our water.” “That’s okay,” he says. “Are you looking for something?” “ I’m looking for gravel,” says Lajjo. “There! You can use that.” Only two more things for Lajjo to find! Then Lajjo goes to find the village carpenter. “Fixer Baba, Fixer Baba, may I borrow your hammer and hole punch?” “What is it for, Lajjo?” “It’s for a game I’m playing with Daadu,” she says. “A game! Who has time for games when the whole village is thirsty?” Though he grumbles a little, he gives the tools to Lajjo. Lajjo lays out all the items in front of Daadu. “Done!” she says proudly. Daadu smiles and turns the bucket over. He makes a hole in it with the hammer and punch. Lajjo watches eagerly as he places the cotton cloth at the bottom of the bucket. Then, he pours fine sand over the cloth into the bucket. “Lajjo, will you help me fill the bucket with gravel?” asks Daadu. Lajjo helps Daadu pick out all the tiny stones, and put them in the bucket. They then fill the bucket with larger stones. Daadu takes a bottle filled with muddy river water and pours it into the bucket. “Why did you do that?” Lajjo asks, puzzled. Daadu just smiles. Not long after, clear water starts dripping down from the hole in the bucket. Daadu collects it in a glass. “Lajjo, we made a filter that changes muddy water into clean water,” says Daadu. “Go give this glass of water to your Mai and Babu.” Mai and Babu are overjoyed! They boil the water and drink it. Soon Prateek, Fixer Baba, Mai and Babu surround the bucket. “Great work, Lajjo!” they cheer. The next day, the army comes in boats laden with supplies for the flood survivors. Lajjo’s family is relieved. And in their boat is a special surprise for Lajjo! Make Your Own Water Filter Materials Needed: - 1 plastic bottle - 1 pair of scissors - 1 clean cotton cloth - Sand - Gravel (fine and coarse) What to Do Use a pair of scissors to cut off the bottom of the water bottle. Punch a small hole in the bottle cap with the pair of scissors. Stuff the bottom of the bottle with a cotton cloth. Pour fine sand into the bottle till the mark. Fill the bottle with fine gravel till the mark, followed by coarse gravel till the mark. Pour water slowly from the top. You will find clean water dripping down from the bottom. Note: Boil the water before drinking it in order to kill harmful germs.
author: Ajit Narra

title: Weight!
text: Story Description A girl learns how to balance weight, through games in school using balloons and scales. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Weight ﻿w-ai-t ﻿I used some scales to measure my weight. I was heavy. Difference ﻿Dif-ur-unce ﻿The difference between the weights was big. Scales ﻿S-cay-ul-s ﻿We used scales to balance weights. Balloons ﻿Ber-l-oo-n-s ﻿We blew up balloons during the experiment. Our school teacher Mrs. Patel told us about an experiment with weight. We were going to use a box and balloons in our example. I took a balloon from school and went with my mum to the doctor's surgery. I weighed the balloon on the scales and it was very light. I got my younger sister to drop a box and the shopping bags on top of me. The box was light but the shopping bags were heavy! I felt the difference in weight. The next day at school, Sajid and I blew up balloons. He knew how to do it properly, but I kept blowing too much air into mine! Mrs. Patel showed us how to balance weight. We placed some balloons on the scale opposite pieces of clay pot, and when the scales levelled we knew they weighed about the same. We began popping balloons one by one, until the scales tipped and the other side was heavier! This showed us how to decrease weight gradually. I stood on the class scales holding a net of balloons. Mrs. Patel popped some balloons and I felt the weight go down. We checked the scales and the weight decreased as all of the balloons popped. As a class, we had so much fun, and now I know how to use scales! Post-Reading Questions What are scales used for? What is heavier? A balloon or a pot? Re-read. Ask: What is Mrs. Patel doing? Re-read. Ask: What happens when the children pop the balloons? Re-read. Ask: What happens to the weight when Mrs. Patel pops the balloons? Why is weight important?
author: Hello English

title: Sandra's Big Red Balloon
text: Story Description Sandra loses her balloon on a lake and needs help to get it back. She finds a fish who is willing to help her get the balloon. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Accidentally ak-si-den-ter-lee She accidentally let go of her balloon. Carefully c-air-fer-lee She walked carefully into the lake. Towards tuh-war-d-s The fish swam towards the balloon. Branch br-an-ch She used a tree branch to poke the balloon. Sandra was walking close to the lake, when she accidentally let go of her big red balloon. The balloon landed in the lake and she needed help getting it back. She asked a man to help her. "I'm sorry I can't help you," he said. "I cannot swim!" Sandra went to the lake and trod carefully, making her way towards the balloon. But suddenly the water got very deep. Sandra felt afraid. She turned back before the water got any deeper. She went to the tree by the lake and snapped off a branch. Then she went to the water's edge and tried reaching for the balloon. But the branch was far too short. Sandra was crying and feeling upset, when a little fish rose to the surface. "I'll help you get your balloon," said the little fish. The little fish swam to the balloon but could not reach it. So it blew as hard as it could. But the balloon would not move. The little fish went to find a bigger fish, and it surfaced by the lake. It saw Sandra crying. "Don't worry," said the big fish. "I'll help you get your balloon. Climb on my back!" The big fish took Sandra across the lake. Sandra reached and got the balloon, and the big fish took her back to the bank. "Thank you so much!" she said to the big fish. She walked home, happy to have her big red balloon again. Post-Reading Questions Why would the man not help the girl to get her balloon? How did the big fish help the girl? Re-read. Ask: Why did the girl snap a branch off the tree? Re-read. Ask: What did the little fish do to help the girl? Re-read pages 13-15. Ask: How did the big fish help the girl to get her balloon back? Why is it important to ask for help?
author: Hello English

title: Hare and Tortoise
text: Story Description Lion sends Hare and Tortoise off together to find more food in another land. Hare and Tortoise, despite their differences, must learn to work as a team. Pre-Read Vocabulary and Phonics Detective de-tec-tiv Hare and Tortoise were two great detective s. Accomplish a-com-pl-ish They could accomplish any task while working together. Arguing ar-g-yew-ing They disagreed and were arguing all of the time. Pleased p-lee-z-d Lion was very pleased and happy with their work. Hare and Tortoise were Lion's two best detectives. "We need carrots and greens," said Lion. "I want you two to go out and find a new patch of land where they grow." "Work together this time!" said Lion. "We will," they said. Lion knew that even though they argued, Hare and Tortoise were friends. When they were a good team, they could accomplish any task. "I have an idea," said Hare. "I'll go on your back and you carry me across the water." "How about you hop and carry me on your back?" said Tortoise. "Because I always do the most difficult work," said Hare. "I'm always carrying you places," said Tortoise. "What are you doing?" said Tortoise. "Eating some carrots," said Hare. "I found them so I get to eat them." "You should share your carrots," said Tortoise. "I get hungry too." "Let's stop arguing," said Hare. "We need to find this land. Where do you imagine it is?" "Across the sea where the big rocks are," said Tortoise. "Where the beach is?" said Hare. "Yes, there are big fields there," said Tortoise. Suddenly they heard music coming from across the sea. "Are you thinking what I'm thinking?" said Tortoise. "I hope so," said Hare. "I'll swim across and you sit on my back," said Tortoise. They made it across the sea, past the beach and the rocks, and found the source of the music. There was a farm in a field growing carrots and green vegetables, and the farmhouse was playing its radio. "I wonder where they are?" said Lion, getting worried. "Those two work well when they are a team, but they always argue over petty things. I hope I can trust them." A short while later, Hare and Tortoise returned and told Lion about the farm they had found. This was great news because now they had a bigger food supply. All of the animals were relieved because they would not go hungry, all thanks to Hare and Tortoise's teamwork, and Lion was very pleased. Post-Reading Questions ﻿What does Lion order Hare and Tortoise to look for? Despite their differences, what can Hare and Tortoise do? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What are Hare and Tortoise arguing about? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What do Hare and Tortoise both see? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why is Lion so pleased with Hare and Tortoise's work? ﻿ Why is it important to work well in a team?

title: Rabbit's Kite
text: Story Description Rabbit lets go of his kite and it gets stuck in a tree. The villagers come together to help Rabbit get his kite back. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Snapped sn-app-d The line snapped and the kite flew away. Chased ch-ay-s-d The rabbit chased after the floating kite. Falling f-all-ing The kite began falling in the wind. Favourite f-ay-vor-ut The kite was Rabbit's favourite toy. Rabbit was playing with his kite when he let go of the line. The kite flew away. A boy and a girl saw Rabbit's kite stuck in a tree. They tried to pull it free. Unfortunately the line snapped and the kite flew out of the tree. A bird saw the kite fly from the tree and chased after it. The bird tried to peck and grab hold of the kite, snapping the line again. Rabbit saw the kite falling from the sky. He couldn't believe his luck! There it was! But he was too slow. He could not catch the kite. Rabbit cried, looking at the remains of his kite. It was his favourite toy. Rabbit's Mum picked up the kite and told Rabbit not to worry. She could fix it. The very next day, Rabbit hopped to his Mum and said thank you for fixing his kite. He was so happy! He ran through the fields, playing with his kite, promising not to let go of the line again. Post-Reading Questions ﻿ How did Rabbit lose his kite? Why did Rabbit get upset? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What happened to the kite? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Rabbit's mother do? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why was Rabbit so happy? ﻿What is your favourite toy?

text: Anu was sitting with her friends in her classroom. miss leela was teac hing their c lass M iss leela is writing something on the blac kboard. But the blac kboard looks blurry. title: The Note Less Travelled
text: …small hand almost touching 3 and big hand at 4 spaces before 12…sooo 4 minutes before 3, Sangram counted in his head while staring at the big clock that hung just outside the classroom window, next to the shiny school bell. It was a hot sleepy Friday afternoon and he couldn’t wait to go home. But just when he was going to start packing his things slowly under the table, he heard Ma’am clap her hands for attention. He looked up to hear her say, “I have some exciting news for everybody!” It must be something big for her to stop from teaching till the bell rang. “It is our class’ turn to host the special Monday assembly and I thought we just had to do a talent show! I hope to see everyone from my favourite class performing something or the other” she finished with a smile. The bell rang right on the dot and instead of everyone squishing out the doors like normal, his classmates were all buzzing around in groups with their friends discussing what they should perform. Sangram was just as excited but he already knew what he was going to pick for his talent. I’m going to sing for everybody, just like my Baba, he thought with a smile on his face. He had time and again watched his father in awe as he sang and played the piano in big big malls. Sangram knew his Baba must be a big star and couldn’t wait to be just like him. He was pushed out of his daydream by a poke in the back and he turned around to see Kaushik, one of the other boys from class 5-B standing behind him. “What are YOU going to do for the talent show Sangram? Have a tea party with your dolls?” he laughed. The other two boys behind Kaushik laughed along with him. Kaushik had seen one of his dolls in his school bag and had teased him about it since then. Sangram had felt very embarrassed about it. He had stopped bringing them after Kaushik made fun of him that first time. Sangram tried to change the subject quickly- “Actually I’m going to sing a song!” Kaushik only started laughing more “Ha! What a girly thing to do, you should just start wearing a pinafore to school and plait your hair, you girl.” Sangram pushed past Kaushik and his friends, tears falling down his face and his bag still wide open, to go run onto his bus. Sangram started becoming more and more angry, this was all his mother’s fault, she only got him that doll and made him start singing. Kaushik would not have made fun of him if he didn’t do those things. He slammed the door shut when he reached home, fully planning on running to his room. “Is that you Sangram?” his mother called out from the kitchen. “ Come help me cook while Saurabh dada takes care of your sister.” On hearing this, Sangram became angrier. “No! I don’t want to cook! And I don’t want to play with my sister or sing, those are girly things and I’m a boy!” he shouted at her. “Sangram! Don’t you dare speak to your mother that way! What on earth has happened to you?” She looked so angry at him, she never looked this angry at him. He couldn’t make anyone happy these days. He simply couldn’t hold it in anymore, all the sadness came back and he started crying looking at his mother. Next thing he knew he was on the sofa and she was hugging him, shushing him as he continued to cry. Finally, he slowed down. “Okay now tell me babu, did something happen in school today?” she asked him, continuing to pat his back. “My classmates make fun of me Aai! They call me a girl” he cried out. “They say I shouldn’t be playing with dolls or singing, why did you get me that doll Aai! This is all your fault.” He couldn’t help adding in the end. “Shush now! You’re the one who also wanted one when I got one for your sister, what’s wrong with playing with your doll? You love Rani! and you love cooking! Why Ajji just loved the sheera you made the other day.” “But it’s wrong, I’m a boy and those are girl things!” Sangram just didn’t know how he could continue doing those things, he must stop cooking and singing and playing with dolls. Whatever would he do to have fun now? His mother just continued to look at his sad face. “Hmm okay. Tell me this. Do they make you happy?” “Yes but-“ “Are you hurting anyone doing it?” “No, but it makes them upset and- “ “Sangram by singing and playing with your dolls are you hurting anyone?” “No.” His mother continued that same mother stare. “But it makes them upset and it’s so difficult and I’m a boy so I shouldn’t!” Aai is not able to understand! I want to cook, play with my dolls and sing. But it makes me feel so bad when Kaushik makes fun of me. How can I bear that? “What if I told you, that when I wanted to start working as an accountant, my father said no? He said girls shouldn’t be working, they should be at home? And you know how much I love my work! And my working is not hurting anyone, so should I have stopped?” “Ajoba was angry?” “Look Sangram, people get angry all the time for many different things, many times things that should not upset them, it is not their business. You just got angry with me, should I stop what I am doing? Listen to you?” Sangram just continued to stare. His mother sighed and settled into the sofa, “okay” she said in a whisper, “I’m going to tell you a secret now.” Leaning towards Aai “what is it!” Sangram whispered back excitedly. “Those things people said to you, people have said to your Baba too” Sangram was shocked, he couldn’t imagine anyone saying these things to his baba. His mother just nodded knowingly, “Yes I’m not lying. So just because people made fun should he stop singing?” She asked. “No! I love his singing!” came the immediate response. There could not be a world without his baba singing. His mother just looked at him pointedly again. Sangram sighed and leaned back into the sofa as well. “But why do people make fun of me? It makes it so difficult!” “That babu, is a million- rupee question. Many different things, but you don’t need to worry about that, that is for them to understand on their own, you focus on doing what you love and being whoever you want, does it matter if these things make you a boy or a girl if it makes you happy?” She didn’t wait for an answer she just gave him one last hug and continued onto the kitchen. “Don’t think this excuses you from your chores mister.” Sangram hurried behind her with a smile on his face. After Sangram finished helping her clean up, he turned to her and said-“There’s this talent show we’re having on Monday, I thought I would sing? Should I still do it Aai?” She smiled and looked at him, “What do you think hmm?” Filled with new hope, he ran to his father who was in the middle of his own practice. Sangram waited for Baba to notice him and then quietly asked, “Baba, will you teach me a song for my talent show?” “Sure Sangram!” Baba smiled, pulling Sangram onto his lap. They practiced for the show all weekend, and Sangram felt himself getting better with his father’s help. Every time he sang, he forgot about Kaushik and the other mean boys from his class and he felt happy. He still couldn’t help but worry about having to face his class again on Monday. Sunday night before their practice, Sangram hesitantly mentioned to his father, “Baba, people in my class make fun of me. They know I love to sing and they tease me for it, why do they do this? How can I sing in front of them?” Hearing this, Baba put his hand on Sangram’s head and said, “Babu, there will always be people who will make fun. You have to be strong and continue to do the things that make you happy. If you love singing, you should do it with all your heart. If you let other people hurt you then you will never be able to do what you enjoy.” Keeping this in mind, Sangram went to bed only a little nervous but mostly excited about the next morning’s talent show. On Monday morning, Sangram woke up extra early and put on his best ironed uniform. It was a special day, especially because Baba decided to walk with him to school. Before going inside, baba knelt down to Sangram and said, “Remember what I told you yesterday? Now, don’t worry about the boys who made fun of you or the prize you might get if you win. When you go on stage, close your eyes, think of how much you love singing and just do it with all your heart. Aai, me and your brother and sister are here with you no matter what.” The time of the talent show finally arrived and Sangram suddenly heard his name being called out by Ashwini Ma’am. He rushed up to the stage but not before noticing the boys point and laugh at him. But, he remembered his Baba’s words, his Aai’s words. I need to fight for what I love! Sangram reminded himself. So he closed his eyes and just sang. When he opened his eyes after finishing the song, he couldn’t believe it! All his classmates and teachers were clapping and cheering for him, even Kaushik. At the end of the day, to his surprise, Ashwini Ma’am announced him as the winner and he was awarded a big shiny trophy to the cheering of his classmates. More important for him was that, that was the day Sangram went home not only with a trophy and friends but a smile that reminded him to always believe in himself and fight for the things he loved in life. WOW! He's so good!
