title: Sloth Climbs to the Top
text: Story Description Sloth tries to climb to the top of a tree before he falls asleep again. On his way up, he encounters several creatures that keep waking him up. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Already all-re-dee The sloth had already made it half way up the tree. Climbing cl-eye-m-ing The sloth kept climbing the tree. Sleepy s-lee-pea He was feeling very tired and sleepy. Squeezed s-kw-ee-z-d The sloth squeezed the snake. When Sloth woke up, he was already very tired. "It'll only be an hour before I sleep again," he said to himself. "I need to sleep somewhere safe," he said. "I know! I'll climb to the top of this tree." Sloth climbed the tree trunk and he felt his eyelids getting heavy. He was about to fall asleep. Suddenly a giraffe started licking him and it helped him stay awake. Sloth kept climbing and felt sleepy again. Suddenly a cluster of bees from a hive attacked him and he woke up. Sloth climbed and felt sleepy once more. Suddenly a snake tried to bite him, but Sloth squeezed its neck before it could get to him. Sloth was so tired he felt he could sleep while climbing. He prepared to take his rest. But a bird started calling and it woke him up. "Finally, some rest," said Sloth, happy that he had climbed all the way to the top of the tree. Sloth had gone past the giraffe, the bees, the snake and the bird......but only in his dreams. Sloth made it to the middle of the tree, where he fell asleep. Post-Reading Questions What was Sloth's mission? What creatures stopped Sloth from getting any sleep? Re-read. Ask: How long is it until Sloth falls asleep? Re-read. Ask: What awoke Sloth from his sleep? Re-read. Ask: Did Sloth really make it to the top of the tree? Name something that stops you from getting to sleep.
author: Hello English

title: Harriet the Hip Hippo
text: Story Description Harriet performes a dance and hopes to get other animals moving too. Just when it appears that nobody is joining in, she gets a surprise. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Hippo ﻿hip-oe ﻿The hip hippo loved to dance. Cricket ﻿cr-ik-it ﻿The funny cricket enjoyed joining in. Donkey ﻿don-kee ﻿The donkey wanted to dance, but couldn't. Meerkat ﻿m-ear-cat ﻿The meerkat was curious about the dance. Harriet was a hip hippo who loved to dance. She didn't always get her moves right. Because of her flat feet, she would slip over! The cricket watched her with delight, copying her moves. He liked the hand patterns she made. Harriet danced underwater. She moved her arms along the surface and her feet on the river bed. As Harriet dried off on the land, the cricket danced around her, getting drenched in water. Harriet tried stomping and swinging her arms. The sleeping snake watched Harriet sway and he moved his body like her. He could meander and zig zag. Harriet lifted her arms and legs, and the cricket danced with her. The donkey saw Harriet and wanted to join in, but he was carrying too much water, and if he dared to dance, his buckets would spill everywhere. Harriet practiced standing on one leg. The bird saw what Harriet was doing and tried standing on one leg, but it was too difficult for her. Finally Harriet stopped dancing because she felt alone. She did not see anyone else dancing. It made her upset that nobody shared her joy. But the meerkats had seen her dancing and had been inspired to make their own cool moves. And Harriet was amazed when all of the animals turned up, following her by dancing. Harriet felt happy again, and every day the other animals joined in together and danced along. Post-Reading Questions Who was the first creature to dance with Harriet? Which creature danced like Harriet? Re-read. Ask: What happened to the cricket as Harriet dried off? Re-read. Ask: Why couldn't the donkey dance along? Re-read. Ask: What was Harriet's big surprise? Do you enjoy dancing?
author: Hello English

title: One-Legged Monsters
text: Story Description Annie gets woken in the night to find three one-legged monsters in her room making noises, and she follows them into the next room. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿One-legged ﻿one-leg-id There were three one-legged monsters running around. Playfully ﻿play-fu-lee ﻿The monsters ran away playfully. Clanging ﻿cl-ang-ing ﻿There was a clanging noise coming from the drawer. Volumes ﻿ ﻿vol-y-oom-s ﻿ ﻿Big volumes of books fell from the shelf. Annie was sleeping in her bed when all of a sudden there was a loud bang. The noise stopped and Annie opened her eyes. Thinking nothing of it, she went back to sleep. Then came another large and loud bang that woke Annie up. "What was that?" she wondered. Suddenly three one-legged creatures - one pink, one orange and one green, began dancing and laughing in her room. Annie got up and the monsters saw her. They ran to the door and looked at her. Annie smiled at them and the monsters hid playfully. Annie got out of bed and went to the door. She watched the pink monster going through the cutlery draw, making clanging sounds. The green monster climbed on the bookshelf and threw big volumes of books on the floor. Then the pink monster began singing with a spoon, pretending it was a microphone. The green monster began reading a book to his friends, while they listened. The green monster laughed at the story he had read. The orange and pink monsters joined in the laughter. The story was hysterical. The green monster read more stories, the pink monster sang loudly, and the orange monster danced and stomped his feet. Annie looked on, enjoying the monsters having fun, until she was tired and she went back to bed. Post-Reading Questions What kind of noise woke Annie up in the night? What did the pink monster pretend the spoon was? Re-read. Ask: What did the monsters do when they saw Annie? Re-read. Ask: What did the green monster throw? Re-read. Ask: The pink monster sang and the green monster read. What about the orange monster? Think of a monster. What colour is it? What does it do?
author: Hello English

title: Trip to the Playground!
text: Story Description A girl goes to the playground and plays on all of the rides. Then she makes a new friend on the see-saw. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Slide ﻿s-l-eye-d ﻿The slide goes all the way down. Tricky ﻿tr-ik-ee ﻿It is tricky to go across the bars. Roundabout ﻿r-ow-n-dur-bao-t ﻿The roundabout makes me feel dizzy and funny. Building ﻿﻿ bill-ding ﻿I am building a castle in the sandpit. I love the park! There are so many fun rides! First I'll go on the slide! I'll climb the tricky steps to the top......then I'll slide all the way down! Yippee! Mama will take a picture of me on the roundabout going around and around. I'd better hold on! Building castles in the sandpit, I've made a new friend! The see-saw is fun but I need someone to join me! My friend joins me and I go all the way up! Mama takes a picture of me and my new friend having a great time! I play on the jungle gym, going across the bars and hanging upside down! After the sand pit, the slide, the bars, the see-saw and the roundabout......it's time to wave goodbye to my new friend and go home! Thank you for taking me to the park, Mama! Post-Reading Questions What ride does the little girl go on first? Where is the girl and her new friend in the photograph? Re-read. Ask: What does the girl need to do on the roundabout? Re-read. Ask: What can the girl do on the jungle gym? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What ﻿phrase ﻿does the girl use? What is your favourite ride at the playground?
author: Hello English

title: The Sneaky Hyena
text: Story Description A hyena comes up with a plan to eat a bird, but he needs help from another bird to catch his dinner. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Hyena ﻿hi-yee-na ﻿The hyena had a funny laugh. Cape ﻿cay-p ﻿He wore a cape made of feathers. Feathers ﻿feh-thur-s ﻿The feathers came off the cape. Smashed ﻿sm-ash-d ﻿The hyena smashed into the ground, but he was all right. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ The hyena was walking the desert when he saw a tasty black bird on a branch. He knew the bird would see him and fly away, so the hyena came up with a plan to win his dinner. The hyena asked another bird to help him fly. The bird thought the hyena was crazy. "I'm serious," said the hyena. "I need to catch my food." "But you'll hit the ground," said the bird. "You can't fly." "I have a plan," said the hyena. "Don't worry about me. I'll be fine." Later the hyena returned wearing a cape of feathers. "See? I'll simply float to the ground!" he said. "This looks dangerous," said the bird. "But if you really want to fly, I can lift you into the air." "Let's do this!" said the hyena, impatient to get up high. The bird lifted the hyena off the ground, and the hyena saw his target bird below. But the hyena was too heavy to carry, and his cape of feathers fell off. The bird let the hyena go, and the hyena aimed for the target bird, ready to eat it. The hyena saw his food look up, and it flew away. "Oh, no!" said the hyena......and he smashed into the ground. Post-Reading Questions What does the hyena wear when carried by the bird? Does the hyena get his dinner? What happens? Re-read. Ask: What does the bird say to the hyena? Re-read. Ask: What does the hyena carry? Re-read. Ask: ﻿When the bird sees the hyena, what does it do? ﻿ Do you think the hyena would have caught the bird, if his cape didn't break?
author: Hello English

title: Ram and Rodge
text: Story Description A hyena comes up with a plan to eat a bird, but he needs help from another bird to catch his dinner. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sighed s-eye-d The boy sighed because dogs were not allowed there. Soothing s-oo-th-ing The sunshine and the heat was warm and soothing. Spectacular sp-ek-ta-k-yew-lur The view of the beach and the sea was better than good. It was spectacular. Retrieve re-tr-ee-v The boy threw a stick and the dog retrieve d it. "Let's play, Rodge," said Ram to his dog. They kicked the ball around the house together. "If you want to play, go outside," said Ram's mother. "Playing indoors is too dangerous. You'll break something valuable." "All right," said Ram. "Come on, Rodge. Let's go outside and play!" Ram and Rodge played with the ball in the street, when a man came over to them. "Be quiet," said the man. "You are both being noisy. Play somewhere else." "All right," sighed Ram. "Come on, Rodge. We'll go to the park and play!" Ram and Rodge sat in the park watching the people and looking at the plants. A man came over to Ram. "Dogs are not allowed in the park," said the man. "The sign says so. You'll have to leave." "All right," sighed Ram. "Come on, Rodge. Let's try playing on the beach!" Ram and Rodge loved the beach. The waves were high and there was a soothing cool breeze. It was a spectacular day. Ram and Rodge ran and chased one another on the sand until they were tired. Ram threw the ball for Rodge, who jumped into the sea to collect it. "Be careful of the waves!" said Rodge, as Ram went underwater to retrieve the ball. "Rodge! Where are you? Oh, no!" But everything was fine. Rodge surfaced and ran to Ram with the ball in his mouth, and he dropped it at Ram's feet. "You're a good dog," said Ram. Post-Reading Questions Where were Ram and Rodge finally allowed to play? What did Rodge do when Ram threw the ball into the sea? Re-read. Ask: Why is it too dangerous to play in the house? Re-read. Ask: Why couldn't Ram and Rodge play in the street? Re-read. Ask: Why did Ram and Rodge love going to the beach? If you had a pet dog, where would you play?
author: Hello English

title: Bob the Blob
text: Story Description Bob is Natasha's secret. He is a big friendly blob who can change shape and turn into things big and small. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Transform ﻿tr-ans-for-m ﻿ ﻿Bob the Blob could transform into many things. Imagination ﻿ ﻿e-maj-in-ay-sh-un ﻿Bob could turn into something from Natasha's imagination. Hideous ﻿hid-ee-uh-ss ﻿He could be a hideous monster or a friendly creature. Secretly ﻿see-c-rut-lee ﻿Bob secretly hid in Natasha's school bag. Natasha kept a secret. There was something strange that lived in her house. Natasha owned a blob that could change shape and turn into many things. Natasha named the blob, 'Bob'. Natasha made paper planes which didn't fly. But Bob would help out. He could transform himself into a windy blob, and he could make the planes cruise in the air. Natasha would ask Bob to take the shape of her imagination. Bob could listen in and focus, and he could show Natasha the images in her mind. She saw gingerbread men! Natasha asked Bob to turn into different creatures - some nice and some hideous! Bob turned into a rain puddle and a big purple fluffy ball with legs. Whenever Natasha's mother was around, Bob would hide in Natasha's school bag. When she went away, Bob changed shape and became very thin and small, showing himself secretly. Natasha went outside and looked at the night sky. She saw stars across the city. Bob turned into a giant display of coloured lights, adding lots of colour to the sky. One night, Natasha saw Bob was waiting under her bed. She asked what was wrong. Bob admitted that he was terrified of the cat, because it would try to play with him. Natasha couldn't believe that, of all the things Bob could be afraid of, he was terrified of a small cat! But when the cat fell asleep, usually when Natasha was drawing or colouring in, Bob showed himself and slept beside them. And every night when Natasha went to bed, Bob cuddled Natasha until she fell asleep. Post-Reading Questions What can Bob the blob transform into? What is Bob scared of more than anything else? Re-read. Ask: What does Bob the blob turn into? Re-read. Ask: When Natasha's mother is around, where does Bob hide? Re-read. Ask: When does the cat fall asleep? What would you make Bob the blob transform into?
author: Hello English

title: The Body Builders
text: Vava’s sister, Chinnu, is growing fast. When he first met her at the hospital, Chinnu was small and hairless. Vava was terrified to hold her because she was soft and looked like a pink worm. Now she has black hair, just like him. Her nose is round and snub, just like Ammamma’s* nose! And her eyes are the same colour as Amma’s, and Amma’s sister Banu Chitta’s.** *grandmother in Malayalam **mother’s sister in Malayalam “It’s amazing,” Vava tells Banu Chitta, whose stomach is looking more and more like a big, hard egg these days. “At first, Chinnu was just a speck in Amma’s stomach, like the baby in your tummy. Now Chinnu looks a little like all of us!” Chitta says, “What do you think this one will look like?” When Amma was pregnant with Chinnu, she had explained that Chinnu was taking her time to grow in Amma’s belly. She would come out only when she was strong, and ready to meet the world. “Chitta, your bump is smaller than Amma’s was when Chinnu was inside her. Are you sure there’s a baby in there?” “Haha, very sure,” Chitta says. “This baby is still a very small combination of cells. But it is hard at work in there. All the cells are dividing and multiplying. Slowly, they will form groups of cells that will become eyes and ears and all the other organs.” “Ah! I know what a cell is,” says Vava. He leans out of the window to grab a pomegranate from a tree. “If this fruit is like an organ, then each seed is like a cell!” he says. Vava knows that a cell is the smallest and most basic unit of life in the body— not just in his body, but in every organism. “Yes, Vava, cells are the building blocks that make up all living things,” says Chitta. “But if all living things are made of cells,” Vava says, “then a cell could become anything, right? My new cousin could be a panda!” Chitta laughs. “Then, we’ll call the baby Panda Anda!” “I don’t want Panda Anda!” Vava says, stomping his feet. “Cells are smart, Vava,” Chitta says. “Each cell carries information about the job it will do and what it will become. This information is called DNA or deoxyribonucleic acid.” “What does DNA look like?” asks Vava. “DNA is like a spiral ladder, and it has two strands which look something like noodles,” says Chitta. “It contains a set of instructions called genes that comes from both parents.” This reminds Vava of the noodles he saw in the kitchen. “So I got these genes from Amma?” asks Vava, holding up two strands of noodles playfully. “Half Amma and half Appa. One set of genes from Amma and one set from Appa,” says Banu Chitta. “So Panda Anda would be a panda if his or her parents were pandas. Instead the baby has me for a mother and your uncle for a father,” explains Banu Chitta. “So that’s how a cell knows what it is! It is in the DNA!” Vava says. “But how does Panda Anda know how to make skin and hair and eyes and fingers?” asks Vava. “Inside all our cells is a blueprint,” Chitta explains. “You remember the architect had shared a blueprint of this house with your mother when it was being built?” “Oh, yes,” Vava says. “That is how we knew where the windows, doors, walls and the roof would go.” “Our DNA is like this blueprint. It tells our cells where to go and when to start building,” says Chitta. “As each cell divides and multiplies, the gene instructs it to become an eye, a finger or a pair of lungs.” “So each living being is really like a house that’s building itself,” Vava says. “That’s amazing.” “It is,” Chitta agrees. “And it keeps building and repairing itself for the rest of our lives. That’s why you are growing so tall!” “I don’t have to do anything to grow,” Vava says, giggling. “My DNA is doing it for me.” “Well, you have to treat it nicely,” Chitta says. “Eat well, sleep well and give your body the right amount of work. Then it will do its job easily and efficiently.” “I will, I promise!” says Vava. TRIVIA SNAP Do you know how many cells are there in an average human body? Scientists say there are about 37.2 trillion. Cells are very, very small and can only be seen under a microscope. If every cell in your hand was the size of a grain of sand, your hand would be the size of a school bus. MAKE YOUR FAMILY TREE Draw your family. Try to find features you or your parents or siblings might have received from someone in the family tree. Does your brother’s crazy hair come from Uncle Prithvi in Nagpur or Aunty Binbin in Palampur? Does your cousin get her dimple from her grandmother?
author: Supriya Nair

title: CHILD TALK
text: Hari comes to me to learn Hindi. He is a student of Class III. He does not like to write. Often, his work is untidy, so, I make him redo it neatly. One evening, he was preparing for his test. He still had a lot of answers to do. Quite tired, he just sat there and refused to write. I was firm and said, 'No bargaining, Hari. You have to complete it all and then leave.' Immediately, he said, 'Bargaining! only in Maths.' Sandya, another student was also there. Both of us laughed aloud. Hari thought we were making fun of him. 'Really! in Maths I have studied,' he replied innocently. I made him understand that I was not making fun of him. He just sat there without saying anything. Then, Sandya said, 'Auntie is not teasing you, she is happy with what you said.' He gave a wide-eyed look and started writing quickly. He completed his work before his Mother came to pick him up. What do you think of this story? Do you like to read books? When do you read books? Why books do you like to read?

title: Rama's tiffin box
text: It is lunch time, Rama's favorite time at school. Rama is feeling hungry. She opens her tiffin box. Rama opens it to find it empty. Oh no! Amma has forgotten to pack her tiffin in her tiffin box. Rama is hungry but she has not brought any lunch. What will she do now? She says to her friend Nitin, " I have not brought my tiffin and I am very hungry." "Don't worry.",says Nitin,"I will share my tiffin with you". Nitin asks his other friends, "Rama has not brought her tiffin today. Shall we all share our tiffin with her?" "Yes", say all their friends. Rajan has brought idli. Neeru has brought Rajma chawal. Nitin has brought sandwiches. They all share their tiffin with Rama happily. Rama is not hungry anymore. She is very happy. "Thank you all for sharing your tiffin with me. I am so happy to have good friends like you", said Rama to her friends. Her friends are very happy too.

title: THE WORLD NEEDS TO KNOW
text: THE WORLD NEEDS TO KNOW Everybody thinks that humans are really smart and talented. But have you ever thought that humans are the only living beings who kill their own people. Well, black ants don't kill black ants. Red ants may sometimes kill black ants but only because they want the red ants want their population to be more than the black ants. Humans kill each other which helps the animals by their increase in population. If animals population increases then maybe they will kill us. I say if we stop the war and killing, then hopefully everything will be balanced and every body can live in peace. But now, humans are not so smart after all!!!

title: Welcome Home, Baby!
text: Veena is playing with her father. She is very happy and wants to enjoy her time with her father. Her father is happy as well and wants to spend time with her. Her mother is bringing her a baby sister home. Her grandparents and parents, and of course, Veena are happy and all smiles. "Time flies," says her grandmother. "Looks like you were born just now. You have a baby sister now." The next day, her mother is busy with the little baby. Veena pulls her mother's shawl and troubles her. The baby is all bubbles with saliva, 1 crying. Veena seeks attention! Grandma comes to the rescue 2 of Veena's mom. Grandma tells stories to Veena and makes the baby sit on Veena's lap. Veena is happy. The little kitten 3 is also a part of their family. The baby is also happy. "Clap, clap!" sings Veena as she claps her hands. "It is time for your sister's nap," says her mom. Veena continues on a joyous tone, "Clap, clap, nap on mom's lap!" She then proceeds 4 to a nearby shop with Grandpa and their kitten. Veena calls out "Meena, Radhika, Mala, Janaki, Deepika, Priyanka, Vaidehi....Oh, I am out of breath 5!" These are the names Veena has suggested for her little sister. The family finally picks up "Vaidehi" as both Veena and Vaidehi begin with the letter "V". The naming function went on well and now everybody in Veena's family call out in a harmonious 6 tone, "Vaidehi! Vaidehi! Welcome the newest member of our family, Vaidehi!" 1: Saliva: watery liquid secreted into the mouth by glands, providing lubrication for chewing and swallowing, and aiding digestion. 2: Rescue: save (someone) from a dangerous or distressing situation. 3: Kitten: a young cat. 4: Proceeds: to move or go forward or onward 5: Breath: the air taken into or expelled from the lungs. 6: Harmonious: forming a pleasing or consistent whole
author: Brindha Vinodh

title: The Fox and the Cheese
text: He saw a girl drawing water from the well. she used a rope that had buckets tied at both ends. so when one bucket comes up the other would go down. she filled water and went home The fox was thirsty. He in to the well. He saw a piece of cheese in the well. He was very happy. He wanted to reach the bottom of the well. He got into the bucket and reached the bottom. Alas!There was no cheese. it was the reflection of the moon. He drank some water. He looked at the sky and began to howl. A wolf was passing by. He heard the noise and walked up to the well. He saw the fox inside and asked "What are you doing The fox replied:"Here is a big piece of cheese. I am eating it. its really tasty. If you want some cheese,do join me". The wolf was greedy and foolish. He quickly jumped into the other bucket. The wolf was quite heavy. As the wolf reached the bottom' the fox came up. The fox escaped.

title: Monkey the Prankster
text: Story Description A lion seeks advice from a monkey on how to be more human. The monkey gives the lion some strange advice. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Noble ﻿no-bul ﻿The lion is a noble king. Advisor ﻿ad-v-eye-zur ﻿The monkey was the lion's personal advisor and friend. Moustache ﻿muss-t-ash ﻿The lion thought he had a moustache of whiskers. Tricked ﻿t-rik-d ﻿The monkey tricked the lion into thinking he was human. The lion was the proudest and bravest animal in the kingdom. He commanded respect, he was noble, and he was caring. But there was one thing he wanted more than anything else. "I'm not human," he said to Mindy. "You can't actually be human, but you can pretend to be human," said Mindy. "I'm crossing my arms," said the lion. "Do I look human enough now?" The lion went for a walk and he found a monkey practicing some stretches. "Are you a wise monkey?" said the lion. "The wisest of all monkeys, I am," said the monkey. "Are you seeking advice?" "Yes. I am a king," said the lion. "Can you teach me to be more human in my behaviour?" "As you wish," said the monkey. "I can help you to become more human." The lion and his monkey advisor went for a walk and saw some humans playing. "They talk like they have lots of money," said the lion. "Is that the way I should talk?" "Your majesty," said the monkey. "You should talk like them. Hold your head high, like that of a man who is well respected. Then you will be more human. And wear flowers on your bottom. All good kings do that too." "Hello," said the lion to Mindy and Chris as they were out playing. "Charmed to see you both. What a pleasant day." "You're acting strange, lion," said Mindy. "Be more relaxed," said Chris. "So I shouldn't act this way?" said the lion. "No, just be normal," said Mindy. "And don't wear flowers on your bottom." The lion felt confused. "Look!" said the lion, riding an elephant. "Only a king rides giant beasts." "Oh my, your majesty," said the monkey advisor. "You really do look like a king. But there is something you are missing to be human." "A haircut," said the lion. "No," said the monkey advisor. "You should go and see how the humans ride an elephant to understand." The lion saw a group of humans with an elephant. There was a very important person riding on the elephant, and he was sitting inside a little shelter. "That's it! I need a shelter of my own and I'll be just like a human!" said the lion. "Then I can wear a fitting red robe, and then I will be a human!" The lion rode on the elephant and passed his monkey advisor. "It's a great shelter," said the monkey advisor. "Does it make me too much of a cat? I despise those tiny cats. They are not worthy! I am the king!" "You look wonderful, your majesty," said the monkey. "You are certainly the greatest human. Oh! I forgot you were a lion!" The lion was so pleased that the monkey had mistaken him for a human. "Elephant, do you like my human moustache?" said the lion. "They are just whiskers," said the elephant. "Yes, but they are human whiskers." "If you say so," said the elephant. "Greetings, fellow human sister and inferior cat!" said the lion. "There is a glorious day ahead of us!" "Why are you talking like that?" said Mindy. "Did you drink from the lake again?" "I'm a human now," said the lion. "My monkey advisor said so." "You are a lion," said Mindy. "And this is a cat, your close relative." "So I'm not human?" said the lion. "I'm sorry," said Mindy. "You never will be a human. You are a lion. Don't try to be someone that you are not." The lion apologised to the cat, then he told some jokes and they both laughed together. "Looks like that monkey has been tricking me," said the lion. "Yes," said Mindy. "In fact, the monkey is not really an advisor, or a wise one. This morning he was caught stealing prata from our neighbours." "What?" said the lion. "He's actually a pransker. He tricked you into looking silly with flowers on your bottom." "Oh, no," said the lion. "Always be careful who you take advice from," said Mindy. "And remember to accept yourself as you are." Post-Reading Questions What is an advisor? What did the monkey tell the lion to wear on his bottom? Re-read. Ask: What did the elephant arrive riding on? Re-read. Ask: What was the lion sitting inside? Re-read. Ask: What did the monkey turn out to be? What do you think is the message of the story?
author: Hello English

title: Ride on the Magic Tuk-Tuk
text: Story Description A man called Gerald owns a magical tuk-tuk. He gives a ride to an old woman and her cat, taking them high over the city to their destination. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Ordinary or-din-air-ee The vehicle looked like any normal, ordinary tuk-tuk. Appreciation a-p-ree-she-ay-sh-un The tuk-tuk showed its appreciation by beeping its horn. Unpredictable un-pre-dic-tur-bul The city people were unpredictable and ran across the road. Outmanoeuvre out-man-oo-vur Gerald tried to outmanoeuvre the other cars and buses. Gerald owns a tuk-tuk. But it is no ordinary automobile. This little beast is a gem. It is one of a kind. Gerald takes extra good care of it, because he knows how special it is. Gerald cleans the tuk-tuk each day, wondering what kind of passengers he will have during the day. Will they be famous? Will they be rich? Will they give him a satisfying tip? Gerald pulls up and collects an old woman and her black cat. The old woman asks for a ride into the city. "Sure, come aboard," says Gerald with a friendly, welcoming smile, taking her fare. The tuk-tuk gives out a little toot in appreciation, and they drive off. But Gerald and the tuk-tuk secretly dislike the city... In the city it is a few degrees higher than usual. There is heat. There is humidity. There is pain, toil and sweat, and all of the other vehicles are impatient and hot, creating a tense, swelling atmosphere. Gerald wishes he was outside of the city, driving along the safer country lanes. Driving the tuk-tuk through the city is painful and tiring! Not to mention the noise and the unpredictable people running across the road! Then there are the other tuk-tuks all weaving and turning. Gerald has to guess where they are going, and he takes his tuk-tuk skidding in all directions, trying to avoid them, to outsmart them and outmanoeuvre them. Gerald thinks about his special tuk-tuk's secret power, and he wonders whether or not he should use it. Gerald flicks a switch and immediately he and his tuk-tuk feel relief and happiness. They spring into the air and rise above the queues of vehicles that are all beeping impatiently. But Gerald can get where he wants to go faster, and more reliably, thanks to his impressive magical tuk-tuk's power. They look down on the other vehicles as they roam freely. The tuk-tuk plays its magical horn and beeps its trumpets loudly as they soar across the sky. "This is wonderful," says the old woman. "I never paid for this kind of service. How does the magic work?" "I made a promise not to tell anyone," says Gerald. "But you will tell me later, won't you?" says the old lady. "I'm a man of my word," says Gerald with a wink. With one special magical twist of the Godly elephant's trunk, the tuk-tuk becomes empowered and embalmed in pure energy. Gerald, the old woman and the cat yelp in surprise as their tuk-tuk turns into a giant tuk-tuk train, hundreds of carriages in length! Suddenly everyone in the city riding a tuk-tuk finds themselves on the tuk-tuk train. Where are they? Where are they going? What is this train? As quick as it comes, the train disappears, as does the elephant God's magical power, and Gerald finds himself soaring once again through the open skies, in his single tuk-tuk, wobbling through the turbulent clouds. The passengers in the other tuk-tuks return to the land at their destinations. That was quick! How did that happen? Did they just see an elephant? Did they fly? "Where did we go?" says Gerald, and the old woman and the cat feel perplexed. The tuk-tuk suddenly activates an invisibility cloak, and it springs helicopter blades! Now they move at speed as the tuk-tuk beeps its musical horns through the sky! "There's our stop!" says Gerald, passing the church, the ancient city walls, the intersections and the sports stadium. "I can see our home from up here!" says the old woman to her cat. The tuk-tuk lands and slots carefully back into traffic travelling in random directions. Gerald feels relieved that the journey takes only a few minutes. After all, being stuck in that dense transportation line could have caused them to wait for hours! Gerald stops at the stadium and a crowd cheers, having seen the tuk-tuk's magic. "Thank you for a wonderful ride!" says the old woman. "You're welcome," says Gerald. "Any time you need a tuk-tuk, call my number and I'll be there in a few minutes to collect you!" "You said you would tell me the secret of how the tuk-tuk works," says the old lady. "Yes," says Gerald. "But I'm a man of my word and I always keep a secret!" Post-Reading Questions Describe the powers of the magical tuk-tuk. What does the magical tuk-tuk transform into while flying? Re-read. Ask: Why doesn't Gerald enjoy driving through the city? Re-read page9. Ask: What does the tuk-tuk play as they soar through the sky? Re-read. Ask: Why wouldn't Gerald tell the old woman the secret of the tuk-tuk? If you could have a magical vehicle, what would it be? What powers would it have?
author: Hello English

title: Three Little Pigs
text: One morning one of the three little pigs went out to buy bread,jam and fruits.The other two little pigs stayed at home and played with their toys. They had lots of toys. Wooden frogs, tin soldiers and racing cars made of cardboard colored red,yellow,blue and green.They played and played until they felt hungry.They began to search the cupboard to find something to eat. "Look what I have found!" shouted one of the pigs,and hung a piece of something before the other's nose and dangled it. "A piece of roasted chicken!"cried the other pig."I want to have a little bit of it too!" "Wait till I taste it and find that it is good to eat",cried the pig who was holding it and took it away from the other and began nibbling it. "Tastes awesome!"he said and gobbled. Soon he ate all up and the little pig who was watching him began to cry,"Wee,wee wee,I did not get any roasted chicken and am feeling hungry." "Wee,wee, wee!"he went on crying.Soon the eldest pig returned from market, and was angry with his brothers for being greedy.He had saved the roasted chicken,for Winter was coming,and there would be snowfall.So he gave them no bread and jam and fruits. ﻿
author: Joysree Das
illustrator: Ella Clark; Josh Morgan; Phùng  Nguyên Quang; Youm Kosal

title: Earthquake!
text: Story Description An earthquake strikes and a family takes cover. The boy, Billy, tells a tale about what causes an earthquake. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Mischievous miss-ch-ee-vu-ss The spirits inside the earth are funny and mischievous. Debris de-br-ee Because of the earthquake, lots of debris fell off buildings. Vibration v-eye-br-ay-sh-un The vibration during the earthquake caused a huge shaking. Genie jee-nee The spirits are like genies trapped in the planet. Billy, Brenda, Grandma and the dog held on as they took cover in Billy's bedroom. A massive vibration travelled through the ground, making everything shiver. It was a huge earthquake. This was Brenda's first time experiencing an earthquake, but not Billy's. He had been through an earthquake before. "Why won't it stop?" said Brenda. "It's so loud!" "It's a devil travelling through the earth," said Billy. "It is violent and angry and wants to punish us!" "What? You mean a ghost is doing this?" said Brenda. "Stop it with these ghost stories," said Grandma. "You're scaring your sister." "I heard earthquakes were caused by a mischievous spirit trying to either escape, or shake the planet," said Billy. "I experienced an earthquake before. It was terrifying." "First I felt the vibration," said Billy. "Then I hid under a table. The solid surface above me would provide shelter in case of falling debris. So I stayed underneath, then ran down the stairs and out of the house, which started to collapse. Then rocks were tumbling in the street before the earthquake stopped." "It's all because of the evil spirits trapped in the earth," said Billy. "They need to get out. So they shake the earth violently to get free. But some spirits are more naughty. They really shake the earth so much that they cause trouble." "The mighty spirit blows a huge wind from its mouth that makes the sea shrink from the mountains, and makes the mountains crumble." "Then, the spirit divides the plates of the earth, tearing them apart. The friction creates the vibration, and the whole area trembles." "The spirit kicks the mountains and tears into them, making chunks of land fall off. There are massive waves in the sea that are so high they crash against the land." "Just remember that if you can't get out, and it's too unstable, then find shelter. Find that table. Find something above you that will protect you from anything falling." After the earthquake stopped, Billy went to inspect the damage. "We are lucky this time," he said. "Just some plant pots have broken and roof tiles have fallen off. It could have been worse." Billy held on to his dog as he, Brenda and Grandma saw the neighbours talking about the earthquake. "That was close," said Grandma. "Billy, you shouldn't tell scary tales of spirits to Brenda." "So the spirits are not real?" said Brenda. "No, but I like to imagine they are," said Billy. "Like there's a huge genie wobbling the earth and laughing to himself." "That's enough!" said Grandma to Billy. Post-Reading Questions What did Billy hide under during the earthquake? According to Billy, who is responsible for causing an earthquake? Re-read. Ask: How did Billy escape during the earthquake? Re-read. Ask: How much damage was caused? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What does Billy admit to? What do you think happens during an earthquake?
author: Hello English

title: BELL THE CAT
text: There was a grocery shop in a town. Plenty of mice lived in that grocery shop. Food was in plenty for them. They ate everything and spoiled all the bags. They also wasted the bread, biscuits and fruits of the shop. The grocer got really worried. So, he thought "I should buy a cat and let it stay at the grocery. Only then I can save my things." He bought a nice, big fat cat and let him stay there. The cat had a nice time hunting the mice and killing them. The mice could not move freely now. They were afraid that anytime the cat would eat them up. The mice wanted to do something. They held a meeting and all of them tweeted "We must get rid of the cat. Can someone give a suggestion"? All the mice sat and brooded. A smart looking mouse stood up and said, "The cat moves softly. That is the problem. If we can tie a bell around her neck, then things will be fine. We can know the movements of the cat". “Yes, that is answer," stated all the mice. An old mouse slowly stood up and asked, "Who would tie the bell?" After some moments there was no one there to answer this question. MORAL: Empty solutions are of no worth.
author: SITHARA RENJAN
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Priyanka Agarwal; Tanvi Bhat

title: Don't Snatch the Honey
text: Story Description A group of bears try to steal some honey when they are surrounded by strange ghosts - a group of elders who protect the woods. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Dismissed di-ss-mi-ss-d The bears dismissed their fears and continued. Honeycomb h-un-ee-c-oam There was lots of honeycomb in the bee hive. Centuries s-en-t-yur-ee-s The ancestors had protected the woods for centuries. Insatiable in-say-she-a-bul The bear's hunger could not be satisfied. It was insatiable. A group of bears made their way through the woods and came to a mysterious tree. It had crooked branches and strange red flowers growing from the trunk. The bears found this very unusual. Furthermore, there were many hives attached to the thicker branches, and immediately the bears were interested. As the bears looked at the hives, they failed to notice the nose, eyes and mouths emerging from the trees. There was something different about this particular forest. It was frightening. It was enchanting. But the bears continued to hunt down the hives, ignoring their worries. The bears spread themselves out across the woods, shaking each tree for hives, searching the branches and reporting to each other what they had found. One of the bears swore they could see something move in the tree, like a wooden face, but the other bears dismissed the comment. The bears climbed the trees and went straight for the hives. At once, hundreds and hundreds of bees flew out, angry with the bears, and they began their swarming attack. The bears called off the hive hunt when the bees turned into thousands in number and started chasing the bears away. The hives smashed, revealing the sheer number of bees, and the bears panicked, dropping their collected nectar and honeycomb. But the bears could not get away quick enough! The bees stung and stung over and over, sacrificing themselves to protect their colony. The stings were so bad that some of the bears lost their hair, got covered in honey and swollen bumps, and rolled around on the ground in pain. The tree trunks changed shape and turned into ghosts, watching the bears getting attacked. The bears made it back to their homes, and the bees fled, searching for a new place to build a hive. At night the bears kept watch for the bees and more hives they could hunt down and steal. The atmosphere had changed. There was fear and panic. They had not calmed down since the bees had attacked. Out of nowhere came a ghost in the form of a tree trunk, and it grabbed a bear around the throat. The bears joined together as a pack and fought back, fending off the trees. There suddenly appeared one strange ghost in the shape of a man. He descended from the sky and sat on a bear's back. At once the bees, who had returned to attack the bears again, immediately flew off when the ghost arrived. The ghost explained to the bears that they should not touch the trees, because they were sacred families who had lived on the land for centuries. The ghost accompanied the bears and led them to a new spot, where they could find fresh food and water, so they did not have to scavenge in the trees anymore and bother the ancient ghosts. The bears found human food and drink near the city. They found scraps and remains - some fresh, some that had been sitting there for days. The age of the food didn't concern the bears because of their insatiable hunger. They gulped down all of the food they could find. But the bears thought twice about returning to the woods to face off bees again. They would not risk being stung and chased. The man ghost brought breads and eggs and cakes to the bears, who ate to their hearts' delight. Over several days the bears found multitudes of food that they took to their dens, including foods they had never tried before. Happy with their efforts, the ghosts returned to the trees, informing one another about the bears, and returning to their original forms. They were happy that the trees would not be bothered by the bears, and that the bears had found a new path and a new place to forage for food. Post-Reading Questions What did the bears do when they first saw signs of spirits in the trees? Who visited the bears to show them a new place they could live? Re-read. Ask: What did the trees transform into? Re-read Ask: Why did the ghosts want the bears to leave? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the ghosts bring for the bears? ﻿Describe the ghost's actions towards the bears. ﻿

title: Leaf Dance

Speckled leaf, rotten leaf, torn leaf. Soon the wind blows and the dance begins. The leaves dance the "leaf dance". They stretch their imaginary hands And dance in a circle to the beat of the breeze. Whoosh... Whoosh... Whoosh... Some bits of paper join the dance. I see a pink ribbon join the dance. I join the dance too. We all dance the "leaf dance". The wind stops blowing. The leaves go to sleep. I hear the school bell ring. I run back to the classroom. I will come back tomorrow for the leaf dance. Will you?

title: The Buffalo Tree
text: Story Description A buffalo finds a new place to stay, when suddenly a bird drops a seed on his head. Staying still, the seed grows into a tree, and many animals and people come to see the wonderful tree growing on the buffalo's head. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Refreshed ﻿re-fr-esh-d ﻿The buffalo felt refreshed in the shade. Sufficient ﻿sun-fih-sh-un-t ﻿There was sufficient room for all of the birds. Delicacies ﻿de-li-ca-sees ﻿There were rare food delicacies in the town. Dumbfounded ﻿dum-fow-n-did ﻿The people were shocked and dumbfounded at the tree. There was a buffalo that had been wandering the fields close to a town. The buffalo had trekked for about 200 kilometres looking for a new place to live. Tired from its walking and travelling, the buffalo decided to take a rest on a beautiful green field by the town. As it searched for a place to sit, a passing bird dropped a seed which landed on the buffalo's horn. As the buffalo sat, very soon it noticed something strange was happening. On its horn, a little tree was beginning to sprout leaves and a stem. The buffalo found it funny, and it kept still, wondering how big it would grow. Soon there was a rainstorm and the buffalo felt refreshed and clean after the shower. The passers-by opened their umbrellas and took shelter, but the buffalo enjoyed the rain and the cool. As the days passed, the rain had nourished the tree. The buffalo kept relaxing and stayed still. People and animals started noticing the tree growing on its horn. Even the dogs, the goats, the rats and the children came. The buffalo stayed very patient despite all the attention he was getting. The buffalo bathed in the sun as cows, dogs and other buffalos went past. The tree grew big enough to give the buffalo sufficient shade. Now he was happy and cool, sheltered from the sun. Soon the tree grew big enough so that birds visited and landed on the big leaf. The birds fed off the bugs crawling on the buffalo, and the insects crawling on the tree. Word from the birds travelled around and the buffalo became a very popular feeding destination. Very soon tens of birds arrived, grooming the buffalo and feeding from his fur. The buffalo was so happy with all of the new friends he was making, that he even gave them individual nicknames. The birds made friends with the buffalo. Passers-by noticed the buffalo being very happy. The birds fed him grass, vegetables, fruits and all kinds of delicacies. The birds began building nests on the tree because the buffalo remained so relaxed, patient and still. The tree grew to a substantial size and now its leaf sheltered a wider range of land around the buffalo. More people and farmers visited the buffalo just to see what was happening, and they were amazed and dumbfounded at the size of the tree. The birds finally laid their eggs and watched them hatch, all thanks to the buffalo keeping still. The buffalo knew it would have to remove the tree and move on soon, but before it did, the buffalo enjoyed one more sunset over the town. If you keep still and stay in one place, it is more beneficial to you than constantly moving around. The buffalo, just like the tree, must establish firm roots and stay put. Post-Reading Questions How did the tree start growing on the buffalo's head? What creatures stayed on the tree? Re-read. Ask: How did the buffalo behave with all the attention he got? Re-read. Ask: What did the buffalo give to the birds? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the buffalo know it would have to do? ﻿What do you think is the lesson of the story?
author: Hello English

title: Water Hyacinths
text: Story Description Water hyacinths grow in hot and humid climates. Meera goes out on a boat with her mother on the river delta, to pick water hyacinths for cooking and weaving. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Hyacinth hi-ya-sin-th There are many water hyacinth s that grow by the river. Marshes mar-sh-iz The river is surrounded by wet marshes. Croaking cr-oh-king The frog makes a croaking sound. Unfortunately un-for-tune-ut-lee Meera has to wear her hat a lot because, unfortunately, it is always hot and sunny. There are so many river deltas in Vietnam, where water hyacinths grow. These hyacinths can be eaten, and many people collect them. Meera goes on the boat with her mother to get hyacinths for dinner. She likes the boat ride because she can sit on the edge of the boat, and reach for the hyacinths as her mother rows. The water hyacinths grow in the ideal hot, humid and wet climate. The environment supports insects such as dragonflies, and many small fish. Meera goes out to sell baskets and boxes that her mother weaves from the water hyacinth sticks. The hyacinth material is tough and ideal for making things. Meera gets off the boat to wander through the marshes, going across the water hyacinths. On her way she sees a big yellow toad croaking on a lily pad. Unfortunately it is too far for her to reach it. Meera watches the other boats coursing along the river, weaving around the marshes and following the meandering shape of the river. Every so often there is a pole where the boat can be moored, so that Meera can look for more hyacinths. She often wears a hat that casts a big shadow, protecting her from the hot sun and keeping her cool. Some ducks paddle close to the lilypads and the hyacinths where Meera picks and cleans them, and separates the flowers from the stem. When enough hyacinths have been collected, Meera and her mother return home and lay out the hyacinths to dry on mats. Often butterflies come to investigate what they are doing. They take the leaves and prepare them for cooking as the dog sleeps, and sometimes Meera's brother and their friends help out. Meera's mother chops the hyacinth stems for cooking, while Meera prepares the spare ones that can be used for material. The kids play with the sticks and wave them around while Meera's mother looks on, giving them soup as they play. It's nearly time for dinner so Meera gets ready to eat. They separate the sticks from the flowers to use as building material for slippers, baskets and boxes. Meera's mother is an excellent weaver, and she makes all of the shoes that are sold locally. Then Meera sits down for dinner with her father, and they eat shrimp soup with fried hyacinths. They are fresh and delicious ingredients, and the dish is easy to make. Post-Reading Questions What is the weather like where Meera lives? What plant is grown in the rivers? Re-read. Ask: What creatures live by the marshes? Re-read. Ask: What happens to the hyacinths once they are collected? Re-read. Ask: What three things can hyacinths be weaved into? Name another plant material that can be used for making things.
author: Hello English

title: Reading Outdoors
text: Story Description Harriet and her father go walking at the weekend to read stories and have a picnic. While they read, two sneaky goats come along and try to steal their belongings. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Particular per-tik-u-lur On that particular day, it was hot and sunny. Immediately imm-ee-dee-ut-lee They sat in the shade immediately, because of the heat. Belongings be-long-ings They put their belongings on the ground. Trough tr-off There was a drinking trough by the house. Harriet and her father went walking every weekend, and whenever it was a sunny day. She loved spending time with her father, reading books and petting animals. On this particular day the sun was high in the sky and it was the middle of summer. Harriet wore a big straw hat and her father wore his baseball cap. Their hats kept bumping into each other. They found a spot to rest and Harriet placed her books carelessly on the ground. Two goats, Dinkle and Dankle, were wandering through the area and they saw the books. They immediately thought of eating them. Dinkle took one of the elephant story books in his mouth and began chewing, but he could not bite through the strong spine. Dankle laughed at him. Suddenly Harriet pounced on them and shooed them off. Dinkle was startled and Dankle jumped at the fright. They ran off and Harriet collected her books, reminding herself to take better care of her belongings. Harriet climbed on her father's back and he carried her to a tree, where there was a fresh bucket of water and a feeding trough for the animals. "Time to sit in the shade," said her father. "Away from the sun for a while. In this weather we'll bake." "Can we eat and read now?" said Harriet. "Not yet," said her father. "Remember hygiene. Always wash your hands first. I saw you scaring off those goats. They are dirty animals, especially those two. They roll around in mud. To be safe, wash your hands in the bucket of water." Little did they know that Dinkle and Dankle had sneaked up on them and were watching closely, waiting for scraps of food to come out. "Whoops!" said Harriet's father as he washed his hands. "There goes the soap!" Harriet giggled and chased after it. To the goats' surprise, Harriet and her father only had a small picnic, but they had plenty more books made out of paper. Harriet sat on her father's knee as he opened the book. She pointed at the animals and described their features, and looked through a pocket dictionary to guess how to pronounce the words. "Your hat is in my mouth," said her father. "Oops, sorry!" said Harriet. "Your reading is improving quickly," said Harriet's father. "Within a few months you'll be able to read books for teenagers, and then young adults." Harriet was so happy and confident about her reading. She closed her dictionary shut, just as Dinkle and Dankle ran away. "I have it! I have it!" shouted Dankle, as he ran away with a sock in his mouth. "It has to be more delicious than the books," said Dinkle. "But it's been on someone's sweaty foot." "I don't care about the sweat and the cheesy smell," said Dankle. "I'm starving!" Harriet and her father saw the goats take off with the spotted sock and laughed between themselves. "Of all the things they could have taken," said Harriet's father. "Our picnic, our hats, our books...they decided to steal a sock." Post-Reading Questions What did Harriet and her father enjoy doing every weekend? What did Harriet's father say about her reading skill? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What should Harriet have done better? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What is it important to do before eating? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Of all the objects the goats could have stolen, what did they take? ﻿Why is important to take care of belongings?

title: Will You Be My Friend?
text: My name is Clover, and I don't have many friends! I will try to make friends and I will never give up on finding some! I know that if I never give up, I will get what I want, and if I keep trying I will find a friend! I tried my best to make friends with this six-eyed monster, but he was very mean and he didn't want to be my friend. Still, I won't give up! I tried to be friends with the bats in the cave but they did not want to be my friend! They were very loud too! "Squeak, squeak, squeak!" went the bats. Still, I won't give up! I tried to be friends with the spotted dogs, but they really did not like the way I looked! They said if I had spots like them, then they would be my friend. They think I look funny! Still, I won't give up! I tried to be friends with the monkeys, but they would only be my friend if I knew how to climb the trees and eat bananas. I don't know how to climb the trees and I hate bananas, so they didn't want to be my friend. Still, I won't give up! I saw a door and knocked on it to see if anyone was home. I went to see if they wanted to play with me and be my friend. Then came a loud roar: "ROAAAARRRR!" - someone was there! I wasn't scared and so I tried to push the door open, but it was too big and heavy. I kept on pushing and I never gave up! Inside the house, there was a big monster! I asked if it wanted to be my friend. He told me no one wanted to be his friend either. We became best friends! I learnt to never give up, because if you try and you do not give up, then for sure you will get what you want, just like I did. I found my new best friend because I never gave up!

title: The First Day of School
text: My name is Joy, and it is my first day of school! I am afraid that I will not make any friends, but my mom said that I just have to be myself. I can show my friends that I never give up and that I am caring for others! The first lesson was music, and everyone was singing a song. But I didn't know how to sing it, because it was such a hard song to sing! I felt sad because everyone except me was singing it but me! I said to myself, "I will practice everyday until I can sing the song. I can do it!" Everyone bullied me, and they laughed at me because I could not sing the song. I felt very sad. But I showed them I was caring by forgiving them, even if they laughed at me. I told myself again, "I will not give up! I can do it!" I felt very sad! I went to my mother and she hugged me. She told me to continue practicing and show my classmates that I never give up! She told me to show my classmates that I am very caring and loving, so they can like me. I told myself before I went to bed, "I will not give up. I can do it!" I asked my mother to come with me to school and plant some flowers. I tried my best and everyone smiled at me because of how hardworking and loving I was. I was getting tired, but I said to myself, "I can do it!" After not giving up, and practicing how to sing the song every night, I sang it when I went to my class. My classmates were very surprised and happy that I could sing the song. Everyone was very happy with me and wanted to be my friend, because I tried my best and I never gave up on making friends, as I was very caring and loving! I finally met my best friend. His name is Porky! We are very good together! I learned to never give up! I learned to always try and say to myself, "I can do it!" I learned to always show my classmates that I am kind and caring and loving, even if they bully me!

title: Faire the Sheep
text: My full name is Faire Grace. I always love forgiving my friends! I always try my best to forgive them if they do bad things to me or to others! My little brothers like to sleep with me because my wool is very big and warm. I am always angry because they snore very loud. "GRRRRRR!" But I forgive them even if they make me sad or angry! I always tell them, "I forgive you!" My friend always likes to borrow my bike! I always feel very scared that he might break it and I'll get angry! I don't want him to take my bike! But I always let him borrow it and forgive him if it breaks! I tell him, "I forgive you!" I have my own swimming pool, but my other friend always like to swim inside my pool without asking! I always feel very angry and sad that he is always using my swimming pool! But I always let him swim here. I just tell him he can use it! I tell him, "I forgive you!" Even when I am doing my morning exercises, my little brother wants to annoy me. He always makes a lot of sounds when doing it with me. His sounds make very angry and I am annoyed that he is always there when I exercise! But I let him stay and I say to him, "I forgive you!" All my friends feel sad that they are using my things. But I always forgive them! They come to my house and want to throw a party for me, to say thank you to me for always letting them borrow my things! They love me because I always forgive them. I have many friends for being very forgiving! I am very happy that I have many friends. I have learnt to always be forgiving, even if they are very annoying, or if they make me sad and angry! I should always forgive them even if they are not my friends! You should always say, "I forgive you!"

title: My New Shirt
text: Story Description A girl called Emily wants to wear something new for school, so she tries to wear one of her father's shirts. But she doesn't know how to put it on properly. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Properly ﻿prop-ur-lee ﻿She didn't know how to wear the shirt properly. Preparing ﻿pre-pair-ing ﻿Her mother was preparing dinner. Giggling ﻿gig-ling ﻿Her brother was giggling because she was wearing the shirt inside-out. Straighten ﻿st-ray-tun ﻿They straighten ed her dress and combed her hair. Emily sees herself in the mirror. She sees how nice she looks in her school uniform. "I want to wear something different, something new," she says. "I wear my school uniform every day. It's getting boring. I know! Perhaps Mum and Dad have clothes that I can wear!" Emily goes into her Mum and Dad's room and she hunts through their closet, sifting through all of their clothes. She finds something that belongs to her Dad. It's a white shirt. "What's this for?" she says. "When am I supposed to wear it? It doesn't look casual! And how does it go on? It looks weird!" Emily sits in the room and tries to put on the shirt. But she's confused. She puts it on and cannot find the buttons. "Where is the part for the head?" she says. "Do my arms go through these holes? I'm lost!" She takes off the shirt and carries it with her through the house. "I have an idea," she says. "Perhaps Mum can show me how it fits on properly!" Emily finds her Mum in the kitchen preparing dinner. Her Mum sees her and starts laughing. "What are you laughing at?" says Emily. "You're not going to wear your father's shirt, are you?" says her Mum. "You'll look silly." "Can you show me how to wear it?" says Emily. "Not now, dear," says her Mum. "I'm busy." So Emily finds her father feeding the chickens in the barn. He sees her carrying one of his shirts. "That belongs to me," he says. "What are you doing with it?" "I want to wear it but I don't know how. Can you show me, Dad?" "Another time," he says. "I'm busy feeding the chickens." Emily walks through the village and she finds a boy carrying buckets of water. "What are you doing?" he says to her. "I'm going to wear this shirt," says Emily. "You can show me how to put it on." "Not now," he says. "I have to take this water to the farm." Emily moves along and finds old Mrs. Harris raking leaves in her yard. "Emily, what are you doing with that shirt?" says Mrs. Harris. "I'm going to wear it," says Emily. "You can show me how to put it on." "Oh, no," says Mrs. Harris. "I'm cleaning my yard. Maybe another time." Emily finds Mr. Harris in the fields walking with one of his cows. "Hello, Emily," says Mr. Harris. "Why are you carrying around a shirt?" "Because I want to wear it, but nobody will show me how to put it on," says Emily. "Will you?" "I'd like to show you," says Mr. Harris. "But I have to take my cow to the shed." "Nobody wants to help me," says Emily, returning home. "I guess I'll have to figure it out for myself." Emily goes into her room and struggles, taking the shirt on and off, getting it upside down and inside out, until she finally thinks she has it solved. But then, Emily sees her mother, father and brother standing in the doorway. They are all giggling. "What are you laughing about?" she says. "You've got my shirt on back to front!" says her Dad. Emily quickly takes off the shirt and sits in silence, worried about putting it back on. "Don't worry, Emily," says her mother. "We'll show you how to wear a shirt." "I've changed my mind," says Emily. "I'm going to wear one of my dresses instead." So Emily puts on a new white dress, does her hair and shows off to her Mum, Dad and brother. They comb her hair and straighten her dress. "How do I look?" says Emily. "It suits you much better than that shirt," says her brother. Post-Reading Questions What happened when Emily tried to wear her father's shirt? Who did Emily ask to help her put on the shirt properly? Re-read. Ask: Why couldn't Emily's mother help her? Re-read. Ask: What did Emily decided to do? Re-read. Ask: What did Emily want to wear instead? Why is it important to ask for help when you are unsure of something?
author: Hello English

title: Riding A Bicycle
text: Story Description Siti gets a bicycle for her sixth birthday and learns how to ride it, but she faces many problems, such as fear and lack of stability. Siti must learn to overcome them and be able to ride. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Stabilising stay-bill-eyes-ing Her father put stabilising wheels on the bicycle so Siti wouldn't fall off. Practicing pr-ac-tiss-ing She kept practicing balance and control. Courage cuh-r-idge With determination and courage, Siti learned how to ride. Persistence per-sis-tun-ss It took practice and persistence to get it right. Siti got her first bicycle for her sixth birthday. She was fascinated by her present, but the hardest part was to come. She would have to learn how to ride the bicycle. Her father took her outside into the garden, and he showed her how to sit on the saddle and hold the handlebars. Siti felt unsteady, but she rolled forwards several metres at a time before stopping, just to get a feel for the bicycle. "It's fun but tiring!" said Siti. "You'll eventually get the hang of it," said her father. After a few times practicing in the garden, Siti was ready to ride further. She went to the edge of the garden, to the end of the street, and then she returned home. The stabilising wheels helped her keep balance, but she knew they would have to come off if she was to improve. Her father removed the stabilising wheels and Siti took off. "Slow down! Remember your balance! Don't go so fast!" her father shouted. But Siti was already rolling quickly. Her feet took off from the pedals and she had to use the brakes to slow down. Siti asked for the stabilising wheels to be put back on, so her father fixed them on to the bike. One day, she was out practicing in the street when she rode over a big rock. Siti wobbled and her feet came off the pedals again. Siti fell off the bicycle to one side, and the bicycle landed on top of her. She bashed her elbow and knee on the ground. Her grandmother saw what happened in the street and she came to the rescue. Siti cried in pain. Her grandmother took her to see her mother, who comforted her and wiped away her tears. "I don't want to ride that stupid bicycle ever again!" said Siti. "It'll be ok," said her mother. "Why don't you ride your bicycle anymore?" said Siti's grandfather. "I fell off," said Siti. "A lot?" said her grandfather. "No, just once. But it was very painful, and I don't want to ride it ever again." "But you only fell off once," said her grandfather. "The trick is persistence and practice. You have to keep failing to succeed. Don't try to ride the bicycle. Don't try to balance. Just ride it freely, and don't control the bicycle so much, then everything will click into place." Siti's grandfather helped her fix the bike with a few tools, and he removed the training wheels. "There you go," he said. "When you ride, just relax and be effortless. Let the bicycle do the work. Don't be conscious about fighting against the bicycle. Just lose yourself in the ride, and everything will work. You will balance with no effort." Very soon, Siti rode with a greater ease. She did slip up a couple of times, nearly falling off, but she retained her balance. Now with greater courage and smoothness, and without fear, she let the bicycle flow and she relaxed into the movement of riding naturally. Siti learned more control through giving up control, and more stability through not trying to be stable. Soon she was riding like a professional. Her father saw her and cheered. He was amazed at the transformation. From that moment onwards, Siti rode her bicycle to school every day. Post-Reading Questions How did Siti finally learn how to ride her bicycle? What major problem did Siti have when learning how to ride? Re-read. Ask: What did Siti say after she fell off her bicycle? Re-read. Ask: What two things did Grandfather tell Siti to give up? Re-read. Ask: How did Siti's father feel when he saw her riding well? What things are important when learning something new?

title: Reeti and Mithu
text: She hates vacations. She prefers going to school. Her father gets her toys and books, tells her, her favorite tales. He does Yoga every morning. Reeti likes it and tries to do it herself. Her mother is a poet who is busy on the computer. Reeti loves to see her work. She loves looking at her mother's growing belly. The belly is round and big as it has a baby inside. Her mother assures her," Very soon, you will have a brother or a sister to play with". Reeti is excited about this, but at this point, she has no one to play with. She has no friends who live close enough for her to play with. One evening, their neighbour, Das uncle rings their door bell. He's seen standing with a black cage that has a bright green parrot in it. He says,"We are leaving the city. Do you want our Mithu? He can speak!Reeti's parents look uncomfortable with the idea of keeping a bird in a cage but Reeti's excited,"Yes, uncle!" That is how Mithu and Reeti becomes friends. Reeti says, "Hello Mithu". Mithu looks at her and says, "Hello". Reeti finds it amusing and asks,"What is your name?" Mithu says, "Hello". Reeti says," No! Your name is Mithu. Say Mithu. " Mithu says, again,"Hello". Reeti says," No! We will try again! My name is Reeti. Mithu, listen carefully. My name is Reeti. What is your name?" Mithu says,"Hello". Reeti laughs," No! You are a very naughty boy,Mithu. " Every day, Reeti tries teaching Mithu new words. "Say ba-ba. Say maa. Say Ree-ti. " However, Mithu keeps saying, 'hello'. One day, mother takes Reeti to a birthday party far from the city. It's her friend's birthday. All her friends are there. They have a lot of fun. Reeti brings back a piece of cake for Mithu. But where's Mithu? Just then, father enters the house with Mithu in his cage. Mithu says, "Hello". Father says," I took your friend to the park for some fresh air". Reeti's relieved. She brings the piece of cake to Mithu but he does not touch it. Reeti's vacation's nearing its end. One day, she spots a bunch of parrots flying to the tree outside her window, chirping loudly among themselves. Reeti brings Mithu's cage near the window. That seems to make him mad. He starts chirping and flapping his wings. He tries flying. Reeti asks,"Are they your friends,Mithu?" Mithu does not answer. He stares at the parrots outside the window. The bunch of parrots leave as hurriedly as they had come. Reeti asks,"What were they talking about,Mithu?" Mithu's sad voice forms the word 'hello'. Riti's vacation is over. The first day of school. She meets all her teachers and friends. They play happily during the tiffin break. The huge trees around their playground houses many birds, happily chirping away. Reeti comes back home to find Mithu quietly sitting in his cage. "Hello Mithu", she whispers. Mithu looks at her silently. Reeti keeps her school bag aside and opens the window. She then, opens the door of the cage. "Go Mithu! Go find your friends", she says. Mithu looks at her. Reeti says, "Go Mithu. Fly away!" Mithu takes one step after another away from the cage, looks back at Reeti for the last time and says,"Hello" and then, spreads his wings and flies to far and wide, closer to his friends. Who can pet animals? Anyone who is trustworthy enough and is looking for a being to love, can pet animals. If you feel lonely and sad, a pet can get you through it. A pet is also capable of making you happy. It will play with you and make you happy. It will teach you important things about life and bring fun to it. Tell me who doesn't want it? Will you or won't you pet an animal? Sure, it's fun to pet an animal, but don't hurry. Just think about it for a while. -Are your parents okay with the idea? -Do you really want a pet? Remember, it will be with you till the end of its lifetime or yours. It is not a toy that you can discard after you are done having fun with it. -They require a steady supply of food, clean drinking water, exercise and love. One must train them, bathe them and take them to vets. This means, you will have an extra amount of daily work. Do you have enough time for that? When it will come in with muddy paws or chew things around, will you be able to forgive it? Am I really ready to pet an animal? Do you want a pet because your best friend has one? What are you thinking of getting? - a dog? a cat? or, something else? Are you even considering petting a mouse? Stop here and ask yourself a few questions. -Do I have enough time to look after pets? Having a pet is a huge responsibility. Be it training it or feeding it, or simply providing it with love. You might have to spend a lot of time for your pet. -Do I have enough space to accommodate a pet? Small animals like cat, fish or birds can fit themselves into a house of any shape or size. However, animals like dogs require space to run around or to exercise. What kind of pet do I want? If you want an animal of a special species, you must speak to the specialist or the veterinarian. Or, speak to the people who already have such a species and find out about their food habits, their general temperament and so on. After that, carefully consider if you can pet such an animal. How much can I spend? All pet animals require food and a place to stay. For their health, they require daily checkups with the veterinarian. Other than immunity and other injections, in case the pet's sick, it needs to be taken to the clinic. Are you ready for these expenses? Will it be loved by everyone at your home? Maybe you love animals but do your family feel the same about it? It is essential to know the mindset of your family members before bringing a pet home.
author: Shaoni Dasgupta

title: Amma, There is a Bat in My Sambar!
text: Amma! There is a bat in my sambar! Eesh! I do not want her in there. I know you told me to shut the windows tight. But I forgot this one on the right! Phew! The bat has stopped swimming in my food. She seems to be in a very bad mood. She is flying in circles around my face, Flapping her wings, making my heart race. Watch out! Hide! Run for your life! She’s dropping poop bombs. They are not very nice. “Suppi, relax” Amma whispers, “I think she wants to go back to her brothers and sisters.” Amma turns off the fan and all the lights. I open the windows and don’t put up a fight. Amma is right! (Is she ever wrong?) The bat takes off on her wings, webbed and long. I rush to the window and wave goodbye, As she swoops up a tree that touches the sky. It is back to the table for dinner now, Though I’m not sure we should eat that sambar somehow! Have you ever seen a bat flying about and felt scared? Did you think the bat was going to sleep in your hair for the night? Bats are not at all interested in hanging upside down from your hair. They would rather rest their feet in the branches of a tree or the roof of a cave or the wall of a building! If a bat comes into your house, don’t get frightened. Our winged friend may be just as scared as you are. Instead, turn off all the lights and fans, leave the windows wide open and wait patiently. They will find their way out in the dark! What to do if a bat comes to visit you?

title: The Drought
text: Story Description There is a drought and water is running out. But it is going away too fast. Two girls, Sunita and Pamela, discover two men are stealing their local water supply, and they come up with a plan to stop them before the water goes away. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Drought dr-ow-t The lack of rainfall caused a drought. Reservoir re-zer-v-wah The place where water is held is called a reservoir. Illegal ill-ee-gul Doing s omething against the law is illegal. Persuaded per-sway-did They didn't want to leave, so they had to be persuaded to go. The lack of rainfall had caused a huge drought. There wasn't enough water to go around, and sources of water were scarce. With their vital source running out, people collected rain water in buckets and vases, and retrieved as much water as they could from the drying lakes. Little did the people know that, in the distance, two men were taking the remaining water by pumping it out of the local reservoirs and into their truck, to sell. Sunita and Pamela talked about what was happening. "When is it going to rain?" said Sunita with a frog balancing on her head. "This hot weather cannot go on." "We just have to wait it out and have faith," said Pamela. "What can we do?" "The water is drying up unusually fast," said Sunita. "Our family is down to using buckets." "So is ours," said Pamela. "There has to be something behind this. The reservoirs cannot dry up so quickly, even in hot weather. I have a bad feeling." Sunita went to a local man who was fishing in a pond. "Tell me what you've seen," said Sunita. "There are two men with a truck taking the water with a pump. It's illegal," said the man. "I tried to stop them but they were too strong. At this rate, we'll run out of water next week." Sunita took Pamela with her and they found the truck and the pump. "You can't do this! It's immoral and illegal!" said Sunita to the bad man, getting angry. "You cannot take our water supply." "I can do what I like, and you can't stop me," said the bad man. "There has to be a way," said Sunita. "I can stop them. If only I was their size, then I would be strong enough to make them go away!" Sunita prayed for rain but nothing came. With the persistent heat, all of the water was almost gone. Sunita knew only a miracle could bring more water. "Perhaps I have to be brave and properly stand up to these men!" she thought, and she persuaded Pamela to confront them with her. Late one afternoon, Sunita and Pamela rushed to the source, trying to disable the pump. The bad man got out of his truck and prepared to seize Sunita and Pamela. "You can't stop us!" said Sunita. "You're messing with the wrong people," said the bad man. Suddenly a powerful thunderstorm brought heavy torrential rain. The place was flooded within minutes. The bad man knew the truck would be stranded in a flood, so he commanded his driver to get them out of there. Sunita and Pamela cheered for joy at the rain replenishing the land, and the bad men going away, and everyone could enjoy water again. Post-Reading Questions Who was stealing the water from the local area? What cured the drought in the end? Re-read. Ask: Why did Sunita have the feeling that something was wrong? Re-read. Ask: What did Sunita decide to do? Re-read. Ask: What did Sunita and Pamela try to remove? Why is water a valuable source?
