title: The Balloon
text: Laila was very excited today, for today was her 6th birthday.She was going to get new clothes, new shoes, and lots of presents. Every year on her birthday, Laila's father would take her to the market and buy her lots of balloons. Laila loved the balloons, and would play with them for many hours. This year was no different. Her father had bought lots of balloons for her to play with. As Laila began to play happily, a small boy came up to her. He was wearing torn, dirty clothes. "Can I play with a balloon?", he sweetly asked Laila. "No, my daddy bought it for my birthday!", Laila replied. On hearing this, the boy became very sad. As he was walking away, Laila felt sorry for him. She called him back and gave him a balloon."Don't give it to anyone.", she told him. But by that time, the little boy's friends had also come up to her. "Will you give us a balloon too? We have never played with one", they asked her politely. They were also dressed in torn clothes. "Why are you all wearing such clothes?", Laila asked them. "Our parents don't have any money to buy us new ones.", a tiny girl replied. Laila became very sad on hearing this. "You can take my balloons, I have already played with them." Laila smiled and said. She gave all the little children one balloon each. "Thank you!", the small boy said. He seemed very delighted. Later, all the children hugged Laila, and then ran away to play with the balloon. This made Laila very happy. Skipping and dancing, Laila went back to her home. "Where are the balloons, Laila?", her father asked her. "I gave it to the little children, daddy! They said they had no money. They were so happy!", Laila replied. "I'm very proud of you, Laila. You should always think about the poor children.", her father said. He felt blessed to have such a thoughtful daughter. "Sharing is caring, right daddy?", Laila smiled. She felt very happy and jolly, for today she had made someone else happy.
author: Sakshi Mishra

All the men were all going to wait for the night and then follow then follow the animals.one boy also wanted to go but all the men just laughed."you are to small to do anything as great as this," but this boy followed the animals quietly.and eventualy he found the dark forest kingdom.but he had to say the special word which was:sasa bobo.and the gates open.he called the people were all shocked at the boy."how did you do it?"asked a man."well,started the boy, everynight i snick out of my house and lookafter these animals.they helped me find the dark forest kingdom," "well i guess this boy will be the ruler of the dark forest kingdom,said a man. "and he will get 1000000000000000,0000000000000,"said another man. And so the boy got everything he was promised and he ruled the dark forest kingdom with pride.
author: Nuriyah Hassan
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Alyssa Pachuau; Mansi Thakkar; Rayika Sen; Salim  Kasamba; Shikha Nambiar; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: A Little Help from the Weather
text: Story Description A girl escorts a captured turtle back to its family, and the weather helps save a bunch of fish after a serious earthquake. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Determined de-tur-min-d The girl was determined to help the turtle get home. Sympathetic sim-pa-thet-ic She became very sympathetic to the turtle's problem. Kaleidoscopic kul-eye-do-scop-ic Something which the eye finds detailed and patterned is called kaleidoscopic. Generated jen-ur-ay-tid The clouds generated movement and moved the fish across the sky. One time, an earthquake struck the land, tearing the lakes and beaches into two. The water disappeared into the crevices, leaving hundreds of fish stranded without water. Without any help, they would die, and with nobody around to help, the fish had no hope of surviving. A girl called Nisha often walked the beaches. After the earthquake, she found an abandoned turtle caught in a fisherman's net. Luckily the turtle was still alive, but it was shocked from the trauma and unable to move. Nisha felt very sorry for the poor turtle and was determined to help it get back to the sea. One of the frogs managed to escape to another pond. Able to cross the land safely, the frog made its way to the hillside, where it encountered some trees and clouds. It explained to the clouds about the disaster, and the clouds immediately felt sympathetic and offered their help. Nisha removed the strands of wire from the net as she plunged the turtle back into the sea. It was a very heavy creature, and it took all of Nisha's strength to lift its weight and put it into the water. She followed as the turtle garnered strength and stamina to move underwater. The clouds heard about the disaster and immediately travelled to the rainbow to describe the matter. It talked about the fish being stranded with no water and no way to return to the sea. The rainbow was alarmed by what it had heard, and it offered any kind of help it could to the clouds to rescue the fish. Nisha encountered swirls of beautiful kaleidoscopic coral with ranges of colours, the likes of which she had never seen before. She removed even more of the net and the turtle loosened up and felt freer, gathering speed. The rainbow followed the clouds and the frog to the disaster site. The fish were barely able to breathe and they did not have long left to survive. The frog handed each fish to the rainbow, which sucked them up into the sky with a magical force, and passed them on to the clouds to keep warm and fed. Nisha found seahorses and eels as she passed through the dense coloured coral, following the turtle to where it was taking her. This was the first time she had ventured so far into the sea, and she didn't realise a world like this existed underwater - a world filled with such beauty. Eventually the turtle stopped and four of its family members arrived to greet it with relief. Nisha was happy that she had escorted the turtle back into the sea, to help it find its way home. Now she could return to the shore knowing the turtle was safe and happy. The clouds, linking arms, gained strength and speed, moving over the towns to find a new patch of sea. They collected all of the fish, kept them safe and prevented them from falling back to the land. They generated wind to move themselves as the frog pointed the way. Finally, they reached the sea. The weather was pleasant, and there was much less risk of an earthquake happening. The sea was deeper and the mountains were taller at the new location. The fish fell into the water and immediately felt replenished and fed, returning to their natural habitat. Post-Reading Questions What did the earthquake do to the sea life? Who else, along with the frog, helped the fish to a new location? Re-read. Ask: How did Nisha help the turtle to swim? Re-read. Ask: How did the fish get into the clouds? Re-read. Ask: How did the clouds move themselves across the sky? Would you rather help the fish or the turtle?
author: Hello English

title: Deborah Goat Builds A Shelter
text: Story Description Deborah is the only goat in a field of rams. All of the rams have made their own shelter, but Deborah doesn't have one. She tries to build her own shelter without any help. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Complicated com-pl-ih-cay-tid Making a shelter did not have to be complicated and difficult. Toiled toy-l-d Deborah worked very hard. She toiled to build her shelter. Swishing sw-ish-ing The wind was whooshing and swishing through the fields. Foundation f-ow-n-day-sh-un A well-made shelter has a strong foundation. Deborah was the only goat in a field full of rams. The rams all knew how to construct a sun shelter, but Deborah had never made one before. The sun was high in the sky, and all Deborah had for shade was a big leaf sticking out of the ground. She clung to it, but she couldn't hide from the sun. The leaf was too small to cover her. "How do they make it?" she wondered as she watched a farmer constructing a brand new shelter made out of wood and hay. "It looks professional. I can't build something that complex." She wondered if she would ever have the skill to make her own shelter. The day was hot by the afternoon and Deborah wished she could crawl under herself and hide in her own shadow. The rams didn't seem disturbed by the rising temperature, and they spent all day eating grass and watching her. Deborah decided to do something. "Perhaps my shelter doesn't have to be complicated," she wondered. "It can be simple!" So Deborah collected reeds and shoots from the ponds for materials, forcing some crabs and frogs out of the way. She went back and forth to the pond, working up a sweat, until she had collected enough plants for weaving wood together. Then Deborah collected lots of leaves from the woods - really big ones large enough to provide shelter from sun, the rain and the winds. She carried so many leaves that she couldn't see where she was going, and she bumped into a ram, knocking him over. As the afternoon drew on, Deborah planted four trunk posts to act as corners for her shelter. She toiled very hard and tired out her body as she dug up the soil. It was a difficult task, but she was determined to finish her mission. She dragged pile after pile of leaves, shrub, bush, trunk, twig and weaving material into place, and her shelter began to take shape. Suddenly the temperature dropped and the atmosphere changed. Deborah felt a change in the weather coming, so she worked faster to complete her shelter. Suddenly clouds came - thick, heavy ones - and the wind picked up speed. It also picked up some of her materials, swishing them around in the air as a gale blew across the land. Deborah had to jump and catch them, and position them back into place on her shelter. She worried her shelter would be destroyed. Fortunately, the wind only blew a few leaves away. The basics were secured into place - a solid foundation, walls and a roof. As the gale blew, Deborah crawled inside and waited. The walls and roof took the full force of the wind, but they stayed strong and intact. Very shortly, the wind died down and disappeared, and the clear sky emerged again, bringing the hot sun. The land heated up, but Deborah felt safe. She stayed in the cool shade inside her new shelter, and she felt very proud of herself for completing the work all on her own. Post-Reading Questions Why did Deborah want to build a shelter? What did Deborah learn through the process of building by herself? Re-read. Ask: What are the first materials that Deborah finds? Re-read. Ask: What are the three important parts of a shelter? Re-read. Ask: ﻿How did Deborah feel after completing the work? ﻿What skills do you think Deborah gained by working on her own?
author: Hello English

title: The Sun makes new friends !
text: Once upon a time, Water and Earth were best friends. Water and Earth would always play and hug each other. They were very happy. And that's when the jealous Sun came along. As you know, he is always so hot. Being so hot all the time made him very lonely and very angry. ”Grrr”, he said, “I have no friends”. He was very jealous of the friendship between Earth and Water. “I want to play with water too”, the Sun thought. So, he used all his power and slowly, bit by bit, turned Water into steam and separated Water from Earth. All the water floated into the sky became clouds and stayed far far away from Earth. Earth started feeling sad without her friend. “Water, come back”, she said, “I feel lonely without you” Water was really smart. She thought of a plan. She started coming back down in the form of Rain every few months. Water also knew that the Sun would see them and feel jealous again, so she made the sky very dark and covered him up with dark clouds. Water and Earth happily played for sometime. By then, the dark clouds had disappeared and the Sun came out and saw them. Earth saw the hot angry Sun and told Water, ”We should invite him to play too” “Yes, yes!”, Water replied. Earth, Water and Sun now became really good friends. They played together and were very happy. When all three of them happily smiled together, a bright and shiny Rainbow was formed! Rainbows are formed when there is Rain on Sunny days. Have you seen one? Can you name all the colours of a Rainbow?
author: Shashank Monappa

title: The Clever Crow
text: The Clever Crow once a crow felt thirsty... she was really tired She saw a pot near a house with only little water at the bottom. she thought and thought and finally had an idea she started collecting stones and put them in the pot... soon the water rose and she could drink it. she was happy.

illustrator: Padmanabh; Pradeep Thennatt; Wiehan de Jager

title: Fish and Chips
text: Story Description A boy named Chips goes fishing with his father and sees fish under the surface. He makes friends with a fish and decides to adopt it. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Enthusiastic in-th-ew-zee-a-ss-tic He saw that the fish were energetic and enthusiastic. Jealously je-luss-lee The cat looked at the fish jealously. Wrinkle r-in-cul Staying in the bath too long gave the boy wrinkle d skin. Release re-lee-ss The boy decided to release the fish back into the sea. Chips was sitting on the end of the pier watching his father fishing, joined by a hovering sea gull. Chips wondered what life was like under the sea. He saw fish swimming around and enjoying themselves, so he assumed they were very lively and enthusiastic. But one particular fish jumped so high. He managed to avoid Chips's father's rod, and he leaped with pure enthusiasm and energy out of the water. Chips cheered because he thought it was amazing. He hadn't seen anything so cool before. Chips jumped into the sea. It was cold at first but it soon became warm. The fish joined him and played along. Chips's father held on to him while he practiced his swimming, and the fish watched as Chips and his father had fun. "You can talk?" said Chips, watching bubbles come out of the fish's mouth. "It sounds like you want to come out of the water!" Chips heard what sounded like a laugh from the fish. Then suddenly the fish flipped again and landed straight in Chips's arms. "You're adorable," said Chips. "You know what I'm going to call you? Fish. We can be Fish and Chips! We'll make a great team!" Chips took Fish home and gave him a bath, while the cat looked on jealously. "What?" said Chips to the cat. "I'm not allowed to have new friends?" "I don't think your new friend will last very long with me around," said the cat. Chips had his nightly bath and Fish rested against a post. Chips noticed something was wrong. Fish had changed colour from blue to red. "I think he needs your help," said the cat. "He shouldn't be out of water for too long." "Poor Fish!" said Chips. "Here, come back into the water." Fish enjoyed the warm bath and swam around, splashing water over the side of the bath. The cat crept away when water started spilling towards it. Fish and Chips splashed with madness until Chips started to wrinkle, meaning it was time for him to get out of the bath. "We should stop playing now," said Chips. "We've already created a big mess!" "I understand you want to keep me as a pet," said Fish. "But you have to release me back into the sea now. I miss my family and that's where I belong. Don't worry, though. I'll come to the beach whenever you are there, and we can play again!" "You're right," said Chips. "It's not fair on you. I should take you home." And so Chips released Fish back into the sea, and Fish was very happy, because he could see his family and stay friends with Chips, as long as Chips didn't bring the cat with him, and his father fished in a different area. In fact, the very next week, Fish appeared to Chips when he went swimming, and they played together again! Post-Reading Questions Why did Fish and Chips get along so well? What did Chips realise it wasn't fair to do? Re-read. Ask: What did Chips realise that Fish could do? Re-read. Ask: How did the cat react to Fish being kept as a pet? Re-read. Ask: What did Chips realise that it was wrong to do? What do you think Chips learned from the experience?
author: Hello English

title: The Python
text: Grandfather made six small balls of rice that day. And, around the three of them, tracing the shape of the steel plate, was the gentle sambhar. He looked at the small boy, his grandson, who was looking away. His eyes were scanning the sky. A cloud in the shape of a lost lamb floated by. Grandfather looked at the clock. It said: Already Very Late For Lunch. The boy had sleep for breakfast. Grandfather was not going to let him have the sky for lunch. So Grandfather took a ball of rice, but the boy’s mouth opened only when he wanted to suck on his own tiny fingers. It otherwise remained very closed. Until there came a python. ﻿ It came one evening. No jeeps with loudspeakers announced its slithery arrival. It came to the house of a little boy who never opened his mouth. It came because the little boy, who always played outside with the trees and the birds, also always forgot to close the door of his house. It came from a book. Or from a newspaper Grandfather had read yesterday, or the day before, or the day before that day. It slithered down from his mind. Out from his very old lips. It came one evening, without announcement, because of what Grandfather said. He said, “Once upon a time…” “And then? And then what happened?” The boy asked, his mouth open. “And then,” Grandfather said and placed one small ball of rice into the O of the boy’s mouth. “And then, from the darkness of the house, because there was no electricity, arrived a man with a staff that glowed.” “And then?” “And then,” Grandfather said and placed the second ball of rice. He watched the boy chew it down in anticipation. “And then, the man gently tapped on the python’s head with the glowing staff. Three times. Tak, tak, tak.” The boy closed his mouth, but this time to smile. “And then?” The balls of rice began to disappear from the plate. “And then,” Grandfather said and placed the final ball of rice into the boy’s mouth. “The man with the magical stick told the python that he cannot come to the house of his little child again.” “Why?” The boy asked. “Because,” Grandfather smiled, his caterpillar eyebrows waking up above his eyes. “Because the little boy has promised the old man that he won’t forget to close the door again.” The plate was empty. “Will you forget to close the door again?” Grandfather asked. “No!” the boy said, shaking his head. After, they walked back inside the house. The boy closed the door behind them. He looked at the door, felt his hands around the golden knob. After he was sure, he looked up at his grandfather, his mouth open. And he burped. And both of them did not stop laughing for a long, long time.
author: Ananthu MC

title: Raju and his Magical Lunchbox
text: Raju was six years old. He loved reading, playing with friends, looking at dogs and birds from his window and everything else except eating. He was a fussy eater. Whatever his Amma made, he complained and refused to eat. Amma did everything she could to make Raju finish his lunch. Sometimes she made sheera, sometimes paratha and at times sandwich. She thought that by seeing his friends eat healthy food, even Raju would finish his lunchbox. But nothing could please Raju.. One day Raju's Aajo (his grandfather) gifted him a new lunchbox. It was plain steel lunchbox, which he had painted in red colour. Aajo told Raju that it was a magical lunchbox. Everyday he could wish what he wanted to eat and it would appear in his lunchbox. Raju was very excited to use this magical lunchbox and was waiting for his school to reopen. It was first day of school and Amma had packed 1 Banana and 4 slices of Apple in his lunchbox. Raju was eager to see if his new lunchbox was truly magical. So, as told by Aajo, Raju wished that his lunchbox was filled with ice cream and jalebis. And voila! As he opened his lunchbox he jumped to see his favorite food in his red lunchbox. Raju gobbled everything and couldn't stop smiling the entire day. When he went home, even Amma was delighted to see his lunchbox empty. The next day, Amma gave Raju chapati roll, filled with cabbage and green peas vegetable. But our friend Raju knew what to do. As soon as it was lunch time, Raju wished that he ate chicken burger and french fries. And again his wish came true. Raju showed his lunchbox to all his friends but did not share his favorite food with anyone. With each passing day, Raju wished for more and more junk food in his lunchbox, while Amma thought that Raju has become a good boy now and ate everything healthy which she made for him daily. After two weeks, however, Raju started complaining of stomach ache after dinner. He even vomited and started crying unbearably in pain. When Amma took him to the doctor, she was shocked to know that Raju had severe stomach infection due to eating outside and stale food. When questioned about it, Raju did not reply anything. He was just feeling sorry for himself, for being so selfish and eating junk food without telling Amma. After two days, Raju felt better and went back to school. This time, he opened his luncbox with a smile, but instead of wishing that his lunchbox be filled with junk food, he thanked that his Amma gave him delicious home made food. Raju was no longer fussy about eating everything homemade. He had learnt a lesson that home made food is not only healthy but delicious too. He also understood that junk food could be eaten but only once in a while. Raju went home happily and hugged his Amma.
author: MANISHA BHISE
illustrator: Jayesh Sivan; Kalp Sanghvi; Kshirin Shetty; Niloufer Wadia; Priya Kuriyan; Radhika Tipnis; Rijuta Ghate

title: The golden games
text: Hello, I am Shyama. This is my village. Will you play with me? Here are few games we can play. 1. Tyre racing game This is an interesting racing game. Take a stick and tyre. Use the stick to move the tyre forward, don’t let the tyre fall. And, The race to the farm begins. 2. Pithu This is also one of the traditional games. It is played with two teams. A team stacks the seven stones before the other team hits the stack of stones with a ball. 3. Gilli- Danda In this game, Gilli (small stick) is hit with the danda (bigger stick). The one whose gilli goes farer wins the game. 4. aankh micholi Here, a blind-folded child tries to get hold of the other children playing. The one who gets the hold is blindfolded for the next turn. 5. hopscotch In hopscotch, one has to throw a flat stone (marker) in one of the boxes drawn on the ground. Hop into the boxes skipping the box with the marker. While returning from the boxes, the player has to make sure to get back the marker. 6. Five stone game Throw the five stones down. Pick up a stone and throw it in air and pick up one stone while catching the stone in air. Throw a stone and pick up the two. Throw a stone and pick up the three. Throw a stone and pick up the four. Come, let’s have fun! Olden day sports Hop scotch, Tyre racing, Pithu, Gilli-danda, Aankh-micholi, skipping ropes, swaying on a tyre swing, five stones are some of the olden days games. Due to various factors like, development of technology and indoor games, lack of playing areas, busy schedules- the olden games are no more played now-a-days. These games should be revived for all their benefits. Benefits of the olden day games All the games are played close to nature. They keep the children physically and mentally fit and active. Sunlight forms vitamin D in our body which makes the bones strong. These games also improve the level of concentration, physical balance and judgment skills. Above all, they help the children to develop very important life skills- physical, interpersonal and social skills. Name the games you can see children playing in this picture.
author: Riddhi Nath
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Ajit Narayan; Kathy   Arbuckle; Mohit Kataria; Mohit Suneja; Promina Shreshtha; Samidha Gunjal

title: Venu's New Friend
text: Venu jumped out of bed the moment he opened his eyes. It was his first day of school after a long summer break. He couldn’t wait to see his friends and his new class teacher for grade 2. He quickly wore his new uniform and shoes, hurriedly ate the delicious Pooris and Channa masala that his mother set before him, grabbed his neatly packed school bag and set off for school. The decorated classroom looked warm and inviting. His new class teacher Miss. Radha was at the door to welcome the students with a bright smile. She was a gentle and affectionate teacher who looked out for every student in class. As Miss Radha greeted the class cheerfully, Venu noticed a new boy standing, worried and confused, next to his teacher. “This is Vihaan, your new classmate. Although he doesn’t talk much, he is very special!” exclaimed Ms. Radha. Venu took an instant liking to Vihaan. He signalled to Vihaan to sit next to him. Although Vihaan didn’t seem to look, he quickly came and sat beside Venu. "It is going to be a great school year”, said a happy Venu to his new friend. Vihaan sat silently with his head bowed down. Even as Venu tried hard to engage in a conversation, Vihaan looked away. Suddenly, Vihaan moved out of his seat and started jumping up and down. All the children in class including Venu were surprised. Calmly, Miss Radha held Vihaan’s hand and led him back to his seat. “Children, Vihaan is a very smart boy like all of you. Sometimes, he might feel like jumping or walking around the classroom. We must understand him and be friends with him. Can we?”, asked Miss Radha. All the children nodded their heads vigorously. As the days passed by, Venu understood his friend better. Although Vihaan did not talk much, he listened intently. He was a whiz at math and even helped Venu with difficult math problems. Vihaan could read, write and paint extremely well. The friendship between the two boys deepened as they shared their pencils, erasers and food. Miss. Radha noticed that the boys helped one another and stood up for each other. Venu spoke a lot about Vihaan to his parents. After a few weeks Venu’s parents invited Vihaan’s family over for dinner. Both the families had a great time, especially the boys. Later Vihaan’s parents explained that their son had a condition called Autism, because of which he had faced a lot of trouble in his previous school. He did not talk much and couldn’t make friends easily, related his sad mother. Listening to all this intently, Venu quickly said, “but I will be Vihaan’s best friend”. Everyone smiled joyfully. Vihaan slowly moved next to Venu and hugged his best friend with a smile on his face.
author: Bhuvana & Sedricia
illustrator: Godwin  Chipenya; Natasha  Mehra; Rupesh Sudhanshu; Sheetal Thapa

title: Blee Bloop the Lost Alien
text: "Bye!", Aliya said joyfully as she waved goodbye to her classmates. It was finally Friday. She couldn't wait to go back home to enjoy her weekend! ﻿Aliya was walking along the river when suddenly she heard a weird sound. "Blee Bloop HELP! Blee Bloop HELP! WATER! BLEE BLOOP DROWN" shouted a little green alien. Aliya quickly reached her arm to save poor Blee Bloop from drowning. Aliya took Blee Bloop to her house. She took good care of him by giving him a towel and food to eat. Blee Bloop ate the noodles Aliya cooked! Blee Bloop still hadn't spoken since Aliya saved him from drowning. "Don't be scared, you're safe now!" she said to him. "You can sleep next to me in my bed where I can protect you!" She hoped that the next day Blee Bloop would talk to her. Blee Bloop finally spoke. He said he was looking for a new planet to call home. But his rocket accidentally crashed on planet Earth. "Blee Bloop wants to live in Jupiter!" he said. Aliya got on Blee Bloops rocket to go to Jupiter. But Blee Bloop suddenly said, "I don't want to go to Jupiter anymore. I want to stay with you Aliya. I like planet Earth! You are my best friend!" Aliya and Blee Bloop both went back to Aliyas house. Blee Bloop chose to stay on planet Earth because he wanted to not just find a house, but also a home. A home is where you feel loved. He wanted to stay with Aliya because she showed Blee Bloop love which made her his home.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Anupama Ajinkya Apte; Chaaya Prabhat; Dỗ Thái Thanh; Kavita Singh Kale; Pallak Goswamy; Phạm Hoàng  Giang; Vibha Surya; Vidyun Sabhaney

title: Clary and the Rainbow Koi
text: One day,Clary was catching fish for her family dinner. She saw something sparkling in the water. She had never seen something like this before. Her net could not catch the fish, so she bravely dived in to catch it. "Wow! Aren't you a beautiful fish! You're definitely too pretty to eat!", said Clary as she held the fish gently with two hands, while her eyes were captured by its beauty. "Thank you," said the fish. Clary screamed, "What? A talking fish? I must be dreaming!" "No, you're not," said the fish. "I am Nitosha, queen of the Rainbow Kois. I shall reward you for not eating me. Allow me to take you to my kingdom." Clary hesitated as she didn't know how to swim. Notisha told Clary not to worry, as when she holds her, she will also be able to breathe underwater. Notisha is not only beautiful but also magical. Clary coudln't help but admire how beautiful the ocean was and how fast they were swimming towards the deep ocean. They arrived at the Kingdom and Clary was so amazed. She saw fish as big as her. "This could feed my family and I for a whole week!" thought Clary. She swam with all the sea creatures and imagined she was one of them. Clary was having so much fun! She was loving the ocean and the kingdom so much. She didn't want to leave. Notisha asked her if she wanted to stay there forever. Although Clary loved the kingdom, she loved her family more. She asked Notisha to bring her back home as she believed that family came first!
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Gracie; Lê Thị  Bích Khoa; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Sunaina  Coelho

title: The joy of goodness
text: In a village far far away lived a boy named Navin. He was seven years old and he was a well mannered boy and all the teachers adored his qualities. As a child he had almost all the good qualities of a boy. His parents were proud to have such a good charactered son. If he saw someone carrying heavy pots and struggling, without a second thought he would rush to help them. I'm sure you would have guessed how the common people felt about him as well! As years passed Navin grew and started losing his good qualities.He had new friends and they were the head reason of making him lose his goodness. He felt that what was the use of helping so many people when he doesn't get anything in return. He started losing his reputation and slowly everyone had a certain kind of dislike towards him. His parents had no clue why he changed to become like how he is now and they started getting worried because of so many complaints they got about him. He would break the pots in which the ladies carry water from a far off river after waking up a five o'clock in the morning. He would irritate small little kids by possible ways like taking their lollipop. He would not speak properly with the teachers either and all of this was his everyday complaints. Once there was a discussion between his friends of going and visiting the nearby village since of their aunt lived there. Navin instantly agreed over the plan without caring about his exams nearby. During the evening he was packing a bag and his mother asked him. "Navin, where are you going? It's dark and it's not safe." "I'm going to the nearby village where my friend's aunt lives." he replied "But Navin you have exams coming near and your last time's grades weren't good either and over that it's dangerous to go at this point of time." she pointed out "I'm going ma and I can study for my exams there also. It's not like they are tomorrow." he replied His mother protested but he paid no attention to it. He walked out of the house towards the meeting point. They started off their journey and reached the spot the next morning. His friend's aunt welcomed them pleasantly. She fed them delicious paneer butter masala, rotis, pedas and so much more. In the afternoon he came out and looked around. The village was busy and as he was looking around a sight caught his eyes. Behind the house there lived a poor man. He had almost nothing. His hut had holes and his door was half broken. He came out and was feeding a family of cats. There were three small kittens and one mother cat. He fed them an acceptable amount of milk. Navin thought that maybe he gave because he had enough and thinking that he left that spot. The next day he had a lots of fun around the village by doing the same kind of acts and since they were guests to the village no one suspected it was them. He came back in the afternoon and again he saw the poor man repeating the same thing he had done the previous day. Now, he thought why a man of so much poverty is giving the cats milk besides the point that he does not have proper food to fill himself? Then....why? He made up his mind to ask that man this question the next day. Next day.... As he saw the man giving the milk he went straight up towards him and asked "Uncle you're so poor and still why do you give these cats milk even when you have no food enough to fill yourself." The poor man smiled and replied "I'm surely poor but giving these cats my share of meal makes me happy. If I wasn't giving them food they would have probably not been here now." He looked at the cats and continued "Son, happiness is not achieved if you're rich by money. You should always be rich by your heart so that after you're gone all the good you have done might make a change in this world so that it becomes a better place filled with love." Those words touched Navin. Now he remembered how happy he used to feel when he helped someone. Why people liked him before then now. Everything made sense to him. After that he became the same old Navin and his friends left him because they did not like him helping others by stopping them from their means of fun. So what? Navin got new and better friends again and from that day every time he helps someone he remembers those words told by that uncle. "Spread love on this earth."
author: Saachika Bhattacharjee
illustrator: Aindri C; Amy  Slatem; Ayoub  Makotha; Brian Wambi; Jacob Kono; Matson  Chagulilo; Rob Owen; Sarah Bouwer; Sheetal Thapa; Shirish  Ghatge

title: Ogi the Rhino
text: My name is Ogi and my mother always tells me to listen to her! Everyday I always have to listen to her because she says that she wants me to be safe! One day, I was very hot so I wanted to swim in the mud! But mother said do not go to the river without her. I always listen to her, so today I decided I wouldn't listen to her. I feel much better in the cold mud! After a long day in the mud, I forgot my way back home! I was very scared and I should have listened to my mother when she told me not to go without her! I am very sad and scared because I am alone, and I miss my mother! I felt so sad and scared because it was getting dark! I wish she was here and I wish that I had listened to her! I ran as fast as I could but I fell inside the ground! There was a pit that was set up by people! I fell to the bottom and I hurt my leg! After crying for hours, I saw my mother scared and worried looking for me! I cried so much that she saw me and finally she came! I said sorry to her for not listening to her! I told her that from now on, I will try to listen to her. My mother loves me so much and I feel safe and happy with her! I have learned to listen to her. Do you listen to your parents like I do?
author: Repostly Admin

title: Hope and the Bumblebees
text: My name is Hope, and I am the queen of the hive! We are very hardworking, and we never give up! Our job is very hard, and we have to make honey and protect our home from bears! It is very hard to be a bee! But everyday we tell ourselves that we can do it. Every day, I always tell the other bees that they are doing great! I always tell them to say, "I can do it!" After they say that, they make so much honey and they try their best to work! A hungry bear came to take our honey! We had to defend our home from this bear so he does not take any! He was too big to fight but we told ourselves, "We can do it!" We are able to fight the bear, because together we are very strong! We always tell each other to never give up no matter how hard the work is, or how hard it is to protect our hive! We never give up! After the hard fight, we go back to work to make honey from these plants! It is very hard to collect the pollen to make honey! We are very tired everyday, but we always tell ourselves, "We can do it!" And we never give up! Many times I want to give up because I have to carry the pollen to the hive, and it is very heavy! But I always try my best no matter how hard the work is! At night we stop working and we relax! We can finally have our rest, and we fly next to fireflies! I have learned to say, "I can do it!" no matter how hard things get. Can you do it?
author: Repostly Admin

title: What An Adventure
text: I decided not to go with my friends on a camping trip, and I chose instead to go on an adventure with my mother! We will go snorkeling and see lots of fish! I love my family, so I want to spend time with them! After the long road trip in the car, we took an aeroplane to go to the best spot in the country for snorkeling! I can't wait to spend time with my mother! We took a boat and went to see the fish and the coral reefs underwater! We had to be very careful because there are a lot of stone fish and sharks! I can't wait to be in the water with my mom seeing the fish! I love my mother so much! We set up our gear and suits before going into the water! I was happy and excited to spend time with my mother! It was worth it to choose my mother over my friends! I made the best choice because I love my family before my friends! "Oh, no! Sharks!" My mother told me to swim slowly and away them! She held my hand as the sharks swam away slowly, not seeing us! I was very scared but felt calm with my mom, even when something so scary passed us by! I love her so much, she protects me! "WOW!" A lion fish swam near us! I wanted to touch the lion fish but my mother said they are very dangerous, and we should not get too close to them. The lion fish looks beautiful and I loved the moments looking at the beautiful underwater environments. I loved spending time with my mother. She knew how to have an adventure! We saw beautiful schools of fish - groups of them in yellow and blue! I was happy that I could see all those beautiful fish that I would never have seen on a camping trip! I am so happy I chose to spend time with my mother! Our adventure finished, but I enjoyed everything that I saw and felt! I felt scared, excited, calm, safe and happy, and the most important thing is that I felt loved! I have learned that I should love my parents! What adventures will you go on if you choose your parents instead of your friends?
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Brad Cuzen; kiran venugopalan; Lê Hoàng  Bích Phượng; Rajiv Eipe

title: Sorry For Having Fun
text: My name is Lois, and my mother always tells me to never go out of the house! But I love having adventures! I know I should respect my mother, and always let her know where I am. But it's time to have fun outside of my home! After I sneaked out of home, I went deep into the jungle and I made friends with a squirrel. She was very kind and the squirrel told me that she always listens to her mommy! She said that she wants to respect and obey her mother. The squirrel brought me to see her family! Her family is very kind, and they told me that I should always listen to my mother becasue I will be safe. Her parents told me to not lie about anything, but tell her all about the adventures! I had so much fun with the squirrel family, and they brought me around the whole jungle to take care of me and show me an adventure! They also taught me how to love my parents and they taught me how to respect them too. They said I should not leave the house without telling my mother. I went on so many adventures around the forest! The squirrels were very kind and they showed me around a lot of places! It's time I go my own way and see the jungle by myself! The moon looks so beautiful! I went on so many adventures and I have learned so much from the squirrels! I felt very sad and angry with myself that I didn't listen to my mother. But I felt happy and calm too, becasue I know how to love and respect her. My mother was very, very angry at me! I said sorry to her for not listening, but I told her about my adventures! I had fun, but I now know it's more fun to love my mother!
author: Repostly Admin

title: Luna the Crocodile
text: My name is Luna. I am very hardworking and I never give up! I have two brothers, and I am the one that never gives up! I am learning to swim soon and I always tell myself, "I can do it!" I'm never giving up! I will always try my best! Father crocodile brought me to the lake early in the morning so he can watch me swim! I was afraid to jump in the water, but I was brave and jumped anyway. I didn't want to give up so I tried my best! After trying and trying, I was so tired I could not swim properly! I kept on falling down and I was very tired from moving my feet in the water! But I told myself "I can do it!" And I kept trying! After trying and trying, I could finally swim properly because I never gave up! I was very, very happy that I could swim like Mother crocodile and Daddy crocodile! I was very happy that I never gave up, and could finally can swim because I tried my best! I made friends with a funny looking snail! He was very stinky! I wanted to just swim away but I wanted to be kind too! So I became friends with him, because even though he was stinky, he was very kind! After a long day of swimming, I was very happy and joyful that I knew how to swim. I tried my best to learn! I was very brave to swim all by myself! I finally came home to my mom and thanked her for everything! I have learned that I should never ever give up and always try my best to achieve my dreams! Because I didn't give up, I learnt how to swim! I know you can do it too!
author: Repostly Admin

title: Mighty the Bear
text: My name is Mighty. I love getting more than what I have! I have already climbed the highest tree, higher than all my friends have been. Today I am planning to go to the very top where no one will ever go! I finally saw the tree that I was going to climb! I am very greedy and I always want more than what I have. I always want to be better than everyone! So today is the day I go to climb an even higher tree! After climbing and climbing, I reached the point all my friends have reached! They are all afraid of going higher! I climbed and climbed to get more than what I need! After long hours of climbing, I finally reached the very top of the tree! I felt so proud of myself that I was able to reach the top! I could see the whole forest up there and almost reach the clouds! I felt proud for awhile but I was thinking of going even higher! I wanted to climb a mountain! Suddenly a branch broke off the tree. I shouted and I fell straight down! I managed to grab a tree before I hit the ground so I didn't fall too far. I was able to hang on to the tree! I was very scared and I know now that being greedy and wanting more is dangerous! I ran straight home to tell my mother what happened! I have learned to not be greedy but be happy with what I have right now. You shouldn't be greedy too!
author: Repostly Admin

title: Oscar and the Sea Serpent
text: My name is Oscar. I am very patient and I always wait and wait. That is why I love fishing. I love being patient because good things will eventually happen! After waiting for hours, I was very happy that finally something bit my hook! I was very happy that I was patient, because something happy or great happens when you wait. A giant sea monster jumped out of the water. He told me he was happy that I was patient. He wanted me to go with him under water so I could meet his friends. The sea monster showed me around the beautiful ocean! We swam around and saw so many beautiful things there! I am so happy I was patient, because I went on a great adventure! The sea monster brought me to his friends! Now I have many friends! We played together and swam all over the coral reef! We had so much fun together that we became best friends! The sea monster felt happy too because I was very patient and waited. What an adventure! I was so tired, so the sea monster brought me home! I had so much fun! I have learned that I should be patient and just wait and trust that everything will be alright! I am just so happy that I am patient and happy I went on these adventures!
author: Repostly Admin

title: The Red Heroes
text: We are firemen - also known as the Red Heroes! We stop dangerous fires! We are very brave and caring towards other people. We save lives. Mr. Green Horse warns us of a fire! The station bells ring - ding, ding, ding! We join together as a team to stop a fire from destroying a school. We work together because it makes our job safer! We are very brave because we fight fire! There is so much fire and smoke! Suddenly, we heard a scream! It came from the classroom! We are very brave to go inside the school. Everything in the classroom is broken and burnt. We saw the student and we rescued them. We are like superheroes! We saved a bunny from the fire! We are so relieved that he is safe. The fire is going out now. We'll make sure everyone got out of the school. After a long day, the fire was finally extinguished. It was very dangerous but we had to make sure everyone was rescued. The school celebrated with us! They thanked us for saving them! We must always face the dangers in our lives.
author: Repostly Admin

title: Let's Make Lanterns
text: My name is Bella, and I love my mother so much! I decided to make a lantern for her! I always want to listen to her and follow what she says! After finishing my lantern, I started heading home to my mother to surprise her. I wanted to show her that I love her so much! As I walked home, I saw many beautiful lanterns hanging outside people's houses! I liked their design and that the kids made the lanterns for their parents. They must love their parents so much! I made my lantern so beautiful, that my mother will see how much effort I put in. She will be very proud of me because of how hard I tried! I knocked on the front door to tell her I'm home. I really hope she loves it! My mother saw my lantern and she loved it so much! She was very happy that she got that! I love her so much and I love seeing my mother happy! Of all the lanterns she had, mine was her favorite because mine was made with love! I have learned to love my parents and always listen to them. I also learned to care for them. How about you?
author: Repostly Admin

title: I Want To Be A Police Officer
text: To be a police officer, we have to have to be a leader who can handle problems. We must not be afraid of anything and must stop problems from happening again. To be a police officer, you must be fast! You can never tell when something bad happens, so you must always be ready. Then you can save or catch people just in time! To be a police officer, you must be kind and helpful to others. You need to always be calm, so when you speak to people, they can see that you are kind. That way, the people feel happier talking to you. To be a police officer, you have to always be determined! You must always tell yourself, "I can do it!" To be a police officer you should try your best even if you fall down. You must always try to get back up! To be a police officer, you must be brave and tell people not to do bad things! This man is sitting on a tree and it is not allowed! You have to tell him to get down. To be a police officer, you must solve problems as quickly as you can. This old man said that he climbed the tree because someone was chasing him with a dog! The police officers have to fix this problem as soon as possible! Finally, it is important that if you want to be a police officer, you should listen to others. Let them speak and let them tell you what they think! You need strong morals to be a police officer.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Bindia  Thapar; George Supreeth; Neeta Gangopadhya; Suvidha Mistry

title: It's My Birthday
text: My name is Andrew, and I love my parents so much! It is my birthday soon and they told me they love me. They said they would give me a birthday gift that is so amazing! My parents love me so much! I told them that I always obey them and I always listen to them. I always want to respect them and follow what they say. Now my parents wants to make me very happy becasue I have been such a good boy! They told me that I was a very good boy because I always listen to them. Dad told me to not look becasue he is getting my birthday present. He said that I will be very surprised! They got me a puppy! I was so happy becasue the puppy was so cute! They told me that I deserve to have this puppy because I always obey them. Me and my new puppy are best friends already! We always play hide the slipper, and he always wins! My mother told me that I can have even more gifts and presents even if its not my birthday. But only if I obey what she says and love her and take care of her! I can get more gifts and presents if I am kind! I want to be very kind from now on. I have learned to love my parents and obey them! I should care for them and my siblings! I also learned that I want to be kind because I will get a lot of gifts!
author: Repostly Admin

title: Granny Remembers!
text: Story Description Granny recalls a tale of the past with old fashioned items and skills. She speaks about knitting, writing letters, and old fashioned telephones, and how important they used to be. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Constantly con-st-un-t-lee Granny said people constantly sent each other letters. Permission pur-mish-un They used to write formal letters of permission. Cord cor-d The old telephones had wires and chords connected to the wall. Unlimited un-lim-it-id We didn't have unlimited data plans. Tanya came to see her grandmother while she was knitting. "Granny?" said Tanya. "Why are you knitting all of the time?" "Ooh," said Granny. "This is my hobby. I love to knit. I can't do much else at my age." "But you do it constantly," said Tanya. "Knitting is an important skill, my dear," said Granny. "I can make my own clothes. I knitted clothes for your mother so we didn't have to buy the expensive ones in the shops. We saved a lot of money. You should learn how to knit, Tanya. That way, you can make yourself a jumper or a pair of socks. Maybe you can make something nice for your friends." "I remember the days when we had many skills," said Granny. "We fixed our own cars, made our own tools and household appliances and we made repairs to our houses. We didn't call the local services because it cost too much for them to fix things for us. We learned these skills ourselves to survive. And knitting was one of those crafts which unfortunately, as time has gone on, is being lost." "But why are we not learning these skills, Granny? They sound really important." "Times have changed, Tanya. We think we have less time to do things these days. Actually because of technology, we have become lazy. I recently knitted a jumper for your mother to wear at Christmas, and she loved it. Oh, and there's something else we don't do anymore." "What's that?" said Tanya. "Letter writing! We didn't text or email when I was young. We wrote exciting letters to each other. It used to be really good fun." "What did you write about?" said Tanya. "Oh, we would write letters to boys we liked, and letters containing secrets to friends, notes of thank you, notes to ask for permission, and greeting letters at birthdays and at Christmas. And we wrote in to the local newspaper to try and win competitions." "Was the world different back then?" said Tanya. "Was their colour? Did things still stay on the floor or did they float around? Were things a lot bigger?" "No, no," said Granny. "We had colour and things did not take off and fly. Things were not bigger. Except for telephones." "Telephones were big?" said Tanya. "They were huge and they sat on the table," said Granny. "They had a round number pad, and you twisted the dial to call a number. You placed the receiver to your ear, which was attached to a long cord." "I would love to see one!" said Tanya. "There's one on the table!" said Granny. "I've decided I'm going to learn some important skills," said Tanya. "Having listened to your story, I feel it's necessary for me to improve. I am slacking." "Well, you're a wise little girl," said Granny. "What exactly are you going to learn?" "First I'll learn how to knit," said Tanya. "Then I'll learn how to write letters. Then I'm only going to use an old fashioned telephone. But only as long as it has unlimited texts, calls and internet data." Granny laughed to herself. Post-Reading Questions What three things does Granny remember? Tanya agrees to use an old fashioned phone, but on what condition? Re-read. Ask: Why is knitting your own clothes a good skill to have? Re-read. Ask: What did Tanya think was real about the past? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Notice how Tanya looks at the old telephone. How does she feel? ﻿If you could have an item from the past, what would it be and why?
author: Hello English

title: Leo and the Magical Flute
text: Every weekend Leo visits his grandpa, John. He's always excited to visit him because Grandpa John tells him stories about his fun childhood. When Leo arrived at his grandfathers house, he saw him holding a big wooden flute. "Grandpa John! Grandpa John! I'm here!", said Leo with joy while running towards him. "You're just in time for one of my stories, Leo," replied Grandpa John. Grandpa John started playing the big wooden flute but Leo heard no sound. "I can't hear anything!" complained Leo. Grandpa John laughed and said, "That's because only animals can hear the music." Leo was amazed. "Oh, that's why! I thought something was wrong with my ears!" Leo and Grandpa John both laughed. Grandpa John told Leo that he always used to play the flute when he was young. He said that different kinds of animals gathered together and danced to the music he made. Animals such as deer, squirrels and raccoons! Grandpa John's favourite animal was a gorilla, so he was very happy when the gorilla danced when playing the flute. The gorilla sang as well! Leo wanted to try and play the instrument. "Grandpa John, can you teach me how?" he asked. Grandpa told Leo that he just needed to think of the animal and blow the magical flute. Leo then thought of his favourite animal, a bear, and he blew the magical flute. Then suddenly a big brown bear danced towards them! It looked so happy! Grandpa John saw how much Leo liked the magical flute, so he gave it to Leo to keep. "Thank you,Grandpa John! You're the best!" shouted Leo with glee. Now every time Leo visits his Grandpa John, he brings the magical flute with him and they both make music and dance with animals.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Garima Gupta; Mary Marble; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Paneendra  Suresh; Partho Sengupta; Shivika Nayyar

title: The Green Bean festival
text: This summer, mom sends Mushroom to grandmother’s house. In the morning, Mushroom wakes up early to follow grandma… To visit the green bean field, The beans are the same length as pencils, smiling at Mushroom playfully. When the sun goes up high, the grandmother and Mushroom eat green bean rice with sugar together. It’s so cool in the field. And the sound of leaves is so soothing. “Hello Green bean seed.” “Wake up, Mushroom!” As Mushroom is still surprised, the Green bean already pulls her away. “I’m green pea.” “I’m bean sprout.” “I’m bean seed.” “I’m a bean seed With many stories to tell Tet* is coming Come with me quickly” *Vietnamese New Year Lunar new year When Grandma put the beans in the water We turn yellow This is banana leaf with pork and sticky rice “Banh chung” is square. “Banh tet” is round. Pickled bean sprouts are added. To make the meal good. Sticky rice in water. Kneaded around small rounded pieces of bean. Grandma is skillful in wrapping the cakes. Next to the fermented sticky rice Are four-cornered rice dumplings That make the New Year meaningful Grandma is arranging the table with sticky cakes and baked cakes “Wanna eat? Wanna eat?” “Mommy piggy and little piggies” Adding a star-shaped lantern, Mushroom smiles brightly Hihihihi... Grandma smiles, “What are you smiling about?” Mushroom wakes up, rubbing her eyes. Grandma asks: “What do you like for dinner?” “Dessert made with sugar and green bean flour Rice gruel with green lentils and braised pork Brussel sprouts with braised fish Beansprouts with tofu.” Mushroom smiles and thinks she will tell grandma the story tonight. The story is named “The Green Bean Festival”. A poem for Banh chung (square rice dumpling) and Banh tet (round rice dumpling) Wrapped inside the leaves Are sticky rice and green bean Pork in the center Again, rice and bean around One square, one round Pickles to be included Besides the apricot blossom My tet is coming back A poem for pyramidal glutinous rice cake Sticky rice in the ash water Delicious green bean with stuffing Crispy and full without stuffing Dipping in white sugar Inside the pyramid Behind the leaf Like a golden season Calling for summer
author: Alisha Berger

title: The Corn Sisters
text: Aby and Anne saw their father sewing seeds. Their father told them they were corn seeds. Aby and Anne's father asked them to plant, water and harvest the corn crops. After planting the corn seeds, they watered the sprout that grew a week later! Two weeks later, the sprout grew and turned into a plant! Aby and Anne were so happy! Three weeks later, the plant had grown bigger! Aby and Anne dug the soil for the big plant. Four weeks later, the corns were starting to appear! Five weeks later, Aby and Anne harvested and collected the corns! The corns were ready to be cooked. Aby and Anne looked so excited to cook all the corns! Aby and Anne's Father boiled the corns and they all ate together! "Yummy!", said Aby and Anne. They worked hard to plant, water and harvest the corns.

text: Water is important because i t is used to grow plants. Water is important because we need it to hydrate ourselves. Animals also drink water to survive. Why do you think water is important?

title: Doctor, Why Do I Have Four Eyes?
text: Lisa told her mom that her eyes were acting strange, so they went to the hospital. Lisa told the doctor how she felt. The doctor then told her to look at an Eye Chart. When Lisa said she couldn't see the letters, the doctor explained that she was not sick. Her eyesight was bad. "Doctor, why do I have four eyes?" said Lisa. The doctor explained that she didn't have four eyes. She was wearing eyeglasses! Eyeglasses are worn to help people with poor eyesight see better. Lisa looked at the Eye Chart once again, but this time while wearing glasses. She was so surprised that she could see the letters! "Thank you, doctor, for helping me with my problem!" said Lisa with a big smile. "No problem!" said the doctor. "Take good care of your eyes, especially now that you've got four of them." Lisa and her mom both went home happily. Lisa is so excited to wear her new glasses to school! Do you have two eyes or four eyes?
author: Repostly Admin

title: I'm a Tough Goat!
text: Story Description Gerald is a stubborn goat who is headstrong and thinks himself to be tough. He decides to escape and show other animals how tough he is. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Whizzed w-iz-d The goat whizzed by, going so fast. Resilient re-zil-ee-unt The goat thought he was resilient, but the desert was too hot for him. Scarpered sc-ar-pur-d The goat scarpered when the laughing hyena suddenly appeared. Puny p-yew-nee The goat had puny legs but a firm head. There was once a farm with lots of goats, and one night, Gerald the goat was restless. "I'm sick of this place!" he bleated. "I'm going to escape. I know I can look after myself because I'm strong enough! Ha!" The other animals shouted at Gerald to be quiet. In the morning, Gerald encountered the pig, who was eating a yam. As he was enjoying his meal, Gerald whizzed past and snatched the yam out of the pig's mouth. "Hey, pesky goat!" said the pig. "You come back here with my breakfast, or I'll sit on top of you!" "Ha!" shouted Gerald. "I'm a tough and fast goat. There's no way you can catch me!" Gerald ran away from the farm and found a tree on a hill. The day got warmer and Gerald needed a place to rest for a while to get his energy back. He had not stopped running since he had left the farm. He took a rest at the very edge of a rock face......without realising that it was a dangerous and slippery rock face. He lost his balance and slid down the slope, performing a back flip and landing in front of a bull. "You don't belong out here," said the bull. "You're a goat. You should be back at the farm with your water. This area is far too dangerous for you to live in." "Ha!" said Gerald. "I'm a tough, resilient goat! I can outlast hot weather. All I had was a little accident and I won't let that stop me!" Later, Gerald found some long pieces of grass to eat. They satisfied his hunger, but Gerald couldn't find any water. He felt frustrated, but calmed himself down, reassuring himself that he would not go thirsty. It felt strange to Gerald with no other animals around. The bull had moved on and he was left all alone. "This is peaceful," he said uneasily, secretly wanting the sounds of other animals to accompany him. "But I'm a tough goat. I don't need other animals around me to feel happy." Gerald found a sheep enjoying the sun in a field. "Silly sheep!" said Gerald. "He doesn't know I'm here. I'll sneak up on him and bite his ear. Then he'll be terrified!" Gerald put his plan into action......when suddenly a hyena came out of nowhere and scared the sheep and Gerald away. "Get off my land! Ha! Ha! Ha! Hoo! Hoo!" said the hyena, licking his lips. "I eat goats for breakfast!" "Yeah?" said Gerald as he ran away. "Well...I eat yams, because I am a tough and mean goat!" Gerald found a local farm and hopped the fence, landing in the chicken coop. The chickens were alarmed when they saw Gerald and they scarpered for safety, knocking over their food bowl. Gerald charged at them and they got away. "Ha! Stupid chickens!" he said. "I'm a big, tough and powerful goat, and you're just puny birds who can't fly!" "Get out of here, this is not your farm!" shouted a dog, which came towards Gerald to fend him off. "I'm not afraid of a little dog!" said Gerald, shoving his horns forward and lowering his head. The dog gave Gerald a giant shove, and Gerald felt scared. "That's enough!" said the dog. "You get out of here!" "I will!" said Gerald. "Like I need your silly little farm! I'm a big, tough and brave goat, and I'm not intimidated by you!" Gerald decided to run back to his farm, where he saw his fellow goats all concerned. "Why did you run away?" they said. "We heard about what happened with the chickens and the dog." "I just wanted to show I'm tough," said Gerald. "I can survive alone out there." "You don't need to run away or to prove how tough you are," said the goats. "It's nasty to bully others, and a strong goat doesn't need to prove himself." Post-Reading Questions Describe Gerald's attitude and character. Why does Gerald challenge himself by running away from the farm? Re-read pages 6-7. Ask: What doesn't Gerald realise about the hill? Re-read pages 9-10. Ask: What happens when Gerald plans on surprising the sheep? Re-read. Ask: What is the lesson of the story? What do you think of Gerald's behaviour?
author: Hello English

title: The Best Gift
text: It was December 25th: Christmas Day! James looked for his christmas gift under the christmas tree, but it wasn't there. James found his gift inside his father's closet! James also saw a gift under his mom's office table, and it was also for James! James saw another gift for him in his father's closet, but this time he was sad. He was sad because he didn't have any gifts for his parents, even though they had a lot for him. James asked his mom what gift she wanted, but she replied, "You're the greatest gift to me, James!" James thought of an idea! He wrapped himself as a gift, since his mom told him that he is the best gift to her!

illustrator: Alicia Souza; Devendra  Pandey; Nompumelelo  Mdluli; Prashant Miranda

title: Nana's Hospital Trip
text: Story Description Nana starts having bad headaches that won't go away. She goes to the doctor who discovers a blood clot on her brain. Nana must go to the hospital to have it removed during an operation. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Surgeon sur-jun Someone who is trained in operating on a body is called a surgeon. Anaesthetic a-na-ss-th-et-ic The surgeon injects the patient with an anaesthetic to make them sleep. Delicate Removing the brain is a very delicate and careful job. del-ih-cut Procedure pruh-see-jur The action of opening the skull and removing the clot is called a procedure. Nana was having health problems. She kept getting strange pains in her head, and she could not get them to go away no matter what tablets she tried taking. She didn't know what was causing the pains. She went straight to the doctor to find out what the problem was. The doctor took X-ray scans of Nana's brain, and found something interesting. "You have a blood clot on your brain," said the doctor. "Ooh, that's horrible," said Nana. "Is it serious?" "Don't worry," said the doctor. "We'll operate right away to remove it, and you'll be well afterwards." "Blood clots are common in old people," said the doctor. "The procedure is very simple. We open your skull, remove the clot from your brain, then close you up again." "I'm taking you to the theatre," said a nurse. "Ooh, what play are we watching? Is it Shakespeare?" Nana joked. The theatre is a room in hospitals where operations take place. The medical team got their instruments ready for the operation. Opening the skull is a very complicated process that takes numerous types of tools to open. It is also a very delicate procedure, so the surgeons have to be so careful not to damage the brain or the skull. Surgeons are highly trained people. The surgeons shaved Nana's head, opened her skull and removed her brain. Upon seeing the brain, they found the clot. It was big, and it was attached to the right hemisphere of the brain. No wonder she had been in so much pain! It was the size of a tomato! The surgeons carefully removed the clot, making sure not to damage the brain, the most delicate part of the entire operation. They worked closely with patience and focus. They then replaced the brain inside Nana's skull and sewed her shut in a long process, watched over by many surgeons who had the job of making sure the operation ran smoothly, and making sure that Nana was well while she was in deep sleep. When Nana woke up when the anaesthetic wore off, she remembered something important. "I felt like I had left my body and gone somewhere," she said. "There were clouds and large rays of light, and there was a staircase. I was flying." Nana wondered where she had gone. For a while Nana was not hungry after she recovered. That, and the hospital food was terrible. "The surgeons found a blood clot the size of a tomato," she said to the hospital staff. "That's amazing," said the staff. "No wonder I couldn't eat pizza," she joked. Very soon, Nana felt well enough to eat, and the doctors discharged her from the hospital and she went home. In celebration of her being well again, her family made her a giant cake. Everyone was relieved to see Nana back to being her old self again, full of joy and laughter, and without pain. Post-Reading Questions What caused Nana to go to the doctor? What did the X-ray reveal was attached to Nana's brain? Re-read. Ask: What does the doctor explain to Nana? Re-read. Ask: How many hemispheres (halves) does the brain have? Re-read. Ask: What couldn't Nana do for a while after the operation? Why is it important to see the doctor?
author: Hello English

title: Baby's First Family Photo
text: Whose bright orange wrapper is this? It is Mama’s. Whose blue shirt is this? It is Papa’s. Whose yellow head wrap is this? It is Gogo’s. Whose yellow head wrap is this? It is Gogo’s. Whose green and yellow flowery dress is this? It is mine! “I love my orange wrapper.” Mama twirls. “I love my blue shirt.” Papa bows. “I love my yellow head wrap.” Gogo jiggles. “I love my pretty red dress.” Big Sister jumps up and down. “I love my green flowery dress.” I clap my hands. We are ready. SNAP

title: Rainbow
text: Story Description A story and an explanation of how variety represents humanity. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Diverse d-eye-vur-ss We live in a diverse world of colour. Visible viz-ih-bul The rainbow is the visible spectrum of light Tribes tr-eye-b-s Many tribes make a country, many races make one people. Viewpoints v-yew-poy-n-t-s There are as many viewpoints as there are people in the world. I have an idea. You see how everything has a range of colours? The butterflies have patterns and the flowers are attractive? We live in a diverse world. What if the clouds weren't white? What if they were all painted different colours? And everyone could be wearing different colours to each other. You see this combination of colours? It's a rainbow. It represents the entire spectrum of visible light. When it rains and the sun comes out afterwards, we can see rainbows. We see them because light appears at a certain angle from the sun. The water droplets in the air are hit by the light at this angle. This is called refraction, and it creates an arc of the visible spectrum in the sky. The question is, what if there was a rainbow in the sky all of the time? Now, wouldn't that be the perfect spectacle! Never mind city skyscrapers and mountains and parks. You would always see a rainbow! Many people wonder where a rainbow begins and ends. What is there at the end of a rainbow? When exactly does it appear? The rainbow represents us. We're all of different backgrounds and races. Wherever you are in the world, you see the same colours in a rainbow. We have many different viewpoints, but the world is still one place. Several tribes, one country. Several races, one people. Many different coloured clouds, one rainbow. Post-Reading Questions What causes a rainbow to appear in the sky? True or false? Like the rainbow, there are many colours of people in the world. How many human races are there in the world? What do you think the message of the story is?
author: Hello English

title: Kid Hornbill's Test
text: Story Description Kid Hornbill's father gives him a test to pass - he must choose which of the animals gives the best advice, and then come up with his own meaning of life. If he passes the test, then he can be called a grown-up. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Resonated rez-on-ay-tid Something hadn't resonated with Kid Hornbill about what the scorpion said. Philosophy fil-oh-soh-fee The love of wisdom is known as philosophy. Imparting I'm-par-t-ing Each animal was imparting its wisdom upon Kid Hornbill. Wisdom wiz-dum Then Kid Hornbill went away to find his own wisdom. "Young lad," said Father Hornbill. "This is the sacred flattened berry. I give this to you if you pass a test. Once that test is passed, you are no longer a boy. You are a grown-up." "Wow, what is this test?" said Kid Hornbill. "You must receive advice from the elders of the wood. You must decide whose advice is best, then come up with your own life philosophy," said Father Hornbill. "Ok," said Kid Hornbill. "I am ready to take the test." First Father Hornbill brought the flying squirrel to give advice to his son. The squirrel felt scared being in Father Hornbill's beak, so he blurted out his words very quickly. "Aah! Spread your wings and fly! Float through the air effortlessly! Aah!" After imparting his wisdom, the flying squirrel was allowed to get away. Next Father Hornbill brought four snakes that had been clinging on to a tree trunk. "Impart your wisdom upon my son," said Father Hornbill. "Glide through the grass," said one. "Don't look back, keep going forward," said another. "And always be sneaky," said the other two. Next Father Hornbill brought a lizard that had been lying on the beach. "Give your wisdom to my son," said Father Hornbill. "Relax, kick back and take life easy," said the lizard. "Stay warm and look around you. You never know what's going to pick you up by its beak." "Thank you," said Kid Hornbill. "But lizards can be very sneaky. I don't think I can trust you." The lizard was allowed to go away and crawl under its favourite rock. Next came the vampire bat. "Give your wisdom to my son," said Father Hornbill. "Don't look at the direct sunlight," said the bat. "Don't be a bloodsucker or a leech, and always cover your mouth when you sneeze. Achoo!" The vampire bat sneezed into its wing covering its mouth. "I must go because there is sunlight. Always hunt at night!" The vampire bat escaped. Next came the bird. "Give your wisdom to my son," said Father Hornbill. "Look all around you in an entire circle," said the bird. "Blink slowly and pay attention. See things from a great distance. That way you can pounce on your prey. Also wear something fashionable to draw attention to yourself. I have a red belly. It's unique." "Thank you," said Kid Hornbill. Then his father allowed the bird to fly off. Father Hornbill brought a scorpion. "Give your wisdom to my son," he said. "Be quick on your feet and with your limbs," said the scorpion. "Float like a moth, sting like a scorpion. Get away before anyone notices. That way you can always win. And don't ever get caught. Then it's over." "You sound like a sneaky one," said Kid Hornbill. "I'm not sure I can trust you." The scorpion scurried away. "Well, you have received the advice of several different creatures," said Father Hornbill. "It is now up to you to decide who gave the best advice, then come up with your own life philosophy." "Thank you, father," said Kid Hornbill. "I'll consider what they said and make a decision." Kid Hornbill flew through the air to a new area to consider the advice he had been given, but none of it sank in or resonated with him. It was silly advice, and some of it was strange. There had to be something fresh, something new that he could come up with and use. He realised his best help could only come from within himself. He sat and meditated, then made his decision. He then returned to see his father. "You're ready?" said Father Hornbill. "Yes," said Kid Hornbill. "The best advice came from the flying squirrel, to spread my wings, because it is the most practical advice." "Very good," said his father. "Now what is your own life philosophy?" "Look beyond your bills." "Very funny!" said his father. "Congratulations! You have grown up, my son!" Post-Reading Questions Whose advice did Kid Hornbill take and why? What piece of wisdom did Kid Hornbill create himself? Re-read. Ask: Why didn't Kid Hornbill trust the lizard? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What do you think the bird's wisdom means? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What activity did Kid Hornbill do in order to concentrate? ﻿What is philosophy?

text: They prance in, arm in arm ﻿ Sometimes, they thunder and roar, Or creep like thieves, quiet and calm. The PHRRR sounds like a conch shell, The air, ruined by the fart’s smelly smell. title: Tim's Daily Routine
text: Tim wakes up early in the morning when the sun rises. He moves as slowly as a sloth because he has no energy. Tim's mother then helps him dress because he might be late for school. Tim showers with cold water. He pumps water from the pump outside his house. Sometimes the birds come to drink the water. After the shower, he eats his breakfast. Tim eats a big breakfast to have a lot of energy for school. He loves everything his mother cooks! His favourite food for breakfast is bread and fried eggs. Tim walks to school. It takes him ten minutes to get there. Tim loves going to school because he loves to read. I n school, he and his classmates read a lot of books. After school, he changes into his home clothes and he eats a meal his mother prepares. He eats with his two cats, Mimi and Gigi. After, he gets ready to do his homework and read more books! When he has finished his homework and his reading, he then goes outside and play with his two dogs. Their names are Riley and Rex, and Tim loves playing catch and fetch with both of them. After a long day, Tim goes to bed and his mother and father kiss him goodnight. Is your daily routine like Tim's?
