title: Who's that Baby?
text: Hello! Who’s that baby? That baby can walk. Just like me. My wiggly toes. That baby’s wiggly toes! Oh? That baby’s gone! Who’s that baby? My waving hands. That baby’s waving hands. Want to play? Oh, no! That baby’s gone! Who is that baby? My cute nose. That baby’s cute nose. I make a funny face. So does that baby. Oh! That baby is... ME! Goodbye!
author: Chisanga Mukuka

title: Aahna's Pride
text: Story Description To show her cultural pride, Aahna wears her local traditional jewellery to school, and some children start to bully her. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Ecstatic eks-ta-tic The girl was so happy she was ecstatic. Callous ca-l-uss The children made callous, cruel comments about her dress. Tradition tra-dih-sh-un Wearing the jewellery was a local tradition. Adjusted a-just-id The children slowly adjusted to her looking different. Aahna visited the local jeweller to receive a cluster of gifts that her mother had ordered for her. It was a set that included earrings, rings, a headpiece and bracelets. Aahna was ecstatic. She had never worn traditional jewellery before. She was excited to celebrate her local tradition by showing off the jewellery. Aahna went to school wearing her new jewellery, expecting the children to be impressed. But once she sat down in class, the children made fun of her. They said she looked weird and cooky. They called her old, like a granny. They made fun of her for celebrating the local tradition. The teacher Mrs. Singh brought the bullies to the front of the class, and confronted them for making fun of Aahna's headpiece. "You don't poke fun at Aahna," said Mrs. Singh. "She is wearing our traditional jewellery. Now you go back and apologise to Aahna, then sit down." "Yes, Mrs. Singh," said the bullies. When she got home, Aahna felt angry and frustrated. She was so upset that she threw the jewellery across the floor. She swore never to wear it again. Those children had been so callous and nasty to her for wearing nice things. "Give it another try," said Aahna's mother. "Wear the jewellery to school tomorrow and the children will get used to seeing you looking different." "Ok, Mum. I'll try," said Aahna, so she went to school wearing two headpieces this time. Aahna tried to join in a football match, but the children ignored her and played by themselves. "Why are they leaving me out?" said Aahna. "This is unfair." Aahna had had enough when, during drama class, one of the children pretended to be her, making fun of her by doing a traditional dance. But the rest of the class praised Aahna for wearing the jewellery, and the teacher comforted her for being upset. Aahna went to see the principal about the matter. "I'll see to it that the children no longer make fun of you," said the principal. "I wear a traditional hat because I am a Malay, and many people make fun of me for doing that. But I wear it with pride. If anyone else makes fun of you, then come and see me, and I'll put an end to the silliness. You are showing your pride for local tradition, and there is nothing wrong with that. In fact, it should be celebrated." Aahna thanked the principal and left. Aahna told the story of what had happened at school, and the children getting used to her jewellery and being kind to her, and Aahna's mother was relieved. "Ignore the criticism and carry on as you are," said the jeweller. "I suspected this might happen. Over time the children will return to being normal with you." "He's right," said Aahna's mother. "Don't let anyone wear you down." Two classmates, Raj and Sita, saw Aahna walking to school one morning. "Wow, you look beautiful," said Sita. "Thank you," said Aahna. "You're very brave for wearing our traditional jewellery," said Raj. "I can't believe the kids in class made fun of you." "They're so mean," said Sita. "Don't worry, because we support you." Over time, the children adjusted to Aahna's clothing, and when they saw how determined she was to celebrate her culture, they even joined in her dances, clapping her along and supporting her. As for the bullies, they left Aahna alone when Aahna stopped being concerned with them. They felt silly for making fun of their own culture, especially after the principal warned them. From then onwards, Aahna wore her jewellery with pride. Post-Reading Questions Why did Aahna want to wear the jewellery? How did the children respond to Aahna's new look? Re-read. Ask: What did the teacher do when she caught the bullies? Re-read. Ask: What did the principal tell Aahna? Re-read. Ask: Did Aahna have close friends to support her? Name something traditional about your culture. What makes it unique?
author: Hello English

title: Spot and Spike
text: Story Description At the annual undersea party, Spot the fishball plays a trick on Spike the undersea cactus. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Especially es-pesh-a-lee ﻿Spot liked the cake, especially the last piece. Festivities ﻿fes-tiv-e-tee-s ﻿The festivities included a party and entertainment. Buffet ﻿buh-f-ay ﻿There was lots of food to choose from at the buffet. Conceal ﻿con-see-l ﻿He tried to conceal what happened by pretending to be innocent. It was the annually celebrated Undersea Urchin Cove Multinational Sea Faring Friends Convention, and a fishball called Spot, and a cactus called Spike, were sitting together enjoying the festivities, eating all of the delicious, scrumptious food they could find at the buffet. Spike was eating a slice of cake when Spot realised it was the last piece on the buffet, and he wanted it. "Look!" yelled Spot. "A gigantic hammerhead shark is trying to bash its way through the building!" Spike gasped. He was terrified of sharks, especially the ones with heads shaped like hammers, and teeth like sharp nails that could chop him in half. When Spike looked quickly to make sure he wouldn't be gobbled by the humongous jaw of the shark, Spot painted the slice of cake with red dots made from strawberry sauce. "Hee hee!" he thought. "This will fool Spike!" Spot worked hard to conceal his laughter, just cackling under his breath. Spike looked back, and having not seen any hammerhead shark or any threatening predator, felt very confused. "Perhaps I was just seeing things," said Spot, whistling to himself as if nothing had happened. "Yeah, maybe you were," said Spike. Spike got a fright when he looked at his cake. Suddenly it was covered with big red spots. "Yikes!" he said, staring at the cake. "This looks horrible! What happened?" Spike imagined himself breaking out in a horrible red rash covered in red spots, itching all over. "Aaaggh!" said Spike, getting up, throwing the cake and screaming. "I don't want the terrible red spotted disease! Get this cake away from me!" "No problem," said Spot, licking his lips. He caught the cake and ate the entire slice in one go, as Spike searched for somewhere to wash his hands. Post-Reading Questions What was the name of the event? What was Spot's main aim? Re-read. Ask: How did Spot distract Spike? Re-read. Ask: What did Spot draw all over the cake? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why did Spike throw the cake and run away? ﻿What is your favourite food at a party?
author: Hello English

title: Crow's Inner Beauty
text: Story Description Crow is always looking for pretty objects. She steals a pair of earrings. Feeling guilty about what she's done, she has to be honest about who she really is inside. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sincerely sin-see-er-lee The crow apologised sincerely for stealing. Obsessed ob-se-ss-d She was obsessed with herself and her looks. Popular pop-you-lur She was a popular bird. Valuable val-you-a-bul She thought the earrings were expensive and therefore valuable. There was once a crow who was obsessed with her beauty. She thought that everything revolved around her looks. The better she looked, the happier and more comfortable she felt. Each day she flew high, searching for items she could find to enhance her looks. Just for fun, she would float and sway in the sky, trying to get the attention of other birds to acknowledge how pretty she was. One day she flew inside a woman's bedroom window and landed on her bedside table. There she found rings, chains and bangles made of gold, platinum, bronze and silver. She saw a pair of earrings with a red and white pattern that reflected the sun, and she fell in love with them. She just had to take them. The crow clasped the earrings in her claws, flying all the way back to her nest, making other birds see what she had stolen along the way. First she showed off the earrings to a peacock, who took an immediate interest in them. "Marvellous," said the peacock. "Where did you get them from?" "I bought them from a jewellery store," said the crow. "Aren't they wonderful?" "Yes, I suppose they are," said the peacock, unsure. "They are even more spectacular than the feathers you show off," said the crow, irritating the peacock. The crow laughed at her own cruelty, when the sun suddenly came out and reflected the earrings. She saw the shining and was so happy that she almost fell over laughing, because she knew the earrings would make her so much more popular. Everyone would be envious of her for owning such an expensive pair of earrings. The crow hid the earrings in her nest and stole someone's shopping, just to see what was inside. She found eggs, milk, flour and butter, and a jar of something that looked like jam. But there was nothing truly valuable inside. She ate the contents of the jar, which tasted like tomato, but the food did not satisfy her. "I should wear my new earrings," she said. But the earrings were far too heavy and big to fit on her face, or on her beak, and they were too heavy to carry on her feet for a long time. "I'll find a way to wear the earrings for longer," she said. "Look what I have, the most expensive pair of earrings!" said the crow, showing them to a parrot and a goose. "You just wanted to show off, didn't you?" said the parrot. "That's why you stole them." "I didn't steal them!" said the crow. "But the whole village saw you take them," said the parrot. "I just wanted to be popular," said the crow. "These are beautiful to wear." "You already are popular," said the parrot. "You don't need to wear expensive items to show your worth. However much you value yourself is your true value. If you feel insecure inside, getting attention won't help you. You must learn to be happy, because that is your true beauty." The crow flew the earrings back to the owner's bedroom, and apologised sincerely for taking them. The owner was flattered and offered some bird seed to the crow, which she ate. For returning the earrings, and admitting to the wrongdoing, the woman saw the crow's true inner beauty come through, and the crow left satisfied with a greater understanding of who she was. She would no longer steal anything or try to show off for attention. And she would learn to be happy. Post-Reading Questions Why did the crow steal the earrings? After realising her mistake, what did the crow do with the earrings? Re-read. Ask: What did the peacock think of the earrings? Re-read. Ask: What else did the crow steal? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the parrot explain to the crow about value? ﻿Where does true value come from?
author: Hello English

title: Catch the Kite!
text: Story Description Marty gets a new kite for his birthday, when suddenly on a windy day, the strings snaps and it flies away. The whole family chases after it. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Overjoyed oh-vur-joy-d Marty was overjoyed to get a kite for his birthday. Drifting d-rif-ting ﻿The kite was drifting through the sky. Rapidly ra-pid-lee Suddenly the kite fell rapidly. Stalled st-all-d The kite stalled and began to fall. For Marty's birthday, the whole village had donated some money to buy him a kite. When Marty received the kite on his birthday, he was overjoyed. He had always wanted to learn how to fly one. When Marty flew his kite outside on a windy day, his father watched to make sure he didn't let go of the kite. Marty learned quickly how to maintain the kite's height and to make it sway and dodge and dart around in the sky. But then, one very windy day, Marty's kite string snapped. The kite lifted off and flew away. Marty was shocked. He hadn't expected a gale to gust so hard through the village. Marty watched his kite escape. "Dad!" Marty cried out. "The string has snapped! The kite is getting away!" Marty's father saw the kite drifting in the distance and immediately stopped fixing the car. Marty watched the kite and ran after it, as his father ran closely behind him, catching up. Marty's mother watched her son and her husband chasing the kite. She stopped what she was doing and chased after them. Marty's sister watched her mother chasing her father chasing her brother chasing the kite. She stopped playing on the grass and ran after the group. Marty's aunt watched her niece chasing her sister chasing her brother-in-law chasing her nephew chasing the kite, and she immediately stopped what she was doing and ran after the group. Then Marty's uncle saw Marty's aunt chasing everyone, and he also gave chase. Then the dog saw everyone running after the kite and he thought it was a big fun game, so he chased the whole group, barking along the way. Marty, Marty's father, Marty's mother, Marty's sister, Marty's aunt and Marty's uncle chased after the kite, watching it drift through the air, as the dog chased after it too. Suddenly the wind slowed and the kite stalled. It dropped towards the ground rapidly. Marty prepared to jump and grab the kite. "Wait!" they all cried to Marty, as he jumped to reach the kite. His feet took off from the ground......and he caught the kite, landing in a gigantic splash in a deep puddle, which sprayed and soaked everyone. "I caught it!" Marty shouted out, as the rest of the family looked at him, before they burst into laughter. Post-Reading Questions Who donated money to buy Marty a kite for his birthday? What caused the kite string to snap and fly away? Re-read. Ask: Who was the first to chase after the kite and Marty? Re-read pages 8-12. Ask: Who else joins in the kite chase and what do you notice? Re-read pages 14-15. Ask: What does Marty do when he lands? What is the best birthday present you have received?
author: Hello English

title: Who Ate My Cookies?
text: It was December and snow was starting to fall. The winter breeze was in the air and the feel of the cold strong wind was everywhere. It was Sophie's favourite time of the year, as she loved looking at the christmas trees covered in lights. She was going to have cookies and milk every single night! But Sophie was confused to see that there was nothing on the table for her to eat. "Who ate my cookies? Who drank my milk?" Sophie said. "Grandma, Grandma! Someone ate my cookies! Someone drank my milk!" she said.. Her grandma told her that maybe it was her father. Sophie quickly ran to her dad and asked if he had eaten her cookies and had her milk, but he said no. He told her to ask her mother. Her mother told her that maybe it was Santa. Cookies are his favourite snack and milk is also his favourite drink! "Santa?" asked Sophie with excitement. The next night, Sophie hid behind the christmas tree. She decided to stay there until she caught Santa. But instead of seeing Santa Claus, her cookies and milk were actually being consumed by a mouse! She was so sad that it wasn't Santa. THE END

title: Wizzardji
text: Story Description A multicoloured, multi-patterned old man comes to a village, and tells a story about a strange and mystical adventure. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Venture ven-ch-ur ﻿ ﻿Wizzardji will venture to many different places. Intuitive in-ch-yew-it-i-v ﻿He had an intuitive feeling inside that something was wrong. Fiery fire-ee ﻿The cave was a fiery pit. Disadvantage dis-ad-van-t-idge ﻿They were at a disadvantage because they had less players than the other team. One afternoon following school, a group of schoolchildren were walking home when they saw a strange old man by a tree, with an owl and a baby elephant following him. They stopped to say hello. "I am Wizzardji," said the old man, wearing his patterned coat and hat complete with dangling fruit. "This is my wise owl Ollie and my elephant assistant Mini. We have had many adventures together. You wouldn't believe the kinds of worlds that exist out there. Oh, children. If only you knew what other worlds exist!" "Tell us more!" said the schoolchildren, as a local old woman saw the old man and became suspicious. "Don't worry about her," said Wizzardji as the children laughed when the woman felt frightened. "She's just not used to seeing a multicoloured eccentric elegant old man. Now children, listen up, because I shall tell you a special tale of where Mini, Ollie and I have ventured." Wizzardji removed his magical hat, when suddenly his hair appeared as a gigantic cluster of big green leaves. The children were shocked when it sprouted out from nowhere. "Ha ha ha!" said Wizzardji. "I bet you weren't expecting that! Oh, where was I? That's right! I was about to narrate to you an important story!" "Stories usually begin while getting up one morning, stretching and climbing out of bed," said Wizzardji. "Which is funny because that's exactly how this story begins. I stretched my arms, saluted the three cat spirits of the waking state, and stepped out of my sleep home into this world. There awaited me for breakfast some of the finest pancakes, waffles and honey sandwiches you will ever lay your eyes on. When my stomach was full, it was time to see my two good friends." "There was my baby elephant Mini and my wise old owl Ollie, who came to me with some emergency information." "Two fiery spirit rocks have disappeared from the village, Ollie told me, and they must be recovered. Apparently my eccentricity and wild nature is the only thing that can find them. Of course Mini was excited and asked if he could come along on the magical adventure, and I allowed him to. So the three of us set off together, ready to find the rocks." "We crossed the calm sea using a giant blue whale, with its babies in pursuit, and some dolphins accompanying us for security. You see, the sea only stays calm if you feed it sugar or candy, so we brought along hundreds of cherry flavoured lollipops to drop under the surface. That way the sea would stay as calm as a pond, happy and allowing us a safe and smooth crossing. We were relieved to reach the far shore unharmed." "Using my inbuilt intuitive powers, I scouted the grounds for more information on the two missing fiery rocks. Ollie said that I should tap my wise walking stick on the ground, and when I did, I felt the history of the place. I got down on the grass and started seeing tiny little people and villages. Mini suggested we shrink ourselves, so using my magical hat, waving it around in the air once, we shrank ourselves to the size of baby ants." "The locals were playing a friendly football match. They said the only way to unlock the stones is to beat them at a game. So we agreed to play. It was Mini and I versus the three of them." "Being a decisive centre-forward, and Mini being good in defence, we played against them. With two players versus three, we were at a disadvantage. Also, the young ones committed bad fouls. They kept tripping me up. Luckily, we scored in the very last minute, and we won the game 1-0." "Mini's last minute goal released the sacred fiery stones back onto the planet, and we found them in a nearby cave. They were very hot to the touch, and I almost burned myself when holding them up. We returned the stones to the village and left with our mission completed." "Then Mini grew his wings and flew into the air, then Ollie extended his legs and took off with me holding on to them. We flew across the land and the sea, back to our home in the wilderness." "So, children, I shall return one day with a better story to tell you, having been on a more challenging adventure, with my life hanging on the edge of a cliff, after hunting a greater treasure! Until then, remember to wear many different colours, and don't be afraid to take a risk in life! You never know what treasure you might discover!" At that point, Mini grew his elephant wings and flew. Post-Reading Questions Describe what Wizzardji looks like. What was the mission he was given? Re-read. Ask: What do you feed the sea to keep it calm? Re-read pages 10-11. Ask: How small did Wizzardji have to shrink everyone? Re-read. Ask: What does Wizzardji advise the children to do? Where do you think Wizzardji will go on his next adventure?
author: Hello English

title: The Annoying Woodpecker
text: In a small village, there lived a boy who chopped and carved wood. His name was Billy and woodwork was his favourite hobby. When Billy went to sleep, he was awoken by a sound going toot-toot outside his window. "What is that annoying sound?", complained Billy. He looked outside but no one was there. The next day, he saw a wooden cart outside his house. He thought someone had left it, but little did he know it was the work of someone unexpected. Billy asked his dad if he was the one who had carved the cart, but his dad said no. Billy wondered who had built it. Billy planned to find out who had carved the wood. Billy stayed up all night carving wood. The toot-toot sound returned. Tap-tap-tap. "What is that annoying sound?" complained Billy. Billy didn't find out who or what it was. Billy got up the next morning to chop and carve wood. He didn't expect to find out who was building things and making those noises. Billy saw a bird. It wasn't a person who carved the wooden cart but a woodpecker. Toot-toot-tap-tap, pecked the woodpecker. The woodpecker helped Billy carve wood and they happily made things together. The annoying sound was no longer annoying. THE END
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Iddi  Marumba; Isuri Dayaratne; Kathy   Arbuckle; Rob Owen; Suvidha Mistry; Vinayak Varma

title: The Special Squirrel
text: There once lived a squirrel named Chip who didn't feel special, because he looked like every other squirrel. He wanted to change something about himself. Chip decided he would change his tail to make himself a unique and special squirrel. He took a long time deciding which tail to pick because there were lots of choices! Dr Bear cut off Chip's tail and replaced it with a longer tail. Chip loved his new long tail. He definitely felt special. Chip was on his way back home when he noticed he was feeling tired in the middle of his journey. His long tail was too heavy for his body and he decided to go back to Dr Bear to replace it with a shorter tail. Chip went back to Dr Bear to change his tail again. Chip got a raccoon's tail. He liked it better than his previous tail as it was a shorter and lighter. But on his way home, he was chased by a dog who thought he was a raccoon. Chip ran as fast as he could to Dr Bear gain. "I want my old tail back," he said. Dr Bear then reattached his old tail. Even though Chip looked like his fellow squirrels, he realised he was still special because he was the only squirrel named Chip! THE END
author: Repostly Admin

title: The Talking Snowman
text: Kay, Kate, Kirsty and Kelly went to Alaska to play in the snow. It was their first time playing with snow. They loved how soft and white it felt and they loved looking at the snowflakes falling from the sky. They played different kinds of activities such as snowboarding, climbing up the mountain and having snow ball fights. But Kelly accidentally lost her balance and fell! She rolled and rolled until she turned into a snowball. She felt so dizzy. She got to the bottom but she couldn't move or talk inside the snow. They all searched but there was no sign of Kelly. Until they stumbled upon a talking snowman! "Help!" said the snowman. They were surprised. "It's me, Kelly" said the snowman. It was Kelly. She had rolled in so much snow and become a snowman. THE END
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Isaac Gergan; Parvati  Pillai; Priya Kuriyan; Sirawon Khathing; Suvidha Mistry

title: Mother's Magical Tree
text: I'm turning ten tomorrow, and my mother said she would tell me the secret of her favourite tree. We have lots of trees outside our house, but the biggest one always stands out. The tree glows and blossoms every night. I've always wondered what kind of fruit the tree is growing. Tonight is the night mother will tell me everything. I am so excited. "These are not fruits, they are fairy eggs," she told me. "Each of them contains a fairy with magical powers. Ever since I was young, I've been taking care of them." I am so excited to meet the fairies. My mother says they have magical powers. One fairy was named Clary, and her magical powers were connected to dreams. She helped my mother not have any nightmares. The second fairy was named Aliana. Her powers were connected to animals, which explained why birds were always near the tree. The third fairy I met was Kyle. His powers were connected with the night. This explained why the tree blossomed more at night. Now that I am ten years old, it is my duty to also take care of the tree. THE END
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Audrey Agnier; Debbie  Faber-Human; Iddi  Marumba; Lavanya  Naidu; Lutfia  Kamish; Mamun Hossain

title: I Hate Bats
text: Tommy was helping his mother cook the evening dinner. Suddenly, Tommy and his mom heard something outside the kitchen window. Tommy hoped it wasn't a bat because he hated bats! "Mommy! There's a bat!" screamed Tommy. He'd had a phobia of bats since he was three years old. "Put the lid on the soup!" warned Tommy's mom. But Tommy was too scared to open his eyes and see the bat. Splash! The soup spilled everywhere as the bat landed in the soup! Tommy cried and screamed even more. Tommy was so terrified. He hid under the table, as after the bat came out of the soup, it started pooping everywhere! The bat finally flew outside, but Tommy was still crying and he was still traumatised. The bat was happy because he finally ate a hot meal, after a long time of just eating worms. "Tommy, the bat is gone, don't worry," said Tommy's mom. From now on, Tommy and his mom will always remember to close their windows at night! THE END
author: Repostly Admin

title: Yogu and his Vegetable Friends
text: Yogu was excited to eat his lunch. It was his favourite - mixed vegetables! He was also excited to share them with his friends. But when Yogu tried sharing his vegetables, his classmates didn't accept them and they were disgusted. Yogu felt sad that nobody in his class liked vegetables but him! Ew! Who even likes vegetables? Vegetables are so disgusting! On his way home, Yogu thought of a plan for his classmates to start liking vegetables. He picked magical flowers from a special tree that made things come to life. He crushed the magical flowers on top of fresh vegetables and they came to life! "Hi Yogu, eat me! I am healthy," said the tomato. The next day, Yogu brought the talking vegetables to school so that they could teach his classmates about how healthy foods! The vegetables explained to Yogu's classmate that they should be eaten on a daily basis, as they are good for everyone's body! They provide the proper nutrients for the body to maintain its health. Yogu's classmates understood how important vegetables were for their bodies, and couldn't wait to go home and tell their parents to buy vegetables for them to eat during lunchtime! Yogu was so proud of himself and his vegetables friends. Yogu then sprinkled the magical flowers on them and they went back to being normal vegetables! DO YOU LIKE VEGETABLES?
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Greystroke; Narayan Prasad  Bohaju; Nishikha A; Padmanabh; Saurabh Pandey

title: Cammy the Camel
text: Cammy wanted a new habitat. "I'm tired of the desert! I'm tired of this boring hot sand!" she said. She wanted to move somewhere more interesting and fun. Cammy tried to move to the ocean because she liked how the water felt. It was definitely colder than the desert. She had no problem with having a water supply! But Cammy quickly got annoyed because the animals kept on disturbing her. They loved resting on her humps which always woke her up in her sleep, so she decided to change her habitat again. Cammy traveled to an even colder area - a place filled with snow. She admired the beauty of the cold air and white snow. But Cammy felt too cold! She was covered in snow! She couldn't sleep so she decided to change her habitat again! Cammy felt home sick. She missed the desert. She realised that living in the desert was the most suitable place for her to live, so she travelled back. "Home sweet home," said Cammy. She promised to herself that she would stay in the desert, as she knew she belonged there. THE END
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Jitendra Thakur; Muniza Shariq; Siraj Saxena

title: The Ant's Magical Shoes
text: There once lived an ant, an ordinary ant named Andy. He loved his simple life. He didn't have any friends, though. He always played by himself. Everyone thought he was simple and boring. One day, he stumbled upon some magical shoes. These magical shoes gave Andy the power to make everyone's attention focus on him. Other animals started noticing Andy, and he loved the attention. It was all thanks to his magical shoes. Even the coolest animal, Eli the elephant, noticed Andy. Andy felt so cool! Eli was too focused on paying attention to Andy, that he accidentally trampled on Andy's house. Andy realised he would rather be simple and normal, than cause too much trouble. He threw away his magical shoes. Besides, he liked his simple life much better. THE END
author: Repostly Admin

title: Grandpa Fish and the Radio
text: Once upon a time, there was a little village. In the little village was a little stream. In the stream, several families of frogs, tortoises, and fish lived happily in each other's company. The fish family was the largest of them all. The fish family was also the most respected. The reason? A big fat radio that occupied pride of place in their underwater home. Grandpa Fish was the head of the fish family. He was obeyed in most things, not just by the younger fish but also by the frog and tortoise families. But there was one thing over which he simply had no control: the family radio. Never did Grandpa Fish get a chance to listen to the news. The younger fish, frogs, and tortoises simply adored film music, and would not move from the radio's side as long as it was playing. By the time he had convinced the younger ones to let him listen to the news, it was usually too late. Most often, all Grandpa Fish heard was the newscaster saying, "And that is the end of the news..." It was very annoying. One day, Grandpa managed to convince the younger ones a little earlier than usual. Rushing to the radio, he tuned in to the news, and heard the newscaster say, “And before we end, the headlines once again…” The Breaking News on the River Radio network that morning was very frightening. “A group of humans are using a new technique to capture the maximum number of fish possible!” said the newscaster. “They are poisoning the water of the rivers one by one! When the fish die, the humans just trap them all in their nets and take them away! They could be coming to your river very soon!" Grandpa Fish was stunned. He quickly relayed the information to the rest of the fish and to the other river creatures. Numb with fear, everyone sat quietly thinking about the next course of action. No one wanted to listen to film music now. Meanwhile, the daughter of the village headman came to the river to fetch some water. Grandpa Fish and the headman had been friends for a long time. Swimming quickly to the surface, Grandpa Fish informed the girl that there was an emergency. "Please tell your father to come and see me immediately," he said anxiously. The headman came at once. Grandpa Fish first made sure his guest was comfortable and even offered him a cup of coffee. Only then did he bring up the subject of the frightening news he had heard on the radio. Noe the headman was worried too. Thinking quickly, he came up with a plan to make sure the river in his village, and all the creatures in it, would be safe. The headman quickly reassured the old fish and his clan. “Don’t worry, Grandpa Fish,” he said. “I will see to it that you and your fellow creatures will be safe from those terrible human beings.” The younger fish, frogs, and tortoises realized what a huge disaster it would have been had Grandpa Fish not listened to the news on the River Radio network that day. Ashamed of their earlier behavior, they resolved to mend their ways in the future. Use your imagination and color this picture any way YOU like. Use your imagination and color this picture any way YOU like.
author: Adriana Baldibia-Bejar

title: Journey to many lands
text: Every beautiful thing was destroyed because of the earthquake. Tiny foot and Mama decided to look for new land. And so, they began their journey in search of marvelous new places. One day, they arrive at a splendid, glorious place that was dressed in lush green trees, fruits, and flowers. There was an explosion of color everywhere which made them breathless. Tiny foot screeched, 'This is amazing. Look at all that food, Mama. Can we please live here?' 'All right little woman, we sure will. But first, we need to keep our eyes peeled for our herd of dinosaurs.' 'What's that?' 'That is a group, Tiny foot. Dinosaurs that look alike; travel together, and stay together. They form a herd. We have so many different dinosaurs, my tiny one. And so we have different herds for different dinosaurs.' 'So would we be keeping an eye out for a herd of long necks?' 'Exactly, smart you!' And so, they carried about venturing into the deeper parts of the forest. Exploring can be such fun and joy. But little did they know of the velociraptors picking their trail. Velociraptors are little dinosaurs but don't be fooled by their size. They are meat-eaters. And these ones, in particular, have been hunting since morning. And their search has now come to an end. 'There goes our lunch!', one of the wicked raptors squawked. They race ahead and leap right in front of the long necks. Tiny foot squeals and backs off. Mama is all set to defend her little one. Mid way through the fight, one of the raptors grab hold of Mama's leg. She wails in pain. But soon enough, they all pause for now they hear the thundering feet of a galloping Club-tail; also known as an Ankylosaurus. She charges forward, then sharply swings her club-tail at the raptor with its teeth clamped on Mama, and gives a hard whack on his face. He flings in the air, out of sight. Watching this, the other raptor dashes off for cover. You wouldn't want to mess up with an Ankylosaurus. It's body is covered in spikes and a heavy tail to boot! Well armoured, this one! 'Thank you for saving our lives'. 'Oh, it's nothing dear. I always come in handy in these parts', Club-tail bellows with laughter. 'Are you new here? I haven't seen you around in these parts' 'Oh yes, we are. We just got here two days ago', answers Mama. 'So then I'll show you around to folks of your kind and many more.' 'How marvelous of you! I'm already beginning to like you', smiles Mama. And so they tagged along with Club-tail until they reached a stunning valley with flowing waters and colorful leaves covering them. Mama and Tiny foot got along with their herd and some of the other herds of dinosaurs. Under that starry night, when all was calm and quiet. Tiny foot with droopy yet sparkling eyes, said, 'I'm happy here, Mama. I've made some friends. But some of them look really different from me.' 'I'm glad too, Tiny foot. I've met some lovely dinosaurs as well. Some of them do appear different. But I like that. It makes them more interesting and exciting', Mama said with a gleam in her eyes. They've finally found their happy place.
author: Adriana Baldibia-Bejar

title: The Forgetful Squirrel
text: Story Description The forgetful squirrel has forgotten his way home, and must ask others where he lives in order to get back. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Bearings ﻿bear-sings Bearings are the senses of direction. Chameleon ﻿cam-ee-lee-un ﻿A chameleon can change colour to disguise itself. Unfamiliar ﻿un-fam-ill-ear ﻿The squirrel was unfamiliar with the area and felt lost. Recounting ﻿re-cow-n-ting ﻿ ﻿The squirrel sat in bed recounting his great adventure. There was once a really forgetful squirrel who lived on the edge of a forest. He shared his tree with moles, reptiles, mice, birds and many different kinds of creatures. One day the forgetful squirrel remembered that he had to put some planks of wood across his windows to protect them. He started hammering them into place. With the job finished, a gust of wind came that blew off the planks of wood. The forgetful squirrel had to start is work all over again, but he forgot that he needed to complete the task, so he carried on, travelling away from the forest to another tree, where he searched for acorns. "I'm sure I should be doing something else right now," he said to himself. Suddenly the gust turned into a full blown gale. The squirrel let go of the tree and got carried through the air, passing lots of flies that were also getting carried by the wind. He tumbled, rotated and turned, losing all of his bearings. He didn't know where he was. He landed softly on his head with a dull thud. He found himself in a field he did not recognise, with a man running away from the breeze. The squirrel found an acorn but it was too big and heavy to carry. He was more concerned about getting home. But where did he live? He was completely lost. "Hello," the squirrel said to a chameleon. "Hello, Mr. Squirrel," said the chameleon. "What can I help you remember today? Haha!" "I can't find my home, I don't know which way it is from here. Can you help me?" "Oh, dear. You've only gone and forgotten where you live!" said the chameleon. "Perhaps the flies can help you," said the chameleon before wandering off. The squirrel found another tree and saw a fly hanging around waiting for his partner to return. "Do you know where I live?" said the squirrel. "Let me guess...somewhere inside a tree. That could be any tree around here though." The squirrel found a tree with multiple little homes, all of which housed either collected nuts or squirrels. "Hmm...this doesn't look like my neighbourhood," said the squirrel. "I should search elsewhere." The squirrel suddenly saw a tiny blue bird appear from a red door in the tree trunk. "Can you help me find my home?" said the squirrel. "You don't look as though you live around here," said the bird. "You should try a different part of the forest." So the squirrel ran across the ground and navigated different trees, coming to a new part of the forest. But he still didn't recognise his home, and the surroundings were still too unfamiliar. The squirrel saw a little girl monkey sitting on the branches. "Who are you?" she said with interest. "I'm the forgetful squirrel, only now I can't find my home. I know where I live though. I'll know it when I see it." The monkey girl laughed. "Hello, squirrel," said Mole. "Mole! You're here!" said the squirrel. "That little monkey girl said she knew you." "Yes, it's good to see you back home." "Wait," said the squirrel, noticing his door and the nuts. "I live here!" The bash on the squirrel's head faded away, and he got his memory back. Squirrel kept warm, chewing on some nuts next to the fire, recounting his day. Then he remembered that he had to cook and take out the trash! The forgetful squirrel was safe and sound back at home. Post-Reading Questions How did the squirrel forget where he lived? Even though the squirrel got home, what did he forget to do? (Clue: he was doing this at the beginning of the story) Re-read. Ask: What did the bird tell the squirrel? Re-read pages 13-14. Ask: Who did the monkey girl and the squirrel both know? Re-read. Ask: What two things did squirrel remember? How can we stop being forgetful?
author: Hello English

title: Crossing to the Island
text: Story Description A boy goes fishing and tries to help a bunch of animals to the island, using his boat to cross from one shore to the other. But some of the animals are very heavy! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Homeland ho-m-land He went to the island off the coast of his homeland. Capsized cap-sai-z-d The boat capsized and threw everyone out. Heaviest heh-vee-ist The buffalo was the heaviest animal on the boat. Stable st-ay-bul The cat stayed stable and balanced. Francis loved fishing. He would often go to his favourite island, just off the coast of his homeland, where he would set up his rod and box, waiting patiently for fish to bite. One day he saw a bunch of different sized animals who wanted to come to the island, but they were unable to make it across the sea. Francis decided to help them across. First of all, the dog wanted to cross to the island. Francis rowed his boat to the shore and the dog stepped aboard, but unfortunately the dog could not stay relaxed and keep steady. Francis and the dog fell out of the boat, which capsized. They had to swim to the island. Next, Francis went to help the goat at the shore. "Are you ready?" said Francis. "Yes," said the goat. "I'm getting on now." Just as the goat stepped on the boat, he slipped and fell, and the boat threw Francis out. They had to swim to the island. Francis took the boat and went to help the pig across to the island. "Are you ready?" said Francis. "Yes, I'm climbing on," said the pig. As the pig sat down, he toppled, and the boat turned over, throwing them out. Francis returned to help the horse across. "There's no way you're fitting in the boat," said Francis. "You're far too big." "We'll see about that," said the horse, and as soon as he stepped on the boat, it flipped, sending Francis into the sea. Last to come was the buffalo, the heaviest of the animals. "I wouldn't even consider it," said Francis. "Well, let's try," said the buffalo. He placed his foot on the boat, and Francis fell out. The last creature was the cat, who climbed onto the boat safely and slowly, one paw at a time. The boat rocked slightly but the two were stable inside. Then Francis rowed across to the island as the cat held his fishing rod. "You're very light," said Francis. "I win," said the cat. "I am the first one to ride the boat without it capsizing!" "Hello, friends!" the cat called to the island. "I beat all of you! Haha!" Francis and his new animal friends played as he caught fish. The only problem was that soon he would have to take the animals back to the land, and fall out of his boat all over again! Post-Reading Questions What kept on happening when Francis put the animals in his boat? Which was the only animal that made it to the island safely? Re-read. Ask: How did the dog make the boat tip over? Re-read. Ask: What did the cat shout to his friends? Re-read. Ask: What was the next problem that Francis faced? Do you think Francis will fall out of the boat again?
author: Hello English

title: The Magical Blanket
text: Story Description A mother tells her son Ryan a story about a magical blanket used throughout history by famous people and animals. When Ryan doubts the story, he test the blanket for himself to see if the story is true. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Ability a-bil-it-ee Did the blanket have a magical ability? Ownership own-er-ship Many people had fought over the blanket's ownership. Floating flow-ting The frog was floating on a blanket. Blanket blank-it Ryan doubted that the blanket had any magic. Ryan settled into bed as his mother was about to tell him a story. "What's the bedtime story tonight?" said Ryan. "Well, it's very special," said his mother. "It's about this very blanket. There's something about it that you don't know." "I know you knitted it!" said Ryan. "Actually, I didn't," said his mother. "This blanket has been passed through the family. It's a special, magical blanket." "No, you're joking," said Ryan. "I'm telling the truth," said his mother. "Many warriors of the past fought over this blanket and used it!" said Ryan's mother. "Warriors like the ancient princes who kept mice in their beards and fought with long, sharp swords. They even used the blanket as headwear and clothing, because of its magical ability to protect whoever wore it!" "It didn't always belong to the princes," said Ryan's mother. "Even animals fought over its ownership. There is the tale of the brave tiger, who used the blanket to get his revenge on his enemies." "There was a dastardly fox clinging to the blanket, about to let the tiger drop hundreds of feet into a deep valley. But the tiger climbed up the blanket, pulled it out of the fox's mouth, and then ate the fox in one giant bite. From then onwards the tiger used the blanket for protection and to keep warm." "You're making this up!" said Ryan. "There is nothing magical about this blanket," he said. "Besides, it has an elephant, a cat, a frog and a fox knitted to it. That is where you got the story ideas for the tiger and the fox. You can't fool me, Mum." Ryan's mother laughed and let him drift off to sleep. "Goodnight, love," she said. The very next day Ryan went outside to play. "Where are you going?" said Ryan's mother. "I'm putting your magical theory to the test," said Ryan. "I'm going to see if there really is magic in the blanket. I'll prove you wrong." Ryan took the blanket into the yard and pulled it over his head. Ryan's sister poked her head out of the back door. She thought she would see Ryan playing and doing something strange with his bed blanket, but to her surprise, he had vanished. "Mum, Ryan's not there," she said. "I wonder where he could be," Ryan's mother laughed to herself. "I know who to call." In fact, under the blanket, a magical pipe had suddenly appeared. Ryan climbed into it, going underground into pitch darkness. He walked for a long time until daylight poured in from above. He found another pipe with a ladder and he climbed out. He stood next to a tree, which looked exactly like the one in his yard, but he was standing in an open field. "Maybe there is some truth to this magical blanket after all," he said. "Where am I?" Ryan wondered. He hid behind the tree when he heard a strange sound coming from some water. He looked again to see a big pond, and something funny and peculiar in the middle of it. There was another magical blanket, and somehow it was floating on the water. On it was sitting a frog with a phone to his ear. "Yeah, I see him," said the frog. "Don't worry, I'll tell him." "Are you the frog on my blanket?" shouted Ryan. "Your Mum's calling," said the frog. "She asked you to go home because your lunch is ready." Post-Reading Questions When he heard the blanket's story, what did Ryan think? Who did Ryan's mother call after he disappeared? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Where did Ryan go? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What was amazing about the tree? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿Who was the frog talking to on the phone? ﻿Do you think Ryan eventually believed the blanket was magical?
author: Hello English

title: Catching a Mermaid
text: One day, the Lee Brothers went fishing. The waves were really big, but the brothers weren't scared as fishing was their hobby. Something caught their bait, and they felt a big fish! They were so excited since their father would be so proud of them. But, instead of reeling in a big fish, they caught a...mermaid?! They were so shocked to see a mermaid. The mermaid begged them to not eat her, and they let her go. The next day, they went fishing again. But this time a gigantic scary fish appeared and it was ready to eat the them. But the mermaid came to save the day! The mermaid scared away the fish to thank the brothers for not harming her. THE END

title: Liam the Lion Tamer
text: A wild lion was captured and it was put in a zoo. It got even wilder as children would growl back at it, and sometimes even throw rocks at it. One day, the zookeeper was sleeping, so the lion took its chance to escape from the zoo! The lion invaded a restaurant and everyone ran for their lives! The lion enjoyed eating all of the foods. Everyone was terrified and no one knew what to do. Then Liam bravely went towards the lion. Everyone feared for his life! Liam put his hand near the lions mouth, and surprisingly, the lion was calm. Liam and the lion had a connected. Liam then told the lion to go back into its cage, and it did. Everyone praised Liam and officially made him a lion tamer. Liam visited the lion every weekend and they became the best of friends! THE END
author: Repostly Admin

title: Sheila and the Bean
text: Story Description An ant named Sheila tries to carry a bean sprout across a kitchen to her home, but she struggles with the challenges she encounters. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Avoided ﻿a-voy-did ﻿The ant avoided the dog because it was dangerous. Tiptoed ﻿tip-toe-d ﻿The ant tiptoed past the chick very quietly. Vanishing ﻿van-ish-ing Vanishing is another way of saying 'disappearing'. Disappear ﻿d-iss-a-peer ﻿The ant disappeared into the hole. Sheila the ant had been scavenging for food when she found a bean in the garden. This was good news because an entire bean was a week's worth of food for Sheila. "This bean is really heavy," she said. "I can barely carry it on my back." Sheila lived in the kitchen wall, so she had to carry the bean all the way from the garden into the house. With a firm grip on the stalk, Sheila took slow, staggering steps towards the house. "Oof!" said Sheila. "This bean must weigh ten times my body weight!" Ants can carry up to 50 times their own body weight, but Sheila wasn't that strong. Suddenly, as she was making her way through the hall, a pair of human feet and a broom appeared. "Oh, no!" cried Sheila, as the broom swept the bean out of her grip. The bean landed far across the carpet. Sheila avoided the broom, but the dog woke up and ate the bean in one swift bite. Sheila returned to the garden and found another bean in the soil. It was just as big and as heavy as the first one. As Sheila was pulling the bean from the ground, a chick went over and tried to peck at the bean. "Shoo! Go away!" said Sheila. "This is my bean. You have your chicken feed!" Sheila hid under the bean as the chick's sharp beak pecked at the soil. The chick returned to her chicken food and left Sheila and the bean alone. "Thank goodness that's over," said Sheila. With one strong and swift tug, Sheila loosened the bean from the soil and it shot out. Sheila fell over and the bean rolled towards the house. "Well, that saves me some carrying to do," she said, getting up and retrieving the bean. Sheila dragged the bean through a puddle by the laundry room. "Agh!" she said, beginning to sweat. "Why does this bean get stuck in water?" She lost her grip and her legs slid forwards, and she fell into the puddle. "Perhaps I should have hunted for something lighter," said Sheila. Sheila made it to the living room, carrying the heavy bean on her back. Her tiredness was turning into exhaustion. "I'm not sure how much further I can go," she said. "I'm running out of energy." As she struggled, she noticed the sleeping dog opening an eye. "Oh, dear," she said. "If the dog wakes up and sees me, I'll be eaten. I had better be quiet." Sheila tiptoed by the dog, hoping that he wouldn't notice her. But just as she passed him, the dog sniffed dust on the carpet and sneezed. A powerful wave of air hit Sheila and knocked her over. She dropped the bean, but at least it did not roll away. The dog then went back to sleep, and Sheila sighed in relief. Sheila made it into the kitchen carrying the bean. She climbed on to the cooking surface, where she found the kettle and pans. "Not far to go," she said, seeing her home - a tiny hole in the kitchen wall. The counter was slippery with water, and she slid, reaching out to hold the electric blender for balance. Now she was really struggling, because the weight of the bean was becoming unbearable. Feeling herself about to drop the bean, there was suddenly a voice. "Sheila?" it said. "Sheila!" said Clive, her younger brother. "I've been looking for you! Where did you disappear to?" "It's a long story," said Sheila. Clive pushed the bean as Sheila dragged it through the water. Clive's help made the task easier for her. "Let me get the other ants to help us," said Clive, vanishing into the crack in the wall. Sheila rested, putting the bean down by the pans. "All this trouble for a week's worth of food," she said to the bean. "But we made it to my home. Sometimes it's worth hunting for treasure." The other ants came and carried the bean through the wall, and Sheila and Clive went home. Post-Reading Questions Where did Sheila live that was so far away? What obstacles did Sheila encounter inside and outside of the house? Re-read. Ask: What did the bean get stuck in? Re-read. Ask: What was Sheila about to do? Re-read. Ask: How much food had Sheila acquired? What do you think is the lesson of the story?
author: Hello English

title: Focus
text: Story Description Dean is not enjoying school because he cannot focus. His father teaches him a method of concentration to help him improve his studies. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Tedious tee-dee-uss The subject was so boring it was tedious. Concentrating con-sun-tray-ting Dean had difficulty concentrating in class. Progressed pru-g-ress-d Dean had progressed well by learning to focus. Immersed im-mur-s-d He enjoyed the subject so much, he became immersed in his work. After school, Dean went Mango picking in the local plantations. He climbed a tree and reached for the nearest ripe mangos, knocking them off and collect them from the ground using a basket. "Concentrate...focus," he said to himself. He reached and tried to grab a mango when he saw a beautiful butterfly. He fell off his branch and landed under the tree. "That was silly," he said. "I feel like doing something else now." During school, Dean listened to the teacher for the first few minutes. He joined in the class reading, but after a while, he felt bored. He got out his own adventure book from home and started reading. "Dean, you must focus and pay attention," the teacher said, catching Dean reading his own book. But Dean drifted into his own world, finding the class work tedious. One day his mother checked on him from the classroom window and found that he was not concentrating. Dean refused to join in during class, and one teacher lost his temper. "This is school, Dean, not playtime!" the teacher snapped. "In the class you do work and contribute. If you want to read or play, you do that at home. You must learn how to focus properly." Dean was uninterested with the angry teacher. It seemed that everybody was always complaining about him. "Do you want to play football and kite with us, Dean?" said Danny and Anita, his school friends. "Forget it," said Dean, feeling sad after the teacher had shouted at him. "I'm going home." "What's wrong with Dean?" said Danny. "He loves playing after school." "I'm not sure," said Anita. "I hope he's all right." "Wake up, Dean," said his mother. "It's too early," said Dean. "I haven't finished sleeping yet." "It's Saturday," said his mother. "And it's already nine in the morning. You should get up." "Thank goodness it's not a school day," said Dean. "I've had enough of studying. What are we doing today?" "You're helping your Dad with grocery shopping," said his mother, and Dean groaned. "He has a surprise for you." "These aren't groceries," said Dean. "They are books." "That's right," said Dean's father. "Surprise!" "This is the surprise?" said Dean. "Your teacher spoke to me about your lack of focus. I'm going to show you how to pay attention, so you don't feel bored." "Do you see what we are doing?" said Dean's father. "We're placing the books in alphabetical order," said Dean. "Hey, there's some really fun and interesting stories here. Perhaps I can read some." "Later you can," said Dean's father. "For now, you must finish the task that you have started. Performing work can be just as fun and playful as playtime. If you treat your work as fun, then you can focus properly." "How are you finding the work I've set you?" said Dean's father. "I'm enjoying it," said Dean. "I haven't thought about playing because I have been having fun." "And you didn't even notice your favourite book on the ground," said Dean's father. "Your focus is improving. I understand you are having problems with maths." "I'm not very good at maths," said Dean. "That's why I have been struggling to pay attention." "Let me show you how fun maths can be," said Dean's father. Dean got a load of maths books and read through them, doing the simple problems. When he found them too easy, he progressed to the harder problems, not breaking his focus. The books kept his attention as he enjoyed doing the problems. If some problems were too difficult, Dean's father showed him how to find the answer. Very soon, Dean felt like he was descending a deep staircase in his mind. He felt happily immersed in learning. He could visualise the questions and the numbers, the divisions and the multiplications. "I never realised maths could be so much fun," he said. "This is much better than trying to pick mangos. Why didn't I understand this before?" Dean realised that by giving something a chance and paying close attention, he enjoyed learning new things. "How was school today?" said Dean's father on Monday evening. "It was better," said Dean. "What did you do?" "We had maths in the morning. I answered all the questions correctly and got praise from the teacher. He said my focus has improved. I was not distracted at all." "Very good," said Dean's father. "I see you're hiding your catapult." "Yeah, I'm going to fire some rocks at the tree trunks, but not until I've finished my homework," said Dean. Post-Reading Questions What happened when Dean could not focus in class? How did Dean's father show him how to focus and enjoy maths? Re-read pages 9-10. Ask: What kind of task did Dean help his father with? Re-read. Ask: How did Dean test himself? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Dean discover about himself? ﻿Why is it important to try some things before dismissing them?
author: Hello English

title: Super Turtle
text: One day, a turtle was swimming peacefully while looking for food. Its favourite food was seaweed. But suddenly, the turtle noticed a girl drowning. Instead of looking for food, the turtle knew he had to help the drowning girl. This turtle was no ordinary turtle. This was the one and only Super turtle! It morphed into its superhero costume and rushed to save the girl. Super turtle told the drowning girl to hold onto its shell, and Superturtle carried her out of the ocean. Superturtle was so strong! The other sea creatures looked at Superturtle saving the girl and they were all so amazed. The girl was saved with the help of her other friends as well. They asked her how was she able to to rise up to the surface, since she was already deep down in the sea. She said she'd explain later. The girl explained that she was saved by a turtle. Her friends laughed at her, but when they saw how serious she was, they believed her. The girl gave Super turtle lots of seaweed for saving her. Super turtle felt so happy. THE END
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Isha  Valentine; Jaikar Marur; Lê Thị  Bích Khoa; Maya  Ramaswamy; Michael Tymbios; Prom  Vichet

title: Best Friends
text: Story Description A mouse watches a goat playing hopscotch and wants to be her new friend. He goes over to her cabin to try and wake her up to play for the day. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Energetic en-er-jet-ic The rat was lively and energetic. Lethargic le-thar-jic The goat was tired and lethargic. Burrowed buh-road The rat dug in its paws and burrowed into the cabin. Encouragement in-cu-rij-munt The rat gave the goat some encouragement while playing. Georgina the goat was very fond of fishing. She took her rod to the shore, where she sat for hours watching the sea surface. Then she realised she had not put the rod under the water to catch fish. "I knew I was doing something wrong," she chuckled to herself. Georgina and her goat friend Bill wanted to play hopscotch, so Georgina drew a grid for them to use. Little did Georgina realise that a rat was watching them play, excited to join in. But the rat was a little too shy to go over and ask. Georgina and Bill jumped around playing hopscotch until they were tired. The rat's name was Ronald and he was a very energetic rodent. He climbed trees, scurried across trunks and did road running. He was full of energy - almost the opposite to Georgina, who was lethargic and lazy. The very next day, Ronald had nothing to do. He thought of Georgina and wondered if she would like to play. He had been too shy to ask, so he thought he would take a chance and ask her out. Ronald rapped his knuckles against Georgina's door. "Hello!" he called. "It's Ronald the rat. I was watching you play hopscotch yesterday, and was wondering if you would like to come outside and play with me today. Hello?" "Oh, maybe she's ignoring me," Ronald wondered. Ronald jumped up and down and from side to side, waving his arms. He realised that Georgina wasn't ignoring him. In fact......she was fast asleep in bed. It was already ten in the morning, and she wasn't even awake. "What a lazy goat!" said Ronald, laughing to himself. "I know how to wake her up!" Ronald found a weak part of the ground outside where the soil was soft. He burrowed as fast as he could, making a big hole under the door. His little legs and arms worked quickly, and he made clouds of dust and rubble as he got through. "Go away, Bill!" said Georgina. "I'm not available today. I am ill." The scurrying and digging continued and Georgina got annoyed. "That silly goat won't take a hint," she muttered. "Bill, I'm not interested! Leave me alone!" "Oh, you're not Bill," said Georgina. "You're not even the same kind of creature." "Pleased to meet you, I'm Ronald. I was watching you play hopscotch yesterday and I want to be your friend." "Well...why not, I suppose?" said Georgina. "Good," said Ronald. "Now get up, lazy bones. You're oversleeping!" "Whoa, don't pull my leg!" said Georgina. "My body will wake up naturally." "Unlikely," said Ronald. "I doubt you were going to get up at all today. Come on, we're going outside! Ngghh!" "Ahh," said Ronald. "Now I'm exhausted. I think I pulled a muscle." "I'm Georgina. What are we going to do today, Ronald?" "Anything we want," said Ronald. "How about a game of hopscotch?" "Sure, but you'll have to teach me how to play. I forgot." Ronald taught Georgina how to play hopscotch. In fact, he had to teach her three times until she remembered. Suddenly Georgina felt alive, and all of her tiredness had gone. She threw a rock and jumped around the board. Ronald watched, clapping and giving her encouragement. "What are we going to do next?" said Ronald. "Choose an activity." "How about we go to the beach?" said Georgina. "It's too far away," said Ronald. "Well, we can try going fishing." "That sounds fun," said Ronald. "But I don't have a rod." "You can borrow mine," said Georgina. "Because you're my new best friend." Post-Reading Questions What are the differences in character between Ronald and Georgina? When is the first time that Ronald sees Georgina? Re-read. Ask: ﻿How did Ronald get inside Georgina's place? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿Who did Georgina think was making the noise? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Georgina allow Ronald to borrow? ﻿What makes a good friend?
author: Hello English

title: All Right on the Night
text: Story Description Kaashi plays the role of a dancer and a prince in the school play, but on the night of the performance, something goes wrong. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Relentless re-lent-luss They carried on practicing their lines relentlessly. Realistic re-al-ist-ic They needed a tiger that looked more realistic than fake. Rehearsal re-hur-s-all In the rehearsal, they practiced their lines and positions on the stage. Improvise im-pruh-v-eyes When they forgot their lines, the girl improvise d and made something up. At Kaashi's school, the students were putting on a performance of The Brave Prince - a play about a group of people defending a kingdom against nasty invaders. Some of the students were playing animals like goats, horses and monkeys, and they had to be sewn into their outfits. The costumes were very hot inside and uncomfortable. Kaashi was the star of the show. She was playing the lead role of the warrior prince - a cunning, brave and relentless young man intent on protecting his people. Kaashi had to wear a fake moustache to show that she was portraying a man. But her moustache was wonky - it kept sliding off her face, and she had to stick in back on! The cast rehearsed their lines and their scenes. In one scene, Kaashi's friend Aabha was playing the queen, and she was being attacked by a tiger. The producers laughed as the actors got their lines wrong. "It needs to look more realistic," Aabha complained. "We could get a real tiger." On the night of the play, the theatre was fully prepared for the guests. Parents, siblings and friends started arriving. The theatre was filling up, and Kaashi felt nervous. "Don't worry," said one of the actors to Kaashi. "You'll be fine. Remember the saying - it'll be all right on the night!" The theatre was almost full and last minute rehearsals and dressing was taking place back stage. The teachers were sitting in their chairs, and the principal wished everyone good luck. But Kaashi was still concerned. She kept peeking out of the curtain. There, on the front row, she saw her parents and her younger sister Meena. They saw Kaashi and waved. Meena was really excited to see Kaashi in her costume, and she couldn't stop giggling. Kaashi waved back to them, feeling a little more comfortable. "Now I can't mess up because my family is watching," she said. Kaashi could not resist peeking out, and she hid when she saw the final seat taken. The lights began to fade and Kaashi's heart beaten faster. She began to sweat as her nerves kicked in. She got the feeling of butterflies in her stomach. The other actors ushered her back stage to take their positions. Kaashi's scene soon arrived. She was with Mrs. Kumar, who was playing her mother in the play. Kaashi took to the stage and performed her dance, as the knights behind her discussed their lines. They had clearly forgotten them, so Kaashi improvised and continued dancing, giving the knights time to remember their lines. Nobody in the audience noticed the mistake. However, in the very next scene, Kaashi went to pick up a shield when she slipped on the stage and fell hard. She bashed her knee, her ankle bracelet tore off and she lost her forehead jewellery. The audience gasped, and the stage producers quickly drew the curtain across so nobody could see anything more. Mrs. Kumar fetched the first aid kit as Kaashi cried. "I ruined the play! I ruined everything!" she blurted out. "No, it's not your fault," said Mrs. Kumar and Aabha. "You must rest. The play will continue." But Kaashi was very determined. After the audience heard what had happened......the play went on, and Kaashi assumed the role of the prince, using her hair after her moustache fell off. She could not dance because of her bad knee, but she stood still and delivered her lines perfectly. At the end of the play, everyone gave Kaashi a round of applause for being so determined to continue. "I knew it would be all right on the night," she laughed. Post-Reading Questions What role did Kaashi play in the performance? How did Kaashi rescue the show after her fall? Re-read pages 8-10. Ask: Who did Kaashi see in the audience? How did she feel? Re-read. Ask: What did Kaashi do when the knights forgot their lines? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What happened to Kaashi's fake moustache? What is the lesson of the story? Consider Kaashi's accident.
author: Hello English

title: The Sun and the Moon
text: The sun and the moon were best friends! They were inseparable. They loved looking at the stars together and looking under them to see the earth. One day, the sun felt so hot! It accidentally burned the moon. The moon thought it was deliberate so it got mad! The moon ran away and the sun was so sad. The sun's tears were dripping so hard that it rained on earth. All the animals tried to comfort the sun but the sun didn't stop crying. The moon hid behind the biggest stars so that the sun wouldn't find it. The moon lost a part of itself because of how the sun burned him. The sun asked the fish in the oceans for help, but they said they can only see the moon at night hiding behind stars. The sun tried looking for the moon until midnight, but the sun couldn't help but sleep. To this day, the sun is still looking for the moon to say sorry. This explains why the sun can be seen in the morning and the moon can be seen at night with the stars. It sometimes rains because of the sun's tears from crying. THE END
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Greystroke; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Salim  Kasamba; Tapas Guha; Vidyun Sabhaney; Wesley   van Eeden

title: Will the Missing Baby Whale
text: Jenny was riding her submarine deep down in the ocean when she heard a sea animal crying so loud. She thought it must have been a whale. She wondered why it was crying so she drove her submarine closer to the loud sound. Jenny spotted the crying whale and asked the translator in her submarine, "What's wrong? Why are you crying?" The whale gave out a loud scream and said, "I can't find my baby Will!" I can't find my baby Will. I'm so sad. Mama whale teamed up with Jenny to find Will by asking other sea creatures. "I saw a crying baby whale earlier, and it looked just like you!" said a jellyfish. Jenny's submarine heard a baby whale's weeping, and with the help of the jellyfish, they all teamed up to find baby. Jenny suddenly saw a baby whale like figure and quickly swam towards it. Then there he was! Baby Will! Mama whale quickly swam towards him. Mama whale thanked Jenny for helping her. "I'm so glad to have you back," she said to Will.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lê Thị  Bích Khoa; R. Surendran; Sonali Zohra

title: Atchoo
text: My grandma visited me after such a long time. I was very happy because I really missed eating the yummy foods she cooked! She even brought her cat Fidel with her and they were going to stay for a week. While grandma was cooking, I played and took care of Fidel, and he was the nicest cat! He had such soft fur and had such cute ears and whiskers! He liked licking my arm and face. The next day, my nose felt so itchy! "Atchoo!" I loudly sneezed. I thought it was just a normal sneeze but I couldn't stop! I thought it was nothing, so I just continued with my day and I took care of Fidel. I fed him his favourite - canned tuna! He ate so happily. But the next day, I felt so sick! I couldn't get out of bed! I sneezed nonstop and my nose felt so so itchy. I wanted to take my nose off! Grandma and mama took care of me and Fidel also watched over me in my room. "Atchoo!" I kept sneezing. It had been one week since I'd started. I was so sad that I couldn't taste grandma's cooking. I was also sad that Grandma and Fidel had to leave. The next day, I suddenly felt much better! I still went to the doctor just in case it was serious. The doctor asked if I was allergic to anything and I answered no. The doctor said it might be because of animals. Fidel! No wonder why I kept sneezing! I was with him the whole time. Now I know that I'm allergic to cats, I can't hang out with him.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; George Supreeth; Priyanka Agarwal; Rai; Subinita Deshaprabhu; Tanvi Bhat

title: The Crab that Lost its Shell
text: One day, a crab lost its shell. It was so sad because it felt so empty. It went to a dirty beach to find a new shell. The crab tried a candy wrapper as its shell, but it felt too thin! It still wanted its original shell. The crab tried an egg shell, but it was not strong enough to protect the poor crab. It still wanted its old shell back! The crab tried a lemon as its shell, but it felt too uncomfortable as it was wet! Suddenly his friend crab told him where he could find a shell, and he was so happy. He found a beautiful green shell similar to his old one. He was invited to the shell party.
author: Repostly Admin

title: The Frog Wanted a Star
text: Mr Frog loved night time more than day time. This is because he loved stars, and he always looked at them and wished he could keep one. He loved how they twinkled and loved how yellow they were. Mr Frog really wanted a star, so he climbed up the tallest coconut tree he could find to reach the nearest star. Even though he was scared of heights, he tried his best to reach to the top. He got to the top of the coconut tree and stretched his arm out to catch the nearest star, but it was still too far! He stretched and stretched but then he accidentally fell! Suddenly, Mr Frog not only was next to one star but thousands of them! He had never felt happier. He was finally able to touch one and suddenly it spoke to him! "Hi, Mr Frog! My name is twinkle sparkle." Mr Frog couldn't believe it! A star was talking to him! Mr Frog hugged Twinkle Sparkle and suddenly Mr Frog started glowing and he morphed into a star himself! Hi Mr Frog! My name is twinkle sparkle. Twinkle Sparkle and Mr Frog floated across the sky. Mr Frog was having the time of his life! But suddenly he noticed he lost his glow and became a frog again, so he fell from the sky! Mr Frog screamed as he fell. Mr Frog opened his eyes and saw his frog friends Fred and Francis. "You're finally awake!", said Fred. "That was a pretty hard fall," added Francis. "You saw me become a star?", asked mr Frog. Both Fred and Francis laughed. Mr Frog wondered why. Fred and Francis explained that Mr Frog never even got near to a star. He fell from the tall coconut tree and dreamed it all up. Mr Frog felt upset because it was so real. Poor Mr Frog. "I'll try again next time," he said.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Proiti  Roy; Shrujana Shridhar; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: Mary the Musician Magician
text: Mary loved music. She could play every instrument! She could also make every instrument come alive! Mary speaks a magic spell and the instruments play by themselves. She's not only a musician but also a magician! But one night, all her instruments disappeared except for her flute! Mary was really worried because she had a talent show the next day and she had to perform with all of her instruments! Mary, with the help of her flute, looked for the rest of her instruments. They followed the music prints of the instruments and they went a long way. They arrived in a cave and inside there was an evil witch! The witch hypnotised Mary's instrument to go to her because the witch was jealous of Mary's magic. "What's your secret?" the angry witch asked as she couldn't make them play music. The witch didn't know Mary had a spell! The witch went crazy because she couldn't figure out how to make the instruments play. Then suddenly she exploded! Mary and her instruments ran back to their home! They were so lucky to have escaped from the witch. Mary and her instruments were able to perform in front of everyone and everyone was so amazed!
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Wesley van Eeden; Shivika Nayyar; Wesley   van Eeden

title: Too Many Balloons
text: There was once a girl named Lily. She loved balloons! Her mother gave her a dollar every day and she used that dollar to buy a red balloon. She now had ten balloons! She was so happy. She had five on the right and five on the left. Everyone called Lily the balloon girl. Then suddenly, she started flying! At first, she felt so excited like a bird, but when she kept getting higher, she felt so scared! Suddenly a magical golden bird appeared and it helped Lily! It popped the balloons and helped Lily slowly come down to the land. Lily thanked the golden bird, and she used her dollar that day to buy the golden bird a treat instead of a red balloon. She learned that she shouldn't have too many balloons.
author: Repostly Admin
illustrator: Moses  Dhladhla; Sunaina  Coelho; Wiehan de Jager

title: Pigeon Pals
text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description A grandfather educates his grandson about pigeons, and his grandson wants to learn how to fly. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Gregarious gre-g-air-ee-uss A social species is known to be gregarious. Strut s-t-ru-t The pigeons bob and strut on their feet for attention. Aerodynamic air-oh-dai-nam-ic A bird can fly because it is aerodynamic. Furiously f-your-ee-uss-lee The birds fight in the air furiously for command. "Tim, I want to teach you something," said his grandfather. Tim joined him on the balcony. "How much do you know about pigeons?" "Not much," said Tim. "I know they gather in big groups and people feed bread to them." "Pigeons are marvellous birds. They descended from rock doves, which live on mountains and cliffs by the sea." At the mention of birds, Benny the cat woke up and stretched his paws. "Look, here comes a flock of pigeons," said grandfather. "Do they always travel in large packs?" said Tim. "Yes, packs of between 50 and 100. They are gregarious, which means they are a social species. They keep together and hunt for food for the survival of the group." Grandfather pointed out a pair of birds flying together over the rooftop. "These two are a couple, Tim. They breed and stay together for life. Pigeons are loyal." Tim saw a pigeon preparing to land on the balcony, when Benny the cat saw the bird at the last minute, reaching out and swiping with his paws. "Benny wants to eat him," said Tim. "The bird is too fast for Benny," said grandfather. "We have some seeds and berries on the railings and on the floor," said grandfather. "They want to eat that. Can you see them swarming around, keeping themselves aloft?" "It looks like they are forming a pattern," said Tim. "That's exactly what they are doing. They will form a flock around a food source." Just then, Tim's grandmother showed up. "I'm teaching Tim about the pigeons," said grandfather. "Now Tim knows that male pigeons walk funny and strut, puff up their feathers and fight for a female's attention." "You did that for me!" said grandmother. "You used to strut and dance." "I can see them fighting," said Tim. "They are flipping and turning over in the air." "One of them will dominate and the others will give up," said grandfather. "Do pigeons have enemies?" said Tim. "Well, they do have a predator." "What's that?" "There is another bird that will eat pigeons," said grandfather. "The peregrine falcon - the fastest bird in the sky. It feeds on pigeons in the cities." "Sometimes pigeons are annoying," said grandfather. "Like right now. That pigeon is dropping its payload on the cat's head! Shoo! Go away!" The pigeon pooped on Benny's head and then flew off, leaving Benny feeling annoyed. Another pigeon perched on the outside light, and another started walking into the house. Tim's grandfather ran out of patience and scared the bunch of birds off the balcony, because they were everywhere! "Do you think I can fly?" said Tim. "It's not possible," laughed grandfather. "Your body is not designed to fly. A pigeon's body is, because it is aerodynamic." At that moment, Benny the cat swiped with his paw, catching a pigeon by surprise, which leaped into the air and flew off, far away from the cat.
