Tim started whistling, and the pigeon close to him enjoyed the sound. "Maybe I have to get stronger and more flexible," said Tim. "Then I can at least lift myself off the ground." Tim performed a series of stretches and moves to make his body looser, and the cat copied him. Tim flapped his arms furiously and fast at the sides, trying to get himself to take off. "It's no use," said Tim. "I'm too heavy. I can't get off the ground." Grandfather laughed. "I told you, you can't fly!" he said. The pigeons watched with interest and enthusiasm, using their special recording glasses to take a video of Tim, and show it later to their friends. "Many places consider pigeons to be a pest," said grandfather. "But I consider them harmless. They are friends. They just look for food. They can be messy, pooping all over the city squares, but what creature isn't a little messy? If you see a pigeon, treat it well." One of the pigeons felt so calm around Tim, that it simply walked up into his arms and rested. "Looks like you've made a friend," said grandfather. Post-Reading Questions How many pigeons come together in flocks? How are pigeons like people in behaviour? Re-read. Ask: What annoying thing does the pigeon do to Benny the cat? Re-read. Ask: Why can't Tim fly like a pigeon? Re-read. Ask: What should you do if you see a pigeon? Do you think pigeons are pests or friends?
author: Hello English

title: The Bear Essentials
text: Story Description Bear feels something is missing from his house, so he goes out looking for honey to put in his living room. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Splattering s-pla-tur-ing Bear didn't realise he was splattering paint everywhere. Outsmarted ow-t-s-mar-tid The bee easily outsmarted bear and escaped from him. Engrossed in-grow-ss-d Bear was so engrossed and fixated on eating his watermelon. Devouring de-vow-er-ing He was eating so fast that he was devouring the fruit. Bear had the bear essentials. He had his favourite red chair. His walls were multicoloured with colours blending into one another. He had Van Bear's famous painting of sunflowers. He even had a landscape painting of the famous ship, HMS Woods. But Bear felt there was something missing. "I just need one more item for my collection," he said. With a burst of energy and an idea, he sprang up off his chair with enthusiasm. "I need honey!" he said. "Where's the honey?" Bear said, wandering out of his multicoloured house and past his multicoloured garden. "If only I had the honey. I need my bear essentials." Bear waddled and wobbled his way towards the woods. Bear found a tree, and on the lowest branch was a hive dripping with the freshest, purest honey he could find. Bear licked his lips and dribbled. "Oh, that sweet goodness," he said. "Why are you just out of my reach?" Bear jumped but he still couldn't get the hive out of the tree. "I can bearly reach it," he said. "If only I had worn my shoes. Then I wouldn't have bear feet." Bear jumped higher and prodded the hive, and some honey dripped out, splattering on his head and over his ears. "What's that?" he said, as something flew over his sticky head. "A bee! It's coming for me! Well, I'll swipe that bee before it stings me!" Bear punched the air and kicked and swiped with all of his might, but the bee outsmarted him and darted and avoided him. There was a puddle of mud close by, and bear jumped, launching himself at the bee. "I've got you this time!" he said. "You bearly got me!" said the bee, and Bear fell into the mud with a huge splash. Bear found some long grass and relaxed, laid bear to the bright blue sky. The bee watched him from above. "What is that bear doing?" he said. Bear closed his eyes. "Well, if I can't get any actual honey, then at least I can dream of eating honey." Bear found some berries and chewed on them, getting a red stained mouth. Bear went to the town where he found a giant bucket of paint. "There's no honey in here," he said. "There's not a single hive to be found anywhere." The bucket of paint was filled with different colours. Bear splashed around but he could not find any honey. Instead, he was completely covered in paint. "I can't bear this," said Bear. "There must be honey somewhere." "Excuse me," said Bear to a construction worker painting a huge wall. "Have you seen any honey pots around here?" "There's only paint pots here," said the worker. "And you're stepping in them!" "Oh, dear!" said Bear. "I am so sorry! Look, there's that bee again. I'm going to catch it and steal all of its honey!" Bear ran after the bee. The bee flipped and whizzed, darting back and forth through the air. Big slow Bear was no match for the tiny bee. Bear decided to dance to give himself a better chance at catching the bee. He moved his hips and torso, but the bee simply flew through his armpit. Bear went around in circles, making himself dizzy, and he slipped on some rocks. "Ooh, what's this?" said Bear. Bear found a dripping ripe piece of watermelon by the rocks. He bit into the fruit and licked his lips. "It's so juicy!" he said. "Who needs honey when you have watermelon? I'll devour this and hang the watermelon skin on my living room wall! This is what my house has been missing!" The bee poked his tongue out at Bear and flew back to his hive. Bear didn't miss the bee because he was so engrossed in devouring his delicious watermelon slice! Post-Reading Questions What did bear feel was missing from his home? Bear looked everywhere for honey, but what did he end up finding? Re-read. Ask: What did bear slip straight into while chasing the bee? Re-read. Ask: What did bear not realise that he had done? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What method did bear use to try and catch the bee? ﻿Describe Bear's adventure and his character.
author: Hello English

title: Wiggle Jiggle
text: Wiggle jiggle wriggle! I am a wiggly worm. Yummy in my tummy! Flowers and leaves are my favourite food. Wiggle jiggle wriggle! I am a wiggly worm. I love the rain. Pitter -patter on the leaves. Wiggle jiggle wriggle! Watch me wiggle and dance. My magic poo makes plants grow BIG. POO!!! I love to see my plants grow. Yellow, red, blue and green. I am a wiggly worm. Wiggle jiggle wriggle! Wiggle when you see me in the garden. Wiggle jiggle wriggle! Where am I now? I’m here in my cocoon! Oh wait! I’m not a wiggly worm! Flitter flutter flitter! I am a butterfly!
author: Mathapelo Mabaso

title: Daydreaming Delilah
text: Story Description During creative writing class, Delilah imagines different characters and stories she could write about. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Daydreaming day-dr-ee-ming ﻿Delilah spent the lesson daydreaming what to write about. Futuristic few-chur-ist-ic ﻿She saw a futuristic world. Super Heroine soup-er-heh-ro-in ﻿She was a female superhero - a super heroine, saving the world. Imagination im-a-ji-nay-sh-un ﻿Delilah used her imagination to see a story. Delilah's favourite class was English. During English class, her favourite activity was Creative Writing time. One day, she had 30 minutes to write a short story on any subject she liked. So Delilah started her favourite hobby - daydreaming. She went into her imagination and looked for something to write about. What would she create? She imagined she was on a different world with a green sky and buildings made of sand. It was a world where she could blow bubbles and fly. This is incredible, she thought. I can move around just by blowing bubbles! The faster Delilah blew bubbles, the sooner she could get higher and reach the goat near the clouds. But she went straight past the goat and got swallowed up by the cloud! Then Delilah had to eat her way out of the mist. Delilah saw herself on a warm, sunny and orange world, with the ability to fly. She also had big, floppy ears that blew in the wind. She flew as fast as she could, passing an aeroplane and waving to the passengers inside. Delilah imagined herself to be on a hot, fiery world filled with lava. She was inflated like a huge ball, bouncing from place to place. When Delilah blew out, she took off. But she could not stop herself bouncing from one piece of land to the next. "It's too hot to live here and I can't control myself!" she said. Delilah imagined herself to be a fighting superheroine. She was the Divine Vine, queen of the forest and hero of the trees. Her arms were made of vines, fruits and flowers, and she could fire her long arms and fruit at anyone. She fired tomatoes at a many cruelly running away with a tree trunk. "Leave my friends alone!" Delilah said. Delilah saw a futuristic world with factories and robots. She was a detective who had to sneak inside a building and shut it down. She confused the robots. They could detect life, but they could not see it. Delilah ran around wearing an invisibility cloak, making faces and laughing at the robots. Delilah saw herself as a completely flat person trying to break into a room filled with secrets. No girls were allowed inside, so Delilah slid perfectly under the door through the tiny gap, and back outside once more with the book of boy's secrets. Delilah saw a small fire that had to be put out. She had the ability to fire steam from her belly button, which extinguished the fire in seconds. She could also boil water and warm a room up in seconds. Delilah saw herself as a super hero, as the queen of the class, as the most intelligent student. She stood on the desk and the sun shone upon her, lighting her up. But when she stopped daydreaming, Delilah realised she only had 10 minutes left to write something, and she had not even written a single word yet! Post-Reading Questions How much time did Delilah have to write a lesson? What did Delilah suddenly realise after all of her daydreaming? Re-read. Ask: On the lava world, how does Delilah move around? Re-read. Ask: Why can't the robots see Delilah? Re-read. Ask: What can Delilah make from her belly button? Do you think Delilah finished her story? What would you write about?
author: Hello English

title: Sing to Me
text: Mama loves to sing. She sings high. She sings low. She sings like a twittering bird. Mama loves to sing. She sings high. She sings low. She sings like an angel. Mama loves to sing. She sings high. She sings low. She sings like the pattering rain. Mama loves to sing. She sings high. She sings low. My mama loves to sing to me.
author: Nicole Levin

title: A Bad Feeling
text: Story Description Anita gets a bad feeling that someone needs her help, and she leaves her class to investigate the hills. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sensation sen-say-sh-un Anita felt a strange sensation in her stomach. Refused re-f-use-d The elephant refused to move at all. Complained com-play-n-d The elephant complained about its sore foot. Salute suh-lew-t The elephant gave Anita a trunk salute for helping. Anita's class was having an outdoor lesson day. They were studying Geography when suddenly there as a noise. None of the class could hear it except for Anita. She felt the noise inside her stomach. Something was happening in the distance, and Anita felt anxious. There was danger. Someone was in need of help. She could not ignore her senses. "Excuse me, miss," said Anita. "I forgot my class book. Can I go back and get it?" "All right," said the teacher. Anita followed the noise towards its source. It was coming from somewhere high up. She looked to the hills. Just then, a parrot perching on a tree branch called down to her. "You must help," it said. When Anita looked behind her, the parrot was gone. She was left alone in the field of flowers. "Excuse me," Anita said to a crow. "Have you seen a parrot here? I swear I just heard one." "The only parrot I know lives on that hill," said the crow. "Are you all right, little girl?" "I feel that somebody needs my help," said Anita. "I must go. I'm in a hurry." Anita reached the hedgerow and the open fields, where she found various kinds of flowers. There was another strange sensation guiding her also, encouraging her to go to the hills. She could not see anything, but she felt as if many energies were surrounding her. She had heard stories of the spirits of the land protecting the place. "I had best not do anything to upset them," she said. As Anita began climbing the steep slope of the hill, she saw the parrot that had been calling to her. "There you are," she said. "I need your help," said the parrot. "My friend is in trouble. Please come as quickly as you can. Hurry!" Anita ran up some steps and chased after the parrot. "Please be quick," said the parrot. "He is in great distress." Anita got that strange feeling in her stomach again and proceeded after the parrot, descending some slopes and passing huge boulders. The wind was stronger on the higher ground and she felt herself losing her balance. "Oh, my," said Anita. "I thought it would be a person in need of help, not an animal." "The elephant has a bad foot. A bunch of mice chased him up this slope. Being terrified of them, he ran away. While he was running, he stepped on a nail. He refuses to go down the hill back to his home, because he's afraid the mice are still there." "You need that nail removed from your foot," said Anita to the elephant, who refused to move. Anita climbed on the elephant, who took slow steps forward. "Take your time and be slow," said Anita. "We don't want your injury to get worse." "He lives down the hill at the farm," said the parrot. "You'll have to show me the way," said Anita. Along the way, the elephant raised its trunk in pain and wobbled, trying to shrug Anita off his back. "I'm here to help you," she said to the elephant. "I felt you call out in pain. It's not far to your home. You have to help me by walking the rest of the way. If you don't, then you will be stuck here and your foot will get worse. Please let me take you back to the farm." The elephant complained. "If I see any mice, I will chase them away," said Anita. The elephant agreed to let Anita take him home, and they moved on over the hills, going down into the valley. Eventually they arrived at the farm, where the locals removed the nail from the elephant's foot, stitched the wound, and comforted the poor creature. They thanked Anita for being in the right place, and the parrot said farewell to her. The elephant raised its trunk to salute Anita for her kindness, and Anita returned to her outdoor class. Post-Reading Questions When did Anita realise that someone needed her help? Where did the trail of clues lead Anita to? Re-read. Ask: What was Anita's first clue? Re-read. Ask: Why did the elephant refuse to move downhill? Re-read. Ask: How did Anita convince the elephant to walk? Describe the feeling when you know something is wrong.
author: Hello English

title: The Tale of the Tail
text: Story Description Ralph the squirrel has an abnormality - he was born with a very long tail. Tired of exhaustion from dragging his heavy tail, Ralph asks a doctor to fix him with a new one. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Abnormality ﻿ab-nor-mal-it-ee ﻿Ralph was born with an abnormality, having a very long tail. Slender ﻿sl-end-ur ﻿Ralph's new tail was sleek and slender, like a squirrel's. Environment ﻿en-vai-ru-munt ﻿Ralph was tired of running away from predators in his environment. Exhibit ﻿eg-zib-it ﻿The old tail was put on an exhibit wall at the hospital, so everyone could see it. Ralph the squirrel had an abnormality - he was born with a very long tail. Ralph's tail was so long and heavy that he was always tired from carrying it around. "There has to be a solution to this problem," said Ralph, sitting exhausted by a tree. "I'm tired of carrying this heavy, long tail. It's wearing me out!" One day Ralph had had enough... "Doc, doc, I need your help," said Ralph, running into the hospital. "What's wrong, my boy?" said the doctor, but it didn't take him long to spot the problem. "My goodness, how do you carry that around with you all day?" "I pretend I'm a monkey," said Ralph. "Please can you fit me with a new tail? Preferably one that is smaller. A lot smaller." "There's usually a waiting list for an operation," said the doctor. "But yours is a special case, my little friend. I am going to help you get a better tail." "Thanks doc, thanks," said Ralph. "You don't know how much this means to me." "First, my boy, I have to examine you. Let's go out to the yard." Ralph followed the doctor to the yard, and the doctor saw the true length of Ralph's tail. "You are a unique specimen," said the doctor. "That means you're one of a kind, Ralph." "I'm tired of it getting trapped in things," said Ralph. "Like doors and in trees and around branches." "I see that your tail has caused you a poor quality of life. All right, my boy, we will operate early on Monday morning." "Thanks, doc," said Ralph. Monday morning came and went, and Ralph awoke at the hospital with a new tail. A little cat's tail! "How do you feel?" said the doctor. "I feel great! And what a wonderful tail! Black and white and bushy." "It's the closest thing we could find to a normal tail," said the doctor. "It's good enough for me," said Ralph. "Let's put it to the test!" Ralph slept like a cat on the grass. However, a dog had been watching Ralph, and he barked really loud. "I'm not a cat, I'm a squirrel!" said Ralph. But the dog kept chasing him over tree trunks and through flowers. The dog would not slow down and Ralph had to hide in a tree. "I don't think this tail is good either!" said Ralph. He went back to see the doctor. "What's wrong, my boy?" said the doctor, seeing Ralph running through the door again. "Back so soon?" "No good, doc," said Ralph. "Now my life is in danger. Dogs and cats chase me. Birds come after me. I don't know what they think I am, but they want to eat me!" The doctor tested some new technology on Ralph, by giving him an artificial squirrel's tail. He trimmed around its edges to make the tail the right shape. "Just a few more adjustments and it's done," said the doctor. "Excellent. Let's wake our patient up and see what he thinks!" Ralph felt confused. His new tail was as light as a feather. Also it was attractive, and bushy, slender and sleek. He could carry it around easily. It did not get trapped. And it looked exactly like a normal squirrel's tail. Ralph sat perched on branches. No predators came near him. No other squirrels laughed at or made fun of him. He blended into his environment. He felt like a normal squirrel. "How are you doing, Ralph?" said the other squirrels. "Hey, your tail looks cool. Did you get it trimmed?" "It's a long story," said Ralph. "Let's just say I'm an entirely new squirrel." "Great to hear that," they replied. "You never want to lose your tail." Ralph went straight to the hospital to see the doctor. "How's your new tail, my boy?" said the doctor. "Oh, it's wonderful. I can carry it with me everywhere. It's light weight. It dries quickly, and nobody tries to attack it. I can't thank you enough, doc, I really can't. I'm so grateful." "I'm just glad that you're happy with a good quality of life now," said the doctor. "What happened to my old tail?" said Ralph. "Oh, I'll show you!" "We made a tail exhibit," said the doctor. "That's amazing," said Ralph. "Look at all of these different tails! There's my old one!" "Now my students can learn about transplants and tails," said the doctor. "Your tail will stay on this wall because it is special." "Good, because I prefer my new one!" laughed Ralph. Post-Reading Questions Name the different tails that Ralph had, and his problems having a long tail. What kind of tail was Ralph happy with? Re-read. Ask: What did Ralph keep getting his tail trapped in? Re-read pages 8-10. Ask: Why did Ralph go rushing back to the doctor? Re-read pages 11-13. Ask: How did Ralph's new tail improve his life Re-read. Ask: What did the hospital create as an exhibit on their wall? If you could change one thing about yourself, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: The Disappearing Coconuts
text: Story Description Glue, newspaper and coconuts are disappearing from Ameena's house, and her parents are confused as to why. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Sheer sh-ear The number of coconuts around was a sheer large one. Raided ray-did Someone had raided the bowl of buttons and taken many. Culprit cul-prit Nobody knew who the culprit was of the crime. Rosette row-zet Ameena had made a beautiful rosette out of her materials. Ameena noticed that her father was bringing home lots of coconuts from the beach. The sheer number of coconuts gave Ameena a great idea. She started taking them one by one, hoping that her father would not notice them going missing, since there were so many of them. Ameena took them, one by one, as her father cut them open to scrape out the insides. As he worked, he suddenly realised he had a few less coconuts than he came home with. "What's happening to my coconuts?" he asked. "Where are they disappearing to? I swear that I came home with more coconuts than this." Ameena sat in her room, secretly painting the coconuts. She had sheets of newspaper, glue and pots of paint with brushes. She had coconut shells dangling from string attached to her ceiling. But what was she doing to all of the coconuts? Granny returned from the market to see her bowl of buttons and bits and bobs raided, lying knocked over on the floor. "Who could have done such a thing, and why?" she asked herself. "Were they looking for something valuable in that bowl?" She suspected Ameena's mother. Ameena searched underneath her carpet for something important. "Now where did I put it?" she said. "That was a really good button. I can't believe I've lost it." Ameena had been working on a painting, but she needed that button for a very important project. Suddenly her glue was missing. Ameena's mother came back from the shops to see that her newspaper was missing. She loved reading her daily newspaper, but someone had just swiped it away. She asked Ameena's father, but he denied taking it. That could only mean that either granny or Ameena was the culprit. "Have you taken my newspaper?" said Ameena's mother to granny. "No, have you been stealing my buttons?" said granny. "Of course not." "Then I wonder who has been taking our things!" Finally, Ameena's father confronted her. "Where have all my coconuts been disappearing to?" he said. "Have you seen my glue?" said Ameena. "I'm working on an important project and someone has stolen it from me." Ameena finished her project and allowed everyone into her room. They saw the coconuts and the newspaper. Ameena showed them the painted coconut rosette covered in buttons. Ameena's mother, father and granny were all amazed at the artistic work she had created, and Ameena apologised for stealing the coconuts. "By the way, I took the glue," said granny. ﻿ ﻿Post-Reading Questions ﻿Why did Ameena steal the coconuts, and what did she make out of them? How did father know his coconuts were going missing? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did granny find when she entered the room? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What happened to mother when she was going to read the paper? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the family see that Ameena had made? ﻿Name something that grows which is used during Hallowe'en.
author: Hello English

title: New Glasses!
text: Story Description Kira goes for an eye test and realises she needs glasses. Kira sees how her eyesight improves over time. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Fuzzy fuh-zee Kira's eyesight was blurred and fuzzy. Trademark tray-d-mar-k Kira grew to like the glasses. They became her trademark item. Fashionable fa-sh-un-a-bul The children thought Kira's glasses were fashionable. Identity eye-den-t-tee The glasses gave Kira a sense of identity. Kira was very upset. She had been having problems seeing things properly. She wanted to play football, but she could not focus on the ball. She could not see the face of her dolly. Everything became fuzzy. "We're taking you to the hospital to get your eyesight tested," said Kira's mother. "The doctor will know what is best to do." "Oh, no!" said Kira. "I don't want to wear glasses. It's ok, Mama. My eyes are fine. I've changed my mind about seeing the doctor." "What's wrong?" said her mother. "Is it about wearing glasses?" "Yes, all the kids will make fun of me at school." "Let's just get your eyes tested first," said her mother. Kira went to see the specialist eye doctor, who gave her a pink pair of glasses to read things at a distance. Kira read words on a board. "Very good," said the doctor, even when Kira got it wrong. "Now we'll trying something else." "Here's a board with lots of letters," said the doctor. "The letters get gradually smaller and harder to read. I want you to cover one eye at a time and read the letters for me." "E, F, P, T, U, X," said Kira. As she went down the list she slowed her reading and struggled to see the letters. "Now cover your right eye," said the doctor. Kira placed her hand over her right eye and started reading again. "E, F, P, T, O, X, L," she said. "And the next line please," said the doctor. But Kira could not read the letters. They were to fuzzy. So she guessed the answers and laughed. The doctor told Kira that she was long-sighted, and that she required special glasses. He wrote a prescription and gave it to Kira's mother. Very soon, Kira walked around wearing a new pair of glasses. "Hi, Sammy," said Kira. "Kira, is that you?" said Sammy. "Wow, you're wearing glasses, I didn't recognise you! You look great." Kira looked around a tree. The colours were sharp and clear like never before. She saw each individual leaf in a different colour, the rough edges of the branches, and the beautiful patterns on the birds' bellies. "It's fantastic," she said, feeling the leaves and the tree bark. Kira even tried playing football, and to her delight, she could clearly see the ball and time her shots correctly. She used to miss the ball or accidentally kick another player, but this time she could focus properly. "I think you'll make the team now," said Thomas. "So how are your new glasses?" said the doctor on her return visit. "They're great," said Kira. "None of the kids make fun of me. In fact, they're quite fashionable. I can play football again and run. I can see my dolly's face, my mother's face, and all the faces of my friends. I can see the birds and trees very well." "Excellent," said the doctor. "If you have any other eye problems, don't hesitate to come back and see me again." Kira felt that her glasses gave her a better identity. They were now a trademark, and all of her friends commented on how great they looked. Kira's fear that her friends would not accept her was just a worry. "Now you can come exploring and fossil hunting with us," said Mark. "You won't fall down any steep hills." Post-Reading Questions At the beginning, why was Kira scared of getting glasses? What things could Kira see more clearly after wearing her glasses? Re-read. Ask: What did Kira's friend say when she saw the glasses? Re-read. Ask: How had Kira's football skills improved? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the doctor advise Kira to do? ﻿What do you think the lesson of the story is?
author: Hello English

title: Big Fish, Little Fish
text: Story Description Lido the little fish gets taken to the deep sea to learn survival skills, when he encounters a big shark. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Poisonous poy-zun-uss There are poisonous reefs in the sea. Somersault sum-ur-salt The little fish performed a somersault to escape the shark. Wheezed w-ee-z-d The fish wheezed and caught its breath. Channel chan-ul There was a little channel where the fish could hide. Lido lived at the bottom of the sea with his friends the octopus, the crab, and the green girl fish he liked. His mother kept a constant look out for bigger fish who could eat them. There was always danger present, but Lido was very relaxed for a fish. He was too calm. "Where are you going, Lido?" said the lobster, peeking over the bank. "My mother is taking me to the deep sea outside the village, to get me used to deeper waters. She says I'm now old enough to learn how not to get in trouble." "Good luck, my friend," said the lobster. "Hope you don't see a shark!" Which is exactly what Lido encountered. His mother had warned him to keep by her side, when he drifted a little too far back. The shark woke up and saw his lunch swimming by. "That's a really big dark rock," said Lido. "Mum! Look at this rock! It's shaped exactly like a..." "Shark!" Lido called out. The shark flipped and lashed, making Lido somersault in the water. Lido couldn't see the shark as it prepared to turn and devour him. The shark got closer, just when Lido's mother rushed to his aid. She embraced Lido in her arms and swam away. The shark was shocked at how quick his mother was. He had nearly got a free meal. "I told you to stay close to my side," said Lido's mother. "Otherwise predators will see you alone and go in for the bite. You must listen to my advice. It will keep you alive in deep waters. You are lucky I wasn't so far away, or that shark would have eaten you." "I'm sorry, Mama," said Lido. "And don't touch things you're not sure about," said Lido's mother. "You never know. It could be poisonous. It could be a camouflaged predator. Stay close to my side and swim with me." "You're right, Mama," said Lido. "I'm sorry." Out of nowhere, the shark snapped its tail and made a dash for Lido. The little fish saw the big fish at the last moment and squealed. But his Mama did not hear him, because she had just been carried away with the current, and she struggled to escape from it. She called out to Lido, but he could not hear her. The shark chased Lido, snapping its jaw constantly. Lido remembered his mother's advice: keep darting and dashing, dipping and weaving. Confuse the fish and it won't get you. Lido was running out of energy and breath. He wheezed as the shark closed in with its gigantic mouth. Lido cried and panicked. He was helpless. He knew this would surely be his last moment alive. Lido closed his eyes and went through a narrow channel between two rocks. The shark bashed its face against the hard surface, then turned around, looking for a way to get to Lido. But the shark was too big to fit into the gap. The shark tried fitting its nose and mouth through the gap, but it could not open its jaw. Lido was just a little too far away to be caught. The shark gave up and whacked the rocks with its tail, then it swam away to look for a different meal. "I'm so sorry," said Lido's mother, helping him out from the narrow channel. "I was carried away with the current. I left you open for attack. I'll never do that again." "It's all right, Mama," said Lido. "I escaped from the shark all by myself." "What?" said Lido's mother. "The shark tried to eat me, so I squeezed into that tiny area. It gave up and swam away." Lido's mother put a fin around him and led him home. "I'm so glad to be back home," said Lido. "Look, there's Baby Octopus and his friends! Hey!" "Hey there, Lido," said Baby Octopus. "Did you see any sharks today?" "One big one, and it nearly ate me," said Lido. "Be quiet," said Lido's mother. Post-Reading Questions Who takes Lido into the deep ocean to learn survival skills? Why does Lido's mother tell him to stay close to her side? Re-read. Ask: What happened to Lido's mother and what could she not do? Re-read. Ask: How did Lido get away from the shark? Re-read. Ask: What did Lido's mother say when she was reunited with Lido? What do you think is the lesson of this story?
author: Hello English

title: A Hidden Talent
text: Story Description Greg gets bullied at school, when suddenly he makes a new friend and discovers a hidden talent within himself. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Clumsy c-lum-zee He was clumsy, always dropping or forgetting things. Lettuce let-iss The bully said he should make friends with some lettuce. Enthralled in-thr-all-d The class was enthralled and captivated by the performance. Bumbling bum-bl-ing The three made a funny, bumbling trio. "You should always give a helping hand when you can," said Greg's mother, as she watered the flowers. "I like watering the flowers with you, mum," said Greg. "We have such a wonderful garden. There's so much beauty here. It's a pleasure to help out." Greg enjoyed helping. He liked drawing insects, especially butterflies, and he designed a little garden house for them to hide in, so they could be protected from predators. The trouble was, Greg was clumsy, and he could not build it by himself. He needed help. At school, Greg built a tunnel for the ants to crawl into, because he was concerned for their safety. "Go home, my friends," said Greg, watching the ants go through the tunnel safely back to their ant hill. "Greg, don't go near those ants, they are dirty," said his sports teacher. "Ha, ha," said some of the bullies. "Greg's only friends are insects. That's really sad." "Hey, Greg," said one of the bullies at lunchtime. "I have lettuce in my sandwich. Am I eating one of your friends? Perhaps you want to say goodbye to the lettuce before I eat it. Ha ha!" Greg felt upset and started crying. All he wanted to do was help others. Greg got home from school and cried to his mother. "There, there," she said, soothing him. "Those boys are just being mean. Don't listen to them." Even the fox felt sorry for Greg and offered him a hug. Greg spent his lunchtime by himself on the bench. One day another student came to see him. "I'm Pete," said the little piglet. "I saw what you did for the ants yesterday, and how those boys treated you at lunch. I get treated horribly too." "I'm sorry to hear that," said Greg. "I'm tired of those boys." "Do you like music?" said Pete. "I love music," said Greg. Pete sang some songs and Greg joined in. They discovered that they sang well together, and made a great double act, performing jokes and funny dance moves. They soon got the attention of some of the other boys. "We should form a team," said Pete. "We can help each other out," said Greg. Every lunchtime, Greg and Pete wrote a new song and performed it to the boys, who clapped, laughed and cheered. "You two are hilarious," one of them said. "You're not so bad after all." Even the bullies came round and viewed Greg and Pete differently. During one music class, Greg and Pete showed off a new song, and the class and the teacher were enthralled. Soon Greg and Pete received demands to form a band with the other boys. The bullies stepped forward to ask them to form a group. "We're sorry about giving you a hard time," said the bullies. "Can we join you? We can sing." "I believe in helping someone out," said Greg. "Let's see what you've got." The former bullies had great voices, and they acted as a humorous bumbling trio of singers. Greg played the trumpet and Pete kept the beat going. The group often played outside in the evening. They formed a very tight rhythm section and had a great routine of jokes, and the principal was so impressed when he saw them play, that he asked them to play for the whole school during Friday assembly. "I can't wait to go to school now," said Greg. "Every day is fun!" "That's a change," laughed Greg's father, having seen their band rehearsals. "Are you excited about the assembly?" "It's going to be incredible," said Greg, meeting Pete and the rest of the band inside, and waving goodbye to his dad. "Good luck, boys," said Greg's father. "Help each other out." Post-Reading Questions What did Greg enjoy doing the most? What did Greg discover about the bullies? Re-read. Ask: What did Greg and Pete discover about their talents? Re-read pages 12-13. Ask: How did the bullies change with Greg, and what were they invited to do in front of the school? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Greg now look forward to every day? ﻿What do you think is the lesson of the story?
author: Hello English

title: From Here to There
text: Story Description A snail has to take many paths to get to her husband in the new lands, carrying her babies with her on a long journey. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Hitch-hike hit-ch-hai-k The snail had to hitch-hike its way across the land. Slithers slih-th-urs The snail slithers along the branch. Sanctuary san-c-chew-ary There was a safe new home and sanctuary for snails. Travelled tra-vul-d She travelled far across the land to her husband. There was once a snail with a shell that looked like three scoops of ice-cream. The other snails had spiral shells, but this snail was unique. The snail asked its friends for directions to the new land, because her husband was waiting for her there. They said that going without transport would take her too long, so they recommended hitch-hiking. The snail took its three babies along, because they were going to be reunited with their daddy. "Are you excited to see him?" said the snail. "Yes, yes, yes," said the little ones. "Then hold on, because we are going on a bumpy adventure!" "Can you take us to the new land, toad?" said the snail. "Well, that is a very long way. It is too far for me," said the toad. "That is a shame. We will have to ask someone else." "I can take you part of the way," said the toad. The snail put her three babies inside her shell and slithered on to the toad's back. "Whoa, not so fast," said the snail. "You can trust me," said the frog. "I have the most flexible, darting legs in the land. I'll get you there in next to no time." After the ponds and lilipads, the toad dropped the snail off. Then the snail asked a rat to take it the rest of the way. "I can take you part of the way," said the rat. "Don't get lost," said the snail. "Don't worry. I have the sharpest nose in the land. I always know where I am." The rat dropped the snail off and the snail found a hare, who agreed to take her part of the way. "Don't jump too high," said the snail. "Don't worry," said the hare. "I have the longest leap in the land. I'll get you there in next to no time." After leaping and travelling through warrens, the hare dropped off the snail, and she found a deer. The deer agreed to take her part of the way. "Careful of your antlers," said the snail. "Don't bump into anything." "I can fend off any predator with my antlers," said the deer. After the deer dropped off the snail, she found a cow resting in a field. The cow agreed to take the snail part of the way. "Be careful of rivers and creeks," said the snail. "I don't go anywhere near water except for a drink," said the cow. "So don't worry." The cow dropped the snail off at a farm, and the snail found a wild horse. The horse agreed to take her part of the way. "Don't jump over any fences," said the snail. "I was a racing horse. I'll get you there in next to no time." After travelling with all of the animals, the horse dropped off the snail at the new land sanctuary. "Thank you so much," the snail said to the horse. "Me and my babies are happy now." "You must have taken many roads to get here," said the horse, and the snail laughed. The snail was reunited with her husband, and she told him the tale of how they had travelled. The three babies got out and hugged daddy. They loved their new tree branch and sanctuary. Now the snail family could stay together in one place, as joyful and as happy as they could possibly be. "I knew you would get here in next to no time," said the husband. Post-Reading Questions Who was the snail going to travel across the land to be with? What was the place called where the snails lived? Re-read pages 7-11. Ask: What do all the animals say that they can do for the snail? Re-read. Ask: What kind of horse did the snail travel on? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why were the snails so happy? ﻿What do you think is the lesson of the story?
author: Hello English

title: I Can See You!
text: Story Description Rico the rhino doesn't want to play hide and seek, but when given the chance to find the other animals, he realises what a great game it is! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Directions dye-rec-sh-uns The animals ran in different directions. Distance dis-tun-ss The rhino could see the animals hiding from a long distance. Eyesight eye-s-eye-t The rhino had great eyesight, and he could see where the animals were hiding. Rustling russ-ling The snail made a rustling sound in the leaves. Rico the rhino lived in a big dense forest with lakes and all kinds of colourful creatures around. He was terrified of the big fat rat, who would ask him for money to cross the river bank. He was scared of the bees, who attacked him whenever he and frog tried raiding the hive. He and skunk always got caught stealing eggs from the eagle. Life for Rico was funny yet difficult in the forest. One day all of the forest animals gathered together. There were so many of them! They decided to play games as a big group. "What are we playing?" said bear. "Hide and seek," said deer. "Let's select who will be 'it' - eenie meanie miney mo..." "Oh, dear," said Rico. "I always get caught playing this game." He put his foot in the middle. They selected frog to be 'it' and to go looking for them. Frog counted to a hundred, but when he got to fifty, he fell asleep. All of the animals hid behind rocks and bushes. They could hear snoring. "He's dropped off to sleep again," said squirrel. " We should go and find him instead," said monkey. "I have an idea," said bear. "Why don't we all hide and find Rico?" "I'm not sure that's a good idea," said Rico. "I'm so bad at hiding." "Oh, you'll think of a great place to hide," said rabbit. "I'll try," said Rico. The animals counted to a hundred, but Rico couldn't decide on a place to hide. "Here we come, ready or not," said parrot. They found Rico a few seconds later by the pond. Rico burst into tears. "I can't play this game. I'm terrible at it. Please, let's play something else." "Don't worry," said deer. "It's just a game. Perhaps you needed more time to hide." Rico sat by the pond and looked into the water. "I heard rhinos are excellent at finding things," said bear. "Why don't we all hide and you look for us?" "Really?" said Rico. "That sounds more fun." Rico counted against a tree and all of the animals fled in different directions. "I wonder where they'll hide?" said Rico. "They can't get that far. I have fantastic eyesight. I can see a bear from a great distance." "Here I come," said Rico. "Ready or not!" The animals gasped and cackled. "You're all hiding behind the trees. I can hear skunk laughing and bear breathing." Rico was right. The animals showed their faces. "How could you possibly hear that?" said tortoise. "I told you rhinos are amazing," said bear. "Beginner's luck," said tortoise. "I bet you can't do that again." "Well, let's try," said Rico. He counted to a hundred and the animals hid once more. When Rico finished counting, he pounced away into the forest. He heard scuffling and breathing. "Found you," he said to monkey. "And you, squirrel." Rico walked around the forest when suddenly he heard a bird tweet from the bushes. Deer hushed the bird, but it was too late. Rico was already on their case. He popped his head through the bushes and said, "Gotcha!" "Aww," said owl. "Rico is too good at this game. Let's play something harder." "I want to have a go at finding you," said skunk. "But this time you've only got thirty seconds to hide. I'm counting from now...one...two...three..." The animals wondered where to hide and some scattered in different directions. Rico tried to freeze like a statue when skunk went by, as did monkey and squirrel. Rabbit thought that by covering his ears, he would be invisible. Skunk caught all of them. Skunk slowly found all of the animals, except for one. The animals teamed up but none of them could find the snail. He was small and very good at hiding. "I wonder where he could be?" said squirrel. They tried the trees and by the lake, when suddenly there was a little rustling movement in the leaves. "Snail!" they all cried, and snail popped his eyes up from a leaf. "I suppose it's my turn to find you," said snail. "This is going to take a long, long time." Post-Reading Questions Why was Rico upset while playing hide and seek? What did Rico discover he was very good at doing? Re-read. Ask: Who gave away the animals' hiding positions? Re-read. Ask: Where did Rico find all of the animals hiding? Re-read. Ask: Who was the last creature to find, and where was it hiding? Name three things you are good at doing.
author: Hello English

title: Brewster Rooster's Match
text: Story Description To settle an argument, Brewster the rooster takes on a millipede in a football match of wits and talent. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Millipede ﻿mil-lih-pea-d ﻿The millipede is a long creature with many legs. Disallowed ﻿dis-al-ow-d ﻿The goal was disallowed because the millipede cheated. Protest ﻿pr-oh-test ﻿The chicken ate the football in protest at the millipede. Wiggling ﻿wig-ling ﻿The millipede was wiggling his body in celebration. Millipede had been stealing Brewster the rooster's stash of seeds, selling them to chickens in other farms. Annoyed with millipede's behaviour, he decided to confront the creature. "I'm not going to let that millipede steal any more of my stash," said Brewster. "Those are my seeds to sell." "I'm not going to let you steal any more seeds," said Brewster. "They belong to me." "Actually they belong to the farm," said the millipede. "So anyone can take them." "Then I'll challenge you to a game of football. Whoever wins gets to keep the seeds." "You're on," said the millipede. "But I must warn you. Others say I'm a good player." "Good player," scoffed Brewster while eating during his football training. "He's no Messi or Ronaldo. I'll show him who is a good player. I'm smarter than that millipede." Meanwhile, millipede was watching Brewster from a tree with his friend. "What's he doing?" said millipede. "He's just eating," said his friend. "I haven't seen him kick a ball yet." "Roosters don't need to train," shouted Brewster. "I'm already prepared." The match day arrived and Brewster and millipede met on the football pitch. "Have you prepared well enough?" laughed millipede. "I didn't see you practice at all," said Brewster. "Well, someone has a fat belly. I think you'll be too slow for me." "You'll be surprised." The match began and Brewster and the millipede tackled each other and pushed one another around. Brewster scored the first goal! Then millipede equalised with a header. Millipede scored again and then he cheated. "I'm not playing until you apologise," said Brewster. "That was a deliberate handball." "How can you tell the difference between my arms and my legs?" said millipede. "I can't even tell myself. Some of my hands feel like feet." "I'd like to see you use your back legs!" said Brewster. "They are weak!" Millipede apologised, and at half time, the score was 5-1 with millipede winning. "I told you it would be a nasty scoreline," said millipede. "Two of those goals were disallowed because you cheated!" said Brewster. "It's only 3-1." "I see you're still upset over my natural talent," said millipede. "It's an unfair match. You have fifty arms and legs. I have two of each." In the second half, Brewster scored two quick goals after he caught his breath, outsmarting millipede. The score was 3-3. Then suddenly, with only 10 minutes remaining, millipede scored a great goal with his back legs, putting himself in the lead at 4-3. "That was a magical goal," said millipede. "You were just lucky," said Brewster. "I tripped and fell." "The ball crossed the line!" said Brewster, claiming a goal. "No, it didn't," said millipede. "Yes, it did!" "No, it didn't." "I've had enough of your cheating," said Brewster. With only two minutes of play left, Brewster ate the ball in protest. "Wow, that was really silly," said millipede. "Now not only will you lose, but you'll bounce away." Brewster choked and spewed out the ball. It rolled away. The game ended and millipede declared himself the winner at 4-3, despite Brewster protesting. "We're never playing together again," said Brewster. "Good, then I can retire undefeated!" declared millipede. Brewster sulked and returned to the farm. Meanwhile, millipede celebrated. "After match bath! After match bath!" he said, wiggling around in a puddle. "Now I can take all of the seeds and make as much money as I want. Ha ha ha!" But the joke was on millipede. During the family dinner, Brewster heard them talking about the seeds. Any animal caught stealing seeds would be kicked out of the farm. Straight after dinner, Brewster gave all of his seeds to millipede. "How very generous of you," said millipede. "You're welcome," said Brewster. Post-Reading Questions Why did Brewster the rooster challenge the millipede to a football match? Why did Brewster eat the ball in protest? Re-read. Ask: What did Brewster say about the millipede? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the millipede say about his goal? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿How did Brewster get his revenge on the millipede? ﻿Do you think the millipede played fairly? Who was the better player?
author: Hello English

title: The Sink is Leaking!
text: Story Description Two girls discover that their sink is leaking, and they get help from their father and a plumber to fix it. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Spilling sp-ill-ing Water was spilling from the sink and the pipe. Fountain f-ow-n-tin There was so much water it was like a fountain. Plumber plum-ur Their father called for a plumber to fix the sink. Valve v-al-v The plumber replaced a valve and fixed the pipe. Kelsey and her younger sister Radhyana were playing with the sink, seeing if they could fill it to the brim without it spilling. When they turned off the tap, there was a pressure build up in the pipe. The pipe burst, sending water shooting out all over the floor. Water travelled out of the tap into the sink, and it overflowed. Kelsey and Radhyana ran to get help. Their father tried fixing the tap with a hammer, but water kept pouring out. Kelsey stared into the sink, watching water spilling over the edges. "Oh, dear!" she said. "Oh, dear, oh, dear," said Radhyana, watching water springing like a fountain from the burst pipe. "The whole house is going to flood." "No, it isn't," said their father. "I'm calling a plumber." As their father called for a plumber, Kelsey and Radhyana made boats out of coloured paper. "Now we have a lake in the house, we can make boats and watch them sail," said Radhyana. "Look, I painted eyes on my boat," said Kelsey. "Now it looks like I am always watching you!" "It's a sunny day outside," said Radhyana. "Perfect for sailing a boat." "Oh, my goodness," said Kelsey. "Look at all of the water. It's forming a gigantic puddle!" "That's even better! Now we have a big place to test out our boats. We should tell dad to cancel the plumber." Just then, a yellow and black car pulled up outside the house. "I'm the plumber," said the woman. "You have an emergency." "Please don't fix the sink," said Radhyana. "Yeah, we've made boats," said Kelsey. "Goodness me," said the plumber, seeing the horrific state of the street. "There's water everywhere. It must be even worse inside the house. I had better fix this problem at once." "The whole house is a pond," said Radhyana. "Wh...what are you doing?" "I'm turning off the water supply," said the plumber. "That way the water will stop coming out of the tap and the burst pipe. "Don't do that," said Kelsey. "We made boats." "Yes, but you don't want to live in a flooded house, do you?" said the plumber. "What are all these strange devices?" said Kelsey. "This is my toolkit. I carry it everywhere I go. I can fix any problem with my tools." "You can watch me work if you like, now the water has stopped coming out." "Ok," said the girls. They watched the plumber twist the tap in the sink with a spanner. They watched the plumber replace a valve in the pipe and fix on a new section to cover the crack. "There," said the plumber. "All done. Now everything is back to normal again. It's going to take a while to clean up the puddles though!" "Did you hear that?" said Kelsey. "It's going to take a while for the water to disappear." "Then we should make the most of it and have fun," said Radhyana, jumping up and down in the puddles. Post-Reading Questions How did the Kelsey and Radhyana break the sink, causing a spill of water? What did the plumber do to fix the sink? Re-read. Ask: Why did Kelsey and Radhyana make boats? Re-read. Ask: What did the plumber see when she arrived? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why were Kelsey and Radhyana celebrating outside? ﻿What should you do when an emergency happens?
author: Hello English

title: The Spooky Night
text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description Henry and his friends go out one evening to the abandoned park and find a demolished house. They encounter something strange. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Abandoned a-ban-dun-d The children found the abandoned house by the park. Unravel un-rav-ul They unravel led the chain for the swings. Shrieked sh-ree-k-d The children shrieked when they heard a scary sound. Vampire v-am-pie-ur A bunch of vampire bats suddenly flew past. "Henry, where have you taken us?" said Gareth. "I'm sure we're not supposed to be here." "Chill out," said Henry. "Don't be such a baby! It's just the park." "This is the abandoned park, isn't it?" said Mary. "We're not allowed to play here." "It's not abandoned," said Henry. "It's just that nobody comes here anymore. We must be the first people in years to visit." "The people in the town said to never go to the abandoned park," said Gareth. "It's haunted." "It is not haunted," said Henry. "Ghosts are not even real. I know because I've never seen one. Come on, let's have some fun." "Well, it can't be that bad," said Mary. "Perhaps Henry is right. We can play here after all. It's not dangerous." Gareth still wasn't sure, but he followed Henry anyway. The children soon found a slide and swing set. The swing was wrapped around the metal pole, as if it hadn't been used in years. "Come on, I'll race you to the swings," said Henry. "Great idea," said Gareth. "Whoever loses has to unravel the chain." "I'm going to beat both of you to it!" said Mary, spreading her arms and running. "Look at the moon," said Mary. The children gasped. "It isn't usually that big," said Henry. "It must be a super moon," said Gareth. "That is when the moon is at its closest distance to the earth, so it looks bigger in the sky." "I don't remember it being so hazy," said Mary. The children continued to play around the swings and slide, dancing, singing songs and telling stories into the night. It was nearly home time, but Henry convinced the children to stay. Henry looked up at the moon and saw clouds pass over. But the moon did not go behind the clouds. It was in front of the clouds. Henry felt something was wrong. "Ooh, this is the abandoned house," said Henry, taking the children past the park to a new area. "Henry, this is bad," said Gareth. "We are definitely not allowed to be here. It could be dangerous." "Relax," said Henry. "Why be scared of some old ruins?" "If we don't go home now, we'll all be in trouble. And we won't be allowed to play together again." Henry ignored Gareth and started investigating through the ruins. Gareth waited near the house, too scared to go inside. Henry found a hammer and started bashing the ground. "Hey, I've found something," he said, hitting a hard metal object. "I think it's an old fashioned safe. There might be money inside. Gareth, give me some help!" But Gareth did not reply. "Gareth? Where are you?" Suddenly, a white sheet with holes appeared. "Oooooh!" it said. "Go away! Go away!" "Ghost!" Henry shrieked. He dropped the hammer and covered his eyes with the fright. Suddenly a cluster of vampire bats flew past, making a huge shadow creep across the ruins. "No!" cried Henry, thinking the bats were going to attack him. "Gareth, get me out of here!" Gareth came and dragged Henry out by the hand, and everyone went home. The next day, Henry told the story to the rest of his friends. He explained about the safe and then seeing the ghost and the vampire bats. "I thought my life was in danger," said Henry. "I was very brave." "No, you weren't," said Mary. "I saw the fright in your eyes." "What?" "The ghost - it was me wearing a sheet," said Mary. "But what about the moon?" said Henry. Nobody could answer. Post-Reading Questions Whose idea was it to go to the abandoned park? What did the children notice about the moon? Re-read. Ask: What did Gareth advise Henry not to do? Re-read. Ask: What did Henry see at the abandoned house? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Mary confess? ﻿What do you think about the children going to the park?﻿
author: Hello English

title: Homework hero
text: Haven't we all dreamed of having a superhero who does our homework. Long time back there was a scientist who made this dream come true. He invented the HOMEWORK HERO. The scientist did not want children to never do their homework, so he made some rules. The homework hero would only come and save you from your teachers once a month. He wouldn't help lazy and lethargic children who didn't have a genuine reason. One day a boy named Dan didn't do his homework since he was ill and had to go to the doctor. Little Dan didn't know about the homework hero. He was extremely worried but didn't find time to do his homework. The next day he quietly tiptoed into his class and sat in the corner of the room making sure no one could see him and hoping that his teacher would forget about the homework she had assigned but she didn't, in a few minutes she asked everyone to submit their notebooks. Dan now was as scared as a puppy. After a while when the teacher entered in to distribute the books, she was extremely impressed and happy that Dan had done his homework right. she was surprised since Dan never gave all correct answers. Dan too was surprised, he didn't do his homework. Later that day, Dan told his mother what had happened. She didn't look surprised. she gave him a smile and giggled. Dan was confused. She then told him that she and every other mother in the world were the homework heroes who help their children. Dan gave her a huge hug and a broad smile.
author: RIDDHI SHOBHAVAT
illustrator: Delwyn Remedios; Godwin  Chipenya; Ma'ayan Rosenzweig; Rai; Rijuta Ghate; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Suvidha Mistry

title: The face in the mirror
text: Rose, Chris and Elena were huddled under a blanket in Elena's room reading a book titled ' THE BLOODY BOOK OF HORRORS'. when they came across the story of bloody Mary, Elena gasped in fear. "Lets stop reading this appalling book and play some games instead." said Elena in a terrified whisper. " but we've just reached the best part!" insisted Rose. Chris then came up with a devilish idea of summoning BLOODY MARY herself. On hearing this, little Elena let out a squeal of fright and wrapped the blanket tighter around herself. Rose, meanwhile started carrying out the preparations for their little experiment,goaded on enthusiastically by Chris. In a few minutes the lights were turned off, the blinds were drawn and a lit candle was procured from the attic. Rose then had to tow a wary Elena to stand in front of the mirror along with them.﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ When they were all assembled, Chris spoke out in a loud and clear voice."Bloody Mary" he shouted. So did Rose. Shivers were running down Elena's back and the room seemed colder. "we have to say it one more time" said Chris."I wont say it" said Elena. Chris and Rose both were getting jumpy by now. They both said it together and waited with bated breath. Was it a ghastly shape in the mirror? yes! It was the pale face of Bloody Mary herself! The children shouted in fright. ''What is all this noise?'' Came their mother's voice out from the darkness. The children then realized that the reflection they had seen was their mother's. She had just come up to check why the lights in the room were off. The children felt foolish for believing a silly urban legend and sheepishly went to bed.
author: RIDDHI SHOBHAVAT
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Alankrita Amaya; Alina  Aphayvanh; Kalp Sanghvi; Lauren   Nel; Magriet Brink; Matthew Specht; Tapas Guha

title: Hop in the Bag
text: Story Description Harold is a travelling rabbit who gets chased by dogs and lions. He looks for somewhere to stop by before he carries on with his journey. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Galloping ga-lup-ing The lion was galloping after the rabbit. Impatient im-pay-shun-t The rabbit was impatient to move to the next farm. Excited ek-sight-id He felt excited by getting a free ride. Sneaked sn-ee-k-d He sneaked into the bag and the farmer carried him all the way. Harold the rabbit was carefully minding his own business, whistling to himself as he walked by the farm, when a dog suddenly appeared. The dog shocked Harold, who shrieked when it growled at him, licking its jaw. The dog took off and chased Harold around the farm. Harold leapt and jumped as fast as he could, kicking with his back legs as the dog caught up with him. Harold dived under a hedge too small for a dog to fit inside, and the dog waited, growling and trying to burrow his way in. When Harold thought it was safe to come out, he found a field on the far side of the hedge. There were rows of trees and shrubs with tasty leaves. Harold helped himself to the shrub leaves, eating one leaf after another, until he was completely full up. Then Harold felt tired and went to sleep under a tree. Night time came, and Harold was woken up by a growling noise. He thought the dog had returned to eat him. But it was worse. Harold ran away when he saw a lion galloping fast towards him. The lion was much bigger and more ferocious than the dog. Harold hid in a barn. The lion gave up looking for him. In the morning, Harold found many white rabbits waking up around him. The farmer returned from the fields with freshly dug carrots. Harold sat down against a log and ate as many carrots as he could. Shortly after breakfast, the rabbits fell asleep in their huts. But Harold had to move on. He could not stay at the farm. He felt impatient and bored, and he really wanted to find a place where he could stay. Harold had an idea. The farmer had arrived with carrots in a bag. Perhaps he could climb into that same bag and get a free ride elsewhere. Harold felt very excited. When the farmer returned, Harold sneaked past him and into the bag. The rabbits ate more food and the farmer watched them eating. When they were finished, the farmer picked up his bag. Harold kept a close eye on the farmer, to make sure he wasn't seen. The farmer walked and walked to some distant fields on a long path. When he arrived, he set the bag down. "Oh, my goodness!" said the farmer, getting a shock when Harold jumped out of the bag and ran towards the next farm. "You sneaky little rabbit!" he said. Harold was happy because he was allowed to stay at the next farm. Post-Reading Questions After Harold escaped from the dog, what bigger creature chased after him? How did Harold manage to get into the farmer's bag? Re-read. Ask: What food did Harold help himself to at the farm? Re-read. Ask: Why did Harold want to leave the farm? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why was Harold happy after his free journey ﻿in the bag? ﻿Describe Harold's personality.
author: Hello English

title: The Special Message
text: Story Description Rabbit discovers that someone is trying to send the animals a message. He gathers a group of animals together to travel and find the source of the message. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿ ﻿ Barrage ﻿ba-rar-j-e ﻿ ﻿Suddenly a big barrage of arrows landed. C﻿ommunity ﻿com-yune-it-ee ﻿The community was alerted to the attack. Encountered ﻿in-count-er-d ﻿The rabbit encountered another attack of arrows. Forgetting ﻿fur-get-ing ﻿The mayor kept forgetting to attach the message. Rabbit and his friends were wandering through the jungle when suddenly a barrage of arrows fell. "Take cover!" he shouted, and all of the animals hid in the bushes and behind the trees. "There's more," said Rabbit. "Watch out!" Another flurry of arrows fell and hit the trees. Then the arrows stopped coming. "I think someone is trying to send us a message," said Rabbit. "I have to tell the community," said Rabbit. "Someone is trying to send us a message." He hopped on his way through the jungle to find the other animals, holding an arrow for evidence. "Did you hear about the arrows falling?" said Rabbit. "Is someone attacking us?" said Rooster. "I'm not sure, but someone is trying to send us a message. You must come with me." "We have to find Ostrich and tell him about the arrows falling," said Rabbit. "Good idea," said Rooster, as they travelled over the hilly forest. "Ostrich, did you hear about the arrows falling?" said Rabbit. "Yes, is someone attacking us?" said Ostrich. "I don't know, but someone is trying to send us a message." "Let's alert Hippo to the news," said Rabbit. "Then he can come with us to find out what is happening." "Hippo, raise your head!" said Ostrich. "He can't hear you," said Rooster. "Hippo, did you hear about the arrows falling?" said Rabbit. "No, I must have been underwater. Is someone attacking us?" said Hippo. "I don't know, but someone is trying to send us a message. You must come with us." Rabbit, Rooster, Ostrich and Hippo approached the city gates, where the arrows came from. "The arrow shooters must be in there," said Rabbit. "We have to be very careful." "Hello, animals," said the gorilla guard. "How can I help you?" "Someone is firing arrows at us from the city," said Rabbit. "We think someone is trying to send us a message. We're here to find out what is going on." "Ok, go on inside," said the gorilla guard. Rabbit encountered Mayor Bear, head of the city. "Someone fired arrows at us," said Rabbit. "We think someone is trying to send us a message." "Yes, I fired the arrows," said Mayor Bear. "Why?" said Rabbit. "I was trying to send you a message, but I kept forgetting to attach it." Post-Reading Questions What did the rabbit think the attack of arrows was? What did the rabbit decide to do? Re-read pages 10-11. Ask: Why couldn't the hippo hear the animals? Re-read. Ask: What did the rabbit say to the gorilla? Re-read. Ask: ﻿Why wasn't the message understood? ﻿Explain why so many arrows were fired.
author: Hello English

title: Who Are You?
text: Story Description A little domestic cat meets various families of big cats in the wild. He insists that he is a real cat, but they don't believe him. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Mutant m-yew-tun-t The big cats thought the little cat was a mutant. Rewarding re-war-ding It is a very rewarding experience to be a cat. Similarities sim-ih-la-rih-tees The big cats saw similarities between themselves and the little cat. Mannerisms man-ur-is-m-s The little cat shared their movements and body mannerisms. "Who are you?" said the two big leopards on the high branches. The cat looked up in surprise. He had not expected to see any other cats around. "I'm a cat," he said. "So are we. But you look different. Should we eat you?" "I don't think so," said the cat. "I don't taste very nice." "How come we don't see any more of your kind?" said the leopards. "Well, we don't live outside. We live with humans," said the cat. "You live with people? That's disgusting. How can you be around them? They're filthy." "They are kind, caring and loving towards me. But mostly because they feed me every day." "Gah!" said the puma as it stared straight into the eyes of a stranger. "Oh, hello," said the cat. "You must be out hunting at night. Lovely fish." "Who are you? Are you a spy? Are you out to eat me?" "I'm a cat, just like you." "I don't believe you," said the puma. "You're too little." "Oh, wow," said the cat. "A pair of big eared cats. Now that is unusual." "Who are you?" said the first big cat. "What are you?" said the second. "I'm a cat, just like you. See? My ears can stand up too. Ping!" "Are you some kind of mutant?" said the first big cat. "You don't have spots," said the second. "I'm so thirsty," said the cat. "How can you bear this hot weather?" "Who are you? What are you doing in the desert?" said the desert cat. "I was looking for water. Just joking. I am finding out about other cats." "Well, you can't be a cat because you can't survive in the desert." "A pair of cats playing with a ball of string," said the cat. "How amusing." "You wouldn't understand because you are not a cat," said the big cats. "Oh, really? I bet you'll tap it and then jump away because you're frightened." "We're not scared of a little ball of string." The big cats got distracted by a passing mouse and left the ball of string alone. "Believe me, chasing the ball of string is more rewarding," said the cat. "You won't catch that mouse. But I can, because I'm small enough to fit into a hole." "You've been bothering the members of my tribe," said the aggressive tiger. "Actually, they have been bothering themselves," said the cat. "For some reason they are scared of me. I'm not sure why. I am a cat, just like you." "You cannot be a cat," said the tiger. "You are too small and weak to be a true predator." The tiger looked at his reflection in the pond. He saw similarities between himself and the little cat. In fact, the reflection confused and scared him slightly. "Is that really me? Why am I so massive? Why do I feel scared? I'm a big cat! I can't be scared!" The tiger stormed off, feeling embarrassed. As the tiger walked across the fields, he noticed the animals running away and the birds flying away from him. He had a fierce presence. He also felt that he wanted to be close to the animals, like a cat, just lazing and relaxing all day. "I can't deny my cat nature," said the tiger. "Perhaps that little creature was right." "You were right," said the tiger. "You are a cat. We see it in your features. We see it in your movements and mannerisms. And so, we wish to give you official cat status. This means you can be part of our tribe and see us any time." "That would be an honour," said the cat. "And don't forget to bring human foods for us," said the tiger. "We have heard they are tasty." Post-Reading Questions What did the big cats not realise about the little cat? What did the tiger finally understand about the little cat? Re-read. Ask: What does the big cat think the little cat is? Re-read. Ask: How did the cats get distracted from their playing? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What does the tiger give to the little cat? Name another cat behaviour.
author: Hello English

title: Molly's 10th birthday
text: Molly was waiting for had finally arrived, it was her birthday! She was woken up by the loud noise of a party popper and a birthday sung by her parents. She was delighted. Later in the morning she had delicious pancakes for breakfast. She quickly had a bath and got dressed. She wore her new pink dress which was adorned with flowers. She looked like a princess. She then decided to write out invitations for her marvelous birthday party. she sent an invitation to each and everyone from her class. When she went to put all the invitations in the mail, a huge dog tore her dress. "oh no! what am i going to do!", She cried while shooing the dog away. She then decided to wear an old dress from her closet. She shoved her sad feelings away and decided to decorate her house. She blew tons of balloons. While she was hanging the streamers, her little brother, Manny burst all the balloons. She was even more disappointed. She still gathered hope and finished decorating. She then proceeded to the kitchen to prepare a cake for herself. While collecting all ingredients, she realized that she was out of flour! She rushes to the nearest store. When she reaches home, she looks at the mirror and finds out that there were pigeon droppings on her head. Poor Molly she has to have a bath again! She has a quick shower and then goes to the kitchen to start her baking. It was really Molly's unlucky day because when she started she started baking, the flour went all over the kitchen. Molly had lost hope and went to remove the invitations out of the mail but to her surprise, all of them were sent to her friends. Molly, disappointed, went to clean the kitchen. After a few hours, she realized that none of her friends had shown up. She was kind of glad but also curious. Out of curiosity, she walked over to her best friend's house and noticed that the lights were switched off. She had a mere thought that the electricity had gone. She accidentally pressed a button and HA! the lights were on and all of friends and her parents yelled 'SURPRISE!' It was Molly's best birthday ever. ﻿MORAL: NEVER LOSE HOPE HAVE FAITH IN YOURSELF
author: RIDDHI SHOBHAVAT
illustrator: aumika shetty; Karen  Vermeulen; Marleen  Visser; Nicci  Nathanson; Rijuta Ghate; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Soumya Menon; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: Oil Spill!
text: Story Description An emergency radio message causes Fred, the leader of the local fish, to evacuate everyone from the area. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Various v-air-ee-uss There are various life forms living in the sea, including fish, dolphins and sharks. Environmentalist en-v-eye-ru-men-tuh-lih-st The environmentalist is concerned about protecting the sea environment. Spillage sp-ill-idge There was a nasty oil spillage that needed cleaning up. Emergency E-mur-gen-see In an emergency, call 999 and ask for police, fire or ambulance. The sea creatures were a cluster of friends living off the coast. Their home was made of coral, plants and rocks, and it was a wonderful place to live. There were turtles, big fish, little fish, frogs and various other life forms living together. The group leader was called Fred, a big yellow and orange fish. "Listen up everyone," he said to the community. "I heard some news from the shore. They are going to broadcast an important radio message. We have to listen to it. Come with me." Fred turned on the radio and tuned in to the news station. The static disappeared and there came a man's voice. "There has been an oil leak off the south coast," said the radio man. "Boats are advised to leave the area. Due to the amount of oil spilled, sea life could be affected." "Fish and birds could get covered in oil. Environmentalists are already heading to the area to help the wildlife. The oil is expected to spread quickly over several hours." That was the end of the message, and Fred switched off the radio, wondering what to do. "We must move the animals to the shore," said Fred, advising everyone to leave in groups. "Where are we going?" said the flying fish. "Fred says we have to move to the shore for our safety," said the turtle. "We don't want to be covered in oil." Fred moved to the shore with another group. "We can't survive here for long," said Fred. "We will have to return to the water after a while, but for now it is the best place to be." "Why are all the fish washing up on the shore?" said a local man. "Go back!" Fred was confused. The radio message told him to evacuate the area. The man at the shore told them to return to the sea. Fred wondered what to do. "We can't survive at the beach, and we can't survive out at sea," he said. "Where else can we go?" An emergency broadcast came on the radio and everyone listened. "There has been a mistake," said the radio man. "The news concerning the oil spill was wrong. There has been a spillage of olive oil and sunflower oil, not crude oil. No fish will be harmed. The sea is safe. We apologise for the error." "We had better tell Fred," said the group of fish. "He has taken the fish to the shore. Our home is safe to live in. Let's find Fred and get everyone to return." "I don't see any oil yet," said the flying fish. "This water is getting too shallow for us. When the tied goes out, we could get stranded. Let's take a risk and return home, even if the oil is coming." Fred was swimming to the shore, taking many fish with him. When he arrived, the man was no longer there. "The man must have received the news," said Fred. "He is probably planning to take us to a new safe place, before the oil gets here." Just then, Fred heard some fish shouting his name. "A false alarm?" said Fred. "But how? It's oil!" "They just spilled some olive oil and sunflower oil," said the fish. "The radio announcer said so." Fred laughed to himself. "No wonder that man was telling us to get away from the shore. We would have been stranded!" Fred took all of the fish back home. Post-Reading Questions Why did the radio broadcaster apologise? Why did the man tell the fish to swim back towards the sea? Re-read. Ask: What caused the emergency? Re-read. Ask: Why did Fred move the animals towards the shore? Re-read. Ask: What kinds of oil actually spilled into the sea? If you heard the first radio message, what decisions would you have made?
author: Hello English

title: The Good Old Days
text: Story Description A grandmother and a girl's father talk about the good old days of the past, remembering what it was like without technology, and how they thought things were simpler. Then suddenly, a fire breaks out. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Manually ma-new-a-lee ﻿A car with five gears is manually operated. Intuition in-chew-ish-un ﻿ ﻿People use their intuition when making decisions. Oblivious Ob-liv-ee-u-ss ﻿She was not aware at all. She was oblivious. Adorable A-door-ra-bull ﻿ ﻿There was an adorable stray cat playing with some string. "I remember the good old days," said granny. "When things were much easier and simpler. These days things are too complicated." "What do you mean, granny?" said Khush. "Look at cars, for example. Back then we had gearsticks. We had to manually change gear up and down depending on the speed and the slope. Now cars are automatic, and very soon, cars will drive themselves." "Driverless cars," said Khush. "How will that work?" "Cars will have in built navigation and sensors," said her father. "Computers in the car will make human decisions." "But computers are not human," said Khush. "Exactly," said her father. "Computers cannot make snap human decisions like we can, based on emotion, timing and intuition." "I think humans would be safer drivers," said granny. "Even the post has changed," said granny. "The postman comes less often, and often gets lost. They rely on computer maps for going to the right location." "In the old days, the postman would ask neighbours and memorise his route," said granny. "He would use his mind and social skills. We are losing both of these abilities." "We cannot rely on technology too much," said Khush. The postman was lost and did not ask for help. "Wait until you get a car, Khush," said Khush's father. "You don't need to read a map anymore. Just follow the voice that tells you where to go." "You mean my inner sense of direction?" said Khush. "I mean the satellite navigation. I was looking for a village once, and the sat nav thought that a path was a road. I took the path and nearly drove into a river. Then it told me to keep going!" "That's not the only problem," said Khush's father. "Phones are everywhere and everyone is on their phone. They don't pay attention when they cross the road. Sometimes they will walk in front of you and give you a fright. You slam on your brakes and shout, but they are oblivious. They don't even realise what they've done." Suddenly the building's fire alarm sounded and everyone had to be evacuated. Khush felt scared by the loud noise and got a fright when the sprinklers went off, soaking the floors. The postman comforted Khush, seeing that she was upset. "Are we going to be all right?" said Khush. "We'll be fine," said her father.
