"The fire brigade will arrive within five minutes using their map system, finding the fastest possible route. We will descend using the emergency elevator and go outside." "I'd like to be a fireman," said Khush as they made it out of the building. "You'll have to wait until you are older," said granny. "Why?" "It's too dangerous a job for you right now. You're a little girl, and besides, you need to be big and strong like the firemen. The uniform would be too big for you." "I can imagine you would look silly," said her father. The firemen went inside the building, found a terrified cat, and quickly dowsed the flames with water. Very soon the fire was out, just leaving smoke, and nobody was injured. "Thank goodness for technology," said Khush. "Or the firemen would not have arrived so quickly." The firemen brought out the scared cat, and the postman and granny saw it trembling. Khush picked it up and gave it a cuddle. It began purring and being sleepy. "It's adorable!" said Khush. "Can we keep it, dad? I want to play with it every day." "It might belong to someone else, but if it's a stray cat, I don't see why not." Many people outside stopped to take pictures of the fire on their phones, and Khush's father groaned. Post-Reading Questions What do cars have now that they didn't have in the past? What two important skills are being lost today? Re-read. Ask: How did the man nearly cause an accident? Re-read. Ask: Name one positive aspect about technology. Re-read. Ask: ﻿ What did Khush find after the fire was put out? ﻿ What kind of technology do you use? Is it helpful?
author: Hello English

title: Monkey Business
text: Story Description Two rival monkey gangs are always trying to steal from each together, but can they learn to share and get along? Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics meandering mee-and-er-ing There was a great coursing river meandering through the land. succulent ﻿suh-kew-lun-t ﻿ ﻿The juicy fruit tasted ﻿succulent ﻿. obnoxious ﻿ob-nok-shu-ss ﻿The ﻿obnoxious ﻿monkey was rude and annoying. abundant ﻿a-bun-dun-t ﻿ ﻿The forest was ﻿abundant ﻿ ﻿ ﻿with mangoes and bananas everywhere. The grey monkey leader was out scouting for food one day when he came across a new area. There were mango trees, fruits of many kinds, bushes and berries, with a great coursing river meandering through the land. It was the perfect spot for his tribe. The grey monkey leader jumped and grabbed the mangoes, pulling them off the branches. He tasted one and it was ripe and succulent, juicy and delicious. He knew the monkeys could live there with plenty of food for a long time. The rest of the monkeys arrived and began eating the bananas, mangoes and lemons, making bridges with old wood and swimming in the river. They had so much fun in their new home, kept safe and watched over by the grey monkey leader. Little did the monkeys know that another dark monkey tribe lived close by. The dark monkeys spied on the grey monkeys, watching their fun and laughter. "Look at them," said the dark monkey leader. "Loud, obnoxious and uncivilised. That is not how a monkey behaves. We are animals of dignity and pride. We must chase them away at once." When the grey monkeys were drinking by the river, the dark monkeys sprang a surprise attack. They wielded clubs and began whacking the monkeys over the back and pulling their tails. "If you want to behave like beasts, then you deserve to be treated like one!" said the dark monkey leader. The grey monkey leader immediately withdrew his group and retreated from the woods and the river. The grey monkeys had nowhere else to go except the empty plains and the desert. It was much hotter there and more uncomfortable. Barely any humans travelled across the landscape. There were animal bones everywhere. The grey monkey leader left the desert in search of a better land. He climbed rocks to give himself a panoramic view, reaching over a wide area. He saw mountains, shrubs and grassland, and plenty of trees. Could there be fruit available? There was! The grey monkey acquired a huge stack of bananas from a tree. The place was abundant with fruit. It was overflowing with food! So the grey monkey made his way back to his tribe in the desert, to tell them the good news. The monkeys cheered and celebrated when they saw what their leader was hiding. He had travelled a long way just to provide them with food. The monkeys gave up chewing on the animals bones and dead trees for their special treat. The monkeys handed out the bananas equally, to make sure everyone ate some food. They were ripe and delicious. The grey monkey explained where he had taken them from - a far away land rich in fruits and vegetables and nuts. The monkeys agreed that they should go to this new land and live there, because it had plenty of food and a water source that would last a long time. They knew they could not survive in the desert. It was too hot and there was not enough water. At the same time, the dark monkeys got together and protested at their leader. They were very angry. They were running out of food, but their leader wanted them to stay in the woods. There was tension and anger. The leader felt helpless. To their surprise, the grey monkey gang came. The dark monkeys prepared for a fight, and the leader hung from some branches. The grey monkey spoke to their leader. He told them of a new land with food, and offered to share the land with them. There would be no more fighting between their groups. The dark monkeys agreed to share what food they had left. They all enjoyed papaya, mangoes of several varieties, and bananas. They groomed one another and told stories, and realised they had the same goals. With everyone happy, the two tribes joined as one and made their way to the new land together. Post-Reading Questions What did the dark monkey leader think of the grey monkeys? How did peace develop between the two gangs? Re-read. Ask: Why did the grey monkeys move to the desert? Re-read. Ask: Why did the grey monkeys agree to move to the new land? Re-read. Ask: What did both monkey gangs realise about each other? If you could go to any place in the world, where would you go and why?
author: Hello English

title: The jumping monkey
text: The monkey loved to jump from tree to tree. Apple trees were his favourite He also loved mangoes. He kept jumping and eating. He was very happy. Suddenly, a little branch the monkey was sitting on broke. He almost fell into river. His friend pulled him by the leg and saved him in time.
author: Anu Alex
illustrator: Ketan Raut; Ruchi Shah; Salim  Kasamba; Seng Visal; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Youm Kosal

title: What is the Future Like?
text: Story Description Leena lives in the future with her robot Tyke. They go on adventures together, until Leena discovers something amazing about Tyke. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics architect ar-kih-tec-t The chief designer of a building is called an architect. motorised mow-tur-ise-d The wheelchair could move on its own because it was motorised. magnetic ma-g-net-ic The toy sticks to the fridge because it is magnetic. calculation ca-l-cue-lay-shu-n The girl's calculation showed there were only 25 days left until Christmas. In the future, things are very different. There are more machines and robots. There are more ways of getting around. But some things like cardboard boxes are still the same. Leena enjoys smashing into cardboard boxes in her motorised wheelchair. It's a bit like a game of bowling to her. Unfortunately Leena cannot ride her wheelchair on the roads, because the vehicles are super fast and dangerous. Fortunately, she can slide her wheelchair inside another vehicle. The cars don't have wheels. They hover which means they don't touch the ground. The road is magnetic. No vehicles can possibly crash into each other. Travelling by car is very safe. Leena's wheelchair hovers too. She can travel across the sea. She takes stock with her, delivering parcels to far off places. She has a robot assistant too. His name is Tyke. Leena blows bubbles so that Tyke can zap them with electric bolts. Pop, pop, pop! Leena enjoys playing in the park on the hover see-saw. If she needs any help, and just in case she slides off, Tyke is there to push her back on. Leena and her friend play on the see-saw all day. Sometimes they take the see-saw with them somewhere else. Leena's father Dave works from home. In the future, most people work from home, or a remote place such as a cafe, restaurant, a bar or the park. A lot of people even work on the beach! With many offices online, everyone is just a click away. Dave can be contacted at any time. Leena looks at her father's plans for designing new buildings. Dave is an architect. He employs robots to build new structures faster than people can. "I like the design," says Leena. "But there is not much space. We should spread these buildings out." Leena plays with her father's design, and her father lets her because he wants her to learn. Tyke performs all the calculations. Tyke holds a screen for Leena while getting her food from the high shelf. He does everything he can for Leena, and Leena always says thank you. "Thank you for taking the boxes for me," says Leena. "Thank you for storing the boxes for me," says Leena. "Thank you for tidying my room and doing the cooking," says Leena. And Tyke always says, "It's a pleasure to serve you." Tyke never complains and never gets angry. But one day Leena discovers something. She sees that Tyke is not working properly. He keeps pausing. He looks sick or unhappy. Leena cannot tell. "What's wrong?" she says to Tyke, but he doesn't respond. Then, to her surprise, she sees that he is showing her a picture of a boy. The boy is crying. Leena feels upset. "Why are you crying, my dear?" she says. "What is making you feel upset?" "You forgot my birthday," says Tyke. "You did not say happy birthday to me." Leena spends the rest of the day playing games with Tyke, making him feel happier. She sings happy birthday to him, cleans his files, they link arms and swing in a circle until they are both dizzy, and Leena reads stories to Tyke. They are like best friends. "Thank you for making my birthday so special," says Tyke, and he hugs Leena. Leena is so shocked! Her robot is experiencing emotions! Is that even possible? It is as if Tyke has an awareness of who he is. From that day forward, Leena no longer treats Tyke as a robot. She treats him like a human being. Post-Reading Questions What kind of things does Tyke do for Leena? Do you think Tyke has an awareness of his own? Re-read. Ask: Why is travelling by car so safe in the future? Re-read. Ask: Where do people work in the future? Re-read. Ask: Why does Leena decided to treat Tyke like a human? What would you like to see happening in the future?
author: Hello English

title: The Big Funny Pink Hippo
text: Story Description Maureen finds a big pink hippo that makes her laugh. The hippo becomes her friend and starts to do clumsy things. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Telescope te-le-sc-oa-p Danny looked through the telescope and saw the moon. Several se-v-ru-l There were more than a few cats outside. There were several. Disgusting diss-gus-ting Picking your nose is a disgusting habit. Trampoline tr-am-pu-lee-n Let's jump up and down on the trampoline before dinner. One day Maureen was walking through the fields looking for pink objects. She was wearing pink blusher on her cheeks, and she found some pretty pink flowers. "I wonder if I can see any more pink objects," said Maureen, using her mini telescope to look across the fields. "Oh, wow," said Maureen. "What is that? It's pink all right." Maureen cast her telescope across the sea and saw something pink paddling. It had big teeth and nostrils, and a very long snout. It was just waddling very slowly, swimming in circles. "What a strange fish!" said Maureen. But was it a fish? It was a hippo! It greeted Maureen, who thought it was cute. "Don't look behind you," said Maureen, teasing the hippo by tickling it. The big funny pink hippo laughed a goofy laugh, which made Maureen laugh too. Then neither of them could stop laughing. The hippo turned around and tickled Maureen, who squealed and ran away. "Let's play on the see-saw," said Maureen. "I'll get on first, then..." Suddenly the hippo sat down really hard, bouncing Maureen several feet into the air. "It's more like a trampoline now," said the hippo, laughing to itself. "Don't sit down so hard!" said Maureen. Maureen went home to her kitchen, to find something for the hippo to eat. "Now, what do hippos like to eat?" she said. "Tuna fish? Spaghetti? Beans? I wonder what they like." Maureen had to act quietly, otherwise her mother would hear her taking food. Maureen's friend Noreen cooked some food, because Maureen could not decide what to feed the hippo. They had lunch together, and they gave an apple and a milkshake to the hippo. The hippo finished the milkshake and kept slurping through the straw. Then it opened its mouth wide and burped really loud. "Finished!" said the hippo. For dinner, Maureen had eggs and bacon again. This time Maureen gave the hippo an extra banana. The hippo drank the milkshake first, then ate the banana, then asked Maureen to hand over the eggs and bacon. "You're such a greedy hippo," said Maureen. "Feed me more!" said the hippo. Maureen filled her pool so the hippo would feel at home. She checked on the hippo and saw toenails and fingernails in the pool. "That's disgusting," said Maureen. "I can't believe you cut them in the pool!" "It's my home now," said the hippo as some bubbles rose to the surface. "Ugh!" said Maureen. Maureen was too lazy to walk to school. She asked the hippo to carry her. But the hippo opened its mouth wide and swallowed her whole. The hippo walked all the way to the school and then spat Maureen out from its stomach. "Wait until the kids hear I was eaten by a hippo!" she said. The next morning, Maureen woke up to find the hippo was gone. "Where did it go?" she said. "It never gets up this early." The hippo disappearing made sense to Maureen. There had been no burps, snoring or strange windy sounds in the night. It had been unusually quiet. Maureen asked her mother where the hippo had gone. "I saw it walking away over the fields," said Maureen's mother. "I think your friend has gone away." "That can't be true!' said Maureen, feeling sad. Maureen took her telescope and searched the fields for the hippo. She could not find it anywhere. Then suddenly, a voice came from the distance. "Don't look behind you," it said. Post-Reading Questions Why was Maureen upset when the hippo disappeared? Describe the hippo's personality. Re-read. Ask: What happened to Maureen when the hippo sat on the see-saw? Re-read. Ask: Why did Maureen think the hippo was being disgusting? Re-read: Ask: How did Maureen feel when she found the hippo?
author: Hello English

title: The Tower of Cups
text: Story Description Meerah likes to show off to customers in the restaurant. She learns how to create a stable tower of cups. She realises she must practice stacking the cups to make a tower. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Entertainer en-ter-t-ai-ner The clown is a funny entertainer. Demonstrate de-mon-str-ate "Allow me to demonstrate how this machine works!" Patience p-ay-sh-un-ce Waiting for a bus requires patience. Perseverance per-ss-e-v-ear-un-ce The attitude of not giving up is known as perseverance. "Daddy," said Myra. "I'm going to build a real tower of cups, like the entertainers do at the market." "That sounds interesting," said Myra's father. "It's going to take time and practice to build one." "I don't think so, daddy. I think I can already make one." Myra's father ran a family restaurant in the town, and Myra enjoyed talking to the guests, singing, dancing and showing off. Now she could demonstrate her tower of cups. "Don't you just love a busy day, Don?" said Myra's father. Don was the old man with a grey moustache. "Especially on a rainy day," said Don. "It gives me something to do!" "Both of you stop talking and pay attention," said Myra, as she started building a tower of cups. She arranged the cups to form a base, placed another layer of cups on top, and they all fell off into the sink. "Keep practicing and you'll get better," said Don. But Myra struggled. Rohan the waiter kept spilling his dishes all over the floor, trying to balance one plate on top of the other. Myra tried to balance on cup on top of the other, but her stack kept tumbling over. She tried and tried but got frustrated and gave up. She noticed Rohan was struggling. "Focus on one cup at a time," she said to herself. "I wonder if I can build a tall stack of cups that looks like that castle?" said Myra. "It looks beautiful." Myra had an idea. Maybe if she treated the cups delicately, like she was building a house, then she would learn to have patience and balance them properly. This time Myra kept practicing with patience, and she was able to create a second level of cups. She gasped in delight when the cups stayed upright. She felt she had improved. "Now the tricky part," she said. "Another level!" Rohan went past balancing the coffee. The more he worked the more he improved also. Myra wondered if it was possible to stack cups one on top of the other, just as Rohan was doing with the coffee. She managed two cups, then three, and then placed a fourth on top. A fifth would have knocked the stack over. Rohan had learned to balance five plates while carrying them to the tables. He was cooler and more relaxed. "If I can stack the cups like this," said Myra, "then there's no reason why I can't make a tower." Myra sat with some paper cups and painted them to look like a castle. She formed the rooftops with a pot and pieces of coconut. It was beginning to look like the castle by the bay. "One day I'll build a castle just like this," she said. As Myra was practicing, the cups kept falling off. She became angry, wondering why she was failing. Running out of patience, she tried and tried to build three levels, but the cups kept collapsing. Rohan was distracted by Myra and he slipped on the floor. The four coffee cups he was carrying flew out of his hands. "I'm building a tower of cups," said Myra to some customers. "One day I will break the world record. I will make the tallest tower of cups in the world." Myra built the cups to three levels and the customers clapped their hands. Myra had made three levels, and now she worked on making the fourth. Rohan sweated with nerves as he carried two heavy bowls. He could feel them wobbling in his hands. "No...no..." he thought. "Yes...yes..." thought Myra, as she placed the final cup on the top. "Phew!" said Rohan as the bowls stabilised. "I almost dropped them!" "What a relief," said Myra. "The tower of cups is complete. Now I can finally show everyone. Dad and Don were right. It takes time, patience and practice to master something." "Dad," said Myra, taking him out to the porch. "Watch this." Myra built one level of cups, then a second, then a third, and finally a fourth. The cups stayed upright. Myra's father clapped his hands in delight. "Well done!" he said. "You've made the tower!" "And now I'm going to try making the tallest tower of cups in the world!" said Myra. Post-Reading Questions Discuss the difference between a tower and a castle. Think of a word to describe how Myra feels when her cups fall down. Re-read pages 2 and 3. Ask: What skills are required to build a tower of cups? Re-read: Ask: Why did Rohan slip on the floor? Re-read: Ask: Now Myra has finished the tower, what does she want to do?
author: Hello English

title: Ammachi's Incredible Investigation
text: “Oh no, the unniappams have disappeared!” said Ammachi. “Someone must have stolen them!” said Sooraj. “But who?” asked Ammachi. “It could have been Penny,” said Sooraj. “Or maybe it was that civet from the attic.” “Or do you think Appachen took them?” asked Sooraj. “Hmm,” said Ammachi. “Perhaps.” “We must lay three BRILLIANT traps!” “There’s only one way to find out,” said Ammachi. “Oh? How?” “Haha! Yum!” “First we need more unniappams.” “Aren’t they all gone?” asked Sooraj. “No, I hid some in the kitchen,” said Ammachi. “For emergencies!” “Our first trap is for the civet,” said Ammachi. “When he comes through the window, he’ll fall right into this basket. His weight will make the lid fall shut automatically.” “Amazing!” said Sooraj. “This one is for Penny. If she tries to eat the unniappam, she’ll be instantly trapped under this bucket.” “Brilliant!” said Sooraj. “And this hidden camera will catch Appachen red-handed,” said Ammachi. “If he lifts the unniappam off the plate, this string will slip out and trigger the camera’s shutter.” “Genius!” said Sooraj. “And now we wait.” An hour passed. Ammachi was in her rocking chair, reading her favourite science book, when Sooraj came running. “Ammachi, come and look! The traps have been sprung!” “Oh!” said Ammachi. “Let’s see!” “But the unniappams are all gone!” said Ammachi. “Again!” “The basket trap is empty!” “So is the bucket trap! How odd!” “The camera didn’t go off either!” “What a clever thief,” said Ammachi. “Maybe we should lay THREE MORE traps!” “YES!” said Sooraj. “But what will we use as bait?” “Don’t we have three more unniappams left in the oven?” asked Sooraj. “A-HA!” said Ammachi. “Not so clever after all, I see!” “Eh?” said Sooraj. “What?” “How did you know that there were THREE unniappams left, Sooraj?” asked Ammachi. “And HOW did you know they were hidden in the OVEN?” “Ahhh…. I…. Ummm…. Ohhh….” “And I didn’t tell ANYONE ELSE how the traps worked. Only YOU could have sprung them without getting caught!” “Okay. OKAY!” said Sooraj. “FINE! You caught me. I AM the unniappam thief!” “I KNEW IT!” said Ammachi. “Heee. Those unniappams were TOO irresistible, Ammachi!” said Sooraj. “You’re such a good cook!” “Hahaha! You little flatterer!” said Ammachi. “Who gets to eat the remaining unniappams, Ammachi?” “Hahaha! Come, we’ll share them!” “Oh no!” said Ammachi. “The unniappams are GONE! AGAINNNN!” "Hehehe!" *NYUM-NYUM* *SCRUNCH* *MUNCH-MUNCH* ﻿ ﻿*CHOMP-CHOMP* *TAKA-TAKA-TAKA* How to catch a thief: 1. Look for clues! 2. Make a list of suspects! 3. Lay traps! 4. Ask clever questions! 5. Write down everything you’ve discovered! 6. Go and catch your prime suspect! 7. Caught the wrong suspect? Oh no! 8. Repeat steps 1 to 7!
author: Vinayak Varma

title: That's Not A Bird!
text: Story Description Haroon enjoys growing flowers in his garden, but one day a strange scent comes that damages his flowers. A cluster of birds fly over his garden, but on closer inspection, Haroon sees they are not real birds. Haroon goes to Mr. Nasir to investigate what is happening. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Putrid p-yew-trid The nasty, putrid smell stayed for a long time. Artificial ar-tih-fi-sh-ul The banana was not real. It was artificial. Inspection in-spec-shu-n The boy thought he had seen a dog. On closer inspection, it turned out to be a cat. Redesign ree-dih-zi-n The car was not built properly. It needed to be redesign ed. Haroon had a large garden outside of his house. The garden was surrounded by tall mountains, meadows and fruit plantations. Haroon's garden was his dream, and he was passionate about tending to it every day. He planted seeds and dug the soil to plant new flowers so they would grow firm and strong. Suddenly, one day, a strange, putrid smell hovered over the area. It lingered and did not go away. "What is that horrible smell?" said Haroon, trying to trace where it was coming from. Haroon followed the scent, and he found that it, as well as some music, was coming from Mr. Nasir's direction. Mr. Nasir lived in the town past the hills. "The birds seem to be following it too," said Haroon. But on closer inspection, the birds did not look real. "What on earth is going on?" said Haroon, as a swarm of fake birds and insects flew around him. They took off and got higher, then disappeared back towards the town. When Haroon got back to his garden, he noticed that some of the flowers had died due to the bad smell. Haroon didn't understand what was happening. "How is this possible?" he said, sad that his plants were suffering. Haroon went to Mr. Nasir's house and asked him about the artificial birds and insects. "They are remote controlled," said Mr. Nasir. "Like drones. They can swoop and sway, roll and dive. I designed them and many people are buying them around the town. The nasty smell is a byproduct of their fuel. Think of it as exhaust fumes." Mr. Nasir apologised for the fumes killing Haroon's flowers. The weather got hotter, and to both cool down his flowers and get rid of the bad smell, Haroon installed fans around the garden, to provide his plants with fresh, cooler air. "That should keep them alive," said Haroon. "I hope I don't see any more of those annoying toys flying over my garden." But then, the birds and insects returned, as did the bad smell. Haroon went to the park and saw many people playing with the toys. There were too many of them in the sky. The situation was becoming dangerous. Suddenly, the birds and insects crashed into one another, and the people turned violent and aggressive. They threw down their remote controls in anger, and started beating one another, blaming each other for the crashes. "But Mr. Nasir said they were programmed to avoid one another," someone said. Haroon was seething with anger at Mr. Nasir's actions. "You just made quick money but didn't program your toys properly," said Haroon. "They're colliding all over the place." "What? I designed them not to!" said Mr. Nasir. "And they're killing my flowers. You need to get rid of those toys and don't fly them around my garden ever again. Do you understand?" "I'm so sorry," said Mr. Nasir. "I'll give everyone a refund!" Mr. Nasir visited Haroon and gave him some new plants and trees to look after, as a way of saying sorry. Very soon, Haroon's garden was colourful and filled. The two men embraced and Haroon apologised for his anger, as did Mr. Nasir for making lousy toys. The two men became good friends, and Mr. Nasir promised that none of his toy birds or insects would fly near the garden. And Mr. Nasir redesigned the toys, finding a way to get rid of the nasty smell. Post-Reading Questions Describe how Mr. Nasir upset Haroon. Find a word that describes Haroon's attitude towards gardening. Re-read. Ask: What is the nasty smell associated with the birds? Re-read. Ask: How did Haroon protect his plants and keep them cool? Re-read. Ask: How did Mr. Nasir apologise to Haroon?
author: Hello English

title: A DRAGON CALLED WHATEVER
text: The ceramic animals watched Lidwin carefully through their glazed eyes as she kneaded a lump of clay. Then, as her nimble fingers began to shape the clay deftly, a small grey ceramic cat mewed, and nudged a yellow cat standing beside him on a wooden shelf. “What do you think she is going to make with that lump of clay?” the grey cat whispered curiously. As the pink cat craned his neck to get a better look, a large grey and white ceramic cat with a pink nose spoke up. “She’s making another big cat, just like me! There’s no doubt about it! I am the cutest creature here. I am always admired and appreciated by all those who come into Lidwin’s studio. Look! She has already fashioned a big belly, and a small curved tail for the new cat.” The grey and white cat purred proudly in satisfaction. A little brown and white dog yapped crossly. “You silly cat! I’m tired of you - always boasting about yourself. Look carefully at the new animal’s legs and feet. Do they look as if they belong to a cat?” As the grey and white ceramic cat looked again at the figure that Lidwin had shaped from a lump of clay, he blinked uncertainly, and fell silent. “He’s quite right,” another brown ceramic dog agreed with a bark. “The new animal doesn’t have paws! Its unlike any animal here.” “Why don’t we wait till it gets a head?” a pink owl suggested sensibly. “Then we’ll know for sure what kind of creature it is. But it's not an owl, of that I’m certain. It doesn't have feathers or wings.” “It’s not a rooster either,” crowed a green and white spotted rooster, vigorously shaking the red comb on top of his head. “Does the new animal have a small, curly tail?” asked one of a family of shiny, pink ceramic pigs politely. “If it does, then it’s a pig. We will welcome another pig into our family with cheerful oinks!" “No! The new animal has a thick, stout tail. It seems to be quite different from all our tails,” the pink owl remarked slowly. “Let’s wait patiently and see what kind of head Lidwin makes for him.” The little ceramic animals stood quietly on their shelf and watched anxiously as Lidwin punched and moulded a large ball of clay, and made a head for her newest creation. And when she was finally satisfied with the head that she had crafted, Lidwin sat back and smiled at her creation. “Good grief! What kind of animal has she made? Whatever it is, it’s not a cat,” squeaked the grey and white ceramic cat shrilly, as he stared at the new animal. "It's certainly not a pig either," squealed one of the pink ceramic pigs. "Doesn't look like a rooster either," said a green spotted rooster. “Look at the size of its head!” murmured a white sheep,twitching his drooping ears and rolling his round eyes in fright at his companions. “Whatever this animal is, it’s definitely not a sheep! And don’t those teeth look just fearsome?” “They really do,” agreed a pair of goats. “This is a scary-looking animal, whatever it is, even though it does not have horns on its head, or a beard on its chin like we do!” “Have none of you noticed the sharp spikes that the whatever has running down its back and tail?” the leader of a herd of ceramic cows mooed agitatedly. “I’m going to keep my herd away from him, that’s for sure!” “Well, I am going to make sure everyone in my herd is friends with this Whatever animal,” said a grey ceramic elephant firmly, raising his trunk, and waving it respectfully in the direction of the new animal. “He is much bigger than we are, and Lidwin seems to like him.” “Let’s wait till Lidwin finishes making the new Whatever,” said a large, colorful rooster who was sitting on a shelf with his wife, Mrs. Hen. “Hey, look! She’s got her paintbrush out. She’s getting ready to paint the Whatever.” “Lidwin is painting the Whatever yellow,” quacked a duckling loudly in excitement. " It's just as I thought..." “It’s going to be yellow like me! I knew it! Lidwin is making another duck!” “You silly duckling,” hooted Mrs. Owl who was sitting beside Mr. Owl and their colourful baby owl. “Part of me is as yellow as you are, are but I’m not a duck, and neither is the Whatever. Look at those teeth, and the spikes on its back! I don’t know any duck that has those!” “I think that the Whatever has a very interesting appearance,” said Mrs. Poulet the hen with a big smile. “I have teeth too, but you must agree - they add immensely to my charm.” Mrs. Poulet’s husband, a large red rooster crowed in agreement. “I’ve been watching silently, but listening carefully as you all argued about the Whatever,” said a bright yellow cat with eyes as large as saucers. “But now that Lidwin has started painting the Whatever yellow, it’s crystal clear to me – the Whatever is a cat like me with large eyes…” “Shush, you silly cat,” said one of a family of three owls. “Our eyes are as big as yours are, and are as big as the Whatever’s eyes too, but we are not so silly as to immediately jump to the conclusion that the Whatever is an owl! Look at those spots on its body. Owls don’t have those." Another of the three owls spoke up. “Lidwin has opened the door of the kiln! I think that the Whatever is going to be put into it. Let’s wait and see what it looks like after the first round of firing of several hours is over.” When Lidwin opened the door of the kiln twenty- four hours later, three roosters that had been carefully keeping their eyes on it, swayed and gasped. “Oh gosh,” one of them said, “I think the Whatever looks quite scary. Look at those teeth and claws! I really can’t understand why Lidwin is smiling so happily at it. And do you hear what she’s saying? She’s saying that she’s delighted that the first dragon she has ever made has come out so well.” “The Whatever has to be popped into the hot kiln again to make his surface smooth and shiny,” the yellow cat murmured. “We will know more about him after that’s over.” In a few days, the dragon’s final glaze firing was over, and he emerged from the kiln. He had orange spots on his smooth, shiny body and chest, and the spikes running down his back were purple. He had an enormous mouth and sharp teeth. The dragon blinked his large blue eyes, and looked around curiously. “He’s not going to be here for long,” a member of the owl family remarked. “ Lidwin said that someone has already bought him, and so he’s going to be delivered to his new owner tomorrow.” When the dragon Whatever heard these words, he suddenly let out a roar. “I want to live here forever,” said Whatever, looking around worriedly. I like being here, especially since I am the only dragon in this studio. I am not going to agree to be delivered to someone else!" "You have no choice in the matter," said the brown ceramic dog, letting out a sharp bark. "All you can do is hope that you get a good home where you will be well looked after, and where your owners will not let you fall down." “What happens if I fall down?” the dragon Whatever asked, in a voice that quavered. A rooster replied brutally. "If a ceramic animal falls down, it breaks into pieces, and perishes." “Going away to a new home sounds just terrible. I just want to stay here,” Whatever said with a gulp. Then he started sobbing, loudly and noisily. "He’s a baby dragon – that’s why he is blubbering,” Mrs. Owl remarked. Then suddenly, Mrs. Owl had a brainwave. “What are you crying for, Whatever? You are a dragon, and you must surely know that dragons can fly! You can fly back to us whenever you want to.” Whatever stopped crying.. But then, his orange dragon face crumpled again. “How can I fly? I don’t have any wings,” he exclaimed. He started howling again. Mr. Owl glared at Mrs. Owl crossly. "Look what you've done!" he said. But Mrs. Owl, a quick witted bird, told Whatever that his wings would sprout as he grew, and he could then fly back to Lidwin's studio. “Will I really sprout wings?” asked Whatever seriously. “Of course,” replied Mrs. Owl. The other ceramic animals agreed. This assurance seemed to calm the little dragon down, and he was quiet the next day when he was packed in bubble paper, and taken out of Lidwin’s studio. When he reached his new home, Whatever the dragon was placed on a table beside a tall wooden angel. The angel ignored the little dragon. “I’m Whatever the dragon,” said Whatever proudly. “ I’m not staying here long. As soon as I grow, and my wings sprout, I'll fly back to Lidwin’s studio.” Then Whatever asked the angel “Do you know any magic spells that will help my wings sprout quickly?" The angel smiled."I've been here so long that I have quite forgotten all the magic I once knew...." "Please think hard, and try to remember,"Whatever implored the angel. Whatever looked so woeful that the angel felt sorry for him, and she nodded. “Alright,” she said. “I’ll try to think hard and remember my old magic spells. But I must warn you, it’s going to take a long time – you must be patient.” Whatever smiled. “I will be patient and will wait as long as you wish. I’m in no hurry, because dragons, like angels, live forever….” All the animals that appear in this story are handmade ceramic originals
author: Santhini  Govindan

title: Unathi and the Dirty, Smelly Beast
text: Something is following Unathi. It is dirty. It is smelly. It is a beast! Unathi is good at running. The beast is good at chasing. Unathi is better at jumping. The beast is better at splashing. Unathi is best at climbing. The beast is best at digging. Unathi and the beast both love singing! It’s time for Unathi to go home. The dirty, smelly beast wants to go home too! “No dirty, smelly beasts in the house!” says mama. Unathi and the beast are good at sneaking. Unathi is good at dressing up. The beast is not. Unathi and the beast can hide in the bubbles. The beast is not dirty. The beast is not smelly. The beast is clean and lovely.
author: Jon Keevy

title: The Missing Toy Cars
text: Story Description Four siblings - Stacy, Dean, Magda and Eddie - enjoy playing with their toy cars. One day granny's dog Ronnie steals the cars and hides them in the garden tree, and Magda goes to retrieve them. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Retrieve ree-tr-eve ﻿ ﻿The owner threw a stick and the dog retrieve d it. ﻿Rivalry ﻿r-eye-val-ree ﻿There was rivalry between the two competitors. Forbidden ﻿for-bid-un ﻿It was more than not allowed for me to climb the tree. It was forbidden. Relieved re-lee-v-d ﻿ ﻿I was relieved to see my granddaughter safe and unharmed. There was a cottage close to a farm, and at this cottage lived a family of six, with four children. The children were Stacy, Dean, Magda and Eddie. They had a passion for playing outdoors over the large open land surrounding their home. They also loved playing indoors with their toy cars. Inside the house, the four siblings built a race track. They would push the cars along the track and fight each other out of the way to win! Stacy's favourite model was a green car shaped like a vintage American family car from the 1970s. Eddie's favourite vehicle was a blue truck without the container on the back. Eddie enjoyed the truck because he thought it looked strange not carrying a heavy load, and he wondered if one day he could sit on the back of a real empty truck, getting taken along a busy highway and feeling the fresh air. The siblings made the cars and trucks motorised so they could be operated by remote control. This stopped them from fighting each other along the track. Yet cheating still happened because there was an intense rivalry between the two brothers Dean and Eddie, and the two sisters Stacy and Magda. They would try to knock each other's vehicle off the track. Sometimes the dog became excited and ruined the race by trying to eat the cars. Stacy loved her green car, Dean enjoyed the red bus, Magda treasured the three-wheeled tuk-tuk, and Eddie was obsessed with the blue truck. One day, grandma's dog Ronnie ran away with the cars. It was Stacy who realised they were missing. She saw Ronnie climb the tree, and soon afterwards, two of the cars dropped out of the branches. The red bus and the yellow tuk-tuk were still missing. Magda volunteered to find out where Ronnie put the cars. "You silly dog!" she called down from the tree. "These are our favourite toys and you've ruined our game. If only you could speak, then you could tell me where you hid them." Ronnie sniffed around the tree for hidden bones. Their parents saw Ronnie climb the tree and they went looking for the cars. The children were too afraid to tell mum and dad that Magda was in the tree, as they would all get in trouble. Tree climbing was forbidden, so they kept quiet. The cows meanwhile took a great interest in what was happening. "I've found the cars!" Magda called out, knocking the red bus and the yellow tuk-tuk out of the branches. But Magda could not get out of the tree. She was too scared to climb down. Ronnie barked at her, sensing her anxiety. "Ronnie, go and get mum and dad!" she said. "Hurry! I don't want to fall! Please, go!" Mum and dad came to the rescue, grabbing Magda by the feet and pulling her out, catching her below. Magda explained why she had climbed the tree, and she got into trouble. The three other siblings shared the blame, but at least they had their toys back. "Just don't let the dogs near the toys when you're playing," said Mum. Stacy, Dean and Eddie all laughed at Magda for getting stuck. At least granny was relieved to see her. "I hear Ronnie got you in trouble," said granny. Post-Reading Questions Why did the children make their toy cars motorised? Find two words to describe Magda 's actions in the story. Re-read. Ask: Why was Eddie so fascinated by the blue truck? Re-read. Ask: Who stole the toy cars and hid them in the tree? Re-read. Ask: For what reasons do you think Magda got in trouble? If you were Magda, would actions would you have taken?
author: Hello English

title: Life's Lighter Moments
text: Once there lived a happy family, they had two children. One was a girl called Mavis in the age of 10,the other was a boy called Danim in the age of 8. Mavis is a very intelligent, kind and beautiful girl she loves to play chess with her brother because she always wins against him. while Danim is a very naughty boy how really hated to play chess with his sister and also hated school. Every saturday Danim and Mavis got 10 kr each as pocket money. Mavis put her money into her piggy bank storing it but Danim use to spend it the very second he got his money. One day as usual Mavis and Danim got there pocket money, Mavis told Danim to store his money too but he refused and said “I will buy a big bar of tasty chocolate!”.On Danim's way to the chocolate shop his money fell out of his hands and rolled into an extremely narrow hole on the road. He put his hand into the hole in hopes of finding his money but he could not find any of his money. Worse than that was his hand got stuck inside the hole! There was lot of traffic because it was the rush hour, and Danim was very scared that a car might come and crash him. Then a lot of people huddled around Danim to see what has happened. Some of the people were stout, some were fat and some were extremely thin. As Danim's hand was stuck, a sharp pain hit his arm with a clear shot. At that moment a kind-hearted lady entered the crowd. She was very kind and loved to help other people. Then after a little while knowing what she was doing she walked to the front and kneeled beside Danim, the lady said “ I will help you”, Danim said “thank you”. Then she said to the crowd to call the firetruck so a stout woman who had a phone called the fire truck. The lady rubbed butter and soap to Danim’s hand while they were waiting. They tried and tried but it didn’t work then after half an hour, two firefighters showed up. They used a special kind of grease to get Danim’s hand out of the hole. Danim felt relief about his arm and he was not sad about the chocolate and why should he be? Because the lady who helped him was the owner of the chocolate shop and gave him two big boxes of tasty chocolate. He liked this experience more than any other experience. He went home very happily and told the whole story to his family. Mavis said “now will you store your money?” and this time Danim said “I will Mavis”. And then they lived happily again.
author: Adriana Baldibia-Bejar

title: Maddy Moona's Menagerie!
text: My name is Maddy Moona, And today I’m turning five. Dad promised I could choose a pet, A real one! Something live! We’ll travel across the whole wide world, Searching Mali through Tibet, Until we find the perfect one... Oh, I know just what I’ll get! I’m going to get an elephant. I’ll ride on it to school. My brother Billy can walk behind he’ll think I’m awfully cool. But... what if Ellie caught a cold? I guess she’d sneeze.... A LOT! There is no tissue big enough to wipe up all that snot. I’ll keep him in the bathtub and brush his pearly whites, But... what if flossing all those teeth takes me all day and night? I want a Nile crocodile sent to me by the pharaohs. I’ll call him Tut and feed him soup, fish fingers, and baby marrows. Perhaps a pair of porcupines, for games of robbers and cops. Their prickly quills will be handy for holding up sweetie shops. I can munch away on candy bars while my gang sharpen their spines. But... what if my sharp-shooting pals put me in the firing line? Maybe I need a stealthier plan. Let’s clear out the store with funk! There isn’t a smellier critter on earth That’s what I want - a skunk! But.... what if I can’t go into the shop after Skunky has let off his stink? Sweets are no good for my teeth anyway. A rotten idea! I need to rethink! A rhino! The horns, the big stomping feet, the armour on both of its flanks! Billy would never chase me again. It would be my own personal tank. But... what if Billy raises his temper and Rhino goes on the rampage? Crash bang boom! The teacups! The plates! Now I’m grounded ‘til I’m gran’s age. I need a beast to tame my brother. With teeth, sharp claws and a roar. A LION! I could feed it Billy biltong... Yes! A lion would settle the score. But... a lion has a huge appetite. Skinny Billy won’t satisfy. And once Brutus has a taste for us Moonas, he’ll see me as Maddy stir-fry. Dad thinks I should choose a cuddlier pet. My parents are so hard to please. They want me to have a pet I can hug. A python? A python has squeeze. But... if Snakey develops too much of a crush, he’ll suffocate me with affection. To be honest, I just can’t marry a snake! And reptiles can’t handle rejection. No, reptiles aren’t the way to go. I definitely need something taller. A giraffe would be awesome. I’ll slide down her neck, and think up a long name to call her. But... something more than eight foot tall is no good. Our house has a rather low ceiling. I’d spend hours massaging cricks out her neck. My fingers would lose all their feeling. None of these are the perfect pet! Oh what, oh what will I get? Those animals just don’t work. None are my perfect partner in crime. I want something with fur, a pet who will follow. Oh, wait! I know - a canine! My Bandit is the biggest bark on the block! He’s the fastest pup in the west! Nothing can stop us. Not Billy nor bedtime. I love my Bandit. He’s my best!
author: Rachel Zadok

title: Palesa Can Walk!
text: Palesa can’t sleep. It’s her birthday tomorrow. She’s one year old! All her friends will bring her lots of presents. Seth will bring a... What will Seth bring? A rattle! And Sandile? A drum! But what about Aunty Mamsie? Oh, she’ll bring a cake, balloons, a trumpet, a talking doll, a computer, and... and... and... LOOK! Palesa’s fast asleep... TRII-IING-TRII-IING! “Happy birthday!” comes from the door. “Come in! Come in!” Mommy shouts. On her stool, Palesa’s eyes grow bigger and bigger. Over there, against the wall, the pile of toys grows and grows and grows. “Mine!” Palesa screams. “Mine!” she waves her angry arms. But everybody’s busy playing. “MINE!” And, with one big heave, pushes herself up. She goes and gathers the toys. Everybody stops. Then they all clap their hands. “Hurray! Palesa can walk!” Look! Now everyone is happy. Palesa is happy to play with her friends.
author: Sindiwe Magona

title: Searching for the Spirit of Spring
text: The Winter cold had passed. Spring was coming to Nkanyezi’s village. Soon the villagers would gather to celebrate the new season. Nkanyezi looked forward to the Spring festival more than any other day in the year. One warm morning, Nkanyezi overheard two village elders talking about the festival. “The people of Ndlovu have lost their spirit of celebration,” one sighed. “How can we have a Spring festival in a village that has forgotten how to celebrate?” asked another. Nkanyezi was worried. “How will the sun shine again unless we sing to wake it from its winter slumber?” she asked herself. Nkanyezi thought for a long time. “I must find what we have lost,” she decided. “I must go in search of things that will bring back the spirit of celebration to my village.” The elders gave Nkanyezi their blessing for the journey. They gave her a bag to carry the things she would find. Nkanyezi was afraid, but she believed she would succeed. Nkanyezi walked all day. She hiked up a hill, and down into a valley. She sailed across the great river, and climbed between sharp rocks. She marched across the plains until she reached the shadow of the red mountains. As night was closing in, Nkanyezi arrived at a village of patterns and colours as she had never seen before. She told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people. The mother of this tribe gave Nkanyezi a gift. She told the girl, “With love we give to you this paint to restore colour to a village that has gone dull.” Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the paint in her bag. Early the next morning she went on her way again, excited with this gift of colour. Nkanyezi walked all day, through a vast forest of giant trees. As the sky became too dark for her to see, she heard the sound of beating drums. She hurried towards the drumming, feeling the spirit of dance coming to her tired feet Nkanyezi found herself in the village of the Bhubezi. People were sitting around a fire, drumming and singing. She had never before heard such wonderful music. She told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people. The Bhubezi invited her to rest and stay the night. In the morning the chief called on Nkanyezi. “My child,” he said, “here is a special drum. It plays a new song every time you beat it.” Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the drum in her bag. She went on her way again, delighted with this gift of music and dance. On the third day of her journey, as she passed a field of fat cows, her nose started to tingle. An aroma tickled her taste buds and her mouth started to water. She followed the scent, and arrived in a village to find people standing over steaming pots of stew. This tribe was famous for its feasts and Nkanyezi had never before tasted such flavours. After she had eaten her fill, she told the village elders about her journey to bring back the spirit of celebration to her people. The next day, the council of cooks gave her a secret spice blend. “Our daughter,” they said, “with these spices, happy tummies are guaranteed! We give you the gift of good food.” Nkanyezi thanked the elders and put the spices in her bag. She knew she had everything she needed.With new energy she started the long journey back to the village of Ndlovu. When she arrived home the villagers gathered around her to hear of her adventures. She told them the tales of what she had seen, heard, and eaten. Then she opened her bag to share the gifts given. The people rejoiced to receive these treasures. Through the generosity of others and the courage of Nkanyezi, the villagers again found the colour, song and dance in their lives. And so the spirit of celebration was restored to the village of Ndlovu.
author: Mosa Mahlaba

title: Where's My Tail?
text: Story Description A spotted pig called Piggy goes out to find his lost tail, but he travels far from home and gets lost. Piggy's day turns into an adventure to find his tail and find his way back home. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Temporary ﻿tem-puh-rare-ee ﻿Piggy put on a tree stump for a tail as a temporary replacement. Summit ﻿suh-mm-it Piggy walked all the way to the highest point of the hill - the summit. ﻿ Original ﻿o-ridge-in-al ﻿This other tail is nothing like the original. Traced ﻿tr-ey-ss-d ﻿I traced my steps to find my way back home. Piggy got up one morning in his forest home. He looked in the mirror and realised something horrible. "What happened to my tail?" he said. "Where is it?" Piggy looked around his home but he couldn't find his tail anywhere. "I don't believe it," he said. "I swear I had it last night before I went to bed. Oh, well. I had better go around and look for it." "Yesterday I went walking up this hill," said Piggy. "Perhaps I dropped it on the way up, or on the way back down. Either way, I'm going to check. It must be here." Piggy walked up the hill but he couldn't find his tail. "I have an idea," he said. "Maybe I dropped it here at the top, and a bird took it away into the mountains to use for a nest." Piggy felt sleepy after his walk, and took a nap close to a balloon seller. Someone placed a balloon on him so that when he woke up, he would have a gift. But the wind gathered speed, and when Piggy woke up, he was in the sky with a pink balloon wrapped around his middle. A bird popped the balloon and Piggy landed in the snowy mountains. "I'm so far away from home now," he said. "I won't get back today! I had better find my tail instead. It has to be here somewhere." He found a tree stump and used it as a temporary tail. Piggy climbed even more until it was freezing cold. He reached the mountain top but he could not see his tail. He found a sock at the summit and used it as a tail. "Oh, that's nice and warm," said Piggy. "You're a long way from home," said the yak. "I'm looking for my tail," said Piggy. "Your tail is missing? That's a sad end," the yak joked. "Well, have you seen..." Suddenly, Piggy slipped. A gust of wind blew Piggy over the edge of the mountain. He floated down on to much lower ground. On the way, he tried on some tails he'd collected throughout his journey. "Not bad," he said. "Not bad. Ah, but they're nothing like the original!" Piggy walked until he arrived at a desert. "I'm completely lost now," he said. "Now I can't find my tail and I can't get home. This is a disaster!" He crawled along the sand until he reached a cactus. "Must drink water," he said. Luckily, a camel found Piggy and gave him some fresh water. "I have more stored in my stomach if you want it," said the camel. "Don't make me feel sick," said Piggy. "I really need to find my tail. Sometime yesterday I lost it." "Well, it's not here in the desert. You need to head back to the forest, my friend. Sit here in the shade and rest first." After Piggy left the desert, he found a steep slope with woodland. Along the way, Piggy slipped in the wet grass and tumbled down like a sledge. He rolled all the way off a high cliff. Piggy landed in the sea. He felt he was getting much closer to home. He swam with a cluster of jellyfish as he found his way to the beach. From there he found his way home to the forest. Suddenly Piggy encountered a grey fluffy monkey hanging off a branch. "Don't suppose you've seen my tail, have you?" said Piggy. "It's on your bottom!" laughed the monkey. "There's not mush-room for another one!" Piggy was not amused. "Where could it be?" "It's always in the last place you look," said the monkey with a laugh. Piggy traced his steps back home and, lo and behold, he found his tail where it had been all along. "I remember now!" he said. "I took it off before I went to bed last night!" Post-Reading Questions How did Piggy end up high on the mountain? What three things did Piggy use as a replacement tail? Re-read. Ask: What did Piggy do as he fell down the mountain? Re-read. Ask: What did the camel offer to Piggy? Re-read. Ask: What did the monkey say about finding Piggy's tail? Have you ever lost something important and found it later?
author: Hello English

title: stories for us
text: once there was a village in which I and my friend Ram used to live. my father was a priest and his father was a sweeper. one day our parents got to know about our friendship my parents scolded me very harshly and ordered me to end my friendship with Ram. but after 5 years of friendship, it was really hard for me to say to him that our friendship is no more without any reason. then the next day my father went to the village temple and I asked my mother that why Papa did this to me, then my mother replied that Ram is not of our cast then suddenly my father enters. I tried very hard that cast just a second name of a human it doesn't have any connections with the person's nature. I told my father how many times Ram helped me in difficult situations when every one of my cast refused to help me. After a revolting discussion of approximately 2 hours, my parents agreed on our friendship. That day I learned the value of true friendship.
author: Krishna sharma
illustrator: Anonymous; Michael  Sagikwa; Therson  Boadu; Ujwala Waghmare

title: Venkatesh's festival
text: Wanna know why I used this image on the front cover, ok ill tell you I am a resident of a small village called Venkatesh. this is the time of our biggest and holy festival. this festival is celebrated for more than 200 years and I hope it will be continued. in this festival my mother cooks deliciously tasty sweets which are my favorite part of this festival. oh!...., I didn't tell you my name, is Samantha but my family and friends call me as Sama. This festival is celebrated for 5 days in the month of August. in this fest every one decorates their houses, puts lights, distributes chocolates and gifts to the young ones and the most interesting part of this festival is it's fair. there are enormous kinds of food stools, clothes, gaming centers, and hammocks, swings, and seesaws. Today, it is the fifth day of the festival. in the evening the priest of our village will do a maha-pooja and then well all go for the visarjan. and now my friends' ram and Laxmi are playing with me as our parents are busy in the preparations. its the time of visarjan, I will really miss this festival until it comes again the next year. my friend Laxmi started crying, do you know the reason for her crying, she wanted to go along with the murti! what kind of funny it is, isn't it? okay, friends, we meet the next year until then be happy, be safe. goodbye.!
author: Krishna sharma
illustrator: Aphisith Souphavongtay; Godwin  Chipenya; Priya Kuriyan

title: Sona Decides to Save the Rainbow
text: Little Sona Loves Rainbow! Rainbow gives her happiness. She loves Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo and Purple colors of the rainbow She wonders "What are these colors about"? From where they come from? They look so beautiful! What she does not like is eating fruits & vegetables. Her mother tells Sona that the fruits and vegetables are good for her health. But Sona was not interested in them at all. One day her mother hugged her and asked, "Sona, Do you know how the rainbow got all the colors? " "No mother. Do you know? Please tell me", Sona asked Her mother stared telling her, "Once upon a time there was no rainbow" Sona was surprised! "Is it"? She wanted to know more. There were no colors in the world. The whole world was black & white. The world was so dull without the colors A beautiful fairy came to the earth. She was not happy with the world in black and white, she wanted to add colors to it. She prayed to the mother nature The mother nature told her "My dear Fairy, first create a color palette of 7 colors, then add colors to the world. Fairy asked, "how"? The mother nature blessed the earth with colorful fruits and vegetables. The mother nature told, "take the colors from these fruits and vegetables" Wow! said fairy with happiness, looking at those colorful fruits and vegetables She took Red from Apple & Tomatoes, Orange from Oranges, Yellow from Pineapples and Pumpkins, Green from Kiwis and Green Peas, Blue and Indigo from Blueberries, and Purple from Grapes and Jamuns She uttered spell "Apati Bapati Zippp Zzappp zoommm"!!!! and a beautiful rainbow appears on the sky taking the colours from the fruits and vegetables. and then she gave colours to the world. Green to grass and trees, blue to the sea and so many colourful flowers, birds and animals. The world became so colourful. But the fairy was not happy as the colors of the rainbow were not bright and she was concerned that the rainbow should not fade away in years to come. "What to do"? she asked the mother nature. The mother nature told with a loving voice "My dear fairy, do not worry whenever a child will eat a fruit or a vegetable the color of the rainbow will become brighter. Rainbow will continue to exist, till the children of this world are eating fruits and vegetables." Fairy was very happy. "See Sona today you can see a rainbow because of all these years children from the past generations are eating fruits and vegetables, your grandmother ate, I ate. We have saved the rainbow for you and all the other childern of this world of today's generation. don't you want the children of the future should see the rainbow too? asked the mother with a voice full of love and concern Sona, of course, wanted that the children of the future should see the rainbow too. Sona decides to save the rainbow. She starts eating Fruits and vegetables every day and since then, whenever she has seen the rainbow, she has found it getting brighter and brighter.
author: Rituraj Mishra
illustrator: Helga Parekh; Ketan Raut; Manjari Chakravarti; Niloufer Wadia; Phạm Hùng  Vinh; Priya Kuriyan; Suvidha Mistry

title: The Jungle
text: The Jungle. This is a jungle. The jungle has many animals. This is a monkey. It likes to sit on its branch. This is a bird. The bird likes to fly. This is a deer. The deer likes to run. The monkey, the bird and the deer live happily in the jungle.
author: Advitya Hajela
illustrator: Chandana Bandara  Samarakoon; Kumudini Kondhalkar; Nancy Raj; Soumya Menon

title: The Power of Truth
text: Once upon a time, bus, train, and airplanes had not been invented for travel. People used to travel in caravans, carrying their stuff on the camels. Not every city had colleges and universities. In those times, Baghdad was a famous center for education. A young, bright, boy was going to Baghdad for higher education. His mother packed his stuff for the journey. She discreetly sewed 40 gold coins in his jacket, as expense for his education. The mother advised the son to never lie, and set him off with the caravan. It so happened that on their way, the caravan was surrounded by bandits, who started looting their stuff. A bandit came to the boy and asked him, "do you have anything valuable?" He said, "Yes, I have 40 gold coins. My mother sewed them to my jacket." The bandit was astonished to hear this. He asked the boy, "Why did you tell me, you know I would take it from you?" The boy replied, "My mother had asked me to never tell a lie." This truth had a profound impact on the bandits, and they were very ashamed. They returned their looted stuff to the travelers in the caravan, and repented from banditry. Do you know who was the boy who spoke the truth in a difficult situation? The boy grew up to be a learned person and is very well known as a pious person even now. His name is Abdul Qadir Jilani.
author: Saima Aman

title: FRIENDSHIP LASTS FOREVER
text: Once there lived two best friends, Sheena and Riti. They were next door neighbours. Sheena's little brother, Sam, was a cute but naughty. He was always playing pranks on his sister. Sam's favourite sport was to scare Sheena with a roar of the tiger. Little Sam was so brave that he himself was scared of the dark. One day, as he planned to scare his sister, waiting under the bed, he screamed and jumped with fear as he saw his mother also hiding next to him. 'Bang!' his head struck the bed. "Riti! Riti!" Sheena whispered in Riti's ears as she lay fast asleep in her little cosy and comfortable bed. It was time to play hide and seek in the beautiful ground with birds fluttering and singing. "Come and find me, if you can," shouted Sheena at the top of her voice, hiding behind a tree. "Here I come!" screamed Riti. Not a single day passed when the two lovely friends didn't meet. They sat on branches and talked for hours, sharing every little detail of the day. Nature was their best friend, too. They sang and danced to their hearts' content and enjoyed every moment spent together. In the spare time, they told scary horror stories to each other turn by turn. "There are ghost hidden in the closet," warned Sheena. Riti's heart throbbed loud enough to be heard. "Where?" she enquired. "Behind you," Sheena said laughingly. And then it was Riti's turn for the haunted house story. Riti's story had a ghost inside the mirror. Every time Sheena looked into the mirror, she looked in horror as if looking at a ghost instead of her own image. They both enjoyed the adventure. Sheena tried hard to get rid of the fear of the Mirror Ghost and finally her little lamb, Timmy, helped her in shedding off the fear. Sheena and Riti loved each other and remained friends forever because.... "FRIENDSHIP LASTS FOREVER"
author: Giti Tyagi

title: Adventures of 3 Ghosts
text: Once there were three mischievous ghosts Kaalu, Yamlu and Bablu who used to scare everyone together. They had a power to transform into any scary creature. One day they had a fight and decided to end their friendship.They decided that they would frighten everyone in their own ways. Kaalu transformed into a scary creature, went inside a little boy's house and decided to scare him but the little boy was not afraid of him and he dozed off. Kaalu felt insulted and left his house. Yamlu transformed into a green spider and went inside a little boy's house but the little boy laughed and said " I am not scared "and ran into the basement. Yamlu became angry and left the little boy's house. Bablu transformed into a 3 headed ghost and went to a playground to scare a little girl but the little girl wore a scary mask and scared Bablu instead. The little girl ignored Bablu and went to play in the garden. Bablu became sad and left the playground. Kaalu, Yamlu and Bablu decided to meet since they were unsuccessful in scaring anyone. Kaalu came riding on a camel. Yamlu came riding on a Giraffe.Bablu became a red balloon and met his two friends. They repented for their mistakes and Bablu said that only if they are united people would be scared of them and not when they are alone. Kaalu and Yamlu smiled and agreed to what Bablu said. They decided that from now on they will remain together and scare everyone. They decided to start their mischief by scaring a little boy together. The little boy got scared and started shouting. Kaalu, Yamlu and Bablu were happy as they were able to scare someone after teaming up together. Kaalu, Yamlu and Bablu teamed up again to scare a man. The man got afraid and closed his eyes. They understood the power of team work. Kaalu, Yamlu and Bablu decided that they will not fight from now on and be friends forever. Kaalu, Yamlu and Bablu promised each other that they will not break their friendship ever again. They sat on a creature and embarked their journey to the next city to scare more people.
author: Ramkumar Iyer

title: THE GIRL WHO HATED MATH
text: Once there lived a 10 year old girl named Akshu who hated the Math subject, though she scored good marks. She never liked studying Math and not a single day passed without she showing abhorrence for it. One day when her mother was teaching her a topic in Math, Akshu frowned and said, “ Why should I study Math, it’s of no use.” I HATE MATH Mother thought of an idea. She said, “ Do one thing don’t study Math but don’t use anything related to math." Akshu said “Wow! That’s great!! I will not do or use anything related to MATH. I will neither use math nor study math.. Thank God.” Mother added, “ If you use anything related to numbers, shapes, measurements you will have to study Math then." "I WON'T ", shouted Akshu. Akshu looked happy and quickly switched on the T.V but the moment she took the remote she had to keep it aside as it has numbers and she would have to use it to see her favourite channels. She wanted to know the time so that she could go and play with her friends but the moment she looked at the clock she realized it has numbers too. Next she ran to the computer to play games but the keyboard has numbers, she wouldn’t be able to use it too, also games would have scores. She thought of reading a book but the moment she opened the book she saw the page numbers and chapter numbers. She closed it and kept it aside. fairy tales 60 pages grandpa stories 250pages Bugged with it, she thought of eating a cake and went into the kitchen. She asked her mom to bake her a nice brownie cake but the microwave oven had numbers too. She thought of going to the nearby shop to buy herself some snacks but she would have to use money which has numbers on coins and notes and buying something would involve calculation. In the kitchen, her eyes fell on the calendar which had numbers in the form of dates and the year. She realized that everything has something to do with math. " Oh god! Math everywhere. " She took mom's phone to speak to her friend but she couldn’t use it as the phone had a password to be typed and the phone connects to people using numbers! She tried to play games on the phone but the game had a timer to be set and points to be scored within a set limit. She tried to see a craft video but it had measurements of paper and shapes and she kept the phone aside with anger mounting up."Enough of it now!" She heard her friends calling her ” Akshu, it’s 4 ‘o clock come down to play.” Akshu ran down and found her friends getting ready to play cricket. She couldn’t play as it had numbers (no. of players in each team,order of batsmen, bowlers, runs, score, no.of balls bowled.. etc.) She refused saying, “ Let’s play indoor games.” But most of the board games had points which were numbers and she came back running home looking very sad............... " This is unbelievable. Maths is chasing me everywhere." She came back to mom saying, “Amma I give up, I have realized that nothing is possible without math and numbers. I promise you I will now study Math with interest as it is the life line of everything in the world. Without Math we wouldn’t be able to do anything." "Yes my dear, everything revolves around Math and you cannot avoid it. Love Math and it will love you back." Saying this Amma hugged her.
author: Deepalakshmi Iyer
illustrator: Hari Kumar Nair; Jemma Jose; Ramkumar Iyer

title: HEALTH IS WEALTH
text: Amidst the screams and enthusiasm, the football match was in full swing. The two teams- The Pink Panthers and The Blue Dragons- were drawn at 2-2 and the next fifteen minutes were crucial for the outcome of the match. "Why don't you go and play, Rohit?" asked his teacher. Rohit, too, wanted to play. Due to physical weakness, he wasn't very energetic and got tired very soon. "I feel tired all the time. I can't run or play for a long time," Rohit replied sadly. Rohit's sister, Rupa, was a bubbly and lively child. She was always on her toes, dancing and frolicking all the time. Rohit kept to himself and did not participate in any of the activities, neither at home nor in the school. His parents got worried due to his failing health. They decided to consult the pediatrician. Meanwhile, Rohit started losing interest in studies also. The appointment was fixed for the next Tuesday. At the clinic, Rohit saw many children of his age group. "Probably they, too, suffer from weakness and loss of energy,"thought Rohit. And surely they did. The children complained of weakness and inability to play like other children of their age. The doctor told Rohit that most children of his age ignore the healthy food and binge on junk food instead of healthy snacks. "As the name suggests, the junk food is a 'Junk'. It takes away all the energy from the body leaving us incapable of performing even the normal daily chores," warned the doctor. "Eating and watching Television simultaneously is a very bad combination where health is concerned," the doctor further advised Rohit. "Some children are very fussy and refuse to eat anything that is offered. Not eating a proper diet and being choosy in eating leads to many deficiency diseases," the doctor continued to enlighten Rohit. "What are deficiency diseases?" Rohit asked inquisitively. "Our body needs many types of nutrients that are present in a variety of food items. If we do not eat proper food, the body is deprived of the nutrient, thus leading to the deficiency disease," the doctor explained. "Have you heard of the Rainbow Diet, Rohit?" "No, doctor," Rohit replied softly. "A rainbow diet consists of food stuffs of all the colours that we see in the beautiful rainbow- Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red. We include the food items of all these colours and it is said to be a complete diet," the doctor explained patiently. "Do you ever go to the vegetable market with your mother?" enquired the doctor. "Sometimes I do," Rohit replied excitedly. "What is your f avourite vegetable that you like to purchase?" Rohit was confused as he didn't have an answer to the question. " I don't like any vegetable. So I wish my mother doesn't purchase the bottle gourd, the lady's finger, the pumpkin, the tomatoes or in fact, any vegetable," Rohit's eyes sparkled as he spoke. "Oh, that is the reason you are always tired," the doctor said thoughfully. "So, what do you do while your friends take their lunch?" the doctor was curious to know. " I normally go out to the ground and while away my time sitting on the bench. I don't feel hungry nor do i like any of the food items," Rohit told clearly. "Ah! I have found the real cause of your illness now," the doctor said delightedly. "Will you do whatever I ask you to do, Rohit?" the doctor asked. "Surely I will." "Next time when your mother is working in the kitchen, you go and help her in washing or cutting the vegetables. stay in the kitchen and look carefully at the procedure of cooking. Offer you help and appreciate the labour involved in preparing the dish," the doctor advised. "OK doctor, I will lovingly do that,"Rohit was excited with the suggestion. When Rohit went home, he remembered the doctor's advice and followed it diligently. When the food was served, he was reminded of all the efforts and the hard work he had done to help in preparing the dish. He was feeling hungry by that time and the aroma of the tasty and sumptuous dish made him gulp down the food without any fuss or complaint. He loved to watch the vegetable vendors from the window of his room looking at other people and children buying the fresh vegetables and soon grew fond of all sorts of vegetables and fruits. he no longer was a fussy and complaining child and always looked forward to completing his meal. He, no longer, had to stand and wait on the outskirts of the playground as he was equally energetic and could participated in any physical activity just like his friends did. He got an opportunity to make new friends and enjoyed his playtime like a normal healthy child. Childhood is an important phase of a person's lifetime. Importance should be given to the healthy diet and exercise to help the children grow and develop in a healthy and happy manner. Wishing all the children a Healthy and Happy life!
author: Giti Tyagi
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Agantuk Samaresh; Divya George; Jayesh Sivan; Niloufer Wadia; Partho Sengupta; Rijuta Ghate; Sahitya Rani; Santosh Pujari; Shailja Jain Chougule; Soumya Menon; Tanvee Nabar; UK Nhal

title: The Obedient dog
text: I was going to school in my car. It was raining heavily, but we were roasted and suffocated inside the car with closed windows, i wasted away the hot yet beautiful summers and didn't even realise it. Suddenly it was time to go back to school looking at the clouds i was wishing,”let there be a flood,a landslide, a tornado anything but without hurting us close the school for a month”, as we crossed panaji and reached santa cruz the rain slowly stopped, as i was looking outside, my face bloomed with happiness, it wasn’t a joke nor was it our car that splashed water on an unknown person standing on the road side,but a cute white dog, it was white but a stray after playing in the dirty water it looked grey he had a bushy tail and a pinkish nose, smiling at us,stood on the boundary wall of a house, he was so cute that you had no choice but to smile as you could never remain sad after looking at such a joyful face,as the days passed i got used to school, almost everyday he used to stand there and as our car passed him used to jump down and go away as if he was just waiting for me, on the days i saw him my day went happily, but the days i didn't see him i surely got a scolding from teacher. After observing this for a month or so i was sure enough to say it was my lucky dog, then why didn’t i call him the lucky dog but the obedient dog? I thought that god had sent it for me to tell me about the day ahead, he was doing the duty given to him by god honestly and was obedient, but honest and obedient dog would be a big name, i called this obedient dog ‘obediento’. I got to know more and more about him, he had a brother who just looked like him, but the only difference was that its eye was circled black. I never saw obediento’s brother in the morning but in the afternoon while coming back, i always saw him laying in garbage and chasing stray pigs. The obediento had 4 modes of telling me my future 1. He used to not be there that meant that my day was horrible 2. He used to sit down on the ground that meant my day was to be good 3. He just stood up on the wall with no expression on his face it meant that my day would be very good 4. He used stand up smiling removing his tongue out it meant a bunch of new opportunities and praises from teachers from that day till today many things have changed my uniform pant from short has turned long, i have turned from junior to senior, many things have changed on the way from home to school but obediento still stands there waiting for me every morning. -------- saras sardessai
author: Saras Sardessai
illustrator: Anupam Arunachalam; Deepa Balsavar; Garima Gupta; Josh Morgan; Krupa Thakur-Patil; Niloufer Wadia; Sachin Pandit; Sheshadri Mokshagundam; Visvesvaraya National Memorial Trust

title: Sringeri Srinivas's Cow Must Moo!
text: One day, Sringeri Srinivas, the banana farmer, came home from the cattle fair with a new cow. “We will call her Laxmi,” said his wife, Parvatamma. But who was that behind Laxmi? It was a black and white cat with green eyes. “She walked with us all the way,” said Sringeri. “We will call her Manuli,” said his daughter, Uma. The next day, Sringeri took Laxmi to graze in the field. Manuli followed Laxmi. The other cows were curious. “Miaow,” said Manuli to them, softly. “Mooo,” they said to her, swishing their tails. “Good Laxmi,” he said, stroking the animal. Laxmi gave more milk than all the other cows. Sringeri was very happy. In the evening, it was time to milk the cows. All the other cows turned their heads. Who was making this funny sound? Not a 'MOO'. A big, cow-sized 'M IAOW'. Suddenly, Laxmi gave a loud 'Miaow'. “Miaow,” sang Laxmi. “MOOOOO!” they all bellowed in surprise. “Miaow,” said Manuli. “Miaow?” Sringeri was puzzled. Why does this cow go 'Miaow'? “I do not know. But it is OK!” said Parvatamma. “She is just different. Maybe Manuli taught her. But see how much milk she has given!” The next day, the same thing happened. Laxmi gave lots of milk. Then she gave a cow-sized 'Miaow'. Manuli gave a cat-sized 'Miaow' too. This time the other cows were not happy. “MOOOO!” they shouted. “MOOOO!” “Please give milk,” Sringeri Srinivas begged the cows. They glared at Laxmi. And they refused to give milk. But the cows turned away. “NOOOOO,” they seemed to say! Sringeri was angry at this strange new cow. “I will take Laxmi back,” he said, giving his famous frown. “But she gives so much sweet milk!” said Parvatamma. “Please let us keep her!” “Well then, teach her to moo by tomorrow,” said Sringeri. “Or she MUST GO!” Parvatamma and the children spent the next day trying to make Laxmi moo. MOO They took Sringeri's new mobile phone. They showed her videos of other cows mooing. They mooed at her too. MOO They also did an aarti for Laxmi. They fed her sweets. MOO They prayed to their gods. “Please make Laxmi moo.” All the neighbours came to help. Shivanna brought sugarcane. Shankara brought cooked rice. “Moo, Laxmi, moo,” they all said. Laxmi liked all the attention. She gave even more milk than usual.
