title: Mission Chocolate Cake
text: Say hello to the McAvery Colony of Ants. We are a smart, hardworking community, who LOVE sweets. We love Indian sweets like laddoos and barfis. We also love chocolates and lollipops! Messenger Ant Steve comes with a message! There is a whole chocolate cake in the kitchen! Quick! We must get to the cake before Nala, the ever hungry cat, wakes up! But we are well prepared to handle such situations. We march forward to our target, as Jessy and Simba look on. Oooh, Pachiamma the maid, is cleaning the kitchen! We must not get caught. Up the cupboard we go! We must not get distracted by all the other goodies. We reached the cake, and we have it all to ourselves! Yummy! So, that's another successful mission for the McAvery Ants. Remember, sweets taste good only when shared!
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: The Magic Socks
text: Munna was excited! His mum had given him some money to buy himself something at the toy store. Should he buy a bat? Should he buy a ball? On his way, he saw a woman carrying a bundle of socks. "Oi boy," the woman said, "want to buy these magic socks?" "What makes them magical?" Munna asked. "Just use your imagination, and they turn into any creature you want". Munna washed the bundle of socks and hung them to dry. But nothing magical happened. Munna wore a pair on his feet. Awww, they felt nice and fuzzy! But still no magic! Munna took them off his feet and wondered what to do. Oh, that's right! The woman had asked him to use his imagination! Hmm... Poof! One pair became a purple elephant! Another pair became an orange cat! What a great time he had playing with his new friends! He could create so many imaginary creatures with just these pairs of socks! What fun! When his mum was back, she asked him if he had gotten bored, playing all by himself. "Oh no, mumma! Not at all!"
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: Win Together
text: I need another hand Once an old lady sowed a seed It was going to be a Carrot Tree The seed grew into a seedling and the seedling into a plant With a little bit of manure The carrot started to grow! I thought of picking the small carrot And make a tasty sweet dish! I caught it by it's tail, pulled it hard But nothing came into my hand Oh nothing worked, nothing worked I need another hand Then came the old lady's nephew We pulled it harder together But nothing worked, nothing worked I need another hand Then came the old lady's dog Huffing and Puffing we pulled together Oh nothing worked, nothing worked I need another hand Then came the old lady's cat When she heard everyone shout When everyone pulled it hard together The carrot came out! Oh look at this, look at this We have finally won!
author: saurabh dangwal

title: Everyday Magic
text: "And the prince and the princess, flew away on their unicorn, and lived happily ever after. The End". Minnie sighed deeply. That night, as her mother was tucking her in bed, Minnie said, "Mumma, I wish there was magic in my life - the kind I read about in fairy tales!" "There's magic in everyday life too, Minnie," Mumma replied. "There's magic in the way you pack your books by yourself, like a big girl, the night before school. It must feel great to be able to plan your day and do your own work." "There's magic in the way you get to pass beautiful and colourful fields every morning, to get to school". "Plus, I get to do with Nina, my best friend!" ﻿ " There's magic in all the new things you learn at school everyday." "I do love Dipali Ma'am! She is so sweet and so smart, Mumma!" "There's magic in how you get to laugh and play with your friends at school. You get to be carefree and have fun without any worries." "There's magic in how you do your homework and read all your lessons, every evening after you come home from school. You have your very own books, stationery and everything you need!" "I study everyday because I want to be smart like Dipali Ma'am!" "There's magic in how you help me do the dishes after dinner. I feel so proud of you!" "I want to be just like you when I grow up, Mumma!" "There's magic in everyday life because God has blessed us with beautiful lives in a beautiful world. Stay happy, Minnie and you will find magic in even the simplest things." The next day after school, Minnie came running to give her mother a hug. "You were right, Mumma," she said, "everyday is magic!"
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: Shepherd for the Day
text: Story Description Ashley lives on a village farm with his family. Bessie, the prize cow, has given birth to a calf, which Ashley plays with and looks after. Seeing the bonding between his son and the animals, Ashley's father gives him the job of being a shepherd to the cows. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Conditions cun-dish-uns Poor weather conditions had been forecasted for the afternoon. Shepherd sheh-pur-d Ashley's father gave him the job of being a shepherd to the cows. Drenched dren-ch-d The rain came down so heavily that everything was drenched. Amateurish am-ur-chur-ish Ashley thought his shepherding skills were too amateurish, and could have been better. Ashley lived in a village that had a cow called Bessie. She had recently given birth to a calf, which Ashley played with every day. Ashley wanted to keep the adorable little animal, but his father said the calf had to stay close to its mother and bond properly. "I can see you adore them so much, how would you like to be their shepherd?" said Ashley's father. "Really? What does that involve?" said Ashley. "You accompany the cow and her calf, and make sure they and all of the cows are fine. You take them to different places and bring them home safely. Make sure they get food and fresh water." Ashley had never been given such an important responsibility before. He jumped at the opportunity. "Your first duty will be to watch and protect Bessie and her calf," said Ashley's father. "They're our most valuable cows." Ashley stood in the field watching the cows graze, but also keeping a careful eye on Bessie and the calf. The calf was off playing near the bushes and sniffing the other cows. After a while of standing around, Ashley's legs began to ache. "This is harder than I thought," he said. A huge rainstorm suddenly drenched the fields, and while finding shelter, Ashley lost Bessie's calf. "Oh, no! I'm so clumsy!" he said. He started calling for the calf. Bessie felt distressed, wondering where her calf was. The other cows ran towards the trees and bushes. Soon, the rainstorm drifted off, and out from a hedge popped the little calf! It sprang out and ran to Bessie. "You were sheltering from the rain," said Ashley to the calf. "Don't worry now. The storm has gone." Bessie licked her calf all over. Bessie let Ashley pick up her calf and cuddle her. She felt very safe and secure in Ashley's arms. "I'd better be honest to Dad," said Ashley. "Perhaps I'm not ready to be a shepherd just yet. There's more to this job than standing around and watching. I lost you, and I won't let it happen again." "You must have been soaked," said Ashley's father. "I was," said Ashley. "The rain came on so quickly that the cows hid under the trees. I had no time to round them up and leave." "And I lost the calf," said Ashley. "It ran and hid in the bushes. I'm too amateurish at this job." "Don't beat yourself up," said Ashley's father. "This is only your first time. I knew you'd run into difficulty. You did well in the poor weather conditions." "All you do is keep the animals moving to new areas where they can graze," said Ashley's father. "They're under your control. You can take them wherever you want." "Thank you for your help, son," said Ashley's father. "So you're not going to fire me?" said Ashley. "Ha! Not this time. But are you sure you wouldn't rather clean out the chicken houses?" "That's so gross!" Ashley laughed. "I'm going to stay being a shepherd." Post-Reading Questions What job does Ashley's father give to his son? What causes the calf to get lost? Re-read. Ask: Where was the calf hiding? Re-read. Ask: What does a shepherd generally do? Re-read. Ask: What does Ashley's father offer to him as a different job? What kind of responsibilities would you like to have?
author: Hello English

title: The Changing Crow
text: A crow was walking along enjoying the beautiful sunset. Suddenly, as it looked at its shadow, it saw something peculiar and strange. It was purple with blue and yellow feathers. The crow moved its eye around to make sure it wasn't dreaming. It was real. Story Description A crow magically turns into a purple dinosaur overnight. The dinosaur is scared and finds two children as friends, but he soon unleashes his craziness around the town and has to be stopped. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Curious c-your-ee-uss The children were curious about the dinosaur. Whimpered wim-purr-d The scared dinosaur whimpered. Agitated aj-ih-tay-tid The dinosaur became agitated and upset, and went on a rampage. Townspeople t-ow-n-s-pea-pul The townspeople hid from the frightening dinosaur. Scared, the crow took flight and went back to its nest. Overnight, something magical and unusual happened. The crow transformed into the very thing it had seen in it shadow. It became a curious purple dinosaur. The crow didn't know how it had happened, but now it was much bigger and stronger, and full of energy. It bounced along! The crow suddenly felt very afraid, having become a beast overnight. A family of a boy, a girl and a granny comforted the poor creature, which had found its way to their back garden, looking for a place to hide. The poor crow could not describe what had happened to the family, and it whimpered. They fed the dinosaur some slices of tomato, and it gobbled them up ferociously. But little did they know that the dinosaur was actually a crow. "It's so alive," said the boy. "I've never seen such an active creature before!" The children laughed and told jokes and stories to their new friend, who was full of cheer and character. The dinosaur leaped around their house. The children adored it so much that they fought over who could take it to the school and the market. While they were arguing over ownership, the dinosaur suddenly tore away and went to the market. It felt angry and frustrated. Something was happening to the magic to make it agitated and jumpy. The dinosaur stole tea from a seller and found its way to the fruit stands, where it stole several different oranges, tomatoes and mangos, devouring them and leaving the stall in a mess. The whole town spoke of the dinosaur running wild. The boy and girl caught up with it, and saw that its feathers were falling off. Perhaps they had been fooled, they wondered. The creature wasn't exactly everything it seemed to be. The girl seized the dinosaur and pulled off some of its feathers. It looked dark underneath. She wasn't sure what it was, but she felt something was wrong. The dinosaur took the girl's weight and kept charging through the market. The dinosaur threw the girl off its back and kept running away, now angry and scared. The townspeople took cover, as did granny, who was terrified and shocked. The dinosaur charged at every stall, and the sellers took cover. The dinosaur took off and shed most of its colour. The magic was wearing off, and it was returning to being a crow. It flew high over the boy, who was trying to chase it on his bicycle, and it came crashing down on top of him, pecking at his hair. "Get off, you big lump!" said the boy. The dinosaur started shrinking into a bird, and the children saw what was happening. The dinosaur squirmed and squawked, and it began to sound like a bird, chirping and even crowing. "It's not a dinosaur at all," said the girl. "It's a crow." The bird shrank away and flew off, and the children had to help the market sellers restore their stalls. The bird had done a lot of damage. "Maybe we should find it and make sure it's ok," said the boy. "I think you're right," said the girl. "He is our friend." Just then, the bird reappeared. The girl was eating an onion bhajee when it emerged. The crow quickly snatched the bhajee out of her hands, and flew away with it. The crow waited but the magic did not work again. It would not become a dinosaur. It was an ordinary crow, and it relaxed into its body. The girl wondered if she would ever see the crow flying around again. One day the crow returned, as the boy and the girl were sketching dinosaur bones. "Are you going to cause trouble?" said the girl. "I don't think so." The crow stayed with the children and played with them each day. Yet the magic of the mystery remained. Just how did the crow transform into a colourful dinosaur? Post-Reading Questions Where did the dinosaur hide after it transformed from being a crow? What did the dinosaur do to scare the townspeople? Re-read. Ask: Where did the children want to take the dinosaur? Re-read pages 10-12. Ask: Why did the children suspect something was wrong? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did the crow steal from the girl? ﻿Describe the dinosaur's change in character through the story.
author: Hello English

title: Don't Eat The Sugar
text: Story Description A boy dreams of eating sugary foods, when a parcel comes for his grandmother. It is sugar, and she hides it under his bed. The boy finds the sugar and eats it, against his grandmother's wishes, and everything starts to go wrong. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Hilariously ﻿hil-air-ee-uss-lee ﻿Henry's tongue grew hilariously long and his friends laughed. Intensified ﻿in-ten-sih-fy-d ﻿The dreams Henry was having intensified. They felt so real. Hyperactive ﻿hi-pur-ac-tiv ﻿The boys were all hyperactive, running everywhere with so much energy. Rumbled ﻿rum-bull-d ﻿ ﻿Henry was rumbled by his grandmother. She had caught him. Henry brought in a package for his grandmother one morning. It felt heavy, and he wondered what it was. "Go ahead and open it," said his grandmother. Henry tore off the paper and saw that it was a box of sugar. "Now, whatever you do," said grandmother, "don't you dare eat this. It's special sugar for baking. If you eat this sugar, something terrible will happen to you." "Something terrible," giggled Henry. "So spooky! Silly grandmother is trying to scare me. Ha! That won't work." That night, Henry dreamed of all the tasty cakes his grandmother was going to bake. But she had been too mean. Her voice played over in his head. "Don't you dare eat the sugar...the sugar...the sugar..." "Huh," Henry thought. "I'm going to find out where that sugar is and see what it tastes like. I'm not listening to my mean old grandmother." The dreams intensified and Henry saw himself eating a massive carrot and chocolate cake. It was so sweet and delicious, that Henry dribbled in his sleep. "I can't wait any longer," said Henry when he got up. "I have to find that sugar." "I'll put it under the bed," said grandmother. "That way, Henry won't find it and it's safe." "Hah," thought Henry, spying on his grandmother. "So that's where she's hiding the sugar. Well, I'll wait until she's gone and I'll take it!" Henry told all of his friends about the sugar, and they encouraged him to steal it. "Come on," they said. "It's only under your bed. You gotta share that amazing sugar with us." Suddenly, grandmother found them talking. "Three boys together," she said. "Now that's a recipe for cooking up trouble." Henry waited until his grandmother was in the shower. He sneaked under his bed and took the sugar, and he found some freshly prepared cakes. He ate all of them while hiding under the bed. "So sweet!" he said. "Silly grandmother won't know it was me who ate the cakes. I'll blame it on the dog." Henry sneaked out of his home and took the box of sugar with him. He started licking the sugar off his fingers. He felt really happy and full of energy. "Oh, wow. I have to share this with my friends," he said. "Uh, oh," said Henry. "Now there's a leak in the box. The sugar is falling out! I can't keep the sugar anywhere else, so I'll have to eat it." He started eating the sugar very quickly. Henry shared the rest of the sugar with his friends, and they all got hyperactive. They wrestled, climbed fences, broke pots, trampled on garden, chased farm yard animals and laughed a lot together. Henry went home and finished the last of the sugar. He hid the empty box under the bed. He felt a headache coming on. "Oh, no," he said. "I've eaten too much sugar. I'd better not be sick, otherwise silly old grandmother will find out it was me who ate it." "Argh!" said grandmother, just as she was about to start baking a cake. "Now I can't do any baking, because somebody has eaten all of the sugar!" "You little brat!" shouted grandmother. "You ate the sugar!" "No, I didn't!" said Henry. "It was the dog, and my two friends." "So they came in the house and took it?" said grandmother. "Not possible! It was you. You even have sugar crumbs on your fingers!" "Oh, no. I've been rumbled!" said Henry. "Silly grandmother," said Henry, escaping from her. "She'll just have to buy another box of sugar. Uh, oh. What's happening?" Henry looked in the mirror and saw that his tongue was growing longer and longer. It wouldn't stop. "Help! Aiiee! Help!" Henry was so scared that he hid under his blanket. He touched his tongue against his chest and squealed. "I'm thorry for eating all of the thugar," he said. "I thouldn't have done it! I like thweet thingth too much." "Oh, my goodness!" shouted grandmother, as Henry left the house. "I told you something bad would happen if you ate my sugar!" Henry's friends were shocked, and they laughed when they saw his hilariously long tongue. "Take me to the doctor!" shouted Henry. Post-Reading Questions Where did grandmother hide the sugar? What kind of cake did Henry dream about? Re-read. Ask: What happened to the sugar box, and what did Henry do? Re-read. Ask: Who did Henry try to pin the blame on? Re-read. Ask: What did the sugar do to Henry's tongue? Why is it important to not steal?
author: Hello English

title: The Funny Dream
text: It was a warm, dark night. Mayank was sleeping in the verandah. You could not hear a sound, except that of... Mayank giggling in his sleep! He had just had an awesome dream in which he was a super-hero, who could kill monsters with his laser vision. Mayank got up to drink a glass of water. He was eager to share his dream with somebody... but with whom? The next morning, Mayank was describing his dream to his mother. But even before he had finished, his mother said, "Yes, Mayank, that's funny! Now get ready for school! I still need to pack your dabba... Oh, dear!" At school, he was describing his dream to his teacher. But even before he had finished, his teacher cut in and said, "That is not how vision works, Mayank. The retina creates an upside down image.. blah.. blah.." "Oh, God! Not another lesson on vision!" Mayank thought, miserably. After he came back from school, he tried describing his dream to his father and the other workers. But they were just pretending to listen. "Yes, Mayank, very good..." his father said absently, and turned back to his friends, "now, what if we split the manure..." Mayank was very disappointed. He wanted to share his funny dream with someone, but no one seemed to be interested. All the grown ups were busy in their own worlds. Then he had an idea! Oh, how he rushed to the park to tell his friends about his funny dream! Mayank found his friends at the juice shop, and recounted his dream to them. They laughed heartily - which was exactly the reaction Mayank was hoping for! Then, all of them played a game where they pretended to be monsters and super-heroes with laser vision. Oh, how nice it was to just be a silly kid!
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: The Enormous Pumpkin
text: Story Description One day, an enormous pumpkin rolls down a big hill and lands in a village. The villagers don't know what to do with it, until something from the inside it starts hatching out! Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Enormous ﻿in-or-m-uss ﻿Something rolled towards the village. It was an enormous pumpkin. Calamitous ﻿cuh-lam-it-uss ﻿The calamitous ride took the pumpkin down hill. Ghastly ﻿gas-d-lee ﻿What was inside the pumpkin was ghastly and scary. Chaotic ﻿cey-ot-ik ﻿The pumpkin cracked open in a chaotic way. Something huge had grown out of the undergrowth near the village. An enormous pumpkin sat in the middle of a big field. It had crushed many plants and forced many animals to leave their homes. One day, the pumpkin started moving. The enormous pumpkin rolled down the mountain at a calamitous speed. It missed some huts and nearly hit the chickens and birds who were running from it. The pumpkin rolled and jumped, all the way down the slope, until it stopped at the bottom outside the village. The village women heard the thudding stop of the enormous pumpkin. It had felt like an earthquake. They tried pushing it backwards, but it was too heavy. Even some of the chickens tried to help move the giant vegetable. The women rested against the pumpkin, trying to stop it from getting any closer to their village. It was exhausting to keep it in place. The pumpkin gradually inched closer to their huts. One of the boys saw the women struggling. He went to tell the men of the news. "An enormous pumpkin has rolled into our village," said the boy. The men went to inspect and they relieved the women of sitting and stopping the pumpkin. The thing was humongous. They had never seen anything so brilliant! "We have to carry this to the village and show everyone," they said. "People will come from the next region to see it! It will make our village famous." Suddenly, a little rumbling sound came from inside the pumpkin. The men retreated. The animals watched. The pumpkin rolled on to its side. Then it rolled on to its other side. The pumpkin shell opened very slowly. Fingers emerged, combined with patterns and seeds. One of the men cried out for help. "Don't do that," the other man said. "You'll scare what's inside. This is incredible." The shell burst open and a huge monster climbed out. The men couldn't believe what they were seeing. They had never seen anything so gigantic and chaotic looking before. The men ran for their lives, and to warn the other villagers to flee. But the ghastly look on the giant's face turned to one of joy and friendliness. The monster scattered pumpkin seeds - thousands and thousands of them - across the fields. The last of the seeds flew out of the pumpkin, and the monster retreated inside. The men returned later, but there was no sign of the monster. It had vanished entirely. All that was left was the pumpkin shell, and thousands of seeds scattered across the land. The next season, thanks to the pumpkin monster, thousands of big, healthy pumpkins had grown in the fields. The villagers were able to sell their harvest and make enough money to live off for several years. Post-Reading Questions What hatched out of the enormous pumpkin? Who stopped the pumpkin from crushing the village? Re-read. Ask: Describe the monster from inside the pumpkin. Re-read. Ask: What does the pumpkin monster do? Re-read. Ask: How long would the money last for the villagers? What is the lesson of the story?
author: Hello English

title: The boy who was always late for school
text: Rahul is always late for school. He throws a tantrum while waking up. Today Rahul thinks its Sunday so he woke up at nine in the morning. The bus leaves at nine, and when his Mama woke him up they went to school in a rush. When he reached to his class everyone was laughing at him when Miss Sharma was scolding him. Tara and Ahan were his best friends at school, when he got scolded Miss Sharma made three of them stand outside the class, they got scolded because they would always accompany him in his pranks and tricks. Today is Tuesday, Rahul, and Ahan’s most boring day because today is the art class. Tara loves art class she says it's her favorite class in the school. Today is also a sports class so, in the sports class, Rahul is so excited that when he swings his favorite cricket bat he doesn’t hit the ball he hits Sanvi with it. When they reach class Rahul says sorry to Sanvi but she goes to the medical room very quickly. When she came back with a cube of ice in her hand Rahul tried to say sorry but when he did they became friends. Today is finally Saturday and Rahul has some plans with his friends but his Mama wants him to do his schoolwork first so he whispers to himself ‘ I should do my work. When he finished his work he went to play with is friends. Today, his mother gave him a good lesson and from that day on Rahul was always early when he had to go to school. Now, Rahul even likes to study!!
author: Aathira Karthik

title: Bad Mood
text: Chutki, the Squirrel was in a very bad mood. She was yelling at her squirrel-neighbours and making a scene. Pammy, the Girl, came outside to see who was making all that noise. "What's wrong, Chutki?" Pammy asked. "I'm in a bad mood!" Chutki grumbled. "Let's go on a walk, Chutki. Then you'll feel all better!" Pammy said. So, Chutki, who was still in a very bad mood, and Pammy set off on a walk. "Aren't these flowers pretty, Chutki? They smell wonderful!" "Hmmph! I don't like them! They're tickling my nose!" "Look, Chutki! What a beautiful sunset!" "Hmmph! I don't like it! Let's go back, it's going to get dark now." "Let's dip our feet in the river, Chutki! The water looks great!" "Hmmph! I don't want to! I don't like to get my fur wet." Just then, the river splashed on Chutki and Chutki got drenched. "I'll help you dry off, Chutki" Pammy said, kindly. "Ooooh, I'm in such a bad mood!" Chutki grumbled. "Chutki, do you want to talk about why you're in such a bad mood?" "Maybe..." "Last night," Chutki said, "I had a bad dream that bears and wolves were chasing me. So, I'm too scared to go to bed tonight, because, what if my dream comes true?" "Oh, Chutki. I'm sorry you had a nightmare. But nightmares don't ever come true. And if bears and wolves attack you tonight, yell my name and I'll come save you!" Pammy said. "Thanks, Pammy. I'm not in a bad mood anymore!" "Next time, just talk about why you're in a bad mood. Then you'll feel all better."
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: When I Grow Up
text: Hello, I am Mindy. Earlier this week, I was very confused when someone asked me, "Mindy, what do you want to become when you grow up?" You see, I don't really know! Mumma is a pastry chef. Sometimes, I help her bake her orders. She thinks I'd make a very good pastry chef, when I grow up. My best friend Jia and I, take ballet lessons together. She thinks we should become ballerinas when we grow up. I also take singing lessons. Amare thinks he and I should start a band! My other best friend Chandana wants to start a veterinarian clinic with me, when we grow up. A veterinary doctor is a doctor for animals. I love animals and that did seem like it would be super fun! I was so confused! So, I wrote my Papa a letter. I explained what everyone had said and asked him, "What should I become when I grow up, Papa?" Dear Mindy, There is plenty of time to decide what you want to become when you grow up. Actually, you could be all these things and so many other things! So, right now, just work hard at everything you're learning and be kind to everyone. The future then, will take care of itself. From, Papa Well, I think that is superb advice!
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: My Feelings
text: Sometimes, I feel angry. I want to say rude things and yell at everyone. But being angry is of no use. If I say rude things, I'm just going to hurt someone's feelings, and feel awful about it myself. Instead, I drink a few sips of water and count to ten. I tell myself to talk only when I'm feeling better. Sometimes, I feel proud of myself. I feel so good about what I've done that I want everyone to clap and cheer for me. While it's important to be proud of yourself, it is not okay to become arrogant. Arrogance is when you think nobody else can do what you've done - and that's never true! Instead, I smile and say thank you when someone praises me. I also listen to feedback that will help me do even better, next time. Sometimes, I feel sad. I feel a knot in my throat, and my chest feels heavy. I just want to cry and cry. It's okay to feel sad. Everyone feels sad every now and then. But it's not a very nice feeling to stay sad, and the longer you stay sad, the worse you'll feel. Instead, I try and think of happy memories. I think of all of my favourite things, like ice cream and cartoons! Then, I tell myself that that even though I'm sad now, I won't be sad forever. Sometimes, I feel curious. While learning about something new, I feel amazed and have lots of questions. I feel doubts and questions rising in my mind, like bubbles rising up a soda drink! While it's very good to be curious about the things you're learning, it can be a little annoying for the other person, to have to answer so many questions. Instead, I make a note of all my questions. Then, I ask the person when they have time to answer my questions. When I'm getting my doubts answered, I listen carefully and I wait for the other person to finish talking, before asking my next question. Sometimes, I feel like I want attention. So, I start acting funny on purpose, or do anything that will make people watch me. I want to be the centre of attention, all the time. But, that's not the way it works. I need to watch and listen, and let others be the centre of attention, so that, when it's my turn - they'll watch and listen to me, too! Instead, I just close my eyes for a second and try to calm down. I tell myself that I don't need attention to be important. Sometimes, I feel a burst of energy! I feel like running and screaming and jumping, all at once! It feels great, but then, I don't know what to do with so much energy. I just get nervous and jumpy, and find it hard to concentrate. Instead, I take a few deep breaths. In my mind, I make a list of all the useful things I can do, without anyone's help. I start doing these one after the other. And I tell myself that it's okay if I don't get everything right in my first go. Sometimes, I feel happy. I feel light enough to float up the sky, like a fluffy cloud! It's important to be happy because only when you are happy, you can make someone else happy. But in doing what makes you happy, you should make sure that you are not hurting or harming yourself or anybody else. Most importantly, always remember, your feelings matter.
author: Sudeepta Rao

title: What's in the Package?
text: Story Description Ariel and Jane's mum orders a special set of gifts for Ariel. They collect the package from the post office, but Ariel isn't allowed to open it yet. She wonders what could be inside, as her sister Jane teases her. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Deliver ﻿dih-liv-ur ﻿The gift was delivered to the post office. Addressed ﻿ ﻿uh-dress-d ﻿The package was addressed to Ariel. Rattled ﻿rat-ul-d ﻿Something shook and rattled inside the box. Package ﻿pa-kij ﻿ ﻿She guessed what the package contained. Mother went to buy fruit from the market stall, and then she stopped at the electronics store to buy an important gift. It was for Ariel, her youngest daughter. It could not be delivered straight away, so mother was happy to wait for a while, until it arrived at the post office. A couple of days later, mother went to pick something up from the post office. It was a box, and it was addressed to Ariel. "I wonder what's inside?" said Ariel's older sister, Jane. "Can I see?" said Ariel. "Not yet," said mother. Once they got home, Jane picked up the box and rattled it around. Several items shook inside. "Put it down," said Ariel. "That's my box. It's not fair." "I have a good idea of what it is," said Jane. "Do you want me to tell you?" "No!" said Ariel. "Mum! Jane's teasing me again." "I think it's a pair of shoes," said Jane. "What do you think?" "I think it's a dress and a pair of shoes," said Ariel. She felt the box and it seemed too heavy for just two items to be inside. "Let's see if Mum will let you open it yet," said Jane. "Nobody's opening anything until after dinner," said their mother. "You two, come and help set the table." "Do we really have to?" said Ariel. "If you want to open that package, then yes," said their mother. After dinner, Ariel and Jane knelt down beside the box. "I'll help you remove the white tape," said Jane. "Then you can lift the lid." "Ok," said Ariel, very excited. "I wonder what could be inside!" Ariel lifted the lid and two puppets sprang out. They had shaved heads and earrings. "Cool! Traditional dolls!" she said. "I've always wanted these for my bedroom." "Hold on," said Jane. "Is that it? It's a heavy box. There has to be more in there." Jane and Ariel felt the box, but now it was light, even with the puppets inside. "These puppets don't weigh much," said Ariel. "I don't understand where the extra weight came from. Hold on...I have an idea." "What is it?" said Jane. "Perhaps someone opened this box already and took something out. This is suspicious." Just then, their mother came into the room. "Mum!" they both said. "Are you looking for this thing?" said their mother. They both jumped for joy. "I got a phone!" said Ariel. "I'm so happy for you," said Jane. "Can I play with it first?" Post-Reading Questions ﻿Where did Ariel's mum collect the package from? What did Ariel and Jane think was inside the box? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What does Jane and Ariel's mum tell them to do? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What two items to they find in the box? ﻿Re-read pages 11-12. Ask: ﻿Why did the box used to be heavier? ﻿Name a gift you would like to receive in a box.
author: Hello English

title: Fat King Skinny King
text: Story Description A king chases after his prize greyhound racing dog. The dog is so fast that the king cannot possibly catch him, but in trying, the king changes something about himself. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Overgrown oh-vur-grow-n The king had turned into an overgrown version of himself. Greyhound grey-how-n-d The king had a pet greyhound who was a very fast runner. Canine cay-nine The greyhound was an energetic little canine. Reattached ree-a-ta-ch-d The king caught his dog and reattached lead to him. There was once a fat king who ruled a kingdom of fat people. The people never went outside, and all they ate was ice-cream, chocolate, chips and things dipped in fried batter. The king doubled in size from all the unhealthy food he had eaten. He was twice the man he used to be. His tunic and overall were too tight around his body, and his head had overgrown his hat. He often stood with his arms and legs outwards to balance his weight, or he would fall over. The skinniest creature in the kingdom was the king's favourite prize dog - Bucky the racing greyhound. This dog was a fast little canine. The king took Bucky off his lead, and suddenly Bucky ran away from the king. "Bucky, no!" yelled the king. "That silly dog is going to jump in the river and chase the ducks!" The king sweated and his heart pounded as he chased after Bucky. But Bucky was having a great time. He knew the king was fat, and he was determined to do anything to get him to exercise. The king panted and panted with his tongue hanging out of his mouth. Suddenly, Bucky jumped into the air, and the king slipped. Bucky took off like a light aeroplane. He had seen something. "No!" shouted the king. Bucky kept leaping after a bird, who saw the dog coming and avoided him. Bucky could smell the bird - it was delicious. The bird panicked when the dog jumped higher and higher. The bird was too smart and strong for Bucky, and it took off, escaping into the trees. Bucky got tired and slowed down. Then, suddenly, the king sprinted as fast as he could and dived on top of Bucky, reattaching his lead. "I've got you, boy!" he said. "You're a good dog." The king looked at himself. All the running had caused him to shed the weight and become skinny. The king was overjoyed and shocked. He couldn't stop laughing. When the king returned to his land, his people were inspired by his quick weight loss, and they all started chasing after their dogs. The people lost weight very quickly, choosing to eat healthily. Bucky laughed to himself. His plan to get the king slimmer had worked. "Now you can walk me every day, your skinniness!" thought Bucky. Post-Reading Questions ﻿ What are greyhound dogs famous for? What happened to the king after he chased Bucky? Re-read. Ask: ﻿What did Bucky do that was unexpected? ﻿Re-read pages 8-9. Ask: ﻿What happened to Bucky after he chased the bird? ﻿Re-read. Ask: ﻿What could the king do with Bucky now he was skinny again? ﻿What is your favourite kind of dog?
author: Hello English

title: Where Imagination Flows
text: Story Description A story about stepping away from the crowd, and going on your own adventure. It requires courage, determination and openness to allow your imagination to move. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Spontaneous ﻿spon-tay-nee-uss ﻿If you stop thinking, something spontaneous happens all by itself. Avoiding ﻿a-voy-ding ﻿You can spend a lot of time avoiding the issue. Impatient ﻿im-pay-shun-t ﻿The journey can be long, making you feel impatient to get there. Rhythm ﻿ri-th-um ﻿Everything comes together like the rhythm of a band playing well. You can spend a long time thinking of what to play. When you stop thinking for a moment, Something spontaneous and new appears all by itself in your mind. You can pretend to be a lion hunting by a tree. Or you can sit bored wishing you could join in. You can pretend the bar is attached to a tree. You can cross to a land with a bush-baby and a happy dinosaur. Or you can be too scared and keep away. You can talk about things together and come up with new ideas. Hey, I wonder where our imagination will take us? Perhaps you'd surf a wave while avoiding a shark. Or perhaps you're not in the mood to play. Maybe you get your own idea. You're steering a ship through rough, tall waves on stressful seas. You can join your friend with a lion's mane, clapping and dancing your way through the plains. You don't need a care in the world and the fun can never end. You can dream of visiting outers space and seeing blazing meteors. Or you can be impatient to get to school. You can turn the minibus into a spaceship, experiencing the stars. Who said journeys have to be boring? Then your imagination opens and the void fills with everything. The fun comes flooding in. You feel the music, you see the colours, you feel the waves, and a band-like rhythm comes together. When that happens, you're not afraid to leave the crowd, and to go on your own adventure. No matter where it takes you, no matter what awaits you, you ride with the flow. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿Post-Reading Questions What does imagination require? Where can your imagination take you? What is required to not be afraid of going on an adventure?
author: Hello English

title: Magnificent
text: Story Description Serena's father has a laboratory containing many objects. She introduces her friend Jimmy to four items - a microscope, binoculars, a telescope and a magnifying glass, and he learns about how they work. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Magnificent mag-nih-fih-sun-t Something that is amazing and big can be magnificent. Magnifying mag-nih-fai-ying Looking closer at something is making it bigger, hence, magnifying it. Magnetic mag-net-ik Two objects can have an attraction that draws them together, being magnetic. Magnanimous mag-nan-ih-m-uss Somebody who shows great kindness to an enemy can be magnanimous. The root is the Latin word, 'MAGNUS', meaning 'great'. "What are you doing in my laboratory?" said Serena's father. "We're just looking around," said Serena. "We promise that we won't touch anything." "That's all right, then," said Serena's father, leaving her and Jimmy to play together. "That was close," said Serena. "This looks really cool," said Jimmy. "What is it?" "That's my father's microscope," said Serena. "You can see really small things. Take a look." Jimmy saw cells on a leaf, bacteria on a slide, and really tiny mites and bugs. "They have really amazing patterns," he said. "Wait until you see what these can do," said Serena. "You think you can see small things? Well, wait until distant objects become closer! A pair of binoculars." "Wow," said Jimmy, and Serena laughed. "But you have to look through the other end," she said. "Otherwise the world is tiny!" "I can see the tiny patterns on the bird feathers," said Jimmy. "If she keeps still, then I can make out all the texture and colour." "They are a type of magnifier," said Serena. "Magnifier, huh?" said Jimmy. "Sounds ﻿magnif ﻿icent." At nighttime, Serena took Jimmy to her house roof. "Now, this is called a telescope," she said. "You use it to look at very far away objects." "I can see the moon closer!" said Jimmy. "It's full of holes. It looks like a burned pizza." Just then, a giant shooting star crossed the sky. "That's a meteor burning up," said Serena. Jimmy zoomed in even closer on the telescope. "It's so powerful," said Jimmy. "You can see very, very far," said Serena. "Even past our own solar system. I don't know how Dad made it possible." A cluster of planets filled the sky. "Zoom in on the moon and tell me what you see," said Serena. "Magnificent!" said Jimmy. "I can see two more planets beyond. One has a giant frisbee stuck around it. "That's Saturn," Serena laughed. "The other one is Mars, the reddish brown planet." "Now, this is for seeing small things, but not too small," said Serena, as they played in the sandpit. "It's a magnifying glass." "Magnificent," said Jimmy. "The lady bird looks gigantic. It now has big black spots. I can see its eyes. They look strange and pointy." "So we've seen many objects we use to look at things," said Serena. "We have the microscope, the binoculars, the telescope, and the magnifying glass. Can you think of any other thing with a 'mag' we can use?" Jimmy thought and shouted out, "Magnets!" Post-Reading Questions What four items did Serena introduce Jimmy to? Describe what Jimmy saw in outer space. Here is a list of things. For each object, state whether you would use a microscope, binoculars, a telescope or a magnifying glass to look at them: Bird feathers Spider legs Germs Cells The moon Asteroids An island in the distance Boats at sea Rocks found on a volcano. Fleas ﻿
author: Hello English

title: Good Lion, Bad Ostrich
text: Story Description Once per year, the leader of the animal village appoints two parents to swap their offspring. This time, Ostrich and Lioness must swap kids and look after them, for the council to make sure they are doing a good job. But things go wrong. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Inspection ﻿in-spec-shun ﻿There was a yearly inspection of the animal village. Neglect ﻿nig-lec-t ﻿Ostrich showed great neglect towards the lion cubs. Reluctantly ﻿rih-luc-tant-lee ﻿The lioness reluctantly accepted what the elephant had said. Offspring ﻿off-spr-ing ﻿The young of animals are called the offspring. The elephant, leader of the animal town, called in two animals. He ordered the ostrich and the lion to come forward. It was the yearly inspection of the town, and the elephant wanted to know how well they were taking care of their loved ones. "Ostrich, you will take care of the lion cubs, and Lioness, you will take care of the young ostriches," said the elephant. "The swap will last for two days. I want to see how well you both take care of someone else's offspring." Lioness was very angry with being told to give up her cubs for two days. She reluctantly accepted what the elephant had told her. As soon as Ostrich had the lion cubs, she ordered them to stay indoors and told them not to play. "This is a precious house," she said. "I don't want you to touch anything, do you understand? If you do, then I will beat you." The cubs were terrified of Ostrich. They sat perfectly still. Meanwhile, Lioness took Ostrich's three little ones home with her to look after. She looked back with concern on how her cubs were doing. "You don't have to stay indoors," she said to the little ostriches. "You can play outside in the yard and I'll watch over you." The ostriches enjoyed their outside freedom and fresh air. Ostrich was gone all day long, and she left the cubs a bowl of bones, as she thought that's what lion cubs would eat. The cubs were starving and tired, and they did not get any other food all day. They sat, upset and feeling dismal. The little ostriches enjoyed worms on a bed of grass. Lioness had hunted them. They were delicious and filling. They thoroughly enjoyed their stay with the Lioness, who kept watch on them from a distance. The Lioness heard how Ostrich had treated her cubs, because the monkeys had been spying on Ostrich, suspicious of her behaviour. Lioness called Ostrich over to her house and she waited for her to turn up. Seething with anger and fuming with frustration, Lioness shouted at Ostrich. "How dare you treat my cubs this way! You starved them! You kept them indoors! They are supposed to be outside, and you have to feed them lots of food. I treated your offspring with care and love. You neglected mine!" "Go ahead and tell them how you were treated," said Lioness to the little ostriches. "We were well fed and kept outside all day," they said. "We had a lot of fun with Lioness. She is so protective and caring. Can we stay with her longer? Please?" "There, there," said Lioness. "You three have been wonderful." "I have to clear my name," said Ostrich. "But those animals on the council are hard to convince, and I don't think I can compete with Lioness." At the end of the swap, the council and animals gathered for a meeting. Lioness told in great detail how Ostrich had neglected her cubs. Ostrich tried to fight back by lying about Lioness, saying she behaved in the same way, but the monkeys gave evidence. The council was appalled at Ostrich's behaviour. "How can this happen to me?" said Ostrich. "I'll get that Lioness back in any way that I can! She'll be sorry." With Ostrich's reputation lost, she had to win back the trust of the village and care for her offspring properly. She gave up her attempt at getting revenge on Lioness, and eventually, Lioness forgave Ostrich for her actions. Ostrich admitted that she neglected the cubs and her own offspring because of her deep insecurities. Lioness sympathised and helped Ostrich to become a much stronger, better and more loving animal. Post-Reading Questions How did Ostrich neglect the lion cubs? How did Lioness treat the little ostriches? Which animal became aware of Ostrich's bad behaviour towards the cubs? What did Ostrich try to do at the council meeting? Find words to describe both Ostrich and Lioness's behaviour during the swap. What does the story tell us about truth and lies, and how to care for others?
author: Hello English

title: All Aboard the Bus
text: Story Description A young boy called Tad leaves his hometown on an overnight bus, heading for the capital city to see his grandparents. A lot of things happen on his curious and bizarre journey. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Enthusiastic ﻿in-thew-zee-ast-ic ﻿Tad was very enthusiastic about going on a journey. Plantations ﻿plan-tay-shuns ﻿The town was surrounded by fruit plantations. Reminded ﻿rim-eye-n-did ﻿The smells were strange and they reminded Tad of something. Bustle ﻿bus-ul ﻿The big capital city was full of activity and bustle. Tad arrived at the bus station, ready to take the overnight express to the capital. "Why do they call it the express if it takes all night to get there?" he wondered. "I wonder how long a normal bus would take." Passengers and traders arrived with their bags and produce. The bus was getting crammed with people. They still had to take bananas, watermelons and cases aboard. With room running out, they started strapping cases to the roof. A young man started helping people find a place on the bus. He was really enthusiastic. "Why do people carry their bags on their heads?" Tad asked a man. "Because people get their pockets picked, not their brains," said the man. Everyone rushed on to the bus. A woman held a baby, and a big guy took up nearly two seats. Someone sat in the wrong seat and had to get up and change. "I wonder how the bus will move with all this weight?" said Tad. Tad looked out of the window as they left the bus station. He waved goodbye to the people of his town for a visit to his grandparent's house. "I wonder what kinds of things I'll see on the way," he said, as the bus went on a dusty road by palm trees, plantations and mansions. The man sitting next to Tad felt uncomfortable sitting next to a large lady waving a fan in her face. "She's enormous," the man said to Tad. "She's even sitting on my seat." "Maybe you should sit on her knee," said Tad. "What?" said the man. "If I do that, she'll hit me with her book." Later, Tad and the man watched some sellers board the bus at a country stop. They carried biscuits and sweet things, and their prices were very high. Tad ignored them as they went around the bus. Suddenly, the young man who had been helping people get on the bus, got up and started shouting. "Someone has stolen my bag!" he yelled. "Sit down!" said the bus driver. "Not until someone admits to stealing my bag!" The young man inspected under his seat, and there was his bag, just where he had left it. He apologised to everyone and sank low, hiding his face. The day turned into night and Tad slept. It was very hot and uncomfortable inside the bus, but thankfully some people had gotten off at the previous stop, allowing more air to circulate. The bus smelled of armpits and bad breath. Tad tried to ignore it, but the armpit smell reminded him of fried onions. The very next morning, the bus stopped and some traders boarded. The people looked different and spoke in a weird way, and this amused Tad. They sounded clumsy and didn't say their words properly. Also, they had more life and energy in them. Now Tad knew he wasn't too far from his grandparents. Tad saw the capital city from his window. There was chaos, energy, hustle and bustle everywhere. There were markets, restaurants, stalls, diners, bars, carts, horses, buses and cars. It was loud, it was noisy, it was smelly, and Tad loved the change of atmosphere. Tad fell asleep and someone woke him up. "Hey, kid. You've arrived," said an older man. "You'd better get off before the other people get on." Tad grabbed his bag and got off the bus. People boarded the bus when he got off, and he waited at the new bus station. Then a little later, he saw his grandparents waiting to collect him. "How was the journey, Tad?" they said. "It was...interesting..." Tad replied. Post-Reading Questions ﻿ Who was Tad going to see in the capital city? Apart from passengers, who else boarded the bus? Why did the young man feel embarrassed after asking what happened to his bag? Why did Tad wonder if the bus would be able to move? Who sat next to the man, and why did he feel uncomfortable? What kind of journey would you go on? How would you travel?
author: Hello English

title: My Little Porcupine
text: Story Description A girl has a little porcupine as her best friend, who takes her to magical lands, makes the world turn upside down, and serves as her inspiration for drawing. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Porcupine poor-kew-p-eye-n The girl had a little pet porcupine, and it was her best friend. Porridge Poh-rij The girl and the porcupine saw something that looked like porridge. Invoke in-v-oh-k The porcupine was so good at telling stories, he invoked feelings in people. Convince con-vin-ss The porcupine could convince others so well. My little porcupine always accompanies me. He is so cute. He is adorable. I cannot let him out of my sight, because he gets into trouble if he goes too far. I give him little high fives when I do my homework. He is always there when I am glum. His bright multicoloured spikes make me laugh and raise me up. He always wears a straight face to stare at my sadness. Sometimes we go to this strange world where everything looks like porridge. We step in these holes and we sink. Inside it's really warm, but we can't see what's there. I think it's oats and milk. I sometimes bring my little porcupine to school, but I hide him from the teacher, otherwise he'll be confiscated, or sent to some zoo. He tells stories of adventure, woe, happiness and strife to my friends. They get embarrassed or cry because he is so good at invoking feelings in others. When I'm alone, my little porcupine will suddenly pounce on my head and sit there, staring down at me. When I try to reach him, he bounces away. We both have our strange habits. I like to sit watching a tooth in my hand that fell out. Ouch, it hurts! He likes to sit watching the root end of a carrot. He is convinced that he can see it grow. I ask my little porcupine for a favour. I say that, since my tooth fell out, I'm going to look weird until another one grows back. So, can we go to a magical land for a while? And he springs into action, making rainbow and star magic appear from his multicoloured hair. I drop my books, papers and pen, because I'm so shocked by what he can create. We're carried along on a magical water wave with a two-eyed umbrella to protect us from the rain. This way, we can't escape, and we have to spend more time together. My little porcupine is so crazy that he can reverse the world and make it appear upside down. It hurts after a while, though, because all the blood rushes to my head. My little porcupine is my best friend - the greatest friend and companion of all - and he is my inspiration to write. He brings the colour to my world. Oh, look. I have another tooth now! Slow motion high-five! Post-Reading Questions ﻿What two special abilities did the little porcupine have? When the little porcupine was around other people, what was he good at doing? What did the girl and the little porcupine sit inside when they went on an adventure? When the girl plays with her tooth, what does the little porcupine watch? What does the little porcupine do when the girl is alone or not looking? Describe what your perfect little animal would look like.
author: Hello English

title: Stop Crying, Please
text: Story Description A baby is very unhappy, but he is too young to speak and say why. He keeps on crying, and the family guesses what to do to get him to stop. Meanwhile, outside, a boy is playing an annoying trumpet. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Perplexed ﻿pur-plex-d ﻿The village was confused and perplexed as to why Liam kept playing. Communicate ﻿com-ew-nik-ay-t ﻿Alan could not communicate with words, so he cried to get their attention. Fanfare ﻿fan-fair ﻿Liam played a horrible sounding fanfare in the street. Scooped ﻿sc-oo-p-d ﻿The man scooped up water with his hands and put it in the trumpet. "What's wrong with Alan?" said Bill, as he came through the door flying his handmade aeroplane. "Why is he crying so loudly?" "I think he's hungry," said mother. "You can help me feed him." From outside came the noise of a trumpet. After feeding Alan, he was still crying, so his mother gave him some affection, and Bill played with one of his toys and made faces at him. But Alan kept on crying. He was very distressed. The trumpet noise got louder. Even though Alan couldn't talk, he tried his best to communicate. What was really upsetting him was the sound of the annoying trumpet coming from outside. But Alan could not express his distaste in any other way except by crying. Bill and his mother tried everything to calm Alan down, but nothing worked. Outside, Liam was playing his trumpet. He got all the kids to listen to his new song. Everyone was perplexed and confused. They expected him to produce a good sound. Instead, the trumpet was deafening and sounded like someone stepping on a whoopee cushion. "Can you hear that, Mum?" said Bill, as Alan reached out for the trumpet to stop. "I think he is bothered by the noise outside." Liam kept walking through the streets playing a rubbish fanfare on his trumpet. It was painful to listen to, and the villagers told him to be quiet. Nonetheless, Liam ignored them and he kept playing by himself. A coconut picker saw Liam's trumpet left by his bike. He scooped up some sea water and filled the end of the trumpet as a prank. He pretended nothing had happened, and he waited in a tree to watch. Liam returned, picked up his trumpet and tried to play. But as he played, he blew out water. The man in the tree laughed. Suddenly the trumpet sound stopped, and Alan stopped crying. "There, there," said Bill. "It was that annoying trumpet that was making you upset. I wonder what happened to it?" As Liam was walking by the shore, he slipped and accidentally threw the trumpet into the water. The village was so happy and relieved that it had fallen to the bottom of the sea. Even the dog couldn't retrieve the trumpet, despite diving in. "It looks like that's the end of my terrible playing," said Liam. Post-Reading Questions ﻿What was causing Alan to cry? How did Bill and his mother try to stop Alan from being upset? Despite the village's protests, what did Liam continue to do? Describe the prank that the man played on Liam. What did Liam accidentally do to the trumpet? Name a musical instrument that you find annoying. What instrument do you prefer?
author: Hello English

title: Baani and her Balloon
text: Baani is all SMILES! Baani is all GIGGLES, As her new Balloon BOBS and WRIGGLES… Up and Down it GOES, It bounces off the wall, It tickles her teeny weenie NOSE. Naughty Balloon Skips and DANCES, Clapping and Jumping... Along with it Miss Baani PRANCES! That night, right next to her snuggles Balloon in BED, She Smiles as it winks at her, Oh So bright and lovely in RED! Soon Baani and her Balloon, Are soaring off to meet Mr MOON. Merrily across Dreamland they ZOOM … They Soar HIGH AND HIGH, Baani bounces the tiny clouds and tickles the twinkling stars, as they whiz across the SKY! Oh what DELIGHT, Oh what a Sparkling SIGHT! Nightly Night, SLEEP TIGHT…It’s time to wish you GOODNIGHT!

title: Riding On Raindrops
text: Story Description A group of children stand at a shore, when suddenly a storm carries them through the sea and underground, where they ride on magical raindrops which take them to another place filled with life. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Tropical ﻿troh-pic-ul ﻿The children stood in the tropical weather. Crevices ﻿c-rev-iss-is ﻿The cave opened up and revealed tiny crevices. Spectacular ﻿spec-tac-you-lur ﻿The view from the sky was spectacular. Extraordinary ﻿ex-tr-oar-din-air-y ﻿ ﻿The children saw extraordinary things that they never imagined could exist. The children gathered at the shore. There was a magical tropical storm coming. That could only mean one thing - an adventure awaited them. As soon as they stepped into the sea, the tide carried them through a vast cave network. They swam with the water, guided by the flow, through crevices and dark, hidden areas. They tumbled out to sea, and suddenly, crystal-like rain drops made them fly away. They left the sea and soared into the sky. They felt themselves shrinking really small, and the raindrops became gigantic! They were big enough to sit on the raindrops, which felt like melting ice, and it was difficult to stay on with all of the sliding around. The raindrops took them on a journey past lava flows and volcanoes, through hot, musky and dry atmospheres. The children suddenly expanded and fell off their raindrops, landing on cool, solid ground in a place with colour and life. There were trees and flowers everywhere. The children gathered and talked about their flying experience, and one of the girls mentioned the amazing monkey she had seen. The others remembered seeing it to, past the volcanoes and by the forests. The children found a device planted in the ground. It was a pair of viewing glasses, but these were extraordinary. The children had never seen anything like them before. Looking through it, they saw invisible animals. There was an orangutang and its offspring sitting and watching the visitors. They were so hairy, friendly and colourful! Another child saw a spiky looking bird by some leaves. It had a long, sharp beak and feet with three claws. One of the children saw a tiger hopping through the sky, watching over them. It was big and fearsome. It was larger than any of the other animals. Finally, they saw the biggest of all the animals appear in the sky, in a floating ocean. It was a huge whale with a gigantic horn for a nose. It glanced down at them and smiled. The children were in awe. It was spectacular. The raindrops returned and the children shrank. This time the journey was faster. They sped along through the sky, getting battered by the wind. They didn't know where they would be taken. The raindrops stopped in the clouds, and the children played with them. They could mould and scoop them together, forming shapes. The clouds were cold and wet to the touch. Some of the children threw the clouds at each other. Very soon, the children fell from the sky and were taken over muddy soil, where friendly worms reached out to greet them. The children touched them as they went by, when they suddenly grew to their original forms, and the raindrops left them back at the beach. The children gathered together and remembered what happened, so they could tell their story to their friends. Post-Reading Questions ﻿After getting carried away by the sea, where do the children go? What happens to the children so that they can ride the magical raindrops? What do the children see through the magical viewers? What is the largest of all the animals? What can the children make with the clouds? What creatures do the children find buried in the soil? If you could go on a magical adventure, where would it be?
author: Hello English

title: It's Good To Have A Skill
text: Story Description Tom and Tammy inquire about how to fix every day things. Their curiosity leads to more discoveries, and eventually to the possibility of getting paid to fix all kinds of things for customers. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Repairman ﻿re-pair-man ﻿Someone who fixes things is a repairman. Electricity ﻿ill-ec-tris-ih-tee Fixing a plug requires knowledge of electricity. Puncture ﻿punc-ch-ur ﻿Very soon, he could fix his own bike tyre puncture. Reassembling ﻿ree-a-sem-bl-ing ﻿ ﻿The iron required reassembling to be put back together. Tom and Tammy were playing indoors one day, when they accidentally knocked over Aunt Maria's iron. It fell to pieces and they didn't know how to fix it back together. "What are we going to do?" said Tammy. "I don't know how to fix it," said Tom. "Now we're in trouble." They found Aunt Maria at work in the market, and she took the iron apart, inspecting the interior components. "You only broke one of the connections," she said. "Nothing to worry about, see? I've fixed the connection." "Oh, that looked easy," said Tammy. "Maybe if we learn to fix things ourselves, then we can be more independent," said Tom. "We might make some money from doing repairs." "That's a great idea," said Tammy. "Right now, we can't do much." Just then, Tammy's bike suffered a puncture. They found Jim the bicycle repairman, who took out the inner tube and found the puncture. He covered it with tape and replaced the inner tube on Tammy's bike, pumping it back up again. "Good as new," he said. "Can you show us how to do that again?" said Tom. "It's easy enough to fix a puncture," said Tom. "But my shirt is torn. I wish I knew how to sew." "Why don't we learn together?" said Tammy. "I know a little bit about sewing." Tom and Tammy worked together to fix a small scale model of the world. It took a long time, but it wasn't tiring. In fact, Tom and Tammy shared a lot of jokes and stories while they were busy. Very soon, the globe was fixed once all the sewing was done. "It's all in the handy work," said an old tailor, after Tammy still couldn't sew his shirt. "Can you show me how to do that?" he said. "I want to know so next time I can give it a try." Tom and Tammy went to the spare parts store, where the shop owner had all sorts of gadgets and fixings. He had televisions, radios, photographs, shoes and all kinds of items that he was putting back together. They spent some time with him, watching how he worked. "I've figured it out," said Tammy. "Let's take apart the iron." "Again?" said Tom, feeling concerned. "Aunt Maria will get angry." "Don't worry, Tom. We can both work with one another at putting the iron back together. We have to learn, don't we?" After reassembling the iron, Tom was able to repair his own tyre punctures, and make minor repairs around the house. He felt like he had progressed. Tom watched closely as he learned about electricity, changing fuses, using spanners and wrenches, seeing the uses of nuts, screws and bolts in action. He picked up his handy work skills very quickly after seeing the shop owner doing his daily work. A couple of weeks later, Tom and Tammy arrived at the market. There were handy stalls everywhere. People were queueing to have their things fixed. "What are we doing here?" said Tom. "We watch and we learn," said Tammy. "Then very soon, when we have the same skills, we can have our own stall." And so it was that Tom and Tammy both volunteered at the market, gaining the necessary skills to provide themselves with work. Tom fixed the tiny components of clocks and watches, and Tammy knitted rugs and patchwork. They gave themselves the skills necessary to earn a living, and very soon, they opened a shop and they ran the business together. Post-Reading Questions ﻿What is the first thing that Aunt Marie showed Tom and Tammy how to fix? What is the first thing that Tom fixed by himself? Who did Tom and Tammy watch while he was working? What did Tom and Tammy fix together? Eventually, because of their new skills, what were Tom and Tammy able to do? If you could fix something, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: Going to the Park
text: Story Description A girl finishes school when a stray dog shows up at her door. She takes it to the park with her grandmother, and they play games together. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Crawling cr-or-ling The insects were crawling along the tree trunk. Varieties var-eye-et-ees There were many varieties of flowers in the park. Distracted dis-trac-tid The dog was distracted by a rabbit. Slobbering sl-ob-ur-ing The dog was so out of breath, it was slobbering. "Hello," said Jeanie, opening her front door to find a stray dog standing outside. "You must have followed me home from school." "Woof," said the dog. "You want me to come out and play. I know! Let's go to the park. Just a moment." Jeanie asked her grandmother to take her to the park, and the dog followed them. Jeanie took her grandmother's hand and they walked by the grass and the trees until they found a bench. "I'm going to have a look at the trees," said Jeanie. "Will you be all right if I leave you for a moment?" "I'll be absolutely fine, dear," said grandmother. "You run along and have fun." Jeanie saw the insects crawling along the tree branches. They were hiding away inside the cracks of the trunk. Jeanie found many varieties of bugs making their homes inside the tree. Next, Jeanie played fetch with the dog, throwing the ball for him, and waiting for him to come back with it. One time, the dog didn't return. He had been distracted by a rabbit running into a bush, and he tried to catch it. Jeanie ran to the woods and picked some pretty colourful flowers to bring for her grandmother. Then she went looking for the dog. He had disappeared. "There you are!" said Jeanie, finding the dog hiding next to a tree. The dog barked and hid again, until Jeanie found him hiding in some bushes. "You smell so bad," she said to the dog. "You've been rolling in the mud, hiding by the trees, sneaking into the bushes and slobbering everywhere. You need a bath." "Thank you for the flowers," said grandmother. "Have you had a good time?" "I had a great time, grandmother," said Jeanie. "But I haven't finished playing yet." "Oh, why not?" "Because someone needs a bath." "You?" said grandmother. "No, the dog! I don't smell bad!" "You do smell bad," said the dog, annoyed at being given a bath. Post-Reading Questions ﻿What did Jeanie find outside her front door? Who did Jeanie take with her to the park? What did Jeanie see crawling on the tree trunk? How did the dog get distracted while playing with Jeanie? What did Jeanie give to the dog? What games would you play in the park?
author: Hello English

title: Ajji Can Drive
text: "What?! What am I seeing?! Can it really be? I rushed forward to where Ajji was. "Ajji?" I asked, "are you really going to drive today?" "I thought of just trying..." Ajji replied. You see, it has been a month since Ajji got her license, but she has been too scared to drive in the city traffic! Her car has just been lying in the garage till now, with nothing to do. "Oh, Samanvi, I'm so scared!" Ajji said. "Don't be scared, Ajji. I'll come with you!" I said and got in the car. "Just remember the rules: 1. Be alert and look all ways before moving. 2. Do not be in a hurry, but do not stop suddenly in the middle of the road. 3. Stay calm." Turned out, Ajji was worried for nothing. She was an absolute natural at driving! We cruised past the apartment buildings in our area and merged with the city traffic. We even ran into Girish Anna, my school auto driver. "Great going, Ajji!" he said. We stopped and ate ice candies. Slurrrpp! Now, we're back home. Today, Ajji's car finally got out of the house! "High Five, Ajji! You were awesome!" Vrrrrroooooom Vrrrrrrrooom!!!!!

title: Making Friends with Snakes (But from a Distance)
text: Come on, Anna. Get her out! Here comes Bhuvaneshwar’s yorker. And here comes Mitali’s straight drive! I’ll get it... Snaaaaake! Thangachi, get me your bat! Where is it? Right next to our ball. ANNA, STOP! Before you hit us, please listen to our story. I’m Naagin, a venomous Spectacled Cobra... and I’m Dhaman, a non-venomous Ratsnake... and we’re here to make friends with you. BUT from a distance. You know, snakes are just like people. Yeah. In so many ways. We’re beautiful. We’re colourful. We love to dress up. (Indian Rock Python) (Malabar Pit Viper) ﻿(Ornate Flying Snake) Just like some people prefer to sit alone with a book, we like to be left alone too. Yeah. Dhaman and I don’t really enjoy each other’s company. We’ve just come together for this book. Sigh. The things we do for you! But there are some differences. And that’s what makes us snakes! Unlike most people, we’re unable to hear sounds. We can’t digest ten idlis... or drink milk. UGH! But we LOVE our food! But our sharp tongues and the Jacobson’s organ on the roof of our mouths give us a keen sense of smell. Checkered Keelbacks love fish and frogs. Shieldtails love earthworms. Vinesnakes and King Cobras eat other snakes. SLURRRRPPP! Most of us love rats and mice. We eat all the pests that destroy your crops. Remember, snakes down here on the ground are very frightened of humans, even children, towering over them. The only time we bite is in defence. Most snakes found in India are non-venomous and harmless to people. Like ME! Yeah, but Dhaman can inflict a really stinky odour. Hey, that’s just my defence mechanism! But there are four common venomous snake species— including YOU! Right. They’re responsible for 50,000 human deaths from snakebites in India every year. Most bites are accidents that can be easily avoided, if you get to know us better. So let’s meet the Big Four venomous snakes! Sorry, I’m using four grass strands because I don’t have fingers. THE BIG FOUR 1. Spectacled Cobra I can easily be identified by my hood and characteristic markings. I am a great swimmer and love to hang out around water. My appetite for rats brings me to fields, houses, messy kitchens and granaries. When I’m threatened, my first response is NOT to bite. I do everything I can to warn you to stay away: raise my hood, hiss, and even make false strikes with my mouth closed. It’s only when none of this works or if someone steps on me, grabs me or injures me, that I am forced to bite. My venom can prove lethal. Raised hood: stay away. False strike (with the mouth closed): you need to back off right now. Actual strike: you need an ambulance! 2. Saw-scaled Viper Most people think I’m harmless because I’m tiny. Yep. Really tiny. But my venom is very potent and I can strike with lighting speed! I hang out in dry, open areas. I am difficult to spot because of my camouflage. So if you’re playing in these fields, you need to be watchful for me. But don’t you worry; I’m not that difficult to identify! You can tell I'm a Saw-scaled Viper by the zigzag patterns on my back. I too warn before I bite. I coil up like a jalebi and hiss, with my scales rubbing against each other making a saw-like sound. (Yes, that’s where I get my name!) Hissss: this means “This isn’t a jalebi you would want to touch” Strike: Told you so! 3. Common Krait Namaste! I’m among the most docile of snakes... and yet lethal! That’s because my venom is the most potent of any Indian snake! You can identify me by the thin white bands on my black hide. Other non-venomous species like this Wolf Snake may resemble me, but best to keep away from us ALL. Wow. You’re the worst alarm clock ever invented, Krait! In my search for other snakes, rodents and lizards to eat, I crawl close to people sleeping outdoors without a mosquito net or on the floor. When they move or roll over in their sleep, I bite in self-defence. 4. Russell’s Viper I’m the grumpiest of the big four. I like my personal space. A lot. If disturbed, I can get REALLY cranky! I’m often mistaken for non-venomous Boas and Pythons, and handled, and that’s a fatal mistake. Remember, if you see a chain-like pattern of markings on a snake’s back, it’s me. This is an Indian Rock Python. Keep away. This is a Common Sand Boa. Keep away. This is me. Turn around and go home. I sit hidden in bushes, camouflaged in leaf litter, waiting for my prey to come to me. This can be dangerous for people walking in the dark without a torch. Avoiding this guy should be easy, right? You kids don’t like to hang around grumpy old uncles anyway! You snakes aren’t as bad as we thought! You seem like a fun bunch, if we keep our distance... But how exactly do we keep a safe distance from snakes? Avoiding us is easy. You just need to take these simple precautions. 1. When working in open fields or playing in open areas, watch where you place your hands and feet. Probing with a long stick can easily detect our presence. 2. Always use a torch at night when you walk outdoors, even near your home. 3. If your regular path is littered with leaves, clear the litter with a rake. 4. Clean your homes, kitchens and storehouses regularly to keep them rat-free. 5. When sleeping outdoors or on the floor, create a physical barrier around you with the help of a well tucked-in mosquito net. Four rewards: no mosquito bites, no scorpion stings, no krait bites, and you get to snore away happily until morning! Rarely, snakebite accidents can happen despite taking the best precautions. You need to remember to take these steps. Do not take the victim to a tantrik or a snake charmer for treatment Do not suck the wound Do not cut the wound open Do not tie ligatures around the wound Do not burn the wound Do not apply herbal pastes over the wound Immobilise the affected limb Rush the victim to the nearest hospital that can deliver Anti-Snake Venom and emergency care I hope it never comes to that because I think you creatures are quite beautiful. And play an important role in nature and our lives! Aww, thank you! I’ll remember to help my mother clean the kitchen after every meal, so that rats don’t visit my house for scraps. I’ll remember to tell my parents to buy a torch immediately so that they return safely from the fields every evening. And I’ll remember to tell Uncle to use the mosquito net. He loves to sleep outdoors and wake the whole village up with his snoring! That’s the spirit, kids! While you’re at it, don’t forget to thank us for all the rats we eat, each time you burp after a bowl of curd rice! Hahahaha! Madras Crocodile Bank Have you ever been to the Madras Crocodile Bank? It’s a reptile zoo in Chennai, which works for the conservation of reptiles. Its project ‘Snake Conservation and Snakebite Mitigation’ teaches people about the importance of identifying which snakes are venomous, how to avoid them, and using antivenom serum. Get more information about snakebites and the Croc Bank at

title: Birdie Fight
text: "White Birdie, hurry! The Birdie Family is fighting again!" "It all started when Yellow Birdie said she wanted the auditorium to practice her dance for the show on Saturday..." "I said I needed the auditorium to practice the drums, and she came at me, like a wild bird!" "Then Blue Birdie tried to bully us and have the auditorium for himself to practice his song for the show... and now all the Birdies have taken sides and everyone's fighting! "It got very bad, pretty quick. Help us, White Birdie!" "Gather around, Birdies. It's time for a little talk. Now, all of you need the auditorium, but only one group can have it at a time. So, we know what the problem is. Fighting and arguing won't lead us anywhere. We all end up angry, hurt and tired. So, try and think of a solution instead. Every problem has a solution." "So, let's make a time table such that each group gets equal time to practice at the auditorium. We all get the auditorium, then. Fair?" "Remember, we don't get anything by fighting. What we want is to put on a good show on Saturday." "Thank you, White Birdie!"

title: WHO WILL TIE MY SHOELACES?
text: Roshan was excited. He was going to school. It was his first day. He wore his uniform, picked up his bag. His mother had filled his water bottle. He had taken his lunch box. His new socks and shoes were waiting for him. He managed to slip on his socks and into his shoes. But what about the laces? His mother was drying clothes. His father had left for work. His sister would not dirty her hands by touching his shoes. His grandmother could not bend and tie them. Roshan was getting angry. He tucked the laces inside his shoes and set off to school. Before the school assembly started, the teacher checked everyone’s uniform. “Why haven’t you tied the laces?” asked the teacher. Little Roshan, looked up, put his hands on his hips and asked, “My mother is busy, my father is away, my sister is of no use and granny is too old. Who will tie my shoe laces?” The teacher quietly bent down, knelt and tied Roshan’s shoe laces. He had a small smile on his face.
