title: In Search of a Friend
text: Once upon a time, there was an Owl named Hooter. Hooter didn't have any friends. So, Hooter decided to request the animals that live near its home to be his friends. Firstly, Hooter went to the peacock. "Hi" hooter said politely and asked, "Will you be my friend?". "Hi", replied the peacock proudly, "you don't have colourful feathers like me. So, I cannot be your friend". Then Hooter met many other birds. "You are too big", t he young chicken said. "Your eyes are too big!" exclaimed the Myna. "Your legs are too small", told the stork. Hooter was very sad. Hooter approached a dog and asked, "Will you be my friend?" "You have wings", the dog barked and replied, "And you don't have four legs. Thus, you cannot be my friend". The disappointed Hooter returned to his home. It was night fall. Suddenly, Hooter heard a call. Hooter flew in the direction of that call. Hooter found that it was an owl in another tree that has sounded off that call. "Who are you?", asked Hooter, "I haven't seen you earlier around here." "I'm Hootey", said that owl sadly, "I have been disoriented due to a storm and could not find my way back to my home." Hooter wanted to help Hootey. "Why don't you stay with me", asked Hooter, "We can stay together and there is enough space." "Thanks for your help", Hootey exclaimed happily, "You are helping me like a friend. Shall we be friends?" "Definitely", said Hooter delightedly, "We can be friends." Hooter and Hootey became very thick friends and lived happily ever after.

title: The Camel's Humps
text: Story Description A camel leaves his home and goes on a long journey to find the remaining members of his family. On the way, he crosses many landscapes, and some animals use his humps as a place to stay. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Habitat ﻿ha-bih-tat ﻿The camels were searching for a new habitat. Blistering ﻿bl-iss-tur-ing ﻿The wind was blistering against the camel's skin. Jabbing ﻿jab-ing ﻿The camel felt a jabbing sensation on his hump. Stranded ﻿str-an-did ﻿The camel didn't want to be stranded and stuck in the desert. There was a family of camels crossing the desert. The camels were heading to a new habitat with fresh water and enough food to last them a long time. Unfortunately, during the journey, some camels had been left behind. Lofty, the lookout, decided to go back and find them, and catch up with the group later. Lofty began his journey by swimming through the sea. A bunch of fish watched as Lofty went past. They had never seen a camel before. To them, he looked weird and bizarre. He had these strange bumps on his back. Very soon, Lofty reached the far shore where he found windy ground. Lofty found his way through open fields and forests, following the tracks that the camels had made. Lofty came to a river where he drank some water to quench his thirst. As he was busy, he didn't see a couple of frogs making a shelter on one of his humps. They were too small for him to notice. Suddenly, one of the frogs tried jabbing a leaf into his hump to create some shade. Lofty stuck his head up. "Agh, it's a sea monster!" the frogs cried, taking off with their leaf. Lofty gave the frogs a tough look before he continued on his way. Next came a blistering dust bowl with dry land. The heat was unbearable. Lofty hid in the sand to protect himself and to stay cool. As he buried himself, he didn't notice two tortoises looking for some hills to rest on. The tortoises climbed on Lofty's humps and went to sleep. Lofty felt something warm and strange on his hump. Lifting his head, he tipped the tortoises off, giving them a stern look. Lofty found the snowy cold lands, and hid under the snow to shelter from a storm. During the snow drifts, two rats had made a home on his hump. Lofty lifted his head and the rats were terrified when they saw his face. They escaped and ran away as fast as they could. Lofty saw two humps in the distance. He wondered if they were his missing family members. He went to take a closer look. They were just hills surrounded by clouds. Disappointed, Lofty rested in the snowy fields by the trees, coated in snow. His humps were so warm that the snow melted around the tops. Lofty was giving up hope. He had gone so far, yet there was no sign of the other camels. If he went any further, he would also lose his family heading in the other direction. He felt stranded and lost, and one cold night, he wondered what to do. He didn't give up hope. The very next day, Lofty reached some flat hills, and suddenly he saw a cluster of four camels all sleeping. They were relieved to see Lofty, and they all rested as a group. Very soon, Lofty guided them back to the front, many hundreds of kilometres away, where the entire family was waiting for them, happy and relieved that they were alive and well. Post-Reading Questions Why did Lofty leave and walk all the way back? What was the first obstacle that Lofty crossed? Which kind of creatures tried to use Lofty's humps as a home? Why did Lofty start to give up hope of finding his family members? Where did Lofty eventually find them? Describe Lofty's behaviour during the story.
author: Hello English

title: How Zebra got his stripes
text: Long, long ago, when Zebra's skin was still white, a terrible drought occurred. For months not a single drop of rain fell. The grass turned dull, the trees became bare and the rivers dried up one by one. Springbok, Warthog and Zebra had to walk very far each day in search of water. One morning when Springbok arrived at the only watering hole, he heard an angry voice say, “Make way! Scoot! Or heads will roll! This is Baboon's watering hole!” Springbok's eyes widened. Baboon was sitting on a rock next to the watering hole, grilling bananas over his open fire. “But I'm so thirsty, my tongue feels like biltong,” Springbok said. “Where will I find water?” Baboon growled. “Not my problem! Scoot! Or heads will roll! This is Baboon's watering hole.” Springbok saw Baboon's long teeth and was scared. He turned around and trotted away. After a while Warthog came trotting along. But as soon as he lowered his head to take a sip of water, he heard an angry voice, “Make way!Scoot! Or heads will roll! This is Baboon's watering hole!” Surprised, Warthog turned around. He saw Baboon sitting on the rock next to the watering hole grilling his bananas. “But I'm so thirsty, it feels as if I've eaten dust,” Warthog said. "Where will I find water?" Baboon growled. “Not my problem! Scoot! Or heads will roll! This is Baboon's watering hole.” Warthog bristled at first, but when he saw Baboon's long teeth, he got scared. He turned around and trotted away, tail in the air. After a while Zebra turned up at the watering hole. Before he could take a sip of water he heard an angry voice. “Make way! Scoot! Or heads will roll! This is Baboon's watering hole!” Zebra snorted and looked up. He saw Baboon sitting on the rock grilling his bananas. “But I'm so thirsty, it feels as if my tongue slept outside my mouth last night,” Zebra said. “Where will I find water?” “Not my problem! Scoot! Or heads will roll!This is Baboon's watering hole.” Baboon showed his long teeth. Zebra wasn't scared. With clip-clopping hooves he stormed at baboon. He was so angry that he ran right through Baboon's burning fire. Sparks and smoke and bananas were flying. Baboon tried to escape, but it was too late. Zebra kicked him so hard that he flew through the air. “Ouch!” Baboon yelled. His butt landed on a sun baked rock. The rock was so hot that it burned off Baboon's hair. From that day Baboon has never had hair on his butt. And Zebra's skin has never been lilywhite again. Baboon's fire burned stripes onto his skin. It was now safe for the animals to drink at the watering hole. And each morning, as they came to drink water, Springbok, Warthog and Zebra sang, “Come wet your throat here while you stroll, this is everybody's watering hole!
author: Jaco Jacobs

title: Down the Slope
text: Story Description A group of girls go on vacation to a skiing and snowboarding resort. While playing, two of the girls go on a walk and fall over, getting hidden in the snow. The other girls must find and rescue them, and take them back to the resort. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Toboggan tuh-bog-un ﻿The girls sat on the toboggan and went down the slope. Aided ey-did ﻿The girls were aided by their friends, who rescued them. Snowboarding ss-no-boar-ding ﻿ ﻿The most popular activity was snowboarding, because it was really cool. Skiing ﻿sk-ee-ing ﻿The activity of skiing takes a lot of practice and balance to get right. Lara, Sofia, Marie and Jane were a group of friends on vacation in Norway with their school. They had gone skiing and snowboarding while staying at a mountain top resort. They took walks, rolled around, slid down the slopes and played on the toboggans. The outside temperature was very cold - it was about minus ten degrees. One day, Sofia and Marie were out walking down the slopes, while their friends were chatting outside the resort, planning what activities they were going to do for the day. Suddenly, a massive slice of snow shifted and they slipped down the mountain. Intense strong winds blew them along the slope. They lost contact with each other and tumbled. Lara and Jane heard their cries for help. Lara tied a rope securely around a strong tree. Unfortunately, more friends got stuck in the slipping snow. Lara hauled her friends to safety at the top of the hill. The tree was sturdy enough and it took all of their weight. As one of the friends was being pulled up, they slipped, and they slid all the way back down the hill. Lara and Jane found Sofia and Marie covered in snow. They all walked very slowly, aided by the rope, until they got back to the resort. But then, as they were walking the final few paces, one of their friends slipped, sending them further down the hill. They had to crawl back to the resort. "How was your day, girls?" said their teacher. "Very cold," they said. "Do you have plans for tomorrow?" "I think we're going to stay in tomorrow," said Sofia, and the whole group agreed with her. Post-Reading Questions What happened to Sofia and Marie as they were walking down the slope? Who noticed that Sofia and Marie had fallen in the snow? What did Lara do with a rope and why? What happened when the group reached the resort? Their teacher asked them what they would do tomorrow. What did they agree to do? Where would you go on vacation?
author: Hello English

title: Clever brother
text: Once upon a time, there was a man who had three sons. The youngest son was the cleverest and his father liked him the most. Then the man realised that his two other sons were jealous. So when the father died, he left all his cattle to his two elder sons. He only left one ox for the youngest son. But the brothers were still jealous of him. One day they said, “We've got to slaughter your ox.” He was the youngest so he couldn't protest. He said, “If that must be so, there's nothing I can do. But please give me the hide.” When they slaughtered the ox, he took the hide. After drying it, he climbed a tree with it. As it got darker, a group of merchants came to sleep under the tree. In the middle of the night, the young man started beating the hide with a stick. When the stick hit the hide it sounded like thunder. The merchants thought that a storm was coming. They ran off leaving their goods behind. The young man picked up the goods and took them home to his brothers. They asked, “Where did you get all these things?” He said, “The price of hides is so expensive that I got all this for my one hide.” The brothers quickly slaughtered their cattle. They went to the market and called, “ Hides for sale! Hides for sale!” The people at the market said, “We don't want your hides!” They were very angry and said to their brother, “You fooled us, so as a punishment, we're going to burn your hut.” The smart brother said, “There's nothing I can do, but please give methe ashes.” They burnt his hut. He took the ashes in a bag and went away to a rich man's hut. The rich man gave him permission to sleep in his hut. When he was going to eat, he said to the rich man, “Look after this bag, it has got a lot of valuables.” In the morning he started shouting. The rich man went to ask him what was wrong. “Someone has taken all my valuables and replaced them with ashes!” moaned the young man. The rich man didn't want his reputation to be ruined. So he said, “I'll fill it up with anything you want.” He filled it with wheat, teff and all sorts of seeds. The brother went home and said, “Look, ashes have become very expensive. See what I managed to buy from selling those ashes.” The brothers went and burnt their huts as well. They took the ashes to the market and shouted, “Ashes for sale! Ashes for sale!” Everybody said, “How stupid you are, who'll buy ashes?” The brothers were very angry and decided to kill their younger brother. They tied him up and put him in a basket so that they could throw him over a cliff. While they were carrying the basket to the cliff, they met an old man. He said to them, “My cattle have run away, will you bring them back for me?” The brothers put down the basket and ran off. The young man called from inside the basket to the old man. He asked, “What's wrong with you?” The young man replied, “They want me to become a king but I don't want to be one.” The old man said, “If I get into the basket will I become king?” And the young man answered, “Yes.” The old man let the young man out of the basket and he got inside. After the brothers returned with the cattle, they picked up the basket and threw it over the cliff. The young brother took the old man's cattle back to his hut. His brothers were amazed that he was still alive, but all they said was, “Where did you get these cattle?” He said, “There are many cattle at the bottom of the cliffs. If you jump off the cliffs in baskets, you will find some too.” The older brothers got into baskets. The clever brother threw the baskets over the cliffs. He lived happily ever after.
author: Elizabeth Laird; Mulualem Daba

title: Ox and Donkey
text: A poor farmer had an old ox that didn't like to work. The ox didn't want to plough the farmer's field. He wanted to stay at home and eat grass, drink water and rest. The farmer had a donkey, too. The donkey and the ox were friends. At the end of the day, the ox and the donkey talked to each other. “I'm so tired,” the ox said. “I worked hard all day. The plough is big and heavy. The farmer never lets me rest.” The donkey thought, “The ox is lazy. He doesn't like to work.” He cried, “Do you think your plough is heavy? Believe me, my friend, it is light! I carried a sack of grain on my back today. It was heavier than your plough, I am sure.” The next day, the two animals met again. “I had a bad day today,” the ox said. “My master's field is far away, and it was full of stones. I worked hard all day. I didn't have any rest.” “You worked hard?” asked the donkey. “Today I travelled many kilometres to the market in the town. I'm sure I worked harder than you.” The next day, the ox came home late again. “Oh, my friend,” he said to the donkey. “Today was a very bad day for me.” But the donkey didn't want to listen to the ox any more. He said, “You're always tired. When the farmer comes, lie down and say, 'Moo! Moo!' He will think that you are ill. He will let you rest.” The ox liked the donkey's idea. “Thank you, dear donkey, that's a very good idea,” he said. The next morning, the ox lay down and closed his eyes. “Moo! Moo!” he said. The farmer looked at him. “My poor old ox is sick,” he said.“ But I must plough my field. Who will help me? Perhaps the donkey! He can pull the plough today.” The farmer tied the plough to the donkey, and began to hit him with his whip. “Go on! Faster! Pull!” he called out to the donkey. The donkey worked hard all day, and in the evening he was very tired. The donkey slowly walked home. The ox said, “Dear donkey, I had a lovely day today. I ate some grass, drank some water and I rested. I want to rest again tomorrow. Give me another idea.” The donkey thought, “His work is much worse than mine. I don't want to do it again tomorrow.” The donkey said, “Be careful. The farmer said 'My ox is always tired and now he is sick. If he is not better tomorrow, I will kill him, and we can eat the meat.'” The ox was very frightened. He cried, “Really? Did he say that? Then I will work tomorrow. I feel quite better now. I'm not tired at all!”
author: Elizabeth Laird; Melese Getahun Wolde

title: Are You the Woodpecker?
text: Killi and Killan were two parakeets who lived in a hole high up on a silk-cotton tree. One day, a storm came and blew down their tree. Killi and Killan cried birdy tears for their lost home. A passing crow heard the noise and asked why they were so sad. “Our tree is gone, we have no home,” they sobbed. “You need a bird who can peck wood to make a tree hole. Why don’t you ask the woodpecker to make you a new home?” said the crow. So Killi and Killan set off to find the woodpecker. Tiu Tiu. Killi and Killan heard a loud sound from the bushes below. “Are you the woodpecker? Can you make us a new tree hole?” they asked. “No, I’m the tailorbird. I stitch leaves together to make my nest.” Pleased-to-meet-you! Killi and Killan heard a fluty whistle in the trees below. “Are you the woodpecker? Can you make us a new tree hole?” they asked. “No, I’m the bulbul. I bring twigs to build a cup nest.” Shichweeee shichweee. Killi and Killan heard a screeching sound. “Are you the woodpecker? Can you make us a new tree hole?” they asked. “No, I’m the weaverbird. I weave grass together to make my hanging nest.” Ti-tee-too-wit? Killi and Killan looked down in the grass. “Are you the woodpecker and can you make us a new tree hole?” they asked. “No, I’m the lapwing. I make my nest on the ground.” “We’ll never have a home again” said Killi. “Don’t give up hope” said Killan. “Let’s try a little longer.” Toktok-toktok! Killi and Killan saw a bird hammering at a tree branch. “Are you the woodpecker? Can you make us a new tree hole?” they asked. “ Yes, I am, ” said the woodpecker, “ but I'm busy making my own nest. You'll have to ask someone else. ” The parakeets looked at each other in despair. Tuk..tuk..tuk! On a nearby tr ee was a round green bird. “I can help you,” she said. “Who are you?” sobbed Killi and Killan. “I’m the barbet,” said the bird. “I make my nest in trees by pecking out a nice round hole. I can make a new tree hole for you.” And so she did.
author: Suhel Quader

title: Eight-Legged Creatures
text: Story Description A mother teachers her son and daughter about spiders, including where they live, how they work and what they do during their lives. The children learn how spiders make webs and hunt for food, and how they are helpful towards people. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Paralysing pah-ra-lie-zing A spider's bite works by paralysing its prey, so it cannot move. Assessing a-seh-ss-ing The spider crawled along the leaf, assessing its surroundings. Tarantula tut-ran-chew-la One large variety of spider is called a tarantula. Eyesight eye-sigh-t Wolf spiders have incredible eyesight. "What are these?" said Nicky and Henry to their mother. "Eight-legged creatures," said mother. "Also known as spiders. They live in our house and they live outside." "I find them creepy," said Nicky. "I think they're cool," said Henry. "Don't touch it, Henry," said mother. "Why not?" said Henry. "It's assessing its area. It wants to build a web. If you disturb the spider, it will go elsewhere. Let it examine the leaves and find a place to set up a home." Nicky noticed several different spiders on the wall. "There are many varieties," said mother. "House spider, cross spider, wolf spider, and there are some really big ones too." "Not that big, I hope," said Nicky. "Wait until you see a tarantula," said Henry. "Look," said mother to Henry. "It's crawling up the tree towards its web." "It has a web?" said Henry. "Why?" "The spider spins a web to catch its prey - mostly flies. You can find webs in our house. Look at the corners of the ceiling. Spiders live indoors too." "Indoors?" said Nicky. "They had better not!" "They do you no harm," said mother. "Spiders are not interested in humans. They are interested in hunting. Look, there's a daddy long legs. It's a different variety." "It's so scary," said Nicky. "Look at its gigantic legs!" "They can't bite, so they don't have access to their venom. If they could, they would be extremely poisonous." The daddy long legs jumped and floated through the air. "Ugh, it's like a mosquito!" said Nicky. Henry looked under rocks for more spiders, while mother and Nicky examined the tree and the shrubs. Henry was a little afraid of the spiders, even though he pretended he wasn't. He had been scared after learning that they also lived in houses. He checked under his bed, and luckily, he didn't find any. "That's a relief," he said. "I can sleep well tonight." Nicky and Henry learned that wolf spiders have excellent eyesight. They found one and shone a torch light directly at it, and its eyes reflected, making a cool glow. "Be careful of that one," said mother. "It bites." Nicky walked away. The cross spider is an expert at weaving amazing webs. It waits in the centre for its prey to get stuck against the web. It moves in and bites the prey, paralysing it. When the prey cannot move or struggle anymore, the cross spider eats its prey. "I think this is my favourite one," said Henry. "It's a real hunter." "It's time for dinner," said mother. "That's enough of spider researching for the day. What would you like to eat?" "I have a web of ideas," said Henry. "Don't be so gross," said Nicky. "Who wants to eat flies?" said mother, joking, and both Henry and Nicky complained. Post-Reading Questions ﻿Name some places where you think spiders live. What kind of spider has excellent eyesight? Describe how a spider catches its prey. Are spiders harmful to humans? Name a variety of large spider. What is unique about the daddy long legs? ﻿What is your favourite kind of bug, and where does it live?
author: Hello English

title: The Hidden Jewel
text: This is the story of a young boy named Rehan Khan. He could understand everything the teacher said or taught. Kids at school were good to him, supported him in all of his work. He loved painting. However, Rehan was not always happy or attentive in class. His teacher observed this for sometime and then confronted him. He replied," Ma'am, I do not see any meaning of studying when you have to be sad when you grow up. We have to fight for food, a decent house and many more necessities." The teacher understood that he needed a lot of boost to his confidence. Starting then his teacher repeatedly reminded Rehan that he is an excellent person and needs to have confidence in himself. He was appreciated for all the small or big tasks he performed in class. This small act of the teacher meant a lot to Rehan. He started taking part in constructive acts in the class. He also initiated to help the teacher when needed. Rehan started to show tremendous improvements in almost all aspects of school. This cheered him up. He started reading and painting without thinking too much about the results. Teacher was really happy and she told Rehan," I am very proud of you Rehan, this is exactly what I wanted you to do. work without thinking about the result. Work on yourself because you want to see yourself a better person everyday. However, I want you to keep in mind that there will be sad moments ahead, but you have to be positive and move ahead." Rehan Smiled and thanked his teacher for her kind words. The teacher spoke to the whole class after Rehan. She told them to understand that we should focus more on our present and be positive about the future, as this would lead us to become happy individuals. Well, we do need happy individuals as we grow up, don't we?
author: Pooja Pandey

title: All About Beans
text: Story Description Jenny and her grandmother go to the fields to pick beans and vegetables for their dinner. Suddenly a happy bean appears and talks to Jenny. He reveals to her the secret world of underground beans, and their destiny. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Greenest gr-een-ist Jenny searched for the healthiest, greenest beans in the field. Nutrition new-tr-ish-un Jenny ate beans a lot for healthy nutrition. Benefits ben-uh-fits There are health benefits to eating beans, because they contain protein. Community com-yew-n-it-ee The entire bean community hoped that one day they would be chosen for dinner. Jenny and her grandmother walked by the hills outside of their farm. They were on a dusty road which led to vegetable and fruit plantations. It was a bright summer's day, and they both wore hats to keep themselves cool from the sun. "Remember to wear your hat, dear," said grandmother. "And do you remember what I taught you?" "Search for the greenest beans," said Jenny. "That's right. Come back to me when you have collected a whole bucket of them." Jenny walked through the giant plantation of beans and vegetables. She felt the leaves and the beans, inspecting them. Some were soft and long, and they were ready to be picked. Just then, something caught her eye. "Hello," said a little green object, and Jenny gasped. "You can talk?" said Jenny. "That's right. I'm a different green bean. In fact, there's a bunch of us who can speak. We're here to help you pick." The bean tickled Jenny's nose with a leaf, and she sneezed. "Where have you been all this time?" she said. "I come to this field three times per week." "Oh, we've always been beans," said the bean. "And we've always been here, in this field. We don't often come out from underground." "We keep little pet pigs, you see," said the bean. "They protect us from predators. The pigs are fun, too. They roll around, chase us and then fall asleep." Jenny held a little pig in her palm. "It's so cute," she said. "But I don't believe you live underground." "Quick, get under the sheet," said the bean. "What sheet?" said Jenny, as the bean lifted the soil with its hands. "I don't believe it." "It's all real," said the bean. "This is where we hide from the strong winds and rain." They crawled underground and found two seats. Jenny talked about how the beans could develop a world of their own. "Oh, no," said the bean. "We're not interested in that. We just get by and serve others. We like to help the people pick the best beans for their nutrition." Just then, a few more beans showed up, plus a couple of sprouts. "Welcome to the community," said the bean, and the others started playing musical instruments and singing. "We don't have a care in the world, see? This is what we do every day. We have fun." "I wish I could live like you," said Jenny. More beans arrived and started lighting lanterns, drawing pictures on the ground and eating food. They started to dance, and Jenny joined in. "We dance because we don't know if we'll be picked," said the bean. "We hope we get picked. That's what we want. We belong in a soup or a delicious dish." "And you don't mind that?" said Jenny. "Not at all," said the bean. "It's the greatest destiny for any plant, to be consumed for the benefits we give. Don't worry about us. We don't feel pain. We just change state inside your body, that's all. Then we go back into the ground, and grow out again. It's all a cycle." At home, Jenny and her grandmother prepared the beans that they had picked. "Well, I won't eat you," said Jenny. "But beans are scrumptious. How would you like to be my pet?" "It would be an honour," said the bean, as Jenny made bean soup and jelly. "But promise me one thing - that one day, you'll eat me. It's my dream." Jenny made her promise. The happy beans swam in a hot soup while grandmother prepared the rest in the sink. "It won't be long before dinner," she said. "Jenny, go and wash your hands and set the table." "Ok!" Jenny called out. The bean helped himself to some cake for desert, as Jenny finished the bean soup with delight. "How was your bean soup?" asked grandmother. "Very tasty, granny," said Jenny. "I can still feel the beans swimming around in my stomach! I think they're having a party in there!" Post-Reading Questions How did Jenny know which beans were ready to be picked? What suddenly spoke to Jenny in the field? What didn't Jenny believe about the beans? What did the community of beans start doing with Jenny? According to the bean, what is the biggest dream of all beans? If you could bring a vegetable to life, what would it be and why?
author: Hello English

title: Gemma the Designer
text: Story Description A girl writes to the local council about suggesting a new bus route leading to her village. She draws a map with great detail, and with the support of her family, she delivers it, hoping that she will get a response. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Recognised re-cug-nize-d Gemma was recognised as the person who designed the route. Designer dih-zai-nur A designer is somebody who creates and plans something in detail. Route r-oo-t The new bus route would go past the lake. Council cow-n-sul Gemma sent her bus route plan to the local council. "What's Gemma doing?" said her father, as she sketched an outline of the garden on a piece of paper. "She's drawing a map of the area," said her mother. "What on earth for?" "The town wants a new bus route, so Gemma has decided to design one." Gemma got to work marking out areas for the bus to go past. She was determined for the council to consider her map. Being 10 years old, she thought the council might listen to her a bit more than others. "Dear Council," she wrote in her letter. "My name is Gemma and I am 10 years old. I heard about your proposal for a new bus route, and I know the perfect place for it to go. Please find my attached map of the area, which shows my idea for the route. Yours sincerely, Gemma." Gemma wrote the council's address on the envelope and stuck a stamp in the corner. Then she posted it in the letterbox. "And now I have to wait!" she said to herself. Oh, no! Gemma had forgotten something very important. She had made a mistake on her map. She had meant for the bus to go past the lake, not the factory! Gemma phoned the council to tell them. Gemma felt bad for making a mistake on her map. She thought that now the council would not listen to her. She felt embarrassed. A week later, the postman arrived and spoke to Gemma's father. "There's a letter addressed to your daughter from the council," said the postman. "That's unusual. She's not in trouble, is she?" "No, no. My daughter has designed a new bus route," said Gemma's father. "What an intelligent girl," said the postman, handing the letter to Gemma's father. Gemma opened the letter from the council. Inside was a map of the new bus route, based on Gemma's drawings. Her schoolfriend Pete showed it to the class, while Gemma described the route. The council had decided to use Gemma's idea for the new bus route. Gemma was so happy. The bus would start at the lake, continue past the local letterbox, past the doctor's surgery, around the woods, and along her street, before continuing into town. The council thought Gemma's plan was a brilliant idea. In fact, it was the best idea they had received out of all the ideas sent to them. Very soon, work on the new bus stop began by the lake. Gemma took her friends and relatives to see. They were all very proud of Gemma, who had worked hard to create something for her town. She was recognised in the local paper as the route designer, and she received praise from the mayor and the council. Well done, Gemma! ﻿ Post-Reading Questions What did Gemma﻿ design for the council? What did Gemma write? What mistake did Gemma make, and what did she do? What did the postman give to her father a week later? Who did Gemma show her plan to, and who helped her to present it? If you could design something new, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: Four Lambs and a Fox
text: There were four lambs living in a house with their mother. Mother was on her way to the market. “You will open the door only when I say open the door, my children,” she warned her lambs. Meanwhile, a fox was nearby and heard the mother. He went to the house and said, “My children, open the door.” One of the lambs said, “No, that is not our mother's voice. Our mother's voice is soft.” The fox was angry. The fox wanted to make his voice like the lambs' mother. He decided to eat butter. He went to a shopkeeper. “Give me some butter, or I will kill you,” threatened the fox. The shopkeeper gave him butter. The fox went to the lambs and said, “My children, open the door.” A lamb looked through the keyhole of the door and saw the black leg of the fox. “No, our mother's legs are red!” shouted the lamb. Fox was not successful. Fox thought of another way. This time he planned to paint his legs with pepper powder. He went to a miller. “Give me pepper powder, or I will eat you,” the fox threatened. The miller gave him pepper powder. Fox painted his legs with the powder. He went to the lambs' house and said, “My children open the door.” The lambs opened the door. Fox swallowed three of them. The fourth lamb was hiding. Mother came back from the market. She said, “My children, I have come. Open the door.” The fourth lamb was terrified and couldn't open the door for her mother. When no one opened the door, the mother sheep kicked it open. She called her lambs. The fourth lamb came out of hiding. Her mother asked “Where are the others?” Shivering, the lamb replied, “The fox swallowed the others!” Her mother said, “The fox might eat us too. Let's move to another place.” They set off to another place. While they were travelling they saw the fox. He was sleeping. The mother approached the fox. She heard the voices of her lambs inside the fox's belly. “Bring me a razor blade, thread and a needle,” said the mother to her lamb. The mother cut the fox's belly with a razor blade. She found her three lambs inside his belly. She filled his belly with stones and stitched it together. She took all her lambs back to their house. When the fox woke up, he found it very difficult to get up. He tried to drink water at a river, but he lost his balance. He fell into the water and drowned.
author: Angesom  Abadi

title: How Tortoise's nose became crooked
text: Once upon a time, Tortoise and Squirrel were very close friends. One day, Squirrel said to Tortoise, “My friend, we have no money, but market day is getting close. What business can we do to make some money?” Tortoise responded, “You know I can make clay plates. I want you to join me in making plates to sell.” “Okay my friend, tomorrow evening I will join you to make the plates,” Squirrel said. On the day of the market, Tortoise went to the marketplace. He saw two people fighting in the distance. He put down his clay plates and went to watch the fight. When Tortoise got there, he saw that it was his friend Squirrel fighting with Mole. Immediately, without finding out what caused the fight, Tortoise took a big stick and began to beat Mole. “Leave my friend alone!” shouted Tortoise. Mole turned to face Tortoise and bit him deeply on the nose. Tortoise's nose began to bleed. Tortoise had impatiently entered into the fight. Since that day, Tortoise has a crooked nose to remind him not to be so hasty.
author: Taiwo Ẹhinẹni

title: Friends Become Enemies
text: Once upon a time there lived two friends, Hyena and Hare. Hyena was a hardworking farmer. He woke up early every morning and went to work in his field. Hare woke up when it was already broad daylight. He would yawn and stretch. Then he would go looking for food. Most mornings, Hare would take some seeds from Hyena's granary. Then he went to his field and pretended to work. He would light a fire and roast the seeds. He did nothing, except eat roasted seeds. At harvest time, Hare went and stole his friend's ripe maize. He carried it to his own granary. Hyena complained about the stolen crops. Hare answered, “Maybe the neighbours stole your maize. They are suffering from famine because they are lazy.” Hyena thought about this problem for a long time. He came up with an idea. He collected gum from the trees. He put that sticky gum around the whole field. The thief would get stuck in the gum. During the night, Hare went to Hyena's field to steal more maize. Before entering the field he looked around to see if it was safe. Hare did not see the gum that Hyena had put around the field. Hare stood in the gum and was stuck. He started shouting for help. Hyena heard the shouts and ran out to catch the thief. He could not believe his eyes. It was his friend Hare who was stuck in the gum! From that time, Hyena went his way and Hare went the other way. That marked the end of their friendship.
author: Kennedy Amandu

title: Lam Learns to Let Go
text: Story Description A boy called Lam helps his father run a pet business selling birds. One day, the birds desire to be set free, and one bird tells a story to Lam about learning how to let go. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Precious ﻿p-re-sh-uss ﻿The hat was very precious to the boy. He did not want to lose it. Uprooted ﻿up-roo-tid ﻿The wind was so strong that some trees were uprooted from the ground. Distracted ﻿dis-tr-act-id ﻿The boy was distracted by a cow, and he let go of his hat. Eventually ﻿ih-ven-chew-al-ee ﻿ ﻿It took a long time, but eventually, the boy understood. Lam and his father kept birds to sell as pets. There weren't many customers, so they only made a little bit of money from selling their parrots. One day, Lam asked to see the birds, and his father allowed him to. "If they are asleep, then don't disturb them," said Lam's father. "I won't," said Lam. "It's time for you to set us free," said one of the birds. "But you're a pet," said Lam. "I can't do that. We'd go out of business." "Please listen to my story. Lam, we want our freedom. You must find another way to make a living. Don't keep us as pets any longer." The bird told a story to Lam, who listened closely. There was once a boy called Harold, and he had a precious hat. He received it as a Christmas present when he was younger. Every time he went outside, he wore that hat. It made him look funny and cool. Harold took good care of his hat. He didn't want to lose it. Harold played outside wearing his hat, and he often chased the cows, who loved his company. He would chase them around the barn and the farm, but the cows were always too fast for him. Sometimes Harold played alone with his hat, running in circles, climbing trees and crawling through the bushes. He was in a world of his own, having so much fun. But then, one day, a gigantic gust of wind came. The wind blew across the land, bending trees and plants. Some trees were uprooted and they fell over. Harold was afraid that his hat would lift off his head and blow away. He was also afraid that the wind would carry him high and blow him into the distance. Harold was distracted by the cow he had been chasing, and suddenly, he let go of his hat. It took off and was carried away by the wind. "Oh, no! Come back!" shouted Harold. Harold cried and cried but his hat would not return. He went looking for it, but it was lost. The cow tried to comfort him. "There, there," said the cow. "You can always get another hat." "You don't understand," said Harold. "That was my precious Christmas gift. There's no other hat like it. It was one of a kind!" "You have to learn to let go," said the cow. "That hat is never coming back. Look at the things you do have instead." "That's so sad," said Lam. "Harold never saw his hat again." "Yes, but he learned to let go," said the bird. "If you set us free, we'll come back and visit you. Unlike the hat, you will see us again. You and your father are better off fishing. There is a higher demand for fish and you'll make more money." "I'm going to explain to my father why you must be set free," said Lam excitedly, jumping up and down. "I'll tell him that we can earn more from fishing." "Do your best," said the bird. "That's all we ask of you." And so the birds waited as Lam went to persuade his father. "You're right," said Lam's father, checking over his accounts. "In the past, the fishing gave us a better living. I just preferred birds. It's not fair to keep them in a cage all of their lives." So Lam and his father set the birds free. For the first time in their lives, the birds were truly happy. "That Lam, he was a good boy," said one bird. "He learned to let go of the things he wanted." "When you let go," said the other bird, "then you are also set free." Lam and his father made a great profit out of fishing, and Lam's father eventually made enough to buy a property on a big piece of land. Post-Reading Questions What kind of business did Lam help his father to run? What did the bird say when Lam went to visit? Why did Harold enjoy wearing his hat so much? Who did Harold used to chase around the farm? What happened when the big gust of wind came? Name a precious item that you have. Will you keep it?﻿
author: Hello English

title: Eagle's needle
text: Once upon a time Eagle and Hen were best friends. The two of them were together and chatted from morning till dusk. Eagle's chickens couldn't wait to visit Hen's chickens and play with them. One day Hen approached Eagle. “My friend,” she said. “I have to ask you a big favour. Rooster's pyjama pants are torn. He is really grumpy about it. They are his favourite pants. I want to mend the pants, but I don't have a needle. May I borrow your needle?” Eagle nodded. “Of course, dear friend,” she said. “But please take good care of it. It is an heirloom needle. My grandmother gave it to me.” “Of course, my friend,” Hen said. She took the shining needle. “I'll return it tomorrow.” Hen went away to mend her husband's pants. The next morning, as usual, Hen was on her way to Eagle. But oh, goodness – the needle was gone! Hen anxiously called her little chicks together. “Has anyone seen Eagle's needle?” she asked. “No, Mommy,” the chickens cheeped. “Help me look for it,” Hen said. Hen and her chickens looked everywhere. In every bush. Behind every lump of grass. Inside all their nests. But Eagle's needle was gone. Eagle waited the whole day for Hen to come and visit. By dusk she was getting annoyed. She flew to the farm yard. “Good evening, friend,” she greeted Hen. “Why didn't you visit me today?” “I I was very busy,” Hen said. “And where is the needle you borrowed from me?” Eagle asked.” “Hen swallowed.” “Oh, Eagle I am so sorry. I lost your needle.” “Lost it?" Eagle was angry. “Don't worry,” Hen said quickly. “My chickens and I will find it.” It must be here somewhere. Eagle was very angry. “I can't believe you lost my needle,” she said. “The needle I got from my grandma. You'd better look for it. If you haven't found it by tomorrow, I will come and grab one of your chickens.” The following morning Rooster had barely started crowing when Hen called on her chicks. “Kids, you must help me look for it,” she said. “We'll scratch around this whole farm yard. Eagle's needle must be here.” Look carefully when you see Hen and her chickens again. Up until this day they are still scratching around in the dust, looking for Eagle's needle. And when Hen notices an eagle flying in the air, she anxiously clucks: “Quick, little chicks. Hide beneath my wings. If Eagle sees you, she will catch you. She is still annoyed about her grandmother's needle.”
author: Jaco Jacobs

title: Pontshibobo's tree
text: Once upon a time, there was a young man called Pontshibobo. When he was little he was a very good boy. He had grown into a very good man. He respected everybody he met. Pontsihibobo had a friend called Hippo. He was not respectful like Pontshibobo. One day Pontshibobo and Hippo were walking down the street together. Hippo had an idea, “Let's go and smoke a zol,” he said. Pontshibobo was surprised. “Why do you ask me to smoke with you? You know that I don't smoke.” Hippo got cross. “If you don't want to smoke with me you can't be my friend,” he said and walked off. Pontshibobo went home and sat under the tree in his yard and cried. “Why are you crying?” asked the tree. Pontshibobo got a huge fright. He had never heard a tree talking before. He told the tree about Hippo. “I have lost a friend,” he said. The tree asked Pontshibobo, “What do you really wish for?” Pontshibobo thought for a while. Then he replied, “I want a house. I am grown up now and I want a home. I want to marry and have children.” The tree also thought for a while. “Take my leaves and my branches and build yourself a house with them,” he said. Pontshibobo did as the tree told him and he built a small, beautiful house. He married and had children. He was happy. But the tree was not happy. Pontshibobo had forgotten all about him and he felt sad. “I need a friend,” the tree said to himself, “or else I will die.” Just at that moment Pontshibobo came into the yard. He heard what the tree said, and he saw that the tree was very sick. Pontshibobo was also sad. He had forgotten all about the tree that had helped him build a house for his wife and children. “I am so sorry,” he cried and gave the tree a big hug. When the tree saw that his friend was back he smiled. He grew new branches and fresh leaves. Pontshibobo's children climbed up the branches of the tree. Pontshibobo and his wife sat in the shade after a long day at work. They told stories and laughed and were happy. Pontshibobo and the tree were friends forever.
author: Buhle Vilakazi

title: Shepherd and his Best Friend
text: Tarik was a Grade 4 student at Elementary School. His school was in Menz district in the province of North Shoa, Ethiopia. Tarik had a dog called Buchie. Where Buchie was, Tarik was there too. When Tarik's mom gave Tarik food, he shared it with Buchie. Tarik and Bedilu were in the same class. They were shepherds when they were not at school. One Saturday morning, Tarik and Bedilu were taking their flock to the common grazing land. They also carried their school books to study for examinations. Bedilu said, “Let's play kisara for few minutes to relax our minds.” Tarik replied, “No, we should start studying!” “We will study soon. Please play!” Bedilu begged. In the end, the boys played kisara. (Kisara is a game where players take turns throwing flat stones or coins into a small hole, standing about a meter away.) Without noticing, they played the game for about two hours. When they looked, they couldn't see their sheep anywhere. They ran everywhere searching for the sheep. From a distance, they saw a wolf chasing their sheep! Then they saw that the wolf had killed Tarik's sheep. He began crying. He knew that his father would punish him severely. When Bedilu took his sheep home, Tarik didn't go home. He decided to spend the night in the big tree not far from his house. He slept on a low branch and Buchie slept below him on the ground. At midnight, Tarik was woken by a loud scream of hyenas. He got such a fright that he fell off the branch, down to the ground. Tarik heard sounds of animals near him but it was too dark to see them. He began sweating, thinking that it must be hyenas. Suddenly, lightning flashed light across the sky. Tarik was able to see around him. There was Buchie standing guard and protecting him from two snarling hyenas. Buchie saved Tarik, what a friend he was indeed! The boy scrambled back up into the tree, taking Buchie with him. Together they would wait for morning and then go home to face Tarik's father.
author: Biniam Asfaw

title: Pride Comes Before A Fall
text: Story Description A cheeky blue monkey sees a gigantic pumpkin and wants to steal it. He climbs to the top of a water tower where it is safely kept. Meanwhile, a friendly red monkey sees the blue monkey trying to steal the pumpkin. Pre-Reading Vocabulary Phonics ﻿Outstretched ﻿ow-t-str-ech-d ﻿The monkey fell with his arms outstretched in front of his body. Plummeted ﻿plum-it-id ﻿The monkey plummeted through the air. Hobbled ﻿hob-ul-d ﻿The monkey got up and hobbled on one leg. Congratulated ﻿cun-grat-chew-lay-tid ﻿ ﻿The woman congratulated the monkey for being brave. A blue monkey arrived in a village searching for food. He was desperate to eat. He had been hungry for days. On the top of a water tower, the monkey spied a giant pumpkin. He just had to take it. He felt that he had no choice. A red monkey, who lived in the village, was sitting by his house and playing a beat on his drum. The blue monkey sneaked around the houses, when the red monkey saw the intruder. The red monkey followed him by the houses and towards the water tank, wondering what he was going to do. The blue monkey searched around to make sure the coast was clear. Happy that nobody was there, he picked up a ladder and laughed to himself, sneaking by the water tower. "Careful, now," he said to himself, positioning the ladder so it was steady. He climbed a couple of rungs and stopped when the ladder wobbled. He got down and adjusted it, and happy that it was fixed in place, he began climbing. "Aggh!" said the monkey, pushing the pumpkin. He realised how heavy it was, and he stopped for a moment. He thought to himself. "How am I going to get this down from the tower? I can't even lift it up!" That left the monkey with one choice. He would have to roll it off the building, and hope it wouldn't smash when it hit the ground. Suddenly, the red monkey jumped up on the opposite house roof. "Stop!" he yelled. The blue monkey froze, startled by his appearance. Out of panic, he let the pumpkin go, and it kept rolling. "No!" he cried out. The pumpkin rolled off the tower and plummeted through the air. So did the blue monkey! He tried to rescue the pumpkin, but it was too late. He fell with his arms outstretched. Oof! The blue monkey hit the side of the water tower and then the ground. It was a hard fall. He looked to one side - the pumpkin was still fully intact! It had not split apart! "What a stroke of luck!" he thought. "Now to get away with the treasure!" But the blue monkey couldn't get up straight away. The impact of the fall had winded him. Then he saw the red monkey right in front of him, looking stern and fierce. "Leave our village, and never come back!" said the red monkey. The blue monkey hobbled to his feet and slowly left, watched closely by the red monkey. As soon as he thought he was out of sight, the blue monkey ran away, setting his sights on a different village, hoping they had something like a giant pumpkin he could take away. In the morning, the red monkey pointed out what had happened, and told a woman the story of the night before. She was horrified. She couldn't believe a monkey would break in and try to steal it. She congratulated the red monkey for his bravery. "At least the pumpkin is still intact," said the red monkey, and despite the long fall, indeed somehow it was still in one piece! Post-Reading Questions ﻿Who saw the blue monkey enter the village? How did the blue monkey climb the water tower? What did the blue monkey see at the top of the tower? What happened when the red monkey suddenly appeared? What happened to the pumpkin after it hit the ground? Describe the red monkey's actions.
author: Hello English

title: Fana and her animals
text: Fana and her family live in Debre Birhan, a busy town in Ethiopia. Fana is a Grade 3 student. She is good-hearted and wise. Fana loves animals. She has a cat, two hens, a goat and a dove. She spends time with these animals, feeding them, and playing with them. One day, Fana was playing in the school yard with her friends when she saw children throwing stones at doves. “Why are they hurting the doves?” She asked herself. She stopped playing and ran towards the children throwing stones. At first her friends didn't understand what was happening, then they followed her. “Stop throwing stones,” shouted Fana. The other children ran away. Fana caught the two injured doves. She saw wounds on their wings. She decided to take the two doves home to look after them. She fed the doves. In the evening she told her family what she saw and did during the day, and how she saved the doves. In the morning Fana and her parents went to the clinic and got medicine for the doves. After a few days, the doves' wounds healed. Fana felt very happy. Fana always tells her friends, “I love animals. Animals are useful to us and they are our friends. We must protect and preserve them.”
author: Foziya Mohammed

title: Three boxes of wealth
text: There lived an old man called Hagos. He lived with his three sons. Hagos wanted his sons to have wealth after his death. He prepared three boxes for them. Hagos went to his neighbour Haile and said, “I want my sons to have wealth. I have prepared three boxes. I want you to give them the boxes after I die.” After Hagos died, Haile called the sons together. He told them, “Your father gave me these boxes before he died. You will each find your name on one of them. Take yours please.” The sons took the boxes and opened them. The first box had gold in it. The second box had soil. The third box had animal dung in it. The one who found gold was very happy. The other two were not happy. They started quarrelling with him. “You are brothers, you should not quarrel. Let me take you to a wise old man to advise you,” said Haile to the three brothers. Haile took the brothers to the wise old man. “Good morning, we have come to ask advice about inheritance,” said Haile to the old man. Haile told the wise old man about the three boxes that Hagos had left for his sons. “Now they are quarrelling because only one received gold,” explained Haile. The wise old man asserted, “Your father had a reason for giving each of you a particular box.” He continued, “The one who received gold, your father wants you to be a merchant. The one who received soil, your father wants you to be a farmer.” “The one who received animal dung, your father wants you to be a cowboy. Your father wanted you each to have his own profession,” the old man concluded. After they listened to the old man's advice the three brothers agreed. They worked in their professions and lived happily.
author: Angesom  Abadi

title: The Bumbling Bouncing Ball
text: Story Description Anita has a mysterious bouncing ball that is packed with energy. She accidentally drops it, and it bounces away really fast. Anita chases after the ball, while the ball goes through building sites, past electricians, families and runners. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Profusely ﻿pruh-few-ss-lee ﻿The workers were sweating profusely in the heat. Electrician ﻿ilec-trish-un ﻿An electrician nearly caught the ball. Construction ﻿cun-struc-shun ﻿A bunch of construction workers were busy when they saw the ball fly past. Bumbling ﻿bum-bl-ing ﻿ ﻿The ball was a bumbling, careless thing, bouncing into everyone. Anita was playing with a mysterious purple ball that she had purchased from an old man at a market. She had not played with it yet, so she took it with her on her way to meet her friends. During her walk, she accidentally dropped the ball. To her surprise, it didn't stay on the ground. It bounced high away into the sky. "Come back!" she called out. The purple ball kept on rolling, bouncing in steps as it made its way through the park. It didn't slow down. Instead, it sped up. People moved out of the way as it passed, worried that they would be struck by the bumbling ball. The ball bounced straight through a construction site, where builders, mixers, scaffolders and painters were all working together, trying to complete a wall. The ball skimmed through them, almost knocking off their hats, and one builder almost fell off the poles backwards when he saw the ball coming at them! Anita chased the ball through some quiet fields. There were some police officers taking a break, when the ball suddenly whizzed past them. They almost dropped their tea when a blur went past their faces. The girl reached high and jumped, but the ball kept getting away from her. Some flower pickers were having a rest by the fields, preparing their flowers to sell while sharing funny stories. Just then, Anita ran through, followed by the ball. The pickers were too busy to realise that a purple ball had just gone by really quickly. The ball bounced along a path of joggers who were sweating profusely. They got a shock when the ball bounced in between them, beating them to the finish line. Even Anita ran faster than them, determined to catch the ball. Anita came across a group of men and women sweeping the pathway. They were too busy enjoying their work to notice the ball leaping over them. A family was enjoying a picnic on their balcony by the town square. Anita climbed a wall when the ball bounced on to the balcony. The family was relaxed and enjoying one another's company, and only one person saw the ball bounce over the plates and the food. Anita yelled after the ball, but it kept bouncing away from her. A construction worker was busy inside a sewer hole, when he saw the ball coming and made a grab for it. But the ball bounced straight over him and continued on its journey. Anita followed the ball by some tea sellers, where she stopped to buy a cup. The ball jumped over them and continued on its way, and Anita ran with a cup of tea in her hand. Yikes! The ball went into the fields and bounced on a bowl that a woman was carrying! One woman stuck her hand up to catch the ball...but she missed it! The ball bounced even higher as it gathered energy. It went far away from the girl, and travelled so high that it disturbed a bunch of electricians trying to fix a lamppost. They almost fell off! Just then, the ball bounced off a tree. Anita saw the moment unfolding in front of her. She jumped as high as she could, and she caught the ball with both hands! It was the end of an exhausting, stressful venture across the town and the fields. She promised not to bring the ball outside ever again, and she went on to see her friends. Post-Reading Questions Who did Anita buy the mysterious ball from? What happened when Anita dropped the ball while she was walking? Who did the ball bounce by first? Who was in the park on a break when the ball travelled by? On its entire journey, did the ball damage anything? Name something you would not bring outside.
author: Hello English

title: Chandra's Confused Computer
text: Chandra’s Computer was SOOOO Confused! That Night just before bedtime Chandra had Said, “My Cute Computer is SOOOO like me!" "Oh you are my Best Buddy!” And she’d clapped her hands in Glee!!! Now the Computer was SOOOO confused! What did Chandra mean by ‘ LIKE ME’ A human and a machine, the same. HOW COULD THAT BE??? “Humans come in all sizes and shapes, DIFFERENT models and DIFFERENT makes. They are Men and Women, Mummies and Grannies, French, Indians, African and Chinese…” THE SAME CHANDRA AND ME, JUST CANNOT BE!!! Just then..."Tick Tock Tick Tock" “Same as you OFCOURSE!" Chimed in Grand old, Clickety Clock! “Desktops, Laptops, IPads and Smart phones too. Different models, different Makes, different sizes and different shapes!” “ But Clickety Clock, where are my ears and eyes? ” “And where is my mouth?” “I don’t eat and I don’t shout!” With a Strike Clickety Replied, “Why does a Human need an eye or an ear? TO UNDERSTAND - To see, to hear. For that you’ve got the Keyboard, the webcam, Why even the microphone, MOUSE and the Scanner. Yes to take it all IN …” *INFORMATION* SOME COMMON COMPUTER INPUT DEVICES: KEYBOARD: IT IS THE MOST COMMON INPUT DEVICE. IT HAS KEYS SIMILAR TO A TYPEWRITER WEBCAM: THIS IS THE VIDEO CAMERA. MICROPHONE: TO CAPTURE AUDIO. MOUSE: A HANDHELD DEVICE TO CONTROL A SCREEN’S CURSOR OR POINTER. IT IS SHAPED SUCH LIKE A MOUSE; IT EVEN HAS A TAIL! SCANNER: FOR AUTOMATIC DATA COLLECTION- CAPTURES IMAGES. On hearing this, Computer’s MONITOR shone brightly, “BUZZZZZ CRACKLE BUZZZZZ”, the SPEAKERS spoke in glee! “Now it is all becoming so clear,” “Clickety Clock, thank you so much my dear!” “To spit out Information I’ve got a PRINTER.” To reach OUT I also use my SPEAKERS and SCREEN Wow I am such a SUPER DUPER MACHINE!” *INFORMATION* SOME COMMON COMPUTER OUTPUT DEVICES: MONITOR/SCREEN: IT IS AN OUPUT DEVICE THAT SHOWS INFORMATION IN PICTURE FORMAT. IT LOOKS JUST LIKE A TV SCREEN. SPEAKERS: POPULAR OUTPUT DEVICE. THEY PRODUCE AUDIO OUTPUT OR SOUND WAVES. PRINTER: THIS OUPTUT DEVICE PRINTS OUTPUT ON A PAPER. "Like my Buddy Chandra, I have a Brain too, Why it is my CPU! It gives and takes Instructions, Thanks to it, I make Crackling Computations. And of course it guides all my communications!" *INFORMATION* CPU: THE CENTRAL PROCESSING UNIT HANDLES ALL INSTRUCTIONS AND PERFORMS THE PROCESSING FOR THE COMPUTER. IT COMPRISES OF: CU - CONTROL UNIT; ALU - ARITHMETIC LOGIC UNIT IMMEDIATE ACCESS STORE OR MEMORY. "Ofcourse My Buddy Chandra is so LIKE ME, Dear Clickety it's all become most clear you see... Chandra's HARDWARE is her body parts like her Hands and Feet, And HER SOFTWARE her thoughts and dreams so SWEET!" *INFORMATION* HARDWARE: PHYSICAL PARTS OF THE COMPUTER WHICH YOU CAN TOUCH LIKE KEYBOARD, SCREEN, STORAGE DEVICES. SOFTWARE: CODE INSIDE YOUR COMPUTER WHICH YOU CANNOT TOUCH OR SEE. "Thank you Dear Clickety, for making it so easy for me... Just like Chandra, you too are my Bestie!" "Wel-come, wel-comeee chimed back good ol' Clickety, Filled with laughter and glee, for her not-so-confused-anymore Buddy!" *COMPUTER SPEAK* 1. Name some input devices and some output devices 2. Why do you think the Mouse is called 'Mouse'? Does it have any similarity with a real mouse? 3. Are there any question which you have? Which Confuse you? 4. Who is YOUR best buddy, who makes you clap in glee?
author: Rutuja Joshi
illustrator: Delwyn Remedios; Sunayana  Nair Kanjilal; Supriya Parhad

title: Neo finds her pig
text: Neo takes her pig for a ride on her bicycle. She hits a stone in the road. The pig falls down. It cries. It says, “Hooeeeee, hooeeeee!” Tsotang finds it. He says, “Haaiee, who does this pig belong to?” Tsotang chases it, until he catches it. He takes the pig to the chief. The chief tells him to look after it. Neo passes by on the path. She hears the pig grunting, “Hmmm, hmmm, hmmm!” She goes in. She is happy to see her pig. Neo says to her pig, “Come, let's go home. We will not ride the bicycle again.
author: Sehlopasa Malea LeaASP

title: A father's lesson
text: In a village, there was a young boy whose name was Abula. He did not like to read or even to open a book. He was a lazy pupil. He behaved badly. Abula stole his mother's money to buy sweets. Even when she hid her money, he found it and took it. After eating all his sweets, Abula would play with his friends. After a while, Abula stopped going to school. He stayed out playing the whole day, only returning home in the evening. Abula's mother noticed this and became worried. “Our son is not behaving well. I do not think he is attending school. He is also stealing money from me,” said Abula's mother. His father thought about how best to change Abula's behaviour. He said to his wife, “Next time, hide the money within the pages of a book. He never even opens a book, so the money will be safe there.” The next day, Abula looked for his mother's money. He searched everywhere but he did not find anything. He decided to go to the nearest market to find some money. His father saw where Abula was going. “My son, I know why you are going to the market. Now go back inside and look in the books for money,” he said. A bula was puzzled, but he went and searched in the books. He found the money that his mother had hidden. The next day, he looked in the books again. But there was nothing hidden there. He went to his father to ask why there was no money in the books. His father smiled and replied, “My son, do you want to get enough money to buy many sweets?” Abula answered, “Of course, father.” His father said, “Listen to me carefully. Read your books and attend your classes. You will find rewards in books. Do not give up.” “But father, reading is a difficult activity. Books are boring!” Abula replied. F or a while, Abula's father was quiet. He thought about how to encourage his son. Then he said to Abula, “Let us read together. I will help you to find the wealth in books.”
author: Abraham Bereket; Hardido  Temesgen; Yohannes Firew

title: From Boy to Warrior
text: Story Description A young boy is initiated in his tribe to become a warrior, undergoing training and tests. He helps protect his tribe and village from an enemy. This story takes a look at how different cultures work. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Acclimatised a-clai-ma-tai-z-d The young man must become acclimatised to being a warrior. Conditioning cun-dish-un-ing He undergoes intense body training and conditioning to turn him into a strong man. Inventory in-ven-tur-ee The spear and shield are the two most important items in his inventory. Retaliate ree-tal-ee-ate The tribe retaliate s by fighting back against the enemy. Hello! My name is Atman. I belong to a South African tribe. I am a doctor providing medicine for my people. I have been given the responsibility of showing outsiders how our tribe works, and showing them importance of close community. Please listen as you uncover this new world that I'll show you. This is a young man of our tribe. He is not yet old enough to be a warrior, so he helps with daily tasks such as cleaning, cooking, preparing weapons, applying bandages, and giving aid where necessary. His mentor is impressed with his work. He is an inquisitive young man - always asking questions of how and why, and what it takes to be a strong leader and a brave warrior. He takes any advice he can get from the senior warriors, and he applies it to his own learning. Eventually, his mentor tells him he is old enough and ready for warrior training. This delights the young man, and he leaves immediately to gain knowledge and get acclimatised for being a warrior. The first thing the young man learns is the importance of his weapons. He learns how to clean, sharpen and look after his spear and shield. These are the two most important items in the young man's inventory. He must look after them and use them well. The young man enters the field and walks several kilometres per day. He performs exercises that train all of his body from head to toe. Every day he is exhausted, conducting mock fights and battles. But this is all conditioning for what comes later, and when he is a warrior, he will always be ready and sufficiently prepared for action. After months of training, the young man is presented with his own warrior's spear. This weapon will stay with him for life. It is a great honour to receive one. This act marks the transition from young man into warrior. Now he is ready, and he becomes a well respected member of the tribe. The zebras are scared by the arrival of an opposing, threatening tribe. The tribe is determined to conquer the land and call it their own. Our tribe is alerted to the seriousness of the situation. The warriors prepare their weapons and get ready for war. The young man has not fought before, but he goes into battle with his mentor, knowing he has a guide and a close friend by his side. He is scared, yet he is filled with courage. The vicious, opposing tribe burns nearby huts and trees to try and force our tribe away from our land. But we stay where we are, ready to engage the enemy. "Off we go, son," says the mentor to the young man warrior. "I'll stay close." The young man listens to his mentor as our tribe retaliates against the enemy, clashing with them in the fields. After the altercation, the enemy tribe is pushed back by sheer strength. We congratulate ourselves and celebrate by dancing in the village. The festivities continue and the mentor congratulates the young man for fighting bravely. He is now officially a warrior. Post-Reading Questions Before he trains as a warrior, how does the young man help the tribe? Where does the young man gain knowledge? What are the young warrior's most important tools? How does the young warrior prepare for a future battle? What does the young warrior receive when he is ready? What do you think is the most important trait for becoming a warrior?
author: Hello English

title: Are you an ulluu?
text: He was reading a book. But the book was upside- down. "Are you an ullu, reading the book upside-down?" One day he was going out. But there was a pit in the ground ahead. "Are you an ullu? Didnt you see the pit?" He was sad. Why does everyone call me an ullu, he thought. Just then, an owl flew past. He carried him away. "Who are you?" "I am an ullu!" "Really! Do you also play at night?" "No..." "Do you read books upside-down?" "No...." "Do you fall in pits like i do?" "Absolutely not!" "If you don't do all this... then how can you be an ullu?" "Haha! Now I understand. My name is Ullu!" "But YOU are not an ullu. You are a simple little kid." "Come, I'll drop you home." "But tell me, why is your name Owl?" "Oh, are you an ullu that you cannot understand a simple thing like this?" "But YOU are an ullu! I am just a simple little kid."
author: Vibha G

title: The Mango Tree
text: Story Description A boy rides a hot air balloon across the country. Suddenly a gust of wind carries him to a new spot, where he finds a mango tree. But during his adventure, he is not alone. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Swayed ﻿ss-way-d ﻿The hot air balloon swayed in the wind. Sunflower ﻿sun-fl-ow-ur ﻿There was a giant sunflower field. Intrigued ﻿in-tree-g-d ﻿The boy was interested and intrigued by the lonely tree. Crammed ﻿cram-d ﻿The boy shoved and crammed lots of mangos into his small bag. Once upon a time, a boy was flying his hot air balloon across the country, in search of new fruits and foods. He flew across a beautiful dusty mountain range, surrounded by flowers and rivers. Suddenly the boy encountered a storm. Powerful winds blew the hot air balloon sideways, and the boy couldn't control the balloon. He held on for his life as the balloon swayed and tilted through the storm. The boy carried on through the storm, and suddenly there was a clear bright blue sky all around. He landed the balloon in a field of sunflowers and took a walk. It was a lovely warm day. As the boy was walking, he saw a tree standing on its own in the distance. Intrigued, he wanted to find out what variety it was, so he set off towards it. When arrived, he found fruits hanging off the tree. He reached up and picked one. It was sticky and soft. It was a mango! The boy knew he could stock up on delicious mangos that would last him a long time. But then, he also saw something else sticking out of the tree. It was long and furry, and the boy pulled on the object. Suddenly, a monkey fell out of the tree eating a mango. The boy was startled and anxious. He'd never encountered a real life monkey before. He went to grab his umbrella to defend himself from the furry creature. But the monkey stayed calm, and the boy felt calmer too. "Mmm, wow!" said the boy, as they sat down. The monkey was very calm and cheeky, and the boy relaxed in his company. "I've never met a creature like you before," said the boy. "Me neither," said the monkey. "I guess that makes us both strange." The boy and monkey laughed while they ate the soft, juicy mangos. The boy bid farewell to the monkey, who rested in the shade under the tree. The boy skipped away while whistling a song, happy with his stash of mangoes crammed into his bag. The boy took off in his balloon, heading towards home, and remembering the tree and the monkey. He didn't have a map, but he knew that one day he would see the tree again, and possibly the monkey too. Post-Reading Questions What mode of transport did the boy use to get around? What carried the balloon away in the sky? Where did the boy land? What did he see in the distance? What did the boy pull that was sticking out of the tree? Imagine a far away place. What would you find there?﻿
author: Hello English

title: Lazy Anansi
text: There was a spider called Anansi. Anansi was too lazy to cook his own food. Instead, he used to visit his friends and eat the delicious food they had cooked. One day, Anansi was passing Rabbit's house when he smelled green vegetables cooking. He was very excited. Rabbit said to Anansi, “They're not quite ready yet. You can help me to wash up while we wait.” Anansi replied, “Sorry, I have things to do. I'll come back later.” “How will I call you when they're ready?” asked Rabbit. Anansi thought for a minute. “I'll spin a web,” he said. “I'll tie one end around my leg and one end to your pot. When the greens are ready, pull on the web string. I'll come right away.” So Anansi tied the web to the pot, and walked on. Anansi saw Monkey and his wife, cooking beans in a large pot. “Come and join us! The beans are nearly ready.” Monkey said. Anansi replied, “Sorry, I have things to do. Let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot. When the beans are ready, pull on the web string, and I'll come.” As Anansi walked by Warthog's house, he smelled sweet potatoes. Warthog told Anansi, “My pot is full of sweet potatoes and honey! Come and share my food with me. Take this fork and help me to stir it.” Anansi replied, “I'll come back later. Let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot. When the sweet potatoes are ready, pull on the web string, and I'll come.” By the time Anansi arrived at the river, each of his eight legs was tied to a pot of delicious food. Then, Anansi felt a pull on one of his legs. “Rabbit's food is ready!” Anansi thought, licking his lips. He felt a second pull. And a third. And a fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth pull. Everyone was pulling on the web strings at the same time! “Stop! Stop!” he cried in pain, as his legs were stretched thinner and thinner. But no one could hear him. Finally, the web strings could hold no longer. They snapped, one by one. Anansi rolled into the river to soothe his painful legs. But his legs would not return to their normal shape. Anansi was too embarrassed to go to any of his friends that day.
author: Ghanaian  Folktale

title: Aku and her ice cream
text: One day, mother was cooking. She called, “Abena, Ajua, Akwasi, Aku, food is ready! Bring your plates!” Mother gave each of them some fufu. She gave them some soup. Then she gave them some meat. She said to them, “Go, sit down and eat.” Aku looked at her fufu. She looked at her soup. Then she looked at her meat. She put her plate down angrily and cried. Mother asked, “Aku, what is wrong with you?” “My meat is the smallest,” Aku cried. “But you are the youngest,” mother said. Aku cried harder. She threw herself on the ground. Mother did not want Aku to cry. She called loudly, “Abena, Ajua, Akwasi, bring your food quickly!” The children brought their food. “Now Aku, pick the meat you like,” mother said. Aku smiled happily. She looked hard at Akwasi's meat and thought, “Akwasi's meat is big.” She looked hard at Ajua's meat, and thought, “Ajua's meat is bigger.” She looked hard at Abena's meat. Abena's meat was the biggest. She said to mother, “I want Abena's meat.” “Abena, give your meat to Aku and take hers,” mother said. Abena was unhappy. But she did not want to disobey mother. So she gave her meat to Aku. “Mmmm, this meat will be sweet,” Aku said. She sat on a stool and ate happily. Pii! Pii! It was the ice cream man outside. He rode a big bicycle with a small horn. Aku loved ice cream. “Abena, get my bag,” mother said. “I want to buy ice cream for all of you.” Abena brought mother's bag. “Four ice creams, please,” mother said to the ice cream man. She paid and gave each child an ice cream. “One, two, three, four,” counted Aku. She looked at her ice cream. It was small. She looked hard at Akwasi's ice cream. It was smaller than hers. She looked harder at Ajua's ice cream. It was the smallest of all. She was happy. “My ice cream is the biggest,” she thought. “Wait,” she thought. “I must see Abena's ice cream too.” She moved closer to Abena. Then she opened her mouth wide and cried. “What is the matter, Aku?” mother asked. “Abena's ice cream is bigger than mine,” she cried. Mother said, “Aku you are a greedy girl!” Aku cried harder. She threw herself on the ground. Mother was unhappy. She did not want Aku to cry. Mother said to Abena, “Please give your ice cream to Aku and take hers.” Abena was unhappy, but she did not want to disobey mother. She gave the ice cream to Aku. Aku's eyes shone with happiness. She looked at the big ice cream and smiled. “Mmmm, this ice cream looks good,” said Aku. She opened her mouth wide and took a big bite. “Ajiish!” she shouted suddenly and spat out the ice cream. “What is the matter now?” mother asked. “This ice cream is bitter,“ wailed Aku. Mother took Aku's ice cream and bit into it. She frowned. “There is something wrong with this. It is spoilt,” she said. Then mother added, “Sorry Aku, you cannot have another one. Now do you see that it is bad to be greedy?”
author: Agnes Gyening-Asiedu

title: Tina's Dream
text: Story Description Tina falls asleep holding a glowing ring, and she gets transported to a strange dream world, where she has peculiar friends and there is food everywhere. Tina goes from place to place in the dream world, discovering new things. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Accompanied ﻿ac-um-pan-ee-d ﻿Several strange creatures accompanied Tina in the dream. Goodies ﻿gud-ee-s ﻿Tina found lots of goodies buried in the candy floss. Burping ﻿bur-p-ing ﻿After Tina drank so much orange soda, she was burping a lot. Gigantic ﻿jai-gan-tic ﻿The tower of jelly was gigantic in size. After playing outside for most of the evening with her friends, Tina's parents called her inside for bed. Tina waved goodbye to her friends and then joined her parents indoors. She brushed her teeth and got ready for bed, and as the sun went down and darkness came, Tina felt very tired. She yawned and found a ring on her bedside table. She took the ring in her hands. It was lighting up. She had never seen the ring before. As Tina asked why, she slowly started to drift off to sleep. As soon as Tina fell asleep, she went into the dream world. She felt herself flying over some rolling green hills at nighttime, accompanied by some mystical creatures. She didn't recognise them at all. They kept soaring away. Tina flew with her alien friends across a village made entirely of mushroom houses. Tina found the place completely bizarre. She had never seen anything like a mushroom village before. The buildings were soft and squishy. Little children mushrooms and adults bounced around in their houses. Tina flew over a sea of food and she reached down, trying to grab all of the delicious goodies! She saw lollipops, a penguin, two ice-creams, jelly, a dolly and a cake. Also, a cricket bat was hidden inside some pink candy floss! If you look closely, there are a couple of other items! Next, Tina and her friends landed in a sea of orange soda. Her friends gave her a straw and she drank as much as she could. But then her stomach was filled with gas! She couldn't stop burping! Tina arrived at a field filled with different flavoured cakes. There was strawberry and lemon, lime and watermelon. She chose the lemon cake and found that it was covered in jelly flavoured soft gems! She took a gigantic bite, but she couldn't eat any more because it was so sweet! Her friends gathered around her and they floated in the air for a while.
