"There is still one more place that we have to take you to," they said. Tina felt so excited. "Where is it? Where is it?" she asked. "Come with us and you'll see." Tina followed her friends and found an island with elephants and cats. On top of the island were building blocks made out of thick jelly. She pushed the tower of blocks and it wobbled, making her laugh. Her friends warned her not to eat it, otherwise her dream would end. Tina ignored them and chomped on a piece of block, and suddenly she felt herself falling! "We told you not to eat the jelly blocks!" said her friends. "Now we're in the woods, and the dream has to end. You won't see the big prize!" "Oh, no," said Tina. "I should have listened to you. Tell me what the big prize is!" But suddenly, Tina's friends vanished and she was left alone. Then she started floating and spinning in the air. She felt very dizzy. She woke up with a shock and found herself on her bed. The glowing ring had gone. She wondered just where she had been. She wondered what the big prize would have been. Post-Reading Questions ﻿Tina eats the jelly block and gets sent out of the dream. She cannot see the big prize. What do you think the big prize would have been? What is the first thing that Tina flies over? What flavours of cake did Tina find in the field? Describe the mushroom people. Name something that wasn't mentioned in the pile of candy floss. If you could fly anywhere, where would you go to?
author: Hello English

title: Elephant and Chameleon
text: Once upon a time in a big palace, there lived a king and his beautiful daughter, the princess. Elephant lived in a house on one side of the palace. Chameleon lived on the other side. At this time, there was a terrible drought across the land. The king had an idea and called his two neighbours to the palace. The kind said to Elephant and Chameleon, “I want you to stomp on the ground with your feet until water comes out.” The king promised the princess in marriage to the one who succeeded. Chameleon had no hope since he was very small. Elephant was extremely happy since he was so big and powerful. Elephant went to the field and started stomping on the ground. A lot of dust came, but no water. Elephant stomped on the ground until water was almost coming out, but he was too tired. He gave Chameleon a chance to try. Chameleon started stomping on the ground. After a short while, water came out. People could not believe their eyes! So the King gave the beautiful princess to Chameleon. Elephant went home annoyed.
author: Stella  Badaru

title: Fox and Rooster
text: There was a time when all the animals lived together as friends. One day they decided to have a meeting to elect a king. Rooster wanted to be king. So he lied to the other animals. He told them, “The red comb on my head is fire! Don't touch the comb on my head!” The other animals believed Rooster. They decided to elect Rooster as their king. The animals hoped that Rooster's fire would help them in cold weather. Then came a day when it rained. And rained. And rained. It was cold. Everything was wet and cold. “Where can we get fire to warm our bodies?” Rabbit asked the other animals. “We can get fire from the comb on Rooster's head,” replied Monkey. “Rooster is our king because he has fire on his head,” said Monkey. The animals agreed with Monkey. They sent Fox to collect fire from king Rooster. Fox found Rooster in a deep sleep. So he decided to take fire without asking Rooster. Fox collected some dry grass. He put the grass next to the comb on Rooster's head. Nothing happened. The grass did not catch fire. “Wake up king Rooster!” yelled Fox. “We need fire now.” But Rooster could not give fire to Fox. Fox was angry. He went back to the other animals. He told them the truth about the comb on Rooster's head. From that day, no one was afraid of Rooster. And foxes eat roosters and their families.
author: Vincent Afeku

title: Anansi, the Crows, and the Crocodiles
text: One day there was a great famine in the land. No one had anything to eat except the crows. Each morning they flew a long distance to where there was a tree with ripe figs in the middle of a wide river. Then they flew back with the figs for themselves and their relatives. The sight of so many figs made Anansi's mouth water. How could he get them for himself? He thought of a plan. He carefully covered his bottom with sticky beeswax. Then he took a piece of clay pot and went to see the crows. “Please could you help me?” he asked. “I need a live coal to get my fire going again.” As they were getting the coal from the fire, Anansi carefully sat firmly on one of the largest figs, so that it would stick to his bottom. He thanked the crows, and hurried home to enjoy the fig. But one fig wasn't enough for him. He went back a second time, and did the same. When he went back a third time, the crows began to get suspicious. “Why do you keep coming back to us to get a coal?” they said. Anansi answered, “Every time when I get home, the coal has burnt out.” “You're lying!” said the crows. “You just want our food!” “That's not true,” said Anansi. And he started crying. The crows felt sorry for him. The next morning at first light, each crow gave him a feather. He flew with them to the fig tree in the middle of the wide river. When he saw the luscious figs, Anansi wanted them all for himself. Each time a crow tried to pick a fig, he shouted out, “That one is mine! I saw it first!” And then he took the fig and put it into his bag. Eventually he had all the figs and the crows had none. He was left all alone as the darkness began to fall. “If I don't want to stay in this tree for the rest of my life,” he said to himself, “I'll just have to jump into the air like the crows.” So he took a deep breath, jumped, and PLOP! He fell into the river right among the crocodiles. “What do we have here?” said a gruff crocodile voice. “A tasty morsel to eat, nyum”. “Oh please don't” said Anansi. And he began to cry. “I'm one of you, don't you know? I got lost in the days of your grandfathers and no one was able to find me. You're the first of my relatives I've ever met!” He cried so much that the crocodiles felt sorry for him. The oldest crocodile said, “We'll know you're one of us if you can eat and enjoy mud soup just like we do.” They gave him a pot of dirty brown water. “Just like my grandmother used to make it!” Anansi said. But he made a hole in the ground with his back foot, and a hole in the pot with his front foot. As he pretended to drink the soup, it oozed down through the pot into the hole beneath his feet. “Delicious!” he exclaimed, giving back the empty pot. "Now we know you are definitely one of us," the crocodiles said. So they allowed Anansi to sleep in their hole with them for the night. "Tomorrow morning I'll tell you the story of my life," said Anansi as they fell asleep. Early the next morning, before first light, Anansi woke up one of the crocodiles. "I want to go and fetch my wife and children from across the river, so that they can help me tell my story. Will you help me before the others wake up?" he asked the crocodile. The crocodile was grumpy at being woken up so early. “Please help me! You swim much faster than I do,” Anansi said. The crocodile agreed, and Anansi rode on his back to the bank of the river. He climbed off quickly. “I'll be back soon! Don't go away!” Anansi said, as he disappeared through the grass. As far as we know, the crocodile is waiting for him still, with just his long snout and his beady eyes above the surface of the river.
author: Ghanaian  Folktale

title: The Slithering Snake
text: Story Description The wind tells the story of how he learned to move - just by watching a slithering snake go about its day. The wind compares itself with the snake, showing how the two are similar. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Blistering bl-ih-stur-ing The blistering heat caused the wind to be warm. Unpredictably un-pre-dic-tub-lee The wind moves like the snake, unpredictably in any direction. Wily why-lee The wily snake meanders and sways on the ground. Encompassing in-come-pa-sing The wind is all- encompassing and everywhere. I am the wind. I can be weak and I can be strong. I am blustering and I am calm. Given the time of year, and the time of day, I act accordingly. They say I sway and swarm and act unpredictably. They say there's no guessing as to what I will do. Let me show you where I got my moves from. You won't believe what I tell you is true! Of all the creatures, the one I find the most interesting, and relate to entirely, is the snake. The slithering, creeping snake. It has an elongated body and a large head. It glides and spreads across the ground in sweeping movements. It can launch itself powerfully with a single bite. Snakes are like the wind. They weave and turn aimlessly. They blow where necessary. Nothing escapes their path, and nothing blocks their path. Creatures are afraid of the winding, wily snake. They avoid it at all costs, lest they be snatched and eaten in one aggressive bite! Snakes play in the air, on the ground and in the water. Nothing escapes their all encompassing movement. They dive for food and they rise to eat dragonflies. They can live on any terrain. I am just like the snake - ever present everywhere, no matter whether over land, sea and sky. I cannot be stopped. Sometimes I have to think about where I am going to blow, and how strong I am going to be. Just like the snake rests, he wonders where he will strike next. What will it be, a frog or a butterfly, or even a worm as my next meal? He wonders just as I wonder - where shall I blow the strongest? The desert, the flat land or through the city? The snake wonders about the spider. He can devour the creature and break its web in one swift pounce. I can tear down buildings and trees, disrupt power lines and cables. But sometimes, like the snake, I can just let things be. Sometimes there is no need for my wind. The snake admires new life, just as I do. I provide refreshment for a baby sleeping at night with my cool breeze. The snake enjoys watching the deer scarper and scamper on the grass, playing together. The snake likes to stay close to water, where it feels rejuvenated and young, where it feels the most potential. It admires sea life, and living by the shore. My wind spreads vastly along the coast and provides coolness against the hot sun. I create waves and patterns on the sea like a painting that disappears. My ripples spread but leave no trace. That's me, moving like a snake, weaving in and out of the trees. I'm fresh and clear, warm or cold, as I choose. I feel free and happy, swarming around the oceans and the land, rising and falling. It's like a song to me, and I move with rhythm. I move up and down, left and right, and all directions, like the wily snake. You can't guess which direction I'm headed in, because I'll change. You cannot predict me, because my movement is spontaneous. You can't tell if I'm coming, but you can tell when I'm gone. I enjoy watching the birds swooping in my wind, using it to lift themselves and glide for food. The snake watches too, because some of these birds are strong enough to snatch him in their claws and carry him off to be eaten. The snake is always alert to the sky predators. The snake dreams of having legs and being able to run and walk. I dream of having a form, so I can create more of my force. I would love to see myself as a solid being, just as the snake would, with height and feet. But as I am, I am fine and happy. I can go wherever I want - through windows and doors and through buildings. But I do have a habit of leaving a trail of destruction. I'm strong but clumsy, guided but careless. In that respect, I am not like the snake. He is careful and cunning, and he enters without a sound. Post-Reading Questions What does the wind enjoy comparing itself to? In what ways is the wind just like a snake? What does the snake like to watch when it is not busy? Where do the wind and the snake like to be the most? What do the wind and the snake dream about having? What do you compare yourself to?
author: Hello English

title: Don't Worry, Bee Happy
text: Story Description A bee teaches us the importance of working hard, but not being anxious. He teaches the message of everything is going to bee alright! And the importance of working alongside other creatures, who, despite being different, have the same goals. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Respect ﻿rih-sp-ect ﻿The bees and the flies developed great respect for each other. Enthusiasm ﻿in-th-ew-zee-az-m ﻿The bees and the flies worked together with enthusiasm. Predictable ﻿prih-di-c-tab-ul ﻿The attitude of a bee was very predictable and could be easily guessed. Sworn ﻿sw-or-n ﻿The spider was a sworn enemy of the bees. Bee happy? Why? Bee cause, why not, of course! That's our attitude as bees. I'm happy to be a bee and I'm happy to simply be! I love flowers and collecting their pollen, and taking it back to our hive to convert it into food. It's a simple, repetitive job, but there's so much fun contained in the exploration of food. Look at this beautiful purple flower! I bet it contains a lot of pollen. I'm going to harvest it and transport it back to the hive. Everyone will be impressed with this grab! Uh, oh! One of our sworn enemies, the spider (alongside the fly), has appeared! I foolishly thought I could crack its web, only to find the spider in the middle. The end of the web caught my foot and I got stuck. Luckily I snapped free, and the spider just stared. It looked scared. "Don't worry," I said to it. "I won't harm you. I'm just looking for pollen. Feel free to catch flies and go on your way. But don't eat us bees. Let us bee." The poor spider was terrified that I would take revenge, but I left it alone. I made friends with the spider and then departed, knowing that I had done a good deed for the day. I already had a lot of stories to tell the other bees, and it wasn't even lunch time yet! Speaking of lunch, later on, I got trapped in a plant which closed up. It was a poisonous plant that loved to eat insects and bugs for lunch. I found a fly in there, and we were both stuck. The plant's poisonous liquid rose higher. It was designed to digest us. "We have to find a way out," the fly said. I tried everything, but nothing opened up. It seemed as if we were going to be slowly eaten. But then, the plant opened up and a bunch of flies pulled us free. We were so tired from that day, that by the time we escaped, it was dark, and neither of us could find our way home. We relaxed and talked on a safe patch of grass. We found out we were very similar. We spoke a different language, but we both had the same goals. Furthermore, she was a girl! Suddenly, a swarm of both bees and flies came looking for us, because we didn't arrive back home on time. They found us on the grass and quickly separated us, because we were from opposing tribes. It was strange seeing all the bees and all the flies working together to rescue us. The next day I felt much better and I explained my story to the bees. But they felt embarrassed because I was found alongside a fly. A girl fly! Later that night, I met up with the girl fly again. We talked a lot more, and she was so happy that she lit up inside. It must bee love, I thought. What else could it be? The night was beewildering and I felt I was beecoming very comfortable with the fly. Just then, a bunch of bees arrived and warned us about what we didn't see. We failed to notice the snake, the toad and the giant bug creeping in on us, ready to eat us in one bite. The bees got us out of there. For the second night in a row, we were rescued. "I wonder what happens to us tomorrow night?" I said to the fly, and she blushed. I dreamed about that girl fly, because I'd never met anyone like her before. She couldn't be a bee. Flies were very different. Bees were very predictable, even though they were my bee-loved brothers and sisters. "You can't be with a non-bee because it's not who you're meant to be," said my pal. He was very confusing. He couldn't explain to me in simple terms why I couldn't date a fly. He was unhappy about it, but I just let him bee. "Hey, great news," some of the bees said. "You know the age old war and hatred we had against the flies? Well, thanks to you and your fly friend spending time together, the flies have reached out to us. We're going to be working together from now on, peacefully. Who thought that would ever be?" "I think we should just bee cool about it," I reminded them. And so it was that we set off in a swarm towards the fly grounds, and we greeted their tribe with respect and enthusiasm. Like I said, we were a different species, but we had the same goals, and that brought us together, sealing our bond. And my fly friend? Well, she's still with me. I guess some things are just meant to bee! Post-Reading Questions ﻿Describe what a bee has to do with flowers. Bees and flies both fly in a special group called a s w _ _ _. What did the bee get attached to, and why was he scared? Suddenly, where did the bee get trapped, and who was he with? What happened when the bee and the fly got to know each other? What is the lesson of the story, and what happens to the bees and flies in the end?
author: Hello English

title: Crocodile Tears
text: Story Description Casey is a crocodile who sheds fake tears. He does this for two reasons - to get attention, and to lure his prey in. One day Casey tries to warn he animals of danger, but they don't believe him because of his bad reputation. Casey must find a way to get the animals to trust him again. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Crocodile ﻿crok-oh-dial ﻿The pond was home to a sly crocodile. Seriously ﻿sear-ee-uss-lee ﻿Nobody took the crocodile seriously because he always lied. Apologised ﻿a-pol-uh-jai-z-d ﻿The animals apologised to the crocodile for not believing his story. Reputation ﻿rep-yew-tay-shun ﻿ ﻿The crocodile improved his reputation by telling the truth. Casey was a crocodile who lived in an environment filled with lots of different animals. Casey was always crying, and always feeling upset. But the other animals knew it was fake. Casey would cry for two reasons - to get attention, and to lure his prey into a trap. Naturally, other animals kept their distance from Casey, and they never trusted what they called his 'crocodile tears'. Two boys came to the pond to hunt for fish. Instead of using rods, they fired shots at the fish from their rifles. Nobody except for Casey was around to witness what the boys were doing. The boys walked away with a lot of fish, and Casey felt terrified. He cried more, then found the animals in the distance. "Two boys are shooting fish in the pond," Casey explained. "We don't believe you, or your tears," said the animals. "You always lie and make up stories." Two different boys arrived at the pond with nets. They were trying to catch butterflies. Casey tried to warn the butterflies and the animals, but once again they saw his tears, and they didn't believe him. "Please, you have to come with me," said Casey to the butterflies. "You are in danger. Two boys are hunting you." "We don't believe you," said the butterflies. "The last time you told us we were in danger, you ate one of our friends. You are a sly crocodile." Casey tried to warn the other crocodile, but it was too busy eating a fish. "The boys shot that fish," said Casey, and the crocodile told him to go away. The frogs wanted a piece of the fish, as did the snake and the rat. Casey felt like nobody was listening to him. Casey kept on crying and nobody paid attention, until the tortoise said, "Perhaps we should take him seriously, this one time. He could be telling the truth." "I am telling the truth," said Casey. "Are you being honest?" said one of the butterflies. "Yes," said Casey. "Two boys shot at the fish, then two more came to hunt butterflies with nets. I can show you where it happened." Casey took the butterfly to where he had seen everything take place. When they arrived at the shore, the boys were hunting with their nets, and they were terrified when they saw Casey. The other two boys with rifles ran away. Casey chased them off with his sharp teeth, and the butterfly now believed his story. The butterfly returned to the animals and told them that Casey had been telling the truth. With the dangerous boys gone, a swarm of butterflies returned to the pond. They felt safe enough to stay at the pond once again. The animals apologised to Casey for not believing him, but Casey realised his fault. Had he told the truth before, his words would have been trustworthy. Casey got some of his reputation back, and the animals started to like him again. Post-Reading Questions ﻿Why didn't the animals trust Casey's tears? What were the two reasons for Casey always crying? Who came to shoot fish with rifles? What did the animals do when Casey tried to warn them of the boys? Who was willing to trust that Casey was telling the truth? What do you think is the lesson of the story?
author: Hello English

title: Hyena and Tortoise
text: A long time ago, in the village of Mkosi, there lived a greedy hyena. In a nearby village, lived a timid tortoise. The hyena and the tortoise were friends. Hyena heard that across the great western river lived bees that made delicious honey. These bees traveled once a year, and were away from their hives for a whole week. “We must get that honey while the bees are away,” said Hyena to Tortoise. The tortoise was afraid to go. But he was too timid to refuse. The next morning, the two animals set off for the beehives. The hyena walked very fast but the tortoise dragged behind in fear. They went up a hill, down into a valley and across the plains. Then they crossed the great western river, and walked further. Finally, they saw beehives in trees on a hill. The hyena ran to the trees energetically. The tortoise almost fainted because he was so tired and hungry. When Hyena reached the biggest beehive, he wasted no time. He called to Tortoise, “Quickly, climb up the tree and knock down the hive.” The tortoise struggled slowly up the tree. He knew he could easily slip and fall. This annoyed the hyena, who started yelling at Tortoise. When Tortoise touched the beehive, he heard the buzzing of bees. They were still in their hives! The tortoise was startled and fell out of the tree. The big beehive fell too. The beehive landed on the tortoise. Honey covered him completely so he was hidden! Hyena started to lick up the honey. The bees were not pleased. The bees stung the hyena on every part of his body. Hyena decided to run for his life but the bees followed him. The hyena ran down the hill, through the river, across the plains and into the valley. The bees swarmed around him all the way, stinging him. The tortoise, still under the big beehive, noticed that everything was quiet. The beehive and honey had dried on his back. Soon the tortoise realised that he no longer needed to crawl into a bush to hide. His hard new shell of honey could protect him. The hyena was so tired and full of stings that he fainted before he got home. When he woke up, he discovered that the stings had caused patches in his fur. This is how the tortoise got his hard shell, and the hyena got his patches. Hyena swore that he would never again steal. But the hyena and the tortoise are no longer friends.
author: Alice Mulwa

title: How Ant saved Dove
text: It was a hot summer day in the dry forest. Little Ant had no water for many days. “I need a drop of water, even if it falls from a leaf,” cried Little Ant. But even the dew had dried up. “If I do not have water, I will die,” cried Little Ant. “I must go to the river I heard about.” “The river is full and strong. It will sweep you away,” warned a wise squirrel. But Little Ant was extremely thirsty. “I will die if I don't drink some water.” So, he went to look for the river. He walked past tufts of grass and over dry branches. He walked until he heard water splashing. It was the river! He could hear waves. Little Ant took a long sip of cool water. He was so happy he did not see a wave coming. Little Ant tried to grab some grass floating past him. But he was swept away by the water. “Help me someone. Help me please!” he called. “Quick, climb on,” said White Dove, holding a branch in her beak. “I will stay here until I can thank the dove,” decided Little Ant. “I will wait until she comes back to drink.” One day as he waited, two boys came to the river. They had their slingshots. “There is a big white dove that comes here to drink,” said one boy. “We will have it for supper tonight.” “I cannot let the boys kill White Dove,” thought Little Ant. “But I am so tiny, what can I do?” Just then White Dove flew down from the tree to drink. Little Ant had an idea. He jumped onto one boy's foot. Little Ant bit that boy as hard as he could. The boy jumped. “Ouch!” he shouted. White Dove was startled and flew away to safety. That was how Little Ant thanked White Dove for saving him.
author: Judith  Baker; Kholeka  Mabeta

title: The kingfisher and the sea
text: There once lived a king in the southern part of Okugbe Island. This king had not known pain in his life. Not even for a minute. One morning he was imagining what pain would be like. His head was bowed, “There are so many poor people in my land. How can I feel their pain?” he asked himself. Day and night, he wished he could experience pain just once. Then one night, he dreamed and heard a voice. “I have heard your wishes. You will experience pain,” said the voice. The voice continued, “Build seven large boats that can contain all your wealth and family. Then sail away to the northern part of Okugbe Island.” The king was very happy. Soon, the seven boats were built and ready to sail. The king loaded them with his wealth. The day before the king and his family left, he held a feast. Everyone attended. Leopards, snakes, rabbits, snails, birds and even ants came to the feast. The king addressed the people, “My family and I are going away to the other part of Okugbe Island. We want to feel the pain that other people feel.” People whispered amongst themselves. The elders did not believe him. But who could question the king? So everyone drank and feasted. The next day, the king and his family sailed away. For the first two days, the boats rolled through the waters. The sky was clear, the sea was calm and the trip was a happy one. On the third day, the sea became rough. The sky became cloudy. A great storm came upon them. The boats were overturned. The king was helpless as his wealth and family were lost to the sea. The king alone survived. But he was now a kingfisher bird. Kingfisher flew to the shore. He still hoped to get his family and wealth back from the sea. Kingfisher dived into the sea many times. He was not able to rescue his family or even part of his wealth. “If only I had known, I would have been happy with my life,” he cried silently.
author: Peter Omoko

title: Interconnected
text: Story Description A story about how the internet, something which was small to being with, has grown into a global phenomenon of bringing people together and keeping them interconnected. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Interconnected ﻿in-tur-cun-ect-id ﻿We live in a world where we are interconnected. Landline ﻿land-lie-n ﻿The internet connection used to be made using the landline telephone line. Destination ﻿des-tin-ay-shun ﻿The internet travels to any destination. Transmitted ﻿tran-z-mih-tid ﻿ ﻿Signals are transmitted through the air. Many years ago, a bunch of people got together with a great idea. They wondered what would happen if the world was interconnected by a global network. Then we could share information, knowledge and wisdom with anyone we wanted. It was an idea that would change the world and how we communicated with each other forever. The internet became like a huge transport network. Packets of date are sent through wires at the speed of light. They are opened in order at their destination, and gradually a file downloads. Using the map, from Switzerland, the data can travel to Germany then to Poland and Ukraine, before it reaches Russia. It can travel in any direction. The internet used to require a dial up modem. Your computer would connect to the internet via telephone lines, connect to a server which took a couple of minutes to do, and then you would gain access. If someone picked up the landline telephone, you would get disconnected! Fast forward to the present day. Your connection is wireless and it is transmitted through the air to your phone or PC. Connections are super fast and spread wide across the country. Internet is now available even in remote areas. The super servers and big computers make it possible for the internet to go to your home computer, laptop, your phone in your bag, and enables you to listen to music, and lets you remember to switch off your phone in the cinema! Do you remember the first time you used the internet? It was a strange and exciting experience, knowing that you were connected to the entire world in an instant. The phrase 'world wide web' came from the concept that the internet represents a huge spiders web, connecting every site, archive, document, file, photo, video and audio file together over one super massive network. The amount of content on the web is incalculable, meaning you cannot estimate just how much information is online. In the future, we will have yet more ways of communicating. With advances in technology, who knows how we might view the internet? Perhaps we will no longer require touch screen devices when the internet covers the world. Our children are born into a developed world with technology constantly advancing and changing. In such a world, it is difficult to keep up. With technology, things used to move gradually. Now, we must educate our children so that they are not left behind, as technology accelerates, and the world changes. The internet is now the main source of our entertainment. Sites and apps create new ways we can sing, dance, share fun, play sports and post videos of pets. We can even reach the internet from great heights and long distances from civilisation. You can post a picture from a mountain top, or a lake in the wilderness. The internet is spread so far and wide, and it is so accessible, that it is likely to always be with us. Post-Reading Questions How was an internet connection made before Wi-Fi? Data is sent and received in p _ _ _ _ _ _. True or false? The internet is available in a lot of remote areas. Describe the experience of using the internet for the first time. Why is it called the world wide web? What do you think of the internet?
author: Hello English

title: Grandfather's Allotment
text: Story Description Danny helps his grandfather look after his allotment, and his grandfather teaches him about beetles, insects, and all types of things found in the garden. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Allotment ﻿a-lot-mun-t ﻿Danny's grandfather kept an allotment that grew with vegetables and herbs. Challenge ﻿cha-lin-j ﻿Danny saw catching beetles as a challenge. Beetles ﻿bee-tul-s ﻿There were many beetles, both on the allotment and inside the house. Equipment﻿ ﻿ih-kwip-mun-t ﻿Danny needed to use his grandfather's equipment to catch the beetles. "I'm getting too old to maintain this allotment," said Danny's grandfather. "My legs are not what they used to be." "You mean they used to be ears?" asked Danny. "Ha, ha! No, I mean my legs are very old and tired at my age. I need someone younger with more energy than me to maintain it. Someone like you, Danny. Are you up for the challenge of learning?" Danny felt delighted that his grandfather had chosen him to look after the allotment. "I have to catch some beetles," said Danny's grandfather. "But I'm too slow and they easily get away from me. No matter how hard I try, the beetles escape." "I'll help you catch the beetles, granddad," said Danny. "I'm really fast and very sneaky. They won't see me coming for them." "I admire your spirit," said Danny's grandfather. "But first you need the right equipment." "I'll catch as many beetles as I can, and you can teach me how to look after the allotment," said Danny. "Well, there's a lot for you to learn," said Danny's grandfather. "How long are you willing to stick around?" Danny went off to learn about beetles, while his grandfather walked around the allotment, checking on the vegetables and the herbs. Very soon he sat down and took a nap. Meanwhile indoors, Danny found several bugs on the wall while he was watching TV. He captured them inside a jar and then went back outside to hunt for more. He found his grandfather's fishing net, and he swiped to and fro, catching more beetles and bugs that were buzzing above the flowers. Danny crept very slowly across the ground, getting on his hands and knees and getting covered in mud and dust. He spied a lone beetle crawling alone, and he reached out to grab it gently, placing it in the jar. To find more beetles and bugs, Danny used his grandfather's magnifying glass to scour the ground and hunt for more. He saw many more hiding under tree trunks and in bushes, and he was able to use the net to collect more. Soon, Danny had a jar filled with beetles. "Look, granddad!" said Danny, presenting the jar of bugs and beetles to his grandfather. "This is excellent work," said Danny's grandfather. "Well done. And you used my fishing net and magnifying glass to hunt for them! You are an intelligent boy. I have a short nap and look what happens. You've solved my problem!" Every day, Danny learned a little bit more about gardening, until he had the sufficient skills and he was ready to help his grandfather look after the allotment. Post-Reading Questions Why does Danny's grandfather need help with the allotment? What does Danny's grandfather ask him to collect? What does Danny's grandfather do while Danny looks for beetles? What three items does Danny use to catch the beetles? What does Danny's grandfather say about him when he receives the jar? Talk about an outdoor activity that you enjoy.
author: Hello English

title: The Countryside Song
text: Story Description A rhyme about a boy who lives in a loving and joyful community, where every day presents a new adventure to him and the opportunity to have fun. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Barking ﻿b-ar-king ﻿The dog was barking loudly. Atmosphere ﻿at-muss-fear ﻿The atmosphere was welcoming and relaxed. Silence ﻿sigh-lun-ss ﻿There was silence at nighttime. Memento ﻿meh-men-toe ﻿ ﻿They took a picture as a memento of the day. Timmy lives in the country, Goes to visit his fun tree, Where he finds a monkey, Dances with a donkey, Runs about, Jumps and shouts, Happy and joyful and free. Timmy sees the tree from far away, The dog is barking and wants to play, Let's climb to the top, I'll run and you hop, We can play fetch, sit and stay. There goes the donkey with its blonde hair, As the picnic eating family sees him, The peaceful atmosphere surrounds there, The dog steals a sandwich from the food bin. Timmy's best friend waves hello, While Timmy eats his breakfast, He eats quickly and then goes, I think he ate a little too fast! Friends hug and animals dance, The birds squawk above, The donkey brays and the monkey chants, He's pointing that he's seen a dove. The family goes out together, Everyone walks in a line, The father thinks he is clever, The baby wants to try and climb. The sea looks warm for swimming, The dog leaps in the pool, Everyone is winning, Paddling and keeping cool. Let's have a photo, Everyone squeeze in together, A lasting memento, That we can cherish forever. That was the one when, Timmy put his finger over the lens! Baby can barely stand, But he can do a handstand, Watch him wobble, He falls, gets up and hobbles, They all play in the sand. What a fun time we had, A wonderful day out, I feel so glad, That I want to shout. And the next day will bring about, More joy and fun to sing about. Everyone rests through the night, Silence through the skies, The stars are out and bright, With the dancing fireflies. Timmy dreams of all the things, He hopes tomorrow brings. Post-Reading Questions ﻿ Where does Timmy play at the beginning of the story? What does the dog do during the picnic? Who comes to see Timmy while he is eating his breakfast? What do they jump into to keep cool? Timmy takes a photo but what mistake does he make? Describe your perfect day.
author: Hello English

title: The Storm
text: Story Description A tale of a devastating storm that burns forests and tortures the land, until the people learn how to rebuild after the storm has gone. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Surge ﻿sur-j ﻿The strong storm caused a surge in the sea, creating tall waves. Salvaged ﻿sal-vij-d ﻿The family salvaged what they could during the storm. Mischief ﻿miss-chee-f ﻿The storm wreaked havoc and mischief across the land. Awkward ﻿or-k-wur-d ﻿It was an awkward experience trying to walk through the strong winds. The storm caused a surge in heat. The heat caused the air to be hot. The hot air sparked fires amongst the trees. The animals fled the blaze and headed for the hills. The birds took flight from the branches and salvaged what they could, taking their home with them. The storm was sharp and aggressive. It blew trees sideways. The strongest trunks were uprooted and they toppled over. Leaves flew off their branches. The whole ground shook with the force of the storm. The storm clouds crept in and showed their animal faces. The snake, the bull and the God of mischief. The people tried to fight the wind but it was too fierce. They dropped the foods they carried and were forced away from the land. Two young boys stuck on a rock defended themselves from the wind. They encountered the flying leaves and twigs, and all kinds of debris from the forest. They took slow steps forward to descend the awkward rock. A brother and sister hid in the long grass with the fruits, leaning into the storm as it blew upon them. They wondered when it would end, or if it would get stronger. They couldn't have prepared for such an event, as nobody saw it coming. The storm battered the local villages and sent people and material flying. One family held on for their lives as the relentless storm tried to carry them away. The winds had a great effect on the sea. They transformed the tranquil surface into violent thrashing waves that were taller than boats. Some boats like this one were washed all the way to the shore, due to the sheer strength of the sea. A group of people on a yacht were heading home when the waves attacked. They rose so high that they pushed the yacht in all directions, and nobody knew where they were going. The yacht went underwater and rose to the surface. After a while, the people saw land, and they were grateful to be home. Very slowly, the storm began to drift off. The winds lightened and only the grass swayed. The people returned from hiding in their homes, and started rebuilding what they had lost. The fires were extinguished and the animals returned to their habitats. The birds flew back, but their homes were destroyed in the fires. Luckily, they found some other trees that were undisturbed, and they were able to build new nests. Storms, surges and heat are all unpredictable, and sometimes there is nothing we can do except ride them out. After they happen, we often remember what is most important to us. Our homes can be destroyed, but families and friendships cannot be split apart. Post-Reading Questions What caused the forest to burn, and what did the animals do? How did the two boys get off the big rock? What happened to the waves in the sea with the strong wind? What happened to the yacht that was in the sea? How big were the waves? Name another natural disaster.
author: Hello English

title: Bella's way home
text: When Karina was done playing with her friends, she noticed that Bella was no where to be seen.... Karina thought that bella had gone back home, so she continued playing.Karina got tired of playing in the park.She did not know that Bella had gone out of the city. Then she reached home but she could not find Bella...…….. K arina went to her mom crying, she told her mom whatever happened in the park.... Karina got very scared, she started thinking about the time when Bella and she used to play together.. Karina started praying,that Bella would be found sooooon. Karina asked her dad if he had any idea to find Bella Dad had a great idea "lets make posters and spread the news in the newspaper that will help.. maybe somebody has seen her.. A new day arrived.... Karina and her mom went to the market. on the way Karina was singing Bella's favourite song and Bella was there only but Karina did not notice and kept singing Bella's favourite song Bella came running to Karina and jumped on her.. Finaly Karina found Bella and Bella found Karina.... AND SINCE THEN KARINA ALWAYS TOOK CARE OF BELLA …. THE END!
author: Aarna Agarwal
illustrator: Anupam Arunachalam; Lante Collier; Manobendro Golder; minakshi singh; Rishi Anu; Santosh Pujari; Sharanya Singh

title: Dogs are Best Friends Too
text: Max loved his owner Bill. Max got to go on fun trips with Bill. One day while walking with Bill, Max met two other dogs named Shelly and Ben. Then Ben introduced him to another friend Toby. Toby was a nice dog. Max was glad to have more best friends that he met on his walk with Bill.
author: Jessica Hutchins

title: Washing Our Clothes
text: Story Description A look into the lives of people who live together in a close community. Children play in the street while adults wash their clothes. Everyone tries their best to help out. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Attention ﻿a-ten-shun ﻿The cat wants attention when its owner is busy. Pantry ﻿pan-tree ﻿Sam's sister gets things from the pantry to help outside. Properly ﻿proh-pur-lee ﻿Sam observes how his mother and father wash their clothes properly. Fragrance ﻿fray-grun-ss ﻿Sam enjoys the fragrance of a freshly cleaned towel. Everyday, we wash our clothes outside. We enjoy it because it gives us the chance to play with the buckets and dance in the puddles. All of the village washes their clothes this way. Auntie hangs up her bedsheets and rugs to dry in the warm air. The birds like to perch on the roof and watch her work. While she waits for her clothes and sheets to dry, the neighbour plays with her son and feeds him. He is energetic and always happy, smiling and laughing. Mama uses a bucket of warm water and soap to wash our clothes. While she works, our cat Eddy meows at her for attention. He likes to distract her when she is busy. My sister likes to help out by getting the things that Mama and Papa need for washing. She collects buckets from the pantry, and pots and pans for cooking. I play with my brother Liam. That's me, Sam, in the middle, while my brother tries to wash my face with a sponge. I clean the sheets while Auntie hangs our clothes on a line. When the washing is almost one, the neighbours chat and we jump around having fun. Sometimes we knock things over like buckets and bottles, and we get into trouble. As a family, we all work together to get the washing done. Papa helps Mama with the simple stuff. He isn't as good as her when it comes to cleaning, and she often reminds him to do it properly! Mama taught Papa how to sew. He wanted to repair his own clothes and he is really enthusiastic about his new skill. He always shows Liam and I how to sew a button on to a shirt. Our friend's parents are always talking and laughing in the street, especially when they are washing their clothes. Their space is a bit smaller than ours, but they still seem happy with what they have. The woman down the street likes to daydream when she washes her clothes. I often wonder what she thinks about. I asked her and she told me she dreams about mangos. Her dog does it as well, but he dreams about playing with toys. When the washing is done and dried, everything smells so great and fresh! I like to run around with my clean towel and smell the fragrance. It's some kind of flower. I'm not sure what Mama puts into the cleaning mixture. Then we do the washing all over again at the weekend! Post-Reading Questions ﻿ ﻿Where do Sam and his family wash their clothes? Describe the surroundings where Sam lives. Who hangs her bedsheets and rugs while a bird watches? Why do Sam and Liam sometimes get into trouble? What did Sam's father learn as a new skill? Describe how your clothes are washed.
author: Hello English

title: The Flight of A Lifetime
text: Story Description A girl dreams of becoming a pilot, inspired by Amelia Earnhart - the first woman to fly across the Atlantic Ocean solo. She works hard on her journey to achieving her dreams, while a boy has always wanted to fly on a big plane. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Fascinated fass-in-ay-tid The boy was absolutely fascinated by aeroplanes. Professional pruh-fesh-un-ul The girl dreamed of becoming a professional pilot. Commercial com-ur-sh-ul She wanted to fly commercial planes that carried passengers. Civilian siv-ill-ee-un There are two types of aircraft - military, and civilian for the public. A young girl had a dream. She wanted to be a professional pilot one day. She had read all about Amelia Earhart - the first woman to fly across the Atlantic Ocean solo, and she was fascinated by her. She built toy aeroplanes, and even though they didn't work, she knew that one day she would understand aeroplanes and be able to pilot them. A young boy was so excited about flying. He had never been in an aeroplane before. He had not experienced the sensations of taking off, cruising and landing. He held his boarding pass and waited as everyone got inside the cabin. The young girl used to dress up as an astronaut, making her own space suit and helmet out of a bicycle helmet, a bin bag, plastic rings and plastic bags. She studied the night skies and she memorised the constellations. She used run around outside with paper aeroplanes. They flew and glided through the air for a while, but they were nothing compared to a real fighter jet or commercial aircraft. The boy often dreamed of piloting a really fast plane, like the kind you can fly upside down. He fantasised about flying a military fighter jet over the Eiffel Tower, seeing the rest of Paris below. As she got older, the girl dreamed of soaring in the skies alongside a big Boeing jet, or an Airbus, helping the plane glide through the sky at high speeds. And meanwhile, the boy enjoyed his flight as the plane cruised. His mother read a magazine, while the boy kept looking at the sky and the ground, enthralled and fascinated. They had gone through airport security and it had taken a while, because the airport had to make sure everyone was safe. The boy went through the metal detector and his bags went through the scanner, to make sure there were no dangerous objects inside. The girl stayed up all night studying aircraft, from engineering to aerodynamics, to system controls and the design and the makes of aircraft. She studied intensely, memorising even the small details. The boy had woken up that morning, studying his papers on aeroplanes, and he realised he was going on holiday. He was so excited to be flying in a plane, and he collected his tickets and got ready to go to the airport. For most of the journey, he just looked outside the window, seeing the incredible shapes of the clouds, other planes passing in the far distance, feeling the turbulence and seeing buildings on the ground. He couldn't believe just how high up he was. He couldn't believe he was flying. It was unreal. The girl thought about Amelia Earhart, who waved down to her from her old fashioned aircraft. If Amelia could make it, then so could she, she thought. The boy and his mother landed at their destination, and they took a while to watch the aircraft taking off and landing before they left. Every time watching a plane arrive and depart was an incredible sight. The girl realised her dream and made it come true. All the years of studying and preparation paid off, as she took the pilot's seat after many hundreds of hours of training. She flew the plane with the boy and his mother aboard. She was officially a captain, and the plane belonged to her. The boy watched the girl pilot take off, and wow, it was so loud and fast. He could not wait to fly again. This time he would sit at the front of the aircraft, and hopefully, if he was allowed to, he could meet the captain and the co-pilot! Post-Reading Questions Which famous﻿ woman inspired the girl to become a pilot? What was the boy holding on to when he prepared to board the plane? What did the girl make out of plastic bags and household items? The boy spent most of the time on the plane doing one thing. What was it? What did the girl eventually become after lots of studying and practice? If you could become anything, what would it be?
author: Hello English

title: Storytelling Is Fun
text: Story Description A girl called Lorrie sees a storytelling woman in town who captures her imagination. Lorrie becomes interested in telling her own stories as the town gets inspired by the woman. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Storyteller ﻿store-ee-tell-ur ﻿The woman storyteller captured everyone's attention. Captivated ﻿cap-tiv-ay-tid ﻿The little girl was captivated by the woman's stories. Inspiration ﻿in-spih-ray-shun ﻿The woman storyteller was an inspiration to the little girl. Artistic ﻿are-tiss-tic ﻿People started to express their artistic and imaginative sides. One day there was a woman sitting in the park. She was telling stories to the children about far away lands, magical adventures, great monsters, wizards and ghosts. The children sat by her for hours listening to her tales, and even some adults joined the group, captivated by the stories and her acting. When the story time finished, one little girl remained behind. She wanted to speak to the woman. Her name was Lorrie and she shook the woman's hand. "How can I be like you?" said Lorrie. "I love your stories." "You want to be a storyteller?" said the woman. "It's a very difficult job." "I believe that I can tell good stories, and get people's attention." "Let's sit down and I'll tell you what you need to become a great storyteller," said the woman. "First, you need to capture your own imagination," said the woman. "You need to be willing to say yes to any idea that comes, no matter how wild or crazy it may seem. Then you must develop characters, and a great plot, and make suspense, fear, excitement, joy, happiness, sadness, anger, revenge, desire - all of these things. You must draw these from your heart, from your inner most being, and bring them to life in the world." Lorrie went away with good advice and a lot of information. "I'm going to become a storyteller," Lorrie started telling her busy mother and father. "I'll write the best stories in the world, and I'll narrate them to crowds. People from all over will come to listen to my amazing stories." "If you really want to do this," said Lorrie's mother and father, "then you must read books, see films, and fill your mind with information. Then, once you have your inspiration, you must write and read your stories." "I understand," said Lorrie's teacher, after hearing her story about how she wanted to become the world's greatest storyteller. "First you must focus on your education. Learn maths, science and languages, and then find a way to support yourself while you pursue this dream. This is the sensible thing to do. Don't spend money you don't have." The storyteller woman had left her mark on the town. It seemed as if magic flowed everywhere people went. There was colour, laughter, there were tales and there were good times. People suddenly had their own stories to tell, and they weaved them together like the storyteller woman did. Lorrie discovered that her friends had been infected with the magic brought to the town. Now they were weaving their own colourful, artistic worlds with creatures, buildings, characters and mythical beings. Lorrie shared her own adventures she had invented with them. "The woman is coming back to our town," Lorrie said excitedly to her brother and to her neighbours. "Let's all go and see her. I want to narrate my stories to the crowd." The woman told her stories and allowed Lorrie to play out some of the parts, then she gave Lorrie the chance to tell her stories. The crowd was enthralled and praised both of them. "This is your first step into a bigger world," said the woman. "You must practice and write each day to maintain your skill. And always read. Keep reading." Lorrie was now on the right path. Post-Reading Questions ﻿There was a woman in the park. Why were people interested in her? After Lorrie saw the storyteller, what did she want to do? How did Lorrie's maths teacher respond to her wanting to be a storyteller? How had the storyteller woman changed the town? When Lorrie heard the storyteller was returning, what did she ask to do? Name a special skill or talent you want to develop.

title: Who Stole Bhaiya's Smile?
text: Chiru and Bhaiya used to play all the time. They’d explore caves under the staircase and fight the aliens on the mango tree in the backyard. Bhaiya always made Chiru laugh. “Mangasura is from Mars and she is here to destroy your house! Ha-ha!” Bhaiya roared. “Aaaah! I will trap and gobble up Mangasura. Bahahahaha!” Chiru said. But it’s been a long time since Chiru and Bhaiya have played together. Bhaiya doesn’t like playing with anyone these days! “Why don’t you feel like playing?” Chiru yells at Bhaiya. “I don’t want to," Bhaiya says. "I am stuck with this big monster on my back.” Chiru names the monster Dukduk. “Dukduk must be mean and grumpy,” Chiru thinks. “It feels like he's swallowed up Bhaiya’s smile.” Dukduk always seems to be with Bhaiya. “Tell your monster to go away! I don’t like him,” Chiru says. Sometimes, Dukduk grows bigger than a truck. Bhaiya gets angry about everything on those days. He even chews his food angrily! Mama thinks she knows how to make Bhaiya feel better. “You should go out for a walk. The fresh air will do you good,” Mama says. On other days Dukduk seems to be holding on to Bhaiya. He doesn’t even let Bhaiya get out of bed. Papa keeps asking Bhaiya about his mood and telling him how to fix it. “What’s wrong, why aren’t you eating your food?” Papa says. “Eat well and your problem will go away.” There are days when Dukduk is small and floats around like a kite. Then Bhaiya gets out of bed and plays with Chiru. But he gets tired very fast. Nani and Nana tell Bhaiya what is wrong with him. “Arre, you kids and your problems. In my day, we were tougher!” Nani says. “You are just too distracted,” Nana says. “It’s all in your head. You just have to put your mind to it and you will snap out of it,” everyone says. “I will try,” Bhaiya says. “It isn’t that easy.” Chiru tries distracting Bhaiya. “Look at this new book, Bhaiya! Aren’t the pictures pretty?" Chiru says. “They are okay, Chiru.” Bhaiya says. “Bhaiya, have you seen the new train set?” Chiru squeals. “Hmm, nice,” Bhaiya says. “Mangasura is here! Run, Bhaiya,” Chiru yells. “Not now, Chiru. I don’t want to play,” Bhaiya says. “Dukduk is making him sad and angry,” Chiru thinks. She throws a pillow at Dukduk. “Take that, you horrible thing! Get away from Bhaiya. G ive back his smile.” It is Bhaiya’s birthday today. Chiru has baked a cake. “Thank you, Chiru,” Bhaiya smiles. Chiru frowns. Bhaiya’s smile is very different these days. Chiru sits next to Bhaiya. “Is your new friend making you unhappy?” Bhaiya nods. “I feel like being happy, but it’s hard work on most days,” Bhaiya explains. “How long do you think your friend will stay?” Chiru asks. “I don’t know,” says Bhaiya. “It’s okay,” Chiru says. “We can play whenever you feel like.” Bhaiya smiles his old smile. Dukduk becomes smaller. Now Bhaiya is even getting help from Doctor Aunty. Dukduk is still there. On some rare days, he is big. Chiru waits for them to pass. M ostly, Dukduk is small, and on those days Bhaiya likes to play. Dukduk = Depression When you break your arm or have a cough, you take medicine to feel better. The brain, like any other organ, can get hurt and may need help to heal. Sometimes we feel sad. We cry, we sulk and we get angry, but the mood passes and we feel better. It is normal to feel sad. Some of us have a sadness that stays for a long time. The brain helps us think, act and feel. When we are sad all the time, it changes our behaviour. We don’t feel like doing anything. It makes us feel unwanted. It may feel like a big monster is sitting on you. It even feels like the monster will never go away. This monster is called depression. When you see someone who is sad for no reason, talk to them. Tell them that you may not understand how it feels, but you can see it is hard and you would like to help. If you feel that way, tell your family and friends. It also helps to talk to someone like a psychologist or psychiatrist.
author: Sanjana  Kapur

title: A Great Invention
text: Story Description Gemma is a little girl who enjoys books about mechanics and engineering. She tries to come up with a way to switch on the cooker without touching it, so she designs a way to make it activate itself, by using a set of household objects. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Mechanics ﻿muh-can-ik-s ﻿Gemma took an interest in mechanics. Experiment ﻿ex-peh-rih-ment ﻿ ﻿ ﻿She planned an experiment in the kitchen. ﻿ ﻿Utensils ﻿you-ten-sil-s ﻿Gemma used utensils in her experiment. Patiently ﻿pay-shun-t-lee ﻿ ﻿She waited patiently for the soup to cook. Gemma enjoyed reading books on how to design new things. She enjoyed engineering and mechanics, and began to understand how things work. She decided to come up with a way to switch on the cooker, without touching the cooker. She would invent something to make it activate itself. "The kitchen is ready for your experiment," said Gemma's mother. "Please don't set fire to anything. And don't do anything dangerous, ok?" "I won't," said Gemma. Gemma took over the kitchen and began placing everything in its correct position for the experiment. She used tomatoes and potatoes, and a rolling pin to rest against the cooker switch. Gemma placed a ladle in position on the shelf, completing the next part of the experiment. Alongside the ladle, Gemma placed spoons and a ball. "What are you doing?" asked Gemma's mother. "You'll see," said Gemma. "I'd rather now know. Don't break any of my expensive utensils." Gemma set the ball on the shelf. She watched with glee as the ball started rolling towards the spoons. She couldn't wait to see what would happen. The ball struck the spoons, pushing them into each other and the ladle, causing them to fall, and the ladle to collapse off the shelf. The ladle fell and hit the end potato, and the end potato rolled and hit the other two. The last potato pushed against the tomatoes, which then rolled and hit the rolling pin, pushing the cooker switch on. "Whoopee!" Gemma cheered, and her mother clapped her hands. "It worked! I found a way to turn the cooker on without touching it." Gemma then waited patiently as her soup cooked in the pot. "And now to study and prepare my next experiment," said Gemma. "Maybe I can design a way to prepare dinner without cutting the vegetables!" Post-Reading Questions What does Gemma take an interest in? Where does her experiment take place? What kind of objects does Gemma use in her experiment? What is the aim of Gemma's experiment? Describe how the experiment works, and what happens at the end. After her test works, what does Gemma plan to do next?

title: The Most Valuable Treasure
text: Story Description Max the dog wakes up one night to find other animals that are already awake. He goes in search of the farmyard treasure, asking different animals where it could be, when he eventually realises where the most valuable treasure really is. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Twinkling ﻿twin-k-ling ﻿The stars were twinkling in the night sky. Valuable ﻿val-yew-a-bul ﻿The most valuable treasure is inside you. Treasure ﻿tre-zh-yur ﻿Max searched for the farmyard treasure. Peacefully ﻿pea-ss-full-ee ﻿He slept peacefully under the stars. Max was sleeping next to his mother one night, when suddenly a big noise jolted him awake. He couldn't get back to sleep, so he decided to get up and go for a walk. "Wow, the moon is so bright and all of the stars are twinkling," said Max, as he played by himself, leaping around the yard and looking up. He looked around and noticed that some animals were awake. "I wonder why they don't sleep at night?" he said. "What are you doing up, Max?" said a grasshopper. "I thought you would be sleeping." "A big noise woke me up," said Max. "I'm looking for something to do to tire me out." "Well, I know something that will make you tired," said the grasshopper. "Have you heard of the farmyard treasure? It's the most valuable treasure you can find, and it's buried somewhere here at the farm." "Wow, I have to find it!" said Max. "Max, why are you up so late?" said the vampire bat. "Dogs sleep at night." "I'm looking for the farmyard treasure. Mr. Grasshopper said it's the most valuable treasure that you'll ever find." "Ah," said the bat. "Then you really have to dig deep to find it. I have heard it is buried so deep that it takes a long time to find. I would suggest you talk to the firefly. She can help you more." "Wow, thanks, Mr. Bat!" said Max, before he skipped along. "Max, what are you doing around here?" said the firefly. "I'm searching for the farmyard treasure," said Max. "But I don't know where to start." "Then you had better start looking close. It's not as far away as you think. That's all I know, but if you meet a fox, maybe he can tell you more." "Thanks, Miss Firefly! You're a great help!" said Max, before he continued on his way. "Oh, it's you, Max!" said a very shocked and surprised fox. "I thought you were a rabbit. What are you doing over here?" "I'm looking for the farmyard treasure, and Miss Firefly said you could help me." "Indeed I can, Max. The treasure is so close, that no matter how far and wide you search, you can never be any closer or further away from it. That's what I know. But if you see an owl, she can help you more." "Thanks, Mr. Fox!" said Max, carrying on. Soon, Max saw an owl holding a rat. "Max, you're not asleep?" said the owl. "No, I'm looking for the farmyard treasure, and Mr. Fox said I'm always close to it." "He's right," said the owl. "In fact, one could say you can search beneath your feet, for wherever you stand, there it is. If you go to the lake, it is by the lake. If you go to the field, it is in the field." "I'm still confused," said Max. Suddenly, the rest of the animals arrived, all laughing. "What are you laughing about?" said Max. "Didn't you get it, Max?" said the owl. "The greatest treasure, the farmyard treasure, is hidden deep inside you. When you discover that your true being, the joy inside you, is the greatest treasure you can have, and that nothing from the world can profit you, then you are free. You have found the greatest riches in life." Max understood and jumped for joy. "Where did you go?" said Max's mother. "I found the farmyard treasure," said Max. "Oh, really? And what did you discover about the treasure?" "That it's inside me. I am the treasure. The joy and happiness inside me is the greatest gift anyone can share." Max's mother gave him a kiss and they both slept peacefully through the rest of the night. Post-Reading Questions What woke Max in the middle of the night? Which farmyard creature told Max about the mysterious farmyard treasure? What did the firefly say to Max about the treasure? Which animal told Max to look beneath his feet? What did Max discover about the treasure, and why did he find it funny? What is the greatest treasure to you?
author: Hello English

title: Gupta the Champion
text: Story Description Gupta is a princess who wants to become the lifting champion of India. She must train well and have a good diet in order to be strong enough to win. Gupta competes in a competition where the strongest people in India try to win the weightlifting trophy, and become the strongest person in India. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Competition com-pur-tish-un Gupta trains for her upcoming competition. Weightlifting wey-t-lift-ing The competition is about weightlifting. Preparation prep-ur-ay-shun Gupta must do lots of preparation if she wants to win. Training tray-ning The training involves lifting very heavy objects. Gupta was a princess, and she was the daughter of the king and the queen of the region. Gupta was very strong - the toughest in her entire family - and she enjoyed lifting heavy things and proving her strength. One day, Gupta decided to compete in the All-India weightlifting competition, to show who was the strongest person in India. Her mother started feeding her lots of protein such as chicken and eggs, in preparation for the competition. Gupta had a target weight. She needed to weigh the same as a hundred gold bars. She sat at one end of the scale, but she found that she did not weigh enough. Gupta needed to get bigger and fatter to be able to compete and win the competition, otherwise she would not be able to lift heavier things. So Gupta trained more each day, lifting slightly heavier things until she put on that weight. Her arms and legs became enormous. She could feel her core strength. It was very impressive. Very soon, Gupta could lift the fattest man in the land - Raj. And Raj was amazed with how Gupta lifted him off the ground with such ease. She was nearly ready to be a competitor. Gupta lifted puppies, wooden objects, and heavy antique chests to develop her small flinch muscles. These smaller muscles supported her main ones, and made her stronger. For her final preparations, Gupta climbed rocks with her bare hands, sometimes using only her fingers. To increase her stamina, she swam daily, and kept eating big chickens to maintain her weight and muscle mass. The contest began and the strongest from all around India came to the kingdom to compete. Gupta lifted and dragged massive tree logs. Another woman squatted huge logs, a man raised an expensive chest, and another man carried a chest filled with jewellery. The competition was close and fierce. The final deciding round arrived. None of the competitors could lift the golden throne. The person who could lift the throne the best, would win the competition, and take home the trophy. It was down to Gupta. She had lifted Raj, but never anything else so heavy before. She took the stance and prepared to lift the chair. Gupta squatted and pushed upwards with all of her might, trying to raise the throne above the ground. For a moment, she froze and wobbled, and then she lifted her legs with the last of her strength, and raised the throne high into the air. Gupta received the trophy and won the competition! All the months of preparation and training got her through the final lift, and she decided she would return the next year to defend her title, as the strongest person in India. Post-Reading Questions Why does Gupta train by lifting heavy objects? What is Gupta trying to win by entering the weightlifting competition? How does Gupta prepare for the competition? Describe Gupta's a ttitude and behaviour. How does Gupta finally win the competition? What kind of attitude do you think is required to win something?
author: Hello English

title: Don't Tread On Us! Part 1
text: Story Description Three friends - Steve, Dave and Patricia, go on a camping trip. While playing cricket, they find snakes hiding in the grass. When Steve is about to attack them, the snakes try to persuade the friends that they are friendly and welcoming. But then, later, a girl gets bitten, bringing the snake's reputations into dispute. Are they really safe? Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Accidentally ﻿ak-sid-ent-a-lee ﻿The kids accidentally hit the ball into the long grass. Needlessly ﻿need-luss-lee ﻿Sometimes the snake will needlessly bite. Responsibility ﻿riss-pon-sih-bill-it-ee ﻿Snakes have a big responsibility not to bite people. Hazardous ﻿haz-ur-duss ﻿ ﻿Snakes are hazardous because their bites are poisonous. Snakes are incredible creatures. They spring up out of nowhere and surprise you. Snakes can leap out of a pond and eat frogs. They snatch worms from the mud. They sneak up on birds from a tree branch. They eat other little snakes and they take mice from the grass. They really are sneaky, silent creatures. One day three kids - Dave, Steve (carrying a bat) and Patricia were playing cricket when they lost their ball in a patch of long grass. When they searched for it, they found a snake hiding in the growth. Steve raised his bat, ready to whack the snake. The snake panicked. It was terrified of the people. "Just a minute," said one of the snakes. "You can't just go and whack my friend around the head with your bat. We're a peaceful species. You don't need to kill us." "I'm not concerned," said the other snake. "They were just reacting like scared people do. I don't blame them for being terrified. I was scared of them too." "Everything's ok," said the first snake. "I'm Tony, and this is my friend Rob who you were about to squash." The three people laughed because the snakes were so kind. "What are you doing?" said a third snake. "You can't associate with people." "We're just having a friendly conversation," said Tony. "Anyway, what are you doing here?" said Rob. "We're camping out for a few days," said Steve. "I'm Steve and this is Patricia and Dave. We're friends." "Delighted to meet you all," said Tony. "We won't harm you." That night, Tony and Patricia heard something moving around in the grass. Concerned about more snakes, they went out searching with their torches. They came across Tony and Rob, who were just hanging around and talking. "No need to be worried," they said. "We won't harm you." Rob had had a dodgy past. He once bits someone's foot for accidentally treading on him. But Rob learned his lesson - to not react and needlessly bite people. With his poisonous bite, he could do a lot of harm to beings, and that was a great burden as well as a big responsibility. He knew just how hazardous and alarming he was. Soon many of the snakes joined the group, and when Steve, Dave and Patricia played cricket again, they found more snakes had turned up. The snakes were interested in the new people. As the group carried out their chores, sometimes Tony and Rob would check on them, to make sure they were safe, and that no dodgy snakes were around. The group felt comfortable having their snake friends visit. Then, in the night, word of a snake bite travelled around. A girl was taken to hospital after being bitten in the middle of the night. Geoffrey the culprit claimed it was accidental. He had been chasing a rat when he thought one of the human girls was going to grab him, so in self-defence, he bit her. Who knows what would happen next? Find out in part two... Post-Reading Questions What kind of animals do snakes hunt and eat? When they were playing cricket, what did Steve and his friends hit the ball into? When looking for their ball, what did Steve find and how did he react? What did Tony and Rob try to convince the people about? When was the last time that Rob bit someone? What do you think will happen after the girl gets bitten?
author: Hello English

title: Don't Tread On Us! Part 2
text: Story Description In part two of the story, the snakes ask Geoffrey why he bit the girl, while Dave, Steve and Patricia are updated on the girl's condition in hospital. The snakes also go into their background to explain their past. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Discharged diss-char-j-d The girl was well again so she was discharged from hospital. Declaring dih-cl-air-ing The doctors were declaring that the girl was fine. ﻿Poisonous ﻿poy-zun-uss ﻿Geoffrey the snake had poisonous fangs. Untrustworthy ﻿un-truss-t-wur-th-ee ﻿Geoffrey's friend Oik lied a lot, so he was untrustworthy. In the first part, Dave, Patricia and Steve had been playing cricket, when the ball was hit far and into long grass. The group searched for the ball for a long time but couldn't find it anywhere. Suddenly they found Tony and Rob the snakes, who turned out to be friendly. They had a conversation and then collected their missing ball. But later that night, a girl had been bitten by one of the local snakes, and the news came through to the group. "You said you wouldn't bite anyone," said Dave. "Yet that girl was bitten." "No doubt it was Geoffrey," said Tony. "He's to blame. Geoffrey is the most aggressive snake and nobody hangs around with him. Let's find and confront him." The snakes went off to find Geoffrey. Geoffrey had very sharp fangs and he was poisonous. He often lashed out for no reason, but when Tony and Rob asked him, he said he acted in self-defence, but Tony and Rob didn't believe Geoffrey. They thought he did it because he was always miserable and annoyed. Geoffrey hid away because he was embarrassed about biting the girl. Instead, he sent his only friend Oik out to talk to Tony and Rob. Oik tried to explain Geoffrey's side of the story, but Oik was known to be untrustworthy and often not telling the truth. After all, Oik did enjoy stealing other snake's prey and foods. The girl was taken to hospital where her arm was attached to a splint. Luckily she arrived before the poison took hold of her body, and the doctors injected an anti-venom antidote into her body, which quickly healed the girl and relieved her pain. The next day, the doctors discharged the girl from hospital, declaring her to be healthy. Tony followed the news and told Dave and his gang while they were cleaning the campsite. Rob told the others, and fortunately the snakes kept their reputation as being calm and friendly to humans. Geoffrey confessed it was all because of favouritism in the snake group. Henderson was always seen as the smartest, at the top of the ladder, while Geoffrey only ever made it to being the second favourite snake. Tony was third and Oik was positioned last, because he always told lies about the other snakes. Rob took no interest. Tony opened up about his own past to Geoffrey. He was once a charmed snake and forced to dance, meagre trash food to eat and milk to drink, which he hated. In fact, Tony and Rob suffered a similar story when they were younger. They explained to Geoffrey that the past could not be used as an excuse to bite, and that it is possible to change and become a better snake. The campers said goodbye to the snakes and promised to return. Tony and Rob were pleased to have met a friendly bunch of humans for a change. They kept their eye on Geoffrey, and Oik, making sure they wouldn't harm anyone. Post-Reading Questions Which snake bit the little girl in the night? Who was Geoffrey's friend and what excuse did Geoffrey give for biting? What did Geoffrey confess to doing and why? Which of the snakes was the most and least favourite? What did Tony open up to Geoffrey about, and what did they say to him? Do you think that the people will return to see the snakes in the future?
author: Hello English
