title: No House For A Mouse
text: Story Description A mouse named Matt wonders what life is like elsewhere. Following advice from the pets in the house, he decides to go and find what is at the bottom of the sea, a secret so powerful that it might change his life. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Aspirations ﻿asp-ih-ray-shuns ﻿Matt had great aspirations to go out and see the world. Exploration ﻿eks-pl-or-ay-shun ﻿He wanted to go on an exploration to see what was outside. Astonished ﻿uss-ton-ish-d ﻿Matt was astonished at what he had found. Wilderness ﻿will-dur-nuss ﻿ ﻿ ﻿Penelope the parrot said that the wilderness was a difficult place to live. ﻿ ﻿ Little Matt the mouse lived in a comfortable house high on the hills outside of the town. He had lived there for many years, and he was good friends with the house pets. He was talking to Max the house dog one day about his ambitions. "This house is no house for a mouse," said Matt. "I must see the wider world." "If you feel you must," said Max, "then you must go and see what is out there." Matt then went to Penelope the parrot to share his idea of going out to see the wider world. "It's a dangerous place and exploration is not fit for a mouse," said Penelope. "I see mice get hunted by birds all the time. You will not last long out in the wilderness." Matt spoke with Gertie goldfish the very old fish. She was wise and cunning. "I really want to broaden my horizons and see the world," said Matt. "Here's what you should do," said Gertie. "Go and find out what is at the bottom of the sea." "The sea! A great idea!" said Matt. "I'll go there at once." "Wow!" said Matt. "I can't wait to find out the secret of what's at the bottom of the sea. Is it eternal life? Treasure? Fame and fortune? I should go!" Matt creeped out of the door that the farmer had left open, and he went outside. Matt scurried all the way to the sea, where he jumped in, wished himself luck, and sank through the layers of fish, plankton and seaweed towards the bottom. He couldn't wait to see what he would find. But Matt didn't stop falling. The sea was deeper than he had anticipated. The light faded and it got darker and darker. "Oh, no," thought Matt. "What have I thrown myself into?" Matt kept on turning and sinking. But then, a strange warmth surrounded and nurtured Matt. He felt cherished and loved. He felt cuddled. He felt his hunger satisfied. He could smell cheese. He could feel the company of other mice, and suddenly, he hit the bottom of the sea. "Agh!" said Matt, as he felt himself pulled away at an astonishing speed. He opened his eyes and he was soaking wet, sitting on the floor of the house. He looked around and saw the fireplace. Penelope the parrot was standing on her perch. Max the dog was sleeping on the sofa. Gertie goldfish the very old fish was swimming in circles and smiling. "How can it be that I'm back at home?" said Matt. "Perhaps this is just a dream and I'm still underwater," said Matt, running around and looking at everything to make sure it was real. "This cannot be happening. Where am I?" Matt ran all the way outside and saw the hills covered in snow, the trees with their bare branches, and he felt the wind of the cool night, seeing the house in the distance. "Maybe I am home," thought Matt. He went inside. He found Gertie and explained what had happened. "Do you understand?" she said. "That's the magic of the sea. It takes you back home. No matter how far you travel, and no matter where you go, you always go back somehow." Matt was astonished. He sat in front of the fireplace laughing. "Maybe I do belong here after all," he said. Post-Reading Questions Why did Matt want to leave the house? What did Gertie goldfish the very old fish advise that he do? What happened to Matt when he jumped into the sea? What started happening as he sank to the bottom? What did Matt realise when he was suddenly returned home? Where would you like to explore?
author: Hello English

title: Fight in the Jungle
text: Story Description The jungle animals fall out after the elephant scares everyone, prompting a big fight to take place. After a while, it is up to one animal to stop the fighting and for the whole group to resolve their differences. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Responsible riss-pon-sib-ul The jungle animals must behave in a responsible way. Insensitive in-sen-sit-iv The elephant was very insensitive towards the other animal's feelings. Nibbling nib-ling The pig tried nibbling their legs. Spikey spy-key The porcupine's body was very spikey and sharp. The monkey woke up one morning to a peaceful sunrise. He was enjoying the serene silence until the bird woke up too. The bird started cawing and crowing really loud, and the monkey had to put his fingers in his ears to block out the noise. "Why do you have to call so loud every morning?" asked the monkey. "That's the way I wake up," said the bird. "Once I sing, then everyone has to get up. It's a rule." The monkey had had enough of the bird's irritating singing, and so one morning, the monkey woke up a little earlier, just before the bird did. He looked at the bright rising sun on the horizon, which made him sneeze really loud. "Ah....ahh...ahhhchooo!" went the monkey, and the bird jumped out of her nest. Later, a huge elephant stomped into the jungle, raised its trunk, and cried out really loud. The noise was so loud that the ground shook. The porcupine, the monkey and the other animals all ran away in fear. The elephant stomped and laughed to itself. "You can't go stomping around and disturbing the entire jungle like that!" said the tiger. "You're a huge animal. You have to be more responsible." "Where's your sense of fun?" said the insensitive elephant. The animals became annoyed and got into huge fight. They toppled the elephant, who dragged the buffalo, the pig, the monkey, the deer, the porcupine, the bird and the tiger onto the ground. "Now we're all stuck," said the deer. "Look at what you've done, elephant!" "It's not my fault that you're all too serious to laugh," said the elephant. The monkey wondered what to do. Now the pig was trying to scare everybody by nibbling at their legs, and he waited for the monkey to come down from the tree. "It's all right," said the pig. "It's safe to come down from there. I won't hurt you." "I don't trust you and your silly tricks," said the monkey. Suddenly, the buffalo came charging in and scared everyone with its horns. The animals cleared the way and the buffalo missed, instead smashing his horns into the tree trunk, where he got stuck. "Now look what you've done to my home!" said the monkey. "And mine!" said the bird. The deer started charging at everyone with its spikey antlers, and the animals backed off. "So you're going to copy the buffalo and be an idiot!" said the monkey. "I have no time for you animals at all." "Stop it!" the tiger roared in a gigantic voice which shook the jungle more than the elephant did. "Enough of this fighting. We are better and more mature than this. We need to put aside our differences and protect the jungle as one team. This fighting will not continue any more." The animals listened and obeyed the tiger. "I'm sorry I kept waking you up in the morning with my singing," said the bird. "From now on, I won't do that anymore." "That's ok," said the monkey. "And I won't deliberately sneeze on you. I'm sorry too." The monkey and the bird forgave each other, became friends again, and learned how to share the tree. Post-Reading Questions How did the bird keep waking the monkey in the morning? What did the monkey do to get his revenge on the bird? How did the elephant scare everyone? When he didn't apologise, what happened to the animals? Who decided to end the fighting with a big roar? Why is it important not to fight?
author: Hello English

title: Creating New Worlds
text: Story Description Debbie is a little girl who enjoys playing with a new toy - a model world. She imagines what would happen if there was no gravity, and she creates a new world with several new planets. The people of the model earth struggle as Debbie creates a nightmare in her imagination for them. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Replica rep-lik-a The model earth is a replica of the original. Unbelievable un-bill-ee-vuh-bul What is happening to the model earth is unbelievable. Miniature min-it-chur The miniature people live on the model earth. Pretending prih-ten-ding Debbie is pretending by using her imagination. Debbie plays with some of her toys and finds something that she had not seen before. She lifts it into the air. It is a replica sphere of the earth. She starts to wonder about travelling around in space. She sees the world upside down and imagines what lies on the bottom and on the top. She sees a woman walking past a hut as a truck filled with wood goes past. It's extraordinary! The model earth has a world of its own going on. Debbie imagines herself on a space shuttle going around that world. She is the only person in space - solitary, and all alone. There is a strange silence in the vacuum of space. Suddenly, a satellite whizzes past. A strong rope connects Debbie to the docking module, so she doesn't float off into deep space. On her walk, she encounters strange worlds that are so close to the earth, it's unbelievable! There's that truck again, and it's going around the rings of a new planet. There is a tree growing somewhere in space! "Are you having fun, Debbie? You look like you're in a world of your own," says her mother. "Yes, mum," says Debbie. "I like playing with the cars, and the model earth is my new favourite toy." Debbie studies pictures of the earth. She sees that people live all over its surface, but they don't fall off because of gravity. She starts to imagine what life would be like without gravitational force. Wouldn't that be interesting? Debbie carries the model world and starts to shake it, pretending there are miniature people living all over its surface. She starts to turn and tilt the world, causing trouble for the people who live on it. It's a disaster! The people of the model earth hold on for their lives as gravity suddenly disappears! They find themselves clinging on, trying to avoid falling on to the dangerous rings of a new planet that came from nowhere! They look and see an evil overlord - a little girl - shaking and turning their delicate blue green world. They have nowhere to escape to. They are at the mercy of the little girl playing a game in her imagination. As the girl turns the world, the beings come up with a plan. They climb the gigantic space tree to escape from their doomed home world. Only the tree can save them now. Perhaps one day they can return to their world when the evil little girl has gone! "That was fun! I wonder if they all escaped?" says Debbie. "Were you playing with the model earth?" says Dad. "Yes, I was. I had a lot of fun," says Debbie. "It looks like you were creating new worlds with it!" says Dad. Post-Reading Questions What new toy does Debbie play with? What does she wonder about people on the other side of the world? What new things does she create and what does she imagine? How do the people of model earth struggle? How do the people of model earth try to escape? What kind of world would you create?
author: Hello English

title: Parakeet Paradise
text: Story Description Two parakeets migrate for the summer to a new land to set up a home. They search for a tree to build a new nest, but the place is so busy that they cannot find one. It's a race against time for them to find a suitable spot to raise a family. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Parakeet ﻿pa-ra-kee-t ﻿The cluster of parakeets migrated for the summer. Feathered ﻿feth-urr-d ﻿They were beautiful feathered creatures. Occupied ﻿oc-yew-pie-d ﻿Most of the branches were occupied by other birds. Sheltered ﻿shel-ter-d ﻿ ﻿Their home was perfect and sheltered from the wind. The long awaited summer had come, and it was time for the birds to find a new home. They had arrived after migrating from the cold winter lands to the warm temperate regions. The first sign of summer was the sighting of yellow and blue feathered birds. A girl and her dog sat in the garden, watching these wonderful birds displaying their feathers, and marking the arrival of summer. The flowers bloomed and gave vibrant, bright colours to the land. Two parakeets - a couple - were searching for a place to build a new nest for their family. They searched a tree but many of the branches were already occupied by other birds. "You can't nest here," they said. "This tree is taken." The parrakeets flew on. Suddenly, hundreds of parakeets flew through the air, and the couple lost track of each other. They called out, but they could not see one another through the flurry and flutter of feathers. When the parakeets passed, they were reunited, and they looked down at the trees below. As the habitat was getting busier, they had to act fast to secure a place for their family. The parakeets found the ideal tree- tall, strong, with a wide trunk and higher branches, so predators could not knock out their nest, and the tree would be resistant from the winds. But just as they were about to choose a branch, they saw a woodpecker hammering away with its beak. Pieces of the trunk fell out, and they knew the tree would not be as strong after. The parakeets flew towards another tree. There was only one very good branch, and it was already occupied by a different big bird, guarding over its nest eggs. "Sorry, this place is taken," said the bird, and the parakeets flew away. "There has to be somewhere we can rest," said the female parakeet. "Don't worry," said the male parakeet. "We'll find somewhere, even if we have to inspect every single tree." They found a bird guarding its eggs, and they explained that they were looking for a place to nest. The bird told them of a nearby area where most of the birds had missed, and it was perfect for raising a family safely. The parakeets immediately took off, saying thank you to the bird. And they found the perfect tree - high up, away from the predators, and sheltered from the wind. They were happy that they had found a safe home to raise their future family. ﻿ ﻿Post-Reading Questions ﻿What season marked the arrival of the birds? What is the first thing that the birds did? What did the parakeets keep on looking for? Why didn't they nest on the tree with the woodpecker? Who helped them find a branch? How far do you think the birds travelled?
author: Hello English

title: Future plans
text: A nice Saturday morning Little Sara and her friend Mia plays basketball in the backyard of Sara's house. Sara's Grandpa sits on the place attached to their house. Mia says " Sara I think if I keep on playing basketball for some days, it will be easy for me to reach my future plan. "Sara asks "what is a future plan?" Mia tells "you don't know what is a future plan? and anyhow I will tell you what is it tomorrow because I have to live now to my house" Sara says "wait Mia please tell me what is a future plan now wait Mia wait" Mia doesn't listen, she says "bye Sara see you tomorrow bye bye" Sara is sad! Grandfather says "Sara I will tell you what is a future plan." Sara smiles a little. "Grandfather what is it what is a future plan" asks little Sara curiously. Grandfather says "Yes Sara I will tell you what is a future plan" "A future plan is a plan or thinking you do for your future" "Basically it is a future goal" says grandfather. Sara says "Oh grandfather now I get it she says. Sara and grandfather play for some time after the conversation. Sara loves singing. Sara says " Grandfather I think my future goal is to be a good singer" Grandfather says " Oh little Sara!"
author: Divya Keerthi

title: King For A Day
text: Story Description The villagers complain to the king about the changes in the country threatening their lives. After the villagers claim that only a real tough man could run the kingdom, the king invites someone to perform the duties of king for the day. He chooses a kid called Alex to do his job. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Instability ﻿in-stur-bill-it-ee ﻿There was instability and uncertainty in the people. Rumours ﻿roo-murs ﻿They had heard many rumours of things happening to the country. Determined ﻿dit-ur-min-d ﻿The king was determined to prove to the people that he was right. Traditions ﻿truh-dish-uns ﻿ ﻿He appointed the boy as king for the day, which broke the traditions. There was instability and confusion in the village, and the king understood the people's frustration. The country was changing, and people were afraid that the change would affect the village. People worried about losing their jobs and running out of money. The king was tired from the rumours that people had been spreading, that he was going to quit. But the king was determined to stay on the throne and in power. "We're worried about our food!" "We don't want to pay higher taxes!" "We'll lose our village and our traditions!" "The country's leadership is weak! They will corrupt the king!" "You are a weak king!" These were some of the protests that the king heard everyday from the people. Finally, the king addressed the people to quell their fears. "This village will remain safe and secure, despite the changing country," he said. "I promise you that as your king I will look after all of you. If we work together, we can get through any challenge. We must stay strong." Some of the people fired back by accusing the king of being old, losing intelligence, and being unable to make good decisions. "As long as there is breath in my body, I will serve this village," said the king. The people said that only a real tough man could run the village, which angered the king. He didn't expect such a horrible remark. He decided to prove the people wrong. "Only a real man can run this village, you say?" said the king. "If you really think that is the case, then I will give you a nice surprise." The king asked for a child from the crowd, to be king for the day. A boy stepped forward and gave his name. "Alex," said the king. "From tomorrow morning until tomorrow evening, you will have my duties and responsibilities as the king. You will run the village. You will have my powers." "Oh, wow!" said Alex. The people were shocked and stunned. They didn't expect the king to pull such a crazy move. The next morning, Alex arrived to take over as the king. Alex's first duty was to tend to a land argument. A local man was enraged because he was unable to buy more land than he needed. He wanted to throw a family off their property so he could use it for his own ends. "You cannot steal what belongs to other people," said Alex. "But, your majesty, I offer them lots of money to move away," said the man. "Money means nothing to me," said Alex, and the man stormed off, getting a wave from the king. Alex wore a crown and special garments, had all the food and drink he could ask for, and he even had his own private guard to keep him cool with a giant fanning leaf. "It doesn't seem so bad being the king," said Alex. "Wait until you have to make really difficult decisions," said the king. "And intervene when things go horribly wrong." "I can see how difficult this job must be on a bad day," said Alex. Upset about the decision, the man who wanted the land sent out some of his henchmen, who hid in the long grass. They easily gave themselves away, and the villagers started to panic. "You think you can deal with this one?" said the king. "I'll give it a try, but if it gets too much, can you be the king again?" said Alex. The king laughed and said he would take over if things got too rough. The villagers started shouting when they saw some strange men and a big, aggressive dog barking at them. They were scared and tried to get the king's attention. "If you won't give the land to us, then we'll take it by force," said one of the henchmen as his dog growled. "If you do that, we'll punish you and send you away," said Alex. "Who's this little boy?" said the henchman. "He's in charge today. You address him, not me," said the real king. Meanwhile, the king had a trick up his sleeve. He found one of his old village friends who kept pets. "Do you have it ready?" said the king. "Of course, your majesty," said the pet seller. "I think this should be enough to frighten them off." He passed the box to the king. The henchmen and the dog were silenced when they saw a box being carried out. "The king has a son?" the henchman said to himself. "The king's favourite dog just died and we're burying it," said the pet seller. "And you came here to complain on such a sad day? That's very inappropriate." "I've offended the king big time," said the henchman. "I must leave at once and lower my head in shame. He won't forget this." The prank worked and the henchmen left. Everyone congratulated Alex for being such a brave little king. The king smiled and waved at Alex. He had done an excellent job being the king, but by the evening, he had to give up the crown and the king was reinstated. "It's not easy being a king, is it?" said the king to Alex. "I'll stay as being just a kid for now," said Alex, and the king sent him home with a basket of presents for doing a great job. The villagers saw what Alex did and they were silenced. They didn't complain to the king anymore. Post-Reading Questions What were the villagers worried about? How did the king call their bluff? What was Alex's first duty as the new king? What happened when Alex sent the man away? What kind of trick did the king play on the henchmen? What would you do for one day only?
author: Hello English

title: Water For The Village
text: Story Description Rodney is an ambassador for his village which desperately needs a water pump. Currently, the villagers have to walk too far just to collect fresh water, so Rodney plans on hiring a team to build a new pump. At the same time, a cat and a dog fight over water. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Installing in-staw-ling The villagers were interested in installing a new water pump. Improving im-proo-ving They knew that they would be improving their village. Attitudes at-it-chew-d-s Some of the attitudes towards the village were horrible. Demotivate dee-mow-tiv-ate Those who committed crimes tried to demotivate the people. Many local villages had received a water supply and installed a pump, but Rodney's village was still without water. People had to walk five kilometres per day to collect water from the nearest source. Rodney wanted the village to have their own pump. "We will have to work together and install a pump ourselves," he said, so determined to make it happen. Later, Fred was out walking when he tripped on some rocks. He looked at the sole of his foot and saw that it was bleeding. It needed to be cleaned, but there was no fresh water to clean his cut. "Don't you see?" said Rodney to the neighbours. "Fred hurt his foot. We are lucky that we have enough medical supplies to treat him, but without a water supply, we cannot clean cuts and apply bandages. This is another reason why we must build our own pump." Very soon, more and more villagers got on board with Rodney's idea, and they all learned together how to build a pump, and where to look for a water source. The village celebrated the beginning of their new team project. Unfortunately, some of the village did not have the same attitude towards improving themselves. Many thugs and gangs hung around the shops, intimidating people and trying to demotivate them. Crime was still high, and Rodney was determined to put an end to it. Thankfully, a boy who had fallen and broken his leg received medical treatment, and was seen by a doctor. As his leg healed, he asked his father to help with the water project in the village. His father said he would provide all the information and help that he could. Even the animals were delighted with the news. A wily dog sat outside his house as a cat came creeping in, trying to sneak some water. "I hope you're not here for my bowl," said the dog. "Oh, no," said the cat. "I have my own water at home." "I was talking about the food," said the dog, making the cat shocked and nervous. The cat drank from the dog's bowl and ran away over a fence. The dog was a poor climber, so he could only watch the cat get away after drinking his water. The dog was furious. Later, the dog saw the cat drinking from a water source outside of the village. The dog sneaked up on the cat and drank some of the water. The cat was startled to see the dog, and it ran off as quickly as it could. "Don't you drink my water again!" shouted the dog. The villagers discovered a water source and built a pump. Over time, they completed the project and could walk a short distance to collect as much water as they needed. The whole village was happy and relieved, and they congratulated Rodney on his idea. The crime rate also fell. The cat and the dog became friends, because now they could share water. They played together and lazed around, and sometimes the cat would still tease the dog by drinking its water. Some things never change! ﻿ Post-Reading Questions ﻿ What idea﻿ did Rodney have for the village? How far did the villagers have to walk each day to collect water? One of the boys fell and cut his foot. Why did this encourage Rodney? Not everyone was in favour of a water pump. Who tried to bring others down? How did the dog surprise the cat? Why is it important to work in a team?
author: Hello English

title: A Game of Cricket
text: Story Description Lisha has been playing cricket since she was very young, and her school organises and all-girl's game, where she is the captain of her team. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Batting ﻿bat-ing ﻿The batting team scores as many runs as they can. Bowling ﻿boho-ing ﻿The bowling team tries to get the batsmen out. Fielding ﻿feel-ding ﻿The fielding team, which is the bowling team, chases after the ball to return to the wicket keeper. Catching ﻿cat-ch-ing ﻿ ﻿ ﻿The fielders are catching the ball. A catch gets the batsman out. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ Lisha had been a huge fan of cricket, ever since she was very young. Her father used to play in a local team, and he taught her the rules and the basics, such as bowling, batting and fielding. When she came home from her practice lesson, Lisha watched cricket on the TV. While she was having fun practicing her batting skills, pretending to hit balls for fours and sixes, her mother spied on her from the kitchen. She was happy that her daughter was learning how to play a sport. As Lisha learned more about cricket, and understood what was happening on the field, she became very passionate about playing and watching the sport. Every time she saw an injustice during a match, she would stand up and shout. "That was clearly out!" she would say. "I think you're ready to play with a hard ball now," said her father, having seen her progress from a young age. "These are gloves. They protect your hands from the ball. They have extra padding around the thumbs. You wear these when you are batting." The school organised an all-girls game of cricket. Lisha was the captain of her team, and she got her players ready on the field. They inspected the pitch. It was going to be good for batsmen. The umpire tossed the coin and the captains called heads and tails. The opposing team won and they decided to bat, meaning Lisha's team would field. Lisha bowled really well and didn't give away many runs. She bowled out the opposing team's best batsman with a great delivery. The crowd cheered. When it was Lisha's turn to bat, she scored many runs. She whacked the ball over the boundary in the air, and scored six runs, until she was caught out, having scored 42 runs for her team. While her team was fielding, Lisha's best friend took several catches, stopping the opposing team from scoring so many runs. Lisha cheered on her players. The opposing team's batsman hit the ball and ran. Lisha's team mate picked up the ball and gave it to the wicket keeper, who hit the ball against the stumps, and got the batsman out. Everyone celebrated such a great move. That crucial "run out" won the game, because Lisha's team was able to score more runs to win. They celebrated by lifting the trophy after the game. ﻿ ﻿Post-Reading Questions What has Lisha been playing since she was very young? How does Lisha develop her understanding of cricket? What does her father tell her that she is ready for? How many runs does Lisha score during the match? Who wins the match? If you could develop a skill, what would it be?﻿
author: Hello English

title: Trip to the Market Place
text: Story Description A girl called Lily takes you on a tour of her local market place, including fruit and vegetable markets, side streets, the fish place, the flower stalls and what she is having for dinner. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Bargain ﻿bar-gin ﻿The market is a great place to find a good bargain. Struggling ﻿str-ug-ling ﻿She was struggling to carry her bag because it was so heavy. Confectionary ﻿cun-fec-shun-air-ee ﻿She wanted some candy from the confectionary stall, but her mother said no. Spicy ﻿spy-see ﻿The food that her mother made was very spicy. Hi there! My name is Lily, and I enjoy going to the market place with my mother. There are so many things available to buy, and there is so much colour, noise and life there. It is an exciting place to find bargains and hidden treasures. Let's have a look and see what we can find together! This is the central market place in my town. Notice the variety of things on offer. Look at the stack of lovely coconuts in the centre, and the woman selling cantaloupe melons and mangos beside it. At the front, two women are arguing while they sell grapes. There's a bored man watching a woman shouting about the poor quality of his produce. Well, I'm going to buy some bell peppers (1), and then have a look at that rare fruit at the back (2). Someone is bartering for the price of that vegetable (3), so I'll go over and watch. That is one gigantic watermelon sitting in that crate (4). It's so big that it could feed an entire family for two weeks! Oh, dear. Someone has upset the shopkeeper on the left after protesting at his prices. This is the bag I use to put the produce inside. Hey, there's not enough room for all of my things! I'm going to need a much bigger bag. Mum! This is the fish market! There's a man hiding behind his stack of fish. Perhaps he has seen someone from the past, or he is avoiding getting caught! Two guys are struggling while pushing and dragging a crate of fish. The man at MCK is shouting out the deals he has to offer. This fish market is a noisy place! My bag is so heavy from ordering the fish and going around the fruit market. Mum has taken it for me because it weighs too much, and I can't carry it any longer. Thanks, Mum! We're at the flower market now. The main seller (1) is busy making deals with the customers. There's a stall that sells necklaces made of flowers. They look really pretty (2) and the seller is always kind, giving us compliments! The woman (3) has bowls of flowers arranged neatly, and unfortunately, an uncle (4) has let go of his grandson's hand, and he is trying to run away. Come back! I'm unhappy because Mum won't allow me to eat any sweet things, or go to the confectionary stand. She says the sugar will ruin my appetite, and that I won't eat my dinner. She's right, but even so, I just wanted a few sweets! Now we're off to the back streets and the mini stalls, to see if there's any older produce we can buy for less than half of the normal price! There's a tub of tomatoes. Maybe we can have a dish of salsa to go with dinner! Wow, what a wonderful dinner. Thanks, Mum! She's made rice with a spicy tomato sauce, fried fish and potatoes. It's delicious. Now all I need is a glass of water, quick! It's so hot and spicy, my mouth can't handle the heat! Ah! Post-Reading Questions Where does Lily enjoy going to? What kinds of things does she find at the market? Whose grandson was trying to run away? Who was hiding behind the fish counter? Where does Lily go to find even cheaper food? Where is your favourite place to go?
author: Hello English

title: Peepre in the Postbox
text: Peepre looks out of the anthill. The sun is a boondi laddoo in the sky. Pish-phoosh, phish-sphloosh. Peepre climbs onto a green leaf. Whooosh-whoooshooo. A breeze lifts the leaf up, up, up. And into... … a red postbox. It is dark inside. Peepre walks into a cover. It has red, blue and green stamps. Khich-khish, khich-khish. A hand sweeps all the letters into a giant bag. A postwoman carries the bag away on her moped. Jhug-jhugetty, bumpetty-brump. Khachaak. Peepre bumps into an airmail letter. She crawls into a birthday card. Dhakatta-dhiti. The postbag lands on a table. Letters pour out. Thakata-tham, thuddata-thud, goes the stamp. Letters fall down, down, down. Swish-swash, swish-swash. Piles grow. To Delhi. Mumbai. Kohima. Kundapur. Pune. Bengaluru. Peepre clings to the card. The card lands in a crowded postbag. The bag is tossed into a postal van. Parpetty-park, honketty-honk. Peepre reads an upside-down postcard, “Do you like school, Tunu? Love, Didima.” On a pink letter in blue ink, “Can you sing a moon tune?” Screee-chhhk. The van stops. Kheech-khatak. Gates clank. Shhhh-phat. A letter falls through the door slot. Tarara-triiiing. Peepre hears a doorbell. ‘Maaaaa! Ajji sent me a card.’
author: Aditi De

title: A Prank Goes Wrong
text: Story Description Two best friends, Ash and Dennis, play football together every day. They grew up in the same neighbourhood and know each other very well. But one day, Ash asks Dennis to help him do something bad, causing trouble to their friendship. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Prankster pra-n-k-st-ur Ash enjoyed being a prankster, playing tricks on his friends. Willingness will-ing-nuss An important part of friendship is having the willingness to forgive. Goalkeeper g-ole-keep-ur Dennis enjoyed playing the position of goalkeeper in a football match. Attention a-ten-shun Playing a prank on the shop would bring a lot of attention. Two boys, Ash and Dennis, were the best of friends. They grew up together, and played football with one another every day. They played pranks on their friends and went exploring and on adventures. Ash and Dennis didn't mind competing on opposite teams during a football game. Ash was a talented centre-forward, trying to shoot and score goals. Dennis was a gifted goalkeeper, catching most of Ash's shots on goal. "I have an idea," said Ash one day. "Let's skip the football and play a prank on the local shop. It will be hilarious." "I don't think that's a good idea," said Dennis, being more cautious. "We'll get in big trouble. It's not the same as pranking our friends." "Come on," said Ash. "If we can hide a rat somewhere in the shop, it will scare the customers. Then the news will be in the paper and we can laugh about it! Just think of all the attention it will bring. They'll never know it was us." "All right," said Dennis. "But just this once. We cannot get caught, understand?" Ash hid the rat on the shelf, but then he stuffed his pockets with chocolate and sweets. Dennis called him out. "It's just a bit of fun," shouted Ash. "Don't be such a sissy!" "I can't believe my best friend would try to steal from a shop!" said Dennis. "What kind of person are you? You're horrible!" As they were walking home, Ash's mother received a call from the shop, telling her about Ash stealing from the shelves. The shopkeeper also found the rat. "I'm very disappointed with you," said Ash's mother. "And to even think you would drag Dennis into your cruel plan. That is appalling behaviour. No wonder Dennis doesn't want to be your friend anymore. He doesn't trust you." Ash's mother made him go to the shop and apologise for attempting to steal, and putting a rat on the shelf. "I could have caused the shop to be closed down," said Ash. "And I would have got in trouble with the police for stealing. I'm sorry to have put you through that mess, Dennis. I'm sorry, Mum." "It's all right," said Dennis. "I forgive you." "Why did you forgive me?" said Ash. "Because you're my best buddy, and a sign of a strong friendship is a willingness to forgive." "I'm very grateful for your kindness," said Ash. "We should stick to playing football from now on." "But you have to be the goalkeeper now," said Dennis, and they laughed. Post-Reading Questions What kind of sport do Ash and Dennis enjoy playing together? What positions do they play during a game? What does Ash want Dennis to help him with? What happens when Dennis sees Ash stealing chocolate from the shop? What does Ash's mother tell Ash to do? Why is forgiveness important?

text: It was Rita’s 6 th birthday. The party was over and she was unpacking all her gifts. The most interesting gift she found was the one given by her grandma. title: The More I Give, The More I Have
text: Story Description Nelson and Nancy are two siblings who help a woman called Tabatha at her farm, playing in the fields, vegetable picking, and collecting produce. Tabatha teaches them the importance of sharing and giving, for the more one shares, the more they get. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Troublemaker ﻿truh-bull-may-kur ﻿The boy was a craft young troublemaker. Supervising ﻿soo-pur-vai-zing ﻿Tabatha was always supervising the children, making sure they were fine. Kindness ﻿kai-n-d-nuss ﻿The children understood that acts of kindness created a loving atmosphere. Service ﻿sir-miss ﻿ ﻿Tabatha understood that her most important trait was to be in service. Nelson and Nancy enjoyed playing on the tree by the lake. Nelson liked to hang upside down with his arms stretched out, getting dizzy, and Nancy liked to splash Nelson with water, getting him soaked. Nelson and Nancy played on the land belonging to a woman named Tabatha. It was her farm, and it consisted of crops and animals. Nelson and Nancy helped Tabatha with her chores, including carrying barrels, bowls of eggs, collecting wood and picking vegetables. Suddenly, as they were walking towards Tabatha's farm, a strange young man started shouting at the cows. He was very angry and he scared Nelson and Nancy. He chased after the cows, screaming as he ran off. Nelson and Nancy quickly ran away to Tabatha's farm, where they felt safe. Tabatha calmed the children down after they explained what the young man had done. "He is a known troublemaker," said Tabatha. "I'm glad you told me about him. Now I can tell his parents, and they'll make sure he behaves!" Tabatha prepared two big bowls of fish curry and rice for Nelson and Nancy, as a way of saying thank you for collecting the produce from around the farm. "I hope you like it," said Tabatha. They ate very quickly, because the food was so delicious. "Wow, thank you, Tabatha, you're an incredible cook," said the children. "I'm very proud of having you two as my helpers," said Tabatha. "You should always know that, whatever happens, you are always welcome to stay here at my farm, and play in the fields. As you go through life, offer to help others in the same way that you have helped me. But never force your help on someone. Many people will push you away due to your kindness. Do not be troubled about this." "What wonderful children you have," Tabatha said to Nelson and Nancy's parents. "They are sweethearts. They help me all of the time on the farm. Today they encountered that tearaway boy who causes trouble. But luckily the boy was more interested in chasing the cows." "I appreciate you supervising them," said Nelson and Nancy's father. "Children, you should pay attention to what this wise woman is telling you." "Yes, Dad," they replied. For the rest of the summer holiday, Nelson and Nancy helped Tabatha to sell her produce at the regional markets, travelling to different towns and encountering many different kinds of people. The experience of selling, service and travel helped them to grow individually, and to learn how to build as a team. Their people skills improved, as did their ability to listen. They learned that in order to be successful, they must charge fair prices and be friendly to their customers. "The three most important parts of selling are service, service and service," said Tabatha. Tabatha even gave the children some of the profits, which paid for the toys they wanted to buy, like a bicycle, some artwork and a computer. "We make a great team," said Nelson. "We do," said Nancy. "And we have learned to give to others, and never to take. Relationships are not about give and take. They are about sharing. The more I give, the more I have." Post-Reading Questions ﻿What did Nelson and Nancy enjoy doing at the tree by the lake? How did they help Tabatha and her farm? What scared Nelson and Nancy all the way back to Tabatha's farm? What kind of meal did Tabatha cook for the children? What did Nelson and Nancy learn from interacting with people while selling? Why is it important to give and to not take from others?
author: Hello English

title: So Noisy!
text: Story Description Ronald wants to study while his sister Rebecca wants to play. Rebecca creates a lot of distracting noise, which makes Ronald struggle to do his homework. When Rebecca steals some of Ronald's books, Ronald has to draw the line and set boundaries for his sister. A story about learning how to respect one another. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Keyboard ﻿key-bored ﻿The cat walked all over the keyboard and made a noise. Tantrum ﻿tan-trum ﻿Rebecca threw a tantrum when she didn't get what she wanted. History ﻿hiss-tur-ee ﻿The history book spoke about events from the past. Geography ﻿jog-ra-ph-ee ﻿ ﻿The geography book talked about volcanoes and earthquakes. Whenever Ronald tried to study, there was too much noise coming from his sister. Ronald's sister was called Rebecca, and she had a cat called Ginger. Rebecca would hum and sing while the cat meowed and stepped all over the keyboard. "Maybe one day I'll be able to work in peace and silence," wondered Ronald, as he watched the cat happy stepping across the keys. Rebecca was a very active girl. When she wasn't playing the piano and trying to sing in tune, and when she wasn't painting pictures with the cat and making a mess, Rebecca was usually outside shouting and skipping, and chasing after Ginger. The cat would bite Rebecca and run away, making her very angry. When Ronald took a break, he would assist Rebecca with many things. He helped her find the cereal and the fruit. He made her a cup of tea. He even shared some of his paper with her so she could keep on painting. "That looks wonderful," Ronald would say after Rebecca showed him the paintings she had made. "Just remember to keep quiet while I'm studying." Then Ronald would return to studying and Rebecca would make more hand and paw print paintings with Ginger. As Ronald was studying, Rebecca suddenly took interest in one of his maths books. "Give it to me!" she shouted. "No! I'm still studying," said Ronald. "You can read it once I'm finished." "I want it now!" Rebecca snapped, snatching the book away. "I want the other book too," said Rebecca. "Well, you can't have it," said Ronald. "This is my physics book. If you take this from me, then I can't do any studying." Rebecca kicked and screamed on the floor, throwing a tantrum. Rebecca took more and more books from the shelf, leaving Ronald with nothing to do. He just sat at his desk, staring at the floor. "I wonder how long Rebecca will take with those books?" he said in a bad mood. Meanwhile, Rebecca felt very happy. Rebecca read the maths and physics books. She was captivated by the lessons and by what she had discovered. She didn't want to let the books go, even though she knew she would have to give them back to Ronald. She gradually read through her pile of books and returned the finished ones to Ronald, so he could continue studying. Rebecca read through some poetry, history and geography books, finding out about the past, the world, and the great literature written throughout the ages. Later, Rebecca crept into Ronald's room. "I want those maths and physics books again," said Rebecca, and Ronald felt scared. "But I need them to do my homework." "Give them to me!" Ronald felt a surge of anger inside, and suddenly he shouted. "No!" "These are my homework books. This is history. This is geography. I have a lot of work to do, and I need these books to create answers to the questions." Rebecca felt upset. She knew that Ronald was right, and she realised how mean she had been, just stealing his books while he was busy. She slowly walked away. The next time, Rebecca asked Ronald kindly to borrow books. The way she asked, not demanded, made all of the difference. Rebecca learned to not be rude and barge in, but to respect Ronald's space and quiet time, only asking him when he was finished with his studying, if she could borrow his books. Post-Reading Questions What kind of things did Rebecca enjoy doing with her cat Ginger? Sometimes Ronald would lend a hand. What did he help Rebecca with? Why did Rebecca suddenly start screaming at Ronald? What did Rebecca realise that she had done wrong? How did Ronald say no to Rebecca after trying to take his books again? Why is it important to respect each other?
author: Hello English

title: Eddie's Birthday Party
text: Story Description A girl called Edina - Eddie for short - invites her friends over for her birthday party, where they get up to all kinds of mischief and play games. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Apologised ﻿a-pol-uh-jai-z-d ﻿Billy apologised for arriving so late to the party. Savoury ﻿say-vur-ee ﻿They ate sweet and savoury snacks for their dinner. Shrieked ﻿shree-k-d ﻿The girls shrieked when the saw a bumble bee buzzing around them. Cupboard ﻿cub-urd ﻿Gupta tried to hide in the cupboard but she got stuck. It was Eddie's seventh birthday party, and all of her friends had gone to her house to celebrate. But there was something wrong. One of her friends was missing. Just then, Billy arrived late. He saw how sad Eddie and her other friends were and he apologised. Now the party could begin! "I'll pick you up in three hours,' said Billy's father, before going back to the hotel he worked at. Eddie had spent the day waiting for her friends, opening small presents, and thanking people for their gifts. It was a lazy day. Eddie ate too much chocolate and spread herself out over the carpet, feeling sick and listening to the radio. Then her neighbour Cherry turned up to give her a birthday badge. '7 today', it read. The party went on and Billy suggested playing a game of hide and seek. Everyone disappeared, and Eddie went looking for them. She opened the bookcase to find Eric and George stuffed inside. They had been holding their breath to stay hidden, and Eddie laughed at them. "Thank goodness you let us out!" they whined. "The doors locked us inside!" The guests at the party were as follows: Harriet with the bowtie, Cherry the neighbour, Eric, Sajid, George, Billy who had been late, Tabatha who was feeling sad, Amber and Gupta. Everyone danced on the sofa to music. Billy tried to pull some fun moves until Amber tried to steady him, worried that he would fall over. Also, Sajid ended up stumbling into Cherry and pushed her off the sofa on to Eric and George. It was time for the birthday dinner, and once they had finished, Gupta went off to play with some toys. She had completely forgotten about Eddie's birthday cake and the happy birthday song. "Oh, no!" said Eddie. "I have to find Gupta. She's wandered off again." Eddie surprised Gupta with a slice of her birthday cake. "Here you go, Gupta," she said. "A slice of chocolate cake with a cup of orange slushy fixed into the top. "Ooh, thank you so much, Eddie!" said Gupta. "I forgot about the cake!" "Tabatha, why are you always looking sad?" said Eddie. "It's just my face," said Tabatha. "I'm not actually sad and I'll prove that to you!" Tabatha chased after Benny, Eddie's dog, trying to make it put on a dress. But Benny was too smart and he ran away from Tabatha, who chased him around the house, looking sad again. Eddie was so happy with her fun party, even when Sajid had brought her a card saying 'happy sixth birthday', even though she was seven. The place was covered with balloons and dinner had been delicious - a mixture of sweet and savoury dumplings, sushi, sop and rice. Before going home time, the kids played in the garden. Amber and Harriet shrieked because when they were dancing, suddenly a bumble bee turned up to join in. "Just ignore it and have fun," said Eddie, not realising that Harriet and Amber were both terrified of bees. They both ran indoors. Gupta got stuck inside the cupboard, Eric and George fell off a stack of chairs, someone rolled Cherry in the carpet, Amber ran around the house trying to escape from the bee, and Eddie closed her eyes, trying to find the rest of her friends. Everyone received a goodie bag on their way home, and they talked about Eddie's future ninth birthday party. "But in a year I'll still only be eight," said Eddie. Post-Reading Questions Who arrived late to the party? What kind of games did the kids play? Who forgot about the birthday cake and went off to play with toys? Who fell off the sofa right on to Eric and George? What happened while the girls were dancing in the garden? What would your perfect birthday party be like?
