title: Kara and Granny Ahyoka
text: Kara and Granny Ahyoka were passing through the jungle talking about nature, and how amazing nature is, when it’s still. Kara looked up through the trees and to the sky. Beauty it is! Lush green trees, cool breeze and beautiful blue sky made her day. Granny Ahyoka is an avid nature lover. She often quoted that it’s the same energy that is flowing in us, humans and nature. She lived in a small hut near the jungle and Kara lived a little away in the village with her parents. Granny Ahyoka and Kara are not related to each other by blood, but they have become thickest of friends due to their love for nature. Kara met Granny Ahyoka when she came to visit her parents, who provide Granny with her daily food. Kara’s parents are farmers in the village and they consider Granny as their mother. Kara’s father Para, many a time tells Kara that “Life is beautiful when you consider every creature on this planet and beyond, same as "you”! What is within you, is there within everyone. When you just treat every other living being as a family of yours, you will be very happy my child.” Thus, villagers adore Kara for her nature. Kara is a fun-loving girl, very helpful and adventurous. Granny Ahyoka is the most generous woman one could ever find. She goes to jungle every day with Kara and collects fresh vegetables and fruits from the jungle, only to come back and give them to the village. Granny Ahyoka has been an epitome of kindness. She is an inspiration to many in the village and villagers follow her footsteps. As a mark of respect and love, Para and his wife have taken up the responsibility to provide her with the daily food. It so happened, that one day there was a heavy down pour and Kara and Granny Ahyoka couldn’t come out of the jungle. Granny Ahyoka fell sick due to the bad weather condition, which appeared like a storm. There were trees in the jungle that were uprooted, and the wild animals were also moving in the jungle. Kara was a bit worried about Granny but she didn’t give up. It was late night, and both Kara and Granny Ahyoka were feeling hungry. Granny asked Kara if she was getting scared. Kara promptly replied with a smile “Why Granny? Should I get scared?”. Then Granny smiled too and replied “No dear Kara, I was just checking if you are getting scared. Fear is an illusion anyway! It just complicates our mind. When you know about the energy that’s there in each of us, why fear my dear? ” Kara acknowledged what Granny was saying and figured out that it’s time for her to get some food for Granny and move her into a safer place. She ran across the jungle in the rain to identify a shelter so that she can bring Granny into that. On the way she identified some banana trees. She plucked some ripe and raw bananas. As soon as she moved from the banana tree, she heard some noise in the bushes nearby. Remembering what Granny said about fear, she boldly moved in the direction of bushes. “Gushhhhhh!” and there it was! An elephant looking at the bananas in Kara's hands. The elephant looked unsettled due to the storm. Kara walked a bit and stood by its side and started pampering the elephant. She gave her some bananas and connected with it by touching her forehead to the elephant’s forehead. The elephant was very happy and gave a nice little pat to Kara with its trunk. Kara remembered and admired Granny Ahyoka and father Para for what they always say, “One energy in all!”. With the left over bananas under her hat made of palm leaves, she ran back to Granny. She held Granny’s hand and took her to the nearby shelter. She made fire and put those raw bananas into the fire. Meanwhile Granny was acting as if she fell asleep, to tease Kara for sometime. Kara took the cooked bananas and was trying hard to wake Granny up. Granny was silently smirking for a while and having fun. She however, couldn't resist her hunger and therefore, woke up to eat the simple and yummy food cooked by dear Kara. After eating, Granny and Kara started drawing on the walls of the shelter about their journeys in the jungle and under each picture, Kara captured the lesson she learnt from Granny. Kara also drew her new friend, elephant with bananas on the wall. After all, life is about capturing bright moments and beautiful lessons, isn't it? “Grandpa, what do the names Kara and Ahyoka mean?” asked Dhatu. Dhatu is the grandchild of Para, who was listening to this story of his mother Kara, when she was a child and then Granny, Ahyoka. Kara is all grown up now, goes to jungle for work and she is now a mother too. One day, she found Dhatu in the jungle and she brought him home. From that day, Dhatu is Kara's son. Remember, "One energy in all". Para replied “Kara means pure, Ahyoka means bringer of happiness and Dhatu means creator. How apt and wonderful are these names? Isn’t it?”. Dhatu smiled at Para's reply and drifted off to sleep.
author: Sudha Dastrala
illustrator: Alina  Aphayvanh; Greystroke; Jacob Kono; Nguyễn Thị  Ngọc Bích; Niloufer Wadia; Nimret Handa; Rohit Bhasi

title: Clean-Up Day!
text: Devi and Madhu were best friends. One day they went to the park to play but all they saw there was trash, trash and more trash! Heaps of garbage bags were piled high and dirty flies flew around them. Madhu closed her nose. Devi said, "We must do something about this." The next day during sports practice Madhu got a brilliant idea. She whispered to Devi, "How about we do our sports day in the park!" After practice Madhu explained her idea, "We will keep the sports day event in the park and raise money to clean the park and place proper dustbins. Dance groups from our community can also do a clean India inspired dance!" S the next day, they immediately decided to talk to their principal- Ms. Anitha. Much to the girls' delight and excitement, she readily agreed. She also said that she was very proud of Madhu and Devi for coming up with the idea. So all the kids practiced hard and everyday they sold more tickets to people who wanted to attend the sports day celebrations. Meanwhile, Devi and Madhu were busy organizing the whole event. They called up the park and asked if they could borrow the track ground for a day. They made important calls and wrote beautiful slogans to inspire others to go green and reduce their garbage. With all the money, they bought five big dustbins that would be placed in the park for everyone's use! Finally, it was the day! Children screamed and shouted, cheering for their favorite teams. Beautiful drills showed the real meaning of cleanliness and posters about cleanliness were put up in the park. the newly bought dustbins were placed in every corner do people could use them. more money was collected during the sports event as people bought homemade food from the students of the school. Devi and Madhu's teams won first place in the relay event. They were very happy with their effort. They got a big shiny trophy not just for winning the race, but also for cleaning up the park and making it beautiful again. Some days later, when Madhu and Devi went back to the park, they saw it had become beautiful and green. People were using the trash cans and the whole park didn't smell like garbage anymore! They were very happy with their work and decided to save the environment in all the ways they could!
author: Sanjana

title: Peeping into the life of a crow
text: As I saw a murder of crows flying across the magical sky flapping their wings and cooing, it seemed to me as if they were spirits of nature. It never came to my mind that how easily we get our food and how harder is it on the part of crows to get their food. Though the crows eat just anything on earth, it is still tough to move from one place to the other in search of food. Most food is taken from the ground, but also from trees as opportunity arises. They are highly opportunistic birds and given their omnivorous diet, they can survive on nearly anything that is edible. These birds can be seen near marketplaces and garbage dumps, foraging for scraps. They prefer large trees with big crowns for nesting and such large trees are also getting cut in a reckless manner which in turn has robbed the crow of their right to live in their place of choice. Crows are performing a useful function and keeping our environment free from rotting carcasses. Of course, the carcasses are only tasty bit of mouth-watering food for them but we humans know to what extent we are getting benefited because of these scavengers. It's a bit awkward but crows which are generally unloved species, are performing a very valuable service. Without these scavengers dead animals would be scattered around our environment rotting and causing a hygiene hazard. Crows are very social species and live in large extended family groups. That does not mean, however, that they are friendly with all other crows. Just as we humans are social and love our families and friends, we also have been known to fight and kill each other on occasion. Birds may fight for a number of reasons, such as defending territory boundaries or defending some other resource. A very mysterious thing about the crow is still to be unfolded - Crows are known to behave strangely around their dead. They gather around and squawk loudly nearby. Why the crows follow such a practice has largely remained a mystery till date. In India, crow is considered auspicious and is a welcome bird bringing good tidings and blessings of the dead. When a crow perches itself on a branch towards a home and is continuously crowing, it is said to bring good news of arrival of guests or mail! When there is death, rice balls with sesame seeds are offered to the departed and fed to the crows. Seldom we realise to what extent these black ugly looking scavengers are valuable ……
author: Rehan  Sheikh
illustrator: Lindy  Pelzl; Padmanabh; Shivam Thapliyal; Shreyas R Krishnan

title: The Old Woman and her Hen
text: Long ago in a small village in Goa lived an old woman. Her hut stood in the centre of all the other huts. In the morning she worked in the fields and earned some money to feed herself. The old woman also owned a hen that laid eggs. Every afternoon, the old woman would take the eggs and sell them to the local shopkeeper. Sometimes she would keep an egg for herself. At night she would boil the egg and eat it with a thin lentil soup. The egg would fill her stomach and give her some strength. Now the hen that belonged to the old woman was quite smart. If the hen clucked once, then it meant she would lay 1 egg. If the hen clucked thrice, it meant 3 eggs. If the hen clucked five times, it meant 5 eggs. The entire village was amused at this clucking and laying of eggs. One day a wealthy man came from the city. He boasted of the big buildings, the shiny cars and the huge shops that he was used to in the city. Many of the villagers present there were impressed by the city man’s stories. “Does the building you live in almost touch the sky?” asked Vilas, the fisherwoman. “You go by this car everywhere? So you don’t have to walk at all?” asked Yeshwant, the farmer pointing to the city man’s yellow colour car. “People in the city don’t have to fetch water from the well? How lucky!” said Ratan, the shepherd. “But do you have a hen in the city who can predict how many eggs she will lay?” Hearing this pointed question, all the villagers turned around to see who this question came from. It was Veena, the farmer’s daughter. “Keep quiet” her father warned her. “Do you not see? He is a man from the city. He has such wonderful stories to tell.” “Oh please don’t scold her” said the city man. “But dear girl I cannot believe you, till I see the hen.” “Ok then follow me” said a proud looking Veena. They all went to the old woman’s house to watch her hen. As they all sat, waiting for the hen to cluck, the city man announced- “If this hen actually predicts the number of eggs she will lay, I will pay this old woman Rs.100 for each egg.” All the villagers cheered! The hen clucked, one, two, 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10! “She has clucked 10 times, that means she will lay 10 eggs” screamed Veena in joy. And of course the hen laid 10 eggs. The city man had no choice but to pay the old woman the money. “But maybe you just got lucky today” the city man said. “Could this not have happened by chance?” So the city man stayed on for another five days in the village, and each time the hen clucked and predicted the number of eggs she would lay. By the end of five days, the old woman had enough money to buy herself a cow, another hen, and to repair her hut that had been damaged by the rains. And what did she do with the rest of the money? She gave it to Veena’s parents for her schooling, for new books, for better clothes and to take a bus ride to visit the city. ACTIVITY Use this story to study numbers while learning different animal sounds: Cow Moo Moo Moo Moo 4 Donkey Heehaw Heehaw 2 Pig Oink oink oink oink oink oink oink 7 Cat Meow 1 Have fun!
author: STORY KI BORY TEAM
illustrator: 211 Studio; Ajit Narayan; Aphisith Souphavongtay; Audrey Agnier; Marleen  Visser; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Proiti Roy; Shadrach Munene; Swati Agarwal

title: Sam changed his life
text: Last year, I ranked last in my class. My friends laughed at me. Our teacher said, “Sam why don’t you think about why you came last in the class.” I thought hard. Why did I come in last? I decided to observe the other students and see what they did. Aha! They read books. They take notes. They study! I told my mother “Mom, I would like to do better in class.” “You can do better, Sam," she said. That evening, I grabbed my books and studied. My sister also helped me with my work. Mother said, “Read books, do your homework, and ask your teachers questions so that they can help you,” The more I studied, the more my reading skills improved. I continued working hard with my friends, Matata and Jeni. I asked teachers when I had questions and they were happy to help. One day, we had a test in the class. When the results were out, I was no longer the last. “Hurrrayyy!” I was the happiest boy in the class. “So… I can do it,” I told myself. I decided to work harder than ever before! At the end of the term, the teacher read out the results. The third in rank was Matata. The second was Jeni. Guess who was first? “The first is … Sam!” The teacher gave me books and a bag as a prize. “Sam, do you have anything to tell your friends?” she asked. “Yes!” I said. “You can do better too if you want. I was the last. Now, I’m the first. It’s all because I worked hard and had help from my friends.” When I went home, my mother saw my happy face and immediately knew I had good news. “Sam, you are all smiles,” she said. “Do you have something to tell me?" “Yes, I am first in my class! Look at my nice new bag. Look at the books! From now on, I’ll always work hard.”
author: Bansi Dhara

title: My Family
text: I have a large family. Let's meet them! This is my mom, and this is my dad. This is my brother, Neetu and this is my sister, Meetu. These are my paternal grandparents, and these are my maternal grandparents. My mom has three sisters. I call them 'Mausi'. And next... My dad has four brothers. I call two of them 'Thaauji' and two of them 'Chachaji'. Along with them... I also have two 'Thaayi' and two 'Chachi' as well. Let's see... There are five, young children in my family too. We all together cause mischief in the house. Look at how big my family is! Oh, wait! I almost forgot about Bujo. It wags its tail and barks, "Bow, bow, bow!!"
author: Shriya Badanhatti

title: WHEN A HAATHI IS NOT A SAATHI!
text: The village folks were in a dilemma. They had to prevent rogue elephants from devouring their crop! “The pachyderms feast on OUR food!” grumbled Anika. “I will give BAD elephants a nasty WHACK with a stick!” said Charinda, Anika’s little brother. “Elephants will WHACK you BACK with their big trunks!” warned his amma. “An electric fence around our fields will give the pachyderms a NASTY shock!” said Devinda. “Too dangerous,” said Gehan. “It could electrocute them and maybe kill them.” “The LOUD din we made last time made the jumbos go away,” reminded Devinda. “Yes! But the noise made us deaf,” grumbled Devinda’s grandfather. ““Our animals wailed in fright. We had cats snarling, hens clucking, babies wailing and dogs howling like wolves!” “My frightened hens did not lay eggs for weeks!” said Chitru. “My goats kept kicking me when I went to milk them!” said Himali, Anika’s friend. “Our dog hid under the bed for three days,” said Anika. “It forgot HOW to bark!” “My cat climbed up a coconut tree and refused to come down even when I showed it a FAT rat!” said Gehan. “Let’s burn firecrackers,” suggested Mohan. “We could also mix automobile grease, hot chilli-pepper oil and tobacco. This paste can be rubbed on our fence. Elephants will faint when they sniff the HORRIBLE smell!” said Devinda. “ Good idea!” shouted everyone. “My Lankan cousin says jumbos do not like to eat thibattu, lemon, orange, lasia, sesame, ginger, turmeric and black pepper,” said Suresh. “We should grow these near the fence around our fields. The jumbos will think we grow food they do not like and go away!” Devinda’s mobile phone rang. “My cousin says an elephant is walking towards our village,” said Devinda. “I can see it!” shouted Mohan. “LOOK!” They all fled into their homes. They would have to make a din to chase the pachyderm away as there was no time to do anything else! They did not see Gehan’s small brother, Rohan, sitting atop a tree. He held a hollow, wooden stick in which he had trapped ten angry bees! He saw the elephant trundling towards his village. Naughty Rohan grinned happily. He knew what he wanted to do with his bees! As the elephant came close to his tree, Rohan quickly unplugged his hollow stick from one side and pointed the open end at the elephant. He hit the stick with his hand. The angry bees flew out of the open hole and buzzed around the huge elephant. It turned around and fled back the way it came! “ I did it! ” shouted Rohan, slithering down the tree. “My bees chased the jumbo away!” “Elephants are scared of ants,” said Gehan. “I never knew they were also scared of bees!” “I am an idiot!” exclaimed Mohan. “We know you are!” retorted Gehan. “Last week,” said Mohan, “My cousin told me about a wildlife TV show in which they showed farmers in Kenya make wire fences with a beehive dangling at every 20 metres. When the wire fence sways, the bees rush out of their hives and scare away the elephants. The jumbos do not want to get a nasty sting in their sensitive eyes, big ears or long nose!” “And YOU withheld THIS elephant-repellent strategy from us!” accused Devinda. “I’m allergic to bees!” protested Mohan. “THAT is why I NEVER thought about this solution for our elephant woes!” The villagers now use the Kenyan BEE plan. Bee-hives dangle from a wire around their fields. The gap between each hive is 20m. When an elephant touches the wire, the hives will shake. This disturbs the bees. These then come out and buzz around the elephant. The buzz of the bees scares away the haathi! The villagers too benefit from this plan. They sell the bees’ HONEY to earn more MONEY! The bees also do useful work for them. Many types of nuts, vegetables and fruits need bee pollination to yield fruit. For the farmers it is a win-win situation. Bees SCARE away elephants and also provide the farmers with a more nutritious crop! Will this haathi bhagao strategy work? Like Mohan and his village compatriots, we too must WAIT and SEE!
author: Hema Rao

title: The Grim Reaper - a poem.
text: All around the world I've been Collecting souls of pure and mean I hide in plain sight Even the greatest crumble to my might Beware, for your time to come fast You know that life cannot forever last So live your life to the fullest Make no enemies from the smallest to biggest Be compassionate and kind Spread joy from your mind So live your life Before the reaper takes it from you
author: Dhairya Salwan

title: HOW THE FOREST KINGDOM WAS SAVED BY A RABBIT?
text: Once there lived a lion.He was the king of the forest. The animals didn't like the lion, because he was lazy and very cruel. There lived a rabbit.He was a sculptor. One day the King called the Rabbit to his palace. The Rabbit was very much frightened to go to the palace. Rabbit was afraid of being killed and eaten by the cruel King, but he had to obey the king's call.Somehow he gained some courage to go to the palace. Next day morning Rabbit reached the palace.He was presented before the King.He greeted the king. "Good morning! My-lord." "I'm the sculptor you called for." "I am at your service lord........Please order." The King began to speak........ "I have heard that you are a very good sculptor." "Make my statue." Rabbit: "Sure my lord,I will make a beautiful statue." He was in joy to listen but the next sentence gave him a shiver. The king said: "...it has to be lively just like me." Rabbit was shocked to hear the words of the king.How can one make a live statue, but however he didn't utter a word and returned from the palace shuddering. On the way he met one of his old friend the Porcupine. They were happy to meet after a long time and soon began to share their news. Though our Rabbit was happy his friend Porcupine could feel the tension. He asked: " Tell me dear rabbit what happened?I feel you are very tensed." Rabbit told him about the king's demand and all his fears in making the impossible statue The Porcupine consoled his friend.He told he had an idea. He had a very kind,strong and Good Lion as his friend from the neighboring forest. They decided to seek his help.They went to meet the Good Lion. The three of the m set a plan to save the Rabbit as well as the forest kingdom from the cruel lion. Some days passed by. The Rabbit went to the palace to meet the King.He said: 'My lord!'Rabbit said:" The statue is almost finished.Kindly come and give suggestions." The King Lion readily agreed to it as he was very much eager to see the statue and they immediately set for Rabbit's house. Meanwhile the Good Lion took the place of the lion-king statue at the rabbit's house. Very soon the Rabbit and the King Lion reached his home. Porcupine and the Good Lion was in their places as planned. The King was over joyed to see a very strong, healthy and lively lion statue. He went near the statue to have a close look. As he was about to touch it he had a strong snap at his face.The impact was so fierce that his vision blurred.He could feel hundreds of spines piercing his face and chest. The pain was immense.He was panicked by the sudden attack and fearing his life ran away from the forest. The animals were so happy that they made the Good Lion their king and clever Porcupine and brave Rabbit as the courtiers. as told by: DHANANJAY S.NAIR
author: neema s.nair
illustrator: Bhubaneshwar workshop  for children; Kingshuk Chaudhary; Promina Shreshtha

title: Luke see, Luke do. Luke hear, Luke say.
text: Luke adored his father. He followed him everywhere he could and learned a lot of things by watching his dad do them. He was a kind boy who always looked for opportunities to do good things. Even though he was only six years of age, he already had a big heart full of love and respect. His mom came home one day to find all the flower seedlings she had planned to plant that evening, already perfectly set in the ground, even better than she had thought. She Asked who did this. Luke answered and said: “I did mom. Just for you.” "aaahhh...I just got dirty for a good cause", Luke commented with giggles. This warmed his mother’s heart and filled it with joy. “Who helped you?”, she asked. Luke told her no one did. Mom asked: “How did you know to do it this way?” Luke answered: “I saw dad do it many times. Hear at home and at granma’s house. He told me boys must take good care of their mothers.” His mom was surprised but happy that he learned a good thing and did it for her. His dad came home carrying lots of groceries and asked mom to pack them since he was a bit too tired. Mom said she will do it as soon as she was done with the laundry. Luke overheard. While they spoke, he packed them exactly how he saw dad do it many times before, just more quietly. When done, he went into the living room. When mom came to the kitchen and did not find any groceries on the floor, she laughed and shouted to her husband not to play such games when she is so tired. Luke’s dad came from the bedroom where he was just resting on the bed, to see what his wife was on about. all the while, Luke was listening He said to her: “That was quick. You packed them up in no time and without any noise.” She looked at him a bit shocked but said nothing. She went to the cupboard. When she opened it, it was full of groceries. She opened the fridge and found it packed up as well. All was packed up and in order. They both called Luke at the same time. He came into the kitchen from the living room laughing. Dad asked if he did it. He told them he did. Dad asked: “But how…”. "It was easy", he said. I just did it how I saw you do it, Dad. The hard part was doing it quietly. They all laughed. Mom told dad how Luke planted her seedlings after school. His parents were so happy with him that they agreed that he deserved lunch and a movie on Saturday. Luke could hardly wait for two more nights to pass by and it is Saturday. Saturday came soon enough and Luke woke up with the fun he was going to have on his mind. Mom was already done cleaning the house and dad was outside from his run. They had breakfast and prepared to go watch the mid-morning movie then have lunch wherever Luke chose. While dad had a quick shower, Luke did his regular Saturday morning chore of washing the breakfast dishes. He was so happy. He said a prayer in his heart. He was giving thanks to God for his parents and all they have. When they were all done, they got into the car and drove to the mall. When they got to the mall, they ran into dad’s boss with his family. Luke knew him very well because he sometimes goes to work with his dad. Luke’s parents began to tell them what Luke has been doing and what they decided to do for him. His dad’s boss reached into his pocket and pulled some money notes and gave them to Luke. He said to Luke, as he gave him the money: “Good behaviour must be greatly rewarded. Keep it up, Luke.” The boss and his family were there to do some shopping. They said goodbye to Luke’s family and began to walk away. As they walked away, Luke spoke very disrespectfully about Penny, the boss’s daughter. All went painfully silent. The scene became tense instantly. The boss, red-faced, turned and asked Luke where he learnt such words from. Luke said I heard my dad say them about your wife, Mrs Carol. When I asked Him and Mr Japhta what it meant, they said it meant to carry her up so she never had to touch the ground with her feet again for a very long time. I too would like to carry Penny so that no dirt ever touched her feet again, Luke added. The children were not really aware of how bad things just turned. Mrs Carol began to cry, Her husband became even angrier. Luke’s dad was so ashamed that he just froze. Luke’s mom, very disappointed with Luke’s dad, walked across to apologise to Mrs Carol and comfort her. Luke's dad was in trouble in so many ways with nowhere to hide. The boss stepped up into Luke’s dad’s face and told him he was fired. He told him if he ever came to his company again, he would have him arrested. Looking at Luke, the boss told him that what he said about Penny was very bad and his dad lied to him about what it meant. He bent down to his knees so he could look at Luke in the eyes and said: "I was so happy to know that you have a good heart to see good and do it, to hear good and do it. Now I am deeply sad because your dad also taught you such a bad, bad thing." He told him never to say that again to anyone. Luke looked at his mother's face as one looking for truth. He was hoping his mothers' eyes would tell him what the boss said about his dad was a lie. Luke found what he did not want to see, it was true. They never watched the movie or had lunch. they Turned back to enter their car and drove back home. The boss and his family drove away to another mall. Luke was very sad because his father taught him the wrong thing when he always tells him to avoid doing wrong. He was mostly sad because his dad, whom he holds in such high regard, lied to him. This shook his tiny world in a bad way and he was never the same again. From that day on, he doubted most of what his dad would say to him. This affected his relationship with his dad in a bad way. Dad tried to be nicer to him by buying him nice toys. He even tried treating his friends to great meals but it did not change. It did not take the pain away. One afternoon, dad came to sit next to him. He asked Luke what he was doing. Luke told dad that he was reading a book. Dad told him he has heard him when he reads out loud in his bedroom. He told Luke that he was a very good reader and that he should keep it up. Luke liked his complement and thanked his father. The men of the house smiled at each other after many days of sadness. Dad said he was happy Luke kept on reading because it will make him smart. Luke looked at him and said: " I really love reading dad. It helps me see the world without going anywhere." His dad, proud of his son said: "Look how wise you are at such a young age and I was not the one who taught you to read." Luke, surprised, asked him who taught him. Dad told Luke that it was his grandmother who taught him then mom carried on from where she left off. Luke was not really aware of this and thought it was one of the things his dad taught him. Dad went on to say he is wise and learned many other things all by himself. Mom came home to find a happy Luke on her bed Reading a book. When she opened the door of the bedroom, Luke insisted she come sit with him a bit. He told her everything that happened with his dad today and how happy he was. Mom was also glad they are making peace. His father lost his job. His mother lost his innocent son and a friend in Carol. Their home was not so nice for a long, long time. Mom was the only one working and it took dad more than three years to find another job. Life became really hard. They found a way to forgive each other for everything but still, it was never the same again. His mother took him to the movies and lunch two weeks later at a different mall, on a different day. Luke continued to do amazing things for his mom because he loved how it made him and mom feel. Luke and his dad spent a lot of time reading together and to each other. They a way back to each other again through reading and doing a lot of other things together. The more Luke and dad made peace, there was also peace between mom and dad. Luke saw. Luke did. Luke heard and look still said but from now on, he thought carefully before speaking. Bey for now... we may meet again on the otherside of this walk in the park...
author: Nthabiseng  Machedi
illustrator: Ariful Islam; Gail Spencer; Greystroke; Keo  Phunphalla; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Seat Sopheap; Shivika Nayyar; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Wiehan de Jager

title: Not Green!!!
text: Mia and Tia are friends. They are writing the 'NOT GREEN' list. They are writing things that are not green in color on their note. "A cat is NOT GREEN!" says Tia. Mia agrees, "A cat can never be green". They draw a cat on their note. "Pumpkin is NOT GREEN! I have seen all of them are Orange," Mia says. They draw that too. Now Tia's turn. She says "Clouds are NOT GREEN! They are black, grey or orange or red or white. But they are never green!" Oh, no! Tia cannot get a thing that is not green. What can they do? Mia gets an idea. She says they can spot things that are not green using the books. They read the book and spot things that are always not green together. That bear is NOT GREEN! This dog and rabbit are NOT GREEN! These flowers are NOT GREEN! But that butterfly has green. This elephant is NOT GREEN! That dress is NOT GREEN! and the house and the shadow are NOT GREEN!!! It is a lot of fun to spot things that are NOT GREEN!! Can you also find NOT GREEN things in your book?
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan

title: Diya's Birthday Gift!
text: Diya is so happy. Her mother said to her that they are going to their native for the summer holidays. She likes being at native with Nana(grandpa) and Nani(grandma). Diya loved them so much. She loved everything about her native. She can play outside all day long. She liked to run around the garden near her house where there are many flowering plants and trees for shade. Her Nani will read her a lot of stories daily. The stories where so interesting where Raja and Rani will be ruling their country. Some problems will occur. Raja will solve the problem using his intelligence. Sometimes he will roam in his country in disguise and spot the problem. There were a lot of morals in those stories. Raja will always be wise and honest. When some Raja was not wise, his minister will help him. All those stories made Diya feel brave and happy. She would tell all those stories to her friends when she is back at school after the leave. She also liked her Nana, who will take her around the village in the evening and showing her all the things there and explaining about them. He did know a lot about how plants grow, and their importance to life on earth. When they walk around the garden, he will show the plants in there and tell what plant it is, what it is used for. There were lots of trees in the garden. Diya liked the mango tree the best. It was so big and when she goes there in summer, it was full of fruit. Nana will say that the mango tree was planted by her mother when she was studying the sixth standard. And now it had grown really big and giving fruits to them. "This year when we are in native, I will try to climb up the tree. And I will pick my mango.", Diya said to her mom. "I will sit on a branch and eat that mango and the next one and another after another. I will eat only mango this year and drink Nani's mango lassi. All birds in the tree will come and say 'Please leave some fruits for us' to me. " Diya's imagination began to grow wildly. Her mom laughed at her and said before that we have to plan and prepare for the travel. She jumped out of the chair she was sitting in. "Yes! I will help you! I will take all my dresses and things I want to take to the native. I am a grown girl now. So I know what dresses I should take." She ran to the room where dresses are kept and began to put them on the bed for packing. "I will also join you and we can pack together." said her mom. They started arranging dress, and toiletries in their bags. Diya is really happy to help her mom in packing things. When she saw her mother took her birthday dress from the drawer to pack she was so excited. "Are we celebrating my birthday in our native this year?" she asked. "Oh yes, " said her mom with a big smile on her face. Her mom and Diya did get to their Native as per plan. There Diya was having lots of fun. She did not miss any of her favorite things like Nani's story, an evening walk with Nana and the mango tree planted by her mom. A week after they come there, Diya's birthday came. She was really happy to celebrate her birthday with Nana and Nani. She wore her new dress they had packed and wondered what gift she will be receiving from her grandparents. In the morning, they all went to a temple nearby. When they come back, Nana and Nani went back to their normal work. She thought maybe they will be giving the gift once lunch is prepared. Lunch was served with sweets and her favorite mango lassi. This does not fulfill her wish for a gift. So she went to her mom and asked secretly about the gift from Nana and Nani. Her mom smiled at her and told her to go and play. She said she will definitely get a gift. When it became evening, it was time to walk with Nana. She went running to Nana and found him in the garden. "I knew you will come searching for me. Now finally it is time for the birthday gift," said Nana with a big smile. He handed Diya the gift and it was a MANGO PLANT!. Diya felt the present to be very special. Then, they both dig a hole in the garden and planted the Mango plant. Nana told her ways to care for the plant and when to water the plant. He told Diya should water it whenever she is in native. Diya enjoyed her holidays at native with Nana and Nani. She got to meet new kids there. They all become friends soon. They all will be playing together. They all played games and run around the garden. They made a swing and played under the tree shade. One of them helped Diya learn to climb the mango tree. They spent a good time under the tree. She learned a lot of other things too. She learned swimming and riding a bicycle all as fun. Whenever she goes around the tree planted by her mom, she felt proud of it. She told all the other kids about it and also showed them hers in the garden. She even dreams of kids playing under the tree she had planted on her birthday. And she never forgets to water it or take care of it. Diya loved her Nana's gift of all she got. She knew it will remind not only about herself but also Nana whenever she would see it. And she felt so grateful for the gift. She now knew what is the best thing she could gift her loved ones.
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan

title: Nancy's love box
text: Nancy is an eight-year-old girl. She likes to collect small toys, stickers and all the things she likes to keep. She would put her tiny bouncy balls, into her old plastic Easter egg shells and pretend to be a real egg. She will peel off glittery stickers from cards, and keep it in her note. Also, she gets tiny toys from her piano class treasure box like shiny rings, design erasers, small cars, glows in dark wands... She would put all her collections in a box, which her mom gives to her. She had decorated that box with gift wraps and ribbons and made it look like a pink castle. She called that box her love box and would put all the things she got into it. She will play with some of those things but always remembered to keep it back inside her love box. One day, Judy one of her friend visited her home for a play date. Nancy was excited to play with her. She showed her friend her love box. Judy became very fond of one shiny ring and asked her if she can have it. At first, Nancy was not happy with the idea of giving that to Judy. But later she thought Judy is a good friend and gave the ring to her. Next day, Judy showed her ring to all other friends at school and told everybody about Nancy's love box. Nancy felt really proud of her collection. Also from thereafter, Nancy began to share her things with her friends whenever she thought of appreciating them. She would give them toy on their birthday, card with glittery stickers and shiny rings when she visited others house. This made Nancy feel good. So she started to do this often that her collection began to grow less. But Nancy did not notice this. One day, Nancy's teacher got to know this collection and asked Nancy to bring her love box to school the next day. But when she got home Nancy noticed that she had left with only one thing in her love box. Anyhow she took the box to the school. Nancy's teacher was so happy to share the habit of collecting with the entire class. She insisted that everybody should have a hobby like this. Nancy got an idea. She stood up and said, she had decided to give the love box to the class. She said, anyone can drop the things inside the box and when they need to appreciate others, can take a thing from the box to give to their friends. This became a big hit with the class. Everybody began to use this and Nancy became a very good friend of everyone else in the class. She indeed made one more love box to keep at home and continued to collect items so she can gift her family and friends.
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan

title: In the Classroom
text: “Sir, Bhola is making faces at me.” “No, sir, I was scratching my ears, so my face was a bit twisted.” Teacher, with perfect confidence and without opening his eyes, said, “Ah! Always being naughty! Keep standing.” For half a minute, the class was quiet. Then voices were heard again. “Why aren’t you standing up?” “Why should I stand up?” “Sir told you to stand up.” “No way! Ask Gansha. Hey, Gansha, didn’t Sir ask him to stand up?” Ganesh stood up slowly and began calling Teacher. “ Sir! Hello, Sir!” Teacher replied, irritated, “Yes, go on!” Ganesh asked anxiously, “Whom did you order to stand, Sir?” Teacher opened his eyes, glared at Ganesh and snapped, “I’m ordering you—keep standing!” And immediately closed his eyes again. Ganesh kept standing. The class was quiet again for a minute or so. Then, suddenly, Bhola said, “Didn’t sir ask him to stand on one leg?” Ganesh said, “No, never. He just said, ‘Keep standing’.” Bishu said, “But he held up one finger. That means you should stand on one leg.” Ganesh could not deny that Teacher had held up one finger while scolding him. Bishu and Bhola kept insisting, “Stand on one leg right now, or we shall tell sir.” Poor Ganesh hastened to stand on one leg. Immediately, Bhola and Bishu started arguing. One said Ganesh should stand on his right leg; the other said, no, left leg first. Poor Ganesh was in a fix. He tried asking Teacher again, “Sir, which leg?” At that moment, Teacher was dreaming of something and snoring in great surprise at the strange dream. At Ganesh’s question, he was startled out of his sleep and woke up choking. Poor Ganesh had not imagined that his question could bring forth such a response. He was frightened. “Oh, no! What will happen now?” Bhola said, “Run and get some water.” Bishu said, “Quickly sprinkle some water on his head.” Ganesh ran out of the classroom, brought back a large jug of water from somewhere and began pouring it on Teacher’s shining bald head. Teacher stopped choking, but when Ganesh looked at his face, his hands, with the large jug of water, began shaking. Everyone was scared and looked grave. But poor Shyamlal had such a face—such a happy, smiling face—that he could not look grave even though he tried. Teacher’s anger went and settled on him. In a voice like the low growl of a tiger, he said, “Come here!” Shyamlal almost started crying. He said, “What did I do? Gansha poured the water, so what can I do?” Teacher was a fair man. He let Shyamlal go and turned towards Ganesh. He was still holding the jug of water. Without waiting for a question, Ganesh said, “Bhola told me.” Bhola said, “I just told him to get the water. Bishu said, ‘Pour it on his head’.” Bishu said, “Did I ask him to pour it on sir’s head? He should have poured it on himself; his head would have cleared then.” For some time, Teacher sat glaring at everyone. Then he said, “Fine. You are kids, so I won’t punish you. Make sure that you don't do anything like this again.” Everyone heaved a great sigh of relief. But nobody could understand why Teacher had suddenly softened. Only Teacher himself knew which of his childhood pranks he had suddenly recollected. translated from Ajob Shaja by Sukumar Ray
author: Kamalika Mitra
illustrator: Ayoub  Makotha; Canato Jimo; Rijuta Ghate; Ruchi Shah; Sanjay Sarkar; Shailja Jain Chougule; Students of  Himalayan Public School; Suvidha Mistry

title: Good Friend!
text: "I don't like to be a friend with Sharmi anymore", declared Renu as she came home from school. "Why? What's the matter?", asked her mother. "You know we both are really good friends. But still, she complained about me to the teacher and the teacher made me walk all the recess time. So I'm not a friend to her anymore", Renu continued reasoning. "Renu, tell me all that happened at school today. I will help you with this friendship thing", mother said. "Today during recess at school, we all were playing and running around the playground. I fell and hurt my elbow. See this, here", Renu showed her elbow to her mother. "Did Sharmi pushed you down?" mother asked. "No, I tripped and fell. But that's not the reason. " "Okay. I'm all ears. Tell me", said mother. " As I fell, and hurt myself, I and Sharmi went to a teacher for first-aid. Teacher cleaned it with cotton and applied ointment over this. And then we went to sit on the side of the ground and we rested under a tree shade. This bruise was hurting me very badly. So at some point, I told a bad word to say how bad it hurts me. " "And Sharmi told teacher about you being foul-mouthed?" asked her mom. "Yes!", said Renu. "You know what. Sharmi is a very good girl and she has done exactly what I would expect you to do when you are a good friend to somebody" said her mom with a smile on her face. "What? She made me walk all through the recess period, while all others are playing and you are supporting her?" Renu asked her mother with water ready to reel down in her eyes. "No Renu. Listen to me", her mother wiped the tears away and continued, "A good friend is not the one who will be with you only when you have fun. A good friend is one who will be with you on fun and sad times. She will be the first one to congratulate you and also to correct you when you do the wrong things. Sharmi did the same. She wanted you to behave well in all situations. Using bad words will not help you at all. Did it relieve your pain?" "No!" said Renu. "See. That's the point. It won't help you. When people hear you say bad words, they will think you are a bad person. And Sharmi does not want you to continue saying bad words. So she complained to the teacher. Can you now understand? Are you still mad at her?" asked her mom. Renu did understand. She nods her head. And she said, "You are right mom. I will also be a good friend hereafter. And I will thank Sharmi tomorrow when I see her because she made me realize how wrong I was".
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan

title: Up above the world so high!
text: Let's Go Outside. Lay on your back and watch what is there in the sky? Are you ready? Can you see the blue sky and clouds? Some are white, some are grey. But when it is going to rain, the clouds are dark and black. If it looks black now, g et inside the house. Come back later to look up! Sometimes you can see kites swaying in the sky Waving a real big 'HI'! Or a lot of butterflies If flowers are near-by!! You may see crows fly Oh! can you hear them cry? And airplanes zipping across Leaving white trails as they pass It becomes bright orange and red When the sun is ready to set! Next, come the moon and starry night! Look what a beautiful sight! Wait! it's not yet over! Let's use a telescope to see deeper!! Those shooting stars are meteors! Burning as they fall to earth!! Can you see the stars forming patterns? Those are called constellations! There are lots of satellites orbiting. In the space between the moon and the earth. They are man-made. To help us in various ways. One of which is ISS(International Space Station). Where astronauts work flying around the station! Farther than the moon, come lines of planets in our solar system. They all orbit our sun just like we do. They look shiny but not twinkle at night when you see with naked eyes. Humans have launched rockets into space. It helps us understand what is life's base. Sun, its eight planets, meteors and comets form the solar system. We have sent a satellite that has crossed the whole solar system and continues to travel into space. Its called Voyager 1. It is the most distant man-made object from the Earth. Lots of stars combine to form Galaxy. Our solar system is in a galaxy named "Milky Way". There are lots and lots of galaxies in Space. Yet Earth is the only place to host life as far as we know!!!
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan
illustrator: Aditi Dilip; Ankita  Thakur; Deepa Balsavar; Hari Kumar Nair; Mbongeni Fongoqa; Shivika Nayyar; Vidyun Sabhaney; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Game of CAMOUFLAGE
text: Can you spot the hare in the photo? Look carefully. It is camouflaging(read as KA-MUH-FLAA-ZHUNG). Camouflaging mean to hide in a surrounding by making it to hard to see. Many animals and insects in nature uses camouflage to protect itself from its predators. Predators are animals which would attack and kill them. They use lots of techniques to blend in its surroundings. Sometimes they use their natural body designs and patterns to resemble its surroundings like the moth sitting on the dry leaf. Can you spot the leaf-insect hiding in the picture? It is using its resemblance to the surroundings to hide. What about this lizard? This lizard is using its pattern on body as a disguise to approach the prey it wants to eat. Yes! Sometimes predators use its resemblance to nature to hide itself from prey so they wont escape easily. Even big animals such as cheetah uses its spot to camouflage while hunting. Its spots are helpful to hide in the bushes and dry grasses. Now spot the frog hiding in this picture. Some animals hide themselves by being so close to the ground. This helps them to remove their shadow and making hard for others to see. This Mantis is using the same technique to camouflage. Can you see the Gecko hiding on the bark of tree? Where is the owl in this picture? This one is really hard. Can you spot the plant hopper? No? Its sitting on the lower left stem with its two legs and the front legs on the thin stem. We humans also use camouflage technique. The military uniforms are based on resemblance to the surroundings. The army planes painted are blue to minimize them being spotted.
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan
illustrator: Arkapriya Koley; Jayaprakash Bojan; Karthikeyan S.

title: My Grandma's cat
text: Wilson is my grandma's cat, but he's not a normal cat. He doesn't like to catch mice, I think he would prefer to be friends with them. A few weeks ago I started to notice that Wilson was going out every day after lunch, I though he was just going to visit his friends that live nextdoor. ﻿But one day I decided to follow him. It turns out that his best friend was a beatiful tiger, they would spend the rest of the day in the forest next to the lake. Now I understand why Wilson doesn't go out with other cats, it must be great to have a tiger as a friend and I'm glad he has one. I'm going to keep the secret, my grandma is not ready for the big news.
author: Valentina Isadora Vittini

title: Surprise! Surprise!
text: I asked Ajji," May i Please have these yummy for my tummy Laddoos?" She my heart as she uttered,"Not now, beta, may be a little later, not today though, you will get it tomorrow." But I had no patience so,I could not wait till tomorrow With a heavy heart i thought for the park i asked Ajja," May I go out to play with my friends?" he got me into his sweet lovely trap, he simply said," Little later you may go my chap, before that you have to take your nap." But I had no patience to wait till the nap Then i saw my superman dress,With all my heart i went to mom to address," Can i wear my new costume and do my zip,. zap, zooom" O her words cleared my doubt when she plainly refused saying you may wear it when we go out The box attracted me to it right from the start, How to take permission from dad to open it is an unknown art. He refused right away and told me to simply wait. I wanted it right there i knew for sure, So I could not wait any more. I went to bed with a heavy heart, why do they never learn to say 'yes'? why the elders cannot learn that art? I went to bed all annoyed Next day when i entered the kitchen it was a sweet surprise. Ajji came to me with a smile She said in her volume which is usually low,," You can eat these laddoos now." Ajja said,' bring your bat and ball, its time to hit the six as cricket will b e played by all."Papa also gave me permission to open the box and before i thought it was a haux, I had everyone around me clapping and smiling and loudly they say," Happy Birthday!"
author: jyotsna kothari

title: The Lion & The Fox
text: Story Description A fox finds a hyena skin floating in a river, and immediately tells the local king, a lion, what he has found. The lion tells the fox that he planted it there, as a warning to a chimp and a hyena to stop stealing from the river area. When the chimp and the hyena go to see the lion, the lion invites the fox to play a trick on the two animals. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Hyena ﻿hi-yee-na ﻿The laughter came from the hyena. Tempting ﻿tem-p-ting Despite the danger from the crocodile, it was still tempting to steal from by the river.﻿ Shrieked ﻿sh-ree-k-d ﻿The hyena shrieked when he found the hyena skin in the river. Rewarded re-war-did ﻿﻿ The lion rewarded the fox with an outside chair and a house extension. In a vast, quiet and colourful land, a fox was navigating the valleys while the leader of the land, a lion, watched over his kingdom. Suddenly, the fox went running up to the lion with important news. After telling the lion what he had seen, the lion ordered the fox to go with him immediately to his village. The fox had been walking by the river shore when he saw something strange sticking out of the shallow area. The fox thought he had seen a reflection of something on the bank. On closer inspection, the fox found a hyena's skin in the river. Shocked, he went to find the lion and tell him of the discovery. "The crocodile is back," said the lion to the fox, in a private meeting in his tent. "That's what your finding means. The crocodile is hunting by the river again. I thought he wasn't coming back, but it looks like he has returned." "Oh, that is scary!" said the fox. "But it's a joke," laughed the lion. "What you found is an old hyena skin that I placed there yesterday. It was intended to scare off a chimp and a hyena that keep stealing food from there. I need to teach them a lesson. Can you help me, fox?" The fox agreed to help the lion and the lion explained his plan. Very soon, the chimp and the hyena were in the area. "Oh, boy," said the chimp to the hyena as they approached the lion's hut. "We had better behave ourselves around the king. We don't want him to know we've been thieving again." "Don't worry," said the hyena. "I won't tell him a thing. Hopefully from hearing one of his stories, we can find a new place to steal from." "Good plan," said the chimp. "Well, if it isn't my good friends, the hyena and the chimp!" said the lion. "How are you doing?" "We're fine," said the chimp. "But we're stuck for money." "Oh, that sounds terrible," said the lion. "Perhaps I can tell you another one of my educational stories." "Yeah," said the hyena. "We were hoping that one of your stories could give us some inspiration to, you know, make a living." "Come on inside," said the lion. "I have the perfect tale for you." The lion began telling his new story: "One day, there was a monkey taking a ride on a crocodile's back to the shore. They were hunting for food together. The croc was getting annoyed with the monkey, because he kept pestering him to swim faster. Suddenly the monkey started talking about finding a treasure trove of food." "Oh, that's interesting," said the hyena and the monkey. "I hear this island has a lot of food," said the monkey. "Coconuts, pineapples, wild animals, and lots of other fruits and vegetables. There's a whole bounty of sweet food waiting to be found! Let's go over there." "All you ever think about is your stomach," complained the crocodile." And you never pay me for these river rides. Where's my share of the food?" "I don't have to pay you, because you're just an ordinary croc!" said the monkey, making the crocodile even angrier. "Here's the deal," said the crocodile. "If I give you a ride back across the river, you have to give me half of the food you find, otherwise I won't bring you back here again." "Oh, that monkey is stuck now. He will get so much food, but he won't get to keep it all," said the chimp. "There's more to the story," said the lion. "The crocodile demanded an up front fee, meaning he asked for money from the monkey right at that moment." "But the monkey blew a fart sound at the crocodile and ran away," said the lion. "The crocodile got up and chased the monkey to the trees. Ever since then, nobody has seen that monkey...or that crocodile." "Wow, that's scary," said the chimp. "What kind of monkey was it?" "A chimp," said the lion, scaring the chimp. "Rumour has it that the crocodile also hunts...hyenas." The hyena shrieked and swallowed hard. "Oh, no," he said. "Whatever we do, we cannot go down to the beach and hunt around," said the chimp. "Because we'll get hunted, right?" The hyena knew about the food and treasures hidden by the river, and understood what the chimp was talking about. But still, despite the danger, the hyena found the river area tempting. The chimp insisted they hunt elsewhere. The lion gave the fox a quick wink, and the fox silently laughed under his breath. "Are you really sure about this nasty sounding crocodile?" asked the hyena. "Because I would love to spend time by the river, so I just need your assurance that what you are saying is true." "I speak nothing but the truth," said the lion, sternly and seriously. The chimp took a step back. "All right, we have to go now," the chimp said to the hyena, as they planned to steal from somewhere else far away. The lion rewarded the fox with a lovely outside chair and an extra room built on to his house. There he could relax and watch the sunset everyday, seeing the flocks of birds fly in packs over the region. The hyena, meanwhile, went hunting down by the river shore, and he found the hyena's skin that was planted by the lion. He screamed and he and the chimp ran far away, determined never to try and steal from by the river again. The lion and the fox's trick had worked! ﻿After Reading ﻿What did the fox find in the river and which animal planted it there? What does the fox agree to do with the lion? What happens in the story that the lion tells to the chimp and the hyena? Why does the crocodile get annoyed with the monkey? What do the hyena and the chimp end up trying to do anyway, and what happens? What do you think is the moral of the story?
author: Hello English

title: Chattori Jeebh
text: Ronit is very excited. Mumma......Sehaj has invited me for a birthday party today!! Can I go Pleeeeeease!! "Yes you can beta, But be careful what you eat." Said Mother "Enjoy the party". Ronit goes to the party. Hurray!! Mridul, Piyush and Neena were also there. "The cake looks tasty!" Neena Shouted "Give me the balloons",exclaimed Piyush. All of them ate laddos, cake, samosa and drank juice..and much much more Ronit came back happy but by 10' O clock he felt uneasy. He started vomiting. He started shouting," Mumma!! Mumma!!" His mother came running to his room. 'What happened?" asked mother. " I have a terrible pain in my stomach." cried Ronit Mother patted Ronit with love and brought a glass of cold milk for him. Ronit drank it and laid in his mother's lap. He slept peacefully and woke up in the morning fully recovered. He came running to his mother. " I am feeling absolutely fine! What did you do? You are a magician!" Mother smiled and said, " That is not true. I realized that you had eaten a lot of junk food in the party yesterday. This caused acid flow in your digestive system. I just gave you cold milk which is a base to neutralize the acidity." "It was not MAGIC but SCIENCE ".
author: Openderjeet Kaur
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Megha Vishwanath; Nicci  Nathanson; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Rijuta Ghate; Ruchi Shah; Sandhya Prabhat

title: Moutushi's Song
text: Sinha Little Moutushi is very busy today. She flies from one branch to another on the big neem tree. On the big neem tree is a big beehive. Bees buzz around, collecting nectar. “I want nectar too,” Moutushi says to herself. “Let me look around and see if I can find some nectar,” Moutushi thinks. It is a cold winter afternoon. In a big house by the neem tree, Didima is enjoying the afternoon sun. Flowers are blooming in the pots on the balcony. Phat Phat Phat! Moutushi flies down to a pretty red flower. She drinks nectar with her needle-like beak. “Aah, my tummy is full!” Moutushi is feeling sleepy. “I will rock myself to sleep on the branch of this tree.” Two mynahs come flying to the balcony. They start fighting with each other. Oh no, Moutushi’s sleep flies away. She hates fighting. Moutushi decides to fly away as well. Phat Phat Phat! Before she goes, she sings a little song for Didima. “Didima calls, ‘Where are you?’ I am here. Tui, tui, tuu. Didima says, ‘Are you lost, are you?’ No, I am right here. Tui, tui, tuu. Didima asks, ‘Did you drink the nectar, did you?’ Yes, my tummy is full. Tui, tui, tuu.”
author: Sukanya  Sinha

title: Rolling
text: Glass can roll. Bottle can roll. Fork cannot roll. Soccer ball can roll. Takraw ball can roll. Racket cannot roll. Longan fruit can roll. Sweetsop fruit can roll. Banana cannot roll. Pipe can roll. Bucket can roll. Broom cannot roll. Tomato can roll. Chinese turnip can roll. Turmeric root cannot roll. Someday we will be able to roll. We want to roll too.
author: All Children Reading Cambodia

title: Mori's secret
text: A long, long time ago, in the deep, dark jungle lived a beautiful and proud peacock whose name was Mori. Mori was always the life of any party. He would display his beautiful feathers for his friends to admire. He could always bring a smile to anybody's face. One day, Dimple, the deer visited Mori. They had a nice little chat about the weather, and moved to discuss more serious things. Like their hobbies! Mori let Dimple on a secret - Mori loved to dance but was too shy to show anybody her dance. Dimple had a fantastic idea! "Why not dance when it rains? That way nobody is outside and you can dance like no one is watching!", said Dimple. "Oh! That is such a brilliant idea, Dimple! Why didn't I think of it!" Ever since that day, the peacock always danced when it rained! A flamboyant dance to show off his colourful tail feathers. A dance that nobody who watched would forget. So go on, and watch from afar!
author: Iswarya Balakrishnan

title: It's Too Loud!
text: Story Description Marco works collecting bananas and walking cows. The city is so loud and busy, and Marco gets upset at all of the noise. Marco looks for a way to get rid of the noise so he can work well and feel happy again. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Bellowing bel-o-wing﻿ The car horns were bellowing into Marco's ears.﻿ Revving ﻿re-v-ing ﻿The vehicles were revving their engines. Deafening ﻿def-un-ing ﻿ ﻿The noise was so bad it was deafening. Yield ﻿yee-ul-d ﻿Marco had a good yield of bananas because he had found so many. It's too loud! Marco had a job moving cows and collecting bananas from around the city. He couldn't concentrate, because he was surrounded by constant noise: mooing from the cows, meowing from the cats, bellowing from the bulls, and loud banging coming from the city. Marco always had a headache, and he couldn't escape from the noise. "I'm tired of this noise," said Marco. "If only I could get some silence and peace!" His cows were terrified by the loud traffic, the screeching, the beeping and the revving engines. They were so scared that they ran, taking Marco with them. "I can't do this anymore!" said Marco, as some construction workers powered up their drills and made a loud clattering noise. "I still have ringing in my ears," said Marco, as he struggled to sleep. "When will it ever end?" To make things worse, insects buzzed and whizzed around Marco while he was in bed. The noise was constant. Even when he tried to rest, Marco sat up wide awake whenever there was a sound. "I can't even get to sleep!" he said. At the weekend, Marco sat outside by his favourite tree. As he was enjoying the park, he was suddenly struck by a tennis ball. Lots of dogs ran around Marco, barking and fighting over the ball. Then a cow sneaked up on Marco and mooed loudly in his ear. "I've had enough!" said Marco to his wife. "I'm going to resolve this noise problem once and for all. No longer is noise going to bother me." "What are you going to do?" said his wife. "I'm still figuring it out!" said Marco. "Hmm...what is that? It looks interesting," said Marco, as he watched a man walk by wearing headphones and listening to music. "It drowns out noise by playing music. I have to get one for myself so I can concentrate at work!" The next day, Marco left the house wearing something he had bought for himself. It was a pair of headphones, and he had also bought two pairs for his cows. Now he could work in silence and peace, ignoring the traffic zooming by and the deafening sounds of the city. He felt calm and relaxed. So calm was Marco, that for a while, he took off his headphones and performed his job better. With extra concentration, he found more bananas than ever before! He worked with a smile on his face and a skip in his step, despite the noise. He knew he could escape from the noise at any time, just by putting on his headphones. Marco came home from work feeling happy and upbeat. The family was surprised at seeing the new Marco, who was not stressed out, and who took everything in a relaxed way. "Hello, everyone!" said Marco. They were so happy to see he had changed. "Wow, Dad sure is different," said one of the kids. Marco surprised everyone with his massive yield of bananas. In just one day, he had found a week's worth. He sold them to the market stalls, and he made more money than he had ever made before. Marco kept on working with his headphones on. His secret to success? No distractions and no noise! After Reading Why did Marco feel stressed? What kinds of things create lots of noise? What did Marco wear to give him relief from the noise? Who else did he buy them for? How did Marco's family react when they saw he had changed? What was Marco able to do with better concentration?
author: Hello English

title: Dreaming cat
text: In the era of pirates on the island of ClawVile there was a kitten named Olivia. She was a pirate and all other animals were terrified of her skills in fighting with a sword. She had a crew who worshipped her and followed her every step with complete faith. Every pirate's pride lies in their crew and ship and her ship spoke her message loud and clear: Cats Rule! To make her dream come true, she worked hard and fought all her enemies. It took her 15 years in capturing all islands, except for one and they were her worst enemies. It was the Fox Island, she was now one step away from her goal of capturing the world and getting defeated would be a nightmare that she was unwilling to see. So she fought with all she had. Her and her crew faced a lot of difficulties and were severely injured many times but all of their hard work and sacrifices were rewarded with the sweet truth of conquering the Fox Island. Even Though it took them 2 months, their achievement was all worthy of their work. Now Olivia was the most powerful and undefeatable pirate in the world and everybody bowed at her feet. At that time Olivia felt truly happy and invincible. She knew that from now on nobody would treat her and her tribe badly or disrespectfully. Suddenly Olivia jolted up and realised she was on her bed and that her conquering the world was all just a dream, her first reaction was being so angry that she could just trash her surroundings but her second reaction ended up making a motto to turn this dream into an actual reality and then live happily ever after. So that night Olivia slept with her now only single goal to achieve; to capture all islands and paint the entire world with her mantra.i.e, Cats Rule.
author: Tanisha Jain

title: HOLIDAYS
text: One day, Sloka took her little brother Sameer to the library where their uncle Sudheer worked. Uncle Sudheer welcomed them into the library. He explained to them about the various interesting books in the library. Sloka and Sameer then began searching for a suitable book to read. They liked all the books and decided to read them one by one. They began reading. They read a few books they liked. They decided to visit the library everyday during the holidays.
author: Annapurna Sharma

title: The Tiger Toy's Biscuits
text: Story Description The tiger toy makes his own biscuits and sells them. With the help of the cat, he tries to sell as many as he can for his business. But after a while, something starts to go wrong, and all of the animals can feel it inside. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Clumsy ﻿clum-z-ee ﻿The cat was known to be clumsy, always dropping her biscuits. Admiring ﻿ad-my-ur-ing ﻿The tiger toy was lying down, admiring his fat belly. Especially ess-pesh-ul-ee﻿ ﻿The tiger toy made biscuits, especially for his friends. Unbelievable ﻿un-bih-lee-vuh-bul ﻿﻿ ﻿ ﻿The tiger toy felt it was unbelievable that the monkey wanted to buy all of his biscuits. "Wow, what are those?" said the animals as they watched a cat go past pushing a cart. "Are they what I think they are?" "Socks," said the youngest animal. "No, they're not socks. They're biscuits and cookies. for sale. Wow, they look delicious. Hey, cat! Stop!" The cat saw the toys and shouted, "These are not for you! They are all mine!" "What a strange cat," said the animals. "Come and get your biscuits!" called out the tiger toy, walking along the beach and searching for the animals. But there was nobody there. He walked along the entire length of the beach and didn't see anyone else. "I wonder where they are," he said, scratching his head. "And I wonder how many biscuits the cat has sold already." "Hey, give us your biscuits!" cried out the toys, as the cat felt startled by their sudden ambush. They chased after the cat, trying to snatch the biscuits. "You can't take these, they don't belong to you!" said the cat, eating the biscuits. "We'll see about that," said the pig, as the deer and the monkey chased after the cat's cart. "Ah, Mr. Piggy!" said the tiger toy. "What are you doing out here alone?" "I'm waiting for the tide to go out so I can play sand tennis," said Mr. Piggy. "Otherwise there's not enough room to play." "Well, while you're waiting, how about a biscuit?" "They're a strange shape," said Mr. Piggy. "I made them myself, that's why. I can't make perfect circles. Hey, you could help me out by buying a couple. Try them and see for yourself how tasty they are!" After Mr. Piggy bought some biscuits, the tiger toy went back to his home kitchen. "Wow, I managed to sell some biscuits, but not all of them!" he said. "Now to make another batch and to see how many the cat has sold." The cat was helping the tiger toy to sell his biscuits, but the tiger knew the cat was clumsy and silly. "How's it going?" he asked the cat over the phone. "I did it again," said the cat. "I ate them all." "You selfish cat." "Well, let's see how many of these I can sell," said the tiger toy. "With a bit of luck and sales charm, I can make a packet from these." The tiger toy piled his different varieties of biscuits high into the air, carefully balancing them as he pushed his cart into the street. But before long, the tiger toy was bored. Nobody bought his biscuits. Instead, he started eating them one by one, until he could no longer stand up. He spread himself flat on the ground, admiring his fat belly and looking at the clouds. "I shouldn't have eaten all those biscuits," he said. "I'm just as bad as the cat." Very soon, Mr. Piggy came over and sat next to the tiger toy. "What are you doing here?" said the pig. "I feel sick from your biscuits." "So do I," said the tiger toy. "I should change the recipe so that others don't get sick too!" They both spread themselves flat on the ground, sweating, fat and feeling sick from the biscuits. Soon the tiger toy started to feel better, and he changed his recipe. He cooked more biscuits and found a monkey toy hiding in a tree. The monkey toy bought a few biscuits, tried them, and she really liked them. "They're unbelievable," she said. "I want to buy the lot from you." "That's fantastic," said the tiger toy. "And another three entire cart loads as well!" said the monkey toy. The tiger toy couldn't believe his ears. It felt like Christmas. All of the toys came over to celebrate the tiger toy's success. The cat apologised for eating all of the biscuits and then she agreed to help the tiger toy sell more of his new biscuits. "We're going to make a great team," said the cat. "Only if you don't eat all of my biscuits," said the tiger toy. "I'm making an entire batch of biscuits especially for all of you, because you are my friends," said the tiger toy. The toys cheered and ate the new biscuits, but then they slowly started to feel sick. Then the monkey toy phoned, complaining of stomach pains. "Oh, dear," said the tiger toy. "I've done it again!" After Reading What did the toy tiger make and sell? Who helped the toy tiger, and what did they do to cause trouble? Who bought biscuits and felt ill after eating them? Who suddenly decided to buy three batches of biscuits? Why did the toy tiger suddenly celebrate? Despite changing his recipe, what happened to someone when they ate the biscuits?
author: Hello English

title: Reflections
text: I and my friend Raghav got down at Vijayawada station and began walking out. There was a lot of hurly-burly at the station with crowds of people getting on and off the trains and vendors with an array of food. "Ever since Amaravathi has been made the capital of Andhra, the population here has increased manifold", said Raghav, walking, carrying his suitcase with one hand. "All these crowds you see are just people coming and going on small jobs. There is no connection between them and the fact that Amaravathi has been made the new capital of Andhra", I corrected. Then, right in front of our eyes, a man approached a wearily dozing passenger, adroitly pulled out his wallet, extracted all the cash and replaced it, after counting the notes as if he had all the time in the world! So right-royally did that man walk up to the passenger and take out his purse that it took a while for it to sink in that he was a thief! By the time we raised an alarm, shouting, 'Thief, Thief', shook the passenger awake and apprised him of his loss, the thief has already escaped. No one caught him. And we the witnesses couldn't chase him, being old you see. The now fully awake passenger began to howl. Raghav, having seen him lose hundreds, pressed a ten rupee note into his hand and asked him to take some coffee. I didn't do even that. 'Almighty Lord, protect us!', I muttered, too unnerved to be clear about who was to be protected from whom. We checked our purses and suitcases and were about to head towards the foot over-bridge to exit when a man approached me. 'Do you recognize me?', he asked. I adjusted my spectacles and after examining him closely, answered, ' I am sorry, I don't. Perhaps because I am old'. His forehead was covered with thick horizontal lines of ash and a big vermilion dot. He seemed familiar, yet unfamiliar. 'You are from Nellore, aren't you, don't you recognize me', he asked again. 'Yes, I am from Nellore too, however I don't recognize you', I answered. 'I am Venkatramana from your neighbourhood medical shop - do you remember now? Kumar's brother in law.' Thus saying, he turned to two women and a man standing a little further way. 'You go on, I will join you soon - go, go', he waved them on. We couldn't make out whether they heard him or not, but we did clearly and understood that they were related to him in some way. Soon a small boy joined the trio of the women and man, and they moved from there. The gentleman in front of us, continued his great address. 'There are too many thieves at large sir. They were my wife, my sister in law and my father in law. That child is my boy! Early this morning, we went to the Durga temple and a rascal thief emptied my pockets. Now I am left with no money to even buy tickets to go home. If you could please help me...', saying thus, he stopped us. He says we know him. We might also face this kind of trouble. Didn't we just witness a robbery in broad daylight? How can one not help even a known person? I anyway did not help the unknown victim just know. Yet how much could I help?, I pondered. 'How much do you need', I asked, in the manner of a really generous person. 'Just one thousand rupees, will help all of us to go back to our place', he said, pointing in the direction of the departed folk. 'That much I do not have. I can offer you five hundred', I said taking out a note from my pocket. 'That is not sufficient for my expenses, but I can always ask a few more people', he said and departed. 'How could you give away so much?', asked the so far silent Raghav. ' You didn't offer a paisa to the previous passenger'. He waited awhile and remarked, 'You didn't believe what you witnesses earlier! However, you believed someone who claimed to have been robbed miles way and gave him money...?' 'Let it be Raghav. Merit or demerit, only the Almighty knows. Even if I have been deceived by them, even deceits need to survive - they are human too!!', I replied. By the time we got down from the bridge, we caught sight of at least four-five more thefts and deceits. 'Oh! this whole world seems to be full of thieves and robbers. Is there no humanity left...?, Raghav was moaning, when we heard a voice crying out behind us, ' Side...side, give way, give way'. I moved aside a little and turned back to see...An old women suffering from leprosy... her whole body covered with wounds oozing pus. Her legs and arms were hanging on each side. She seemed unconscious...Looking closely, I realized, she was being carried by a young lad in his arms. 'How dutifully he serves that old woman everyday! Surely, these two were connected in several past lives.. Not even one's own son lavishes such care...', raved a woman selling fruits from a basket. It was then that I realized that this goodness, this humanity was the first and foremost facet of the very same Lord who seemed to allow thefts and deceits.
author: Anuradha Guda
illustrator: Preeti Krishnamurthy; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Santosh Pujari
