title: Playground
text: We want to go to the playground. How do we get there? We could ride a bicycle. We could ride a motorbike. We could ride a tricycle taxi. We could ride in a horse-drawn cart. We could ride in an ox-cart. We could drive a race car. We can drive a big car. We could row a boat. We could ride an elephant. No! We should walk.
author: All Children Reading Cambodia

title: Animals Also Have Hobbies
text: Story Description From cats and chickens, to dogs and frogs, foxes and little things that fit in small boxes, animals have hobbies just like people do. But animals have strange and funny hobbies. Keep your eyes sharp and your attention focused, because you might catch an animal doing its favourite thing! Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Hopping ﻿hop-ing ﻿The frog is known to be hopping mad. Missing ﻿miss-ing ﻿Be careful, you may be missing a pair of socks. ﻿ ﻿ Unsuspecting ﻿un-suss-peck-ting ﻿The unsuspecting culprit is usually a mouse. Mischievous ﻿miss-chee-vuss ﻿The dog is known to be naughty and mischievous. Animals also have hobbies. We don't see it, of course, because they only engage in their hobbies when people are not around. Once the animals are left alone, they get up to all kinds of mischief, fun and games. This cat enjoys stealing expensive women's hats. The owner will be very surprised when she sees her cat wearing her hat at the horse racing, not to mention using her money to bet on a horse! Paws for a photo! This tiger loves going for a swim when he's not being filmed by news cameras or people going on a safari. He takes a long bath where he searches for items to eat, such as a fish, a flower, a butterfly, an empty cake wrapper, and a herb. He likes to think he is bathing and dining! This crocodile is always active and hunting her prey. When no other animals are around, she sits and lazes by the pond, waiting with her fishing rod to catch an unsuspecting trout swimming in the shallow waters. She quickly gobbles up the fish before the other crocodiles return, and pretends she is still hungry. How mischievous, like Davy Croc-ett! This grasshopper enjoys reading in its spare time. Nobody would know, of course, because people always see grasshoppers leaping far from one place to the next, always moving and never keeping still. But if you sneak up on one, like this grasshopper, you will see it reading about astrophysics and nuclear equations. That really bugs the other insects! This bee is usually flying around colourful flowers and taking pollen to its hive. But when nobody is watching, it likes resting on the edges of teacups, playing a game called 'tea surfing', where it tries to walk on the water's surface without falling in. If you're lucky, maybe you will see this bee's odd beehaviour. Don't fall in the cup, it's a stinger! Snakes are not frequent guests at a birthday party, but they are known to enjoy a slice of cake, and sometimes the whole cake, eating it all in one wide bite. When nobody is looking on your birthday, pay attention to the cake, and a giant, long anaconda may sneak through your garden and try to steal a slice. Thuthpiciouth! Have you ever seen an empty boat at a lake? The next time you do, watch carefully for a goat to turn up. They secretly love rowing boats from the shore to the middle and getting stuck in them. Goats are poor swimmers, so they wait for the water's flow to take them back to the shore. If you see one doing this, call the fire brigade in to help. That may cost them a few bucks. Silly billy! Fish are usually found inside a pot, boiling away and turning into your dinner, but fish secretly wonder what the other side of the pot lid is like. Fish enjoy sneaking out while they are being cooked, just to settle on the lid. When you see soup being prepared, watch the lid carefully, because a fish might just jump out and squeak at you! Foxes wear socks-es. That's a real rhyme. Foxes run away when anyone comes near them, but at night time, they are less afraid. They might sneak into your house and dive into your sock drawer, stealing a couple of pairs. In the morning, always check your drawer for missing socks. You can always blame two missing pairs on a sneaky, sly fox. Do you think mice enjoy living inside a hole in the wall? Of course not! They dream of owning their own house made of cheese. They steal cheese to make their houses in gardens. When you walk through your garden, always check the edges of the grass and the plants for a mouse building a house. Now you know who stole the cheese to build a soft cottage! Chickens don't just cluck, run around and poop eggs. They are the most artistically talented of the farmyard bird variety. If you can't find your newspaper, or you are missing toilet roll, you know a chicken somewhere has nabbed it from you; furthermore, you might see strange sketches showing up on walls in your house! Those are made by roosters! What a wake up call! Dogs and frogs, frogs and dogs. Unlikely friends, but certain buddies! Yes, when you are away from home, your dog and a local frog like to play basketball in your garden. Frogs are hopping mad, and dogs are rough players, and they like to fight together. If you come home early, you might catch your dog and a frog shooting points through the hoops! It's barking mad! After Reading What insect enjoys trying to surf on the edge of a teacup? Which animal likes wearing women's hats and going to horse races? What are the dog and the frog known to do together? Who is likely to be stealing your socks at night? Describe what mice like to do. Describe what fish like to do. Talk about an animal you like and explain what its hobby is.
author: Hello English

title: Let's Fly
text: Bird can fly. Parrot can fly. Horse cannot fly. Fly can fly. Cicada can fly. Lizard cannot fly. Owl can fly. Pelican can fly. Gibbon cannot fly. Egret can fly. Hornbill can fly. Lion cannot fly. Tawny owl can fly. Mosquito can fly. Sheep cannot fly. Someday we will fly. I want to fly too.
author: All Children Reading Cambodia
illustrator: San srei nou ch nou ch

title: The Mundu Magicians
text: Unni’s grandmother had a bad cold. She blew her nose into her soft, old mundu. “Aaashhhcheee!” Ammumma had many old mundus. Mundus older than her cat Bisko. Older than Unni too! Mundus that were even older than the mango tree in her backyard. Unni’s favourite mundus were the ones with the orange lines. Orange like the rising sun. “This is an old one, Unni. You can have it.” Ammumma always made something new out of something old. Just like magic! GILIMI-BILIMI-ALIMI-BU! A cradle and nappies for baby Renu. Wicks that light up the night too. GILIMI-BILIMI-ALIMI-BU! Covers for pickle jars. Shoo, flies, shoo! Spice bags for cooking a yummy stew. AKKADAM-PAKKADAM-CHAKKADAM-DEE! A braid, a cape, a dress, Look at me! ﻿ AKKADAM-PAKKADAM- CHAKKADAM-DEE! I skip, I swing, I climb a tree! “Aaaaaaschhheee!” AKKADAM-PAKKADAM-CHAKKADAM-DEE! “Hankies for you Ammumma, see!”
author: Gayathri Bashi

title: Where Did My Family Go?
text: Story Description Leonard has a big family who are very noisy. Tired of the sound, Leonard goes to hide in a quiet room, when suddenly he discovers that his family have disappeared. Leonard wonders what has happened as he is left alone with his cat, Kitkat. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Struggling ﻿strug-ling ﻿Leonard was struggling to keep calm with all of the noise around him. Gossiping ﻿goh-sip-ing ﻿The family were creating a lot of sound, gossiping and fighting. Chaotic ﻿kay-ot-ic ﻿The family was chaotic, with people running around in all directions. Relieved ﻿rih-lee-v-d ﻿Leonard was relieved to see his family. He thought they had gone forever. ﻿ ﻿ Leonard was part of a big family who lived in a very noisy house. Leonard often played with his cat, called Kitkat, and they sang and danced together, creating mayhem and a big mess everywhere they went. They danced over grandma, his sister Shelley, toppling over plants and sofas, and sometimes falling out of the window. "Why does Leonard have to be so annoying and chaotic?" his older brother Howard asked Grandma. But Grandma was already asleep, and so was Grandad, hogging the sofa by the garden. "Never mind," said Howard. "I'll just talk to myself." The cats often slept in a bundle together on a hot day, and the family would spend the entire afternoon and evening outside. Howard lazed around eating chips, while their father read a book by the window, and Leonard would be reading the comics he had stolen from Howard's bedroom. One day, the noise was too much for Leonard, and he escaped into a quiet room. The family was shouting, arguing and gossiping outside, and they didn't realise that Leonard had gone. "I wish I could have some peace and quiet to myself, just once!" complained Leonard, covering his ears. Suddenly the noise stopped. Leonard waited a while before emerging. He could not find his family. Where had they gone? He desperately ran up the stairs, thinking of where Granddad could be, but even upstairs it was unusually silent. Kitkat followed Leonard as he searched for his family. "Waah!" cried Leonard. "They've left me here forever! They are never coming back! Why is there never anyone around, and when they are there, all they do is be loud, and they're not interested in giving me attention or playing with me! I'm sick of it all!" Kitkat protected himself from Leonard's tear shower with an umbrella. Leonard gave up on looking for his family for a while. Instead, he noticed what a great time he was having with Kitkat. They were just chilling next to the back door, eating fruit and playing with toys. After a while, Kitkat fell asleep, and then Leonard snoozed too! "Oh, boy!" said Leonard. We have the entire house to ourselves! I wonder what we'll do. Hey, let's create some trouble!" They clanged pans and pots together, playing the drums, Leonard played his brother's piano and his sister's clarinet, and Kitkat chased after a mouse on some string. They ran up and down the stairs, tiring each other out. "Maybe my family will never come home?" wondered Leonard. Leonard realised how fun his family could be, sometimes. His brother and sister weren't too bad for company, and occasionally they played together and created a lot of laughter and fun. Leonard realised something else. He was starting to miss his family. Leonard went back to his quiet place and hid as it began to get dark. Kitkat went with him as always, loyally following by his side. Leonard thought of his Granddad and how he used to give out free candies. He remembered his mother and father hugging and holding hands, and the sound of his sister Shelley's hairdryer. Suddenly, three people came running in from the rain. It was grandma, grandpa, mum and Leonard's little baby brother Shaun in a pram. "We thought we had lost you!" said his mother. "We're so sorry we forgot about you." "It's all right," said Leonard. "Kitkat and I had a great time. But I did miss you." Then father, Shelley and Howard came running in, struggling with the wind against the umbrella. "We're so sorry, Leonard. We missed you so much," they said. "I'm just glad you're home," said Leonard. "We can be a family again." And very soon, the entire surroundings were noisy as usual. After Reading Leonard's family creates a lot of n _ _ _ _. Where does Leonard go to get away from everyone? What does Leonard suddenly discover afterwards, and who is by his side? After Leonard gives up looking for everyone, what does he do? What does Leonard start doing after he finishes playing? What surprise does Leonard get at the end of the story?
author: Hello English

title: I Know
text: I go to school in the first month. I open a book in the second month. I learn to write in the third month. I learn to count in the fourth month. I learn addition in the fifth month. I learn subtraction in the sixth month. I learn to pack my school bag in the seventh month. I learn to play sports in the eighth month. I learn to read a book in the ninth month. I learn to color in the tenth month. I learn to draw in the eleventh month. I am at the top of the class in the twelfth month.

title: ACTIONS SPEAK LOUDER THAN WORDS
text: Everyone was praising her brother and not her. Her father jumped with joy when he heard her brother came first in class. Her mother gave him sweets when she heard that he would receive a prize on the stage on Republic Day. Her grandfather twisted his moustache proudly when he heard he ran faster than the others and her grandmother was happy when she learnt that he shared his songs with others. Chinnu was feeling miserable because no one praised her or gave her any sweets to eat. Chinnu got an idea - she decided to tell every one that she was also doing something, just like her brother. She told her parents, 'Tomorrow for the Republic Day function I am going to sing a song that I wrote on the stage.' Everyone praised her and said that they will attend the function. Chinnu thought that no one usually attended flag hoisting function and so she lied about her singing. Now what will she do? She wrote a song in the book only as a hobby. She has never performed on stage. Moreover, she has not given her name for the function. She felt tensed that others will soon find out her lies. She couldn't sleep the whole night and got up in the morning fearing of what might happen. In the school, she saw the teachers praising her brother for achieving many medals. She realized that her brother was not speaking lies like her. After flag hoisting, when every one was performing on stage, Chinnu was sweating with fear. When they reached home, she was sure her parents would scold her for not singing. But she was surprised with their behavior: 'There wasn't sufficient time for the function' said her father. 'She was dull from morning, maybe she has sore throat,' said her mother. 'She will surely get another opportunity and she will practice nicely and sing,' said her grandfather. Chinnu understood that they all came to know about her lies and she felt ashamed. Chinnu learnt a lesson. She decided only to speak about things that she could do. She realized that anyone would praise good actions. She began practicing for the next year's event.
author: Annapurna Sharma
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Arun Ramkumar; Deepa Balsavar; Greystroke; Kalyani Naravane; Lavanya  Naidu; Satya  Krishna Prakash; Shamim Ahmed; Tanvee Nabar; Tarique Aziz; Wesley   van Eeden

title: What do you see?!
text: What do you see? When you are up in a tree! Can you see me? Oh, please dear tell me! Yes, I can see tiny you. And those birds that flew. I have very nice view. Up here in the tree!! Oh sure! I agree! What else can you see? Standing Up on that tree, Don't you feel scary?? No I don't feel fear. It's really great here. There is a squirrel so near! From where does it appear?! I see a man work there. He is planting a tree with care! I know it is earth's welfare, Sure I will do my share! Let me turn and glance, There is grass of vast expanse. Perfect to run and dance! Can we take a prance?! Its time for your turn, But we have to return! Or our parent will concern, We can come again for fun!
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan
illustrator: Brian Wambi; Sanjay Sarkar; Therson  Boadu; Vinayak Varma

title: This...These
text: This...These This is a chicken. It is eating its food. These are two ducks. They are swimming. These are three birds. They are flying from the nest. These are four black birds. They are flying in the sky. These are five egrets. They are flying to the lake. These are six snakes. They are slithering out of their cave. These are seven horses. They are jumping over the fence. These are eight rhinos. They are digging up the trees. These are nine wolves. They are howling. These are ten elephants. They are dragging the timber. They all live happily.
author: All Children Reading Cambodia

title: What Are They Saying?
text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description ﻿A cute little yellow bird flies to different places, encountering animals that are talking about all different kinds of problems. ﻿ Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Slithering ﻿sli-thur-ing Tweety saw the snake slithering across the ground.﻿ Galloping ﻿gal-up-ing ﻿Tweety saw a goat galloping and jumping in a circle. Chirped ﻿chur-p-d ﻿Tweety chirped at everyone she met. Vinyl ﻿v-eye-nul ﻿Tweety saw a stick insect on a vinyl record. ﻿ ﻿ This is Bonnie, a little tweety sunflower coloured bird. She likes to call, eat, sing, hide and stand still. Her friends call her tweety the sweetie, because she is adorable and cute. Her favourite hobby is chirping to other animals. She likes to listen to what they are talking about. They say all sorts of things! Tweety takes flight and comes across a snake all by itself. Tweety chirps at the snake. "Someone told me there was a deer on the ground," said the snake. "I've slithered my way everywhere searching for this deer, and I cannot find it. A deer is a month's worth of food. I think those mice played a trick on me." Tweety flew onwards and found a cow grazing in a field. No other cows were around, and tweety chirped to the cow. The cow said, "I'm here because my friends said, if you have three brown spots, stand by the daisies. Now I realise that I'm the only one in the cow group with three spots. Everyone else has four." Tweety flew on and found a mouse standing alone in a barn. Tweety chirped to the mouse. It said, "I'm here because my friend said, if I wait long enough and look at the moon, I will watch it mature and turn into cheese. I knew I was right! The moon is indeed made of cheese. But I wonder what variety..." Tweety flew on and found a stick insect lying down on a record player. Tweety chirped at the stick insect. It said, "I'm lying down on this vinyl record because it spins around. I asked my friends how the world revolves in a circle, and they told me this is the best way to see how. But I feel dizzy now, and I didn't expect to hear music either." Tweety flew to the jungle and found a lion. Tweety chirped at the ferocious creature and it roared: "The other lions said my walking was too boring. Now I have to walk with my arms raised out, and very slowly, and with my mouth open. They tell me I should walk like a zombie, but it doesn't make me feel alive." Tweety flew on to a big open field, and she saw a goat galloping around. She chirped at the goat and it stopped. It said, "The other goats told me if I stand still, then the sky will fall down. Well, nobody wants that to happen, do they? So if I keep on running in circles, then the sky will stay up!" Tweety flew on and stopped when she saw a dog barking outside of its house. The dog said to her, "I know my owners have only gone to the shop for an hour, but I bark because I'm scared. They may never come home! They might forget all about me! Woof! Woof!" Finally, Tweety flew back home, but just outside, she saw a snail slithering across the ground. She looked up from her meal and the snail said, "I move so slowly, because whenever I feel something strange, I retreat back inside my shell for protection. But nothing ever happens to me. All I have to be afraid of is shoes, and everyone here wears sandals, so that's ok!" After Reading Why was the dog standing outside his house barking? Why was the goat walking in circles? Why was the lion walking in a funny way? What was the stick insect doing? Why was the mouse waiting for so long looking at the moon? What was the snake searching for?
author: Hello English

title: It is easy to help!
text: Hello! I am Molly. I like to help. Helping is fun. I help my granny to peel green peas. I help my dad to put things up! I help my mom to get ready to work. I help by hanging clothes to dry! I always keep things in places where it belongs. I also set plates and spoons when it is time to eat. I like to help my little brother, when he cannot do things himself. It is fun to help. It is easy to help. Words List: and help always keep also like belong little brother peas cannot peel clothes plates do ready dry set easy spoons eat things fun time granny when green where hello work
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan

title: First day at school
text: Today is my first day at school. Mother is holding my hand and walking with me. I've grown up now I say. Lets Go! Mother is holding my hand tightly. A lot of childern are near school. Some come by bus. Some come by car. Some come by Rikshaw. Some by Bicycle and some by walk, Like me. We reached the gate. Mother leaves my hand. She stopped at the gate. I have to go inside alone. There are m any unknown faces all around me. I walk one step. I take another step. I look back. As i move forward, mother begins to appear small. Will she disappear? I run and go to her. I don't think i am grown up. I hold her hand and say "Don't Go" All have gone inside. Only i'm outside. Teacher didi comes outside. She smile at me. I smile too. Mohther says "Raani when you come out, i will meet here". I leave her hand. She wave her hand. ﻿I run and go inside. Mohter will meet there after leave.
author: Manas  Jain

title: SHALU AND SHIRO
text: There was a little girl called Shalu. Shalu was the only child. She got bored of her toys. She wanted a little brother or sister but she was the only child. She spends most of her time near the well in her backyard. One day, Shalu was very sad and started crying. She heard some noise from the bushes. She saw that there was a hungry dog. She fed him a few biscuits and the dog started licking her. Shalu asked her parents if she could keep the dog. Her parents let her keep the dog. Shalu named him Shiro. Shiro and Shalu became best friends.
author: KHUSHI PAL

title: Bonbon Learns To Share
text: Bunnypops was coming back from the city, and on his way back he had picked up fresh and juicy carrots from the nearby farm for his baby boy Bonbon. Bonbon was overjoyed to recieve the carrots that his father had brought for him. He took them and went to the backyard. As he was eating his carrots, his two best friends Icy and Niks came over. When they saw the juicy carrots, Niks said, " Hey Bonbon, those carrots look delicious, would you share a few with us?". ﻿ ﻿ Bonbon was furious. He said " NO! My father got these carrots for me and they are mine and mine only!" This made Icy and Niks very upset. They went away without saying anything. After a while Bonbon hears music and laughter. THERE MUST BE A PARTY NEXT DOOR!! He goes to check. When he looks over the fence he see's his friends are having a picnic. He asks them if he could come too but Icy says " No Bonbon, you cant come, you didnt share your carrots with us." This breaks Bonbon's heart. He runs to his mother and starts to cry. His mother consoles him and says, " Son there is greater joy in sharing your things with others than having them allby yourself". Bonbon takes his carrots and goes to his friends and says, "Niks, Icy, I am very sorry that i was selfish earlier, here you guys can have my carrots too". And thus the three friends had great fun at their little picnic.
author: Abhra Sengupta

title: Counting Bunnies
text: It’s a typical Tuesday night. Working on my laptop till the sun peeked had now become a ritual. The only source of light in my pitch-black room was my brightly lit laptop 4:21 am, my clock read Sighing, I get up, somehow managing to topple all the empty cups of coffee on my table and made my way to my bed. stared at my ceiling, knowing no matter how hard I try, I will not sleep a wink tonight. My ceiling was my blank canvas on which I painted pictures every night. Pictures of what I could, would do, if I did not live in this concrete jungle. My routine was disturbed when I saw something move Startled, I get up and sit on my bed What I saw was something I did not expect. Shadows. No not the scary ones. Shadows of cute little bunnies I kept watching one bunny after another, just hop in a straight line. 1,2,3,4……..23,24…35………51,52,53……….zzzzzz The first time in almost forever, I had a good night’s sleep.
author: Deepshikha Chaudhuri

title: The brave Goat
text: once in a village there was a priest who had a lot of followers and used misguided people. he used to make his followers do the practice of killing animals and always misguiding people as usual one day the priest decided to sacrifice the goat. He decided to call up two of his follower the follower went to the priest as he had called him up with the goat. he told his follower to take the goat to the riverside decorate him give him a bath and bring him back here the follower took the goat to the river side and the goat randomly started laughing the servants started asking him what is wrong? after sometime the goat started crying out of nowhere the servant got really angry at the goat and told him if you don't tell me what is wrong i will kill you right here the goat said kill me anyways you are going to kill me when we go back to the priest the follower took the goat to the priest and told him that the goat started laughing and then after a while he started crying the priest got angry and started asking the goat you stupid goat why were you laughing? tell me the reason the goat replied while they were giving me the bath i recalled a memory from my past life where i was a priest like you and i killed a goat and now in my current life i am goat and called stupid. so if you kill me even you will turn into a goat in your next life the priest was shocked and told his follower to stop with this practice and tell all the people in the village, the goat went back with his master happily.
author: Yash  Kunzarkar

title: Say no to Plastic Waste!
text: There was a boy John. He used to play near the lake side. Lake was beautiful and it has fishes too. But he saw lot of plastic waste in the lake. He was upset and he decided to help the fishes. He went to the stall there and explain the storekeeper condition of the lake. He requested the storekeeper to replace plastic straws by paper straws. After few days, John went again to the lake and saw a lot less plastic waste. This made him HAPPY.
author: Bhawna Jaipuria

title: Shep, Larry & Moe
text: Story Description Shep and Moe are two brothers who work with their friend, Larry. One day, Larry falls over and Shep gets sick. To do well and help each other, they have to work in a team. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Tyres ﻿t-ai-ur-s ﻿A tractor has four tyres. Clumsy ﻿cl-um-zee ﻿He keeps falling over because he is clumsy. Rescue ﻿re-ss-k-yew ﻿The tractor must rescue the scooter from the road. Attention ﻿a-ten-sh-un ﻿ ﻿The sick tractor needs care and attention. Shep is a red tractor, while Moe is a blue tractor. They are brothers. Larry is a yellow scooter. Larry is Shep and Moe's pal. They fix and paint cars together. Larry is a little clumsy. He often goes out on the road alone, and sometimes he crashes. One day, Larry falls on his side. "Oh, no," says Moe. "What happened?" "I went too far and ran out of fuel," says Larry. Moe gives Larry some fuel, and helps him to ride home. Larry feels ill and he leans against Moe. "Thanks for rescuing me," says Larry. "That's all right," says Moe. "But remember: next time, don't run out of fuel!" "I will. I mean, I won't," says Larry. Moe grumbles at Larry. Meanwhile, Shep is in the field. It is a very hot day, and Shep's tyres get stuck in some mud. He cannot move. Shep spins and spins his wheels to try and free himself. Luckily, Shep escapes. He returns to his barn. But Shep feels ill. He has a fever from being out in the sun for too long. Here comes Larry and Moe to the rescue! They know that Shep needs some care and attention! They collect some paint and rollers from their warehouse. "Ah, that feels much better," says Shep, as Moe and Larry cover him with a fresh layer of paint. "There's a tissue in your exhaust," says Moe. "No wonder I've been feeling clogged up!" says Shep. Shep is well again, and he goes back to work. Moe and Larry go out. When they return, they see that Shep has painted three cars all by himself! They are: A Ford Able A Citroen Fruit and......A VW XYZ Shep, Moe and Larry do so well by working together in a team. After Reading Why does Larry fall over in the road? Who comes to rescue Larry? Who gets his tyres stuck in mud? Why can't Shep work when he gets home? What do Larry and Moe do to help Shep get better? When Larry and Moe go out, how many cars does Shep paint?
author: Hello English

title: Ming-Ming, Fat Little Bear
text: Ming-Ming, fat little bear, Woke up one day with a standing-up hair. Now every bear has lots of hair But a standing-up hair is very rare. Ching-Ching, fat mother bear, Looked at Ming-Ming’s standing-up hair. “Ming-Ming, fat little bear, What’s that hair doing up there?” To look into a mirror there. “By golly and gosh, how does it dare!” Ming-Ming, fat little bear, Climbed on to a toppledy chair Ding-Ding, sisterly bear, Took advantage of the hair. Tried to plant a flower there. Ming-Ming said, “Don’t you dare!” Pulled another up in the air. “Hey Ming, you have a pair.” Bing-Bong, brotherly bear, Poked about around the hair. Tring-Tring, telephone bear, Wanted to plant an antenna there. Ming-Ming, smart little bear, Simply said, “Don’t you dare!” Jing-Jang, disco bear, Wanted to paint that single hair Shiny here and sparkly there. Ming-Ming said, “I like it bare.” Ding-Dong, iron-man bear: “Standing-up hair I swear! How the people will stare. Let’s shave your head in the public square.” “Let it poke up here and there, Hair should have a bit of flair!” Ming-Ming, fat little bear, Began to like his standing-up hair. Now Bing-Bong, brotherly bear, And Ding-Ding, sisterly bear, Both want a standing-up hair. They use some oil here and there. Ming-Ming, fat little bear, Went to bed in his cosy lair. When he woke to the sun’s bright glare, The standing-up hair? Just wasn’t there.
author: Jerry Pinto

title: I Want To Be A Pirate
text: ﻿ ﻿I want to be a pirate and find a treasure chest ﻿ ﻿ ﻿I will have a pet parrot who sits on my left ﻿ ﻿I want to be a pirate but I need pirate things ﻿ ﻿ ﻿I will search Mama's closet ﻿ ﻿she might have something that blings! ﻿ ﻿ I want to be a pirate I will need some cloth and thread To make an eyepatch and a scarf to tie around my head I want to be a pirate but I have nowhere to go ﻿ ﻿I'll draw myself a map and find new lands to explore ﻿ ﻿I want to be a pirate But Mama says I'm just a little boy I will grow up and become the finest and the bravest pirate, AHOY!
author: ankita unnikrishnan

title: The Little Red-Haired Porcupine
text: Story Description A little porcupine lives in a field with some animal friends. One day, the porcupine tries wearing clothes and the animals make fun of him. Upset, the porcupine goes for a walk and finds a mouse who helps him to feel better, and gives him something unexpected to surprise his friends. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Porcupine ﻿por-k-yew-p-eye-n ﻿The porcupine is an animal with prickly fur. ﻿ ﻿ Frightened ﻿fry-tun-d ﻿ ﻿The animals were frightened because the porcupine looked different. Astounded a-stow-n-did ﻿The animals were astounded to see the porcupine's red hair. ﻿ ﻿ Apologised a-pol-uh-j-eye-z-d ﻿The animals apologised to the porcupine for being mean. A little porcupine lived in a small village with a tiger, a rabbit, a bear and a pig. Everyone was getting along fine, until one day, the porcupine started wearing clothes. All of the animals laughed at him. "You look ridiculous!" said the rabbit. "I'm just trying to be more like you," said the porcupine. No matter what the porcupine wore, the animals made fun of him. The porcupine felt sad. He could no longer play with the animals. He felt there was something missing about him. "Where are you going?" said the tiger. "You look upset." "I'm going away for a while," said the porcupine. He didn't tell them where he was going. The porcupine went on a long walk, where he found some bright and colourful mushrooms and flowers. He picked a lovely white flower and admired its beauty. "Wow, it's so perfect," he said. "It doesn't need changing at all. Not like me." A lively bird tweeted from the tree and the porcupine said hello. Later, the porcupine walked straight into a storm. A gale blew through the land and gusts of leaves hit the porcupine. There was nowhere for him to hide, and his fur got covered in leaves and twigs. He rolled around on the floor in laughter, realising he could not get away from the wind. Soon, he came across a mouse, and they talked for a while. The porcupine explained his problem. "I don't understand why the animals were mean to me," said the porcupine. "They are always kind." "It's because you looked different," said the mouse. "They didn't expect it. You surprised them." "What must I do to win them over?" said the porcupine. "I can't give in to them." "You don't need to win them over," said the mouse. "They must accept that you have changed. Many animals prefer things to be the same. What you did frightened them." "Come with me," said the mouse. "I have an idea." The porcupine went to the mouse's house and the mouse got his paintbrush and paints. "I'll paint your fur a different colour," said the mouse. "It will give them a big surprise. If they don't like you wearing clothes, then wait until they see your hair!" The mouse brought a mirror for the porcupine to see himself in. "It looks brilliant!" said the porcupine. "And it's such a bright, brilliant colour! I love this." "Go back to your friends and see what they say," said the mouse. "Thank you," said the porcupine, and he went on his way. When the porcupine got back, all of the animals were shocked and astounded at what he had done. He looked like a completely different porcupine. In fact, when he returned, the animals thought he was someone else! The animals apologised for making fun of the porcupine and they played together, on the seesaw, the swing and on the rocking horse. Their lives returned to normal in the quiet field, and the mouse decided to stay with them. Very soon, the paint washed off and the porcupine's coat was brown again. All of the animals laughed. They knew it wouldn't last. "What do you think about me wearing clothes now?" said the porcupine. "At least buy something that fits you well!" laughed the pig. ﻿After Reading ﻿Why did the animals make fun of the porcupine? What did the porcupine find when he was walking? What did the mouse say about the porcupine's friends making fun of him? How did the porcupine change? How did the animals react to the porcupine? Who decided to stay in the animal village?
author: Hello English

title: Aarav turns two!
text: Aarav loved to play. He played in the sun all day. Then his grandmother called him with a tap, “Aarav, shall we take a nap?” “No, Ammamma!” Aarav weeped. “I do not want to sleep!” He sang a song. He did a dance. He would not stop. Not a chance! His grandfather came out and said, “Aarav you must go to bed.” “No, Taatha!” Aarav weeped. “I cannot go to sleep!” He played with the birds. He played with the butterflies. He played till there were stars in the sky. Then his mother came out and said, “Aarav it is time to go to bed.” “Please, Mama,” Aarav said. “I have to play. Because today is my birthday!” “Ok Aarav,” said his father. “We can play.” “But tell me first, how old are you today?” Said Aarav, “Dada, I’ll tell you." "Today I am two!” Mama and Dada joined in the games. Taatha and Ammamma did the same. In sun and rain they will play, because today is Aarav’s birthday!
author: Nisha Vernekar
illustrator: Lý Minh  Phúc; Megha Vishwanath; Phan Thành  Đạt; Sukhada Rahalkar

title: Baking the Cake
text: Story Description Natalie and her father bake a cake to share with their community. Natalie learns what ingredients go into a cake. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Baking ﻿ ﻿bay-king ﻿ ﻿ Baking a cake takes practice and patience. Mixture ﻿mick-s-ch-ur ﻿Many ingredients go into a cake mixture. Slice ﻿sly-ss ﻿A piece of cake is a slice of cake. Neighbours ﻿nay-bur ﻿ They share the cake with the neighbours. Natalie's father decides to bake a cake. He wants to share it with the neighbours. He goes to the supermarket to buy ingredients. He rides his bike and puts Natalie on the front. Natalie's father buys flour, milk and butter. He buys eggs, salt and sugar. He gets all the ingredients for making a cake. With the ingredients ready, Natalie and her father are ready to make the cake. Let the cooking begin! Natalie helps her father mix all the ingredients together. They weigh the ingredients to get the right mixture. Oh, no! They forgot to add the baking soda! Natalie quickly rescues the salt from the floor. They add the salt to the baking soda. Oh, no! They broke an egg! Natalie adds another egg to the cake mixture. Oh, no! Some of the cake mixture is blowing out of the box! It's dusty and powdery. It makes Natalie cough! Natalie's father turns the cake mixture over in the bowl. He turns and folds it until it is ready. He spreads the cake mixture on a tray. He places the tray in a hot oven. He checks the time on the mixture packet - it takes an hour to bake. An hour later, the cake is ready! It smells delicious, but it has to cool down and get decorated first. Natalie's father say it's time to eat the cake. Natalie, her sister and the cat take the cake from the table. Natalie's father cuts the cake into slices. They hand out pieces to each other and the neighbours. It's a fantastic cake! After Reading Name the ingredients that go into a cake. How long did it take to bake the cake? Which ingredients did they forget to add at the beginning? Why did Natalie have to wait before eating the cake?
author: Hello English

title: The Wonderful World of Reading
text: Story Description Steph and Liam's Granddad gives them a library card so they can hire books. But Steph and Liam haven't been to the library before. They discover a magical world of adventure and intrigue that has been waiting for them. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Fascinating ﻿fa-sin-ay-ting ﻿The book world was fascinating. Marvelling ﻿mar-vul-ing ﻿They were marvelling at the choice of books on offer. Intriguing ﻿in-tree-ging ﻿The library was intriguing and mysterious. Carefully ﻿c-air-ful-ee ﻿ ﻿They chose their books carefully. "You kids are complaining of having nothing to do?" said Granddad. "Here, take this." "What is it?" said Steph. "It's a library card. You can go to the library and hire up to six books at one time. Reading is good for your brain. It's exciting and fun. There's a whole new world of fun waiting for you." "Is he going mad again?" asked Liam, Steph's younger brother. "Who would find reading so fascinating? What about playing computer games or going to a theme park?" "I know," said Steph. "But maybe granddad is right. Reading something fun will be good for us." They left home and went towards town. They arrived in town and found the library. Steph and Liam stood outside looking in, marvelling at the colours of books on display. "I'm not sure about going in," said Liam. "I'll wait for you outside." "Come on, it will be fun," said Steph, leading him inside the library. "Good morning," said the librarian. "Welcome to the library. How can I help?" "This is our first time at a library," said Liam. "Well, don't be shy. Come inside, and I'll help you find some interesting books." Steph and Liam walked inside. "Wow, this one's all about cartoons and how they have changed over the years," said Liam. "I found a book that explains dreams," said Steph. "It's called 'Between Waking and Sleeping'. It sounds intriguing. "Those books will be difficult to read," said the librarian. "Let me help you find some easy ones." "I think you'll like these books," said the librarian. "They are adventures for kids your age." "Look at the pictures, they're amazing," said Steph. "I like the aeroplanes," said Liam. Steph went backwards and forwards to the shelves, choosing piles of books to read. Liam sat to one side, taking his time and deciding carefully which books he wanted to read. "Do you like birds?" he said. "No," said Steph. "Do you like fairy tales?" Steph read some mythical tales about Gods and demons, while Liam immersed himself into bird books. They swapped books and then Liam read about monsters and goblins, and Steph read about the fastest flying birds in the world. "I like what you're reading," said Liam. "I like what you're reading too!" said Steph. Time flew by as they were having fun. Neither of them realised they had been reading for three hours, until Liam looked at his watch. "Oh, no!" he said. "We had better get home before granddad wonders where we are." "Time to choose the books we want to take home," said Steph. Steph and Liam chose their books and took them to the librarian. The librarian stamped the books and said, "Make sure you bring them back within three weeks." They went home and continued reading, and they apologised to granddad for being late home. "That's ok," said Granddad. "I would have been gone for a lot longer than you!" After Reading What does Steph and Liam's granddad give to them? Who shows them what books they might like? What type of books does Liam read? What type of books does Steph read? What kind of books do you enjoy reading?
author: Hello English

title: Tiger, Tiger, Where Are You?
text: Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you see my watery trail by the lake? I took a nap in the cool water. Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you see my pugmarks on the soft soil? Look hard, I could be coming or going! Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you see my claw marks on the tree? I was marking my territory Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you smell my scent on the rock? The spray helps a tigress find me! Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you see what I ate yesterday? The hair and nails should give you a clue. Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you hear that loudmouth l angurs' warning? They told the entire forest where I was. Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you hear my growl? I want other tigers to know that this part of the forest is mine. Tiger, Tiger, where are you? I was just here. Didn’t you see my false eyes? I tricked you. Tiger, Tiger, where are you? Here I am. You found me. Meet Mujahid and his Team Members Researchers at the National Centre for Biological Sciences, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, attempt to understand living systems. Mujahid is a part of the Ranthambore Tiger project, where Uma Ramakrishnan (Senior Fellow, DBT Wellcome India Alliance, NCBS) and her group (Anubhab Khan and Kaushal Patel) are trying to understand the genetic impacts of isolation and inbreeding on endangered species. This is why he spends a lot of time tracking tigers - through their pugmarks, claw marks, and scat!
author: Mujahid   Khan

title: The Many Legs of the Millipede
text: Story Description Mally the millipede lives on snowy ground. One day, a bird attacks her, and she breaks her legs. Mally looks for help to fix her legs. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Danger ﻿day-n-jur ﻿The birds were a danger to the millipede. Stretched ﻿ss-tre-ch-d ﻿The millipede woke up and stretched its legs. Escaped ﻿eh-scay-p-d The millipede escaped from the bird.﻿ Gigantic ﻿j-ai-gan-tic ﻿The bird was gigantic compared to the millipede, who was tiny. ﻿ ﻿ Mally the millipede was sleeping happily, sheltered from the birds under his leaf. Birds were a big danger for Mally, and so he stayed away from them, just in case they tried to eat him. Soon, it was safe to come out, and Mally stretched her body and legs. She wondered where she would go. On a walk, she suddenly saw a small bird. But to Mally, it was gigantic. The bird stared at Mally. Suddenly, the bird tried to eat Mally, and Mally escaped from the bird, hurting her legs. The bird flew away. Mally cried for help, wandering across the snowy ground, searching for other insects. Her legs hurt badly. Very soon, she found a spider. She called for it but the spider did not reply. Then Mally realised the spider was asleep. In a panic, she shouted, and the spider woke up. She asked the spider to help fix her legs. With sympathy and care, the spider carefully used its web to fix Mally's legs. Mally said thank you to the spider, who waved farewell to Mally. Her legs felt better. Mally walked through the snow until she found a new home. She was safe and well again. After Reading A t the start of the story, what was the millipede doing? What was the millipede hiding from? How did the millipede get its leg broken? What does the spider do after the millipede asks for help?
author: Hello English

title: A Camel for Kelam
text: Pabu loved to spend time with animals. He had a family of four dogs, five cats and a horse named Saffron. He loved Saffron the most. Every morning, Pabu brushed Saffron’s mane and coat. Then he saddled Saffron and rode into the desert, far beyond his village in Rajasthan. Pabu had a niece named Kelam. She too loved animals. “Pabu,” she said one day. “Bring me a camel for my birthday.” “Where do I find a camel for Kelam?” Pabu wondered. “There are no camels in Rajasthan.” People said camels came from Lanka. It was far, far away, across the big blue sea. Lanka was ruled by a grumpy king who did not share his camels. Pabu loved to travel. He also wanted to see a smile on Kelam’s face. So he came up with a plan. Pabu saddled Saffron. Then he rode into the desert. He rode all night and all day and all night again, till he saw the vast blue sea for the first time. The sea looked endless and Lanka seemed so far that Pabu wasn’t sure if he wanted to go there any more. But he and Saffron boarded the next boat. That night there was a storm, a storm so terrible that the winds crashed and the waves lashed. The boat was wrecked. Pabu and Saffron came ashore in a strange place. There were no trees, no bees, no flowers and no rain, just sand. Pabu and Saffron galloped away from the sea. Where were the green trees of Lanka? Where was the grumpy king? Where were the camels? Pabu saw a grand tent in the distance. Then he saw camels—many, many camels. “Hooray,” he cried. “I’ve reached Lanka.” Suddenly, Pabu was surrounded by men on camels. “Welcome,” said the leader of the camel riders. He looked like a king and he looked happy. Pabu was not in Lanka. He had reached Arabia. He spent many days with the happy king in his grand tent. He learnt how to groom camels. He learnt that the grumpy king of Lanka had stolen many of the happy king’s camels. After some weeks, Pabu grew homesick. He wanted to go home with a camel for Kelam. The happy king gave Pabu a baby camel. He told Pabu to ride across the sands towards the rising sun. Then Pabu, Saffron and the baby camel made their way home. Pabu reached his village just in time for Kelam’s birthday. The village welcomed Pabu. Kelam welcomed the baby camel. And that is how the first camel came to Rajasthan. Phad is a folk art style practised by the Bhopa community of Rajasthan. The artist paints on a cloth scroll called phad. Phad art features stories of folk heroes, one of whom is Pabu.
author: Anu Chowdhury-Sorabjee

title: I'm Growing Up!
text: Story Description Martha is a little girl with a baby brother called Jimmy. Martha wants to be a baby forever, but she knows she is getting older. As her brother hogs all of the attention. Martha realises she has to change and grow up, and accept that things don't stay the same. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Balloon ﻿buh-loo-n ﻿She played with a water balloon ﻿ until it popped and soaked her. Ignoring ﻿ig-naw-ring ﻿She felt like her mother was ignoring her and not being there for her. Attention ﻿a-ten-shun ﻿She wanted the same attention that her younger brother was getting. Plastered ﻿pl-as-t-er-d ﻿She plastered the toothbrush all over with toothpaste. "I don't want to grow up," said Martha, playing in her old baby's crib. "I want to be a baby forever. It's not fair." Martha sucked her thumb and rocked the cot. She played with her rattle until she got bored. "Why do I have to get older?" she said. Martha had a baby brother called Jimmy. He was two months old. His mother was always caring for Jimmy and not giving her any attention. "Why won't you play with me?" said Martha. "I'm helping Jimmy go to sleep," said Martha's mother. "I have to take care of him." Martha tried playing alone. She threw around a water balloon, until it popped over her head. She looked for ants and flies on the floor to collect, until they started crawling up her arms. She even played with her old baby's rattle, until the top fell off. She felt frustrated at being ignored. "Won't you play with me, Auntie?" said Martha. "Not now, Martha," said her auntie. "We're looking after Jimmy. He needs feeding soon. Why don't you go and play outside? It's a lovely warm day!" Martha felt very upset and angry. She felt like she was being sent away. "I know what to do," said Martha. "I'll tell them I saw a handsome prince on horseback riding through our village. That will attract Mum and Auntie outside, and then finally they will play with me. I can't believe my baby brother is hogging all of the attention. It's unfair." Martha went back indoors and told her mother what she saw. "And the prince went past on a shiny black horse," she said, but her mother simply laughed. "It's a funny story, because it's so bad," said Martha's mother. "It clearly didn't happen. Now you can help me put away your brother's toys. And be quiet, otherwise you'll wake him up." "I wonder what Daddy is doing," said Martha. "I'll go and check on him." Martha's Dad was shaving and brushing his teeth. Martha watched him and then inspected his mouth. "Daddy, you have little bits on your teeth that need cleaning off," she said. "Looks like I have to go to the dentist," he replied. "You should try brushing your own teeth. It's difficult!" Martha got excited at being allowed to brush her own teeth. She plastered a toothbrush all over with toothpaste and began brushing away. After a couple of minutes, the foam had built up in her mouth. She had to spit it all out. She discovered that brushing her own teeth was very difficult. "I'm growing up," she said. "I have to learn. But I'll miss being a baby." Later, her mother finished putting Jimmy to bed, and she combed Martha's hair. "Now we can spend time together," she said. "I think you're grown up enough to comb your own hair. Let me show you how it's done. You're not a baby. You're growing up." Martha felt so happy that she wasn't being ignored anymore. Because Martha had shown that she was growing up - learning to comb her hair, brush her teeth, and no longer sleeping and playing in her crib - she was allowed to help look after Jimmy. She bonded well with her mother, father and auntie, as they took turns to hold Jimmy and feed him. "I'm not a baby anymore," said Martha. "Now I'm a little girl. I'm growing up!" After Reading ﻿Why did Martha feel jealous of her baby brother? What did Martha want from her mother? How did Martha try to lie to her mother to get attention? What did Martha's father advise her to do? What kinds of things kept Martha behaving like a baby? Why was Martha eventually allowed to help look after Jimmy?
author: Hello English

title: Why?? Because...
text: Sun is setting and the sky is turning orange. Ma calls out "Tinni, the Sun is going down. Soon it will get dark. Let us go back home." Tinni looks at Ma and asks " Ma, why is it getting dark?". "Sun is setting Tinni", said Ma. "Yeah with Sun we get so much light! But Moon also gives us light at night, Ma. Then why is night so dark?" "That is because Moon's light is so much lesser than of Sun."Ma replied with a smile. Tinni still has a question, "So the Moon is not as bright as the Sun! But why?" "Why does my little Tinni has so many questions? Why?" now Ma was laughing. "Tinni let's hurry up. Papa must already be home." "Oh yes! Let’s hurry up. I have to show him the spider I made in the school today." said an excited Tinni. Papa tells Tinni, "Tinni Go and wash your hands for dinner. " "Why can’t I eat with dirty hands papa?" "Because dirty hands have lots of germs. If these germs go into your tummy, then your tummy will hurt." But Tinni still had a question, "Why do germs make my tummy hurt?" "Because germs are bad." replied Papa. "Why papa, why are they bad?" Just then, Ma comes in, "Tinni come, help me arrange the table. The food is getting cold." "Coming Ma! I can already smell the tasty food!" Tinni is tired after the dinner. As she falls asleep, Tinni is flying in the sky. She is amazed to look at the stars and has another question to ask, "Why do you not meet me in the day time? Where do you all hide?" What, do you think, the stars would have told Tinni?!
author: Anju Chhillar
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Audrey Agnier; Canato Jimo; dakshayani velagapudi; Proiti Roy; Promina Shreshtha; Soumya Menon

title: The Nose of all Noses
text: Zahra’s Dadima has an unusually large nose. It is quite a thing of beauty. Not only is it large, it also has a big mole on it. Perhaps to make sure that no one ever misses it. Zahra’s nose is nothing in comparison. “Dadima, why do you have such a large nose?” Dadima’s nose quivers a little before she breaks into a gleeful laugh. “Oh, Zahra! Mine is the nose of all noses. It picks up scents that others cannot even imagine.” Zahra’s eyes grow big with disbelief. “For instance, right now, I can sniff the air and tell you...” Dadima closes her eyes, her nose swells, her nostrils flare, her mole quivers and her chest puffs up. Your Ammi is about to make biryani for lunch, our neighbour is crushing henna leaves for her hair, and the cat has just done a pee-pee.” “HUMMMM HAR HUMMMM! “SNIFF SNORT SNIFF!” Zahra tries to sniff out these secrets too. “Could you teach me this magic, Dadima?” Dadima smiles. “When I was a little girl, my nose was trained at my father’s old attar shop. If you try hard enough, you can train yours too.” She picks up a dusty old crystal bottle from her dressing table. “This is from one of the oldest shops in Old Delhi, where attars are sold among jewels to those with fine noses,” Dadima whispers. “Take a whiff and see where your nose takes you.” Dadima uncorks the bottle and brings it to Zahra’s nose. “Hummmm har hummmm!” Zahra breathes in the dust. And “ACHOOOO!” “Be gentle, take your time and imagine...” Zahra takes a slow and deep breath. When she closes her eyes, her nose swells, her nostrils flare and her chest puffs up, just like Dadima’s. “HUMMMM HAR HUMMMM!” And just like that, she smells flowers sweet and fresh. The flowers remind her of festivals. When Zahra opens her eyes, she is in a garden. For miles and miles there is nothing but rows of roses. It is no longer a Mumbai afternoon. It is dawn and some people are plucking pink roses in the garden. “What you sniffed was the ruh-e-gulaab, a perfume made from roses in this garden in Kannauj,” says Dadima. Dadima and Zahra stealthily follow the rose pluckers to an old brick-walled factory. There the rose pluckers tip the petals into a great copper pot in a large brick kiln. Dadima and Zahra watch in wonder as the attar is made and poured into delicate glass bottles. “Is ruh-e-gulaab the only perfume they make, Dadima?” asks Zahra. Dadima pulls out another little bottle from her kurta. Zahra closes her eyes, her nose swells, her nostrils flare and her chest puffs up as she takes a deep breath. “HUMMMM HAR HUMMMM!” This attar reminds her of the first monsoon shower. The monsoon-shower attar transports them to a grand marble palace where a Nawab sits amid crystal bottles. He sniffs them at great speed and then hurls them across the room at an even greater speed. A puny man quivers in front of him, holding a casket full of little glass bottles. “None of these will do! These smell like the rain,” grunts the angry Nawab. “Where is the signature scent you promised me? You’re supposed to be the best perfumer in all of Awadh!” “Hukum! I’m sure this is the attar you wanted,” says the perfumer, fumbling amongst his things. Unfortunately, Zahra’s tummy chooses this minute to rumble. It’s lunchtime and she’s very hungry. “WHO IS THAT?” thunders the Nawab, whose keen ears have picked up the sound. Before Zahra and Dadima can skip away, the Nawab catches them sniffing at the bottles he has been throwing away. “Dadiji, are you spying on me?” asks the Nawab. “I would have punished you but I can see you have a keen sense of smell and the nose of all noses. Come here and help me pick an attar that can become my signature scent.” Dadima sneakily drops her old crystal bottle amongst the perfumer’s things. She pretends to find it and does a more dramatic version of her sniff. “HUMH HA HURRRUMPH GUR GURR HUMH HAAA HUI!” She hands the Nawab a bottle. The perfumer, Dadima and Zahra wait anxiously as the Nawab takes a sniff from the bottle. “This is exactly what I wanted! What is it?” He looks at the baffled perfumer. “Ruh-e-gulaab, the soul of roses from Kannauj. This is what the perfumer brought for you,” says Dadima. Just then, they hear another distant, angry rumble. “GUDU GUDU, GTTTRRRR, GUDU GUDU.” “What was that, Zahra?” asks Dadima, as her nose twitches with worry. “That was my tummy, Dadima,” says Zahra. “It’s time for us to head home. What scent reminds you of home, Zahra?” Dadima asks her. “Biryani!” says a hungry Zahra, without missing a beat. “I have Awadh’s most delicious biryani to offer. Khansama! Get some for Dadiji and this child,” the Nawab commands his cook. But Dadima quietly pulls out a tiny copper box filled with a spoonful of fragrant biryani. They close their eyes, their noses swell, their nostrils flare and their chests puff up as they take a deep breath. HMMMMMMMM HAR HMMMMMMMMM! They open their eyes and find themselves at the dining table, just in time for biryani. Attar is a perfume made from flowers and plants. It has been around for centuries, maybe more than 4000 years. Kannauj is often called the attar capital of India. Mughal emperors loved to wear attar. Gulab Singh Johri Mal was an attar maker who started his shop in Old Delhi’s Dariba Kalan during the reign of the Mughal emperor Akbar Shah II. His family runs this shop even today.
author: Meera Ganapathi

title: A Sparrow far from Home
text: One day, a young sparrow named Ronald wanted to see the world and asked his mother. But his mother did not want him to go out of the house due to her fear of predators. Ronald was not satisfied with his mother's response. So, one night he quietly sneaked out of his house. He could only see darkness everywhere and he felt scared. Suddenly he felt a net around him! He was captured in a cage by a hunter! The next morning, Ronald woke up in despair. He was so upset that he said to himself ''I wish I had heeded my mother's advice and not gone out of my house!'' Just then a little boy came inside with a bag which had his sketch book and drawing materials. The boy drew a very beautiful drawing of the sparrow and fed it some food but felt sorry for it. Ronald looked into the boy's big brown eyes and hoped he understood his pain. To Ronald's joy, the boy looked here and there and opened the cage! Ronald happily chirped a beautiful song for him to show his gratitude and flew away to his home. That day Ronald learnt a valuable lesson that any place in the world is not as good as home. He said to himself, ''This was the most adventurous experience I ever had in my life!'' and the sparrow went to sleep in the comfort of his nest with his family around him. Moral of the story - Never think your home is not as good as any other place in the entire world. Home sweet home!
author: Shruti Diggavi
illustrator: Jayesh Sivan; Maya  Ramaswamy; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Samidha Gunjal

title: Mrs Penguin's Perfect Palace
text: “I wish I had a HOUSE!” said Mrs Penguin. “I don’t like living in rubbish.” “Dear Mrs Penguin,” said Papa Penguin. “We will build you a palace.” So the Penguin family set to work. “The sand is making me itch,” grumbled Sissie. “The measurements are wrong,” said Boetie. “I’m hungry,” said Gobbles. Mrs Penguin sighed. She was doing all the work. At last the castle was finished. But the tide came in and washed it away. “We’ll try again,” said Papa Penguin. “Come children, we’ll build Mama a mansion from stone.” So the Penguin family set to work. “The stones are heavy,” grumbled Sissie. “The measurements are wrong,” said Boetie. “I’m still hungry,” said Gobbles. At last it was finished. But the wind came up and blew it over. Mrs Penguin was cross. “I’m not doing any more work,” she said. “We’ll try again,” said Papa. “I can’t think of anything,” said Sisi. “It’s too hard.” “We haven’t got any cement,” said Boetie. “You can’t build a proper house without cement.” “I’m hungry,” said Gobbles. Mrs Penguin sighed. She was never going to get her home. “Just look at all this mess,” she said. Then Mrs Penguin had an idea. “Boetie, fetch wood,” she said. “Sissie, find nets.” “Gobbles, pick up plastic. Papa, fetch the hammer.” All day they worked. “I’m tired,” said Sissie. “Keep working,” said Mama. “The measurements are wrong,” said Boetie. “Keep working,” said Mama. “I’m still hungry,” said Gobbles. “Keep working,” said Mama. “It’s going to be wonderful,” said Papa. “You’re doing a good job,” said Mama. So they worked and worked and worked and worked … … and at last the house was finished. “Welcome to your palace,” said Papa. Mrs Penguin clapped her flippers. “Thank you,” she said. “It’s Mrs Penguin’s Perfect Palace.”
author: Helen Brain

title: When I Grow Up
text: What do I want to be when I grow up? When I grow up, I want to be a dancer and dance on a stage. When I grow up, I want to be a firefighter and put out big fires. When I grow up, I want to be a nurse and make sick people better. When I grow up, I want to be a musician and play in a band. When I grow up, I want to be a mechanic and fix cars and tractors. When I grow up, I want to be a teacher and teach children to read and write. When I grow up, I want to be a soccer player and score the winning goal. When I grow up, I want to be an astronaut and fly to the moon. When I grow up, I want to be a chef and make food for my family and friends. When I grow up, I can choose whatever I want to be! What do you want to be when you grow up?
author: Michele  Fry

title: Dragonfly in Details
text: A dragonfly is an insect that have long body, two pairs of transparent wings and large eyes. It is a carnivorous insect. Carnivorous means it feeds on other animals or insects as food. As all insects dragonfly has three parts of body: A head, a thorax, and an abdomen. The Head: The head is large with two big eyes. Dragonfly can see all around itself. It has two large compound eyes, with about 30 thousand lenses. However, the human eye with only one lense can see more sharply, though only front and sides. It has a small mouth with mouthparts adapted for biting. Dragonflies do not have teeth - they use their very strong mandibles to eat their prey. They use the antennae to catch the prey. They don't sting. And when they land on you don't worry because it is considered lucky. The Thorax: The thorax of dragonfly has 6 legs like other insects and two pairs of wings. Despite having 6 legs, the dragonfly doesn't walk very well. It use its legs to catch and hold its prey and to climb on plants. The long leg joints bear rows of spines (hair like). The spines in the front leg is modified into 'eyebrush' to clean its eye surface. The wings are long and patterned. The patterns of dragonfly wings are like fingerprints - no two are exactly the same! The patterns are formed by the veins. The veins carry haemolymph (scientific name for blood of insects) and also helps to stiffen the wings during flying. The hind wings are broader than the fore wings. Dragonflies keeps it wings parallel to its body while flying and resting. It is a great flyer. Dragonfly can fly forward, backward, side to side, upwards and downwards. It can even hover in midair! Each wing can move independently of each other. The strong muscles at the base of each wing helps control wing shape and angle separately. This helps dragonfly to fly in all directions even in strongest winds. It can fly long distances and most heights compared to other insects. It can fly with speed of 36 to 54 km/hour. The abdomen: The abdomen of dragonfly is long and slender. It consists of 10 segments. Life Cycle: Dragonfly life cycle has 4 stages: Egg stage Dragonfly normally lays eggs on plant leaves near water or on water surfaces. The eggs may take time of a days to months or more to hatch depending on species. Nymph stage or Larval stage Most of the life of Dragonfly is spent in this stage.Dragonfly nymph will have 6 legs, wing sheaths and expendable jaws. It will breath through gills and it will have voracious hunger. It will eat insect larve, worms, snails, tadpoles and even small fish. It will be under water for months to years depending on water temparature. In warm water, nymph stage will take only few months. In colder climates, it will take even 5 years to develop to emergence stage. Emergence stage The nymph transformation into final molt will take place out of water. For several days, the final-stage larvae live near the water margin. As they get ready for their final molt, they start breathing air. The larvae then climb up emergent vegetation where they redistribute their body fluids, as they push their thorax, head, legs and wings out of the larval skin. This emergence stage takes upto 3 hours. Adult stage After emergence, the adult must wait for several hours for its wings to harden before making their first flight. It will take days for its color to become bright. The life of adult is generally no more than two weeks. Adult dragonflies mostly eat other flying insects, particularly midges and mosquitoes. They also will take butterflies, moths and smaller dragonflies.They can eat hundreds of mosquitoes every day. Do you know? There are over 5,000 species of dragonflies. They have been on earth from around 300 million years. Group of dragonflies are called swarms. Predators that eat dragonflies include fish, ducks, birds, and water beetles. In Japan, dragonfly is associated with courage, strength and happiness. It is considered as good luck. In Europe, it is linked with evil or injury.
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan

title: I Will Help You
text: Mama Heron hurts her wing and leg on barbed wire. “Ouch!” “I am hurt. I can’t get home to my children.” “Please help me.” “I can’t get home to my children.” “Why are you crying Mama Heron?” “I will help you,” says Lungile. “Thank you, Lungile!” The next day, Gogo sends Lungile to the shop to buy bread. On the way, he stops to play with his friends in the river. Eish! The money is gone. “Don’t come home until you find that money!” “Why are you crying, Lungile?” “I lost the money Gogo gave me to buy bread. We have no supper now.” “I will help you.” Mama Heron’s sharp eyes see the coins shining in the water. “Thank you, Mama Heron.”
author: Andrea Abbott

title: I am a Puppet
text: Where do I come from? Outer space? Cave paintings? I am a puppet. From left to right: •Karagoz: shadow puppet from Turkey •Bangarakkha: leather shadow puppet clown from Karnataka •Pulcinella: glove puppet from Italy •Mr Punch: puppet from England I have many brothers and sisters. From left to right: •Kalasutri Bahuliye: string puppet from Maharashtra •Opera dei Pupi: string puppet from Italy •Yakshagana Gombeyatta: string puppet from Karnataka •Tarer Putul: string puppet from West Bengal I have cousins too! Shadow puppets, glove puppets, rod puppets. From left to right: •Wayang Kulit: shadow puppet from Indonesia •Pavakathakali: glove puppets from Kerala •Bunraku: rod puppets from Japan And I have friends all over the world. Some are fat. Some are tall. Some are round. Some are small. And they are purple, blue, orange, and black. From left to right: •Magarina: muppet from Delhi •Tarer Putul: string puppet from West Bengal •Petroushka: clown puppet from Russia •String puppet from Rajasthan •Life-size puppet from Delhi Wouldn't you like to have family and friends like mine?
author: Anurupa Roy

title: THE CAREER DIARY OF A CONFUSED CHILD
text: Doctor I always think about what I would be when I grow up. The best thing that comes to my mind is becoming a doctor. Yes, I will become a doctor. I will help people who are ill. I will give free medicines to poor people. I will not give injections to anyone. I will not hurt anyone. When I will become a doctor, I will cure my mother of the pain which she feels in her legs. She works all day for us so I should give her medicines. I will never give her an injection. I do not want to hurt my sweet sweet mother. Architect No, I will not become a doctor. If I become a doctor I will have to wear white coats and no colourful clothes. I will become an architect. I will draw designs of big buildings. I will make designs of schools, hospitals, and other’s houses. I will create models of buildings which will look just like the real buildings. I will not take money from poor people. I will make free drawings of their bungalows and buildings. But if they have bungalows, how can they be poor? Police Officer No, I will not be an architect. What if I design a building and it falls down? So many people will die. And I will have to go to jail. Instead, I will become the owner of jails. I will be a police officer. I will arrest all the thieves and robbers. I will beat them and help the good people.. I will wear a beautiful uniform. It will be better than my school uniform. Everyone will salute me. All the bad people will be afraid of me. Post-Man No, I will not become a police officer. If I beat and keep any bad person in the jail, who will take care of his family. His children will cry. I love the khaki uniform so I will keep it and become a post-man. People will wait for me at their doors. I will ride on a bicycle. On my back, I will keep a leather bag and all the letters will be in it. So many children will get letters from their father because of me. Their fathers work faraway, that is why. When I will sit in the post-office, there will be many letters around me. White, yellow, green, khaki, all colours on envelopes. It will be so much fun! Farmer It will be fun, but no, I will not become a post-man. What if I miss some letters? What if few letters get lost? The Post-Master will throw me out of the post-office. It would be better for me if I become a farmer. I will sow the seeds, plough the fields and cut the crops. So many people will get food because of me. Everybody will be happy with me. I will work hard in the fields during the day and then sleep peacefully at night. I will sleep between the crops on the earth. It will be cool enough. Soldier Sleeping on the earth is good. But what if some insect goes into my ear. I will become deaf. No, no. I do not want to be a farmer. I will better be a soldier. I will stay near the border and protect my country. I will not let any enemy enter my country or to harm my country. I will fight with anyone who tries to kill innocent people. I will try not to kill anyone but if the enemy is bad then I will teach him a good lesson. Poet No, I will not be a soldier because I will have to stay far away from my parents. I cannot do that. I will instead become a poet. That way, I will always be at home with my parents. I will sit under the mango tree in the garden and write poetry. There will be nobody to disturb me. When I will finish writing I will show my poems to my father and mother. They will be very happy and proud of me. My dear mother will show the poems to everyone in the neighborhood. I will be so famous. Teacher If I become a poet then I will be able to tell others about the good things in the world. But a poet gets no salary. Then how will I buy anything from the market with no money? I will instead become a teacher. I will go to my own school and teach the students. I will tell stories and good things. I will not beat anyone. I will try to teach them with love. I will not give a lot of home work to my students. I will remain all the day in the school. Vendor If I remain all day in the school then when will I go to my favorite places such as the market. No, instead of becoming a teacher, I will be a vendor. I will spend my whole day in the market selling things. I will get to meet so many people, everyday. I will sell things at good prices. I will not take too much money from people. But it will be bad when the sun will burn my skin in the afternoon. Anyways, in the evening I will enjoy the cool breezes. Pilot Enjoying the air is good but everybody does that. I want to do something new. Something that only few people are able to do. Yes, I will be a pilot. I will not be a vendor. I will fly planes. I will sit in the front seat of the plane and control all the buttons. There will be many buttons but it is okay. I will do my work. I will fly in the air with my huge plane. Clouds will float below my plane. It will be so much fun. Shepherd No, no. I will not fly planes. What if I forget any button or switch. The plane will crash. No, no. I will live in the mountains. I will become a shepherd. I will roam on the clean and quiet hills. My sheep and goats will eat the grass from the hills. My sheep will give me wool and my goats will give me milk. I will sell the wool and milk to get money. And then, I will buy a lot of sweets with that money. I will eat lots of sweets. Auto Rickshaw Driver Eating too many sweets will spoil my teeth. I will not be a shepherd but I will be an auto-rickshaw driver, yes. I will buy a yellow and black taxi and roam around in it. I will sit on the driver’s seat and other passengers will sit beside me or behind me. I will take people to different places they wish to go to. That way, I will get money for roaming around. I will not be able to see my parents again and again but then I will get to go to the places I have always wanted to see. Potter What is the use of being someone when your parents cannot see you. I will not be an auto-rickshaw driver but a potter. I will sit at home and make pots of clay. I will make pots on a wheel. They would be both big and small. I will not only make pots but also jars, cups and bowls. I will make very beautiful things from clay. People from faraway places will come to buy my creations. I will be the most famous and the most-richest potter in the world. Blacksmith Pots made of clay can break very easily. My hard work will be of no use if the pots break. I won’t be a potter. I will be a blacksmith. I will make all things from iron and they will never break. I will melt the iron in the fire and hit it with my big and powerful hands. I will give shape it. I will make knives, plates, axes and swords. The things I make will be strong. They will be brittle like clay pots. ME No. Nothing. I want to be nothing. I want to be just what I am. What I will do with the money? What is the use of gold and silver? Why should I go on collecting useless things like a fool? I want to do what I do now. I want to play with my friends. I want to do mischief. I want to sleep on my mother’s lap. I want to go to the market with my father. Holding his finger gives me the biggest power. I want to hear grandma’s lovely stories. I want to believe her stories. I wonder. Is it possible? Can I always be what I love being – Me?
author: Aftab Yusuf Shaikh
illustrator: Aishah Urooj Shaikh; Ajanta Guhathakurta; Bhramara  Nayak; Henu; Isaac  Okwir; Lauren   Nel; Lavanya Karthik; Natasha Sharma; Ninoshka Dias; Ntembiso  Velemane; Radhika Tipnis; Ram Soni; Sanjay Sarkar

title: How about you?
text: Who are you? Is that goo? Eeuw! I want some too. We are two. How old are you? Six hundred and thirty two? I like blue. Do you too? I choose two shoes. Which do you choose? Horseshoes!? I make toys with boys. We make lots of noise. Whaaa! eurgghhh... aargh! I take a nap on Gogo’s back. I don’t nap! I stay upright all through the night. The ball goes THWOCK! Buddy, you ROCK! That’s what we do. How about you?
author: Margot Bertelsmann

title: Piku's Little World
text: Piku loved summer afternoons. He played with the cats that dozed on his window ledge. He chased the sparrows on the balcony. He fed the squirrels that lived on the mango tree. But most of all, Piku loved the stories Mummy read to him in bed. The heat made the cats curl up in a ball. The sparrows slipped into their nests. The squirrels hid among the leaves. Sometimes Mummy fell asleep in the middle of a story. But Piku lay awake, listening to her snores go khhhh khhhh khhhh. He shut his eyes tight if the shadows made scary faces on the wall. Until evening came with a cool sigh. But Piku did not like summer evenings when… the lights went off, phut. He huffed and puffed over his sums by the lantern. The mosquitoes sang pnn pnn pnn. The geckos ran tut tut tut. The crickets called crr crr crr. Sometimes he went to the terrace with Papa to look at the big black sky. They counted the twinkling stars, spotting the bear and the dog that hid among them. When the lights came back on, everyone went aaaaah. Then one day Mummy was gone. Piku came home from school and asked the cats if they knew where Mummy was. They purred and licked his hand. He asked the sparrows. But they twittered away. He asked the squirrels, who squeaked and ran. Piku asked Papa if he knew where Mummy was. Papa said she was gone far away, for a very long time. So Piku waited for Mummy every day. He played with the cats and sparrows and squirrels all afternoon. But no one read him a story anymore. The shadows made scary faces on the wall. At night, he counted the stars in the big black sky. And the shadows filled his dreams with spiders and cockroaches and ants. Then, one afternoon, Piku picked up a book and turned a page. And oh! Kings and queens, fairies and witches were suddenly alive. The words made them laugh and cry, sing and dance. Since that day, Piku read a new story in bed. The cats stopped by to listen as they licked their paws. And once again, his dreams felt soft like teddy bears and bunnies — and sometimes they were lit with his Mummy’s brightest smile.
author: Somak Ghoshal

title: Monkeys Share
text: I'd like one more banana", said first monkey. The second monkey said, "I will take one more banana." The third said, "No. I'll take one more banana." Fourth monkey said, "No! I am the eldest. So I'll take one more banana." The fifth was the beloved of all. He said, "Mother! Give me one more banana." Mother said, "No! I will not give more bananas to anyone. Everyone will get bananas, equally." "Everyone stand in a line!" On hearing this, everyone stood up to make a line. Mother gave equal number of bananas to each one. "Mother, we have got 3 bananas each, for the 6 of us. That means a total of 18 bananas have been divided. Now two more bananas are left. How will you distribute them?", asked the smallest monkey. "Now, I'll cut each banana into 3 pieces." Saying this, mother cut both bananas into 3 pieces and distributed them to everyone. "Oh mother! Everyone got three and a quarter of bananas. Chhotu shouted and hung on a branch after eating the bananas.
author: Mohini Shesh

title: Tortoise Finds His Home
text: One day Tortoise was walking through the veld. He was searching and searching. He gazed into the distance and squinted at the grass. “Yes, I’m looking for my house.
