Millipede ran circles around poor Chicken, scoring goal after goal. Chicken got angrier and angrier. Watch out, Millipede! "Let's have a penalty shoot-out," said Chicken, hoping that this would prevent Millipede from using her legs to dribble around her. "Sure thing!" said Millipede confidently. First Millipede was goal keeper. Chicken scored only one goal. Then it was Chicken's turn to defend the goal. Millipede kicked the ball and scored. Millipede juggled the ball and scored. Millipede headed the ball and scored. Millipede tapped the ball and scored. Chicken grew angrier by the minute. "This is unfair," she thought, "Millipede should only be able to use two of her legs. She is cheating!" While Chicken was busy thinking her angry thoughts, Millipede slyly kicked the ball around her and through the goalposts. Millipede scored five goals! Chicken was furious that she had lost. "I want a rematch," she demanded, "and this time you can only use two of your legs!" Millipede started laughing because her friend was making such a fuss. "What a sore loser you are!" she said, "Why didn't you use your wings to flap the ball into the goal, or your feathers to blow it over my head? You lost fair and square, my friend!" "You see," said Millipede, "soccer is really all about strategy. You need to use your brain and have a plan." "Are you telling me I don't have any brains?" shrieked Chicken. "How dare you!" But before Millipede could answer, Chicken opened up her beak and swallowed her. As Chicken was walking home, she met Mother Millipede. Usually Chicken loved to see her friend's mother. Mother Millipede told wonderful stories and baked the most delicious leaf cakes. But today Chicken marched right on, hoping Mother Millipede would not recognize her. "Hello dear," Mother Millipede called, “Have you seen my child?” Chicken didn't say anything. Mother Millipede was worried. "Chicken is acting very strangely!" she thought. Then Mother Millipede heard a tiny voice. “Help me, Mom!” cried the voice. Mother Millipede looked around and listened carefully. "Where is that voice coming from?" she asked. "Have you got someone inside your stomach, Chicken?" Chicken looked around sheepishly. She didn't know what to do. "Who have you eaten?" asked Mother Millipede. "Don't tell me you've eaten my precious baby!" Mother Millipede shouted, “Use your special power my child!” Millipedes can make a bad smell and a terrible taste. Chicken began to feel ill. "I don't feel so well," she moaned. "I need to go home and lie in my bed." Chicken burped. Then she swallowed and spat. Then she sneezed and coughed. Millipede tasted disgusting! Meanwhile, Mother Millipede stood beside her, cheering. "Well done, my darling!" she shouted, "Keep on working that special magic! You'll be out in no time." Chicken coughed and coughed until Millipede came out. "Hooray!" shouted Millipede, "I'm free! I escaped!" Mother Millipede was relieved to see her child alive and well. "Come quickly," she whispered, and her and Millipede crawled quickly away. They climbed and climbed until they reached the top of a tall tree where they could hide. From that time on, all chickens and millipedes have been enemies.
author: Right To Play

title: Outer Space
text: Story Description A boy and a girl wonder what it would be like to live in outer space. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Especially ﻿eh-ss-pesh-ul-ee ﻿We would have to be careful, especially when walking in space. Gravity gra-vit-ee ﻿Because there is no gravity, we would float. Floating flow-ting ﻿Our food and drink would be floating around the room. Furniture fur-nih-ch-ur ﻿ ﻿All of the furniture would float off the ground. Kids, listen! There is something you're not aware of. There is an entirely different world out there waiting for us. It is filled with magic and wonder. It is a place that we are always trying to understand. One day we will go out there, far from this world, and discover new places. What is Dad talking about? I think he's going crazy. There's enough entertainment in this world. What could we possibly want from up there? Put your hand down. Your armpit smells really bad. Wait a minute. What if Dad was right? There could be another world up there waiting for us. It must be filled with amazing things, like ice cream, pancakes, drinks of all kinds. Even pizzas. I imagine there are pizzas up there, and the people who go there must have a great adventure. It must be difficult to live up there without gravity. How are you supposed to do simple things like eat and drink, and go to the toilet? And there isn't much space. It must be very cramped. You would bump into a lot of things. What if there was no gravity down here? Then look at the furniture. It would lift off the ground. We'd float in the air. Wouldn't it be incredible? Uh, oh! The salad is falling out of the bowl! Oh, it's all right. It's just floating! We would be flying around the earth at several thousand miles per hour. We would be travelling so fast that we would go around the world in just one hour, spinning all of the way. In space, there will be no need to clean up your mess, because it will just float. You can walk into the food, instead of bringing the food towards you. Dinnertime will be a strange experience. Imagine all the different flavours of ice-cream we could have in space. And space itself is freezing cold so we could store it outside. We could have as much ice-cream as we want. That means we could even eat upside down or spend all day that way. We might forget which way is the right way up. We could go food hunting in space. We would have to wear a protective space suit, because nobody can survive in the conditions of space. What about water? Maybe when I'm drinking it, it would slosh around my body. That would feel really weird and cool. I can't wait to go to space. Especially with a group of people like my family and my friends. We can share the whole experience together. The only question is, will we be able to get our food delivered? ﻿After Reading ﻿If you could go to outer space, what would you do there? What things would happen in space? What would you see? If you could take someone there with you, who would it be and why?
author: Hello English

title: Megan and the Bridge of Life
text: Megan, Frits and Princess Elavuarasi hid amongst the roots and vines as tree trolls thumped closer. “GRRRR!” They flared their wooden nostrils, and sprayed snotty chlorophyll on everyone. “Ewww…” the princess cried. “You’ve ruined my favourite dress, you… cauliflower!” The trolls moved closer, swishing their trunk-thick arms, missing Megan, Frits and the princess by an inch. “This way!” Megan tugged on the princess’ snot-covered clothes. “I’m a princess and I follow no one,” Princess Elavuarasi said. “GRRRR!” The trolls splashed more goopy chlorophyll all over her face. “Ugh, fine! I’ll come,” the princess said. “Down here,” Megan whispered, kneeling down on the bridge. She had found a crack large enough to slip through. STOMP STOMP. The trolls marched closer. CHOMP CHOMP. They almost bit Megan’s nose off. “Hmmm hmmm mmm,” Megan began humming to calm herself. Princess Elavuarasi grabbed Megan by the shoulder and shoved her into the crack. The three of them slid down, crashing into branches and bumping into rocks as they tumbled onto the bridge below. Megan dusted herself off the ground. “Hmm hmm hmm.” She was surprised to hear voices humming back to her. Megan ran towards the sound. “WAIT UP!” the princess said, following Megan and Frits. She slid down roots, swung on vines, and jumped across large gaps. Megan and the princess reached the centre of the bridge. “Wow!” they chorused. Roots twisted, turned, coiled, and braided to make walls, arches, and doorways. “What are they?” the princess said, pointing at the centre of the room. There were at least a dozen men with twig-shaped bodies and tumbleweed heads, humming and singing as they bunched roots together. “What are you doing?” Megan asked, peering over their shoulders. “Making the bridge stronger,” the twigman replied. “Who are you and how did you get here?” “My name’s Megan and I’m finding my way back home,” Megan replied. “Back home?” the twigmen said. “You’ll never find your way back home.” “But… but… this is the bridge to go back home!” Megan cried. “It has to be! The twigmen grabbed a bunch of roots. “You see this? There are a thousand little roots in this bunch, and your world is connected to just one of them.” “THOUSANDS?” Megan was surprised. “Only the Supreme Plant knows where they go. You could ask the Supreme Plant, but it’s a shame you can’t speak the plant language.” “But I can speak plant!” Megan lied. “Well, why didn’t you say so! Right this way. If you can’t speak plant you might be sent to a different world by mistake, and you’ll be stuck there forever!” Megan followed the twigmen and saw a tree at the center of the bridge, its roots bulging out in every direction. “Mr. Supreme Plant,” Megan began. “I want to go home. Can you please show me how?” “ He’s not the Supreme Plant!” the twigmen snapped, “she is!” They pointed at a lone dandelion under the great tree. “Oh,” Megan replied. “Can you tell me how to go home, Supreme Plant?” The plant said nothing. “I thought you knew how to speak plant,” The twigmen raised their eyebrows. Megan began to tremble. “I… I...” she said. She noticed that the plant was shaking with her. Megan flapped her arms and the plant in turn swayed with the breeze. Megan jiggled, wiggled, and spun around twice. The dandelion glowed. “I want to go home.” Megan said. The Supreme Plant loosened a few of her feather-like seeds. The seeds began to float up slowly. “It worked! She is showing us the way!” Megan ran after the seeds. “What did the Supreme Plant say?” the princess asked, struggling to keep up with Megan. “She told us to follow the seeds,” Megan said, “but we don’t have long!” They jumped through hoops, crawled through small spaces, and slipped through cracks until at last they found themselves in front of a large ladder made of old roots. The seeds drifted upwards. And they followed. One by one they returned to the top deck. Megan followed the glowing seeds into darkness. She saw the light on the other side of the bridge. “Frits we’re almost home!” she squealed, but Frits didn’t reply. Megan turned, but neither Frits nor the princess were behind her. CREAK! CREAK! The bridge began to shake. It was the trolls. They must have caught whiff of their scent. Megan held on tight. She could see her town in front of her. Behind her, she heard the tree trolls. Megan thought hard. The seeds would open the gates. She couldn’t leave without them. Megan took a step closer towards her town, but then she heard the princess scream. “Mrrrowww!” Frits was yowling in pain. The last of the seeds drifted away. And with a sinking heart, Megan heard the gates coil shut. “Frits, I’m coming!” Megan ran back the way she came. She burst through decaying roots, sliding across the bridge. “Help me!” Elavuarasi was crying. An injured troll was hanging off the side of the bridge. Frits and the princess stood over it. They were desperately trying to step on its hands and send it falling. Frits was scratching the troll’s bark-covered fingers, and the princess was kicking it. “Stop it!” Megan yelled, pushing Frits and the princess off the troll’s hand. “GRRR,” the troll groaned. It slowly climbed back up and drew itself to its full height. “GRRR,” it growled, sending green snot flying everywhere. Megan stood in front of the troll and swayed back and forth, flapping her arms. “GRRR,” the troll growled, softly this time. “It does not want to hurt us!” Megan yelled. “It’s here to protect the bridge.” “How do you know?” “There’s something about this place. I can now speak plant. The troll… it’s scared and angry. It says humans kill trees.” Megan touched the tree troll’s face. It winced. She stroked the creature's nose. “We just want to go home,” she mouthed. The troll looked at Megan sadly. It swayed its arms. It was telling her that the seeds were gone. The troll looked down – there was a dandelion sprouting on its big toe. But unlike the Supreme Plant, the dandelion on the troll's foot had just one seed. The troll plucked the seed and gave it to Megan. The troll’s branches creaked, its roots withered, its trunk turned to dust. Megan looked at the seed in her palm. It glowed – dimly at first and then into a bright flash. Megan woke up near the cable car, to the painful licks of a sandpaper tongue. “Meow,” Frits said, rubbing himself against her. “Frits,” Megan smiled. She raised her head slowly and found a rock with a shoestring attached to its nose standing over her. Megan grinned. She was right about the missing cats wanting to play with the strange rock. But somehow she couldn’t find the other cats. Megan stood up and dusted her clothes. “What’s this?” she asked, glancing at a furry seed stuck in between her fingers. “It’s a mystery seed, Frits! Want to find out what it is?” “Meow,” Frits replied, as Megan carried him. “Raahi is going to be so happy. Isn’t it a beautiful day, Frits?” Megan flapped her arms as she walked into the sunset. But Frits kept staring into the the mist. By the cable car, stood a figure dressed entirely in black. It was one of those things only cats could see. Frits watched the figure flap her arms in joy. “Meow,” Frits said in farewell. The princess brought her fingers together. SNAP.
author: C G Salamander

title: Garden of Thoughts
text: In the garden of minds where chaos seems interfering, Where stress and depress twins shall haunt you, You must plant the seed of thoughts. Nurture it everyday with knowledge and observance, Pray for its steady upbringing in wisdom, Water the seed of thoughts to sprout gradually into something unique, Let the warmth of ideas strengthen the plant of thoughts, Chanel it with education, And let it grow taller and taller. Let it be that huge tree which can stand firm by its own roots of wisdom and independent enough to share the beauty of its growth, Let it be mighty in its appearance but grounded as it used to be not forgetting its origins, Let it bear the best innovative fruits of its endeavours, And its taste be the sweetest and never seen or heard before ones, Discipline thy tree to stand upright to wade of the envious minds, Armour your thoughts through thick and thin of temptations Be ready to face the seasons of varied opinions launched by the like and unlike minded trees But your tree shall sway in what is right, And gracefully brush off the unwanted leaves of lies. Be at the center of that garden that other young plants look upto you While other trees watch you with pride, And finally, be that tree of thought that intruders hesitate to cut you down and look at you respectfully. - Natasha
author: Natasha  Punnoose
illustrator: Aditi Dilip; Avishek Sen; Sarthak Sinha

title: Learning How to Fly
text: Today is the day I learn to fly. Help! Thump I hit and hurt my head. Wheres my mommy? Mommy I fell from my nest trying to fly. While little bird lets get back up and try again said mommy bird. Here we go little bird said mommy bird. I'm flapping my wings mommy. Here we go. Mommy I got it. I'm flying. See my little bird if you keep trying and not give up you will succeed.
author: Leeora Avant

title: Painting the Fence
text: ﻿Story Description ﻿ Tony and Tania play outside when their father gives them a task - to paint the garden fence. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿ Paintbrushes ﻿pay-n-t-bruh-sh-is ﻿Papa gave some paintbrushes to Tony and Tania Carefully ﻿c-air-ful-ee ﻿They painted the gate carefully, to stop paint getting everywhere. Practice ﻿pra-k-ti-ss ﻿They needed to practice before they painted the gate. Sleek ss-l-ee-k﻿ ﻿ ﻿The paint looked smooth, sleek and shiny. Tony and Tania are brother and sister. Tony likes to paint pictures, and Tania enjoys swinging on tree branches. One day Mama surprised Tony and Tania by playing outside with them. They played hide and seek, and catch together. "Papa has something for you," said Mama, and Tony and Tania got excited. "Here," said Papa, giving them paintbrushes and pots of paint. "I want you to paint the gate. Practice first so you can get it right. It'll be fun." Tony and Tania dipped their hands in the paint and made red, yellow and blue handprints on the pavement. They spent a long time making handprints - so long, in fact, that by the time they had finished practicing, they were covered in paint! Tania tested the paint on the wall. It was bright and sleek. It looked great. Tony and Tania watched two men painting a new wall in the distance. They saw how carefully and slowly they painted. They decided they would be very careful too when painting the gate. Tony and Tania painted the gate slowly and carefully, but sometimes they would paint each other by mistake! Tania got covered in green paint, and Tony got covered in red paint! "Are you finished?" said Tony. "Yes, are you?" replied Tania. Tony opened the gate. It was red on one side, and green on the other. "Look at the gate, it looks great!" said Tony. "I think Mama and Papa are really going to like it." "Thanks, Mama," said Tania, as she gave her a cloth to wipe her face. Tony wiped the paint off his arms. "Here is a drink and some food for both of you," said Mama. "Now, let me and your Papa go and see your new blue and yellow gate." "Oh, no!" said Tony and Tania. After Reading Who played with Tony and Tania outside? What did Papa ask Tony and Tania to do? Before they could paint, what did Tony and Tania have to do first? Who did Tony and Tania copy while painting? What colour did they paint the gate? What mistake did they make?
author: Hello English

title: Friends Who Cares
text: Once upon a time, way back in 1960, there were four friends whose names were Aman, Peeka, Amit and Jagoo. They live in a hostel in Delhi. One day, Jagoo's father called him and asked him to come back home who lives in Palampur. Jagoo got scared and ran to his friends and told his friends, "Friends' Friends' please help me, my father called me at home urgently" On the way, when they were going to palampur, Amit one of his friend asked him, what has happened there at palampur. Jagoo said "it is a mystery even I am also not aware off." When they reached there, Jagoo's father told the whole story about the house where he was working as watchman since long. The mystery was there were two builders named Prabhu and Deva who wanted to build a five star hotel instead of that beautiful house where the Jagoo's father was working. Father told that when the landlord and landlady were alive, builders didn't have the courage to come near that house and destroy it. In 1962, when they both passed away, these two builders started troubling the Jagoo's father and they started destroying the house. Then, all friends thought of a plan, that two of the friends will act like sheikhs and will give them a lesson to the builders so that they will not trouble the Jagoo's father again. So Aman and Peeka dressed up like Sheikhs and they started living in the house. When one day Prabhu and Deva came to destroy the house and messing up with Jagoo's father, then Aman and Peeka came out of the house and they told that we have purchased this house from landlords. Prabhu and Deva started fighting with them and Sheikhs threatened them, if they even think of destroying this house, the consequences will not be good for their family. Prabhu and Deva got scared from Sheikhs and ran away. So, it is rightly said "Good Friends are those who can make your problems as their own... Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed".
author: Namit Kalra

title: SAVE OUR TREE!
text: It was the last period and everyone could go home after the school bell rang. But little Kumuda was worried. Her favourite tree was going to be chopped down for a new playground. "Where will the birds build their nests, now?" she thought... “Where will the stray animals take shelter when it rains heavily?” she wondered, on her way back home. As soon as her mother returned from work, little Kumuda told her everything that happened at school. Even her mother felt bad for the poor tree. Helpless little Kumuda began crying inconsolably. Her mother asked, “Will crying, save the tree?” Little Kumuda said “no” amidst sobbing. “Then why are you wasting time, shedding tears? I know you'll think of a solution by morning". The next morning, when little Kumuda was getting ready for school, her mother instilled courage in her. "Go, talk to your friends, teachers and convince them” she said. Little Kumuda smiled. After breakfast, a determined little Kumuda set off to school, ready to save her favourite tree. She met her classmates on the way. She told them how important the tree is, not just for them but for animals, birds and insects too. Her friends agreed to join her mission. The children wrote letters, urging students of other classes too, to join their campaign to save their tree. The letters and posters were put up on the notice board. The children then spoke to their social studies teacher about the tree. The teacher was more than happy to help them out. He encouraged the children to spread the word and promised to support them throughout. The next task was to convince the strict science teacher. The children reluctantly approached her. But when she smiled after listening to their plea, the children breathed a sigh of relief. She told them to talk to the headmaster about the tree, because they could do nothing, without his permission. The headmaster patiently listened to what little Kumuda had to say. He was proud of her concern towards environment protection. He then assured her that he would talk to the school management and let her know by November 26 th. Finally, on November 26 th, an assembly was held. The headmaster announced that it was “World environment protection day”. And on this day, he gave little Kumuda and her friends the good news, they were waiting for. “The tree will not be felled. It will be a part of the new playground” said the headmaster. All the children cheered as little Kumuda received a pat on her back. Little Kumuda thanked her friends. All the children congratulated each other. Some broke into a dance, while others started singing! Their joy knew no bounds. They then went away to play games. Little Kumuda stood underneath her favourite tree and looked at the happy faces of her friends; the friends who stood by her, for a good cause. What a way to celebrate ‘World environment protection day’! She’ll never forget this day.
author: Adithimanasa T S

text: Once upon a time there was a parrot. His name was Roxy. He was very open minded. One day Roxy met with an owl. His name was Roza. He was also very like minded. Thy sat on a tree and started gossiping. They liked each other. After a while they became good friends. After few months one day they misunderstood each other. They left the place and didn't meet for a long time. Got to know that a butterfly thought an idea. He went to Roza and told about Roxy's false illness. After a moment they forgot all their misunderstandings and issues and again became forever friends. Now the story of their friendship is popular in the whole animal world.

title: My Pet German - A True Story
text: Namit love pets, he wanted to bring a dog as a new family member in his home. But no one wants to support his wish, as pets requires too much care, space and attention. Everyone in Namit's home is working and no one is having time to take care of a pet. One day Namit started crying, when he saw a pet seller on the roadside holding a black color little dog who was only one month old. Somehow, he insisted his parents to take that "pup" home and named that pup "German" When Namit and his parents entered their home along with German, Namit's grandparents became very angry, Namit's Father said lets see whether we can keep a German or not. After a week, when Vaccination started for German, he became little frustrated and this frustration resulted again in unrest in grandparent's attitude towards German. One day, Namit's Grandfather told Namit's Father that he did not want to keep German at home and asked him to take it seriously and take an action, That day, Namit's Father asked one of his friend (Mr. Raghav) to take German to his home, who was out of town and he said that he will take German after a month, then all vaccination will also be done. After a Month............ Now the day arrived for Namit The day of loosing hope, The day of sadness and disappointment, The day of loosing a friend When Mr. Raghav entered Namit's home to take German, suddenly day of sadness becomes the day of Happiness and hope for Namit, when his grandparents stopped giving German to Mr. Raghav. Namit's Grandparents said "Now we both are also attached to German and We can keep him as our new family member in our home". It has been rightly said that "A dog is the only animal on the earth that loves you more than he loves himself"
author: Namit Kalra

title: Bombay Ducks, Bombay Docks
text: The twinkle of a million stars On the shimmering sea so far In the distance I can see The boats are chugging towards me Soon they’ll come in with their catch The bombils we’ll then sort and batch On the bamboos they will dry Two, three days in the sun that’s high Bombay Ducks are not birds, you see They are fish served fresh and dry It’s the first day of the summer vacation. “No school until the rains,” Vandana tells herself. She lives in a koliwada along the shores of Mumbai and belongs to the Koli community, the original residents of Bombay. Her family owns two boats. Every day her father and grandfather set out to catch fish. During the holidays, Vandana helps sort the catch. ​What time the fishing boats leave the koliwada depends on​ ​the tide and the mood of the sea. Today, the family’s boats​ ​come in with their catch at 3 in the morning. ​As dawn breaks, the women settle down to sort the fish. Later in the day, Vandana and her friends will help them. Bombils or Bombay Ducks are strung out on the bamboo racks like fat, glistening commas. The shrimps are spread out on clean concrete rectangles. From Vandana’s house up high, this looks like a patchwork quilt. ​April and May are the busiest months of the year for Vandana’s family. By the last week of May, the strong winds and rough seas make it too dangerous for their tiny boats to ride the waves. ​When the monsoon sky sends down rain, day after day, night​ ​after night, there is plenty of time to talk and rest. The family​ ​sits around Aaji. They listen to her stories and mend fishing nets.​ ​Vandana loves the tales of a time when there were hundreds of​ ​fishing villages on the islands that are now known as Mumbai. ​Aaji tells her tribe of listeners that​ ​th​​ough people think Bombay was made​ ​up of seven islands, a long time ago,​ ​there were 25 islands. “The shorelines​ ​were dotted with fishing villages.​ ​Then came the city. It was hungry for​ ​roads, bridges and development.”​ ​Today there are​ ​only 36 koliwadas left. ​“Our koliwadas might be disappearing, but our Bombay Ducks remain. Have you ever wondered how a fish got such a name?” asks Aaji. “We have always called the fish bomelow, bomello or bombil. But the story goes that the Bombay Duck got its name from mail​ ​trains or daaks. The daaks carried the dried fish far inland.​ ​From daak it became duck during the British Raaj,” she adds. ​Aaji feels the Bombay Ducks and its famous docks are what make this city special. “Aaji, tell us more about the docks where ships were built,” says Vandana, who often​ ​visits Sassoon Dock with her Baba. ​“The docks stood on the eastern shore of the islands,” says Aaji. “In the beginning, they were just bunders or landing places. Then they​ ​became places to repair boats and build ships, when trade increased.” ​“Not just Kolis, but many different communities were part of building the ships and the docks,” recalls Aaji. The Parsis, the Wadia family in particular, she says, were big shipbuilders. Then there were Maratha and Christian carpenters from Bassein and lascars from the west coast, and even Chinese fitters and Pathan riveters. ​ Lascars: A term Europeans used for sailors from South Asia. Fitters: Someone who installs machinery. Riveter: Someone who fixes things, often with a hammer. ​Agashi and Bassein, ports that lay just north of Bombay, were famous for their timber. Great ships that crossed the oceans were built here between the years 1550 and 1600. ​The Mazagon and Bombay dockyards​ ​came in the 1600s. Many historic​ ​ships that fought in naval battles​ ​were built here.​ ​HMS Trincomallee is one of the oldest​ ​warships afloat today. It is in a museum​ ​in England. The Treaty of Nanking, which ended the​ ​Opium Wars with China in 1842, was​ ​signed on the HMS Cornwallis,​ ​a 74-gun frigate built in Bombay. ​Ships from all over the world docked at Bombay. They shared the seas with boats from the little fishing villages. ​Vandana feels proud that she belongs to a community that has always lived and worked by the sea and shaped the city’s docks. She’s happy that her life is linked to the shimmering sea. ​​​ For over 500 years the Kolis have lived and​ ​worked around Mumbai’s coastal waters.​ ​They fish and man boats.​ Docks are places where boats are anchored, but​ ​the docks in this story are also places where ships​ ​were built.​ ​ Between 1550 and 1600 great ocean voyaging​ships ​​were manufactured at Agashi and Bassein.​ ​The carpenters of two villages in Bassein, Small​ ​Carpentry and Big Carpentry, worked in the​ ​Bombay Dockyard till very recently.​ The earliest dockyard was commissioned by​ ​Governor Aungier in 1671. Ship repairs began​ ​at Mazagon Dock in 1673 and shipbuilding​ ​officially dates back to 1774.
author: Fleur D'Souza

title: Fighting Over Toys
text: Story Description Eric enjoys stealing his brother Martin's toys and playing with them. One day he gets chased by an elephant. Martin tries to rescue Eric and get his toys back. Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics ﻿Recovering ﻿re-cuv-ur-ing ﻿Martin was recovering from a high fever. Argue ﻿are-g-yew ﻿The brothers would argue over toys. Shadow ﻿sh-a-d-oh ﻿A big dark shadow came over Eric. Relief ﻿ree-leaf ﻿Eric felt relief once he was safe. ﻿ ﻿ Martin felt sick, and so instead of going to school, he stayed in bed. His mother checked on him. He had a high fever. Martin felt worried because sometimes his younger brother Eric would steal his toys, especially when he wasn't around. And now being stuck in bed, Martin could not keep Eric away from his stuff. While Martin was asleep and recovering, Eric went and played with all of Martin's toys. He played with the train set, the buses, the trucks, his kite, and read his books, including his diary. Eric was happy because Martin wasn't there to stop him. Martin woke up and went to see Eric. He caught him playing with one of his purple elephants. As they argued and grabbed the toy, twisting and pulling it, one of the elephant's legs came off. "Now you've broken it!" shouted Martin. "It was your fault!" said Eric. Eric snatched the elephant and ran as fast as he could. He made it to a tree in a field. There were some elephants living nearby. Eric threw the toy in the tree and stopped to catch his breath. Eric looked up and saw a massive shadow looming over him. Suddenly an elephant roared, and Eric took off, running away with all of his energy. The elephant, upset that Eric was near his family, chased after him. Eric found a tree with some low hanging branches. He climbed up the branches and sat high in the tree. The elephant was angry and it pulled on a branch, trying to get Eric down from the tree. Eric stayed where he was, too scared to move. Eric found some courage and moved away from the elephant, climbing higher in the tree. Very soon the elephant got tired and gave up. Eric sighed in relief. Eric heard rustling in the branches. He looked and he felt shocked when he saw Martin climbing the tree. Martin had been watching the whole time from his bedroom window. He reached for Eric to grab his hand and rescue him. "I lost the elephant toy," said Eric. "Don't worry about it," said Martin. "I just want to bring you home. Here, take my hand." But just as Eric stretched to grab Martin's hand, Martin slipped on a branch and fell out of the tree! He tumbled towards the hard ground. Just as Martin expected to hit the ground with a heavy thud, an elephant's trunk reached out and seized him. Eric climbed down from the tree and ran away. "Look! He's still got the toy elephant!" said Martin. "Let's run after him." The elephant charged after Eric. The elephant caught up with Eric and Martin said, "I know you still have my toy. It's time to give it back, Eric." "I told you I lost it in the tree!" said Eric. "Oh, all right," said Eric, giving Martin the elephant toy. "I give in. You can have it back." "Thank you," said Martin. "And now to take the elephant home." Martin rode the elephant to its tribe and went home with Eric. "Promise me you won't tell mum about this," said Eric. "I'll be in so much trouble." "Don't worry," said Martin. "I'll keep it a secret." But as soon as they got home, Martin told his mum what Eric did, and he started to cry. "How dare you!" said their mother to Eric. "You can buy Martin a new toy out of your pocket money!" Eric felt cheated, but he learned his lesson. He would not steal things from other people ever again. Dishonesty breeds dishonesty. After Reading While Martin was sick, what did Eric do? Which toy did Eric steal? Where did Eric hide when the elephant chased him? Who saved Martin from falling out of the tree? What did Martin promise to do? What did Martin actually do, and how did Eric spend his pocket money?

title: The thirsty crow
text: It was a hot summer’s day. A thirsty crow flew into a village in search of water. The crow flew over the houses, fields, and trees. But he didn’t find any water. After a long time, he came across a farm. Under one of the trees on the farm was a pitcher of water. Happy that he found some water finally, he swooped down to the tree and then down to the ground. He quickly moved towards the pitcher and looked inside. There was very little water in the pot. The crow put his beak inside the pitcher but could not reach the water. The water level was too low, and the narrow opening prevented his neck from going all the way down. He tried to push the vessel down to let the water out, but it was too heavy. The crow was disappointed. He was really thirsty and needed a drink of water badly. He could have given up and flown to another farm, looking for water. But he didn’t. Instead, he looked around and thought, “What else can I do?” He saw that there were a lot of pebbles on the farm. And, he had an idea! He collected a pebble and put it into the pitcher. He collected another pebble and another and put them all in the pitcher. As he added more and more stones, the water level came up to the brim.
author: Akshith Choudary
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Padmanabh; Pradeep Thennatt

title: dack to school
text: I am a primary school teacher. Do you know that even teachers attend classes from time to time? We become students and learn from senior teachers! In one such class, I met a senior teacher, Mrs. Sasikala. She was a kind person and was a good teacher. She was part of the Municipal Department that looked after education. Her job was to ensure that every kid in her locality would attend school. She was our favourite teacher in the training sessions. That’s why we were disappointed when she didn’t come to take our class for a couple of days. Then, much to our relief, she started taking our class again. She explained her absence — she told us she had gone in search of her missing students. “What missing students?” we all asked. Mrs. Sasikala then told us what she had been doing for the last two days. “We try our very best to get all children to attend school. These children come from poor backgrounds. When a child is absent for more than three to four days, I visit their place to see what’s the problem,” said Mrs. Sasikala. This time two children stopped coming to my school. They were children of construction workers. I visited the construction site and learnt that some of the workers had moved to another construction site far away. The supervisor told me where to find them. So, I took a bus to that construction site far away. I found the parents of my missing students.” “I was shocked to see my students working at the construction site, carrying bricks on their heads. I asked the parents why they had stopped sending their children to school.” Madam, we go where our work takes us. If we don’t work, we won’t have enough money to buy food. Now that we work here, how can we send the children to a school that is so far away?” the mother said. “I told them I could find a school nearby. The next day, I took the children to the nearest Municipal School and got them admission there. Now the children are back in school,” Mrs. Sasikala finished her story with a smile. We were all relieved to hear that those children were back in school. We felt very proud of our teacher who took so much trouble to get those children back to school. Soon, the training session was completed. I went back to my school. On my return, I found one of my students had stopped attending school. She came from a slum across the railway track. That evening I found myself crossing the railway track, on my way to the slum, in search of my missing student.
author: annam arush
illustrator: Godwin  Chipenya; Linh Chi; Padmanabh; Ruchi Shah; Shalini Jithesh; Students of  Himalayan Public School

title: Sports Day
text: ﻿Story Description ﻿A purple gorilla called PG almost forgets to go to his friend Annie's sports day. When he turns up, he sees Annie competing in a race. Annie runs despite having an injury. Can she win? Before Reading - Vocabulary and Phonics Stadium ﻿ss-tay-dee-um ﻿The contest was held inside a big stadium. Ceremony seh-ruh-moh-nee﻿ ﻿The crowd watched the prize giving ceremony. Athletes ﻿a-th-lee-t-ss ﻿The competitors were fit athletes. Podium ﻿po-dee-um ﻿Annie stood high on the podium and received her medal. ﻿ ﻿ PG the purple gorilla was playing frisbee with his friend. Suddenly, PG remembered that he had to do something important. "Oh, no!" he said. "It's my friend's sports day. I almost forgot! I had better go to the stadium." PG's friend Annie was going to race, even though she had injured her foot. She looked for PG but couldn't see him in the crowd. "I wonder if he remembered," she said. Annie watched the opening ceremony. She looked closer at some of the athletes. There, walking with them, was PG! What a naughty gorilla! How did he even get there? It was time for Annie's race. She concentrated and waited for the start gun. Everyone was completely still and silent. Bang! The started gun sounded and the athletes ran fast, heading towards the finish line. The crowd went crazy, shouting and cheering them on. The girl in the green shirt was winning, when suddenly, Annie came running past her to steal first place. She did it! Annie won the race by less than half a second! She was so happy and cheerful as she crossed the finish line. Annie's followers were so pleased that she had won. They waved coloured paper in the air and sang her name. Annie congratulated the other runners for taking part, but the girl in the blue shirt was angry that she had come last in the race. The crowd cheered as Annie stepped on to the podium and received her winner's gold medal. It was a glorious moment for her. Annie also won a trophy for being voted the best athlete of the year at her school. The athletes posed for a picture, and suddenly PG appeared behind Annie, surprising her. PG told his friends all about sports day. They were thrilled to hear that Annie had won. They asked PG if he would compete next year. "Maybe," he said. "If they have an eating contest." After Reading Where did PG almost forget to go? What kind of mischief did PG get up to at the stadium? What was wrong with Annie? By how much did Annie win the race? What two things did Annie receive as prizes? Who sneakily appeared in the photograph of the athletes?
author: Hello English

title: I Know My Rights
text: Rights for you, rights for me, Rights are there for everybody, Rights lift up and rights defend, Rights are like your best friend. Rights stop things from going wrong, Our rights make us very strong! Rights are the need of the hour, Your very own secret super power! Every girl like me deserves The chance to breathe in this world. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO BE BORN. Kho-kho, cricket, kabaddi, Swinging, sliding, hide-and-seek. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO PLAY. Meeting friends, new and old, On the streets and in our homes. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO MEET AND MAKE FRIENDS. You might not see me in a crowd, But you’ll hear my voice – it’s extra loud! I HAVE THE RIGHT TO HAVE MY OPINIONS RESPECTED. Around me is a big strong bubble. Step too close, you’ll be in trouble. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO NOT BE SEXUALLY AND PHYSICALLY ABUSED. I know that I have got the choice To change the world with my voice I HAVE THE RIGHT TO SELF EXPRESSION. I don’t want to cook and clean, Help fix cars or serve tea. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO NOT BE SENT TO WORK. I won’t hide or stay indoors. I have the right to learn and soar. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO SPECIAL CARE, SUPPORT AND EDUCATION. What, why, where and how? My questions need an answer now! I HAVE THE RIGHT TO INFORMATION. I HAVE THE RIGHT TO KNOW MY RIGHTS. 1 Everyone under 18 has these rights. 2 All children have these rights, no matter who they are, where they live, what their parents do, what language they speak, what their religion is, whether they are a boy or girl, what their culture is, whether they have a disability, whether they are rich or poor. No child should be treated unfairly on any basis. 3 All adults should do what is best for you. 4 The government has a responsibility to make sure your rights are protected. 5 Your family has the responsibility to help you learn to exercise your rights, and to ensure that your rights are protected. 6 You have the right to be alive. 7 You have the right to a name, and this should be officially recognised by the government. UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in Child Friendly Language 8 You have the right to a nationality (to belong to a country). 9 You have the right to an identity – an official record of who you are. 10 You have the right to live with your parent(s), unless it is bad for you. You have the right to live with a family who cares for you. 11 If you live in a different country than your parents do, you have the right to be together in the same place. 12 You have the right to be protected from kidnapping. 13 You have the right to give your opinion, and for adults to listen and take it seriously. 14 You have the right to find out things and share what you think with others, unless it harms or offends other people. 15 You have the right to choose your own religion and beliefs. 16 You have the right to choose your own friends and join or set up groups, as long as it isn’t harmful to others. 17 You have the right to privacy. 18 You have the right to get information that is important to your well-being. 19 You have the right to be raised by your parent(s) if possible. 20 You have the right to be protected from being hurt and mistreated, in body or mind. 21 You have the right to special care and help if you cannot live with your parents. 22 You have the right to care and protection if you are adopted or in foster care. 23 You have the right to special protection and help if you are a refugee. 24 You have the right to special education and care if you have a disability, so that you can live a full life. 25 You have the right to the best health care possible, safe water to drink, nutritious food, a clean and safe environment, and information to help you stay well. 26 If you live in care or in other situations away from home, you have the right to have these living arrangements looked at regularly to see if they are the most appropriate. 27 You have the right to help from the government if you are poor or in need. 28 You have the right to food, clothing, a safe place to live and to have your basic needs met. 29 You have the right to a good quality education. You should be encouraged to go to school to the highest level you can. 30 Your education should help you use and develop your talents and abilities. It should help you learn to live peacefully, protect the environment and respect other people. 31 You have the right to practice your own culture, language and religion - or any you choose. 32 You have the right to play and rest. 33 You have the right to protection from work that harms you, and is bad for your health and education. If you work, you have the right to be safe and paid fairly. 34 You have the right to protection from harmful drugs and from the drug trade. 35 You have the right to be free from sexual abuse. 36 You have the right to protection from any kind of exploitation. 37 You have the right to not be punished by anyone in a cruel or harmful way. 38 You have the right to protection and freedom from war. Children under fifteen cannot be forced to go into the army or take part in war. 39 You have the right to help if you’ve been hurt, neglected or badly treated. 40 You have the right to legal help and fair treatment in the justice system that respects your rights. 41 If the laws of your country provide better protection of your rights than the articles in this Convention, those laws should apply. 42 You have the right to know your rights! The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child says that every child must have all these rights. If you feel that you or someone you know is/are being denied their rights, then speak to an adult about it. You can call Childline on 1098 and talk to someone there. To know more about child rights, visit
author: Menaka Raman

title: Fluffy and Zozo's lovely incident.
text: I always wonder what is the connection between a dog and a bee? I just wonder this because my dog, fluffy loves to hear the buzzing sound of bees. Recently it has made a bee friend. I named it Zozo. Zozo the bee is fat and round.It loves to sing and dance in front of fluffy but i am afraid that it may sting [bite] him. Bees are harmful and some may also sting us.But we need to be careful and make sure not to disturb these insects. I would like you to read this incident about these two lovable friends. So it is time to go into the story. One day Zozo was collecting nectar from a flower. Suddenly a strong wind blew past it and Zozo could not control himself and was dragged by the wind. He landed on a flower which tried to eat him. It was an insect eating plant. Zozo was so scared. It was protecting itself by hiding behind a tree! but the winds took it and landed it on a pile of leaves. Zozo saw a white, fluffy thing running towards it! guess who it was? it was Fluffy. He saved Zozo from being taken away by the strong winds again. He covered Zozo in his hair and took It to its kennel and he was hearing Zozo singing in his buzzing voice. How lovely is this incident? I bet you must have imagined it in a wonderful way. I wish and hope that you love this story. Thank you and read my other stories too! Meet you next time.
author: Vijita R
illustrator: Isuri Dayaratne; Sushree Sangeeta Samantara; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Puchku Seeks a Song
text: From the window of her classroom, Puchku can see the jamun tree. It stands with its branches spread out, like it wants to give you a hug. Under its shade, even the hottest day feels cool. But the tree is naughty – it drops fruits that leave bright purple splodges on Puchku’s uniform. There are also birds that hide in its leaves and slyly poop so that it goes SPLAT! on her head. Every day, when it’s time for tiffin, Puchku runs to the jamun tree. Sometimes Dodla runs faster than her and gets there first. Boltu is always last. There’s always a butterfly or a worm or a flower that makes him forget the race. Today, Puchku beats Dodla to the jamun tree by three seconds. But someone else is under the jamun tree before them. Who is that? Is it a bowl made of branches, twigs and leaves? And look! There’s someone in the bowl, with two little eyes and one little beak. “Hello,” says Puchku. “Do you think it’s a baby pterodactyl?” Dodla asks Puchku. He likes the word pterodactyl. The “p” is silent, like a secret. “Maybe it’s a baby dragon,” says Puchku. “That’s a baby bird, dummies,” says Boltu, finally at the jamun tree. “But birds make noises,” says Puchku. “Pigeons coo, crows caw, parakeets chatter, peacocks squawk, kites screech. If this is a bird, why is she quiet?” Boltu scratches his head. “You know how we talk, using words?” says Boltu. Puchku and Dodla nod. “Birds use song in just the same way,” says Boltu. “That’s how they talk to each other. So maybe this baby bird doesn’t know her song because she’s too small?” Dodla looks worried. “But without a song, the baby bird can’t talk to anyone! She’ll be so alone.” hello there! hi! knock knock who's there? ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha Puchku decides this is a mission for the (BPD) 2 – Brilliant Plans Department by Boltu Puchku and Dodla. “Boltu, Dodla, we’re going to find this baby bird her song.” Boltu gets some cotton wool. Dodla finds a cardboard box. Puchku draws a map of the places where they could look for a song for the baby bird. Need help? Don’t worry. CALL! Brilliant. Plans. Department. B. P. D. Boltu Puchku ﻿Dodla Cardboard Box Baby bird Map Cotton wool First, the baby bird and the (BPD) 2 go to Melody Aunty’s music classes. Carefully, Puchku brings the baby bird out. PHOO PHOOO PHIUUU! Imran is playing the flute. “Is this your song?” asks Puchku. The baby bird is quiet. They take the baby bird to different rooms. KWIEEEE KWIEEEE TWANG plink MMHMMGROOOMPH DUBA DUBA DUBA DUBBLE WAAAAAYOOOON PATINK PATINKKKK TA RA PUM RUM PUM “Is this your song?” asks Puchku. But… … the baby bird is quiet. She looks at Puchku. Boltu scratches his head. Dodla looks sad. “Don’t worry,” Puchku tells the baby bird. “We’ll find your song.” GHWOING GHWOING Dodla plays a new tune on his rubber band guitar. HIC HIC ﻿ Boltu hiccups. “Is this your song?” asks Puchku. The baby bird is quiet. Could it be the SQUEE-TOOOO whistle that Police Uncle uses? Could it be the CLICK CLICK CLICK CLATTER CLATTER CLATTER of the sewing machine? Maybe it is in the shoe that goes SQUEAK Could it be in the pressure cooker that goes SQUEEEEEEEEEL when its work is done? Maybe it is on the radio that SINGS in so many voices? Puchku borrows her mother’s mobile phone and they play all the ringtones, one by one. “Is this your song?” Puchku asks the baby bird. Dodla’s stomach GROWLS. (They forgot to eat tiffin!) “Is this your song?” asks Puchku. But the baby bird is quiet. GRRROWL Maybe it’s in one of the doorbells on Puchku’s street? Puchku, Boltu and Dodla ring each one, but... pat-a-tang TING TONG TRRRRRR! … the baby bird is quiet (even though some of Puchku’s neighbours are loud). At the end of tiffin break, the (BPD) 2 has no more brilliant plans. “What do we do now?” Boltu asks. “We’ll take her to Wildlife Didi,” says Puchku. And so they sadly walk to the staff room, to find the biology teacher in her usual corner. “Puchku, Boltu, Dodla, what happened? You look sad,” asks Wildlife Didi. “We found a baby bird, but we couldn’t find the baby bird’s song,” says Puchku in a sad voice. “We looked everywhere!” says Dodla in a sadder voice. Boltu sniffs even more sadly. “It’s okay. You won’t always get it right.” Wildlife Didi gives Boltu a hanky. “But the baby bird still doesn’t have a song!” Puchku wails. “But she has you, right? You won’t leave her because she doesn’t have a song like the other birds?” asks Wildlife Didi. Puchku, Boltu and Dodla shake their heads. “You just have to be patient,” Wildlife Didi tells Puchku with a smile. Puchku picks up the baby bird carefully and says, “Baby bird, you just keep your ears open. Any sound you like, you make it your song. And I’ll sing it with you. Okay?” The baby bird nods her little head and says, “Cheep.”
author: Deepanjana Pal

title: Mary is Sick
text: This is Mary. Mary is 5 years old, just like you. One day, Mary was not feeling very well. Her tummy was hurting very much. She did not know what to do so she yelled for her mom. Her mom came running to her room to find out what was wrong with Mary. Mary did not look very good, so she decided to take Mary to the hospital to find out what was wrong with her. On their way to the hospital, Mary was very scared of what the doctor was going to do to her. She even started crying. Her mom, hugged her tight and assured her that everything was going to be all right and that the doctors are going to make her feel better. Once at the hospital, Mary was very calm. The doctor examined her hear, throat, ears and found that Mary had a stomach bug and that she needed to take some medicine in order to feel better. On their way home, they went to the pharmacy to pick up Mary's medicine in hopes of it making her feel better. Once at home, Mary felt so much better thanks to the medicine the doctor gave to her.
author: Ana Maria Rodriguez
illustrator: Aripana Foundation; Bianca de Jong; Karen  Vermeulen; Subi Bosa; Tanvee Nabar

title: Ariz Pockets the Desert
text: For my brother, Azhar. Ariz was always proud. At times, for his super grades at school. On some days, he would be proud of the toys that he had but his friend, Amir, did not have. On some other day, for his win in the races. And sometimes for being a favourite of Dadijaan. Grandpa was seeing this for many days. And one day, he decided to teach him a lesson. So, he took Ariz to the beach. Ariz frolicked in the water and ran with the waves. In the sand, he tried to build a castle but that he could never do. He asked his grandfather, ‘Dadajaan! Why is this soil so different from the soil outside our house?’ Dadajaan answered, ‘This is not soil, my son. This is known as sand.’ ‘Oh! Why is there no sand at our place?’ ‘Sand is found mostly on beaches. And the desert are full of sand.’ The boy was excited to learn about the desert. He filled his pocket with a handful of sand when they were returning home. And when anybody asked him about it, he would say, ‘I have the desert in my pocket.’ Grandfather was pleased. He let the boy shout all day long, ‘I have pocketed the desert! I have pocketed the desert!’ At night, before bedtime, Ariz was called to Dadajaan’s room. ‘Why do you go around shouting you have the desert with you?’ he asked the boy. ‘I have sand in my pocket and you said the desert is full of sand. So, I have a desert in my pocket.’ Grandfather laughed so hard that his glasses fell down from his nose. Dadajaan said, ‘You have only a handful of sand and yet it is your desert. The same way, we have only few qualities in us and we think we are the most perfect and better than others. Only fools are full of pride.’ Ariz became sad for a moment. His face fell. Then it brightened. He smiled as he understood what grandfather wanted him to learn. And then, he was many things after that, but never proud again.
author: Aftab Yusuf Shaikh

title: Everyone Has a Right to a Bath
text: Bruckert Mrs Earthworm is angry. She is fed up of being covered in mud and never being able to have a proper bath. She insists that her husband install a bathtub with running water. The bathtub is easy to make. Mr Earthworm finds an old flower pot lying in the kitchen garden. He patches up the few holes and some gaps. And it’s done! The installation of running water at their home was quite another thing. The first attempt was with straws connected to the surface. But the flow was too weak and during heavy rains the mud rose obstructing the mouth of the pipes. He improved his device by connecting a garden hose directly onto a drainpipe. The flow was absolutely satisfactory. But this water was not suitable for Mrs Earthworm. She finds that it had too much residue, is not clear enough and does not smell good. There was another more important problem that dampened Mrs Earthworm's craving for a bath - the temperature. The water is too cold! Mr Earthworm got back to work and added a filter and a handmade water heater. Now it’s perfect. Mrs Earthworm can finally relax in the bath that she so wanted.
author: Danielle Bruckert

title: There's an alien in my house!
text: There’s an alien in my house... We are under attack! The walls are changing colour. It must be the alien. The air is getting warmer. It must be the alien. Strangers keep coming. It must be the alien. We need protection. I build a fort. Mom and Dad normally build with me, but these days I feel invisible. It must be the alien. I hear a weird noise in the middle of the night. It must be the alien. We are under attack! I am an army of one. 1 step, 2 step... I am the army. 3 step, 4 step... Ready for battle. 5 step, 6 step... Away with you, alien! 7 step, 8 step... I get closer. 9 step, 10 step... I am by its head. Woah! I get a fright. It is tiny and it......looks like me?! How can that be? Is it really an alien? Maybe it’s a friend. Maybe it’s my friend? 1 step, 2 step... We are now an army of two.
author: Refi loe Moahloli

title: A Very Busy Day
text: Today is a very busy day! Mama and I have lots of things to do and see. We walk to the station and find people in a queue. Old people and young people, loud people and quiet people, all going to town. Through the minibus window, I see cars driving by. Fast cars and slow cars, big cars and small cars. There are so many buildings in town! Tall ones and short ones, glass ones and brick ones, everywhere I look. Mama and I walk in and out of shops. Shops for clothes and shops for books, shops for bags and all sorts of things. Mama tries on some shoes. Red shoes and green shoes, high shoes and low shoes. Hello! Ola! Jambo! Bonjour! In a big store, we fill a trolley with food. Boxes of cereal, and sacks of fruit. Bags of flour and bottles of juice. Mama shows me the toys and asks me to choose! There are soft toys and round toys, loud toys and fast toys. Today we’ve bought lots of things! Bags of food and bags of clothes. A pair of shoes and even some treats. Back at home, in our quiet house, I take out the special gift that Mama bought just for me!
author: Chisanga Mukuka

title: The New Road
text: Chapansi and her best friend Luano love collecting inswa. They love to play on the old dirt road.......even if Mama would tsk-tsk because the stones hurt her feet. One day, big cars arrive. Mama calls them Caterpillars. They cover the road in black stuff. Mama calls it tar. The road is smooth now. Like walking on a mattress! But when Chapansi and Luano go to the road to catch inswa...... they only catch three! Chapansi used to love playing chiyato with Luano. But there are no more stones on the road to play with. Chapansi is worried. What if the inswa can’t breathe anymore? Chapansi kicks the road! Chapansi goes to Mama. ‘Don’t be sad, my child. Inswa will always find a way out,’ she says. One rainy day, Luano comes running to Chapansi’s house. ‘Inswa is back!’ Inswa is back! It defeated the road! Mama was right after all!
author: Fiske Serah  Nyirongo

title: My Dog
text: Dog is Pet Animal,I Love My Dog. My Dog Name is Tipu. Tipu have four legs; it has two cute eyes. it has two ears, sharp teeth and a small tail on the back. It is said that a dog is a man's best friend because the dog is a faithful and Friendly animal. My Dog Tipu is Very Intelligent And Responsive Pet that Protect me From Dangers. Everyday I am Playing With my Cute Dog,he is my Friend. My Dog is eat Biscuit,Bones,dogs Food He also Drinks Water. My Dog Tipu is my best Friend Every Time. I love my Dog,You are the Best!!
author: Prachi Bhopi

title: Come Stay With Me
text: Tendai Turtle lives in the water. Tendai’s best friend is Bunny Busi. She lives in a tree. Granny Turtle has hurt her shell. “We have to go to help Granny,” says Mum. “Come stay with me,” calls Busi. Tendai stays with Bunny Busi in the tree. They play all day. They sleep all night. Mum and Dad come back with Granny. “How are you, Granny?” asks Tendai. “I am better now,” says Granny with a smile. “We fixed her shell,” answers Mum. Granny gives Tendai her favourite flute. Tendai plays the flute and everybody dances.
author: Nasrin Siege

title: The Great Tidy Up
text: ‘We are going to have so much fun while Gogo is having a nap,’ says big sister Khwezi. ‘Ooh yes!’ says little brother Mzamo. ‘What will we do?’ ‘We will clean the house for Papa and Mama while they are out.’ ‘That’s no fun,’ says Mzamo. ‘Uh uh, no. Not me. I don’t want to clean up!’ ‘But Papa and Mama will be so proud. Let me show you how much fun we will have!’ says Khwezi. ‘First we will put the toys away!’ ‘Now we will sweep the stoep!’ ‘Now we will wash the dishes!’ ‘Now we will wash the windows!’ ‘Now we will polish the floor!’ ‘Now we will wash the clothes!’ ‘Now we will hang the clothes up!’ “SURPRISE!” ‘I have been watching them the whole time and they have been little angels!’ says Gogo.
author: Corinne  Lamoral-Rosmarin

title: Dudu's Hat
text: “Hey, Dudu,” Dumisani says. “I bet you can’t throw your hat through that window.” Dudu looks up at the open window. It’s so high up the classroom wall, she can’t see what’s on the other side. “OK,” says Dudu. “I’ll count to three.” They take their hats off and stand ready. “One...” says Dudu slowly, “two”... “THREE!” But Dumisani’s hat gets close. It hits the windowsill and rebounds, turning three times in the air before coming to rest on the head of the stuffed rhino below. Dudu and Dumisani throw their hats towards the window. Dudu’s hat lands softly against the wall and slides down onto the shelf underneath. “Again!” she says. Dudu and Dumisani laugh so hard, Dudu has to hold her tummy. The friends fetch their hats, and Dumisani counts, “One, two, three!” Dumisani’s hat sails through the air, makes it past the windowsill, bumps against the frame and falls through the window. “YES!” he shouts. Dudu’s hat is on the shelf again. “Again” says Dumisani. “Do it again,” Dumisani says to Dudu. Dudu gets her hat, balls it up in her hand and squints at the window. “One, two, three,” says Dumisani, and Dudu throws. But her hat bounces off the windowsill and slides down the wall again. “Uh uh,” says Dudu. “Let’s go outside to the swings.” She fetches her hat and puts it firmly on her head. “Ah, please, Dudu?” says Dumisani. “Here, I’ll help you.” “Point your other hand at the window,” he says. “Now throw from your shoulder.” Dudu takes a deep breath and throws. He takes Dudu’s hat from her head, balls it up, and puts it in her hand. Her hat swoops up, opens like a gliding bird, flies through the window, and disappears. “Yes!” Dudu and Dumisani shout, lifting their arms in victory. “TEACHER!” Dudu shouts to Teacher Lethabo. “Our hats fell out the window!”
author: Sarah  McGregor

title: Why Birds Sing at Dawn
text: A long time ago, in the forest of Happy-Land, birds and trees could talk to each other. There was a bird family with three children: Blue, Pink and Yellow. They all lived on a big wise tree called Mamango. Mama Birdie’s voice was beautiful! She would wake up early to sing her song. But drought set in on the land. Rivers dried up and leaves fell off. Mamango thought long and hard. “Maybe we should get the magic worm that brings rain. But who can go?” “I will go. I am not afraid,” Mama Birdie said. Everyone missed Mama Birdie, and her song. Would she ever find her way back home? “What if we sing Mama’s song?” Yellow asked. “Mama said if we sing her song, she will find her way back.” “But I don’t know how to sing!” cried Pink. “Have you tried singing?” Mamango asked. “I have tried singing,” said Yellow. “I can teach you.” Early the next morning, Yellow sang Mama’s song: And rain started falling. “It’s a beautiful morning! We wake up and shine!” Eventually, all the birds joined Yellow in song. Mama Birdie found her way back to Happy-Land. And from then on, birds sang at dawn.
author: Zanele  Dlamini

title: I'm the Colour of Honey
text: My name is Amanda. I live with my Mummy, my Daddy and my dog Porsha. My Daddy says I’m the colour of honey. My Mummy says I look like a beautiful sunset. But I don’t look like either of them. Only Porsha is brown like me! When we go out some people stare at us, or ask us lots of questions. “Is that your Aunty?” asks the woman at the store. “No! It’s my Mummy!” “Is that your Teacher?” asks the man in the park. “No! It’s my Daddy!” “Why don’t you look like them?” “Because I’m the colour of honey. And I look like a beautiful sunset.” “But your Daddy is like a night sky,” says the woman at the store. “And your Mummy is as white as the blank pages in a book,” says the man in the park. “Why do you look so different?” The next day I wrap a towel on my head and swing it around just like Mummy does with her hair. “Is that your Aunty?” asks the woman at the store. “No, that’s my Mummy!” I run home and get some black paint. I smear it on my face. “Nice face painting!” says the man in the park. He points to Dad and asks, “Is that your teacher?” “No, he’s my Daddy!” My tears wash the paint away. “Why don’t I look like you, mummy and daddy?” “Amanda, show me that smile, that’s just like your Daddy’s.” I don’t feel like smiling. “Come on Amanda, look at your dimple. It’s so pretty, just like your Mummy’s!” Mummy and Daddy make me smile. And I make them smile too! “Look!” I say, “My teeth are white, just like yours.” “Yes, and your heart is red, just like ours.” How many colours are you?
author: Maïmouna Jallow

title: Teju's Shadow
text: “What’s that?” Teju hides. “It won’t find me here!” He runs. “Why are you following me?” Leave me ALONE! Go away. Go away. GO AWAY! “Teju! What are you doing?” “It won’t go away!” “Your shadow?” “It follows me everywhere! It’s like a super secret spy!” “Well, there’s one way to make a shadow disappear...” Later that night in Teju’s bedroom, the light goes off......and then on. And off......and on. Teju can’t sleep. Mum gives Teju a big hug. “Do you want to see something amazing?” “What’s wrong Teju?” “It only goes away in the dark, but I’m scared of the dark!” Mum and Teju make shadow puppets until he falls asleep. After school, Teju waits for Mum. “I’m bored.” Teju stands up, he jumps, he dances. His shadow does the same. “Cool!” When he goes to bed that night, Teju leaves his night light on. “Goodnight Shadow!” When he goes to bed that night, Teju leaves his night light on.
author: Sope Martins

title: Mama Antelope's House
text: Long ago, all the animals lived in a village. Mama Antelope had a big house. One day, Hare wanted to play a trick. He thought and thought and thought… He crept into Mama Ant elope’s house. He closed the door and made a lot of noise. Mama Antelope came home. “Who is in my house?” she cried. “Hyena, please help! Someone is in my house.” CLINK! PING! Knock, knock, knock! “Open the door!” howled Hyena. But the door did not open. CRASH! SNAP! BOOM! BASH! But the door did not open. Giraffe called Zebra. “Open the door!” yelled Zebra. Zebra called Elephant. He was big and strong. “Open the door!” commanded Elephant. But the door did not open. BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! Mama Antelope was sad. All the animals were sad. Who was in Mama Antelope’s house? The birds sang. The butterflies flapped. The bees buzzed.“Open the door!” they all cried. Baby Antelope came home. “Who is in our house?” “Please open the door,” she asked sweetly. The door opened. It was Hare! Hare was smiling. He loved tricks. Hurrah! Hurrah! Mama Antelope and Baby Antelope are happy. The animals are happy. Mama Antelope’s house is open at last.
author: Florenca  Marundu

title: The day I learnt to say goodbye
text: I came home running from the bus stop. It was 2:30 in the afternoon. I opened the gate, but it was too quiet. So I called out,"Bozo come on out sweetie." Suddenly a cold wave ran down my spine. I had just recalled that my best friend, Bozo was not around anymore. I slowly walked into the house and went to my room. I changed and laid down gazing at the fan. I started remembering everything. We had Bozo even before I was born. He was a german shepherd and such a beautiful one! He had jet black fur, with hazelnut-colored streaks around his mane. He was the first friend I ever made in my entire life (of thirteen years so far). After I was born I never needed a caretaker. If mom and Nani were busy and I started crying, it was Bozo who would come and rock my cradle. He was always near it just in case I started bursting tears. When I was three I had the joy of having a baby brother. That is when I and Bozo became friends. We would distribute duties to take care of him. At the age of five, I started getting chores to do, but nothing could beat the peeling of peas. Now Bozo just loved peas. So every time I sat down to peel peas in the verandah he would follow me, wagging his tail, and secretly I would throw him some peas to eat. Everyday when I came back from school Bozo would be the first one to greet me. He would wag his tail, bark in joy and tug on my tunic till I would pet him. Though there was one thing Bozo despised - baths!! If anyone would ask," Who is going to give Bozo a bath?" everyone would make excuses. Even Bozo would go away and when he would be called to bathe he would lift his leg up to show that he was peeing.One day I asked my mother if I could give him a bath. At first she refused but then in the end she said yes. So I took off his collar and took him to the bathroom, but the moment I put water on him he started splashing it all over the place! I eventually calmed him down and put soap on him (though he splashed that off too). After we were done my mom came in and she was horrified! She still forgave us because I was a kid and she knew Bozo. Although Bozo was a big dog I loved taking him for walks. I used to tell him about school and I still think he understood everything. As I grew older so did Bozo. He became weaker and lost his energy, but I still spent all the time I could with him. Playing with him, trying to cheer him up. soon he could hardly move. On a windy day, I was sitting with Bozo, his head in my lap, as he could not sleep. Once he slept off I went into the house to help with some chores. After two hours or so I went to wake Bozo up to feed him."Bozo sweetie, time to get up", I whispered to him but he didn't get up. I shook him a little but he still didn't move. I called my Nanu to check it out. He checked and looked up at my mother. I could see pain in his eyes but I didn't understand anything. Seeing the perplexed look on my face, my grandfather called me to the steps of the verandah. I asked him, "What happened to Bozo Nanu?" He replied, "Beta, you know you are just like your mother always wanting to know what is going on. Well, Bozo...he has gone somewhere, to the best place in the world."Where is that?" I asked intrigued. He replied pointing to the sky, "There, in the clouds, that's where he is. Of course, he will miss you but he also has to meet his mother Coco." "Coco?" I asked."Yes," he said, "Coco, the mother of the luckiest dog in the world..." As these words echoed in my brain, I sat up and thought about what nanu said. Truly Bozo was lucky to leave so peacefully but so was I, to get such a loyal pet and a true best friend.
author: Sarah  Kesar
illustrator: Selina Masego Morulane; Aditi Dilip; Jess  Jardim-Wedepohl; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Ruchi Mittal; Scarlet Reeves; Shailja Jain Chougule; Siddhi   Vartak; Yuvaka  Srestha

title: Mr Earthworm Wants a Bath - Early STEM
text: Mr Earthworm is very angry. He likes looking pretty, and is fed up of being covered in mud and never being able to have a proper bath. So he asks his wife, who is very handy with tools, to install a bathtub with running water. The bathtub is easy to make. First Mrs Earthworm finds an old flower pot lying in the kitchen garden. She patches up the few holes and some gaps. And it’s done! The installation of running water at their home was quite another thing. The first attempt was with straws connected to the surface. But the flow was too weak and during heavy rains the mud rose obstructing the mouth of the pipes. She improved the device by connecting a garden hose directly onto a drainpipe. However, the flow was not quite satisfactory. Mrs Earthworm thought hard. Then she found another bowl to collect the water. She made a knot to act as a tap. Now the water supply was perfect. The next problem was that this water was not suitable for Mr Earthworm. It had too much residue, is not clear enough, and it does not smell good. Mrs Earthworm had listened carefully in Science class, and so she knew how to make a filter using sand, seeds, and stones. Mrs Earthworm was really proud of her work. But when she presented it to Mr Earthworm, there was a small problem. There was something else that dampened Mr Earthworm's craving for a bath - the temperature. The water is too cold! Mrs Earthworm got back to work and added a handmade water heater, all they needed to do was light the fire to warm the water in the pipe. Now it’s perfect! Mr Earthworm can finally relax in the bath that he so wanted so much. - THE END - This book has been modified from "Everyone has a right to a bath" by C yrille Largillier. This story explains the problem solving process an engineer often goes through when designing a solution. In this story, Mr Earthworm likes to look pretty and Mrs Earthworm works on finding him a solution, this modification of the original story aims to shed light on typical gender stereotypes. author: Danielle Bruckert
illustrator: Cyrille Largillier; Danielle Bruckert; Ruchi Shah; Students of  Himalayan Public School

title: Janice and the bear
text: One fine, sunny day, Mama Bear was going to get some honey from the Bees. When she reached she met Mrs Bee."Good Morning Mrs Bee." said Mama Bear."Good Morning Mama Bear." replied Mrs Bee,"Its your lucky day today as today we just made some fresh honey." "Great!", said Mama Bear,"Perfect for my honey and oatmeal cookies." Mama bear helped Mrs Bee to take the hive down and in turn, Mrs Bee gave her a huge pot full of honey. Mama Bear went home delighted that she could make some cookies for her family. Mama Bear reached home, wore her apron, went into the kitchen and started making cookies. Soon, the kitchen was filled with the aroma of cookies baking. After a lot of time and effort Mama Bear's cookies were finally ready and how delicious they looked and smelt. At the same time a girl named Janice was passing by. She smelt the cookies and started following the smell. After following the smll for about half an hour she realized that she had come deep into the forest and could not find her way out. She was tired and scared and it was getting dark so she decided to stay therefor the night. The next morning Mama Bear went out for a walk and saw Janice sleeping on the ground. She pitied the girl and decided to take her home. She picked Janice up, took her home and put her in bed with her children. When Janice woke up she was shocked to see herself in a bed next to small bears. She was so scared she screamed,"Aaahhhhh!!" "Shush!", she heard a voice. She went into the kitchen and saw Mama Bear."Come dear, have some breakfast." said Mama Bear. Janice sat down at the table. She saw a bowl of hot porridge and ate it. She then asked,"Who are you? How did you find me?" Mama Bear narrated everything to her. After Mama Bear told Janice everything she asked Janice,"How come you are here?" So JAnice told her all about the scent of the cookies and Mama Bear had a hearty laugh. Then she said,"How about I take you back home? It won't take long." This delighted Janice. Her eyes lit up, she smiled the widest smile she could. She hugged Mama Bear and said,"Thank you so much!!" So Mama Bear packed some food, water and cookies (especially for Janice). They started off and after a long walk they rested and took a small nap. As they were sleeping, Janice felt a drop of water on her cheek. She woke up and realized that it was raining. She woke Mama Bear up and told her that soon that part of the forest would be flooded and that they had to get out fast. But the town was still an hour long walk and Mama Bear had to fulfill her promise. So she said,"Janice climb in my shoulders." Janice did as she was told and Mama Bear walked through the flood. Mama Bear fulfilled her promise and made sure that Janice reached home. The moment Janice reached she raced to meet her mother. She was delighted to see her daughter. She thanked Mama Bear and took Janice in the house. Janice came running out and hugged Mama Bear once again and gave her some cake. "Thank you" she whispered in her ear and ran back in. As Janice and Mama Bear grew old, they could not visit each other often but never forgot each other and lived happily ever after.
author: Sarah  Kesar
illustrator: Delwyn Remedios; Mitrarun Halder; Nilomee Jesrani; Rijuta Ghate; Sunaina  Coelho; Suvidha Mistry

title: Misha Goes To Manipur
text: Misha is excited to go to manipur. First she read a book, slept for 2 hours then her mother woke her up. After some time she ate pav bhaji. When she reached manipur, she met her friends, she was very happy. When it rains she likes to play in the rain. Now she is at indra gandhi international airport. So sad misha will miss all her friends.

title: Vegetables party.
text: Once the vegetables planned a party. So Brinjal and Beetroot were hearty. Spinach and Banana came running. But Radish woke up late. Dressed in red, Tomato forgot the date. While Onion grew its hair tall, Garlic welcomed all. Cucumber offered flowers, green and Pumpkin ate the leaves, unseen. Bitter Gourd was feeling hot. So Chilli said "Thank you" to the lot.
author: Aarti Nyayadhish
illustrator: Diana James; Narayan Prasad  Bohaju; Niloufer Wadia; Padmanabh

title: Things, my friends and I do together.
text: My friends and I love playing volleyball. Girls run a race. Anil kicks the football. Sonali eats but she spills. Sangeeta and her friends dance. Anita cried while the bird flew away. Rajnish ate after sitting down. Amit climbed while grandmother watched. Sangeeta writes and Moti jumps. Vishalti and Babita are reading. The others are standing. Ram was happy to see the postcard. Guess, what the others are doing?
