She took the mirror off the wall and peered at the back. It was just wood. No people hiding there. Manasa walked around the mirror and peeked. Maybe it wouldn’t see her. But no. There was Mirror Manasa, looking sneaky. ﻿ Manasa stomped towards Mirror Manasa and lifted her leg high. ﻿ “HAI YA!” ﻿ Mirror Manasa did the same thing. She didn’t look scared at all. ﻿ “I don’t like them,” Titus whined. Manasa swung a cricket bat. It slipped from her hand and flew KRACK into Mirror Manasa’s face. CLINK! CLANK! CRASH! Bits of mirror flew everywhere, glass flashing. Titus began to cry. “Manasa!” Amma came running. “Don’t move! Don’t touch the glass. It’s dangerous!” She picked Manasa up, and then Titus. She carried them away from the broken mirror. Then Amma carefully swept the glass up. “I was so angry,” Manasa told Amma in bed that night. “I don’t understand where Mirror Manasa came from!” Amma drew a mirror. “See, it’s just glass. The shiny layer at the back? It turns light back to you. BOUNCE! ” “You stand in front and the mirror will BOUNCE you back as a picture. ” Manasa looked at the picture. Manasa in, Manasa out. “Like a ball!” Manasa said. “BOUNCE!” “Yes,” Amma nodded. “You show the mirror your face and the mirror bounces it back.” “But no sound,” Manasa said. “Mirror Manasa didn’t speak.” “No sound,” Amma said. “The shiny bit only bounces light, not sound or taste or smell.” Shiny Layer Light Manasa Mirror Manasa looked at the picture. Manasa in, Manasa out. “Like a ball!” Manasa said. “BOUNCE!” “Yes,” Amma nodded. “You show the mirror your face and the mirror bounces it back.” “But no sound,” Manasa said. “Mirror Manasa didn’t speak.” “No sound,” Amma said. “The shiny bit only bounces light, not sound or taste or smell.” “So Mirror Manasa won’t be there in the dark?” Manasa asked. “The mirror needs light to see, same as you,” Amma yawned. “Aha!” Manasa was pleased. “That’s what Mirror Manasa is. Light bouncing.” “Mmmm,” Amma said and fell asleep.
author: Shalini  Srinivasan

title: Home
text: “Tip-top drip-drop,” I sing with the rain, jumping over puddles on my way home from school. The crinkly metal sheets covering the houses in our village sing along: “Tip-tip-drop drip-drip-top.” I love the rain! But sometimes I completely disapprove of it. It’s not as bad as beetroot, but I get annoyed when the sky can’t decide if it’s happy or sad. “Again?” I complain to the clouds. Again, the clouds send down a neverending river of droplets. Dada says our family has lived in this village, Feizung, since the grandparents of the great-grandparents of the great-great-grandparents of our great-great-great-grandparents! That is more than three hundred years. We make scarves and shawls, each one special. But I love most the shawls that Dada makes. They are so big and soft — I sleep with one of his shawls curled under my arms. Amma weaves words instead of threads. She is the most theatrical storyteller in the whole village — unlike Abbu, who tells stories at the pace of an old tortoise. Our village is surrounded by rice fields — lush, green and vast — with homes made of bamboo scattered like stars in the sky. Our country is big, but we are not allowed everywhere. Amma says we can only go to places where people look like us. Luckily, the village has everything I need—my family, my friends, and fields to play in. The only thing we lack is a doctor. Which is why, when I begin sneezing more times than a train choo-choos, Amma takes me to a doctor in the village two hours away. As we prepare to leave the clinic, I hear the masjid’s loudspeaker. But instead of singing, the imam is shouting. “Run west. Everyone, run west. Run with what you have in hand. Don’t go home. There is no time. Armed men are coming towards us and burning everything they pass. We are afraid they may kill anyone who crosses their path. Run west. Run!” The imam sounds terrified. All I have in my hand is Amma’s hand and all I can do is to hold it tight. Everyone else is holding something or carrying someone. And so, we run. We run west, with hundreds of other people. Just like many droplets create a river, we form a river flowing west. Each droplet is a person walking, running, stumbling. This neverending river crosses rice fields, orchards, forests and hills. New droplets join. Many are lost along the way. But the droplets I want most — Abbu, Dada, Mami, the rest of our family — never join the river. The people-river crosses what Amma says is a border. She says we are in a new country now. But everything looks the same. Do rivers know they have crossed borders? Do they even know what borders are? We are in an open, and barren field. On one horizon, rice fields fade into where our home was. On the other horizon, a town fades into the ocean. The empty field slowly fills up with tents and huts. Food is not grown here. People give it to us. Water does not come from wells. It arrives in trucks. Amma says we are safe here. But what about Abbu, Dada and Mami? Are they safe? I look and look all around me. Safety seems to have become an open field inside an invisible bubble. Here, we are all living in the hope of going home, some day. Is it even possible to feel safe without a home? Safe, without my family and friends? I often wonder, where is home? Is it here? Or is it where my family is? Can home be in two places? A part of my heart will always be in Feizung. But is it still home if we never go back to it? School starts. Two years pass. Abbu, Dada, Mami and everyone I love never come. Amma and I are still here. We are told we cannot leave this camp. But everyone also keeps saying we can’t stay forever. On one side there is still the road to Feizung. On the other, the ocean. Sometimes we think of escaping. But today, I have school. “Hasina, did you cover the books in plastic?” Amma shouts as I hurry off to school in the rain. “Yes, Amma, I did,” I yell back, trying to be louder than the crinkly plastic sheets that sing, “Tip-tip-drop drip-drip-top.”
author: Fausto Aarya De Santis

title: Amma! Amma!
text: "I need nails and some rope. And flowers,"says Amma. So Appa takes Ashok and Baby to the market. "Amma!" "No, Baby! That's not Amma. Amma has long, black hair,"says Appa. "Amma!" " No, Baby! Amma does not have a beard." "Amma!" " No, Baby. Amma is not old. Amma is young," says Appa. T h ey go home with the nails, rope and flowers. T ak -tak-taphaak! Look! Amma has made a cart for Baby! Baby thought of Amma when she saw the girl, the man with a beard and the old lady at the market. I know why Baby thought she saw Amma at the market. Do you? Clever Baby!
author: Asha Nehemiah

title: What Shall I Wear Today?
text: Something is wrong with the buttons on this shirt. And these pants are so tight that they're starting to hurt. This skirt is much too long for me. And this top is too tight! Do you agree? My pants are too old. They need to be stitched. And these golden stars are making me itch. I think I'll try on these trousers instead. But they pull and tug and are hard to put on. What will I do? All my options are gone! How about this dress? No, I think it's too bright. What about my brother's stripy t-shirt? That would be a funny sight! Or how about my daddy 's jacket? No, I think they would be much too long. I 'll try on my mother 's scarf instead. Oh no, I've put it on all wrong! I can't reach anything else on the washing line. So I'll have to find something else of mine. These clothes seem to say, "We don’t want to agree" But an idea is beginning to come to me. I'll mix and match to create my own style......so that finally I can relax and smile!
author: Right To Play

title: Look Within The Universe!
text: The author, Abhay Murthy, creates a fascinating parallel universe with adventure, intrigue and science! Join Ampory, Joseph and Gudugu as they team up to problem solve for the Space Government!! About the author: Abhay Murthy is a cat cuddling, India loving, keyboard playing eight year old with a wild imagination. There was a boy called Ampory. It was the night before his 9 th birthday. When he was asleep, he dreamt about a black hole. It seemed that everything that he wanted for his birthday, was floating in a swirling black hole! He woke up with a startle. Then, he saw it. He saw everything that was in the black hole was right there, in his room! He had read about black holes in his science books but had not heard of one that gives gifts! He asked his parents if they gave him the presents. “No”, they said. Then he went over to his friend’s house to ask for help. “Do you want to help me find out who gave me the presents?” he asked Joseph. Joseph said, “Of course! But we will need to stick with this and not give up”. Ampory agreed. The boys discussed where to start first. They finally thought they should make a spaceship to fly to space to see which black hole gave the gifts. They wanted to make a spaceship that would let them travel without anyone noticing or knowing. Ampory and Joseph built a spaceship with oxygen tanks that would not run out of air. Then, the first planet they went to was Mercury. They checked all around there. They saw a few pieces of paper lying around that they picked up. The last piece said something very important. It said, “ If Ampory comes to find who this is, you will find something helpful at the last planet ”. Ampory knew what the last planet was! He said, “We should go to Neptune!” Joseph said, “Okay, let’s head back to the spaceship”. ﻿ They started their journey to Neptune. On the way, they made really thick spacesuits so they would not feel cold there. They saw someone on Neptune and went up to him and asked him if he knew of a black hole that gave out gifts. He said he did! He told them, “My name is Gudugu. Look right next to Saturn. It sucks up lots of presents from galaxies all around. The strange thing is, it sucks in only gifts! You need to destroy it so the presents go back to the other galaxies. That is your answer. You need to find the black hole, somehow destroy it and send the gifts back to those other universes”. Then Joseph asked, “Can you come with us”? Gudugu said, “Okay, I will come with you”. They all went to Saturn and saw the black hole. They saw gifts swirling and moving all around. They saw a huge one in the center. They thought, “It seems like the only way we can return the presents to all the galaxies is to take that big present from the middle and that should destroy it”. They tried to touch the big gift in the middle and then it just pushed them back. Then they didn’t know what to do.... Gudugu said, “We need to think of what the black hole does not like. Let’s put some trash in the black hole and see if the big present will nudge out of it’s big boundary”. They went back to the spaceship and brought back trash and dumped it into the black hole. The big present broke loose from the middle. They waited for a few seconds and then worked together to destroy it. Once they destroyed it, the black hole exploded. After the explosion, Gudugu gave them a letter. It said.. Dear Ampory and Joseph, We want you to come and help us once a week to solve these little problems in space. If you want, you can join this little group of space government! We are a group that comes together and solves problems for all these universes and galaxies and different planets. You just have to remember to look within our entire universe! -Gudugu, Space Government. Ampory & Joseph told Gudugu that they will help out on Saturday nights. They wrote “okay” on the paper and gave it to back to Gudugu. The black hole had become normal. Ampory and Joseph thanked Gudugu and went back home. At home, they noticed that all of Ampory’s presents had disappeared. He was happy the gifts had returned to the other planets! He also saw new gifts that were from his parents. He was very happy and thrilled about his journey that nobody had noticed. He was also happy that he was a part of the space government and could look within space and help out other universes every week! T O I N F I N I T Y A N D B E Y O N D......
author: Abhay Murthy
illustrator: Alicia Souza; Chaaya Prabhat; Greystroke; Isha  Mangalmurti; Ishita Sharma; Kavita Singh Kale; Lauren   Nel; Ouk  Ratha; Satya  Krishna Prakash; Somesh Kumar; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya; Vidyun Sabhaney

title: Sharanya Speaks to Robots
text: Hello, everyone! Please welcome our new student, Robu. Sharanya wants to be friends with Robu. Hello! But he doesn’t seem to understand her. Hi Helloooo oooooooo oooooooo oooooooo oooooooo! Oyeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee Psst! Why won’t you talk to me! Then, all of a sudden, Sharanya has an idea. POP Sharanya codes a message for Robu. Robu’s brain reads the code and he finally replies. HELLO How to Code a Robot The brain of a robot is a computer. To communicate with computers and give them tasks to do, we need to know how to speak their language. The code-based language that computers understand is called a programming language. And the person who writes code to communicate with machines is called a programmer. There are many programming languages to help us talk to computers. Some of them are C, C++ and Java. Would you like to talk to computers too?
author: Tanvi Bhat

title: Lost in the Internet
text: Kunal loved the Internet. He was always asking Mummy for her phone so he could watch videos. “Don’t watch for too long or you’ll get pulled in!” Mummy warned him. First, Kunal watched a video of cartoon ninjas. Next, he watched one of a volcano spewing lava. Then, he watched one of a baby playing with a dog. With each video, Kunal’s face came closer and closer to the screen. Suddenly— SCHWOOOOOP! — Kunal was sucked into the Internet. First, Kunal watched a video of cartoon ninjas. Next, he watched one of a volcano spewing lava. Then, he watched one of a baby playing with a dog. With each video, Kunal’s face came closer and closer to the screen. Suddenly— SCHWOOOOOP! — Kunal was sucked into the Internet. “Where am I?” Kunal had landed on a platform in a strange train station. All around him, trains whooshed in and out through tunnels. A sign popped up above his head. It read “Core Router”. Core Router “How did I get here?” Kunal wondered. “And how will I get out?” Then Kunal saw a woman on the platform. She looked very busy directing the trains. “Excuse me, aunty. Where are all these trains going?” Kunal asked her. “I’m Transmission Control Protocol,” she said, busily, “But you can call me TCP. These trains are taking data to different parts of the Internet.” Kunal watched TCP as her hands swiftly moved things around on a large screen. “Wow,” Kunal said. “What are you doing, TCP Aunty?” “I’m routing data through the Internet, of course,” replied TCP. “Everything has to go fast, fast, fast!” The trains whooshed away, carrying data in every direction. “Are all the phones and computers on the Internet connected?” asked Kunal, an idea forming in his mind. “Yes,” said TCP Aunty, “All the devices on the Internet are connected. These tunnels are actually wires, cables, radio waves and satellites in space.” “TCP Aunty, if all the devices on the Internet are connected, can you help me get back home?” “Of course!” TCP said. She looked Kunal up and down. “We’ll send you by packet switching. First, we’ll break you into a few thousand pieces. Then we’ll send all your bits by different paths and put you back together later.” “TCP Aunty, if all the devices on the Internet are connected, can you help me get back home?” “Of course!” TCP said. She looked Kunal up and down. “We’ll send you by packet switching. First, we’ll break you into a few thousand pieces. Then we’ll send all your bits by different paths and put you back together later.” “No!” Kunal said, hurriedly. “Is… Isn’t there another way?” “Hmmm,” TCP frowned. “Sending you all together by circuit switching is a lot less efficient. But if you insist. Now let’s ask your mother for your address.” “But I know my address,” Kunal said, confused. “Not your home address,” replied TCP. “Your Internet address!” She opened up a chat window in the air and quickly explained everything to Kunal’s mother. “We host a website on my computer—KunalBabyPictures.com. Can you find that?” said Mummy. “We can find your Mummy’s computer using the Internet Protocol or IP,” TCP said. “Every computer and website on the Internet has a unique number called an IP address.” TCP opened a big book with ‘DNS’ written on the cover. “This book contains the IP address of every website on the Internet,” she told Kunal. She looked through it carefully until— “Found it!” “Here,” said TCP. “You’ll need to be encrypted so that nobody else can grab you on the way.” TCP handed Kunal a hat and silly glasses with a nose and moustache attached. “You’re very sensitive data indeed!” she said. “Goodbye, TCP Aunty!” Kunal replied, cheerfully. Kunal was moving fast, very fast. His arms and legs tingled. And then—POP! He was back home. “My dear!” Mummy said. “It’s good to have you back. Next time, learn about the Internet by reading about it, not getting lost inside it.” Kunal loved the Internet, but he loved being home even more. What is the Internet? The Internet is the name for all the different computers, phones and tablets that are connected to each other. It is a system that is spread across the entire world. It lets us transfer data from one computer to another through copper wires, fibre-optic cables, radio transmissions and satellites in space. Every device that is connected to the Internet has a unique number called an IP address. How Does Data Travel? Many kinds of data are sent through the Internet, such as emails, web pages, videos, chats and pictures. The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is a set of rules and procedures used by computers to transfer data by first breaking it into chunks called packets. Then the packets are put back together again (in the right order!) when they reach their destination. This method of data transfer is called packet switching. In circuit switching, the entire data is sent through a single path. This is a less efficient method than packet switching. How Does Data Travel? Then the packets are put back together again (in the right order!) when they reach their destination. This method of data transfer is called packet switching. In circuit switching, the entire data is sent through a single path. This is a less efficient method than packet switching.
author: Kris Stokes; Madhurima Chakraborty

title: RIA Sorts It Out
text: Every winter break, Abel posts a card to his Ammachi. And it usually reaches her on New Year’s Day. Today, Amma asks Abel to write the address on the card himself. He has learnt to write numbers and the alphabet at school. Abel writes the address nervously. Amma sticks a stamp on the envelope. Abel runs to the post box and drops it in. It’s Christmas Eve. Amma is cooking payasam, Abel’s favourite sweet dish. But Abel is stomping his feet angrily. “Abel! What happened?” asks Amma. “The postmaster won’t understand my handwriting. Ammachi will never get my card,” he wails. So Amma takes Abel to meet Postmaster Wilson. “Wilson Uncle!” Abel cries, “What if Ammachi doesn’t get my card, because of my handwriting?” “Don’t worry,” Postmaster Wilson says. “All the letters are sorted by our robot RIA.” RIA reads the address, identifies the postal code and sorts each postal code into the correct pile. But Abel is still worried. “Uncle, please see if RIA has sorted my card correctly.” Postmaster Wilson looks for the letter and finds it in the right box. Amma looks at the card. Abel’s 7 looks like a 1. “Then how did it land in the right box?” Abel is surprised. “RIA sorted your card correctly because it learned by looking at the handwriting of millions of people,” says Postmaster Wilson. “That is why it could understand your 7 even though it looked like a 1.” “RIA is so smart!” says Abel. “It’s because RIA keeps learning from numerous examples every day. This is called Machine Learning,” the Postmaster says. “So will Ammachi get her card?” “Don’t worry, Abel. She will get her card by New Year’s Eve,” Postmaster Wilson replies. Postmaster Wilson is right! Ammachi gets the card on New Year’s Day. When she calls Abel, he tells her all about their adventures with the amazing robot at the post office. What is Machine Learning? When we are born, there are very few things we know how to do. As we grow up, we learn new things. Like us, computers can learn through experience, and learn to do a task without being told how to do it. For example, if we want a computer to tell the difference between a cow and a cat, it needs to be shown thousands of pictures of cats and cows. The computer will study the pictures and soon work out for itself that cats are small and cows are large, or that cats have shorter noses than cows. The more pictures of cows and cats a computer studies, the fewer mistakes it makes telling them apart. This book is a work of fiction. Though the technology depicted in the book exists, the characters, situations, and events are entirely made up.
author: Sonal Sher

title: Delicious Food
text: Home made cooked food is always delicious. Rice, curry, vegetable (Subji)... Look so yummy! Hot hot wheat roti increases my hunger. Along with roti and rice, fruits are also important. Such a colourful look and sweet-sour taste! Green, leafy vegetables give us iron and fibre. Eat those plenty of. Milk is a complete food. We always try to add milk or milk products in our food, such as curd, buttermilk, paneer. Wait, wait. Food journey is incomplete without sweets. Right? Have a look at these. I know, all of us love ice-cream. Sweet and cool.... Some people celebrate their birthdays by cutting cakes. But try to avoid eating junk food. It does not give us strength and nutrition. Always respect the person who grows food for us (Farmer), who cooks food for us (parents), and the food itself.
author: Asawari Doshi

title: CHINNU NEGGINDI
text: I ee aadhivaram podduna karate pariksha undi time emo ayyipotundi. Tanaki nidra emo pattatledu. "em avutundo repu? Ela jarugutundi? Tana balam saripotunda?" chinnu sannaga, poduggga unde pilla. Schoolulo konni nelala kritame cherindi. Kottaga cherindiga, ekkuvamandi snehitulu leremo. Andukani khali samayallo enni veelu aithe anni cheseyalani aathram. Valla amma eppudu chepparu, "annitikanna balanga undali manam." ani. Andukani okaroju velli evarito cheppakunda karatelo cheripoyiindi. 'intha okkapalachaga unnavu, nuvvem pagala kodatavu evi ayina?' ' abbayula atalu emiti, vinta kakapote!' 'ayina idi enduku upayogapadutundi chaduvu meeda dhyasa pettaka!' chinnuki vatannitilo amma cheppina 'balanga marali' okkati nacchindi. Hobby gane cherina akkada andarito gattiga potipadalsi vacchi, tanu nijamga varandariki kanna sariramlo sattuva, ekagrata pettadamlo enta balahinamga undo ardham chesukundi. Chinnu enno sarlu oorikega cheranu vadileddam anukunna sare, valla teacherugaru oppukoledu. Ammalage, 'nuvvu balamga mari teeralsinde!' annaru. Roju chetulu, kallu bobbalekkevaraku sikshanicchi kani intiki vellanichevaru kadu. Ala konnallu roju kashtapaddaka karate pariksha deggarapadindi. Chinnuki aandolana pattukundi. Tanakemo inka baaga ravali, ravatledu anipistundi. Valla teacher emo "nuvvela teeralsinde, chekkaga paalu, pandulu, kuralu, roju tinte chalu, edi ayina gelichestavu" antaru. Roju ayithe ade dinacharya. Breadlu, chapatilu pandula rasam, kuramukkalu tintondi. Ade paniga gunjilu, pottaki, bujala exerciselu cheyyistunnaru. Ade alochanalato chinnu sagam sagam nidrapoyindi aa ratri. Marunadu pariksha samayaniki modalayyindi. Chinnu poddunne lechi ika edi ayithe adi avutundi, akkada valla andarikanna takkuva balamtho unte aa stage meedane padipovali. Kaani parikshaki vellakunda maanakudadu ani nischayinchukundi. Ventane pandula rasam, rendintala tiffin chesi balamga feel ayyindi. Okkakarini varusaga stage paiki pilichi parikshistunnaru. Chinnu vantu raane vacchindi. Lopala ela chestanu anukuntune stage paiki vellindi. Oka roundu lo pratyardi nundi tappinchukovatamu aithe, maro roundu lo edutivallani mattikaripinchadam. Balamga maranu ani nirupinchukotaniki idokkate chancuani unna balam anta upayoginchi e roundu ni kuda daatindi. Ika aakaruga, chetto konni rallani pagala kottali. Appatike teevramga alasipoyunna chinnu, 'ika na valla kaadu' anukundi. Okasari kottindi. Rendosari kottindi. Chetulu bobbalekke kanuvula deggara raktam ravadam modalu ayyindi. Teacher garu deggarakocchi, "gelisthe balamunnattu kadu chinnu, badalo unnappudu ninnu nuvvu enta munduki tosukogalagataniki prayatnistavo adi balam. Noppi, alasata anta kuda nee manassulo untundi." ani dhairyam chepparu. Chinnuki ika pallu bigapatti ekagrata upayoginchi marokkasari prayatninchindi. Ee sari pagilayi. Gelavatam kanna chinnuki tana sareeramulo prati baganni anubhuti chendindi. Ikapi balaheenata ante bayata chuttu andaru ani matalu vinadam, sareeram cheppe sakulu vinatam matramenani chesukuni intiki aanandamga cuppu pattukuni bayaluderindi.
author: anirudh prakhya

title: CHINNU WON!
text: Translator: anirudh prakhya chiinu has karate exam this sunday morning. Clock is ticking. She is unable to sleep. "what will happen tomorrow? How will exam happen? Will her strength be enough?" chinnu is thin, tall girl. She joined school few months ago. New joinee might not have many friends. So in free time wants to do as much as she can. Her mother always told her, "we should be stronger than everything." so one day she went and joined karate without telling anyone. 'you are so weak, what will you break?' 'boys games are weird!' 'anyway what use is this why not study instead' of all these chinnu only liked her mother's saying "be stronger". Even though she joined for a hobby, she had to compete and learn she is physically weak and lacks concentration than others. Chinnu wanted to quit many times but her teacher did not agree. You have to 'be strong like your mother' teacher said. Daily teacher trained her until her hands swell and then left for home. After training hard for many days karate exam approached. Chinnu started becoming anxious. She wanted to train further but is unable to. However teacher said "you have to go to exam, drink milk, eat fruits, vegetables daily, you will surely win." follow same routine daily, eat bread, chapati, drink fruit juice, eat salad. In the same way do sit ups and shoulder exercises. With these thoughts chinnu stay half awake that night. Next day exam started on time. Chinnu woke up in morning and decided to attend exam and faint on stage if needed. Immediately after drinking fruit juice, and eating double breakfast she felt stronger. One by one everybody was called to stage and examined. Chiinu's turn also came. She went on stage worried about her performance. One round was about slipping away from others while another round was about defeating others. To prove strength this was the only way and so she participated in next round also. Final round was to break stones with hands. Chinnu was tired and wanted to quit. She hit once. She hit twice. Her hands swell and bleeding started near her eyes. Teacher came near her and said, "winning is not proof of strength, convincing yourself to move ahead in pain is strength. Pain, tiredness is all in your heart." chinnu kept her teeth together and with concentration tried once again. Without bothered about result, chinnu felt every part of her body. After this weakness is listening to everybody, but chinnu won the cup and went home by only listening to her body.
author: anirudh prakhya
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Bianca de Jong; Hanrie  Coetzee; Jemma Jose; Manavee Chadrasena; Ntembiso  Velemane; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Stephen Wallace; Sunaina  Coelho; Swarga Bhattacharya; Tanvee Nabar; Thulisizwe  Mamba

title: How Bittu Bottu Got Better
text: Andy Prakash was only eight years old, but he studied in Class 10. He had more brains than the whole school. More brains than the students, more brains than the teachers and even more brains than the principal! The walking, talking proof of his super-intelligence was Bittu Bottu, a robot he had built all by himself. Bittu Bottu could answer any question. “Bittu Bottu, how tall is Mount Everest?” “About 8,848 metres above sea level,” Bittu Bottu replied. “Bittu Bottu, why did the chicken cross the road?” Well, almost any question. Bittu Bottu did Andy’s homework. Bittu Bottu did Andy’s housework. “ Andy! Clean your room yourself!” Bittu Bottu did Andy’s lab work. “Who bought all this? Diodes, resistors, capacitors and transistors... And look at the electricity bill! ANDY! ” One day, Andy sent Bittu Bottu to school in his place. “Andy Prakash!” “Present, teacher.” The class teacher kept Bittu Bottu back at school and sent Andy’s parents an angry text message. “ANDY!” “Ma, I want Bittu Bottu back. I miss him! Please write the teacher a letter,” Andy told Amma. “That robot spoils you. I won’t write it.” “Pa, please write a letter to my teacher!” “What, and get big electricity bills in return? No, of course not.” Andy climbed into school that night. That was when he found… a diode an IC a transistor Andy followed the trail of Bittu Bottu’s parts to the computer lab. “Bittu Bottu is falling apart! I must have overworked him,” he thought. “Where are you, my poor BB? Are you in the computer lab? I have your parts, BB!” Andy found the lab locked. CRUCK CRUCK Someone was coming! Andy hid behind a pillar as Security Anna walked past the computer lab. What could he do now? How would he give the parts to Bittu Bottu? “Hey, Bittu Bottu,” Andy whispered. Bittu Bottu was too weak to walk or talk. Andy threw the diode, IC and transistor into a bag and pushed it through the window. Bittu Bottu fixed himself with the components. He crawled, little by little, to a corner. “What are you doing, Bittu Bottu? Are you okay?” asked Andy. “I am charging my battery, Andooo...” “Ah, good boy! But don’t call me Andooo!” “Okay, Andooo...” The next morning, Andy gave the teacher a letter from his mother. Respected Class Teacher, My son, Andy Prakash, studying in your class, has promised to do all his work without help from his robot. Kindly do the needful and please return the robot to him. Thanking you, Yours respectfully, Andy’s mother P.S. This letter was not written by another robot or by Andy, but by me. Bittu Bottu was allowed to go home with Andy that day. Now Andy did the housework himself. He did his lab work himself. Andy even did his homework himself... But not always. Bittu Bottu is made of four basic parts. 1. Power Supply Robots need electricity to do work. Bittu Bottu has a rechargeable battery inside and solar powered cells outside. Diodes, resistors, transistors and capacitors control the power as needed. 2. Actuators Actuators are motors that use power to help the robot move. Big motors help Bittu Bottu move from place to place. Little motors move his head and arms. 3. Sensors Sensors allow a robot to see and hear. Bittu Bottu’s sensors are cameras and microphones that work as his eyes and ears. 4. Controller The controller is the brain of a robot. It understands the information from the sensors and tells the actuators what to do. It can be programmed to follow human commands. A controller is usually made of integrated circuits (ICs).
author: Ashok Rajagopalan

title: When I Grow Up
text: When I grow up, I will build many things. Big and small things. Wild and amazing things. I will use science to build them all. First, I will build a bridge. After that, I will build a very tall tower. And then, I will build the longest road in the world. It will start at my room and go right up to the moon! When I build these structures, I will be a civil engineer. I will build engines too. Some engines will be in rockets and some will be in planes. The plane will take us from country to country and the rocket will fly us all the way to Mars. My Anaideo* will come with me on all my trips! When I build flying engines, I will be an aerospace engineer. *Anaideo means grandmother in Assamese. I will build a vehicle that travels under the sea. It will be made of steel and aluminium, and it will be very fast. We will swim with the fishes, sharks and whales. Anaideo will say, “Slow down, Papori!” But secretly, she will love it too. When I build my submarine, I will be a marine engineer. But I won’t stop at that. I will produce electricity from small particles. One tiny particle will light up our whole village. Anaideo will be so happy that she will throw a big feast! When I make power like that, I will be a nuclear engineer. I’m not done yet! Next, I will build a robot. Her name shall be Gogo. Gogo and I will have many adventures. We will paint the walls and do the dishes. We will catch Anaideo many, many fishes! When I build my robot, I shall be a robotics engineer. Gogo and I will build a firewall. It will guard computers and the Internet from bad guys trying to steal other people’s secrets. I will be like a superhero! Anaideo will be so proud. When I protect the Internet, I will be a cybersecurity engineer. I will build a machine to clean the sea. And another to clean the air. The animals will be healthy and people will breathe easy. I will save the earth with my machines! When I make machines to clean the planet, I will be an environmental engineer. I will build a new ear for Pempem (she lost it in a fight... grrrr). Then I will build a new set of teeth for Anaideo. Finally, I will build wings for me! When I build artificial body parts, I will be a biomedical engineer. And I will soar over the world looking for more things to build. Engineers Build Our World Engineers make, plan and design the world around us. They build computers, machines, structures and materials that make our lives easier. Who built the television in your home? The cars and buses on the streets? The X-ray machines in the hospitals? They were all planned and built by engineers.
author: Priyadarshini Gogoi

title: ITCH! GOKU! ITCHING, GOKU!
text: I do not know!" shouted amma's daddy after lying on the bed, manu started again. Itch! Goku! Itchy itch! Durada goku! Manu tries too much gokakudadu! Gokakudadu plays vaikunthapali. So many stories can be trampled. Forgot it! Slowly, the blisters disappear. Manu counts. 10,9 and 8,7,6 and 5,4,3,2 plus 1. One day manu shirts up all the itchy scratches disappear! Manu can play the thumb again. Flies, counts. 1,2 and 3. 4,5 and 6. 7,8,9 and 10.

title: HOUSES OF ANIMALS
text: Translator: anirudh prakhya animals also live around us birds build their houses high. That's all for the bees too. Spiders roam their homes. Tiny termites build taller houses snails and tortoises grow homes on their backs the fish live in the water. While frogs live in the water, even on the ground. Rabbits and rats roost under the ground. Monkeys and chimpanzees turn their trees into houses. Bears and foxes live in caves. Crocodiles are in marshy places. The deer live in the woods. You know, tigers out there too! Some animals live close to us, some live far away. But you know what we all have one thing in common, with all animals. A large house we all build our houses in one big house: the same as our planet
author: anirudh prakhya

title: Our Living Room
text: I am Rina. This is my brother Sonu. We love each other. We play together in our living room. We have a bookshelf in our living room. My father keeps many books in the bookshelf. I read one story everyday. I am very neat. But my brother is very messy. He throws his toys, books, shoes and pens on the floor. We have a sofa in our living room. My parents like to sit on the sofa. We also have a carpet in our living room. The carpet is on the floor. I like to sit on the carpet. My brother and I help our mother in cleaning the house. I sweep the floor. My brother cleans the bookshelf. We love our home a lot.
author: Story Teller

title: Mangalyaan: A Journey to Mars
text: If you look up at the sky on some clear nights, you will see what looks like a shining red star. That’s the planet Mars. Ever since humans invented telescopes, they’ve looked at Mars and wondered: what is it like on Mars? Is there life up there? We can look at Mars from down here and try to guess. But what if we could actually travel there? Mars is one of the nearest planets to Earth in the solar system. And yet it is so far away that if you were to drive to it, it would take 1,200 years to get there. In an aeroplane, even at top speed, it would take 30 years. Take a look at this. If the Earth were this big… the Moon would be around here. And Mars would be somewhere over there, half a kilometre away. Cars and aeroplanes cannot take us there. To go to Mars, we need spaceships. On November 5, 2013, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched a spaceship that would travel to Mars. It was called Mangalyaan. Mangalyaan carried no humans on it. Instead, it carried four instruments, including one powerful camera with which to look at Mars from up close. Mangalyaan The first challenge facing Mangalyaan was the huge distance to be travelled. Flying straight to Mars would require a lot of fuel. And fuel is expensive. So the scientists of ISRO tried a more creative solution. They decided to “throw” Mangalyaan towards Mars, as if from a sling. Only in this case, Earth’s gravity played the role of the sling. Mangalyaan first started to “orbit” Earth. Then, it was put into bigger and bigger orbits by firing the engines six times. Each time, it picked up more speed. When Mangalyaan was at its fastest, it was given one final push. With that, it escaped Earth’s gravity. Since Earth also moves in orbit around the Sun, its speed was added to Mangalyaan’s. Earth, in other words, acted like the hand throwing the slingshot. But Mangalyaan didn’t fly straight to Mars. This is because Mars itself moves in orbit around the Sun. The scientists had to aim far ahead, so that Mangalyaan and Mars would both reach the same point in space at exactly the same time. 1. Mars was over here when Mangalyaan was launched 2. Mangalyaan’s path to Mars 3. Mangalyaan “caught” Mars over here 10 months later 4. Earth moves in orbit around the Sun 5. Mars moves in orbit around the Sun It’s a long, long way to Mars. Mangalyaan travelled for 300 days and covered 62,00,00,000 km. Over such a long journey, it was very important that the spaceship stay on the right track. Otherwise, it could easily miss Mars. Mangalyaan could tell where it was by the position of the stars around it. It sent this information back to Mission Control on Earth. Here, mathematicians checked to see whether the spaceship was still on the right path. When needed, they sent signals to the spaceship telling it to fire its engines and correct its path. 1. Dish to talk to Earth 2. Fuel tank 3. Solar panel to power the ship's electronics After many months in space, Mangalyaan was almost there. With just a few days to go, Mars’ gravity started pulling the spaceship in. As the spaceship neared the red planet, it had to slow down to enter into orbit. This had to be done very carefully, otherwise it could crash into Mars or fly away forever. It was a tense moment for everyone. However, on September 24, 2014, perfect entry into Mars’ orbit was achieved. Even today, Mangalyaan continues to orbit Mars and send pictures back to Earth. This is an actual photograph taken by Mangalyaan. We still don’t know for certain whether there is, or ever was, life on Mars. But isn’t it amazing that we could reach a destination so far out there? Now we can dream of sending people up there too. In fact, ISRO is already building a new spaceship that will take humans into space. It is called Gaganyaan. Gaganyaan will take three people on board and is set to take off in a few years. Would you like to be on it? What Is Gravity? It is the force that pulls all objects to each other. The Moon and Earth pull each other. So do the Sun and Earth. However, the heavier an object is, the greater its gravity. This is why small things, like this stone, fall to the ground. The much heavier Earth pulls the stone to itself with its high gravity. The stone also pulls Earth to itself but the stone’s gravity is so small that Earth moves only a very, very tiny amount that is not noticeable. What Is an Orbit? When I throw the stone, Earth’s gravity still pulls it, but the stone travels a bit before falling to the ground. When I throw it harder, it travels farther before falling. But what if I could throw it really, really hard? At just the right speed, the stone will travel all the way around Earth and keep going. It will have entered into orbit. In this exact manner, Mangalyaan was placed in orbit first around Earth and then around Mars. In space, lighter objects orbit around heavier objects due to gravity, like the Moon around Earth and Earth around the Sun. Orbits are generally elliptical (oval) in shape.
author: Nikhil Gulati

title: Cycling Day
text: Today is 24th of December. I ride the bike with my friends, Ray and Sovy. We go to Tai Po and a park. The park is so big and lots of fun. We have "siu mai" and fishballs in the food stalls. It has a pool and a bicycle trail. I like the bicycle trail because it looks like a mountain. Sovy also learns how to ride a bicycle without the helping wheels. At five o'clock, we ride the bicycle back home.
author: Hoee Robot
illustrator: Ankitha Kini; Nguyễn  Thị Nếp; Offei Tettey  Eugene; Pallavi Raikar; Soumya PV

title: Croak
text: PLIP PLOP PLIP! PLIP PLOP PLIP! PLIP PLOP PLIP! Raindrops plipped and plopped on the roof of the school. “Namaste, Masterji!” sang the children. Masterji beamed. “Namaste, Namaste, Namaste!” When Masterji turned to the blackboard— CROAK! Someone hopped in through the window. The children squealed. “Look behind you, Masterji,” they said. “There’s a frog in the room!” “Oh, really?” Masterji said, pretending to be surprised. “And what does your frog look like?” “It’s BIG and PODGY,” said Akif. “It’s GREEN and SPOTTY,” said Rani. “It’s WET and SLIMY,” said Munni. CROAK! In English class, Masterji said, “Turn to.” “Look behind you, Masterji,” said Farah. “The frog is sitting on your chair!” “Great! I hope she likes it here.” CROAK! “Now where did I keep my glasses?” asked Masterji during Maths class. “Look behind you, Masterji,” said Bishal. “The frog is wearing your glasses!” “Never mind, I can see just as well without them.” CROAK! When it was time for Science, Masterji said, “Here’s a bat hanging upside down from a tree.” “Look above you, Masterji,” said Akif. “The frog is hanging upside down from the fan!” “A frog that thinks she’s a bat, eh?” CROAK! At lunch, Masterji asked, “Where are my aloo parathas? I’m sure I packed three more.” “Look behind you, Masterji,” said Munni. “The frog is munching on your aloo parathas.” “Well, at least someone loves my cooking.” CROAK! When it was time for Games, Masterji said, “Where’s the football?” “Look behind you, Masterji,” said Rani. “The frog just scored a goal.” “Fantastic! She must join our team.” CROAK! The last bell rang. Masterji waved cheerily to the children as he cycled away. “Look behind you, Masterji,” the children squealed. “The frog is sitting on your bag!” “Good! I could use the company.” “I didn’t fall for any silly prank today!” CROAK!
author: Kavitha Punniyamurthi

title: The Mighty (Little) Hunter
text: I am a hunter big and brave. I catch all the leaves and things that trail. This morning I hunted a leaf. It fell to the ground. It was huge and wrinkly and made a WHOOSH sound. It flew, I ran I jumped and chased. I shook it with my jaws. I smashed it with my paws. It was soon all dead. CRUNCH STOMP SCRUNCH CHOMP Totally, all dead! I called to my fellow hunters, little cats all. But I could not see them I didn’t know where I was! I was not worried Because I am brave. So like a hunter I hid to watch and wait. I mewed, I meowed I called out loud. No one meowed back I felt a little bad. After long someone replied. I hid behind a big gate. Their voice was wrong. Their steps were strong. The big cat has told us about human monsters. I jumped and ran, but it put out its long BIG PAWS and caught me! How loudly I shouted, how strongly I screamed. With my claws and teeth I tried and tried to kill it! But the monster caught me by my neck like the big cat does. It picked me up and brought me close. I could see the small whiskers in its nose. I didn’t like its smell and I didn’t like being held. So I screamed some more and then I peed all over. That taught it a lesson! It put me on the bench. Quickly I turned, and CHOMP I went. I held that paw tightly and bit with all my might. The big monster cried in pain, it was a funny sight. Before I could run, it caught me again and carried me somewhere from lane to lane. Then under a big tree it put me down. I looked around, it was my own compound. I was so happy I meowed out loud. I forgot to bite that horrid monster who carried me about. I ran to my tree and called loudly. My fellows came running and I told them my story. I am a great hunter ferocious and brave. Today I killed a leaf and fought a monster. Tomorrow I’ll have even more adventures!
author: Shals  Mahajan

title: Katie the Cat and Daniel the Dog
text: There once was a shy cat named Katie and a playful dog named Daniel. They lived together in a house. Katie thought that Daniel was trying to catch and attack her, but he only wanted to play tag. Katie did not understand Daniel's body language at all. When Daniel barked, Katie got frightened. Daniel was just hungry for food. When Daniel yawned, Katie felt like he was trying to scare her away. Daniel actually wanted to take a nap. Katie was so afraid of Daniel that she jumped on the chair whenever he approached. There once was a shy cat named Katie and a playful dog named Daniel. They lived together in a house. Katie thought that Daniel was trying to catch and attack her, but he only wanted to play tag. Katie just did not understand Daniel's body language. MEOW!!! One day, Katie was taking a walk as usual. All of a sudden, Daniel rushed to her and bumped her off the road. At first, she was so mad at him. BOOM!!! A car zoomed by and crashed. Windows were shattered, and the car was flipped upside down. Katie was so thankful that Daniel had saved her life. She felt sorry for not understanding him before. Daniel loved her so much! They became really good friends. Meow! Woof! From that day on, they both lived happily and peacefully ever after. THE END
author: Abigail Fung
illustrator: Candice  Botha; Deepa Balsavar; Prashant Soni; Sandhya Prabhat; Vusi  Malindi

title: Lucy's lost marble
text: This is Lucy. Lucy's hobby is to collect marbles. She found her first marble in a park. Her mother said somebody should have missed it there. It was very smooth and beautiful, so Lucy wanted to keep it. It shined like a star when she looks at the light through that marble. Lucy was attached to its blue and green color and so she started her hobby of collecting marbles. Lucy would collect it from all the places. She would ask her mom to buy her marbles instead of toys. She would ask her friends if they have any marbles which they don't play with. And she always browsed parks and playgrounds for the luck of getting one more as she did for the first time. The marbles collected by Lucy were very colorful and smooth. They looked like candies that will not get sticky by air. Some looked like a miniature of planets shown in her school books. Some of them had little air bubbles trapped inside them which made them so beautiful than others. Lucy treasured her collection so dearly. Also, she liked to play with them and show her collection to her friends. She had a special jar for keeping the marbles safe. She would always save them in that jar after playing with them. And she never forgot to count them to make sure she had gathered all of them without missing even one. As days and months passed her marble collection also grew. One day, her little brother Leo came across Lucy's collection of marbles when she was at school. He was so excited and wanted to play with them. He also knew that he has to be careful because if he lost one of them it will end him up in trouble. So Leo said 'I will play with only two of these and put it back. That way Lucy will never know even I touched it.' to himself. So he selected his favorite two marbles from the jar and played with them for a while. Then he got bored playing with only two. Also, the marbles in the jar were very tempting. So Leo took a handful of them this time and started playing with them. His imagination went crazy. Robots had marble eyes, spiders lay marble eggs.. even mouse played snowballs with those marbles. After playing amply for hours, he put them back into the jar and keep the jar in its place. Little that he knows is one of the marbles is missing now. The next day, Lucy found out one marble in her collection is missing. She even said it was THE marble she got very first from the park. She was very sad and full of questions. She told her mother about how every time she counts her marble before putting it back and her memory of counting them to 28 - (the total number of marbles she had collected so far) even two days before. She was so sure she never missed the marble particularly her very first marble. On seeing how badly Lucy was missing her marble, Leo got really upset and he apologized to his mom that it was his fault. He then joined Lucy to search for the missing marble. Lucy asked him all kinds of questions like "where did you play?", "What did you do next?", "How did you play that?"... Leo answered all of those. He said how he got bored of playing with only two, and when he took out handful he forgot to count them. So he really did not notice one is missing when he put them back. He told how he played robots, then spiders with eggs and rats playing snowballs with marbles. Suddenly he saw Lucy's face lite up brightly. She started asking where he played snowballs, how he shot marbles and all. She even agreed to lend a few more marbles to him to play now. Her brother was really puzzled. But started playing snowballs again as he did the day before. As he shot his marble, it rolled to the corner close to the drawer in the room. Lucy and he moved to take that marble and saw a sock laying below the drawer. "Aha!! I found it! I found my missing marble!" Lucy jumped with joy as she took the sock and saw her first marble under that. Leo was also very happy. He promised Lucy to count marbles every time he plays with them. And he said he would also start collecting marbles because it was really fun to play with them. Questions to ask yourself: 1. Do you have hobby of collection? or ask your parents did they have any? 2. What do you think about Lucy counting marble every time she is putting back? why she is not counting when getting out? Do you have any better trick to keep the marbles safe from missing? 3. Do you think using others things without permission is good habit like Leo did in this story? I personally feel having a hobby of collection helps you developing habit of saving and maintaining which will help you as a grown up. So I encourage it.
author: Jeyalakshmi Ganesan
illustrator: Dhaanya  Arora; Lili   Probart; Mary Marble; Ngawang Dorjee; Phạm Hoàng  Giang; Shohei Emura

title: My family
text: Ours is a big family. She is my mom. He is my dad. Meet my elder brother Neetu and this is my little sister Meetu... Our grandparents are here... My mom has three sisters. They are my aunts... My dad has four brothers. Two of them are elder to my dad and two of them are younger than my dad. I call all of them 'uncles'. With my uncles....my aunts are also here. We have five little children in our family. When we meet we do lot of mischief. See, ours is a bigggg family! Oh no!I forgot about Bujo. Bujo waggles its tail and says "woof woof woof" all day.
author: Anasuya Adusumalli

title: Where is my bat?
text: I lost my bat. I am not fining it now. I looked behind the door. But could not find it there. I have looked in the cupboard. It is not there either. I looked under the bed. I did not find it there. I searched in suitcase. It is not there either. I have searched on the attic. I could not find it there too. I have searched here and there. I could not find it anywhere. See, it is there in sisters hand.
author: Anasuya Adusumalli

title: Spiky the Egret
text: All over the world, exotic birds flutter across the sky. This is a story about a flock of exotic birds who happen to have the biggest hearts in the bird kingdom. My name is “Spiky the Egret” and here is my story. I live in a forest filled with beautiful green trees, wild shrubs and smooth blue lakes. The lakes are my favorite as they provide me with juicy shrimp and tasty fish While other creatures struggle to fill their stomachs, I am lucky as I follow my father’s advice to hunt smarter and not harder. Here is my trick. I create a shadow over the water with my feather wings. Fish are attracted to the shadow, mistaking it for a lake bank and swim straight into it. I enjoy the fresh taste of the fish. When the sun is strong the lake reflects my image like a smooth mirror enabling me to admire my pointy spikes. During the hot days of summer, the wind can bring a nice breeze mixed with the scent of trees. Sometimes the wind has a bad temper that can ruin nests, break branches and level trees. One summer day the sky suddenly darkened and thunderous winds rattled and shook the trees, splitting some and uprooting others. Nests were flying in the air and spinning around in circles like swirling sparrows at dusk. I hid behind a shrub but the strength and speed of the wind lifted me up and twisted me in the air, carrying me far away. When I landed with a thump, I realized that the storm must have carried me into a strange faraway forest. The trees reached the sky. As I looked carefully around, I noticed that there weren’t any lakes but there was a long winding river that looked like a snake slithering along the ground. On the banks of the river I saw gigantic plants with the most beautiful yellow and burgundy colored leaves I had ever seen. The storm had caused me to lose some of my feathers and my legs and body were aching as I tried to walk. I got scared and started to shiver. I didn’t know what to do. I decided to close my eyes and go to sleep. The next morning, I heard sharp piercing sounds mixed with peeps and chirps. As I opened one eye and then the other, I saw an entire flock of strange looking birds surrounding me. They made me laugh. The birds looked at me with amusement that equalled my own. After flipping a fish at my feet, one of the birds spoke up and said, “My name is Shoeface Billy. Can I offer you some of the fish that I carried in my beak?” I gladly accepted and ate the small fishes fast as I was starving. Then the birds introduced themselves and started to tell me all sorts of interesting stories about themselves. Shoeface Billy said, “All bills are not created equal. Some are long and sharp while others are short and dull. The majority are in-between. What makes my bill special is that it is bigger than my head. I have a flying style that no bird can match. I can fly with my head retracted. I am a relative of pelicans and storks. I have been blamed for being slow in performing my daily errands but I am fast when it comes to catching a fish. I think that doing things fast does not allow appreciation of what one is doing.” When Shoeface Billy finished, the bird next to him introduced himself by saying, “My name is Flapsy Kague. I am the only bird with cone shaped flaps over my nostrils. They bother me as I can not clean my bill thoroughly when I bathe in the river. Unlike other birds I do not like to fly high as it can get cold way up in the sky. I learned to use my wings like a glider. These carry me faster when I am in a hurry to catch a lizard or eat a snake or when I am chased by a crazy raccoon or a wild cat. I am admired by some humans so much so that the name Kague is given to the tribal people of the beautiful island of New Caledonia in the Pacific Ocean. Yet some non-Kague people think that I am the “ghost of the forest”. I am surprised by this description, as I do not believe in ghosts and the only ghost, I am familiar with is my shadow.” Then the next bird hopped up and introduced himself by saying, “My name is Coney Guan. I have a red horn projecting from my head. I am still trying to figure out its purpose. I like to live on high grounds. I especially like mountains with plenty of trees and flowers since they provide me with food and shelter. I enjoy spending much of the time in trees since most of my troubles happen when I am on the ground, sipping water or bathing. I like to eat fruits and leaves and when I feel like indulging, I eat orchids. I have been living here for many years and I don’t like to go anywhere else. My mother told me once that if you are content and happy in what you have in a place you should not ask for more because you might not get it in other places.” The next bird wandered over and introduced himself by chirping, “My name is Goldy Crane. I am one of the tallest birds in the forest. I also have sharp vision that allows me to spot intruders from a far distance. This is probably the reason that cranes enjoy some of the highest longevity in the bird world. According to Japanese folklore, cranes can live a thousand years! I like to eat seeds, corn and small fish for my major meals and I cherish berries for dessert. When I indulge, I like to eat insects. Unfortunately, these are difficult to catch. My favorite hobby is dancing. In addition to strengthening my legs, dancing reduces stress and creates a joyful world. I like to travel during the winter. I fly with the same flock of cranes every year, heading towards warmer weather. When we fly, we not only maintain an exact flight formation but we arrive on the same dates and exact locations from year to year. We feel proud about this accomplishment. Unlike humans, who need calendars, airports, computers and plans, we accomplish the same thing with minimum effort by utilizing what nature has given us.” When Goldy Crane finished her story, the flock suggested that I should go to sleep to get some badly needed rest. They promised that they would visit me the next day. I slept deeply that night and woke up with a nice warm feeling owing to the generosity and kindness that these delightful creatures offered. The sun was shining on the forest and many flocks of birds reeled across the sky making wonderful formations and delightful sounds. I decided to spend some time exploring the area but suddenly I heard the same chirps that I experienced when the storm dropped me into this land the day before. I was thrilled to hear that beautiful sound again. My new friends were coming to visit as they promised! After they swooped in, they asked whether I would like to explore the forest. I enthusiastically accepted their offer. We decided to explore the river area. It seemed to be the center of a lot of activity by birds and animals. I was not surprised as no one can live without water. We strolled to the river. Along the way we came across silver springs and tall trees with curvy trunks and large flat leaves the size of elephant ears. I guess that trees can be as different as us birds. I could not help thinking that I should have traveled and explored the wider world around me when I was living in my old forest. When you have a chance to see more of the world than your normal sphere, your mind and heart open up to more wonders. I was interested in exploring the banks of the long winding river. It was full of green bushes and grass that would be just right for hunting food in the future. I was right. I spent a lot of time during the following weeks fishing and foraging in these grounds. The variety of trees and vegetations allowed me to try new types of crops and seeds that made my life in my new forest more enjoyable. I learned that my friends in the flock met in the morning to catch up and chat. Then each one would go his or her way to hunt, fly, stroll and perform daily rituals. At dusk they would meet up (and include me) so that we could share the events of the day. After that, we would retire to sleep, each one choosing and flying up to perch in his or her favorite tree. The Trip Home Months passed and I started wondering about my old forest and the places where I used to hunt and bathe. When I shared my thoughts with my friends, Goldy volunteered to use her skill in navigation to take me home if I wanted. She asked me whether I could provide her with a noticeable landmark that could help to identify my old forest. I told her one landmark was a series of mountains with wavy slopes that surround the lake where I used to go fishing. Goldy said that would be enough for her. The whole flock decided to join us. The next morning, we took off with Goldy leading in a V-formation. After almost an hour in the air, Goldy started to nose down and we followed her, descending in slow circles. Within minutes I recognized the mountains and saw the large lake where I used to fish, day in and day out. I was glad that we had made the trip successfully and I was grateful that I had the chance to see my forest once more. After a short and a successful hunt in the lake area for food, I offered to take my friends to my favorite tree and the small pond where I use to bathe. As we approached the area, I searched in vain for the big leafy tree where I spent most of my days and nights enjoying its shade and fruits. This was gone. My favorite bathing pond was as dry as a desert and new grass was shooting from where lovely cool water had once sparkled. I felt sad as I recognized that my old world has not only changed but disappeared completely. My friends must have sensed what was going on in my mind and Coney broke the silence by saying that the place was too hot for his horn. He suggested we go back to the lake area where he and the flock could enjoy the cool breeze of the lake under the shade of some shrubs. The flight back to a new life As we finished our midday meal, the others noticed that I did not participate in the conversations about life in my home forest. My mind was occupied with more important thoughts, realizing that my friends were going to leave soon. I could not help myself and abruptly cut into my friend’s conversation, saying, “Hey guys, I’m coming with you if you will take me when you fly back. I just realized that I have nothing here to stay for.” Flapsy clapped his wings repeatedly as a sign of happiness with my decision. This was joined by loud peeps and chirps from the others that echoed around the lake. At dusk, I flew up and away with my friends, my heart full of joy and happiness. I thought about how I would be starting a new life with friends who were kind and caring. While we were in the air, I could not stop thinking of how strange feelings are. The same heart that was full of sadness and sorrow in the morning was now pulsating with joy and anticipation in the evening! I also thought about the irony that something good can result from devastating events. In my case, for example, what was better for forgetting the misery of the recent past than looking forward to a promising new and meaningful life? THE END
author: Nidhal Rashid

title: Not Enough Guest !
text: Rabbit goes to a birthday party. Hey, who is this? A caterpillar! She is also going to the party. Can you count how many shoes she is wearing? Soon an army of ants marched to the party. Butterflies were running late! Very soon, the swarm of butterflies were all set to flutter their colorful wings and join the party. What's this? More animal guest? Can you name some of the animals here? It was cake cutting time but the bear wanted more guest to join in. At last, the bear agreed to cut the cake and begin the party. All the animals ate, danced and sang happy songs before going back home.
author: Abhyudaya Negi
illustrator: Alina  Aphayvanh; Eshita Munshi; Hari Kumar Nair; Nompumelelo  Mdluli; Salim  Kasamba; San srei nou ch nou ch; Shrujana Shridhar; Tanvi Bhat; Vishnu  M Nair

title: What are they Playing
text: What is the problem are these boys fighting? Yes or No. I hope they are not. Now they have a ball. They are not fighting they are playing and trying to win a game. Jim in the red and Bobby in the yellow are against 3 other players. Thats not fair. But Bobby has the ball they wont stop him. He will score. More boys come to play now. Freddy in the blue is here he is a good player. Yes more players come this is Joe he is the best player he will score I know. Come on Joe. Daddy Long legs came to play he has the goal in front of him he cant miss. Yes its a goal toDaddy Long legs you are a champ. We can still beat you said Freddy. We are tricky we have a plan. Come on guys lets show them. Look out there is tricky Eddie number 8. Hold said Eddie lets play next goal wins. Okay Okay okay! Eddie cant stop Freddy here is trouble Oh no number 8 Eddie has the ball can we stop him. Yes Jimmy has the cup he's the winner. The smallest player on the field scored the goal. Andy the ant scored with the butterflies helping him. Ant got squashed by a mud giant too bad so sad. You can do it Jimmy. No you cant said Freddy. No said Joe will stop you. Thats it last goal we win the cup. yeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeha grandma we did it! Yes it was the best game of the week. No of the month. It was really the best game of the year. Stop now said Jimmys Father. Time to eat. You are all winners because you played good and fair. No cheating. Cool players. They are good good game great game come again another day
author: Mike Wyatt
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; Brad Cuzen; Catherine Groenewald; David Chisha; Eric Nii  Addy; Jesse  Breytenbach; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Olivia Villet; Onesmus   Kakungi; Prom  Vichet; Renate van Rensburg; Sanjay Kisku; Sunando C; Suresh and Ajay; Therson  Boadu; Vusi  Malindi; Wiehan de Jager

title: Samuel and Pam
text: This is Samuel. He is going to a new school. He is excited but scared. This is Pam. She is also going to a new school. She is also excited but scared. Samuel meets Pam in the new school. Samuel asks Pam, "Do you want to play together?" Pam says, "Yes!" Samuel and Pam are now friends. They are not scared anymore because they have each other.
author: Danielle Ng

title: Ramu and his good deed
text: Once upon a time, there lived one boy in a village. His name was Raju. It was a rainy season. Raju went to a pond. He took his fishing rod and went for fishing. Suddenly he saw a dog in the pond. He took his umbrella to save the dog. He used his umbrella like a boat and sailed into the pond. He put the dog inside the umbrella and saved the dog. Raju saw so many fishes in the pond. He also saw a beautiful rainbow. Raju finally reached the river bank. He had so many fishes in the basket. Raju went home happily as he saved a dog, saw so many fishes, a beautiful rainbow and also gave a fish to a hungry cat.
author: Salma Saisankalp

title: Help Ever, Hurt Never
text: One day, a boy went to sea. He started catching fishes. Suddenly rain started pouring heavily. A little dog fell into the sea. The boy wanted to save him. So he took his umbrella and went into the sea. He used his umbrella like a boat. The boy saved the dog using his umbrella. Both of them saw many beautiful fishes swimming in the sea. The boy and the dog enjoyed sailing in the sea and saw a beautiful colorful rainbow. The boy caught many fishes and put them into the basket for the dog to eat. Finally, the boy took the dog and went home.
author: Yousuf Saisankalp

title: Do good, Be good
text: One day, Ramu went to sea to catch fish. It was a rainy day. The boy saw a cat drowning in the sea. He took his umbrella and floated into the sea. The boy saved the cat. They both saw many fishes in the sea. They also saw a colourful rainbow. They enjoyed being in the sea. The boy caught many fishes. He put them into the basket. The boy took his fish basket and went to his home. He saw a new friend, a cat. He gave a fish to the cat and they all went home happily.
author: Bhuvaneshwaran Saisankalp

title: The friendship between Rahul and a dog
text: One day, it was raining heavily. Rahul was fishing on the river bank. He saw a dog in trouble. He went to help the dog. Rahul saved the dog with the umbrella. Both of them saw a shoal of fishes. They saw a rainbow on the river bank. Rahul was very happy to save the dog. He put all the fishes in the basket. He saw a new friend, a cat. He gave a fish to the cat. The cat took the fish in its mouth and they all went home.
author: Rithish D Saisankalp

title: Fruit Fruit and More Fruit
text: We buy many fruits like apples and oranges. I really like bananas. There are many kinds of bananas. Green, yellow, orange, red and brown bananas. The market has many different kinds of fruit. Can you see pineapples, bananas, oranges, coconuts, persimmon, apples, mangoes and grapes. Cane you see the little dog hiding? ﻿The apples in the apple tree are ready to pick. There are some children looking at a basket of fruit. One boy looks hungry the other children are surprised. The market man threw dirty water at the bus. The children are surprised. I wonder what the bus driver would be saying? ﻿ The children are running. They are doing exercises at school. More children are running and doing exercises. My brother is testing all the different kinds of fruit. I must get there quick before he eats everything. ﻿ The children are eating and enjoying mangoes. My sister in the mango tree swinging in the branches and talking to the bird. I think the bird wants to eat sweet mangoes. ﻿ My mother is eating Noodles. She has already eaten some fruit. ﻿ At the fruit market the man is chasing away the monkeys from eating his fruit.
author: Mike Wyatt

title: Pussy-cat Mew
text: "Pussy-cat, Pussy-cat, where do you go?" "To London, to visit the palace, you know." "Pussy-cat Mew, will you come back again?" "Oh, yes! I'll scamper with might and with main!" PUSSY-CAT MEW set off on her way, Stepping quite softly and feeling quite gay. Smooth was the road, so she traveled at ease, Warmed by the sunshine and fanned by the breeze. Over the hills to the valleys below, Through the deep woods where the soft mosses grow, Skirting the fields, with buttercups dotted, Swiftly our venturesome Pussy-cat trotted. Sharp watch she kept when a village she neared, For boys and their mischief our Pussy-cat feared. Often she crept through the grasses so deep To pass by a dog that was lying asleep. Once, as she walked through a sweet-clover field, Something beside her affrightedly squealed, And swift from her path there darted away A tiny field-mouse, with a coat of soft gray. "Now here," thought our Pussy, "is chance for a dinner; The one that runs fastest must surely be winner!" So quickly she started the mouse to give chase, And over the clover they ran a great race. But just when it seemed that Pussy would win, The mouse spied a hole and quickly popped in; And so he escaped, for the hole was so small That Pussy-cat couldn't squeeze in it at all. So, softly she crouched, and with eyes big and round Quite steadily watched that small hole in the ground. "This mouse really thinks he's escaped me," she said, "But I'll catch him sure if he sticks out his head!" But while she was watching the poor mouse's plight, A deep growl behind made her jump with affright; She gave a great cry, and then started to run As swift as a bullet that's shot from a gun! "Meow! Oh, meow!" our poor Puss did say; "Bow-wow!" cried the dog, who was not far away. O'er meadows and ditches they scampered apace, O'er fences and hedges they kept up the race! Then Pussy-cat Mew saw before her a tree, And knew that a safe place of refuge 'twould be; So far up the tree with a bound she did go, And left the big dog to growl down below. But now, by good fortune, a man came that way, And called to the dog, who was forced to obey; But Puss did not come down the tree till she knew That the man and the dog were far out of view. Pursuing her way, at nightfall she came To London, a town you know well by name; And wandering 'round in byway and street, A strange Pussy-cat she happened to meet. "Good evening," said Pussy-cat Mew. "Can you tell In which of these houses the Queen may now dwell? I'm a stranger in town, and I'm anxious to see What sort of a person a real Queen may be." "My friend," said the other, "you really must know It isn't permitted that strangers should go Inside of the palace, unless they're invited, And stray Pussy-cats are apt to be slighted. "By good luck, however, I'm quite well aware Of a way to the palace by means of a stair That never is guarded; so just come with me, And a glimpse of the Queen you shall certainly see." Puss thanked her new friend, and together they stole To the back of the palace, and crept through a hole In the fence, and quietly came to the stair Which the stranger Pussy-cat promised was there. "Now here I must leave you," the strange Pussy said, "So don't be 'fraid-cat, but go straight ahead, And don't be alarmed if by chance you are seen, For people will think you belong to the Queen." So Pussy-cat Mew did as she had been told, And walked through the palace with manner so bold She soon reached the room where the Queen sat in state, Surrounded by lords and by ladies so great. And there in the corner our Pussy sat down, And gazed at the scepter and blinked at the crown, And eyed the Queen's dress, all purple and gold; Which was surely a beautiful sight to behold. But all of a sudden she started, for there Was a little gray mouse, right under the chair Where her Majesty sat, and Pussy well knew She'd scream with alarm if the mouse met her view. So up toward the chair our Pussy-cat stole, But the mouse saw her coming and ran for its hole; But Pussy ran after, and during the race A wonderful, terrible panic took place! The ladies all jumped on their chairs in alarm, The lords drew their swords to protect them from harm, And the Queen gave a scream and fainted away A very undignified act, I must say. And some one cried "Burglars!" and some one cried "Treason!" And some one cried "Fire! they are burning the house!" And some one cried "Silence! it's only a mouse!" And some one cried "Murder!" but none knew the reason; But Pussy-cat Mew was so awfully scared By the shouting and screaming, no longer she dared To stay in the room; so without more delay She rushed from the palace and scampered away! So bristling her fur, and with heart beating fast, She came to the road leading homeward at last. "What business," she thought, "has a poor country cat To visit a city of madmen like that? "Straight homeward I'll go, where I am well fed, Where mistress is kind, and soft is my bed; Let other cats travel, if they wish to roam, But as for myself, I shall now stay at home." And now over hills and valleys she ran, And journeyed as fast as a Pussy-cat can; Till just as the dawn of the day did begin She, safely at home, stole quietly in. And there was the fire, with the pot boiling on it, And there was the maid, in the blue checkered bonnet, And there was the corner where Pussy oft basked, And there was the mistress, who eagerly asked: "Pussy-cat, Pussy-cat, where have you been?" "I've been to London, to visit the Queen." "Pussy-cat, Pussy-cat, what did you there?" "I frightened a little mouse under her chair!" title: Sumi Budhi and Sugi
text: Sumi Budhi was woken up every morning by Sugi. As roosters crowed outside KOOKROOKOO Sugi honked into a sleeping Sumi Budhi’s ear indoors. KYUK KYUKKYUK KYUK “Your best friend wakes you up early every morning,” said Moso Hadam, Sumi Budhi’s husband. “Yes, it’s good to wake up early,” Sumi Budhi replied. She opened the door and began sweeping the racha, the courtyard. Swish swish, went Sumi Budhi’s broom. Sugi trailed after her, bobbing her neck. Sugi picked out ants and worms for breakfast. From the roof, Bhutu the naughty cat, watched Sugi eat. KWAK KWAKKWAK KWAK GOBBLE GOBBLE SWISH SWISH After sweeping the house, Sumi Budhi picked up a pile of clothes lying in a corner. “I need to buy soap to wash these clothes,” she said to herself. There was a tiny grocery shop at the end of the village. Sugi marched behind Sumi Budhi all the way there. KWAK KWAKKWAK KWAK “Johar,” said Sawna, the shopkeeper, greeting Sumi Budhi. “Johar,” said Sumi Budhi. “How is your companion today?” he asked. “Good,” Sumi Budhi smiled. “As always, she woke me up this morning.” Then Sumi Budhi walked to the pond. Sugi waddled behind her. In her beak, Sugi held two bars of soap—a white one for bathing and a brown one for washing. Two other women, Baha and Miru, were at the pond, washing clothes. “Sumi Budhi’s companion is so smart,” said Miru. As Sumi Budhi washed clothes, Sugi swam in the pond. Every few minutes, she let out a happy cry. KWAK KWAK KWAKKWAK KYUK Sugi ducked under water and hunted around for tiny, glassy-looking fish. At home, Moso Hadam roasted fish, and cooked rice and pui leaves. The fish smelt delicious. “I can’t wait to eat,” Sumi Budhi said as she oiled her hair. Moso Hadam was peeling onions when Bhutu sneaked into the kitchen. “Wait,” Moso Hadam told Bhutu. “You will get your share later.” MYAAAU “No,” said Moso Hadam sternly and went to wash the onions. Bhutu stopped whining and stared at the roasted fish. Seeing no one around, Bhutu moved stealthily towards the plates and was just about to grab the head of a roasted fish when— TUBUKKK Sugi pecked Bhutu, first on the tail and then on the head. Tubuktubuktubuk Moso Hadam rushed to the kitchen. “Dhurr… pusi!” he shouted at Bhutu. “Get lost, you cat!” Bhutu ran out the kitchen and on to the roof. He looked sad. Seeing Bhutu sad, Sugi felt sad too. She flapped up to the roof and sat near him. Tenderly, she began rubbing her beak on Bhutu’s body. “Just look at them!” said Sumi Budhi. “Come. Come down both of you.” “Should we eat?” Moso Hadam asked Sugi and Bhutu. Sumi Budhi and Moso Hadam shared a piece of fish with Bhutu. And Sugi pecked on rice and pui leaves.
author: Hansda Sowvendra Shekhar

title: The Wicked Wife
text: Once,there lived a lady called Kolyma.Her husband's name was Moggallana. They both took care of each other and loved each other very much. Kolyma had a very wicked nature. Kolyma didn't like Moggallana's ill parents. One day, Kolyma said Moggallana to go and leave his parents in the forest. He was not ready to displease Kolyma so, one day he took his parents to the forest and said,"We cannot take care of you so please live in the forest." With this he left the forest. When Moggallana was going back he fell into a pit and broke his legs.One man was passing by the pit. Then he saw Moggallana. His legs were broken and was unable to move his legs. The man helped him to get out. Then Moggallana realized his mistake and went back to the forest to his parents back. He was very ashamed. This story proves that if one does wrong things he has to pay for his misdeeds.
author: brahmtej singh

title: Dogs
text: Photographer: Hashim Badani Dogs are very loyal. They protect their owners' house. Dogs can get very dirty. They may need a bath! Dogs love to sleep. When they do, they dream about food! Dogs love to run and play. They will always fetch the ball! Dogs are the best pet. They are so much fun.
