title: Building a Building
text: On a breezy July afternoon, Meenu and Elango walk home from school. The shortcut takes them past a piece of land that has stood vacant for years. But today, it is buzzing with activity. “Let’s take the shortcut, Meenu akka!” Gurra-gurra-gurra! A huge vehicle moves back and forth, slowly scooping out clumps of bushes, grass and rocks. GURRA GURRA GURRA “Look, Mani mama is driving the bulldozer!” says Meenu. The children wave at Mani mama, the site supervisor. He waves back. “Tea break!” Mani mama's voice booms across the site. GURRA GURRA GURRA “What’s going on here, Mani mama?” asks Elango. “We are building a new school for you,” says Mani mama, wiping his sweaty face. “It will take nearly a year,” says Mani mama. “We are clearing and levelling the site now. Off you go, there’s too much dust in the air!” “Yay!” Elango jumps with excitement. “Our old asbestos roof leaks when it rains. And during the summer, our classrooms get so hot!” “When will the school be ready?” asks Meenu. Every afternoon, Meenu and Elango pass the site and watch the men and women at work. One day, they notice a woman looking at some charts. “This is Radhika akka, our civil engineer,” says Mani mama. “Would you like to see our floor plan?” asks Radhika akka. “What’s a floor plan?” asks Elango. “It’s a drawing that shows the design of the building. You can see where each room is, and where the windows and doors will be,” explains Radhika akka. “That big rectangle, is that the library?” asks Meenu. “Yes, a library with books and computers!” A week later, Elango and Meenu see a big vehicle digging deep, square-shaped holes. “Look at that giant robot scooping out mud,” yells Meenu. “That’s an excavator,” says Mani mama. “Today, we will start working on the foundation. It’s the base that supports the weight of the building.” By the first week of August, more holes have been dug. Cartloads of long steel rods have arrived. Meenu and Elango watch benders bind the rods to make steel frames and a lot of noise. Clang, clang, clang! Gada, gada, gada goes the cement mixer. “It is mixing cement, sand, gravel and water to form concrete,” says Mani mama. GADA GADA CLANG CLANG GADA The children watch as steel frames are lowered into each hole. “Look, they are pouring concrete around the base of the steel frame. The concrete becomes hard once it dries and this forms the foundation below the ground,” says Radhika akka. On a sunny morning, Meenu and Elango watch the workers set up wooden planks along the sides of the steel frames. “The planks form a casing around the steel frames. Concrete is poured into these wooden casings. Once the concrete hardens, the wooden planks are removed and the pillars are ready,” says Radhika akka. “Oh, it’s like the moulds used to make ice lollies!” Elango exclaims. “You pour the juice into a mould, leave it in ice until it hardens and then remove the mould.” “Exactly!” says Mani mama. “Now let’s get some ice lollies!” By October, the first slab is ready and the pillars have been raised to roof level. The brickwork starts in November. Meenu and Elango watch the masons place brick upon brick. The masons slap the cement over the bricks. Splat, splat, splat! Then, they smoothen the surface with trowels. As the walls of the building come up, the rain comes down. “I hope it stops pouring soon! We need to finish the brickwork in a month,” says Mani mama. On their next visit to the site, Elango asks Mani mama, “Is that the roof coming up?” “Yes, but be careful!” says Mani mama. “The workers are connecting the pillars using beams. They will set up metal plates underneath, fix steel rods over them and pour concrete over that. Once it sets, the plates will be removed and the roof will be ready.” “How does the roof stay up until the concrete hardens?” asks Meenu. “See those wooden poles? They hold up the metal plates from below until the concrete sets,” says Radhika akka. By the end of March, the roof is complete. While Meenu and Elango write their final exams, the carpenters fit the windows and doors. The electricians wire the building. The plumbers install pipes for drinking water and drainage. The workers paint the building and install lights, fans, switches, bolts and locks. When school reopens in June, the smell of fresh paint still hangs in the air. “Brand new fans, brand new benches and a brand new blackboard!” cries Elango. “Same old Bhaskar Master!” chuckles his science teacher.
author: Kavitha Punniyamurthi

title: Thank You, Teacher!
text: I wake up in the morning, get ready and come to school Eagerly wait outside the class, to be greeted by you! All the games we play, I enjoy every bit of the day Learning ABCs and 123s, about our world and everything in it. Glitters, colours, so much fun, you make my day so colourful, All those hours you take to prepare, we are all oh so thankful. When something seems terribly hard, I turn to you and ask for help. You taught me that it's ok to make mistakes, to get things wrong, Learn from them and try again, eventually, you will get it right. When I go home at the end of the day, I look forward to school the next day!
author: Vinamrata G Krishnan

title: My first time going fishing
text: At the summer holidays, me and my friends went camping all by ourselves with other kids. My mother and father did not go with me. When we first got there, my tummy was full of swirling butterflies while I was setting up the tent. But, at the same time, I was feeling happy because I can spend time with my friends. At the next day of camping, me and my friends and with the other kids were waiting beside the lake for the camp leader to come to tell us our activities for today. After a while, the camp leader shouted “we are going fishing!” I was thinking that fishing would be awesome because it was the first time for me to go fishing! It was afternoon at 12 o’clock, and I was waiting for the camp leader to show us how to fish. While I was waiting,it was shocking hot outside! I even need to fan myself with my hand! Afterward, I drank an enormous bottle of cold water! After a while, the camp leader taught us how to hook bait on the fishing rod. It was so difficult that I need the camp leader to hook for me every single time! But, too bad, the turtle in the lake always ate the bait. I was feeling hopeless when I was hooking my last bait on the fishing rod. I put it in the gleaming, sparkling water. Not so long after, the fishing rod started to move a tiny bit...... Immediately, I pulled the fishing rod up. There was a wiggling fish splashing water all over the floor! But nothing could had prepared for me for what happened next.......... Bang!!! My fish fell on the floor!!!
author: Allie  Cheung
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Craig Aldred; Krupa  Gedia; Moses  Dhladhla; Nirzara Verulkar; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Soumya Menon

title: The Rooster That Crowed Too Soon
text: Red Rooster felt it was time he showed the new drake that had come to live in the barnyard that he was both a very brave rooster and a, ruler of the barnyard. So the next time he saw the drake he said: “I suppose you have been in many battles, and no doubt the home you have just come from will miss your protection as well as your company.” “No,” replied the drake; “I was never in a battle. I do not quarrel with anyone. I believe in living in peace with all around me.” “Oh, well, that is all very well for you, perhaps,” said the rooster; “but for me, it is a different matter. I have to protect all the hens and chickens along with myself. I can whip any rooster around here, and no one dares to come into my yard.” The drake did not reply, for just then a strange rooster came into the yard, and Red Rooster ran at him with sweeping wings. He pecked at the intruder and spurred him until he was glad to run away. “There, what did I tell you?” said Red Rooster, coming back to the drake. “I am the greatest fighter around this part of the country. I am not afraid of anything.” “Oh, don't talk so much about it,” said the dog from his house near-by. “I think there are a few things even you are afraid of, Mr. Rooster. I guess you would run from a fox.” “I am not afraid of a fox,” said Red Rooster. “I can scare him by crowing loudly. Master knows when I make a great noise it is time for him to find the cause. Oh, I am very brave and can take care of myself.” Red Rooster felt so brave that he thought the highest place he could get on the wall would be a good place to talk about his bravery, so he flew up on the wall by the gate, and then to the top of the hen-house. Madam Pig was in her pen on the other side. “Madam Pig,” he said, “did you see me whip that impudent rooster that came through our yard?” Madam Pig grunted that she did not, as she could not see over the wall. "You surely missed a great sight," said the rooster, stretching his neck and strutting along the roof. "I am a brave fellow. I never allow anyone, who does not belong here, to come around here. I have just been telling the new drake about my prowess and bravery. ” “Mr. Drake,” he called, as the new drake and his family waddled past the hen-house, “if you need protection at any time do not hesitate to call upon me.” A robin perched upon the roof not far from him, and Red Rooster flew at him. “Go away,” he said. “I am very fierce and brave, and if you were as large as a cow I should attack you just the same. I am not afraid of anything.” Red Rooster strutted up and down, crowing and thinking how brave he was, and so intent was he upon his greatness that he did not heed the warning cries that came from the fowls in the yard below him. In a moment a big hawk swooped down and held the Red Rooster in his claws. He started to fly just as the shot from a gun was fired, and Red Rooster fell to the ground. He jumped up and shook himself, and looked in time to see his master pick up the dead hawk. “I guess that hawk won't show himself around here again,” he said. “That was a very hard fight, but I won, even if I did get a tumble.” “Well, if you are not a conceited fellow!” laughed the dog; “but I was not the only one that saw the hawk start off with you, and we all know that if the master had not shot it, you would not be here to crow to-morrow morning.” “No,” piped the robin from a tree; “you were telling me how brave you were, and the hawk was not half as large as a cow. You were not very brave when he came upon you. You did not do a thing. Oh, dear! It was so funny to hear you crowing about your bravery and then to soon see you caught by a hawk that is only a little larger than you.” The drake and all his family were listening, and Madam Pig had put her head over the wall to listen. Poor Red Rooster felt that it was no time to crow about his bravery, so he walked away with all the dignity he could muster. “He crowed too soon,” said the drake. “He crowed too much,” said the dog. “He crowed too loud,” said the robin, “or he would have heard the warning cries from the hens and chickens.” Classics on: about the project At we understand the need for children to read good literature as it nurtures growth and development of personality and social skills, it helps develop emotional intelligence, it provides opportunity to learn about and appreciate your culture and that of others and it transmits important literature and themes from one generation to the next. title: Little Mankoo's Big Dream
text: Mankoo has a dream! Butterfly wings make her eyes gleam. She dreams of flying in the sky and seeing the world. No matter how impossible it may seem! With a heart as big as her dream, Mankoo loves to help anyone in need. "Kaka! Kaka! Let me help you with those bags," says Mankoo to Bholu Kaka. "Little lamb, don't you worry! Let's go and look for your mummy," she consoles the sobbing lamb. One afternoon when Mankoo comes back from school, she sees Nani sitting and peeling peas. "Can I help you Nani?" asks Mankoo. Nani smiles and gives Mankoo a pod to peel. Mankoo opens the pod to take out the peas, when she feels something wriggle. She opens the pod some more... " A round green pea with BIG BIG EYES!!" Oh wait!! This isn't a pea! "It's a wriggly CATERPILLAR!!" Mankoo screams with excitement. She runs to her room with the caterpillar in her hand and puts it on the leaf of a plant in the window. "You can live here little one," whispers Mankoo into the caterpillar's ears. The caterpillar wriggles some more and starts nibbling on the fresh green leaf. That night when Mankoo sleeps in her bed, she hears someone calling her name. The voice seems to come from near the window. "Oh dear! Who could be calling me at this time?" Mankoo wakes up frightened. "Pstt...pstt...Mankoo!" says the caterpillar, a little louder than before. Mankoo jumps out of her bed and runs to the caterpillar. The caterpillar smiles and waves at her. She rubs her eyes twice to make sure she isn't dreaming. "I want your help, Mankoo ". "I have eaten a lot in the last few days and now I am big enough to go into my cocoon and rest there for a few days. But I don't have a cocoon!!I don't know how to make one!!" Says the caterpillar sadly. "Oh!! I can use Nani's silk threads to make a cocoon for you. I know what it looks like. I saw it in a book," says Mankoo. And now, Mankoo spends all her free time after school in making the cocoon for her little friend. Mankoo makes a beautiful pink cocoon for her little friend. The caterpillar wriggles and rolls in excitement. But it's now time to say goodbye. "Goodbye my friend. Till we meet again," says Mankoo to the caterpillar with a heavy heart. Mankoo is walking back home from school, when she sees something bright and colourful behind the old Banyan tree. She goes closer to see what it is! "WHOA!!" Mankoo gasps in amazement! It is her caterpillar friend who has transformed into a big, beautiful butterfly!! "Come on, Mankoo! Hop on!" "It's time to fly and touch the sky." The beautiful butterfly says excitedly. Mankoo hops on her friend's back and in no time they both are touching the clouds. Mankoo pinches herself hard to check if it is all a dream! No, it isn't! Little Mankoo's big dream has come true!!
author: Abhilasha  Khatri

title: How I Feel
text: ​Sometimes my heart beats fast. Sometimes I scream and shout. Some things make me giggle. Other things make me pout. ​Can you tell me how I feel? And can you tell me why? Can you tell me why I smile? What makes me want to cry? ​Sssss! Do you hear that? What is that hissing sound? I freeze, I gasp, I tremble. My eyes grow big and round. Can you tell me how I feel? ​Wheeeee! Today is special. Nani is coming to stay! My face glows, my eyes shine. I jump and shout, “Hurray!” Can you tell me how I feel? ​Ewwwww! My shoes are stinky. I think I stepped in poop. I clench my fists. I wrinkle my nose. Yuck! Yucky doo! Can you tell me how I feel? ​​​I have to return this library book, but I tore it by mistake. I chew my nails. I sweat a bit. My knees begin to shake. Can you tell me how I feel? ​Is that enormous package really a gift—for me? My mouth falls open. My eyebrows fly up. I wonder what it could be. Can you tell me how I feel? ​Iiish! I squirm and shuffle my feet. I told a lie today. I hang my head. My face is red. I don’t know what to say. Can you tell me how I feel? ​Sniff! Nani is leaving. I stand and wave goodbye. My mouth curves down, my eyes are red, and I begin to cry. Can you tell me how I feel? ​Grrrr! I’m not sleepy! I don’t want to go to bed! I gnash my teeth. I stomp my feet. My face is fiery red. Can you tell me how I feel? ​Mamma’s hugs are lovely. Cuddly, warm and tight. I sigh and smile and kiss her cheek. My eyes are big and bright. Can you tell me how I feel?
author: Varsha Seshan

title: Lights in the Water
text: It is late. Amma and Achan are asleep. Is Maisha asleep? No! Maisha goes out. Where does she go? Maisha goes to the beach. She visits Uchli. Uchli is a flying fish. Is Uchli happy? No. Uchli is upset. Why? The moon is missing! Last night the moon was up in the sky. Tonight it is not. Where is the moon? The moon did not rise from the sea. Is she lost under the sea? We must find her! We must look for the moon. But how? How will we see? How will we see when the moon is not up? Then, Uchli sees a light in the water. It glows and fades and glows again. Uchli shouts: "I have an idea! Get on my back.." They swim to the lights. Maisha takes a breath. The go under the water. Maisha gasps. Tiny animals glow in the sea. It is like a sky of stars. Who are these tiny animals? "It is plankton," Uchli says. "Can the plankton help us?" Maisha asks. "Can they help us see? We need light to find the moon." The plankton say they will help. The plankton give light to the sea. Now, Maisha and Uchli can look for the moon. Maisha hears a deep voice. It is a firefly squid. The squid has blue spots of light. "I can help, too," says the squid. "I saw the moon go this way!" "Hold on tight!" says the squid. The squid pulls Maisha through the water. They all swim down. Down, down, where it is very dark. But the plankton and the squid give light. Still, they see no moon. They meet an anglerfish. This fish has sharp teeth! But Maisha feels brave. "Hello," Maisha says. "Have you seen the moon?" "Yes," says the fish. "She went this way!" ﻿ They all swim. Maisha spots something! It is the moon. She is stuck under a rock! The squid helps to lift the rock. The moon slips out. "How did you get stuck?" Uchli asks. The moon answers: "I came here to meet my cousins, the moonfish. But my light faded and I got lost in the dark. Thank you for finding me." The moon jumps back in the sky. Maisha is happy. "So this is where the moon comes when she is not in the sky!" Uchli and Maisha wave goodbye. They swim back to the beach. Maisha sees the moon and stars in the sky. Now she knows there is also light in the sea! MEET THE LIGHT-MAKERS Many animals are able to make their own light. Can you name some of them? Plankton glow when there is movement in the water. This helps to scare away predators that might eat the plankton. Sometimes the movement of waves or boats can cause these sparks. The firefly squid has special organs called photophores (fo-to-fours). The photophores make light to scare away the squid's predators, to attract food for the squid, or impress a mate. Anglerfish make their light from the glowing bacteria inside them. When a plant or animal makes light, that is called bioluminescence (bye-oh-loo-min-ess-ens). Fireflies and g low-in-the-dark mushrooms make light above the water.
author: Lea Shaver

title: The Good Cook
text: Once upon a time, there lived a cook called Jenny, But all her family and friends did not like the food that she made. So her dad and mum told her to practice more and remember that 'Practice makes perfect'. So she did. On Monday, she cooked some soup. It tasted super horrible. On Tuesday, she cooked some soup again. It tasted yucky. On Wednesday, she cooked some soup again. It tasted a little yucky. On Thursday, she cooked some soup again. It tasted a little delicious. On Friday, she cooked some soup again. It tasted super delicious! Jenny became a good cook. Now she understood why her parents told her to remember 'Practice makes perfect'!
author: Nathaniel Ng

title: The Runaway Pig
text: Lalita is the pet pig of Mini Singh the potter. Mini loves his pig. He lets Lalita do whatever she wants – like digging up the pathways, gobbling up his tiffin and even teasing Gauri the dog! Lalita shuffles over to the bag of cucumbers hanging from the badaam tree. Unnngggghhhh mmmmnnnngh! Lalita stands on her tippy toes, stretching her snout towards the bag. She feels quite like a giraffe. Floooom floooomm cawwwrrr! Two big black crows fly down and nod encouragingly. Klink klink klink! Just then, the bells on the pottery gate tinkle. Harrumph-harrumph-pharrrrrrumph! Lalita snorts in delight. The pottery gate is wide open! She forgets about the cucumbers. She forgets about the crows. She forgets about Mini the potter and Gauri the dog. Ta-dhump, ta-dhump, ta-dhump dhump dhumppp! Clicking her heels, Lalita trots out of the open gate. Sniff-whiff-whiff! Lalita raises her snout and smells the air. Who is this furry animal in the middle of the path? It is taller than her. It has knobbly legs and greyish white hair. It has long ears, a long tail and a long face. Harrrrrumph! says Lalita, always happy to make a new friend. But Jenny the donkey has no time for friendly pigs. Jenny turns and… thakekk! She gives Lalita a hard kick. Yowww oowww owww! Lalita yowls as she staggers back. Lalita grunts softly and keeps walking on. Ta-dhump, ta-dhump, ta-dhump, ta-da-da-da-dhuppp? Who is this black beast walking so slowly? It has one big nose and two big horns. It has broad hooves, a wide back, and a large head. Where is it going? Whiffle-sniffle-whiffle! Lalita’s nose quivers. The buffalo is going to a pond full of water. Lalita forgets her fear and trots towards the water. But... The buffalo walks right into the pond. Splish, splosh, splish, splosh! Sploooobugullbbbb! Buloooossshgb! She plonks down and splashes water all over Lalita. The pond is full of buffalo! Disappointed, Lalita shuffles away. Ta-dhump, ta-dhump, ta-dhump ta — Out of nowhere, a scruffy dog appears. Snarling, the dog moves slowly towards her. Grrrr rrrgh grrrrrrrr! Lalita picks up all her four hooves and runs as fast as she can. Ta-dhump, ta-dhump, ta-dhump, ta — dhaaan! dhhhissshhhh! She finds herself in the middle of a thicket of bushes. Swuuuup-wooosh swuuuuup-woooosh! Lalita pants and gasps. She is tired. And she is very hungry. Buzzzzzzzzzzzzzz! Zzzzzzzziinnnnng! A pesky mosquito buzzes near her. Flappa-wappa-wap-wap! Lalita shakes her head, flapping her ears. The entire bush shakes. Mulberries begin to rain down on her. Delighted, Lalita gobbles up the berries, the ripe and the not quite. Plop! Plop! Plop! Plop! Her nose and and her tongue now a delicate purple, a very tired Lalita settles down in the bushes. And falls fast asleep! In her sleep, she dreams of kicking cucumbers and swimming donkeys. Tomorrow will be a brand new day. Who knows what new excitement it will bring? One thing is for sure, Lalita’s adventures have just begun!
author: Rohit  Kulkarni

title: The boy and the dog
text: One day it was raining heavily. A boy went fishing.The boy saw a dog drowning in the river. He wanted to save the dog. He used his umbrella like a boat and saved the dog. The boy and the dog saw many colourful fishes. They also saw a beautiful rainbow. They reached the river bank. Many fishes fell into the basket. The boy gave a fish to the cat. The boy,cat and the dog went home happily.
author: Rithish Sai

title: The new planet
text: Nick and his team were preparing to take off from earth to an unknown planet in another solar system to see if it could be inhabited by humans. Their biologist, Stacy had researched and found out that there is at least one planet with life in every solar system. They decided to go and explore their closest solar system. They reached the planet in a few earth days. The planet was a white one. It didn't look like Earth or feel like it either. They explored many parts of the planet but didn't find a sign of life anywhere. Nick banged his foot on the surface in anger and disappointment but then he was surprised when the surface started cracking like an egg. They all fell in. They opened their eyes and were completely shocked. There were plants and tiny living creatures everywhere. Stacy figured out a way to communicate with them. She asked them if she could get humans on that planet. The creatures panicked and pleaded them not to do so. The little creatures wanted to protect their planet from any harm. Nick and his team learnt a lesson from that and decided to go back to their planet to protect it and care for like the creatures did instead of finding a replacement for it.
author: Riddhi Shobhavat
illustrator: Delwyn Remedios; Dorian  Dutrieux; Fahad Faizal; Kavita Singh Kale; Mary Anne Hampton; Sandhya Prabhat; Tanvi Sawant, Mahika Arora; Vidyun Sabhaney

title: Animals of Uganda
text: These are giraffes. They have very long necks. They eat leaves from tall trees. What colour is a giraffe? This is an elephant. The males have white tusks. They have large ears. Elephants have long trunks. They use their trunks to pick leaves off the tall trees. Elephants eat grasses and leaves. What colour is the elephant? This is a crocodile. It lives in the rivers and lakes. It has a long tail. It has a wide mouth and many sharp teeth. It eats fish and other animals. What colour is the crocodile? This is a lion. It has big, sharp teeth. Male lions have a mane. Where is the mane on this lion? This is the crested crane. It is the symbol of Uganda. It has long legs and a crown. What are the colours of the crested crane? These are water buffalo. They eats grasses and live near rivers and lakes. What does a water buffalo have growing on its head? These animals are called zebras. They have black and white stripes. What other animal do you know that looks like a zebra? Here are two different types of animals. There is a mother warthog with her babies. Warthogs have tusks too. How many warthogs can you count in the picture? The other animals are antelopes. They eat grasses. What colour is the antelope? What types of animals do you see? Where do they live? Which one would you eat?
author: Wendy Parry

title: A rainbow tale
text: Udoo, Erdoo and Eryum gathered around mother. With plenty of love in her heart and her totem in her hand, mother cleared her throat and began the story: There was a little girl called Yana. Yana's aunt told her about a pot of gold at the end of a rainbow. Yana was curious about that pot. Did the pot contain gold coins, or lumps of gold in black rocks? Yana imagined that if she looked at the sky long enough, she would get some answers. She smiled at the birds. She wondered how the gold got into the pot. And, where at the rainbow's end would she find the pot? Yana wished that she knew the exact spot! As she thought about her rainbow quest, Yana saw a green frog jumping in the bushes. She could not resist, she jumped around with the frog for a while. Then, checking the sky, she said goodbye to the frog. Yana went on her way in search for the end of the rainbow. She began to think about the rainbow's colours. In a flash, red came first to mind. She recalled the day her family almost had a bad accident because a driver didn't stop at a red light. Yana was thankful because no one was badly hurt, although they all had cuts and bruises. Everyone got a huge fright. After red, Yana thought of the colour orange. She loved sweet oranges. Sweet, sour and bitter were the tastes she experienced while eating oranges. Thinking about a sour orange made Yana's mouth taste sour! Yuck! Do you know that taste? Yana's thoughts moved from oranges to a bowl of dark indigo beans, and her stomach made noises. She realized that she was hungry. Her rainbow quest would have to wait for a while. It was time to eat some food! She ran into her aunt's kitchen. The air carried the aroma of the fried chicken and fresh bread. Yana washed her hands and her nose led her to the food. She ate a little chicken with a large piece of bread, and then she drank water. She looked down at her dress. What a mess! Stains from the chicken, and water spilled. So she changed into a beautiful purple dress. Later, Yana and her aunt went out to the park together. They lay on the grass with a book. Yana eagerly peered into the pages itching to finally know more about the hidden pot of gold. Yana's aunt chuckled at her excitement and they both burst into peals of laughter. They began to read the story together. It was a tale about how the rainbow colours came to the land of Tonota, and a little boy called Mpho. For the longest time, the people of Tonota only knew the green of plants and the brown of soil. But Mpho had dreams of clouds in glorious colours! He told the elders about his dreams. They said, “If you name the colours, we can bring them to life.” The elders asked for the help of rainmakers from across the land, and they gathered together. Mpho began thinking about the colours in his dreams. Then, these words came to his mind, “Red, blue, orange, yellow, purple, green, and indigo.” The colourful clouds filled the sky! The clouds hung in the air, and the rainmakers formed a circle, holding hands. The rainmakers looked up to the clouds and the colours formed a beautiful arc. This was Tonata's first rainbow! People cheered and rejoiced. And just then, Mpho noticed a pot at the end of the rainbow. A pot filled with gold! “What an amazing rainbow story! Now I know where to find my pot of gold!” exclaimed Yana to her aunt. Her aunt smiled, happy she shared her favourite childhood story with her niece. “But, no more rainbow quests for you! The pot of gold can only be found by accident!” With those words, mother finished her rainbow tale. Udoo, Erdoo and Eryum jumped up and gave her a standing ovation. Then they held hands like the rainmakers, pretending to make their own rainbow! “Mother, does every land have its own rainbow story?” asked Erdoo thoughtfully. “Yes, my lovelies,” said mother. “Tonota's rainbow started with Mpho's dreams of colourful clouds. And remember the Magical Rainbow River and its rainbow ice-cream?" “Mmmm, rainbow ice-cream, that's my favourite story,” said Eryum looking at mother hopefully as the children gathered around her again.
author: Mimi  Werna
illustrator: Edwin  Irabor; Jesse  Breytenbach; Offei Tettey  Eugene

title: I Want to Ride a Motorbike
text: This is Diya. At age 8, she saw a woman on a bike. The image stuck in her head. At age 9, her father took a shortcut through a one-way and was cut off by a woman driving a car. Even though it was his fault, he muttered, “Lady drivers.” Diya never forgot this. At age 11, she sat in a plane piloted by two women. She waited to meet them after the flight, and even took a photo with them! At age 12, she became the best cyclist in her society. She won most races! 11 years 8 years 9 years Now, at age 14, Diya knows she wants to be a pilot. But first, she will ride a motorbike. Diya tells her neighbour Shayan about the bike she wants. “Girls can’t ride motorbikes. How many girl riders have you ever seen?” he says. “There are many! You just don’t know,” Diya tells him. Diya keeps telling Appa and Amma about bikes and motorbikes. “Appa, did you know that bikes are safer than scooters?” “Amma, did you see that article I sent you? Eighteen women biker groups across India! They do long rides together every year. I also want to go!” “Shayan told me his cousin drove from Delhi to Bangalore on his motorbike. Imagine that!” “Diya, if you spent even half this time on Maths, you would do much better on your tests. Go do your homework,” says Appa. Diya is finishing her homework, when her mother comes to her room with a book. “What’s this, Amma?” “It’s a photo album, from when I was in college.” Diya excitedly pores over the photos. “Is that Anita Chithi on a motorbike?” she asks. Anita Chithi lives in Mumbai. She’s Amma’s best friend and Diya’s favourite aunt. “Yes, that’s her and that was her bike for a few weeks. When not in class, Anita would be out all the time, all over the city. I didn’t know she was also learning to ride a motorbike from her friend.” “She had a Yamaha. That is so cool! Why did she have the bike only for a few weeks?” “She told her father that she needed to buy a two-wheeler for her classes and for a part-time job, so he sent her the money. He thought it was a scooter.” “But she bought this Yamaha!” Diya was amazed, and she also understood why her mother never told her this story. “When he found out, he was not happy. He told her to sell the bike immediately or she would have to leave college and go back. So she sold it. She was very sad about it.” “I can imagine,” says Diya. “I just thought you would like to see this photo,” says Amma. Over the next few weeks, Diya thinks a lot about Anita Chithi and her Yamaha. She later asks Amma if she can call Anita Chithi. Farah Aunty picks up. “Hello Aunty, this is Diya. How are you? Is Anita Chithi there?” “Oh hi Diya! Wait, I’ll just give Anita the phone.” Diya gets straight to the point. “Anita Chithi, you know what? Amma showed me a photo of your Yamaha!” Anita takes a moment to reply, “Oh, she still has those photos.” Diya replies, “That’s so cool, Chithi! I had no idea. I love motorbikes, but Appa thinks I shouldn’t ride. He says it’s not for girls. Everybody says women can’t ride. It’s so irritating,” Diya hesitates before continuing. “Will you teach me please?” Amma overhears this, and is surprised. She smiles. Anita Chithi is as surprised. “You need to first get a Learner’s License, Diya. You can only do that when you’re 16.” “Yes, that’s next year. But I want to learn from you. Will you please teach me?” “I’d first have to check with your parents…” Diya looks hopefully at Amma. Amma nods. “Amma says yes! And I can tell Appa later, like you did,” she says. “No no, you shouldn’t. Why don’t I speak to Amma and we’ll see how to ask your father, okay?” “Okay, thank you Chithi!” “I understand why your Appa is worried. You have to remember, the most important thing is to be safe and considerate — as a rider and as a person. Biking is fun, but it matters more what kind of rider you are than how fast you go.” That night, while Diya is in her room, she overhears Amma and Appa. “Why did you show her that photo? Now she won’t drop it,” says Appa. “She wants to be independent. Isn’t that a good thing?” replies Amma. “She can take the bus. Why a motorbike? It’s not safe!” “You congratulated Rahul so enthusiastically on his Learner’s Licence. Why this double standard?” Diya is sad. Appa will never understand. The next evening, Shayan and Diya race home from the cricket ground as usual. Shayan is so bent on winning, that he swerves ahead, narrowly missing a young child by the side of the lane. “I won! See? Even on a cycle, I’m better.” says Shayan. “You could have hit that little boy. What is wrong with you?” Diya says. She runs up to the boy to comfort him, unaware that Appa is watching from upstairs. That evening, Appa calls Anita Chithi. A few days later, Appa walks into Diya’s room while she’s playing a game on the computer. “So I heard you called Anita?” Diya looks up, nervous. “Appa, please, Chithi said she’ll teach me, so it’s safe. I’ve started saving for it also. You know, bikes are actually safer than scooters. They have bigger wheels…” “You know this much about bikes, but how much do you know about helmets?” Appa says. Diya is confused. “You’re first going to have to buy a helmet. You need to be safe,” says Appa. “Does that mean Chithi can teach me?” “Yes, when you go to Mumbai next year. If you still want to learn.” “Thank you Appa!” She hugs her father. “In exchange, when you become a pilot, you have to fly me everywhere.” “Me also!” says Amma. “Done. But first, rides on the motorbike,” says Diya. Pioneering women bike riders around the world: - Annie Londonderry was a Latvian immigrant to the United States who in 1894–95 became the first woman to bicycle around the world. - The American civil rights leader, Susan B Anthony, wrote in 1896, “I think the bicycle has done more to emancipate women than any one thing in the world. It gives women a feeling of freedom and self-reliance.” - Bessie Stringfield, an African-American female motorcyclist, in the 1930s (decades before the Civil Rights Movement), rode across America countless times, and even entered men’s motorcycle races (only to be denied the winning prize when they found out she was a woman). - Elspeth Beard, architect and motorcyclist, is noted as being one of the first women to ride a motorcycle around the world, between 1982-1984. - Roshni Sharma is the first Indian woman to ride a motorbike from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in 2014. - In 2018, an all-women biker contingent from the Border Security Force (BSF) called ‘Seema Bhavani’ or Border Bravehearts were part of the Indian Republic Day Parade for the first time ever!
author: Aarthi Parthasarathy

title: An Ode to Cricket
text: I don't ask for much Just let Virat stick to the crease Don't let him run out please! If he runs out, That would be it Batters will come and quickly leave Tears will be shed on every sleeve Half the country will grieve. And me? I'll bite my nails I'll chew my tongue off I'll buzz like a bee I'll pee and pee and pee. Did you know? Virat is like my elder bro His century is my pride and show No, really! As soon as I eat this biscuit Or when that chair creaks When Mom calls out Or when Didi shrieks Virat loses sight of the ball His wicket threatens to fall! Now you see? Just like that, we lose It's a price we all pay The world cup slips away We all sigh and brood India falls into a bad mood. So dear God, I don't ask for much Just let Virat stick to the crease Don't let him run out please!
author: Sherein Bansal

title: The Elephant's play time
text: There was a little elephant in the forest. He likes to play all day. One morning he was playing with his friend little tiger. Then the daddy elephant said," children stop playing, it's time for little tiger to go home,his daddy is waiting for him". So the little tiger went back to his home. Then the little elephant cried and sadly said,"I'm not finished playing daddy, I want to play more. Can you play with me?". Daddy elephant said,"no I can't my boy, I have other jobs to do let's go home". Little elephant pleaded, " Then can you take me to little tiger's home, I want to play more, I don't want to go home". Daddy elephant said, "Okay, but only for an hour". They reached little tiger's house and played with his toys happily. After an hour, when daddy elephant said,"It's time to go home my boy". Then the little elephant cried and sadly said," I'm not finished playing daddy, can you take me to little panda's house. I want to play more, I don't want to go home". Daddy elephant said, "Okay, but only for an hour". They reached little panda's house and played between trees happily. After an hour, when daddy elephant said,"It's time to go home dear boy". Then the little elephant cried and sadly said," I'm not finished playing daddy, can you take me to little fox's house. I want to play more, I don't want to go home". Daddy elephant said, "Okay, but only for an hour ". They reached little fox's house and played hide and seek happily. After an hour, when daddy elephant said,"It's time to go home dear boy". Then the little elephant cried and sadly said," I'm not finished playing daddy, can you take me to grandpa and grandma house. I want to play more, I don't wanna go home". Daddy elephant said, "Okay, but only for an hour". They reached grandma and grandpa house and played happily. They also visited his uncle and aunt elephants. Little elephant was really happy, but daddy elephant got really tired. After an hour When daddy elephant said,"It's time to go home dear boy". Finally little elephant said," Okay daddy lets go home". After a long day daddy elephant was finally happy to go home. By the time they reached home,t he night was very dark. When they were about to fall sleep little elephant asked, " Daddy will you play with me tomorrow, If you are busy i'm happy to play with my friends like today". Daddy elephant panicked and said," No my dear boy, I'm happy to play with you tomorrow". Little elephant laughed funnily.
author: Bavish Adhithya

title: Doctor Donut
text: Doctor Donut was the busiest doctor in the Dessert Hospital. His patients loved his sweet medicines and his gentle treatments. He rolled out of his room for his daily visits to the various wards, in his white chocolate coat, with nurse Croissant jogging behind him. His first stop was the sponge cake room, to check his patients. “Doc, ours bums are paining,” three round cakes waddled over the table. “Does it pain while sitting?”the doctor asked. “Yes,” the cakes replied. “Stick cherries and strawberries heated in maple syrup to their bottom,” Doctor Donut told the nurse. “And make them lie upside down until they feel better.” “We are feeling cold,” several funny shaped cakes shivered. “A bath with pink chocolate will make them feel better,” the doctor said to the nurse. “What about me doc?” a round cake asked. “I’m feeling very itchy.” “Do you have rashes?” “No, I just feel like scratching.” “A dressing of white cream and blue icing sugar will cure it,” Doctor Donut smiled at the flaky cake. “Doc help me,” said a heart shaped cake with a large crack across it. “Do you have any pain?" doctor donut asked. “No,” the cake replied. “I just feel cold and tired.” The kind doctor smiled. “Nurse, cover him with a thick colourful blanket and stick gems, flowers and leaves over him." Doctor Donut rolled out of the room, wheeling down the corridor with nurse Croissant jogging behind him. He stopped outside the cup-cake ward. The small cakes, with human faces, were groaning in pain, clutching their stomachs, they rolled from side to side. “Doc, we’ve a hollow feeling in our stomachs,” they rubbed their bellies. “Hmmm…” Doctor Donut prodded the cakes with a candy cane. He made a few of them turn upside down. “This is an epidemic,” he frowned. “Get the injections ready,” he said to the nurse. “Please doc, no syringes,” the cup-cakes shivered in fear. “Not even injections filled with hot chocolate?” the doctor’s kind eyes’ twinkled. “I promise that you won’t feel any pain,” he smiled. “Infact, you will feel nice and warm.” “No,” the cup-cakes said running all over the room. Doctor Donut frowned. This epidemic was contagious. If he couldn’t treat it, then within a short time it would spread across the hospital and there would be no desserts left. “Let nurse put you to sleep,” the doctor said gently. “We’ll decide your treatment in the morning.” The cup-cakes lay down on their backs. Nurse Croissant fed them a spoonful of hot milk with honey. Within a few minutes the cup-cakes were snoring soundly. Filling a syringe with hot chocolate, Doctor Donut jabbed the cupcakes in their stomach. As the hot chocolate filled their stomachs, their stomachs swelled. “Cover them with a red velvet blanket,” Doctor Donut told the nurse. “They will be completely alright by tomorrow morning.”
author: Rachna Chhabria
illustrator: Archana Sreenivasan; Brad Cuzen; Kanak Shashi; Magriet Brink; Mary Anne Hampton; Mieke van der  Merwe; Nompumelelo  Mdluli; Tanvee Nabar

title: The Dark Cloud
text: The large room in the sky was filled with clouds. Small clouds, big clouds, clouds shaped like birds, clouds shaped like animals, swirled in the room. The cloudmaker in white robes, stood in his house in the sky. Opening a large window, he said to the clouds, “Find your place in the sky.” Clouds floated out through the window, spreading in all directions, swirling and twirling in different patterns in the sky. “Wait,” the cloudmaker said to the dark cloud hiding behind a group of fluffy white clouds. The dark cloud didn’t hear the cloudmaker. It moved closer to the smaller clouds. “Don’t follow us,” a duck shaped cloud said to the dark cloud. “You don’t belong with us, you don’t look like us.” “But, I’m a cloud just like you,” the dark cloud said in a hoarse voice. “You don’t even sound like us,” a sheep shaped cloud said. The white clouds drifted away. The dark cloud followed the other clouds, watching them transform into different shapes. The cloudmaker flew behind the clouds, waving his feather, parting the clusters of clouds huddled together. But, there was no sign of the dark cloud. Soon the sky was filled with clouds. The cloudmaker searched for the dark cloud. The dark cloud tried to twirl and swirl like the other clouds. But, its body refused to co-operate. Only strange sounds and a flash of light emerged from it. The cloudmaker raced across the sky to the point of the lightning. The dark cloud stood alone, looking sad. The cloudmaker twirled his feather, bringing the black side up. He patted the dark cloud with his feather. The dark cloud made strange sounds, as thunder rumbled out of its body. Rain poured down from the dark cloud’s body. The other clouds watched jealously from far. Suddenly they floated towards the dark cloud. “Will you play with us?” they said, eager to play with their new and special friend. The dark cloud played with them, feeling light and happy.
author: Rachna Chhabria
illustrator: Alicia  van Zyl; Bianca de Jong; Carlos Amato; Greystroke; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lauren Holliday; Linh Chi; Megan Andrews; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: The  Generous Cactus
text: There grew a cactus alongside a beautiful rose plant in a shruby desert town. The rose plant had beautiful blooms and attracted many visitors like the bees and the butterflies. The rose would remind herself everyday, " I am such a beauty ". She was proud of her crimson red flowers and velvety soft petals. The rose bush was very proud of its beauty and looked at the cactus harshy. The rose bush would often murmur " Oh.... my..... my.....! How could such a thorny and ugly thing ever live on Earth? I have to live along side such a disgusting thing ". Oh! Oo! This cactus looks like an ugly green frog. I wonder who looks at him. Slowly the summer approached the sun became hard and the rose bush started to wither. The rose bush was worried. Looking at the cactus the rose bush thought "The cactus is not fading? It looks just the same as did on the first day we met". That evening, the rose plant decided to talk to the cactus. It called out " Hey cactus! you look fresh. I am withering. Can you please help me get some water." The cactus replied with a smile " Sure beautiful rose, tomorrow I will see that you are hydrated ". The next day the cactus calls out to Mrs Woodpecker sitting on the babool tree. " Hey Mrs woodpecker, please come and prick my stump with your beak, I will be grateful." "Certainly" replied Mrs Woodpecker and flew to the cactus to do what he had asked. Mrs. Woodpecker slowly pecked on the cactus. S oon water began to ooze from its moist stump. The watery fluid flowed to the rose bush and it again became fresh and vibrant. The rose plant thanked the cactus and thereafter became best friends.
author: Shalini Mahapatra
illustrator: Abhishek Choudhury; Aditi Dilip; Amy Jane Harkess; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Kumudini Kondhalkar; Natasha Sharma; Vinayak Varma

title: Chikkiri Chakkiri
text: Chikkiri chakkiri, Round as a plum. The cat played her flute And the mouse beat his drum. Imbilli kimbilli, Roses so red. The pig leaped right over The buffalo's head. Jhataka mataka, Kettle of tea. The cow danced the bhangra Around the neem tree. Thandana thindana, Jamun so sweet. The dog sang ghazals to The old parakeet. Karukku murukku, Oh, what a bother! We’re spotted at play By the farmer’s grandmother! Dhadaka bhadaka, Hearts beat like drums. Will she blurt our secret Out to everyone? Jingiri jangiri, Shiny, bright sun. She kicks off her slippers And joins in the fun!
author: Lavanya Karthik

title: One big family
text: I love to sing. I love to fly. I love to eat insects. I love to hop in trees from limb to limb. I am from a big family. Some of my relatives have feathers and others not. Some are popular and some are hated. Some are very big and some very tiny. Some are harmless and some are poisonous. Some are fast and some are very slow. Some are very talkative and some are quiet. Some are rare and some are common. Some can fly (even under water) and some cannot. Some can sing but some cannot. Some can talk and some cannot. We are so different but we belong to the same big and united family.
author: Isamotu Ismaila
illustrator: Gerhard Van Wyk; Lauren   Nel; Measa Sovonnarea; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Suvidha  Mistry

title: Fairy Rosy
text: Once upon a time, there was a beautiful heaven. Little bit far, there was an ugly hell. In the heaven, there lived a beautiful castle. In the castle, there lived three family members. They were Fairies. They were the king, the queen and the young princess. The young princess name was Rosy. There was a bad witch with no name. She was a wicked witch. When Rosy turned five, her mother made a beautiful birthday cake. When she was about to blow the candles and cut the cake, an indoor thunder-storm came and destroyed the cake. The witch made the indoor thunder- storm and destroyed the cake. The witch was invisible. But Rosy killed the witch with her magic power and they lived happily ever after. THE MORAL OF THE STORY IS "BE WISE AND BE BRAVE."
author: Chanasya Das

title: Tails
text: Look at the dog's tail! It's nice and curved. The tongue is also curved and hanging outside its mouth. Look at the horse's tail! It's hanging like an ornament. When the horse walks on the road, it bounces up and down. The monkey's tail is long! It is full of mischief. It dances and prances on the tree, Looks like a human being. The squirrel has a big tail! and it is very beautiful. Soft as cotton, it has a kind heart. The cow's tail on a daily basis, swings and rings like a bell. It shares its healthy milk with you. The crocodile's tail is when seen will leave you awe struck. The whole town will shiver, and your heart will tremble. The lion's tail is majestic, just see how proudly it stands. The whole town will bow before it and say "As you wish, your Majesty" And the snake has no 'tail', the snake itself is like one. Like a rope, it slithers on the ground.
author: Arun Subramani

title: Who do you think you are?
text: Toby flipped to the last page of his math book, contentedly. Then somebody stared at Toby. Toby knew that someone was staring at him but he didn't mind. Toby read the last sentence of his math book. Toby was clever that he knew a student had came to school, but he didn't know the name of the new student. When Toby looked at the student who was staring at him, he was gone! Who was the student staring at Toby? Then Mr. Bok told the whole class it's time for lunch. Mr. Bok was a gentle and kind teacher, he was new to the school too! At lunch, Toby spotted a student staring at him again. When Toby started eating his lunch, he felt a sudden pain at his back, he cried "Ouch!" And when he looked around to see who was hitting him, he saw a boy with glaring eyes, and a wicked grin. Toby shivered for what he had seen. The boy walked slowly to Toby arrogantly, then whispered in Toby's ear, "Who do you think you are? You think your math is good? I will show you who is the math king..." Toby stood there as still as a stone. When lunch was over, Toby was quiet. He thought to himself, " I never brag I'm good at math, why did the boy talk to me like this? Have I done anything bad to make him so angry? Who can teach me what to do?" Toby was so focus like he was deaf, he couldn't hear Mr. Bok was talking to the class. Suddenly, Toby's eyebrows raised and his heart was beating like a drum! He remembered now! He's the new student from another school... "Toby, can you give me the answer of question number three?" "Sorry, Mr. Bok, I don't know..." said Toby in a soft voice, looking at the floor. "It's okay, I can ask someone else to help. Yes, Derek!" "That's soooooooooooooo simple! The answer is one trillion thirty-eight thousand eighty six hundred ninety nine!" Derek smiled like winning a battle. "Good try Derek but I'm afraid it's wrong" said Mr. Bok. "Oh... Derek, this guy who hit me is called DEREK." Toby thought to himself. That day after school, Toby was still feeling frustrated. " Welcome home!!! Guess what I've cooked for you?!" asked Toby's mommy. But Toby didn't respond. "I've cooked Mami Noodles for you. " But Toby was not excited at all. Mommy brought out a big bowl of Mami Noodles. After Toby finished his Mami Noodles, he went to bed and fell asleep. Toby dreamed that Derek bullied the whole school. When Toby opened his eyes, he saw mommy sitting next to him. "Are you okay? Are you hungry now? You've skipped your dinner, " mommy asked. "Mommy, I... I'm so afraid, I had a nightmare about Derek!" stammered Toby. "Derek? Who's Derek? I haven't heard that name before," said mommy in a worried voice. Then Toby told mommy everything about what Derek had done on him. Mommy said "It's time for a revenge!" "Revenge? Did you say revenge mommy?" Toby's eyes almost popped out. Mommy winked her eye and said "Yes, a revenge." "Let's discuss how to teach Derek a lesson!" exclaimed mommy. They thought and thought for a long long time, but still had no idea what to do. "Oh...sorry boy, I can't think about any bad thing to do..." "Ah! Mama I know! I am good at cooking, right? What about I invite Derek to our home and I cook him a delicious dinner. Maybe he will love me after eating my yummy food!" suggested Toby. "Ooh-la-la! You are such a clever boy. I think your plan is just perfect." Mommy gave Toby a big bear hug. The next morning when Toby arrived school, he searched for Derek everywhere, but he couldn't see him. Suddenly, Derek came by and wildly pushed Toby! Toby was shocked that he cried "Ooof!!!" When Derek turned away, Toby stopped him, "Hey, bro! Do you have time tonight? Can you come to my home, please? I want to cook you a super-de-dooper yummy mozzarella ricotta risotto, plus deep-fried chicken wings in chilli sauce!" "Oh...mozzarella?! Oh Ricotta?! Ooooooh chilli sauce?!?!?! All my favourites..." thought Derek to himself, mouth watering. "OK!" said Derek happily, dancing around at the hallway. Toby was so surprised that Derek enjoyed eating as much as he did. After a happy eating and cooking that night, Toby and Derek became best friends forever. Toby realised that Derek was a great chef too! So together, they decided to sign up for the Master Chef Junior Contest. THE END
author: Benjamin Ma

title: Sol the Centipede
text: Sol the centipede laid on the grass feeling sad on a sunny day.'The frogs are playing so happily. When will I have friends like them?' he sighed The frogs have frogs,the snails have snails,the grasshoppers have grasshopers,even the centipedes have other centipedes.But Sol did not have anyone.He felt too shy to talk to anyone! 'When will Sol ever make friends!'worried Sol's parents 'Oh you worry for nothing! Sol will find his way!' said Sol's grandmother merrily The frogs,the snails,the grass hoppers and the other centipedes often thought of Sol Some said 'I wonder if Sol would like being friends with us' some thought 'If Sol talks to us we will talk to Sol' Some did not notice Sol that much! Sol cried and cried everyday 'I do not have any friends,everybody has friends,everybody needs to have friends,no one likes me maybe?' On one such rainy day Sol was sitting alone.Suddenly along the pouring drops he saw a tiny flower standing alone,smiling and shining. The flower smiled warmly at Sol and Sol smiled back. Sol gathered some courage and asked the flower 'Dont you get bored by yourself?Standing alone?Where are your friends?' 'Hello there!I do get bored sometimes but mostly I don't. It is nice to stand in the rain like this.I like looking at the sun and the butterflies.Often I sing by myself.I like it a lot!' 'The Sun greets me,the Bee and I hangout,the grasshopper drops by too at times.It's fun.' But it is also fun when I am by myself!' Sol that day heard something that he had not heard before.He felt something he had not felt before.He saw something he had not seen before.He looked at the sun that stood by itself,the huge tree and the tiny butterfly. Sol looked at himself.He looked at his tiny hundred legs that could take him anywhere.He moved around looking with wide eyes at the things that he had never seen.How refreshing the rain felt,how sweet was the smell of the soil,how swiftly he could move! Slowly slowly Sol started doing things by himself.'It is fun to be by myself sometimes 'he thought. There were days when Sol got bored and there were days when Sol just stood at one place happily looking at the flowers,the snail,the sky. One day Sol was taking a stroll when he noticed a tiny frog looking at it with curious eyes.Sol looked at the frog and smiled warmly at it.The frog smiled back! What do you think happened next?
author: Pallavi Raikar

title: My Best Friend The Cat
text: I had a cute cat. Her name was lucy. She was my best friend. One day my Grandma came, she had a dog. The dog was very angry when it came to my house. It started to chase Lucy. Meanwhile, it got dark and Lucy climbed and hid on the tree and the dog also got tired searching Lucy. It slept under the same tree. Lucy was also tired and she started Meowing Lucy very quietly climbed down the tree and tip toed into the home. we both slept together. Grandma took her dog with her.

title: The Mysterious egg
text: Once upon a time there were three friends. Shalu the elephant,Sara the deer and Sana the monkey. They played and had fun under the Rosewood tree from dawn to dusk. The Rosewood tree was a home to many parrots. The parrots could be heard gurgling, whistling, trilling and squawking. The parrots made nests and laid eggs. They too enjoyed to see Shalu, Sana and Sara having fun throughout the day. One day the friends found an egg lying below the tree. The egg had cracked and the chick was pushing out itself. The three friends watched the tiny birdie sqweking. The friends did not know whose chick it was. They thought of taking it to their friend Pok the peacock. Sana the monkey lead the way jumping and shooing the other animals and making way for Shalu. Shalu the elephant carefully tucked the birdie in it trunk and marched fast towards Pok's nest. On their way to Pok's nest, the wise Eagle who sat on the Sal tree and halted Shalu. Sara narrated the episode of the mysterious egg and told that they had decided to leave the birdie with Pok the peacock. The Eagle offered help and asked them to leave the birdie with him. Where are you three heading in such a haste? Poppy the parrot returned to her nest in the evening and found an egg missing in the nest. She was worried and asked the three friends if they had seen her egg. The friends told Poppy thet they had found an egg that hatched.Not knowing about its parents they had left the with the Eagle. Poppy was worried that Eagle would eat the birdie. The friends rushed to the Eagle. The Eagle was just about to eat the birdie. Shalu the Elephant pushed the Sal tree and down came the Eagle. Thud......!!!!! fell the Eagle The birdie slipped out of the Eagle's claws and flung in the air. Sana the monkey jumped Wooo...............ahhhhhh!!!!!! it shouted lound and caught the birdie. Sara the deer ran to Poppy the parrot and informed that they had save her birdie. Poppy hurriedly came flying to Shalu. Trill............ trill.................... she cried. Shalu had curled the birdie in her trunk. Shalu walked to the Rosewood tree and placed the birdie safely in Poppy's nest. Poppy thanked the three friends. squawk.....squawk........ squawk.....squawk........ They were happy that the mystery of the unknown egg had been solved and the birdie had reached its nest.
author: Shalini Mahapatra

title: Lost tooth
text: Once there lived a little girl named Tina. She lived with her mom and dad. Her mom and dad were very proud of their daughter as she was helpful, kind and well-mannered. In Tina's class there was a girl who was acquisitive and rude named Meena. One day Meena's tooth broke, on the other hand even Tina's tooth broke. Both them were delighted as they could give their tooth to the tooth fairy and get gifts. Also they wanted to keep their tooth safe. Meena wanted more teeth to break so that she could get more gifts. After a while Meena saw Tina in a purple t-shirt thinking how to keep her tooth safe,Meena decided to steal Tina's tooth. She stayed back from P.E (physical education) with an excuse of headache. She searched the whole class for Tina's tooth, she even searched in Tina's backpack, but she did not find the tooth. That day she came for a sleepover at Tina's home and stole her tooth. She wasn't aware that god was watching her. God told everything to tooth fairy. He asked tooth fairy to not give any gift to Meena and show the footage to her parents as well as the school teachers. God also told to give two special gifts to Tina. Next morning Meena got ready in her yellow and orange dress when Meena's parents opened the T.V they saw the footage. At school the principle found the footage on his table and he showed it to the whole school. Meena was very sorry on what she had done. No one wanted to sit near her or be her friend except Tina who was still polite and kind to Meena. even after what she had done. Do you know what the gift was for Tina? It was two kits in which you can make inventions for disabled people. Tina loved the gifts. She loved the gift as it was crafty and helpful.

title: Grandma Goes Cuckoo!
text: I had never met Grandma. Mother said she lived far away. It took two planes, a bus and a three-hour car ride to get to her home. We were too small to travel so far and Grandma seldom left her home. Her home was on the outskirts of a forest, nestled among large acorn trees. Squirrels by the dozens hopped outside all day, their bushy tails upright and lightly swaying in the breeze. The home itself looked like a tree: every inch of it covered with evil ivy that grew in all directions. Grandma had a pair of scissors tucked away in her housecoat at all times so she could snip it away, lest it cover the doors and windows and permanently lock Grandma in. But when you stepped inside her home, a feeling of warmth and safety greeted you: bright yellow walls, a slow crackle at the fireplace, handpicked orchids in every room and the smell of chocolate chip cookies “because Grandma is always baking”. This is how Mother always ended the description of the home she grew up in – Ivyhouse, Acornwood, PO Box 1001. Mother said that Grandma was like a teacher to all those around her. There was a large community of loggers that lived in Acornwood, who felled trees, cut them and carried them in trucks to big markets where it was traded for currency, grains, vegetables and poultry. Grandma taught the loggers how to count so they could get a good bargain in the markets. She showed their wives how to stock grains to make them last all year. And she taught their children good manners by explaining verses from the Bible. She had just one daughter, my Mother, and schooled her at home. Science lessons in the kitchen, Mathematics in the backyard, English on the rug near the fireplace, and Art under the largest acorn tree! When Mother grew big, Grandma and Grandpa decided to send her to the city to study. Soon after college, Mother got married and settled down in an even bigger city far away from Acornwood. Some time ago, Grandpa died suddenly of a heart attack. Grandma stopped going out of the house altogether, in the hope that Grandpa would come home unannounced someday. But before he could walk in again through those doors snipped clear of ivy, Grandma died too. The loggers found her on the kitchen table of her home. There was a platter of chocolate chip cookies cooling beside her. Mother left for Acornwood right away, and when she got back she shut herself up in her room all week. She didn’t have breakfast, returned her barely-eaten lunch and had to be coaxed by Father to have dinner. When Tina, our cook, tiptoed to Mother’s room every evening to give her her dinner, we could hear Mother sobbing. Not words or wails; just a persistent sob like a drizzle that mists window panes on a gloomy day. Then one day, weeks after Grandma had baked her last set of cookies, we finally saw her! We got back from school to see her picture hanging right where the cuckoo clock had been. Oh, that cuckoo! It always seemed to have a reason to come out and prance every hour. Mother had finally caged that happy bird and stowed the clock away. Grandma had large black eyes like Mother’s. Her cheeks were hollow as if someone had scooped out ice-cream from them. Her nose was sharp like our strict headmistress. It was good to see Grandma's face every morning before going to school and after coming back. It seemed like she was with us all the time. A week after Grandma made her way into our living room, a funny thing happened. I had been sitting at the dining table all afternoon after school, solving rather difficult problems on fractions. No one was home: Mother was away at a friend's house, Tina had gone to the market, and Aroon was at the park. “ Stop biting your nails!” said a hoarse old woman's voice that I had never heard before. I looked up and all around me. The voice continued “Do you know harmful bacteria like to make tiny homes under your nails? When you eat them they make even bigger ones in your tummy, keeping you up all night” It was Grandma! I looked at the frame. It had turned hazy at the edges and Grandma’s face in it was animated like it is in the movies. As she spoke, the fine lines on her forehead became deeper and her cheeks more hollow. Her eyes though seemed kinder. When she finished speaking, as if by magic, she formed back into a flat picture. Her thin lips that had been moving up and down a second ago, formed into a smile once again. The frame too went back to being hard and sharp-edged from its earlier hazy state. I checked my watch - it was 4:00 pm sharp. I shook my head and continued to do my homework. But as time passed, I realized I had not been day-dreaming. Whether I was watching my favourite cartoon on TV or lying on the couch reading Harry Potter or secretly trying out Mother’s nail paint, Grandma was quick to catch me. “Watching TV like that will spoil your eyes! You will be able to see a pin right in front of you but not a ball coming at you from far. You will have to wear spectacles all your life” “Read the Bible! Every verse unfolds a different kind of mystery that Harry and Voldemort together won’t be able to solve” “Nothing in this world can be hidden, young lady! Better to tell your Mother straight up than to make her sniff it out of you.” It seemed that all her lessons were meant for me because no one else in the room heard them. Aroon spilled his milk over the rug but continued to play with his toy cars. Mother lied down on the couch while watching her favourite soap opera. No one was alarmed. Grandma only picked me. And she spoke every hour! Like the cuckoo clock. Without fail. “I see that you help your little brother with his homework. Good girl! Always remember that only by helping others will we learn how to help ourselves” No, I had not dared to tell Mother. She would scold me. Worse, she would cry. How can you joke about your Grandma, she would say. She was still sad about Grandma. We would often see that faraway look in Mother's eyes when Aroon and I giggled together on the dinner table. Or that time when she walked away from the living room when a show on National Geographic channel showed a tiger playing with its cubs. And once when Aroon thoughtlessly asked Tina to bake him some chocolate chip cookies I thought Mother would burst into tears again. I decided I would rather listen to Grandma’s hourly sermons than make Mother sadder. Grandma, on the other hand, continued with all her might. She spoke louder and longer. I could see more expressions on her face now. Like when she was really mad at me her forehead would crumple up like paper. And when she cracked a joke I could see the hint of a dimple on her hollow cheeks and hear a tiny chuckle at the end of her sermon. “Hey, you Cinderella! Where do you think you’re going leaving your shoes behind? Put them back or someone may slip. And it won’t be your knight in shining armour, mind you!" Grandma laughed as she said this. ﻿Then just as it had begun, it stopped too all of a sudden. I got back from school one day just before 2:00 pm. I carefully put my shoes on the rack, lest Grandma reproach me. I waited for a minute or two, then five, but didn’t hear a whisper. Happy that I had finally silenced Grandma, I strode into my room. But at 6:00 pm I walked into the living room again blowing a bubble gum. It irritated Mother to no end when I did this. And I knew Grandma wouldn’t be too far behind. I kept blowing till the gum resembled a pink tennis ball right near my face. I gave a final blow and it snapped right on my face! A sticky mess that covered my nose and cheeks. It took me an hour to remove bits of the gum plastered all over my face. But when I was done with all the cleaning, I realized that Grandma hadn’t said a word. I went back to the living room and stared at the frame for long. Grandma continued to look straight at me unblinking. I stuck my tongue out at Grandma. She didn’t find it funny at all and remained like the lake on a calm summer’s day. Was Grandma upset with me, I wondered. Or had she managed to make her grand daughter a good mannered girl finally? I had to agree that by way of her short hourly lessons, I had learnt a lot of good habits. A few days later, I heard Mother sobbing all over again. She had been on a cleaning spree, and a fling of the duster had brought Grandma’s picture crashing down. When I got back from school, the cuckoo clock had been put back on the wall, and Grandma's picture was placed on the mantelpiece underneath. For days, I waited for the cuckoo clock to do its dance hoping to hear Grandma’s voice. But Grandma remained quiet and at peace. I missed Grandma, but was happy that I had got a chance to know her though I had never met her. And I’m sure somewhere she was glad to have found an obedient grand daughter in me.
author: Gayatri Hingorani

title: Dino in the house
text: It was six in the evening and Ravi was walking back to his house with his friend, Mohan. They had finished their exam's and were walking home which was a couple of kilometers away from their tution and they had to pass through a forest. while they were in the forest the heard a loud wail and they ran towards the sound and at the sight they found something which Mohan fainted after seeing. It was a..................................... A mother Dinosaur was wailing and was half dead. There was an egg right next to it. The mother dinosaur breathed her last breath. Mohan just woke up from his shock and told Ravi," Buddy! do you see what I see? Ms. Malhotra taught us that dino's were extinct long ago." "Apparently not," said Ravi with his eyes still glued at the mother dinosaur."I think we should take the egg with us Mohan" said Ravi with concern in his eyes. "yes! you are right" said Moh an. Then they heard the hatching of the egg and they were watching closely. Then a few second later, came a baby dinosaur from the egg. The baby dinosaur was blue in color. It was nearly one foot tall with a long tongue and blunt teeth compared to the mother dinosaur. Ravi and Mohan ran home holding the younger dinosaur which was quite heavy, they quickly took him home, hid him in the basement of Ravi's house and Mohan took off to his house and came back with his sister Mina. Mina was as suprised as Mohan when he saw the dinosaur for the first time. She asked Ravi and Mohan where the found him and whether their parents knew. Ravi's parents were very strict and so were Mohan's parents.."absolutely not, they won't agree to pet him. We are keeping him a secret". The three of them decided to make the Dino their pet and they will feed him at regular intervals with their own pocket money. They decided to name him Tommy. Since they wanted to keep Tommy a secret, they took him for walks very early in the morning or late at night. The dinosaur grew very quickly and the children started running out of pocket money. After a few months, it grew very big to keep in the basement and when it grew 7 feet, Mohan thought that we should take him to the jungle and play there with him because the city was to dangerous for them as they may be spotted and Tommy would be killed. They played in the forest hoping it would make a difference, but unfortunately a group of archaeologists found Tommy and reported it to the the main branch. The following day it was on the newspaper, but the kids tore the news paper so that they do not know about Tommy. They had to part with Tommy to save him. ﻿﻿﻿ ﻿ The kids had a long debate on whether Tommy should leave, Mina was on the verge of tears but Ravi and Mohan convinced her that it was for Tommy. They started moving towards the jungle with Tommy sneakily and quickly. Right then came a cop who started shooting at Tommy but it did not have an effect on Tommy he broke the policeman's car and the kids stopped the cop from shooting Tommy and proceeded to the jungle. Bade him goodbye to save and start Tommy's new life. they had tears in their eyes and they had only one picture in their mind. it ﻿was of
