author: Giteshwari Gujar
illustrator: Kusha Kumar Barik; Sugrib Kumar Juanga

title: Crow and her friends
text: There once lived a crow and her friends who were always happy. But they are now sad because of the rain. The wind and rain had destroyed their nest. The crow went to an old Mango Tree. Crow: Can we build our nest in this tree? Mango Tree: Lucky me! Now I won't have to be alone here. Crow: So shall I bring all my friends here? Mango Tree: Yes. Bring them. Everybody came and built their nest in the tree. One day a woodcutter came to the forest. Everybody got scared. But the crow thought of an idea. She went to the snake living under tree for help. She told the snake " If the woodcutter cut this Mango tree, even you wont have a house to live in". "So what should I do?" the snake asked. "When the woodcutter comes tomorrow, you should bite him" said the crow. Next day, the woodcutter came with an axe to cut the tree. According the Crow's plan the snake bit him. " Oh my God. a snake bit me. I am never coming back to this place." Saying this the woodcutter ran from the forest.
author: Smruti Harindran
illustrator: Greystroke; Priya Kuriyan; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Vinayak Varma

title: The Magic Scents!
text: The sun peered from its nest and smiled so bright that the land of Chirpur bloomed with so much joy. Children were frolicking,Men were working in their fields while the women went to the pond nearby to get some water. The king wants us to supply 1000 potatoes to the palace tomorrow let's start our work right away! The town seemed as a place where nothing could go wrong,but alas this peaceful town was ruled by a king greedier than a pack of pigs! King Jamun,the ruler of the land was always in search of treasure. Gold,Silver,Diamond,Ruby,Sapphires and more were used to decorate every bit of the royal palace. One night, when the king was in his royal chamber, he couldn't resist the beauty of the moon and decided to take a stroll down by the garden. As he was passing by the orchids, he caught the scent of something delightful. The king was mesmerised! He ought to have a perfume made by that scent. The next morning, the king made a proclamation.He announced that the person who entraps the mystical aroma into an evergreen perfume will recieve 1000 gold coins! This left behind a baffled crowd of ministers and courtiers... 1000 gold coins! The king has lost it! The village is surely going to lose all its money in this goosechase! What are we going to do!? 1000 GOLD COINS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! A fortnight later, came an old woman with a large black bag claiming to possess the worlds most magical scents in it. And when she opened the bag lo and behold were bottles of every shape and colour. Some were thin and some were thick, some with red,some with blue and some were even spotted. the kings jaw dropped in awe at the very sight! The king asked to buy every single one of the woman's perfumes.But, he was in for a suprise when the total count came up to 250000!!! The king nearly fainted, the ministers let out cries of surprise and they all began the search for the king's missing scent... But alas, the king couldn't find his scent...he went through every bottle from the woman's bag but still couldn't find what he desired most in the world. That's when he heard a booming yet crippled voice, the voice of the old woman.. NO! No! NO! WHERE IS MY SCENT?? Uhhh..Maharaj, There aren't anymore perfume bottles left. 'O king, your greed has overturned your wisdom..that scent you smelled was purely an illusion to show you how illogical and immoral your judgement has become..' The king was in tears and promised to refine his ways, a few years later the town of Chirpur became well known only and only for its perfume business, with their top brand being 'The Magic Scents"! O King, your greediness knows no bounds! For once, pay attention to your kingdom and its people! They are the REAL TREASURE Thank You Grandma.. You fixed our king...
author: Mahathi And Smruthi Sathish
illustrator: Beatrice Clearwater; Bindia  Thapar; Nancy Raj; Priyankar Gupta; Vusi  Malindi

title: The pub g addict
text: There was a boy named johny who was 9 years old and was in 4th.When ever he comes from school he sits in front of computer and start playing pub g. one day his friend fell from the stairs and he started revive and everyone started laughing on him and he started hitting every one.And all of them complaint the teacher. The teacher told to principal johnson. And he called johny and scold him. But still he hit everyone.So he was resticated. His mother scold him but still he played pub g.His father got transferred to Mumbai and he joined a new school.On the second day of the school teacher was teaching that we should not play games tab,mobile and computer but johny started shouting 'pub g zindabad' and he got last warning to be suspend but not told his mother that he got last warning from school to be suspend. One day a teacher saw him fighting with Rohan and got suspend but still didn't told to his parents, they thought that he was going to school but he was in a park near the school. He was enjoying riding of slides with other children & then he saw his father in that park only. He ran and hide behind the bushes. One child came & ask him why you are hiding behind the bushes. His father saw him that he is hiding himself behind the bushes. His father scold him and take him to his house. His mother saw his coming with his father. She asked his father about the ma matter. His father told her mother whole story. Then they asked Johny why he was in the park. He told them that he was suspend from school for one week due to fighting with Rohan. His parents advised him not to play PUB G game as all this problem occurred due to PUB G Only. He promised his parents that he will never play PUB G again. He become a good boy & never played PUB G again.
author: Mannatveer Singh
illustrator: Deepa Akilan; HRISHIKESH WAGLE; Joanna  Mendes; Rijuta Ghate

title: You can make the change- Break the chain of corona
text: There is quiet all around the Earth. The coronavirus pandemic is spreading fear among the people. Whole world is locked out to fight against coronavirus. Everyone is advised to stay home. But Suman is getting bored. Ahum..ahum..! hacchhuu! Suman has cold since two days. After spending whole day cleaning at home, she wants to step out in the evening to buy some noodles. She wants to eat just noodles tonight. At the shop, unknowingly she is carrying the coronavirus and infects the shopkeeper lady. She returns home. She cooks the food and eats while watching TV. OH, NO! She touched her mouth while yawning as she is sleepy. The virus is now spread to her body. Next morning, after waking up, she makes the tea. WHAT!? NO TOASTS! She can’t drink tea without her toasts. She takes the bag and gets ready to go to buy the toasts. She doesn’t know but she is carrying the virus with her. She purchases a pack of toast and gives the money to the shopkeeper. While waiting to get the change, viruses are again left on the grocery table. The other customers come and carry the virus with them one by one. They too get infected and the cycle continues. Imagine, what would have happened if Suman would have stayed home. Would the cycle of the virus have continued? So friends, still do we have need reasons, or say excuses, to step out of home? Avoid going out unnecessarily. BREAK THE CHAIN. Save lives. This is the service you can do to the mankind, to your country and to the whole world by just staying home. Let's defeat corona. This is our duty. Join hands to break the chain of corona. Stay home, stay safe! We have got only one life, let's give it a chance!
author: Riddhi Nath

title: The Clever Crow
text: Once upon a time there was a crow. He was very intelligent. On one sunny day, after flying in the sky for a very long time, he became thirsty. While he was flying, he saw a pot under a tree. He flew fast and sat next to the pot. With hope of finding water the crow looked inside the pot. He saw that the pot is filled half with water. He tried drinking water using his beak but he was not able to reach the water. He started looking around and that's when he saw a straw lying on the ground. The crow had a clever idea. He picked up the straw and put it in the water. He drank water using the straw. After quenching his thirst he flew away happily.
author: Smruti Harindran
illustrator: Eswari; Jibin Mohan; Shailja Jain Chougule

title: The wise Frog
text: Once upon a time, a group of frogs were playing outside there houses. Suddenly, a snake, who was very hungry, came to attack and eat them. The frogs got scared, and started jumping here and there. A wise frog who was sitting very far with his grand son was looking at what was happening. He told his grand son "The snake can be beaten if all the frog come together and attack him. But no one is brave enough to go against him.". The wise frog looking at the beautiful flowers thought 'The world sure is beautiful, but it needs to become a little more brave and fight for themselves'.
author: Smruti Harindran

title: The Laddoo Code
text: One morning, in Class 2B... “Psst, Anjali! Pass this note to Ritvik,” whispers Rahul. Anjali passes the note to Madhu. Madhu passes it to Anwar. Anwar passes it to Sanya. And Sanya passes it to Ritvik. Ritvik reads the note – Nani made laddoos! Meet me behind the canteen. But Anjali, Madhu, Anwar and Sanya have read it too. “Laddoos!” “Oh no, I don’t think we’re getting any...” Everyone jumps on the laddoos. Soon, there are no laddoos left. The next day… “Anjali, pass this to Ritvik, na?” Anjali tries to read the note again, but can’t understand it. Madhu can’t read it either. Neither can Anwar. Nor can Sanya. But Ritvik knows exactly how to read it. Ritvik wraps the strip of paper around his pencil, just the way Rahul did when he wrote it. And the secret message is revealed! Making and Breaking the Code Rahul converts his message into a secret code so that no one else can read it. This method of protecting information is called encryption. Ritvik wraps Rahul’s note around his pencil to reveal the message. This method of changing encrypted information back into plain text is called decryption. Computers also use encryption and decryption to keep information safe. Want to send secret messages like Rahul and Ritvik? Wrap a strip of paper around a pencil and write your message on the wrapped paper. Then unwrap the paper and give it to your friend. Your friend can read the secret message by wrapping the paper around another pencil.
author: Saksham Arora

title: Caterpillar Looks for a Shoe
text: It hurts her foot to walk without it. “May I borrow a shoe from you, Spider?” But Spider's shoe is too small. Caterpillar is sad without her shoe. She goes to Frog. “May I borrow a shoe from you, Frog?” But Frog’s shoe is too big. She goes to Grasshopper. “May I borrow a shoe from you, Grasshopper?” But Grasshopper’s shoe is too scratchy. She goes to Crab. “May I borrow a shoe from you, Crab?” But Crab’s shoes are used for digging. They are too sharp for walking! Caterpillar is too tired to search any more. She curls up on a leaf to rest. Caterpillar decides to make a cosy cocoon to sleep in. Days pass by. And when Caterpillar steps out of her cocoon... She doesn't need shoes any more!
author: Pashmina Mohile

title: Shall we play, baby brother?
text: Oh, dear brother my little brother, Shall we play with the ball? Let me show you how to throw or do you like it to roll? "Booo boo boo" The little hands grab the ball And to the mouth it goes. No! no! dear, It is not the juicy plum. It is not for you to slurp. Oh dear brother my little brother, Shall we play with the xylophone? Let me play you music And will you sing a tune? "Baaa Baa Baa" The little hands pick the mallet And to the mouth it goes. No! no! dear, It is not the lollipop. It is not for you to suck and sip. Oh dear brother my little brother, Shall we play with flash cards? Let me show you one by one Or will you choose one? "Dooo Doo Doo" The little hands take a card And to the mouth it goes. No! no! dear, It is not a biscuit. It is not to taste. Oh dear brother, my little brother, Shall we have lunch? Let me get you a carrot stick Sure you like to munch. "Aaah Aaah Aaah" The little hands pick the carrot And goes rat-a-tat-tat. No! No! dear, It is not a drumstick. It is not to beat but to eat! ACTIVITY Would you play with Ball OR Plum? Would you eat a Carrot OR Mallet?
author: Saranya Padmakumar
illustrator: Alicia  van Zyl; Herminder Ohri; Josh Morgan; Kavitha Mandana; Kobie Nieuwoudt; Mary Anne Hampton; Natalie Hinrichsen; Nirzara Verulkar; Ntembiso  Velemane; Rajiv Eipe; Sanjay Kisku; Sinomonde Ngwane; Tamsin Hinrichsen

title: My brother Anshu
text: I am Lavanya and he is my brother Anshu. He loves me. I miss him a lot. He plays with me. We love our toys. We both have some dinner together. After that we both watch chota bheem. And Chota bheem is our favourite cartoon. After that we have a sleep over with our toys.

title: Let's walk with Tiny Ant
text: I am your tiny friend Ant. I am hoping all of your are fine. Come let go outside and take a walk. Oh its morning already! Let's go outside and take a walk. Wow! The nature is so beautiful. Let's sing. Let's dance. Let's all play together. This beautiful nature is providing us with so many types of delicious food. Lets all eat the sweet fruit from this tree and sleep for sometime. Wow! All I want to do is look at the beauty of the nature and live happily forever.

title: Lion and Elephant
text: One day many animals were drinking water near the lake. The Lion and Elephant saw that there was no place for them to stand and drink the water. So the Lion thought of an idea. He roared very loudly. All the animals got scared and started running here and there. The Elephant and the Lion drank all the water the wanted. Then the friends happily went back to their homes.
author: Smruti Harindran

title: On the Metro
text: “Get up, Zeba! We are going to see the Qutab Minar!” Abbu nudges me awake. “Is Ammi coming too?” I ask. “Maybe she will join us later.” “How are we going, Abbu?” “We’ll take the Metro,” he says. A man in a suit and dark glasses is in a hurry to get to the platform. “Excuse me!” he says. “Excuse me!” And he bounds up the moving stairs. We roll up, up, up on these stairs and I feel as though they might gobble me up. In our village, we don’t have stairs like these. When the train arrives at the platform, I try to catch a glimpse of the driver. The shiny doors slide open. Whoosh! Whoosh! How do the doors know when to open and when to shut? Abbu and I enter the compartment. It is cold. Brrrr brrr. “The doors are closing,” says a voice. The train is like a long, hollow, silver snake. Silver seats and silver pillars and silver rails to hold on to. A nani sitting across from us is fast asleep. Her head rests on the shoulder of a man reading a newspaper. He smiles and doesn’t wake her up. The train begins to move. “Abbu, look at that big glass building. It’s so tall. The people going up and down and across inside it look like ants. Is the Qutab Minar taller than this?” I ask. “I hope so!” Abbu laughs. In the village, Param has the tallest house. It has five floors. But this looks much, much taller. Beep. Beep. The doors are opening. Is that a jungle, in the middle of the city? It’s just like the one near our village! “Didn’t you come here with your friends and teachers from school?” Abbu asks. Yes, now I remember. My friends, teachers and I came here. We brought slogans, banners and posters with us. We also sang songs. “Save Earth, save trees, save me!” my poster read. A squirrel ate peanuts out of my palm. Beep. Beep. The doors are opening. Whoosh! Whoosh! A group of girls enter. They giggle and chat. I think they are friends. One has blue hair! And many earrings. She even has a ring on her pierced lower lip. One of them is carrying a guitar. Beep. Beep. The doors are opening. Whoosh! Whoosh! Some more people get in. “Look at that!” A little boy points to a big, yellow palace zooming past. It looks grand. I wonder who lived there. Next time, I will take Abbu and Ammi to explore it. Beep. Beep. The doors are opening. Whoosh! Whoosh! “Look, Abbu, the cars are not moving! There is a traffic jam.” “That’s why we take the Metro, Zeba,” Abbu replies. An aeroplane flies overhead. The cars crawl below, on the criss-crossing flyovers. We are zooming past, somewhere between the sky and the earth. Whoosh! Whoosh! Some people get off but more get in. Everyone moves a little, shifts a little. Now there is just enough space for everyone. I hear so many voices, speaking in so many languages. A lady with a baby enters and there is nowhere for her to sit. Abbu offers her his seat. Day abruptly turns to night. We are underground. I can see reflections in the glass. This looks like a secret tunnel with lots of pipes and wires along the walls. A man who has been on the phone for a long time yells, “Hello? Helloooo? Hellooooo?” Has his phone stopped working? Beep. Beep. The doors are opening. Whoosh! Whoosh! The lights blink. “I am going to the driver’s cabin,” I say. I get off and run. “Slow down!” Abbu exclaims, hurrying. “Salaam aleikum, Ammi!” Ammi is in her spotless white uniform. And her white cap. “Walekum assalam, Zeba.” There are dozens of knobs and buttons. I wonder how Ammi remembers which ones to press. “Are you coming with us?” I ask her. She nods. She presses a button. The doors slide open and she gets out. “Ammi, you drove so well. It was fast and smooth and there were no bumps, and you waited for everyone to get on before you went ahead.” Ammi laughs and hugs me. “When I grow up, I want to be just like you,” I tell her. I hope the uniforms are silver and shiny by then. Just like the Metro!” Then we walk to the Qutab Minar. Ammi, Abbu and I.
author: Neha Singh

title: Ella and her dog, Fluffy
text: One day at Wolfheart city in England, Ella and her dog, Fluffy Went to the beach to take a walk. The willow trees were swaying slowly, the birds were chirping peacefully, the happy noises of children and adults playing, the cool breeze of the peaceful wind, and the smell of the ocean. Ella watched as Fluffy barked as joyfully as she could be. While Ella was walking on the beach,Ella smelled a pleasant smell that caused her tummy to grumble. She smelled the strong smell of chocolate ice cream and the fresh smell of strawberry ice cream. Immediately, Ella walked towards the ice cream truck. When she was in the queue,Ella pulled out her wallet and counted how many money she had. Ella decided to buy a double scoop. When it was Ella’s turn, she accidentally dropped Fluffy’s leash and Fluffy ran off as fast as a racing car! Ella shouted despreatly “Come back, Fluffy!” Unfortunately, Fluffy could not hear Ella and even ran faster! But with no choice, Ella snatched her money back that she had given to the ice cream vendor. Afterwards, Ella whispered to the person behind her in the queue “I can let you go first.” After saying that word, Ella started to search for Fluffy. Ella asked every person walking by, “Have you seen my dog?” Most of the people shook their heads. Finally, Ella came across an old women with green glasses. Ella asked the same question that she asked everyone else, the women replied back “what colour is that dog?”At that time, Ella’s heart was filled with joy and she leaped into the air. Ella thought, “this women must have seen my dog.” Ella replied, “ My dog is white with green eyes.” But to her disappointment,the women replied, “I wish I could help you.” A shiver of disappointment went down to her spine and Ella nodded sadly. It was midday by now, so Ella went to the police station and asked the police, “Have you seen my dog called Fluffy? She has green eyes and white fur all over her body. “One of the policeman replied, “Yes, the dog is now here. “ Ella’s heart leaped with joy. Out came Fluffy. Tears of joy rolled down Ella’s cheek. Ella sobbed and hugged Fluffy tightly around her arms, “ You made me so worried about you!” Said Ella. The police told Ella, “Fluffy came to the police station, here because she knows that she is lost and she does not know how to go home, so she came here. Ella asked, “how did Fluffy come to the police station, here? “ The police answered, “It was near the beach. “Ella turned around and said to Fluffy, “You are so smart!! “ And the police led them to the EXIT. After this adventure, what adventure will they come across?? I am so curious to find out!!! THE END
author: Allie  Cheung

title: Mary's First Skating Lesson
text: “I’m so excited about my first skating lesson!” exclaimed Mary with a big smile. She talked and talked and talked to her mom until they arrived at the skating school. In full skating gear, Mary was ready to meet Coach Jim. “This is gonna be fun,” mumbled Mary to herself. Coach Jim held Mary’s hand. She was shivering as they stepped into the skating rink. Coach Jim grabbed a chair nearby and showed Mary step-by-step how to slide on the slippery ice. He advised, “Remember, don’t let go of the chair! Don’t walk. Slide!” But Mary was not quite listening. She was attracted by a beautiful girl who was swirling on the ice, a bit far away from her. “Wow, she’s so good!” thought Mary. Suddenly, Mary’s hands slipped and she fell onto the cold, hard ice. “Ouch!” she cried in pain, “My knees!” Tears were rolling down her face like raindrops on a windowpane. “I wanna go home,” whined Mary. She bit her lips and refused to stand back up. Moments later, Mary stopped crying. Coach Jim asked with a friendly smile, “Do you want to rest on the chair?” This time, Mary did not refuse. Sitting on the chair, she began to feel bored. She looked up and saw her mom waving at her outside the skating rink. “Oh, Mommy is watching me. I think I can show her what a good learner I can be,” so she waved back merrily and said to Coach Jim, “I think I’m ready now!” When Mary’s mom picked her up, she hugged her and asked with a sweet voice, “How was your first skating lesson, honey?" Mary had a big grin on her face. “It was a good start. I fell down but I stood back up.” “I’m so proud of you!” “You’ll be even prouder when I become the best skater in my school!” Mary giggled.
author: Carrie Man

title: A Girl Called Cheeku
text: Sen Pillai Cheeku is not too big Or too small. She's not too short Or too tall. She doesn't talk a lot, Or play too long. But Cheeku always speaks up When she sees something wrong. title: Cricket Prayer

title: You go, I'll sing my song!
text: This is a story of two birds. Listen carefully to all their words. One was a sparrow, the other a crow. One lived above, the other below. Everyday they said hello! While the sparrow was action pack, the crow needed to pick up the slack. One day, dark clouds filled the sky. The crow heard the sparrow sigh. " Dear Crow, its going to rain. Will you join me to gather some grain?" Together we can search as a pair, And we will have enough to share. The crow shook his shiny head and without even waking up he said, " You go now, and we can meet. Some bread and butter, I shall eat. Cool water, I need to sip. In the lake, I will take a dip. On a green branch, I'll sing my song. Caw, Caw, come sing along. " The sparrow understood his game, But remained set in her aim. Without any rest, she filled her plate, Back home, she called her mate. " Dear crow, I have brought the food. Come help me clean it, if you are in the mood." The crow yawned, before he did respond. " You go now, and we can meet. Some bread and butter, I shall eat. Cool water, I need to sip. In the lake I will take a dip. On a green branch, I'll sing my song. Caw, Caw, come sing along. " The sparrow went back to her nest, to clean the grain, she did her best. Again, at the crow, she glanced And decided to give him another chance. She patiently knocked at his door, As she had done many times before. " You go now, and we can meet. Some bread and butter, I shall eat. Cool water, I need to sip. In the lake, I will take a dip. On a green branch, I'll sing my song. Caw, Caw, come sing along. " The rain poured with all its might, It did not stop in the day or at night. The hungry crow now awoke, He flew around the trees of oak. The bird in black did not succeed. He could find no grain nor oat nor seed. Famished, he approached the sparrow. Hoping she would share what was in her barrow. " Dear sister, I know you care. Do you have any grain to spare? " The sparrow heard his helpless plea. This was her true moment of glee. " You go now, and we can meet. Some bread and butter, I shall eat. Cool water, I need to sip. In the lake, I will take a dip. On a green branch, I'll sing my song. Chi, Chi, come sing along. "
author: Jazreen Deboo

title: Little Nyasa - A better Tomorrow
text: Before she could reach for her spear, Nyasa collapsed. The shadow of the dead piranha was her last memory. The silt gradually deposited by the Zui Mui river had given form and shape to its banks. The Hazanga tribe was enchanted by the banks. They moved from the nearby lands and decided to settle down there. The Chief of the river dwellers was Onwas. A red bellied piranha had the sharpest teeth and strongest jaw among all the fish in that river. When the tribe decided to make the riverbank, their home, they had to be safe. They had to be safe to catch fish. Fish that would feed them, and, earn some money for them. So, Onwas threw a spear and brought an end to the notorious piranha. Onwas had a seven-year-old daughter at home. Her name was Nyasa. But as they say, everything comes with a price. Nyasa was the one affected. When her father killed the piranha, a shadow of the dead fish emerged from it. The dead fish’s shadow cursed Onwas. It said, “You killed me today. I will make sure that the one you love the most will not live for long either.” Before Onwas could rush back home to protect his family, his people, the doom had struck. Nyasa was playing outside her house. Suddenly, she spotted the sun being devoured by a giant shadow. The shadow had a tail like a fish and when she moved her gaze, her eyes spotted the fins and her hand moved in reflex. She wanted to put up a brave fight. However, the piranha’s shadow caught her before she could attack it. When Onwas reached home, he heard from his people what had happened. They said, Nyasa was cast a spell by the frightening shadow. Soon enough, the spell had turned Nyasa into rock. Onwas was overcome with grief. His family was still mourning when a little turtle crawled up to their doorstep. It was no ordinary turtle. It could talk. It told Onwas that he could get his daughter back if he promised never to harm any water creature in the river or adjoining lakes anymore. The turtle also asked for two tear drops from Nyasa. Onwas promised on behalf of himself and his entire tribe to be the protector of all water bodies in that region. The tribe also pledged to change their occupation to farming. Very soon, Nyasa came back into life from being a rock. Nyasa became emotional on seeing her family and two crystal tears appeared in her eyes. Onwas spared no moment in collecting them in a clay tumbler and handed it over to the turtle. The turtle smiled and said, “From tomorrow, these tears will take the form of two lakes. Lake Nyasa and Lake Nungwi. To remind every human that aquatic life is precious. It is as precious as any human life. Peaceful co-existence is a must for a better tomorrow.”
author: Naisha Kalpavraksh

title: The Fast
text: I am out on my walk with my mumma. " Hey Guggi, are you up early today?", asked maushi from next door. 'Guggi'?, I thought, but my name is Brando... I looked quizzically at Mumma but she seemed to ignore it and replied, "yes". After we were home, Yashodabai came to work at ten o'clock just like every other day. Running around her in joy is my favourite action everyday, when she comes home. Today i licked her too, I was extra happy. But, she scowled at me, " Eh Guggi, that's enough, have a lot of work on hand". Oh no, once again! Maushi from next door called me Guggi today and Yashodabai too... she comes to us everyday. I felt like screaming at her and say, " I am NOT Guggi but Brando"! But Yashodabai was nowhere around to hear me out. She was already on her chores and I went back to sit down in my usual place. In a while I was dozing and I completely forgot whether I was Guggi or Brando. In the afternoon, while Yashodabai was leaving she said to Mumma, " Tai, Guggi's food is over and you need to order for it". This time too Mumma didn't correct her to say that I wasnt Guggi but Brando and that really made me sad. Guggi lived in this house before I came. I can still smell him sometimes but I have also been here for some months now.. Once a guest had come and had commented, " Have you named him Guggi as well?" Finally, I made up mind to correct whoever calls me Guggi, myself. Wont wait for help. immediately the bell rang, I barked and Mumma opened the door. " Aunty, please will you tie up Guggi, i feel scared", Radha from next door was screaming. Not again... I was really angry this time. My anger was expressed over my evening meal... I just didnt touch it....I couldn't believe it that I was called Guggi throughout the day and by so many people. Mumma was worried. She reacted to Pappa, " Brando hasn't eaten at all today, looks like he has an upset stomach". Pappa got scared and decided to take me to the doctor..."Let's take him to the vet, he needs medicine now". I recognise both the words, Vet and medicine, very well. I hate them and before I could run away to avoid going to that horrible vet for those terrible medicines, Pappa put my leash on me and bundled me in the car. Within a while, the car was outside the vet's clinic. As soon as I saw the other dogs at the clinic, I broke out into a thunderous bark. I jumped around crazily in the car and that broke the brake light at the back of the car. Pappa was furious and hollered at me, " Guggi, behave yourself" That's it. That was the last straw. I was mad by then. I decided not to step out of the car at all. Ultimately, with two more collars and leash on me and four men from the back came to pick me up from the car. I had no option but reached the vet's table. " Hey Brando, I hear that you haven't eaten your food today. Let me give you an injection and you will be fine in a jiffy", said the vet. I hated the vet, but He called me BRANDO! I quietened down a bit but just for a bit. As soon as I saw the injection in the vet's hand I leapt with a jerk and raced towards the road. The people on the road were terrified to see me run and they began to run helter and skelter as well. Women and girls started screaming in a cacophony. Somehow, i just took off. No body on the road could stop me. I finally stopped at a place where I noticed many dogs eating something. I suddenly felt hungry and heard rumbling sounds in my stomach. I decided to get a taste of it and all the dogs around there created a pandemonium by barking at me. A few stones were thrown at them which finally made them run away from there. One stone landed on my foot too. I ate up all the food at once. I burped loudly and satisfied was wondering what to do next. Before I could decide on my next move, I heard a loud siren of a car which stopped next to me. A few cops jumped out of the car and i saw my Pappa behind them too. Pappa was angry and screamed at me, " Guggi, if you do this again then I will beat you up today". The police heard this and commented to Pappa, "But didn't you say that your dog was called Brando? Why are you calling him Guggi now? You are cheating us and trying to take away somebody else's dog..." " oh no, this is our Brando", said Pappa and called me out loudly in his usual tone, 'Brandooooo". I ran towards him and jumped and licked him. That finally made the police believe that I was actually Brando and not Guggi. We reached home. I was tired, scared and puzzled and ran straight to sit on mumma's lap. That day I also took another decision. What ever happens, I will never disregard my food.....I can never fast and I never will. Even if anyone calls me Guggi, No problem.
author: Aditi De

title: My Home Needs Cleaning
text: I must clean up. We have to sweep, mop and scrub to make the house look good again. We have a cleaning chart which shows who does what and when. I sweep the house every morning. My brother washes the clothes. I like a clean home but I don't like some chores. I like cleaning the bathroom but i don't like sweeping the house. ﻿We are usually done cleaning up by lunch time. After lunch, I play football with my friends. After playing, I must shower before supper. When my home is clean, it makes me smile and we are happy. title: Home
text: I went out of the gate. I am in a hurry. I do not have time to play. I do not have time to talk. I want to go home quickly. I walked through the alley. That narrow alley. I can see the crowds in front. There is a wide road over there. There is a large traffic on a large road. Cars, trucks, bicycles, motorcycles and trolleys. Some are moving in this direction. Others are in that direction. I know how to go through the gaps between cars to go to the other side. I reached the road divider. There is traffic in front of me. There is traffic behind me. I have to be careful. I am on the other side now. I almost ran into a vendor. He yelled at me, so I said "Sorry" as I ran away. I passed by the shops. In them are people buying different items. There is a game shop. I cannot stop. I walked faster and faster. I found fish shops, big fish and little fish, long fish and fat fish. I ran and ran and ran in the alley. Finally I arrived at home. Oh awesome! I am not late. My dad goes to work in the afternoon. His bicycle is still here so my father did not leave yet. My father came out of the house, my mother following him. I hugged my father tightly and he embraced me tightly too. Afterwards he went to work, now I don't need to rush, I have a lot of time.

title: A Little Like You
text: Rinki couldn’t remember who she was! She just couldn’t remember the word. Was she a Highnosesdust? Ginormosauce? Whymarvellous? She decided to go for a walk and find out. Maybe she would meet someone who looked like her! “I’m large and grey like you. Am I an elephant too?” “Harrumph,” said Elephant. “What you say is true, but we’re taller and bigger than you. Our trunks are like pipes, our ears are all flappy. Rinki, we’re different from you.” “I have a horn like some of you. Am I a deer too?” “Hafloof,” said Deer. “What you say is true, but we’re shorter and smaller too. We have antlers, not horns, and they grow like two trees. Rinki, we’re different from you.” “I love mud and water baths like you. Am I a water buffalo too?” “Oonph,” said Water Buffalo. “What you say is true, but our horns are long and curvy. Our skin is a bit hairy, not folded or bumpy. Rinki, we’re different from you.” “I have bumpy skin like yours. Am I a crocodile too?” “Hurrranngh,” said Crocodile. “What you say is true, but we’re flatter than you. We have long snouts and shiny tails. Rinki, we’re different from you.” Rinki thought hard as she walked over to the pond. In the water, she saw herself. Big nose. Half-moon horn. Crumpled skin. Oh, now she remembered! She was a rhinoceros! She was a bit like the others, but she was different too. “Mostly,” she thought, “I am just Rinki.” Meet the Indian Rhinoceros Rinki is an Indian rhinoceros who lives in Kaziranga, Assam. Indian rhinos mostly live alone. You might see them in groups when they are mating or when they’re very young and need to stay with their mothers. Single horn on top of the nose. Like a unicorn! Lips can curl and grip favourite foods like grass, leaves, branches, fruits, and water plants. Three toes on each foot Legs that can run at about 40 kilometres per hour Bumpy patterns in some places Thick skin that falls in folds Indian rhinos are some of the biggest land animals in the country. They're bigger than humans but smaller than elephants. Animals you can meet when you visit Kaziranga, Assam. Indian Elephant Barasingha or Eastern Swamp Deer Marsh Crocodile Wild Water Buffalo Kaziranga is also home to tigers, otters, turtles and many species of birds.
author: Suchi Govindarajan

title: Discovering Dinosaurs
text: Long, long ago, long before humans walked the Earth, the world was full of reptiles called dinosaurs. There were reptiles that lived on land, swam in the sea, burrowed under the ground, and even flew through the skies. There were dinosaurs that were taller than buildings, shorter than stools, bigger than construction cranes, and smaller than ducks. They came in all shapes and sizes, just like humans! The Ornithomimus was the fastest dinosaur. It could run as fast as a scooter! The Hadrosaur was the dinosaur with the most teeth. It had more than a thousand! The Pentaceratops was the dinosaur with the biggest head. Its skull was bigger than a refrigerator! The Quetzalcoatlus was the biggest flying reptile. The distance from the tip of one wing to the other was longer than a telephone pole! The Micropachycephalosaurus was the dinosaur with the longest name, but it was very small — no bigger than a 4-year-old human! The Therizinosaurus had the longest claws. Each claw was half as long as a bed! The Argentinosaurus was one of the largest dinosaurs. It was larger than a cricket pitch! The Shuvuuia was one of the smallest dinosaurs. It was the size of a hen! So, where are all the dinosaurs now? Dinosaurs disappeared millions of years ago. No human has ever seen one. All that’s left of them are fossils, which are often buried deep underground. Scientists are still searching for fossils to learn more about these amazing creatures. Dinosaurs existed for 175 million years until Earth was struck by a meteor 65 million years ago, which slowly killed all the dinosaurs. When the first dinosaur bone or fossil was discovered in 1677, scientists thought it was from a giant man! By the 1800s, scientists began to realise that they belonged to a different species that no longer existed. They called them ‘dinosaurs’ which means ‘terrible lizards’ in Greek. Palaeontology, the study of animal and plant fossils, soon became popular. Palaeontologists have discovered around 700 species of dinosaurs, and are still finding more. Dinosaur fossils are most commonly found in China, South America and North America. Do you want to see a dinosaur? Then look around you. Many scientists believe that birds are descendants of dinosaurs. Those terrible lizards are still among us!
author: Anjali  Alappat

title: Tigers
text: This tiger is call jumpy because he loves to jump. But something weird has happened. Juts jumpy can jump but others cannot. Jumpy did’t learn how to jump. But others learn. Jumpy was the only tiger can jump. So one day he saw his friends Their are starlight Carla and others. So his friends ask Jumpy how to jump. Jumpy said juts try to lift your legs it the air and jump. Tiger Carla is too lazy to try. She said:”I will never be able to jump up high.” So she sat on the grass all day long. Her feet shrink smaller and smaller...because she doesn’t use them. It is almost 9pm at night, she decided to head home and wanted to stand up....poor Carla couldn’t stand up......her feet were as small as cat’s feet.....”Oh No Oh No....help help”.... Luckily, Carla only had a dream...she woke up from her scream. Her feet are still the same size, Jumpy is beside her and said⋯Carla， let’s try to jump. She tried and was able to leap with Jumpy happily. The End....
author: Neko Chung
illustrator: Anant Shahane; Arjun; Ashok Rajagopalan; Chiradeep Majumder; Sreevidya Gowda; Vanishree N

title: Flower power
text: Today is Nandana's mom's birthday. Her mom loves flowers. Nandana is thinking deeply about what kind of flowers she can draw on the greeting card. Do you think she will draw one red hibiscus? Do you think she will draw the white jasmines? Do you think she will draw a pink lotus? She wanted the card to be unique unlike anything else. After a lot of thinking she came up with a brilliant idea. She created a beautiful and unique greeting card with flowers of different shapes triangles, squares and circles. Do you think her mom will like it? Happy birthday mom, Love Nandana
author: Surekha Reddy

title: The Wise Dog
text: THE WISE DOG Tina and Rohan were playing with their dog Bruno. Bruno was a little puppy. Mother called Bruno to give him a treat.Meanwhile, Tina's friend came with some good news. "I am leaving my puppy Bubbly here.I need to go to the mall".And then she left.Bruno and Bubbly started playing.The children went to their studies. After some time Bruno came with a loud bark,"WHOFF,WHOOFF" he shouted. Tina went to see what happend. Oh my god, she said. Rohan also came out and saw that Bubbly was gone.They asked Bruno,but he had no clue.They asked Dammu uncle,he said she was on the footpath.They started searching,Bruno started sniffing and lead them to her house.They found her in her home.She came all by herself! What a wise dog! It was a crazy day!! THE END
author: sanvi

title: The bear-cub who wanted the moon.
text: He has an idea. If he could just climb up high enough... perhaps he could reach the moon! He sets off into the forest, all alone, looking for the highest tree he can find. Aha! There it is! Bibo is delighted. He climbs, up and up and up, high above the ground. But he isn't being careful...all of a sudden, the tree can't support his weight. CRACK! Bibo tumbles down, all the way to the bottom! And then - all goes quiet in the forest. Poor Bibo! But in the meanwhile, his mother, wildly worried, has set out in search of her little baby. After hours of anguish, she finds her bear-cub trembling, huddled at the foot of a broken tree. "Oh Bibo! What did you do?" she exclaims. "I wanted to reach the moon," the bear-cub whimpers. "You just had to ask me!" his mother sighs. A mother can do anything for her baby. Even bring down the moon! THE END
author: Akhila (Abhaydhara)

title: The Rabbit and the Elephant
text: There was once an elephant in a jungle. His best friend was a rabbit called Gampu. They would both play together. One day the elephant fell asleep. The rabbit was jumping all over the elephant. All of a sudden, two hunters came there. The rabbit tried to wake up his friend, but the elephant wouldn't get up! The hunters had aimed their guns at the elephant - when the rabbit leapt onto them! The guns went off, "BANG!". Hearing the noise, the elephant woke up and starting running. The hunters apologised to the elephant. His life was saved. The rabbit had saved the elephant's life! Smart little Gampu! The elephant was forever grateful to his friend.
author: Akhila (Abhaydhara)

title: I Know My Rights
text: I have rights. You have rights. We all have rights. Rights make us strong. Boy or girl... We all have the right to be born. We all have the right to play. We all have the right to be friends with any other child. We all have the right to say our ideas, and for adults to hear us. We all have the right to be safe. We all have the right not to be abused. We all have the right to talk, to sing, to dance, and to make art.. Every child has the right not to go to work. We all have the right to be cared for and the right to go to school. We all have the right to books in our own languages, and to learn more about all of our rights. 1 Everyone under 18 has these rights. 2 All children have these rights, no matter who they are, where they live, what their parents do, what language they speak, what their religion is, whether they are a boy or girl, what their culture is, whether they have a disability, whether they are rich or poor. No child should be treated unfairly on any basis. 3 All adults should do what is best for you. 4 The government has a responsibility to make sure your rights are protected. 5 Your family has the responsibility to help you learn to exercise your rights, and to ensure that your rights are protected. 6 You have the right to be alive. UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in Child Friendly Language 8 You have the right to a nationality (to belong to a country). 9 You have the right to an identity – an official record of who you are. 10 You have the right to live with your parent(s), unless it is bad for you. You have the right to live with a family who cares for you. 11 If you live in a different country than your parents do, you have the right to be together in the same place. 12 You have the right to be protected from kidnapping. 13 You have the right to give your opinion, and for adults to listen and take it seriously. 15 You have the right to choose your own religion and beliefs. 16 You have the right to choose your own friends and join or set up groups, as long as it isn’t harmful to others. 17 You have the right to privacy. 18 You have the right to get information that is important to your well-being. 19 You have the right to be raised by your parent(s) if possible. 20 You have the right to be protected from being hurt and mistreated, in body or mind. 21 You have the right to special care and help if you cannot live with your parents. 23 You have the right to special protection and help if you are a refugee. 24 You have the right to special education and care if you have a disability, so that you can live a full life. 25 You have the right to the best health care possible, safe water to drink, nutritious food, a clean and safe environment, and information to help you stay well. 26 If you live in care or in other situations away from home, you have the right to have these living arrangements looked at regularly to see if they are the most appropriate. 27 You have the right to help from the government if you are poor or in need. 29 You have the right to a good quality education. You should be encouraged to go to school to the highest level you can. 30 Your education should help you use and develop your talents and abilities. It should help you learn to live peacefully, protect the environment and respect other people. 31 You have the right to practice your own culture, language and religion - or any you choose. 32 You have the right to play and rest. 33 You have the right to protection from work that harms you, and is bad for your health and education. If you work, you have the right to be safe and paid fairly. 36 You have the right to protection from any kind of exploitation. 37 You have the right to not be punished by anyone in a cruel or harmful way. 38 You have the right to protection and freedom from war. Children under fifteen cannot be forced to go into the army or take part in war. 39 You have the right to help if you’ve been hurt, neglected or badly treated. 40 You have the right to legal help and fair treatment in the justice system that respects your rights. 41 If the laws of your country provide better protection of your rights than the articles in this Convention, those laws should apply. Every child must have these rights protected. If you feel that your rights or others' rights are not being protected, speak to an adult about it. You can call Childline on 1098 and talk to someone. To know more about child rights, visit
author: Lea Shaver

title: The Big Rain
text: I love the rain. But not this year. This rain is too much. It rains so much, the river floods. I am scared of the muddy water. We must leave now! We will be safe up on the hill. It is hard to walk in the water, but some army men help us. Oh no! I left my doll at home! We cannot go back now. Not until the water is gone. Now can I go get my doll? Mai yells, No! Our home is under water. We do not even have water to drink! But Daadu says, your doll will be fine. Let us play a game now. Yes, I want to play a game! Find all the things on my list. Then I will show you a prize. I read the list. I start to hunt. pail cloth rocks sand hammer nail I run to Mai. "I need a cloth", I say. "Do you have one?" "Here," Mai says, "take this." She cuts a cloth from her sari. Babu helps me find a pail. We fill it with sand. My friend is thirsty too. "Do you have any water?" he asks. "Sorry," I say. "We drank it all. Now I am looking for rocks." "Look there," he says. I see the rocks. Only two things left! I find a wood fixer. "May I have a hammer and nail for my game? " I ask. "Who has time for a game when all of us need water?" he says. But he lends me the tools. I found all the items! Daadu smiles. Then h e makes a hole in the bucket. He puts the cloth on the hole. Then he pours in the sand. I help him fill the pail with rocks. We put the tiny ones in first. Then the big ones go on top. Then he puts muddy river water in the pail. Why? Soon, clean water drips from the hole. Daadu fills a glass. We made a filter. It takes the mud out of the water. Mai and Babu boil the water to kill germs. Then we drink it! Soon the army comes in boats. They bring us food. And my doll! Make a water filter You will need: - scissors - sand - rocks - clean cloth - a bottle What to do Cut the bottom of the bottle. Put a hole in the cap. Put the cloth on top of the hole. Pour in the sand, less than half full. Then add small rocks, more than half full. Fill it with the large rocks. Pour in water slowly. You must boil the water to kill germs.
author: Lea Shaver

title: A Book for Puchkuu
text: Where is Puchku?” Puchku is busy. She has a book to read. Puchku reads all the time. "Why are you always reading?" asks Boitu. "Come, watch TV with us!" says Dodla. "Books are more fun!” says Puchku. Words become stories and WHOOSH! You are in a new world! But today, Puchku is sad. She has read all the books in the library! "No more books!" wails Puchku. "What will I do?" But, wait! What is that? Puchku looks up and sees... "More books!" But t he shelf is too tall. Puchku is too short. How can she get up there? Maybe a wash line? How about chairs and tables? If only Puchku had a giraffe. Or a monkey. Puchku has a plan. She calls two boys for help. Up, up, up they climb. Puchku has her hand on a book! But then, it all goes wrong. AAAAAAAAH! “What is this?” It is the Very Tall Librarian! She puts Puchku down. "Can I help?" "I have run out of books,” says Puchku. The Very Tall Librarian smiles. May I pick you up?” Puchku nods. “I will take this one," says Puchku. "Thank you!" “Take this one too,” says the Very Tall Librarian. "I loved this book when I was small. You will grow too." she tells Puchku. "Until you do, just ask for help." But Puchku does not hear. She has a new book!
author: Lea Shaver

title: Superhero Amber
text: SUPERHERO AMBER It was night time. Amber was dreaming of herself being a Superhero. When she woke up in the morning, she quickly brushed her teeth, had a bath. She saw a small bird in her garden. The bird was stuck in some threads. Amber came out rushing and screamed “OH-NOO”. She wanted to help the bird. She went to attic and searched for her box. There was her old suit. She used to wear it at parties. It had some satin ribbons to make her very own belt with a special superhero symbol. She wore that suit. Amber went running in garden to help the bird. But the small bird spread out his wings and flew away to his nest. ‘No Luck’ said Amber, but I will find some other job to help someone today. Then she saw her old neighbor ‘Mrs. Merry’, trying to cross the road. Amber rushed toward Mrs. Merry, and helped her to cross the road. She came back to the house and shouted “Mission Accomplished”. Then she saw her little brother Jim playing with a ball. The ball went into the big mulberry bush. He was sad. Amber was watching all this and said, ‘Don’t worry. I’ll get your ball. She went into the mulberry bush but was not able to reach. She called Jim with a stick, and they both were able to reach to the ball. Amber said, “We make a great superhero team. Let’s make a suit for you too”. They both went in house to make a suit for Jim. ----- THE END -----
author: sanvi

title: My Appa and his Sounds
text: That shape over there is my Appa. He is sleeping. To know him well, like I do, you have to use your ears more than your eyes. You have to listen to Appa and his sounds carefully. Hhh hgh ghh hhh When Appa sleeps, he breathes quietly. Like wind through leaves. I can make that sound by cupping my hands over my mouth and blowing gently. Hhho-hhha-hhho-hhha. But sometimes, Appa snores as loud as thunder. I can snore like Appa by grunting through my nose like a pig and then flapping my lips like a horse. Kroaa-tbphpht-kroaa-tbphpht. Hhho - hhha - hhho - hhha Kroaa -tbphpht Kroaa -tbphpht When Appa wakes up, he scratches his arms and legs. I can make this sound by tearing paper into small pieces. Krrrsk-krrrsk-krrrsk-krrrsk. When Appa stands up, the bones in his legs pop and crackle. Like cloth flapping in the wind. I clap with two fingers to make this sound. Khat-khat-khat-khat Krrrsk-krrrsk Krrrsk-krrrsk Khat -khat -khat -khat Appa chews loudly with his mouth open. I stomp through slush after the rains to make this sound. Squish-squash-squelch-squalch. When Appa eats something hard, it makes a breaking, crushing sound. I step on dry leaves and twigs to make this sound. Karak-muruk-katak-latak. Squish-squash squelch-squalch Karak - muruk katak - latak When Appa drinks water, the ball in his throat rises and falls. It makes a deep, muffled sound. When I go swimming and my ears get blocked, everything sounds like Appa's drinking sound. Guduk-guduk-guduk. Guduk Guduk Guduk After lunch, Appa burps from his mouth. This means the food was good. Appa's burps sound like slow lorries going up a hilly road. Rrraaahhhrrrhhh! If Appa burps from his bum, then his stomach did not like the food. His bum burps are musical. I pull my cheeks back tightly and blow while keeping my mouth closed. Pheeeooooowoink! Rrra aahh hrrr hhh! Pheeeoo ooowoink! If Appa's nose whistles, it means that he is getting a cold. He sometimes takes a sharp breath to clear his nose. When I drag a chair on the floor, it makes the same sound. Tststszszstztz! When Appa is fully sick, his nose gets fully blocked. He then has to pant from his mouth, like me when I run very fast. Hhhun-hhhun-hhhun. Hhhun- hhhun- hhhun Tststszszstztz! Appa has a large, loud laugh that can be heard three houses away. I roar like a hungry tiger-monkey to laugh like Appa. HROAHAHAHA! HROAHAHAHA! My favourite Appa sound is one he can't make alone. He needs me to make that sound. It's when he kisses my forehead with a loud, wet smack. MMMPPTZTZCHUAH! MMM PPT ZTZCH UAH! How do ears hear sound? Sound waves travel into the ear canal until they reach the eardrum. The eardrum passes the vibrations of the sound waves through the middle ear into the inner ear. The inner ear is shaped like a snail and is called the cochlea. Finally, the sound waves reach the cochlea which contains thousands of tiny hair cells that can sense sound. Sometimes the hair cells inside the cochlea get damaged and people may not be able to hear well. This can happen because of old age, injury or illness. A hearing aid is a small electronic device that can help such people hear better. Inner Ear Outer Ear Middle Ear Ear Canal Ear Drum How does a hearing aid work? A hearing aid is worn in or behind the ear. It makes sounds louder using three basic parts: a microphone, an amplifier and a speaker. 1. Sound enters the hearing aid through the microphone. 2. The microphone passes on the sound to the amplifier, which increases its power and makes it louder. 3. These amplified sounds are then sent to the ear through the speaker. Do you know of somebody who could benefit from using a hearing aid? Take them to your local ENT (ear nose throat) doctor for a checkup. Microphone Speaker Volume Control Amplifier Battery Earmold Ear Hook
author: Venkataraghavan Subha Srinivasan

title: An Unforgettable Birthday
text: Matthew bounced off his bed, charged at the door and skidded into the hallway. “Aha! This is the best birthday I’ve ever had!!” thought Matthew. His heart was racing, then he shouted “This is good.” Soon his mom and dad were awake. Matthew grabbed a book to read. Before he knew he had to eat breakfast, he slammed the book and sat down. His mom was busy putting on decorations this and that. “I hope the decoration is not boring.” he muttered. The decoration was filled with ribbons and balloons. Matthew liked them but he wanted his friend Howard to come. Meanwhile Howard was snoring and snoring. Matthew didn’t know that so… he phoned Howard. This proved to be a mistake! A BIG MISTAKE! Howard jerked up, stormed out and … took the phone and said “I’m sleepy! Call back at 8:30am!” He slammed down the phone and went to sleep. Still both of them were excited because they were going to have fun at Matthew’s birthday party. At 8:30am sharp, Matthew called Howard. “Briiiiiiiinggggggg!” shouted the phone. Howard answered the phone “Blah Blah Blah Blahhhh!?!?!?*!” “Beep Beep!!*!!@*?” This was the voice on the other end. Finally, Howard croaked “Goodbye*?!@!” After Howard woke up, he wanted to surprise Matthew by buying a cake to wish him a happy birthday. Howard was jumping up and down, saying to the shopkeeper “This one!” His hands were swinging wildly. His eyes were popping out. His mouth was talking as fast as scissors. Howard’s heart pounded with excitement. He liked the cake he chose. Matthew was impatient because he waited for Howard for a long time. Matthew kept checking his watch – only 10 minutes but to Matthew it was a Million-Billion-Zillion years. Matthew got ready for the Million-Billion-Zillion years wait. All the time he stomped right-left-right-left until he screamed “Oh my gosh, this is tiring!!!” Matthew stood up and put his hands on hips. His eyes drooped and said “I can’t take it anymore!” Then he decided to eat lots of chocolate, cotton candy, popcorn, gummy bears, sweets, ninja-shaped lollipop and nuts. He was so tired he could barely walk. Matthew was so full and stuffed up that his belly was filled to brim. He thought he was going to be sick. And boy did he pop! Matthew felt like cockroaches, butterflies and caterpillars climbing in his stomach. “Yochie! Ouchie!!!” Matthew yelled. He was jumping up and down and groaning with pain. He felt like his stomach was ready to burst with the fire, insects and the pain. Hot red cackling fire was running up and down his throat and stomach. He howled with pain. His stomach was burning with 600000 o C fiery fire. He vomited just in time in the toilet. “Tut Tut Matthew, You need to sleep! GO RIGHT NOW!!!!!!!” bellowed his mother. “Go! Beat it!” “Dinggg!! Dingggg!!! Dingggg!!!” yelled the doorbell. Once Matthew’s mom opened the door, Howard howled “MATTHEWWWWWW, WHERE ARE YOOOUUUU!!????!” The door slammed… slammed so hard that Howard’s nose got a big, fat, painful bonk! “Youuuuuuooochhieeeee, what was that for??!!!” he barked at the door. Matthew’s mom slammed the door because the noise was deafening! Howard was curious like a MAD LION, he rushed in Matthew’s room and bombed the door. Matthew groaned and felt annoyed. Howard kept talking and talking. Matthew’s face scrunched up and turned red. He angrily narrowed his eyes and his lips pursed together. Matthew became a fire breathing dragon. He thought he couldn’t stand it anymore and wanted to swallow Howard. Howard ignored the narrowing eyes of Matthew and even screeched “Eeeeat the cake! It’s yummy! It’s beautiful! Eat! Eat! Eat!!!!!!” Matthew yelled at Howard “Shut UP!” Howard immediately burst into tears. Tears trickled down his cheek and he ran out of Matthew’s room. Quickly, Howard’s parents rushed to comfort him but it was no use. Howard screamed and cried even LOUDER!! Meanwhile Matthew blamed Howard “IT’S ALL HIS FAULT!!!!” But Matthew's parents said “You should not have shouted at him. He’s just 7 years old!” “Well, I suppose he doesn’t have to TALK AND TALK AND TALK!!!!!!!” Matthew scolded. But talking to them didn’t work. Both Matthew and Howard couldn’t calm down. Matthew’s house was very noisy. Matthew’s friends tried to comfort them by giving popcorn and orange juice. But with all the wailing and pushing… “BANG!!!!” All of a sudden, the popcorn scattered around. And the cups of orange juice fell down like a GIANT WATERFALL!!! The sticky and slippery juice crashed on top of the popcorn. Now the floor was very messy. But giving them food was no use either. The kids made it even worse. They stared at the floor, their mouths were wide open. The kids were shocked at what they spilled. Then the kids and parents all cleaned up the mess. Finally, Howard and Matthew calmed down. Matthew’s mom gave him medicine and hoped he would get well soon. Everyone’s wish came true that Matthew got better. Matthew laid on the sofa like a lazy koala. His arms were on the side of the sofa. “Ahhhhhhhhhhhhh!! This is LIFE!!!!!!!” he thought. One of his legs hang on the sofa. “Glorious!” He scratched his butt while he sung a song no one knew. “What are you doing?” Howard asked. “Scratching my BUTT!!” Matthew replied. “EWWW!” said Howard. His legs were like rubber. “What a disgusting smell!” he thought with surprise. Then he realized it was Matthew, he had FARTED! Everyone covered their noses. “Yuckity! Yuckity Yuck!” But everyone giggled with glee. Everyone’s faces were planted with a smile. Suddenly Howard and Matthew remembered the argument. “Sorry!” they both said at the same time. They both gave each other warm hugs by stretching their arms out. It was time for the party to begin. All the kids rushed to the dinning room. All the eyes stared at the cake. The cake surprised Matthew. His eyes shone brightly, his mouth blurted “WOW! Thank you, Howard! This is my favorite cake!” It was a mango cake with Iron Man figure on top which could glow once Matthew blew on it. Then Howard happily gave Matthew more presents to cheer him up. Matthew looked like a hungry kangaroo and kept gobbling the cake. His mouth was stretched wide open. Blobs of cake dropped to the floor, the crumbs of cake were like rocks falling down from Mount Everest. At this moment, Howard wordlessly looked at Matthew and thought “Oh no! He’s going to be sick again!” Howard patted Matthew softly and said “Hey friend, don’t eat too much junk food or you will get a stomachache again just like before!” Matthew kindly agreed “Thank you for reminding me! Remember our friendship! You know what? Always forgive each other. Don’t argue too often.” Lastly they fist bumped excitedly.
author: Wilfred Law

title: Tall or Short !
text: I had not always been this tall. I was very very short. I was the shortest in my class. People always called me shorty as i was very short. I felt sad and angry when my classmates teased me. Everyday i went home and thought why am I so short? Why can't i be tall or taller than everyone else. One day I was going to school. On the way to school, I saw a statue. "Even the statue is taller than me," I said. The next second I grew taller. " I feel like I have grown taller," I said happily. Again I grew taller. "I am tall as everyone else," I said and again I grew taller. Then I understood that whenever I say tall,taller or tallest I grow tall. Now I got greedy and I repeated again and again the words "tall!..tall!...tall!". The very next thing I see is that I am as tall as a giraffe. Now I could finally fit in. I reached school but I was not able to get through the door as it was smaller than me. Since I could not get inside school, I decided to play cricket with some other people. But I was not able to play because when I approached them, they ran away yelling"Giant!". I felt hungry. I went to a shop famous for its cheapest food in town. Everyone I came near ran away screaming either"dangerous monster"or "big giant". I never thought it will be more difficult to fit in after I was this tall. "I wish I could be short again" I said. Then suddenly I turned back into my original height. I was happier than ever and from then on I enjoyed being who I am.
author: Tarun Sundhar
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Catherine Groenewald; Hari Kumar Nair; Tanvi Bhat

title: Funny Birds
text: How did it get that way? Hornbill, hornbill, where is your hair? What does a hornbill's head look like? Vulture, Vulture, where is your hair? What if you had no hair? Would you need shampoo? Would you need a comb? Can you name these birds? Start at the top and go clockwise. Himalayan Monal Common Hoopoe Indian Vulture Eurasian Spoonbill Red-whiskered Bulbul Racket-tailed Drongo Brown Fish Owl Great Indian Hornbill Do birds really have hair? No! Some birds look like they have hair on their heads. But they are not really hairs like ours. They are very thin feathers. A group of thin feathers on a bird's head is called a crest. Crests are useful in many ways. They make birds look attractive. Some birds can open and fold their crests to send signals to other birds. Some open their crests when they want to frighten away other birds and animals. The furry worms on the owl’s head are called ear-tufts. They are not really ears, just bits of skin covered with feathers. These help owls hide more easily, making them look like they are part of a tree. The ear-tufts also help them look attractive (to other owls) or scary (to other birds and animals). The hornbill’s helmet is called a casque (rhymes with mask). Like ear-tufts and crests, casques make hornbills look good. This helps them find mates. A hornbill’s casque also makes its beak stronger. With a strong beak, hornbills can pick and eat fruits more easily.
author: Lea Shaver

title: Just the Way I Am
text: Why is this sheep sad? She does not fit. She is too wide for the gate. Will yoga make her thin? She tries it. But she is still too wide to fit. Will jogging make her thin? She tries it. But she is still too wide to fit. Will swimming make her thin? She tries it. But she is still too wide to fit in the gate. Will riding make her thin? No! I do not want to try that. I just want to go home. S he thinks and thinks. Now she has a new plan. What will she do now? She did it! How did you do it? You are still so wide! I am fit. I am fine just the way I am. But the gate was too small. So I fixed it!
author: Lea Shaver

title: Shaan's incredible insects
text: Shaan is curious about incredible insects. He went to the garden to find few incredible insects. He took the magnifying glass along with him. Let's join Shaan to find few incredible insects. Look, Shaan spots a lady bug, an insect that is red with black spots. The lady bugs are very helpful insects, they eat bugs called aphids that harm plants. Look, Shaan spots beautiful butterflies, these insects have colourful wings. Look, Shaan spots a dragonfly, this insect is an expert flier, it hovers like a helicopter. Look, Shaan spots honey bees, they live in hives. They are always busy making honey. Yummy! Look, Shaan spots a grasshopper, this insect eats plants and grass. A grasshopper can not only fly, it can also jump. Look, Shaan spots leaf insects, these insects look like leaves they are also called walking leaves. Look, Shaan spots a group of ants, they are social insects. A group of ants is called an army. After looking at all the bugs, Shaan was curious to count the black spots on the lady bug. He went back to the lady bug and started counting the black spots.
author: Surekha Reddy
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Lavanya  Naidu; Maya  Ramaswamy; Sabyasachi Hazra; Sam  van Riet; Sheena Deviah

title: I Miss My Dog
text: This is my dog. Oh no! My dog made a big mess. And she ran away. I miss my dog. Is she a good dog? Does a good dog beg? Does a good dog run away? Does a good dog chase? No, dog, no! But she loves me. And I love her. We play and have fun. When I feel sad she sits with me. Look! Look! My dog is back! Good dog!
author: Lea Shaver

title: A Duck is Hurt
text: How would you take care of it? Would you give it food and water? Would you give it a warm bed? Would you be kind? Now the duck is better. But the cat sees the duck. What do you think will happen? The cat pounced on the duck. Now the duck is hurt again! What would you do? Would you take care of the duck? What would you do to help the duck heal? How will you feel when the duck is better again? Maybe some day the mother duck will find her baby. How will she feel? How does the duckling feel? Would you be sad to see the duckling leave? Would you be happy for the mother duck? Was it the right choice to take care of the duck? How do you know? You might feel happy for the duckling and the mother duck. You might feel sad to see your pet duck go. You might feel proud for doing the right thing.
author: Lea Shaver

title: The Dog's Eggs
text: How many eggs do you see? She sits on her eggs. This keeps them warm. She sits all day. She sits all night. One day she had to go. She had to find food. A dog is by her eggs! Oh no! Will the dog eat my eggs? The dog did not eat the eggs. He just likes the soft bed! The dog took a nap. The eggs hatched. The dog woke up. "Mama! Mama!" said the baby birds. "Who, me?" said the dog. I am not your mama. I just took a nap! The dog ran away. The birds ran too. Stop! said mama bird. That dog is not your mama. I am! The babies came back. And mama bird gave them a big hug. THE END
author: Lea Shaver

title: the poor dreams to become a rich man but left as a dream
text: There used to be a happy family living in a undeveloped village.There were of poor children and adults out side who lived in small and compressed cemented house,this family was one of them But only one of them had a big and a rich house in the center of the river. the family heard many features of the house and wanted a house but it was not in there budget. The place had many rooms decorated by many pebbles which can glow in the dark. Their dream could not be obtained till 5 year of hard work to the government.There dreams where to get a car with many servant to open the car doors. A diamond ring for every one in the family. when the owner of the rich house came for a walk and saw the hard working man who was fishing till he to the best of his labor when the rich man asked for a fish and thought that if he would have gave a pieces of his hard work he would have gave his entirety property. The fisherman thought"A rich man can take a pieces of this hard work for free, never ", he then refused and sent him away from this place and his dream remained as a dream. From this we learn the moral is that sharing is caring and also that if you give something there is always a return.
