title: Champion Chiku
text: She didn't speak much, Didn't go out for lunch. She never liked to swing, But stories she used to think. She didn't swim in the pond, she didn't go to the mall. She didn't eat a lot, She didn't feel very hot. It was a stormy day. There were no lights. It was dark everywhere. Everyone was very scared. They thought their own shadows were ghosts! Brave Chiku knew what to do. She lit a lantern and told everyone lovely stories. She even sang songs. Everyone was very happy! She sparked hope in everyone!
author: Sarvika Tuli

title: Catiline and the Bowl of Milk
text: My name is Greedy Catiline. You seem not to like my name. I was born in your home town. Don't ask me where my hometown is. You and I were born there. I may look young, but I am older than you. I am always feeling the pang of hunger. Anytime I had cause to run, hunger will be the next thing. On that faithful morning. I heard a very loud. Gbo Ah! The noise was so loud that I thought it was a bomb blast. I was so afraid to the point that my tail curled in between my legs. What could that be? I asked myself. Then, another bang. Gbo Ah! This time, the sound was deafening. I had to run to the nearby place to hide. Though I was not sure of where I was hiding. The whole place does not look safe. As this was going on, I saw people running in different directions. What could have happened? I ask myself again. But I could not get any answer. Was there a war between these humans again? Were the armed robbers back again in our area? Why were they all running up and down? I could even see adults and children also running. This must be very serious. Well, I thought to myself, I must make myself secured and safe. So I laid low. Then the loud noise came upon again. This time, it was coming closer and closer to me. I was also becoming more and more afraid. What could be? I asked myself one more time. Then, I need to be safe. So I had to run to another place. The place was a bit lonely. There must have been some people there. But I did not see anyone. Though the place was not that dark. Then I became so hungry because I have not ate anything that morning. As I was thinking of what should eat. Just ahead of me was a plat of milk. I could not believe it. A bowl of milk? So I licked it all of it. And I was satisfied! But who put the milk there? Then, something bad happened to me. It was too much for me to bear.
author: Samuel A Eyitayo
illustrator: David Chisha; Deepa Balsavar; Priya Kuriyan; Sahil Shaikh

title: If Roads Could Speak
text: I do, but my big brothers and friends don’t! Road: So tell them that nobody likes to be dirty. Child: But how can I tell, I am very small. Road: We are roads, if we do not keep clean, then you will not be able to move around anywhere! Child: I did try once, but they all scolded me! Road: If anybody throws dirty things on you, would you say the same thing even then? Child: No - no! Please forgive me! I will talk to them again and I will try to keep you as clean as I am. (And then the roads were clean.)
author: Raghav  Krishna
illustrator: Khushbu Vala; Nguyễn Thị  Ngọc Bích; Rob Owen; Sarthak Sinha; Tanvee Nabar

title: Karuppatti Chocolate
text: It is not only Manju who comes there to play but there are few other friends who also like to play with them. There is a mud pot kept in the kitchen for children to quench their thirst while playing. Manya's mother puts few vetiver inside the pot so that the water will be cold and aromatic. Vetiver: A root of a Indian grass used for aromatic and medicinal purposes. Fetching a tumbler of water from that pot and drinking is a favorite of all children. At that time, Manya's father would give everyone a small piece of Karuppatti. Manju named it as Karuppatti Chocolate. Karuppatti: Palm jaggery in Tamil language is Karuppatti. "Karuppatti chocolate.. Karuppatti chocolate.. Who wants it?" Manju shrieks as she enjoys chewing her Karuppatti piece. She then asks Manya's father, ''how do people actually make this? This is so tasty." For that her father replies, "the other name of Karuppatti is palm jaggery. First if we climb up the palm tree 'palmyrah' and slightly scrape the tender spathes, we can see milk dripping from it which is nothing but the sap or the juice of the palm. They would tie a small pot using a rope tightly under it to collect the sap. Spathe: A sheathing bract that encloses the flower cluster of palm tree. They would also coat the pots with lime so that the extracted milk will not get fermented. After the sap is collected in all the pots, they would transfer it into a large vessel, boil well, filter and then pour the hot liquid into smaller moulds or coconut shells. Once it is dried in the sun, it turns harder and we can get the karuppatti that we want from the moulds. If you directly drink the sap that is collected in the pots, then it is the palm juice which is also called as pathaneer or neera. This drink is rich in iron, fiber and calcium. Drinking this delicious and cool neera will relieve body fatigue. This is how karuppatti is made. What we are eating now is the same karuppatti that is cut into smaller pieces. We can use it for making sukku malli coffee by adding dry ginger, coriander seeds and palm jaggery to the boiling water." "Wow!!! so much of information in this Karuppatti Chocolate", exclaimed Manya with gratitude. Manya and Manju rushed to the kitchen to make sukku malli coffee.
author: Meenakshi Veeraragavaprabu

title: What is love?
text: One day, Farhan learnt the word 'love' in his school and he began to think 'What is love?How do I love?' He went to his Abba and asked 'Abbu what is love?' Abba smiled and said 'When you play downstairs and I keep glancing at you to see if you are safe.That is love!' Farhan smiled at his Abba and ran to his Ammi. Farhan asked his Ammi 'Ammi what is love?' Ammi smiled and said ‘When you share wonderful stories from your school and I listen to them everyday!' Farhan blushed and went looking for his Roshni Aapa. Farhan asked Roshni ' Aapa, what is love?' Roshni was busy drawing something and felt irritated with Farhan.She said 'Farhan, go away don't disturb me!Farhan felt sad about this. Farhan then went looking for his beloved Irsu.Farhan looked at Irsu and said to himself ‘If I ask Irsu,he won't be able to tell me what love is!’ Irsu saw Farhan and went running to him.He was so excited to see Farhan that he licked Farhan's face and jumped on him! 'Oh my Irsu! May be this is love?' Farhan exclaimed with joy. Farhan then went to meet his friend Tejashri and asked her 'Teju do you know what love is?’ Teju narrowed her eyes,scratched her head and said ‘Hmm,remember when you got 2 chocolates in your class and saved one for me?I think that is love!' Farhan smiled and said ‘Do you remember Teju, once when I fell down and cried so much, you quickly gave me water and hugged me? I think that is love too! Teju grinned and said ‘Yes Faru you are right!' Farhan then happily returned home and saw Roshni sitting in a corner.He ran to her and gave her the Imlis that he had bought from Shanku kaka's shop. Roshni looked at Farhan and said 'Faru,I am sorry that I shouted at you,what were you asking me then?' Farhan said 'Aapa,I wanted to know what love is and I got the answer!' Roshni's eyes twinkled,she smiled and said 'Faru,may be saying sorry like I did is love as well!' Farhan smiled brightly and hugged Roshni.Today Farhan got to know there are so many meanings of love and so many ways to love! What is your way of loving others?
author: Pallavi Raikar

title: The Thirsty Camel
text: It was very hot, so Pyaro could not walk. He was very thirsty. Tired Pyaro was thinking that there will be a river on the other side of the desert. To get to the other side, Pyaro started walking faster. Finally, Pyaro got to the other side of the desert. But there was no river, instead there was only a road and spiky cacti. Poor Pyaro…He had to sleep without drinking any water in the dry desert.
author: Raghav  Krishna
illustrator: Greystroke; Muniza Shariq; Ninoshka Dias; Priya Kuriyan; Rajiv Eipe; Sanjay Sarkar; Vinayak Varma

title: Picnic
text: There were five friends...... Monkey,Mouse,Rabbit, Squirrel and bear. There was one garden in the forest. One day, all went for the picnic. All played hide and seek. They played thief and constable. They ran around alot. They played for long. Monkey said, ' Lets eat something now. Let us bring something." All brought onething or other. Rabbit brought carrot. Bear brought cabbage. Squirrel brought tomato. Mouse brought radish. Everything was washed, cut and mixed. It was now turn to eat. Bear was surprised. He said," Wow! It is amazing. What should it be called." Mouse said," This is chaat." Rabbit said," This is Pachranga," Squirrel said," No, it is mixture." Monkey said," This is called salad. Eat well. Be strong." Mouse said, " Now onwards I will eat this only. I will grow to a lion when I am big. All laughed.
author: Rita Bansal

title: MY ROLO
text: Tina and Mina were sitting in the room and looking outside the window.A green colour car was coming on the road with her shining line on the front. Tina caught her view and overwhelmed to see that car, Tina is very fond of car. The car went on their way and thus Tina became sad that she would not get more time to see or even touch. Tina was thinking continuously for some days. After some days, a fair came in her town. both were very excited to go for fair. Mumma, Daida, Mina and Tina went for fair visit. All had enjoyed many rides,, golgappa and ice-cream. All were setting off for home. Tina saw same kind of car in the toy shop. She ran and started talking to shopkeeper. Mumma, Daida and Mina followed her and they listened both conversation. Then Daisa asked for the price, which is not much expensive. Daida purchased the car for the Tina. Tina became very happy and named her toy car"Rolo".
author: Sarika vidhya
illustrator: Gauri  Sirur; Kavya Singh; Keo  Phunphalla; Natasha  Mehra

title: The big woes of Little Gyan Dev!
text: Gyan Dev was a nine-year-old boy who loved books and hated going to school equally. His parents, Bhimi and Ramavtar, could not understand why, as he was good at studies and had many friends. Bhimi and Ramavtar allowed Gyan a week’s off from school, with a single condition that they would ask him one question at the end of the week and he would have to answer honestly. Gyanu could not believe that his parents agreed and was overjoyed! Gyan submerged himself in his favourite books. He was an excellent narrator too; his friends enjoyed his passionate narrations. Perhaps, that was a huge motivator. Two days went by and he was brimming with ideas that needed an audience. Excitedly he went see his friends one by one, but to his dismay all were at school. In the evening Gyan visited his best buddy Aditi, and told her about the one week no school plan! Aditi felt a little jealous. Lets listen to your narration with our gang for an hour and then we all need to complete our homework, there is too much already! ” “Just an hour?” asked Gyan. “Sorry.,” replied Aditi. Gyan had the best one-hour of his day. He had to wait another 24 hours to be with his friends. Gyan’s mother had relived him from regular routines also; there was no bath time, sleep time, or any other time that he loathed. At night, when the lights went out, Gyan kept turning and tossing as he could not sleep, staring into the darkness waiting to be embraced by sleep was a very boring thing to do; all book monsters felt alive and close! He asked his mother in the morning, “ I can’t sleep, am I unwell?” “Gyanu, you could not sleep as you were not as tired as you used to be!” Bhimi explained smilingly. As Gyan ate his breakfast he could not stop thinking of the lonely day ahead and his school days. His books were always there, but no one to share the ideas with! One evening after a story narration by Gyan, one of his friends, Parth said “Hey Aditi, that origami plane you made was amazing, it flew so high!” Aditi feeling proud of her creation replied “Yes! I learnt it from the new art teacher.! Gyan you know? Oh sorry, I forgot you don’t come to school these days. “ Gyan felt as a ghost during such gleeful conversations of school time fun. It was as if he was watching from away not being there. Gyan began to feel ill at ease. Even reading and ideas need inspiration and companionship. He thought to himself, probably life is better with school and routines. Finally the week was over. Gyan wondered staring into the book in his hand how every Sunday used to be so special after six days of school but not this Sunday. “Gyanu, the time has come to answer the question.” Said Ramavtar in a comforting tone. “Yes dad, ask away! ” Gyan said. “Gyanu, do you enjoy being at home?” asked Ramavtar calmly. “ No dad, I feel I need, my books, routines and friends, to be free and happy!” “ Gyanu, I understand, remember routines are not made to burden us, they are meant to make our lives happier and organised.” Explained Bhimi. There was a warm family group hug and Bhim could not have been happier to see his class teacher on Monday!
author: Siddhant  Chaturvedi
illustrator: 211 Studio; Angie & Upesh; Anja  Venter; Fahad Faizal; Ruchi Shah; Shailja Jain Chougule; Students of  Himalayan Public School

title: Nothing without mobiles
text: Once there lived a boy named Ameya. He always saw his mother,father and his elder sister Priya working on mobiles. Whenever he asked his parents for mobile,they would say"Go do studies, solve sums etc.". One day Ameya was talking with his friends."My mother never lets me have mobile"said Ameya. Umesh said "Because you are not pushing her to do that." "I told my my mother that I will not eat if you don't give me a mobile." said Aarvi. It was 7 in the evening, S o Ameya ran home with an idea in his head. The next morning Ameya talked to his mother about the phone, but she didn't listen. So he began to throw tantrums of not going to school till he gets a mobile. His mother came to him and said"We will give you a mobile if you listen to what I will tell you now." "OK!"said Ameya. Mother explained something about playing on mobiles. She said, "When we were kids like you, there were no mobiles. We would just play with our siblings and friends and also do studies with them." We used to have lot of fun playing cards, ludo, carrom and much more with our parents and relatives. If you built a robot in a game you will not be able to play with it,but if you built it with toys like 'Mechanix' you can play with it. If you cook some food in a game,how will you know its taste, aroma, texture in real? Instead wont it be more exciting to gather all your friends and cook and eat together! You can surely have mobile to play, but for some time, only when you finish all your daily chores. "Sorry mama! Now I understand."I promise, I will do exactly as you and Dad say. Thanks Mama! "If you make robot with the help of toys like 'Mechanix' or 'Robotics' it will be more fun.You can call your friends home, cook and eat together. Doesnt that sound more exciting!" Ameya understood his mistake and promised his parents that henceforth he would listen to them always.
author: Vagmi Ghanekar

title: my little silly kitty
text: My silly billy kitty name is Claire.She is a girl. Let me tell you what she loves to do hide under...PANS! She is a very very silly. My silly billy kitty loves to jump.She loves to play.I'll tell you a secret she jumps up to the fridge! I love my little kitty and she loves me.THE END.

title: The Secret of the Waterfall
text: Chapter 1 An Exciting Plan for the Holiday Once, there were three children and a dog. Their names were Josephine, Jeremy and Jack. Timothy, the dog, almost understood everything the Three said. One day, the four of them were at the beach near Josephine and Jeremy’s home. Jack was their cousin. “What should we do this summer holiday?” asked Josephine, the youngest. “What about horse-riding?” replied Jeremy. “Good idea!” said Jack. “Woof! Woof! Woof!” said Timothy. “I’ll count that as a YES,” said Jack. “Anyways, we’ve got to ask mom and dad first.” Josephine said. “Wait, first we need horses,” said Jack, “or else we can’t go even though your mom and dad approve.” “Good point.” Jeremy agreed. Everyone was excited, even Timothy. ﻿ Chapter 1 An Exciting Plan for the Holiday O nce, there were three children and a dog. Their names were Josephine, Jeremy and Jack. Timothy, the dog, almost understood everything the Three said. One day, the four of them were at the beach near Josephine and Jeremy’s home. Jack was their cousin. “What should we do this summer holiday?” asked Josephine, the youngest. “What about horse-riding?” replied Jeremy. “Good idea!” said Jack. “Woof! Woof! Woof!” said Timothy. “I’ll count that as a YES,” said Jack. “Anyways, we’ve got to ask mom and dad first.” Josephine said. “Wait, first we need horses,” said Jack, “or else we can’t go even though your mom and dad approve.” “Good point.” Jeremy agreed. Everyone was excited, even Timothy. After the three asked, the got the horses. “Mom said we only need two horses,” said Jeremy, “Josephine and I on one and you on one.” They went to the farmer’s barns to get the horses. “Shall we take Mary and Trotter?” asked Josephine. “Yes,” said Jack, “they look like the strongest.” They brought Mary and Trotter home and put them in the field. “Now, let’s pack up,” said Josephine. Soon, it was time for bed. The three fell asleep as soon as their heads hit the pillow. Timothy always slept on Josephine’s legs. Josephine liked to have him there. Chapter 2 The Journey begins… T he next morning, they got on the horses and set off onto the hills. “Should we have lunch at Rabbit Hill?” asked Jack. “Yes, let’s eat there,” said Jeremy. Soon, they arrived Rabbit Hill. Jack and Jeremy spread out the picnic mat on the grass while Josephine unpacked the food from their bags. Suddenly, Timothy barked and barked. Nearby was a couple. They were reading a treasure map. Timothy did not like them. The couple glared at the children, then kept reading the map. “They look wicked and mean,” said Josephine, “I don’t like them.” They asked a boy who had his tent next to theirs if he knew the couple. “Wearing jeans and jerseys?” the boy asked. “Yes, and carrying a big bag with them,” Jack answered. “They are Maggie and Dick, who seldom talk to others. A very mysterious couple I would say,” The boy told them. “Thanks,” said Josephine. But, Jeremy was interested in the map. Could it lead to a treasure of silver and gold? Jeremy was determined to get the treasure. After lunch, Jeremy told Josephine and Jack his plan, “We will try to steal the map at night, ok?” After Jack and Josephine agreed, Jeremy planned when to go. At night, Jeremy and Jack woke Josephine up. They crept over to the couple’s tent and saw them asleep. They saw a map in a bag lying beside Dick. Soon as Jeremy’s hand reached the bag, Maggie suddenly turned over, facing towards Jeremy, with her eyes closed. “Phew!” Jeremy thought, sweating, “she almost saw us!” They quietly took it and returned to their tent. Josephine switched on her torch to read the map. “This leads somewhere near Gloomy Water River. “Jeremy concluded. “Shall we go?” asked Josephine. “Certainly,” said Jeremy, “I doubt if the treasure was stolen and hidden by some wicked people. We have to find the treasure before Maggie and Dick, and hand it over to the police.” Early next morning, the Four set off for Gloomy Water River. The couple didn’t notice the map was gone yet. The Four climbed over two mountains, went through a few valleys, and finally reached Gloomy Water as the Sun set. “We’ll camp here tonight,” said Jeremy. “What an exhausting day!” exclaimed Jack. “We’re racing with Maggie and Dick to get the treasure,” said Jeremy. “Let’s start searching tomorrow.” Chapter 3 The Gloomy Water and the Waterfall T he next morning, they woke up and found that Maggie and Dick’s tent was quite near to them. “They’re still asleep,” Josephine whispered, “let’s start searching before they wake up.” After a quick breakfast, Jeremy took the map out. “I think the treasure should be hidden somewhere in the river,” said Jack, “which means it might sit on the sandy bottom of the river.” “Perhaps it’s in a sunken boat under water?” said Josephine. “Let’s sail on the river and see,” said Jeremy. The Four found a little paddle boat in a boat house nearby. SPLASH! They heaved it into the water. Then Jeremy went in the boat. He helped Josephine in, then Jack. Timothy followed and jumped in. The boat rocked violently as they went farther from the bay. They followed the map and finally reached a waterfall. “Wait,” Jeremy said, “the route shown on the map leads straight through the waterfall.” “What?” said Josephine. “We’ll have to go through the waterfall then?!” said Jack. “No way! We’ll get all wet!” Josephine cried. Tim licked her hand. “As wet as Tim’s licks!” Jeremy teased, “come on! Let’s do it!” Suppressing their worries, the Three paddled towards the waterfall. Amazingly they went straight through without getting wet. “I think the waterfall is an illusion,” said Jeremy. “A what?” asked Josephine. “An illusion.” said Jack. “something that feels like real and looks real. But if you pretend it’s not there and just walk through, you won’t get wet.” Chapter 4 The Secret Behind the Waterfall T he Four looked around. They were surrounded by lots of rocks. Jeremy looked at the map and back at the rocks. “I think the treasure is behind the rocks.” Jeremy said. They paddled around and looked behind all the rocks. But all they found was a plastic bottle and a piece of tissue. “Wait,” said Josephine, “look at that last piece of rock again. They paddled back to the last rock. “Look!” said Josephine. Behind the rock was a tunnel. “Shall we go down the tunnel?” asked Jack. “Yes,” said Jeremy, “we will. Does anyone have a rope?” “What for?” asked Josephine and Jack at the same time. “To tie the boat to a rock.” Jeremy replied. “You are lucky. I have a long one,” said Josephine. She handed over the rope to Jeremy, who tied the boat to a rock. The Four got out of the boat and walked into the tunnel. It was pitch black in the tunnel. “Let’s use our torches,” said Josephine. They switched on their torches and kept going. Suddenly Josephine yelled. In front of her was a large treasure chest. There was a key in the lock. Jeremy turned the key and opened the chest. Inside was countless diamonds, jewels and valuable jewelry. Jeremy carefully picked up a golden crown. “I think I know where these came from,” he said. “Wait! Wait! Wait!” said Josephine. “First, how should we lift the chest and carry it back to the boat?” “Beats me,” said Jack. “Let’s have a try,” said Jeremy. The three tried to lift the chest up. Tim slid under the chest to help. “Good idea, Tim,” said Josephine. “Yes,” said Jeremy, “he’ll definitely help us carry the chest.” They managed to get it out of the tunnel and onto the boat. But soon they found themselves in another big trouble ---- Maggie and Dick were also out on a boat. They children looked through the waterfall. “I think we won’t be able to get away,” said Josephine, nervously. “We must hand over the treasure to the police. We will find a way to pass them!” said Jeremy. “Ah! I know! We can put our jerseys over the chest and pretend that is a pile of clothes.” suggested Josephine. “I doubt,” said Jack. “if our jerseys could cover up the whole chest.” “There’s no other better ways. Let’s try,” said Josephine, eagerly. Together, they quickly put all their jerseys on the chest. “Sounds like a good idea, Josephine,” said Jeremy. While Maggie and Dick were looking away from them, they rowed through the waterfall. But… Suddenly Maggie and Dick turned around and saw the children emerged from the waterfall. Chapter 5 Tim, the Hero T he children were surprised. Dick sneered, “well, well, well. Fancy meeting you thieves here!“ The children were even more surprised. How did Maggie and Dick get to know that they stole the map which is now inside Jeremy's pocket?“ "I bet that's the treasure, Dick." said Maggie, pointing at the pile of jerseys. "That's only jerseys and clothes," lied Jeremy. "Well, I wasn't even asleep when you nasty three crept into our tent to steal the map." said Dick. The children gasped. So that’s why Maggie knew that they had the chest. “Well, I’ll get that treasure in no time,” said Dick. He leaped for the chest. “Go, Tim!” said Jack, releasing Timothy. Tim leapt at Dick, who jumped back in surprise. “Y- Y-You got a dog?” spluttered Dick. Maggie and Dick hadn’t noticed Tim because he flopped down on the bottom of the boat when they set off. “Dick is allergic to furs!” exclaimed Maggie, “AAARRRGGGHHH!!!!” and both of them started to yell and shout. Dick began to sneeze and sneeze and sneeze. Tim jumped back onto the boat and the children quickly rowed past Maggie and Dick’s boat and back to the tent. After putting the contents of the chest in their backpack, they headed to the nearest police station. GRRRR!!! A-a-choo!!! Chapter 6 The Journey Ends A t the station, “so they’re Maggie and Dick?” the policeman asked, after the children told him the story of their adventure. “Well, well, well. Officers go get them!” said the officer, who turned to the children and continued, “Maggie and Dick had been stealing treasures around the world. They planned to sell these treasures in France. Thank you all for stopping Maggie and Dick and handed over the treasure to us.” “Shall we give you a lift home?” asked the officer. “Thank you, officer. This holiday journey is long enough,” said Jeremy. Later as the children arrived home, they repeated the story to their mom and dad. “Well, it looks like you guys had another memorable adventure this summer,” said dad. “Yeah…. It was fanta-stick!” said J eremy. Everyone laughed. ~ The End ~
author: Zita LO

title: The Power of One
text: Tring tring tringggg! It was the last day of school. The students of Class 6 gathered around Didi's table for lunch. They passed food around and dipped into each other's dabbas. Ajay fed a roti to the school dog, Gundu. "What are your plans for the summer vacation?" Didi asked the students. "I will practice my football skills, just like Messi," said Anita. "I'm going to make lots of toys," said Rafiq. "I'm going to eat vada-pav and samosa-kachori every day," said Vivek. "I am going to Lonavala Adventure Park," said Pragati. "They have so many rides there. Like the water slide and the train that goes up and down!" said Thomas. "And Pragati is going to ride them all." "But the tickets are 60 rupees," said Faiza. "You are so rich Pragati." "No," replied Pragati. "I am only spending the money that I saved." "You can go to the amusement park too," said Didi, smiling. "You just have to save like Pragati did." "Yes," agreed Pragati. "If we save just one rupee every day, it can add up to a big amount." "Saving a rupee a day is easy," said Seema. "Let's try? Then maybe all of us can go to the adventure park." Everyone agreed. When the holidays ended, they would go to the adventure park together. Summer holidays were full of fun. Rafiq made toys from whatever he found lying around. He sold some of them to his cousins, and saved one rupee for every day of the holiday. Prasad taught his younger brother maths, and saved one rupee each day from the money his father gave him for it. Devi saved one rupee every day from the ice cream money her mami gave her. Ajay's father was the head gardener for the municipality gardens. He gave Ajay one rupee for every sapling that he helped him plant. It was the first day of school. Didi helped the class add up the money that they had saved. Each student had saved enough to buy themselves a ticket. Everyone celebrated, except Ajay. "What happened, Ajay? Are you not happy with how much you saved?" asked Anjali. "I didn't save any money," Ajay replied. "Gundu fell sick last week, so I spent all my savings to buy him medicines. And now I have no money for the adventure park." The class fell silent. Finally, Nimbaram spoke up. "Don't worry, Ajay. We can all save a little more together and buy you a ticket." Nimbaram was right. Within a week, Class 6 had saved enough money for Ajay's ticket! Finally, Class 6 was at the amusement park. "AAAAAA!" Rafiq and Prasad squealed from the giant wheel. Whooosh! Faiza splashed out of the water slide. Schoop! Ajay and Anita shot out of the water coaster. Class 6 had a great time, and all because they had saved one rupee a day! How do I start saving? 1. Decide on a fixed amount of money you can save in a day or a week. It can be as low or as high as you please. 2. Make a piggy bank out of a small box or an old tin to keep the money you save safely. 3. Resist the temptation to take money out of it! 4. Keep a record of how you are spending your money. This will help you see if you can spend less and save even more.
author: Payoshni Saraf

title: Gopi
text: He does not like anything. He gets angry on everything. Happiness, too, shies away. This was the talk of village when anyone saw Gopi. Nobody called him by his name. But he was not like this since beginning. He used to be happy and ever singing boy. Suddenly, one day he was a changed boy. How it happened? Just read out..... One day Gopi mother said,"Gopi, go and get water from the well. I have pain in my feet".Gopi said,"Do not worry. I just fetch water from the well." People used to bring water from well in ancient times. People used to line up their utensils in a row. The water was filled as per their turn. Mother said," Son, I have already queued my utensil early morning at five. You just go hurriedly and fill it." By then, I will get ready with food for you. Gopi reached well in his playful mood. he searched his utensil. It was no where. He asked from his neighbor aunt too, if she had seen his utensil. She refused. All of sudden, his eyes fell on some naughty boys. They were playing with that just like ball. He recognized it and ran towards them. He politely requested them to return his utensil. The naughty boys paid no attention. Rather they pushed him back. They also put allegation on him, " This is our utensil. how dare you to steal it!" Gopi was shaken by their outrageous behavior. He got furious because he was called a thief. Many people who heard this noise, gathered around. Some people believed those naughty boys and gave Gopi a good thrash. Poor Gopi could do nothing. Nobody was there to listen him. 'Thief! Thief!" This sound made him thief in people eyes. Gopi was now filled with anger only for everyone.When he came back home, his mother was too distressed deeply. His mother tried to console his son that people must have misunderstood you. Sometimes truth is beyond what one sees at the spot. No one spares ones time to go to depth of truth. We should not stand all people in one row. But Gopi was not ready to listen and agree upon her mother. And next day, he too started same things that naughty boys used to do. He was called angry man and irritable boy. People started complaining about him to his mother. Mother got tired of his continuous daily complaints. She could not make out how could she change her son. She was sitting deep in her thoughts. Her eyes fell on a bird. It was trying hard again and again to fly its little ones. But little ones could not fly. The bird thought a trick. The bird brought food grain for its little one but perched on a distant branch of the tree. The bird called its little ones," Come, take your food grain." The little ones were hungry. Their paws were in movement. One was too young but other could make out to reach her mother after four - five trials. It had its food. The bird's consistent effort and determination showed the success. Gopi's mother was inspired by it. She took some firm decision. she wanted to show his son path of goodness. She went to her neighbor and said to tell his son,"Do not search for her mother." The neighbor was shocked and surprised. When Gopi came back home, he called his mother many times. Mother was nowhere. Gopi was trembling. He was roaming in village silently. No one paid any attention to him. All were scared of his anger and misbehavior. He looked for his mother in each and every corner of the village. Mother was nowhere. At last, he sat under a tree and started crying. People came near him and asked the reason of his crying. Gopi was surprised to see so many people around him. These were same people who once disliked him. All were concerned today. Before Gopi could utter a word, Neighbor said,"Gopi's mother has gone somewhere. Let us find her.All said in chorus," Sure." All children, ladies and gents were in small group and went in different directions to find his mother. Gopi came back home. All were very supportive and consoled him. All promised to find his mother. They said, " We will search again in morning if we do not get her now." Gopi was a little disappointed. He started crying again. Suddenly, he heard his mother voice. His mother was saying today. And Gopi was listening. Mother said," There are some people in the universe who believe wrong people and tease innocent ones. These are not trustworthy. We need different strategy to teach right. It does not mean that we should also be bad like them." Gopi understood the whole. Next day, Gopi apologized of his bad behavior from all people.
author: Rita Bansal
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Angie & Upesh; Naina Bhardwaj; Phidi Pulu; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Rajiv Eipe; Sanjay Sarkar; Soumya Menon; Suvidha Mistry; Vartika  Sharma

title: Junuka and the Rice Rakshasas
text: Junuka is visiting her Anaideo's* village during the holidays. She has decided to grow some rice for her school project. "Be careful of the rice rakshasas," Anaideo tells her. Everyone in the village is afraid of the rice rakshasas. *'Anaideo' means grandmother in Assamese. But Junuka is not afraid. Junuka must plough the field before she sows the rice seeds. "This will take all day. I wish I had some help," she thinks. Suddenly, she senses something creeping towards her... KHAS KHAS KHAS "AAAAAA!" shouts Junuka. "Rice rakshasa!" The rakshasa flashes its claws and... "Aha! Your soil is ready for planting." SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH "I'm Trakshasur," says the rice rakshasa. "Climb on, I'll help you sow the seeds." Junuka thinks for a minute. Then she climbs on Trakshasur's back. He carries her as she scatters the seeds. They flood the field with water. Over time, the seeds become seedlings. "Time to move them to the big field," says Trakshasur. Junuka pulls out the seedlings and Trakshasur bundles them up. Now they go to get the big field ready. Trakshasur ploughs the big field and Junuka floods it. The soil becomes soft, muddy and ready for planting. Then Junuka hears a slimy, wet sound... "SLLUUUUUURRP!" "AAAAAA!" shouts Junuka. "Rice Rakshasa!" "This is Plantasur. She will help us plant," says Trakshasur. Plantasur picks up the seedlings with her long, red tongue. She bites the mud. She plants dozens of seedlings with every bite. Soon the field is full of seedlings. Junuka puts up scarecrows to protect the seedlings. The rice grains bloom and soon it is harvest time. Junuka hears a sound in the bushes... DRRRRRRRRRRRRRR "AAAAAA!" shouts Junuka. "Rice rakshasa!" "This is Harvasur. She will help us harvest," Plantasur tells her. THWACK! CRUNCH! THOOO! Harvasur cuts the crop, traps the stem and spits out the straw. Until there is a mountain of grain. "Now we must remove the husk from the grain," says Harvasur. "Come, let's visit our friend Dhanasur at the mill." They find Dhanasur in a dark corner of the mill. He's a rakshasa with two heads. "Hello," says Junuka. "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!" shouts Dhanasur. "A human child!" "This is Junuka. You have to help her," says Harvasur. Dhanasur opens one mouth wide and Junuka pours rice into it. Finally, they have shiny, white rice. That night, there is a harvest feast at the village. Junuka brings the rakshasas with her. Junuka shows the villagers all the rice they harvested together. "The rakshasas only want to help us," she says. BURRRRRRRRRRRRP! Junuka has a great time at the feast. And so do the rice rakshasas! Machines used in rice farming Rice farming is a long and difficult process. But with the help of her four friends, Junuka can grow rice easily. Just like the four rakshasas, these machines make farming quicker and easier: Mechanical plough Like Trakshasur, this machine helps farmers to loosen and prepare the soil for sowing rice seeds. Rice transplanter Like Plantasur, this machine helps the farmer plant rice seedlings. Combine harvester Like Harvasur, this machine cuts the crop, collects it and separates the stems from the rice grains. Rice husker Like Dhanasur, this machine removes the brown husk from the grain to give us white rice.
author: Preeti Hatibarua; Priyadarshini Gogoi

title: When I Grow Up, I'll Have a House
text: When I grow up, I’ll have my own house. The books will crawl up the walls And lie on the floors and sprawl on the bed. They’ll take over, yes, and if I have to, I’ll sleep… with my body curled around books. like this like that like this like that like this like that like this like that In my house, there’ll be felt pens And glitter pens and paints And brushes and fountain pens with Thick nibs and pencils with all kinds of points. Fat points for fat lines and thin points for thin lines and in-between points for writing secret letters to spies. Also oil paints and watercolours And fat-fat-FAT books of paper. If you say, “ Paint inside the lines”; If you say, “The sun is never that colour”, My bodyguard Lothar will show you out In the nicest possible way. In my house, there’ll be a sack full of blocks. A million gazillion pieces of blocks. Not for me. I don’t like blocks. But I will like everything else in my house And I hate to share. So you can have the blocks And build anything you want. Please. Sorry. Thank you. In my house, I’ll run the clocks Slow in the holidays, slow in the mornings So slow that I can sleep the dozy out of my eyes. When I get up, I’ll dig my nose And turn the boogers Into a hard lump of green and yellow Snot which I will keep under my pillow. It will be part of my WORLD-FAMOUS, NEVER-BEFORE, NEVER-AGAIN SUPERTENDOUSTIC, AMASTAZOUNDING SNOT-BALL COLLECTION (Pride of India) Yes, I am going to have A snot-ball collection. It’s my house, not your house. You collect what you want. I collect what I want. See? In my house, I’ll keep a feather And all kinds of weather A saddle of leather A horse and cow together. In my house, a poem will rhyme All the time. Me and my pink panda Will sit on the verandah. Me and my red pup Will drink from the same cup Me and my brown bear Will share a rocking chair. Then if someone says, “Go inside,” I’ll be outside. In my house, the inside will be the outside And the outside will be the inside. In my house, I’ll have a room With a funeral band going Because a funeral band is fun If no one’s dead. Really. Phoom- pOOm -OOm I’ll also have a dare room. It will be a bare room. It will be a gloom room. It will be a doom room. You have to be brave And sleep in a grave. And if you put your hand under the pillow… Ooh. Oooooh. OOOOOOH. When I grow up, When I grow up, Such a long time To when I grow up. And I need that home NOW!
author: Jerry Pinto

title: House on the Hills
text: I live in Delhi. Today I am going to introduce you to my friend whose name is Garo. Garo is from Eastern state of Meghalaya. Meghalaya is a very beautiful state. It is known for its greenery and special types of homes. So why not enquire from Garo and learn more about Meghalaya and the special types of homes. Garo: Thank you Rohan for introducing me. So, let me take you to a trip to Meghalaya. A special type of home is built in Meghalaya. These homes are different from the other normal homes. These homes are not built using very costly materials. These are built from bamboo, wood and dry grass which grows in the jungle. Rohan: Only using bamboo, wood sticks and dry grass? Are these homes long-lasting? And what happens during rains? Garo: Yes, yes…. These homes are long-lasting and also stay put during rains. These homes are made in a special way. The roofs of these homes have a slanting or sloping roof which does not allow the rain to stay over it. The water slips and drains down from these types of roofs. These homes are made upon long bamboo sticks to stay safe during heavy rainfall. These homes are made together by the entire family. The tradition of building these kinds of homes is transferred from one generation to another. These beautiful homes add more charm to the beauty of Meghalaya.
author: Deepa Gagwani

title: I will( not) go to school
text: It was morning! Mother called in routine," Aarvin, get up. Get ready. You need to go school." " I do not like to go to school. I will not go," said Aarvin. " You must go to school," mother said smilingly. Aarvin did not agree.he said," Mother, I really do not want to go to school." Mother tried to make him understand and said," See! Your father is also going office, I have also a lot of work to do. Your all friends will also be in school." But Aarvin was adamant. " Ok! Do not go to school", mother said. " What will you do now the whole day?" "I will play! I will play! I will play the whole day", said Aarvin in a very playful mood. He ran outside. Bhola kaka was attending the plants outside in garden. " Will you play with me, kaka? I am not going school today," Aarvin said joyfully with a clap. " Not at all! I have to water the plants. I have other tasks to do too. I can not play with you." There was a sparrow in its nest in the garden. Aarvin asked," Sparrow, will you play with me?" Sparrow said," I can not play. I need to feed my youngones." One hen was roaming there. Aarvin asked," Dear hen, will you play with me?" Hen said,"Aarvin baba, I have to sit on my eggs to hatch it. I can not play with you." Suddenly, Aarvin eyes fell on bee hives. He asked bees," Will you play with me?" Bees said," We can not play. We have to make honey." A cow was grazing grass in cow shed. Aarvin asked," Will you play with me?" Cow said," Aarvin, I can not play. Milking is to be done just now." Several goats were going on the road. Aarvin asked," Sister, will you play with me?" The goat said," No, dear we have to go for grazing." Aarvin was very sad. All were busy in their tasks. No one has a little time for him to play. Aarvin thought, only if I was in school, I would have been with my friends. Mona Miss would have told nice stories. She must have taught wonderful things. I could also play with my friends in the ground. Aarvin ran towards home. It was lunch time. Father was also at home for lunch. We all had our food together. Father said," Why did you not go to school, Aarvin?" " I wanted to play", Aarvin said," But nobody came to play with me, Each one was having some important task to do." Father said," What will you do tomorrow, now?" " I will go to school tomorrow", said Aarvin happily. " Because Aarvin likes to go to school," said three of them in chorus.
author: Rita Bansal
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Harshvardhan Gantha; Kabini  Amin; Madhuri Purandare; Ouk  Ratha; Padmanabh; Partho Sengupta; Rijuta Ghate; Sarah Bouwer; Sheetal Thapa; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Zainab Tambawalla

title: We Can Stay Safe
text: I are staying safe at home. We hope that you are too! Do not go out if you feel unwell. If we get a fever, a cough, or it gets hard to breathe, we will first call up our doctor or the help line to tell us what to do. I felt sick in my tummy once... I just ate too much! Why Is Neema Singing Happy Birthday? Written by Bijal Vachharajani Illustrated by Priya Kuriyan Neema stays safe by washing her hands often and well. She uses soap and she sings for 20 seconds. Happy birthday to me, Happy birthday to me, Happy birthday, dear Neema, Happy birthday to me! Happy birthday to me, Happy birthday to me, Happy birthday, dear Neema, Happy birthday to me! Uma Versus the Virus Written by Meera Ganapathi Illustrated by Renuka Rajiv If you want to cough or sneeze, Make sure you use Atishoo! please. If a tissue can't be found, Hurry, bring your elbow 'round. Farida Plans to Not Touch Her Face Written by Maegan Dobson-Sippy Illustrated by Jayesh Sivan Farida keeps her hands busy. She shares seeds with the birds. Cheep cheep cheep! “If we don’t touch our faces, then the virus can’t make us sick!” she tells Amma. Who Returned Bhaiya’s smile? Written by Sanjana Kapur Illustrated by Sunaina Coelho Bhaiya feels the world is getting scary. His monster friend gets bigger and bigger. Dukduk has eaten up Bhaiya's smile. Bhaiya talks to Mama and Papa and plays with Chiru. Then he feels less alone. Now Bhaiya does not have to feel locked up. Meera and Ameera Keep a Safe Distance Written by Nimmy Chacko Illustrated by Lavanya Naidu Ameera, did you hear? There’s a new virus that makes people very ill! ACHOO! KHAU-KHAU! If we are too close, the virus can jump from them to us. We must stay six feet away. Good thing our paper boat is ready! Nani’s Staying Inside Her House Written and illustrated by Deepa Balsavar Now is not the time to roam. Nani wants you safe at home. The park can wait another day, Just for now, indoors you stay. Nani says: Do what’s right. Stay indoors, day and night. And if you can, do a good deed, So many others are in need.
author: Lea Shaver
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Jayesh Sivan; Lavanya  Naidu; Priya Kuriyan; Rajiv Eipe; Renuka Rajiv; Sheena Deviah; Sunaina  Coelho

title: Helping hand
text: He was one of topper student in studies. He used to excel in sports too. He was having very friendly nature. Hence, he had so many friends. Rehan had a sister named Mariam. She was very chirpy and naughty. But she loved her brother very much. Rehan's father was software engineer. His mother was having her boutique. Rehan's father used to give him pocket money every month. This month, Rehan requested his father," Please give me Rs.50/- more." " Why so dear? What extra expense has come on your way this month? All your wishes are fulfilled by us," said father in harsh tone. " Please give for this month only. You may give me less money next month," said Rehan sheepishly. Rehan never spent in useless things. His father gave him Rs. 50/- extra and warned him, " I am giving this time only. I will not give next time." After doing studies, Rehan was getting ready to go out. Mariam said," Where are you going, bro?" " I am going to a book store. I need one book." " I will also go with you. I also need one glitter pen for making card." Rehan agreed. Mariam took money from her piggy bank and went along. When Rehan reached to book store, he said," Please give me Sixth class arithmetic book." The shopkeeper handed over book to him. Rehan gave him money. The shopkeeper counted the money and said," It is Rs.fifty less." Rehan told him surprisingly," I have given you total 400/-. I purchased it for this amount last time." " Now the price is increased to 450/-", said shopkeeper. Rehan had taken extra 50/- from his father to get this book for 400/-. He had no money now. He returned the book with heavy heart. Mariam asked shopkeeper for her glitter pen. When shopkeeper was finding pen for Mariam, she told her brother that she had seen this book on his study table only this morning. Rehan told Mariam that he needed that book for his friend, Vikram. He lost his book. His parents can not afford to buy new one. Mariam apprehended saddness and helplessness of his brother. She requested shopkeeper to cancel her glitter pen and give arithmetic book. Mariam gave her Rs. fifty to Rehan. Both came back home taking book in hand. At dinner time, mother came to Rehan room to call him for dinner. she saw new arithmetic book. She said," Have you lost your arithmetic book?" Before Rehan could say anything, Mariam narrated the whole story. His father over heard the whole conversation standing behind the door. He was very happy. He said,"Bravo! It is very good to help others." He hugged his both kids, Rehan and Mariam. Mother gave icecream after dinner to all. Next day, Rehan handed over book to Vikram. In return, Vikram too hugged him.
author: Rita Bansal
illustrator: 211 Studio; Priya Kuriyan; Rijuta Ghate; Sanjay Sarkar; Tapas Guha

title: A bear makes unforgettable memories
text: I just need to set my camera and start taking photos. Click Click Woah! The warm sunlight is so beautifully captured by my camera! I have no words to describe the breathtaking landscape in front of me. I hope the pictures I took will show this beauty of nature I'm telling you about. Click Click. Oh! But wait! Even though everything is so spectacular, there is something wrong. There is something I need. But what is that? Oh! Yes! Now I understand. My eyes are actually the best camera and my brain records the best memories. I will just sit here and soak it all in. No camera, no clicks. Just me and majestic Mother Nature. I will keep these memories forever in my heart. Now everything feels just right.
author: Elena Duta

title: The dancing diva
text: Once upon a time, there was a girl called Tiana. She is a little girl who lived in a poor family. Her dream is to become a ballerina. Each day after school, she would go to the dancing studio and look at the dancers how beautiful they are. But her mom doesn’t know that. After she watched them end the class, she will quickly run back home, her mom will be mad at her. Until one day, she saw this poster on her way back home. It says ‘ Everyone could be a dancer no matter who you are, if you’re blind, death, you can’t walk, or you have no hope, you will still succeed your dream. You just need to work hard, practice a lot, then you will succeed your dream. By Lilliana Carla. ‘After she saw this, she might have a chance. One night, when Tiana is sleeping she saw a gift from her grandmother. She might think that this is a pair of ballet shoes, when she opened it it was really ballet slippers. She told her mom immediately and asked her if she can go to ballet classes. Her mother said yes, by the next morning, she is going to try out her first class. They were going to ballet class now, Tiana was scared if her friends don’t like her. But mom said ‘ When you were small, you actually already know how to dance a little, so don’t be to hard on yourself, just have fun! ‘ Tiana said ‘ Ok mom. I will!’ After a while they had arrived at the studio. Mom gave her a big hug and left. Tiana took her bag and went in the studio. She went in to the register counter. After she registered, she went in to the classroom to meet her teacher. Luckily there were no students, only her teacher is here. Her teacher is called Ms Lia. She is very kind, caring and loves to dance. At first she fell a few times, she couldn’t get the grip on how to stand on tippy toes. But after she tried a few times, she got it. Each day after school, Tiana practiced her dance wearing her golden ballet shoes. She practiced and practiced, until it was time to have dinner. When she was eating, she sang her dance song along, because she loved it. She is really excited for tomorrow because she can learn to dance again. But tomorrow, it is her first time with other students. She’s nervous. Today’s the day, Tiana said to her mom ‘ Mom let’s go! It’s time. And mom, will the students laugh at me because I am bad at it? ‘ Mom said to her kindly ‘ Of course not! You are a well trained little girl. You dance very beautifully no one will ever laugh at you. ‘ When they arrived, Tiana quickly put in her ballet shoes and went in the classroom. But then ‘Ewww! Ewww! ‘ When she walked in, she saw a beautiful dancer dancing upon a cloud, she liners her feet up in the air like a butterfly. She landed on the floor gracefully and took a bow. Ms Lia said ‘Hi Tiana. This is Alina. She is going to be your teacher today. She is one of my students as well. I need to visit my grandma she has disease, be a good girl ok? Bye! ‘ The lesson has ended. After two weeks it’s time for Tiana’s performance l She wore a sparkly tutu, her golden shoes and a bow. Her mom and dad came to watch. The audience gasped, they all was shocked how beautiful she danced. After the show was over, she fell down of the stage, she sprang her ankle and fell, she couldn’t for a three years. Years had passed, her ankle was healed. She went back to the studio and learnt how to dance again. She was ready to perform on the big stage with soaks shining out the audience’s light. On that night, she danced a duet with a boy called the Dancers Dream. She danced happily and that’s how she succeeded her dream. This story tells us that a dream is not a dream, you just need to work hard, keep practicing and never give up. You will succeed your dream. This is the end of my story. Thanks for reading. Hope you like it. Bye!:)
author: Conan Unicorn
illustrator: Aimee  Ayres; Mary Anne Hampton; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: Mini' Wish
text: She ordered pizza for herself. She was enjoying it fully. She did not even ask once to Mini for courtesy sake. Mini also desired to have it. She expressed her desire to her mother when they came back home. " See! This is very costly.And also, I do not have enough money now. Your school fee is also pending to be paid," said mother. Mini suppressed her desire,seeing her mother helplessness. She went to park for good change. There was no one in the park. She stepped further and sat in between trees. " Mini, why are you sad?" Mini was surprised to hear sound. She turned around. Nobody was there. " I am in front of you." Mini saw that the sound was coming from the tree. " How can you speak?", said Mini surprisingly. " I am WISH TREE. I fulfill the desire of good and true children like you," replied the tree. Mini was amazed with joy. " Can you fulfill my desire too?" " That is why, I called you. Please tell me what do you want?" Mini was about to say that she wanted to have pizza. But she paused. She thought that there must be many children who wanted to have pizza. With this thought, she said," I want so many pizzas." " You are being greedy. How can you eat so many?", scolded the tree. " I will eat only one. I will give one to my younger brother, Bittooo. I will distribute rest of pizzas to the poor children who can not afford it," Mini clarified. " Bravo! I knew it already. I was just teasing you," said The WISH TREE laughingly. Mini got so many pizzas that the all pizzas were set in two huge pyramids. Mini and Bittooo sat on each pyramid respectively. Both had their pizza. After that, Mini stuffed the pizzas in carry bags. Mini and Bittooo went to nearby orphanage. The pizzas were distributed among all children. The remaining were distributed among street children. At last, one pizza was also given to Sheena aunty. Mini said," This is for your daughter." Mini and Bittooo came back home happily.
author: Rita Bansal

title: Hurry up! Mother
text: I woke up early morning. I rubbed my eyes. Mother was not in scene. " Mother!Mother! Come soon." Mother said loudly from other side," Yes, son. Get up. Freshen up." I take my bath in speed. I wear my shirt myself. I need to go early. " Mother, listen me." " Yes! I am coming." Mother assures him. " I need to boil milk". I will then come. I comb my hair. I button up my shirt. I get ready full. " Mother, come soon." Mother hands over dress to sister. She helps her to get ready. There is so much to do. But I am in hurry. " Mother, I am getting late". I take my bottle and bag. I wear my slippers too. " Now let us go. Mother, hurry up." Yes!, I am coming." Allow me to make a braid for your sister. I need five minutes more. Then we will go." I want to go just now. I am not going to wait. I am feeling like to cry. Sister has gone to school. And I am still here. " Okay, It is done. Only, I need to fill water." Mother always has something to do. " Mother, hurry up! I will not wait now." " Just let us move now. Just now." I pull my mother's hand out. " Arre! Let me switch off the light." Now we are out of home. Mother latches the home securely. " Let us go, my son." Now I am happy. I am with my mother. She is calling me lovingly her son. And I am going to school.
author: Rita Bansal

title: Anand
text: I go late, Mrs. Maskarenyas will be very angry. Unni uncle will say to pick garbage without leaving a ﻿single one. Anitha aunt cannot beare the smell. In the 4th cross street, there is a new family who are kind. But their dog is not like them. Alas! This takes time to clean. I like to go to saleem's house. Saleem and I are friends. He likes to play drums. I like to dance. It is time to go to school. Tata
author: Hayanthika S.M

title: Party in the Jungle
text: I am sad because nobody dances or sings in the jungle ", said Kukoo, "and I feel like dancing and singing." "That is because no one knows how to dance and sing," said Becto, "but, I have an idea! Why don't you teach others how to dance and sing! Then we can have a party in the Jungle!" "Come one! Let's start with you!" said Kukoo while giving Becto a few lines to sing. Now, whenever he gets time, Becto sings and dances! Becto's mother Gungun loved his dancing and singing. She taught him how to sing a few more songs. Now, wherever he would go, Becto would sing and dance. By practising over and over again, he became an expert in dancing and singing. Becto's friend Juju loved his dancing and singing and asked Becto to teach him too. Kukoo was very happy with the way Becto was practising. "Becto, you are a very fast learner!", said Kukoo while congratulating him. "Ma'am, I want to master singing and dancing very quickly, which is why I am working so hard," said Becto. To this Kukoo replied, "If you wish to learn quicker, then start teaching your friends too." "Yes ma'am!," Becto said as he went to his friends. "My friends! Come on! Come here! Let's have some fun by learning how to dance and sing," shouted Becto to all. First came Forgo, the Frog. Becto taught him how to dance and sing. Then came Dakdak the Duck and Hariyal the Parrot. Becto taught them how to sing and dance too. ﻿Together, they began practising how to dance and sing. By now, every animal in the jungle knew how to dance and sing. title: Padget Goes To School
text: Foreword For children: A lot of the readers of this book may not know what a sanitary pad is. A period (also called menstruation if you want a longer word) is a natural process because of which a woman bleeds for 5-7 days a week, every month. Similar to giving birth to a child, this process only happens in female bodies. A pad is an item worn by females when they are on their periods, to prevent the leakage of blood. This book is not only for females but for every gender and age group because periods are nothing to be ashamed of. They are a normal bodily process, and everyone should be aware of it. For parents and teachers: I hope that this book lets you open the discussion about periods with your children. It is important to talk about the changes in their peers’ and their own bodies to be able to understand them. We all have bodies. There is nothing to be ashamed of. Padget the Pad Padma the Pad: Padget's Mother Mr. Len the Ruler: Padget's Math Teacher Andy the Bandage: Padget's Friend Polly the Potted Plant: Padget's Friend Rolli the Rock: Padget's Classmate Ray the Eraser: Padget's Classmate Chloe the Colour Palette: Padget's Classmate Meet the Characters He wants to make new friends and learn new things at school. Padget is 7 years old now and is ready for his first day of school. He has been dreaming about this day for many years. Padget can’t wait to share it with his friends. Mother Padma has packed strawberries for his first day. On arriving school (“Object World Primary School”) he sees Andy the Bandage, Polly the Potted Plant, and many other objects he didn’t recognize. He couldn’t wait to speak to all of them On arriving school, he saw Andy the Bandage, Polly the Potted Plant, and many other objects he didn’t recognize. He couldn’t wait to speak to all of them. Mr. Len asked the class to add 4+3. His first class was math with Mr. Len. He was one of the first objects to raise his hand. Padget loved math. Mr. Len gave a chance to Rolli the Rock instead. Rolli said 6. But Padget knew it was 7. Soon the bell rang, and it was recess. Six They spoke about how scary Mr. Len is. Padget sat with his old friend Andy and a new friend called Chloe the Colour Palette. She was also in their math class. "What is 6+3?" he asked the class. The next day in math class Mr. Len asked another question. Padget waved his hand too, but Mr. Len ignored him. Nobody raised their hand. Except Padget. Padget knew that he must not speak out of turn. But he was very sad. Later that night, Padget told Mother Padma about what happened in his math class. Mother said, Some people are ashamed of objects like pads. So, they choose to ignore them and pretend like they don’t exist. “But even we are useful objects,” said Padget. That’s not fair! Next day when Mr. Len asked the class another question, only Padget raised his hand. Again. Mr. Len ignored Padget. Again. Padget stood up and said, I know the answer Mr. Len was furious. He said, Do not speak out of turn In his innocent voice, Padget said, “Sir, I am just like the other objects. I am useful too. Why don’t you treat me equally?” There was a moment of silence. Andy stood up then. He said, “I absorb blood like Padget too. He is just as useful as anyone of us here.” “We’re all useful objects, please treat us equally.” Soon all the students began to stand up. All of them said the same thing. Mr. Len was taken aback by this new group of students. He realized that he should have been fair to all of his students, no matter how different they were. He nodded towards Padget and told him to answer the question. The whole class clapped for Padget. Padget beamed and said, Fourteen Mr. Len understood his mistake and never treated any student wrongly again. Vocabulary with Padget! Arriving: Reaching Recess: Break Pretend: To act like Innocent: Harmless To be taken aback: To be shocked Beamed: Smiled

title: Ammu and the Sparrows
text: ​He waited and waited. All day he waited. But Ammu’s Amma and Accha didn’t come. They would come soon, any day, Ammu told himself. Crows came, pigeons came. He even heard a screech of parakeets somewhere. ​They didn’t come the next day. Nor the day after that. Ammamma threw a fistful of leftover rice on the parapet. The pigeons flocked down to peck at it. Ammu looked into their eyes. They stared back. Unblinking. Then the crows came. They were bold. They jabbed at blobs of rice and hopped closer. Ammu looked into their eyes. They stared back. And cocked their heads. ​He remembered the times when he, Amma and Accha had played together. Then suddenly the three of them were not together any more. ​Where were the little birds? “Maybe they don’t like rice,” Ammu thought. He spread a spoonful of porridge on the ledge. He left breadcrumbs. It had been four days, but they had still not come. ​Next morning, Ammamma was ready with bits of dosa. “Come,” she called him. Ammu sighed. Amma still hadn’t come. And the little birds still hadn’t come. ​Ammamma looked sad. Ammu asked her, “What are they called? The two little brown birds.” “Sparrows,” said his Ammamma. “Kili. Do you miss them? “No, I do not!” said Ammu. But his grandmother knew Ammu’s heart. “Amma sparrow and Accha sparrow must be busy,” she said. ​Suddenly they were there. The two little brown birds. ​“Which is Amma, which is Accha?” asked Ammu, his heart bursting with joy. He hoped that the pale, brown one was the Amma sparrow. It looked soft and gentle. “The one with big eyes, with lines around them, is Accha sparrow,” said Ammamma. ​That Sunday, Ammu and Ammamma sat down together to make a sparrow feeder. As they cut the holes and filled it with seeds, Ammamma said, “The court has not decided yet.” Ammu looked away, his eyes brimming. “They love you. You do know that? They need some time.” ​That evening three sparrows came. Not two. Three. Ammu wanted to leap and he wanted to dance. But he stood as still as a statue. He did not want to frighten the birds away. They hopped onto the feeder and hopped off, their beaks busy. ​“Are these the same sparrows?” Ammu asked. All sparrows looked the same to Ammamma, but she peered at them carefully and said, “Oh yes! Amma and Accha sparrow have even brought a baby sparrow along.” Ammu smiled.
author: Vinitha R

title: Black Hats White Hats
text: The Internet is an amazing network. People use it to do lots of different things. Whenever you use the internet to watch a video or send a message, your phone or computer sends and receives data. The Internet is an amazing network. People use it to do lots of different things. Whenever you use the Internet to watch a video or send a message, your phone or computer sends and receives data. Your data can be any information about you, from your favourite ice cream flavour to your birth date, your email password or your bank account number. Your passwords and personal information are sensitive data. It is very important that sensitive data is kept secret. This is because there are people on the Internet who might try to steal it! People who try to steal data are called hackers. Hackers steal data for many different reasons. Meet Agent B. He’s a black hat hacker. Black hat hackers steal data in order to harm people or help themselves. Agent B might steal your email password and send fake emails from your account. New Mail To: Sub: CC|BCC Congratulations! You won 50,000 rupees! Hit REPLY to get your money. Reply He might also steal your bank information and take money right out of your bank account. And who is that, sitting on the fence? That’s Agent G. He’s a grey hat hacker. Grey hat hackers steal data too, but they will not always use it to harm you. They may hack you first, and then offer to show you how to better protect your data—for a price. If you don’t agree, they might decide to harm you. But don’t worry! There are other people who work to protect people like you from hackers on the Internet. Meet Agent W. She is a white hat hacker. She ‘attacks’ the security systems that protect data in order to test them. This helps Agent W to find weaknesses and fix them. Click! Click! By doing this, Agent W and white hat hackers like her make sure that your data is protected. They make the Internet a safer place for everyone. You too can help white hat hackers keep you safe on the Internet! • Keep your password, name, address, the name of your school or any information about your family safe. • It is important not to talk to strangers on the Internet or share any personal information with them. • Don’t join any social media websites without the permission of a parent or guardian. • If someone tries to send you something inappropriate online, tell a grown-up you trust, like a parent, family member or a teacher. • Don’t share pictures of yourself online without your parents’ permission. • Don’t download or install anything on your computer without your parents’ permission. • If you have any questions about something you read, ask your parent or guardian. • If you are talking to someone online and they make you uncomfortable, remember you don’t have to talk back to them!

title: The boy with bad luck
text: There was once a boy called Jeremy. He always had bad luck each day. Every time he goes to school, bird poop will fall on his head. At school, he would have the lunch that was thrown in the garbage can. He always say to himself ‘ Is there anything that can be a good luck to me! ‘ Each day when he goes to school, he would wear a frown face to school. He didn’t laugh or smile at school. He just sat on his chair and waited for the school bells to ring and eat. His mom always encourage him to be happy and make some new friends, but he can’t. When he arrived at school each day, he would sit on a wall. People always looked at him asking if he’s ok? He told them ‘ My father died last night! I am so sad. Why do I always have the worst luck? ‘ Jeremy asked. A girl said ‘ Maybe because your father might have a disease and died. But I am sorry for you. ‘ He walked away, and went in the classroom. When he went in to the classroom, each student need to talk to the teacher how they feel today. But Jeremy always says It am feeling sad, so don’t talk to me ok? ‘ The teacher was silent ‘ Oh ok... ‘ He walked away and sat behind a student tall, to cover up his face. He also doesn’t like anyone noticing him. At lunch time, he would go back to his home to eta, but when he got home the food his mom cooked for him was rotten, because his mom can’t see anything, so she doesn’t know that that’s rotten. He said desperately ‘ Uhhh... I will never have anything good luck to me. ‘ He went back to school again. ‘Time for singing the school song! ‘ A teacher announced. All the students went to the hall and stranded they all sang perfectly except Jeremy, his singing voice was terrible, everyone looked at him. They stared at him for a long time. Some mean boys laughed at him. This wasn’t good. It’s but the time they go home. After school, everyone has left. Jeremy and his friend walked across the road. There were mean boys following them secretly, then they put a water bottle under Jeremy’s pants and said he peed on the floor. Everyone laughed. Jeremy was embarrassed. When he got back home, he stood out of his balcony crying with tears spreading out his eyes. His dog came out hiding behind the door. He cried and cried he praised ‘Dear Lord, could you please help me, can you please give just for one day, just give,e good luck. ‘He sobbed. He ran back in and hid under his wooden torn bed. It was night time, the sky was dark and shivering cold. Jeremy sat beside a wooden bench and looked in the sky, ‘ Hmmm.. I wish I could be some of the lucky kids one day. ‘He hesitated to himself. He saw a wishing star passed by he makes a wish and went back into his room and dreamt of being a lucky kid. This story tells us that we should always treasure the time you had in your life. You should always thank god for giving you a wonderful world. Some kids aren’t as lucky as us. They might have no food, no clothes, no games or books, so we should treasure what we have and don’t complain. No matter who you are just look at the bright side and there is the future ahead of you. This is the end of my story. Thanks. Bye!

title: A letter for Amma
text: Dearest Amma, I know you are smiling reading this letter from me as we just spoke on the phone a few hours back. Today evening when I was sketching, Manju Aunty brought some lovely sabudana vadas for me and said that I should be proud of you. I wanted you to know that I am very very proud of you. I know we will speak again on the phone tomorrow but I forget many things when I see your face. So, I am writing this letter to you to tell you everything that's on my mind right now! Amma, I am proud of you, but I am also a little worried, and I think everyone here is a little scared too. When Thatha and Paati are watching TV, they discuss serious things and Anna and I are gently led to another room to play. Last week though, I happened to see on the TV, so many sisters like you taking care of unwell people. I realized that you too are doing the same, and that there is something scary about it this time. I couldn’t sleep that night. Paati then told me a story. Let me tell you Amma. 'Once Krishna and his older brother Balaram were walking through a dense forest. Suddenly a very big rakshasa appeared before them. Balaram was very scared and asked in a trembling voice, “Who are you?” The rakshasa laughed and bellowed, “ahahaahaha, I am your fear”. Hearing this, Balaram was even more scared and the rakshasa grew even bigger. He stood like a tall, huge mountain in front of Balaram. Balaram fainted in fear. The rakshasa turned to Krishna who was playing his flute and roared, “Look at me, I am your fear!” Krishna smiled as he looked at the rakshasa and continued playing his flute. The rakshasa became smaller and smaller and smaller. The rakshasa was now almost the size of an ant. Krishna picked him up and put him in his pocket, and woke his brother Balaram up and showed him the little rakshasa. ' I think Krishna must have kept the little rakshasa to remind himself to be brave. I am sure you are carrying a little rakshasa in your pocket and it’s really tiny. Anna tells me that every time we act brave, our ‘courage’ part of the brain becomes more and more stronger. I told you I want to be a gymnast. And now I realize that along with making our body strong, we also need to make our mind strong. Amma, there are also some wonderful things happening around us. Yes Ma, I read in the newspaper, that thousands of flamingos have come to Mumbai. Looks like a beautiful carpet of pink on the blue lake. Anna explained that many birds and animals are roaming carefree, now that people are home. I am happy they are free, but I am sad that they can’t be with us together – all of us, free and happy together, caring for each other. I hope everyone who is sick feels good soon. I wish that everyone who is not at home, is back home soon too. And I will come back soon to you. Can we go and see the flamingos Amma? Or would they also have returned to their homes from where they’ve come? Whatever makes them happy.. I love birds, When I grow up I want to study birds too. Love and kisses, Akku

title: Giga's Birthday Cake is missing
text: Today, Chica and Gauri were in a rush to meet their Giga in Kerala. Her name is Laila, she is their grandma and she's going to turn 63 years old. Then they asked their Bhaya Aditya to get the cake and put it in a freezer, so they could carry it and put it with their luggage in the airplane. Their muma even packed some Kaju barfi and cupcakes to eat in the plane. They were so excited! When they sat in the plane, Aditya Bhaya said " oh no! The cake has gone missing." muma replied "it's one of your stupid jokes, Aditya". " You don't believe me, don't believe me. Chica and Gauri, you come with me. You'll see muma, I'll prove it to you " Aditya Bhaya says. The girls went giggling all the way because the was a common sight of Adi (Aditya) Bhaya arguing with muma. They weren't surprised because they knew that Aditya Bhaya was not responsible at all. They also knew they had to keep this a secret because if they told Giga then she would definitely cancel the party and sit at home eating mangoes and feel sad on HER birthday. So every hour, Mami and Mamu would call mama and ask her if they found any luck. They kept looking for the cake but couldn't find it. The girls and their mother gave up searching for the cake. But surprisingly, Adi Bhaya did not give up. He kept searching and searching for at least half an hour. But then even he gave up. He walked back to their seat, he told Muma that " muma, I'm sorry. I ate the cake and lied to you.I'm really sorry." Muma snapped back at him " well, I know you understand your mistake but there should be consciences. text: Not too long ago, there was a girl named Shivani who lived under Jasola Flyover, in Delhi. She loved learning new things and acquiring more knowledge every day. She was extremely smart and inquisitive and was extremely curious about everything around her. She loved school and she loved studying because it helped her find answers to all her queries of the universe. One day, she walked merrily to school, talking and laughing, as usual. The girls sang and danced, and discussed the previous topics taught in school and debated about different things they had learnt, skipping happily along the lane, all the way to school. She entered the class and unpacked her things, arranging and stacking her books along with the desk neatly, as usual. She straightened her sleeve smiled brightly at the teacher and cried, in unison, '"GOOD MORNING MISTER MEGHANATH". She took her seat and sat bolt upright, excited to learn the new concept that would be taught to her. The teacher looked sternly at Shivani. He held 2 papers in his hand and kept taking momentary glances at them. He continued to gaze at her with the same stern face, until he finally cleared his throat and said, " Shivani! Your Aadhar card is invalid! it states a different address, therefore you cannot study here anymore! You do not live in this locality! Shivani was absolutely and utterly thunderstruck. She did not understand. All her education, taken away by a piece of paper? Her friends, education, and fun taken away by this measly little paper? This was preposterous! This could not be happening. But it was. She murmured a goodbye to the class and dragged herself outside, sobbing all the way back home. Shivani's parents were construction workers. Since they got assigned different plots from time to time, they had to constantly keep moving. Shivani could not help it. She did not know what to do! She kept asking her parents to resolve the problem, but they were far too busy. They were always working to help provide for Shivani, But all the same, she was miserable. Shivani spent her time helping around the house and doing tasks to assist her parents, but she never forgot about her school. She spent all her time working, and thinking of the wonderful life that slid out of her firm grasp. Such wonderful friends, new things to discover and such carefree and joyful times. Shivani was sure that they were all over! One day, Shivani heard of a few teachers from an NGO who were always within the locality teaching children who could not go to school. Shivani became happier at thought of her life being handed back to her. She thought of her subjects, the students the teachers, and what all they would learn. She began to go there and soon became happier than ever! Then, all of a sudden, her problems were resolved! She and her parents would go with her NGO teachers, to update her Aadhar card, so she could continue leading her life. She was thrilled at the thought of returning to her school and meeting her old friends again! she was bursting with joy! Now, Shivani helps other children like her receive their documents to get an education. She helps at the NGO and today, Shivani has helped 22 children in her locality. She still spreads awareness about these causes, and continues to inquire about the problems of the universe and study to solve them!
author: Anahita Neogi

title: The Good Unicorn
text: Once in the land of unicorns, there was a unicorn who was very good. She loved to go to the magical unicorn park. She liked playing there.
