title: Search of puppy
text: They both live opposite to each other. They both play together daily. Vishu did not come today for playing so Pakhi ran towards his home. She saw that Vishu was playing with a little cute puppy. Puppy started barking. Pakhi was scared. Vishu said," Pakhi, do not get afraid. This is my pet. Lo! You feed him biscuit and pamper too." Pakhi started pampering him. Puppy was also seeing her with affection. Both became friends. Vishu said," Let us play ball." Vishu threw a ball at a distance and said," Go! Puppy go! Bring the ball." Puppy ran after ball. Pakhi and Vishu too ran. Arre! Where puppy is gone?Puppy was no where. Vishu started crying. Pakhi consoled him and said," Do not cry. Let us find him out." They both ran ahead. Arre! We have reached to road. There are so many cars. There are so many buses. It is so crowded. Both started crying now. In the meanwhile, both saw a policeman coming towards them with a stick. Both were terrified. The policeman asked," Who are you? Where are you going all alone?" Vishu narrated the whole story fearfully," My puppy!." The policeman said," Puppy! What puppy! And do you know the way to your home? What is your address?" Vishu started crying aloud. Pakhi said at once, " She knows the way. My mother has memorized me. It is #203, Sona street." Bhola was seen coming towards them with puppy in hand. Vishu was happy to see and ran to hold him. Puppy too pounced over to Vishu. Pakhi hugged her mother. Her mother said," Where have you been all alone like this? What would happen if you were lost?" Pakhi said at once," How could I?I know my home address.#203,Sona street. Is not it? " The policeman too smiled. Mother thanked policeman and took Pakhi in her lap lovingly.

title: The Colorful Elephant
text: Long,long ago in India,a baby elephant was born. He was loving & affectionate. He was also black. However, he did not want to be black No matter, how much his mother begged him, he did not agree or listen. One day, he was so worried that he wandered around the Indian streets. That same day it was Holi. The kids sprayed colored water on the elephant. He was happy, but his mother was quite worried. Then he went to a pond. He saw his reflection in water and thought he was quite messy. He splashed inside the pond and cleaned himself up. Then, he realized he's great as he is and wanted no change in the way he looks.
author: Ruthva Santhosh Kumar

title: Gilloo
text: Gilloo Blackplum was tree. Many other animals too lived All were fearless and kind. Sparrow, parrot and squirrel Unique friends of Gilloo Do anything with blink of eye One day....... Gilloo sleeping in squirrel nest Appeared from nowhere A black furious cobra Gilloo was very scared It started crying It lost its senses too. A wise parrot sitting in between black plum leaves He also made a hue and cry Sparrow, squirrel, ants, butterfly and myana All ran toward parrot " Oh bro! Who is crying and why?" Parrot asked them to find a way. Our Gilloo should be saved. One cobra spreading its fangs sitting in nest. Myana put a idea Crow at once obeyed A wooden stick was arranged All held it in their beaks tight. Parrot brought cotton and thread Wrapped it around the stick Myana ignited it All moved towards nest holding stick in mouth The stick was burning The cobra got frightened. The cobra left the nest and ran out Gilloo was relaxed and confident The cobra never came back Gilloo was never teased again All lived happily With their sorrows and joys. A good friend in need is A good friend indeed. Only then it is true friendship.

title: The Bunny Rabbit
text: Once in a little land of rabbits, there was a timid and shy rabbit. That rabbit was very very shy. Everybody in the rabbit land was very bold but she was very frightened of everything. Her mother kept saying not to be shy and fearful. But this rabbit won't listen. She was continuing being shy and fearful.One day, when she was going to school, the maid rabbit said that there was no school because the fox was roaming around in the Rabbit land. She got scared and started crying. Then right at that time, a friend of hers came and said that her mother was looking for her. Now the little rabbit became little courageous and started walking towards her home. On the way she saw her mother was about to be attacked by the wicked fox. She got angry and said 'How dare you.' She thought what to do to save her mother. Then the little rabbit distracted the fox by pelting stones at it. The fox got angry and started chasing her. She ran fast and escaped the fox. In the meanwhile, the mother also ran and escaped. After some time the mother rabbit peeped out of the burrow to see her baby approaching. They hugged each other and the mother was very proud of her daughter. The baby rabbit was never timid or frightened of anything again.

title: The Black Cats
text: We have to be careful not to miss them. The other cats don't like the black cats, they think the black cats are not like them. But there are people who don't trust them. These animals don't like to be petted. They like to bite. In any case, the whole world believes that they bring bad luck. There are lots of black cats all over the world. And they are adorable. The black cats need a place in our heart.
author: Ahona

title: My new pet
text: I love animals. My parents take me to the zoo sometimes where I love to watch and feed zebras, monkeys and giraffes. My friend Megha has a little cat called "Buttons" who plays with her all the time. When I visit Megha, I play with Buttons too. I like playing with Buttons as she makes me run around and tries to do whatever I am doing. She is also lovely to pet and caress. My birthday is coming next week and I want a special gift this year. I told my mother today - "I feel alone in the house when I come back from school, can I get someone to play with?". My mother laughed and said, "I play with you and so does your dad. What else do you want?". It seems she did not get the point. I don't want to play with her. I want someone naughty to play with. Think my dad will know what I want. He is in the kitchen making coffee. I go and hug him from behind and ask him, "Dad, do you know what's coming next week?". He lifted me in his arms and said, "Yes, it is my daughter's birthday". Time to spring up my question! I said, "Dad, I want a special gift this year, one that can sleep with me". Dad smiled and said, "Aren't you too big for teddy bears?" Who else do I talk to? Maybe Krishna, my big brother - he goes to a big city college and he will know what I want. Krishna is playing cricket in the park with his friends. I call out to him -"Hey Krishna bhaiya, do you know what I want for my birthday next week?" Krishna shouted back - "Yes I do. You want my big box of candies that's hidden in my room. I am never giving that to you". It is my birthday today. I am cross with everyone. No one knows or cares about what I want for my birthday. I am wondering who do I talk to. Mom, Dad and Krishna bhaiya wished me happy birthday but no one asked me about a birthday gift. I don't want to stay at home and I will go to Megha's house for the day. I told my mother and rushed away in a hurry. Better to be with Buttons today! It is evening and Megha said she and Buttons will come with me to my home as she wants to pick up some books from me. We all walk back home. Buttons is purring and squealing in delight as I pet her. I wish I could keep Buttons with me - she would sleep with me, play with me and I could talk to her for hours about my school and my friends. While I was imagining this, we reached home. The house was dark. But then, the lights came on and I saw my friends surrounding a big cake. My family was smiling in the corner and hiding something behind them. "What is this? What are you hiding?"- I said. Just then, Buttons threw herself on the package and out emerged another cat - a white fur ball. Now I knew it - my parents got me a cat for a birthday gift. They knew what I wanted.
author: Shweta Bajpai
illustrator: Arindam Dhar; Daishawn Hairston; Ninaivahini Sivakumar; Rijuta Ghate; Sandhya Prabhat; Shanta  Hitang; Soumya Menon; Yuvaka  Srestha

title: My great journey to Varanasi
text: It was a sunny wonderful morning when my family took off to reach Varanasi to meet our maternal grandparents and our maternal uncles. We travelled from train. As soon as we arrived the station we saw a train which was gorgeous and had delicate colors. We went to our platform and waited for a while. Just then we saw a monkey show going on the platform. It was very hilarious which made everyone laugh.We even saw a small train for kids to enjoy while the train is arriving.After waiting for a while the train arrived filled with many people on the first compartment. We boarded the compartment and sat on our seats. After that another family came and told that this was their seat and so we checked and got to know that we are in the wrong compartment.We rushed to our compartment which was 2 compartments away.We sat on our seats and ordered a somsosa(a triangular savoury pastry fried in ghee or oil)and a coffee. We all were tired as we could not sleep at night as our train was early in the morning and after that we needed to rush here and there. We started eating our breakfast and decided to sleep after eating just then some more people came to our berth and sat.So we could not sleep.We all settled down and started playing cards which made our time pass. We played till noon.Then we ate lunch and my parents slept where as my sister started playing games on the laptop and i was reading a book named "The Famous Five"written by Enid Blyton o my kindle. While reading i saw a man with a mask on his face taking something out from someone else's back and so I made a video of him cause i was not sure if he is a robber.I woke my parents up.I called and distracted him till my parents were watching the video. They told he is a robber and everyone started beating him but the truth was he was not a robber, he was taking a brush from his bag and was wearing a mask as he was down with cold.We were ashamed and apologised for the mistake. We all started watching our favourite series named as "Panchayat".At night we got very tired and so slept early around 9:15 pm.In the morning we reached VARANASI at 1:pm.It was a great and one of the best train journey ever. We told our whole train journey to our maternal uncles,aunts,grand fathers and grandmothers.
author: keshav agarwal
illustrator: Karen Lilje Lilje; Niloufer Wadia; Rai; Shadrach Munene; Siraj Saxena; Subinita Deshaprabhu

title: THE BLACK AND THE WHITE MONKEYS
text: Once upon a time,there lived two families of monkeys-the white monkeys and the black monkeys.The white monkeys were afraid of the black monkeys as they harmed them often. One day the white monkeys were sitting by the side of a brook and were enjoying the taste of their favourite mango.One of the monkeys saw few banana fruits and a banana sapling floating on the water and it jumped into the water to pick them up. The family members shared the sweet banana fruits among themselves.They decided to plant the banana sapling so that they could eat tasty bananas later on. The black monkeys were sitting on the top of a tree.They observed the white monkeys planting something.They could not see what sapling it was called and leader of the black monkeys called out to them"Hey fools!Come here." The leader of the black monkeys ordered"Whatever may be the sapling you planted,the lower part of the plant would belong to us as it grows." The white monkeys agreed to the foolish leader and they wanted to teach them a good lesson. The white monkeys watered the plant regularly.Days passed by and the plant grew tall.The monkeys decided to share the plant as decided earlier.They moved towards the place where the plant stood.The black monkeys were shocked to find ripe banana fruits on the upper part of the plant. The white monkeys pardoned the black monkeys and they shared the banana fruits with the black monkeys.The black monkeys felt sorry for being cruel to the white monkeys and also for their foolishness.The two families became friends from then on.
author: Jayasudha  Bhaskaran

By the time the rain had stopped and Rahul and Meena marched out of the house ready to play horay they said as the marched and then they shouted''' yay our map is finished ''and walked to a tree totally ready to climb. They climbed up the tree and had a idea that next time instead of a map we will roam the whole world and yes we will stop fora small vacation.Then they fell asleep still dreaming about the world..............
author: Jiya G

title: BUNNY ESCAPES!
text: A farmer owned many rabbits.He reared them in a farm and did not let them play outside.The rabbits would wait for their master every morning as he would bring them carrots and leaves.They lived happyily in the farm as they did not know the glory of the world outside them. Bunny was a smart rabbit and was curious to experience the world outside.It had heard many interesting stories about the beauty of the world outside them from its grandmother when it was young.Bunny thought deeply to find a good idea to escape from the farm. How will I escape from here? Atlast Bunny got a good idea.It planned to hide inside the basket in which its master brought them carrots and leaves.He thought of jumping out of the basket once they reach the forest as its master has to go home through a forest. Let me hide inside the basket Bunny jumped into the basket without letting its master know its plan.The master did not know that bunny was inside the basket and he carried it home.He went through the forest area as expected by Bunny. The master felt the basket heavier than usual and opened it to find what it was.As soon as its master opened the basket,Bunny jumped out of the basket and ran into the forest.The master chased Bunny for a while but he failed and he returned home with the empty basket.
author: Jayasudha  Bhaskaran

title: cursed tortoise An Indian tale
text: There once was a chatty tortoise who lived in a beautiful lake with his two geese friends. They lived happily until one day the lake was washed out. It would be easy for the geese to find a new home, but it would be difficult for the tortoise due to how slow he crawls. It could take him months to find a new place to live. The geese decided to help the little tortoise by putting a stick in their beaks at each end and the tortoise would be in the middle. But he was a chatty tortoise. Meaning he wouldn't be able to talk for the entire flight. On the way there was a duck. She laughed and laughed at the thought of a flying tortoise. 'Hahaha! How silly you are,flying on a stick!'she quacked. The tortoise lost his temper and spoke. 'come here and say that bird brain!' but the tortoise had let go of the stick and was falling... The tortoise landed with a THUMP in a market. He counted all the things that reminded him of home there. He soon fell asleep. When he woke up, he was back in the lake but unable to speak. The duck had somehow cursed him with her mean words, but now the tortoise knew how to control himself.
author: Rosalyn  koopa-shaser
illustrator: Jemma Jose; Nuwan Chathuranga Athulasiri; Rosalyn  koopa-shaser; Samidha Gunjal

title: Nani's Glasses
text: I love my nani, From her hair to her toes, But what I love the most, Sits at the tip of her nose. You see my nani uses glasses, She needs them to read, They hang around her neck… “Let me try them,” I plead. “No dear,” comes her quick reply, “You’ll spoil your eyes, Glasses are important, And can’t be tried for size.” Nani calls them her specs, I think that sounds so funny, She says they are meant for her eyes only, And cost a lot of money. I run into Nani's room, There they are, right on her bed, I just HAVE to try them, Never mind what Nani said. I quickly sit them on my nose, And everything looks blurry, I look at our cat, He seems less furry! I can hear footsteps, Someone’s coming in! I take them off, quickly, And run out with a grin. And then there’s my nana, He says, “My eyes are just fine.” He brings in the newspaper, And can’t read a line. “Arrrgh!” says he, “It must be the light,” Though we all know for sure, He has poor eyesight. Why doesn’t Nana like glasses? I think they are super-cool, If I could only get a pair, I’d wear them to my school. I speak to my mumma, But she shakes her head, She takes me and buys me, Sunglasses instead! Now I’m really happy, As happy as can be, I call them my shades, They’re the best – don’t you agree? And when they slip down, To the tip of my nose, I look just like my nani, From my head to my toes.
author: Nalini Sorensen

title: My diary!
text: My name is Aisha and I am 10 years old. This book is about my daily diary. Read the next pages if you want to. --------------------------------------------------------------- /17 I live in a small neighborhood in Noida and all the people who live there (even the kids) have a group. There are about 120 children in our neighborhood and we have been divided into groups by the people who own our houses. Today my friend Gauri just told us that she is moving to Mumbai, oh no! When I tell this to Muma, she is quite not- surprised. " Oh, Anushka (Gauri's muma) told me yesterday when you Gauri, Meena, and Kimara (my friends)were playing at the park, me, Anushka, Pinky, and Amalika (my friends's moms) were having a group FaceTime call and Anushka told us this news. " said muma. I still can't believe that Gauri is leaving. I said to muma " muma we have to make Gauri and Anushka aunty the best Farewell party". Muma says " of course we will Aisha. We will start planning tomorrow, ok".For dinner today we had some delicious pasta and I cried " muma we have to put this on the menu for the farewell." Papa said " Arre, who's farewell? Oh, is this Rahul Gupta's farewell you talking about (Rahul Gupta is Gauri's Dad. Papa likes to call him by his full name, not only Rahul.)" papa how do you know? And Pankaj Bhaya (my older annoying elder brother) do you also know?" I ask. " Of course I know. Kirti (Gauri's closest cousin) told me." Big Bhaya's seem to know everything. Anyways good night. I will write tomorrow. /19 Today is a school day and cybersecurity day and tomorrow is Saturday. And today at school some Didi's from class 12th came and told us about cybersecurity. " today you youngsters will be making your own chart on cybersecurity." one Didi said. We are not youngsters! We are 5th graders. Most of us are 10 years old! After making the chart the Didi's left and we voted which looked best and has the most information. I came first and Sameena Dingra (one girl in my class) came last because she drew the most and wrote the least. And plus she's the least to succeed: voted by the class president Raj Sharma. He is a fat and rich boy who keeps giving his friends money thinking that they are his friends but they are not his friends. They just pretend to be his friends so they get money. Ma'am said that since Raj Sharma has so many friends he shall be class president. Ma'am should have made me class president because I'm so kind and I would never put poor Sameena in such a difficult spot. Second thing about Raj: he doesn't have respect. Suppose he has this maid and her name is Tweety. When he calls her he is like " Oh, Tweety come here ". He calls her by her name! She is 26 years old and he is 11 years old. And he is really good at drawing since he started doing art classes since he was 5 years old. Of course, since he is so rich he can throw around money everywhere. Last year, he joined this school, and our class and I heard rumors that he got kicked out of his first school and his parents did not mind and just put him in this school. If I were in his place I would have been scolded like how. /17 Sorry, I wrote after a long time. We had a really hard math quiz to do and loads of homework. I really wish homework was not invented. It is so boring and if we didn't have it then we would catch up with our friends, watch tons of t.v and play video games. Anyway, today we have to plan tons of the farewell and I am so not going to help muma, Pinky aunty, and Amalika auntie. I, Meena, and Kimara are going to play loads of video games while those Ladies are going to chat all day long, order some stuff and call people for delivery. After half an hour I, Meena and Kimara are really hungry. So our mum's make us some yummy Nutella and peanut butter sandwich and tell us about the farewell. " We will be hosting it at Meena's house because it is really big, and girls this is a surprise farewell so please don't tell Gauri, Rahul uncle or Anushka aunty. Understood " says muma. " yes Auntie " says Kimara on my and Meena's behalf. /17 Today is the food truck party! A food truck party happens in neighborhoods in Sector 2 (the sector where I live) monthly. It happens on every 19th of a month. On the day of the food truck party there is a theme of food to eat. Suppose last month on 19th June the theme was Italian and it happens in the night so the rest of the meals will not be Italian at all. If you don't follow this rule then you will not get to the Italian party. And food trucks all over the sector will serve Italian. Last month, Pankaj Bhaya didn't go because he ate pasta for lunch. Everyone gets a message of the theme the night before the party. In every neighborhood, there are at least 30 food trucks. Sometimes you can put up your own food truck, like last month me Gauri, Kimara, and Meena put a lemonade truck in Kimara's car and made our own lemonade. We made Rs 1500 last year because it was really hot and people needed a refreshment and we gave them a chilled lemonade for Rs 10. The theme of this year is Mexican I think, and mummy told me that there is going to be a chocolate and vegan taco truck. Yum! " My muma told me that there is going to be a fruit custard stand too, Aisha! I can't believe this is my last food truck party," says Gauri sadly. " Didn't your muma say you are going to leave on 19th August?" Kimara says. " oh, no she will leave on the day of a food truck party! " said Meena. Gauri said " I don't think so. Pops (what Gauri calls her father) told me that we will leave at 12 'o'clock in the night and the party stops at 10 only." oh yay, you not going to miss it " I say. Then suddenly a singer jumps on to the stage of the food truck party and says " we want to thank you for coming to this food truck party. We want to celebrate the leaving of a member of this special group who is standing right next to the stage. Say your farewells to miss Gauri Gupta, Mr Rahul Gupta and Mrs Anushka Gupta." I hear lots of clapping so I start clapping too. Then my parents and I go into Meena's humangas mansion. I asked my mum why is the farewell so early and she said that because Gauri will leave at 12:00 today. What a coincidence!! Instead of the party happening outside like usual it happened in Meena's house. After tons of partying, we finally had to say goodbye to Gauri. We were really sad because when I had just moved to sector 2 Noida from Gurgaon DLF, I was sitting alone in the park and she comforted me and became my first friend in Noida. I was feeling really sad when she left but I knew I would visit her in Mumbai and I could easily text with her on the computer. /17 Today I woke up at 5:00 so I can text Gauri if she is awake. I start texting her and she texts back. After 1 hour of texting, she goes to sleep and I get ready for school. Suddenly, I see raindrops pouring. Half an hour later, muma gets an email from the school saying that the school is closed due to heavy rain. Yay, no school. But muma even gets an email saying that Pankaj Bhaya will go to school because he is in 9th grade. No Bhaya also! And mummy, papa have to go work. But no school for me! My parents drop me off at Kimara's and Meena comes over too because even both her parents go to work. My parents dropped me off at Kimara's house because it is huge and her mum is a stay at home and she has many maids to take care of her. We play and eat lunch with her, then my and Meena's mum come to pick us up and we really had a fun time! /17 Today Meena has some news to tell us. I'll give you the hint she gave me and Kimara. Meena's hint: I am an only child. Could you figure out something? Well, Kimara did. " oh, you are getting a puppy?" she says. Meena tells her " Yes! We are definitely getting a puppy"." Guys, we will talk about this later. There is a movie releasing today its name is Descendants 2". I say. " Have we even watched Descendants 1, and you are saying we can watch part 2," Kimara says. Meena replies " yeah, we don't even know what is Descendants is,". " Don't worry. My father got premiere tickets from his office to go to the Descendants 1 movie." I said. " do our parents know about this?" Kimara worried. " yes of course they know. Aisha told her father to tell our parents." Meena said. And it was set. We put on our best clothes and went to the movie theater with our fathers. So, after the movie, we were really happy and Kimara and Meena's parents gave the money to my Papa. That is the end of my diary. BYE!!
author: Aathira Karthik

title: The Clean Cat
text: This is my house. Mommy, Daddy and Kina live here too. The best chair in the house is for me. But sitting on the lap is even better, isn't it? Kina is my best friend. I wait for her to come back from school. I clean myself even without water. I don't need to take a bath like Tommy. Psst... tell no one that I'm hiding here. 1...2...3...Got you! Mommy scolds me when I bring tasty food from the garden. I can climb trees. I can hump. I know all the shortcuts here. Sacha lives nearby. He annoys me. That makes me very angry. Please tell Sacha that the tiger also belongs to our cat family. We have very sharp claws. My friends sometimes make a lot of noise at night. At that time, I am still in bed. Tails can speak! Did you know how animals and birds use their tails to tell us something? A dog wags its tail when it's happy. A cat puffs its tail when it's angry.
author: Gayatri Aich

title: The Travelling Bug
text: Binita Beetle was bitten by the travel bug. She packed a bag and set off on a big adventure. Ow! “Adventure, here I come!” Oh no! Binita Beetle saw the last Caterpillar Special pull away from the bug-stop. She ran behind it, waving her arms and yelled “Stop!”. But, it just wouldn’t slow down. Then, Binita Beetle spotted Shaggy-dog. She jumped onto his back. Shaggy-dog brought Binita Beetle to The Land of Singing Trees. They gifted her The Bag of Songs. As Binita Beetle was walking, suddenly she tripped! The Bag of Songs landed right on her antennae. And the antennae started to play music! Binita Beetle was thrilled! She swirled, twirled and danced her way to The City of Jewels. Here, she met Mr. Kokto and his family. They were also singing and dancing! Binita Beetle played her musical antennae and danced with them. The music filled Binita Beetle with a sense of happiness like never before. And she wanted to share it with everyone. So, she went to The Mountains of Snow. “Ya juley,” everyone sang and danced. After traveling across the world, Binita Beetle finally came home. She sang and sang, and played everything she’d learnt. And her Garden of Music kept growing and growing. The Travelling Bug and the Travelling Sketchbook Once upon a time, there was a Sketchbook who got bitten by the travel bug. Ow! So it jumped into Rajiv Eipe’s bag in Bengaluru. Luckily for the Sketchbook, Rajiv Eipe was an illustrator and he dreamed up Binita Beetle who travels the world. Like Binita, the Sketchbook too wanted to travel. So they set off to Kalyani Ganapathy’s desk in Coonoor, who helped her hitch a ride with Shaggydog. From there, the pair (the bug and the book) travelled to Itanagar, and Ogin Nayam gifted her The Bag of Songs. Tanya Kotnala invited them next to Dehradun, and she accidentally opened The Bag of Songs, and turned it into a musical antennae. From there, Lungshai Leisan in Manipur dreamed up new friends for the pair of them. So the two set off to Ladakh to make more new friends, including Prabhakar Dabral. Tired and happy from all that singing, dancing and making new friends; Binita Beetle and the Sketchbook returned to Bangalore. First stop to Ruchi Shah who gave them a happy ending. Then home at last, to the Pratham Books office. And now their story is in your hand and we know that Binita Beetle and the Travelling Sketchbook were read happily ever after.
author: Kalyani  Ganapathy; Lungshai Leisan; Ogin Nayam; Prabhakar Dabral; Rajiv Eipe; Ruchi Shah; Tanya Kotnala
illustrator: Kalyani  Ganapathy; Lungshai Leisan; Ogin Nayam; Prabhakar Dabral; Rajiv Eipe; Ruchi Shah; Tanya Kotnala

title: Let us count the eggs easily!
text: She loves to play with birds by chasing them and to feed the cattle in the farm. It was an early Sunday morning." I have got up",she shouted as soon as she got up from bed. "Will you please help Raghu to collect and count the eggs?",asked her grandma. "Kavya,please come here",said her grandma. Vrrrrr Raghu started to count the eggs. "One,Two,Three......Fourteen......." It was then that his dog took one of his slippers and ran away. "Hey!Seenu,don't take away my slipper",he shouted. He resumed to count."Twelve,Thirteen.....Oh my God!I forgot where I stopped the count.Was it Twelve or Thirteen?",he got confused. He then started to recount the eggs in the basket from the beginning. "One,Two.....Sixteen"It was then that he saw Puneeth holding his cycle. "Hey Puneeth!Take your hands off my cycle",he shouted again. "Fifteen,Sixteen....I lost the count again.Where did I stop?Alright.Let us take away the eggs now and will count it later on",he said. "My teacher has taught me an easy way to count. Is it not easy to count upto ten than counting upto hundreds or any large numbers?",she asked. "Hmm!I can count even upto crores!",he said. "But counting upto ten is far more easy!Place ten eggs in a basket.Take another basket and then place ten eggs in it again.basket.Repeat the same until the eggs get over.Atlast,you will have many baskets with ten eggs in each." Raghu wondered at her idea. Raghu counted ten eggs and he placed it in a basket.He took next basket and placed another ten eggs in it. He completed his task very soon."I have placed all the eggs.How many eggs are there in total?Tell me",he asked Kavya. "How many baskets do you have?",asked Kavya. "Five baskets.Each basket has ten eggs",he said. "Fifty eggs!",exclaimed Kavya. "How did you count so fast", grandma wondered. "Granny!There are ten eggs in a basket.There are five baskets in total.That means,five baskets with ten eggs each.That is,ten plus ten plus ten plus ten plus ten.Fifty!Fifty eggs",said Kavya. Raghu and Kavya went along with grandma to the market ans sold the eggs.It was a joyful experience for them. As soon as they reached home,they helped grandma in counting the money they obtained by selling the eggs.They had rice and tasty egg kurma for dinner that night! Ones and tens Ten is a group of 10 ones. One egg,One hen,One basket 11=1 ten+1 one 23=2 tens+3 ones 12=1 ten+2 ones
author: Jayasudha  Bhaskaran

title: Shikari's Cycling Adventure
text: Shikari just could not stay still. He loved playing football, hockey, kabaddi, cricket and enjoyed running and cycling. His real name was Shivaprakash, but because his hometown was Shikaripura, his friends called him Shikari. Shikari worked at a sports store after graduating from college. The work kept him busy but he was bored. He longed to play sports and was always dreaming of adventure. It seemed to Shikari that his life had suddenly taken a pause. Until one day, Shikari heard something on the radio. “India is hosting the Asian Games” “Delhi, ” Shikari thought, “I have never been to Delhi and I must go to see the Games!” A brilliant idea entered his mind. The idea of a thrilling adventure. A thrilling cycling adventure! “What if I cycle till Delhi? I have never cycled so far. It will be exciting to travel through new cities and towns.” His friend Richard offered him his cycle for the trip. Shikari wrote a letter to his parents to seek their permission. At first, they were hesitant. It was such a long journey and there were no mobile phones back then. But seeing his enthusiasm, they gave in. Shikari started training. He ran 20 km every week. He cycled 70 km every week. He exercised to make his muscles stronger. He ate fruits, nuts and paneer and drank milk every day. He packed lightly, but smartly. He bought tickets to the Asian Games. He mapped his travel route on a map. Shikari could not wait to start! Finally, he was ready. October 1982 Day 01 Bangalore, Karnataka One bright morning, Shikari set off for Delhi on his cycle. His parents and friends came to see him off. Shikari’s adventure had truly begun. Click Claak, Click Claak, squeak Day 02 Gauribidnaur, Karnataka All the people in the town gathered around when they saw Shikari on a cycle with luggage. They introduced him to Basavraj who had gone on an all-India cycle expedition the previous year. “Would you like to join me on this trip, Basav?” Shikari asked. “Yes!” Basav said excitedly. Shikari was happy, he liked Basav’s company. In two days, the two men set out towards Delhi together. Day 06 Penukonda, Andhra Pradesh Shikari and Basav started their days early. After a light breakfast, they started pedalling. Click Claak, Click Claak They took a break for lunch and were off again. Click Claak, Click Claak They took a short nap and pedalled again until sunset. Click Claak, Click Claak ﻿ Day 10 Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh They cycled 100 kms every single day. Click Claak, Click Claak At night, they would sleep wherever they could find space – railway stations, guest houses, temples or homes of kind strangers. Each day and each night was a new adventure. Day 14 Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh Shikari and Basav noticed dark clouds gathering over their head. The wind started to blow strong and loud Hisss… Hisss… Thunder rumbled through the sky as it rained heavily. Before they knew it, they were in the middle of a storm. The two men did not have raincoats. An idea struck them - why not make a raincoat on their own? They bought big plastic sheets from a shop, cut holes for their arms and neck and aaha! A makeshift raincoat was ready. They pedalled on. Click Claak, Click Claak Click Claak, Click Claak Day 16 Nagpur, Maharashtra When the road was steep, Shikari and Basav had to stop pedalling and push the cycle uphill. They saw snakes, bison, deer and jungle cats along forest roads. Click Claak, Click Claak, Click Claak, Click Claak Day 18 Narsinghpur, Madhya Pradesh It was a bank holiday, and the two friends did not have any money left. They were tired and hungry. “Where are you two headed?” a cycle-shop owner asked them. After hearing them out, the shop owner offered them tea and lunch. He also gave them Rs.100 for the journey ahead. “How will we ever repay you? Thank you for helping us,” said Shikari with tears in his eyes. They set out for their next destination. Click Claak, Click Claak, Click Claak, Click Claak Day 23 Delhi Click Claak, Click Claak, Click Claak, Click Claak Shikari and Basav cycled by the majestic India Gate. Yes! They had made it to India’s capital, Delhi. The many days of cycling in the harsh sun, the difficulties they had faced and the pain in their legs all seemed to disappear. Now Delhi and the Asian Games awaited them. November 1982 Day 27 Delhi The Asian Games began with pomp and show. The two friends saw boxing and badminton matches. They saw world athletes competing in wrestling and gymnastics. The Games mascot Appu smiled from the stadium walls as they watched tennis and volleyball matches. They were amazed at the strength of the weightlifters and the agility of the swimmers. The Women’s Hockey Finals was a thrilling match between India and South Korea. Shikari was at the edge of his seat throughout the match. India won and he was overjoyed. Shikari now looked forward to going back home. Meet the real Shikari This story is inspired by Shivaprakash Honnashettar’s real-life adventure of cycling from Bangalore to Delhi for the Asian Games in 1982. He was 25 years old then. Mr Shivaprakash recently retired as the Sports Secretary of St. Joseph’s Boys’ High School in Bangalore. UTTAR PRADESH Jhansi Agra Follow Shikari’s cycle ride to Delhi from Bangalore: DELHI KARNATAKA Bangalore Gauribidanur ANDHRA PRADESH Hindupur Penukonda Gooty Dhone Kurnool Mahabubnagar (now in Telengana) Hyderabad (now in Telengana) MAHARASHTRA Nagpur MADHYA PRADESH Sagar Gwalior
author: Payoshni Saraf

title: pip pip and my sister is a sissy poems
text: Pip pip is from the zoo, a zoo called water loo. When you here COO COO! pip pip asks to leave the zoo. No matter how much pip pip begs there, no-one seems to care. There has to be a new chapter to pip pips page, she can't stay here eating sage in her cage. My sister is a sissy, she's afraid of dogs and cats. A toad can give her tantrums, And she's terrified of rats. She's afraid of things with stingers, things that sting and things that crawl. Just the shadow of a spider sends my sister up the wall A lizard makes her shiver, A turtle makes her squirm, She positively cringes at the prospect of a worm. She's afraid of things with feathers, she's afraid of things with fur. She's afraid of almost everything... How come I'm scared of her?
author: Rosalyn  koopa-shaser
illustrator: Isaac  Okwir; Karnak Gabani; Maya  Ramaswamy; Samidha Gunjal; Stephen Wallace

title: Haley leaves
text: Haley lived on a farm in Devon, she wasn't the happiest of dogs. But she guessed it was ok. She didn't have much company. Yes there were plenty of animals, cows, sheep, horses, chickens,pigs, you know the drill. But Haley still felt lonely at times. Haley was on cow herding duty that same day. Coconut, a little calf with a high temper, was the hardest to herd, that's what Haley enjoyed. Challenges. Coconut mooed loudly a huffed even louder to show she was up for this, no matter what. Haley pounced excitedly chasing coconut all over the farm until the cows were taken in for milking, coconut followed. Cow fun was over, now time for those horses...the hardest of all. See, the horses always tease Haley. Especially butterscotch, she calls her a mutt... I hate herding the horses because they make her look bad in-front of thee owner, the farmer. They don't listen and they probably never will. Lucky they have went back to the stables. You, mutt! Get over here! Come on, skid! I heard the other animals talking about me... 'can't see why not...oink!' 'yeah but it's the only way,moo,' 'I don't know..cluck,' 'Whatever, let's just do it, I cannot take her running around the field trying to capture me, moo, let's get rid of her!' Coconut said that. Haley was in total shock. But she quickly left the farm before anyone did anything bad to her. No-one knows where she is now...
author: Rosalyn  koopa-shaser
illustrator: Magriet Brink; Marleen  Visser; Michael  Sagikwa; San srei nou ch nou ch

title: Best birthday party!
text: Sriya was very happy! Her birthday was coming up! It was on May 19! And today is May 18! Just one more day and then, she will be 6 years old! Yaaaaaa She wanted to call 2 of her best friends to attend her party! Nali and Maya. She called and said" Nali! Maya! It is my birthday tomorrow! Can you pls attend the party? Both of them said that they would attend the party! Sriya was happy She ran to her room and took 2 bags. She wrote to Maya on one of the bag and to Nali on the other bag. In each of the bag, she put 1 lolipop, 1 chocolate, 1 book and one glittery pencil. She would give it to her friends as a party bag! Then she grabbed her planning book and wrote down activities. Water games, pin the tail to the unicorn, play dolls, cut cake and then sing happy birthday to her! She could not wait until tomorrow! Then, her mom called her and told her to sleep. Tomorrow was a big day for her! She was turning 6! She can't wait to have a party with her best friends. When she woke up, she ran to the living room. Her mother and father were waiting for her! They came and hugged her and said " Happy birthday!" She was very happy! It was her birthday! She helped her mom bake the cake, she played with her parents, she ate yummy food for breakfast! She also watched her favorite movie! She was so busy playing, she forgot that it was almost time for her friends to come! It was time for her to change into her party clothes! She went to her room and opened the closet. She chose a pretty pink dress to wear for the party! Yahoooo! Her friends will come in a while! She also got a pretty crown to wear. Now she was all ready. Her parents told her that she looks like a princess! She waited and waited and waited. Her friends did not come! She looked at the time. It was 6 o clock! Her friends were supposed to come at 5! She was upset! She ran to Maya's house. There Maya and Nali were playing. She got angry and said. "Maya! Nali! Why did you guys not come to my birthday party?" Maya came and said" Sorry Sriya! We are playing." Sriya was angry! She ran home! She went home and cried! She was very angry that her friends did not come to her party and played without calling her! After sometime, her friends came back and said " Sorry Sriya! We were making a present you and it took a long time. Please forgive us!" Sriya was ashamed. She did not solve the problem correctly by crying. She even made her friends sad. Now sriya said sorry. " Sorry my dear friends. It is my fault too. Now let us forget the past and have the party!" Her friends loved the idea! They all had the party! They enjoyed. Then they cut Sriya's cake. It was delicious. It was Sriya's best birthday
author: Niyati Makkithaya

title: Kindness is more important!
text: Once upon a time there was a beautiful peocock, it’s name is Peau. She always admired herself. She is greedy and selfish, because she is very pretty. She lives in a forest, with other animals. Since she was very beautiful, everyone liked her. In the same forest, there lived the crow named Coco. Since she was black, no body liked her. One day, Peau was walking in the forest and saw the crow. Then she suddenly turned away and said “ eww, I do not want to walk where Coco is there.” Hearing Peau say that Coco felt very sad. Suddenly A girl, who loved peacocks took a big net and trapped Peau. Peau was shouting for help, but nobody came, except Coco. Coco flew and scared the girl and let peacock free. Then Peau thanked Coco and said” Thank you so much! I’m so sorry Coco, can we be best friends?” “ Sure” replied Coco. From day onwards, Peau and Coco became best friends and soon everyone in the forest became friends with her and was very kind to her.
author: Harini Shrii Vengata Raghavan
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Padmanabh; Priya Kuriyan; Wiehan de Jager

title: FLUFFY THE CAT
text: This is fluffy. As you can see she is eating fish. Do you like fish??? When her mother scolds her,she sits on the wall and watches the children play next door fluffy hopes that they give her something to eat like usual. If not,she goes to their kitchen and eats something like fish. This is her owner dan. He is very kind he feeds her everyday.. Everyday she has fun with the children. title: The Adventures of Chaddi Head
text: Most children want to be a dozen different things when they grow up. But not Junaid. He already is the best superhero in the universe. Most superheroes don’t seem to understand where their underwear is supposed to go. But Junaid knows the best way to wear underwear… It gives you: 1) a super-cool costume 2) a super-secret disguise 3) a superhero name: Chaddi Head is on the head. With great chaddis come great possibilities. Unlike his Ajji’s favourite superheroes, Junaid doesn’t wear the same chaddi all the time. He has the perfect chaddi for every adventure. When everyone is asleep and Junaid wants to sneak into the kitchen, he knows which chaddi he needs. Black Chaddi Head is a ninja who eats chocolate laddus for a midnight feast. Junaid hates vegetables. His grown-ups love vegetables. When Junaid goes to the market with Pappa, he must make a Very Important Choice. Junaid has to eat at least one different vegetable every day. But Chaddi Head gets to pick which one. When Junaid feels like eating carrots, Red Chaddi Head goes to the market. Purple Chaddi Head only wants to eat brinjals. Orange Chaddi Head is always in the mood for pumpkins. But White Chaddi Head NEVER EVER goes to the market! Because cauliflowers are just evil little trees used by Chaddi Head’s enemies to destroy his powers. Junaid has a special maroon-and- yellow-checked chaddi for school to match his uniform. But no one wants to be Chaddi Head’s sidekick! Pappa thinks Junaid’s classmates are just as boring as his Ajji’s same-colour-chaddi-every-day superheroes. Ammi knows that one day Chaddi Head will find the best sidekick in the universe. Sometimes Junaid thinks an animal will make a good superhero sidekick. Grey Chaddi Head talks to his neighbour’s cat hoping she will join his team. But the cat has other ideas. Travelling with Junaid’s Ammi is even more dangerous. All the women in the train love pulling his cheeks. So Blue Chaddi Head sits next to the window and becomes invisible. At the park, Junaid is an explorer in the wild, busy studying all the grown-ups. Colourful-and-covered-with-flowers Chaddi Head remains hidden by looking like a bush. But today, the grown-ups are not the strangest things in the park. Is it (finally) time for Chaddi Head to save the day? “You will never escape me! MUAHAHAHAHA!” He runs in the direction of the evil laugh. HELP! HELP! It’s coming from that cardboard bedsheet fort. “Nobody is going to rescue you!” Chaddi Head crawls through the door. “Let them go!” he says. In the fort is a girl. She towers over her prisoners. “Who are you?” she asks. “I’m Chaddi Head, the best superhero in the universe!” he says. “Who are you?” “I’m Queen Chaddar, Empress of the Blanket Empire,” she says. “The best super villain in the universe.” “I’m going to rescue you,” Chaddi Head tells the prisoners. “No, he is not,” Queen Chaddar disagrees. There is only one way to settle this. Chaddi Head picks up a branch and runs towards Queen Chaddar with his tree-sword. “AAAAAAAAAAA!” She trips him with her Cape Of Lost Hope. “MUAHAHAHAHA!” Chaddi Head falls but is not defeated. He uses the only weapon he has left. He throws a chaddi missile. A mistake! Queen Chaddar wears it as a crown to steal his powers. She traps Chaddi Head in her Cape and sits on him. Now Chaddi Head is a prisoner too! “Kavya! It’s time to go home!” comes a voice from outside. “You may have won this battle, Queen Chaddar,” Chaddi Head says. “But I will win the war.” “I will have even more prisoners in my castle tomorrow,” Queen Chaddar says. “I will save them all!” “I will defeat you again!” “Let’s find out who wins next time,” says Chaddi Head. “Same time, same place!” declares Queen Chaddar. On the way back home, Junaid smiles. A superhero sidekick would be fun to have. But definitely not as fun as the best supervillain in the universe.
author: Parinita Shetty

title: my grown up life
text: when I am 30 I will have an adopted daughter. I will be a zoologist. a zoologist is a person who studies animals. because I want my daughter to come in contact with animals, I will get her a puppy called moonstone. author: Ira S.B.

title: The Survival
text: The survival The year was 2050 and the world as we knew it was gone for ever. Everything had changed so fast. We were living in a world filled with technology, a time when electricity was fuelled by the sun and our clothes changed their colour at the touch of a button. Everything was great, the world was spinning and we were learning more every day. That was until the asteroid came. I was only eighteen at the time, to young and inexperienced for what was about to happen. I remembered the day so well, I’d been at school, not paying any attention to my math teacher as he droned on about numbers. There was a loud bang and the ground started to shake, the windows smashed from vibrations and the room was filled with screams of terror. You could see the fear in our teacher’s eyes. The shrill alarm sounded around the school as we all piled out of the building. My heart stopped when I saw the growing cracks in the ground. What was happening? I tried to contact my mum on my phone but it was no use. Nobody’s phones were working. I watched in confusion something was very wrong. All order quickly vanished as panic took over. The teachers failed attempts to keep us all together were overpowered by the rumbling of the ground. Everyone scattered from the school and I ran as fast as I could, aiming for one place, home. As I sped through town I saw people crying and screaming as they watched their houses shatter and fall to the ground. There were flights breaking out in the streets and fire spreading from car accidents. This was really bad. The moment I saw my house my life stopped, half of the building had crumbled and I could hear the cries of my two-year-old brother coming from inside. I wasted no time as I scrambled through what use to be our living room. The only thing that was fueling me on was the need to get to my brother. He was screaming with all his might, I took him in my arms and held him close to my chest. “It’s alright Daniel” I cooed looking around frantically. “MUM!” I called praying to hear her reply. My family had never been big we had moved here last year after my father left us. I rushed into what was left of the kitchen and that’s when I saw her, my mother’s body crushed beneath part of the house. I ran over to her tears blinding me. I could hear the house slowly collapsing around me but I had to get to her. Daniel’s wails filled the air as I fought through the rubble. She was dead. The fact dawned on me as I held her lifeless body in my arms. Daniel called out for her as the floor started to give way above us. I took my brother, kicking and screaming and ran out of the house just before it completely collapsed burying my mother with it. The earth changed the day and so did I. No one saw it coming. As the asteroid passed, the world went into chaos all technology malfunctioned and the weather became hostile. First it was tornadoes and earthquakes and then it was the heat. People started to panic and half the world’s population perished within the first six weeks. Nothing was ever the same, people split off into groups, some made camps in rundown cities and others took off on their own, trying to stay out of harm’s way. Daniel and I joined a group of thirty, most families from my old street. I didn’t know where else we were supposed to go, so we followed the group wholeheartedly. It became clear after the first few weeks who we looked to for leadership. A middle aged man named Nathan made most of the decisions he was the one who kept us alive for so long. It wasn’t long before our numbers started to dwindle. People from other groups became savages the worst taking over the towns and cities. We learned how to survive on very little and kept to save areas as we travelled overall it wasn’t a bad way to live, we had friends around us and our little group became our family. I should have known that it wouldn’t last forever. they entered, but it seemed that everyone else was happy with our new friends including Nathan. We travelled together for a few weeks and they became a part of our family. We were foolish to trust One night a group of six travellers approached our camp. I was weary of them the moment them. We had been walking all day looking for somewhere to make camp for the night. We usually kept away from the big cities but our new friends led us closer and closer. I could see Nathan wanted to find shelter somewhere else, but from the looks of things we didn’t have enough time to be picky. There was a sand storm approaching and we needed to find shelter. Slowly and cautiously we entered the town walking past broken buildings, no one was around and I kept my eyes peeled for any form of life.. Daniel was clung to my side like always, all was quite. The only sound came from our boots as they echoed on the ground with each step. We saw the shadows first, boxing us in like sheep to the slaughter. Daniel let out a small cry and some of the older women gasped as the reality dawned on us. We had been tricked. Our so called friends had led us in to a trap. We tried to fight back but in the end it was futile. Nathan was the first they killed, his body covered in blood as it lay lifelessly before us. Time seemed to freeze as we saw our leader dead on the ground. The adults of the group attacked while some tried to flee. They were all killed before our eyes. Only five children were left standing beside me crying out in fear. We were captured and put into a dark and dingy building already filled with children of all ages. Daniel cried into my legs and I stooped down to comfort him “don’t worry Dan, everything will be alright” I promised as I found a damp corner that was empty. I knew it was a lie, we were probably all going to die. It was just a matter of time. I didn’t want to tell him the truth. I didn’t want to believe it. Every night two of them would come and choose one of us. Once you were chosen you never came back. Everyone stayed silent and kept to themselves. Even the children from my old family became strangers. The fourth night they came surveying their choices. Daniel clung to me and I tried my best to hide him from their eyes. One of them looked at me an evil grin forming on his face. “That one” he called pointing a finger straight at my brother. “NO” I yelled as they tugged Daniel from my arms.. I stood up scratching and crawling at the man who held my brother. I was kicked to the floor, but I stood again screaming and hitting. It was all a blur of fear and emotion but the moment I hit the ground the fourth time my heart sank. My arm was broken and my nose was now poring with blood. I couldn’t force myself to stand and fight any longer. I was curled up on the floor my tears were mixing with my blood as I watched them walk towards the door with my crying brother in their arms. “STOP” a small girl who looked two years younger than me called as she stood from her place at the back of the room. I met her eyes and she gave me a small smile. “Take me Instead “she offered fearlessly walking over to the men. I watched frozen in my place as the men contemplated the trade. With a crude laugh they grabbed the girl and tossed my brother aside. The girl had sacrificed herself to save my brother’s life. I didn’t even know her name. After that day people seemed to band together, there was now more silence and we were no longer strangers. We decided to fight back the next time they came. There were only seven of us who were able to give a good fight, but it was enough. The next night we made our break for freedom. We had the element of surprise on our side and we made it out of the city and hid in the nearby caves. There is only one goal now. Survival. From that day we fought for our freedom for each thing we need and some more people joined our group and we lived happily ever after. ---The end---
author: krothapally Varshith

title: Papa Knows a Lot, but Mamma Knows Everything
text: “Wake up! Deepu, wake up!” yelled Deepika’s mother. “It’s a Sunday morning and I have to rush to the weekly village market to fetch the fresh vegetables and fruits.” Deepika woke up, rubbing her eyes and bid goodbye to her mother. Just then, Deepika heard a loud sound coming from their backyard, “Ouch!! Shoo shoo!” She rushed to see what was going on. Her father was screaming at someone. "Go away, why’re you after my life, you black crow? For God's sake, let me fill some water from the well! I don't know from where out of the blue this annoying creature came and started pecking me hard on my head. Ouch ouch!!!" bawled Deepika's father. Shoo!! Stop! Shoo! “Ugh! Ouch!” screamed Deepika, “You stupid cro…ouch! It’s hitting me too!" Hearing all the clutter, their neighbour, Lakshmi came out with her greedy dog, Lalu. “What’s the noise all abou… ouch! Stop you crow! Oh..so this is the root cause of the problem!” realized Lakshmi. “The crow is thirsty. I'll get a bucket of water.” But the crow didn’t care. Rather, Deepika tripped over the bucket and converted the backyard into a small pond! Ouch! Ouch! Dharaam!!! “Go and bring your dadi, Deepu!” said Deepika’s father. Soon Deepika got her granny on her wheelchair. She looked at the crow suspiciously and said, “Hmm…I get that now…The crow is none other than my great grandfather, Alokanand. He’s hungry! We must give him his favourite dish, jaggery payasam (an Indian dessert made of milk, rice, and nuts).” She then made a yummy payasam, and placed a huge pot full of it near the well. But the crow didn't even look at it. H earing the chaos, Bindiya mausi (aunty), who was making rotis (bread) in the kitchen, came with a long and sturdy belan (the bread roller). “What's this noise all abou… ouch! Get away you cruel cro..ouch! Wait… ouch!” she screamed in a shrilled voice, trying to hit the crow with her belan. But the crow escaped. Deepika’s father then got an idea, “Let me call Bulchul Pandey, my inspector friend.” Bulchul Pandey rushed to rescue them, “What’s the thing my frien…ouch! So this is the thing. Wait… I’ll shoot it with my gun.” But he missed the shot. “We can scare it b y the scarecrow, which my farmer friend, Ram Khilawan has,” said Deepika’s father. Soon Ram Khilawan came with his scary-looking scarecrow and positioned it near the well. But the crow didn’t even give a damn. It instead chased Ram Khilawan and shooed him away. Hmm! Chala aya mujhey daraane!!! “Let's feed it with corn. I am sure it will be satisfied then!" claimed Bhulwa, the techie of the village. But that didn’t work too. They were all frustrated by now. Gargle says, "Crows love to eat corn." Right then, “Deepu..arrey oh Deepu…open the door! Look what I got for you.” called out Deepika’s mother. “Oh..mamma..she came back...I am sure she will solve this problem.” exclaimed Deepika with relief. Then they all told her the entire story before Deepika’s mother could utter a word. “Oh… show me the crow,” appealed Deepika’s mother. Off they went to see the crow. “Oh… ouch! So this is the… ouch! Wait a minute…She looks worried,” explained Deepika’s mother. She took Deepika's binoculars and looked carefully to see what was there on the roof of their storeroom, next to the well. “It’s a nest! The mother crow is trying to protect its eggs.” she whispered. “And so it’s hitting everyone thinking that we could harm them. We need to just leave them alone for a few days, and things will be fine.” And Deepika’s mother was right! Deepika remarked with glee, “Papa knows a lot, but mamma knows everything!”
author: Disha Kumar

title: DOG DIARIES I: The wish that came true
text: 15th FEB, 8:00am D/D, I woke up I stared at my dog collage the umpteenth time! *Sigh* "I wish I had a pet dog or a puppy! Ahh well, At least mum and dad are searching..." It was true they were looking for a dog for my family to ADOPT. We were searching on FB, rescue centres etc... I got up and did my daily chores. Then I went to play with my friends. 12:20 in the afternoon. I came back at lunchtime and had lunch. As I had a bit of pending H/W I started doing it. M om called me downstairs after thirty minutes or so and said," Prisha, we have narrowed down to 2 dogs: A labrador or a treeing cur! We will be visiting both of them on Saturday okay?" She showed me their pics. They were both cute but there was something about that little treeing-cur that made me want to adopt her! Too excited to say anything, I raced upstairs and marked the day on my calendar. 5 more days! Just 5 more days! I was starting to get sleepy.... A nap was in order! 3:00 PM I woke up and stared at the clock. 3:00 pm ALREADY! Suddenly my sister rushed in and was like: "Quick! come downstairs! Dad is waiting..!" I climbed downstairs groggily and I was feeling cranky like I always did when I sleep for a long time in the afternoon. My sister was already outside in the Verandah. I finally reached and heard a small yapping sort of sound... Was it my pet dog?! Unfortunately NO. But, there was a small dog, at the other side of the wall and was stuck it the wired fence! My dad asked one of the kids who was playing on that side to pick her up gently and give her to him (my dad). The dog was a female, we named her Lucy. She was brownish- back in colour and super- adorable! My friends came to call me to play and were shocked to see a tiny dog licking them up! I explained everything to them and my Dad ordered us to get a few bricks and fill up a bag with sand to make Lucy's bed! 3:30 PM Lucy's bed was bordered with bricks and had sand inside! She looked supercute in their with her brown fur and huge black eyes! Her tail wagged super fast! 50 km per second! (Just Kidding😉) She looked so happy! My sister and my friends started playing with Lucy. I wanted to join in but I had H/W to do! 😢 9:30 PM Night time came, but whenever we left Lucy, she would bark like mad!(We could not bring her inside as her fur made my dad sneeze) So we all sat there and left one by one until only my uncle was there... She finally slept, and so did we..! 12:00 Midnight Suddenly, we heard Lucy's tiny yaps. But that's not it, after Lucy's bark there was a grown up bark too! And then one more! We went downstairs to the frontyard and were shocked to see Lucy barking at two other grown up dogs who were at the other side of the wall! You won't believe it! They were Lucy's parents! T hey had the same fur and eyes as Lucy's! Standing with them there were to more pups. One was black and the other was brown. They were Lucy's siblings! She had been sepersted from them and gotten stuck in the wired fence! All four of us (Mom, dad, my sister and Me) and five if you count Lucy hopped into the car and drove to the other side of the wall, this was a rather long way because we had to go all aroung our colony and then we would reach the other colony which was behind ours... 12: 15 When we finally reahed, it struck me and my sister that we had not even been with Lucy for a whole day and we had to return her to her parents. Tears formed in our eyes. We took lots of pictures with little Lucy and kissed her... We left her on the street. She looked scared but when the two other dogs came she started licking them tumbling around them... The 2 other little puppies also came out! It felt so good to see the family re-united! We watched them walk away until they turned left into a street and we could not see them anymore. After sometime we all tumbed in the car and drove back home. This was an experience that we would never forget. 16th Feb D/D, Today we saw Lucy playing around with her siblings! S he looked really happy! I was glad! We kept seeing her for a few days playing there. But then we soon stopped seeing her there, though we did catch glimpses of her mom, or perhaps her dad sometimes... I might have stopped meeting her, but that hyperctive cutie will always have a place in my heart! GOOD NIGHT DIARY Anvi Stay tuned for part 2!

title: The Perfect World
text: It was a cold winter night. The sky was hazy with pollution. In the city, everyone had slept except for a young girl. She sat on the bed next to her sister thinking how the world would have been without pollution. She was so engrossed in the thought. Suddenly, Peace, her sister, woke up. "What's wrong with you,Happy? Why are you not asleep?"She was so caring towards everyone, just like Happy. "Am just thinking about the World. It's completely polluted. We can't even go out without our masks!" Happy added with a sigh. " I know sissy. It is really getting worse. But for now, Let's sleep." ''Okay" Happy replied with a smile. It was midnight, and Happy shot up from the bed. She looked terrified but happy. Then, she woke Peace up and told her what she had thought "You know what? I found a way to clean the world!" "Really? Am looking ahead to it" Peace said enthusiastically. Then Happy explained everything to Peace. "Listen. Tomorrow morning we'll have to go to our garden. We'll have to find a seed and-" "But how will we find it, they're too small" Peace snapped in the middle. "Am getting right there. We'll have to say ' The Perfect World ' to it. And you'll see what happens." "Am in. But how do you know this?" "I got a dream about it. And I know it's real!" "Great!", Peace replied....The Perfect World... The next morning, they went to their garden. They found a digital seed. When Happy said the code-word, a minor blast threw them behind. When they got up, they were amazed to see an entrance to the Perfect World. "The Perfect World!"Happy and Peace said in chorus. Everything was clean.They looked around and explored the place. Then, they invited everyone into the new world.Till their original home recovered, they stayed in there and became much lively. When others got to know about this cleanliness, they too discovered the seeds. Soon, Earth became The Perfect World!

title: The Lifelong Question
text: How long do human beings live? Around 72 years. Does that sound like a long time? Humans share this planet with many amazing creatures that live much longer and shorter lives than we do — from hundreds of years to a few hours. In the coastal waters of the Pacific Ocean, Sea Otters live for about 20 years, while Red Sea Urchins can live for 200 years. In the icy Arctic waters, Greenland Sharks can live for 400 years, while the Lion’s Mane Jellyfish lives only for one. Found in the floodplains of South East Asia, Asiatic Elephants can live for 70 years, while Elephant Grass lives for up to 15 years. In the forests of California, Bristlecone Pine trees can live for 5000 years, while Clark’s Nutcrackers live for 15 years. In Indian jungles, Crested Serpent Eagles can live for 40 years, while Rat Snakes live for 10 years. Found in South East Asian countries, Oriental Honey Buzzards live for around 20 years, while Death’s Head Hawk Moths live for about three months. Found in many parts of South Asia, Indian Pipestrelle Bats can live for over 25 years while Mosquitoes live about one month. Found on every continent except Antarctica, House Sparrows live for about 5 years, while House Flies live for about one month. How different life spans can be! A pine tree can live for thousands of years, while a moth has only a few days under the sun. No matter how much time we share on planet Earth, we all play a role in keeping it healthy and balanced.

title: Suppamma Loves to Craft
text: She collected trash from the street. She sculpted vegetables using nails and a screwdriver, and she spoke to plants. “Wow, you have so many new flowers today! How do you keep them from falling off?” Suppamma often got into trouble for breaking things when she should have been studying instead. When Suppamma was in the 3rd standard, the teacher asked each student to build a model house. Suppamma looked at houses in her neighbourhood and finally decided on building a small version of her house. She collected sticks and sap from the trees, cardboard and paper from the streets, and she started putting them all together. But when she saw that it looked different from her own house, she knocked it down and started over. This time, she plastered the sticks to the cardboard with mud and even added windows. Suppamma was very proud of her house. She woke up early in the morning and carefully carried it to school. Suppamma stayed at the back of the class while her classmates crowded around the teacher. “Sir, look at Suppamma’s house! It has windows!” said Mani. “Did you make this yourself, Suppamma?” asked the teacher. “Yes sir, I made it all by myself,” replied Suppamma. “How did you make it?” asked the teacher. “Sir, I gathered twigs from the neem tree and leaves from the banyan tree,” Suppamma told her teacher. “But, there aren’t any banyan leaves here,” said the teacher. “Yes sir, I decided not to use them,” replied Suppamma. “Very good, keep making more houses,” the teacher said, patting her on the back. Suppamma’s classmates crowded around her cardboard house the entire day. One day, Amma caught Suppamma cutting carrots to make wheels for her cart. “What are you doing! Why are you wasting carrots?” Amma snatched the cart out of Suppamma’s hands and threw it away. Suppamma held back her tears and continued building. Suppamma reached the 8th standard with a lot of difficulty. One day, there was a special event at school. Trainer Thatha taught Suppamma and her class to make useful things from trash. Trainer Thatha took straws, paper cups, rags and ropes and turned them into useful household objects. Suppamma helped Trainer Thatha. She memorised the names of all his different tools. Suppamma practiced and practiced. And soon she became almost as good as Trainer Thatha. Suppamma made bird dolls instead of solving maths problems. She made ladles for the kitchen instead of doing her homework. This made Amma angry. “Stop wasting time and do your school work!” Amma yelled. “I learnt this at school, so it’s school work, ma,” Suppamma replied. One day, Suppamma saw an old coconut shell in the waste. She picked it out, wondering if she could use it to make something. Suppamma collected three shells that day. She polished the first shell and drank coffee with it every day. She tried to use broken pieces of the second shell to play hopscotch. And she used the third shell to make a doll. Trainer Thatha taught Suppamma how to use a drill to make holes. He also taught her how to cut coconut shells and piece them together. Suppamma drew a bird on a coconut shell. Then she drew a pair of wings on another shell. She cut the shapes out of the two coconut shells and pasted them together. Her face overflowed with excitement. When Suppamma failed her 10th standard exams, Amma and her teacher were very angry. Suppamma pretended to be sad. But she was secretly excited about all the time she could spend making new things now. She began to collect coconut shells. After all, coconut shells were free. Suppamma found sandpaper to smoothen out the shells, brushes to paint them and needles to punch holes in them. Suppamma made a bangle out of a shell. Then she made an elephant and a fish. She made jewel boxes, a ladle and even a human face. Children drank coffee out of her cups… ate murukku out of her bowls… and bought her coconut shell buttons. Soon people stopped telling Suppamma that she was wasting her time. Children came to learn crafts from Suppamma. People wondered if Suppamma had started a school. “Bring coconut shells when you come.” “Hold it like this.” “Polish it and make it smooth.” “Now draw a fish on it.” “When you come tomorrow, draw a horse and bring it back.” Schools invited Suppamma to conduct craft workshops with her coconut shells. One day, Suppamma wondered if she could start selling her toys. She decided to put up a stall at the Pondicherry Crafts Fair. Suppamma’s craft stall was a success. “How much is that dove earring?” “75 rupees,” said Suppamma’s mother. “Is that a Buddha statue?” “Yes, pick it up and see.” After the crafts fair, Suppamma finally opened a coconut craft shop in her house. And that’s how Suppamma’s love for crafts made her successful!
author: Thirupurasundari Sevvel

title: Have You Ever Heard a Whale Sing?
text: The beach can be a very noisy place. Eeee, eee, eeee! The gulls cry. Woooooo, hoooo. The wind howls. Wusssh, dussh. The waves rise and crash. Now imagine that instead of being close to the ocean, you are under it. It isn’t much quieter down there! Tuk, tuk, tuk! crackles the snapping shrimp. Hroah, hroah, hroak! grunts the lemonfish. Woaaaaah eee ee ooo woooah rrr aaah! Woaaaaah eee ee ooo woooah rrr aaah! What’s that sound? Trrrrrrrrrrrrrrr! A boat passes by. It’s whales, singing in the distance —strong, loud and melodious! Whales sing short and long songs. Some songs last just a few minutes. Some songs can go on for half an hour. Whales can also sing the same song for hours on end. There are many kinds of whales. Blue Whales and Grey Whales are named after colours. Humpback Whales and Bowhead Whales are named after the shapes of their backs and heads. Omura’s Whales and Bryde’s Whales are named after people. Omura’s whale is named after Hideo Omura, a whale biologist. Bryde’s whale is named after Johan Bryde, a whaling businessman. Songs vary between different species of whales. A Blue Whale will sing a different song from a Fin Whale, just like humans speak different languages. Humpback whales are excellent composers. They mix and match notes together. If you listen carefully, you can tell that each song is made up of patterns of several notes. Blue whales sing much simpler songs. Their songs consist of just a note or two. But they make up for it by being very loud! Blue Whales can be heard over 1,000 km away. Imagine a friend singing in Bengaluru and you being able to hear them in Mumbai! Bengaluru Mumbai Bowhead Whales that live in the cold Arctic ocean are also musicians. All through winter, during days and nights of complete darkness, Bowhead Whales sing their songs under the frozen surface of the sea. Not just one song, but many different ones. Fin Whale songs are so low-pitched that humans can't hear them. Scientists place specially built microphones and recorders in the ocean to hear them! Why do whales sing? As far as we know, only male whales sing. Scientists think that it is to impress female whales or tell each other, “Look what a powerful voice I have, this means that I am bigger and stronger than you!” We may not understand what these songs mean, but we do know that they are beautiful to listen to.
author: Divya Panicker

title: JIMMY AND HIS NEW FRIENDS
text: One day Jimmy lost his way in the forest as he went for a walk. "Hello my dear friend,what are you doing there?",asked Jimmy. "I am pecking the wood",replied the woodpecker. "Why do you peck wood?" "I peck wood to find food such as ants or other insects.I also peck wood to drill holes in the trees to make nest". ﻿ Jimmy came across a porcupine on his way. "Oh!You have got quills all over your body!",exclaimed Jimmy. "I use this to protect myself from enemies",replied the porcupine. "Who are you enemies?". "Fishers,foxes,bears,wolves and mountain lions are my enemies". Jimmy then met a flock of hornbills. "Wow!You have got heavy bills"wondered Jimmy. "It helps us in fighting,preening,constructing the nest and catching prey"replied one of them in great pride. "Where do you live in?" "We live in holes or cavities in the trees and rocks". Jimmy was excited to meet an elephant. "How large you are!Do you eat so much?"asked Jimmy. "I spend nearly 12 to 18 hours a day to feed." "How heavy are you?" "I am an Asian elephant and I am around 4000 kilograms in weight.My friend who is an African elephant is around 6000 kilograms in weight." Jimmy heard a buzzing sound and looked around. "Oh my dear little bee!What are you doing here?" "I am collecting nectars from flowers to make honey". "Do all of your friends have stings?" "Only the female bees namely workers such as me and the queen bee who lays eggs have stings.The male bees or drones do not have stings". Jimmy came across two monkeys on his way. "Oh my dear monkeys!You have got such a long tail!",exclaimed Jimmy. "Our tails help us in leaping and hanging upside down from trees.They help us to hold and grasp objects such as food". "Hey grasshoppers,what are you doing there?"asked Jimmy. "We are eating the leaves,flowers,stems and seeds of this tree". "Wow!Do you have many legs?" "We have six jointed legs.Our hind legs are used for hopping and jumping". "How many wings do you have?" "We have two pairs of wings." Atlast Jimmy found his way and reached his kennel. Jimmy was happy for he made many new friends.
author: Jayasudha  Bhaskaran

title: Kick, Start, Go!
text: Brrrmm Brrrrrmmmm... Check zero. Do you know how a motorcycle works? A motorcycle needs petrol to run. But what exactly is going on inside the motorcycle when it runs? A motorcycle is basically the same as a cycle. The main difference is that a cycle is pedalled by your legs. But a motorcycle has an engine that does all the work. Engine Let's take a look inside the motorcycle engine. The engine is made up of three parts: cylinder, piston and crankshaft. IN Spark plug OUT Cylinder Piston Crankshaft It also has two gates, IN and OUT, which open and close to let petrol enter and smoke leave the engine. To get the engine started, you have to give it a kick. The kick makes the crankshaft spin. When the crankshaft spins, the piston moves up and down inside the cylinder. When the spinning crankshaft pulls the piston down, the IN gate opens and lets petrol enter the cylinder. Petrol from tank IN (closed) IN (open) IN (open) OUT (closed) Then the spinning crankshaft pushes the piston up, the IN gate closes and petrol gets compressed inside the cylinder. IN (closed) OUT (closed) Then, a spark sets the petrol on fire... Spark plug...making it explode like a firecracker. The piston is pushed down with great force, and it makes the crankshaft spin even faster. IN (closed) OUT (closed) OUT (closed) OUT (open) Now, when the piston moves up again, it pushes all the smoke out through the OUT gate. IN (closed) OUT (open) The crankshaft continues to spin, the piston moves down once again, petrol enters the cylinder and the whole cycle is repeated over and over. 1. Petrol goes in 2. Spark 3. Boom 4. Smoke goes out The engine keeps running until it is turned off or it runs out of petrol. While the engine runs......the crankshaft continues to spin......making the back wheel of the motorcycle turn. The back wheel drives the motorcycle forward......while the front wheel is used for turning. And the smoke from the engine is let out from a pipe in the back. Next time you sit on a motorcycle, you will know what is going on inside this amazing machine. Parts of a Motorcycle Accelerator Brake Headlight Engine Petrol Tank Seat Tail Light Smoke Outlet
