title: Ma, Is That You?
text: Bibi, Azeem, Juzer and Thei Thei are having a meeting in their secret meeting place. They hear a voice at their door. “Hello beta, it’s Ma! I brought snacks for you and your friends. Please open the door.” “You don’t sound like Ma,” says Thei Thei. “What’s the secret knock?” BAMBAMBAM “That’s not the right knock. Sorry, we can’t let you in!” says Azeem. ROOOAAAR “I will get in one day!” shouts the monster from behind the door. A few moments later… “Hello beta, I bought a new game for your secret club! Please let me in!” “What’s the secret knock?” asks Juzer. “That’s the correct knock!” says Bibi. “It is?” gasps the monster, “I mean, of course it is. Now let me in!” “First show us your secret club card,” says Azeem. The monster slips a card under the door. “Sorry, wrong card!” The monster bangs on the door. “I’ll get in soon!” she cries. A while later, there’s another knock at the door. “I found a puppy for you,” says the monster. “Please open the door!” “What’s the secret knock?” asks Bibi. “That’s correct!” says Bibi. “Why wouldn’t it be? Now let me in!” cries the monster. “First show us your secret club card,” says Azeem. The monster slips a card under the door. “That’s the right card,” says Thei Thei. “Now show us your handprint. Place your hand against the window pane.” THUMP! A large, furry paw with long, sharp nails appears on the glass. “That’s not Ma’s hand. Go away!” say the four children. “ARRRRRR!” replies the monster, shaking her fist. “I would have gobbled you up if it wasn’t for your passwords!” A few minutes later, there is one more knock at the door… It’s the right knock. A piece of paper slips under the door. It’s the correct secret club card. Then—THUMP!—a hand print appears against the glass of the window. “That’s Ma’s hand!” Thei Thei swings open the door. It’s Ma, holding a tray full of mithai! How do Thei Thei, Bibi, Juzer and Azeem keep their clubhouse safe? Thei Thei, Bibi, Juzer and Azeem use three ways of checking to make sure that their visitor is actually Mummy. This method of making sure that a person is who they claim to be is called authentication. It is often used in security systems so that the wrong person cannot get hold of important information that does not belong to them. Since the four children use three steps to confirm the identity of their visitor, their method is known as multi-factor authentication (MFA). MFA ensures that there is more than one level of security to protect important information like emails, social media profiles, bank accounts, etc. So although the monster passes the first two tests by cheating, the third test still stops her from getting into the clubhouse.
author: Aakanksha Mittra; Parth Nadkarni

title: A Door to a magical market!
text: One day Rita went to her uncle's house.Her uncle told her,"Do not climb this mountain. Villagers say it is not safe!" The next morning, the girl wondered what was up there? She asked her uncle what was up there? Her uncle said," I do not know". The girl decided to climb the mountain. The next day she woke up at 5am and while her uncle was snoring she took some equipment, water and snacks and stepped out to climb the mountain. Once she reached the top she was amazed by what she saw. She saw a huge wall with a green arch door with a number 142 painted on it.The wall and its door just stood there staring at her and she was tempted to open it. She walked cautiously towards the door,took a deep breath and pushed open the door. Suddenly there was a bright light flash and when her eyes slowly adjusted back to normal she was in a different world. There were all types of foods and colors and people and kids. She said to herself,"How is this not safe?"She wanted to know about this place so she went to a boy's parent and asked what is this place. The parent said," Welcome. You are the new girl every one is talking about. Let me show you around." Her son said hi and the woman said," Come along my dear child."The little girl was worried but the woman said there is nothing to worry about. The girl followed her through the crowd, then she saw a small house. Inside it were people who were very happy. The woman said these people are happy because a new guest had arrived in the market.The girl asked who the guest was and the woman smiled and said the guest was her!!! The girl was delighted! One of the ladies served tea and another lady told her about the place and showed her pictures about the place. There was also a small little puppy prancing around happily. There was a girl who said," Do you want play with me?" Rita said okay and they went to her room.They played for some time and when it was time to go they said bye and then Rita went with the woman to another house. When she entered the house she saw five men waiting for her on the sofa. The women told Rita to introduce herself. Rita then gave an introduction about herself and the men liked her and said "Wow!" The girl said thank you and she learnt about the people and the places from them. She also asked why the house was so big. The men explained that theirs was a large family and needed a big house. Then the woman showed her to the next room where there were old people who said welcome in a hoarse voice. They took an old book from a cupboard and showed her magical fruits in the book and told her all about it. They also told her scary stories about the bad witch of the marketplace and how she took over the market and how they bravely fought back. The girl asked granny if the witch would come back but granny said she did not know. That evening, she said let's take a photo of the whole family. All of them said cheeeeeeeese!!!! and then they said byeee!!! The woman took her back to the magic door and though Rita was sad to leave she stepped back into her world and closed the door and climbed down quickly back to her house. When she came back her uncle asked," Where were you??" The girl said I went to play and went swimming. Since I needed to change to swim clothes, I went to the shop and bought a new swim suit and had fun. Her uncle looked at her suspiciously but went on with his work. Rita climbed back to her bed and slept like a log as she was very tired. She visited the market every day and shared her poems to her new friends. One of their favorites was: " One tree can start a forest, One smile can begin a friendship, One hand can lift a soul, One word can frame the goal. One candle can wipe out darkness, One laugh can conquer gloom, One touch can show you care, One life can make the difference. Be blessed today, Be that one today."

The teacher asked," Why are you not changing your clothes for playing?". The girls realized it was play session and they rushed into the room for changing their clothes. They came out happier than any one else in the school. They made friends with one girl who was very kind with them. They played skipping, they plucked flowers,built small mud houses, rolled over the little hills and played hide and seek too.They danced and sa ng all day, got dirty, fed the fish, talked to the plants, climbed trees and the day never seemed to end. After they were done they changed back into their school clothes. At social class,they had to study about the environment and life on earth. They learnt many things even about the corona virus and how humans faced difficult times. They read about the different types of monuments and places in the world. Sia giggled because someone farted in the class and then every body started laughing. After school the girls sang and played for some time,packed their bags and finished left over food. They recalled whatever they learnt that day and played with their rag dolls while the boys acted like soldiers and some of the boys acted like heroes and villains. After playing for some time they walked back home happily. When they reached home they changed their dress ate their dinner and told all their adventures to their mother. title: Your Body Is Yours
text: Did you know that no one in the world has a body exactly like yours? Our bodies share many similarities and differences, but each body is unique. Isn’t that incredible? Your body may be big small round wobbly. square hairy No matter what your body is like, it is very, very special. And your body belongs to you. It's important to get to know your body well. After all, it's yours for life. Are you familiar with these parts of your body? Forehead Chin Shoulder Belly button Vulva Thigh Toe Ankle Chest Palm Nostril Elbow Buttock Penis Your body changes as you grow older. Have you noticed this? Your body may get bigger smaller rounder hairier squarer wobblier. No matter how your body changes, your body will always be very, very special. Your body belongs to you, so tell someone if you’re uncomfortable when they touch you. Especially if it hurts, or doesn’t feel right to you. It may not always seem that easy, but it’s perfectly fine to show your discomfort. You can say, “I don’t like it when you touch me.” Or “Don’t do that.” Or just a loud and firm “ NO! ” If they don’t listen to you, you can always walk away. Or even shout. Remember, it doesn’t matter who it is. If you’re being touched in a way that makes you feel uncomfortable, you always have the right to say no. Even if it’s someone you love, or someone who says they love you. Because your body is yours alone, and no one else’s. Don’t let anyone make you feel otherwise. If for some reason that person does not listen to you, don’t worry. It’s not your fault. It’s never your fault. Tell your parents what happened. Or tell any adult whom you trust and feel comfortable with. It could be a teacher, a grandparent, an aunt or an uncle. Someone who will listen patiently and find a way to protect you. Because remember, your body belongs to you, and no one else. It doesn’t belong to your mother. Or your father. It doesn’t belong to your sister. Or your brother. Or your best friend. Or even your pet! Your body belongs only to you. Your body is precious, and so you must take good care of it. But it’s not always that simple, is it? Here are some questions and answers that may help you understand how best to protect your body. Which are the parts of my body that no one should touch? No one should be allowed to touch or see your private parts. When you’re young, your parents may touch these parts when they give you a bath, or change you, or even when you’re unwell. As you grow older, you will be able to do all this on your own. A doctor or nurse may touch these parts when checking your body, but it’s best to have a parent around when this happens. This also means that it’s not right for you to see or touch anyone else’s private parts. Remember, private parts are private and private means that it is just for you. Which are my private parts? Each of our bodies is unique. So think of it like this — anything that is covered by clothes in this picture is private. I felt uncomfortable when someone touched me. But it wasn’t a private part. Is that okay? It’s NEVER OKAY for anyone to touch you in any way that makes you feel uncomfortable, even if it’s not a private part. At times like this, it’s best to say “I don’t like it when you do that.” Remember, your body belongs to you and no one else. If you ever feel confused about any kind of touch, talk to your parents, or to any adult whom you trust. Is all touch unsafe? Definitely not! A kiss from a parent, a hug from a relative, holding your friend’s hand — these are all ways of showing that you care. But if you ever feel uncomfortable by any kind of touch, you can still say no. Which also means that if someone says no to you, you need to listen to them. If someone has touched you in a way that hurt or made you feel uncomfortable, and you think you need help, you can also call 1098. 1098 will connect you to Childline, an organization that helps children in difficult situations.

title: Sia and Mia's Trip to the Wildlife sanctuary
text: It was a hot Sunday morning and Sia and Mia were having a competition for who could finish a 200 page novel first. It was their favorite book which they were reading for the 75th time. Suddenly her mother came rushing in and she was looking very excited. Sia and Mia were eager to find out what happened. Their mom said that the school has organized a field trip for your class to the Nickel wildlife sanctuary on Tuesday. The next day at school, they immediately went to the library and searched for wild life sanctuary books; then they found the book and opened it and found pictures about animals and insects.They found a bunch of different types plants and birds and also looked at the top 15 sanctuaries.Nickel wild life sanctuary was in the second place and they were very excited for the trip the next day. The next day it was time to go to the wild life sanctuary in the bus. All of them were excited to go in the bus and one of the students were sleeping and some were yawning as it was very early in the morning. One of the watchmen blew the whistle and they all set off. As they were travelling one of the boys vomited on the way out of the window and it was so gross. Once they reached Sia and Mia both got down from the bus. At the entrance they saw a farm and saw a man harvesting the corn. Sia and Mia and all her classmates helped him harvest the corn and after they finished, he gave them a whole basket of corn to take to the next part of the sanctuary where they would see the wild animals. The school bus stopped at the first stop where they saw many monkeys prancing around the trees branches. They fed them lots of bananas and the monkeys gobbled them up hungrily. Next stop was at the cave zone where a pride of lions were taking their nap. The lion cub was excited to see the bus and was jumping around the daddy lion. The mommy lion just stared at our bus sleepily. The bus moved on but suddenly the driver put his brakes because he saw something on the road. Sia peeped through the front window and saw a huge green snake. She screamed and shrieked out of fear and when the other girls saw the snake the whole class was yelling and shouting. Finally the teacher calmed them all down after the snake quietly slid away. The bus moved on towards the exit and they suddenly spotted the most colorful bird ever. Mia remembered seeing the picture in the book from the library and they all were awed. The school bus drove out of the park and they stopped at a small tea shop for snacks and drinks. After the tour they went to a small local shop and bought some biscuits for the whole class even for the teachers were hungry after the snack. Wait!did I say snack, they had a heavy lunch and then Sia Mia went back home and went to sleep peacefully.

title: Mia's Birthday
text: Mia and Sia were excited for the next day because it was Mia's birthday and they were throwing a big party. They were going shopping with their mom in the evening to buy items for the party. They made a list of things they needed including the cake, decorations and return gifts. Their parents took them in the car that evening and they bought all that they needed. The next day Mia woke up and jumped up and down and she checked if everything was there. The only thing which was missing were the return gifts. They got broken crayons instead. Mia was sad but her mother said," I have an idea. You can put them in a cupcake tray in pieces of different colors. Then put it in a microwave at 180 degrees for 20 min and let it melt. Then put it in the freezer for 20 in and then take it out. The crayons will be in a cupcake shape and the mix of colors will be beautiful.Mia said that it is a great idea. The two girls decided to paint pictures about their friends and family and decorate the house with balloons. They ordered the cake and packed the return gifts and when everything was ready, they wore their beautiful dresses and combed their hair and got ready. "Put some music!!,"said Mia and their mother put on the music. Suddenly the bell rang, the friends had arrived! Mia ran to the door and all her friends came at once and they all lined up at the table and sung the happy birthday song and cut the cake. After that they played games and watched a movie. At night their parents came to pick them up and they all said good bye. It was night time and Sia and Mia looked at their mom and her mother said it was time for the girls to go to bed so they changed their clothes and went to bed. RECIPE FOR CRAYON CUPCAKES STEP1: Break the crayons into small pieces of length inch and remove all the paper STEP2: Place a mix of the pieces into each cupcake mold to fill in up to half of the mold. STEP3: Preheat the oven to 180 Deg C and place the tray inside. Bake for 20 -30 min till all crayons melt. STEP4: Take out the tray and keep it in the freezer to cool. Once the crayons harden, take it out of the mold and you get cupcake shaped crayons.

title: My family
text: I am TukTuk. My family is really big. Let us meet all...... This is my mother, And this is my father. My brother is Neetoo And my sister Meetoo. See..... My paternal grandfather - grandmother and maternal grandfather- grandmother have too arrived. My mother has three sisters. I call them all 'Mausi'. And see.... My father has four brothers. Two are elder than my father and two are younger. And more.... My two elder aunts and two younger aunts are also here. See, See, See...... My family has five little kids too. We all have great fun time. See! How big is my family. Arre! Arre! Boozo is left uncounted. It always waves its little tail throughout the day And say " Bhoun"! Bhoun"! "Bhoun"!

title: Soup for mother
text: They were caring for each other. Mother was a salesgirl in a jewellary shop. She used to take care of each wish of her children. One day, mother fell ill. Faiz called doctor and explained his mother condition. Doctor asked to take care of his mother. Doctor told that vegetable soup will strengthen his mother. Faiz had already learnt soup making from his mother. So he decided firmly to make it. Fiza was also ready to help her brother. Both took out carrot, tomatoes, spinach, cabbage etc from the refrigerator and washed too. Faiz cut all vegetables. Fiza was also helping. Onion was cut in small pieces carefully. A little garlic was also peeled and cut. A little corn flour was used to make its slurry. At last, Faiz lit the fire carefully. A pan was put on fire. A little butter was added. When hot, garlic, onion and green chilly was added. Fiza was watching everything with great interest. After some cooking, all cut vegetables with a little salt was added. It was left as such for a while. A little black pepper and corn flour slurry was added then to boiling vegetables. When all vegetables are cooked well, soup is poured in a bowl and served to mother. Mother was very happy to have soup. Mother hugged both her children.

title: Foxy fox
text: Once upon a time, there were a lion, a fox, a chimpanzee and a hyena living together in one village. While living together, one day the chimpanzee and the hyena conspired to get the fox killed. And they secretly met with uncle lion. They approached uncle lion and said "uncle lion, you are very majestic. How come you still live without shoes?". Uncle lion thrilled by their story said " you are right, i needed shoes but who can make one?". The chimpanzee said " uncle lion! Ms. fox knows very well how to make shoes?". " Ok then, bring the fox to me" ordered uncle lion. The chimpanzee and the hyena brought the fox in front of the lion. And the lion ordered her to make him shoes. The fox after accepting the order from the lion, she approached the lion and whispered " well, do you also know that the best shoes are made from a hide of a chimpanzee and a hyena?" Uncle lion having the best shoes in his thoughts replied " just make me the shoes, i will bring you the hide you need". He went and killed the chimpanzee and the hyena, brought their hide and gave it to her. The fox, knowing that the lion would kill her if she doesn't make him the shoes, was scared. And she conspired a solution. She took the hide and submerged it in a big lake. The lion threatened her because she couldn't deliver the shoes sooner. She told him that she submerged the hide in a lake in order to be softer. And she said that she was going to get it. The fox went to the river, and after a little while, she came back to the lion and she said "There is another lion in the lake that looks like you and he couldn't let me take the hide". The lion was angry and together with the fox he run towards the edges of the lake. When he saw a reflection of himself on the surface of the lake, he jumped to grab him. He drowned himself and died.
author: Dawit T. H

title: My Garden
text: He was very naughty. But he did not harm anyone. He would swing on the trees, eat their fruit, and run in the garden. The children would be very happy to see him. He loved his garden. Nowadays, Natkhat was very upset. Children would play in his garden and throw all the garbage in the garden. Some bad children would also harm flowers. Natkhat remembered his mother's learning. It is our responsibility to keep our environment clean and tidy. But the poor monkey could not understand how to explain to these children that they were doing wrong. One day some children came for a picnic in the Garden. They danced a lot, jumped and sang songs. They ate the food that they had brought and then they threw all the garbage around and went away. Natkhat became very sad and started crying loudly. Seeing him crying, Chintu came to him and said, "Natkhat my friend, why are you crying?" While Crying he said, "Look, these kids have made my garden so dirty. How should I explain to them?" "Friend, do not tell, do it and show. Let's both clean it together." Chintu said. " but...." "Those children have not yet gone, look they are near the swings." "Chintu, do you think they'll understand?" "Why not. Come, let's try." Saying that Chintu started picking up the paper. "Hey friend, they are all coming here," Natkhat said, as he hurried. "You keep picking don't look there." "Okay."........." "Hey, Chintu, what are you doing, and what is this Natkhat doing with you?" "Natkhat and I are trying to clean this garden," Chintu said while picking up the banana peel. "Sorry, we made a mistake. Come, let us do it together." Suddenly Natkhat started jumping and said, "Hurray, now we all will keep the garden clean." Everyone's faces blossomed.

title: Muni is Angry!
text: Muni is a little 5-year old girl. She is a pretty girl with thick hair and is always in a jolly mood She gets angry very rarely. She lives in a family of seven. Eight actually, if you count the ginger-coloured fur cat Nannu😺 or Nanna as Muni called him. Her mummy*, her papa *, a big bhaiya *, an elder didi *, Dada *, Dadi * and of course Muni herself! But today, Muni is angry! Let us start at the beginning. Muni was bored. She went to Deva Bhaiya. He was doing basket weaving. Muni asked "Bhaiya, Bhaiya I am bored can I weave with you? "Oh no Muni, you might hurt yourself with the woods splitters" Muni frowned and went to Diya didi who was stitching clothes for the barbies. "Didi, Didi I am bored can I stitch with you? "Oh no Muni, you might hurt yourself with the needle" Muni groaned and went to Mummy who was making yummy pakoras as it was a cold day. "Mummy, Mummy I am bored can I cook with you? "Oh no Muni, you might hurt yourself, the oil is hot and you are short" Muni sighed and went to Papa, who was lying under the car, fixing it. "Papa, papa I am bored can I fix the car with you? "Oh no Muni, you might make your pretty fair face black! Why don't you go inside and do something else?" Muni scowled and went to see what dadi was doing. She was sewing a beautiful woollen hat "I am sure Dadi will let me sew with her" Said Muni to herself. And off she went to ask "Dadi, Dadi I am bored can I sew with you? "Oh no Muni, you might hurt yourself, the needle is sharp. Why don't you go listen to dada playing the Harp?" Muni grimaced and went to dada who was not playing the Harp as dadi had said. He was cutting paper! Muni knew immediately what dada was doing! He was making something! "Dada, Dada I am bored can I craft with you? "Oh no My darling, you might hurt yourself, this scissors could poke your eye out! Now go! Muni left the room with her eyes full of tears, As soon as she got outside near Nanna's kennel she started sobbing. She complained "I am too small to do anything!! I will never talk to my family again! they never let me do anything!" And she was about complain more, when the cute kitty purred. "Oh no Nanna I forgot about you! You did not do anything to me. You are my best friend! Let us run away from home!" And so Muni picked the cat up and ran straight towards the front door when she heard a shout from her mother. "Muni the Pokaras are ready to eat. I have put some sauce on your plate! Come and Eat!" "Hmm, maybe I can forgive mummy, only mummy. Oh and I can take some pakoras with me when I am running away from home!" Muni told herself. After she finished eating, Muni was about to get up when everyone came into the room carrying a gift box and screamed ﻿SURPRISE! Muni ran to the gifts and opened them. These were the spectacular gifts Muni got: Bhaiya: A big picnic Basket Didi: Three dolls wearing gorgeous dresses Dadi: A beautiful woollen hat Dada: The best gift of all (according to Muni) A nameplate with her name stylishly written 'Marvellous Muni' Muni ran outside and searched for her dad. She found him by the car, smiling. He asked Muni "Muni, what is today's date?" Muni replied "why it is 17th July. Oh wait, there is something special today. Hmm wait is it indepen- Ho My birthday! I forgot!! HAPPY BIRTHDAY, MUNI! everyone shouted. Then everyone sat in the car. Muni looked around her. Bhaiya's basket was filled with yummy pakoras and juice. Oh and also cookies, bread- butter, apples and Some muffins. Didi's dolls were in Muni's lap, Dadi's hat sat on Muni's head, Nannu was sitting on his seat, Papa was driving the newly-fixed car, there were some kites on the floor of the car and last but not the least, Dada's Nameplate was fixed above the car numberplate. Then finally the car stopped. Muni still did not know where they were going to celebrate her birthday.she stepped out of the car. It was the picnic ground! Yayy Muni is very happy! Enjoy yourself Muni! and Happy birthday! * Papa- Father in Hindi Mummy- Mother In Hindi Didi- Sister in Hindi Bhaiya- Brother in Hindi Dadi- Grandmother in Hindi Dada- Grandfather in Hindi

title: THE STORY OF RAIN
text: It was a sunny day and Neelu was thirsty. He looked for water in his water can.But the can was empty. "Where is the water in this can?",Neelu asked the rat. "It was you who used the water to fix the bicycle tube",replied the rat. "I am sorry.I forgot it",said Neelu. Neelu went to the tap to fill water in the can. "Oh my God!There is no water in this tap.Let me go to the other water pump and pump some water." But there was no water and Neelu felt sad. 'What will I do now?',Neelu thought for a while. Neelu went to the icecream vendor. "Will you please lend me a can of water.I am very thirsty",said Neelu. "Get lost!"shouted the vendor. He then went to the tea master. "Will you please lend me some water",asked Neelu in tears. But he did not give him water and drove Neelu away. It was then that Neelu saw the water van on the street. "Stop!Stop!"shouted Neelu. He followed the van. But the driver did not stop the van. Neelu could not walk further as he was tired. He took out his harmonica and started to play it and sang songs. 'I will not stop singing until I get water',he thought to himself. Everyone in the street covered their ears with their hands and ran away on hearing Neelu's song. Atlast God sent rain to the Earth to stop Neelu from singing. Neelu danced in the rain happily. Neelu stopped singing and he collected as much water as his can could hold. From then on,Neelu played harmonium and sang songs whenever he was thirsty. People too started to sing songs to get rain.

title: Swara and The Caged Parrot
text: Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Swara. She lived on the other side of Mangiri hills. In the evenings, she loved playing on the hills with her friends. The road which leads to the hill was a tree- lined road. It was winter time and the hills received chilly winds in the evenings. Swara and friends saw a tiny parrot on their path one evening. Swara's joy knew no bounds. Swara chased down the parrot and caught it at once. The terrified parrot looked at her helplessly but Swara did not leave her. She bought a cage for the parrot and put her inside the cage. The parrot shrieked loudly "Tain, Tain", yet Swara tuned deaf ear to her wild screams. The parrot uttered a yelp as if hurt to seek attention of Swara but failed to get any. She brought the parrot home. Placing it on a window sill, she admired the beauty of the parrot. She offered some nuts. The parrot ate them but never stopped her scream. Swara's mother entered the scene. Jumping with joy, Swara motioned her mother to speak to the parrot. Her mother spoke to the parrot softly but the parrot turned its head to the other side. Swara asked her mother why the parrot looked weak and uninterested. Her mother knew the real reason. She said, " Swara, birds are beautiful and it is natural to bring them home and admire them. They are a miracle of nature just like you. But remember, we should not cage them. They love being in their own surroundings. You live in a house and they live with the nature, trees and in the fields. If you are seperated from us and this place, would you feel comfortable?" "No Mumma, No.", cried Swara hugging her mother. "Then let's open the cage and get her out. Let her fly to its own surrounding. Even if we put her in golden cage or offer her fresh fruits and nuts, that will never bring her real joy. Her real joy is living in nature and with her friends", said her mother warmly. Opening the cage, Swara and her mother let the parrot out. As soon as the cage was opened, the parrot squealed in delight. The dull face of her was completely gone. Wearing the natural enthusiasm, she circled the house twice and flew far away. Swara was happy to see the parrot's squawk. It was surely a blissful sight to see her wings flapping. As she reached some distance, all her friends accompanied her and welcomed her warmly to her home. The following day, Swara was back in the garden with her friends. They jumped, ran and skipped. Near the meadows and around the trees, they saw few birds which chirped gleefully and there on a tall tree, was a parrot looking at her. Swara winked at the parrot and the parrot squeaked in response. Happy was how everything looked. "Empathy is putting yourself in one's shoes. Empathy is feeling others pain." Name the characters in the story. Name at least one setting (place) from the story. What did you learn from the story? Adjectives are describing words. Can you name 3 adjectives in the story? Parents - Read aloud to your children and help them understand the difficult words.
author: Saranya Iyer

text: Today is Monday. It is Anie’s first online class today. ‘Wake Up Anie. You have your class.’ Mother said waking her up. Today is Monday. It is Anie’s first online class today. ‘Wake Up Anie. title: Badshahi park
text: It was last stage of hide and seek. Unknowingly, children crossed the old road. They reached to 'Badshaahi park'. It was only for name sake. Neither it has any royal touch nor any greenery. Yes, the grass was outgrown up to knees. Perhaps, no gardener has touched it since ages.Flowers might be a possibility ever but now all changed into wild growth. There was no water. There were swings but all damaged, rotten and broken. They were dumped nearly. The slides were in debilitated condition. Its stairs were left with only two steps. The slide was all perforated having fear of injuring a person if one slides over. The circular swing was too rusted to move an inch. It led to so horrible sound that children would have fled, if at all it moved with force. The crux is that 'Badshaahi park' was meant to be a horror site than an entertainment park. The royalty of 'Badshaahi park' was limited to the tomb in its center whose no wall was standing erect and safe. Some neighboring children came here to play in the evening uninterruptedly. No one bothered to question them. There was a long grave inside the tomb. It got flattened with passage of time. Now it looked like a hump. It is said that it is a grave of a cruel king. No body was allowed to get education during his life period. He feared that people would protest against him, if educated and grab his throne. That is why, his kingdom had neither school nor any library. If he saw any book in any home, he used to burn that home completely. There was a scholar in his kingdom who was world famous. People around the world used to visit him to gain some knowledge. The cruel king just hated him. He was helpless. The scholar was too famous to hurt him. The king kept waiting for the opportune time to trap him in false accusation. At last, he was hanged to death for false allegation of theft. This was full moon night, when the scholar was hanged. It is known that the king remained restless even after his death. Every full night, he used to be out of control. He used to make loop of any rope and try to hang himself. His guards had to work hard to save his life. One day, his guards missed the chance to save him. the king hanged himself to death. That was also full moon night. It is said that King was not at peace even then. His madness continued. On full moon night, king comes out of his grave and encircles around it. If there is any passerby, he grabs him and requests repeatedly for a rope. The passerby faints there out of fear. There were a few passerby through the park there after. It was evening. The children were making happy noises in 'Badshaahi park'. Now it was turn of Julfi to play as thief, he closed his eyes and started counting.....one.....two......three.......The children were running here and there to hide themselves. six....seven....eight..... All children got hid themselves here and there except Ashhar. He could not find any place. nine.. Ashhar had only one place before him, the tomb. ten.... As soon as the counting was done, Ashhar jumped inside the tomb. Julfi saw him jumping. He started shouting," No! No! Ashhar, not there." Ashhar was so scared of julfi voice that he came out at once. He saw Julfi suprisingly. " What happened? Why did you cry so hard?" " You should not have hid there." " Why? What is there?" " There is a tomb inside. That king tomb." " Then, so what?" " You know it well. Do you not know what happens during full moon?" On hearing this, Ashhar laughed loud. This was beyond Julfi's mind why he was laughing so loud? Julfi was pissed off. Upon it, Ashhar laughed more. Ashhar called other children too nearby. " Pinky.....Kaasni......Sheeloo.....Dharma.......Badkoo.....all should come out here.Who will play with this timid mouse? Come at once." The children were perplexed. What could have happened! All came running. " Arre! Why are you fighting?" said all unanimously. " Who will play with him?" Ashhar pointed towards Julfi and laughed again. " Why? What has happened?", Kasni came forward. " He says, do not go there inside the tomb. Someone will overpower you." " Julfi says right," Kasni favored Julfi. This encouraged Julfi too. "You do not know, what happens there?", Sheelu too favored Julfi. " Arre! Let Ashhar hide himself there only if he wants so. Why you all are bothered?", Badkoo intervened. " If he hides himself there inside the tomb, somebody must go there to find him. Who will go? Who will go inside tomb near grave?", Sheeloo raised her voice. " You are all coward and timid.... only rats.....I do not want to play with you." No body liked his version like this. Julfi was in high spirits because almost all friends were in his favor. He stared direct in Ashhar eyes and said," You think yourself a brave person, is it?" " I do not only think rather I am a brave person," Ashhar retaliated at once. " Can you go inside the tomb at night?" " Yes, I can." " During full moon night too?" "Yes! In full moon night too." " Beside grave too?" " Yes! Beside grave too." " Well! It is decided now. You will go inside during full moon and nail on bedside of grave." " I agree in total. Anything more." " If you win, We all will give you a cricket bat. And if you are a looser......" " The question of loosing does not arise. Hence, there is no need to think over." Ashhar was filled with pride. All knew him very well. How furious he is now! All kept silence then. Now the problem was to know the full moon night. Which day will be it? Kasni pointed towards sky. All raised their heads up. The full moon was shining bright. Today is only full moon night. " It is ok. I will go today only," said Ashhar with great confidence." Who will bring nail and hammer?" " I will bring that," Julfi did not want to miss this chance. " Well, Its fine. Let us meet at night here at right 10 p.m.", Ashhar went away trampling the grass. All children too headed towards their homes. At 10, full moon on blue sky was looking like a milky spot. Ashhar was checking his watch again and again. He was being impatient. It was sharp 10 at night. He peeped into his living room. Every one had gone to their rooms. His elder brother was engrossed in watching 'Comedy Circus' on television. His brother could not realize any mischief behind his back. Ashhar closed his room silently and went outside with soft feet. As soon as he was out, he started to run towards 'Badshahi park'. Julfi was already there near broken gate of park. Supervising all around, Ashhar just relaxed. There was nobody around neither inside nor outside park. "Have you brought nail?", Asked Ashhar whispering. Julfi handed over the nail. "And hammer?" There was hammer too wrapped in newspaper. " Now you stay here only, I just go and come back," said Ashhar throwing newspaper there only. Ashhar entered inside gate holding nail in one hand and hammer in other. The long grass was illuminated with moon rays. Swings, slides and revolving swings were all milky in moonlit night. Everything was looking unusual as if descended from magic world. Ashhar saw the tomb. He was shocked. There was dome without any ground. The tomb was appearing to float in air. Ashhar boggled for a while. He winked his eyes two three times. He saw again from top to bottom. He laughed on himself only. The ground was there only. It was the magic of moon light. Each corner was lighted turn-wise. Ashhar stepped further. Now he was near tomb. Moon light was penetrating through small window's broken net and falling on grave. The grave was turned milky. As soon as Ashhar stepped inside varandah, he felt as if grave is changing its side. He was trembling. He was posing to be strong. He tried to put other foot inside. What is this??? He could not lift his foot. He was glued to ground. Hurriedly, he pulled up his foot. Chattak...... He got his footwear damaged. He started believing that something bad was going to happen. He took unnecessary trouble. Soon he whiled away this thought. He took his damaged footwear. It was smeared with gluey excreta. He just threw both footwear there only and climbed to varandah. He peeped inside. He felt as if grave is changing its side. He was startled. He closed his eyes tightly and prayed to God. Soon he was composed. He opened his eyes and saw that grave was same to same. It did not change its side, neither right nor left. His palpitation increased. He was not same Ashhar. He was becoming weak and timid time and again. He put a quick glance over nail and hammer and moved ahead. He was inside the tomb. He turned around to inspect the situation. The patches of moon light were scattered all around. He turned his head above to ceiling. Arre! What is this? There was a black spot hanging from ceiling. Soon it moved ahead towards Ashhar. One....Two......Three....That spot was divided into many big spots. Before he could think, he was slapped on head,forehead and cheeks. He stumbled down. The bats clinged on other side of ceiling. Ashhar was totally terrified. ' Now if i lose a moment....',Ashhar did not think more. He just nailed hard on grave head. The attempt was unsuccessful because his hands were trembling. He made another attempt. 'Thak'...was so terrifying sound that he was greatly afraid. The nail had gone inside. Ashhar was relaxed over mission accomplishment. He wanted to get up, but could not. He fell down there only, as if someone was pulling his shirt. He collected all his courage but somebody again pulled him down. He fell down so vigorously that his head was injured. He again made an effort but rolled down there only. "Is grave pulling me down?" His hands and feet were cold with this thought. The whole tomb was swirling round before his eyes. The walls were leaving their place and moving ahead toward him. Fast....fast.....He listened some whispering voice too before he was unconscious. "Rope! I need rope". And that is all. He knew nothing there after. When Ashhar opened his eyes, he was at home. The home was crowded with people. All were staring at him. Julfi came forward. He put his hand on his forehead and said," It is nothing,friend. You just nailed your shirt along the nail. You were terrified perhaps." All laughed. Ashhar closed his eyes in embarrassment. " See, This is for you only", said Julfi. He opened his eyes. A bat was shinning in Julfi hands. Absolutely new. Ashhar saw surprisingly. " We all knew that you will go there and win the bet. There is some jumbling but fine. Lo! This bat is yours." Ashhar closed his eyes again. This was a gesture of gratitude.
author: Rita Bansal

title: Nina and her New Friend
text: It was a Tuesday morning and ten-year-old Nina was getting ready for school. Nina was already in her uniform and was about to wear her shoes. Her school-bus would arrive in fifteen minutes and Nina had just enough time to get her hair done and eat her breakfast. Her mom came and gave her a bowl of Upma. In the busy morning, Nina was happy she got to spend time with her mom. Amma observed that her uniform has changed from last year. She told Nina, “ Your uniform has changed. You will transform into a woman as well”. Just then, Nina heard a honk. Nina rushed to get into her bus. “What did Amma mean when she said I will become a woman?” Nina thought to herself. Her best-friend, Vinay, came and sat next to her in the bus.“ Hey, do you know why Kavita has been absent from school for the past fifteen days?” He asked her. Nina didn't know. The whole morning at school, Nina was feeling sick,very uneasy and felt like monsters were attacking her tummy. When the bell rang, Smriti ma’am, her English Teacher came near Nina and said “ Nina, come with me to the staff-room”. At the staff-room, Nina cried a little bit. “ My stomach has been aching since morning. I don’t know why. My body is also feeling weak”. Nina was feeling scared and puzzled. “Nina dear, don’t worry. Your uniform has blood stains in it.Congratulations! You have attained puberty and have gotten your first period. This is very normal for a girl. Your mother will be here soon and you can have some rest at home. Here, please take this letter-we have approved your leave". In case you have any questions, please don't hesitate to ask your mother or me or any familiar elder you feel comfortable with” Smriti ma’am said. Nina felt relieved. She was glad that she had so much support during this transitory phase. Her mother had come by then. She taught Nina to use a sanitary napkin. On her way back home, Nina was told that she should be careful about hygiene, particularly during her periods. As her mother was buying more sanitary napkins, Nina was told that her favorite meal- Rajma rice was being prepared at home as a celebration. Nina skipped happily!
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar
illustrator: Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Sonali Zohra; Tanvee Nabar

title: Hope, Where are you for Mulu?
text: Hope, Where Are You? is the story of six children around the world who are experiencing school closures because of the Pandemic. Each story follows a similar pattern of frustration/challenge, finding their hope and importantly spreading their hope to others. It is a part of the six-book series Hope, Where Are You? JOIN THE #HOPEWHEREAREYOU MOVEMENT I miss everything about school, even the two-hour walk to get there. I spend my days helping my mother while my sisters play. Staying busy keeps my mind off my hunger. I listen to school lessons on the radio when my dad is not home. Today, I overheard my father saying that he might not let me go back to school. My older sister was married at twelve. I’m just 11; I have dreams of becoming a teacher. I need to go back to school. I’m worried about my younger sisters. I’m scared for myself. My teacher, Amina, comes to my house with two men I have never seen. They bring with them a box of food for our family. My mom takes me and my sisters outside to get water. She says, “Let’s stay out here for a little while; they need to speak with your dad.” The three spend a long time talking to my father. I wonder what they are talking about. Dad pulls me aside to tell me, “I have decided that you will be returning to school.” He continues, “Can I see you teach some math to your sisters?” I’m quite excited as I explain the wonders of numbers to my sisters. Even my mom and dad decide to participate. I believe I will become a teacher. Finding that warm and fuzzy feeling inside, I eat my piece of chapati and dream about my future.
author: Armand Doucet; Elisa Guerra

title: Hope, Where are you for Nikau?
text: Hope, Where Are You? is the story of six children around the world who are experiencing school closures because of the Pandemic. Each story follows a similar pattern of frustration/challenge, finding their hope and importantly spreading their hope to others. It is a part of the six-book series Hope, Where Are You? JOIN THE #HOPEWHEREAREYOU MOVEMENT We moved last weekend into a house in the country, and I feel lonely. I loved the city, the energy, the people. But now, everything has suddenly shut down. I won't be able to go to school and make new friends. My older brother Kauri is helping my parents unpack. I was done with my room pretty fast; I don't have much. We move quite often, wherever dad can find work. So, I got rid of everything apart from my tools, because I love to tinker, and my rugby ball. In the backyard, all I see are rolling hills and moving boxes, nothing else in sight. I feel invisible. I'm not myself. "Why don't you build something with your tools?" Kauri believes we are happiest when we are building with our own hands. My brother is right. I cut and rearrange the cardboard boxes to build my old neighborhood, and then I use markers to draw the people I miss so much. I imagine what they are feeling during the lockdown. I put old rusty cans all over my cardboard world and draw germs on them. "Ah, that’s a good idea!" says Kauri again.He joins me with my rugby ball. "Let's do something about these germs." I start throwing my rugby ball to knock them down. I feel empowered. I imagine myself defeating the germs to free my friends in our old Neighbourhood. "This is brilliant," says Kauri. He pulls out his phone and sends pictures of my game to our old friends; they want to play as well! We create a chat group to share our best throws. Laughing hard, I say, "Everybody needs to do this, it feels so good!" "It feels even better because we are doing it with friends," says Kauri. I realize I'm not alone; I feel like myself. Finding that warm and fuzzy feeling, I create a video, challenging more friends and former classmates to join our game.
author: Armand Doucet; Elisa Guerra

title: Rope Shuns Tortoise Over Weaverbird
text: Once there lived Tortoise in a great thick forest under the shade of a big mahogany tree. Rope was her neighbour as he had built his home along this mahogany tree. He was tall and winding and grew from the bottom to the branches of the tree and could see the foot and branches of the tree at the same time! One day, Hunter went prowling through the forest to look for some wild meat. He passed by the mahogany tree but didn’t see Tortoise. When he had gone by, Weaver bird perched on the mahogany branches and began singing: “I’m Bird, Bird, Bird; I’m high, high, high; I travel far, far, far; I’ve a beautiful house; I’ve beautiful feathers; beautiful feet. Blue... green... red...gold.” She flapped her wings together boisterously as though clapping! She was the most beautiful bird with its multi-coloured feathers and had built the most delicate house well furnished with imported furnishings! Tortoise heard Weaver bird singing and felt uncomfortable and restless. She asked Rope, “Please, Rope, tell Weaver bird up there to stop singing. She’s making too much noise and this part of the forest is a quiet place.” “Why should I tell her to stop singing?” Rope asked before adding, “Allow the girl to enjoy herself!” “You don’t understand, Rope,” Tortoise pleaded, “if she doesn’t stop, Hunter who just passed this way will come back and shoot her!” “And what is that to me?” asked Rope. “Please stop bothering me.” Tortoise tried to reason with Rope. “If Hunter shoots Weaver bird, she’ll fall down here. And if she does, Hunter will find me and take me too!” “Well,” Rope cynically retorted, “that’s between the two of you. I don’t care...” “You don’t care! You don’t care!” Tortoise threw a jibe at Rope, nauseated. “I used to think you were wise. Don’t you know that if Hunter gets me and Weaver bird, he’ll need something to tie us with, and that puts you in danger’s way too?” Rope was silent for awhile and then became angry that Tortoise had called him a fool. He retorted, “Leave me alone. I don’t care what happens!” He didn’t respond to anything else Tortoise said thereafter! True to Tortoise’s words, Hunter came by and shot down the singing Weaver bird. Rope heard the exploding gunshot and didn’t hear the singing anymore! He looked up to see if Weaver bird was still perched on the branches and then saw an object sail past him. Weaver bird fell close to Tortoise who attempted to flee but he was slow as usual! Before she could take three steps, Hunter was already there. “Heee! Look at that,” Hunter gleefully shouted, “I shot a bird and God has given me a Tortoise too!” He picked up Tortoise first and then Weaver bird. He looked around, cut Rope with his sharp machete and tied Weaver bird and Tortoise together! He gallantly matched to his meticulous and immaculately well built palace with food enough for his children and grandchildren to dine for generations! That is how tortoise lost, weaver bird died and I grew tall. Then I learnt that, even the longest snake has a tail!
author: Cornelius Wambi Gulere
illustrator: Aripana Foundation; Herminder Ohri; Iddi  Marumba; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Kishor Joshi; Mahbubur  Rahman; Mangkonephet  Sayasane; Salim  Kasamba

title: Hope, Where are you for Bo?
text: Hope, Where Are You? is the story of six children around the world who are experiencing school closures because of the Pandemic. Each story follows a similar pattern of frustration/challenge, finding their hope and importantly spreading their hope to others. It is a part of the six-book series Hope, Where Are You? JOIN THE #HOPEWHEREAREYOU MOVEMENT My parents are both doctors. They are needed at the hospital, so my aunt is staying with me. When she arrived, I refused to say goodbye to my parents and hid in my room. Now, I miss them. I miss the experiments that we would do together, tinkering, and 3d printing. My aunt only loves to watch television. I’m ashamed of myself. When my aunt spoke to my parents today, I spied a nasty rash on my mom’s and dad’s faces. They are wearing medical masks all the time. I wish I could help them somehow. I have always loved science and technology, so I enjoy the "virtual classroom" with Mr. Chun. His lessons are the highlight of my day, and the only time I feel like myself. But today, I am quiet when he proposes a project. My friend Jin realizes something is wrong. I would usually be excited. He calls me after class and asks, "How are things going, Bo?" I confess my behavior and worries for my parents. I wonder how I can help. "You still have that 3D printer at home?" asks Jin, "Why don't we use it for the project?" Mom and Dad call, I answer. "Look, Bo!" she says, as they model the brand-new headpieces that Jin and I collaborated to design and 3D print for them. Dad asks, "Do you think you and Jin can make some for our doctor and nurse friends?" With pride, I answer, "Of course!" Mom and Dad are beaming. I am very busy, feeling more like myself. Finding that warm and fuzzy feeling, I get ready to start 3d-printing more headpieces.
author: Armand Doucet; Elisa Guerra

title: Mummy's Glasses
text: “MY GLASSES!” Uh-oh. I know that voice. Mummy has lost her glasses. Again. No fear. Mirchi and I are here. We will find them. Under the sofa we find ONE key. No glasses. On the wire we see TWO birds. No glasses. In the kitchen we open THREE drawers. We find FOUR toffees from my birthday! No glasses. “Shhh…” Look what we found. mew! FIVE kittens in a blanket! No glasses on them. SIX plants on the windowsill, swaying left and then right. No glasses. We look on the chair, under the table and in SEVEN shelves. No glasses. EIGHT bags of groceries on the dining table. We find poha inside them. We find fruits. We even find a chocolate bar. But no glasses. Mum’s coat has NINE pockets. We find... ONE coin, TWO tea bags, THREE pens, FOUR cards, FIVE hairpins, SIX keys, SEVEN bills, EIGHT buttons and NINE walnuts... Still no glasses. “WOOF!” “MUMMY!” “What?” “YOUR GLASSES!” “You helped me find my glasses! You deserve a treat.” So Mummy makes TEN big tasty laddoos for Mirchi and me. “MY PHONE!” yells Mummy. Uh-oh.
author: Tanu Shree Singh

title: Hope, Where are you for Kate?
text: Hope, Where Are You? is the story of six children around the world who are experiencing school closures because of the Pandemic. Each story follows a similar pattern of frustration/challenge, finding their hope and importantly spreading their hope to others. It is a part of the six-book series Hope, Where Are You? JOIN THE #HOPEWHEREAREYOU MOVEMENT My brothers are doing homework. Mom is teaching her high school classes. Everybody is staring at screens. I am bored, bored, bored. I try to follow my classes on the computer: it’s hard, I miss playing outside with my friends, and I miss dancing. It feels like my skin is crawling, and I’m antsy. I wish time could go faster. Maybe I can speed it up if I run really fast. Oops, I disturbed everyone again. “Just. Stop. MOVING!” screams Mikey, and “Arrrrrgh, not again,” yells Peter. I’m getting on everybody’s nerves. I’m not myself. “Kate, could you try to read quietly for a while?” I sit still for two minutes, and my legs start twitching. I’m ready to burst out. I’m going to get in trouble again. All of a sudden, the phone rings! I run and answer. It’s Mrs. Robinson who enquires, “How are you, Kate?” I sneak underneath the table, with tears welling in my eyes I whisper “I’m being bad, I can’t sit still.” Mrs. Robinson reminds me that at school, we use Yoga to calm down in the morning. She suggests that I practise after waking up and promises to send her videos to mom. A week later, I am leading my family through Mrs. Robinson’s yoga! I’m finishing with the tree pose. I’m really good at this, even my brothers can see it. “Thank you, Kate,” Mom says. “What a wonderful way to start the day.” I feel helpful. I feel wanted. I feel like myself. Finding that warm and fuzzy feeling keeps me calm and focused all day.
author: Armand Doucet; Elisa Guerra

title: Hope, Where are you for Gaby?
text: Hope, Where Are You? is the story of six children around the world who are experiencing school closures because of the Pandemic. Each story follows a similar pattern of frustration/challenge, finding their hope and importantly spreading their hope to others.It is a part of the six-book series Hope, Where Are You? JOIN THE #HOPEWHEREAREYOU MOVEMENT We are home all the time. It is not easy. I try to keep up with “distance learning,” as my teacher calls our lessons on the computer, but sometimes I get distracted. Nico and Felipe, my little twin brothers, cry a lot. It drives papi nuts. He gets angry and yells at mama. I hate it when this happens. Mama says that papi is worried about his business. She tries to comfort me with “Everything will go back to normal, and we will be fine once this is over.” I hope she is right. My family is not itself anymore. The next day I'm distracted when my grandfather calls. I'm fearful he will hear Nico and Felipe crying, and Papi's loud voice in the background. Grandpa asks, "What's wrong, Gaby?". I can't stop myself; I tell him that my parents are stressed and fighting a lot. The twins cry constantly. I don't bake with my dad anymore. I miss the smell. I miss walking under the Jacaranda trees with him while I share my school stories and eat our freshly baked cookies. Grandfather says, "Gaby, I have an idea for your class project. Why don't we write the story of how these days have been for you? I'll help with your writing, and you can do the drawings." “Your Grandfather called,” Mama says. She hugs me and whispers, “Your Dad and I would love to see your story.” I finish reading it to them, and they sit in silence. Papi leans over to Mama and says, “I’m sorry” and gives her a big hug. He turns to me with a large smile on his face, “Gaby, why don’t we bake cookies?” Singing and baking, I feel like myself again. Finding that warm and fuzzy feeling, I decide to share my story with my teacher and classmates in my next lesson.
author: Armand Doucet; Elisa Guerra

title: Hope, Where are you for Alessandro?
text: Hope, Where Are You? Is the story of six children around the world who are experiencing school closures because of the Pandemic. Each story follows a similar pattern of frustration/challenge, finding their hope and importantly spreading their hope to others. It is a part of the six- book series Hope, Where Are You? JOIN THE #HOPEWHEREAREYOU MOVEMENT It's been a couple of weeks since we started learning from home. My teacher made sure I brought my books and things home, including my violin, before the school closed. It's been hard. Grandma has been very sick. I can see my parents are worried. I'm worried as well. We can't talk or visit grandma. I'm very sad. I am struggling to express my feelings and don't want to bother my parents. We live in a small apartment, but I still feel very alone. I'm not myself. We get the phone call that Grandma is gone. Just like that. I didn't get to say goodbye. Mrs. Rossi, our next-door neighbor, calls: "I heard the news, Alessandro. I'm so sorry." I stay quiet, not sure what to say. Mrs. Rossi continues, "Don't forget your violin, Alessandro. In these times, you can express yourself through your music." I mumble a thank you for the call and hang up. I look at my violin for a long time and finally pick it up. Playing, I start to feel relief as tears roll down my cheeks. My parents are watching me, smiling. My parents tell me that grandma always loved to hear my music and that I should go out on our balcony to play for the sky. I step out early evening and start playing. To my surprise, other neighbors come out and play their instruments, and people begin to sing. I feel like myself again. Finding that warm and fuzzy feeling, I hope grandma can hear my music.
author: Armand Doucet; Elisa Guerra

title: Mittu The Parrot
text: Once upon a time there lived a little parrot called Mittu in a small forest. He and his cousins loved eating red chillies. He loved the chillies the most. One day, he thought to go to the neighbouring village. When he arrived there he saw many huts. One hut had 3 big chillies in front of it. He was delighted. He was very happy. He flew to the hut but, unfortunately he was shooed away by the woman of the house. He did not give up. He was not in a mood to give up. He tried again when the lady was away from her hut. That time he picked up 2 big chillies. He stocked up a few chillies for the next day. He was very happy. Then when all his chillies were over, he thought '' I have eaten a lot, now it's time to work hard and find some nuts in the forest.'' saying that he returned back to his house. He worked hard to find nuts and lived happily ever after.
author: Anvita Nair
illustrator: Wesley van Eeden; NIVEDITHA M; Sanjay Sarkar; Soumya Menon

title: my mamma
text: Deepa Balsavar, Promina Shreshtha, Radhika Tipnis, Raihana A, Soeurm Kakada My mamma will take care of me very well. But she always tells my brother to finish everything on his plate. My mamma's dream is to grow up and make me a big officer and scientist. My mamma also brings new clothes for festivals to me and my brother. My mamma also tells my brother to clean his room because he is not very good at keeping his room clean. After he cleans his room it will be clean, but he will again dirty it. But my mamma is very patient to wait until i go to sleep My mamma is the best mamma EVER.
author: Sandhya Revuri
illustrator: Amalendu Kaushik; ASM Tanvir Hassan Raju; Deepa Balsavar; Promina Shreshtha; Radhika Tipnis; Raihana A; Soeurm  Kakada

title: my doll
text: One fine day I went to a doll party, there were many different types of dolls on a red mat.I could not get my eyes off them. Even I wanted a doll, I yelled to my mum and dad. My mum was kind enough to bring me a nice doll wich costs of 70 pounds. It had a beautiful pink dress on. Now I was taking it everywhere I go. I love my doll. It is all because I have a kind and a hard-working mum
author: Sandhya Revuri
illustrator: Chiradeep Majumder; Melany  Pietersen; Priya Kuriyan; Tawfiq Ahmed  Anwar

title: A Little Help for Cumulo
text: Can you see the little cloud peeking from behind the curtain? That’s Cumulo. She’s hiding. Cumulo’s face is bright pink. She is sweaty. She wants to hide so no one can see her. Do you know why? When Cumulo goes to the cloud park, she tries to float. But no matter what she does—whoop! She turns upside-down. Cumulo feels the other clouds staring at her. Are they pointing? Are they laughing? Cumulo flies all the way home. She had really wanted to float in the park. But now she just feels like hiding. “Cumulo! What are you doing inside?” It’s Cumulo’s cousin, Pufflo. She doesn’t want to tell him what happened. What if he laughs at her? Cumulo tells him anyway. Pufflo smiles. “When I first went to the park, I couldn’t float either. I would just hang there,” he tells her. “I thought everyone was laughing at me. I wanted to run away!” Cumulo can’t believe it! “What did you do?” she asks. “I just thought about how much I wanted to float! And you know what?” says Pufflo. “Pretty soon, I forgot about everyone else! I was just floating and having fun. Come on, let’s go to the park together.” Cumulo isn’t sure. What if all the clouds laugh at her? “We will float together,” says Pufflo. “Just think about floating and having fun!” “I just thought about how much I wanted to float! And you know what?” says Pufflo. “Pretty soon, I forgot about everyone else! I was just floating and having fun. Come on, let’s go to the park together.” Cumulo isn’t sure. What if all the clouds laugh at her? “We will float together,” says Pufflo. “Just think about floating and having fun!” There are many clouds in the park. But Cumulo feels better because Pufflo floats with her. He even floats upside-down with her! Cumulo doesn’t think about the other clouds anymore. She just thinks about floating and having fun! And then, something amazing happens. Some other clouds join them and float upside-down too. They all spend the afternoon together, floating upside-down. Cumulo is so happy that she turns orange, then yellow, then purple!
author: Kuzhali  Manickavel

title: YOGA
text: I can do that u can so please like my story one day minu saw her dad doing yoga but her grandma told dont do u ma but before starting yoga she watched some videos how to do that excersixe in her laptop. But minu always smile and have positive energy in her mind so she told her grandma i can do and i will show u she did it and shownrd her grandma she was suprised. Moral be positive.
author: Snehal Raut
illustrator: Ana RoGu; aumika shetty; Krishna Bala Shenoi; Radhika Tipnis

title: The Mighty Tethys Sea
text: Here are some fossils. Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of a living organism, plant or animal. They tell us what life on Earth was like hundreds, thousands or even millions of years ago! This is the fossil of a creature called an ammonite. Ammonites were squid-like creatures that lived in the sea 400 million to 65 million years ago. Paleontologists and archaeologists are scientists who dig up the ground to find fossils. When they dug in the Himalayas, they found lots of ammonites. But how did the fossils of sea creatures end up on the tallest mountains in the world? To answer this question, we have to go back a hundred million years, when the Earth was quite different. Back then, Earth had only two enormous continents: Gondwanaland and Laurasia. Between them was the gigantic Tethys Sea. LAURASIA GONDWANALAND THE TETHYS SEA Just beneath the surface of the continents and the sea sits a layer of Earth called the outer crust. This outer crust is made of very large moving pieces called plates. Earth’s plates are almost 100 kilometres thick and made of solid rock. But underneath is a layer of molten rock that allows the plates on top to move really slowly. OUTER CRUST TECTONIC PLATES MOLTEN LAVA As the plates moved, the two supercontinents began to break apart into smaller and smaller pieces. LAURASIA GONDWANALAND TRIASSIC PERIOD JURASSIC PERIOD All of the pieces began moving, each off on its own journey. We will now follow the journey of two plates in particular. NORTH AMERICA SOUTH AMERICA ANTARCTICA EURASIA AFRICA INDIA AUSTRALIA CRETACEOUS PERIOD The Indian plate was a fast-moving plate. It moved closer and closer to the Eurasian plate until......BAM! It collided right into it! This collision was so powerful that it caused the bed of the Tethys Sea to rise up, sea creatures and all, and form the Himalayas. How do we know all this? Well, remember the ammonites? Until the fossils of these sea creatures were discovered, we didn’t know for sure that plates were under the continents and oceans, moving about. EURASIAN PLATE INDIAN PLATE And you know what? The plates are still there, beneath our feet, moving very, very slowly. (Except for when they move suddenly, which causes big earthquakes!)
author: Juvena Jalal

title: Counting Cookies
text: Once upon a time, there was a cow called Ginger who lived on a farm. A little girl called Abby also lived on the farm. One day, Abby spotted Ginger and saw that she wanted to eat cookies. Abby had ten cookies. Abby went outside and gave half of her cookies to her new friend. Abby was left with five cookies. Ginger was very happy. She loved cookies! Abby saw just how happy Ginger was and so she gave Ginger the last five cookies. Abby was sad. She only had two cookies left! So Abby went back home to bake more cookies with her mother. The next day, Abby took Ginger twelve cookies. Ginger ate eight of them and left four of the cookies for Abby. Abby and Ginger carried on sharing their cookies. They became great friends.
author: Hana Lou

title: Alung and Mak Otek
text: Pung has chickens as his pet. A Pelung rooster named Alung and a hen named Mak Otek. Mak Otek has three newborn children. Alung the Pelung rooster is Mr. Pung's favorite pet. Alung has a beautiful voice. Alung is a singing contest winner. Of course Mr. Pung gives more attention to Alung compare to Mak Otek. That is why Mak Otek dislikes Alung. "Alung again, huh" Mak Otek Grumbled. "Alung, Mr. Pung gave you a lot of delicious food again! I should be the one that recieved a lot of food for my children!" Mak Otek yells. "Here, give it to your kids. I do not really like it." Alung said. "No,thanks! I will look for worms to feed my children!" Mak Otek answered with anger. Alung is sad. Actually, Alung wants to be like Mak Otek and her children. He wanted to look for worms too. In the late afternoon, Mak Otek should go into the cage. But, suddenly a ferret comes attacking. The ferret wanted to catch Mak Otek. Mak Otek shocked and yells, she wants to scare the ferret. Unfortunately, the ferret is not scared of Mak Otek. "Please, help my children! Please!" Mak Otek screams. Suddenly, Alung uses his loud and beautiful voice to make Mr. Pung comes out of his house. Luckily Mr. Pung comes out of his house after he hears Alung's loud voice and quickly keeps the ferret away from his pets. In the end, Mak Otek and her kids are safe. Mak Otek is very thankful to Alung. She feels sorry for always disliking and envying Alung. From that day, Mak Otek sees Alung as a very kind rooster. They become a best friend in the end. THE END
author: Hilman Haqiem Budiyanto

title: Sekar and Aniah
text: You are a new pupil in this Eagle 2 nd grade, right?" "Let's play together" " Do you want to be my friend?" That was the first time I met Aniah, a new pupil in my class. I went to an international school in Singapore. Since then Aniah has become my best friend and we always play together. We are friends despite our many differences. I am Indonesian, while Aniah is Indian. I have short hair, while Aniah has long hair. My favorite pet is a cat, while Aniah likes dogs. I celebrated Eid feast, while Aniah celebrated Christmas. I have a younger sister, while Aniah has a younger brother. Although we have many differences, we also have many similarities. I like to visit Aniah's apartment, she also likes to visit my apartment. While we playing, we also like to make songs together... "wa wa wa hamburger" is our creation. Pizza is our favorite meal, we make pizza together when I visited Aniah's apartment. When we have free time at home, we love watching Captain Underpants cartoons. Aniah and I love "Binnie Boo" dolls. Every time we play together we imagine that the dolls are papa, mama and their children. Everyday after school, we like to walk together down the Dakota River before splitting up to our respective apartments. Suddenly that day came... My Papa told us that all of our family had to go back to Jakarta. Im very sad. Aniah is also sad after knowing this news. We have to live far apart in different countries and different schools. But I am not worried, we'll still be able to talk even though we are far apart through video calls using mama's cellphone. Every time we talk, we talk about many new things in our respective places. "How are you Aniah?" " How is your school?" "Let's get the Binnie boo dolls out."........... There are still many differences between us... But there are also many similarities... Even though we are far apart....
author: Siti khofifatul Ulya
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Aditi Dilip; Radhika Tipnis; Resiandari; Rohit Kelkar

title: Alung and Mak Otek
text: He is a winner. For that reason, Mr. Pung paid more attention to Alung than to Mak Otek. and that's why Mak Otek doesn't like Alung so much. "Huh... Alung again and again!!" Mak Otek grumbled. "Look, Alung! Mr. Pung gave you plenty of the fancy meals even though I need them more than you do, for my kids!" complained Mak Otek. Alung replied, "You can take my meal for your kids since I don't really like it" "No! I don't want that. I can just look for worms for my kids!" Mak Otek answered angrily. Alung feels sad. He actually really wanted to hunt for worms just like Mak Otek and her kids. As the sun began to set, it was time for Mak Otek and her children to went back to their chicken coops. But all of the sudden, a fox stopped by and tried to kidnap one of the chicks. Startled, Mak Otek started to scream to scare the fox. Unfortunately, the fox didn't seem to be scared of her. Mak Otek screamed frantically, "Help!! Please help my child!" All of the sudden, Alung made loud noises with his squeaky voice to call Mr. Pung. Thanks to Alung, Mr. Pung showed up and approached Mak Otek and her children. He succeeded to scare away the fox, and Mak Otek and her children were safel Mak Otek felt so thankful to Alung. She also felt bad for hating Alung and being jealous of him. Ever since that day, Mak Otek took Alung as a very kind pelung chicken. They become friends that always share everything...

title: The Missing Friend
text: One morning, Velan, watchman of a zoo, woke up with a shock. Velan asked the bear," Our friend is missing, have you seen him?" "Go and search in the forest. People who have spotted him will tell" replied the bear. He searched the entire forest for the missing friend. "Ask the heron,who is at the bank of the pond. He will know" sang the owl and the frog. "Have you seen my friend?" Velan asked the heron. "The tortoise lives in the river. Ask him lovingly. He will tell a way" said the heron. "My brother, who lives on the ground, will tell through his barks" said a half-sleepy tortoise. Velan approached the puppy and asked "Have you seen my friend?" "How does your friend look?" asked the puppy. "He is brown in colour and he eats a lot of fruits!!" replied Velan. "I know. Come with me!!" said the puppy. On reaching the entrance gate, Velan found his friend, with a fruit in his mouth. Overjoyed, he thanked the puppy.

text: Lia Mr Pung has a pelung chicken or could be called pelung long crower and a hen. Their name was Alung and Mak Otek. Mak Otek just hatched her chicks.
