title: Aiman and Her Bag
text: She had me as her bag and her best friend. She woke up in the morning and prepared for school. I looked at her from the corner of the room and I felt so happy because she will bring me to school with her. Aiman carries me on her back every day. My heart beat fast as she run. I leaned on her back until we got on the bus. Aiman loves me so much. She let me sit on her lap. I met new friends on the way to school, we chatted and sang a song. As we arrived at school, we run with each other best friend. Aiman had a lot of stuff in my belly. She brought colorful books, notes, an eraser, a pencil and her lunch box. Hm.. this delicious smell must be coming from her lunch box. I'm always beside her wherever she goes. She jumped here and there with me staying on her back and made the stuff barge in my belly. During lunch break she left me at the class with the other bags. I had a great time with them. We laughed and sang together even though I felt lonely and I missed Aiman. As the class ended, Aiman put her stuff in my belly real quick and hurry home. I gasped for air because she run fast to catch a bus. Aiman put me in the corner of the room as she got home and forget me. I looked at her from afar. As she grew up, her stuff also increasing. She was getting tired to carry me on her back. Is there anything that could decrease our burden?
author: Szahara Gita

title: The wish of Appu
text: Once upon a time there lived an elephant named Appu in the zoo and he was very sad because he was the only animal which was black in colour. In the same zoo there lived a tiger named Siva. On seeing Appu, he asked," What happened to you?" In a dejected tone, Appu replied " I am the only animal who is black. Look at you all, how beautiful you look." Handing over the stripes from his body, Siva said." Hey Appu, you can take these." Appu was very excited and delighted to hear this and readily accepted the offer. Seeing this, the pea cock gave its vibrant colours to Appu.. And the cuckoo lent her voice. Appu danced in ecstacy and hopped around singing cu cu. The children who visited the zoo were unable to identify Appu and enquired " Where is Appu, Where is Appu?" Appu became unhappy again. He realized his mistake and transformed back to his original self.
author: Aashirwaadh Creations
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Deepa Balsavar; Lavanya Karthik; Padmanabh; Rob Owen; Ruchi Shah

title: The Rabbit who Became a Chef
text: I eat only raw carrots everyday," said Rabbit to himself. "I'm bored of eating raw carrots!" "What should I do to make these carrots tastier?" One day, Rabbit went to a peasant's house and saw a pot boiling over heat. Right after he got an idea, the peasant's dog barked and chased him. "Hmm," thought Rabbit. "What should I do now?" Rabbit tried to leave the carrots in the sun. But, the carrots were still raw like they were before. Then, he put them on fire. When he bit into them, those carrots tasted bitter! He thought and thought and thought about what should he do. ﻿ Finally, he got an idea! First, he found an old tortoise shell. Then, he gathered some branches. ﻿ And three stones. Yippee! Rabbit finally found a way to cook his carrots. ﻿He was so happy that he invited his friends over. And they ate the yummy cooked carrots.
author: Kalista D. T

title: The Special Painter
text: He wants to make a beautiful painting. Theo loves to draw. His mother was a painter while his father was an art teacher. His right hand was missing fingers, but he still dreams to be a painter. He wants to make a beautiful painting. Theo's mom enrolled him in an art class at the children's centre Teacher asked the children to draw a zoo. They were super excited. Na wants to draw a peacock. Ti likes to draw a cat. Bin wants to draw a polar bear. Hoa asked him. "What do you want to draw?" "All of them!" said Theo Ti was sharpening colour pencils. "Will you use pen brushes or colour pencils?" asked him. "I will use both." said Theo Bin took out her colour box and asked. "Will you draw with your left hand?" "I will try to draw with my both hands." Theo answeed. Na mixed some colours and asked. "Which colour will you use?" "I will use all of them!" said Theo excitedly. But Theo cannot hold a brush with his right hand because he does not have fingers. His brush kept slipping off. Firstly, Theo tried to draw a chicken. Soon after, his hand smeared with colors. Theo almost give up. But he found a cute shape in his palm. It looked like a chick! Theo had an idea! Theo smeared his hands with brown colour. He chuckled.. "Now I painting with my own hands." Theo place his palm on a corner of the paper. He smiled and splashed the brown colour at some point. Soon it formed a cute puppy. Theo then made another mark of yellow with his hand and arm. He added orange dots on top of yellow colour. And it became a giraffe! After that. He painted his foot with brown colour and step on the paper. Then added some curve and circle. How cool! A cute bear formed! Theo painted his heel with blue and red colours. Then, he place it on the paper from the teacher. He added some lines, and a few colourful birds appear on the paper. "A train which take us to tour around a zoo was missing" said Theo. "Does anyone want to draw it with me?" It was amazing class! Together, they made a wonderful painting!
author: Ellyza Nurhayati
illustrator: Nguyễn  Minh Hải; Nguyễn  Minh Hải

title: Hide From The Bees
text: We accidentally hit a beehive! Run! Hurry! We have to hide from the bees! We hid under a blanket. Uh oh, they know where we are! Where else should we hide? Lets try hiding in the water! Oh my, this river does not help. The bees still know where we are. Where else should we hide? Wait! I know! Do you see the smoke over there? We ran to the smoke. I remembered grandma's advice. Grandma said bees are afraid of smoke. I guess she was right. The bees started to fly away. Bye, bees! Fly away! Sorry that we bothered your home! Yeaay! The bees are back in their beehive. Everything is under control!
author: Amadea Anna

title: Tutu's Friends
text: Tutu is a sweet, naughty girl. She is always up to some mischief. She has a lot of friends. Come, let's meet them. This is Tuntun the Cow. She eats green grass. She gives a lot of milk. This is Sona the Fish. She keeps Tutu entertained. This is Turr Turr the Frog. Tutu and Turr Turr chitchat on the banks of the lake. This is the mischievous monkey Khonkhon. Tutu and Khonkhon both hang upside down and play together. And now we meet Choonchoon the Mouse. He is really odd. He sits on the tree branch and tells Tutu stories. This is the sweetest dog: our brave Sheru. He fetches the newspaper early in the morning. He reads out the news to Tutu. Tutu loves all of them. She lives in a special world.
author: Shalynee S

title: THE ROOSTER AND THE HEN
text: One upon the time, there lived a farmer in the village, named Mr. Pong. He has a rooster, Alung, and a hen called Mak Otek. Mak Otek just hatched her children. Alung is the pride of Mr. Pong's chicken. Because of his long melodious crow, Alung became a champion chicken. Mr. Pong treated a well to Alung but not to Mak Otek and her children. That's why Mak Otek didn't like Alung because she was jealous of him. "hmmm slung..alung..and slung", grumbled Mak Otek. "Look, Mr. Pong gave you lots of food and it's scrumptious Alung! Whereas, I need it more to feed my children", shouted Mak Otek "You can take this food and give it to your children. I don't really like it", replied Alung. "No! I'd better find a worm for them", Mak Otek answered. Alung murmured sadly, actually, he wanted to be like Mak Otek and her children who could scavenge the land and found the worms. The day was getting dark, it was time for Mak Otek and her children to get into the cage. Suddenly, a weasel came and approached Mak Otek and her children. The weasel wanted to catch Mak Otek's children. Mak Otek was shocked and shouted. She tried to drive away from the weasel. Unfortunately, the weasel was not afraid of her. "Help me... please help my children", shouted Mak Otek. Suddenly, a shrill Alung appealed to Mr.Pong. After hearing Alung shrill, Mr. Pong rushed out of the house and helped Mak Otek and her children. Finally, the weasel stayed away and Mak Otek's children were saved from danger. After that incident, Mak Otek thanked Alung for helping her. She felt sorry for being jealous of him until hostile to the Alung. Since at that time, Mak Otek believed that Alung was a kind-hearted chicken. THE END
author: lilis Setyowati

title: The Smartest Frog
text: Nobody wants to play with him. One day, The Frog feels sad, and he ran away. He jumps to a house and hides under the bed of a boy. The boy's mother come in to check his homework. "You don't have a good grades," said The Mother. "Don't you want to be a smart boy?" The boy never work hard at all. He is very lazy. Until one day, all of the letters and numbers is falling out from the page of the book! The Frog is still hides under the boy's bed. He jumps for joy when he sees all of the letters and numbers. "I will learn it all!" he said. "I will be the smartest frog and nobody won't make fun of me!" The letters and numbers got dusty because they have not been used for long time. The Frog learns how to spell and write with the help of the letters. The numbers help The Frog to learn about how to count and study mathematics. The Frog is study hard for months...... and now, he can read like an expert! Uh-oh! One day, the boy's mother found The Frog inside her house. The Frog is forced to leave the house. However, The Frog had learn many things, and he decides to go back to study in the garden. "The Frog now can read, write, and count," said other frogs. "Whoa! Can you teach us, Frog?" In the next morning, the lazy boy open his book. "What?! Where all the letters and numbers gone?" He shouts. He doesn't know that The Frog is carried out all of the letters, and now, he is the smartest frog in the garden!
author: Putri Wulandari

title: Yummyyy... A Cup of Milk Tea
text: She goes up, up, and up. She doesn't stop running "Mom, Dad! Come on! We've to get there before the sun sets." Mira said to her parents Her mother replied, "Mmm... I love this freshness air". Mira said," I love this fragrance and the sounds of dried leaves on my feet." Daddy said, "Hmmm... I also smell something delicious. A cup of Milk tea!" " 2 cups of milk tea, please." My daddy asked to the seller. " And a small cup of milk tea for my daughter," Mommy said. "Yes, sure. Wait for a minute", said the seller Sssrrrrkkkk...... He turned on the stove with a match and put a pan of water on the fire. The water gets hotter The small bubbles get bigger The water starts to boil The seller pour a glass of milk into the pan. "Mom, look how they mixed. The color changes. Wow. That's amazing!', said Mira. Mommy said," Now, look. What will happen when the tea is combined." Mira waited patiently, two minutes later Mira was surprised, "Ooh, the color's changing again" "Is the tea ready, uncle?" asked Mira "Almost!" Said the tea seller Swooosh, swooosh, swooosh... The tea seller pour tea from a pan into three cups with a filter. Tea leaves are left in the filter After that, the tea seller added sugar into the cups. It's Mira's job to put sugar into the tea when Mama and Papa made it at home. She likes the sound of a spoon when stirring sugar. Mira saw the sugar in the glass dissolves. "Now the tea is ready! Mira said See. The tea seller makes tea Can you explain the steps for making tea? Late/ dissolve: The tea seller add sugar to the tea, sugar mixed with tea and dissolves, the tea is sweet This process: the time of a solid object mixed with liquid objects Filter: The tea sellers use filters to filter the tea, Tea leaves are left in the filter This process: the time of a solid object in a liquid discarded using a filter Spread: The smell of tea spreads from the tea house to Papa's nose through the air. This process: when a substance is moved from a place that contains a lot of the same substance to a place that contains little of the same substance. Convection: when making tea, heat under the pan went up because of the fire. The Cold water above the top down. This cycle continues and finally all the water gets hot. This process: When heat flows with liquid Conduction: The tea sellers put the pan on the stove, turn on the stove, and the pan gets hot This process: When heat is moved from solid objects to liquid objects
author: Adilla Chrisna

Otek was surprised and screamed as loud as possible hopping that it will drove the civet away. Unfortunately, the civet does not even flinch." HELP.... HELP MY CHILDREN!", Otek screamed in fear. Suddenly, a high pitched sound was heard. It was Alung calling Mr. Pung out of his house. Luckily, Mr. Pung immediately approach Otek and the chicks when he heard Alung's voice. The civet was successfully repealed. Otek shows her gratitude to Alung because she always envy him all this time and spreading hate on him just because of something that was not really important. Since then, Alung is seen as kind-hearted and valuable pelung chicken. In the end they become a really good friends. FIN

title: The Story of Martha
text: Martha was a 11-year-old girl. Marathon running was her passion. She joined her school's marathon club and succeeded in all her marathon contests and made everyone proud. One fine day, while Martha was eating her breakfast, her mom leaped into the dinning room and hugged Martha. She couldn't understand anything and was confused. Then, her mom said that Martha was selected for the district level Marathon competition!! Martha was so happy. She decided to practice very hard for the competition. Then, she called her cousin and best friend, Zoe, who studied in the same school as Martha, and told her about the news. Zoe was also a marathon runner but wasn't as good as Martha. In fact, Zoe envied Martha. But the news of Martha being selected for the district level made Zoe's envy turn into jealousy. As soon as Martha hung up the phone, evil thoughts began flooding Zoe's mind. She was thinking of a plan to not let Martha participate. That is when Zoe's older brother, Zen, interrupted her thoughts. He was curious of what kept his sister so lost in thought. Zoe opened up and told him everything. Zen, who was unlike his jealous sister, felt happy for Martha. But, he didn't say anything about it to Zoe. He had a plan in his mind. He would listen to Zoe's evil ideas and inform it to Martha and both of them would figure out a way to stop her. Zoe said that she would somehow injure Martha's leg so that Martha couldn't play and since she is the second best marathon runner, she would be selected. Zen had his own plans. Soon, Zen was walking to Martha's house to tell her about Zoe's evil plan. Martha, on the other hand, refused to believe him. She trusted Zoe. Even though Zen told her everything, she still refused to believe. The sun was beginning to set and Zen was walking back home, thinking what he could do to save his cousin sister. Soon, he came up with a plan. Time flew and it was finally one day before Martha's competition. Everything was going as per the plan for all the three of them. Martha practiced very hard, Zoe was working on executing her plan and Zen was setting up some costumes for his plan. The sun set that day. Martha and her parents went out that night as Zoe had invited all of them for a family dinner at her home. Everybody in the family was present at Zoe's house. Zoe sat next to Martha during dinner time as usual. They were casually chatting but Martha didn't mention anything about Zen's warning of Zoe's evil plans. That night, everybody's attention was on Martha, which made Zoe even more jealous. So, she set out early to execute her plan. She went to the nearby forest and examined for any dangerous animals and then switched off the lights in the street so that Martha wouldn't have a clue of where Zoe was leading her to. She then spotted Martha in the corner of the room, standing alone. She invited Martha for a walk, which was actually a plan for injuring Martha's leg. Although everything was going according the plan, Zoe smelled something fishy about Martha. She seemed, well, different. But Zoe didn't have any time for investigations. She carried on. She was talking with Martha and walked to the dark forest. She immediately recognized the trap in the grass that she had set for Martha and walked towards it with Martha by her side. On the other hand, the bright and always curious Martha didn't have any suspicions, which was unusual. Zoe slowly led Martha into the trap and suddenly, Martha slipped and fell with a thud. Zoe smiled on the inside but pretended she was sorry on the outside. She helped Martha get up and examined the wound. It was a pretty big wound, just as she expected and took her home. Soon, Zoe was back home, screaming that Martha was hurt. Everybody looked shocked, instead of immediately rushing and helping her. They said that Martha was standing right behind them. Then, Martha appeared out of the crowd and waved at Zoe telling her that she was right there for the past thirty minutes and that it was her brother Zen, who was hurt. Zoe was terrified. She looked at the face only to see her older brother winking at her ans he whispered, "Your evil plans won't work as long as I am here". On seeing Zen wounded, everybody rushed and took him to the doctor for medical aid, while Martha and her family left home as she had to wake up early for the following day's contest. The next morning, Martha woke early and was surprised to get a phone call from Zen telling her that what he said earlier was true and that he had gone as Martha the previous night to trick Zoe. The next morning, Martha woke early and was surprised to get a phone call from Zen telling her that what he said earlier was true and that he had gone as Martha the previous night to trick Zoe. Martha thanked him with a whole heart and he said that it was a brother's duty to protect his sister from harmful people, even if it was against his own sister. Then finally, it was time for the marathon to begin. All the students from Martha's school was present to cheer her, except for Zoe, who decided to stay home after what had happened the previous night. Martha ran confidently that she would get a prize and yes! She did get a prize! The first prize!! Everyone felt so happy for her, even Zoe, after she heard that it was her sister and best friend who had won. She immediately went to the arena to apologize after realizing what a horrible mistake she had done. Martha accepted her apology and both the sisters lived happily ever after. She immediately went to the arena to apologize after realizing what a horrible mistake she had done and told Martha everything and also that she had learned her lesson from Zen, who scolded her heavily the previous night. Martha accepted her apology and said that she already knew about Zoe's plans but still trusted her. Zoe felt even more sad after hearing how much Martha trusted her. She swore to never repeat this mistake and Martha immediately hugged her. Both the sisters then lived happily ever after. Many years later, a little girl named Ruby, was reading a story book. Her mom came in and asked her what she was reading. Ruby replied, "Mom, do you know, a girl named Martha who lives in our country won the gold medal for marathon running for six times in the Olympics? I am reading a book about her. Did you know that her sister Zoe had won the silver medal every time Martha won the gold? I also wanna become like Martha and one day and then people will publish stories about me!!" This way, everyone knew about Martha, the Marathon Champion and she became a role model for everybody. They also knew about Zoe, the silver medalist in marathon running, who was Martha's best friend and a great sister till the very end of her life. THE END

title: How I celebrated my Grand Mother's Birthday
text: One day, I woke up early because it was my grand mother's birthday. My mother made cake, ice-cream and vegetable pulav in lunch for the whole family. I was sitting with my grand mother and talking to her on different topics. She also enjoyed talking with me. At around 2:00 pm we started for lunch. I also tasted pulav a bit. Whole day we spend our time in doing preparation for birthday. In the evening, my grand mother cut the cake and we enjoyed a lot after that. We are not able to eat ice-cream on the same day because it was not settled down. But we enjoyed the same on the second day from the birthday. So, it was a great fun. I love my grand mother so much.

title: Rainbow
text: “Hi Grandpa. I secured the first rank in the school. All my friends are way behind me.” “But Samyak. The Assessment sheet doesn’t say good about your behaviour.” “Grandpa, is that something to care about? Check out my marks. You will be stunned.” “How was your performance in sports?” “Lower than normal. Ravinder always does well in sports. A vagabond!” “And how is your performance in music and singing?” “Grandpa, when I sing, the whole class just runs away. Ritu, Varma uncle’s daughter, sings very well. Because of her, my school stood first in the entire state in the singing competition.” “Samyak, you are an intelligent guy. Tell me how does a rainbow get formed?” “Grandpa, fine drops of water remain present in the air after rainfall. When the sunrays go through these drops, it gets split into seven colours.” ﻿ “You are right Samyak. A rainbow never forms in dry air. Similarly, you can never appreciate others’ talents with a narrow vision! Just like air when it gets enriched with water droplets it forms a rainbow if you can enrich your vision, you begin to see special talents in not only the people around you but also in plants and animals.”. Samyak’s views had changed. He could rainbow of different colours not just in his class, but in the entire world.

title: Gopika and the four missing eggs
text: There was a cheery little girl named Gopika. She was then ten years old. She lived with her dad Karthik, mom Nandhini and her elder sister Swastika. When Corona Virus hit India, the Indian Government announced lockdown for fourteen days. That meant no one would go outside unless it is an emergency or to buy some essentials. So, she and her sister could not go to school, likewise, her dad and mom could not go to work. This gave them a lovely chance to spend plenty of time together as a family. They all were so happily playing together, cooking together and more importantly eating together. Gopika and her sister baked a delicious cake for her mom’s birthday, to surprise her. They haven’t stopped there. They continued baking frequently.The family was at bliss until one day the four eggs went missing. One morning, her mom noticed that the four eggs she kept in the fridge disappeared. She asked Swastika if she used them up for baking the cakes. Swastika said, “No Ma, I haven’t used them up.” She asked her husband if he made an omelette for himself, to which he replied, “No dear, I have not cooked them.” She asked Gopika if she had seen the eggs, Gopika responded, “No Ma, Did we have eggs at home?” At last, everyone realized that the eggs disappeared in a mysterious way. Swastika wondered, “How did this happen? Was there any unsolicited presence of somebody/something in the house last night? Were they hungry when they visited our house? Did they eat them up?” It was a bit scary to ponder over this. So Swastika stopped thinking about the missing eggs. Suddenly, Gopika’s behavior became very strange after the eggs have gone missing. Gopika stopped spending time with her mom, dad and her elder sister. She was aloof most of the times. This unexpected change puzzled her mom and her sister. In spite of them asking repeatedly if something bothered her, she refused to open up. She was never like that before. She would talk non-stop, the moment she opens her eyes in the morning and till she falls asleep in the night. In fact, she would constantly badger her mom if she could have a pet after Rakhi was made to stay out of the house, near the compound gate. Rakhi used to play a lot with her when he was small. After he was all grown up, he became unbearably mischievous, tore the curtains and messed up the entire house. So, from then on, her mom strictly told that he needs to stay out. Gopika was very upset over this. But then she understood the trouble her mom went through because of him so she kept quiet. From that day, she started asking her mom for some indoor pet, like fish or a turtle. She said that they would never bother her. But, her mom would give different reasons every time for not having one. Still, she would persuade her every day, hoping, one day her mom would give in. Now, that too stopped. She almost stopped asking anything from her mom. Her silence put the entire family in distress. One day, after her dinner, she announced that she would sleep alone in the guest room. Gopika and Swastika shared a room. Her mom and her sister exchanged confused looks because she couldn’t manage sleeping alone before. So her mom asked why suddenly that she wants to sleep alone. She said she just needed to practice staying alone. Her mom was not very comfortable with this idea. She sat her down and convinced that she ought to spend more time with her sister as she would be leaving home soon, to pursue her further studies. She couldn’t say anything now so she went along with her sister. However, she would wake up early morning and move to guest room immediately. This continued for about five days. On the sixth day, as soon as she finished dinner, she went into the guest room and lay down. Despite her mom’s coaxing, she would not budge from the guest room. Her sister also went in and tried to talk to her. After about half an hour she said okay and moved to her room, unwillingly. The next day morning, when her mom woke up and came out of her room, she saw Gopika already lying in the guest room. When she crossed the room and moved forward to go the kitchen, she noticed a hand towel lying under the dining table, on the floor, all wet and crumpled. It was very evident that someone had used the hand towel to wipe off something from the floor. This pissed her off but she did not want to yell in the morning. She had fixed a quick breakfast for the family and started to clean up the house. When she moved to clean the guest room, she saw the unfolded wet blanket lying on the floor. Gopika was still hanging in there. The room was terribly stinking. She spotted broken eggs in front of guest room toilet. She lost her temper and asked Gopika to explain how the eggs got there. Gopika said, “The eggs were broken near the dining table and so I tried to clean it.” Her mom asked, “If it was broken there, how has it reached here?” She stood silently without uttering a single word. Now her mom raised her tone and asked her to speak up. She still didn’t open her mouth. Hearing the commotion, her sister came in and saw the broken eggs and her angry mother. She smelt something fishy and asked Gopika if she took those missing eggs. It didn’t seem like Gopika would open up to her sister too. Some time has passed, Gopika stood there with an embarrassed look. Both her sister and mother stood where they stood, still looking for an answer. After some time Gopika realised that she can’t get away until she responded. She finally opened her mouth and said, “You might think, I am a fool or a stupid, but do you remember ma, how much I wanted a pet? So, I was trying to hatch these eggs by keeping them under this pillow. I thought I would hatch chicks from those eggs and that is why I wanted to sleep in the guest room. But yesterday night, someone sat on this pillow and broke them.” She very well knew it was her sister who sat on it, the previous night, while she tried to convince her to move to their bed room. But she didn’t dare blaming her sister as she knew both of them were already mad at her and she didn’t want them to flare-up still. After hearing her out, both her sister and mother laughed uncontrollably. Relieved Gopika joined them too!

title: Kolams by Susheela

title: Bholu lost his mind
text: "it was a long hard day," said Bholu after school. "Finish your homework after lunch," cried Maa from kitchen. "I don't want to go to school anymore. Can I watch some television?" "Oh ho.....! Stop it now! Quit being lazy!" "Baba will be home soon, finish your work quickly." Chitter-chatter.....Chitter-chatter....... He rambled on..... "No homework please Maa, It takes so long." "Ufffff" "You've lost your mind!" "Now get a move on.... Finish your work, before the sun is down." "WHATTT.....? I have lost my mind? Now That's a puzzle...! I must look for it...... I must hustle." "For how will I work, without my mind? Oh Kalu! Help me look. Will you be so kind?" Sniff-sniff.... Ruff-ruff..... He looked all around. Back with a huff and a puff, "It's no where to be found!" "What's the hitch?"asked Ramu, who is back from bazaar. "Oh! my mind is lost," said Bholu. "I've been looking for an hour." "Ah! Poor little you! I'll get on it right away. As soon as I find it, I shall convey." Katar-khatar.....Patar-patar.... Ramu looked here and there. Back with a huff and a puff.... "Your brain is no where!" Swish.....Swoosh...... a round the house, Bholu moved in a flurry..... He slammed into dhobi uncle..... " Oh! Why such a hurry?" "I lost my mind you see!"said Bholu. "I have got to find it soon." "I must finish my work, before I see the moon." "Oh my! Such a pity! Wonder if it's in my bag! I'll look through the clothes, don't you worry lad." Ruffle-ruffle....Shuffle-shuffle.... He looked through the bundle. Back with a huff and a puff,"It's not there," said dhobi uncle. Out came didi, amidst all the muddle. "What's all the noise?What's the trouble?" "Oh!My trouble is double," said Bholu. "I don't know what to do!" "My homework is not done, and I lost my brain too." "You lost your Brain? How could that be?" " Maa said I lost my mind." "She is always right......isn't she?" "Oh ho....... "She meant...... You've gone crazy! You silly little clown..... You can't really loose your mind. It's always around." Chukkle-chukkle....Giggle-giggle...... She laughed like a drain. Then...... With a hug and a tug...... She continued to explain.... "Your brain is in your head, nice and safe.. my dear Bholu, It can never go away, just like..... My love for you! " "Ah! So I didn't loose it after all!" Bholu began to wonder. "Now get under way," snapped didi. "Oh! What a blunder!" Bholu ran to his desk, to get to his work. Finished in a jiffy, and got up with a jerk. Honk-honk......Whomp-whomp...... Baba's car is here! With a huff and a puff.... Bholu gave a loud cheer. Baba asked with a hug, "Did you do your homework today?" "Oh yes! All of it!" said Bholu. " Good job!" "Now lets play.......... "

title: The One and Only Human Body
text: Let's take a walk through the human body. From head to toe, it is filled with organs, bones, muscles and blood. Everything in it works very hard to get us through the day. The brain is most active when we sleep! It keeps track of the sleep cycle. Awake → Light Sleep → Deep Sleep → Dreaming → Awake The smallest organ The pineal gland is shaped like a pine cone and sits in the middle of the brain. The smallest bone The stapes is quarter the size of an almond and is found inside the ear. The smallest muscle The stapedius is ten times smaller than a button. It is also found inside the ear. The biggest organ The skin makes up 16% or 1/6th of our body weight. The biggest bone The femur is located in the thigh. It can carry up to 30 times our body weight. The biggest muscle The gluteus maximus can be found in the buttocks. It stops us from falling backwards when we stand or walk. Teeth are protected by the hardest material in the body — enamel. It’s harder than bones! Every person has tongue prints and fingerprints that are one of a kind! The liver filters the blood that goes from our digestive system to the rest of our body. The liver has the power to grow back! Just a quarter of this organ is enough for it to grow back to its original size. The small intestine helps digest the food we eat. If it was stretched out, it would be 20 feet long. That is the height of an adult giraffe! KHARRRRR! KHARRRRR! That’s the sound you hear if we can’t breathe easily while sleeping. Snores are a sign that the path from your nose to your lungs is not clear. LUB DUB! LUB DUB! That’s the heart while it pumps blood. There are tiny waves of electricity created in the heart that make it beat. GRAAUP! URRP! That's the sound of the stomach sending back the extra air that was swallowed while you ate. There are some parts of our body that aren’t very important. The appendix looks like a sac and is attached to the large intestine. Although we can be healthy even if it is removed from our body, it is not entirely useless. It contains bacteria and tissues that help keep the intestine healthy. The tailbone is the lowest bone in the backbone. Since we don’t have tails, this bone doesn’t do much. The human body is wonderful and weird. In some people it goes out of its way to stand out! The longest nose ever measured was 8.8 inches long. That's nearly the length of two green chillies. The heaviest brain recorded weighed 2.3 kilograms. That’s the weight of a dozen apples. The longest human tooth extracted is recorded as 3.67 centimetres. That’s as big as a medium-sized grape. The longest moustache ever measured was 4.29 metres. That’s 20 times the length of a cucumber.
author: Niranjana Sivaram

title: The Best Soup Ever !!
text: I Love soup. But, its become so boring!! So, I have an idea.... A Stupendous one..... A tremendous one...... A gigantic one.....to make it INTERESTING I am going to make the BEST SOUP EVER But, how? I have the WORST Ingredients Let me travel the world to source the choicest stuff from across the world... Let me go to the deep woods To find the Black Wood-chuck Her egg is the sweetest one on earth, perfect for my soup But, she is the most BITTER bird-person known. Then I need to travel to England to find the rare, white-tailed tiger I will get the most delectable, peppercorn Quite a COMMON spice for my soup. I need to get some salt the purest of salt From the town buck who lives in a village. But, I must remember to wash my hands afterwards as the buck is quite DIRTY Ginger from the African boar to add some zing to my soup I will contact my friend who will wake the LETHARGIC boar and get it for me And finally, some salty gong leaves, for garnish It will add a whole lot of taste to my BLAND soup. Blend it all. VOILA! Is it INEDIBLE now? NO.. Its not.. The tastiest, yummiest, soup-erous, s soup is ready to be devoured. SLURP, SLURP THE END
author: Aniruddha  Iyer Bali

title: Chulbul's tail
text: There was a squirrel. It was very naughty and agile. Its name was Chulbul. It used to hop up and down the tree. It used to jump on feet sometimes. And sometimes, it used to run after birds. One day, it was nibbling walnut sitting on the branch of a tree. It glanced her tail. " Oh! What a rubbish tail it is! It is too light to feel at back," it gave a thought. " What should be done?", Chulbul was in deep thought. An idea struck in its mind. It should take help of Doctor Bombo bear. It went to Doctor Bombo bear in hospital. Tails, legs and ears of different animals were displayed in the cupboard at hospital. Chulbul was waiting for Doctor to come. It thought to choose one tail by then. Chulbul was inspecting different tails. After giving a serious thought, it liked the tail of a monkey. As soon as Doctor Bombo arrived, chulbul jumped over the table and took its position. " Doctor, Please fix monkey tail to me," said Chulbul with excitement. Doctor Bombo peeped from his specs and asked," What happened to your tail?" " I want to change my tail", insisted Chulbul. "Arre! Monkey tail is not suitable for you", Doctor Bombo explained. " I do not want to listen anything. Please change my tail." " It is fine. If you insist, I will change your tail", Doctor Bombo adjusted his specs over nose. Chulbul was happy. Doctor Bombo interchanged its tail with monkey tail. " Wow! It is fantastic ", Chulbul danced with joy. " I will now sit on high tree branch hanging my tail like monkey brother", Chulbul walked ahead with this thought. But, what is this? It can not walk freely. It was feeling its body too heavy to carry. Chulbul got worried a little.Hardly, it could cross the door. It was difficult to move ahead with its heavy tail. Somehow, it could manage to reach near tree by dragging the tail. " Let me take some rest on tree", it tried hard to climb. But, What is this? It could not go up even an inch. It tried many times. Every time, it fell down. At last, it was exhausted fully and hence, rested there only. " No, this is not right tail. It needs to be changed", it lifted its tail in hands. It reached once again to Doctor Bombo while stumbling. " Doctor, this tail is too heavy. Please fix something light", Chulbul said in a weary voice. " I refused to fix it already", scolded Doctor Bombo. " I am sorry, Doctor. Please fix cat tail", Chulbul suggested while agreeing its first mistake. Doctor Bombo interchanged monkey tail with cat tail. "This tail is definitely lighter than monkey tail", it moved ahead with this thought. It was deadly tired with this interchange of tails. It decided to take rest behind a tree. It was so tired that soon it fell down to fast sleep. it woke up with a loud sound. Oh God! A big dog was running towards it, assuming it to be a cat. Chulbul ran fast. The dog was following it. " Uff! This tail is a great hindrance in my fast running. My own tail was so light. How easily I could run!" Chulbul repented on its mistake. Again it visited to Doctor Bombo while stumbling now and then. " Doctor, Please save me", it went inside while screaming. The dog was standing outside. He was barking continuously. " Now what happened?" asked Doctor Bombo. "That dog is after my life. I do not need any one's tail. You please fix mine only", Chulbul said firmly. " Now you understood", Doctor Bombo smiled. He again interchanged the tails. Chulbul heaved a sigh of relief with its own tail back. It walked ahead towards its home. Now there was no worry. Its lips sang a song. " It is lovely to have own tail, Very light and unique. It can jump and run, No heaviness at all."
author: Rita Bansal

title: The Special Diwali That Went By
text: Aachooooooooooo! Sanaa sneezed. My my! I am so sacred, Patti. Just because you sneezed doesn't mean you have the virus, Sanaa. Uma patti explained. Uma paati prepared a hot cup of chai with grated ginger for Sanaa. Though the new virus has flu-like symptoms, you can defeat it if you follow simple rules. Do you know them? Well, I do know. You should wash your hands often with a good soap. When you sneeze or cough, use your elbow and not your hand. In fact, I learnt to open the door with my elbow. Patti gave Sanaa a warm smile. Yes, that's the new normal! And I stay at least two meters away from people. Two meters is my four arms length. Of course, I wear my mask when I go outside. You're a bright girl, Sanaa! Patti, how can we celebrate the festivals during this pandemic? Festivity is all about meeting family and friends, right? Sanaa wanted to know. Apparently, this year's celebrations will be different from the ones in years gone by. But we shouldn't let the pandemic take away the glitter, color, and excitement of our festivals. I am not going to tell you how to do that. Instead, you'll. Patti explained. Sanaa thought for a real long time. And then she knew what exactly she had to do! She ran to Amma and tugged her saree. Amma, I came up with a plan to celebrate Diwali. Will you help me? I need Manaas' help too. Absolutely, dear. Let's make a small gift hamper of sweets, diyas, some nice but rarely-used clothes, books, and toys and donate them to needy people. Sounds like a plan, Amma said. Sanaa called up her besties - Ryan, Krishna, Amandeep, and Armeen to tell them about their plan. All of em were super excited. Armeen said, Let's call it the "Basket of Light and Hope" - just what your name means in Arabic, Sanaa. Sanaa ransacked her huge bundle of clothes and picked up her outfits that were in excellent condition. This new red pullover doesn't fit me any longer. I can give this one away. I will give away three of these nice cosy kashmiri shawls. After all, I don't need all of them. Then, Sanaa collected her story books that she no longer needed. What's Diwali without sweets? The festival that's inextricably linked with mouth-watering sweets and s avouries. Amma was making juicy, deep-fried jalebi, the most comforting gajar ka halwa, and the absolutely delicious fudgy little blocks of Mysore pak. And of course, the yummy fritters in all shapes and sizes. The whiff of pure paradise! Amma has prepared so many sweets and fritters that we will have to round up a crew to eat them. Sanaa announced gleefully. Well, I will do my bit to help you to finish them. Armeen laughed. Sure, after we finish packing them. With Maanas' help, both the girls carefully packed the sweets in nice, tight gift boxes. Sanaa and Manaas collected the goodies from all their friends that included sweets, nice winter clothes, books, color pencils, diyas, and crackers. They packed the goodies in boxes and dropped them at Shalini aunty's place. Shalini aunty runs a NGO and would drop them off to the needy children. Now, it was Manaas' turn to decorate the house with freshly picked mango leaves, simply called thoranam. "Krishna, can you please help us to make a nice arrangement of flowers?", Saana asked. "But we typically do a pookolam only for onam and not for diwali." Krishna was surprised. Why not? Pookolam is flower rangoli; the idea is to deck up the entrance with some nice kolam. OK pookolam it's. Krishna agreed. Ryan, Krishna, Amandeep, Armeen, Manaas, and Sanaa decorated the house with flowers, diyas, and lamps. The entire neighborhood reverberated in a festive note. What a wonderful Diwali it was, Patti. Thanks for the idea. But it was your idea, Sanaa. On my part, I decided to sponsor a child's education. It doesn't take much - just Rupees 500 per month, but that's some child's dream to study. I too will do it for the next Diwali, Patti. I do have a good amount of pocket money. Why just this Diwali, shouldn't every Diwali be about giving and sharing, Patti? Of course! The true spirit of every festival and not just Diwali lies in sharing, caring, and about spreading happiness. In fact, that's the entire purpose of life. Oh, I love you, Patti. Sanaa enveloped her Patti in a huge bear hug!
author: Lakshmi Venkat

title: Why do frogs stay in the rain?
text: They had a happy life. All had lovely names. But to tell all their names will take such a long long time. So, let's get to know our darling froggies. Want to know their names? It's funny... Jhimikkan... Dumukkan Both are good swimmers... and call out loudly nothing else but... pokroommm... pokroommm... Singing is what they loved to do. Ha ha... what fun; Sing pokrommm pokrommm Ha ha... what fun; Hop hop all over And one day... before the rainy season, there came a guest who looked more or less like our froggies. Four legs, a head, a totally green thing.... it swam just like them, took rest on the banks,... Huh! After all, what was there to talk to the newcomer?!! And then Jhimikkan saw that... the guest put out the head... pulled it back... Wow! Awesome! Jhimikkan and Dumukkan longed to go and say hello. If possible... they can even ask... What? Heh, heh... that thing about the head... Thus they went near the tortoise. Mind you, it was a good tortoise.. The froggies began, "Greetings!" "I'm Jhimikkan..." "I'm Dumukkan..." "Are you okay?" "We came to say 'hello'" "Did you like our pond?..." The tortoise said, "I'm tortoise... came from the banks of Kingini river just to see the forest. I like everything here. What fun!" "Brother... er..." Jhimikkan interrupted. "Please don't feel bad... let's hear..." Tortoise: "Feel free." Jhimikkan: "Errr... heh... how do you pull back your head in? Could you please tell us?" The tortoise was amused. He asked... "Why do you want to know?" Dumukkan said, " Brother, then we also can see..." "What?" "About what is happening inside the tummy... that is, when we pull the head in..." The tortoise couldn't help laughing. Fools! "Oh... so you also want to pull back your heads, don't you? Here, listen... when it rains... heavier the rain, the better... just hop on to that rock and look up to the sky and pray loudly." "O God! Give us the boon to put out and pull back our heads." Both the froggies agreed in unison. " For sure we shall pray." It was since that day that frogs began to croak loudly in the rain.
author: Sneha Susan Shibu
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Kishor Joshi; Partho Sengupta; Proiti  Roy; Sangeetha Kadur; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Trần Lưu  Đăng Nguyên; Vongsavanh Damlongsouk

title: What Was That?
text: Tape had just started working in this jungle camp. One day, Hiren realised they needed to go buy some more food. “I have some work to finish. I will not be able to go,” said Rakesh. “I also have to finish work. I will also not be able to go,” said Tape. Poor Hiren would have to go alone. “I better leave now, so that I can return before dark,” he said. So off went Hiren and bought lots and lots of food. It was getting dark as the young man made his way back to the camp. So he started walking fast. Sarak, sarak, sarak, sarak. What was that? Scared, Hiren stopped in his tracks. He peered into the dark and saw… … a Barking Deer running away. Sarak, sarak, sarak, sarak. Sarak, sarak Sarak, sarak Laughing, Hiren started walking again. Khatak-khatak. Khatak-khatak. What was that? Scared, Hiren started running. He turned around and saw… … a Capped Langur jumping from one tree to the other. Khatak-khatak. Khatak-khatak. Khatak-khatak. Khatak-khatak. Shaking his head, Hiren started walking again. Suc-suc-suc. Suc-suc-suc. What was that? Scared, Hiren hid behind a tree. He looked out and saw… … a Marbled Cat crossing the path. Suc-suc-suc. Suc-suc-suc. Suc-suc-suc Suc-suc-suc A little ahead, Hiren heard something. Sring, sring, sring, sring. What was that? Hiren trembled with fear. He looked around and saw… … a Porcupine moving in the bushes. Sring, sring, sring, sring. Sring, sring Sring, sring Relieved, Hiren walked on until he was near the camp. Chhalak-chhalak. Chhalak-chhalak. What was that? Frightened, Hiren wondered if it was an elephant coming his way. He ran to his camp and saw… his friends stomping and pretending to be elephants! Chhalak-chhalak. Chhalak-chhalak. Chhalak-chhalak Chhalak-chhalak
author: Rajesh Khar

title: Travel Diaries
text: I eat Puchka? Daddy, cannot you find a job in Kolkata itself? " Nina asked her father. "Don't worry, Nina. You will make new friends. You will also find new places to eat Puchka" consoled her father. But, Nina could not be convinced. Her mother and father tried a lot to cheer her up. They offered her a variety of food items in order to cheer her up. But,Nina was very adamant. 'I don't want to eat anything! ' huffed Nina. Nina's parents had lost all of the ways to console her. Suddenly, Nina's father smiled. "I can see something there...." he began. "Oh yay! I love this game!" said her mother. "I can see something in brown colour" her father told them. "Are they slippers? Or are they mountains? Oh oh, they must be suitcases!" exclaimed her mother. " You are right- they are suitcases" her father confirmed and clapped his hands. Nina's attention shifted from her book to the game. " It's my turn now. I can see something in yellow" her mother told them. "You mean, mustard fields? " her father guessed. "It's my hairband!" said Nina. "That's right!" said her mother and clapped hands. Nina started laughing and participated in the game. "I can see something in blue" started Nina. "The skies!" her mother told them. "I can see something in brown there.." her mother told them. "The mountains!" guessed her father. "I can see something in white colour.." said her father. "That's a cow!" exclaimed Nina. "There is something in green color..." started Nina and pat came the reply from her parents that it was grass she was referring to. Her mother spotted something in black and Nina identified it as a crow. Her father spotted something tall in brown color. It also had spots. "Are you referring to a leopard?" asked her mother. "No! It is a giraffe!" Nina looked outside through the window and said 'Indian forest don't have giraffes. You are pulling our legs!" Everyone started laughing. Her parents spread a blanket on the seat. They also got the pillow ready for Nina. "Shall we play this game after going to Delhi?" asked Nina. "Ofcourse! The game will be much more fun in a new place!" her father told her.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Health and Hygiene
text: There was a village. The village was very dirty. People were sick. No one thought about hygiene. One day some officers came there and they held a meeting to solve the problem. They announced that dustbins would be kept at corners for people to throw waste and people wil not throw waste in open. All obeyed to the officers but some refused to do that. Next day the dustbins were kept there. But at the evening officers found that there was garbage all around the dustbins. They made a plan to find people who are not obeying. They placed CCTV cameras near dustbins such that no one can see them and next morning they saw a man throwing garbage outside the dustbin. They held a meeting again and said that some people are not obeying to them. They said that the man who is responsible for this is identified. They will announce his name publicly tommorrow if he does not pay fine today. The meeting was over. A man came and sat on officers legs and he started crying. He apologised for his mitakes and he promised that he will not do it again. Later the village became clean and tidy.
author: Satej Kolhe
illustrator: Greystroke; Kishor Joshi; Neeta Gangopadhya; Rajiv Eipe; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Mia is looking for her cat
text: She looked for him in all his favourite places: by the window......under the table......on the bookshelf, next to the red book......on the blue sofa......and also in the draw that she always left open especially for Kosh. But he was nowhere to be found! Mia thought that Kosh had escaped through the window and that probably he would never come back. When it was time to sleep, she went to bed still very sad, but... surprise! Kosh was waiting for her there! He had simply fallen asleep under Mia's bed.

title: Where Did My Call Go?
text: When we speak into the phone, our voice enters it in the form of sound waves. The sound waves rush into the microphone and are changed into electrical signals. Microphone The phone’s antenna changes the electrical signals into electromagnetic waves. These waves are picked up by the closest cell tower... and then sent to a large cell tower. The large cell tower passes on these waves as signals through wires, where they travel... along mountains... over roads... and even undersea... until finally, the signal reaches the large tower closest to the person being called. The large tower then converts the signal into electromagnetic waves... and sends it to the cell tower closest to the phone you are calling. The phone’s antenna receives the electromagnetic waves. And the phone changes the waves into electrical signals. Finally, the electrical signals are converted back into sound waves using the speaker. Speaker And that’s how sound is heard on the other side. Sound waves Electrical signals Electromagnetic waves Small cell tower Large cell tower Underground wires Large cell tower Small cell tower Electromagnetic waves Electrical signals Sound waves How a Call Travels
author: Samidha Gunjal

title: Malini's Experience with Bad Touch.
text: Malini's birthday just passed by. She was a very happy 13 year old. Unlike many of her classmates, she loved the whole journey of growing up, meeting new people, solving problems on her own. Her mother always encouraged her to not be afraid of changes. Her mother was a very busy person. She managed household, went out to work and also did a lot of volunteer activities. Malini always considered her as one of the inspirations, right from her childhood. Malini's childhood was a very happy one. She was always exposed to a lot of baby-sitters. Malini loved that experience! Every baby-sitter used to treat her with so much of love and she always remembered to be thankful for the same. One of her favourite baby-sitters is Taklu Uncle and his family. They used to take care of her like a princess!Taklu uncle always used to give Malini toffees! He knew Malini loved them. Anyways, coming back to her teenage years, Malini also noticed that with each birthday,her body changes. She was so puzzled and sometimes disgusted. Why do bodies have to change? Is it not enough that her teachers, her grades,her friends and her eating habits were changing?Now her body is also changing? Malini was so curious about hair in her armpit. The next day, Taklu Uncle came with a jar of toffees! Imagine,a whole jar of toffees! She was so thrilled. Uncle said,'You are growing up so fast and I am unable to believe it" Come here and take these toffees. Hey! you have changed a lot." Saying this, he took her hand and he slowly moved his hands to those two small bulging dots that were appearing on Malini's chest. Malini was feeling a little weird. Well, Taklu uncle always touched her hand and hugged her since childhood. but it wasn't uncomfortable. This touch right then was making her feel very queasy. Will uncle stop giving her toffees if she tells this to someone? He is anyways the favourite uncle of everyone!He makes everyone laugh, does Yoga and keeps everyone happy. Who will believe her? That night, she kept looking at the jar of toffees. She sat her parents down and told the entire story. Her mother said " It was very brave of you to open up like this! Good girl. You must not encourage any kind of touch that makes you feel uncomfortable. Please come and tell us always in case you someone misbehaves with you. And if someone does touch you like that again, scream. We are always there for you and we love you". She was glad that she told her parents this incident. She was very proud of herself. She threw the toffees outside the window. She told herself that it is okay if Taklu uncle didn't give her toffees. But it is never okay for anyone to make her experience an uncomfortable touch. She can allow people to hug and touch her only if she consents to it. Malini felt so relieved.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Tup-tup-tupak
text: There was a forest. A very dense. One day it rained heavy. Next day, it was sunny. All animals were out. There was a sound, suddenly. Tup-tup-tupak! All were frightened. The lion thought. The cheetah thought. The elephant thought. The bear thought. What is this sound? The bear was afraid. He hid himself in bushes. The deer trembled. He ran away. The cheetah too ran away. The lion said," I am not afraid." But soon he too disappeared.All big animals left the space. The ant said to its friends," Let us find out Tup-tup-tupak. Let us see who is it? We are all together. There is nothing to worry." The rat said," Bravo! ant bro." The firefly said," I will lead." The cat said," I support you." The rabbit said," I will also not be left behind." All went in search of Tup-tup-tupak. Suddenly they found, the rain water was dripping from the leaves tup-tup-tupak. The same sound was all around. The ant said with proud," See! This is it." All nodded in unison and smiled away.
author: Rita Bansal

title: Sabrang
text: One old lady put a seed in the soil She wanted to grow carrot A seedling came out Slowly it grew into a plant. She added a little mannure Carrot grew more and more She thought to pluck it And prepare hot halwa. She hold it on the top But nothing came out Really nothing came out Call one person more. Only then her grandson came He also pulled it along Nothing has come, nothing came out Call one person more. Only then her dog came there All pulled it with full force Nothing has come, nothing came out Call one person more. Then came old lady cat Overhearing hue and cry All pulled it with force The carrot came out at last. Lo! It is strange We did it. Chandoo Chandoo has a little brain Always busy in reading Always showed high brain Like a learned man. One day busy in reading had high dreams To do something big To earn great name. If any house is on fire I will reach running at once I will jump inside the fire I will fight for others till end. I will sacrifice for others I will earn good name The one who takes other's pain Is real hero and saint. Munni came while running "Come soon", Chandoo bhai Brother has burnt his hand Making a great hue and cry. Mother has gone out for work I have a lot to do. How can I do all the tasks Please bring some medicine. Chandoo got startled And angry over Munni Why came here running Why not applied alum or haldi? Do not bother me for silly things Do not you ever come. There is always a nuisance of home Should I leave my books aside? Getting upset with Chandoo anger Munni ran back to brother. She pampered her brother And spent the whole day. Mother came in the evening She listened Chandoo's doing. She went to Chandoo's room Fretful on his inhuman deed. Your younger brother was in pain Why can't you bring balm? You say yourself a scholar But you are a stone and proud. You are useless for home What for your studies to me? Uff! What the hell! You may be lion in street, but a fox at home. Old man crushed under Motorcar O grandmother! My grandmother! "What happened?", she said. It is bad, very bad. "Oh God! What is there?" That our beloved old man Crushed today under motorcar How badly injured he is! He is in pain, a lot of pain. He is lying and crying there Bathed himself in tears No body is there to his rescue The motorcar driver too fled away. Grandmother was terrified prayed God for his life Let us see the old man who is crushed under car. Both came out on the road Stepped fast toward the spot Grandmother turned around The old man was nowhere. Old man was lying flat on ground The toy motor was on his belly "Oh,my God!",said grandmother And Old grandmother too laughed. I am a little girl I am a little girl I am not afraid of anyone I do what I love to do I do not agree with anyone. I have my innocent face My eyes are dark and black I keep hopping here and there Like a playful butterfly. Beetles make sound at night "Fairies come," mother says They lullaby at night To sleep all good child. I say innocently Please call them inside. Mother clap me lovingly Asks me to sleep. I came out of home During my dreams I wanted to know the secret Of fairies who sleep us. There were stars far in sky They were smiling at me They were twinkling Lovingly they were calling me. All of sudden, a pair of feathers Were attached to my shoulders They were helping me to fly high They took me a far. I was flying high in milky way I saw a group of fairies The queen fairy came to escort me I, at once, went with her. All the fairies were together They all hugged me tight It was morning! Wake up my child! My mother has come to me.
author: Rita Bansal

title: The magical story book
text: Maya was planning to go to her grandma's house.She was packing her clothes,money,water and food.So the next day she started in a taxi to the railway station.She got into her train.She slept for some time.She woke up and ate.Then after a few hours,she got off the train. When she got off, she booked a taxi to go to her grandma's house. When she arrived, she stepped into her grandma's house. Her grandma said "hi dear, how are you?".Maya said "I am fine". Her grandma said "Come in,I will make some tea, till then you can explore the house Maya said "okay". Maya went up stairs to her room to put all her stuff in the room. Then she went down to get the tea. Her grandma came with the tea and she placed it on the table. Maya sat down on the table her grandma said "I have some thing for you, I will be right back".Her grandma came back with a book Maya asked "what's so special about it?". Her grandma said "once you finish reading it, you go inside it".Maya asked is that even possible?. Her grandma said yes it is, this book was passed through generation and now I am giving it to you. Maya looked so surprised. She took the book and went to her room to put it back.She came back and said "I have seen crazier things so I am not that surprised". Her grandma said "good because for a minute I thought you didn't believe me". To be continued... make sure you read part 2:)
author: Aadhya Sivakrishna

title: All about dogs!
text: Who does not like dogs? Dogs are wonderful pets and are also were cute. You can share your feelings with dogs, play with them when you are bored, teach tricks and many more! Are you planing to get a dog, are you having trouble choosing which dog you want? This story tells you about 5 amazing dogs! I am sure that you will find the right dog for you after you finish the book. What are you waiting for? Flip the page to get to know more about dogs! This is a Golden Retriever. It is also called Yellow Retriever or Goldie. They are amazing swimmers! They also have lots of fur which is good for cuddling. If you are cold, take a glass of hot coco and cuddle up with a Golden Retriever. They are also good at tricks! This is a German Shepard! German Shepherds have a nickname called K-9 cop. They are usually found in Germany and that is how they got their name. They are also very good at police service. They are very obedient. They also have sharp pointy ears. This is a Pug! You can find them in China. They are super cute because of their flat face. They also have lots of wrinkles, bug eyes and a very curly tail! This is a poodle! Poodles make a great pet. They are very intelligent. They are also very energetic. They have lots of energy! Sometimes, they can get a little stubborn but most of the time they are very obedient and are very good with children. If you are a child, I highly recommend you to get a poodle instead of other dogs. Aren't the cute and adorable? They also help you in different ways. That is why they are called the man's best friend.
author: Niyati Makkithaya

title: Tina's talk regarding Ghee.
text: This is filled with such good aroma!" asked Tina. " It is made from the smooth and white colored butter" Ma told Nina. "What is butter made from?" " It is made from churning the sweet and sour curd" " What is curd made from? " It is made from cream. Cream is the top layer of milk that is found when milk is boiled". "Where do we get milk from?" " We get it from Kapila, our cow." " Why should Kapila give us milk? " " Because we take care of her and also feed her grass." "And so?" "And so she gives us milk! And The kitchen is like a science class. We learn a lot regarding physics, chemistry while cooking. We can make many delicious items from milk in the kitchen. How would you like to take your milk?
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Nature
text: The colors of the rainbow are red orange yellow green blue and purple. A rainbow is a multi colored arc that forms in the sky. Trees are very important to earth because it gives oxygen to people. If we did not have trees we would not be able to breathe. Flowers did not always exist they first appeared 140 million years ago. Broccolis are actually a flower. Some plants like orchids do not need soil to grow they get all of their nutrients from the air. Rain occurs on other planets in our Solar System but it is different to the rain we experience here on Earth. Rain falls in the form of water droplets, this is called precipitation. Rain can also fall in the form of snow or hail. Snow is light and fluffy but dangerous snowstorms come often in places that are cold like for example, Alaska. Snowstorms can come on snowy mountains. Birds come in many colors. They also come in many breeds, like the sparrow, robin, red jay (shown in picture above), blue jay and lots more. Birds are all beautiful in different ways. Mountains have lots of snow sometimes and mountains supply fresh water to half of the world's population. Mountains can be very rough and hard to climb.
author: Maya menon

title: When the Monkeys stole the Hats
text: He sold caps! One day, Mama walked for a long time. A very very long time. And so, he felt sleepy. Out of sleepiness, he went and sat under a tree. He fell asleep after sitting under the tree. What do you think would have happened after he fell asleep? There were a few monkeys who were on the top of the tree. What do you think the monkeys were upto? The monkeys climbed down the tree. What would have happened after the monkeys climbed down the tree? The Monkeys opened the bag filled with caps. They were so excited on seeing so many colourful hats! After that, the monkeys started wearing the caps! The monkeys were filled with happiness. And so, they started playing with each other. Suddenly, Mama woke up and so, all of the monkeys climbed up the tree! The monkeys looked at ﻿Mama. Mama peered into the bag. To his shock, he could not find any cap in the bag! Where would the caps have gone missing? Mama looked up. He saw the monkeys on the branches. The monkeys were wearing his caps! " How can I get my caps from the monkeys?" thought Mama. Ahh! An idea struck Mama. He threw his caps at the monkeys. The monkeys got very angry! They threw their caps at Mama. ﻿ Mama ﻿ was overjoyed and he took all of the caps back! How is the story? Who is smarter between the two? Is ﻿Mama ﻿ smarter or are the monkeys smarter?
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: The difference between us!
text: Having just moved from Michigan to Seattle, Abby was having trouble fitting in at her new school. Most of the girls in her class used to judge her because of the way she looked and her skin colour. Abby used to sit alone during break and lunch, while people would whisper about her. She did not fit in at all, and would go home crying most of the days. One day on their way back from school, a girl named Harper sat down next to her. Abby was surprised and happy at the same time. However, Harper did not talk to Abby much and ignored her. When they got off the bus to go to home, they both saw a small white puppy, who seemed to be lost, walking in their avenue. They ran towards him and started to make sure that he was okay. Slowly Harper and Abby started to talk to each other while taking care of the tiny puppy. They realised that they had more in common than they had thought. They became fast friends and when they went to school Harper explained to everyone that Abby was the same as the rest of them and also unique in her own way, which was a good thing. A ll of a sudden everyone understood and apologized to Abby about their behaviour and treated her the way that they treated everyone else. Abby now fitted in and everyone treated her fairly even if, she looked different. Maybe the difference between all of us is smaller than we think!
author: Nitya Kashyap

title: BROTHER AND SISTER
text: Once upon a time, there was a sister who lived with her brother. The sister's name was Sheetal. The brother's name was Amit. It was a hot day. Sheetal and Amit wanted to play in the lake. Sheetal requested her parents that can we play in the lake? Her parents told her that yes you can go. Sheetal & Amit played in the lake for some time. Then it was getting dark. They decided to go to there home. The sister wished that if it did not get dark we could play forever. They were very sad & went back home. The parents thought that we should make their favourite dish at dinner. They became really elated. Then they had their dinner. Then they went to sleep. The next day they got ready, had their breakfast, and went to their room to study. The parents got very happy. Their father went out to buy vegetables to eat. Their father came back. Their mother cooked delicious food for them. They had a delicious meal after studying. Then after eating their lunch they went out to play in the park near their home. After they reached the park they met their friend Raju who had also come to the park to play. Sheetal, Amit & Raju had a great time playing in the park. Amit, Sheetal's brother got hurt on his leg on their way home. But Amit managed to come back home. Their father asked Sheetal what had happened on the way home. Sheetal told how Amit had got hurt on his leg. Their mother them that Amit will get fine & healthy. After a few days, Amit was healthy again. He started walking, running, & jumping. Thank You
author: Pranesh  Trivedi

title: Gapuram a great helper
text: Gapuram was a very grateful elephant, as all the villagers built a house to keep him safe. One day the villagers became very poor and they did not have money. They started starving without food. The milkman did not have milk, the tailor closed the shop as he did not have money to buy the needle. The postman passed the message all across the village, that the people are dying out of hunger. Gapuram. heard about the news and felt very sad. He then decided that he must help villagers. He thought about ideas all night. The next day, he became magical elephant. He realised that he can deliver food just like food delivery boys. He walked miles away from the village and looked for a restaurant where he could bring food for the villagers. He took rest under a huge tree in the afternoon as he was tired. He woke up in the evening and made a loud sound by yawning. He started walking ahead and saw a beautiful lit place. He said " Voila, here is the restaurant. " He felt happy and started walking towards it. He requested the manager. to give food to the villagers who were very poor. The restaurant people felt very empathetic, they did a charity for poor people.
author: ARNAV SETHNA

title: A Hairy Problem
text: Shireen had brought jangri in her lunch dabba. “It looks like you’re eating Manasa’s hair!” said Shwetha. “Jangri-head!” Ravi said. They all laughed. Manasa used a ruler to check her hair: curly. She checked Shireen’s hair: straight. Shwetha’s hair: mostly straight. Ravi: straight again. “Not fair!” Manasa said. In the playground, Ravi bowled a ball to Manasa and said, “Eyyy, Jangri-head!” “STOP IT!” Manasa threw her bat down and ran away. After school, Amma took Manasa to the sweetshop. “We only have jangri,” the shop lady said. “See! It looks just like your curly hair!” “I won’t eat it!” Manasa stomped her foot. Titus was waiting to greet them when they got home. “Hi, Manasa!” Manasa checked Titus’s hair. “Straight! It’s not fair!” Manasa yelled. “Everyone has straight hair except me!” “Your Amma has curls,” Titus said. “You get your curls from me,” Amma told Manasa. “I don’t like curls!” Manasa yelled. “They look like jangri!” “Mmmm jangri,” Titus said. “Slurp!” Manasa started searching Amma’s cupboard. “Aha!” Manasa said. She had found Amma’s big sewing scissors. “I don’t want your curls, Amma,” Manasa said. “Cut them off!” “No, Manasa!” Amma said. She put the scissors on a high shelf. “I hate my hair! It looks like jangri!” Manasa burst into tears. “Jangri is yummy,” Amma said. “And your curls are beautiful.” “Why do I have curls, Amma?” Manasa wanted to know. “Titus doesn’t.” “Titus’s parents both have straight hair, so he got it from them. I get curls from my Amma and Appa,” Amma said. “Everyone gets some things from their parents. That’s why we all look different.” Manasa sulked. “I didn’t ask for your curls!” “We don’t get to choose,” Amma said. “Some parts of you look like me and some like your Appa.” She showed Manasa a photo. Manasa’s Appa had straight hair and a huge smile. Amma pointed and said, “See? You have his smile.” “Shiny teeth,” Titus said. “Is it my hair?” Manasa asked. “Or is it yours?” “It’s your hair,” Amma replied. “But it looks like mine. And your smile looks like your Appa’s.” “You look okay,” Manasa decided. “I’ll keep you both!”
author: Shalini  Srinivasan

title: Ma! Come on!
text: I woke up in the morning. I rubbed my eyes. I didn't see my mother around. "Ma, Ma! Come quickly!" Ma peeked from the corner. " Yes, dear! Get up! Freshen up!" I bathed quickly. I wore my shirt. I had to go early. "Ma, listen to me!" "Yes, yes! I'm coming," Ma said. "I have to boil the milk now. I'll come after that." I combed my hair. I buttoned up my shirt. I was ready. "Ma, make it quick!" ﻿ Ma was busy giving sister her clothes. She had to help sister. Ma had lots of work in the morning. But I was in a hurry! "Ma, I'll be late!" I grabbed my bottle and schoolbag. I put my shoes on. "Come on! Ma, make it quick!" "Yes, yes, I'm coming! Let me complete braiding sister's hair. I just need five minutes. Then we shall go." " I want to go now. I won't wait for you! I feel like crying. Sister went to school already. And I'm still here." " Just a minute, I'm almost done! I just have to fill water in the pot." Ma always does some work or the other. "Ma, make it quick. Now I can't wait!" "Come on now, come on!" I held Ma's hand and pulled her out. "Oh, dear! Let me switch off the lights, atleast!" Now we were out of the house. Ma was locking the doors. "Come on, my king, let's go!" Now I'm very happy. Ma is by my side. She called me her king. And I'm going to school!
author: Shriya Badanhatti

title: Little Seema
text: She went home through a forest. She saw a squirrel on the way. It ran. She also saw a monkey. The monkey jumped with happiness. Seema was happy as well! Seema reached her house finally. Her mother gave her a puppy as a gift. The puppy licked her. Now, Seema has a good friend to play with. So, she is a happy girl!
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Am I Good Enough?
text: Meera has so many friends but I have only one friend. Am I good enough? Meera knows all the answers in class. All the teachers ask her to solve problems on the blackboard. They never ask me. Am I good enough? Meera plays football so well. Everyone loves playing with her. I fall down and get hurt every time I play. Am I good enough? I tell my best friend Aria about how I feel. She didn't know I felt this way. Aria asks me to think about all the things that I love doing. I love painting and I am really good at it. Colours make me happy! I love music and I sing every day. I eve n won a singing competition in school. I am good at playing on the monkey bars, and never fall off. But what I love the most is my best friend Aria, who is always there for me when I need her!
author: Ariyana Mehta

title: THE EVIL CAKE
text: One day it was mia's birth day.she went to a cake shop and found a nice cake she picked it up and she went home but when she got home all the frosting got smudged in the box from all the bumps from the ride home on her cycle.she found a cake recipe in a book called:be careful cook's.mia thought it meant to be careful of the yummy taste but it really meant the recipe could be magic. After she frosted the cake she decorated it with candy and sprinkles she thought of having a bite but she then said to herself no i must wait for the party.after she finished decorating her cake she started to make a picture of what she wanted to look like if she had super powers.after all she was very good at drawing. Just when she was about to start she had to select her party food.after some time she drew. Mmmmm yummy after 3 hours her picture was complete she liked it she stuck it on her bed and started decorating for the party and asked her friends to help and her mom told her the cake she made was nice but it was too big and with the leftover frosting can be used to decorate another cake so she found a recipe in that same book and she started to make it by the time she finished baking and decorating everything was done her birthday began there was- singing dancing and most importantly cake!!!!!! She said it was the best day of her life but there was a twist as beautiful as the frosting was it made every one evil but only the person who made it wold not luckily there was a cure so she raced to make the cure cake wile her mom held off the evil people luckily she could make it and they were back to normal. author: LILA
