title: Sizing Things Up
text: The world is full of creatures and things. Some are big. Some are small. Most are somewhere in the middle. These are some of the biggest things we know. These are some of the smallest things we know. Some things look big because they’re surrounded by smaller things. The same things may look small when they’re surrounded by bigger things. What looks big from close by, may look small from far away. Things make bigger things. Bigger things make huge ones. Huge things make ginormous ones. Ginormous things make super-duper-mega-jumbo ones. Things are made of small things. Small things are made of smaller ones. Smaller things are made of tiny ones, which are made of eeny-teeny-weeny things. But even the eeny-teeny-weeny can make a super-duper-mega-jumbo difference in this big-small world.
author: Aparna  Kapur

title: What happened to Juno?
text: She named it Juno. Vidhya was so thrilled. Juno meant the world to her. During school-time, Juno would wait for Vidhya in the porche. Once Vidhya returns from school, it would scamper around her with happiness. Once, Vidhya spotted something in Juno's mouth. She noticed that it was a plastic bag. She pulled the bag from it's mouth swiftly. She narrated the entire story to her mother. "How did Juno get the bag?" wondered her mother. "I don't know. But, please don't use plastic bag henceforth" said Vidhya. "Okay. I have a few plastic bags for emergencies. I will throw them out tomorrow." said her mother. Vidhya went to temple with her mother the next day. Juno did not run towards her to greet her. Instead, it was lying in the corner. She called Juno. Juno didn't wake up. Her parents told her that the pet maybe sleeping. Vidhya tried to put Juno in her lap. It tried very hard to let out a bark. Vidhya started crying. Just then, Amma (Vidhya's mother) noticed the dustbin having fallen down. The dustbin consisted of all of the plastic bags that Vidhya advised to be thrown away. The plastic bags in the dustbin were torn. Amma knew what had happened. She rushed Juno to the hospital. The doctor did a surgery and removed the plastic bag from Juno's mouth. Juno needed a few weeks to recover. Vidhya took care of it so well. Vidhya told her parents " We have saved Juno. But what will happen to the number of animals on the road? The road is filled with plastic bags. She was so worried. Her father comforted her. He said " We will use cloth-bags. We will also see that all the plastic bags are thrown into the dustbin. Please pass this advice onto your friends". Vidhya assured that she will definitely tell her friends.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar
illustrator: Narendra Dengle; Rijuta Ghate; Santosh Pujari; Suvidha Mistry

title: The Birthday gift
text: Today was She Sparrow's Birthday.The He sparrow forgot about it. So the She sparrow was not talking with him and neither did she eat..... "What gift can I get for her?", he thought for a very long time. "There has to be something special that she would really like, he agreed,something that would make her feel great indeed". He tried to remember the gifts he had given to her before... The tasty treat that I gifted her last time took a back seat. Her stomach got upset when she ate it. The year before that was no different...... Yukky bug... U taste horrible "The fruit that I had given her before was not at all sweet. She threw it way in complete discreet". The day had gone by and the night swept in, but the Sparrow was not allowed to get into his love seat. He had to stay out of the nest,gazing at the sky without any rest. The night felt sorry for him and gave him a tight hug before the dawn begin. The coat of the He Sparrow had gone black.When the She Sparrow gazed into it, She taught that the sparrow had fought with the mighty night, to get her a Kajal for her lovely eye sight..........She was happy with the gift and so was the Male Sparrow who kept the black color around his neck as a loving treat. Mighty Night,the Sparrow said....... All so Black,all so bright. That's how we know that the She Sparrow has a lovely eye sight,with a hint of Kajal and the He sparrow with a coat of black color around his neck sparkling the night light.....
author: Gunjan Gangey
illustrator: Deepa Akilan; Madhuri Purandare; Samidha Gunjal; Vidyut Jauhari

title: THE AUTOMATIC CYCLE
text: Once upon a time, their lived a girl. Her name was Khanak she lived with her younger brother named Shyam. They both wanted a cycle because they did not have a cycle. But their parents said that once you grow you can buy a cycle. Khanak & Shyam said that we are tall enough to ride a cycle. Khanak & Shyam requested their parents to buy a cycle. Their father told them that we will buy a cycle tomorrow. Khanak & Shyam got really elated after their father said yes to them. The next day Khanak & Shyam went to the market with their father. Khanak & Shyam bought best & the strongest cycle from the shop. After they returned to their home they had their lunch & went to ride the cycle their father had bought. After Khanak & Shyam sat on the cycle it started moving on its own. They were scared but a little happy also. Khanak & Shyam were not scared at all after they rode it for some time. They rode their cycle near their house. They took turns to ride. One sat back while the rode the cycle. When Khanak & Shyam reached back to their home. They told their parents about the Automatic cycle. Their mother had made yummy dinner for them to eat. Khanak & Shyam had the delicious dinner & went to sleep. The next day Khanak & Shyam went to the school with their Automatic cycle. Khanak & Shyam told their friends about the Automatic cycle in the school. Khanak & Shyam's friends were jealous. At night when Khanak & Shyam were sleeping their friend Raju, quitely took Khanak & Shyam' s cycle to his home. The other day when Khanak & Shyam got ready for school. Khanak & Shyam went out to go to school. Khanak & Shyam could not find their cycle. Khanak & Shyam were getting late for school so their father suggested them to go with him in the car. Khanak & Shyam agreed with their father & went to school by car. As Khanak & Shyam reached their school they saw their friend Raju, their friend with the Automatic cycle. Khanak & Shyam aked Raju that why he had taken their Automatic cycle. Raju told that he was jealous & wanted the Automatic cycle. Khanak & Shyam said that we forgive you this time but don't do it again. T hank Yo u

title: The Rainbow and the prayer
text: A poor farmer had two daughters. They were raised by him as their mother had passed away in one such gloomy day. The girls were obedient & best, sweet and full of zest. After they grew up, the farmer married one in the east and other in the west. He was happy as he could finally rest. On the wedding day, the villagers said, "Ohhhh!!!...the two poor inseparable sisters would be separated, one settling in the east and other in the west". The women of the village making faces and frown, gave farewell to the two sisters for the destined town. The two settled well, one near the mighty rivers of the east and other near the dry forests of the west. The farmer thought, finally he could rest. But the other day his phone rang, his daughter had called, who was married in the east. She complained about the heavy rain, which flooded her field. The crops were rotting, the sun was not ready to rise, said she with the teary eyes. The daughter asked him to pray in the village temple which would bless them with bright sunlight and fortunes of ample. As he reached the temple complex, he received another call from the other daughter, who had settled in the west. She sobbed as she said, there was no way to settle down the hot Sun in the west. The forest was burning, the animals were dying, as the sun refused to take any rest. She asked her father to pray for all the best, to let the rain shower in the west. The farmer was confused, what to do? One wanted the sun to rise and other wanted it to set. So he prayed to the sun, one day you shine and the other day you rest. Please rise in the east and rest in the west. So as he prayed,there was sunshine and rain in the temple complex, with moist ground and birds dancing in the apex. He came out smiling, looking at the sky,there was a rainbow shining in the sun, drizzling and sparkling in the rainfall with so much of fun. Now we know that the two sister's prayer were heard, as they rejoiced, looking at the rainbow raising in the east and setting in the west. The farmer now finally rests..........
author: Gunjan Gangey
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Aphisith Souphavongtay; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Sahitya Rani; Seema Misra; Sinomonde Ngwane

title: The black Cat
text: There lived a black wild cat in a dark cave in Kurinjimala. He passed his time chasing and teasing the little mice in that cave. The mice wanted good riddance from his nuisance and thought of a plan. Once when he was away,the little mice began digging a deep pit at the cave's entrance. All the mice pitched in and dug a deep pit and they covered it with twigs and leaves. That night when the cat came back, he fell in the pit and couldn't get out. They re-filled the pit with soil and the cat got stuck there. They leaved in peace ever after.
author: Primna Kenneth

title: Kachru's Strange Song
text: K achru Singh Patel and his wife Radha lived in the village of Prahladpur. Kachru Singh would spend the entire day gazing at the sky and sleeping. Meanwhile, Radha would get up before dawn, rush to catch the train to the city and then go from one house to another, cooking. The kind Madams and Sirs often offered her food to take back home. Radha would return to the village in the afternoon and share the leftovers with her husband. One day, Radha brought back some dosa batter. Kachru, snoring under the shade of a jamun tree near their hut saw Radha and started grumbling about starving the entire day. Hungry herself, Radha began preparing the dosas. While greasing the hot pan, she thought, “This greedy man will wolf down the dosas without thinking about my share. Maybe I should make my dosas later. But what if he sees them then? Let me make all six now and give him three.” She poured some batter on the pan. When the batter started bubbling, she turned it over to cook on the other side. Radha repeated this process six times. Every time a dosa was ready, she removed it and splashed water on the hot pan, making it sizzle. She poured some batter on the pan. When the batter started bubbling, she turned it over to cook on the other side. Radha repeated this process six times. Every time a dosa was ready, she removed it and splashed water on the hot pan, making it sizzle. She gave three hot and fluffy dosas to Kachru who gobbled it up in no time. After a ferocious burp, he asked Radha for more. Radha replied, “Oh, but there are no more left.” “Oh, but I know you made six dosas!” Kachru Singh said. Radha stood there amazed and confused. How could her lazy husband know this? Kachru Singh said, as if he knew exactly what she was thinking, “Oho, you think I am just a lazy no-gooder, don’t you? When I lie down under the jamun tree, I meditate and pray to the gods. I am now in possession of magical powers. I hear more than others, I see more than others, I know more than others." Radha did not believe a word her husband said. She took her share of dosas to her friend Rohiya’s house and over the yummy meal, they laughed together at Kachru Singh’s nonsense. Soon, the word spread in Prahladpur and everyone was talking about Kachru Singh Patel’s magical powers. A few days later, Kachru was resting under the tree as usual. Rohiya’s baby son was playing near his house with a noisy rattle. Suddenly, baby Aniruddha began howling. Rohiya came and picked him up. “What has upset you? Where is your toy?” She looked here and there but could not find the rattle anywhere. By evening, there was hullabaloo in the village. Rohiya had declared the rattle to be missing and nobody could find it. In tears, she went to Kachru Singh Patel. “If it is true that you have magical powers, help me find my rattle. It is made of real silver and was given by Aniruddha’s great-great-great grandmother.” Kachru Singh made a big show of consulting the gods. He began singing a strange song. I was listening when the dosas sizzled, sizz-sizz-sizzle. Each dosa said, sizz-sizz-sizzle. Then he announced, “Go look in the thickest shrub between your house and mine.” Lo! The silver rattle was found and everyone considered it fortunate that such a powerful man lived in their village. One night, there was chaos. Guddu, the old dhobhi of the colony, could not find his beloved donkey Kaidai. He went to Kachru Singh Patel’s house. “Please help me! Kaidai is gone!" One night, there was chaos. Guddu, the old dhobhi of the colony, could not find his beloved donkey Kaidai. He went to Kachru Singh Patel’s house. “Please help me! Kaidai is gone!" Kachru Singh agreed and asked for a day’s time because the donkey god Daikai Dev was available only in the mornings. The next day, Kachru Singh woke up before his wife and headed out. He began looking for Kaidai everywhere. A few men with camels were going through the village. One of the men was saying, “Let’s not stop here. There is a small lake nearby. There will be grass for the camels there and a tree’s shade for us.” Kachru Singh began following them. When he reached the lake, lo! Guddu’s donkey was fast asleep on lush grass. Kachru Singh woke the donkey up and tried to make him move. But Kaidai refused to budge. Kachru Singh sat down, exhausted. Nibbling on a blade of sweet grass, he began singing. Kachru Singh woke the donkey up and tried to make him move. But Kaidai refused to budge. Kachru Singh sat down, exhausted. Nibbling on a blade of sweet grass, he began singing. I was listening when the dosas were sizz-sizz-sizzling I was looking at the noisy rattle when it was fall-fall-falling and I looked for Kaidai where lush grass was grow-grow-growing. Kaidai got up suddenly with a loud bray. Kachru Singh led him back to the village and handed him over to an ecstatic Guddu who couldn't believe his eyes and ears. By now, the word had spread far and wide. One early morning, the mayor of a nearby city came searching for Kachru Singh Patel … but, that’s another story. Perhaps you would like to hear it from Kachru Singh himself. He sits under the same jamun tree in Prahaladpur, singing a strange song about sizzling dosas.
author: Rakhi Iyer

title: Tall And Short (Vikas's Family)
text: Pa is getting my hat. Pa is tall. Ma is getting my shirt. Pa is taller than Ma. My sister Lalita is getting my book. (In English we call younger sister also as ' Sister ') Ma is taller than my sister. My brother Vinay is getting my bag. My sister Lalita is taller than my brother Vinay. And my brother Vinay is taller than me. I’m the shortest in the family. Oh wait! There is our puppy, JoJo. Jojo is getting my slippers. Ha ha! JoJo is the shortest. Yes! JoJo is shorter than me. I’m shorter than my brother V inay. My brother Vinay is shorter than my sister Lalita. My sister is shorter than Ma. Ma is shorter than Pa. Wow! Pa is the tallest, and JoJo is the shortest.
author: Sirisha Kandukuri

title: Sily jokes
text: The snale and the garden. Once up on a time a snale named steve he wanted to eat all the vechtabls in the farm one day steve wanted to go to the home farms so that he can eat all the food in the wrold and he did and he did't know that some one is there and woshed him away to a snake he said you bin to a farm have you no I haven't let me ask okay? No you can not ask are you lieing? He broke a bus AND HE BLOO UP THE BU POOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO! AHHHHHHHHHHHHH! HOW DAR YOU BRAKE MY BUS YOU FIX THE BUS ALL BUY YOUR SELF I MY OFFIES NOW! Oooooo you fixed my bus think you Mr Snale you are good at fixing my bus
author: Miller Zha

title: Corona Hair
text: It was lock down due to Corona pandemic. Jay and Bella had to stay home all days for weeks. It was fun at the start - Wake up late,run around in pyjamas, snack all day, read, paint and play all day long. They liked to dress up and their Cat aka "Catson" joined in too. They pretended as astronauts and detectives and had heaps of fun. Weeks passed. They noticed that their hair is growing wild and long and getting in to their eyes. They hadn't visited the hair dresser for months. Jay had an idea.Let's pretend as hair dressers and give ourselves a hair cut.He grabbed a scissor and chopped Bella's hair and his too. The next thing they knew was that- they looked freaky. A yelp came out of Bella's mouth."What did you do?" Mum and dad ran in to check the yelping. Bella and Jay couldn't hide any where. Catson was looking up with wonder in his eyes. " Oh my darlings..., You look absolutely weird but adorable. Is this the CORONA hairstyle?". They all couldn't stop laughing.
author: Primna Kenneth

title: Many Colours of Girls
text: Some are completely bald. ﻿Some girls have short hair While some have long tresses. And some girls will ride on the back of anything that moves - a cycle, a horse or even a donkey. Many like climbing tre es. Some love making dolls and caring for them. Some are fond of flying kites, or playing Gilli Danda. While some enjoy singing at the top of their voice, Some girls hum a gentle tune. Others like to run out of their homes. They are happiest when at the playground. Some girls prefer to stay home, and clamber onto their father's lap. there are others who have no any interest in it. They are just as merry in scruffy clothes and with tousled hair. While there are those who love to dress up, Girls can be well-behaved and calm. But sometimes they can be naughty and mischievous too. Now and then girls get very angry. And they S-C-R-E-A-M. Girls can be so many things - helpful, kind, naughty, happy, mischievous as well as annoyed. Children can be whatever they want to be. Because every child is really unique.
author: Priyanka Nayar

title: Meet My Family
text: I have an interesting family. Do you want to meet them? These are my parents. Both my mother and my father work in the postoffice. This is my older brother, Raj and my older sister, Rohini. We play games together, especially during the holidays! These are my paternal and maternal grandparents. I like it when they come to visit me. These are my father's brothers. My father has 2 elder brothers and 2 younger brothers. They are my uncles. (We use ' Uncle ' for both elder and younger brothers of the father and mother. These are my father's sisters. They are my aunts, Shanta and Susheela. The girl in the pink clothes is my cousin Latha. She is Susheela aunty's daughter. Oh, and I almost forgot. This is my dog, Neelu. She's almost two years old and everybody loves her! This is my family. Now you can tell me about yours!
author: Sirisha Kandukuri

title: A Curse or a Blessing?
text: For many months, the skies were dry. Lomongin, the famous rain-maker, talked to his gods. People gathered outside his home, anxiously waiting for a message of hope. When he came out, he assured people that the creator was going to give them rain soon. They would be able to plant their crops. Children played outside as we waited for the rains. Later that day, we saw big white clouds in the far east. I knew they were rain clouds. People were still thinking about what the rain-maker said. Mother shouted loudly, “There! The clouds are now dark. Come inside.” The rain poured down. We had waited for the rains! At first we rejoiced. But the rains did not stop. There was water everywhere. The bridge linking our village to the mainland was washed away. Houses were washed away by floods. What was a blessing, was now a disaster for us. Everybody had prepared for planting. But now they could not plant. People of my village had longed for rain but now they did not want it anymore. We had no bridge to cross on. Many had no homes. And, we had another problem! We saw crocodiles swimming everywhere. This had never happened before. We were confused. We could not go shopping because all the shops were across the river. Children couldn't go to school because schools were across the river. What should have been a blessing, became a curse to us. Lomongin, the rainmaker, was disappointed as well. The only one who was happy, was Kapuus with his eight cats!
author: Alfred Esinyen
illustrator: Marleen  Visser; Natalie  Propa; Silva Afonso

title: Amara and Animals
text: Amara was nine years old. She went to Kerema primary school. Her favorite subjects were English, Science and Social Studies. She wanted to be a lawyer when she grew up. Amara loved animals very much. Amara lived with her mother, Margy. She was a very hardworking farmer. Amara's father died when she was 5 years old. When Amara was not at school, she spent her time with Mbisa, the goat. She cleaned and fed it. Amara also had her pet, Simba. Her mother did not like dogs very much, but she let Amara keep Simba. Whenever Simba disturbed her, she would shout, "Go away before I kick you out." Amara felt sad. One Saturday, they had visitors from the women's group. Amara was happy that her mother's friends had come with their children. They could play football. Her mother had prepared the food that the group liked. Amara was reminded by her mother to keep Simba locked up. It barked at strangers. Amara did not lock up Simba well. The visitors were surprised to see the dog in the room. Mama Oto asked, "Why do you allow the dog to come inside the house?" Amara's mother called Amara to come and take Simba out. Amara did not hear her mother calling because they were busy playing. When Amara went to the house, she called Simba out. Simba was very obedient to Amara. After the meal, the visitors said, "We'll also treat our dogs well like Amara. We mistreat them and yet they are so helpful." Afterwards, Amara's mother apologised for being mean and cruel to Simba. Amara was happy that her mother accepted her dog at last. When Amara is in school her mother feeds Simba. Her mother's friends have learned to be good to their dogs.
author: Judy B. Maranga

title: Akai's Special Mat
text: When Akai was a little girl, her mother used to put her to sleep on a beautiful mat. Akai's aunt made this special mat from palm leaves. The mat had bright pink, blue and green colours. It was different from other mats that Akai's mother had in the hut. The land around Akai's home was very dry, hot and full of stones. There were many scorpions, spiders and snakes too. But Akai was never in danger of being bitten by these dangerous creatures. Her mother said, “Her special mat protects Akai from any harm.” Akai was a clever child. She discovered where the nearest shallow well was. Akai also knew where her grandmother's manyatta was located. She often went to drink camel milk with her grandmother. One day, Akai was not so lucky. She left to go to her grandmother's manyatta, but she got lost in the hills. Akai was afraid. She sat under an edome tree and waited for help. Soon she fell asleep and had a dream. This is what Akai dreamed. She was lying on her special mat. A woman who looked like her grandmother was watching over her. The old woman smiled and gave her a bowl of camel milk. Just when Akai stretched out her hand to take the milk, she woke up. Akai opened her eyes slowly. When she looked up, she saw a small blue bird on a branch above her. When Akai got up, the small blue bird flapped its wings and led the way for Akai. She followed the bird. Akai came to a place where the path went in two different directions. The blue bird dropped a piece of a mat that was like Akai's own mat. Picking up the piece of mat, Akai saw footprints that she knew were her mother's. Soon she saw the shallow well from where they fetched water. Akai's family sang and danced to welcome her home. They slaughtered a goat, roasted the meat and celebrated their child's safe return. Akai sat on her special mat and enjoyed eating a big piece of roast meat.
author: Ursula Nafula

title: My best friend
text: Ariane loves to play. She plays with me every day. ﻿ ﻿﻿ My friend loves to jump, once she jumped over a giant hole. She loves looking at herself in the river. ﻿ Everyone knows my friend because she is very generous and friendly. She is friends with the elephants, the giraffes, the lions... I love my friend. She's my best friend in the whole wide world.
author: Evelyn Burrows

title: HONEY the cat
text: Once upon a time in a small country on the sea there was a cat named Honey because it was so sweet. A day returning from its walk, Honey found a red fish in the bowl on the kitchen table. Bubble, the fish, was very sad because it felt alone. So Honey thougth to help it and took it into the sea. Bubble was happy for this idea and very grateful to Honey. Bubble could go back to its home and be with its large family. It never forgot Honey and sometime it comes back to greet it.
author: Giorgia Dell'Orto

title: Kuwomba the Anxious Cloud
text: Kuwomba was the happiest cloud in Cloudpuram. She loved her sweet shop and she loved making sweets. One day, Kuwomba got a party order for 1,000 sweets! At first, she was excited. She imagined all the great clouds at the party enjoying her sweets. Then she started to worry. What if she couldn’t make 1,000 sweets? What if no one liked them? What if, what if, what if… Kuwomba couldn’t sleep. She kept thinking about the 1,000 sweets and ‘what if’. She couldn’t eat. Her hands were sweaty. Her tummy felt like it was flip-flopping inside her. Then she started to worry. What if she couldn’t make 1,000 sweets? What if no one liked them? What if, what if, what if… Kuwomba couldn’t sleep. She kept thinking about the 1,000 sweets and the what-ifs. She couldn’t eat. Her hands were sweaty. Her tummy felt like it was flip-flopping inside her. Kuwomba tried working harder but she couldn’t stop worrying. “What if everything goes wrong? What if I can’t do it? What if everyone hates my sweets?” she thought. She became small and grey. Her hands began to shake. Her heart was racing all the time. She couldn’t even breathe properly! One morning, Kuwomba couldn’t get out of bed. She was miserable. She still had so many sweets to make! What was she going to do? Kuwomba’s older sister, Apik, came to see her. Kuwomba began to cry. She told Apik everything. To her surprise, she started feeling better. “Okay, let’s take some deep breaths together,” said Apik. They breathed in slowly for ten counts and out for ten counts. Kuwomba began to feel fluffy again. “Now let’s go for a little float,” said Apik. They floated among giant, peaceful clouds. Kuwomba looked at the big puffs and pretty colours. Her heartbeat slowed down. Her hands weren’t sweaty anymore. “We will make the sweets together,” said Apik. “And it’s okay if we don’t finish all of them.” “What do you mean?” said Kuwomba. “Let’s just do our best,” said Apik. They started making sweets. It was easier with two people. Kuwomba tried not to worry. Whenever she felt a 'what if' coming, she thought about making the best sweets she could instead. She took deep breaths and talked to Apik. This always made her feel better. On the day of the party, Kuwomba had only 700 sweets. She felt a little sad. She went out for a float. She took slow, deep breaths and began to feel better. In fact, she felt proud and happy. She knew she had done her best. At the party, the sweets were a huge hit. Kuwomba even got more orders! “Next time I’ll ask for help when I make the sweets,” said Kuwomba, with a smile. It was her first big smile in a long time. Once again, Kuwomba was the happiest cloud in Cloudpuram.
author: Kuzhali  Manickavel

title: A Forest Adventure
text: It was a sunny morning. Anu woke up at 7:00 am and she was really excited. She had a field trip to Nallamala forest - a big forest in Telangana. She hurried and got ready quickly, had breakfast, packed her bags and boarded her bus. In the bus, she sat in her seat beside her friends Sneha and Aditi. She was smiling wide and said, “Hi!” waving at them. "You look really happy today, Anu!” Sneha said. “I have a field trip today!” Anu said, grinning. “So, where are you going?” asked Aditi, curious. “To Nallamala forest!” Anu announced. “I am really excited!” “Are you sure you want to go to a forest on this sunny day?” Sneha asked. “I just don’t care!” Anu replied. “I just love field trips!” They continued the bus journey by playing games, talking about their friends, etc. After their bus reached school, Anu ran to her classroom and waited for her friends. She checked the snacks she brought: chips, wafers and juices. Slowly, her friends entered the classroom. Before the assembly, the girls and boys in her class had a debate on who is going to get the backseat in the bus. At last, the boys got the backseat. After the assembly, all the students set their bags and got ready to leave. They were told that they had to leave section wise. In the bus, Anu and her friends enjoyed a lot. They played games, sang songs and shared their snacks. After about two hours, they reached the forest. The students set up a picnic, explored the forest looking at the trees, animals and insects. Anu and best friends, Reena, Divya and Soumya, found a beautiful spot to play. They decided to play Hide & Seek. Divya and Soumya had to count and Anu and Reena had to hide. As they both started counting till 100, Anu and Reena ran into the woods. A few minutes later, they found themselves completely surrounded by trees. They looked back and saw nothing but trees. “We are lost!” said Reena, sadly. “Let’s look around and see if we can find someone who can help us,” Anu assured her. They walked a few miles and saw a cave. “Maybe we can rest in that cave for a while” Anu told Reena, pointing to the cave. “I’ll go and find something to eat, I’m feeling hungry. ” Reena said. “Ok, I will find a few stones to make fire,” Anu concluded. “It’s dark inside the cave.” Anu found few stones and sticks inside the cave and rubbed them hard together until she saw signs of fire. She put a few sticks so that the fire can sustain for a longer time. The fire completely lit up the cave. Anu looked around and saw a hollow passage which was really dark. She felt really curious to know what was inside, and if she could get any help. She took a stick and got some fire on it and went inside. After a few steps inside the cave, Anu heard loud snoring. She assumed that there was someone inside to help her and ran inside. There, she saw that a lion was sleeping in that cave. She dropped the fire stick and shouted, ”Aaaaaahhhhhhhhhhhh!!!” While Anu and Reena were in the woods, here Divya and Soumya were searching for them. “We made a really big mistake sending those two to hide,” said Divya. “Yeah, the two best friends must have found good hiding places and must be hiding together,” Soumya replied with certainty. “I think it would be better now if we stop chit-chatting and start finding them,” Divya said. “Now let’s go!” They looked around, warning each other not to go too far, and after about an hour, they were still looking for Anu and Reena. “Divya, I think they are lost,” Soumya said. “Maybe, you are right. Now let’s report this to Revati ma’am,” agreed Divya. “She might help us find them.” Saying this, they quickly went to Revati ma’am. Revati ma’am was their class teacher and was good at observing things. Divya and Soumya decided she was the one who could find Reena and Anu. By the time they reached Revati ma’am, they were huffing and puffing. “Ma’am, huff, ma’am, hhh!” “What happened, Divya and Soumya?” Ma’am asked, with concern. “Ma’am, we were playing Hide & Seek in a beautiful spot of the forest. Both of us had to count, and Anu and Reena had to hide. We searched for them for more than an hour, but still didn’t find them. We think they’re lost!” Divya explained. “Oh my! You made a mistake sending those two. Both of them together don’t care about the rest of the world,” Revati ma’am said. “Now, let me send a message to all the parents saying that we would have to start late. But if any of your parents live nearby, they can pick you up.” “Ma’am, I live nearby, but I don’t want to leave until we find Anu and Reena!” Divya said with determination. “Me too!” Soumya agreed. “Alright, I’ll tell both of your parents and inform Anu and Reena’s parents too!” Ma’am said. “Now show me where you were playing so that we can look for more clues.” Divya and Soumya showed the spot where they were playing and ma’am looked around and found a candy-shaped clip. “This is Anu’s clip!” Soumya pointed to the clip and said. “Hmmm……” Ma’am murmured and picked up the clip. Meanwhile, Anu was stuck in this cave with a lion snoring right in front of her. She was still figuring out how to escape without making noise when Reena entered the cave. “Anu, where are you?” She was looking for Anu. Anu couldn’t speak because if she does, the lion will wake up. Already she almost woke up the lion. Anu was still thinking about the lion while Reena entered the lion’s den. She didn’t seem to notice the lion, because as soon as she saw Anu she yelled, “Anu! How could you be so irresponsible? You were supposed to stay near the fire!” “Ggrrrrrrrrrrrrr!” The lion was fully awake now. Anu was absolutely terrified, but Reena stayed as calm as possible. “Relax,” She told Anu. “It’s okay,” Then she did something which gave a shock to Anu. She picked up the fire stick Anu dropped, pointed it to the lion and said, “Stay back.” She said that in a tone that was calm but threatening, even to Anu. The lion got tensed, and took a step back. Part of Anu was relieved, but part of her was feeling sorry for the lion. She believed that it was wrong to threaten animals. “Wait! Don’t do that! It will scare the lion!” Anu told Reena. “Shh!” Reena warned, putting a finger on her lips. She gave the fire stick to Anu and slowly walked towards the lion. Anu was stunned. She knew Reena was brave, but she never thought that Reena was brave enough to face a lion. The world should know this. Wow! Anyway, as she walked towards the lion, the lion took a few steps back. Slowly, the lion began to relax. Reena moved forward and touched the lion’s mane. “Poor thing, his leg is badly injured.” she mumbled and turned towards Anu. “ He needs help! Don’t worry, this lion is completely harmless. It’s just 5 years old.” She said. “How did you know?” Anu asked with uncertainty. Reena smiled. Then she said, “I’ve told you many times that I’ve been to Africa. There, I learnt about wilderness survival. I also studied lions, how to recognize their age by looking at their size. I also learnt to read their expressions from our tour guide, who owned a lot of lions. This one is not like the other lions, hunting for food. It doesn't have friends because all animals run away from it, because it looks scary. Now come on.” Anu hesitated at first, but she trusted Reena’s word. So she moved forward and felt the lion’s mane. It was amazingly soft. She asked Reena, “What do you think we should call him?” Reena thought for a while and started to say something but Anu stopped her. “After watching Lion King, I think we should call him Simba. What do you say?” Reena smiled. She looked at the lion and said, “Simba.” Simba roared with satisfaction. Anu and Reena started chatting with Simba as if he understood everything. While the girls were with Simba, Revati ma’am and their two friends were looking for more clues. They followed the path in which they found Anu’s clip and found themselves in the middle of the woods. Divya looked down and found two sets of footprints. “Look!” she said, pointing to those footprints. “Let’s follow the trail!” exclaimed Soumya, excited that they were going to find their friends. Alas, her excitement did not last for long. Soon, the sets of footprints led to different directions. Revati ma’am sighed. “Maybe they are not Anu and Reena’s footprints,” She said. Divya’s eyes lit up. “But maybe we can find someone else who might have seen them!” “Alright then! Both of you can follow the footprints towards the left and I will follow the other one,” said Revati ma’am. Divya and Soumya agreed. The girls followed Anu’s footprints, which led them directly to the cave. Revati ma’am followed Reena’s footprints, which first led her to a few trees and then to the same cave. As soon as Divya and Soumya stepped into the cave, Revati ma’am also came inside. First, they were hesitant. But then they decided this was the place where they will find us. “This place is completely lit up with fire,” Soumya said, looking at a passage where smokes of fire fell down everywhere. They followed the fire into the hollow passage and saw Anu and Reena. They didn’t seem to notice Simba because Divya directly went to Reena and hugged her. “Reena! I’m so happy to see you!” she said. “Me too!” Reena replied. Then she saw Simba and shouted. “Aaaaahhhhhhh! Www-what is this llll-lion doing hhhh-here?” she asked. “Come on! Let’s run away before it hurts us!” She started pulling Reena and Anu by their hands. “Stay calm, Divya. It won’t hurt you!” Anu consoled her. Divya was unsure and looked at the innocent-faced lion. “But it’s a wild animal!” she said, still frightened. “Divya is right!” Soumya interfered. “You can’t trust a wild animal, that too a predator!” Even Revati ma’am started saying all about lions and the three of them started arguing with Anu and Reena. They explained about what all happened and Reena told all about what she learnt in her journey to Africa. After a long chat, they understood what Reena and Anu were trying to convey. “So what are we going to do with Simba?” Soumya looked at Anu and Reena for an answer. Both of them exchanged looks and nodded to each other. “We have been discussing this,” Reena started. “Yes, we have decided that we can hand Simba to the forest officials so that he can be cared for,” Anu continued. “But when?” Divya asked. “Let’s think about it later,” Soumya replied. “Yeah, for now, I am hungry,” Anu said, hugging her stomach. All of them burst out laughing. They walked back to their playing spot, and had their lunch. The time was 3:30 pm now. After having their lunch, they went back to find their bus. They expected to see nobody, but all their friends were still there playing and waiting for them to be back. Their class MLA (class leader), Pragya was the first one to see them. “Hey! Are you both alright?” she asked Anu and Reena. Then she spotted Simba. Instead of being scared, she turned excited. She shouted to everyone, “Hey everybody, listen! Anu and Reena are back with a lion!” Everyone ran to them. Karan, the eldest boy in their class was the first to come and look at the lion. “Where did you find it?” he asked. They narrated the entire incident to everyone. At last, they said his name was Simba. “Great name!” a girl called Shreya said. “Hey!” Soumya told me. “I almost forgot. While we were looking for you, we found this.” She gave Anu her clip. Anu smiled. “Thank you!” she said. All of them, including Simba, boarded their bus and started chit-chatting. Few kids were bombarding Reena and Anu with lots of questions. The girls joyfully answered all their questions. Very soon they reached office of forest department. As kids were engrossed in excitement, they didn't realize they reached office. They met officials and explained them whatever happened and then handed over Simba. The officials were surprised and impressed on the bravery displayed by the children and appreciated them for the kindness and concern towards the lion cub. They also offered children a special tour on their next visit. After reaching home, Anu told all her adventures to her parents. They were scared at first but then got impressed and felt happy at the bravery Anu and Reena had shown. Next day, the school Principal Geeta ma’am visited each classroom, (in the whole school) and told about Anu and Reena’s adventures. She said that from now onwards she will arrange trips for the whole school to go to Nallamala forest every year. All of them learnt a lesson: We should not judge a book by its cover. Just because an animal is from the wild, we should not leave it in a helpless condition.
author: Nishita Ande
illustrator: 211 Studio; Abhimanyu Ghimiray; Ad Sarin; Ajay Hembron; André Kieswetter; Arun Ramkumar; Bindia  Thapar; Brian Wambi; Dr. Sushma  Singh; Isaac Sikhakhane; Jai Bhagwan Gupta; Marleen  Visser; Niloufer Wadia; Partho Sengupta; Sunaina  Coelho; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Halloween
text: One night until Halloween!' Thomas shouts. He loves sweets. The night before Halloween, Thomas can't sleep. When he comes back from daycare, Thomas is ready to go trick-or-treating. He is dressed as a superhero. He goes with his friends Max, Tristan, Antoine, Emma and Theo. He comes back home with loads of sweets. Thomas is tired and dreams of having all the sweets in the world. But when he wakes up, all the sweets he collected are gone! How terrible!
author: Evelyn Burrows

title: Bin's Big Joint Family
text: This is everyone. 1. Grandma 2. Grandpa 3. Bin (and Cat) 4. Uncle 5. Aunt 6. Their Baby 7. Bin's Parents There are too many people! Bin feels he has nowhere to play. At last, his family takes their afternoon nap. Cat gets the yarn. Now Bin and Cat can play. It is so much fun! CRASH! Uh-oh. Everything is a mess! The yarn is tangled. The baby cries. Mom scolds Bin. Dad scolds Bin. Even Grandpa scolds Bin. Bin talks back. I have no place to play! This house is too small! Ours is too big a family! Bin cries loudly. Bin cries softly. Bin falls asleep. Bin wakes up. The house seems strange. There’s no baby, no Mom, no Grandma. There is no Grandpa. No Dad. No Uncle or Aunt. Bin and cat are home alone. " This is great! We can play however we want!" thought Bin. Suddenly it is dark. What happened? The sky flashes. " Where is everyone?" thought Bin, scared. Then come his mom and grandparents. And the baby. It starts raining. Then Dad is home! Uncle and Aunt are home too! Bin feels safe now. Bin starts playing with his cousin, the baby. His grand parents tell him a lot of stories. His uncle and aunt play with him too. "Sometimes it is nice to have a big joint family. ", he thought. And he can always play outside.
author: Sirisha Kandukuri

title: What Happens When You Flush?
text: Nozy crept out of Nikhil’s pocket… “Ahhhhhh! Nikhil, keep your rat away from me!” yelled his sister. Startled, Nozy leapt at the sink but fell into the toilet bowl instead. Whooooosh! Nozy splashed into an underground pit. As he got used to the darkness, he saw another rat. “Hey! You’re new here. I’m Cheeky. What’s your name? Want to look around?” she said. “I’m N…Nozy… Where am I?” asked Nozy. “Underground inspection chamber. It’s where the toilet and kitchen pipes join the sewer,” said Cheeky. SPLAT! Nozy was covered in foam. “You’re lucky that wasn’t poo. Heehee hoohoo!” laughed Cheeky. Cheeky and Nozy darted into a pipe. They jumped into a round pit. It had large and small pipes going in and out of it. “Small pipes carry wastewater from each building to this large pipe,” said Cheeky. “Look, a manhole!” Cheeky said. Nozy looked up, “A man with holes? Where? Where?” “Calm down, it’s just a hole in the street. Humans use it to check and repair the sewer.” Cheeky and Nozy darted into a pipe. They jumped into a round pit. It had large and small pipes going in and out of it. “Small pipes carry wastewater from each building to this large pipe,” said Cheeky. “Look, a manhole!” Cheeky said. Nozy looked up, “A man with holes? Where? Where?” “Calm down, it’s just a hole in the street. Humans use it to check and repair the sewer.” They scurried through the sewer. “Ugh! This really stinks,” said Nozy. “Oh, it’s just poisonous gases. Don’t breathe too hard,” said Cheeky. “Come on!” They sped on until... SPLASH! Nozy fell into the canal where the sewer ended. Cheeky dove in too. The water flowed through a grill. But Cheeky and Nozy were held back, along with a heap of nappies, plastic covers, water bottles and a very large armchair. “You wouldn’t believe what else ends up here,” said Cheeky. “Once the whole sewer was stuffed with report cards.” “What happened then?” asked Nozy. “The grill filtered out the trash, and it was removed and recycled.” Cheeky and Nozy climbed over the pile and sat on the canal wall. Nozy rubbed up against the wall to clean himself. “I like my fur soft and clean,” he said. “In the sewers, we say the dirtier the better,” said Cheeky. “Want to see something fun?” They ran along the canal wall to a long, narrow tank. “That’s the grit tank. Can you see the floating dirt sinking to the bottom?” GRIT TANK To landfill Cheeky pointed to another tank. “If any dirt escapes from the grit tank, it settles down in this one and is removed. This is the sedimentation tank.” “Look! Rainbows on the water!” gasped Nozy. “Oh, that’s just floating oil,” said Cheeky. SEDIMENTATION TANK To filtration tank To trickler filter Cheeky and Nozy scurried past the grit and sedimentation tanks. Nozy pointed to a circular tank ahead. “Hey, It’s raining over there!” “That’s just the trickler filter,” said Cheeky. “It’s full of good bacteria. When water goes through the pebbles, the bacteria eat the dirt and clean the water.” TRICKL ER FILTER To oxidation tank OXIDATION TANK Nozy spotted another tank. “Is that a magic cauldron?” he cried. “It’s bubbling!” “No, those are oxygen bubbles,” said Cheeky. “That’s the oxidation tank. Oxygen is pumped into the water to make the good bacteria grow.” To settlement tank Finally, they reached the last two tanks. Cheeky pointed at the first one, “That’s the settlement tank, where leftover dirt settles down.” “What happens in the other one?” asked Nozy. SETTLEMENT TANK To outlet in the sea “In the filtration tank, water flows through a bed of charcoal to remove the stink. Then a sand bed traps the last bits of dirt.” FILTRATION TANK Air Vent To outlet in the sea SPLAWHOOSH! The water flowed from the filtration tank into the sea. “That almost looks clean!” said Nozy. They tumbled out onto the beach. Sniff, sniff! “I can smell bhelpuri,” said Cheeky. “And I can smell Nikhil!” said Nozy.
author: Vani Vasudev

title: Hashim learns to make pickle!
text: They will remain fresh" said Hashim's father. His father told him that germs cannot live without water. "How do I remove the water-content from mangoes?" Hashim asked his father. " Add water to it!" Hashim and his father dried the mangoes in the sun later. Then, they put all of the mango pieces in a glass jar and added oil to it. The oil prevents the germs in the air from entering the mango jar. " Father! We have made pickle!" said Hashim. How do we safe-guard our favorite fruits and vegetables? Boil potatoes and dry it out in the sun to get potato fritters. When you cook apple (or any favorite fruit) with sugar and lime, you get jam. Add salt to tomatoes and dry it in the sun. Add oil to the dried tomatoes to get sun-dried tomatoes. Mix lemon with salt to get lemon pickle.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Beware
text: I hated that uncle. He used to come to my house. He stared at me when he came. He asked me to come near by and also teased me. I never went near him. I hated going near him. I tried to escape his touch somehow or other. I shared about this at home. I told everything to my mother. My mother spoke to the uncle and warned him. He stopped coming to our house after that.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Busy Busy Sun
text: The sun rises in the morning, by the east side. I hear the cock crow at dawn. The sun moves over Terfa's compound before the morning meal. I smell the aroma of bier and akpupa following the sun to my window. The sun goes behind a tree at school during lunchtime. Then it arrives in a puddle in the middle of the playground. The sun stands above my head. My shadow stands beside me. I play the shadow game with my friends. My shadow grows bigger, then smaller. We run after it. My shadow grows longer, then shorter. We run after it. I stand, my friends stand. We see our shadows sway. We grow tired and return to class. After school, we go home. The sun yawns. I see the sun sink slowly in the west. I see my shadow on a wall. It is time to go to bed. The sun goes down behind the clouds. I lay down in my bed, and dream of the sun traveling afar.
author: Mimi  Werna

title: I love bunnies
text: They love to play. They are herbivores. They eat grass and carrots. Bunnies have big ears so that they can hear well. Bunnies have to look for their food. Sometimes, it's difficult. They have to hide if there are hunters nearby. Bunnies are very small so they can fit through little holes. Bunnies are adorable.
author: Evelyn Burrows
illustrator: Imphir; San srei nou ch nou ch

title: What's up, Navi?
text: "What's up, Navi?" mama asks her sweet little baby. "I am reading a colorful book, mama" Navi says happily. Dada asks, "What are you doing dear Navi?" "I am sitting on my orange chair, ready for breakfast, dada" replies Navi. Thatha calls out "What's up, Navi?" "I am driving my Red car, Thatha!" Navi answers with a glee, "Do you want to join?" Avva hugs Navi and asks, "What do you want to do Navi?" "I want to fly to the blue sky, Avva and play with the stars!" replies an excited Navi. Pinni asks "What's up, cutie?" "You look so pretty in green!" Navi blushes feeling shy! "What's up, Navi?" babai asks. "I am ready to party in pink" says Navi with her naughty smile! "What are you doing Navi?" everyone asks. "I am going to sleep and dream a wonderful dream!" replies a very sleepy Navi. That's all folks! Good night! Sleep tight! Navi says Bye!
author: Divya N

title: A beautiful day at the beach!!
text: It was a beautiful morning, Jack woke up and started stretching. He checked the room and no one had woken up yet. He tip-toed to the bathroom to brush his teeth. He ate breakfast, finished his homework and wondered what to do because there was no work for him to do now. Then, everyone woke up. They didn't have any work to do too. They decided to go on a walk. As soon as it became hot, they stopped to drink some water. Jack looked to his side and saw a sign of a beach and asked his parents if they could go to the beach. His parents said "yes". Luckily they had their swimsuits in the stroller where his baby sister was sitting in. As they went to the beach more and more people passed by them. The baby ran and started playing in the sand. Jack jumped in the water. They played and played in the water and sand.They had so much fun. It was sunset and the family was relaxed. They watched the sunset and went back home. They decided to watch a lovely movie to complete their beautiful day. Jack had so much fun and dreamed the whole night about the beach.
author: Vaishnavi Gunti

title: Monkey and the Mangoes
text: Once there was a monkey who could not find any food for days. One day he came across a forest full of mangoes. When he got there he came to know that there was a demon in the forest who killed anyone who entered the forest to eat the mangoes.He also came to know that he was dumb. So he thought for a while until he got an idea. He went up to the demon and said that " O, Demon, I was on my way to tell you that I saw another demon who claimed that he is the king of this forest". The demon replied "Oh, that is not true. I am the king of this forest. Take me to him." So the monkey took the demon to a deep well and when the demon looked down,the monkey pushed him with all his might. He fell down the well,drowned and died. The monkey rushed to get the mangoes with excitement. Then he nearly ate two trees of mango's. MORAL - Brain is stronger than brawn. Note- Inspired by a Panchathantra story.
author: Jai Kumar
illustrator: Abhishikta Dutta; AJAY AMITABH SUMAN; Salim  Kasamba

title: Favourite food
text: We are going to learn about food. What is your favourite food? My favourite food is fried rice. ﻿thinking... (so many options) I like ice-cream a lot everybody likes ice-cream I eat ice-cream every day but I also like bread bread with jam and milk makes a good breakfast great!
author: Kristina  Tancoo

title: Jump
text: I jump up, I jump down. I jump up to ring the bell. I bend down to touch my toe. I move from side to side, I twist, I turn. I roll, I run. I clap, I sing, Oh! It is so much fun! I swing from side to side. I move my head up and down, touch my chin to my chest. Then all I do is roll my eyes and run along. Hop, skip and jump, my warm up is all done!
author: Gauri Mehendale

title: Mangoes
text: I finished the last mango today. We had bought four and now there are none. This makes me sad, because I love mangoes. I can eat them all day long. Why must good things always be over? I have an idea! Let's bury the mango seed into the soil. Soon there will be a tree that will give me mangoes everyday. I shall share them with my family and friends.
author: Medha Agarwal

title: Fishes in the basket
text: I see a basket. There are many fish in the basket. The fish have scales and gills. The gills help the fish to breathe underwater. These fish are found in the salty ocean. My father sails his boat into the ocean every morning. He catches these fish using a net. My mother weaves the net when she is not cooking or cleaning. At night, we cook the fish. I love to eat a good fish dish.
author: Medha Agarwal

title: Orange
text: To me orange is not just a colour, but a taste which is full of childhood nostalgia. No, not the orange fruit, which needs to be peeled off before eating, it is but a small orange coloured as well as orange flavoured candy wrapped up in a transparent orange coloured wrapper of some local company in Kolkata. My childhood and this story of orange candy goes a long way. When I was in my primary school, Baba used to pick me up everyday after classes. We had to walk a short distance of 15 mins to reach the auto rickshaw stand and everyday he handed me one orange candy on the way back. I used to excitedly pop one in my mouth and relish the tanginess. He also did the same. It was like a daily ritual for us which nobody knew about, not even Ma. A few months after his death, when my mother was taking his trousers for a final wash, she called me up and handed me down his things from the pocket to keep in his drawer. Among the many things that she took out was, a wallet, some bus tickets, a few coins covered in tobacco leaves, and... two orange candies. The same ones that we devoured during our 15 mins walk. He had stopped picking me up from school since class 8. A school bus was arranged for me. We got busy with life, I made new friends, tried coping up with the ever increasing study load and the memory of those afternoon walks took a backseat. When Ma handed me those orange candies, I was reminded of a certain period of my life. It reminded me of a long forgotten taste. A taste of joy. The sweet orange smell of those afternoons still linger in the air. Orange to me is now the colour of the sky on those afternoons we spent walking home together. Somehow Baba made his last gift a memorable one.
author: Mousumi  Roy

title: Priya's New School
text: Today is Priya's first day of school! She just moved from California to New Jersey. She is going into 2nd grade. She is so excited to visit her new school and make new friends. Priya's older brother, Rahul, told her that 2nd grade is very fun! "Priya come downstairs for breakfast." "Coming Amma!" Priya put on her blue cap and went downstairs. Rahul and Amma were sitting at the table. "Where is nana?" Priya asks. "He is at work," Rahul says. Priya smells pancakes. It smells delicious. Priya sits at the table and quickly eats all of her food. She takes her backpack and walks to the bus stop. When Priya gets on the bus she sees everybody talking to each other. She notices that everyone already has friends from last year. She is scared that nobody will want to be friends with her because she is new. "Hi my name is Priya. Can I sit next to you?" Priya asks a girl. "NO WAY! This seat is saved for my BFF Moana!" Shouts the girl. Priya sits alone in the back of the bus. She is sad. She thinks that she will never make any friends. When Priya arrives at school she does not know where to go. Everybody else has already been to this school last year so they all know where to go. "Excuse me. Where is Mr. Mick's classroom?" Priya says stopping a boy. The boy looks at her and then runs to his class. Priya is upset. "HI! I am Mr. Mick. I have never seen you around before. You must be the new student Priya." "Yeah,"Priya says. "Everyone settle down. I would like you to meet the new student Priya." Everyone stared at Priya. "Ok class lets start learning. Can anybody tell me what 12 plus 67 is? How about you Priya." "Um, 84?" The entire class chuckled because of the wrong answer to the easy problem. Priya put her blue cap over her eyes so nobody could see the tears in her eyes. Priya had no friends, her entire class thought she was a joke, and her teacher thought she was dumb. This was going to be the worst year ever. Priya sat alone at lunch and swung by herself at recess. Finally she got home. "How was school Priya?" Rahul asked. Priya ignored him and ran to her room. She shut the door and cried. Priya thought that her class did not like her, but maybe during lunch she could become friends with a kid from another class. Priya though that that was a good idea. She decided that tomorrow she would make a bunch of friends during lunch. Priya woke up. She put on a pink sweater and a white skirt. Then she put on a pink headband and white bunny slippers. Priya was ready to make some new friends at lunch. The first 3 hours of the day passed. It was finally lunch time. Priya took her lunch box and went to get a spoon for her fried rice. As she was walking to the lunch table she slipped and fell. The entire school looked at her and started laughing. Now everyone hated her. Priya is mad and sad. When Priya went home she went to amma. "Amma, I am never EVER going to school again!" "Why Priya? You don't have a choice you have to go." "UGHH!" Priya was so mad. She went to her room and cried. She wished she had never moved. She like her old school and her old friends. Now she didn't even have any friends. The next few days of school passed. Priya still had no friends. Everyday during lunch Priya would sit alone in the back of the room, and during recess she would walk around the playground watching the other kids play. During her classes she sat in the back of the room with her head down, never raising her hand. She never talked to her brother or her parents. When she went home she sat in her room staring at the wall. "Priya!" "Yes?" "You have mail!" "I don't care." "Come and read it." "No!" "Rahul!" "What ma? "Give this mail to your sister." "Ok." Rahul came to Priya's room and gave her the mail. Priya opened the letter. Hi Priya, How are you? I have seen you around at school. I see that you don't have that many friends. Don't worry about the mean people in school! You can sit with us from tomorrow!:) Kavya Priya was so happy, because of the letter. Then she thought that why would anybody ever give her a nice letter after she was so clumsy and horrible at school. She decided to ask Kavya. Dear Kavya, Thank you for the letter. I was wondering why are you being so kind to me after I was nothing but miserable and clumsy at school? - Priya Priya, I wrote the letter because I wanted to be a kind person. You should always remember that no matter how mean or miserable other people are you should look for the good in them and help them. Remember to be the best person you can be and never give up. I can't wait to see you in school tomorrow. - Kavya Priya was so happy. She learned something very important from Kavya. She new that she was going to have the best year ever. She did not know if she would like Kavya's friends, or if her teachers would like her, but now she knew that no matter what she was not going to give up and she was going to be the kindest person ever, just like Kavya was to her. Dear Kavya, Thank you for being my friend. - Priya
author: Akshara Datla

title: Where is my bat?
text: I lost my bat. I am not finding it anywhere. I saw it behind the door. But it was not there. I saw climbing up on box. It was not there too. I saw under the bed. But it was not there. I searched inside the box. But it was not there too. I saw up and down all around. On all the sides of home. It is not here, It is not there. No where! No where!
author: Rita Bansal

title: Brindavanamum Nandakumaranum
text: Hello children!! Our Sanatana dharma teaches us various dharmas (righteous actions), that one has to follow in life. These dharmas distinguish us from other animals, birds and living beings and make us unique. Dharma means ' way of life '. Lord Sri Rama is called 'dharmatma', embodiment of dharma, because He showed us how to walk the path of dharma even under adverse situations in life. There are dharmas for everybody - 1. dharma that has to be followed by children and youth, 2. dharma followed by married couples and families 3. dharma followed by people who would like to move away from family life and spend the rest of the life in serving Bhagawan 4. dharma that has to be followed by people who have renounced worldly life This dharma can be divided into two: 1. Vaidheega dharma (the various dharmas shown by our Vedas), 2. Bhagawatha dharma (the dharma shown by Srimad Bhagawatham).
author: Tamil Vagupu
illustrator: Manobendro Golder; Samit  Shrestha; Shailja Jain Chougule; Sharanya Singh

title: The Hare and the Tortoise (Again!)
text: We all know that Hare lost the race because of its laziness and over confidence. We also know that Tortoise won the race because of its continuous, stable walk and slow pace. All the animals in the Jungle got to know about this too. But all the animals had huge respect for both of them. Hare and Tortoise remained good friends even though they raced against each other. Tortoise was never proud of his winning the race. The Hare never had any kind of anger towards Tortoise. Months passed. The Lion, King of the jungle where the Hare and the Tortoise lived, had to have an important discussion with the other Jungle's Lion King, but he could not leave the Jungle immediately, as he had some important work. He thought for a while and sent Hare and Tortoise as his messengers to the other king. The Hare and Tortoise came to meet the King. "One of you need to go to the next animal kingdom," said the Lion. "You have to meet the king and discuss important matters, and tell me his views on the matter, you can go now," said the Lion. While they were leaving, "You just have one day's time to finish the work," reminded the King. The pathway to the other Kingdom was full of thorns and stones and they had to cross two rivers too. The Hare and the Tortoise, after a deep discussion, understood that this task could not be completed by one, they had to depend on each other. So they decided to travel together to the next kingdom. According to their discussion, the Hare would carry Tortoise on his back and move forward, wherein, the Tortoise would carry while crossing the river. They both liked this plan. Next day, they gathered information from their king and started their journey towards the other kingdom. The Hare was crossing the pathway full of thorns, taking quick strides. The Tortoise was scared to life, so it held the Hare tight. The moment they reached the river, they exchanged the places. The Hare sat on Tortoise back and Tortoise swam through the water quickly. They reached the other kingdom within no time because of this plan. The Hare and Tortoise met the King Lion, and discussed the matter with him. After a long discussion, The Hare and the Tortoise began their return. As they knew the path, they knew how to cross it, so the return journey was easy and quick. The two competitors worked together and finished the work before the time and reached the king. Due to this, all the animals came to know about the value of Helping each other and its benefits. Colour this picture, as per your choice. Colour this picture as per your choice.
author: Deepika shailesh

title: The Book of Stolen Secrets
text: Psst. How do you keep a secret safe? You could whisper it. But someone might overhear you. I hate hunting. I KNEW IT! You could send a secret message. But it could fall into the wrong hands. You could write it in code. But someone might crack the code. You could share it with just your closest friends. But someone might pretend to be a friend to get the information. As long as there have been people, there have been secrets. And as long as there have been secrets, there have been people trying to steal them. When computers and the Internet came along, they made sharing information with other people a lot easier. Unfortunately, this made stealing information easier too! Sometimes, you might not even know you are sharing secret information... …for someone else to find. Sana S Kempegowda International Airport Name: Sana Sheikh Flight from: BLR Flight to: AMS Mobile Number: 0000000000 Email Address: sana.s@zapmail.com Departure: 18:25 Arrival: 6:45 Seat: 14A Information thieves are always looking for new ways to steal secret information. And they can be very sneaky. Enter your bank details and win big! They use stolen information to pretend to be someone they are not, to steal money from bank accounts or commit other kinds of crimes. But don’t worry! The information you share is usually protected in lots of different ways. These protections are called cyber security. Enter your bank details and win big! SCAM! Cyber security analysts and engineers are always studying how information thieves steal information. This helps them find new ways to protect it. CYBER THIEF You can make cyber security experts’ job easier by being careful about sharing personal information online. HOW TO STAY SAFE ONLINE: 1. Don’t share information like your phone number, birth date or home address online. 2. Don’t click on links or emails that promise you an expensive gift or item! 3. Use a password that cannot be easily guessed. 4. Before you upload a photo or post on social media, think about whether you would be OK with your mum, dad or grandma seeing it. If not, don’t post it. 5. Avoid talking to strangers on the Internet. 6. If a stranger tries to talk to you and won’t stop, tell a grown-up you trust.
author: Ashwitha  Jayakumar

title: Sheeru & Deeru's unusual friendship
text: The name 'Sunderbans' is special and casts a magical spell. Enclosed by thick mangrove forests or the "Sundari trees" huge saline mudflats, these forests offer you an experience of witnessing the best of both flora and fauna. The trees that look partially suspended in water are interconnected with water channels. There are small islands all over. The red blazing blooms of Genwa find its match in the yellow blooms of Khalsi making it one spectacular watch for the visitors. Forests are the protector of life. They give fresh air. They provide homes to animals and birds. From simple seed, with mud, water and sun, come all this, the towering gentle tree giants. In the forest, there is a sense of kinship with the flora, of an ancient soul that stretches into everything that lives. It is here under the nascent rays of a sun, the tree born to rise each day. In the canopy animals, birds thrive and live delightfully. The fragrance of wet forest soil, sweet-sour berries here and there, wildflowers, rotten leaves, nuts and mushrooms on the floor, herbs and shrubs all make the forests a beautiful place to reside. Generally, the sun blooms into the sky with a warm yellow glow and the rays fall scattered all over the floor. Mangrove trees throng the place. With their roots submerged in water, they are the only species of trees in the world that can tolerate hot, muddy salty seawater. Many fishes and small water species spend a lifetime in the mangroves. Apart from this; Sunderbans is home to one of the most iconic species - the Royal Bengal tiger. The natural home of a tiger is forest. They have a strong body with brown and black stripes on the fur which makes it very beautiful. They have strong paw and jaw. Their tails are long and slender. In one corner of the forest, a pair of ferocious tigers lived in a cave. One morning, a mother tiger gave birth to a lovely cub. Both the parents' papa tiger and mamma tiger looked at the male cub with pride. They were happy. The cub's half-opened eyes and small paws looked pleasing. Mamma tiger named the cub 'Sheeru' a symbol of strength, courage and dignity. There lived a deer family in another corner of the forest. The stag or papa deer was big and possessed solid antlers. He had brown shiny skin and piercing eyes. Mamma deer or doe was equally pretty and docile. They have a cloven-hoofed or split hoof, typically compact torsos with long, slender legs and small tails. On the same day, when the tigress gave birth to Sheeru, the family was blessed with a male calf. Mamma deer was happy too. Out of sheer happiness, she named him Deeru. By nature, tiger cubs are playful and rather active. They will pounce on one another and chase blowing grasses or even their mother's tail. Sheeru seemed a curious cub. He pulled his father's tail while sleeping. He used to bite it hard. Each day, his mischief's created trouble for his parents. His appetite increased. The mother's milk was insufficient. Sheeru's mother grew anxious with each passing day, as soon, she will have to leave him alone and hunt for food. Papa tiger was worried but left with no other choice. A morning when the sky was red, mamma tiger went in search for food. She advices Sheeru to stay in the cave. Papa tiger is taking care of him. But after some time, he too leaves as hunger kept knocking at his stomach. Sheeru played in the cave. But the walls of the cave couldn't hold him for long. He strayed out and didn't pay heed to his mother's advice. Sheeru played near the cave. Then, his curious nature propelled him to explore. He ran after butterflies. He played with flies. He chased birds. He came too far from his home. And wandering, he reached vast grassland where Deeru and his family were eating grass. As Sheeru is still a baby and small in height not everyone in the herd can see him. Deeru was the first who glanced at the new tiny friend. Deeru peeped from the gap of tall grasses. He saw a strange face looking at him. He is not from the herd. And only two months in this world, Deeru never encountered a hunter. He slowly moved towards him. Sheeru too looks anxious. Suddenly, they came face to face with each other. They both bounced back. Deeru steps closer. He asks Sheeru about his identity. Sheeru looked puzzled. He doesn't know much about himself. He murmurs his name. They leave aside hesitation and jump to play. They play hide and seek. They chase each other. They enjoy splashing water in the nearby water pool. After some time, mamma deer comes searching for Deeru. She gets a shock when she notices him in the company of a tiger cub. She shouts and asks him to stay away from Sheeru. Deeru feels sad. He wants to play more with his new friend. But no one from the herd agrees to it. Sheeru starts crying. He is far away from home and his new friend's family is avoiding him. Deeru comes forward in support of his new friend. He doesn't want to leave him. Now, the deer family is perplexed. Finally, the deer family succumbs to the wishes of Deeru. They allow Sheeru to stay with them until he finds his family. Frightened inside, they move inside deeper parts of the jungle with Sheeru in their herd. Here, when the mamma tiger finds Sheeru missing, she roars like thunder. The entire region shivers in terror. She along with Pappa tiger searches all possible nearby areas, but without any success. Here unaware of his identity, Sheeru becomes best of pals with Deeru. On a bright, sunny day at the forest, they used to hang out, and played their favorite game of tag. They ran zig and zag, trying to get away, in the bushes. Sheeru is faster than Deeru and finally catches him before he can make it to the base at the water fountain. Sheeru saw new faces in the wild - a flying fox, a wild boar, a macaque and a fox. There were elephants and other big cats in the forests. Uncared for surrounding, they roll around with each other in mock fighting positions and leap through the tall grasses energetically. Sheeru eats grass like Deeru. Whenever they splash in the water, small fishes or frogs leap out in fright. One day, a small fish accidently went inside Sheeru's mouth. He spitted it out in disgust. In the company of deers, Sheeru has not grown much big in size. He stayed lean and small. Mamma tiger has grown ferocious in absence of her baby. She kills every animal on her way. She is restless. On a hunting trail, she spots a bunch of monkeys sitting on a big branch. She asks the team leader about spotting any tiger cub in the area. The head looks here and there. After scratching his head he answers, "Oh! A few days back, I saw a cub that looks like you with a deer family on the other side of the forest." This clue was enough for her. She alongwith Pappa tiger ran the whole stretch of forest. They ran for hours and reached the place as told by the head monkey. They hid behind bushes. They couldn't believe their eyes. Sheeru was right in front of their eyes. But he has not grown up to be a strong cub. He is small and undergrown. They observe him eating grass like deers. They trail him to the pond where instead of eating fishes he is playing with them. They thought to confront him. As Sheeru was alone for some time, mamma tiger approaches him. She gets close and hugs him. Sheeru gets frightened. He has forgotten his mother. Mamma tiger reminds him about her. But Sheeru doesn't have any concrete memory. "You are staying with deers? You are a tiger cub. You are built to kill and eat them. They are our food. How will we survive? This is the law of nature. See how small and timid you have grown," Mamma tiger scolds Sheeru. "I don't know who I am. For so many months, I am staying with my friend Deeru. They are so friendly. They never ask me to kill. They eat grass and shrubs. I like them too. Why to kill?" Sheeru argues with his mother. "I will need to teach you in a different way. You won't listen. You have forgotten who you are? I will come back soon…" Mamma grunts angrily. Sheeru is shaken in fear. How can he tell this chance meeting to his friend? They will be frightened too. So, he promises to keep this meeting a secret. After a week, the deer family along with Sheeru was returning into their home. As they were nearing home, Papa deer hears the cracking of twigs and leaves underfoot. A smell of beast hovers in the air. No clue of what is ahead! Clutching his fear tightly, he keeps moving forward with the herd members. Voices are coming nearer. All of a sudden, a big tigress attacks the Papa deer from behind. The tigress grips his neck tightly just about to kill. Deeru and Sheeru stood petrified. Others ran in panic. The mamma deer requests and pleads the tigress to leave his husband. Deeru too pleads with tears. The tigress loosens the grip and allows the Papa deer to breathe. "I will spare your husband's life. But in return…promise me that you will order Sheeru to leave your herd. Explain to him that he belongs to the breed of hunters. He will not grow big and strong and rule the forest if he eats grass instead of meat," Mamma tiger roars in terror. Deeru understands. He requests Sheeru to abide by his mothers' wish. The entire deer family begs him to leave. "I will listen to you, mother. But in return, you have to promise me that I will remain life-long friends with Deeru. I will hunt but never prey on Deeru's family. We will remain best of friends," Sheeru pleads with teary eyes. "I promise. You two will remain best of friends," Mamma tiger promises. And the two friends walked out separately into their lives. Whenever they crossed their paths in the forests, as promised, they remained best of friends.
author: Madhumita Mandal

title: The Dividing Lines
text: Last night’s dream was quite remarkable what I saw was beyond the thinkable all those lines on the globe… the dark lines, the black lines the thick lines, the long lines the deep lines and the dividing lines the lines that… separate them and us just began to melt away lines disappeared without a fuss as if magically erased away The soldiers carrying guns and mace standing stern face to face were stunned like a peculiar case they threw their guns off and burst into loud laughter suddenly there was no enemy race People burst out with joy happiness swept across the lands the lines had given way… to festive celebrations on every side where bombs had once been the routine laughter erupted in directions unseen who belonged where was hard to decide ‘Kislaya Uncle’ no longer understood the divide Some leaders were in a commotion others got going with agitation how wars could now be fought? how would they ever win an election? In they brought a map again hastily and got a box of black ink quickly They again started drawing the lines the dark lines, the black lines the thick lines, the long lines the deep lines and the dividing lines But hardly did they know what lay ahead love, when it touches the human kind harmony and friendship occupy the mind warm hugs can even move the dead Nobody can draw the lines anymore colours will fade the ink quickly away and it will not hold its place therefore!

title: Chiku's Bravery
text: She is neither fat nor thin and neither tall nor short. She is thrifty with her words and a very quiet girl. She plays very little and speaks up regarding injustice. She does not swim in the pool. She does not climb trees. She does not throw peanut skin. She doesn't roam near the market. Once, there was a storm and the electricity stopped. The people were scared of literally everything! But, Chiku took charge and lit the lamp. She told many stories and sang many songs. Everybody started feeling happy because of Chiku's courage.
