title: Thank God its Funday
text: It was a clear night, the sky glittering with stars. Sophie was in bed reading her favorite book of bedtime stories. In between turning pages, she occasionally gazed up at the sky through the window, thinking of another week of school and routine. Today was a Sunday, full of activities followed by an evening visit to the market to stock up for the week that lay ahead. In some time, she said her prayers and dozed off to sleep. As the alarm rang, Sophie and her little brother Lionel woke up rubbing their eyes It was Monday morning and the children had to get ready for another week of school, studies and homework, hobby classes, and other routine activities. Mum was already up, preparing their breakfast and tiffin, and arranging their uniforms. Soon, the school bus would be honking outside their compound. Tuesday arrived, and the routine was pretty much the same as Monday. Children would wake up, get dressed, pack their bags, gulp breakfast and whoosh... off to school. After classes, the school bus will drop them at the Day care, and rest of the day will continue. In the evening, parents will pick them up on the way back from work. Once at home, get fresh, have dinner and off to sleep... zzzzz... zzzzzz... zzzzzz. Only to wake up next day to repeat the cycle. Today was Wednesday and Sophie thought "Wow, its mid-week already!" But, as her parents reminded her of the routine school/day care tasks, she started thinking, "Will I ever get sometime to think of my favorite things on these weekdays?" As the thought kept popping up in her head, she realized that she would have to find a way to solve this problem. All through rest of the week, Sophie kept thinking if 'time' could be re-calculated to keep some of it only for oneself. With a new sunrise, Thursday arrived. Sophie was happy that weekend was nearing. But otherwise, it was just another regular day. Again the thought appeared, "Why everyday would I have to attend school, do routine activities, but get no time to think the way I like, and do as I like?" With the issue bothering her to no end, Friday dawned. Sophie heaved a sigh of relief, "Wow, it's the weekend, finally!" Sophie woke up a little late than usual, as it was a Saturday morning. Weekend at last! Sophie was very happy but immediately after she had a relaxed breakfast, she realized she had to rush to art class. And thereafter come home, eat lunch, go for swimming in the afternoon, then visit the library and finally, return home. By 9 pm, Sophie started feeling very sleepy.Before dozing off, she asked her mom, 'Won't I never get to play as I like?' Mom said nothing in return but kissed her and Lionel good night and her dad whispered in her ears, 'My dear daughter, sweet dreams!' After a relaxing sleep, Sophie woke up next day with a feeling of 'thrill'. She was thinking to herself..."Today is going to be special!" But alas, Sunday turned out to be just another day of routine activities with a pre-planned schedule. Finally as Sunday got over, with a visit to grandparents in the morning, swimming in the late afternoon followed by shopping essentials for the week ahead, it struck her that throughout the week, she did not get a single day to call her "own"! A day when she will not be questioned as to what she is doing, when she would not have to follow a "routine", when her mind can wander free wherever it wants... ﻿ S ophie had little sleep that night. She lay awake, wondering how could she find a solution, till her thoughts made her weary and exhausted. Finally, as rays of the morning sun brightened up her room, a bright idea came to her mind. Sophie collected her thoughts and finally announced, "No school, daycare, or activity class today! Let this be the 8th day in the week called 'FUNDAY' where we will do whatever we want... let children play to their hearts' content on this day!" Her parents were initially startled at such an idea, and tried to persuade the girl to dismiss the thought. But as they listened to their daughter who spoke her mind and gave reasons behind her idea, they started realizing how children felt at being subject to such routine, day after day. They agreed to give the day entirely to Sophie and her brother. They thought to themselves... indeed this idea never crossed our mind that all of us need a day for ourselves. A little girl made us realize this today. Yaay! Sophie is relaxed and happy and so are all at home. She and her brother spent the day on their own terms and were overjoyed!
author: Sunandini Sen

title: THE COW WHO LAUGHED
text: “Rukku, see what I have got for you!” Kishan shouted. Rukmini, who was in the kitchen, came out. Her husband was standing in front of their house holding a rope at the end of which was a cream coloured cow. “This beautiful creature, whose name is Gowri, is a gift for you. “Where did you get her?” “I bought her in the village fair for R48,000.” Suddenly they heard a funny sound. “Did you hear someone laughing?” Kishan asked. “I thought I did. But there is no one here. We must have imagined it.” “As I was saying, I paid R48,000...” Once again there was a sound of laughter; this time it was loud and clear. “Moo-ha...Moo-haha...Moo-hahaha!” Rukmini caught Kishan’s hand and shook it roughly. “Ki…Ki…Kishan. It was Gowri who was laughing.” “Have you gone mad? Who ever heard of a laughing cow?” Rukmini was suspicious. Her eyes were still on Gowri when she asked Kishan, “Where did you get so much money from?” “I have been saving for more than a year,” Kishan replied. “Moo-ha...Moo-haha...Moo-hahaha!” Kishan and his wife looked at Gowri and then at each other, their jaws dropping in surprise. Gowri’s lips were drawn back, her large milky white teeth were bared, and she was shaking with laughter: “Moo-ha...Moo-haha...Moo-hahaha!” Inopportune moments “How can a cow laugh?” Kishan’s neighbour Rahim asked in disbelief. “I’ll prove it. Come, let us go to the cowshed.” Gowri was standing chewing cud when the two walked in. Kishan told Gowri three jokes. Gowri looked at him without blinking an eyelid and continued chewing cud. “Kishan, I told you cows don’t laugh. Are you trying to make a fool of me?” Rahim stomped off in anger. * * * One day, the farmer couple was in the cowshed feeding the animals when Birju Lala, a politician everyone hated, walked in. “Kishan, I have decided to contest for the post of sarpanch in the Panchayat elections.” “That is nice,” said Kishan without looking up. “Both of you must please vote for me. I will work 24 hours a day and make our village the most prosperous in the country.” As he waited with folded hands for Kishan to respond, Birju Lala heard a funny sound. “Moo-ha, Moo-haha, Moo-hahaha!” Birju Lala looked at Kishan, his eyes turning red in anger. “You don’t believe me!” he thundered. “Of course, I do.” “Then why are you laughing at me?” “I didn’t!” “Then it must be your wife?” “Lalaji, why will I laugh at you?” Rukmini asked. “Then who laughed? There is no one else here.” “Lalaji, sometimes my cow Gowri laughs.” Birju Lala’s face turned red, matching the colour of his eyes. “Do you take me for a fool? I won’t spare you, Kishan. First, you laugh at me and then, tell me a cock and bull — or rather a cock and cow — story about a laughing bovine!” With these words he stomped out. Kishan looked carefully at Gowri who was staring at them poker faced. * * * Rukmini was deep in thought. Suddenly, and idea came to her. Unlike Kishan, she was a sharp lady. She was sure her surmise was right. “Kishan,”she called out, “that day when you told me you paid R48,000 for Gowri, you were lying, weren’t you?” Kishan, caught off guard, could only stammer. “H..h..how do you know — I mean what makes you think that?” “Every time someone lies, Gowri laughs.” “I sold the necklace your mother gave you for R48,000, bought Gowri for R33,000 and the rest of the money I gambled away,” Kishan said, hanging his head in shame. Gowri’s ability to catch a lie, and laugh when she did, became the talk of the region. Every time there was an election, candidates would be asked to make their speeches with Gowri in attendance. If Gowri laughed their fate was sealed. When marriages were solemnised, the bride and the groom were asked to repeat their vows in front of Gowri. If they passed the Gowri test, they were allowed to go ahead. Gowri soon became a celebrity and in her shadow, Rukmini and Kishan also became famous. One day, the correspondent of an international magazine asked Kishan, “Did Gowri’s unique ability ever get you into trouble with your wife?” “No, of course not!” he shot back. “Moo-ha, Moo-haha, Moo-hahaha!” laughed Gowri, who was standing right beside him!
author: Ramendra Kumar

title: When Mr.Rabbit cooked!
text: I have been eating raw carrots so far... "Let me cook and eat it. " "How do I cook?" "Let me ask for help in this house" But, there was a dog that started barking. He also chased the rabbit. "Oh dear! What do I do now?" thought the rabbit. He kept the carrots in the sun. The carrots didn't cook. He cooked the carrots in the fire. The carrots became too bitter! "How do I cook and eat this? " Thought the rabbit furiously to himself. He found a tortoise shell. He gathered twigs. He also found stones! The rabbit lit the stove. He also invited his friends to eat. Everybody enjoyed eating the finely cooked carrots!
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: A Different Kind Of Sambar!
text: How does one make that? " " i shall cook and show you" said Bhavya. "We can take purple onions and dark-blue brinjals. We must cut these into small pieces using a knife. We must then take green long drumsticks, yellow toor-dhal, orange carrots, and juicy red tomatoes. We must rinse all of these,cut them and put them in a vessel. We should also add some brown colored tamarind water. Yellow-colored sambar powder and salt must be added. All of this must be cooked. Stir it gently. Boil the gravy in mild heat for sometime. This is now one makes Rainbow Sambar!"Bhavya told her Paati.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: My Ball
text: Once a time I bought a ball, from a big mall! But one day my ball fell down the cliff, I wanted to save it but my neck was stiff! Half side of the ball was blue, oh god just give me a clue! Other side of the ball was red, same of the birthmark on my head! Then suddenly somebody came, in front of my eyes, and it turned out to be,my best friend eating pies! The he gave me my ball and said thank you, and ran away till his wild cat said mew!
author: Varad Kandewad

title: Wonderland
text: "WOW! Look at that magnificent structure! Those tall buildings, the flowers, and the trees are so amazing. I wish I were the one sitting on top of those things!" said Maya. I am so happy and exited today! Hi my name is Maya, I am a kid who loves to play. I am pretty sure that all of you kids do too! I am also fascinated by tall buildings, flowers, and animals. I mean aren't they all so beautiful? I also love to play with my friends. They are so nice to me and I have so many friends. In my school all my friends know me as the "Wonder girl," it is because I always wonder about things. Right now I am with my mom walking down the joyful street of our neighborhood. Here everyone is kind to each other. We come here for a walk everyday! It lets us enjoy the happiness of life. A few days later Maya and her family decide to go to the nearby city in which they were going to explore the mall. So the next day they went to the mall. "When we went to the mall, we were shocked!" said Maya. There were so many people there. And when I said so many, I meant it! This was my dream, I had always wanted to see a mall very crowded. The reason behind that is it was such a friendly place! After we mall explore the mall we came outside we were surprised to see that there was a rainbow! Everyone was taking photos of the enormous and beautiful rainbow that was shining above us,I have to admit that it the best rainbow ever! It was so far the best day of my life. I had seen so many things that I loved! The only thing that was yet to be seen were the beautiful flowers, trees and animals. As soon as I said that my parents decided to take us to the zoo right away, I was like... THANK YOU! If I were to see the zoo as well then it would officially be the best day of my life! We saw the zoo and it was amazing. The birds chirping and the tall trees letting us breathe fresh air and so much more. Today is confirmed as a day in my "Wonderland!"
author: Raghusamartha Harish
illustrator: Dỗ Thái Thanh; Mango  Tree; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Nguyễn  Minh Hải; Niyati Makkithaya; Nyambura Kariuki; Offei Tettey  Eugene; Sanjay Sarkar; Shamim Ahmed; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Family and Friends
text: My name is Raman. I am 8 years old, I love to play! I have a family of 3 people. My father is a mechanic, he works a lot! I help him sometime by going to his shop! My mother is a Housewife, she does a lot of work also. I also help my mother with her chores. Once again, I am Raman I love to play and hang out with my family. They are the best. My grandpa and grandma live in their houses in Kerala, I live in Chennai with my mom and dad. I also have a lot of friends, in my school everyone is my friend. I like to play sports with my friends. Me and my parents go to places every week, it is so fun. Last week we went to a movie theater and watched a movie. I love my Family and Friends, they are the best!

title: Chanchal and Nirmala - The Vegetables
text: Chanchal, the naughty girl and Nirmala, the cow are best friends. On a Monday morning, they go to the market. So many vegetables are there! MOO! Some potatoes and tomatoes, you must have seen Lady fingers and spinach, oh so green! A carrot and a radish, thin and long. Cauliflower and cabbage, round and round! Chanchal and Nirmala buy them all! So many dishes they can make! Oh so good all of them taste! Tomato Potato Spinach Lady Finger Cauliflower Cabbage Carrot Radish
author: Shubhangini Dhall

title: Everyone, Follow Gappu's Moves!
text: Gappu had raised her right hand. Gappu can't dance! "Taka Taka Pap Pap Pum!" " Everyone, please run around the room fast " Komal miss told the class. Oh dear! Gappu is running slowly! Gappu can't dance. "Thaka Thina Thin Tak. Everybody jump high" Oh dear! Gappu is sitting down. Gappu can't dance. "Thupi Thuup Thitli Thin Thin Everybody, bend your right leg inwards. " "Oh dear! Gappu is lifting her leg in the opposite direction! Gappu can't dance. Everyone noticed that Gappu was dancing incorrectly and started laughing at her. But, Komal miss knew the way to deal with the situation. " Everybody, follow Gappu's moves" Komal miss said. "Thaka thimi thai. Some hands can move down, some hands can move up. Thaka Thaka Pap Pap Puum. Some run around the room fast, some run around the room slow. Thakka thina thin tak. It doesn't matter whether you sit or jump! Thop Thop Thaka Thin Thin Everyone dance together. That's all that matters!" Gappu can dance! And you can dance too!
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: The Birthday Plant
text: Today is my birthday. I have turned five years old. Now I reach upto father's waist. And can glance down from the terrace wall. I can take out and eat candies hidden by mummy in the upper shelf of the refrigerator. Now I can reach the kitchen shelf. And can wash my hands in the bathroom sink without using a footstool. Today mummy has baked a cake for me. And has prepared lots of ice-cream too. Mummy has prepared rasgullas and samosas as well. But I will get to eat all these in the evening when all my friends will arrive. All my friends have arrived at home. They have brought various presents for me. Aanvi has gifted me a doll and Aryan has brought a football for me. Mummy papa have also brought lots of toys and clothes for me. Now is the time to cut the cake. Just then the doorbell rings. Gardener uncle is there at the door. He takes care of the plants of our block. Looking at all the children he says, "it seems today is little Mishthi's birthday." Mummy calls gardener uncle inside the house and offers him a slice of the birthday cake. Gardener uncle smiles and heads outside. He brings a beautiful plant from his cart. He hands over the plant to me and says,"for your birthday, Mishthi." I smile happily and say thanks to gardener uncle. I tell gardener uncle, "this is my best birthday gift. I will take good care of my birthday plant." A big smile spreads on gardener uncle's face.
author: ASHIMA KHANNA

title: Joe, the brave bird
text: One day in a forest, there lived a bird named Jill. Jill had a son named Joe, Joe was a young bird and he was at the ripe age for flying.But Joe was too scared to fly, so Joe stayed in the nest. (three weeks before) Joe the bird was scared of flying because the one time he tried to fly he fell out of the nest and hit his head, and since then Joe was scared of flying and Jill would try to get him to fly. But Joe always stayed put and never leaved the nest. One day he went to his friend, the Ant, he asked his friend," Ant; do you think flying is a good thing?" Ant replied,"I have never tried to fly and I never will! My uncle, Don, tried flying once and he broke his Leg!" Joe thought that flying must be a bad thing. He did not want to break his leg so he said " I will never fly again!" The next day he asked his friend, the Hen, the same thing " Hen; is flying a fun thing to do?" H en said, "I have never tried to fly and I never will! I heard that flying will hurt your wings!" Joe did not want to hurt his wings so he decided that he will never try to fly again! The next day Joe asked the wise duck the same thing he asked the others " Duck; Is flying a fun thing to do?" Duck thought about it for a moment and said to the curious bird, " Joe I think that flying is very fun and I think you should try it to!"said Duck. Joe thought about flying and said to the wise duck, "Duck, I think I will try to fly!" He told his Mother that he wanted to try flying, and his mom was glad to help her son fly. After a few tries Joe got the hang of it and he was never scared of flying since then. Joe showed all of his friends that he could fly and all of them were amazed! " I cannot believe it.", said Hen "wow!", said Ant and Duck said nothing, because he knew Joe could do it all along he just needed to believe in himself The end
author: Brahan  Eashwer
illustrator: R. C. Pradeep Kumar; Tanvi Bhat

title: Timbu, The Lonely Tree
text: In the country of India, there was a small village called Tenalipuram. The people of Tenalipurem were proud of their beautiful trees. All the trees stood in bunches, Except for the lonely tree, Timbu. It is not really happy. It is sad. Timbu was planted alone. There were some plants next to him, but Timbu thought he was better than them. One day, Timbu heard the village Patti say a story. Timbu also listened for he was bored. It was about a tree like Timbu and some plants. The tree in the story found out that everyone is equal and treated all the plants equal. Timbu had a great idea to make friends. He makes friends with the plants! Now Timbu has friends, Best Friends!
author: Keerthi Lakshmi Narayanan
illustrator: Aditi Dilip; Jesse  Breytenbach; Ketan Raut; Lavanya Karthik; Sam  van Riet; Sarah Bouwer; Shadrach Munene; Srikrishna Kedilaya

title: The elephant and the mice
text: There was and elephant. He was very thirsty because his town became dry and there was no water left! He thought, "I will go to another village in search of water." He walked down the road and reached Mousterville where lots and lots of mice lived. Mice even came below his huge feet and died. He went to the mouse queen, Mousatoria, and told her about this problem. She told her to find water in another village and also said that she would help him if needed because he was honest. The elephant found a village with water but hunters trapped him in a net. He trumpeted loudly and his sound reached Mousatoria. She sent her mice for help and the mice cut the net and set him free! The elephant went to Mousatoria and thanked her smiling!
author: Prisha Mehta
illustrator: Katrin Coetzer; M. L. Sudesh  Kumara; Nilesh Gehlot; Raju Babu Shakya; Rob Owen; Siddhi   Vartak

title: Playing with Breakfast!
text: Dosa like a handkerchief. You can be certain that the little girl is Uma. Everybody says that Uma is a very good girl. It is very true. Uma is a good girl. In spite of her good qualities, Uma has a very bad habit. Uma loves playing with her breakfast. She cleverly hides her breakfast somewhere or other when her mother is not watching. That is how the Dosa became a handkerchief. She wrapped it in the shape of a triangle and pinned it in her uniform. If her mother makes Vada for her breakfast, she wears it in her fingers like a ring. She wears Vada rings in many of her fingers and walks like a queen. She doesn't like Bondas. She hides it in between her teeth and her cheeks bulge like a fourth-standard girl. With that, she bids her mother goodbye. Uma's mother is a very good cook. She is popular in her colony for her Idlis. But, Uma doesn't care about her mother's cooking. She takes the idlis, puts it in her pocket and uses it like a bed to sit on it during bus travel. Uthapam becomes her hat. She serves Pongal to Malligai, her cat. No magic can make her eat breakfast. But today, she had a problem. Amma has given mashed Upma in a plate for her. What will Uma do today? She can't use it like a handkerchief. She can't put it like a ring. She can't keep Upma in her mouth because it will melt. It won't work if she uses it like a bed. Wearing it like a hat is not possible because Upma will fall. She can't feed Malligai because everyone knows that Malligai hates Upma. Having a dearth of ideas, she finally ended up eating a spoon of Upma. Wow! There is something delicious inside her mouth. Is it the cashew nut that is salted and sauteed in ghee? In order to eat another cashew nut, she ate another spoon of Upma. Now, she found a piece of tasty carrot! Yumm! She ate another spoon of Upma because she was now curious to taste the next mystery item. Now, there is a hard and a sour small piece of ginger! Uma couldn't contain her curiosity. She continued to eat Upma. Suddenly she yelled because she bit a green chilly. In order to take away the spice, Uma ate all the Upma that was there in the plate. The spice ended finally. That is not the only thing. Her plate was empty as well! "Uma, where is the breakfast that was on your plate in the morning?" asked Amma. "It is inside my stomach!" laughed Uma. Nowadays, Uma doesn't play with her breakfast. She has become a very good girl. Everyone was happy seeing this change. Except one creature! Her cat, Malligai! If you see her, give her some Pongal to eat, okay?
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Me and My Family
text: I dedicate this book to my friend Ardi. Hello`! I am Anna. I am a college student. I study philosophy. I like philosophy. I am an American. My birthday is on April 8th. I have a sister and three brothers. Yes, I have a lot of siblings! I have a father and a mother. My two brothers are not a college student. One of my brother is a college student. My sister is a graduate student. My mother is very pretty. And my father works hard. And this is my family and me. Author Bio: My name is Anna Henry. I am an American. I am a student at Kennesaw State University. I study philosophy. I am a freshman. I love poems. I have a cat. The name of my cat is Sam.

title: I am big!
text: I am Maya. I am 4 years old. Yes! 4 years! Everybody tell me that I am small but 4 years is BIG. " Maya darling! Let me carry you little girl." Baba says. I am angry. " Baba! I am a BIG girl" I say. " Maya! Those clothes are too big for you. You are small for them." I am angry. " Mama! I am a BIG girl." I take the scissors to cut paper. Mama comes and snatches it from me. She says " Maya! You are little! You will hurt yourself." I am angry. " Mama! I am a BIG girl. Not little." I run to get my bike. Then I see Rahul's bike. I go and sit on that. Baba stops me and says " Maya! You are young to ride your brother's bike. Take yours please." I am angry. " Baba! I am a BIG girl!" Mama and me went to the flower store. Mama was holding my hand. Mama says " Maya. Do not leave my hand. You are little." I am angry. " Maaaaaammmmmmaaaaaaa! I am a BIG girl!" This is not fair! I am too small to wear mama's dresses. I am too small to cut paper with scissors. I am too small to ride Rahul's bike and I am too small to walk by myself. I am BIG! I yell. Then Baba says " Maya. If you are big, then you can go to school. I will send you to school tomorrow." I am scared. " Baba. I am not big enough to go to school. I am too small" Mama and Baba laughed. The said together. " Maya. You said that you were big." I glance at Mama and say. " Mama. You were right. I am small. But after I am big, I will do things big people do."
author: Niyati Makkithaya
illustrator: Jayesh Sivan; Mayur Mistry; Nandhini Chandrasekaran; Nicci  Nathanson; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Shanta  Hitang; Tawfiq Ahmed  Anwar; Zainab Tambawalla

title: My Walk With My Aunt
text: I love walking. I love walking especially with my aunt. I love it when my aunt holds my hands. I love it when my aunt lets go of my hand as well. We don't walk fast. We stop and we say hello to a dog, to a cat, to a mouse, to a crow and to a tree. My aunt loves collecting flowers from the street. I love collecting stones from the street. I love collecting all kinds of stones: big ones, small ones, round ones and flat ones. But, the best kind of stones are the smallest ones. The stones that can almost disappear when I put them in my pocket. My pockets get filled with stones after I finish my walk with my aunt. My grandmother gave me a pod of peas from her basket,today. Dilip anna gave me a clip from his magical shop. Nirmal akka gave me this sticker because I waited patiently. Anjum aunty gave me a button from her jar of buttons. After coming home, I took everything out of my pocket and put it in my yellow jar. In case I find a small stone in my pocket, I will give it to my aunt.
author: Priyadarshini Sivakumar

title: Why does Mira have an itch
text: He had just raised his hand that Bablu shouted, 'Mummy, didi is itching'. 'Come Meera and work.' 'But mother I am itching.' 'Quiet itch stool!' Said the mother laughing. Bablu too started laughing loudly. Meera left her face hanging. Poor thing too. Nobody believed her words Mother had filmed the entire head, but not a single head had come out. Pulling a lot of hair from that fine-toothed comb did not work. She also brought a shampoo to remove rashi. But there was Russian. Lemon, right, oil - everything was seen. There was no difference. If she pays attention to Bablu, she might not like it. ' "Yes it will," said the mother. ' No mother. I really itch. ”Meera said. If it happens, let's go to the doctor. They put big needles. 'Mother replied. ' No no. Do not inject I will not itch anymore. ”Meera said crying. Mother gave Bablu the task of keeping an eye on Meera. Bablu was no less than any detective. Kept running after meera 'Mother's Spoon,' Meera screams But what would she do if she used to get itchy. It was very difficult. Baba also used to listen to the mother. I could not understand what stories were telling my heart. Immersed in this thought, one day she started crying in class. The teacher was shocked when she saw it. Calling him separately asked the reason for crying.. 'I don't need a needle teacher. But what should I do with itching? ' That evening, the teacher reached Meera's house. She was accompanied by Doctor Madam. The teacher told Meera's mother, 'Today the doctor saw the children in school. But how did Mira and Bablu miss out? That's why doctors have come to see them. ' The doctor looked at the two children and said, 'Hey! Meera is allergic. Doesn't it itch? ' 'G. It keeps itching all day. 'Mother immediately replied. Meera started crying. 'I don't need a needle.' Needle not merry. I'll just give medicine. You will get well soon. ”The doctor said. 'Sometimes we do not believe in children. This can make things worse. 'Teacher explained to the mother. Mother immediately embraced Meera and started turning her hand. Then Bablu shouted, ‘Mother. You are itching for Sister. ”Hearing this, everyone laughed out loud

title: Arun in Ruins
text: Arun inspected the statue in the abandoned palace. He plucked the jewel out of the statue’s forehead. His pet skink, Arunachalam, hung on tight. Gadagadagadagada! The pillars began to shake. Radaradaradarada! The walls shivered. Karaak! The floor cracked. The door behind him closed with a DHUD! “How dare you take my pottu?” boomed a voice from the statue. “Give it back to me.” Arun was so scared that his arms and legs turned to semiya. The jewel slipped out of his fist and shattered into many pieces. “The light from that jewel held the door open,” the statue said. “The jewel will take years to grow back. Now you can never leave.” Arun looked at the broken jewel in panic. “There must be some other way.” “There is one other way, but you must hurry.” The statue closed its eyes. “Wake up!” Arun punched the statue’s chest, scattering centuries of dust into the air. “Look, Arunachalam, there’s a note here! It says that to open the door, we have to complete the circuit. Here’s what we need: The hair of a current creature to power the circuit, A hair clip from the resisters to control the current flow, A jewel from the upstairs place to emit light And feathers from a wirebird to connect everything together. I wonder what a current creature looks like. I bet it’s small and fuzzy!” Suddenly Arun heard growling behind him. It was the current creature, ice blue with anger. It was neither small nor fuzzy. “Good doggie! Nice doggie!” Arun stammered. Then he swiftly plucked a hair from the creature’s eyebrow. “Raar raar raar raar raar raar raar!” the current creature snarled, ready to pounce. “HELP!” Arun cried. Three girls appeared out of nowhere and swatted the creature’s nose. “Arf-arf!” The current creature lowered its tail and ran away. “Thanks a lot!” Arun said, to the girls. “But why are you so tall?” “Er,” they replied “Why are you so short?” “I don’t have time to waste,” Arun rolled his eyes. “I need to find the resisters.” The girls laughed. “We are the resisters.” “Oh!” Arun smiled. “Can I have your hair clip please?” “You can have it if you can reach it.” Arun hopped and jumped and leaped. But he was still too short to reach their heads. “I’m sorry for calling you too tall!” Arun said, out of breath. The sisters grinned and handed Arun one hair clip. He thanked them, and then asked, “Is that the upstairs place?” “The upstairs place! You mustn’t go there,” said the resisters. “The wirebird pecks anyone who goes there.” “A bird?” Arun laughed, “I’m not afraid of a silly bird.” Arun and Arunachalam climbed up to the jewels around the wirebird’s nest. Arun grabbed a jewel but dropped it to catch a baby wirebird that had wandered too close to the edge. “Ka kaaaaa!” The mother wirebird swooped down and grabbed Arun by the shoulder. “Put me down!” Arun yelled, clutching a clump of the bird’s feathers. “I was helping.” The wirebird dropped him. “Argh! I can’t believe we lost the jewel!” Arun said. “Click… click… click…” Arunachalam grinned. The jewel in his mouth sparkled. They ran past the upstairs place, past the three resisters and past the current creature. At last they were in front of the statue. Arun pinned the jewel to the statue’s chest. He fixed the resisters’ hair clip under the jewel. He peeled out two wires from the wirebird’s feather. He pinned one under the jewel and the other next to the hair clip. “Why isn’t the light turning on?” Then, all at once, he remembered. He touched the hair of the current creature to the open wire. FLASH! It was the brightest light Arun had ever seen. The palace door swung open. “We did it! The statue is going to reward us!” “GET OUT!” the statue roared. Arun and Arunachalam dived out the door. Gadagadagadagada! The pillars began to shake. Radaradaradarada! The palace walls trembled. Kaaaarrraaaaaaak! The palace crumbled into ruins. “No one’s going to believe what happened, Arunachalam,” Arun said. “We don’t have a single jewel!” “Click… click… click…” Arunachalam smirked. The jewel in his mouth sparkled. What is an electronic circuit? An electronic circuit is a path through which an electric current can flow. It has components such as a battery, resistors and LEDs that are connected by wires. Electronic circuits are built to do certain tasks, for example, the task of an LED circuit is to make the LED glow. To make your own LED circuit, you will need: 1. An LED (light emitting diode) An electronic component that produces light when current flows through it. 2. A resistor An electronic component used to reduce the flow of current. 3. Two wires Wires are metal threads covered with plastic, used to carry the electric current. 4. A nine-volt battery The component that supplies power to the circuit. 5. A breadboard A platform upon which to build the circuit. Build your own electronic circuit Note: Make sure you have an adult or teacher around when you are trying out this experiment. Step 1 Fix the LED to the breadboard. Step 2 Pin the resistor to the long leg of the LED. Step 3 Pin one wire next to the short leg of the LED and one wire right next to the resistor. Step 4 Connect the wire next to the short leg of the LED to the negative side of the battery. Step 5 Connect the wire next to the resistor to the positive side of the battery. Step 6 When the light turns on, your electronic circuit is complete!
author: C G Salamander

title: Pica the Pig
text: Pica the pig It was a great day for Pica the pig. Playing with his friends in the mud,getting all dirty seemed like great fun to him Oh oh,it was go go time for Pica.Pica went and took a bath looking all pink and clean Until next time Pica and friends!

title: I should do something.
text: I do something? Should I throw a ball? Should I fondle my little brother? Should I play drummer? Should I do cycling? Should I wear my new frock? Should I untangle wool ball? Should i water the plants? Should I feed grass to billy? Or should I draw? Should I fly a kite? Should I laugh aloud?
author: Rita Bansal

title: Lonwabo's Recipes
text: Lonwabo was a ten-year-old boy. He lived with his mother and grandmother. Lonwabo’s grandmother had the most beautiful and rich vegetable garden. He enjoyed helping his grandmother weed the garden and water the vegetables. He had to fetch water from the river. He was not a lazy boy. He would walk down the hill and up again. He would pass his friends playing soccer and they would laugh out loud and say to him, “Lonwabo why do you do that? That is a girl’s job, we would never do that.” Lonwabo laughed them off and continued with his journey. He would think about all the happy times with his grandmother in the garden. These thoughts made him forget about the long journey and about his friends’ comments. He liked guessing how many carrots would be in each bunch before his grandmother pulled them out of the ground. Lonwabo’s grandmother always prepared lunch for him, while he was at school and his mother was at work. Every day he came home to find his food already prepared and left out on the table for him. Immediately after taking off his school uniform, he sat at the table, said a little prayer and began to eat. His grandmother prepared all kinds of meals for their lunches. He loved his grandmother’s tasty meals. When he finished eating, he would wash his dish, take a book and pencil and go and sit next to his grandmother. He asked her about the ingredients in the meal he had just eaten and carefully wrote down every little detail. He told himself that when grows up, he is going to open his own restaurant. He will name the restaurant after his grandmother and make all the meals that his grandmother makes for him.
author: Mihlali Kumalo

title: Anny & Che
text: Out there in a small town,there lived an aniyathi and a chechi.They were always together loving one another so heartfully.They were so bound together that everybody felt they were born for each other,even they themselves believed it to be so.Chechi called aniyathi 'anny' and aniyathi called chechi 'che'! note:'aniyathi' means younger sister and 'chechi' means elder sister They dreamt together,they played together and they went places together.They always had their hands put upon each others' shoulders. They grew up together laughing, crying, fighting and loving. They were the best friends of all and were the happiest of all sisters. Anny and Che, though studying in different grades loved to learn together.They read stories and poems together and even did maths sums together.Their amma and achan guided and supported them.They came to know that words were pearls of wisdom which would make the world a better place. Music was also one of their greatest passions.They sang together,appreciating and mentoring each other.They motivated one another to perform well on stage.Anny knew che and che, in turn, knew anny more than anybody else.One was incomplete without the other. One day it was heavily raining outside.The sound of raindrops knocking at the window awakened anny and che.With the cool shower outside,they had not felt like taking the blankets off.However, they could not miss their rare rainy play-time that day. As they started making big and small boats out of old newspapers.Their kitty hid her face mewing in anger as she could not join them for fear of getting wet in the rain.Rain was always a danger signal for anny's Kinginimuthu and che's Tinkerbell.Perhaps the most recent tug-of-war between them should have been over the name of the kitty.Ironically, the kitty was unresponsive to both the names! Rainwater flowing through the front yard smoothly carried their beautiful boats forward. Anny and che felt delighted to see their boats sail in sweet friendship.Just as their captains, the ships moved together in harmony.The sisters remembered the words they had read: 'If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together.' As the rainbow smiled over the earth dipping their clothes in vibrant hues, both anny and che expressed their own wishes to the Sky-God which they did not even share with each other as it is said that wishes won't be fulfilled if disclosed to someone.The Sky-God blessed them, being the only one to know that they had wished for the same'To be loving sisters forever'!
author: Gauripriya M R
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Biplob Chakroborty; Chaaya Prabhat; Siraj Saxena; Suvidha Mistry

title: Laila And Her Balanced Diet
text: Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Laila. She used to eat a lot of junk food. As she eats a lot of junk food her stomach began to grow big. She started to put on weight. One day her mother Aysha called Laila into her room. Her mother said, " I want to talk to u Laila". Laila said "okay mama". Her mother said "you're putting on weight Laila. Its because you're eating a lot of junk food. I think u shouldn't eat junk food anymore. You should eat the right amount of healthy food. Laila asked, " but how??". Her mother replied, " by using balanced diet". Laila again asked, "What is a balanced diet?". Her mother said " a diet consisting of a variety of different types of food and providing adequate amounts of the nutrients necessary for good health is known as a balanced diet. "Ok mama, from the next day onwards I will start my balanced diet", said Laila. Like how Laila said she started her balanced diet. A few months passed by. There were a lot of changes in Laila. She became thin and slim. Her mother was surprised to see her. She said" Laila you have changed a lot u look thin and slim. Laila said " yes mama, I know, I have become thin slim."Its because I took diet seriously. 'Yes Laila, your right", said her mother." from now on I will eat only healthy food, Laila said. "Good job my dear ", said her mother, and they lived happily ever after.
author: fathima  nawal

title: The Lazy Ant
text: It was summer time and most of the ants in Ant City were collecting food. But Lazy Ant was lying on his back on top of a rock basking in the sun. As Lazy Ant’s mother and sisters were busy collecting food, he just glanced at them, whistling and waiting for them to fi nish. But when it was time to eat, Lazy Ant would suddenly jump up. Lazy Ant always complained when he was given work to do. In fact, he was so lazy that he would even cry! Instead of working, Lazy Ant would chat non-stop, and so when it was time to go home, his work was left unfinished. One day Lazy Ant’s mother found him sitting on a rock as usual. His mother was angry and she punished him. Then she told him to quickly fi ll a sack with food. Lazy Ant grumbled as he began working. He knew that he would not be getting any food if he didn’t work. By the end of that day, Lazy Ant’s sack was full. His mother was very happy to see that her son had worked so hard. Lazy Ant’s mother prepared a special meal for supper to reward her son. He enjoyed the meal along with the other ants who had worked hard all day. The next morning, Lazy Ant was the fi rst one to wake up and he prepared breakfast for his mother. All the other ants were shocked by the change in Lazy Ant’s behaviour. He went up and down off ering help to any ant who needed it. The elders of Ant City even celebrated the change in Lazy Ant’s behaviour with him. And from that day, Lazy Ant saw the importance of working together with others. Working together creates peace, joy and harmony.
author: Cebo Solombela

title: The Elephant Who Went to the Moon
text: ‘I want to go to the moon,’ Eshan said. Ma laughed, patted Eshan on his head, and said, ‘The moon is way too far. You can become an astronaut when you grow up, and then fly to the moon!” The next day, Eshan told his teachers and friends that he would be an astronaut when he grew up, and fly to the moon. Some of his classmates teased him. But his best friends, Raju Rabbit and Sundari Squirrel, supported him. Eshan started reading many books about outer space. He got to know many interesting things! A month passed. His parents gifted him a telescope on his birthday. In the assembly, his headmaster announced a competition. The winner would get a chance to be a part of the team that would go to the moon! Eshan got busy preparing for the competition. Eshan’s father would help him practise running and climbing. His mother would help him practise swimming and jumping. His teachers gave him many books from the library to read. Day One of the Competition: The Written Test. Eshan had prepared well for the test. He made sure he had his pencils, eraser, and sharpener. His best friends, Raju Rabbit and Sundari Squirrel, came carrying his big water bottle that he had forgotten. The test was easy for Eshan. He had prepared really well for it by reading lots of books! Day Two of the Competition: The Project Presentation. Eshan felt jittery as he climbed the stage to present his project. His hands became sweaty and he dropped his stuff. But then he gathered up his courage and started to show how solar and lunar eclipses occur, using a globe, a ball, and a torch. Everyone clapped for Eshan. Day Three of the Competition: The Physical Test. Eshan ran as fast as he could and came third in the running race. When Eshan had to use a rope to jump across a pit, the rope broke and he fell down. He felt bad and was about to cry. Raju and Sundari came to him with his big water bottle and consoled him. The last event was swimming. Eshan swam really well and came FIRST! Day Four of the Competition: The Interview. In the interview, Eshan was asked about his hobbies and interests. One interviewer said to Eshan, ‘Never before has an elephant visited the moon!’ Pat came Eshan’s reply, ‘Then I will be the first!’ Another interviewer said, ‘We do not have spacesuits in your size.’ Eshan immediately answered, ‘Then you should make one for me!’ The interviewers were impressed with Eshan’s answers. His parents and classmates were very happy and congratulated him. Eshan had ten weeks of training. The day was fixed when Eshan would fly to the moon as part of the team. It was shown live on television and on the Internet. Wearing a spacesuit made specially for him, Eshan became the first elephant to go to the moon!
author: Shyamala V

title: The Fish and Chicken's Wedding
text: There once lived a chicken, called Cikizwa, who was an orphan. One day Cikizwa was out looking for food when she saw a mole coming out of his hole. She started speaking to the mole, but he ignored her. Tears poured down Cikizwa’s face as she wept bitterly, and so the mole apologised for hurting her feelings. Then he bought some cooldrink and scones. They ate and drank them together and then they both felt much happier. From that day on, the mole and Cikizwa became great friends. The friends often hugged each other tightly. They loved and looked after each other. One evening, Cikizwa said goodbye to her friend and went home. That night, Cikizwa had a dream. She heard her mother’s voice asking, “When is Cikizwa getting married?” “Oh, I must have been dreaming,” said Cikizwa as she woke up. Now, in the place where Cikizwa lived, there was a cruel elephant. Elephant often said really unkind things to Cikizwa to try and make her unhappy. One morning, when Cikizwa greeted Elephant, he snubbed her and said, “Ha, ha, ha! Go away, you orphan! What do you want from me? You’re so skinny. It’s as if you haven’t had enough mealies to eat!” Cikizwa was heartbroken. On her way home, she met Gusha Bhoqo. As soon as she saw the kind sheep, she poured out her heart to him. She told him about what Elephant had said to her. Gusha comforted the chicken and he was even able to make her smile a little. Then Gusha invited Cikizwa to have supper at his home. They had tasty samp, cooked with beans for supper. Afterwards, Cikizwa danced joyfully with the Gusha family as the music played. She danced so much that she sent the dust flying and forgot all her troubles! The next day it rained and rained. It rained so heavily that many animals were swept away by the nearby river. Cikizwa was safe in her little coop because her father had been clever enough to build a drain nearby so that it didn’t get flooded. But Cikizwa still felt sad about what had happened to some of her friends. Once the rain stopped, beautiful, colourful flowers appeared and there was a cool breeze. Cikizwa was out enjoying the sunshine when she saw Elephant limping along and crying loudly. Kind Cikizwa quickly called an ambulance. When the ambulance arrived, Elephant got the help he needed. His leg was bandaged and he was given an injection to help with the pain. As soon as Elephant started to feel better, he thanked Cikizwa for her kindness. Then he said, “Cikizwa, my child, never change who you are. Keep on respecting and loving everyone.” Some time later, Cikizwa went down to the river to enjoy herself. There were already a few people and animals there. Some of them were fishing, and then braaiing the fish they had caught. They ate the fish and fluffy freshly-baked roosterkoek. Cikizwa noticed a beautiful fish and she found out that his name was Gumbi. Gumbi and Cikizwa got to know each other and quickly became friends. Cikizwa even decided to stop eating fish out of respect for Gumbi. Some of the other animals laughed at them and said, “How can a fish and a chicken be friends?” But Gumbi and Cikizwa didn’t care. They became even closer. Gumbi taught Cikizwa how to swim and dive, and Cikizwa taught Gumbi how to scratch in the sand for food. Eventually Gumbi asked Cikizwa to marry him. Cikizwa agreed immediately. Together they decided to have their wedding the following Saturday at a place that they both loved near the river. Their wedding day arrived. The sun was blazing hot. What a wonderful wedding it was! The animal choir sang beautifully. Iguanas, whales, crocodiles, seals, sharks, dolphins, sheep, cattle, dogs, antelopes, hares, porcupines, water snakes and other animals all sang together: “It is enjoyable here at the wedding of the fish. It is enjoyable here at the wedding of the chicken!”
author: Madoda Ndlakuse

title: Queen of Soweto
text: Basetsana Makgalemele was born in a township called Soweto. She was her parents’ third daughter. They named her Basetsana, which means “girls”. In Tswana culture, calling your daughter that means your next child will be a boy. This actually happened. Her parents’ next child was a boy. Her parents, big sisters and younger brother all called her Bassie for short. When she was a child, Bassie was very shy. She liked to sing and dance in her room on her own. One day at school netball practice, the coach told two girls to pick teams. Bassie stood on the edge of the field hoping someone would say, “Come play with us!” But nobody wanted her on their team. Little did they know, Bassie would become one of the most popular girls in the country. On weekends, she and her brother and sisters helpedtheir teacher mom and bus driver dad to pay the bills. They made sandwiches to sell at local soccer matches. They tried to sell everything as fast as they could so they had time to play with the other children when the game was over. By the time Bassie turned 16, she was a beautiful young woman. She was so beautiful that she won two beauty competitions in one year: Miss Soweto and Miss Black South Africa. But Bassie was not only beautiful on the outside. Shewas also beautiful on the inside. Even though shewas a beauty queen, she still cared about the community where she grew up. Bassie was also very smart. She worked hard atschool, especially on her favourite subject: science.Her hard work was rewarded when she was the top science student at her school in matric. That’s notall, she was also Head Girl. The shy little girl was now one of the most popular girls in school. Bassie’s father always encouraged his children toread. He gave her a book called The Power of Positive Thinking. From that book, she learnt that being optimistic is the key to making your dreamsa reality. She dreamt of winning Miss South Africa.Not only did that dream come true, she was evencrowned First Princess in the Miss World competition! Bassie’s mother was her role model. Bassie described her mom as a “fierce, hardworking Xhosa woman who did not suffer fools”. She was a teacher and Bassie had plans to follow in her footsteps, but things don’t always go as planned! After winning Miss South Africa, she became a TV presenter. Shewasn’t a teacher, but like her mom, she washard working. Her career in TV led to her opening her own television production company. She was now a successful business woman. Bassie’s motto is: “To whom much is given, much is expected.” She believes that you are given a gift so that you can give to others. Bassie does this by volunteering, giving of her time and money and even creating jobs. She is involved with projects and charities to help people in her community. One that is very close to her heart is the Nelson Mandela Institute. Bassie had a very close relationship with Nelson Mandela. When she was crowned Miss South Africa, Madiba wrote her a letter of congratulations. In the letter, he called her “our Queen”. They shared a passion for children and education and the belief that an educated nation can help fight poverty. In 2002, Bassie married Romeo Kumalo and became known as Basetsana Kumalo. Together they established the Romeo & Baset sanaKumalo Family Foundation. The foundation looks after orphans - children who don’t have a mom anddad. Bassie has had to learn to balance her busy work and family life. She has her own company called Basetsana Women Investment Holdings. She and Romeo have three children, two boys and a girl. Bassie sees her role as mother to her children as her “highest calling and greatest privilege”. Bassie says the secret to her successis “courage, determination,passion and staying committed to the course”. Despite all hersuccess, she remains humble while trying to make the world abetter place. Being beautiful on the outside is not what makes you a beautiful person. It’s a heart filled with love and generosity. And that’s why Bassie is our beautiful Queen.
author: Jessica Taylor

title: Chanchal and Nirmala - The Colours
text: Chanchal, the naughty girl and Nirmala, the cow are up to something. On a Tuesday morning, they look for colours. Chanchal's mother grows green spinach. They also try her yummy, yellow lemons. Together they look up at the sky. It is bright blue. Look at Chanchal's rosy red cheeks! Look at the big black beard, on that sadhu! Take a break! Have some white milk. Let's make some butter and ghee. Golden in colour they will be!
author: Shubhangini Dhall

title: Chanchal and Nirmala - Sports Day
text: Chanchal, the naughty girl and Nirmala, the cow are back. It's a Wednesday afternoon and today is Sports Day. Nirmala will take a test of Chanchal. Chanchal passed in cycling......running, high jump and long jump. She made a record in swimming! Football, basketball, she knows it all! Cricket and hockey, oh so easy! Did Chanchal pass the test? Of course! She could beat all the rest!
author: Shubhangini Dhall

title: Chanchal and Nirmala - Spooky Kitchen
text: Nirmala, the cow and Chanchal, the naughty girl heard something strange. It was a Thursday night. They heard sounds from the kitchen. They listened through the door. What did they hear? Clash! Clash! The plates made a sound. Clink! Clink! The teacups dinged. Chop! Chop! The knives hit the board. The forks and spoons made some weird beats. Suddenly, the fridge door closed loudly! They opened the door and were shocked! Chanchal's brother Shyam, was munching on sweets!
author: Shubhangini Dhall

title: Rocky,Lucy and Ginger
text: Me and my friend Rocky,Lucy and Ginger Me and my friend Emannuel (Emu) were just walking around our society one day. We found three small kittens below three scooters in the parking lot. No one was taking care of them. So we both decided to take care of them. After a few weeks, my friend Kartik disturbed us while playing in the club house of the society. Then he decided to show something to us.We went with him and saw our three little kittens.One was black and white, second one was brown and white and third one was black, brown and white.We named them as Rocky, Lucy and Ginger. Ginger always likes to eat and play with his other siblings.Lucy likes to climb and sleep in our society and Rocky always pays attention to us and listens to what we say. And Rocky is my favourite among three. He never misunderstood us. We all were enjoying each other's company. We had fun together during our summer holidays. When my school started, before leaving for school, I looked at the three kittens and said bye to them.They lovingly looked at me. I missed them during my school hours and after coming back from school and I played with them. My friend Aryan fed them multigrain chips and some milk. Whenever we saw them, Emu started singing the songs like Believer and Thunder, and all of the kittens started listening to the songs very carefu lly he songs very carefu lly We started spending minutes, hours, days with them. The worst thing was after a few weeks, the watchman uncle of the Oxford building called some cat catchers to catch them. All of us didn’t want kittens to go away from us because they are as close as our siblings to us.Since I and Emu are such close friends of the kittens, we treated them as our siblings. That’s why we were worried when we heard about it But unfortunately, the day came and they are caught by catcatchers.We felt devastated and lost them permanently.We even didn’t know if they would come back again. But still they come to me in my dreams. If they would come back, I would like to say the words as below: welcome back my friends, you are still a part of my family.
author: Ahan Nandgaonkar

title: What you should do in a time of covid 19
text: You all know that there is a sickness that has spread all across the world. The name of the sickness is called Covid-19. You all know the sickness can effect anyone. So I'm going to tell you the things you must do to be safe. Number 1: Always stay inside. Now we all know that it is so boring to stay at home when you could be partying with friends. But if you go out the virus may get you. So that is why the president has declared that we should stay inside. The name for this is called Lockdown. Number 2: Always wear a mask when going out. Now Iknow most of us hate stuff covering our mouths but this necessary. The doctors believe that the virus goes in your eyes, nose or mouth. So that is why it is important to wear a mask when going out in public. But its not necessary to wear it inside. Number 3: When go in a shop use the hand sanitizer that is provided. Now it is the law to use sanitizer to enter a shop. All shops must provide their customers with hand sanitizer. Never enter a shop without being sanitized. And don't touch anything if your not going to buy it. Number 4: Dont hug, shake hands, kiss or visit close relatives or friends. Yes I know that it is hard not seeing your best friend in like forever but you just need to wait a bit. The virus could be on your BFF and buy hugging her it gets tranfered to you. And the it effects your family and the everyone in the neiborhood. So you can save life by not hugging anyone. Be the hero. SOME HEROES DONT WEAR CAPES, THEY WEAR MASKS
author: Nuriyah Hassan
illustrator: Brototi Mondal; Ellen Heydenrych; Floriana Giotta; JAI BHATIA; Namit Kalra; Sonakshi Verma; Valentina Gonnella

title: Free Kulfi
text: She went upstairs throwing tantrums When will I hear the bell of Kulfi kaka? 'Tun...Tun....Tun...a sound came from street Bhanwari took her small purse and ran behind. " What will you take today, Bhanwari?" Kaka asked in low voice. "One for mother, One for father And one for Babloo....." Bhanwari counted on fingers swiftly. " Two and one makes three. Three kulfi at rate of five each makes fifteen." " Grandmother says that she wont eat one daily. Stealthily she licks at night daily." Kaka asked," How much you totaled?" Bhanwari stressed a little more. " Three and one becomes four. And it will be then twenty. " And for you? ", kaka said laughingly. " Oh! I forgot tatally, Kaka. Take now total twenty five for five." Suddenly, a crow flew over Bhanwari head. It came near her. Took one kulfi from her hand. And Lo! It was gone. Bhanwari was sad. She told kaka, " I had only twenty five." Kaka said,' Dont worry, Dear Bhanwari. You will get one free kulfi" Bhanwari face was lighted with joy. Tun...Tun...Tun...Kulfi kaka gone. Other street, and more kids.
author: Rita Bansal

title: The Picture Day
text: Maria was so excited to have the picture day. She was looking in the mirror all day! But one thing happens was that her tooth had fallen out and she felt very bad she could not smile for picture day. She told her mother. She told her not to worry. I am sure the tooth fairy will come and take your tooth. But if today night you put the tooth under your pillow she will leave a coin there. Maria was surprised to here and went to sleep. The next morning she found a coin when she opened she saw it was a chocolate coin! She ate it. She went without smiling and wearing glasses and a beautiful dress. When they clicked the photo she realised that her friends like Sunita had told her 'everyone has something wrong' like Sunita had a bandage on nose and Verma fractured his bone. But Maria got the best smile award!
author: Triambika Chauhan
illustrator: Suman  Maharjan; Triambika Chauhan; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: The Mat
text: I have a mat. It has many colours. It is knit by hand. I put it on the floor. I sit and stand on the mat. It is so nice and soft. I lie down on it and read. I sleep on it too. When not in use I roll the mat up. I keep my mat under the cot.
author: Gauri Mehendale

title: Chanchal and Nirmala - My New Shirt!
text: It was a Friday afternoon. Chanchal the naughty girl got new clothes. There was a beautiful blue shirt! It had red and yellow stripes. Chanchal rushed to show her shirt to Nirmala, her cow. "Nirmala, we fasten the buttons to wear this shirt." "T his is called a pocket." "I can keep my toffees, coins and small things in it!" "This is a collar." "Close this button and I can wear a tie!" "These are the cuffs of my shirt." Chanchal looked very smart! Now all her friends also want new shirts!
author: Shubhangini Dhall

title: Gleem learnt a lesson
text: Everything was going fine in the forest, until the old lion king died. The old lion king was kind and cared about every animal in the kingdom. His kingdom was very big, it expanded from one end of the rainbow to another. The king was fond of colors and liked all the different colored animals. When he died, all the animals were very sad. The mighty golden tiger, Gleem consoled them and told them, that they needed a powerful king. With a heavy heart, the tiger himself became the king. Gleem was very strong and had a beautiful golden body, with no stripes. His friend, a golden langur suggested him that they should paint every animal in their kingdom, golden. Gleem liked the idea immediately. So, both of them dissolved golden color in the pond and the king gave orders that every animal should take a dip in it. All the animals were very upset at this order. They wished to remain as they were. But, at the same time, they couldn’t make their new king angry. A zebra refused to take a dip in the pond, so, Gleem killed him Toby, the black colored elephant was going with his group to the pond. Toby was good natured, but he was also a fighter at heart. When he saw a herd of golden animals, coming sadly from the pond, he told his mom, that “I like to be as I am” and then he raced as fast as he could toward the green bushes, that no one in the forest had ever gone to. Toby ran and ran till he got very tired. He had never come to this part of the forest before. He saw colored elephants there. They told Toby, that this part of the forest was enchanted. All of the animals were kind to him, especially blue colored Rangeela. All of them were firm believers of diversity. They believed that the world was beautiful because of animals of different colors! Those animals could talk to clouds. They asked clouds to shower over Toby’s part of the jungle to wash away the golden paint. It poured heavily and all the animals came back to their natural colors. After the rain, animals came out and started singing and dancing. Toby also came back and told Gleem that he should be a kind king and accept his kingdom as it is, like their beloved old king. Gleem realized his mistake and asked for forgiveness from animals of his kingdom. Toby also sprayed some water that he got from the enchanted forest at tiger. That water left black stripes on his golden body. Tiger realized that the black stripes made him more beautiful. It would always remind him of the importance of diverse colors!
author: Sumita Sharma
illustrator: Anuradha Marwah; Greystroke; Huynh  Vu Tuong; priyanshi panwar; Raju Babu Shakya; Rob Owen; Vanishree N

title: Ahaan's Book
text: Where is my new story book? I am not getting it," I saw under the sofa. The book is not there. I saw it on the table. It is also not here. It is also not even in bag. Ahaan went to his grandmother to know its whereabouts. Grandmother was reading his book. He said,"This is a good story." His grandmother read him the story again. Ahaan said," I love stories." I should always read new books.
author: Rita Bansal
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Deval Maniar; Greystroke; Priya Kuriyan; Priyanka Kumar; Rohit Karandadi; Sonal Goyal; Sonal Gupta Vaswani

title: We went to market.
text: There are so many shops. There are so many people. Some people do shopping.. Others do only window shopping. What will my mother do? First of all, we went to ration shop. Mother bought wheat,rice,sugar and pulses. We did not bring bag for ration. The shopkeeper will send ration at home. After this, mother stops at vegetable shop. I said," Will you buy vegetables now?" Mother said," No". Vegetable vendor shouts," Come! Come! There are fresh vegetables." Why mother stopped over here? Arre! This is oil shop. The shop is filled with oil smell. Mother complains," The oil is very costly." The shopkeeper felt bad. Now, we reached to fish market. Some people dislike fish smell. But I like it very much. See! How fisher woman is dressed! Can you see fat ca ts? These just rest here and get fat eating fish. We stopped at dairy. Mother bought ghee and cheese. Why do not they keep ice cream? I love it. What do you think? Will my mother buy ice cream for me? "Do you want to buy some utensils now"?, I asked mother. There was nobody at utensils shop. People buy utensils only When there is marriage or festival. Stop! "Mother! Do not go to this shop," I said loudly. My mother loves to visit cloth shop. The shopkeeper shows many sarees to her. But she takes nothing. Toy shop! I only wanted this. How big is teddy bear!. I want this scooter and this toy truck.... I promised mother that I will only touch and feel the toys. I will not insist to buy. I will only take one toy on my birthday
author: Rita Bansal

title: I can help!
text: I am Rita, I am six years old. I like to help Aai and Baba. I put my toys in the toy box. I keep my books neatly on the table. So, I tidy my room. I help Aai to dry clothes. I help Baba to clean up the kitchen. I help Aai in the garden. We water the plants. I help Baba to clean and paint the garden gate. Good children like to help at home. I am a good girl. Do you help Aai and Baba at home?
author: Rajeshree Kumar

title: Pintu Butterfly
text: This is a story of Pintu..a beautiful butterfly. She was born in Rahall’s garden. Mother Butterfly had hidden her eggs under the dahlia leaf. As she wrapped them in her special mammas safety gel-she wished.."May all my Little ones be safe here Please God May at least one of them be very special, unique,a butterfly like none Other." Mother butterfly prayed and flew away after she had hugged and kissed and sealed them with all her love. Weeks passed by. Then one warm sunny afternoon, all of the eggs hatched and out crawled the woolly caterpillars!! They perched the leaves of the dahlia and soon started munching at them. They ate and ate all day all night!! Crunch Crunch Crunch!! The last to wriggle out was Pintu.She slowly stretched her foot out-Oh!! she had so many tiny feet!! One by one they all found a place to on the leaf and then-Pintu looked up at the bright sun shining down at her. She smiled at it and looked around.The green leaves all around her was like one big jungle But, between them up higher up she saw some bright colors..what was THAT!!? She was curious..of course the Dahlia flowers!! Pintu felt a rumbling in her tummy!! Oh what a strange feeling it was.The soft green leaves under her feet looked tempting and beckoned her. Gingerly she crawled over and nibbled.Wow!!...they sure were tasty.Pintu munched on till l she was full. Then she said to the little leaves “Thank you sweetie!' The leaf was happy!!" What a nice caterpillar this one is..I must be nice to her too." She decided. "Pintu..this is a big bad world.You got to be really careful.There are enemies all around you. If you are not cautious, you shall be trapped and you will be gone even before you see this world." Said Genie the leaf. Pintu halted. Hundred little feet screeched to a stop. Pintu smiled at Genie and said,"I am new and I know nothing! But I am glad I have you with me! Wont you give me a hug?” Just then a squirrel whizzed passed them..”There!! did you see him?He is one of them too.. Beware of the spider,the eight legged devil.Stay away from the spider's spell Dare not crawl into his web. Hide below my leaves when you see any birdie" Caterpillars are voracious eaters you know, and so was Pintu! He kept nodding his head and just ate and ate all day long. Soon Pintu got fatter and fatter, until one day she just did not want to move any more. That night she slowly wriggled under Genie and wrapped herself into a warm blanket of silk- a cocoon! This time she slept too long.Genie knew Pintu was into her beauty sleep; she gladly hid her dear friend under her. Pintu hung there almost lifeless like a twig..she had eaten enough to keep her going a long time. Days passed while Pintu slept. One morning,Pintu woke up and felt choked inside her little quilt.She started pushing herself out. It Was a struggle, not easyat all But,Pintu would not give up. Push Push Push. She managed to emerge from her cocoon. Her beautiful wings flared out gradually Oh!she was a beauty!! Her wings a spray of all colors Pintu slowly spread out her lovely wings..while Genie gasped in delight"Oh!! look at that!"She squealed in delight. Pintu’s wings lifted her up!! This was sheer magic..she was really flying!! Up she went with Genie down below clapping her hands and yelling out in glee, “Go baby go! ' Pintu looked around Rahall's garden of flowers, she glanced at the clear blue sky above her. Spring was in the air. Everything was so magical! Pintu smiled and screamed in delight, "Hello world! " Pintu finally dived down into the dahlia and kissed Genie goodbye before she flew back into her colorful world. Flitting from flower to flower she would sing a song, smile and hug the flowers in the garden all day On the old rose plant sat one big old butterfly who saw Pintu. She knew it was her dream child for sure. She smiled in pride as she looked up and thanked God for making her dream come true!
author: Kamla Ramamurti
illustrator: Brunda Anandarao; Herminder Ohri; Kunal Parikh; Lavanya  Naidu; Megan Vermaak; Ounla  Santi; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Sanjay Sarkar

title: The Firefly
text: This is the story of a small bug. But a bug who dreamt big. Not only did he dream big he also made them come true by his determination. He was born on the big neem tree in Rahail’s garden. When he came out of his egg and looked at the bright daylight, his eyes cringe in disgust.He did not like the brightness around him. He noticed, the world was getting noisier and noisier all around him. He hated it all the more. When all other creatures got busy searching for feed and doing their normal chores. This one hid in a small hole and refused to step out. He lazed around in the hole saw the world whizzing around him.T he bees buzzing, the birds chirping..children hopping around the flower beds, the butterflies flitting from flower to flower. But he just sat there and sulked all day. Pintu titli saw him and was a little upset. She loved to see happy and gay folks all around her. So she flew up to his hole and asked him "Why was he sulking all day?"Jugnu the bug was angry he said-”Leave me alone I do not want to talk to anyone” But sweet as she was, Pintu would not stop at that. She collected sweet nectar from the rose plant and visited him the next morning”Hey!! come on have a sip and see what I got for you. Am sure you will love this refreshing drink."Jugnu was angry again. But he was hungry too. So he stuck out his head and took a sip..Hmmm it sure was divine. jugnu loved it. Pintu titli sat down on the nearest neem flower and said “Jugnu, have you ever tasted the juice of the neem flower? Am sure you have not.It is bitter. You would not like to be like this flower would you? But when you sulk and not eat,you will soon turn bitter Think about this." said Pinto as she flew away promising to come back to him the next morning. God, who makes all creatures big and small also saw what was happening to Jugnu.So he went down to the tiny wormy and said "Jugnu,I like to see all my children happyand gay, But I find you are upset.Well,what do you want? Ask and I shall grant it to you.But you must make your decision by tonight.”God said this and vanished. Jugnu got worried. Oh he did not want to be bitter at all!! he just wanted to be different- he did not want to be colorful like the butterfly. He did not like the busy bees and their angry drones...he just did not like the chirpy birds too!! What did he want then?What was it he pined for? As he was looking at all these creatures..it became evening.The birds settled in their nests, kids ran away home, the bugs and bees went into deep slumber. The birds in the nests were still restless and chatting up about the events of the day.No one bothered to turn around and find out what his problem was. Jugnu felt lost and lonely. He had waited all day for Pintu the butterfly. But today she was not there to give him a sweet drink. He was sad. He sulked and withdrew into the hole. And got to think. He saw life slowly grind to a standstill and the garden engulfed in darkness. When all seemed still, life started ticking once more Jugnu noticed there was a new awakening! The owl fly out of his hole. Jugnu was fascinated, He climbed the highest branch of the neem tree just to see where Mr.Owl went when all was dark. But alas!! in the darkness,Jugnu could see nothing. As he sat engulfed in the beauty of the night.The soft glow of the moon and the twinkling stars blinking and winking at him made him happy and calm. Jugnu sat still and heard the crickets creaking The sounds of the night engulfed Jungu in its mysterious world.He was bewildered. He had found an answer for God's question after all. “Yes!! I want to be like these creatures of the night.I want a less noisy world, a world full of mystery and adventure. I want to go deep into the dark woods and fly around. I want to explore! This is what I want. But I cannot fly like the butterfly nor can I see in the dark like the wise owl."He sighed. He waited for God to come back to him. God came and said, ”Well Jugnu your time is up!! tell me what you wish to be?” Jugnu looked up into God's eyes and said “Please give me the power to fly and see through the darkness of the night. I love the world when it is dark and cool and full of mystery.” God was happy and He said-”Jugnu I give you small wings to fly and I also give you the strength to your legs, because what I did to your eyes I cannot undo. From today, if you rub your feet you shall have a torch that will guide you through the darkness and help you take a new adventure trip each night” Before Jugnu could say anything, God was gone. Jugnu rubbed his legs and loo!!It glowed all around him like a candle in the darkness. When he flapped his new found wings!!He could really fly!! Jugnu swerved and took a dive like an airplane. He flew all around the garden enjoying his new found freedom! All the creatures of the day slept..but Pintu alone was awake..she saw the glow worm and she knew it was Jugnu. No one else could be so beautiful and happy so late in the night. Pintu smiled as she closed her eyes in slumber She knew Jugnu had found a way to be happy and unique as he always wished to be. She was happy for him.
author: Kamla Ramamurti
illustrator: Jano Strydom; Mahbubur  Rahman; Measa Sovonnarea; Partho Sengupta; Rohit Kelkar; Sou  Kimsan; Thea   Nicole de Klerk
