title: Who is the Best ?
text: mmmmm ⚽ There's a town named Palm Springs, California, USA. There's a Kid lived there w ho's name was Jimmy. He's kind of Bully in his Class and Neighbourhood. He always pushed himself in the first place by pushing others and he used to Threaten all Students and seize away thier Lunch Boxes and Quarrels with Kids in Neighbourhood. He was very sincere and smart kid before. Somehow he felt suprior to be best in his class and neighbour. That's how he becomes to be mischievious and takes advantages of other kids who were weak in compare to strenght and knownlege. No one was capable to stand against him because of lackness in power & wisdom. His family wasn't aware of his behaviour. If any complaints comes about jimmy they ignorned it They thought that jimmy were a Decent kid. As soon as he realise theirs no to stop him, He's courage increased! ⚽ ☕ One DAY, His Grandpa was roaming at Balcony while drinking Tea. Where he saw that his grandson is scoldind and Quarreling with other kids. Grandpa figured out that all the complaints that were coming about Jimmy's misbehaving were all True. Grandpa felt guilty about it that why I haven't noticed it earlier, I could have stop it. He went on thinking that how to realise Jimmy that he was misbehaving with other children. Then he remembered something old thing that he (Grandpa) had learned from his Father. Somehow he felt that he can use that same way to teach jimmy a lesson. ☕ LATER: ON THAT NIGHT 🌙 Grandpa was resting in his waving chair at his Room. Finally he decides to improve Jimmy and make him realise what he was doing. So on, Grandpa called Jimmy to his Room. As Jimmy heards grandpa's voice he just flash towards that direction (Grandpa). He loves his Grandpa so much! Jimmy arrives at door asking for that whats the command to Grandpa. Grandpa giggles to hear that sentence and said calm down yourself and sit down Grandpa said that today I saw you outside, You were misbehaving with your friends. He realise that he's been caught off. Grandpa slighly told jimmy that I hasn't told about that to anybody. Jimmy got relived! Then Grandpa asked jimmy that would he likes to hear a story? 📖 ☀️ Jimmy was very nervous to think about how his family would feel about knowing that he was spoiled. So he nods his head to hear grandpa's story Grandpa smiled and starts the story: Far, Far away from here! Somewhere in Savana Desert. There lived three animals who were best friend to each other. Always helps and support to each other. Whoever is in need! One was Cheetah as Fastest Runner on Land, Second was Eagle as Highest Flying Bird, Third was Crocodile as Deepest Diver. They all were the Superior on their territory. Everybody respects and obey infront of them. They are the best in their own subtle. Nobody was capable to match them. One day, They all gather to meet each other near the pond where Croc lives. While they're talking, Cheetah raised a Question that who's the Best among us? Everybody got confused and response with an unexpected way. ☀️ 🍂 Then all come up with an answer. Cheetah: Whoever can run faster than me I'll honour him as Best. Eagle: Whoever can go fly higher than me I'll declear him as Best. Crocodile: Whoever can dive deeper than me I'll crown him as the Best. Each of them knows that we can't beat each other. Neither they Lose, Nor they Win. They all still trying to debacle each of them but as you know Cheetah can't Fly and Dive, Falcon can't Run and Swim and Crocodiles can't Fly and Run that much. So, Everytime the results comes the Same. From that Day, They all got a Lesson that How much Talented, Strong, Powerful we can be but we can't Defeat everyone. We all should cooperate with each other. So, They all live Happily. (THE END) Afterwards, When Story ends Grandpa asks Jimmy a question. What did you learn from this Little Story? 🍂 Jimmy: We can't win over everything however strong we are. We should cooperate with others. Grandpa: I think you have learned your Lesson. So, Don't scold and quarrel with your Friends. You should cooperate with them, Even if you Sharper, Faster compared to them. Grandpa: Let me ask you something. Can you defeat me compared to my knowledge, Can you? Jimmy: No, I can't. Grandpa: Hmm. But I can't defeat you in Speed like you would run faster than me because you are younger than me. Jimmy: Yeah, I get what you want me to learn. Grandpa patted his head and said: Okay, Be a Good man from now. Next Day, Jimmy apologized to everyone who he bullied and ask for forgiveness. He also sought that he won't misbehave with his Friends and Classmates. Since from then, He becomes a humble friend to everyone. THE END
author: Deepanshu  Garg

title: Clever Lion
text: This is story about a clever Lion from deep inside forest in Gir in Gujarat. The Lion was very clever and wanted to be king of jungle even he grow old. So he decided to play a trick with fellow animals in Jungle. He invited all animal for a weekend meeting to announce his retirement and to choose a wise another animal if they find. Every one agrees and decided to join the meeting. In the meeting Lion says to all, " I know I grow old but I am not able to find any suitable animal to carry one my job after me. So I request you to meet me in my den one by one and share your thought. If you know any one who can help in this, you are free to share their details with me" One by one all animals went inside and came back saying that Lion should remain king for the jungle! Every one was coming back with a smile. There was a rabbit who was also watching this and not able to understand what is happening in den. Why every one is making him king again! So he decided to check with himself. Rabbit turn came and he went inside and greeted Lion. Lion Asked him - Just answer one question and we will get the result immediately. Rabbit said "Yes". Lion asked him - Who is most clever in jungle? You or me? Rabbit said "ME" without much thought! Lion says - "Here you go! I was saying this to every one that Rabbit is most intelligent and I was so right, So I should remain a king!" Rabbit was surprised and amused. Now he knows why all animals were happy with him. He was playing with his words cleverly. Rabbit went back helplessly and praising kings trick!
author: Kritika Mishra
illustrator: Eshita Munshi; Jean  Fullalove; Ketan Raut; Meenakshi Palaniappan; Nanvi Jhala; Promina Shreshtha; Rupa Prakash; Wiehan de Jager

title: Kalyani's first day at dance class
text: "Amma..... Amma".... Im back from school, kalyani says as she returns from school in the evening. Ok kutty ma,go and change you clothes...…. says Amma from the kitchen, cooking Kalyani's favorite aromatic Drumstick sambhar with potatoes ready to be tossed in the pan. Amma,Amma!Im going to play now Preeti is waiting for me at the park,if Im late somebody will take the seat on the swing....says Kalyani in her Orange frock. Wait Kalyani!!!! Amma shrieked as she scampered across the dining hall. have your chocolate milk first,besides don't you remember we have to go to your Bharathanatyam dance class today,kanna "said Amma. Amma quickly darted into the bedroom and got her dance uniform a perfectly stitched magenta salwar with a parrot green colour pyjama and a corresponding dupatta,looking at the clothes Kalyani burst into tears inconsolably saying,"Amma no,I don't want to go to the class,Im scared you 'll leave me and go." Amma gave a very reassuring smile and said "No,Kalyani Ill stay back with you at the class ". Kalyani reluctantly went to the dance class with Amma. At the dance class stood a beautiful lady with a wide grin, in a yellow saree that looked like a sunflower while her mouth went on, "Thaikya Thaiki Tham,and the girls in the class went chukka chukka chum with their feet tapping hard on the floor.That was Kalyani's dance teacher Swathilekha mam!!! Kalyani stood beside the other girls Moni,Soumya and Rithu.Kalyani was yet to come to terms with her new class while the other girls smiled and tapped their feet with exuberance to the meliflous "Thai Thai Tham "by their teacher. Slowly with every "Thaiyyum Thatha Thayyum Tha "Kalyani's face lit up like a newly bought 100 watts bulb,she went from sitting to bending and finally Kalyani was in Love with her dance class. What more?? looking at kalyani's happy face,Amma was happy too with a wide grin on her face. kalyani enjoyed the class so much that she jumped and hopped all the way home like a kangaroo saying "Thai Thai Tham,Thai Thai Tham.."

title: Meera and the Mango tree
text: Once upon a time in a place in coastal Andhra pradesh, there was a girl named Meera. She was 9 years old, very energetic and intelligent. Her parents were in the medical profession and worked full time, so she spent most of her time with her grandmother. Her granny was an energetic lady who was also very hard working and sweet. Meera hung out with her granny most of the day time and at night she would sleep next to her. Granny always had some interesting stories to narrate. Meera listened to a story every night and dreamed of the beautiful and exciting characters in the stories she heard. She dozed off to sleep night after night imagining herself in the world full of adventures and possibilities. It was summer season and also the most favorite season for Meera for various reasons. Delicious mangoes, jams and squash that her grandmother made were among the most favorite things to her. She helped her grandmother in the making process which was her most memorable past time. She also loved the mango tree in her backyard and admired its beauty and spent most of her evening playing under it, sleeping under its shade most of the summer. On that particular Friday, Meera woke up early, to the voice she heard from the kitchen.It was the familiar call from her granny asking her to wake up and get the day going.She woke up lazily yawning and finished brushing. She noticed a few new faces in the compound and ran to her grandmother.On questioning, granny answered that they were the men that came to cut mangoes from the mango tree. Excited about the day ahead, Meera got ready to be involved in the process of pickling mangoes.She sat among the workers and was happy watching them work. She also heard them talk about a lot of things, some of which she found interesting. One of the working men, a tall old man with white hair and mustache started narrating some folktales about mango trees from their village. He said that big trees like mango and banyan trees can sometimes be home for evil spirits at night, who are waiting to capture and take away children who are ill behaved. The sound of evil and spirit made meera wonder whether her mango tree, the one she grew up watching was indeed a resident of evil spirits at night. With these disturbed thoughts in her mind she ran all day trying to concentrate on her favorite pickling process. Soon she forgot about the evil spirits and enjoyed the day. The process of pickling involved all the aunties from the neighborhood who sat and cut the mangoes into equal sized pieces, mixed them in with a whole lot of ingredients and made it into a tasty jar filled with joy. At night she had dinner with the new pickle and retired to bed with granny. She asked granny about evil spirits and granny told her that they were not real and she never saw one.However some people do believe they exist and also believe that they reside in big trees and come out at night. Meera was terrified but managed to fall asleep.Next day she forgot all about the evil spirits but somehow never approached the mango tree. She kept avoiding the mango tree for the coming two weeks. When granny asked for the reason she kept avoiding the subject. Her tiny mind kept processing the mango tree as an evil spirit and the hatred towards the most loved mango tree began to increase day after day unknowingly. That summer season came to an end with meera almost developing fear and aversion to the most beloved mango tree. Months passed by and Meera ignored the mango tree and was busy with her school work and friends. Granny was busy with her kitchen chores. One evening the announcement came in the radio about a giant storm predicted to hit the town accompanied by thunder showers.Dark clouds soon covered the sky and rain started pouring with whooshing winds. Meera ran scared to granny who assured her that there was nothing to worry and that they were all prepared to handle any storm that came their way. The storm started and lasted for almost three days. The electric lines were damaged with no power for almost 48 hours with darkness everywhere. Their house being the biggest was home to many others whose houses were flooded with water. Almost 35 people took shelter and Meera spent her time helping everyone around the home.That particular night the storm became worse than expected. Doors kept banging and were shut. Few candles and lamps were lit to manage the house. At night the storm started uprooting trees, electric poles and causing fatalities nearby.This was the worst storm that hit their village in years.She could see the dark clouds filling every where and the sound of thunder made her quiver. Suddenly in the middle of night meera heard loud banging noises and sounds of thunder rattling her. She shivered in terror assuming that her whole house would come down on her. She ran and hugged her granny who reassured her and put her to sleep.She kept praying to god for the safety of everyone in her house.The following morning she woke up to a silent and bright day. The rain has stopped finally but the damage done by it was immense. She heard people talking and went in that direction. She was surprised to see everyone gathered near the mango tree. She made her way through the crowd and reached her dad and asked why people were near the mango tree. Her dad replied, Meera, this tree saved all our lives last night. A large electric pole and a coconut tree fell last night and to our luck they were stopped by this giant mango tree from falling on to the building and collapsing it and probably injuring everyone in the house including you, granny and all others. Meera felt a sudden feeling to happiness followed by regret about how she thought that the tree was evil and ignored it all these months. She ran from her dad and hugged the tree with tears rolling down her cheek, kissed the tree and thanked it for protecting them......
author: Hima Adusumilli
illustrator: Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Kavya Singh; Priya Kuriyan; Tapas Guha

title: Chintu and his dream

title: A genuine friendship
text: Renu and her friend always play in the park. Renu will never give a chance to play with her ball. Renu's friend, Drithi also wanted a chance to play with Renu's ball. One day, Renu kicked her ball up high, and it got struck in between the branches of a tree. Drithi kindly said,"Don't worry Renu, I will climb this tree and get your ball!" Drithi climbed the tree. She scooped the ball and slid down the tree. She handed over the ball to Renu. Renu felt sorry for not sharing her ball. Renu passed the ball to Drithi and pleaded, "Can you forgive me Drithi, for not sharing the ball?" Drithi had forgiven Renu and they both played with the ball.

title: Plants
text: These are born, grow, reproduce and die. The parts of a plant are: root, stem, leaves and fruit. Some fruits are seeds and give life to more plants. There are different classes of plants: such as: medicinal plants, for example: peppermint, wormwood, others which serve to decorate and are ornamental like roses, orchids and sunflowers, among industrial plants we find cypress, cedar and pine. However, the tastiest plants are the edible ones like pumpkin sprouts.

title: The Fussy Daddy
text: Holaram was very angry! He came out of his room with anger and frustration. He was so angry that he even shouted at his baby girl, Priya, for not eating fast. She was scared and her plate fell. So much that she got grounded for a week! Next day, Holaram's wife, Damyanti, along with Kriya and Priya tried several ways of cooling him down. They gave him a haircut but that did not work. "Who does not like hair cuts!" said Kriya. They told him to go out for a stroll with Gary, their dog, with a smile on his face. He felt embarrassed when everyone looked at him. He had a BIG frown on his face. Priya gave him a newspaper but that did not work either. Kriya gave him a massage that made him relax. Then a loud thud on the floor made the sound "DINGGG!". This made him frown again. He had a big frown on his face. Finally, Priya gave him their cat, Kitty. He got a smile on his face and played with Priya and her sisters the whole day. MORAL- The things that make you happy will always make you have a smile on the face.

title: Bedtime Stories by Dad
text: Dad was once a young boy. Dressed in red shorts and a white top. With a round nose and a big smile. He cycled to school every time. He gobbled up rice all the time. author: Bhavya  Singh

title: Starry Skies
text: Did you know that you and the Sun are made of the same things? Our bodies are made up of tiny things called atoms. Atoms are everywhere! They are in animals and objects, in books, roads, oceans, the sun and the whole universe. Atoms come close together and then move far away from each other. This happens inside you, inside me and inside everyone and everything you know! Whizz! Whoosh! They are buzzing with energy. The same thing happens in space, where there are lots of gases and dust particles floating around. In some parts of the universe, lots of dust particles collect, forming a cloud. As the cloud grows, it becomes very heavy. All the atoms inside begin to fuse together. When the cloud becomes too heavy, SWOOOOSH, it collapses! Atoms come rushing to the center of the cloud and are squeezed so tight that they stick together and form bigger atoms. This releases heat and light. Any two Hydrogen and Helium atoms that fuse together release energy. When millions of atoms do this, a very hot, very bright, very big ball of energy is formed. And then a star is born! To us on Earth, stars may look tiny. But they are actually HUGE. Do you know which star is closest to us? The Sun! The Sun is big, bright and gives off a lot of light. All the other stars in the sky are also fiery balls like the Sun. Some of them are even bigger. But they are very FAR away. That is why they look tiny to us. If you start counting the stars in the sky, you will be counting all night. And the next night too! There are THAT many stars in the sky! And these are only the ones we can see. There are GAZILLIONS of stars in the universe! Young stars, old stars, big stars, little stars, hot stars, cool stars, and even colourful stars. There are Red Giants that glow big and red. There are White Dwarfs that are extremely hot. Stars can also be yellow or blue! Stars change colour as they grow older. The Sun is now yellow. As it grows older, it will become bigger and redder, expanding like a balloon. Then it will shrink, becoming white. Stars sometimes explode too! This is called a Supernova. This releases large amounts of dust, gas, and atoms — everything that a star is made of! We won’t be around to see the Sun change colour because stars live for billions and trillions of years. The Sun is a young star. It’s only 4.6 billion years old. The oldest star we know is 13.2 billion years old. The universe is 13.8 billion years old. When it comes to stars and the universe, everything is very large. The Sun is so massive that more than a million Earths could fit inside it. The Earth is so enormous that billions of people can live on it. And we are all made of so many atoms that they’re impossible to count! The next time you go out during the day, remember how big and hot the Sun is. And at night, look up at the tiny twinkling stars and remember how large they really are. Compared to everything else in the universe, we are the small ones!
author: Sandhya Ramesh

title: Stay at home, Bumpy
text: Stay at home, Bumpy And do what Aaji tells you to Wash your hands frequently with soap and water And boost your immunity by eating an orange too! title: An egg for bride wealth
text: Once upon a time, there was an old woman who loved her grandson very much. She gave him an egg as a gift. She said, “From this egg you will get bride wealth for your marriage when you are of age.” And the boy went on his way. First he met some blackberry gatherers who asked him for the egg. They used it to shoot at the berries and it broke. The boy cried, “EiEiEi! You have caused trouble for me! The egg was not mine. It belonged to my grandmother. And grandmother didn't give it to me for nothing. She gave it to me to get bride wealth.” So the berry gatherers gave him the stick they used to bring down the berries. And the boy walked on. Next the boy met some builders who asked him for his stick. They used it to build a house and it broke into pieces. The boy cried, “HeeHeeHee! You have caused trouble for me! The stick was not mine, it belonged to the berry gatherers. And they didn’t give it to me for nothing. They gave it to me in place of my egg. The egg was not mine. It belonged to my grandmother. And grandmother didn’t give it to me for nothing, She gave it to me to get bride wealth.” So the builders gave him a bundle of grass for thatching. And the boy walked on. Next the boy found a herdsman who asked for the boy's bundle of grass. The herdsman gave it to the cow and the cow ate it all up. The boy cried, “EEE! You have caused trouble for me! The grass was not mine. It belonged to the builders. The builders did not give it to me for nothing. They broke my stick. The stick was not mine. It belonged to the berry gatherers. And they didn't give it to me for nothing. They gave it to me in place of my egg. The egg was not mine. It belonged to my grandmother. And grandmother did not give it to me for nothing. She gave it to me to get bride wealth.” So the herdsman gave the boy his cow. And the boy walked on. While on his way home, the boy came across a marriage celebration. The bride's family asked him for his cow. He gave it to them. And they slaughtered it and ate it all. The boy cried, “EiEiEi! You have caused trouble for me! The cow was not mine. It belonged to the herdsman. The herdsman didn't give it to me for nothing. He gave it to me in place of my bundle of grass. The grass was not mine. It belonged to the builders. The builders didn't give it to me for nothing. They broke my stick. The stick was not mine. It belonged to the berry gatherers. They didn't give it to me for nothing. They gave it to me in place of my egg. The egg was not mine. It belonged to my grandmother. And grandmother didn't give it to me for nothing, She gave it to me to get bride wealth.” Then the bride's family said, “We have nothing left to pay you. But let us give you the bride." And so, the saying came to pass that, "What goes round comes around!”
author: Cornelius Wambi  Gulere

text: Hi! I am Zoya! This is my tiny red blanket under which I hide whenever I feel scared, which is most of the times! Weird names people call me scares me! Uncertainties scare me! title: Pick It Up
text: “Yippee!” Zonke shouts when the school bell rings. At last he can go home. This afternoon he wants to play soccer with the other boys. “Hey! Look out,” a voice suddenly rings out in front of him. He never noticed Bheka. Bheka growls at him. “Sorry,” Zonke quickly replies. He wants to walk around Bheka. But Bheka suddenly pushes him. Zonke stumbles. Bheka laughs. “Do you have big feet that you fall so easily?” he mocks. Annoyed Zonke straightens himself. A girl, Thandi, helps him.“Thank you,” Zonke says. “You’re welcome,” Thandi says. “I saw everything. Bheka really is a bully.” Zonke runs home. It’s quite hot. Fortunately the house isn’t far. Suddenly he notices something in the road. He stops. What is it? It is as big as the palm of his hand. It is brown. And it is made from leather. It’s a wallet! Zonke can’t believe his luck. He quickly glances inside the wallet. Wow, it contains money! Zonke’s heart beats faster. Then he puts the wallet in his pocket. He quickly glances around to see if someone noticed. Yes! Somebody is approaching. It’s Bheka. He is only a few steps behind Zonke. Zonke hurries on. He hopes Bheka hasn’t seen him. He doesn’t want to glance over his shoulder again. The wallet lies safely in his pocket. When he gets home he will take it out and see how much money it contains. At home Zonke puts down his school case. Then he walks to the shady tree next to the house. Carefully he takes the wallet from his pocket. His heart beats faster. He counts the notes. Fifty one hundred a hundred and fifty two hundred Rand! He is mega rich. But then he hears a familiar voice. “What are you hiding?” It is Bheka! Zonke hides the wallet behind his back. “Too late. I saw you picking something up,” Bheka says. “That’s why I came to check you out.” Bheka pulls Zonke’s arm. His eyes grow wide when he sees the wallet. He takes it. “Wow! This is nice. Are you going to keep it?” Bheka asks. “I I don't know yet,” Zonke stammers. Bheka also counts the money. “You know the saying: finders keepers.” Bheka whistles. “You must surely keep it. If I picked it up, I would keep it.” “But somebody lost it,” Zonke says. Bheka laughs. “So what? They were careless. That’s why it’s your money now.” “I will have to think about it,” Zonke says. “You don't have to think about it,” Bheka says. “I’ll tell you what to do. KEEP THE MONEY. Buy yourself a new pair of shoes. Or a soccer ball.” “No!” a girl’s voice sounds. It is Thandi from school. “Zonke, the money doesn’t belong to you. You don’t have the right to keep it.” “What do you know, Thandi?” Bheka asks. He pulls a face. “You’re just trying to be miss smarty pants. Zonke doesn’t have to return the money.” Zonke listens to the two of them. He doesn’t know what to do. He would like to keep the money. But Thandi may be right. You can’t take things that don’t belong to you. Even if you pick them up. Bheka suddenly stands right in front of him. Bheka folds his arms. “So, what are you going to do, Zonke? Will you keep the money? Or will you try to find the owner?” Zonke thinks and thinks. “I’m going to return it,” Zonke suddenly says loudly. Thandi smiles. “That’s the right thing to do. You’ll see.” Bheka shakes his head. He returns the wallet to Zonke. “You’re a coward,” he says and leaves. “You’re not,” Thandi tells Zonke softly. “If you keep the purse you will be as ugly as Bheka himself.” Zonke smiles. He is glad she has helped him make the right decision. “How are we going to find out whose money it is?” he asks. Thandi looks inside the wallet. She takes out a bank card. Gugu Dube is written on the card. The name sounds familiar to Zonke. Thandi removes something else from the wallet. It’s a small picture of Gugu and her children. Now Zonke recognises her. “She lives nearby. Come along. We’re going to return her wallet.” Together Zonke and Thandi run along the gravel road. Auntie Gugu’s door is open. They knock. In a moment someone comes to the door. It's auntie Gugu. Shame, she seems to be crying. Zonke feels bad that auntie Gugu is crying. But then he takes the wallet from his pocket. Auntie Gugu’s sad face immediately turns happy. She laughs. “My wallet!” she shouts. “I can’t believe it.” She checks the money in the wallet. “And all the money is here. I am so happy. I had to go and buy some food. But then I lost my wallet. I thought we would go hungry this week.” She gives both Zonke and Thandi a kiss on the forehead. Then she danced around with joy. After a while Zonke and Thandi walk home.Zonke is very glad that he did the honourable thing. Thandi is right. If he kept the wallet, he would be just as ugly as Bheka. But today he actually feels like a hero!
author: Fanie Viljoen

title: Fly Safe, Godavan
text: “Rania, Rania!” called Saleem mamu. “Come and see the godavan.” Rania stopped playing with her goat and ran to Saleem mamu. In the mung bean field was a big bird with a black crown. It was taller than her, but not as tall as Saleem mamu. Frrsht! The godavan’s tail feathers stood up straight. Poof! The godavan’s neck inflated like a balloon. Saleem Mamu smiled. “We stopped putting pesticides in the field and so the godavan has come here to find a mate. He is showing off for her.” The next week, Saleem Mamu took Rania for a walk. He pointed and said, “Our godavan’s mate has laid an egg on the ground. We have to keep it safe from being trampled by the cows and goats and camels.” Saleem Mamu told Rania to protect the nest but not go too close to it. “Shoo!” said Rania to the cows and goats. “PHURRR,” Rania scolded the camels. “You’re safe,” whispered Rania to the godavan and her egg. One night there was a terrible storm. Thunder boomed like a drum. Lightning flashed over the sand dunes. Rania wondered if the godavan and her egg were okay. In the morning, Rania went to check on the nest. “Oh, no!” she cried. “The storm has destroyed the egg.” Saleem Mamu laughed. He pointed to the pieces of eggshell on the ground. “It has hatched! ” Rania no longer had to protect the nest. But she still had to keep Ma and the chick safe. “The chick can’t fly yet,” said Saleem mamu. “So we have to help Ma keep it safe from predators.” The little godavan chick followed her Ma everywhere. Rania often saw them in the mung field and the grassland. Thik-thik-thik They ate insects and grass seeds. Rania once saw a pack of dogs enter the field. She yelled for Saleem Mamu and together they chased the dogs away. “Uff,” thought Rania. “Keeping our godavans safe is a lot of work. I can’t wait till our chick can fly away from danger!” The godavan chick was getting bigger and bigger. She could now fly and was almost as tall as her Ma. Sometimes, Saleem Mamu had trouble telling them apart. But Rania always knew which was which. One day, Saleem Mamu took Rania to the edge of the field. She saw towering windmills and electric wires running from pole to pole. “The birds will soon fly away to find new feeding grounds,” he said. “But they fly so low that they might collide with the wires.” “Surely the godavans are more important than electric wires?” thought Rania. She didn’t know how to protect the godavans from the wires. But Saleem Mamu found a solution! The next week, he called some men. They worked for days, placing wires underground and attaching bright mirrors to the wires over ground. “The mirrors will reflect sunlight. The godavans will see the flash and know to fly higher,” explained Saleem Mamu. Rania was helping Abba in the field when she saw the godavans. The two birds took a short run up and began to flap their heavy wings. Slowly, slowly they lifted off the ground and flew safely over the wires. “Fly safe, my godavan birds,” yelled Rania. “And come back soon.” The Great Indian Bustard was almost declared India’s national bird! This beautiful species lives in grasslands. The female nests on open ground and lays just one clutch of eggs every year. It is a very tall and heavy bird. Great Indian Bustards fly low and close to the ground. They have weak frontal vision, which means they can't always spot power lines in time to fly over them. The Great Indian Bustard was once found in many parts of India, but today the only viable populations are in Rajasthan and Gujarat. The threats faced by Rania’s godavan are real. Fewer than 150 Great Indian Bustards survive in the wild, making them ‘critically endangered’. Fortunately, conservationists in India are working to breed them in captivity, so that they never go extinct. These birds can then be released back into the wild, so long as we keep their grasslands safe. Meet the Godavan

title: The Foolish Rabbit
text: It was a thick forest. Many animals lived in that forest. Leo, the lion, was the king. Any king would care for his subjects and kingdom. But Leo was no good king. He killed the animals for satisfying his hunger. He never cared for them. The elders, who saw anyone like Leo, would curse them saying that their stomach is filled with poison. Leo has a big appetite. He used to hunt any animal he found carelessly and recklessly. Of all the animals, rabbits easily used to fall prey. As time passed, the animals in the forest began to vanquish one by one due to Leo.Rabbits were on the verge of extinction. The remaining rabbits called for an emergency meeting to talk about their extinction. The Rabbit finally decided to leave the forest and go elsewhere. One little rabbit claimed that he would teach a lesson to Leo, and the rabbits don't need to go anywhere. The old rabbits warned him.They said him that it is a complicated issue, and tried to stop her. The rabbit disagreed. He said that her mother said many stories about the witty nature and problem solving skills of rabbits. The little rabbit said that he would take care of all problems. The old rabbits said, "Look here, boy. You do not know the older days. Back then, every animal had the minimum sense to let every animal live. But your generation? You are habituated to being spoon-fed by your parents. You have book-knowledge only.You do not know what the world is like out there." But he did not listen. He persuaded everyone to give him the whole noon's time. All the rabbits agreed, thinking that a noon's time wouldn't do much bad. But our rabbit here hasn't seen a lion yet. He had only heard about the lion in stories. As soon as he reached the lion's den, he heard a blood-curdling roar, and he froze in his place. Luckily, the elder rabbits followed this mischievious rabbit. The other rabbits dragged the petrified rabbit away from the den. After the rabbit came to his senses, he was a little bit dejected that he was not able to solve the problem. The rabbits then decided to move away. The elder rabbits thought not to spoon-feed everything and teach everything to their kids. They thought that it is better if some things were left to learn by the young ones themselves.

title: Zuzu and her pumpkin vine.
text: Once Zuzu came across some pumpkin seeds at her Baba's farm and decided to sow them. She got back home and sowed the seeds in a teeny tiny pot. She decided that she will take good care of it. So s he religiously watered it every day. In fact she over watered it. She kept it in her bedroom where there was no sunlight so that nobody touches it. After sowing the seeds she immediately started thinking of the pumpkins that this little vine would yield. "Some would be big." exclaimed the little girl. "So big and heavy that I wouldn’t be able to carry them. I might even need a truck to take them to the market" Zuzu said. "Some would be so small that I could even juggle them…." She thought. "The rest would be of a decent size……and extremely easy to handle" She said to herself. She had also decided what she was going to do with all these pumpkins. She would give one to her Aaji and ask her to make her favourite “Bhoplyacha purya”. “How delicious!” she exclaimed while salivating. She would give a big pumpkin to her Mumma, and ask her to make “Bhoplyachi kheer”. “So yummy and creamy….. I love it”,Said Zuzu. Zuzu thought that she would give some little pumpkins to her Tara Didi. “Didi will be so happy” She murmured. “I am going to ask Tara Didi to make a pumpkin pie for me…… I just can’t wait" Said a very happy Zuzu. I will sell the remaining pumpkins at the wholesale market, said Zuzu. The next morning Zuzu noticed that her little plant had 4 bright yellow flowers. She got so happy and told all her friends and family. She just couldn’t wait until she saw all the pumpkins that she had imagined. But unfortunately her happiness did not last for a long time… After 2 to 3 days her pumpkin vine died. Zuzu was so sad that she started crying. She went to her Baba and told him what had happened to the vine. Baba explained her that she had sowen the seeds in a teeny tiny pot. The pumpkin vine needs a lot of sunlight and water, some fertilizers much more space and soil to grow and nourish. "Your vine didn't get the proper care and nourishment, so it eventually died." Said Baba. “Oooooooooo that’s why it died … oh!! My poor pumpkin vine……..”Replied Zuzu. She thought for a while and said "Ahh!!! Now, I know how what went wrong. Thanks Baba!" The next day she decided to sow some more pumpkin seeds but this time in her Baba's farm so that she could grow the biggest pumpkin ever.....

title: Around the world through Grandma's stories...
text: She refused to come to the city even though Nandhini's dad asked her to come. She will be able to see her grandma only once a year when she comes to the village during her summer holidays. Even during this summer vacation, Nandhini will go to see her grandma. Grandma used to buy a lot of toys for Nandhini to play when she comes during her holidays. Grandma used to tell many stories using them. Grandma used to ask Nandhini to close her eyes while telling stories. She could listen to the stories only while closing her eyes. There was magic in Grandma's words. When she started telling the stories, the scenes happened right in front of them. Once, Grandma took the cycle toy and asked "Did you ride it?" Nandhini felt that she was riding the bicycle and heard the bell ring 'Trinng...Trinng..' When grandma used to tell stories about thunder, they used to hear the noise of thunder "Bang..bang.." A scared Nandhini asked grandma not to say such stories. So, grandma started telling happy stories. Once, when grandma was showing the auto toy, she said that the auto flew like a helicopter. "Trrrruuu..Trrruuu..Trrruuu.." The auto started flying with wings on top of it. Once, when grandma told a story about flying on a broomstick, they were able to feel the wind while flying. The next time, grandma took a small ambulance toy and asked,"Do you know who is going to ride this ambulance toy? It is little Nandhini!" That's it! Nandhini shrunk to the size of the ambulance. Another time, when grandma said that Nandhini and she were riding on a boat, Nandhini was able to imagine fishes jumping near the boat. Here, Nandhini has started by train along with her mother, father and little brother to spend her summer holidays with grandma and her stories. As soon as she reaches the village, she is going to ask for many stories and spend her time with grandma. Yes; where did you go for your holidays?!

title: A Balanced Diet
text: I team, Tarique Aziz, Yuwak Shrestha Translator: Scarlett Schutte There are many types of food in the world, like fruit and vegetables of all different colours. It is very important that boys and girls, like you, eat a variety of foods It is very important that they eat a variety of vegetables. Every vegetable has a benefit for your nutrition. An example is spinach. Spinach has lot of vitamins and has minerals like iron and magnesium. Potatoes have benefits for the body because they contain fibre and potassium. Also potatoes lower the risk of heart disease. Do you know how they say potatoes in Spain? ‘Patatas!’ Carrots have lots of fibre and are a source of potassium and antioxidants. Potassium is good for you because it reduces the risk of strokes and high blood pressure. Carrots are also very good for vision While apples are a fruit, they are also a source of antioxidants and fibre, similar to carrots. Apples can reduce the risk of cancer and diabetes. Bananas are one of the fruits with the most benefits. They give you vitamins, potassium and magnesium. They are also good for your skin and your heart. As well as this, they are good for your digestion and they give you lots of energy. Watermelons are good to eat after exercise or sport because they can help you with hydration given that they are 92% water. Rice and other grains are also important to eat. These foods help you to feel full quicker, especially brown rice. While you can eat meat and dairy products, you don’t need them as much because with more fruit and vegetables, your diet will be healthier. A balanced diet is simple and it is fun to maintain a healthy body and mind. Having a healthy body and mind is very important in life because it will help you to live a longer and healthier life. Questions to discuss: What are the benefits of vegetables? What is your favourite fruit or vegetable? What are the benefits of fruit? What defines a good diet? What foods do you like to eat? Questions to discuss: What special dishes do your family make? What dishes do you know how to prepare? What type of foods are unhealthy? Do you think you have a balanced diet? Do you think Guatemalan food is healthy?
author: Scarlett Schutte

title: I want cake
text: I want cake for breakfast! Mother: No way. You need to eat healthily. Child: Why? Healthy food does not taste good. Cake is very tasty. Mother: It doesn’t matter. But don’t you want to be tall? Child: Yes. Mother: So you need to drink milk and eat vegetables. Milk has calcium which strengthens your bones. Do you want to be strong? Child: Yes Mum. Mother: So you need to eat meat to get protein. If you don’t like to eat meat, you can eat beans for protein. Child: Why is protein important? Mother: Protein is good because it helps you to develop muscles. Child: Tell me more about nutrition. Mother: Do you want to have good vision or be intelligent? Well, eat lots of fruit and vegetables because they have important minerals. Child: I know that carrots help your eyes. Mother: Exactly. Child: I want to grow tall and strong. Mother: That is good but you cannot eat cake for dinner. Child: Okay. I will drink milk. Then I will eat scrambled eggs to get protein and bread to get carbohydrates. I will also cut myself a banana and a strawberry. They are my favourite fruits. Mother: Now if you do this everyday, you will be strong. Questions: What did you eat for breakfast? Do you eat a healthy breakfast? Why is it important to eat healthily? Do you also want to eat cake for breakfast? Should you ever eat cake? Why is protein important? Why are carbohydrates important? What are some healthy foods to eat? Why do you want to eat healthily? What are some of the health problems that develop if you don’t eat healthily?

title: Cookie learns to share
text: Cookie the dog lives with Sahana, Priya, Mom and Dad. Cookie loves Sahana and Priya, and they love her too. They take good care of Cookie and enjoy playing with her. Sahana is Priya's older sister. She likes sharing her things with Priya. Cookie is confused this morning. She notices that something is different. Everyone at home looks very excited. Sahana and Priya whisper every time Cookie comes close to them. Cookie wants to ask Mom what is going on? But, Mom and Sahana say, “Bye Cookie, we will be back soon.” And, they drive off. Dad is making snacks for Priya and Cookie so, they wait by the window. Cookie dashes to the front door when she hears it open. She stops halfway and sniffs. Is it a treat for me?” “Look Cookie, we have a friend for you. Her name is Tootsie. Do you like her?” Asks Priya showing Tootsie to Cookie. Cookie sniffs, gently touches Toostsie, turns away and says. “I like her. But, is she going to live with us forever? I hope not.” After a few days Cookie knows that Tootsie is going to stay. Tootsie says, "Please play with me Cookie." But, Cookie doesn’t want to play or share any toys or treats. She is used to playing and sharing with just Sahana and Priya. Cookie wonders, "Will Sahana and Priya love Tootsie more than they love me?” She thinks, "Do I have to share my toys and share Sahana and Priya with Tootsie?" After a while, Cookie begins to play with Tootsie. Cookie realizes that Sahana and Priya will always love her. They have enough love to give to Tootsie too. Very slowly, Cookie learns to care for Tootsie and share some of her treats and favorite toys. Tootsie asks Cookie, " Can we be friends?" "We are more than friends," says Cookie. "We are a family, and I will share my things with you just like Sahana shares with Priya. Now I know that sharing is caring."
author: Chaya Sheela Ubhayakar

Akka grabbed her work and away they hopped. BOING! BOING! BOING! came Bottu. But all he could see was... Anna's scrunched up ears, Appa's jingling toolbelt, Paati's pom-pom scarf, Thatha's paint-dripping tail, and Akka's noisy anklets disappearing around the corner. “ Wait for me! ” Bottu cried, trailing behind them. BOING! BOING! BOING! Amma was busy in the kitchen. Ahhhh... UMMMM! Just then, Anna, Appa, Paati, Thatha, and Akka ran in. “ Bottu's awake! " they cried. Amma grabbed the bowl and followed behind the rest of the family. HURRRRY, Amma! Boi…ng… boi…ng… boi…ng… came Bottu. Then rahul asked do you know my fathers name is also mohan then they played together one day he fall sick as he was having chills,headache,stomachache,cold and vomiting. He was not well and dind't go to school. Then they went to the docter she said that you are having malaria this is a dieseses in which a mosquito bites a person. And she asked do you apply mosquito cream or were mosquito band?? title: the battle of healthy and junk food.
text: this is a boy his name is rohit he loves junk food he loves chocolate, chips and sweets this is meena she loves to eat healthy food like salad,chappatee and tamato Rohit and Meena started arguing whether Junk was the best or healthy food. Due to this argument disturbing everyone, the Principal of their school casted a magic spell. Rohit and Meena got transported in a game, in which they had to deafet each other's team Rohit's junk friends were too lazy and they did not have the energy to fight, while Meena's healthy friends were full of stamina and were killing all the junkies, with their power.At last Rohit's team was defeated. Meena and her healthy team won the prize. Rohit and Meena came back to their own world. Rohit realized the importance of healthy food. he started eating healthy food. They both promised each other to eat together, and they also planned to have Junk food party once in a month. So eat healthy and stay healthy THANK YOU;)

title: Lido Eats With... ( Read & Illustrate)
text: Lido liked eating. Eating a lot-a lot of everything She liked eating idlis- a lot of those! She liked eating butter-pasta-a lot of those! And she liked eating all of it with -FINGERS! She never used a spoon. Dad didn't like it. He said sternly, " Lido,eat with spoon." Grandmother didn't like it. She said in a miffed tone, " Lido, don't dirty your hands.Use a spoon." Her teacher said gently,'' Lido, use spoon. You're spilling the food." BUT Mom said lovingly," Wow Lido! My grown up girl. You can eat on your own!" Lido enjoyed eating with fingers and licking them. One day Lido and her family went for a picnic. They chose a shady patch, under a tree, beside a lake. Mom spread out the mat. Lido, Grandmother, Dad and Mom sat on the mat. Dad took out the picnic food- Idlis, bread-jam, fried -rice,momos,and Plastic Spoons. The caretaker looked at them. She walked towards them and pointed to a sign board. ' NO PLASTIC ZONE. Use of plastic prohibited'. Spoons went inside the bag. And Dad, Mom, Grandmother and Lido - All ate using FINGERS!! And they all enjoyed it!!

They look beautiful they have beutiful hair with lovely eyes. Sushma said i don't belive in fairy you are a fool. Suman said you alway say that. Suman was little abset so she Saw up, she surpised she said see there sushma was not able to say anything because she saw a beutiful fairy Wow she is so beutiful fairy said i am forest fairy. sushma said i can't belive it. text: One day tara was looking at the fan for a very long time.She wondered "How people invented fans." Tara thinks for a while.Suddenly she thought of an idea."I will make a story about this topic and tell it to my family"she thought. So the next day she started writing the story.The name of the story was "Who invented the fan?"It took one whole day to finish her story. title: Banku and Tornado
text: Banku the bear was going to hunt for food with his friend Sammy the snake as he did not have a family. Banku was grumpy.Blistering wind was making him uncomfortable. ''I would go back to my home if I was feeling like that '' Sammy said.The wind was blowing very hard now. Banku neared to kitty's house. When he reached he saw kitty flying in the wind so banku grabbed her tail. Suddenly the wind stopped. And...THUD!!!!!!! Kitty fell down After that both of them were headed to Banku's cave but when they reached there the cave was not there. They started digging and found his cave. After that day kitty also started living over there. Then they lived happily ever after.

title: Too big, Too small
text: I cannot lift you up", says mother. "You are too big!" "Shanu, you cannot go to school alone!" says father. "you are too small!" "Shanu, you cannot sleep in Babu's crib!" says grandfather. "You are too big!" "Shanu, You cannot carry Babu to the park!" says grandmother. "You are too small!" Shanu was surprised. Too big! Too small! How can she be too big and too small at the same time? Too big to put on her old pink dress. Too small to make Roti in the oven. Too big to climb on grandfather's back? Too small to carry Babu herself? "Am I right for Keka?" thinks Shanu. Mother says laughing, "Why, you are big enough to go to school." "And you are small enough for me to carry you on my shoulder", says father. "You are big enough to go for morning walks with me," says grandfather. "And you are small enough for me to tell you stories," says grandmother. "And you are always good enough for this!" says everyone together, and they hug her warmly.
author: Shinjini Giri

title: Ritus life
text: Once there was a little girl named Ritu. She lived in a village. She was known as the lower cast. She always had to work with her family. All she did was work in the farm, clean dirty places and do all horrible jobs. She was never able to play and go to school like the other kids. Even the upper cast kids did not like the lower cast kids! So we had to play alone together when we were free. So Ritu thought that when she would grow up she would run away from the village and study hard. A few years later Ritu is now 15 and it is night in the village and everyone is asleep. Now Ritu packs her bags and runs away. She finds a hut where she can stay for the rest of the night. Ritu was lucky she saw a school nearby the hut. The next morning Ritu goes to the school for addmisson and the school was nice since they did not care about upper cast and lower cast they thought that they were both equal. Now she enters her class room but the teacher dose not like the lower cast poeple. so he made Ritu stand at the back and study. It was break time. Ritu tryed talking to the other kids but instead of talking with her they bullied her! After school she was finding a job and then a old lady hired her as her maid. Now nobody can stop her from moving ahead! Every day she had to listen to others negitivity but she did not stop! She worked all day and all night she did not give up! She would barely get enough sleep at all! Years pasted she has now graduated and got a job! She has got a job as a... Police! So hard work always brings success!
author: Anushree Paul

title: Birthday of the Bear
text: This story was written in collaboration with a group of boys from ﻿ Patzun ﻿in Guatemala. ﻿ ﻿once upon a time, in the jungle of Guatemala, A bear turned one year old. The bear wanted that day to come, but due to such excitement, he forgot to invite his friends to celebrate. When he realized, on the same day of his birthday, it was too late. He found no friend. The poor little bear became very sad and walked home. He opened the door and suddenly at that moment all his friends screamed... Surprise!! The bear was very happy and said, "Thank you!"

title: Friends
text: Children are best friends. They are seven and eight years old. Friends are very friendly and they meet new friends every day. They want to be friends with the whole school. In the morning, they study with their classmates. They learn math, science, writing, and history. They like science because they can test their ideas. Now her parents are also friends. They perch after school and play soccer. Friends love to talk to each other. Each child has many stories to tell. They make cookies at home with their mom. They want to bring the cookies to share with the entire school. Cookies are very tasty. Sometimes they argue but they will always be friends.

title: Food Folly
text: I sit at the table, but I don't want to eat. Everyone has finished, t heir plates are clean. I sit. I kick my legs. I will not eat. Onion is slimy, coriander tastes like soap. Garlic is stinky, with ginger there is no hope. I nibble on my poli. I paint with the dal. I make the cauliflower into a tree. Baba gets up. Aai cleans the table. Baba says I can have a laddoo w hen I finish my food. Quickly I chew my food, I swallow it down. One, two, three.... twenty bites, food is gone. I am done. Yum, besan laddoo is my favorite.

title: Stay Together
text: The four of us are at the table together. Ajoba is talking to Aai, he sounds loud and tense. Aai looks down, she pecks at her food. She gets up, and walks away in total silence. Now it is three at the table, Ajoba, Ajji and me. I tell Ajoba, I am happy he is here to stay. But when he makes Aai sad, he makes me sad. "I don't want things that way. Please Ajoba, I hope you understand". I go in, Aai is standing at the window, looking away. She sees me, she wipes her face. I stand with her. I give her a tight embrace.
author: Yogita Soman

title: Different and Similar
text: Zoey came to live with Ansh when she was a little puppy. Ansh loves her very much and takes good care of her. Zoey is well behaved and affectionate. She is four years old now. Ansh, Mum and Dad like dogs and cats. So, they bring Billy, the kitten, home. When Billy is introduced to Zoey, she is amazed. "He is so tiny and I am so big. I must look after him." She thinks to herself. Billy is nine months old now. Zoey and Billy have similar trays with bowls for food and water. But the size of the trays and the bowls is different. Zoey has the big tray with big bowls because she is bigger than Billy and needs more food and water than he does. Billy is very curious and likes to look into everything. But, Zoey does not. However, she follows Billy wherever he goes. She knows that he is small and wants to protect him. One day Billy tries to climb over the bathtub to look into it. Zoey stands behind him to make sure that he does not hurt himself. Zoey and Billy know that they have to follow the house rules. Like, when Ansh is in the study room, they cannot go in. One day, Billy sees that Ansh is studying and the door is slightly open. Billy knows that he should not enter. However, he is mischievous, and tries to sneak in. Zoey notices and quickly blocks his way. She knows that Billy is breaking the house rule by going in and will get into trouble. Billy is very fond of Zoey. He knows that she loves him and takes good care of him. He shows his fondness by curling up and snuggling with Zoey every time she lies down. Zoey and Billy are different. Zoey is cream and brown colored Billy is black. Zoey barks and Billy meows. Zoey is well behaved and Billy is mischievous But, they are similar too. They are both animals. They both have four legs and a tail. They both have a nose, two eyes and two ears. And, they both love each other and Ansh very much.
author: Chaya Sheela Ubhayakar

title: Toss the Ball
text: It is a big park. We play in the park. We toss the ball in the park. ﻿ The ball is big. The ball is round. We kick the ball. We throw the ball. We run around the park. We run with the ball. We love to toss the ball.
author: Gauri Mehendale

title: Why Do Crickets Chirp?
text: Critter and Cratter were two crickets who lived in the wild, dark forest. Critter was a girl cricket and Cratter was a boy cricket. Critter was a quiet cricket. Cratter was not. One day, Critter told Cratter, "Let's go out of this forest and do some exploring. Critter wanted to go and see the many other creatures in the world. On the way out of the forest, they met Pipa the elephant. As they were saying goodbye to Pipa, she trumpeted. Critter and Cratter stood and watched with amazement Next, they bumped into Ruby the lioness. She roared. Critter and Cratter laughed instead of getting scared. Ruby smiled. As they entered the village outside the forest, they came across Zeeza the snake. She was sunning herself in the field with her babies. They all hissed. Critter and Cratter said hello! While they passed the village playground, they met Kip-kap the bumble bee. Kip-kap buzzed with excitement. She was very happy to meet other insects. Critter and Cratter waved back! Their next stop was the apple orchard. There they met Flippy the mouse with her children. They all squeaked very loudly. The whole village could hear them. Critter and Cratter closed their ears and giggled. Walking down the road, Critter and Cratter met Clifford the dog. Clifford was a cricket fan and he barked with delight. Critter and Cratter were dog lovers and they scratched Clifford under the chin. Critter and Cratter were now tired. They had met so many animals. But the next minute, they met two humans walking down the street. They spoke and said their names were Yamini and Madhav. Yamini said, "Hello Critter, I have a question for you. Why don't crickets trumpet, roar, hiss, buzz, squeak or bark? Why do crickets chirp?" Critter was puzzled, no one had asked her that before. Madhav had a different question for Cratter. He asked, "Why do only boy crickets chirp? Why don't girl crickets chirp?" Cratter liked Madhav's question. Critter and Cratter looked at each other and said, "We've met so many creatures but only these humans ask us so many questions!" They nodded at each other and said, "We had better explain!" So, Critter and Cratter went to Yamini and Madhav and replied, "You want to know why crickets chirp?" Critter said to Yamini. "Crickets chirp because they can!" And Cratter turned to Madhav and said, "Boy crickets chirp and girls don't because everyone is different and that's just fine!"
author: Yamini Kamath

title: my health my way
text: One day, Ram came running to his mother and told her about his ailing friend Raj. Raj was suffering from constant fatigue and stomach issues. He also told his mother that Raj often misses his school too due to his illness. Ram asked his mother what could be the reason of his illness Mother replied that kids with weaker immunity often fall sick. Ram asked his mom, " what is immunity and how it is related to our health?" Mother explained, immune system in our body helps in fighting against many diseases and to build stronger immunity we should follow a healthy life style. Ram asked, " how can we have a healthy life style? " Mother replied, healthy life style is a combination of balanced diet and excercise. We should eat healthy food like fruits, vegetables, pulses and grains in right proportion for better intake off vitamins, protein and minerals which helps in building stronger immunity, bones and overall health. Ram questioned anxiously,"what all we can do in physical excercise?" Mother said," we can do physical excercise in many ways like - yoga, jogging, skipping or by playing any sport. Ram, we all should engage ourselves in some kind of physical activity and follow healthy food habits. " Ram said excitedly, "mom,now onwards I will never miss my horse riding class as it is my favourite sport and is a great form of excercise " Mother said " Ram today you learnt the importance of health in life. Now let's go to your horse riding class. " Ram said yes mom let's go I want to keep my self healthy in my way.
author: Saanvi Kamalakar
illustrator: Aaryan  Rattewal; Aneesh Jape; Angie & Upesh; Proiti Roy; Siddhi   Vartak; Someone Maybe

title: Grandma and Venki
text: Have you ever been to a trip with your grandma? Have you ever tasted the coconut water? If yes isn't it yummy? This story is all about Venki's excitement for tasting the coconut water for the first time. Venki was again and again insisting his Grandma to go for a trip to the jungle. But grandma was really tired that day and was not that happy and excited for the trip as Venki. Before going to the jungle, Venki saw a coconut tree and asked his grandma to give him the coconut hanging on the tree. Venki did not even knew that it was a coconut and it seemed like a big toffee for him. Grandma decided to climb the tree and bring the coconut for Venki. You can see the efforts made by Venki and his grandma to bring the coconut. It was a fun. Finally grandma brought the coconut and seeing Venki's excitement decided to show him that coconut has some water inside it and it is not a toffee but a fruit. Venki was very happy to see the coconut water and in the excitement he forgot about the trip to jungle. Now Venki and Grandma both were happy even without a trip. Venki and his grandma drank the coconut water and are now eating the coconut happily.
author: Triveni  Gurav

title: The Lost Bruno
text: Once upon a time, there was a girl called Rani. She loves puppies. So her Mom and dad gifted her a puppy. She named him Bruno. She feeds him, puts him to sleep, make him bath and always plays with him. They loved each other so much. One day Bruno got lost. Rani became very sad. She started crying very badly and searched her whole home. But she could not find him. So she told her mom and dad about it. They went out to the street searching him. First, they met a Cat. Rani asked the cat “Catty, did you see my Bruno anywhere?”. Catty told “Yes. He was taken by a girl and a boy in the south direction”. Rani became more sad and started crying. Chamy told “Yes. He was taken by a girl and a boy in the West direction. Bruno was barking a lot”. Rani became more upset and cried very much. She became more angry and wanted to punish the girl and the boy. Then they walked south. Next they met a Chamy, the Chameleon. Rani asked the chameleon “Chamy, did you see my Bruno anywhere?”. Then they walked West. They met a Pagi, the Pigeon. Rani asked the Pigeon “Pagi, did you see my Bruno anywhere?”. Pagi told “Yes. He was taken by a girl and a boy this way. I followed them and found the place where they have him. Come behind me.” Pagi started flying. Rani and her parent followed Pagi. They reached that place. As soon as Bruno saw his family, he jumped out of the gate and ran towards them. Rani became very happy. She made a plan to make Bruno attack them. But dad and mom told rani that it is not good habit. They called police and the kidnappers were arrested. Rani never ever left Bruno alone.
author: Vetha Rithika

title: We are going to the zoo
text: We are going to the zoo What fun it would be! We'd love to see a fox or an elephant reptiles or some honey bee First we saw an elephant taking bananas with its trunk Eating the bananas with the peels biting huge chunk Next we saw a big bee hive But where were all the bees? The bees have all gone away To collect nectar from the flowers on the trees Then we saw two blue birds Sitting on a branch They were invited by their friends For fruit and cherry lunch After that we saw some cranes splashing in the water they were having a party bursting in laughter Next we saw the angry Lion But don't go near the cage It may break open And eat you in a rage Then we saw some playful monkeys swinging from branches having lots of bananas taking munches after munches Finally we saw the giraffe eating leaves from the tall tree It can look over the entire zoo with its long neck Don't you agree?

title: Entrance of Baby's house
text: It is the sound of Amma sweeping the entrance. Here is my little rangoli at the entrance! Amma, Mi.......lk! It is the sound of Alamelu Akka's voice! Akka asks, "Wow, did the baby draw the rangoli?" Thoppp! Baskar Anna threw the newspaper at the entrance! He quickly left on his bicycle. Honk! Honk! Anna's school bus is here! Moorthy uncle asked, "Did baby eat?" "Bye, baby!" Appa is ready to leave! "What does baby want when I come in the evening?" asked Appa. "Tomato! Onion! Carrot!" Kokila aunty's vegetable cart has come. Aunty says, "I heard that baby likes and eats all the vegetables." Tring! Tring! Mani uncle has got the post. Who has sent it? "Aunty has sent Diwali greetings from America," said Amma. Tup! Tup! Tup! There is a knock at the door! Who has come? Our neighbour, Porkodi grandma has come. "Baby's clothes fell into our house, I have brought them," said grandma. Cling! Cling! The sound of glass bangles! Who is that? Aha, aunty! "I have brought payasam for dear baby," said aunty. Kada... Kada.. The sound of the bike at the door! Appa is here! Haiya! Appa has brought a bunch of balloons. Wong! Wong! Today's last guest at the entrance. Bairav! He ate the curd rice served by Amma and slept. Do you know who comes to your house door everyday? Have you met the person who brings milk and the newspaper? Do you know the people who live in the next house and in the opposite house? If you do not know, ask your parents and get to know them!

title: She can
text: T his is M adeline. M adeline is a dancer. S he works hard and practices every day so that she can keep learning new steps in ballet. M adeline likes to do ballet. S he especially loves to preform in a theater in front of a huge audience. N othing can keep M adeline from doing what she loves. H ere is M imi. M imi is a doctor. She works all day long to treat her patients. M imi loves interacting with her patients. Nothing matters more to her than taking care of others. M imi balances all her responsibilities well. She takes care of her family and the hospital too. T his is A nna. A nna is an architect. Some people told her that men are meant to be architects and not women. But A nna did not listen to them. She believes that women can do anything they want to do. A nna loves her job. She is capable of doing it just as well as anyone can. A nushka is an astronaut. She works for ISRO. ISRO stands for Indian Space Research Organization. There are not many women in the field. A nushka is brave and courageous. She used to dream about space and rockets when she was little. Now, her dreams have come true. A nushka loves her job. Madeline, Mimi, A nna, and A nushka are all dedicated, compassionate, and strong women. T hey are leaders in their field and strive to work for the benefit of others. T hey believe in themselves. T hey can achieve anything they set their mind to. And so can you.

title: Gauri's pet

One day Gauri went to the school, and tom ran towards her and then got lost in the way. then when Gauri returned home from school she noticed that her tom was not there, she called out 'tom'! 'tom'! there was no response. she got scared. The next day when she went to the school she was very sad. her teacher called out and asked what had happened, Gauri told everything,that what had happened. Then suddenly a girl came in with a pet dog and asked,' whose pet is this '? and then Gauri looked at the pet and smiled, oh this is my pet!. and once again Gauri and tom stayed happyly! THANK YOU!

title: Ulysses
text: Ulysses is my cat. He is 7 years old and he is very sweet. He loves eating, his favourite food is fish. One day I cooked an octopus. It looked delicious! Unfortunately I left the kitchen, just for a while, because the phone rang and I had to answer it. When I came back, this is what I found: My cat was hiding under the sofa and the octopus had disappeared! He had eaten all of it!!! So I prepared a stew with what I had! Ulysses went to sleep, thinking I had forgotten everything about it! But, he was wrong! In the evening he came miaowing because he wanted to eat again but I didn't feed him. He had had enough for that day, don't you agree? So he left to look for food outside! But then he came back and after playing with me, he jumped on his cat bed and fell asleep.

title: TRUMPET ELEPHANT THE FIRST BOOK OF THE SERIES
text: THIS STORY'S NAME IS TRUMPET ELEPHANT THE FIRST STORY Once a upon a time there lived a baby elephant it is the king elephant's son. the baby elephant's name is sprad it always carries people like given a picture example. one day it's birthday came!. even in that day sprad was working very hard. after his work had been finished he was crying 'why every Day I am working so hard'. before sprad was sleeping a doorbell came in a sad face he went to see who is that suddenly nobody was there then he was about to close the door that time every elephants, his friends, his parents made sprad afraid and gave him a better day by celebrating his birthday.
