text: Mandy is a cute child who loves to catch honey bees. Mandy don't scare to any one whether it is honey bees! Sometimes she becomes sad sad and sad!!! She loves to see ants in the garden. Mandy's mama also loves to see it!! Sometimes she use to cry very loudly! AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!! A lot of time mandy becomes very lazy. Mandy loves bread with honey becomes it is too much funny!!!! Mandy's whole family likes honey as they have so much money! Thanks
author: Suman  Rai

title: My Clean Buddies...!
text: Hi! I am Munna. I love to wake up early in the morning. This is my friend 'Twisty the Toothbrush'. It helps me to brush my teeth twice a day. This is my friend 'Soppy the Soap '. It helps me to clean my body and keeps me away from the viruses. Hey Whippy.. Wait! Wait! hee hee hee.. This is my friend 'Whippy the Towel.' After the shower, it wipes my body dry. Oh... Buddy... Slowly! Slowly! This is my friend 'Buddy the Earbud.' It removes my earwax and keeps my ears always clean. Look, friends! This is my friend 'Nikky the Nail cutter'. It helps me to cut my nails very carefully...! The Clothes are my friends too. They help me look neat and tidy. Hurry up... Harry...! This is my friend 'Harry the Hair brush'. It combs my hair nicely! This is my friend 'Snowy the Shoes'. They protect my feet! Now, Come on Snowy...! We have to go to School. Bye. Bye.
author: Rasika Rewale

title: Disagreement Among Occupations
text: In a village there was a disagreement among people of different occupations. Everyone thought their work was the most important! The teacher said that he had the most important occupation. “Without teachers you could not go to school and learn.” The builder said that he had the most important occupation. “Without builders you would not have schools to learn in or houses to sleep in.” The carpenter said that he had the most important occupation. “Without carpenters you would have no furniture for your houses and schools.” The doctor claimed that he had the most important occupation. “Without doctors and nurses you could get sick and die.” The farmer said that she had the most important occupation. “Without farmers you would not have food to eat.” The student argued that students had the most important work. “Without students, there would be no teachers, builders, doctors, farmers, or carpenters.” Eventually everyone agreed that all the occupations are important. We need teachers, builders, doctors, farmers, and carpenters. But everyone has to be a student first!
author: Beatrice Inzikuru

title: Emotions Come and Go
text: Ada is chuckling because she heard a funny story. She is smiling. What is Ada feeling? Gisa is feeling grumpy. He has a scowl on his face. Why is he irritated? Yuadoo is scared of the dark. Everyone feels fear sometimes. But Yuadoo can ask for help. Chidubem is worried about his school work. He can tell his teacher. He can ask for help. Lushan is playing around! It's okay to be silly sometimes. Eruro is feeling sad. It's okay to cry. Emotions come and go. Ayator is bursting with happiness. He is joyful. Emotions come and go. Hadiza is bored. She needs to find something to do. Ayo is angry. He is frustrated. Anger is a difficult feeling. Labake is excited. What's the cause of her excitement? Mother made her favourite food. Zege felt sleepy. He was very tired. "But wait, is 'sleepy' an emotion?" asks Efe. Efe is confused! Can you answer his question? Tega is feeling surprise and shock. He heard some gossip. Is it true? Yebo is sick. She feels miserable. She needs some medicine and rest to feel better. Sekyen is feeling content. She has finished her chores. Now she can play. Vandefan does not have chores today. He shows two thumbs up to Sekyen. "Good job, now let's play!" he says.
author: Mimi  Werna

title: Goat, Dog and Cow
text: Goat, Dog and Cow were great friends. One day they went on a journey in a taxi. They reached the end of their journey. The driver asked them to pay their fares. Cow paid her fare. Dog paid extra, because he did not have the correct money. The driver was about to give Dog his change. Suddenly Goat ran away without paying. The driver was very annoyed. He drove away without giving Dog his change. That is why, even today, Dog runs towards a car to peep inside. He is looking for the driver who owes him change. Goat runs away from the sound of a car. She is afraid she will be arrested for not paying her fare. Cow is not bothered by cars. Cow takes her time crossing the road. She knows she paid her fare in full.
author: Fabian Wakholi

title: Elephant and the lion
text: Once upon,a time there used to be lion and he always thinks that he is the only king of the world. But one day he saw a elephant carrying a person so he goes running to the elephant and asks him "hey elephant why are you carrying a unknown person i should be the one you should carry not him"said the lion with a greedy face. So he starts climbing the elephant. But the elephant with anger drops the lion onto the ground and tells him with a annoyed face "why should i carry you you are just a failure you are not as great as my king at all."said the elephant with anger. And then a monkey comes and laughs at the lion who as fallen onto the ground. The lion "but i am a"the elephant left without letting the lion finish the sentence. Monkey asks him why did the elephant throw the lion onto to the ground so then lion answers"he is not listening to me even thought i am a king what should i do"asks the lion. The monkey answers "my lord prove him that you are a king so that he can trust you."answers the monkey. So the king takes the advice and goes into his den to sleep. He dreamed about him being the greatest king and then he goes back to sleep. The next morning he see's the elephant still carrying the human king around. The lion felt sad and he goes back into the den feeling when will the elephant believe that the lion is also the king of animals. The lion kept on thinking solutions for the elephant on trusting the lion. So the lion was fed up of this situation. He went near the elephant the next morning the lion goes to the elephant and tells him that he is the king of the jungle. At that time he did not believe the lion at that sudden moment a wasp comes and pokes the elephant and the elephant jumps and yells and throws the man to the ground but the lion runs and saves the person. So the elephant starts to believe that the lion is the king and carries him. So the elephant felt shame on himself and apologizes the lion and carries him high and even the lion apologizes for being very greedy and gets to know there are many other better kings too. And then both of them become the best friends.
author: Rithvik Chowdary

title: Father, Son and Donkey
text: A father, his son and their donkey started a long journey. On the way, some people asked them why they didn't ride the donkey. The father invited his son to ride the donkey while he walked. They continued like this for a while. Then, other people they met remarked, "Look at this rude boy riding a donkey while his father is walking!" As a result, the son jumped down and his father rode the donkey. They continued their journey. After some time, other people said, "Look at this rude father riding a donkey while his son is walking!" So the father and son decided to ride the donkey together. But a few minutes later, some people remarked, "Look at these rude people! There are going to kill the donkey. Finally, father and son understood that they could not escape from people's remarks. They decided to use their own minds to do the right thing.
author: Tagel Aboneh

title: Buzzing Bee
text: A busy little bee, flutters from flower to flower. Buzz! Buzz! Buzz! Hardwork is your power. Roll in yellow pollen and drink nectar golden. The flowers turn to fruits! You are natures magician. At the end of the day, you rush back to the hive. In a honey comb lyre, sweet secrets you hide. Then dance with your friends and sing songs of new life.
author: Medha Agarwal

title: Annual Haircut Day- ONCE AGAIN!
text: I must cut my hair on this Annual Haircut Day!” “Well, don’t ask me! ” Parvatamma declared."You know I have so much extra work now. There is the cooking and the cleaning and the farm work. Today, I have no time to cut such long hair.” “Why should I need you?” asked Sringeri, puzzled. “As usual, I will go to Bhimanna, the barber.” OHO! Suddenly, he remembered. Bhimanna’s shop was closed. It was because of the COVID-19 pandemic. There was a lockdown everywhere. The village, the country, and in fact, the whole world was troubled because of one little virus, named SARS-CoV-2. Sringeri Srinivas peeped out from his gate. The main road of the village was quiet. He could see the closed barbershop in the distance. Out came Sringeri’s famous frown. “Hmmph!” he growled. “Am I going to let one tiny little virus prevent me from keeping my promise to my Gods? Never!" He picked up his phone and called Bhimanna. "You know, it is my Annual Haircut Day today. Can you help me?” In a kind voice, Bhimanna replied, “Sringeri Anna, you know I cannot help you this time. It is dangerous for both of us.” “What shall I do? Nobody will help me now,” wailed Sringeri. Suddenly, little Uma stepped up bravely to her angry father. “Appa, until the lockdown is over, why don’t you try a new hairstyle? We will help you.” Soon, the children had crowded around their father. Shiva checked the internet to find ways to style hair. Shankari pulled out a chair, a comb, and a mirror. Little Uma found some pins and ribbons. The children had a jolly time, styling Sringeri’s long, thick hair into many, many shapes. It was the best time the family had enjoyed since the lockdown. “Idea! Idea! I have an idea!” shouted Sringeri, jumping out of the chair. All the combs and pins and ribbons went flying about. Sringeri Srinivas stormed out of his house and out of the farm gate, right on to the village street. “ Devare! My Gods!” he said, waving his hands at the sky. “I have an idea.” Sringeri Srinivas was so loud, that all the villagers peeped out of their homes. Youngsters came out, wearing masks. The cows ambled up. The monkeys swung by. The birds flew closer. The dogs pricked up their ears. After so many weeks, something was happening in the village. Everyone was curious. “ Devare, I had made a promise to you that I would cut my hair on this auspicious day every year. But now, because of this... this virus-birus, I cannot get a good haircut,” Sringeri explained. "So, I am making a new promise. Until our scientists find a cure for this illness, I will NOT cut my hair. Even if it becomes as long as the... as the king cobra in my cousin’s village, I will not cut my hair until our scientists succeed." "And I will make a donation to help them too,” Sringeri swore, putting his hand to his heart. The whole village roared in approval. Somebody picked up a drum. Byrappa began to sing. The little children began to dance. Soon the news spread far and wide. Sringeri Srinivas was doing a special penance for the health of his village, and of the world! When the lockdown lifted a little, they came to see Sringeri Srinivas’s long, amazing hair. Many villagers were inspired to grow their own hair! “I hope our scientists find a cure soon,” prayed Parvatamma, standing outside the village temple. “I really hope so too,” whispered Bhimanna, the barber.
author: Rohini Nilekani

title: Scientific fun that whistles
text: Nivi was tapping the feet on the floor rhytimically. she was waiting for the cooker to whistle. Suddenly a idea struck her. Nivi kept the chapati rolling pin near the knob of the gas stove. After that she lined up the tomatoes and potatoes. After that she took the spatula used for mashing lentil juice. Nivi, placed it very carefully on the edge of the spoon board that was above the cooker. Near by she made her grandmother's five table spoons to stand by in a line. Her grandmother uses these tablespoons to drink the soup At last Nivi kept her favorite plastic ball on the spoon board directly above the steam outlet of the pressure cooker. Shh! The ball is moving a little. Shhh! The ball is moving a little more. Shhhh!Third time the ball rolled off. Nivi jumped in joy, clapped, danced and whistled. The ball rolled and hit the tablespoons. The tablespoons fell on the spatula. The spatula rolled and fell down from the spoon board. DONG! The spatula made the potatoes to roll. The potatoes rolled and pushed the tomatoes. The tomatoes piled on the rolling pin. The rolling pin knocked the knob of the gas stove. The knob rotated and gas stove also turned off. After few minutes, Nivi carefully opened the pressure cooker. Inside was delicious cooked rice. Yummy! Nivi happily started reading her book again. Install a machine yourself by your Genius Nivi, installs a type of machine named " Roop Goldberg". It works on the principle of "Action and Effect". It is similar to that of playing a carom board game. In the carom board, when you strike a coin it hits the other coin, the second coin is moved and made to fall into the bag. In a " Roop Goldberg" machine, the easiest task are done in a complicated way. All the objects that are launched to do, together reach a common goal in a complex way. Some tasks can be done in a simple way. But, is it not fun to set up a machine to do a task? To make a spatula fall you can devise a "Roop Goldberg" machine by yourself. Like this only. THINGS NEEDED A thin book rolled up like a cylinder- 1 A smooth sticks that are placed in a slanting manner -2 Thick books -2, Measuring Scale -2, Marker - 1 Eraser -1, Ball -1, Note Books -3, A light plastic jar -1, Rope Bundle -1, Table Spoons -1, Bowl -1 Light Stick -1. Roll the book which is rolled like the cylinder down the slope. The cylinder will hit the two books that is placed there. The books will hit the ruler that is balanced like a measuring pan on the top of the marker. Because of this the ball will be tapped lightly. Now the ball will hit the three note books. They will fall on the tip of the second ruler which is balanced like a measuring pan at the top of the eraser. The jar which is placed at the other end of the ruler is attached to a piece of rope. The piece of rope hangs over the thin rod at the top. When the third note book falls on the ruler, it lifts the jar,lowers the rope and makes the table spoon to fall into the bowl
author: Vidya Srinivasan

title: My aunt
text: My aunt has ears that listen, arms that hug and hold, a love that's never-ending, and a heart that is made of gold. BLESSINGS TO HAVE A AUNT Aunt - a double blessing. You love like a parent and act like a friend you are the best. I smile because you are my aunt. I laugh because there is nothing you can do about it! Only an Aunt can give hugs like a Mother. Keeps secrets like a Sister, and share Love like a Friend. HOW MUCH I LOVE MY AUNT For My Aunt, no one in the whole wide world could love you more than me cause you are as sweet and nice as any aunt could ever be. I love you..... passed the moon and the stars, the planets and the sun wrapped around everything times twenty million, bajillion times infinity! That is how much I love you aunt. Praising my aunt If you think I am perfect you should see my aunt. People say I am perfect because I am the best aunts nephew. Just like parents, aunts know the importance of instilling proper behavior and manners. However, they usually take a gentler approach to discipline than parents. They can teach their niece or nephew a lesson without resorting to threats or shouting. I love that you are my aunt. Aunt is a safe haven for a child. Someone who will share secrets with you and always be on your side. Happiness is being an auntie. I have a beautiful aunt. The one who never grew old her smile is made of sunshine and her heart is made of gold. Aunt is a sunshine in a heavy rain. I love my aunt she is simply amazing and I just can not imagine my life without her. My aunt brightens the day by being herself. Your aunt is both your mirror and your opposite. Be jealous I have the best aunt in whole world. Aunt's are like flowers that brighten your day. An aunt is a gift whose worth cannot be measured except by your heart. Aunts are joined from heart to heart. Aunt is like a mom but she is cooler. For everything in life that your parents say no just call your aunt. Aunts fill our heart with happiness and coolness. My aunt will support me untill I die. My aunt is my friend forever. I will pray to god every single day of my life for giving me such a nice aunt. My aunt has a nose to smell and two hands to give me a tight hug. You are the best flower in my heart aunt I love you most........ She is the one you go to for your advice.... She is the one you love to play with.... She is the one you call when you're helpless.... She stands up for you in front of your parents.... She is the one you look up to.... She helped you understand your parents very very well...... An awesome aunt can be a lifelong mentor for any kid. Now, as an aunt to one nephew, I'm starting to understand what it takes to earn the title of “ Cool Aunt.” Being a cool and involved aunt is a choice.... But it's a boon to nieces and nephews, as well as their parents....... 1)Have Fun, Make Memories.... 2) Be A Good Example.... 3) Shape Their Interests.... 4) Give Thoughtful Gifts.... 5) Be One Of Them.... 6) Follow Parents' Rules.... 7) Offer To Babysit.... 8) Always Keep Your Promises. An aunt is someone special to remember with warmth, think of with pride, and cherish with love. My aunt also loves me the most...... Aunts play a unique role in a child's life. It's a special calling. Some women “ aunt ” as second mothers, friends, or teachers. They give an extraordinary kind of love to their nieces and nephews. Parents teach and advise their kids, grandparents spoil them, and aunts provide all of this to their nephews and nieces............ To the best aunt ever, thank you so much for everything in life. Love you loads and hope you will always be there for me when I need you. Thank you my lovely aunt for showing me how to be a good person and making some exquisite memories. You are my sunshine on a cloudy day and I love spending time with you. You have showed me all the good things in life and always helped I love you the most and you are the best aunt in the world. I have always done mistakes and you have corrected it I do not care about how other people feel about you but I feel you are the best aunt I have ever seen.
author: Omkrishna melanta

title: The Lion, The Horse and The Jealous Minister
text: Once upon a time, in the lion king's court there lived a fox who was a minister.One day the king was feeling very lonely so he asked his minister to make an announcement, that the animal who will prove to be a true friend to the king will be greatly rewarded. Anyone who wants to participate must report in the garden behind the palace. Every animal trusted the king so all the animals decided to participate. They all reached the garden behind the palace early next morning. The king came out of his palace and took a look at the animals. At the end of the line he noticed a shining brown horse. He went near the horse and asked him ''why do you want to become my friend.'' To this the Horse replied''even I am a very lonely animal and am in need of a friend.'' The lion decided to make the horse his special friend and soon they did everything together which made them very close friends. The minister was very troubled because he wanted to dethrone the king and become the king himself and for this he had to come very close to the king which he could not do in the presence of the horse. The minister decided to take help from the intelligent monkeys in return of 100 bananas. He rushed towards the monkeys with the offer of a 100 bananas for an idea. The greedy monkeys gladly agreed. They started thinking, then suddenly a young monkey had an idea he shared his idea with everyone ''why don't you push the king and his irritating friend into the valley of wonders.'' The plan was made that the minister was going to take the king and the horse out for a walk along the valley of wonders and when nobody is looking he would push the king and the horse into the valley of wonders. They thought this to be a full prove plan but a deer heard their conversation while she was passing by and made a great hole in their plan by telling the horse and the king every single word she heard. The horse and the king decided to back fire this plan on the minister. The next morning when the minister asked the king and the horse to come for a walk with him both of them happily agreed. When the trio reached the valley of wonders the fox started running towards the king and the horse but both of them were ready for this so when the fox was about leap at them they moved out of the way and the fox fell into the valley of wonders 6 months later the fox soon recovered from his fall down the valley of wonders, and as he wanted to dethrone the king he was sealed inside a water melon for 2 years as a punishment. As there was vacancy for an attendee the horse was made minister. The king and the new minister always remained best friends.
author: Shradha Pattanaik
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Kishor Joshi; Mdu Ntuli; Rohit Bhasi; Siddhi   Vartak; Wiehan de Jager

title: The missing wooden doll
text: Once upon a time there was a silly girl called Lathika. People called her Laughable Lathika. She used to make funny faces and make sad people cheerful again. She loved to talk to her friends when they were sick and sad. She had a favourite toy, a little wooden doll. One sunny day Lathika was cheering up a sick friend and she went to take her wooden doll and it was not there but Lathika was not affected she said- " I know it will be here let me go to my room." But it was not there it used to be on the little shelf what her dad built for her. Lathika said in a cheerful voice-" hahaha dad must have hid it let me go ask him" Lathika went to her living room and saw her brother Lakshman and her Father Ram she used to think she was in the Ramayana because her brother and her father s names are from the characters of the epic Ramayana. Then she said- "dad did you take my wooden doll please I really want it!" Her father scolded- "No lathika i have not seen it and you are 10 years old you have to take care of your things! Her 5 year old brother followed- "Yes lathika always take care of your things! Lathika sat by the window and sighed this is the first time she was sad! She thought to herself- "where could it be?" Then her mom came in a cheerful voice she asked-" lathika did you see so many people eating my tasty fresh hot gulab jamun?" Lathika said in a sad voice- "Nice mummy you make the best sweets in town...." Her mom said-" ohhh Lathika my beautiful girl what is wrong?" Lathika murmured- "m... my doll i-is missing." Her mother gasped-"What really?!" Then lathika said in a strict voice- "why will I be joking mummy!!!!" Then her mother started chuckling-" ohhh latika what day is it?" Lathika annoyed said-"what mummy my birthday?!" Her mother said smilng- April fooled hahaha! oh my god lathika how can you fall for this!" Lathika s eyes grew wide and opened her mouth wide it looked like she was about to scream but then it was just a loud laugh HAHAHAHAHAHA Her mom said- "your dad was also in this and even your little brother!" Lathika said-"then where is my doll?" Her mother handed it to her. Then our cheerful lathika was back on track. She hugged her family and all was well she enjoyed this day.
author: Ew NO
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; Angie & Upesh; Jemma Jose; Kavya  Bagga; Melany  Pietersen; Shreya Shruti

title: Why Hyenas Limp
text: Many years ago, hyenas were starving. Because of a famine, even goats, sheep and cows migrated to other places. Hyenas had nothing to eat. They gathered in one place to discuss the issue. One of the hyenas said, "In our culture, we eat anything that is fleeing. Look, these clouds are fleeing." This hyena believed that the clouds were migrating to another place. He said, "Let's eat them." Immediately, all the hyenas looked up and saw the clouds moving in the sky. One of the youngest hyenas asked, "How do we reach the clouds? They are very far away from the ground." The oldest hyena said, "Let the strongest hyena stand on the ground and then let the rest of us stand on each other's backs. We will climb on one another's backs until we reach the clouds." They agreed and started climbing up on one another's backs. Soon, there were no more hyenas left remaining on the ground except the strongest one. After the last hyena climbed up, the hyena on the ground thought that the others had started eating. He asked, "Why don't you give me some of the food you're eating?" However, the hyenas did not reach the clouds. They didn't find any food and so they had nothing to give to the strongest hyena standing on the ground. The strongest hyena became impatient and moved to the left side. All the others came falling down to the right side. As a result, even today all hyenas limp on their right side.
author: Oda Wako Genale

title: Kaju finds a way to deal with mommy's anger
text: Kaju is a 6 year old girl, who lives with her mom, dad, dada and dadi in small town called Ramgarh Cantt which is situated 45 km away from Ranchi, Jharkhand. Fun Fact: Did you know- Mahendra Singh Dhoni is an Indian cricketer from Ranchi, Jharkhand. Kaju has been at home since the last few months because of the coronavirus pandemic. She has been doing her online classes, writing online exams and playing all by herself with her toys. It's not easy for her mom to copy all the questions posted by the teacher everyday. Her mom gets so tired after long day of working in the kitchen. Kaju knows that now a days mom gets very angry when she asks for any help again and again. Today evening mom was very tired and Kaju could not figure out how to add three digit sums given by the teacher. Mom got very angry and she was about to scream at Kaju when Kaju had an idea. She said "Ma, count from 10 to 1, please! Ma count". The mother got really confused but she started counting backwards and guess what by the time she reached one her anger had vanished. Next day, Kaju knew what to do when mom gets angry or when dad's get angry she was happy, she had a solution finally. But sometimes it was not that easy and the adults would refuse to count. So, she found another way. Kaju would say" Ma, I think I want to use the loo" and she would go and sit with her Dadi till her mom cools down. This trick also worked. Kaju realised that adults get angry sometimes but it is important to remind them to calm down. She understands that everyone is stressed these days because they cannot go out and they have to help kids with their studies as schools are closed. She has decided that she will help the people around her to calm down when they are stressed. There are times when Kaju does not know what to do so she goes to other adults in her house to relax. She has also learnt that yoga and music helps people to calm down and now she has made a point to do yoga with her parents and they listen to calming music together. Kaju's message to all the kids is to help people around them to calm down by applying the above strategies.
author: Priyanka M

title: Scientist's Science
text: Chantu was a little curious boy.He was always mistreared. In his school progress he always use to get O+.He use to read many popular books for adults. ﻿Even famuos scientist tested his brain he was normal. ﻿A boy who is jealous of Chantu"s intelligence tried to copy,but Chantu knows some one would copy him.He wisely turned his paper and the other boy could not copy him. ﻿To trick Chantu one boy came and asked him "Which is the last number"?Chantu answered there is no end for numbers.The other boy was shoked. ﻿One day Chantu recieved the Padma Bhooshan award and may gifts and boquets.
author: Podicheti Sreevathsaa
illustrator: Christabel Shin; Sanjay Kisku; SRIJAN TRIVEDI; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Sukhada Rahalkar; Vibha Lohani

title: How I caught a gang of thieves
text: Hello Everyone, I am Ratna. I live in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. I like the place where I live a lot. But the problem is that Nehru Colony, the street where I live is full of thieves. Everyday many houses and malls get robbed. Not only that, half of the jewelry shops on the streets are completely empty. I have grown up all around robbers, and that is not a good way to grow up. It's really scary when you know that there are many robbers around you, but you are not sure where exactly they are or when they will spring up on you to steal your valuables. Robberies are so frequent in Nehru Colony that you could compare it with rain in Cheerapunji. One day the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh had an announcement to make, He told every body that the opening ceremony of the Nehru Antique Museum was to take place in 2 weeks, and that everyone living in Noida must attend it. The Antique museum was being made since 2 years and now it is ready. The museum is filled with priceless antiques and arts. I am so excited. I am excited but also worried as I said the antiques in the museum are priceless and there are many thieves in Noida, and I am pretty sure they will try to rob the museum. I hope they keep tight security over the antiques. The thief gang must be planning their tactics to steal the antiques. Today is the day we are going to the antique museum and I am not at all worried about the security of the antiques because I am ready with my full proof plan. Did not understand, let me explain, but before you listen to my plan I am going to tell you what tools I am going to use to chase the thieves. 1. A very cute look that can melt even iron. 2. Pepper spray 3. 10 handkerchiefs I will need my cute look to make the camera in charge of the antique museum to give me the CCTV computer. After getting the computer I will check where the thefts are taking place. After confirming where the thefts are happening I will confirm who exactly the thieves are, then I am going to practically do a surgical strike on them, their eyes can stand gold,copper,and silver but I am pretty sure that their eyes won't be able to stand pepper spray. The next day, after getting into the museum I rushed towards the CCTV computer control room, I didn't need my cute look because I didn't see anyone in the control room! I started checking the CCTV footage and found out that in every section a man dressed in black was stealing some antiques. I smiled as they didn't know what they had gotten themselves into. I sneaked out of the control room and made my way towards the first section. In the hustle and bustle, I spotted the black thief pretty easily. I took out my pepper spray and sprayed a little of the pepper spray in the thief's eyes and tied his mouth before he could scream. I did the same with the rest of the 7 thieves then I called the police. 5 months have past since I caught those thieves. They turned out to be Noida's most wanted thieves.The Police decided that I should be rewarded. They gave my parents One lakh rupees as reward amount for my act of bravery. This week I am going to Delhi to receive the National Bravery Award from the President of India.
author: Shradha Pattanaik
illustrator: Ann Maria; Arindam Dhar; Kavya  Bagga; Magriet Brink; Manavee Chadrasena; Melvyn  Naidoo; Niloufer Wadia; Noorain   Ahmed; Smitha Shivaswamy; Subinita Deshaprabhu

title: The Boy who knew the Language Of Dogs
text: Once there was a boy who knew the language of dogs. He was always made fun of by his friends because he was special and the others were ordinary. As a result, he was always sad. Luckily, he had a dog as a friend. He spent his days taking him out for walks from morning till evening. At night, he would cuddle up with his dog and go to sleep, dreaming that everyone would stop making fun of him and that they would let him play with them. He would rather grin in his sleep when he was dreaming.The little boy's dog slept as still as a statue and the boy used to ruffle his fur like it was a soft cushion. One day, the boy and his dog were on their daily walk when the dog saw another dog. Days passed and the little boy's friends realized that they shouldn't have made fun of the boy and sought forgiveness. The boy forgave them and everyone lived happily ever after. title: Fruits of Freedom
text: Wamaitha and her grandchildren sat outside her house. The children were excited because they really enjoyed listening to their grandmother's stories. Wamaitha began, “Long, long ago.” She paused and looked at her grandchildren's faces glow with curiosity. Wamaitha continued to tell the story: “In the early 1960s beyond the hills and valleys was a village called Mongu. For years, it had been invaded by people from Kitwe village. The people in Mongu were forced to work for long hours with little pay. All they produced was taken to Kitwe village. The little that remained was sold to members of Mongu village at high prices.” One night in 1963, the people of Mongu held a secret meeting with the consent of their masters from Kitwe. They had decided enough was enough and wanted back their land. They sat and began to weigh the odds of them winning. They knew Kitwe had a strong army and better weapons. They began to put ideas across but time flew fast and they had no solution. Just as they were about to give up, a young man stood up and said, “I think I know a way.” They were all curious and asked, “Tell us!” The young man began, “My grandfather told us about a man named Ubuntu who lives across the forest. He grows a fruit called Freedom which gives people strength to do anything. Let us find this man.” They were all silent and did not know what to do. Since no one else had a better idea, they said, “You go and find this Ubuntu.” The young man set out to find Ubuntu. After five days of going through the forest he came across big house. He was very happy. He found an elderly man. The man asked, “What do you want?” The young man answered, “I want Freedom.” Immediately he said that, the man's eyes grew bigger. It was so long since anyone had gone in search of the fruit. They talked for a long time. Ubuntu decided to give the young man the fruit. He said, “Listen carefully. Once you eat this fruit you will acquire wisdom and knowledge which will help you to lead your people to independence. This fruit will make you the leader of your people. Rule them with humility.” He handed a fruit in the shape of a grape and added, “Follow my instructions and your land will prosper. Now, go and tell no one about me.” The young man went back to Mongu. Just as the old man had said, they were able to chase the people of Kitwe away and get back their land. A celebration was held in the whole land. The young man was praised for his courage. He became the first King of Mongu village. As king, he was wise enough to rule his people well. He served them with humility and considered them in every action he took. THE END. Wamaitha said, “My dear grandchildren, the fruit of freedom comes to each one of us at a given point. Be wise enough to use it well. Remember your actions do not only affect you but everyone around you.” Satisfied and happy, the grandchildren went into the house. Wamaitha sat back and watched them go. She hoped the stories she told them every day would build them into better people and leaders for tomorrow.
author: Rose Mburu

title: Polygon Family
text: “This year we are going to have a special family gathering,” announced Mom Polygon. “Who is coming? I hope all the Polygons will be there. I miss my cousins,” said Khosi. “I miss my side of the family the most, the Quadrilaterals,” smiled Mom. “Yes, it’s a long time since we saw Rectangle, Square, and Rhombus,” said Dad Polygon. “Don’t forget, they have three children now!” Mom reminded Dad. “What about cousin Scalene and her children? Are they coming?” asked Vusi. Mom answered, “Yes, they are Polygons, although they are not Quadrilaterals. Their surname is Triangle. The kids are Isosceles and Equilateral.” “Oh yes, the Triangle family!” exclaimed Vusi. “But they look a lot like the Quadrilaterals.” “No, not exactly,” said Mom. “Triangles have three sides, while the Quadrilaterals have four sides, like me.” Dad Polygon added, “I am excited because my three other cousins will be here, they are Pentagon, Hexagon and Octagon. They are also part of our Polygon family.” Vusi asked, “Dad, why we are called Polygons?” “We are called polygons because we are 2-dimensional shapes. We are made of straight lines, and our shape is closed, as you can see, all our lines join up. Our cousins the Triangles, the Quadrilaterals, the Hexagons and the Pentagons will all be visiting,” replied Dad. “Did you say that is Octagon coming? Is she also our relative?” asked Khosi. “Of course my daughter, by just looking at her you can see she belongs to our family. You need to look carefully at the number of sides your cousins have, otherwise you might not be able to see the difference. Cousin Octagon has eight sides because her name starts with Octa,” said Dad. “Okay, what about Pentagon and Hexagon?” asked Vusi. “Cousin Hexagon has six sides because his name starts with Hexa,” replied Dad. “Pentagons have five sides. Our teacher told us that Penta means ‘five’,” added Khosi. “And remember that Tri means three and Quad means four. That’s what makes your Triangle and Quadrilateral cousins look different,” said Mom. “Dad, how many sides does Heptagon have?” asked Vusi. Dad laughed and said, “I am not going to tell you. Remember we took a photograph with them at your uncle's wedding. I want you to look at the photograph carefully and tell me what you observe.” Vusi looked at the photograph and quickly answered, “Heptagon has seven sides!” Khosi added, “Yes, remember our teacher told us that Hepta means ‘seven’.” “Oh my wife, can you see how clever our children are? Okay, what about Deca, what does it mean?” questioned Dad. “Ten! Ten!” shouted Vusi and Khosi together. “Yes, that's why one of your cousins is called Decagon, but he is not coming because he has to represent the swimming team. There are so few Decagons at their school,” Mom told them. Then the children asked, “Mom and Dad, can we invite our friend Circle from next door?” Their parents agreed that Circle was welcome to join the family gathering. Just then they heard a knock at the front door, and Dad got up to check. “The Quadrilaterals are here! Welcome! Welcome” called Dad. The rest of the family jump up to greet Square, Rectangle and the three Rhombus children. The Quadrilaterals are happy to arrive first. The Triangle family knock on the door soon after the Quadrilaterals. Scalene, Isosceles and Equilateral are tired after their long journey, but they are so pleased to be with the rest of the family. Finally, Octagon and Heptagon arrive with their children, two Pentagons and Hexagon. They have also brought three Squares with them. Octagon explained, “I hope you don’t mind that three Quadrilateral children from the village have come with us. They have never visited the city before.” “Friends and family are always welcome here,” smiled Mom. Then she sent all the children outside to play. “What game are we going to play?” Vusi asked the other children. Equilateral squealed, “Let's play the tessellation game!” All the Polygon children started to tessellate. “Can I play with you? I also want to tessellate,” said Circle. Vusi said, “Shame, I’m sorry you can't tessellate my friend.” One of the Squares added, “Can’t you see your shape, you are not a Polygon. Circles can't tessellate.” Circle was sad and felt left out. It's not so much fun playing together when someone is left out. Vusi said, “Hey guys, let's rather play a game that Circle can also play.” So the Polygons and Circle played happily together until the delicious food was ready.
author: African Storybook Initiative; Lindiwe Tshabalala

title: Grandma's Bananas
text: Grandma's garden was wonderful. It was full of sorghum, millet, and cassava. But best of all were the bananas. Although Grandma had many grandchildren, I secretly knew that I was her favourite. She invited me often to her house. She also told me little secrets. But there was one secret she did not share with me. Where she ripened bananas. One day I saw a big straw basket placed in the sun outside Grandma's house. When I asked what it was for, the only answer I got was, "It's my magic basket." Next to the basket, there were several banana leaves that Grandma turned from time to time. I was curious. "What are the leaves for, Grandma?" I asked. The only answer I got was, "They are my magic leaves." It was so interesting watching Grandma, the bananas, the banana leaves and the big straw basket. But Grandma sent me off to my mother on an errand. "Grandma, please, let me watch as you prepare." "Don't be stubborn, child, do as you are told," she insisted. I took off running. When I returned, Grandma was sitting outside but with neither the basket nor the bananas. "Grandma, where is the basket, where are all the bananas, and where..." But the only answer I got was, "They are in my magic place." It was so disappointing! Two days later, Grandma sent me to fetch her walking stick from her bedroom. As soon as I opened the door, I was welcomed by the strong smell of ripening bananas. In the inner room was grandma's big magic straw basket. It was well hidden by an old blanket. I lifted it and sniffed that glorious smell. Grandma's voice startled me when she called, "What are you doing? Hurry up and bring me the stick." I hurried out with her walking stick. "What are you smiling about?" Grandma asked. Her question made me realise that I was still smiling at the discovery of her magic place. The following day when Grandma came to visit my mother, I rushed to her house to check the bananas once more. There was a bunch of very ripe ones. I picked one and hid it in my dress. After covering the basket again, I went behind the house and quickly ate the banana. It was the sweetest banana I had ever tasted. The following day, when Grandma was in the garden picking vegetables, I sneaked in and peered at the bananas. Nearly all were ripe. I couldn't help taking a bunch of four. As I tiptoed towards the door, I heard Grandma coughing outside. I just managed to hide the bananas under my dress and walked past her. The following day was market day. Grandma woke up early. She always took ripe bananas and cassava to sell at the market. I did not hurry to visit her that day. But I could not avoid her for long. Later that evening I was called by my mother and father, and Grandma. I knew why. That night as I lay down to sleep, I knew I could never steal again. Not from grandma, not from my parents, and certainly not from anyone else.
author: Ursula Nafula

title: Happy Akai
text: Akai had no shoes. Other children her age had shoes. “It is difficult to play without shoes,” said Akai to her mother. “Akai, I think it is time for you to have shoes,” said mother. Mother woke up Akai early the next morning. Akai and her mother went to the market. They went into a shoe shop. Mother bought shoes for Akai. At night, Akai thought about her new shoes. Akai put on her new shoes. Akai thought about how she would show off her shoes. Akai wore her new shoes again. She danced around the room. “Akai, you must not wear shoes in bed,” said mother. Akai was so happy to have shoes for the first time.

title: The lost boy
text: Shivam and his mother were getting ready to go for a walk. They lived on the fourth floor of a building in a big condominium. They used to take a walk in the garden surrounding the building every evening. Shivam and his mother climbed down the stairs. They decided to take a walk around the garden. Shivam held his mother's hand as always and they started walking. On the way, Shivam saw another boy riding his bicycle. Amused and excited, in no time Shivam had let go of his mother's hand. He ran towards the bicycle. The bicycle sped up and disappeared near the big gate that led to the street. And so did Shivam who was running behind the bicycle. Shivam's mother did not see Shivam anywhere. She ran towards the gate but Shivam was not in sight. Shivam's mother looked on the street. She asked each and every person if they had seen her little boy. She asked the shopkeepers if Shivam was with them. But alas! nobody had seen him. Now Shivam's mother panicked. She was worried, Where was little Shivam? She decided to look inside and ran to the garden. But Shivam was not to be found. She was almost in tears. She did not know what to do. But she did not lose hope. She knew she would find him. Where had Shivam disappeared? She continued her search in the street and returned to the garden again. This time she saw a group of kids playing in the garden. She decided to approach them. As she came closer, she heard one of the little boy with his back facing the mother say to another boy,'' My mother is lost. Can you help me find her?"

title: The Rabbit That Never Gave Up
text: Once upon a time and in a faraway land, there lived a tiny rabbit. The rabbit had a name. Its name was "Elycia". One day while Elycia was searching for food in the woods, she heard a melodious music. The music sounded as if it came from sky. "Chirp, Chirp!" Elycia looked up and saw two songbirds chirping happily on a tree branch. The birds also danced gracefully in the sky. "Wow! That is nice!" Elycia thought to herself. Quickly, Elycia hopped back to the hole where she and her mother stayed. "Mummy! I want to learn to dance!" Elycia said happily to her mother. She hopped excitedly around her mother. Mother rabbit said, "This is good, but most dancers are tall. You are too short. You need to put in more effort. Never give up until you reach your goal." The next day, Elycia went to find her friend, Monkey Monica, to help her practise growing taller. Monkey Monica stood on the high end of a tree and instructed Elycia to hop to where she was. For three months, Elycia could not hop high. She was too short! She felt sad about this failures to hop higher. She wanted to give up. She was so sad that she cried as she said to her mother, "Mummy! I cannot do it! I am so short. I cannot hop high. I will not be able to dance next time..." Just then, Mother rabbit said, "Never give up. Don't quit until you reach your goal. Keep going! Keep trying! I have been trying to fix this broken kite for the past three months. I have not given up fixing it." Elycia felt comforted by her mother's kind words. "Yes! Never give up! Keep trying! Give your very best!" Elycia said to herself. For the next five months, she practised harder and harder. She hopped every day and every night. Finally, she was able to hop very high! And she did a somersault in the air...! "Yes! I can hop high now! I can dance now! Yes!" she exclaimed. The next day, Elycia went to find her friend, Elephant Kathy. She showed her dance to Elephant Kathy. She hopped over Elephant Kathy, spun in the air, and landed awesomely! "Great job! You can dance now!" Elephant Kathy shouted joyfully. "My friend! Remember: Never give up and you will one day achieve your goal!" Elycia said.
author: Chen Jiaxin Steven & Elycia Koh

title: Weekend....downloading...ugh!
text: Mallu has been working all day. She’s a Internet Robot. If you want to be a Internet Robot, and if you think that robots don’t go to school, they do. The World Wide Web is they’re school. Yay! Today is Saturday! And Mallu has been looking forward to this weekend. But she has a problem. She has received approximately 100 million emails from children all over the world. She is making notes to calculate the amounts. But there is another 100 emails. What will Mallu do? She doubles the amount of emails and she finds out that 200 emails have to be sent to the other people. But Mallu is tired. So her friend, Netty, solves the problem. “Mallu, you get some rest. The Internet also has some time to sleep, not only humans.” Look, traveling is fun too! So Mallu gets some rest. And in the morning, she finds her work done and her boss says her work is amazing. Now Mallu is a very happy robot. You can see her, smiling back at you while she does her work!

title: Will Arif's house survive the rains this monsoon?
text: It was a heavy a monsoon night. Generally children love rains but it was not same with Arif and his grandfather. Arif's house was made with thatched hay and wooden planks. So rains and thunderstorms brought fear of being washed away. The rains at night were the worst ones as it was difficult to sleep with the dripping roof and the fear of finding oneself in another island in the morning. Arif would close his ears and pray for the rain to stop, and would keep asking his grandfather " Grandpa, will our house drown today?". Grandfather would say" No, No don't worry!! Nothing will happen, our house will survive this rain." But Arif did not believe this and he kept checking the window in small intervals in case the water drowned the house. Arif and his grandfather stayed in one of the slums of Mumbai and the conditions post rains are not a pretty sight there. The houses leaks when it rains heavily, the mud gets washed away giving space to rodents and cockroaches to enter the houses. The smell from the drain that mixes with the rain water is everywhere in the air which makes breathing impossible causing stench in the houses and the lanes. Though kids loved the puddles. As if the devastation brought by the rains was not enough the fear of Coronavirus Pandemic was looming on their heads. Getting a proper meal itself has been a challenge these days, generally Arif’s days include helping his grandfather sell pani puris in the street they live. But from last few months everything has been very silent, they are not allowed to put up the Pani Puri stalls. Even if they put there are hardly any customers. Did you know: Pani Pari is Indian street food that is liked by all ages, it is a ball filled with potato masala and sour and sweet tamarind water. Arif with his grandfather and many other in their community have been dependent on the meals distributed by the NGO’s (Non Profit Organisation) in times like this, but Arif has been enjoying these food packets lately. Everyday he received different food in the packet. Sometimes Chapati rolls, sandwiches, one day there were cup cakes too. Many families have been distributing food to the areas where the impact of Corona and rains has brought misfortune to the jobs and businesses of many people like them. But today, it was not the food problem that was keeping Arif awake, it was the fear of drowning that was not letting him sleep. He asked his grandfather again, “Grandpa, will our house drown today?” His Grandfather was asleep by this time and Arif had no other way to find out how much the street was under water but to depend on the sound of the continuous rains. The rain sound never stopped, Arif knew that by now half the house must be in water, the clothes drying outside would have been washed away. The street dog that sleeps on the street, where would he go to seek shelter? What if it rains like this till morning? He wondered if he shall wake up his grandpa and ask him to come and sleep on his tiny bed, his grandpa used to sleep on a thin mattress on the floor. The rain sound never stopped, Arif knew that by now half the house must be in water, the clothes drying outside would have been washed away. What would have happened to the street dog that sleeps outside their house, where would he go to seek shelter? What if it rains like this till morning? He wondered if he shall wake up his grandpa and ask him to come and sleep on his tiny bed, his grandpa used to sleep on a thin mattress on the floor. Arif opened his eyes in the morning and he panicked as his grandfather was not there on his bed. Generally he was the one to wake up his grandfather. Arif knew that the house would have floated somewhere and his grandfather would have been washed away due to heavy rain. With tears in his eyes, Arif wished he had told his grandfather to join him on his bed at night. The sound of the rain continued and Arif gathered some courage to get out of the house to see where he had drifted away. When Arif walked out of the house everything appeared same as before, the lamp post in the same spot where it used to be, the dog wagging his tail and chewing on bones. People were sitting on the pavement and enjoying their food and he saw the same faces that he saw everyday. Arif felt so confused, just then his grandfather tapped him from behind and handed over a food packet to him. Arif was so happy to see his grandpa, he hugged him tightly. Arif asked – “Grandpa how is that everything is in its own place, when it rained so heavily at night? Didn’t we drown? His Grandfather said," it had stopped raining long back; it must have been the sound of the fan that confused you". Both of them laughed and ate their food together and guess what was in the food packet today- “Biryani!”

title: THE JACKAL AND THE DRUM
text: Long ago in a forest, there lived a jackal called Gomaya. One day, he was hungry and came across a battlefield. In one corner of the field lay a large drum under a tree. When the wind blew a tender branch close to the root of the tree struck the drum producing the sound of drum beat the jackal examined the drum from all sides and then beat the drum with his front paws. The drum made a sound. The jackal thought that there might be some small animal inside the drum and that would make a very tasty meal for him. But he found the top of the drum too tough to tear off.So the jackal came up with a plan and began to beat the drum with his both front paws. The sound of the drum filled the whole jungle. A leopard came curious when he heard the sound of and came near it. The jackal said to the leopard 'Your Majesty' there is some animal hiding inside this drum. Since you have sharp and strong claws, you can tear off the top of the drum and catch the animal inside the drum. The leopard, who was hungry, hit the top of the drum with his heavy paws. The drum burst open with a loud noise, but there was no animal inside. The leopard became angry and killed the jackal. MORAL: GREED IS ALWAYS HARMFUL
