title: The leopard and the zebra
text: One bright sunny day at the serengeti plains, a zebra was walking under a tree to cool down. All of a sudden he heard a terrible noise from the branches of a Baoba tree above him. He looked up and saw a leopard! Feeling scared, the zebra didn't knew what to do. He seemed to be frozen in the place. But before he could move the leopard said,"Can you please help me down? I am stuck in this tree and am afraid to get down.""Do you promise you won't eat me If I help you?"asked the zebra, "yes" the leopard said. "Ok, here is the plan"said the zebra. "you gently jump into my back and then I will kneel down and you can walk off my back." "That's a great idea said the leopard. So the zebra stood under the branch were the leopard was. The leopard gently jumped down into the zebra. then, after getting onto the ground, the leopard said "Thank you so much! I promise I will pay you some day. The next evening, when the sky was turning dark and the moon was raising at sky, the zebra was eating grass on the plain. He was busy eating that he didn't the lion sneaking through the tall yellow grass. Just then the leopard spotted the lion who was preparing to attack the zebra. Remembering the kindness the zebra showed him, the leopard quickly and fiercely ran to chase the lion away. The lion saw the leopard coming and quickly ran in the opposite direction. The zebra was joyful that he was saved from the fierce lion. "Thank you so much you saved my life!." In response The leopard said "I told you that i would repay your kindness some day" From that day the zebra and the leopard were glad to be best friends.

title: The Hungry Snail
text: One day, a snail was sliding along in a garden. After some time, he felt very hungry. He kept on moving till he saw an apple tree. Three apples had fallen down the tree. He slid ahead as fast as he could towards the apples. He opened his mouth and took a bite. CRUNCH! YUM! But when he took a second bite, he saw many worms inside the apple! The snail was very scared. He thought they were snakes! The worms wriggled out of the apple. They saw the snail, its enormous eyes and tentacles like two huge horns. “It’s a monster!” the worms screamed and wriggled away in fear. The snail was happy. He could now enjoy the apple all by himself.

title: Marry - The Golden Bird
text: Once upon a time.There lived a bird named Marry. She was a golden bird. She lived in a castle,in a cage with royal family. Marry sang new songs for them every day to please them and enjoy living in palace. One day King and Queen thought that it wasn't good for the bird to live in the cage for so long, After many discussions they planned to leave Marry in the forest. So one fine day with heavy heart they left Marry in Jungle. Once in the forest, Marry has to build a nest to stay. Unfortunately, she didn't knew how to build a nest because she lived in a cage whole of her life. So Marry decided to ask for help. Just then a pigeon passed by, Marrysaid 'Kee!Kee!' "can you please help me in building my nest Mr Pigeon"?.The pigeon stopped by and replied 'Utter! Utter' "yes, why not. Come let's build it". While they were working on the nest, a Lion pass by and surprisingly asked them -"Roar, Roar!""What you guys are upto"? The birds replied hastly "Kee Kee Utter Utter""We are working on building nest sir". Lion didnot find that job interesting and left the place. The birds were continuing with making their nest and in some time they finished making it. Marry and Pigeon was done with building nest. Marry thanked Pigeon and she left the place. Pigeon has promised her to visit her once a day as they were good friends now. After a while she noticed a monkey near by in next tree. Just when she saw him, Monkey asked Marry - 'Chatter! Chatter', Who are you"? Marry did not like his playfulness and sudden question but she replied by saying that She is a golden bird and she is new to this forest. Monkey asked her again if Marry is interested in coming over with him to fetch the food near by. But Marry declined by saying that she is not interested to be friend with him as she didnt quite like his playful behaviour and too many questions. Marry was proud of her Golden peak and she has not much thought about monkey offer to hunt for food. After monkey left for next tree she realise her mistake. She realise that any one can be friend if you are respecting them and communicating properly. She has experienced that with Pigeon and lion just now. But she forget this lesson and ignored monkey advise which was very useful to her. She decided to correct her mistake now. In no time Marry was in next tree and said 'Kee!Kee', Sorry Monkey I ignored your good suggestion but looking at your face! I should not have done this. I am sorry" Monkey replied that no need to worry because it was not deliberate. Marry has got another friend and identified the place for food as well. She was ready to survive in big jungle.

title: My Journey To Success
text: This is a story about how I found my way to success. I am currently a doctor, yes, as you can see I have fulfilled my dream. I was actually from a poor family. I knew that they did not have the money to afford medical college. But, I was desperate to go to medical college and become a doctor. You may think it was impossible to actually have enough money to afford it. But, as I told you, I had done it. Here is my story, starting from when I was 15 to how I saved up a lot and then, finally became a doctor. It all started when I saw many doctors helping my family. It used to warm my heart. I remember when my father caught a high fever. We did not have the money to afford proper treatment. I knew how hard it might've been for my family! Then, I don't remember his name, a doctor offered to treat him for free. I still remember how delighted we were. That was probably the incident that inspired me to become a doctor. I had told my parents that I would treat everyone for free. They were so proud! Well, then I promised myself that I would be a doctor when I am grown up, whatever it takes. I then found out that my father had lost his job. Even though it barely gave him any money, it helped to keep up the household. Now there was no way I could get into medical college. I was so extremely sad, and I spent many nights awake, imagining how I can help my family, and also get into college. Those times were hard for me, but, when it happened, I thought that the storm shall pass one day. And of course, it did pass one day or the other, and I cannot be more grateful. One day, after I was returning from a walk around the neighborhood (as I did not go to my school when my dad lost his job) my rich friend from the nearby city invited me to a coffee shop near her house, in town. I was happy, as I did not have so much luxury to visit coffee shops each day. So I went. She got me a "Latte" and sat down with me to enjoy her coffee. I asked her who makes these delicious drinks. She said they were called "baristas" and they were the ones making the drinks. That was it! I signed up for the job, and the manager said that I could start next week. I was overjoyed. So from the next week, I was a barista in the coffee shop. It was hard to adjust, like what was in a latte, and how many pumps of mocha is perfect with coffee, or how much whipped cream I should use in a hot coffee. I tried to memorize it all up, and I did the best I could. It smelled quite delicious and I wonder how I didn't take a little sip out of them. Well, it went on like that for quite a few years. There were some funny incidents in the middle as well, like when I got a regular customer who kept on asking for "five extra pumps of hazelnut". That "hazelnut" thing tasted absolutely delicious, and I cannot deny I used to eat a pump of it without and coffee, just for a bit of taste. I was earning money! I can finally save up to get into medical college, and help my family! I was so extremely happy. As they say, I had "Found my way out of the dark cloud", and was overjoyed about it. Many years later, I finally had the money to pay for my college. Oh, and I was also studying oncology (medical) at home, as my best friends had gotten me a bunch of books from the library about medical and I was reading them the moment I got home from work at the coffee shop. I remember myself saying to my mother, "When I am a doctor, I would not forbid them from drinking coffee no matter what!". It makes me laugh when I think about it now. And then my time for college came. I was excited. It seemed as if I had mice in my stomach, no, snakes. It felt like there were snakes in my stomach. I mailed a paycheck to my college and then I got ready to leave for college. I left a $2100 paycheck back at home with my parents, as I had no worry over money anymore 'cause I was about to be a doctor, and I would get enough money from it. The time came. My parents came with me to the airport... I waved goodbye to them and there were a lot of hugs and promise of letters before I left, continuing the path to my dreams. There you have it, that's the story of my journey to success. I hope many young ones will be inspired by this to follow their dreams and work on them, by not giving up in the middle. I went to college and studied until I was advanced enough to be a doctor. And now I am back in my old hometown in the States, as a doctor, and I cannot be happier. Always try following your dreams, instead of running away from them. It's the best thing to do. Thank you for reading, and all the best for your future.
author: 💗Prisha💗

title: Sparrows and Pinky
text: Dev Eight-year-old Pinky was standing in the balcony with her father when a bird came there. Pinky asked her father. "Which bird is it?" Her father told. "D aughter, this is a sparrow. It is found everywhere in our country. When we were little, we used to sprinkle a lot of sparrows in the courtyard of our house in the village. They used to like it very much." Then Pinky's Mummy also came there. They told. "In my house too, the sparrow used to make its nest in the skylight above a window. The sparrow kept chirping all day long in the small garden." Pinky became curious to know more about sparrows after listening to her mother and father. Her mother gave him a book in which many interesting things were written about the sparrow. Pinkie started reading it. In the afternoon when everyone sat down to eat, Pinky's father asked. "Tell us what you read about Sparrow too." Pinky is happy to hear of her father and tells that the sparrow's scientific name is Passer Domesticus. It is commonly found in Asia and Europe. Goraiya: This small bird is light brown or white in color. It has yellow feathers and yellow beak and feet on its body. The male sparrow has dark spots near its throat. Its length is 14 to 16 inches. Sparrow eats small grains, seeds and grains found in the soil. "Well done, you have read the book with all your heart." Pinky's mother said happily. Pinkie said with some thought. "You guys were saying that there were many sparrows in your childhood. But I have seen sparrows for the first time today." Pinkie's father answered seriously. "Daughter, the reason for this is the changing environment. People live in flats in cities where sparrows do not get window lights, balconies to build nests. Increasing pollution also has a bad effect on them. So the number is decreasing." Pinky's mother also explained. "Sparrow eats insects living in the soil. But due to increasing use of pesticides, now insects are getting eliminated in the soil. Mobile tower waves are also reducing their lifespan." Pinky became depressed after hearing all this. Seeing her sad, her father said while explaining. "Don't be sad. We can still try to save the lives of these birds." "How is that, father?" "We can keep grains and drinking water for them to eat on the roof of the house or in the balcony. They can put trees where they can live. They can live on them in wooden and office boxes or in pottery. We can make nests and keep them in the balcony or window. With these small steps we can save the sparrow. " Pinky jumped with joy after hearing the solution. She said. "I will also make their living room in the balcony."
author: Rishita Dev

title: My birthday
text: Today is my birthday. Nobody wished me. My mom is drying clothes with my little sister and my dad has gone to office. In spite of being my birthday it is even more boring than other days. Dad comes from office. Dad tells me to go to bed.I asked him why so early. He replies just,switches of the lights and goes out of the room. Suddenly the lights get on, my friends pop out and shout HAPPY BIRTHDAY. My mom and dad enter the room with A cake and some gifts. I tell all of them Thank you for the surprise. This is the best birthday ever.
author: KIMAAYA Rao

title: Craby crab
text: Once upon a time there lived a lazy crab called craby. He never let the other animals come on the water. He also didn't let the people come. The people made a plan to catch the crab. One time he chased a fish in the water which was a magical fish. A hunter came to catch the crab. Another crab heard the sound. He helped the crab. And craby became kind. The other animals lived happily in the water.

title: The Story of Help Us Green
text: Bholu the bear had a busy day. He was a reporter in the television channel Aaj Ka Jungle. Today, he had to take the interview of Ankit Aggarwal, the founder of Help Us Green. He had set up the company in 2015. The company specialised in recycling flowers into vermicompost. They made many creative items out of it. Bholu: Hello, everyone, today we have one of India’s most creative businessmen amongst us. Not only does he run a huge organization but saves the environment while running it. Welcome, Mr. Ankit Aggarwal, how are you? Could you tell us a little something about your company, Help Us Green? Ankit Aggarwal: Hi Bholu. I am well. Our company – Help Us Green recycles flower waste. By recycling this waste, we achieve many purposes, we save our rivers, promote organic materials and produce biodegradable products in a creative way. Bholu: You said something about saving our rivers, how does this happen? Ankit Aggarwal: Hi Bholu. I am well. Our company – Help Us Green recycles flower waste. By recycling this waste, we achieve many purposes, we save our rivers, promote organic materials and produce biodegradable products in a creative way. Bholu: You said something about saving our rivers, how does this happen? Ankit Aggarwal: You would have definitely noticed that devotees from various religious places throw a lot of flowers after worship in our rivers and ponds. This is especially true of Ganga and Yamuna. Many tonnes of roses, jasmines, daffodils, lilies and lotuses are thrown into water bodies. They float on water bodies and rot away. They pollute the water a lot. I observed that foam had formed on these flowers. On examining it closely, my team and I realized that this foam was actually a fully biodegradable type of fibre. We thought that we should use this fibre creatively. Even the water we use for recycling is completely purified. Bholu: So you started making vermicompost out of this foam of flowers that you call florafoam. You used it to create incense sticks (called phool). Ankit Aggarwal: Not just incense sticks, it is also used in biodegradable packing of electronics. It has replaced thermocol in many instances as it is 27% cheaper than thermocol. This is especially good as thermocol is one of the world’s biggest polluters. The biodegradable packaging can be disposed off by burying it into the earth. We aim to make 11 tonnes of such material everyday and are opening a plant in Kanpur for that purpose. Bholu: I understand. Are you thinking of launching any new products? Ankit: Yes, definitely, our next range of products also include mosquito repellents and diabetes medicines. I really look forward to this expansion. I am also planning to expand our units to Mathura and Vrindavan since the water bodies out there tend to get very polluted. We have also started manufacturing leather from flower waste. It can be dyed by beautiful natural colours and looks very stylish! We plan to sell this leather to top designers. Bholu: This sounds great. What do you consider as your biggest victory in this entire process? Ankit: I feel that my biggest victory has been to save our Ganges from pollution, in whatever little way we could, and the empowerment of rural women. Mostly village women are involved in our factory-work. My aim is to generate full-time employment for five thousand women and empower them economically. Bholu: That is truly an inspiring idea. What is the one factor that really helped you? Ankit: I think the fact that the products are made from flowers that were once offered to gods, have made our products seem sacred. Some people thought that we will not be able to sell our products as they have been made from waste, but this was entirely wrong. People were very happy to buy them. This Diwali we even ran out of stock! Bholu: That is indeed great. You have already won many prestigious awards for your initiative. I wish you more awards, more luck for your future endeavours and wish that many others get inspired by you and work towards saving our rivers. Thanks a lot for humouring us. Ankit: Thanks, this was my pleasure.
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: Jealousy is not good
text: Once upon a time there was a small girl named Ashley. She was a very good girl. One day at school her friend bought a very nice pen. Everyone went to see the pen. Ashley got very jealous. She also wanted that pen. That day when everyone went for lunch, Ashley took her friend's pen and put it her bag. When everyone came back Ashley's friend shouted. "Who took my pen?", shouted Ashley. Nobody answered. The teacher asked who did it and everybody told that it was Ashley, because she was there when everyone was at lunch. The teacher asked Ashley if it was her and she told it was her and she gave it back to her friend. "I am sorry", said Ashley.
author: Leyna Nukarapu
illustrator: Krishna Chandran; Rijuta Ghate; Sanjana Desai; Shailja Jain Chougule

title: The New Play Area
text: Once upon a time, long ago, there was a city. On the outskirts of this city was a slum. The people who lived in it were quite poor. They had no proper roads, markets or schools. The surroundings were filled with filth and dirt. There was always an awful smell in the air. The children were unhappy as they had no place to play. But the worst thing was that a marshland had formed right in the middle of the slum. Since the government did not make any provision to pick up the garbage, all the garbage was thrown into this marsh. The waste water from the homes too accumulated here. More water entered into this pool when it rained. Things got worse as this dirty pool became a breeding ground for mosquitoes and other pests. This led to dangerous diseases like malaria and dengue. Everyone hated this but did not know what to do. After some time the pool started brimming with water and this dirty, infected water started entering people’s homes. “We hate this water, it is of no use. It has only brought misery and sorrow in our lives,” everyone used to say. It was only when the elections were held to elect a member of the local municipal area and a resident of their own slum was elected to represent their interests that the people of the slum felt a little relieved. The man elected was Rajendera Singh. He worked as a taxi driver to earn a living, but his passion lay in serving the society. “Now I will use my power to solve the issue of sanitation in my slum.” “The fault lies not with natural resources like water but how we use them. We must use our resources to their fullest potential without exploiting them. There is a difference between using and abusing resources,” he would say. He was also very fond of children. One day he called for a meeting with the children. “Children, I have arranged for your admission at the local government school. But I wish to ask you, what do you miss the most in your lives? What should be developed?” “A playground! We have nowhere to play. We don’t have proper facilities to spend our free time,” everyone said in unison. Rajendera Singh thought that he had two problems at hand, one of sanitation and the other of recreation. Why not merge both and come up with a solution? Singh liked reading books, too, he believed that the knowledge he gained from books was his real treasure. Even without any access to the internet, he had immense general knowledge. He read about a startup a small company run by a small group of passionate people in Africa that installed pumps under merry-go-rounds. These pumps were installed under polluted water bodies. They also had purifiers within them to purify the water quickly and thoroughly. The energy generated from this entire process of water purifying powered the merry go round to keep operating in circles. Rajendera Singh found this idea both inspiring and innovative. He went to the post office and bought a Re. 1 postcard and sent it to the startup, requesting for their help. The management of the startup agreed to his request and came to his service. Their services were expensive, but they were more than happy to help. Singh spent all his monthly salary and his funds that he received from the government to pay the startup. They installed big blue pumps and swings on top of them. The swings were bright red, blue, green and yellow. On the request of their parents, tight black seat belts were installed as well, so that the kids wouldn’t fall off! When the work was done, all the slum kids were called. Now they had recreation facilities as good as the other kids. They didn’t have to wait for the rich kids to get down from the swings so they could use them. The water was no longer smelly. It splashed white and crystal blue. Now the water was being used, not abused. This is the soul of water conservation, using the resource, but sustaining it for a long time - for many people, and many purposes. As the laughter of the kids spread in the air like music, Rajendera Singh felt that he had got his ultimate reward.
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: The helpful boy
text: There lived a boy. He was very quiet and he liked being alone. He observed things properly especially animals. One day while he was enjoying the nature he saw a butterfly with a broken wing. The boy immediately helped the butterfly. Within a few days of care the butterfly was fine and flew away. The boy became happy. From then onward he started helping other animals in need.
author: KIMAAYA Rao
illustrator: Brunda Anandarao; johan koshy; Lavanya  Naidu; Nguyễn  Minh Hải

title: The Handpump
text: Once upon a time, many years ago, in a town was a hand pump. The town was a small one, disconnected from the rest of the world. It was filled with dust during the day and on winter mornings, it was wrapped in mist. Usually it was very quiet, the only faint sounds that one could hear were the chirping of birds and the moving of bullock carts. In the same town, there was a huge mansion. In it, an old woman lived all alone. All her family members had died. She did not like speaking to people. She had a hand pump through which she used to draw water. This made things easy for her as it was not comfortable for her to go far away to the well or the little stream that was situated just outside of town. Then, one spring she noticed that the flow of the water from the handpump had reduced considerably. By summer, the handpump ran dry. Not even a drop of water came out of it. The old lady wondered what had gone wrong. Soon, all the water stored in the house in pots would get exhausted. What was she to do? She couldn’t use her hand pump now. She asked the vegetable seller who passed by her house about the water shortage. He informed her that not only her mansion, but the entire lane, the entire town and actually the entire district was suffering from the same problem. The townspeople had used so much groundwater that the water levels had fallen drastically. Now, their wells, tanks and hand pumps were all dry. “What will we do now?” said the worried vegetable seller. “We should have thought about this earlier when we were recklessly drawing water from those huge borewells for our factories and agriculture. But there is no use crying over spilled milk,“ the old lady said and sighed. “Something needs to be done urgently. We must revive our groundwater tables,” she said firmly. But they both knew that the path wouldn’t be easy. Earlier, the old lady did not speak much to people but she knew that if she had to stand up for a cause, then connecting to people would be the key. She especially gathered all the town’s ladies and they organized meetings every Thursday at some or the other person’s house. Not only did they discuss something constructive, but they also formed a strong social circuit. Slowly, the children and later the townsmen joined too. By the time rains were due, almost the entire town used to be at these meetings. The town hall that was locked up a few years ago because everyone was busy chatting on the internet, was now reopened. “We have closed all the major borewells, and most of the water that we take is from the little stream outside the town. But I still don’t understand why the water tables are not rising,” said Sheetal, a young sixteen year old. “Sheetal, groundwater is not replenished overnight. It will take some time, maybe a few years,“ said the village sarpanch. “Monsoon is just about to begin. I am sure that when the rains come, everything will get sorted out,” said the old lady. “I think we are going in the wrong direction. We are not focusing on what we should,” said Navin. Navin was a primary school teacher at the Government Town School. He taught Geography and knew a great deal about plants, animals, rivers, mountains and land. “What do you mean that we are not focusing on what we should?” asked the old lady politely. Navin said, “I feel that we are not taking the right steps. Even if the rains come, it will do little good in reviving the groundwater. Our main problem is concrete. Concrete does not absorb rainwater the way earth does. Most water runs off from the surface of the concrete or gets evaporated. This is the biggest way water is wasted and the reason why water tables do not revive.” The people of the town understood the point he was trying to make. They decided that they must increase more open spaces in the town, free from concrete and cement so that water could seep back to the soil. Under the guidance of Navin, the village took several steps in this direction. The spaces that were littered with plastic bags and tins were cleaned and open spaces were created. The concrete pavements outside the homes and shops were broken down and land was exposed. The Panchayat prohibited the construction of any concrete building for the next two years, till the time the groundwater hadn’t revived. Fresh tanks were installed and the old ones were cleaned to store water when it rained. Once enough water was stored, it was thrown onto a dry patch of land. The parched and thirsty earth absorbed the water very quickly, giving a moist fragrance. And guess what, four months after the rains were over and these methods implemented, the old lady decided to use her hand pump again. At first, there was a trickle, then the water came out in full intensity, it was sweet, fresh and crystal clear. The same was the case with the whole lane, the town and the entire district. The groundwater was finally revived! The town people were now in a closely-knit social circuit and happier than ever before!
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: The Eating-Joint
text: Rohan’s father owned a small eating-joint on the national highway. Many vehicles used to stop by the joint and passengers used to savour a healthy snack or a small meal. Many tasty items were prepared including chole-bhatture, Indian thalis and a variety of curries. Many type of sweets like gulab jamun and halwa were made too. Rohan loved the food. Often he used to rush back to the joint after school to consume a tasty meal on a charpai under the banyan trees. Rohan was a brilliant student and when he passed school, he got admission in a reputed college. He used to come home only during the holidays. Once his education was over, he came home and wanted to start his own business. His father had grown old and wanted him to take over the responsibilities of running the joint. Rohan was not ready for this, but he still accompanied his father to the joint. The joint was the same as the one he had left years ago. “It is so expensive to run this joint. Our profits are at an all time low. If the expenses keep rising, I will have to close this joint that I built with so much effort” Rohan’s father said unhappily. “Don’t worry, daddy. I will help you find a solution to this problem. I will find out where exactly the problem lies,” Rohan reassured his father. He started looking around the joint. The vegetables, fruits and spices were bought at low prices from a nearby town. Their customers paid them well. “I wonder, then, how does it become so expensive to run the joint - when our monthly costs are under control - why is our monthly bill so high?” thought Rohan. The next day Rohan was enjoying piping hot aloo parathas. He felt thirsty and ordered some water. He drank a glass of water. He was still thirsty, so he ordered another glass. When the second glass came, he drank just half the glass and his thirst was quenched. He threw the leftover water away in the sink. As soon as he threw it in the sink, he realized something. It was the wastage of water that made running their small joint so expensive! He noticed that almost all customers did not empty their glasses. The water was mostly wasted. Their workers washed the utensils under running tap water, this led to further water wastage. The joint was also cleaned using water from pipes rather than water stored in buckets. They were using more water than needed everywhere! They had to buy more water at more expensive prices. All this made the functioning of the joint costly and difficult. Moreover, so many litres of water that were being wasted could be used for better purposes. Rohan decided to do something about this. He made colourful posters urging his customers to order only as much water as they would actually use. He personally spoke to his customers to prevent water wastage. He installed a huge pit and requested his customers and employees to throw the leftover drinking water in it. A pipe was connected to this pit. This pipe discharged water into a garden in the backyard. The plants grew taller and stronger in the garden and were laden with beautiful blossoms. He asked his staff to store water in buckets and use them for chores like cleaning and washing. He also minimized the water used in cooking by rationing the amount of water that would be enough for each day. This made cooking quicker and the operating of the food joint more efficient. Soon, the news of this type of water management spread far and wide. Rohan was interviewed by prominent magazines, and later that year, their joint won the Most Eco-Friendly Organisation of the Year Award. This made their joint very famous and more people started visiting it. Rohan had realized that it was important to conserve its resources for the organization to be successful. He took over his dad’s eating joint and also opened a small business of his own where he educated different restaurants on how to save resources like water to be successful.
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: Little Dams
text: Flood. The word itself scares us, doesn’t it? It is a situation where there is water - too much water- everywhere. We like to blame it on too much rain, but more often than not, natural disasters like flood and drought occur due to the lack of disaster management by human beings. Related to this fact, is the following short story: In a large forest, in a faraway land, there were many lakes, ponds and streams. The animals had a lot of water to use, maybe that is the reason they did not realize it’s value. They used too much water for everything, almost twice of what was actually needed! They crossed all limits in using water - using it for washing clothes, for farming, for household chores etc. But what was indeed tragic is that they did not make any effort to save water. Water depleted from the water resources. One summer it did not rain at all. As the little animals had not stored any water to face a crisis such as drought, they soon realized that there was no water left in the forest. They had to bring water tanks from the big city. This cost them a lot, and to top it off, the water was also not sufficient. They pledged that they would save water for the future in case of such a crisis. Someone had told Sher Singh, the lion and the king of the forest, that dams should be constructed to save water. He was concerned about the well-being of his subjects. He immediately sent for help. He wrote a mail to a civil engineer in the city, who knew how to build roads and dams. He came to the forest and built a large dam that was very tall and made of cement. “Now we will not have any problem in saving water,” the animals said happily and danced at the inauguration party of the dam. Next year, it rained a lot. It rained so much that all the ponds, streams and lakes started overflowing. The dam was used to save all the rain water and also store water from the water bodies so that they wouldn’t overflow. The little animals had planned that once the rain began to recede, they would open the dam in many steps and slowly the water would be allowed to exit from the dam back into the huge river outside the forest. But things did not go as planned. The floods got over but the dam now contained too much water. Since it couldn’t contain so much water, it exploded. The entire forest were flooded. Many animals were drowned, their homes collapsed and the fields disappeared under water. Everyone was left in tears. Some time passed. This time the animals decided to take steps more wisely. They spoke to many experts over Skype and realized that water management is the key to avert such disasters. They decided to construct dams made mostly of natural materials like mud and clay that were small in size and could hold water within a limit. Many such little dams were constructed on water bodies across the forest. Even if these dams broke down or were damaged, it would not lead to a large disaster. They were also not very expensive to make. What was more important was the fact that water storing mechanisms were now present all over the forest rather than in just one location. “Now everything will be alright,” said Sher Singh in the Annual Village Conference. Indeed, everything was normal after that. Thereafter, the animals realized their mistake and used water wisely. They stored water in their little dams and used them during droughts. In years of floods, water was stored in these dams and they regulated the amount of water present in the water bodies. Thus, knowledge of water management made the little animals wealthier and wiser.
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: Drop By Drop Makes the Ocean
text: Once upon a time, there was a little village in a faraway land. Just outside the village was a pond. It was dark blue and deep in the middle. Beautiful creepers grew along its boundaries. They had pink and white flowers and a lovely fragrance. All the little boys and girls loved the pond. They often came to swim and play in it. In summers the cool water would refresh them from all the dust and heat. “It’s so nice and beautiful,” they would all say. Then one day, some men who were not from the village came to the pond. They started diverting the water from the pond to small channels to the nearby fields. These channels looked like small streams. They called them irrigation channels. The elders around them said that it would help the plants in their fields grow taller and greener. The plants after some time grew taller and stronger. But the pond was not as deep as before. It became shallow. The little boys and girls could also see the bottom of the pond was now filled with rocks, fish and water plants. They felt bad but decided to remain quiet.Some time later, a factory came up near the village. It let out a lot of thick black smoke that smelt very bad. It also discharged many chemicals into the pond. When these chemicals travelled from the pond to the irrigation channels to the fields, many plants died. The pond became black from blue and smelt horrible. It smelt so bad that the children did not like going near it anymore. They could not even think of splashing water and playing in it as before. “This is so dirty. How can we play in it?” they exclaimed. Then came the summers. It was scorching hot. The pond dried up completely. There was not a drop of water left in it. Such was the heat that the beautiful creepers around the pond died too. The children started crying. “Why are you crying?” asked Motu’s granny who had come to visit Motu from the nearby village. The kids told them what had happened over the past few months. Granny was very upset too. “This is not done,” she said. “Human beings have become very selfish and greedy. For short term gains, they quickly use up all the natural resources. Now the pond has dried up. From where will we get freshwater for our daily use? We must revive the pond.” “But how?” all the kids asked in unison. “I have a plan in mind. I will first ask the village elders to close these irrigation channels for some time. They are responsible for draining almost all the water from the pond. But all you children have to help me as well. Do you use Facebook and WhatsApp?” “Yes, yes, we love both Facebook and Whatsapp and use them all the time to speak to our friends. “Okay,” smiled granny, “now you will use Facebook, WhatsApp and other social networking sites to spread awareness about what is happening to your village pond.” “But why would people be interested in knowing what is happening to a pond in our little village, granny?” asked Motu. “Why not?” said granny. Most people in our country” still live in villages. Even those who live in cities came from villages. We must be concerned about what is happening in our villages, especially when it comes to the destruction of natural resources, because they contribute to our very existence. If we are able to generate enough awareness about the exploitation of natural resources, help will surely pour in. We must be positive and keep working to achieve what we truly want. “Yes, granny, you are right. I have some photographs of the pond when it was dark blue and deep and so clean. I will use those photographs to make a video and compare those images with the present-day situation,” said Chintu. “That’s a great idea!” Motu agreed. “We can also interview our parents to help people understand the situation and spread those videos on WhatsApp groups. Guys, let’s get to work. We must make our pond like before.” “My daddy is a journalist in the newspaper Our Village Times. He can surely help us in spreading this news to nearby villages,” said Pinky “Good, my kids, I am glad that you have understood my point. Every effort counts, remember - drop by drop makes the ocean.” A few days later Motu called all his friends home where his granny was waiting for them. Tea and biscuits were laid out for them. “Namaskar, granny!” all the kids greeted her and sat down. It looked like a very purposeful gathering. Once they had settled, granny started speaking. “I have wonderful news,” she said. “I spoke to the council of elders, the panchayat. They were more than eager to address the issue. They have decided that only a few irrigation channels will function now, even that, only after the pond revives. This can only happen after it rains. Secondly, the impact of the news in the newspaper of Pinky’s father was so much that the government forced the factory to first purify the liquid waste it produced and only then discharge it into the river. Now the pond will no longer be polluted.” “Yipee!” said Pinky. “Do you know granny, the videos on the degradation of our village pond have gone viral on YouTube and Facebook. People have offered to help us in every possible way. Many people have also shared similar stories about how ponds, canals, lakes and wells have dried in their villages and towns. We have all formed a WhatsApp group where people can share similar stories about how water sources near them are under threat,” said Chintu. “I think we can also plan to spread this message in forms of posters and other creative art in our village melas. This will support our cause towards bettering the environment.” “See how you have already come up with such brilliant ideas? I really like them. This can become a movement in our entire state, and who knows, maybe even our entire country! If you truly believe in something, tell yourself that it can happen, it will happen, and it must happen!”
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: We All Need to Save Water
text: Winter had come and all the little animals of the jungle were very excited for the Christmas holidays. The baby bear, Golu, asked his mummy and daddy to take him somewhere on a family trip. “Where do you want to go? Some water park?’’ Daddy knew Golu loved games and activities involving water. He liked splashing around in small puddles throughout the day, during the rainy season. “Yes, yes!” Golu’s eyes gleamed with joy. “I think this time we should do something new. We should go to some place where we learn something and have fun as well.” ‘’Where do we find such a place?” asked a puzzled Golu. “I think we should go to Rani Ki Vav, a famous stepwell in Gujarat,” said daddy. “What is a stepwell?” asked Golu. “You will find out soon,” replied mummy. A few days later, they reached Rani Ki Vav. At the entrance, they were greeted by Ramu, their tour guide. “Wow!” exclaimed Golu, as he entered the stepwell and saw many staircases and so many beautiful sculptures on the walls. The structure was huge with multiple corridors, verandas and tanks. Ramu told Golu that the structure was made to store water. “Only to store water? Is storing water so important?” asked Golu. “Yes, it is indeed. This area is a dry region. It rains very less. People in the olden days had a lot of wisdom. They knew that it was important to store water when it was available so they could use it in the future. This stepwell was built in the memory of King Bhim by his wife Udaymati. She could have simply built a monument, but as the Queen, she wanted something that would be useful for her subjects. It took twelve years to complete, but when it was ready, the people in the nearby areas did not have to struggle to obtain water. Even today in the villages of Rajasthan and Gujarat, women walk many miles to fetch water.” “I am so lucky. I get water by simply opening a tap” said Golu. “And you still waste it when you open the tap to fill the bucket, go somewhere else, forgetting that you had to close the tap, while the bucket overflows,” Golu’s mummy scolded him mildly. “It is so beautiful,” marvelled Golu’s daddy in the background. “Yes, it is one of the most important heritage sites in India. Recently, the image of this step well was printed on the new hundred rupee note. But the real takeaway that tourists learn from this site is the importance of water conservation.” “How?” asked Golu. “The structure comprises of many layers of stairs and underground tunnels that helped in cooling or warming the water, according to the weather. As we are using too much water these days, groundwater tables are dipping, many companies based in cities are using ancient technology to build new water conservation systems. Modern day infrastructure to save rain water, like rainwater harvesting is also being inspired from older technologies,” informed Ramu. Daddy exclaimed, “Hm, I understand. Even we were thinking of installing a harvesting plant at home since I am concerned about water conservation too. I know a friend of mine in Italy who started a campaign regarding water conservation. The participants were required to send three ways as to how they conserved water at home every week to him and he displayed those chits on a board near a famous heritage site made for storing water. It was a very meaningful exercise.” “The way human beings are harming water resources worries me. We all need to save water from now on, or else we will face shortage of drinking water too,’’ suggested mummy. “Oh no!” exclaimed Golu. “But you can prevent this from happening, by following some simple steps everyday. Close the taps when not in use, water the plants using a mug or bucket and not a pipe. Try to use as less water as you can while washing and cleaning household items. Also be aware of how others around you are wasting water, like in water games in amusement parks, for example,” explained Ramu. Golu smiled, “I will keep this in mind, Ramu uncle. I will send you chits about how I saved water each week and you can also put them on a board nearby.” “So our Golu will become famous as well!” daddy said and everyone smiled. “Good, Golu. I am proud of you. If all children work hard like you, India will not face shortage of water. No one will have to stand in long queues for a bucket of water.” “Thanks for all your guidance, Ramu. We will see you soon. Till then, goodbye,” said Daddy, as they left for home. Golu got some important lessons about water conservation and explained them to his other friends in the forest. Within a few years, no one in the forest suffered from water scarcity as they had done before. You will also like to do the same, won’t you?
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: Cutting Paani and the Crown
text: “Wah! This place looks beautiful! What is going on?” exclaimed the rabbit, gazing at the banyan tree clearing in wonder. This was where all the important events like the Council Meetings, Habitat Discussions and Talent Shows happened. “Well, in a few hours, Simba is going to appeal to all the animals of the Forest to crown him as the King,” said the fox. “Do you think he would make for a good King?” inquired the monkey. “A good one? He will help the Council move ahead in the right direction, I think he’ll make a great one,” replied the rabbit. All three of them gazed at the clearing, watching the hardworking ants decorate and set up colourful garlands for the occasion while setting up seats for the seven Council members. Meanwhile, Simba paced in his chamber anxiously, holding the Buzzbee article which talked about the 6 things Simba will have to do to win over the denizens of the forest. It said that the lion’s chances of winning would increase a lot if he presented a new strategy today during the Crowning Ceremony. He knew that he just needed to pick a problem and find a solution. But he wanted to solve a problem with a simple yet significant solution and he didn’t have much time to come up with ideas. He had to be in the Banyan tree clearing in another half an hour and would be crowned as the new King of the Jungle if he won the Council’s approval. The brainstorming session with his team had not given him any good ideas he could present. Nothing he could come up with met both, his goal of involving all the animals of the Jungle and helping everyone. His bird clock told him that he needed to leave now to avoid being late for the Council meeting. On the way, as he looked around at the trees and the river hoping for inspiration to strike, he realized how limited the resources were. Anything that could reduce wastage seemed like a good idea. After all, Why Waste something so precious? He strode into the clearing and marveled at how festive the place looked. Glasses of water and fruit juices were placed everywhere for all the animals who were seated. He swaggered into the clearing and moved past the animals who might soon be his subjects. He could hear them talking about him. “The mischievous cub has grown up into a majestic lion”. “I think he will make for a good King. He has a clear head on his shoulders.” “Isn’t he too young to lead a kingdom though?” These were some of the remarks he heard as he moved to the front to address the gathering. As he looked at their glasses filled to the brim, an idea started to form in his mind. He started his speech and greeted the large gathering with,“Animals, birds and insects of the forest! Lend me yours ears! I am here to talk to all of you about why you all deserve a new King who is just, fair and savvy enough to solve our current problems with practical solutions. The world does not become a better place overnight but can be
author: Divya Ramesh

title: The Changemaker Trio Save the River
text: One day, Hali the elephant, Maya the bird, and Kenn the turtle were sitting around in the midday sun trying to figure out something to do. “Let’s go climb on the big rocks!” said Hali. “That’s too scary,” answered Kenn as he shrunk back into his shell, “Maybe we should take a nap instead.” “It’s too hot out to take a nap,” Maya remarked, “Let’s go for a swim!” The Changemaker Trio all excitedly murmured their agreement and set off towards the river. When they arrived, a disgusting, strong smell greeted them and the surrounding bank was covered in garbage. “I don’t remember the river smelling this badly,” Hali observed, “It’s quite strange.” “Is it safe?” Kenn wondered out loud, “I don’t want to get sick.” “Of course it’s safe,” Maya responded as she waded in, “we have always swum here.” “I’m going to stay out here and just watch you guys,” Kenn announced. Hesitantly, Hali followed Maya into the cloudy, smelly water. The two began to play a fun game of tag. Hali began to squirt the water up into the air using her trunk. Hali and Maya laughed and splashed as they cooled off from the heat. “Are you sure you don’t want to come in?” Maya asked Kenn. “I’m sure. The river doesn’t look very nice today,” answered Kenn. Maya dove gracefully underwater. She resurfaced coughing and had large dots all over her body. “I don’t feel so good,” Maya stated as she made her way out of the water, “I don’t feel very good at all.” Seconds later, Hali followed her out. “Now that I think about it, I don’t feel too well either,” Hali agreed, “My head really hurts and I have a rash.” “Oh no,” Kenn commented, “I knew it wasn’t safe. We should go to Doctor Darya.” The three friends slowly began their trek across the forest and towards Doctor Darya’s office in the grassy land. Kenn led the way for the other two animals who were still far from feeling their best. As the Sun began to descend from the sky, the three animals finally approached the Doctor’s office. Knock! Knock! Knock! The animals stood as they waited to be welcomed into Doctor Darya’s care. Finally, a large rhinoceros approached the animals with a warm smile on her face. “Hello! I’m Doctor Darya,” the rhino said, “Come on in and tell me what’s wrong.” The friends entered the office and proceeded to tell the story of what had brought them there. “It was so hot out and we wanted to go swimming in the river,” Maya described. “It stunk so bad and there was trash everywhere,” said Hali. “But they still went in,” Kenn added. “We probably shouldn’t have,” Hali noted, “It gave me a headache and a rash.” “It gave me a rash and a cough,” Maya related. “You are probably right,” Doctor Darya remarked, “That river has become extremely polluted because of the human’s lack of sewage treatment. That means that when the humans go to the washroom, their waste isn’t always properly contained. This contaminates the water and brings a lot of big problems.” “That’s not good,” Hali said unhappily, “Can we help fix this?” “Yes, we need all the help we can get to help bring awareness to the pollution of water,” Doctor Darya offered. “Everyone can do their part in helping fix these issues whether you be a kid or an adult. You could help by telling people about the issues with wastewater treatment or you could even help by cleaning up the trash you saw on the bank.” “That’s so cool that we can help,” Maya exclaimed, “I never knew that I could help make a difference even though I’m a kid. Let’s start helping as soon as possible!” As soon as Maya and Hali felt better, The Changemaker Trio returned to the dirty riverbank, this time, along with their other friends. They were ready to help make a difference by picking up the trash and posting posters describing the issue of wastewater treatment. Hali, Maya, and Kenn left feeling good that they now understood that they could make a difference despite their age. They want you to know that you can make a difference too!
author: Riley  Damiano
illustrator: Harshika G; Presley Damiano; Rhea Nandy

title: Water, Water Everywhere, Not a Drop to Drink
text: “Water, water everywhere, not a drop to drink,” said the English teacher. He was teaching a poem to the students of class ten. Gopal was the topper of the class. Though he was a good student, his teachers and friends did not like him as he thought very highly of himself and could be very rude. When the teacher was explaining this, he asked him, “Sir, how is it possible that there is water everywhere, but no drop to drink? I agree that most of the earth is covered with salty water that cannot be used for drinking. But we also have so much freshwater in our rivers, ponds and lakes. We are all using that water. Sir, don’t think you are making any sense!” “With respect to your question, if we only consider fresh water, then the sources of freshwater are consistently depleting, especially in big cities like ours. Groundwater tables are falling, lakes and ponds are either very polluted or are drying up. Wells and tanks are also not in a good state,” the teacher replied. “Whatever,” Gopal said haughtily. The teacher was deeply hurt by Gopal’s remarks. He decided that the only way in which Gopal could be taught a lesson was not by scolding him but by showing him the mirror of reality. A few days later, the annual picnic for all students of Class 10 was organized. The teacher purposely took them to the water department of the city’s municipal corporation. All the students whined about what a boring place it was as it looked like a huge office where people were sitting on uncomfortable-looking chairs, working on thick files. The teacher approached one such middle-aged man, he was reading report from behind his black, horn-rimmed spectacles. “What are yo doing?” he asked. “Making the annual reports on water scarcity in the city. Most water tanks in the southern and western parts of the city have dried up. I have no clue how will we manage water supply in those regions. We supply them water once in three days, but I think now we will have to supply water once in seven days.” “Those are poor quarters of the city. They don’t protest much. Though they aren’t getting affected now, the rich will also be affected sooner or later,” another official joined their conversation. Gopal seemed very surprised. “That is not all! The six major lakes of the city have become toxic. We will soon not have sources to produce paper, manage hydroelectricity or fisheries,” the first official said. “To top it off, the weather department has predicted acid rain, which further endangers all water sources, including groundwater. It also causes soil erosion and robs the soil of its fertility. So, on the one hand we are facing water scarcity, and on the other, we are also dealing with water toxicity.” “Another matter of concern is that statistics show that most regions are hit by a certain phase of severe drought due to less rain once in every five years. Our city can be struck by such a situation any time now,” the teacher said. Gopal was very worried now. “What will we do if such a time comes? Will we have enough water for washing, cleaning and other household chores?” A young office clerk gave a worried laugh, “Son, water for household chores is a far cry. It may also happen that we don’t have enough water to drink... maybe the government has to set a limit as to how much water each individual can use in a day.” “So, basically, we will have water everywhere but perhaps not even enough to drink as it has been exploited so much that it has become unfit for further use! exclaimed the lady official. Gopal realized his mistake. His classmates and him exchanged worried glances. He recalled the line in the poem: “Water, water everywhere, not a drop to drink.” “Can nothing be done to prevent this from happening?’’ Gopal asked. “Well, rather than leaving everything to the government, we as citizens must be aware of the importance of water. We must consciously save water in our homes, schools, colleges and offices. We must raise our concerns against water pollution so that the government feels pressured to take the necessary steps to save our resources,” explained the officials. The teacher saw that his students had understood their mistake. “Most importantly, we must not take our natural resources for granted. They can be snatched away. This rule applies not just to water, but land, air, forests and wildlife. They all live independently, but interdependently.” “We understand,” nodded Gopal humbly. By taking his students outside the four walls of the classroom, the teacher not only taught a proud Gopal the unpredictability of our state of life, but also made his other students more environmentally conscious citizens.
author: Pavithra Rajesh

title: The Water Cycle
text: A lonely cloud was floating all alone in the sky. It looked sad. Suddenly, a gust of wind came from behind, forcing the cloud to float even further. The wind asked him, “Why do you look so sad, Mr. Cloud, everything alright with you?” “No, my dear,” said the cloud, “I am not all happy. I don’t have enough water in me. How will I show my face to the farmers in the villages who are waiting for rain for their crops. And how will I meet the little kids in towns and cities who want relief from the scorching heat? There is almost no water in me.” “Why is there no water in you, Mr. Cloud?” asked a little bird that was flying in the air when she overheard the conversation between the wind and the cloud. “Ah, little bird. Want to know everything, don’t you? The water cycle has been disturbed this year.” “What is the water cycle?” asked the little bird. “The water cycle manages the flow of water in nature. Water evaporates from water bodies and forms water vapour. This water vapour reaches the sky and turns into tiny water droplets. These water droplets then, form clouds like me. Due to too many droplets, the cloud becomes heavy and discharges the water, this water again reaches back to the water bodies. Then the cycle starts again. When there are too few droplets, the cloud is unable to provide any rain to anyone. That is the situation with me,” replied the cloud. “This year has been particularly bad. Human beings have been using water so rapidly that there is very less water in all the water bodies,” said the wind. The little bird felt very bad for the cloud. When it grew dark, she flew back home. She narrated what the cloud and the wind said to her mamma and papa. They felt very bad for the cloud. The next day, when mamma and papa bird went to work, the little bird decided to go to the countryside and speak to the people there. she flew and flew till she reached the countryside. There were some milkmaids resting under a tree. “Hi, everyone!” said the little bird. The milkmaids seemed to be surprised on seeing her. “Hello, little bird! Do you wish to speak to us?” “Yes, I indeed wish to. I wish to discuss how the water levels in streams, ponds and lakes are so low. Do you know that the water cycle is disturbed because of this? Clouds do not contain enough water to provide rain.” replied the bird. “Yes, we know that. But what can we do? The water bodies will only be revived after it rains,” answered a milkmaid. “But we can’t wait till it rains heavily. Besides, it will not rain heavily until evaporation takes place. And large-scale evaporation cannot take place until there is enough water in the water bodies,“ the little bird said, explaining the basic principles of the water cycle. If it doesn’t rain then neither us nor you will have enough water for household chores or even drinking,” explained the little bird further, “do you want to get into such a situation?” “I understand. This is so sad,” said one milkmaid. “We must do something,” said another. “But what can we do?” commented the third. “We must start saving water bit by bit and channelize it to our lakes and ponds,” said the first milkmaid. “If we want to save water bit by bit, we must try rooftop rainwater harvesting. I googled it last night. It is very simple and cost-effective. Whenever it rains, the rainwater slides from the roof to collect the water. A storage tank is installed in the ground to collect the rainwater. It may sound expensive, but it is actually not. If we try, we can arrange for a makeshift rooftop rainwater harvesting system.” “But we are poor people. We don’t have any savings as such, so how can we manage to build such infrastructure on our own?” asked the first milkmaid. “In that case, we should run a fundraising campaign. We can go from door to door asking for funds and run a campaign on social media as well. From the funds collected, we can easily buy the required materials,” said the second milkmaid. “This is a good idea,” everyone agreed. From the very next day, they began implementing their plan. As soon as they received the funds, they installed one rooftop rainwater harvesting system. Within a year, most homes had a rooftop rainwater harvesting system. Both animals and humans contributed to these funds and learnt to live in complete harmony. They also started experimenting with other kinds of water conservation systems like reviving old stepwells and creating new drains and dams to store water.
author: Bhumija  Rishi

title: Ron's bird house
text: Ron looked sad. His closest friend Anvi had sent him her selfie with her pet parrot Tia. Ron also wanted to keep a pet bird at home but his mom did not allow him. Ron's dad approached him. "Let me see the photo" he said. Ron showed the pic. " Anvi looks happy but... Tia looks sad. Doesn't she?" Ron looked at the bird closely. She looked sad indeed. " Why is she sad?" Ron asked "Because she wants to be free. Who would like to live in a cage!" Dad said. "Do you want to have a happy pet bird?" asked Dad. "Can I REALLYYYYYYY... have a happy pet bird" Ron exclaimed. "Yes, I can help you have one. Why don't you build a bird house?" Dad said. "Lets build one". Rons face brightened up. Ron and his sister Tiasha collected pieces of plywood and joined them to make a bird house. They hung it on a tree branch. The day passed by. Not a single bird came to Ron's bird house. "You have to wait son. The birds need to make sure that your bird house is safe. Keep some water and bread crumbs to attract them" A week had passed and Ron was very angry on his dad. "You promised me a happy pet bird. I have been waiting for so long. Not a single bird has visited our bird house" Just then a beautiful bird came and sat on Ron's bird house. Very soon another bird joined the first one. They had twigs in their beaks. Ron's face broke into an 'ear to ear' smile. By the end of the next week, the bird family had settled comfortably in the bird house. Ron had named them Puchki and Puchku. In a months time they laid eggs, which hatched soon. Puchki and puchku were busy all day, bringing food for the young ones. Ron used to click their photos, which he posted to his friends. He was get famous day by day. He was busy attending phone calls of his friends. Looking at Ron's popularity, Anvi released her pet parrot. Tia was now free and she joined the flock of parrots staying in the nearby tree. Everybody was happy Nest man of India Do you guys know about the state bird of Delhi..... Well, it is Sparrow, commonly known as gauriya (In Hindi). Unfortunately, this particular bird a rare species in the capital today. About two decades back, Rakesh Khatri, a resident of Delhi got really concerned watching this alarming rate of decrease in the number of sparrows in NCR. Ever since, h e built small nests for these birds and placed them all around: balconies, rooftops and even under flyovers. To the pleasant surprise of everyone, the sparrow is now back in Delhi. We are all proud of you.
author: Reyansh Roy

title: HAPPY TEACHERS DAY !
text: I thank you all for trying so hard to make us understand the concepts in Maths and other subjects too. When someone asks the question twice, you answer them with great patience, which I adore the most. When students don't follow the rules, you explain again and again even just for one person. I love you all very much, and you're like my super heroines who has sprang up to teach us. I am very grateful and thankful to all my Teachers. Bye bye hope to see you all very very soon in school.
author: Stuti

title: Lily sees a rainbow
text: Lily was a ten year old girl. She wished to see a rainbow. One day she was walking with her mother. It started raining. Tippy tap...tippy tap..it was drizzling. Whoosha...whoosh...whoosha...whoosh.... Here comes the thunderstorm. Quick, quick, open your umbrella, says Mother. Ok Mom, says Lily Lily opened her umbrella and suddenly the sun came out. The sun shone its light on the raindrops. A magical rainbow formed in the sky. Look Ma...a rainbow!!!! Lily was really happy. She finally got to see a rainbow. Asking questions about the rainbow, Lily chattered away with her mother forgetting all about the rain and her umbrella. As soon as she reached home, Lily ran inside the house and told her brother about the rainbow.
author: Naishaa Bansal
illustrator: Edwin  Irabor; Jesse  Breytenbach; Jesse  Breytenbach; Musonda  Kabwe; Offei Tettey  Eugene; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Shrenik Appari; Sinomonde Ngwane

title: A Student and an Almond Tree
text: There was a village called Kambattu near Tiruvannamalai in northern part of Tamil Nadu, India. the village was very beautiful. There was a river with full of water and farmers were cultivating paddy, sugarcane and ground nuts. Murugan was a student in the Kambattu primary school. He was studying in 5th standard. He was looking forward to going to higher grades. He was enjoying his childhood in the village. Murugan's father Krishna Murthy told Murugan that, next year he should go to Thiruvannamalai as there was no 6th grade in Kambattu. Murugan listened his father quietly. Krishna Murthy searched for a good school in Tiruvannamalai, the district head quarters and finally found a school for Muru gan to pursue studies from 6th standard. Kala was Murugan's mother, she told, "you need to study well and get rid of family debt". She reminded Murugan of the drought in the village and told how difficult it is to survive. Murugan listened to his mother quietly. Kala gave him motivation to study well. Murugan's family condition had a deep impact on Murugan as he started 6th Standard in a new school. Murugan's mother Kala told Murugan about a verse from Tirukurral, written by Tiruvalluvaur, the great Tamil poet, "For educated, there are two eyes, for uneducated, there are two wounds in the face" First day, Murugan went to school and observed the environment, teacher, friends in the school. He also observed trees and birds while commuting between school and his village. He was feeling dizzy in the class. The teacher use to teach the subject, given homework and conduct exams. but he was not able concentrate at all. He was thinking that there was some issue in his body and reported to this to his parents. Murugan parents took him to hospital but no doctor was able to diagnose the problem. Murugan did not have any option but just continue the way he was. Due to this he failed in all the subjects. One fine day, On the way school, Murugan sat under an almond tree and observed how birds were eating and enjoying. Murugan also started breaking the almond nuts by stone and started eating. He enjoyed the nuts and went to school. The Next day also, he stopped at the almond tree, ate the nuts and also neem fruits that was eaten by many parrots and other birds in the tree. Murugan enjoyed the nuts, fruits and birds chirping a lot. This continued for a forty eight days. After that, he felt very fresh in the morning and he was interested to go school early for his studies. while going to school, as usual, he ate some almond nuts and neem fruits. Now, Murugan felt very fresh and sharp in his studies. Almond and neem had given him all the required nutrition and energy that was missing! Murugan completed his studies successfully. He scored well and got first rank in his school and in the district. Murugan joined his passionate profession and lived a happy life with this family.
author: P B Senthil Kumar
illustrator: Abhishek Choudhury; Abin  Shrestha; Ayoub  Makotha; Brad Cuzen; Catherine Groenewald; Gayathri Kalyanaraman; Jayesh Sivan; Lily Banerjee; Ninoshka Dias; P B Senthil Kumar; Padmanabh; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Tanvee Nabar; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Nina and her Dog
text: Nina is becoming sorrow day by day, because whenever she asks her parents for dog, they always denied. After few days, again she asks her father for a dog but he says " we can't afford a dog,Nina ". She makes a grumpy face and goes away from there. Then Nina decides of collecting her own money and then buying a dog. Nina calls her all the friends to help her collecting money as she is very eager for a dog. One day Nina peeps into her piggy Bank and starts jumping. She screams with joy and starts whirlling all over her house. Everybody in her house gets confused about her happiness and joviality. When her parents get to know about this,they are out of blue due to her efforts. They understands her, " Why did you collect money by your own?, we are just planning to buy a dog on your birthday." Nina utters sadly, " I was not sure that you will buy a dog for me,I thought you didn't have enough money to fullfill my desire because you can hardly earn for our livelihood, that's why I took assistance from my all mates and cut my unnecessary expenditure. ". Her parents become very content to see her daughter's sagacity.Finally day arrives when they altogether go to a shop and take a adorable puppie with brown fur.Nina cuddles her parents and thanks them.
author: Aahana Mishra
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Dhiman  Sarkar; Phùng  Nguyên Quang; Santosh Pujari; Shanta  Hitang; Tanvi Bhat; Ujwal Nair

title: Small moments count Big
text: Small things really matter and they have their own importance. We forget to smile. We even forget to stay happy. Small things can be as simple as popping a bubble wrap. Watching the sunset or sunrise. The smell outside after the rain has stopped. Having sometime to yourself to read a book you love. Taking the time to help someone. Small actions make up our habits. Small words make up our thoughts. The little things we overlook build up the big ones. Small things build friendships and relationships. With each act of kindness, you will be enough to spread more love and optimism into the world. Be the reason someone believes in GOOD. Make your loved ones remember the little things about you. The way you smile, your scowl, what you would have done or said in a given situation and the way having you around made them feel. Watch your favorite movie, go for window shopping or listen music. we have a lot of pressure to save things for the right moments, but if it makes you happy, then why can't any moment be the right moment? Why wait? Starting from today make every small moment count. Live laugh and love.
author: samudra roy
illustrator: JP Brouard; Kalynne Vorster; Maaham Rizvi; ROSH; Sandhya Prabhat; Sinomonde Ngwane

title: The Two Elegant Cranes
text: They trawled from one end of the lake to the other looking for tasty food. We often spotted them with desperately flailing fish held in their beaks.They looked bautiful.Literally beautiful. The water level in the pond fell every night and a small mound of earth that emerged was their home for the night. This mound was a safe haven as nocturnal predators such as fox, wild cats and mongoose could not reach them easily. The two cranes called and and sometimes sang at the break of dawn. This was the signal for people to rise and begin their day. The people enjoyed their singing. I had never been able to see the pair of cranes at close quarters. Whenever we approached them, they would immediately move away with long-legged strides. Their bright red beaks and the velvety glimmer on their necks looked enchanting. Sometimes, we would run after them. When this mood seized us, they either moved to some place that was beyond our reach, or took a short flight that left us far behind in their wake. Often they would perch on the mound of earth inside the pond. Then they would beautifully fly away. At the end of the monsoon, we spotted a little crane along with the pair. He marched proudly between the long-legged ones, matching them step for step. I was utterly fascinated by the little crane. I would try very hard to get close to him but the older pair kept me firmly at bay. One day, some of us boys from the village entered the pond to pluck some lotus flowers. It was the middle of the afternoon. Everything seemed silent and still in the lazy heat of the sun. The people who worked their fields from dawn would go home by the afternoon. At home they would talk and laugh for the rest of the night. We spotted the pair of cranes in the pond, playing with the baby crane. All of us took it into our heads to chase the little crane. We ran and ran and ran and ran! As the pair of cranes ran pell-mell, they lost the little crane somewhere. All of us wanted to catch the little crane but he eluded us. He was not able to fly as yet but so swiftly did he move that none of us were able to keep up. He moved left and he moved right and we couldn’t catch him. We were so intent on pursuing him that none of us stopped to think that even if we did manage to catch him, how would he survive without his parents? We ran and we ran among the stalks of millet in the fields, hell-bent upon catching him. The hot sun beat down on our heads so that they fairly clicked and crackled. The little crane somehow managed to emerge from the field of millet. One of us aimed a stick at him ﻿.His name was James(the one who struck the poor crane).He fell down instantly! The moment he fell, we all froze in dismay. We ran to his side and tried to revive him. Someone tried to prop him up while someone else stroked his feathers. Another boy straightened his thin legs. One of us ran to the pond and brought some water in cupped palms and dribbled it on his beak. But he did not rise again. We were very sad for the baby crane. His parents combed the boundary of the millet field and searched desperately among the stalks, calling all the while. They took short flights for an aerial survey and continued to call but to no avail. Their voices grew dim as they kept up their anxious search. We all stood in a huddle under the jamun tree and berated our friend as we watched this sad display of love from the little crane’s parents. Finally, they found their baby. As soon as they saw him they stood facing each other and spread their wings as if to protect the little one and gently stroked him with their beaks. They stood and wailed and mourned their little one for a very long time, shielding him with the canopy of their wings. Sometimes they would raise their beaks heavenwards and cry. They would flap their wings and raise their voices together. Sometimes they cried separately. Their pain turned into tears dripping from our eyes. They started crying heavily for their little one. How sweet looking was the little crane. As the evening shadows lengthened, bereft of hope, the pair of cranes left.Probably extremely sad. I have never forgotten this incident from my childhood. Perhaps the crane family showed me how we must love all living beings without wanting to possess them. I wanted to share this message with everyone an our planet. Please protect all life forms on earth. After all, they are also living organisms. Even if they are unable to speak,they also feel pain,love and freindship.
author: Kautilya Agrawaal

title: MOM's BOY
text: One fine day Vishikh is playing all around the house. Amma called him and said to sit along with her. Amma: What are you doing Vishikh? Vishikh: Amma I playing with my favorite. Amma: Oh! title: Monkey Business on Stage
text: Khajuria village was suffering from Ramlila fever. It was nothing new, as Kallu said, they got it every year. The fever usually started a month before Dussehra. As the low, dark grey monsoon clouds drifted away and the sky turned a glittering blue, there were festivities in the air and everyone began talking about Masterji and the Ramlila. Everywhere in the village, at Dharampal’s chai shop, in the vegetable fields, at the grocery store, in Moti Dadi’s courtyard and at the tube-well, there was a single question being asked. Kallu often said admiringly, “Masterji is the producer, director, scriptwriter and music composer of Ramlila and only he knows what we will see this year.

title: Umbrella
text: UMBRELLA! Oh don't get confused he is a dragon fly.He's very busy buzzing around. Dragon flies are mostly seen when it's about to rain. They move in a group buzzing around! UMBRELLA loves playing hide and seek in the rain. Look at him he's so happy and he is trying to hide behind the leaf. His friends are looking for him. Do you think Umbrella will be soon caught by his friends? Hey where is Umbrella? did you see him they started asking one another. No said the friends, let's go and look for him we are late. Oh! look at this creature.......... While going near the pond Umbrella saw his friends. Hey! come here friends look at this creature, Suddendly a creature came out of the water. title: A lone star
text: There was a lone star in the dark void known as the Universe. It's bright light was warm and gentle, and as it spread so did life around the Universe. The star was no more alone in the cold. It's glow brought happiness and joy. Everyone loved and workship the star, till one day some of her flatterers asked her to increase her light in the hope to prosper more. And the star carried out their request, since that was her duty now. As its glow grew, the warmth and lifeful sooner became harshness and scorching. It was so bright that for a moment the whole known Universe turned entirely white. As soon as the light dissipated the star happy and proud of her work turned to see the happy faces of its flatterers. But... there was no more laughter and cheers for the star, who turned back to be alone in the void. A lone star.
