title: Will a lion brush its teeth?
text: She is Laya, a very smart kid. Even though she is a bubbly girl, she has a fault. Laya does not like to brush her teeth. Every day, Laya will refuse and argue with her mother who asks her to brush her teeth. Laya's mother used to tell her daily about the benefits of brushing the teeth twice, once in the morning and once at night. Laya's mother used to tell that brushing the teeth is necessary for the protection and health of the teeth. Whatever her mom says, Laya will say yes and then run off to play. In spite of her mom's advice, Laya was never interested in brushing her teeth. One day Laya had a doubt. Do goats, lions, and tigers brush their teeth or not? Laya set out to find the truth. She went to the goat that is brought up in her house and asked, "Do you brush your teeth?" The goat said, "I don't brush my teeth. You ask the hen." She asked the hen the same question. The hen said, "We don't have teeth. You ask the dog." Laya also asked her puppy Tommy. Tommy also told that it does not brush its teeth. Tommy asked her to go and ask the cat. Laya asked the cat. The cat said, "I don't brush my teeth. You go and ask the calf." Laya went to the back of her house where the calf and cow were tied and she asked them. They both told no. The cow said, "Maybe wild animals in the forest brush their teeth." After hearing what the cow told, Laya walked and walked and reached the forest side. She asked the same question first to the bunny rabbit who had sparkling teeth. The rabbit also said, "I don't brush my teeth. Ask the cheetah that comes at the back." After saying this, the bunny rabbit jumped and ran away. After walking a little far, the cheetah came. Laya asked, "Do you brush your teeth?" The cheetah said no and asked her to ask the bear that comes at the back. She asked the bear. The bear also said no. Laya thought that the bear told a lie. So she jumped up on the bear and twisted its ears. The bear cried with pain, and the cheetah ran off in fear. Hearing the voice of the bear, the king of the forest, the lion came. The lion came and asked, "What is the noise?" Laya asked the lion, "Do you brush your teeth?" The lion said, "All those are the work of humans. No animal brushes its teeth." Laya wondered aloud, "You all don't brush your teeth. Then why are they asking me to brush my teeth daily?" The lion laughed and said, "We don't eat foods rich in carbohydrates. Humans eat a lot of food filled with carbohydrates. This food gets stuck in between the teeth and stays there." A cat came there and said, "Yes." The lion said, "Foods that stay in between the teeth will affect the teeth. They ask you to brush your teeth to clean it well." Laya found out that brushing the teeth was necessary. She thanked the lion and jumped happily and walked towards her home. Hereafter, Laya will brush her teeth daily.
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Henu; Karmacharya K.K; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Mamun Hossain; Partho Sengupta; Promina Shreshtha; Rajani Muralidhar; Rohit Bhasi; Samit  Shrestha; Santosh Pujari; Sushmita Viswanathan

title: Counting the food!
text: How many animals live in the jungle? Zero? One? Two? Three? Or maybe more? An insect? An insect is not an animal! How many animals live in the jungle? Zero animals! The bug is gone, but there is a tiger. Tigers are orange and black. How many animals live in the jungle? An animal! ﻿ T he tiger is looking at a tree. There are birds flying around the tree. H ow many animals is there in the jungle? Eleven animals! But what is in the tree There are monkeys and birds in the tree. The bird is singing! How many animals are there in the jungle? Two animals! What else is next to the tree? The bird sees a porcupine under the tree. How many animals are there in the jungle? Three animals! What else is next to the tree? Wow! That's a lot of animals! title: Real Beauty
text: Look at me. L ook how beautiful I am w ith green feathers and a red beak. Look at you. You are as black as darkness." The puppy looked all around and sadly said, "Yes. Just as the parrot told, no one is black. The cock has a red comb. The rats are brown. So, everyone is beautiful. Only I'm black." The puppy sadly asked its mother, "Mummy. Why I'm so black?" The mother told, "What is wrong if you look black? Why do you worry about that? Everyone praises how loyal we are. Instead of feeling proud about that, why are you thinking about your color and feeling sad?" But the puppy always had an inferiority complex about its colour and worried about it. So, the puppy could not sleep that night. The puppy came out of its home, wagged its tail, and ran about here and there. As the dog kept running, it realised that it had entered a forest. Suddenly, the dog heard a scream. The dog was taken aback. The dog looked in the direction of the scream. An owl with large eyes was sitting on a tree branch. It was very scary to look at the owl. But the puppy gathered courage and asked the owl, "Are you happy?" The owl said, "Yes. I'm very happy. Why do you have that doubt?" The puppy said, "Your large eyes look so scary. The whole forest vibrates when you scream. Are you not worried about that? But, you are telling me that you are happy." The owl angrily said, "I'm the night watchman of this forest. Do you know that? Moreover, did you not hear people telling that owls are very intelligent? All these make me proud. Go! Go!" The puppy got scared and ran away. A fox came in front. The puppy stopped the fox and asked, "Hi Fox. Are you happy?" The fox said, "Why are you asking? What is lacking in my happiness?" Hesitantly, the puppy said, "No. You are short. People also tell that you are cunning. Don't you worry about that? That is why I asked." The fox told, "When I'm not worried about my height, what is your problem? I don't bother if people call my intelligence as cunningness. Do you know how many friends I have saved by using my intelligence? I'm proud of all that. So, I'm happy." Saying so, the fox ran away without waiting for a reply. ﻿ At that time, a shining firefly came flying and cast a brightness upon the dark forest. The puppy wagged its tail and stopped the firefly. The firefly stopped flying for a few seconds and asked the puppy, "What is it?" The puppy said, "Now you are casting brightness. But no one can see you at night. That must make you sad. I think there is no happiness in your life." The firefly said, "Who told you that I'm not happy? I give out light when light is needed. Isn't that enough? I'm helping my friends as much as I can. That happiness is enough for me." Then, the firefly flew away swiftly. Now, the puppy saw a bat hanging upside down on a tree. The puppy looked at the bat and said, "You ugly bat, do you know that you are not beautiful? When everyone walks and flies straight, you alone are hanging upside down. You must be sad about that." The bat laughed and said, "Haha! I'm not worried about my appearance or hanging upside down. I'm of great help to the farmers. That makes me happy." The bat then flew out of the tree. The puppy now understood everything. It ran fast towards its home. Its mom was worriedly waiting outside the home. The mom lovingly asked, "Where did you go my dear pet?" The puppy told all that happened. The puppy said, "Hereafter, even I'm not going to worry about my appearance or colour. Tell me, who is as loyal as us? I'll think about that and feel proud." The mom kissed the puppy on its forehead. Later, they both went to sleep. "Dear Children. What the puppy told is true, right? Beauty is not in colour or appearance. Our character, how we behave, and how we help others, is most important. That is real beauty."
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The Western Horse
text: Prakash was a ordinary boy.He had one brother-Praveen,and his Parents-Padmaj Srivastav and Ramini Srivastav. He was underestimated in his family except for his brother. Praveen treated him like a teacher and that made him happy. One day,his parents and Praveen had to go to Delhi for Praveen's college application,so Prakash started living with his best friend-Ravindra. Ravindra was their neighbor and 3 weeks younger than Prakash. Prakash had tripped over Praveen's favorite child toy-a toy horse. He got a flick of memory near him- They loved horses!!!He was surprised and inarticulated by the memory.The very same night,He dreamt about horses and the next day set out for an adventure-bring home a horse for him and his brother.While packing, Ravindra found him and looked inexplicable. He asked Prakash "What are you doing?" Prakash didn't want Ravindra to know so he prevaricated "Mum and Dad called me and said they will return early."The next moment,in a jiffy, Ravindra went and catechized his mum"Mum,did Prakash's mum text you that they will come early?" Luckily Prakash was eavesdropping and he had his mum's phone to call his parent she typed that they would be coming early secretly and Ravindra's mom said yes!!! As he was passing a hay field he saw a stranger on a mat. Prakash looked enervated while the stranger-Raghbir looked vigorous. He noticed Prakash and said"Hi.I am Raghbir. Come and sit,come on." Prakash agreed and interrogated"Why are you alone?""I need my pet" replied Raghbir. My horse ran west. I wanna find him.""I need a horse as my pet too!! Lets team up!" propounded Prakash. They agreed. Raghbir took of his hood to reveal a hat which divulged his long hair in a ponytail.They high-fived each other and set out for the journey.It had taken them 5 minutes when an aeroplane soared above them. It was the plane taking his brother and parents to Delhi!!! Prakash realized that his parents flight was delayed!!! They had plenty of time. They set of to west to Mumbai. There they rested under the trees shade for the night. They took out their book about horses and read for 30 minutes. Then they ate the fruits and went to sleep. When they woke up in the morning, they set out to the journey near Mahabaleshwar and Matheran. they found a horse foot print there. They followed it to a stable with horses!!!!!!!!!!!! They had found Raghbirs western horse!!! And Prakash and Raghbir rode their pets and took them home. Their horses stopped for water and sadly,there they departed. They went in their own ways and went to there own homes. Prakash saw his family aeroplane and came home before them. Praveen saw the surprise and jumped happily. They then lived happily ever after!!!!! Hello, I hope you liked the story and please love it and you will keep hearing from me!!!!!
author: Aadish Acharya
illustrator: Pallab Brahmaputra   dey; Aditya Gupta; Ajay Hembron; Ethan Thomas  Bishu; Rijuta Ghate; Riya Gogte; Rupesh Sudhanshu; Subinita Deshaprabhu; Tanishtha Teotia

title: What is my special skill?
text: There was a little boy called Adrien, he always thought that he was an average kid who was neither good at studies nor at sports…. All his friends has some or the other special skills. Like his friend Rani, she was so strong that she could lift up to 20kgs. His friend Munnia had such a beautiful voice that it would attract birds. His friend, Shrinivasan was so good at Mathematics that he could solve the most complex problems within no time. But Adrien was still wondering what his special skill was ….. He kept on thinking….. He asked his friends, his cousins, his family but unfortunately nobody knew what it was… He thought harder … but he could not find it out. So he felt downhearted. Later on his Amma assured him that he definitely has a special power. He was extremely upset, so he decided to do what he absolutely loved. He went to the kitchen to help his Amma. Little did he know that she had made his favorite dish for lunch "Meduvada and Sambar" to cheer him up. Amma you are just the best....he said. While having this delicious "Vada Sambar". Adrien thought of making something special for his friends. He wanted to make a dessert, but which one? He was confused..... Then his Amma suggested that he can make "Narali paak" Adrien exclaimed with joy “YESSSSSSSSSSS” So he and Amma got to work! Amma broke few coconuts and Adrien started grating them.... Amma heated a kadai and added some ghee to it. Then she added some desiccated coconut, sugar and milk powder. Stirred it well and cooked the mixture until it became dry and thick. She also added some cardamom powder and dry fruits. Simultaneously, Adrien greased a dish with loads of ghee. Amma transferred this hot mixture immediately into a container and spread it evenly. After cooling down the mixture, Amma cut it into small pieces and Adrien put it in a jar. The next day when Adrien went to the school. He shared the "Narali Paak" with his friends, which he had made on the previous day. It had turned out to be so delicious that they finished all of it within seconds. Everyone was impressed by his cooking skills. That is when Adrien realized that his special talent is “COOKING AND MAKING PEOPLE HAPPY” Adrien returned back home happily and told his Amma what happened at school. Amma replied that “Everyone is unique. We all are equally intelligent and skilled in some or the other way. We just need to discover our special talent and let it work it's magic.”
author: Tarka Indulkar
illustrator: Aratrika Choudhury; Debasmita Dasgupta; Imile  Wepener; Rajiv Eipe; Vibha Surya

title: Sunny Bunny And Foxy
text: Once upon a time, there lived a fox named Foxy. One day Foxy was feeling hungry - "I am starving for food", he said. Soon he saw a rabbit passing by. Her name was Bunny. When she saw Foxy, she screamed "Aah!!". Foxy caught Bunny when he heard Bunny's sound and he said "I caught you now!". Another rabbit named Sunny saw Foxy going to eat Bunny. title: make a new world
text: once upon a time there lived a girl sophia who was really young.She was playful and naughty.She had big eyes and 2 ponytails.One day when she was running in her garden she found a seed which was in oval shape she was not familiar with that before.She was puzzled. She was not understanding which seed was it.she thought of many fruits like pears,orange,pineapple etc but she still din't understand.She thought [this seed is really special]so without even telling her parents she planted the seed in her garden. she worked really hard.She used to come every evening and used to pour water.She did her best.Her parents were observing her day by day,her parents were thinking she is kind of moody. that plant grew taller and taller.Sophia was really happy to see the tree in that stage. slowly it became a tree and started giving mangoes. title: Come, let us play together!
text: He is Raju. He is six years old. Raju has autism*. He can't speak properly. He hesitates to mingle with others. So, he mostly prefers to be alone. *Autism is a nervous system disorder that impairs the ability to socialize. Other children don't play with children like Raju who have these defects. It is a sad situation for special children. They always play alone. Just like other special children, Raju also played alone. Even though Raju knows that others are ignoring him, he can't tell it out or express it. Raju plays in his dream world and enjoys it. Because no one invited him to play, most of the time Raju watched television. His mother kept asking him to go and play. Do you know what Raju likes? Riding a bicycle. But he does not know to ride the bicycle alone. His grandpa teaches him daily to ride the bicycle. Raju is very excited during such times. Keerthana is Raju's next-door neighbour. She is 10 years old. She is very active in studies and sports. She is very kind too. She likes Raju a lot. One day, Raju's grandma asked Keerthana to take Raju along with her to play. Keerthana agreed and went to Raju's room. There, as usual, Raju sat alone. Keerthana called him to play. Raju did not hear what Keerthana said as he was in dreamland. Keerthana came out of the room sadly and went near Raju's grandpa. She told him, "Raju does not come if I call him for play. Why?" Grandpa said, "He does not know how to mingle with society. We only have to teach him that." Keerthana asked, "What is the meaning of that grandpa?" Grandpa told, "The elephants we see in the city are trained. When they were wild elephants, a Kumki* elephant trained them. Like that, we have to show things that Raju likes and other children have to train him." *An elephant that trains wild elephants Keerthana got an idea after she heard what grandpa told. Keerthana said, "You don't worry grandpa. I will make Raju play with all the others." Keerthana took a spinning top and showed it to Raju. Raju has a lot of interest in things that spin. So, his attention turned towards the top. Keerthana showed him the top and said, "Come, let us play." She made him come out of the home to play in the streets. Keerthana spun the top on the street. Many children got interested in the top and came near Keerthana to play. But, everyone looked at Raju and moved away. Keerthana told them that only if they include Raju in the game she will give the top. Because the children were eager to play with the spinning top, they agreed to include Raju. All of them joined together and played with the top. Keerthana was very happy because everyone included Raju in the game. The following days, Raju played happily with everyone. He played according to the rules of the game taught by Keerthana and became friends with everyone. Nowadays, Raju is never alone. Because of Keerthana, Raju got a circle of friends. He always plays happily with the other children. In your friends' circle, you will include special children like Raju, isn't it?
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Agantuk Samaresh; Aindri C; Ajanta Guhathakurta; Angie & Upesh; Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Bindia  Thapar; Divya George; George Supreeth; Harshvardhan Gantha; Henu; Jacob Kono; Rijuta Ghate; Sanjay Sarkar; Shohei Emura; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Tanvee Nabar

title: Miley learns to swim....
text: Miley,5 year boy who loves to play games and and discover new things.. So let's see how miley learns to swim... It is a hot and a sunny day outside. Miley returned from school and reached home.Greetings from mom, Miley didn't answered. Miley's mother said " What happened miley why are you looking so upset today". title: The brave Giraffe
text: Once upon a time, there was a lion living in a forest. One day, the lion attacked a cow. Cow was scared and did not resist. The lion killed the cow. Few days later, the lion came across a giraffe. The giraffe was eating grass. Suddenly. the lion pounced on the giraffe. The giraffe was alert so he took his neck up and ran away. The lion could not chase him. The giraffe saved his own life. The morale of the story is: Do not be afraid of anyone and be brave.

title: A Thirsty Crow and a Pot
text: Once, There Was a Crow name Lony, Finding Food With His Friends because he was Very Hungry And Then He Saw Some Tomatoes.His friends Start collecting For their family but the Lony Wants to Find his food Himself Only Than He fly,Fly And Fly Only. He saw a Little Pond and near it He saw Some seeds. He Start Drinking In it And his hungry stomach filled. *The Moral Of the Story Is We should Be Independent On Ourself Only. We Should Not Be Independent on Any One.
author: Yashi Jorwal

title: A letter to my human
text: Dear Reader, We want you to help us with only one thing. Can you make cleaner, safer, and healthier homes for animals, birds, and us? Read this story to see what we can find out about germs and microbes. Do you know what germs are? Germs are teeny tiny microbes and they are unseen by the naked eye. They can be any where. If you are hygienic, and if you are healthy, they won’t come near you. Another kind of microbe is called fungus. Fungus grows on trees and food that has gone bad. If you touch or eat fungus, you’ll fall sick. Food germs Some germs grow on food too. Most of them are unknown, so people don’t have information about them. Some germs are very, very, very slow and some are very very fast. Ok, now that you have learned about germs, here are some letters that you might like to read. Hi humans! I’m so happy that you have started cleaning our environment because our forest has become very dirty indeed. Picnickers were trashing our environment. I hope you stay well from corona!! Thanks, Grizzly bear Hi... I’m really shy to say my name so... Anyway, thank you for cleaning up my pond. Now I have six tadpoles and one wife. Too shy, Toad. Hi hi hi!!! Thanks a lot! No long letters, Hare
author: Anna Chacko

title: Meena learns the value of time
text: Meena came from school she threw her bag and started watching TV. Her mother said to her '' your lunch is ready'' Meena said''okay''. Meena saw that it was her favorite chhole-puri. Then her mother looked around and said that''you haven't clean the room. Everyone in the family loved Meena. She was good in studies also. Suddenly the doorbell rang, it was her aunt, Meena hugged her. Then she asked her''aunt where is my chocolate''. Her aunt said '' leave the chocolate!! you are still in your school uniform''. She said ''Meena I have bought you the tickets for the magic show, it will begin at 4:00 pm''. Meena saw the clock it was 3:40. Her aunt said ''hurry!''. Meena ran to her room and then she washed her face and then ran away to change her clothes but it was 3:46. She had no time to change, so she ran to find her sandals but she couldn't find them, so she wore the same slippers. Her aunt said'' I have to fill the petrol in my car''. Meena didn't had her lunch yet. She was hungry but she had to go to the show, so she ran towards the gate and then opened the door then quickly sat in her aunt's car. They reached to the petrol pump, aunt quickly filled the petrol. Then Meena's aunt drove the car quickly but it was already 4:00. The show had already started thought Meena. All fault was of her only. She whispered quietly to her aunt ''I am sorry aunt for being late''. She smiled at her and said ''I have the tickets of 7:00 pm not 4:00 pm ''. She told her, ''I wanted you to teach the value of time''. Now you could have your lunch. They stopped at an ice-cream parlour. On the way to home, Meena told her aunt that she had learnt the value of time. Her aunt smiled and when they returned to home, Meena went to the bathroom and changed her clothes, ate her lunch and when it was 6:30 pm they went to see the magic show. Meena enjoyed it.

title: Granny's Sari
text: Granny's favorite sari was a special one. It had the picture of a forest. There, on the border, were pictures of spotted deer playing in the grass and fat lions sleeping on the rocks. Near the rocks was a silvery stream where a mother bear was busy catching fish for a baby bear. High up in the tall trees were monkeys eating fruits and squirrels eating nuts. When granny wore her sari, it would seem that all the animals printed on it were alive and moving as she walked. Granny had washed her sari and hung it on the clothesline to dry,when the wind came and blew it away. "Oh, no! My favourite sari has flown away!"said granny sadly."Don't worry granny,"said Anu,her little grand daughter,"I am sure we will find it." So granny and Anu went tomorrow to find their sari as it was getting dark outside. They met a policeman."Please Mr.policeman, have you seen my granny's sari?"said Anu politely."Of course, I have, yesterday I was chasing a robber who stole jewellery.He was running so fast that he was about to escape when a sari came flying down and wrapped him. The robber 'couldn't see and he bumped into a tree. I caught him and put in jail.Next week, I am getting a medal but the sari flew again". Anu and granny went forward.They met Mrs. Rao. "Good morning mrs. Rao...have you seen my granny's sari"?"Yes i have,yesterday, my daughter wanted to pluck some mangoes but the branches were too high.There came a green sari flying from the sky and settled to the topmost of the branch. She held the sari and shook it,many mangoes fell down.Here please take few..but the sari flew away". So Anu and granny kept walking when they saw Lakshmi, the fisher woman."Hello Lakshmi",said Anu."Have you." And she stopped because Granny tapped her shoulder and whispered, "Shhhhh....look!" There in a row stood Lakshmi's three children wearing new clothes.The eldest boy wore a green shirt of which were pictures of spotted deer playing in the grass.The girl wore a dress which was having a picture of a parrot on one pocket and a squirrel on other.The third boy wore a shirt with a picture of a fat lion sleeping on a rock!"What a wonderful day it is"said Lakshmi."I was wondering to make new clothes for my children, when a green colored sari came flying down and settled on my lap.I asked everyone of my neighbors,but they said that it wasn't their sari.So I cut it up into clothes for my children.Don't they look smart"?"Of course, Lakshmi". said granny."They look wonderful". Later that evening, Anu asked granny,"Are you sad because Lakshmi cut up your favourite sari to make clothes for her children"?"Oh no," replied granny with a big smile."When my sari was with me,it made me happy.After it flew away from me,it made so many people happy. I m not sad.I am happy.I always knew that my sari was very special." Anu,Granny and Grandpa ate fish that they had brought from Lakshmi and the mangoes that Mrs. Rao has given them....And they lived happily ever after. MORAL: We should never be angry or sad when someone has taken your thing by not knowing that it's actually yours...
author: Aarohi Tripathi

title: Natural Foods
text: Every day, I eat natural foods. Every day, I drink a glass of coconut milk in the morning. Every day, I eat a banana. My lunch consists of cucumber slices, oranges, grapes, small carrot pieces, and other fruits. My evening snack consists of groundnuts, dry fruits, roasted gram, and boiled tapioca and corn. For dinner, with great interest, I eat coconut flower with palm sugar. I also eat almonds, pistachios, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, cashew nuts, and other fried nuts. Natural foods are good for a healthy body. So, please make a habit of eating natural foods.

title: What insect is this?
text: I like insects a lot. Every night, I like to listen to stories from my mother. If the story is about insects, then I like the story more. Moreover, I read a lot of books to know about insects. I go to the garden near my house along with my friend Aadhi. There we see different types of insects. Using my father's binoculars, I can see different coloured insects. What insect is this? This is a spider. It is an insect with eight legs. It spins a spider web to live inside it. What insects are these? These are fireflies. These insects glow in the night. What insects are these? These are bees. A bee sucks honey from a flower and stores the honey inside a beehive. What insects are these? These are ants. Ants actively go behind one another. They build anthills and live inside it. What insect is this? This is a dragonfly. The arrival of dragonflies indicates upcoming monsoons. What insect is this? This is my favourite butterfly. These eye-catchy butterflies drink honey from the flowers. Today, I saw a lot of insects. Now, I'm going to fly away like a butterfly. Aadhi! Come and catch me. Haha! Did you know? Insects are the guardians of nature. We should not destroy them or be afraid of them. Those who research about insects are known as entomologists. Poochi Venkat wrote a book named "Insects: The Guardians of Nature." This book has a lot of information and also colourful photos of insects. Finally, here is a riddle about insects: Uncle built a tent. If removed, it becomes pieces. What is it? Answer:Spider Web

title: Language and Script!
text: Disha is a wonderful and smart girl. She is 8 years old. She is flexible in accepting the perspective of others. She has a sweet voice and speaks in a very level tone. She always takes a moment to think about what she wants to say before talking. She is a disciplined and well-mannered girl. Her hobbies are drawing, art and craft, reading books. One day her grandparents gifted a book. As she saw the book she fell in love with it and wanted to read it on the same day. The book was about "Language and Script". She opened a book and started to read. Language: Language is used to communicate, consists of a set of sounds and written symbols. We, humans, need language to establish and maintain relationships with each other. Language enables us to express feelings, desires, and emotions, etc. God blessed humans with a voice by birth. No other creatures have these special skills. Animals use gestures or sounds to convey their moods. For example the dog's bark, lion's roar, bird's chatter, etc. We, humans, learn the language from our mother's womb itself by hearing the voices, sounds, etc. As we grow we try to speak the letters, words, etc. The language can be expressed in three ways. 1. Sound (Speech) 2. Gesture (Action or Sign) 3. Graphic (Writing or Pictures) * When we humans use voice to communicate, it is called Sound (Speech). * When we humans use actions or signs to communicate, it is called Gestures. * When we humans use a symbol or drawing to communicate, it is called Graphic. We acquire our way to survive using these. In the world, there are many languages
author: Sushma Dhayapulae

title: What Was It?
text: It was 27 November 2018.The winter has started taking its harsh behaviour. Cold and icy winds rushed into the rooms. The air began to cool down. The temperature also drooped slowly.At night, the room would be filled with coldness and even when the windows are closed,the cold wind will enter the room through the airholes and the conclusion would be shivering. Clara as usual went to the market to buy some things for the Eve of Christmas as per her mother's long shopping list. While returning from the market, an old man, their neighbor who was leaving the house,gave her a paper roll. After returning to her house, she opened the paper roll; it was a calendar. She took it to the hall and hanged it in the wall and changed January to November. She sat on the sofa and switched on the television. She started watching a horror movie, her eye was caught at once on the calendar,it was showing the month of March instead of November.Thinking it was the presence of a ghost,she quickly grabbed the calendar and ran to the backyard and burned it.Icy wind blew and hit on her face.Leaving a cold breath heavily and chattering her teeth,she ran indoors. Still a question was left behind,was it the strong,mighty gusts of wind or was it a specter that changed the calendar?Confused with her question,she tried to recollect the incident.
author: ABHIRAMI KRISHNA
illustrator: Brad Cuzen; Isaac Gergan; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Pawnee Maiden; Shailja Jain Chougule; Sirawon Khathing

title: The Blue Beautiful Butterfly
text: I was sitting on my bed and watching butterflies from my window. They were fluttering their wings. Just then I saw something on the shutters. It looked like a bottle of medicine. There was a note beside it and it read " Drink This, Maximum Limit: 1.5 hour ". I didn't understand that. I thought it would just be something by my father, he is a scientist. I took no more time and drank it. Then after a minute I started getting wobbly and I shrunk to the size of the butterfly I was watching. I wanted to go out but the door was a little far as I was so small. Luckily, the window near me was open so I climbed it. I thought I would just jump from the window, but when you are so small the world around you is so big. From the window it looked like I was going to fall from Burj Khalifa! I jumped and landed on a trash can. From there I jumped to the ground. There I saw a butterfly resting on the ground. I quickly jumped on the butterfly. It started flying and reached a flower. It started sucking nectar from the flower with her tongue, which functions like a straw for them to suck it. Then it moved away. It went to her friends and I could hear them chatting. One said " Oh what a lovely day!" Another said " Let's go and find more flowers!" Then all of them started fluttering their wings and started flying. They left the garden and rose high in the sky. I was surprised by how they looked like but the climax was when the butterfly that I was sitting on made a loop. It felt like I was riding a roller coaster! Then after a while they landed in an orchard. They were very happy because they found a lifelong supply of nectar. One said "Yay! Let's have a party to rejoice." Another said "Good idea! Then they started preparing for the party. They had a party on a leaf and there was a runway from where they flew to the flower to get the nectar. They had a wonderful time and there was a butterfly who sang in the Butterfly language, "ButterFleasian". Then their party was over and they went to sleep in their new mansion made from leaves. It started to get late and I had to get home. I was thinking of how to do that and then a paper plane flew towards me which was thrown by a child. Just then I got the idea! I jumped on it and I flew with it and reached my street! My home was just near so I walked carefully. The entrance to my home was closed but I was so small that I could pass from the little space beneath the door. Suddenly there was a vibration in my body organs. My cells started to expand and I got back to my same height. I remembered that it said the maximum time was 1.5 hours. I was happy and looked for my father. I told him everything and said " That bottle of your potion you gave me was very nice". He replied. "What Potion? I didn't give you any." I was surprised and then said to my father "Wow!" "A mystery!" Butterflies Butterflies have the typical four-stage insect life cycle. Winged adults lay eggs on the food plant on which their larvae, known as caterpillars, will feed. The caterpillars grow, sometimes very rapidly, and when fully developed, pupate in a chrysalis. When metamorphosis is complete, the pupal skin splits, the adult insect climbs out, and after its wings have expanded and dried, it flies off.

title: everywhere dinosaur and dinosaurs !
text: Banti was amazed. He decided the pool's name - 'dinopool'! Banti was having so much fun in this trip. While looking outside, he felt sleepy and soon he slept. In his sleep here saw dinosaur eating mangos. This is amazing! Banti was going to his mama's village. There he was also going to eat mangos. In his dreams he saw dinosaurs flying. Fire was coming from the flying dinosaur's mouth. Banti was laughing in his dreams. Suddenly when light flashed on his face, he opened his eyes. But what did he saw? One tall dinosaur was throwing fire the boats in ocean. It is amazing! Actually it was the light house! Everywhere dinosaurs and dinosaurs!!
author: Sanskruti Khurde

title: who will win this game ???
text: Kala went to their grandfather's house in the village to celebrate the summer holidays. Both are good friends.Like them,their Grandfathers are long time friends. One day they called both of them and said, “Nila, Kala, we are going to conduct a competition for both of you, whoever wins they will get a great prize." Hearing that, Nila and Kala shouted "Hey..." and had fun. Both said yes to them. Both grandfathers looked at each other and smiled as they began to explain about the rules of the game and competition. "We will leave each of you in separate gardens so that both of you cant see each other. We will give you a paper with questions separately. W hoever finish and handovers the answer first will get prize. When asked,"are you both ready?", both nodded their heads with excitement and smile. Paper was given to both. The two greeted each other and parted ways. Nila,first opened the paper in her hand.First question, " I have an eye-catching color to look at I will not go town if I am fat The head as a crown But not the King-who am I? " Like Nila,Kala also opened her paper, The first question in the paper reads as, " The owner of the soft finger Owner of Greenness The Empress of the Town as long as she is skinny - who am I? ” Both are thinking! since nothing is understood,Lets see the next question!Both started reading.second question, Nila, " There is a relation between myself and nose Even if it doesn’t rain, the word cap exist in my name- Who am I? " kala, " Suitable for the sun The one who owes beauty Who has water but There is no water in the name - who am I? " They read it, with the conclusion that they could look at the last question left. Nila, " The first among three people It contains three different tastes From Kids to adult Everyone likes me - who am I " Kala, " Owner of red color If behaved Incessantly it becomes crushing weirdo - who am I " The two went in search of answers to the puzzles. Nila, as she browsed in the garden, carried eggplants, wedges and bananas by hand as answers to puzzles. Shortly after she left, Kala arrived at the scene. The grandfathers, who saw both their responses, said Kala had won. The two saw each other looking at each other and explained to them with a smile. Despite Nila came first between you two, because one of her answers incorrect.Besides being late,because all the answers being correct,Kala won this game. As we appreciate your effort, and we present this flower plants to both of you. well,now Lets see the detail description of question and answer! Nila's first, Brinjal has crown in its eye-catching purple head. No one will buy if this vegetable becomes old. Second, Capsicum is related with nose, it has word cap in its name. We have customary to say that the nose is red like chillies. Third, Mango is the first among the three fruits(Mango,Jackfruit,Banana). It has three flavours, acid taste(astringent)when it is fruit newly from the blossom, sour taste when it is unripe, sweet taste when it is fruit. Everyone loves mango. Now kala's, First, Ladyfinger is green in color and it is compared against Ladiesfinger. It is used when it is fresh and small. When it is aged it will be trashed. Second, cucumber is very suitable for the sun. It is used for beauty. It has water in it but no water in the name. (E.g. coconut water) Third, Tomato is red in color, if it fall slightly, it will be crushed. Because it has a high water content it can easily rot. Both got to know each other well. Also, Nila realized his mistakes. The two friends happily went to plant...
author: sai s

title: Unmasking the culprit
text: King of Dystopia never trusted anyone. One day- “I’m sure my spies do no work. I’ll test them!” So, one night disguising himself as a poor man, the king went and stuck posters all over the city stating that “THE KING IS A FOOL” The very next day he summoned all the spies. “Tell me who is responsible or I will boil you all in oil.” One of the spies stepped forward and replied, “Your majesty, you are responsible.” The king became glad and said, “My dear man you’re right. Keep this pearl necklace as a gift.” “But tell me…” he continued “How on earth did you know it was I who had stuck those posters?” “Very simple your majesty! Only you would have known so much about yourself! ” replied the spy.
author: Alana  Shaji

title: 4 blind man see an elephant
text: Asannya came to a village with his elephant. The villagers gathered to see the elephant.Four blind man lived in the village.They also gathered with the rest of the village. The people patted the elephant.It was tame and so did not cause any problems. One blind man grasped the elephant 'neck and said,"The elephant is like a pestle." The second blind man caught the elephant'tail and said "No the elephant is like a piece of rope."The third blind man found the elephants'ears. He said,"Why! The elephant is like a dustpan".The fourth blind man was holding a leg, so he said,"No,no,the elephant is like a pillar". In this way the four blind man described the elephant.But because they didn't have eyes they couldn't see the whole elephant.
author: D.Jahnavi jhanavireddy@gmail.com
illustrator: Brian Wambi; Idowu Abayomi  Oluwasegun; Rob Owen; Sandra   McDougall

title: TWO SONS
text: Once there was a father who had two sons. He wished to bring them up with good habits and manners in every activity of their life. However the eldest son followed his fathers advise at every level. Whereas the younger one, in the company of bad friends picked up bad habits. Thus the elder brother came up in ranks in his studies and he came first in all subjects with the result he was widely respected by his teachers and elders. The younger brother, because of his bad habits could not cope up with his studies and failed in all his subjects. Thus he became disliked by his teachers and others. Moral:- We should follow our parents advise so that we are successful in life.
author: Gauri Pai
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; Alina  Aphayvanh; Brian Wambi; Nan Hom Noon; Ram Kol; Rijuta Ghate; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: Courage
text: Once upon a time, there lived a fat monkey in a forest. The monkey was called "Jason". He was round and fat because he ate a lot of food and did not like to exercise. Therefore, he could not climb onto and swing on trees. Jason was very bored for many years because he did not know how to climb trees. He was also angry with himself because he did not know how to swing on the trees. But o ne day he decided to face his problems courageously! He thought to himself, "I will climb trees! I will swing!" Over the next few months, Jason worked hard in exercising. He was so hardworking that his face turned blue every time he exercised. However, he persevered in his exercises every day even though he was extremely exhausted... After a few months, Jason finally could climb onto and swing on trees! He lost 10 pounds of weight. He felt a lot lighter, and he was proud of himself. He shouted, "Yay! I've made it! I've made it!" In the end, Jason was able to play with his friends on the tall trees. Jason reflected and learnt that everyone should overcome their own problems with courage and bravery.
author: Chen Jiaxin Steven & Elycia Koh
illustrator: Priya Kuriyan; Ranga  Mahaarachchi; Robyn Penn; Rohit Bhasi; Ruchi Shah

title: Bapu

title: Fun with Kittu
text: K ittu was a 7 years old boy studying in third class. One day in school,Maths teacher conducted a test out of 25 marks. In the next class, sir distributed Exam paper to the class. Kittu got 25 out of 25. So sir congratulated him and said " keep it up". ﻿ In the evening he reached home and hurriedly he took a chair and kept it near the almirah, which was the highest place in his home. While he was climbing on the chair, his sister Mittu screamed, "mom...mom.. Kittu anna is climbing on the chair". Suddenly mother came and caught him. Mother asked " why are you climbing on the chair? ". Proudly he said, " Mom, I want to keep my Maths Exam paper on the top of the almirah because my sir said to me "Keep it Up".

illustrator: Ayoub  Makotha; Karen Lilje Lilje; Rajiv Eipe

title: Sock Puppet Tales
text: "Hello! I am Ricky the sock puppet! And I will tell you the story of the Mouse Puppet and Sock Sage!" said Ricky the sock puppet. Starting the story, a poor mouse puppet fell from the claws of an eagle puppet. The mouse puppet was screaming for help and the eagle puppet lost its dinner! The mouse puppet had fallen from the eagle's claws and ended up in front of a cat who thought God gave this tasty meal! Seem like every puppet wants to eat him, except... the Sock Sage! The sock sage came running and saved the poor mouse puppet from being eaten by the cat puppet, and the mouse puppet said "Oh great sock sage, thank you for saving my life, but please turn me into a cat puppet so I don't get afraid and eaten" said the mouse puppet. The sock sage turned the mouse puppet into a cat puppet, but later the cat puppet came back running from a dog puppet and asked the sock sage to turn him into a dog puppet, and sock sage was kind and did so. Again, the dog puppet came running from a lion puppet, and asked the sock sage to turn him into a lion puppet, even though the sock sage was getting annoyed, he turned the dog puppet into a lion puppet. After a long time, the lion puppet had eaten most of the animals in the jungle and couldn't find the rest, so he went back to the sock sage, not for help, but to eat him. When the sock sage was peacefully meditating, the lion puppet pounced onto the sock sage, but the sock sage heard the lion puppet and dodged him. Then the sock sage got angry and turned the strong and big lion puppet into a weak and small mouse puppet. The mouse puppet knew what his mistake he made and said "Oh sorry, the great sock sage, I do not deserve the power of a lion puppet, I shall leave soon." But the sock sage forgave the mouse puppet and told him to stay and he did. Soon they became best friends. Moral: Instead of being greedy for more, be happy with what you already have.
author: Rithvik Nakul

title: A Visit to the Dentist
text: One day when I got up in the morning I had a bad toothache. I couldn’t eat or drink anything because of the pain. I was crying because of the pain. Seeing me crying my mother called up the dentist. The dentist asked my mother to bring me to the clinic for him to check. So both of us went to see the doctor. While I was sitting outside the doctors room waiting for my turn I was so afraid. I don’t like injections or the big things the doctor put inside the mouth. So the doctor examined my teeth and said I have cavity and it needs to be filled so that there is no pain. I was so afraid so the doctor gave me a medicine after which I couldn’t feel anything. The doctor did a lot of work on my teeth and filled it with white cement. Before leaving the doctor asked me to eat less sweets and made me promise that I would brush twice a day everyday. I was happy that the pain was gone and came back home.
author: Adriel Nitin
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Debbie  Faber-Human; Nicola Smith; Nyambura Kariuki; Parag verma; Samidha Gunjal

title: Chintu And Bintu
text: Once upon a time, there were two sons Chintu and Bintu. Chintu and Bintu are the sons of the sea god. They love to play with water. But never wasted water. Chintu called Bintu and said "Bintu look over there.There is lots of water.Lets play with it. This is the best day ever. Then they went to a beach.In the beach Chintu met a man.His name was Magnus. The man told to Chintu that there is a treasure nearby. But Chintu ignored Magnus and played with his sea friends. He was bored so he decided to tell his sea friends about Magnus, what he told to him.His friends got interested so they said to Chintu "Chintu lets go find that treasure." So he gave enchanted sea suit to his sea friend he also invited Bintu for the treasure hunt.Then they all swam to the island where the man told to go to find treasure. Then they found the island and started digging.Finally they found treasure.Then they took the treasure and gave it to the sea god.

title: Gibby the Frog
text: Gibby the Frog loved diving. One day, there was a diving competition which he wanted sign up for, so he did.That night he went to see where the diving competition took place. It took place near a very tall coconut tree. Gibby hoped that he would win the competition because the prize is Gibby's favourite food lasagna.He prayed and prayed to God thinking that god can make him win.He really wanted that lasanga. The prize is a chicken lasanga his personal favourite. Gibby felt sad for the vegeterian divers but at least they were participating. Gibby even tried to find a shooting star to make a wish.He could not find one so he made a wish with the moon. The competition on the following morning. When Gibby woke up and saw the time, there were 2 minutes left until the competition started. Gibby ran so fast that he was able to reach in 3 minutes. Gibby was ready to dive! When Gibby's turn came- Gibby climbed the tree. When he reached the top, Gibby was little scared as he looked down but he put back his fears and... Jumped Splash! He had won! Gibby was very happy that he won the competition but he was most excited about eating the yummy lasanga. Hip! Hip! Hooray!
author: Aarav  Bansal

title: Moon come back
text: Ruhi loved the moon. She sang a song called ' Moon Moon oh shiny moon'every night. But today she saw there was no moon. She thought how did this happen.She said to herself 'Didi loves cookies,maybe she ate the moon..' She went to inspect Didi. She said 'no,ask Mama'.She thought Mama put the moon in the jewelry box. She asked 'Mama did you take the moon?'.She said' no ask Papa'.She went to Papa. She thought 'Papa must have put it in the moon painting'.He said'no' too. After that Ruhi was so tired that she slept on the couch. The next night she was in relief,the moon was back at last.She muttered 'naughty moon' and sang her song.
author: Mishka Gulia
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Garima Gupta; Kalyani Naravane; Kruttika Susarla; Sarthak Sinha

title: THE OWL
text: At night, when all is still, The forest's sentinel Glide silently across the hill And perches in an old pine tree, A friendly presence his!, No harm can come From night bird on the prowl. His cry is mellow Much softer then a peacock's call. Why then this fear of owls Calling in the night? If men must speak, Then owls must hoot- They have the right. On me it casts no spell: Rather, it seems to cry "The night is good - all's well, all's well"
author: avika singh
illustrator: Ariful Islam; Megan Lotter; Prashant Soni; Sain Thuokna

title: Our garden
text: This is our garden. My father planted Banana and Drumstick trees. My mother grows a greenish vegetable such as cucumber,bitter guard,squash,cauliflower. My grandfather planted beans,snow peas and long beans. My grandmother grows herbal plant such as aloevera,basil,camphor tree. My sister had grown green leaves such as mint,corriander leaves,spinach,curry leaves. I have planted fenugreek and corriander seeds. My younger sister have rose and jasmine plants. We all have to grow vegetables,fruits and green leaves in our backyard or terrace. To live a healthy life.

title: Come, Come, Heavy Rain!
text: This is my father. My father always dresses up well. He wears glasses. He wears pants and a shirt. My father likes a lot to wear a sweater over his shirt. At those times, my father looks even more handsome. One day, when my father started to go to the office, the rain started pouring. It was very heavy rains. We all were joyous. Father goes daily to the office on his motorbike. That day, in the rain, how could father go on the motorbike? Father thought that he can take the umbrella and go on a bus. But, he couldn't find his umbrella how much ever he searched for it. My elder sister came out of the house and started playing in the rain. When my younger brother saw a frog that jumped and played in the rain, he also came out and played. Look. At the back of my brother is a snail. Its beautiful house is on its back. Father did not know how to go to the office. He got angry. Poor father! When I saw my brother and sister who played in the rain, I laughed out aloud. My mom started to look at the rain and said, "Why is rain pouring like this?" ﻿ My grandpa was reading a book. He looked at my brother and sister who played in the rain and laughed. Grandma carried the baby in her arms and told, "Little one. Look at the rain." Then grandma sang. "Heavy rain, come, come! I will pound beetle nut for you, I will sieve temple sand for you, Heavy rain, come, come! After some time, the rain stopped and the sun peeked. Father got ready to go to the office. Rain went and the Sun came, Dum, Dum, Dum!
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Greystroke; Madhuri Purandare; Priya Kuriyan; Reshma Barve; Rijuta Ghate; Siraj Saxena; Zainab Tambawalla

title: What am I ?
text: Sai Sowmyanatha was in class 5-A. His family called him Sai fondly. He was a happy-go-lucky boy. Every day he went to school with a broad smile on his face. Every year he looked forward to the first day of school. There was Ananya, Akshit, Bhuvan, Prajeet in class 5 -A. What a happy group they were! What a delightful day he had all day! Some times digging into Nischit's tiffin box, or gushing over Prajeet's drawings or sometimes chit-chatting on Bhuvan's desk! Sai just couldn't stop talking! One day Rupa Miss was teaching adjectives in class. "Class, I want you all to write one sentence that describes you the best". That is your homework for the day ", she beamed as she went through their grammar book. Ananya was the best dancer in class. She learnt Bharatnatyam and danced gracefully. Sai knew Ananya would write " Graceful Ananya". ﻿ Bhuvan danced well. While Jishnu swam well, Akshit was very melodious when he sang a song...and the kids always gushed when Prajeet displayed his artwork in class. Even Dhruv was a charmer - he spoke at length about exoplanets and the marvels beyond the solar system! Sowmyanatha wondered what he was good at! Sometimes he did experiments in the kitchen just like his Science miss, Sonal ma'am. Sometimes he just loved dancing like Mahesh Sir, his dance teacher....and sometimes he just made a funny face... such as rolling his eyes!...and on most days he loved to paint. Sometimes a rainbow, sometimes clouds... or trees swaying in the wind!.... from green to brown...from orange to red...the colors danced a happy dance in his mind. But what was he? Was he a painter??? Was he a dancer? What was he good at, he wondered. All his friends were good at what they did. From Bhuvan, the dancer to Jishnu, the swimmer, to Akshit - the singer, Sowmyanatha knew all his friends would have nice things to say about themselves. Worried, he went to amma asking help. and his amma said... "You are friendly, kind, and helpful...." " You share smiles with all your friends "... That makes you... "A KIND BOY "... Sowmyanatha went to sleep, with a smile plastered on his face. He knew what he had to write the next day! He may not be the best dancer He may not be the best singer... or an artist But what he knew was - He was the kindest boy around! Children here, children there. Adding brightness everywhere... Some are quiet, some are LOUDDD... Some are dreamers, some are thinkers Some are naughty, some are NICE... But above all, they add SPICE In an otherwise boring LIFE...
author: Vani B
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Anupama Ajinkya Apte; Deepa Balsavar; Dilna K Chandran; Karmacharya K.K; Krishna Chandran; Lutfia  Kamish; Nguyễn  Minh Hải; Ouk  Ratha; Rajiv Eipe; Reshma Barve; Reyansh Roy; Rijuta Ghate; Shailja Jain Chougule

title: The Braveheart
text: Author Rabindranath Tagore was born on 7 May, 1861 to Maharshi Debendranath Tagore, one of the leaders of the Brahmo Samaj, and Sarada Devi. He was a distinguished Bengali poet, writer, painter, playwright and composer of songs. He was homeschooled by a variety of teachers in a variety of subjects. He composed ‘Sishu’, ‘Dakghor’, ‘Birpurush’, ‘Proshno’, ‘Sahaj Path’ and others for children. He was the recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in the year 1913. In 1915, the prestigious ‘knighthood’ was awarded to him by the British Raj but he soon renounced it as a protest to the Jallianwalah Bagh massacre of 1919. A highly renowned artist, he was known for introducing the Indian culture to the West which led to his establishment of the ‘Vishwabharati’ University in Santiniketan which is a mosaic of the East and the West. Two of his song compositions, “Jana Gana Mana” and “Amar Shonar Bangla” were chosen by India and Bangladesh respectively as their national anthems. Rabindranath Tagore passed away on August 7, 1941. About the Poem ﻿ Published in 1903, ‘The Braveheart’ translated from ‘Birpurush’ revolves around a little boy who paints the picture of his bravery where he accompanies his mother on a journey and saves her from dacoits. The fantasy of saving his mother and being applauded for it is the projection of the will of rising beyond being an ordinary child. Imagine, on a voyage far away With my mother off I go one day Mother, in a palanquin you ride The doors parted a little on the side I trot along on a bay horse so bright Clip clopping, not letting you out of sight The horse’s hooves disturb the muddied trail And raise a cloud of dust to hang beside Twilight comes, the sun sets itself low It seems we’ve reached the twin-ponded meadow Its desolate everywhere I see No one there, Ma, but you and me! Perhaps you are afraid in your mind “Where are we? How did we get here?” I say, “Look, there’s the river bank O Mother mine, no cause for you to fear!” See, the burrs lie thick upon the ground In the middle the path has turned around The cattle – none of them do roam As evening fell, all of them went home. Who knows where the two of us are going It’s hard to see as darkness brings the night Did you call to me as if to ask, Beside the lake – is that not a light?” And then with a blood-curdling roar Who was it that down upon us bore? Cowering in a corner of your seat You send prayers up with every heart-beat. Your bearers drop you, quaking with fear In thorny bushes they’re trying to hide Imagine I call to you and say, “Don’t be afraid, I’m still by your side.” With clubs in hand and shaggy mops of hair Behind each ear a red hibiscus they wear I roar at them “Just stop, don’t you dare One more step and of your fate beware!” “Can you see my unsheathed sword In moments I shall slice up each of you.” They jumped again in rage at my threat, Louder their angry bellows grew. “Can you see my unsheathed sword In moments I shall slice up each of you.” They jumped again in rage at my threat, Louder their angry bellows grew. “Don’t go farther,” you tell me in dread “Just be quiet and watch me,” I said. I gallop up to them and then I spring My shield and sword now loudly ring. What a royal battle did then rage You’d shiver if the tale of that be told So many ran away to save their lives So many heads in heather that day rolled! Perhaps your tender mother’s heart then thought “My son is dead, for so many he fought” Bathed in blood and sweat to you I come And say. “Oh mother, come, the fight is done” Out you jump from your palanquin, Give me kisses and hold me tight, And say, "How lucky that my son was here Or can you just imagine my plight! ” So many things happen to me and you, Oh, if only this could come true! Oh what a tale it would turn out to be Everyone who heard would wonder too! Dada would say "How could it happen? How strong is he, my little brother?” Neighbours, friends and everyone would say, “How lucky that he was with his mother!” **Dada: Elder brother.
author: Swagata Sen Pillai

title: What do I see?
text: I see? I watch the fishes! What do I see? I look at the river! What do I see? I look at the mountain! What do I see? I look at the plants! What do I see? I look at the flowers! What do I see? I watch the birds! What do I see? I look at the sky! What do I see? I look at the sun! What do I see? I saw so much beauty! I was mesmerized by the natural beauty!! Thanks!!

title: Dreams came true.
text: Hey, a girl named Suzane. She lived in a village. She was having a dream to" be an Author". She wanted to study in an English school first to became an author. but they were poor. As her father has the job of a guard. And in her family, her grandmother, her father, and her brother, and Suzane herself only were there. They live happily together. Her grandmother doesn't know that Suzane has a dream to study and became an author. One day, her grandmother noticed that she was reading a book and having fun in it. she goes to Suzane and asked" Suzane, do you have the interest to read books?. Suzane says " Yes, grandmother. I have a dream to become an author but first, I need to learn English, then only I can be an author. Grandmother says "Hmm... Let's eat first food then let's talk about it, alright?". Suzane says" Ok, grandmother". Suzane's birthday was near. So, the grandmother thinks that let's give a surprise to Suzane. She talks about it with Suzane's brother. Suzane. So, they start collecting money for Suzane's birthday party. After a few days, her father gave a surprise by coming home because he does his job in the city and they live in the village. On the day of her birthday, she invited her friends and celebrate with them and her family also. Everyone start giving gifts to Suzane. In the morning her family gives surprise of going to the English school. She was very very happy and excited also. So, she gets ready quickly to go to her school. She was even happier when she gets to know that her brother is also coming with her at school and there is also a library. So, Suzane and her brother go to school with their father. When Suzane reach school she go to the library and start reading books. As well as his brother to. They were having fun in their new school. Then their class teacher introduce them to the class. But when they come to home they get to know that their father got a call and need to go. So, they all went outside the house they wave their father. Then they told everything what they had done in their school today. Ten, Suzane's dream came true as when she grow up she became a famous author and learn a fluent English also.

illustrator: ASHIMA KHANNA; Catherine Groenewald; Parvathy Illustrations by Rakshita

title: The Golden Boat
text: Author Rabindranath Tagore was born on 7 May, 1861 to Maharshi Debendranath Tagore, one of the leaders of the Brahmo Samaj, and Sarada Devi. He was a distinguished Bengali poet, writer, painter, playwright and composer of songs. He was homeschooled by a variety of teachers in a variety of subjects. He composed ‘Sishu’, ‘Dakghor’, ‘Birpurush’, ‘Proshno’, ‘Sahaj Path’ and others for children. He was the recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in the year 1913. In 1915, the prestigious ‘knighthood’ was awarded to him by the British Raj but he soon renounced it as a protest to the Jallianwalah Bagh massacre of 1919. A highly renowned artist, he was known for introducing the Indian culture to the West which led to his establishment of the ‘Vishwabharati’ University in Santiniketan which is a mosaic of the East and the West. Two of his song compositions, “Jana Gana Mana” and “Amar Shonar Bangla” were chosen by India and Bangladesh respectively as their national anthems. Rabindranath Tagore passed away on August 7, 1941. About the Poem Published in 1894, this poem goes beyond poems written for children by Tagore as it instills a philosophical aura which reflects the poet’s realisation about the ultimate meaning of human life. Allegorical in nature, this poem is a picturesque beauty which touches upon the question of humans unable to leave a stamp in the larger scheme of the cosmos. Thundering clouds in the sky, the rains pour down. By the riverside I sit, hopeless and alone. The harvest is gathered, Profuse and lush. Razor edged, harsh, the river swells to a flood. The rains come down As the paddy is cut. In my little field Lone am I, Frolicking and capering, The river meanders by. A canvas across yon I see the shadow stains of trees, A village overcast at daybreak, a sun playing hide and seek. Lone am I In a little field On this side. Singing a song, rowing a boat, Who comes ashore? I look - Is it someone I know? The billowing sails Carry the boat away Naught a glance cast Come what may. Waves part And break, helplessly so I look - It’s someone I know. Where do you go? To which foreign shore? Stop awhile Bring your boat to moor. Go where you long Gift whom you please – But take away with a smile My golden harvest, Just stop awhile. Fill your vessel Take all you can load. — Is there more? — None, it’s all aboard. Years by the river, I have been immersed Today I gave it all. Gifted, disbursed. Now take me too, have pity, take me aboard. There is no space, No space at all The boat, it is too small. My golden grains Have filled it all. The monsoon sky is laden With rain-filled clouds, I remain alone by the riverside, empty and forlorn The golden boat has taken it all. All I had is gone.
author: Tilottama Shome

title: Radha dared to go home alone
text: Once there lived a girl named Radha. She lived with her mother, father and brother. She was only four years old. Every day, she saw Rohan going to school in the morning. She also wanted to go along with her brother. But, how? She was only 4 years old! She waited for days to months and months to year. After waiting for a long Two years, she was now ready for going to school. She was overjoyed with happiness. One fine day, she started going to school with her brother. She liked her school, teachers and friends. When she came back from school, she asked her mother "Ma can I live in the school"? Ma started to laugh and said, "no dear, school is a place where you go for studying and learn new new things, you can't live there like home". She was eagerly waiting for the next day. When Radha was getting ready for the school next day, her mother told her that she had some urgent work at office and she would not be able to pick Radha up after school. She instructed Radha to come with Rohan. Radha agreed. When the school was over, Radha waited for Rohan near the gate. But, Rohan didn't come. Radha was sweating with fear and she thought that Rohan had gone to home without picking her. She started to cry. Luckily, after sometime she realized that she had been told to stand at the bus stop. But she was standing inside the school compound. Radha ran and ran and she reached the bus stop to see whether Rohan is waiting for her or not. There was no one! Radha thought and decided "I know the way to home and I will go myself". She started to walk. After walking for around 20 minutes, she stopped near a big banyan tree. Her leg was paining hardly. She couldn't walk ahead with her paining leg. She thought of sitting somewhere. She felt very thirsty and looked in to her bag for some water. But the bottle was empty. She look around and saw a small shop. She went there and asked the shopkeeper for some water. The shopkeeper was a kind man and he gave her a glass of fresh water. Radha said "Uncle, I don't have money to pay for the water". The man replied, "no need child, have it". She thanked the shopkeeper and started to walk for home with some more energy. At home, her mother was very angry with Rohan who forgot to pick Radha from school. She was worried that where Radha was and how she will reach back home. She decided to go to the school. But, she couldn't see any sign of Radha in the school. She started to cry fearing to loose her child. But, Radha walked and walked and some how managed to reach home. Radha told Rohan about how she walked to home alone. Immediately Rohan telephoned her mother and informed that Radha had reached the home safely. Radha's mother was very happy and proud of her daughter because she walked all 3 km and reached the home without any one's help. Radha got a kiss form her mother and a special dinner that night.

title: The Day Vedanth Thought He Tore The Sky!!
text: Read along to find out what happens when a little boy is fed up of the sun's heat and sets out to seek revenge. Instead, he ends up worried that he may have unintentionally torn the sky!! One fine summer day, when the sun was burning up, there was a little boy, named Vedanth, who had been feeling very annoyed with prickly heat boils on his body. He was furious with the blazing sun because its heat made him sweat terribly and gave him itchy spots that made him so uncomfortable. Today, Vedanth was feeling absolutely fed up with these wicked heat boils!! Vedanth decided that today was going to be payback time for the sun! He thought of his newly acquired bow and arrow set and planned to prick the sun with an arrow so that it may feel discomfort and itchiness too! Perhaps, once the sun had experienced the discomfort for its own, it would stop making little kids like Vedanth itch with heat spots!! He ran to the toy room to bring his weapon out. On the way out, Vedanth, who was essentially a sweet and caring boy, remembered that his parents and teachers always inspired him to be kind and considerate to all beings. So, he decided to also pick up the jar of talcum powder that his mother used to calm his heat spots. He thought of sprinkling it over the second arrow so that the itch caused by the first one’s prick, could be eased. After all, Vedanth did not want to hurt the sun! He only wanted it to realize the discomfort that itchy sores cause. Surely, Vedanth was not naughty like the fiery summer sun!! He only wanted to teach it a lesson so that it stops breathing fire and making everyone feel so hot, sweaty, and itchy!! The sun too needed to be taught a lesson in kindness, thought Vedanth. Armed with all the things he needed, Vedanth ventured out on his mission. Finding a perfect spot, he aimed his bow and arrow towards the sun. He pulled at the bowstring and let the arrow go skywards. Moments later, he released the second arrow, after having generously sprinkled talcum powder over it. Finally, the sun will get a taste of it's own medicine and will stop making everyone and everything so hot, thought Vedanth. As soon as he had shot the two arrows, the sky turned an angry black colour and there was roaring thunder. Suddenly, there was a downpour of water droplets from the sky. Vedanth was shocked! He was worried that his arrows had burst the sky and caused the downpour. He ran to his mother to confess how he had torn the sky. Nervously, he explained to her, his reason for wanting to prick the sun. He added, with pure innocence, that he had not meant to hurt the sun or the sky and had in fact, shot a second arrow with talcum powder to soothe the itchiness caused by his first arrow. Vedanth was preparing for his mother to thunder down upon him like the roaring sky!! Unexpectedly, his mother hugged him tightly!! She assured him that the rain was not his fault. She explained that rainfall is a natural process that takes place due to evaporation by the sun’s heat. Vedanth felt comforted to know that he had not torn the sky and was delighted that the sun was indeed apologetic about the excessive heat and had therefore made it rain through evaporation. For Vedanth, the pleasant rain shower was the sun’s way to make up for his mischief!! Vedanth went out merrily to dance and play in the refreshing rain to celebrate the day that he thought he had torn the sky!! About the Author 'The Day Vedanth Tore The Sky' is written by Vedanth Kumar, an imaginative 7-year-old boy from New Delhi. Apart from writing, Vedanth also enjoys reading story books and poetry. His favourite authors include Roald Dahl, A.A Milne, Ruskin Bond and various others. He does not consider himself a bookworm, but never goes to bed without reading a story!! Like any 7-year old, Vedanth enjoys the regular features of childhood – playing with his friends, watching TV, gorging on cheese pizzas, defeating his opponents in board games, and racing his many toy cars over any possible surface!! Dedications This book is a birthday gift for my lovely Maasi (aunt) and my fabulous Nanaaji (grandfather). Happy Birthday to both of them!! I dedicate this book to my loving Parents; my wonderful Thatha (grandfather) and Paati (grandmother); my most beautiful Naani (grandmother); my awesome Arpan (uncle); my coolest Atthai (aunt) and incredible Fufu (uncle); my dearest Dhruv, Harini, Harshini, Tia, Navya, Maadhaaav, Rishabh, Ishu; my most inspiring teachers - Sahiba Ma'am (class 2-Cuckoos), Geeta Ma'am (class 3-English), Divya Ma'am (class 3-EVS), Sangeeta Ma'am (class 3-Math), Harshita Ma'am (class 3-Hindi), Neha Ma'am (class 3-Music). I am also grateful to Chanda aunty and Sonu didi for looking after my house and me!!

title: Madhu tells, Don't Want
text: Little Madhu said, "Don't want, Don't want" to whatever people tell her or give her. If her mom called her to have food she said, "Don't want, Don't want." If her father gave her a fruit she said,"Don't want, Don't want." Madhu said,"I don't want these vegetables. I don't want this tiffin. This dress is not nice. I don't want." "Do I have to go there? Don't want, Don't want. I don't want that doll." Like this, Madhu always said, "Don't want. Don't want." Because of this, her mother and father worried a lot. One day, suddenly, Madhu stopped telling don't want, don't want. Her mother noticed the change in her and asked the reason. The reason Madhu gave shocked everyone. "On Saturday, when we went out, a little girl asked for money. When I was about to give her the money, you told, "Don't want. Don't want. Don't give." That girl cried and went as she could not buy anything for her to eat. When you told,"Don't want. Don't want that day, I got angry. I realised you will also feel angry when I always say, "Don't want. " Madhu asked, "Mom. Why didn't you give money to the little girl that day? Isn't she a poor thing?" Madhu's mother kissed her and placed her on her lap. Then she explained to Madhu. "Madhu. Do you know why father says don't go if a stranger calls? Don't take what strangers give? Some people kidnap small kids like this and make them beg on the streets. If we give money when the kids beg, the kidnappers will take many more small children with them. That is why I said, don't want, don't want." Madhu asked, "Then how can we help such kids?" Her mom said, "You can help them. But, you have to make sure it does not end in danger for them or the other kids." Madhu told her mom, "After I become a big girl, I will also help as much as I can." Saying so, she hugged her mother. Like this, Madhu stopped saying, "Don't want. Don't want."
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Brown
text: ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ Once there lived a dark skinned girl named Anna.She was 4 years old. She loved colours. She used to spent her day painting and drawing colourful pictures. The teacher came in and made Anna to sit alone because all the children in the class didn’t want to sit with her. But Anna didn’t cry, she was a brave girl. She ate some cake and went to play. The next day Anna went to school and sat on her bench alone. Now it was their lunch break. Anna has brought some chocolate cake. All the children in the class came towards Anna. The children wanted to taste the cake Anna has brought. She gave all the children small pieces of cake. All the children enjoyed the chocolate cake. She asked her mother "Mother, all the people like the dark brown colour chocolate, cakes, biscuits,and all other food items which are brown in colour. But why doesn't they like people with dark skin. The next day Anna asked the same question to her teacher. The teacher was surprised by the little girl's thinking. All the children were also wondering about this now.
