title: The Selfish Wolf
text: This was the month of March. The spring was coming and the farmers were busy harvesting their crops. A farmer was going to sell his crop in the market that he had harvested recently. On the way to market one of his bull run away from his bullock-cart in the deep jungle nearby. In the jungle there was a lion king living with two wolves. The first wolf named Titan was very silent and polite but the second wolf named Sparta was clever and selfish. Sparta wanted to be the king of the forest. So he had an idea! He thought that he would tell the bull that the lion is thinking to kill you. On the other hand he told Titan to tell lion that the bull wants to kill you. And the next day the Lion and The bull had a fight in which both killed each other. As the lion got killed in the fight Sparta was thinking he has become the king of the forest. But when Titan came to know that Sparta had used him in the killing of the lion. He was very angry. And he thought he would not allow Sparta to become the king of the jungle. So Titan told Sparta that he also wanted to become king of the jungle. This annoyed Sparta and both the wolves fought terribly and killed each other.
author: Hardik Chaudhary
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Gauri Kathula; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Journey From A Novice To A Veteran Archer
text: Chapter 1: The Beginning The story starts in a small cottage with a poor boy, named Jon, actually, Jon was not an ordinary boy and he had long hair too. In school, he was called a pitiful, fat loser, because of his effeminate habits and poor situations. As one day, he was walking down from school to his home, he thought if he could change his reputation. Just before he got home his mother was sobbing and he asked "Mother...", and just then his sister Lydia came and yelled "Oh brother, are you mad, can't you just look at her and discover what had happened?", Jon then too shouted, "Are you a termagant, you're always screaming and howling here and there." After a while, Jon tried to control his temper and poped the question, "What happened my mother dear?", his mother replied, "Oh, my son, what should I tell you, we are turning insolvent. We have no money left, your father is also foiled with his crops.". This moment, Jon was kept in a self-made seclusion. (May fate decide...) Chapter 2: The Ultimate Opinion and View As a non-fatalist, Jon was on his reasoning, he didn't believe in bin fate. As he was on his way to the market, he mused, "What can I do so that I can gain a living, switch my effeminate reputation and take the place of a real, consonant man?". Next off, he saw a man making fat, hard money by shooting bullseyes with bow and arrow. He got the clue of becoming an archer, he kept a word of honour to give his blood and sweat to become a legend, he told the troth to his mother and went to the market to find his equipment and tools. (Look what did he find in the next chapter.) Chapter 3: Vow To Become When Jon found a bow and arrow, he went home to practise. He developed and indefatigable attitude towards archery, as days passed, now he wanted to aim real things so he bought fruits and vegetables. First of all, he tried to aim the watermelon. When the arrow dragged towards the target, the watermelon and all eatables came alive and said: "You are a loser aren't you, and you're trying to aim at us? Ha Ha Ha...". When they were trying to make fun of him, he raged with anger and set his aim. He showed up his arrow and shot it in the sky, vowing "I take the pledge that, I may become history's greatest archer & be the cynosure for every eye. I will destroy all sadists and evildoer, and always stake my life to save the world and humanity, I may always stop the world from going into wrong and deadly hands." (What would happen next?") Chapter 4: Writing a Saga Just when the arrow reached the sky, a lightning thunder flashed through his eyes, Jon was literally amazed! An unknown, mysterious voice came "You may come to me and I will train you.", and just before him a pair of stairs appeared. When he climbed up the stairs, a holy God came to him. He taught Jon for years and years, until one day, Jon returned as an invincible, invulnerable warrior, though he was an almighty, he didn't boast of his power instead he became an ascetic, altruistic samaritan to help mankind. Later, Jon became the only rescuer and protector of the people, he gained the respect of a versatile hero of all time. However, we all know that a moment of happiness doesn't last forever, and a disaster occurred. A demon wanted to put an end to earth and humankind. When Jon went to convince him, he threw him out and refused. So Jon was forced to battle and the battle took months to end but at the last Jon was stabbed with a knife. After the battle ended, the demon gave up but a tragedy also had taken place. Just after the terrible battle, the mayor of the city made a statue of Jon with his bow in his memorial, appreciating him as a veteran archer and martyr for all. - Anant Deep Agrawal THE MORAL OF THE STORY The starting point of all achievements is "DESIRE" The stronger the desire, The greater, happy the motivation, The stronger the motivation, the greater the achievement. If You want to achieve something in your life and you desire for that then you can achieve it through hard work and dedication. The next time you're feeling scared or depressed always think of Jon, from him you can always learn about a burning vow and desire.
author: Anant Deep Agrawal
illustrator: Greystroke; Mohit Suneja; Nan Hom Noon; Suvidha  Mistry; Wiehan de Jager

title: We can be together again
text: Jager It was spring in most parts of Europe. The weather was fine, it was warm and sunny and every day after school, the children would go to the park to play with their friends. Life was wonderful, as it should be for any child in the world. One evening everything changed. They announced on TV that everybody had to stay at home starting the next day and nobody was allowed to go outside unless they had to buy food or go to the doctor. And all this because of an invisible enemy, a virus. Some children were sad that they couldn't see their teachers and friends anymore.......others were really happy to play their favourite computer games and sleep as long as they wanted... Many had the chance to be together all day long after a long time and they made the most of their time spent as a family. Days passed, weeks passed, and the children started missing their days at school, some even longed for the homework they used to get every day. Everybody missed school, even the parents who had to find ways to keep their children busy in the house. One day, everybody had the biggest surprise: the first class in weeks...only it was online. All the children were thrilled to see their friends and teachers again, even on the screen. They felt like hugging, kissing and shaking hands, but the screen wouldn't make it possible. The teacher always advised the pupils how to stay safe and healthy and she offered any support she could to those who needed it....But nothing could replace the days at school... Many children drew rainbows and displayed them in the windows of their homes to keep their hopes up. Finally, the doctors found a solution to defeat the enemy! Everybody learned how to protect themselves and life made sense again, even if in a very different way. It was hard, but people could be together again, and children happy to go back to school. When there is will, there is a way!
author: Magda Cojocaru
illustrator: Akshara Datla; Anitha A.S; AYUSHMAN SAHU; Delwyn Remedios; Huynh Thi  Kim Lien; Narendra Dengle; Niloufer Wadia; Rijuta Ghate; Shamim Ahmed; Shanta  Hitang; Shreya Shruti; Sinomonde Ngwane; Swastik Mukherjee; Vusi  Malindi; Wiehan de Jager

title: THE SEEDS OF SUCCESS
text: Once upon a time, in a village, lived a boy named Mohan he was 5 years old, he lived with his mother and father he also had 2 brothers and 2 sisters. He was born in a poor family. His father was a postman. In his neighborhood, lived a boy Sohan, who was also of 5 years and he too lived with his mother and father and had 1 brother and 2 sisters. He was also born in a poor family. All the children liked playing together.. but Sohan and Mohan were best friends! They both went to the school together, played together, and even shared their secrets with each other. One day, they thought that they should plant saplings, so that they grow in some years and become trees then give fruits., vegetables and then they sell them to earn money. So they decided to collect seeds of whatever they ate. But keep it as a secret between them. After a few months they had collected many seeds and then thought that they should plant them now in the forest which is near the outskirts of the village as it was very close to their house. After a few years when Mohan and Sohan had grown up. They saw that the trees that they had planted had grown very nicely and then they took the fruits and sold them in the market. They had earned a lot of money in a few years which could last them a life time. They stored all their money in a ''gullak'' (piggybank) and were wondering about how will they tell all this to their parents now. A few more weeks passed away.. but suddenly one day.. A few months passed away..... But suddenly on day, Mohan's mother found the ''gullak'' which Mohan had hidden. She was shocked to see so much money in it.. She thought.. '' From where did all this money come from??.. should I ask Mohan's father about it.? But I don't think all this money is his.. Has Mohan started to STEAL?? I should confirm before reacting.." After a few minutes- When she asked Mohan's father about it.. He said even he did'nt know.. When Mohan came back home with more money..He saw that his mother had found all the money so he had to tell everything to his family he told what he and Sohan had done.. His family was shocked to know that their son has earned all this money!! His family was very happy and proud of Mohan.. After a few minutes they went to Sohan's house and told her mother all about their work what they had did as a team. Sohan's mother was also very shocked and could not believe all this.. Sohan's mother loved to make pickles, she made very tasty pickles but she could not make. due to the shortage of money in their house. So after so many years she again made the tasty pickles and everyone liked them very much. Then she decided to make pickles and sell. In a few months, her pickles got famous everywhere and soon they started a company. Whereas Mohan's mother had a passion of knitting so she started making winter clothes and sell them to earn money.. Soon, both the families had a lot of money. So they decided to use all that money wisely and to let their next generation lead a better life. After that day, both the families lived happily ever after. MORAL- One should always plan for the future and work hard also. PLANNING FROM BEFORE FOR FUTURE HELPS IN ACHIEVING BIG AWARDS AND LEAD A WAY TO SUCCESS.
author: Pragya Mishra

title: Fascinating journey of a caterpillar
text: One beautiful morning, after a rainy night, a little boy named Vihaan jumps in joy after spotting a tiny caterpillar on a leaf. He watches in wonder, the colorful caterpillar and its graceful crawling. Each morning, Vihaan runs to the garden to find the caterpillar eating the leaves of the bushy plant. He watches in awe, as the caterpillar eats the green crunchy leaves and slowly becomes bigger, fatter and rounder. Many days later, the caterpillar suddenly stops eating and finds a hidden, safe place. It hangs upside down from a leaf and starts shedding its skin. Then within minutes it magically spins itself into a 'pupa'. Vihaan's eyes are amazed to see the pupa form a hardened protective case around itself. What happens inside is a mystery! Vihaan kept watching and waiting patiently for many days but nothing changed... And then, one fine morning, to his wonder the case around the pupa splits open and the butterfly emerges." Wow" he exclaims. The wings are still wet and soft. In a few hours the wings become dry and strong. The beautiful butterfly then takes off to the air in search of flowers. Vihaan waves goodbye asking the butterfly to come back to his garden to lay eggs.
author: Rashmi Gopal

title: Clara's house
text: On a sunny hot day Clara the goat saw some people building a house! "I want a house of my own, Which will look even better than this!" said Clara and she decided to create a house for herself. Peek a boo! Clara was looking for some leaves in the forest! She knew exactly what she was doing! She was already tired! but she did not give up, and she managed to get some leaves. All the leaves which Clara collected kept on flying away, so she thought up a really clever idea! DIG! Clara started digging in the ground and stored her leaves there until she started building. splish, splash! "Look! there are leaves in the lake!" said Clara. Now Clara got very tired! She gathered all her leaves and now its time to build! The wind was fast! fast enough to break Clara's house! but Clara managed to save her house and continued building. Yay! Clara's house is ready! even better than the one she saw!
author: Avni Malik

title: Always save water
text: Lakshita was a wise teacher, who lived in South Africa. She loved nature much and lived amongst tree,flower, mountains, birds and animals.She was very calm. Many people used to come to learn from her. She always taught everyone to respect nature and save environment by giving simple examples from daily life. one of her student was a young girl, Neha. She used to respect and follow her teacher. Lakshita was getting ready for bath. She found the water in bucket too hot. She called her student Neha and told her to get some cold water. Neha got cold water in a bucket and began pouring it in bucket of hot water. Lakshita said, "That's better." Some cold water left in the bucket. Neha threw it away. Lakshita saw this and got very upset. Neha was surprised to see her teacher losing temper. Lakshita said, "Why didn't you use this water for plants or animals?" Neha was quit. Lakshita said, if we keep wasting water, we will have no water. Without water,not only us,but plants and animals too will die. You could have used this water for watering plants, bathing animals or for drinking." Neha understand the lesson about saving water. She said 'sorry' to her teacher and promised to use all resources wisely.
author: Akshita Singh

title: The little goat
text: One day, there was a little goat that lived in a bushy habitat. "Hi little goat" I said. " Halo" the little goat said. The little goat said, "Oh, I am so hungry." Then the little goat ate the grass. "Wow, this is fabulous!" the little goat said. "Nyom, nyom, nyom." Nyom! Nyom! Nyom! The little goat was looking for new venture. Firstly, he saw a bird. " Hi bird!" said the little goat. Then it went away as he wished to meet something else. Then the little goat saw a rhinoceros. " Hi Rhinoceros!" said the little goat. Then it went away politely and tried looking for something else. And then it met something. it was beautiful, it was friendly, And guess what he met was what he had been searching for. He met his mother! They had been separated since he was a child as there was a tiger. The little goat's mother protected it but they had not been together after that. And the little goat's mother stared at her princess. But a herd of elephants went between them, the elephants pushed the little goat away. His mother yelled for his name and tried to save him but it did not succeed. The night came. The mother goat was worried that it would not see its princess again. First the little goat was afraid but it knew everything was going to be fine and it would tried again the next day. The mother goat called its princess wishfully it would return. Then she saw her princess and the little goat saw its mother too. The went to be together soonest possible. " Oh, you are my gorgeous princess!" said the mother goat. Then they went home and promised not to leave each other again. Then there was a happy ending.
author: Eng Hock Tan

title: Drake a miraculous dragon
text: Drake was having sunbath under the sunshine while drinking the mango juice. If you had seen him, definitely you would have thought that he did not have the intention to win in the competition. But do you know? He wanted to win the competition earnestly. The only thing was that, he a bit... a bit lazy. Drake decided to go. Along the journey, he practiced spitting golden yellowish fire. But the results were only ashes. Aduh! " This is not good for a dragon." definitely the mother dragon will say. Pitiful, Drake started to cry. What could he do to make his mother feel proud? Out of the blue, Drake met his trainer - monster chili. The Monster chili asked him to eat RED chili. The chilis worked magically. He trained and trained and then...he was successful in spitting the gold yellowish fire....With his new strength and the lighting from his fire, Drake was able to provide guidance to the vessels on the sea. From the day onwards, no ship was reported missing. And that made mother dragon extremely proud.

title: Willy's World
text: Willy is a child like any other: he does tantrums, he hates vegetables, but he can win you over with his contagious smile. He's just an ordinary boy, but with a little difference: he's deaf. He can hear some sounds, but he can't grasp an entire word. So he uses the sign language to communicate with other people. Today is him first day of school and Willy is very frightened. He thinks that the new classmates won't accept his disability and that they will tease him. His grandmother tries to reassure him and suggests him to wear hearing aids which herself uses to hear better. After saying goodbye to the grandmother, Willy is ready to go to school. Willy arrives at school and his teacher, Mrs. Grey, greets him with a reassuring smile. Willy feels immediatly comforted. Mrs Grey knew that Willy is deaf, so she attended a course on the sign language in such a way to communicate with him. The teacher explains him that other children will greet him very well and that he can communicate with them in many others way. Before entering the classroom, Willy meets one of him classmates and they start talking. "Hi, I'm Rebecca, what's your name?" asks the girl. Willy can only grasp her name and tries to respond in the sign language. "Oh, I know the sign language!" Rebecca exclaims gesticulating. "My little sister is deaf too" Willy is very surprised... He has a new friend now! Rebecca and Willy enter into the classroom. Their classmates seem nice, but Willy hears some of them whisper and laugh at him. Rebecca intervenes to difend her new friend and say: "What's up? He knows a special, secret language that allow him to communicate with aliens and that you don't know!". Rebecca winks at Willy and he smiles at her back. While the teacher asks to the pupils to introduce themselves drawing something that other have to guess. It's the interval. Willy, Rebecca and other classmates are playing " You got it!" with a ball in the courtyard. The hearing aids allow Willy to hear the sound of the ball which bounces behind him and the screams and laughs of other children, so he can know where they are even when it's turned. Willy and Rebecca are sitting close at the canteen. They're very hungry and they are telling jokes to each other. Willy feels so happy. He couldn't imagine that his first day of school was so incredible! After the lunch break, Willy and Rebecca go out to the school playground. They meet the classmates that made fun of Willy. "Hi Willy and Rebecca... we're sorry for teasing you before. Can we become friends and play together?" they ask. "Sure! But you have to learn the aliens' language before!" They all burst out laughing. And that's Willy's story: a story that teaches us that diversity can be a wonderful opportunity to listen to the world with different hears!.
author: Roberta Sessa

title: Pavithra's Mystery Village
text: Everyone was scared of the ghost-like figure of the giant lizard and they ran away. But, the giant lizard was a very gentle animal. The giant lizard could not talk like other animals. So, other animals and humans found it difficult to understand the true nature of the giant lizard. Pavithra was a little girl who lived in the mystery village. Even though she was young, she was very loving and kind. She was never jealous, greedy, or angry. So, she was not afraid of anyone. Everyone appreciated and respected Pavithra. One day, in the village panchayat, they told that the giant lizard hunted other animals and ate them. So, their livelihood was affected. So, they decided to send the giant lizard out of the village. So, the giant lizard was sent to a faraway forest. The giant lizard felt very sad because people were not around. It did not like to live with other wild animals in the forest. But, the giant lizard could not do anything. The giant lizard never hunted the farm animals and ate them. One day, when Pavithra met the giant lizard she thought of all that happened. Nobody hunted the animals in that beautiful village. She realized there was a mystery. When Pavithra accidentally fell into a river, the giant lizard only saved her. Pavithra got scared when she looked at the giant lizard. But, the lizard was very kind and gave her tasty fruits to eat. At that time, Pavithra understood that the lizard was harmless. Then Pavithra was not afraid and became friends with the giant lizard. She also found out that the lizard eats fruits and vegetables. She decided to somehow save the giant lizard. That same night, she went to the place where the farm animals lived. The farm owner went out of town and kept his friend's dog to guard his farm. The dog was friends with animals that are awake at night. So, it slept in peace. Suddenly, when the dog woke up, the cow near it was missing. The dog sadly went in search of the cow. The dog saw an owl. The owl said, "I saw a fox that came from the forest. The fox is very cunning. So, go fast and save your friend." The dog went quickly and saw the fox waiting for the cow. The dog was shocked. At the same time, Pavithra also heard what the owl told the dog. She took giant lizard with her for help and ran to the forest. The giant lizard immediately came to help. The fox was speaking cunningly with the cow and was trying to take it into the forest. At the right time, Pavithra and the giant lizard saved the cow. The cow was moved to see the friend lizard who helped it. The fox got scared of the giant lizard and ran away. After saving the cow, the dog slept peacefully. Pavithra made a vow that she will bring back her lizard friend, who helped at the right time, back to the village. When the farmer returned to the farm, the dog told him what had happened. The farmer told this to the village head. The village head could not believe the story and was stunned. He felt sad because they drove the giant lizard away from the village even when it did not do any harm. Pavithra told the truth to the villagers. The villagers scolded Pavithra for going alone in the night. Pavithra told, "It was a morning when you all decided that the giant lizard was dangerous, right? But the giant lizard helped me in the night. We can do good at any time of the day and all the times are right times." Pavithra said, "You all did not investigate properly and punished the giant lizard. The lizard which looks like a giant is good. The small fox is cunning. Elders were afraid of the lizard. Even though I'm young I understood the love of the lizard. So, we should not be deceived by looks. The village head has to take the right decision. Please bring back the giant lizard into the village." ﻿ The villagers understood their mistake and allowed the giant lizard to come back to the village. The giant lizard ate its favourite fruits and played near the river. Pavithra realised that if we do good it will bring victory.
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Palm Tree
text: Author Rabindranath Tagore was born on 7 May, 1861 to Maharshi Debendranath Tagore, one of the leaders of the Brahmo Samaj, and Sarada Devi. He was a distinguished Bengali poet, writer, painter, playwright and composer of songs. He was homeschooled by a variety of teachers in a variety of subjects. He composed ‘Sishu’, ‘Dakghor’, ‘Birpurush’, ‘Proshno’, ‘Sahaj Path’ and others for children. He was the recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in the year 1913. In 1915, the prestigious ‘knighthood’ was awarded to him by the British Raj but he soon renounced it as a protest to the Jallianwalah Bagh massacre of 1919. A highly renowned artist, he was known for introducing the Indian culture to the West which led to his establishment of the ‘Vishwabharati’ University in Santiniketan which is a mosaic of the East and the West. Two of his song compositions, “Jana Gana Mana” and “Amar Shonar Bangla” were chosen by India and Bangladesh respectively as their national anthems. Rabindranath Tagore passed away on August 7, 1941. About the poem ﻿ Published in 1922, this poem is a part of the collection Sishu Bholanath. The Palm Tree with the mind of its own wants to wander in the sky, leave the earth behind. This poem explores both the power of imagination and the yearning to return home. One legged palm tree Topping all trees Peep into the sky; It wants to fly Tearing black clouds Wonders how to get wings. On its round leaves On the top It spreads that wish; Imagines the leaves to be wings To fly Leaving behind its home. Swaying leaves Make noises daylong Imagine they are flying. Palm Tree imagines travelling in the sky Beyond the stars And imagines going somewhere. Then wind stops Leaves do not move The mind returns; It knows the soil is its mother And loves its corner On this earth.
author: Sanghamitra Ghosh

title: Pumpkin Crush
text: Author Sukumar Ray was born on the 30th of October in 1887 and went on to contribute a great deal of creativity and freshness to the genre of children’s literature. He was a celebrated writer and poet from Calcutta who was born to Upendrakishore Ray, a famous painter, illustrator, musician and a Bengali writer himself, and Bidhumukhi Devi. Sukumar Ray studied the art of photography, lithography and printing technology at the School of Photo-Engraving and Lithography in London and became the pioneer of the same in India. His illustrations, writing and unique sketches often found their way in Sandesh, a children’s magazine which was launched by his father in 1913. He opened up a refreshing genre of nonsense literature that combined a great sense of humour, absorbing wit and a sharp ability of observation that fascinated both children and adults alike. Some of the famous and quirky fictional characters he invented include Kumropotash, Huko Mukho Hangla, Pagla Dashu, Hijibijbij and so on. Abol Tabol is a popular collection of his rhymes and poems for children which first appeared in Sandesh but was later published as a book. Sukumar Ray passed away on the 10th of September in 1923, leaving behind his son, Satyajit Ray. About the poem Published as a part of Abol Tabol, Ray’s collection of nonsense verse, in 1923, translated from ‘Kumropotash’, ‘Pumpkin-Crush’ revolves around a creature whose physical attributes remain vague, except for its relationship with Pumpkin, kumro, in Bengali, as derived from the title. Viewed as a whimsical character that the narrator asks the reader to stay away from and practice equally whimsical regulations so as to not disturb the titular character. The poet warns that if one flouts these rules, he is not to be blamed! If Pumpkin-crush dances Let no one come to the stable where the horse prances Don’t you look right, left or back – please don’t be free Lift your four legs and swing from the mottled radish tree. If Pumpkin-crush weeps – Beware! Beware! don’t go to the roof to sleep! Under a blanket crouch low in the loft, In the tune of Raag Behag, sing praises, gentle and soft. If Pumpkin-crush smiles – One-legged by the kitchen you must stand all the while! You must speak Persian in harsh whispered tones Then fast three times, and stay on the grass, prone. If Pumpkin-crush runs – Quickly climb window frames, and you are done, Fill your pipe with red-hued water, to apply on your lips and cheek Take care though, skywards, that no one should peek. If Pumpkin-crush calls – Everyone must wear black and throng flower-potted halls Slap spinach and cream on your head and pose A rock-hard brick loofah does rub on your nose. I see these rules you are going to flout If Pumpkin-crush hears of it – well, then, watch out! See how my words turn out to be true Don’t blame me later, I am warning you!
author: Swagata Sen Pillai

title: The stork and the mongoose
text: This story is from an old Indian book called panchatantra written by Vishnu Sharma. The story goes like this. Once upon a time there was a stork family living on a neem tree. Under the tree there lived a foodie snake. It ate up all the stork eggs and babies. The storks were very sad. They were crying all day long. Sad really sad. ﻿ ﻿The stork named Baka went to a lake nearby in storky village. It was very thirsty. But the thought of teeny tiny ﻿ ﻿ ﻿baby storks made her eyes well up. ﻿ ﻿There was a crab watching the stork. The crab was cruel. His name was karkata. He acted kind and told the stork "why don't you take help from nakula the mongoose, it will get rid of the snake." ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿Nakula the mongoose went to the neem tree. They fought long and hard battle. And finally the snake was killed. The storks were happy for a while. Mongoose knew that storks had their nests on the tree. Whenever he got hungry it came to the neem tree and feasted upon the storks, their eggs and babies ﻿ ﻿Now all the storks became food for Nakula the mongoose one by one. And there was not a single stork left. Poor stork family. The cruel crab acting as a friend of Baka the stork misled it and the whole family was now dead. Sad. ﻿ ﻿Moral of the story ﻿ ﻿Do not trust people who have bad inside and are acting to be good outside. They are cruel. ﻿ ﻿
author: Bhargavi Vardhan

title: Catch the Moustache Thief
text: Author Sukumar Ray was born on the 30th of October in 1887 and went on to contribute a great deal of creativity and freshness to the genre of children’s literature. He was a celebrated writer and poet from Calcutta who was born to Upendrakishore Ray, a famous painter, illustrator, musician and a Bengali writer himself, and Bidhumukhi Devi. Sukumar Ray studied the art of photography, lithography and printing technology at the School of Photo-Engraving and Lithography in London and became the pioneer of the same in India. His illustrations, writing and unique sketches often found their way in Sandesh, a children’s magazine which was launched by his father in 1913. He opened up a refreshing genre of nonsense literature that combined a great sense of humour, absorbing wit and a sharp ability of observation that fascinated both children and adults alike. Some of the famous and quirky fictional characters he invented include Kumropotash, Huko Mukho Hangla, Pagla Dashu, Hijibijbij and so on. Abol Tabol is a popular collection of his rhymes and poems for children which first appeared in Sandesh but was later published as a book. Sukumar Ray passed away on the 10th of September in 1923, leaving behind his son, Satyajit Ray. About the poem Published as a part of Abol Tabol, Ray’s collection of nonsense verse, in 1923, translated from ‘Gonf Churi’, ‘Catch the Moustache Thief’ is a fun poem that revolves around the boss of a certain head office who throws a fit saying that his fat, shiny moustache is gone! Ray beautifully wraps the tenets of nonsense verse around unreasonable hierarchy in an organisation and the effects of the same through this poem. He also, under the disguise of humour, takes a dig at prevalent norms of masculinity as the protagonist goes on to equate his identity with the existence of his moustache. The big boss at the Head Office was mild, we would think, Who thought he was so mad and would raise such a stink? There he was, happy and fine, sitting on his chair A little dozy, a little cosy, when up he leapt like a hare! Oh shiver me! Oh catch me! His eyes big and round I’m a goner, oh woe me, he wept and howled. Some said, call the doc, some said, where’s the poolish? Some said, beware he bites, don’t do anything foolish. They ran helter skelter, huffing and puffing, When, ‘My mooch is stolen, catch that thief!’ sir started bawling. A stolen mooch? Impossible! Who has ever heard of it? The moustache is right there, hasn’t fallen one bit. That’s what they all said, showing him a mirror A mooch that is stolen, has happened, like, never! Hissing with rage, sir was a potato in hot oil, He sputtered, ‘Don’t believe you, you ugly, horrible boys. Dirty, tiny, scraggy, bushy, disgusting and bad, Such a mooch was last seen on Shyam Babu’s milkman. If you say this nasty moustache is mine I will fire you and also levy a very hefty fine.’ Choking in rage, sir dashed out in his books, One must never trust idiots and fools. The monkeys in my office are just the worst None can tell where they vanished—my fat, shiny whiskers. Oh how I wish I could grab their mooches and dance Shave their stupid heads with my razor and prance. These moustaches on you and me—can they ever be sold? Our mooches are ours forever and that’s how this story is told.
author: Sudeshna  Shome Ghosh

title: The flight to freedom
text: The Butterfly was freely roaming around in the garden. It was a very breezy day. She felt some heavy footsteps coming towards her. She fluttered a bit but soon before she realised it, she was caught in a net. She cried out loud" HELP,HELP!!" but her voice didn't reach any ear. The Fly catcher pushed the beautiful butterfly in the Big metal pot. She helplessly fluttered with many other colourful butterflies inside. Her little mind raced with 1000s ways to escape but all were in vain. She noticed the world looked so different from inside the metal pot. But she did not loose hope! She decided to find out why did the flycatcher trap all the butterflies. She soon found that he was collecting just not butterflies but many other insects like caterpillars, beetles, moths, wriggly worms etc and would churn them in a grinder to create a yucky paste and would consume it. Yuck! She sensed soon she would be grinded soon. She had find a way out of the jar before she gets caught in his grubby hands. She motivated other captured butterflies and shared that if all of them together created a big ball of butterflies, and banged the metal pot it will topple down and smash on the floor & the lid will open! She also warned them that they must fly super fast so that they do not get caught again. They all united together to action out the plan. The next morning when the flycatcher was looking out of the window to see if there were any more insects, he heard the smashing sound of the glass jar. Before he could react all the butterflies swiftly flew out of the window. The flycatcher was left dumbstruck.
author: Prisha Goyal

title: Chitter chatter!
text: Gollu is a boy. Everybody likes Gollu but there is only one problem........... Gollu talks too much! Oho! will you EVER stop chatting? Oh! now he is talking! whenever he starts, He can go on for hours & hours! all the people in his family get sick of his talks! But the family members are glad only for one thing................. title: How did the Fat king become thin?
text: He had a very thin dog. One day, they both went for a walk. The thin dog suddenly saw a bird. He ran after it. The fat king ran after the thin dog. They both ran for days. The king finally caught the dog. And, to his surprise, he was now thin!

title: A Snake in My Bathroom
text: Nitya walked down the stone passageway to the roomy bathroom at the far end of the bungalow. The old family home was surrounded by lush greenery and spread out in the way only old city bungalows did. The bathroom, as was customary, was located at the far end of the house, away from the residential rooms. She unlatched the door and pushed it open, only to freeze. There, on the cold tile floor, lay coiled a metre-long snake. Brown gleaming scales caught the faint light streaming in from the open window. Nitya gasped. Her heart began to thump in her chest as the snake slithered away from the door. The girl saw two beady black eyes as the snake darted out its forked tongue once, twice. It was huge; long with a sinuous body that took up a large portion of the bathroom. Nitya couldn’t help herself. She slammed the bathroom door shut and took off down the corridor, shouting for her father. He appeared, looking worried. “Nitya? What’s the matter? Why are you shouting?” “There’s a huge snake in the bathroom, Appa!” she gasped, her face all flushed. “It looked at me and I thought it was going to attack me!” “A snake?” Her father quickly made his way to the bathroom and slowly slid the door open. He was greeted by a low warning hiss; the snake was agitated from the ruckus and none too pleased at being disturbed once more. Nitya’s father picked up the clothes washing stick and advanced into the bathroom, keeping the door open behind him. Nitya lingered at a distance, watching fearfully. Her father poked the snake in its midsection, trying to persuade it to slither towards the open window. The snake, predictably, did not react well to this. It raised its head and, quick as thought, struck at the man. He leapt back, startled, and Nitya screamed. “Nitya! There is no need to scream; Appa is fine.” Her father joined her. “The snake was scared, that’s why it tried to bite me. But see, I didn’t get bitten.” “I hate it; it tried to kill you!” Nitya wailed. “Just kill it, Appa. Throw rocks at it.” Her father shook his head. “No, putta. That snake is scared. I’m much bigger than it is, and I had a stick. I should not have poked it. Perhaps, that’s why it tried to bite.” “But you could have died.” “No, no, putta. That isn’t a venomous snake. It’s a rat snake; we have had them around here often when I was a boy. Now that the rains are back, the snakes are back too.” He closed the door once more. “I’m going to call Mahesh anna (who was a snake rescuer known in the area). We must get it outside. Snakes don’t live in bathrooms, after all!” Nitya hung back as he walked off quickly towards the living room, where the telephone hung on its receiver. She inhaled deeply, and opened the bathroom door once more. Perhaps the snake was tired of reacting, or perhaps it thought the little girl seemed harmless, but it ignored the creaking door this time. It slithered in a small circle, its coils curling and stretching like an accordion. Nitya gazed at its shining scales, which were actually a mingled mix of shades of brown, not just a dull uniform colour. The snake’s eyes were like obsidian, and Nitya realised that they did not blink. The tongue forked out every few seconds as the snake tried to find its bearings. The large window from which it had arrived was clearly too high for it to reach. It must have fallen in, realised Nitya, feeling a sudden burst of pity for the agitated reptile. The snake coiled itself and then slowly stretched up, up, up towards the window, but could not reach it. It swayed there, trying to find a route to the cool soil and thick bushes that lay beyond. Nitya’s father reached out to Mahesh anna who was in the neighbourhood, and the snake rescuer reached their house within ten minutes. Her father led him to the bathroom. Nitya followed them but stopped at a distance from the bathroom, suddenly realising that Mahesh anna was about to pick up the snake. Mahesh anna produced a metal rod with a U-shaped hook attached at a right angle at the end and an opaque sack with a PVC pipe attached to it, which he held in his left hand. Advancing into the bathroom, he carefully maneuvered the rod towards the snake, and held its body still using the hook as the reptile thrashed and hissed. He picked the snake by its tail and then used the rod to handle its head, taking care to keep the snake away from his body. He let the snake enter the sack and tied it decisively. “What are you going to do with it? Are you going to kill it?” Nitya asked, feeling a mix of curiosity and worry. Mahesh anna smiled reassuringly. “No, no, I am not going to kill it. I will release it outside your house in an abandoned plot or a field.” Nitya was surprised by his response. “But won’t it come back? What if it bites other people?” “It may or may not come back,” replied Mahesh anna. “But you don’t have to worry. Just leave it where it is and wait until it moves away, or call a snake rescuer. Rat snakes are harmless. They even control pests, like mice. If they did not live near our homes, the mice would have eaten all our rice. See how important snakes are? Also if you remove harmless rat snakes from here, this place could be occupied by local venomous snakes, such as cobras or vipers.” Our little Nitya was astonished to hear this. She felt a new respect for snakes. She shuddered at the thought of mice eating all the rice. How could she eat curd rice then? She decided to hope that the rat snake found a nice home soon, where it would eat the mice but stay out of her home. The little girl and her father thanked Mahesh anna as he took the snake away. Nitya sighed in relief once the snake was outside. She couldn’t wait to rush to the snake-free bathroom!
author: Priya Ranganathan, Dincy Mariyam

title: Come on Champ !
text: Do you like swimming? The thoughts of wading in cool water during the hot summer months makes a lot of us sigh in relief. Arav was one such boy - he hated summers and loved to swim. He had been training everyday in a big pool with his coach for the regional swimming competition. With his hard work and dedication, he had been able to build a brilliant speed and strong stamina. He also made sure his diet was healthy and ensured he slept well. His father had taught him swimming since he was 4 years old. The first time he looked at a swimming pool, he fell in love with the deep blue water and the mosaic on the floor. He would love to play dead man and do doggy poodle every day. While his friends would stay at home, he would ask him mother to take him to the pool even in afternoon. Every family beach vacation was a perfect excuse for Arav to swim in the cool and deep blue ocean without any boundaries. Arav's parents would sometime worry about his focus on studies due to his love for swimming. Arav attended school and did barely what was needed to pass exams but spent every extra second on his swim lessons. His parents now hoped that the regional competition will be a great test for all of Arav's preparation for the last 6 years and he will hopefully qualify for the national training camp for children. Arav wanted the same and was very excited. Arav and his parents went for a holiday to his father's village and he was overjoyed to see a big canal where one could swim. One day while Arav was swimming in the canal, he heard cries of help. There was a girl drowning in the canal. He quickly swam up to her and with the help of a fellow boatman, saved her. She was older than Arav and while saving her, his arm had a muscle tear. The local doctor told him that it will take at least a month for him to heal back to swim again. The regional swimming competition was only 2 weeks away. Arav was heartbroken. How will he ever heal to not just participate but beat his competition to ace the regionals. His parents were sad too but for them, Arav's well-being was more important. They told Arav that there will be another year to participate and he should instead focus on his health for the time being. Arav could not hear of it and could not sleep through the night while dealing with his anguish. Next day, the girl who he had saved, came to see Arav and got a bunch of roses to thank him. Arav was not interested in meeting her but his mom met her. His mom asked the girl,"How did you fall in the canal, beta?". The girl told Arav's mother - "Aunty, I want to be a racing champion but my parents refused to let me participate in the competition and my father refused to take me to the village across the canal for the race. I was trying to swim and reach the competition" Arav heard the girl from his bed in the room next door. He was deeply moved. The girl, a sportsperson just like him, was crossing barriers to follow her passion. How could he let any roadblock stop him and realized there was no time to waste. He went to the other room and told the girl, "You are a champion already and I am sure you will win the next race!". He then told his mom, "Can we please return back home and get a physiotherapists's help to get me back to swimming?" ﻿Mom was delighted and they soon went back to the city and Arav's father met the best physiotherapist. The therapist told Arav, "It might be very tough to prepare for a swimming competition in 2 weeks - are you sure you can do it?". Arav said, "Yes Sir. I owe it to myself to give it my all to this effort. I might not win but I don't want any roadblock to bog me". The therapist was impressed and exercised daily with Arav. Soon Arav was feeling fit and all ready to compete. Arav told him mother to invite the girl he had rescued for the competition. The stage was set and the referee blew the whistle. Arav started cutting the water like a bullet out of a rifle but a sudden pain shot out of his arm and his head spun. He focused on the finish line and with his grit, he was able to come third. The judges praised him for his effort. After the prize ceremony, Arav went to the girl and handed his medal to her. "You inspired me to truly act like a champ".
author: Shweta Bajpai
illustrator: Aashna Sharma; Jemma Jose; Kavitha Mandana; Mugdha Kapri; Priya Kuriyan; Prom  Vichet; Reet Kaur Chhabra; Shirish  Ghatge; Thulisizwe  Mamba; Zoya Anjum

title: Appa is angry
text: ''Nandini!!'' called Appa. ''We're going to be late for Divya's wedding! Come quick.'' ''Coming, Appa! Give me one minute!'' Nandini was getting ready. She wondered what the wedding would be like. ''Amma!! Are you coming?'' asked Nandini. ''Don't worry my child. I am coming. I just need a moment to get ready. Get in the car with Appa. I will come in a minute or so. Ok?'' As soon as they arrived, they saw so many guests! There was Shiru chachi and Vijay chachoo, Mandan kaka and Mira kaki, and of course, Nandini's beloved cousin brother, Dhiru. Dhiru ran to Nandini's mom and shouted ''Vidya Kaki! Nanidini! So good to see you both again! But where Sanjeev kaka?'' Nandini's mom said, ''He is coming, Dhiru. Wait.'' ''While we wait for Kaka to come, why don't you unpack the sweet boxes?'' Said Amma ''Ok! Come on, Dhiru Let's go'' Dhiru and Nandini ran up to unpack the sweets and plate them. They entered the room. They felt like they entered mithai heaven. Of course, they couldn't resist. They started to dig in. Just then...''Nandini!'' Appa came. Nandini gasped. ''Nandini, you know better than to eat the mithai!'' ''Sorry, Appa'' ''It's ok, my little princess'' Then, all of them hugged, and fun at the wedding. The end

title: The Helpful Princess

title: A day on Ravi's farm
text: Ravi is a farmer. There is a barn in his farm. Ravi has a lot of farm animals. Kirti is a cow, she is white with balck spots. Kirti gives milk for the farm. Raju and Rani are rabbits. They are white and fluffy. Rinku and Champa are ducks. They swim around the pond with their chicks. Roopa is a chicken. Roopa gives Ravi eggs everyday. Ravi grows a lot of vegetables on his farm. Everyone on Ravi's farm are good friends. They all work hard on the farm.

title: Tell me the Next Word Game
text: Manju were playing games. Manju said, “Let us play a new game. I will tell a word. You have to then tell a word with the last letter of the word I told. If I tell fro g, you can say g rapes. If I say sal t, you can say t iger." Anju said, “Ok. I will start. My word is L aughter.” Manju said, “It ends with R. R obot is my word.” Anju said, “Robot ends with T. T elephone is my word.” Manju said,” It ends with E. E xercise!.” Anju said, “It also ends with E. E lephant!” Manju said, “It ends with T. Hmm, T alk!” Anju said, “K. I have two words in mind. Ok. K angaroo!” Manju said, “It ends with O. My word is O wl.” Anju said, “Owl ends with L. My word is L ove.” Manju said, “This is a nice game to recall words. I will tell my brother about this game.”

title: The kind man
text: Once there was a very bad man.His name was Ram.He never helped anyone.He always saved his money and never shared anything with anyone.Once when he was residing at a hotel for some time he took all the things from the room and bathroom like soap,brush, toothpaste, hand wash etc.And once when he visited a garden he took out 7-8 small plants.But his wife was very kind and caring.He also had a son. One day his wife became very ill.He did not have enough money for his wife's treatment so he became sad and sat down under a tree.When people got to know that his wife was ill they collected money and gave it to the doctor and the treatment started.After treatment his wife became well again.Ram realised his mistake and from then on he helped people and became very kind,polite and humble and lived happily ever after.
author: Rohit Sharma
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Alex  Zablon; Angie & Upesh

title: Chef Meena makes Vegetable Salad
text: Chef Meena wanted to make a low fat but a healthy snack for her kids. She decided to make a vegetable salad that has no oil but is full of vitamins and minerals. She opened her fridge and was thinking about which vegetable to pick. “Pop” jumped Cathy Carrot.“I am rich in Vitamin A and I’m good for eyesight,” said Cathy Carrot. So, Chef Meena pulled out two carrots from the fridge. As she was watching, she saw Trim Tomato rolling down towards her. Trim Tomato winked and said, “I am rich in Vitamin C and help to remove toxins from the body.” Chef Meena smiled and picked two tomatoes. Cushy Cabbage danced and plopped herself into the Chef’s hand. “I have lots of Vitamin B1 and help to produce energy from the nutrients. ” Otto Onion peeped out. Onion said, “I have folic acid. I help to generate good red blood cells and prevent anaemia. ” Brisk Broccoli laughed and said, “I have more proteins than other vegetables and help the body to grow and be healthy. ” Cozy Corn joined the fun and said, “I have a lot of magnesium and help in blood glucose control. ” Chef Meena took onions, cabbage, broccoli, and corn also from the fridge. Chef Meena cut and chopped all the vegetables. And added salt, pepper, coriander leaves, and lime juice and passed on the delicious salad to the kids. The kids enjoyed the wholesome and colourful vegetable salad.
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Antra Khurana; Ellen Heydenrych; Kabini  Amin; Narayan Prasad  Bohaju; Phan Thành  Đạt; Raymond Diby; Shriya Nulkar

title: I am a big boy now.
text: " Bunty, Have one bite beta. You haven't eaten anything. How are you going to grow?" said mother, running behind Bunty with a plate in hand. Bunty was bouncing his ball and hopping around. He was shaking his head from side to side, trying to avoid the food offered to him by his mother. Mother was fed up of running behind him all the time to feed him. She got angry and scolded him for not eating. She asked him to go to his room immediately. Seeing mother's angry face, Bunty started crying loudly, "Waaaaaah, I don't want to eat. Waaah...I don't want to grow up." Although upset with his behavior, mother hugged him lovingly to make him stop crying. Bunty slowly drifted off to sleep. That night, Bunty had a dream. He was walking alone in a beautiful garden. In his dream he saw a little brown and white puppy sniffing around. He asked, "Hey little puppy, what are you doing?" The puppy looked up and said,"Bhow...wow...I am searching for food" and continued sniffing around. "Searching for food? Why? Doesn't your mother feed you?" Bunty asked. "My mother does her work. This is my work. I have to do this so that I don't stay hungry." said the little puppy. Bunty was puzzled with the answer but he continued walking around the garden. Soon he saw a pond and in the pond was a yellow duckling. She was constantly dipping her beak into the water. "Hey little duckling, Why are you dipping your beak into the water again and again?" asked Bunty. "Quack Quack, Can't you see? I am searching for worms to eat." "Worms, you eat worms? Yuck!" "By the way, where is your mother?" asked Bunty. "I don't know" replied the duckling. "She left me a long time ago. I am hungry so I have to look out for my own food." Thinking about the puppy and the duckling's words, Bunty continued wandering in the garden. He came across a small bird under a huge tree. The small bird was pecking around. Curious about what the bird was doing, Bunty asked,"Hello birdie! What are you doing?" The small bird replied "Can't you see I am searching for food. I am very hungry. Please help me to find food." Bunty bent down to help the hungry bird to find food. But he could not find any. They searched and searched for a very long time. The hungry bird started crying, "Waah! I am hungry....I am hungry..I want seeds and grains and fooooooooooood. Waah!" Hearing the bird cry, Bunty also started feeling hungry and cried out loud." Waah...I am hungry too... I also want food. Mammaaaa" Suddenly he felt someone shaking him and saying, "Hush my little boy, don't cry. It's just a dream." Bunty opened his eyes and saw his mother. Mother said," I have already made masala cheese sandwich for you, isn't it your favorite? Now come on, get up and brush your teeth. I know you must be very hungry." Smelling the yummy cheese, Bunty quickly got up and brushed his teeth. He began wondering about his dream. "Animals really have to work hard for their food he thought" as he ran towards the dining table to eat his masala cheese sandwich. Mother was about to pick the sandwich to feed him, but Bunty stopped her. He looked at his mother and said, "Stop! Don't feed me. I am a big boy now Mamma, I will eat this myself." Mother was surprised to hear Bunty's words. She wondered what happened to her little boy overnight. She just smiled lovingly at her "Big boy".
author: Mamta Paigankar

title: HARE AND TORTOISE
text: Once upon a time, there lived a hare.He was very proud of himself. "I am so quick to react and so fast to run. None can match me,"he mocked at other animals of the jungle.One day,the hare was wandering outside his burrow. He saw a tortoise slowly tottering away. 'Hey there, lazy fellow! What a slow pace you have! And what's that load on your back?" asked the hare. "That's my shell. It protects me from danger," said the tortoise politely. "Hah, you can slowly only crawl on the ground. See how swift I am. Can you match your speed with me?" mocked the hare. The tortoise thought "we must teach him a lesson". The hare called all the animals and told "tomorrow I and Tortoise have race you all should come". The next day the race is going to start and the judge is the LION. The race started and the hare go half of the forest and the hare thought I think he must come to my place at afternoon hmm let me take a nap. Some minutes after the tortoise came to the hare's place and the hare was deep sleep and the tortoise gone to the end point and the hare wake up and ran very fast when he came to the end point the tortoise was getting medal. Than the hare and tortoise become friends.
author: MIRDHUL KUMAR
illustrator: André Kieswetter; Chathurika Jayasooriya; Padmanabh; Rob Owen; Subi Bosa

title: Advik's path to bravery
text: One day there was a boy, and his name was Advik. He lived in a village in India, the name of the village was Okia. His Father was the Leader of the village and he was very brave but sadly Advik was the opposite of brave. He was almost scared of everything! Sometimes even his own shadow could scare him actually not sometimes all the time.. He had a younger sister and mother which he loved dearly. And he was very happy with his life. One day his father had to go for a very dangerous battle. His father needed all the help he could get so fearful little Ryan had to come to the battle to because he needed to help. When the Village reached the battlefield Ryan could not even look he was too scared to, but his father said if you believe you can do it then you can do it and his father left for the battlefield. Advik did not know that his father's army was in great trouble so when Advik opened his eyes he saw what was happening he was so desperate to help that he ran there was a gun on the floor he picked it up and startled the enemies so that his village could easily kill them, but Advik didn't know what he had done! His father was very proud of him and so was his village. The village went back home and celebrated the defeat of their enemies! Little Advik didn't exactly know what he did but he knew he helped his village and for that he was happy. And from then on Advik wasn't scared of anything! THE END..
author: Sianna David
illustrator: Lily Banerjee; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Priyankar Gupta; Shadrach Munene; Suvidha Mistry; Vusi  Malindi

title: Make others Happy
text: Banu could not wait till her brother returned from play. She was not patient. She finished her share of adhirasam. Her brother came back home after playing. He went and washed his hands and feet. He was about to start eating his share of adhirasam. Immediately, Banu ran fastly towards her brother and stretched her hand in front and asked for adhirasam. Her brother said, "You already ate your share. I won't give it. Go." Banu was angry and walked with tears on her face towards her mother. Within a few moments, half of the adhirasams in Balu's hands went to Banu. Balu was advised to share and eat. Banu was overjoyed because she got some more adhirasam. She went to the balcony and started eating. A crow came fastly and gulped the adhirasam in Banu's hands. The crow flapped its wings and Banu was hurt by the wings and the nails of the crow. She started crying loudly. Hearing her cry, Balu and their mother ran and came. They saw Banu closing her face and crying. They helped Banu to calm down. They applied medicine to Banu's wounds. Then they shared the remaining adhirasams and the brother and sister ate happily. Like this, we have to make others happy and get happiness.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: MARLEY RECOGNISES MASHA'S BOND OF FRIENDSHIP
text: Once there lived a Butterfly, her name was Marley, she had beautiful pink wings, she didn't like to make friends with anyone. She just wanted to wander here and there. On the other side there lived a Butterfly, her name was Masha, she had beautiful violet wings, she had made many friends. But she was not able to make Friendship with Marley. Marley often refused the Friendship. Masha asked many time to be her friend. Masha was also very Kind and Helpful. One day Marley was sucking the nectar of an unknown flower, which was really dangerous, it was poisonous, without knowing this, Marley was sucking the nectar from that flower. Masha was passing through that way, she saw Marley sucking the necta r from that unknown flower. Masha understood that the flower was poisonous. So Masha suddenly went and warned Marley that it was a p oisonous flower. But Marley didn't stop sucking she thought that Masha was just making fun of her. After some time the poison entered into Marley's body, suddenly she fell down, but Masha catched her and took her to a nearby flower and placed her on a flower. After sometime Marley woke up and flew away even without THANKING MASHA FOR SAVING HER LIFE. One Day the BUTTERFLY COMMITTE introduced a Competition, That "Whoever Makes The Maximum Number of Friends Within 2 Days" will be awarded " MANY FLOWERS WITH SO MUCH NECTAR". Everyone was happy,but Marley was sad because she didn't have even one friend. Masha came to Marley and said " YOU CAN MAKE FRIENDS WITH MY FRIENDS". Masha said "OK I WILL MAKE FRIENDS WITH YOUR FRIENDS, BUT YOU SHOULD BREAK YOUR FRIENDSHIP WITH YOUR FRIENDS, WHO ARE NOW GOING TO BE MY FRIENDS" Masha said "OK". The Day Arrived everybody came along with their friends. The result was announced " THE WINNER WAS MARLEY" She had won with the MAXIMUM NUMBER OF FRIENDS. Everyone was shocked, Marley was awarded with the flowers. Masha asked Marley "That can you be my friend". Marley said " FIRST YOU SAVED MY LIFE FROM THAT POISONOUS FLOWER, THAT TIME I DIDN'T RECOG NISE YOUR FRIENDSHIP THE SECOND TIME YOU HELPED ME FOR THIS COMPETITION, NOW ONLY I WAS ABLE TO RECOGNISE YOUR FRIENDSHIP. THANKYOU SO MUCH MY DEAR FRIEND- LETS BE FRIENDS ". They both flew away happily, sharing the flower's nectar. IF YOU MAKE FRIENDS, YOU CAN GET MORE ADVICES AND HELP.
author: Shivani K
illustrator: Mahbubur  Rahman; San srei nou ch nou ch

title: I wish I could fly
text: I wish I was a mighty bird, living in my little nest, Singing many sweet songs was what I would do best. I would love to eat barley and rice, and make friends with birds that are nice. And all through the day, you know what I would do? I would fly around with my perfect wings - a zip, a zap and a zoom! I wish I was a brilliant colored butterfly. A green, a blue, a red in color, a dot, a stripe, a speckle in order. And when I will not be busy looking pretty, or looking for nectar in roses and lily, I will fly like a glider over the flower beds. Over the ponds and the green fronds, and up above all my friends! I wish I was a rainbow kite, Strong and light at the same time. Made of paper, glue and string, with a rectangular body, a ruffled tail and powerful wings. I would slowly lift off to shake hands with the clouds, and then fly whoosh and swoosh as I went about. When I grow up to be bright and intelligent, I wish I would be a pilot in a plane. Pilot Preeti - everyone would call me, and I will wear a shirt which will bear my name. ﻿I will sit in a cockpit and turn the buttons, push and pull the levers to run the engines. I will fly up and down and touch the sky, and bring people home and help them to fly!
author: Shweta Bajpai
illustrator: Iddi  Marumba; Lavanya Karthik; Measa Sovonnarea; Sabyasachi Hazra; Sheena Deviah

title: As You Like It
text: It always did its work actively. A cat noticed the rat and it planned to catch and eat the rat one day. One day, the cat saw the rat going out. It wanted to eat the rat and started chasing it. The rat was afraid and started running. The rat ran fast and escaped from the cat. The rat felt very sad and told what happened to its dog friend. The dog consoled the rat. But, the dog became angry towards the cat which ill-treated its rat friend. The dog wanted to punish the cat. One day, the dog waited for the cat to arrive. When the cat came, the dog chased the cat just as how the cat chased the rat. The cat realised its mistake and asked the dog to forgive it. The cat felt sad about what had happened because of the mistake it did. The cat thought that it should not harm anyone in the future. After knowing the good decision of the cat, the dog, and the rat accepted the cat as their friend. They all started to give and take and live happily.
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Sahil Shaikh; Vusi  Malindi

title: Bedtime Stories
text: One story was about, "talking frog". In another story, there was a king with a long beard. My momma sometimes tells about "flying elephants". In one story, can you believe? A fox and tiger were friends. And Tiger falls into a pit! How will the tiger come out of the pit? Then, a clever fox saves the tiger. This is a nice story of all the stories. And I fall asleep, listening to the story.
author: Neelima Dondapati

title: What....Where are the clocks?
text: It was the first day of summer holidays and Meena was super excited she called her friends they danced together the whole day,then rahuls baby brother asked Meena "Meena didi i was asking can you come to mine and Rahul bhaiyas house for a sleepover ". Meena thought and said " yes sure i can come as my mum said i could do anything with friends today but i better inform her".Everone was excited and the time had come.... Meenas mom handed Meena her night dress and she walked to Rahuls house, there she met all her other school friends she was extremely happy then Rahul suggested to watch a horror movie about clocks disappearing forever, Meena refused and hit her head on the pillow and closed her ears that she could not hear the movie.Everyone was enjoying the movie and getting scared to but they had each other. Then in Meenas dream something unusal somethng scary so creepy walking in her nerves happened it was so scary that she woke up and shouted which startled her friends Meena told her friends about her dream by hearing the dream the friends said " Meena it is the same thing we are watching on the tv. Meena went back to bed now she was relaxed and slept quietly..... who said the morning would be as amazing.... The mother of Rahul and Ram was back at the time they were busy watching the movie Meena was stillll calm and fine but still very scared. Back in the living room the children were very tired so they went to bed and ya there was something unusal which happened......................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... When everyone woke up they woke up with a splash of water on thier face not with thier alarm clocks Meena started looking about the house and saw that all the clocks disappeared and she called her mom and asked her if she has the clocks but she answered no. and the children hatched a plan to split up and ask the neighbours about thier clocks but the answer was no. They were wandering in the back yard then all of them heard a loud sound and it went MUNCH GOBBLE MUNCH MUNCH. they were all scared then Meena said " Guys i have a idea lets go talk to the monster hiding behind the bushes '- before she could complete Rahul poked in " how do you know its a monster Meena". Meena replied the same events happened in my dream and your movie remember. But forget that it is THE CLOCK MONSTER It is the monster which ate up all the clocks Meena continued and the monster chomped and chomped and then Meena went closer to the monster and said " dear monster we know how much you love clocks but us humans can have a lot of harm without them. please return the clocks to the whole world. The monster understood and gave the clocks to everyone... What a startling sleepover. Wow what a sleepover thanks for reading now go create your own story thats the end
author: Jiya G
illustrator: Alankrita Amaya; Imile  Wepener; Nicci  Nathanson; Partho Sengupta; Sheena Deviah; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Tanvi Bhat; Tarique Aziz

title: The Story of a Butterfly
text: I can't stay inside this darkroom anymore. Please. Save me. Please let me out." Mother: "Dear one, don't worry. I'm here only. Be a little patient." After a few days... Baby: "I can't be more patient than this. I myself will try." Mother: "Dear one, look how beautiful you look. Eat these green leaves." Baby: "Uvek! Not nice. I want to drink sweet honey just like you." Mother: "Dear one, for that, you have to grow up. Now, you eat these leaves." Mother: "Eat some more leaves. Then only you can become strong." Baby: "Chee! She keeps on asking me to eat, eat. Do I have to always listen to her? She drinks sweet honey from beautiful flowers. But, for me these bitter leaves. Aah..." Mother: "Dear one, have you not slept. It is time to sleep." Baby: "Go, mom. I will not sleep. Do I have to always do as you tell? You are happy. But, look at me." Mother: "Dear little one, you don't have to always listen to me. But, I will only tell things that are good for you. Keep that in mind. Baby: "Now, you go. I'm going to sleep. Don't advise." Baby: "I slept for a long time. Oh! Mummy, look at this. I have also changed into a butterfly just like you. Mother: "I'm very happy. You have become a beautiful butterfly now." Baby: "Thanks, mom. Because of you, I became a butterfly." Mother: "You have got strong wings because you underwent pain. Now, fly away and drink honey from the flowers."
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Brunda Anandarao; Hari Kumar Nair; Herminder Ohri; Kavita Singh Kale; Lavanya  Naidu; Sharmila Pal; Tanvi Bhat

title: Angry Akku
text: Akku was ANGRY! "Akku! Akku! Look at the pretty sunflowers!" said Appa, as they rode through a field. "Oh no! They’re TOO YELLOW! They’re making my eyes hurt!" said Akku. Akku! Akku! Look! Look at all the monkeys!" said Appa, pointing at the roof of their house. "oh no!" said Akku. Go AWAY! "Here, drink some buttermilk," said Appa. "It’ll cool you down." "NO!" said Akku. "I DON’T WANT ANY!" "Try a sip, at least?" "OKAY! FINE!" said Akku, and tried a sip. It wasn’t all that bad. She had another sip. And another. In no time, the glass was empty. "Would you like a vada?" asked Appa. "NO" said Akku. "Just one little bite?" "Okay, FINE!" said Akku, and took a bite. It was quite good. She took another bite. And another. In no time, the plate was empty. "Good girl," said Appa. "Now will you tell me why you’re so angry?" "NO!" said Akku. "Was it something I did?" "NO!" "Was it something Amma did?" "NO!" "Did something happened in school today?" "MAYBE!" "Oho." "Would you like to draw it?" asked Appa. "Here’s a nice sheet of paper and some crayons." "Okay, FINE!" said Akku. Akku drew a brick… "This is the BRICK that I tripped over this morning," said Akku. "You’re right. That is a brick!" said Appa. And Akku drew a boy… "This is Bikku, The BOY who laughed at me when I fell down!" said Akku. "You’re right," said Appa. "He shouldn’t have laughed at you." And Akku drew an idli… "This is my idli," said Akku. "It fell out of my lunch box when I tripped over the BRICK!" And Akku drew a crow… "This is the CROW that flew off with my idli," said Akku. "The crow must have been very hungry," said Appa. And Akku drew her teacher… "This is my teacher, Amala Miss," said Akku."She helped me up when I fell down. And then she hugged me." "That’s nice of her," said Appa. "And then she patted my back and said, you would be fine. I DON’T like to be hugged and patted. "Are you alright now?" I’m okay now." "That’s good." "See how well you draw, Akku?" said Appa. "You’re a real artist! Will you draw something for Amma too?" "Okay!" said Akku, and started drawing some more. "This is a little white mouse… and this is a boat…and this is a coconut tree…" "And this is a sunflower…and this is your cycle, Appa… and this is a dog…and this is a frog…" In no time, Akku had forgotten all about the BRICK that made her trip and fall. And about the BOY who laughed at her. And about the IDLI-CROW. And Akku even forgot about being ANGRY. 10 Things to Do If You Feel ANGRY like Akku: 1. Laugh loudly and jump around with your arms in the air! 2. Slowly – very, very slowly – breathe in, and breathe out! 3. Drink some water! Or buttermilk! 4. Eat a piece of fruit! Or a vada! 5. Tell a grown-up about how you’re feeling! 6. Write about how you’re feeling! 7. Draw it out! Paint it! 8. Play with a pile of clay! 9. Make up a song about your anger! Sing it aloud! 10. Do the happy dance!
author: Puja Sharma

title: sambar story
