title: Dolly learns to make friends
text: Dolly was a rude girl. She never cared for anyone's emotions. Dolly used to hurt people with her harsh comments. Because of her nature, Dolly hardly has any friends in the neighborhood and even in her class. One day a new girl joined her class. Her name was Cathie. When she entered, she asked Dolly, "Hello dear, May I sit with you?" "No, I do not like to sit with a stranger" Dolly replied. After a week, the teacher announced a singing competition. In that, Dolly sang very well. As Cathie was new, she could not sing properly. Dolly insulted Cathie, "How horrible singer you are!” Such incidents happened many times. Every time Cathie ignored Dolly. Cathie was a kindhearted, friendly, and talented girl. She believed in being nice to everyone. One Day, Dolly was going to school on her bicycle. She tripped and fell in a muddy puddle. Many of her friends passed by, but no one helped her. Everyone just laughed at her. As she fell on her back, she was not able to get up on her own. After some time, Cathie saw a group of kids making fun of Dolly. Immediately she said to them, " Instead of helping, you all are teasing her. Then what is the difference between you and her?" Then Cathie said to Dolly, "If you were nice to them, someone might have helped you." Cathie came forward to help and took her to the doctor. Dolly realized her mistake and promised to be nice to everyone. Now Cathie and Dolly are best friends.
author: Miss Story (A.G)

title: A narrow excape
text: Hello out th... WOW!You are so big!You must be a human!Ok whatever you are,hello out there!My name is Teeny the mouse and I live in a place underground called Magicoland where there are cats and mice only. Not even air is there! It’s magic! That is why this place is called Magicoland! We can survive without air. We can also survive without food. So we don’t have to go out in fear of the cats in search of food. Anyway, today I went out to get some D-E-L-I-C-I-O-U-S berries. As I crept out into the inaudible night,the trees rustled giving me goosebumps. As I pussyfooted to the berry bushes, I heard a disguised noise every 5 seconds. I felt scared. So, I darted towards a bush. Whoops, I thought as my foot steps echoed. Too late. The thing or cat(because that was what it looked like)charged at me, mouth opened. I sprinted back to my hole and slammed the door, panting. The next day, I heard my brother, Roger chuckling to himself. When I asked him why he was chuckling, he asked me if I had gone out in the night and seen a cat. I said yes. Then he told me the cat was actually a trick played by him. I glared at him. Then I started laughing. Then he started laughing. Then we laughed and laughed until we could laugh no more!
author: Yash Nadhavajhala
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Amy Uzzell; Aruna Keerthi Gamage

title: The Mynah's Egg
text: On a bright sunny day, Sona and her sister Ziya were sitting in the garden and talking. Ziya was 11months older than Sona and their parents told Sona to call her sister didi but Sona always called her by her name. Sona asked her parents" why should I call her didi? I am only 11 months younger than her", after that her father nor mother told Sona to call Ziya didi. And actually, Ziya didn't mind Sona calling her by her name. While they were talking, Sona pointed to the mango tree and said"look Ziya, a beautiful brown colour bird with her 2 pretty eggs on our tree with her nest!", Ziya looked and then said, "oh that is a Mynah and her eggs". Suddenly Sona asked, "can I take one of those eggs? because even if I took one, one will be left for her"." No Sona!" cried Ziya "how can you think of such things, the Mynah loves her chicks the way our mother loves us. If somebody asks her that 'you have two daughters right? so give me one of them because even if I take one, one child will be left for you.'Will she give one of us?", Ziya asked."Certainly not she loves us like her two eyes," cried Sona." So will you take one of those?", Ziya demanded. Sona didn't reply, she badly wanted one of those eggs so made a plan and waited for a chance. One week passed by. On a hot Sunday afternoon, after they had their lunch, their mother told them to go and sleep and she and their father went upstairs to sleep. Ziya and Sona went to their bedroom and laid down on their bed. After a while, Ziya was in the world of dreams. Sona was waiting for this chance, she went and checked her parents' room and saw that they too were asleep. After confirming that the coast was clear, she quickly darted to the garden without making any noise and waited for the Mynah to go away from the tree. After ten minutes or so, the bird flew away in search of food. Sona ran to the tree and quickly started climbing up. She was excellent at the gym in her school so she could climb like any monkey. She reached the nest, took one of those beautiful eggs, quickly climbed down, darted to her bedroom, hid the egg under her pillow and slept peacefully. Later in the evening, they went to play in their garden. Ziya heard the mother Mynah making a sound, just like crying and she was searching for something. Ziya looked at the nest and saw that one egg was...... missing!." Sonaaa", she cried, "did you take one of those eggs?".Sona hated to say lies so she said "Yes I took one, only one, what happened? ". "The mother bird is very unhappy about it and look she is crying, poor thing", said Ziya, who was a great animal lover." Sorry Ziya, I will bring back the egg now itself, it's under my pillow", said poor Sona." No use of that, birds don't accept an egg touched by a human being, you keep your dear egg!poor bird. Sona now onwards, please do you have been told to do", said Ziya. Sona felt guilty, ashamed and sad and from that day onwards she did as she had been told to do and respected and admired Ziya very much. And after that, she called Ziya didi. Moral of the story; "Do as you have been told to do by your elders. They have experienced the world more than you.
author: Eesha Bejoy

title: MY DEAR LOVELY TEACHER
text: I love my teacher she teaches us about what we wont to become A teacher is a person who guides students in gaining the knowledge and values in a society. My Favourite teacher is Mrs. Setha suranjalu. She teaches us science as a subject. She is fun-loving and spiritual person,She is very polite and friendly in nature. Mrs. Setha suranjalu used to teach us Mathematics. She was a very humble, kind and helpful person. She made learning maths fun which otherwise used to be a tough subject for me. Now maths is my favourite subject only because of her and her teaching methods. Thank you teacher for guiding us, inspire us and make us what we are today. Thank you for always pushing me to try my best. I’ll remember both the academic and life lessons that you have taught me. I wanted to let you know that I really enjoyed your class. Your class was fun and I learned a lot from you. I wish all of my teachers were more like you. Dear teacher… we are bidding you farewell but we our hearts will never say goodbye to the wonderful things you’ve taught us. Awesome teachers like you, rare to come by. It is impossible for us, to say goodbye.
author: Lenora Dsouza

title: My Sweet home
text: We love to read books. We share our food in school. We help each other to learn. We keep our kitchen neatly. Our Kitchen is very big. There is always a rush in the kitchen. We have a big office room. There are many chairs for the visitor. There is a computer in the corner. There are many books in our library. We all love to dream. Everyone sleeps on their bed. We clean our playground every day. We play kho-kho game in the playground. We really like to play. We all share everything. Everyone is very friendly to each other. We always go together everywhere. We help each other when any of us is in trouble. Everyone is very good here.
author: KANSEY TRUST

title: Princess found a frog friend
text: There was a princess called Princess Tiara. She lived with her mother, father, brother and sister in a palace in Kenya. One day Princess Tiara was going for a safari in a jeep with her brother and sister to see the wild animals in the grasslands. She was feeling excited and a little nervous because she was worried that the lion might try to attack the jeep. So she sat in the middle between her brother and sister. Suddenly they had an accident because the jeep banged and crashed into the lion. The lion pounced on top of the jeep. The princess panicked and started to cry. She had got hurt on her head and it was hurting and blood was gushing out. The brother and sister were not hurt so they tried to help the princess by putting bandage and some medicines that was in the first aid box in the jeep. Now a green shiny frog jumped out of the grass and he licked the lions back. The lion felt disgusted so he ran away. Then the frog jumped on the princess's head and licked her wound and she felt better. The frog was a magical frog. They were very happy so they took the frog back to the palace. She showed the frog to her father and mother. The princess became friends with the frog. The frog helped the princess to heal all the patients in the kingdom. The king was so happy that he gave the frog a special name. The frog was from then on called Sir Websley the frog.
author: Rehaan Patel
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Bella Wong; Kavita Singh Kale; Niloufer Wadia; Proiti  Roy; Vongsavanh Damlongsouk

title: The Tiger
text: I JAVIA It is not easy being a tiger. Yes, tigers are cute and fierce But tigers are also big and heavy. This makes it difficult for them to hunt for food. A tiger eats once, after twenty attempts When a tiger walks through the forest, COF! COF! COF! The langur sounds, like an old man coughing! COF! COF! COF! AUUUU! JAUUUU! The barking deer sounds like a scared dog! AUUUU! JAUUUU! spotted deer sounds like a small bird! AU! AU! AU! AJUUUN! AJUUUN! The tiger does not know where all the animals are.
author: AAROHI JAVIA

title: Two Friends
text: There were two girls Timmy and Rippy. They did not have parents. Timmy was rich and had a house and Rippy was poor without house. Timmy was happy and Rippy was sad. They worked in a village near a city. Timmy used to sell clothes and Rippy was looking after sheep. After sometimes, Timmy got big house and Rippy got small house. And they lived happily in their houses. But they got a lot of work. And They did not find time to meet each other, So they decided to change their work. Timmy decided to be a baker. Rippy decided to be a dancer. After sometimes, Timmy got big baker shop and Rippy became dance teacher. From that day they lived happily ever after.
author: Mahika Rathor

title: The Lonely Frog
text: Beyond the green grass field, was a pond. It was no ordinary pond. It was a special pond. How special you ask? It had all types of flowers with all the colours you could ever imagine. The pond had water of purple colour. All the people there used to say, “Whoever touches or drinks the water from that pond, turns into a frog.” And not just a normal frog, a frog with unique powers. Powers like heat breath, teleportation, super strength, the power to jump ten times higher than an average human, the ability to stretch its tongue further than one metre and so many more such powers. The young ones of the frogs also had unique powers, powers just like the humans who were turned into frogs. But there was one frog who always isolated herself from other frogs. Her name was Zakia. She isolated herself because of her ability to live on land and in water. She was always bullied by her friends because of that. They thought she was lame and boring. They would say, “Get out of here, we only hang out with cool kids, unlike you.” They would push her and call her stupid and dumb. Zakia was always unhappy, and would lock herself in her room and lie on her bed crying with her hands covering her face. Zakia had no siblings. She always complained to her parents when she was bored. Her mother would say, “Don’t be sad Zakia. They are the ones missing out having an amazing friend like you.” “What is wrong with me? Why am I being treated this way?” she would ask herself. The pond was always beautiful and amazing. Humans thought that the pond and the organisms in it were a danger to their species. Not only because the water would turn them into frogs, but also because of the powers the frogs had. The humans tried to destroy the pond, but were not successful because the frogs would fight back. However, there was one thing that was able to destroy the magic of the pond. That was sand from the ocean. If the humans found out about this, the pond and its creatures would be doomed. This is because, if the ocean sand was spread around the pond, the frogs would turn into statues, the flowers would die, and the water in the pond would turn grey. One morning, Zakia was woken up by the loud sound of her fellow frogs screaming. “What is happening?” Zakia asked herself in a scared voice. She quickly ran outside to see what had happened only to find herself looking at the most horrible thing she could ever imagine, “Oh my goodness! Noooh!” she shouted. She could not believe what she saw. The pond was grey. The frogs had frozen like statues and the flowers were dead. “This could only mean one thing: the humans have found out how to destroy the pond. And now I am the only frog here,” she told herself while staring at the pond from outside her home. She started to cry. Tears were running down her cheeks like a waterfall. “Why me? Why am I the only one left? Why am I not a statue like others?” she asked herself. The more she asked herself these questions, the angrier she got. She started punching the water thinking how beautiful it used to be. Then suddenly, the water turned purple again. You can only imagine how happy and shocked Zakia was. “Yes, yes, yes, oh my gosh!” she screamed with joy, while jumping up and down. “How could this happen?” she asked herself, “What have I possibly done to turn the water purple again?” She touched the flowers near the pond. “I remember how gorgeous the flowers were.” Then suddenly the flowers she was touching came back to life. Zakia was shocked now even more than she was before and she could not move. She figured out that she has the power to fix things and bring them back to their normal state just by touching them and thinking about how they used to be. She was so happy. Then she began to bring all the dead flowers back to life. Then she sat down by the pond and thought, “If I can bring dead flowers back to life, can I bring my fellow frogs back? There is only one way to find out. I should try it.” She rushed to her mother and stared at her with sadness and tears in her eyes. Then she tried to bring her mother back to life. She thought, “I remember how my mom used to be, breathing and alive.” Then her mother opened her eyes. “Mother! Mother! Can you hear me?” Zakia asked. “Yes, Zakia, I can hear you,” her mother replied. Zakia’s mother asked, “What happened?” Zakia told her mother everything that had happened including her newly discovered powers. Then she went on and brought back to life the rest of her fellow frogs. When Zakia was 15 years old, she was chosen as the leader of her frog community. This was not only because of her powers but also because of her bravery and quick thinking. She carried on leading her community and the pond remains immortal.
author: Nakiete Mlaki

title: The Poor Lady
text: Once upon a time, there was a poor lady. She was living in a little village with her four children. She had a dream of flying. She did not have money to buy an aeroplane. She wanted to see the clouds, the moon and stars up close. Every day she sat under the tree and looked up at the sky. One day as she was walking under the tree, she saw a stick. She picked up the stick and went home with it. At home, the stick started to talk. “ I know you want to fly, I will help you. ” The lady was happy. “When will I fly?” She asked. “Tomorrow, at night.” “Really?” She told her children about flying with the stick. “Mum! Are you sick or just tired?” “Tomorrow night, look through the window. You shall see me flying.” The stick turned into a wooden plate a nd made her fly. She saw the moon, the hills and the clouds. Then, she saw the lights. After half an hour, she came back home. Next time I will fly with my children.
author: Larry Semiono

title: The letter
text: Joan Chan woke up and jumped up and down, today was her birthday! She climbed out of her bed and hugged her brother, Mike. He patted her and said,"Happy birthday, Jo!". Soon after, she brushed, bathed and wore her brand new floral dress. Grandma gave her a small toy she had made herself and Papa and Mumma gave her a book. The title of the red book read,"My small book of Big stories". Joan was overjoyed. In the evening there was to be a birthday picnic in the nearby fields with her friends. Soon the time came and Joan sat down on the mat and began to cut her birthday cake. Meg, Somu, Rita, John were singing and soon everyone got a piece of cake. A few hours later, it was bedtime and as Joan lay on her bed she looked at the window. What was that? A shooting star! Joan made a wish. What d'you suppose it was? A new race car? or perhaps a motorbike? No! She wished that her baby tooth would soon fall out. She was 7 years old now and her first tooth hadn't fallen yet. The next morning she woke up and while brushing she felt something wriggly. Her first baby tooth was gonna fall out! She screamed with joy. 2 days later it fell out. She had heard her brother say," There are tooth fairies who take your tooth and give you a gift in its place. If you have kept it clean of course!" So the following day she brushed her tooth and buried it under her pillow. The next day, to her enormous surprise she found a letter underneath. It said," Dear Joan Chan, greetings. I am the head toothfairy, Meiky Alsette and I am very impressed with your tooth and its cleanliness. You are very fortunate because you have received a letter from the tooth fairies. We consider it a great achievement as very few humans have contact with us. If it is convenient to you, you can write back to us. You can post your letter to the following address,"Eiffel tower top, Champ de Mars, 5 Avenue Anatole France, 75007 Paris, France." Also place the letter under the TV. Our greetings to your family and we hope to hear from you soon. Until then Au Revoir friend." So these fairies live in France, huh? thought Joan. I'll ask Papa to book tickets to Eiffel Tower top and then we can go and visit them she said to herself. The next day Joan showed it to all her friends. Somu and Rita wouldn't believe it but Meg and John felt that fictional creatures might exist. When she told her mom and dad, they just laughed. But Mike believed her tale. Soon enough there was a letter under the TV. Joan would sit in front of the Telly, as her family called it and wait for the reply letter. A few weeks later came the letter. This time the background was in blue and not pink. Soon enough, there was a flurry of letters passing between that Head fairy and Joan. What did they talk about? Oh, almost everything under the sun, including race cars. Meiky Alsette loved race cars or so she said. But Joan had a big surprise coming! Any guesses? Meiky Alsette, the head tooth fairy waaas......... Mike! Mike? Mike who? Mike, Joan's brother was pretending to be a tooth fairy to make Joan happy. Mike revealed this to Joan in his latest letter.Joan was astounded! Surprised? Did you actually believe in tooth fairies? Now I'm surprised. Might wanna go to Eiffel tower top to check if they are there. But of course, magic exists for those who believe in it. This story goes to show that we can do anything for our loved ones. So keep lovin' keep givin'
author: Aalyah Marisa
illustrator: Aalyah Marisa; Dixa Barooah; Jayesh Sivan; Nicole Soto-Vasquez

title: Plants that Heal
text: Aditi woke up with a cold. “ Achooo! Ahh…..Ahhh….Ahhh…ACHOOO”. Her grandmother said “Looks like you have a bad cold, Aditi.” “Yes grandma, yesterday I had a chilled soft drink. Besides, I got wet in the rain” said Aditi. “Don’t worry Aditi. I will give you some tea with lemon grass and ginger. You will feel better,” said grandma as she went off to the kitchen. Aditi followed grandma to the kitchen and watched as grandma put some fresh lemon grass and some crushed ginger to the boiling water. The aroma of the tea invaded the kitchen and Aditi said “ I think I am already feeling better.” Grandma laughed and said “You will be better when you have a hot cup of this tea. When I was a child, we had no doctors in our village. So, my mother always had some herbal medicines for small ailments like fever, cold and cough.” “Grandma, tell me more about these herbal medicines.” “Surely Aditi, here first have this cup of herbal tea. And then we will go to the garden and I will show you that our garden is indeed a small pharmacy full of medicinal herbs and plants. Here I have even noted all these plants in this book.” Aditi drank the tea and was happy to find that her throat felt better. Then she and grandma went to the garden. “Look at this plant Aditi” “Yes grandma that is tulsi or Holy Basil. We worship the tulsi plant. Grandma, does this plant have medicinal properties?” “Aditi, tulsi leaves contain some essential oils and these help to treat respiratory ailments. Tulsi leaves are rich in antioxidants and help to relieve stress. A paste of tulsi leaves can be used to treat skin ailments like itching of skin. Tulsi is also useful for people who get asthma attacks,” explained grandma. “Oh… I did not know we have such a useful plant right in the middle of our garden. Grandma, which other medicinal plants do we have here?” asked Aditi. Grandma called out “Come here Aditi. This is lemon grass or Citronella. I just used some of these leaves in the tea you just had. Like tulsi, lemon grass also has antioxidants and this helps to take toxins away from the body. A cup of lemon grass tea can help to bring relief from cold. It is also useful if you have an upset stomach. People with high blood pressure or high cholesterol should regularly consume lemon grass tea. If taken properly, herbal medicines do not cause any side effects” “Grandma, if herbal medicines are generally safe, then can a person stop all other medicines and just take herbal medicines?” “No Aditi, I was just going to explain that. People with any major health issue must go by their doctor’s advice and take the medicines prescribed by the doctor. One needs to inform the doctor of the herbal medicines taken. Plant based medicines are natural and do not usually cause harm. But sometimes the problem may be chronic or severe. Hence one must consult a doctor and follow the doctor’s advice. I too take herbal medicines if I have a problem. But if there is no relief or if the problem seems to increase I go to the doctor.” “Okay grandma. I too will remember that. Now let us look at some more medicinal plants.” “Come here" said Grandma. "This is ginger. Ginger is used in our daily cooking. Ginger is good for digestion. It also helps in treating cough and cold.” “Grandma, we often use ginger and garlic in our food. Does garlic also have any special benefits?” asked Aditi. Grandma responded “Yes…yes…garlic actually belongs to the onion family. Garlic contains a compound called as allicin and this has many benefits. For example, garlic helps to reduce high blood pressure and lower cholesterol thus protecting your heart. And now, let me show you one more wonderful plant. Come here Aditi.” Grandma took Aditi to a plant with nice long and broad leaves. She tore a bit of a leaf and gave it to Aditi to smell. Aditi said, “This fragrance is so nice grandma. Mother uses these leaves to make some nice sweet dishes. What is the name of this plant?” “This is turmeric or haldi. The turmeric we use in the ktichen is actually the underground stem of the plant. When it is dried and ground, we get turmeric powder. Turmeric is known for its antiseptic properties. In olden days, when people got hurt they often applied turmeric to the wound. Turmeric is useful to reduce the symptoms of arthritis. It boosts the immune system. Turmeric is used to detoxify the body.” “Grandma, mother sometimes gives me turmeric milk or haldi doodh when I have a sore throat.” “Yes Aditi. Turmeric milk has good antiseptic properties and is useful to treat throat infection.” Right next to the turmeric plant was plant with fleshy leaves. Aditi asked her grandma “Grandma, what is this plant called? Its leaves are quite fleshy and thick.” Grandma explained, “That is aloe vera. Actually it stores water in its leaves as it is a succulent. If we cut the leaves we get a gel like substance. Aloe vera gel is used to make many beauty products. It can be taken to reduce high blood sugar. It is rich in vitamins and minerals and can be used to treat skin problems like acne. You can apply aloe vera gel in case you get a sunburn. The gel is really soothing.” Aditi saw a plant with long leaves and she recognized it immediately. “Grandma, this is another useful plant. We call it adulsa. And mother gives it to me when I have cough.” “Yes Aditi, this is indeed Adulsa or Adhatoda. The plant is used to treat cold, cough, chronic bronchitis and asthma. It is an expectorant and helps to remove phlegm. The leaves can be used to treat skin ailments like scabies.” Grandma then took Aditi to a huge tree and asked “Do you know the name of this tree?” “Yes Grandma. This is the neem tree. On Gudi Padva, that is the first day of the month of Chaitra, mother insists that we eat a few neem leaves. They are quite bitter.” said Aditi. Grandma explained “Neem leaves are bitter, dear Aditi. But the neem tree is a wonderful tree. A paste of neem leaves is used to treat skin diseases. If some neem leaves are boiled in wate, we can use this water to wash our hair and get rid of dandruff. Twigs of neem were used to clean teeth in days when tooth brushes and tooth pastes were not available. And yes, these neem twigs not only cleaned your teeth but they also kept the mouth free of harmful bacteria." “I also see mother adding neem leaving to stored rice and other grains.” “You are right. Neem helps to keep the rice free from insects. Using neem leaves is far better than adding harmful pesticides to our grains. In the olden days, trees like neem were grown in every garden. Dear Aditi, we have had a nice walk in our lovely garden, but now I think we need to get back to the house. I will make some breakfast for you and give you some warm milk with turmeric. It will help you get better soon.” “Grandma, I am already feeling better. The ginger and lemon grass tea really worked.” “I am glad you are feeling better, Aditi. The walk in the garden also must have helped you. Actually, our body has the capacity to treat itself whenever we fall sick with minor ailments. Using medicinal plants and herbs is good. But yes, if we still feel sick, we need to see the doctor.” said Grandma. "Grandma, I think it was the chilled soft drink I had yesterday that gave me a bad cold. " said Aditi. "Aditi, cold is caused by a virus. But yes, chilled drinks especially those with artificial flavours can really irritate the throat." explained Grandma. "To quench your thirst, it is best to have water or natural drinks like coconut water, lemon juice or buttermilk." " I will remember that next time" said Aditi as she and grandma walked back to the house. Hope you liked the story. I also hope you learned about the wonderful plants that heal. Nature has given to us a big pharmacy in the form of plants. Our ancestors knew the uses of these plants and used them quite effectively. We should be proud of this knowledge and learn more about it. This knowledge about medicinal plants is part of our Indian culture. We call such knowledge as Indigenous Knowledge or Lokvidya. We should try and explore more of this knowledge.
author: Agnes Dcosta
illustrator: Agnes Dcosta; Charles  Norris-Brown; Narayan Prasad  Bohaju; Natasha Sharma; Priya Kuriyan; Sangeetha Kadur

title: The Sweet Twins Nisha and Trisha
text: Nisha and Trisha were twins. Their faces looked alike. Their eyes, nose, lips, cheeks, and other features looked the same. Nisha asked her mom one day,” Mom, why do they call Trisha and me as twins?” Their mom said," I t is because both of you were inside my stomach at the same time and were born with a few minutes difference." Their friends and family members sometimes found it difficult to identify who was Nisha and who was Trisha? To differentiate between them, their mom usually dressed Nisha in shades of green and Trisha in shades of pink. They also had different hairstyles. Nisha had two ponies, and Trisha had a bob cut. When they went to school, they had to wear the same uniform. So, people found them out with their hairstyle difference. Nisha had a sweet voice, and Trisha had a husky voice. But, how did their mother know the difference? Nisha had a tiny mole on her chin. Trisha did not have a mole on her chin. The twins celebrated their birthdays on the same day. The twins also celebrated their similarities and differences and lived happily.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Value small things
text: Suma stayed with her mother in a village, her father had passed away few years back and her mother Savita was a domestic help in some of the nearby houses. Suma went along with her mother to the houses and would stay in a corner and see her mother work hard. Her mother would always tell her, ‘Suma I want you to go school and study hard so that you don’t have to live a life like me’. ﻿Suma barely understood what her mother meant by these words, but Suma knew that she wanted to make her mother happy Suma joined school the next year, she often went bare foot and half fed many times, but she never complained, she always saw her mother’s face and all the hard work that her mother took in raising up Suma. Days passed by for Suma in school, she didn’t have many friends as they always avoided her for being poor and they often made fun of her. One day the teacher gave them a test, she asked ‘What are the 5 things that make you happy? All the children had so much to write. Some wrote of the house, their toys, their dress, different types of food etc. The teacher asked the students to read their answers. All the students in the class gave their favourite and most liked things. Reena said she is happy with her toys, favourite food, her dolls, her mobile games, her new dress. Ravi said he is happy when he goes for shopping with his parents, movie theatre, ice creams, pizza and toys It was now Suma’s turn to answer, she was frightened as her answer did not match with that of her classmates. She was hesitant and knew that, they would laugh at her again. Suma had something different to share, her mother’s hard work and efforts inspired her to see life in a special way. In a very feeble voice Suma answered – the things that make me happy is “ that I can see, I can hear, I can speak, I can move, I can feel and care for others” The difficult times made her value even the smallest things so preciously. Hearing this answer all her classmates looked at her in surprise. The teacher clapped and the entire class joined in clapping for Suma. The teacher told the class, we should value what we have in our life and be thankful to God for all the blessings. Since then all her classmates became her friends and always supported her in the school activities. Moral of the story: Value the gifts from God and treasure them always.
author: Reni  Francis
illustrator: Karmacharya K.K; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Promina Shreshtha; Rajiv Eipe; Santosh Pujari; Sheetal Thapa

title: Samy's birthday
text: "Yay! It is my birthday " shouted Samy. He was very excited for his birthday. Samy thought he would get lots of gifts,a cake of his choice and he could even go out to a restaurant. So he got of from bed,brushed his teeth and went downstairs. But when he went downstairs he could not find anyone, so Samy thought that his parents and friends forgot that it is his birthday today. Samy went to his room and started crying. Suddenly Samy's parents and friends Jumped out of the curtains and wished him happy birthday.They gave him lot of gifts.When it was night Samy's parents took him to a restaurant,they all ate yummy food and when they were done eating, they ordered a cake.Samy cut the cake and had lot of fun
author: Vansha Lakshita Nukarapu
illustrator: Aneesh Jape; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Nompumelelo  Mdluli; Phạm Thị  Thu Trang

title: Never too late to accept your mistakes !!
text: There was a girl named Aisha. One day she went to her coaching class and the teacher conducted Science test. But Aisha didn’t know any answers. She still gave the test. When result came she was sad because it was her worst performance. She told her mother that she scored.But in reality she had scored just 3 numbers in the test. She thought her family members especially her younger brother will laugh on her. She kept on thinking about her lie and after few days she was fed up and decided to tell the truth. She went to her mother and said I had scored just 3 numbers in my test and that she lied to all. Her mother said, its fine next time we will be prepared for these surprise tests. And her mother guided her that we should not bother about what others will think. And her mother guided her that we should not bother about what others will think. The most important thing is that you tried and that’s enough. And that she should study hard and be ready for next tests and give our best efforts. That day Aisha learned truth is always better and it helps us to achieve best.
author: Trisha Bhandoola
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Drisha NC; Karen  Vermeulen; Melvyn  Naidoo; Shaurya Upadhyay; Sulagna  Roy

title: The School thief
text: It was a fine morning, all the children were going to school. They were very excited. They all ran to their class. As soon as they entered the class they went and sat in their places. The teacher made an announcement, " Class, there has been an issue going around the school, some students reported to the principal that their things have been robbed when they were in class When the teaches says this a girl enters class. The teacher asks who she is, so she replies "Teacher I am from grade 4 and as you know there has been robbery one of my classmates also has been robbed when she was in the playground, so I wanted to tell your students not to go to the playground". The teacher said "Ok class did you all hear what she said no going to the playground until the issue is solved". " Ok teacher!" shouted the class. As the teacher was saying this the principal entered the class and said that he wanted to say some good news. " The issue has been solved" said the principal. Everyone was happy. The End

title: Ravi Goes Playing
text: Once there was a boy named Ravi. He lived with his family. He loved playing. One day his Grandmother told him "Ohh Ravi, your friends are here why don't you go outside to play?" Hearing this Ravi jumped out of his bed and got ready. He drank his milk as fast as he could and took his bat and ball immediately. Day went on and Ravi was enjoying with his friends. Now it was noon and Ravi was very tired so he went home. His grandmother said " You are finally here I was waiting for you and now that you are here go take a bath and eat your food". Since Ravi was a good boy he followed his grandmother's instructions.After eating he went in his bed to read a book and then he fell asleep.This is how the whole day in Ravi's life went.

title: Become a slender king
text: Taleb Mteir There is a fat king. The fat king has a slender dog, the fat king went for a walk with his slender dog The dog saw a bird. The dog ran after the bird. The king ran after the dog. They ran, ran, ran, ran for days The king caught the dog Now the fat king has become a slender king.
author: Naba Taleb Mteir

title: The Cat And The Dog
text: Once upon a time there lived a cat and a dog.They both were very good friends.They used to eat together. The cat loved to eat with the dog. They liked to catch each other. Every time the cat used to go on barrels,drums and sometimes on a tree and dog jumed and jumed to catch her. Only sometimes he could catch her. They liked to sleep with each other in the shiney sun light. They both like to sleep under a big tree. Their most favourite game was to chase each other. The dog used to run behind the cat and the cat used to run as fast as she could.
author: Shaurya Khodade

title: Road Accident
text: I was bewildered Witnessing a sudden death, Henna was painted On the hands of a newlywed! The bride marked happily A black tip on the forehead Who knew it'd be the sign Mourning life-lamp on the street! Gifted a peaceful land as fringe Spreading by the Motherland Twisted in that Hem of Sari A bride lost her husband! I wondered if I was there In the death procession? It seemed as if I was on the stream! Is that fate(!) On the way life is being defeated? Even more the Severe tunes The screaming of the survivors!
author: Abu Sayeed
illustrator: Rob Owen; Samidha Gunjal; Shanti Devi; Sharanya Singh

title: Lilly and Sam
text: Lilly and Sam were best friends,both of them liked jumping,rolling and lying on the grass.They also liked getting messy,having fun. They looked for insects.Sam was really good at sniffing out treasure. They used to have a lot of fun. when Lilly was at school,Sam used to play with the neighbor's cat,Dolly. Lilly and Sam also read books together.They would snuggle on the couch and imagine the pictures. One day, as Sam was running around, he slipt and fell in to the river!Lilly rescued him.
author: Sarah Parveen

title: Lion and the mouse
text: Once there was a lion in a forest. One day when that lion was in a deep sleep a mouse came there. The naughty mouse started playing around by jumping on lion's tail. Lion's sleep was disturbed because of mouse. He glared at the mouse in anger. Mouse got scared and said, "Oh King! Please spare my life and in return I will help you when you are in need" Lion felt sorry for the mouse and let him go. Mouse ran from there being thankful. Another day, Lion was caught in a hunter's net. The mouse saw the lion and came there. Mouse freed the lion by cutting the net with his sharp teeth. Lion and the mouse became friends and lived happily. Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
author: Raghavi Sarada

title: My brother who loves competition
text: We never felt any harm in this but one day it became a big danger. He started to say me and my mother we do not come in their family and not only us he started saying every one boy and girl. title: Too Many Bananas
text: Sringeri Srinivas was having a very bad day Nobody wanted the sweet,ripe Bananas he was growing on his farm. Not to his family. Not to his neighbour. Not to his friends. Not the Traders who could sell bananas in Far away markets. And not even his cows. No thank you they all said. The bananas are sweat but we had too many. We can not eat any more. Poor sringeri srinivas! what was he to do now with his rich harvest of bananas. He decided to seek help the farmers centre in Doddooru,a big town near his village. off he went carrying the best crop of bananas. surely someone there would have a good idea for him. A few days later, Sringeri Srinivas returned home looking very happy. He went back to growing bananas on his farm. But he did not offer the fruits to anyone anymore. Not to his family. Not to his neighbour. not to his friends. Not to his traders who could sell the bananas in far away markets and not even to his cows! Everyone became very curious. where were all the bananas going? One day, neighbour shivanna arranged a very big pooja. The priest asked him to get 108 ripe bananas as an offering to the gods. Shivanna ran to sringeri srinivas. I am sorry for saying no to you before, but now I need 108 ripe bananas. Can you help me,please? Sringeri Srinivas tapped on his chin. well my crop has just been cut. But let me see what I can do. You may start your pooja. I will surely come. The pooja started. The whole village came to watch. The priest began chanting. Soon it became time to offer bananas to the gods. Just then, came Sringeri Srinivas carrying a big bag. From the bag, He carefully took out 27 packets and laid them out before the holy fire.Each packet was carefully wrapped in banana leaf. One each one was written - High Quality halwa, S.S. Farms. Sringeri Srinivas offered one to the priest. Each one has the pulp of 4 bananas. There are 27 packets. So here are your 108 ripe bananas. The priest was so surprised that he forgot to chant. In silence, One child began to laugh. Soon the whole village started laughing and clapping. Now we know what Sringeri Srinivas does with all the bananas that he grows. Did you know the facts about bananas? Bananas float in water because they are less dense in comparison. Bananas are one of the most popular fruits in the American diet. Bananas grow on plants that are officially considered an herb. The banana is actually classified as a berry.
author: Dhanush Sajaneesh

title: The Lion and the Mouse
text: A lion was once sleeping in the jungle when a mouse started running up and down his body just for fun. This disturbed the lion’s sleep, and he woke up quite angry. He was about to eat the mouse when the mouse desperately requested the lion to set him free. “I promise you, I will be of great help to you someday if you save me.” The lion laughed at the mouse’s confidence and let him go. One day, a few hunters came into the forest and took the lion with them. They tied him up against a tree. The lion was struggling to get out and started to whimper. Soon, the mouse walked past and noticed the lion in trouble. Quickly, he ran and gnawed on the ropes to set the lion free. Both of them sped off into the jungle. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Moral of the Story: A small act of kindness can go a long way
author: Dayamay Halder

title: Ragman
text: There were five minutes left for school leave, but Chinu could not wait. He looked outside. No one was there. Then the bell was heard from somewhere nearby. " What's going on, Chinu?" The teacher said "Sorry Akka," Chinu said, "What is that…" Then, "Paperwalla, paper! Old newspaper, scrap! " Chinu's father, a scrap man, sang. Chinu's grin was shining to the outside. The school bell rang. Chinu ran to his father. A big smile was playing on his face. He was the only child in school whose father used to come to pick him up. Chinu jumped and sat on the cart and hung his feet. Father pushed the cart and called out loud, "Pepperwalla... litter!" Chinu also called. Wow! What a loud voice for both of them! When a janitor stopped them, Chinu jumped down. With an empty sack, he went with his father. Today whatever sack they get will be filled in this sack. ﻿ From this house, newspaper. Newspapers and magazines from that house. From the lower house, newspapers and magazines and empty bottles. Chinu ran and brought another empty sack from the cart. They were about to go up in the elevator! Chinu's eyes became big and round. From the fifth floor, newspapers and magazines, bottles, cans and books were found. By the time his father was talking to the woman, Chinu covered everything like books were at the top. Where he could see them. Now Chinu had to share the hand of father to push the cart. After saving everything at home, Chinu's father called him. "You have something," he said. The same book that Chinu had been watching all afternoon. "Thank you father!" Chinu said after that, they had to call him thrice for dinner.
author: Bhavana Sunil

title: The Yellow Umbrella
text: Raamu and Shaamu are best friends. When they are together they ask for nothing else. They would sit and chat for hours. They loved to discuss nature, current affairs and how some humans in their selfishness are ruining mother nature. Shaamu is very grumpy today because three men came in the morning with some huge machines and cut off the large Peepal tree. Shaamu had cried loudly but to no avail. The men did not pay any heed to this little frog croaking near the pond. “Why are you so grumpy today?” asked Raamu. “Don’t you know why I am so?” fired Shaamu. “Yeah, I do but what can we do.” “I wish we could do something. Now we have no shade. This heat is too much to bear. How will we enjoy nature and discuss so many other things?” muttered Shaamu. “That is very true.” agreed Raamu. An old stork with a large backpack overheard their conversation. “I know it is bad manners to overhear someone else’s conversation, but if you don’t mind may I say something.” Shaamu was about to say, “Yes we do mind and we do not allow strangers to randomly barge in ”, but Raamu said, “Yes, Ms Stork, please go ahead. What do you have to say? “Thank you” Mr.. ah.. “I am Raamu” “Very pleased to meet you Raamu. I am Mrs. Shaanti. And may I know your friend’s name who doesn’t seem very happy today.” “He is Shaamu, my best-friend. Usually he is very jubilant, but today he is unhappy because some men cut our favourite Peepal tree.” “Yeah I do understand. But are you just going to be sad and grumpy or are you going to do something about it.” “There is nothing much we tiny creatures could do.” snapped Shaamu. “That is very true. But nobody can make you sad or grumpy without your wish” explained Mrs. Shaanti. “You seem to be very wise. Could you please explain what you mean? Asked Raamu. “I have traveled far and wide and I have seen the world. Outer circumstances and situations should not affect our internal peace and state of mind. We should never blame others for our sorrow or our sufferings. We need to find our own peace.” Shaamu and Raamu heard Mrs. Shaanti with apt attention. Shaamu was already feeling better. “If you are grumpy because the blazing sun will not let you enjoy nature and chat with your friend, I have a solution.” Mrs. Shaanti opened her back pack and moved her beak around looking for something. “Here it is. This will take care of your problem” She pulled out an umbrella and handed it over to Shaamu. “What shall I do with this stick? Asked Shaamu. “This is no ordinary stick. Do you see the small button out there? Press it and see.” He pressed the button and voila! A beautiful yellow umbrella opened up with tiny red flowers. “Wow! This is so cool. And I don’t feel the heat.” “Yes, now you can sit with your friend under the sun and chat for as long as you wish.” said Mrs. Shaanti. “Thank you so much for your kindness,” said Raamu and Shaamu in unison. “That is my pleasure. Now please allow me to say good-bye. I have a long way to go.” “Yes please. But do visit us whenever you come here. It has been a great pleasure to meet you.” exclaimed Shaamu. “I shall surely do that. Bye-bye.” “Bye-bye”
author: Nirmala Sonathi

title: Circle of Good deed
text: Tina, Mina and Nina were childhood friends living in Mumbai. They were very close to each other, they went to the same school and stayed in the same building and always played together. They were very kind and helpful to others. Tina would often help the elderly uncle and aunt during an evening walk, while Mina would help in carrying the bags of food stuff to the home of the elderly. Nina had a very neat handwriting, she would often help old uncle and aunt to write letters to their children. All the inmates of the building were very happy of them. As they walked to school everyday, they saw a girl with her mother selling fruits and vegetables. They felt very sad for her. One day Mina asked the little girl her name, very softly she replied, 'Suman'. Suman was six years old and stayed with her mother. She never went to school as her mother was the sole bread winner for their house and she could not afford to send Suman to school. Hearing the sad story of Suman, the friends decided to help Suman. They thought of different ways to help Suman and they did not want to burden their parents. Mina's mother, Renu aunty was a social worker in an NGO for girl education. The three friends went to Renu aunty and told about Suman. Renu aunty assured them to help Suman get admission in school. At the same time Tina, Mina and Nina visited the NGO and saw beautiful cards and other decorative articles. Renu aunty explained that the money collected from the sale of these articles help in the education of the needy girls. They got an idea to help Suman with their own talents. Tina was very good in drawing, she made creative handmade cards and Nina in her neat and beautiful handwriting wrote good messages on the cards. Mina was artistic and made good decorative articles such as flower vase, pen stand, decorative flowers etc. They handed over their art work to Renu aunty to be displayed at the NGO. In their small way they contributed their work. Soon Suman was in the NGO school and was studying very hard and scoring good marks. Days passed by and it was friendship day, Suman made a hand made card for Tina, Mina and Nina, she wrote a beautiful poem thanking them for their care and support. The three friends were very happy and satisfied in helping Suman to go to school. Suman's mother had tears of joy and thankfulness for Tina, Mina and Nina. On Republic Day, the inmates of the building applauded and felicitated Tina, Mina and Nina for their good deed in helping a girl child receive education.
author: Reni  Francis
illustrator: Aman Randhawa; Isaac Sikhakhane; Mlungisi Dlamini; Saurabh Pandey; Shalini Jithesh; Siraj Saxena; Suvidha Mistry

title: Day And Night
text: One Night, Tara looked up at the night sky and wondered what would be at the other side of the world. She had a question....what would it be on the other side right now? Day Or Night? On the other side Maddy, in America was coming back from school...it was noon. Maddy new Tara very well. He called her up and she wasn't happy as it was the middle of the night. Maddy was surprised... he said "But it's noon Tara...What are you talking about?" " I am angry because it is night in India and I was sleeping. Said Tara." "But Tara...it is noon here. I don't understand". Said Maddy " Oh we'll talk about This when you visit me. Remember You are coming after a week?" After a week Maddy and his family landed in "IND- INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT" Maddy was surprised to see how different India was from America. His family got to the road and went to Tara's. They have arrived. Tara and Maddy are happy to meet and they hug each other. Then they have a long chat and play till their parents call them. They are having dinner and Maddy asks about his question to Tara's papa, who is a scientist. Tara's father explains to Maddy that "The sun is in the center of our solar system. The earth is a round ball. Half side faces the sun and half side is dark. The half side facing the sun is bright which is day. The side which is completely dark and sees the moon is.." "Night!" Maddy Shouted. "Wonderful! Any more questions beta?" Asked Tara's papa. "Yes. How are we experiencing both day and night if half side only faces the sun. Does the Earth Move?" asked Maddy. "Wow! Nice question.Yes...You see Maddy...there are 24 hours in a day and the earth doesn't stay still. It rotates. You must noticed that around June there are 12 hours of day and night. It means that the earth is rotating equally. Half day you have the bright light of sun and half day night. Maddy was surprised. Tara was speechless. Now they were going to sleep. Maddy and Tara went to their bedroom. They both were talking all the time...they loved ﻿"Day And Night" ﻿.
author: ARNAV KUMAR
illustrator: Aditi Kakade; Brunda Anandarao; Ellen Heydenrych; Mbongeni Fongoqa; Priyanka Kumar; Sharath Ravishankar; Shreeya Wagh; Soumya Menon; Subinita Deshaprabhu

title: Nurture our Nature
text: Science Exhibition Day' the poster was put on the school gate. The school was buzzing with students all around. Students from different classes were all ready with their projects. Adi was also very excited about his project for Science Exhibition Day. The students got their exhibits of working and non - working models, charts, projects, posters and many more. Adi was in Class VI and their exhibit display was in the school auditorium. Adi walked with his exhibit to the room, all the students were whispering and giggling. Adi kept his exhibit of three potted plant of chilli, tomato and beans. The other students had big working models, projects on laptops and games on science and facts. He felt sad and small in front of them but he was very confident about the exhibit. As the Event Judges went around each table and looked at the exhibit and heard the explanation, Adi waited patiently. Mr. Sam their School Principal saw Adi's exhibit and patted his back. The Judges came to Adi's exhibit and asked him to explain. Adi's project was "Nurture our Nature". Adi explained about the potted plants and the kitchen garden at his house and the plants cultivated in his garden. He alongwith his parents has taken this initiative in all the 28 flats of their building. Adi explained the steps of kitchen gardening, he said let us take the example of a chilli plant. Take a medium sized pot, put soil only half the level of the pot, put the chilli seeds into it and cover it with soil, the soil should not filled till the brim of the pot. Pour water and place the pot in a place to get adequate sunlight. After few days the seeds will germinate into tiny saplings. The judges were amazed by this small idea of turning our home kitchen as garden thus making our home self sufficient. Finally it was time for announcing the Prize Winners of the Science Exhibition. Adi got First prize among Class VI students for bringing life in each one's home. Adi was asked to speak a few words, he said, 'Let us all pledge to 'Nurture our Nature' and bring life through Kitchen gardening. Their Principal was proud of Adi and all clapped for him.
author: Reni  Francis
illustrator: Abhimanyu Ghimiray; Magriet Brink; Phạm  Thu Thùy; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Suvidha Mistry

title: Name, Place, Animals, Things Game
text: In the game of Names, Place, Animals, Things - Name is the name of a person. Place is any city, country, or continent. Animals can include animals or birds. Things can be any object. Any number of players can play the game at the same time. But, 3 or 4 players at a time will be fun and manageable. Let us watch how two players Tarun and Raghu play the game. First, both of them draw lines in their notebooks as shown. To start the game, Tarun starts thinking in mind the alphabets from A to Z. Raghu will suddenly stay stop. Tarun thought of the letter P when Raghu said stop. Now, both of them have to write Name, Place, Animals, Things that start with the letter P. Once they complete, both of them will tell the answers. They can give marks or scores. Let us see what Tarun wrote - P rakash, P aris, P anther, P ot What did Raghu write? P rema, P eru, P ig, P in Let us see how much each score. For every correct answer, you give 10 marks. So, Tarun scored 40. Raghu also scored 40. Now Raghu has to start thinking the alphabets from A to Z in his mind. Tarun stays stop. The letter Raghu thought was N. Let us see what Tarun wrote. Tarun did not know the name of an animal or bird in N. So, he scores 30. Let us see what Raghu wrote. Raghu wrote answers for all the columns. So, he scores 40. Now Tarun thinks of the alphabets in mind, and the game continues. At the end of the game, you can add the marks of each player. The player with the highest mark is the winner. Cheers!
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Anitha Selvanathan; Miza Magalhães; Nan Hom Noon; Nompumelelo  Mdluli; Priya Kuriyan; Ram Kol

title: Bullying : What did Jack do?
text: One day, a boy named Jack went to a new school called Brooklyn Free High School. Over there he saw that the kids could make their own time table and do as they like. One day, he thought he would go to the science lab for seeing some fun things to the school's public microscope. He went and he saw that a 10 - year - old boy was standing next to the microscope. He went and asked " Excuse Me. Can I just have a peek at the microscope?" " NO" said the boy " Get your own microscope if you want to see through a microscope!" Jack was very sad. He Went home angrily and sadly. His father tried to cheer him up but he was very sad. Everyday, he would follow his own time table but the boy had stolen it and so had followed Jack to his own periods. One day, Jack got an idea to make the bully stop bullying him. He went to his time table that he had stuck in his room and modified it every day. That way, he would always be out of the bully's way. The bully noticed it and modified his own time table but he never got a chance to bully him. One day, during the lunch break, he caught a tiny bug and put it inside Jack's lunch box. When Jack opened his box, he saw that most of his idlis had been eaten by the bug. Jack got very angry. He went and told the teacher. The teacher heard everything and decided to teach him a lesson. He baked a chocolate cake that was filled with chilli powder. He gave it to Jack and Jack gave it to the bully. The bully took it and understood that it was a trick. He took the cake and threw it in the dust bin. The next day, Jack was taking a stroll in the play ground with his only friend, Tim. Tim was very kind and always helped Jack in times of need. When Jack was walking down, the bully intentionally threw a glass bottle from the higher floor at them. Jack got hurt and his head started bleeding very badly. Tim went and told the school nurse and the principal. Mr. Leonard, the English teacher saw everything and gave a recording of ti to the principal. The principal announced over the microphone " Colin Denimor. In my office now!" The bully went inside the principals office and he caned him for hurting Jack. The bully realized his mistake and made up for it by sending him and invite on Thanksgiving for a nice lunch and day. THE END
author: Shiven Nair

title: The Brave Little Fish
text: Avin the fish went on a vacation to the ocean with his family. Don't go far away, his mother said. But Avin did not listen to her! He swam far away. His mother tried to bring him back. Just then a big whale came and ate his mother. Avin was very sad. "I will save my mother" he said. Brave Avin swam into the giant whale's mouth! He went in and in until he found his mother. Then he pulled her out and the next time the whale opened his mouth, they swam out.

title: Today I Will
text: Today I will... light candles for the festival. Story Description Let's explore all of the things that you can do today. ﻿ Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Chasing ch-ey-s-ing Today I will be chasing birds. Freezing fr-ee-z-ing Today it is freezing cold outside. Eagle ee-gu-l I saw an eagle today. Guava g-wah-v-a I will eat a guava today. Today I will... read my favourite book. Today I will... chase a cat chasing a squirrel. Today I will... help my sister pick vegetables. Today I will... keep warm because it’s freezing cold. Today I will... eat lunch under the big tree. Today I will... ride a camel in the hot desert. Today I will... buy guavas from the market. Today I will... wear the same colour as my friends. Today I will... watch the eagle fly. Today I will... just look out of the window. Today I will... do a small favour. Today I will... play with my friends. Yay! Post-Reading Questions Explain the difference between today and yesterday. Describe three things that you are doing today.
author: Puja Sharma

title: Butterfly
text: One day, a butterfly emerged from its cocoon. It looked around but could not find its family. The butterfly was sad. "Where is my family?", it asked the bees. "They are migrating", the bees said. "What is that?", asked the butterfly. "It means flying to a warm place for the winter", the bees said. "Why?" asked the butterfly. The bees replied, "Butterflies need warm temperatures above 80 degrees F to fly. If the temperature falls below 55 degrees F, the butterflies become immobile". "I shall also migrate and find my family", said the little butterfly. It immediately pumped its wings with body fluid (butterflies don't have any blood in them; they are cold blooded). It rested till its wings became dry and hard. Then it started flying super duper fast! After some time, he met another butterfly who was also flying. So they flew together. Then they met other butterflies. Soon a big flock of butterflies was flying together. A little boy saw the butterflies fly and said, "Butterflies make the sky bloom! Their wings shine in the sunlight!!" Soon the little butterfly reached the end of the migration. There he saw his family and they were all happy to see each other!
author: Avin Kulkarni
illustrator: Lavanya  Naidu; Nuwan Chathuranga Athulasiri; Ounla  Santi; Rashmi Gopal; Shreya Shruti

title: The Monkey & The Foolish Crocodile...
text: Long time ago lived a monkey on the banks of a river.. One day the Monkey saw a Crocodile coming out of the river.. He wasn't scared and said ''hi'' to the crocodile.. The crocodile did the same too and they both became good friends.. The crocodile used to visit the monkey everyday.... On a Sunday morning the crocodile was dying of hunger... He asked the monkey whether he had something to eat.. Without any delay the monkey gave him a few rose apples to eat.. The crocodile was very thankful and asked the monkey whether he can take some for his wife... The monkey agreed.. When the crocodile's wife ate those apples, she thought that if the monkey only ate these sweet apples everyday his flesh also must be very sweet and she can have him for dinner.. So she thought of a plan and pretended to be ill and told his husband(the crocodile) that she can only get well when she eats a monkey's flesh.. So she asked him to call the monkey for dinner The crocodile didn't want to harm his friend and also didn't want to lose his wife.. So he decided to kill his friend... He went to the monkey and said ''Hey friend, me and my wife have invited you to a dinner party would you mind coming''.. The monkey said ''Oh that's great, i'll surely be there.. So the monkey sat on back of the crocodie.. But then, the crocodile stooped in the middle of the river.. The monkey said that ''Why did you stop''.. The crocodile says '' I want to kill you, my wife is ill and she can only get well when she eats a monkey's flesh.. The monkey was shocked and surprised but he didn't react.. The monkey was clever enough and thought of a plan.. So he said that '' Ok, but i forgot my flesh on the branch of the tree''.. So they went back to the tree.. The monkey jumped on the branch and escaped and said to the crocodile that ''You can go and tell your wicked wife that his husband is the biggest fool in the world and was leading to a wrong step....
author: Ananya Singh

title: The cat and the fox
text: Once a Cat and a Fox were traveling together. As they went along, picking up provisions on the way a stray mouse here, a fat chicken there they began an argument to while away the time between bites. And, as usually happens when comrades argue, the talk began to get personal. You think you are extremely clever, don't you?" said the Fox. "Do you pretend to know more than I? Why, I know a whole sackful of tricks!" Well," retorted the Cat, "I admit I know one trick only, but that one, let me tell you, is worth a thousand of yours!" Just then, close by, they heard a hunter's horn and the yelping of a pack of hounds. In an instant the Cat was up a tree, hiding among the leaves. "This is my trick," he called to the Fox. "Now let me see what yours are worth''. But the Fox had so many plans for escape he could not decide which one to try first. He dodged here and there with the hounds at his heels. He doubled on his tracks, he ran at top speed, he entered a dozen burrows, but all in vain. The hounds caught him, and soon put an end to the boaster and all his tricks. The Moral Of This Tale "Common sense is always worth more the cunning" 😊😊
author: Anishka Singh

title: Lallu's sweets
text: He was very fond of eating sweets and he ate sweets all day. Mom said, "You are small now. Don't go outside alone. I will make all the sweets at home. The sweets in the market are not clean." But Lallu did not listen to his mother and took his bag and went to the market. On the way, the Cat saw him going alone and thought, "Today is a golden chance, I will eat him!" As soon as Lallu reached a quiet street, the cat jumped in front of Lallu. Lallu was extremely frightened. He threw his bag there and ran to his house at his highest speed. Seeing his fearful face, mother understood everything. She embraced him and said affectionately," I will make all the sweets at home for you." That time, Lallu understood that it is always good to listen to our elders.
author: Bulbul  Verma
illustrator: Bulbul Sharma; Deepa Balsavar; Herminder Ohri; Priya Kuriyan; Tanaya Vyas

title: Poofy Goes Shopping
text: Poofy was getting ready for autumn. poofy has a small family of daddy, mummy, brother Locky, sister Leeky and Poofy. she wore her red scarf and her boots. She carried her beautiful red hand bag and went shopping. She bought lots of nuts. She bought gloves for her mummy. She also bought it for her dad. She forgot to buy something for Locky! She jumped into the bus and reached home. She gave everybody their gifts. Locky was waiting for his gift. Poofy said, "Oh my! I forgot to get something for you!! I am so sorry." Locky started crying. He said' "How could you do this to me? "Poofy felt very sad about for her brother. So, she grabbed her red handbag and rushed out to buy him something.
author: Shriya Kokkonda

title: Ammu's fabulous village fair
text: Once in a small village there lived a little girl named Ammu.She loved to go for fairs with her friends. Ammu doesn't had parents she lived with her grandmother. Once there was such a huge village fair in her hometown. She took permission from her grandmother and went to her friends. Ammu asked all of them " friends can we go for the village fair by today evening...Are you ready? ". One of her friend Kriti shouted "Sure Ammu ". All had the same opinion all were ready to go by today evening itself. They reached at the village fair. All of them were so exited to see what all are there to enjoy. First each of them took five tickets for themselves.Ammu and Kriti went near a giant wheel and gave one of their tickets.They sat on one of the seat of the giant wheel. Kriti said" it was wonderful ". Ammu immediately replied " yeah! ". Later when they checked their bag they couldn't see any of their tickets. Ammu shouted "it's all missing ". Kriti I think it had been lost from us. "Oh! " Ammu said sadly. Later...when they were walking sadly they note that one man was following them. They felt scared. They walked by hiding from that man. But he was still following them.After walking a lot they took rest under a tree. That man suddenly entered to the scene and looked at them.They were scared because all their friends were busy playing at somewhere else in the fair. Even they don't know where their other friends where. But unexpectedly that man smiled at them and said... "Have you both lost your tickets?". Kriti and Ammu said " yes uncle we had ". That man said " First of all myself I'm Nandakumar, when I was walking towards the giant wheel you both were running to the park that time all your tickets were coming out of your bags. Suddenly I took it and put it in my pocket. To return that tickets to you both I was following you two. "Here's is your tickets,take it.Now go and enjoy other rides with these tickets ". Ammu and Kriti happily received it from Nandakumar and used it for other amazing rides. After playing and enjoying a lot they went near a snack shop, there they found their other friends they told all that happened. Then all of them returned to their own homes and Ammu also returned to her home and told all that happened at the village fair to her grandmother.. After her dinner she went to sleep while laying on the bed she recollected all that happened today she said herself " IT WAS A FABULOUS VILLAGE FAIR " and laughed Ha,ha, ha.... It was all over. She hugged her grandmother and slept.
author: Niswasa EV

title: A PARROT AND A CAT
text: Once upon a time their lived a parrot with their children in a big tree.Every day she go in search of food for their children. one day she flew in search of food for their children.She flew and flew, then she sit in a window of the kichen.Inside the kichen she saw milk in a bowl she was very happy and she flew in the kichen and dringing the milk. A cat was seeing it,he was very angry seeing that the parrot is dringing his milk he jumbed over the parrot, the parrot was so scared she flew away from the window.Then the cat said:you go now Later I will catch you,then he drink the milk and went to find the parrot"s nest. title: Yami and Sofi
text: Sofi and Yami live in the same neighbourhood, play in the same park, and both are best friends. They both race to Yami’s home and Sofi opens the fridge to get a snack but Yami‘s fridge is empty with just a small container of milk for her brother, Joy. Sofi asked “Why doesn’t your mom go the grocery store?”. Yami:“We don’t have any money.” Sofi: “What if you get hungry?” Yami: “We have some bread.” Sofi: “I guess I’d better go home,” Yami requested Sofi not to tell anyone. Sofi’s went home and opened the fridge and it is full of milk, eggs, cheese, bread, fruits, jam and vegetables. Sofi shared her food with Yami because she understood how hunger feels! Despite Sofi’s very best efforts, Yami ‘s fridge is still empty and finally ends up telling her mom what is going on. They then buy food for Yami ‘s family to help them out.

title: The baby elephant
text: Once upon a time, there lived a baby elephant. Elephant was a really naughty elephant. His parents used to tell him over and over again that he has to pay attention to his surroundings. He was scratching his back and not paying attention. Suddenly he fell in to a hole. He started crying for help and trumpeted a lot. Elephant trumpeted super loudly. His friends herd him. Lion told Hare and Turtle that Elephant was in trouble. Lion would pull Elephant out of the hole. Tortoise and Hare will rush to find Elephant's parents. Finally Tortoise found Elephant's dad. Elephant's dad said: i'm so happy that you are safe. Remember, always pay attention to your surroundings. The End

title: Lilly

I play around with toys... and I play with other cats too And have yummy food too But I still won't forget the fun with my friends

title: The old women and the fat hen
text: An old women kept a hen that laid a egg every morning without fail. The eggs were large and delicious, and the old women was able to sell them for very good price at market. '' If my hen would lay two eggs every day '', she said to herself ", I would be able to earn twice as much money!" The old women decided that the best way to make the hen lay an extra egg was giving the hen extra food twice so she also gave the hen food at evening the hen was so much happy. The hen became fatter and fatter. On e day the old women looked at the nest there were no eggs. The hen had became so much fatter and lazy that she had stopped laying eggs. moral: thing don't work as planned short stories like this will come soon f animals

title: Arun and his Pet Dog
text: Arun went out for fishing. It was heavily raining. By then a lovely dog was struggling to come out of the river water. Immediately Arun used his intelligence and turned his Umbrella upside down and swam through the river and saved the dog. At that time he saw lovely colour fishes in the river. He also saw a beautiful rainbow. On reaching the shore when he unfolded the Umbrella he saw a lot of colour fishes falling on his basket. He becomes so happy that while saving the dog he completed his fishing also. He spared some fishes to the cat nearby and walked back home with the beautiful colour fishes and the pet dog.
author: Dr Devika Subramanian

title: Do Good: Good happens
text: Devika Subramanian Ramu went fishing on a rainy day. By that time he saw a dog struggling in the river. Using his intelligence he turned his Umbrella upside down and swam to save the dog. After saving the dog, Both witnessed the colourful fishes in the river. He also saw a colourful rainbow and reached the bank of the river along with the dog. title: The fishermen and the koi fish
text: The fishermen had caught lots of fish as the pond was about to dry. Now they are after a group of koi fish. They koi fish were planning on how to go to a safe lake. I have an idea but we will all have to work together. All the koi agreed. They all had different parts in the plan. One koi was searching for something that will help them get to a new pond and the other koi prepared for the long journey. The koi spotted two people standing near the pond with a bucket filled with water. The koi called his friends and told them to jump into the bucket before the people near the pond leave with it. Hurry up! we need to get to the market in ten minutes! The koi jumped into the bucket but were spotted. They were put in an aquarium. looks like jumping is not our skill. suddenly a pelican showed up and took all the koi in it's mouth. The pelican flew away before the people came. soon the pelican came to a big lake and threw the koi on the ground to eat them with his friends. When the koi got the chance they started moving and fell into the lake. The koi were happy that they were able to find a lake to live in. They loved the journey from the small pond to the big lake. Their little hearts were beating fast while they made the journey to the big lake. They found a new house and lived happily.

title: The meeting of mice
text: Once there was a family of mice. They would have been happy if there wasn't a cat in the same house. Whenever they went to the kitchen to take some food the cat would chase them. One day the family of mice holeded a meeting. The grandfather mice told, we should do something otherwise the cat will chase all of us. No one had any idea. At last the youngest mouse stood up with an idea. He said we should tie a bell around the cat's neck so we will get to know that cat is coming. Every body agreed. Finally the grand father told who will be brave to tie the bell around the cat's neck? moral: sometimes thinking smart is easy but hard to carry out short stories

title: The Tortoise And The Bird
text: A tortoise was resting under a tree, on which a bird had built its nest. The tortoise spoke to the bird mockingly, “What a shabby home you have! It is made of broken twigs, it has no roof, and looks crude. What’s worse is that you had to build it yourself. I think my house, which is my shell, is much better than your pathetic nest”. “Yes, it is made of broken sticks, looks shabby and is open to the elements of nature. It is crude, but I built it, and I like it.” I guess it’s just like any other nest, but not better than mine”, said the tortoise. “You must be jealous of my shell, though.” “On the contrary”, the bird replied. “My home has space for my family and friends; your shell cannot accommodate anyone other than you. Maybe you have a better house. But I have a better home”, said the bird happily.
author: Devaganga P.S

title: Simba - The lion
text: Once there lived a brave lion who dearly loved his people and took great care of them.His name was Simba.His wife was also very brave and her name was Nalia.They had two children, Mufasa and Aslan.Their people remained very happy. Simba had a huge army whose general was a wicked villainous tiger.He always wanted to be the throne. Once a huge army of another forest attacked Simba and his people.Their army had a pack of 2000 wolves, 1000 panthers, 1000 monkeys, 500 snakes, 500 rhinos, 5 tigers and some more elephants, foxes, eagles and vultures and there head was a large black panther.While Simba's army consisted of 1500 wolves, 750 panthers, 600 monkeys, 400 snakes, 200 rhinos, 2 tigers and some eagles and vultures. A massive war broke out.Then one day between the war, Simba's general went to the large black panther and made a deal with him that he would give him more military support and he after winning the war has to made him the king.The black panther agreed.So in between of the war the bad tiger send some troops to him.One day Simba and the black panther came in front of each other and started fighting.All the small wars stopped and saw the most amazing fight between a black panther and a lion.They both fighted fiercly for many hours and after some time the black panther slipped and fall into the valley but Simba caught hold of him and started pulling him upwards the black panther was astonished that his enemy is saving his life.But then suddenly the general saw a good chance to kill Simba so he ran faster and pushed Simba in the valley.Simba fell into the valley but holded the black panther by his foot.The tiger tried to pull up the black panther but as Simba was hanging on his foot he could not be able to pull him up.Seeing this Simba sacrificed his life and fell to his death.Then the black panther came up.The tiger laughed.The black panther got very angry and killed the tiger.The black panther was very sad for Simba's death.Then suddenly from the back he heard a sound.He turned back and saw Simba coming up.Actually when Simba was falling a 5 eagles came to rescue him.All the people were very happy to see Simba back.After that the war ended and Simba and the black panther become friends and never fought again.
