title: New Year Resolutions
text: Whenever a New Year starts, people make New Year Resolutions. What is a resolution? A resolution is a firm decision to do or not to do something. People resolve to start good things and stop bad habits. Let us look at a few common resolutions that people make. One of the common resolutions people make is to go to the gym or exercise daily. Some resolve to read more books. Some decide to go to bed early and get up early. Some decide to help their mom in the kitchen and with other household chores. Some decide to learn a new skill such as stitching, swimming, playing an instrument, painting, or a new language. Some decide to volunteer more and help more people. Some decide to eat more nutritious and less fatty foods. Some decide to be punctual and on time. Some resolve to climb the stairs instead of taking the lift. Some decide to write a journal or diary. Others make resolutions to stop bad habits like smoking. Some make resolutions but break them in a few days or months. Whatever resolutions you make, it is good to stick to them through the year. Happy New Year! Good luck to keep up your resolutions.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Jack and Joe
text: It was a sunny day. Two boys, Jack and Joe started their bikes to go to Mr. Sam’s home to help him in his garden. The children knocked on the door, but Mr. Sam was not there. They thought he might be working in his garden. Joe asked “Can we help you in your garden?” Mr. Sam said “Yes, why not”. Mr. Sam gave work to water the plants. When they were working on the garden their grandfather called them for dinner. “I guess it is time for dinner,” said Jack. Then they went home. When they came back to Mr. Sam’s house. They started watering the plants and had fun. Then suddenly they heard a noise and went to check it. They saw Mr. Sam lying on the ground. Jack said “Are you ok Mr. Sam”? Then Mr. Sam replied “No, I think my leg broke.” So Jack called for his grandfather to come and help. When he saw him in trouble, he took him to a hospital in a taxi cab. When Mr. Sam was sent to a hospital, where the children and the grandfather went with him. Then he was sent to the room to check what happened to him. After the checkup the doctor found out what happened to Mr. Sam. The doctor said, “He broke his leg and he will be unable to walk until it heals.” Joe asked “Can we see him?” The doctor said, “No, we are still putting bandages on his leg. So you can only see him tomorrow.” So the children and their grandfather went back home. When the children reached their home, they felt so sad that they wanted to help Mr. Sam in the garden. So they started making the garden beautiful everyday. When Mr. Sam became ok to walk, the children and their grandfather came to pick him up. When they reached his house, Mr. Sam was surprised about how his garden looked. And said “Thank you” to the boys.

title: Colours on Your Food Plate
text: "Hi Gerald, have you finished your lunch?" asked Gerald's dad James. "Yes, Dad," said Gerald. "Did your food plate have all the colours?" asked James. Gerald asked, "What do you mean by that Dad." James said, "A healthy food plate will have food items with green, yellowish-orange, reddish pink, blue, and violet colours." Gerald asked, "What is the relationship between the food and the colours?" James said, "Green stands for fruits and vegetables." "Yellowish orange stands for rice, wheat, bread, potatoes, and other starchy foods." "Reddish pink is for beans, meat, fish, and eggs." "Blue is for dairy products such as milk, curd, soya milk, and cheese." "Violet is for oils and low fat spreads," said James. Gerald said, "Ok Dad. I will make sure that my food plate has the colours blue, reddish pink, yellowish- orange, blue, and violet." James said, "Also make sure that the biggest share is green and the smallest share is violet." Note: The colours and the food items keep changing with times and countries. This is a sample food plate colour.

title: Neel's New Mother
text: It is the annual PTM day at school and Neel’s teacher has asked to see his mother. But nobody at school knows about Neel’s unusual secret. Will his secret be revealed? Hi! I am Neel and this is my new bike Gio. Papa gifted it to me last week. Papa is my best friend. Papa plays football with me and treats me to ice cream every weekend. We have a PTM at school today and Madam Joseph has asked to see my mother. She doesn't know about my secret. I have an idea. I can ask Lili aunty to be my mother. Lili aunty has come to our house today. She is very nice. She got lots of chocolates for me. "I am so happy without a mother. Why do people keep asking me about my mother?", Neel wonders. Neel and Papa drop Lili aunty at school and go to the playing arcade two blocks away. Neel, Papa and Lili aunty dress up nicely and get inside Papa's car and take the Blueburn Link Road to reach Neel's school. On the way to school, Neel is worried. If they get caught, Madam Joseph will know his secret and his favourite aunty will get scolded. Madam Joseph overhears this conversation. She smells something fishy but keeps quiet. Neel has never talked about his sister before. She remembers the names of his Teddy Bears and yet she can't recall a single instance where he talked about his sister. Lili Aunty goes to meet Neel's teacher. Suddenly her phone rings. "Hello! Mumma is busy, Tanya dear. She will call you back soon". Daddy is a little surprised after hearing the events of the day but eventually laughs when he hears how two adults conspired along with little Neel in executing his plan to fool Madam Joseph. After the PTM, they drop Lili aunty home and thank her for helping them protect their secret. On reaching home, Neel sees Daddy's red car and rushes inside. His Daddy has gotten cupcakes for him. Next morning, like every other day, Neel, Papa and Daddy have breakfast. Then they get ready and set out for their respective destinations. After the PTM Madam Joseph checks the student register. She calls up Daddy and he explains everything to her. The students enjoy the story a lot. Neel contemplates, “Maybe my secret is not so unusual after all. I think I can share it with Madam Joseph and all my friends. I can tell them that I do not have a Mother because I have a Daddy and a Papa. Maybe I should not have lied because nobody would treat me differently after all.“ Madam Joseph reads a story to the students that day. "Once upon a time there was a boy with two eyes, two ears, two cars, two legs, two hands, two fathers and a dog..." This book aims to bring into light the lives of the people belonging to the less talked about LGBTQ+ community of India. In today's world it is important that children get to learn to be accepting of all kinds of people. Hence representation of the LGBTQ+ community in children's literature is the need of the day.
author: Suvodeep Saha

title: The wise tree
text: In a deep forest a man was lost and was roaming around the forest at late night. He saw an old tree. Ah! Let me climb this tree, sit on it's branches and sleep for sometime. I will leave as soon as the sun rises. He said. Luckily, there was a ladder lying next to the tree, so he picked it up and started climbing the it. Soon it was morning, the man was in no mood of waking up or continue his journey. So he again slept. Suddenly, a voice called out to him. Who was that? The man swiftly woke up and was completely taken aback to see that the tree was talking! It is I, the wise old tree. The one you are sitting on right now. The voice said. And you should be finding out a way to go out of this forest as you see, there are many dangerous animals around here. And why should I listen to you? Asked the man. Let me tell you a story. Said the tree. A couple of years ago, there was this lazy bee. One day it had to go with it's friends to another forest. Unfortunately, it got seperated and now was lost. Then sat in one of my branches. I said to it: hey little bee, shouldn't you find a way where you can be with your friends sothat you can But the bee paid no heed of my advice. The next morning when I woke up the bee was missing! Then some other bees came to me and asked: hey, have you seen our friend? I said: I did. But when I woke up she was not there! She must be searching for you all! The bees searched and searched but he was no where to be found. Moral: Make sure that you finish your work at time.
author: Aarushi  konda

title: TALKING TIGER
text: Once upon a time, there was a pretty palace. It was so pink. It was having purple doors. There were purple flags on the top of the palace. The kingdom was very great. The king and the queen were having a beautiful princess. Her name was Priya. Priya got a new ball for her sixth birthday. She saw something white in the window, then she dropped her new ball on the floor. She goes closer to the door and went outside. She liked all the flowers and the garden. There, Priya saw a bunny and she tried to pet it, but it ran away. She followed the bunny, wherever it went. The bunny went to the deeper forest. It ran deeper and deeper and deeper….. She realized that she was lost. She went near the tree and began to cry. Then she saw a bush, it was crying as the same. She digs it out of the bush. It was a baby tiger. She saw the tiger’s paw was bleeding. She put a band-aid on the tiger’s paw. The baby tiger smiled at her and she smiled back. She said “I can’t speak tiger voice”, then she was surprised. The tiger said “ I know where the bunny is “ She asked “Where?”. The tiger said, “ At one tree trunk ”. She saw a tree with a hole. The tiger said, “we can’t go inside the tree trunk, because it's too small”. Finally, the bunny came out of the tree trunk. She asked the baby tiger “how to go out of the forest? “ Then the tiger said “You have to find the way by your own, the way out of the forest.” Then she learned carefully what the baby tiger has said. She soon found her castle. She went closer, closer and closer… Then she enjoyed her dinner. She remembered to meet the baby tiger in the forest. The baby tiger said its name, its name was “tigery". Priya and tigery were best friends forever. Moral: If you save creatures and people, they will become your friends and help you, if you need them.
author: Chandini Joshnaa R

title: Two proud goats
text: One person could pass through that bridge at one time. Once a goat started passing over that bridge. Another goat came from the other side on the same bridge. They stood in front of each other, right in the middle of the bridge. A goat said angrily - "Let me pass first. Second quote - "I have come so far, you go back. Let me cross first." Both stubbornly insisted. Then got entangled with each other because both the goats were foolish. The result was that both fell into the river and drowned. Education - Stupid people suffer harm by insistence.

title: Sharing is caring
text: Sam, Andrew, Lia and alia were best friends. They live in the same apartment They go to the same school. Andrew is the eldest in their group. Once their school is over they all meet up in the park and they play. One day It was raining very heavily so they decided to play in Andrew's house. The friends always play with cars. title: Clever Mouse.
text: Prasad Yadav There was a fat cat. And there was a little rat. The cat followed the rat. But the nimble rat always survived. One day the cat caught him in a place where it was difficult to escape. The rat started trembling with fear. Just then the rat thought of a solution. He started jumping and singing. The cat thought for a while and said yes.. The mouse said that he has adopted me. So you are my aunt. Hearing this, the cat caught him in his paws and fell in love.

title: The Mysterious Maze
text: Wake up Wake up Mom shouted “ Everyone, Wake up!Wake up!We are going to the maze today.” I said sleepily “ How are you so wide awake mom, didn’t you just wake up.” said Harry. Mom replied “ I woke up way before, who is going to pack all the food, water,games,sleeping bags, etc. It is going to take a long time to be out of that maze.Don’t forget there is a warm up session before the maze, now go and get ready quickly.” Dad and I get ready as fast as the speed of light and we start putting our luggage in the car. We had two heavy bags and one light bag which I was going to carry. Dad asked “ Why can’t we use suitcases, this is too heavy, it will drain my energy in a second.” Mom replied “ There is no flooring in the maze, it is grass. The wheels will break but don’t worry this is the brand new techno bags. It has four wheels and it will just follow us like a dog. It will be like we have nothing with us. We just have to command it by talking. My bag was the best, it was very light, it had mostly a water bottle and some other stuff. We left for the maze. Vrooooooooom There was a huge traffic jam because a truck had fallen down but luckily didn’t burst. The police said it would take two hours till the truck was removed so they switched on the great and wonderful;,extraordinary Google Maps. The lifesaver of the journey to the maze. We were going another route but there was traffic but normal traffic, no accident. It took a long time to go the highway. We decided that the next hotel we see we will eat there. When we entered the hotel we saw a familiar car. When we went inside we saw a friend of ours. We went and sat with them. They said that they were also going to the maze too. After we finished eating, my friend came in our car. The other car was following us. Then suddenly the other came and asked why we were going so slow. My dad said he didn’t notice that we were going slowly. We found that our car was punctured. We didn’t know what to do. We took out the spare tyre but we didn’t know how to fix it. Luckily there was a truck driver having some tea. We asked him but he said he would do it but… I am in a hurry. We told him that we would pay money then he fixed the tyre in two seconds but then we had another problem. Since we were driving with a flat tyre for so long the fuel level was very low. We told my friend to go on but they realised that they also have low fuel so this was a big problem. There was a fuel station nearby so they had to push one of the car to the station and fill it fully and drive the car back to the other and transfer some of the fuel and then they fill both the cars fully. Then suddenly when they were trying to start the car it was not switching on. Then they found out that the battery was dead. Luckily in the fuel station there was a jump start wire but there was no other car to jump start the car. Dad said “ How could this day get any worse.”Then it starts to rain heavily. “Why did I say that.” said Dad. My friend's dad asked if they had a car which we could use to jump start. They replied that they didn’t have a car or bike.Dad said “ How did they even come here and how will they leave. Do they live here, maybe.” Harry shouted “ Dad, there is a car coming here!” Dad asked the driver “ Is it ok if we use your car to jump start ours as the battery is dead.” The driver replied “No way, how am I supposed to trust you and I don’t even know you. Get lost” Dad said “ That person is in a very grumpy mood and he said no. I think he is having a bad day like us or maybe got black listed.” When Harry just spotted and shouted “ Daaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaad, there are a bunch of batteriesssssssssssssssssssssssss!!!!!” We took the batteries and jump started our car but because of the rain it was too dangerous. Harry said “ This is the worst day in my lifetime!” We saw a garage and we started our car there and we left at last. Dad said “There will be no more problems, we can go straight to the maze.” When they reached the maze they found out that their tickets had expired Dad said “ OH MY GOD. WE ARE NOT LEAVING THIS PLACE UNTIL WE DO THE MAZE, IT DOESN'T MATTER IF IT IS 6 O'CLOCK, GIVE ME NEW TICKETS!” Mom asked “ Are you done?” Dad replied “ Yes, that felt good.” Harry said “ You will be the best manager in the world.Let’s go now.” They went together in the gigantic maze. They got strapped up and took our luggages. Harry’s friend said “ We look like superheroes “ Harry said “ Let’s go superheroes, this maze is a piece of cake.” Dad said “ These are your weapons. In case you feel hot use this extraordinary fan and if you feel thirsty use this magical bottle of water, it can heal you you know and everything else in the bag which might look small it has so much in it.” The weapons were actually mini fans in case we got hot and their bags. Harry said “ you watched too much of Harry Potter.” Dad replied “ How did you know I watched Harry Potter?” Harry said “ You just told.” After 5 hours they were still in the maze. It was 11 o’clock and the maze was shut down. Harry said “ This is the first time in my life that I drank so much water, I think we drank like 4 litres and finished all the lemonade and food in the first half and I am starving and sleepy.” They all tried to find a way out but since all of them were so sleepy that everyone toppled over each other and slept. They were in a pile. They woke up in the hospital which had a nice bed and was like a proper 1st class hotel room. Harry said “ This turned out to be the best day of my life. “ Dad said “I thought you hated this.” Harry replied “ I do not regret saying that was the worst day of my life, it was just the worst time to my life, only that particular period but the hospital is the best. When I go home I sleep for the full day. “ All of us went home and just fell on to our bed and slept for the rest of the day.
author: Amitosh Obla

title: Bulbul went to School.
text: Prasad Yadav Bulbul was a fickle girl. She always kept on jumping around here and there. Sometimes she used to jump rope. Sometimes she used to play chainlet. But she also used to share mother's hand in household chores. Used to take care of younger sister. She used to prepare her younger brother and send him to school. She was also tempted to go to school when she saw other girls going to school. He also had his mind to study in school. She hid and watched the children reading. Once the teacher didi saw it. Call him to him and say "You too come to school. I will explain to your mother, father." After going to his house, the teacher explained to his mother, father that education is very important. title: WHY IS UNCLE PAJJI SOO FUNNY!!

Inside the shelfs and in the cowshed, But no one was able to find Uncle Pajji. BUT WHERE COULD UNCLE PAJJI BE? Well Uncle Pajji was in his banana plantation field. On that day Uncle Pajji came back and announced I AM VERY FUNNY!!! THE PEOPLE AND ANIMALS LOOKED AT HIM TRING TO SAY " WE KNEW THAT BEFORE UNCLE PAJJI!" " WE KNEW THAT BEFORE UNCLE PAJJI!"

title: Cock's whereabouts
text: Once upon a time, there used to be a lot of chickens in a village. The village child had harassed any one chicken. The cock got upset, he thought I would not make a sound the next morning. Everyone will keep sleeping, then everyone will understand my importance, and will not tease me. The cock did not say anything the next morning. All the people got up on time and started doing their work, on this, the chicken understood that no work stops without anyone. Everyone's work goes on. moral education: Do not boast. Your importance is revealed to people without informing them.
author: lavkant dwivedi

title: Plants
text: Me and dad were happily walking across the park until we saw few men chopping down a tree. I asked: Dad what are they doing? They are cutting the tree. Said dad. Why? I asked. I don't know. Said dad. But hey, do you know what will happen when trees are getting chopped off? Once trees get chopped off, we cannot breath. Trees also take out all the carbon dioxide, it is home to many birds, gives us fruits and a lot more! Then why are they chopping it off? Look, long ago there were trees everywhere. But humans had to cut the trees down to clear the way and make houses, buildings etc. Said dad. So we should plant more and more trees right? I asked. Yes, we should. Said dad. Did you know that 30 percent of the world is covered with trees? Make sure to plant more trees because unlike us they use carbon dioxide to breathe. How to plant a tree: Step 1: go to your garden or take a pot and fill your pot with soil. Step 2: take a seed and put it deep inside the pot. Step 3:give it water and make sure that it gets enough sunlight. Step 4: take care of it well
author: Aarushi  konda

title: First day at school
text: It was my first day at school. Mom is holding my hand and going with me. "I am grown up now" I said. "Lets Go...."! Mom is holding my hand tightly There are allot of students near the school. Some come by bus. Some by car. Some by rickshaw. Some come by bicycle and some by walking, like me. We reached the gate. Mom left my hand. She stopped at the gate. I had to go inside alone. I have very unknown faces around me. I walk one step. I take the second step. I look back. As I go on, mother looks small. Will she disappear? I run towards her. I don't think I have grown up. I hold her hand and said "Don't go!" Everyone has gone inside. Only I am outside. Teacher Didi comes outside. She smiles at me. I smile too. Mom said, "When you will come out I will meet you here only." I left her hand. She waved. I ran inside. After school gets over mom will meet me their.

title: The Traffic Light
text: One day there were a lot of cars and they caused heavy traffic jam. Because there was no traffic light. There were cars coming from all directions as the Traffic lights were not working, there were cars from right, left and middle that caused a lot of traffic. People got out from their cars and started chatting what to do. They all decided to make 3 volunteers representing three traffic signal lights. One representative for Red light to Stop the traffic, second representative for orange light to signal slow down and third representative for Green light signaling the traffic to move. The volunteers managed the traffic well and soon after sometime the traffic lights started working. Everyone was relieved. And traffic went smooth thereafter. So following rules always helps and makes situations better. We must follow rules.
author: Trisha Bhandoola

title: Venus has an odd day
text: I live with my mum, dad and older sister. It's our lunch time, there's oats, (yummy!) There is a big boy who takes care of us with many other dogs, his name is Robin. He takes us for walk, to the vet and more. I am a bloodhound, so whenever he loses things in the fields, I help him! Many times people come and buy the dogs from Robin and give him a card or some paper, (they call it cash.) He gives them the chosen dog after they pay. Today a boy and a girl came with their parents to pick a dog. They finally picked me! I was Robin's favourite dog, they couldn't take me! But Robin had to give me, he told them "He's a special dog, take good care of him." I am now with them for the past few months, they are a great family. I run with them, they feed me and I find their lost things. I still miss Robin, I want to see him. I will hopefully see him again.
author: Zoe
illustrator: Catherine Groenewald; Hashim Badani; Sumedha Sah; Sunando C; Suvidha Mistry; Terry E Gunn; Zoe

title: A Fun Day For Kiwa and Pops!
text: It was a hot sunny day. Kiwa and Pops were roaming on the hill. Kiwa had a hat of hay made on and Pops had a red cap. They wanted to do something fun... They had taken a book with them and sat under the big shady mango tree, with the sun shining brightly behind their back. They started by reading a book on elephants and facts about elephant. Kiwa asked Pops, ' Do elephants really have such trunks that can drink so much water?' Pops nodded. 'Cool!' cried Kiwa. 'Yep.' replied Pops. They finished the book and closed it. Next was playing with... 'Slippery Soap!' cried Kiwa. They washed the soap to make it slippery in the nearby bucket and also washed their own hands. 'Let's play!' said Pops. Pops squeezed the soap and WHOOOSH! It slipped out and flew into the air. 'Yay!' exclaimed Kiwa. The soap fell in their nearby barn's threshold. 'Let's do it again!' said Kiwa. As they tried it again a few more times, the mother goat and the baby goat from the barn came out and almost started chewing the books on elephants. But Kiwa came in from behind and grunted, 'Stop!' The goats were frightened. The book fell out of their mouths (they were sharing) and they ran away! So it was a funny day! Kiwa and Pops started laughing and taking their things, headed back home as the sun was setting. And the goats thankfully headed home to the barn through the window...

Tanisha wanted to stand there and cry. Aanya hugged her and started telling her “Let’s go!” No, no, no, I fell!” cried Tanisha. So what? Let’s go! You are my friend and I want both of us to finish this race. Let’s go! said Aanya. Tanisha started crying louder and said I made you lose! "Waaaaah!" Tanisha wailed! "We lose if we don’t finish, so let’s go! Don’t cry! Let’s finish!" said Aanya. And off they went. Hand in hand. Pausing for little hugs and wiping tears. Soon, they were giggling again. title: What is Gender?
text: Gender is a definition of society about what a man or woman should do. Society determines how a particular gender will behave and what roles and tasks they can take up. This gender definition extends to the personal and public lives of people. The common genders are male and female. Genders can also be referred to as man and woman, and masculine and feminine. Common roles of masculine genders are father, uncle, brother, nephew, husband, and more. Common roles of feminine genders are mother, aunt, sister, niece, wife, and more. The roles for each gender changes with time. Gender roles vary from society to society or from country to country. For example, In India, in the early 20 th century, women were mostly housewives But times have changed and now women are astronauts, engineers, pilots, doctors, and police officers. So, the gender roles have changed over time. Similarly, in the olden days, men were the sole breadwinners and took up various roles such as doctors, lawyers, and business owners. Now, women also work and equally share the economic burden of running a family. In the olden days, in some communities, men inherited all the property and women had no share in it. In recent days, this has changed and women also get an equal share of their parents’ home and land. Some gender stereotypes specify that a man should not cry. But, in the current times, men are also encouraged to show their emotions and cry. Similarly, nowadays, men also help in cooking and babysitting. Gender inequality or Gender discrimination is a situation in which men and women are not treated as equals or given equal opportunity. Gender inequality exists in access to education, jobs, and healthcare. We as citizens should strive to end Gender Discrimination.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Collective And Intelligent Behaviour In Insects
text: Bees are very efficient pollen finders. This is because they use a very efficient method. First, they send out scout bees who search for places with lots of flowers and then return to the hive. Once they return they perform a complicated series of wiggles called "The Wiggle Dance" which tells the worker bees where to go. Ants may seem small and not very smart but actually they are quite intelligent creatures. One example of their intelligence is the way they hunt slugs. Slugs have a sticky coating which most insects would get stuck in but the ants sprinkle sand on the slug so that the sticky coating is covered with sand and the slug can easily be killed and eaten. There even is a species of ant called the Paramedic Ant that heals its injured comrades and sends them back into combat. The ants which are too injured to heal push the ones trying to heal them away so that they don't waste time trying to heal the unhealable. Termite mounds may seem to be just big piles of dirt but in reality they are that and much more. Termite mounds are cleverly built with a fungi garden that helps break down wood, a hatchery/nursery which houses eggs and young termites, a royal chamber for the queen termite, and even a ventilation system to keep the mound cool. Another interesting fact about termites is that to make sure the that the walls of the mound don't get too dry some termites form a water brigade. They form this by lining up and transferring water from a source from one termite's mouth to another and repeating this till the water reaches the mound. Some insects like wasps plan far ahead of time to provide food for their unhatched eggs. For example some wasps kill a caterpillar, or any other small creature of that size, and then lay their eggs in it. When the eggs hatch the larvae will eat the dead animal and make their way out.

title: Birds That Sing Their Name
text: Imagine having our names being based on the shape of our nose, our hairstyle, our body colour, or the way we speak! It would be funny. Can you think of the names you would be called? This is exactly what people who study birds do when they name the birds they see. These scientists, called ornithologists, name birds by the features they see. Ornithologists observe birds. They see the colour of their body feathers, shape and size of their body parts and their food habits and they name them. For example, a Black-winged Stilt is called so because its wings are black in colour and it has long legs that resemble stilts. A Spotted Dove is a dove with a lot of spots on its body. A Green Bee-eater, is so called because, well, it is green and eats honeybees and other insects. Some get their names because of the way they sing. Take the Asian Koel. Have you ever listened to them? The female Koel gives out a bubbling call, and the male birds call Koo… oo …Koo.. oo and sometimes Ko.. el … Ko.. el … Ko.. el. And that’s why we call them Koel! When anyone gets their name based on the calls and songs they produce, these names are called onomatopoeic names. Can you think of an example? Now let’s explore some birds that call out their own names. If you listen to a Common Cuckoo, you will know why this bird is called, well, a cuckoo! When it calls, it has two notes which sound like... Cuk …koo… Cuk …koo… Cuk …koo… Have you seen this pretty looking bird called Eurasian Hoopoe? Hoopoe has got a far-sounding repetitive Upupup…upupup…upupup…. Hence, the Latin name of this bird is Upupa epops. In many Indian languages crows are named after their call. In Hindi they are called Kauwa, In Tamil they are called Kaakka, In Telugu they are called Kakki, In Assamese they are called Kaauri, In Bangla they are Kak. All resembling their call Ka ww… ka ww… ka ww. In Hindi, Grey Francolin is called Teetar, since they give out a loud and repetitive call - K a- tee -tar…. k a- tee -tar… k a- tee -tar. In Telugu, Red-wattled Lapwings are called Uththuthhi which sounds like their call. Uth.. uth …ut hii thi..… Uth..uth… uthii thi..…, they go! In Tamil, the Common Hawk-Cuckoo is called Akka Kuyil since their repetitive call sounds like Akka.. Akka.. Akka …. Akka! Which means elder sister in Tamil. Most of us surely have nicknames given by our school mates and friends. And so do birds! For example, birdwatchers call the Red-wattled Lapwing as the Did-he-do-it bird, since its alarm calls sounds like Did-he-do-it? Did-he-do-it? Pity-to-do-it? Common Hawk-Cuckoo is also called the Brain Fever bird as their ceaseless call sounds quite like saying Brain Fe ver…brain fe ver….brain fe ver! When the Indian Cuckoo calls, the words sound like O ne more bo ttle… one more bo ttle… Of what, is your guess! The Puff-throated Babblers’ calls sound like I’ll beat you…I’ll beat you… Bird calls can be funny that way. The Brown-cheeked fulvetta calls are written as Daddy...chocolate..Daddy... chocolate. Daddy give me chocolate. Go out and listen to the songs and calls of the birds around you. Can you hear what they’re saying? Can you make sentences of their sounds? Write these down in your notebook and share with your friends. When you see these birds later you will remember their names!
author: Panchapakesan Jeganathan

title: Amelia's Wonderful Glasses
text: Why can't we go to the ice cream shop, Mom?" asked Amelia. "Because it is closed," explained her mother. "What about the park?" persisted Amelia. "That's also closed," mother responded. "I don't like this town! Everything is closed!" exclaimed Amelia. Amelia went to her room, but none of her toys interested her. She searched high and low for a new adventure... but there didn't appear to be anything fun to do in the entire house! Bored, she laid down in the garden, when a shiny object on the ground suddenly caught her attention. She got down on her knees and elbows and carefully crawled across the lawn, following the little specks of color that were hidden beneath the flowers. She reached out her arm and there they were! A pair of very big, round glasses covered in colorful thread and shiny buttons, with a yellow feather in the center. "What strange glasses!" said Amelia as she put them on, and in that very moment...Everything changed! The flowers transformed into birds with long beaks. Her house — an enormous yellow castle! And her mother, who greeted her at the door, was fluttering a pair of big, rainbow-colored wings in place of hands. That day Amelia discovered a great secret: she knew that to create any adventure she wanted, all she had to do was put on her wonderful glasses. Now it's your turn! Use your imagination to create your own wonderful glasses with the materials that you find around your home.
author: Veronika Dzirkal

title: Tinku and his musical world
text: One day little Tinku's parents got tickets to a music concert. Tinku along with his parents visited the Rajdhani auditorium in Old Delhi. He was fascinated with the instrumental music played during the concert. One instrument that caught his interest was the harmonium. Few days later Tinku visited his Grandparents who lived in Chandigarh. In the evening he heard his Grandfather play the harmonium. He sneeked into his Grandfathers room and quietly observed his Grandfather play with the keys. After his grandfather left the room, he quietly moved near the harmonium and tried to play it. He was fascinated with the sounds coming from within. After dinner Tinku went to bed. In his dream he imagined himself surrounded by instruments And ready for a concert where he was going to perform in front of the audience. Next morning Tinku told his mom about his dream. He looked very excited and requested mom to enroll him in a music class. After returning to Delhi,one weekend Mom took Tinku to a music school. He was very excited about the classes. Tinku then got a opportunity to take part in a talent hunt competition conducted by his school. Tinku won the competition and was appreciated by his teachers and the Principal. His happiness knew no bounds. He went home and promised his mother that someday he will play even better in the same Rajdhani auditorium.

title: O Rain Come
text: It was a hot summer afternoon. Lilato fanned herself. “If only it could rain,” her brother, Mayamiko, said. It was too hot to let the children play outside. Lilato heard it first. It sounded like a stone bouncing on the roof of the house. Lilato looked at Mayamiko but he didn’t look at her. Ndo-ndo! She tiptoed to the window and looked up at the sky. The sky was grey, almost black in colour. Lilato started to sing the song her best friend, Mwansa, had taught her. Wemfula isa isa O rain come Twangale na mainsa So we can play in the rain Wemfula isa isa O rain come Twangale na mainsa So we can play in the rain Lilato sang, rubbing her fingers together. Ndo-ndo-ndo-ndo-ndo-ndo! More raindrops fell from the sky. “Maya! It’s raining!” Lilato yelled. “It’s raining!” They ran outside the house. Mama was already putting buckets around the house to collect rainwater. They ran to the road in front of their house and joined other children. A chorus of wemfula isa isa twangale na mainsa, was heard all over the neighbourhood. The sky opened and poured more rain, joining into the music of the day.
author: Fiske Serah  Nyirongo

title: Yapo Saves The Day
text: Yapo loves to play with his soccer ball! He often tries dribbling tricks with his dad. An elastico, a rainbow flick and even...... a bicycle kick! Yapo is the star of the Under 6 Team of Tino Football Club. He is quick and nimble on the field. Yapo scores most of the goals for his team. Yapo, however, does not like to pass the ball. Coach Tazi often reminds Yapo to share the ball with his teammates. One day, Tino Football Club was playing Kuma Football Club. Yapo tried many times to score but the Kuma team was too strong. By half-time, Kuma was leading 2 – 0. Coach Tazi gave the team a stern pep talk, ‘Play together and pass the ball to whoever is free! Yapo, pass the ball!’ When the second half began, Yapo was made to sit on the bench. His teammates were a little scared to play without him, but they remembered to play together. Nat scored the first goal for the Tino team. ‘WOOHOO!’ cheered the crowd. Three minutes before the end of the game, Lindi scored the team’s second goal! ‘LADUMA!’ they shouted. Coach Tazi called Yapo back into the game, ‘The score is now 2 – 2. Take us home, boy! Remember to play with your teammates!’ Lindi kicked the ball to Nat, who passed it to Yapo. Yapo dribbled between two opponents and when he was about to take a shot, he spotted another Kuma player running towards him. Yapo saw Lindi following close behind, remembered Coach Tazi and passed the ball to her. Lindi turned towards the goal, and took her best shot! ‘GOAL!’ cried Coach Tazi. The Tino crowd went wild with joy as Lindi’s teammates ran to hug her! Yapo was very happy that his team had won 3 – 2. But he was a little disappointed that he had not scored any goals. ‘Congratulations for a mighty comeback!’ beamed Coach Tazi to his team. ‘Well done, Yapo, for passing the ball to Lindi.’ ‘You may not have scored a goal today, but you certainly helped your team to win. Well done, son!’ smiled Dad, as they walked home together.
author: Rujeko Moyo

title: 2020- A Verse Year
text: I hope you all have had an awesome winter holiday? And managed to keep illness and fears at bay!! Happy new year. Yes, a new decade. A new Year It been so cold all across the world. Brrrr….. I know,I am a a bit late But, what to do winters make us all HIBERNATE!!! Thanks to Corona still going steady, I got delayed in getting our news capsule ready!! New restrictions, New lockdown rules…. No offices and no schools Still wearing masks Washing and sanitizing has been a task Social distancing is the new norm As the virus is still in Top Form Its been more than a tea-cup in a storm What a year, it has been. Can anybody tell me? if like this anybody has ever seen? January 2020 was the beginning of the new year We all rejoiced as this was a leap year What fun it will be, we thought To have an extra day To bask in the sun and play!! The world woke up to news of A new "Sars Virus" Aha, we said It's far away in China It can’t dare and scare us We had our jackets and coats on Picnics and bonfires in our lawns And everywhere we looked People were celebrating Sankranti and Kite Flying Pongal and Magha And Jallikattu (bull fights) were still debating Republic day parade We all watched with bated breath Our defence forces were in full gear They do protect us with sometimes just bare And the stunts on bikes Were such a brave dare The fog and haze Could not keep us away Colourful and Flamboyant State-wise "JHAANKIS" Like every year Managed to enthral and amaze us February was to be the month To celebrate love But, the world started to take a bow To the Sars Covid 19 That was making headlines US President Donald Trump Came to India for Trade talks And as we were grappling with it Covid started to on our doors knock Kerala was the first state to report This deathly infection No one it seemed was safe From this dreaded infraction The year end exams That are our annuals Seemed as tough as ever And the board children Complained that hard work Was perennial Annual Budget was presented by Our Honourable Finance Minister To have all understand the nitty-gritty So, we can all pay tax I am sure its difficult to administer March was a time for schools in India To shut down for summer holidays But, before that Corona decided To snatch that joy away. Holi a festival of colours This time had to take a detour There were whispers in the air That a mask and sanitizer Were much needed for our care Europe in the midst of the Virus Started to throb And going out in groups Was considered more deadly than The dreaded mob India decided to have a Bharat Bandh A day to reconcile and reckon A day to stay home To reflect and to confine The evening reverberated with Clangs of music We clapped and greeted To all our front line workers Who were working hard Inspite of all the risks 24 th March was a red letter Our beloved P.M announced A nation wide lockdown On hearing this, Some celebrated While some just broke down April came and we were still off school No new books, no classes Aha how cool But not for long This did not last This super nice song We were introduced to zoom and teams And we could meet our friends And mates While the screens beamed Teachers grappled to innovate With new technology And we all could study From the comforts of home In our pajamas all cosy Who were working from home And while they slogged online We were still engaged in Online tomes. The month was a long arduous battle We had to cook, clean and take care of our cattle We all chipped in While mumma cooked Daddy cleaned. Sour dough breads and Banana cakes Were all made at home World-wide they became The king of bakes!! We learnt to eat healthy We learnt to enjoy our time It was quite a while And it purely was sublime The skies were clear The roads still And we all spotted rare birds Some even a hornbill May brought the boredom Of losing out on our freedom No more summer holidays When we could swim all day Or with friends play We sat at home And started to find solace In Books Evenings were spent Playing board games That were gathering dust In some corner and crook We got tired of screens And we eagerly awaited To run and cycle And hear the ice cream wallah scream Tokyo Olympics 2020 were postponed For the first time due to a pandemic Oho no, we all said This is just EPIC As the date for it next year Is really unknown June was the first phase Of Unlocking People decided to go back to Their home towns And migrants decide to do the walking Back to their villages While they trudged Good Samaritans did the rest They stood up to give them the best There was pandemonium As we didn’t know Should we travel to meet Our grand parents? Or do a virtual greet and bow!! July was when people started Slowly and Steadily Stepping out The roar of the engines and hum of The cars and trains Were heard hooting aloud The sky became dark with monsoon clouds But, we still could not go down To jump in puddles Or sail away our paper boats We sat at home and caught A double rainbow The gumboots and raincoats The umbrellas all were Still in the shadow Schools re-started And books came home We realized its so much fun To be in school, it aint a bore August, the month of our Independence Did make us less dependent Some started going to office While some were still working from home And were their own bosses Raksha Bandhan and Janmashtami Were all celebrated on Zoom We saw our family online And Krishna came home Places of worship Were still shut shop But we all prayed fervently And it was getting diffcult to cope September we started hearing About the new vaccine We all hoped this year Santa came early And give us the medicine Doors were opening up Shops returning to life The restaurants were getting decked up And we all were ready to face this strife October welcomed Maa Durga And we hoped, she the protector Will take the form of Kali And destroy this Corona Asura Pandals did live streaming And bhog and kichuri were Home delivered on pre-booking Halloween was a no-go And trick and treats were a no show November was the month of elections Choosing a president for US of A One of the most powerful nations Election in Bihar too was talked about And people taking sides Deciding on the winner Was all rampant Diwali was ushered in The festival of lights A festival to celebrate A festival so bright. The AQI worsened Skies were engulfed in smog To bring much needed joy Say “NO TO FIRECRACKERS “ Said every girl and boy! Thanksgiving was a time to reflect And staying at home was the wisest Families thanked first responders And our health workers Who stood up and fought Daily, against this adversity December came and brought with it The first ray of hope The vaccine arrived in United Kingdom And we all cheered and said WELCOME Margaret Keenan was the first one to Get the immunity shot Covishield or Covaxin Both will be transported In super cold conditions And will be closely guarded The year end we laid out our tree Mistletoes and Wreaths Cookies and milk for Saint Nicholas Were laid out to decorate We all wrote to Santa Pleading for a Xmas miracle To be able to meet and hug To let us all be free The year has been difficult The year has been tough And we all did our best Even though, sometimes it was rough The vaccine has reached India And we all can be rewarded But, a bit more patience and caution Is all that is still needed!! The journey has taught us New lessons Be not in a hurry To forget them To be responsible To be kind To help each other And serve humankind I hope, I managed to Engage you With this news capsule We must fasten our seatbelts And welcome 2021 With a hope and prayer heartfelt As, I bid adieu to you Its been great seeing you all Albeit virtually But, I will be back soon With my next news episode Till then stay safe and stay home

title: Dragon Fruit
text: The Dragon Fruit is also known as Pitaya or Strawberry Pear. It grows on a climbing cactus plant. The fruit has origins in Mexico and Central America. Ripe Dragon fruit has dark pink leathery skin and green scaly spikes on top of the skin. Some varieties have yellow or red skin. When you cut open a ripe pink Dragon Fruit, you can see a white pulp with tiny black seeds. This Dragon fruit is the most common variety. Red-skinned Dragon fruits have a red pulp, and yellow-skinned fruits have a white pulp. The pulp or flesh is juicy and sweet and tastes like Kiwifruit or Pears. The pulp is scooped out of the skin and used to prepare dishes such as smoothies, fruit salads, ice cream, and juices. The skin is not edible. Can you see the Dragon Fruit pieces on top of the fruit salad shown here? Dragon fruits are rich in Vitamin C and other antioxidants, and Iron. Are you planning to eat a Dragon Fruit now?

title: Kamal Visits Gagan
text: He lived in a village, and the hustle and bustle of the city were very strange to him. The autos rushed by. Many people went on scooters. The boy on the cycle ringed his cycle bell. Tring! Tring! "Oh. It so noisy in the city," said Kamal to himself. Kamal could not resist comparing this city with his village. In his village, chickens walked on the road. Bullock carts carried people and moved at a slow speed. He was awakened from his thoughts by a car that whizzed by. Vroom! Vroom! "One day I must buy a car and drive in this city," thought Kamal. Kamal looked around for his friend Gagan who will be waiting for him. Gagan was from Kamal's village. But, Gagan came to the city two years back for a job. On the way, Kamal saw a horse pulling a buggy or carriage. One man was sitting in the buggy. Kamal had read in books and seen pictures of men who pull rickshaws. "At least, this practice of men pulling other men was stopped several years ago," he thought. There is so much noise pollution in the cities. Kamal closed both his ears with his fingers. "Is that Gagan? Looks so much like him," thought Kamal. He walked towards the man who looked like Gagan. Wow, Gagan! Hello, Gagan! Kamal ran towards Gagan and hugged him. Kamal and Gagan walked to Gagan's home. They recollected their old memories of the village. Gagan shared his stories of living in the city. They laughed together.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Friends, A Poem
text: 1.Friends How good to lie a little while And look up through the tree! The sky is like a kind big smile Bent sweetly over me. The sunshine flickers through the lace Of leaves above my head, And kisses me upon the face Like mother, before bed. The wind comes stealing o'er the grass To whisper pretty things; And though I cannot see him pass, I feel his careful wings. So many gentle friends are near Whom one can scarcely see, A child should never feel a fear, wherever he may be.
author: Akil  Ramanathan

title: Tuna The Porcupine
text: Tuna the porcupine was very lonely and sad. For even though she had a number of friends in the Evergreen forest she could not play with them. For whenever she would go to play with her friends in the park her quills would pierce the skin of her friends. Tuna decided to remain alone most of the time. It was then that Dina the mouse decided to talk to her. "Don't worry dear everything will be fine". Dina said after hearing Tuna's story. Dina could sew very well. She stitched a shirt for Tuna. "Now all your quills will be covered and no one will get hurt anymore." Dina said to Tuna. All was well again. Tuna would wear her shirt and go to the park to play with her friends and no one would get hurt anymore.

title: The Boy and the Fish
text: Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Avish in a small town. But, he had no friends. Neither in school, nor in the whole town. There was a river nearby, to the left of Chacha Rajgandha's house. He sat there. He felt calm for a moment. But, after some time he saw a big fish trapped in a net. He took it out with all his might and strength. And, the fish jumped on his lap. The fish was free again. It went in the water. It also showed its tricks to the boy who saved him. But, Avish was sad when the fish was leaving. He said,'' Remember me! I'll come everyday''., and the fish made a big noise to his new friend as if to say, ''See you Soon!''. Next day, when Avish was reading a book about fish in school, Naina said,'' Are you well?'' ''Why? What Has happened?'', Avish asked ''Nothing, you and a book, umm.., doesn't suit you. And, why in the whole world would you read a book about fish?'',Naina asked. ''It is because of my friend.'', Avish said. ''You have a friend?'', Naina said. ''Yes!'', Avish replied. ''Who is it?'', Naina asked again.'' Avish told her everything about the fish. He also told her about various types of fish. He said, ''Come with me!'' Of course, Naina was amazed after seeing the fish. Naina told the whole class, and Avish had loads of friends. But, he would never forget the fish who made him lucky and always visited 'Candy', the name of the fish, in the evenings. ﻿

title: Adventure Around South Africa
text: Chanri and Boipelo are going on an adventure around South Africa. Their journey starts in Kimberley, in the Northern Cape. In Kimberley you will find the Big Hole! Tjoeke puff toot-toot, they travel to Cape Town in the Western Cape. Chanri and Boipelo pick juicy grapes at the farms. Tjoeke puff toot-toot, then they head off to Bhisho, in the Eastern Cape. The two friends have fun at the Elephant Park! Tjoeke puff toot-toot, they pass through the Free State. They admire all the pretty roses blooming in Bloemfontein. On to Mahikeng, in the North West. The train slows down to meet Rina the rhino at the National Park. Then our friends speed on to Polokwane, in Limpopo. Toot-toot toot-toot! They're running late, so the train doesn't stop in Johannesburg, Gauteng. From the train they see many cars and people in this busy city of gold. Tjoeke puff toot-toot, they travel to Emalahleni, in Mpumalanga. They visit a big coal factory to get fuel for their train. Chanri and Boipelo end their train journey in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal. They share sweet bananas with their friends, and talk about their adventure around the country. Do you remember the provinces and their cities?

title: The Little Farmer
text: Chimi was roaming with his mother in the vegetable market. He saw lots of vegetables around and was very curious to know how they grow. He looked around and was pleased to see green capsicums, red tomatoes, purple brinjals and white radish. All the vegetables reminded him of a colorful rainbow. Chimi said "Mumma, Why do we buy vegetables from the market? Can't we grow them at home"? His Mumma said, "It is not an easy task to grow vegetables at home. Farmers put in a lot of effort. I don't have so much time to look after a plant. It needs lot of care and love, just like a little baby ". While buying green leafy vegetables, Chimi asked "Mumma, Is it possible to grow green vegetables at home "? Mumma replied, "Yes of course". Chimi asked curiously, "Mumma, Which plant can be grown fastest at home"? Mumma said the fenugreek (methi) plant grows in a week. Chimi said "Lets grow it at home. I promise to take care of the plant. I will reduce my TV time and look after the plant." Chimi asked, "Mumma, how do we grow a fenugreek plant"? Mumma replied, "We have to sow seeds in the soil. Then, we need to water the plant daily. Roots suck up minerals and transport them through the stem to all the other parts of the plant. Air, water and sunlight help the plant to grow". Chimi insisted "Mumma, I want a sapling too. I want to take it home and grow it. Once it grows, we will remove its leaves and cook a yummy meal for Papa, you and me". Mumma said "Ok, we will sow fenugreek seeds. But you should be patient enough and wait for it to grow." After returning home, Chimi changed his clothes, ran to his mother and said "Give me a pot, soil and fenugreek seeds". Together, they sowed fenugreek seeds in the little pot they had. Mumma said, 'Chimi, Promise me that you will water it daily. Chimi promised that he will. The next morning, Chimi got up and ran to see if the seeds have grown into a plant. He did not see any plant. Disappointed, he ran to his mother and cried "Mumma, There is no plant yet. When will I get to see the plant"? Mumma said "I had told you. You should wait for nature to do its magic". Five days passed. The plant had still not grown. Chimi was disappointed. He put extra water and mixed the soil and seeds with mud. Sadly, the plant was spoilt. Chimi started crying loudly. His parents came to him and saw the mess that he had made. Chimi hugged them and started sobbing. His Papa hugged him back and said "We had told you, a plant needs a while to grow. Just like you cannot be an adult in one day. You should let it take its own time". Chimi realized his mistake. He apologized and said "Papa, Mumma, Can we grow another plant? I will look after it, just like how you and Papa look after me". Chimi's parents helped him sow seeds in a new pot and explained to him how much water he needs to put, and how sunlight helps a plant to grow. They also gave him a book to read on how a plant grows. Every morning Chimi would water the plant. Many days passed, it started showing tiny leaves. Chimi was so happy to see it grow. Soon it grew big. He was finally able to pluck its leaves. He ran to his mother, and requested her to make lunch using his home grown fenugreek leaves. Chimi's mother prepared a delicious sabji and served it to him. Chimi ate happily and hugged his mother and said "I now know that it takes patience to grow vegetables at home. I will now take up gardening as my new hobby. I will grow tomatoes too". Chimi was happy at the thought of having his own home grown vegetable garden and him becoming THE LITTLE FARMER.
author: Aryansh Dhume

title: Amara and the Magic Tree
text: Amara was walking through the park. The trees in the park were green and healthy. But, there was one tree that was brown and dry. "This tree needs water," said Amara to herself. She watered the tree and it came to life with new growth. It was a magnificent green tree. Then, the tree spoke! "You watered me and brought me back to life," said the tree. "I'm a magic tree, I shall grant you three wishes." Amara made her first wish. "I wish for a red bicycle," she said cautiously. Abracadabra! A red bicycle appeared. She made her second wish after thinking for a few moments. "I wish for a radio," said Amara. Abracadabra! A radio appeared. Amara made her third wish. "I wish for pink crystal earrings," she said happily. Abracadabra! Pink crystal earrings appeared. The magic tree said, "You have everything that you wanted." Amara smiled, "Yes I do, but those things were not for me." The magic tree looked confused. "The bicycle is for my older brother. He outgrew his bicycle. The radio is for Dad. His radio broke. The earrings are for Mum. She loves fancy earrings," explained Amara. "And they will all share with me!" she added.

title: How the Toad Got Its Skin
text: Mod the toad was tired of living in water. "Be careful," said the turtle. "Your skin will dry out." But Mod was curious. She hopped away. She looked all around. She met a purple chameleon next to a puddle of water. The chameleon started turning pink! Mod jumped away. Then she saw a hyena starting a fire. The fire spread around Mod. She was afraid. The fire burned her skin. She jumped back, into the puddle. But her skin was already full of blisters. Mod found a home under a rock. Her new skin was dry and rough. Now only frogs have smooth skin and live near water.

title: Journey into the Skies
text: It was a warm summer afternoon. I should have been playing with my friends, but Mom doesn’t allow us out, anymore! She always says, ‘Coronavirus’ and ’lockdown, whatever that means. Her answer is always ‘NO’ every time we ask to go out and play. It’s not fair! How can Mom expect a nine-year-old boy to stay at home? What happened to “Go play out in the fresh air.”? I watched wistfully as the birds sang, and the leaves rustled in the soft breeze that was hitting my face through the open window. I was desperate to meet my friends! The urge to go out was so tempting, just to run around in the fields, to sit by the bank of the lake, watching how the birds devoured the seeds… I sighed and walked to the out of my room and went to my elder brother, Jason’s room. He was typing something on his laptop. “What are you doing?” I asked, sitting on the bed “Some school stuff,” he replied in-between the vigorous Clickety Clack “It’s a holiday!” I said, flabbergasted. “Why will the school give you work to do?” “It’s a project,” he said, matter-of-factly. “Don’t you just feel like running away somewhere? I’m so bored of staying in the house all the time!” I complained. He smiled vaguely at the screen. “I’ve been thinking about it as well, and I have an idea,” he grinned. He stood up from his chair, walked over to the door and closed it. Then, he whispered, “Here’s the plan.” The next day, we started working towards our plan. Jason collected old, tattered clothes. I began working right away, carefully cutting each cloth in the shapes as Jason instructed. Our tables were soon laden with piles of colorful cloth pieces. “This should be enough,” Jason announced. “All we need now is something for the basket.” The plan was finally coming together. Despite being faded and almost falling apart, our old, plastic ride-on car was chosen to serve as a convenient basket. Once we put it all together, Jason and I were quite impressed with ourselves.. It was marvelous engineering by us, with a ride-on car at the bottom, ropes holding the car to the balloon. The remarkable thing was the box in the centre to hold the fire that actually powered the entire machine. “Okay, no time to waste!” Jason exclaimed, and we jumped into our newly made hot-air balloon standing out in the lawn. Jason pulled out some matches, and lighted the wood in the aluminum box. The hot-air balloon slowly filled up with the smoke from the fire as we sat in the car basket – all set to fly! As we rose into the air, Mom came running out. “What do you two think you’re doing?” She shouted as we rose higher and higher. “Escaping the Coronavirus!” Jason shouted back. Mom shouted something back, but her voice faded. “I think she asked us to put out that fire, like we really would.” Jason remarked. We stopped talking for a while, and admired the view. I leaned slightly over the edge, and I could see tiny little dots, running around a city that looked the size of a large dog. “Look, at the cars down there, just like ants!” I exclaimed to Jason. “Oh, what a great discovery,” he replied sarcastically, rolling his eyes. “Of course we can see the cars, you dummy!” As we rose higher and higher, the air seemed to become less, and I had to take big gulps of it to satisfy my lungs. It also seemed unusually cold, as though winter had arrived early. “Oh no, I didn’t plan for this,” Jason said, suddenly hugging me. “What?” I asked, pushing him away. “The higher we get, the colder it gets! We need to stay warm!” He replied, shivering. We huddled together as the hot-air balloon stopped rising higher. Off in the distance, I saw gigantic fluffy, white clouds, heading towards us. They looked very welcoming, but I knew that they were just water vapor. Soon, the cold was unbearable. My lips froze. I couldn’t feel my fingers or toes. I was getting worried. What if I get frostbite? What about hypothermia? All of this, only to get away from home for a short while. Suddenly a bright light fell on my eyes and they snapped open. I was in my cozy bed, shivering as my father had opened the windows and let the chilled breeze into my room. I looked around at my alarm clock, which read ‘7:00’, so I pulled the blanket over my head and went back to sleep, hoping to continue my journey in the hot-air balloon.
author: Ameya Karaba

title: The Rainbow Cover-Up
text: Why was Bhanwari so worried? Ma brought her ten new books for school, But Bhanwari forgot to cover them. Oops! “Look here, didi,” said Bablu. He had a way out of this bind. He had cooked up a brilliant idea in his mind. There, he pointed at the Peepal tree. “What?” wondered Bhanwari, and looked up to see. Stuck on its branches were three rainbow kites. Violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red flashed in the light. “Well done, Bablu. We can cover two books with one kite, So that’s three kites to cover six books.” “But Bablu, don’t forget, there are more. Six of ten are sorted. But what about the other four?” Just then they heard a call from the street, “Peanuts, peanuts, a piping hot treat!” “Oh, Moongfali Mamu!” called Bhanwari. “I need some help. Please help me, look! Do you have some paper to cover my school books?” “Here you go, little one,” said Moongfali Mamu, handing them two newspaper sheets. “Bablu, one newspaper sheet will cover two books. Two will cover four! Six plus four equals ten. We don’t need any more!” The next day, her friends asked, “Where did you find these rainbow books, Bhanwari?” Bhanwari said, “It’s the magic of Moongfali Mamu and a rainbow tree.”

Sally was surprised that this wild cheering did not matter him at all. Then Sally's friend told her that the boy is Benny and he is deaf as well as a good badminton player. Sally was amazed, How can a deaf boy play so well? He cannot listen to the instructions that a coach gave the players. But Sally realized that his motivation was the action of the wild cheering his friends gave him. Sally's friend also told him he has learnt badminton through sign language. Throughout the camp Sally observed the Benny's game and his normal behavior with his friends. Last day of the camp dawned with great excitement everywhere. The best players name will be announced. Sally was confident that she will win, but when the winner was announced Sally was disappointed since Benny was declared the winner. title: Living or Non-Living Things?
text: Every day, we see a lot of things around us. But, are they living or non-living things? How can you know that? Living things eat, grow, breathe, move, reproduce, and respond to their environment. Non-living things do not eat, grow, breathe, move, reproduce, and do not respond to their environment. For example, in the picture, the girl is a living thing. The bowl, spoon, and ribbons are non-living things. Living things are made up of biological cells. Non-living things are made up of chemical elements and compounds. Living things digest their food and excrete the waste. Non-living things do not excrete waste. Examples of living things are human beings, animals, birds, trees, and plants. Few examples of non-living things are books, tables, shoes, brushes, and clothes. Some non-living things will exhibit a few qualities of living things. Still, they are non-living things. For example, the Sun and a self-driving car can move. But, they do not give birth to young ones like living things. So, they are not considered living things. Similarly, a block of snow may grow in size due to more snowflake deposits. But, snow is not a living thing as it cannot move by itself. Activity 1: Name the 2 living and any 8 non-living things in this picture? Answer in the next page. Answer: The girl and the woman are the 2 living things. Plate, glass cups, flower vase, table, bed, pillow, sweater, gloves, photo frame, and earrings are non-living things. Activity 2: Name any 5 living things in the picture. Name any 5 non-living things in the picture. Answer in the next page. Answer: The 5 living things are the dog, man, woman, girl, and the trees. The 5 non-living things are car, basket, blanket, logs or sticks of wood, and dress the people wear.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: I wonder..........
text: "I saw a goat in a field. It was black in colour but there was some white colour on its leg. It had four legs, a bushy short tail, two long long ears and two horns. It was eating grass. When I touched it, it did not attack me. I think it is a pet. It was very very soft. It said “maaaaaaaaah, maaaaaaaah” when I gave it some grass." Aahanaa "I wonder......can it be my friend? Can it eat chicken and fish like me? I wonder if it is a boy or a girl? Can it understand my language? I wonder how it looked when it was a baby? I wonder if all goats are black or white or they can be of different colours?" Aahanaa "I saw an anthill in the forest. That anthill was brown in colour. It was a triangle in shape. The ants were moving around. The anthill looked like a fort. " Aarav "I wonder if ants are having a party in the anthill and eating food. I also want to be small and join the party with the ants." Aarav "A caterpillar on a leaf. It has many legs. It has two antennas." Devaansh "I wonder where it is going. I wonder why it has many legs. I wonder why it is eating leaves." Devaansh "The caterpillar was green. It had poison tail. It had yellow and green eyes with white spots. It had little and lots of legs." Kushagra "I wonder if the caterpillar will have a long life. I wonder if the caterpillar likes to eat dry leaves. I wonder if that caterpillar had a long long travel. I wonder if the caterpillar has a big family And l wonder if the caterpillar has enough food I wonder if the caterpillar has a warm and a big house with a fan, chairs, tables, bed and a bathroom." Kushagra "I see Big birds with long neck, skinny legs and pink feathers. These are flamingos." Meriam "I wonder.........what do flamingos eat? I wonder where do they live? I wonder if they can fly high in the sky? I wonder how big are flamingo eggs? I wonder what colour are the eggs? I wonder if I can make pink cake with the eggs." Meriam The End. Meet our authors and illustrators Aahanaa has been actively observing nature around her. Spotting bugs, bug houses, butterfly eggs in her garden, exploring, creating with natural materials and illustrating her observations became part of her everyday learning. She visited her grandma in Kishanganj during her winter break. There in the village, she observed corn fields, tested bamboo’s flexibility and saw animals. The goat in the book was one of many animals that she met during her winter holiday. Aarav loves animals and superheroes. Enjoying the rain, picking vegetables and fruits, collecting, sorting and creating with natural materials, showing us around his garden full of colourful flowers, plants with patterns were some of his nature explorations. The anthill in the book was found in a jungle during a family holiday. It reminds him of a miniature fort that his family built in the garden as part of their Diwali celebration. Devaansh has been observing nature as part of his learning in the unit. Despite being an avid lover of cars, Devaansh has managed to spend time observing nature around him. Listening to birds, watering plants, exploring leaves and spider webs are some of the highlights of his nature explorations. The caterpillar in the book was spotted by him on his balcony garden. Kushagra has always shared his love for nature. Through short video clips and photographs of observing frogs and snails, chasing butterflies, learning to climb trees, using materials from nature to create stories and taking us on tours of his orchard and vegetable garden, Kushagra has explored nature in many ways. Recently he found a caterpillar in his garden which became part of our book. The caterpillar is safely back in the garden. Meriam has observed and wondered about the trees in the wind, sharing videos and photographs of her nature observations and play. From playing in the snow and building snowmen and collecting eggs from the hen house to giving us a grand tour of her grandpa’s farm in Morocco, she has done it all and kept us entertained and mesmerised about nature and it’s versatility, beauty and vulnerability. She visited a zoo and saw many animals including birds during her winter break. Credits: Observations, wonderings and illustrations by EY1 Scribed by EY1 Parents Photographs by EY1 Parents Title suggested by Ms Karishma P3 Teacher Cover design by Ms Anu Edited by EY1 Team
author: EY1  Learners

title: Holi Celebration
text: Holi is celebrated in the month of March. The main sweet eaten by people on this festival is 'Gujia'. Holi is the festival of colours. On this festival, people play with water guns and put gulal on each others' faces. In this picture, a girl is sprinkling water on a boy. Grandma is applying gulal on mother. Grandpa is applying gulal on grandma.There is gulal and different colours spilled on the ground. Holi is celebrated because on this day Hiranyakashipu wanted to kill his son Prahlad as he was a great devotee of Lord Vishnu so he tricked along with his sister Holika to kill Prahlad in a bonfire but at the end he was saved by the Lord Vishnu which marks the end of evil. It is the most important festival of Hindus. In this picture, the whole family is enjoying this festival.
