title: Kindness makes everything possible
text: Once, there was a sweet little kitty named Loyla. It always wanted a owner but no one ever adopted it. It saw some food in it's food bowl and some nuts. It decided to eat it. Then a mouse came asking for food. Cats always hated mouse. But Loyla was different. Loyla is very kind. It didn't taught that the mouse was it's friend or enemy. Also it had enough food. So, she decided to share some food with the mouse. And she also gave it some nuts. Loyla and mouse would have enough food. For the first time, a cat did not make a mouse it food, but it gave some! The mouse was very surprised. A cat, a mouse's enemy was ready to give it some food? The mouse took some time to accept the food. But when Loyla said it was very sure about what it is doing, it accepted it. They both were eating happily. They looked like friends. Other cats and mice did not believed their eyes. The cats and mice exchanged their looks. They are crazy, they said together. After Loyla and the mouse finished their food, they hugged each other. Then something amazing happened. The mouse changed into an angel. The angel made Loyla's eyes closed. Loyla was sleeping peacefully. It felt so comfortable. It never felt so comfortable before. It felt like she is in Paradise. It slept and slept and slept until something disturbed it. Someone was tickling it. It opened one eye. It saw an old woman. Loyla could not believe it. It was finally adopted! It was like a dream. All because of it's kindness. The old woman hugged her. Loyla was so happy. This would never happen if it would not shared the mouse its food. After all, kindness makes everything possible!
author: Meenal  Bansal

title: Friendship is the best
text: Once there was a truck named Monty. It has a order to deliver vegetables to the garage. The day was Perfect to do the work. Monty started its journey to the garage. Also, there was a scooter named Lara. Lara was very happy that the sun was bright because for many days, it was cold. Lara decided to take a drive to enjoy the weather. But Lara was driving very fast. Driving fast can be very dangerous. Also it takes a big amount of petrol. She is going to cross the speed limit. But she didn't care and was just singing. Suddenly, Lara crashed to a tree. Monty saw it. Monty rushed to help Lara. Luckily, Lara was not much damaged. Monty said, Be careful next time. Monty helped Lara to stand. They both introduced their selves. "Thankyou so much Monty, but I have less petrol." said Lara. Monty said, " I wish I could give you some, but I have a long journey." But then, a truck named Roger came. Roger saw everything. " May I help you?" Roger said. " It would be a pleasure if you share some petrol" Lara said. Roger gave some of its petrol to Lara. They all became like friends. Then they reached the garage. Roger invited Monty and Lara to stay at it's home, as it was near the garage. Monty and Lara accepted. There, Roger introduced them to the cars there. They enjoyed staying there. But the next day, Roger was sick. It had a high fever. Monty and Lara came and asked the reason for Roger's sickness. Roger said, I have a special red paint to keep me healthy. Without it, I will be badly sick. But I am out of it. Will you please go to the market? Monty and Lara rushed to the paint shop. They bought some rollers and the special red paints. Also they bought blue and yellow paint for themselves for future use. Then they went to Roger. Then they started to paint Roger. Roger was feeling better. "Thankyou friends, you are the best." said Roger. "This is what friends are for." Monty and Lara said together. The next day, it was Monty's birthday. Roger and Lara threw a big party. It was fun. They were best friends. They visited each other regularly. It is so fun to have friends.
author: Meenal  Bansal

title: A unique friendship of Heron and fish
text: We all know that the heron and fish have always been hostile and the heron always eats the fish cleverly.They had been a major critics of each other.But earlier they were good friends.Their story is that there was a pond in the Tajpur forest with many fishes.There was a head of those fish, called the fish queen. The fish queen also respected all the fish and always used to lead them. All the fish believed her as their queen and obeyed her every command. Time was going well. One day the fish queen was collecting food on the banks of the pond. At the same time, a heron fell on the shore. It seemed as if he was injured. He fell unconscious as soon as he fell. When the queen fish saw the unconscious heron, she threw some water at him. Heron came to his senses with water splashes but could not move due to his injuries. The queen fish was afraid to go near him, because he was out of water. And she can't live out of water. Moreover, she was afraid that he would harm her if he became conscious. The fish queen gave voice to her companions. The fishes gatheredThe fish queen asked everyone to pull the heron and bring it to the edge of the pond. Everyone pulled him to the edge of the pond. Now the fish queen made medicine from the weed of the pond for him. He was still unconscious. The fish queen saw that a hunter had injured him with an arrow. Now the fish queen herself looked after the Heron day and night. She used to give him medicines and also used to cleanse his wounds on time and apply medicines. The fish queen's hard work paid off and heron has been cured. The fish queen now allowed him to remain in his pond. Heron also now started living comfortably in that pond with all the fishes. He thanked the fish queen for giving him new life. He promised the queen fish he will someday owe her efforts Time passed. The fish queen and heron had a close friendship. Heron used to protect all the fish from predators and other carnivorous animals by making them aware of the danger. Some animals were now getting envious of the heron due to their inability to eat the fishes and they Used to hate their friendship. There was only one Kalu crow in them because whenever he goes to eat the fish, the heron used to alert the fish and the crow has to starve. The Kalu crow killed some fish from another forest one day and put them near the pond of Tajpur forest and started crying loudly and started saying ﻿ ﻿ ﻿, " Hey, look, someone has killed the fish of the pond." Hearing this, all the animals gathered. Fish queen also felt very bad when she saw all this. But she could not understand that who would have done this as her lake was protected by the heron. The crow after seeing the fish thinking said loudly," so this work is done by the heron because noone can be close to fish until he's here. The Heron said, "It is a lie". But the rest of the crow's companions also insisted that the heron was guilty." Now the fish queen also believed the point of the crow that this act is of heron's. She asked the heron to go out of the pond. Even after giving a lot of cleaning to the fish, the queen fish did not believe his words and got him out of the pond. Heron became very sad because he was innocent. Now tge crow had fun, he used to eat fish everyday with great tricks and the fish queen believed that Heron is doing all this. One day when a hunter came to catch the fish from the pond, the heron made a noise and made the fishes aware of the hunter. ﻿ But all of them were considering it as heron's trick. They did not become unsteady, the Heron decided to struggle against the hunter to protect them.The hunter killed him with his knife in an anger. While dying, he told his companions to tell the fish queen that he did not kill the fish. Heron's friends did the same but at the instance of Heron's friends also ﻿ the fish queen did not believe the heron. His companions were saddened to see the sacrifice of the Heron. Now they thought that when their partner was grabbed under a false accusation of eating fish, then why not really start eating fishes now. From that day onwards, the Herons started eating fishes from the ponds with great tricks.
author: saloni vijay
illustrator: Aruna Keerthi Gamage; Benjamin  Mitchley; Deepa Balsavar; Ketan Raut; Michael  Sagikwa; Natasha Sharma; Onesmus   Kakungi; Padmanabh; Sharanya Singh

title: Jackal and crow
text: Once there was a cunning and greedy jackal. He was very hungry. He was wandering here and there in search of food. Suddenly, he saw a flying crow with a piece of bread in her beak. He followed the crow. The crow sat on the tree. The jackal wanted to take bread from the crow. So, he made a plan to grab the bread. He started praising the crow. He said to the crow," Dear, You are very beautiful. Your voice is very sweet. Will you please sing a song for me?" The crow was very pleased to hear her praise. As soon as the crow opened her mouth to sing a song, then bread fell down. The jackal quickly picked up the bread and ran away. Now the crow felt very sad on her foolishness. The crow lost her food, finally. MORAL OF THE STORY - Beware of flattery and never trust anyone blindly!!
author: Arnav Chaudhary

title: The chicken and the millipede
text: Once, there was a chicken and a millipede. They both were friends. One day, the chicken invited the millipede for a game of Football. So they went to the ground. While walking, they had chat. "Do you know I am champion of Football?" said the chicken. "Well I will try my best to play with you." said the millipede. The game of Football started. They both were playing good. But the millipede was playing better than the chicken. They were playing and playing until the millipede had the chance. The chicken immediately rushed to the goal. The millipede was thinking where and how to goal, to the right, to the left, very fast or slow? When millipede was ready, he shot the ball hard. GOAL! The millipede scored. The chicken said, "Huh, it was just your luck. Wait and watch how I score." But the millipede scored more points than the chicken. "Hey! you are cheating millipede!" said the chicken. "No, I am not and also you are the champion, so what happened, loser?" said the millipede. This gave the chicken an idea. "I am hungry. Let us take a break." The millipede was also tired, so it agreed. But the chicken was not hungry. It was a plan. It gulped the ball in it's tummy. The break time was over. "We can't play football because I cannot find the ball anywhere." said the chicken. The millipede was sad. It was playing so well. It wanted to defeat the chicken. But then the chicken started to cough. It coughed and coughed until the ball came out. "This is what happens to cheaters." said the millipede angrily. The chicken was embarrassed. The millipede was no longer friends with the chicken. He started playing with the water.
author: Meenal  Bansal

title: Blueprints?
text: Will my ears grow as long as Grandpa's? What makes us look like Kin? Tell me where'd I get my long eyelashes and where'd I get my chin Where'd I get my Ice cream sweet tooth and this nose that wiggles when I talk? Where'd I get dizzy daydreams and my foot-rolling side step walk? Did I inherit my sense of humor and these crooked,ugly toes? What if I balloon like uncle Harry and have to shave my nose? How long after I growing until I start to shrink? Am I going to shrink? Am I going to lose my teeth, Some day? My hair? My mind? Do you think I'll short or tall or thin or bursting at the seams Am I naturally this crazy? Is something in my genes? I'm more than who I am, I'm also who I'm from. It's a scary speculation Who will I become?
author: Aarna Singh

title: The unhappy snake
text: There was once a snake. He did not liked as it was. One day, the snake saw a flock of birds flying in the sky. "I wish I could also fly as these birds in the sky. They are so lucky." thought the snake. Next, it saw some fishes and a swan in water. "I wish I could swim like the fish in the water. They are so lucky that they can see the beautiful underwater scenery." thought the snake. Then, the snake saw some ants. "I wish I had legs so I can walk anywhere. It would be so fun to have legs and go anywhere and I could run, there are so many things that I can do with legs." thought the snake. Next, the snake saw a spider building its web. "I wish I could be a spider. They are so lucky that they could build their own web easily and also they can find food easily." thought the snake. Then it saw some fawns dancing. "I wish could be as happy as these fawns. They have no tension, they are so happy. And I am mostly sad and stressed." thought the snake. "There are so many things about these animals. They can swim, they can fly, they can jump, run walk with legs, they remain happy. But what is so special about me?" thought the snake. It went to a pond and thought what so special was about it, "Well, there is one thing that is very special about me, I can slither like no other animal can do, also I am very strong. MORAL- WE SHOULD BE HAPPY ABOUT WHAT WE ARE AND WHAT WE HAVE.
author: Meenal  Bansal

title: Apollo and the cat
text: He Illustrator: Catherine Groenewald Translator: Yeeco He Once upon a time there was a dog, that lived in a house close to the campaign. He was named Apollo and he loved going for a walk in the forest. there was some times when he camped in the forest with a tent. He was a domestic pet. But there was a cat in the house. Apollo hated the cat. The cat didn't do anything when there were people in the house. When all the people went out, the cat always scratched Apollo. When the people came in, she stopped. Our story starts when it was a beautiful afternoon. There were some people that went out of the house. the cat waited so that all the peo ple were outside. She sat by the door. when all the people were outside, the cat closed the door. She slept to have more energy to scratch the dog. But when she slept, Apollo made cilli sauce fall in the cat's bowl! A person opened the door. The cat jumped, ran and screamed! The person put some cat food in the cat's bowl so that she wont scream. She didn't notice that there was chili sauce! M MMMEEEEEOOOOOOWWWWWWWWWW!!!!!!!!!!!!!! (I couldn't find a image for this...) The cat wanted to scratch Apollo but the person was looking! So Apollo said to the cat: -you'd do good to not scratch me! And then he went away.

text: He was holding his father's hand tightly. The school is very big. He said to his father," i will be lost in this big school. " 'Don't worry my child", said father goat. title: Words
text: We all know how powerful words are. Words can give hope. Words can show kindness. The importance of words is indescribable. Words are forms of communication, a way to build connections. Words can be wishes, hopes, dreams, thoughts...Words are a powerful way of self expression. Words can be said out of fear, spite, anger... Or they can be said out of joy, love, hope, kindness... Words are powerful. They can be inspirational or heartbreaking, kind or cruel, cheerful or blue. Words are the intricate and colourful voices or thoughts that come from everyone. Child or adult, words can give hope.

title: Kind children of Irukkam Island
text: Irukkam Island is a land of farmers. The children of the island love to sit under the Neem tree. Sukanya went to school but could not find her brothers. She went home angrily. Sukanya is angry at her brothers because they did not go to school that day. Mathan told Sukanya akka that he saw a cat stuck on a tree on his way to school. He wanted to help it. title: The three little pigs
text: Once there was a mummy pig who lived with her 3 little pigs. One day, she sent them to seek their fortune. Mummy pig packed some food for the 3 little pigs. ''Remember '' she said,''Whatever you do, do it the best way you can. And keep away from the big, bad wolf!'' The 3 little pigs had lots of fun along the way. Each took his turn to slide down the hillside in a trolley they found and made merry going 'oink-oink in delight. Suddenly, it started raining heavily. ''We need to build houses for ourselves '', said the 3 little pigs. So, they went in different directions looking for material to build their houses. The 1st pig built his house with straw. The 3rd pig warned him that brother, your house looks good but I don't think straw houses can stand a storm so it better builds your house with bricks. But the two pigs just laughed at him. The 2nd pig built his house with sticks. The 3rd pig too warned him too that a stick-house won't be able to face strong winds. The 2nd pig paid no heed to his brother's advice. The 3rd pig built his house with bricks. The 2 brothers warned him that you're wasting your time not building his house with sticks or straw-like we did. The little pig did not mind his brother's jokes and continued working. And 1 day came the big bad wolf. All 3 little pigs got scared and ran to their houses The big bad wolf said: Let me in, Let me in little pig or I'll huff and I'll puff and I will blow your house away. Not by the hair of my chinny chin chins. In the next moment, the wolf bought the whole house down. The little pig ran to his brother's house to save his life. They hoped they were safe. But, the wolf was powerful and easily bought the house of sticks down. The two brothers ran hard for their dear life as the wolf chased them. The 3 brothers hoped they were safe. The big bad wolf said: Let me in, Let me in little pig or I'll huff and I'll puff and I will blow your house away. Not by the hair of my chinny chin chins answered the little pigs from inside. The wolf tried to huff and puff proudly but could not do it. The wolf was a wicked animal and taught. I have an idea. ﻿ ﻿The pig lit a roaring fire with a large kettle of water over it. The wolf smashed light into the hot kettle of water and screamed: ah! My back hurts. The pigs got the opportunity to beat the wolf with a broom and sticks. The wolf climbed up the chimney and ran away forever. moral: Whatever you do, do it the best way you can because that's the way to get along the world. Publisher: Ayaansh Kumar
author: Vinita Roli
illustrator: Akansha Gupta; Anvi  Gupta; David Chisha; Deval Maniar; Eloy Estrada; George Supreeth; Wiehan de Jager; Youm Kosal

title: Appam Anna; The Day Dreamer!!
text: Appam Anna was often found day dreaming. Many times he closed his eyes and flowed with his dreams. "Look Look; its Appam Anna dreaming again", Said little Guriya and Giggled, while everyone watched in amusement. What is Appam Anna dreaming of today?? lets look inside!! Ohhh!! Its the Bananas this time, it seems he thinks he is the Banana king of the town; may be he wants to sell bananas now!! Where should I get the Bananas from, should I take it from Ranu farmer; Thought Anna Ranu farmer was amazed to see a buyers for his bananas as no one wanted to buy them, they being from the trees, so close to the sewage. He happily sold them at half the market rate and Appam anna felt very proud of the bargain. Soon Appam Anna was seen with a huge pile of Bananas on his trusted cart. 'But where did he get it from, all the trees in the Village had raw banana left on them except for the trees near the sewage'; wondered the Villagers. Where is Appam Anna taking his cart full of Bananas?? Wondered the men and wondered the Fauna!! Appam Anna took them to the market and tried selling them, but no one wanted to buy them it seems. "No no, your bananas are too Sour, my baby is choking" Said Aarti Amma "No no, your bananas are too Sweet, they will spoil my fritters" Said Anil, the Udupi owner. "No no, Your Bananas are too Salty, we can't even swallow them" Said Ajay and Vijay, running away. The news of Appam Anna's bad bananas spread in the village like wild fire, No one wanted to take them, not even for free!! Because of being close to the sewage, the fruit took after the dirty water and spoiled its taste. What is wrong with the Bananas, wondered Anna, some say its sweet, some say its sour and some say its salty. What will I do with sooooo mannnyyyy Bananas Now?? Should I throw them away, or should I eat them up, what should I do?? Asked Appam Anna to himself. I should never have bought them from the owner of those trees. Said Anna. Finally Appam Anna decides to take the Bananas to the forest and burry them to turn them into Compost. He realizes what mistake he had made, and decides 'to be wise and have a vision to his dreams before investing his time and money into it.' "Dream Big but think before you Leap"

text: Once there was a girl named Rinku. She used to go to the garden everyday for strolling. It was summer time. A sparrow was sitting on the tree. It was feeling very hungry, but didn't have anything to eat. Just then she finds Rinku sitting under the tree. The sparrow goes near Rinku and says, "Hey dear, I am too hungry. I searched a lot for grains, but couldn't find any. Could you give me some grains, please?" Rinku feels pity for the sparrow. She tells it, "Dear sparrow, just wait her. I'll bring some grains for you." Rinku goes home in the hot Sun and comes back with some grains for the sparrow. Rinku gives the grains to the sparrow. The sparrow becomes very happy and Rinku forgets about the hotness of the Sun watching the sparrow eat the grains. The sparrow flies away happily and Rinku also returns home smiling. Rinku shares her experience with all her friends in school. She requests everyone to keep grains and water for birds in front of their houses.

title: The fair kingdom
text: Once upon a time, in India, there used to live a king called Valampati Ambedkar. He was famous in the near by and far away lands for his loving nature. People used to respect and love him a lot. Still, one thing used to tease him everytime he sat by his window and saw all the children laughing, hopping and chatting with their parents. He wanted to become a father. At last he thought to go to Saint Arimva Kuntha to ask him what to do. Saint Arimva Kuntha said " You are by far the best king we have had in our kingdom, so do not worry, because, one day the Gods will bless you and your queen with a child, but for now take the flower which you can see blooming beside the river and tell the queen to have one petal with milk everyday.. After a month the Queen gave birth to a beautiful child. The king invited everybody from his kingdom and near by kingdoms that day itself. Saint Arimva Kuntha came, but, an uninvited guest came as well. She was the nature goddess. Amazed by the child's beauty and smile on his face she gave him a boon " You will be the fairest king of all." Just after saying that, she disappeared and a bright light sparkled. Today is the prince's fifth birthday! He got diamond statue of him from his parents this year. When the prince sat for dinner with the other children, a child with black skin was sitting right to him. He did not like the boy's skin's colour after comparing it with his own skin colour. From that moment ownwards, he started hating people with black skin colour. Years passed by and the young prince grew up. After his parents' death, he was crowned as the king. People were expecting a lot from him.To heir surprise he turned out to be bad. The new king soon got married. The queen was not at all of the king's nature, and sometimes she held meetings against the king's wrong decisions. At last the day came for which all the people with black skin were scared. They were banished from the kingdom, as well as his own child who was only sixteen years old. When only fair people started living in the kingdom, everybody from the other kingdoms termed the kingdom as ' The Fair Kingdom '.. Why will my father banish me from the kingdom? Seeing no way left, they thought to go to the forest and live there and not show their face to anyone. At first, they faced difficulties but after a month or two everything was as normal as it was in the kingdom.After a few days, the queen came to the forest and also started living with them. They were all much happier in the forest than in the kingdom. In the forest they could eat fresh fruits, feel close to the nature,see the birds like parrots,parakeets,hornbills, etc. One day an old enemy of Valampati Ambedkar attacked the kingdom. The news spread everywhere but other kingdoms did not want to help the king. If Valampati Ambedkar was alive they would help happily. When his own people living in the forest heard this they hurriedly went to fight for their kingdom. They won the battle. The king stopped them at the moment when they were leaving for the forest. He said " You all saved the kingdom and now you all are leaving.Why? I am really sorry for my deeds,but, please do not go back." Now, I know why few people have black skin colour." After that, the young prince married and lived happilly ever after with his queen and daughter. Are you interested to know how the king came to know why few people have balck skin? Well that is a story for another day.

title: Strawberry Fruit
text: Strawberries are bright red fruits. Strawberries are juicy and have a combination of a sweet and sour taste. A cut Strawberry looks like the picture. Strawberries are rich in Vitamin C and Manganese. Strawberries are used to make jams, milkshakes, cakes, pies, ice cream, and chocolates. This is a picture of a Strawberry milkshake or smoothie. The tiny seeds of the Strawberry fruit are yellow and are on top of its red body. China is the highest producer of Strawberries. title: Palmyra Sprouts
text: The Palmyra sprouts are underground sprouts of the Palmyra Palm tree. They are also known as the Palmyra tuber. These sprouts are the underground shoots from a germinating palm seed. The seed at the top of the sprout and root below the sprout is cut off and only the tuber is eaten. The tuber or sprout is edible. The tuber has an outer sheath that is usually removed while cooked at home. The tuber is either boiled in water or roasted in a fire. In villages, the tubers along with their outer sheath are kept inside an earthen pot. Then the pots are covered with hay and the hay is burnt. The tuber gets cooked in the heat. The tubers have a lot of fibre and are nutritious. The tubers are rich in iron, folate, calcium, and magnesium. They have Omega-3 fatty acids that are good for heart health. They are rich in proteins. And have very few calories. Palmyra grows in many of the South Indian States. As per a 2018 study, out of the 8.59 crores of Palmyra in India, 5.10 crores are in Tamilnadu. They also grow in Srilanka, Indonesia, and other southeast Asian countries. In Tamil, Palmyra sprout is known as panang kizhangu. In Telugu, it is known as Thegalu or Gaygulu. Happy nutritious eating!
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: 'I Don't Believe You!'
text: One Friday Ann was late to school. It was her class' assembly day. She tried to catch her bus, shouting that she had assembly, but the driver just sped off with the words, 'I don't believe you, I waited at your stop for the allotted three minutes.' "Ugh!" groaned Ann inside. Her mother would have to drop her. In the car, Mom asked Ann whether she'd packed her things. Yes, she nodded. But then she thought whether she should tell her mother something else that might anger her. She risked it. 'Mom, I'm sorry to tell you this now, but my pen-box was stolen yesterday.' 'I don't believe you! Your new pen! It was so expensive. I guess you just lost your box.' Ann KNEW her box was stolen. At school Ann discovered her assembly had been pushed to the afternoon. She was extremely thankful, since she was ten minutes late. The good thing was, it was free period. But in math class came another disaster. Ann was asked by her teacher why she hadn't brought her homework. Ann said her dog had eaten her homework. 'I don't believe you! Timeout.' Inside Ann started to cry. What a disastrous day! She stood outside the classroom and walked past her, her best friend. 'Ann! Why are you outside class?' 'Dog huh huh... ate my huh huh... homework' said Ann in true tears, this time. 'I don't believe you. Dogs don't eat homework, that's just a lame excuse. Anyway, why would Biscuit do that? Huh, bye!' Ann just couldn't stop sobbing. When Ann was allowed to enter class again, she found all the windows covered with blinds and both doors shut behind her. Science teacher had come in. She tapped at her phone a few times and said that their assembly would not happen. The class heard a few rain sounds coming from outside and assumed that there was a shower. All but Ann. 'I don't believe you.' That's all Ann had been hearing throughout the day. The phrase spun around in her head making her dizzy. Her mother, teacher, best friend, even her bus driver had said it. So then, she said confidently, 'I don't believe you!' That seemed to startle the teacher very much. 'You have no right to-' Ann found her hands growing to an enormous size and punching the doors. She ran out of the class and her hands shrunk back to normal. She opened the blinders out to a sunny blue sky and called her classmates to see. They were horrified. How dare the TEACHER lie to us! they thought. 'Wow, guess I can't trust you now can I?' said Ann, stripping the teacher to her chair. Then the class ran out to the assembly stage and found the whole school sitting there waiting for the performance to begin. Ann's bus driver was there too. Clearly, he must have understood the morning's situation better. When Ann sat down in the backstage area she noticed two grey box-like figures in the distance across the room. She checked the stage outside, calculated and went to inspect the objects. One was her beloved pen-box, with the pens inside, while next to it was a minicamera with a 'John' tag on it. John. How could Ann not have guessed? She used the camera to take a snap of the pen-box's location and quickly slipped both items into her pocket. It was time for her to speak onstage. She left. After assembly she baffled John and left for her bus to home. She had told him that she'd be taking his 'stuff' for a while. John didn't know what to do, other than shrug his shoulders. On the bus, Ann was (again) thinking about the 'I-don't-believe-you's that day. One of her problems had been solved, one was about to be solved and the remaining two, she would try and fix. 'Mom! Look at this!' said Ann the moment her mother picked her up from the bus stop, showing her the camera, pen-box and photos. 'I guess I have to believe you now!' replied Mom. Later that evening Ann's math teacher rushed into the house. 'Where's your homework? This is urgent!' To her surprise, Ann's mother stood defensively and said, 'You have no right to just barge into someone's house asking for homework! Besides, there's much more important stuff than homework. I bet you haven't graded a single class' exam papers. And I suppose you know our dog has eaten the homework; Ann must have told you that. We had to get an X-ray done and take out the paper.' The scared teacher ran out of the house as if she'd seen a ghost inside. And yes, as expected, this news reached all of Ann's class, including her best friend. Now that all her matters had been solved, Ann settled down on a couch and continued what she was doing.

title: The Vicious, Deadly Kick
text: The Vicious, Deadly Kick Eli ostrich was in a bad mood. Pippa ostrich had poked her on the head with her sharp beak. She had refused to apologise. “You kicked me yesterday!” accused Pippa. “My poke was tit for tat for hurting me!” “ I told you it was an accident! ” shouted Eli. “I was going to kick a hyena, but you ran towards me. My KICK landed on you! I will lay my eggs in another place. I refuse to share a communal nest with mean folks like YOU!” So, Eli scratched out a shallow hollow pit in the mud some yards away from the ostriches’ communal nest. She sat on her eggs and pretended that she could NOT hear them or see them! Eli soon got bored. She was an ostrich who liked to walk around. She HATED sitting in one place! “I’ll go for a short walk,” said Eli. “I need to stretch my legs. Maybe I will find a FAT gecko to MUNCH for lunch!” She was not worried about her eggs. The eggs were heavy. Eli was convinced no one would be able to lift and carry an egg away! Eli’s short walk ended up as a long walk. She forgot that she had to SIT on her eggs! When Eli came back, she was horrified to find that one egg was missing inside the pit nest in the ground. “An egg of mine has gone!” wailed Eli. “What should I do?” Eli put her head on the ground and wept. Pippa came running to her. “I saw a BIG chimpanzee near your nest,” said Pippa, when Eli told her about the missing egg. “He must have taken your egg to have it for lunch.” “ A baby ostrich was growing INSIDE the egg! ” shouted Eli. “ How dare anyone EAT my baby for lunch! I will catch the thief and KICK him straight to Timbuctoo! ” “I’ll come with you,” said Pippa. “Eli, I’m really sorry I poked you!” “And I’m sorry for kicking you!” apologised Eli. “I have a NASTY temper. It is time I learnt to control my anger. I do NOT want to be an ANGRY ostrich mom.” They found the chimpanzees in their riverine tree colony. Eli spotted a chimpanzee showing off her egg to the other chimpanzees. “ HEY! That’s MY egg! ” shouted Eli. “ Give it back to me! ” “Finders Keepers!” mocked the chimpanzee thief. “Losers Weepers!” screeched his friend. “Papa Leo!” said Lulu, Leo’s partner. “Did you steal THAT egg from this ostrich?” “The egg was in a hollow in the ground,” said Leo. “NO ONE was there. If she is the egg’s mom, she should have been SITTING on it. I thought it was an unwanted egg!” “Every egg has a mom,” scolded Lulu. “Suppose an eagle carries our junior away? What will you do?” “ I’ll chase it and TEAR its wings away! ” shouted Leo, angrily. “Exactly!” retorted Lulu. “SHE too will do what you will do. What is good for the goose is good for the gander too! Return THAT egg to the ostrich mom immediately. Otherwise, I will not let junior be with you. I want him to be kind. NOT cruel like YOU.” “I’ll carry the egg back to your nest,” muttered Leo. Pippa, Eli, and Leo went back with the egg. Leo placed the egg carefully into Eli’s hollow nest in the ground. “Now I have a reward for YOU!” declared Eli. She gave Leo a hard kick on his belly with her strong leg! He flew high in the air and fell down on a huge boulder, many yards away. Leo was badly bruised all over and his body ached. “ OUCH! ” yelled Leo. “ I gave your egg back. Show some GRATITUDE, you MEAN ostrich!!” He limped back home. Leo was convinced that Eli had broken all his bones! He was shocked that none from his family showed him any sympathy. “You deserved THAT hard kick,” said Lulu chimpanzee. “What you sow, so shall you reap!” “I HAD to punish Leo for what he did,” said Eli to the other ostriches in the nest. “I do NOT believe that one should forgive and forget. HE will remember my HARD kick whenever he is tempted to pick up another bird’s egg!” Eli is now wiser. She has made the decision that she will ALWAYS lay her eggs in the communal nest. The other ostriches will take care of her eggs whenever she feels an urge to EXERCISE her LONG, STRONG legs by walking away from the nest! Word power! Communal nest – the dominant male ostrich scrapes out a pit in the ground. The dominant female lays 7 to 10 eggs in the centre of this dump nest. Other lesser females lay eggs around these eggs. A communal nest can have 60 eggs in it!
author: Hema Rao

title: On Mondays I Want to Hide
text: If Monday were a man, he would be a school principal. He would have eyebrows like caterpillars, and a voice as hard as a hammer. “Wake up. It is time to work,” he would say. ​When Monday comes, I want to hide. ​If Tuesday were a woman, she would be an old aunty. Her saree would be the colour of dust. She would visit every week. She would drink tea and talk, talk, talk. ​We would yawn and wait for her to go. Tuesday is the slowest day of the week. ​If Wednesday were a girl, she would wear purple spectacles. She would wear a neat uniform, and have three sharpened pencils. She would solve her sums, drink her milk, and pack her school bag. ​Wednesday is a busy day. ​If Thursday were a boy, he would wear a yellow T-shirt. His head would be full of gymnastics and lollipops. ​He would jump and run. He would be in a hurry. ​On Thursday, I make happy plans. ​​If Friday were an older sister, she would be getting ready to meet her friends. She would laugh and she would giggle. She would wear stars in her ears and have stars in her eyes. ​Sometimes I wish every day was a Friday. ​If Saturday had a twinkly smile, it would be just like my best friend. We would play hopscotch. We would read books. We would sit and watch the rain together. I wish Saturdays would never end. ​Sunday would be a bald grandfather. He would eat, sleep and tell stories. ​He would be jolly in the morning, but cross in the evening. ​On Sunday, I wash my hair. And try not to think about Monday. MONDAY TUESDAY WEDNESDAY THURSDAY FRIDAY SATURDAY SUNDAY ​Which is your favourite day of the week?
author: Shabnam  Minwalla

title: Friends
text: SPIDER FACTS: A spider web is made out of silk that they produce. Spiders have 8 legs. BEE FACTS: Bees live in colonies. They build a honeycomb out of wax. Bees have six legs. Honey bees have yellow and black stripes and are hairy. ANT FACTS: Most ants live underground. They live in colonies. They build tunnels for different uses under the ground. Ants can carry things 10 times bigger than themselves. Ants have 6 legs. Once upon a time there was an ant, a bee and a spider. They were best friends. One day they wanted to build their own home but they didn't know where they could live together. So they made separate homes. They were very sad that they couldn't live together. One day the ant had a great idea! She said, "Let's think of what we have and what we can do best." The spider said, "I can give my silk." The bee said, " I will give my wax." The ant said, "I will stitch them with leaves and whatever else I find beautiful." They worked all night. At dawn they had a beautiful home where they could live together.

title: Happy Ugadi!
text: Ugadi is the New Year’s Day that is celebrated in the states of Andhra, Telangana, and Karnataka. The name Ugadi or Yugadhi in Sanskrit means New Beginning – yuga means new, and adi means beginning. On Ugadi, people draw beautiful Rangoli designs on the floor. Pachadi is a special dish made on Ugadi. This Ugadhi pachadi has jaggery, tamarind juice, neem flowers, salt, pepper, and cut mango pieces in it. So, the dish has a sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and spicy hot taste. This dish signifies that life in the New Year will be a combination of sweet, bitter, and sour events. And we have to learn to accept all these events equally. People wear new clothes and clean their houses thoroughly. They visit Hindu temples and give money for charity. Here the family is enjoying the Ugadi pachadi. On Ugadi, they make torana or mango leaf decorations to hang on the doors. A metal pot or Kalasa with water is arranged with coconut and mango leaves on the top of the pot. Ugadi festival falls in the March or April of every year. The Ugadi festival falls on Tuesday, 13 April, in the year 2021. Ugadi day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa or New Year in Maharashtra. Happy Ugadi!

title: Jungle Jamboree
text: Once upon a time, in a land far away there was a jungle. The king of the jungle was Levo, the Lion. Levo was a caring King, he always helped the other animals whenever they were in trouble. The animals in the jungle lived peacefully under the wise rule of their king but there was no place assigned according to their nature due to which the small animals were unable to move. The birds hopped behind the trees to avoid the leaping leopards, the grasshoppers got flatten by the larger animals, the fish slid away when they heard the thundering hooves of the horses, ants scurried of when the hippos moved about and the squirrels looked misshapen on being stepped on so often. One day, the small animals went to Levo, the king of the jungle to complain him about the larger animals. Levo's most loyal friend Victor, the leopard must have seen humans living separate places so, he went to Levo and told him about everything he saw. Then Levo went to the waterhole and he noticed the animals differences and behaviour there. So then he got the idea of giving space to the animals. Levo said to the birds that you can live in trees the sky is their playground, he said to the the grasshoppers you can live undergrowth, He said to the worms you can dig on wet ground so you can live on wet ground. Then at last, the animals were able to move. The large animals were not troubling the small animals and they happily lived after.

title: Tiny's Safe Place
text: Ira, or as she was fondly called Iru, was all of 6years old. One day she accompanied her father to the market. While she was waiting for her father to finish, she suddenly heard a soft ‘meow’. Iru ran to her left and looked behind the bushes- a very small, weak and furry ginger kitten looked up at her with bright green eyes. The kitten looked like it had not eaten in days. Iru felt bad for it. She suddenly remembered her mother saying, ‘Always help whoever you can’ She gently picked up the kitten in her hand and decided to take it home. “I will call him Tiny, since he is so small” When her father saw the kitten, he could not help smiling. But he reminded Iru, that they would have to discuss keeping it as a family. At home, it was decided, that they would keep the kitten provided that Iru would feed Tiny 3 times a day and make sure he had water to drink. Iru’s excitement knew no bounds. Slowly she and Tiny developed a deep friendship. Iru made sure that Tiny was well taken care of and Tiny found a friend in Iru. One day, Iru was looking lovingly at Tiny while he purred on her lap, when her mother asked, “What are you thinking, Iru?” Iru replied, “Just like you are my safe place, I am happy that Tiny has found his safe place with me”

title: A Boy's Call
text: There was a lonely sea. It had no fish in it. The fishes that came into the sea through the rivers died because the sea was full of salt. One day a little boy came who was 6 years old. The sea saw the boy and said, “Little boy, I am a lonely sea. Please help me, by making me clean, and then some fish can live in me.” The little boy said, “I can see why the fish are all dead, Once I am done cleaning you, the fish will love you as a bed.” The boy got straight to work. But the boy was small and the sea was vast. He knew he couldn’t take out all the salt. He prayed to God, “Dear God, please send help so we can bring life into our lonely sea.” God smiled at the boy and said, “I am sending my team.” Then he requested the clouds, the sun and the wind to work as a team and make the sea fresh. The wind was very friendly so she said, “I would love to make the sea, as fresh as a daisy.” The cloud was lazy so he said with a big yawn, “I don’t feel like working on a Sunday, I feel like having a fun day. It is too much effort to make it rain, It’ll make my ankle sprain.” The sun hated humans for destroying earth so he said in a cynical voice, “I would never help a human, they are small and meaningless like a cumin.” God smiled and said to the cloud, “If you help someone out of a sticky situation, you will earn a new friend. If you are in trouble later, that boy will be the superhero that I’ll send.” The cloud thought for a moment and said, “Fine, I’ll help.” Then God turned to the Sun and said, “Not all humans are bad, don’t feel sad, do this human a favour and you’ll feel glad.” That seemed to convince the cloud and the sun. They all went together to help just the way God wanted. The sun shone and brought the salt in the air. The wind blew the salt and the clouds rained giving fresh water to the sea. Soon the sea became fresh and full of life. The sea thanked the boy for it was his pure heart that made God answer his call. P.S I wish my heart was pure like the boy and that is good because I have something to learn from him.

title: What is a Food Chain?
text: The Food Chain shows how different living things eat each other to survive and live. The nutrients and energy are passed on to the living things through the food chain. The food chain from bottom to top can be represented as Primary Producers -> Primary Consumers -> Secondary Consumers -> Tertiary Consumers -> Quaternary consumers -> Apex consumers. Primary producers make their food from sunlight. Plants and trees are examples of primary producers. The primary consumer eats the primary producer. For example, a deer eats plants. So, the deer is a primary consumer. The secondary consumer feeds on the primary consumer. For example, a tiger may eat the deer. The tiger is the secondary consumer. The picture shows a food chain where the plants on the ground are primary producers. The insect in the frog’s hand is a primary consumer which eats the plants. The frog is a secondary consumer and eats the insect. The snake is a tertiary consumer and eats the frog. The mongoose is a quaternary consumer and eats the snake. The bald eagle is the apex consumer which eats the mongoose. Apex consumers or apex predators are birds and animals that are not eaten by other birds and animals. For example, an eagle and an adult lion are apex consumers. Whether humans can be considered as apex consumers is debatable. When a human eats a vegetable cutlet, the human is a primary consumer. When a human eats a beef cutlet, the human is a secondary consumer. Decomposers eat the waste and remains of plants and animals. Fungi, bacteria, and earthworms are examples of decomposers. The food chains interconnect and form a food web.

title: Something's Stuck Around the Duck
text: It was Saturday and Kavitha and Nandini wanted to do something fun. “I’ve got a new ball!” said Kavitha, full of excitement. “Let’s go to the park.” At the park, they noticed a large pile of garbage next to their favourite patch of grass. “Yuck!” said Kavitha. “There’s all sorts of things here—rotten food, old wrappers and plastic bags!” “It stinks! How can that duck sleep next to all this garbage?” Nandini wondered, pointing at it. The girls moved a little distance away from the smelly garbage. Kavitha threw the ball high into the air and Nandini just managed to catch it. “Whoosh!” shouted Nandini, as she tried her best to throw the ball just as high back to her friend. But Kavitha let the ball slip through her fingers and it rolled away. “Oh no,” cried Kavitha, “my new ball has rolled into the stinky rubbish!” She ran quickly towards the mound of rotten waste. Suddenly, she stopped. “Nandini, come quickly!” Kavitha shouted to Nandini, waving for her to come at once. The duck they had seen earlier was not actually sleeping. It was lying very still and looked uncomfortable! Without getting too close, the girls saw that there was something wrapped around the duck’s beak. “I think she’s tried to eat some of the garbage that is lying here.” “It looks like something plastic, let’s try and get it off,” suggested Nandini. “She looks like she needs help right away. She can hardly open her beak!” Nodding, Kavitha moved closer to the duck. As she closed in with a final step, the duck flapped its wings, squealed and moved away quickly. This time, Nandini tried but the duck seemed even more frantic. “We are scaring her,” said Kavitha. “She should stay still. She can’t breathe properly because of the plastic thing around her beak and we are making it worse.” The girls looked around anxiously to see if they could find someone in the park to help them. “How can we catch the duck?” Nandini asked the lady who was walking past them. “I don’t know,’’ said the lady. “Who looks after the ducks in this park?” Kavitha asked the man sitting on the bench. “I don’t know,” said the man. “Who cleans up the garbage here?” they asked the other children playing in the park. “We don’t know,” said the children. “How can we help the duck?” Nandini wondered. “Nobody knows,” Kavitha sighed. How could it be that no one knew what to do? “If we don’t help, then who will?” Nandini asked, tearfully. “We will help the duck, Nandini, don’t worry!” Kavitha jumped up. “My neighbour, Bhavna aunty is a vet. She’ll know what to do!” The girls found that Bhavna aunty was not home. They would have to wait until she was back from work. They went to Kavitha’s house in the meantime. “Why are you back so soon, girls?” asked Kavitha’s dad. “Are you bored with your new ball already?” “My ball! Oh no!” groaned Kavitha. In all the panic, they had left the ball behind. Nandini explained what had happened with the duck. The girls were quiet, waiting anxiously for Bhavna aunty to come and help. Moving her hand carefully, Bhavna aunty untangled the plastic from around the duck’s beak. The duck looked up at her. She could breathe properly again! Bhavna aunty put her down and the duck scurried away quickly. “It’s not the first time I’ve seen an animal suffer because of plastic rubbish lying around on the streets and in parks,” Bhavna aunty said as she held up the curling plastic that had been tangled around the duck’s beak. “I wonder what this is. I’ve never seen anything like this before,” Kavitha observed. “Let’s take it home and show my dad.” Kavitha’s dad heated up some milk for the girls to drink while they waited. He agreed it would be best to let Bhavna aunty handle the duck. “Dad, why is there so much garbage in the park?” Kavitha asked. Kavitha’s dad stopped. He had not really thought about it much. “I suppose it is because the government hasn’t put up any bins. People dump their garbage everywhere. What else can people do? And, even when there is a bin, it overflows with garbage because no one empties it.” The girls listened carefully. Kavitha’s dad poured the milk. “Also, lots of materials like plastic take a long time to decompose so they end up lying around for a long time,” he added. Nandini wanted to ask what ‘decompose’ meant but suddenly there was a knock at the door. It was Bhavna aunty. “I hear there’s a duck in trouble. Let’s go to the park, quickly!” she said briskly. They found the duck almost exactly where they had left her. The plastic thing was still wrapped around her beak. “Every time we tried to go near her, the duck…,” Nandini didn’t have a chance to finish her sentence before Bhavna aunty grabbed hold of the duck just below the neck with one swift move. “Don’t worry girls, this is how you handle a duck,” said Bhavna aunty, seeing the alarm on the girls’ faces. She tucked her other hand under the duck’s body and cradled her gently. Moving her hand carefully, Bhavna aunty untangled the plastic from around the duck’s beak. The duck looked up at her. She could breathe properly again! Bhavna aunty put her down and the duck scurried away quickly. “It’s not the first time I’ve seen an animal suffer because of plastic rubbish lying around on the streets and in parks,” Bhavna aunty said as she held up the curling plastic that had been tangled around the duck’s beak. “I wonder what this is. I’ve never seen anything like this before,” Kavitha observed. “Let’s take it home and show my dad.” At home, Kavitha’s dad was shocked. “This is a slinky. It’s a toy just like one I used to play with when I was a child almost thirty years ago! You can’t buy these any more, not these small ones anyway. I wonder how it has lasted so long! It looks brand new.” “Is this what you meant when you said earlier that plastic takes a long time to decompose, uncle?” Nandini asked curiously. “Yes, I suppose so. I just didn’t think it would take so long!” “I wonder just how long this toy will stay like this?” Kavitha said, switching on her computer. Together with Kavitha’s dad, the girls looked online to find out more about plastic. “Wow, it says here that plastic takes about 450 years to decompose.” Nandini was stunned. “Even when plastic does decompose, it releases harmful materials which can hurt animals according to this website,” added Kavitha. “Apparently chewing gum is made of plastic! Ewww!” Nandini exclaimed. The girls realised that many things they had were made of plastic. Many of their toys, the bottles they drank out of, the bags used for shopping...it was a very long list! “So many bits of plastic and other garbage are just lying around in the park where we play. Other animals could get hurt too,” said Nandini. “If we don’t do something about this, then who will?” Kavitha said, feeling unhappy. “You’re right, Kavitha,” said Nandini. “So…why don’t we clean the park ourselves?” “That’s a great idea. Perhaps we can ask the local corporator for help,” Kavitha’s dad added, thoughtfully. “The local corporator looks after the needs of our local area. They are part of the local government, called the Municipal Corporation,” Kavitha’s dad explained. Nandini, Kavitha and her dad went to speak to the local corporator and told her the story of what happened to the duck. The local corporator agreed to help them to clean the park. She organised for the garbage to be cleared up and taken away. She also made sure that bins were put up around the park and emptied every Friday. “Let’s also make signs to tell people to throw their garbage in the bins,” said Nandini, excitedly. Three weeks later, when Kavitha and Nandini went back to the park, it looked like a different place altogether. “The park is so clean! And many more people come here now,” Kavitha said, looking around. “I just wish we’d found my ball when we cleaned up the park,” she sighed. “It is clean, but have you noticed something?” Nandini asked. “Noticed what?” “The park is clean but look at what that girl is drinking from, a plastic water bottle. And that woman is carrying her shopping in a plastic bag.” “You’re right!” exclaimed Kavitha. “Even that man is using a plastic straw.” The park was clean. People were throwing everything away in the bins. But what would happen to all those plastic things in the bin, the girls wondered. Where did they end up? At school the next day, they asked their teacher. “Most garbage goes to landfills,” their teacher explained. “These are large spaces where garbage is dumped. It stays there until it decomposes.” “But plastic takes so long to decompose! Does it not just blow away?” Nandini asked. “That’s exactly what happens sometimes. Lots of plastic ends up in rivers and oceans this way or in other places,” their teacher explained. “It can harm animals, and even humans.” “We all need to stop using so much plastic,” Kavitha said. “Yes!” agreed Nandini, “and we should tell people why and what they can do instead.” “Because if we don’t do it, who will?” cried the girls together. A few days later the girls made a presentation in the park to people from their local community.“There is around 5.6 million tonnes of plastic waste in India every year. That’s the same as the weight of 5.6 million elephants!” Nandini explained. “Most of this plastic goes into landfill sites, oceans or other places. We don’t reuse it.” “Animals, especially ones that live in the sea sometimes think this plastic is food. They try and eat it. But this makes the animals very sick because it gets stuck in their stomachs. This can even cause them to die!” Kavitha continued. “In Indonesia, a whale washed up on the shore and was found to have 1000 pieces of plastic inside its stomach!” “When plastic is left in landfill sites, bad chemicals seep into the groundwater. This then flows into lakes and oceans. This also hurts sea animals,” Nandini highlighted. “When humans eat seafood, the plastic and chemicals end up inside us. This can make us very sick too,” Kavitha expanded. “On average, one person eats 70,000 tiny pieces of plastic (called microplastics) every year!” “Animals can also get tangled up in plastic things and they get badly hurt or die,” Nandini added. “Thank you so much for bringing this to our attention,” said an elderly man who had been listening attentively. “But plastic is in so many things that we need, like bottles and bags. How can we use less plastic?” “It’s not hard,” explained Nandini, eagerly. She pointed to the table beside her. “We brought these things to show you. Stainless steel bottles and glasses are better than plastic, and you can reuse them many times. You even get steel straws these days!” People came forward to look at the things the girls had brought. “So, really, we need to make better choices about what we use,” said one young woman, holding up a paper straw. “I could use the same cloth bag every time I go grocery shopping, rather than a new plastic bag from the shop each time?” suggested a man. “Exactly!” cried the girls. As the meeting came to a close, everyone in the park was busy chatting about what they could do differently. Nandini overheard some children saying they would ask for second-hand toys, rather than buy more plastic ones. “What a great idea,” thought Nandini, smiling. Kavitha and Nandini were really pleased. “I think we’ve made a real difference,” Nandini beamed. The girls were playing in the park the next day. Suddenly, they heard a loud ‘quacking’ sound. It was the duck! And she wasn’t alone. Waddling behind her were eight little ducklings! “Wow!” cried Nandini, but not as loudly as Kavitha who had spotted her lost ball rolling next to the ducks! Grinning with happiness, the girls walked home from the park. Suddenly, without warning, Nandini lost her balance on a loose paving stone and fell onto her knees. “Ouch” she cried, “I’ve scraped my knee.” “Don’t worry, we’ll clean it up at home,” said Kavitha, “…and then let’s see if we can talk to the local corporator at the Municipal Corporation about these loose paving stones.” Kavitha and Nandini were active citizens in their community. They took responsibility for issues in their local community and helped to resolve them. Kavitha and Nandini saved the duck and worked with the Municipal Corporation to clean up the park. They also then educated other people (citizens) in their community about the problems with using plastic. They brought about a positive change in their community. There are many ways you can be an active citizen. Below is a pledge you can take to show your commitment to being an active citizen. I ……………………………………………. take the Active Citizenship Pledge. I am a citizen of India. I care about my responsibilities and my rights. I care about my friends, family and my community. I respect the rules of my city and my country. I pledge to: • Take care of my school, parks, playgrounds and other public spaces. • Treat everyone with respect. • Save water and electricity at home, school and wherever I go. • Follow road safety and traffic rules. • Segregate waste and always throw garbage in the dustbin. • Use public transport. • Minimise use of plastic materials.
author: Katie Pyle

" i cannot eat you as you look so ugly and dark, my tummy will ache if i eat you and you sound so horrible and i would also talk like you kaaw..kaaww " Wicked women releases the crow from the cage. " i cannot eat you as you look so ugly and dark, my tummy will ache if i eat you and you sound so horrible and i would talk like you kaaw..kaaww ", says wicked women and releases the crow from the cage. title: The Family Feud
text: Once there were two families who lived in a village. The two families were the Aditi and Diti families. All the people in the village knew that both families were rivals and had a generations-long feud, though the Aditi family didn’t want to be rivals. Nobody remembered what that feud was about or which family started it, but the hatred of each other followed for generations. Both families refused to ever leave the village after education and loved their home village. Both families consisted of a single mother and two female kids who were twins. The Aditi family was a nice and peaceful family who wished the feud could end. Their twin girls, Aditu and Adita, frequently tried to be on good terms with the Diti families twin girls, Ditu and Dita. Aditu and Adita had been taught by their mother to spread happiness and get rid of hatred and feuds as it could only harm. Sadly, Ditu and Dita were taught to preserve the honour of the elders, which they took as upholding the families' feud. Meanwhile, both twin pairs had finished their studies and graduated. Ditu decided to become an artist, and Dita pursued her dream of being a chemical biologist. At the same time, Aditu had decided to become an Emergency Medical Responder (EMR) and Adita had decided to become a doctor specialising in Emergency Treatment, as they both wanted to help people. One fateful day, Ditu got into a serious car accident, and she was almost fatally injured. Ditu was bleeding profusely, unresponsive and not breathing, almost on the verge of death. Dita was informed by her friend who was at the scene and arrived almost immediately to the accident zone, sobbing crazily. She and her sister were poor and couldn’t get insurance. Dita thought that Aditu (the only EMR in the village) wouldn’t treat her sister because she didn’t have to, as the law stated that Emergency Medical Responders (EMRs) didn’t have to treat if they didn’t want to. She was also scared she couldn’t pay the doctor fees and save her twin. Just after a few minutes, Aditu arrived at the scene of the emergency with her ambulance, and to the shock of the village people and Ditu’s twin sister Dita, Aditu started treatment on Ditu and was able to resuscitate her and keep her alive during the trip to the hospital, with Dita crying and worrying that she couldn’t afford treatment. Once they arrived at Adita's hospital, Adita didn’t allow Ditu to be admitted at first. She then remembered her mother’s advice and saw Dita’s tears flowing down her face, and thought about how much she loved her twin. Adita relented and treated Ditu’s injuries. Ditu soon recovered after receiving two months of expensive treatment for free in the ICU and recovered from her almost fatal injuries, which included excessive blood loss, head trauma, broken ribs and neck, and severe deep cuts. At last, Ditu and Dita learnt that conflicts should be put behind, and the generations-long family feud was over. Ditu and Dita thanked Aditu and Adita profusely and established a strong friendship with Aditu and Adita. Their families lived in peace and harmony for generations to come! Moral of the Story: Hatred can only harm, so we should always forgive others.
author: Yoga Jay

title: Sheela Donates Her Frocks
text: Rakesh asked his wife Neeta, “Neeta have you sorted out all the old clothes for donation?” Neeta said, “Yes Rakesh. I have some old sarees, your pants and shirts, and a few of Sheela’s frocks. I have arranged them on the table.” Sheela heard her mom's voice and came to the hall. Sheela asked, “Who are you giving away my frocks to, ma?” Neeta said, “We have clothes which we have not been using for a long time. Some of your old frocks you used just once or twice. So, we are planning to give it away to an NGO that collects such clothes to give to poor people.” *NGO means Non-Governmental Organization Sheela said,” But, anyway they are not new clothes.” Rakesh said, ”Yes. But some people still need such gently-used clothes. The NGO will again clean and process these clothes before giving to the poor people.” Sheela said, "Ok Dad. I'm so happy to give my clothes to help poor people." The calling bell rang. Rakesh said, “The man has come to collect the clothes. Put all the clothes in the bag.” Neeta put all the clothes into a bag. Neeta opened the door and handed over the clothes bag to the man from the NGO. Did You Know? You can donate your rarely-used or gently-used clothes to Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) that distribute the clothes to the poor and needy. Some flat associations organize drives when they collect old clothes from all the members of the flat. The flat association then hands over the clothes to a person from the NGO. If the clothes are torn, they are sent to places where they recycle clothes. Otherwise, they send the clothes to self-help groups that make small bags or pouches out of the clothes. Hope you will continue donating your clothes that were used just once or twice and are in good condition.
