title: A Dog Called Shoo
text: “Shoo!” cried a man on a bike. “Get out of my way.” “Shoo!” yelled a mother. “Stray dog, beta. Don’t touch it.” “Shoo!” shouted the owner of the coffee shop. “Don’t scare my customers away.” The little brown dog shrank into a dark corner. Everybody always said, “Shoo!” So she began to think that was her name. Shoo hadn’t always lived on the streets. She had once lived with a family. The boy threw terrible tantrums all the time. “Show me a trick!” “Bring me that stick!” “Up on your legs!” But Shoo didn’t know how to perform any tricks. She was scared. Soon, the boy got bored with Shoo. It was time for a new toy. One day, the father left Shoo at the bus stand and drove away. Shoo waited and waited. But he never came back. The dirt of the streets stuck to Shoo’s fur. Slowly, Shoo learnt to dig for food in the bins. First, it was hot and sticky. Then, it was wet and chilly. Cold and hungry, Shoo lay by the rubbish heap. One day, she spotted Adit walking down the street. He came closer and looked at Shoo. He pulled out a lunch box from his school bag. There were still some idlis left. Every day after that, Adit would share his lunch with Shoo. In the beginning, Shoo was shy. She would wait for Adit to leave before she gobbled up her food. But soon, she began to jump up with a little yap when she heard the sound of Adit’s shoes. Thap, thap, thap. One day, as Adit turned to go home, Shoo followed him. Every time he looked back, Shoo would hide behind a pushcart, a tree, a scooter. Adit stuck his hands in his pockets and whistled as he walked. When Adit reached home, he said, “Papa, look, we have a guest! Can she stay with us?” Shoo followed Adit everywhere. She sat outside the bathroom while Adit sang in the shower. When Adit went to school, she lay at the front door, waiting. Shoo worried. What if Adit went away? What if he never returned? A year flew by. Shoo and Adit became best friends. Shoo understood that if Adit ever went out, he would always come back. Shoo had a new name now. “Toffee, give me back my book!”
author: Kavitha Punniyamurthi

title: Noni and Poltu
text: Miss said, Toll dogs will be caught and loaded onto trucks and taken away'. Noni loves dogs. Grandpa says," Dogs are our best friends". Noni has also kept a dog at home - Poltu. Poltu is a nimble puppy. He is laughing. Grandpa gave it to Noni as a gift. Since then, Noni and Poltu have been very close. Poltu is growing fast. It has also been a little naughty. She likes Noni very much. Noni always plays with him after school. Noni feeds him and takes him outside. Noni also feeds her community's street dog. At first, she was afraid of street dogs. Some were scary looking. Gradually Noni started giving them milk and bread and they became his friends. Now seeing Noni, they don't bark. Noni told Grandpa what Miss had said at school. "I don't like the idea of ​​catching dogs and taking them away. Is there any way to keep them here, Grandpa? ” Grandpa smiled and said, “There is a way. We're not even trying! ” "How are you, Grandpa?" "Let's write a letter to the Animal Development Board asking for help." Grandfather said. "Can they save the street dogs?" Noni asked. "They can show us what to do." Grandfather said. Grandpa reassured him, "Now run with Poltu and tell the postman's uncle to send this letter by express mail." I am sure that the Animal Development Board will help us to find some solution to this problem. ” "Smile, thank you, Grandpa!" Noni hugged Grandpa. Grandpa reassured him, "Now run with Poltu and tell the postman's uncle to send this letter by express mail." I am sure that the Animal Development Board will help us to find some solution to this problem. ” "Smile, thank you, Grandpa!" Noni hugged Grandpa. Noni and Poltu went to the post office. On the way, Noni added a letter from herself and Poltu to her grandfather's letter: "Please save my friends." Noni and Poltu's request. ' When the mail arrived, Noni handed the letter to the postman. Noni also explained the importance of the letter. "We'll send this letter right away, Noni." Said the postman's uncle. A few days later, the postman's uncle returned with a letter for Noni. It was sent by the Animal Development Board. The Animal Development Board has decided to vaccinate the dogs of Noni toll and send the slightly sick dogs to the animal shelter. The board also suggested that noni dogs could be registered as volunteers after 15 years of age. Grandpa read the letter and told Noni. Noni jumped for joy. Together with Poltu and Noni, we have not only been able to save other dogs, but also to make people aware of dogs.
author: Samipya Jha

title: Didi's Colorful Treasure
text: There was a large ground near his house. The field was of a strange type. There were no trees, no plants, just garbage was garbage. The entire city was full of thrown things and filth. Those children did not go to school. The whole day was spent walking in the field. Used to search for plastic bottles. Used to remove the pieces of cloth… They knew a lot about waste. One day, Didi came to the garbage field. A red scarf was draped around the neck. She sat in a place, staring at the wandering children. She started looking at something from her bag. At first the children were staring from a distance. Then came a little closer and started looking. Didi had plenty of books. Thick, thin, colorful, full of stories. The children kept coming closer. At first the children were staring from a distance. Then came a little closer and started looking. Didi had plenty of books. Thick, thin, colorful, full of stories. The children kept coming closer. Let's make Didi's place beautiful. The children brought a chair-table from the trash. Someone brought a rug, some curtain. Brought some piece of luggage from somewhere, which was also found in the trash. Didi did not come one day. The next day did not come either. Troubled children kept waiting. Started reading the book in many things. They started reading and teaching others by himself One day they finds Didi's address in the book. The children immediately set out in search of Didi. Do not forget to carry a bag of books together. While searching, the children read the number of a bus. While walking, I understood the name of that road. Because Didi had taught them all. Where is Didi's house? Where is it? Children got upset after searching. Going back tired, someone saw a red scarf. Didi was lying on the bed. She was looking sick and sad. There was neither a smile nor a glow on the face. The doctor gave medicine. But the didi was not getting well. The children ran and reached there. Didi was hugged. Showed them a bag of books. Children read something. Didi smiled again. The glow of his eyes started coming back. Now the didi is coming again. All the children are beginning to gather. Have started meeting everyday in the evening. Have started laughing and reading a lot. Together, children have started having fun, children, sisters and their books!
author: adwitya bahl

title: The Drawing Competition (Part 1)
text: "Wake up!" said Jeff the Hippo. "It's Saturday. Go away." Snorted Helen the Donkey. Helen was wondering why did Jeff wanted her to wake up early. "Why is Jeff making me wake up early on a sweet Saturday morning?" Helen thought. "I want to show you this amazing poster at the sidewalk!" Jeff explained to Helen. "Ugh, fine." Helen agreed. When Jeff & Helen arrived to the sidewalk, Helen stared at the poster in shock. It was a Drawing Competition! "JEFF! Why didn't you tell me it was a drawing competition?!?" shouted Helen while staring at Jeff. "Well, I tried to wake you up but, you didn't listen to me!" argued Jeff. "Well anyway, how do you get in the competition Jeff?" questioned Helen. "Well, the instructions say that you draw your best drawing and sent it to them on Outlook." Jeff explained to Helen. Helen was pretty excited and anxious at the same time. When Jeff left, Helen saw an another Hippo that she didn't know. "Hello.." said Helen The mysterious hippo dragged Helen into a car. "HELP, HELP! Someone get me out of here!!!"
author: Gabriel Tong
illustrator: Jess  Jardim-Wedepohl; Rajiv Eipe; Wiehan de Jager

title: Arun Goes To Market
text: Arun’s mom dried his wet hair. She said, “Now put on your best clothes. We are going to the market today.” Arun said, “Sure mom,” and ran to his bedroom to dress up. Arun and his mom carried few bags and reached the Bahut Achha market. Arun said, “There are so many shops here.” Arun’s mom said, “Let us first buy some vegetables for this week.” She bought 1 kilo of tomatoes and onions, half a kilo of potatoes and carrots, half lettuce, and a bottle gourd. They kept walking in the market and reached a toy shop. Arun said, “Mom, please buy me a cricket ball. Mine has become old." They got the ball and paid money at the bill counter. They kept walking in the market and came near a fish stall. Mom said,” Arun, I’m going to buy your favourite seer fish and fry it today. I know you like them as they do not have small bones.” They bought 1-kilo seer fish and put it in their bags. Next, they reached a grocery shop. “5 kilos raw rice and three packets of 1-liter sunflower refined oil,” said Arun’s mom to the shopkeeper. The man packed the things and Arun's mom paid. Next, they reached a shop selling garments. Arun said, “Mommy, can we buy pant cloth for me and dad in the same colour? We are planning to wear matching dress on my birthday.” Next, they walked through the market and reached a utensils shop. “We don’t need any new utensils, Arun. But, I just wanted you to know the many things that are sold at a utensils shop. Vessels, plates, spoons, sieves, coconut shredder, and many more.” Next, they went to an oil depot. Arun’s mom said, “Please give a liter of coconut oil.” Then they walked past a dairy shop that was selling milk products. Finally, they happily walked out of the market area with all the bags filled with things.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The Best Birthday Present
text: It was nearly time for Bora's graduation day. Her mother took her to town, to choose her dream dress. Bora tried on many dresses that day. Finally she chose her favorite dress by her own for graduation day. When they were leaving the shop, Bora saw a very beautiful necklace. She wanted that necklace so much. But her mommy has not enough money to buy that necklace. "It is lovely, my angel. But, right now I don't have enough money to buy it. So, later I will buy it for you, dear" said her mother. Bora did not give up to buy it. She decided to save money and buy that necklace herself. She put all her pocket money in a piggy bank under her bed. "I will wear that necklace on my graduation day" thought Bora. Eventually, she had saved enough money and bought the necklace. Then, Bora remembered that very soon it was her mommy's birthday. "Oh! I have spend all my money, what will I give her?" she wondered to herself. Bora was very excited on the morning of her mommy's birthday. "Happy Birthday, Mommy!" she said, and giving a present to her mother. Her mommy opened the present box and surprisingly found the beautiful necklace that Bora liked so much. Mommy hugged her daughter and said, "I love you, my angel! You are my BEST BIRTHDAY PRESENT! ".
author: Khin Zar Chi Oo
illustrator: Balaram Mandal; Khin Zar Chi Oo

title: Amazing stories
text: Prudence stays up Prudence the kitten was very exited. Mommy had promised to take her hunting by the light of moon. I can't wait! I can't wait! meowed Prudence, running around in circles. You can only go if you take a nap this afternoon, warned Mommy Cat. "Otherwise you will be very tired" But prudence was much very exited to take a nap. When it was afternoon Prudence was busy to tell everyone in farm that " I AM A BIG GIRL NOW" By dusk everyone knew that she was going to hunting but she was no where to be found. Where could she be? Suddenly Mommy cat heard a snoring noise. It was Prudence all things had warned her out. Mommy cat smiled, Never mind there is always tomorrow. What's in a name Once upon a time a mongoose asked to a tailor bird. Hi, tailor bird, he said. Then he asked why are you called tailor bird. The tailor bird said,I am too much busy please wait. The mongoose saw as she perched tiny holes into two huge leaves. Then she flew and brought some silk from spider webs and sewed it into the tiny holes she had made in the leaves just like a tailor! When it was done the tailor bird asked do you still wonder why am I called tailor bird? No, said the mongoose I can see it. ' You are called tailor bird because you sew just like a tailor he said aloud. The Thrush It was winter and Tufty the thrush lived in a home of a happy family. She enjoyed seeing the children playing joyfully. When spring arrived she realized she needed some place safe from the playful cat to built a nest. Tufty searched and searched until she found an old teapot on the shelf of a window. After couple of days she had 5 eggs. After few more days they hatched. One day the oldest boy found the thrush's new family. He closed the door so the playful cat can not come. It wasn't long when they were ready to make a trip to the garden. She led them down to much the juicy worms and watch the children play. The boys cried" LOOK AT OUR THRUSH'S NEW FAMILY" Dear reader, I want to tell you that from now on ward I am going to write stories about one fantastic mouse. It would not have pictures but I am sure you would like it. But before you read it I will publish a book name introduction and in that you will meet each and every mouse which would come in the story. And I promise that I will do publish the first book and introduction in 5 April to 20 April and that's a promise. See you soon
author: Swara Sutariya
illustrator: Kalyani  Ganapathy; Samit  Shrestha; Santoshi Sahu; Siddhi   Vartak; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Sunaina  Coelho; Swara Sutariya

title: The Boy And The Turtle
text: On a summer vacation, a boy and his father had gone to a beach. They saved the dying creatures, and kept them under their hotel cottage room The boy found an old book in the beach, and learnt how to speak to animals from that book. One day, a fisherman caught a 188 year old turtle. It was wrinkled and suffered to get out and go back to the sea! The boy saw the turtle and went running to his dad and told that a fisherman had caught a 188 year old turtle! The boys father who was a Animal Safety Officer, went down with the boy and when they reached the place, the boy said "STOP!!!! DON'T DO THAT!!!!". The fisherman replied, "What's your problem?" The boys father replied, you have done a crime by catching a turtle over the age of 50. I am an Animal Safety Officer." Leave him now!! said the stern voice of the boys father. The crowd got scared and scattered away. The boy ran to the turtle and whispered, you will be let out! The turtle got relieved and got relaxed. Then the fisherman left the turtle in the sea and went back grumpily. The boy and the father than went to the hotel restaurant and treated themselves with an ice-cream for saving another life
author: Vihaan Sandur

title: Learning to help
text: I always want to help. I like helping and being helpful. I can help my little brother. It makes him happy, and it makes me happy. I help my mom, and she helps me. Together, we work as a team to get ready quickly in the morning. In the afternoon, I help my dad at the store. When I help him, I learn a lot about everything that's sold at the store. But sometimes I make mistakes, and play with things I shouldn't play with. My mom gets upset that I don't treat her things carefully. Other times I have accidents. My dad gets mad that I break his things. When I make a mistake or have an accident I get sad. Reading a book sometimes helps me feel better. But what always makes me happy is being with my grandma. She says that EVERYONE makes mistakes and that we have accidents because we're learning. Just like my brother, who's little, and still doesn't know how to set the table. He makes a lot of mistakes, and has a lot to learn! I'm already big and can do a lot of stuff. But sometimes I need help from a stool or from my parents. It's fun helping others, even if I sometimes make mistakes,
author: Miles Rodriguez

title: Mars
text: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, being larger than only Mercury. In English, Mars carries the name of the Roman god of war and is often referred to as the " Red Planet ". [16] [17] The latter refers to the effect of the iron oxide prevalent on Mars's surface, which gives it a reddish appearance distinctive among the astronomical bodies visible to the naked eye. [18] Mars is a terrestrial planet with a thin atmosphere, with surface features reminiscent of the impact craters of the Moon and the valleys, deserts and polar ice caps of Earth. a thin atmosphere, with surface features reminiscent of the impact craters of the Moon and the valleys, deserts and polar ice caps of Earth.
author: Arnav Kulkarni

title: Apricot and Peach
text: They like each other a lot. Peach and Apricot have a little dream. They want to live in the same house so they can see each other every day. It must be so fun. Peach is a cooking queen, and Apricot is a foodie. In the morning, Peach cooks delicious food and Peach makes coffee. They have similar taste, so they can eat both Chinese and Korean food well. Today, they are going to each French style bread and fried eggs! Apricot loves and is good at drawing. Their house would be full of her drawings. Peach is Apricot's number one fan and always supports her drawings. Peach believes more people will like her drawings in the future. Apricot and Peach have same hobbies. They both love to knit and watch movies. That is why they will watch movies while knitting. They can both make airpod cases and hats. Now, it's time to go out. Apricot and Peach and both getting ready while listening to their favorite songs. Peach usually gets ready quickly, but Apricot is slow. However, Peach always waits for Apricot. That day, Peach and Apricot went to a Korean restaurant to eat pork belly. Out of all side dishes, Apricot loves radish and Peach loves cucumber. It's good that they will never have to fight for food. They are happy to eat delicious meat. Roommates have to go get groceries together. Apricot wants to eat so many of things that Peach tells her to choose only three. After buying their favorite snacks, it's time to go home. The summer night breeze is very nice. Peach and Apricot's favorite drama is on television right now. They are excited to see it on sofa. Of course, they have their midnight snack ready. Today, they are going to eat Chimaek (Chicken and Beer). They both have the same thoughts, "Diet starts tomorrow." The moonlight is pretty and the night air is good. It's time to go to sleep. Although they use the same room, they have two beds. Peach's bed is purple, and Apricot's bed is yellow. They would probably fall asleep fast while chatting together, right? I hope so. 'Good night', my friend. Although they can't achieve this little dream right now, but they believe it will come true someday. Even right now, they are waiting for that day to come while living is separate places. Small happiness always starts from small things. About the author: Hello, I'm Stephanie Son. I am Chinese and currently is a junior at University of Washington. I love to dance and cook. When I have time, I also listen to music and watch movies. This is a true story of me and my friend.
author: Claire Park
illustrator: Amrita Dasgupta; Chaaya Prabhat; Gieve Patel; Jodi Williams; Kripa B; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Riana Mavity; Rosalyn  koopa-shaser; Stephanie Sun; Sudhir Patwardhan; Suman  Maharjan

title: Island Exploration
text: Joseph is sleeping right now. Ahh~bibimbap..bulgogi..soft tofu soup..sounds delicious~~ Suddenly, he woke up in an island! Uh...Where am I? Which island is it? Where is my family? I need to call them. But, where is my phone???? (voice): Oh! you finally woke up. We waited for a long time. Please hurry. Joseph: Um, who are you? Do you know this place???? (voice): Don't worry! Come inside! Joseph: Is..it okay? Where are you taking me? *Joseph goes inside the building and talks with the travel agent.* Tom: This is our new island! Joseph: A new island? Tom: You can fish, catch bugs, meet friends, build a house...you can do a lot of things here! Joseph: But, how do I meet my family and friends? What about my past life? Tom: You don't have to worry! Your family is doing well. This is a fun place with a lot of things to do! Let's first look at the tools. Chapter 2: There are a lot of trees! Joseph: I'm a little bored...What should we do? Joseph: I want to take a walk while looking at trees! ﻿Joseph: Wow, there are a lot of trees here. It's really beautiful! Joseph: We cut trees to make different tools.﻿ ﻿ * two hours have passed* Joseph: If I use this tree, I can make a fishing rod, shovel, and a ladder! Joseph: The weather is hot, and I worked a lot, so I'm very tired and hungry. What do I do? Joseph: Oh, I'm going to fish now! Chapter 3: Joseph goes fishing! Joseph: What fish should I catch? Joseph: Wow! It's a bass! Joseph: This must be delicious. You can make a lot of dishes. *He is dreaming of food while napping.* Joseph: What time is it? It's a little late. I will then go home and cook this fish. *Joseph went home and cooked the fish, and ate it well.* Joseph: This fish is really good! But, I'm very tired right now, so I'm going to sleep. Chapter 4: Joseph meets friends! Hamlet: Wow! You are a newcomer. Excuse me, but who are who? What's your name? Joseph: I'm Joseph. Who are you? Hamlet: I'm Hamlet. Nice to meet you. I started living in this island two years ago. The life here is so fun. Joseph: Oh, really? Isn't this fun a little weird? How do you spend your time? Hamlet: Weird? Not at all! Try swimming or doing sports! Exercise or try meeting a lot of new people. Joseph: Sounds fun! I don't have a house right now. Do you want to build it with me? Hamlet: Sure! Shall we go? Joseph: Yes! Let's go! Chapter 5: Build a house with a friend! Hamlet: I don't like this house...It's too small...Shall we decorate it together?! Joseph: What should do first? Hamlet: Use the tree you cut last week. Joseph: What color should I use? Hamlet: How about blue or white? Joseph: Let's make the bedroom here! Hamlet: Yes, do you have a window, chair, and a bed? Joseph: Yes, I have them. *Joseph and friend build the house until night.* Joseph: The house looks cool! I love it! Chapter 6: Explore the museum Joseph: Look! Is it a new museum? Hamlet: Oh really? Should we go together? James: Welcome! This is a new museum. If you are interested in history, there are a lot of things to see. Hamlet: How much is the ticket? James: It's ten bells. Joseph: Oh right, we didn't buy the tickets. Can we purchase them? James: Of course! *Joseph and Hamlet buy tickets and go into the museum.* ﻿Joseph: Wow, the fish are very big! Can you please take a picture of me? Ring Ring...Hamlet is calling. Hamlet: Excuse me, but who are you? Another friend: I'm Joseph's friend. I prepared a party. Please come! Hamlet: Okay! We'll go now! Chapter 7: Congratulations on your new life! Joseph: Wow, this island is so clean and has a beautiful view! Hamlet: If you were not here, we would not be having fun! *Looks like someone familiar came.* Tom: You came! Please come this way. There are fruits and cookies. Joseph: Why are we celebrating? Tom: When there is a newcomer in our island, we always hold a party. Joseph: Thank you for bringing me to this island. I love the people here, and there are a lot of fun things to do! Tom: Thank later, and look at the camera for now. We are going to take a picture! ~The End~ Introducing the Authors Kim, William (Kim Jae Yoon) Hello! I'm a senior at the University of Washington. I am 20 years old, and my hometown is Kent in Washington state. I'm learning computer engineering at the University of Washington. After this semester, I'm going to work at Microsoft! Also, we learned Korean and wrote this book together! The reason I want to learn Korean is to talk with my family. I'm a little said that I can't talk well in Korean with my parents. These days, I don't really work out outside, but I run at the park every week. I like to skate, play tennis, and play the guitar. Thank you for reading our book! Chen, Austin Hello everyone! I'm Austin from California. I'm currently a senior at the University of Washington. Although my major is computer engineering, I started learning Korean, because I'm very interested in Korean history. It's been a year since I started learning. I'm not Korean so I think it's very difficult. Therefore, I study Korean for about two hours everyday. I am taking Korean class at my university. This June, I will graduate. I want to travel to Korea and will continue to study it. Hope you enjoy reading our book!
author: Claire Park

title: College Life of a Girl
text: I will start talking about the college life of a woman. This story starts in 2019, September. September 24, Tuesday "Wow...it's my first day..." Harjot said to her sister. "Are you ready? Do you know where your classes are?" Harjot's sister, Jasgon asked. "Of course! I already checked a week ago! I'm just nervous..." said Harjot. "Of what?" asked Jasgon. "I have a cold right now. What if I take the subway too late? What if I can't find my classes?" "Gosh! You are fine! You are smart! I'm sure you will do well!" "Really? I'm still worried.." The next day, September 25, Wednesday "Ooh! The weather is nice!" said Harjot as she went out of the classroom. Harjot sent a text to her friend. "Where are you?" Harjot's friend, Nasmoon replied. "Front of the library." Harjot also sent a message, "Okay, I'll be there in five minutes! What restaurant do you want to eat lunch at?" "Anywhere! You choose." "Alright! Then let's choose at the Avenue." Nasmoon replied, "Okay!" 5 minutes later "Hey! Long time no see! Oh! Arminata is also here! Have have you been?!" said Harjot to two people. "Wow!! Hello! Right, it's been a while!" replied Arminata. "Yes! I've been well!" said Nasmoon. "Let's hurry! I'm so hungry!" said Harjot. Arminata replied. "Yes, let's go!" The three girls found a good restaurant while walking at the Avenue. The name of the restaurant was Aladdin Gyro-Cery & Deli. This is a very famous restaurant. Although there were a lot of people in line, the three girls waited in line. While eating, Arminata said, "Since I have class in 15 minutes, I'll leave early!" Nasmoon also said, "Me too! Let's go!" Harjot also replied, "Yes, I have a part-time job now, so I was going to go too. Let's go!" The two girls went back to college, and Harjot took the subway to go home. After he part-time job, she went home. After showering and eating dinner, she went to sleep. November 11, Friday Today is Harjot's birthday! She became 19 years old today. She had too many classes, so she could not meet her friends. After class, she had to hurry home to turn in her essay. She celebrated with her family with a cake. The fall semester ended early and winter break came early. Before the end of fall semester, Harjot and her friends went to Jay Park's Concert. It was so exciting. Harjot spent her winter break by working part-time jobs. All she did was studying and working, so time passed by quickly. However, Harjot's classes were a little hard for her. Therefore, she had a difficult time. Harjot decided her major. She wanted to major in communication and minior in art history, because she was interested in them. February 12 Harjot went to the new art museum, because of art history class. She had to go alone since her friends were busy. There were Asia's paintings and sculptures. Harjot liked Indian paintings the most, they were the most memorable. Spring semester-present Harjot was looking forward to this semester. However, because of coronavirus, they take classes online. It's very difficult to learn through online. Even though Harjot is working part-time jobs, she does not feel happy. The life is very strange right now. We don't know when it will end. Harjot is very worried. She hopes coronavirus goes away soon. Hello! I'm Harjot. I'm 19 years old. I studied Korean at my college for a year. When I have time, I watch Korean dramas and entertainment shows. This is a portrait of me drawn by my friend.
author: Claire Park

title: Things I Love
text: I live in the United States of America. I'm at San Antonio and I like it. I like San Antonio, because the sky is pretty. The flowers are also very pretty. I love Korean food so much. I especially like dumplings and galbi. These are the dumplings I made. They are very delicious. I also like galbi very much. I ate this galbi with my friend in Korea. It was so delicious. author: Claire Park

title: Hakeem's Hiccups
text: In the bylanes of Sabzi Bazaar, Amidst the rows of drying achaar, Mixing powders and potions in pots of clay, Hakeem sahib was busy seeing patients all day. By evening the Hakeem’s lips were chapped. His tummy was rumbling like a thunder clap. A glass of water would have been divine. But he was fasting, and it wasn’t yet time. Listening to Sodawala’s tick-tocking heart, Hakeem found his pulse was two beats apart. As Hakeem sahib reached for his white pepper antidote, He felt a bubble race all the way up his throat. Hic hic hic! Oh my, oh dear. I’ll hold my breath, I’ll pull my ear. His hiccups came and went, This was a most unusual event. Hic hic hic! Examining Machhiwali’s pale yellow eye, Hakeem sahib wrote out a nuska for rye. “Hold your breath, pull your ear.” Oh my, oh dear. Hic hic hic! Mithaiwala showed up with a wart on his chest. The Hakeem said a haldi poultice would work best. “Hold your breath, pull your ear.” Hic hic hic! Oh my, oh dear. Snap. Crackle. Pop! Keep calm. Hakeem sahib was setting the bone in Sabziwala’s arm. “Hold your breath, pull your ear.” Oh my, oh dear. Hic hic hic Little Munna came crying with a tummy ache, “Ajwain and saunf for you, and no more cake!” “Hold your breath, pull your ear.” Oh my, oh dear. H ic hic hic! As the hic-hic-hiccuping Hakeem locked up for the day, He was surprised to see… his patients in the way! With colourful platters of food, each swore To have a foolproof remedy of yore. Machhiwali had cooked a fiery red stew, With spicy fish roasted on the barbeque. Sodawala had made a special lemonade, Brimming with fizz and pomegranate. Mithaiwala had brought a basket of roat, Crunchy and sweet to coat the throat. Sabziwala got karela by the kilogram, Something bitter to push down the diaphragm. As they argued as to which cure was best, Out jumped a ghost, stirring unrest! Machhiwali screamed, Sodawala jumped in fear, Hic-hic, said the Hakeem loud and clear. Hakeem sahib pulled off the white sheet, And Munna beat a hasty retreat. “Why? Oh, why this silly horseplay?” “Amma says a good fright will scare the hiccups away!” But wait, where did Hakeem sahib disappear? Wasn’t he just… umm… right here? Everyone peeked inside an open door, Where Hakeem sahib’s family sat cross-legged upon the floor. Hand on his heart, he said, “Thank you, friends, for your kindness. I would now like you all to join us.” And, as if on cue, they all knew what to do. They put down their platters and sat cross-legged, too. Begum, Faria and Raheem brought cups and plates, And the family handed everyone some dates. As the azaan rang out from the east, They dived into the waiting feast. No more hic-hic-hiccuping Hakeem! But wait, why does he look like he ate some neem? “Oh no! I think a little bubble is stuck and now it’s quickly making its way up!” They all waited with bated breath, As Hakeem sahib let out a … Great... Big … BELCH! Hic
author: Sadaf Siddique

title: Monumental Maths
text: It had to be magnificent. Something no one had ever built before. Bigger than anything anyone had ever seen, or would ever see. It was to be a tomb fit for a king. A Pharaoh of Egypt. His body had to be preserved for eternity after his death because the ancient Egyptians believed that would help him pass safely through the afterlife. So they had to build a tomb that would last forever. The architects racked their brains for the perfect building plan. It had to be faultless. They couldn’t just build something as tall as 30 giraffes piled one on top of the other and wait to see if it stood. They looked to mathematics for the perfect plan. First things first — what shape should it be? Nothing fancy, and definitely not like a giraffe! Draw a cube and a pyramid, both with the same v olume. The pyramid is almost three times taller! Cube with side a = 2 cm Volume = a 3 = 8 cm 3 This definitely looks more impressive, while using the same amount of building material. So, the architects decided, a pyramid it would be! Pyramid with same base as the square but three times the height, that is, a = 2 cm h = 6 cm Volume = a 2 h/3 = 8 cm 3 First, they built a firm, square base to create a solid foundation. They built this layer with massive limestone and granite blocks, each one the size of a truck. Then they put another layer of blocks on top of this, but slightly smaller in area. On top of this went another square, still smaller — until smaller and smaller squares stacked on top of each other created a pyramid. The final piece at the top, a little pyramid by itself, sat elegantly, supported by the mathematically sound structure beneath it. Seven hundred years ago, Egypt was rocked by a powerful earthquake. Most of the newer buildings fell, but the pyramids stood strong. They are still standing strong. But would this tomb be strong enough to last forever? And then making some smaller triangles along the sides. A fractal is made by starting with a simple geometric shape, like a triangle. Over in another part of the world, southern Karnataka, a group of 11th-century Hoysala chieftains wanted to leave their mark on the world. They were not yet emperors, but growing stronger, and they wanted to show their expanding power. So, what else expands? A fractal geometric shape! And then some more little triangles on the sides of the smaller triangles. And then some more, making the design quite complex. A fractal expands outwards from a central point, becoming more detailed and intricate as it grows. Perhaps this is what the Hoysala architects had in mind when they built their temples on platforms to create an effect of movement and grandeur. Like the Kedareshwara temple at Halebidu, built on a staggered square platform. The temple also follows a s taggered pattern within t he platform boundaries, creating a dramatic effect. The architects got more c reative and played with different shapes. Like the s tar-shaped base of the Chennakeshava temple a t Somnathpura. Six hundred years after the Hoysalas, another architect used mathematics to create the effect of grandeur. Francesco Borromini had to build the 'ideal Italian corridor', measuring 99 feet long with a life-sized statue at the end, in the Palazzo Spada in Rome, Italy. But there was a problem. He only had 26 feet of space. So he used a technique called 'forced perspective'. He built pillars close to each other, and made them smaller and smaller in size as he moved towards the end of the corridor. He created a gentle slope for the floor. At the end of the corridor, he placed a child-sized statue. All these mathematical tricks combined to make the corridor look almost four times as long, and make the statue at the end appear double the size! Speaking of size, what would it be like to walk around inside a mathematical instrument that is as big as a house? This is exactly what the Rajput king Sawai Jai Singh built 300 years ago. Sawai Jai Singh, apart from being a ruler, was an astronomer and mathematician. He would calculate the movement of stars and planets using small brass instruments. But he was not very happy because they were not as precise and accurate as he wanted. To get better readings, he decided to make the instruments bigger than anyone had ever imagined! He built 19 structures that measure and predict the movement and position of the Sun, stars and planets. He also built the world’s largest sundial, standing 73 feet tall and 9 feet wide. This can be seen at the Jantar Mantar in Jaipur. For thousands of years, architects have used m athematics to create monuments that are really s trong. But that’s not all. Architects have used the concept of symmetry to design some of the most beautiful buildings in the world! The walls of the Keshava Temple in Somnathpur, Karnataka, are covered with intricate carvings that are like mirror images. Every part of the Taj Mahal is symmetrical. The building itself... Its reflection in the clear pool of water... The line of fountains bisecting the reflection... The gardens on either side of the structure... The patterns on the walls... The tiles on t he floor... Down to the last drain hole. Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest religious c omplex in the world. It is also symmetrical. The Mayan architects built the pyramid of Chichen I tza, Mexico, with symmetrical precision. It’s not just the main structure of the Brihadeshwara Temple in Tamil Nadu that is symmetrical... The designs carved on the vimana are symmetrical, too. When architects use mathematics in their designs, what do we get? Strength, grandeur, beauty and illusion! Like mathematics, these designs never grow old. The buildings built from these designs have stood for centuries and can still be seen today.
author: Veena Prasad

title: Minho's Amazing Day
text: Today is December 29th. Up until now, Minho's life was always normal. However, today, he will have the happiest day ever. Mom: Minho, why are you not up yet? Today is Monday. You have to go to school! Minho: I'm up now! Could you make breakfast please? Thank you! You are the best! Mom: Breakfast is ready! Wash up quickly and eat it with me. Minho: Okay. He finished his breakfast and got his backpack. Minho was ready now. He is now going to school. Mom: Are you sure you'll be fine? Is there enough time left? Minho: Yes! It only takes 10 minutes from home to school by bus. I'm fine! Bye! Minho waited for the bus at the bus station. He was worried because the bus was late. It's a relief that he was not late to school. All students are excited because winter break starts tomorrow. During recess, Minho talked with his best friend, Jihoon. Jihoon: Hey, Minho, what are you going to do during break? I'm going skiing with my dad. Minho: That sounds fun. I don't know yet. My mom didn't say anything about it. Jihoon: Why? That's weird. Usually people make plans one month before. Minho: Really? Jihoon: Maybe it's because you didn't do well on the last test. Your mom was really mad. Minho: Oh, that's right. Maybe that's why she didn't plan for the break. School ended. All the students had a smile on their face, because they have waited for this day for a long time. Jihoon: Bye! See you in three days! Minho: Bye Jihoon! Oh, mom! Why are you here? Mom: Hurry up and get in the car. I can't park here for long. Mom: Good job today son. Minho: What? You are scaring me, mom. Did I do something wrong? Mom: No you didn't. You are the best. Minho: Mom, why are you driving this way? This is not the right way. Mom: We are going to the airport. Minho: What? The airport? Mom: Yes, that's right. We are going to go to Jeju Island. Minho and his mom are in the car. Minho: This is awesome! Mom: Is there anything you want to do? Minho: I want to eat delicious food and see beautiful views. I also want to see the ocean. Mom: Okay, let's do all. Minho: Mom, you are not kidding right? Is this for real? Mom: Yes, your dad is waiting at the airport right now. He got the tickets and I booked a hotel with ocean view and reserved a good restaurant. Minho: I'm so happy right now. Why didn't you tell me before? Mom: This is called a surprise trip. Don't you feel excited? Yes: Yes, I like it very much! Today is a very good day. The trip to Jeju Island will also be very exciting. About author Hello. I'm So Jae Moon from China. My hobby is listening to K-pop and watching Korean entertainment shows. I have been learning Korean at UW because I wanted to travel to Korea and watch shows in Korean. I'm not fluent yet, but I will study very hard to be good at it. I'm a fan of a boy group WINNER, so I named the main character as Minho. This was my first time writing a book in Korean. Thank you for reading.
author: Claire Park
illustrator: 211 Studio; Angie & Upesh; Brad Cuzen; Deepa Balsavar; Dr. Sushma  Singh; Ekta Bharti; Fahad Faizal; George Supreeth; Jiwen Xiao; Lindy  Pelzl; Linh Chi; Padmanabh; Rijuta Ghate; Ruchi Shah; Students of  Himalayan Public School; Tanvi Bhat

title: Supermarket
text: I dedicate this book to my dad. Dad, have fun reading this.﻿ I'm a rabbit. My family is very fun. I have a lot of younger siblings. My family is big! The family is hungry. So, we go to the supermarket. I am at the supermarket. I want to buy fruits. I love apples, bananas, and grapes. However, my younger siblings do not like bananas. So, I buy apples and grapes. Wait! There is someone next to the fruits. It's Cat! Cat is my friend. "Cat, how are you? What have you been up to?" "Hi Rabbit. I'm doing well. I'm busy, so see you later!" "Okay, goodbye!" ﻿ ﻿About the author: My name is Alexis Pusky. I'm an American high school senior. I love to dance.
author: Claire Park

title: Rabbit's Days
text: Rabbit loves to ski and watch movies. She lives with her five families. Rabbit has parents, grandma, and one younger sister. January 6th-- Rabbit's Hobbies Rabbit likes to cook whenever there is time. Rabbit likes Korean good and is interested in Korean culture. She is also studying Korean very hard at school to visit Korea next year. Studying Korean is fun, but grammar and pronunciation is a little hard. So, she is looking for a friend who can help her study Korean for about one to two hours every week. January 16th-- Rabbit's Birthday Today is Rabbit's birthday, so she is planning to have a party at home. The party starts at seven. Rabbit invited her friends, bought a cake, and finished getting ready for the party. It's a relief that all the invited friends can come! She is thankful for all the presents, but she wants a hat and a bag. February 1st-- School Day Today, there are morning classes from eight. Every Monday and Friday classes start early. She went to sleep early yesterday to wake up early. Rabbit gets ready for school. She eats breakfast with her family at about six, and goes to school. Today's weather is nice. She walks to school while listening to music. March 10th-- Short Trip Rabbit came to Vancouver yesterday. Before coming, she bought a bus ticket, got her passport, booked a hotel, and exchanged money. She left on the night vacation started. It took about two hours to get to Vancouver. The weather was nice there, and there were many things to see. There were a lot delicious food, and the view was beautiful. She also met up with her friend and went shopping. Rabbit wants to go again. March 14th-- The Day Rabbit Met Her Friend Rabbit wants to eat dinner with her friend this weekend. She wants to talk and have a fun time. She is looking for a good restaurant nearby the school. The price is also cheap. The lady who owns it is very nice. She has to reserve in order to invite a lot of friends. April 1st-- Rabbit's Blog Rabbit's hobby is cooking and watching American movies. Rabbit and her friend watch movies and cook every Saturday. These days, Rabbit cooks everyday, because she has to stay home. She is not that good, but she posts pictures of her food on her blog. Visit Rabbit's blog often. April 15th-- Moving Day Rabbit's family is busy everyday to move. The current house was a little far from school. So, the family wanted to move. There are a lot of packages, so her parents' friends are helping. The friend invites them to dinner tomorrow evening when they finish moving. April 25th-- Korean Class Homework Today there is homework, and the theme is "Me in 10 Years". She am currently in Seattle, but she will be living in China ten years later. Rabbit is a student now, but she will be a data scientist and earn a lot of money. She also does not have a car right now, but she will be driving a Tesla ten years later. She lives with her family right now, but she will live with her husband, daughter, son, and cat in a pretty house. May 5th-- A Bad Day Rabbit can't go out because of coronavirus these days. She didn't feel good, because there are so much homework. She also can't go to school and meet her friends. She can't eat out either, so it's very tiring to cook everyday. These days, she does online shopping and buys a variety of things. Author's Biography: I am Rowen Liao from China. I'm a sophomore. I love the Korean Drama, "Inheritors". I love Korea, and I'm learning Korea to visit there. I am living alone in Seattle right now, and I'm looking for a Korean friend who can help me study. I can teach the Korean friend English or Chinese.
author: Claire Park
illustrator: Imphir; Juhi  Agarwal; San srei nou ch nou ch

title: Neighbourhood Dreams
text: Megha went to bed. Soon, she started dreaming. She saw different scenes of her neighbourhood in her dream. First, she saw the Gandhi park. Her friends were skipping, playing cricket, going down slides, swinging on swings, and climbing the jungle-gym climbers. She saw aunties and uncles sitting on the benches. Some men were doing laughter yoga. Others were walking around. There were tall trees in the park and there were blooms of orange, yellow, and violet flowers. A man was pushing his son in a wheelchair. People were standing in a queue at the ticket counter at The Paradise Cinema theater. The movie was a super hit. Wonder how many days it will run. Hey, look. There was a library. There was a book shop selling books. And there were so many roadside book shops. They had spread the second-hand and low-cost books on the road and people were browsing the books. The marketplace was buzzing with activity. There were fruit sellers and chat shops. A dairy shop was selling dahi, milk, and paneer. Other men were walking and selling accessories and bags. There were also roadside cloth shops selling bales of cloth. Then, she looked into the school playground. Some children were playing Hopscotch. One girl was walking with under-arm crutches. But, her friend came happily running towards her to play. Megha then saw multistoried apartments on the roadside. There were water tanks on the terrace of a flat. Hey, there is a bakery. Then slowly her dream vanished and she continued to sleep.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: In the Land Where Beetles Rule
text: In the land where beetles rule Feet may not touch the ground. In the land where mice are men Huge hares hunt the hound. In the land of snowy owls Night and day are turned around. In the land of nightingales No other voice may sing or sound. In the land where humans rage Everyone goes underground. In the land where fish are first Oceans eat up all the ground. In the land where the full moon reigns Bats and acrobats astound. In the land where the spotted deer live Axes are barred, trees abound.
author: Suniti Namjoshi

title: Manu and his Grandma
text: One day Manu was playing games with his friend. Manu never listened to his mother or anyone, he just played games and would do what he wanted. He played games for an hour, would throw the things here and there. His mother was very tired of him. Manu went to the kitchen and asked "Ma, can I go to Grandma's house. Ma says no and says "Manu grandma may be too busy with her farm work, I think she might think bad in this busy time. He dosen't listen to his mother and goes to grandma's house. He talks a lot with grandma, he would only listen to his grandma. Grandma said why do you play games for a lot, and do not listen to your mother? He was stable and had no answer. She explained that we have to never be rude with others. I made a mistake Grandma he said. Then he plays little time with his friends and Grandma. He enjoys so much. Manu asks grandma can you come to my house? Grandma says yes. They reached home. Now Manu had learnt that we have to never be rude with anyone. He enjoys his dinner with his family and grandma and goes to sleep.
author: Julakanti Ishitha Sree

title: Mukundhan's story about the sea
text: In the sea there lived two parrot fish. Their names were Munch and Crunch. They liked to munch on coral to keep the coral reef safe by scraping off the algae. In the coral reef there lived clown fish too. They cleaned their homes. Their homes were Sea Anemones. The Anemones protect the clown fish by stinging predators if they come close. In the coral reef there lived jellyfish too. They sting their predators with their tentacles. Some even sting humans and some do not, like the Moon jellyfish.
author: suji v
illustrator: Deepti Sharma; Prabha  Mallya; Rajiv Eipe

title: Cotton Doctor
text: Margaret Ann Bulkley was born. Margaret lived in the rainy, green kingdom of Great Britain, Great Britain, Great Britain. Margaret was smart, curious, and divine dreams. She also did not lack courage and resistance to all injustice. Margaret's parents paid for her brother's law studies. They spent the last money so that he could marry the daughter of a wealthy man. Margaret was smart and had big dreams. However, there was not enough money to teach her even to be a governess or a nanny. Margaret was brave. - I want to be a doctor! - she said. Unfortunately, two hundred years ago the girl could not become a lawyer, politician, or doctor. Uncle Margaret, James Barry, was a famous painter. He was friends with General Miranda of Venezuela, the owner of a beautiful and large library, which numbered over six thousand books! - I want to read this! And this one! That one too! Margaret shouted. She was smart and curious. She made a great impression on the general. When Margaret's uncle died, he left her a sum of money. Enough for your medical studies, General Miranda said. But I can't be a doctor,said Margaret. The boys can, said the general. - And you can dress up as a boy. Margaret did not lack the courage to fight for her convictions. She really wanted to become a doctor. So she cut her hair, learned to speak in a low voice, and put on boys' clothes. From that moment on, no one noticed Margaret was a girl. She took the name James Barry, after her uncle. When Margaret's uncle died, he left her a sum of money. Enough for your medical studies, General Miranda said. But I can't be a doctor,said Margaret. The boys can, said the general. - And you can dress up as a boy. Margaret did not lack the courage to fight for her convictions. She really wanted to become a doctor. So she cut her hair, learned to speak in a low voice, and put on boys' clothes. From that moment on, no one noticed Margaret was a girl. She took the name James Barry, after her uncle. James Barry studied medicine diligently. He studied 13 subjects and worked hard all summer while others went on vacation. However, he was close to not being able to take the final exam five years later. The lecturers decided that he looked too young! Yet James Barry didn't have a beard for a very different reason. Dr. James Barry was brave, curious and had big dreams, so he joined the army. Thanks to this, he could get to know the world! In 1816, Dr. Barry's army was sent to Cape Town. Cape Town is a mysterious town in South Africa, and South Africa is very far from Ireland. Dr. Barry was really looking forward to it. Dr. James Barry was slim and short. He walked in platform shoes and stuffed his clothes to appear taller and heavier. The people of Cape Town called him the kapok dokter - a cotton doctor. - I'd like to cut your ears off! - dr. Barry shouted at whoever challenged him. He even dueled with pistols once! Fortunately, they both missed. Why did the doctor duel so much? Margaret was brave but terrified. She knew that if someone discovered her identity, they would not let her be a doctor. Everyone had to believe Dr. Barry was a man. Dr. Barry has always fought injustice. The island of Robben was inhabited by lepers who had been banished from Cape Town. They were sent to the island because the townspeople thought they could get infected easily from them. Dirty houses and inadequate food only worsened the condition of the sick. Dr. James Barry asked Cape Town leaders to provide better living conditions and healthier food for the islanders. Years later, Dr. James Barry worked in a military hospital. There he met Florence Nightingale, a nurse. She was called a lady with a lamp because she checked the wounded people at night by lighting her way with a lantern. During the war, she became famous for requests to the command for better conditions and food for soldiers. Dr. Barry had been asking for the same thing over the years. Dr. James Barry has traveled all over the world. He has worked in South Africa, Saint Helena, Barbados, Mauritius, Trinidad and Tobago, Malta, Corfu, Jamaica, Crimea, West Indies, Canada… visited 11 places in total. Oh what of adventures he had! People didn't find out he was a woman until 1865 when Margaret died. The same year, Dr. Elizabeth Garret Andersen became the first doctor in Great Britain. Dr. James Barry proved that girls are smart, brave, dream big and fight for their beliefs. And that they can definitely become doctors!
author: Hanna Chomen

title: Veeru Circus
text: It will be fun to watch the circus," Viru said happily. In the circus, Veeru was happy to see Madari walking on a rope, doing different tricks and a red-nose clown. He repeatedly played applause. That night, Veeru dreams that he has a circus of his own. The next morning, he has invited Mother, Baba, Grandma and Grandpa to see Veeru Circus. Veeru will now go on a high rope to show off the rope feat. "Veeru Sambhal's walk, there is a fear of you falling into it," mother So Veeru Madari laid the rope on the ground and walked on it with great precision. Everyone clapped and Veeru thanked everyone. Veeru now thought of leaping from the middle of a burning circle. "This is very dangerous, there is a fear of burning with fire," Baba warned Veeru. So Veeru Juggler played his big player Now Viru made up his mind to bounce six balls together. "Oh little Viru Veeru, if the balls fell on your head?" Dada said. So Veeru took a big laddu and bounced it up. Laddu fell directly into his mouth. Everyone clapped again. For the next feat, Veeru wants to summon a lion locked in a cage. His book contains many illustrations of the lion of the circus. "Veeru is not a good thing to get wild animals juggled in a cage?" The lion may get angry too, ”the grandmother explained to him. So the Viru ring master of the circus called his beloved dog Bozo and shook hands with him. "Thank you Bozo," Veeru told him. Now Veeru, the red-nosed clown, began to buckle his waist. But in this hanging-jerk, his necker moved down. Everyone started laughing out loud. "You had a lot of fun, Veeru, you showed fun games," Dadi said. "What a fun circus we saw!" Mother, Baba, grandfather and grandmother said together.
author: Vandita Sharma

title: The ugly toad and a unfriendly bear
text: Once upon a time, two friends lived near a lake. One was an ugly toad and the other was an unfriendly bear. Both of them loved to play with each other. One day, they were playing so, the bear noticed that the toad was ugly. Then he said to the toad “ I don’t want to be your friend anymore because of your ugliness ”. Then he went far away and reached a rain forest. There were many wild animals. So, the bear got frightened. The toad was very disappointed. He thought “What should I do now as my friend has lost me ’’. He thought and thought. Finally, he got an idea. He could follow the footprints of the bear. And he found the bear but the bear could not spot out where was the toad. Meanwhile, a lion came and wanted to eat the bear. He ate the bear but could not spot the toad because of his ugliness. This saved the toad but not the bear.
author: Anaisha Jain
illustrator: Amar Soni; Anjora Noronha; Chhoun Sambath; Eshita Munshi; Rob Owen

title: The little naughty Sam
text: Me and my family just celebrated my birthday, I was born at night at exactly 8:34 pm. My mom said I could only open my gifts at that time. She hid them somewhere, I was bored, so I thought to brake the rules and find them! I found one present, that is good, I am so excited to see what’s inside but first let’s keep looking! Wait, this is not for me this is for Dad. He goes in anger and starts looking again. This is not mine this is my sisters present. Grghhhhhhhh. He looks again hoping for his gift Nope, not mine, this is moms gift. A ha, this better be mine! Let’s see Yes!!! It’s mine it’s mine! Yayyy His mom finds out that Sam is looking for his gift, but bye that time it was 8:34 so he was not in trouble! He was allowed to open his gift But Sam, never try to find your present like this again, ok mom! Wowwwwwwww Thank you mom! For these! He learned his lesson and Finally got his gift!
author: Mia Singh

title: A Very Busy Year
text: I don’t like my birthday. I don’t like the day. I don’t like the month. ​All months are special. Except my month. ​January is as exciting as a new notebook. It feels crisp and clean. It is the first month of the year. ​February. Later. Later. Later. ​March is as cheerful as a box of crayons. Spring brings pink leaves on the peepal tree, orange flowers on the gulmohar tree, red pompoms on the ixora plants. ​​​April is as confused as a seesaw. There are school exams and sweaty days. But also juicy, golden Alphonso mangoes. ​May is as happy as a yellow butterfly. The summer holidays are lazy and long. There are cousins and cricket matches. Train journeys and prickly heat. ​June is as suspenseful as a mystery book. What will happen when school starts? Will my best friend Renu be in my class? Will mean Miss Menon be my class teacher? ​ July is like the dhishoom-crash-bang in a film. The monsoons take over. Winds howl. Clouds thunder and grumble. My umbrella flies away. Then mummy scolds and I sulk. ​August is as inspiring as Jana Gana Mana. For Independence Day we march. We paint flags green, orange and white. ​September is as busy as a concert. Teachers’ Day is our favourite day. Renu and I sing songs. We make cards. We make gulab jamuns. All for Miss Menon. We love her now. ​October is as bright as a queen’s crown. Diwali brings diyas, sparkly, shiny earrings and jootis and rangoli. I eat too many laddoos. ​November is as cosy as my pink sweater. Winter is slowly creeping in. The days are short. The nights are cold. ​December is as chilly as a refrigerator. I shiver for fun. Even school days feel like holidays. It is the last month of the year. A new year is waiting. ​See. All the months are special. Except February. February is boring and muddled. ​​​Other months have 30 or 31 days. February has 28 days. Then every four years it has an extra day. 29 February. I was born on 29 February. My birthday comes once every four years. ​I am upset. Wouldn’t you be, too? I would like to celebrate every year, just like you do.
author: Shabnam  Minwalla

title: The Bird and The Snake
text: There was a bird called Peggy. She had three eggs. She was a happy little bird, until one day, when a snake appeared in the area! She was scared. She got to know the snake's name. It was Lemmy. The day had passed and Peggy went to bed. The next morning, she had an idea but she was also worried the Lemmy might take the eggs. "I'm going to replace the eggs with stones!" She said. She replaced the eggs, and hid the real nest behind a bush. "I think this is a great idea!" said Peggy. Lemmy liked the eggs of Peggy's kind but Peggy is a smart bird. The day was over. Peggy went to bed. The next day she went out to find food but she really just hid behind the bush that the real nest was behind. Lemmy had spotted the fake nest while he was slithering in the area. Lemmy was very excited. He slithered up the tree and stole the eggs which were really stones. He went to his area and swallowed the stones! Lemmy was slithering by a pond and fell fell in it and drowned. Peggy was delighted to hear this! Hearing this not even one single snake ever came to the area! Peggy and her chicks lived happily ever after! THE END
author: Deeksha Santhakumar

title: Around You: States of Matter
text: ​In the market you can spot fresh orange carrots, shiny purple brinjals, glasses of delicious watermelon juice. ​You can also see steam rising from cups of hot chai at the tea stall. ​So many delicious things, and all of them so different. Some things look small, some look big, some are heavy and some light. Some feel too ripe and some unripe. ​Do they have anything in common? Yes, they all take up space and have weight. Even the air we breathe. Anything that occupies space and has weight is called matter. Almost everything around us is matter. ​Matter can be found in three states — solid, liquid and gas. Carrots, brinjals, the glass and the cup are solids. They have a definite shape and take up a fixed amount of space. ​The watermelon juice in the glass and the chai in the cup are both liquids. They do not have a definite shape. They take the shape of the glass and the cup. They can be poured. They flow. But they also take up a fixed amount of space. ​The air we breathe is a gas. Gases have no definite shape and do not take up a fixed amount of space. Unlike a liquid, air can be squeezed into a tiny space or expand to fill a large space. All matter is made up of tiny particles. In a solid, these particles are packed very tightly together, which gives a carrot or a cup its fixed shape and size. In a liquid, the particles are packed loosely and can move about easily. That is what allows water, oil, juice and chai to flow smoothly and not have a definite shape. ​In a gas, the particles move about even more freely. They can be squeezed into a small space or spread out in a large space. This is why gases do not have a fixed shape or size. STATES OF MATTER Most objects are solids, liquids or gases. However, they can change their state from one to the other when there is a change in the surroundings. Water, which is usually a liquid, behaves like a solid when it is put inside a freezer. There are also objects which cannot be strictly called either a solid, liquid or gas. Solids usually have fixed shape and liquids do not. However, a piece of sponge seems to have a fixed shape like most solids do but it can change shape very easily.
author: Sukanya  Sinha

title: Football Trouble
text: Here are Kanu and Timo. They are brothers. They play football every evening. They like playing football. Today, Mama asked them to buy some food before playing football. Here they are in front of a row of shops. Kanu and Timo watch some of their friends playing football on the field in front of the shops. "Let's play football, only for a short while, and then go to the shop," said Kanu to Timo. Kanu kicked the ball to Timo and Timo kicked the ball to Kanu. Football is so much fun. "Football is even more fun if more of us play together," said Kanu to Timo. "Hi friends, can we play with you?" Kanu asks the boys. "Sure, come. The more the merrier," says one of the boys. The boys have so much fun. Kanu is the goal keeper. Can he save the goal? Timo tries to kick the ball over Kanu's head. Kanu jumps high and catches the ball. Good job Kanu! They play till they are tired and dirty. Suddenly Kanu remembers that Mama wanted them to buy some food. Here they are at the shop. "It's your fault, Kanu. You wanted to play football. You lost the money." Timo yells at Kanu. Kanu cries. Kanu and Timo walk home. They are scared and upset. Mama will be angry. "Mama, we are sorry." say Kanu and Timo. "Kanu, you forgot to take the money and you forgot to buy food." says Mama "I went to the shop myself, so you two have to help me feed the chicken." says Mama. Kanu and Timo are happy. "We must complete all important tasks before we play football." says Kanu to Timo as they feed the chickens and ducks.

title: Nest Interiors
text: What!!! Messed up your room again??? Parrot Mom was upset as her two daughters " kili " and "Gili "messed up the room several times. Parrot Mom said," Go and look at other birds and use their ideas to organize and keep your stuff in place". So, kili and Gili set off on their mission to look for ideas.... On their way,Gili said " Hey I see something hanging down from the tree like a pot,lets quickly go there and take a look at that ". As they arrived,they found a small bird popping out its head from the nest. "Hey "!!!! its a weaver bird!!!!!exclaimed Gili. HELLO kids,said the weaver bird. We are here to take ideas to make our nest more beautiful and organized said Gili. "Yes, I can make waterproof pots hanging from the tree", added the weaver bird. slowly,Kili and Gili stopped by the community weaver birds's nest,and admired the way they were living together in large groups or pots hanging down from the trees. Just after a short break at the community weaver spot, Kili and Gili found a huge bird on the edge of the cliff,with tiny heads popping out of the nest. They stopped by to understand that it was the Bald eagle with its tiny babies,in the nest made out of twigs and sticks. Bald eagle then said " I like to build my nests on tall trees and cliffs " and my nests are quite spacious for us to snuggle with. After having visited the Bald eagle,kili and Gili then continued on their epic journey. Next, during their flight,Kili shouted,"Hey look down Gili there s a beautifully decorated nest,with flowers and fruits and twigs and sticks,"Wow",it also smells so good Kili!!!! saying so,kili and Gili swooped down to the sweet smelling nest. " Hello "Said a bird in blue as though he had just jumped out of an ink pot. My name is Bower bird,I love doing a lot of interior decorations with flowers and seeds available around me, I love to keep my house clean. Just next to the Bower bird, was a bird with a long beak, and a beautiful body. "I am a wood pecker I love to peck inside the trees to make a hole,I love making holes too." said the woodpecker. Kili and Gili were pleased to see so many different types of birds and the variety of nests and the materials around them with which the birds have decorated and organised. After having gone out for a day Kili and Gili had a ton of ideas and worked hard to clean up their nests and got the best materials to add colour and decoratives to their nest. Kili and Gili having learnt about nests,built some of their own and spent happy hours playing on the tree... Parrot Mom was happy,,so was Kili and Gili!!!!!!!!! DID YOU KNOW Bower Bird: As the name suggests bower bird species are remarkable for their bower building habits.They not only construct architecturally elaborate structures of sticks and other vegetable matter but also decorate them with numerous and various often colourful, natural and where ever available human made objects.Bower birds have been associated with high intelligence and artistic or aesthetic senses beyond those of other birds. Weaver Birds weaver birds use a variety of plant materials to build their nests,including strips of grass, leaves,twigs and roots. A weaver bird has a strong,conical beak which it uses to cut blades of grass that it will use in nest building.The weaver bird can tie real knots in nest material with its beak and feet.By tying knots,the bird makes the nest more secure. Community weaver I nstead of building individual nests,all the male communal weaver birds work together to build large nests which houses as many as 400 birds.A communal nest can fill up an entire tree canopy and may last for 100 years. Bald eagle: Bald eagle typically builds its nests high up on the tree tops or cliffs using sticks or may be lined with moss,grass,plant stalks,lichens,seaweed or sod. ﻿ ﻿
