title: Diego and Mariana's Books
text: They were Diego's books and he didn't want Mariana to play with them. Mariana held on tightly to one end of the book, Diego held on to the other end, and they started to fight over it. At the end of the fight, Diego was left with his books. Mariana went away. She was upset. Diego didn't like seeing his happy sister being sad. He knew that the right thing to do was to share. The next day when Mariana came screaming to ask Diego for a book, he decided to do something different. He asked her to wait. He could not give her the green book, as he was reading it. But he would lend her the red one. Mariana took the red book, but she wanted the green one as well. She started to scream angrily. Diego didn't want to fight again, so he gave her the other book as well. He gave her ALL his books. At the end of the day, Mariana was very happy with all the books. But Diego was left with nothing to read. Diego was sad. What could he do so that both he and Mariana were happy with the books? The next day, Diego had a great idea. He would make new books, so that Mariana could have her own books to have fun with. He showed everything to Mariana and together they started to make new books. Mariana was so happy to be able to make her own stories. Diego was happy to hear all the great stories that Mariana told him. Some days Mariana told Diego her stories, and on other days, Diego read his books to Mariana. They were both happy. Reading and writing books together was so much more fun than fighting!
author: Catherine Davis

title: I don't want to talk!
text: I like school, but I don't like talking in front of the class. When the teachers speak to me, I feel like I am in a spotlight. I get scared! I don't like talking in public. I feel like there are thousands of butterflies in my tummy... The butterflies move around, I don't know what to do! I am scared! Oooooh noooooo.... When I am scared, I think of my friend Deborah. She always gets worried too. She taught me her special technique to control fear. Deborah said that I can hold an imaginary umbrella. It is just like Mary Poppins' umbrella! Deborah says that I can imagine going to a happy place, like a garden. In the garden there is a farm. There are animals. Deborah says that I can speak to them. The butterflies become words and they fly far away! Deborah says that I can also imagine a very simple garden. An empty garden. I can imagine that I am in that garden, sat on a bench. I can breathe in...s l o w l y...... one...two... three... And I can breathe out...s l o w l y...... one...two... three... When I am ready, I open my eyes. The butterflies have disappeared! Be brave! That's it! Well done! You can also imagine your garden, just like Viola. You can have a happy place to go to when you are scared, as well.
author: Catherine Davis

title: Nimmi's Online Friend
text: Nimmi sat in front of her computer. She just fought with her school friend and was mood off. She entered the Friendchat website. She logged in and was browsing. Nimmi got a friend request from someone named Preethi. Wow. What a beautiful girl she is thought Nimmi. Nimmi accepted the friend request. You have a friend request from Preethi. Nimmi typed, “Hi. Where do you live?” Preethi typed, “I live in a place called Koozhangal in Chennai.” Nimmi typed, “How old are you?” Preethi typed, “I am 15 years old.” Nimmi and Preethi exchanged a lot of details like this. After a few days, Nimmi again logged into the Friendchat website. Preethi was also logged in. Preethi typed, ”I like your profile photo. Can we meet soon? How about meeting this Friday at the Central Railway Station.” Nimmi typed, “Ok. Sure. At 5 pm.” Just as Nimmi was typing, her aunt Manju entered the room. “Who are you chatting with Nimmi, “ asked her aunt. Nimmi told everything about Preethi to her aunt. “Koozhangal. There is no place in Chennai known as Koozhangal. And she looks very old in the picture. Does not look like a 15-year-old. She also resembles a famous model I know, “said Nimmi’s aunt Manju. Nimmi thought about what all her aunt said. “Could this Preethi be a fake person,” she thought. On Wednesday, Preethi chatted with Nimmi and reminded her to come alone to the railway station. Nimmi told her aunt about the meeting at the railway station. Her aunt said, “I will come along with you and hide behind you. You go alone near the railway coach and wait on the platform. I will watch you from a distance.” Nimmi and her aunt Manju went to the railway station on Friday at 5 pm. As Nimmi was waiting alone on the platform, a hand touched her shoulder. She startled and turned back. It was not Preethi. It was a middle-aged man who was smiling at her. Nimmi said, “I don’t know you. Who are you?” The man said, “I’m Prakash. I like to make friends with all age groups. You look more beautiful in person than the online photo.” Just then, her aunt who was hiding and watching came and hit the man. She had also alerted the railway police. In the police station, the woman police said, “There are a lot of men online hiding behind photos of women in their profile. They try to make friends with young girls and may later engage in mischievous acts. It is good you told your aunt about your online friend. Never go out to meet a stranger without informing elders or guardians.” Nimmi and her aunt Manju thanked the police and left.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Fossils: Tales of Long Ago
text: Fossils can answer many questions about our past. About beasts that are extinct. Early humans. Places that were once cold but are now warm. Forests that have become deserts. Fossils are remains of plants and animals. Some may have turned to stone with time, while others have remained preserved — with flesh and bone — under ice or in tree sap. Fossils are rare because they have to survive climatic changes over thousands of years. In 1828, British explorer William Sleeman discovered the first dinosaur fossil in our country, in the Narmada valley. The fossil was named Titanosaurus in 1877 by Richard Lydekker, a British naturalist and geologist. Fossils can be of many kinds. The most common fossils are replicas of animals or plant remains. They are created when dead plants or animals are thrust under water. When this happens, the soft parts rot. But the hard parts, like bones, teeth and shells are remain. Soil, mud and pebbles pile on it and form a cocoon. Over time, even the bones, shells, and teeth dissolve leaving gaps. But minerals in the water fill these gaps and create replicas. These are body fossils. Body fossils have been found across the country. In eastern Gujarat, scientist Dhananjay Mohabey dug out a body fossil of a snake devouring a dinosaur hatchling. In Madhya Pradesh, Vishal Verma, a school teacher discovered hundreds of dinosaur-egg fossils along the Narmada river. In Tamil Nadu, ‘Fossil’ Subramanian collected fossils of ammonites. Ammonites are ancient soft-bodied molluscs that are survived by their spiral shells, some of which are the size of truck wheels. Sometimes, fossils can also be an entire animal or plant, or part of an organism, trapped in their natural form and preserved for millions of years. These are called true form fossils. Palaeontologist Ashok Sahni and his team discovered spiders and insects in the sticky amber sap in the coal mines of Vastan in Gujarat. Trace fossils are insect burrows, footprints or even poop. Scientist Vandana Prasad found traces of rice pollen in fossilised dinosaur dung from Maharashtra. That’s how they discovered that some dinosaurs had chewed on rice grains. Tiny fossils are called microfossils, like the remains of the 1-mm thick prokaryotes—single-celled primitive organisms—unearthed in Madhya Pradesh. When the bones and teeth of fossils are visible to the naked eye, they are called macrofossils. Some macrofossils can be gigantic, like the 18-foot Ichthyosaur, an aquatic reptile whose skeleton was found by palaeontologist Guntupalli V R Prasad and his team in Gujarat. Then there are living fossils. These are species that lived millions or even hundreds of millions of years ago and exist even today. ​The ten-legged, blue-blooded horseshoe crabs found in the mangroves of the Sunderbans in West Bengal are living fossils. They are early relatives of spiders, and in danger of extinction. They predate dinosaurs by about 200 million years. FOSSIL MAP Fossil of snake devouring dinosaur hatchling Gujarat Ichthyosaur fossil Gujarat Spider and insects in amber sap Gujarat Dinosaur-egg fossils Madhya Pradesh Titanosaurus Madhya Pradesh Horseshoe crabs West Bengal Fossils of prokaryotes Madhya Pradesh Dinosaur-dung fossil Maharashtra Ammonite fossils Tamil Nadu
author: Anupama Chandrasekaran

title: Roy's Noisy Secret
text: It was on a windy afternoon that Roy tried on his Achamma’s anklets. No one else was at home, except Vasco the dog. The anklets had been tucked away in an old wooden box, deep inside Amma’s rattling cupboard. It smelled like a garden in there. It made Roy want to sneeze. Roy knew that he should not have been in his parents’ room. And certainly not twirling in Achamma’s precious anklets. But he couldn’t help himself. Achamma never used to take off her anklets, not even when she slept. Ching, ching, ching! Roy ran towards the mirror. Ching-chiiiiing! He leapt into the air. CHING-CHING CHING-CHING-CHING Roy threw a shawl around himself, and paced up and down the corridor. Just like Achamma used to when she had trouble sleeping. The doorbell rang just then. Who could it be? CHING-CHING, A-CHING-CHING-CHING. “Open the door, Roy. I’m soaked!” Roy froze. Amma wasn’t meant to come back this soon! When Roy tried removing the anklets, only one came off. He quickly placed the anklet back in the rattling cupboard. Then he ran to the door with the other anklet still strapped on. AYYO! “I forgot my umbrella,” Amma sighed. Roy walked beside her slowly, careful not to let out a single ching-ching. The last time he had sneaked into his parents’ room, he had accidentally broken a flower vase. “No more going into our room when we’re not around,” they had warned him. His heart beat wildly in his chest. Nobody could find out what he had been up to. Life with a secret anklet wasn’t easy. “Why can’t you wear shorts at home, Roy?” Achan said. “Pants don’t dry easily in this weather.” “The mosquitoes, Acha!” At school, his friends looked at him curiously. “Ayye! Who wears socks in pouring rain?” Reshma laughed, jumping into a puddle. “These socks are from Russia,” Roy lied. “Did you hear that noise?” Achachan asked, springing from his chair one evening. “What noise? I hear nothing!” Roy yelled. “A ching-ching,” Achachan whispered. “I hear frogs. But they don’t ching-ching.” Roy felt a tiny lump of sadness in his throat. He didn’t like lying to his grandfather. After a whole week, Roy was tired of his noisy secret.The lies made him feel queasy. But if he told his parents the truth now, would he be in trouble? Amma’s temper was no joke. Achan didn’t like rules being broken. Roy used every imaginable trick to remove the anklet. But the annoying thing refused to leave his ankle! That week, Roy overheard Amma tell Achan, “I can’t find your mother’s anklets. Well, one anklet actually. I’ve looked everywhere!” “Is only one missing?” asked Achan. “That’s strange!” “Where, where, where could it have gone?” she cried. “I should’ve been more careful.” Amma sounded crushed. Roy had a sinking feeling in his stomach. He took a deep breath and marched into their room. Vasco followed. “I’m sorry, Amma,” Roy muttered, lifting up his pants. “Roy! What are you even doing with this?” Achan asked in an unsteady voice. When Achan was angry, his ears turned red and his moustache quivered. Roy wished he could turn invisible just then. “I didn’t mean to… I know I shouldn’t have… I…” “It...it’s all right, Roy,” said Amma. “But you should have asked one of us.” And then Amma twisted something — kudup, kudup — and the anklet just slipped off his leg. Just like that! “The next time, just ask, okay?” Amma said softly, taking Roy’s hands in hers. That night, Roy thought of his Achamma. Her thunderous laughter, her soft hands with a million criss-crossing lines, the way she sat by the window — always gazing out. Would he ever stop missing her? The next morning, Achan’s ears were no longer red. His moustache swayed, but only because he was humming as he trimmed Achachan’s nails. Roy pretended to be busy with homework. He hoped no one would talk about yesterday. And they didn’t. Haavoo! But it wasn’t easy to hide his grin as he listened to the ching-ching around the house. CHING CHING
author: Yamini Vijayan

title: Where is my Bat?
text: I lost my bat. I cant find it anywhere. I searched behind the door. It's not there. I checked on the shelf. couldn't find it there. ﻿Searched under the cot. It's not there either. ﻿checked in the box. There is no trace of it. Searched the whole loft. couldn't find it there too. ﻿I searched for it everywhere. couldn't find it anywhere. author: Raghavi Sarada

title: Jayanth Bookstore
text: It was a lazy Sunday, and Shreya and her brother Manoj were getting bored. “Shall we go to the Jayanth bookstore?” asked Shreya. Manoj nodded and they both walked to the Jayanth Bookstore in the main city. On the way, Shreya asked, “What books do you want to buy?” Manoj said, “I want to buy books by the famous children’s author Ruskin Bond.” Shreya said, “Yes. I heard The Blue Umbrella is one of his popular books.” Then, they reached the Jayanth Bookstore and walked into it. The owner Jayanth invited them inside the bookstore. “Only you two have come. Your father did not come along?” Shreya said, “He has to attend online training and so did not come with us.” Shreya and Manoj started to search the racks for the books they wanted. “Here is a book about Salim Ali, India’s Birdman,” said Manoj. Just then, Jayanth uncle sat near them and helped them find more interesting children’s books. “Here is The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes. Here are Tintin comics. These are books by Enid Blyton.“ Shreya and Manoj picked some books and sat in the bookstore. They read a few pages to see if the books were good. Finally, Shreya and Manoj selected the books they wanted and paid the bill at the counter. Shreya and Manoj walked out of the bookshop with their favourite books.

title: Copy shadow
text: Today there was a meeting in the school. Mother came to school After the meeting, Mam asked me - "Do you want to go home with your mother?" I quickly said yes mam. I was very happy. know why? Because I like to walk. I enjoy seeing different flowers, trees, people, shops on the way. Every day I come by school bus. Just hastens to reach home. I don't get to see anything properly. I was walking slowly. Mother also knows that I am very young. She also used to go slowly with me. I was stopping sometimes while looking here and there. Mother was saying - "Come quickly, the sun is very bright." I tried to walk a little faster. Now we were about to reach home. Then I stopped seeing some black and black shape on the road. Mother was pulling me to walk forward but I did not have to go further. Mother asked me- "Are you tired?" But my focus was on the black-black shape on the road. I was afraid too. Why does it go with me Used to be? Is there any monster in this story? Mother knows everything about me, but today she is in a hurry to go. Didn't see that I wanted to show them something. I pulled the mother's hand out loud and gestured to the mother. Look at this - "A little black-shaped shap (shape) is made on the road." Mother told me- "This is your shadow (shadow)." I started thinking- "Ma'am at school Our circle, oval, Tell the rectangle shape. Never tell this strange shape On the way, I saw - "Sometimes a shadow appears and sometimes disappears." Questions arose in my mind…. Where does this shadow come from? Where does this shadow disappear? Now we have reached home. Mother said- "Look at the front wall." Hey! what is this? Two to two black on the wall Shapes " How did this shadow come from the road to the wall? Is it both shadows? I kept watching them for a while. Mother told- "Big One's Shadow Mother and Little Shadow My" The funny thing was - If mother held my hand, then mother's shadow also took hold of my shadow. Shadow was copying …… copycat shadow.. I started laughing out loud. In the evening, the mother took me to the park behind the house. There Mary, of trees, saw its shadow. I saw where the sunlight is where it is A shadow is formed. So sometimes a shadow appears and Never ever Mother told- "Sunlight comes directly to the earth. When anyone comes in the middle of sunlight, the light does not find a way. If there is no light, it becomes dark. We call it shadow. Mother also said - If the shadow is ours then it takes the same shape as us. It is not a copycat. Sometimes it becomes big and sometimes small. The shade is always black. We get scared by seeing the black shape... Mother promised me - "She plays me a lot of shadows Will teach " Today was a great day. It was more fun than watching cartoons on TV. Now I gave up fearing the shadow and made friendship with him. Science related to shadow- The shadow can be made of any living or non-living object, provided it blocks the path of light or stops it. To become a shadow it is necessary to have light, object and any curtain / wall etc. on which we can see the shadow The shadow of the same object made of different substances is not the same. There are different types of substances like - Transparent material - This substance allows light to pass through it. Eg- glass, water Opaque substances- These substances do not allow light to pass through them, so if you see an object through these substances, it will not be visible. Eg- wood, cardboard Translucent material - must have seen such substances which allow some fraction of the light to pass, so if you see an object across these substances, it will appear blurred. Like thick plastic.... Activity Look at the different substances around you. Find out which object is transparent or opaque? Make a steel glass, glass glass and plastic glass shade. Whose shadow It is formed correctly. Make a note In the same way, there are many more.
author: Vandita Sharma

title: The story of the toothpaste
text: They used tooth sticks to clean their teeth back then. A tooth stick was simply a twig with a frayed end. Sometimes, they tied boar hair to one end for that extra shine. And toothpaste tubes were not invented yet. Instead they had jars filled with toothpaste. So, they dipped the toothstick into the jar and brushed their teeth. Every other member of the family dipped their stick into the same jar! Isn't that disgusting? Yes, it is. One morning, a boy named Lucius refused to use that jar anymore. He declared "I will use tooth powder". But the problem remained in his mind - "There must be a better way to use toothpaste", he thought. A few years later, Lucius went to Paris. He was studying to become a dentist. There, he saw artists squeezing paint from metal tubes on to their paintbrushes. He came up with an idea. "Why couldn't the same type of tube be used to hold toothpaste?! " There was a small problem - How do we get the toothpaste into the tube through that little opening? You might have wondered about this yourself too. When you squeeze too much toothpaste. And you have toothpaste all over the sink. "What can help us get toothpaste into the tube - A ear bud? A really tiny spoon? A toothpick?" There was a much better way. Without opening the cap. They opened up the other end! It was easier to fill the toothpaste from the bottom end because it was larger. They pumped the paste into the tube through something like a syringe. After that, all they had to do was seal the end tight so that the paste would not leak. Today, toothpaste tubes are filled using machines. All the empty tubes are lined up on a conveyor belt with their caps downwards and the unsealed end pointing up. A big container filled with toothpaste is fixed above the conveyor belt. Toothpaste is filled into these tubes as they move along the conveyor belt. But the paste is not filled all the way to the brim. About half an inch is left so that it can be sealed. Now the tube is ready to be squeezed! Ancient Indian wisdom for good teeth Many people in India use 'Datun', the twig of a neem or babool tree, instead of a factory-made brush. Datun keeps teeth and gums healthy. Look at the pack of your tooth paste /powder. You will see a list of herbs and spices that are good for teeth - mint, clove, cinnamon, black pepper and tulsi. Eating fibrous fruits and vegetables, like apples and carrots, is good for cleaning teeth. Fun with toothpaste caps
author: gurpreet kaur

title: The Birthday Cake
text: At the end of a street, there was an old house with yellow walls, a creaky gate and a tiled roof. An old woman lived there, alone. Azad, Haniya, Charulata and Piyush were often found playing on the street, screaming and shouting. “Don’t make so much noise!” their parents told them but the four children never listened. They kept screaming and shouting as they played games. Once, their cricket ball fell inside the old woman’s garden. They waited for her to return it to them. She didn’t. This happened many times. The children never got their ball back. One evening, the four of them jumped over the wall. They wanted to try and get the balls back. Long shadows fell on the garden wall. They looked up and saw the woman at the door. “She looks creepy” Piyush whispered. “Fool!” Haniya whispered back. They all ran away, a little scared. From that day, they stopped playing on her side of the street. One day, the children saw a postman cycle to the old woman’s house. She took the envelope from him and went in, shutting the gate in his face. The postman was back on his cycle and about to leave when Haniya stopped him. “What did you give her?” she asked. The postman smiled. “A birthday card from her insurance company.” “They are her friends?” Charu asked. The postman shook his head. “Old people don’t have friends who can send them cards for their birthdays?” Haniya wondered. “That’s not true. Old people have friends. But who would want to be friends with her?” Piyush asked. He was the youngest and got scared easily. “Imagine no one wishing her for her birthday!” Charu said. “But she must be a hundred years at least. There’s no one her age to wish her” Piyush said. “We can wish her,” Azad said. “Yes, and I’d still like people to wish me for my birthday even if I’m 100,” Charu said. “So? You want to go and wish her? She’ll gobble you up!” Piyush said. “No, but what if we…” Haniya trailed off. “What if we… what?” Azad asked. “What if we bake a cake for her?” Haniya said. Everyone looked at her like she was mad. But then, cake! How could they say no to that? “Can you make it look like a cricket ball?” Piyush asked. “Maybe she’ll get a hint then.” “No,” Charu said, rolling her eyes. Everyone was excited now. They decided to bake the cake at Charu’s house. Her mother never minded if they made a mess in the kitchen. But they all had to pool their money for the ingredients. “Why are we doing this again?” Azad grumbled as he collected everyone’s pocket money. He would be going to the shop to buy what they needed. “Can you imagine not celebrating your birthday?” Haniya replied. When they had bought the ingredients, they chose an easy recipe from a book. The kitchen did become a mess but everyone had fun – there was flour, bits of broken eggshells. “Can we slice the top off to taste it? She won’t know if the cake is short, no?” Piyush asked. Azad shook his head. “No, you won’t stop at just that!” Charu argued. “Can I at least taste the icing?” he asked. “You can lick the bowl when we finish,” Haniya said. The children frosted the cake as best as they could. It was a little wobbly. “Do we have to give it to her?” Azad said, when it was finished. “Come on, we know how to do it now. We can bake one for ourselves later. But it’s her birthday today,” Haniya reminded them. Charu’s mother helped them put the cake on a tray and they walked down the road. Everyone was nervous. What if she threw away the cake? They waited for the old lady to come outside her house. She appeared at the gate, her eyes squinting as she looked at them. “What is it?” she asked them, sharply. “Happy birthday, Aunty!” they all said together. For a long time, the old woman said nothing. At last, she opened the gate and let them in. Piyush entered last, staying close to Charu. They looked around the garden. In one corner, they saw all their cricket balls piled up. No one said anything. “Come,” the old lady said, opening the door of her house. Inside the house, the children sat on the edge of the sofa. They put down the tray with the cake on the centre table. “Sit. I’m getting a knife,” she said and walked away. “Knife? Why?” Piyush asked, looking scared. “To cut the cake, silly,” Charu admonished him. They looked around the house. Almost everything was dusty and neglected. “Look! It’s her,” Haniya said, pointing at some photo frames on a shelf. In the photos, she was young and happy. “See? She was not always a hundred years old!” Charu pointed out to Piyush. The old lady walked back inside and the kids returned to the sofa in a hurry. In her hand, there were plates along with a knife. She cut the cake and served them. “Don’t think this will make me return your cricket balls when you play outside again,” she told them but her tone was not harsh. The children looked at each other as they ate quietly. Then Azad cleared his throat. “You also eat the cake, aunty. It’s good. We made it,” he said. The old lady nodded and ate some of the cake. When the children got up to leave, she said, “Take your balls and go.” Some days later, a ball fell into the old lady’s garden. At first, she seemed annoyed. Then she smiled, picked it up and threw it back to the kids. Look around you and you’ll see how different we all are from each other. Whether it’s the way we talk, the way we think or the way we look, no two people are exactly the same. Fraternity is the idea that while we are different, we are all equally important. It is an idea of kinship, and of mutual support. We all have emotions, dreams and hopes. We all feel pain, happiness, anger and love. Promoting fraternity among the citizens of India is one of the central tenets of our Constitution. We can all come together, to become one, no matter who we are. Fraternity
author: Andaleeb Wajid

title: The Garbage Beach
text: Sonia and her classmates are going to the beach today. They love to play in the water and build sand castles. It is the best. But then Sonia saw lot's of garbage. Plastic bags, candy wrappers and waste! Sonia, while dancing with the crabs, slipped on one of the plastic bags and fell. Sonia knew that anyone can get hurt if the waste will be covered around the beach. Sonia called all of her friends and said: friends, all this garbage is ruining our beach. To prevent that, we should clean up this beach. Everyone agreed and started picking up garbage. But it took forever. So Sonia said: It will take a long time if we continue like this. So we should split up. Pinky, Rahul, Amaya will go and clean near those rocks. Me, Raj and Monu will clear here. Ran, Dhaniya and Sathya will make sure no garbage enters the water. We have to do this before evening. And so they did. The work was done by evening and they enjoyed it a lot. Though they couldn't play in the water or build sand castles, it was fun cleaning up the beach. They called the garbage truck to take away all the garbage which they had put in the garbage bags. You should have wait for me as every day I Come to pick garbage in the beach. Said The garbage man. It's okay. We were glad to help. Said Sonia.
author: Aarushi  konda

title: Im older, Im the ruler
text: Once upon a time there lived a girl. Her name was Tina. She was 9 years old. She had a brother named Sam and a sister named Alice. Sam was 5 and Alice was 7. Tina always wanted to help mother with cooking, and so Alice had to play with Sam. They both liked to play different things and in different places. Alice liked to play on the slide in the adventure playground across the road. But, Sam liked to play in the big cloth tent he had made outside. Alice would always shout I’m older, I’m the ruler! That meant that since Alice was older, Sam had to listen to her. And that’s how she made Sam play in the adventure playground. But on the first night of winter all the three children wanted a drink of water. And so mother went to the well to get some water, but it was snowing and dark, so she said that Tina could not come. While the children were waiting, they played some board games like Ludo and Happy Hippo. Alice said she wanted to play in the adventure playground and Sam wanted to play in the tent. But it was snowing outdoors, and Tina wanted to stay inside the warm house. But they started fighting for the tent and adventure playground. Then Alice said "I'm older, I'm the ruler". Suddenly Tina got up from the couch and said "That's it, I'm older, I'm the ruler!":) And that's how Tina made Sam and Alice, her siblings, stay indoors while it was snowing outdoors.
author: Anushka Nair

title: Wild Cat! Wild Cat!
text: Some wild cats have stripes. Like the Tiger! Some wild cats have manes. Like the Lion! Some wild cats have spots. Like the Leopard and the Leopard cats! Some wild cats are the best climbers. Like the Clouded Leopard and the Marbled cats! Some wild cats live high up in the mountains. Like the Snow Leopard and the Pallas's cats! Some wild cats live in the desert. Like the leopard and the Desert cats! Some wild cats have hairy ears. Like the Caracal and the Lynx! Some wild cats love the fish Like the Fishing cat! Some wild cats are the smallest wild cats in the world. Like the Rusty-spotted cat! Some wild cats look like the house cats. Like the Jungle cat and the Golden cat! But they are all wild cats
author: Anik Reddy

title: The Chatty Turtle
text: A talkative turtle called Ronny lived in a lake deep inside a forest. He would talk all day long with anyone- from tiny ants to giant elephants. But Tom liked to talk most with his best friends-a pair of geese called Bo and Mo. The three friends lived in the same lake. One day, they noticed that the water in the lake was drying up. It hadn’t rained all year. Many animals in the forest were leaving the forest in search of water. Bo and Mo decided to leave too. With a heavy heart, they came to say goodbye to Tom. “But why are you saying goodbye?” asked Tom “Without water, there soon won’t be any fish in the lake. I too want to leave.” “We would love to take you along,” Bo said sadly. “But you cannot fly. How will you come with us?” “Oh, that’s not a problem. We just have to find a sturdy log of wood. You hold the log with your beaks and fly. I will hold on to the wood with my mouth. That way we can all leave together,” Tom said.Mo looked worried, “That’s a nice plan. But Tom you love to talk. When we are up in the air you can’t open your mouth.”Tom laughed, “I can keep quiet when it’s important. Let’s go guys! It’ll be an adventure.” The three friends left the next morning. Tom was excited. He had lived all his life on the ground. Now he could see mountains from a height. Even the tall elephants looked tiny from the sky. He wanted to discuss all this with his friends. But remembering Mo’s words, he kept his mouth shut.The three soon passed over a village. The villagers had seen geese fly before. Tom was confused. “What are these villagers blabbering?” he wanted to ask. But the moment he opened his mouth, he dropped straight to the ground. He hit his head on a rock and died.
author: Pentagon Polygon

title: Karma Has Canines Of A Dog
text: Devyansh was going out so he pulled the main door open and was shocked to see a dog sleeping on his doorsteps. He thought for a while and then kicked the dog aside. The dog wailed loudly. The next day, Devyansh’s son Raj was playing with the same dog. He was pulling the dog’s tail. Raju’s mom saw this and scolded him. “Leave the dog at once, he will get hurt”. Devyansh shushed her and said, “Relax, it’s just a street dog. Why do you even bother?” Later that night, Devyansh and his son were having dinner. Raju left half chapatti on his plate and pushed it towards his mom, “I am full maa”. Devyani, Raju’s mom was about to pick up the plate when Devyansh spoke, “Are you going to feed the dog?” Devyani nodded in reply. Devyansh gave her a frustrated sigh and said, “Just keep it in the fridge, I will eat it tomorrow.” The dog barked the whole night by their window but Devyani couldn’t feed him. She was helpless. The next day, Devyansh went out and checked his doorsteps for the dog. He wasn’t there. Devyansh was disappointed; he wanted to kick the dog again. Suddenly, the sky made a loud thundering noise. Devyansh looked up. The sky was getting dark and from among that darkness, grew a blue cloud. The cloud kept growing in size. From behind that cloud, appeared a big monster. The monster was holding a dog chain, and laughing uncontrollably. Just then Devyansh realized that he had grown a tail and dog ears. He got really scared. The monster above him roared, “You have tortured the dog enough, now it’s my turn to torture you” Out of its own accord, the dog chain in the monster’s hand caught fire and he laughed maniacally. Devyansh woke up with a jolt. He was sweating all over. ‘Just a dream’, he thought but his heart was terrified. It was thundering outside and huge beads of rain were smashing on his window. Devyansh stood up and started searching for a big cardboard box. He found the box and took it outside and along with it carried some biscuits too. The dog was cowering in a corner of his lawn. Devyansh covered him with the thick box and spread a large polythene sheet over it. It was only after feeding the dog and providing him with a home-like arrangement, that Devyansh felt some kind of relief.
author: Chandni Bisht

title: Parade
text: I SKILLS FHS, Harshvardhan Gantha, Ishita Sharma, Jayesh Sivan, Neeta Gangopadhya, Sharanya Singh, Shirish Ghatge Translator: Srishti Sharma Munna and Rukku were playing football with their friends on the street. A parade was going on. A lot of people were a part of it. Slogans of freedom and revolution echoed in the air. All the children came running towards the road to see the parade. The children were of the age 4 to 12. Some children were playful. They started moving with the crowd repeating their slogans. Munna was the oldest of them all. Someone handed him a flag. The kids now repeated the slogans with even more excitement. They are enjoying it as a game. They looked like a part of that parade. There were policemen standing ahead. Munna was slightly scared of them. Rakku, who was walking with munna, said, "we have come a long way, now we should go back" Munna said, "you guys should go back, I will return this flag and join you". Rakku and other friends went back. Munna started looking for the man who gave him that flag. He wanted to return the flag and go back home now. The man was nowhere to be found. The parade came closer to the police. Behind the parade someone burned down a motorcycle standing at the corner of the road. An explosive sound came and it started burning. Seeing at the parade turning fiery, Police started lathi charge on them. The parade turned into a stampede. People started running back and police men followed them. Munna also turned and started running. He was suddenly pushed by someone and fell on the ground. A lot of people ran over him and he fell unconscious. Munna woke up in a government hospital. He was surrounded by Amma, Bapu, Rakku and other children from his neighbourhood. Seeing him conscious made Amma and Bapu's eyes wet with happy tears. Amma held her hand on his head. Bapu asked angrily, "do you even know what was the Parade about?" Munna answered with a low voice, "no." Bapu asked him again, "then why did you go to the parade?" Suddenly all the children said, "Bapu please forgive him, none of us will ever go to a parade again" Munna also said, "yes, we would not" Bapu said, "It's okay, I forgive you". He believed that the children have learnt their lesson.
author: Srishti Sharma

title: The Monkeys In The House
text: On a delightful summer evening, when I was 10, my family went out on some work. I stayed back at home since my leg was injured. While watching my favourite cartoon on TV, I was startled by a strange noise of clattering dishes from the kitchen. At first, I ignored it, but the sound continued and grew louder. As I entered the kitchen, a strange noise caught my attention. To my surprise, three monkeys were sitting on the counter, staring at me with big eyes. I felt a sudden jolt of fear and immediately ran to grab my phone from the sofa. Rushing towards the balcony, I shut the door behind me and shouted for help. Fortunately, one of my neighbours heard me and rushed to call the security guard. I was also trying to reach my parents on my phone, but they were not answering. There was no response despite raising an alert on the apartment's security app. It was a terrifying experience that left me feeling really frightened. I had been trying to reach my dad on the phone for a while and finally, he answered. I explained the situation to him and he rushed back home. However, he forgot to take the house keys with him while going out. This left me in a difficult position as I couldn't go outside to open the door for my dad since there were monkeys who might attack me. I decided to stay in the balcony as my dad tried to scare the monkeys away by continuously ringing the doorbell. His plan worked, and the monkeys went away because of the loud sound. I went to the door to let my dad in. When he entered the house, it was in a really bad and smelly condition. The monkeys caused a lot of chaos, destroyed fruits and veggies, broke eggs, and almost ruined my science experiment. My main concern was their safety since there were many sharp objects like knives in the kitchen. But my parents arrived to help clean up the mess. It was a very scary moment for me. But even though this was such a scary and potentially dangerous situation, it reminded us always to keep our kitchen windows closed and have a spare set of keys. It's amazing to think that even in moments of adversity, problem and danger, there may be a hidden blessing waiting to be discovered.
author: Shanmukh Teja Kota
illustrator: Aayushi Sanghrajka; Aparna  Nath; Lindy  Pelzl; Ruchi Shah; Salim  Kasamba; Sankar Kalita; Srikrishna Kedilaya

title: Look Into My Home
text: This is my house. It is called Gulmohar Villa. This is the hall or living room. This is the first room in my house as soon as you step in. Here we have sofas, a large LCD TV, and chairs to sit on. This is the bedroom. Here we have a large double cot with a soft mattress on it. Pillows and blankets are on the bed. We have AC for our bedroom. An almirah with clothes stands inside the bedroom. This is the kitchen. The gas stove, vessels, pulses, spices, and garnishing powders are here. The fridge also stands in the kitchen. This is not a separate dining hall, but an extension of the main hall. The dining table is here and all of us have our breakfast, lunch, and dinner on the table. This is the bathroom. Buckets and large tubs full of water are inside the bathroom. A geyser for hot water is fixed on a wall in this room. A western toilet is a part of our bathroom. It is also a place for lizards. This is the entrance of the hall where we keep our footwear. Everyone is happy when visitors come home.

title: Barefoot Kanu Dadu
text: I am Chinar and I am eight years old. I hate addition and subtraction. I love dogs and comic books. Most of all, I love to play football. “I am going to be like the great Megan Rapinoe. I am going to win the World Cup,” I tell Ma and my brother Spandan. “My favourite is Bembem Devi,” Ma says. “Huh! No one is better than Sunil Chhetri,” my brother Spandan says. But what does he know about football? He plays only cricket. Ma takes me to Cross Maidan every Saturday evening. My four best friends, Insiya, Kandy, Ramanpreet and Seema, also come. We play football for two hours. Today, Insiya is wearing sparkling new football shoes. They are light green with orange laces. “I want new shoes like that,” I tell Ma at night. “You already have good shoes,” Ma replies. “Have I ever told you about my grand-uncle, Kanu dadu?” “No. Who is he?” I ask. Kanu dadu had five brothers and two sisters. All six brothers, Shuren, Manu, Kanu, Khoka, Shailen and Moni, loved playing football. The sisters, Soudamini and Suhashini, loved music. Kanu dadu was good at his studies but all he wanted to do was play football. His parents didn’t have much money and were always worried about him. Kanu dadu and his friends began the Wari Football Club at his house—5, Ware Street, Wari Para, in Dhaka. It became one of Dhaka’s first football clubs. None of Kanu dadu’s friends had proper shoes. They all played barefoot. “Didn’t they hurt their feet kicking that hard football?” I ask. “Yes, they often broke their toes. Kanu dadu’s mother kept a bowl of turmeric and lime paste in the corner of her kitchen. They put that on their toes for relief from the pain,” Ma tells me. One day the Maharaja of Cooch Behar saw Kanu dadu play a match. He promised to give him Rs 25 every month for his studies. In those days, Rs 25 was a lot of money. So Kanu dadu went to Calcutta in 1909 to study at Presidency College. It was there that he joined the great football club of Calcutta—Mohun Bagan. “I know Mohun Bagan! They wear maroon-and-green jerseys,” I say. Kanu dadu played for Mohun Bagan for many years. He continued to play barefoot. It was 1911. The British ruled India. Till then the Indian Football Association Shield was a tournament only for British regimental teams. Kanu dadu and his Mohun Bagan teammates were going to change that. They played in the famous IFA Shield final against the East Yorkshire Regiment team. The British were beaten 2–1. By eleven Indian men, ten of them barefoot. The Reverend Sudhir Chatterjee was the only Mohun Bagan player who wore football boots. Kanu dadu was just 21 years old. “They must have been so happy,” I say. The whole stadium erupted with joy. There must have been 80,000 people cheering wildly. They threw umbrellas, pens, sticks, hats and mats into the air. After the famous victory, Kanu dadu got a lot of love from everyone. The bus conductors did not charge him a fare, a sweet shop gave him free sweets. The big bicycle factory, Sen-Raleigh, gifted him a cycle. “I would have given him a pair of good shoes,” I tell Ma. “He did get good shoes then. But Kanu dadu still preferred to play barefoot,” Ma smiles. “Should I play barefoot, too?” I wonder, sleepily. But before Ma can say anything I fall asleep, and dream about scoring goals. ​​Author’s Note Jitendranath (Kanu) Roy was my grandfather’s older brother. He played for Mohun Bagan football club from 1911-1917. The IFA Shield is one of the oldest football​ ​competitions, and was dominated by British army teams till Mohun Bagan beat the East Yorkshire Regiment on July 29, 1911. With the Indian freedom struggle gaining​ ​momentum, Mohun Bagan’s victory was a crushing blow to the British. Even today, July​ ​29 is celebrated as Mohun Bagan Day.
author: Ananya Dasgupta

title: Max Turtle's Tale
text: In a big ocean lived a small baby turtle named Max. He lived with his family and he loved his home. One day he was playing away from his home He saw lot of transparent things! He was surprised to see that… He saw an Octopus resting nearby and asked him, what is this? Octopus said, it is Plastic! Human from up dump it here........ Max asked again, can you help me clean this raining Plastic? I do not like this. No, I cannot, It is too much for me, replied octopus sadly. Then He saw a Dolphin swimming Max asked, can you help me clean this raining Plastic? I do not like this. No, we cannot clean this, said Dolphin sadly. Max was sad, he wanted to clean but he could not...... He decided to swim up, he saw a boy playing near the shore. ﻿ ﻿ Boy! He said, is your home also dirty like ours? No no.. We clean it every day! Replied the boy But my home is very dirty, said Max sadly. Can you help me clean it up?? Hummmm … Boy started thinking and said I will ask my friends to help. Boy called all his friends and told them about poor baby turtle’s story. His friends smiled and they started picking up plastic to put in the bin. Then they promised that they will not allow others to litter. Max was very happy!!! Friends Not only Max but all the sea creatures need our help. So please avoid using plastics. This way we can help all little “max” around the world.

title: Sharing is Fun
text: I have a best friend named Anita. She is kind and considerate, also beautiful and responsible. He likes to help his mother. Every time I go back to the village, we always play together. We used to play hide-and-seek in my house. One time, after getting tired of playing, we watched television, and saw there was a McDonalds ad. Anita asked if I'd ever tried it, and I said it's been. Without a second thought, I told him that he wouldn't be able to enjoy it because we live in the city and he's in the village. he's sad. We used to eat together at my house, but that day he said that he wanted to eat at his house only. I asked him to come back after lunch. That night I had to go back to town. We said goodbye and then I left. Then I realized that I'd been rude to him. A year later, I went home. On the way, I stopped by at McDonalds and bought a burger. After arriving in the village, I met Anita and hugged her. He said his vacation had already begun that day. I told you that I had a gift for him. However, he had trouble guessing the prize. Then he opens up and sees that it's a burger. He exclaimed with excitement. He shared the burger with his mother and brother. He's very happy. Me too.

illustrator: Madhuvanti Anantharajan; Rijuta Ghate; Suvidha Mistry

title: Poorani Cuts Her Lovely Locks
text: Poorani has very long hair that extends to her waist. Poorani loved to try different hairstyles on different days. One day, she wore her hair in double plaits. Another day, she put on a ponytail. Sometimes, she preferred a single plait. Sometimes, she let her hair loose. She loved to decorate her long hair with flowers. One day, Poorani was reading a magazine. One article in the magazine spoke about how people can donate their hair to make wigs for bald cancer patients. Immediately, Poorani wanted to do the same. She showed her mom the magazine article. She told her mom, “Mummy, can you cut my hair in a close crop and give the remaining long hair to me?” Her mom agreed and used a comb and scissors to cut Poorani's long hair. Snip, Snip! Poorani was happy when her mom gave her long locks in hand. She measured the cut hair and it was more than 12 inches long. Poorani said, “I will now send this to the NGO that makes wigs for cancer patients.” The NGO sent an appreciation certificate to Poorani for donating her hair. Poorani was very happy. Did You Know? When Cancer patients undergo chemotherapy, they lose their hair. To make them feel confident again when they go out, some NGOs make wigs for cancer patients. Anyone with long hair can donate hair to make a wig. But before cutting the hair, you should wash your hair with shampoo. You should not apply any oil or hair spray. The minimum length of the cut and donated hair must be usually 12 inches. If someone at your home is good at cutting hair, you can cut the hair at home itself. Otherwise, you can get it cut at a salon of your choice. Some NGOs suggest names of salons. After cutting the hair, place it in a zip-lock bag. Then place the bag inside a padded envelope. And then you can mail or courier the envelope to a physical address. Usually, a single wig is made with the hair of several women. Men can also donate hair. Check the minimum length of hair requirement first, as different NGOs have different minimum length requirements. You can bring a bright smile to the lips of a cancer survivor.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Bedtime Bobble-Wobbles
text: Little Maya is fast asleep. What’s that? She hears a squeak. She sees shadows bouncing around. Shhhh, she tries not to make a sound. Three funny monsters are hopping on one foot. Maya isn’t scared; they are rather cute! Green Bobble-Wobble bounces towards the reading nook. He is searching for his favorite book. His friends listen as he reads a magical tale, “Once upon a time, there was a flying whale…” Pink Bobble-Wobble wants to sing all night. She grabs a spoon and dances under the moonlight. Clang, clang, clang! Bang, bang, bang! Orange Bobble-Wobble jiggles and wiggles. Ha-ha-ha! His friends burst into giggles. They dance and sing and read all night. Maya thinks they’re quite a delight! Yawn! Maya crawls into bed; it’s time to sleep. Out the door, the Bobble-Wobbles silently creep. Keep one eye open; you never know… …when the funny Bobble-Wobbles will want to say hello! Boing! Boing! Boing!

title: Mini's First Vote
text: ​Mini is a student in Standard 6. She has one dimple, two bouncy ponytails and a busy, buzzing mind that runs in three directions at once. Sometimes, a busy, buzzing mind is useful. Sometimes it isn’t. ​It is useful when Mini is doing homework, cuddling the cat and dreaming of the summer holidays. All at the same time. ​It is inconvenient when Mini goes to her favourite sweet shop. One part of her mind wants laddoo. Another wants gulab jamun. A third wants barfi. “I will choose tomorrow,” Mini tells her mother. Mini can never, ever decide. ​​ ​This week, though, Mini has to make a big decision. Bigger than picking sweets. Bigger than choosing a book from the school library. This week, Mini has to vote to elect the next school captain. ​Arun is in Standard 8. He has already voted twice—last year, and the year before. “Whom should I vote for?” Mini asks, when they are on the way to school on Monday morning. “It’s your vote,” Arun says. “You must decide.” “But how?” Mini asks, looking confused. “Read the posters,” Arun tells her. “Listen to the speeches. See if the promises make sense. Then you decide whom to vote for.” ​Mini has never voted before. Students can only vote after they reach Standard 6. “You have to choose the best person for the job,” Arun says. Four students are running for the position of school captain. The walls of the school are bright with their posters and promises. At break, Mini and Mohsin read all the posters. ​​​​​​​​Diya’s posters are rainbow-coloured and sparkly. After all, she wins every art competition. ​Pratik’s posters promise more sports—cricket, football and chess. He is the captain of the cricket team. ​Rubina’s posters are plain and a little untidy. They talk about making the school a more fun place. VOTE FOR DIYA VOTE FOR PRATIK VOTE FOR RUBINA For better school experience ​Akshay’s posters are full of pictures of Akshay. He is the most fashionable, confident boy in the school. His posters are bigger than the blackboard. “Such big posters are against the rules,” Mohsin whispers to Mini. “But Akshay will win. He gets whatever he wants.” ​​ VOTE FOR AKSHAY ​All day, Mini’s mind runs in three directions. “Should I vote for Diya?” she asks her mother in the evening. “Her posters are pretty.” “Or for Akshay?” she asks her father at dinner. “His posters cover the entire wall.” ​“Or for Pratik?” she wonders at bedtime. “Mohsin likes him best.” “It’s your vote,” her mother says, switching off the light. “Nobody can tell you.” Mini wishes that she didn’t have to decide. “The only thing I know is that I don’t really like Rubina’s posters much,” she says. ​On Tuesday, the candidates distribute badges. ​Diya’s badges are shaped like stars ​Pratik’s badges are like circles. ​Akshay’s badges are as big as kitchen towels. They have chocolates taped to them. ​Rubina’s badges are small and messy. On each badge she has written ways to make the school a more fun place. Stop Bullying Keep Your Classrooms Clean Music at Breaktime Mini eats a chocolate on the way home. “Maybe I’ll vote for Akshay,” she says. “He will hand out chocolates if he wins.” “Akshay is breaking all the rules,” Arun says. “He is not supposed to make such big posters, or give chocolates, or force people to vote for him. But he will win anyway.” Wednesday is the day for speeches. Diya’s speech is as pretty as her posters. She talks about more art and dance classes in the school. Pratik is full of energy. His speech is about sports. Akshay is loud. His speech is about how great he is. Rubina is shy. Her speech is packed with ideas—ideas that Mini loves. Mini and Mohsin are eating chutney sandwiches when Bhaskar marches up to them. “You better vote for Akshay,” he says, aiming a kick at Mohsin’s ankle. “Nobody can tell us whom to vote for,” Mini says. “You can’t threaten us.” “Really?” Bhaskar jeers. Mohsin is scared. Mini is angry. “Our vote is secret,” she says. “We don’t need to be afraid.” “Aren’t you voting for Akshay?” Mohsin asks. Mini shakes her head. For the first time in days she is not confused. She whispers a name in Mohsin’s ear. ​​​​​​On Thursday, Mini stands in line. When it is her turn, she walks up to the ballot box, picks up a square of paper and writes a name in block letters. She folds the paper and puts it into the box. Whom do you think Mini voted for? Whom would you vote for? BALLOT BOX At lunchtime, Principal Kapoor announces the results. Mini is sad that Rubina has lost. Rubina’s posters were plain, her badges were ordinary and her speech was soft and nervous. But her ideas were so wonderful that she got Mini’s vote. Secretly, Mini is happy that Akshay has lost. Pratik is their new school captain. CAPTAIN At home, Mini tells her mother about the elections. “I think I have learnt to choose,” she says. “And I think I have learnt a little about voting. I can’t wait for the next school elections.” BALLOT BOX

title: Two Ducks
text: Once there was a purple duck. It loved to swim in nearby pond. One day while swimming, it saw another duck stuck in a net. That was a yellow duck. It was calling, "Help me! Help me!". Purple duck quickly swam to it and chopped the net with its beak. Yellow duck got free. Yellow duck said, "Thank you so much for helping me" to the purple duck. Then on they both became friends and started to play and swim everyday together.
author: Tanya Arora

title: The elephant and his tusks
text: In a haunted jungle with trees like huge, scary ghosts,there lived an elephant with his family and friends..He was a happy fellow. He played with his family and other baby elephants near the riverside..His name was Ecladin because he loved the character Aladdin.He was happy until some hunters came there were named ‘Tapers’. They were killing every single elephant they saw. Ecladins father, grandfather and grandmother were victims to the tapers,they were soon killed.After that day,he roamed around the jungle with a pale unhappy face.He was scared and lonely. One day as he was having his dinner,he heard shot sounds tuck tuck tuck. He ran and saw his mothers head bleeding like Willy Wonka’s downfall!!! That was the last person in Ecladins family dead. After that tragic day, he hid himself in a cave and never came out of it After a few days,there was a phone call from his friend, Dixima, the monkey who lived in the Central Park.He told that he was coming to visit him. Ecladin initially tried stopping him from the visit but later agreed. When Dixima came, he saw his friend hiding in the cave looking very sad.He asked Ecladin “what’s the matter”? Ecladin told the tragedy that had happened. Dixima wanted to help. He said,“if we make long tusks it may scare the hunters” Ecladin agreed. When the tusks were ready they looked too scary to wear. Ecladin put them on.He looked tall as a tower and poor dixima looked tiny as a mouse. Their next move was to find the hunters. After some research,they found the hunter’s and the captain name was Lamindo. Ecladin went to him gathering all his courage and trumpeted loudly swaying his trunk left to right and showing off his white strong tusks they looked deadly. The captain was shocked to see the white tusks that glared at him and shouted,“run for your life waaaa waaaa waaaa”. After that day no hunters came to the jungle. The idea was a success and all the elephants wore the tusks to protect them from humans. This is how all elephants are seen having white strong tusks to keep themselves safe. Dixima helped his friend, spent some enjoyable time there and then returned back to his own Central Park. After a few years Ecladin was seen with a sweet little baby elephant. He had got married and that was his baby who also got tusks.All elephants from that day got tusks and this can be seen from generation to generation. THE END
author: Aarna Solanki

title: TAKI and their cat friends
text: Carrot lay on the mat in front of Kavya’s house. He is a young cat. Kavya is certain he is a teenager. Cucumber is sneaking into the garden and stealing Carrot’s food. “Cucumber is Carrot’s mom”,said Asma. “Pineapple and Onion are Carrot’s siblings; I have seen them play together”, Tanisha joined in. “Look at that big grey cat!!!!! He seems to be the boss”,said Ila. Poof was glaring at her. All four friends walked noiselessly to the box in the garage to peer at Colsy, Shadow, R uby and Orange, the newly arrived kittens. “They are Cucumber’s new babies”, Kavya whispered. Orange and Ruby are having a staring contest. Shadow and Colsy playfully roll over each other. Colsy is the cutest of them all. There is one mysterious guest who visits now and then. He is a big orange and white cat. TAKI named him Garfield. TAKI spend many happy hours observing the cat family. Who is TAKI? Tanisha, Asma, Kavya and Ila are friends. They are TAKI. They play together in the evenings and have great fun.
author: TAKI team

title: How the Wolf Got its Howl
text: Long time ago, wolves and dogs used to live in the jungle together because they were all part of the dog family. They all used to bark to talk to each other. They mainly said woof-woof, bow-wow and arf-arf. There were 2 small wolf pups called Mark and Lucas who loved to play with each other all day, They had so many games to play, so they decided to play in the night too. It would be so good if we can play in the night also. OK Let us meet up tonight. So they came out in the night creeping as quietly as a cat and started to play. But they thought if they bark they will wake everyone up. So they decided to come up with a new sound. Mark tried to roar but that sounded like a lion. Lucas went oink-oink but that sounded like a pig. Mark tried to caw-caw but that sounded like a crow. Finally, they both tried howling “aaaaaoooooooooooooooo” and that sounded that no other animal, so they liked it. When other wolves heard it, they liked the sound. And from that day onwards, all the wolves started howling, especially at night.
author: Samar Sriranjan

title: Watch Out! The Tiger is Here
text: It's not easy being a tiger. Yes, tigers are beautiful and fierce. But tigers are also big and heavy. This makes it difficult for them to hunt for food. Out of every twenty times a tiger hunt, it eats only once. When a tiger moves through the forest, KHAU! KHAU! KHAK! The langur calls, just like an old man coughing! KHAU! KHAU! KHAK! AWOOOO! H AWOOOO! The barking deer calls, like a scared dog! AWOOOO! H AWOOOO! OOW! OOW! OOW! The spotted deer calls, like a little bird! OOW! OOW! OOW! The whole forest knows the tiger is here! AHUUUN? AHUUUN? The tiger wonders, where has everyone gone?
author: Anik Reddy

(May 2021) CarryMinatiPersonal informationBorn Ajey Nagar 12 June 1999 (age 21) [1] Faridabad, Haryana, India Nationality IndianEducation Delhi Public School SocietyOccupation YouTuberYouTube informationAlso known as Carry Ajey CarryMinati Channels CarryMinati Location IndiaYears active 2010–presentGenre Comedy gaming commentary Subscribers 30 million (CarryMinati) 9.06 million (CarryIsLive)Total views 2.3 billion (CarryMinati) 979 million (CarryIsLive)Network One Digital Entertainmentshow Creator Awards Updated: 3 May 2021 Ajey Nagar (pronounced [əˈdʒeː ˈnaːɡər]), better known as CarryMinati, is an Indian YouTuber and streamer. [2] He is known for his comedic skits and reactions to various online topics on his channel CarryMinati. [3] [4] In January 2021, Nagar was the most subscribed individual creator on YouTube India with 28 million subscribers on his channel CarryMinati. [5] His other channel CarryisLive is dedicated to gaming and live streams. [6] In May 2020, his roast video titled "YouTube Vs TikTok - The End" caused controversy on YouTube India. title: At The Zoo
text: Ira and her mother were going to the zoo. Ira's father was out to work and had given them 2 tickets to the zoo. Ira loved animals so she always enjoyed going to the zoo. Ira, with her the day which was today as zoo day. Ira was getting her shoes on while her mother was waiting for her. Ira took her backpack. Her mum took a suitcase with things for both of them. When they reached there was a lot of rush but they got a chance to get their tickets entered and go inside the zoo. Ira loved all kinds of animals but from all she best loves farm animals. So she requested her mother to take her to the farm animals section. She saw many Roosters there. At the farm animals section she met other children who had come to visit. Ira made 2 more friends. They together played on the fields and around they met the animals around and fed them with food which was provided to them. They promised to meet again some time. As Ira was about to leave the section, it started raining! she did not carry a umbrella so she enjoyed the rain. mother children from around came along and started playing in the rain. Then Peacocks in cages started dancing and birds started singing and chirping in chorus. Everyone loved rain. Then It was time to go home but Ira Pleaded to her mother for a quick round to see all the animals at the zoo. Her mom agreed. Then they saw all the other animals in the zoo. Her dad had come to pick them up with the scooter. Her mom went by car and Ira and her dad by the scooter. Driving, Ira kept seeing the fields and was enjoying the ride. She was happy When they were home Ira called over the girl she met at the zoo for dinner sitting together Ira could see her friend loved the food. Ira said good night to her mother and fell asleep. Thinking time What activities do you do at the zoo? What do you do when a friend comes over? ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ The End

title: Pigeon Chicks
text: There is no shortage of pigeons or crows in our neighborhood. I have grown tired of them. Pigeons destroy every plant of mine. At first I thought that they are eating only the new buds, but no, they are uprooting the plant itself. I’m so angry with them! They keep on pooping everywhere. You must be knowing, pigeons do not work hard to build a nest. Even if they do make one, it does not have any form or shape. They destroyed the plant in one of my pots and brought 2-3 straws and kept in it. And gave eggs on them. Next day, a crow stole an egg from the pot. Now, I also had to worry about their eggs. So, I kept the pot in the shade. To protect it from the crow, I had curtained it from outside. I had kept water and grains for the pigeons near the pot so that they do not have to go away from the nest. Now there were two eggs in the nest. A few days later two chicks came out of the eggs. The crows started hovering around again. Now my brother and I had to become guards for the chicks. We started guarding together. In a few days, both chicks were big enough to learn flying. I was very proud of the parent pigeons. Together they were teaching both of their chicks to fly. The first lesson of flying was taught on a nearby balcony. In one shift they would take the one chick. Both the pigeons would sit on either side of the chick. Chick was called up to the window sill. For a long time, they keep coo cooing. Then all three would fly together. Both of them would remain close to the chick while flying. I was moved by their dedication and efforts, of trying to teach their chick to fly. "Now my responsibility has been fulfilled", thinking this, I was freed from worrying. But what is this! Now the crows started nesting!
author: Sarita Narula

title: Mango Tree Ghost
text: Once there was a boy named Ramu, who went to his native place. He wanted to eat the mangoes from his farm, so he asked his grandmother "Grandma! I want to have some mangoes from those trees." Grandma said "No!! don't, those trees are haunted" Ramu asked "Why are they haunted???" Grandma said "they might be full of mangoes today, but tomorrow they will be empty." That same night Ramu was awake, he went near the mango tree, he ate some mangoes. Then he saw the 'mango seller' dressed all white. He understood, who was the ghost!! He thought of a plan....Idea!!!!! Ramu said in deep voice "Who are you and what are you doing here????" the mango seller panicked and shouted "Ghost Ghost!!'' Everyone in the village woke up and caught the thief. Grandma searched for Ramu "Ramu...Ramu, where are you?" Ramu's voice came from top of the tree "Hi Grandma!!so you have also met Mr. Ghost" Grandma said "Good job Ramu! Now, you can eat as many mangoes you want" Ramu said "No...NO..not anymore!!" because after the ghost went Ramu had already eaten many mangoes and he was full....BURP!!!
author: hariaksh rao

title: elephant without a trunk
text: In a jungle there lived a baby elephant, his name was Colt. Colt had no trunk and that made his life really hard, He was really sad. After a while he met a friend, an elephant, whose name was Claire. Claire was really nice and she had a trunk. Colt was jealous but at the same time he was also happy to make a friend. A year past they both grew up but Colt’s trunk was the same as usual. He felt very unhappy about it. They heard about a cave and where there is plenty of gold. They reached there and saw all the gold and a magical lamp. Claire shouted “COLT COME HERE! I FOUND A MAGICAL LAMP! Come lets try it!” Colt came running and was shocked to see the amazing, beautiful lamp. They took the lamp and rubbed it, a genie came out “whhooshhh” the genie said “Hello my majesty! how may I help you? ” Colt said “get me a trunk please” the genie said “your wish is my command. The trunk started growing and Colt was as happy. He was as happy as a bird. He started dancing and singing and Claire too could not believe her eyes. This is how Colt got his trunk.
author: Anaaya parikh

title: Lesson Learnt
text: In the busy street of Mumbai lived a girl Rena with her family Her parents were Mr.Rohan and Mrs. Myra. Rena’s parents were very hard working. On the other hand Rena never studied nor she listen to what other people say.She too did not help her family members with any work at all.One day when she was coming back home she was very sad.Her mom asked- What is the matter Rena? Rena replied sadly,” Mom I have a maths test next week.”Mom:So what Rena?Its ok I will help you practice. Rena:” Well, it’s good that it is next week so I CAN PLAY UNTIL THEN YEAH “, she shouted. Her mom told her not to shout and said softly: Yes,you can play now but you need to study hard in this week to get good grades. Rena:”maybe” and laughed away. Her mom thought " I hope she studies well” and went back to work But she was wrong about Rena. Rena wanted to play for long.So,she played with her toys and lied to her grandpa that she had studied and watched TV.The week passed and and then it was finally the day of test. But Rena was getting scared as she got closer to school.All the classes were over now it was time for the maths test Like all students she got a paper full of 20 Questions she stared at the paper because the test was very hard. She realised that she should have studied for the test instead of playing but what do I do now?,she asked herself. “ Hmmm,I think it is better to try my best or ask someone…but no it is a test and you can’t ask oh yes maybe I can say my head hurts so I don’t have to do that test anymore yeah! She thought and did as she planned but the teacher said: ok Rena let’s go to the medical room I am sure they have a medicine for head ache. ok? and then you might be able to complete the test.Let’s go.” Rena nodded.While they were in the hall,Rena spoke softly and sadly,”Teacher, I am sorry I lied to you. I don’t have a head ache.I didn’t know the answers to the test because I didn’t practice the whole week. I am very sorry. “Teacher replied: “That’s not nice but I will give you extra 10 mins for practice but you have to stay for long at school today to do the corrections later. Rena thanked the teacher but couldn’t solve the test.She was afraid of the results as she knew she would fail the test! Rena got very upset with herself.She got only.She walked home crying.Her family rushed to see what had happened she sighed and said: I am very sorry.I should have studied in the week. I told you all that I was studying but no,I was playing the whole week and now my marks I am very very sad and sorry too saying this she ran to her room and lay down on the bed Her brother knew what had happened,so he went to her and said,”Rena I know you didn’t get good grades but what can we do if we cry Come on,it’s ok.You ’re going to do better next time. Now that you have learnt your lesson,right? “. Rena replied: Yes you are right I will do better next time Thank you for making me understand. And she did, in the next test she got.This time she was very happy and learnt a lesson that one should give priority to studies and balance work and play. THE END
author: Shreya  Kalhan

title: The life funcho
text: FUNCHO Funcho, India's Top Comedy Youtube Channel Aims To Make Audience Laugh Out Loud With Their Content This Year 17 March,2021 04:48 PM IST | Mumbai | Partnered Content Share: Text Top Funcho channel on YouTube has more than 1.9 million subscribers, Funcho founders Shyam Sharma and Dhruv Shah believe its India's most loved comedy channels on YouTube Funcho founders Shyam Sharma and Dhruv Shah Someone has once said, "Comedy keeps the heart sweet." This is truly what Funcho founders Shyam Sharma and Dhruv Shah believe in. Today, they run one of India's most loved comedy channels on YouTube. From 2017 till now, their YouTube channel has gained lots of subscribers and their content has won many fans. If you are working why is their channel named as Funcho, well there's an interesting reason behind it. The word means laughter. These two founders who are engineers by profession love making people laugh. They feel happy when they see someone's expression changing from a normal one to a big laughter. Their fans keep telling them how much they love their content. The appreciative response keeps Dhruv and Shyam motivated every day. Funcho channel on YouTube has more than 1.9 million subscribers. The content they cover there varies from sketches to skits, jokes on trending topics or day-to-day, relatable stuff. Along with creating good videos, they keep their fans entertained on social media with memes and jokes on Instagram. Their Instagram page has more than 500K+ followers. Funcho's popularity has immensely grown over the years not only among the Youth but even grown-ups. Hence, Shyam Sharma and Dhruv Shah were invited at several instances to cheer the audience at several events and college festivals. The duo even collaborated with many celebrities for exciting videos. Funcho not only creates funny content but also music videos. Their video Gardi became an absolute fan favourite and was trending at top on YouTube for days. title: Monu and Meena learn to Share!
text: Monu was playing with his toy car and Meena was playing with her dolls. It was Sunday. Both of them looked happy playing with their toys. After a while, Monu asked for Meena's dolls. Meena refused to give it. After lunch they started playing again. Meena asked for Monu's cars, but Monu refused. They both started fighting and shouting loudly. Mummy heard loud noises from the kitchen and got disturbed. She said ' Monu and Meena, I don't want any noise. Don't talk to each other, I'm getting disturbed.' Monu and Meena kept quiet and continued playing. After an hour, Monu remembered that he had a appointment from the doctor so he went. Meena also went with Monu. When the doctor saw both of them looking sad, The doctor asked their mom about what had happened. Their mother told everything to the doctor. The doctor said " It's ok, I'll explain them." When Monu's teeth operation was about to start, The doctor said " You'll have to come with me inside the room. You can call anyone inside if you want." Monu called Meena to come with him. Meena went inside with him. After the operation, The doctor said ' Wow Monu, You are a very brave boy.' Monu smiled. The doctor said ' Meena you're also very nice, You supported Monu while he got scared.' Meena smiled too. The doctor continued ' So I am giving you a chocolate.' She paused and continued ' Oh, There is only one chocolate left, How will you both eat it? Hm, I guess you both will have to share it.' Monu and Meena looked at each other angrily. But just then they thought how they supported each other in the operation. They looked at each other and then looked at the doctor. They both decided that they will share the chocolate into 2 pieces and eat together. They both were happy. The doctor was also happy. Monu and Meena hugged each other! Moral of the story - Sharing is caring and Caring is sharing. Monu and Meena were first fighting together but they both helped each other too.
author: Aadya Atri

title: Short Necked Giraffe
text: In a forest that was very colorful because of the trees and flowers. There lived a giraffe named Hannah. Hannah was very pretty but she didn’t have a long neck nor did the other giraffe’s. She was happy mostly but we go on that later Like everyone knows that giraffes love to eat leaves from very juicy trees. One day Hannah saved a scientist who lived in the forest. His name was Ben who came to a forest for a mission. That day the scientist was finding a very rare leaf and he found that on the very top of a mountain. A big stroke of wind came and then the leaf went on a branch which was a little down for the edge of the mountain. the scientist tried to reach it but he slipped. Hannah nearby heard Ben say “ help!! I am going to fall for the edge of this mountain help! please help me!!!”. She went running to that mountain and with her teeth, she pulled him up from his coat and she saved the scientist’s life. Ben said that “ He would do 1 thing for saving his life” Hannah asked if he could maybe invent something that makes the giraffe’s necks longer because we can’t reach any leaves on the trees. “That would be hard but I see what I can do,” he said A week later Ben had told Hannah that the invention was ready, he called it the longonater. He zapped Hannah on the neck and in a few seconds she was able to reach any leaf on the trees. Hannah told all the other giraffe’s and one by one most of them had long necks. Ben was very happy that he was able to help all the giraffe’s but he remembered that he needed to check how much battery because there were a lot of giraffes who wanted long necks. Ben saw that he could see it saying that it said 1 zap power only left. Ben told all giraffe’s “ Sorry but I can only zap one more giraffe but I can make another one in 1 week” “booo booo boo” the giraffe’s kept saying. I am a week later. “Ben is the longonater 2 done,” Hannah asked “ almost I just need a battery can you just get me one from inside,” he asked “sure thing...all your batteries are dead Ben” “oh dear without the battery it won’t work” “I have an idea I need rain...it will rain in 2 hours,” he said. Hannah asked how that would help and Ben said “ where there's rain there thunder and where there's thunder there's lightning and lightning produces electricity” The lightning is going to hit giraffe lake. Hannah told that she had a boat they could use and in a few minutes, they were in the middle of the lake. Then the lightning struck and it charged the battery so nice that it never died. One by one all the giraffes. “Looks like my job is done here,” Ben said Thank You
