title: Grain grains
text: I used to grow up wherever I wanted to. My scorched grains in the Hindustani subcontinent meet in Mehargarh. These grains will be about seven thousand years old. I am the oldest of all cereals. " As soon as the rice grain or paddy wheat was finished, it started to roar, "I am basically Indian grain. My oldest grains have met Koldihwa and Mahagada in Uttar Pradesh. These grains will not be less than seven thousand years old, yes. " Now it was the turn of pulses. Arhar said, “Rice brother, you are not the only native Indian grain. We have not come from America-Wamerica anywhere. Our oldest grains have also been found in India - from places like Gufarakal, Burzholm and Chirand. Gufarakal and Burzholm are located in Kashmir and Chirand in Bihar. Nidhi and Golu were listening to this debate of grains. Together, they locked the grains in the compartments. After this, after writing the name of the old places related to them on a slip, he pasted them on the coaches. One thing was repeatedly piercing Nidhi's mind that even before these grains, there was a human being. What did he eat before that? He put his point in front of Golu. Golu said, "Before the beginning of farming, humans used to hunt animals for their food. Used to collect fruits-flowers, grains, plants-leaves and eggs etc. Humans started growing crops about twelve thousand years ago. These grains, which were arguing above each other, had their existence even before, but humans did not have control over their growth. Just as animals were domesticated, so too did humans domesticate these plants over time, and it was with this domestication that farming began.
author: BHADRA ASWIN

title: The boy who does what he feels like
text: I haven’t cycled today". He rushed out leaving the opened book as such. When came back tired after bicycle ride... Mother: Did you finish your homework? He: No. Will do it just now. He was taking a bath. "Oh, forgot to give the seed to grandfather!" He rushed to grandfather with the dripping towel on him, without closing the running pipe. Grandpa: What is this! Why are you here like this Child: Let's plant the seeds, Grandpa. Grandpa: We will. But first, wipe your body with a towel and put on dry clothes. My boy, you need not implement then and there what you feel like doing. You have to learn to be patient and wait a while. The next day. Boy in class room. The physics teacher is checking homework. Teacher: Why didn’t you do the homework? Child: I.... (aside) I felt like taking a bath after riding the bicycle, while taking the bath, thought about planting the seeds.. then.... some other thing.... thus forgot the homework.. Malayalam class. The teacher says to another boy, "Didn't I tell you to read that particular book and write the essay?" Boy: Didn't I too tell you to go to the library and read that book? You didn’t mind..... that’s why you got scolded now. Teacher.: Boy, I'm talking to him. Do not interrupt. You need not say then and there what you feel like saying. Wait a while. Speak only when it is appropriate. Got me? Chemistry teacher is teaching. Child: (aside) feel like drinking some water. (Loud) Hey... throw me the water bottle "- he called out to another boy on the front row. The whole class looked back in shock. 'What?' The teacher asked angrily. Child: That... I... water... Teacher.: Boy, is this the way to behave in class? You have to keep manners in public. Why not wait until the class is over and then go near him and ask for it? Do not implement what comes to mind immediately. You do have patience to think twice before you carry out what you have in mind. Well. I ban your football game today evening for this bad behavior. You should be with me from 4 to 5 p.m. instead. Evening. With the teacher. Teacher.: Do you understand what your problem is? You do not have the patience to wait. You have to learn to control that behavior. Okay, here's a book. Copy these passages to this paper neatly. The boy sat there for an whole hour and wrote. ﻿ Five o'clock. Teacher: If you do not act with patience and restraint, you will still get similar punishments. Do not immediately say or do anything that comes to mind. You have to think, speak and act with patience and control. Okay, You may go now.
author: Devi Sree Anil
illustrator: Iddi  Marumba; Nyambura Kariuki; Vartika  Sharma

title: Goplu's Train Ride
text: ​Every Wednesday, my Thammi picks me up from school. Thammi says that trains are the fastest way to travel in this city. ​Thammi smiles at everyone. Even strangers. She says if you smile at people, they smile back. Sunil Uncle is Thammi’s friend. He always gives me a toffee through the holes in the grille. Trains have grilles too. I put each finger in one square and hold on tight as the train sets off. ​Inside the train, aunties do all kinds of things. They cut vegetables.They knit sweaters. ​They put on make-up. Some even sleep, sitting up straight. ​There seem to be fewer people on our side of the grille. More and more aunties get into the other side. I see a little girl on the other side of the grille. Will she be my friend? I give her a shy smile… ​…And she smiles back! Thammi was right. I turn to tell Thammi about my new smile friend. ​But Thammi is busy. She’s taking out my snack from a box. Today, there’s luchi-jam roll. My favourite. I turn to show it to my friend. She has a packet of chips. We smile as she passes me one tiny chip. ​Thammi tears a piece of the luchi-jam roll. But it doesn’t go through the squares of the grille. Our station is here. I am sad that I could not share anything with my new friend. Just then, Thammi taps my pocket. I remember Sunil uncle’s gift. ​I fish out my favourite toffee… And I quickly give it to my friend. She smiles. I smile back and get off the train.
author: Timira Gupta

title: The chalk
text: I remembered the chalk of my childhood. A white pencil made of stone to write on a slate. This chalk was small, big, thick, thin, long, ie many types. From the front she used to be sharp. I used to enjoy writing with white chalk on a black slate. The other side of this pencil was wrapped in silver, gold or other colored paper. Our lives were stuck in this chalk and colorful paper. Bringing chalk from the 'Markand' shop by taking five paise from the mother was a celebration. This chalk was small, big, thick, thin, long, ie many types. From the front she used to be sharp. I used to enjoy writing with white chalk on a black slate. The other side of this pencil was wrapped in silver, gold or other colored paper. Our lives were stuck in this chalk and colorful paper. title: Hungry Pod & Healthy Pod in The Big Cake Contest
text: There was a Cake Contest in Podville. Hungry Pod decided he would enter the contest and make the world’s best cake. He loved to eat but he also loved to cook. YESSSS!!! Hungry Pod went to the market to buy everything he needed to make a cake. On the way he met Healthy Pod. Hungry Pod went to the market to buy everything he needed to make a cake. On the way he met Healthy Pod. “Hello Healthy Pod,” said Hungry Pod. “I am going to bake a cake for the Cake Contest. You can eat some of my cake when it’s ready.” “Oh no,” said Healthy Pod. “I never eat cake. I only eat spinach and broccoli. See? That’s why I’m so fit.” “I can eat anything,” said Hungry Pod. “I am always hungry.” Off he went to buy everything. Hungry Pod reached the market. He bought butter, eggs, sugar, chocolate and flour. But Instead of sugar, he got some salt. It looked the same to him so he didn’t realise what he had done. OOPS! He went home and began to make the cake. He mixed everything nicely together in a big bowl. Finally he put the cake into the oven. Then he covered it with gooey chocolate. He couldn’t wait to eat it. Yummmm!!! Hungry Pod decorated his cake. He put colourful sprinkles on it to make it shine. Finally his cake was ready. He carried his cake carefully to the Cake Contest. There were lots of cakes, but Hungry Pod’s cake looked the nicest. Everyone was sure he would win. Hmmm!!! Fussy Pod was the judge. She took a big bite of Hungry Pod’s cake. “PHOOOOEEEEYYYY!!!” “This cake is terrible,” she said. “It tastes salty, not sweet.” Everyone looked at poor Hungry Pod, who had gone red. He suddenly knew what had gone wrong. He must have put in salt instead of sugar. Healthy Pod put his arm around Hungry Pod. "Don't Worry, Hungry Pod. Your cake is still the best decorated" Hungry Pod got the prize for the best decorated cake. Hurray!!! CLAP CLAP CLAP CLAP CLAP He and Healthy Pod went home. Hungry Pod made a new cake. This time he remembered to put sugar. The cake was delicious. Even Healthy Pod, who only eats spinach and broccoli, ate a big, big slice. MMMMM...

title: I Can, You Can't
text: In the ChottaMotta forest, every animal boasted about being better than another animal in some way. Let us listen to what they told each other. The elephant said to the cheetah, “I’m bigger than you.” The cheetah said to the elephant, “But, I can run faster than you.” The tortoise said to the monkey, “I can live on both land and water. You can only live on land.” The monkey said to the tortoise, ”But, I can climb trees. You can’t.” The dolphin said to the octopus, “I can perform in a circus, but you can’t.” The octopus said, “But, I have eight legs and can change my colours.” The lion said to the giraffe, “I’m the king of the forest.” The giraffe said to the lion, “But, I’m the tallest animal, taller than you.” The peacock said to the snake, “Look how beautifully my feathers spread when I dance.” The snake said to the peacock, “But, my bite is more poisonous than yours.” Uh-oh! What all the animals told to show their superiority over others. But, did you notice that the same animals that boasted could not do a few things the other animal could do? Similarly, each of us is unique and has a unique talent or strength. So, we must not compare ourselves with others. Comparison is the thief of joy.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The Secret World of Mehlli Gobhai: The Man Who Found Art Everywhere
text: Jerry had heard that said often enough but he didn’t really believe it. One day in 2002, he and his friend, the artist Mehlli Gobhai, were walking in the hills around Gholvad. It was September and the rains had turned parts of the countryside green. ​“How lovely it all looks,” said Jerry. “Too much green,” said Mehlli. “I thought everyone likes green,” said Jerry. “I do, too. But when the trees are bare, you can see their shapes. You see how it is all geometry. Life has geometry underlying it.” Mehlli Gobhai: Untitled, mixed media on canvas, 2006 ​They walked to an anicut and stood listening to the music of the water gurgling and singing beneath them. ​“The water is brown,” said Jerry. “That’s why I came back to India. I remember walking in a wood in the United States of America and coming to a stream that ran so clear that I could see the stones at the bottom. I prefer this kind of stream,” said Mehlli. “Why?” asked Jerry. Mehlli said: “This stream is rich with mud. It is fertile. It will leave some mud on the banks and other things will grow. This stream carries life.” ​In 2012, Jerry was walking in Gholvad again. It was May, and the area was dry. The ground was hard and waiting for the rains. He could see the shapes of the trees. And when he came to the anicut, he thought again of the rich mud of the stream. In some ways, talking to Mehlli had felt like being on the banks of a muddy stream. Mehlli Gobhai was born in 1932. Bombay was very different in those days. The world was very different, too. India was under British rule. Even television was in the future. ​The Second World War broke out in 1939 and the Army requisitioned Gobhai House, Byculla, where the family was living. The family moved to a bungalow by the sea in Andheri, one of the seven bungalows of Saat Bangla. Then the Navy requisitioned that house, too. Perin Gobhai, Mehlli’s mother, decided that she had had enough of moving and being moved, and she bought the family a flat on Carmichael Road. This was wise because in the years to come Minocher Gobhai, Mehlli’s father, would suffer losses in business and Perin would keep things going by giving lessons in bridge and taking in boarders. ​Mehlli had a slow loris as a pet. He would spend his time in the evenings catching cockroaches and offering them to the slow loris. It would extend a long arm slowly and take the live insect and crunch it up happily. No one knew about the slow loris, and since it was a very quiet creature—and lazy too—Mehlli managed to keep it hidden in his room. Then one day, it found its way into the dining room. His mother insisted it go to a zoo and so Mehlli gave it to a French air hostess, who took it with her to Paris. She wanted to show it to her friends and scooped it up. The animal must have been in a bad temper after the long flight. It nipped off the tip of her finger. The next day it was in a zoo. After Mehlli finished college, he joined J Walter Thomson where he worked on advertising campaigns. In those days, artists would do “roughs” (sketches) to show the client. The client would ask for changes and then they would be refined. Bobby Kooka of Air India took one look at Mehlli’s roughs and said they did not need any further work. They could be used as they were. Later, Mehlli went to London to study art. He moved to New York and worked in advertising again, but what he really wanted to do was paint. So he gave up his job and started taking lessons at the Art Students League. There he was taught by the legendary Robert Beverly Hale. “He didn’t just teach us to draw an arm from the outside,” Mehlli would say. “He began with the bones and then he drew the muscles on to them, added the tendons, the fat and finally the skin. So we learned how an arm worked, not just how it looked,” Perin was worried about her son. Perin: Will he ever settle down? Minocher: Why should he settle down? He should strive to move up instead. But Mehlli also had to pay the bills, so he began to do illustrations for children’s books. There was To Your Good Health: A Russian Fable, and A Hindu Boyhood by Sharat Shetty. He didn’t like some of the things he was offered. Eunice Holsaert, who was his agent, said, “Why don’t you write your own books?” And he did. There was Lakshmi the Water Buffalo Who Wouldn’t and Ramu and the Kite. He was fascinated by folktales and classics of Greece and Persia. He loved the Gita Govinda by Jayadeva and Mughal miniatures and Rajput paintings. You can see how all these crept into his work. ﻿ ​ He also began to be recognised as a very fine artist. He took part in a show at the Bronx Museum. The New York Times wrote about him. He got his Green Card. That meant he could live in the USA but some part of him wanted to come home. ​“I would visit India and look at how gracefully the Lamani women would walk home, balancing pots on their heads. I would look at the glorious colours of tribal art and how a vendor would arrange his combs in a beautiful pattern and I felt I had to come back,” Mehlli would say. The odd thing was that when Mehlli was in New York, he used great big swathes of colour, perhaps because he was missing India. But when he got home to India, his palette changed and became quieter. He was interested in the darkness of the garbhagriha in a small temple. He wanted to capture the essence of things. He wanted to cut away anything that wasn’t necessary. So he would put up a canvas or a piece of handmade paper. He would take a black thread from his mother’s sewing box and divide up the space. Then he would sit and look at it for hours. Mehlli Gobhai: 2 Untitled, mixed media on canvas, 2007 “This is the most important moment,” he would say. Sometimes he would move the thread a little to the left or the right. Once he got it where he wanted it, he would draw the first line and heave a sigh of relief. After that he would begin to work. He used brushes, knives, cloth and dusters, sprays, anything that he thought he needed. “What if you make a mistake?” Jerry asked him. “Mistakes are always welcome.” “You’re not serious?” “A mistake can show you what you wanted to do, or it can show you what could be done if you let go.” A pause. “If you never make a mistake, it’s because you’re never taking a risk.” “But it’s still a mistake, right?” “Only if you think of it that way.” A crow emerged from under an armchair and began to totter about quietly. “Who’s that?” “Kauwwa.” “I can see that much, but why is he here?” “I found him under a truck. He can’t fly.” “What if he dirties your painting?” “Who knows, he might even improve it.” ​Here’s an experiment. Look at the drawings below. You can see a face. You can take away many of the details but it will still be a face. That’s what abstraction does. It takes away unnecessary details. Finally, you get this. The emoji? That’s an abstraction. But what if you don’t want to paint a face? What if you want to paint a thought? What if you want to paint a feeling? How would you paint that? ​When Mehlli had finished a painting, he would not title it. “Why not?” Jerry asked. “Because the viewer should name the painting. I don’t want to explain what I’ve painted. I want my viewer to say, ‘This is what I see.’ ” Different people see different things. “An old piece of leather.” “Something on the point of bursting into flames.” “A great darkness. A silence.” “Something that came into being on its own. An outcropping of rock. A crystal.” Mehlli Gobhai: Untitled,mixed media on paper, 2006 Try that. Look at a painting and name it yourself. It doesn’t matter if you joke. It doesn’t matter if you don’t understand. You’re not supposed to understand art or explain it. It’s supposed to make you feel, make you think. Give the painting a name. Here is one of Mehlli’s works. Can you see the Nandi Bull, the mount of Lord Shiva? Look for the horns and the hump. See how the image suddenly jumps out at you? With modern art, you go on a journey. You have to look and look again. You have to untrain your eyes and set your mind free. You have to try and follow the painter’s thought. Mehlli Gobhai: Untitled, lithograph, year unknown When he was in his seventies, Mehlli had a stroke. When he could not paint, he lost interest in life. He withdrew into his mind which was still full of images: the leopard cub at the court of the Rani of Kota, chasing the palace maids who would run away giggling; the snake that came to drink at his water hole where he would fill his pot when he visited Himachal Pradesh; the house Charles Correa designed for him in a chikoo orchard in Gholvad; his beautiful Saluki Salim, running alongside his bicycle in Central Park; his friend Andrew Kelly reading a book; walking in the hills and a cloud descending so that all the birds went quiet and all the trees began to fade... Mehlli Gobhai (1932–2018)
author: Jerry Pinto

title: Deeptha's Diary
text: I could behave myself with mother, that was really good. That is, not to retort to mother. I congratulate you, Deeptha, for being able to control yourself! The reply was at the tip of the tongue. But at the right time, I remembered my decision "never retort to mother (anyone) again". I still need to be able to keep it up. But the daydreaming in the social science class. There is no change to it. Though there is a piece of console. Today it was just ten minutes. Luckily teacher called me back. That is a wonder that she understands when I go dreaming! It was not right Deeptha, that you eat that soya curry secretly at lunch. Too bad. You have to pay attention. Don't be so selfish. Doesn't mother always say that if you share with others, it will taste better... Well! I, Deeptha, will remember it always. That incident happened during the play time this evening! When I saw Hita's behavior, I felt really angry and dislike towards her. How could she say that so rudely and so cruelly? But... don't I behave like this too... Well!. Thinking about each case.... Yes.. I say like that too, rudely, cruelly... That's not right. Don't you remember what was said in that class, "Our opinions and suggestions and criticisms should be said and pointed out. Do not hold them back. But they should all be done with humility, love and respect." It was only when I saw Hita's behavior that I realized I too was really behaving like that. Both of us should change this bad habit. I'll talk to Hita tomorrow itself. How enjoyable was the Malayalam period today! How beautifully Dipin recited that poem! Everyone applauded and how his face glowed! Overflowing with joy! It was good that you complimented him personally too. That made him even happier. I appreciate you for doing so, Deeptha. Well Done, Keep it up! Why did I quarrel with Jeeva? And that too, soon after she exhibited that stunning painting of hers? Have you noticed, Deeptha, that you get angry every time you see her beautiful paintings? Why? Really angry? You too like that pictures... Then..... are you.... are you jealous.... Jealous that you can’t paint beautiful pictures..... But Deeptha, right, you may not be able to paint beautifully. But what other talents you have! You help your friends and others, How patient you are to listen to what others have to say, You have the ability to take initiatives and work hard to make it a success. Then why bother with the inability to draw pictures! No! Do not be jealous. You also have a lot of talents. Not everyone has all the abilities. So no more jealous of Jeeva. Meet her tomorrow and appreciate the beauty of her pictures. If you can do that, you can get rid of jealousy. Surely you should appreciate Jeeva. Do not forget. Tomorrow.. Remember.. I’ll stop for today by talking about the presentation I made in class. Today in physics class I presented about Newton's color disk. But that was a flop. My mannerisms and appearance were not right. Some important points were left out too. Annu told me that I was curling my hair with one hand all the time and it should be controlled. If I had practiced well, I would have been able to perform a little more beautifully... It was prepared in a rush and so you didn’t get time to practice! That’s all!! Now you understood it is important to prepare well in advance. Enough for today! Tomorrow I will be a better person than today. Sure. Ok. See you tomorrow!
author: Devi Sree Anil
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Devi Sree Anil; Jemma Jose; Lutfia  Kamish; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Preethi Rajalakshmi; Sayan  Mukherjee

title: My Grandma
text: My grandma is a hardworking woman.mom is working so grandma does all the house chores.but she nevaer complaints about it. She even reads us stories. Whenever we want some help in studies and mom and dad are not home grandma helps us. She do's all the house chores and when we were babies she used to take us to the terris and put us on mattress and would dry the clothes. Sometimes when i am free i help grandma in her chores like planting seeds and washing dishes. My grandma is a all rounder.she can do everything.
author: Owellete Moonlight
illustrator: Ashok Rajagopalan; George Supreeth; Kobie Nieuwoudt; Nandita Likhate; Sreeparna Pal; Wiehan de Jager

title: Everyone is Unique
text: In the ChottaMotta forest, every animal boasted about being better than another animal in some way. Let us listen to what they told each other. I can climb trees. You can't. I can live on both land and water. You can't live in water. I can do circus and entertain people. You can't. But, I have eight legs and can change my colours. You can't! I’m bigger than you. I'm the largest animal on land. But, I can run faster than you. I'm the King of the Forest. You are a nobody. But, I'm the tallest animal. Taller than you. Look how beautifully my feathers spread when I dance. Nothing happens when you dance. But, my bite is more poisonous than yours. Uh-oh! What all the animals told to show their superiority over others. But, did you notice that the same animals that boasted could not do a few things the other animal could do? Similarly, each of us is unique and has a unique talent or strength. So, we must not compare ourselves with others. Comparison is the thief of joy.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: When will mom come
text: Grandpa can buy our potatoes.. But we bought potatoes on our own, and today we can buy eggplant, said Grandpa. Doc.... Doc.... Doc... Doc.... Then at 10 o'clock.. Grandma................. Buy and eat... Grandpa is frying appalam Roja is noisy... Then at 1 p.m. Grandma and I will go to school in Akkavoda after this holiday. Come... Rose... Daddy called us to go home at noon. author: harshspac 1577

title: Snip, Snip, Snip!
text: “Hi! I’m Lulu, Kit and Pat’s pet cat. Can you see me curled up in the corner?" Snip, snip, snip! “Kit is cutting shapes out of paper. Pat is reading. I think I’ll take a nap.” “Huh, what is Kit doing? Don’t cut your hair with those scissors, Kit!” Snip, snip, snip! “Oh, no! That didn’t turn out too well. Now Pat is cutting his hair too!” Snip, snip, snip! “Uh-oh! Now they both have funny haircuts. Mom and dad will not be happy to see this.” “How will Kit and Pat cover up their messy hair? Caps, hair bands, hair clips, scarves, woolen hats…” “…helmets, a big green hat. They even found these cool sunglasses. Don’t I look purr-fect in them?” “Pat has put a pot on his head and is pretending to be a soldier. Hey, put me down, Kit! Meowww! ” “Down come the curtains. Let’s pretend to be superheroes and fly away! Whoosh! ” “Ah…These flower pots seem to fit just right. Let’s pretend to be plants and catch some sunshine.” “Kit, be careful up on that tree. Let’s pretend to be monkeys. Hoo-hoo-haa-haa! ” Thump, thump, thump! “Whose footsteps are those?” “Oh-oh! Here come mom and dad!" “What will they do? What will they say? Can we pretend to be invisible?” Hahaha…Hehehe! “Mom and dad can’t stop laughing!” “But wait till mom and dad come inside. They won’t be laughing then. There’s no way Kit and Pat can hide this mess!” “Next time, I’m going to pretend to be a magician and make those scissors disappear! Abracadabra! ”
author: Megha Mehta

title: Gopal Gharial has a good life
text: One morning, Gopal discovered that he couldn't do everything that he used to. He was scared, his world seemed new. Strange. But most importantly, Distant. He felt confined. But he was slowly getting the hang of it. He paused and took stock of the world around him. When he finally got out again, He stopped to smell the lillies, made new friends and planted some trees. He smiled at the little things and cared about everything else a whole lot more He had fallen in love with the world all over again. But most importantly, he was kind.
author: Vaishnavi Giri

author: Bala  Sankari

title: Adventure In The Mesozoic Era
text: Once, there was a boy named Siddharth. He never used to like to go to school, but he loved making models and science. One day, his science teacher was teaching the students about nature. Hearing about nature, Siddharth coolly slept off. In his sleep, Siddharth was transported to the Mesozoic Era and landed on an Apatosaurus with a big thud….”Booooom”. The Apatosaurus looked at his back and said: “Welcome to the Mesozoic Era.” Siddharth could see various kinds of dinosaurs all around him. He jumped off the Apatosaurus’ back and wandered around looking at the tall conifers. Giant and small reptiles surrounded him. Siddharth ran towards the north direction and managed to climb one of the conifers. Perched on the top of the tree, he was able to clearly see the world of dinosaurs and its landscape. As he looked down, he saw a Stegosaurus under the tree. With an intention to strike a conversation with the Stegosaurus, Siddharth curiously asked him: “Hello Stegosaurus! am I in the Pangaea supercontinent?” The seemingly weak Stegosaurus nodded affirmatively. Siddharth was super excited to be in the supercontinent, as he loved the Jurassic Period. Siddharth, who was sitting on the tree saw the Stegosaurus enervated due to heat. Concerned, he jumped down the tree and was again surrounded by dinosaurs. While some dinosaurs were herbivorous, some were carnivorous. Some even wanted to pounce and eat him. But Siddharth was brave and calm and checked the Stegosaurus’ pulse. The dinosaurs were touched by Siddharth’s compassion and became his friends. The Stegosaurus was weak, dehydrated and immobile. It couldn’t walk till the river to drink water. So Siddharth had an idea. With the help of his dinosaur friends, Siddharth started building a tunnel from the closest point of the river to get the water near the Stegosaurus. Siddharth successfully channelised the water towards the frail Stegosaurus. But suddenly, the supercontinent started shaking and cracking rapidly. The tectonic plates were shifting. Siddharth was being moved to another part, while the dinosaurs were on the other side. As Siddharth was being dragged towards India in Asia, the dinosaurs were pulled towards the Northern Hemisphere going to North and South America. Siddharth was shocked about the moving tectonic plates and waved goodbye to the dinosaurs with a heavy heart. Just then Siddharth’s friends Vaibhav and Tavish were screaming from the door: “Sidddddddddddaaarrrth wake up, wake up, the bus is about to leave.” As Siddharth was in deep sleep Vaibhav came closer and jostled Siddharth to wake him up. Siddharth woke up and rushed to catch his bus. In the bus, Siddharth was busy narrating the story to his friends and teachers.
author: Siddharth Shivani Venugopal
illustrator: Pradyumna Ravi; Sheetal Shetty; Siddharth Shivani Venugopal

title: Jolly Fair
text: The fair had started in the city of Mahira. Children and elders were equally excited about going to the fair and enjoying the games and food. Farida was excited that day. Her family was planning to go to the local fair. Farida thought of all the different things at a fair - Ferris wheel, balloons, windpipes, candies. She pulled her mom’s dupatta in excitement. Farida and her family entered the fair. Farida saw the Ferris wheel rotating. P eople enjoyed the ride, but some of them were afraid and screaming. A man was selling balloons. Farida asked the man, "How much is one balloon." The man said, "10 rupees." Farida said, "Give me the blue balloon with stars on it." The man gave and she walked holding the balloon in hand. A man was selling ice creams in an ice cream cart. He was selling chocobar, mango duet, vanilla, strawberry, and chocolate ice ﻿ creams. Farida's mom bought a strawberry cone and tasted it. A merry-go-round went round and round. Farida was happy to see her school friends Srini and Shweta at the fair. A man was selling biryani and Gulab jamuns. Farida and her sister went and bought 2 plates of biryani and 5 Gulab jamuns. Farida could not resist buying the cotton candy also. Farida and her sister finished eating all the food they bought at the fair. Now, they were ready to leave the fair and go home.
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Aindri C; Kishor Joshi; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Shamim Ahmed; Shohei Emura; Shreya  Sen

title: Loving Pod and Grumpy Pod in The Puppy Surprise
text: Grumpy Pod was feeling sad. He had no friends. He looked out of his window and saw everyone having fun together. But you see, Grumpy Pod had no friends because he was so Grumpy. If anyone tried to talk to Grumpy Pod, he would snap at them. When Geeky Pod tried to show him his new computer, Grumpy Pod growled at him and said, “I’m not interested.” When Healthy Pod asked him to come for a walk, Grumpy Pod snarled at him and said, “Oh go away! I hate walks.” All the Pods in Podville left him alone. Poor old Grumpy Pod! Cafe He would have lunch by himself. He would water the plants in his garden all by himself. He would watch TV by himself. He was really a very lonely Pod. But there was one Pod who saw Grumpy Pod’s loneliness and that was Loving Pod. You see, Loving Pod loved everyone. She was sweet and friendly and kind. “I must help Grumpy Pod make friends,” she said to herself. Loving Pod had an idea. “Grumpy Pod needs a pet to cheer him up,” she thought. So off she went to the Podville Pet Shelter to get a pet for Grumpy Pod. The Podville Pet Shelter had kittens and puppies and goldfish. Loving Pod looked at them all. Finally she chose a sweet little brown puppy. The next morning, Grumpy Pod had just finished his breakfast, when there was a knock on the door. He opened the door, but there was no one there. Then to his surprise, he saw a basket on the ground. And what do you think there was in the basket? Yes, the sweet little puppy. “Whose puppy is this?” said Grumpy Pod, grumpily. The puppy jumped up and wagged his tail. He tried to lick Grumpy Pod. He rolled over and waved his legs in the air. He looked so funny that Grumpy Pod laughed and laughed and laughed. He never felt so happy in his life. The little puppy would sit by Grumpy Pod’s feet while he read the paper. He would curl up next to him while watching TV. Grumpy Pod began to like having him around. Grumpy Pod named the puppy Brownie Pod. He had such a good time with Brownie Pod, that he forgot to be grumpy. He made friends with the other Pods. Soon he wasn’t lonely any more. “Why Grumpy Pod, we will have to change your name soon,” said Loving Pod. And instead of being grumpy, Grumpy Pod just smiled at Loving Pod. “You must get a pet, Loving Pod, it’s fun!” he said. Loving Pod just smiled to herself. No one knew her secret that it was she who had given Grumpy Pod the puppy and made him so happy.
author: Sonia  Mehta

title: Tigers adventure
text: Tiger was walking in the forest. A tragedy had occurred. His entire Tiger clan had fallen because of hunters. He was the only one left. As he walked in the moon light, a fire was spreading from the south. It had not rained for several days and a stupid traveler set a wildfire. All the animals had started coming north. It was not safe for the Tiger at all but he had no choice. The Tiger often used to come to the marsh to quench his thirst, but since last week he can only come at night or else he will be shot. The Tiger stood on his tall favorite rock and watched as the nearby village cattle returned. He never attacked the village or its cattle. As the Tiger lapped at the water, he wondered how long the wildfire would last. He could see a red glow and often scuttling animals. Night started falling. The burning noise got louder and louder. After the Tiger could not smell men, he started to hunt. The options were very less. Usually he could only eat a small Deer. Today he caught only a Rabbit. A week passed. The wildfire had died down, but only a few birds and monkeys were visible. The Tiger was getting desperate. He hadn't eaten in 2 days. Suddenly he saw movement in the grass. A buffalo had strayed from the group. Stricken by hunger, the Tiger pounced on it. The buffalo was flabbergasted by the attack. The buffalo tried it's best to defeat the Tiger, but was not strong enough. At the village the news spread like fire. People gathered to decide what to do. Vishnu, who owned the Buffalo said" I will go kill the Tiger". Saying this Vishnu went to his mud hut and brought out a double barreled gun. That night He climbed a tree near the marsh and waited. Soon the Tiger came to drink water. Vishnu took the aim and shot. The tiger hearing the noise ran away. Vishnu had missed completely. Vishnu returned to the village.. For a few days the Tiger stayed hidden. After a while when he couldn't bear the hunger, he went to the Village at night and attacked a fine Cow. The Cow mooed waking up all the Villagers. They chased the Tiger to the marsh. He was just about to cross the bridge when he suddenly slipped. The Tiger was washed away to another land. He had gone unconscious. He woke up slowly and saw the land. The land was beautiful. It was filled with grass and animals of all sorts. The Tiger enjoyed his life in the land. Even the villagers were happy. They thought the Tiger was dead. All of them lived happily ever after.
author: Arav  Gupta
illustrator: Barkha Lohia; Kavita Singh Kale; Krishangi Oberoi; Krishna Bala Shenoi; Manjari Chakravarti; Rob Owen; Vusi  Malindi

title: City in the forest
text: Once upon a time, in the forests of odisha lived six birds. One of them was dull colored dinku. The others did not make friends with her. The little orange bird named pinku came to her and asked "why aren't the other birds playing with you?" Dinku replied "They don't like my color, so they don't talk to me" pinku told her bright colored friends to be good with dinku. They thought for a while and agreed to play with dinku. ﻿There was a city beside the forest in which the birds lived. Parvati and Gopi were trying to save a tiger who wandered too close to a old falling building. ﻿The birds thought it was too funny how both the tiger and the people were scared of each other. They sank down under a tree laughing. ﻿The media people started pouring in and asking parvati and gopi too many questions. ﻿From that day onwards gopi and parvati were called animal saviors. They saved hundreds of animals form dying because of the city. They tried hard to take the cities away from forests. ﻿Let's not cut trees, Let's not disturb the animals, Let's not use them for circus, movies and media.
author: Bhargavi Vardhan

title: Solar Eclipse
text: It feels like the night has fallen. But it is not the night, it is Solar Eclipse. Actually, the moon orbits the Earth and the Earth orbits the Sun. And it is interesting to know that the Moon and the Earth rotate on its own axis. And when they come in a straight line where the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, the shadow of the Moon falls on the Earth. That is why, for some time, the Sun is not visible at all! This is called Solar Eclipse. ﻿ ﻿The Moon is much much smaller than Sun. It is even smaller than the Earth, Even then it covers the whole Sun! How? Because Sun is much far away, about 400 times away from Earth in comparison to the Moon! That is why the Sun, about 400 times bigger than the Moon, looks equal to the Moon. Far away items look smaller than the closer items. Oh! So now I understand, that is how the moon covers the Sun. Solar Eclipse is very beautiful but we should not look at it directly with naked eyes because it is harmful. So now the question appears that how can we see this natural phenomenon without harming our eyes? Well, we can see this natural beauty through television news channels or we can wear special sunglasses to see this phenomenon. ﻿ ﻿Looking at the Sun can harm our eyes. Even though the Sun is hiding behind the Moon, the Moon can not cover the Sun fully. The remaining ring like visible part of the sun is called Ring Of Fire and this ring of fire may harm our eyes severely. So please don't look directly at the sky during Solar Eclipse
author: Advika .

title: I see colors everywhere
text: Manu wondered how many colors he can see in his daily activities. Manu's mother washed some clothes today and Manu helped hanging them. He saw so many colors on the clothes. After Manu hanged the clothes in the clothesline, he felt hungry. So he went to the kitchen and took a packet of chips and ate them, he saw that the chips also had colors on them. It was yellow in color. Manu could find many things in the kitchen which had colors but the most colorful were the vegetables. Now it was evening and Manu was at the park. It had rained some time back and it was sunny now. Yes, you are right! He saw a rainbow. Manu saw that the rainbow had shades of colors and it was beautiful. Manu ran home. "Amma, Amma, I saw a rainbow", said Manu excitedly. Is that true? Amma asked peeping out of the kitchen window. Yes, yes, see it for yourself, jumped Manu. It was time for Manu to eat dinner. and he saw so many more colors in his plate too. And after dinner he slept. Manu had a wonderful day, what about you?
author: Akshara Karthik
illustrator: Akshara Karthik; Gayathri Bashi; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'

title: Mouse in the House
text: There was a mouse in the house. Grandma saw it first. "Mouse!" she screamed, jumping up the sofa. The cushions fell on the floor. “Where?” asked Dad, climbing up the window. He pulled the curtains down. “There!” shouted Mum, leaping up the table. The plates fell with a crash. “Catch him!” said Mike to the cat. The cat looked at the mouse and fled under the bed! “Mouse!” screamed Mike, running behind the cat. “I will chase it out!” said Mum bravely. She took out the broom and poked here and there. “Mouse!” shouted Dad. “Behind you!” Mum looked at the mouse, and fled under the bed! "I know what to do!" shouted Grandma jumping down from the sofa. She rolled up a newspaper and poked here and there. “Mouse!” yelled Dad, climbing the window even higher. “To your left!” Grandma looked at the mouse, and fled under the bed. “Oh no!” said Dad softly. He couldn’t go any higher. He climbed down carefully, and fled under the bed before the mouse could see him! "Mouse in the House!" shouted everyone together. That woke Baby up. She sat up on her mat, rubbing her eyes sleepily. What was that on her pillow? It had two eyes, four feet, and a long tail. "Mouse!" said Baby, clapping happily. Baby looked at the mouse, and the mouse fled, with Baby right behind him! Leaping up the sofa, climbing the window, jumping up the table, tumbling over the cushions...... running in between the curtains, scurrying over the plates, and out of the door!
author: zhong fu

title: No Smiles Today
text: Mike were good friends. They had so much fun together. They shared secrets in class. They ran races on the way home. She was always cheerful. One day, Amy came into the classroom slowly. Her head was bent. She looked sad. “Did someone scold you?” asked Mike. Amy shook her head. She sat down and did not look up. She did not answer ‘Present!’ when Sona Miss called her name. Sona Miss called again, louder this time, “ Amy Lee!” Amy raised her hand. “Do you have a sore throat?” her teacher asked her. Amy shook her head. Her cheeks were red and it looked like she had a fever. “Are you feeling okay?” Sona Miss asked. Amy nodded, still not daring to look up. “Why does Amy look so sad?” “Is your little brother okay?” “Is your puppy okay?” “Is your grandmother okay?” Amy kept nodding her head to each of her friends. But she did not look up. Mike wanted to make her smile. He had an idea! He took out something from his bag. As he ran to show it to Amy, it slipped out of his hands. Amy saw something flying towards her and she grabbed it. It was a BIG, green, rubber frog! Amy's eyes flew open. Then she opened her mouth to laugh. THEN Mike and her friends saw why she had not smiled or talked all day! Four of her front teeth had gone missing!
author: zhong fu

title: Don't Wake the Baby!
text: Jack have not been happy. They are not allowed to make noise when the baby is sleeping. But the baby is ALWAYS sleeping! They are not allowed to run in the house. They are not allowed to chat at snack time. They are not allowed to scream, no matter what. But the toughest rule is this one. When the baby is asleep, Jane and Jack must whisper. If they want to laugh, they can only giggle softly. But one day, the story they are reading is so funny that they can’t help laughing. Jane and Jack crack up. Oh no! The baby is sleeping. The baby wakes up crying. Mum is angry. She yells at them to go play outside. Jane is sulky. She doesn't like being yelled at. Jack comforts her. He says that it will be more fun to play outside. They can be as loud as they want! After playing football for a while, Jane and Jack are happy again. Jack kicks the ball. GOAL! The ball flies across the garden. BANG! Oh no! The baby is awake! What will happen now? The baby wails. The baby is so loud that his crying breaks the milk bottle. It cracks the pot. It cracks the window! The baby is so loud that his crying lifts the roof off! Their brother won't stop crying. Jane and Jack rush inside. Where is Mum? Jane holds the baby and sings. But the baby keeps crying. Jack dances. He does tricks. But the baby keeps crying! What makes a baby stop crying? Soon, Jane and Jack are crying, too. That's when Mum gets home. Mum picks up the baby. She comforts him. She sings a lullaby. The baby stops crying. Now Jane and Jack understand. It's impossible for babies to be quiet. So it’s better to just not make noise. Sshhhhh!

title: Lily's Red Bean Plant
text: Lily said. "Now I can grow my own red bean plant. ” First, plant the seed, Lily read. So she did. “You’re doing great, Lily!” the book told her. Now, water it. La La La! Lily sang as she did just that. “My red bean plant will soon grow up,” Lily told her friends. “You have to water it a lot to keep it healthy," they said. "Just like kids have to drink a lot of milk to grow big and strong!” A few days later, the red bean sprouted. “Look, Mom!” Lily called. "It's growing!" The next morning, Lily watered her plant again. " La La La! Drink, drink, drink!" she sang. "If you drink more water, you'll grow up faster!” "Oh my, Lily, not like that!" said the book. Lily watered again at noon. La La La! "Oh my, Lily!" the book said, louder now. " My pages say not to water a plant at noon." But Lily kept right on watering. La La La, La La La! Oh my, Lily! You've forgotten to read me! The next day, Lily gave her mother instructions as she left for school. "Give my plant more water at noon, please!" “Have you read the book?" her mother asked. "In my pages, it says to water the plant only once a day," the book said sadly. Oh my, Lily! Three days later, Lily was sad, too. "My poor plant!" she cried. At school, she talked to her friends. “I have been taking such good care of my plant. Why is it so sad?" “What does the book say?” they asked. “Oh my," Lily said. "I stopped reading it." At home, Lily showed the plant to her mother. “I'm sorry, Mom,” Lily said. "I'm going to read the book now." "That's a great idea," her mother replied. Do not water the plant too much, or its roots will become soggy. Lily read. The leaves will then droop and turn brown. “I’m so sorry, Red Bean,” Lily whispered. “The plant won’t be sad, because he knows you love him," her mother said. "You can show him your love by learning how to take good care of him." "You can also say sorry to the book, because you ignored her. She needs your attention, too!" A few days later, Red Bean was healthy again. Now Lily and her gardening book were best friends!
author: zhong fu

title: The day there was no story left
text: Minu loved listening to stories. She listened to stories from her Aaji (Grandmother), who told her about Ram and Sita and Krishna and Vishnu. She heard stories from her Ma (mother), who told her stories of sparrows and crows and some that sounded like little songs. She always jumped and danced and heard these stories over and over again. She enjoyed stories from her Pa(father). He told her stories of animals and birds and horses and donkeys and little girls and boys and fishes and of himself. He kept telling her stories till he fell asleep. She enjoyed the most with her Aaba(Grandfather), who could tell a story of anything and anybody. One day he told her a story about getting bored! I know, it sounds crazy, but he did. And Minu just could not stop laughing and imagining how each character was behaving in that story. She even thought it was about her because she would often complain about getting bored, when no one was telling her stories. And when, nobody had anything new to tell, she would sit down with her books. At night, she would drift off into imaginary worlds of story characters and La La Land. Stories made her happy. Stories made her imagine a new world. She could dream of them, she could see those characters with colourful dresses and big moustaches, yellow fluffy ducklings and brown horses with silky shiny tails, and huge castles with mouses as big as cats. She would wonder how those dwarfs made a tiny, spectacular house with everything in it. She would love to live in one such house someday. Afternoons were lazy, Minu did not like sleeping though, and so did her Aaji. They both sat through hot afternoons with closed windows and pulled curtains. Aaji put on her glasses and stitched pretty dresses for Minu’s dolls. And while making those dresses, she told stories of being kind and generous. Minu even imagined herself in those stories. Sometimes, she thought everyday was from a storybook. In the evenings, she would wait for her Aaba to tell her stories. Stories of people they saw on the streets, animals that moved around, crows and pigeons fighting for that piece of bread. Nights would often be stories from Ma from a book or even better hilarious made-up stories from Pa. Minu believed she would sleep well and wake-up happy if she heard a story before going to bed. No one thought it was true but she still believed in it and quite strongly though. She would throw a tantrum and cry and make it really unpleasant for everyone if they refused for a story. It did work on most days but some days no one wanted to tell any story. “I will read that book sure, but listening to a story is very very important,” she would insist. And one such day, when no one told her any story, because they were all very busy and it had gotten very late at night and even her crying and throwing pillows had not worked, she had to go to bed without listening to a story. She tried to read a book, but she was so upset that all she could see through her tears was blurry letters. She kept the book aside and tried to drift away into an imaginary world. But she was very angry and she simply cried herself to sleep. Strangely, no one heard her sob under her blanket. “They are all too busy to care,” she thought. The next day, Minu woke up early. Earlier than most days. She did not find her parents on the bed, like everyday. They would be up before her and mostly busy in their work. Aaji, organising the almirah, Aaba napping with newspaper on his chest, Pa working on his laptop and Ma busy with chores. Everything was usual until Minu asked Aaji to tell her a story. Aaji, just could not think of any. “But you have so many good books, just read anyone from those, but it should be a new one,” argued Minu. Aaji, took out those books but could not find anything new in them. “You are acting like you don’t want to tell me a story!” said Minu, very irritated with this silly trick of Aaji. “I am trying to read, but I can’t see the story here anymore,” Aaji tried to explain. “Who would believe this? I know, you can’t fool me now with these tricks, I understand everything,” Minu was agitated as she stomped out of the room. “Aaba, never says no, he doesn’t even need books to think of stories, he can make his own stories,” thought Minu. She saw Aaba, sitting by the window and looking at the kids playing on the street. “Aaba, tell me a story”, she demanded. “Yes, of course,” he said, delighted to see Minu. “What story would you like to hear today?” asked Aaba. “hmm, any story, okay wait...story of a crow, but something new, a story that I haven’t heard before...can you tell that Aaba?,” asked Minu. “Let me think.” “Oh! I really can’t think of any such story, nothing is coming to my mind right now,” said Aaba. He did look like he was trying to think of a story. But he just could not think of anything. Or was he just pretending. “This cannot be possible! You always make new stories, how can you not think of anything today,” Minu was shocked. She thought she should give him some time and then, he will surely come up with a fantastic story. So she asked him to think of a story and she would come back again to listen. When Minu went back to Aaba (After what seemed like several hours), he was still struggling to think of a story. “I can’t believe this!” Minu was almost pulling her hair. Aaba was looking at her through his glasses, and he did look very helpless. He then quickly started looking through some of Minu’s storybooks for ideas. It was quite strange that he was all puzzled looking at the books. “Minu!” he gasped! “Minu, come here, is it just me, or even you cannot see anything new or interesting in these books?” he asked quite genuinely. Minu did not care to listen anymore. By now she had gone to Ma. Ma picked-up Minu, they both sat on the jhula (swing) and kept thinking. Ma could just make up a story from everything that Minu did or did not do. Minu was sure ma will tell her a story. BUT.... even Ma could not think of anything. Not even a funny parody song. She was an expert in creating these hilarious songs with random rhyming words. Her songs would be funnier in times of distress. While Minu kept wondering what funny song Ma would come up with, she saw her get up from the jhula and leave. “Where are you going? Where is my Story?” Minu was getting restless now that even Ma could not think of any story. With very little hope she went to Pa. He cupped her sulky face in his big palms, pouted a funny pout and asked her why she looked upset. Before Minu could say anything, Pa himself offered to tell her a story. Minu was delighted. Her eyes lit (just for a split-second). And just then, something happened and Pa too could not think of any story. “I am sorry, Minu, it’s so strange but I am unable to think of anything,” he said with a very sad face. Minu was now in tears. What has happened to everyone? How come no one remembers any story? How come no one can think of any story? How come they can’t even read from books? “Is this really real?”Minu wondered. She also kept thinking of ideas to find out what had happened. “I should start with the books first,” she thought. She went straight to her book shelf. There sat all her favourite books, neatly arranged, until now. But today wasn’t any other day, she did not have to worry about the arrangement of books. Minu started pulling out one book after the other. Panchatantra, Gruffalo, Bookasura, Blue Umbrella, the Twits, Mr Fox, Vikram-Betal and almost everyone was on the floor. To Minu’s utmost shock, there was nothing.....YES! NOTHING.....in any book she took out! Where did the lion and the mouse go? Where is the monster? Where is Binny? Where are Mr and Mrs Twits? Where are Charlie and the Kings and the Wolves, the Pigs and The bears, the Dwarfs, Suppandi and the countless characters that spoke to her through their stories??? The books were nothing but plain pages. Minu kept taking out book after book and all she could find was blank pages. She was clueless and tears kept flowing from her eyes. What was happening? So, everyone in the house was not pretending? NO ONE....NOT EVEN BOOKS had stories in them. Why was this happening? Where were all the stories? What was Minu going to do now? Minu had to find out. She JUST HAD TO! She looked into all the books to find a clue. But No Luck! Minu dug into her craft work, her drawing books, toys, Ma’s dairies, Pa’s notebooks, those drawers that were filled with bills and random paper and almost everything that she could. Sigh! There was no clue. Minu kept thinking and thinking and thinking till she almost fell asleep on the floor. “But, Hey! No, I can’t be sleeping now, NOT NOW,” Minu told herself. And just then, just how sometimes a nice new game occurs to you from the same old toys, Minu had an idea. What if no one had a story to tell, Minu had all the stories in her mind. So she straightaway went to Aaji and Aaba... sat by their side and said, “If you cannot think of any new story, let me tell you one today.” And she began telling stories to them. She was so happy, she told them four stories. Yes, two each (that’s how she would ask them to tell her). To her extreme delight, they both remembered some very nice new stories of Krishna, Vishnu and some stories of fishes. Also, they were so pleased to hear stories from Minu, they kissed her forehead, gave her some extra laddoo and said, “You should tell us stories often, they are so interesting. And you are so smart.” She tried the same trick with Ma and Pa and they too told her some very funny stories about dogs chasing them and some even funnier songs. Pa even gave her his new scrapbook to work on. Ma hugged her tight, kissed her and they both too asked her to tell stories often. “What amazing stories you have, you should tell us often,” they said too. Minu felt a new warm, fuzzy happy feeling. She liked how it felt making someone happy.This made Minu proud of herself. Also, her plan had worked! But what about the Books! How could she tell a story to a book? She went back to her books. Looked closely at all of them again, and that’s when she realised that the books were always having their stories in them just like before. She was just too scared and worried earlier, that she could not see anything in the books. Also, she had read them so many times, she did not find anything new or interesting in them anymore. However, Minu was pleased to see all her favourite characters back in her books. She hugged her books and arranged them nicely in the bookshelf. She re-read some of them again. Minu loved them even more now. Probably, she needed some new books with new stories. And so Minu thought, maybe, we just have to give back what we get and we will get double of that. Like double the stories, double the happiness and a bonus of seeing someone happy. Not to mention, those candies, hugs, kisses and many more goodies. Telling stories to her grandparents and parents was actually as much fun as listening to stories from them. Now, on some days Minu makes sure she tells everybody stories. Sometimes, the ones that she has heard. Sometimes, the ones that she has read. She is also making plans of giving away some of her toys and books to children who would like them or don’t have them. But on most other days, she still lies down demanding one story after another, until everyone is out of stories, for real. And, that is alright, I guess.
author: Supriya Khandekar

title: Gloria's Idea
text: Gloria’s Idea Cream the Rabbit is very confused. She sat on her chair and was lost in her thoughts. “Who has been stealing all the carrots from my garden?”, she said to herself. Cream had started her own garden after she retired as a school teacher. She had planted many flowers, vegetables and creepers in her garden. The carrots were very plentiful. But recently, Cream noticed that a lot of carrots had been missing from her garden. One day, Cream’s neighbour, Gloria the giraffe came to her house. She said, “Hi Cream, what are you thinking?” Cream offered Gloria some fruits and then she told her, “Someone is stealing all the carrots from my garden”. Gloria said, “Oh! That is really sad. Your carrots are really tasty. You grow them organically. We have to get the help of someone to catch this thief. I will soon get back to you”, said Gloria and left. Next day, Gloria called Cream and said, “I have spoken to road-maker Zumba the zebra. He said he will help us. He will bring some tar, that is used to make roads. Tar is a black fluid that is sticky. I will also come with him”. Next day, Zumba and Gloria came to Cream’s house. Zumba laid tar on the pavement leading to the garden in the evening. Then he left, “Call me if you need any help”. Cream and Gloria finished eating dinner and went to sleep. At midnight, they heard the howling of a fox. Both of them came to the garden and saw Figgy the fox carrying four carrots. A cart full of carrots was lying nearby. But his legs were stuck on the tar and he could not move. Cream said, “Oh, you are the carrot thief!” Gloria said, “Figgy, you must not steal. Cream puts hard work in growing her carrots. We will tell the police about this. Figgy got scared and said, “I am sorry, I stole the carrots. I will repay Cream the money I got when I sold the carrots. Please don’t report this to the police. Then, Zumba came and helped Figgy out of the tar. Then, Figgy promised Cream that he will work in her garden to help grow carrots and sell them too.

title: THE INTRODUCTORY HISTORY OF THE MOST AWESOME MARS ROVER
text: Curiosity is a car-sized Mars rover designed to explore the Gale crater on Mars as part of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) mission. Curiosity was launched from Cape Canaveral (CCAFS) on 26 November 2011, at 15:02:00 UTC and landed on Aeolis Palus inside Gale crater on Mars on 6 August 2012, 05:17:57 UTC.The Bradbury Landing site was less than 2.4 km (1.5 mi) from the center of the rover's touchdown target after a 560 million km (350 million mi) journey. The rover's goals include an investigation of the Martian climate and geology, assessment of whether the selected field site inside Gale has ever offered environmental conditions favorable for microbial life (including investigation of the role of water), and planetary habitability studies in preparation for human exploration. In December 2012, Curiosity 's two-year mission was extended indefinitely,and on 5 August 2017, NASA celebrated the fifth anniversary of the Curiosity rover landing.The rover is still operational, and as of June 3, 2021, Curiosity has been active on Mars for 3137 sols (3223 total days; 8 years, 301 days) since its landing (see current status). The NASA/JPL Mars Science Laboratory/ Curiosity Project Team was awarded the 2012 Robert J. Collier Trophy by the National Aeronautic Association "In recognition of the extraordinary achievements of successfully landing Curiosity on Mars, advancing the nation's technological and engineering capabilities, and significantly improving humanity's understanding of ancient Martian habitable environments." Curiosity 's rover design serves as the basis for NASA's 2021 Perseverance mission, which carries different scientific instruments. ﻿
author: Naman Ravi  Argekar

title: eating life
text: There are so many delicious food cooked in our country that just mentioning the name makes the mouth water. From Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Gujarat to Arunachal Pradesh, you will find dishes of different tastes everywhere. There is one thing behind the dishes made in different regions, which binds them all in one thread, they are spices. Yes, it is these spices, which make the food delicious. If the food does not contain the right amount of spices, then the fun of eating becomes gritty. Have you ever thought that these spices also have a history? Knowing how many foreigners came to India in search of spices. Spices of India are mentioned in the travelogue of Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang in 629 AD and Marco Polo's compositions of 1298 AD. The nutmeg plant is believed to have been first seen in Rome around the 1st century AD. By the way, this plant, which is called 'Green Gold', is basically the origin of the land of spices 'Indonesia'. Egg-shaped nutmeg thrives in warm areas. Apna Desh is the largest producer of turmeric in the world. India alone accounts for 80 percent of the total production of turmeric in the world. Turmeric tea is very popular in the city of Okinawa, Japan. Apart from these, there is another important spice - black pepper. Black pepper has a special place in world trade. Pepper once had so much power that it changed the history of the world. Most of the sea voyages from the west were in search of pepper. It is also called 'black gold'. Historians tell that due to black pepper, the Portuguese explorer Vasco-da-Gama reached India on 20 May 1498. After that the Portuguese not only increased business here, but also expanded their business empire to the South-East Asian countries.
author: Vandita Sharma

title: new direction
text: Poonam was coming to school everyday after much persuasion. The matter was such that the village school was only up to the seventh standard. To study further, children had to go to school by traveling a distance of 15 kilometers by bus, but traveling was not allowed. That's why she was sad. Despite being top in studies, the matter of not going to school next year was haunting him. 26 January came. This time all the children were stunned to see the chief guest in his school. His guest was the first woman sarpanch of the village. The flag was hoisted by the hand of the sarpanch. The girls felt proud seeing the flag hoisting by a woman. With his speech, he won the hearts of all the children. Suman was most happy because the sarpanch madam had announced to start further classes in the village itself. That too from next year. Now no one had to go far and there was no fear of missing anyone's school. On the second day Poonam was ready even before Suman's arrival. Now his dreams were flying high in the sky with the tricolor.
author: Vandita Sharma

title: ek kisaan kee yashogaatha
text: Gujarat is one such farmer. This is from 2004. Dhirajlal sowed the seeds of groundnut of 'Gji20' caste in his field. Groundnut is the main crop of his region. That year the groundnut crop got diseased and Dheerajlal's entire crop was ruined. But like other farmers, Dhirajlal did not give up. He carefully inspected the entire crop and found that there were some plants which were not affected by the disease. He understood that the survival of those plants meant that they had the ability to fight disease. Dheerajlal now sowed the seeds from good plants in the next season. As a result, this time the number of disease-fighting plants had increased. Thus Dhirajlal carried out this experiment for three years and finally succeeded in obtaining disease-resistant seeds on a large scale. Dheeraj Lal distributed some samples of that seed among the farmers of Amreli, Rajkot and Bhavnagar districts of Saurashtra. He got good response from these farmers. The seed of Dheerajlal is now known as 'Dheeraj 101'. From this seed the crop is ready in 95 to 105 days and each plant produces about 30 to 40 pods. This variety of groundnut, which is resistant to diseases like mildew, tampera and gives high yield, is a symbol of Dheerajlal's endurance.
author: Vandita Sharma

title: Swapnil learns Swirl painting
text: Swapnil was a fourth grader who had a great sense of colours and exceptional painting skills. Needless to say his favourite pastime was painting and colouring. However, he was a daydreamer and would often miss out on the instructions given by his parents and teachers. His mother would repeatedly tell Swapnil to remain vigilant and to observe his surroundings keenly. Swapnil rarely paid any heed to what his mother said. One fine day during the art class Ms. Kalavati was explaining the students about "Swirl painting". She poured the bottles of red, purple, green and indigo oil paints in a small tub filled with water. The paints formed a curly swirly pattern on the surface of water. She then gently laid a plain sheet of paper on the water surface. The paper remained afloat for a couple of minutes before Ms. Kalavati picked it and put it up for display. As soon as she held the paper up, all the students were awestruck. The curly-swirly pattern of the oil paints had now gotten imprinted on the sheet of paper. All the students in the class now wanted to try "Swirl painting" except Swapnil. Swapnil was again lost in his own thoughts and had barely heard to what Ms. Kalavati had told them. When the class got over he packed his bag and got ready to leave. On his way out he saw all his classmates were holding at least one sheet of "Swirl painting" in their hands. He now, felt a little bad for not having a fancy piece of artwork to take back home. "I will make a swirl painting as soon as I get home", he said to himself. He again began daydreaming about how he would make all his friends jealous with his stunning artwork. He took one good look at the materials Ms. Kalavati had used - paper, tub filled with water and colours. However, these colours were not crayons rather they were in liquid form and came in bottles. He had never used liquid colours before however, his dada was in eighth grade and used colours that came in bottles. Swapnil hurriedly went home. At home, he immediately gathered all the materials and poured the colours in water. The colours dissolved and got mixed with the water and when he dipped his paper in it, the paper ended up having dull monochromatic shades. He tried it once again but his efforts did not bear any fruit. Now, disappointed Swapnil wondered where did he go wrong? He blamed the colours for being of poor quality however, deep inside he knew that was not the case. Next day, Swapnil went straight to Ms. Kalavati. He showed her his "artwork" and stood there with his head hung low. Ms. Kalavati immediately recognized where Swapnil had gone wrong. She quickly fetched for her entire collection of bottled colours and instructed Swapnil to pour them in a tub filled with water. As Swapnil poured the colours one by one he observed that some colours mixed with the water while others formed a layer of swirly-curly pattern on the surface of the w ater. Ms. Kalavti asked Swapnil to gently lay a sheet of paper on surface of the water. When Swapnil picked up the paper from surface of the water this time, the shiny curly swirls of the oil paints had gotten imprinted on his sheet of paper. Swapnil was overjoyed. Then with a bright smile Ms. Kalavati said to Swapnil," Swapnil, the colours that you used yesterday were "poster colours" which mix with the water easily however, the colours that I used were "oil paints" and they do not mix with the water. Swapnil realized that his past failure was a result of his daydreaming and decided to remain vigilant always from that day forward. That evening after school a vigilant yet happy Swapnil took a fancy artwork home and proudly displayed it to his family members. Why do poster colours mix with the water while oil paint does not? Poster colours have a base made up of gum arabic that mixes well with the water and hence are considered to be miscible in water while, oil paints have a base made up of linseed oil that does not mix with the water and is therefore, considered to be immiscible in water.

title: The Chemistry Of Lemonade
text: One afternoon, Maitri, and her friends were playing an kh-micholi under the Peepal tree. It was a hot summer afternoon and the kids had already be gan to feel thirsty. Raju kaka’s chai shop was just next to the Peepal tree and he often used to leave a jug full of lemonade for the kids. However, today it seemed like he had forgotten all about it. Therefore, Maitri and her friends decided to ask kaka to make some for them. When they got there they realized Raju kaka was very busy serving the customers. He saw the kids and said, "Sorry kids, I have been very busy all day and could not make lemonade for you. But, I have all the ingredients why don't you make some for yourself? The recipe is written on the board." All th e kids hurriedly took the ingredients and gathered around the board. The board read - Add sugar, salt and lime juice to a jug full of water. Then, add some chaat masala, ground black pepper and ground cumin to it. Stir well and ensure that all the sugar and salt has got combined with the water. Garnish with mint leaves and serve. Maitri asked, "Why aren't we needed to wait until the chaat masala, ground black pepper and ground cumin combine with the water as well?" Athrv answered, "Because, sugar, salt and lime juice are SOLUBLE in water while, chaat masala, ground black pepper and ground cumin are INSOLUBLE in water." Maitri asked again, " How can one tell whether the ingredient is soluble or insoluble?" Athrv said, "Maitri, SOLUBLE ingredients like salt, sugar lime juice dissolve in water without leaving any undissolved particles behind while INSOLUBLE ingredients like ground black pepper and ground cumin do not dissolve and leave behind a lot of particles." Other kids and Raju kaka joined the conversation, too. Ishmeet questioned, "Friends, do you know what do we call a lemonade made up of sugar, salt, lime juice, water, chaat masala, ground pepper and ground cumin?" Amairah blurted,"A MIXTURE, because, not all the ingredients are soluble. But, do you know what do you call a lemonade made with only sugar, salt, lime juice, and water?" "A SOLUTION ", Jake answered confidently. He continued, "The sugar, salt, and lime juice are the SOLUTES because, they dissolve completely and are present in smaller quantities in the lemonade and the water is a SOLVENT because, it is present in a larger quantity and solutes dissolve in it. Rannvijay intervened and shouted loudly," SOLUTES + SOLVENT = SOLUTION ". Maitri repeated the same in her mind. She was amazed by 'the chemistry of lemonade'. By now, Amairah was stirring the lemonade and it was almost ready for serving. Raju kaka, too, had just got the fresh batch of pakoras out of the rolling-boiling oil in his kadai. While arranging the pakoras in the plate he asked Maitri,"What happens when I add mint leaves to a lemonade made only with sugar, salt, lime juice and water?" Maitri started recalling the entire conversation again. Do you think you can help Maitri answer the question?

title: Famine
text: Our Masterji has said that three-fourths of the earth is covered with water. Then how did we get famine here? Why don't we bring that water?" Hey! That's sea water! Such water is not used in famines.” Saying this, father went out for his work. Pintu's enthusiasm had increased immensely. He went to his grandfather and asked the same question again. Grandfather started telling Pintu about the famine. He said, “Sea water is salty. Its water is not used for drinking or for agriculture. That water becomes steam. Steam rises. Clouds are formed from the steam and then it rains when the steam cools.” He added, “Where there is little rain, there is famine.” The question came to Pintu's mind, “If we always have less rain here, will there always be a famine here?” Then Grandfather said, "Hey! Famine can be overcome. There are many solutions for this. Water should be used sparingly. It is important to stop every drop of rain water and seep into the ground. Trees should be planted in order to get more rain. Our old ponds are no longer of use. They need to be cleared and water from where there is good rainfall should be taken through canals to the famine-prone areas.” Pintu said, “Ji Dadaji, now I understand the matter” and he ran out to play. As soon as he reached the courtyard, his feet stopped and then a new question started raising his head.

title: imperial tunnel
text: It was the scorching heat of the skin. The forests, fields, fields and barns had all dried up. No leaves on the trees, no moisture in the ground. There is no pond far and wide, no well, no puddle in which even two drops of water can be seen. In such a situation, a horseman with dry throat and puffy face was wandering here and there for a drop of water. His and his horse's sweat dripped together on the ground and instantly evaporated. His horse was also crying with thirst, but there was not even a trace of water anywhere. Suddenly a woman appeared from afar with a pot on her head. The rider immediately aided the horse. Reaching near, he begged the woman to give him some water to drink. The woman felt pity seeing his face. He took off the pot from his head and the rider went on throwing the water falling in his Anjuli in a hurry. When the water came down the throat, it came to life. When she regained consciousness, she asked the woman, "Why have you come to this deserted forest. Who are you? What do you do?" "I sell milk. There she went behind the mountain to get water,” the woman pointed to a distant mountain. The rider said, "You saved my life. Ask, what do you ask?" The woman chuckled and laughed. Said, "Oh wow! Just now, two drops were clamoring for water. When his throat got wet, it was like becoming a king. Go go east from here. There is a well there, give your horse some water to drink." The rider insisted that he must ask for something. The woman asked to get rid of the chase, "If you want to do something, then do one thing... Rip the chest of this humble mountain and build a tunnel." For water, the women of my village have to climb and descend twice on this rocky mountain.” Saying this she went ahead. The horseman also moved towards the east. The next day the woman passed through that place to get water and saw that many laborers were digging the mountain. The woman asked a worker, "Brother! Why are you digging this mountain?" The worker replied, "The king is safe." The order of the king's safety?" "Yes! He was passing here yesterday. He too was thirsty and his horse too but no water was found anywhere. Good luck to a woman who made them drink water with her pot..." "Well, the horseman himself was safe!" The woman shuddered in her heart. He thought at least the name should be asked. "What is the name of your King Salamat, brother?" The worker stopped his hand for a moment. He looked at her in amazement and said, "Sher Shah Suri... what else?" The worker again started shoveling. That tunnel still exists today and so does its story.
author: Vandita Sharma

title: strange birds
text: It is estimated that there are about 8,000 bird species on the land. By the way, all birds lay eggs and small chicks come out of those eggs. But birds have different and unique ways of incubating eggs. A bird named 'Genette' also incubates eggs by keeping it on its feet. There are also some species of birds that lay their eggs among large piles of leaves, straw and soil. Eggs keep well warm due to the heat of the sun and the humidity of the leaves placed in the pile. The cuckoo's method of hatching eggs is very unique. She lays her eggs in the crow's nest. This is how crows incubate their eggs.
