title: snail and turtle race
text: I run faster than you in tortoise. The tortoise said, I am laughing at your words. The whole forest knows that I run faster than you. If you're not sure, run and see. The snail said, Look turtle, don't talk about pride. I accept your challenge. Who would decide whether to win or lose, for this a creature of the forest had to be chosen. The snail said, it has to be recognized that we walk the slowest in the whole forest. Can't call cheetah or deer to decide our race. Let us call the ant, it also runs like us. The turtle said, don't laugh again and again friend. The ant is no match for me. She crawls just like you. Come on, I'll accept your point. tomorrow is Sunday. Call the ant, the decision must be made. Yes, remember the big field. That small field, according to me, is small. What is yours, you spend the whole day just going round a tree. The snail said, the ant will have to tell that tomorrow it should reach the big field of the forest. The tortoise said, this is where the ant will be. There are only ants in the whole forest. Lo, I took the name and the ant was seen. The snail asked, where is the ant? The tortoise said, you will not see. is very small. Coming down from the hollow of the tree. The snail said, okay brother, only you tell me. The turtle made a sound. Cheetji, where are you now? You don't see The ant said, tortoise brother, this is me. Why are you remembering The tortoise said, you already know the snail, argues a lot. Was saying that he runs faster than me. You tell me, the word running sounds good from his mouth. The ant said, don't say that tortoise brother. Tell me, what are you saying? The tortoise said, he has seen a big field of forest. The ant said, yes I have seen it, it is far away from here. The tortoise said, I do not feel far at all. Tomorrow morning, there will be a race between the snail and me. I have to win, but the snail will be satisfied. The ant said, okay, I will meet you there tomorrow morning. The tortoise said, okay see you tomorrow. Yes, both the snail and the ant, start walking towards the field from now on. I will reach there in a while. The monkeys sitting on the tree listened to the snails and tortoises. The monkeys while talking among themselves said, it will be great fun to see this race. The monkeys told the whole forest in no time that tomorrow morning there is to be a race of snails and tortoises in the big field. The snail and the ant began to walk as soon as it was dark and the tortoise started walking towards the great field after midnight. It was morning, but all three could not reach the ground. A large number of animals gathered around the big field to watch the race. The ant, snail and tortoise could not reach the ground for half a day. Bear explained to everyone, we are all wasting our time waiting for him. I don't think he will be able to reach here. On the other hand, the tired ant said to the snail, I am wasting my time in the affair of both of you. I am going back to my home. The snail said, I can't go away anymore. Anyway, it is afternoon. If you see a tortoise, then tell me to fight again. While returning, the ant found the tortoise. The tortoise said, I am very tired. If you find a snail, then say, this race cannot be done now. Later, if you get time, there will be a competition.

title: The mongoose, the farmer and the farmers wife
text: About the authoress - An inspired poetess and authoress who gains her inspiration for Emily Dickinson. The Mongoose and the farmers wife One day a farmer and his wife were blessed with a son. They decided to get a mongoose as a companion for him. A few months later, the couple had to go out, leaving their son at home. While the wife was worried about leaving the baby alone, the farmer assured her that the mongoose would look after him while they were away. The farmer’s wife returned earlier than her husband and found that the mongoose’s mouth was stained with blood. She immediately accused the animal of killing her child, and in a fit of rage threw a heavy thing at the mongoose (the mongoose died immediately). She then rushed in to check on her son, but what she found was a dead snake lying in the room while her baby was safe and sound. Seeing this, the farmer’s wife realised that the mongoose had actually saved her son’s life. Realising her mistake, she went out to see if the animal was all right, but it was too late and the mongoose had breathed its last. She was absolutely heartbroken and reproached herself for her actions. About India & its folk stories - India is a very diverse and rich country. It is mainly recognised for its spices and cloth. Indian folk tales always conclude with moralistic values. Indian folk tales always have a sense of humour in them. There are many Indian folk tales (Panchatantra, Akbar-Birbal etc)

title: Patience is a Virtue
text: Once there was a clever, patient, hardworking, kind, honest, generous and playful bunny.She was loved by all.Her name was Snowball and no wonder because she was the fluffiest and cuddliest creature in the forest.She used to help everyone in need.Once she even helped a lion!! Even the lion, despite being a carnivore, couldn’t help cuddling her. One day a great storm blew over the jungle.During the storm animals got trampled, trees got uprooted, all the food was taken away because of the storm, the twigs blew away, nests got ruined and homes of animals were destroyed!! A lion and a doe of another forest heard of this and decided to distribute food to the animals.So the lion killed a lot of animals for the carnivores(because they were too scared and worried to hunt)and omnivores, and the doe collected a lot of vegetables and fruits for the herbivores and omnivores. They took the food and went to the forest to distribute the food.They told the animals to line up if they wanted food.The lion and the doe said they would give food every day.All the animals stood in a line and started fighting about who would get food first.Snowball waited patiently for her turn, and finally it came. But all she got was some berries and carrots.The next week on Monday the same thing happened, she only got a pumpkin, but when her mother cut it she found many carrot, pumpkin, cabbage, watermelon and pea seeds!Snowball’s mother asked her to return the seeds. Snowball did as she was told, But when she got there the lion and the doe said together “this is a gift from our side because of your patience!!’Snowball was overjoyed.Her mother helped her plant the seeds, soon the seeds became plants.Voila!! She and her family never went hungry after that day, only because she was patient! ﻿ ﻿ MORAL BE PATIENT

title: Bully Me Not
text: “Fallana Dhimkana, time for dinner” called Amma Hoping seriously that tonight there would be no drama! Supper time the twins often fought, at the dinner table for their favorite spot. Fallana sauntered in with her face in a book, “So Amma what did you cook?” “Some beans and chappatis for both of you.” “Where’s Dhimka? Please chew!” Fallana looked around, Dhimka was nowhere to be found. “Why should I eat the beans alone?”, Fallana said, in a low undertone. Dhimka emerged soon after, ate her dinner as if it tasted of plaster. “Yoooooo Dhiiiiiiiii”, as Fallana joked, “What’s up? You ok, dear?” She turned to Fallana,”Whyyy do I stammerrr? And you don’tttt?, she asked. Dhimkana felt wretched, but said, “Just like how you sketch like an artist, and I don’t”..." So what is this really about?", Fallana quizzed. “Nothingggg. Time forrr beddd”, Dhimkana said. Next morning, Fallana woke up with a start, “Oh dear, did the alarm fall apart”? She nudged her twin, who sat up with a scowl on her chin. “Falli, I am unwell.”, saying so Dhi stayed in bed. “Lucky you, Dhi!, Away to school Fallana fled! Pampered by her mother, Dhi felt comforted She missed her sister, she confessed. Back at home, Fallana ran to see her sister, Her foe, her confidante hipster! “Yo Dhi, How you be? Without you, school was boring dead!”, h ugging Fallana, Dhimkana smirked, “Whhhhaaaat if the older kids chatted instead, a nd not heckled youuuuu upon?”, she said. Fallana asked, “Someone bullying you?” she was aghast! “Why didn’t you say so? Let’s tell Amma, let’s go!” Dhimkana nodded no and heavy tears began to flow. “Thhhhhey were horrible”, she muttered, “Theyyyyyy never bothered me when we are together. Buttttttt that day I was alone, I guess that made them strongerrrrr...."....Theyyyy cornered me after the lunch break bell, I raaaaan so fast, many a time I fell... Theyyyyy guffawed, as I stutttttttered to protest, “Letttttttt me go”, I stressed. I hate my stammerrrr, why am I so?”, Dhi whispered. “Oh Dhi, I love you so much, stammer and all”. She hugged her twin, “Hey we can’t let them win, We need to stand up na”, said a worried Fallana. Tears and later with a warm cuddle, the twain came together in a huddle. Next day, off they went to school, determined to keep the bullies at bay! The plan was simple enough, Dhimka had to call their bluff. If they caught her alone, she was to stand up on her own. If the bullying continued unabated, confide in Miss Ramola, they decided. The first two periods were long agony, when would the clock set them free? Soon the lunch bell rang, Dhimkana’s heart went bang-bang. Fallana was nowhere to be seen, what could this mean? She could hear them near, even her sweat smelt of fear. In the empty classroom, Dhimkana stood, being scared, it’s no good, with a prayer in her heart, she knew it was time to be smart. The bullies four, they all seemed a blur, swiftly they moved towards her. Said, Bully number one, “We are here for just some fun!" “Llllllllleave me alone”, Dhimkana courageously uttered. It was four against one, either she won or would be done! She made a choice, and found her voice! As the Bullies 4 came closer, she looked over their shoulder, t here stood her twin, with a huge grin, Standing with her, was Miss Romola, their class teacher! The Bullies 4 turned with a whirr, “What is going on here?" “We were discussing the Math test, that’s all Miss, they were asking about this!” The Bullies 4 furiously did nod, “Hmmm…run along”, Miss Romola said As the twins walked on ahead, the Bullies 4 called out, “Hey wait up Dhimkana! Thanks for not ratting us out!” Fallana and Dhimkana smiled till their lips felt sore. “As long as you promise, not to bully anyone, anymore!” “We promise!”, said the Bullies 4. Fallana tugged her sister, “You Ok?" Dhimakana said, “Yeeees! Thanks for showing me thhhhe wayyyyy!”

title: And what about this Summer?
text: Mani, a small boy who always goes to his Granny's house during his summer holidays. Whenever he returns he would carry something with him, like, Granny's hand-knitted sweaters, Granny's photos, Granny's pen, etc. Let us see what would he choose to carry with him this time. His granny reads a lot of books and she collects new books before summer begins because she narrates new stories to his grandson Mani during his visits. He loves to hear stories from his granny that's one of the reasons why he comes here all his summer holidays. One day she thought that who would narrate him a story after she lefts the world. So, she decides to make him read on his own but every time she fails. Always his reaction is "noooo grrraaannnyyyy noooo......". This makes her sad. So, she decides to pretend that she is unwell. This makes him unhappy and he can't able to stay there without hearing stories from his granny. Days pass and finally, Mani realizes his granny's situation and decides to read by himself. So he picks the new books from her collections and he narrates the story to his loveable granny every single day. While hearing the stories from her grandson, she is like 'wohoooo I made it, I made it.' After some days Mani notices that his granny is gradually getting normal, which makes him a delight. Oops! don't tell to Mani that his granny has been pretended, only you and I know that. Eventually, the day comes, his summer holidays ends and he is ready to depart and for this summer he takes his favorite books with him from his granny's bookshelf. "There is no substitute for books in the life of a child" -Mary Ellen Chase

title: Kalu Pillay's Jungle Journey
text: One day Kalu Puppy went somewhere secretly. When he did not return till night, Pinky and Neelu went out to find him with a lantern. On the way, Pinky meets Dinu the Dinosaur and Miku the Rat. He asked them, "Have you seen our Kalu puppy?" They both said, "We haven't seen it." Dinu and Miku also set out to find Kalu. Kalu Puppy reached the forest while walking. There he saw Gillo Squirrel. She was resting sitting in the den of a tree. There was also Meena Bee. Kalu asked Meena Bee, "Where can I find Lalu Owl?" Mina Bee said, "Go straight ahead." A little further in the forest, he saw the Chamchu bat hanging upside down on a tree branch and the colorful chameleon sitting on the trunk of the tree. He asked the Chamchu bat, "Where is Lalu Owl's house?" The bat said, "Go straight ahead." He had gone a little further that Lomu fox, Hariya grasshopper, Chhutki bee and Peelu owl all surrounded him. They started scaring Kalu. But Kalu was not scared. He asked Kalu, "What are you doing in this forest at the moment?" Kalu said, "I am a friend of Lalu Owl and have come to meet him." Hearing this, he let him go. At last Kalu reached near the tree on which Lalu Owl lived. Lalu was shocked to see Kalu coming suddenly and was very happy. Both kept talking for a long time. Then Lalu said to him, "It's been a long night now you should go back. People will be waiting for you at home." Kalu went back towards the house. When he reached back home, the smell of delicious food was coming from far away. Water came in his mouth. Actually mother was cooking food at home. On returning home, he was scolded a little for not informing. Kalu called everyone Sauri. Then after having delicious food prepared by his mother, he lay down and slept comfortably.

title: A Star tree
text: Once upon a time there was a seed in a forest that had just started to grow its first leaves. It was deeply excited to finally meet the world. One day an ant who was building its tunnel stopped by and the seed asked it: -Ant, you know the world up there, tell me what is the most beautiful thing? The excited ant said to the seed: -There are many beautiful things in this world. There are flowers, blackberries and acorns. But the thing I like the most are the stars because they are like small shining diamonds. The excited seed replied: -When I grow I want to be a star tree -Seed, the stars don't hang from trees, they hang in the sky- explained the ant From that day on the seed spent its days imagining excitedly what life would be like if he could be a star. As time went on the seed shot out of the ground and was transformed into a small plant. It waited anxiously for night to fall so that it could meet the stars. When it saw them for the first time its leaves trembled. They are beautiful!- it exclaimed in complete awe. A beetle that was trying to sleep in a bush nearby woke up upon hearing all the noise. -Is everything ok small plant? asked the startled beetle. -I'm sorry, today is the first time that I have seen the stars and now that I have, I know that one day I am going to be such a tall tree that I will be able to caress the stars with my branches. The beetle who was somewhat sceptical explained -The stars are beautiful, they always cheer me up in the dark night. But they live very, very high up in the sky. No matter how high I have flown I have never been near enough to reach them. The beetle's words did not put off the little plant. Every day it tried its hardest to grow and grow. With the help of its roots it searched for the best food and little by little it grew bigger until it transformed into a young tree. One day a bird started to build a nest in the young tree's branches. Whilst it saw the bird build its nest the young tree asked -Bird since you fly higher than the pine trees have you ever met a star? -No, young tree, I have never flown that high but the stars always guide me on my flight at night, they help me not to get lost. - with every new thing that he was learning about the stars the young tree was more keen than ever to meet them. The months passed and although the young tree tried its hardest to grow it could no longer grow any taller. It stretched out its branches and moved its roots but it could not manage to grow more. One day something surprising happened. From its branches apples started to grow. They were shiny red. In all of the forest the animals stopped by to see these beautiful apples. The rabbit and the caterpillar said that they were the most delicious apples they had eaten. But the young tree who had just found out that it was an apple tree, wasn't happy about the surprise news. It wanted to be a really tall tree so that it could meet the stars. But to the surprise of everyone in the forest it was an apple tree. The only apple tree in the whole forest, the shortest tree in the whole forest. Travellers who passed through the forest notices the beautiful red glossiness of the apples and its delicious taste and they started to have little breaks under the apple tree's branches. Even still the apple tree looked up at the sky every night and filled with despair it looked up at the stars. One night the ant, worried to see his friend the apple tree looking so sad, said to it: - Dear apple tree, don't be sad. Your apples are a wonderful gift. They are the shiniest red I have ever seen and their taste fills everyone who eats them with delight. All of the forest animals love you and take care of you. You even help humans to not lose their way through the forest and you give them a comfortable place to rest. Upon hearing the ants words the apple tree felt happier. Although it was disappointed that it could not be taller and meet the stars it decided to work its hardest to make the most delicious and beautiful apples possible. One day a traveller and his daughter sat down to rest under the shadow of the apple tree. After eating with her father, the girl started to climb the tree's branches. Whilst she played amongst the branches, she collected apples for the rest of her journey. Soon an apple fell from the tree and broke in half. The girl quickly descended the tree to see the apple that had fallen. Surprised she ran to show her father what she had found inside the apple. - Father, look a star, the apple has a star inside it! The apple tree that was listening carefully could not believe what it was hearing or seeing. All its life it had tried so hard to meet the stars without realising that inside its beautiful apples there were stars. Shining stars, stars that made travellers happy and guided them on their journey. In the end the apple tree had managed to be a star tree. Claire Smith June 2021

title: My Sweet  Totu
text: In a town called 'Pandavapura', there was a little girl by the name 'Sumitra'. She was a very lively and bubbly child. She used to get up early in the morning everyday and go for a walk in the fields and river side. She loved seeing the birds, rising sun, farmers going to the field and women near the river. She loved birds and tried to speak to them. One day Sumitra went to the town market with her father. She saw lots of people in the market selling fruits, vegetables and other things. But her eyes went to a corner where she saw a person selling parrot. She was thrilled. She wanted to immediately take it home. She convinced her father and brought it home. She called him Totu. Totu enjoyed Sumitra's company and played with her. Soon, it became the pet of everyone in the house. Also all her neighbour's loved Totu. Every day she used to wake up at five in the morning, take her parrot with her to see the beautiful morning scene in her town. She used to speak to Totu about everything she saw and felt. Everyday she used to teach Totu, 'Sumitra wake up', 'Sumitra wake up'. So, one day to her surprise before her mother came to wake her up, Totu started shouting 'Sumitra wake up', 'Sumitra wake up' till she opened her eyes. Sumitra hearing Totu's voice was thrilled and jumped from her bed in great happiness. She ran across her house with full joy and exclaimed 'Totu' is my voice assistant. It understands what I speak and replies to me. Everyone in her family were thrilled and surprised. All her neighbors across came to her house to see how Totu could be her voice assistant. She showed them how Totu could respond to her and give reply appropriately. When she said "Totu, is father at home', It would say 'Yes, Yes'. When asked 'Totu, Is grandma sleeping', It would reply 'No, No'. "Wake me Totu". It said "Sumitra Wake up". So, in this way Totu was Sumitra's Voice assistant. It understood whatever she told and replied back correctly. It learnt many new words from her over a period of time. So, in the same way a Voice Assistant is equipped with speech recognition and Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies of Artificial Intelligence to understand what we speak, reply back with an answer, learn new things over a period of time. It converts our speech to digital data, uses NLP algorithms to process the speech, search for an appropriate answer from its memory and gives back the reply. That's the power of NLP in AI.

illustrator: Niloufer Wadia; Samidha Gunjal; Sanjay Sarkar; Shailja Jain Chougule; Sonal Goyal; Soumya Menon; Sumit Sakhuja

title: The Ice-cream Lover
text: Cheeku looovvvvvved to eat ice cream. She could have ice cream everyday - for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Cheeku’s mumma was worried about her health. So, they decided that every Sunday would be her Ice cream day. It was easy to not think about ice cream on Monday and Tuesday. But then, Cheeku couldn’t wait for Sunday to come. She waited and waited and waited, and, finally Sunday came!! Cheeku was the happiest!! Cheeku opened the freezer in the evening to bring out her favorite chocolate ice-cream. She had seen it there two days ago and was really looking forward to eating it. But to Cheeku’s utter shock, her favourite ice cream had disappeared from the freezer. She was confused…. and disappointed. Who ate her favorite chocolate ice-cream on a non-ice cream day?? Cheeku’s mumma said, “I can go and bring it for you…” But, Cheeku didn’t want her mother to go and leave her at home. There were other ice-cream flavours in there and she decided she would eat a Cornetto ice-cream. She peeled the paper off the ice-cream and started licking it… little by little… Suddenly, her cone broke! Cheeku hated to eat broken cone and ice-cream. Cheeku knew that her ice-cream would leak without the cone...So, she had to finish her ice-cream quickly. Unfortunately, her mother had a work meeting to attend at the same time. Tears started to roll down Cheeku’s cheeks. She couldn’t eat her favourite ice-cream, then the cone broke and now her mumma had a work meeting to attend! She cried and said "Mumma, don't go to your meeting". Her mumma said… “Oh Dear… I understand that this is so hard for you. It wasn’t fair that someone had eaten your favourite ice-cream flavour… and that your cone broke!...” Cheeku started crying even louder. Her mumma was showing her that she understood how Cheeku must be feeling…. After crying for sometime, Cheeku was still upset. Cheeku threw all the pillows and the bedsheets off the bed. Her mumma said, “It really must have been so upsetting!” Cheeku then lay on the floor herself and said "I should have asked you go to the shop Mumma…” “Oh sweety. It’s not your fault. Sometimes it is confusing for us on what we should do!” said mumma. Cheeku said she didn’t want to trouble her mumma. Her mumma thanked Cheeku for thinking about her and sat next to Cheeku and let her cry. Cheeku's mother sat down and helped Cheeku make a feelings journal with few pictures and that is what you are reading right now.:)
author: Parenting Matters

title: Fair and Unfair
text: Siddharth was a young boy. His day began by reading the newspaper. He would start from the back of the paper—the sports section. Siddharth loved watching the Indian Premier League (IPL) and Andre Russell was his favourite player. Siddharth was excited to see Andre Russell in the news. He had hit most sixes and won the match for his team— Kolkata Knight Riders. And suddenly.....he was sad. He read that a black person George was killed by a white person. Looking at his garden and enjoying the chirping of birds, bees sucking the nectar from flowers and butterfly sitting on the plants Siddharth thought: “The Earth has so many living beings, such as plants, animals and human beings." While the plants, insects, birds, animals, etc. live in absolute harmony without looking at each others’ colours. I t’s the humans who look at their fellow humans as “ Fair ” (White) and “ Unfair ” (Black). Siddharth wondered, “Why humans created this Fair and Unfair discrimination? What’s Unfair’s fault for not being Fair? Why should Unfair not be treated fairly?” Siddharth was musing on the issue of discrimination. “From the days of Gandhi travelling in steam trains, to my age of high-speed trains, humans have made great progress in technology and their ways of living. But discrimination still continues—from Gandhi to me.” Siddharth’s favourite colour was black. He did not see humans as Fair or Unfair. But the sad news pained him and he recollected his own incident. Siddharth had never travelled by bus beyond 6-hours, and was looking forward to the 17-hour long bus journey from New Delhi to Manali. During the travel, he made friends in the bus. Language was no barrier for him. He could not speak Hindi, so conversed in English. He spoke to the two boys sitting behind their seat. On exchanging their names, the boys asked Siddharth, "Are you from the South?" Siddharth being too young didn’t understand what South meant. So he asked his mother innocently, “Mother the boys sitting at the back are asking if I am from the South, what does it mean?” After his mother’s explanation, Siddharth got back to them and told proudly, "I have come from Bangalore, which is in the South." Further, the boys told, “Well, people in the southern part of India are ‘ Black ’.” Just before Siddharth’s trip to Manali, his mother had finished narrating a story about Gandhi. He was reminded of him, and shot back at the boys saying, “There is nothing known as ‘Black ’ or ‘ White ’, we are all equal.” After this conversation, Siddharth sat back and narrated about it to his mother. She said, “Siddharth, you are right, we are all equal. There is nothing known as ‘ Black ’ or ‘ White ’.” Siddharth pondered, "While a Fair conductor threw Gandhi out of the train in South Africa for being Unfair, why Indians themselves are terming each other as ' White' or ' Black'!" Until then, Siddharth never knew that just like the British, an Indian too would look at his fellow Indian as " White " or " Black ". The discrimination in his own country made him very unhappy. To Siddharth, humans were colourful with unique interests, talents and identity. He regarded both Fair and Unfair as sensitive people, who longed to be loved and hugged including Siddharth. So Siddharth started praying for Fair and Unfair to live in absolute harmony.
author: Siddharth Shivani Venugopal
illustrator: Namitaa Pradeep; Pradyumna Ravi; Sheetal Shetty

title: Amaze-Shamaze Salt
text: She tore a piece of chapati and began to chew it. 'Oh ho! It has no salt. I cannot eat it. Maybe Ma forgot to add salt while making breakfast quickly." Saying this, Meera shut her tiffin box and went out to play. Meera shut her tiffin box. What would you have done if you were in her place? Would you have shut your tiffin box too or would you have eaten the bland food? Salt is indeed such an ingredient that makes our food tasty and healthy too. However, too much salt in a dish can make it taste bad. You might already know that the intake of salt is important for human beings, animals and plants. This is because our bodies cannot make salt on their own. If we do not eat salt, our bodies' chemical equilibrium along with the working of our nervous system and muscles can get severely affected which may even lead to death. This is why we must consume salt in the food that we eat. The sweat that our bodies produce when we are under the hot sun, the blood in our bodies and the tears that stream out of our eyes, are all salty. Do you know why? This is because salt is involved in all the major processes of our body. Specialists believe that in order to stay healthy an individual must consume a maximum of 6 gms of salt per day. You must be wondering, where does salt come from? Salt is one of the useful minerals found on Earth, which is available all around us in the seas and in underground ancient dries seas. But seas and oceans remain the biggest source of salt. A kilometre of deep-sea or ocean water can give us up to 260 lakh tons of salt. Salts are of many types. We obtain white salt through evaporation and what we call black salt or sendha namak, is obtained from underground dried seas. China is the largest producer of salt. There are stories about Salt in the pages of History that never fail to amaze us. In ancient times, Roman soldiers used to be paid by salt. At the same time, salt was buried with the dead and also used to preserve food. Even to this day, many food items are preserved using salt. Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March was about salt too. These were some of the events in History that are about salt but salt plays an important role in our daily rituals and customs. Do you know that in ancient times, salt used to be sprinkled over the stage before a play? This was done so that it could be protected from the evil eye. Have you heard of a ritual or custom which involves salt? What do you think about such rituals and customs?
author: Sanjana Rajamohan

title: Ramu's Dream
text: It was the year of 1985. Ramu was an young boy of 6 years old. He lived in a small town which was very far from a city. He had never been to a city. He always used to ask his father to take him to the city as his masterji from school had told him that a city has many interesting things like vehicles, big houses, cinema theatres, street lights and many more. By listening to all these he was fascinated to see the city by his own eyes. One day, in the school, masterji came late to the school. Ramu was eager to know what happened because he liked masterji very much. Masterji told them that he had been to the city, so he started narrating all the new experiences he had in the city. He told them about new gadgets and many more things. Masterji told the children that in the next class each one of them will tell about their dream city which they will see after 20 years. Ramu came home excited and started thinking about the city of future. Soon he fell asleep and started dreaming about it. In his dream he was sitting in a vehicle which was driving by itself. It took him to a his office where he had automatic door opening system which greeted him by his name. It said 'Good morning Ramu. Have a great day". After his office when he came home, the food was hot and the lights of his room were on and the room temperature was perfect to the weather. His mother was telling a machine to clean the dishes and dust the floors. His father was watching his favorite TV program. His sister was looking at a screen and talking with her friends. His door bell rang and it said, 'Ramu wake up, Ramu wake up, Sham is here to play with you'. Suddenly he jumped from his bed to play with Shamu. "Oh! oops, it was a dream" he exclaimed. He felt very nice about the city in his dream but was not sure whether his masterji would like it. In school, the next day, Ramu was the first one to be called to tell about his dream city. When he narrated about the concept, all the children laughed at him. But masterji was amazed at the imagination of the small boy. He said "Ramu, your very creative and way ahead of your times. Your dream will soon become a reality in the coming days. Study well and develop whatever you have dreamt of". Ramu was thrilled. He never knew that his idea was something phenomenal. He worked hard throughout his school and college days and became a Computer Engineer. He joined a big tech company and was part of many new technological developments like Smart Home, Smart City, Smart gadgets etc. Such amazing dreams by youngsters has paved way for new technological advancements which we now call it has Artificial Intelligence. AI provides us many applications which can be used in any field and to make our lives better, smarter and sustainable. So, children Dreams can become True. Technological Advancements can be used for the betterment of the society that we live in. Let's use the technology as a boon not as a bane.
author: Smitha R Athreya
illustrator: Bindia  Thapar; Jit  Chowdhury; Joanna  Mendes; Ram Kol; Sulagna  Roy; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Golden Light Ball
text: Rohan was a little boy living happily with his mom, dad and a pet dog Jules. He awoke one morning to hear his mother say “It’s Lock down again”! Oh No! thought Rohan; he had just restarted school a short while ago after a looong lockdown. He could not understand any of this. He always wore his mask and listened to his mom and dad. Then why a lockdown again? Rohan was a little boy living happily with his mom, dad and a pet dog Jules. He awoke one morning to hear his mother say “It’s Lock down again”! Oh No! thought Rohan; he had just restarted school a short while ago after a looong lockdown. He could not understand any of this. He always wore his mask and listened to his mom and dad. Then why a lockdown again? He was feeling shocked, sad and angry all at the same time. He looked at his mama’s face. Her lips were in the shape of an arch and closed tight. He turned around to look at his papa. A spectacle on the nose, with his eyebrows raised up he sat peering into his laptop. Rohan turned to look at the dog; Jules, sat with his belly on the floor and his nose flat on the ground. “no more long walks for you Jules” said Rohan feeling sad for him too! He was feeling shocked, sad and angry all at the same time. He looked at his mama’s face. Her lips were in the shape of an arch and closed tight. He turned around to look at his papa. A spectacle on the nose, with his eyebrows raised up he sat peering into his laptop. Rohan turned to look at the dog; Jules, sat with his belly on the floor and his nose flat on the ground. “no more long walks for you Jules” said Rohan feeling sad for him too! He slowly, walked towards his toys, took his wooden blocks and sat at the windowsill. Warm Sunshine was streaming in. “At least no lock down there” said Rohan aloud. He soaked in the warm golden light; the rays were hitting the windowpane kissing his cheeks. He felt warm right through his body. Rohan climbed on to the windowsill playing with the sun’s rays. He moved the curtain and it played “peek a boo” with him. The colours of the rays when it hit the pane, changed from golden yellow to orange then to pink. The silver button in his pajamas shone bright like a diamond. Rohan closed his eyes and let the sunshine stream into him, like water from the shower. He crossed his arms across his chest and hugged himself. The golden sunshine became a golden ball of warm light around him. He felt so good, happy, joyful. He saw himself rolling around inside this golden ball. Thank you, sunshine! He so wanted to share this golden light with everyone. He jumped down from the windowpane his arms still crossed over his shoulders. He hopped and skipped over to his mom and hugged her; wrapped his arms around her waist and said “take my golden light my Mother". His mother’s face lit up like a million suns! He ran next to his father. His dad picked him up in his arms ‘come into my golden light ball dad’ Rohan whispered in his ears as he hugged him tight. His father’s eyes shone like a bright sun. Jules jumped up balancing on two feet and his mother joined in for a group hug and all of them fit into Rohan’s golden light ball. They all felt so much better inside this golden ball, warm safe and secure. Every morning Rohan would play at the windowsill with the sun and his golden light ball grew bigger and bigger. He could now invite his grandparents, all his friends and all those whom he loved. The golden light ball touched everyone and made them joyful, happy and bright like the Glorious sun. Rohan always carried his invisible golden light ball around him spreading warmth and happiness. Rohan realized that it could be a long while before he could meet his friends. His mother let him speak to them over the phone sometimes. Rohan soon told all his friends about playing Peek a Boo with the sun. He told them about his secret golden light ball. They all wanted to be in his Golden ball too. So, every morning Rohan would invite one of his friends into his Golden ball. Oh, that was fun! They held each other’s hands and tried to move around in the Golden ball. It was not easy, for they would easily fall and the roll around like the little piglets in the haystack. That was fun too! Every morning he invited one of his friends to play with him inside the Golden ball. After a while the sun and the golden ball would move away, and Rohan then carried on playing with his other toys in the room. Some days Rohan spent time with his mother putting up pictures of all his friends on the walls of his room. Every Monday they would change these pictures, so Rohan felt as if he had met all of them. Soon he had invited all his friends from school, his friends from the building, his cousins and all the children he met into his warm Golden ball. It took him a long time but when he was done, the golden warm light had spread to everyone and to every house and to every little child. The days passed quickly the summer sun was now hiding behind the clouds. Sister Rain came down, but the children and the people were still filled with warmth, joy and happiness because of Rohan’s Golden light ball. They all now waited with excitement; eagerly looking outside for the Rainbow in the sky. That too shall come said Rohan, looking at the window sill.
author: Latha  Madhu

title: Hedgy The Hedehog
text: One day a hedgehog was sleeping in a park near the tree. His name was Hedgy. He woke up and wanted to cross the road. When he was crossing, he heard a car coming towards him. He quickly rolled over like a ball to the other side of the road. When he crossed the road, he saw a woodcutter was cutting a tree. Hedgy saw that the tree was going to fall on him. So he quickly rolled and saved himself. When he looked around, there were many trees chopped. It was a forest. He found a perfect tree to make his home. He dug a hole near the tree and lived there. Then a squirrel came to Hedgy. He knocked at his door and said " I am Squiz " Hedgy was happy, and they became good friends. They both then lived in the same house.
author: Manav K M

title: As you sow, so shall you reap
text: Rohit was the only child of Mr and Mrs Sharma. They lived in a big city. From childhood Rohit was an obedient child. He used to follow whatever his parents told him They always used to tell him "Make friends with others if they have good handwriting only". "People who have clean homes are good people". "Talk to those who are good at studies". "Girls are weak" and many more such thoughts. All these prejudices were sowed to him at a very early age. Unknowingly he imbibed these qualities within him and made him quite choosy about the people whom he mingled. Suddenly one day his father got transferred to another city. Rohit got admission in a new school In the new school, Rohit was welcomed by the teacher and the students but he found it very difficult to make new friends due to his mind block. His new classmates tried a lot to make friends with him, but they failed because of his strange behavior. Suddenly he used to ask, "Show me your handwriting". When he went to their place, instead of playing he was seeing whether their house was clean. He used ask "What is your rank" and many such weird questions. Because of his strange behavior he could not make any friends. Rohit became sad and unhappy as time passed. He could not understand what was happening to him. One day, his mama came home to see them. He saw that Ramu had become quite shy and lonely. When he discussed with him and his parents he understood the problem. Mama told Rohit's parents about the kind of prejudices that they had put in his mind which has made him biased. He was trained in this way from childhood which is causing all the problem. He told his parents "If you sow biased thoughts of yours to your child, he will also grow up with biased opinions". "As you sow, so shall you reap". So, in the same way if we develop smart systems with our own biases, it will get trained in the same way and will give us biased results. The examples of Amazon recruitment system or the famous Pro Publica Judiciary biased system of USA are all examples of bias in AI. It discriminated people based on gender and race respectively. This can also be termed as "Garbage In Garbage Out" in AI. As responsible citizens of this country let us not try to feed in the bias that exists with us or in the society to the AI systems that we are going to develop. Let's all learn the AI Ethics and make the AI systems not only smart but also sustainable to our human race.
author: Smitha R Athreya

title: Aiman's School Bag
text: Agus Saputra Aiman is a little girl. I'm her schoolbag. I'm also her friend. Aiman gets up early and gets ready for school. I'm watching her from the corner of the room. I'm excited because Aiman will invite me to her school. Every morning, Aiman carried me on her back. When she walks quickly, my heart beats quickly as well. I leaned on her back until we reached the road. I sat comfortably on her lap inside the bus. Aiman loves me so much. On my way to school, I met with another schoolbag. We spoke, sang until we finally arrived at school. Without hesitation, we jumped and running with our personal owner. Aiman keeps a lot of things in my stomach, such colorful books, notebooks, eraser, pencils, and his lunch box. Hmm... this delicious smell must be comes from her lunch box. Those things collided inside my stomach. Aiman jumped up while I'm still fastened to her back. She was running here and there. I'm always by her side. Aiman left me in class during lunch break. I feel lonely, but there are a lot of other bags here. We spoke, laughed, and sang again, but I missed Aiman. Do you know what Aiman did after school? Oops, he stuffed everything into my stomach rapidly! She wanted to go home immediately. As she ran as fast as lightning to catch the bus, I gasped for breath. When Aiman arrived home, she put me in the corner of the room and simply forgot about me. I watch her from a distance. My burden grows as Aiman advances her class. She began to have difficulty carrying me on her back. Is there anything we can do to decrease our burden?
author: Anjas Wahyu Agus Saputra

title: The Lion and the Rabbit
text: Once upon a time, there was a proud, evil lion. He said he was the king of the jungle. Every day, he would mercilessly go hunting and kill many animals for his food. Soon, all the animals were worried. They held a meeting and decided that if the lion continues to do this, then no animal will survive. So, they approached the lion and told him a proposal. Each day, they said, they would send one animal to the lion’s den. This way, the rest of the animals for that day will be at peace, and the lion would not need to go hunting. The lion liked the plan. So from the next day, the lion would wait in his den while the others sent an animal for his meal. This happened for many days. Finally, it was the turn of a very old but wise rabbit. He was forced to be the meal of the day for the lion. He decided to put an end to this. So, he took a longer route and made sure he got to the lion’s den very late. The hungry lion who was angry roared at the rabbit and asked him why he was late. The rabbit then told him that he was late because another stronger lion was chasing him. He told the lion that the stronger lion claimed to be the king of the jungle. When the lion heard this, he was furious. He asked the rabbit to show him where the other lion was. The rabbit took the lion to a well. He pointed inside and told the lion that the other lion was inside. When the lion looked in, he saw his own reflection but thought it was another lion. He roared in anger, and the reflection did the same. Brimming with anger, the lion jumped into the well to fight with the other lion but ended up falling to his death because of his stupidity. The moral of this story is that sometimes, intelligence is more important than physical strength.
author: Shraddha Bhanot

title: The Thirsty Crow
text: Once there was a crow. It was a hot day, and the crow was extremely thirsty. He kept flying around, looking for some water. After a very long time, he finally found a jar of water. With great happiness, he flew to the jar to drink the water. But when he tried to put his head into the jar, he realised it was too narrow. He tried to tilt the put, but it was too heavy. Sad and frustrated, he kept thinking. Finally, he saw pebbles on the ground. He had an idea. One by one, he put the pebbles into the jar. The water level slowly rose, and the crow could drink the water.
author: Shraddha Bhanot

title: Floppy The Bear

title: The Most Important Work Of All
text: We are able to get carbohydrates, proteins and fibre from rotis, dal, vegetables, fruits, milk, curds, fish and meat. It is using this nutrition that our body is able to ensure that all organs function properly. The food we eat makes us fit us to walk, run, read and work in the field, house and office. Do you know that in our society women work the highest number of hours? Commonly in our families, women wake up the earliest and go to sleep the last. If we begin to count the number of tasks they do, we would end up with a very long list. Ensuring there is enough food to eat, cleaning the house, taking care of children and the old, ensuring animals have enough food to eat, are all part of women's daily work. Along with this, they also work outside the house - in fields or the office. You will be shocked to know that in many countries, women get the least amount of food to eat. Women end up eating food that is remaining after everybody has eaten in the house. Why does this happen? Water, air and food belong to all of us. Women work more than anybody else. They require as much energy as the work they do. They are not paid for most tasks that they do, is this why their work is not considered as important? Think about it, if women stopped working entirely, would our families and worlds be able to sustain themselves?
author: Sanjana Rajamohan

title: The greedy heron
text: By a deep forest pond, there lived an aged heron. He was old and his eyesight had dimmed. He could no longer move as fast as he once used to. He could no longer catch fish and other little creatures that lived in the pond. “At this rate, I will starve to death!” After some thought, he came up with a clever plan. He waded into the reeds and rushes that grew by the edge of the pond and stood there sighing deeply, not bothered to catch the fishes that swam up close to him. A crab noticed this strange behaviour and sidled up to him. “Hey Uncle Heron, why are you so sad? Is everything alright?” “Oh, my son,” replied the heron, wiping away a tear. “I sit here waiting for death. Astrologers have read the stars and say that for twelve long years, there will be no rain. This pond, that you and I love so much, will dry up and disappear. All my friends, you and the little fishes that swim so merrily about, will die! So I sigh and weep.” The crab scuttled off and told the other little creatures in the pond what the heron had said. “We are going to die! What shall we do?” They cried in panic and rushed off to the heron and begged him to save them. “What gullible idiots! My plan is working perfectly!” thought the heron with satisfaction. Pretending to wipe off another tear, he said, “Not far from here, there is a lake. It is deeper and bigger than our little pond. Lotuses and lilies float upon it, and it will survive any drought. If you want, I can carry you there, one by one, upon my back.” The little creatures believed the heron and rushed to clamber upon his back. The heron was delighted at the smooth success of his little scheme. “One by one, one by one!” he said, and the fishes, frogs and turtles all queued up, excitedly awaiting their turn. The wicked heron would take the creatures one at a time upon his back and soar up into the sky. Once out of sight, he would alight on a large and lonely rock, and there, make a leisurely meal for his passenger. In this way, he made sure of a steady supply of food for himself. He no longer had to fish or make any effort at all as the water creatures kept lining up every day to be taken to the wonderful lake. Only the crab was unhappy. “Uncle,” he said, “Why have you left me out? You have flown so many fishes out, but I am still here in this pond, waiting for death. Please take me to our new home!”. "oh! sorry I forget you come on my back and I will take you to the new home!". In the middle of the journey, the crab asked "uncle how much time it will take to reach the home?"."you are such a nincompoop! I am not going to take you to the home I am going to eat you!" When the heron said this the crab became angry and bitted the heron's neck! and he asked uncle heron to take him to the pond immediately then they both flew back to the land and the heron died there the other fishes that were in the line came to know that the heron wanted to eat them. After that the fishes did not buried him they left the body there and lived happily ever after! MESSAGE FROM THE AUTHOR- Hello, I am prisha pandey I study in class 5-h in the Khaitan school.
