title: Vehicles for Transport
text: A car is a four-wheeled vehicle that runs on the road. The modern car was invented in 1886 by Karl Benz when he introduced the Benz cars. A small car can carry 3 passengers apart from the driver. Homes and offices have separate parking spaces to park the car. The price of cars ranges from 2 lakhs to 10 crores based on the make and the model. Google has introduced self-driving cars that operate without a driver. A bus is a four-wheeler public transport. The bus got its name from the Latin word Omnibus. About 50 people can sit in a bus including the driver and the conductor. The conductor takes care of giving tickets and blowing the whistle at the bus stops. Most of the schools in India have a school bus. In India, the buses are commonly single-decker or have only one floor. Abroad, you can find many double-decker buses. Trains run on railway tracks. A train is made up of many connected coaches. The passenger trains have 24 to 26 coaches. Trains that run within a city have only seats. Trains that run across districts have both seats and berths or beds. This helps people who travel overnight to sleep. Goods train has 58 wagons. High-speed rails are very fast trains known as bullet trains. A cycle or bicycle is a two-wheeler. There are two pedals for the humans to rotate with their legs and move the cycle forward. The cycle chains are used to transfer power from the pedals to the wheels of the cycle. Bicycles are safe for the environment as they do not emit any smoke. Postmen, milkmen, and newspaper distributing guys use the bicycle to travel easily on the streets. The bicycle tyre is pumped regularly with Nitrogen gas to function properly. Auto Rickshaws are three-wheelers and can carry 2 to 3 passengers at a time. Autos start a meter that runs from pickup to drop point. The meter shows the final amount to be paid at the drop point. Nowadays, modern auto drivers provide free Wi-Fi connection, a mobile charging point, TV, and a tablet PC inside their autos. They also provide newspapers and magazines to read. A scooter is a two-wheeler that runs on roads. There is one seat for the rider and one seat for the passenger behind the rider. There is a platform for the rider to rest the feet. People who ride on a scooter wear helmets to protect their heads during accidents. Old model scooters had a kick start. Nowadays, you can start a scooter by pressing a button. An aeroplane, airplane, or plane carries passengers in the air. An aeroplane has two big wings on the sides. The pilot sits in the cockpit in the front. The other end of the plane has a rudder. The Wright brothers, Orville and Wilbur, invented and flew the aeroplane in 1903. Aeroplane usually has business class and economy class. Business-class seats have more facilities than economy class. A boat is used to carry 2 or 3 passengers on a river, coastal area, or lake. One man holds and moves the oar. This helps the boat to move forward in the water. Boats of various sizes are used to show the tourists around in a place. Fishermen use boats to catch fish. Boats can move with wind power or motor power also. Paddleboats use manpower. Sailboats use wind power to move. A truck is a four-wheeler that is used to carry goods and cargo on land. The backside of the truck which carries the things is usually open at the top. The cab is the area in the front where the driver sits. The truck is also known as a lorry. Tractors are used in farming, construction, and mining to pull or push equipment. The word tractor was based on the Latin word “trahere” which means “to pull.” There are two-wheel and four-wheel tractors.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: A Wish
text: Rina and Trisha were good friends. One day, they went to walk in nature. They saw streams, trees, mountains, and flowers. Suddenly, a blue fairy appeared in front of them. The fairy said, “You both look like smart girls. I want to grant you both a single wish. What do you both wish for?” Rina said, “Shall we ask for a big truck full of chocolates?” Trisha said, “I don’t like chocolates that much. Let us ask for 100 new dresses for each of us.” Rina said, “Oh no. I recently bought a lot of dresses. Let us ask for a smartphone.” Trisha said, “My parents do not allow me to use social media. So, a smartphone will not be of much use.” Like this, both of them were fighting and could not decide which wish to ask for. The fairy lost her patience. The fairy said, “Dear girls. You both are not able to decide. So, I will grant you both a wish I like.” Rina and Trisha agreed. The fairy said, ”I grant you both lot of wisdom and intelligence. Material things will destroy and have a short life. But, wisdom is everlasting. It will help you during both good and bad times.” The fairy flew away after granting the wish. Rina and Trisha were happy with the wish granted to them. Eureka!
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: A visit to grandma
text: Manya and Aanya were 2 twins who lived in Mumbai. Manya was a curious girl who had brown curly hair. She loved going on adventures. Aanya too had curly brown hair. She had big eyes and a dab hand at puzzles and quizzes. They were exited as they were going to their grandma's home in Bangalore. Their dad's friend who was going to Bangalore too, suggested that he should take the kids with him. The trip was long but very fun. For lunch they stopped at a dhaba nearby. Manya and Aanya ate parathas,sabzi and a big glass of thick, creamy lassi and were full for the rest of the trip. When they reach Bangalore they looked at the houses with delight. As their dad's friend stopped the car, the kids looked at the house. Grandma's house was a spacious bungalow with a garden in the back. The cement was cracked and they could see the maroon red bricks inside. The porch had a small swing on which grandma was sitting on. She was in her late 70s but was as active as a 10 year old. She had a dusky complexion and her long gray hair was pulled up into a tight bun. The kids quickly ran and hugged grandma. She was overjoyed to see them. The kids changed their clothes and grandma quickly ran to the kitchen to whip up a snack. It was kheer! Aanya and Manya gobbled up the food! The house was big and very spacious. There were huge bedrooms and a decked up kitchen with all the supplies grandma needs to make a feast. For a few days, Manya and Aanya went outside and played with the other kids in the neighborhood. They played hide and seek and went cycling with the bicycles that their grandpa bought for them. Every day they used to collect veggies and fruits from the backyard garden and in return, grandma cooked delicious food. At night they used to go to their grandparent's room. Their room was brightly lit and had a high ceiling! There were a couple of windows and a stuffed bookshelf. They went there to look at old pictures of their parents and to listen to interesting stories told by grandma. Sometimes Manya and Aanya used to prank grandpa by taking the newspaper and hiding it somewhere. These kind of things always kept the house cheery. After a week or so, the kids had already made a huge group. There was Rohit, their neighbor's son, Amit,Reena,Krishna and Harit. They always looked for adventure together. One afternoon, Rohit came rushing in, exited and happy. He was skinny, dark and tall. When Manya asked Rohit what happened, he said "The circus is coming to town! They are going to perform this weekend!" The kids squealed in exitement and begged their grandparents to take them to the circus. After a lot of pleading and begging, grandpa and grandma finally caved in. After dancing for a few minutes grandpa finally spoke "I will only take you all to the circus this weekend if you do extra chores around the house and do no mischief." The kids promised to not get into any sort of trouble throughout the week. The whole group knew about the circus and was exited to go together. Days passed by and the weekends were a few hours away. They waited all day and night. The day of the circus finally came. Rohit,Manya and Aanya were the most exited. Grandpa drove the car to the circus grounds. They saw big red and white tents towering over them. The shining lights and the food mesmerised the kids. Before the show started, grandpa bought them butter popcorn and roasted peanuts. As they settled down in their seats, it started to rain cats and dogs. The spectators all ran outside, rushing towards their cars frantically a nd driving away. All the kids were devastated. They had waited for this circus for a whole week and now there was no way to watch it. As their car reach home the kids got out slowly. For a few days the kids were sad. They did not go out to play a lot and they did not hear any stories too. Grandpa tried to take them to the park every day, but it did not make a difference. The kids stopped helping with chores around the house and sat in their beds all day. Before the circus left, grandpa pleaded them to perform once but the circus master refused as he had to go to another town to perform. The circus trucks drove off and grandpa returned home disappointed and tired. Their sadness increased gradually, day after day. One day grandma decided to make their favourite treats. She worked all day to make coconut barfi, paysam and kheer. But the kids just pushed away the plates and went to their rooms.Grandma and grandpa were really worried for the children. The grandparents were getting tired and the kids were soon getting bored. All they did was sleep and sit. They watched tv with their grandpa, but it only cheered them up for a few hours. Their friends recovered from sadness quickly and even tried to cheer them up. Some days grandma used to take them to the terrace to see the twinkling stars but thoughts about the circus always lingered in Manya's and Aanya's heads. The grandparents were soon getting worried that the kids wouldn't want to visit Bangalore anymore and that their behaviour will reflect on their actions at home. They had to do something before it was too late. The grandparents did everything they could do but nothing worked. Soon they got fed up too. One morning grandma came inside happy. She said that she got a brilliant idea. She decided to make a circus in the empty grounds. Grandpa was exited so he called a meeting and explained the plan. Every week the community met together to discuss plans. Grandpa and Mr. Sumit were the supervisors of the group. The committee members decided to set up everything in the following week. But there was 1 huge proble m. They organised the meetings and looked after everyone. T hey did not have enough money to make this all happen. This news really saddened the community. Just as the project was going to be shut down, an unsuspected help came up. The principal of a big school, who was a great friend of grandpa, agreed to supply the money needed. When grandpa heard of this, he thanked his friend with all his heart. By the time the project was finalised, Grandma had already gathered her team of women to help her cook the food. They each had a special job to do. One cooked the popcorn, one made roasted peanuts and the rest made beverages and snacks. The whole community worked hard and made a huge circus. There were stalls of all kinds, a huge circus tent and a kitchen for preparing food. The circus was finally ready! Everyone was very exited to surprise the children. The next morning, Manya and Aanya woke up to the nudging of Rohit. Sleepily they woke up and quickly got dressed. The house was empty and Grandpa and grandma were nowhere to be found. When they went outside, they saw Rohit's mom calling them to the car. The three of them sat inside and Rohit's mom started driving. When they looked outside and to their surprise, they saw a huge circus. Mr. Sumit was the clown, Mr. Mahesh was serving popcorn, grandpa was the ring master and grandma was making the food. Anybody and everybody was at the circus. Manya and Aanya met the rest of the group near the entrance. The looked around the stalls together. There were fun games like Hit the bulls-eye and knock the pins. There were amazing prizes too. Aanya knocked all the pins down and won a cute plushie. When it was time for the main act, the kids rushed in and took their seats. Before the show started, grandpa bought all of them popcorn and roasted peanuts. When everyone settled down the tent went dark. Then suddenly a trumpet of an elephant was heard. The dancers were all dancing around the elephant, Trapeze artists were flying in the air and grandpa was doing magic tricks. The funniest part was when the joker came. He made funny jokes that made people roll on the floor with laughter. When the show ended they all dispersed from the tent. All the kids were laughing and smiling as they came out. Grandpa and grandma were overjoyed to see smiles on their faces!
author: Sneha Javia

title: Community of birds
text: A beautiful weaver bird's nest swayed as the wind blew quietly out side the window. An old grandma was sitting and knitting a colourful patchwork blanket. She was seated on a comfortable rocking chair which looked quiet antique. The beautiful swirly patterns gave it a rustic look. As she sat, her young and sweet little grand children came running in. They all said together, "Can you tell us a story grandma?" Grandma hesitated at first but nodded yes when the kids pleaded. She told the kids to settle down. All of them began fighting to sit right in front of grandma. Their fighting almost toppled over grandma. She hushed them and they settled down on the mat. After the kids settled down quietly, Grandma started telling her story. "This story is called the 'community of birds'!" Once there lived a family of weaver birds. They had a beautiful daughter who was going to live with her mate soon. The girl had soft, brown feathers. Her quaint beak looked perfect. The day she had to leave, she was anxious and worried. She had never flown completely unescorted before. As she arrived she saw a flock of weaver birds. She immediately identified her mate. He had brown feathers too but he had a secret. He had a special blue feather. That was what attracted the female weaver bird. As she approached she noticed grass strands in his beak. She was confused so she asked what he was doing. He put the strands aside and replied, "We need shelter from the harsh seasons. We need a home to bring up our kids. You should start collecting strands too. She did not know what to do so she asked him, "How will I know how to weave, I have never done this before!" He replied calmly "Do you remember how you house looked, We are weaver birds we are born to weave." The female weaver bird and her mate both worked hard. When it was shaping, a storm destroyed their home, but they never gave up. They kept on weaving, strand after strand. After months of hard work and toil their efforts finally bore fruit. They both looked contently at their nest. It was looking mesmerising. The nest was a beautiful shape and it was cozy and warm. The nest stood right above a small pond. The nest hung form a banyan tree that was situated just outside a city. They lived happily for a few years with enough food and water. Every day the female weaver bird used to chirp sweetly before dinner. The kids playing under the banyan tree found this very useful as they used to get a mouthful from their mothers when they used to be late for dinner. Seeing smiles on the kids' faces made the female weaver bird overjoyed. In the middle of July, 2 young chicks were born to the female weaver bird. She went outside to chirp but the practice soon got tiring. As time passed the chicks grew into young birds who were ready to leave the nest. As monsoon approached with dark clouds she decided to teach them how to fly, find food and to live independently. Soon the chicks flew off to begin their new life. The monsoons arrived with beautiful rains. The koels used to sing everyday as the crystal beads fell on their feathers. The banyan tree was huge and empty for a very long time. The female weaver bird yearned for company now that her chicks were away. After a few weeks, her yearning came true. She heard the shrill voices of parrots in the nearby hollow; 'knock - knock' and it grew loud oh! a new neighbor that's Mr & Mrs Pecker. She flew over and investigated. " Hi,welcome to the colony. How about a tea party?" The parrots and peckers gladly accepted the offer and they soon became very good friends. Other birds got attracted to the banyan tree too. They found the location, food and the water very convenient. Soon came in the sparrows, bulbuls, crows and many more flocked in. The banyan tree became the most famous spot in the area to dwell. Various types of birds lived together. They trusted each other a lot, so sometimes they let other birds babysit their chicks. As the birds lived together, In the nearby city a fight had broken out between 2 communities. The fight lasted for weeks and none of the sides was ready to give up. None of the sides wanted the other to win. The government tried to stop this, but the people just beat the government agents up. Everyone was affected by the fight. People were forced to stay inside to avoid getting harmed or hurt very brutally. One day the leader of the opposing side noticed the little bird community as he was strolling. He noticed that all the birds were different but they still lived in peace and harmony. This made him realise that peace is the best thing a person could have. The next day the man decided to sign a peace treaty to never fight ever again. When the people asked why, he narrated the incident about the bird community. He said that this made him realise the importance of peace. The fight was subsided and everyone lived in peace. " Wow " said the kids looking at grandma with awe. Grandma said "Yes see how a bird community avoided a war? This story avoided a war today too!" The kids looked puzzled and confused. Then grandma laughed in delight "I am talking about your fight!" Hearing that the kids all burst out laughing! THINK ABOUT IT Look around you. Do you see a tree? Did you notice that there is not only 1 nest but many nest on that tree? What does that tell you about? Do you live in peace too?
author: Sneha Javia

title: Mountains & Hills
text: Most events that happen to you are, temporary. But have you thought about the surrounding, does it stay always? Yes, but changes are made by humans.Mountains or hills I always wonder… Even if we try and move them they won’t move at any time! On Mountains and Hillsides time passes very slowly.That is Magic of Nature. We grow trees on the mountains but they won’t move. Farmers grow crops on hills but they don’t move.That is the miracle of mountains and hills. Any time you need a peaceful place to read or rest you may choose the hills yourself, and the nature around you welcomes you there. Swift breeze whistle in your ears, trees swaying slowly, their young trees bowing with respect. Birds dancing happily, some make a melodic tune. Birds sometimes get scared until you give them food and pet them well, you must also be kind and friendly with birds. The diversity between them looks colourful that’s unimaginable. As you climb up the hills on youngster oak trees squirrels sprint around it to get the nuts. Their twin big tooth helps them to munch into the nut.Squirrels give small squeals too. The insects around the hills aren’t scary, the busy bees don’t sting people. They stay and work calmly. The gorgeous, charming butterflies whisper to the bushes of flowers as the flap their colourful wings that are very delicate. You move on up the hill, lost with wonderful thoughts of nature. Not realising that you are away far from your home. But that won’t scare you until Mother Earth leads you home. The twilight finally arrives, the sun leaves the sky pink, purple, indigo blue and they all make a magical,shimmering sky full of stars. The fireflies are ready to shine as you reach the top, the wind that blows from the sea and touches your pale face and leaves you… with a smile of brightness that will bring happiness and joy to the world. Then once again tomorrow the sun will shine at the mountains and hills with golden rays.Nature is always the key to peace and happiness. When you nurture Mother Earth, she give you back beautiful weather and nature will be unimaginably amazing.
author: Kirtimayee Swain

title: How to be a marist
text: To be a marist, we need to do things that aren't bad. Examples: help people who need help, have empathy with everyone, always thank God for everything and so on. Now, i'll show some ways how to be a Marist. We should always look for someone to talk to, because you can meet a person who plays with you, talks to you, always calls to be together and that's how a good relationship is created, isn't it? You can make friends now, can't you?;) Her name is Mariana. She likes to walk around the garden every afternoon. However, there’s something about her that not everyone can have, that's happiness. A great example of being Marist is always being happy, because it helps to maintain an excellent quality of life and also helps us to enhance our daily life better. I love being happy and so will you. His name is Pablo. He was sitting and thinking about his life. He loves seeing people walking on the street. There is an old woman who always goes to the market to buy fruit on weekends. Pablo is always there to help her, because he is kind and has love in his heart. Isn’t that amazing? While Pablo was watching the street, he got some ideas about how people could help others with simple things.:) They are Marcos and Roberta. They were in the park and found some beautiful animals. Marcos thought "I'm glad there are people in this world who preserve the forest so that animals can survive, just like me and my wife". We always should think like Marcos, because it is important to people imagine the world without trees, and conclude that it would be much harder to survive. This family is simple and humble. The mother is explaining to the childrens how they can be happy when they grow up. These schildren used to be very annoying when they were babies. But as they were very small, they knew nothing about the world. So, the mother waited for them to get "older" to that she could teach them the attitudes of a "good person". if she was a bad person, she wouldn't be a marist. All these examples are about being a Marist. Just practice and learn. Many things have been made by humans practice. Just do good.

title: The Fox and The Crow
text: One daya crow stole a piece of cheese and sat on a branch of a tree to eat it in peace. At that moment a clever fox was passing by Sniff! Sniff! "What is that I smell?" he said. He stopped under the tree and saw the crow. "Mmm. I'd like to have a bite of that cheese," he thought. The fox looked up at the crow and said, "You are a fine crow! What lovely shiny feathers you have! You are the King of the Birds!" When the crow heard the praise of the fox, he became proud and happy. the crow flapped his wings triumphantly. And the fox went on, "You must have the most wonderful singing voice. King of the birds, let me hear a sweet song. The crow thought, "The fox could be right. I am th king of the birds. I'll let him hear my sweet voice." The crow opened his beak and began to sing, "Cra! Cra! Cra!" Then the piece of cheese feall through the air. At once the fox ran to it and ate it up. Then the fox said to the crow, "Silly crow. That was the worst voice I've ever heard, but most of all, you're the most stupid bird I've ever met! And thanks for the cheese." And he ran off into the woods.
author: mamta udar

title: MY GOOD HEALTH CHATER
text: A healthy diet is a diet that helps maintain or improve overall health. A healthy diet provides the body with essential nutrition: fluid, macronutrients, micronutrients, and adequate food energy. Good health is the most valuable gift available to the mankind on this planet. Good health is an essential pre-requisite for the persistent and adequate functioning of an individual and a society. Health of an individual is a basic necessity for carrying out day to day activities. Physical non-wellbeing is a problem not only for an individual but also for a society. A sick person’s primary concern is to maintain physical wellbeing of his body. Other pursuits of life become secondary for him. THINGS WE SHOULD DO TO BE HEALTHY 1.WASH YOUR HANDS. 2.MAINTAIN Hygiene 3.WE SHOULD GIVE REST TO OUR BODY. 4.WE SHOULD DO YOGA FOR 1 HOUR. 5.WE SHOULD ALWAYS BE HAPPY

title: I am Sooo Bored!
text: Little Pihu was so busy… Yes busy playing a Video Game on the mobile! “Pihu, why is my mobile in your hand? And without permission too, n o more screen time!”, her mother scolded. “But Mama, there is nothing to do, Absolutely NOTHING!” “I am Soooo o b ored ” Pihu answered back defiantly! Smiling, her Mother took her to the window… “Pihu. Look at that Banyon tree, standing so Tall, for so long!Does he look bored? He looks rather busy trying to reach for the Stars? Gosh is he sharing a joke with Mr. Wind?” “Ma, surely he is Messaging the Moon!” Pihu answered Sneakily. “Look at those loooong wires hanging from those branches!” she exclaimed pointing at the prop roots. Laughing, her mother pointed to a beautiful butterfly, “Oh Pihu, look at that beauty, throwing caution to the wind! Or is she the carrier, carrying gifts with her fluttering?” “Ma, she’s definitely doing a ramp walk, from flower to flower,” clapped Pihu,“Yes, she’s quite a Model!” And Pihu turned around strutting in front of the mirror her arms swinging. “And Pihu is that Sparrow, Singing Karaoke at the top of her lungs?” “Or do you think she is teaching her little ones about Nature?” “Nah Ma, I think she is surely scolding her babies, just like yooooou. It is more musical though,” giggled Pihu her gaze fixed on the Singing Sparrow. “And Ma look at those Clouds playing hide and seek,” said Pihu dreamily... "Or maybe peek-a-boo with Mr. Sun?” “Pihu I think they are sending us a message I think it’s going to rain soon,” her mother replied. "I love the scent of the wet mud, the sound of pitter-patter raindrops... " her mother whispered smiling gently. "And I also love dancing in the rain, licking those trickling droplets off my lips!!!" Laughed Pihu twirling around merrily holding a make-belief umbrella… " Sight, touch, smell,taste and hearing...ah our five basic senses, our rain Goddess stirs them all, doesn’t she, Pihu?” "And Ma, look at that Coconut tree! It looks just like an umbrella, doesn't it? " Yes Pihu the Palm family surely have got their act together. From fruit to oil, from baskets to furniture they are so useful!" "Ma just like the palm of my hand which is soooo useful!" Pihu clapped, giving her mother a wave and a hi-five in one shot! “Oh Ma look at that Squirrel playing the clown, digging and rolling!” “ Woooow, he’s faster than Usain Bolt, scrambling up that tree so fast!” “You know Pihu we can learn so much from the Squirrels - they not only help with cleanup but even help plant more trees! Squirreling away is just the trait we should all take away…” her Ma continued explaining… “Ma, you know we can also learn a lot from doggies toooo," squealed Pihu pointing at a couple of strays frolicking down the street without a care in the world! "You know they are called Man's best friend!" "They are so much fun and kind and I loooove how they wag their tails! Can we get a pet dog Ma?" Pihu took a chance yet again. Yes, she really really wanted a pet dog! Her mother rolled her eyes smiling at Pihu. Just then there was a ping at the computer. "Oh oh" exclaimed her mother, "work calling Pihu, I have got a lot of work. Sorry but I need to go now..." "It's ok Ma, I have sooooo much to do myself!" "Maybe i'll model just like our butterfly or dance or maybe read that book on dogs or...", Pihu continued her nose still pressed to the window. Idioms and Phrases: 1. Reach for the Stars: to try to do something that is very difficult and impressive. She always gave her all, reaching for the stars! 2. Throwing caution to the wind: To do something without worrying about the negative or bad effects. Throwing caution to the wind, he jumped right into the water. 3. Top of her lungs: as loudly as possible. Jeevan was screaming at the top of his lungs so that he could be heard by all. 4. Get your act together: to organize yourself so that you can do something properly. She is doing so well since she’s really got her act together. 5. Playing the clown: to try to make people laugh. Everyone loves having him over, he always plays the clown. 6. Squirreling away: to put (something) in a safe or secret place especially so that it can be kept for future use. She is quite a saver, keeping most of her salary squirreled away. 7. Without a care in the world: to have no worries at all. He’s a happy man without a care in the world! 8. Man's best friend: used to refer to a dog or to dogs as a group. Of course a dog is Man’s best friend!
author: Rutuja Joshi
illustrator: Akanksha  Agnihotri; Sangeetha Kadur; Sanjay Sarkar

title: Rohan's Birthday!
text: Have you ever celebrated your birthday in your house? Yes, I have. Let me tell you about a boy named Rohan, who celebrated his birthday in his house and enjoyed a lot. title: Nanammal and Kamalathal Travel by Road
text: Nanammal and Kamalathal are best friends. Nanammal teaches yoga. Kamalathal runs the local idli shop. Nanammal likes Kung Fu movies. Kamalathal only watches comedies. Nanammal hates being late. Kamalathal is never on time. But there is one thing they both love to do... —travel. Nanammal and Kamalathal are going on a holiday. “The train leaves at 9.30 in the morning. Don’t be late,” says Nanammal. Nanammal is packed and ready to go. She cycles over to Kamalathal’s house. Trrring trrrring! Pon ponnnn! The auto arrives to take them to the bus stand. Will all of Kamalathal’s things fit inside? “Oh no! There’s no place for us in the village bus. It’s full,” says Kamalathal. “We’re going to miss our train!” cries Nanammal. “It’s all your fault.” Chin-chik-chin-chik-chin-chik. Palani, the farmer, passes by in his bullock cart. “I have an idea,” yells Kamalathal. Nanammal and Kamalathal are finally on their way to the train station. Mpaaaaaaaaaaa! Mpaaaaaaa! Oh no! The train is leaving! Are they too late? “Whew! Well that was an adventure,” says Nanammal. “And we haven’t even reached Goa yet!” says Kamalathal. What are the different modes of land transport that Nanammal and Kamalathal take to reach the station?
author: Menaka Raman

title: When We Are Home
text: Our home tastes like the sweet, crunchy til pitha that Anaideo grinds up in the kitchen. Our home sounds like Papa’s loud snores shaking the bedroom as he takes his afternoon nap. Our home looks like Ma weaving on the loom in the living room while Huntu and I wrestle. Our home feels like a cool, splashy shower in the bathroom after a hot, sweaty day of playing outside. Our home smells like kopou flowers and ripe jackfruit as we sip tea in the courtyard. One day, we will be home again.

title: Why Is the Anganwadi Empty?
text: Rita is the Anganwadi* teacher for her village. *Anganwadi: Rural child care center for children between age 3 and 6 The children have left the Anganwadi Center. She is marking the attendance record. There are twenty young children in the village. Only five students attend regularly. Rita is worried. Rita has her next meeting in two weeks at the Rishikesh office. She needs to convince parents before that. She also needs to make tikka cards* for these children. *Tikka cards: Vaccination card She visits children who did not take admission. All parents give different reasons for their children not coming. Some say other children of the village will fight with their children. Some don’t want their children to eat at Anganwadi. Some grand-parents want to teach their grand-children at home. Some say their children will cry when they are away from their mother. And many are not at home, but in the city. Only two parents agree to send their kids from tomorrow. At the end of the day, Rita is tired and goes home. The next day, Seema comes to pick up Pari from Anganwadi. ‘Why are you upset?’ asks Seema. Rita tells her everything. ‘I have an idea that can help,’ says Seema. Rita looks at Seema curiously. In the evening Seema goes with other parents to convince the villagers. Sonam, Chutki, Pinku and Anuj go with her. She takes Pari’s notebook and drawing books. Other parents also help her. They all go to different houses. Seema goes to Pinku’s house. Pinku’s Dadi doesn’t want to send Pinku’s little sister Mahi to Anganwadi. She says that Pinku’s mother can teach the children at home. Mahi cries every time she leaves home. ‘The children can learn at home but going to Anganwadi they will make new friends,’ says Seema. ‘Yes, I have so much fun in school,’ says Pinku. ‘Dadi she will cry for a few days because she is not used to leaving her mother but it will help her,’ says Seema. ‘Okay Seema I trust you. We will send Mahi to Anganwadi tomorrow,’ says Dadi. This way parents convince villagers to send their children. Rita thanks Seema and other parents. Next day there are ten more students in class. Many children were crying but Rita knows they will stop crying after a week. Rita starts making all the children’s tikka cards. She is happy that the children of the village will be more healthy and safe now.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: Who Is Incharge of the Payment?
text: It is raining heavily in the village. Lalu Chacha takes his truck out. He reaches the road near the river. Suddenly his truck stops. Lalu Chacha steps out but his leg gets pulled in the daldal. ‘Oh no, not again!’ he shouts. Every year this road becomes a daldal*. There is no other road to reach other villages. Lalu Chacha shouts for help. Some people help him get out of the daldal. *Daldal: Marsh ﻿ In the evening Chacha visits ward member Rajesh. He tells him about the incident. Rajesh says he will try to convince the Gram Panchayat to solve this problem. Entire monsoon season passes without any progress. The villagers lose hope but one day the Gram Panchayat* announces a road project passed by Zila Panchayat*. The construction will be done under MGNREGA work. The villagers are overjoyed. They get employment and a pakka* road. *Gram Panchayat: Local governance body in a village *Zila Panchayat: Electoral governance body of a district *Pakka road: Concrete road The work for the road starts. Lalu Chacha and other villagers work for seven hours everyday. In a few months the road is complete but villagers have not received any money. ﻿ ﻿ All the villagers go to the Thekedar* to ask for their salaries. ‘Don’t worry you will get your money. I am not in charge of this, go ask your ward member,’ he says. The next day they go to the ward member Rajesh. ‘Don’t worry you will get your money. I am not in charge of this go ask the Gram Pradhan*,’ he says. *Thekedar: Contractor *Gram Pradhan: Electoral head of the local governance body of a village The next day they go to Gram Pradhan. ‘Don’t worry you will get your money. Zila Panchayat* told us they will inform us as soon as they pass the money,’ he says. The villagers are upset and angry. Nobody is taking responsibility for the payment. Months go by without any answer. *Zila Panchayat: Electoral governance body of a district Finally, one day the Panchayat announces that the money will be transferred in their bank accounts by Friday. On Friday everyone goes to the bank. They take out the cash from their Bank accounts. When it is Lalu Chacha’s turn, the accountant says his account does not have money. ‘How can this happen?’ Lalu Chacha is shocked. He goes to talk to the bank manager. Next in line is Charu Chachi. The accountant says she has twenty thousand rupees. Chachi is surprised. She also goes to the bank manager. ‘First you don’t pay us on time and when the payments are done, there are mistakes. I want my money today,’ demands Lalu Chacha. When Charu Chachi listens to this she understands what has happened. ‘I have received ten thousand extra and Lalu Chacha has not received any payment,’ says Charu Chachi to both of them. ‘Oh no, that means my money has gone in Chachi’s account,’ says Lalu Chacha. The manager apologizes for this mistake. The problem is solved in another hour. After six months Lalu Chacha finally receives his salary. He goes home happy but tired.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: When Will the Power Come Back?
text: Chutki and Pinku are attending online classes at Chutki’s house. In today’s class we are learning about the Anganwadi* center. Teacher requests Chutki to read. Chutki reads “Rita is the….” and suddenly the screen is black. The light goes out, the battery dies and the phone switches off. Sometimes the powercut lasts for days. They were worried and angry. *Anganwadi: Rural child care center for children between age 3 and 6 The children come out of the house. They meet Sonam and Anuj there. ‘Oh no! I’m tired of these power cuts,’ said Pinku. ‘When will the power come back? When will we study?’ said Sonam. ‘Remember when we went to Gram Sabha?’ asked Anuj. ‘Yes, the problem of water was solved there,’ said Chutki. ‘Maybe we can talk about this problem in the Gram Sabha*,’ said Anuj. ‘That’s a great idea. We should talk to Salim bhai, the electrician. He will know what to do,’ said Pinku. *Gram Sabha: Gram Sabha is the meeting organised by the local elected governance body with people in a village. They all go to Salim Bhai’s shop. He is fixing Chaman Chacha’s fan. The children tell him about the problem. ‘I cannot help you with this, children,’ says Salim Bhai. ‘There has to be some solution. We cannot study like this,’ says Chutki. ‘In Kimchi they have put up a solar power plant. If we had one then we would have electricity all the time,’ says Chaman Chacha. ‘Why can’t we have one?’ they asked. ‘Everyone from the village needs to agree,’ he replied. ‘Everyone in the village faces problems because of electricity, I think they will agree,’ said Sonam. ‘Yes, we can fix this like we fixed the water shortage problem,’ said Salim bhai. The children are happy to see Salim Bhai encouraged. The next day Salim bhai spoke with other villagers. Lalu Chacha and Krishna Bua agreed to help. Villagers had doubts about the money. Salim bhai has a solution for this. He suggests that the Gram Panchayat* can fund this project. After a week, more and more villagers are convinced about the Solar Power project. They decide to discuss this idea in the Gram Sabha. *Gram Panchayat: Local governance body in a village ﻿ The Sarpanch* has doubts about the budget and the availability of land. Krishna Bua suggests using the roofs of the school to set up this plant. The villagers convinced the Sarpanch to request for Vidhayak* funds to fund the project. The Sarpanch had no choice when everyone wanted this. She agrees and connects with the Vidhayak. The villagers and children are overjoyed. They know they can fix any problem together. *Sarpanch: Electoral head of the local governance body of a village *Vidhayak: Member of legislative assembly
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: We have no problem!
text: I CHARAN The mountain goat lived in Una Sakuland. Sakuland was a unique country. It stretched from the coast to the forests, from the valleys to the mountains. All living beings loved their country Sakuland. There was grass for rabbits and deer, insects for snacks for birds and bears, and fish for crocodiles and wild cats. And there was clean, cold water for everyone to drink. Una lived on the top of a mountain, far above the rest of the living beings. Climbing up and down the rocky mountain trails was a very difficult task and also took a lot of time. Una spent little time with other animals and got used to being alone. Rather, she loved being alone - she could do whatever she wanted, whenever she wanted, being alone. Sometimes Una thought that the rest of the animals were a bit stupid. "Why do they all have to do everything together? Can't they even go to the stream alone to drink water? I'll go," Una thought. All living beings had their own favorite way of doing things. But Una thought that my method was the best. Gradually, the climate of Sakuland began to change. But the creatures did not pay any attention to it. One day, the whales, which spend most of the year in the sea off Sakuland, announced that they were going elsewhere. "NS?" The tortoise asked. "It feels so good to be here." "The water is too hot for us," said the whales. "We have to go further north where the weather is cooler." Whales like to live in cold water and the waters of Sakuland became too hot for them. Turtles will miss the melodious songs of whales. But he didn't think much about it. "At least we don't mind," thought the tortoises. "Uh, you're showing useless tantrums," Una thought to herself. "It's too hot or cold, I don't care. Whales should try to be like me." All creatures quickly forgot the whales. But then one day, the turtles also started leaving their homes. "Why were you guys happy here, weren't you?" Wild cats asked. "There's very little sand left for us here," said the turtles. Turtles lay eggs on sandy beaches. "Where has the sand gone?" Wild cats asked. "What do you know, all we know is that sand used to be up to a big rock," said the big, old tortoise. "But the big rock doesn't look very big anymore - a large part of it is now submerged because of the rising waters." "Very bad has happened to the poor tortoise. Well, we don't mind," thought the wild cats. Seeing the tortoises leaving, Una thought, "What does it matter to me if the sand has gone under water? Turtles should have acted wisely like me and decided where to stay." She went to find grass for breakfast and then forgot about it. After that the wild cats also left from there. They could no longer catch fine fish in the stream. There was very little water in the stream now. The deer thought, "Oh, it was too difficult for the feral cats. But at least we are in good health." Una looked at the stream carefully, "The wild cats were quite strict, but perhaps they were not as strict as me." One day what Una saw was strange to her. Every year the snow of the mountain she lived on melted like a snowflake, and its stream was filled with water. But this time there was much less snow. Una couldn't quite believe her eyes and thought, "Maybe the snow on the mountain hasn't really subsided. It just looks like it today." But after that strange animals started coming to Sakuland. Everyone wanted to be friends with the cows. But she paid no attention to anyone - she just went on grazing and chewing. And their number was huge! When the grass began to disappear, the deer were a little worried. Gradually the deer had to move out of Sakuland to graze their favorite grass. "Uh--they just don't know what I'm supposed to eat," thought Una. "Sometimes I work by licking the moss on the rocks. And the moss doesn't taste good at all." As long as Una could live, she remained on her mountain. But now he often started lacking enough food and drinking water. At last Una, hungry and thirsty, came down the difficult mountain path. He tasted some grass growing on the hills, but it was not what he liked. She found a stream of water in a valley, but the taste of the water was not the freshness she was accustomed to. Now Una understands why the rest of the animals left Sakuland - this is very important. It is that you should eat the food which is best for you and there should be water around you. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ All the creatures he knew had left Sakuland when they found it difficult to find food of their choice, or they became more thirsty due to the water stream turning to muddy water, or else the trees in their place were more than others. They were cut down to build a house. When climate change was affecting the lives of others, Una and her friends kept thinking, "At least we don't have a problem." When the sea began to warm, the whales went in search of a better hideout. Then the tortoises, deer and una did not worry. When climate change was affecting the lives of others, Una and her friends kept thinking, "At least we don't have a problem." When the sea began to warm, the whales went in search of a better hideout. Then the tortoises, deer and una did not worry. But later he had to admit, "Now we have a problem too." Una had to admit that friends had their own Being around is very important. He decided to find them. But we don't mind! Una and her friends in Sakuland are facing climate change just like us. We humans are constantly releasing more greenhouse gases into the atmosphere than ever before – carbon dioxide is released from the burning of coal and mineral oil. Carbon dioxide is also released when we cut down trees. Apart from this, methane gas is released from the digestion of fodder in the stomach of cows and buffaloes, nitrous oxide is released from cars and other vehicles. These greenhouse gases mix with the atmosphere and cause global warming (global temperature rise) and climate change (climate change). As greenhouse gases add more heat to the atmosphere, the ice at the poles is melting and the sea level is rising. All this means that the weather pattern is changing - now it is cold in summer and hot in winter, and even rains do not come on time. This phenomenon of change in climate is called climate change. due to climate change When trees are cut, the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere increases. The forest, the home of the animals, perishes and they have to travel far and wide in search of food. Due to untimely rains, farmers are not able to take crops properly. Often, they sow seeds but there is no rain and the crop is ruined. Just imagine a world where there would be no mangoes or chocolates because the crops were ruined by too much rain or no rain at all! - The changing mood of the weather also affects humans. For example, people have to leave their homes during storms, floods or droughts. The amount of pollution in the environment also has a bad effect on our health, due to which we get sick very often. Climate change is affecting humans, the earth and all living beings on it.
author: VAKATI CHARAN

title: What Is Your Emergency?
text: Lalu Chacha’s son, Rakesh is getting married. The people of the village are making 30 kilos of arsa*. Some are mixing rice atta* and gud*. Some are making the chulha*. After everything is ready they fry the arsa in oil. *Arsa - Arsa is a sweet Pahari delicacy that is prepared on special occasions like weddings and traditional celebrations. *Atta - Whole wheat flour *Chula - A brick and mud stove *Gud - jaggery When the arsa are ready the children come running and pick three four pieces each. They give some to Lalu Chacha. ‘Hmm...hmm these are my favourite,’ he says and keeps eating till he goes to sleep. On the wedding day everyone is wearing colourful clothes. People are dancing to the tune of mask baja* and dhol damau*. Everyone is searching for Lalu Chacha. Anuj goes to his room to call him. He doesn’t come out. Anuj goes inside. Lalu Chacha is sleeping on the bed with hands on his stomach. ‘My stomach is in pain. I feel very sick,’ says Lalu Chacha. ‘Oh no, I will go call Krishna Bua. She will know what to do,’ says Anuj. *Masak Baja - Masak baja is a traditional musical instrument from Uttarakhand played in special occasions *Dhol Damau - Dhol Damau is the traditional instrument which is used in almost every occasion in Garhwal Krishna Bua comes running. 'My stomach is in pain, I had too many arsa yesterday,’ says Lalu Chacha. Krishna Bua asks him to drink ORS. She calls the ambulance number 108. They ask ‘Who is the patient? What is your emergency? Where are you calling from?’ Bua gives them all the answers. ‘Hold on, I will connect you to the Primary Healthcare Center (PHC) of your gram sabha* ’ *Gram Sabha - Gram Sabha is the meeting organised by the local elected governance body with people in a village The woman at the PHC asks the same questions. Bua answers them quickly. ‘The ambulance cannot reach your village. You will have to send the patient to the bridge, ' says the woman from PHC. ‘Okay we will try,’ replies Bua. Krishna Bua asks if any two people can lift Lalu Chacha and take him to the bridge. ‘Lalu Chacha is too heavy to be lifted by two people’, says Anuj. Then Krishna Bua sees the bride's doli*. ‘Maybe we can take him to the bridge in this doli,’ says Krishna Bua. ‘This is a little strange but we don’t have a choice,’ says Chaman Chacha. *Doli - Doli is a palanquin used to carry the bride in a wedding They put Lalu Chacha in the doli. Four guests lift the four sides of the doli. They reach the bridge in half an hour. The ambulance is waiting for them. Chaman Chacha and Krishna Bua go with Lalu Chacha. They take another hour to reach Lakshpur Primary Healthcare Center (PHC). ‘You are late, the Doctor left an hour ago’. ‘This is urgent! Can you call the doctor? It is his son’s wedding today’ says Bua. The nurse calls the doctor and explains the situation. Krishna Bua requests the doctor to come to the PHC. The doctor agrees and reaches the PHC in 30 minutes. He asks Lalu Chacha some questions. ‘Hmm… you need to eat more bananas and rice this week. And please don’t eat any more arsa. I will give you some medicines that will reduce the pain,’ says the doctor smiling. Krishna Bua gets a call from Rakesh. The barat’s* car is near the PHC. It will pick up Lalu Chacha from the PHC. Everyone is happy now. Lalu Chacha will feel better and they will reach the wedding on time. *Barat: a celebratory wedding procession that escorts the groom with their friends and family to the bride's place.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: Pari's Polio Ravivar
text: Sonam and her niece Pari are playing with Khadu*. Sonam’s sister Seema is making amodi*. Krishna Bua comes to her house. ‘Tomorrow we are organizing Polio Ravivar* in the Public Health Center (PHC). Sonam, come with Pari for her polio drops,’ says Krishna Bua. Seema looks worried. *Khadu: Mountain sheep *Amodi: Unripe mango’s vegetable *Ravivar: Sunday ‘I don’t want to give Pari any polio drops. Last month she got a fever after taking drops,’ says Seema. ‘Fever is a side-effect of the drops. It protects the child from polio disease,’ says Krishna Bua. ‘I trust you Bua so I will come tomorrow,’ says Seema. Krishna Bua went to other houses. Many people complained that the PHC was far from their house. They were right, first they needed help to reach help. Lalu Chacha was alert after the wedding incident. He advised villagers to take care of their health. He also gave lift to mothers and children in the truck. This time many villagers came with their children to the Polio Camp outside PHC. Krishna Bua was happy to see so many children. There were five ASHA didis* from five villages and some Panchayat members. *ASHA Didis: Primary health activists in Indian communities She was helping the nurse with distribution of iron and calcium medicines. Seema took Pari to the polio drops stand. ASHA Didi is giving the drops. Seema looked worried. Bua took Pari and helped the other ASHA Didi. Seema looked away. Pari cried after having the drop but stopped after some time. ‘Don’t worry Seema. My children have also taken drop,’ said Bua. ‘This is good for Pari but I was scared. Thank you for coming with me Bua,’ said Seema. Krishna Bua smiled and helped other children get their drops. Children were happy to get shahtoot* after the drops. *Shahtoot: Mulberry
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: We Love Celebrations!
text: Chutki, Pinku, Anuj and Sonam are taking a walk in the village. They look at the water tanks and solar plants at every house. ‘Our villages have changed so much in this year,’ says Pinku. ‘Yes, now we have electricity and water tanks,’ says Chutki. ‘Many students are going to Anganwadi*. Everyone is using the new pakka road*,’ says Anuj. ‘We have solved many problems,’ says Sonam. *Anganwadi: Rural child care center for children between age 3 and 6 *Pakka road: Concrete road ‘Do you think we should celebrate?’ asks Pinku. ‘We love celebrations!’ they said with excitement. ‘Every year we have a thaula to welcome the spring months. We can celebrate these new changes this year,’ says Sonam. The children decide that this year’s Baisakh Thaula* will be bigger. *Baisakh Thaula: Spring fair In the coming days, everyone starts preparing for the thaula*. The adults decide to bring homemade items. Lalu Chacha is helping to get things from the city by making rounds in his truck. *Thaula: Fair On the day of the thaula, people from nearby villages visit. The village is decorated with flags and spring flowers. Everyone is singing to the tune of Bedu pako, bara masa*... as they walk to the Thaula. *Bedu pako, bara masa: Folk song of Uttarakhand Sarpanch* is selling arsas* with Charu Chachi. Lalu Chacha is going to eat many but Pinku comes and stops him. ‘We cannot have one more emergency,' says Pinku, taking the arsas away from Lalu Chacha. Lalu Chacha looks sad. Charu Chachi starts laughing and doesn't give him more arsas. Krishna Bua is selling the Garhwali special kode ki roti* with makhan* and chutney*. Aashi Madam and Sonam are enjoying the yummy roti. *Sarpanch: Electoral head of the local governance body of a village *Arsa: Arsa is a sweet Pahari delicacy that is prepared on special occasions like weddings and traditional celebrations *Kode ki roti: Finger millet chapati *Makhan: Butter *Chutney: Thick sauce made from vegetables or fruits Akbar Bhai and Salim Bhai are selling toys. There are dolls, cars, mobile phones and tiny drums for children. Chutki gets a mobile phone for herself. Seema and Rita Madam have made jhangora ki kheer* and jalebis*. Pari and Mahi love the kheer* so much that they finish the entire bowl. Dadi has made baskets and lamps from bamboo sticks and bhimal*. The people from other villages love her baskets. She has already sold twenty of them. *Jhangora ki kheer: Barnyard millet pudding *Jalebi: A sweet snack *Kheer: Rice pudding *Bhimal: Grewia tree In the evening the Sarpanch is telling everyone about the teamwork of the village. The Sarpanch thanks everyone for bringing together this lively mela*. After the speech, Rakesh and Rajesh play the dhol* and masak baja*. The villagers dance in celebration. Chutki, Pinku, Anuj and Sonam are very proud of their village. *Mela: Fair *Dhol: Dhol is the traditional instrument which is used in almost every occasion in Garhwal *Masak Baja: Masak baja is a traditional musical instrument from Uttarakhand played in special occasions
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: The past of the dinosaurs
text: A long time ago there lived the dinosaurs. There were many types of dinosaurs like a Her bivorous and Carnivorous. Her bivores ate plants and Carnivores ate meet. Dinosaurs survived happily on earth. Then one day, a star full of life began to come closer to earth. It crashed into earth and created a big explosion. The explosion was felt all around the world resulting in forest fires and volcanic eruptions. Some dinosaurs escaped the event but after a while they all became extinct. Then mammals, birds and amphibians and other animals thrived on the Earth. Then, Humankind evolved from apes and transformed the world with their intelligence. Now there are only bones and fossils left. And this is the story of the dinosaurs.

title: Rani Laxmi bai
text: Rani Lakshmibai was born on 19 November 1828 [4] [5] [6] in the town of Varanasi into a Marathi Karhade Brahmin family. [7] She was named Manikarnika Tambe and was nicknamed Manu. [8] Her father was Moropant Tambe [9] and her mother Bhagirathi Sapre (Bhagirathi Bai). Her parents came from Maharashtra. [10] Her mother died when she was four years old. Her father was the Commander of the war of Kalyanpranth. Her father worked for Peshwa Baji Rao II of Bithoor district. [11] The Peshwa called her "Chhabili", which means "playful". She was educated at home and was taught to read and write, and was more independent in her childhood than others of her age; her studies included shooting, horsemanship, fencing [12] [13] and mallakhamba with her childhood friends Nana Sahib and Tatya Tope. [14] [15] [ dubious – discuss ] Rani Lakshmibai contrasted many of the patriarchal cultural expectations for women in India's society at this time. [16] Rani Lakshmibai was accustomed to riding on horseback accompanied by escorts between the palace and the temple, although sometimes she was carried in a palanquin. [17] Her horses included Sarangi, Pavan and Baadal; according to historians she rode Baadal when escaping from the fort in 1858. Her palace, the Rani Mahal, has now been converted into a museum. It houses a collection of archaeological remains of the period between the 9th and 12th centuries AD.
author: Arya Tanushree

title: Friends can be anyone
text: Aiden was one of the kindest boys around. He lived with his grandmother in a small village in Africa. One day, his grandmother decided to bring him a gift. She knew that he had always wanted a lawn car, so she bought a small one for him. Aiden was delighted when he saw the small car. He decided to take it for a spin. He went to the garden, and saw a crane crying by the lake! Aiden asked the crane if anything was wrong. "I was looking for food to feed my babies, when my leg hit a tree!" was the poor crane's reply. Aiden felt sorry for the crane, and offered to help her. The crane readily agreed. He hoisted the crane on his cart, and pushed her to his home. When they reached, Aiden bandaged the crane's leg, and pushed him back to the garden. The crane thanked Aiden. Aiden ran back home........that too, JUST in time for dinner. Aiden woke up the next day, totally forgetting his encounter with the crane. He looked outside the window. the sun was shining like anything. "It's the perfect time for soccer!" he thought as he got dressed. He called up his friends, and all of them started kicking the ball around. But unfortunately, while Aiden was trying to shoot a goal, the ball hit his grandma's window! His grandmother heard the sound of the shattering glass. She came out, her face fuming. Aiden knew he was in BIG trouble. "Aiden!" she yelled "That glass cost almost all your gramps money! And here you are aiming balls at it? No TV for you today!" Aiden walked away sadly, and soon began to start crying. He soon reached the garden. He sat down on a rock next to the pond and started sobbing harder than ever. The crane saw him, and she recognized him at once. He swooped down and asked him what's wrong. Aiden was surprised to see the crane. He told her that when he was playing football, he accidently broke his grandma's window. The crane felt sorry for him, after all, it was all an accident! The crane talked to Aiden and Aiden soon forgot all about windows. When Aiden went home that day, his grandmother appologized to him, for going too hard on him. Aiden appologized as well, saying he was sorry for the broken window. As for the crane, she and Aiden became best friends, always having each other's backs!

title: A NAVARASA EXPERIENCE
text: It had just rained but the sky was clear now. Shravan and his friend were walking back home. And it started drizzling and at the same time the sun peeped out from the clouds. They saw something very beautiful and mesmerizing. What was it? A lovely rainbow in the sky. Both of them were absolutely spell bound and were in awe of it. It looked very beautiful. A lovely rainbow in the sky. They were absolutely spell bound and were in awe of it. It was very beautiful. Suddenly a cat jumped out of nowhere and Shravan's friend screamed and ran and fell into a puddle of water and splashed water everywhere. All the kids around were laughing out loud at him. Shravan's friend got really furious at the kids for laughing at him. He shouted at them, "Stop it all of you. Bring me a handkerchief or a snack towel." At the junction, Shravan said "Bye "to his friend and turned left and his friend turned right and both walked towards their homes. As Shravan walked home he heard a puppy's yelping sound. He looked here and there. He spotted a puppy in a pit near a drain. H e wanted to help the puppy. He felt very sad for the puppy and wondered how he could help him. The puppy had wounds in his paw. But looking at the drain made him feel disgusted.. How was he to go near a drain and pick up the puppy? It looked so dirty! Also Shravan was scared and thought what if the puppy's mom came looking for it and found Shravan touching it! What if she gets angry and attacks him! Suddenly there was a loud thunder and Shravan was very scared of thunder. The thought of the puppy's mother and the thunder really scared him and made him sweat profusely. He gathered some courage, picked up the puppy and ran to his school. He asked the janitor for help and they both went to the Vice- Principal' s office. Shravan decided to ask the Vice -Principal Mam to call a veterinary doctor. The Vice - Principal Mam appreciated his gesture and his brave decision to bring the puppy to the school and agreed to help him. The doctor treated the puppy's wounds and in no time the puppy became active and stopped yelping. The doctor's treatment had been so effective in such a short time, that Shravan felt it was like a miracle. He wondered how quickly the puppy had recovered. He thanked the doctor and the Vice- Principal for their help and quickly took the puppy to the same place from where he had picked him assuming that the puppy's mother would have come looking for it. When Shravan left the puppy near a tree, its mother came looking for it and both were so happy to see each other. Seeing the reunion Shravan felt so relieved.His heart and mind was at peace. He went home and told his mother about it. It was a NAVARASA experience for him that day which he would never forget. Next day Shravan was praised by the Vice- Prinicpal in the Assembly and the whole school clapped for him. RAUDRA RASA- ANGER (Red) 4. KARUNA RASA- COMPASSION (Grey) 5. VEERA RASA - COURAGE (Orange) 6. BIBHATSA RASA- DISGUST (Blue) 7. ADBHUTA RASA- WONDER (yellow) 8. BHAYANAKA RASA- FEAR (Black) 9. SHANTA RASA - PEACE (White) The doctor treated the puppy's wounds and in no time the puppy became active and stopped yelping. title: Jealous Grace
text: Grace used to live a jolly life with her parents and grandparents. Until her baby brother was born. Her grandmother used to tell her stories and her mother used to give her gifts. Her grandfather used to take her on walks. She was at her happiest stage! Until, her baby sister was born......... The baby used to get everything she wanted. Kites, fruits, colors, sketchbooks and what not! Grace was becoming jealous day by day, but the worst part was when she got the most special thing! All the attention Grace used to get!! Grace tried soo hard to get the attention back. She would plead her mother to carry her, not the baby. But the baby, named Twinkler, meaning "star" would start crying. Grace was over this! Grace could not cope with this anymore. A fine day, definitely a boring one for Grace, she looked around and found no one near. She tried to get into the crib. Her intentions were to push the baby and make her fall, so she ghastly gets hurt. But it wasn't worth a try. Her grandpa came in and caught her! She was scolded a lot that day. One day she thought of taking away the baby to the pond side and leaving her. She thought and thought curiously. Her inner self told her to do it! Oh no! She took the baby and started running away. She thought after leaving the baby everyone will think she fell off somewhere and later forget about her. But Grace's grandmother caught her! Grace was scolded a lot and grandma said" If you do one more wrong thing you would be kicked out!" This time Grace was confused, she asked her inner self again! "Do you think what I am doing is right?" Grace asked, and the inner self said, "it is your choice but, do not harm the baby if you want to become important. It is a vulnerable soul, do not be greedy. One day she got a pink frock from her grandpa, grandma, dad and mum, and they said "Grace we understand that you are trying to be together with us and be loved, after all you are our daughter. Forgive us, we totally forgot about you since Twinkler was born. Do you think you could forgive us all?" Grace then said in a miserable voice "I will have to think about that alone" So everyone left. The inner grace suddenly appeared again! "Grace, now it is a fair game" forgive everyone! Grace still thought, she realized that she was being a big burden on her elders. And Twinkler was being a burden on her! She thought of the fun she could have with her sister if she was not so jealous. Grace understood the meaning of love. She forgave and said sorry to everyone, once again, the whole family reunited!

title: Why is Ved crying?
text: Ved is playing with his friends. He has fallen down. His knee is hurting. "Stop crying Ved" say his friends. "Boys don't cry" Ved doesn't stop crying. All his friends are laughing at him. "Ved is a sissy" "Ved is a girl" "Go away sissy!" "girl!" "sissy!" Ved runs upstairs to appa. "oh oh" says Appa "that looks like it hurts a lot, let's clean it up" Appa and Ved are in the bathroom. Appa wipes Ved's knee gently with a wet towel. "Vedu, I am going to put some antiseptic now, it'll sting a little okay?" Ved nods his head. Ow that hurt! Appa helps Ved wash his face. Ved has stopped crying. "Better now?" appa asks as he and Ved sit down on the sofa. Ved nods his head. "appa" he says "why shouldn't boys cry?" "Who said boys shouldn't cry?" asks Appa "When I started crying, my friends said that I shouldn't cry, they said boys don't cry. Only girls and sissies cry" "Ved, let's understand first, what makes people cry" says appa "All living beings cry. There are two different reasons. The first one is called physical pain when your body can feel the pain like you did when you fell down and the other is called emotional pain when it hurts inside like you felt when your friends laughed at you" "Then why were my friends laughing at me" asks Ved "That's because people think that crying is a sign of weakness" says appa "however, that's not true, it's good to cry because it makes us feel better. If boys are not supposed to cry then we wouldn't have tear ducts in our eyes at all" "What are tear ducts appa" "Tear ducts are tiny tubes in our eyes that drain out the tears that are formed in our eyes" "So it's okay for boys to cry?" "of course it is, I cry too" says appa with a smile "and it doesn't mean I am weak" Ved is feeling better now. He smiles at appa "Thank you appa" "you are welcome Ved" appa gives him a hug.

title: The Peacock Who Wished To Fly
text: Once upon a time, there was a peacock named Praline. He always wished to fly. One day, he looked up in the sky and said to himself, 'I want to fly like the other birds too!' 'I will fly up too!' he said, excitedly. 'And no one will be there to stop me from flying high.' After sometime, he came up with an idea and started working. He looked at his big tail and said, 'This big tail is the reason why I can't fly up. But I can't loose my beautiful and precious tail either. I can't fly with these. I'll just have to steal feathers from other birds. First, he stole a feather from the goose. 'This white feather is strong and light enough to help me fly up.' He said after taking one of the goose's feathers. After that, he quietly stole a feather from the parrot when he was looking away. 'This is nice enough to help me fly.' He said after taking a green feather from the parrot. Next, he stole a feather from the sleeping owl. he stole some feathers from the owl. He took them and went away. On his way down the road, he saw two colorful birds with beautiful feathers. He quickly took there feather and ran away. On his way further, he saw two more birds and took there feathers too! when he counted all the feathers, he just needed one more. So, he went to the clever eagle to steal. But he was a little scared of them. As soon as he stole a feather, the furious eagle looked at him and frowned. Praline ran as fast as he could to save himself and finally got all the feathers. He lay down all the feathers he had stole from other birds and wove them together. After that, he wore the feather in his tail and when he stretched them, they spread out like a fan. Praline was very happy and got ready to fly. But the feathers weren't lifting him up! Praline was disappointed, but on the other hand, the feathers made him look even more attractive than ever before! Praline no longer wished to fly. He was happy being the most gorgeous bird in the jungle.

title: The Great Rifasa
text: Nothing seemed right. By now, the clouds should have cooled the land with many showers. But the water holes were still dry. All the animals of the Kabini forest were hot and thirsty. One day, things got stranger still. The sun was already peeking past the highest trees. But something was missing. Where had the human tourists in their safari jeeps gone? They never missed a day, come rain or shine. They should have been driving around noisily everywhere, disturbing everything. The animals began to get very curious. Surely, the humans must be somewhere! The sloth bears, with their sharp snouts, started sniffing around. “Here, Papa, here,” shouted a bear cub. “Diesel smell, diesel smell!” Papa bear shuffled to his son and inhaled deeply. “Good catch, Cubby, but those are not fresh. Keep trying.” All over Kabini, the animals began their own safari — The Great Rifasa. It was to hunt down the lost human tourists and their jungle jeeps. They decided to search all the favourite tourist spots. Some elephants and chital deer strolled to the backwaters of the Kabini dam. They must be here somewhere, thought the animals. But there were no jeeps to be found. Kajal, the beautiful tigress, took her two young sons to the temple tank. “No doubt they will be looking for us here,” she thought. But after a long wait, she too had to give up. No humans today. “They will be looking for us at S-Bend,” growled Chukki, the tigress. “Let’s go there.” She beckoned her three young cubs and their older brother. But the entire stretch till the Power Line was very quiet. Round and round the Kabini forest, all the animals went. They searched along the water bodies. They trekked up to the highest point in the forest and down into the deepest valley. The langurs and the bonnet macaques peered from the tallest trees. The serpent eagles and the hawk eagles soared above the clouds, looking for the moving vehicles. But they spotted no jeeps, no humans. There was no click, click, click of cameras. No binoculars glinting in the sun. Nothing. The animals of the Kabini forest could not rest that night. The next day, and the day after that, it was the same story all over again. The humans had simply disappeared. For a while, some of the animals enjoyed the peace. Good riddance, they thought. Now they could freely wander about and lie on the roads. The predators could hunt in the open. Everyone could breathe cleaner air. But soon, animal after animal started to tell a different story. “My cubs love to run away and play. Sometimes, the humans find them even before I can,” confessed Naama, the tigress. “Let’s hope they come back soon.” The elephant mother trumpeted in agreement. “They can be irritating,” she said, “but they build paths for us to cross the jungle and avoid the prickly lantana plants.” “Yes, and I do pretend to charge at them sometimes,” Tambu, the young tusker, laughed. “It is so boring without them.” The Kabini animals decided to act. After many years, the Jungle Council was called. Mighty old Bhogeshwara, the long-tusked elephant, took charge. He commanded the langurs to gather all the animals. Soon the jungle was abuzz with their myriad coughs and screams. “Come for an important meeting,” they called out. “You will all be safe. No predator will attack. Come, come to the backwaters now.” One by one, all the animals came out to the open grassland near the water. Elephants and big cats, deer and monkeys, squirrels and jungle fowl, bears and gaurs, otters and crocodiles. What a spectacular sight it was. “My friends and, well, a few enemies,” harrumphed Bhogeshwara. “We are gathered here today because of a tragedy that might affect us all. The humans are suffering from a great illness. My cousins from the nearby zoo told me about it. The disease they call COVID-19 is so dangerous that they are hiding in their homes. Earlier they were like us,” he looked at the elephants around him. “They used to live in herds. Now they have to be like you, Chukki,” he said to the mother tigress. “They have to stay just with their own families. Maybe they are not visiting so as to keep us safe. Isn’t that kind? But they may not return anytime soon.” “Does that mean we can roam freely now?” Scarface, the leopard, sawed. “A jeep nearly ran over me the other day,” he said, shuddering at the memory. Doey, the fawn, stepped forward. “But I like humans,” she said, boldly. “They always smile and wave at me. No tiger attacks us when they are around.” “I too love the tourists,” Paara, the peacock, preened. “They truly appreciate my beauty. Do you know how many photos they click of me dancing?” The langurs only laughed. “Oh, we can easily control them,” said Langa, the biggest of them all. “As soon as we call, they gather around us, pointing their big cameras here and there. I often give false alarms just to fool them. It is fun.” “Let’s face it. We miss them,” declared Spanner, the tiger. Many animals nodded. “You? You miss them?” came a sneering voice from the bushes. Karia, the world-famous black panther, emerged like a silky silhouette against the sky. “Excuse me! It is I who should miss them the most. For six years, people from all over the world have come here for me and only me! I just have to yawn and cameras click like gunfire! All of you,” he looked around disdainfully, “are only the surplus of the safari. After all, I am the only black panther humans can hope to spot.” The other animals looked at Karia, who had jumped onto a fallen log. He was rather handsome, his yellow eyes glistening, his tail curling. But why so much arrogance? Some of the tigers were amused. The leopards were not. “But when will they return? Don’t they miss me? “ Karia continued, quite unaware of Scarface’s baleful look. Only a loud silence echoed through the forest. “All right then, we agree that the tourist humans mean us no harm,” trumpeted Bhogeshwara. “Come, let us pray for them to be safe enough to return. We will continue our Rifasa until then.” The Kabini animals bowed their heads. From the mighty elephants to the little mongoose babies, everyone prayed for the well-being of the humans. The forest became still. Maybe the animals of Kabini crafted some magic that day. In cities and towns, the humans too were missing the forests. While praying for the health of their loved ones, they saved some wishes for the wild animals they tried to protect. At last, scientists developed vaccines against the virus! When the pandemic receded and the lockdown was lifted, nature lovers rushed back to Kabini. A few animals were on a Rifasa the morning they heard the first rumble of the jeeps. “Hurrah!” the elephant herd trumpeted, letting the whole jungle know the humans had returned. What a treat awaited the tourists that day! The tigers, the bears — even the elusive Karia — came right up to the jeeps, almost as though to say, “Welcome back. We know you love us. We missed you too.” As the human safari started again, the animals finally ended their Great Rifasa.
author: Rohini Nilekani

title: A LESSON FROM A FROG TALE
text: Once there was a group of frogs in the jungle. They were returning from a social gathering. Suddenly two frogs fall inside a deep pit and found themselves in great difficulty. Their friends tried to help them, but could not do anything as the pit was very deep. Their friends decided there was no benefit of making any effort. They gathered around the pit and started shouting that you should give up because you are going to die soon. At last one of the frog gave up and stopped making efforts and soon died. The other frog kept jumping with more efforts even he was extremely tired and in pain. Suprisingly he jumped outside the pit and finally survive. His friends, asked him, why he did not stop trying where as the other frog followed their advise. The frog then answered by reading there lips that he was deaf and when he saw their gestures, he thought that his friends outside the pit were encouraging his efforts and cheering him up. That was the reason why he kept trying and succeed. The morel of the story are - 1 - We should always use encouraging words. 2 - We should always cheer our friends. 3 - We should always keep working in right direction.
author: Raji Keshri
