title: The Champion Princess
text: Princess Oona is worried. The Amartya Championship, the one in a leap year weightlifting contest in her kingdom, is close by. But she weights 43 kilos while according to the rules, she must weigh 50 kilos! The Amartya Championship was one in a leap year contest. In the championship, contestants had to lift different things to show there strength. It was named after the greatest athlete in the Eastern Realm. Oona loves to lift weights. As a child, she would lift... dogs, cupboards, tables, chairs... and even her dad, the King! “How did practice go Oona?” Asks her mother, the Queen. “ It's going fine mother,” says Oona to her mom. “But I still have to put on three kilos!” The Queen gives her some parathas. “Eat well my dear,” she says. “You’ll get there in no time.” As she eats, Oona remembers the last championship. That was many years ago. Prince Arun of Nehal had won the contest. He had been stronger and faster than everyone else in the championship. Oona has other dreams apart from just winning the championship too. She wants to go to Himkashi. The land of snow. And go skate there. “Can I have another paratha mother?” Oona asks the Queen. Her mother laughs. She starts thinking of her past. Many years ago, she had also dreamed of winning the championship. But she never could. She was happy to see that her daughter was carrying on her dream. Days pass and Princess Oona trains harder. She runs up and down the rocky mountains. She swims in the long river. She eats meat, fruits and vegetables too! She works so hard that her muscles build up, and because of them, her weight increased. It is the week before the Championship. Princess Oona stands on a weighing scale. "50 kilos at last! I've done it!" Oona is exited. She flexes her muscles. Oona is very happy. On the day of the Championship, Oona gets ready. She is exited but nervous too. The competition begins. Oona sees that a lot of people have participated. A boy with a yellow turban, a girl with a blue blouse, and of course, Prince Arun. They lift a lot of things. Rocks, logs, cupboards and treasure chests. The judges watch. Is he shaking? Is she tired? Can they lift it? Oona is tired but she's not giving up! She is putting all her strength in lifting the object. Oona was close to winning but Arun is in the lead. Soon the final round begins where participants had to lift The Golden Throne. It is time for Oona to lift the throne. She gets excused. When she almost gives up, she thinks of Himkashi and Amartya. The Golden Throne slowly lifts up. The scores are displayed and Princess Oona wins! Oona has fulfilled her dream of being the champion of The Amartya Championship. Now it is time to go to Himkashi and skate. Princess Oona is the Champion Of The Amartya Championship! Princess Oona did not go to Himkashi. She is happy being the Champion.
author: Vaishno Warade

title: The bird's merry go round
text: Variety of birds living in a forest unitedly. They were chirping with each other about the arrival of a new animal in the forest. "Did you see the teeny weeny creature." "What do you think whose, baby can it be?" So sad! the baby has no family. No! No! I cannot see the infant all alone. In this kiosk of chirping, the forest filled with lots of musical sound. The tiny baby cried out loud, Wah! Wah! Wah! The whole forest echoed with the sound. The birds remained silent. Now, what should we do? How shall we take care? Where shall we find a family to this little baby? The birds flew in circles over the baby, seeing this the baby started laughing heeee!! heeee! heee!! The birds soon understood the way to keep the baby happy, so that it does not miss its family. But the main worry still remains the same. How to give a family to this child? The birds thought and thought, but to no avail. Soon they saw a big eagle hovering up high in the sky. Hello sir, can you help us. The eagle flew down and asked, What's the matter my friend? All birds chirped together, look at the infant, how helpless it looks. Can we get some help. The eagle glanced at the baby and said sorry i cannot help you. Hip! Hip! Hurray! The eagle picked the baby and the other birds made a circle of merry-go-round. On the count of three, we shall fly, said the eagle. One, Two, Three, here we go, The eagle flew with the baby and the birds made a circle of protection below the baby. They flew to the nearby village and dropped the baby inside a house. The lady of the house was joyous to see the baby. She was praying for a long time to receive a baby. She exclaimed! god has granted my wish. I received a baby from heaven. She took the baby and went around in the house and into the streets and neighbourhood shouting with joy. She thanked god for the bundle of joy and the birds also remained happy.
author: NITYA SUBHASH GUPTA
illustrator: Horn Samon; Lavanya Karthik; Prashant Kumar Singh; Rijuta Ghate; Suvidha  Mistry; Wiehan de Jager

title: To the dentist!
text: It's such a fun day! Having my cousin over... The best thing ever! My cousin is Tanvi, and she's a little bit bigger than me. I was having just so much fun! Carrom, Tag, Ludo, and so many other fun games! And, oh my gosh, we are also going to the carnival today! Could ANYTHING ruin the fun? Absolutely not! And oh boy, isn't she cool! And the most fun person to be around. She plays with me whenever she can. She's at the top of her class too! Hang on. Mom's calling me. Be right back. We are making hats out of leaves but she's calling me. Anyways, let's go. "Come here! I want to tell you something." said mom. "Yes, mommy, what is it?" I asked. "We're going to the dentist. Before the carnival. Tanvi's coming too." said mom. "What? No way!" I said, shocked. "No way isn't possible here, Jess. Please understand, regular checkups are important" said daddy. "B-b-but it's my first check-up..." I stuttered. Sigh. I saw that they were getting angry now. There was no way out. Even if I disagreed. I went to Tanvi. And showed her by a mirror how great my teeth were. She was shocked for a moment after hearing about the dentist thingy and how scared I was. She then calmed me down. "It's just your imagination which makes you think that some things cause a lot of pain, even when they don't. Your thinking makes up your reality, right?" said Tanvi. I agreed with her, a little more encouraged. It was now time to go to the dentist. I had drew a picture of a boy, a bit scared though, like me, to make me a little less scared, knowing that more kids are scared of dentists than me. We reached the hospital. I anxiously waited for my turn to come. Tick, tick, tock, went the clock. Waiting, waiting, bored, was me. The door opened. The dentist looked friendly, unlike I imagined him to be! The dentist started checking me now. Not at all painful it was! He checked my teeth, gums and mouth. That's all! I came out after the check-up, waiting for the results. Tick, tick, tock, went the clock. Waiting, waiting, bored, was me. Again. And after the moment, came the results! Daddy and mommy saw it first. Then me. I was ecstatic! My teeth, gums and mouth were perfectly healthy! Hip, hip, hurray! I was super-duper-looper happy! My teeth were healthy! I told Tanvi about it. Tanvi also showed me her teeth. They were pearly white! But how? She brushed her teeth and never refused to go to the dentist. I hugged her. Without her help, I would've never escaped the fear of dentists! Mommy and daddy are so proud of me! Now, my fear of dentists is gone. Is yours too? "Daddy, I'll try all the games in the carnival today!" "And empty my pocket?"
author: Khushi Lalwani
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Nyambura Kariuki; Shirish  Ghatge

title: The wind poem
text: I saw you toss the kites on high And blow the birds about the sky; And all around I heard you pass, Like ladies' skirts across the grass-- O wind, a-blowing all day long, O wind, that sings so loud a song! I saw the different things you did, But always you yourself you hid. I felt you push, I heard you call, I could not see O wind, a-blowing all day long, O wind, that sings so loud a song! O you that are so strong and cold, O blower, are you young or old? Are you a beast of field and tree, Or just a stronger child than me? O wind, a-blowing all day long, O wind, that sings so loud a song!
author: Priti Gulati

title: The Bonds of The Mouse and Pigeons
text: Once upon a time lived an interesting mouse. What was interesting about him is that he loved to talk with everyone, even if they were going to eat him! Everyone loved the mouse. One of his favourite visitors were the pigeons. The little mouse loved to take a ride on the pigeons back. And the pigeons loved to talk to the little mouse. The mouse however had a very tough time with the hunters. They always troubled his friends and whenever he wanted to help them he just couldn't because the hunters would just kick him away. But he wouldn't just give up! Even though he was small and wasn't as strong as the hunters, he still would bother them buy biting and cutting the hunter's nets. He would also bite them when they harmed his friends! But now the Hunters had enough of him. they set up a trap for him and placed some delicious cheese. The little mouse went out in the forest to see some of his friends. He found some cheese on his way and h e thought he'd take some of the cheese for his friends but the poor mouse fell for the trap. He was tangled in the net and was struggling to get free. He tried to cut the net by biting it but the net was too strong. But he wasn't going to be stuck in the net for too long. The pigeons were following the little mouse and keeping an eye on him to make sure nothing goes wrong. And when they saw the small mouse trapped in the net, they rushed down and help him. They tried to cut the net but it was too strong for them too. The mouse first of all thanked them for coming to recue him, then he suggested that they can carry the net with him to somewhere safe. And so they decided to go with that plan. All the pigeons held the net with there claws and flew away with the net and the little mouse. When they reached the little mouse's burrow, they called Mister Tiger to cut the net so that the little mouse could be free. Mister tiger came and cut the net and to say thank you, the little mouse offered some of the delicious cheese, he had found, to everyone.
author: Aarav Singh

title: Diya and Deepu's Punyanagari Adventure!
text: "D for DUMB DEEPU, DEEPU," teased Diya! "I am not Dumb. And I hate you!" snarled back her brother Deepu. Yes, it was just another day, yet another day in the Dixit household. And Diya and Deepu were at it again; teasing and fighting! "Oh no," muttered Pincchu, "I'd better do something or else the whole day is going to be YAK YAK YAK again..." And Diya and Deepu stared at Pincchu in amazement. And no wonder, for Pincchu was their new pet pup!!! The pup was their special gift from their wise old Ajoba- G randpa..."And he was talking in English; yes the Dog was talking in Human Language!" Pincchu just stared back at them cockily, his tail wagging. Yes, the dog oops cat was out of the bag! Ajoba had warned him to be careful, but...Well,what could he do, except grin and bear it! "Bow bow...,"he tried, but surely he couldn't trick them now! And surely he was not one to keep a secret either. "Bow, listen now both of you are part of this big SECRET too! And if you keep your mouth zipped, you'll be duely rewarded..." Young Diya grinned back, "Secret, Wow BIG SECRET. Well the p roof of the pudding is in eating it. I'll believe you only when I see it; when I get the reward! " Pincchu wagged again,"Bow Bow, Diya tonight the MAGIC begins but ONLY if you two stop this racket! This is ' PINCCHU PROMISE!'" How Diya and Deepu waited for nightfall but time seemed to just CRAWLLL that day. Their A ai- Mum tugged them in bed at last. Pincchu too snuggled up in his doggy bed, hoping that the kids had fallen asleep. But in vain."Psssst... Pincchu," soon he heard a loud whisper. It was Diya of course! "Bow, bow," he replied. "No tricks Pincchu, remember your promise? Show us your MAGIC NOW!" "Miss, hop on my back. Tell me where you want to fly off to, and yes I will take you places!" snarled back Pincchu. "Oh sure and pigs will soon grow wings and fly! Besides you are just a pup. And soon you'll be a pup with a BROKEN back," laughed Diya. " TRY ME, Miss" barked Pincchu! When challenged, Diya sat on to his back hesitantly. AND to her amazement the back grew bigger in size, wider and longer! Of course, Deepu too clambered on. "Where to Miss?" woofed Pincchu quite pleased with himself now. "Really, you can really take us anywhere we want to go? REALLY??? Well, to Parvati Hill, the crown of our City, Pune!!! Let's see if you can really do that!" grinned back Diya. And to her amazement, Pincchu Plane just TOOK OFF. "HANG ON TIGHT for your maiden voyage," the pup yapped as they flew right out of the the window into the dark night. And Up, UP and UP they soared. Diya and Deepu stared, their eyes wide open in amazement. "Whooo..." screamed Deepu, excited as they passed through a huge cloud. He even tried to grab on to a dazzling star nearby. "Hey buddy, hang on," yapped Pincchu. "Be careful, that's Mischievous Maya. Believe me she can be quite a DRAMA QUEEN!" Deepu almost slipped off as Maya star grinned and winked right back at Pincchu! "Yippee YAAA, wow that's PARVATI HILL! Yes I can see it down there..." squealed Diya clapping! "Do you know how many steps we have to climb to reach the temples at the top of the hill, Pincchu?" asked Diya testily. "108 Miss Diya! And yes there are 5 temples at the top," yapped back Pincchu! "Diya look, we can also see the Peshwa museum down there. There are sooo many swords and old coins in the museum! And see, it looks almost like a palace next to the temple, doesn't it?" asked Deepu. "Yes Deepu, that's because it was actually built as a palace meant to be lived in, " said Pincchu. "But that's old news, that was yesterday. Today, the Parvati water tank down there, supplies water to HALF the city of Pune! That's quite special too. " Said Pinchchu. Deepu stared down in amazement with a "WHOOO..." "WHOOO! Is that SARASBAUG?" asked Deepu pointing to the greenery in the vicinity. "Yes, Deepu, that's our Talyatla Ganpati- Ganpati temple in the lake, indeed!" woofed Pincchu. "Oh we have visited the temple so many times with Ajoba, but today it looks so magical and mysterious. Look at the glittering water in the moat. I think it is chatting with the stars! Yes, teasing Maya Star! The moat looks so much bigger and deeper now, doesn't it?" "You know, Ajoba told me that once there really was a lake down there. And a small Ganesh temple stood in the middle of it. But it all dried up; so sad..." said Deepu. "AND Ajoba also told me that the Peshwas planned TACTICS against their enemies in boat rides in that very lake. Oh so EXCITING!" added Diya. "And is that Taljai hill down there? " asked Deepu pointing down to the lovely green hilly area nearby. "Yes, ofcourse Deepu.You guessed it right!" Woofed Pinchchu. "And you know there is also a BHOOT bangla, a ghost bunglow there just before the Taljai mata mandir - the goddess temple!" Exclaimed Deepu. " No way Jose, that's just Deepu talk." quipped Diya. " Miss scary boooo, oh soooo scared aren't youuuu," teased Deepu. And Diya turned to pinch Deepu at alarming speed.... "Hey hey, hang on Miss or you might just fall off my back. Hey Diya did you see peacocks up there when you visited? Do you know, the hills are home to LOTS and LOTS of peacocks? Many migratory birds come there too," yelped Pincchu in an attempt to calm Diya. "It is Punyanagari's photographer paradise!" "And also eating paradise, i simpy looove the bhel at the chowpatti there, " Diya closed her eyes, her mouth watering. "Oh Mr Whooo and Miss Me too, look at that amazing view. Time has simply flown by!" To their amazement night had crept away and dawn was just breaking out. They could see the first rays of the sun, well almost.The duo was dazzled by the sight; they gazed in amazement at the orange hue. A sight to behold indeed. It sure was a first for them! And a first for Pincchu too; Yes first time the dashing duo were silent, silently holding hands staring joyously at the MAGIC... Pincchu hated to break the silence. "Time to dash home kiddos, before your A ai comes to wake you up," he whispered. "But Pincchu we want to see so much MOREEE, and i want to choose now" wailed Deepu. "Please, please, please! Diya chose Parvati but i want to see so much more!" "Yes, yes there sure is soooo much more to explore, I agree. But that's for another day. And Next time you will choose Deepu. I promise. And that's Pincchu Promise..."
author: Rutuja Joshi

title: How the mouse got his year(from Kazakhstan)
text: The Year of the Sheep is the simplest for people, bringing the most happiness and the least burden. The Year of the Cow often brings difficult winters with merciless blizzards and snowstorms. A man who is born in the Year of the Dog is destined for an unforgiving life that will forever test his patience. Years of the Sheep, Horse, Cow, Snake, Snow Leopard, Chicken, Snail and Boar have their own signs and meanings too. But the first year belongs to the Mouse. Let us tell you the story of how the little Mouse got his year. For an endless amount of time, the animals found themselves fighting and arguing constantly over who should get the first year of the Eastern calendar named after them. Cow said, “I provide men with milk to drink, food to eat and pelt to keep warm. The first year rightfully belongs to me.” “Well, not only do I provide men with everything that you do, but I can carry men to faraway lands on my back,” replied Horse. “Poor Horse, you are so fragile,” challenged Camel. “How can your strength be compared to mine? Put half of my load on you, and you will fall and groan. You also live in idleness, when you are blessed with plenty of food. Your appetite is fed with good hay and oats, and your thirst quenched with spring water. Yet, I eat mere thorns and can survive without a single drop of water for several days on end. My milk is also very tasty, my meat is edible and my pelt is sturdy.” Pushing everyone aside, Sheep ran to the middle and declared, “From what wool would a Kazakh man make a felted cloth to cover their yurt? Why, a sheep’s wool of course! My wool can grace any man with a wonderful sheepskin coat. Take a hunk of a lamb and you have the best meal for yourself. The milk and cheese that comes from me is unique from any of yours. The first year should be mine.” For once, the animals couldn’t argue or deny what Sheep had said. Could he be right? Suddenly, Dog jumped into the middle of the animals’ huddle. “Nonsense!” Dog exclaimed. “If it weren’t for me, your precious wool would have been gobbled up by the wolves.” And in this futile fashion, the animals argued until the last rays of sunshine sank behind the mountains and the purple skies grew dark and filled with stars. As Cow, Horse, Camel, Sheep, Dog and even Rooster argued, Mouse did not make a single peep. Once the animals grew tired and silent, Mouse spoke up. “Whoever sees the sunrise first, shall get the first year of the Eastern calendar.” The animals were delighted, each one thinking they were guaranteed to be the first to see the sun. Camel had no doubt that his height would promise him victory in seeing the sunrise first. Mouse stood next to Camel as the animals gathered to face the East. Camel laughed. “Poor little foolish Mouse, you can’t possibly think you will be the first to see the sun,” Camel grinned. “Waiting one hour in the morning is better than waiting two hours in the evening,” Mouse responded. “Oh please,” Camel huffed. “I am the tallest of all and will be the absolute first to see the sunrise.” Before the dawn, the animals began looking into the distance. Camel could feel something tickling the top of his hump. “The sun! The sun!” Mouse shouted, pointing and jumping with excitement. Only then did Camel realise that Mouse had quietly climbed up his long hair to stand on his hump. Angry, Camel threw Mouse off his hump and squished him with his foot. Sly little Mouse escaped and slipped into a nearby pile of ashes. Mouse claimed the first year and Camel’s arrogant thoughtlessness lost him a year in the Eastern calendar. To this day, Camel continues rolling around in that same pile of ashes, hoping to trample over Mouse and get his year back.

title: Rani Finds A Friend
text: There was once a little girl called Rani. Her favourite toy was a big doll with a bright red dress and hair braided in two long plaits. She called this doll Missy. One day, Rani's parents took her to a picnic spot by a river with other family friends. One of these families, the Srivastavas, had a young daughter called Pritha. She was older than Rani by a few years. When Rani was telling stories to Missy by the river, Pritha came there and began to listen to it too. Rani had never shared her stories with anyone else before but Pritha was all ears for it! Her eyes grew large in amazement listening to it and a big smile lit up her face. “Do you like my story?” Rani asked, delighted! “Yes, yes, I love it!” replied Pritha, crossing her arms in front of her chest as if hugging something. Rani was very pleased with herself for this effect on her new friend! She began to tell her story more ardently and thoughtfully. Soon it was sunset and time for the evening snacks the families were planning to have there. By this time, the two girls were busy taking turns to build stories to tell Missy. They were in no mood to eat. Pritha thought of giving the food to Missy. She too didn't open her mouth to eat! “Rani, Missy isn’t eating because we aren’t!” said Pritha. “Oh!” said Rani, “what do we do now?” “Let us eat first and then she will eat too!” Pritha replied. So then the girls happily had some pakodas with chutney and watched the setting sun together. Once they were full, neither felt like talking. They sat there watching the river flow and the birds returning to their shelters, for some more time. “Burble, burble, burble!” said the river. Rani felt like floating away with the river to the lands of gods and goddesses. Her grandmother had told her many tales of them. “Chirp, chirp, chirp!” said the birds. Pritha secretly wished to fly like them! “Why do they sit on the trees?” she thought. “If ever I fly, I will reach for the sky!” Both little girls thought how beautiful it all was! Soon, the families packed up and the picnic was over. When Rani came home, she found two pebbles in her bag. Pritha had collected these at the riverbank saying she loved them and wanted to take them home! Pritha's mom called over phone to say Pritha was asking if her friend had found her special gift. Rani's mom informed her that her daughter was busy, happily making a card with crayons. Who do you think the card was for, reader?
author: Dona Wording

title: The Picnic
text: There once was a great family, which consisted of a mother, a baby and a girl...The mother's name was Rita and the girl's name was Fanny.The baby's name was Lucy.This family was going on a picnic today. They met another family soon which was also going on a picnic, which consisted of a father whose name was Jack and a baby whose name was Tina.They all went towards the picnic area.The babies giggling, because they couldn't talk.Rita told Lucy that they were nearing the picnic spot. Then they found the picnic spot, laid down the mat and put out the food.Soon few birds came to look at them and plead for food.Little Lucy offered them a toast.Rita and Fanny looked from the bird to Lucy, thinking what they would do. And then, as quick as lightning, one of the birds snatched the whole toast! Lucy was confused..In fact she did not even know what actually happened as the bird was so fast!She slowly went back to her spot on the mat.Now Fanny and Rita wondered what would happen.What do you think will happen? What happened was rather like any other bird.They chased each other for the bread down the hill they went.Fanny, Rita and Lucy just stared at the birds.Now everyone was staring, who in the end would get the bread? They ran up the hill too!The astounded faces just followed the birds.In fact it was so much of a thing that they had forgotten about the food!Lucy stared, Rita stared and Fanny stared hard at the birds Now the birds had run off with the toast, soon Lucy spotted another animal."No, don't give your toast to that animal we shall loose all the toast's here!" Fanny and Rita cried with their arms flailing in the air.Luckily Lucy listened to them. Finally they all rested and started eating...Muffins, juice, apples, milk, etc.They throughly enjoyed the picnic!Everybody was soon finished, so they started to head home But what they didn't know was...That in the crowd of birds they couldn't see a squirrel snatch the piece of toast in the end. And also that in the end when they were not looking the animal snatched the other piece of toast and ate it hungrily.
author: Syna Bhaware

title: Let's have fun!
text: I was bored. He was bored. She was bored. They were bored. EVERYONE WAS BORED!!! Even playing with a thread was fun. What could I do? I wanted ADVENTURES!!!! Like the last time, we went train hunting. Hmm... Didn't daddy say mommy knows everything? Let's ask her!!! Mommy said, "Look at the clouds there?" "Yes, mommy" I replied. "Go and see the shapes of the clouds. If you look closely enough, you may find butterflies and even candy!" replied mommy. "Yay, okay!" I exclaimed, thrilled. Seconds passed, minutes passed, 30 minutes passed and still I was only able to see fog. It was really foggy. Next stop, daddy! What will he say? "Read a book, Sophie.." is all he said. "What? You know that I hate books!" I replied. Daddy likes to read books a lot. "Then read E-books. You like your iPad, you may like books." he said. "Search on, books by Khushi Lalwani" he said, hanging the clothes. "Yes! She's my favorite author!" I said, electrified, she must have published a new book! Dad was happy to know that I liked books (at least a bit). I won't read an E-book now, I'll read a real book by her! Isn't dad a genius? I asked my big brother to read me a book by her called "To the dentist!", while I was cutting a piece of cloth trying to turn it into a perfect rectangle for my doll's blankie. Stars, triangles, cones, everything! But... It wasn't adventurous. I asked Cody (my big brother) what I could do. Although he was bigger, he was shorter than me. "We can play-pretend soldiers!" he said full of beans. '"Yea!" I replied.....And got bored soon. I went to my bedroom. Wow! I am in the clouds!!! A-and it has a cat, holding a scepter! With a fish on its back!?! And sweets were near him! And what's that? Is that pink toilet paper? Wow, the cloud's so fluffy! Wait, is it dissipating into thin air? AAAA! And I woke up. All a dream. Maybe I accidentally slept. I just played with Lenne, my cat. She's always having something over her head, like now. Why are you laughing? And after a while, I thought I could draw. I was not-so-good, not-so-bad... But got bored. This is what I drew. Maybe I could sew? And, oh wow! Again I started cutting, then started sewing. Mommy said I was great! Daddy said it was glorious! Cody said it was marvelous and read me my favorite book. Yay! It was so fun to sew! Even though it isn't adventurous, it's fun! And yes, mommy was with me while I was sewing as it's dangerous for kids. I found a new hobby! Word corner! title: How Big Is a Whale Shark?
text: How long is a whale shark? Longer than a giant grouper But shorter than a siphonophore. How heavy is a whale shark? Heavier than 100 common dolphins. But lighter than a humpback whale. How deep can a whale shark dive? Down to 2,000 metres, but not as deep as the Arabian Sea. How fast can a whale shark swim? Faster than Greenland sharks. But slower than a swordfish. How big is a whale shark? Smaller than a blue whale. But bigger than any other fish in the sea. Comparisons help us to make sense of the world. They help us size up the world around us. Here are some ways to compare Slower Faster Taller Tinier Heavier Larger

title: BORN TO STAND OUT
text: Once upon a time there was a boisterous little girl named Ella who was sometimes good, and sometimes bad-tempered. In fact trouble was synonymous to her. People in the village had almost accepted her for all her deeds and misdeeds as she had lost her mother at a very early age. Ella was the apple of her father’s eye. He meant the world to her. Now that her father had no work, she wanted to to step out and support her father. What a big dream for a little girl like her! "I will go out first and see what I can do?," said Ella emphatically., ever so cheerfully, oblivious of the harsh realities of the world she was stepping into. So she packed up a bundle, quietly bid goodbye to her father who was fast asleep unaware of the dangerous plans of his beloved daughter. She went farther afield into the country. And as she journeyed along her eyes fell on an old lamp rather very old and dirty lying on the street. She picked it up after a moment’s hesitation. ’ Have I got the lamp of Aladdin? pondered Ella. Will there be a genie for this lamp? She started rubbing the lamp vigorously waiting for the Genie to appear. But it was all in vain. This is just a useless lamp. I must throw it away. On second thoughts let me just keep it as a memoir. Ella had walked quite a distance. She was feeling rather hungry. She had reached the bank of a river. She could hear loud sobs.She looked around and saw Mrs Toady “ Ella. my baby son is missing. He has never been away for so long. I have searched around his favourite place.You must help me trace him said she in a croaking voice. Ella stepped back. The evil voice in her said out aloud. “Stop Ella. Why must you help find the baby of Mrs Toady?. It is none of your business. Ignore her and go ahead. The good voice then said Ella no you can’t run away. It is your duty to save Mrs Toady’s baby. She needs you now." Ella made up her mind to listen to the good voice in her. Without a moment’s delay she jumped into the river.At a distance she found the liitle tadpole gasping for breath. She picked him up and brought him to the bank and revived him back to life. Mrs Toady could not control her tears. She promised Ellla “If ever you need my help, just call out to me and I will be there for you. After a little while she heard a motorcycle pass by.The cops were in hot pursuit. Ella remembered it was none other than Cranky Monster on the loose. Cranky Monster was a dreaded criminal. She needed to act fast. The evil voice in her warned her ‘ Ella have you lost your mind? Why do you want to risk your life? Stay quiet, stay safe. The kind voice spoke” Ella you are a brave girl, Remember what father taught you, You must stop the criminal right now. You must be selfless.” Ella pulled out her catapult and took an aim at Cranky Monster. It was in no time that Cranky Monster was caught red handed by the cops. The cops were full of praise for the little,brave Ella. They handed a huge sum of money to Ella for helping the cops to catch the criminal.Ellla was taken home by the cops. Ella’s father was so relieved and happy to see his daughter safe and sound. He heard the adventures that Ella had on her way. Her father embraced her. His eyes were moist. He was proud of his daughter Ella’s father said” I am happy that Ella you paid heed to the good voice in you.This is your conscience that guides and shows the right path.This kindles the values of kindness, selflessness, courage grit and determination which you have shown through your actions. The entire village came to know of the brave deeds of Ella. From then on Ella always followed her conscience. The end.

title: Rathna and the Ring of Fire
text: Today is a day like no other. For one full minute, the sun will disappear behind the moon. There will be a thin ring of fire where a bright golden ball used to be. Today, there is a solar eclipse. Rathna is an astronomer at the planetarium. She and her friends are very excited about the solar eclipse. After all, it is a sight nobody should miss. Rathna knows many secrets of the universe. Like what happens when a billion-year-old star dies. And how the sun can disappear behind the moon. Rathna shows people the best views of stars, planets and distant galaxies. Sometimes through telescopes. Sometimes from her sky theatre, and sometimes from ancient observatories like the Jantar Mantar. Today, there are two hundred eclipse glasses on Rathna’s table. These glasses must be worn while looking at the ring of fire. Two hundred visitors head to the telescope and projection boxes to take a closer look at the sky and the sun hiding behind the moon. Soon the sun is out and Rathna has another surprise in store. She guides the visitors into a dark room with a domed roof. This is the sky theatre. This is where Rathna keeps a giant projector. Everyone leans back in their seats and looks up. The roof has turned into the night sky! She guides the visitors into a dark room with a domed roof. This is the sky theatre. This is where Rathna keeps a giant projector. Everyone leans back in their seats and looks up. The roof has turned into the night sky! Rathna will now take them on a journey through the universe. RATHNASREE NANDIVADA TIMELINE November 26, 1963: Rathnasree Nandivada is born in Hyderabad. 1992 -1996: Rathna gets a PhD for her research on the life cycle of binary stars from the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research in Mumbai. She works in laboratories across the world. 1996: Rathna joins the Nehru Planetarium in Delhi as a senior astronomy educator. 1999: Rathna becomes the director of the planetarium. 2000 onwards: Rathna works to restore the Jantar Mantar at Delhi and Jaipur and use them as open-air physics laboratories for students. 2014: Rathna becomes the chairperson for the Astronomical Society of India’s Public Outreach and Education Committee. May 9, 2021: Rathna passes away from COVID-19. This story is an account of a day in the life of Rathnasree Nandivada, who was the director of the Nehru Planetarium in Delhi.

title: Thia And The Naughty Rainbow Chameleon, Oscar
text: This is Thia. One day, while she was playing in the park, Thia saw something hiding in the bushes. It was an animal. A chameleon. She asked her parents if she could keep it. When they agreed, Thia was overjoyed. She named her pet chameleon, Oscar. But it was not easy for Thia to find Oscar as he camouflaged with the surrounding. So one day, Thia decided to colour him with crayons. So, on the first day, Thia coloured Oscar yellow. Now Thia thinks that Oscar has no place to hide because yellow is a bright colour. No! Oscar is clever and hides among the bananas! Thia looks everywhere but just cannot find Oscar. She looks for him the whole day! Yet, she could not find him. At last, she found him on the basket of bananas. The next day, Thia colours the chameleon orange. The next day, Thia coloured Oscar orange. Now she thought that she would be able to find him easily. The same thing happens once again. Oscar runs away, Thia looks for him the whole day, she finds him in the basket of oranges and colours him another colour the next day. The next day, Thia coloured Oscar red. You know what happened! Thia let Oscar go, and bamm! She couldn't find him! At last she found him in the basket of apples. Now Thia is very, very angry! Thia now colours her chameleon green. She thought that green was the only colour that would help her spot Oscar easily. Thia searched everywhere, but could not find Oscar. At last, she found him on a pile of pears! The next day she coloured Oscar bright blue, as blue as the oceans. Now were do you think Oscar hid this time? Hint: Oscar did not hide in any fruit baskets this time! Instead, he hid on a water painting in Thia's house! Thia looked in every fruit basket in her house, but she could not find her pet chameleon! Angry, Thia wanted to sit on her favourite pink chair by the painting, and she saw something stuck to the painting beside the chair. She touched it and saw Oscar trying to hide on the painting! So, next, she painted Oscar a beautiful violet colour. Now this was her last hope! Where was he hiding now? On the plate of violet grapes! Now Thia was out of hope. Just then, she got an idea for the next day! She coloured him with all the colours of the rainbow! Thia found out that Oscar would not be able to hide anymore, so she let him go any were in the house and out too. Because she knew that she would be able to catch him anytime! Oscar didn't mind much because Thia would never let him get hurt. So that is how, Thia and Oscar became good friends.

title: Cyber Space- Nila's learning space
text: Nila was a sweet and only child of Mr and Mrs Kannan. She was an obedient and studious child. She would always listen to her parents and her grandparents. Her grandparents lived with her family. They lived in a joint family. Since her aunt had very young kids, her grandparents often traveled to their native. It was monsoon time and rains were pouring. Since Nila could not go and play with her friends, she immediately logged into her system to start a chat. She called her friends and they started a discussion on the cartoons and movies that each of them had watched over the weekend. The conversation was going all good when Preeti said" Hey Nila, Why do you watch such stupid movies?”. You should be playing some interesting online games. It is so boring, we are not interested in your story. Nila got angry and felt embarrassed that all her friends were laughing. She decided to unfriend Preeti from the chat. After a few minutes, Nila realized that all the other friends had left the group chat. She stared at the computer. She imagined if Preeti was right in front of her, things would be so much easy. She was upset that she was the one who was left out. None of the other girls called Nila for the next two days to ask how she was doing. Nila's aunt had come home to drop her grandparents. She saw that Nila looked sad and lost. She asked, ”Nila, What's the matter?" Nila could no longer hold her tears and began to weep. She narrated the incident to her aunt. Her aunt then said, " Why don’t you apologize, they are your friends and will understand you and accept you". She rushed to the system and sent a message. Even after a long wait, she didn’t get a revert. Nila kept staring at the system when she noticed that her girl’s gang had included her in the group once again. She was very excited and she immediately joined the group. The next morning Nila met Preeti's elder sister on her way to the bus stop. She said that Preeti would not be able to come to school as she had a temperature. Preeti's sister then said, "Nila, I know what happened the other day in your group chat. You must have felt very humiliating and upset that you were removed from the group. "Nila, cyberspace is very dangerous. You can be mistaken easily, you had just pressed one unfriend button and you lost your friends. And I don’t want you to lose good friends Nila’s school bus had arrived, she got on the bus and was lost in her thoughts. She understood her mistake. She promised herself that never again she would be so impulsive and do something that hurts another person's feelings.

title: Dev's vacation at Mahabalipuram!
text: It is time for another adventure with Dev. He and his family are driving to Mahabalipuram to celebrate his father's 35th birthday! They start driving early in the morning listening to songs and eating their snacks. This is his second trip to Mahabalipuram. They reach the hotel and Dev loves his room! It has a lawn outside for him to play with his dinosaurs! He also loves jumping on the soft bed. Dev quickly changes his clothes. It was quite sunny, so they decide to eat their lunch. The uncle in the restaurant gave him free chocolates! Dev and his family then head to the beach. He holds his father's hands and runs to the water. He loves digging his feet in the sand when the waves come in. He also chased crabs. Dev and his mom built a sand castle with his beach toys. All three of them then played frisbee. Dev was fully drenched now. His Dada says, "Let's get more wet" and they run to the swimming pool. Dev's father knows how to swim well. They wade in the water, collecting flowers for his mother. Dev loves swimming with his father. They were exhausted by now. Dev and his family have dinner at a restaurant by the beach and walk under the stars. They then go to their room and fall fast asleep. Dev was super excited about his next day! The next morning, after a quick breakfast and a swim, Dev and his family head to a nearby crocodile park! This was Dev's favourite part of the vacation. There were so many crocodiles. Big ones, small ones, young ones, old ones. Some crocodiles sleeping with their mouths wide open. A few uncle and aunties were also cleaning a crocodile paddock. A brave uncle was keeping the crocodile at bay while the others cleaned. Dev also bought a wooden crocodile toy! Dev and his parents then went exploring the city. They went to temples, light house which was very scary, Arjuna caves, Krishna butter ball and had lunch at a tiny little shop. Dev's mama also bought a painting for their home. It was so hot, dev ended up eating two ice creams! They went back to the hotel and at dinner surprised Dada with a birthday cake and a birthday dinner. Dev went back to his room and played with his toys. He looks up at the stars in the sky wishing this vacation would never end!

title: Have You Ever Climbed a Tree?
text: I love trees. I love eating their fruits and smelling their flowers. And most of all, I love climbing them. I want to climb every different kind of tree in the world. I want to climb a jackfruit tree. It has a thick trunk for a good footing, and strong, sturdy branches to hold my weight. But I will need to watch out for falling fruit! I want to climb a chinar tree. In autumn, it glows with bright, red leaves, and becomes the best hiding place. But, in the winter, there are no leaves left to hide in. I want to climb a betelnut tree. Climbing would be easier if there were branches on the trunk. But I will take it as a challenge and hop, hop, hop to the top! I want to climb a moringa tree. It looks easy to climb, at least to me. But the trunk is so thin that the higher I climb, the more it will bend downwards. I want to climb a mangrove tree, with its spindly branches and giant, exposed roots. But to climb a mangrove tree, I will have to splash through muddy, crocodile-filled water first. I want to climb a khejri tree. It would be tricky to climb the many thin, thorny branches. But I will twist and dodge and avoid getting pricked. I can’t wait to climb trees all across the country. Can you name the different trees in the pictures and mark them on the map?

title: Mouse in the House
text: There was a mouse in the house. Grandma saw it first. "Mouse!" she screamed, jumping up the sofa. The cushions fell on the floor. “Where?” asked Pa, climbing up the window. He pulled the curtains down. “There!” shouted Ma, leaping up the table. The plates fell with a crash. Catch him!” said Mithun to the cat. The cat looked at the mouse and fled under the bed! “Mouse!” screamed Mithun, running behind the cat. I will chase it out!” said Ma bravely. She took out the broom and poked here and there. “Mouse!” shouted Pa. “Behind you!” Ma looked at the mouse, and fled under the bed! "I know what to do!" shouted Grandma jumping down from the sofa. She rolled up a newspaper and poked here and there. “Mouse!” yelled Pa, climbing the window even higher. “To your left!” Grandma looked at the mouse, and fled under the bed. “Oh no!” said Pa softly. He couldn’t go any higher. He climbed down carefully, and fled under the bed before the mouse could see him! "Mouse in the House!" shouted everyone together. That woke Baby up. She sat up on her mat, rubbing her eyes sleepily. What was that on her pillow? It had two eyes, four feet, and a long tail. "Mouse!" said Baby, clapping happily. Baby looked at the mouse, and the mouse fled, with Baby right behind him! Leaping up the sofa, climbing the window, jumping up the table, tumbling over the cushions.... running in between the curtains, scurrying over the plates, and out of the door!
author: Manisha Agarwal

title: Story of Forest Ecosystem
text: Once upon a time in a beautiful forest, there lived a deer. It was searching for food to eat. It found some plants and ate them. After some time, the deer heard some footsteps of an animal. It was frightened. The animal was walking on dry leaves and it jumped out of the bush. It was a tiger! ﻿Today you are my feast. Help! Tiger is chasing me. As soon as the deer seen the tiger, it ran away. The tiger chased it. They ran for a very long time but unfortunately, it was the deer's last day as the tiger pounced on it and ate the deer leaving some remaining parts. a few moments later, a group of vultures saw the remaining parts of the deer and started to eat it. Some more scavengers joined the feast. They were very happy eating the remaining parts. After finishing the remaining parts leaving the bone, they left the place. Today, the tiger left some parts for us. Let's invite some more animals This is how forest ecosystem goes that way. All the animals in that forest lived peacefully in that way.
author: Anwesha Mishra

title: Good things for me (tell me now )
text: I have to go to school everyday? This is good for you. Why do I have to bath everyday? This is good for you. Why should I not play in the sunlight? It is not for good for you. Why can't I wake up late? It is not good for you. Why should I sleep everyday? Your body needs rest. Why should I listen to you? You very well know why.
author: Deetya Poojari

title: Tara and the woods
text: It was evening, and Tara wanted to go and play in the woods, Amma warned her to be back by 7:30. But Tara did not stop to hear, she sprinted down the path into the woods. She climbed up a tree with the squirrels, challenging them to a race, Tok tok tok, katar, katar, Tara heard the noisy sounds of her friendly oak tree. The squirrels on the tree gathered by Tara, squeak, squeak, squeak, They sang in chorus around her. The winds lifted Tara's hair high. Tara climbed to the other side of the tree branch and sat there, observing the town. The cows were taken inside by their owners and the owls took flight into the oak. Tara was eager for adventure, sitting down on a tree branch was not enough for her!, She wanted to walk on the branches. She, with caution and seek of adventure, walked cautiously on the branch for her very first time. Then Tara climbed high, almost reaching the sky the squirrels joined her in the adventure as she looked up into the evening sky. It was time, almost time, she had only 30 more minutes to go, but " no I won't go I don't have school tomorrow what's the hurry? " she thought, and again climbed of the tree into the woods. Till the time she climbed down, It was dark, very dark and she knew it was going to get late, but again she did not care as she did not have to go to school. She stood up and talked to the leaves with a smile, after a while she waved goodbye and left for the hillside for the glimpse of the moon. Upon reaching, the wind did a low growl, and gushed with power. Tara stood there looking at the moon, and prayed that amma does not scold her. With that, she turns back towards home. Through the times she gets a squirrel in her hair and plays with it. When she reached home, she saw her mother standing at the front with a frown on her face, she pointed at her watch which showed the small needle on " 8". Her mother brought her inside bathed her, then ate dinner with her ma an pa, and then Tara slept still feeling like she slept in the trees..
author: Jiya G

title: The three friends
text: Once upon a time there were three best friends in a city. They loved to play with each other. they do almost everything together. One day, they were playing hide and seek, two children were hiding and the youngest was seeking. While finding he saw a bird and called out to his friends, both of them came out from its hiding place to see the bird. They were curious to see where its going. Lets go and hide. I am good at hiding I will find you soon With curiosity, the three friends went to follow the eagle. They were chasing after the eagle for a quite sometime. Two minutes later, they lost it. When looking where they are, the girl saw a black cat. Is it an eagle? I think it is going to North direction Lets follow it! Cat licking its fur It was hungry, the girl gave some milk. The cat saw a mouse and began chasing it. Frightened, the mouse ran away. The three friends also chased after the cat. Running, running and running, will this chase ever end! After running for a quite sometime, the cat lost the mouse and stopped. the exhausted friends also stopped and looked around and they saw the same eagle. It is a black cat. Lets help it. Cat is chasing the mouse Wait for us kitty. Oh No! Oh my! Eagle came to snatch the mouse! The eagle came to snatch the mouse, but the cat was fighting for the mouse. We should help them Well, the mouse escapes from both the cat and eagle and hid in its cozy hole. The eagle flew back to its nest and the three friends fed the black cat some milk and it becomes a pet for the youngest member. And they lived happily ever after. You can become my pet.
author: Anwesha Mishra

title: Gappu Cannot Dance
text: Komal is showing the students of grade 1A the dance steps for Wednesday's class play. Taka dhimi tai! "Lift your left hand up" Oh...Oh! Gappu lifts her left hand up. She doesn't know how to dance. De dana dan ghoom ghoom! "Run fast around the room". Oh...Oh! Gappu runs too slow. She doesn't know how to dance. Tap Tapa Tap Tap! Everyone jump up. Oh...Oh! Gappu sits down. She doesn't know how to dance. Dhin Dhinak Dhin Dhin! Put your right leg in. Oh...Oh! Gappu puts her right leg out. She doesn't know how to dance. Everyone laughs at Gappu and make fun of her as she doesn't know how to dance. Now, Ms. Komal knows what to do and tells the class "follow Gappu". Taka Dhimi Thai! Keep some hands low and some hands high. De dana dan ghoom ghoom! Run fast and slow around the room. Tap tapa tap tap! Jump as you wish. Dhon dhinak dhin dhin! Just make sure you dance too. Gappu can dance, along with you.
author: Shanmukh Teja Kota

title: Beauty is missing
text: Beauty was missing, and Jincy Jose, the new constable at Erumannoor police station… who immediately got down to work. “So, tell me about Beauty,” Jincy said. “Well, first things first, she is a beauty,” said Tessamma. Honk! Honk! Beeeep! “Honestly, she’s a traffic stopper. “While she’s being milked at dawn, she insists on listening to Western classicalmusic on her radio. “While she grazes, it’s always music from Bollywood. “ When she wallows in the pond — it’s her beauty regimen, you see — she prefers romantic Malayalam songs. “And at night, she always sleeps to soft instrumental tunes.” “What excellent taste in music,” thought Jincy. Jincy decided to go around the village and ask folks if they had seen Beauty. She ran into Thommachan, but he hadn’t seen Beauty. “Sorry, I don’t know any buffalo called Beauty and frankly, I don’t like buffaloes. I only like my cow Chandanakutty and she doesn’t wallow in the mud like those buffaloes.” he then met the sisters Remani and Savithri, who were on their way back from the local pond. They hadn’t seen Beauty either “I have told Tessamma a hundred times not to let Beauty walk around without a noose.” said Remani. “What’s the harm in giving her a few whacks with a stick? But no, Beauty’s skin is too sensitive it seems. Hmph! Anyway, who would steal that useless Buffalo?” “Hee-hee,” giggled Savithri. “If she were a pretty cow, I would steal her.” A little ahead, Jincy ran into a man who seemed to be repairing his truck and making a big noise. There was loud music playing from his truck. Jincy shouted, “Excuse me, have you seen a beautiful black buffalo wandering around here?” “Why’re you asking me? I’m new here. I’m just repairing my truck. My truck is full of jackfruit. And those buffaloes are such social animals. She must be busy socializing with friends. Anyway, like I said, why would I know anything about a buffalo who listens to the radio? It might rain today. Do you think it will rain today? I think so.” J incy went on ahead Jincy cycled all around Erumannoor with very little luck. “Sorry, haven’t seen any buffaloes.” “Disappeared in the middle of the night? She’s probably been sold off at the meat market already.” “Maybe she just decided to run away?” “Beauty? My daughter’s name is also Beauty! “How will you find her when you can’t make out one buffalo from another?” Dulquar Ikka had not seen Beauty, either, but he let Jincy stick a poster about Beauty at his tea stall. Jincy was tired. Bzzzt...bzzzt... bzzz...squwaack... psheww! Just then... BRAAAAANG!! Jincy had a brainwav e! She ran back to Beauty's shed. Beauty, of course, was missing. But so was something else. That night, Jincy ventured out to set some things right. In the darkness of the truck, something other than the fireflies was shining. SCHSSSHEW Jincy had found Beauty! Shaji Kuttappan, Beauty’s kidnapper, was promptly marched off to the police station. “How did you figure it out, Jincy?” asked Tessamma. “It’s simple. Shaji said he hadn’t seen a buffalo who listens to the radio. I never told him about Beauty listening to the radio. Shaji stole Beauty so that he could sell her off in the next village at a butcher’s. But things hadn’t really gone according to his plan.” Shaji had tried hard to get Beauty out of her shed. But Beauty refused to move. So Shaji thought he might as well take the radio. To his happy surprise, Beauty couldn’t imagine being without her radio. So she followed him into his hideout — his truck, which was under repair. Tessamma was thrilled to have her beloved Beauty back. “I must say,” said Inspector Gopi, “Beauty is indeed a beauty.” Beauty and O ther B uffaloes Buffaloes are highly intelligent animals who love socializing with others of their kind. They're often found wallowing in mud or taking dust baths in order to protect their sensitive skin from sunburn and insects that bite. They enjoy grazing and being outdoors. Research shows that buffaloes also like listening to slow music. It helps alleviate stress and relaxes them.
author: Josvanth Krethik

title: Child Perspective
text: Monday, October, 2021.. I heard our bedroom door being opened. I did not bother at all.. Cause I knew it was mummy who came in to wake my akka, Sam. While Sam akka wakes u p early, I will wake up only by 10. On Sundays, both of us will wake up only by 9:00 am After a few minutes, I heard Appa, waking me up. What? My time to wake u p is 10 and Appa is waking me up early? Does he dare to change my routine? I woke up with a long face. As I walked out, Akka came to me, hugged me and Said - " Good Morning Cheeky little piggy ". At times, when she says I'm a cheeky little piggy I would get irritated... The only thing I'll do is beat her on her forehead. Then she will shout and give me a good whack on my bottom. I walked to the hall and Saw Amma working. So, Appa did wake me on the correct time. Amma always starts working by 9 in the morning. I love sitting on the sofa behind someone. That's not all, I'll play with their hair!! I love being squished.. When I do that, Amma gets angry and calls out to Akka. She would Rush out, then show me my favorite toys and distract me. When I Said " Toys " You will think I'll play with fluffy toys... Not Really.. I'll play with the kitchen vessels. I love pretend cooking.. Most of all I love the mixer. When Amma or A p pa is cooking something, I'll too get a vessel and pretend to cook like them. Eating Breakfast is such a boring thing. Akka will come and feed me my Idli's and Dosa 's. I never listen to her.. Some days, She gives me a dirty look. I never bother. The only way to make me eat is by giving me my I pad. Baths are somewhat okay. But I hate hair baths. Because the sham poo (A thing which is like soa p but is in liquid form) gets into my eyes Then, comes my favorite or maybe the most favorite time of the day!! Can you guess what is done at that time?? Of course!! Reading books!!! I used to read Sam Akka's To p 10 of Everything books. Some days The set of 5 encycleo peadias (Which was bought for Sam Akka when she was studying LKG). And the other days " The Go pi Dairies ". I don't really read, I would see the pictures and guess the scene Lets ski p a few hours and move into my slee ping time in the afternoon. Either Amma or A p pa used to send me to slee p. That's when Sam Akka used to write the classworks, Read Books, practice music, Revise the portions taught (Academics and Grammar) and more things which are lots of fun. S peaking of Music, I'll tell you what will ha p pen during bed time (at Night)... Sam Akka and I, would pretend to be Royalty. Then, Akka will sing 1 song a day. Do you know my most favorite songs??? they're from animation movies.. And those are - Let it go (From Frozen), How far I'll go (From Moana) Remember Me (From COCO) and All is found (From Frozen II). Hey!! I'm not a girl, I'm a 2 years Boy baby. I know you're thinking that I'm a Girl because I like All is found, Let it go and How far I'll go. I like these because the first time I heard them I liked them. Sam Akka would sing those songs before going to bed. That's why I love them.. In the evening, Mummy would give us corn / channa. Then, coffee. After that, we would watch some cartoons. They're - pe p pa pig, Masha and the Bear and Butter bean's cafe. Each of my favorite cartoons have their own beauty. I love pe p pa pig because the pig family is similar to ours.. Which means, I'm George pig and Akka is pe p pa pig! Funny!! Masha and the bear is among my most favorite, because I like the kids in it which includes Masha, Dasha, panda and penguin. And I like the song " C'mon Everybody lets get cooking ". So, I like Butter beans cafe. After Dinner, Bed time. Not before hearing a song and pretending to be Royalty. I'm Glad that I have a beautiful family. Thank you for Reading the book about me!!!
author: Shyamala Ramkumhar

title: Our Aspirations
text: It is a sunny day. Chutki is going to school in Lalu Chacha’s truck. Pinku is trekking up the same hill. ‘Thudddd!’ falls Pinku, slipping on the gobar. ‘Hahahaha’ laughs Chutki. Pinku frowns at Chutki. She always laughs at him. He goes to Anuj’s house to clean the gobar. ‘What happened?’ Anuj asks. ‘I slipped on some gobar,’ replies Pinku. ‘But why are you angry?’ ‘Chutki saw me slipping, she will tell it to the entire class now.’ ‘Don’t worry, I won’t laugh. I will also talk to Chutki about this,’ said Anuj. 'Thank you Anuj you’re very kind,’ said Pinku smiling at his friend. 'Now let’s go to school we are late,’ said Anuj picking up his bag. They stop at Charu Chachi’s little shop to buy tiny toffees. When they reach the bridge, goats block their way. Pinku plucks some mangoes from the huge mango tree. ‘Nom Nom!’ They say eating the juicy mangoes. The goats have left. Now they are more late to school. They run from one side of the bridge to another. Finally! They reach their school in Lakshpur. They slowly enter their class and sit behind everyone. On the blackboard Pinku sees a big English word, ‘A-S-P-I-R-A-T-I-O-N-S.’ Pinku scratches his head and wonders what does it mean? Aashi Madam asks, ‘What do you want to do when you grow up?’ ‘I want to write poems for children!’ says Chutki. ‘I want a big shop in Rishikesh,’ says Pinku proudly. ‘I want to be a Gram Pradhan and and take care of my village,’ says Sonam. ‘I want to be a tour guide and tell people about the beautiful places,’ says Anuj. ‘Wow! All of you have different aspirations,’ says Aashi Madam. ‘Madamji so this ‘aaz-peee-ra-tionns’ are dreams?’ asks Anuj. ‘Correct, Anuj. Now let’s go outside,’ says Aashi Madam. ‘Yayy!’ exclaimed the kids. In the middle of the school ground there was Pali Peepal. They all stand under the tree. ‘Do you think trees have dreams?’ she asked them. ‘No, how can trees have dreams they can’t think,’ said Chutki. ‘Maybe Pali Peepal wants to cover the entire school courtyard with its shadow,’ said Pinku. ‘Do you think it can achieve this dream?’ asks Aashi Madam. ‘Yes, it can,’ said Sonam. ‘What will it need to grow tall?’ ‘Sunlight, rain and soil,’ replied the children. ‘Hmm… is that all?’ asked Aashi Madam. Chutki looked up at the big tree and saw a sparrow’s nest. ‘Madamji it will also need birds!’ she exclaimed. ‘Very good Chutki, what will the birds do?’ ‘They will dance, play and sing songs for the tree,’ said Sonam. ‘What do we learn about Pali Peepal?’ asks Aashi Madam. ‘Pali Peepal needs sun, rain, soil and birds to achieve its dreams’ said Chutki smiling.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: The Plant Whisperer
text: Jaishree, a young engineering student, looked at her noisy machines. “Aiyyooo! So frustrating,” she thought. Beep-Beep Beep Grrrrr Grrrrr Grrrrr Brrrrr Brrrrr Brrrrr She missed Paati’s garden. The garden had birds. Trees. Plants. Grass. Best of all, the garden had... Treeni, her best friend. Treeni’s branches were like arms, on which she climbed and played and slept. Jaishree called her father. “Daddy, I am going to study plants.” Humphh! Daddy was an engineer and didn’t like it. “I can convince him later,” Jaishree thought. She moved to a college to study plants. And study she did. She finished two degrees in five years. “But there are SO MANY questions that I do not have answers to.” Do plants listen to each other? Do plants talk to each other? Do they fight? Can they be friends with each other, like Treeni was mine? Jaishree went many places in search of answers. From New Delhi she went to New York and back to New Delhi. Sadly, the answers were nowhere to be found. Until she went to France. That was where she heard a story. A lonely mustard plant could not grow properly under stress. It was small, sick and sad when the temperature was too high or too low, or when the light was too bright or too dim, or when the soil was too sandy. But when the mustard plant had a friend nearby — another mustard plant — they both grew tall, green and happy. The mustard plants were helping each other! Alone, they were weak. Together, strong. They helped each other, like Treeni helped little birds and squirrels. They protected each other, like Treeni protected younger plants from harsh sunlight. But Jaishree still had more questions than answers! Why do plants help each other? How do plants help each other? Jaishree thought and thought and thought. She read and read and read. She spoke to people, helpful and unhelpful, but NOBODY had answers. Luckily for Jaishree, mustard plants were fun to work with. Growing them was not difficult, and she needed only one simple tool. A paperclip! Jaishree used a paperclip to sow 4,000 tiny seeds, one at a time. She did this whole exercise many, many, many times. But she didn’t get all the answers all the time. She failed and failed and failed. She failed 21 TIMES! Jaishree had more worries. Humans are not always as helpful as mustard plants. She was often told wrong and unkind things. “Women cannot do science.” “Indians cannot do science.” “STOP BUGGING ME,” Jaishree thought. And she carried on with her work. Finally, Jaishree succeeded. “Oh yes, I have found it!” She found that plants helped each other all the time. She found that some mustard plants helped only similar mustard plants. Other mustard plants helped mustard plants that were not so similar. As Jaishree knew, exciting answers always lead to more questions! “That’s curious. Why would some plants do one thing and others do something else? Why can’t all plants help each other in the same way?” She found that plants which grew with strangers learnt to help those strangers. This behaviour is shaped over many many years by another curious thing called evolution. Jaishree thought, “Imagine if we could find out which seeds to grow together so that they help each other. Wouldn’t that be fantastic? “We could produce so many seeds in so little time with much less money!” But what seeds grow together? How should they be grown? Then, there are other questions too. Are plants smart? How smart are they? Jaishree is on a journey to find these answers. In the meanwhile, she learns every day from her helpful plants. “If only humans helped each other more, the world would be such a wonderful place!” What did YOU learn from plants today? Do you know H Jaishree Subrahmaniam? Dr H Jaishree Subrahmaniam has loved plants since her childhood in New Delhi. She quit an engineering degree to study botany. In 2017, Jaishree started her PhD in France. Her research focused on altruism in plants. Using mustard plants (Arabidopsis thaliana), Jaishree discovered that plants help each other grow better in times of stress. Her research also explained that plants that have grown around “strangers” for millions of years have learnt to extend help to them, while other plants only help plants that are similar to them. In 2021, Jaishree was selected for the prestigious Marie Curie Fellowship (named after a very important woman scientist) to pursue her postdoctoral research. She will attempt to find out whether plants can be considered intelligent or smart. This journey, however, was not easy. Jaishree had to face racism and sexism many times at work, but her undeterred motivation kept her going. She is actively involved in taking science outside laboratories to anyone and everyone. She is also a social worker, helping create an equitable and welcoming space in science for women. She believes humans have a lot to learn from plants, especially how to extend help in times of stress without being selfish.
author: Sayantan Datta

title: Where is Bhuri Bakri?
text: It was a rainy Sunday morning in Sirasu. Chutki was cooking with her Mummy. She cut some onions and tomatoes. She was cutting some potatoes when she heard some sounds from outside. ‘Mehhh! Mehhh!’ screamed her goats as they ran in different directions. The sound of thunder scared Chutki’s goats. They ran in different directions. Chutki kept the knife and ran to catch the goats. She had thirteen goats, 5 white, 4 black and 4 brown. She found three goats under the Neem tree. Two goats outside Pinku’s house. Four running in the jungle. Three more in Lalu Chacha’s field. She brought them back to the house. She counted the goats. There were 5 white goats, 4 black goats and 3 brown goats. She looked carefully at the brown goats. ‘Oh no Bhuri Bakri is missing!’ Bhuri Bakri was one month old. She runs very fast and eats grass. She is small and scared of thunder. How will Chutki find her? Chutki was crying now. Sonam was passing by and asked Chutki what had happened. Chutki told her Bhuri Bakri was lost. Sonam hugged Chutki. ‘Don’t be sad Chutki, I will call all the kids from the village and we will help you find Bhuri,’ said Sonam. In ten minutes all the children were out except for Pinku. Pinku was still angry at Chutki. All the children looked everywhere in the jungle but could not find her. Pinku was going to the tank to drink water. He heard some noises. He went close to look. He found Bhuri Bakri. ‘Here you are Bhuri!’ Pinku was happy to find Bhuri. He once lost his dog Muttu like this, he knew how sad Chutki must be. He picked Bhuri up and went to Chutki’s house. Chutki was crying all day. When she saw Bhuri Bakri she became very happy. All the children sat around Bhuri and clapped. ‘Thank you Pinku for finding Bhuri. I am sorry I laughed at you when you fell,’ said Chutki, giving Pinku a big smile. ‘You’re welcome,’ said Pinku forgiving Chutki. Anuj asked Chutki, ‘How did Bhuri run away?’ ‘The shed door is broken. The goats were scared of thunder so they ran away.’ ‘We can fix the door,’ said Sonam. Everyone said yes. ‘I can get some wood,’ said Anuj. ‘I can borrow Pappa’s hammer,’ said Pinku. ‘I will get a latch,’ said Sonam. ‘I have some nails and screws,’ said Chutki. Next day they all met outside Chutki’s shed. They worked together and made the new door. The new door closed perfectly and the goats could not come out. ‘Thank you friends for coming together and helping me. Now Bhuri Bakri and all the other goats are safe,’ said Chutki. They were all happy with their work. Bhuri Bakri jumped happily around them and smiled at them.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: Bedtime by granny
text: BEDTIME!!! Best time! Seeing the sky, Hearing the bells chime. And seeing the mother bird flutter-fly. Listening to granny's story tonight. About princesses, mountains and hills. About the soldiers who fight! And about villages and mills. That's all about a good story night! This story is written by Kavya C Nair.
author: Kavya C

title: The foot story
text: On a sunny morning, Raghu and Grandpa were sitting and having tender coconut on the beach. (Lets now imagine a conversation between Raghu and Grandpa's foot) Raghu's foot: " Ah, an ant is biting you. Why don't you cover yourself in a shoe, you look so bare and rugged?" Grandpa's foot: " Well, I can survive without shoes too and shooed the ant away" Raghu's foot: My feet are like a butterfly, soft and tender. Grandpa's foot: Sure. Can you describe what is the most excited thing you walked on? Raghu's foot: Oh! The soft couch and the tiles of the house, any other time I am covered in a shoe. Grandpa's foot: Unable to breathe, tucked inside a shoe, you have not lived a free life. Grandpa's foot: I have walked the fields, beaches and hills. I touched the riverbed and laid my leg in puddles and thorns too. I have seen the world and thus despite being rough, I can walk through any situation because I am strong. Raghu's foot: Wow, I want to become like you someday. Can I? Grandpa: Off course, you can. Get rid of your shoes now and feel the sand beneath you. (Raghu obliged happily and they started walking in the beach barefoot) Grandpa's foot: I am so glad, aren't your footprints beautiful? Raghu's foot: Yay Yay Yay, free and beautiful. Moral: Living closely with nature is bliss
author: Sahitya Billuri
illustrator: Dr. Sushama Khurde; Sam  van Riet; Siddhi   Vartak; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Wiehan de Jager

title: Oceanic Pollution
text: . In the depths of the beautiful northern Pacific Ocean there were two lovely fishes Joe and Nemo. The hated their home. It was so polluted and full of some dirty material. They wanted to move to some other ocean. Their parents unfortunately died a few days ago due to that dirty material. They got tangled in it and suffocated to death. Not only their parents but many of their friends and relatives died due to that dirty material. Some died by consuming it and others died by getting trampled by it. Nemo and Joe wanted to investigate. The wanted to go to the surface of the ocean and see who was responsible for this pollution but they were scared to go alone so they asked their friends the mermaid and the whale to accompany them. Both of them happily agreed. So Nemo, Joe and their friends mermaid whose name was Alice and the Whale whose name was Recker(known for losing his temper) started their journey. Once they reached the surface they found out that humans were throwing the dirty material into their home. They were shocked. The respected humans till now but it seems like they dont deserve our respect. Humans were responsible for their loved ones' death! They tried to shout at them and say not to throw dirty stuff in their home. How would humans feel if they threw dirty stuff in their home. Their voices were too low to be audible to the humans. They told Recker to tell the humans not to throw dirty stuff in their precious home. He immediately shouted DONT THROW THIS DIRTY STUFF INTO OUR OCEAN. Nemo said not that loud Recker! His shout was so loud that the avengers who were nearby heard it and immediately came to the ocean to see what was up. Then the fishes told the Avengers everything about the dirty material, their parents and other loved one's death. Then Iron Man told that he would make a chemical today that would clean the ocean and come back tomorrow. The fish, mermaid and the whale were so ecstatic. Tomorrow their home would be clean again. Yay!!! They happily returned to the depths and told their remaining friends and relatives about Iron Man. They would not believe it. Then Nemo said "Fine see for yourself tomorrow" The next day Iron Man came and put the chemical into the ocean. The ocean immediately became clean. title: Chomp, Gulp... Burp!
text: Our body needs food to live, move and grow. It breaks food into small pieces that can be swallowed. This is called ingestion. It then removes waste bits and sends the useful parts of the food into the bloodstream. This process is called digestion. The animal world has bodies of all sorts, and each species ingests and digests food in its own way. Some sip their food right up. Mosquito Bee Butterfly Some splash it first, then… slurp! Spider Fly Some swallow their food whole. Bird Whale Octopus Some chew before they swallow. Some swallow first, then chew. Monkey Bear Human Cat Giraffe Goat Yak Cow Some squeeeeze and then… gulp! Boa constrictor Some have one stomach. Some have two. Elephant Some have none. Jellyfish Trichoplax Some digest food quickly. Some work slowly. Lion Mouse Some are even s-l-o-w-e-r… Sloth and some are very fast. Shark Which one is the strongest? Burp! Crocodile Butterflies, bees and mosquitos only drink liquid food. Spiders splash their prey with special juices that dissolve their bodies, making them easier to digest. Some birds swallow small stones that help grind food down in a part of their stomachs. Boas and pythons swallow their prey whole. Then their bodies secrete juices that digest the food completely. Bees have two stomachs — one to digest food and one to store nectar in. Meat is digested faster than plant fibre. That is why lions digest food faster than mice. Chew, Swallow, Burp! Cows have four chambers in their stomachs to help them store food. The food is then brought back up for chewing. Goats and horses have three chambers in their stomachs in which food collects and ferments. Sloths have three chambers in their stomachs too, and can take up to two weeks to digest a meal of leaves. Sharks have very strong stomach acids and enzymes that speedily dissolve the food they eat. Crocodiles have a unique combination of strong teeth, powerful stomach juices and stones that they ingest to grind food in their stomachs.

title: Life in a City Pond
text: I came to the City of Pune. It was night and I was awake in my new house. I heard frogs croaking loudly. In the morning, I was standing on the balcony. I was able to see the pond from where the sounds must have come. Over the next year, in the summer, the pond was dry. But when the rains came, the pond became full of water. Blue and green colours were in and around the pond. The chocolate brown rods of the Typha plant danced in the wind. Hey, the kingfisher has found a fish in the pond. Baya weavers made their nests. Scaly-breasted munias sat on the reeds. A pair of lapwings protected their nests. Flapshell turtles lazed on the banks. The spot-billed ducks swam in the pond. They searched for snails to eat. Dragonflies, butterflies, and damselflies flew above the pond. Mongooses ran near the pond. If a mongoose is there, can a snake be far behind? A water snake looked around. Who made all the deafening noise in the night? The hundreds of frogs and toads and crickets. The owls rested on the trees. The Indian Night Jar sat on the ground and looked around. One day, I got the scare of my life! Some people walked around the Flapshell Pond. It looked like they were surveying the area. I found out from my neighbours that they planned to drain the wetland and make buildings on it! My heart sank. I could not let this happen. A friend and I mobilized the neighbourhood kids. We invited a couple of press reporters. The next day, the newspapers carried news of the children’s appeal. Other residents of the area also started calling up various officials to tell them to save the pond. Then a couple of environmental organizations joined in. We invited the city commissioner too. At first, he was not convinced, but when he experienced the monsoon magic, he realized it would be a shame to destroy the pond. Finally, people cancelled the idea of constructing buildings over the pond. The pond was declared off-limits to any construction. The pond was a beautiful place. It enriched the lives of many birds, animals, and insects. Save a Pond! Is a pond near your house threatened by construction or pollution? If it is, can you join with your friends and parents and their friends, and tell everyone that you want it saved? And if people who want to build on it ask why you want it saved? A simple answer: because birds and insects and other animals also need a home to stay in! If you saved a pond, share photos and news about it on social media. It could encourage others to save a pond too!
