title: Mina Makes a Dash
text: Mina hates running during PT class. Every day, when Uma Miss makes the class run around the playground, she has a new excuse. “My ankle hurts.” “My stomach aches.” “I think I saw a snake!” Uma Miss blows her whistle. BVEET! BVEEET! BVEEEET! Time to head back inside. “Don’t forget, Sports Day is in a month! All of you have t o take part in the 400-metre r ace,” says Uma Miss. Mina remembers the last Sports Day. She had run super fast and almost reached the finish line before she fell. Everyone laughed. That’s why she hates running in front of other people. “Just practise, Mina!” says Zora. The next day, Mina goes to school early. She doesn’t want anyone to watch her practise and laugh at her. The playground looks so big and empty. There’s so much space to run. How far is 400 metres? So she asks Uma Miss. “Two loops of the playground is 400 metres,” Uma Miss explains. “Two rounds? That doesn’t sound too bad,” Mina says. Mina starts near the playground gate. She runs past the big Gulmohar tree. She’s almost at the bench. This is harder than she thought. She trips and catches herself. Phew! She’s made it halfway. How far is that? One round is 200 metres, so I’ve done 100 metres, she thinks. The next week, Zora comes with her. When she shouts, “READY! STEADY! GO!” Mina runs as fast as she can. She dashes past the big tree, the bench, and the water cooler. She stops at the gate and leans against it, sweating. “200 metres!” says Zora. Mina is thrilled. She only trips twice on the way to class. Mina is determined to run two loops of the playground by the end of week three. Sports Day is only a week away! She starts to run. Big tree. Bench. Water cooler. Gate. Big tree. Bench... Uff, this is hard. “350 metres!” says Aran. “You’re getting closer!” Sports Day is tomorrow. Aran, Zora and Anna are waiting for Mina at the playground. “You can do this!” Anna says. Mina runs as fast as she can. She dashes past the big tree, the bench, the water cooler, the gate. She stumbles, but keeps going. She’s almost at the gate, and... “400 METRES!” shouts Aran. “Now you just need to do this tomorrow,” Zora says. “Without tripping,” adds Aran. Mina laughs. She knows she is now ready for the race tomorrow. She only trips once on her way to class. She hardly notices it. People all over the world use metres to understand and communicate distances. A metre is a standard unit of measurement. We use metres to measure distance, which includes height and width. 100 centimetres make 1 metre. 1000 metres make 1 kilometre.

title: Forest Ecosystem Story
text: Once upon a time, there was a big and beautiful forest which had many animals and birds in it. Everyone lived there in harmony, except a lion, who was very selfish and called him the King of the Jungle. He wanted everyone to listen to him. A few days later, everything was going well. The plants were absorbing nourishment by the nutrients produced by decomposers which went into the soil, herbivores like deer were eating plants, carnivores like jaguars were eating deer, and scavengers such as vultures were eating dead organisms such as the dead deer. Though everything was going well, an idea struck the selfish lion. He decided that he has the right to be the King of the Jungle and everyone should listen to him. He climbed a large rock and made the loudest roar ever. All the animals gathered there to see what was happening. The lion announced that he is now the King of the Jungle, and everyone must listen to him. The animal crowd started talking. Suddenly, a rabbit shouted, “No! You have no right to be the King! We can live on our own without any orders.” The lion replied, “If you do not agree with me, then I will eat you. I’m already very hungry. The rabbit looked to the left, then to the right. Everyone was staring at him and talking. The rabbit had no choice. He agreed. A few days later, the animals decided to talk about this. But before they could talk, the lion came, and everyone ran away. The lion was making people come to him so that he can have food. He made all the animals work for his welfare. He made animals to do various things for him. A group of zebras was grazing. They decided to talk about the lion because they could camouflage, and the lion will not be able to understand that where one zebra starts from and where it ends. One zebra said, “What shall we do about this?” The other replied, “Hmmm… I think we should take the advice of the smart fox.” Another said, “What if the lion sees us talking about him?” Then another said, “We can cover the wise fox. He will be in the middle of our group.” And so was done. The fox came into their group to talk. The lion was sleeping at that time. The fox advised, “We all live in an ecosystem and are dependent on each other. The lion is making the mistake to be the King. I recommend that you make all the animals move to another place, far away from the lion. Leave the plant matter and dead animals there.” One zebra questioned, “What would happen from this?” The fox replied, “The lion is carnivorous. He will not eat plants or dead matter. When you all are gone, he would not get food.” And the zebras told all the animals about this, and they started moving away. But there was a problem. There was a monkey near the lion. He had to entertain him when he wakes up. One zebra was going there to inform the monkey, but the lion was sleeping. If the zebra made any noise, the lion would wake up. The zebra had no choice other than to go away. All the animals except the monkey left the place. Soon the lion woke up. He was hungry. He saw the monkey. He said, “Hey monkey! I want food! Get it from somewhere!” The monkey said, “I had to entertain you right now. And I do not know how to hunt.” The lion said, “Then call any animal here!” And the monkey searched the whole forest but could not find any animal. The lion was very hungry by now. He decided to search the forest by himself. He tried but failed. He was guilty of his own actions. He realized that the animals in an ecosystem do not need to be ruled to live. He also realized that being selfish is bad. He, being tired, came on top of the large rock he stood on before, and made a loud roar. The animals heard it, and thought that the lion was very hungry and was going to hunt them. They decided to move back in fear that the lion must be sprinting towards them. They came back to the large rock and spot the lion. The animals thought that the lion was going to hunt them, but something else happened. The lion said, “Friends, I am sorry. You do not need to be ruled. From now on, you all are independent.” The animals were surprised, but happy. They all started living happily again.

title: Marine ecosystem-little fish pleko!
text: Once upon a time, there lived a small fish named pleko he was probably as small as half of your thumb, he wanted to know how the ocean works. So pleko went to his uncle deeko, pleko said "uncle, I want to explore the ocean and see how it works" his uncle said "go to calm cave and you will find the great clamomamo the clam, he is a wizard" So pleko went to clamomamo and said "Oh great wizard I want to see and understand how the marine world works" so clamomamo said "small fish, take this bubble and get comfortable in it, to understand the ocean you will have to get eaten and understand the food chain,this bubble will protect you from getting hurt. And then clamomamo gave pleko a piece of seaweed, he said "little fish, this piece of seaweed will help light up your area" so pleko said thank you and started exploring. Suddenly, pleko saw a shadow above him, when he looked up he saw a huge piece of kelp, it was the producer, he saw a sea snail nibbling on the kelp, this was the primary consumer, he then saw a tiny dot becoming bigger and bigger, then he realised that it was some big fish, specifically a grouper. The grouper ate the sea snail, as it was the secondary consumer,and it also swallowed pleko, then, pleko found himself in the grouper’stomach, he was safe because of the bubble, the seaweed illuminated the place then, when the grouper was sneezing, pleko quickly swam out. So pleko quietly followed the grouper as he thought it would lead him to another adventure, Then, after a few minutes, he saw a sea lion, this was a tertiary consumer,it swallowed pleko and the grouper,pleko found himself in the seal’s stomach,like before, the bubble protected him and the seaweed lit up the area. Then pleko swam out of the seal’s mouth and held on to it's back,thinking he would find another adventure, then he saw a quaternary apex consumer, an orca, it wrestled the seal and pleko quickly hid behind coral and watched,and the orca ate the seal and swam away, then pleko found himself in familiar surroundings. IT WAS HOME!!pleko quickly swam to his home and told his family "now I know how the ocean works, one creature eats the other and maintains balances even one tiny change can affect the whole process, and I guess that the name for this chain is the “food chain” "

title: Save the forest!

Kalia knew it was a good idea. So, when the moon showered its magnificent light on the forest, Kalia took pictures of a couple of foxes and even a picture of a night loris. The night was indeed magnificent. ﻿But while taking a picture, he saw some mysterious men holding razor-sharp spears. " ﻿ ﻿Must be the night hunters". ﻿ ﻿Thought Kalia. The night hunters were a group of men who travelled far from villages, to hunt exotic and rare animals. The next morning, Kalia drew a picture of India highlighting the last visits of the night hunters. He realized his favourite forest was their next visit! The next few days, Kalia spied on them and took photographs of them hunting down the most exotic and rare species of animals. He knew he had to do something and quick. He showed the images to the people of the village who were indeed furious. The night pushed away the morning in a blink of an eye. The villagers were at every corner of the forest. When the night hunters appeared, they trapped them in nets and bet them. The next morning, they threw the men out of the village, who ran for their lives.

title: A Butterfly Smile
text: "Line up class! Let’s go to the park," Laila Miss says. All the students hold hands, chattering away. Kavya stands by herself. As they start walking, Laila Miss asks, "Does anyone know what a caterpillar becomes when it grows up?" Kavya’s stomach flips. She knows the answer! Should she say something? Kavya and her family have just moved to Bengaluru from her village. They live at the construction site where her parents work. It’s hard living in a half-finished house. The air smells of smoke, and the honking traffic makes it hard to sleep. The towering buildings, zooming cars, and busy people make her feel very, very small. Kavya has been coming to school for a week. She still hasn’t spoken to anyone. What if they make fun of her accent? Or tease her because she’s never been to school before? Kavya takes a deep breath and raises her hand. In a noisy city like Bengaluru, she can’t be quiet forever. "When caterpillars grow up, they become butterflies," Kavya says. "That’s right!" Laila Miss says. "Caterpillars are only caterpillars for a few weeks," Kavya says. "They spend that whole time eating leaves." "They must get very big," says Mary, her classmate. "They do!" "After they eat and eat and eat, caterpillars weave cocoons on the sides of plants. They go inside, where they grow and change," says Kavya. "That’s correct," Laila Miss says. "They stay in the cocoons for about two weeks. When they come out, they are butterflies." "Look, we’re at the park!" Mary says. Kavya gasps. The park is covered in butterflies! Blue butterflies the colour of rivers. Yellow butterflies the colour of sunlight. Orange butterflies the colour of ripe chikoos. Black-and-white butterflies the colours of starry skies. These are all the colours Kavya misses from her village. She feels her heart flutter. "Every year, butterflies travel thousands of kilometres to come to this park. They are here for more food, better weather, and a safe place to lay eggs," Laila Miss says. "This journey is called migration." "Don’t they get tired, flapping their wings for so long?" a classmate asks. "If there is a strong wind, they don’t have to flap their wings," Kavya says. "They spread their wings and glide." "That must be bumpy," Mary whispers to Kavya. Kavya thinks about the bus ride to Bengaluru – squeezed in between all the luggage. Bumping and tumbling for hours and hours and hours. Is that how a butterfly feels on the wind? "When butterflies migrate, they follow rivers. To stay healthy, they stop along the riverbank to soak up minerals with their feet. It’s called mud-puddling," Laila Miss says. "Mud-puddling?" Mary says. "That sounds like fun." Mary and Kavya smile at each other. "It is," Kavya says. "But now puddles are hard to find." In Kavya’s village, men in trucks take sand away from the river. The weather gets hotter and hotter. There is less and less rain. Last year, the river went dry. The butterflies didn’t have enough water to mud-puddle. Kavya’s family didn’t have enough water to farm. That’s why they moved to Bengaluru. Last year, the river went dry. The butterflies didn’t have enough water to mud-puddle. Kavya’s family didn’t have enough water to farm. That’s why they moved to Bengaluru. "You know a lot about butterflies, Kavya," says Laila Miss. "That’s because they are my favourite insects," says Kavya. "Why do you love butterflies so much, Kavya?" asks Mary. How can Kavya choose just one thing? She loves how their bodies are sometimes spotted and sometimes striped. How they drink nectar with their long noses. How they spread pollen, which makes more flowers grow. "They fly far, but wherever they land, they make new friends," Kavya says, squeezing Mary’s hand. "They’re very small, but they’re also very brave." "Just like you," Laila Miss says. Kavya smiles a smile as wide as a butterfly’s wings. Make A Butterfly Rest Station Butterflies in India migrate twice a year. Their journey is getting harder and harder because our forests and rivers are disappearing. Butterflies don’t have enough places to rest. Many get tired along the way. One way to help butterflies is to make safe spaces for them to stop and have a good meal. Here’s how to make a butterfly rest station: Find a flat vessel with high edges, like a thali or a plate. Butterflies love bright colours. Paint the vessel red, yellow, or orange. Fill the vessel with butterfly food. I t’s easy to make! Mix four cups of water with one cup of sugar. Add pieces of over-ripe fruit. Butterflies love bananas, guavas, mangoes, papayas, and oranges. Keep the vessel out on your veranda, windowsill, or anywhere outside. Clean and refill the vessel every two to three days. To attract even more butterflies, plant flowers that butterflies love. You can plant verbena, geraniums, dahlias, or sunflowers. You don’t need a lot of space – you can plant them in pots on the ground, or keep them on windowsills.

title: The Moon Will Come Down
text: There was once a girl named Mini. She didn't like to study or go to school. Her parents wanted her to study, so that she could become something good, but Mini wouldn't agree. Instead, she liked to tease others and make fun of them. Not even a single day passed when her parent's didn't get to listen about her complaints by others. Once, when it was a full Mmoon night, the moon seemed to appear more rounded and bigger than other nights. Mini thought that she could climb onto the roof and catch the Moon. She ran up to the roof, but the Moon risen higher up again. Now she thought that she could catch the Moon from the village's tallest house, Mangdu Chacha's house. Thus, she went to Mangdu Chacha's House, but the Moon had again risen higher up. Now she thought that the Moon had gone to the other side of the hill. Mini thus went to the hill, but the Moon had risen higher up once again. Mini felt dismayed because of her unsuccessfulness, but she didn't give up. She had full faith in herself that if she tried, then she could surely get hold of the Moon. She asked the Moon, "Whatever height I try to catch you from, you rise above it. Can't I ever get hold of you?" The Moon smiled and answered, "Dear Mini, when you study and become something good, and earn your name and soar to new heights, I will come down for you myself." Mini became satisfied by the Moon's answer and returned back to her home. Now she had a new enthusiasm inside herself, to study and become something good. After all, she wanted to touch the moon.

title: Khuyay
text: It was her favorite place because there were so many beautiful trees. There was a very special one that she called "Khuyay." Khuyay was large and leafy, and many little animals lived in the tree. Different species of birds made their nests there, bees built their hive there and made lots of honey for themselves, and there were also little worms and brightly colored insects. The girl especially liked to watch the sloths climb slowly up the beautiful tree and hang from its branches. After feeling this whole explosion of life in her heart, she would rest under the shade of her favorite tree to fill her spirit with peace and harmony. Then she would go home happy and energetic. One morning, she got ready as usual to visit the mountain and Khuyay. Imagine her surprise when she found, in her almost secret place, machines and men who were marking all the trees, not just Khuyay, with paint. The girl didn't understand what was happening, but her heart told her it was not good. She ran in a hurry to tell her father, who worked in an environmental protection organization. The girl understood immediately that those men wanted to cut down the trees to take them to the wood factories. Her father explained that this was forbidden in that area. Then, he asked the local residents and the authorities for their support to stop these men from cutting down the trees in the valley, which served as the lungs of the whole region. Those men intended to damage a protected area. But more than that, the girl felt that harming Khuyay would have been like ripping her heart out and destroying all life in her and in all the trees in the world. From that day on, the girl knew that when she grew up she wanted to be like her father and protect nature. title: And Sister started going to School
text: One day her mother asked her sister to stay at home in the middle of work. Then the boy said, "Mother, why is Didi not going to school today?" Mother replied, “There is a lot of work at home today so Didi will not go to school.” A few days passed like this. One day again the boy asked his mother, "Mother, why didn't Didi go to school?" Then the mother said, "Son, you go to school, what will your sister do after studying?" The boy sadly went to school. One day in school his teacher said, "Son, you come to school everyday but why doesn't your sister come?" The boy told the teacher that mother tells what did Didi do after studying? Hearing this, his teacher said, "Son, ask your mother to come and talk to me tomorrow." When the boy told his mother about the teacher, his mother said that she did not have time to go to school. The next day the boy told the whole thing to the ma'am. Then his teacher went to his house. Going home, she explained to his mother that just as it is important for boys to study, it is important for girls to study as well. A girl can read and write and handle the whole house well. The boy's mother understood the teacher's point and she started sending her daughter to school every day. Slowly seeing him, all the people of the village started sending their children to school every day and then their village started changing. ﻿ Google Story-A-Thon ﻿ Story-A-Thon was an online contest launched on 8th September 2020, Inte rnational Literacy Day, by Google, for little authors from 5 - 11 years to explore their creative writing skills and share their own original stories. title: Today, I got a BFF
text: One day, in a dense forest, a little elephant, was playing the game of `How much water fits in your trunk?’ all by herself. Her name was Sonia. Her Mom and Dad were preparing for lunch. Sonia usually had no one to play with of her age, therefore she was often bored. Suddenly, she heard huge thumps coming from a distance. She was frightened. Sonia ran to her Mom and Dad immediately and said “Mommy, Daddy there’s someone coming near our area! What should we do?”. Her Mom replied “Really! Let’s go and check quickly!”. They rushed to the place and saw an elephant family. They were new to the forest. Sonia’s parents spoke to the family. They soon came to know that the family was shifting just near their area because there was a very severe drought in their old place. As the adults were talking, an elephant of Sonia’s age came to her and introduced herself “Hello! What’s your name? I’m Molly, Nice to meet you!” Sonia replied “My name is Sonia. Where did you come from?”. Molly said “I’ve come from north India.”. As they said this they started walking. They spoke about other things like how was your home? What games do you know? etc., and asked lots of questions to each other. Sonia took Molly to see the forest. She showed Molly the places she loved the most. Sonia explained a lot about all the trees, animals and some dangerous places where they were not supposed to go. They talked and talked until they reached the river. The fresh air refreshed them. Molly liked the place a lot. They splashed water at each other, made jokes and laughed till stomach ache. They sat on a rock for a while looking at the sky which was beautiful. They didn’t even notice what time it was as they were having a very good time. After a while they went to see the rest of the forest. Once they explored the whole jungle, they started playing games like wrestling, who plucks more fruits? etc. Molly’s favourite game was wrestling. Soon, the Sun went behind the mountains. Sonia and Molly were feeling really very tired by then. They returned to their homes, had a good dinner and slept with the good things they did in the whole day caged in their minds. The next day they woke up, bright and shining. They had breakfast and were off to play. While they were playing Sonia was realizing that she wasn’t bored anymore and with Molly’s company she was even more happy. Molly was thinking that Sonia is a good friend. They helped each other like true friends. Sonia was happy as she got a friend finally. They remained best friends forever by helping, being kind and respectful to each other. The End

title: Fruit of Hard Work
text: Once both of them bought a bigha farm together and thought that they would do farming together. The crop that will be ready will be sold and a house will be built with the money that will be received. Om worked hard day and night in the field, while Ghanshyam was busy worshipping God. The crop was harvested and sold. Om said, “I should get a higher share of the money because I have worked hard in the field.” On the other hand, Ghanshyam said, "I also worshipped God day and night, which has produced a good crop." When this quarrel escalated, both of them went to the chief. After listening to both of them, the chief gave rice mixed with each sack of pebbles and said, "Get it clean tomorrow. Then I will pronounce the verdict." Om started cleaning the rice with all his hard work. He cleaned as much rice as he could overnight. Ghanshyam only prayed to God. In the morning the chief asked both of them to show the rice. Om had cleaned more than half the rice. When asked to Ghanshyam, he said, "I have prayed to God, the rice must have been clean." When seen, the whole sack of rice was like that. Then the chief decreed – “Work is successful only by working hard. No work gets accomplished by merely praying dependent on God. So Om has worked hard. So he will get more money." title: Bananas of Hajipur
text: She woke her father and Kishore together and exclaimed "Hajipur is here!" Then Mr. Ram Prasad opened his eyes and looked out of the window. The train really had arrived at Hajipur station. He glanced at his watch and the time was 1:00 am. There Kishore also got up from his seat and got near the window. In the silence of the night we could hear a number of voices shouting "Banana! Banana! Sweet and delicious bananas of Hajipur. Komal called out "Banana selling uncle! Please come here," to a passing banana seller. He arrived near the window and asked "How many bananas?" Ram Prasad asked the price, "What is the cost?" "Rs. 20 per dozen," the banana seller replied, "These are Hajipur's famous bananas. Eat two and feel good. They give the enjoyment of sweets." Ram Prasad said, giving a hundred rupee note, "Give me two dozens." Kishore was curious to know about these bananas. He asked the banana seller, "Uncle, what kinds of bananas are there in Hajipur?" He spoke as he was counting the bananas with his fingers, "Malbhog is Hajipur's most expensive banana. Mudiya and Batisa bananas are also available here. They are also used to make curries. Kofta, chokha, chutney, kachri and its roti is also very delicious. After cooking mudiya gets sweeter than jaggery." "Why are Hajipur's bananas famous, Uncle?" Komal asked curiously. "Because the banks of the Ganges provide suitable soil and climate for its production. Here the work of making cloth from the fiber of banana thread has also started." the banana seller explained. Then the train whistled and started moving. "Bananas! Bananas!" the banana seller called out and disappeared.
author: Sanjana Wuyyuru

title: Raju learns his lesson.
text: Once upon a time, in the big jungle of “Happypur” lived a monkey named Raju. He was very naughty. He was always jumping around. He was always hungry and ate anything he could lay his hands on. Raju- I am hungry. I want to eat a burger. Rani (Raju's Mom) - Finish your bowl of vegetables and rice first. You can have a banana or an apple afterwards. Raju- No, I want a burger and I want fries. I want a fizzy drink too. Rani- No! Raju, these are Junk food. These are bad for your health. Raju (throws a tantrum)- Mom! I want a burger or pizza and chips only. Raju- No, I don't want to eat the vegetables. I will eat the burger and chips. After an hour Raju- Aah! Aah! My tummy… It’s aching! Monu, the rabbit meets Raju on his way back to home. title: Once Upon A Weedy Coral
text: In the deep trenches of The Great Barrier Reef, there flourished a colony of bright red, orange and golden coloured corals. The corals were sweet homes to many big and tiny sea creatures. Not only did the corals provide food, but also acted as play-grounds for its residents. They were inhabited by Stephen, the starfish, Oaken, the octopus, Jiggly, the jellyfish, Weedy, the coral and Miu-Miu, the clown fish They all used to have a gala time, swimming around the corals, while the corals merrily swayed. But, their happiness didn’t last long because suddenly, the humans started to attack the coral colony. They had a lot of economic benefits by catching colourful fish and mining for sea salt. By hearing this, the coral buddies were shocked and upset so they planed a meeting Miu-Miu started, “friends we are having a disaster and we might be the next target for the newly opened aquarium in Sydney we cannot let this happen are you with me then Stephen said but we are too small and the humans have so many tools with them how can we fight against such mighty enem.. Suddenly, Oaken stopped Stephen and said, “We might be small from the outside, but if we unite and make a plan, then we might be able to tackle the big humans.” Then, everyone started to tell their ideas. Jiggly started, “I could use my stinky tentacles and scared the humans back to their land. ‘‘ Then, Oaken said, I can use my poisonous I am black liquid to blind the humans for 30 minutes. ‘’ Then Stephen said,’’ I cannot help alone, but I need hundreds of me. We will make a giant net and capture the humans. ‘‘ Miu-Miu gave a high-five and said,‘‘ United we stand, divided we fall.” Every day they used to meet, not with joy, but fear. Finally, one day, they heard strange sounds. They quickly prepared themselves for the attack. Thing wet as they had planned. The humans panicked and fled. It was a true victory for the coral buddies. They all swam merrily and celebrated their victory. Then Miu-Miu gave a high fin and said, “See, I told ya’, united we stand, divided we fall.”

title: Gola Gola
text: Mariyu has finally decided what she wants to eat at the mela. “I’m going to gobble gulabi golas at the mela today,” she says. “It will make my tongue nice and pink.” “My favourite golas are yellow like mangoes!” Yohan tells Mariyu. “I want a blue gola!” says Akira. “I want a gola that’s both pink and blue,” says Armaan “In that case, I want a gola that’s yellow and blue,” says Muskaan, wheeling in. Ammar chooses an orange gola. Dipu wants a pink and yellow gola. Dua likes green golas. Mehek wants a purple gola. Mariyu scratches her head. How will she remember everyone’s golas? In comes Yohan, saying, “I know what to do!” Mariyu paints a pink circle. Yohan paints his circle yellow. Akira paints a blue circle. And Dua, Ammar and Mehek find shades of green, orange, and purple where the circles overlap. Armaan touches both pink and blue. Muskaan touches both blue and yellow. And Dipu touches the yellow and pink. “I want a gola with all the colours,” says Sid. “Where do I paint it?” “Right here in the centre, where all the circles overlap,” replies Mariyu. Golas and Venn Diagrams So many gola choices! Mariyu was able to cleverly use a Venn diagram to solve that problem. Venn diagrams explain sets and the relation between sets using images. A set is a collection of things, or numbers, or shapes, or as in this case, colours. Union of two sets means all the parts of the two sets. So a union of pink and blue golas (like the one Armaan wanted), would have a pink top, a blue bottom, and a purple middle where the blue and pink overlap. Intersection of sets means just the place where the two sets overlap. So the intersection of pink and blue is purple, like the gola that Mehak wanted.

title: The Animal Plot
text: In Jind, Janu plays with her buffaloes. Numbers 1 2 3 4 5 Animal Bird Cat Dog Buffalo Numbers 5 4 3 2 1 Animal In Ferozepur, Fagun pets the pigs. Bird Piglet Squirrel Pig Numbers 5 4 3 2 1 Animal In Bhopal, Bela gathers her goats. Cat Bird Dog Goat Animal Numbers 5 4 3 2 1 In Partapur, Pappu counts the camels. Camel Dog Goat Bird In Baghjan, Bunny looks for her hens. Numbers 1 2 3 4 5 Animal Fowl Fish Duck Chick Bar Graphs Bar graphs represent information using mathematical pictures. They are used to count and compare numbers and data, and show how things change with time. Bar graphs have an x-axis and a y-axis. One axis usually has a category (like types of animal) and the other has numbers, which we can use for counting (like the number of each type of animal). So, you can now add up all the animals and see how many there are. Take a look at the bar graphs, and answer these questions. 1. Does Janu have more birds or buffaloes in Jind? 2. Count the number of pigs and piglets in Ferozepur. 3. How many goats does Bela have in Bhopal? 4. How many camels, dogs, goats and birds are there on Pappu’s farm? 5. How many ducks does Bunny have to feed every day? Answers

title: Achchachi's Bagbrella
text: “Lost your umbrella again?” asked Achchachi. “I was very careful this time. I think I left it on the bus,” replied Sahyadri. “Please don’t tell Amma!” said Sahyadri. “But now I need a new umbrella.” “OK, we don’t have to tell her,” replied Achchachi. “Let’s see if we can make a new one.” “I think we have everything we need,” said Achchachi, digging into his toolbox. “But what about the cloth for the umbrella?” asked Sahyadri. “Look inside that box and pick whatever colour you like,” said Achchachi. “These are so colourful!” said Sahyadri. “But we don’t have enough to make one umbrella,” said Achchachi. “But we can make a colourful one by combining all the different colours,” said Sahyadri. “Do you want a red one with a bit of yellow? It’ll look like the sunset,” said Achchachi. “But look! This purple one is so beautiful,” said Sahyadri. “Let’s add more colours!” said Sahyadri. “Hmm... I think it needs a little more colour,” said Sahyadri. “A red semicircle would be perfect.” “How about a bit of green?” “Let’s try some pink. “Some orange. “And maybe some vermilion.” Finally, after adding and removing, increasing and decreasing, arranging and rearranging, Sahyadri and Achchachi were all set. Achchachi snipped, snapped, clipped, taped, and burned the midnight oil… and made the umbrella just in time for school the next morning. On their way, it began to rain. Sahyadri tugged at the plug Achchachi had fixed to her bag. ZAP! Sahyadri’s Pie Chart All the pieces of cloth in the umbrella come together to form a pie chart. A pie chart is a circular diagram used to represent data. A chart makes it faster and easier to understand data as compared to numbers. Pie charts are divided into slices to show all the parts within one large unit. In Sahyadri’s umbrella, all the colours are used equally.

title: Guess My Job - A Quiz
text: You would have known the various jobs or professions in this world. Take a look at the 4-word clues given and guess who does the job. For example, if the clues are letter, postbox, mail, and cycle, the answer is Postman. Try to find the other answers now. 1. Stethoscope, Prescription, Thermometer, Torch. Answer: Doctor Doctors use a stethoscope, thermometer, and torch to check a patient. Doctors write prescriptions for patients. 2. Blackboard, Chalk piece, Notes of lessons, Exams. Answer: Teacher Teachers use the blackboard and chalk piece to teach. They write notes of lessons and conduct exams. 3. Sea, Boat, Net, Waves. Answer: Fisherman Fishermen go on boats on the sea that has waves. They cast their net in the sea to catch fish. 4. Stove, Spoon, Recipe, Hotel. Answer: Chef Chefs work in a hotel. They use the stove and spoon to cook. They write recipes for various dishes. 5. Tractor, Seeds, Fields, Plough. Answer: Farmer Farmers sow seeds in the fields. They use a tractor to plough the fields. 6. Blueprint, Eyeglasses, Steel ruler, Calculator. Answer: Engineer Engineers create a blueprint for their engineering drawings. They also use eyeglasses, steel rulers, and calculators to do their work. ﻿ 7. Whistle, Lathi Stick, Cap, FIR Answer: Police Police wear a cap and use the whistle and lathi stick. They file a First Information Report (FIR) for crimes. ﻿ 8. Broom, Mop, Dishwasher Soap, House. Answer: Maid Maids clean the house with a broom and mop. They use dishwasher soap to clean the vessels. 9. Hammer, Screwdriver, Wood, Backsaw. Answer: Carpenter Carpenters use the hammer, screwdriver, and backsaw to make furniture out of wood. 10. Headpan, Shovel, Bricks, Cement. Answer: Mason Masons use headpan, shovel, bricks, and cement to build a house.

title: Paati's Gold
text: Selvan and Savi did not like it when Paati and Appa fought. This time, Appa was upset about his rice crop failing year after year. “I told you not to plant that lab-created rice,” said Paati. “Everyone said it was a high-yielding rice variety. The production was high for the first few years. Then it didn’t work,” said Appa. “Not only did it not work, our soil lost its richness, the groundwater depleted and our crops suffered,” said Paati. “That Golden Rice ruined our fields. I don’t know how to recover from this loss,” said Appa. “Don’t worry! I have real gold for you and my grandchildren,” said Paati. Appa left in a huff. “Paati! You know Appa is struggling to make ends meet. Why do you keep saying you have gold for us?” said Savi. “If you really had gold, we wouldn’t be in such misery, Paati,” said Selvan. “One day you will see, Selva. Only then will you understand what real gold is,” said Paati, smiling. Paati and Appa shared a bittersweet relationship. But they both cared for each other. When Appa came home from the fields, Paati would give him kaapi and appam. Appa would cook her idlis with par-boiled rice batter, the way she liked them. They even went for morning walks together. That night Paati coughed a lot. Appa sat next to her, giving her medicines. Savi and Selvan massaged her legs. “Savi, please bring me the wooden box from the locker in my cupboard,” said Paati. “Do you have the real gold hidden in the box, Amma?” teased Appa. Savi and Selvan giggled. “You are right. This box contains real gold. If you spend it wisely, it will relieve you of your misery,” said Paati. Paati opened the wooden box. Inside were different rice seeds. They were native varieties of rice that Paati had saved over many years. It even had lesser-known varieties like kattuyanam and garudan samba. Kattuyanam rice is drought-resistant and flood-tolerant. Garudan samba has great health benefits. Appa couldn’t believe his eyes. He hugged Paati and cried. “This is real gold, Amma. You are right.” “Appa, why did Paati say this rice is gold?” asked Savi. “One day we will see. And we will understand what she meant,” said Appa. Several months passed. Appa’s fields flourished with Paati’s rice. Many of Appa’s friends came to him looking for help and advice. Appa helped them the same way Paati had helped him. He gave them 2 kg of rice each with a promise that they would return 4 kg from their yield. He used their portions for further distribution among farmers in his village. Those farmers did the same. This chain continued and expanded. Soon, the whole village was thriving with many varieties of indigenous rice. Everyone had enough to eat and enough to sell. Appa, Selvan and Savi enjoyed evening kaapi and red rice appams with Paati. They looked at their golden, ripe paddy fields with pride. They had understood what Paati meant. This was real gold. Know Your Rice The rice you eat at home comes in many different varieties, like basmati, sona masoori or kolam. Both kattuyanam and garudan samba are from Tamil Nadu. Kattuyanam is a red rice and is also called the forest elephant rice. It grows so tall that it can hide an elephant. It helps to hold floods and fertilises the soil. Garudan samba is a brown rice. It is rich in nutrients and fibre. It is best used for making the dish, puttu.

title: Donkey in an Elevator
text: ﻿ The tall buildings in cities have elevators. Some people call them lifts. People use the lifts to go up and down and also to carry heavy things. One day, a donkey came to see the city. In his village there are no tall buildings and so no lifts. But he remembered his master made him carry heavy things on his back to some of these tall buildings during constructions. When he came to one of the tall buildings, he was surprised to see, how the people carry their heavy things up so high. “How can they do it without a donkey like me?” he said to himself. He came to the building and there was a man at the desk. He was the security guard. “What do you want?” asked the guard. “Excuse me,” I want to know, how the people carry the load up so high without a donkey like me?” asked the animal. “Does the elevator have tall legs and strong back like me?” asked the donkey. The guard decided to show the animal. So, he chose a time when there was nobody around and took the animal into the lift. He pressed the button to the 20 th story and up went the lift. The donkey was surprised. But suddenly the lift stopped at the 15 th floor and the door opened. Two little fellows standing at the door with a small bag were surprised. “You donkey, what are you doing here?” they shouted. The donkey was upset. He replied, “You lazy fellows, you cannot carry a small bag downstairs and you need the elevator to carry you and your bag. Just imagine how much load I carried to build this building. Can I NOT take a little ride? " Then he walked off.

title: Little Jumbo
text: Little Jumbo playing about, Felt suddenly thirsty and began to shout: "I'd like some water nice and cool If only I could find a little pool! Little Jumbo then quickly thought, "My ears are BIG and can drink a lot." So down went a ear into the pool, But no water came and he felt like a fool. Little Jumbo then dipped his tail, Hoping that this plan won't fail. But alas, only his little tail got wet, For not a drop of water could he get. Little Jumbo wailed and cried, "All the ways I've tried and tried." His mother just then passing by, Looked at him and gave a sigh. "Little Jumbo, how very silly, Use your trunk, you little billy. Dip it in and suck in well, And then your thirst you can quell." Little Jumbo drank with glee, And thanked his mother joyfully. "Oh Mama dear, it's good to see, You are drinking just like me!" Little Jumbo shed tears of joy, And hugged his mother like a good boy. "Oh Mother dear, I love you so, Now off to the jungle, let us go!"

text: Once upon a time there lived a group of monkeys. They were in a desert and they were too hungry. So one of them went to find food. The monkey climbed a mountain. title: Let's Eat
text: Some hunt, some pluck, some simply swallow in a hurry. What do animals like to eat? Toothpaste on brush or rotting leaves, she will eat anything that is around. Here comes the cockroach. There goes the hare at top speed. He does not waste any nutrients. After grasses and seeds, he also eats his own poop. Who is digging? It is the beetle, who buries dead birds and rats. He is storing food for his babies. The crocodile is waiting to eat his prey whole, even if there is hair and bones. The hyena gives a gleeful laugh. A carcass or just the left toe, she is happy to eat any leftovers. The snake slides into a hidey-h O le. He doesn’t care for an omelette, he gulps the eggs whole. The octopus can change her colour. Watch her drop down on a clam. She pulls it into her arms and mouth and then it is gone. The leopard is out hunting at night. She eats creatures big and small — hares, jungle fowl, chital, rats. Up on the tree, the grey langur is combing her baby’s hair. She picks out lice and puts them in her mouth. Now that’s a crispy snack. Leopards hunt, langurs pluck, crocodiles simply swallow in a hurry. Now we know what animals like for dinner, what do you like to eat?

title: Tricolor chart
text: One day Pooja and Neha were talking among themselves. Pooja said, "Lata's son is not developing well. He seems so weak." Neha replied, "You are right, her elder son seems very healthy." Pooja again said, "But how do we know whether her child is healthy or not. Health cannot be ascertained by looking at it." Neha said, "Come on, let's go to the Anganwadi didi and ask." Both reached to Didi. Pooja asked her, "Didi! We have a friend, Lata. Her baby looks very weak. How do we know whether the child is developing properly or not?" Didi said with a smile, "I'll tell you now." She opened the vaccination card and showed a chart and said, "This is growth. -Chart means a table showing the development of children. In this you can see three colors – green, yellow and orange. Green color tells your child is healthy. Yellow color means the child has progressed towards malnutrition. And orange color means the child is malnourished. If the baby's weight is in the yellow or orange zone, it needs more care. There is more need to take care of his food and drink and cleanliness. The weight of the child at the time of birth should be at least 2.5 kg. If the weight is less, then his physical development will decrease. That's why it is important to know the exact weight of the child." Neha said on hearing this, "It is very difficult to keep weighing." Didi immediately replied, "No problem in that. Go to the nearest Anganwadi center. There, children up to the age of six can be weighed, that too absolutely free!" "Free!" The two friends came out of their mouths together. Sister laughed, "Yes. Absolutely free." Pooja excitedly said, "Now it will not be difficult to ascertain the exact development of Lata's son." Neha also nodded her yes and both the friends started towards Lata's house.

title: My first trip by train
text: Hello! My name is Riya. I live in Pune with my parents. I love my friends, playing in the parks, My school. But what I love the most is my Grandpa! But unfortunately, My grandpa lives in Delhi, So you must of guessed I don't see him nor visit him that often. One day, During my summer holidays, My father said, ''Riya! look, we are going to Delhi to visit you grandpa!'' I jumped with joy and my parents smiled, when I saw the tickets. My parents smiled as I jumped with joy. The next day, My parents and I reached the train station at 4:00 AM. While I was waiting, I saw that the station was crowded with loads of people. The train master was blowing the whistle, Some of them were selling stuff and Some of them were even trying to catch the train while it was moving!. So, I held my father's hand... tight Now it was our turn to get on the train. I was about to get on, but I had heard a voice. It was the train driver! ''Hello,'' Said the driver. ''Hi!'' I replied back excitedly. Then I went on the train with my parents. My parents loaded the luggage on the train and sat down. The train was crowded... Just like the station!. I also sat down. It was a 1day and 2 hour flight to Delhi. I was getting bored. '' Mummy, Papa, I am bored. What should I do? '' My mother said '' Riya, Why don't you read that book which you had bought along with you? I opened the book and started reading from where I had stopped. After 5 mins of reading, I stopped and looked out of the window. Oh! What a view it was! Mountains, Valleys, Flowers, Trees Etc., Etc.!!! So, we slept in the night and woke up just in time when the train arrived at Delhi station. We got off and headed of to Grandpa's house. When we reached there, My grandpa welcomed me with opened arms. '' Grandpa!'' I screamed loudly. '' '' Oh Riya, I have missed you so much!'' He greeted me. My parents also greeted him. Then I freshened up and ran to the doorstep with my grandpa and started listening to his childhood stories.

title: Detective Kaka 1 - The mystery of the Missing Chicks
text: Once upon a time, there lived a very smart crow. This crow's name was Detective Kaka. As his name suggests Detective Kaka solved mysteries. The only problem is that he has never solved a mystery. Atleast, not till now. It all began on a hot summer afternoon. Detective Kaka was fast asleep in his office when someone came barging in. It was Mother Hen, she was in tears. After Detective Kaka calmed her down he asked her what happened. Mother Hen was teaching her chicks how to whistle. After whistling so much she decided to get them a drink of water. But when she came back they were gone. Mother Hen told Detective Kaka that she suspects Mean Fox. Detective Kaka told her not to accuse anyone without any evidence. But Mother Hen insisted that Mean Fox kidnapped (in this case chick napped) her children. After a lot of arguing Mother Hen somehow convinced Detective Kaka to investigate Mean Fox's house. Mean Fox's house was deep in the dark part of the woods. It was once light blue in colour but now it was a faded shade of blue. When Detective Kaka went near Mean Fox's house he heard a strange whistling sound. He thought it was the wind so he kept on walking. Detective Kaka gathered all his courage and rang the doorbell. Mean Fox opened the door, he looked terrifying. Detective Kaka saw a cage covered by a cloth. He was sure the whistling sound was coming from there. Detective Kaka barged in and took off the cloth from the cage. The chicks were inside!!! Mean Fox asked Detective Kaka how he figured it out. Detective Kaka said that Mother Hen had told him that she was teaching her chicks how to whistle and a whistling sound was coming from the cage, so he suspected the chicks were there. Mean Fox was arrested and Mother Hen was reunited with her chicks.

title: Flying Home
text: It was the beginning of October and everyone in Kheechan was waiting to feed and care for the cranes that visited them every year. “Mama, when will the koonj arrive?” Raju asked Bhanwar Ram. “Beta, they will be here soon,” said Bhanwar Ram. “By November.” Raju began a countdown to the date of arrival. It would take about four weeks for the koonj to arrive from the Mongolian plains where they nested. They would fly over the Central Asian plains and then over the Himalayas and finally land in Kheechan. A day went by. Then two days, then five days. In seven days, it had been a week. 7 days = 1 week Then two, then three. Soon it had been four weeks, almost a full month. 14 days = 2 weeks = a fortnight About 4 weeks = 1 month How much longer would it take for the birds to arrive? Raju was growing impatient. He had spent the month helping Bhanwar Mama stock up on grains for their feed. Raju counted, a year has 12 months and the koonj usually stayed in Kheechan for five months. This meant they would be here until the end of March. He would get to spend almost half a year with them. He would feed the cranes, and look after the wounded and tired ones that had made the long journey. 6 months = half a year 12 months = 1 year Then one day, Raju looked up at the sky. He saw hundreds of koonj gliding and sailing, soaring and racing. All the villagers ran out of their homes with bags of millet and scattered it on the ground. Raju ran to join them. His friends were back home. The Koonj Calendar Every year, thousands of koonj, also known as demoiselle cranes, migrate from their home in Central Asia to Kheechan in Rajasthan and parts of Pakistan. They stay there for around five months and the villagers feed them every day. There are 7 days in a week. There are 30 or 31 days in most months. Only February has 28 days. There are 4-5 weeks in a month. There are 12 months or 52 weeks in a year.

title: No Smiles Today
text: Arun were good friends. They had so much fun together. They shared secrets in class. They ran races on the way home. She was always cheerful. One day, Shanti came into the classroom slowly. Her head was bent. She looked sad. “Did someone scold you?” asked Arun. Shanti shook her head. She sat down and did not look up. She did not answer ‘Present!’ when Sona Miss called her name. Sona Miss called again, louder this time, “Shanti Kumar!” Shanti raised her hand. “Do you have a sore throat?” her teacher asked her. Shanti shook her head. Her cheeks were red and it looked like she had a fever. “Are you feeling okay?” Sona Miss asked. Shanti nodded, still not daring to look up. “Why does Shanti look so sad?” “Is your little brother okay?” “Is your puppy okay?” “Is your grandmother okay?” Shanti kept nodding her head to each of her friends. But she did not look u Arun wanted to make her smile. He had an idea! He took out something from his bag. As he ran to show it to Shanti, it slipped out of his hands. Shanti saw something flying towards her and she grabbed it. It was a BIG, green, rubber frog! Shanti's eyes flew open. Then she opened her mouth to laugh. THEN Arun and her friends saw why she had not smiled or talked all day! Four of her front teeth had gone missing!

title: Talk and Talk
text: You and other people talk to convey messages to each other. You can talk with friends, family, colleagues, helpers, and customers. You can talk on a stage in front of a crowd. You can talk over the mobile to a person who is far away from you. You can talk with others over a Zoom Call, Skype, Google Talk, or Microsoft Teams through a computer or mobile phone. You can talk with your dog and call them by their name. You can talk with virtual assistants like Alexa and Siri and ask them to do a task. The talks can be one-way or two-way. One-way talk is when only one person talks. For example, you can give a speech on a stage. Two-way talk is when everyone talks and listens. For example, you and your friend can talk with each other. You can talk in any language you know. Most of the time people talk in their mother tongue or English. Can you think of any other situations when people talk? Happy Talking!

title: Rani's First Day At School
text: It is Rani's first day at school. Her mother is holding her hand and walking her to school. "I am grown up now", Rani says to her mother. "Let go my hand, let go!" Her mother holds her hand even more tightly. There were many children reaching the school already. Some children came by bus, by car, some by rickshaw, cycle. And some came by walking, just like Rani. Rani and her mother reached the school gate, and her mother let go off her hand. Her mother stays at the gate. Now Rani has to go inside alone. There are many new faces all around her. She takes one step, then another. She looks back, her mother was getting smaller and smaller as she walks away. She thinks. will my mother disappear and feels scared so runs back to her. She doesn't feel so grown up and holds her mother's hand and says "Don't go away". All the students were inside by now, Rani was the only one outside. The teacher comes out and smiles at Rani. Rani smiles back at her teacher and let go off her mother's hand. Her mother says, "Rani, I will be here when you come out." Her mother waves to her and goes away. Rani went inside. She was now happy, her mother will be there after school!
author: Samridhi Singla

title: Every Rupee Counts
text: Banko has been saving money. He wants to donate it to Power Paws because he loves animals. “Sunkho, wait, I’m counting… 1, 2, 3, 4,” Banko says. “Banko, one 10-rupee note plus one 1-rupee coin is not equal to two rupees. You have to count the value of the money,” says Daee. “Let us first make different piles.” “So many coins!” “Don’t worry, Banko. I will give you a 10-rupee note in exchange for your twenty 50-paise coins,” says Daee. 1 x 50 Paise = Rupee 2 x 50 Paise = 1 Rupee 20 x 50 Paise = 10 Rupees “Banko, how many 10-rupee notes do you have?” “Twenty-five,” says Banko “That makes it Rs250,” says Daee. “Banko, now give me all your 10-rupee notes.” Daee then takes out some notes from her purse. “A 100-rupee note, and three 50-rupee notes in exchange for your 10-rupee notes. How much is it, Banko?” “Ummm...is it Rs250, Daee?” asks Banko. “Yes!” says Daee. Four 5-rupee coins Fifteen 2-rupee coins Fifty 1-rupee coins One 100-rupee note Three 50-rupee notes Total Rs20.00 Rs30.00 Rs50.00 Rs100.00 Rs150.00 Rs350.00 How much money has Banko saved in notes and coins? “Now Banko, altogether you have Rs350. If you give Rs250 to Power Paws, you will still have Rs100 left. What do you want to do with it?” Daee asks. “We’ll get a big football for us and a small one for Sunkho!” says Banko.
author: Mala Kumar

title: Love your Family
text: Once I was talking to a classmate named Fernanda, when she told me that she had three brothers. They were Francisco, Fernando and Alecsandro. title: The Story of Dakshi
text: Once there was a girl called Dakshi, Everyone would make fun of her because she had a disease called Lobster Claw Syndrome which causes the split of hand fingers and toe. She was so irritated to hear the same thing from everyone, Even her father was too ashamed of her. Then she said to herself " Why was I born with this disease!! " Dakshi, Began to cry. The Next Day, Dakshi got some interesting news, Her mother said to her " Dakshi, There is a competition in the school. You must participate,Dear. ".How many people would be there, Amma?? " asked Dakshi. " The whole school must be there,Dakshi" Amma replied. Dakshi yelled NO!!. Her mother asked " Why Dear??" Amma, You know everyone makes fun of me and laughs at me. Now, In front of the whole school, How.....Can I face everyone, AMMA "!!! Said Dakshi. Dakshi's Mother felt sorry for her and said " Dakshi, Don't behave like this, Even if you have this disease, You have the perfect talent!... Anyhow, Dakshi accepted, And joined in the competition. After a Few Days the competition day arrived, Dakshi Became a little worried!.... Her mother dropped her in the school and wished her a BEST OF LUCK.. The moment she entered the school every single student started laughing by looking at her hands and toes. As Dakshi knew it would happen, Poor Dakshi felt sad. But everyone was laughing except a man, Who was nodding his head. Dakshi got confused and approached towards that particular man, And asked him " Why aren't you laughing Uncle, isn't funny? " After a few seconds he replied back. Dear, How can it be funny? You have this disease called Lobster Claw Syndrome and Everyone is laughing at you, Teasing you....But it doesn't mean you have no talent and your not at all perfect! You are the best, You can do anything and You're the bravest.. But..don't be scared, little girl! Be Confident even towards the whole world... don't be a scared cat!! Then only you can become fearless. When the man taught her a big lesson she understood how to overcome and face the whole world.... DING DING DING The school competition is going to start! Dakshi, Hurried up and seated in her bench and started to write for the competition, She was fully focused.. In the same time a little tensed. She completed writing after some minutes and gave the paper to the teacher.. Soon, Every student completed their exam! The children went back to their houses, thinking about their exam results, Especially Dakshi was nervous about the results. A few Days Later, At last, it is the time of the exam result day. Dakshi's heart was pumping fast... The teacher said to everyone that the results are going to announce now! " The Exam topper is.................... DAKSHI ANIL!! CONGRATULATIONS DAKSHI........Everyone was shocked to hear that a child who has Lobster Claw Syndrome got topper in the exam?? Everyone was surprised Dakshi began to cry with happiness. Her mother hugged her! Now she remembered that man's words, WE SHOULD NOT LISTEN TO OTHERS.. AND DO THE THINGS WHICH MAKES YOU HAPPY. She was so happy like crazy.
author: Dakshina Anilkumar

title: Smile Please!
text: Once upon a time, there was a fawn running in a race through the forest. He ran past joey the rabbit with ease and was ahead. He even flew past the big-big elephant and was surprised at how fast he was. He jumped over the stream feeling refreshed by the cool water. He kept running without hesitation of losing. He zoomed past the crumbling wall with facileness in excitation he didn't fixate on where he was running. He missed a step and stumbled over an astronomically immense boulder and fell. title: A LESSON GIVEN BY A CHILD TO HIS FATHER
text: Sanjay was a carpenter. His mother died a long time back. His aged father,Ramlal, lived with him. Ramlal was very weak. He could not even walk well. It was because Sanjay did not give him enough food. He had given his father a small earthen plate for eating his food. Sanjay gives his father rice everyday for his meal but the small amount of rice did not fill his apetite. His father would happily eat the rice without any complaint. H e used to abuse his father badly. S anjay had a son. His name is Manish. Manish was just ten years old. He was a very good boy. He loved his grandfather. He had great respect for his grandfather. He did not like his father’s attitude and character, because his father was treating his grandfather cruelly. One Ramlal was eating his food out of earthen plate that his son had given to him. The earthen plate fell down. The plate broke into pieces. The food also fell on the floor. Sanjay was working outside. He saw the broken plate and was very angry with his father and used very harsh words for his father. The old man felt bad about what happened. He was sorry for his mistake. Sanjay's words wounded him very deeply. Sanjay's son, Manish, saw this. He did not like the behaviour father. His father was ill-treating his grandfather. He was afraid to speak against his father. He was sad about his grandfather. But he was not powerful to stand in support of his grandfather. The next day Manish took some of his father’s carpentry tools and a piece of wood. He worked with the tools to make a wooden plate. His father saw him working. “What are you making, Manish?" he asked. “I am making a wooden plate!" replied Manish. “A wooden plate! What for?" asked his father. “I am making it for you, father. When you grow old, like my grandfather, you will need a plate for food. A plate made from earth mat break very easily. Then I may scold you severely. So, I want to give you a wooden plate. It may not break so easily." The carpenter was shocked to hear this. Only now he realized his mistake. His father was kind to Sanjay. He had looked after him very well. Now, he was old. Sanjay was treating his father severely. He was now very sad about his own behavior. He realized his mistakes. He then became a different person. From that day, Sanjay treated his father with great respect. He gave up drinking too. Sanjay learnt a lesson from his own son. MORAL OF THE STORY- We must should honor our elders at all times. It is our duty. It brings us their blessings and makes them feel loved and honoured so never disobey your elders.
author: Niharika Chawla
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; Habib Ali; Nishith Mehta; Partho Sengupta; Priya Dali; Proiti Roy; Swathi Sambasivam; Wiehan de Jager

title: Unity is Strength!
text: Hi everyone! Today's class will be about Unity. So does anyone know about what unity means? No one raises their hand. Well unity means standing as one. This is a word for togetherness or oneness. So, today we are going to listen to a story about Unity. Once upon a time, an old man lived with his three sons in a village. The three sons were hard workers. Still, they quarrelled all the time. The old man tried a lot to unite them but he failed. Though the villagers appreciated their hard work and efforts, they made fun of them on their fights. Months passed by and the old man fell sick. He told his sons to stay united, but they didn’t listen to him. So, he decided to teach them a practical lesson so that they would forget their differences and stay united. The old man called his sons. He told them, “I will give you a bundle of sticks. Separate each stick and you will have to break each stick into two. The one who breaks the sticks quickly will be rewarded more.” The sons agreed. The old man gave a bundle of 10 sticks to each of them and asked them to break each stick into pieces. They broke the sticks into pieces in minutes. And again they started to quarrel among themselves as to who came first. The old man said, “Dear sons, the game is not over. Now I will give another bundle of sticks to each of you. You will have to break the sticks as a bundle, not as separate sticks.” The sons agreed and tried to break the bundle of sticks. Though they tried their best, they could not break the bundle. They failed to complete the task. The three sons reported their failure to their father. The old man replied, “Dear sons, See! You could easily break the single sticks into pieces, but you were not able to break the bundle! So, if you stay united, nobody can do any harm to you. If you quarrel every time with your brothers, anyone can easily defeat you. I request you to stay united.” The three sons understood the power of unity and promised their father that whatever be the situation, they would all stay together. So, how's the story? did you all like it? Well, I sure did. So can anyone tell me what they learnt from today's story? Few students raised their hands. Amelia, tell me what you learnt. Amelia replied, "I learnt that if we stay together no one can harm us or break us. Well done! I am happy to see that you understand the story well. Moral: United we stand divided we fall. Unity is Strength!
author: Rebecca  Motha
illustrator: Amy  Slatem; Emily  Berg; Maithili  Joshi; Manisha Naskar; Natasha  Mehra; Priya Kuriyan; Swathi Sambasivam

title: Shanti's friend
text: Shanti had to get up and make tea for her uncle and aunt. Shanti was 11 years old. He lived in the city with his uncle and aunt. It has not rained in Shanti Village for two years, He had no choice but to move to the city. The crops wither in the fields, There was little and no food for the villagers to eat. Shanti's dad fell ill and Mom didn't know what to do. She had no money to buy her medicine, and she had no food to feed Shanti, Papu, and Goodi. The children stopped going to school in the village. By the way, Shanti's uncles and aunts living in a big city were very nice people. “Don't worry,” said the uncle. “Shanti can live in the city with us.” “I can help with the housework and maybe even go to school,” said my aunt. “You are so kind to send me to school,” said Shanti's mother. “I’ll go to build a new road and see if it saves people. I could make a lot of money so we can all live together.” Shanti came to the city by bus with his uncle and aunt. The city was very big and dirty. There were many houses, but few trees. Shanti missed the banya n tree in the village he lived in before and the pond he often washed there. Here, you had to bring water from a roadside faucet into a bucket. Many people lined up to drink the water. Sometimes there were fights. Occasionally, someone pushed Shanti's water bottle aside and Shanti arrived home late. Then my uncle scolded me. Because my uncle had to wash with the water and was late for work. But Shanti knew he was lucky. There was plenty to eat here. And Mam Dara loved her baby. So she worked hard and wondered when she could go to school. If you ask her aunt, her aunt will say, “I don't have time for her to go to school. But next year it might be possible, when my heart is a little bigger.” She was shanty, she was disappointed, but she tried to do a good job. She, however, made mistakes from time to time. At that time, her uncle and aunt were angry. Shanti was scared when his uncle and aunt were angry. Her uncle's voice was as loud as thunder, and her face looked sharp as a sword. “Useless bitch!!” exclaimed uncle and aunt. “You are stupid, lazy and worth nothing!” Once, my uncle scolded Shanti a lot. Shanti was so scared that he ran away. 'I should just go home,' Shanti thought to himself. But I didn't have the money to buy a bus ticket. how can i do it? He sat under the tree and pondered. It was a nice tree. It wasn't as big as a banyan tree in town, but it had shade. Shanti leaned against the tree and closed her eyes. Suddenly someone whispered: “Don't cry, Shanty! you are a great kid You are very fast and clever.” Shanti looked around, but there was no one there. Maybe it's not a tree? Trees cannot speak. “Shanti, what do you think your aunt would have been without you? Who would have helped her aunt?” someone said again. “And if you hadn’t helped her aunt, how could she have fed Papu and her goodie?” Shanti knew she was right and she laughed. But no one has ever said that. Shanti also looked around her. ‘Some trees can speak,’ she thought. She shanty she wiped her tears and went home. After that, whenever work was done, I went to a tree and sat down. Sometimes I would take an old school book and scan it. She tried to read a few verses to the tree. The tree always said good things. She Shanti realized that she was not alone. I had a friend in this big city. I was no longer afraid. One morning Shanti woke up early as usual. I turned on the gas stove and made tea. I poured two cups of tea and went to give it to his uncle and aunt. I was about to enter the room quietly, but there was a knock at the door. Mamda got up and started crying. “Look what you did!” the aunt exclaimed. “Bring me a biscuit!” Shanti put the car down and ran quickly. Within a minute she returned with her biscuits. Aunt made her yawn. She put the shanty biscuits in her hand. She smiled as she put her biscuit in her mouth and looked at the shanty. Mamda waved her arm as she said, “Ahhhhhh~!” She laughed even Shanti. She heard everything she was saying: “Play with me!” But now I don't have time to play. Shanti had to bring water, wash the dishes, and prepare breakfast. In addition, I had to turn on the gas fire to cut vegetables and cook. “Later,” she said Shanti. "a little bit later." Shanti ran so fast that she couldn't see her feet. Her fingers her seemed to fly and when Santi was working she worked quickly from one side to the other. quickly! I had to sweep the floor before playing with Mamda. The dishes remained. Washed and washed and washed and washed again. Shanti Her hand moved as fast as it was flying again. Quickly, quickly—go! A plate fell from her hand! bang! There was the sound of a plate falling. Shanti was so scared that he ran away. I got out of the house and ran to the side of the road. I heard her aunt shout: “Shanti, you idiot! Do you know how expensive that plate is?” My aunt was really angry. It felt like hitting Shanti. Where can Shant i go? Where can she hide? ﻿s hanti ran to the tree friend. "Help me! Help me!” he shouted. The wide brown trunk of the tree was open. “Come in,” said the tree. There was a large hole in the trunk of the tree. Shanti ran and hid there. “Shanty! Shanti! You naughty girl, I won't let you go! I'll catch you, let's see!" Shanti laughed. “It's safe here. My aunt won't find me.” “ Shanty! Shanty! where are you? Her shanty curled her up and fell asleep. She had been sleeping for a while, but was woken up by the sound of a baby crying. it was like "Quiet!" She heard her aunt cry. But Mamda did not calm down. “Be quiet!” Mamda wept louder. Aunt is back! Is it dinner already? What is Shanti going to do? She just sat still in the tree as she continued. Safe away from those who scold the shanties. Mamda was crying even louder. “I really can’t stop crying. It would be nice if Shanti was here, but I know how to appease Mamda. Oh, where did she run to?” said the aunt. “You scold him too much.” said his uncle. “How are you going to explain it to the Shanti parents? I'm really in trouble!" “I won’t scold you any more. Suddenly the tree spoke again. “If you want to go, you can go,” she said intimately. “But you can come back anytime.” "really? Can I really come back?” “Of course not. This place will always be here, just for you.” Shanti took a deep breath. Shall we go back? Mamda was crying very loudly. "okay. I'll go now. But if you want to come back, I will come again.” “Come anytime...” whispered the tree. The trunk of the tree opened, and Shanti went out. Shanti walked slowly home and rang the doorbell. Uncle opened the door. “Shanty? Where have you been?” asked my uncle. “I went to see a friend,” Shanti replied. “I was tired. And Shanty...I'll check the school tomorrow." Shanti looked out the window and looked at the tree friend. He smiled and said nothing. Now I will no longer be afraid. title: Help a friend
text: it was a holiday and Imani, Aliyah and Nia went out for a walk. "What a beautiful day" said Imani. "The sky so blue and the sun so bright" Nia said. "Lets go near the river" said Aliyah. title: The Two Brothers!
text: ONE- Once upon a time, two brothers who lived on adjoining farms fell into conflict. It was the first serious rift in 40 years of farming side by side, sharing machinery, and trading labour and goods as needed without a hitch. Then the long collaboration fell apart. It began with a small misunderstanding and it grew into a major difference, and finally, it exploded into an exchange of bitter words followed by weeks of silence. TWO- One morning there was a knock on John's door. He opened it to find a man with a carpenter's toolbox. "I'm looking for a few days work," he said. "Perhaps you would have a few small jobs here and there. Could I help you?" "Yes," said the older brother. "I do have a job for you. Look across the creek at that farm. That's my neighbour. In fact, it's my younger brother. Last week there was a meadow between us and he took his bulldozer to the river levee and now there is a creek between us. Well, he may have done this to spite me, but I'll go him one better. See that pile of lumber curing by the barn? I want you to build me a fence - an 8-foot fence - so I won't need to see his place anymore." THREE- The carpenter said, "I think I understand the situation. Show me the nails and the post-hole digger and I'll be able to do a job that pleases you." The older brother had to go to town for supplies, so he helped the carpenter get the materials ready and then he was off for the day. The carpenter worked hard all that day measuring, sawing and nailing. About sunset when the farmer returned, the carpenter had just finished his job. The farmer's eyes opened wide, his jaw dropped. There was no fence there at all! FOUR- It was a bridge - a bridge stretching from one side of the creek to the other! A fine piece of work - handrails and all - and the neighbour, his younger brother, was coming across, his hand outstretched. "You are quite a fellow to build this bridge, after all, I've said and done." The two brothers stood at each end of the bridge, and then they met in the middle, taking each other's hand. They turned to see the carpenter hoist his toolbox on his shoulder. "No, wait! Stay a few days. I have a lot of other projects for you," said the older brother. "I'd love to stay on," the carpenter said, " but I have many more bridges to build!"

title: The way Sun moves
text: Every day we see the sun. It rises in the morning and goes back down in the evening, and then comes night. The way we are able to see the sun in our country, just like that can other countries see the sun, daily the same way too? In India, the sun can be seen 250-300 days a year. But in some countries, the sun rises up but doesn't go down for days or it goes down but doesn't rise up for days. This happens in Canada, Finland, Greenland, Norway, Ruse, Sweden, and Iceland's northern side. In these countries, the sun can only be seen between April and August. During that time there is summer over there, and the sun is up 24 hours of the day. When winter comes the sun goes down and it stays like that for the entire winter, the sun is down so it's dark too. The people who live here are used to this. One more example of this is the continent of Antarctica. In Antarctica, the sun rises only in the winter months. Sun only rises there after the month of September. The sun doesn't go down for months. The sun starts to go down in March. This difference of day and night happens because of the earth rotating around the sun and because it is tilted a little bit. Because of it spinning around on its axis and being stuck to it a lot of interesting things happen in the world
