title: The Dordles  Go Home (Book 3)
text: The Dordles were lost and needed fuel to get home. They had tried coal, wood and oil as fuel but they were of little help. The Dordles needed to find a better fuel to take them home. Fuel like coal took millions of years to form. There was very little coal left on Earth. So the Dordles went looking for fuel that was there in plenty and would never run out. Dordle B set sail for the seas looking for energy sources. Along the way, he found: Rivers Dams Tides Waterfalls Dordle D took to the skies and realised that she could harness the energy of the wind and use it to power their ship. Dordle E packed his bags and said goodbye to the others. He would travel to the Sun and steal its fire. Sadly he didn’t make it all the way to the Sun, but did find a way to use its energy. The Dordles found all sorts of new sources of energy. Like geothermal energy, using the heat from under the earth. And nuclear energy, which they got by splitting very small particles called atoms. They built devices that helped them better harness energy. After months of trying, the Dordles finally had the energy they needed. They turned on their engines, fastened their seatbelts, lifted off, and zoomed away from Earth. What Is Renewable Fuel? Renewable energy is collected from renewable sources in nature. Sunlight, wind, rain, waves and geothermal energy (heat from the ground) are always around us, regardless of how much we use them. Biofuel is made from agricultural, industrial and domestic waste. We can harness energy from these sources and use it to power our houses, vehicles and factories. Energy from these sources is less polluting. What Is Nuclear Fuel? Nuclear fuels are used in power plants to generate heat and electricity. Heat is created when the nuclear fuel undergoes nuclear fission. This is where an atom with a large nucleus is split into two or more atoms with smaller nuclei. The nuclear fission reaction produces a lot of heat, which is then used to generate electricity. Nuclear energy is not renewable since the nuclear fuel has to be mined.
author: C G Salamander

title: The Dordles Find Fuel (Book 1)
text: The Dordles were lost and needed lots and lots of fuel to get home. Their ship needed energy to lift off, and the Dordles needed fuel to generate energy. So they made a list of all the fuels they could think of, and left in search of them. Dordle B, the leader of the group, burrowed into the ground in search of coal. But he was surprised to find almost all the coal used up. So he left with a piece of coal the size of his hand. Dordle D, the smartest of the three, trekked to the densest forest. But she was shocked to see just one tree. Dordle D had to settle for a few dry branches. Dordle E, the tiniest Dordle, sailed to the oil fields that never dried up. Dordle E was lucky to leave with a few drops of oil. The Dordles gathered their fuel, and put it into their ship to burn and generate energy. The engines roared, the lights came alive, the ship lifted off. But sadly they didn’t get very far. Disappointed, the Dordles did what Dordles do best. They ate till their tummies reached their chest. What Is Fuel? A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy when it undergoes a chemical reaction. Materials such as coal, wood, oil and gas provide us with heat, light and energy when they are burned. Energy can be used to cook our food, keep us warm and make our engines run. Fuels come in different forms. They can be solids like wood and coal, liquids like petrol and kerosene, or gases like Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) and biogas. We use fuel to drive cars, generate electricity for homes and power factories.
author: C G Salamander

title: The Dordles Save Fuel (Book 2)
text: The Dordles were lost and needed to get home. They had used up all the coal, wood and oil they had collected. Now they needed to find and use fuel smartly. They learned that coal came from animal bones and plants, kept under pressure for millions of years. But there was very little coal left on Earth. So they came up with a plan. Dordle B, the oldest Dordle, left to get firewood. He only used fallen branches, and planted more trees when he was done. Dordle D, the brightest Dordle, turned off all the lights on the ship to save energy. While Dordle E, the youngest Dordle, buried a bone he found, with the hope of it turning into coal. The Dordles looked for other ways to save fuel. They replaced things that were broken and things that used too much energy. They cycled and walked when they searched for fuel. They even found bio-waste and turned it into biofuel. The Dordles had collected more fuel than before. They were sure that they would be able to leave the planet this time. They started their engines, put on their seatbelts, and their ship zoomed into the sky. Tired and hungry, the Dordles knew what to do next. They ate till their tummies touched their necks. This time, the Dordles got far, but not far enough. What Are Fossil Fuels? Fossil fuels are fuels that were formed from the buried remains of plants and animals that lived millions of years ago. They are found naturally under the earth, and are the most-used fuels in the world. Fuels such as coal, crude oil and natural gas are all considered fossil fuels because they originally came from fossils. Fossil fuels are limited in quantity, because it takes millions of years to make them. They are also bad for the environment. Burning fossil fuels produces too much carbon dioxide. This leads to global warming and the melting of the ice caps, causing the oceans to rise and climate change to speed up. Luckily, just like the Dordles, the world is looking to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and switch to fuels that are clean and safe for the environment.
author: C G Salamander

title: The Nightingales house

She also wanted to live there, but all the birds denied her from living there. The nightingale got sad. She didn't have anywhere else to live. There was now a very slight sunshine. There was a swan swimming in the river. The swan would either pet its neck with its beak, otherwise he touched the water with it. The nightingale sat at the river-bank, looking sad. Suddenly, the swan looked over at the nightingale. He swan over to her, and asked "O nightingale, why are you so sad?". The nightingale replied "My house has broken down. The birds living on the Banyan tree have not allowed me to live there either. Now where do I go, what do I do?" "Come with me", and the swan took the nightingale with him. Both of them reached the other end, to find a big Peepal tree. "From today, you will live in this tree." The swan told the Nightingale. She was very happy, and both of them became good friends Then, one day, there was a flood in the river. Due to it, the Banyan tree had wet soil collecting around it. When the nightingale saw this, she quickly told all the birds that the tree could fall at any point and that their children were not safe. The crow said that they needed to find a new place to live, quickly. The nightingale said softly, "My peepal tree is very big. You all can come live there." Everybody followed the nightingale to the tree and lived there happily. The nightingale had also made a lot of new friends!

title: Mama Mia
text: The Runaround Express train ran through a landscape of charming hills, tunnels and valleys in the Himachal region making twelve stops. On one cold December night, the signal was red and the train came to a screeching halt at an unscheduled stop at a station called Shantigaon. The clock at the station struck midnight. The station was deserted. There was slight snowfall that night. The snowflakes shone brightly under the streetlights and fell softly on the grass next to the platform. Shantigaon was as silent as its name. Now, it so happened that there lived a rich landlord named Ajay in Shantigaon. He was the village chief. He hated noise of any kind. He lived all alone in a large mansion. He was very grumpy, and he considered Silence literally Golden! He never played. He never sang. He never even laughed. Even the villagers had become this way. The children in Shantigaon never giggled. The people didn’t chit-chat. Even the dogs didn’t bark. But all of that was about to change. A lone passenger got off the train at Shantigaon that day. He was wiry thin and wore a very long checkered coat. He carried a guitar case and had a rucksack slung over his back. He settled himself on a wooden seat on the platform and dozed off. Mamma Mia thus arrived in Shantigaon. The next morning, at the crack of dawn, he strolled into the village. “Where can I get some breakfast?” he asked the tea vendor who silently pointed to the stall nearby. ‘That’s strange!’ he thought. He was used to being asked a million questions by villagers when he was touring. ‘Where do you come from? ‘What is your profession? What brings you here? Where are you going?’ and such. Mamma Mia loved to talk and share his travel tales. He walked up to the food stall and asked the waiter, “Hey buddy, what can I get for breakfast today?” The waiter handed him a menu and silently walked away to clear the dishes from the nearby table. ‘So strange!’ Mamma Mia thought. A few children were playing cricket nearby. Not a single sound from them too! None of them waved at him. ‘Very strange!’ he thought. He spent an hour walking about and observing everything around the village. He was very perplexed. Not a single villager spoke to him. They went about their chores completely ignoring him. Such a strange village! He walked up to an old banyan tree and sat down. He decided he would make the people of this village have some fun today. He’d make them talk and laugh and perhaps even dance. He opened his rucksack and pulled out a glittering red box. As soon as he unclasped the lid, a flash of light emerged from it. Several small stars glittered in rainbow hues around the box. Several villagers saw the spectacle and gathered around him. Curious, a small child walked up to him. Her name was Azka. Mamma Mia took out a shiny neon green candy from the box and gave it to her. The candy was glowing. A barber from a nearby shop could not contain his curiosity and came forward to try the candy too. Mama Mia offered his candies to everyone around. Now, the candies were mischievously special. They made you share all the funny and embarrassing stories from your life. Azka was the first one to start. She shared her amusing tale. “I went to the island city last year,” she began, giggling. “And I was standing near a fountain for a picture. On a whim, I dipped my toe in the fountain and waddled my foot in the water to strike a pose. Before I could say cheese, I lost my balance and toppled over, headfirst into the fountain! I was quite a sight as I came out drenched from the freezing cold water. Everyone was laughing. And my brother was laughing the loudest!” As soon as she had narrated her tale, she gasped and clasped her mouth. She realized she had just told everyone about the most embarrassing moment in her life. But soon, the village wrestler went on to share his funny story from his visit to the beach last week. He had been standing under a tree and gloating about how strong he was when a coconut fell on his head. He was knocked out for one hour! More laughter followed as more and more stories were told by the villagers. By now, a large crowd gathered around Mama Mia owing to the commotion. The news reached Ajay and he rushed on his horse to where the crowd had gathered. “What is this ruckus you are creating in our village?” he screamed pointing his stick at Mama Mia. “And why are you all giggling so much? Don’t you know that this village is called Shantigaon and you are supposed to maintain SILENCE!” he shouted, quite mad at the villagers. “Why do you like silence my friend?” asked Mama Mia. “What is life without a little madness… a little fun… a little laughter for everyone?” Mamma Mia stood up and began to play his guitar. A melodious and mesmerizing tune emerged from the notes he strummed. The song rose in pitch and tempo and all the kids and villagers began to dance. “ Songs are special, songs are sweet They always help you stay upbeat. Sing a song and dance along And you will live for very long Play a flute or play a drum With your bro or your bum chum Music is special, and one of a kind It brings a little madness in your mind! So sing with me… yea dance with me… And have a little fun with me…” Mama Mia reached out with his hand to Ajay asking him to join in with the dancing villagers. Ajay hesitated at first, but soon the magical tunes from the guitar won him over and he tried to match the dance steps shown by Mama Mia. When the melody of the music died down, the food stall owner got some snacks for everyone. Ajay slowly walked away from the crowd and stood staring at his reflection in the water by the lakeside. Mama Mia walked up to him and put an arm around his shoulders. “Tell me, why do you not like to have fun? It is not a crime! Why do you enforce silence in your village?” “It was a long time ago,” Ajay narrated his tale. "I lived in my beautiful village in the south amid lush greenery and sunflower fields. I loved playing the flute and often sat on the banyan tree and played the flute in the evenings on the outskirts of the village. On one December evening, we got news that a gang of bandits would be passing by our village. If we maintained silence and avoided any light, they may pass by without attacking the village. The village chief asked us to maintain absolute silence and darkness in the village. No one would make any loud sound. No one was to light a fire or switch on any lights. Everyone followed the rule. Except me." “After a game of cricket, I was exhausted. And like always, I pulled out my flute, sat on the tree, and started to play. I had completely forgotten about the village chief’s instructions. The bandits heard the tune and attacked our village late that evening. Many villagers lost their life savings and belongings. Many were hurt.” Tears were streaming down Ajay’s face as he narrated his tale. “My dad held his head in shame as the villagers accused me of their misfortunes. When I went back to the village, I saw the rampage with my own eyes. I decided I would never play the flute again!” “It’s not your fault. You were just a little kid. Don’t be so harsh on yourself,” comforted Mama Mia. “Look. Everyone in this village loves you! They follow all your instructions. Let them have some fun sometimes! Teach the kids how to play the flute! Let them enjoy the joy of music that you enjoyed as a child!” Ajay nodded and wiped his tears as he walked back to the banyan tree where the villagers had gathered. “I have an announcement to make,” Ajay called out in his authoritarian voice. “I want all the children in Shantigaon to learn a musical instrument from today.” “What will you learn?” he asked, looking at Azka. “A banjo!” she said excitedly. “What about you all?” Ajay asked the other children. “I will learn to play the dholak,” said one kid; “A guitar,” said another; “A mouth organ,” said a third. A frail voice called out from a cot in the corner, “A sitar.” It was eighty-four-year-old Kamalaji. Everyone cheered. The landlord arranged a feast for the village that evening. They had a grand campfire. Mamma Mia burst out singing his favorite songs as the villagers cheered along. As he walked around the campfire, Mamma Mia’s footsteps left a colorful trail. A burst of red, blue and green flashed every time his foot stomped on the snow. The kids followed him around as he played his guitar. “What will you learn?” he asked, looking at Azka. “A banjo!” she said excitedly. “What about you all?” Ajay asked the other children. One by one they shot up their hands to answer. “I will learn to play the dholak,” said one kid; “A guitar,” said another; “A mouth organ,” said a third. A frail voice called out from a cot in the corner, “A sitar.” It was eighty-four-year-old Kamalaji. Everyone cheered for her. The landlord arranged a feast for the village that evening. They had a grand campfire. Mamma Mia burst out singing his favorite songs as the villagers sang along. As he walked around the campfire, Mamma Mia’s footsteps left a colorful trail. A burst of red, blue and green flashed every time his foot stomped on the snow. The kids followed him around as he played his guitar. At ten p.m. that night, Mamma Mia packed his rucksack and bid goodbye to the villagers. The entire village followed him to the station. “Can’t you teach me to play the guitar like you? Why do you have to go?” asked Azka, holding Mamma Mia’s hand in hers and tugging at his rucksack. At 10 p.m. that night, Mamma Mia packed his rucksack and bid goodbye to the villagers. The entire village followed him to the station. “Can’t you teach me to play the guitar like you? Why do you have to go?” asked Azka, holding Mamma Mia’s hand in hers and tugging at his rucksack. “I will come back again with wonderful magic tricks and treats for you!” said Mamma Mia, giving her a high five. “But remember, only if you have learnt a new musical instrument!” “Come back soon!” she called as Mamma Mia boarded the train. From that day onwards, the villagers at Shantigaon enjoyed every moment of their lives. They laughed, giggled, gossiped, danced and, of course, they learnt to play musical instruments. Life in Shantigaon was as fun-packed as Mamma Mia’s songs. “I will come back again with wonderful magic tricks and treats for you!” said Mamma Mia, giving her a high five. “But remember, only if you have learned a new musical instrument!” “Come back soon!” she called as Mamma Mia boarded the train. From that day onwards, the villagers at Shantigaon enjoyed every moment of their lives. They laughed, giggled, gossiped, danced and, of course, learnt to play musical instruments. Life in Shantigaon was as fun-packed as Mamma Mia’s songs.

title: Loyal Subjects
text: One evening, a fox went to her house only to find a beautiful diamond ring. It was very shiny, and the fox was shocked to see it. Whose ring could it be, and why did they leave it here? The fox was tensed. What could she do with such an expensive ring. She thought for a while, and then decided to leave for the Kings palace. She reached the palace in an instant, and told the whole story in one breath. The king smiled after hearing her story and said, "I know whose ring it is". The fox was more surprised than ever after hearing what the king said. She said, " Your Majesty, you should immediately return the ring to its owner. Whoever is its owner must be upset right now.". "This ring belongs to you. I was testing the loyalty of my subjects. I left this ring on your door. You have passed the test, and now you may keep it." The fox was overjoyed. Tears of happiness coming out her eyes, she thanked the king and returned home.
author: Mukund Sharma

title: The lion and the squirrel
text: There was once a den. In that den lived Doris Lion. He was very dangerous. Near the den lived Briec squirrel. He was also super smart. Some squirrels even called him a walking encyclopedia! One fine day Doris went to find some food. He did not notice a glue puddle the hunters had made. When he got stuck in there he tried to get out. But he realised that Rita Rabbit was also stuck and very close to him, he reached for Rita Rabbit but he suddenly remembered he was stuck! He was terrified! What is gonna happen Doris thought. Briec heard Doris's cries and went to see what happened. He took a rope and lassoed Doris and Rita. He blew a whistle and the other squirrels came they all pulled and Doris and Rita came out. Rita was ungrateful, but Doris was grateful. He and Briec became friends. Briec 's mom told him Doris had invited him."Bye mom," Briec said as he scurried away. Briec went to the lions home. The lioness was not happy. She was muttering in the lion's ear "You can't be friends with your food." One day the lioness got a plan. She wrote a letter. Turn the page to see what she wrote. DEAR WHATEVER YOUR NAME IS, THE LION DOES NOT WANT YOU HERE NOW RUN AWAY BEFORE HE EATS YOU. LOVE LIONESS💔 Briec was heartbroken. He turned to Doris and said "Bye." "Bye? What do you mean?" said Doris. "Well, the lioness said you did not want me.You do not love me," said Briec. "No, I do want you.The lioness does not want you" said Doris. "Doris? Maybe that is why she wrote the" "letter yes," interrupted Doris. Then they both hugged. The End💌

title: North, South, East, West
text: Dear Class 4B, Priya Miss must have told you that I won’t be coming to school for the next five months. I’m travelling across India with Amma and Appa. July 26, 2019 They will teach me history, geography, science and maths. But I’ll be back next year. I miss you all and hope you miss me too. Love, Shaana Hi everyone, You won’t believe where I am! July 30, 2019 Love, Shaana I’m way up north, at the Thajiwas glacier in Kashmir. The glaciers are white and blue and we have to wear four layers of clothes. Appa and Amma love it here, and they like throwing snowballs at each other. But they say there was much more snow last year. I also like the snow, but my hands are shaking from not wearing gloves, so I don’t think I can write any more. Send my love to PT Miss and Library Sir. Dear Class, We took another train yesterday and reached Himachal Pradesh. It is very quiet, and we can see so many mountains from our cabin. Colourful birds wake me with their chirping when the sun rises in the east. August 15, 2019 I also think I hear bears growling in the west when it gets dark. But Amma says that’s just Appa snoring. I would love to meet a bear and give it a hug. With love from your best friend, Shaana Hi everyone, Did you know that Arunachal Pradesh is far away from Himachal Pradesh? Himachal is in the north but Arunachal is all the way in the east. I thought all the Pradesh states sat next to each other. We took two trains and drove a long time to get here. This morning, we walked through a forest to reach our treehouse. The forest here is so thick that if you blink or stop to tie your shoelaces, you will get lost. August 27, 2019 I love Arunachal the best so far and am beginning to enjoy myself. I hope we get to see red pandas. With love, Shaana September 2, 2019 Dear classmates, It did not take any time at all to travel south west and get to the Sundarbans in West Bengal. Today, Amma and Appa took me out onto the river in a small boat. Amma tells me that places like the Sundarbans are called wetlands. I never knew such a place existed, and that it was possible for trees called mangroves to grow in seawater! But Amma is sad about how much this place floods today. We also saw crocodiles and a lonely snake while boating. I hope they don’t follow us home. How is everyone? Are you missing me yet? Love, Shaana September 29, 2019 Hi everyone, We travelled across the country, all the way from east to west, from West Bengal to Gujarat, and it took us two and a half days! I don’t know why my Amma and Appa brought me to the middle of the desert. It’s hot, dry, and there’s sand everywhere. It’s like a beach without the sea! But I do really love the clothes here. They’re so pretty and colourful. I am sure you’re all studying hard for your half-yearly exams. Amma gave me a test today, and I passed with 88 per cent. Love, Shaana October 1, 2019 Dear class, Today was the best day ever! We drove east from the desert to the Narmada river, which flows all the way to the centre of India, and it only took us six hours. In the afternoon, Amma, Appa and I went rafting in the river and you won’t believe how wild and scary it was. I always thought rivers were calm, but up close they’re really fast. Appa says that there used to be a lot more water, and rafting was much scarier then. I was fully wet by the time I was done, and Appa was so scared that he swore never to go rafting ever again. I love the water so much and can’t wait to go back. Your best friend, Shaana October 20, 2019 Dear classmates, Amma and Appa are fast asleep, and I should be sleeping too, but I just love looking out the window. I think we’re in the southwest part of the country, in Goa, and you won’t believe how nice the plateaus look. There are so many hills here, and beaches too. There are also a lot of tunnels that the train goes through. I used to be afraid of tunnels, but I’m not any more. Someday, I wish we could all go on a tour of the plateaus. Maybe when we’re in class 11. Love, Shaana November 1, 2019 Dear friends, I can’t believe we’re in the same state again! We travelled south, and I will be home soon. We reached Chennai yesterday, and on the way to Puducherry, we decided to learn how to surf. I think I’m good at it now because I only fell down twice. Amma and Appa splashed water on each other and behaved like children. It’s a good thing I was there to control them. The beaches here are not like the ones we have on our island. The waves are a lot rougher and the water is browner, but I still like it here. Your best friend, Shaana November 21, 2019 Hi everyone, I just crossed the Pamban bridge. I could see the ocean on both sides. How amazing that a train can travel across the sea like this! I’m almost home, and I can’t wait to give you my final letter in person. Love, Shaana November 23, 2019 Dear classmates, I thought Amma and Appa would be tired from all our travelling, but we made one last stop at the Olaikaadu beach before we reached home. And I’m so happy we did. Amma wanted to teach me how to dive, but they did not have diving suits my size, so I spent the day floating and looking at the fish while my parents dove below me. We found all sorts of pebbles on the beach, and I can’t wait to give them to you in person tomorrow. Your best friend, Shaana December 1, 2019 Dear Amma and Appa, I can’t believe we travelled across the whole country! I know we’re going to miss visiting the forests, glaciers, deserts, wetlands, plateaus and mountains. And we are going to miss hearing all those new languages and meeting all those different people. But we’re finally home now, and we can join our friends again. I hope we get to travel like this again, and maybe next time we can take our friends with us. With love, Shaana *Map is not to scale and only for the sake of representation
author: C G Salamander

title: Once upon a Coin
text: “Daee, can we please see your coin collection?” asks Banko. Banko is very keen to know more about coins. He likes to spend Sundays finding old ones so that he can also have a collection like Daee. “What do you see on these coins, Banko?” asks Daee. “INDIA!” says Banko. “And three lions.” “This side with the lions is called ‘heads’,” says Daee. “That’s a bull and a horse pulling a wheel or chakra. Just like the chakra at the centre of our flag. “And Daee, what are these two animals below the lions?” asks Banko. “Now Banko, if you flip the coin, you will see the ‘tails’ side. Look it says five rupees, which is the value of the coin,” says Daee. “What is special about this coin, Daee?” “This is a 2-rupee coin celebrating the ninth Asian Games held in 1982, the year your mother was born.” “Look Daee, here’s one from 2015, the year I was born. It’s a coin that celebrates Dr B.R. Ambedkar’s 125th birth anniversary!” says Banko. “Coins are so heavy, Daee!” says Banko. “That is why we have notes. They are light and easy to use,” says Daee. On these coins, can you spot... a) Our national animal? b) The person who wrote India’s national anthem? c) The national flower? d) The place where the leaders of the country gather? e) An ancient form of exercise? Answers: a) Tiger b) Rabindranath Tagore, c) Lotus d) Parliament of India e) Yoga
author: Mala Kumar

title: How Anansi found a wife
text: Anansi was enjoying himself. He had nothing to worry about. Suddenly Anansi thought he wanted a wife. All the male forest animals had wives. Anansi climbed a tree to see if any village was there. But if Anansi wanted to go to a village he had cross the river. But the river was infected with crocodiles. Hungry crocodiles. But it started raining as soon as he got down from the tree. Anansi took shelter in a cave nearby the river. Anansi began daydreaming. But suddenly there was a snore. The cave was home to the crocodiles! Anansi began to tickle the crocodiles. Please don't tickle us pleaded the crocodiles. Ferry me across the river commanded Anansi. The crocodiles obediently ferried Anansi across the river. Anansi found a woman standing near the river and asked her if she would be his wife. The woman agreed happily. Then the crocodiles ferried Anansi and his new wife back to the forest. Soon they were married and lived happily ever after.

title: Rajmohana Keloth: The Bug Finder and Her Big World of Tiny Insects
text: It was nap time at the nursery school. While the rest of her classmates were asleep, four-year-old Mohana watched an army of ants marching in a row. Mohana gently picked up the ants in her palm, and discovered they have a distinct odour, an unpleasant one. She often watched the praying mantis sitting on the wall, move its foreleg from side to side, waiting for its prey. She carried green grasshoppers on the back of her palm when they accidentally hopped indoors. On rainy days, she squatted by the swarms of termites on the floor and felt their wings with her fingertips. She watched as their wings fell off and the insects walked away, untroubled. Mohana longed to become a scientist who studies insects. Years later, she studied zoology, joined the Zoological Survey of India and became an entomologist pursuing taxonomy. An entomologist studies insects. Some entomologists study insect taxonomy. They identify and organise different species of insects by shape, by size, by pattern and even the way they develop over time. Mohana’s job took her to the deepest jungles. No one had seen women travel to far-flung remote areas for forest surveys, but Mohana had become an entomologist to discover unusual species of insects. On her first forest survey, she wore flimsy shoes, which gave way, and she had to walk through the forest, barefoot. This taught her never to step out without a pair of good field shoes. It was twilight in the Wayanad hills when Mohana saw a banyan tree sparkling as though lit up by stars. As she tiptoed near it, she spotted thousands of fireflies. Deep in the Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary in Kannur, she came across a resting population of migrating milkweed butterflies. There were also thousands of blue tiger butterflies on low branches of a tree. Sensing movement, all the butterflies set to flight as one, as Mohana gasped in wonder. Mohana’s work drove her to study the tiny wasps that belonged to the Hymenoptera insect family. The wasps were so minuscule that they couldn’t be identified without a microscope, but they played an important role in maintaining balance in the ecosystem. She studied their habits, published research papers on them and discovered over 150 new species. Mohana even had a species named after her, Dipara mohanae. From wasps to termites, the more species Mohana found, the more she wanted to discover. Insects are pollinators, pests, soil engineers and more — they influence human lives in many ways. Being an entomologist, Rajmohana Keloth knows and appreciates this every day. Get to know Mohana May 9, 1971: Rajmohana Keloth’s birthday. 1975: Mohana’s first memory of observing insects. 1993: Mohana completes her post graduation in zoology specialising as an entomologist. 1994: She gets her dream job and joins the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) as a junior research fellow. 1996: Discovers four unknown species of insects and has her first new species publication. 1999: Gets her PhD degree and joins postdoctoral research. 2004: Rejoins the Zoological Survey of India as a scientist and has worked there ever since. Mohana’s favourite bugs Nasute termite soldier Click beetle Bumblebee Stream glory damselfly Antlion Clearwing moth
author: Shweta Ganesh Kumar

title: A tree of stars
text: Once upon a time there was a seed in a forest, which was just beginning to sprout its first leaves. She was deeply excited to finally see the world. One day an ant came by that was building its tunnel and the seed asked him: -Hormiguita, you who know the world above, tell me what is the most beautiful? - The excited ant told her: -There are many beautiful things in this world. There are flowers, blackberries and acorns. But what I like the most are the stars because they are as brilliant as little diamonds. The excited seed replied: -When I grow up I want to be a tree of stars.- -Semillita, the stars do not hang from the trees but from the sky. - explained the ant From that day on, the seed spent her days imagining what her life would hopefully be like if she could be a star. As time went by, the seed sprouted from the ground and became a small plant. Anxiously she waited for the arrival of night to meet the stars. When she saw them for the first time her little leaves trembled. "They are beautiful!" She exclaimed in wonder. A beetle trying to sleep in a nearby bush woke up to hearing the great commotion. "Is everything okay, little plant?" Asked the scared beetle. -I apologize, today is the first time that I have seen the stars and now that I have met them, I know that one day I will be a tree so tall that I will be able to caress the stars with my branches- The somewhat incredulous beetle explained to her -The stars are beautiful, they always make me happy in the darkness of the night. But they live very, very high in the sky. No matter how high I have flown, I have never been close to reaching them. - The beetle's words did not discourage the little plant. Every day she struggled to grow and grow. With her roots she looked for the best nutrients and little by little she grew bigger until she transformed into a young tree. One day a bird began to create its nest in the branches of the young tree. As she watched him build his nest, the young tree asked him: -Bird you who fly higher than the pines, have you ever met a star? - -No, young tree, I have never flown so high, but the stars always guide my flight at night, they help me not to get lost.- With each new thing the young tree learned about the stars, she wanted to know more and more about them. Months passed and although the young tree struggled to grow, she no longer grew taller. She stretched her branches, moved her roots but could not grow any more. One day something surprising happened, apples began to grow from her branches. They were bright red, throughout the forest all the animals came to see such beautiful apples. The rabbit and the caterpillar said they were the best they had ever tasted. But the young tree, who just discovered that she was an apple tree, was not happy about the surprising event. She wanted to be a tall tree so she could meet the stars. But to the surprise of everyone in the forest, she was an apple tree. The only apple tree in the whole forest, the shortest tree in the entire forest. The travelers who were crossing the forest, noticed the beautiful red glow of the apples and their rich flavor and began to take short breaks under the branches of the apple tree. Even so, every night the apple tree looked at the sky and was full of sadness gazing at the stars. One night the ant, worried to see his friend the apple tree so sad, he told her: -Dear apple tree, do not be sad, your apples are a beautiful gift. They are the brightest red color I have ever seen and their flavor makes everyone who eats them happy. All the animals in the forest love you and take care of you. You even help humans not to get lost on their way through the forest and give them a comfortable place to rest. With the ant's words the apple tree rejoiced. Although she was disappointed that she was not taller and could not meet the stars, she decided to strive to make the richest and most beautiful apples possible. One day a traveler and his daughter sat down to rest under the shade of the apple tree. The girl after eating with her father, began to climb the branches. While playing among the branches, she picked apples to continue their journey. Suddenly an apple fell to the ground and broke in half. The girl hurried down from the tree to see the apple that had fallen. Surprised, she ran to show her dad what she had found inside the apple. -Dad, look at a star, the apple has a star inside! The apple tree that was listening carefully could not believe what she was hearing and seeing. All her life she had struggled to meet the stars without realizing that within her beautiful apples there were stars. Stars that shone, that cheered and that guided travelers on their way. In the end the apple tree had managed to be a tree of stars. Short story based on the story "The apple that wanted to be a star"
author: Alexis  Ferrari

title: Every Minute Counts
text: Adil is always late to school. His class teacher, Miss Rupal, is angry. “You missed 15 minutes of maths class today,” she scolds him. “You missed 15 minutes of art yesterday.” Adil feels terrible. “Why am I never on time?” he asks his best friend Paro. “Where do all the minutes go?” Paro decides to help Adil find the lost minutes. “At what time do you wake up?” she asks. “Ma wakes me up at 8am,” Adil says. “If I’m feeling lazy, I lie in bed for five more minutes.” “What do you do next?” Paro asks. “I take 25 minutes to get ready and 15 minutes to eat breakfast. It takes 20 minutes to walk to school. "Together, that is one hour. I should reach school by 9am.” Paro writes, 25 + 15 + 20 = 60. 60 minutes make an hour. “Do you always get ready on time?” Paro asks. “Sometimes I have to sharpen my pencil,” Adil says. "Sometimes my milk is too hot to drink. “Sometimes I have to find my Hindi book. But those things take seconds.” “If you add all the seconds, you will get four or five minutes,” Paro laughs. “Maybe three minutes,” Adil agrees. 60 seconds make a minute. 180 seconds make three minutes. “I have seen you playing with Bittu’s puppies and buying sweets on the way to school,” Paro says. “I play with the puppies for five minutes,” Adil says. “And spend less than two minutes buying sweets. That makes no difference.” “Every minute makes a difference,” Paro says. “If you add the extra time in bed, the time to sharpen pencils and everything else, you take 75 minutes to get to school.” 5 minutes extra in bed 3 minutes extra while getting ready 5 minutes playing with the puppies 2 minutes buying sweets = 15 minutes “That is not one hour,” Paro says. “That is one hour and 15 minutes. Do you know what that means?” “Yes,” Adil groans. “It means that I will have to wake up 15 minutes early — at 7.45am. "It means Miss Rupal will be happy, and I will be sleepy and sad.”

title: Win some, Lose a Few
text: That's Riddhi and Siddhi! That they are best buddies, all can see!!! They are so different, yes poles apart, Siddhi loves Cricket, and Riddhi loves painting and art… Riddhi is Siddhi's biggest Cheerleader, when Siddhi hits the Sixes and Fours with the most precise aim!!! "My Bestie Siddhi is better than Sachin and Virat," Riddhi does claim! Siddhi is most proud, the cup in her hand says it all... She's sure, she will win each match, big or small! And with Riddhi there to cheer, She is most confident, she has no fear... But today Siddhi is angry, she's lost the match, you see. And she also feels betrayed by her best buddy!!! In rage when Siddhi tossed her bat! Riddhi scolded her JUST FOR THAT! She's decided, she hates Riddhi. And she hates cricket too. She's going to play a new game. Also make friends brand new! For a bit it's fun, b ut soon she realizes it's not the same. She really misses her bestie and her striking Game! Her Baba seeing her face asks, " Why the gloom, why are you so sad?" "Baba it's the Cricket and Riddhi who has made me so mad!" Soon she tells him all, But her Baba just hands her the bat and the ball! And her Baba says, "You win some, you lose a few. "You just pick up that bat again and continue... Also, Riddhi and this bat are your best friends, You'll lose it all, if soon you don't make amends..." Siddhi soon realizes her folly. All she needs is her friend to keep her jolly. Yes in life you win some, you lose a few... But Friendship so precious, you should always value! Good friends are precious pearls, valuable and rare, Win or lose, rain or sunshine they will be there. Dear Friends, there is something more to learn too... It's all about enjoying the game, it's never about losing or winning, Each play brings fun, each ball brings a new beginning...

title: The Naughty Children
text: Chinnu and Krishnan were naughty children. Chinnu and Krishnan were so naughty, they steals mangoes from a vendor. Their mother thought of an idea and wrote something on a paper and went outside. Chinnu's mother worked in a tailoring shop. Chinnu loved touching fabrics, but her mother didn't allow her to stich anything." If you don't be careful, you will accidently prick your finger" she always say. Chinnu obeys. Krishnan saw the paper and said it to Chinnu " Chinnu, Amma has written that an old shop has toys inside it. Should we go there?. Chinnu nodded. They went to the shop. Chinnu whispered to Krishnan" Amma said was right. It is so dusty here." They saw toys and some candies. "Look at that candies, Krishnan!" Chinnu squealed. "Aren't those beautiful?". "Yes.... but these two also are beautiful" Krishnan said. Suddenly they heard a grumpy sound "Who are you?" he roared. He had a candy in his shirt-pocket. "Oh", he said thoughtfully" Do you want to see a magic? The children nodded. " Then enter that room" he pointed to a glass window and gave them a pair of spectacles. They went inside and peeked outside to see what was happening. Suddenly, the room turned black. " Hey!" Krishnan shouted. When Krishnan and Chinnu opened his eyes, he couldn't believe his eyes. They were in a magical land. Then he saw a denture coming near to them. "Run!" he shouted to Chinnu and grabbed her hand. But he hit his head on the mid-air" Hey! How can we escape if we cannot run outside?" The denture said " I will eat those who steal!". " We will not steal again" they cried. They ran in circle till they were completely exhausted and slept there. When they woke up, they saw a familiar face. It was their mother's. "Mother" asked Chunnu " where are we?". Mother said" Home, of course!". They became surprised and discussed. "We might been dreaming But how could we both have the same dream?" Krishnan said. " I think god is trying to show us not to steal. Their mother smiled to herself. Her trick have worked What was Amma's plan? The one who we have met in candy store was Amma's collagemate. She planned to make everything real by giving the children 7D glasses. With this glass, we can see everything real. When they were exhausted and slept, he took them back home to make them feel that it was a dream.

title: Where are the Hilsas?
text: Kolnagar was a small village away from the cities. It had a river named Ruprekha flowing next to it. The river was a source of fishes for the local fishermen. The fishermen would go out fishing in their small wooden boats and return in the evening with their catch. River Ruprekha was previously famous for Hilsa fishes. The silver colored fishes that came from the sea to river Ruprekha during rainy seasons. But now, the Hilsas have disappeared and have stopped coming to river Ruprekha. Joy and Diya lived in Kolnagar with their parents and grandparents. They were eight years old and went to the local primary school. One morning, Joy asked his grandfather, "Dadu, the fishermen were talking about Hilsa fishes the other day. Why don't Hilsa fishes come to our river anymore?" "Ever since the new Kolnagar Thermal Power Plant has been set up, the Hilsas have stopped coming to the river" replied Dadu sadly. Joy was curious and thought of asking his teacher, Srabani Miss. "Miss, I have a question" said Joy in the class next day. "Yes, Joy" said Srabani Miss calmly. "Miss, why are the Hilsa fishes not coming in our river? Dadu and the fishermen said that previously there would be loads of Hilsa fishes" asked Joy. "The new Kolnagar Thermal Power Plant set up on the banks of the river Ruprekha might have to do something with the Hilsas. It might be causing air and water pollution with smoke and fly ash" said Srabani Miss. "What is fly ash?" asked Diya, Joy's twin sister. "Fly ash is the ash particles left after burning coal. It can pollute the river water if it is not stopped from mixing in the water" said Srabani Miss. Joy thought that there must be some way to reduce the fly ash from polluting the water. "Miss, can we research about thermal power plant waste management and think of a solution?" asked Joy. Joy and Diya spent time in the school library to read various ways in which ash can be used. The next morning in class, they discussed various ways in which fly ash can be used. Fly ash can be mixed in cement and made concrete bricks. Joy and his friends went to the Manager of the Thermal Power plant along with Srabani Miss. They discussed about the water pollution and ways to reduce it. They suggested that instead of throwing the fly ash in the river water, it can used to make cement and concrete bricks. The manager showed interest and promised to implement the solution. Soon Kolnagar Thermal Power Plant was not only producing electricity but also fly ash bricks. The water pollution in river Ruprekha reduced and gradually the river became clean. The Hilsas were back again!!

title: How do we get pure and fresh ghee?
text: She loves it even more with a spoon of ghee spread over it. " Maa, this ghee looks so fresh and smells good. How do we get fresh and pure ghee?" "We get ghee by melting soft and white butter." "How do we get butter?" "By churning sweet and sour curd with this churning stick." "And how do we get curd?" "From rich and creamy milk. When we add little curd or lemon juice to warm milk and leave it undisturbed overnight, fermentation occurs and we get curd. This is called CURDLING." "And where do we get milk from?" " From our cow Kapila. She gives us milk." Maa, why she gives us her milk?" "Because we give her grass and food to eat and take care of her with lots of love." "Oh... then?" Then what... we get milk and you get to enjoy your puran poli with the pure and fresh ghee." A kitchen is like a science laboratory. Cooking involves many physical and chemical changes. Milk can become a lot of yummy things like curd, butter, ghee, buttermilk, paneer, ice-creams.... wow!!! How would you like to have your milk?

Sappy got so scared that he told everyone in the house – “There is a dinosaur in the house.” Everyone crowded out of the house, except Pop because Tab was his friend. It had been raining so the water was up to their feet and so they all went to the shed. Meanwhile; the city was flooded because the drain pipes were blocked. Tab rescued all the people by going near their houses and asking them to climb up on his back. Tab walked and walked with people on his back until he found a plain space. title: Oh, Storm! Wait!
text: ` It was a time when truth could not hide itself any longer and decided to come out from behind the curtains. Many years ago, in a village name Kakara situated near the navy blue river banks and azure sky where the yellow sun ruled the sky lived a granddaughter and her grandmother together. The girl's name was Kiara, who was only 9 years old, was very curious about everything. Everyday she used to ask her grandmother about what happened to her parents. Granny always replied that they went very far and you need to wait till you grow up to know their story. The grandmother was fed up to answer the same thing and could not hide it any longer. It was bedtime. The little girl loved to hear her grandmother's story. The granny said that it was time for her to know the story about her parents. The season was of spring and she was going to come. Her mother went inside in the operation ward and I heard a loud cry from outside the door, the first cry of yours. You had little hazel eyes and you were sleeping to glory, not knowing you have entered this world. You were just four days old when your parents went near the seashore to get you some clothes from the stall there. Kiara's eyes were very sleepy and she was nearly going to sleep. Granny continued with the story. To your parent's disappointment the stall was closed and a lash of rain began. They did not know a storm was coming. When they were returning home, the storm gobbled them up and none of your parents were able to survive. Kiara was in her sleep and a tear rolled out of her eyes. She muttered "Oh, Storm! Leave them, let them live a little bit with me, a little bit with me. Oh, Storm!"
author: Saanvi Ghosh

title: Yellow Earth, Brown Earth
text: Avi wakes up early. It is a good day. Avi is visiting Yellow Earth today. Yellow flowers, Avi makes bunches. dried-up flowers, tiny flowers. Yellow flowers— Avi looks for the perfect stick to poke the earth with. Smooth stick Avi keeps looking for treasures. bumpy stick. Smooth stick— Avi collects seeds. Brown seeds, black seeds, red seeds, green seeds. Brown seeds, black seeds— Yellow Earth is a happy place. Avi is visiting Grey Earth today. Big puddle, small puddle, no puddle. Big puddle, small puddle— Grey Earth is a wet place. Drip! Drop! Plish! Drip— Avi is visiting Brown Earth today. CRUNCH crunch CRUNCH crunch— Avi stomps on the dry ground. Avi smiles at the bright sun. Long cloud, round cloud, thin cloud. Long cloud— Brown Earth is a joyful place. Avi watches the Earth change every year. Yellow Earth, Grey Earth, Brown Earth— Avi is looking for a stick. Off to Yellow Earth again! Patterns Are All Around Us The day, the week, the month and the year — all have patterns that repeat. The seasons change every year and come back the same way. Every year, winter is followed by summer, which is followed by the monsoon. Look around you and try to spot these patterns. Go back to the beginning of the book and look for patterns you might have missed.
author: Sanjana  Kapur

title: Chop Chop Sizzle

title: All About Teeth
text: Teeth that keep getting replaced Teeth that sharpen themselves Teeth that are stout Teeth that are fangs Tooth that looks like a horn Teeth that are jagged Teeth that are orange Teeth that don’t stop growing Teeth that filter Teeth that gnaw on coral Teeth like those of a vampire Teeth that are tusks More About Teeth Crocodiles can replace all of their teeth by regrowing them. Hippos sharpen their teeth by constantly grinding them together. Tigers have stout teeth so that they can hold their prey in place. Cobras have modified teeth called fangs. They use their sharp, hollow fangs to inject venom into their prey. A Narwhal’s tooth looks like a long horn. It is believed to be used for exchanging information about the conditions of the water they are in. Sharks’ jagged teeth are a combination of pointed lower teeth and triangular upper teeth, useful for cutting into prey. Beaver teeth have a coating of iron, which makes them orange and also very strong. Squirrels have teeth that never stop growing. This helps them because they gnaw constantly. The Crab-eater Seal has specially modified teeth to strain the small krill, which are its food. Parrotfish have about a thousand teeth, cemented together in rows, to form a beak with which they bite into coral. Male Musk Deer with long and strong fangs are considered healthy and beautiful by other deer. Elephants use their tusks for digging, lifting, gathering food, stripping bark from trees, and as protection for their trunks.
author: Rohan Dahotre

title: All About Beaks
text: Drilling beak Fishing beak Colourful beak Grain-crushing beak Spoon beak Filter beak Nutcracker beak Sound-amplifier beak Needle beak Sword beak Pouch beak Storage beak More About Beaks Woodpeckers have strong, sharp beaks. With these beaks they drill holes in trees to make nests, and also to find insects to eat. Kingfishers have long, pointed beaks, which do not disturb the water surface when they dive in to catch fish. Toucans use their colourful beaks to show off their beauty as well as for self-defence. Sparrows’ cone-shaped beaks are stubby but sharp. They are capable of crushing seeds in a very strong grip. Spoonbills use their long, flat, rounded beaks to search for fish, amphibians and crabs along the bottom of muddy water. Flamingos’ bent beaks help them filter out very small plankton, tiny fish and fly larvae from shallow, muddy water. Parrots use their hook-like beaks for cracking open hard nuts. Hornbills have unique helmet-like structures on their beaks which help their call travel farther by making the sound boom louder. Sunbirds have long, curved beaks that point downward. They use their beaks to reach nectar, small spiders and insects deep inside flowers. Hummingbirds have very long, thin beaks with which they probe deep into flowers for nectar. Pelicans scoop up fish in their beak pouches. The water drains out, and the fish are swallowed. Puffins can catch and carry a bunch of fish at a time in their beaks.
author: Rohan Dahotre

title: All About Claws
text: Grabbing claws Climbing claws Running claws Digging claws Floating claws Slicing claws Gripping claws Hanging claws Trekking claws Fishing claws Lifting claws Grooming claws More About Claws Owls have sharp, curved and powerful claws with which they can grab and carry away their prey swiftly. Koalas have long, sharp claws on their front and hind paws, which help them grip and climb tall trees. Ostriches have three front toes and no hind toe, which helps them run fast. Armadillos have huge front claws with which they dig deep into the earth to reach ants and termites. Pheasant-tailed Jacanas have super-long toes. They help spread the bird’s weight over a large area, allowing them to easily walk across floating vegetation. Crabs’ claws, called pincers, are used for fighting, catching prey and slicing it apart to eat. Monitor lizards use their long, strong claws while climbing, to cling to steep rock surfaces or trees. Bats use their strong claws to hang upside down while roosting. Snow Leopards have extendable claws which allow them a firm grip while climbing trees or mountains. Kodiak Brown Bears find fish underwater and pin them with their claws. Eagles have four very sharp and strong talons with which they can lift even heavy prey. Monkeys use their claws to pick lice from each other’s hair.
author: Rohan Dahotre

title: Treasure Box
text: Give me thirteen marbles. I will give you thirteen precious things in exchange. I can give you ten white pebbles. I can give you three blue balloons. Ten and three make thirteen. 10 + 3 = 13 Please, Seema. Please. I need some of your marbles. Do you want eight shiny beads? Do you want five seeds that look like red peas? Eight and five make thirteen. 8 + 5 = 13 Wait. That is too much. Ten white pebbles and three blue balloons and five red seeds make eighteen precious things. 10 + 3 + 5 = 18 You want ten white pebbles and three blue balloons and five red seeds plus eight shiny beads? You are greedy! Ten and three plus five is eighteen. Another eight makes that twenty-six. 18 + 8 = 26 Please, Seema. Please. I really need thirteen marbles. Be a kind sister. Okay fine. I will give you ten white pebbles and three blue balloons, five red seeds and eight shiny beads. Please, Seema, do be kind. I do need those thirteen marbles.

title: The World That Mai Built
text: 17 … 18 … 19 … 20... Ready or not, here I come! I love playing hide-and-seek in Mai’s colony. So many secret spots to hide in, and I know them all. Mai built this colony years ago. S h h h … I have to hide before Prema finds me. Mai made this bamboo bridge when Mama was little. Crossing the bridge is the safest way to reach school in the rainy season. That is when the stream gets rough. Now it’s summer, and the stream is just a trickle. So under the bridge is the perfect place to hide. But the cobwebs can make you sneeze. Aa... aa aa... ch o ooo! Oops, I think Prema heard me. This basket has a great view. I can see Paalamma feeding her cows. We built that cob cowshed last year. Mai showed us how to mix mud, straw and lime. Prema and I got really messy. Ou ch! An ant bit my bum. Time to find a new spot. The library is our favourite place. I love the wind tower. Mai built this so that hot air can escape and the library and the books remain cool. I can spot Prema heading this way. Prema will never find me in this storeroom in Mai’s office. The office is the first building that Mai built. She added something called a skylight to the roof so that the sunlight can stream in. Mai’s old things are on this shelf. And these rolled-up sheets are drawings for new houses. Mai calls them blueprints. Uh oh, I can hear Prema’s jingling anklet. The store room door is opening! “Ha, Gopi! I caught you!” Mai is an architect. She makes big homes and small homes. She makes big offices and tiny offices. She sketches and makes drawings of how these buildings will look. If you wish to become an architect like Mai, you will have to study science, maths and architecture.
author: Nandita Jayaraj

title: What House Shall I Build Today?
text: What house shall I build today? A Toda hut with bamboo walls and a granite door? A bhunga house made of mud? A Kashmiri house with a wooden zoon dub balcony to stand in and wave at the moon from? A kettuvallam with wooden planks to float on the water? A Naga hut with roofs of tall wild grass? How about a Jaisalmer haveli of sandstone? What house shall I build today? A Nicobar house standing tall on bamboo stilts? Or a Ladakhi stone-and-brick house with a willow twig roof? A house powered by energy from the Sun? Or a city skyscraper made of cement blocks and mortar? What house shall I build today? Will you come visit me there?
author: Shweta Ganesh Kumar

title: When a Forest Wakes Up
text: From behind the stony backs of snoring hillocks, The sun jumps out, roaring into a bright morning. The air hums and flutters, dancing around in circles. As the sun walks the land, the soil twists and churns colours. Trees whisper old secrets to each other, through millions of buried messengers. Branches open their mouths wide, to swallow the sunlight. Then the sun hides behind a herd of giant grey clouds, Who trumpet and shower, filling the trees with water. As the wind sweeps the clouds clear, the water flows downward, a jolly river. By evening, a painted sky soars high. Birds fly back to flowers to thank them for their colours. A dark, sleepy night perches on the sun. The forest prepares for a new show, a new day. And floating by the horizon, the sun, never too far away.
author: Sudarshan Shaw

title: Mr. Vegetable
text: One day, in a small village near the city. There lived an old man who only farmed. He lives in a house near a field by the roadside alone. That old geezer is usually called Mr. Vegetables… Once upon a time, when the old man was gardening, he was approached by a little girl. The girl was not a resident of that village. she is a relative of one of the residents of the Satellite village. she walked over to the old geezer and then greeted him warmly. "Good morning, Grandpa. What are you doing this early?” asked the girl "Uh. Hi, I'm gardening. who are you, little girl?” Grandpa asked the girl. "I'm Alula, I'm Uncle Anton's nephew," she says. Mr. Vegetable thought for a moment, remembering the face of Uncle that the girl mentioned. "Uncle Anton, whose house is at the end of the alley, grandpa. He just moved to this village a few months ago,” the girl added. "Ah, yes. I know, sorry I kind of forgot." replied the old man with a laugh. Alula, the little girl approached the grandfather who was gardening. "If I may ask, what are you planting?" Alula asked. "I'm growing vegetables." “Only vegetables? Isn't this village famous for fruit? But why are you growing vegetables?” asked Alula again. "Haha, it's been a long time since I've been growing and selling vegetables. In fact I was an agricultural engineer. So when I retired I decided to grow crops, especially in the major vegetable field." It was clear that grandfather was picking his vegetables. “Why only vegetables? Aren't fruits better than vegetables?” she asked as she continued to follow the grandfather. "Look, vegetables and fruit are all equally good. But if you can eat vegetables and fruit at the same time, that's even better. Oh yeah, people in this village call me Mr. Vegetables. Because out of all the farmers in this village, I'm the only one who sells and grows vegetables." Obviously. Then Alula helped Mr. Vegetables to cultivate the crops. Starting from hoeing, planting, to picking the vegetable crops. Day after day changed, Alula the little girl every day visited the garden belonging to Mr. Vegetables. Occasionally she also accompanied Mr. Vegetables to the market to sell his harvest. she was very happy to get to know Mr. Vegetables during the Satellite village holiday. Until her last day in Satellite village came, she had to return to the city immediately. “Grandpa, I have to go back to town this afternoon.” she said in a sad tone. "Wow, that's nice. Your school holidays are over, right?” asked Mr. Vegetable "Yes. I have to go back to school next week. Thank you, Grandpa. because of you, now I like to eat vegetables. You know, the kids in town hate vegetables” she whispered. "Hahaha, of course, it's not because of me. That's because you already understand the benefits of vegetables. I'm just accompanying you." Mr. Vegetables said with a chuckle. Alula and Mr. Vegetable laughed. Time is running fast. Alula must leave the Satellite village immediately. she brought various vegetables from Mr. Vegetables. Vacation in the village this time was very pleasant. Alula got a lot of valuable experience during the school holidays in Satellite village. Alula was eager to return to Satellite Village to meet Mr. Vegetable again, and to repeat all the fun farming activities. The next day, Alula was back in school. she wrote down her experience of going to Uncle Anton's house, and meeting Mr. Vegetables. In front of the class, she proudly reads stories of her experiences during her vacation to her friends. “Friends, eating vegetables is very important for our bodies. Never leave vegetables on our food plates. From now on, let's eat lots of vegetables, fruit, and protein to keep our bodies healthy." Alula added at the end of his speech. All friends applaud Alula. title: The camel and the bird
text: Once upon a time, there was a camel named Dheru who travelled the desert with a man, Teju. One day, when Teju had gone to fetch water from an oasis nearby, Dheru came upon a bird. The name of the bird was Sohni. She was a spotted forktail travelling with her group. Her group had stopped to drink water, but having already had her fill, Sohni had set off to explore. After some talking, a quarrel started between Dheru and Sohni about who was greater, camels or birds. The quarrel continued till Sohni and her group left. Many days after Dheru and Sohni had met, Sohni's group was travelling again. But this time, Sohni got separated. Panicking, the started fly lower. Suddenly Dheru called out to her. "Hi!" he said. Then Sohni told him what had happened. As Dheru had travelled the desert several times, he guided Sohni her way to her group. Sohni thanked Dheru and said "I will never forget your favor. If you need help, just call us." and flew off. Then a long time after Dheru helped Sohni, he and Teju were travelling again. While travelling, they got stuck in a pit of quicksand. Not being able to escape, Dheru panicked and started thinking of something that could save him and his master. Suddenly, he remembered Sohni's words and gave out a loud call. Heeding his call, Sohni and her flock flew to him and helped him and Teju out of the quicksand. Dheru thanked she and her group gratefully. What we learn from this story is that all of us are equally great and no matter how small, or big, an animal is, they can always be of help somewhere. None of us here are useless or talentless.

title: The Forgetful Elephant Story
text: There once lived an elephant named Peter, who was the most forgetful elephant ever. It was almost as if he could never remember anything when the need be. He would often forget where he had kept his things. Or, he would forget if he had breakfast or not and end up having it twice. Sometimes he would even forget what he said to his friends and even the favorite character in his favorite movie. But the worst part of it all was that, Peter would often forget the plans he had made with people. He was notorious for always being late, that was in the case he remembered to actually show up at plan. But most of his friends had accepted Peter the way he was; except Suzy. Suzy was Peter’s wife, and she was growing tired of Peter ditching plans all the time. Of course, Peter never intended to miss their hangouts, but somehow he would always end up forgetting. This made Suzy feel less important in his life day by day. One day Suzy met Peter and said: “It is our anniversary tomorrow and we will go out for dinner, if you’re not on time, we’re done for good.” Peter was worried that he would upset Suzy this time. There had to be a way for him to remember. He took out a red ribbon from his drawer and tied it around his trunk. He thought that next morning when he would look at the ribbon it would remind him of the dinner and he would not miss it. That night Peter went to sleep thinking he was on to something. But, the next morning when Peter woke up and looked at himself in the mirror, he saw the red ribbon. But he had forgotten what it was for. He knew it had to remind him of something, but he no longer knew what. Peter panicked and panicked, he paced all around his house trying to figure out what it was that he was forgetting but to no avail. He called all his friends and all the places he usually went to asking if he had a commitment with anyone, yet there were none. Soon night took over the sky and Peter decided that he would ask Suzy what the ribbon was for. She must remember. Peter rushed to Suzy and expected her to remember but even before Peter had the chance to ask her, she embraced him and gave him the biggest smooch he had ever gotten in all his elephant years. He had arrived in time for the dinner and they ended up going out and having a lovely night, full of love, laughter and fun. But Peter never found out what the ribbon was for.

title: One pound of learning requires ten pounds of common sense to apply it.
text: How did you come to know this? Did you get this answer by reading a book? Now just imagine, a man walking on this broken bridge and is busy reading a book and there is an overflowing river below it. What would happen to him? Will he survive or will he die? Did you get the answers to these questions by reading a story book or your school textbook? If not, then how did you get these answers? Yes, you may all tell that you used your 'common sense'. What is this 'common sense'? This is one of the features which makes living organisms superior to non - living organisms. It is inbuilt. A puppy need not be taught how to cross a road when vehicles are coming. But what about machines? From birth till their death, they have to be told everything. They don't have common sense. Can anyone lead a life only with having 'common sense'? No, as many jobs need book knowledge too. But to apply the book knowledge, we need common sense. People in the world will appreciate us only if we have common sense. Often, many things in our life are not given in books. For example, the procedure of drying clothes, cooking, cleaning and many other works are not explained in books. Does that mean people do not know these things? Obviously not. In the previous picture, a young 5 - year - old girl is able to do her household works herself. From where did she learn them? She observed her mother do those things. What made her to observe her mother? Common sense!!!!!!!!!!!! So, ultimately everything depends upon our common sense. No one can survive without it. Many illiterates, in spite of being poor, have done wonderful and remarkable achievements. For example, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, known as the father of Indian constitution, was a poor and an illiterate boy who lived in a village called Ambavade of Ratnagiri district, Maharashtra. With all his struggles against the untouchability, he became a chairman of the drafting committee. He along with his team of 25 members, formed the Indian constitution. It all involves common sense and analytical thinking. Of course, he had to read books but they were not that helpful when he had to frame the constitution. Laws came into implementation only by common sense. So friends, the society emerged with common sense, evolution has taken place only by common sense. Information technology, too has emerged only by common sense! Philosophy and other subjects work on common sense only!!!!! Science laws and theories and experiments were done by using common sense only!!!!!!!!!! By this, we can prove that necessity is always not the mother of invention. ﻿Holy books like Bhagavad-Gita, Bible and Quran are based on common sense. It is depending on how we understand, interpret and apply them in our lives. This is an interesting and a funny story of why people who do not have common sense suffer in their lives. Once, there lived a teenager (a person between the age of 13 and 19) named Raju. He studied in a college. He was often called 'first rank' because he used to score out of out in all exams. He always used to hold a book in his hand whom we call a 'bookworm'. But do you know what was a strange thing with him? He never had common sense! He was reading his books day and night. His favourite subject was science in which he had read that a heavy object could crush/damage a light object and that a high reactive metal could displace a less reactive metal. It happened so one day that his mother asked him to buy four vegetables and gave him a list. Tomato - 1 kg Carrot - 1 Kg Cauliflower - 1 kg Cabbage - 1 kg Pumpkin - 1 kg Taking the list, he set out to the market. He first went to a tomato shop and asked for 1 kg of tomato and put it into his bag. Then, he went to a flower shop to ask for a cauliflower! He thought it was a type of flower. The flower shopkeeper scolded him, leaving the all the people around laughing. With all the humiliation, he came back to the vegetable shop and bought 1 kg of cauliflower. Then, he asked for 1 kg of cabbage and as well as the pumpkin. He put them in such a way that the tomatoes were at the bottom followed by cauliflower, cabbage and pumpkin at the top!!!!!!!!! Imagine what would happen to the tomatoes and it so happened. When he reached home with his heavy bag, mother took out all the vegetables and started crying loudly only to find the crushed tomatoes whose juice had spoilt not the bag but also her precious earned money. But what was the use? He may have read but because he did not apply, it lead to his downfall. So friends, let us learn this important moral and that we should use them to bring smiles and laughs on the faces of people irrespective of their cultural background. Childhood is a precious time which we never get it back. Let us use it to something meaningful and useful. Spend time reading books, creating jokes and stories, comics and inculcating spirituality in our life. Only these things make a man. Otherwise, he is just an animal with a human body. Ha! Ha! Ha! For these reasons, isn't there a beautiful saying which all of us have heard? ﻿"CHILD IS A FATHER OF A MAN" ﻿Yes, it its true. It means that you are superior to a man especially in terms of changing your bad habits. Its easy for a child to change himself while its a nightmare for a man. You can choose to remove your bad habits and become a good person quickly while a man becomes a slave for his cultivated bad habits which even after death, can never be changed. Until the next book is published, STAY HAPPY, STAY HOME, STAY SAFE AND STAY SPIRITUAL. THANKING YOU, GOOD BYE!

title: Who Stole the Cupcakes?
text: Who could it be?" asked Ammachi "It could be ﻿Penny ﻿," said Sooraj, or the ﻿civet ﻿ who lives in the attic?" "Could it have been Appachen by any chance?" questioned Sooraj "Yes, it could be," said Ammachi "We have to set three ﻿super ﻿traps!" "There is only one way to find out." "Oh yeah, how?" "Ha! Ha! Well played, Mamie. YUM!" "First, we will need more cupcakes." "There are more?" "Yes, I always hide some in the kitchen, just in case!" "Our first trap is for the civet," explained Ammachi. "When she enters through the window, she will fall in this basket. Her weight will close the lid right away." "Great!" cried Sooraj. "This one here is for ﻿Penny ﻿. If she tries to eat the cupcake, the bucket will fall right on her." "Excellent!" "Finally, this hidden camera will allow us to catch Appachen in the act. When he takes the cupcake on the plate, the string will fall and release the camera." "Wonderful!" "There we go, there is nothing left to do but wait and see what happens..." "Ammachi had been reading her favorite scientific work in her rocking chair for an hour when Sooraj suddenly burst into the room. "Ammachi, come quick," he yelled, "the traps are set off!" "Oh, let's go see," responded Ammachi. "And yet, all the cupcakes ﻿still ﻿ disappeared!" "The basket is empy!" "The bucket too!" "The camera didn't go off!" "We are dealing with a very cunning thief," indicated Ammachi. Perhaps we must install ﻿another three ﻿ traps?" "Good idea," responded Sooraj. "But then what will we be able to use as ﻿bait ﻿?" asked Ammachi. "We could take the three cupcakes that are still in the oven?" suggested Sooraj. "AHA!" exclaimed Ammachi. "Not so cunning as that after all!" "Um... uh..." stammered Sooraj. "How did you know that there were ﻿THREE ﻿ cupcakes, Sooraj?" demanded Ammachi. "And how did you know that they were hidden in the oven?" "Well, uh..." "I didn't tell anyone except ﻿YOU ﻿how the traps worked﻿. You are the ﻿ONLY ﻿ one who could have set them off without being caught. "Okay, I confess," admitted Sooraj. "It's true, you figured it out, ﻿I ﻿am the cupcake thief!" " ﻿I knew it was you ﻿," said Ammachi. "I couldn't resist, Mamie. Your cupcakes are so delicious! You are a wonderful cook!" "Haha, little flatterer, go!" "Who is going to eat the rest of the cupcakes, Ammachi?" "Ha! Ha! Come on, we'll share them." "It can't be true!" cried Ammachi. "The cupcakes disappeared ﻿AGAIIIIIN ﻿!" "He! He! He! Yum! Yum!" " ﻿CHOMP! CHOMP!" " ﻿SLURP! SLURP!" " ﻿PITTER-PATTER" ﻿ How to trap a thief ﻿1. Look for clues 2. Create a list of suspects 3. Set traps 4. Ask intelligent questions 5. Note all discoveries 6. Catch your first suspect 7. You got the wrong person? Argh! 8. Repeat steps 1 through 7

title: Nanammal and Kamalathal Travel by Air
text: Nanammal and Kamalathal are best friends. Nanammal teaches yoga. Kamalathal runs the local idli shop. Nanammal is very tidy. Kamalathal is not. Nanammal is shy. Kamalathal loves meeting new people. But there is one thing they both love to do — travel. Kamalathal’s birthday is this week. Her big dream has always been to fly. So she and Nanammal are going to Manali. In an aeroplane! Inside the plane, Kamalathal is so excited, she just cannot stay still. She wants to see where the pilot is, try on the life jacket, and look out of the window. The plane rumbles down the runway and then suddenly, they’re up in the air! “Look at the clouds,” says Nanammal, pointing out the window. “That one looks like an idli.” The best friends arrive in Manali. It’s very, very cold. Nanammal has arranged a surprise for her friend. A hot-air balloon ride! “Can I pull this?” asks Kamalathal. But she’s not allowed to. “Look at the clouds!” says Nanammal, “That one looks like an old man’s beard!” But Kamalathal is sad. She wants to fly the hot-air balloon. Nanammal hates to see her best friend sad. So, she arranges another surprise. This time, it’s a helicopter ride. They fly over Manali, and their stomachs flip-flop as they look down at the snowy mountains, forests and rivers. “Can I push this?” asks Kamalathal. But she’s not allowed to. “Look at the clouds!” says Nanammal, “That one looks like a spinning top!” But Kamalathal is sad. She wants to fly the helicopter. It’s Kamalathal’s birthday. They have hot bajjis for breakfast. “I have one last surprise for you,” says Nanammal. “I’m flying, wheeeee!” shrieks Kamalathal. “Open your eyes and look at the clouds, Nanammal! That one looks like a cat! “This has been the best birthday ever, Nanammal. Thank you,” says Kamalathal. What are the different modes of air transport Nanammal and Kamalathal took to spot the clouds? Where do you think Kamalathal would like to fly next?
author: Menaka Raman
