Whenever the smell touches their nose, they are the first ones to get their bowls filled with the delicious, mouth-watering dish This dish of Amma`` s was also popular amongst all the villagers in their village One day, Amma told Raju & Rani, " Dear, today I will organize a feast of soup for all the villagers " Yippee! Soup for everyone!" said Rani. Raju was also very happy, but he didn`t say anyting When Amma left to get all the ingredients from the market, Raju told Rani," Rani, Amma also has some office work today, how will she make the soup alone?" Rani said,"That` s true. We must help her, but let`s do it secretly." As soon as Amma returned, she went to the office to do some work. When she came back, she saw that Raju and Rani had done all the work and had invited all the guests too! Amma was very happy and they ate the soup happily.
author: Ashlesha Prasad
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Bandana  Tulachan; Kabini  Amin; Shriyon Bhattacharya; Tanvi Bhat

title: When A Cat Doesn't Bath
text: Once upon a time it was the 12h birthday of Sam. His parents got him a brown cat on his birthday. Sam was so joyful he named his cat Jasmine. Next day, he took Jasmine to the bathtub whenever Sam tries to put her in the bathtub Jasmine jumps out. Then he got an idea he took Jasmine and put it in lukewarm water and he washed her with shampoo and soap finally Jasmine was clean.
author: Akshaj Singh

title: Bobby's Dream of Christmas
text: There was once a boy named Bobby. He looked forward to Christmas, as much as he did his own birthday. From the 1 st of December, he would begin counting the days to Christmas. Bobby enjoyed so many things about Christmas – the tall green tree with the star at the top, the sparkling lights, the colourful decorations, delicious sweets and cakes, and gifts wrapped in shiny paper. But there was one thing that Bobby disliked. Every year, in her enthusiasm, Bobby’s younger sister would open one of his gifts by mistake. And every year, his mother would say, “She is just a child. You are the elder one, so you should not get upset, Bobby”. This would make him even more upset. One year, on Christmas Eve, Bobby fell asleep in his bed, dreaming about Christmas day. In his dream, he saw a beautiful Christmas tree with colourful lights, and many large gifts. On a table, there was a large Christmas cake, a gingerbread man and sweets of many colours. He looked around and saw no one else, smiled and thought, ‘this is all for me, only for me’. He quickly opened all the gifts. He ate cake and sweets, until his belly was full. Then suddenly, he noticed that it was so quiet. It did not feel like Christmas, even though there was a tree, a cake, and gifts. He remembered his sister giggling with delight while opening gifts. And his mother’s voice singing Christmas carols as she decorated their tree. And his grandmother humming to herself as she baked their Christmas cake. He suddenly became afraid. Had he ruined Christmas? His fear grew and grew, until it woke him up from his dream. When he woke up, Bobby saw that he was in his little bed, in his little room. It was Christmas morning. He heard his younger sister say, “Mummy, can we open the gifts now?” In his little chest he felt something, like a warmth. It spread up to his lips, and became a large smile. Bobby realized that he had not ruined Christmas. In his heart, he had found Christmas
author: Lynessa Coutto

title: My pet is my best friend
text: It was Christmas evening. I was waiting for my gift. Like other kids I was waiting for Santa Claus suddenly I saw a dog, it was stuck in a pit, it was cute so I picked it up and took it home with me. From that day that pup was my best friend. I always give him dog food and honey, because he likes to eat it. I always make him bath. Now he has grown and he is very strong. But he still loves me and I love him too. He is my best friend. He will always love me and I will love him too. It was my best Christmas ever. I never thought that this day would be my favorite and memorable day of my life. The starting was not at all good but, it had become a special day of my life.

title: The Hairy Hare
text: Once upon a time there lived a hare who had difficulty hearing. He would hear 'berry' as 'burry' and 'rose' as 'rows', a 'flower would become 'flour' as well. However, he had a lot of friends, who would help him out, play with him and also shared food with him. One day, all of them decided to visit a fair where they might ask to pay the fare, but they will also get to play a lot of games. They overjoyed once they reached the fair ground. In the hurdle race - the bear could barely win against the hare. They all had a happy and fun day together. After all the fun they had they left for home before dusk. They hugged each other and headed towards their dens and burrows. The dear deer, hugged the hairy hare and praised on her win. They all slept through the night to wake up to enjoy another happy day together...

title: The Right Tools
text: I am Isha and this is Logu, the mason. He is building the walls, stairs and floors of my new house. “Can I help?” “Would you please pass me that trowel? title: The Elephant and the Mouse
text: Once upon a time, there was a mouse. He was lost in the forest once. He kept sniffing the ground to see if anyone was coming. Suddenly he saw an elephant coming. "D-d-do you kn-n-n-n-n-know the way to my h-h-home" The mouse stuttered. "No" The elephant said "but I will show you. What does it look like?" "Well," the mouse said "It is yellow?" "Okay" said the elephant. The mouse said " My house is big for me but very small to you. It smells like cheese. It is the shape of a mushroom. It has pink windows. It is on Cheese Love Street." "Okay. I will take you there." The mouse thanked the elephant. He went in his house. He offered cheese to the elephant. One day the elephant went out for a walk. The mouse was out to do some shopping.The elephant did not notice the mouse's house. He stepped on it. Then the small house got crushed. When the mouse came he saw the elephant and crushed house. The elephant told the mouse what had happened. The mouse was very sad. "Don't worry. We can build it again." Said the elephant. "We will need bricks." he said. They bought some bricks from a monkey. "Now we will need cement." said the elephant. The elephant told the human builders to give them cement. They stuck the bricks together. "Now we need some paint!" exclaimed the elephant. He loved painting! The mouse was painting the inside. The elephant was painting the outside. The house looked like the same way it was before!😀

illustrator: Aruna Keerthi Gamage; Mohith O; Natasha Sharma; Phyu Mon; Rob Owen; Siddhi   Vartak

title: Sharing is Fun
text: I have a friend named Anita. She was kind and caring, also beautiful and responsible. She likes to help her mother. Whenever I go back to the village, we play together. We usually play hide and seek in my house. Once, after getting tired of playing, we watched television and saw a McDonald's ad. Anita asked if I had ever tried it, and I said I had. Without a second thought, I told her that she wouldn't enjoy it because we lived in the city and she was in the village. She's sad. We used to eat together at my house, but she said she wanted to eat at her house that day. I asked her to come back after lunch. That night I had to go back to town. We said goodbye, and then I left. Then I realized that I had been rude to her. A year later, I returned to the village. On the way, I stopped by McDonald's and bought a burger. When I reached the village, I met Anita and hugged her. She said his vacation had already begun that day. I told her I had a gift for her However, she had trouble guessing the prize. Then she opened it and saw that it contained a burger. She cried out for joy. She shared the burger with her mother and brother. She's delighted and me too.

title: KISAH MAX DAN TALLULAH
text: Max adalah seekor zebra yang keren dan tampan. Max sangat menyukai Tallulah. Tallulah adalah seekor zebra kecil yang cantik. Max sangat senang melihat Talullah memakan rumput di dekat sungai. Tetapi Max malu untuk berbicara dengan Tallulah. Ketika Tallulah menengok ke belakang, Max langsung lari menjauh dari Tallulah. Max berpikir bagaimana caranya agar dapat berbicara dengan Talullah. Aha! Max akhirnya menemukan cara! Max akan memberi sebuah hadiah untuk Tallulah. Max pergi ke sungai dan ia masuk ke sungai itu. Max mulai mencari buah-buahan kesukaan Tallulah. Selanjutnya, Max mengumpulkan semua buah-buahan itu di atas daun lily yang lebar. Dengan sangat hati-hati Max mendorongnya menuju ke tepian sungai. Max akan membawa buah-buahan tersebut untuk Tallulah. Tallulah sedang tidur di tepi sungai. Saat Max hampir sampai ke tepi sungai, daun lily yang berisi buah-buahan tadi sudah tidak kuat lagi menahan semua buah-buahan itu. Sehingga, semua buah-buahan itu tumpah dan berserakan disungai. Max harus memikirkan cara lain. Di malam hari, saat bulan bersinar terang, Max berlatih sebuah tarian buatan Max sendiri. Max memulai dengan melompati bukit kecil, kemudian berputar disatu kakinya. Max melakukan tarian itu berulang kali. Matahari mulai bersinar, Max pergi untuk menemui Tallulah. Ternyata, Tallulah sedang memakan rumput segar di hutan. Max sudah yakin kalau tarian Max tadi malam akan disukai oleh Tallulah. Sambil membawa bunga, Max mendekati Talullah perlahan-lahan. Max memulai gerakan tariannya dengan penuh semangat. Pertama-tama Max berdiri disatu kakinya. Kemudian, melompat-lompat tinggi. Dan memutar tubuhnya dengan lincah dan cepat. Apakah sekarang Tallulah akan kagum kepada Max karena tariannya? Tetapi Tallulah sedang asyik memakan rumput sendirian. Jadi, Tallulah tidak melihat tarian Max dan bahkan tidak tahu kalau ada Max dibelakangnya. Max harus memikirkan cara lain lagi! Max mengumpulkan daun dan bunga yang berwarna-warni. Max juga menangkap hewan-hewan kecil seperti, kupu-kupu, kumbang, siput kecil dan capung. Max memutuskan untuk membuat sebuah mahkota yang keren. Tallulah pasti akan suka melihat mahkota buatan Max. Mahkota itu terbuat dari daun-daun dan bunga-bunga yang telah dikumpulkannya tadi. Max juga menghiasi mahkota tersebut dengan serangga-serangga kecil. Apakah mahkota buatan Max akan sangat menarik perhatian Tallulah untuk berbicara dengan Max? Saat Max bertemu dengan Tallulah dengan memakai mahkota buatan Max tadi, Tallulah sangat kaget. Sehingga Tallulah pun langsung kabur menjauhi Max. Max merasa sangat sedih. Max tidak bermaksud untuk membuat takut Tallulah. Max merasa sangat bingung. Max tidak tahu apalagi yang harus ia lakukan agar Tallulah bisa bicara dengannnya. Ketika Max berada dipinggir sungai, Max melihat tubuh Max ada di air sungai itu! Tiba-tiba Max menemukan cara yang paling bagus untuk bisa berbicara dengan Tallulah. Max sudah tahu apa yang akan ia lakukan untuk Tallulah! Ketika bertemu dengan Tallulah, Max menatap Tallulah dan tersenyum kepadanya. Wow ajaib! Tallulah ternyata tersenyum kepada Max juga! Pada akhirnya, Tallulah dan Max jalan-jalan di tepi sungai. Max disebelah kiri dan Tallulah di sebelah kanan. Max bercerita kepada Tallulah tentang buah-buahan yang tenggelam, tarian spesial buatan Max, mahkota buatan Max dan yang berhasil hanyalah dengan menjadi Max apa adanya.

title: Happy as a Hen
text: Ra Ra Rooster rubbed his eyes. He could not believe what he saw. There was a fried egg coming down from the sky. It landed on four spidery legs on the green grass. “Oh my comb and feathers!” exclaimed Ra Ra. “Who are you?” For out of the fried egg had come a smart hen and a very smart chick. “I am Ma-Cluck and this is K-Chick,” said the smart hen. “We have come from the galaxy Scrambled on our spaceship YOLK.” There was a rush of feathers and Ra Ra’s family of four Mama Hens and six Little Chicks came tumbling out of the bushes. “Is it an alien invasion, Papa Ra Ra?” asked Chiki Chick. “Oh no!” exclaimed K-Chick. “We’ve just come to learn about Earth Hens. We’ve heard that you have a wonderful life here.” “Cru-uk,” said Ra Ra, scratching his wattle. “We’re pretty ordinary. A yard full of insects and worms to scratch for, a place to lay eggs and a wall to get up on and crow.” “Nothing special?” asked Ma-Cluck. She was disappointed. “Special lies over that big wall there,” said Ra Ra. He pointed to a large wall far away. “I hear that there are thousands of hens in there and they live in ABSOLUTE HAPPINESS.” “Take us there, please,” said Ma-Cluck, excitedly. “Oh… I…” said Ra Ra. “Go on, take them,” said a Big Mama Hen. “I’m coming,” said Chiki. “What fun!” cheeped K-Chick. After a bit of a search, Chiki found a hole in the wall. One by one, they all crept through the dusty hole. They shook the dust off their feathers and looked up. What did they see? Big sheds, one after the other, spreading out for miles. Large bins marked CHICKEN FEED. There were piles of feathers on the ground. There was a strong smell of hens but… There wasn’t a sound! It did not look like a place of ABSOLUTE HAPPINESS, at all! Cheep… cheep… cheeeep. The faint sound came from a big shed nearby. “Sounds like little chicks,” whispered Ma-Cluck. “This might be the playhouse,” said K-Chick, softly. “Let’s go and see!” “I’m coming too,” said Chiki. They tiptoed around the shed and reached a wooden door. It was half-open. They squeezed their way in and peered around. It was quite dark. Out of the corner came a little voice, “Have you come to save us?” K-Chick ran forward. His eyes grew round with wonder. “Come and see, Mama!’ he whispered. The other three came forward. There were ten frightened little chicks, huddled in a corner. “Oh my poor chickabiddies!” exclaimed Ma-Cluck, putting her fluffy wings around them. “Why are you hiding here?” “And why are your beaks cut?” Ra Ra’s voice came out loud. “They do that to all the chicks here and then put us in a small cage,” said a chick called Droopy. “It’s so that we don’t peck each other in that tiny cage.” “BAD!” crowed Ra Ra. “Very BAD! What is this place called?” “The Cheery Chicken,” said Droopy, sadly. Just then, there came a shout from outside. “Check in the shed for the chicks. I think a rooster has got in.” “Humans!” Ra Ra was alarmed. “We need to go before they see us.” “Mama, we cannot leave these chicks here,” cheeped K-Chick. “We have to take them with us.” “We will, son,” said Ma-Cluck, pulling out a shining rod from behind her neck. “All of you stand at the door. When those humans open it, run straight to the hole in the wall and get out.” “But…” said Ra Ra. “No time for ‘buts’,” said Ma-Cluck, sternly. “Do as I tell you. Take them and go straight to the YOLK. I will follow.” Ra Ra took charge. He and Chiki, along with K-Chick, took the ten chicks to the door. The door swung open. A large human stood there with a torch. “What is this? Where are the chicks? Who are you?” he shouted. As Ra Ra and the chicks scooted out of the shed, Ma-Cluck let out a stream of blue light from her special Zapper. It curled around the human’s legs and caught them tight! “Ooh, oh! Ooh… OUCH!” shouted the man. Ma-Cluck shut off the Zapper and ran out of the door. “Quickly, Mama!” yelled K-Chick, from the hole. “More humans coming!” Ma-Cluck ducked out just as a human grabbed one of her tail feathers. “You will not pull my tail,” squawked Ma-Cluck, turning to give the human a nice big zap. They rushed to the YOLK. All the chicks scrambled in. K-Chick gave Chiki a quick hug and jumped in himself. “Thank you for rescuing those poor chicks,” crowed Ra Ra. “Wish I could have done more,” said Ma-Cluck. “Someone must help the chicks there. See you, Ra Ra and family. Your yard is the absolute happy place.” The YOLK took off and zoomed through the sky and up through the clouds, back to the galaxy Scrambled. “Where are we going?” asked Droopy. “Have we really escaped?” “Yes, you have,” said K-Chick. “You are coming home with me to Planet Egx. No one is ever going to hurt you again.” As the Earth chicks flew off to a new home, the universe echoed with the happy sound of CHEEP CHEEP! The Earth Hens Hens and roosters are fun to have in a nice big yard. They need lots of space to run about and cluck. They also need a lot of space to scratch the ground and look for worms. Yum! Mother hens love their chicks and protect them all the time. Her chicks listen to her every cluck and obey her always. We must always be kind to hens and chicks and never hurt them in any way.
author: Reena  I. Puri

title: Lilly and Milly

title: A STORY OF A VILLAGER GIRL
text: This is a story about a villager girl who always feel alone.her name is Sara.She studies in good school but because of her background that she lives in a village no one wants to talk to her. Her father is a farmer and she has a step mother who always beat her and tell her to do all household activities.Her mother always give threaten to her that she will not going to tell any single word to anyone. title: RAJPUR'S BHAUJI
text: Rajpur has come from Seemamarhi today. Got lost today. Ramesh Bhaiya has brought Bhauji from the jeep. The Naihar of Rajpur Wali is not very rich and rich, yet the entire jeep has come with the same stuff. Ladood, Khaja, Pidukia, Gaza are filled with the whole world. Dura is also designer. 3 are of bamboo, one of sikk. Which is made by the Mai of Rajpur. Bhauji of Rajpur was telling that her grandmother used to make daliya, mouni, jhaya, phuldali, singardan and dagra from Seek. Mai has learned from Dadi and Bhauji of Rajpur has also learned from Mai. Bhauji said that when she sat down to make nuggets with a sharp knife for the first time, the knife accidentally hit her finger. There was a lot of blood. Then the grandmother said, if the lure of catching Tekua is not there, then this will happen. From that day onwards Bhauji became alert. Every year in the month of Kartik, Asin goes to the banks of the river and brings Seek to cut the grass. He used to soak dry seekh in color and make designer dauri-dolchi, dhaka, singhordani, moniya from it. Bhauji's friend is Lalmuni. Lalmuni enjoys making sun, moon, Nagpuri conch shell, chakra, mace swastika in a porridge. Similarly, the Bhauji of Rajpur also likes to make elephants, horses, flowers, peacocks, leaf fish, toys on top of the throne. Bhauji is a little educated. It is said that this grass is a different type of grass which occurs in North Bihar. Where the land is low and where there is water. That's where it produces. When Ramesh Bhaiya's babuji saw Bhauji's talent, he was very happy. Said, “E bahu to e golden grass, which means gold can make wonderful things from grass.” The women of the village were looking at the goods of Rajpur's Bhuji. Everyone's eyes were on seeing the beautiful arts done on it instead of the sweets kept in the dalia. She was thinking about how she would learn and make the nugget made of seaq and the etchings done on it.
author: Yashvi Pathak

title: Key Lock
text: He started searching for the key lock. He put the key in the lock of the box. The key was too loose. He saw the key in the lock of Kakaji's cupboard. The key didn't even enter it. He put the key in the lock of his mother's bicycle. The key got stuck in it. He pushed hard to get the key. Eventually the key went out. Now he put the key in Grandma's box. Knock! The lock opened. Oh wow! This is the key to Grandma's box!
author: Shayna Gaharwar

title: How the Myna Ate the Sun
text: It was a bright morning. The hungry myna hopped with excitement. Time to feast on her favourite food — the sun. The sun? But how? Isn’t it too big? Too hot? Tooooooo far away? The myna had a plan. It started with the plants, who drank up golden sunshine through their leaves. The sunlight, mixed with sweet morning air and cool water, made a delicious meal for the plants. For extra flavour, there were snacks in the soil. A prickly caterpillar crawled out of his egg. He was hungry enough to eat the whole plant! Leaf after leaf after leaf he gobbled, getting bigger and pricklier. The purple leaves were his favourite — bitter and juicy with a spicy twist. The caterpillar couldn’t eat another bite. He hid under a leaf and wrapped himself up. After much tossing and turning, he was ready to come out — as a moth! Nearby, the gecko licked her eyes clean to make sure she was seeing right. Those wings looked so soft! These days, moths find it hard to see the moon and stars at night. So, they gather around light bulbs instead. Hidden in the shadows, the gecko couldn’t wait any longer. Her long, sticky tongue flew out of her mouth and caught the moth. The wings melted in her mouth. The bushy antennae tickled her throat on the way down. Delicious! By morning, the gecko had tasted all kinds of wings — soft, chewy, and even some mouth-wateringly crisp ones. With each meal, she grew bigger and rounder. Too full to move, the gecko settled in for a nap. The myna’s beak dropped open. Those gecko toes looked SO crunchy! Crunchy toes soft wings juicy leaves and plenty of delicious sunshine The myna gobbled up the gecko with a snap of her beak. She saved the tail for last, which wiggled and squiggled delightfully in her stomach. The myna’s plan to eat the sun had worked! But she was still hungry... Behind her, the hungry cat’s whiskers quivered. Time to feast on his favourite food, the sun. The Food Chain Every time you take a bite of food, you are eating the sun! All living beings, including humans, need energy to grow. This energy comes to our bodies through food. Plants feed themselves by turning sunlight into food! They pass the sun’s energy on to animals, like the caterpillar who chomped up the plant’s leaves, or like us eating vegetables. Some animals also depend on other animals for energy, like the gecko who ate the moth, or us eating fish curry for dinner. This transfer of energy is called the food chain, and it begins with the sun. Other animals are hungry, too! Spiders love to eat moths, just as cats love to eat geckos, grasshoppers eat plants and birds love to snack on caterpillars. When food chains get all tangled up, the result is a food web. Can you draw a food web from animals you see around you? But where does a food chain, or food web, end? When the last animal in a food chain reaches the end of its life, it becomes food for worms, mushrooms and tiny creatures like bacteria living in the soil. After they are done, plants get the leftovers. Nothing in nature is wasted! Mango tree Castor plant Grasshopper Cocoa Tussock Moth Green Lynx Spider House Gecko Common Myna Cat Human
author: Labonie Roy

title: The Adventure of a Plant
text: Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Riya. She loves nature. She plants a tree on her every birthday. And every time her next birthday come, the seed previously sown become a tree. When this time her birthday came, she planted a seed and watered it daily. After few days a little stem come out from the seed. After few weeks, that little plant took the sunlight and water to become a bigger plant. After few weeks more, flowers started to come out from that plant, then Riya said, "Look Mom! Flowers are growing on the plants that I grew on my birthday". And when her next birthday came then the small plant turned into a flowering tree. Do you know how a seed becomes a tree?
author: Sarthak Kundu

title: HOLIDAYS WITH GRANDMOTHER
text: Odongo and Apiyo lived in the city with their father. They looked forward to the holidays. Not just because school was closed, but because they went to visit their grandmother. She lived in a fishing village near a large lake. Odongo and Apiyo were excited because it was time to visit their grandmother again. The night before, they packed their bags and got ready for the long journey to her village. They could not sleep and talked the whole night about the holiday. Early the next morning, they left for the village in their father’s car. They drove past mountains, wild animals and tea plantations. They counted cars and sang songs. After a while, the children were tired and fell asleep. Father woke up Odongo and Apiyo as they arrived in the village. They found Nyar-Kanyada, their grandmother, resting on a mat under a tree. Nyar-Kanyada in Luo, means ‘daughter of the people of Kanyada’. She was a strong and beautiful woman. Nyar-Kanyada welcomed them into the house and danced around the room singing with joy. Her grandchildren were excited to give her the presents they brought from the city. “First open my gift,” said Odongo. “No, my gift first!” said Apiyo. After she opened the presents, Nyar-Kanyada blessed her grandchildren in a traditional way. Then Odongo and Apiyo went outside. They chased butterflies and birds. They climbed trees and splashed in the water of the lake. When it was dark they returned to the house for dinner. Before they could finish eating, they were falling asleep! The next day, the children’s father drove back to the city leaving them with Nyar-Kanyada. Odongo and Apiyo helped their grandmother with household chores. They fetched water and firewood. They collected eggs from the chickens and picked greens from the garden. Nyar-Kanyada taught her grandchildren to make soft ugali to eat with stew. She showed them how to make coconut rice to eat with roast fish. One morning, Odongo took his grandmother’s cows to graze. They ran onto a neighbour’s farm. The farmer was angry with Odongo. He threatened to keep the cows for eating his crops. After that day, the boy made sure that the cows did not get into trouble again. On another day, the children went to the marketplace with Nyar-Kanyada. She had a stall selling vegetables, sugar and soap. Apiyo liked to tell customers the price of items. Odongo would pack the items that customers bought. At the end of the day they drank chai tea together. They helped grandmother to count the money she earned. But too soon the holidays were over and the children had to go back to the city. Nyar-Kanyada gave Odongo a cap and Apiyo a sweater. She packed food for their journey. When their father came to fetch them, they did not want to leave. The children begged Nyar-Kanyada to go with them to the city. She smiled and said, “I am too old for the city. I will be waiting for you to come to my village again.” Odongo and Apiyo both hugged her tightly and said goodbye. When Odongo and Apiyo went back to school they told their friends about life in the village. Some children felt that life in the city was good. Others felt that the village was better. But most of all, everyone agreed that Odongo and Apiyo had a wonderful grandmother!
author: JYOTI SHARMA

title: India: An Incredible country (Part - 2)
text: Significance of building temples in Indian culture You must have gone to a temple to worship god and pray to him. When you enter it, you find a deity of god standing there. You pray and ask him for some boons. Isn't it? Did you ever wonder who, when and how these temples were built? Also, did you ever wonder when, where and how these deities were found? Let us answer these questions in this book now. (Note: The temple in this picture is the Virupaksha Temple in Hampi, Karnataka, India, Asia). How did the method of building of temples start? The practice of building temples was present even 5000 years ago. The kings who had a lot of money was always contributing for the upliftment of the city. One of them was building temples. It was a desire of many kings. Why was the desire of many kings? Let me explain this with an example. Sprinkle some rice or other food grains on the floor. Wait for some time. What do you observe? Many pigeons fly and come from many places to eat these grains and fill their stomach. Is rice so attractive for them? Yes, it is because that is a necessity for pigeons to lead their life. Similarly, when a temple is / was built, like the pigeons, even people from many places migrated and settled near the place where the temple was built. They started building houses for shelter. Slowly, cities, towns, states and countries started growing there. What was so attractive for the people in that temple? It was none other than the deity in that temple. These deities helped people in tough times. It is neither myth, imagination nor superstition. It is true. As I already told you, god is an entity existing with shape as well as with no shape. He has got some characteristics which are totally different from this world. He is infinite. Numbers are his representatives. So, don't you think we can worship numbers in mathematics than to fear it? Yes. People of India knew this and always treated the temple as their heavenly homes. They never wore footwears and entered it. This is how the concept of cleanliness. Many saints such as Mirabai, Purandaradasa, Kanakadasa and many more often went to temples and worshipped the gods there. They even sang parables and sent messages to people just through singing!! They often gave some lectures and also educated people that Prapatti (Surrender) leads to Bhakti (devotion) and Bhakti leads to Mukti (salvation). Mirabai is an incarnation of one of the Gopis also known as Gopika Streeyaaha according to Bhagavatam of Sri Krishna. Purandaradasa is the incarnation of Narada, saint of Sri Vishnu. Madhvacharya and Shankaracharya are the incarnations of Vayu and Shiva respectively. You may all ask a question that why we should worship god only in temples and why can't we do it in our houses. As I already mentioned, we just need two things to attain Mukti. They are: Prapatti and Bhakti. It doesn't matter to god the place you are worshipping him. Still, people prefer going to temple. It is because in a temple, their minds are always focused on their prayers and the god, the sweet sound of the bells, the chants of the priest and the delicious prasad. But in the house, we are often distracted by the TV or radio sound, shouting of our parents, plays of children and many more. Identify these famous temples of India (You can your elders' help also) and have some fun!!! Natural beauty of India Mount Everest Nature has many beautiful things hidden in it. One of them is the Mount Everest. As you all know, it is the tallest mountain the whole world with about 8848 meters. Even though it is not located in India, it surrounds all the three countries: Northern Nepal, Southern China and North Eastern India. Many mountaineers have climbed this Mountain. The first record was broken in the year 1953 where two men: Tensing Norway and Edmund Hillary climbed this mountain and the first woman to climb this mountain was Bachendri Pal of India. Amsun Jansepa is the only woman of India who has climbed the Mount Everest two times in just two weeks.!!! Sundarbans delta, West Bengal Sundarbans is the largest delta in the whole world. Delta is a place where more than one river meets before going into a sea. It is located near Bay of Bengal. It has more than 50 % of world's tigers, 100 % of world's lions and many more animals such as deer, elephant, giraffe, monkeys, crocodiles, zebras, mammoths and many more. It is a natural forest always under protection and not even a single part of it is destroyed. Crops grow here really fast and there is a high yield for farmers. Jog falls, Karnataka Jog falls is the highest waterfalls in India and the second highest waterfalls in the world. It is located in the district of Shivamogga of Karnataka, a state in India. This falls is formed by the river Sharavati. It is used for generating electricity. It is believed that Lord Shiva had once come to meditate here. This place resembled his face and therefore it was named Shivamogga. In Kannada, 'mogga' means 'face.' Gir forest, Gujarat It is believed that Gujarat was named after the forest of Gir. When you look at the map of India, you see that the Gujarat resembles the face of a lion. The Gir forest contains 100 % of the Asiatic lions of the world. It is so because in all other parts of the world, these lions were being threatened and poached. So, all the lions came and settled here. The government of India, in the year 2014, knowing this, passed a law that the Gir forest should not be harmed for any reason. And so, it got implemented and now there is no kind of hunting or poaching in it. Nagarahole Tiger reserve, Karnataka ﻿Even though this park is owned by government it is the only sanctuary where it has paths which leads to other places & sanctuaries. They are 3 in number. One path leads to Periyar wildlife sanctuary of Kerala and the other two parts to Kasaragod and Wayanad respectively. It is said that the Nagarahole Tiger reserve, Rangantittu birds sanctuary, Periyar wildlife sanctuary, Kishkindha (Hills of Hampi) were the part of ancient Dandakaranya forest which was there in India about 10000 years ago. It is a great thing that this was not destroyed in that span of 10000 years. However, India has all the species shown in and 25 protected but in less numbers. Some interesting facts about the natural beauty of India India has more than half of the world's tigers, 65 % of the Asian Elephants, 85 % of the great one - horned rhinoceros and 100 % of the Asian lions. India is sixth on a list of 12 mega - biodiversity countries in the world. It contains two of the 34 biodiversity hotspots of the world - Eastern Himalayas and Western Ghats. These areas are very rich in biodiversity. India contains 172 species of animals considered globally threatened or 2.9 % of the world's total number of threatened species. Eastern Himalayas hotspot has merely 163 globally threatened species including several animal and plant species. India contains globally important population of some of Asia's rarest animals such as the Bengal fox, Marbled cat, Asiatic lion, Indian elephant, Asiatic wild ass, Indian rhinoceros, gaur, Wild Asiatic water buffalo etc. For knowing more, you may contact Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Govt. of India Environment, Forest and Wildlife department Indira Parayavaran Bhavan, Jor Bag Road, New Delhi - 110003 Website: AND HERE I AM THERBY ENDING THIS BOOK. title: Environmental pollution part 2
text: Air pollution is the presence of substances in the atmosphere that are harmful to the health of humans and other living beings, or cause damage to the climate or to materials. There are many different types of air pollutants, such as gases (including ammonia, carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrous oxides, methane, carbon dioxide and chlorofluorocarbons), particulates (both organic and inorganic), and biological molecules. Air pollution can cause diseases, allergies, and even death to humans; it can also cause harm to other living organisms such as animals and food crops, and may damage the natural environment (for example, climate change, ozone depletion or habitat degradation) or built environment (for example, acid rain). Both human activity and natural processes can generate air pollution.
author: Gauransh Kardam

title: Environmental pollution part 5
text: Water pollution (or aquatic pollution) is the contamination of water bodies, usually as a result of human activities, in such a manner that negatively affects its legitimate uses. [1]: 6 Water pollution reduces the ability of the body of water to provide the ecosystem services that it would otherwise provide. Water bodies include for example lakes, rivers, oceans, aquifers, reservoirs and groundwater. Water pollution results when contaminants are introduced into these water bodies. In addition to damage to many species, water pollution can also lead to water-borne diseases for people. [2] Water pollution traditionally is attributed to four sources, which provide the organization of this article: [3] sewage industry agriculture urban runoff including stormwater.
author: Gauransh Kardam

title: Goodnight tinku
text: IT was the bright night. All the animals in Mangu' s farm were sleeping. Except Tinku "I am not seepy, ma" murmured tinku. but Ma did not hear him. She was fast asleep. He turned left, and he turned right. He lay on his tummy, and rolled on his back. But he could not sleep! So he set off into the night to see what he could find. Up in the sky, Tinku saw the moon, white and round, smiling down at him. He felt very happy. ‘Night is beautiful, ’ thought Tinku. Far away on the top of a tree, there were some tiny lights. One spot of light flew down! “I’m a firefly, ” said the spot of light. “I glow in the dark!” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the firefly. Something flew by and hung upside down on a tree. “What is your name, bird?” asked Tinku. “I am not a bird, I am a bat. I can see during the night!” said the bat. “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the bat. A few leaves moved in the bushes. Someone was hiding! “Who are you?” asked Tinku. “I am a fox, ” said the fox. “I go strolling out at night.” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the fox. Two shiny eyes looked at him from a tree. “Who are you?” asked Tinku. “I’m an owl, ” said the owl. “I hunt for food during the night.” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the owl. “CHIRRRRRP! CHIRRRRRP!” “Who is here?” Tinku asked. “I’m a cricket, ” said the cricket. “I chirp when it is dark.” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the cricket. Tinku and his friends jumped and tossed and rolled until Tinku yawned. “I am sleepy. I have to go home now, ” said Tinku. He was happy that he had many new friends. Snuggling close to Ma, he said, “Night is not a lonely place, Ma. Night is full of wonderful beings.” “Yes!” replied Ma. “Your new friends are nocturnal, just like wild dogs. “Nocturnal animals eat, play and work at night. They rest during the day. You must sleep now. Sleep will give you energy to play with your day-time friends tomorrow. Good night, little one!” she said, hugging him tight. The bright round moon shone all night long, spreading her calm light all around. And Tinku slept all through the night!
author: Gauransh Kardam

title: Lazy Anansi
text: Once upon a time, there was a spider called Anansi. He was too lazy to cook his own food. Instead, he used to visit his friends and eat the delicious food they had cooked. One da y, he was walking past Rabbit’ s house when he smelled something cooking. “Greens!” he said excitedly. “They’re not quite ready yet,” said Rabbit. “You can help me with the washing up in the mean time.” “Sorry y, I have things to do. I’ll come back later,” said Anansi. How will I call you when they’re ready?” asked Rabbit. Anansi thought for a minute. “I'll spin a web,” he said, “and tie one end around my leg and one end to your pot. When the greens are ready, pull on the web string and I’ll come right away.” So Anansi tied the web to the pot, and walked on. A short while later he saw Monkey and his wife, cooking some beans in a large pot. “Come and join us!” they said. “The beans are nearly ready.” “Sorry y, I have things to do,” said Anansi before they could ask him to help. “But let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot. When the beans are ready, pull on the web string, and I’ll come. He walked on until he smelled sweet potatoes. “Anansi,” called his friend Warthog. “My pot is full of sweet potatoes and honey! Come and share my food with me. Here’s a fork for you to help me stir.” “I’ll come back later,” said Anansi quickly. “But let me tie one end of this web around my leg and one end to your pot. When the sweet potatoes are ready, pull on the web string, and I’ll come. By the time Anansi arrived at the river, each of his eight legs was tied to a different pot of delicious food. Just then, Anansi felt a tug on one of his legs. “Rabbit’s food is ready!” he said, licking his lips. He felt a second tug. And a third. And a fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth... Everyone was pulling on the web strings at the same time! “Stop! Stop!” he cried in pain, as his legs were stretched thinner and thinner. But no one could hear him. Finally, the web strings could hold no longer. They snapped one by one. Anansi rolled into the river to soothe his painful legs. But his legs would not return to their normal shape. And he was too embarrassed to go t o any of his friends and share their food that da y.
author: Gauransh Kardam

title: Hen and Eagle
text: Once upon a time, Hen and Eagle were friends. They lived in peace with all the other birds. None of them could fly. One day, there was famine in the land. Eagle had to walk very far to find food. She came back very tired. “There must be an easier way to travel!” said Eagle. After a good night’s sleep, Hen had a brilliant idea. She began collecting the fallen feathers from all their bird friends. “Let’s sew them together on top of our own feathers,” she said. “Perhaps that will make it easier to travel.” Eagle was the only one in the village with a needle, so she started sewing first. She made herself a pair of beautiful wings and flew high above Hen. Hen borrowed the needle but she soon got tired of sewing. She left the needle on the cupboard and went into the kitchen to prepare food for her children. But the other birds had seen Eagle flying away. They asked Hen to lend them the needle to make wings for themselves too. Soon there were birds flying all over the sky. When the last bird returned the borrowed needle, Hen was not there. So her children took the needle and started playing with it. When they got tired of the game, they left the needle in the sand. Later that afternoon, Eagle returned. She asked for the needle to fix some feathers that had loosened on her journey. Hen looked on the cupboard. She looked in the kitchen. She looked in the yard. But the needle was nowhere to be found. “Just give me a day,” Hen begged Eagle. “Then you can fix your wing and fly away to get food again.” “Just one more day,” said Eagle. “If you can’t find the needle, you’ll have to give me one of your chicks as payment.” When Eagle came the next day, she found Hen scratching in the sand, but no needle. So Eagle flew down very fast and caught one of the chicks. She carried it away. Forever after that, whenever Eagle appears, she finds Hen scratching in the sand for the needle. As the shadow of Eagle’s wing falls on the ground, Hen warns her chicks. “Get out of the bare and dry land.” And they respond: “We are not fools. We will run.”
author: Gauransh Kardam
illustrator: David Chisha; Lavanya Karthik; Siddhi   Vartak; Stephen Wallace; Suvidha  Mistry

text: Jaya was a lonely little girl. One day her mother took her to a pet store and bought a cat. Jaya named her ‘Minni’. Jaya soon started to like Minni. title: This New Year I Will...
text: "I hate you. I hate you all, you are all just ganging up against me!" Veer yelled at his sister Riya and his cousins. And he climbed up the tree, trying to get away from them all. "You are mad!" Riya glared up at him. Sid and Sia just rolled their eyes used to their cousins' drama. It was always the same story. Pushpa Punji, great-grandma, grinned as she heard the kids quarrelling from the window. Yes, Riya and Veer were at it again. And with their cousins visiting, they certainly were not putting their best foot forward. Time to jump in, she realized. Time to pull out some tricks from her Punji-Potli, punji-bag! "Why this ruckus Kids? What's going on?" " Punji, I hate them all! I want to play badminton but as always Riya is being impossible! And the others are just following her lead, " Veer shouted from the branch. "But Punji there are just two rackets and we are four of us. Stupid Veer has the worst plans as always!" Yelled back Riya. "Besides I hate running here and there, behind that stupid badminton shuttle!" "Now, now calm down kids. Let's end this here. Let's end this now. You know with the New year, it is time for fresh beginnings! Time to forgive and forget. Yes it is time for some Noble New Year's Resolutions indeed! Let's begin this new year with laughter and cheer!" declared Punji in a singsong voice. "What's that Punji? What's a New Year's resolution?" asked Sid. How he loved their Punji and her wise-old tales "Well, sweetheart a New Year's resolution is a promise one makes to start something new and good in the New year. Or even stop something bad." Replied Punji with a glimmer in her eye. "You know my New Year's Resolution is about taking care of my health. And yes, THIS NEW YEAR I WILL cook only healthy and delicious snacks for you kids everyday!" " "YUMMM awesome Punji!!!And MY New Year's resolution will be to finish them all up. Yes THIS NEW YEAR I WILL finish all of my Punji's yummy snacks, " giggled back Riya. Punji smiled; she knew how Riya loved snacking! And yes Riya also loved her video games. "Jokes apart, Riya why don't you decide on less video-games and more fun-games with your brother and cousins instead..." Suggested Punji. " Let me share a secret, you know I loved playing lappa-chappi, hide and seek when i was your age. And just like you,I hated playing andhali-koshimbir, blind-man's buff... " "Yes, THIS NEW YEAR RIYA will play blind-man's buff with Punji," chipped in Veer. And the others hooted and clapped, even shy Siya. Riya too grinned as Punji rolled her eyes. "And what about you, young man, what is your resolution?" Punji asked Veer I think it should have something to do with blowing off steam and patience and..." Riya retorted giving it right back to Veer! "Yes, THIS NEW YEAR VEER WILL turn into a calm, sweet boy. Surely an impossible feat!" Veer responding by sticking out his tongue. But he also gave his sister a high-five nodding in agreement. "And and and Punji, THIS NEW YEAR I WILL try make friends and speak more," stammered Siya.The others stared back at her. That was certainly a first for her for she barely ever said much. Yes, with the new year Siya the bookworm was surely turning over a new leaf! Punji reached out to her to give her a quick squeeze just as Veer gave her a high-five too. "And now it's my turn! THIS NEW YEAR I WILL try to read a new book every day," said Sid. "Well not every day, well at least every week or...." retracted Sid realizing his folly! "Hey, hey no going back on your resolution now Siddy," said Riya pulling her cousin's hair. "THIS NEW YEAR you will have to follow what you have just said. And that's final!" "Well Miss, your turn again what about another resolution..." Punji turned to Riya. " Punji you got to go first," Veer stopped her. "Well, well young man, you caught me there! THIS NEW YEAR I WILL eat less sweets and maybe even talk a little less." Said Punji slyly laughing at herself. "Just not possible Punji!" Shy Siya said in a faint whisper. "Yes, I agree but I am going to try you know. It is all about trying," Smiled back Punji. "Oh, I so love this then..." said Riya "Yes, we can at least try. Well, THIS NEW YEAR I WILL try and brush my teeth twice every day. Once in the morning and once in the evening. I really wish to have sparkling teeth for my smashing smile!" she declared. And of course Veer snorted as soon as he heard her! " If wishes were horses beggars would ride you know..." he laughed aloud. Grinning Punji turned to go back into the house. Yes, she surely had pulled yet another trick from her potli. The New year seemed most promising! The promising new resolutions and the sparkling faces bringing in cheer... Idioms and Phrases: The same story: Something that happens or is said over and over again. Putting their best foot forward: To behave very well in order to gain someone's approval. Following her lead: To do the same thing that someone else has done. Glimmer in her eye: An expression in your eyes that shows that you are amused or that you have a secret. Bookworm: A person who enjoys reading. Turning over a new leaf: Start to act or behave in a better or more responsible way. blowing off steam: Get rid of your energy, anger, or strong emotions If wishes were horses beggars would ride you know If just hoping and wishing for things would make it happen then even the poorest of all people would have everything that they desire.

title: THE UNMADE CAKE
text: Once upon a time, in a city there was a 13 years old girl called Joyce. She lived with her her father- Thomas and mother- Tina. One evening, when Christmas was around, Joyce was studying all alone, suddenly someone rang the doorbell. When she went to the door, she found a letter. It was from aunt Gloria. She took the letter and then she went in the study room. She opened the letter and read it aloud. After reading it, she was so happy. She said to herself: "I will tell this to my mother and father when they come back home." After a few hours, while Joyce was chopping some vegetables, suddenly the door bell rang. She went to the door and she checked from the small glassed hole. They were her parents. She happily opened the door. They greeted each other.... "Hello Mama, Hello Papa, Hello Sweetie, Hello Sweetheart". Joyce told: " I have something to tell you and Mama". He papa replied: "Oh okay, but first we will freshen ourselves up and the we could talk nicely, okay!" She replied: "Okay Papa." After freshening up, they sat and talked in the living room. Joyce told: " Papa, Mama, today aunt Gloria sent a letter and wrote that she will come this week on Sunday and will stay with us till first of January." Oh! is it? All were happy and excited. Joyce replied: " Yes Papa." He asked what time aunt Gloria will arrive, Joyce told by 5.30 pm. On Sunday, Joyce, Tina and Thomas were at the airport, waiting for Gloria. When it was 5.33 pm, Gloria came out. They greeted each other good evening and hugged each other. "I am so tired." told Gloria. Lets go in the car. The four of them went inside the car. After one hour, they reached home. [Gloria sighed], finally we reached home. They went inside the house. Gloria kept her boots in the show rack and asked Thomas: "Brother, may I know where is my bedroom? Sure, said Thomas and showed her bedroom. Gloria thanked him and went inside. She closed the door, went to freshen up and change her clothes. After bathing, she changed her clothes and then went in the study room, hiding something in her hands. Gloria tiptoed to the study room and then she surprised Joyce: "Boo!" "Aunt, you scared me, Hehehe!", said Joyce. Gloria told: "I am here to give you a surprise. Tadaa....!" Joyce responded happily: "Wow.... a Christmas sweater" I love the colour of the sweater, my favorite blue, said Joyce. "Yes dear!" told Gloria. She told" Thank you so much aunty". Gloria went to the living room, where Tina and Thomas were reading books. Then she surprised her sister-in-law: "Tadaa...! I have a surprise for you". Tina thanked Gloria for the sweater with a the reindeer knitted on it. Gloria then surprise her brother: "Tadaa...!" Thomas was so happy for the Christmas sweater. He thanked his sister. Finally, Christmas time came. Joyce, Tina and Thomas wore the sweaters Gloria gifted them. Joyce told: "Mama, Papa and aunty, today I want to bake a small lemon and coconut cake for brunch." All of them were excited to have the cake. Joyce went in the kitchen and took the recipe book. Then she started to make the cake. When Joyce went to the oven to bake the cake, she realized instantly that the electricity power went low. She knew that he cannot bake now. She thought for sometime and suddenly an idea came up. She decided to make lemon coconut pudding instead. After making the puddings, she made creamy snowflakes. Then she took some biscuits and placed below each puddings. Then placed the snowflakes on the top of the puddings. Then...Vola.... it turned out to be a lovely coconut lemon pudding. She then put spoons on each pudding and then took two plates of puddings. She walked slowly and carefully to the dinning table. Gloria then went to the kitchen and helped Joyce to bring the puddings carefully on the table. Tina then said: "Joyce, you told you will make lemon coconut cake? Why did you make coconut lemon puddings?" Joyce explained the whole situation. After she told, all tasted the puddings. Gloria then told: "Joyce, your puddings are so tasty". Tina and Thomas also appreciated:" Yes dear, it is so delicious!" Everyone enjoyed the tasty brunch. THE END MORAL: EVERY PROBLEM HAS A SOLUTION.
author: Chanasya Das

title: Goodnight, Tinku!
text: It was a bright moonlit night. All the animals in Mangu's farm were sleeping. Except Tinku! “I am not sleepy, Ma, ” murmured Tinku. But Ma did not hear him. She was fast asleep. He turned left, and he turned right. He lay on his tummy, and rolled on his back. But he could not sleep! So he set off into the night to see what he could find. Up in the sky, Tinku saw the moon, white and round, smiling down at him. He felt very happy. ‘Night is beautiful, ’ thought Tinku. Far away on the top of a tree, there were some tiny lights. One spot of light flew down! “I’m a firefly, ” said the spot of light. “I glow in the dark!” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the firefly. Something flew by and hung upside down on a tree. “What is your name, bird?” asked Tinku. “I am not a bird, I am a bat. I can see during the night!” said the bat. “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the bat. ﻿ A few leaves moved in the bushes. Someone was hiding! “Who are you?” asked Tinku. “I am a fox, ” said the fox. “I go strolling out at night.” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the fox. Two shiny eyes looked at him from a tree. “Who are you?” asked Tinku. “I’m an owl, ” said the owl. “I hunt for food during the night.” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the owl. “CHIRRRRRP! CHIRRRRRP!” “Who is here?” Tinku asked. “I’m a cricket, ” said the cricket. “I chirp when it is dark.” “Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku. “Yes, I will!” said the cricket. Tinku and his friends jumped and tossed and rolled until Tinku yawned. “I am sleepy. I have to go home now, ” said Tinku. He was happy that he had many new friends. Snuggling close to Ma, he said, “Night is not a lonely place, Ma. Night is full of wonderful beings.” “Yes!” replied Ma. “Your new friends are nocturnal, just like wild dogs. “Nocturnal animals eat, play and work at night. They rest during the day. You must sleep now. Sleep will give you energy to play with your day-time friends tomorrow. Good night, little one!” she said, hugging him tight. The bright round moon shone all night long, spreading her calm light all around. And Tinku slept all through the night!
author: Gauransh Kardam

title: An ungrateful goldsmith
text: Once, there was a traveller named Sushant Hari Singh. He was travelling with a flock of bananas in his bullock cart. It is because in his village, there was no one to purchase his bananas. Therefore, he had to go to the cooperative society by crossing the nearby dense forest. On the way, many bananas fell and nearby monkeys and other animals fought for these bananas. He was often scared of which animal would attack him. He had two bullocks which were enough strong. So, he had nothing to worry. On the way, as he was passing near a well, he heard someone shouting "Help! Help! Someone, please help us! We are not able to live here! This is really suffocating! I think we are going to die here!" Sushant Hari Singh hearing this, pitied and ran in horror to see who was there in the well. When he peeped inside the well, he saw four organisms: A tiger, A monkey, A snake and a man. Sushant Hari Singh immediately put a rope inside the well. After quite a tussle, all the three organisms finally came out except the man. When Sushant tried to rescue that man, the animals, "Oh! Sushant! Don't rescue that man! He is sure to be very ungrateful to you!" But Sushant Hari Singh didn't listen to the animals. He rescued the man too. The man introduced himself as a goldsmith. Goldsmith: Oh! What's your name? Sushant: Oh! My name is Sringeri Srinivas. I am a banana trader. Nice to meet you! Goldsmith: I am a goldsmith. My name is Nanda. I work in the nearby dynasty of Yaravis. Sushant: Oh! Nice to meet you. I hope that Goldsmith: I am your friend. When you are in trouble, you can ask me for your help. Sushant continued on his way. After sometime, he felt tired and decided to take rest. Unfortunately, in that same forest, there was a gang of robbers. They saw him resting. They quickly stopped him, showed him guns, knives and sickles and ordered him to give all the bananas. Sushant refused. The robbers immediately robbed him, tied him and threw him from a cliff top. Sushant fell with a thud. The robbers stole his cart of bananas and his two bullocks. The night had fallen. Sushant was still crying and howling with pain. After sometime, there was a monkey which saw him from a nearby tree. This was the monkey which he had helped when it fall with the rest of the animals. The monkey immediately came down and removed the rope, picked him up and asked him to follow him up. The monkey took him up the hill and made him rest there. The monkey then went to the camp where robbers were fast asleep. It then took all the bananas which were stolen by the robbers. Sushant ate it to the heart's content. The next day, when the robbers woke up, they find all their treasure empty. They foolishly feared that some devil had come. And so, with the bullocks they ran off never to be seen again. Sushant continued on his journey. Later, a tiger called him up from a distance. He feared the tiger but he recalled that it was the tiger whom he had helped when it fell in the well. He went to the tiger's den. As a token of gift, it offered him some food and also gave him a precious golden necklace!!!!!! Sushant Hari Singh took the necklace, thanked the tiger and continued on his way. He then made a decision to pay a visit to the goldsmith whom he had helped. He at last reached the goldsmith's house and the goldsmith welcomed him. Sushant sold some bananas which he had recovered with the help of monkey which in return he got some gold coins. The goldsmith accidently saw the gold necklace in Sushant's hand which the tiger had given to him. The necklace was actually a Xerox copy of the necklace of the princess of the Yaravi king. The goldsmith instead of inquiring him about the necklace, made a wicked plan to somehow captivate Sushant. And so did the goldsmith. When Sushant went to the kitchen to drink some water, the goldsmith immediately took the necklace, ran to the king's palace and complained that Sushant had robbed the necklace of the princess and handed it over to the king. The king immediately sent the guards to the goldsmith's house and Sushant was arrested and put behind the bars even though it was not his mistake. He felt it was illegal to arrest an innocent. But what to do? Even before he could speak the word, the king arrested him. It was the ungratefulness of the goldsmith. The wicked goldsmith thought "Yes!! Now that Sushant is arrested. All his property is now mine!!" And so, Sushant continued to be in sorrow and had to eat whatever was given to him in the jail. Sometimes, he had to go on fast. His family too was sorrowful hearing this incident. All his banana trade stopped. Who helped him at that time? Yes, you are right. It is the snake. It came trough as small hole in the wall of the jail. Sushant at first was scared but later realised it was the snake which he had rescued from the well. The snake had also brought a medicinal herb with him. It gave the medicinal herb to Sushant Hari Singh and said to him that it would go and bite the queen and he should prepare a medicine out of this herb and give it to the queen. Only then, she would recover or else, she was sure to die. And so, the snake unnoticed quietly crept into the room and bit the queen. The queen shouted and yelled. The servants hearing her shout, came running to her room, only to find her fallen on the floor as if she passed away. They saw this snake. They tried to kill it but it escaped from their eyes. Unsuccessful, the servants reported about the queen's snake bite to the king. The king heard this and almost fainted. In that 1 hour time, he consulted many great and excelled physicians but they too were unsuccessful. Finally, when Sushant heard of this, it was now his opportunity to make the king happy and free himself from the jail. He requested the guards to allow him and told them that he had a medicine to cure the queen and so he was let out. Sushant approached and said that he would cure the queen. The king could not believe his eyes. But still, he gave an opportunity to do so. Sushant took the herb to get its juice. This juice was nothing but the venom of that snake. He then applied it to the place where the snake had bit the queen. In no time, the queen regained her consciousness and came back alive. The king felt really happy. He rewarded Sushant with a 1000 gold coins. Sushant could not control his joy that he was released from the jail. When the king enquired about the necklace, Sushant asked where the princess. The king called for the princess. The princess came and in her neck was the same necklace which the goldsmith had shown. The king realized that the necklace which was handed over to the king by the goldsmith was a duplicate necklace. He came to know that the goldsmith was a fraud. He sent his guards to arrest the goldsmith. Sushant Hari Singh took the king's leave and left. Meanwhile, the goldsmith was standing in a railway station waiting for the train. He thought that he was the king's favourite. The guards who were sent by the king finally found the goldsmith, who was trying to board the train and arrested him, and he was put in the jail for lifetime. ﻿Moral: Never be ungrateful to anyone.

title: Transformation: Voluntary or involuntary?
text: What is transformation? Is it voluntary or involuntary? Transformation in simple words means "change". Is change voluntary (in our control) or is it involuntary (out of our control)? This question looks a bit puzzled. The correct answer is that changes are of two types: Voluntary and involuntary. Let us see which changes are involuntary and which are voluntary. Then, we will all understand the secret behind changes. First of all, we all know that things in nature keep changing whether it is natural or man made. Nothing is permanent. To know more about the changes, scientists have classified them as: Physical and chemical. Physical change occur only when the shape, size and dimensions of an object are changed. Here, no new substance is formed. Physical changes are mostly reversible. Example: Tearing of paper is a physical change because only the shape and physical characteristics of paper is changed. List at least 20 more examples of physical change. On the other hand, chemical changes are the ones where there is a complete change in the chemical properties also. As in the picture, cutting of trees is a physical change as there is a change only in physical properties of the tree. But imagine when that same tree is burnt, it is a chemical change as a new substance called ash is formed. It is generally irreversible. List at least 20 more examples for chemical changes. Also, in a chemical change, heat, light and sound is also produced. Example: Reaction of sodium with water. These are scientifically proven processes i.e. these can be seen, felt and even experimented. But there are some other changes which cannot be seen, felt and even experimented. That is a change but not scientific proven. For example: A sad person changed himself into a happy person. This is a change but in which group shall we classify? Physical or chemical? The answer is 'none of these'. Then, what type of a change is this? Yes, it is a behavioural change. This is the third type of a change. Spiritual change Spiritual change is a change where both the mind and the soul of a person change. It can be from good to bad or from bad to good. In this picture, you can see a saint meditating. He may not be saint from his birth. Later on, self - realization has pushed him towards spirituality. Now, I will give you some passages and you have to guess the type of change and have fun. Then, A story will appear. You have to read that answer its questions. Read the following passages and tell the type of change: 1. A violinist had finished his music programme and was returning to his home. On the way, he had to cross a dense forest. While he was walking through the dense forest, four thieves come and block him. They show him their weapons and ask him to give them money and whatever he had. The violinist said that he had no problem. He could give them as much as money they asked. He said to the thieves that he had a small wish which they should fulfil. The wish was that he would play a song and the thieves have to listen to it for 30 minutes. So, the violinist started playing the music. The music was so sweet and enlightening that after 2 hours, the thieves forgot about their demand. After the music, the thieves had tears in their eyes. They fell at his feet and begged for forgiveness. They then left all their weapons. The violinist gave them some money. The thieves then worked in a temple and contributed all the given money for it. 2. A girl named Anusha was a very good cook. She cooked for the whole family in her kitchen. Once, some guests arrived at her house. She had to prepare yogurt for all of them. Accidently, a spoon of curd goes and falls inside a warm milk stored in a vessel. Anusha didn't notice it. In the evening when Anusha went to drink milk for the snack time, she opened the vessel only to find curd. Anusha is wondering about it. Could you please tell her what had happened? 3. There was a hotel. In that hotel, there was a chef who was very haphazard. He was often absent minded. He would mistaken each and every thing and trouble the others. It so happened one day that he had to prepare idli for someone. So, he prepared a batter. He remembered that when he was young, his teacher had said that if a liquid like water was kept in the freezer, it would become solid in shape. Knowing that idli is solid in shape, he kept the batter in a freezer. What do you think might have happened to it? Mention the type of change. 4. He was a teenager. His name started with the letter S followed by R as the 3rd letter, S as the 5th letter and H at the last. He was a very naughty boy. He flew rockets with the other boys in the class whenever the teacher was absent. Once a teacher saw him standing on a bench and playing the ball with the other boys in the class. She at once came into the classroom with a big stick and sent him out of the class for his misbehaviour. The name of the teacher starts with the letter S followed M as the 3rd letter, T as 4th letter and I at the last. Seeing this, S__R__SH at once stopped all his bad behaviour and from then on he became a favourite of S_M_T_I MAM. What was the name of the teacher? What was the name of the student? What type of change is it? Answers for the passages: 1) Spiritual change 2) A bacteria called Lactobacillus has converted milk into the curd. Its a chemical change. 3)It would hardened up. Physical change. 4) The name of the student was Suresh and the teacher name was Sumathi. Behavioural change The monk who sold his Ferrari - Written by Robin Sharma S There was once an American lawyer named Julian Mantle. He was a very well known rich person. He was so rich that he owned a Ferrari car, a private airline of his own and a big bungalow. It was so because he won many cases in the court. As a result of this, he always over concentrated on his career and hardly spent time to bother about his family. This led to conflicts and at last into divorce. One day, when Julian Mantle was arguing a case in the court, he suddenly collapsed in the court floor due to a massive heart attack. An ambulance was called for immediately. Julian Mantle was admitted to the hospital in a hurry. After many days of treatment, luck bestowed upon him and he survived. The doctor then told him that if he wanted to live further, he needed peace and renunciation. As per the doctor's advice, he resigned his job. With the help of remaining money, he climbed up a plane and flew to India and at last reached Shivaliks (Foothills of the Himalayas). There, he saw a number of monks and sages meditating there. One of the monks named Yogi Raman asked him who he was and why came here. Julian Mantle introduced himself and also told the reason of why he had come to Shivaliks. Then, Yogi Raman taught some arts of meditation which the sages used to take salvation or eternal bliss and peace. Julian did not understand what Yogi Raman was telling and therefore, Yogi Raman decided to teach life's moral's to Julian with a simple story and it goes like this: "There was a beautiful garden. In that garden, there were so many beautiful trees, plants, herbs and flowers. Many insects came from different places and sucked nectar from these flowers. It was very clean. In the middle of that beautiful garden, there was a tall lighthouse. In that lighthouse, there lived a wrestler and a red turban was tied to its waist. When the wrestler came out and was walking, he saw a beautiful golden watch lying in the garden. He ran to snatch it but unfortunately he tripped a stone and fell with a thud and fainted. Near to him was a beautiful rose plant. The rose plant game him so much beautiful fragrance that he woke up. When he woke up, he saw a long road covered with diamonds. Unable to tolerate his happiness, he walked on the road and lived a happy life ever after." Here the story ends. When the sage asked whether Julian had understood the story, Julian remarked with a "No". Then, the sage explains what each of the characters symbolize. 1. Garden The garden in this story symbolizes our mind. If a garden is fed with fertilizers, manure and often if medicines such as fungicides, pesticides are blown, we get a good yield of wonderful plants. But that if we don't do these things but rather allow garbage to get accumulated, allow mushrooms and poisonous plants like parthenium grow, the garden will no more remain beautiful but become a dump yard. Similarly, when our mind is trained to fill only positive thoughts in it, it does wonders. But when we don't train it properly, it receives even negative thoughts which ultimately make our mind our own enemy. Some more facts about mind: Remember: 1. Mind is a good servant but a bad master We also remember a Bhagavad - Gita shloka which says: UDDHARET AATMAN AATMAANAM AATMAANAM AVASAADAYET AATMAIVA HYAATMANO BANDHUH AATMAIVA RIPURAATMANAH || 5 || Meaning: One must deliver himself with the help of his mind, and not degrade himself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well. Ultimately, it is based on how we train it. 2. Lighthouse Here, lighthouse represents goal. Goal is nothing but a purpose of life i.e. to make life meaningful, we need to have a goal. After setting a goal, life is all about reaching it. To reach your goal, you need just two things: focus and determination. Focus is that we do not derail from our path and determination means that we should not feel tired during that journey. Many obstacles come but we should overcome them by determination. Some more facts about goal: There is a Bhagavad Gita Shloka which says: VYAVASAAYAATMIKA BUDDHIH EKEHA KURUNANDANAH BAHUSHAAKHA HYANANTAASCHA BUDDHAVYO VYAVASAAYINAM || 41|| Meaning: Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kuru tribe, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is many - branched. 3. Wrestler Here, wrestler symbolizes practice. "Practice makes a man perfect" is a famous proverb which we have heard since childhood. What does this mean? It means that we cannot learn anything just once. Repeating what we have learnt again and again with improving ourselves (correcting flaws) is called practice. In ancient Japan, people who learnt martial arts had to practice everyday for 2 hours. This type of practice was called Kaizen. Some more facts about Practice: A Bhagavad - Gita shloka says: ASAMSHAYAM MAHAABAAHO MANO DURNIGRAHAM CHALAM ABHYAASENA TU KOUNTEYA VAIRAAGYENA CHA GRUHYATE || 35 || Meaning: Oh mighty armed son of Kunti, it is undoubtedly very difficult to curb the restless mind, but it is possible by suitable practice and by detachment. 4. Red cloth Red cloth symbolizes discipline. To lead a meaningful life, along with goal, we also need something called discipline. A set of regulations kept for doing activities in an order to lead a pleasant life is called discipline. Nothing is useful without discipline. This is also one of the qualities required along with focus and determination. Self - discipline means a set of regulations kept by oneself for doing activities in an order to lead a pleasant life. 5. Golden stopwatch Here, the golden stopwatch symbolizes time. Time is very precious. Time once lost cannot be regained back. People who respect time achieve what they really need in their life. We all have heard that childhood is a golden period in a human's life. It is because childhood is a time when a man can be nurtured easily like how we want him to be. His mentality, behaviour can be corrected to make him a boon to the society. Similarly, puberty (age group between 13 to 19) is called a silver period in a human's life. It is because the human body undergoes many changes physically and mentally. Adulthood is called a copper period because in this period we can learn and also achieve what we want and old age is called iron period where we can't work much and we also suffer a lot of difficulties and diseases. But for some people, it is a platinum (costlier than gold) period as they surpass through the old age, engaging in spirituality and passing out of this world in a smooth manner. Nothing is permanent except change because it involves 'time'. 6. Roses Here, the roses symbolize 'selflessness'. If a person is selfish, he cannot lead a happy life. Helping others brings contentment to him and he doesn't become greedy. Selfishness leads to greed and greed leads to hell as holy books say. It is true. 'Selflessness' primarily means 'contributing' and 'helping'. For example, we can praise, hit drums and sing sons, play skits, crack jokes or even interview a company founder like Mukesh Ambani (the richest man in India) and Sudha Moorthy(the co-founder of INFOSYS). But do you think that they will feel happy and content? No. If they have to be happy and content, they have to contribute at least some of their money to poor, grief - stricken and the sufferers of natural disasters. Remember: "Misers donate their money only after death." 7. Diamond road In this story, the diamond rod symbolizes 'present' tense. We should all focus on the 'present' because in 'future', this becomes 'past'. You must have observed some people or yourself crying or scolding yourself about your 'past' and worrying about your 'future'. This should never be done.' 'Present' is the only time where we can modify ourselves. We should modify and move on. Crying on the past and worrying about the future is of no use. If we use our present properly, there is no need of worrying about future. Opportunity knocks on the door only once. So, let us use it. Hereby, I am ending this book wishing you a happy 'present'. TILL THE NEXT BOOK COMES, GOODBYE READERS!!!! "STAY HAPPY, STAY HOME, STAY SAFE AND STAY SPITIRTUAL"

title: No worries Nina, just smile
text: Nina gets ready for school. “ Eat your breakfast Nina and put on your skirt," says her mother. “Coming mother," says Nina. You see Nina is always happy, So everyone tells her the happy girl. She is always ready with a smile. Today was the day of receiving her marks for her 3rd term exam. She was excited if she got full marks. As the teacher was calling everyone names, most of the children got full marks. When her teacher called her name. “Nina-87 marks." says her teacher. “ What!" Nina was shocked!. She got 77% out of 100%. “ Nina please study more." says her teacher. “ Yes Miss," says Nina sadly. It was the first time Nina was sad and shocked. “ Don't be sad Nina. Everyone makes mistakes in life, especially in the exam. Nina just because you cut your marks this year then goes not mean it will cut every time. Besides its playing time. Maybe after playing, you will feel okay. Now run along everyone" says her teacher Nina still felt sad. It was indeed very surprising for all the children when they saw Nina sad. They asked why. But she was so ashamed that she got low marks, So she just turned around without answering their question. Ahmed who was Nina's best friend saw her frowning at a wall. Of course, he didn't believe that she was angry at a rock. He knew she got low marks. As soon as it landed on Nani's hand and it crooked “CROOK". Nani saw the frog and back at her friend and again back at the frog. She had a hearty laugh. She laughed until her belly ached. Then she told she got low marks and also lost 4 of her teeth. Her friends told that its okay Nina. That's what friends are for right? “Yes," says Nina. Ahmed explained to Nina's mom not to be furious with Nina's marks but to tell her to study more. And what happened next? Nina studied hard and got full marks next year. And that's the story of Nina. THE END ﻿
