title: A Rock, A Dog
text: Today, Avi is a rock. Mama calls the rock for lunch. Rocks cannot move on their own. So Mama picks up the rock and places it on the chair. Still, blink, shift. Still— A fly buzzes near the rock. Buzz-uzz-zz, Buzz-uzz-zz, Buzz— The rock sits still. Avi is a koel today. The koel is building a nest. One brown string, two buttons, Oo uuuo! three sticks. One brown string— Woof! Woof! Avi is a dog today. Papa gives the dog some soup in a bowl. Slurp, chomp. Slurp, chomp— Where is Avi? Avi is a chameleon today. The chameleon moves slowly between the curtains. Blue polka dots, white stripes, red-and-golden beads. Blue polka dots— The chameleon is trying to catch fruit flies. One fly, three flies. One fly, three flies— Baa-la-la-la, Baa-la-la-la— Avi is the alarm clock today. The alarm tells everyone what time it is. Mama and Papa have to press the nose of the clock to switch it off. EATING TIME Boop CLEAN UP! Boop PLAY Boop EATING TIME Boop CLEAN UP! Boop Avi is a hare today. Hares like to jump, watch and listen. Hop-hop-hop-bounce! Hop-hop— The hare is tired out by all the hopping around. Papa picks up the tired hare. Snore, foof. Snore— What will Avi be tomorrow? Patterns Are All Around Us There are patterns in the way we play. Arranging blocks, throwing a ball, playing hide-and-seek — all have a pattern to them. What are the patterns you’ve noticed when you play? Go back to the beginning of the book and try to find all the patterns you might have missed.
author: Sanjana  Kapur

title: I Want That Only!
text: She was sitting and reading a book. Even Anil was on a holiday. He wanted to do something or the other. "Mama, what is there in the blue trunk? I want to see!" Said Anil. "Anil, let's see later" replied the mother. Anil brought a stool and kept in on the chair and climbed to bring down the blue trunk. "No, no! no! Anil, whatever more trunks are on top of that will all fall on our heads!" Said the mother. Anil became very angry. He was angry on his mother too. " Let's go to the market and let's buy you something," said the mother. Even after going to the market Anil was very angry. "I want that" he kept showing his finger while looking at the orange. "No, no! Not that! All the fruits will fall down!" Said the fruit vendor. "I want that book" said Anil. "No, no! Not that! Take this." Said the shopkeeper. "I want that!" Anil said it in the interest of taking one samosa. "No, no! Not that! All my samosa's will fall down!" Said the sweet vendor. "I want that!" said Anil. "No, no! Not that! Don't even touch it! The flowers will dry up." Said the flower vendor. Now Anil started to cry loudly. Everyone was looking at Anil. "I want that! It is black!", Said the mother. Anil suddenly stopped to cry. Mother, no, no! Not that!" Said Anil. Let's take the colour of the mud.!" Said Anil. Anil slowly picked up a mud color puppy. "Mother, I am very angry on you! All the puppies would have fallen down!" Mother laughed. Even Anil was laughing. Now then he wasn't angry at all.

title: Gajan's village
text: Once upon a time, there lived a small boy named Gajan. The villagers would not be sympathetic to him as he was an adolescent and they thought he was a curse to the village. Gajan’s parents felt his pain but had no money for his treatment. The village once faced a drought that no one could save the village from. Gajan was so ill that he his arm. He had to be treated. His parents' confidence sank day by day. One day a stranger appeared in the village and he wore strange clothes. Everyone was shocked to see the stranger go to Gajan’s house. Gajan’s parents were scared to open the door after hearing the knock thinking it must be a villager who wanted to trouble them. Even in fear, they opened the door. Surprised with no words to say they saw a sage standing at their door. They welcomed the sage and explained the situation of Gajan. His parents also explained how the village was suffering and looked for any help. Sage: First go get me water I am thirsty. Gajan’s parents: we don’t have any water Sage: If you cannot give me water, I cannot grant your wish. I can grant only one wish. Gajan’s parents (thoughtfully): We do not want to disappoint you. We will think of some ideas to fetch some water for us and you as well. Sage: I have a condition, Get water only for me. His parents thought that the sage was very greedy. They checked with their neighbors. The neighbors did not help them like earlier. Gajan’s parents did not want to disappoint the sage. They thought of going to a nearby village to get water. His father went to get some water with great difficulty. He always remembered to get water only for the sage. In the meantime, the sage asked them after drinking the water if they wanted to save their son or village from drought. His parents after thinking for a long time chose to save the village. Sage granted the wish of saving the village. Sage advised them to check the well. Sage says Gajan to drink water. He drank the well water and he was able to recover. Then the parents asked, “why did you grant two wishes when you had to grant only one?” then the sage answers with a smile “when you were ready to sacrifice your son for the village where no villagers help you, you won my heart.” Villagers also got to know that the village had water around and Gajan’s family was the reason to restore the water back. This turned the villagers happy. This made them thank Gajan's parents and live in harmony.

title: Pincchu takes Diya and Deepu to Sinhagad
text: "Oh, Deepu I am so bored, I hate this dumb and stupid COVID," complained Diya!" You know I am actually WAITING to go back to SCHOOL. Back to REAL school. I really hate this online stuff." "Yes Diya, I sooooo agree with you!" said Deepu. Pincchu their pup, stopped digging and stared at them in amazement! The normally squabbling duo were actually in agreement about something. Thank God for that! "I just want to GO SOMEWHERE! Actually ANYWHERE, far far away from here,” groaned Diya dreamily. "Whooo Diya of course we can! We got Pincchu now, remember!"And with a twinkle in his eye Deepu turned to Pincchu, their MAGIC pup. " Pincchu please please please, you got to take us away from here. It's high time! It's been many days since our last adventure you know." Now, Pincchu was REALLY a MAGIC pup. It was their own special secret! Yes, Pincchu a gift from their charismatic ajoba – grandfather had many tricks up his sleeves oops paws. He spoke human language. He could also change size. He could even fly and teleport them to places within seconds. Yes, he was always full of surprises! And some brilliant tricks. As always Pincchu first tried playing dumb. But Diya and Deepu were not ones to be taken for a ride that easily. " Pincchu remember your Pincchu Promise... " Deepu reminded him. And when Pincchu continued his act, Diya stared into his big brown eyes knowing just how much their pup hated being stared at. "Ok ok Miss, I give up." he yelped. "I promise tonight our new adventure begins." "And Pincchu, this time it is my turn, remember?" Chipped in Deepu before Diya could say another word. Deepu knew his sister well and her way with words. Pincchu wagged his tail in agreement. "Yes, this time you can choose Deepu.Last time Miss Diya we did just what you wanted. We had gone to Parvati Hills, just as you wanted, remember? So now it’s your brother's turn. " That night Diya and Deepu waited for their aai-baba - parents to switch off the lights. At last, their parents were fast asleep. Yes, at last it was time for their adventure to begin. They crept towards Pincchu silently. He was waiting for them, just near their open balcony door. And remarkably he had grown quite majestic, much larger and much longer in size! The duo climbed onto his back without uttering a word eagerly waiting to fly off! Where to young man?" yelped Pincchu faintly. "Whooo SINHAGAD!!!" squealed Deepu quite determined. "But, buu it is HAUNTED, isn't it? Let's go somewhere else..." stammered Diya. "Miss scary boooo, oh soooo scared aren't youuuu..." giggled Deepu teasing. “It’s my turn. And I want to go to SINHAGAD. And if you are scared, you can stay back right here." Declared Deepu. " No way Jose, Sinhagad it is Pincchu," glared back Diya. Pincchu tweaked his ear AND in the blink of an eye they were flying atop the hilly fortress. They were amazed! How they loved being up there! "You know Sinhagad is named after Tanaji who fought just like a lion to recapture the fort back for Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, our mighty king. Sinha means lion, right? Did you know that it was called Kondana earlier?" Deepu questioned. Pincchu wagged his tail in response. "You know Pincchu, it's one of my favorite stories. I so looove the stories of our bahadur- brave Shivaji our Ajoba tells us at bedtime! And stories of his brave mavle - soldiers, especially Tanaji!" Exclaimed Deepu. What a sight, SINHAGAD must have been once the battle was won, with Shivaji's flag hoisted high up in the sky". "Yes, Deepu. Yet that was YESTERDAY. Do you know TODAY Sinhagad is often used by the cadets from our defence academy for training..." barked Pincchu. "In fact, can you see NDA - the National Defence academy? It is right there in that direction," Pincchu tilted his tail a wee bit. "You know, it is the FIRST academy in the world where all the three forces- Army, Air Force and Navy of the Defence Services are trained together." Deepu and Diya both craned their necks, their mouths wide open. "AND the cadets mess is the largest in Asia too," continued Pincchu as he knew how the kids enjoyed their meals. "WHOOO, can we visit NDA then, please, please please..." begged Deepu. " But Deepu, we need prior permission for that. You know, a few years ago, I attended the passing out parade there. What an amazing display of power it was! Why don't you ask Ajoba about a Sunday visit? " Pincchu stated. "Yes, yes, yes am definitely going to do that!" Diya declared clapping merrily. "And look, there you can see the KHADAKWASLA DAM," woofed Pincchu. "Do you know the original dam was built way back in 1879. It was the first of its kind in the World too. However, it had to be rebuilt in 1961; yes, even before your A ai and B aba were born. That year, the newly under construction Panshet Dam broke! The water also flooded the Khadakwasla dam located downstream. Yet for hours the Khadakwasla Dam stood firm, hand-in-hand with our Army Jawans who rushed in to help. Yes, Our Jawans - the soldiers worked so hard to cover the cracks with cement and sandbags for hours. Hence giving the residents of Pune and the nearby villagers much needed hours to flee the riverside! Diya and Deepu gazed at the dam in admiration."Really? That's amazing. Thank you, Khadakwasla Dam, for saving our beloved Punyanagari. Thank you Jawans! Even I am going to join the Army you know..." Diya shouted, "Me too!" Deepu shouted back, their voices echoing. Pincchu wagged his tail grinning from ear to ear. But he also realised that it was time to go back. "Kids dawn is breaking out. What an enchanting view isn't it? And..." "Oh, nooo it's time to dash home, before our A ai wakes up," interrupted Diya feeling sad, "Ofcourse we know we have to go back but I am going to choose the next adventure REAL SOON! Right Pincchu?" "Yes, yes Miss. And that's.... Pincchu Promise..."

title: THE FATHER'S WISDOM
text: Once there lived a very rich merchant Keshav and Virendar. While Keshav was clever and intelligent, Virendar was not witty. He took time to understand things. But both the brothers were well behaved and obedient. They loved and respected their father a lot. Keshav and Virendar grew up to be two very kind and dashing young men. They helped his father in his work. One day their father, the merchant fell seriously ill and was on his death bed. No medicine worked for him and the doctors said that he would die soon. One evening, the merchant called his sons in the room and said " Sons, I know I am not going to live for long. So now it's time for you two to look after all the business that I have. You have been helping me for a long time and know the business. So, I will between my property equally between the two of you. Now it's your hard work and luck. Always remember these words of mine- build a house in every city. Seep comfortably. Enjoy your food. When you lend someone money don't ask them to return it. Live by these words of mine you will be happy. Before he could explain the meaning of his words, he died. After his death, the sons gave his father a very grand funeral and then decided to work on his advice. Each of them took his share and started off on their own. They went to different cities to try their luck. Five years passed by. Keshav, who had following his father's advice became penniless. His brother on the other hand was richer than ever. Keshav was puzzled. Both had started with the same amount of money and followed their father's advice. He wondered why he was poor and his brother richer? Keshav thought and decided to visit Virendar to find out. On reaching Virendar's house, Keshav was surprised to see his patacial house which was even bigger than their father's house. There were expensive cars parked before the house and many servants were there to serve Virendar and his family. "Wow! How prosperous my brother is!" Keshav thought as he waited outside Virendar's house. Virendar was very pleased to see Keshav, welcome," Virendar greeted Keshav with open arms. How are you? What brings you here today? Keshav heaved a sigh and said, " Actually it's been five years since we have met each other. So I thought that I should come and meet you. " Virendar was very pleased to hear this and hugged his brother saying, " Indeed brother! It's so very nice of you to think like that. Do stay here as long as you want. I am glad to have you here. Virendar showed Keshav all over his house and his offices. That night, when the brothers sat down to chat after dinner, Keshav asked the questions that had been playing on his mind for so many days. He began saying, " Actually Virendar I want to ask you something. Remember the advice that father had given us on his death bed? I have done exactly as he had asked. Did you have done the same brother, I too followed father's advice and have achieved all the success that you can see today. ﻿ Keshav looked confused and continued, " I built a house in every city. But because I could not stay there always, I had to hire people to look after the houses. I lent money to people and never ask them to return it, So more and more people borrowed money from me and now I have nothing. Father said that we should sleep comfortably and eat well, so I got expensive beds made and employed expert cooks to prepare my meals. All this have left me without a penny in my pocket. You say that you too have done what father had told us to do, so why are you rich? Keshav's word made it clear to Virendar that he had not understood the true meaning of father's words and that's the reason he became penniless. He looked at Keshav and said, Listen, My brother, you have not understood the real meaning behind the father's advice. When he said build a house in every city, he meant we should make friends living in different places, so that when we travel to those places these friend would offer us a pace to stay and keep us comfortable. I too lent money to people and never ask them to return it. Instead it kept a mortgage. As my creditors wanted to get out of the mortgage quickly, they would return the money as soon as they could. I slept comfortably each night because I would be tired after a hard day's work, and it did not matter if I were sleeping on the bed or on the floor. I ate only when I was hungry, and at that time the simplest meal tastes like nectar." Seeing his brother thoughtful face Virendar continued, " Keshav you should have searched for the true meaning behind father word's. Now tell me. If you say that a person is good-natured ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ and is like a child, do you mean that the person has become a child? No! Not at all! you mean that the person is good-natured and innocent. Isn't it?" Now Keshav realised how foolish he had been" OH! What a fool I have been and I have just squandered my share of wealth that father had given me. I wish I had tried to reason it out, "Keshav thought. " Never mind it's never too late, you can start afresh now and I am sure, that now since you have understood father's word's, you will be successful this time. I will help you to restart your business again, " Virendar assured his brother. Virendar gladly lent Keshav some money to stat off his life again. And this time Keshav judiciously used the money as his brother had done following the true meaning of his father's words. So with hard work And intelligence, Keshav Slowly became rich and successful. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿RUDRAAKSH BEHL ﻿ ﻿DELHI PUBLIC SCHOOL ﻿ ﻿ ﻿

title: Republic Day
text: When did India become a Republic? Republic Day in India is celebrated on January 26 to commemorate the day on which the Constitution of India came into effect. The Indian Constitution was put into effect in the year 1950 in place of the Government of India Act. Even though India obtained independence from British rule in 1947, it took a special Drafting Committee headed by Babasaheb Ambedkar, 166 sessions over the next 3 years to finalise the document and put it into effect. The newly established Indian nation chose to adopt the constitution on January 26 because it is a symbol for the Indian Freedom Struggle. In 1930, well before Indian independence the Indian National Congress led by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru declared Purna Swaraj or complete independence. He did this by hoisting the Indian flag on the banks of the Ravi river (now in Pakistan). Why did they choose 26th January? The date of 26th January was important to the Indian struggle for independence. In 1930, the Indian National Congress had declared ‘Purna Swaraj’ or complete independence on this day, by hoisting the Indian flag on the banks of the Ravi river. Republic Day Celebrations in India In Delhi, the seat of the Indian government, there is a grand parade to mark the importance of Republic Day. Before the parade begins the Prime Minister places a wreath at a memorial called Amar Jawan Jyoti, dedicated to the unknown soldiers that died fighting for India’s freedom. This act is followed by 2 minutes of silence in honour of these unnamed soldiers. T he Prime Minister then takes his place in the president’s box along with other Indian officials and foreign dignitaries to witness the parade. The ceremonies begin with a 21 gun salute once the flag is hoisted accompanied by the Indian National Anthem. The Indian National Anthem The Indian National Anthem was written in a highly Sanskritized form of Bengali called Tatsama. It is taken from the Brahmo hymn composed by Guru Rabindranath Tagore and was first sung as in a session by the Indian National Congress in Calcutta in 1911. Jana Gana Mana was only officially adopted as the national anthem years later in 1950. After the national anthem is played the President gives awards for bravery and varied acts of valour to men and women in the armed forces. This is finally followed by a parade of regiments from the armed forces and floats representing the various cultures of India. The parade ends with a fly-past by Indian Air Force jets. Ceremonies are also held in all the state capitals and flag-hoisting ceremonies are organised by all schools that are compulsory for all children to attend. Beating of the retreat The words beating and retreat in the same sentence sounds very un-republic day-like but actually has nothing to do with beating or retreating. The beating of the retreat which takes place on the 29th of January at Raisina Hill and the adjacent Vijay Chork in New Delhi marks the end of the Republic day celebrations. The chief guest to the event is always the President of India who arrives with a cavalry unit. The ceremony and fanfare involves dispalys by the bands of the Army, Navy, and Air Force. There is also a drummer’s solo, followed by a solemn ceremony where the Indian national flag is taken down to the hymn Abide With Me. The procession ends with a bugle call to retreat where all other flags are taken down and the bands march out to the tune of Sare Jahan Se Achcha.

title: Importance of time
text: Do you know the importance of time? Time is one of the most important aspects of life. You should know why time was made. Time was made to help us (Humans) have a more organized and scheduled life. When the sun rises morning starts, when the sun sets night starts. Most of us don't know the value of time until we experience having less of it. Time is one thing that cannot be brought back. Every second that is passing by will never come again. This date will not come again. When you realize that the time you have spent doing something you like to do goes by faster than the time you spent doing something you don't like to do even if the actual amount of time you spent is the same. Everyone should know how to manage time. You don't know when you'll lose someone or something; making sure that you spend the correct amount of time doing everything is a great life skill. Spending more time doing something less important instead of something even slightly more important or fruitful is a waste of precious time. Let's take this situation; you love your parents but you don't spend time with them that much. Now unfortunately they pass away and you regret not spending time with them. You won't have memories with them. This is a very simple and common example of not using time properly. If you spent that extra time doing some work instead of games then you might get 1 or 2% extra marks in your exam but every percent counts! That 1% after the 99% makes 100%, if that 1% wasn't there then hundred isn't there. So every single effort makes a difference. Change your mindset from "Oh I have to do work" to "oh I need to work", it doesn't matter if you like it or not, you need to do your work on TIME. Make sure you use your time WISELY. Time doesn't wait for ANYONE. Every second goes away and you don't realize it! Every second, every effort and every minute spent using your time wisely and productively counts! Hope this book made you think more about time.

title: Swami Vivekananda
text: Swami Vivekananda 12 January 1863 – 4 July 1902), born Narendranath Datta, was an Indian Hindu monk and philosopher. He was a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna. [4] [5] Influenced by Western esotericism, [6] [7] [8] he was a key figure in the introduction of the Indian darsanas (teachings, practices) of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world, [9] [10] [11] and is credited with raising interfaith awareness, bringing Hinduism to the status of a major world religion during the late 19th century. [12] He was a major force in the contemporary Hindu reform movements in India, and contributed to the concept of nationalism in colonial India. [13] Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Math and the Ramakrishna Mission. [10] He is perhaps best known for his speech which began with the words "Sisters and brothers of America...," [14] in which he introduced Hinduism at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893. Born into an aristocratic Bengali Kayastha family of Calcutta, Vivekananda was inclined towards spirituality. He was influenced by his guru, Ramakrishna, from whom he learnt that all living beings were an embodiment of the divine self; therefore, service to God could be rendered by service to humankind. After Ramakrishna's death, Vivekananda toured the Indian subcontinent extensively and acquired first-hand knowledge of the conditions prevailing in British India. He later travelled to the United States, representing India at the 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions. Vivekananda conducted hundreds of public and private lectures and classes, disseminating tenets of Hindu philosophy in the United States, England and Europe. In India, Vivekananda is regarded as a patriotic saint, and his birthday is celebrated as National Youth Day. [15] [16]

title: The Best Nest
text: Blue Bird is bored. “I am tired of this nest,” he says. “We need a new home.” “If you insist,” says Brown Bird. “But I am not moving unless the new nest is better than the one that we have now.” “Oh yes,” says Blue Bird. “It will be a great nest. I will find the best nest ever!” “Look at this lovely nest! It is soft and cosy. And we can each have our own bed. This is the best nest for us.” But it isn’t! “Look at this beautiful nest. It is so bright and colourful. This is the very best nest.” But it isn’t! “Look at this shiny nest. See how it sparkles. This is the best nest yet.” But it isn’t! “Look at this large nest! It even has its own door. This is the best nest of all.” But it isn’t! “Look at this nest. See how well it has been built. This is the best nest ever.” “Yes, it is,” says Brown Bird.

title: Brave Bora
text: Bora is sitting at the clinic with Baba. Jojo, his stuffed monkey, came too. Jojo is sleeping in Bora’s bag. “I don’t like needles. They hurt!” says Bora. “An injection helps make you healthy. It’s okay to be scared, Bora. Baba will be right here with you. And Jojo too.” “Bora Baraka!” a loud voice calls. “Let’s go Bora,” says Baba. “It’s your turn.” “Let’s come back tomorrow Baba!” says Bora. “Remember what Baba said you will get for being brave enough to get your injection?” asks Baba. “A red lollipop! Okay, I’m coming,” says Bora. The doctor smiles at Bora. “Is this your monkey? Can we examine him too?” she asks. Bora looks at Baba, then at Jojo, and nods. “Now, it’s your turn,” she says. Will you help me give your monkey a small injection so he feels better?” asks the doctor. “TOOP!” says the doctor as she gives Jojo the monkey an injection. “Now, it’s your turn. Is that a superhero on your T-shirt?” she asks. “TOOP!” She says as she gives Bora the injection. “Ouch!” shouts Bora. “Hey, that wasn’t so bad!” “I know it stings a little, but we’re done and you have been very brave!” says the doctor. “One red lollipop for our brave Bora!”

title: Tale Of Two Friends
text: In a city,there lived two friends named Dharmabuddi and Pappabudhi. Cunning Papabuddhi planned to deprive Dharmabuddhi,"Dear friend, I strongly feel it is not safe to keep all our wealth at home. We should bury our money,we can go there and get it." Dharmabuddhi agreed,and they dug a pit deep inside a nearby forest and buried their earnings in it. One night,Papabudhiwent to pit and stole all the money. Next morning,he went to Dharmabuddhi and asked him to accompany him to the forest because he needed money. When both of them arrived at the pit and found it empty,Papabuddhi began shouting loudly,"Dharmabuddhi you stole my money. You must give me half of what was buried here." Though Dharmabuddhi denied it vehemently,Papabuddhi persisted in his accusations.The case was brought in court.There,Papabuddhi said to the judge,"I can produce the gods of the forest as witness. They will determine who is guilty." The judges agreed and asked both parties to be present the next morning at the forest. Papabuddhi went home and told his father,"Father, I have stolen all the money of Dharmabuddhi's money.There is a court case going on,and I can win it only with your help.Go now and hide in a hollow of the big tree in the forest. Tomorrow morning,when the judges and others assemble there,I will ask you for the truth. Then you say that Dharmabuddhi is the theif." The father hesitated to lend support to the wicked plan,but finally he agreed as he loved his son.The next day, while Dharmabuddhi and the judges watched,Papabuddhi went near the tree and shouted,"O gods of the forest,you all are my witness.Declare who among us is guilty." ﻿The father shouted back from inside the hollow of the tree,"It is Dharmabuddhi who stole the money."Dharmabuddhi felt ﻿ ﻿suspicious.He filled the tree hollow with hay,poured oil on it and threw a matchstick in.The fire forced the father to come out of the tree. ﻿"All this is the work of Pappabuddhi's evil mind," said the father to the judges.The king's men arrested Papabuddhi.
author: neha sardana

title: Sindhutai Sapkal
text: Sapkal was born on 14 November 1948, [1] in Pimpri Meghe village in Wardha district in the then Central Provinces and Berar of British India to Abhimanyu Sathe, a cowherder. [2] [3] Being an unwanted child, she was referred to as Chindhi (Marathi for "torn piece of cloth"). Abject poverty, family responsibilities and an early marriage forced her to quit formal education after she successfully passed the fourth standard. [4] Sapkal was married off at age 12 to Shrihari Sapkal, who was 20 years elder to her, and moved to Nawargaon village, Seloo in Wardha. [5] The marriage did not last long and at the age of 20, [5] she was left on her own to care for a girl child. [6] [3] [7] Sindhutai Sapkal later found herself in Chikhaldara, where she started begging on railway platforms for food. In the process, she realised that there were many children abandoned by their parents and she adopted them as her own. She then begged more vigorously to feed them. She decided to become a mother to everyone who came across to her as an orphan. She later donated her biological child to the trust Shrimant Dagdu Sheth Halwai, Pune, to eliminate the feeling of partiality between her biological child and the adopted children. [8] [9] In this constant tussle to survive, she found herself in Chikaldara, situated in the Amravati district of Maharashtra. Here, due to a tiger preservation project, 84 tribal villages were evacuated. Amidst the confusion, a project officer impounded 132 cows of Adivasi villagers and one of the cows died. Sapkal decided to fight for proper rehabilitation of the helpless tribal villagers. Her efforts were acknowledged by the Minister of Forests and he made appropriate arrangements for alternative relocation. [10] Sapkal fought for the rehabilitation of eighty-four villages. [10] In the course of her agitation, she met Chhedilal Gupta, the then Minister of Forests. He agreed that the villagers should not be displaced before the government had made appropriate arrangements at alternative sites. When Prime Minister Indira Gandhi arrived to inaugurate the tiger project, Sapkal showed her photographs of an Adivasi who had lost his eyes to a wild bear. [11] She is quoted as saying, "I told her that the forest department paid compensation if a cow or a hen was killed by a wild animal, so why not a human being? She immediately ordered compensation." [11] After being informed of the plight of orphaned and abandoned Adivasi children Sapkal took care of the children in return for meager amounts of food. Shortly thereafter, it become the mission of her life. [10] Sapkal devoted herself to orphans. As a result, she was fondly called "Mai", which means "mother". She nurtured over 1,500 orphaned children and through them had a grand family of 382 sons-in-law and 49 daughters-in-law. She has been honoured with more than 700 awards for her work. She used award money to buy land to make a home for orphaned children. [12] [13] She died of a heart attack in Pune, Maharashtra, on 4 January 2022, at the age of 73. [19]

title: The Mischievous Golu
text: Once, there was a small puppy who lived with his mother in a farm. His name was Golu. He was very mischievous and his mother, Miss.Ginger always told him to stay out of danger. But, Golu always ignored her words. One day, Golu asked his mother if he can go out and play. But, his mother replied " No my darling, it is already getting dark. If you go out now, you will get lost." Golu was upset. Then, his mother went inside the home to prepare dinner. Golu thought it is a good chance to sneak out of the house. He ran out of his house as fast as he could and came near the river. There, he saw his friend, a baby snake, called Strawberry. Golu saw her and called out " Hey Strawberry! Shall we play something together?" Strawberry replied " Oh! It's already dinner time in my home, Golu. Sorry, I can't play now. We will play tomorrow. Bye! " Golu too said bye to her. As he was roaming around, he slipped and fell inside the river. Luckily, Miss. Parry the Parrot saw this and flew as fast as possible to his mother and told Golu's mother everything. Golu's mother exclaimed " Oh! Golu sneaked out?! Why won't he listen to me? Come let's go save him Miss Parry!" They went there as fast as possible and saved him. Golu said sobbingly," Oh mother! I should have listened to you! I am so sorry. I will always listen to you! Please forgive me!" Golu's mother hugged him and said " I hope you have learnt your lesson, my dear." Golu sobbingly nodded yes. Then, they all went back home and they both thanked Miss. Parry. The End. The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents. Their words are like gold but a lot more expensive. The children who listen to their parents are always successful. Golu didn't listen to his mother and fell into trouble. Always listen to your parents.

title: Look Up!
text: Wow, look up! What do you see? In the morning.. Small sparrows and big hadedas. In the daytime... A flutter of butterflies over flowers. A sugarbird with its long tail. A sunbird with its bright red collar. A yellow-billed kite soaring high in the sky. In the late afternoon... Bees buzzing to their hive. Geese flying home. As the sun sets... The twinkling lights of an aeroplane full of people. Bats eating insects for their dinner. When it’s nice and dark... An owl swooping over a field. A shooting star. Even when we’re dreaming there is so much to see!

title: Mama, What's for Lunch?
text: “Hurry,Thabo. Mama is making lunch,” calls Tumi. “Where are you going, Thabo?” His friends don’t understand why he chooses lunch over their game, but Thabo has a secret. Mama’s lunches are special. On Monday, Mama shapes their food like little bugs that wriggle and crawl, making Tumi shriek in fright. “EEEE!” But they are yummy fruit and vegetables, and not very scary at all. On Tuesday, she makes a lion that roars so loudly the house shakes. “ROAR!” But it’s just delicious pasta and cheese. On Wednesday, Mama creates a chicken that wakes up the whole street. “CLUCK CLUCK PAKAA!” But it’s just a plate of juicy fruit. On Thursday, she builds a noisy truck. Thabo and Tumi cover their ears. “VROOOM!” But it’s a sweet strawberry jam sandwich. On Friday, Mama makes a beautiful garden filled with flowers, birds and ladybugs. “TWEET TWEET!” But it’s healthy pap, beans and a crunchy salad. “Mama, what’s for lunch?” asks Tumi. “Yes, Mama,” says Thabo. “What are you making today?” Thabo and Tumi can’t wait another second. Their tummies are grumbling. Finally, Mama is ready. “What is it Mama?” asks Thabo, licking his lips. It’s Thabo, Tumi and Mama! “Mmm, our favourite, your famous stew and rice.” “Thank you, Mama!” What will Mama make on Sunday?
author: Sally  Partridge

If a lady frog hops past you'd think he would get up at last to bow, and help her on her way? But no, I am ashamed to say that when a lady frog comes by he does not open up one eye!

title: respect elders
text: Animator: Swathi Sambasivam Illustrators: David Yambem, Genevieve Terblanche, Google India, Joseph Murmu, Rajeev Verma 'Banjara', Someone Maybe One day, Amir was alone in the house. His father and mother had gone to shopping. A visitor came to his house, his name was Vinoth. Amir greeted him with a smiling face and offered him a seat and a glass of water. The visitor gave him a pack of biscuits. Amir thanked him. The visitor waited for some time and went away. When his father came home, Amir told him about Mr. Vinoth. His father said, Oh! He is my manager. The next day Amir’s father met Mr. Vinoth in the office. Mr. Vinoth said to him, “what a nice son you have. He is so polite and respectful towards elders”. Amir’s father felt very proud. Moral: you should show respect to the elders like Amir they are older than you by many years.

text: Once upon a time there lived a hyena and a tortoise. The hyena was a very greedy and selfish, but the tortoise was very wise and kind. The hyena said "Tortoise I want to eat honey from this beehive and I want to eat it all alone, so please don't eat my honey". Then the tortoise said "Ok, I will not at your honey, but if you take honey from the beehive then the honeybees will bite you". Then the hyena said "I don't care". The tortoise warned him many times, but the hyena refused and shouted at him. Then the hyena ate all the honey which was there in the beehive. Then the honeybees attacked the hyena. The hyena jumped in water and after that the honeybees decided to leave him. Then after the honeybees went, the hyena got spots on his body, because of the honeybees. Then the hyena saw a village, he went in the village and saw that his friend tortoise was living in that village. The hyena told the tortoise everything and asked for shelter. The tortoise allowed him in his house and the hyena apologized for his greed and selfishness. Then the hyena and the tortoise live happily ever after....

title: The doctor of Andolasia
text: Once in a kingdom called Andolasia, there lived a princess named Andla. She was a beautiful princess, and she was also so, very brave. She was very good at cooking but her dream was to become a doctor so she could help save people’s lives. She was always sad though because her parents thought becoming a doctor would ruin a king’s and queen’s reputation as a high-level, gorgeous princess becoming a doctor would sound cheap to everyone in the kingdom and abroad. One day, Andla finally decided to stand up for herself and talk to her parents about sending her to medical school. “Mom and Dad, I have finally made a decision to stand up for myself and go to medical school.” Andla said boldly to her parents, The king and queen both exchanged a glance of surprise “Honey, we already told you like a million times, you can not become a doctor it sounds cheap” said the queen kindly. “Your mother is right darling, becoming a doctor would ruin all of our reputations” said the king nodding, the princess was offended and stormed out of the room in a flash. The king and queen were upset but they still did not change their decision about it. Then, Andla went to her best friend to ask for some advice, her name was Charlette. She lived across the kingdom, so she told her driver to take her there, after 1 whole hour they reached Charlette’s house. Andla went inside and asked her if she could help her by giving some advice on how to become a good doctor, by knowing this Andla could show her parents that she would be an amazing doctor. “So Charlette, please tell me, how do I become a very good doctor?” Charlette studied In medical college for about 5 years, so she was sure to know the answer to this question. “But Andla, didn’t your parents tell you that you could not be a doctor,” said Charlette confused. The princess smacked her lips and said in a low voice “Oh come on! I really want to be a doctor, I don’t care about what mom and dad say, I can’t live my life going after someone else’s dream, right?” Charlette smiled at Andla and hugged her, she then nodded her head and agreed to teach her how to become a doctor. From then on, she went to Charlette’s house every day to learn the basic steps of how to care of a patient with a type of cancer, she studied this for 2 years, and then she moved on to the professional level of doctoring. One day, when she was about to leave for Charlette’s house, her father stopped her and asked her, “Honey, you have been going out of this house daily for 2 years, do you mind if ask you where you are going and why?” Andla looked at him smiling in fear. “Oh…Uhhh, That ummm……… I am going to-to wa- water the plants out in the garden, you know how much I love flowers and grass r-right?” The king looked at her confused for 2 seconds, and then smiled and let her go, By the time he left the room, Andla was sweating like a pig. She then left the room as fast as she could and asked the driver to hurry. When they reached there, Andla rang the bell like four times, but nobody answered, she then heard a faint sound telling her that the door was open. She entered and was shocked by what she was seeing, her best friend Charlette, was sick on her bed! “WHAT HAPPENED TO YOU Charlette!!!! Are you hurt, are you sick, I hope you are fine!?” said Andla screaming in shock. Then Charlette explained in a very low voice “I was walking out in the park and forgot to take my medicines, that caused me to faint and now I am not feeling so well” Andla immediately sat beside her and gave her some water, she felt really sad for her so when she reached the palace, she went and told her parents if some medical supply from the best hospitals would be given to be able to take care of Charlette. Her parents agreed and until Charlette got better, she was provided help from the kingdom and the best hospital there too. Thanks to Andla, Charlette was saved, and she was able to continue her tutoring classes for Andla. The best friends worked together so hard that made Andla a super doctor, she even got a job at the best hospital there, Empathy hospital. One day, she was leaving for her shift, she suddenly heard a scream coming from her mother’s room. She went there and saw her father lying on his death bed. “Honey, since the last month I am not feeling so well, The doctors’ at the hospital said that I might have lung cancer, the reports will come tomorrow, and I need you to stay here and take care of me while your mother takes my place as king and queen forever because I don’t think I will survive” said the king in a low voice. Andla knelt before him and started crying when suddenly she realized that SHE WAS A DOCTOR! She could help him to survive. She immdietly took him to Empathy hospital and started the treatment, in general it would cost a lot but since her father wasn’t feeling well, she allowed it to be taken for free. She did everything possible to save her father, and finally he was doing fine. She made him take his medications regularly and helped him get better, whenever the queen was busy ruling, Andla was also busy saving an important person’s life. After so many months, The king finally got better, “Oh Honey, We are so sorry for not believing in you, we did not realise how important a doctor's job is until one saved our lives from the dead line. Your mother and I truly apologize and promise to build up your courage instead of crushing it down in the future.” Said the king. Andla looked at both her parents and smiled, she appreciated them and hugged them both with a lot of love and a big smile on her face. They all loved each other and from then on, her parents kept on pushing her to become a wonderful doctor, and soon she became one of the most famous doctors in the whole kingdom, she was so popular that kids would call her, Empathy Andla. The whole family and kingdom lived happily ever after THE END!
author: Abigail Varghese

title: Best Friend
text: Long ago,in a village lived two friends Rose and Lily.Rose was from wealthy family where Lily was from poor family. Despite their status difference they used to stay with each other all the time and were best friend. As time went by both grew up and got busy with there life. With busy life they didn't get much time to meet each other. One day, Lily got very ill and she was given bed rest. When Rose came to know about it. She went to Lily's house to meet her. She didn't stayed there for long and talked much but instead she just took some money out of her pocket and gave it to Lily and left. Lily felt bad but didn't say anything to her. With time Lily got well and worked hard to earn money so that she could return Rose's money. Once Lily earned enough money. She went to Rose to return her money. Still Lily couldn't forgot how rude was rose's behavior towards her. Just after sometime, Rose got ill and doctor suggested her bed rest. As soon as Lily got news of Rose illness,she left all her work and went to meet Rose and stayed by her side until Rose got all well. After this,one day Rose went to meet Lily and said, 'my friend, i feel very guilty. When you fell ill, I gave you money and you returned it. But when i got ill, you stayed by my side whole time and took care of me,How am i ever going to be able to return this favour of yours...? Lily hugged her and replied,"I just wanted to realize that money is not everything and today I am very happy that you understand that....? Moral: Money is not everything.Friendship is all about Care and Affection.

title: The Squirrel and the Mouse
text: One day a great storm was going on. A squirrel was hiding in its home on a tree. Then suddenly a lightning bolt struck the tree. Out of fear the squirrel immediately got out of there. The squirrel started looking for shelter. The squirrel remembered that Mr. Mouse’s house was nearby. So she ran as fast as she could until finally she reached Mr. Mouse’s house. She asked Mr. Mouse if he could let her stay in his house until the storm was over. He agreed and allowed her to stay in his house until the storm ends. As promised, after the storm was over she thanked Mr. Mouse for providing her shelter during storm. Mr. Mouse like a good friend promised to help her in any way she needs any time. The squirrel started looking for a place where she should make her house until she found a place to make it. Coping Mr. Mouse’s house, she thought to make it underground to avoid lightening fear during storm. But it is not feasible for a squirrel to live underground forever. So she got the idea to make a deep house like Mr. Mouse’s in a big fat tree trunk. She called her friend Mr. mouse and they together made her house. After a few days since she made her house she gave birth to few babies. One day when she was searching for food, she found a few squirrels that were homeless so she asked if they would like to live in her house and they agreed so they went to her house and lived happily ever after like a family.

Then the giraffes came o the other side o the watering hole to drink water. Then the group of deer's and warthogs came to the other side of the watering hole to drink water. title: The Foolish Donkey
text: A salt seller used to carry the salt bag on his donkey to the market every day. On the way they had to cross a stream. One day the donkey suddenly tumbled down the stream and the salt bag also fell into the water. The salt dissolved in the water and hence the bag became very light to carry. The donkey was happy. Then the donkey started to play the same trick every day. The salt seller came to understand the trick and decided to teach a lesson to it. The next day he loaded a cotton bag on the donkey. Again it played the same trick hoping that the cotton bag would be still become lighter But the dampened cotton became very heavy to carry and the donkey suffered. It learnt a lesson. It didn’t play the trick anymore after that day, and the seller was happy. Moral of the story: Luck won’t favor always. Moral of the story: Luck won’t favor always.

title: Tia and The Dog!
text: This cute baby here is Tia, eight years before. She had a rare condition. She cries when she is happy and laughs when she is sad. Her parents were worried about her. But they hoped that one day their kutty would be all fine. Tia woke up and went to the kitchen, but found no one. She went on into the living room and was surprised by her parents. "Happy Birthday Kutty!". Tia cried as she was really happy. "Where is my gift, appa?" asked Tia. "You will get it very soon, kutty" said appa. Tia wore a red sequined dress to school. Her friends wished her and gave her gifts. Tia was always the teacher's favorite and was also the topper. So a group of people always teased the teacher and tried to blame Tia. It has never worked. But everyday is a new day! The students teased the teacher and blamed Tia, she was really upset, which made her laugh. This made the teacher angry and he shouted "Get out, Tia! Now!" She made her way out sadly. After a few minutes her friends too came out. She was curious to know why they came out. Tia asked "Why did you come out, guys?". Rita replied "You came, so we did too". "But how?" Tia was confused now. Nick replied "How did you come out?" "He sent me out because I laughed" said Tia sadly. "We toooo!" giggled Sanjeev. While she was entering her house, she came across a small house, but didn't pay much attention to it and entered the house. As she entered, she heard some dog noises from the living room, but wasn't sure if it was a dog. She was interrupted by her beaming parents. She went inside eagerly. “Surprise!! Here is your gift, kutty" said amma. Tia opened it and something fluffly jumped on her. “Aaaahhhhhh” she shouted with fear. Then after realizing it was a puppy “Is this for me? Can I keep it? For real?” She asked with excitement and anxiety. “Yes, you can, kutty” said appa. Tia named the puppy "Tod". After a long, tiring and happy day... Tia went to sleep. She got into her bed. Suddenly, Tod jumped in with her and snuggled inside her blanket. Tia drifted into sleep happily...

title: My Adventurous Birthday Surprise
text: Hi! I am Nicholas. Today I'm going to say my best b'day surprise! I am excited!!! Let's go! My Family: Dad, Ma, Niya, Me. My sister is the best in our family! Today morning, daddy was back from his 1 month project in Africa. He had 2 suitcases now, but before he went to Africa there was only 1. Goodness knows what is inside the second suitcase "Morning!" I went downstairs, heading for kitchen. Ma gave breakfast. It was my favorite porridge. Yum yum! I said, licking my mouth. Just then, Daddy knocked on the door. I opened it for him and gave a big hug 2 hours before class. Good. I looked at my calendar, I was abashed! Wasn't it my birthday today? No one wished me! Never Mind, I thought and went away. Just then, I remembered my swimming classes' test. It was better to do somethin' else than in underwater world. I gotta skip that! I always wanted to become a person who always gets the 1st medal, but all of them was an imagination! I must go out of Ma's room now, Niya is ill-ish in the bed. Stuck In Bed. Suddenly, Ma opened the door. My heart started beating like a Jumbo-Jet. But Ma said "Don't worry baby, come here, do not disturb Niya, okay?" I nodded. I was relieved. Phew! I went to the sofa. Just then, something bright opened up. I had to cover my eyes. Few seconds later, I saw a big treasure box. Nervously, I opened it up. A crown went to my head by itself. Oi... I was quite surprised. When I went outside, I saw not only my house, but also the biggest cake I have ever saw! I bet it was like a 1M kg! (although it is not true) I better go to class now. I bet my paraglider is still there for practice. Oh! It was the best adventurous birthday I ever had! Thank you everyone!

title: Bhima The Donkey
text: Bhima Ramu is the washerman's donkey. His problem is that he can't sleep. That's why he has to listen to the scoldin g ﻿ One day Gauri, the neighbor's cow, asked, "Bhima, why are you sad?" Bhima said, "I can't sleep. Will you wake me up?" "Ok." Gauri said. On the second day, Gauri cried "Mother...Mother..." but Bhima did not wake up. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ Returned from Bhima Ghat in the evening. Moti dog came there. "Moti, I can't sleep. Will you wake me up?" "Yes... yes..." said Moti. The next day, Moti kept barking “Bow… eyebrow…” but Bhima could not sleep. That evening, Bhima met Chinu the chicken. "Chinu, your voice wakes everyone up every morning. Will you wake me up too?" "Okay," said Chinu. The next morning, by saying "Kukdu-ku, kukdu-ku", Chinu kept on banging loudly. But there was no effect on Bhima. In the evening, Bhima saw Kalu the crow moving around. "Brother crow, will you wake me up in the morning?" "Yeah... yes... of course." Kalu spoke. The next day Kalu kept on saying "Kaav... Kaan" but Bhima did not wake up. Now Bhima was disappointed. The next morning a fly sat in his nose. "Come on.. As soon as this happened, Bhima woke up. "Hey, how did I wake up!" "I woke up." Said the fly sitting on his head. "Truth! Will you wake me up everyday?" "Ok." Now Bhima was happy. This trick worked!

title: Love Your Family
text: Once there lived a boy named Arjun. He never obeyed his family members. Whenever anybody told him to do any work he would say, why should I can’t you do? He always thought that friends are more reliable and never cheat him. One day without informing his family members he moved with his friends for a picnic in a jungle. While they were finding good place for the picnic suddenly a snake came and bit Arjun and at the same time there came a big bear. All of them ran away leaving Arjun because he could not walk properly. While finding their child Arjun's parents saw Arjun in front of the bear alone. Arjun's father told him to lie down and hold his breathe. After the bear was gone Arjun’s parents took him to a doctor. When Arjun was save the doctor came and said that if you would have not come on time, the child would have succumbed to death. title: The Stork and the Spaghetti
text: One day a stork went for a walk. She saw a fox eating noodles from a plate. The fox was enjoying the meal and the stork became curious. “Must be very tasty and delicious,” she said to herself. “Help yourself” said the generous fox and he pushed a plate of noodles to the stork. The Stork put her long beak and tried to catch the noodles. But it all slipped and fell into the plate again. She could not taste even a small piece of the noodle. “Is it to your taste?” asked the Fox. “Well, I am afraid not so,” said the Stork. “Maybe you did not cook it in the right way” she added. The fox laughed at her and said “Maybe you do not know how to enjoy it” The Stork walked away sadly. The Fox was also sad that the Stork did not like his food. MORAL: YOU NEED TIME AND PATIENCE TO UNDERSTAND OTHER PEOPLE’S TASTE AND CULTURE. BE KIND AND APPRECIATE OTHERS. THE END

title: The Surprise Party

title: The King's Feast
text: Hello! I am ﻿Mr. King. It is a pleasure to meet you! I am quite sick, and my servant is running over here. So I recently celebrated a feast with my nation. Let me share you the story before this servant comes. Let's goooo! Yesterday night, when I was walking in my palace garden, I thought of my people. One girl had asked me to prepare a feast. I agreed. I decided to do that. As soon as I got home, I asked the musicians to play me a melody. ﻿Strange.... Why are my musicians' mood so sad-angry today? Oh... I raised my hand. Because I know why. Hee hee... The one who is playing the flute is my servant now. Cropped his hair. The next day, which was today, I asked the girl who wanted to hold a feast, "Little girl, everything is ready, by what time should I call my people?" She said "Oh, your Majesty, please, hold the time when you want" She bowed down and slowly went out of the palace gates, saying to herself "I will tell all people that it will be tonight" and informed it to everybody about the feast When I heard that the feast was tonight, I asked my chefs to prepare the most expensive luxurious foods. Almost 3 hours. When I came in, I saw a good scent of my chicken soup. "Ah-ha, time for deliciousness," I said to myself. So many people read the letter and was happy to join the feast. Some of them wrote back, while other made scribbles to the letter. At 7:00 PM, the palace bell rang, and the whole multitude of people ran into the palace hall. I smiled. Their first snack was Ice-Cream Next..... THE GREAT FEAST! Oh..... I think I am sleepy. ﻿10 Minutes later..... ﻿Messenger: Letter | Me: Sleeping Servants: Tea | Me: Snoring I think my best feast is finished. Don't mind my servants. Bye!

title: The two kings
text: Once upon a time there were two kings, Jim and Ben. Jim cannot read or write, because he never went to school and he did not care about education. However, Ben was really smart, well educated, hardworking and cares for everyone in his kingdom. It was peak summer and there was a famine in both of Jim’s and Ben’s kingdoms. Jim had an idea. He said to himself, “I will climb up a tree and sprinkle water on the land and it will help a lot of plants to grow.” Ben also had a similar idea. It was to pour gallons and gallons of water from the royal well. This idea worked and after a lot of days the plants started growing. After a few years, there was a war between Jim’s and Ben’s kingdoms. Jim’s troops were close to Ben’s kingdom and Jim noticed Ben’s land was filled with green fields everywhere. He asked his minister, “How is this land so fertile while our lands are dry?” The minister replied, “Your majesty, King Ben used all his knowledge that he learnt in his school during the famine. May be that’s why.” The war was interrupted by continuous heavy rains and both the kings dropped the idea of war temporarily. One day, Jim remembered what his minister said and asked him, “Can I also learn from Ben’s teacher now, at this age?” The minister said, “Why not? I’ll immediately make arrangements if your majesty wishes so.” King Jim started taking his lessons seriously. After years of education, Jim became smart and Jim’s and Ben’s kingdoms were united and they both were the rulers of the united land. Jim and Ben were the smartest kings in the whole world for a long time. Moral: Education leads the path to be wise and great.
author: Anirudh R

title: The letter
text: The Letter: I will come back I was sitting in the verandah and sipping and sipping a hot cup of tea. The night was moonless and there I was counting the indefinite stars.But then I saw something go past by. For a second I stopped and looked everywhere there was no one around perhaps it must have been the tree. Then I felt a hand on my shoulder. I knew this touch it felt like my brother's.He was a jolly and active young man. But he died in a car accident. Again I looked around no one was there. I was not comfortable there so I went inside. My son came running to me saying "Papa please play with me please ".I couldn't say no to him so I agreed. He was over the blue moon. We played board games and hide seek. Then Ramesh(My son) said baba I will go to the kitchen and drink a glass of water. Minutes past minutes he did not come back Now I was worried I went to the kitchen he was not there. I asked Ramlal(caretaker of the house)"Ramlal did you see Ramesh come here and his replied shocked me to bits and his reply was " No sir, Ramesh is sleeping what happened sir " I was frustrated so I told everything to Ramlal. And he said that the spirit of my brother is still in this house. Nonsense! Spirits do not exist saying that I brushed him aside. I went to the attic then and took out a box it had the pictures of my brother tears rolled down my cheeks for a while I just stared at the pictures I was in the land of thoughts. But Mohan broke the silence he shouted "Sir dinner is ready ". I quickly ate my dinner and went to the bed. In the midnight a shadow went crept inside my room. I shouted Ramlal, Mohan but there was no sign of them the shadow quietly walked towards the table and kept a note. On it was written "Our brother I will come back. The next day I quickly packed my bags and went away to my native home Gujrat and I never saw him again. THE END
author: Bandana Bandana

title: Changers around Me!
text: Maya's science teacher, Miss Veronica, took them to the Chemistry Lab today. There were tinny-tiny bottles with tinny-tiny amounts of liquids both, colored and colorless too. Miss Veronica mixed a greenish-blue liquid and a black,so-called 'solution' and it turned into bright lemon yellow! She told the class "This is change. It is chemical and irreversible in nature." Maya's friend, Arya asked "Ma'am what are chemical change and irreversible change? " Minu asked "if I bake a loaf of bread is that also a change? Soon everybody had a question! Miss Veronica explained "Things are changing all the time. So we classify them into four broad types- reversable and irreversible and physical and chemical. Now if any thing changes it is a change." As the bell rang, Maya and her classmates ran outside. It was home time. Suddenly Maya could see a thousand changes around her. From the eating of an apple to thinking about Zeus! Changes are here, Changes are there, Changes are Everywhere

title: Mother is world
text: ﻿ " We are born of love; Love is our mother." "Mother is the name for God in the lips and hearts of little children." "When you look into your mother's eyes, you know that is the purest love you can find on this earth." "A mother is she who can take the place of all others but whose place no one else can take." Why do I love my mom because My mother takes care of everyone in the house. Every day my mother prepares tasty meals for my father and me. My mother scolds me often but later calmly corrects my mistakes. My mother is also very hardworking because she keeps the house in order and has to work in her office too. Mother is a symbol of love and care.... She is most beautiful, strong, loving, caring and wonderful person. I always wonder how she manages everything perfectly, and is surprised because of her kind nature Mom, you are the best! I am so lucky to have you as my mom.... Thank you for all of the invaluable lessons you've taught me.... I know I didn't always make it easy on you.... You are amazing and appreciated.... Mom, you are irreplaceable.... Thank you for everything you've done for me.

title: I hate online classes!
text: Zaheen woke up early today! Why, you ask? She has to attend her online classes. 'I don't like online classes.' she told her mom. 'I want to go to school!' Zaheen groaned. Her mother just told her to go and attend because she was already late. She logged into her meeting. 'Good morning ma'am' she said gloomily. 'Hi Zaheen! Hope you are doing well.' said teacher. Zaheen nodded and continued with her classes. It was so boring. Math, English and then science. 'When will I talk to my friends by physically meeting them?' she thought. After class, Zaheen went to eat lunch. She said to her mother, 'I want to go to school! I can eat my food while sharing it with my friends there. Instead, I have to eat it alone.' Mother was already tired of Zaheen's continuous complaints. 'Anyways, if you go to school, you will not be able to share your food with your friends.' Mother said in a sort of annoyed tone. 3 After a few hours, Zaheen was writing notes.' If I was in school, I wouldn't have to write notes at home. Me and my friends could chit-chat while we write.' said Zaheen. Instead of writing notes, Zaheen was day dreaming about school reopening. 4 Zaheen thought 'Laptop has become my life!' 'When will I go to school and meet my friends?' She couldn't sleep and went to her mother. 'Mom! I want to go to school!' she said and woke her up. I hate online classes! 'Zaheen!' mom shouted. 'I am tired of you always complaining!' Zaheen was confused and mad 'Why is mother scolding me? I'm the one who should be mad!' she thought. 'Just deal with it! We can't do anything about it Zaheen! It's not in my hands or in yours! Go to sleep!' said mother and left the room. 5 Zaheen was sad. "mom is angry at me.' 'Why?' she thought to herself. 'Have I been annoying her?' With all these heavy thoughts she went to sleep. In her dream, mother came and dropped her in school and she ate lunch with her friends but when she woke up she was upset to find out it was not real. Zaheen ate breakfast sad. She took online classes sad. She played sad and did homework sad. Mother later came and sat beside her. "how was your day?" she asked. "Good" murmured Zaheen. "Are you angry at me?" asked Mom. "Partly, yes." said Zaheen. "Zaheen, you have to understand we can't do anything about it. We can't remove Covid-19 from the world." said Mother calmly. "I wish we could. I hate online classes." said Zaheen. "I wish we could too, but we can't. But look on the bright side, by taking online classes, you can be comfortable at your own home. You only have class till 12, so you have more time to take on other interests. Like how you learned piano! In school, it's always hot but at home it's nice and warm. See, there are lot of plus sides taking online classes. "Yeah..' said Zaheen, just realizing how go od it is. "And I promise, one day school will reopen and you will have lots of fun there." said mother. 'You are right, mom." said Zaheen. "I'm sorry for troubling you so much." "It's ok, sweetheart." said Mom and gave Zaheen a big hug and a big kiss. Zaheen smiled and said "I love online classes!"

It seems yesterday she was born.” Ha!Ha!Ha! “ Let Paa come and decide about having a puppy” said Mithi. “ Paa, Before my sixth birthday I want a little puppy” said Mithi. Paa said, “ Taking care of animals is not a fun because they play all day in the sun. First You give them something to eat and then you have to clean them from top to feet. If they don’t feel well, you have to take them to the vet. “ Paa smiled, “ Can you manage all these? “ I may or may not! Yes, I can! No, it is quite difficult! It's like having a new member in the family! Yes! Yes! I Can No! Might Not! Next morning, “Mithi, aunt Pusha is here along with your cousin Chickoo” said Paa. Mithi jumped off the bed and shouted, “ Chickoo! My Chickoo! Mithi played with Chickoo whole day, taking care of his all the needs. She helped aunt Pusha in feeding him, giving him bath and even in changing the diaper. She took Chickoo in her laps very carefully and swing the cradle softly. ‘ Our Mithi has grown big” said Maa and Paa together. Happy Birthday Mithi! Here’s your birthday gift! Mithi opened the box and screamed with happiness, “ MY little Puppy! My Little Puppy!” She hugged 'Maa and Paa' with joy and thanked them. They said, “ To be responsible -is not about the age. “

title: Jungle Chaos
text: Once upon a time, many animals lived peacefully together in a forest. The monkey was jumping from tree to tree until his eyes fell on a beehive. The monkey was very hungry for something sweet and so decided to take some honey. But he couldn't find the queen bee for taking permission. As he was very hungry he thought that he could take some of the honey. As soon as he took out his hand to take the honey, many bees came out from the beehive ready to sting him. The monkey started running and hid in a bush. He somehow escaped onto a tree. The bees started to sting a tiger. The tiger bolted towards the bisons. Seeing the tiger coming towards them, the bisons started running very fast. All the animals were confused and frightened. They all ran into different directions. An old owl asked the bisons that why were they running. The bisons replied that a tiger was chasing them. Then the owl went to the tiger who was hiding in a cave. He asked "Why were you chasing the bisons?". " I was not chasing the bisons, instead I was being chased by the bees" replied the tiger. The owl went to the bees afterwards, who were chasing the bisons and asked "Why are you chasing the bisons?". "The monkey stole our honey. We are just trying to find him" said the bees. Next, the owl visited the monkey who was sitting on a tree and viewing the chaos happening below. The owl asked "Why did you take the honey from the beehive?". The monkey told the owl that he was very hungry and so decided to take some honey but he couldn't find the queen bee for permission. As he was very hungry he thought that he could take some of the honey and he would tell the queen bee later. Now, he realized that he had done the wrong thing and wanted to apologize to the bees but if he went near them they would sting him. The owl thought for some time and then quickly reached for the bees. He told the bees what had happened and they accepted the monkey's apology. Then, they all went to the tiger and told him everything. The bees apologized to the tiger for scaring him. Afterwards, they went to the bisons and told them the whole story. The tiger apologized to the bisons for scaring them. They all laughed at what had happened due to a simple misunderstanding and became good friends.

title: Friends Forever
text: There once lived a mouse and frog who were very good friends. Every morning the frog would go to visit the mouse who lived in a hole inside a tree. The mouse very much enjoyed the company of the frog, but the mouse did not realise that the frog was growing increasingly frustrated because it was always him who had to visit the mouse and never the other way around. The lazy little mouse did not know it at the time, but he was slowly making an enemy of his good friend, the frog. One afternoon, when it was time to return home, the frog decided that he had had enough of this one-sided friendship. And so the frog tied one end of a piece of string to his leg, and then tied the other end of the piece of string to the little mouse’s tail without him noticing. The frog waved goodbye to the mouse and then dived into the pond at the foot of the tree far below. All at once, completely to his surprise, the string pulled tight on the mouse’s tail and he was dragged from the safety of his tree and sent tumbling into the air towards the pond below. Splash! The poor little mouse could not swim, and as much as he struggled and struggled to free his tail, he could not untie the piece of string. After much splashing and struggling, the poor mouse finally drowned in the pond. ‘That will teach you to make a fool out of me, you lazy mouse,’ thought the frog. But this misdeed did not go unnoticed: high up in the sky, a hawk spotted the little mouse floating in the water below. And so the hungry hawk swooped down towards the pond to grab the little mouse for its dinner. It was only when the hawk grasped a hold of the mouse with its sharp talons that the frog remembered he was still tied to the mouse by the piece of string. Up, up into the sky went the frog, until the hawk came to rest in the tallest branch of a nearby tree. It was then that the frog realised the error of his ways. In setting a trap for his friend, the frog had also set a trap for himself and sealed his own fate. And now he too would be eaten by the hawk because of his wicked plan. There is an old African proverb that goes... ‘Do not dig too deep a pit for your enemy because you may fall into it yourself.’

title: Care for Animals
text: Once lived a father and a son, named John and Tom. John was 40 years and his son Tom was 11 years old. On a weekend they decided to pay a visit to Tom’s grandfather’s farm. Tom was very excited as he was going first time to farm which was 100 Km away from his home. When they reached Tom’s grandfather’s farm, Tom was fascinated to see the farm which was large and beautiful. Tom’s grandfather’s name was Ben and he was 89 years old. Tom was frequently looking at the cow and running behind them. John was helping grandfather for watering the crops. They were enjoying a sunny and breezy weekend afternoon together. Suddenly, there was a gush of wind and there was a loud sound of moo, it was Cora the cow she was hurt, and she was crying. All sat around Cora and they were thinking what happened to her? Tom looked around Cora and saw a wooden stick penetrated in to her leg which was bleeding. He thought that because of wind she got hurt and he told everyone about the situation. Everyone agreed that Cora needs immediate medical care. Grandfather bought the first aid kit and treated on Cora’s leg. Grandfather advised everybody, let Cora rest for some time. The next day Tom visited the farm and checked about Cora’s health. To his surprise, Cora was dancing and jumping!!! Tom was happy to see Cora in good health and promised to visit farm every weekend to take care of the animals. That’s how Tom got his first lesson of helping animals.

title: Dogs
text: The dog is a pet animal. A dog has sharp teeth so that it can eat flesh very easily, it has four legs, two ears, two eyes, a tail, a mouth, and a nose. It is a very clever animal and is very useful in catching thieves. It runs very fast, barks loudly and attacks the strangers. A dog saves the life of the master from danger. One can find dogs everywhere in the world. Dogs are a very faithful animal. It has a sharp mind and a strong sense of hearing smelling the things. It also has many qualities like swimming in the water, jumping from anywhere, good smelling sense. A dog has a strong power of smell. They are more liked by people because of their faithfulness. They are intelligent, they are watchfulness. The dogs have many colors such as grey, white, black, brown and red. They are of many kinds such as bloodhound, greyhound, german shepherd, Labrador, Rottweiler, bulldog poodle, etc. Usually, the dog eats fish, meat, milk, rice, bread, etc. Dogs are sometimes called canines. Dogs are sometimes referred to as man’s best friend because they are kept as domestic pets and are usually loyal and like being around humans. They are also helpful in reducing stress, anxiety, and depression, loneliness, encourage exercise and playfulness and even improve your cardiovascular health. A dog also provides valuable companionship for older adults. The dogs are so loyal to his master that nothing can induce him to leave his master. His master might be a poor man or even a beggar but still, the dog will not leave his master from far off. Dogs see their master coming home from work they rush to them and jump on them to show their love. Dogs are honest friends who are always ready to die to save a friend. It can bite a thief or stranger when they ignore its barking and try to mischief. Dogs always give security to the owner day and night.

title: Gopal Narayan Public Library - Bharatpura
text: Today I tell you the story of a unique library in my state." The children were a little surprised, "The story of the library?" Junaid sir took out some pictures from his bag and moved them towards the children. The children started looking at those pictures, one after the other, the third…. The children asked, "Where is this picture, sir?" Junaid sir said, “This picture is of Gopal Narayan Public Library, Bharatpura. Today I narrate the story of this library. I went there recently. Green fields are visible from far and wide as one enters Bharatpura village. On a high mound in the middle of the same fields stands the library building surrounded by government security guards. Junaid sir said, "You have asked a very good question. Along with the library, Bharatpura also has historical importance. The library was started by a man named Gopal Narayan Singh. His forefather, Raja Kanchan, was a brave and intelligent man of his time. His family had migrated from Maharashtra and settled in Bihar. That was the time of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. He was well respected by the emperor. He had a descendant- Raja Bharat Singh. He built a fort here, which became famous as Bharatpura Garh. In the year 1912, the foundation of the library was laid in the same fort from the rare books and photographs received from his ancestors and some scholars, art lovers. By the way, the library has a huge collection of printed books, five thousand rare paintings, 146 ancient sculptures and two hundred ancient coins, including the coins of the Pala period. But there are some rare and important pictures, calligraphy samples and documents which are very special. Among these are the illustrated 'Shahnama' by Firdausi in beautiful manuscripts in Persian, the illustrated Sikandar Nama by Nizami, 'Vasalis of the tenth century' illustrated 'Gunverag' of the eleventh century, 'Deewane Hafiz' of the eleventh century, the painting of Akbar's son Daniel special Huh. Apart from this, Hatimatai of the eleventh century, Bihari Satsai Tika, Tulsikrit Ramayana are the works to be proud of in this library. Living amidst these creations, it is as if you are sitting in a time machine on a journey to the past. Every word, every picture of them brings their present to the fore. Suresh, a student, asked in surprise, “Sir. Such a big library in a village?" Junaid sir said, “It is natural for you to be shocked. Such a library in a village and so many unique documents in that library, can surprise anyone. Raghuraj Narayan Singh, a descendant of its founder Gopal Narayan Singh, made this library public through a donation letter in 1956, but also put a condition that the manuscripts remain in the library of Bharatpura and his family heirs should be its secretary. This tradition continues even today. This library has also suffered many sorrows. The theft of pages of manuscripts, theft of paintings has given it deep wounds. Wrapped in the golden memories of history and the nostalgia of the present, Bihar's heritage is an invaluable library that you all must see.
author: NAMAN RAJPUT

title: School Of Parrots
text: All were from distant villages. Everyone had lots in their hands. Some even had sticks in their hands. The twilight of the evening was about to fade. People came closer to the forest. Across the forest was his village. If everyone walks through the forest, they will reach the village soon. But, if we follow the winding roads, it will take more time to reach the village. All of these thoughts started on the way through the forest. Everyone had reached the middle of the forest. When suddenly his eyes came in front of him, he was stunned. Saw that there are hundreds of parrots sitting there. All of them queued up in multiple lines. An old parrot is sitting in front. The old parrot is reciting Sanskrit shlokas. And, the parrots sitting in front are repeating that. Seeing this scene, it was natural for the people crossing the forest to be shocked. Everyone reached the old parrot. The old parrot asked him - Do you know the name of Mandan Mishra? The same, with whom Shankaracharya had come to Mithila to debate. Those who crossed the forest after listening to the old parrot said in one voice – why would you not know? We are his descendants. The old parrot said - You must have also known that there were two cages hanging on the door of Mandan Mishra. There was a parrot in one and mya in the other. Both were great scholars of Sanskrit. He had the impression of the scholarship of Mandan Mishra. That is why they used to argue with each other in Sanskrit every moment. All of us parrots are descendants of the same old parrot. We are carrying forward the tradition of scholarship of our ancestors through this evening school. The people crossing the forest felt guilty that they could not carry forward the tradition of their ancestor Mandan Mishra. Even though they are parrots. People decided that like these parrots, they too would carry forward the tradition of scholarship of their ancestor Mandan Mishra.
