The dog was scaring every child in the park because he was barking madly and was attacking everybody who was coming in his way. Arnav and Ram sitting in the swing, tried to run away from the dog. Ram was successful in coming out of the park but Arnav's leg got stuck in a small pit while running away, he tried to get his leg out of the pit but got a strain in his leg and was not able to get up and run away. The dog was about to reach and attack Arnav but Ram was constantly was observing the whole situation.Ram shouted and called for help to a security guard who was few meters away from them. When the guard heard the yelling of Ram, he ran towards the park with is heavy stick. The dog saw the guard coming towards him with the heavy stick in his hand and got scared. The dog instantly ran away from the park and Arnav was saved. Then Ram came to Arnav and pulled him up and hugged each other. In that situation, Ram could have run away but he was a true friend of Arnav and was equally worried about him as was about himself. This shows their true friendship Moral of the story is - we should always help our friend because a friend in need is a friend indeed.

title: When as, Then that
text: I JHA During Champaran Satyagrah, Gandhi ji's slogan was, 'Walk towards the village! wake up the villagers!!' Pt. Prajapati Mishra was a popular activist of the Satyagraha movement. He used to roam from village to village throughout the day forming groups. At night he would stay at someone's house. Ate and drank whatever they got there. One day he reached the house of a poor man. There was no food prepared for him that night. The whole family was sleeping hungry. On seeing Pandit ji, the family members made him and his team seated respectfully and arranged straw etc. for them to sleep. Night had come up. Prajapati Mishra understood that today food was not going to be available. He called the head of the family separately and said, “We have all had our meals. Don't prepare for the food. Just make arrangements for some water to drink." On the other hand, while telling the story to his other mates, he said, "I know that you all are hungry. But we are not free. That's why we should adapt ourselves to whatever the situation is." and more convincingly said, " Sometimes the dust is dense, sometimes a handful of gram and sometimes that too is forbidden." title: The Shoemaker and The Elves
text: They were going through bad time. The shoes that he used to make were not liked and purchased by new generation of customers. He tried making the best design of shoes, but it was of no use. He was left with a small piece of leather which could make just one pair of shoes and had no money to purchase more leather. One night he cut down that last piece of leather to make one pair of shoes next morning. Next morning, when he went to make last pair of shoes, he was surprised and shocked to see a magnificent pair of shoes already prepared. The shoes were so beautiful and finely stitched that it was quickly sold out in the market at a very good price. The shoemaker purchased leather for two pairs of shoes and returned home. At night he again cut down the leather and kept them in the room to prepare two pair of shoes the next day. Next morning he again found two pairs of shoes finely and beautifully stitched. They were also sold out at a very high price. That became a daily routine. Soon the poor shoemaker became rich and famous. The shoes were of so high quality and latest design that even the king and the queen started wearing the shoes prepared by him. The shoemaker's family now had all the comforts of life, but their living was still very simple. One day the shoemaker was telling her wife "We must look for our angel who made our life so comfortable. We should thank him for his incredible help". "the wife also agreed to him. Hence, one night they hide themselves behind the doors to find their angel. At midnight, they found wo elves entering their house dancing and singing through a window. They worked the whole night and make attractive shoes using their little hammer and needles. at the dawn, they left happily leaving behind pairs of finely stitched shoes.both the shoemaker and his wife to thank the elves by making something very special for them. The shoemaker decided to make a new pairs of shoes of them out of very fine quality leather, as they were wearing old shoes. The wife decided to stitch new clothes with finest sil and emboroidered with jwells and precios stones as the clothes they were wearing were old and torn. both the shoemaker and his wife worked hard the entire day. At night they kept the two pairs of shoes and new set of clothes in the room and hide themselves behind the doors. At midnight, The elves came again dancing and singing. The did not see leather in the room, but instead found those beautiful little shoes and clothes lying on the bench. they were very happy and excited and quickly put on the new shoes and clothes and went away. The shoemaker and his family also lived happily everafter. The End:

title: The Different Bird
text: There was a bird that loved to listen to the other bird's sing. The bird listened to their songs and thought, " I wish I could sing like that too." But, the bird was unable to sing. All that the bird could do was click sounds, and it could make a sound like the wind. Nothing happened when the bird tried to sing, just a " click, click, click, whoosh" sound came out. That's all that anyone ever heard from the bird. All the other birds laughed and laughed at her. They all joined in and taunted, " Birds of a feather flock together. Even though you have feathers, you're not like us, so you can't be part of our flock." "Oh dear ", sighed the bird. She sat in her tree and worried. She wasn't exactly sure what a flock was, but she knew the other birds laughed at her, and she knew she was different. The bird said to herself, " No other birds will want to be my friends because they all think I'm strange." Every day, the bird tried so hard to sing, but every day, she just made the same clicking sound. One day, while perched in the forest, the bird heard a new sound. It was the sound of people talking. The bird stopped and listened intently. Then. something strange happened. The bird discovered she could talk to. She was able to say the same words the people in the forest were saying. A man said, " Look at the beautiful trees." Then the bird also said, " Look at the beautiful trees." Another man asked, surprised, " Did you just hear that bird? It talked!" The bird repeated, " Did you just hear that bird? It talked!" Now, all the people in the forest stopped to listen to the bird speak. One person would say something, and then the bird would echo what he had said. The people left, saying " What a special bird!" They heard, " What a special bird!", as they walked out of the forest. The bird had followed them. Every day after that, people would come to the forest, and the bird would repeat what they said. Now, all the other birds looked at her differently. "You are our here," they stated. "You are such a special bird." After that day in the forest, the bird had many friends. She still couldn't sing, but she could talk. Although she was different, she and the other birds agreed that different was special. Being different felt very good. One bird said, " Being different is like being a diamond. There are many rocks, but there are not many diamonds. Sometimes you don't see how bright is a diamond at first. Now, we see how great you are. You are our diamond." If you know someone who is different, remember this story. Everyone is special and everyone can do different things. Don't judge other people. See who they are; learn what they can do. Be their Friend. If you do that, you will find many special people.
author: Ishaan  Patil

title: Raccoon! Do not go on the face
text: Characters: - {Rahul, Suraj, Rosie, Thea, Rosie’s parents, pet shopkeeper, doctor, raccoon} [Rahul and Suraj started a conversation about raccoons] Suraj: - Hello, Rahul all fine? Rahul: - Yes. Rahul: - No they are omnivores; they are small but very aggressive and can even kill a cat. Suraj: - Oh! That’s why I wonder, why they quite often sneak into the garden of houses in cities, when the owners are away. [Rosie joins Rahul and Suraj] Rosie: - What are you doing guys? Rahul: - We are talking about raccoons. Rosie: - What is it? Suraj: - It is a cute foxlike creature roaming in the woodlands of North America. Let me show you some pictures of it. Rosie: - Wow! so cute. [Thea called Rosie] Thea: - What were you doing? Rosie: - I was talking with Rahul and Suraj about raccoons. Thea: - Okay. Rosie: - I think I should buy it as a pet. Thea: - But it’s very… [At this moment, Rosie is called by her parents] Rosie: - Dad, I want to buy a pet raccoon. Rosie’s father: Okay, can you describe about it to me? [Rosie described everything she knew about raccoons] Rosie’s father: - Okay, we will meet the shopkeeper in the upcoming weekend. [On the weekend they went to the shopkeeper] Rosie’s father demands the shopkeeper for a pet raccoon. The shopkeeper said it’s very aggressive and unpredictable in nature. Rosie’s parents tried to make her understand but she did not listen to them at all. The shopkeeper intervened and said we can give you a baby raccoon it would not harm and you can return it when it grows up. The next day Rosie showed the picture of her pet raccoon to her friends. They told her; her pet is very aggressive. Rosie said you all are jealous of me. [The school closes for summer vacation] One day when Rosie was playing and the raccoon bit her. She screamed in pain and then her father rushed her to the hospital. The doctor gave her 18 injections of rabies and advised her bed rest for a month. Moral of the story: - Don’t judge a book by its cover. Conclusion: - We cannot judge a thing by just seeing it because when we see it we only see the outer cover of it, not the inner one.

title: Marching to Freedom
text: Dhani knew something exciting was being planned at the ashram, but no one would tell him anything. “Just because I’m nine years old,” thought Dhani glumly. “I’m sure they think I’m stupid. I am not!” Dhani and his parents lived in a very special place. It was Mahatma Gandhi’s Sabarmati Ashram near Ahmedabad where people from all over India came to stay. Like Gandhiji, they were all fighting for India’s freedom. During their stay at the ashram, they spent their time spinning khadi thread on charkhas, singing bhajans and listening to Gandhiji’s lectures. That morning, as Dhani fed Binni with fresh grass and changed the water in her bowl, he said, “Something’s up, Binni! They all sit and talk in Gandhiji’s room. They are planning something. I know it!” Binni chewed and nodded as if she understood. Dhani felt hungry. He headed towards the kitchen, with Binni skipping along beside him. His mother was fanning the chulha, filling up the room with smoke. “Amma, is Gandhiji going somewhere?” he asked. His mother coughed in the smoke and said, “They are going on a march.” March? Where are they going?” Dhani queried. “Somewhere near the sea. Now stop asking questions and go away Dhani!” his mother said impatiently. “Let me finish the cooking first.” Dhani wandered off to the vegetable garden where old Binda was digging up potatoes. Binda chacha,” Dhani sat beside him, “are you going on the march too?” Binda shook his head. Before he could say anything, Dhani eagerly asked, “Who is marching? Where are they going? What is happening?” Binda stopped digging and said, “I’ll answer all your questions, but first tie up that troublesome goat. She’s chewing up my spinach.” Dhani dragged Binni away and tied her to the lemon tree nearby. Then Binda told him about the march. Gandhiji and some of the men from the ashram were going to walk through Gujarat to reach the sea at a place called Dandi. They would walk through villages and towns for a whole month. Once they reached Dandi, they would make salt. “Salt?” Dhani sat up and frowned. “Why will they make salt? You can buy it in every shop!” “I know,” Binda laughed. “But Mahatma has a plan. You know he always marches to protest against something, right?” “Of course I know. He leads the Satyagraha marches to fight the British government and win freedom for India. But why is he protesting about salt? It’s silly!” “It’s not silly at all, Dhani! Do you know we all have to pay a tax on salt?” “So what?” “Everyone needs salt… that means, every Indian, even the poorest, has to pay this tax,” explained Binda chacha. “That is really unfair!” Dhani’s eyes were hot with anger. Walking for a month!” Dhani brooded worriedly. “Gandhiji will get really tired. Why don’t they take a bus or train to Dandi instead?” “Because, if he goes on this long march and walks all the way to Dandi, the news will spread. There will be pictures in the papers and reports on the radio, and people all over the world will know that we are fighting for our freedom. And that will really embarrass the British.” Gandhiji is clever, isn’t he?” Dhani’s eyes were shining. “Ah, that he is!” Binda’s eyes crinkled with laughter. “He’s even written to the Viceroy and told him what he plans to do! The British have no idea what they are in for!” Later in the morning, Dhani wandered up to the hut where Gandhiji was staying and peered in through a window. Inside, many of the ashram people were talking to Gandhiji. Dhani heard them planning the route along which they would walk to Dandi. He was thrilled to see his father sitting among the people. In the afternoon, when the ashram was quiet, Dhani went looking for his father. He found him under a tree, spinning on his charkha. “Pitaji, are you and Amma going on the march to Dandi?” Dhani got straight to the point. “I am going. You and Amma will stay here.” “I am coming with you.” “Don’t be silly, Dhani. You can’t walk so much. Only the ashram’s young men will go.” “I’m nine and I can run faster than you can!” Dhani replied stubbornly. “You can’t stop me from coming with you.” His father stopped spinning and explained patiently, “Only the people who have been chosen by Mahatma will go.” “Fine! I’ll talk to him then! I’m sure he’ll say yes,” said Dhani and marched off. Gandhiji was a very busy man and it was not easy to catch him alone. But Dhani knew exactly when he would have the time to listen – early every morning when he went for a walk around the ashram. The next morning, as the sun came up, Dhani slipped out of bed and went looking for Gandhiji. He found him in the cowshed checking on all the cows. Then he strolled into the vegetable garden to inspect the peas and cabbage and have a chat with Binda. All the while, Dhani and Binni followed him. Finally, Gandhiji headed back to his hut. He sat down beside his charkha in the verandah and called out to Dhani, “Come here, child!” Dhani ran up, with Binni skipping along. “What’s your name beta?” “Dhani, Gandhiji.” “And this is your goat?” “Yes, Gandhiji! This is my friend Binni, who gives the milk you drink every morning.” Dhani smiled proudly and said, “I take care of her.” “Good!” Gandhiji leaned forward. “Now Dhani, tell me why you and Binni have been following me everywhere this morning?” “I wanted to ask you something,” Dhani began nervously. “Can I come with you to Dandi?” Gandhiji smiled, “You are too small, beta. Dandi is 385 kilometers away and only young men like your father will be able to walk with me.” “But you are not young!” Dhani said. “Won’t you feel tired?” “I am a very good walker,” Gandhiji replied. “I am a good walker too.” Dhani was adamant. “Ah yes,” Gandhiji looked thoughtful. “But there is a problem. If you go with me, who will take care of Binni? After walking for so long, I will become weak. When I come back, I’ll need to drink lots of milk to become strong again.” Hmm, you’re right, Gandhiji. Binni eats only when I feed her.” Dhani lovingly stroked Binna's head, “And only I know what she likes to eat.” “Exactly! So will you stay in the ashram and take care of Binni for me?” “Yes, Gandhiji, I will,” said Dhani. “And Binni and I will be waiting for you.” Fun facts of History In March 1930, Mahatma Gandhi led the march to Dandi to protest against the tax on salt imposed by the British. Gandhi and his followers walked through Gujarat for 24 days. All along the way, they were welcomed with flowers and songs. Newspapers across the world carried reports about the march. At Dandi, Gandhi and his followers collected salt from the seashore and were arrested. The arrest sparked off the Non-cooperation Movement, and people all over India boycotted schools, colleges and offices. There were 78 volunteers who accompanied Gandhi on the march. They covered a distance of 385 kilometres. The march began on 12 March and ended on 5 April 1930. The youngest marcher was 16 years old. The year 2005 marks the 75th anniversary of the Dandi March.

title: THE GRAPES ARE SOUR

But the bunches were too high for him and he was feeling weak. So he sat down for a while to take some rest. On feeling refreshed, he jumped as high as he could, to get at the grapes. But he failed to reach them. Then he again rested for some time and made another bold attempt, but was unlucky for the second time. Forced to give up trying anymore, he just walked away and instead of accepting his failure, he remarked "the grapes appeared to be ripe and juicy, but now I see them to be quite sour." This story, thus, proves that, people generally hate what they can't get.

title: Why Pig has a Curly Tail by Neel Hede
text: There was once a time when pig’s tail was straight. Here is what happened - It was almost night; pig was sleeping in the mud and his tail was sticking out. A hen who was looking around for food happened to come to the place where pig was asleep. The hen thought that the pig’s tail was a worm! She was happy! She pulled and pulled! The pig said, “Ouch! Stop it! That is my tail.” The hen, still very hungry, stopped and went away. After sometime a cat came there. She thought that the pig’s tail was a mouse’s tail. The cat was excited! She pulled and pulled! The pig said, “Ouch! Stop it! That is my tail.” The cat, quite upset, stopped and went away. Then came a dog. He thought that the pig’s tail was a cat’s tail. The dog was thrilled! He pulled and pulled! The pig said, “Ouch! Stop it! That is my tail.” The dog, angry, stopped and went away. Then came a cow. She thought that the pig’s tail was a blade of grass. The cow’s mouth started watering! She pulled and pulled! The pig said, “Ouch! Stop it! That is my tail.” The cow, sad, stopped and went away. Then came a horse. He thought that the pig’s tail was a carrot leaf. The horse was glad! He pulled and pulled! The pig said, “Ouch! Stop it! That is my tail.” The horse, rather miserable, stopped and went away. Then came a donkey. He thought that the pig’s tail was some hay. The donkey was delighted, he pulled and pulled! The pig said, “Ouch! Stop it! That is my tail.” The donkey, disappointed, stopped and went away. Pig was sad, his tail was hurting! He could hardly sleep. When he woke up in the morning, he went to the pond as he always did. And what did he see? His tail had become curly! And that is why pigs have curly tails.

title: Cat and Fox
text: Cat and Fox were best friends. They lived in AwoAwo forest. They ate together, had sleepovers, and loved playing with each other. But someone did not like the happy pair. The grubby, dirty, foul witch. She called them “Unspeakably, tremendously, ugly”. In other words, she hated friendship and happiness. For years, she had tried to separate them by. ● By writing “I Hate You” ● By making one of them annoying There were lots more, but none of them worked. When she was practicing her spells, she got an idea. What if she put a spell on the fox so the unsuspecting animal wouldn’t know the cat? She found a spell in her spell book but it said, “The animal bewitched in this spell will return to a normal state in water”. The witch put the spell on the fox and then added a spell from her spell book called “How to make an animal hate water: SPELL 102:” Her evil plans can be defeated, though. When Cat knocked on Fox’s door, Fox opened the door and said,” Umm…I don’t know and I don’t like strangers. Go away. SHOO!” Cat stormed out of Fox’s porch. She went home and said, “Why are you like this, Fox? I thought we were best friends.” In that evening, the fox went out to the Wallaba Pool to enjoy its a pretty view. Then, Fox slipped on a rock, and…SPLASH! He fell in the water. “Oh! How mean I’ve been to Cat!”, said Fox as he got his memory back. Fox rushed out the water and dashed to Cat’s house. “Hi”, said Cat. “I’m really sorry, Cat. The grubby witch bewitched me. Can we please, please, please be friends again?” explained Fox. Cat said, “Since I know the truth…YES!” Their smiles were as wide as slices of watermelon. The witch, you ask? Why, she was grumbling and grumpier than before.

title: Arjun's day at the Market
text: Arjun and his Amma reach a place through a taxi. Arjun sees many shops selling vegetables, utensils, meat, fish, fruits, clothes, shoes, etc. He saw hundreds of people everywhere. Arjun was confused. "Why have we come to a strange place. There seem to be many people here. It must be an occasion place. " thought Arjun. " Amma there seems to be many people here." says Arjun " Is there any occasion going on here? " " No beta. It is a place where we buy things like clothes, vegetables, fruits, shoes, etc. This is called a market, " says Amma " Hold my hand tight. There are many people here. You may get lost. " says Amma taking him to a shop. " Amma, look there are many flour bags. This must be a flour shop right? "says Arjun " Yes " says Amma taking 1kg flour. " Have a good day " says Makin the shopkeeper. "Thank you, " says Amma. Amma let's buy some prawns. Didi and dada like prawns very much. says Arjun. "Ok, " says Amma buying 500g of prawns. " Thank you, " says Amma to Aali the fishmonger. " Let's buy cucumbers, tomatoes, spinach, bottle guard, and potato" says Amma. " OK. A unty, please give me cucumbers, tomatoes, spinach, and... and..." says Arjun. Arjun forgot what his mother said luckily her mother said the rest to the vegetable vendor. "Haaa. And bottle guard and potato." Amma bought the vegetables and gave ₹ 225/- to the vendor. " 😃 Thank you" Arjun then she's Amma's favorite shop. The garment shop. But what was this, to Arjun's surprise Amma didn't buy anything. Usually, she buys lots of clothes. When Arjun was about to ask the reason her mother said " Garments are my best but we do not have much money and those are not the nesseciary things we need to buy. Arjun, money is also important." Arjun and Amma then went to the dairy shop. “ Amma pl buy me at least 1 ice cream." “No Arjun, Ice cream is bad for health. Now be a good boy" says Amma. Amma takes Arjun away from the dairy shop. Arjun was a bit frowned. Both take a taxi and go home. Why is vegetable market necessary? Vegetable markets provide healthier food items that are fresher than the ones available in supermarkets. The vendors directly come and sell in almost every neighborhood. So it is convenient for almost everybody everywhere. Children must eat vegetables to be fit and active

title: When Adversity Knocks
text: Mary was a young girl. She used to get annoyed with everything. She had a negative attitude towards life. Once, when she felt that life was unbearable, she asked her father what to do. She told him that if she was able to manage and solve one problem, another one followed quickly. Her father consoled her and took her to the kitchen. He asked Mary to take a potato, an egg and two spoons of tea leaves. Mary was surprised, and asked her father, “Do you want me to cook?” No,” her father said. He then took three vessels and poured one cup of water in each vessel. The vessels were placed on the stove. Once the water started to boil, he dropped the potato in a vessel, egg in the second one and the tea leaves in the third one. Why are you doing all these things?” Mary asked, really annoyed with her father. Just wait fifteen minutes,” said her father. The impatient daughter managed to wait for around 15 minutes. Father removed the potato from the pot and placed in a plate. He did the same with the eggs. He filtered the tea decoction using a cup. Now, he placed the two plates, one with the potato and the other with the egg, and the cup of tea in front of Mary. He asked Mary, “What do you see?” “Potato, egg and a cup of tea,” said Mary. No, you are wrong,” said her father. “Look at it closely and answer me. Mary replied the same. Now touch it and answer me. The potato was cooked and was soft, the egg was boiled hard, and the tea carried a nice aroma. Mary couldn’t find the correct answer. “Potato, egg and a cup of tea,” said Mary. No, you are wrong,” said her father. “Look at it closely and answer me.” Mary replied the same. “Now touch it and answer me.” The potato was cooked and was soft, the egg was boiled hard, and the tea carried a nice aroma. Mary couldn’t find the correct answer. Her father said, “The potato was so hard and strong before it was boiled; now it has turned soft and smooth. Also, the egg was delicate but after boiling it became hard. Sip the tea. It is delicious! Mary asked, “What does it mean father? I don’t understand!” “Each object responded differently to water. Each object was put under the same kind of circumstances, faced similar adversities, but reacted differently. The potato, when put in boiling water, became very weak. The soft egg became very hard when we put it in boiling water. And the tea leaves are unique. It changed the water itself, giving it a unique flavour and aroma! It gave something new.” Mary understood that we can create something new and unique even when we experience adversities.
author: Aditi Singh

title: Environmental pollution part 1
text: Pollution is the introduction of contaminants into the natural environment that cause adverse change. [1] Pollution can take the form of any substance (solid, liquid, or gas) or energy (such as radioactivity, heat, sound, or light). Pollutants, the components of pollution, can be either foreign substances/energies or naturally occurring contaminants. Although environmental pollution can be caused by natural events, the word pollution generally implies that the contaminants have an anthropogenic source—that is, a source
author: Yash Kumar

title: Environmental pollution part 3
text: Land or soil pollution Land or soil gets pollution when harmful substances are released into it. land can get polluted harmful substances accumulate on it. causes of soil pollution 1-solid wastes such as garbage 2-Refuse from forests and agriculture 3-Refuse from mines pollution makes soil infertile. It also harms the organisms living in the soil.
author: Yash Kumar

title: Environmental pollution part 4
text: Noise pollution Excessive and unpleasant sound in our environment is called noise or sounds pollution. it causes stress, irritation and can also lead to loss of hearing. the intensity of sound is measured hear is about 20 decibels. Any sound louder than 90 decibels is harmful. causes of noise pollution 1-car and bus horns 2-loudspeakers and loud music 3-home appliances such as vacuum cleaners, washing machines, air conditioners and mixer-grinders. Firecrackers damage to the environment affects us directly. we must do whatever we can to protect our environment. controlling pollution is crucial for life to continue on this planet.
author: Yash Kumar

text: Once upon a time there was a poor family. In that family there was a girl whose name was Maya, Maya's father was a junk collector. Maya went to a nearby school. Any sound louder than 90 decibels is harmful. causes of noise pollution 1-car and bus horns 2-loudspeakers and loud music 3-home appliances such as vacuum cleaners, washing machines, air conditioners and mixer-grinders. Firecrackers damage to the environment affects us directly. we must do whatever we can to protect our environment. controlling pollution is crucial for life to continue on this planet. Pollution is the introduction of contaminants into the natural environment that cause adverse change. [1] Pollution can take the form of any substance (solid, liquid, or gas) or energy (such as radioactivity, heat, sound, or light). Pollutants, the components of pollution, can be either foreign substances/energies or naturally occurring contaminants. Although environmental pollution can be caused by natural events, the word pollution generally implies that the contaminants have an anthropogenic source—that is, a source

title: Why Flamingos sleep, standing on one leg? by Misha Yaram
text: Long ago, a group of flamingos were having fun together. They were playing the "freeze game", where when the music stopped, one flamingo would give an action command and everyone would pretend to freeze. Meaning, they would not move. In the last round, a flamingo gave the command -"stand on one leg and freeze". All the flamingos followed the command. Each and every flamingo was enjoying balancing in this position and so they continued to stand on one leg, smiling at each other. They were all happy at how well they could balance on one foot. After a while the game ended, and all the flamingos went home. Then one day, as the group of flamingos had gathered, who came there? It was a fox. He said to the flamingos -"Ha ha ha, I am hungry and I want to eat some of you". All the flamingos got worried. But there was one clever flamingo who said to the fox - "Look fox we have a challenge for you". The fox thought he was very smart and so he said -"Oh! I love challenges. You see I am a smart fox. Tell me, what's the challenge?" The clever flamingo replied -"We will all have to stand on one foot. If even one of the flamingos lose their balance, you can eat us up. But if we do not, or if you cannot balance yourself, then you will have to go off empty-handed." "Is that all? Alright then, I accept the challenge", replied the fox, with an evil smile on his face. Very soon the flamingos got into their balancing positions. And the fox, try as he might, he could not stand on one leg. He watched the flamingos stand there on one leg. He watched and watched. After some time, he saw that the flamingos were happily sleeping while standing on one leg. The fox felt horrible for not only having lost the challenge, but also because he had lost the chance to feast on the flamingos. He went away & never ever troubled the flamingos.

title: Why do crocodiles swallow stones? by Abhishai Raj Yaram

The crocodile became so greedy, it ate more and more. Finally, it's stomach began to burn. The crocodile had a bad stomach ache. So the crocodile went to the wise owl, who was also the doctor in the jungle. The wise owl told the crocodile that it should swallow a few stones. That would help the crocodile cure the stomach pain. That's what the crocodile did. And in a few hours, the pain had gone away. The crocodile was happy. It told his family and friends about the useful cure given to it by the wise owl. And from that day, crocodiles have swallowed stones to digest their food better. But this is a cure only for crocodiles, not for human children.

Rainbow is not a physical object but an optical illusion.” Martin said, “A full rainbow is actually a complete circle. If you fly in an airplane, sometimes you can see the full circular rainbow.” Martin said, "When the Sun is in the east, the rainbow appears in the west. When the Sun is in the west, the rainbow appears in the east. Sometimes, you can see a double rainbow." Zara asked, “Is rainbow formed only during rain?" Rick said, "No. The spray of a waterfall, mist, and dew can also cause a rainbow.“ Did you Know? A rainbow is formed by the refraction and reflection of sunlight inside a water drop. Sometimes, a monochrome rainbow appears with only the red colour. This is known as the red rainbow. A twinned rainbow occurs when two rainbows have the same endpoints. In a double rainbow, the secondary rainbow is above the primary rainbow. The colours in the secondary rainbow are reversed and go from red inside to violet outside.

title: Tara is not scared of exams anymore !
text: " Tara!, wake up its 7:30 already! You are going to be late for school today. Wake up dear. ", said Tara's mom Maya. Maya pulled the curtains to let the sunlight in. Tara loved sunny days. It always made her feel full of energy. As the sun's rays fell on Tara's face, she quickly sat up. " It is a sunny day mama, I love it ", Tara said. " Good Morning dear, now quickly wash up and get ready for your classes. I know its online, but you still need to be ready on time ". Maya gave Tara her good morning hug, lifted her down from the bed and gently pushed her towards the bathroom. Tara walked lazily to the bathroom. As she was brushing her teeth, she suddenly remembered about the Maths class test that was to happen later today. ``As she watched herself in the bathroom mirror, she got lost in thoughts. She was getting worried if she was prepared for the test. She started to get scared about getting low marks in the test. The thoughts were crowding up in her head, when her Mom called out to her. "Tara, are you done brushing up dear? Come have a glass of warm water." Tara quickly washed her mouth and face and came out. She was visibly upset. " What happened Tara? You look worried. Is everything alright?" her mom asked. Tara picked the glass of water to drink. After a sip, she said "Mama I'm worried about the Maths test today. I practiced the sums yesterday, but I am scared now". "What are you scared of dear?", mama asked. "I am scared I may not remember what I learned. What if I make many answers wrong? What if my marks are low? Mama I'm scared" Tara said, almost crying. Mama smiled. She gently held Tara close to her and said, "Tara, I saw you practice your sums yesterday. I checked your answers and most of them were right. We also discussed on how to work on the sums that were wrong. Do you remember?" "Yes mama", Tara replied. "See, it is all there in your head. You have learned the sums and also know how to correct the mistakes. So now you just need to relax. And if you make mistakes, it is an opportunity for you to learn from it. It doesn't mean you failed. Just work a little more on those for the next time. " Tara had a light smile on her face now. "Mama but what about marks, what if I don't get good marks". asked Tara. "Don't worry Tara, studying is not always about marks, it is about understanding. When you understand what you read, then it becomes learning. And when you learn, marks wont matter. " Mama said with a smile. "Now, quick get dressed and ready for your classes." Mama said. Tara was a little confused. " What did you say just now mama? Studying and learning are not the same? If I learn then marks wont matter?" "Exactly! When you study, you just read what's in your book and memorize it, so that you can answer questions in exams and get marks." Mama said "Then learning?" Tara asked "But when you learn, you try to understand what you read. You think about what you read and become curious to understand more. While learning, you forget about getting marks, and think more about gaining knowledge. Isn't it different?, Mama explained. "Yes mama it is different, learning is more fun". I'll learn from now on and not study" Tara said. Tara was thrilled by her new found knowledge. She understood the difference between studying and learning. Now she wasn't going to be scared of exams anymore!

title: universe
text: It was hot when it was young. It will be cold when it grows old. The Universe spans a diameter of over 150 billion light years. The Universe is 13.7 billion years old. The Earth is not flat – but the Universe is. Large Scale Structures of the Universe The universe is overwhelmingly made up of things that cannot be seen. In fact, the stars, planets and galaxies that can be detected make up only 4 percent of the universe, according to astronomers. The other 96 percent is made up of substances that cannot be seen or easily comprehended. The universe is everything. It includes all of space, and all the matter and energy that space contains. It even includes time itself and, of course, it includes you. Earth and the Moon are part of the universe, as are the other planets and their many dozens of moons. The universe is currently estimated at roughly 13.8 billion years old, give or take 130 million years. In comparison, the solar system is only about 4.6 billion years old. This estimate came from measuring the composition of matter and energy density in the universe. The Big Bang is thought to have kick-started the universe about 13.7 billion years ago. At first, the universe was too hot and dense for particles to be stable, but then the first quarks formed, which then grouped together to make protons and neutrons, and eventually the first atoms were created.

title: The little cat Leo
text: Once upon a time, there was a small cat named Leo. He was a house cat. In the past When he was a kitten he got lost in a forest. title: biography of Gandhiji
text: Born: 2 October 1869, Porbandar Died: 30 January 1948, Birla House, New Delhi Spouse: Kasturba Gandhi (m. 1883–1944) Children: Harilal Gandhi, Devdas Gandhi, Manilal Gandhi, Ramdas Gandhi Education: UCL Faculty of Laws (1888–1891 Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (Mahatma Gandhi) was born on October 2, 1869, into a Hindu Modh family in Porbandar, Gujarat, India. His father, named Karamchand Gandhi, was the Chief Minister (diwan) of the city of Porbandar. His mother, named Putlibai, was the fourth wife the previous three wives died in childbirth. The Salt March, which took place from March to April 1930 in India, was an act of civil disobedience led by Mohandas Gandhi to protest British rule in India.... The march resulted in the arrest of nearly 60,000 people, including Gandhi himself. India finally was granted its independence in 1947. His father, Karamchand Gandhi, was a local politician, serving as prime minister to a number of local Indian princes; his mother, Putlibai, was Karamchand's fourth wife, married when her husband was already in his forties. In 1943, a year after the Quit India movement started, Gandhi undertook a 21-day fast. This was in response to the Viceroy's insistence that the Indian National Congress was responsible for the disturbances of 1942 and that Gandhi admit to it; in response, Gandhi fasted.

title: why
text: why do you yawn? Yawning is a mostly involuntary process of opening the mouth and breathing in deeply, filling the lungs with air. It's a very natural response to being tired. In fact, yawning is usually triggered by sleepiness or fatigue. Some yawns are short, and some last for several seconds before an open-mouthed exhale. why do you need to have food? Your body needs food for three reasons: food gives your body energy, provides building materials for your body, and helps control body processes. Nutrients are chemicals in food that your body needs, include carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, vitamins, and minerals. why do you get hiccups? Hiccups are caused by involuntary contractions of your diaphragm — the muscle that separates your chest from your abdomen and plays an important role in breathing. This involuntary contraction causes your vocal cords to close very briefly, which produces the characteristic sound of a hiccup. why are moles caused in our body? Moles are caused when cells in the skin (melanocytes) grow in clusters or clumps. Melanocytes are distributed throughout your skin and produce melanin, the natural pigment that gives your skin its color.

title: Kiara buys fruits
text: What is one thing that Kiara loves to eat anytime of the day? If you ask her, the answer would be “ Fruits ”. Today she is off to buy some fruits with her grandpa. “Daadu, which all fruits would we buy?” “All that you want Kiara,” replied daadu. “Can I choose and pick my own fruits, please?” “Yes you may. Take this cart and put them in.” The first counter has apples. She picks one and kept it in her cart. Her cart has one apple only. Next counter has guavas. “Daadi likes guavas and so do I,” she thought. She picks - one guava, two guavas. Kiara has one apple and two guavas in her cart. Next she sees oranges. She was quick to pick three. One orange for daadu, one for daadi and one for herself. There it goes - one orange, two oranges and three oranges. Now there is one apple, two guavas and three oranges in Kiara’s shopping cart. A fter oranges comes the strawberries. She thinks aloud and decides to pick four boxes of strawberries. One box for eating fresh strawberries in the afternoon, one for the strawberry shake in the evening, one for the ice-cream for dinner and one for the jam for her bread. One strawberry box, two strawberry boxes, three strawberry boxes and four strawberry boxes. Kiara now has one apple, two guavas, three oranges and four strawberry boxes in her cart. Next counter has grapes. We all love grapes. She counts the members of her family on her little fingers - daadu, daadi, mumma, papa and me. One, two, three, four and five. So five bunches of grapes for all of us. One bunch of grapes, two bunches of grapes, three bunches of grapes, four bunches of grapes and five bunches of grapes. Kiara is so happy to see her cart full. She now has one apple, two guavas, three oranges, four boxes of strawberries and five bunches of grapes. Green grapes for papa and daadi and black ones for daadu, mumma and herself. “Daadu, let’s go. I am tired of shopping for fruits today. My cart is full and I can’t push it anymore.” Daadu smiles and pays for the fruits. He gives the fruit seller the bags they’ve got from home, to keep the fruits. “Thank you,” says Kiara and so says daadu. "Thank you," replies the shopkeeper and keeps the money in his drawer. “Have a good day Kiara. Come back again soon,” wishes the shopkeeper. Bye!

title: Where's beauty
text: Beauty was missing, and Jincy Jose, the new constable at Erumannoor police station…Haha who immediately got down to work.... So, tell me about Beauty,” Jincy said. “Well, first things first, she is a beauty,” said Tessamma. Honk! Honk! Beeeep! “Honestly, she’s a traffic stopper. “While she’s being milked at dawn, she insists on listening to Western classical music on her radio. “While she grazes, it’s always music from Bollywood. “ When she wallows in the pond — it’s her beauty regimen, you see — she prefers romantic Malayalam songs. And at night, she always sleeps to soft instrumental tunes.” “What excellent taste in music,” thought Jincy. Jincy decided to go around the village and ask folks if they had seen Beauty. She ran into Thommachan, but he hadn’t seen Beauty......... “Sorry, I don’t know any buffalo called Beauty and frankly, I don’t like buffaloes. I only like my cow Chandanakutty and she doesn’t wallow in the mud like those buffaloes.” She then met the sisters Remani and Savithri, who were on their way back from the local pond. They hadn’t seen Beauty either. “I have told Tessamma a hundred times not to let Beauty walk around without a noose.” said Remani. “What’s the harm in giving her a few whacks with a stick? But no, Beauty’s skin is too sensitive it seems. Hmph! Anyway, who would steal that useless buffalo?” “Hee-hee,” giggled Savithri. “If she were a pretty cow, I would steal her.” A little ahead, Jincy ran into a man who seemed to be repairing his truck and making a big noise. There was loud music playing from his truck. Jincy shouted, “Excuse me, have you seen a beautiful black buffalo wandering around here?” “Why’re you asking me? I’m new here. I’m just repairing my truck. My truck is full of jackfruit. And those buffaloes are such social animals. She must be busy socializing with friends. Anyway, like I said, why would I know anything about a buffalo who listens to the radio? It might rain today. Do you think it will rain today? I think so.” Jincy went on ahead. Jincy cycled all around Erumannoor with very little luck. Sorry, haven’t seen any buffaloes “Disappeared in the middle of the night? She’s probably been sold off at the meat market already.” Sorry, haven’t seen any buffaloes “Beauty? My daughter’s name is also Beauty!” “How will you find her when you can’t make out one buffalo from another?” Dulquar Ikka had not seen Beauty, either, but he let Jincy stick a poster about Beauty at his tea stall. Jincy was tired. Bzzzt...bzzzt... bzzz... squwaack... psheww! Just then... BRAAAAANG!! Jincy had a brainwave! She ran back to Beauty's shed. Beauty, of course, was missing. But so was something else. hat night, Jincy ventured out to set some things right. In the darkness of the truck, something other than the fireflies was shining. SCHSSSHEW Jincy had found Beauty! Shaji Kuttappan, Beauty’s kidnapper, was promptly marched off to the police station. “How did you figure it out, Jincy?” asked Tessamma. “It’s simple. Shaji said he hadn’t seen a buffalo who listens to the radio. I never told him about Beauty listening to the radio. Shaji stole Beauty so that he could sell her off in the next village at a butcher’s. But things hadn’t really gone according to his plan.” Shaji had tried hard to get Beauty out of her shed. But Beauty refused to move So Shaji thought he might as well take the radio To his happy surprise, Beauty couldn’t imagine being without her radio o she followed him into his hideout — his truck, which was under repair. Tessamma was thrilled to have her beloved Beauty back. “I must say,” said Inspector Gopi, “Beauty is indeed a beauty.” Beauty and O ther B uffaloes Buffaloes are highly intelligent animals who love socializing with others of their kind. They're often found wallowing in mud or taking dust baths in order to protect their sensitive skin from sunburn and insects that bite. They enjoy grazing and being outdoors. Research shows that buffaloes also like listening to slow music. It helps alleviate stress and relaxes them.

title: Big cats
text: ﻿ What is a big cat? All cats are in the family Felidae. T he largest members of this family form a group known as the ‘big cats’. Big cats are really powerful predators that can be found almost in every place in the world except in cold ranges. LIONS The lion is a large cat of the genus Panthera native to Africa and India. It has a muscular, deep-chested body, short, rounded head, round ears, and a hairy tuft at the end of its tail. LEAPORDS ﻿ The leopard is one of the five extant species in the genus Panthera. Leopards are astoundingly strong. They are pound for pound the strongest of the big cats. They are able to climb trees, even when carrying heavy prey, and often choose to rest on tree branches during the day. Leopards are renowned for their agility. They run up to 58km/h and can leap 6m horizontally and 3m vertically. They are also very strong swimmers. CHEETAHS The cheetah is a large cat native to Africa and central Iran. It is the fastest land animal, estimated to be capable of running at 80 to 128 km/h with the fastest reliably recorded speeds being 93 and 98 km/h, and as such has several adaptations for speed, including a light build, long thin legs and a long tail. TIGERS The tiger is the largest living cat species and a member of the genus Panthera. It is most recognizable for its dark vertical stripes on orange fu r with a white underside. Tigers are nocturnal animals. Tigers love to swim and play in the water. SNOW LEAPORD The snow leopard, also known as the ounce, is a felid in the genus Panthera native to the mountain ranges of Central and South Asia. JAGUARS The jaguar is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera native to the Americas. With a body length of up to 1.85 m and a weight of up to 96 kg, it is the largest cat species in the Americas and the third largest in the world. title: We are all safe
text: Mohanipur was a small coastal village by the Bay of Bengal near Puri in Odisha. People lived in thatched mud huts. They owned little pieces of farm land but less crops grew on it. They raised cows, goats and hens. One such family was that of Durga's, a girl of eight. Durga lived in a hut with her father, a fisherman, mother, grandfather, grandmother and a sibling younger to her. But the most devastating thing that disturbed the people of this coastal village was the annual cyclones that hit here. Come mid of May, the cyclones emerged from the sea and wrecked havoc in the lives of the villagers throughout the monsoon. It washed away beaches, uprooted trees, killed the livestock, flooded the crop land and destroyed the huts, leaving the villagers homeless. It is December now. Cyclone is most unexpected. But the villagers were startled when a man from the local panchayat came announcing, "Cyclone will hit in two days. Collect all your important things and move to the Cyclone Shelters as soon as possible. Cyclone will hit in two days..." Everyone drowned in despair. "These days we get warned two or three days in advance. Weather prediction is almost accurate. That can save a lot of life. In our days, no one knew when the cyclone would strike. We lost a lot of friends and family members due to these disasters. There were no Cyclone Shelters then. Saving lives during the cyclone and afterwards was at the mercy of God," said Durga's grandfather sounding positive. "Father is not back from the sea yet. Will he be able to get back by today? Does he know that it's getting dangerous in the sea?" worried Durga. Just then, Durga's father came back. Everyone heaved a sigh of relief. "I was scared for you, Baba!", Durga gasped. "We should gather all the important things, our cows and goats too, and move to a Cyclone Shelter". They stuffed essential things in a trunk and walked to the Cyclone Shelter with their cow and goats. There were more people who had come to take refuge. Everyone looked worried. The weather turned worse in day. It rained heavily. The storm gushed and roared outside. It was dark. The Cyclone continued for two days. After the Cyclone subsided, the families went back to the houses. There was dirty water all around. Trees laid on the ground. Huts were terribly damaged. The village was devastated. "We will have to build our hut again. But thankfully, we are all safe and alive," said Durga's mother.

We all only have one slogan in other villages to make them polythene-free - " Stop polythene, start a new life." "Because he was punished for lying." Papa reveals, “It is the time of King Dasharatha and Sita. Then the river was cursed to be the last. Since then the water of this river has gone under the ground. Out of curiosity, Pinky and Bablu reached the sandy ground of the beach. In the game, both of them started removing sand with their hands. Suddenly a stream of water came out. title: A River Without Water
text: Papa were preparing to go somewhere. Bablu and Pinky were surprised. Where were Mummy and Papa off to? When Pinky asked, Mummy replied, "We are going to Gaya, dear". On hearing this, both of them jumped with joy! The next day they reached Gaya by train. At Gaya, they stepped into the river near the Vishnupad Mandir. The water there was so shallow, that one could hardly bathe. Pinky and Bablu rolled with laughter. "Is this a river, or a pit?" "This is the beauty of this river, my son", said Papa. "This is the only river of its kind in Bihar. It is called Falgu. The speciality of this river is, it has hardly any water". "But there seems to be some water in it, Papa", said Pinky. "Right, because it is monsoon now. After that, during the rest of the year, the river dries up completely, and only sand can be seen. But if you scrape the sand, water comes out, because it is believed to be a cursed river", explained Papa. "Cursed river? But why?" asked both Pinky and Bablu together. "That was the punishment for telling lies" said Papa. "The story is from the times of King Dashrath and Sita. The water in the river would finish, it was cursed. From then, the water disappeared under the ground". Out of curiosity, Bablu and Pinky walked into the sand bed of the river. They began digging into the sand playfully. Suddenly water started flowing out. They began splashing water on each other. Mummy Papa called out to them, "Enough of fun, now come back". By now the kids were wet, playing with water. They enjoyed digging into the sand and seeing water come out!

title: When The Water Came
text: Madhepura was about to break, by then we had left. On the road to Bharrahi, there was an empty hand space to reach the water. When we came, my shoulders were filled with gusto. Stayed in Saharsa for a month. After that tents were installed, so they started living in tents. The corpse was being washed away from behind the house and not knowing how many people got washed away. Had bought 25 kg sawdust and 15 kg murry in the house. When we were going to Saharsa, the train started submerging halfway in Madhepura. Somehow the car was removed from there, then we came to Saharsa. When we were coming from home, then we were thinking that we will not be able to study but we saw that there is complete system here. Now we study very well that we can write properly in the exam. Children's ordeal At the age children should get a chance to play, read and write without any hindrance and understand the world around them, at that age the children of North Bihar have had to go through a terrible calamity like floods. In this, many children have lost their family members, have seen the animals of their house flowing in front of their eyes. All these harsh scenes are imprinted on his mind in some form or the other. It will take them time to forget them. And forgetting is not easy. Reading the thoughts of the children in this compilation, it clearly emerges that how much this sudden flood has struck the hearts of the children. The age in which children of other places are writing about flowers, butterflies, rivers and mountains, at the same age when children of North Bihar sit down to write, they cannot escape the scenes of flood tragedy. If the grown-up generations really have any duty to do towards this gentle generation, it is that when this generation grows up, it should never again have to face the crisis of flood in this form. The elder generation should take this decision today that they should do all the work in this area of ​​North Bihar with great patience so that the floods stop coming.
author: Ardhra Ajith

title: My Life During the Pandemic
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has impacted my life in different ways. I cannot go to school to have lessons in campus. I cannot play with my friends. I cannot go out and dine with my family. However, I can spend a lot of time with my sister, my mum and my dad. We have meals together. We read books together. We play together. title: Angry Fish
text: Rohan, Vihan and Tia met near the river. Tia was exhausted and horrified. Rohan asked' Why are you terrified Tia?" Tia said "All the fish are eating whosoever goes into water. My cat just escaped. " Vihan who was the younger but clever replied after thinking "I have a plan. Let us ask the fish why are they behaving like this?" Others agreed with little hesitation. They all went to the fish, called them using fishing rods and asked the matter. Fish said "People throw garbage in water. We are not able to live and breath. Our many friends have died. we will not spare anyone. Three friends assured them to solve the problem. They went back to their village and conveyed the message to the villagers. The villagers realized their mistake and promised to clean the river and never throw garbage again. Now the fish were happy and children played and had fun in the water. title: Ammu's Shapes
text: Ammu is at school. She is learning shapes. “Everything around has a shape,” says the teacher, “the tall buildings are rectangle in shape. The small windows in the buildings are sometimes square in shape.” “Teacher, the windows of my building are circle in shape!”, said Ammu. “Wonderful, Ammu! Can you find shapes in some more things around you, children?” “My tiffin box is oval,” said Amira. “My eraser has a star shape,” said Mintu. “Teacher, your earrings have two circles,” said Sonu. “Aha! Lovely! So we have so many different types of shapes all around us. Now here is what you must do once you go back home." Do you know what was the home assignment that the teacher gave? "Now all of you must go home and draw yourself using shapes,” said the teacher. Ammu happily went home and she quickly drew herself in her drawing book. Do you want to see how she looks? title: The story of a Black panther
text: I am Cubera, a black panther. I live in Dundera Forest. The Dundera forest has many cats, but there are no tigers and lions. When I was small my dream was to rule the whole Dundera forest. And when I grew up I followed my dream to rule this jungle. To achieve my dream, there was a big block in my way... it was a leopard. His name was Robic. His dream was also to rule this jungle. I heard an elephant talking about him and his strength. Robic was best in hunting and fighting. I was pretty scared. What can I do to beat him and rule the jungle? I am neither strong nor good in hunting. I even thought about just forgetting my dream. But then I thought even if he is stronger than me, I will fight him and see who is strong. So I tried to fight him.. but he defeated me and I lost one of my teeth. I was very sad. And I am sure that if he sees me again he will kill me. So now I'm scared to go out. Then I realized that, being a black panther, I become strong at night. But the problem is, if I challenged him at night he will defeat me. Because, he is also nocturnal like me. But I decided that I will never give up. I want to prove myself. So I started my mission to improve. First I will learn to hunt. But not in the day but at night. I started to go for hunting but I only got rabbits because of the howler monkeys, they are like the siren of the forest. So the first day was a flop. But then onwards I started to hunt howler monkeys, so that there will not make those siren noises. So the howler monkeys stopped howling and I improved in my hunting abilities. Now I am practicing to fight better than him. I started to fight with some monkeys and also some wild cats. They always defeated me. But then I began to study their moves of fighting and then copied it and started to fight with them with their own tricks. Finally, I think I am ready to fight with Robic. I thought the fight will be better at night. So I went to him at night and the moment he saw me he said " You scared little cat I told you that if I see you again, I am going to kill you" I got very angry I said "So kill me you leopordy" Robic said "ok so your wish" The fight started and He was getting weaker because of my attacks. And in between he climbed a tree and jumped at me, it was a terrible attack. It almost killed me. Now I getting weaker because of his attacks. But in pain, I accidently just slapped his face very hard that anyone could not bear it. He knocked out on the ground and his tooth came out. And.... finally... I won. Now I think the whole Dundera forest is mine. Now there are no blocks in my way to rule dundera forest. I am the King!!!!

title: Mummy and Baby Elephant
text: Deep in the forest, there lived a mummy elephant and a baby elephant. Together, they used to go to the lake to drink water. The mummy elephant loved its calf very much. One day, the mummy elephant was very tired and got up very late in the morning. The calf was very thirsty and went to drink water in the lake. When the mummy elephant got up, it could not find the baby elephant anywhere. She asked the giraffe and the zebra, "Where is my baby?" The giraffe and the zebra shook their head. They had not seen the baby elephant. The mummy elephant was very sad. Mummy elephant searched everywhere for its baby. It sat in one corner and started to cry. A rabbit which passed by asked the mummy elephant, "Why are you crying". Mummy elephant replied, "I don't know where my baby is, dear rabbit". The rabbit told the elephant, "Don't worry, I saw your baby playing near the lake. Come we will go and see her." The mummy elephant ran to the lake and found its baby playing there. She scolded her baby for leaving her and going to the lake alone. The baby elephant was very sad. "I am sorry mummy, I won't repeat hereafter", said the baby elephant. The mummy elephant hugged her baby and they happily went back to their home together.

title: The Book

"Bittu and I are making laddo! Your favourite!" Rani came and ate some laddoos. Just then her whole family swarmed around the laddoo box. "Did you find your book yet?" Her mother asked her. "not yet" Rani Said. Later that day, Her mother was busy harvesting grains. "What plant is this?" Rani asked her mother. "That is a book tree." Her mother said "A book tree?" Rani wondered. She couldn't sleep that night. She kept thinking about the book tree. She kept thinking and thinking and she even dreamt about it. Then one week later, it happened! It grew! It grew into a big tree! It had many books on it. And did you know what she found on that tree? Her favourite book! The End

title: The Lion And Rat
text: A Lion lay asleep in the forest, his great head resting on his paws. A timid little Mouse came upon him unexpectedly, and in her fright and haste to get away, ran across the Lion's nose. Roused from his nap, the Lion laid his huge paw angrily on the tiny creature to kill her. "Spare me!" begged the poor Mouse. "Please let me go and some day I will surely repay you." The Lion was much amused to think that a Mouse could ever help him. But he was generous and finally let the Mouse go. Some days later, while stalking his prey in the forest, the Lion was caught in the toils of a hunter's net. Unable to free himself, he filled the forest with his angry roaring. The Mouse knew the voice and quickly found the Lion struggling in the net. Running to one of the great ropes that bound him..

title: Bravo Burli! (A Play)
text: She dreams of the story.) Part 2 (It is morning. The sun has risen and the village people are setting out to go to the jungle for hunting and gathering fruits.) Mother: (shaking Burlimundi) Burlimundi wake up and eat your mandya jau quickly. We have to go to the jungle Burli: (awake) Mandya jau, yummy! Mother: I will go to wash the dishes in the stream. Burli: (licking her bowl clean, begins to clean the kitchen) I will help you. (Accidentally slips a matchbox in her pocket.) Scene 2 (Outside the jungle) Premsila: Hi! Priti and Pramila. Priti and Pramila: Hi! Premsila. (To Burlimundi in a mocking tone) Hi! Small girl. Burli: Good morning, I am not small. I have grown up now. (Everybody is plucking mangoes) Burli: (to her mother Premsila) When will I have my nose and ears pierced like yours and apply black paint on my face? Mother: It's a long way off. You'll wear ornaments when you are much older, not before that! And I will not let you pierce your face with needles to make black lines on your cheeks! (Angry, Burlimundi climbs up a mango tree and hides in its branches) Burli: Aya, where am I? Mother: Oh no! I cannot find my daughter. Maybe a tree spirit has carried her away. (Burlimundi jumps down from the tree) Women: (laughing) Ha ha ha... Look at her! (Burlimundi gets angry and runs towards the jungle.) Scene 3 (In the jungle) Burli: How angry I am. I am going far away from them all, into the jungle. My Abba comes here everyday. (Jungle sounds. Monkeys chattering, birds twittering, owls screaming) Tiger: ROAR Burli: My Abba tells me that the jungle is not a playground for a little girls. Tiger: ROAR (Burli turning around in bewilderment.) Tiger: ROAR Burli: What can it be? Is it thunder? Tiger: (appears in front of Burli) I am going to eat you up! Burli: (thinking deeply) I must chase away tiger. How can I frighten the tiger? Burli: (finding the matchbox in her pocket) How did this come here? This will save me! (Burli sets fire to a branch. It begins to burn wildly.) Tiger: (frightened by the fire) Should I eat her up? A skinny little girl! Why does my stomach feel queasy? Is it because I have devoured a monkey just a while back? (Burli gives a push to the burning bush. It moves towards the Tiger.) Tiger: Backing away… I am leaving this place. Scene 4 Part 1 (Burli comes running to her mother. She hugs her mother tightly) Burli: Oh Aya, I just met a tiger and he did not eat me up! Pramila and Priya: You are such a sweet little girl, Burli. Why would a tiger not eat you up? (Burli still in shock and fright) Burli: I don't know... Maybe because I knew how to light a fire? Pramila: Light a fire? Priya: That's not possible! Mother: (realising that something is wrong) Hush Pramila and Priya. Don't you dare make fun of my daughter. She is a brave girl who can certainly scare a tiger away. I am so proud of her! Part 2 (A little girl is lying on her grandmother’s lap) Little Girl: Where is Burlimundi now? Grandmother: Burlimundi is none other than your grandmother, my child, and she's sitting right in front of you! Little Girl: (amazed and hugging her grandmother tightly) You are surely the bravest grandmother in the whole wide world and I want to be as strong as you! (The little girl puts her head on the old woman lap and goes off to sleep once again) Written by: Arjun Bhillare Yogita Balu Bhillare Facilitated by: Nivedita Bedadur Characters Little Girl Grandmother Burlimundi Premsila Pramila Priya Tiger Narrator About the Story Nivedita Bedadur is a volunteer with Read-a-Story, an initiative that helps children from underprivileged communities become proficient in reading and speaking English. During the peak of the Covid-19 pandemic when schools all over the country were closed, she worked closely with four children – Yogita, Arjun, Vishesh, and Ashiyana – who live in remote areas in Maharashtra. Connected only by a mobile phone, Nivedita used to read storybooks to the children every week. Bravo Burli! is the story of Burli, a little girl from the Kondh tribe indigenous to Odisha, and her brave encounter with a tiger deep inside the forest. Although the children had read numerous stories over the six months, Burli’s story struck a chord. The children could see themselves represented in Burli, and were able to relate to her life and adventures. Yogita (aged 11) and Arjun (aged 14) in particular loved Bravo Burli! So when Nivedita proposed turning it into a play, they eagerly agreed. Although they had never written a play before, they were keen to learn and explore a new format of storytelling.
author: Arjun Bhillare; Nivedita Bedadur; Yogita Bhillare

title: Sringari srinivas becomes happy and then angry,angry then happy

title: My Play Time With Puppies
text: PLAY TIME WITH DOGS Woof woof!!! Do you like dogs? This story is about the dogs in my building. The main characters are Konichiwa, Daniel, Lucy, Milky, Hyna, Mango, Arigato and myself. It all started with one dog called Konichiwa who gave birth to six puppies. Five of the puppies were chocolate brown in colour and one puppy was golden in colour. He looked like a Golden Retriever! I was happy and also very excited and I wanted to see them immediately. I told Mumma “Mujhe dekhne jaana hai. Can I go now?“ But I was not allowed by my Mumma. She said that the puppies were too small and Konichiwa would bite me. When the puppies got a little bigger, I started to play with them every day. Then, one day I brought one of the puppies home. But my Mumma said, “We cannot keep him home as he is too small and he will miss his own Mumma.'' Suraj Bhaiya also discouraged me from taking him home. He said ''Aap ise mat leke jao, isse apni Mummy ke paas rehne do.” Then I kept him back. This made me very sad. Let me tell you about Suraj bhaiya! He is a dog walker. He walks many pet dogs in my building. Some of the dogs which Suraj Bhaiya walks are Eva, Whisky, Pablo, Joey, and Kash. Eva, Whisky and Kash are Labradors. Pablo is a Beagle and Joey is an Indie dog. One day when I went to play with them, one puppy slept in my lap. His name is Arigato. My building friends gave him this name. He is my favourite because he looks the cutest. He is chocolate brown in colour. Arigato plays with me. He runs after me. That day he was just not ready to get up. He wanted to sleep in my lap. I was feeling very happy. My Mumma clicked a picture of mine with him! Sometimes I also get in trouble with the dogs. Once, a dog called Mango tried to bite me and also caught my pants in his mouth. Then another day I found a dog called Lucy eating something. I snatched it from her mouth. She got angry and she bit my cheek. My Mumma got scared and she told me not to disturb the dogs when they are eating. Luckily nothing happened to me, so we didn't need to go to the doctor. I learnt that when the dogs get excited or angry they try to bite me. Now I know - Do not take things from a dog's mouth as it can get them angry. Also do not irritate them. Give them some space. Finally, I have learned to play with them. Now all the puppies have grown up! The puppy which was golden in colour has been adopted. I still go to play with them sometimes. It gives me joy!

title: What is Portmanteau?
text: Kanaga said to Martha, “Shall we go out for brunch?” Martha said, “Brunch. What is it? I’m hearing the word for the first time.” Kanaga said. “Brunch is food that we have between Breakfast and Lunch. Brunch is a combination of the words Breakfast and Lunch. Br eakfast + L unch is Brunch. Br from the word Breakfast joins with unch from the word Lunch to form brunch ” Martha, “Wow. I learnt a new word Brunch.” Kanaga said, “Such words are known as Portmanteau in English. Portmanteau is a combination of parts of different words. The word Smog is a portmanteau. It is a combination of Sm from the word Sm oke and og from the word f og.” Kanaga said, “Some more examples are Spork = Sp oon + F ork Emoticon = Emoti on + I con Chillax = Chill + Rel ax Email = E lectronic + Mail Sitcom = Sit uation + Com edy Frenemy = F riend + Enemy Motel = Mo torway + Ho tel.” Martha asked, “Is portmanteau always a combination of two words?” Kanga said, “No. Portmanteau can be derived from two or more words. For example, the name of the dish turducken is got from the combination of the words tur key+ duck +h en. This is because turducken is made with all these 3 birds.” Martha said, “Ok. I got some clarity about portmanteau. Let us go for brunch now."

title: Water Boy: The messanger send to save the universe
text: One bright sunny morning, a child was born. His name is Harry, he grew up in a small town in Moscow, and there lived a lot of people. The next day, in the morning 5:00AM they woke up to go on a walk near the building they were living at, after walking for sometime, Harry drank some water causing him to run faster. Then, Aaron asked Harry how many superpowers he has. Harry replied that he doesn't know and he told that he will check it out. The next day, Harry and Aaron went to a trip to U.K to live for a few days over there. They also had a pretty garden there. After taking a shower, Aaron told Harry that now they will check his powers. Aaron bought a book and noted down what all superpowers he had, Aaron noted that Harry had super speed, second Aaron asked Harry to fly, but he couldn't fly, second Aaron asked Harry to punch a hard rock and break it, when he tried to do so the rock broke into sand, then he asked Harry that if he could swim fast, but he was very tired and exhausted as it was night time. After bedtime, they went to a swimming pool where there were no people, after that Aaron asked Harry to swim fast, and Harry tried so hard that the water in the pool splashed everywhere, then Aaron told that he had to practice these powers everyday in order to be very powerful. After a few days, there was a boy named 'Lava Boy' and he was so rude to the society that he burned everything using his powers. When the news reached Harry, he was so sad and asked Aaron to help him to make a new suit. After three days, they finished making the suit, and Aaron had inserted some water in the suit, so that Harry could be recharged whenever he needed to. When Harry had gone to the 'Lava Boy', he laughed at him so bad that Harry felt angry, and he told that we can see who is stronger with a fight. After an incredible fight, Harry's water had became less, and Harry was so exhausted, so he thought of not wasting the water and fight him. As a result, 'Lava Boy' was very tired and ran very fast to get some rest, and when 'Lava Boy' had gone back, everyone asked Harry that what his name was, but Harry replied that he had not decided that yet, when Harry had gone to Aaron, Harry asked him to get some water, and Aaron ran fast and came back with some water, When Aaron had brought the water, when Harry drank it, Aaron brought some cotton to wipe Harry's blood off. After wiping the blood, Harry went to take a shower, and after doing that he felt energetic, so Harry asked Aaron to create a name for him. First Harry told, that that the name should be 'The Big Hero', but Aaron told that the name does not match him as he has powers related to water, so your name should be 'Water Boy', and Harry replied Wow! that's a very good name, then they both went to sleep. The next morning, Harry asked Aaron to make a 'Thief Finding Tracker' so that wherever a thief goes he can find him, then Harry told to Aaron to put more water on his suit. When Harry reached 'Lava Boy' he told that he will finish him today, then they both started fighting. After some time, they were very tired, so they again left and when Harry reached home, Harry told Aaron that he could not defeat him as he was so strong. Aaron replied that he should not depend on his superpowers and that you have to depend on yourself. The next day, Lava Boy came back and when Harry checked the tracker he suited up very fast and ran to fight Lava Boy. After some time, Water Boy's water was empty and he remembered what Aaron had told him and he kept on fighting Lava Boy, while one boy gave a bottle of water to Water Boy and with that water he blew it in front of Lava Boy causing him to melt and come back to human. After he melted the news reporters near him asked what his brave name was?. And Harry replied, my name is 'Water Boy' the messenger to save the world. title: Appu's Exam Fear
text: Appu is a very good boy. He listens to his parents, obeys his teachers and helps his friends. One day, Appu when came back home from school, he was a little upset. He did not tell anything when his mother asked him what happened. Nothing, mother. I am alright. In the evening, after finishing his studies, Appu went to his mother. Mamma, may I skip school tomorrow? I am feeling scared to go to school. Only for tomorrow, please. Mamma was surprised at this. Appu always loved going to school. He did not skip school even when the roads were flooded due to heavy rain. Why, Appu? Did you do something that you did not like at school today? In the evening, afterr finishing his studies, Appu went to his mother. No, Mother. It is just that I have an oral exam tomorrow. I have to stand in front of the whole class and answer the questions that my teacher asks. I am scared of doing it. What is scaring you in it? Not knowing the answer. If I do not know the answer to a question then I shall lose marks. You have worked very hard, dear. You will know all the answers. Just think a bit before answering. Yes, I have worked very hard. But what if I make a mistake in answering? My friends will laugh at me. To avoid mistakes, you must think properly before answering. I will not get the time to think, mother. In that case, do one thing. When your teacher asks you a question, request her- 'Ma'am, please may I think for a minute before answering?' That's exactly what Appu did the next day. He fared well in the exams too. So the next time you get scared of making mistakes anywhere, you know what you have to do.
