title: Who Did It?
text: "Catch!" Kimo shouted as he threw a small red ball towards his older brother. "Got it!" Akahi replied as he snatched it out of the air. The two boys had been playing on the beach for hours. Sand was stuck in-between their toes, and sea salt had crusted on their shoulders. "Go long!" Kimo ran down the beach as Akahi launched the ball with as much force as he could muster! The ball soared through the open air...and then disappeared into the trees. "Akahi!" Kimo groaned. He walked to edge of the tree line and peered into the cool darkness. An animal rustled the leaves, startling Kimo and making him jump backwards. "Akahi, will you come with me to get the ball, it's dark under all the trees!" Akahi jogged to join his brother at the edge of the beach. "Come on." He said, leading the way into the dense jungle. The boys crept through the trees looking for their ball. "Look! Over there in that hole!" Kimo exclaimed, pointing at the flash of bright red! Akahi pushed past the roots and vines and hopped into the shallow crater. Akahi paused and spun around with a look of confusion. "What's wrong? Are you stuck?" "No! Come down here and look at this!" Kimo crawled down and gasped. It wasn't a random pit at all. All around them were neatly perfectly stacked stones. "What is this?" Akahi asked. "Rocks." Akahi rolled his eyes at his brother. "I know that silly! I mean: why are they here like this?" Kimo looked a little closer at the stones. "These rocks kind of look like the sides of the old fish pond." "But this is a circle, and it's a lot smaller," Akahi commented. "Not a full circle," Kimo pointed. "It's not finished, there's a small gap over there. Why would someone start this and just stop?" "I'm not sure. Maybe Mama will know! Race you home!" The boys scrambled up the rocks and ran down the beach. Their feet kicking up sand behind them. Kimo ran as fast as he could, but he couldn't quite catch up to Akahi. "I win!" Akahi shouted as he passed the tree line. "But I'm getting faster, so next time I'll win," Kimo said confidently. Akahi smiled and ruffled his brothers hair as they walked over to Mama. "Mama! We saw something strange in the forest," Kimo said excitedly. "Hello to you too, sweet boy," Mama replied with a smile. "What did you see?" "It was a circle-" "Not a full circle!" Kimo interjected. "Right, it was an almost full circle of rocks around a pit in the ground," Akahi finished. "It looked like the sides of the fishpond, but someone just gave up before they finished it. I don't get why whoever built it just stopped." "Ah, I see!" Mama said, pulling Kimo onto her lap. "I know exactly who built it! The Menehune!" "Who?!" Both boys asked at the same time. "The Menehune! They're small, skilled builders, who only work late at night when the sun has gone to sleep." "If they're so skilled, why didn't they finish?" Akahi asked. "Well the Menehune are very secretive, that's why they only work at night, so if someone sees them, they disappear, and the project remains unfinished forever." "Whoa!" The brothers exclaimed gleefully. "Have you ever seen one?" Kimo asked. "No, but your Uncle Kehau always swore he saw a group of them on the far side of the island one night when he was out collecting opihi." "Cool, can we go look for one?!" Akahi pleaded. Mama chuckled softly, "Maybe when you're both older, but not tonight. Come, let's get ready to go to sleep. Where's your little red ball?" Kimo and Akahi looked at each other. "Oops!"
author: Kawai`ola Wong

title: Five Senses or More?
text: Humans have 5 main senses to know and feel the world around them. Sight to see the world through their eyes. People can see other people, nature, and objects around through sight. Smell different things like flowers and food through the nose. Taste different food with the tongue. Tastes like bitter, sweet, salty are felt through this sense. Hear different sounds, speech, and music with the ears. Touch felt through the skin. People are able to recognize a handshake, hug, or a slap through this sense. But, research shows that humans have more than 5 senses. There may be close to 33 senses on the whole. Let us look at a few more senses. Proprioception is how we know to touch our different body parts without actually looking. For example, you can touch your nose without seeing the mirror. Equilibrioception is our sense of balance. For example, we walk around without falling because of balance. Thermoception helps people to know if their surroundings are too hot or too cold. Chronoception is how we know that time is passing. Browse the internet to know the other senses we have and some senses that we don't have.

title: Malia in the Kitchen
text: Malia was a musician. She loved to make all kinds of music. She loved strumming her toy ukulele and singing into her giant green microphone! One day while Malia was making some music, her father called to her. "Malia, could you come to the kitchen please?" Malia carefully set down her instruments and walked down the hall. "Hi, sweetie! I was wondering if you wanted to help me make dinner tonight?" Malia thought for a second. "That sounds nice dad, but I'm already having so much fun making music," she explained. "Well the kitchen is full of music waiting to be made!" exclaimed Malia's father. "Come on! I'll show you!" Malia excitedly put on her apron and followed her dad. She loved to make music in fun new ways! "I keep my knife moving steadily so that I get even pieces of green onion and it makes a beat against the board." Thhhk-Thhhk-Thhhk-Thhhk Malia smiled and patted along to her dad's steady beat. Thhhk-Thhhk-Thhhk-Thhhk-Thhhk-Thhhk Dad dumped the chopped onions into the wok and mixed them in using a pair of chopsticks. Ding-Ding-Ding "It sounds like a little bell!" Malia said. "It sure does!" Dad agreed. Dad turned off the stove and bent down to grab a baking sheet. He held it flat and gently shook it. WEaoww-Ooh-Eeh-Oww "What a neat sound," Malia commented. She took out her shaker and shook along. WEaoww-Ooh-Eeh-Oww WEaoww-Ooh-Eeh-Oww Dad and Malia moved some wonton onto the baking sheet and brought them over to the stove. "These tongs make a great instrument," Dad said. Clack-Cl-Cla-Clack-Clack "How fun!" Malia clapped along to her dad's rhythm. Clack-Cl-Cla-Clack-Clack, Clack-Cl-Cla-Clack-Clack, Clack-Cl-Cla-Clack-Clack Once the oil was hot, Malia took a few steps back and Dad got ready to fry the wonton. "Listen to the bubbling," Dad suggested as he gently put in the first couple wonton. Trrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr "Ooooooh!" Malia blew air out of her lips to mimic the sound. P-B-P-B-P-B-P As the wonton were cooling, Dad quickly assembled a yummy salad. He grabbed a bag of croutons and gently shook it back-and-forth. Chh-chh-chh-chh Malia smiled and pressed her hands together. Chh-chh-chh-chh, Chh-chh-chh-chh Malia helped Dad take the food out to the table. Papa walked into the dining room just as Dad was carrying in the last plate of wonton. "Hi honey! Thanks for making dinner," Papa said as he quickly kissed Dad and took the plate from him. "Eeh! You're gonna catch each other's cooties!!!" Malia exclaimed. Dad and Papa smiled and sat down at the table. "So what are we having for dinner tonight?" Papa asked. Malia loudly answered "MUSIC!"

title: frogs and the snake
text: There lived a big snake near the pond in a forest. The pond was full of big and small frogs. The frogs were living happily under their king’s rule. The big snake became old and weak. He could not catch his prey easily and used to starve. One day, he thought of a plan upon seeing many frogs in the pond. He decided to trick the frogs in order to have meals. He went to the pond and lay there as if he was suffering from illness. A frog was passing by from there. On seeing the weak snake enquired the snake. He said that he had been cursed by a brahmin to serve the frogs of the pond as he had bit the son of the brahmin. So, he had to serve them and eat the food offered by them. Upon hearing the surprising words of the snake, the frog hurriedly went to the king frog and told everything to him. He said that the snake told him that he had been cursed by a brahmin so he would serve us and we need not be scared of him as he would eat the food offered by us. The king frog and the other frogs were delighted to hear this. The king frog and the other frogs cheerfully went to the big snake. The king frog asked the snake about the curse. Ones being assured by the snake that he would not harm the frogs, the king frog decided to take a ride on the snakes back. The king frog and the other frogs gathered around the snake and jumped on to the back of the snake to have a joyful ride. c. The snake swam in the pond with all the frogs riding on his back. The frogs were having a very enjoyable time. The snake was entertaining with all his mighty. The next day, they again craved for a joyful ride and readily hooped on the snakes back. Now, the snake knew that the time has come to fill his stomach with the delicious food riding on his back. The snake while moving around the pool deliberately slowed down his pace in order to show that he was tired. The king frog noticed this and asked him about the reason of his slow pace. The snake said that he had become weak due to starving and he could not move any more. In this way, every day, after the ride on the snakes back the king frog would let the snake eat the frog at the end of the tail. The snake then would quickly gulp it down. This continued for many days, till the snake had eaten all the frogs except the king frog himself, who seemed quite unaware of this fact. The very next day, the king frog uttered the same words after the ride. The snake turned around and saw that only the king frog was left on his back. He said to the king that now there were no frogs except you. He turned around and gulped the king in a trice. Moral: stay away from bad.

title: ONE AND ZERO
text: Once upon a time, there lived two best friends named- One and Zero. They both were very good friends. But something always made them quarrel. One-" Why did you eat my sandwich?" Zero- "I thought you ate mine." But they were very good friends... One day, One asked Zero that - "What makes you special?" Zero was thinking, after a few minutes, he said that- " Don't you know, that I come after every tens or hundreds to form many new digits". After that, Zero asked that - " What makes you so special?" One said - don't you know,that I am the only positive integer divisible by exactly one positive integer " Soon they were in a quarrel... One-" I am much more special than you." Zero- "NO...you are wrong...I am the best number... " And it goes on... Then Zero stopped and said - "Don't you think it is too late for quarrelling?" One too stopped and said - "Oh that's right, we are too late for quarrelling, aren't we? We better get home now. But I still say that you are wrong"...And in the very next morning... It all started again... Then, after a few minutes, One stopped and said-" Um... Zero, I think we should stop quarrelling with each other." Zero agreed and said -" Why don't we swap our jobs and try each other's work..". One appreciate... One- "Ok then... It's fine... I would think it is so easy to do that..." And soon that happened... Zero did One's job and One did Zero's... Soon after that, they had trouble doing each other's jobs... One asked Zero, " Is it easy to do mine?" Zero- " Yeah it's easy, what about you?" One- "Your's is supereasy." But it was not true, they both were making excuses to tell that they worked harder than each other... Soon they both realized that they were wrong...They need to say the truth to each other... One and Zero went to each other and said... One-" I'm sorry Zero, your job is harder...I think I did a bit of a showoff... Sorry..." Zero-" No worries mate, you don't need to apologise...I need to, your job is harder, not mine..." They both were happy and friends again... Moral: No one is bigger, No one is smaller, everyone are same if you look carefully...

Oh, Antsy Ant, you are just WOW! I certainly don't hate you now. Thank you Antsy Ant! Today I have learnt much, I hope we remain friends, always we’ll keep in touch! “It is the ant, not the lion, which the elephant fears.” ― Matshona Dhliwayo Take Aways 1. title: Ammu Understands Math
text: Ammu was a clever girl but slightly different. She could read and write well but always got her math calculations wrong. She loved the letters and words and stories, but numbers scared her. She could never understand how 1+1 came to 2. For her, 1 and 1 is always 11 because you put two ones next to each other with a plus in between which the teacher always said ‘and’. "I can never understand these numbers. If only they were simple like A for Apple and B for ball, I would have topped in math always and mother would have been happy," Ammu often thought sadly. One day, her parents took her to a dance class. She got interested looking at the different movements by the students in the class. She and her parents sat for some time watching other children dance. After some time, Malati, the teacher called out to her in a gentle voice, “Ammu, come. Let us both dance together.” Both Ammu and the teacher stood in the middle of the room. Then the teacher taught her to tap her feet saying ‘1-2….1-2’ and guided Ammu to follow her. Suddenly, it dawned! Ammu finally understood why 1+1=2 and not 11! It just meant one tap on right leg and one more tap on the right leg made two taps on the right leg! Thus, Ammu began learning, enjoying dance and understanding Math! Do you find it difficult to study something? Try to learn it by doing something that you really enjoy like Ammu.
author: Ira Periyavallur (aka Indira VMD)

title: I Am Unique
text: During their sport class, George laughs at Maya and tells her, "Hey Maya, it's that funny bushy hair you got, because of which you cannot see the ball coming. Ha ha ha!". Her other friends also look on and laugh. Maya angrily reacts and says, "George, stop it!". Maya is very upset about what happened in school. She keeps thinking of it and becomes angry and irritable. When her mother picks her up from school and takes her to the sweet shop, Maya ends up throwing a tantrum there. Her mother looks worried, but understands that something is upsetting Maya, which she is unable to express. Still upset with what happened in school, an idea strikes Maya's mind. "I am going to cut this bushy hair short, so that I can be like my other friends!". Upon seeing what Maya is about to do, her mother rushes to her and taking the scissors from her hand, tells her, "Maya, scissors are not for little children to play with." Little Maya begins to cry. Her mother gently asks her what's wrong. Maya tells her mother how her friends in school teased her about her bushy hair. She also tells her mother that she thought cutting it would solve the problem. Maya's mother comforts her and tells her she is unique and beautiful, just the way she is. "What does unique mean, Mummy?", Maya asks. Maya's mother takes her to the garden and shows her two feathers. She explains to Maya how the two feathers are completely different from each other. They have a different color, different shape, different size and also belong to different birds. She tells Maya how in spite of being different, both the feathers are beautiful in their own way. And that's what makes them unique. Mother then takes Maya to the mirror and tells her, "You see Maya, just like those two feathers, we are all different and beautiful in our own way. If anyone teases you about your hair, tell them how we are all unique, yet beautiful. And remember, every time you look into the mirror, say to yourself - I am unique and I am beautiful!". When Maya returns from the school the next day, she goes to the garden. She finds a parrot's feather fallen on the ground. She notices how different it is from the two feathers mother showed her yesterday. "This is unique!", she thinks to herself. The next day while playing in the garden, Maya notices a bulbul's feather fallen by its nest. She picks it and says to herself, "Wow, the bulbul has different feathers too. Mother was right, every feather is unique and beautiful!". Soon, going to the garden and looking for birds and their feathers becomes Maya's favourite pass time. And with each feather she picks, she says to herself, "I am unique and I am beautiful!". Each morning before going to school Maya and her mother also look into the mirror and repeat to themselves, "I am unique and I am beautiful!". And on days when her mother is busy, Maya happily does this by herself. Once again George once again makes fun of Maya's hair., while everyone laughs on. But this time, Maya doesn't get upset. Instead, she tells George that his hair is different from everyone else too. "Different?", asks George. "Yes George. Look, some of the hair on your head stands out from the rest". George looks worried. "But don't worry George, we are all different and unique in our own ways", replies Maya confidently. The other kids around also hear this. With joy and laughter, all the children in school celebrate being unique!
author: Monisha D'costa

title: Mixed Bag of Emotions
text: We display different emotions in a day that depend on the situations we face. Let us look at a few of the emotions and examples of when they arise. Roshi was happy and laughed with joy. Why? Because her uncle told a joke about farts and let out a loud fart. Deepthi was very sad. Why? Her grandfather passed away due to Covid-19. Now, she had no one who will buy her all that she asks for. Pranav was full of fear. Why? Pranav read a story about ghosts and slept. In the night, he got dreams about a giant ghost and got scared. Babu was angry. Why? Someone stole the hibiscus flowers from his garden again. Jacob was surprised. Why? He has seen only a single-decker bus. Now a double-decker bus was going in front of him. Vimal was disgusted. Why? His socks had a bad smell like dog pee on it. Prema was proud and had contempt for others. Why? She was the only female student riding a motorbike to her college. All the others came in a scooty. Banu was shy and hid behind the curtain. Why? She was feeling shy to come in front of the new visitors in her house

title: African animals
text: Alaba sat perched on hunter's rock, watching the pack of zebras curiously as they trotted pleasantly towards the giant lake. "Spread out," Jahzara hissed quietly. The five lionesses in the hunting party circled the zebras, then jumped forward to attack. Back in the territory where the pride of lions lived, Alaba proudly carried a zebra in her jaws. "I caught this all by myself," she told her father, the pride leader, proudly. Hakim barely even looked at Alaba; he was only interested in the food the lionesses had caught. "Why don't we ever get to eat first, if the lions don't hunt?" Alaba asked Jahzara. "Because the lions need to be fed and strong to defend the pride," Jahzara explained confidently. "Besides, it's been the way of the lion since forever. We shouldn't question our ancestors laws. Alaba watched as her father devoured an entire zebra. The only food left for the lionesses was some morcels of zebra that could barely feed Alaba, never mind the fully grown lionesses. The lionesses went to sleep hungry that night. Alaba stayed awake, staring at the stars. She crept away from the other lions and sat down on a large boulder. "Alaba? Why are you still awake?" asked a voice behind her. Alaba spun around, and found one of the other cubs, Hali. "oh, it's just you," Alaba said happily. Hali smiled. "Alaba? Can I ask you something? Do you think it's unfair that we do all the hunting, but the lions eat first and barely leave anything for us? Do you think it's unfair that sometimes lions kill lionesses cubs? I want to leave the pride, but... I want someone to come with me..." She glanced sheepishly at Alaba. "...You." Alaba grinned at her friend. "Of course I'll come with you. We should go now, while it's still dark." Alaba and Hali crept under the baobab tree where all the lions slept, then broke into a run, racing through the plains. Finally, when the two lionesses stopped, they rolled over, exhausted. They fell asleep curled up against each other. The next day, when Alaba and Hali awoke, Alaba smelt smoke and heard car horns bleating. Hali whispered to Alaba: "my mother told me of this place, Alaba. This is the territory of an animal that eats all other. It's the humans, Alaba." "I know." Hali bit her lip. "Alaba, I think we must go there to eat. No animal ventures this near to the village, and my legs are too exhausted from running; we can not walk back the way we came." Alaba sighed. "You're right. If we want to eat, we'll have to go to the Human village. End of book one; read more about Alaba and Hali's adventures in book 2!
author: Maelie Houston

title: Kamal's Musical Family
text: Kamal’s family was a musical family. His mother sang well. Kamal proudly told his friends, “My mom’s voice sounds like Shreya Ghosal’s singing.” His father played the violin. His father told, “I’m happy that I can play the violin. It is the queen of all musical instruments.” His sister played the piano. She has cleared the Grade 6 exam for Piano Players conducted by the Trinity College of London. Kamal played the tabla. His role model was the famous Indian tabla player Zakir Hussain. Kamal always said, “Look how enthusiastically Zakir plays the tabla.” There was a cultural program in their apartments. Kamal and his family decided to perform a song together. On the day of the program, they performed well and the audience clapped loudly. They also won a prize for best musical performance.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: FOLLOW YOUR HEART
text: Once upon a time, there was a girl named Rashi. She lived in a small village with her family. She was a studious child and loved going to school. Her village followed a strange tradition. When a girl turned ten she was supposed to put on some kind of jewelry to mark her culture. So her mother made her wear jewelry on her head and Rashi went to school. Rashi looked at the animals and thought why they don't have to follow such things. On the way to school, she met her friends Ram and Mira. Her friends saw her jewelry and asked her the reason to wear it. Rashi explained the reason behind it. They just laughed at it. When Rashi entered the classroom all the children started laughing as she looked different from the others. It became her routine to come to school in that way. Her jewelry kept increasing day by day. The Hindi teacher came and Rashi complained to her about the children's behavior towards her. The teacher scolded the children and told them to keep quiet as they were being rude to Rashi. She did not even listen what children have to say. It was time for the Art class. The art teacher entered the class and the children wished her politely. She told everybody that today we would portray something. Children were allowed to choose any person to sketch. Everybody was so excited. They loved art class and wanted to show their artistic skills. As Rashi was looking so different everyone wanted to draw her portrait. She happily agreed and sat on a chair and other children started drawing her portrait. Rashi looked at the portrait and was shocked to see her hands were cuffed with gold Bengals. It was made by Mira and Ram her best friends. The principal talked to Mira and Ram about what they did. They replied that we have drawn this sketch which shows that she is not the master of her own actions. She is forced to follow that culture which could be avoided at this age. She can't even handle that jewelry while studying and playing. The teacher also agreed and praised them for their thinking. Rashi also realized that she was not able to understand why she was not happy with all that. She removed all the jewelry and came back to her normal self. She thanked her friends and hugged each other. Other friends also joined them and started playing together happily. In the assembly, Rashi talked about being a super girl means we should always listen to our hearts. If we have a strong will we can convince others and live the life we want. She was praised for taking a great step to come out of an old tradition and live a normal life.
author: Mandeep Chhina

title: Wings and Tables
text: It is a bright sunny day. Ramya and Kiran are playing in the park. "Ramya I like this park very much. So many things to play", told Kiran. "Yes Kiran not only to play, also we can sit nearby the lake and enjoy Nature", replied Ramya. "Hey Kiran, see there! A flock of birds flying there", told Ramya. “Yes Akka.. It is very nice to see the wings moving up and down!”, replied Kiran. “Do you know how many wings are there in the flock?”, asked Ramya. “Akka, what a silly question! All birds have two wings", replied Kiran. “Oh, my intelligent brother! I asked how many total wings do you see in that flock of birds?”, told Ramya. “Hmm, let me count.. 1,2,3,4… oh they flew away.. How can I count now? Did you count Akka?”, asked Kiran Ramya told, “Yes, there were 14 wings altogether!” Kiran replied, “I think you are wrong, I saw only 7 birds!” Ramya told, “Yes, if there are 7 birds and each bird have 2 wings, then there are total of 14 wings! 2 multiplied by 7 is 14! Kiran replied, “Oh can we count like that? I know counting only by 1,2,3.." Ramya: “Do you think birds will stay still and wait till you count? Hee hee.." Kiran: “Akka, can you tell me how did you count so fast?” Ramya: “Yes, sure my little brother “ Ramya explained, "It is like this.." 1 bird has 2 wings 2 birds has 2+2 = 4 wings 3 birds has 2+2+2 = 6 wings So, for 4 birds, can you tell me how many times two is added?, asked Ramya Kiran shouted, "I have to add 2 wings, 4 times!" Ramya asked, “Yes and for 7 birds we need to add two.. “ Kiran replied, “7 times!" Ramya: “Yes, You got it right! When you add a number again and again, you can call that as multiplication. So if you add two 7 times, you can say, 2 multiply by 7. Kiran: “Ah, now I understood.. But how did you add two seven times so quickly?” Ramya: “I know the multiplication tables of 2 by memory, so I told it’s 14. Learning multiplication tables by memory will help you count quickly”. Kiran: “Super akka. This summer vacation I am also going to learn multiplication tables from …” Ramya: “Not me.. Not me..” Kiran: “It is you who told me this.. So you should teach and learn with me! ” Ramya: “Oho, I think I made a mistake telling you this trick!”
author: Vidhya Sriram
illustrator: Annada Menon; Gauri  Sirur; Parag Chitale; Vidhya Sriram

title: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys
text: Rahul the cap seller is walking to a far away Village. He was walking for a long time. He was so tired and it was hot that he decided to rest under a tree. He sat under a tree and started waving his cap so that it would make him cool. Rahul was so tired that he slept. He started dreaming of caps. The tree he was sleeping next to had a bunch of monkeys playing. The monkeys saw Rahul. They slowly swinged down without a noise. They were very curios what was inside the bag. So they thought that they could open the bag. When they opened the bag they found so many caps. So they thought that they could try them on. It looked good on them. They started to run here and there. Then they started to play with the caps. Rahul woke up and went near his bag wondering why it was open. He checked his bag and he was shocked!. There was nothing inside it. He look everywhere finally he found all the monkeys wearing his caps. Then the monkeys started copying Rahul. So he thought up of an idea that if he throwed his cap then monkeys will throw the cap. So he throwed his cap. Then the monkeys started to throw their cap. Now he was happy because he got all his cap back. But the monkeys were Angry

I hope you are clear with you doubt" the sun with ashamed face replied"sorry mr. Rooster. My misunderstanding towards you made me roast your people. I will not misunderstand at anyone anymore."the rooster made him understand not to misunderstand anyone without a proof or evidence.

title: Mr. Ball
text: A little girl was playing with Mr. Ball. Mr. Ball, however was bored of the girl and tried to escape. Wooosh! Mr. Ball went up and up and reached a terrace were delicious pappadams were being made. The girl climbed up the wall and started chasing Mr. Ball. Mr. Ball bounced and bounced, and reached a garden! A gardener tried to catch the ball but she failed. The little girl was horrified. She couldn't lose Mr. Ball, it was her favorite. Mr. Ball was enjoying his freedom. He would never ever return to the girl, never! Mr. Ball continued following the path in the park and the girl continued to chase him. ''Abracadabra come to me!'' yelled a witch who was trying to help the girl but she also failed. The girl was shocked. How would she be able to catch Mr. Ball? Now Mr. Ball couldn't see. He went here and there and finally stopped in a place where two tea sellers were sitting. title: Riya makes Biryani
text: Once upon a time there was a girl named Riya. She was a good girl. She helped her mother in her daily chores. And most of all she loved cooking. One day, there were guests coming for dinner to Riya's house. So, Riya asked her mother if she can help her make the dinner. She said "yes you can". Riya and her mother started making * biryani. Riya Accidently added a lot of spice. She did not know what to do so she started crying. * Biryani is a Indian dish. Her mother asked that what happened she told the whole incident. Riya's mother told it is ok Riya we can make it again but we just need someone to entertain the guests so that we can make the biryani in the mean time. Of course my friends can entertain the guests says Riya. Oh Riya what a wonderful idea please call them right now said her mother. title: My friend Cockroach
text: One windy spring noon, as dry leaves dropped out of the Avocado tree, I saw a cockroach right next to my feet! I took a photograph as I had my camera with me. The cockroach remained where it was. It did not seem scared for it stayed still even when I moved closer. I noticed it had one long antenna and one short antenna. As I watched, it shifted from side to side in the warm sunlight. "Oh my", I thought, "I'm going to find it hard to hit any cockroach from now on. This cockroach is behaving just like me! " I had been standing in the sun too. That's when Viji walked into the parking lot with a broom. She brought along a sack to collect the fallen leaves. I stepped away for a few moments to take a photograph and when I came back, the cockroach was missing! Could Viji have hit the cockroach and put it in her bag? I looked inside the bag. The bag was too full of leaves to spot the cockroach. Where was Viji? I looked around for her. Viji was sweeping at the far end of the parking lot and she swept the leaves towards me. " There was a cockroach there, Viji, have you seen it?", I asked, walking towards her. "No, Ma", she said. "Cockroaches are smart. When they see me coming they fly away. I didn't see any cockroach" Small piles of leaves were being swept towards me as she spoke and suddenly I saw something brown scurrying under two leaves. Sure enough, a closer look showed that Cockroach was there. His back was exposed to the world but his head was under the leaves. Cockroach stepped onto a leaf which I offered him and as Viji watched I lifted the leaf and left him out of harm's way. That was that, I thought, as I walked away. It was not so.... As I walked in the parking lot that night with Siddarth, a little black form scurried out in front of us and I nearly stepped on him. He stayed out there in the centre which was unusual for a cockroach. "Its Cockroach!", I exclaimed. Siddarth jumped back with a THUD. Cockroach tried to scurry away when he heard the THUD. He flipped over on his back and found himself helpless. A fresh green leaf came to his rescue and while he held onto it, he was deposited the right way up on the ground. "By Hades!", said Siddarth, walking away. Cockroach and I regarded each other... In the days that followed, this happened again... and again. I would head out for a walk, Cockroach would appear... we would stand together in companionable silence for a few minutes till I left. Then, one windy spring morning, as leaves and buds blew down out of the Avocado tree. I came across Cockroach. Something was not O.K! He was lying face down with his face pressed against the ground. His back seemed twisted and hurt. There was nothing I could do to help. As I watched, he moved a bit then became still. "He's gone Ma", said Viji, touching Cockroach. She had come by just then to start her sweeping. Then Viji picked him up and put him in her bag. This is a true story. Most of us like happy endings so I wondered whether to leave it at the meetings in the parking lot. Then I decided to share it just as it happened and let it be.
author: Deepa Iyer

title: THE LETTER

title: Wally the Wave
text: Wally was so cheerful during the day. He was so calm and quiet. The sun made Wally the Wave glisten. He sparkled bright and blue. Sometimes he took a spade. Sometimes he took a shoe. The children all jumped on Wally. They splished and splashed - splish splosh. They dipped their favourite toys in the water, giving them a squeaky clean wash. The ball hit Wally the Wave and Wally threw it right back. Wally just loved to play. He gave the ball a great big whack. As the sun set, people made their way back home. Wally looked around. Now he was all alone. Wally hunched his back and was very, very upset. “I hate being on my own,” Wally wept, and wept and wept. Then a big, gray cloud appeared. Wally looked up in despair. “It will pour down with rain,” Wally trembled, “Hello - is anyone there?” The rain made Wally angry. “I’ve had enough,” he cried. Wally pumped up with all his might and transformed into a giant tide. Wally the Wave grew and grew and became scary as can be. He wanted people to come back, so he could be a friendly wave in the sea. No one returned to see Wally, no matter how loud his roar. The angrier he felt, the bigger he got, bigger than ever before. Then all of a sudden, he saw the sunrise. The sun began talking to Wally, much to his surprise. The sun looked at Wally and said, “I understand that you are angry and want to play but at night people go home, so they can sleep tightly in their bed.” “This means time to stop playing Wally, it means time to rest your head.” Wally listened to the sun and decided not to scream and shout. Wally’s happy, cheery face made all the people come back out. Later that day, when night fell and everyone had gone home to sleep. Wally closed his eyes to rest and dream of the fun and games the morning would bring.
author: Riddhi  Jha

title: I Love My Planet
text: When I go shopping... I do not use plastic bags but I use cloth bags instead. I never litter. I put all my rubbish in the bin. I recycle and sort my rubbish into different bins. When I see other people littering... I remind them of the right thing to do. I always turn off the lights when I am the last person to leave the room. I do not overfill my plate, so I do not waste food. I try not to watch too much TV......and spend my time playing outside instead. I turn off the tap while brushing my teeth, to make sure I do not waste water. Water is precious. I remind my family and friends to re-use their bathwater to water the plants. I give away or exchange books and toys I do not need anymore. Instead of travelling by car, my family and I try to take the bus... or cycle... or walk. I save our trees by drawing on both sides of the paper. I plant herbs and flowers in the garden and help to keep our earth green... I water them to help them grow. I make my own colours from flowers and vegetables. We are the children of Gelsenkirchen! and this is how we love our planet.
author: Peter  Reichenbach

title: maloo kallo... and who?
text: Grandma said, "Maloo, lately we have heard strange noises from the garden. Keep the door closed." Soon Malo pulled out the binoculars from his spy bag and headed out into the garden. He scrutinized every plant, tree, and vine with his binoculars. While looking at it, suddenly there was a huge beehive on a tree in the corner of the garden. Malo ran over to Grandma and said, "Grandma, there are a lot of bees around the purple tree!" He said "Yeah Maloo, but I can't make a loud bang when I hear thousands of bees coming in. It must be a thief or a demon!" She said.. Malo grabbed a long stick and headed back towards the garden. Then, the bed of the grass fell to the nose and began to moan. "Kaloo, stop this rampart. Don't ruin the grass!" And that is what I heard. But Kalu was playing his tail out loud and hitting it. Malo drove off near Kaluna. There he saw some big footprints on the grass. Those were bear marks! "Bhesh kalu, trapped bhalu!" Caloo and Maloo Ran over to Grandma. "It's not a thief, not a pirate, not even a demon!," he said. "That's a bear eating a purple fruit, slapping honey!"

title: A RAINY DAY!!!
text: One day a girl named Kirta was cycling in a deep forest when her brother came and hugged her. After that her brother said, " Kirta, mom said that it is going to rain and gave me this raincoat and said to give it to you" Kirta replied, " Okay brother, thank you" After few hours Kirta cycled back home but it didn't rain. Okay brother, thank you. Kirta, mom said that it is going to rain and gave me this raincoat and said to give it to you. Next day the same thing happened... A few days past, And one day she said, "Mom please don't send raincoats to brother. It is not raining" "Okay, but carry this backpack with you," mother said. title: Taberelea's Life
text: A litter of three kittens were born. Taberelea the kitten, her Mom and her siblings moved into a cardboard box. Two weeks later, the kittens rolled out of their box and ran around the basement! The basement was kitten proof. The first kitten was Taberelea's brother, Molasses. Then, her sister, a yellow kitten named Belle. Lastly, Taberelea! One beautiful summer morning, Taberelea's Mom was going outside. Her tail got stuck in the door! Mom and the kittens all go to the vet for a check-up. Mom cat was there the whole day! The kittens were there for half a day. The kittens ate wet cat food for the first time. Taberelea's Mom got medicine and felt better but the kittens did not enjoy the car ride! One day, a strange blanket came into the house. It had the scent of Molasses and Belle's new owners on it and they were going to pick them up in a few weeks. Taberelea's owners knew Molasses and Belle's new owners! The kittens' new owners are Rebecca, Gillian and Christian. A couple weeks later, the new owners came to pick them up and the kittens went home in cat carriers. Belle was in the blue carrier and Molasses was in the pink carrier. Belle and Molasses went home with their new owners. A year later some weird things started to come into Taberelea's house. One day the mother owner had to leave. Taberelea did not know what was happening, the owner came back with some sort of creature! The creature started to pull her hair! Taberelea lived happily ever after... Until baby Henry came along! The end.

title: The Case Of The Missing Puppies
text: One pleasant morning, I woke up with a fright. I felt a cold tap on my shoulder. I saw my cousin brother, Watson Bones, standing beside me. “Are you kidding me? It’s six in the morning!’, I screamed at him. Watson replied, ”Happy birthday, Broownie Wownie." Anyway, today is my birthday. Oops, I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Brownie and I am Butterscotch Anderson's brother. I call him Buttercup. I am the the head of the team, The Tantrum Ten. It is a team in which all of my friends solve cases. We all have different personalities but similar ideas. My buddies, my co-detectives, are the two rabbits, Tutti and Frutti, the two Shih Tzus, Buttercup and I, the two yellow - white Labradors, Bruno and Buddy, the two Goldfish, Goldie and Ginger, and the tortoise, Boondi. We live in a small animal shelter in California. It is called Just Animals. Our owner, McCallister, bought a Jack Russel Terrier, Oscar, today. Right after he joined us, Oscar made Butterscotch uncomfortable by eating from his bowl and sleeping on his bed. The day Oscar arrived, we all got together to celebrate the newest addition to our family. We sang, danced and ran around. Minutes later, two puppies were found to be missing by their parents, who were crying. N othing affected Oscar. He never reacts if a cat runs by. That day, I saw him chasing an old tiger. This is quite unlike a dog. From the time I sniffed him, I felt there was something strange about him. At 8pm, on the day Oscar arrived, I saw him with blood - stained teeth and tiger skin. This is when I got super curious about him and to know what he was he up to. I Immediately informed my friends. I had an idea. Our owner had bought this super device that was attached to my collar. Using that, the owner and I could understand each other. The way it worked was simple: Whatever I would say, in my language, which they described as a ‘bark’, the same somehow got communicated to the owner on a box - kind of thing that stayed with him and his family. They call the box a ‘phone’. So I said, "Master, we are feeling very hot! Please come and remove our fur”. Before you could say, 'Brownie is Brave', Mr McCalllister was there. Oscar suddenly started howling at the moon. Our Master first went to Oscar and started removing his fur. Soon, all the dog's fur came out from his body and we saw a wolf standing before us. Suddenly, the wolf started making strange sounds, as if it was in panic. My other friend, Everest, who is a Pomsky, a breed that is a mix of Husky and Pomeranian, translated everything the wolf said. She could do this as she is part Husky and so is related to the wolves. It turns out that the wolf was saying, ”I had put on a dead Jack Russel Terrier’s skin. I will never trouble anyone in my life again”. But we didn’t feel pity for him at all. Would you? He had killed the two puppies, who were dear to us, the day he joined us. We immediately called the Animal Rescue Service that took him away. Once again, we saved the day for ourselves. To celebrate, we had Vanilla ice cream with banana slices on top. The owner's son, Brian, gave us lots of love and treats. He threw a party for us. We were happy that night, again.

title: A Balanced Nutrition
text: I team, Tarique Aziz, Yuwak Shrestha Translator: Isabel Ramirez There are many types of food in the world, such as fruits and vegetables of all colors. It is very important that boys and girls like you eat varieties of food. It is very important that you eat many varieties of vegetables. Each vegetable has a benefit to your nutrition. An example is a spinach. Spinach has many vitamins and has minerals such as iron and magnesium. Potatoes have benefits for the body such as fiber and potassium. Potatoes also lower the risk of heart disease. Do you know how to say potatoes in Spain? Patatas! Carrots are high in fiber and are a source of potassium and antioxidants. Potassium is very good for you because it lowers the risk of a stroke and high blood pressure. Carrots are also very good for the eyes. Also, apples are a fruit. They are also sources of antioxidants and fiber, similar to carrots. Apples can reduce the risk of cancer and diabetes. Bananas are one of the fruits with the most benefits. They give you vitamins, potassium, and magnesium. They are also very good for your skin and your heart. In addition to this, they are good for your digestion and give you a lot of energy. Watermelons are great for eating after exercising or playing sports, because watermelons can help with your hydration. Watermelons have 92 percent water. Rice and the other grains are also very important to eat. These meals help you feel full faster, especially brown rice. At the same time, you can eat meat and dairy. You don't need to eat as much because with more fruits and vegetables your diet will be healthier. A balanced nutrition is very simple and fun to maintain a healthy body and mind. Having a healthy body and mind is very important in life, because it will help you live a longer and healthier life. Discussion Questions: What are the benefits of vegetables? What is your favorite vegetable or fruit? What are the benefits of fruits? What defines good nutrition? What foods do you like to eat? Discussion Questions: What special dishes does your family make? Do you think you have a balanced nutrition? What dishes do you know how to prepare? Do you think Guatemalan food is healthy? What types of foods are unhealthy?
author: Isabel Ramirez

title: The Mango Tree
text: We love going to Grandmother's village! In Granny's garden stands a big mango tree. So many birds come and perch on it. I like hiding on this tree. Nobody can find me here. Dad searches for me near the well, and Mom searches near the cowshed. However, none of them find me. Oh no! Granny's dog has found me. Now I must climb down. Granny hugs me tightly.

title: Deal and Distribute
text: It is a bright sunny day. Rani and Kavin are going to school by walk. Manju, the Math mam told, "Rani and Kavin, Can you help me to distribute notebooks to your friends?" Both nodded and replied: "Okay Mam!" It's Math Class.. Kavin told, "I want to distribute more books" Rani told, "No, that's not fair. Let us take turns each other, and give two books for each turn." " That's a good deal!" After distributing the books Manju mam asked, "How many books did you distribute altogether?" Kavin told, "Oh mam, I didn't count that" Rani shouted, "I got 5 turns and gave 2 books in each turn. So that means I distributed 10 books. I think Kavin should also have distributed 10 books because we took turns and gave away equally. So 10 + 10 = 20. It should be 20 books altogether, mam." Kavin and Mam told "Yes, that's a good way to count" Kavin asked, "What if we have 21 books?" Rani replied, "It's simple, 21 is an odd number so we cannot divide equally between two persons. So Mam can give that one book!" "Oh super, that's a good strategy!" Both of them are happy that they got an equal chance. And they learnt some Math also.
author: Meera Sriram

title: The Frog's Starry Wish
text: She wanted to jump up to the sky and touch them all. Then one night, she decided to do something to reach them! She climbed a large rock and got a little closer to the stars. But they were still out of her reach. The stars were SO far away! Then, she climbed a taller mound. She stretched out her hands, but the stars were still out of her reach. Then Rana saw a very tall coconut tree and thought: Ah, this will work! She began to climb the tree with great difficulty. She stretched out her hands... but the stars were still out of her reach. Rana was disappointed. She looked down and her heart skipped a beat in fear. She put a hand to her heart and said to herself, "I won't be afraid. I can do it!" ﻿ Then, Rana looked down again and could see a pond. The stars were shining in the water. She saw the stars and rejoiced. Then she dove into the pond. The closer she got to the pond, the closer she seemed to get to the stars. SPLASH! Rana plunged into the water. Then she got out of the pond and sat on the bank. She sat and observed the stars shine in the pond.
author: Sumaiyah Hossain

title: Who Stole Bhaiya's Smile?
text: They explored caverns under the stairs and fought the aliens in the mango tree in the courtyard. Bhaiya always made Chiru laugh. "Mangostruosa is from Mars and has come to destroy your house. Ha, ha, ha!" roared Bhaiya. "Aaah! I'm going to catch and eat Mangostruosa! Ha, ha, ha!" said Chiru. But it's been a while since Chiru and Bhaiya have played together. Bhaiya doesn't feel like playing with anyone these days! "Why don't you want to play?!" Chiru shouts at Bhaiya. "Because I don't," Bhaiya replies. I have a giant monster stuck to my back. Chiru calls the monster Dukduk. "Dukduk must mean cruel and grumpy," thinks Chiru. "He seems to have swallowed Bhaiya's smile." It seems like Bhaiya is always with Dukduk. "Tell your monster to go away! I don't like him," says Chiru. Sometimes Dukduk grows bigger than a truck. Bhaiya gets furious about everything when that happens. He even chews his food angrily! Mom thinks she knows what to do to make Bhaiya feel better. "You should go for a walk. The fresh air will do you good," Mom says. Other days it seems that Dukduk won't let go of Bhaiya. He won't even let him get out of bed. Dad doesn't stop asking Bhaiya about his bad mood and asks him to fix it. "What's wrong with you? Why don't you eat?" Dad asks. "With a good meal, your problems will disappear." There are days when Dukduk shrinks and floats like a kite. Then, Bhaiya gets out of bed and plays with Chiru. But he gets tired very quickly. Yayo and Yaya ask Bhaiya what is wrong. "Oh, you kids and your problems. In my time we were stronger," says Yayo. "You get too distracted," Yaya points out. "It's all in your head. You just have to want it and you'll snap out of it," they all say. "I'll try," Bhaiya replies, "but it's not that easy." Chiru tries to distract Bhaiya. "Look at my new book, Bhaiya! Don't you think the pictures are lovely?" says Chiru. "They're not bad, Chiru," Bhaiya replies. "Bhaiya, have you seen my new toy train?" shouts Chiru. "Aha, very cool," says Bhaiya. "Mangostruosa has arrived! Run, Bhaiya," cries Chiru. "Not now, Chiru. I don't feel like playing," says Bhaiya. "Dukduk makes you feel sad and angry," thinks Chiru. She throws a pillow at Dukduk. "Take that, you horrible monster! Get away from Bhaiya. Give him his smile back." Today is Bhaiya's birthday. Chiru has prepared a cake for him. "Thank you, Chiru," says Bhaiya, smiling. Chiru frowns. Bhaiya's smile is very different these days. Chiru sits next to Bhaiya. "Does your new friend make you sad?" Bhaiya nods. "I want to be happy, but most days it takes a lot of effort," Bhaiya explains. "How long do you think your friend will stay?" asks Chiru. "I don't know," says Bhaiya. "Don't worry," responds Chiru. "We can play whenever you feel like it." Bhaiya smiles with his old smile. Dukduk grows smaller. Now, even Dr. Tita helps Bhaiya. Dukduk is still there. Some days, it's big. Chiru waits for those days to pass. In general, when Dukduk is small, Bhaiya likes to play. Dukduk = depression When you break your arm or have a cough, you take medicine to feel better. The brain, like any other organ, can also get hurt and may need help to heal. Sometimes we are sad. We cry, we get moody, and we get angry, but the bad mood passes, and we feel better. It is normal to feel sad. Sadness stays with some of us for a long time. The brain helps us think, act and feel. When we are sad all the time, it changes our behavior. We don't feel like doing anything. It makes us feel that we are not wanted. It feels like there is a big monster with you. It even seems like the monster will never go away. This monster is called depression. When you see someone is sad for no reason, talk to them. Tell them you may not understand how they feel, but you know it's hard and you'd like to help. If you feel this way, tell your family and friends. It may also help to talk to someone like a psychiatrist or psychologist.
author: Sumaiyah Hossain

title: The Harmony Bridge!
text: Josana Marak are neighbors and best friends. One day, Josana showed Maria a belt that she had spent days working on. "I made it for my mother. What do you think?" Josana asked enthusiastically. "I don't think that she will ever use it. I would never use it," Mary responded. Josana got up and left. The next morning, Maria waited for Josana. They walked to school together every day. But Josana had left without her. For lunch, Maria had brought dry fish curry which Josana loved. But Josana ate with Carolina instead. That afternoon, Maria waited for Josana at home. She wanted to play with the toy cars they had built together with her father. But Josana didn't come. Maria looked at all the things that she had built with Josana in the patio: the flute, the birdhouse and the railroad. She left her cars aside. She threw two thick bamboo poles and put one next to the other. She placed a thinner pole in between the two and tied them, just how she had seen her father do. She tied the other pole the same way, in opposite direction. She placed a lot of smaller poles one after the other and tied each one. She then dusted her hands off and looked to see what she had built. A long and messy rectangle! Josana would have enjoyed the construction of this, Maria thought. Maria tried to lift the rectangle and place it over her shoulders. She stumbled... She tried it again. This time it was much easier. "Where to?" Samuel, her older brother, asked. "To Josanna's," Maria responded. Josana was there, in her usual spot. Maria climbed up to a nearby tree by Josana. "Leave!" Josana said, furrowing her brow. Samuel went up and sat next to Maria. He gave Maria a rope to hold and held onto one himself. Samuel and Maria took a deep breath and lifted the rectangle with all their strength. CRRREAK... CRRREAK!... Oomph...! After, they made it lay down between them. When Maria arrived on the other side, Josana was still furrowing her brows. Her eyes looked over from Maria to the rectangle and over to Maria again. "Do you think we can build a train to run on this?," Josana asked with a smile. From here to there Maria constructed a small bridge to reach her friend Josana. If her bridge was firm on both sides of the tree, this will convert into a beam bridge. A beam bridge is the simplest type of bridge to build. These bridges can be grand, made with steel or concrete, or they can be small, made of wood and stones. Have you ever seen a beam bridge?
author: Daisy Sandoval

title: Avni and the Vacation
text: It was a beautiful morning in Gangtok, Sikkim. Avni and her family had arrived there the previous night for their yearly vacation with her parents’ college friends. Avni and her sister, Mira, were so excited that both of them got up earlier than usual. They ran to their room’s balcony to look at the mountains. They looked so white and beautiful. Their mother had said it was the highest mountain in India. But Avni couldn’t remember the name. Mira said ‘I think it was Kan..Kan..chenJungaa’ They both giggled. The name sounded a little funny. The girls woke their parents up and then ran out of their rooms to meet all the other children, who had arrived late the previous night. The hotel corridor was already buzzing with all their other friends running around and talking to each other. Mira ran and joined everyone. Avni, who was the youngest amongst them all, stood quietly watching everyone, trying to recollect all their names. There were Krish and Sammi, who were brothers. Then there were Tani and Shivi, who were Mira’s best friends. These four had arrived from Mumbai the previous night. Ayaan and Aanya were siblings and they had flown in from Singapore. They had all named themselves the TAMASAKS, using the first alphabet of all the eight children. The TAMASAKS met only once a year, but they had such a blast during their trips that all of them looked forward to these trips the rest of the year. All day, the kids played board games, football, hide-and-seek and exchanged stories from the last year. In the evening, all the families decided to head out for a walk on the Mall Road. Avni expected to see a Mall like she usually did back home. But this was just a road with shops on either side and benches in the middle. What is so great about this Mall? It doesn’t even have a play area, Avni thought. There were tea shops, small stalls selling maggi and momos, shops selling sweaters, shawls and other Sikkimese things. All the parents walked ahead of them, going in and out of the shops, chatting with each other and buying interesting souvenirs. The TAMASAKS walked behind playing rock-paper-scissors and sharing chips and biscuits that they had all packed in their backpacks. The older kids were talking animatedly about the Harry Potter movie they had all seen together the last time. Avni’s parents had not let her watch Harry Potter and now she started to feel left out. Just then, she heard a yelp. It sounded like someone was in pain. She looked around. It came from a thin, brown dog who was being shooed away from a restaurant. A man was throwing stones at the poor dog. Avni’s eyes went wide and her hand flew to her chest. She ran forward to help the dog. How could anyone throw anything at a sweet creature like that? The dog looked really hungry. She called out to the dog and held out some bread, which was in her backpack. The dog came running and ate some bread from her hand. Avni had a wide smile as she looked at the dog and patted his head. ‘Don’t worry, Brownie. You can walk with me now. No one will hurt you then’ she said. When Brownie finished the bread, Avni stood up saying ‘Mira, look at my new ffri..…’ and there was no one around her. She looked this way and that and couldn’t spot anyone from the TAMASAKS or the parents of the TAMASAKS. Avni’s heart started to beat really fast. Where did everyone go? Suddenly the people around started looked like giants to her. She now knew she shouldn’t have stepped away from the group without telling them. What could she possibly do now? Would they realize she was missing? She pulled her jacket more tightly around her, wondering what to do. She climbed up on the benches to try and spot her family from far. But it was difficult to see anything because there were so many people and all of them were wearing similar jackets and sweaters. Avni’s lips trembled. She bit her lip and tried to recall her parent’s instructions long back, on what to do if they were lost. She faintly recalled something about shouting out her parent’s full names. She walked around the shops shouting ‘Raaaaman Venkat’ and ‘Prreeeeyaa Jaaaaiiinn’. A few people turned and looked at her but her voice was mostly lost in the crowd. Brownie did not leave her side. He could sense that Avni was worried and kept nuzzling his head against her. Avni should have listened more carefully to the instructions. Maybe she could go back to the hotel? But what was the name of the hotel? Avni remembered Krish and Ayaan making up a silly song about their hotel name. ‘Soo Maa Sooo Maa Ya ya ya’, they had sung. She climbed up on the bench again, looking around for a hotel named SooMaaYaa, but couldn’t see any building with that name. Avni started to sweat now. The smell of Maggi and Momos floated by from the nearby restaurant. Avni’s stomach started growling. She took out some biscuits from her backpack, gave some to Brownie and ate some herself. Brownie was jumping around her, going in circles. He was happy to be getting all the love. Avni knew her mother’s mobile number and wanted to call her. She was scared to talk to strangers but she saw a mother with a cute baby on the bench next to hers. She asked the nice lady softly, ‘I think I am lost. Can you call my mother?’. The nice lady looked worried and immediately called on the number that Avni recited. But her mother’s phone was switched off! The nice lady asked Avni to sit and wait next to her. Avni finally remembered that her mom would keep repeating. ‘If you get lost, just stay where you are.We will come and get you’ She sat down, her shoulders slumped, resting one palm on her cheek and the other petting Brownie. She didn’t know how long it was before she heard a familiar voice. ‘There she is Mom..Look! With that brown dog..and she isn’t crying too’ It was Mira’s voice. Avni’s heart leapt as she saw her sister and her parents. Her mother, father and Mira, all three hugged her real tight and didn’t want to let go. Her parents kept saying ‘Sorryyy Baby’ and ‘Thank God!’ She noticed there were some tears in her mother’s eyes. She looked up at her and said ‘Don’t cry Maa..I remembered what you said. You asked me to stay where I was and I knew you were coming to get me’ Soon everyone reached where they were and took turns hugging Avni. She felt like a mini celebrity.
author: Charulatha C

title: Frog and snake
text: One day, a snake was wandering around the forest, looking for friends. He was grumpy and angry because he had been searching since 2 hours. Then, he found a frog. He asked him, "Hi Mr. Frog! Do you want to be my friend?" Frog replied, "Yes of course! Why not!" Then, they both planned to meet for dinner. Then, they had dinner. But, suddenly they both had an argument. Snake said, " We are best friends! Why is the monkey interfering in between of us two? The frog's mom was watching all this. Frog replied, " Hey snake, you see, monkey and you are my friend. You and monkey are my best friends! If not, I'll take you to the monkey and you have a talk with 3 of us. (Monkey, Frog and snake) Next, the frog took the snake to the monkey. The snake asked, " Hey monkey! are you this frog's friend?" The monkey said, " Yea I am." Then the snake became sad. Then, the frog and snake got surrounded by Mongoose. The snake showed them his teeth so they'd get scared. But they didn't. The frog said, "Oh no! We're surrounded by Moongoose! What do we do?" The snake replied, " I have no idea! Oh no! They're about to kill us!" The monkey was watching all this. As they were about to get eaten- The monkey saved them! Snake says, "I'm Sorry Mr. Monkey! I judged you a lot! I'm so sorry about that!" Monkey replied," It's ok!" Then frog said, " Let's three be friends!" Snake said, " Hmm... Not a bad idea!" Monkey said, " Ok, But on one condition." Frog asked," What?" Monkey replied, " We all have to be grinned in a mixer. LOL! Hahahaaa" Frog says, " Hahhahahha" Snake also laughs and they all become friends. Moral- Never judge others and teamwork always helps.;)
author: Dhriti Khaitan
illustrator: Jane Taylor; Rohit Bhasi; Ruchi Shah

title: Am I Special?
text: Little Bird was not very happy. He was tired of his nest, and tired of eating worms. "I don't want to be a bird anymore," Little Bird told Mother. "Birds aren't special." "What will you be instead?" asked Mother. "Which animal is the most special?" asked Little Bird. "Let's go find out," suggested Mother. "Mr. Dog, what makes you special?" asked Little Bird. "My wagging tail makes me special," said Mr. Dog. "It always shows when I am happy." First they visited Mr. Dog. "Miss Cat, what makes you so special?" asked Little Bird. "My whiskers are special," said Miss Cat. "They give me the balance to land on my feet." Next, they visited Miss Cat. "Miss Pig, what makes you so special?" asked Little Bird. "My home makes me special," said Miss Pig. "I get to play in the mud all day!" Then they visited Miss Pig. Little Bird was surprised to see another bird flying towards them. "Mr. Bird, what makes you so special?" Little Bird asked. "My wings make me special," said Mr. Bird. "They let me fly and see the world!" "There's one more visit we need to make," said Mother. "Especially you!" said Mr. Bird. Little Bird looked down from the sky and saw all the animals on the farm. "We're all special!" he said. And he felt happy. "Every animal is special, Little Bird," said Mother.
author: Gabby S

title: The Crow And The Lazy Snake
text: Once upon a time, there lived a crow and his wife on a banyan tree. The crow's name was Kaka and his wife's name was Kiki. A snake named Hissy also lived in a hole near that banyan tree. One day, Kiki hatched some eggs. When both of them have gone out for food, Hissy crept slowly on the banyan tree and ate all the eggs. And when Kaka and Kiki returned home, they saw their empty nest and realized that Hissy ate them. They cried very much that day. The next day again when Kiki hatched eggs, Hissy ate them also. This went on for many days. One day when Kiki hatched eggs, only Kiki went to bring food and Kaka stayed at home with the fear that Hissy will again eat the eggs. Then suddenly Kaka saw his friend, the fox. Its name was fizzy. Kaka flew to Fizzy and narrated the whole story. Then Fizzy gave him an idea, "Kaka see, there is a is a palace over there. There lives a queen in that palace and before bathing, she keeps her most costly diamond necklace beside the tank. Today when she will go to bath, she will keep her necklace in the same place where she keeps it everyday. You will go and steal her necklace and the guards will run behind you. After you will reach this banyan tree, drop this necklace in front of Hissy's hole and it will come out by hearing the sound of the necklace. The guards will come there and kill the snake to take the necklace. and your eggs will be saved. Then Fizzy went away. Just then, Kiki came and asked "Are our eggs okay?" Kaka said to her "Yes dear, and from now on, we will live happily" hearing this Kiki said "What! But how?" then Kaka told her the whole plan. Then they just done according to the plan and the snake died. And afterwards Kaka and Kiki lived happily and has so many kids. Moral: Intelligence is more powerful than strength.

title: Giggy Gets Friends
text: Giggy, the giraffe was new to the forest. His home forest had been destroyed by fire and he had run to this new forest. But Giggy was sad because none of the other animals here liked him. They had never seen such a tall animal before. One day, Giggy, saw a bear trying to get something from the top of a tree. "Can I help you?", Giggy asked. "Can't you see I'm trying to get that honeycomb?", the bear replied angrily. But, sadly, he lost grip and fell down. Giggy, with his long neck, was easily able to get the honeycomb. He took it and gave it to the bear. The bear was very happy to get the honey. He requested Giggy's help to get honeycombs from other branches as well. Giggy obliged. Soon Bombu, the bear, and Giggy became friends. Bombu, then, introduced Giggy to his other friends. Soon, Giggy had a lot of friends in the new forest. Nobody was scared of him now. Making friends starts by helping others!

title: A Tale of Potatoes
text: Once a junior school teacher asked her students to bring some potatoes in a bag. Each potato will be given a name of the person whom that child hates. Like this, the number of potatoes will be equal to the number of persons they hate. On a decided day the children brought their potatoes. Some had two, some had three and some had even five potatoes. The teacher said they have to carry these potatoes with them everywhere they go for a week. As the days passed the children started to complain about the stench that started coming from these potatoes. Also some students who had many potatoes complained that it was very heavy to carry them all around. The children got rid of this assignment after a week. The teacher asked, "How did you feel in this one week?" The children discussed their problems about the smell and weight. Then the teacher said, "This situation is very similar to what you carry in your heart when you don't like some people. This hatred makes your heart unhealthy and you carry that hatred in your heart everywhere you go. If you can not bear the smell of spoiled potatoes for a week, imagine the impact of this hatred that you carry through out your life, in your heart?" The Moral: We need to regularly clean the unwanted weeds that we grow. We must learn to forgive those who have not behaved with us as expected. We must forget the bad things. This would keep our mind more open and the cup will always have room for more good.
author: Rishi Vohra
illustrator: Greystroke; Jemma Jose; Phạm  Thu Thùy; Pia Meenakshi; ROSH; Ruchi Shah; Students of  Himalayan Public School

title: Tiger and the Fox
text: One day he watched the fox while hiding behind a tree. A tiger was approaching the area where the fox lived. The tiger had fresh game in its claws. Lying down on the ground, it ate its fill, leaving the rest for the fox. Again the next day the great Provider sent provisions to the fox by this same tiger. The man began to think: "If this fox is taken care of in this mysterious way, its food sent by some unseen Higher Power, why don't I just rest in a corner and have my daily meal provided for me?" Because he had a lot of faith, he let the days pass, waiting for food. Nothing happened. He became very weak. One day close to losing consciousness, he heard a voice: "O' My dear child, you are mistaken, see now the Truth! You should have followed the example of that tiger instead of imitating the disabled fox." 'I made you a Tiger, not a Fox..'

title: How Night Came to Opio's Village
text: Long ago, there was no night in Opio's village. People slept when they were tired and worked when they were awake. One day Opio went out hunting with his dogs. After a short time, his dogs started to chase an antelope. Opio followed them. He ran for many hours. Every time he became tired, he rested. Then he would run again. But he could not find his dogs. After many days, he came to a village. He went to one of the houses and said to the owner, “I have chased an antelope for a long time and I am very tired. I want to rest.” The man said, “Sit down and rest. Would you like some beer?” Opio was very thirsty so he drank some. Then he went to sleep. When he woke up, he couldn't see. He opened and closed his eyes many times. “You have given me something very bad to drink,” he said to the man. “I can't see properly anymore!” “There is nothing wrong with you,” the man replied. “It's night now. Haven't you ever seen night? When the day leaves, the night comes.” Opio asked many questions about the night. He began to like it very much. He and his new friend talked until morning. He stayed for another day so that he could see the night come again. The next morning he asked his friend, “How can I take the night to my own village? I want my people to see the night.” The man explained, “When it starts to get dark this evening, walk to your village. If you look straight in front, the night will follow you. If you look back, the night will go away.” Opio did as he was told. That evening, he began to walk towards his village. He felt the dark night behind him as he walked. He was tempted to look back, but he did not. When he came to his village, the villagers were afraid. They asked Opio, “What disease have you brought to us? What is this dark thing following you?” Opio said, “My friends, this dark thing is called night. You are afraid and I was afraid, too.” Opio continued to explain, “You will learn to like the night. When the light comes we can work and when night comes, we can rest.” And that is how night came to Opio's village.
author: Robert  Ekuka

title: An Orphan
text: Afeefah is a baby white rhinoceros. Rangers rescued her from the bush. Her mum was killed by poachers. The rangers took Afeefah to a place of safety. Afeefah's heart was broken. And, she was afraid that the poachers would return to take her horn. Slowly, Afeefah made friends. She felt safe and played in the mud. She drank nutritious milk at the sanctuary. One day Afeefah asked her friend Aaminah, “Why do they want our horns?” Aaminah snorted, “They believe that our horns are magical!” “But our horns are not magical!” cried Afeefah. “No, of course not. Horns are the same as hair and nails,” said Aaminah. Afeefah and Aaminah are the last of their kind. The white rhinoceros is nearly extinct. They are almost all gone from our world. We can save the rhino and other animals that are almost extinct.
author: Saajida  Patel

title: Ant and the dove
text: One day, an happy ant was happily sitting on a stone. Then, the ant jumped out of the stone. She didn't realize an wave was coming. She was happily dancing. The ant said, " Wohoooo! This is fun! Happy ant! I am a happy ant! " Then she continued to dance. Then, she suddenly turns around, and sees a wave is coming. She got goosebumps. She said," Oh no! Look at this wave! I'm going to die!" The ant was terrified and confused. " O Lord! Help me! I'm in grave danger!" she said. Helplessly, the ant had no option but to swim. Even she didn't know how to swim, she tried. " Oh nooo! What do I do? This is a B-I-G PROBLEM!!!" She shouted, " HELP! Help! SOMEONE HELP! PLEASE!" All of a sudden, the dove wakes up and makes a run for it. He wonders, ' Who is asking for help? I must save them. ' He flies and he flies! He was off to his journey! "Whee! Whoo!" Dove exclaims as he flies. The shouting continued," HELP! I'M DROWNING!" by the ant. The dove grabs a stick and helps the drowning ant. The ant says, " Thank you, Mr. Dove! You saved my life! Thank you! Thank you!" Dove says," Don't thank me! Thank the log! Hahaha" Ant laughs too. Then, The dove was about to get shot by a hunter. But suddenly- The ant saw the dove being targeted but, ant bit on the hunter's feet. The hunter shouts, " AAAAAAAAAAAAAAHH!!!! IT PAINS! WHO BIT ON MY FOOT?!! AAAAAAAH!! OUCHHH!" After that, the hunter ran away. The dove thanked the ant too. The dove said, " THANK YOU SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO SO SO SOOO MUCH!!!!!!!!!! Just like I saved your life, you saved mine! Thank you! Thank you!" The ant replied, " Don't worry! It's my duty!" " We learnt 2 lessons. 1- Help others. 2 - If you do something that helps others, you get it back" Dove said, smiling. The ant asked, " Should we get some ice- cream? " The dove replied, " Why not? Sure. I'll take chocolate and you will take-" "COFFEE! " They both said together. " Hahahaha!" And then finally, the happy ending, they became friends. Yum yum! - By the author

title: Mango Mysteries
text: Hey, look at the mango. Mangoes are ripe, sweet, and fleshy fruits. They have orangish or reddish skin with orangish pulp inside. Inside the pulp is a big seed or a stone. There are different varieties of mangoes in India – Alphonso, Rumani, Banganapalli, Neelum, Malgova, Imam Pasand, Sindhura, Jawadhu. Of these, Alphonso is known as the King of Mangoes. The ripe mangoes shown in this book are Banganapalli mangoes. Mango can be made into different food items – mango pickle, mango ice cream, mango milkshake, mango curry, aam panna drink, and many more. Mango is rich in Vitamin C and Folate. But, 84% of mango is made up of water. Carbohydrates are 15% and proteins are 1%. Mango is the national fruit of India, Pakistan, and the Philippines. India is the largest producer of mangoes in the world. Mango is the national tree of Bangladesh. An unripe mango looks green. Activity 1: Find out the months of the mango season in India? Activity 2: Which part of the mango is shown in the pic? Answers: Activity 1: The mango season in India is in the summer from April to July. Activity 2: The seed or stone of the mango is shown.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Behind You
text: Mom and Dad have gone to work. “Don’t worry, I’ll clean up the house and cook for the kids,” says May. May asks, “Where is the broomstick?” “Behind you,” says Dan. May asks, “Where is the clean sponge?” “Behind you,” says Kim. May asks, “Where is the hose pipe?” “Behind you,” says Chi. At the end of the day, the house is still dirty, the dishes haven't been washed and the garden is a mess. “Fine! If you want to play, I’ll play with you,” says May. The children are tired and hungry after playing. They start to look for May. “Where’s May?” “Behind you,” says the closet.
author: Thao Vo

title: The Lonely Whale Shark
text: I am a big little whale shark and I am sad on my reef. For this turtle has a friend. This jellyfish does too. Even these remoras swim together into the blue. Why am I the only lonely fish? Oh! Look! It is the coming together of whale sharks from everywhere, with very exciting stories to share. I saw an octopus eat a crab. I spoke to a really old sea turtle. A shark with sharp teeth tried to attack me! Have you seen a sunfish? I saw two on my way over here. If I look hard, maybe I will see it too. For there is plenty of fish I have bumped into. Whether on the reef or in the open ocean, if I pay attention, there is enough commotion. I have met a grouper with a funny bone, and a fish that I confused for a stone. A squid that was terribly shy, and a manta ray that thought it could fly! I am a big little whale shark... and I am not so sad anymore. At least, not as sad as I was before. For even though I travel on my own, I am never truly alone.
author: Mahira Kakajiwala

title: Knowledge
text: I have never liked TV. Sir, how does an airplane fly in the sky? Child! I have no interest in airplanes. Ok, sir, tell me this. How does a fan run with electricity? Lali! I have nothing to do with fans and electricity. Alright, sir, let it be. No, no! Child, keep asking! How will you improve your knowledge if you don't ask questions?

title: I Have So Many Friends
text: I have two friends at school. Amit and Sujay. I have many other friends too. Such as this mango tree. This earth mover is my friend. Also, the uncle who sells peanuts. Meet my new friend, who lives next door. You know who else is my friend? My Aaji! These books are my friends too. They take me to so many places! Do you have such friends?

title: Lola Goes Camping
text: Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Lola. She was six years old. She had an older brother named Sam. He was twelve years old. The two siblings lived on Yellow Brick street with their Mother and Father. They went to Waterhouse academy. That was their school. One Saturday afternoon, Lola’s father suggested that he, Sam and Lola go camping in the woods. Mother was an online college teacher, so she din’t have much time for camping. So that day, they packed their suitcases. Lola had her own red suitcase with yellow flowers scattered on it. Lola put her toothbrush, toothpaste, hairbrush, pillows, four books from the flower power series, water bottles, bedsheets, and colouring book with colours. Everyone went into the red car and put their suitcase under the seats. They travelled for half an hour before they reached the woods. They made a three tents, one for father, one for Sam, and one for Lola. Father’s tent was blue with squares, Sam’s tent was red with triangles, and Lola’s tent was purple with circles. Father built a fire between the three tents. The fire made the family warm and comfortable. Then they roasted marshmallows. Lola collected three sticks to hold the marshmallows. They pushed the marshmallows onto the sticks and held it close to the fire. They slept in the tent, and in the morning, they ate bread and butter for breakfast. Mother had packed it in a yellow tiffin. This was the best camping Lola had ever gone too in her whole life:)
author: Anushka Nair

title: Where Is Your School?
text: I go to school every day. Chiki and I see many schools on our way. The parrots fly to a school on a guava tree. The squirrels run to a school on a mango tree. The pigeons sit in a school on electric wires The ducks float in a school on the lake. Baby cows walk to a school in a field. Can you see the tamarind tree? My school is under that tree. And the crows are above me. In a school on the tamarind tree! Chiki goes to school on Sundays. In my home! No books and no schoolbag for her. In the home school, I am her teacher!
