text: It's morning! Today Lala's birthday! Cukkoo!Cukkoo! the alarm rangs. She waked up and starting to jump on the bed and shouted Hurray! it's my birthday. Lala called her mother and told mom today is my birthday. Her mom told yes Lala i know. Happy birthday Lala. Lala told thankyou. Mom can i call my friends pleasee... her mother told yes Lala i already invited.Oh!!! thank you mom. She recived many birthday cards from her relatives and friends those who can't come to the party. The door bell rangs ting tong. Lala opened the door all shouted happy birhday Lala!!! she said thank you mom told here your birthday cake Lala cut. All singing birtday song for her and Lala cutted her cake happily. THE END

illustrator: Candace di Talamo; Google India; Phạm Thị  Thu Trang; Samrat Halder

title: Grandma's Bag of Stories 1 - The Beginning of The Stories
text: Summer Holidays! Nani smiled to herself while she waited for two more grandchildren to arrive. Radha and Ram would be here soon. Arjun and Deepti already arrived previous evening. they have been waiting restlessly for their cousins even though Nani told them that Radha and Ram will arrive next morning, but these two kids would never listen. They went to the railway station with their grandfather [nana] to receive Radha and Ram. Both Arjun and Deepti ran towards their cousins and gave them a tight hug. All of them sat in the back seat of the car and talked to each other like they haven't met since years. Meanwhile at home Nani hurried through her bath, she had finished cooking their favorite dishes and wore a nice floral cotton sari. There! There they came! Nani shouted. The kids came rushing out of the car and quickly went to inspect the garden to see how big the plants, cows, sheep's, buffalos, calves, dogs,pups,cats, kittens have grown. then they hugged Nani and kissed her on her face and ate the scrumptious lunch. Now turns the best part of the HOLIDAYS!!!!!!!!! STORIES!!" yay Nani now open your bag and tell us the real and fictional stories yay." Radha shouted. "yes Nani please" Arjun requested." ok my darlings I am really tired now tomorrow for sure we will hear a spectacular story." said Nani "yay!" shouted all the kids.
author: Saanvi Sharma
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Edwin  Irabor; Kawai`ola Wong; Madhuri Purandare; Santosh Pujari

title: Grandma's Bag Of Stories 2- Stranger Danger
text: One nice sunny day, in Nani's house the kids were playing in the ground. Nani was making chole chawl. The maid was not focused on her work and didn't do any work. Nana took a bath and went in the garden to check what's going on. He heard the kids talking about bad guys and kidnappers. When Nani served them lunch nana talked about bad guys and kidnappers to the children. "Kids do not EVER take anything from strangers. they might hurt you or do something bad and take money from us or your parents so no matter how big the toy chocolate or anything is without our permission don't take anything from others." "ok nana we will never ever take anything from strangers" now let us go and play Uno. In the evening the kids were playing a game in the park. Suddenly an uncle came to them saying" kids do you want this toffee" the kids really wanted to say yes and they almost did when Radha remembered what nana said ''guys remember what nana said do not take anything form any stranger didn't he" yes said the other kids sorry we don't want it then the stranger took out a big teddy bear!! The kids wanted the teddy bear but they didn't took it. They quickly went inside Nani's house and told her everything. Nani came out rushing and told to the man "go away we don't need anything from you or else shall I call the POLICE." AND WOW WHAT A SUPRISE IT WAS NANA ALL THE TIMEEE. He took a test of the children and they passed then nana gave them the teddy bear and had fun in the house.
author: Saanvi Sharma
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; Kirti Phadke; Lavanya  Naidu; Seat Sopheap; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Thao Vo

title: Lina is not sleepy
text: "Mommy, I don't want to sleep!" says Lina, yawning loudly. Her mother smiles. Her mother says, "Alright, but at least drink your milk". Lina drinks the milk. She says, "Mommy, I am still not sleepy". Mommy says, "Okay, but please brush your teeth, Lina." Lina brushes her teeth. Lina wants to read a story before going to bed. As she reads the book she doses off. Lina says, "Mommy, I am sleepy now. Good night!" Lina goes to bed feeling very sleepy.
author: Dhriti Sahu
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Helga Parekh; Maithili  Joshi; Mihir Joglekar; Priyankar Gupta; Sonal Gupta Vaswani

title: I Don't Know
text: I don’t know.” “Shh! Quiet, the baby will wake up.” “Why are you angry?” Aai asked. “I don’t know,” replied Appu. “When you’re very hungry, you get angry, don't you?” said Aai. “I am bored,” grumbled Appu. “Come, let’s play,” said Baba. “Aaji, Aaji, I’m afraid,” said Appu. “What are you afraid of, my dear?” asked Aaji. “I don’t know.” “Feeling better now?” she asked. Just then, Aai called. “Appu, come and see this!” “How lovely the night looks!” “Your fear has gone away, I think! Did the fireflies take it?” Aai asked. Appu giggled. “I don’t know.”
author: Anushka  Ravishankar

title: No More No!
text: I want wafers.” “No, Pitku. It’s time for lunch.” “Then give me some toys.” “No. You’ll make a mess again.” “I’m going to Savi’s to play.” “No!” “No, no, no, all the time! You’re always saying no!” “I don’t like you!” “Okay. So? What should we do?” “I’m going to tell Papa.” “Papaaa, I want another, nicer mother! Not this one.” “And I want another, smarter son! Not this one.” “Whaaaaaat??” “Okay, now?” “Will you take a bite, Mommy? ” “I won’t say no!”
author: Anushka  Ravishankar

title: So Many Guests
text: We have two guests. Sister Sparrow and Cousin Mynah. Here is Aunt Koel. Now we have three guests. Come in, Brother Crow. Now we have four. Here comes Sister Pigeon. That makes it five guests. This way...come slowly, Aunt Ducky. So now we have six guests. Brother Peacock, do come in. Now we have seven guests. Ah! Come in and sit, Grandpa Parrot. That makes it eight guests. Welcome, Granny Owl. Now we have nine guests. Come right in, Uncle Stork. But why are you standing? Hmm, so it all adds up to ten guests. Wait a moment. How did you all know… …that it is my birthday today? Ma, you told them, did you not?
author: Kanchan Bannerjee

title: The Anger Monster
text: Once upon a time, there lived a lion. But there lived a monster in him. He would always think that I will have the fruits of the tree but the monster irritated him so much each time that he would kill the animals and eat them. All his jungle friends left him. He felt lonely. He started to cry. Just then his best friend came snoopy, the bear and asked him why he was crying. He told him that he was crying as all his jungle friends had left him. Snoopy said that you will have to take your monster out but the lion got angry and started shouting on Snoopy. Snoopy bought a mirror and showed it to him. He was looking very bad as he was angry. He immediately calmed down and he started looking nice again. Then he asked snoopy that how should he release the monster. Snoopy said that let the monster say but you don't kill any animal. He also said that the monster will eventually leave him. So the lion stopped listening to the monster and started eating only fruits of the trees. And one day, the monster ran out of the lion and every one became his friend. Written by Eshaan Singh Juneja Illustrators Ajit Narayan, Brian Wambi, Michael Sagikwa, Partho Sengupta
author: Eshaan Singh Juneja
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Brian Wambi; Michael  Sagikwa; Partho Sengupta

title: Happiness
text: Once upon a time in a village in India, there lived a family of parents and their three sons. They were suffering from financial problems. They had 3 kids. the first kid's name was Amit, the second kid's name was Aman and the third kid, the youngest one was Abhishek. It was very hard for Aman's parents to manage their family. Aman's mom was a maid and his father was a labourer. They had to survive on limited food in order to save their money. Amit thought that if he will not focus on studies he would never be successful in his life. Then, he started to focus on studies and started scoring good marks. His brothers Abhishek and Aman saw that their elder brother was focusing on his studies. They also started to study hard and scored good marks. When Aman's parents saw their kid's scoring good marks and focusing on their studies, they were very happy. As they grew up, Amit and Amit's brothers had realized their dreams. Amit's dream was that he wanted to be a a doctor. The day his result came by, he passed his test by scoring full marks. His parents were very happy and distributed ladoos to their neighbours and relatives, so Amit's brothers got inspired and they also became what they wanted to become. The main thing was that they all became successful in their lives. Aman bacame an IPS officer and Abhishek became an engineer. They all lived happily ever after..
author: renu chopra
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Fahad Faizal; Omkar Mahashabde; RIA SHAH; Shadrach Munene; Taposhi Ghoshal; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Boy Who was scared of Balloons
text: Pop! Pop! Pop! What a loud sound the brightly colored floating balls made. It was scary. One minute they were plump and round. Up in the air. The next minute, they had burst into so many thin pieces, and had fallen to the ground. He did not like it. No, he did not like it at all. This had happened on his very first birthday party. Shaunat had cried loudly when the balloons burst. Everyone had comforted him. They took away all the balloons. Only then would he come near his birthday cake. But at the next birthday party he went to, it happened again. There were balloons everywhere. Other children seemed to love the colored balls. They laughed happily and jumped around with them. Some children pushed sharp pens into the balloons so they would burst. And they clapped at the noise. But Shaunat would shut his ears and run away to hide. His parents tried to help him. “Look,” they said. “A balloon is only a piece of plastic. You can blow a little air into it. And if you let it out gently, it won’t make any noise. Why don’t YOU try it?” But Shaunat did not want to try. He preferred not to think about it at all. He wanted nothing to do with balloons that looked lovely, but then burst noisily and disappeared. At school, his classmates quickly found out that he was afraid of balloons. How they laughed at him and tried to frighten him! When they teased him, he folded himself into a ball. He would close his eyes and think of something else. But when the BOOM came, he was still so frightened that he had to get away. Sometimes, he would run to Chimi, his best friend at school. She did not laugh at him. Hey Shaunat! Come, don’t bother with those silly kids. Let’s go do something else! I wish I could stop being afraid. You surely will someday. But let’s wait for the right time. One day, their teacher told the children about a school picnic. They were going the very next day to the national park with the tiger safari. Shaunat clapped his hands in delight. He loved animals, birds, and insects. He loved everything about nature. The picnic would be great. Best of all, there would be no balloons! Chimi, Chimi, aren’t you excited? I may not come. No, but I will be, tomorrow at the park! Why not? Are you sick? How do you know that? “I will be sick with fear,” said Chimi in a small voice. “I am scared of the snakes in the reptile house. I am scared of the monkeys that roam everywhere. My cousin had to take so many painful shots when a monkey bit him! I am even scared of the tigers. And the crocodiles. And I hate spiders too,” Chimi shuddered with a sudden memory of the giant wood spider from the forest she had recently gone to with her family. Shaunat was surprised. Chimi had never shared this secret. Scared of spiders? Why, they were such amazing spinners! His uncle Sujit studied spiders and had shown him so many cool ones. And tigers? Surely, they were the most magnificent animals in the whole world! Suddenly Shaunat remembered what Chimi had said when HE had been scared. “Chimi, Chimi, do come tomorrow. I will sit right with you. I will tell you how wonderful all these animals are, and how special each one is. Really! Maybe you will forget to be afraid. Just like you help me forget about those nasty balloons.” “Maybe EVERYONE is afraid of something, " said Chimi, thoughtfully. “And maybe we all just need a friend to help us be less scared,” said Shaunat. The two friends looked at each other. “I will come tomorrow,” smiled Chimi. “I have an idea. Bring a balloon,” said Shaunat. He felt a little anxious even as he said it. But he lifted his chin and went on. “When you see a tiger, or a snake, you can burst the balloon. Then we can be fearful together!” “And maybe it will be the right time, for both of us,” smiled Shaunat. “To not be afraid anymore.” “I hope so,” said Chimi, giggling with relief at the thought. “But hey, let’s make sure not to scare the poor tiger instead!”
author: Rohini Nilekani

title: My Family
text: My name is Tuk Tuk. I have a large family. This is my mother. this is my father. This is my brother Neetu and my sister Meetu is there too. Look... My grandparents have also come. Dada - Dadi and Nana - Nani... My mother has three sisters. They are my 'mausis'! And look... My father has four brothers.Two of them are older than him and I call them 'Tau Ji' and two of them are younger and I call them ' Chacha Ji '. And with them there are my aunts-my two 'Tais ' and my two 'Chachis'. See... My family has five young children also. We make a lot of noise when we are all together. See, what a large family I have! Oh! Bujo got left out. He wags his tail all day long and says... Bhow!! Bhow!! Bhow!!
author: Rushali Kansal

title: Saru and her Little Secret
text: Mangu is Saru's best friend, but not as brave as Saru, timid, and doesn't move around much. Saru befriends three other children who live in nearby houses. These children are Hari, Manik and Ketaki. Hari's father is a driver, Manik's parents work in the hospital and Ketki's mother teaches in the school. There also lives a Mai, who takes care of the children. Mai's eyebrows are always taut, and whenever she calls on Saru, it feels like thunder. Any time you walk through the front of the hostel at any time of the day, you can hear Mai's voice calling out to Saru by his name. This is because Cypress is never where she needs to be in time. When she sees, she goes near the pond or towards the forest. Now that we have got to know about everyone in the story, let's start the conversation - not from the very beginning but on a happy morning in the month of May! When the rattling of utensils was heard coming from the kitchen, Saru removed the yellow sheet which he had covered from head to toe. He immediately left the bed. Then quickly she got ready after eating boiled rice along with maad. That day was school holiday. Saru knew that the day would be very fun. Whenever it is school holidays, Saru enjoys a lot. He called out to Mangu. But Mangu did not feel like going to the pond with him. Mangu's mind was used to read and write, And he preferred to be in school with Saru rather than fussy on the pond. Saru called his other friends to accompany him. But that day everyone had some other work and Saru was left alone. Still, she ran to the fence alone, without much sadness, and jumped out of the space between the two logs. She knew she shouldn't be doing what she was doing, but she was so excited that she didn't even think to stop. Jumping and jumping on the slope, she reached down to the bank of the pond, leaning on the round stones lying in the mud. There was a big peepal tree on the bank of the pond. Sometimes the passersby would take some time to rest in his shadow, or take a nap. But this morning no one was there. Saru was happy alone because he knew that if someone in the hostel saw him, he would have to answer a dozen questions, and in this case he was bound to be scolded. On the banks of the pond, Cypress enjoyed the most in catching chirayas or dragonfly. The huge winged insect looked exactly like the helicopters whose pictures Saru had seen in books. And he loved to hold their delicate feathers by pressing them between his fingers. “One went, two went, how many went!” Saru slyly moved towards the sitting Chiura, keeping some distance between his fingers, and then, murmuring on the reeds that grew on the banks of the water, hurriedly caught Chiura between his fingers. Caught it Then she would sit the chirare on the sticky leaves of nearby plants, and after a short time weaned her legs from the gluten, she would fly away. While Saru was trying to catch the chirps one after the other, he heard the sound of rattles coming from the nearby bushes. The very next moment the sound got louder and then Saru saw movement in the bushes. The restless cypress, anxious to know everything, moved towards the bushes to see why there was movement. As he brushed aside the twigs that stood in his way, Cypress encountered a tiny creature with large split-like eyes and a strangely sculpted figure. He was like a baby the size of a big mouse. The little creature was shocked to find Saru in front of him and tried to run away from there, but he could not do so. It was as if his feet were stuck in something below. Saru was looking at her in amazement with tearing eyes, and saw that the poor creature was frightened and was trying his best to run away by freeing himself. The more he tried to free himself, the more he would get stuck in the bush. As long as it happened to him, he kept trying to free himself, then that strange little creature got tired and died there. Actually, the feet of that little creature were entangled in the long vine hanging from the tree. Saru cleverly freed him by taking out his feet stuck in the vine. But the poor deer had been hurt and could no longer walk away from it. Saru felt pity for her, and decided to take her home and take care of her until she recovered. Saru felt that trouble might arise for him, so he ran towards the shadow of the tin built to park the tractor nearby. When Mai got tired of calling Suru and went back inside, Saru hurriedly led the terrified creature through the back of the building to the tin-roofed room adjacent to the hostel building. In the shadow of this tin were kept large pots, cauldrons, balaches and other large utensils which were needed only for feasts on festivals etc. Saru glanced quickly into the dark place and decided that she would keep the little creature with her and take care of it until it was completely well. Although Saru himself was only a few years old, he realized that perhaps the creature had broken a leg and would not be able to survive if left alone. After a quick glance at the spot, Saru laid out an empty sack lying there at the bottom of a large brass pot, and cleverly placed the creature in it. That vessel was used only on special occasions. Saru then ran towards the kitchen to get milk for her, but went midway to tell her friends this funny news. In no time, all the friends were standing around that little creature, looking at it. Hari was the eldest of these children, and as soon as he saw the little creature, he said out loud that it was a deer baby. Ketki, who was fond of reading and writing and poetry, quickly decided that the name 'Pillu' would be a good fit for him. Since Mangu was the quietest and gentlest of all the children, he was entrusted with the task of feeding Pillu. Mangu started feeding her milk with a spoon. At first Pillu hesitated, but because he was hungry, he quickly drank all the milk, spoon by spoon. The children decided that it would be better to keep Pillu in the same room with tin roof as there was no one to come and go. Mangu took the responsibility of feeding her and the rest of the children also promised to bring her something to eat and drink whenever possible. By late evening, Pillu was starting to look quite well. He was given milk again, and before that he had munched and ate Bhakri, which the ruby ​​had secretly brought for him. At night, the children went to sleep after unloading the jute sack to Pillu. The children did not rest all night while Pillu slept soundly in his new home. It was not even a good day when the restless children went straight to the tin roofed room. Pillu was sitting upright and when he raised his head, he would have looked over the big fugitive's shoulder. All the children sat down to discuss some important things. They were mumbling among themselves. There was debate. When Mai came out from there, she too stared at the children. thinking that children Why are you gathered here? When everything seemed fine, she went on her way. The children would touch the hairy body of the little puppy and fill it in their arms. Feel his humming. He remained very calm. The children always wanted to have her with them. But he knew that later on when he becomes a big deer, then it will be difficult to keep him hidden in this small room. As soon as the children heard the sound of someone's footsteps, they would hide the puppy in the pot. But no one wanted to go anywhere except Pillu. Pillu was like the little king of his heart! The next day also passed like this. It was morning, so before going to school the children ran towards that tin roofed room. Everyone had taken something for Pillu to eat. He fed Pillu lovingly, and went to school. As soon as the holiday bell rang, all the children hurriedly ran towards the room to reach Pillu. Pillu sat in the pot very calmly, and avoided getting into any trouble. The children also spent the evening playing with Pillu. Now Pillu's weakness was gone, and he had no problem standing. Now it seemed that his foot injury was also recovering fast. As the days passed, Pillu became healthier and more plump than ever. Along with this, Pillu was now more playful than ever. He wanted to spend more time outside his pot, which increased the children's anxiety. The children thought that if someone saw Pillu, their secret would be revealed. Apart from this, the children were also worried about the strange growth of the puppy. He started thinking that why till now Pillu looks like a big mouse and why his height is not increasing like that of a deer. Is it not that it has happened because of keeping it in the pot for so long. He gets upset thinking of this. A few days later one night suddenly there was a noise. Many nights, while everyone was sleeping, the loud sounds of pots and jars falling could be heard. The voices were coming from the same place where Pillu lived. These sounds broke everyone's sleep. All the people ran towards that tin roofed room. And there he stood stoically! Inverted in the middle of the pot, the little puppy was looking at everything with his big eyes. Surely Pillu must have tried to get out of his pot, and in this round all the pots kept one on top of the other fell down. Everything in the room was scattered. People were surprised to see Pillu there. Everyone had something to say. Even in this chaotic atmosphere, Pillu looked as cute as ever. Then a good manus came there. There was selfishness in his words. He pacified the people by saying that there is no need to be afraid of this animal as it does not cause any harm, and may have come here after wandering from the forest. It was still as if I knew everything. She was murmuring with anger. She was saying that she knew that all this mess was done by Saru and his companions, because when they see, they keep on messing up. Calmly speaking Bhale Manus picked up the little Pillu in his lap and called Saru and his companions to him with a gesture. With a smile, he asked the children whether he had been taking care of Pillu. Trusting his sense of belonging, the children told him everything - how they found the puppy and how they took care of him. The children also told him that there was a lot of concern about his little deer being left small. Is it that it was because they kept it in the pot? The children asked. He told the children that the little animal he had taken care of so well was actually not a deer but a 'mouse-deer'. The children were very surprised to learn that their puppy is not a deer at all and will always be small like a mouse, a little like a pig and a little like a deer! The elders decided that Pillu should be allowed to stay with the hostel children. The good man announced that there would also be a sanctuary for the animals. Hearing this, the children started making different sounds with joy. Within a month, a shelter for the stray, sick and distressed animals in the forest was ready. That became Pillu's home, forever! This story is of Dr Prakash Amte, son of renowned social worker Baba Amte. Inspired by a wildlife orphanage. Madiya Gond tribals Baba Amte had started Lok Biradari Prakalp for welfare and development. The organization runs an orphanage for animals under the name 'Amtez Animal Ark' in Hemlakasa Where wildlife trapped in trouble is also given shelter. no one visits this hideaway can go to see. For more information about Lok Biradari Project, see-
author: GAMYA BARANWAL

title: Magical Lamp
text: Night time, now it's time to study but why my lamp is not working. The weather is not so pleasant so that's why I can't see anything outside. Lets turn on the electric bulb. But why the lamp is making faces. I think this is a magical lamp. Ok now it's time to study. It's so noisy because it's thundering outside. Now it's time to do fishing so let's go to river side. But my lamp is not working. Oh I forgot to lit the light. Now let's go. I got a golden fish at home and I put it in the aquarium. And I put my lamp beside it and went to sleep. After that I turn on the bulb and went to sleep. In few minutes I remember that I was studying. Then I opened my book and studied. After studying I went to sleep. And the fish was swimming in the water then suddenly I thought that I haven't given food to fish. When I went outside. The lamp was looking sad. After wasting a single minute I was thinking why the lamp was sad? After some time I understood what's the problem. After some time I realized that a fish can't live in a aquarium so I put the fish back in the sea and went home to sleep.
author: Kanav Aggarwal

title: Naughty Mouse and the fan
text: Once upon a time, there lived a mouse named Spotty. His name was Spotty because he had a big brown spot around his eye,though, most people called him Naughty Mouse because he was very naughty. Spotty lived with his mother in a hole inside Alex and Judy's house. He loved it there as there was lot of food available to him all the time. Spotty was always doing something naughty, he got into trouble and learnt something from it. One day, naughty mouse was lying next to his mother. While his mother was sleeping, he looked up at the fan and a naughty thought crossed his mind and in excitement, he shouted "Yippie!!". His mother woke up and asked, "Is everything ok, Spotty?" Spotty answered "Yes Mother". When Spotty's mother fell asleep, he ran out of the hole, jumped on the sofa and climbed onto the fan. He thought of the fan to be his merry-go-round where he could play and go round and round. Just as he was playing, Judy switched on the fan and Spotty started running faster and faster not knowing what was happening. He got so tired running, that he fell down. Spotty landed on the sofa where his head was still spinning. He was feeling very dizzy and could not move. He started shouting "Help"" Help" " Help"! Fortunately, his mother heard him and she ran to the sofa and pulled him out before anyone could see him. Spotty could have hurt himself but his mother saved him. He said sorry to his mother and promised not to do it again. The moral of the story is "Always ask your parents before doing something new, you might get yourself into trouble"
author: Naisha  Ajmani

title: Every Child is Blessed
text: Ones upon a time there was a boy named Bijoy. He was very scared for his maths class. Today, in the schedule the last class was maths. The teacher came and everyone was exited except Bijoy. E veryone said good morning sir! The sir's name was Mr Raj and he was very strict. Raj sir called two students and then he called Bijoy. Bijoy!! tell me this answer? Really Bijoy was trembling at that moment. He said I don't know. Raj sir asked him to try and Bijoy told whatever was coming in his mind. Sir was so angry and e veryone was laughing at Bijoy. When the school finished, Bijoy was so sad and he was thinking that am I really so dumb? Everyone was laughing at him. The there was a competition of a race. But Bijoy was not confident, he thought he will now lose the race as well. Bijoy was so fast in Race but in the way he slipped and was having so many injuries but he did not lose hope. Finally, he won the race. And, he also went to the nationals and now his school bagged first position due to him. Everyone said sorry to Bijoy and Principal gave medal.
author: Aarav  Mehta
illustrator: Alyssa Pachuau; Audrey Agnier; ISHKIRAT  SINGH; Ruchi Shah; Sanjay Sarkar; Students of  Himalayan Public School

title: A Story of The Camel!
text: There were two camels roaming near the Sahara Desert. It was with their Lords. Suddenly, one of the camels went in another direction with its Lord. After a while, they reached their home. That Camel spent quality time with its offspring. The little one asked a question to the mother camel, "Mommy, why did God make a hump over our back?". The mother explained that as they are living in the desert with water scarcity and they need to travel afar to fetch water. In order to save water, God made a Hump on our back. The mother Camel answered to the little one's question. The mother Camel gave birth to lot more baby camels in the upcoming years. They lived happily in the desert.
author: Prema Lakshmi
illustrator: Deepthi T A S; Kalyan Joshi; Muniza Shariq; rizwan shoukat; Samit  Shrestha

title: Sorrow Family
text: A late night conversation between a wife and husband and they live in a small village. Wife: Rani is leaving tomorrow, she needs to pay 5000 rupees for his semester fee. Husband: (In a depressive voice) We don't have enough money even for our own survival and our daughter's school fee, how can we adjust 5000 all of sudden. Wife: I'm also worried, if we don't pay the fee his studies will get disturb. Husband: I will say Rani to adjust for some more days. (They both pretended as they are sleeping but they are thinking how to arrange the money) Next day morning when Rani is about to leave, her mother came hurriedly from outside and handed 5000 Rs with a smiling face. While the Husband thinking about the money, after some time realized her bangles are missing on her hands and thought she sold those for this daughter’s education. Husband cried inside for not able to adjust the money for his daughter and to compensate this mother had to sell her bangles.
author: Bhavesh Gamesing
illustrator: Alex  Zablon; Aman Randhawa; Dhiman  Sarkar; Joanna  Mendes

title: Which Doctor?
text: When have you gone to meet a doctor? If you have a cough or fever, right. Doctors who check the patients for common health problems are known as general practitioners. But, sometimes, you have a problem in your body that can only be solved by a specialist doctor. Let us look at the different types of specialist doctors. Ophthalmologist – A doctor who takes care of eye problems. Otolaryngologist – A doctor who treats problems in the ear, nose, and throat. Dermatologist – A doctor who treats problems in the skin. Cardiologist – A doctor who treats problems in the heart. Pulmonologist – A doctor who treats diseases in the lungs and other organs that help to breathe. Pediatrician – A doctor who takes care of the health of small children and babies. Geriatrician – A doctor who takes care of the health of old people usually above 60 years. Endocrinologist – A doctor who specialises in the treatment of glands and hormones. Nephrologist – A doctor who treats kidney problems. Neurologist – A doctor who treats problems in the nervous system. Dentist – A doctor who cures problems in the mouth and teeth. Activity 1: Tell which doctor has to be seen for the problems listed below. 1. Meena has a skin allergy. 2. Bhima has high blood pressure. 3. Chacko is not able to see clearly. 4. Jhansi has a high fever. 5. Imran has a pain in his ear. Answers are on the next page. Activity 1 - Answers Tell which doctor has to be seen for the problems listed below. 1. Meena has a skin allergy - Dermatologist 2. Bhima has high blood pressure - Cardiologist 3. Chacko is not able to see clearly - Ophthalmologist 4. Jhansi has a high fever - General Practitioner 5. Imran has a pain in his ear - Otolaryngologist Activity 2: Browse the net and find out 5 more types of specialist doctors. Good Luck!
author: Anitha Selvanathan
illustrator: Aindri C; Anandee Vaidya; Bianca de Jong; Debbie  Faber-Human; Ellen Heydenrych; Meghna Pant; Priyankar Gupta; Radhika Tipnis; Rijuta Ghate; Santosh Pujari; Shirish  Ghatge; Shohei Emura; Swathi Sambasivam; Tanvee Nabar

title: Little Girl in The Forest
text: Once upon a time, in the forest, there lived a little girl. Lisa was her name. Lisa shared a house with a friend named Bobby. Bobby is a small squirrel who's always with her. I will catch you, Bobby! Squeak, Squeak... Lisa and Bobby have been together for a long time. They did everything together, such as playing tennis, hide and seek, hanging around, and going to school. One day, when the sun was shining, they went to school. Lisa and Bobby are very happy because they can see the sunrise from the hill and they can meet their friends again. When they arrived at school, they are greeted by their classmates. Lisa and Bobby are very happy to meet them again. Hello friends, nice to see you again! Hi, Lisa nice to see you too! At school, Lisa studies diligently as she always does. Meanwhile, Bobby plays with his squirrel friends in the tree. When it was getting late, Lisa and Bobby walk to their house together. They walked down the street and looks very happy when remembered everything at school. On their way, they stopped at the bank of a river. Lisa and Bobby decided to take a rest for a while. Instead of resting, they decided to have some fun in the water. Bobby gets soaked after being splashed by water and Lisa used a towel to help Bobby dry himself. Because they were having so much fun playing, they forgot it was getting dark. But lucky Lisa brought a flashlight. So, they can illuminate their steps on the street. Because Lisa's house is on a hill, the path feels long and the road is very challenging where Lisa and Bobby have to go up the hillside. Finally, Lisa and Bobby arrived at the house, Lisa started to talk about everything to Bobby. Even though Bobby couldn't speak, Lisa was still very happy talking to him. The story of Lisa and Bobby's friendship was extremely touching. We can be together as fellow living beings on Earth, even if it is between animals and humans. It's very beautiful when we can protect, love, and enjoy nature together. Between humans and animals like Lisa and Bobby.
author: Tasya Putri Ayunda & Dwi Rosela

title: Take Care and Love Our Sea
text: When the sun wants to rest, its light begins to disappear behind the night sky. An old man approached a place where children were gathered, waiting for his arrival. The closer the man approached them, the more excited the children greeted him when they saw the new book he had brought with them. After the old man came and sat in front of the children, he would start his work there. With faces eagerly awaiting, the children faithfully waited for the story to be read. You don't have to wait long for the story to begin... After the old man came and sat in front of the children, he would start his work there. With faces eagerly awaiting, the children faithfully waited for the story to be read. You don't have to wait long for the story to begin... The morning sun had just appeared, giving light that penetrated the clear sea water making a very beautiful reflection. The fish under the sea dance and swim to and fro to welcome the bright morning. Some are playing, and looking for food, some are just swimming and enjoying the beautiful underwater scenery. All fish are very happy to live in their place, they are always together with other animals who live in the same area. They are happy to live in their place by doing their respective duties. The marine life enjoys their life. Dolphins that jump out of the water beautifully, turtles that swim with the current, and fish that seem to hide in the beautiful dance of seaweed that follows the flow of water. They spend their time looking at the beautiful and unpolluted sea. Until one day came when a foreign object came into their habitat. Slowly some of the marine life died, and some of the fish became carcasses that rose to the sea level. And the life under the sea becomes very dirty and damaged. The marine life that is still alive, confused by the occurrence of their habitat is slowly being destroyed. They are looking for a foreign object that has killed their friends and homes. After seeing the strange things that kept coming, it was a human waste that had been thrown into the sea. The foreign objects come from garbage thrown into the sea, and some of these foreign objects are accidentally eaten by fish and land right on rocks or seaweed. Make them die. The foreign objects are plastic, food packaging, drink cans, and the like. They (humans) easily make marine habitats polluted with their actions that are considered trivial. After some time passed, human help came, who swam under the sea because they saw the many carcasses of fish floating to see what was happening under the sea to make the fish die.. It turns out that there is garbage that comes from humans that is why. They finally came the next day, took the garbage to throw away, and cleaned up the marine habitat so that the living creatures that had lived under the sea become happy and happy again. After taking time, they were finally able to clean up the underwater and make marine life happy. Some of the children who heard it were crying and angry. They don't like the sea creatures to die because of human activities. Even the grown men speak, so they have to make other people understand that under the sea there is life too that we must protect, we should not throw garbage into the sea. So we must aggressively remind people that we should not use plastic materials for packaging our food or goods, to reduce the consumption of plastic that is not eco-friendly. The children understood, and finally, they finished listening to stories about the importance of protecting and loving our oceans. So that no marine life dies and becomes extinct. The man had completed his task, he said goodbye and returned to his house when the dark sky had greeted him.
author: Adinda Novindia Adityawarman and Thasya Octaviany D.P.S

title: DOG

title: Carly's Superhero
text: Growing up every child believes their father can do almost anything for them. Nothing seems impossible in a child’s eyes. Similarly for Carly her dad Patrick was the only superhero she knew of apart from the Avengers. She simply adored her dad. Some say daughters are really close to their fathers. The saying was very true in Carly’s case. Patrick was rather young to be Carly’s dad. He was hardly in his mid twenties when he embraced fatherhood. Parenting is never an easy job but one kind of blends into the role, some with ease while others find their way around eventually. Patrick fell in the latter category. Carly was always a happy go lucky child but an incident changed things. Patrick embraced fatherhood at a young age. He stumbled at first but slowly and gradually got a hang of parenting. Now Carly all grown up as a bubbly five year old simply can’t imagine her life without Patrick. Carly had just celebrated her six month milestone birthday when unfortunately while returning from her party, there was fatal accident and she lost both her parents Mira and Shaun. She was the only one who survived the accident. Shaun was Patrick’s elder brother. The accident was rather painful for Patrick as well because not only did he loose he brother and sister-in-law but lost both his parents as well. Patrick was on his swanky new bike which his Dad had gifted him after his retirement. The accident was too tragic to bear for both. Patrick didn’t even have enough time to grieve when he had to rather grow up and take responsibility at a young age. He was Carly’s only guardian now. Mira’s had lost both her parents early as well. Patrick had a lot on his table. But as they say there is always light at the end of the tunnel. Patrick got the good news that an investor was ready to invest in his business idea. Now he was his own boss and had all the time to look after his daughter. Carly in the beginning took time to warm up to him as Patrick was always busy with his rather happening life. But as they say you know your true friends in a crisis situation. All his friends became his support system and helped with taking care of Carly. One day Carly had just started walking and mumbling a few words and spoke her first word mumma. She gingerly walked up to Patrick and called him mumma. From that day forward Carly found her mom and dad in her uncle Patrick. So look any further there is a superhero in all of us.
author: Ruby  Thomas

title: Education For Everyone
text: One day, there is a little girl named Isabella. She is a cheerful girl who loves to study and read. Her parents have a personal library and Isabella always study in there. She’s very kind to her friends. She also loves to play with her friends. One time, Isabella went outside to walk. When she was outside, she saw a girl and approached her. Isabella is very happy to find a new friend. They have a chat together and She decided to bring her to her house. Inside the house, Isabella asked her about school, studies, and more. The girl also responded to the questions. Do you love to study? Where’s your school? I don’t like study and I am not school anywhere. School is boring. Hearing those answers, Isabella started to explain how fun study and school can be. Isabella tried to convince her that school is fun. In the school, we can learn many things, like drawing, counting, reading, and you can have many friends. It’ very fun! She is convinced that the school is not boring and now she wants to study as well. I think it sounds good. Being with friends and learn together sounds very fun! After that, Isabella invites her to study and learn together in her parents' library. The girl learn a lot from Isabella, she learned how to draw, read, write, and more. They always spent their time together. Not only that, now they went to school together. Isabella’s parents give her new friend a help by sending her to school with Isabella. Isabella showed her friend the class and meet with a lot of new friends. She is having fun in school. Isabella and her friend always went to the school’s library to learn together. She loves to study and read a lot of books with Isabella. Isabella’s new friend is very happy and very grateful that Isabella and her parents gave her help to study at the school. They always together ever since. ---The End--- In summary, the moral value of the story... We all need an education no matter who we are. Helping each other to study is a good example. More importantly, those who are in need like the street kids who don't go to school. They need education, just like us. So no matter who you are, education is always important.
author: Fonza Ara Jovanka and Muhammad Al-Fathaan

title: The Humble Bear
text: ﻿ In a forest to the west, there is a sun bear who lives alone in his house. This bear's name is Bernard. Bernard really likes to eat honey muffins. He maintains and guards the beehive in the tree in front of his house. He is also good friends with the bees. One day, the beehive in the tree in front of his house fell and fell into a puddle of water. the bees panicked and sad. Bernard who saw this immediately helped the bees to clean and tidy up their beehives. Bernard also took the beehive to dry in the oven so that it could dry again. After drying and cleaning, Bernard hangs a beehive on a tree branch in front of his house. the bees were very attracted to the kind Bernard.
author: Carolina Yohana and Putra Yusuf Khomar

title: When the waters came-1
text: There were also some arrangements for food and water. Asthai school was also reopened. Here we are all fine. We are not facing any problems now. It is said that when there is destruction, there is also development. That is why we will keep smiling through such troubles. The ordeal of the children At an age where children should be given the chance to play, study and understand the world around them, the children of northern Bihar had to go through the terrible calamity of a flood situation. There is no telling how many children have lost their family members, or have seen their pets getting washed away in floodwaters before their eyes. These harsh images have been imprinted in their minds in one way or the other. It will take time for them to forget and it is not always easy to forget. Reading their thoughts in this compilation makes it clear how much the sudden flood has shocked the children. At an age when children in other regions write about flowers, butterflies, rivers and forests, when the children of the same age in northern Bihar write, they cannot escape the scenes of tragedy wreaked by the flood. If the older generation want to really fulfil their duty towards this young generation then it should be that when they grow up, they should not have to suffer such situations again. The older generation must decide to patiently work on this area of northern Bihar so that floods can stop. They must not do anything that compels the area to remain flood prone. The older generation must make hard decisions today to save these innocent hearts, this young generation. We have to look again towards the environment and improve the condition of the rivers and forests as living components of our society and move forward to establish a relationship with nature. The stories coming out of these young pens heralds this.
author: Esha Banerjee

title: SAY CHEESE
text: On Ratha Minnie was a playful rat. Minnie played in mud And Minnie became a dirty rat. The other rats started calling him "Dirty Minnnie". So Minnie stopped playing And Minnie became an idle rat. The other rats started calling him "Lazy Minnie". So Minnie started fighting with other rats And Minnie became an angry rat. The other rats started calling him "Grumpy Minnie“. So Minnie never came out of his house and played with his friends And Minnie became a lonely rat. The other rats started calling him “Lonely Minnie". So Minnie was not happy and never smiled And Minnie became a sad rat. The others rats started calling him "Unhappy Minnie“. Minnie met his friend Fannie. "How are you always happy?" asked Minnie. "I eat these magic cheese crumbs and say CHEEEEESE…" said Fannie. Fannie gave Minnie a bag full of magic cheese crumbs. Minnie came out of his house. The other rats said "Oh! here comes the Dirty, Lazy, Grumpy, Lonely and Unhappy Minnie?" Minnie swallowed the magic cheese crumb and said “CHEEEEESE..” The other rats now started calling him "Happy and Smiley Minnie".

title: Gossip
text: Buzhakkad Singh was passing by at the scene. Hearing the sounds of laughter, he asked people sitting there, "Hey brother, what's going on? Please tell me too." Gappad exclaimed with tremendous enthusiasm, “We are both narrating the tales of our grandfather.” "Brother, share their tales with me too!" Akkad said sternly, "On one condition." Buzhakkad asked, "What condition?" The one who hears the story will have to be amazed. Whoever does not applaud will have to pay a fine of two thousand rupees each." "Accepted." Buzhakkad replied. Gappad started first. My grandfather was a great craftsman. Once there was no rain in the village. Village was on the verge of experiencing a famine. Then my grandfather suggested a solution. He asked to cut the bamboos in the entire area. Connected those bamboos to each other and made holes in them in the sky. What was it then, it started raining heavily. The farmers started plowing happily. The harvest was excellent. The name of my family was also recognised." Every person sitting there looked at each other in utter disbelief. Despite not wanting that, everyone had to applaud. As it was now Akkad's turn turn to speak, he also began to gulp, “Hey brothers, my grandfather didn't need to learn any craftsmanship. His hands and teeth were extremely strong. He used to cut a tree into tracks with his teeth after uprooting it to use as a toothbrush every morning. All the villagers used to take those tracks to their homes for free.” Gappad and Buzhakkad had to say, Wow! Wow! Buzhakkad got a mischievous idea after hearing both of their stories. He stated: "Your grandfather was a great man, brothers. My grandfather never did any such thing. The sky once dispersed after being enraged by Gappad's grandfather's deeds. All of Akkad's grandfather teeth were also fallen. Both of your families' fortunes had gotten worse. Then, each family received a loan of two thousand rupees from my grandfather. That loan with you is still pending. Kindly repay that loan today." On hearing this, Gappad and Akkad stopped speaking, they got upset. Both of them started running from there quickly, seeing them running away Buzhakkad and all the people sitting there started laughing.
author: Komal Bisht

title: Rohan sees a Rainbow
text: Rohan loves rainbows and he thinks they are the best. He wants to see a real one. One day he took out his book about rainbows. The book says that rainbows come after rain. Suddenly it started to rain so Rohan runs out. He can't wait to see a rainbow. After it rained he saw something. It was something he wanted to see. A RAINBOW! He is happy. Rohan takes a notebook and draws the rainbow on it. Rohan always remembered the time he saw a rainbow.
author: Jiya Poongavanam

title: Courage!
text: Everyone was looking at him with admiration. But Dasaratha Manjhi, a simple man, was bowing down with hesitation. He was made to sit right next to the Chief Minister. Seeing such a huge crowd, he got lost in the past. His village in Gaya district was dancing before his eyes. A small settlement of Dalit people. A giant mountain standing for centuries next to the village. On the other side of the mountain were the village fields. You have to go around the whole high mountain, only then you could reach to the farm from village. Dasharatha was remembering his wedding. After marriage, his wife would help even outside the house. Dasharatha would leave for the field with the plough and the ox. Wife used to prepare food. Taking the lunch box she would circumambulate the mountain for hours, to reach the field soaked in sweat. Dasharatha would get upset seeing this condition of his wife. One day his wife said, "Dear, this mountain cannot be cut? Had the road been built, the distance of hours would have been covered in minutes. "You're right!" Dasharatha thought thinking, "The road needs to be built!" "But how?" His wife questioned. Dasharatha remained silent. In the evening, Dasharatha called a meeting of the whole village. In the meeting, he told the pain of his wife and requested everyone to do Shramdaan. “If we try together, then we can make a road by cutting the mountain,” he tried to convince the villagers. "Has it ever happened till today that it will happen now? Government is tired of trying to build a road. Had it been possible, the road would not have been built by now? Don't waste our time and labor." Everyone said in one voice, "Let it go as it is. We are all used to it." When Dasharatha started pleading again and again, the elders quipped, "Have you fallen madly in love with your Mehriya? Go now and quietly do your work" Dasharatha returned to his home but he was determined, "Road has to be built." Next Day when everyone woke up, their surprise knew no bounds. Dasharatha started cutting the rock. He was present on the mountain with pickaxe, spade, basket. Now this was everyday routine. He would sweat profusely for hours. Some would call him crazy, some called fool. But it caused no effect on Dasharatha. He fought alone with the difficulties, the diseases and various kinds of obstacles. Days turned into months and months into years. Young Dasaratha became middle-aged and the day finally arrived. The sun's rays did not even reach every house, yet there was a hurrah in the village, “The road is here… the road is here!” Everyone ran towards the Mountain. What everyone saw after reaching there was unbelievable. Everyone rubbed their eyes again and again... the muddy road in the middle of the black mountain was shining like a thin stream of water. Everyone jumped with joy. All of them lifted Dasharatha on their shoulder and started shouting loudly, "Jai Dasharatha Manjhi, Jai Dasharatha Manjhi!" Dasaratha woke up from the cheers of the people. The crowd was shouting slogans in the procession. The Chief Minister stood up to give the title of 'Pahad-man' to Dasharatha. As Dashrath moved forward, the Chief Minister hugged him. Whether a gram alone can break a big rock or not, a single man can break a mountain. Dashrath Manjhi had proved this.
author: Komal Bisht

title: Green and Blissful
text: I went to my village in the summer holidays. There I became friends with Raja. I was proud of my intelligence. I spent all the time trying to prove that I am more knowledgeable than Raja. I only told Raja that June 5 is celebrated as environment day so that people realize the importance of respecting the environment. Both of us decided that on that day, we will plant trees in the garden. On 5 June, I dressed up in a green salvar suite, dupatta and pearl necklace. I went with Raja to his garden. There we planted trees. I said to Raja "I wrote a poem on myself. Shall I recite to you?" He said "Recite". I said "Green and blissful, With nine lakh pearls embedded in the shawl, she was standing in Raja's garden." Then some children passed by and said"Corn, corn". I could not understand why they were calling me "Corn" instead of my name. Then Raja said "They are telling the meaning of the poetry that you sang".
author: Rohit Fernandes

title: The Lion Ran
text: He was wandering the jungle in search of prey. Suddenly he saw a thin woodcutter. He was telling himself " Today barley will come. Let me eat barley then I will cut wood." Then the lion pounced on him and said "You can eat the barley in your next life. First I will eat you." Seeing the lion, the woodcutter got terrified. With streetsmartness, he said "King of the jungle, you eat the barley first and then you can eat me." The lion said "All right, let me eat the barley first." As soon as the lion had eaten the barley, he felt thirsty. The lion said "What is this that you have made me eat? I am feeling thirsty." The woodcutter said "Emperor, kindly drink water from the pond. Till then I will wait here only." The lion pondered and said "You think I am a fool. While I go to drink water, you will escape." The woodcutter said "If you're worried about my disappearing, you can easily find me as my house is in the neighboring village." The lion was satisfied and went to drink water. The woodcutter ran away. Soon the day turned to night. The lion reached the woodcutter's house and roared "Oh deceiving woodcutter. Open the door. I have come to eat you." The woodcutter was scared but opened the door and said "Emperor, as I am going to die. Please fulfill my last wish. I will bring barley. Please eat the barley." The lion agreed. The woodcutter went into the kitchen and mixed a lot of chilly in the barley and presented it to the lion. As soon as the lion ate the barley, he began to perspire. He drank all the water filled in the pots in the woodcutter's home. The lion roared "What did you give me?" The woodcutter politely said "King of the jungle, I added a little chilly for taste. I eat ten times as much chilly each day. Never mind, you can eat me now." Now it became the lion's turn to be terrified. He thought that if the woodcutter eats so much chilly, he must be very pungent to eat. He gave an excuse to the woodcutter saying "After drinking all that water, my stomach is full. I am taking your leave, I will come some other time." Saying this the lion ran away not daring to turn back even once.
author: Rohit Fernandes

title: Essay
text: She was always ready to talk. But she was not interested in reading and writing. For this reason, her Essay book was her worst enemy That day all the students were going to ready out their essay to the teacher. As usual, Sarita forgot that she had to write the essay. Now what would she do? But she wasnt scared at all. When it was her turn, she looked at the teacher and stood up. She help up her book and started reading her essay. Her teacher listened to her in surprise. Her classmates were also surprised. Her essay was very interesting. However, her fun was soon put to stop. Her teacher got doubtful and said, "bring the book here". Sarita have her book to the teacher. Her teacher's doubt was right. The book was blank. Sarita was prepared to be scolded but what happened was the opposite. The teacher said, " If you have so much in your mind, can't you write it down? Sarita was shocked. She never thought of it that way, she said
author: Preethi Ramakrishnan

title: Fly-Fall Poems by B.K.Tirumalamma
text: One small sparrow was sitting on a door Then another sparrow joined it on the door | One and one together are two sparrows now One and one together are two sparrows now || Two small sparrows were sitting on a door Then another sparrow joined them on the door | Two and one together are three sparrows now Two and one together are three sparrows now || Three small sparrows were sitting on a door Then another sparrow joined them on the door| Three and one together are four sparrows now Three and one together are four sparrows now || Four small sparrows were sitting on a door Then another sparrow joined them on the door| Four and one together are five sparrows now Four and one together are five sparrows now || Leaving - they become Five small birds were sitting on a tree Then one bird flapped its wings and flew away in glee| With one of them leaving the five, there are four birds now With one of them leaving the five, there are four birds now || Four small birds were sitting on a tree Then one bird flapped its wings and flew away in glee| With one of them leaving the four, there are three birds now With one of them leaving the four, there are three birds now || Three small birds were sitting on a tree Then one bird flapped its wings and flew away in glee| With one of them leaving the three, there are two birds now With one of them leaving the three, there are two birds now || Two small birds were sitting on a tree Then one bird flapped its wings and flew away in glee| With one of them leaving the two, there is one bird now With one of them leaving the two, there is one bird now || One small bird was sitting on a tree Then that bird flapped its wings and flew away in glee| With the one bird leaving, there are no birds now With the one bird leaving, there are no birds now || Gravity Throw a ball up Throw it higher up See it come down See it touch the ground || Again throw it up See it come down Throw it up and up See the ball come down See it touch the ground || Fly Fly Fly Higher and higher you fly You will come down You will touch the ground || Fly high again You will come down again Fly again and again You will have to come down You will have to touch the ground || B.K Tirumalamma (/1922 - /2001) B.K Tirumalamma was born on /22 - isn't this a wonderful number? Tirumalamma used to love numbers. Her wish was for every child to go to a school and be introduced into the world of numbers and alphabets. To fulfil this wish, she founded a play school in Malleshwaram, Bangalore in the year 1953. In order to simplify teaching mathematics and science to kids, she wrote several simple poems. 'Kanda Akshara Kali', 'Kannada Oduveya', 'Namma Mane', 'Odi Keluva Kathegalu', 'Puttanigala Vaignyanika Kathegalu', 'Namma Bengaluru Mathu Punyakoti' are some of her illustrious poems. These poems are used even today in numerous schools. Tirumalamma also designed low cost teaching aids which can be used to simplify learning for children. Along with her senior teachers, she visited various villages to exhibit the usage of these teaching aids. In 1979, she started a training centre for pre-primary teachers.
author: Nirmala Shekar

title: How the Camel Got His Hump
text: In the beginning of years, when the world was so new and all, and the Animals were just beginning to work for Man, there was a Camel, and he lived in the middle of a Howling Desert because he did not want to work; and besides, he was a Howler himself. So he ate sticks and thorns and tamarisks and milkweed and prickles, most 'Scruciating idle; and when anybody spoke to him he said 'Humph!' Just 'Humph!' and no more. Presently the Horse came to him on Monday morning, with a saddle on his back and a bit in his mouth, and said, 'Camel, O Camel, come out and trot like the rest of us.' 'Humph!' said the Camel; and the Horse went away and told the Man. Presently the Dog came to him, with a stick in his mouth, and said, 'Camel, O Camel, come and fetch and carry like the rest of us.' ' Humph!' said the Camel; and the Dog went away and told the Man. Presently the Ox came to him, with the yoke on his neck and said, 'Camel, O Camel, come and plough like the rest of us.' 'Humph!' said the Camel; and the Ox went away and told the Man. At the end of the day the Man called the Horse and the Dog and the Ox together, and said, 'Three, O Three, I'm very sorry for you (with the world so new-and-all); but that Humph-thing in the Desert can't work, or he would have been here by now, so I am going to leave him alone, and you must work double-time to make up for it.' That made the Three very angry (with the world so new-and-all), and they held a palaver, and an indaba, and a punchayet, and a pow-wow on the edge of the Desert; and the Camel came chewing on milkweed most 'scruciating idle, and laughed at them. Then he said 'Humph!' and went away again. Presently there came along the Djinn in charge of All Deserts, rolling in a cloud of dust and he stopped to palaver and pow-pow with the Three. Djinn of All Deserts,' said the Horse, 'is it right for any one to be idle, with the world so new-and-all?' 'Certainly not,' said the Djinn. Well,' said the Horse, 'there's a thing in the middle of your Howling Desert (and he's a Howler himself) with a long neck and long legs, and he hasn't done a stroke of work since Monday morning. He won't trot.'.' Whew!' said the Djinn, whistling, 'that's my Camel, for all the gold in Arabia! What does he say about it?' 'He says "Humph!"' said the Dog; 'and he won't fetch and carry.'.' 'Only "Humph!"; and he won't plough,' said the Ox. ' Very good,' said the Djinn. 'I'll humph him if you will kindly wait a minute.' The Djinn rolled himself up in his dust-cloak, and took a bearing across the desert, and found the Camel most 'scruciatingly idle, looking at his own reflection in a pool of water. 'My long and bubbling friend,' said the Djinn, 'what's this I hear of your doing no work, with the world so new-and-all?' ' Humph!' said the Camel. The Djinn sat down, with his chin in his hand, and began to think a Great Magic, while the Camel looked at his own reflection in the pool of water. You've given the Three extra work ever since Monday morning, all on account of your 'scruciating idleness,' said the Djinn; and he went on thinking Magics, with his chin in his hand. ' Humph!' said the Camel. 'I shouldn't say that again if I were you,' said the Djinn; you might say it once too often. Bubbles, I want you to work.' And the Camel said 'Humph!' again; but no sooner had he said it than he saw his back, that he was so proud of, puffing up and puffing up into a great big lolloping humph. 'Do you see that?' said the Djinn. 'That's your very own humph that you've brought upon your very own self by not working. 'How can I,' said the Camel, 'with this humph on my back?' 'That's made a-purpose,' said the Djinn, 'all because you missed those three days. You will be able to work now for three days without eating, because you can live on your humph; and don't you ever say I never did anything for you. Come out of the Desert and go to the Three, and behave. And the Camel humphed himself, humph and all, and went away to join the Three. And from that day to this the Camel always wears a humph (we call it 'hump' now, not to hurt his feelings); but he has never yet caught up with the three days that he missed at the beginning of the world, and he has never yet learned how to behave.
author: Advit Aswal
illustrator: Jitendra Thakur; Muniza Shariq; Sangeetha Kadur

title: My first day of school!
text: Today is my first day of school! I am so excited. I get up, brush my teeth, take a bath, eat my breakfast and my dad takes me to school! At school I say good morning to the teacher, say hi to my friends, and get ready for the class. Now it's Math class time. the teacher comes in and we all say 'Good morning mam'. An hour goes though. Now it's recess! everyone takes their water bottles and leaves the classroom. But when they reach there OH NO...a large snake. The school watchman comes with a cage. He scoops the snake into the cage and closes the cage. Everyone happily goes out to play. That was a fun day. We all go home and tell our parents about what happened. They were happy we were safe. I can't wait to go to school again!
author: Varunavi Pulipati
illustrator: Ajay Hembron; Google India; Jayesh Sivan; Mohith O; Priya Dali

title: Mr. Bernard's Farm
text: Today was an exciting day for Nancy Bernard, she was going to visit her Grandfathers farm, from the stories her grandmother had told her while she was at her house, she learnt that the farm had numerous animals and recently, a baby calf was born. She had packed 2 satchels with her, and a few toys for the animals. Nancy loved all kinds of animals. She sat in her car with her grandfather's, one driving one sitting. After a 2 hour drove they finally reached their farm. " Yay, were here " said Nancy as she climbed out of the car and ran towards the farm, her Grandad followed. " Bye Dada " she said as the car made its way back to their home town. " Ah, Nancy how are you doing " asked Grandma " I am doing well, Thankyou " she replied She hugged her and sat down to listen to one of her lovely stories, Grandma loved to rock on her rocking chair. " I am serving lunch, enjoy ", " Thankyou, but I have already eaten I am going out. Nancy saw her Grandfather, looking at the animal enclosures proudly, he had made them from the bamboo which grew nearby. Then he walked away to bring them some food. " Hello Miss cow, how are you doing have you been eating well? what about you Mr. Goat and you Ms. hen " asked Nancy. Then she raced off further into the farm. Further inside, she saw a flock of Hornbills resting on a tree branch, and Tofu the dog looking at them, " You have been a good guard dog haven't you, Tofu here take a treat " Nancy said tossing a treat to the hungry dog. The Hornbills were hungry to, so they flew up the tree to feast on some Mangoes. Nancy walked her way to the barn where she saw Grandfather on the floor and with an open sack of carrots. " Ha ha ha he he " laughed Nancy, " Looks like the animals know their sense of style " " Certainly, the do " joined in Grandfather. Nancy helped him up and walked to the chicken coop. " Oh No " gasped Grandfather, " what have you done naughty chicken " Nancy looked at the mess the chicken had made. " Nancy would you go look for the other farm animals, they seem to have broken free from my Bamboo enclosures " " Sure thing " replied Nancy as she walked away further into the farm. Nancy made her way into the attic where she heard a " Mehh" she flashed her torch light to the stack above and saw a goat enjoying Grandad's hay stock. The goat got scared and fell out of the haystack, but Nancy was able to catch him, she took him to his cage. Then she went to the Milk Yard. " Huh " said Nancy while looking at the ground, " What a lot of sticky stuff " she walked further and saw a cow eating from a bucket, " Doesn't Grandpa feed you enough " asked Nancy " Don't worry i will bring you back with your friends ". Nancy took the cow to its grazing fields. Then she sat down on the grass and took a break. Meanwhile, Grandpa had also landed a victory by finding the naughty duck hiding beneath a basket, and to his surprise had laid an egg. " Oh little duck let me make this place more comfy for you top nurse your egg while it hatches " he said. He brought some grass and hay with a cloth and made it look like a nest. It started getting hot, Nancy made her way home and so did Grandpa but he was slightly late he had to do a lot of work he brought a crateful of eggs home and gave them to grandma. " These eggs look tasty" she said " They are, they came from our healthiest chicken " replied Grandpa. They all ate eggs and went to bed. What a splendid trip! The Animals also went to bed. For an afternoon sleep. Hope you enjoyed reading!
author: Jiya G
illustrator: Imile  Wepener; Isuri Dayaratne; Omkar Mahashabde; Sagar Asnani; Vibhash Pandey

title: If only ! there was no sun
text: Mother said to bunny. Bunny deer opened his eyes and looked at the sky. The white shining sun was visible on the blue-blue sky. Bunny said with a sad heart- "Suraj uncle, why do you come out in the sky everyday?" As soon as you come Birds start chirping... animals start running.. and then... they wake me up Just then a squirrel jumped from the tree in front of him. he woke up slowly and started seeing everywhere. he saw- "mother and hathi dada are talking." Hathi dada was telling mother - "Bunny is still very small. Gradually he will start waking up early on his own." but mother was saying that bunny should wake up early in the morning. Just then bunny ran and cuddled up to his mom. Bunny now went out for a walk in the forest with his mother and Hathi Dada. Mother would walk him to the forest every day and Tells the story of the forest too. Sometimes a lion, sometimes a tree... One day mother told Bunny the story of the goddess of the jungle. Bunny was overjoyed to hear the story of the goddess of the jungle. He started thinking - "Will the goddess of the forest make the sun disappear?" Mother says that the goddess of the forest listens to everyone. one day without telling mom bunny deer secretly left. He had to meet the goddess of the forest. Hathi Dada had told that- "The goddess of the forest lives in the dense forest." The dense forest was far away. Bunny was very tired of walking. Exhausted, he sat under a big tree. He closed his eyes and called out to the goddess of the forest- “Goddess of the forest, Mother would wake me up as soon as the sun came up in the sky. Make Suraj Chacha disappear..... make Suraj Chacha disappear." Bunny kept saying this with his eyes closed. As soon as bunny opened his eyes, it was dark. He was very happy. Bunny was happy that The goddess of the forest agreed to him. Mother's words also came true. Now he had to go to his mother. Thinking how he would go in the dark Bunny began to speak loudly- "Goddess of the jungle, I am bunny deer....... I want to go to mom. You bring back Suraj uncle. Bunny kept saying the same thing over and over again. Then he heard a voice - "Sometimes you say make the sun disappear, Sometimes you say bring back the sun. bunny what do you want? " Bunny cried and said - "Goddess of the jungle, please bring back Suraj uncle. I am scared. I want to go home. " Then he felt that someone jumped and sat beside him. He put his hand on the bunny deer and said- "Bunny, I am Chintu monkey. I live on this tree. Don't you be afraid I am with you." Bunny deer told Chintu monkey that Why did he want to make the sun disappear? Chintu Monkey explained - “Sun is very important. it gives us light And we can see. We get heat from the sun. Trees grow only from sunlight. We eat those trees and plants. We cannot survive without the sun. Understanding the trouble of the bunny, Chintu Monkey said- "The goddess of the forest has not made the sun disappear. This forest is dense. Suraj uncle did not disappear. He is hiding behind the hill." Throughout the night, bunny deer was sitting near Chintu the monkey. He had understood how important the sun was. Today he was waiting for Suraj uncle to come early. As the sun shone in the morning sky, Bunny deer was very happy and started walking towards his house with Chintu Monkey.
author: Komal Bisht

title: Animals in a zoo
text: ﻿ ﻿ once a pon a time there was a zoo in that zoo there were so many animals. the names are: Buggy, Maw, leporpped and prow. Then when a girl lived her name was Joshu. Her age: 9 years old.
