title: The Monkey, Rabbit And The Tortoise
text: There was a cute rabbit. He loved to eat carrots, grass and would play with his friends everywhere. One day he saw a tortoise eating his carrots so he took the carrots and ran away. So he went crying to his mother and told her everything, she told him to share. When day the rabbit was sleeping in a tunnel and saw the same tortoise walking. He screamed at the tortoise that don't come to my tunnel again. So then the tortoise did not came but then the rabbit was eating the monkeys bananas and the monkey saw that. But the monkey did not scream he just went to his house. The rabbit was shocked to see that why did the monkey not screamed at him. He went to the monkeys home and asked. The monkey said the rabbit that I do not scream at anyone because I am polite. The rabbit understood and then he became polite to the tortoise and they all became best friends.
author: Wanika Soni
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Padmanabh; Padmanabh; Promina Shreshtha; Subi Bosa; Tanaya Vyas; Youm Kosal

title: The strange and careless squirrel
text: All the squirrels were playing in the meadow, happily with fun and joy,while one naughty squirrel named Chikki. She was very naughty she never acted like a good squirrel. She always spend her time making fun of others and causing troubles in the house nearby. All the naughty things her mother told her not to do so. She always did these naughty acts. Her mother warned her several times not wander off and trouble others.One day she wandered off and started troubling the little creatures, just as her mother told her not to. She climbed up up a tree to see what else troubles she could make. She also troubled the small creatures on the tree. Suddenly she fell down from the tree. She found herself in another unknown place.She was a little scared but Chikki tried to stand up brave. But when she tried to stand up all the little creatures that she had troubled started laughing at her. She tried to run away but the thought of the little creatures laughing at her made her very scared to run away. Then suddenly an owl flew that way and carried her away.She really did not feel safe when the owl carried her from those horrid little creatures. Then she looked up at the owl and said to put her down trying to act brave. The owl did not respond but looked down at her and put her down. There were two insects. An ant and a bee. The bee hid herself under the metal piece Chikki was standing on.Chikki really did not notice the bee but looked curiously at the ant and her surroundings. She tried to ask the ant her name but she felt guilty of troubling the little creatures Then the owl returned and she asked angrily to fly her home. She would not tell her the way since she herself did not know the way. The owl did not respond she just looked down at her. So she just tried to get home. She missed her mother but she did not learn yet not to be naughty Then she reached a very strange and beautiful place with friendly animals around. They all treated her kindly and they played fun games. She almost forgot the sadness of being lost. Then she woke up to find herself at home cuddled up nice and tight in bed. She promised herself not to be naughty and not tell a word about her strange dream to her mother. Her mother told her to brush her teeth and drink milk which she followed. Her mother taught her.She listened carefully and asked her doubts. Her mother gifted her a book for being a good girl. She sat on a tree and read it the whole day. Now Chikki the naughty squirrel changed all thanks to her dream. That is very good news indeed.
author: HARINI MANIKANDAN
illustrator: Gayatri Hingorani; Prashant Soni; Raju Babu Shakya

title: Pinky's World
text: Pinky was very fond of dreaming. Pinky was a two-year-old fish who lived in the sea. Pinky had a dream that she would meet with humans and talk to them. Pinky would often speak to her parents and they laughed off her words. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ Pinky decided one day that she would go to the boats looking at the sea and talk to the people sitting in it. When Pinky started insisting, the parents took her to the grandmother who was very intelligent. Grandmother explained to Pinky that "Cockboats lay nets in which you can never come back if you get caught" and other dangers. Pinky ignored Grandmother's words. As soon as everyone fell asleep, Pinky started looking at the moonlight falling in the sea and got lost in the world of her dreams. Suddenly her eyes fell on a cockboat. Pinky thought nothing and started following that cockboat. The cockboat picked up its speed and kept moving away from his sight. Pinky gets disappointed seeing her going away and starts going back home. Pinky had come far away from home and the way was unknown to her. Sometimes she could see shining eyes from afar, sometimes someone would pass by at great speed. Pinky panicked and started missing her grandmother and parents. Pinky got so nervous that she hid behind a stone nearby. Then Pinky understood that if she had obeyed her grandmother, she would have been at home with her family today. Thinking this, Pinky started crying. Suddenly Pinky heard a voice from afar that someone was calling her and suddenly her eyes opened. She found that she was at his house and it was all a nightmare. Pinky got up and went straight to her parents, started crying and told about her dream. The parents hugged her without saying anything. Pinky was happy now and understood that it is wise to obey the elders.
author: champak meher
illustrator: Bulbul Sharma; Monappa; Rajiv Eipe; Srikrishna Kedilaya

title: I will also go to Patna
text: I am Tunny. Mother calls me Tuntun. I study in class five. I am the youngest among my brothers and sisters, therefore everyone in the house considers me very small. I enjoy playing cricket and hockey. I also love going out. My mother doesn't let me go anywhere alone. She says, "Tuntun, You are a little girl now. Once you grow up you can go alone." I am very happy today. My elder sister Usha is going to come home from hostel today. Age difference between me and my sister is very big. The older she is, the more she studies. She loves me very much. Maybe that's why I run towards the door even every time I hear a crack of sound asking did she come? Today I am not able to do any work. At last the wait is over. Sister has come. I run to touch his feet. Didi hugs me and falls in love. She brought me a toy - 'a cute rabbit with soft white hair, pink eyes', along with a lot of colorful toffees. Vacation Time flies away with my sister. She started going to the hostel. I wanted to stay with her for a few more days. I also want to visit Patna. After all, it is the capital of our state Bihar. My friend Munni told me that there are many good places to visit and see in patna. Like- Museum, Golghar, Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park, Planetarium, Shri Krishna Science Center, Kargil Chowk, Martyrs Memorial, Mahatma Gandhi Setu, Agal Kuan, Takht Shri Harmandir, Patan Devi, Stone Masjid, Pastor's Haveli, Kamaldeh Jain Temple, Khanqah Imadiya, Khanqah Mujibiya, Dargah Sharif Mitanghat, Buddha Park, Chanakya Law University, Chandragupta Institute of Management etc. I also want to see all these places. Mother did not want to let me go to Patna. I was adamant on going with Didi. Didi somehow convinced mother. Now there was no bounds to my happiness. Both of us sisters boarded the bus to Patna. I am excited to travel, but my eyes got wet while separating from my parents. Dad put his hand on my head through the window. Then the driver sounded the horn and the bus started towards Patna...
author: Komal Bisht

title: At the River
text: Akash went to the river. There were many people there. Ma began washing clothes. Splash! Dada jumped into the river. Akash could not see Dada in the river! Akash was afraid. He shouted, “Dada…! Dada…!” Dada quickly came up from under the water. “Aku, come in for a ride!” Ma put Akash on Dada’s shoulders. They both played in the water. Akash splashed the water. Splish-Splosh! It was so much fun!
author: Rupali Bhave

title: Sam's Treasures
text: Sam and Dara were at the park. A shiny sparkle caught Sam’s eye. A crystal ball! A magic pearl! A treasure for Sam’s collection! “That’s not treasure – that’s junk,” said Dara. She didn’t like the things Sam found. That was fine with Sam. “Time to go treasure hunting!” Off he went with his backpack. Between the bushes Sam found a crown and a magic wand. Under an old log he found monsters and creepy creatures. No thank you! Among the flowers Sam found a chest and a ring. In the stream Sam found a message in a bottle and a wise old wizard. By the lamp post Sam found a sports car and a victory trophy. Time to show Dara all the treasures he had found! Dara was crying. “I lost my ring,” said Dara. “I don’t know where I dropped it.” That sounded like something Sam had found. It was! It was Dara’s ring! “Thank you, Sam! You DO find treasures!”
author: Jon Keevy

title: Grandma's roof
text: We go to our grandma's house in vacations. We love the roof of grandma's house. we enjoy a lot during Diwali vacations. We fly Kites during Christmas vacations. We stay on the roof all the time during summer holidays. we play we sleep on the roof Birds come to eat papads and we fly them away. we pluck guawa's on the roof once i saw a monkey on a tree and i got scared. Grandma says, they have come to meet friends from Mumbai
author: sanjali jain

title: Alex's Super Medicine
text: I’m not feeling so good, Mom. Let’s visit Dr Bongi. She can help. Drink this medicine, Alex. It will make you feel better. But I don’t like medicine. It’s yucky. Jett, I’ll let you play with my shiny red car if you drink my medicine. Eeew, no way! How can I make my medicine taste better? I know, I’ll put it on my sandwich. Urgh! Maybe I should hide it away. I know, I’ll hide it in the garden. Oh no! I’d better try something else. I know, I’ll hide it in a bird’s nest. Aaah! Hmm, maybe I should just try it? Wooah, this is actually so much fun! I feel something... What’s happening? I feel so much better! And all I had to do was drink my medicine. You did it, Alex! We’re so proud of you.
author: Kim  Rex

title: The Box
text: Andi is bored. Max is bored, too. “What’s in the box, Dad?” It’s only fruit and vegetables. “Do you want to play with it?” “What will we do with the box?” Asanda comes to play. “Wow! What a cool box!” WHOOOOSH Paul comes to play. “Wow! What a cool box!” RA HH HR RR Niki comes to play. “Wow! What a cool box!” WHEEEEE What a cool box.
author: Tania  Kliphuis

title: Baby Mongoose Goes Looking For a Frog
text: Bhave Baby Mongoose is bored of eating cluster figs! She sets out to hunt for a frog. But how does a frog look? “Hey, are you a frog?” “No! I’m a heron. A frog has four legs.” “Hey, you have four legs. Are you a frog?” “No! A frog has large eyes.” “Your eyes are as large as the full moon. I am sure you are a frog!” “No! I am an owl. A frog is green in colour.” “Ah! You are green in colour. You must be a frog!” “No! I am a grasshopper. A frog has spots.” “You have spots. Are you a frog?” “I do have spots, but can you see four legs?” “Four legs… Large eyes… Green colour… Black spots…” “You are a frog! Am I right?” “Yes, you are right! I am a frog! And I can jump too.” “Like this!” “Oh no! I will have to eat cluster figs again today!”
author: Rupali Bhave

title: Zibu and Zizo
text: Zibu and Zizo are twin brothers. ‘They look the same,’ people always say. Mama buys them the same clothes. They go to the same school. Zibu and Zizo both like banana bread. Sometimes Zibu and Zizo say... Hello!!...at the same time. Zibu likes soccer. Zizo likes drawing pictures. Zibu likes to talk to people. Zizo likes to keep to himself. Zibu likes counting numbers. He wants to be an accountant. Zizo likes learning new words. He wants to write books. ‘How come Zibu and Zizo look the same, but like different things?’ ask the children at school. 'We look the same, but we are different and like different things and that's okay.'
author: Refilwe  Nsibande

title: What's Next?
text: Fatima is always busy! She loves to run and play. Her favourite part of the day is when Grandpa arrives. “How should we spend our day, Fatima?” asks Grandpa. “I know!” says Fatima. “Let’s go to the park.” “I can see the whole world from up here,” Fatima shouts. “I have an idea!” “Let’s play superheroes and pick up the litter,” says Fatima. “Great stuff! Now you can see all the flowers.” “What’s next?” asks Grandpa. “Weeeeeeeee!” “What a crazy cool kid you are!” says Grandpa. “What’s next?” “How about something cold and delicious?” says Fatima. “What’s next, kiddo?” asks Grandpa. Fatima yawns. “Let’s go home.” “Hello, Fatima,” says Mum. “What did you and Grandpa do today?” “Not much!” they both say. “What should we do tomorrow?” asks Fatima. Fatima hurries to bed. She is excited for her next adventure with her best friend, Grandpa.
author: Rayhaanah  Williams

title: A Tortise Birthday
text: There was a birthday of a tortoise named Evelyn. She thought that everyone would know that everyone one knew it was her birthday but no. She came to the class but nobody wished her. She thought she had a suprise party but she saw nothing but when she returned home. She saw everybody clapping and singing happy birthday. She was very happy. She got many gifts and said this is the best birthday party I ever had.
author: Wanika Soni
illustrator: Devendra  Pandey; Ira S.B; Kishor Joshi

title: When Nani was a Child
text: Today I was sitting with my nani, listening to one of the many stories from her childhood. Most of which she could remember were happy and funny. And we always started laughing when she remembered those memories. Sometimes she would climb trees outside with her siblings. Sometimes she and her friends exchanged messages in the form of poems. Or sometimes she would write her thoughts in her diary. One day, she was chosen to be a character in a school play. Her character was an angel. But the problem was, all she had to do was WAVE. She had absoloutely no lines. That made her a teensy bit bored. So, to keep her mind off the play, she tried many things. She went out to climb the trees, tried cooking, painted, wrote a poem and even thought about her future profession! But nothing worked. Soon she fell asleep, dreaming of the play going well, without having an outburst of boredom. The next day, when the play had started, she went to her place and started waving. She couldn't believe that she only had a small job throughout the whole performance! And those bright lights only left an outline of her for the audience to see. But two minutes before the play ended, she stopped smiling and her arms wouldn't move. She started flopping her arms. She felt silly. what would everyone think of her? They would be laughing and pointing. She growled in frustration and she was so loud that the whole play stopped. She started laughing in embarrasment. Thinking it was part of the play, the audience started laughing too! Everyone was so happy that even the grumpiest of teachers started smiling. It turned out that the play wasn't so boring after all.
author: Varnika Bhuyan
illustrator: Alankrita Amaya; Angie & Upesh; Canato Jimo; Gitanjali Iyer; Iddi  Marumba; Krishna Chandran; Mitrarun Halder; Niloufer Wadia; Partho Sengupta; Sandhya Prabhat; Somesh Kumar; Vibha Surya

title: One strange puzzle
text: There used to be an influx of visitors as soon as they came back to the village. All the women used to gather in the courtyard to meet his wife. On a similar day, gossip was going on in the courtyard. Then Ramnath's sister, Aarti, came and said, "Dhaan Singh's son Dhanraaj Singh Has come to Kathutia pier Who wants to meet should meet Otherwise, he will go to Sheetla pier!" On hearing that, Ramnath's wife stood up and went inside. All the women sitting there were looking at each other's faces. One of them asked Aarti, " What did you say that made the daughter-in-law go inside immediately?" Aarti replied. "It is a puzzle. You too try to solve it." All the women started trying to solve the puzzle. They kept making efforts for quite a while. When nobody understood anything, one of them told Aarti, "We accept defeat. Now you tell us the answer to this puzzle." Aarti while smiling said, "See, Dhaan Singh stands for paddy that is rice. Dhaan Singh's son, Dhanraaj Singh stands for boiled rice water we get from rice. Now rice and boiled rice water are in the hardwood utensils, so whosoever wants to take them should take them otherwise they will get cold which stands for going to 'Sheetla pier'." All the women said together, '"Hey, that was a strange puzzle but why did you say that to your sister-in-law?" "it is because sister-in-law loves boiled rice water and rice combination and it was hot and ready in the kitchen. Didn't you see how fast she ran towards the kitchen upon hearing the puzzle?," Aarti laughed merrily. With her, other women started laughing too.

title: The Beautiful Rose
text: There used to be an oasis at the desert, with some cactus, rose, bougainvillea and date palms. All these plants lived in harmony. Often, travellers would stop at the oasis to drink water and take a break before continuing their journey. Some travellers even camped by the oasis overnight before setting out in the morning. Travelers who stopped by the oasis were always amazed at the beautiful plants, particularly the rose plant because it always had a some flowers on it. The flowers smelled fantastic. Often the travellers would pluck a flower or two from the rose plant before setting out on their journey. Due to this it felt very prestigious and swelled with pride. Gradually the plant grew arrogant. “Hey, Bougainvillea! Don’t lean so much. You are hurting my delicate buds,” it would scream out to the bougainvillea. “Can’t you see your thorns are tearing my leaves off. Keep your spines away when I sway in the wind, you spiny Cactus!” it would scold the cactus plant. “I can’t even move, Rose. You are the one swaying yourself towards me when the wind blows,” retorted the cactus once. “Don’t talk to me like that. I know what to do. You are all jealous of me because all the travellers who come here only look at me and do not even look at any of you," the rose said. The date palm, hearing the argument tried to intervene but to no avail. The rose plant refused to listen to anyone. Now life has its ups and downs, and all living things learn their lesson at some point. This was true for the rose plant as well. Once, the oasis completely dried up and there was not a single drop of water in it. All the plants that were living in the oasis could live for a very long time without water. All of them except- the rose plant. The rose plant began withering and drying up due to lack of water. All the other plants were green and healthy. The rose felt very weak due to lack of water. It wished it could have just one drop of water to drench its roots somehow. Who would give it water, however? From where can the water be brought? Thinking thus the plant felt quite sad. After some time, it saw a small bird sitting on the cactus and dipping its beak to drink some water stored in the plant. On seeing this, the rose felt sadder. The bougainvillea noticed the drying rose. It admonished the rose plant, “See you were very rude to us just because travellers admired your flowers. However, now without water, you are the only one drying up. Rest of us are still healthy and strong.” Hearing this, the cactus quipped in, “Let us not scold the poor rose plant. It was rude to us only because it wanted to look good when people came to camp by. Rose, would you like some water? You seem dry.” The rose plant felt embarrassed of its earlier behaviour. Realizing its mistake, it apologised to everyone around and thanked the cactus for the offer. The cactus asked the little bird to sprinkle some water on the rose plant as she quenched her thirst. The bird took some water in its beak from the cactus and carefully poured it over the rose. The plant felt relieved. “Thank you so much, Cactus and little Birdie. I feel better,” said the rose. Further, it apologised to everyone for the behaviour. The bird, cactus and other plants then nursed the rose plant till the oasis was filled once again with water. Peace and harmony once again reigned the beautiful oasis and all the plants lived happily.
author: Ira Periyavallur (aka Indira VMD)

text: Rashmi was a girl who lived in a forest. That forest was owned by the King and Queen of Worshestishire. One day some men came and started cutting down the trees. Humans should control their greed and try to imporove life on land. title: PROMOTION OF A PRODUCT (Promotion Mix in Business Studies Class 12th)
text: Two sisters, Rani and Rinki are talking about the different methods that a company uses for the promotion of its products. Rani thinks that only advertising is used for promotion of a product but Rinki introduces her to other methods that are used for promotion by the firms. When I think about the promotion of a product, only advertisements come to my mind! Let's go to the library to read about the other methods of promoting a product. They read about the other elements in the promotion of a product. Through conversation they discussed that the promotion of a product includes not only advertising but also other elements like personal selling, sales promotion and publicity. Advertisements have the benefit of mass reach. With the development in art, graphics and technology, now advertisements can be designed to look more attractive and they can be placed on multiple platforms like TV, newspaper, magazines, apps, games, billboards etc With the help of advertisements, a larger number of people can be made aware of the product. Personal selling includes door to door sales. It is a flexible approach. There is direct feedback from the customer. Personal selling is the door to door sales. It is a flexible approach as the salesman can adjust his approach according to the customer. Sales promotion includes free gift offers, free sample, contests, discounts, special offers, scratch card, lucky draw etc Yesterday, I bought a new pencil box and they gave me a free pen with it. This is an example of a sales promotion technique Publicity takes place when favourable news appears in the media about a product. It does not involve direct expenditure by the firm. The message is not in control of the firm since its distributed by the media. People may feel that it is more credible than advertisements. I saw on the news yesterday that a big company is organizing a campaign for spreading awareness about sanitation in various cities and villages. The coverage by the news channels is example of publicity. It is voluntary coverage by the mass media so people believe in its credibility. Thus, they learned about the different ways in which the product of a company can be promoted by visiting the library and discussing with each other.

title: Weekend at our grandma's
text: Usually, we spend the weekend at our grandma's farmhouse. Now the monsoon is going to start. The day was almost cloudy and we spent the day looking at the fields, eating berries, and walking on the village path. Then in the afternoon, it started raining. Soon all the roads and the fields were filled with water and became muddy. In the evening, when we stepped out of our house we took a flashlight. We saw many fireflies flying, we saw them flying away. We continued our way. No sooner do we continue our way than, big fat and the disgusting-looking frog came in front of us. Then my brother jumped over the frog, but he did not notice that the frog was on his head, when we told him, he jumped with a crash! Bang! and boom! He fell into a puddle. Then his clothes got all dirty, but we managed to do so. After that Messy thing, we came out of the forest and we walked on a path that we called the moon path because whenever we go there at night, it glowed because of the glorious moon. Oh! what a view it was, the stars were twinkling and the moon was shining brightly in the sky, After crossing the moon path we reached the main road to get our car. Now, we had finally reached the car we turned off the lights and hopped inside the car. Now that was the end of our trip. We reached home and fell fast asleep thinking about the wonderful weekend we had.

title: Tanya meets Apsara
text: Meera and Tanya skipped merrily, They pranced in the udyan, the park. It was a holiday,you see. No school and no homework! What more could two little girls WISH for? "Oh, how I wish, I could meet an Apsara or a fairy," whispered Meera dreamily. " If wishes were horses, beggars would ride! " Exclaimed Tanya. "That's what my ma would have said you know. There are no Apsaras and fairies, silly girl!" "Besides, what would you do if you met a fairy? It's all very silly." “If I met a fairy, I’ll ask for a wish!” Then Meera broke into a jingle, "I’ll ask for wings and have a home in the sky, Like the pretty goose I will fly … Scaling the Himalayas, soaring high and high!” "Oh, you silly goose! You surely have your head in the clouds. You know fairies and Apsaras are just not real. That's just silly nonsense. IMPOSSIBLE. Stop it, you and your silly Apsara!" Mocked Tanya. "Hey, hey little girl, hold your horses!" Tanya heard someone yell back. She was shocked to see someone hovering above their heads... It was a saree-clad Apsara! "I am not silly. And you know impossible is ‘I am possible’. Yes, I am very much possible!" Tanya was mesmerized! With her sea-blue Saree, swan wings, parrot-feathered earings the Apsara was quite a dazzling sight! "You know normally Apsaras don’t get too bothered by you manavs, humans. But today little girl, you’ve ruffled my feathers. How dare you call us silly? How dare you call anyone silly? It’s bad manners you know, calling names!" Tanya still could not believe her eyes! “Oh, this is all a joke. A very silly joke!” She laughed aloud. "Meera are you a part of this too?" She tried to grab the fairy’s wings to check if they were real. The fairy clasped her hand firmly stopping her. "Stop being so rude, you little girl. Where are your manners?" She roared. "Prove it," challenged Tanya. "Prove to me that you really are an Apsara! Make MY wish come true!" "Ok Miss. Just grab my hand... and your wish is my COMMAND!" Roared the Apsara "Really? Well, I love the water and swimming! And I wish to be in Fish LAND," grinned Tanya teasingly. And before Tanya could say Apsara, she found herself standing near a sparkling blue lake. She was stunned by the twinkling water and the swaying lotuses! "Welcome little girl to my land!" She heard someone greet her. "WH...WHAT, who is that?" she stammered... "Hey it's me, Biliya! Look down, I am here in the water. It was a catfish! And it was speaking to her. She was astounded. "Wow, really, are you really talking to me?" She pinched herself to make sure that it was not a dream. "Hello Miss, look, look at us too!" She heard some shrieks. "Down, down here miss. " We can do somersault too. WHEEE.... Just learnt that in our gymnastics class, you SEEE..." Tanya gawked at the water. She was fascinated to see a school of little fish performing somersaults. And she clapped her hands in glee! She noticed a pair of them whispering to each other. And she thought they were giggling too. "Hey Miss, we are besties, Siya and I! We splash and swim together. We dance and prance together. I am Gia by the way. And we never ever leave each other's side!" When she heard that, tears filled Tanya's eyes. Suddenly she realized that she was all alone. She wondered where her bestie Meera was. She had left her behind! "Oh, where is Meera! Oh, I wish to be back with Meera, my bestie..." she whimpered. And before she could say Apsara, dumbfounded, she found herself back in the udyan. Her bestie Meera was buried in a bunch of flowers. And so was she! "Hey, hey Tanya. Where were you lost? " Meera nudged her. "These Jasmine flowers are divine aren't they? And such glorious hibiscus flowers, Ganpati bappa’s favourite!" Tanya just nodded her head meekly. She was still in a daze. She tried to take in the surroundings. And just then she noticed a bluish haze in the sky. It was a team of Apsaras making their way home, carrying some hibiscus and jasmines too... Take Aways If wishes were horses, beggars would ride: proverb: If you could achieve your aims simply by wishing for them, life would be very easy head in the clouds: be absentminded or impractical Silly goose: when you call someone a “silly goose,” you are saying that they are being foolish in some way hold your horses: used to tell someone to stop and consider carefully their decision or opinion about something Take Aways ruffled my feathers. to upset or offend people could not believe her eyes idiom: (also not believe your ears) to be very surprised have to pinch yourself: phrase: be surprised when something very good happens.
author: Rutuja Joshi

title: Anurag- Real Hero
text: Hello Friends!! Today I am going to tell you a story about a real hero. No, he is not a film star but he is Anurag, a small boy who stays with his parents in Goa. He belongs to a poor family. His parents use to collect garbage like plastic bottles, wrappers, etc. for their living. Anurag use to stay in a slum near beach. He always use to visit beach by evenings along with his parents. He always use to carry one bag along with him when he use to visit beach so that if he sees any wrapper or any plastic bottle lying, he would pick it up and give that to his parents. He just felt that he is helping his parents to earn more but later he started enjoying this. He thought that people should always keep surroundings clean. He was motivated by Swachh Bharat mission initiated by our Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Many people use to visit beach by evening. Among them, there was a group of boys aged 18 to 20 years. They belong to rich families and use to party there till late night. They never cared about others and use to throw garbage in the sea. Many times Anurag saw this and he felt bad as cold drink cans and food wrappers which they use to throw would impact sea creatures and would be harmful to ecosystem. He quietly used to pick that garbage which they use to throw in the beach. He tried to explain them the importance of keeping surrounding clean but they never listened to them. He thought to make those boys understand in a effective way. He took few of his friends and planned to play a street play to explain the importance of Life on land and in water. On weekend they went at the place where those boys were partying and started showing the play. In that they highlighted how by throwing can and wrappers in the sea, fishes and other creatures gets stuck and pay that price for their life. Similarly they showed that by throwing garbage on land, increases pollution and effect ecosystem. Anurag and his friends named their group as EARTH AVENGERS and started doing these plays to create awareness about life on land and life below water. They were able to create awareness about these all in the society. For this they are getting rewarded by Chief Minister of Goa for encouraging people to think beyond themselves, to think about EARTH. I am also going to attend the felicitation of Anurag and his friends. Kuddos to them. HIP HIP HURRAY...... I request you all to be like Anurag.

illustrator: Advit Aswal; Asha Susan  Alex; Brian Wambi; Rijuta Ghate; Shreeya Wagh; Sunaina  Coelho

title: How Tasty?
text: Shruthi said, “Mommy. There is no salt in the gravy. Give me little salt to add.” John said, “Is the sugar in the cornflakes sufficient for you, Mark? I need more sugar in the dish.” Gopal said, “This pappad is very salty. We may land up with blood pressure if we eat so much salt.” Pramod thought, “This banana is not fully ripe. It would have tasted better if it was fully ripe.” Kala thought, “These jalebis are too sweet. My teacher said you get diabetes if you eat too sweet dishes.” Pavithra said, “These mangoes are so ripe and tasty.” Ismail said, “ Try my tasty biryani. It has the right amounts of spices and oil.” Food tastes good only when the ingredients like salt, sugar, spices, and oil are in the right amount. Too much or too less of any ingredient reduces the taste of the food. Similarly, a fruit is tasty only when it is ripe and not when unripe. A balanced tasty food keeps us healthy and strong. Whatever the taste of your food, don’t forget to share it with others.

title: Rose's first day of school
text: It is Rose's first day of school. She was anxious if she would make friends. As she stepped inside her class, she could feel all eyes staring at her. As she was going to talk to one of her classmate, the teacher said ' Students I would like you to meet our new student named Rose.'All the students started to whisper. Rose felt akward, she was going to sit back on her seat when sudenly she fell. All the students started to laugh. She felt very embaresed and was about to cry. it was lunch break all students paired up and talked to eachother exept for poor little Rose. She was upset and thought ''Why did my mom shift me here, I loved my old school.'' After some time, she was was going to the bathroom to wash her hands. When suddenly, a girl came and said ''we are sorry that we all laughed at you.'' she continued '' here is an apology card from all of us.'' Then the girl called Rose to the other girls and they all had a fun time and yes she forgived them and they became friends. From that day on she loved her new school. title: WHY THE CRICKET CHIRPS
text: Before there were seasons, the cricket could fly. He flew faster than the bumblebee. He flew higher than the falcon. And he flew fancier than the flying duck (who was quite a fancy flier). The cricket had flown all over the world. He flew to the East. Then he flew to the West. And then he flew to the South. But he had never flown North. The caterpillar tried to warn him that he should not try. “It’s very cold up north,” said the caterpillar. “Too cold for an caterpillar and too cold for a cricket.” The cricket, however, did not listen, because crickets do whatever they want. He set off for the North that very night. It did not take him long to get there because he was such a fantastically fast and fancy flier. The cricket landed next to a pine tree as the sun began setting. There was snow everywhere he looked. There was snow on the trees. There was snow on the ground. And there was snow on top of the mountains. The Moose came walking over to him very slowly. “Ohhhh…Hello,” said the moose. “Bundle up, nighttime is coming.” He flew up into a pine tree to settle in for a good sleep. He did this quickly because he is such an incredibly fast and fancy flier. The cricket did not listen, because crickets do whatever they want. He flew up into a pine tree to settle in for a good sleep. He did this quickly because he is such an incredibly fast and fancy flier. The Owl came flying over to the same branch. “You should find some shelter from the cold night,” said the owl. The cricket did not listen, because crickets do whatever they want. He decided to rest on a pile of twigs. He was sleepier than he had ever been, from all the remarkably fast and fancy flying. The cricket did not listen, because crickets do whatever they want. He decided to rest on a pile of twigs. He was sleepier than he had ever been, from all the remarkably fast and fancy flying. The cricket slept all through the night until morning. When he woke up he was ready to go home and tell the ant about his trip. He hopped high in the air to start flying, but he couldn’t. Instead he fell right back into the snow. He hopped again, even higher this time, but his wings would not work. They had frozen solid during the cold night. He tried to warm them up by rubbing them together but it was no use. The cricket had to hop all the way home. It took him days and days to return. He tried to warm them up by rubbing them together but it was no use. The cricket had to hop all the way home. It took him days and days to return. By the time he got back, his wings had almost become unfrozen. When he rubbed them together this time, they made a chirping noise that no one in the forest had ever heard before. And every time he rubbed his wings together they chirped a little bit louder and got a little less frozen. But it is important to know, dear reader, that wings are special and fragile things. This is why the greatest care should always be taken around them. They are not meant to be frozen, and once they are, they may never be the same again. Even though the cricket’s wings were no longer frozen, he still could not fly. And ever since then the cricket stays on the ground like his friend the ant, and hops from place to place. And now the cricket is the fastest and fanciest hopper there is. At nighttime, you can hear him chirping, from rubbing his wings together to keep warm. But he is doing much more than just that… The cricket is telling you how warm or cold it is by chirping. He chirps faster when it is warm, and slower when it is cold. This way, you will not make the same mistake that he did. However, that is only if you decide to listen… *Dolbear’s Law states that if you count the number of time a cricket chirps in 15 seconds, and add 40, it will give you (roughly) the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit. *Dolbear’s Law states that if you count the number of time a cricket chirps in 15 seconds, and add 40, it will give you (roughly) the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.

title: the foolish donkey
text: Once upon a time, a salt seller used to carry salt bags on his donkey's back to the market everyday. One day, when the donkey was carrying the salt bag, he suddenly tumbled down the stream, and the salt bag on his back also fell into the water. Since most of the salt got dissolved in water, the salt bag became very light. It made the donkey very happy. The cunning donkey decided to follow the same trick every day. The salt seller came to know about the cunning plan and soon decided to teach the donkey a lesson for his life. The very next day, the salt seller replaced the salt with cotton. Since the donkey played the same trick, assuming that the cotton bag will become lighter. As the cotton became wet, it got heavier and heavier and very difficult to carry. Soon the donkey realized his master’s trick, and it learned the lesson. The donkey did not perform any such trick in the future, and his master was now pleased.
author: S Sai Prateek
illustrator: Bianca de Jong; Samit  Shrestha; Shweta Mohapatra; Vidyun Sabhaney

title: the foolish lion
text: In a forest there lived a lion. He had grown old and could not run fast anymore. As days went by it became more and more difficult for him to hunt. One day while he was wandering through the forest in search of food, he came across a cave. He peeped in and smelt the air inside the cave. “Some animal must be staying here," he said to himself. He crept inside the cave only to find it empty. “I will hide inside and wait for the animal to return," he thought. The cave was the home of a jackal. Everyday, the jackal would go out in search of food and return to the cave in the evening to rest. That evening, the jackal after having his meal started towards home. But as he came closer, he felt something wrong. Everything around him very quiet. “Something is wrong," the jackal said to himself. “Why are all the birds and insects so silent?" Very slowly and cautiously, he walked towards his cave. He looked around him, watching for any signs of danger. As he got closer to the mouth of the cave, all his instincts alerted him of danger. “I have to make sure that everything is alright," thought the jackal. Suddenly, he thought of a plan. The clever jackal called out to the cave. “Hello my good cave, what happened to you today? Why are you so quiet?" The jackal’s voice echoed deep inside the cave. The lion, who by now could control his hunger no longer, thought to himself, “I think it is because I am here that the cave is silent. Before the jackal realises that something is wrong, I should do something." The jackal continued to call out, “Have you forgotten our agreement cave? You are supposed to greet me when I return home." The lion tried to make his voice sound hollow and called out from within the cave, “Welcome home my friend." The birds chirped loudly and flew away on hearing the lion’s roar. As for the jackal, he shook with fear. Before the hungry lion could pounce on him and eat him up, the jackal ran for his dear life as fast as his legs could carry him. The lion waited for a long while for the jackal to enter the cave. But when the jackal did not come in, the lion realised that he had been fooled. He cursed himself for his foolishness that made him lose a prey.
author: S Sai Prateek
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Partho Sengupta; Rob Owen; Vidyun Sabhaney

title: How to catch a Butterfly
text: Today is a beautiful day! and I am playing in the garden, full of trees, plants, flowers and colorful butterflies. Ri likes spending time in the garden. I love butterflies! said Ri "they are so colorful. Just like a rainbow"! "Hey! I want to catch a butterfly!", Said Ri with full enthusiasm, "come with me friends, I will teach you, how to catch a butterfly? First of all, Lets set some rules Rule 1. Not hurting the butterflies. No damage to their wings. Rule 2. Not keeping them in Jars etc. Rule 3. Not playing with them. Rule 4. Gently catch them with the tip of your thumb and index figure and release them back. Lets follow the steps: 1. Wear high boots to protect you from any possible insect bites and thorny bushes. 2. Find a lovely Garden full of flowers and butterflies 3. Find a bushy patch 4. Aim at a butterfly which is flying low. Gently chase them. Tip toe! Tip Toe. The least amount of sounds and movements Chase flower to flower! In the garden, be careful of thorns and other pits Shhhhh! When the butterfly has rested on the flower Catch the butterfly! Wow! Well-done! Have you ever felt how soft their wings are? Don't hold them too tight or for too long!.... Take a closer look... Take a moment to appreciate its beauty! However, a captive butterfly won't be happy. Let's say good-bye. and... Release it!. The butterfly is flying free! Like a small fairy. Now she is happy. Remember! All creatures belong to this earth. Their freedom must be respected. What if you can't catch a butterfly! Hey! That's absolutely fine, Ri said. The act of chasing a butterfly itself is a game and helps us develop our concentration and determination, hahaha (chuckled Ri) It is also not a good idea to catch butterflies too often. The sight of all the butterflies in the garden is simply beautiful if you sit in a garden with your friend. To gain a deeper understanding on butterflies, you can also read books about them.
author: Rituraj Mishra
illustrator: Selina Masego Morulane; Lavanya  Naidu; Mahbubur  Rahman; Nguyễn  Minh Hải; Nikita Modi; Raju Babu Shakya; San srei nou ch nou ch; Sorit Gupto; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Save the life of plants
text: There was a small house with a beautiful garden in the backyard. The garden had trees and colourful flowers. Beautiful butterflies flew in that garden. Butterflies and sparrows hung around the mango and pomegranate trees. In that house lived two brother, Chandan and his younger brother Nandan. Everyday, Chandan looked after the garden. He watered the plants and cleaned the garden. Chandan used to wake up early in the morning to pluck flowers from his garden and distributed it to his neighbours. The neighbours appreciated his gesture and bless him. Chandan used to ask his younger brother to take care of the garden along with him but he never listened. One morning, Chandan saw his younger in the garden and thought that he was plucking the plants. He got furious. Chandan yelled at this little brother, "What are you doing, Nandan?". Nandan got scared and replied, "brother, these plants are infested. I told father and he asked me to spray pesticide on them." This shocked Chandan and he replied, "Bravo brother! You have saved the life of these plants. These plants will shower their blessings on you!"
author: Payal Dhiman

title: Horse of the almighty
text: Hasan was enjoying his evening tea time. His five years old daughter, Fariha was playing with her friends in the courtyard. Next to his chair, there was a small table that had a lantern on it. Near the table, there were some books in English, Hindi, and Urdu. In the dimness of the lantern's light, one could see insects flying around. The was a grasshopper that kept flying towards and from the lantern. Fariha was busy playing with her friends when her father said, "Fariha, come here!". Fariha quickly responded, "Coming". S he bid her friends goodbye before going inside the house. Unlike her friends, s he always obeyed her elders. Sometimes, her family teased her, "Fariha is mature like a grandmother". Fariha took her book and started studying. One of the images in her book caught her attention and she started looking at it intently. Just then a grasshopper flew and landed on her book. Mesmerized by the insect, she asked her father, "Father, which is this insect?", to which her father replied, "Oh this! I will tell you a story about this insect." But Fariha pestered her father, "Father, please tell me which is this insect?", to which Hasan replied, "Grasshopper". Hasan senses that Fariha wasn't amused by the insect's name. Hasan said, "It's called Grasshopper in English." Fariha looked at her father and then innocently turned her gaze towards the grasshopper. Hasan laid his hand on her head and said, "Do you know that your grandfather used to call it 'Horse of the almighty'." Fariha looked at her dad in surprise and then looked at the grasshopper. She said, " 'Horse of the almighty'! But father, is almighty smaller than us that he can ride a horse as tiny as the grasshopper? " This innocent question made Hasan smile.
author: Payal Dhiman

title: Sir Ganesh Dutt Singh
text: I saw a big building with the name "Sir Ganesh Dutt Singh girls hostel". We both went inside the building. I was curious to know about the name " Sir Ganesh Dutt Singh ", so I asked my sister about it. She replied, " Sir Ganesh Dutt Singh was an Indian lawyer, educationist, administrator, and the founder of modern Bihar. He was born in Nalanda district on the 13th January, 1868. " She went on to tell Tinnu, "He was born the day of "Ganesh Chathurti", so his mother, Kamla Devi, and his father, Degnarayan Singh, named him after Lord Ganesh. Ganesh Dutt was fond of playing and wrestling. He got married at the age of 15 to Rukmani Devi. Being an illiterate made Ganesh Dutt a laughing stock in his in-laws family so to gain education, he moved to Patna." She also told Tinnu, "In Patna, Ganesh Dutt graduated in law. He went on to earn a doctorate from Patna university. He served as a lawyer in the high courts of Calcutta and Patna. In 1923 to 1937, he held was active in politics and became a minister. He was the first person from Bihar to serve as a minister for the longest time. He was famous for donating 3/4th of his income. " Tinnu asked her sister, "Why do people call him "Sir" instead of "Shri"?" Tinnu's sister replied, "That's a really good question! Sir Ganesh Dutt Singh was instrumental in bringing modern changes to the society. Because of his contribution to the society, the British government bestowed the title of "Sir". Sir Ganesh Dutt Singh founded the " Sir Ganesh Dutt Patliputra High School ". He donated money and books to education institutes. He died on the 23rd of September, 1934, he died
author: Payal Dhiman

title: Kali's gift
text: He loves to help others. One day, his friend Prem didn't bring his lunch to school. During the lunch break, others didn't bother about Prem not eating. But Kali shared his food with Prem. The teacher was moved when he saw Kali's help. So, he presented Kali with a gift.

illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Dr. Sushma  Singh; Marleen  Visser

title: Crow's picnic
text: Once upon a time, the old Mr. Crow led a meeting with other animals from the jungle. All animals came to meeting including, Bagula mama, Bulbul aunty, Koyal didi, Billi mausi, Tota Ram, Rani chinti, tiny rat, Myna, Sparrow and others. Mr. Crow suggested, "Let's celebrate the new year with a picnic." Everybody agreed to this idea but Billi mausi didn't say a word. Tota ram teased Billi mausi and said, "Why are you so quiet?". Billi mausi said, "I'm wondering who will bring stuff for the picnic." Everybody went silent. Breaking the silence, Rani chinti said, "We will bring things for the picnic." And everybody said in agreement, "Yes, we all will collect and bring things". Koyal didi said, "Let's also discuss what all food should be there". Tiny rat said, "How about we serve doughnuts and rice pudding?". Rani chinti, quickly said, "I'll take the responsibility to get sugar." Bagula mama said, "I'll get rice and wheat flour." "Okay, I'll bring the firewood", Tota ram started repeating. Bulbul didi asked everyone, "How will we get milk?". Everyone looked at Billi mausi. Billi mausi said, "Had someone else taken the responsibility to bring milk, it would have been easier. Anyhow, I'll try to bring it." Monkey mama went to get utensils. In sometime everyone brought things for picnic and started cooking. After watching the food cook, Mr. Crow started cawing. The smell of the food started spreading in the jungle. Crow's cawing and the smell of the food woke up the wolf who was sleeping in his cave. He ran outside his cave and came to the picnic. Everybody panicked after seeing him and fled the scene. The wolf sat down and ate all the food from the picnic. Poor Crow's tiny mistake ruined picnic for eveyone.
author: Payal Dhiman

title: Ant celebrates Chhath puja
text: One upon a time, there were two friends, Mr. Ant and Mr. Pigeon. One day they thought of going out to the river for a walk. When they reached near the river, Mr. Ant asked, "Friend pigeon! Why do people take dips in the river Ganga?" Pigeon: "Don't you know? People are celebrating Chhath puja. People worship the Sun during this festival." Ant: "Oh listen! Why are these women singing songs?" Pigeon: "It's a chhath song, I also know one of these songs.. The banana that grows from the butter...... " Ant: "Loved the song! But how do you know it?" Pigeon: "Some years back I lived in a house, where the family celebrated Chhath every year and sang this song. They kicked me out of the house." Ant: "But why?" Pigeon: "Last year, during chhath, I ate one of their bananas." Ant: So what? Pigeon: During chhath, no one can eat fruits before offering water to the Sun so they kicked me out. Ant: I also want to celebrate this festival and sing the song. Pigeon: No! You'll drown in the river if you got in for the dip. Ant: So what should I do? Pigeon: Okay, let me get a leaf and a drop of Ganga water for you. Then, you can sit on the leaf and I'll pour water on you. I'll also get some fruits that we can offer the Sun. This is how Ant celebrated Chhath first time. She also sang the Chhath song. Kelva je farela ghaud se, aaho par suga merdey. Marbo re sugwa dhanush se, Suga gire murjhaye. Amrood je farela se, Oh par suga merdey. Marbo re sugwa dhanush se, Suga gire murjhaye. Nariyal je farela ghaod se, mm.
author: Payal Dhiman

title: Handmade toys
text: There was a funfair in the city. Ramu and Pinky asked their mother to go to the fair so she brought them to the fair. The fair had all sorts of rides, colorful toys, household items, and other items. After riding, Ramu and Pinky went around looking at the shops. Ramu was eyeing the toys displayed in those shops. While walking, they stopped at a shop. The shop had colorful toys in the shape of birds, turtle, and elephant made from Bamboo. Their mother also looked at a kitchen utensil made from bamboo. Ramu told his mother, "Ma, please buy me a toy." Mother replied, "You already have enough toys, I need this to use in the kitchen." Ramu said, "You already have this utensil!" Mother said, "They all are old. Your granny made them with her hands. In the villages, people still use bamboo to create household items." Ramu asked, "What's bamboo?" Mother said, "Bamboo is grown in farms. It's also made from dried stems, wire, or dried leaves of dates." Pinky asked, "Mother, how do they make colourful things from it?" Mother said, "Let's sit first and then I'll tell you", to which Ramu chucklingly said "Buy me a toy first!" Mother said, "Ok fine!" Mother bought toys to the kids liking and they all sat down in a place. Then, she started saying, "First these dried stems are dyed in different colours. Then, they are given different shapes and designs. These things are not just beautiful but also useful in the daily household work, such as soup, carpet etc." Pinky said, "When I go granny's place in the village, I'll definitely learn how to make toys with it." Mother said, "Ok, definitely learn. We should go home now. It's getting late." Pinky and Ramu along with their mother went home.
author: Payal Dhiman

title: The Swallow and the Crow
text: One day, a young swallow landed on a branch next to a wise old crow. The swallow looked down his beak at the crow and said, " I don't think much of your stiff feathers. You should take more Pride in your appearance." The old crow was very angry and was about to fly away when the swallow continued," Look at me with my soft, downy feathers. They are what a well- dressed bird needs." " Those feathers of yours might be all right in the spring and summer." the crow replied. " But in the winter you have to fly away to warmer countries. In the winter the trees are covered in ripe berries. I can stay here and enjoy then as I have my stiff black feathers to keep me warm and dry." The swallow was dumb founded. The crow held out his wings" What use are your fancy feathers then swallow?" he asked before turning and flying away. The moral of the story is- Fine feathered friends are not worth much.
author: Aaraadhanaa Iyer

title: The Haircut
text: My sister Meena and I are best friends. We love doing everything together! Sometimes, Mom takes us to get haircuts. Meena likes her hair long, so she doesn’t get much cut. On the other hand, I like my hair short. That’s how I always get it done! Meena and I get really bored one afternoon. “I don’t really feel like drawing today,” Meena says. Suddenly, I get an idea. “Meena!” I say excitedly. “Let’s play hair salon!” “Oh, are you sure Dhani? I don’t want to get in trouble with Mom.,” “We’ll be fine! Wait here.” I grab a pair of scissors from the kitchen and chop Meena’s hair off snip after snip. I sure do know how to cut hair! Oh no! I forgot that Meena likes her hair long. I hear footsteps coming towards the kitchen. Mom must be home! Mom walks in and sees Meena screaming at all the hair on the floor. “What’s all the fuss about?” she says. “Dhani cut my hair and now it’s too short!” Meena cries. ﻿﻿I then realize that this was all my idea in the first place. I was selfish, and didn’t listen to what my sister wanted to do instead. “Meena, I’m sorry. I only thought about what I wanted to do, and didn’t think about you,” I say. “It’s okay, Dhani. My hair will grow back soon.” Meena replies. “But now, YOU have to grow YOUR hair long!”
author: Tara Shivakumar

title: Suresh , and WATER
text: Suresh was a very good boy. He loved his mother and also lived with his grandfather. But he had a bad habit,he always wasted water. He would just see the water dripping. Instead of closing the tap, he sat and watched it. He did not close tap,shower etc.His mother was not happy with this. His mother and grandfather decided to teach him a lesson.they stopped all the water. Next morning,Suresh was not able to bath because of no water. He said this to his mom. His mom and grandfather told him about what he had done. Suresh said ‘I am very sorry,I will not do it again’. His mother hugged him and he went to play outside. Now whenever Suresh sees water dripping,he closes the tap or collects the Water.He is a good boy now,has his family is proud of him. THE END.

title: I believe I can fly!
text: Little Mandy sat with a frown. Another long day, a day of no fun! It was the Coffee season in Coorg. The coffee blossoms had become coffee berries. Mandy watched her father, Belli, dry the coffee berries in the yard. Little Mandy wandered around the rice storehouse. She caught something glimmering, as she browsed like a mouse. She dug the rice grains with her tiny little hands. “Papa, papa”, she screamed, “Look what I found?” “Well, it’s my old roller skates, " said Aiyappa, the house owner. He had two little sons called Kariappa and Kalappa. Mandy and Aiyappa’s sons looked puzzled, asking “Roll-what?” Aiyappa showed a video of skaters with roller blades and skateboards. “Roller-blading is a sport you practice with roller skates! Skateboarding is a sport you practice with skateboards!" "We loved our skates and boards when we were little kids,” Aiyappa said. Little Mandy hugged the skates tight. She could not sleep that night! She thought, “How I wish I get a skateboard and I am sure I’ll never be bored!” Her understanding father, Bellie got some wood and carved it to make a skateboard that looked good. He removed the wheels from the roller skates and attached them to the board. Giving the skateboard to Mandy, he said, “Here you go! Go roll with the wheels to your dreams!” Little Mandy wasted no time to practice. Her mind was full of tactics. She held the branch of a mighty tree and hopped onto the board slowly letting her hands go free. The other kids were playing the ‘pull-cart” game on a dried coconut leaf. Suddenly, they heard, “Thud!” Mandy had fallen down and the other kids were all laughing,“Mandy broke her crown!” Mandy’s skin shredded like falling paper pieces. So many wounds, so many bruises! But little Mandy was determined. She was not frightened. The skateboard was her dear friend and skateboarding kept her entertained. She muttered to herself, “I believe I can!” She was soon going to be a strong girl! Off she rolled down the street, she fell, she got up and was quick to be on her feet! Days passed by and one day, the sun was setting. The vast orange hue above was like a painting on canvas. Little Mandy was sweating, her face, a bright red hue after all the skateboarding practice. Meanwhile, Aiyappa’s sons were busy, busy playing video games! “Wheeee!” A thrilling voice caught their attention. It was Mandy who let out a shrill, “I believe I can fly!” Then it happened. A wheel flew to the right! A wheel flew to the left! And in two pieces, “Snap!” the skateboard broke! Mandy started crying, looking like she had sunstroke!" Aiyappa heard the wailing and came running. He tried consoling Mandy, “Don’t worry now! I will buy you a new skateboard. It will be better; it will be big and you will never be bored.” There it was! As the sun was sinking, Little Mandy, Kariappa, and Kalappa were skateboarding. And whoa! It was not just them. They were followed by a beeline of children. The children were learning how to skateboard. An ecstatic Mandy chirped, “I believe I can… and others chorused, “We believe we can… fly to reach the sky!” It was a sight to behold. No child was cooped up inside their homes. The children were not hooked on their phones or playing any videogames! They were all rolling on their skateboards!
author: Shrividya Somanna

title: The Hat Seller
text: One day a hat seller came to a village to peddle his wares One day a hat seller came to a village to peddle his wares One day a hat seller came to a village to peddle his wares After a long walk, he felt tired. So he sat under a tree to rest. He was so tired that he fell asleep quickly. While he was asleep, a group of monkeys watched him from the top of the tree. Then they came down so they could take a close look. The monkeys opened the hat seller's sack and checked its contents. They were very happy when they found hats that were very many and various colors, according to the size of their heads. Soon, every monkey was wearing those hats! They danced happily while wearing hats of various colors: red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple and red. Suddenly, the Hat Seller woke up from sleep, and the monkeys immediately ran back up the tree. When a moment later the Hat Seller got up, the monkeys stared at him and waited to see what he would do. The Hat Seller checked his bag. He felt very sad when he saw it was empty. Not a single hat left. Then the Hat Seller looked up and found the monkeys already wearing his hats! For a moment he thought about how to get his trading hat back. He took off the hat on his own head and threw it at the monkeys. The monkeys thought that the Hat Seller intended to hurt them, so they were furious. Then, the monkeys took off the hats they were wearing and took turns throwing them at the hat seller. Immediately the hat seller picked up all the hats and put them back in the sack. The monkeys looked on in amazement, and laughingly the hat seller walked away to peddle his hats.
author: Ratu Ayu

title: How the APPLES became RED?
text: 'An apple a day keeps the doctors away! said Rena munching a yellow apple. Shocked right? hearing 'a yellow apple' Ok ok don't worry, I'll share with you all the story of RED APPLES. "A long long time ago,when in the Earth no humans and creatures lived, there lived Tiny Tots means fruits and vegetables. They often had quarrels for either falling from trees or getting hit by something. The most happy fruits were the APPLES. They happily did their works and never quarreled with each others. Other fruits took this great opportunity to disturb and trouble the apples. They used to say 'Yellow! Yellow! Dirty fellow!' The apples would always ignore these words. But one day, in Piku apple's house there was no water and he was extremely thirsty. He thought 'Oh, Yes! King Mango stores so much of water in his barrel. I think if I asks him for a little water, he won't refuse me.' Then he went to the palace. Piku asked some guards and then reached where King Mango was sitting. He said 'Your Majesty, I'm Piku. Actually I'm here for a little water from your great barrel. Please can you give me some?' King Mango angrily replied 'How dare you to ask me for water? Don't you know I'm the king of this land. I don't share my precious water to anybody like the dirty yellow apple.' Piku went away saying nothing. From then on no apples came out from their houses. they were slowly becoming red with anger. After one month of the birth of humans, they were searching for food here and there. The fruits and vegetables were running like mad. But the apples remained the same. As they were controlling all their anger, they became red as well as juicy. On the other hand all the fruits and vegetables were trapped in the human's net and died. At last the apples were saved! That's why now we can enjoy eating red and juicy apples. Rena suddenly spoke up 'A red and juicy apple a day keeps the doctors away!'

title: Tit for Tat
text: Rupa were playing Ludo together. They were having fun and enjoying themselves. Suddenly, a mouse ran into the room followed by a cat. The cat was trying to catch the mouse but crashed into the game board. The game board and the game pieces flew into the air and fell all over the room. "Oh no!" said Raju. "What should we do now?" "I remember where the pieces were," said Rupa. "My piece was here and your piece was there, and..." "No!", said Raju, before Rupa could finish what she was saying, "My piece was here. Don't lie!" "Really?" Rupa shouted loudly. "I'm leaving. I will tell everyone that you are a cheater." "If you do that, I will slap you", Raju shouted back. "I will ask Ammi to beat you with the rolling pin", said Rupa. "I'll call the police. They'll lock you up in jail", said Raju. "I will call a gunman to shoot you with a gun." Rupa wanted to win the war of words. "I will plant a bomb in your house." Raju also did not want to lose the war of words. "I will...". Just then, another cat ran into the room. This time, a dog followed the cat. The dog fell on the game board and the pieces flew into the air again. Raju and Rupa looked at each other and laughed. "If I plant a bomb in Rupa's house, my house will also burn", thought Raju. "If Raju goes to jail, who will play Ludo with me?", thought Rupa. "If we keep fighting over a game of Ludo, we will soon start World War 3", Raju smiled. "Let' start the game again", said Rupa. "My piece was here..."

title: The Storm
text: Once upon a time, far far away there was a little village called Limya. The people of Limya were always very happy. They had food, shelter, and they lived in comfort. One day while everyone was working a low rumbling sound came. It was the sky. It suddenly began thundering and raining heavily. Everbody rushed to their houses. The storm continued for many days. People were trapped in their own houses! Thankfully there was enough of food and water so they were able to survive. Finally one day the storm came to an end. People came out of their houses to discover that animals were everywhere! The animals explained that they weren't going to trouble anyone and they promised if the humans gave them food they would live as friends, not foes. The humans thought that was sensible. So after that Limya was the place that animals and humans lived together as one.

title: The Night Dwellers
text: Oakley was tired after the night’s hunt. She perched upon a tree branch with her parents. Oakley gazed at the night sky as she loved the stars and the moon. They had just finished their night hunt and had decided to stop not too far away from home, so they could eat. “Mummy, are we the only things on this planet that can fly?” asked Oakley. “No, my darling. There are many other flying things and they are called birds,” replied Mummy owl. “So I’m a…bird?” “Yes Oakley. We are birds; birds of prey to be more specific, which means we kill other animals to survive,” said Mummy owl. “Now now, everyone, let’s stop talking and eat!” said Daddy owl, frustrated but calm. “Your father’s right, baby. Let’s eat and then learn something new,” said Mummy owl, nodding her head in agreement. “I am hungry too,” Oakley said. They had a delicious meal. Daddy owl had caught a mouse, while Mummy owl had brought some spiders and Oakley had seized some snails between her talons. After their meal, they decided to rest a little before flying back to their tree holes, for the break of dawn was far. As Oakley cuddled close to her mother, she noticed something hanging upside down from a tree branch at a distance. “What is that odd creature hanging upside down? I’ve never seen such a thing!” Oakley said, surprised. “What are you talking about darling?” asked a confused Mummy owl. Mummy owl carefully looked into the distance, hooted and replied, “That’s a bat my darling.” Oakley’s eyes opened as wide as saucers in astonishment. She was dumbfounded! Mummy and Daddy owl began explaining bats to Oakley. “Oakley, the thing hanging from the branch you saw was a bat. It is just like us owls, but different too. Now, Daddy will tell you how they are different from us and I’ll tell you in what ways they are like us,” said Mummy owl. “Alright. Daddy, can you please start?” asked Oakley impatiently. She was very excited. Oakley loved learning new things. “Alright, alright. Oakley, as your mother told you, we owls are birds of prey. But bats, you see, are mammals.” “But Daddy!” said Oakley interrupting her father. “What is a mammal?” “A mammal is an animal that gives birth to their young ones and nourishes them with their milk. But birds like us lay eggs, whereas the young ones of bats are called pups,” explained Daddy owl. “Oh! I didn’t know that there were flying creatures that give birth,” said Oakley happily. “Well, let me continue. Darling, as you noticed, bats sleep upside down but we sleep upright. Now Oakley, look at your talons,” said Daddy owl. “Yeah. What about them?” replied Oakley. “Well, bats don’t have those. Furthermore, bats have fur, while we have feathers and they have teeth unlike us, and feed on nectar, pollen, fruits, insects and fish. We have beaks,” explained Daddy owl. “Now tell her where bats live. She’ll definitely want to know that,” said Mummy owl. “Ah, yes! How could I forget? Oakley, bats live in caves or hang upside down from trees in colonies whereas owls live in tree holes. But a few other birds live in nests up in trees,” said Daddy owl. “Wait…I thought every bird lived in a tree hole!” said Oakley quite surprised with this new information. “Now, it’s my turn to tell you how bats resemble us. The most important similarity is that they too are night dwellers like us. We are nocturnals. All of us have wings to fly and have good night vision unlike other flying creatures and have pointy ears with a good sense of hearing that help us to be active at night,” explained Mummy owl. “Oh! Now I’ve learned all about the two rulers that reign the night!” said Oakley. She lifted her body, stood on her talons and held her head up in pride and declared, “Bravo to the nocturnals! We do not fear the night!”
author: Anushka  Nair

title: The tiger's hunger

title: Vegetable soup for mom
text: This is Somu's house. Somu is lazy in eating. If he got vegetables in his meal, he would get angry. Somu did not believe that eating vegetables would give you strength and improve your health. Somu tried hard to convince Amma not to use vegetables in his favorite cooking. But mom, mom herself? He knew what was best for his children. Just seeing vegetables is enough, Somu used to tie knots. Bell peppers, broccoli, carrots, peas and radishes are what Somu didn't like! One day, Somu got a surprise when he came home after school. The kitchen was empty - empty! His stomach started rumbling. He was hungry. So does his sister Soni. Amma was sleeping in the room; He was shivering in the cold! Soni started getting worried. Somu immediately thought and called his grandmother on the phone. Grandma said it would be good if you make hot vegetable soup for mom. Soni wrote down on paper the way Grandma had told her. He said "thank you" to his grandmother and started working. Somu opened the fridge and stood looking at all the vegetables inside. Later, Somu and Soni made a list of what they needed to make the vegetable soup. Remove all the required vegetables and wash them well. Carefully cut them off slowly. When Soni lamented that Amma was not feeling well, Somub got angry because she was "feeding vegetables". When grandma told her to make soup, these children who thought it was very simple, now they know that cooking is not easy! Somu now realizes that every day, Amma, who used to cook for everyone and take good care of everyone, was having such a hard time! Somu and Soni waited patiently for the vegetables to cook. When the soup was finally ready, he put it in a bowl and gave it to Amma. Both Somu and Soni prepare the soup without the help of the elders of the house! Their happiness knew no bounds. Now mom can drink soup and get well soon... Mom sobered up after drinking the soup! He appreciated the hard work of the children and hugged them. Neighbors were also surprised! Now Somu doesn't get upset when he sees vegetables. Instead he eats happily. Somu now believes that eating vegetables will give you strength and improve your health! Amma, Somu and Soni ate vegetables. have you eaten

title: Silence
text: Sita was a bubbly little girl, who was the apple of her parent's eye. She lived in the vibrant city of Chennai, and found love in travelling with her parents. Be it train journeys, or the bus rides between her favourite places. She loved to spread happiness wherever she went, and most importantly pick up a conversation. She loved talking to people. And when it came to talking to people during journeys, she wouldn't miss it for the world! Sita was also a good student at school, who was always given good remarks by her teachers. Her parents often encouraged her to explore and meet new people. But since she loved talking to people, she would often end up talking a lot. Her father would often say "Kanna, learn to talk when you should talk, and not when it is not needed" and this was one rule that Sita always broke. He reminded her of the same rule on their journey one fine day. She couldn't give up her love for conversations for the world, how could she? So she began talking to every single person on the train. Albeit her kind heart and bubbly self, Sita was regarded as talkative by many a person, which made Sita so self aware about herself, that she began to read books in her own company, in the fear of being called talkative. Sometimes she was so worried about being all alone, that she wanted to fit into the crowd. She would try to be her own best cheery self, and go all about doing the same thing again, and again, talking to people, until it was too much for them to handle. This made her sad. A crestfallen Sita ran to her mother for consolation. Sita loved her parents. Her mother would always give her a hug anytime she was in need of one, and remind her of her beautiful self. She would always do anything to ensure her daughter was happy, no matter what. Seeing his daughter, Sita's dad decided to entertain his daughter with a small activity. He asked Sita to sit down by his side, and look around her. The trees, mountains and the beautiful scenery that was in front of her eyes. Sita was absolutely thrilled! Her eyes went wide in wonder! "What makes a forest so beautiful?" her father asked. To which she immediately replied, "The trees, animals, flowers, insects, birds!" Seeing the excitement in her answer, her father smiled at Sita and told her "It is not just trees, animals, birds, insects, but also notice how silent the forest is, even with everything" Sita could not understand. Her father continued "You are like the forest, Sita. So full of life. You know so many things, that others do not need to know. What you know, should be with you. When people want to know, they will know" A confused Sita asked "How do I know if people want to know?" To which her father replied, smiling at his daughter "When people want to know something from you, they will ask you. And what do you do until then?" Sita couldn't answer. Her father told her "Be silent, kanna. Because when you are silent, like the forest, people see you. They will talk to you. If they want to, they will like to talk to you more." Hearing what her father said, Sita was silent. She continued to read her book, thinking about her father's words, when she saw an old lady ask "What book are you reading?" To which Sita replied "Tinkle, paatti" and smiled at her. The old lady smiled back and started talking to her. Sita talked to her, keeping her father's advice in mind. The old lady was happy talking to Sita and gave her some apples as her gift. Sita was very happy. A happy Sita went back to her parents, not worried about being called a chatterbox, because she now knew how to talk to people, and most importantly, how to be silent. Seeing their daughter's happy face, her parents were also happy. They hugged their daughter and patted her head. They were so proud of Sita.
author: Lakshmi Supriya

title: Good Touch - Bad Touch
text: "I like it when you hug and kiss me Ma, I feel very nice and happy", said Esha. "I like it too, Eshu" replied Ma. "I also like it when Papa and aaji aajoba hug me. I feel so warm and safe." said Esha. "I am sure they feel the same Eshu" said Ma. "I don't like it when the watchman touches me when I am playing. He looks at me in a mean way. I feel scared and sad." "Oh! Is it? He must be doing it when we are not around you. Let me see how I can help you." said Ma. "Let me ask you a question. Have you seen our dog Moti? What does he do when you pull his tail?." asked Ma. "He starts barking loudly and runs as fast as he can", said Esha. "Absolutely right. He does that because he does not like you pulling his tail. If you don't like the watchman touching you, you should scream out loudly for help. Its a bad touch." said Ma. "But then I don't like it when Doctor uncle holds my hand and gives me an injection. i scream out then." Esha said. Ma laughed out loudly and said, "You do feel better after taking that injection, don't you? And we are also there around you then. It's a good touch Eshu." "OK Ma. The next time I don't like anyone touching me when you are not around, I shall scream "NO" and run away as fast as possible." Esha said hugging her doll tightly. Ma said with a laugh, "I am sure right now your doll is not liking your tight hug." Esha and Ma laugh together and give each other a tight hug.

title: Rubik's Cube - A Puzzle Game
text: The Rubik’s Cube was invented in 1974 by Erno Rubik. Erno Rubik was a Hungarian architecture professor. He got the idea to develop the Rubik’s Cube when he taught three-dimensional images in his class on descriptive geometry. Rubik created a 3x3 Rubik’s Cube. In the three-dimensional Rubik’s Cube, the colours on the six faces are orange, green, white, red, yellow, and blue. In the latest models, blue is opposite green, white is opposite yellow, and orange is opposite red. A standard Rubik’s Cube is 5.6 centimeters in length on each side. The Rubik puzzle has 26 mini unique cubes known as cubies or cubelets. The colours are jumbled up when the game starts. Each column in a face can turn independently due to an internal pivot mechanism. You win the game when each face has only one colour. In the beginning, the Rubik’s cube was sold as ‘Magic Cube’. More than 350 million original cubes have been sold worldwide as of now. In 1980, the Rubik’s Cube won the German Game of the Year special award. Nowadays, 4x4 and 2x2 Rubik’s Cubes are also available. A speed-cubing championship was organized by the Guinness Book of World Records in 1981. In 2018, Yusheng Du of China solved the Rubik puzzle in 3.47 seconds and set a world record. Now, people try to solve Rubik’s Cube while skydiving, underwater, blindfolded, or juggling. Solving a Rubik’s Cube puzzle game helps to produce dopamine or happiness chemicals in the brain. Solving any puzzle reduces stress and gives us a sense of satisfaction. Erno Rubik wrote a book named ‘Cubed’ in 2020. Now get ready to twist and turn the Rubik’s Cube, a three-dimensional logical toy. Activity 1: Which colour is there on a Rubik Cube? 1. Violet 2. Black 3. Green 4. Pink Activity 2: Which colour is not there on a Rubik Cube? 1. Yellow 2. Brown 3. Blue 4. Red Activity 3: Who is the inventor of the Rubik's Cube? 1. Enro Rubik 2. Erno Rubik 3. Eron Rubik 4. Eorn Rubik Answers: Activity 1: Green Activity 2: Brown Activity 3: Erno Rubik
