author: Karina B

title: Aarti has a great day
text: Its morning! Aarti says to herself, She thinks of the party she is having today. She then dressed up and wore her glasses. By the time she was ready grandpa had already ordered almond milk and Aarti was so delighted to see her almond milk. They went into the kitchen to make tea and soup for the guests. she said, grandpa this soup needs more salt. Grandpa thinks for a moment and says, You are right about that he exclaimed, I'll add more of that and more sugar in the tea. Some people watched them preparing the food and decided to see what was going on. Aarti then had written something on the fridge board and grandpa wondered, Hmm what could she be writing? She gave a hint, Its a pictograph she whispered. When they left grandpa was already pouring tea in the cups and Aarti said, Oh grandpa! I think that this tea will be perfect for the guests! she exclaimed while jumping in joy after tasting some of the tea. When the guests arrived she then tried to count all the guests in the party to finish the pictograph before they leave. Then the guests ate lunch after Aarti counted all of them to make her pictograph finished. Grandpa later exclaimed, Oh you had written how many people like different beverages! Later after lunch the guests needed to go home from the party so she said goodbye to them while they drove away from their house. Then outside she made a camp along with her brother John. She kept aside her glasses and she and he played in the camp till it was night time. Once she was in bed she removed her glasses once more and she thinks of all the amazing moments she had in the morning, afternoon and of course evening and soon fell asleep. Good Night.
author: Aashi Jain
illustrator: Alicia  van Zyl; Ayesha Punjabi; Cynthia Galvan; Mieke van der  Merwe; Omkar Mahashabde; Wiehan de Jager

title: My Changing Weather
text: The weather outside keep changing always. In the morning, when I woke up, it was cloudy. By the time I reached school, it was sunny. During our lunch break, the weather outside became windy. When it was time to return home from school, it became rainy. My feelings inside me also keep changing like the weather outside. I am happy when my teacher gives me a star in my school work. I feel sad when my brother gets hurt while playing. I get scared when I see a cockroach running around in my house. My parents returning early from office surprise me. However, my brother and myself are the happiest when our parents read stories to us before going to bed. Do your feelings inside also change like the changing weather?
author: Ira Periyavallur (aka Indira VMD)
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Advay Bhatia; Josephine  Versfeld; Lara Berge; Mamun Hossain; Poornima  Chander; Sahitya Rani; Sunaina  Coelho; VERUSHKA DHOUNDIYAL; Vusi  Malindi

title: Every night 2
text: CHAPTER TWO Mistry case The next day: it was really sleepy as well as excitement, for everyone but still nobody falls in sleep. with full of excitement and joyness no one can wait for bus. soon the college bus arrived and everyone have their seat. few hours later- the bus in half the way to miami collage, professor alya stood up and announced " here the shop to buy things, for your needs. soon getting this information every girls rushd to that shop except janfy and shara. professor alya questioned janfy and shara, "why u two were so silent? and why u both staying here?" shara said " I'm just moving now " janfy didn't even reply and sat in her own place. seeing this even boys came down. 2 hour later everybody came back. as soon they came the bus started at 7 pm they reached the Miami college. to be continued
author: Lithisha C

title: IMPORTANCE OF FAMILY
text: Priya is a nice and helpful girl. She studies in a very godd school. She has a friend named adam. She is happy in life. But one day her mother had a heart attack she was reached to the hospital immediatly but the doctors could not save her. She is no more nurse report it to her family. Ok sir. Priya is very sad. She cries a lot, she remembers all the happy moments she had shared with her. Her father comforts her. Its all okay my dear daughter. There lots of hard things in life you have to face. Her father loved her so much and seeing her unhappy he weds back and brings her a new mother. Her father now has an important buisness tour and he has to leave. Bye my sweet daughter. Be with your mom for some months when i will come back i will bring lots of gifts for you. She went to the farm with her new mom where she begans to weep. Her step mother comforts her and they do their work hapilly. Dont cry. Accept me as your mom i will always love you. She even took priya to school. Days turn into weeks. Weeks turn into months. Months tur into years but there is no sign of her father. One day as priya and adam were playing. Her mother calls out they ran to the door and sees priyas father. Father you are back. I missed you a lot. Yes yes i am back and with lots of gift for you too.
author: ANINDITA MAHANTI
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Google India; Kashvi  Choudhary; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Priyankar Gupta; Rijuta Ghate; Rohit Kelkar; Sahitya Rani; Yashika Lakshmi Venkatesh; Zainab Tambawalla

title: The Buffalo's Patience
text: I am thankful to the monkey for teaching me to be patient." The monkey sitting on a tree's branch heard this and felt ashamed. The monkey then immediately went to the buffalo and said, "I am sorry for the troubles caused to you because of my friend." The buffalo looked at the monkey and smiled and they became good friends. Moral: We should be patient.
author: Karina B

title: Sonu's Anklets
text: She liked wearing anklets which made sounds when she walked. And that wasn't surprising because all the girls did such stuff. But, a wish of hers could not get fulfilled. Her father used to get her hair cut and made her wear clothes that boys wore. Sometimes she used to get her wish of long hair fulfilled by making a braid with her mother's scarf. She did not have a brother and her father longed for a son and to fulfill this desire, he used to dress Sonu up like a boy. But Sonu, in her mind, wished for something else. Seeing beautiful frocks and colourful clips made her child mind fill with desires. Her grandfather used to feel sad upon reading her innocent mind, but he did not have a say in the matter. Once Sonu said to her grandfather, "Dadu, please buy me anklets, I will dance wearing them." For the sake of Sonu's happiness, her grandfather then took her to a goldsmith the very same day and bought beautiful anklets of her size for her. Sonu was very happy upon wearing the anklets and she wasn't even afraid of her father anymore. Seeing Sonu so happy, her grandfather's mind also filled with happiness because children's happiness was of the most importance to him. And that is why Sonu's grandfather earned wealth in the form of the love that he received.
author: Karina B

title: Chasing the Deer
text: One day, a leopard saw a magnificent deer grazing. The leopard was hungry and wanted to hunt the deer for its meal. "The deer looks delicious. I am capable of going to the deer very quietly and attacking it! Even the deer would not understand that it's going to get attacked." thought the leopard. The deer was busy chewing fresh green grass. "This grass is very lovely. I must come here everyday. The flowers are so beautifully scented, the grass is so delicate." - thought the deer. All of a sudden, in the open expanse of land, the deer saw the leopard slowly approaching. The deer immediately jumped and started running for its life. The leopard followed the deer. "I must run really fast!" said the deer. The deer put all its might into maintaining distance from the leopard. The leopard was not that fast and soon, it faded away from the sight of the deer. Moral: It is never a good idea to be overconfident about one's abilities.
author: Karina B

title: The Thief and the Dog of the House
text: One night, a thief got into a house. He had brought pieces of meat with him to fool the dogs of the house. The thief entered the house and saw a dog of the house. The thief then threw the meat pieces at the dog. To this, the dog said, "If you think you can fool me by throwing this piece of meat at me, then you are wrong." The thief then throws another piece of meat at the dog. The dog doesn't take the meat piece and answers by saying, "I am a loyal dog of the house. You cannot fool me and cannot hurt my master." As soon as the dog said this, it then immediately attacked the thief. The thief got scared and after some time, ran out of the window. Hearing the dog bark, the owner of the dogs of the house woke up. He came out of his room and sought information about the incident. He then praised his dog and gifted him two more pieces of meat to eat.
author: Karina B

title: It's Raksha-Bandhan!
text: I have many names. Papa calls me Poploo and Mumma calls me Momloo. Papa and Mumma are working from home these days. I am very happy because now I don't have to go to day care. I play with my little sister Gogloo all day. These days, Mumma is busy decorating colourful threads with sequins, starts and beads. She says that the festival of 'Raksha-Bandhan' is coming soon, and so she is making 'rakhis'. She tells me that she will put these 'rakhis' in an envelope, along with some red 'roli' powder and rice grains, and send them to Monu Mama. When I ask her why she will send 'rakhis' to Mama, she says, "Because I love my brother very much." I also love Gogloo very much. I will make one 'rakhi' for her. But Gogloo puts everything in her mouth. Maybe I should paste a candy on her 'rakhi', which she can then eat. Good idea! I will take Mumma's help to make a 'candy rakhi' for my little Gogloo. I also love Boozoo. He always comes running to me when he sees me. We play 'Throw and Catch' together with his favourite orange ball. I know! I will make a ball-shaped 'rakhi' for him. I love my teddy bear very much. He holds me right when it is time to sleep. A 'rakhi' that is soft and cuddly like him is what I will make for Teddy. Oh! I have a new friend who comes to meet me every morning. When I get up and go to the balcony, Kawkaw is waiting for me. While I drink my glass of milk, he munches of biscuits that I lay out for him. I want to make 'rakhis' for Mumma, Papa, Monu Mama, Shrini Mami, Dada, Dadi. I love them all very, very much. Now let me count how many 'rakhis' I have to make. I will make 'rakhi's for Gogloo, Boozoo, Teddy, Kawkaw, Mumma, Papa, Monu Mama, Shrini Mami, Dada and Dadi. That makes it 10 'rakhis'. Let me get started right away! Friends, how many 'rakhis' are you making for Raksha-Bandhan?
author: Mudita Agarwal

title: Bear's Journey
text: There once lived a bear named Kalu. Kalu was thinking whose photo it should take? A voice came from the moon, "Click my photo." So, then, off went the bear on its journey. It reached the moon and saw greenery over there. "Wow!! This seems like a second earth to me."
author: Karina B

title: Obstinate Neighbours
text: Obstinate Neighbors The night is thick and heavy with clouds when I paint the front of The House yellow. I paint quickly and quietly. I don’t want to wake my neighbor up. The brush goes shhh shhh! against the wall and even that is loud. My feet crunch on gravel as I finish up and slip into my home. My neighbor’s cursing wakes me up in the morning. I hear fuck! and shit! I split the blinds with two fingers. The sun shines very bright and I squint to see my other neighbors file outside. They see the yellow paint and shake their heads. One of them points at my home. I come away from the window. Knock knock. I do not answer. I make myself toast with a poached egg. I eat it plain. Butter has a strange, slimy texture and most jams are too sweet for my taste. They pound on the door. The doorknob rattles in its socket before I hear silence on my front porch again. My neighbors assume I painted The House. They are right, but it’s still insulting that they point to me first. Upon purchase, my new neighbor repainted The House beige before moving equally bland furniture (and herself) inside. I must fix it. She does not understand that each house claims life as we do. Their creaks are small sighs and groans, their breath the wind that flutters curtains when their mouths are unlocked. Each house is individual in personality. They have different mannerisms, likes and dislikes that can influence whoever its inhabitant might be at the time. Often, though, its influence is overruled by tenants that bustle about, creating their own noises that muffle their homes. I can hear them. I hear anger when doors slam shut, peace when furniture is aligned and floors are swept clean. Houses do not have control over their appearance, so I help them. I listen and give them a color true to their individuality. The House in question, which you could say is my current “client,” is bubbly, but prone to sickness and somewhat oblivious to the struggles of others. It loves its inhabitants—most of the time—and wishes to give them a cozy embrace. Most of all, The House is very particular about its appearance and becomes incensed when the smallest thing is not quite right. Right now, it is sulking. The little yellow I gave it placated it, but soon it will demand more. In the afternoon I hear the grrr grrr of trucks and metallic clanking and deep voices shouting. Big men in loose denim pants and ugly T-shirts paint The House back to beige. My neighbor comes onto her lawn to survey the men, pointing out the spots that need extra paint. The painters finish quickly, taking my neighbor’s cash and leaving extra paint cans and brushes and crinkled plastic tarps. The House strains against its new skin. It pummels its beige bonds with angry fists and wails It’s so ugly! The neighboring houses think it silly and childish, but they are too old to remember what it was like to be a child. I will The House to be patient. Its paint is still wet. The sun burns hot, then abruptly cools in the evening. Rain is predicted in the next few days, so the air hangs thick like soaked velvet. I shift from chair to chair, unable to settle. I need distraction, so a sandwich is readily made and quickly eaten. I flip through books before putting them down. I stack the books. I eat some mini-pretzels. I play a movie and turn the volume up loud. All is drowned out by The House’s pouts and whines. I doze fitfully and when I sleep, I dream of an infant pouring a dripping yellow sky onto little people that drown in thick sunflower puddles. The night I return to soothe The House, a small red eye blinks from the corner of its porch. A camera makes my job harder, but it is only one. My neighbor is either lazy, or thinks that its presence is enough to deter me. Either way, that is her mistake. I open my paint can and approach from an angle. I grab a handful of viscous yellow and smear it over the lens. The paint is cool and slippery, coating the lens completely while the excess puddles in the dirt below. After that, it is a simple matter to paint as much yellow as I can in the time that I have. I cannot fully free The House, but its grousing quiets and it settles more comfortably into its foundations. There is more cursing in the morning and more banging against my door. This time, my neighbor screams through the door. She says open up or I’ll break the fucking door down. My own home is a demure thing sheathed in light brown. A broken door will cause it tremendous pain and that will not do. My neighbor’s hair is unbrushed and sticks out like fur. She wears a big t-shirt and no shoes. I wish she was wearing shoes. I think feet are so foreign. I forget I have feet until I look down and wonder how something so strange could be attached to me. I know it’s you, she says. I’m quiet. I’ll hear what she has to say. My neighbor turns red. Say something, she says. You are the only person here who would paint my house yellow every fucking night. I moved here and I heard stories about you. You stare at all the houses and peek in the windows and you talk to yourself more than you talk to other people. My neighbor goes on and on. She is quite incensed. Spittle flies from her lips and she jerks her hands about to show just how angry she is. She says, You’re free to do what you want, but Jesus Christ, you have to know you look absolutely fucking crazy. The house was one thing, the camera is just ridiculous. I could put in a report for vandalism! I could call the police! What are you gonna do, deny it? You stupid bitch, I should report you right— I don’t deny it, I say. Her mouth gapes. In addition to a hot temper, she also has strange rules about what is right and what is wrong. The rules of her world apply to everyone. She straightens my trash bins on trash day to match her own. She quips often about the unique color of our shared fence, which is blue, though the blue is not on her side. I’m not bothered by it. My ambivalence (or apathy, in her mind) infuriates her. It’s amusing to see her realize that I won’t fight her, not in this way. She opens and closes her mouth and turns more red. Just stop painting my fucking house, she says. And then she hacks a glob of spit onto my porch and leaves. I see her painting over the yellow with rough strokes of beige paint. Her work is streaky and thick globs drip down the woodwork. It will harden and texture The House, which it will not like. More cameras go up too, one in the opposing corner of the front porch and and two more on the corner nearest to my home. At night, I cover my face and approach not from my home, but through the backyards of neighboring houses. I tell the houses hello and they breathe creaky whistles in return. Many of the houses in this neighborhood are like my own: plain, ordinary, normal. They do not require the same attention as The House. I use paint again to cover the cameras. My work is sloppier than previous nights and The House complains. I tell it that its tenant has made my work more difficult and this is the best that I can do. The House asks if it should do something to stop its tenant. I say no, that goes too far. I try to smooth out the streaky bits, apologize again, then come home. My hands shake as I wash out my paintbrush and dry my hands. I suppose I’m nervous about my neighbor’s threat. I don’t fear the police or the possibility of arrest, but rather I fear that if I am taken away, The House will not be cared for. Who else can do what I do? Without me, The House will push against its bland exterior and cry and cry. Its caterwauling would also bother the other houses on the street, kind as they are. At night I dream again of a yellow paint sky, but this time I am drowning and the viscous liquid is rising and I cannot see through the lemon film that covers my eyes. I am enveloped and smothered in an inward explosion of death. I wake early. I sip tea and let the hot mug burn my hands crimson while I peer through the window. I stand there for an hour, maybe longer, until my tea has gone cold and I find myself shifting from foot to foot. I still when the door of The House opens and my neighbor steps out onto the porch. She sees the damage to the cameras and the return of the yellow paint. She stands there for a moment, then turns back inside. I turn away from the window. She has seen what I’ve done, yes, but what is to come of it? I go through the motions of my morning, washing my face, changing into day clothes and making a bowl of cereal. My ears hear The House’s moans and its companions’ whispers of encouragement, but no sirens. Clouds veil the sun as it dips and a gentle rain coats my neighborhood. An earthy, slightly bitter scent emanates from the lawns and swathes of asphalt. Petrichor: a phenomenon both clean and dirty, clinging and cleansing. The houses love it. They inhale and exhale, inhale and exhale. The rain calms me. I see no flashes of blue and red or the slap of heavy tires on wet asphalt. I don’t know why my neighbor failed to follow through on her threat. Maybe she forgot. Maybe she wants to keep me in suspense and prolong my anxiety. Maybe, far-fetched as it is, she hopes to continue this little feud because she loves a good fight. This will turn into a game, a competition between the obstinate neighbors: one who refuses to admit fault, and one who will never stop.
author: Anushka Gupta

title: The Magical Umbrella
text: Once upon a time, a very small lizard came out of an egg. The lizard saw that there were lots and lots of trees all around and that there was mud everywhere. "Welcome to this jungle", when the lizard looked around she saw six other lizards. "Come dear, roam around a little here", the little lizard started running happily. At that very instant, she heard a weird scary sound. She got scared and ran and hid herself. She didn't know that she was hiding in a magical umbrella. The umbrella thought that the little lizard is scared. All of a sudden, the umbrella started flying. For a moment, the lizard thought that she would touch the skies but the very next moment, the umbrella landed on water. The lizard found itself swimming in a river sitting in the umbrella! The lizard was having a lot of fun. Then, droplets of cold river water sprinkled on the lizard and she started feeling cold and started to shiver and then she sneezed! When the lizard started getting wet, the umbrella provided her head with a roof! Oh brother! What magic! The umbrella-cum-boat got filled with water on going a little further. The lizard thought, "Now this river wants to accompany me in my boat." But the magical umbrella understood that there was a hole in it. So, then, the umbrella flies and goes straight to the shore!!! The lizard starts jumping with happiness. ﻿ ﻿Immediately after reaching the shore, the umbrella changes its form to become a stick and carries the little lizard and starts jumping and reaches a house. ﻿ ﻿The little lizard then jumps off the stick and enters the house and climbs on a wall of the house. Since then, lizards live on the walls of houses and are happy eating small insects, mosquitoes, flies, spiders, etc.
author: Karina B

title: The Great Trick
text: Kasha lived in the village with her parents. She also had a beloved bird. The bird was called Pinku. Pinku had a melodious voice. Pinku loved to play "Bhagam Bhag" in which Kasha had to catch Pinku. Since Pinku was a bird, he would fly high and Kasha would not be able to catch him. Today they played another game of Bhagam Bhag. Kasha started counting. "99...100! Today I will catch you Pinku" said Kasha. She came in the outside and asked her mom "Ma...Have you seen Pinku, Today I must catch him" "I think Pinku is up on one of the trees in the garden, why don't you go and check." her mom replied. Kasha ran to the garden and checked on every tree "Oh Pinku....I will catch you" she said. She found Pinku in the garden and chased him. But Pinku was too fast and Kasha couldn't catch up. She told the issue to her mom. Her mom thought for a while looking at Pinku sitting on the tree and said "follow me!". Kasha was confused but followed her mom. Her mom started to beat some rice while her father helped. Then her mom said to Kasha "Take this and bring it to Pinku". She threw the grains of rice in the air and Pinku was slowly and slowly lured towards the delicious rice. Just as Pinku was about to eat the rice Kasha started to chase Pinku. Pinku ran through the entire garden making Kasha follow him. Kasha couldn't catch up to Pinku and got tired. She had no another idea on how to catch Pinku. Her mom said "maybe you could trick Pinku". She said "I will not play anymore!". "Oh! The come inside to help me" her mom said. They both came inside. Kasha helped her mom to sew a dress while Pinku was hovering above their heads thinking the game is still on. As Kasha helped her mom to make dinner she did not pay attention to Pinku. The bird again hovered on their heads and thought Kasha must not want to play. He sat quietly on the tree. Then she looked through the window and said to her mom "Look! My plan worked, Pinku is quitly sitting thinking the game is over. Now I can go and catch him. Her mom smirked and said "That is very smart". She quietly went behind him and caught him. She started shouting with joy " I caught Pinku!". Her mom came outisde and saw how happy Kasha was. She said "Your plan has worked well". Pinku flew back to his nest giving a wink to Kasha. Kasha knew tomorrow will be another game of Bhagam Bhag.
author: Riddhima Banerjee

title: Bhavani and Badshah
text: This is Bhavani. Bhavani is young. This is Badshah. Badshah is older. Bhavani has two legs. Badshah has four legs and a tail too. Bhavani likes to play. Badshah likes to sleep. Bhavani wants to become friends with Badshah. Bhavani said, "We are going to Badshah's house." To this, his mother said, "Do not go there. Badshah might bite you." His father said, "Do not go there. Badshah might bark at you." His grandfather said, "Do not go there. Badshah is very naughty." Everyone fell asleep in the afternoon. Bhavani took out a biscuit very silently and entered Badshah's home. Badshah was sleeping under a table. Bhavani gave the biscuit to Badshah. Badshah wagged his tail. When everyone finally woke up, they saw Bhavani and Badshah playing together. Seeing them, Bhavani said, "Badshah is good." Now, Bhavani and Badshah have become good friends.
author: Karina B

title: Munni and Sweets
text: Munni wants her father to stay at home more often. And her father wants Munni to be happy. Munni likes eating sweets. And that is why her father brings sweets for her. "Munni, would you like to eat a laddoo?" "Nope" "Munni, would you like to have the Khaja sweet?" "Nope" "Munni, then, would you like to eat the Balushahi sweet?" "Nope, not at all." "Then what is it that you would like to have?" Munni then said, "I will have Kheer! But I will eat it with you and you stay with us in the house and have Kheer with us."
author: Karina B

title: Where Has My Mother Gone?
text: Hooper thought to himself, "Mummy! Where have you gone away?" "I must find my mother", thought Hooper and looked here and there. Hooper saw Ramji's horse far away. "Have you seen my mother?" Hooper asked Ramji's horse. "Nope, Hooper! I have not!" said Ramji's horse, "She must have gone somewhere and shall be back." And saying this, Ramji's horse flew away. Hooper moved on. A little ahead, a spider was spinning its web. "Have you seen my mother?" "Nope!" said the spider and resumed its work and Hooper then went ahead. Hooper then asked the crab the same question to which the crab said, "Hooper dear! I have not seen your mother." "Thank you Uncle!" said Hooper and went ahead. Hooper went near a pond and asked a frog but the frog did not know either. Hooper climbed a tree to look for its mother. But she was nowhere to be seen. When Hooper went and asked the flowers, they said, "Yes! Your mother had come here. Look over there, do you see your mother wandering over the flowers?" When Hooper heard this, he became very happy. "Oh dear mother! Here you are. Where did I not look for you?" said Hooper and felt very happy "Oh my dear Hooper! You came here searching for me" said Hooper's mother and hugged him tight.
author: Karina B

title: Tit for Tat?
text: Roopa were playing Ludo together. They were having a lot of fun. Suddenly, a mouse ran away from there. Then, a cat came there following the mouse and the cat collided with their Ludo game. All the pieces of the game got mixed up. "Uh-oh" said Raju. "Now what?" "I remember everything." said Roopa. "My chip was here, yours was there, and..." "Nope!" Raju interrupted her "Mine was here. Do not lie!" "Is that so?" Roopa shouted loudly. "I am going. I am going to go tell everyone that you are a big cheat." "Well then, I shall slap you." replied Raju. "Then I shall tell mother to beat you up." Roopa took the argument way too forward. "Then I shall call the police and get you locked up in a jail." Raju threatened her. "Then I shall call the goons and ask them to shoot you." Roopa was in no mood to give up. "Then I will bomb your house." said Raju and thought that he would win the argument. "Then I shall..." At that moment, a cat ran away from there. This time, a dog was chasing the cat! The pieces of the game got thrown away once again. Raju and Roopa were left astonished. They both then burst out laughing. "If I bomb your house, then my house would get destroyed too!" Raju began to think. "Or if I send you to jail, then whom will I play Ludo with?" Roopa remembered her words. "If we continue talking like this then soon we might start another world war over a game of Ludo!" Raju said smilingly. "Let's start over again" said Roopa. "My piece was here, nope..."
author: Karina B

title: BEAUTIFUL HANDS
text: Once upon a time, there was a girl named Neeru who lived in a small town named Gokuldham. She was fifteen and was living happily with her parents and siblings. Neeru was very intelligent and always secured good marks. She enjoyed going to school and was very punctual. Her mother was a strong and devoted lady who had been bedridden due to an illness which left Neeru in charge of the household work. One day her mother’s condition became serious and she died. To fulfill her responsibility she had to wake up early in the morning and she had to do all household work daily. She got her brother and sister ready for school and also packed their lunch boxes for them. So, the entire responsibility came on Neeru’s shoulders. She had to take care of the house and her younger siblings. Her father worked outside the village and he used to return late at night. To fulfill her responsibility, Neeru had to wake up early in the morning and do all the household work. She got her brother and sister ready for school and also packed their lunch boxes. Her mother was suffering from cancer because of which she was always on bed rest. Most of the time Neeru had to do most of the work in the household. One day her mother’s condition became serious and she died. After doing all the household work, she went to school every day. However, she always reached school on time. She also used to study late at night. She was very punctual and hard working. On the occasion of the prize distribution function Neeru was awarded the prize for punctuality, she also stood third in the class. When she came to the stage to get the prize, she was hesitant to hold the award. It seemed as if she was hiding her hands. The chief guest saw the condition of her hands. They were rough, scaly and untidy. He was surprised to see the condition of her hands. When she was asked about it, she first refused to explain anything but later she narrated her difficult journey. He was so impressed by her determination that he announced to give her the “Beautiful Hands" prize. He was amazed to see how a young girl not only took the responsibility of her family but also worked hard to achieve the goals of her life. On the occasion of the prize distribution function Neeru was awarded the prize for punctuality, she stood first in the class. When she came on the stage to get the prize, she was hesitant to hold the award. It seemed that she was hiding her hands. In the next special assembly, students were being awarded for their humanitarian traits. Now, it was time for the last award and that award was ‘Beautiful Hands.’ Neeru was not as pretty as the other girls. Nobody expected her to get this award. However, her name was announced. Her hands were not clean because of the household work she did, but even then, she got the prize. Everyone had a quizzical look on their faces, “Why was she receiving this award?” The chief guest got up and said that the condition of Neeru’s hands showed her hard-work. So, in the real sense, her hands were the most beautiful. Beautiful things cannot be judged by their external beauty. The chief guest saw the condition of her hands. Because it was burnt on one side and untidy, it looked so rough. He was surprised to see her hand’s condition because she was extremely intelligent. When she was asked about the condition of her hands, she first denied to explain and then she narrated her life’s story.Then she was struggling hard everyday. MORAL: We should not judge people based on their external appearances; we must appreciate their inner beauty.

title: Father's Unconditional Love
text: Once upon a time, in the outskirts of a city, there lived a taxi driver with his lttle daughter. His universe revolved around her. And although life seemed tough and wearying at times, but the taxi driver never lost his hope. A hope that one day his daughter will grow up to live a better life. "I am full, papa, I do not want to eat anymore." His daughter said. The father said, "Ok, my angel. Now go to bed, papa will come in a moment and tuck you in." "Okay!" The daughter said. Mohan, as that was his name would seldom eat a full meal, for even an extra piece of bun was hard to earn. FLASHBACK - It had been five years since he had lost his wife because of a fatal disease. Things were good back then. Mohan drove his own taxi and earned enough for his little family. But in order to incurthe cost of the treatment of his wife, the gentleman had to sell his taxi. But sadly, he could not save his wife. BACK IN THE PRESENT - "My angel, do you not want you father to tell you a story?" He asked. His daughter said, "Yes papa." Mohan started telling a story to her daughter and she driffted into a dreamland. Now Mohan drives someone else's taxi and even after working through the hours, he ears hardly enough. " Here you go, angel!", he exclaimed. He gave his daughter mil and cereal for the breakfast. His daughter asked him, "Where is your tea,papa?" "Baby, papa doesn't feel like drinking tea today. Come on, now, finish it quickly." Her father said. Every morning, Mohan would drop Sara, his daughter to her school. "Bye papa!" "Be a good girl, Sara! See you after school." And from there, he woulf go into his day, driving tirelessly all around the city. After 7 years "Great day my angel." Mohan said to his daughter. "I am scared papa." Sara said. Mohan said," Don't be scared Sara! You are smart and brave like your mother. Remember, high-school is where the child's personality gets shaped. You are the dough... choose the mould you would want to see yourself shaped into." "Yes Papa." Sara said. That day, as Mohan dropped Sara outside her new school, a sense of pride filled his heart. He was proud of his daughter and he knew his wife would be too. But deep down he also knew that life was going to be more challenging than ever. "Papa, I need to byuy these books." Sara said and handed a list to his father. His father said, " Are -aren't they availablebat the school library?" Sara said, "No." Mohan sighed andsaid, "Ok." Mohan went to a shop and gave the list to the shopkeeper. The shopkeeper sais,"Two dollar, Cash or Card?" Mohan was not having enough money and said, " Um...I-I forgot my wallet, excuse me." He went to another shop and sold his watch to the shop owner. The shop owner said, "You will get seventy five dollars, that's it." Mohan worriedly said, "Please,I need two hundred dollars." Shopkeeper laughed and said, "Two hundred dollars? Are you out of your mind? Seventy five dollars it is, take it or leave it."Mohan sadly said, "I will take it. Wait, you think I can get something for his chain." Shopkeeper hummed and said, " It's an old one but it is made of gold. I will give you two hundred dollars for both." Mohan's breath shivered as he nodded, for thr chain was a gift from his wife. He thanked the shop keeper. Shopkeeper said, "Twelve per cent interest per month as discussed. Sign here and here." After signing the paper Mohan purchased the bookand went back to his home. He said to his daghter,"Here are your books." Sara thanked her father and said,"Papa you are the best!" Days passed since that night and Mohan began to work longer shifts, as Sara's school expenses kept rising. He went to a stall and asked the shokeeper, "How much is that hotdog for?" Shopkeeper said, " One dollar and fifty cents." Mohan said, "Give me one please, I am starving." Suddenly his phone rang and it was her daughter Sara who was calling him. Mohan answered the call and said,"Hello, yes my angel, doyou need anything?" Sara said on the call, "Papa, I am very hungry. Can you get me something on your way?" Mohan questioned, "Didn't you eat your dinner?" Sara said, ''I didn't like it much so I threw it in the trash and cleaned the dishes. Please...... can you get me something?" Mohan felt sad but stil said, "Yes sure, How abuth the hot dog?" Sara said, "Yum! You are the best Papa." Mhan said to the shokeeper, "Can you wrap it up for me please?" Shopkeeper did and gave the hot dog to Mohan. That was one of the several nights, taht Mohan starts sleeping with empty stomach, but he would not mind it. For him, his daughter's happiness was everything. Now, while Mohan worked tirelessly, Sara began to discover a new world around her friends. "This nail polish is so pretty, Susan, it's better then mine." Suzy said to her friend. Susan said, "I know right, my father brought it for me from Hong Kong limited expendition." "Oooh! I love Hong Kong. We are planning to go there during the summer holidays." Susan said. Both the friends said to Sara, " You are awfully quiet today, Sara." "I am just listening to you guys." Sara said. Susan said, "You know, why don't you apply nail polish?"Sara said, " I-I don't wear them to school. I have like a huge collection, you know!" Suzy said," You should wear them to school, you are our friend, remember?" Sara went to her home after the school. Hr father when saw her, smiled and asked, "How was your day Sara?" "Papa, all my friends wear nail polish. I want to wear them too, you know?" Her father said,"I will give you one from the store." Sara said, "No papa, I don't from the local store, I need the branded ones. The ones Suzy and Susan wear." Mohan said, " But Sara-" "Papa please, I don't know, I want it." Sara said. Mohan purchased one branded nail polish for her daughter and gave it to her. The next day, Mohan dropped Sara at her school and said, "Have a great day my angel." Sara reached her school. She saw her friend and said, "Hey Suzy and Susan, Check it out!" Sara showed her polished nails to her friends. Suzy and Susan exclaimed together, "ooh! What a nice shade girl. By the way who is that man who drops you school everyday?" Sara said,"Oh, him.. Um.. he is my taxi driver." The bell rang and the students went to their classes. But Mohan listened every thing. Only the people you love the most can prick your heart as well your eyes. Thatb day, Mohan drove his taxi with a heavy heart., for all this world he was a taxi driver but a father for Sara. That changed that day. Next Day Sra said to her father, "Papa..um.. it's pkay you can drop me here. You don't have to go all the way to the gate." Mohan said,"Um.. are you sure? I have always dropped you at the gate since you were little." Sara said, "Please, papa." His father sighed and agreed. If one could feel, what Mohan has felt that day, they'd know what pain means. Mohan knew that his daughter was embaressed of his profession, but as a lovind father he just shrugged the feeling off. More days passed, and the once innocent and adorable Sara had know grown pmpous and arrogant. "There is a school trip that everyone is going tp next Friday. I want to go too." Sara said to her father. Her father said, "Sure,Where to?" Sar said, "Fort Lauderdale." Mohan was shocked. Sara again said, " Two hundred and fifty dollars include flight, stay and food." Mohan said, "Two hundred and fifty?" Sara nodded. Mohan asked, "Is it something that you cannot skip?" Sara said, "Of course not. What are you talking about? Need to pay the money by day after, latest. Good night papa, you are the best." Mohan sadly smiled and agreed. He again went to that shop and sold his engagement ring for three hundred dollars and gavr two hundred fifty dollars to her daughter for flight, stay and food and rest fifty dollars for her other for her other use. After giving the money to her daughter he said to her, "Now your bag is packe and I have made some toast for your journey." Sara made a disgusted face and said, ' For my journey? Papa, I am flying! You don't take food from home there airline provides you." Mohan said, "Oh! Okay! My bad!" Mohan dropped Sara at the airport and said, "Take care of yourself angel and here keep my phone with you, I will call you when I can." Sara said, "It's an old phone, papa. My friends will laugh at me. It's okay, I will tell them I forgot my phone at home or something." Mohan agreed. After dropping her daughter at the airport, he couln't tell how anxious and worried he was for his daughter. He just wished her a happy trip and left from there. " Oh my god! We are finally going out of the city!" Susan, her friend said. Sara said, " I know right? Where is Suzy?" Susan said, "She is running late, but do not worry. Come let's get our boarding passes." Sara started checking her bag and she said worriedly, "I-I can't find my ticket! It was in my bag. Did I drop it somewhere?" Susan was shocked, she said, "Sara, you can;t board your flight without your ticket. Search it propery." Sara became more worried. Meanwhile, Mohan had now driven into the city with a heavy heart, when he turned towards the passenger seat to seee Sara's flight ticket, he was shocked and said, " Oh my god! My angel left her ticket here. Her flight leaves in an hour and I have come far away from the airport. Ahh! and the traffic!" But Mohan was not going to let his daughter miss her flight. Determined as always, he turned his taxi round and hurled towards the direction of the airport. Mohan drove through the traffic, took short-cuts to finally reach the airport, but just as he was nearing the gate, another taxi from the other side came and collided on his. He groaned in pain and fainted in his taxi. The police and the crowd surrounded his taxi. Meanwhile, Suzy came in the airport. Sara asked her, "Where were you Suzy?" Suzy said, "Sorry, I am late. Sara, it's your driver, he;s met with an accident outside." Sara was extremely shocked and ran outside while crying. She saw her father in the taxi, the windshield scattered and him breathing heavily. When Mohan saw his daughter, he said with a weak voice, "Angel, you forget you ticket!" Tears welled up in Sara's eyes and heart filled with gratitude and love, she at once hugged her father. She said while crying, " I am sorry papa, I am so sorry, I love you papa! I am sorry, I could never be a good daughter." Her father said to her, "You are not good Sara, you are the best." Her friends saw everything and Suzy said to her, "Sara your driver had your ticket." And at that moment, Sara turned to her friends and said, "He is not my driver, he is my father and I am proud of him." And so that was the story of a daughter and her father's unconditional love for her. You see, there are many stories for mother's love butfather's love is as unconditional as a mother's love. It is just that not all fathers can express themselves the way mother's do. So, as children, it is our responsibility to always understand them.﻿
author: Jahnvi Devvanshi
illustrator: Jayesh Sivan; Karmacharya K.K; Prashant Soni; Vian  Oelofsen

title: A Teacher's Weekend
text: Miss Adkins is a first grade teacher. She loves her class! Every weekday, she comes to school and teaches her students. On the weekend, the students go home. They play with their friends, see their families, and have fun. But what do teachers do? Miss Adkins has a secret. On the weekends, she turns into a bird! Miss Adkins's best friend is the sun. But this weekend, the sun is sad. He sees all of the happy children playing, and he wants to play too. The sun can't play with the children, because he might burn them. Miss Adkins says, "Maybe you should play with the fish! You can't burn them, because they are in the water!" The fish are happy to play with the sun. Miss Adkins is happy that her friend is happy. This weekend has been fun, but Miss Adkins has missed her students. When Miss Adkins returns to school on Monday, she is a human again. She is so happy to see her students!
author: Kari Adkins

title: PROBLEMS AND STRUGGLE-The Positive part of Life
text: Once upon a time, there was a boy and his father who lived in a small village called Heerapur. The son always used to complain his father, for each and every thing, for he had to struggle. A Small village- Heerapu r One day, He again started complaining to his father that his life was miserable and he didn't know how he was going to make it easy. He was tired of fighting and struggling all the time. It seemed to him like as one problem was solved, another one soon followed. His father understood the situation and took him to the kitchen. He took some potatoes, eggs and coffee beans. He also took three pots and filled them with water and placed each of them on high fire. Once, three pots began to boil, he placed eggs in first pot, potatoes in second pot and coffee beans in the third pot. Father, "My life is miserable, I am tired of struggling through problems." After half an hour, he turned off the burners. He took the potatoes out of the pot and placed them in a bowl. He then pulled the eggs and placed them in a bowl. He then placed coffee beans in the cup. Now the father asked his son, "Son, what do you see?" He replied, "Potatoes, eggs and Coffee!" Father said, "Look closer and touch them", And this time he noticed that potatoes were soft. Now he looked to the eggs and observed they became hard-boilled eggs. Finally the Father asked his son to smell the coffee. Its sweet fragnance, brought a smile to the son and his father. Son, What do you see? Father, I see potatoes, eggs and coffee beans He asked his father, "What did this mean"?. Father finally explained that the potatoes, the eggs and coffee beans had each faced same problems and struggle, that is, boiling water. However, each of them reacted differently. The potatoes were strong and hard but it became soft and weak. The eggs were fragile until it was put in a boiling water. Then, inside of the egg became hard. But the coffee beans were unique. After they were exposed to the boiling water, they changed the water and created something new, which spread sweet fragnance all around. Father, exactly what does this mean? I am a bit confused... Father asked to his son, "Which one are you?". When problems and struggles knocks on your door, how will you respond? Would you react like a potato, an egg or coffee beans? The boy understood the essence of struggles and problems in life. As these are the only things that makes you stronger and stronger in life. And the only thing he had to do is convert all of them in a positive way and face them. "MORAL OF THE STORY" L ife is full of struggles and problems, but the only thing that matters is how you react and how you convert all the struggles into something positive. As like when coffee beans faced a struggle(i.e. boiling water) it not only mixed in the water but created something new, which spread sweet fragnance all around and brought happiness on everyone's face.
author: Vaibhav Saxena

title: A Symphony Of Friendship
text: Abigail?" I turn to see my best friend, Kaitlyn Leilani with her ruby hair sweeping of her shoulders, sea-green eyes contrasting it. "Hmm" "What are you thinking?" "I was hoping the class would go quiet so I can finish my assignment." "You know that's impossible unless there's a teacher to tame these... howling wolves " I let out a chuckle. Just then our class teacher, Miss Lewis came into our class. The whole class fell silent. "There has been a change in our time table." "I'll be assigning the teams and chores to everyone" she said. "Rhea, Marie and Adam, 'canteen helping' and 'wall painting'. Miss Lewis continued, then my name was called. "Abigail Black, Kaitlyn Leilani..." I was happy for a moment until I heard his name. "..and Alan Carter, 'music hall' and 'library cleaning' Alan Carter. Why? Just why? Alan, Katie and I were once best friends but then he broke a promise that I'll not talk of. Katie forgave him easily but I'm not the forgiving type. "Now children, try your best to finish the chores" The whole class dispersed with their groups for their chores. Just then Kate approaches me. Beside her a boy with brunette hair and sapphire eyes. "He comes under a truce" Kate assures. "Which doesn't mean I'm your friend." he scowls. "Same here" "You really haven't changed, have you? " he grimaces. " Neither have you" "Would you guys stop it?" Katie shouts. She calms down and asks. "The Library?" We both nod in agreement. We both make our way to the library. Katie follows us from behind, making sure we don't start world war III. The library had genres badly arranged. About a thousand books lay on the table to be stacked. We start working like mechanical machines. After what seemed to be hours I heard Alan's perplexed voice masked with euphoria. "Would you guys mind coming here a sec? I've got something to show. We both reached Alan, whose hand held a paper. "Did you tear a book?" I ask accusingly. "No, I did not. Geez, where do you get your assumptions?" "Well, you don't rea-" " THE POINT?" Katie interrupted. Alan shows us the paper. More than a paper it was a map. " A map" he says "More like a map of our school" I point out. "It leads us to the music hall" Katie says, bewildered. "Are you guys up for an adventure?" Alan asks hopefully. "Hell yeah!" I say "No one asked you." "I thought you sa-" "IF we do this adventure of yours would you guys stop quarreling like a pair of toddlers? "We are not tod-" "YES OR NO?" Katie demands. I hesitate but then.. "Fine." "Alan?" "You guys are unbelievable...fine." he scoffs. We then all run towards the music hall, breathlessly. Then we search until I ask "What exactly are we searching for?". "Umm...wait, there's a riddle on the map" he answers. I have a scroll but no quill. I have a bridge with no water beneath. Play me a melodious tune of 2 but 3, hidden in a music sheet. "Umm...uh...A violin! I know you'll have to play something on a violin but I don't know what!" I say. " Apparently, It seems to be hidden in a sheet" Katie adds. "A sheet...hmm...That's it! Sheet music!" I scream. We rummage through a pile of sheet music until we find a book called ' melodious tune '. "Is this it?" I ask. "I hope so" Kate says, tired from searching I open the book to find pieces '2' and 'But 3'. I look carefully. Then Alan peers at it and says " 'But 3' is a piano piece...I thought you said violin. " "I honestly have no idea what to do." I sigh, panic floods my voice. " '2' seems to be a violin piece" He says, trying to calm me down. He's seen those. Those stuff I have when I panic. I put my hand to my chest. " Are you fine? " Katie asks, alarmed. She too had seen those. "Abby, '2' seems to be a mirror duet..." Alan says, astonished. "Why don't you guys play the violin part? I'm no good at that. I'll play the piano piece." Kate suggests. " Sure." I say, my voice cracking. Katie hands us the violins while she sits on the dusty stool of the piano. Then we play. A euphonious melody filled the room. My panic flood was already drying up. Just then something eerie happened. A portal had formed. "Do we enter?" Katie asks " Maybe..." Alan says, puzzled. We enter and then the portal closes. I find myself in a land which seemed foreign to me. Greenery seemed to wrap around the land like warm blankets. A pond showed my reflection, a girl with caramel hair and amber eyes. Trees were bordering a path. Trees were bordering a path. Overall it seemed stupendous. Just then it struck me,the portal closed... We were trapped in here, probably forever. Panic floods my heart and I drop to my knees. "Oh no." I gasp. Katie crouches, trying to comfort me but none of it seemed to work. Alan kneels beside me and says "Abby, never get discouraged. Thousands discouraged Beethoven but did he listen? No, probably cause he was deaf..." I let out a chuckle. It seemed to get better. "Thank you" I whisper "Isn't that what friends are for?" he grinned. I stand up slowly, thinking what adventure awaits us...
author: Aashirya pandiaraj

title: He's gone
text: I get up in the morning, greet my parents, have a delicious breakfast and wait outside for the bus, while my mother caresses my uniform. Hi, nice to meet you. I’m Avantika, Avanti or Ants depending on who you ask. I'm pretty much an average Indian 12-year-old. Anyways, back to the story, the bus arrives and I get in, thankfully the seat next to Aarika, my best friend is empty. I chat with her on the way to school, get through the day with the help of my friends, playing and making jokes. I arrive home with my older sis, Mishita, and play in the playground with sonu, my brother. Then I have my tuition. I play with my adorable dog momo. I walk her out, wash my hands and have dinner with my family. I read for a while and go to sleep on my bed with my stuffed monkey, named Koko. Then, my father would kiss me goodnight. I had a completely average life. That was soon going to change. The weeks passed away with fun On a Sunday morning, my dad and I had an argument. I wanted to go to Vijay’s party today and despite all the persuading I had been doing, Amma and Appa didn’t listen. Sunday was father’s free day and he didn’t think it was a good idea for me to go as Vijay had been hanging around with a bad crowd lately. This wasn’t the first time that my parents had objected to me going to a party and I was set on having it my way. They still said no. I’m really cross all day and don’t even meet dad at night. The next morning, I head to school with Mishi and Sonu. I reach home and see my mother sitting at the table in worry. My mother says, shakingly, “Dad’s in the hospital, Avanti. I just got a call from them, just head with me to the hospital in the car and we’ll talk on the way” “Avanti, move” she says. But I can’t. I feel immobilized. My mother grabs me by the arm and somehow, I reach the car. She says that he got into an accident when he was going out for his lunch break. His car crashed and he’s in critical condition. 15 mins later, I’m looking at my father. He’s in a coma. I don’t go to school almost for a month and Amma also stays at home. The nights and the days are quiet and full of despair, maybe even sometimes hope. Until one day his vitals drop low, and he’s gone. Gone in the blink of an eye. I start crying, crying like the world’s ended. When mom got the phone call she was crushed. The next day the executor came home to read his will, saying that he had left all his stuff to me and amma. Amma tells me his funeral is in a week and after that, I’ll be going to school. She knows it'll be hard for me to return to normal, but she can't compromise my education. The saddest part is that things still happen the way they did. No one stops to acknowledge the fact that someone who was precious to someone has died. The sun still rises in the east, people go about their business on the streets, I'm still expected to go to school and move on in my life.The changes in my life have barely an impact on others. A week later, on the day of the funeral. I’m just standing there as his brother burns him. I can’t remember much about that day, except for the tears in everyone's eyes as we bid him goodbye. It's good that I have family who always support each other through such times. On the day that I have to go back to school, I’m very tired and it can show. I get into the bus and grab the seat next to Aarika. It’s awkward silence for a while before she says, “I’m sorry, you know I’m here for you. I just can’t imagine what it’s like.” I lay my head on her shoulder, look out the window, to see the raindrops and we drive to school. At school, I have to walk through a corridor of pity looks and be treated specially. Avantika take some rest, you can lay your head down Avantika. It's sorries from people I don't even know. I know it comes from good intentions, but I wish those sorries could bring him back. I’m glancing out the window of the bus, looking at a father feeding his daughter ice cream and another buying his daughter a balloon. I have never regretted something so much. I should have done more. I can remember all the fun stuff we did too when I was little. I return home and think bout the events of the day. Aarika’s the only one who’s on my side at school. Most of my friends distance themselves from me, others spread rumors about me, appa and amma. Some say he was a drunkard, others that he was depressed. It’s sad but I adapt, to being the new loser, the gloomy girl. I suddenly wake up with a jerk and realize that this was a dream. Monday didn’t happen at all. In fact, it’s today. Then I realize that my subconscious was telling me that I needed to appreciate my father. I get up and grab breakfast. After that, I ask Amma if we three can spend the day together after school. She thinks it’s a good idea and that she’s been meaning to go to this new restaurant and we could go together there for afternoon snacks and do some shopping later. I quickly got ready and afterwards we all set out in a car. We stopped at the restaurant. It was a pretty cute place, more like a cafe. It was surrounded on all sides by nature. We ate loads of food and ended the meal with a banana split. We then went to the bookstore, where I asked for recommendations from my father and he told me that he was really fond of Hardy boys and Roald dahl growing up. We then headed to the clothes shop where we got a bunch of clothes and had lots of fun in the changing room. I bought a shirt for Appa with my spare money and then we headed to the supermarket to get groceries for dinner. I looked at the sweets section while my parents shopped for groceries. I ended up getting a pack of skittles and a bag of marshmallows, as well as some fruit juice for sonu. We ended the day with a family cooking session and a movie. My appa read me a story before bed. It was the perfect day. Before sleeping, I made sure to apologize for the argument and appreciate my father.

title: Reality of our country
text: Krishi was a small girl in a small village but her dreams were big. She loved reading books and was a curious about everything that went about. She was also a great inventor. Her dream was to study hard and become someone great to help her village and her people. A few years back, she had lost her mother due to dengue. This incident made her determined to help her village so that no one ever suffers from what her mother and family suffered from. As time passed by, she grew into a wise and beautiful girl. Once, a boy was bitten by a snake in her village. All the grown ups panicked and thought that the boy was gonna die but then, Krishi came from amongst the crowd and helped the boy. She first tied a clean cloth tightly above the snake bite to reduce blood flow. Then she asked the boy to stop panicking because, it can increase the blood flow which is not good since it contains the snakes venom. Then she quickly took the boy to the nearest hospital. The boy was saved and his parents were shedding tears of happiness. They blessed Krishi and told her they were ready to help her in any way. By the time she was 15 years old, she had already won several competitions and had made a name for herself. Soon, she had graduated from school and moved on to a big city for her higher studies. She used to think that her village was very big but, after visiting the city her thought went for a toss and she understood that the world was a much bigger place than she imagined. At first she found it hard to settle but soon she found her own ways to make her space in this big and round world... One of the first situations that made her doubt her capabilities was when she was denied admission in her dream college just because she was a village girl. But then the head administrative staff analysed her applications and were very delighted and offered her a seat in the college. This made her extremely happy and made her realise that she can accomplish whatever she wanted to if she just put all her will and focus into it... She was a very ambitious and was a hardworking girl and tried her best to succeed in everything. But this isn't always possible because everyone has their flaws and makes mistakes. She realized this when she failed in her half-yearly art test. She wasn't very good at drawing but she did she enjoy it. She then accepted the fact that no one is good at everything but, we can surely improve at things we are bad at. A long time passed by, Krishi grew into a intelligent and charming woman. She had become a well-known doctor who had gained immense prestige in a short span of time and started working in one of India's biggest hospitals. Even rich people started to take treatments and consultancies form her. But, one such incidence made her think twice about why she became a doctor at the first place....... One beautiful morning as Krishi sat on her rocking chair reading a newspaper, she saw an article that explained the condition of her village. As she read the article, tears started rolling down her cheeks. She felt guilt and sorrow. The people of her village were in trouble. Many of the villagers had died due to dengue. The government hadn't provided the village with enough health-care facilities such as sanitation, hospitals etc. She decided to take a big decision which could change her life.... She decided to leave her job and settle in her village and thought of opening her own clinic to treat the people and suffering for various illnesses. Not only would this take a lot of money, but also a lot of courage. Despite the fear that she might fail, she took the step with all positivity. She reminded herself that no one has ever been successful all the time.... Within the span of 2 month or so, she had established her own clinic in her own village. The people of her village were very proud of her but soon one of the biggest tragedies of her life occured, she lost her father due to heart attack. She felt heart broken but didn't give up hope. She continued working and treating people to make her parents' souls happy. Her clinic was working smoothly but she suffered financially until one day. She received a letter from one of the most well known hospital in the country in which she was asked to join a very big and popular hospital which agreed to give her a commendable salary too. She was now in a very big dilemma. She was bewildered. Should she choose money and comfort or satisfaction but less financial stability. She thought with all mindfulness for a couple of days..... She then remembered how happy she felt when she treated a poor kid who would have died otherwise, just because she was poor and couldn't afford to go to a well-maintained hospital for her treatment. That girl also made her a thank you card. She had made her final decision. She chose satisfaction and helping the poor because there are so many doctors and hospitals treating the people who can afford them but the poor always suffer. There is no one thinking about them just because they can't pay them enough. Krishi was looked upon as an inspiration not because she helped the poor unlike others, but because of her courage and for following her heart and not being selfish.... Every year India produces 67,000 doctors. India has over 1.5 million doctors in total but most of the doctors either work in high paying hospitals or go abroad in search of money. In between all of this, the people who cannot afford such expensive treat suffer the most. Government has tried to open many government hospitals that provide health care facilities with minimal cost. Even though so many steps have been taken by the government, not much has improved. Still the poor suffer due to not finding good health treatment. We should make sure no one suffers in our country just because of financial status. WE ARE THE FUTURE OF OUR COUNTRY....

title: A Girl's Best Friend
text: (This story is written through the eyes of Duke- An emotional support dog who is a Golden Retriever. His thoughts are written in the form of a diary entry.) 5th March 2022, Saturday Today I was really mad at my owner. Considering the very despicable thing she had done! I always thought my owner was weird since she wore a white coat over her clothes for work and talked to some people she called her “patients” And she had other dogs with her too, who were my friends naturally. We all lived together, shared our food and our toys. Our owner didn’t really interact with us much. But I didn’t care, I had my buddies. And once in a while, some humans would come visit her at work and take one of us! One by one, my friends would be given away to her “patients’ and I really didn’t know why. But it was my turn today. And in a few minutes, I was taken to a girl’s house! 6th March 2022, Sunday I felt really mad at my owner but moreover overwhelmed. I was at my owner’s office one day and the next day at some random girl’s place. I missed my friends so much and I even tried to escape but it didn’t work. I think the girl’s name was June since that was what everyone has been calling her lately. She was super young with short black hair, pale skin and a purple hoodie on. She looked really distant and didn’t even look at me! Rude! But I saw a man and a woman with her. They seemed friendly and always gave me treats. Later on, I realized that they were her parents. I never knew my parents, they were given away to them uncanny humans! I felt sad sometimes but my buddies were always with me. 7th March 2022, Monday It took me some time to realize this but I think I know what is wrong with June. She is diagnosed with something called bipolar disorder. Which basically meant she would be super depressed one day and super energetic the other. So that’s why June wasn’t adoring my cuteness the day before!! This explains everything! Her rude behavior on the first day and then her "trying to give me treats" behavior the other. Everyday, June dresses up and carries a book carrier on her back and goes on a bus to a big building where other young humans come too and learn about some numbers and letters. And then she comes home when it becomes really hot. Humans live a weird life. 8th March 2022, Tuesday Today, I went on my very first walk with my new family!!! I finally got to see my neighborhood and I realized that other dogs live in the neighborhood! I mean, that’s straight up disrespectful! Knowing another dog is living in the neighborhood takes away attention from you. So, to claim my dominance I peed on the road! It will surely make the other dog aware and will leave my territory. A random thought that crosses my mind daily is the fact that humans fight each other with weapons and really big tanks to claim their land when in reality, us, dogs just urinate on our territory and the other dogs are like “Okay, I was gonna pee their too, but nobody can defy the pee, so congrats on your new land!” Humans are really so unnatural…. 9th March 2022, Wednesday I saw June crying today and I really started worrying about her. So, I walked towards her and put my head on her lap to comfort her. She eventually stopped crying and started talking to me. “Today, I was bullied so much by a bunch of girls. They thought my condition was weird and they started mocking me. I tried stopping them but they wouldn’t take me seriously. I even tried telling my class teacher but she said that I should ignore them and they would eventually go away.” June said with tears. “Why do teachers say that? That is the most stupid advice anybody and can ever give!” “Gosh! Why does the universe hate me!? What have I ever done??” she said while breaking down again. “You don’t even understand me, why am I talking to you?” She said with a faint smile. I finally understood what I was here to do. I’m here to help June and comfort her with her illness. I quickly brought out my leash and placed it in front of her. I think she understood I was asking her to take me on a walk. We went roaming the neighborhood and I could see that she felt happier. I realized that I didn’t want to go back to my previous home. I wanted to stay here and protect June from all the hate she was getting. I cared for her and wanted to be by her side forever. ~Aadiya Roy 7 A Delhi Public School Nashik (CBSE Budding Authors Program- Round 2)

title: Anil & Anu: Case of the missing necklace
text: Anil and Anu were bored! Since their summer holidays had been announced, the innovative brother and adventurous sister were meandering around their neighborhood aimlessly, having nothing interesting to do at all. “Find some friends or ride your bicycles”, was the only answer they received from their mom when they complained of boredom. On a hot day in April, Anil had a splendid thought. “Let’s start a detective agency! Being young crime-solvers would catch everyone’s eyes and it would help us to pass our time too.” As if reading his mind, Anu paused her crime-thriller movie and walked out to the kitchen where Anil was in a trance about the fabulous idea he had just brainstormed. “You know, we should start a detective agency! We could have plenty of business since people like Anitha Aunty always lose stuff and mishaps happen here and there often.” “You read my mind, Banana.” Anu smiled at the nickname. Her older brother called her Banana for as long as she can remember. It was her favorite fruit after all. “You know, we should start a detective agency! We could have plenty of business since people like Anitha aunty always lose stuff and mishaps happen here and there often.” “You read my mind, Banana.” Anu smiled at the nickname. Her older brother called her Banana for as long as she can remember. It was her favorite fruit after all. “But wait, what will we do for space? We need a place to manage our stuff, right?” queried Anu. “But wait, what will we do for space? We need a place to manage our stuff, right?” queried Anu. “Let’s talk to Amma. She might have an idea,” piped out Anil. Anil and Anu’s talk with their Amma, Sumi, had been quite fruitful. Sumi had let the two investigators use the little garden house as their lair. Satisfied, Anu ran out to set up their office. Sumi chuckled at her two avid investigators. The next day, Anil used the printer at home to print about fifty pamphlets advertising their side hustle. Anu then went and distributed them around the neighborhood. Two days had passed and nobody had called them yet. Disheartened, Anil and Anu gave up. They had packed up and were about to leave when Vani Shanmugham, who was two houses away from them, rang the bell to the dainty little garden shaft. “Let’s talk to amma. She might have an idea,”piped out Anil. Anil and Anu’s talk with their Amma, Sumi, had been quite fruitful. Sumi had let the two investigators use the little garden house as their lair. Satisfied, Anu ran out to set up their office. Sumi chuckled at her two avid investigators. The next day, Anil used the printer at home to print about fifty pamphlets advertising their side-hustle. Anu then went and distributed them around the neighborhood. “Are you Anil and Anu?” “Yes.” “My necklace is missing. It is a family heirloom.” The brother and sister shared a look and invited Vani inside. Vani gazed inside the room, staring at the shovel and the cobweb with the spider at the corner, and said “Do you guys have any experience in these things?” and Anu suppressed a laugh in reply. The duo asked Vani to sit down and asked her to dive into the details of the mystery. “So, the heirloom is passed on for generations and generations. As my great-grandma gave it to grandma, my grandma gave it to my mom.” “Okay.” “I keep it locked away in a petite ivory box at night which in turn, is kept in a drawer. I wear it every day. But after I wore it yesterday, I couldn’t find it. We searched the entire house yesterday but it wasn’t there anywhere in the house.” “Alright, did anyone else wear it or was it just you?” “Usually only I wear it. But my younger sister borrowed it once or twice.” “Okay, can you describe it?” “It is silver in color, has a plumeria in the middle with a tiny V hanging along with it.” “Mhmm, thank you, Vani. We will look right into it.” Vani muttered a tiny bye and rushed back home. Anil sighed. They were new to the ‘detective’ business after all. Anu spoke up after a moment of silence. “What are we going to do now?” Anil and Anu brought out their bicycles and started wandering around the neighborhood. They decided to make their first pit stop at Vani’s house. “Ding Ding” Vani’s Amma opened the door with a cheery smile. “Oh! Vani was just talking about you. Come on in!” The duo accepted the invite and stepped into the lovely Mediterranean house. Vani spotted them and came running. “Hey, guys! Do you need something?” “Do you have security cameras around here?” “Uh, yeah, we do. Come, I'll show you.” The trio went to Vani's Appa's study. Mr. Shanmugham was a tall and thin man with a kind face. He let them look at the camera feed and asked “Have you found out who took it?” “No Mama, but we surely will!” replied Anil. As they watched the camera feed, the duo noticed a burly, young man standing outside a window and staring intently at something glittering inside. They asked Mr. Shanmugham about the young man. “Mama, do you know who he is?” “Oh him! He's Shyam, Ramu Ayya's son.” “Is Ramu away?” “He's our watchman. Shyam lives in the outhouse along with Ramu Ayya and takes care of the garden. Do you want to go talk to him?” They then went to meet Shyam in the outhouse. Shyam was standing outside, throwing and catching stones with his hand. “Shyamm! Shyamm!” called out Mr. Shanmugham. As soon as Shyam saw the group approaching him, he threw the stones down and started sprinting. A confused Vani and Mr. Shanmugham stared at Shyam, glued to their spots. Anil, who always wanted to be a police officer, took the lead and gave everyone instructions. “Anu, you take the bicycle. Vani, you stay back at home. Shanmugham Mama, get your scooter and follow us.” They pursued Shyam and the three cornered him. Shyam started perspiring and whimpering. Anil put on his most serious face and questioned Shyam. “Why did you run Shyam?” “I was scared.” “Why were you scared? Did you take something? Did you do something? Are you hiding anything?” “Aiyo, Aiyo stop! I only stole the mangoes carrots and cabbages from the garden. I'm so sorry!” Mr. Shanmugham looks at Shyam, dumbfounded. Anu and Anil stifle a laugh at his reaction. “So, it was you who stole it! You told me it was a squirrel!” “Mama, how can a tiny squirrel carry such a large cabbage? I thought you studied in IIT and all.” Mr. Shanmugham twists Shyam's ear and drags him back to the house. An anxious Vani was waiting for them back at the house. “Did you find it? Did Shyam have it?” “Nope! Can we look around your house?” “Uh, sure!” And so the search began. Again. Anil looked in the kitchen inside the flour containers and Vani looked in the showcase, coughing due to the heavy dust on her Appa's trophies. Anu looked under the sofa only to find a pair of eyes staring back at her. “Aaaah, Aniiiiiiillll!!” Anil rushes over to her and at the same moment, Kutty, the Shanmugham household's pet dog, leapt on Vani and gave a loud yelp. Exhausted, Vani, Anil, and Anu sat on the couch simultaneously, sighing in sync. Being a detective is hard. Suddenly, a lightbulb clicked in Anu's head. “Do you have a picture of the necklace?” “I’m sure I do, somewhere…,” trailed Vani. Vani ran back to her room and brought back Amma's phone. She opened the gallery and chose a picture. “There! That one.” The necklace was gorgeous. Anu was analyzing the chain when she had an idea. “Does the chain have a clasp?” “Yeah.” “And the “pavadai-sattais” (skirt and blouse) you wear have a zip?” “Yeah.” It finally dawned on a confused Anil. Vani’s necklace had gotten stuck in the zipper of her pavadai-sattai! When Anil and Anu had thought the case was intriguing, it just flattened out to be the easiest case that they’d solved. “Hey Vani, if you don’t mind can we check your laundry?” grinned Anil. Vani led them to the room and showed them the basket. Anu picked up the pavadai-sattai Vani wore yesterday. To Vani’s surprise, the necklace was stuck in the zipper. Anu then explained that when Vani told her that the necklace did have a clasp, Anu figured out that the necklace could have been lodged along with the zipper. Vani’s Amma served cold drinks and pastries as a reward. Anu and Anil were on cloud nine. They hadn’t expected to be detectives, let alone solve a mystery. The duo thanked Vani's Amma and left. When Sumi heard about the wonderful adventure Anil and Anu had, she couldn’t help but say “All’s well that ends well.”
author: Vaishali Saravanan
