I could not imagine myself without you. Are you listening”? Maria cried bitterly. After listening to all this, Olivia was moved too. Tears rolled down from the corners of her eyes. She told everything with difficulty. She confessed. “I wanted to go to the forest just to harm you. I became malicious because I found you were taking my position. You started helping the other girls only to let me down. You became their favourite. Even the teachers also favoured you, better than me. How could a new girl be better than me? Everyone was acting like they could not stop themselves praising Maria. Maria, Maria, Maria everywhere. I could not bear all this. So, I thought of a plan to get rid of you, Maria. Invading the jungle was my plan only. But, you are a gem. I have understood now why everyone loves you. I admit that I was totally wrong. Please forgive me for the last time.” finished Olivia. Her eyes shone desperately. Maria and her friends were stunned to listen to all this. “It was not you, but your selfishness that wanted to harm me. I don't hold any grudges. I have forgotten this all. Now don't regret it. It was all a lesson for you from God," said Maria calmly. Olivia had understood the real meaning of love. With her tears shed all her anger and ill will. After this, they hugged each other. They thanked God for saving her soul. Ellie informed all their anxious parents about their delay. Next day, they bought tickets to watch a friendship movie!
author: Astha Chauhan
illustrator: Rob Owen; Sayan  Mukherjee; Suvidha Mistry

title: My Big Sister Can See Dragons
text: My big sister can do a lot of things better than me. She can swim all the way across the swimming pool. I still grab for Mom when I need to breathe. My sister can read chapter books, even the kinds with hundreds of pages. I can only read the ones with pictures. And when she draws a dog, Mom knows if it’s a German shepherd or a poodle. The last time I drew a dog, Mom thought it was a hot dog with marshmallows for feet. But you know what else my big sister can do? She can see dragons. It’s true. Today, when she came home from school, she suddenly said, "Shhh! Don’t move. There’s a baby dragon behind you." I turned my head, but I didn’t see anything. "Where?" "Oh, you can’t see them. You need a dragon eye in order to see dragons." she said. "Dragons?? You mean there are more that one?" "Of course!" answered my sister. "There’s a whole world of dragons, but only special people, like me, can see them." "Can you teach me?" I said. She told me to half-close my eyes and roll up my eyeballs ‘til things started to look fuzzy. "Nothing’s happening," I said. My eyes were starting to hurt. "Do what you do when we pretend to be sleeping when Dad comes home," she said. So I opened my mouth and let my eyes roll up. And I saw a white blur just behind my sister. "I saw it!" I cried. "At least I think I did. Is it white?" "That baby one is," said my sister. "But there are blue ones, orange ones... and even a polka-dotted one." She said that I should keep practicing so I could see the pink one. Pink is my favorite color. I kept trying. But even the white one was still kind of blurry. I crossed my eyes really hard and saw double of everything... except dragons. My sister said we could have a dragon party. She would invite all the dragons over and we could serve chocolate crinkle cookies. She said crinkle cookies are dragons’ favorite food. We set the table, and I brought out my stuffed lizard toy. I thought the dragons would enjoy meeting one of their cousins. It was the best party ever. My sister pointed out the purple mommy dragon who had little babies hanging onto her. And the slimy green one who liked to live in mushy swamps. And the grumpy old grey grandfather dragon who had no more teeth, so you didn’t have to be scared of him. There was just one teeny-tiny problem. I still couldn’t see anything. But I didn’t want my sister to know. "Look!" my sister said, "The little one is dancing!" I jumped up. "Ooh, can I dance with her? I do ballet!" "No, no, no—she’s over there!" she pointed across the room. "Can’t you see her?" She started to get that look like when she’s about to tell me I’m too little to play with her, so I quickly said, "Yes, I see it! I just didn’t know dragons could dance so well!" Then my sister said something that got me worried. "We need to be careful, though. Sometimes bad dragons come, too. And they might stay behind when the good ones go home." So she looked under our beds, on top of the bookshelf, and inside the laundry basket, and declared them dragon-free. "Ok, I’m going to bed now," she said. "Good night, little sister." She put her blanket over her head and fell asleep right away. That’s another thing my big sister can do better than me. She can fall asleep as soon as she closes her eyes. But I lay wide-awake thinking of the bad dragons. How will I protect us from dragons if I can’t even see them?! Then I thought I heard a little scritch-scritch sound from behind the bathroom door. Oh no! We forgot to check there! I shook her awake. Which is really hard to do. So I sat on her tummy and yelled really loudly into her ear. "Gaaaabby! Wake up!" My sister opened one eye. "There’s a bad dragon hiding in the bathroom! You have to fight him, because I can’t... because I can’t really see the dragons!" You know what she said? But I lay wide-awake thinking of the bad dragons. How will I protect us from dragons if I can’t even see them?! Then I thought I heard a little scritch-scritch sound from behind the bathroom door. Oh no! We forgot to check there! I shook her awake. Which is really hard to do. So I sat on her tummy and yelled really loudly into her ear. "Gaaaabby! Wake up!" My sister opened one eye. "There’s a bad dragon hiding in the bathroom! You have to fight him, because I can’t... because I can’t really see the dragons!" You know what she said? "Oh, Marty, I can’t see them either. I just made them up." Then she pulled the blanket over her head and went back to sleep. Maybe my big sister isn’t more special than me after all. So maybe if I work hard at it, I’ll be able to swim across the pool, too, just like her. And I’ll be able to draw real-looking dogs. And maybe, just maybe, if I keep practicing, maybe I’ll be the one to actually see dragons! After all, just because my big sister says she made them up, that doesn’t mean they’re not really there. Right?
author: Rocky  Sanchez Tirona

title: Missing a Friend
text: Yangjee is riding a bus to the village to visit her aunt. She is sad because she didn’t get to tell her best friend, Lucky, that she was leaving for a few days. “ Lhasso, * Aaru, * ” Yangjee says hello to her aunt. “Come inside and have some food, Aanga. * ” *lhasso-hello *Aaru- aunt (mother's younger sister) *Aanga- a term of endearment used for little girls “Wow, look at all the roti, * mohi, * and sukuti. * If Lucky were here, her mouth would water like mine.” *roti- a round, crispy, puffy bread common in Nepal *mohi- yogurt drink or buttermilk drink *sukuti- meat jerky “Come, Aanga,” Yangjee’s aunt says. ”Let’s go for a walk around the village.” “Oh, look at that chungi * made of leaves,” Yangjee says. *Chungi- a game similar to Hacky Sack played with a ball of rubber bands. It is played in Nepal and Northeastern India. “If Lucky were here, we would have so much fun playing hide-and-seek.” “Look! There are so many fish in the river,” Yangjee says. “If Lucky were here, we would splash around in the water.” Yangjee misses Lucky. “I wonder if Lucky is thinking about me, too.” In the morning, it is time for Yangjee to leave. ”Goodbye, Aaru,” she says to her aunt. ﻿ When she gets home, she says, “ Aama * I’m going to see Lucky.” *Aama means mother “I’m sorry I didn’t tell you I was leaving, Lucky,” Yangjee tells her friend. Lucky is quiet. “Please say something,” Yangjee says. “I missed you so much, Yangjee, and I thought about you every day,” Lucky says. Yangjee hugs her best friend. ”Here, I brought your favorite cream biscuits,” she says. ”See what else I brought for you!” Yangjee says. “Wow, mangoes and bananas from the village!” Lucky exclaims.
author: Yangjee  Thokar

title: The Hill
text: CHAPTER 1 (Journey To The Green Hill) Once upon a time, there lived a girl who in her town was known as Garon. With her, lived a 5 year old girl called Heidi. Heidi's parents died 2 years ago, Garon's grandfather also left her alone. So after all these incidents, Garon was left alone with Heidi. Garon was doing multiple jobs a day, to help Heidi. Garon just wanted money to afford clothes, books and toys for Heidi, but as Heidi was growing up, it was becoming too hard for Garon to take care of her. She at last decided that Heidi will now live with her grandfather, Hansel. Hansel lived in the village of Elgis. He was a kind of a person who didn't to socialize with people. When Heidi was 8, Garon left her at her grandfather's house. At first, heidi's relationship with Hansel was not going so good. But as time went by, it kept getting better. It was the first time Hansel was enjoying to talk and interact with a person. It was night. Hansel got some rice and bread - butter for dinner. Heidi was feeling really hungry. She quickly ate the food and went to sleep in a jiffy. She felt excited for her next day ahead of her. It was soon morning and the sun was smiling on Hansel and Heidi. She woke up, rubbing her eyes. She called out to Hansel and searched for him everywhere in the house, but he was nowhere to be found. Soon, she looked out the window and saw Hansel chopping wood. She wore her slippers and ran outside. She asked Hansel, "What will we be doing today?" Hansel replied, "Today, we'll be visiting the wood, only the outskirts though..." Heidi jumped with excitement. Hansel again said, "We are going to visit the woods, but first you'll have to take a bath in the tub which I have filled with water for you. The soap is kept there too." She quickly came out of the bathroom, shining and feeling fresh. She quickly dressed herself, combed her hair, wore her slippers and went outside. Hansel was already waiting for her. He said, "Shall we go?" She said with excitement, "Yes!" They packed their lunch and went out for the woods. soon, it was afternoon, both of them were starving. They sat down on the soft grass, started eating their meal and enjoyed the marvelous view of the woods. It was becoming dark now. they had to leave, because it was the time when the wild animals come out. They reached their house and as soon as they entered, Heidi started to feel cranky, as she was tired. Hansel suggested her to go to sleep right away. CHAPTER 2 (Meeting Peter) It was the next day now. Heidi went close to the window, yawning. She saw Hansel talking to a boy her age. She went outside and soon came to know that the boy's name was Peter. He used to work for Hansel by taking his herd of sheep for grazing. Heidi suddenly had a thought in her mind and asked Hansel, "Can I go to watch the sheep with Peter?" Hansel said, "That's fine with me, as long as it's fine with Peter." She looked at Peter, hoping that he would say yes, but what he said was, "No! I'm really sorry to say this, but it's already difficult for me to take care of 15 sheep." She said again, "Please, pretty please!!!" Peter reluctantly said yes. He took her and as they were on the path, Peter told her everything that she had to follow. Only if, she wanted to go with him again. She was at her best behaviour and cooperated with Peter. She did everything Peter asked her to do. Soon, it was time for lunch and both of them were starving. They sat down to eat their meal. Hansel had gave them a loaf of bread and some slices of cheese to eat. Heidi looked over the herd of sheep while Peter was cutting the loaf of bread in pieces. Some time passed, Peter saw Heidi sprinting towards him. She stopped and as she was catching her breath, Peter asked, "What happened?" She pointed towards a cliff and said, "A sheep is going towards that cliff." Peter, without saying anything picked up his staff and ran towards that cliff. He jumped towards the sheep and caught it's hind legs just in time. He tried to pull the sheep backwards but the sheep was constantly pulling itself forward. He was about to call out Heidi for help but she was already there, trying to pull Peter back. It was now evening and Peter had brought back all the sheep and Heidi safely. She wished Peter BYE and went inside the house to sleep. She was feeling exhausted. CHAPTER 3 (Going To Meet Garon Again) Some time passed away. Hansel saw Heidi sitting on a chair and watching a photo of herself and Garon. Hansel could literally see in her eyes that she was missing Garon. On the other hand, Garon was also missing Heidi. Both of them wanted to see each other again. So, Hansel decided to go to Garon's house, because he just wished for Heidi to be happy. He went close to her and said in a low voice, "Pack your bags, we're going to visit Garon's." Listening to that, Heidi realised that she had a smile on her face. She quickly went to her room, packed some clothes and was ready to go. When they reached, Heidi sneaked inside quietly when suddenly, Hansel asked, "What do you think you're doing?" Heidi replied, "SHHHHHH! I'm trying to give her a surprise." Hansel got a faint smile on his face and followed her. She went into Garon's room, and when Garon saw her, she ran to her and hugged Heidi tightly. Garon asked, "How did you get here?" Heidi replied, "Hansel brought me here." He comes slowly into the room, expecting that Garon would still be angry with him. But she hugged Hansel tightly and said, "Thank you so much! This means everything to me." Hansel and Heidi stayed at Garon's house for 3 days and really enjoyed this short span of time. From that day, Heidi and Hansel started meeting Garon every month. Heidi and Garon including Hansel were all happy and enjoyed and interacted with each other every month. THE END.
author: Arvin Mohanta
illustrator: Adrie  Le Roux; Adrija Ghosh; Maithili  Joshi; Sonali Zohra

title: My Land, Diverse India
text: The Semester had ended and it was time for the winter holidays. Paheli wanted to spend her holidays reading books, unlike other kids. Her English teacher had said ‘Books are the storehouse of knowledge dating back to millions and millions of years ago.’ Paheli quickly left the school and sat in the car as she was thinking about all sorts of crazy books she could read. ‘Mommy, can you take me to the Library?’ asked Paheli excitedly. ‘May be some other day, Paheli’, replied her mother. ‘Please Mom, It would mean a lot to me…’ and the conversation went further and the mother agreed. As they were getting close to the public library, Paheli quickly dropped her bag and ran towards the library and ran towards the ‘Geo-History Section’. She chose a big book titled ‘My Land, Diverse India’. She borrowed the book and came back hurriedly. They drove back home, Paheli’s happiness knew no bounds. In the evening, Paheli opened the book and was surprised to see the names of many states and union territories. She had never imagined India to be so big and diverse. She opened the book and started reading it. She was amazed to read about various places like Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, etc. ‘Wow! This book is very interesting.’ said Paheli to herself. ‘I wish I was able to visit these beautiful places-’ thought Paheli. Just then she heard her mother saying ‘We are going to Leh and Ladakh!!’. Paheli realized that there was no detail related to Ladakh, so she wanted to explore the place herself. She quickly packed her bags and waited for the next day. The crow-coo of the rooster began and Paheli ran out of her room and cried out loud ‘We are going to Ladakh!’. Soon, they boarded their plane and landed in Ladakh after a flight of an hour and forty-five minutes. ‘Leh is so beautiful,’ Paheli said. They had planned many activities such as boating, skydiving and mountain climbing. One of them was to go skiing in the dry cold mountainous regions of Leh, Ladakh. Paheli sat in the SUV they had rented, and went on a long journey to a nearby mountain. Paheli saw the rich cultures and traditions of Ladakh including the colorful dragon festival, Naropa. The mountain they were about to ski on was near many gompas, who were decorated with bright colors and lights. Paheli entered the skiing resort and saw decorated hallways with paintings of Lord Naropa. Paheli quickly dressed up and ran towards the snowy hills bottom to the mountain. As Paheli and her family were having a great time skiing near the big hill, a strong earthquake of 7.2 magnitude hit the Xining in China and was felt in many parts of Tibet, Akshai China and parts of Ladakh. As Paheli and her family were enjoying, there was a teror near the Tibetan-Indian Borders. Paheli felt something was wrong! She heard the sounds of snow storms from a distance. She began to warn everybody that something huge was on its way. No one paid heed to her warnings! Minutes later the ground tempered and people ran out of the resort in terror. The mountain had caused an avalanche. I think Paheli did a great job!She heard her father commenting. Just then every house turned into pieces of dust, scrap and rust. The earthquake was of the same intensity as that experienced in Kathmandu, Nepal. The big avalanche caused severe damage to Leh, thanks to Paheli no one was injured. And if you're wondering, yes, Paheli finished her book before the new school year! Paheli was ready to tell this crazy story to her friends, when she reached back home! A surreal experience of knowing the unknown!
author: MAHIR TALWAR
illustrator: Selina Masego Morulane; Aindri C; Jupiter  Pradhan; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lavanya Karthik; Olivia Fraser; Samidha Gunjal; Sanjana Desai; Shivam Choudhary; Shubhshree Mathur; Sireesha  Srk; Tasneem Amiruddin

title: Meeting for the First Time
text: “ Aama, * what is that place?” I ask. “Our new home, Yangjee,” Aama replies. *Aama means mother in many languages spoken in Nepal ”Wow, these windows are big,” I say. “ Dai, * where is my doll?” “I do not know, Yangjee,” Dai replies. *Dai means big brother in many languages spoken in Nepal I look for my doll. “My pretty little doll, where are you?” I call. I see a small girl. The girl looks at me from behind the landlady. I want to talk to her. “What is your favorite food?” I ask. “What is your name?” I am surprised. The girl is quiet. “She is shy,” the landlady tells me. ”Her name is Lucky.” “Oh! Lucky!” I say. “What a nice name!” I take Lucky’s hand. We run outside. ”Lucky, what do you like to play?” I ask. Lucky stays silent. ”Why does she not say anything?” I wonder. I am annoyed. But I want to be Lucky’s friend. “Here is your doll, Nani, * ” Dai says through the window. ”Yay!” I dance happily with the doll. *Nani means little girl in Nepali Lucky finally speaks. “I like to play with dolls,” she says. Lucky and I dance happily.
author: Yangjee  Thokar

title: We like Different Things
text: “Hi! I am Yangjee.” “Hey! Come here,” Yangjee calls to the girl. ”What is your name?” The girl says, “Hi! My name is Lucky.” ”Yangjee,” Lucky says, ”why are you so small?” “I am not small,” Yangjee replies. ”You are just tall!” Yangjee says, “Play ball with me, Lucky!” “Okay, okay, I am coming,” Lucky says. “I like to draw with you,” Lucky says. “I like to play dolls with you,” Yangjee says. “I love crackers. You like momos, * ” Lucky says. “I like to play chungi, * ” Yangjee says. ”You like to jump rope.” *Momos are dumplings common to Nepal, Tibet, and nearby countries *Chungi is a game similar to Hacky Sack played with a ball of rubber bands. It is played in Nepal and Northeastern India. “We like different things,” Lucky says. ”But we are still best friends, ” Yangjee says. From a distance they hear Yangjee’s mom yell, ”Come and have your food,” in the Tamang language. From a distance they hear Lucky’s mom yell, ”Come and have your food,” in the Nepal Bhasa language. “Let us go eat,” Yangjee says.
author: Yangjee  Thokar

title: Importance of Family
text: In a family of four member:- Father, mother, sister and brother. In a wood of small Hut. They live in. They daily went to the city for the children. Kids go to the school and parents went to their shop. They sell the cloth. One day a customer went to the shop said give me a paint. The Lady sell the pain and them remember oh no today is last date of fee submission. How acn i forget that. The school fee was 500 rupees. But his mom said that I ache only 200 rupees. In school teacher punished the kid because of fee were not submitted. The girl said the they belongs to a poor family. After one day in night time girl thought that he would earn some money that he stole hundred rupee and she went out to the bazaar and bought some items for sell. Then she moved to crowded area and sell the items but he faced a lot of problem and did not earn a single rupee. After late night she returned home and saw her whole family waited for her. Next day they gave her 500 hundred rupees to submit the fee. Moral:- Without family we don't have anything
author: KV BSF

title: THE PLASPIENS
text: Saraswati Public School was a prestigious school in the city of Harinagar. A boy named Sanidhya of class five studied in that school. He was all rounder and scored 99.9% in his exams. He had a brilliant, detective mind and was a key to lock. He had a glowing face and eyes like One day, Sanidhya and classmates were noting down some maths formulas. Suddenly, Sanidhya and his friend Jagdish heard some strange, terrifying, awkward noises Sah.....sah.....haa.......haaa........oooo. The maths period was over and the teacher left the twinkling stars. His navy blue shirt and white pants completed his smart look. While boarding on the bus, Sanidhya and Jagdish spotted some strange, square footprints. They became very scared and frightened. They could not speak a word. The bus was about to leave and they quickly settled in their seats. class. After two periods, it was the departure time and the children left for their homes.The next day, the children entered the school full of curiosity and excitement. There were butterflies flying in their stomach. The student of class fifth and sixth were going for a adventurous picnic, for mountain trekking. In the bus, everyone was joyful except Sanidhya and Jagdish, those strange voices echoed in their mind with flashes of scary footprints. When the bus finally reached the mountain, the children were very excited and they all started their journey. After walking 2-3 kms, Sanidhya and Jagdish heard the same terrifying voice they had heard in the school the previous day. Sanidhya followed the voice, Jagdish tried to stop him but all in vain.Sanidhya was out of sight Jagdish followed him and saw him lying unconscious on the Mrs Vibha cautioned and warned rest of the children and asked everybody to follow her in a queue. ground where those footprints were seen. He immediately headed towards Mrs Vibha, the team head and told her everything. The whole group became scared.. They spotted Sanidhya,as soon they reached there,they all became unconscious when they footed on those footprints. They did not knew but could feel hanging in space and were definitely not on Earth. Maybe some other unknown planet. Who knows? After sometime, they all woke up from their unconscious state of mind...................... But where were they? Suddenly, a net came and they all were trapped in it. There was a rush and a big hush. But Sanidhya inquisitive mind started working. He got an idea. He took out a knife he had kept for cutting apples in the picnic. He cut the net with it. Hooray! They were freed. They moved further. They moved and moved with an unknown fear and did not knew where they were heading and suddenly came across a dark cave. They went inside it.They held each others hand. Their shoes made the loudest clip - clop sound ever. They became frightened. Suddenly, they came in front of a majestic golden gate. He and his group decided "Please dont be scared. My name is Avenue and I am king of Aliens. We are Plaspiens as you are Humans. You all are our guests "Sanidhya conveyed the message to the whole group. We know you have arrived" made them stopped. The golden gate opened. The humans were standing against the aliens.The aliens pressed a button and only Sanidhya could understand their voice. title: Gratitude
text: Ava Anderson was an 11-year-old girl with long, blonde hair and beautiful blue eyes. She lived with her little brother Ron, and her mother. Her father was in the military. Ava didn’t bond well with her father because he was not at home most of the year. He would get a month's holiday in which he came home, but instead of doing fun activities, he made the kids exercise. He also took charge of training the neighbourhood kids too. Ava would feel embarrassed of her father and one day, she shouted at him, “Papa! Stop making us exercise all the time. Do you know my friends enjoy with their fathers but you just make us do exercises.” Ava’s father didn’t like her tone and scolded her, “Ava is that how you talk to your father?!” A long lecture on moral behaviour made Ava furious and she slammed the door of her bedroom to register her anger. She cried the whole night questioning God. *SPLASH* Ava’s father poured a bucket full of water to wake her up next morning. She disliked it and checked the time, “It’s 7 AM, no training?” Shed questioned sarcastically. “Others enjoy and you only train and make us exercise,” Ava’s father mimicked her and laughed. “URGH!” Ava groaned and started getting ready for her school. Ava’s bus honked and she left bidding bye to her mother. *DING DING* The school bell rang for zero period and all the students gathered in the activity room. “Wow Anya, from where did you get this shiny roller glue?” Ava asked admiring the fancy glue. “My father brought this for me from Florida.” Anya bragged showing off the glue. Everyone’s favourite teacher Ms Stewart greeted her students, “Good morning class! I have a fun activity planned for you all. In this activity, we will thank any one person from the class and state the reason why we are thanking them.” The class understood the activity and Ms Stewart invited Anya to start. Anya was a girl who was a little snobbish but everyone wanted to be in her circle. Ava was surprised when Anya said, “Miss, I would like to thank Ava. She sacrifices her happiness and special moments with her father so that we can share our special moments with our family. We can go to the park, vacations and attend parties, without any fear because her father is protecting us risking his life, fighting at the border. Standing in cold, heat, rain and storm without any complaints.” Every student in the class had a similar response except Ava. “I would like to thank the entire class because they made me realise the value of my father. I have always been angry with him for not being there with us. Also, with the limited time he comes home, he makes us exercise to help us become strong and tough. I never appreciated him, but now my vision towards him has completely changed because of you all. So, I thank you all from the bottom of my heart.” Ava’s school friends asked her if they could also join the exercise and training sessions with her. She realised how fortunate she was to have a father who was, loved by all. That day, when Ava reached home she gave her father a tight hug and explained to him the reason for her behaviour. She apologised for the same and promised him that she would try her best to make him proud. “I love you, dad,” Ava said before sleeping in the safest cradle, her father’s arms.

title: RIYA AND HER DOG
text: . Once a girl, whose name was Riya lived with her family in Delhi. One day, she was playing in the park and saw her friend taking her dog for a walk. She ran to her friend and said, Hi, how lucky you are that you have such a cute dog, I wish I should also have a cute pet. Just then her friend replied, “why don’t you ask for a pet from your parents as your birthday gift, Riya said, “Oh yes”!. Then she went for playing with her friends after playing she went to her house. She asked her parents “Mom, Dad please gift me a cute and loving pets and my birthday is coming soon?” Riya’s father and mother said, “It is not an easy work to take care of a pet you have to take him for walk, give him food, giving him a bath and many more regularly”. She replied, “I promise, I will take a good care of the pet and be responsible of doing all the work”. Riya's father said, “Ok I will think about it”. Riya in a dull voice said, “Ok, I will wait for it”. Every day she asked her parents about the pet again. Finally, it was her birthday. She was very happy as well as excited too. She went to her father and mother and asked about her gift. They told her that “It’s a surprise you, will get it at the end of the day” “I will wait” said Riya”. She invited all her friends to her birthday party. She played music chair with her friends and many more. She had a lot of fun with her friends and they also give her many presents. But, she was waiting for her mother’s and father’s gift. Finally, it was her birthday. She was very happy as well as excited too. She went to her father and mother and asked about her gift. They told her that “It’s a surprise you, will get it at the end of the day” “I will wait” said Riya”. She invited all her friends to her birthday party. She played music chair with her friends and many more. She had a lot of fun with her friends and they also give her many presents. But, she was waiting for her mother’s and father’s gift. The party over, then her father and mother gave her the gift, as she opened the gift it was a dog! She was so happy that she doesn’t have words to explain and she named her as Johnny. Just then her father said, “Now you have a pet. I hope you take a good care of him”. She replied, “ Yes, I will always take care and play with him every day”. Next morning, she took all the care of the dog by taking him for a walk, playing with him, giving him food on time and many more. After some days, she doesn’t take care of the dog. She never gave him time. She always says that “I will take you for a walk in the park tomorrow” every day but she never did that. Riya’s parents were very disappointed with her. They thought to teach her. And said her, “Diwali is coming soon so we will go for shopping tomorrow”. Ok I will also go with you Mom and Dad for shopping” Riya said. The next day, Riya’s father came very late from the office so he told her, "We will go for shopping tomorrow”. Every day Riya’s father told her again and again. It was now one week, and he was only repeating it again and again and Riya was getting so annoyed. Then in very angry she went to her father and said “Dad you are always telling me the same thing again and again why are you doing this?” I can’t understand, please tell me why? What is the reason?” That time, many questions came in her mind. Her father in an angry voice said, “First you think what you doing?” “What am I doing?” she said. He replied. “Because you are not taking care of Johnny who is your pet and you promised me that you will take care of your pet. How are you feeling? She said, “Very annoying and sad”. He said, “Now, how you are feeling, the same Johnny would also be feeling like this, you, shouldn’t break your promise so I thought to teach you a lesson. Hope now your will be more responsible “Riya felt very sad”. From next day, she started to take care of her dog sincerely by taking him for walk playing with him and giving him food on time. After learning a lesson, she also became very responsible. Then she never repeated that mistake.

title: THE CUNNING MAN
text: One night a duck had a most extraordinary dream. The Queen of the ducks appeared and told him that he must leave his home and travel towards the orient, for hundred days and hundred nights. There was an oasis in the Garden of Eden where every species of the animal world lived happily and free. Flower, fruits, delicious food and pure water springs were at their disposal. Fortunately for them, ‘man’ had not yet arrived on the scene to disturb their peace and tranquility. After traveling for hundred days and nights the duck was very tired. He stopped to rest on a rock which was jutting out of the water. To his surprise he heard the Queen’s voice. She scolded and said the he had made a big mistake. Instead of traveling towards the East, as he had done, he should have traveled towards the West. However, now that he was here, he must stay and face a terrible creature: MAN. The Queen told the duck how man was very cruel to all the others animals. He made them his slaves and sometimes even killed them. Naturally the duck was very frightened and he began to search for a place to hide from the strange creature called MAN. He walked and walked and eventually he came to a cave where a young lion cub was lying in the sun shine. The duck was so pleased to see another living creature that he did not hesitate in approaching the lion. The two animals soon became friends. The duck told lion about his long journey and how he had made a mistake by travel direction. In turn, the lion explained that he was alone in the world. He thought his parents had been captured by man and was determined to avenge this deed. He had decided the only way to do this was to fight man. The duck also wanted to live in peace so he promised to help the lion to unite all the animals of the forest in order to fight against man. Having agreed on their plan, the two friends decided to go to sleep, and they would begin their fight for survival against man the next day. When morning came, the two friends did, indeed, begin their task. It was not easy for the little duck to keep in step with the lion who was so much bigger. After a while a four legged animal in front of them. He said that he was a donkey and was running away from the man. This creature called man wanted to make him his slave and the donkey knew he would have to work very hard and would probably be given very little to eat in return. He also knew that he would be treated cruelly in other ways. The lion told the donkey that he was organizing an army against man, made up of all the animals of the forest. The donkey was very interested and asked if he could join. The lion was very pleased to have the donkey in his army and gave him the rank of corporal. The three animals continued on into the forest and soon they met another four legged creature who called himself a horse. He also was running away from man and was very glad to meet with the three friends. The horse told how man had the habit of jumping on his back and making him gallop very fast. At other times, man would make him pull a heavy cart and if he dared to stop, he was beaten with a stick. The other three animals were horrified at this and told the horse about the army they were forming. He willingly agreed to join them. The lion continued to march followed by the other three member of the army. Eventually the came upon yet another four legged animal but this one had to humps on his back. He said, he was a camel and that he was trying to avoid a strange creature called man. After a while the came to a clearing the forest. There they saw a strange up right creature carrying some wooden boards. They had never seen anything like him before. He was not covered in feathers and fur like themselves but wore strange colored objects. Of course, these were man’s clothes but the animals did not know this. The duck thought that this was perhaps man, but as none of them were sure, they decided to be very careful. The camel related how frightened he was of man, who wanted to make him his slave. The lion asked just how strong man was and the camel replied that the lion was certainly stronger than man, but the problem was not of strength. The fact remained that man was so cunning and he always managed to win because of this. This made the lion more determined than ever to overcome man and so he asked the camel if he would join their army. The camel agreed and so, joined the other animals who intended to help the lion in battle against man. So the small army, with lion in front set out once again in their search for man. The lion decided to confront this strange creature but the donkey and the rest of the animals were afraid. In fact, it was man, a carpenter, who after seeing the lion decided to capture him. In order to do this, man had to use his cunningness. He told the lion that he was ill and wondered whether the lion could help him get well. The lion was naturally very flattered to be asked for his assistance. He decided that this creature had realized how intelligent the lion was, so he agreed to help. The carpenter explained how unhappy he was because man made him work day and night. On hearing this, the lion was more determined than ever to find man and kill him. The carpenter was secretly very pleased, as this had been his plan all along. He thought himself very clever. He had not said who he was, the lion still did not know that he was actually man. He had convinced the lion to have a hiding place build by pretending that he also was afraid. The carpenter was keen to begin building the box and it would soon be obvious why he was so anxious that it should be the strongest box he had ever made. So the carpenter began to work. He invited the lion to inspect the box. It must be large enough and have plenty of air holes. The lion got inside the box and tried to make himself comfortable. It was tight squeeze. The carpenter’s plan had worked. As soon as the lion was inside the box he fastened the lid down with some nails that were so large that not even a lion would be able to open it. The lion, who had not understood what was happening, asked to be let out. The carpenter said he was sorry but he had no intention of releasing an animal who wanted to kill man himself. He had proved that man was so much stronger than himself. It had only taken the use of a very simple trap. This left the lion with no choice but to call for his army. They were extremely sad that their friend had been trapped in such a way. The lion told them that he had been very foolish to think that he could outwit man and he had decided to abandon his plan to avenge his parents. They had no alternative but to disband their army. They all agreed to go their separate ways. The donkey would return to pulling carts, the horse would return to galloping with his master, the camel would return to the desert and wait for a caravan with which he could work and lastly the duck would return from where he had come. At least he believed that he would be free of man there.

title: Beautiful Scars
text: I woke up and my attention went towards the big three pang stitches on my right leg. It's been twenty-five years since I got them. The fact that they still blemish my heart intensely.... * Flashbacks and white and grey film… that night, I had a delicious Biryani and filled up my tummy while watching a famous stunt movie with my family. Everything was going great. The clock was about to strike midnight. My sister was busy cleaning the dishes as I was going by the kitchen. I had a mosquito attacking racket in my hand and a mosquito ahead of me upon whom I was trying to attack. As it flew higher, I jumped higher. Without realizing the water on the tiles, I stepped onto it and………. I slipped. The racket jumped out of my hand and fell on the floor tile. I shouted the loudest because of the arising pain. Dad came running. He and Mom picked me up and put me onto the bed near the kitchen. I was not able to feel my leg. Dad ordered my sister to run upstairs and call my paternal Uncle. They both came running; Grandmother as well came running. As soon as she arrived, she just got some holy ointment out of nowhere and started applying it to my maimed leg. I was only 7 years old at that time and didn’t know how to endure such major pain. Also, it was the first time in my family someone had injured their bone that hard. No one knew what to do in such a situation. Except my Uncle, who was once also a medical practitioner. He got a medical bandage and wrapped it around my femur. I still remember how I kept crying out so tumultuously. I felt helpless since I couldn't do anything for myself to reduce the level of pain. The next day, I was taken to the hospital. The x-ray was taken and the results were quite scary and startling for me. No one actually told me the report. I just found it out from my family member's reaction. I felt so depressing when finally, I got to to know that I will have to go through a surgery. A few weeks later, I was hospitalized. I can still feel the sore and throbbing pain after the surgery. It still gives me chills. I also remember a few incidents that happened during the era, in which I was impaired. One night, I was sleeping calmly. The AC was turned on and I was wearing a half-sleeved shirt. As my arms weren’t covered under the quilt, I guess maybe the cold air attacked my upper limbs. At the dawn, my thirst rose and I got up to take a sip of water. My arms were not moving. As a kid, I humorously thought they had froze. I didn't want to wake anyone up. So, I decided to deal with this case by myself. I put some power in one of my arms to lift it and used it to crack up the knuckles of the other hand. At that moment, the pain that struck me was hurting so, so hard. I couraged up and cracked the knuckle of the other hand. My arms sored up with the amount of energy it gained in a second. Now, if I look back, I find this incident very comical After a few months of my surgery, I was able to bend my knee and perch on a wheelchair. I used to go everywhere sitting on a wheelchair, for at least a month. During that month, my respect and empathy rose for the people who couldn’t walk, like me. Before this incident, I had always thought that using a wheelchair was fun as you don’t have to use your feet and you can be as lazy as a sleeping cat. One day, Uncle and Dad took the us out for lunch. Of course, I went but in the very familiarly dear wheelchair. It was a genuine and necessary thing to let me order for my family because I knew everyone’s best-loved meal. Like always, I went to order and while doing so, I don’t know why I thought that I was breaking a norm or two. My family, letting me order made me feel that my regards towards a handicapped female would always stand up. As I woke up and my attention went towards the big three pang stitches on my right leg. It's been twenty-five years since I got them. The fact that they still blemish my heart intensely. That day was the D-day for my plastic surgery. That day would be the last day I would have looked at my scars. I have always disliked them from the moment the scalpel touched my skin to create them. But still, I didn’t envy them. I ate my breakfast and headed out for the hospital. I was proceeding through the subway. I was reviewing my whole life ever since I slipped and fell down till that very moment. The scars were something that were meant to be. After a month of my second surgery. My physiotherapy began and in two days, I was able to walk again. Gradually, I started to walk around normally like the way I did before the fracture occurred. I was able to jump, dance, run, play again. But they say “some minor changes never leave”. And even in my case, they didn’t. They left me some scars. At first, I felt quite uncomfortable and insecure whenever I wore clothes through which my scars were visible. Anything that revealed my knee, where the scars were visible was something, I never wore. But then one day, I heard this song, it might be a normal song for other people but for me it was nerve-racking. It made me feel shameful about how I was close-minded for these scars. They weren’t marks of my painful journey but marks that were meant to be flaunted not to be hidden. It might not be a crime to have them hidden but a foolishness, for sure. Only because I was scared about what people would think? Only because I was not ready for it even after 25 years? Only because I was not ready to accept them? Only because they made me think that I could not be perfect in this stereotypical world? Only because I thought people would criticize me? Only because I thought they would be called a mistake for me? But was this all really necessary for me to think? Couldn’t I be more confident? You know what they say to people who slay hard? “He/she ate and left no crumbs” Till then, my station had arrived, the subway doors had opened and made way for people to pass. I had two choices; either to go and get my scars erased forever or just not go. I thought about both my options and realized that going might make me live with a bit of peace but with a bit of regret. I would regret not using these marks to be confident and courageous. On the other hand, if I had not gone, I would get another chance to be more sanguine and assured. Would this choice make me a sophisticated, worldly and a cosmopolitan woman? Should I had gone out and finished this spiel and followed the dream I had always seen since the last twenty-five years or just accept this and live confidently about the gospel that I had just realized?

title: The floods that ravaged Tirupati
text: It was going to be a joyous day for Anya and Abhay, they were visiting the holy temple of Tirupati. They hop up in the car- Anya started playing with the doll that baba had given her. Its been an hour baba; how much longer is it going to take? ‘half an hour’ he uttered in his mind; but actually said “another 15 mins”. There was a squeal of excitement as soon as the car stopped in front of a glamorously large temple. The reached the entrance which looked like a mere serpent hood. They reach the already long and crowded Vaikuntham queue complex. ‘baba why do we have to stand here’, it is the entrance to the temple my dear. She sighed. They climbed the 3550 steps to reach the Venkateshwara temple on top. before the darshan of the temple they visited the govindraj temple, where the sacred idol of the god is in a sleeping position. baba, the idol is so big; Anya exclaimed. yes it is, it is also considered as one of the most powerful idol and the lord himself transformed to stone. All of them bow before the idol and leave, as darkness was falling upon. Just as they climbed down the steps, an enormous downpour of rain attacked them, a huge amount of bhaktas and pilgrims were stranded there. It was an unprecedent amount of rain, unlike anything anyone had ever seen. “Anya, Abhay hold my hand” he yelled. ‘baba, maa’ whimpered Abhay. ‘stay close’ maa said. ‘lets get out of here’ yelled Anya. Baba stood shocked, it had never rained so heavily in Tirupati before, his mind had completely gone blank. The rain poured down so heavily that in fractions of seconds a massive flood evoked. The pilgrims struggled to stand motionless on the ground. The water swept away people as if they were mere matchsticks. ‘grab my hand, lets move to higher ground’ yelled baba. They climb upon the railings of the Vaikuntham queue complex. ‘ hold tightly, don’t let go’ cried out maa. Anya and Abhay were very panic-stricken, none of them had imagined such a baffling event to be happening. There was a lot of hue and cry. All the pilgrims held onto the railing on the queue and waited until the water had decelerated. The rain was pouring down heavily even after an hour, water inundated whole of the temple- the idol of the god submerged underwater. Darshan of the god was stalled because of the inundation. The four ‘maada streets’ conjoining the temple on the Tirumala hills remained heavily flooded; the two ghat roads leading to the Tirumala hills were closed down because of the unprecedent flood. Even after hours of waiting on the railing, there was no sign of the water decelerating, none of the pilgrims wanted to undertake the venturing decision to get down and go across the water to find shelter and food. Anya and Abhay cried out in hunger, baba and maa felt helpless, baba had the urge to jump down and go get help but the image of maa and the kids horrified without him, held him back. ‘just some more time kids, I am sure some authorities will come and rescue us’ maa said. Abhay sobbed ‘what if they don’t?’, ‘ they will don’t worry, a huge number of pilgrims have been stranded here, it is impossible for anyone to not notice it’. ‘baba, how long are we going to stand here’ ask Anya. Baba uttered in a helpless state, ‘ just until the water level goes down’. It had been 14 hours since they were stranded there, no sign of help- no human contact nearby. All the pilgrims started chanting the name of lord Venkateshwara, A man whimpered, ‘ please help us lord, send some help’, another women cried out ‘ O Venkateshwara please get us out of here’. A whole day had passed by with the pilgrims standing while holding the railing of the queue complex, no food- no water- no shelter. Their feet was ice cold and the kids shivered as the rain poured down on them. ‘ I don’t think we’ll survive for any longer than 2 more hours like this’ whispered baba to maa in a weak tone, we need to get food for the kids or they’ll collapse. Maa sighed in a helpless tone, it is full of peril- we saw how the water swept out people- it is not safe baba- we cannot leave the kids alone in a situation like this. We must wait for someone to come and help us. Baba sighed, he could no longer see the sad faces of his kids, they looked pale and weak without any food and water. All pilgrims rested their heads on the railing, hoping someone would soon reach there to help them. It was around 6 ‘o’ clock, there was a commotion, baba woke up and his eyes brightened to the sight- around 12 people had come to rescue them. There was a lot of push and pull- all the people were trying to hold the rope and get across the area safely. ‘hold the rope tightly, me and maa are just behind your’ said baba, don’t let go no matter what happens. ‘ it might feel like the water is pushing you, but keep walking forward’ said maa. Anya and Abhay nodded. All the people yelled as the force of water was too much to take, a few pilgrims even lost their lives while crossing. A sigh of relief escaped the lips of maa, as the four of them crossed the water safely. The first thing baba did was hurry all of them into the area where the Devasthanam officials had made arrangements for free food. All of them stuffed their mouths with various dishes, a tear escaped maa’s eyes- food never felt so delicious before. After the food- they all thanked lord Venkateshwara for saving their lives, it was indeed his grace who saved the lives of those thousand people who encountered the unprecedent flood.

title: Grace and the Time machine
text: Once upon a time there was a 13 year old girl named Grace. She lived with her mom Eliana. Unfortunately, she lost her father at a very young age. Her mother was a renowned scientist. Grace loved inventions. Her latest invention was a Time machine and she wanted to be the youngest girl to make it.Many scientists were stumped with the complications to make a Time machine but it was really simple for Grace. She used to come home from school and devote most of her time towards this invention. She had made a handful of buttons on her machine which could take her to unknown places - like the land of unicorns, snow dragons, mermaids etc She believed in supernatural creatures and had always been fascinated about it. When she was done making her machine, she went to the land of snow dragons with her friend Hazel without telling her mom. When they reached the snow- dragino kingdom both of them were astonished by the beauty of the place. It was a magnificent and cold place because the snow dragons can not survive in warm climates. It was snowing there. Grace and Hazel were prepared for the climate, they quickly put on their winter clothes. The snow dragons warmly welcomed them and the guards informed the King and Queen that they were foreigners and they came to greet them. They invited Grace and Hazel to the Palace and the king accompanied them. It was dusk and the two girls were very tired and so they had a royal dinner and went to sleep. The next day they woke up to the sound of a violin. King Albert wanted to give Grace and Hazel the tour of the land so they set forth after their breakfast. However, that proved to be a wrong decision because the King of the Fire-Dragino kingdom - King Alex had invaded snow- dragino kingdom in King Albert’s absence. And apparently, King Albert and King Alex were twins. When King Albert got this message, he rushed back to his kingdom. He was devastated at the sight of his kingdom -it was so hot due to the presence of King Alex. First it was warm then it was hot like summer and later it was so hot that the castle caught fire. King Albert confronted King Alex and they made a deal, they would have a war between each other and they could only have two of their subjects from each of their kingdoms in the war. They all prepared for the war commencing the very next day. King Alex chose his most reliable and powerful two subjects while King Albert opted for Grace and Hazel. All were astonished by the decision of King Albert. King Albert chose them for a reason, dragons don’t have hands like humans. His plan was to make snowballs and throw them at King Alex and his men because just like Snow dragons can’t survive without cold weather, Fire dragons cannot survive without hot weather. They stored the snow balls in a Mega Giant fridge because of the weather. Grace and Hazel were delighted to help. The whole day King Albert and his team were busy making snowballs for the war. The Goodies-King Albert’s team and The Baddies- King Alex’s team were ready for war. King Albert went by his plan and defeated his twin brother. His twin fled from his brother's land. The two besties after the war were standing alone with lots of happiness and pride. They were also famished. As soon as King Alex left the land which was burnt came back to life. It was such a beautiful sight. King Albert thanked Grace and Hazel for their help. The two besties wanted to stay there for a longer period of time but couldn't because their parents would be worried that they were missing. The girls bid farewell to King Albert and returned home. When they went back, their mothers hugged them tight. Grace presented the time machine in front of the Mayor in a crowded hall of eminent scientists. The Mayor and his team were impressed and gave their approval to her Time Machine and Grace became the youngest scientist and her dream came true.

title: Path To Plorvis
text: Though he could see people comforting his weeping parents, he knew that they were all just hollow consolations and that no one was as sad as him to see a son, a friend and an older brother die right in front of them. Seven year old Jacob stood there. rooted to the spot; not able to move, watching helplessly as the firemen extinguished the flames wrapped around the building... It's been seven years since the tragedy. Everything had rested back in place. Another windy day indicating the soon arrival of winters. the clear water puddles that lay undisturbed on the road were soon disturbed by to fourteen year olds. "Kyra, let's go back... I'm cold", said the boy. "Shut up, Jacob. We've come this far and we are not going back without winning this game", spoke the girl. "It's just a foolish game of hide and seek. besides, we are too old for this anyway- Hey wait why are you running!" Kyra ran up the hill with Jacob hurrying along in her wake. They soon reached the place they were going to. An old broken mass of what once was a pretty wooden house. "This place was Trevor's favorite", Jacob said in a hushed voice, his mouth suddenly gone parched. "oh yeah. I'm sorry, I forgot. Let's go back" "No it is ok. Mum says i have to move on" They went inside through the door which was off its hinges. A terrible stench filled their nostrils. "EW!", Kyra exclaimed as she pinched her nose like Jacob." why did your brother like this place so much?" " I don't know" They moved in further in the long deserted corridor until they came at a halt in front of a door from which light was coming out of. Hands trembling; Jacob opened the door. A blinding white light flooded the whole corridor. When the light disappeared mysteriously, They opened their eyes and walked inside the room which was empty except for an old mirror which stood at a corner. "A mirror?", Kyra asked, bewildered. She walked toward it and so did Jacob. He looked in the mirror. He was looking at a tall, handsome blond boy who since birth, mysteriously have beautiful lilac eyes. Standing next to him was a comparatively shorter girl with burning red hair and and amber eyes. Jacob had strongly hated looking in a mirror ever since Trevor's death, because according to everyone e looks just like him, which reminds him of his brother. He drew a deep breath and steadied himself. Suddenly, he caught a glimpse of something moving inside the mirror. It was not his own reflection. He looked more carefully. He could swear that he saw a girl with hair black as ebony and eyes green as grass smiling at him. He gasped. "Did you see that too?" "Yes", Kyra replied as shocked as him. "Yes I did" "What was it?" 'No clue" The same girl reappeared in the mirror. This time she didn't just stay there for a fleeting second. "Congratulations on finding the Path To Plorvis", She spoke in an angelic voice." Follow me", she turned and disappeared. "Follow her into a mirror?", Kyra asked. Jacob extended his has, the moment it touched the mirror, everything swirled and dissolved. He opened his eyes. The same girl was smiling sweetly at him, just inches away from his face. He gasped and backed away. "Who are you?" "I am Eileen. Welcome to Plorvis, Jacob Hayson and Kyra Mills" Jacob turned to see Kyra standing next to him. "Where are we?", she asked. "You are in Plorvis. The land of magic and the majestic", the moment she said this, the mist around them cleared, revealing a dark place. Around them, everywhere the houses and buildings were broken. The sky had a scarlet moon. The so called road they were standing on had dent and cracks. "this place isn't magical or majestic at all", Kyra muttered. "I know." Eileen sighed. " This is not the real Plorvis. Darkness has taken over it. But you, Jacob, will fix it" "What?- me? - how?" "You see, long ago this place was a dream land of anybody, but then a prophecy was made. It said that 'soon darkness will take over the magic of Plorvis, leaving nothing but sadness and dismay in its people's hearts. But the only person who will posses the ability to conquer it will be a boy born on the last date of February and his eyes will be lilac in color'. It was supposed to be your Brother, Trevor, since you both have the same eyes and he was born on the 28th of February. But unfortunately he died, passing his role to you" "But my birthday is on the 29th of February" " That is a confusion. We d not know whether the prophecy mean the 28th or 29th. But everybody thought it would be Trevor. But now it is you. Please Jacob, the fate of Plorvis depend upon you", two tears trickled down her face. "What do I have to do?" "Find the Lethal Blade and stat it at Darkness's heart" "Lethal Blade? what is that?", Kyra asked. "The only weapon that can destroy darkness. You have to crack a riddle which only you can hear, to find the Lethal Blade" "Let's do it then!", He said. They both followed Eileen to a huge black door which stood at the middle of the road. He knocked on it and the door sang: ' I'll laugh if I make you cry. But if someone else did so, they'll die. Don't worry, I'll never compliment you, instead I'd love to shove your face down a cake. I'll never say this but it was a euphoric feeling on your birth and I love you more than anyone on Earth.' Jacob pondered for a while. He thought what would Trevor do in this situation. Thinking about Trevor was painful. He remembered the times they had together. How ruthlessly his older brother pranked him, but on the same hand, how much he loved him- That's it! He knew the answer! "SIBLING!" he yelled on the top of his voice. The door swung open at once. Inside was an enormous room, the only source of light there was from a huge silver blade that was kept in front of a huge dark circle, which must be darkness's heart. If it was the heart then the blade must be- " The Lethal Bade", Eileen said. " You deserve to do it, Kyra. We would have never found the mirror if it wasn't for you", Jacob said. Kyra walked towards the blade and SLASH! It's been Seventeen years. Kyra and Jacob's children still thinks that this is a made up story by their parents. But only they and Eileen knows the truth, and who knows? Maybe somewhere Jacob's older brother, Trevor is also swelling with pride that his brother saved a kingdom... ~ AASHI BHARDWAJ

title: THE JEWELED BOX
text: Icy fingers gripped my arm in the darkness the moment I touched that anonymous jeweled box. I had never seen it in my room in my entire lifetime. Surprisingly, neither was it my birthday nor did I achieve anything to have been gifted a present like this. Initially, I decided not to heed much attention to a thing like that which didn't deserve much time of mine but the curiosity aroused more catalytically the more I tried to ignore its existence and ultimately I ended up trying to open that charismatic box thinking that I end up getting some treasure. I was dragged right inside the box and I screamed in horror. But after a few seconds, I eventually realized that I was still in my own room, on the same bed and at the same time. Then, where did the fingers come from? Was it an illusion? Or was I getting way stressed due to my upcoming half-yearly exams and it was all a result of that only? I was half convinced that it was nothing more than a mere imagination when I ended up seeing my headboard. My eyes started broadening in terror, my heart palpitating in panic and my legs began shivering like a vibrating phone. It seemed like my bed's headboard had undergone an exchange program with an ancient one. I started surfing my eyes throughout the room and the more I saw, the broader it got. May it be the furniture or the sudden appearance of red embroidered carpets and curtains, everything from A to Z had been changed. It felt like I had moved to the Dwapar Yuga or even further back than that, when all of a sudden my eyes landed on a portrait of a lady in red saree and ornaments but with a face exactly matching mine. I was intensely shocked to look at myself in attire like that. I got up from my bed and went near the painting to read the name of the lady written as "Draupadi". All of a sudden five men entered the room of around eight to nine feet height at least, highly ornamented and naked chests. They looked at me in utter astonishment (might be because of the night suit I was in) and said something in a language I could barely decode. I screamed in horror to see the chaos all around. When all of a sudden the same woman of the portrait entered the room and all her five husbands stared at me in stupefaction and took out their swords to regard me as nothing else than a result of witchcraft or black magic. I yelled in distress when I accidentally fell upon the same box and all of a sudden my eyes opened up and I woke up from the bed sweating and realizing that it all had been nothing but a mere nightmare. i turned left to grab a glass of water when the glass slipped out of my hand and it started shivering again. I saw the same jeweled box kept aside the jug! Moral: Don't be greedy. Be content with what you have and don't wish for what you do not own because all that glitters is not gold.

title: The Quest
text: Sam looked over the sky, as the once orange ether turned into a deep shade of red and watched the sun go down. She stood before the street that was once aglow with bright lights, but now, all that was left was the destruction caused by the earthquake that struck the city a few days ago. The freshly left scars in people's hearts affected them greatly, the people who lost their homes, lost their families but it pivotally affected Sam, for she grew up in the city itself. In her entire 15 years of life, she had never come across something as disturbing as what she saw that day. To stab a knife in the wound, she had also been separated from her family. She had nowhere to go, nothing to do but sit near a murky pond and wait for help to arrive. That very day, after a few minutes of pondering about, she finally gathered up the courage to recuperate her family. A sense of yearning and hope rushed into Sam as she got up and looked overhead at the sky and decided to plan out her way as pleasant memories with her family came rushing in her mind. A child's first thought is to always go to someone they know, someone they trust whenever trouble arises. Likewise, Sam's first instinct was to approach the one person she knew she could always trust, Monika. Monika was a girl in her late 20s, with a striking appearance and lush brown hair and almond eyes. She had known Sam ever since she was a newborn, thus she could easily pass as family. The only problem being that Monika lived in the suburbs of Mumbai, which was a long way from where Sam lived. Nonetheless, Sam was determined to find her family. The house she used to stay in was just a pile of bricks, but the walls that enclosed the people she loved, her family, was what she called a home. That was the very reason she had to find out where her family was. After what seemed like years, she finally reached the doorstep of Monica's house. She broke into a sweat and her heart started pounding as she knocked on her door. Monika opened the door with a creak and was set back on her heels as she looked at the sloppy figure of Sam. She had so many questions, so many things to talk about. They talked for a good hour and Monika told Sam how perturbed she was about their family after the news of the earthquake and agreed to help find her parents in a jiffy. They couldn't figure out where to start looking but knew the first place earthquake survivors always go to were shelters. As they entered the first shelter, they saw the grieving faces of the survivors and their families. With slow and heavy breaths, they looked around in search of Sam's parents but couldn't find a familiar face in a crowd of unfamiliar figures. They looked around in a couple more shelters but the little hope they had in them started to fade away. With a heavy heart, Sam came to a conclusion that her parents had reunited with their creator in heaven itself. A month went by, and Sam woke up at Monica's house with a radiant glow on her face for it was her birthday. Though there was no news to confirm that her parents were actually gone, the grief had not left Sam's body. Monica tried her best to cheer her up when they heard a knock at the door. The knocks continued for a couple more seconds as Sam made her way to the door and flung it open. It was almost as if her soul left her body for there they stood, two grown up figures of her parents, a smile on each of their faces. Without any second thoughts, Sam swung her arms around them and burst into tears. After what seemed like an entire minute full of tears and bursts of happiness, Sam's parents started explaining how they had been looking for her ever since the earthquake struck their house. "Happy birthday our little girl" they said as they smiled. Sam couldn't help but smile as a teardrop rolled down her face and the realization finally hit her. She was no longer at a house, she was finally home.

title: The Success of the woman from 8th street
text: The room was filled with negative energy and the atmosphere around was terrible. It all felt just like a nightmare except for the fact that it was a reality. Ada was in distress and a sudden phase of anxiety hit her, she started questioning herself what if it was my last day with him or what if I never get to see him again? Ada Wilson was a food truck owner in New York City and was working with her best friend and the love of her life, her husband Blake Wilson. They had been together for 24 long years and were the most charming couple on 8th street. Apart from their amazing journey in life, they were brilliant co-workers as well, and seeing them cook together was delightful. The coordination between them was enchanting and their skills together were perfect. Even though they were incredibly talented their food truck business wasn’t always on the same page. Its refrigerator kept going out of order every month and the grill was just a disaster. Ada and Blake were both middle-aged and with that comes a few problems too. Ada experienced odd panic attacks while Blake had a slight lung diagnosis resulting in short breathlessness sometimes, but that was until one day while cooking in the food truck he almost ran out of his breath and experienced the usual pain, so he used his inhaler which mostly resolved all of the lung problems he faced, but this time it just wasn’t the same.. Later that day, both Blake and Ada went to the doctor for a casual check-up, but little did they know that they were about to hear the worst news of their lives! “Blake has lung cancer,’ said the doctor. The elderly couple were in complete disbelief and were disheartened by the awful news. The doctor recommended Blake stays back and get admitted to the hospital however Blake had other plans, he wanted to cook & enjoy the last days of his life with his sweetheart – Ada. Ada was disheartened to hear that even though her husband knew he wouldn’t last for long, he still wanted to risk his life just to spend some wholesome time with her. Both of them enjoyed some of their last moments together beautifully. “Blake has lung cancer,’ said the doctor to another surgent at the hospital. The elderly couple were in complete disbelief and were disheartened by the awful news. The doctor recommended Blake stays back and get admitted to the hospital however Blake had other plans. He wanted to cook & enjoy the last days of his life with his sweetheart – Ada. Ada was disheartened to hear that even though her husband knew he wouldn’t last for long, he still wanted to risk his life just to spend some wholesome time with her. She started going through severe anxiety attacks, depression, and even to the point of self-hatred. She stopped showing interest in things and was unhappy with everything. She wanted the earth to open in two halves & sink herself in it. As destiny would plan it, she was at a grocery store, and one of her customers from the past saw her & they decided to have a chat. Ada hadn’t talked to anyone for a while, and this was just the little pep talk she needed. The customer had a 7-year-old daughter, and she was just the sweetest child in the world. The young girl came closer to Ada, and said ‘Hi Mrs. Wilson, why did you shut down your food truck? I have been craving for your mouth-watering hot dogs for too long now as it was the only thing I liked. If you don't mind Mrs. Wilson can you please make me some? " Ada felt even though it was just small talk, Ada realized that there were people still rooting for her & there was more to life then just giving up! She soon re-opened her food truck, and it was as positive as a florist in a flower garden. She soon became the talk of the town (In a great way) and was ready to start this new chapter of her life. Coincidently, Ada got lucky to appear on a TV talk show and that was just the beginning of the overwhelming journey she was about to start. She became so popular that she was on every news channel and people felt really touched & were deeply encouraged by her lovely attitude. She went on like this spreading love & positivity, Four years later she gave a speech which made people love her more than ever! ‘I have gone through some really bad phases in my life which hardly anyone of you would be aware of. I had the best husband who was my best friend, soulmate and perfect co-worker. Unfortunately, he died way too soon due to cancer, leaving me in deep pain. I had gone into depression and felt like giving up on life, however soon I realized that there were people who cared about me, who cherished the food I made and loved me to the moon and back. ‘So today, on this podium I Ada Amber Wilson will be donating 3 million dollars to cancer health organizations.’ Every eye in the arena was filled with tears and they clapped for her valuable contribution. She continued with her philanthropic work toward cancer survivors and lived the best life she could live.
