title: Tia's First Pet
text: “Muma, can we get a pet? Please muma, please?” said Tia to her mother. Tia was a bright and cheerful girl with long red hair and hazel-coloured eyes. She had always wanted a pet and had been begging her parents for one since she was old enough to speak. But her parents always refused, saying that a pet would distract her from her studies, it would not fit in their compact flat in Chennai and that Tia would eventually get bored of it and neglect it. When Tia was 10, her father had gotten promoted to Chief Executive Officer at the firm he worked in, because of which Tia's family had to shift to Delhi. Tia was the only child and so often felt lonely. This was one of the many reasons why she wanted a pet. Tia's new house was no less than a mansion. Something peculiar had been happening in Tia's house since the first day her family moved in. Tia's father complained that all the spare change he kept around the house was somehow disappearing. Soon, Tia also realized that all her shiny pens and jewelled hairclips were missing. When Tia took this matter to her mother, she told Tia that all her gleaming rings were also missing. By this time, Tia and her parents were sure that there was a thief in their house. But who could it be? Tia's parents were perplexed because other than Tia's tutor, Raman, nobody ever came to the house. And whenever Raman visited the house, he was always accompanied by Tia or her mother. Also, Tia's house was always warm from the inside. Even in January, Tia's house felt like the inside of an oven. One Saturday morning, when Tia had no school, her mother went grocery shopping. Meaning Tia would have the house all to herself for at least an hour. Tia took this opportunity to explore her large home. She opened all doors she could find and went through all the rooms in the house. Finally, she came across a room near the garden. The room was much warmer and darker than the others in Tia's home. It had a fresh sweet smell. Tia switched the lights ON and saw a trapdoor towards the right corner of the room. The trapdoor was covered in bizarre markings. At first, Tia was scared to open it up. But eventually, she mustered up her courage to open the hatch door. Tia ran to the store room and grabbed a torch, rope, and her cricket bat. Tia then lifted the hatch gingerly and lowered down her rope. Then, with the torch in her mouth, she slid down the rope. Tia landed with a loud thud and flashed her torch around the dark cave-like room. The room was exceptionally large. While flashing her torch around, Tia saw a glimmering pile of the missing coins, hairclips and rings. And atop the pile sat a majestic dragon the size of a rabbit. Tia’s eyes broadened with amazement. The dragon's scales were as white as pearls while its eyes were a stunning blue. They shined like sapphires in the dark room. It seemed scared and was anxiously flapping its small multi-coloured wings. Tia's heart melted when the dragon tried to breathe fire. It puffed blue-coloured flames at Tia. But the flame was so small that it vaporized as soon as it left the dragon's mouth. By now, Tia was sure that the dragon was harmless and picked it up. The dragon tried to resist and bit Tia's index finger with its small sharp-edged teeth. Tia immediately let the dragon go and pressed her pricked finger hard. A tear ran down her plump pink cheek. The dragon, who was now sitting atop the pile once again, felt sorry. It started flying around Tia and gently perched itself on her shoulder. The dragon then extended its pearl-white tail and wrapped it around Tia's bleeding finger. A bright white light emanated from the dragon's tail and the pain Tia was feeling suddenly went away. Tia was amazed and lovingly rubbed the dragon's chin. The dragon cooed comfortably and rubbed itself against Tia's chest. Its lips erupted into a wide smile. Tia sat down on the warm, hard floor and continued petting the rabbit-sized dragon. "What should I name her?" Tia thought to herself. After thinking for quite some time, Tia finally settled on Pura. A name she chose because of the dragon's pure white scales. "You are going to be my first pet! Oh, I am so excited! I will......................... Suddenly, Tia heard a loud "Ding-dong" echo through the cave-like room. Tia's mother was back! Tia placed Pura on the floor and started climbing the rope. " I cannot wait to show you to my mother" shouted Tia as she was about to open the trapdoor. She quickly got up and ran towards the door. As soon as Tia's mother stepped inside the house, Tia grabbed her hand and asked her mother to come along. Tia took her mother to the room with the trapdoor only to find it empty. The trapdoor had disappeared. It was at that moment Tia realized two things: 1) Her mother was not wearing the same sari she left the house wearing. 2) There was a bewildered expression on her mother's face and tears in her eyes. Tia’s mother then burst into tears and told Tia, between sobs, “You have been missing for 6 years! Where were you?”
author: Akshat Singh

title: The Moon Lake
text: Once upon a time, There lived a family of elephants in a forest. The king of the family "Papa Elephant" was a handsome tusker. He was very kind and very caring to his family. One monsoon there was no rain in there forest. So, the ponds and lakes don't filled up with water. From this problem many animals famished or died. So,Papa elephant get worried about his family and said older elephants to find water in every direction. One elephant found a lake with sparkling water in a neighbouring forest. Hearing this the elephant fastly started moving towards the lake. Near the lake lived a colony of rabbits. While walking on the way to the lake the elephant trampled many rabbits to death and injured. The surviving rabbits said to the king of the rabbits to save the colony of the rabbits from the elephants. The king rabbit said, "Let's we all think us for a solution". One smart rabbit said to the king of the rabbits boldly, " Your majesty, please send me to the king of the elephants as your messenger. I will find a solution". The king of the rabbits replied, " Please go, we all hope that you will find a solution for it". After some time the smart rabbit reached the family of elephants, and jumped on a boulder. And said to the king of the elephants," Hey, Papa elephant, I am the messenger of the rabbits and have brought a message for you". The papa elephant signalled the family of elephants not to say anything, and replied " What the message is about that you have brought for me? ". The messenger of the rabbits said, " Don't get angry about the message which I am going to tell you about, I can only say that I am doing my duty ". King of the elephants replied." Ok, I will not get angry, tell the message." The smart rabbit said," Your majesty, the moon god is really angry with you. because, you have spoiled the holy lake and killed and injured many rabbits who are special to them. They have warned you to not kill any more rabbits and spoil the holy lake". The king of the elephants felt very sad about hearing this. Then he said," We're very sorry for killing many rabbits and disturbing the holy lake. please, can you take me to the moon god, I want to apologize him." The smart rabbit replied " Yes, I can " After some time they reached the holy lake, on which was a reflection of the moon. The king of elephants put his trunk in the lake in the respect of the moon god. And said," We apologize for our mistake and we will never repeat it again." And then the family of elephants go back to there forest. Soon, the heavy rain comes the ponds and the lake of the forest filled up with water and the elephants get happy and also the rabbits lived happily. MORAL:- Physical strength is not enough If we don't have Intelligence.

title: The Punishment
text: Punishment Ramu Kaka was a simple man. He was always ready to serve others. He did not want to hurt anyone. He lived in a village in Champaran. He had been hearing about Gandhiji since his childhood. Ramu Kaka hadn't studied much. But he was motivated by Gandhiji's goat and his service to it. Ramu kaka also developed the hobby of bringing up the goats. It was true that it was very easy to fool Ramu kaka. he trusted everyone easily. In the same village lived a young man named Buddu Singh. `Buddu' means a fool but he was not a fool. He was very cunning. Ramu Kaka was left with only one goat. Buddu Singh wanted to have that goat. First, he made the excuse of being sick and started taking the milk from Ramu Kaka everyday. Then he said to Ramu Kaka, "Please give me the goat as it is difficult to come everyday for the milk." As Ramu Kaka wanted to serve others, he gave the goat to Buddu Singh. But he was not happy doing so. A young man, Chakit Ram, heard about this. He knew about the tricks of Buddu Singh. Chakit Ram asked Buddu Singh to return the goat. But Buddu Singh refused to do so. Chakit Ram thought of a plan. He spread a rumour that Ramu Kaka had a jewel. He needed money. So he wanted to sell the jewel. If someone bought it and gave one hundred one goats to him, he would set up his business and will serve people throughout his life. On hearing this, Buddu Singh went to Ramu Kaka. First, he tried to get the jewel by playing tricks. But every time, his tricks failed because of Chakit Ram. After a lot of efforts, Buddu Singh realized that Ramu Kaka would not agree to give the jewel. So he thought of getting one hundred one goats soon. Otherwise, someone else would get the jewel by giving goats to Ramu Kaka. Immediately, Buddu Singh bought hundred and one goats. When Chakit Ram came to know about this, he called a meeting of village council. Buddu Singh came to the meeting with hundred goats he had bought and one goat he had taken from Ramu Kaka. Now he gave these hundred and one goats to Ramu Kaka and asked for the jewel. The members of the jury realized that Buddu Singh had broken the trust. So they ordered, "Give hundred goats to Ramu Kaka. He will make better use of them. Return one goat to Buddu Singh. He should accept it as the jewel." When Buddu Singh heard this judgement, he felt faint. The council was praised for this judgement. Buddu Singh slowly moved to his home.
author: Veena Bhambhani

title: Siblings' Love
text: It's Sunday morning and Alisha goes to the kitchen to see what's made for breakfast & sees that her dad has brought pizza. She calls her younger sister Ashna and says," Ashna look dad has brought pizza for us." Ashna says," Wow! I love pizza let's eat it fast." "Ashna wait a second, let me divide it between us." Alisha takes three slices of pizza and gives only two slices to Ashna. " Alisha what's this? why did you just give me two slices of pizza? " Alisha says," look Ashna you are small so I gave you two slices and I am older so I have taken three slices." "Alisha! what kind of logic is this?" Both the sisters start quarreling over this matter. Suddenly while quarreling Alisha slaps Ashna and Ashna starts crying. Ashna calls their mom. Their mother scolds them and says, "Both of you stop fighting and give me that pizza, I'll share. you two can never leave in peace, can you? Both the sisters replied, "No! we can't" Both the sisters get angry with each other & go to their room. They don't talk to each other all day. The next day in the afternoon when their mom was sleeping, suddenly she heard Alisha's cry that Ashna return this book to me. She woke and went to them. "Oh God! you guys started fighting again." Then Alisha and Ashna 's father says, "come soon darling, we are getting late." "Wait I'm coming, she replied." Today is my birthday & I have to go to shopping with your dad, so I don't want to spoil my mood. Quietly go to your room & study in peace. One more thing till we both come, you two please don't fight. Alisha and Ashna went to their room. Their parents were late in coming home due to traffic. When they returned home they saw that both Alisha and Ashna were sitting comfortably & watching movie while enjoying noodles. Their mom and dad were surprised. Their mother asked," How did this miracle happen? Yesterday, both of you did not even talk to each other, today you even fought & both of you were angry with each other, so now how are you watching TV happily sitting together?" Both of them were so engrossed in watching the movie that they did not even realize that their mom was asking something to them. Then their dad tells their mom," leave, let them watch the movie happily. Don't disturb them. " " Ok! I'll not disturb them but I really wanted to know how this miracle happened? " "Darling! There was a fight between them, there was no war, after all, both are sisters, no matter how much they fight, their love for each other never ends and in the end everything is fine." " You are absolutely right, the relation of brother and sister is very unique and priceless, both of them have a lot of love but there are some fights too." Alisha and Ashna 's mother says," go to sleep now it's too late and tomorrow you have to go to school too." Alisha and Asana go to their room to sleep. Always remember that there is a fight between siblings, not a war!
author: Jigyasa .

title: To My Kakkan
text: I heard that today, my parents are going to come. I don’t know my mother or my father. I am raised by my uncle, Kakkan. He has always been a pillar of support for me. I will forever be grateful to him throughout my life. But I don’t dare to tell him that or it is going to get to his head. My parents left me and went abroad when I was just born. Since then, Kakkan has raised me. Every crucial moment in my life has been with him. My first word, first step, first prize even my first performance has been with him. But my parents weren’t present. I finished my lunch and sat on the couch to switch on the television. Suddenly, the doorbell rang, I opened the door only to find my parents, standing there, looking expectantly towards me. I motioned them inside as I walked in to sit on my couch. My mother rushed to me and hugged me from behind while my father smiled at me. Then all of a sudden, she asked me whether I wanted to go with her to the States or not because she was feeling very lonely there. I was furious by the sheer audacity of this attitude. And my father was constantly trying to showcase his white elephants so that I could fall prey to them. When they were desperately trying to convince me, I laughed and retorted, “You left me during the most important part of my life when I needed you the most.” In anger, I stormed out and locked myself in my room and sat on the bed. I held my knees and began to wonder. I was hurt, “Why did they abandon me? They have come to me when they have no one but me, but I cannot leave my Kakkan alone, He is my everything.” There was a knock on the door. I opened it and saw Kakkan. I couldn’t stop myself, I began crying. Kakkan hugged me close. “Are they gone?” I asked, “No they are eating lunch.” I went back to my bed wiping my tears. “Kaka, why did they leave me?” I questioned him. “I-I do not know my child, I am very sorry” saying that he walked out of the room, leaving me to wonder what happened all this tim e. Sometimes, When I think about that day, I feel that I had made the right decision. I still wonder if had I chosen to live with my parents, how different everything would have been? But it was the right decision because I chose to be with a person who cherished me and took care of me when I was born, that is you, Kakkan. You always looked after me and loved me. I have realized that no matter what the situation is like, we should trust our instincts and our instincts are always right. It is always better to follow our inner consciousness. It has been 20 years since that incident. I haven’t met my parents since that. I have been lonely by myself all these years. Kakkan, it has been about 5 years since you left me for the heavenly abode. I still cry when I think about you. Today, I sit in front of your graveyard and want to reaffirm, that you have always been with me and you will always be with me. Thanks for all that you have done for me. No one can replace you in my life. Thank you, Kakkan.
author: Shrotreyee Bhattacharya

title: Rivers of light
text: RIVERS OF LIGHT ﻿ ﻿ ﻿“They haven’t appeared this winter even once” frowned Neve the Arctic Fox searching the still, twinkling sky for the ever beloved lights.Yet, the sky remained stubbornly inky. The lights which had once been a big part of her childhood now had disappeared. The sky wasn’t showing a hint of colour nor was it giving away the slightest hint of those lights which used to glide and twist and bend in a celestial dance. “I am sure they ought to appear one of these days. It is quite unusual for them to not show up around this time of the year.” shivered Demi the arctic weasel from under the thick coat of the polar bear cub, Icylyn. The cub too sniffed in sympathy, fixing the sky with a strange look.“ I do hope that they will come around shortly. I ought to be getting back home now.” she whispered quietly, not wanting to wake up the other inhabitants of the night, slumping further into the cold snow with a dejected sigh when silence spread its blanket all around the arctic. The only sound that interrupted this silence was the flapping sound of the wings of the snow owl Lumi, who circled and searched the sky with her eyes fixed at the unmoving sky, looking for even the smallest hint of those lights. “Any news up there?” Neve called out eventually, breaking the silence that had settled over them. Lumi, let out a disappointing hoot before nose diving towards the group of friends and landing on top of a nearby tree branch. “None! Not a soul up there. It is dark for miles all around. '' she muttered, with a disappointed face. Accepting defeat, they all made their way back home. The lights had woven beautiful tapestries in the sky, weaving the night with the stars since the beginning of time - far before any of these four friends were born. The fox, the weasel,the cub and the owl were just like the four seasons. Each very different yet very similar at the same time. Watching the lights soaring through the sky every winter was a tradition of sorts, a symbol of their lasting trust and friendship, renewed annually in the dead of winter. When the rest of the land lay barren, their friendship blossomed under the rivers of the sky. But, as time tends to, it moves forward. Night turned into day and the group reconvened to race. While Lumi and Demi were the judges, Icylyn and Neve competed to see who could run faster. “Three, Two,One and go!” shouted the judges in chorus which was followed by the two animals sprinting faster than ever. The patterning of the paws on the frozen ice was followed closely by Lumi, flying high over the two to keep a watch from afar. Just as she sped up to keep up with the competitors, a strange glint in the snow caught her eye. She froze for a moment, before suddenly letting out a long hoot and shooting down the frozen river at a breakneck speed. The other three startled, looking at each other questioningly before Icylyn bellowed “Lumi, where are you going?” The lack of an answering hoot worried them, and with Lumi’s tiny form quickly disappearing into the horizon they had no choice but to follow her. The three friends followed her, shouting and screaming her name to no avail. However, in their haste, they failed to notice the slow but certain change in the colour of the ice of the river. It seemed to swirl with faint light from below the ice. The light itself was not radiant enough to be seen on its own, yet it seemed to paint the ice a pale green.When they found her, Lumi was suspended midair, peering down into the murky river water with excitement in her eyes. “Lumi!” her friends called out, coming to a halt in front of the hole. “ What is the matter with you!” said Demi,gasping for breath. Lumi remained still, before suddenly turning to Icylyn “ I need you to swim down to the river bed, Icylyn. I think there is someone down there” she said, with a hardened expression. Icylyn opened her mouth to argue, but before could, she noticed the green beneath her feet. Immediately, she dove into the water. While the rest waited above with their hearts pumping faster and faster, Icylyn swam to the bottom of the river, to find a brilliantly shining mass of fabric in between schools of fish. She swam further, still unable to recognise anything due to the poor visibility. She nudged the mass slightly with her snout, only for some of the fabric to fall away and reveal the deathly pale face of a woman. Without wasting another second, Icylyn grabbed the fabric of her dress between her jaws, frantically paddling her paws to reach the surface. She broke the surface of the icy cold water and nearly hurled the woman out of water before slowly climbing out herself. As Icylyn emerged with a splash, the rest of the friends jumped back, startled only to scream further at the woman she had brought along with herself. “ I knew I saw something down there!” yelled Lumi, slowly inching towards the open palm of the woman and slowly prodding at it. In the shallow arctic sun, the sickly pallor of the woman seemed to fade, leaving her with a pearly glow that seemed to seep through her skin and bleed into her dark hair glinting with woven diamonds and sea foam. Her dress dripped with gossamer silk, waves and ruffles and tides of different shades of purple and green. She weakly radiated a faint light,with tight lines that seemed to slither across her skin painting it the colour of the gleaming rivers. Neve approached her body and sniffed around. “ She’s definitely alive - “ was all she could get out before being interrupted by a coughing fit. In front of their eyes, the woman took her first breath and coughed, hacking out water and doubling over in pain. Too scared to approach her, the animals stood afar and watched the proceedings with widened eyes. “Miss, are you ok?” said Demi in a concerned tone. “Who goes there? What are you animals doing here?” asked the deity with red rimmed eyes. “We saw the lights coming from a distance and came over to get a closer look when we found you at the bottom of the river. What are you doing here?” said Lumi. However, before the Goddess could respond, Neve suddenly started prancing around the deity. “Are you Aurora the goddess of dawn? All this time I thought that it was just a myth. You do produce the lights right? But where is your chariot and crown which were gifted to you by the fairies?” “ I collided with a star a few days ago and lost both my chariot and the crown. They must have crashed along with me somewhere here! It was a gift I received from the fairies and I can't fix the chariot or the crown on my own.” said Aurora as she started weeping. Surely enough,Icylyn remembered that she had found the goddess beside a pile of rubles which had glowing silver pieces that were scattered everywhere like ice shards.She then looked at the goddess who was weeping and longing for her chariot and her crown. “Maybe we can help you fix the chariot and your crown.” offered Icylyn, half happily and half desperately. At this, Aurora suddenly stopped crying and looked up at the friends who all agreed with Icylyn. Her expression hardened as if she had something come to a conclusion before she responded by saying “The worst that could have happened has already happened. I think there is no harm in trying. ” “Come!” said Neve with a broad smile to encourage the deity. And after this the world witnessed one of the most delightful and excellent examples of friendship. In the middle of nowhere, four animals along with a goddess were working together to bring back what was broken. While the four friends assembled the chariot by using anything they could find in the woods, the deity decorated and enchanted the chariot. As the sun settled, the chariot was too completed. It was dark blue in colour with stars painted all over. Wi With a wave of her hand, Aurora summoned her magical horses. “Aurora,” said Demi shyly. “We couldn’t find your crown and hence we made you one. We are extremely sorry.” The crown, Aurora realised, wasn’t like the one presented in fairytales. It wasn’t golden in colour, nor was it decorated with jewels. It was made with twigs which were tied together with ivy vines and were decorated with forget-me-nots. The middle held a wooden carving which showed Aurora soaring through the sky in her new chariot with her horses. “It isn’t the best but once you meet the guard fairies you can replace the chariot and the crown.” said Neve. “Oh, they are beautiful. I did not even think of visiting the fairies for a replacement! I will proudly ride in this chariot with this crown, showing it off to the whole world.” said Aurora with a smile and glistening eyes. “Here, accept this as a gift of gratitude from my side” and with a wave of her hand, she produced four identical crowns with wooden carvings woven in the middle representing each animal that wore it. “Thank you Aurora!” said the animals in pleasure. “I should be the one thankful. I wouldn’t have been able to soar the sky again if it weren't for you all.I suppose your houses are quite far. How about a ride in my chariot?” said Aurora with a mischievous look. Together they soared across the sky leaving the lights which we now know as the Aurora Borealis and Aurora Australis. Even today, Aurora soars across the sky happily, forever remembering her four friends who helped her re-build her chariot and gave her the most precious gift she could have ever asked for, friendship.

title: Left Out
text: Pillu was a yellow scooter and Bluey was a blue truck. They both were very different from each other yet they were best friends. One day a new tractor came to town. His name Lal Ranga. Lal Ranga met Pillu and they both became friends. Lal Ranga was very popular and Pillu was always by his side. Pillu did not hang out with Bluey and Bluey felt left out. One day Pillu was going somewhere and he was late. In a hurry he sped up and didn't notice a puddle of water and slipped. His engine stopped working and he could not get up on his own. Bluey was passing by and saw what had happened. Bluey helped Pillu up and took him to the nearest mechanic. On the way he could not keep it and told Pillu everything about how he felt left out. Pillu hadn't realized that he was not paying attention to his old friend. He apologized to Bluey and felt bad. Bluey also understood that Pillu was trying hard to balance both side. He organized a party with Lal Ranga for Pillu's birthday. All three of them became good friends and it seemed like a happy ending but right after the party Bluey and Lal Ranga had a fight because they both had bought the same gift for Pillu's birthday.

title: Oh ........... Noise
text: Jeewan had been facing problem in hearing. Often people would complain that he responded after he was called a number of times. So he visited a doctor. After his check-up, the doctor told him that he had become hard of hearing. He asked the doctor, "What could be the cause? I am not that old." The doctor said to him, "Mr. Jeewan, the cause of your hearing loss is the increasing noise around us. This is called noise pollution. This affects our body and mind." The doctor gave him some instructions and wrote medicines for him. After reaching home, Jeewan started thinking about noise pollution. He realized that the noise had increased in the environment. He started thinking about its causes. The number of vehicles on the roads has increased as compared to the earlier times. This has polluted the air. Besides, loud horns add to the noise. People play loud music while partying. Very often, loudspeakers on various religious and cultural programmes cause very loud noise. He read about the noise pollution on internet. He studied the harmful effects of noise pollution. He was surprised to know how noise pollution harms our physical and mental health. We become irritated and aggressive. Besides, it causes high blood pressure, tension, hearing loss, disturbed sleep and many other problems. Jeewan prepared a report on noise pollution. He went to his friend, Professor John to discuss this report. John was the professor of English. He was a good speaker and writer. Professor John understood the ill-effects of noise pollution. He decided to spread awareness about it. He wrote a number of articles on this topic in Hindi and English. He also gave speeches at many places. Jeewan also talked to many people and explained to them the ill effects of noise pollution. He met the officials and got the use of loudspeakers banned. He was honoured by a social organization for his work. Jeewan had to bear the effects of noise pollution. But he did not accept it quietly. He started a fight against it.
author: Veena Bhambhani
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Bindia  Thapar; Greystroke; Jesse  Breytenbach

title: A Failed Invention Finds a New Use
text: Malorie sat down on her bed. Her dream had been shattered. The invention she had been working on for years did not work at all. Her best friend Emma advised her to recheck the system and see if the anti-virus computer chip application worked, but Malorie did not want to try it ever again and no one could help her. Malorie was too hard on herself and called herself a ‘Failed inventor’. Emma told Malorie that the world was in a dire need of an anti-virus computer chip application and she must try again. My invention failed! Malorie got up and put a chip inside her computer which looked like a star. She downloaded the application and opened it but instead of showing the ‘virus free’ button, it was a little yellow chick hopping up and down. Both Malorie and Emma were shocked. They were left perplexed, wanting answers. 'Did Malorie do all the codes correctly? Is this the wrong application? Is this a dream?’ They re-checked all the codes and they were correct. Suddenly, the chick started speaking, “Click letter Z and the Mathematics quiz will begin." They clicked letter Z and five questions popped up the screen. They only had three minutes to solve them. After finishing it, they were awarded ten points. How did this chick come up here? It was a great way to learn Mathematics and there were modules followed by a quiz. Children would love this because of the extremely interesting games in it. They decided to upload the application after re-naming it. ‘The chick’s Math’ followed by a short name ‘TCM’. Parents loved the idea of learning Mathematics on a programme. Some people were surprised as this was the first application to teach Mathematics. Malorie was elated and gave all the credit to Emma for her support. One day, 'The Chick's Math' stopped working. People started questioning Malorie about the application's data. Some people even stopped using TCM. Malorie tried coding down the password but it looked like someone had changed the password. ‘Who could have done something like that?’ Then a familiar voice said, ”Someone very close to you could have done something like that”. Malorie thought of something for a minute and then after joining all dots exclaimed, “EMMA, How could you?” Emma replied,” I couldn’t see your success, YOU ARE NOTHING WITHOUT ME”. Then, Emma started turning the ‘TCM’ into Emma’s Math company but she needed a password to do so. She quickly typed in the password but to her surprise, it was wrong. Oh dear friend! last night I saw you changing the password and blocked you, leave my company alone. Emma had to leave as the security guards pushed her out of the building. On the other hand, Malorie became successful day by day. Her application was being used by every child in every country. Later on, the Prime Minister of India invited her to inspire the young generation by sharing her success story. Malorie advised children to never give up in life. We all face obstacles in our life, but we should face them with a lot of courage and move forward in life. Many children were inspired by Malorie’s speech. Malorie forgot about her past and focused on her bright future ahead. Hard work always pays off!
author: SAGAL KAUR      DHILLON
illustrator: Delwyn Remedios; Maithili  Joshi; Niloufer Wadia; Partho Sengupta; Rai

title: Ravi's Day Out
text: "Yaawwwwnn!" Ravi exclaimed while opening his eyes. He was still feeling drowsy. "What time is it?" Ravi murmured to himself while looking around for a clock around him. Soon, he found the wall clock in his room. It read 7:24. "Late" he murmured. He did not have anywhere or anything to do. The schools were closed due to summer vacation. All his friends were out of city. He even finished his homework out of boredom. He got out of his bed and opened Instagram to check on his friends. Seeing them having fun without him, he felt a pang of jealously in his heart. He decided to look for a occasion of theirs to crash. He messaged one of his friends to inquire about a party to crash. He soon found out about a get-together they were having nearby. He started getting ready to crash it. By 8:00 he was all ready to go. Just one thing remaining, what should he wear? Should he wear something funny and weird or something formal? He decided to wear his old spiderman costume he had for his 13th birthday. It was very tight as he had outgrown it quite long ago, just as he wanted. He packed the suit and a pair of pajamas in a backpack. he went around and found a few wide paper. He thought for a moment and decided what to write. "SPUIDEAR MUAN" Giggling to himself Ravi carefully put the frills in the backpack. Now, with the preparations complete, all that was left to do was crash the get-together. Leaving home, he calculated the path he will take to reach the place. He checked on Google Maps if the place he was told really exists. Fortunately it did, Now he had to reach the place before his friends did. While he was going there, he saw all kinds of things in shops on the way. People swarmed the markets. All types of people passed him. Soon, he passed a firecracker shop. Suddenly, he had an idea. He got there and purchased a few crackers. He then continued on his path. Half an hour later, he reached the spot. He checked for anyone nearby and after an idea. He got there and purchased a few firecrackers. He then continued on his path. Half an hour later, he reached the spot. It was hilltop with a dense forest nearby. Looking down, one could see a vast valley laying down the hill with zig-zag roads leading to the place. Tall trees far away laid with mist around them, hiding their true appearance. A beautiful sight. After admiring the view, Ravi got to work. He checked for anyone nearby and after confirming the absence of them, he got to work. Wiring the crackers, he was often giggling to himself at the thought of his friends freaking out. A few minutes later, he was done with the preparations/ He put his costume on and hid in the forest nearby. 15 minutes later, a person arrives there. Ravi instantly recognizes him as Aditya, a good friend of his. "A good start" he thought. Waiting a few more minutes, more of them came. He was starting to get bored of waiting all alone so he started to watch some videos to spend time. Time flies and by 10:00 a good amount of them had gathered. Ravi decided it was time acted. Lighting the fuse to the crackers, he waited it till the started to burst. The sudden explosions startled many present there. Between this panic, Ravi slipped in between them. Even in the flashy costume, a lot of them did not pay attention to him. Some time later, when most of the crackers had burst, someone noticed a peculiar entity in the crowd. "Hey! who are you?" "I AM........ spuidermuan." "........" "The saviour of people and procter of injustice, I helped defeat the enemy of myself. Praise me for my gre-" Ravi couldn't stop his laughter. The boy asked who he really was. To this he replied that he was Ravi. Many stared in disbelief. How could he have known where they were gathered. They started looking at each other to see if they could find the mole. The gathering slowly turned into a game of seek. Everyone looked around to find the one who leaked about the get-together. Then, everyone's eyes fell on Ravi. Only he could tell who told him about it. Seeing this, Ravi leaked the name of the mole. "It was Arnav." Instantly, all eyes fell on Arnav, who was hiding behind everyone. "......sorry?." Sharp inhaling sounds came from the crowd. "Forget it. Now that he is here, we will just continue as always." said Aditya. This suggestion was a great solution to their anger on the situation. While some did continue to complain, most decided to leave it and went to see if they could convince Ravi to dance in the costume. It was an hilarious sight. Ravi jumped so hard the overtight costume ripped into half, revealing Ravi who wore nothing more than a vest inside. Most of the watchers started laughing while the embarrassed Ravi ran to get a change of clothes from his backpack. Returning home, Ravi felt exhausted but content. He was happy with today's ordeals. Smiling, he went inside and took a shower. He then laid on the bed scrolling through Instagram when he saw the ripped costume with him inside. He felt a bit angry and turned his phone off. Unknown of his exhaustion, he immediately fell asleep
author: Tejas Joshi

title: A World Without ELECTRICITY !!
text: I t was the year 2025. Kimaya was just five years old. She was busy on the PlayStation with her older siblings, the twins, Meera and Vyom. The twins were 11 and were playing CTR after finishing their homework. “When will I get a chance? You two have been playing FOREVER!!” asked Kimaya who was getting annoyed at the moment. Her fists were clenched and she held her breath till her cheeks turned rosy red. The twins saw her face and immediately offered her the controller, afraid lest she got angry. The entire neighbourhood knew not to mess with those kids - the twins, because they were LEGENDARY PRANKSTERS, and little Kimaya because she could throw PRETTY SCARY TANTRUMS when she got angry. To the twins surprise, Kimaya refused and said “Let’s play something in which we all get a chance, like a Hide and Seek in the Yard!!!”. The twins agreed. They all went out to the yard. After a long argument, they chose Vyom to look for them. While he was counting to 50, the girls ran off to hide, giggling. Meera took a turquoise cloth and a green straw. She sat submerged in water in their personal lake covering herself with the cloth. The cloth gave the illusion of water. She breathed through one end of the straw while the other end stuck out of the fountain’s edge. It merged with the grass that grew there. Meanwhile, Kimaya was hiding in her treehouse on the cherry blossom tree. Their scientist parents were trillionaires and had bought the tree for Kimaya and Meera from Japan. It was one of the best things they could have asked for Suddenly Kimaya heard a loud bang. She ran inside and found all the lights were out. The twins ran into the house shocked. Their parents came into the room and told them that the solar storm reached a massive level and caused outages and blackouts across the globe”. The twins looked shocked and asked, “When will the power be back?” “We have no idea." said Mom. "It could be gone for weeks or even months!!” answered their mother, worried about what might happen next. The twins turned towards Kimaya, who gave a baffled look. Of course! She was just five. She couldn't make any sense of what their mother said. The twins decided to change her mood and took Kimaya along to continue the game. Vyom, again started to count up to 50, and Meera and Kimaya hid in their usual places. Meera started to wonder how life without electricity would be? No PS10s, no video games, no TV. There will be no power to use the fridge or freezer, telephone lines will be down, and phone signals will be lost. Mobile phones will be useless as the battery dwindles, with no backup charging option. The gas and central heating will not work, and the PWD will soon stop pumping and supplying clean water. We will be the FLINTSTONES. And worse, nights will be a nightmare? Life without Electricity! Sounds torturous and unacceptable. No emails, no wireless, no mobile communication would exist. Medical procedures dependent on electrical energy, will never be initiated. Costlier Manpower, Closure of Large Industries, The collapse of Economies, A decrease in Productivity, Environmental Concerns, Electrical Equipment will all become junk. Few Sources of Entertainment, More Dependency on Non-renewable Energy, Short Life Expectancy, and a Threat of War. Suddenly, Meera hears a loud noise, and she wakes up with a start. She looks around and sees Kimaya and Vyom playing. She didn’t realize when she fell asleep on the bean bag, but she was happy that it was JUST a terrible dream.
author: Veda Sharma

title: The Most Horrible Day (Poem)
text: Another day, hot and dry Oh when will water come to our life. The branches and leaves have all dried up. Water to drink is not in our cups. Everyone in the village, how they pray. Rain would come right this way I overheard someone say "This is the most horrible day". We use water to wash our clothes. Dirty wear give us loathes We need water to bathe every day. Clean and fresh, that's the way. We need water keep our plants alive. Water is necessary for us to survive. We need water to quench our thirst. For survival that's the first. Finally rain joins after weeks, The wish arrives which everyone seeks. First shower comes and then it go's. Then it come's back many times more. Soon everyone started to worry, As the floods came in a hurry. Soon the roofs started to leak, looked like it will last a week. Then I overheard someone say "This is the most horrible day".
author: Riddhima Banerjee

title: Changing School
text: ﻿ ﻿ It was a nice & joyful day. At 1:20pm, I was going back to my home with my friends who lived beside my house. We were roaming in the path and finally reached ours house. I entered my house and greeted my Mom by saying Good Afternoon to her. She was little upset and wondering something. ﻿ I asked her if she is wondering something but she replied by saying "NOTHING". Then, I went upstairs in my room and changed my clothes and went downstairs to do lunch as I had to go to my coaching in one hour. In Lunch there was RAJMA CHAWAL which is my favourite. After coming from coaching my dad was also at home and we did the dinner together. Afterwards, we were sitting and watching T.V. ﻿ My Dad said, "How is your study going?" I said, "Nice!" He said," Actually there is something that we want to tell you." I said," What is it?" My Mom said, "Your dad has been transferred to Mumbai and we have to go there next week only. ﻿ I said," What! How it happened so sudden and what about my school coaching?" My Dad said," We would get your T.C the day after tomorrow and I have also talked to your coaching teacher and she is fine with it. I said," Oh! but I will miss my friends, my school and my teachers a lot. I can't go to Mumbai, I will stay here and go to my school." My Mom said," Don't behave like a little child, now you are younger and you should obey what we are saying". Dad said," Everyone is feeling sad child but we have to go to mumbai". I said," What about my studies in mumbai and how I will manage it?". Dad said," We are thinking to transfer you from your current school to its mumbai school branch. So, you would not suffer much". ﻿ I didn't had any option instead of saying yes and I finally said YES. We were going to Mumbai next monday by train but I was very sad thinking of how I would tell it to my friends. The next day, I was on the way to my school and reached, I was very quiet and thinking how would be the school in Mumbai and so on... My friend asked me why I am so sad but I didn't answered anything. On our way back to home, I Told everything about my father's transfer to mumbai. They were shocked. One of my friend said, "so, you are staying in Jamshedpur na?". I said with sadness," No, me and my mom are also going". Jigyasa said," What! Then what about your school and most important our friendship". I said," My parents would come tomorrow to school and would transfer me to Mumbai's branch. Vatsala said," But our friendship will broke how we would enjoy together?". I said," I am also thinking the same thing since tomorrow but when I asked my mom she gave me a solution that we would talk one time in every week on video call". Ritul said," We can do that but the way we met everyday for playing and going to school we can't do it online". Jigyasa said," True, I have an idea lets talkto her parents and request them to leave her here". Other two said Yes! I was also hoping that they would agree. In evening my friends came home and i was also nervous. They requested my mom but she refused and explained them and all of them shaked their head and we went in park to play. Ritul said," So, we failed in convincing your mom, now what we will do". I said," Now nothing could happen. I have to go next week to Mumbai". Jigyasa said," Ya! Anything would happen but our friendship will not break. Promise Everyone! Everyone promised and we came back home by playing. It was the day we finally were going to Mumbai. I was feeling really said and we reached station. Our train was here and we reached Mumbai two days later. Firstly it was a beautiful monuments. We reached our new house and it was amazing. Our furniture were already fixed there and the next day was my school. It was the first day of my new school. I was nervous as well as excited. The teachers were just like my previous school teachers. The students were also intelligent, talented and funny also and the school was also big but not like the previous school was. Everyday was without my friends. I talked to them but it was something missing. One day, when I came back home my mom and dad was also at home. I was surprised. My Mom said," We have a surprise for you". My Dad said," We are going to Jamshedpur again as I am transferred again". I was shocked ae well as happy.It was one of the best day of my life. In other two weeks we were back in Jamshedpur and I was overwhelmed after meeting my lovely friends. Afterwards, I came to know that my dad changed his company for my happiness and I was overwhelmed hearing this. Finally, I was with my friends and enjoying coming and going to school.

title: Last Supper
text: For some considerable time, David had known he would kill his Wife. David was a creature of habit, and yet he had learnt to accept his anonymity and predictability as a blessing, not a curse. He rose at the same time, dressed in an indistinguishable manner from those he wore on any other day, ate the same breakfast, took the same route to work. He filed insurance claims till lunchtime, and then he walked to the park. Here he sat for forty-eight minutes to read the newspaper, to eat his sandwich, and then he walked back to the office. To him, this routine had become a comfort. David had made no plans as to how he will dispose her body, nor how he would explain, everyone else around, her sudden disappearance. perhaps he believed that once the deed was done, he would be struck by a brilliant solution, a streak of lightning, a bolt from the blue. David had decided her method of death, however. He would stab her in her eye. The chosen instrument was not a knife, but a knitting needle. He had bound half its length in duct tape so as to provide a firm grip, yet with six inches exposed to be believed that the needle - if driven suddenly, and with sufficient force - would pass directly through her eye and into the brain. There would be a little, if any, blood, and the death would be instant. She had given him fifteen years of comfortable, predictable marriage, and he did not want to cause her any pain or distress. In fact, David did not think it as a murder, but more of an execution for some unknown crime. And so it was, on a cool summer evening, that David and his wife sat on the dining table to eat. She had prepared a Chicken Salad and opened a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc (a White Wine). They ate in almost complete silence, the stillness punctuated by the odd pleasantry, the fact that rain had been accepted but not arrived. 'Perhaps tomorrow', David had commented, finding it ironic that he was mentioning something of which she would know nothing. David Sat calmly, the knitting needle beneath his thigh. He felt a sense at a philosophical resignation regarding the inevitability of what was about to happen. There would be no struggle, no raised voices, no desperate dramas. She taught against hands tightening around her throat. There would be no blood-spatter, no scuff-marks from frantic heels against the linoleum. She would find herself at dinner, and then she would be dead. Perhaps she would not even notice. 'You're having no wine'. He asked her. 'No', She said, 'I have a slight headache, the wine will worsen it'. It was then that David experienced a sudden pain of something. She smiled at him, and smiled in such an innocent and unaffected way, and there had been almost a sense of sadness in her tone. She could not know what he had planned, for he had planned nothing beyond her death. She could not expect him for any deceit. Each day had been the same. He had done the same things, expressed same thoughts with the same words, continued with routines that had remained constant for years. In fact, it was safe to say the single most defining characteristic of their marriage was that nothing ever happened. But now he was feeling something. Was it regret? Was it guilt? Was he even now questioning the determination he had made to kill her? Why was he experiencing a sense of disorientation, a feeling of agitation in his stomach, a feeling wave of nausea? Why did he now feel so weak, so uncertain? He opened his mouth to speak. His words were thoughts, but they were not sounds. She looked at him, the same sense of sadness in her eyes. The stab of pain in his gut was breath-taking. It snatched every molecule of air from his lungs and throat. he had never felt anything like it. The pain did not last long-thirty seconds, perhaps forty. He felt his cheek against the plate of moist salad, and then he felt nothing at all. David's wife carried the wine bottle and glass to the sink. She was methodical as she washed them, ensuring every grain of sediment was removed from both. And then she stood at the kitchen doorway and looked at her "Dead Husband", and she believed that during the last days, as she had planned his murder, she had never felt more than enough emotion to compensate for a decade and a half of feeling nothing at all.
author: Dhruv Dave

title: His Favourite Kheer
text: His Favourite Kheer Between the tiny pathways around coconut groves, giving out heavy breaths, he ran. Stepping on the rocks that stood in his way, he ran. Jumping over the huge logs, he ran. Ignoring the cuckoo’s calls and the scorching sun, he ran. Until he saw her, he ran. Clad in the softest sarees, with thick snow-like hair that went down her knees, with a round bindi like that of the moon, with eyes that were filled with warmth, she stood… awaiting him. The little boy with curly black hair and round eyes, beaming with life, ran and hugged his grandmother, awaiting her special kheer after a tiring day of school. His mother had left this sinful world, when he was an innocent infant. Though his father had remarried, to eliminate the lack of a mother for his little tot, his grandmother strictly prohibited taking him home to his step-mother, for she would never be able to love him as one of her own. His mother's absence never affected him. His life was illuminated with joy and radiant smiles, as his grandmother showered him with all her love and care. The melancholy breeze was replaced with his playful laughter. His childhood abode was an old, traditional Kerala sixteen-block house made of teak and oak. His backyard was the home to banana trees and mango saplings. Coconut trees skirted around his house. Every evening, he used to take his legs as fast as he could and ran home. He loved to be with his grandmother. He used to savour the delicious dishes, especially kheer, she had made for him every evening, while she told him folktales and fables, which went together like milk and cookies. After a brief bath, it was time for puja. He sang all the hymns of Lord Krishna with his grandmother, passionately, word by word, pronouncing them effortlessly like it had been etched on his tiny soul! Sometimes he even surpassed his grandmother, in his devotion to his adored god, Lord Krishna. Later, he sat down with his books and learnt with an attentive mind, grasping all the knowledge in the air. He wanted to grow up, become a pilot and give his grandmother a life of luxury. He was indeed the quintessence for hard work and determination. Time flew like a shooting star, he was now a young teenager yet his incandescent love for his grandmother remained unabating. He topped the class, and was destroying exams like enemies in the battlefield. Now, he had a deep desire concealed in the bottom of his heart, like a tiny seed veiled below the countless grains of sand. He wished for a computer, which many of his pals boasted about. One day, he conveyed his wish to his father, who happily agreed to the same and tried to strengthen their bond and persuaded him to come to his place. But his father’s intentions failed miserably and he gave up. Meanwhile, the boy was on cloud nine as the computer arrived. Hours of chatting and playing games were now his evening mates, as he too could show-off as the owner of something considered an opulence. His increasing addiction to his computer, resulted in many losses, which were unseen to his immature psyche. His grades deteriorated, his creativity declined, long hours of sitting took a toll on his growing body and finally, his everlasting relationship with his grandmother was breaking down like an unmended wall, one stone at a time. He, who used to spend all his time listening to his grandmother’s stories was now captivated by a mini screen which gradually sabotaged their bond. The grandmother tried to pacify her dilapidated heart. "Well! He is a growing child but he’ll always love me!" But fate always decides, doesn’t it… But fate always decides, doesn’t it… One evening, the pampering grandmother had made his favourite kheer and was waiting for him to devour it all, as soon as he came back from school. The tired lad came home and rushed to indulge in his artificial felicity and forgot all about his grandmother waiting for him with the cup of kheer in her wrinkled hands. She waited and waited and waited… Soon, realising that he had forgotten about it, the grandmother slowly walked up the wooden stairs, clutching her wobbly knees, and went to his room. As he was busy playing games with a loud decibel, she patted him on the shoulder and she offered him the cup of kheer, made with all her love, to which he harshly pushed her hand away, as he was too obsessed with his game at the moment. The grandmother, deeply hurt, went down to her room to have a little nap to console her broken heart. The boy, after hours of playing games, saw the split kheer near his table - which reminded him of his grandmother. He rushed down the stairs and went to his grandmother’s room and saw her sleeping. He called out to her, but she gave no response and was as still as water. He shook her but still she remained the same. Nervous thoughts entered his spirit. A sudden chill ran down his spine. His hands went numb with fear. It was only then that he realised that his grandmother had joined his mother and had fled to her new dwelling, far away, only because of his negligence. He went behind materialistic pleasures and forsaked the real gem. Alas! Now all he could do is feel guilty, but nothing else! He tried to wash away his misdeeds. But no holy river or puja could remove the stain of guilt, which was imprinted in his soul. He lay watching the glinting stars, picturing his grandmother, asking her forgiveness. Well! That was all he could do now! He left that home on that day, with this nerve-wrecking incident fresh as milk, in his brain. And to this day, he never laid a foot, in that horrid place, where his grandmother shedded her tears, where she left her bodily form, where he forgot his own blood!
author: Dhriti Shaju

title: A RIDE PAST RESTRAINT
text: Nei-ohh-gghh…! I stretched my jaws as much as I could, and closed my eyelids firmly, trying to fall into a deep slumber.But.. Oh come on! Not again! This has probably been the thousandth time I’ve forced myself to sleep. I was just too exhausted from my work, my surroundings, my life, myself- just everything. I started feeling more and more redundant. ‘Excess of anything is poisonous’ they say- it became my steadfast belief over time as I realised that I was surfeited with life itself. I took a glimpse of my surroundings yet again, just the same brownish green stripes of grass brushing each other until my horizon below and flocks of birds hovering intermittently above. And as always, I could hear the gurgling of the puddle that was beside. The place was aloof, visited by visitors very rarely, not even another kind like me would venture here. It was serene outside of course, but well inside- not really. I wanted to walk away from this zone and find some friends. There was always some hindrance to it, perhaps the nostalgia (of my fellow herdmates) I associated with the place, perhaps my reserved nature or perhaps just my fate. Nevertheless, I feel like I should probably set forth and find a new environment. I’ve always had a small intuition of venturing out elsewhere and exploring, atleast to get rid of this unvaried food. Though this thought has arisen multiple times, I’ve somehow never had the thrust to do so. As I kept thinking, suddenly I heard a rustle of leaves. I immediately opened my half- closed eyelids to see the light brown skin of a lion camouflaging behind one of those tall grasses. But it had aimed at some other prey.Completely struck blank by fear, I seized the bridles and ran as far as I could. This was completely unprecedented for it is the first time that someone has ventured here after four long years. Thus this time, I really felt the need, the need to move out of my comfort. It was now or never. I took refuge under a peepal tree over the night. As the dawn broke, I set off. I took the bridle, and remembered the times when my brothers raced each other while I’d sit timidly watching them.They always competed to finish off at the good old peepal tree. I bid goodbye to the peepal tree too and promised to return with new friends. I walked and walked to come to a fork. I was perplexed on which path to take, and which one would lead me where. While I contemplated, I heard some sound.I peeped through the bush to see a deer and a fox quarrelling over who was more intelligent. I thought I could use this as an opportunity and went over to them. Both of them looked puzzled at me, and the deer asked ‘What species are you supposed to be? Wild, huh? Because I don’t think this jungle belongs to any horses’. While the fox replied with a smirk, ‘I doubt so. As much as I could recollect, horses don’t belong to any jungle I suppose.’ Annoyed by the statement of the fox, I retorted, ‘Um…I am one of the rare species..of hh-horses. My brothers have been c-cc-aptured and taken to town for reasons I am not aware of.I need help to go out of the jungle. So..’. The deer continued, ‘So? You need our assistance, right? I nodded. The fox thought for a while and said, ‘Mr. Rare Horse, It would be my pleasure to help you out but on one condition. You must answer my three questions, three very witty ones.’ If the answers are accurate I’ll show you the way. The deer stared and immediately responded, ‘No, no. I am better aware of the ways of the jungle. I could show you the way more rapidly only if you can keep pace with me.’ Uh-oh! Where have we landed now?! I questioned myself. In an attempt to escape from a fork, I got struck hard by another. Nevertheless, recalling the cunning nature of a typical fox, I accepted the deer's condition. The deer and I started going ahead while the fox gave a crafty look. Then, I galloped high, cantered sprightly with the deer but in vain. The deer had run far ahead and I could only cover one fourth of its speed. I soon got exhausted because I’ve never run this much in my whole life! I continued to walk in the same path for some time, relaxing though frustrated at first, until I heard a loud growl.Quite startled, I reversed to see a tiger hunting a monkey! I galloped silently but fastly in order to not reveal my presence. Then after taking refuge, I saw the tiger pouncing on the mammal, but fortunately the monkey climbed to the pinnacle of the tree and with the help of its long arms and gripping tail flew to the other trees.The ability of the monkey proved to be the weakness of the tiger- obstructing it from aiming further. Naturally after sometime the tiger cooled down, chewed a mouthful of small insects he could capture and left the place. Still in doubt, I walked noiselessly as far as the suspicion went away from me. Then, I came to a halt to see the tall trees shrinking into small strips of grass, shrubs, and herbs. The sun shone brightly on my face, there was no more canopy.It was the edge of the jungle. ‘Yay! I made it!’, I thought. I guzzled down water from a small pond in the town to refresh myself. Then, I carried myself more confidently towards the town in search of my brothers. Initially, I kept out of sight as I did not want anyone to notice a strange creature walking on the road. But I later realised that animals kept in pace with human beings in the modern world. Infact, many humans had a box sort of thing in their hands, which they kept looking at constantly. Few held it close to their ears and spoke too. Wait.. I remember from my vague memory that it was called a ‘phone’. The last time I came to the town with my family, I had seen them too but not this much in use. Well, so I set off again. This time I observed that the small town had sky scraping buildings that grew out of vicinity amongst the mass of clouds. It was present at every nook I saw. Later, I could see a small lake which I remember, along with my herd mates, I had come here for a picnic about five years back. I galloped in the pathway while suddenly a white, polished, small, metal like thing flew past my head making me unstable and eventually making me slip and fall on the water in the pathway. A small girl came out of it, along with her parents. They pressed some random button which made the vehicle compress itself and fly away. I was intrigued by what that vehicle was, while the girl exclaimed, ‘The ride in the flying car was amazing, mom and dad!’ The girl noticed me, and without a second thought started shouting at her parents, ‘I want to ride on that horse! It looks so beautiful, mommy. Pleasee, let me ride.’ I was taken aback and turned to go in the opposite direction unsure of my ability to ride while another horse stopped me. My heart skipped a beat, for it was my brother!! I tiptoed and cantered and exclaimed at his arrival. He too embraced me back. He was proud of my migration, he said, ‘I knew, one day, you would come in search of us past your diffidence.’ I smiled and questioned about the whereabouts of the other brother, and he answered that he too was initially a therapeutic rider but now is in the profession of training horse-like-robots to perform riding and other activities in a finer and more desirable way. I was astonished and asked, ‘Are these robot stuffs replacing animals too?’ ‘Yes’, he said. ‘But do not worry, we’ll ultimately be given more freedom, we can go back to our homes.’ Consequently the girl climbed on my back and I rode and rode and stopped after my brother did. The girl tapped my back with pleasure, thanked me and gave me a fleshy green leaf to eat. ‘Atlast, I can satisfy my hunger!’ I thought. But as I bit it, the bitter- rusted metal like smell and taste sabotaged the impression I had on it. My brother laughed at my innocence and said, ‘This is a modern token of a gift to the horses that ride- which we must give to our riding instructors; ‘tis not a real leaf!!’.
author: Sadhana Sakthivel

title: The Underwater Adventure
text: The Underwater Adventure Contents 1. Our Small World 2. The Water encounter 3.The Unheard voice!? 4. Do Flying Fishes really Fly? 5. Help! A whale gives me lift! 6. Twist in the tail! Our Small World Have you ever thought" Why is the world so unhappy around us????" I just hate it when people shout at me saying" Tie your hair properly!!" or "Your teeth are like nuts!!That scares me out of my skin. So I just finished asking my parents to take me to the beach. My parents told me they will take me to the beach during the weekend. Yoo-hoo!!! I am so, so, so, so, so happy!!! Now I have 1 hour of homework!!!! Uhh!! Okay. I'm kind of out of my breath. By the way, my name is Smitha. The Water encounter It's Saturday, and I'm going to the beach. My beach essentials were kept in a big bag. Did you know that I am a good swimmer? I've been learning swimming since I was a small child and every time I was in the water, it felt so good. Today, my mother had also brought her best sandwiches to eat accompanied by lemonade. The life guard was sitting in his tall chair. I was making a sandcastle. I went to eat sandwiches and drink lemonade and when I came back, someone had broken my sandcastle. My architectural beauty is in ruins and I had no longer a blueprint to make one again. The Unheard voice!? I went back to the waters and as I was swimming, I heard a shrill voice calling out "Hi, what's your name?" I turned around to find a trunkfish staring at me. That was a strange fish which could only move its eyes, mouth, fins and tail however not its body. A brick with extensions in my eyes.... Could animals even talk!? I nervously blurted "Was that you?". The brick moved it's mouth and said "Yes". I told my name and got to know that the trunkfish was called "Puffy". Then I asked Puffy " Do fish have ears and noses?". Puffy said "We do have ears, but unlike yours, ours cannot be seen. It is like we have inner ears. I have an excellent sense of hearing. I can hear a loud voice or footsteps on the shore. We also have noses. We use our noses to hunt. By the way, I smell sandwich." I smell something fishy and got spooked. The fish said" Let me take you to my friend, Jewel the Turtle." I puffed behind Puffy and saw a small, beautiful turtle. After intros, I asked Jewel, "Who locked you inside that?" She laughed and said, "We turtles use these shells to protect ourselves from danger. Our skeletons can bend easily. We carefully fold ourselves and hide in our shells when we sense danger. We also sleep in the same way." Our interesting conversation was interrupted by some fluttering tails. Do Flying Fish really Fly? "Are those fish having a party in the air?" I asked. Jewel told "Those fish are called flying fish. If an enemy chases them, they swim very fast and then leap out of the water. As they come shooting out of the sea, they shake their tails fast against the surface of the water to build up speed for take-off. They have four fins. Help! A whale gives me lift! As I was about to go to the shallow water, a whoop was heard and suddenly, me and Jewel were sitting on something blue. Jewel told we were on a sperm whale, the only whale which could enter the twilight zone. It was also the loudest whale. We were slowly entering a deep, dark place. As we went deeper, I saw some plants and glowing objects. The sperm whale introduced itself as Bumper. It told that in this zone, many animals are "Bioluminescence" animals. They produce light and most of them have big eyes to see in the half-light of the dark depths. The ocean was really interesting. The sea animals glow in the dark and look weird. Flashlight fish, Lanternfish and glowing jellyfish making light in the dark..... I hope they are filled with neon and their batteries don't run dry. Twist in the Tail My mother must have been really worried that I didn't return to the shore for so long and yelled "Smitha, it's time to be out....... Of y our bed " What, was this all a dream???? I wish it was true!!! Smitha raced off to explain her Underwater Adventure to her mother during breakfast. Father told "There comes the idea for your story writing competition, don't you think, darling?" "I love the beach." Smitha is so happy. We will see the wonderful Adventures of Smitha. Trunkfish, Turtles and Sperm whales are so talkative! We never knew they could be like us.

title: Friendship Without A Face
text: The minute hand of the clock dreadfully ticked by. All the children were situated in their seats, fixated on the clock. Despite the teacher rambling about some math concepts, the students didn't care to pay attention. As the clock struck three, the bell rang and all the children from all the classes rushed out of the school. It was the beginning of summer and the children were rambling about how they were going to spend their summer. This was the time, friends would explore the nearby forest and the local film students would try to shoot amateur short films. At the end of the day, nothing mattered to anyone except having fun. Abdul, on the other hand, had a different story to tell. He was the general shy kid in the class and headed straight home after the bell rang, avoiding eye contact with anyone in his way. Once he reached his house, he opened the door and closed it behind him. He heard sounds coming from the kitchen and decided to peek from the corner. He found his parents arguing like usual. Abdul let out a sigh and headed upstairs, to his room. Abdul watched the fan spin over his head, but the sound of it rotating didn't dilute the sound of his parents arguing. He opened his closet and found a kite. He recollected his childhood memories of how he used to fly the kite with his older brother before he had ended his life. The boy walked towards the window and watched his childhood friends ride their bikes. He reminisced about how he would spend his days exploring the woods and building a small castle with them. Abdul headed downstairs and was surprised at how quiet the house had become. As he left the house, he noticed his mother in tears in the kitchen. Although he was tempted to hug her, he'd gotten used to the sight of her crying after the arguments with his father. Abdul visited the library and quickly grabbed a book. He seemed like an anomaly from all the other kids who wouldn't dare to visit the library during their summer. He quickly found himself engrossed in his book, deafening anything around him. Suddenly, Abdul heard a creak next to him. He glanced at the person who took a seat next to him. It was another boy of similar build. Abdul continued to read his book after giving the boy an awkward look. "Hi, my name is Amar!", the boy said. Abdul lowered his book and found the boy stretching out his hand. Abdul shook his hand and replied, "I'm Abdul." He held his book to his face again, trying to indicate how he was not interested in making friends, but Amar wasn't going to give up on his attempt. He tried to stir up a conversation and asked, "What are you doing here all alone?" Irritated, Abdul put down his book and replied, "I don't want to make friends, at least not right now." Amar didn't take long to continue his conversation. He told Abdul about how he was exploring the forest a few days ago and came across a small castle. Abdul's face lit up and he became interested in the conversation. He wondered if Amar had run into the castle that he had built many years ago, but he knew that he could only answer that question if he saw it for himself. The two left the library and ventured into the nearby thickly forested woodland which seemed as if it would devour them. They crunched the twigs on the forest ground. For much of their journey, it was only Amar who was speaking with Abdul closely listening. Amar would talk about how he had recently moved in and had no friends. He would commonly be picked on by bullies and didn't have an easy time at home. Abdul found his life to be closely resembling Amar's and could relate to him more than expected. As the sun's rays began to descend, Abdul's excitement subsided and he grew worried that he would find it difficult to return home. After what seemed like an eternity, the pair finally reached a small castle. It seemed ancient and Abdul froze at the sight of it. He remembered how he built the castle in kindergarten. A smile grew on Abdul's face and he went inside the castle, though he could barely fit. Amar watched the events play out, confused and asked if Abdul had been there before, to which Abdul replied by saying that he was the one who built it. Abdul emerged from the castle and gazed at Amar whose face was illuminated by the bright moon. "Would you like to come to my house?", asked Abdul to which Amar shrugged. Abdul requested Amar to stay for a while and leave after dinner which Amar couldn't refuse. Amar led the return journey and they seamlessly made it out without getting lost. It almost seemed as if Amar had known this path for years. As the pair walked to the house, Abdul explained to Amar the situation at his house and Amar listened attentively. Once they reached the house, Abdul quietly opened the door. The loud creak alerted his mother who was in the kitchen. She glanced at Abdul who was closing the door behind him, while letting Amar in, and asked, "Abdul, where were you for so long?" Abdul looked at his mother, but before he could answer, she turned around and continued cooking. The two went upstairs and stood on the balcony. The night was a full moon and stars spilled over the black sky. Abdul and Amar spent the next half hour getting to know each other better. Abdul's face was filled with joy and he forgot about the arguments his parents were having. He was preoccupied with his new friend who seemed like a gift from heaven. The rest of the night was fuzzy for Abdul who had become tired due to their journey. The next morning, Abdul was woken up by the sound of his parents downstairs. He searched his room and balcony, but Amar was nowhere to be seen. Abdul assumed that he had left and gone home. He could still hear his parents shouting and waited near the stairs until their voices receded. After a while, he went to the hall and asked his mother if she had seen Amar, but to his surprise, she claimed to have seen no one entering the house with Abdul the previous night. Abdul deduced that his mother was busy cooking and must have not seen Amar. Abdul went back to the library and found Amar already reading the book he was reading the previous day. The pair waved to each other and decided to go out for another venture. They biked towards the beach and sat down on the sand. The coarse particles got in between their fingers, but the cool water that washed up on the shore helped to reduce the summer heat. The two didn't talk much that day and instead spent much of the afternoon staring at the sunset and listening to the sounds of seagulls. It brought Abdul back to the memories of his childhood when his parents would bring him to the beach almost every weekend. He got teary-eyed but held his tears back. Amar noticed and said, "My parents told me that when they were kids, they would always go to the beach because the sight would be beautiful." Abdul replied, saying "Well, they sure weren't lying." Another awkward silence set in until Amar broke it by talking about how his parents told him about two swans that would always be seen near the beach. He mentions how both of them would always be spotted together. Abdul looks at Amar, letting the tears roll down. Amar walks towards Abdul and hugs him while patting him on the back, assuring him that everything was going to be fine. The following day, Abdul and Amar met at the park. Abdul brought his kite, hoping that he would be able to fly it high above the clouds. Amar watched as Abdul tried to keep the kite away from the tree, but the wind blew it towards the thorny twigs. As the thread was almost about to snap, Amar grabbed the reel and pulled it in the opposite direction, just like how Abdul's brother would do. The kite began to soar high and Abdul watched in surprise and excitement. Both of them gazed at the kite flying in the blue sky filled with clouds. The few moments Abdul had with Amar were the only time he could forget about the arguments between his parents. He was finally able to stop worrying about bullies and being lonely and now had a friend he could look up to. Abdul turned towards Amar, letting out a smile and saying, "Thank you, Amar." The End
