title: TEENAGE INTRESTS
text: Teenage is certainly one of the most enthusiastic yet the biggest turning points of one's life. it can either shape your future or you end up living in a hell. here's a story of a teenage girl Luna who went through so much but yet helped herself when no one did. Luna was a hard working girl from a very young age. she always scored high in her academics and her parents loved her so much but this is where the real story started.....her parents loved her so much that she used to get whatever she wants to. yes her parents were strict but they pampered their child with everything she ever asked for. Time passed and she was no more a child she was 16 and even though she was still a minor but she wanted to explore the world just like all the pins we see on pinterest. she wanted to have all those hormonal affairs that we call fling. but she was unaware of the disastrous damage that would do to her. But she was overly influenced by everything she saw online and then she took her first step towards disaster by thinking of applying in real she was a lot active in social media and she started to believe the filters on social media sites to be the reality of life. then one day she wore a scandalous outfit to the school because she thought it to be cool but she was very much ashamed of herself later when she realized that the outfit she thought to be so cool, turned out to be the latest gossip all over the school. but she didn't stop then, she was blinded by a veil of online popularity and fame. later she made friends with a group who influenced her to sneak out at nights, and as the youngblood speaks for herself, she started hanging out a lot with them. And not to mention they were a bad influence for her, she started taking drinks before being an adult, she also started to smoke weed and speak in foul language to elders. Many days passed and her condition was degrading she always skipped classes in order to maintain her online presence and she just left to study and when her friends looked at her anymore they used to say '' you are no more the friend we trust on....you are just so changed you.... you.....used to be so sensitive with us but now you have an attitude as if you are the QUEEN OF ENGLAND....I miss the old u'' When these words left her friends' mouth she felt a very strong feeling of regret in her guts but she turned them down and took a half day and went back home. A few days later she was in a restaurant and she snapped a picture of herself eating and she shared it on social media. after her a while she posted that picture she gets a dm saying 'stay where you are I'm watching you' she was very much scared at this one text since the next was very creepy. But luckily she reported to the police with the help of her friends and family and the guy was caught and it was found that he was involved in human trafficking and Luna was just saved from a huge trouble. She was so frustrated over herself that she promised she would never misuse here internet again and she would leave her desire for internet fame as she now understood that such fame doesn't matters in one's life when they have so many real life people who care for her and now she understood that all of her decisions over the past few years were so wrong and now she decided that she would workout on every mistake she made and build a better version of herself.

title: CHANDNI
text: Once there lived an old man in Almora. His name was Abbu Khan.He kept a few goats as pets.He would give each of them funny name. Abbu Khan was however a little unlucky very often, at one of the goats would break the string and go up to hills. It was so because the goats loved freedom. His goats were of the best hills bread. Goats in the hills regions hated to tie with tree or poles. But this freedom cost them their lives. They were eaten by an old wolf. One day when all his goats had gone. He become very sad.He decieded to have no more goats as pets, however, he changed his mind soon after. It was so because without the goats he became very lonely Now, he bought very young goat. He thought it would stay with him for long time. He decieded to love her very much that it would never go away So, he bought a preety young goat. He named it chandni means moonlight. Chandni lived with Abbu Khan for several years But when it grew up it also felt the urge of going up the hills.She wanted to run the hills but his rope would stop her. So she began to hate the rope round her neck. Soon; She stopped eating grass and stop listening the stories of Abbu Khan. she becanme thin and unhappy. Abbu khan did not understand her problem. At last, chandni decieded to speak to him frankly. She asked him to let her go to the hills. Now, Abbu khan understand her problem. He told chandni of the danger of death if she went to hiils because their lived a dangerous wolf who kiil her but chandni said, “she would fight with wolf”. she again and again said she wanted to go to the hills the Abbu khan got angry with chandni and replied “you are not going anywhere. Now, From today you lived in a hut, and not move about freely in the compound. Ungratefully as you are, you must still be saved from wolf “. He pushed close the door But forget to close the window at the back. The same night chandni made that window her passage to freedom. Chandni reached the hills. she enjoyed her freedom. chandni felt that it was the happiest day of his life. she played for hours on the green grass. Then, there was night. there was stillness all around. In that silence, Chandni heard the voice of the wolf She was scared for once go back to abbu khan ‘ s hut? no, she replied to herself,’’ Death in open field is far better than life in a hut ‘’. The wolf came out fron the bushes, and was staring greedily at chandni. The wolf and the goat sized up each other. the wolf was big and ferocious whereas the goat thought healthy, was smaller. but small is not always weak. Chandni stood firms on her legs, head slightly bent and horns jutting out. she was the picture of courage. she looked like a brave soldier ready to fight a treacherous enemy. ‘’ I must put up a good fight ‘’. Chandni thought. ‘’ success or failure is a matter of luck or chance.’’ Chandni fought bravely. They fought with each other all night. The wolf of getting ready to eat her. An assemly Of birds perched on top of a tree nearby was the result of the fight. “who is the winner ‘’?One of them said, “The wolf of course “.A wise old bird declaimed with confidence “chandni is the winner “. Moral: Freedom is for all and it is their right. Never give up till last breath.

title: SHANTI'S FRIEND
text: About the author: Deepa Agarwal was born in the foothills of Himalayas, where most of her stories are set. At present she is living in the city of Delhi. Deepa Agarwal is an Indian writer and poet. She is the author of more than 60 books. Her stories are of different kinds, funny and sad, scary and mysterious. Some are inspired by her own experiences, while others are just made up. “Shanti’s Friend “is one of the stories written by her. About the story: When drought strikes the village an uncle from the city promises to educate Shanti in return for help with the housework. However, there is no school for Shanti, only endless chores and countless fault finding. After a severe scolding, Shanti decides to run away but has no money for her bus ticket. She sits down under a tree to think and the tree speak to her. Shanti always had to get up early in the morning. Just when the sky was getting lighter and most people were asleep in their beds. She had to get up early to make tea for her uncle and her aunt. Shanti was eleven years old. She stayed with her uncle and aunt in the city. She had to come to the city because it didn’t rain in her village for two years. All crops dried up in fields and soon there was very little food to eat. Her father fell sick. There was no money for his medicine and no food for them. Shanti and her siblings stopped going to the village school. But Shanti’s uncle and aunt who lived in a big city were very kind. They agreed to keep Shanti with them and promised to send her to the school. Shanti’s mother agreed and sent shanti with them. Shanti came to the city. The city was huge and dirty. There were lots of houses and very few trees. When she arrived at her new house, her experience from the first week was quiet unpleasant. She had to carry water in a bucket from the tap on the street. She had to stand in long lines to fill the buckets. When she got late, her uncle scolded her. But Shanti knew she was very lucky. She had enough food to eat here. And she loved the baby, Mamta. She worked very hard and always wondered if she could go the school. When she asked her aunt, she said, “There’s no time to go to school. Maybe next year when Mamta is older”. Shanti was disappointed but she never lost hope. Shanti tried to do things nicely but sometimes she made mistakes. Then her uncle and aunt got angry. When they got angry, Shanti got frightened. Her uncle’s voice became as loud as thunder and her aunt’s face became as sharp as a knife. One day her aunt scolded her a lot she thought of running away but she had no money for the bus ticket. What has she to do? She sat under a tree to think. She leaned against the trunk and closed her eyes. Don’t cry, Shanti! You are a clever girl. Shanti looked around but there was no one there. It couldn’t be the tree! Trees couldn’t speak. “Shanti, if you weren’t there what would your uncle and aunt do? Who would help them? And if you don’t help them, how would you go to school?” someone said again. She looked around again. Maybe some trees can speak, she thought. She wiped her tears and went back. After whenever she finished her work, she went to sit under the tree. She felt calm when she sat under the tree. Sometimes, she would carry an old-school book and flip through the pages. She would try and read out the lines to the tree. The tree always said nice things to her. Shanti knew she was not alone. She had a friend, here in the big city. She didn’t feel so scared anymore. One morning, Shanti got up early and made tea. She poured it in two glasses and took into her uncle and aunt’s room. She tried to enter the room quietly but the door made sound. The baby, Mamta, got up and began to cry. Her uncle and aunt started yelling at her and she rushed to bring a biscuit for Mamta. She took the biscuit and put it in Mamta’s hand. Mamta took the biscuit in her mouth and smiled at Shanti. Shanti wanted to play with the baby but there was no time to play right now. She had to fetch the water, make breakfast, and cut the vegetables and other chores. Shanti ran here and there trying her best to finish up the work. She could hear her aunt coming” hurry, hurry!” her aunt said.”Your uncle has to have his breakfast. You have to make his lunch. He is getting late for work, Shanti. Why are you so slow, you lazy girl!” Shanti started working even faster. She accidentally dropped an expensive plate! CRASH! Shanti heard the plate fall. And Shanti was so afraid that she ran. She ran out of the door, out to the street. Her aunt was really angry. She might even slap Shanti. Where could she go? Where should she hide? She ran to her friend. She cried for help. And then, the tree’s broad brown trunk opened up. “Get inside”, it said. There was a big hollow space inside the trunk. Shanti ran and hid there. Soon, her aunt started to worry about her. She couldn’t find her anywhere. But her aunt could never find her. It was dark and cozy inside the tree. Shanti curled up and slept. Slept and slept till she heard Mamta crying. Her aunt was trying to make Mamta quiet but she wouldn’t be quiet. It was evening already! What was Shanti going to do? She would just stay inside the tree, safe from everyone who shouted at her and scolded her. Mamta was crying even louder now Her uncle and aunt realized that if only Shanti were here, everything would be fine. They wondered where she had gone. “You scold her too much”, her uncle said. ”What will we tell her parents? We’ll be in trouble!”.” I won’t scold her anymore, I promise!” her uncle cried. “If only she’d come back, I will never scold her again’. Shanti smiled. Should she go back? It was so much nicer inside the tree. But Mamta was still crying. Shanti knew why the baby was crying. She was waiting for Shanti to come play with her. Should she go? Suddenly, the tree spoke again,”You can go if you want” it whispered. ”But you can come back whenever you want to”. Shanti wanted to stay in but she couldn’t see Mamta crying. She wanted to help her. So, she went back to her house. She walked to the house slowly and rang the bell. Her uncle opened the door. “Shanti? Where were you? He asked.”Visiting a friend”, she said. “I was tired and… I broke a plate by mistake. I was afraid uncle would scold me”. She explained. “Poor girl gets tired working all the time. She’s just a child. So what if she broke a plate? It can happen to anyone “, said her aunt and her uncle agreed. Her aunt offered to make tea for her and cook the dinner while Shanti played with Mamta. Her uncle even agreed to send her to school. They finally realized how important Shanti was to them. Shanti looked through the window at her friend, the tree. She smiled and didn’t say anything. Now, she would never be scared of anyone again. She had found a safe place which would always be there for her. Moral: A true friend is always the one who help you through your hard times and motivate you to overcome your fears.

title: The Story of Brahmapur
text: Brahmapur and My quality Education Brahmapur, my hometown......I know you might not have heard the name before. It is a small city in the state which is only known for Oddisi, temples like Jagannath Puri, it's hockey players or IIT Bhubaneshwar but never for Brahmapur. I was a kid who had although accepted this fact but somehow I achieved my goal sometime later. I hope this story of two chapters will help you understand me and the journey of a student from a small city. Chapter 1 - The part where I go to Delhi I am Priyabrata Nayak, a kid from a rich family that tried to get out of the shadow of my father and his great and successful business in the textile industry. To tell the truth about my family, my father, is an orthodox but honest, loving, successful, and hardworking person. My mother, on other hand, is sometimes strict but always shields me when anyone even tries to threaten me and loves me more than anyone. At last, comes my baby sister, the most annoying person but also my best friend and always a taker of my side. I am going to my hometown by train right now. Since I am getting bored, let me tell you the story of how I became an employee of Ubisoft in the first place even though I did my class tenth in a local school and only got to Delhi to get a quality education when I was 16 years old. It all started when I heard that Adarsh & Aragyajeet Bhaiya, the Prodigal sons of our town had revisited. They were my idols as they were Software engineers working for Ubisoft and lived in California but even after that, They would visit all of us and their parents once in a year (at least) excluding holidays. But this time I got a chance to talk to them and explore the career option that I always wanted to have. But after they went I decided that I was gonna have a discussion with my father about it. The next Sunday I told my father that I need to have a discussion about this topic. Although when I asked him about it in the evening he told me to sit down and the family got at the dining table so that everyone could listen and participate. When I told him that I want to discuss the career options that I really wanted to have. The first thing he told me was that it was a stupid idea. I was going to complete my matriculation at that local school because he could ask me to accept his offer, I told him that I knew that he wishes what is best for me but the advantages of having a chance at quality Education better infrastructure, qualified teachers, and also If I do good, placement opportunities too! was far outweighing the promise of taking over the business and preserve my father's legacy. He, on the other hand, didn't like that and thought he had done all the hard work to set up the business so that we got it easy and offer I complete my education in Brahmapur, I would own the shop after training for some time under his supervision. But what I wanted was to be a software Engineer and an IITian in an MNC. At last, my loving father made me a deal first I give my State Board's Exam and if I get above 95%, he will pay for my trip through flight and also get me into the best school there. Although he was proud of me, even though he knew I wasn't that good but to his shock, I accepted. I guess all I had to do was do whatever it takes to get amazing marks. The next day I went to see my Guide through all this and my favorite teacher and the first thing he said was "That's All He Wants?!" Chapter 2 - The part where I am in Delhi!! After 3 months of severe practice I got exact 94.5% in the state boards and the disappointment on my face was immeasurable. I went to my father crying saying that I couldn't do it and he was right. I am a stupid kid who cant do anything. But the reaction of my father surprised me to a new level. He said that "Beta Stop Crying! And go pack your bags or how will you get ready for you for your flight?" He continued" I am proud of you! this is nothing in front of the hard work you did! Not having any entertainment but only studying all day! That is enough to make me happy and I have lost!" I Hugged him veery hard and said that I loved him smiling from one side to the other side. I got ready and reached the airport with Aragyajeet Bhaiya! Yes! He told me that he was more than happy to work from his home in Delhi and so was his company and he understood what I wanted and he understood my ambition. When we reached there to his house I understood that he wasn't joking when he told that he was a bit successful as he had the most luxurious house I had ever seen and also had an Audi! I was enrolled in the best school after smashing their admission test! Then the days of DOOM began, when I was in Odisha, I rarely spoke English and hindi but that was all they spoke and hence, I was an outcast.. After a few weeks of leg pulling and bullying by my classmates, my class teacher approached me and told me that she wanted to help me improve my communication skills and no one will then make fun of me! I thanked her and that's how my luck shined! After that day I gave my best in my studies but also had fun in between as now, nothing was to come between me and my success. Then, I got to know about the examination on a national level for PCM Students where If I won not only would I get money as a Scholarship but also congratulation from the Prime Minister! That was my way to prove that my father's investment in me was not for nothing. I took the help of my school teachers and bhaiya and did everything in my power to get the felicitation because I didn't want it to go like my state boards. So, instead of hard work this time I did smart work. I made notes on every topic and did practice from different reference books for my preparation and solved model papers and previous year's question papers. I did everything I could and revised till the last moment but this time I took a deep breath and used time management to complete my paper and get time to revise and... I passed! and not just passed I did it with flying colors! I was a part of the group of students who were felicitated by our honorable prime minister in front of my whole family and that was the day my father told me that he was proud of me and for the first time he loved the fact that I proved him wrong! and that shaped my confidence to a huge extent and the support of my parents brought me where I am today! Anyways I got to go meet my parents as I have reached Behrampur or Brahmapur. Bye!
author: Abhyudaya Kumar

title: Charlie and the boy
text: One day, on the way home from school, a boy finds a stray dog. He feeds the dog and stares at it, thinking they can become great friends. He finally decides to give it a name, "Charlie". After spending lots of time together with Charlie, he decides to bring him home. Little did he know that his parents wouldn't approve of Charlie's arrival. Charlie had been sent out from the house when the boy was at school. The poor dog had become very upset and frightened. The boy's parents had tried to convince him that they couldn't keep a pet. However this didn't stop the boy and Charlie's destined meet. On another day back from school, the boy spots Charlie and they reunite. Both of them are incredibly happy to see each other again. The boy keeps the dog safe in a little shelter where he feeds it and plays every day before and after school. Charlie and the boy form a strong bond of affection and care towards each other. They play together everyday until the sun entirely sets.
author: NIKHITA B
illustrator: Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Sahil Shaikh; Sarthak Sinha

title: The sister act
text: Only 5 minutes till the curtains open………..Only 5 minutes till I’ll fulfil my sisters dream. I think back to what brought me here, I remember it as clear as day. A rooftop,A green leotard, a slip and a scream. 10 months ago My twin sister lena and I were sitting on our rooftop enjoying the view of Paris. She was wearing her green leotard. Lena loved showing of her ballet and her favourite place to do it was the rooftop. I told her to be careful but she brushed it off saying saying “oh! Daphne, Don’t worry I know what I’m doing! Despite her reassurance i was always concerned. Ballet was in our blood, No matter whether your a girl or boy, you had to learn ballet.I was never one of those graceful girls.I was someone whom people would call a 'tomboy'. My mother always said that even if Lena and I were identical she could easily tell us apart. "Daphne! Stop zoning out! look, I've been practising my tour jete" "lena you know this is a rooftop, you shouldn't be doing jetes over here" I tried to warn her. She just gave me a look and proceeded to show me. She took a leap, for a second I though that she might nail it, but it only lasted for a second Everything was happening so fast, Her twirl in the air, she was about to land but, her foot slipped! In the second where she realised what was happening to her, her eyes filled with horror, She reached out for my hand but couldn't reach it…….My heart was thundering inside me as I watched my twin fall. Her scream still rings inside my ears. I rushed down the stairs as fast as I could. Why were mother and father never home when I needed them? I knew nothing serious would happen to Lena as our house wasn't that high but my worry did not decrease. Lena was in tears when I reached. Clutching her leg her wails echoed. Hearing lena cry, our kind neighbour Mrs Duval came running. Panic written all over her face. She called the ambulance and our parents as fast as she could. Luckily soon we could here the ambulance. The doctors helped Lena in and drove as fast as they could. Lena was unconscious from the pain. My face was covered in sweat,I never had thought that such a situation would come. Then it struck me, Lena was supposed to perform at the Opera garnier on 10 months. Her whole dream and future depended on it. I hope she still could. When we reached the hospital, I saw that mother and father were there. Lena was taken into a hospital room for checkups. I had to wait outside. One hour, Two hours, I still didn't know what was going on inside. Pacing around, a thousand thoughts ran inside my head. My eyes were unfocused and I was occasionally bumping into people. The nurses were giving me pitiful looks, but I paid no attention to them. I just wanted to see my sister Almost an eternity later the doctor called me. Lena was on the bed. I sat beside her. I was about to say something when the doctor came in. He had a smile on his face, He said "The fall luckily wasn't from a height, so Lena only has a broken leg. its a bad injury, but nothing life threatening". Our whole family let out a sight of relief. Lena scrunched her brow and said "but when will it get better?" The doctor casually replied " a year at least". Lena's face grew pale, I understood her, She had a performance in 10 months, A performance she definitely couldn't miss. "But I have a performance" The doctor just gave her a pitiful look, indicating she can't perform. After the doctor left Lena burst into tears. The whole family consoling her. Thats when I had an idea. "Lena what if…..I pretended to be you and perform" My mother gave me a confused look. But Lena understood. "yes! Daphne, that's an amazing idea, merci!, you can do the show pretending to be me as we are identical! Until then I will pretend to be you wearing all those clothes and stuff, Merci! Daphne you are the best sister ever! I slightly nod my head still unsure of the idea, But the look of glee on Lena's face made all the hesitation go away, from tomorrow I was going to be Lena and fulfil her dream. Present day Yes that's exactly how I got here, I remember how I had to go to her practices and act all charming….many nights I used to think that what am I doing. But the thought of lena happy kept me going. It was a nightmare but, for Lena I did it. The sudden light brought me back from my flashback. The show was going to start. I still had a few minutes if I wanted to back out…..But Lena's face flashed through my mind. It stopped me from moving. The curtains finally rise. This is it, its time for Lena to dazzle.
author: JIYA PATEL
illustrator: Jesse  Breytenbach; Sadhna Prasad; Simóne van der Spuy; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: Nekvarna Sharma
text: Max and Mini dreamt of becoming space explorers. They loved space and everything about it. They would stay in the library after school reading books about planets and outer space. They were fascinated by how mysterious it is. On their way home, max and mini saw a spaceship in the window of a shop. It was very attrctive. They went inside the shop to see its price. It was too expensive. They sum up their money together but it still wasn’t enough. They left the store dejected and disappointed. Max suddenly realized that his birthday was about to come. He decided to ask their parents to buy the spaceship as the gift for the birthday. They both started running towards home. They were eager to tell their parents about the spaceship. When they reached home, they hugged their mother who was setting up the table for dinner. Their mom was curious to know what they were thrilled about. So, Max told about what he wanted for his birthday. Max was disheartened and dispirited and he ran back to his room. Mini had just gotten up and about to make her way to the living room when Max ran past her. He slammed their bedroom door and locked it. Mini got to the living room and saw the spaceship. She saw their dad beside it, bent down on knees with his head down and their dad said, “Sorry.” Mini didn’t want her brother and father to be sad. She looked at the cardboard spaceship their dad had made and got an idea. Mom, dad and Mini got to work. Mice started to dance in Max’s stomach. He didn’t had breakfast and now he was hungry. He got out of bed and opened the door. Mini was by the door with the cardboard spaceship their dad had made. She placed it in front of him and asked him, “Are you ready?” “For what?” he asked. “For our mission,” she said. “Mission?” he said. “Yes. We have a mission. Come on,” she said. Mini got on the cardboard spaceship but left space for Max. Seeing excitement on Mini’s face, he got on the spaceship. Then he heard his dad’s voice. “This is mission control. Are we ready for take of?” their dad said. Mini answered, “Mission control. We are ready for take-off.” Their dad came in the room and positioned himself behind the spaceship. He then started making the sound of the spaceship during lift off and pushed the cardboard spaceship slowly. When they came out of the room, Max was surprised at what he saw. There were many stars dangling from the ceiling. There were moons and planets too. He felt like he was in outer space. Then there mom stated walking towards them holding gray rocks made out of cardboards on a string. “Asteroids approaching,” Mini said. “On it.” Max said. Max shifted his body from left to right trying to maneuver the spaceship away from the asteroids. Their dad steered the spaceship wherever Max shifted toward. After successfully evading all the asteroids, they stopped at the dinner table. On the table, there was a label that said “Best restaurant in Jupiter.” Max and mini got out of the space ship. They walked towards the table as if there was no gravity and bounced around. After they ate, they got back on their spaceship. They spent all day on it, riding across the unknown depths of the space, exploring and unveiling the mysteries of space. They enjoyed letting their imaginations run wild. ﻿ The day eventually came to an end and it was time for bed. Before that, max called out to his dad. With smile on his face, he said, “That was the most precious gift and you are the best dad ever. I love you dad.” Max hugged his dad. His dad ruffled his hair and said that he was glad max liked it. After that, everyone went to bed.
author: Nekvarna  Sharma
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Adrija Ghosh; Aindri C; Lavanya Karthik; Partho Sengupta; Phan Thành  Đạt; Shreeya Wagh; Somesh Kumar; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Steven McKimmie; Vidyun Sabhaney

title: Questions
text: This is the story of a young girl who had run away from home, trying to matter, but ends up finding an answer to a great question. While longing for the endless journey to end, looking out of the window, Elina recalled her actions. She had run away from home, because….. even she did not know the answer to this question, maybe she ran away because she did not feel that she belonged back there at home, or maybe she felt that she was held captive there, she did not know. After ten hours, which almost felt endless, the train stopped at a station. Elina looked out of her window, and realized that she had reached a destination. Getting out of the train, Elina counted the little money she was left with, and gave a sigh of relief. She booked an inn with the little money she had. Lying on the bed of the inn, she once again thought about her actions, and once again, she did not know the answer, and then she fell asleep. But she never woke up! She found herself in a deep dark world. Nothing seemed to be visible in that sinister world, it was covered with a carpet of darkness. She muttered to herself, “Where am I?” and to her surprise, a voice answered, “You are in a place where nobody matters, everybody is a no one.” “But I do not even matter in real life, so what’s new?” asked Elina. “Actually you did matter in the realm of mortals, you just did not know it, you did not choose to believe that you had importance. But now you are trapped here forever. Nobody is here to help you.” “Can’t anyone save me?” “There is only one, the one which is arrogant, pure hearted, and has captivated only love in its heart.” “That thing is nearly impossible to exist nowadays!”, said Elina, starting to lose hope. “Yes, and while you are here, your body is rotting, and after an year of rotting, it will be ready!” “Ready for what?” “Ready to be my chariot to world domination!” After days of chitchat with that voice, a wonderful thing happened! A little ray of hope, woke Elina up! It was a little boy, half the age of Elina. Though the boy looked poor, he was full of enthusiasm. He wore a long pink shirt and a torn pant with a dirty pair of shoes. His blue eyes lit up and his hair swayed as he moved closer to Elina, he sat down beside her and asked, “Elder sister, why are you sleeping at the peak of the day?” “Who are you? What are you doing here?” asked Elina “I am nobody, I’m just trying to run away from my dumb life. I have no parents, no siblings, no one to love or hate me” “You are not no one!” “Yes I am! I don’t have any importance to anyone!” this was the line that struck Elina’s heart and made her realize the answer to her actions. She said, “You do matter, you just don’t know it.” “To whom?” “You matter to me! You are my saviour after all.” “Really?” “Yes!” saying this Elina picked up her phone and dialed, nine-three-eight-four. “Hello….” “Who is this?” said the voice from the other side. “It is Elina, Ma!….” there was a little pause, and then a reply came “Elina! is this really you?!” “Yes ma it’s me.” “Where have you been?” It had been three days since Elina had gone missing. “Ma, I have got to know the real meaning of life!” “We have been worried like hell, where are you?” “I am on my way back home, Ma, and is it okay if I bring a little box of joy with me?” then she hung up the phone. kissing the little boy on the forehead, she said “You are my brother from now on. Yes, you are my little brother!” Elina got to know the real meaning of life, that life is not at all about fame, pride, honour and money. It is more about the importance that you have in someone else’s life. No matter how small or big that importance is in other person’s life, if you have it, you will continue to live your life to the fullest.
author: Rian Sharma
illustrator: B G Gujjarappa; Jagruti M; Joanna Davala; Joe Werna; Kashmira Sarode; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Mary Marble; Rohit Kelkar

title: Getting Ready for School
text: Hi! I am Appu. This is my elder sister Ammu. Every morning, I wake up when my father wakes me. I then go and wake up my sister. We then brush our teeth, do Yoga, bathe and pray to God. After our prayers it is our breakfast time! We toast the bread for breakfast all by ourselves. It is very simple. Just put the bread inside the toaster and switch it on. When it's ready, the timer goes 'Ting!' the bread pops out. It pops directly onto our plates. We then spread butter or jam and enjoy it! After breakfast, we read the newspaper. Meanwhile, our mother is busy packing our lunch and snack boxes with healthy, yummy food. At 8 AM, we wear our socks and shoes. Sometimes, my sister helps me to wear my socks, but most of the times, I do it on my own. After wearing our footwear, we pick our bags, lunch bag and off we go to school! What are the things you do before going to school? Who helps you get ready? What do you do after coming back from school? Enlist the tasks you do after coming home from school.
author: Ira Periyavallur (aka Indira VMD)
illustrator: Adithi Mahankali; Ananya; Ananya Dua; Anupama Ajinkya Apte; Google India; Hayley  Alonzo; Jaikar Marur; Sujay Karthik Sathiskumar; Uddesh Gadge; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: A crack in my friendship.
text: Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Muskan and Deepali, living in same city, studying in same school. They were in class 7 th at that time. They both were supportive with each other’s nature. Muskan has a diary in which she used to write special, sad or any type of event took place in her day. Muskan used to call deepali as deepu. Once they went to park. There, they met a girl named Anamika studying in their school but having different sections. Deepali liked her description, she started spending time with her. Muskan did not liked happening this. She went to Deepali and said, “Let’s read novels. I’m getting bored.” Deepali replied harshly, “But I and Anamika are already reading and yes if you want to read, read it alone.” Muskan said [almost in condition of crying but was trying to control], Okay, okay Deepu.” Deepali, “from onwards don’t call me deepu as Anamika wants.” “ what? Are you certain about what you are speaking about” Muskan replied angrily. “ Yes I am” said deepali. Muskan came home and wrote in her diary. Dear diary, Do you know, today Deepu, [erased deepu and wrote deepali] sorry deepali talked so rudely to me that I was about to cry but I controlled.” I don’t know what happened why she started hating me. She said me not to call her deepu. Next day, in class. Muskan was sitting alone. In canteen Muskan was eating alone. In canteen muskan was eating alone. Same continued for 17 years, till the time she made no friend. Muskan has decided her carrier of CA. After some days someone called her and informed that Deepali has cancer and for her treatment we need 10 lakh. After a year, Deepali was all right. She asked Anamika, “ who paid for my treatment”. Anamika was about to say. Deepali said, “ wait,wait.” She saw someone talking to, “ will you help me with 8 lakh as I paid 10 lakhs for Deepali’s treatment.” “no muskan I can’t. Hearing this, deepali came running and hugged muskan. How rude, this was my love towards friendships. Now stop crying or else I will start crying.” Anamika come here, from deepali’s side I will say sorry to you. Please forgive us.” Why are you saying sorry, mistake is done by me I should sorry. Heartly sorry muskan and deepali.” Its okay. And from now no sorry and no thank you in friendship. Deepali said, and muskan please call me deepu only. Dear Diary, Do you know today my friendship took a new path? I Accepted anamika and made her friend. I got my deepali, oh! Deepu back. I am very happy. Thank god for saving my deepu. -By Vedika Sharma
author: B-0070-17 VEDIKA

title: Oogly's Flight
text: On the borders of a rainforest, in the cavity of a huge Kapok tree, lived a happy owl couple, Mr and Mrs Googly. In their nest, they had 8 eggs. The Googlies were eagerly waiting for their eggs to hatch. The first time parents, had a three week plan to train their children on how to be free, and safe in the wild. After a long wait of 32 days, the owlets started to crack out of the eggs one by one. The Googlies' hearts skipped a beat and were filled with joy. It was wonderful to watch the cute owlets slowly unfurling their fresh little wings, opening their tiny eyes, and stretching their puny bodies. Their mini hoots sounded like little squeaks. The Googlies' were delighted and started singing their first song for their owlets. Hoot hoot hoot! Googlies hoot Googlies hoot Surrounds the woods! Hoot hoot hooooot! Thus singing, the happy Googlies danced around the little owlets. Soon the little owlets felt hungry. They opened their tiny beaks towards their mama. With deep love and warmth, she dropped the freshly collected worms to each and every one of her owlets. As the night started, Mr. Googly instructed the owlets to move out into the forest. “Listen and follow the buzz of the insects and catch them. Insects are tasty, they are crunchy and munchy. Rats are yummy and will fill your tummy. Fish in the pond of the dense forest is the delicacy. I wish you get to relish the fish in the pond." Fly all around, learn all the owly skills and lets get ready for the talent show on the moon lit night. Little owlets were excited and wanted to learn everything and show their parents their owly skills. All the owlets moved, except Oogly. The little one Oogly stepped out of the nest. It was dark. Oogly was scared. He slowly moved towards that fallen old tree trunk nearby and roosted on. The darkness of the woods, the buzz of the insects and the chirps of the crickets terrified him. He closed his eyes and his ears with his feathers and stood there stunned. From that night it was Oogly’s routine to roost on the fallen tree trunk, munch on the worms and stare at the star lit sky. Every morning when the other owlets spoke about the tasty insects, yummy rats and delicious fish, flying high and gliding in the air, Oogly had nothing to say except roosting and eating the worms. Mama observed Oogly but she trusted nature. She knew that nature would help him learn everything that he needs to be a good owl. Days passed by and Oogly was fed up with his routine. He wanted to fly high, glide, eat rats and fish. One night, Oogly made up his mind to move farther away into the deep dark woods to find tasty meals. He decided to ask the stars for help as they always made him feel better Oogly stood on the tree trunk and closed his eyes for sometime. Slowly he turned towards the sky and opened his eyes. He couldn't see any of the stars. Oogly started crying. There was a wind and the wind cleared the clouds. Oogly could see one star and asked for help. To his surprise, the star approached him. Oogly couldn’t move his eyes off the approaching star, right from the skies through the canopy of the tall trees. The star came near Oogly. Oogly exclaimed "Star" and unfurled his feathers to reach the star. But the star spoke. “Hey Oogly, I am not a star. I am a firefly. My name is Flashy. Do you want to fly with me?” Oogly nodded as he knew that the stars sent flashy for his help. Oogly and Flashy became good friends. They flew around the forest, telling tales to each other. From Flying to gliding to catching the insects to scooping the rats and to perching the fish. Oogly learnt everything and sharpened his owly skills. With flashy around, Oogly enjoyed the wilderness of the night time. And together, they did this every night until the Sun began to show his light. Finally on the moonlit night, Googly’s parliament gathered around the lake in the dense forest. Mr. Googly inaugurated the talent show. While every owlet showed their flying, gliding and hunting skills, mama was worried for Oogly. And it was Ooglies turn. Oogly was quite nervous. He looked at the stars up in the sky and smiled. He found flashy in front of him. Oogly soared up high to a great altitude. He waved at the stars to show his gratitude. He swished and swooshed like the clouds in the sky. He looked down the ground and spotted some mice. He swooped swiftly and scooped one out. He moved around the lake and skimmed the water to grabbed a big fish with a great flair. He took a bow in front of his parents And surprised everyone. Watching this spectacular sight, mama felt overwhelmed and was delighted. She thanked nature. Googlies sang their song and danced again. Oogly joined them with great zest as never before. Hoot hoot hoot Googlies hoot! Googlies hoot Surrounds the woods Hoot Hoot Hoooooot!! When all the owls moved to the different areas of the forest, all alone, Oogly decided to live in the Kapok tree along with the stars and with Flashy’s family.
author: Sridevi Srinivasan

title: The Lazy Crocodile
text: The lazy crocodile Once there was a lazy crocodile named Snappy. He was the laziest crocodile in the entire jungle. Once he sat near a pond admiring himself in the pond. A monkey said to Snappy ‘why are you so lazy. ‘ I am not lazy I eat and sleep.’ The monkey went away. Stupid monkey thought Snappy. The monkey called a meeting with all the other animals to make Snappy less lazy. ‘Why don’t we talk to him. ‘Said the tiger. ’ Great idea.’ Everyone said. First it was the zebra’s turn but Snappy did not listen. Same happened to the other animals. At last it was the rabbit’s turn. ‘Not a hope ‘declared the giraffe. ‘ What will you do ‘ said the monkey. The rabbit went to Snappy and said ‘Are you not ashamed ‘ said the rabbit ‘Why shall I be’ said snappy.’ ‘As you are so lazy ‘ said the rabbit. Snappy did feel very ashamed and from that day on he was never lazy
author: Yash Verma
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Anarya .; Gerhard Van Wyk; Hélder de  Paz Alexandre; Joanna Davala; Priya Kuriyan; Raju Babu Shakya

title: The Best Gift
text: My life is miserable. My only job is to sit still and look cute. Even if I wanted to do more, which make no mistake I certainly do, I am not able to. It is quite a restrictive and confining life. I suppose the atmosphere of the store helped. It looked as if it was right out of a fairytale; dim but magical. The books were along the left wall in old wooden book shelves. Twinkling lights were draped on the shelfs to draw away attention from the moss growing in the shelves. To the right was the entrance with a glass door with a bell hanging over it. While unnecessary, the bell certainly added an element of humbleness to the store. Right in the center, in front of my shelf was the cash register. I was located at the very back of the store with a perfect view of everything, which came in handy because I couldn’t move a limb nor turn my head to adjust my field of view. I hear the bell ring and think nothing of it. It was just another customer, just another party-goer looking for a last minute gift or a child whining for a toy. Obviously, everything was going to happen like it always does. The buyer enters, either walking right past me or gives me a glance before dismissing me, and then leaves a few minutes later with a new possession. The man in a suit was surely going to do the same. Although, this new customer did look different than the rest. Other than the fact that the oddball was wearing formal attire at a gift shop, he also looked incredibly tired like he could go into hibernation in a moment's notice. The man took his time looking around but eventually he picked up a musical box and headed for the cashier. “That’ll be 350 rupees; how will you be paying?” The man suddenly became stiff. “I apologize, my budget is a mere 100 rupees.” The cashier pointed towards my shelf. “Sir, you can find items in that price range towards the back.” I froze- well not like I was very active either way; my hands were quite literally sewn to my body, but you get the point. The dapper man walked towards the back of the store and took a look around before his eyes landed on me. “Well, they do say a room without a teddy bear is like a face without a smile.” he said out loud, trying to convince himself to purchase me. He picked me up and walked towards the cashier. He paid a handsome sum of 75 rupees and stared at me while the cashier was printing the bill. Now, maybe I wasn’t the best looking teddy in all the world, but gosh this man looked incredibly displeased with me. His gaze on me was interrupted by the cashier handing him the bill. The man in the suit took me out of the store and I heard the bell ring for the last time. I saw the sky for the first time when the man carried me out of the store. I felt a sensory overload. The sky was the most beautiful shade of blue, sprayed randomly with clouds. The trees out here are nothing compared to what I’ve seen in books at the store. And the people were bustling around, every single one in a hurry to get from one place to another. The man took me into a metal vessel, which I later found out is called a “car”. There was a black seat inside the metal vessel; the man sat down and pulled a thick black rope around himself before putting me inside a bag. Everything went dark. The next thing I knew I was being pulled out of the bag by an old woman. She looked fragile and thin, but do not let that fool you, she had quite the strong grip! “Is this all?” the woman asked, annoyed. “Yes, this was all I could get.” the man replied. “Well did you at least buy wrapping paper?” asked the woman, with an emphasis on ‘at least’. The man sighed, “No, I seemed to have forgotten.” “Lovely.” the woman said sarcastically, “My granddaughter is receiving a present wrapped in newspaper for her 6th birthday!” “I’m trying my best mom!” the man groaned. “Forget it!” snapped the woman before walking off, holding my neck firmly. I was laid on a table while the woman walked off. A few moments later she walked back with scissors and newspaper. She mumbled something under her breath while cutting up the newspaper. She wrapped me up and from then on I had to solely rely on my sense of hearing. I was having a tough time focusing on the sounds, as there were too many of them. I could hear the woman in the distance yelling to talk to the man against the background of clanging dishes. The man, in turn, screamed back his replies out of spite. To top it all off, the ticking and tocking of the clock made me lose my mind! There was an immense amount of tooting horns outside of the house, which I still could not understand. I’ve heard the same sounds before during my time at the store; they came from the metal vessels on the road. Sometimes, the ear-piercing hoots were also accompanied with insults by the humans on the metal vessels. Everything went quiet. To be frank, I was startled. I had gotten so used to the ruckus that silence was now disturbing to me. The man and woman started whispering and shushing each other saying, “Quite down! The school bus is pulling up, she’s here!” I heard the doorbell ring and the man and woman were walking around in a panic, the floorboard creaking and croaking wherever they walked. The man answered the door and hollered in an enthusiastic voice, “Welcome! How was your day? Tell me everything! The voice that replied was soft and sweet, “Everything went well! I passed out all the chocolates, like you said.” “Don't worry,” the man assured her, “There are some chocolates in the fridge for you as well.” The little girl giggled. Then, the man told her to go upstairs and change out of her uniform. Time passed, and I could hear the tip-tap of shoes on the stairs. It seems the girl had returned downstairs to continue celebrating her birthday. Praises were sung as the girl walked down the stairs. The man cheered for her as if he were her biggest fan and was dying to get an autograph. Once the applause had stopped I heard the woman howl “Come! Let’s cut the cake.” The groundbreaking party– which consisted of only three people– started. From what I could hear, it was a typical celebration. There was a painful 2 minutes of un-harmonious singing of ‘Happy Birthday’, followed by hurrahs, then the cake cutting, and more applause– you get the drill. With the birthday bash going on, I sat wrapped in newspaper pondering when I would see light again. As though some celestial being was reading my thoughts, I heard footsteps coming towards me. “Time for presents!” yelled the woman. The little girl was called towards the dining area where I was situated. I felt someone grab me and lift me up. “I know it's not much,” the man said in a doleful tone, “but I hope you like it.” The newspaper around me was torn off and staring down at me were wide eyes. I compared the girl I pictured in my head to the one holding me now. The little girl had dirty blonde hair; she was wearing a pink dress with ruffles and puff sleeves and she was sporting a toy crown bejeweled with plastic gems. The girl looked at me, then her father. She thought long and hard. A tangible tension arised in the room. The girl started grinning from ear to ear, shooting the tension away. “I love it!” the girl exclaimed as she wrapped her arms around me in a hug. Tugged beneath the arms of the child, I felt good. What do the humans say? “Feeling warm inside”? At that moment, I felt warm inside. The girl promised to take good care of me. On the spot, she planned all our playdates. Tea parties, sleepovers, scary stories, building at-home tents, playing dress-up, and the list went on. It seemed as though our schedule would be packed! The girl exclaimed with her whole heart, “This is the best gift ever!” If I could talk, I would tell her the same. Finally being part of a family was the best gift ever.
author: Dhiya Sharmila

title: The Run
text: In ancient times, there was a village called Amerda. In that village the rate of illiteracy is more. Only 3 to 15 members will go to school. These people have to walk upto 10 km. In them there are two friends whose names are Ramu and Krishna. Ramu and Krishna are good runners. Ramu is so passionate about athletic career and practices for 7-8 hours but Krishna didn’t practice for more time. As they were practicing for their career, the time has come “National Sports Event” in which one runner is selected from each state. Ramu and Krishna won all the rounds. This time it is a hard time because in the final selection it between Ramu and Krishna. Everyone thought Ramu will win but Krishna won the race. At that moment Ramu lost himself and went into depression. Ramu didn’t come out from his room for 10 days. One day Krishna went to Ramu’s house and called him but no answer came. Then, he hit the door and shouted that Ramu got scared and came out. Krishna asked “Why are you so depressed?” and Ramu replied “You will say anything because you are the winner.” Then Krishna said “The problem in you is over anxiety because of that you lost the race but, I am not anxious I am happy that you are my opponent.” If a friend wins friends should be happy but not depressed. Isn’t my victory yours. Come lets go and drink a coffee.
author: regalla narasimha
illustrator: Jemma Jose; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Ouk  Ratha; Sunaina  Coelho

title: Cashed In
text: Who could even believe that a trip around the world would take so long," cried Harriet. Josie beamed, "I know! I enjoyed it immensely, although I was so very seasick." Alexandra and Victoria came over to their children, soft smiles on their faces. Alexandra put her hand on her daughter's shoulder and in a near whisper, she said, "Come children, the cook has prepared an absolute feast for you!" Mary jumped excitedly at the thought of food and tripped over her dress in a haste to get to the dining hall. ※ "O-o-oh dear... What misfortune!" Elliot looked at his wife from over the top of his newspaper. Alexandra was staring at the letter in her hands, pale and eyes wide, unfocused. "What is it? I trying to read... honestly." She looked at him motionlessly and finally spoke, "It's... th-the letter... its from Victoria. Elliot, Henry... has gone int-into d-d-d-debt, t-they're going to lose everything." One side of the newspaper fell from his right hand, fluttering in the wind, Alexandra clutched her heart and sat down. "Elliot... please. Lend them money... help the Wilkins, help your friend. Henry needs you." He stared at her, "No." Elliot just said, ever so simply. Alexandra opened and closed her mouth in shock, speechless. Elliot then mumbled that it was late and he was going to turn in. Lying on the bed, he stared at the letter in his hands that he had taken from Alexandra. The date noted was 8 ᵗʰ September, 1854. As he gazed at it without registering what he saw, he pondered on the decision he made. Henry has been my closest friend, is it wrong of me to refuse to lend him money? No... It is my hard earned money, I shouldn't be expected to just give it away. Henry should have been more cautious... the thought of giving Henry Wilkin my money... my precious money... With all this in his head, he soon fell asleep. ※ His two children looked at him, agony on their faces. "Father, give us food, please!" Harriet pleaded him, tears rolling down her colourless cheeks. "I'm hun-gary..." Hugh mumbled, in his toddler voice. Alexandra came to the door of the shack and looked at the children and Elliot. "I couldn't find any food, the dustbins were scoured clean before I arrived," she gasped out. The family looked bedraggled in torn clothes and their unwashed bodies. Harriet fainted from hunger and Hugh cried even more. Then... faces swirled together, voices mixed, Harriet crying for food, Hugh begging for a warm blanket, Alexandra asking for money... ※ Elliot awoke from his nightmare, sweating profusely, he looked at Alexandra, snoring beside him, his shoulders started to shake, he sobbed. ※ "We're here, sire," the coachman announced. Elliot jumped down from the carriage and handed the change to the driver. Flipping the collar of his coat up, against the wind of the harsh Cambridge weather, he walked with a steady gait towards the mansion. The movers had emptied out the house, but the Wilkins were still standing outside, ready to leave. Henry saw him first, smiling ruefully, he said, "We're moving." Elliot swallowed the lump in his throat and started, in a hoarse voice, "Henry, you're my dearest and closest friend, a few days ago, you went into debt, you lost everything, your money, your house... you needed help, but I never understood how drastic it was, I was never poor, I didn't know how it was, I was a coldhearted fool, forgive me, and I, I refused to help you out." " But, " he emphasised, "I have realised my mistake, I've repented, please accept my money and help. You shouldn't have to go live in a filthy old rundown shack!" Henry's sarcastic smile turned into a frosty glare. "I'm not moving to any filthy old rundown shack, I'm simply buying a bigger mansion. I'm rather tired of this place" "But-" "Elliot. A relative of mine, great-aunt Merida passed away last night. Leaving me a huge fortune. I was able to pay back my debts, and get my money back... so I really have no use for your little-too-late-olive-branch. But I have to thank you, because otherwise... how would I have known how selfish and ignorant you are?" With those final words Henry stepped away and got into a carriage with his wife and children, leaving Elliot utterly and completely alone in his heart. His spirit floating in a sea of guilt, loneliness, and misery.

title: A Family
text: Once upon a time, in an apartment lived a family of three- the mother, the father and their son. They had everything they wanted, a good house, a great lifestyle, food to eat, water to drink but one thing that they missed was oneness. The feeling of love and affection towards each other was never seen. Moreover, they were rather renowned for trivial naggings, constant arguments and silly quarrels. They always brawled over daily things like the son wants to see his carton, father wants to see news, mother wants to see the dance show, who will iron the clothes, who will fill-up the water bottles, what to eat and many more … All the members of the family never appreciated other’s achievement neither helped each other as a family, all were only determined to themselves and at most focused on their own work, they had a bad behaviour to each other and always scuffled. Once a new family entered to their apartment during the Kargil War, A Father, Mother and Daughter The Father of the family went to their home, he ringed the bell and the mother opened the door, she said” Hello, The man saw the women and said” Hey! nice to meet you, I’m your new neighbour The mother welcomed him in her house they talked about their surroundings and meanwhile the son and the father arrives they saw the box of sweets in the man’s hand, the son snatched the box briskly, he opened the box and they started fighting again, who will eat the first piece of sweet! The man laughed upon seeing there silly quarrels and said, “Oh! I wish my family was as bonded and loving as yours. Nevertheless I am proud to be a war soldier and I feel blessed to fight on our nation’s border to save lives of many such innocent families. Your smiles motivate me to serve the nation with all honesty and enthusiasm. I am proud to be the soldier of this mother land, although I do miss such quarrels with my family but I am ready to sacrifice my relations to keep safeguarding yours.” Such words of the soldier moved the hearts of the family, they realized how blessed they were to have each other. They understood the true meaning of a family and how important are they to each other. That day, they promised themselves to never fight again and always support and be grateful to each other.
author: Savyansh Tiwari
illustrator: Fahad Faizal; Olivia Fraser; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Savyansh Tiwari; Zainab Tambawalla

title: The 3 Noble Friends
text: Deserted roads, no traffic movement, school & office being closed, entire world working virtually, that was the situation during the pandemic lockdown. People were locked inside their homes. There was silence always spread across on the roads. And in such conditions, there were many reports of wild animals wandering around in various cities. It was as if, humans were locked in a cage and every animal was traveling as though they were the king of not just the jungle but of cities too. One such incidents happened in the Evergreen society of Rampur, that is quite close to the Jim Corbett National Park. There were three friends namely Siya, Dhruv & Krish living in that society. Just like all others, they too were stranded in their homes for weeks. One night while sleeping Siya suddenly woke up with loud barking sound of street dogs in their society. She stood up and went out in the balcony to have a look around. Just then she saw Krish & Dhruv also peeping outside their windows. Siya said, “does anyone of you know why are these dogs barking so furiously?” Krish & Dhruv together said, “No!” None of them could locate any thing around. So, they all went back and dozed off. The next day three of them were standing in their balconies and talking. Just the Dhruv said, “hey! I think I just saw something moving in that deserted cottage of the guard.” They all looked at each other with curiosity & confusion, and decided to secretly sneak out to have a look inside the cottage. They waited for everyone to go for their afternoon nap after lunch. Once everyone was asleep, they signaled each other and sneaked out of their respective homes. Just then they realized that the street dogs again started barking, and this time they saw that the dogs too were looking towards the cottage. The three reached closer to the cottage and Siya said, “let’s be a little careful while opening the door.” As they opened the door, they saw a beautiful brown deer trapped inside that cottage. He looked scared and pale. It was very clear to the three friends that the deer was in danger from the dogs and was hungry as well. Dhruv said, “We have to rescue this poor animal.” Krish agreed and said,’ Off course, we cannot leave him here like this.” Siya rushed back to her house and told her parents all about the deer. And even convinced them to help them save the deer. Siya’s father went along with her to the cottage, where Krish and Dhruv were waiting. All four of them other picked the deer and took him to Siya’s home. As they reached her place, Krish bought loads of dried loose grass and leaves and spread it on the floor so that the deer could sit and feel comfortable. “Let me go and get some green leafy vegetables to feed the animal. And Siya you get a bowl full of water”, said Dhruv. In the meantime, Siya’s father called the jungle authority of the area and told them about the stranded animals. The authority officials asked them to take of the deer until they come and take him off to the jungle. Until then Siya, Krish & Dhruv kept sitting around the deer and made sure that he eats and drinks well. They even tried to play along with the deer by rolling the ball around him, or at times patting him. It was around late evening when the jungle officials came to fetch the deer back into the jungle. The three friends felt a bit emotional, yet they were happy that finally he was going back to the jungle which is his home. The jungle authorities said, “Thank you the three of you for being so patient and kind.” The next day this news was all over the local newspapers and even went viral on the internet. Everyone in and around the society came to know about it and sent their wishes through mails & WhatsApp. Some local news channels even conducted a virtual meeting of the three kids, that was broadcasted on Tv & various sites. Siya, Krish & Dhruv’s school also recognized and applauded their noble deed.
author: Urvi Gupta

title: The sisters
text: Ahh! I couldn’t stop yawning. There is a really big wedding going on to which I was invited. Meanwhile, everyone is making such a noise and as a result, I got bored. So, I kept my headphones on, started listening to a hip-hop song, and found myself singing with it. Suddenly Everyone started to look at me like I have killed someone. I realized that it was time for the prayer. Hey, it’s Shanvi I’m your Awkward best friend. My mom was a famous horse rider and always wanted me and my sister to follow in her footsteps. I also had an older Then sister named Priya who is 2 years older than me and always 2 steps ahead of me. She had perfect grades, and perfect manners also she was the best at horse riding. It was like no one noticed me next to her although mom loved us equally. As much as we were different we are we were inseparable But something that happened afterward changed everything. But I had one thing I didn’t reveal about myself that is I’m really into maths that was the only thing I loved. One day I heard about a maths exhibition that going to be held in our city so, I was excited to go there But I found out that all the tickets were sold so, I went back home sad. The next day when I went to the kitchen I saw a mom holding those tickets to the maths exhibition and I was over the moon and I said to mom oh! Mom, you’re the best. I can’t believe you bought those tickets for me. Then she suddenly said oh darling these are for your sister and her best friend. Just then my sister came to the kitchen. I said to her “ Priya could you please give me the tickets”. Then she said, “Shanvi, I promised my friend that I’ll take her to the maths exhibition so, sorry I can’t give you the tickets”. Then I got angry and said, “So, your choosing your friend over your sister don’t you love me”. Then she said, “I’m sorry I love you but I have to keep up my promise”. Then I got so angry and ran to slap her but I missed her and accidentally broke mom’s most valuable trophy. So, mom scolded me a lot and told me that I had to do the whole household chores for a month. The next day Priya left for the exhibition with her friend as if nothing had happened. I was so angry at both Priya and mom and every second I felt my blood boil and I had to get revenge. I knew Priya was preparing for a scholarship test for months and I also knew that she wanted to pass the scholarship test to get into a good school. When Priya wasn’t at home I sneaked into her room and changed the date of the exam which she wrote in her planner. I knew that the scholarship test is very important to Priya, so I thought that since I changed the test date, she would miss it. Everything was great until after a few days Priya came screaming from her room to the kitchen area and screamed at mom “Mom my tutor called me right now and said that the test was today now It’s too late to take the test all my previous month’s hard work went to waste. Suddenly she looked at me and said, “ Shanvi did you change the exam date in my planner?”. Then I said, “Oh! Now you know how it feels if you lose something you love I felt the same way when I didn’t go to the exhibition”. Then she said, “Shanvi no one cares about your stupid exhibition can’t you understand that you have just ruined my future”. Then I realized that my sister’s life is ruined because of what I had done so, I was guilty But, it was already too late to change anything. All I could do was apologize but Priya had already locked herself in her room. On the other side, My parents kept insisting to Priya join the school that was present in the town in which I was studying. But she said no and told me that she needed some time to get normal after what had happened.. For a few days, Priya mostly stayed in her room and didn’t talk to any of us. Our relationship wasn’t the same anymore, and we barely talked to each other. After a few days, mom and dad forcefully joined Priya at a boarding school. Priya went to a boarding school and I slowly started to feel very lonely. I started to miss the way Priya used to treat me I started feeling miserable and depressed all the time. One day mom saw how I was and said “Shanvi it wasn’t only your mistake because I have never cared about your interests”. I didn’t know you liked maths so much. Hearing that I got calmed a little bit and decided to focus on my grades and study hard. After a few days, I and Priya started communicating by phone. We got a chance to talk once a week and I felt a little better. Although our relationship improved It wasn’t the same as it used to be before. I’m also not sure that Priya had forgiven me but I hope things between us will get better and one day she can forgive me. A few months later I got a free scholarship to the same boarding school Priya was studying. The next day I went to the boarding school. When Priya saw me she said, “Oh! Shanvi why are you here? are mom and dad there with you?”. Then I said, “Hey sis first I would like to apologize for what I have done I am here on a scholarship and we will study together from tomorrow”. Then she said, “I forgave you a long time ago now let me show you around”. Later we found out that we were roommates Then we were full of joy we happily giggled and went to sleep. It had been a few months and I’m still in boarding school life is great and I have learned a lesson to respect my siblings and always be kind to them. Later we found out that we were roommates Then we were full of joy we happily giggled and went to sleep. It had been a few months and I’m still in boarding school life is great and I have learned a lesson to respect my siblings and always be kind to them.
author: Y.shanvi Reddy

title: The Lonely Lion
text: Lion had been lonely his whole life. He was known as a "mini lion", for his small size compared to a regular lion. Lion had always wished to rule the savannah, when others would finally bow down to him instead of bully him for simply being short again. One day, Lion went for a walk when Rabbit came up to him and laughed in his face. "What's the big deal?" Lion roared. Rabbit chuckled, "The mini lion's wearing a crown? Hilarious pretending!" "It's not pretending. Buzz off!" Lion roared as loud as possible, scaring Rabbit away with quiet chuckles. Lion walked up to Crocodile angrily. Crocodile was a bully of every animal in the Savannah, and the forest as well. Crocodile laughed. "Haha! Here's mini again!" Lion couldn't stand it, and roared his largest roar. Crocodile ran off scared of the intense roar. Lion felt proud, and smiled for the first time in years. Lion went into his hut where he saw Fox, his childhood friend. They sat down to have a serious conversation about the other animals constantly bullying Lion. Fox agreed to set up an anti-bully animal group in the Savannah and forest. They called it the Anti-Bullying Group of the Wild. The group grew, fighting against bullies and changing their ways. Lion smiled again. They had even changed the ways of Jackal to make him friendlier. He also decided to join their group. They soon got rid of all of the bullies in the Savannah. The forest only had few left. They thought they would be able to be a national group one day, to eliminate all bullying in wild habitats. It was a dream, a dream they attempted to follow since day one.
author: Panther Feline
