author: Bamboo Blade

title: Keeping a promise
text: Moniri was bored. She had nothing to do. Papa and Mummy were busy watching an old film which they had already watched a million times before. Nothing fun was happening. Suddenly the bell rang loudly "TRING!". Moniri ran to the door to see who was there. "Supri Uncle!" Moniri shouted as a man came in the house. Mummy and Papa did not like Supri Uncle because every time he came he brought an unusual surprise with him. "What did you bring this time, Supri?" Papa said in a blunt voice. "Glad you asked Bhaiya. Today I brought a parrot". Saying this he dropped of the parrot with a cage and shut the door in a hurry. "A parrot! Can we keep him Mummy? Please!" Moniri pleaded her mom. "A parrot is to much work!" Mummy replied. "But Mummy, I am always alone. I have no sibling. This parrot could be my friend!" Moniri said to her mom. Looking at Moniri's plite her mom agreed. "But he shouldn't be seen out of his cage" Mummy said. "Ok!" Moniri replied as she ran to her room. Moniri took the parrot to her room. "Hmmm....I will name you Gred! Because your body is green and your beak is red." Moniri said to the parrot. "Goodnight Gred!" Moniri said as she went to bed. The next day when she woke up she saw that Gred was upset. She went to her mom "Mummy! Why is Gred sad? Do you think he is hungry?" "Hmmm... I would have asked you Tirupali Aunty who is an expert in birds but she is in Kerala for a research trip. Check the fridge for any food that a parrot may eat." Mummy said. Moniri opened the fridge and looked around. All she could see was some dal, an old roti and a slice of cake. Moniri took out the slice of cake. "Mmm..... chocolate cake!" she thought. She took the slice of cake near Gred's mouth. Gred's mouth opened wide and he gulped the chocolate cake. "Moniri, we need to go to the market. Put the bird back and get my red purse" Mummy said. Moniri grabbed Mummy's red purse and kept Gred near the window. "We will be back soon Gred" Moniri said with a pitiful face. As she left the room Gred looked outside. He saw a flock of birds flying freely in the sky. Gred wondered how it must feel to fly freely like the other birds. Oh how Gred wished to be one of them. Then he suddenly heard the door open. Gred suddenly started to flap his wings and tried to escape through the window. Moniri secretly watched as she saw her best friend trying to escape. She felt very upset about this. Moniri started screaming at Gred. "Oh Gred! How could you try and escape from this lovely place. Supri Uncle paid ten rupees for you. Mother will be so upset if she finds out you left. She'd rather sell you in the market for five rupees". Gred just chirped angrily at Moniri in reply. That night when Moniri went to bed she thought "Why would Gred escape?". The next day Moniri went to Gred and said "I thought about it Gred, you just want to fly freely like the other birds. In that case I must release you or I shall remain as your cruel master, but Gred you must promise you won't forget me". Gred nodded. With teary eyes Moniri released Gred from his cage through her window. At first Gred was hesitant to fly, but then he looked back at Moniri with a smile and flapped his wings. Moniri saw Gred as he happily flew in the sky. He joined a flock of birds his kind and flew away. "I will never forget you Gred" Moniri secretly promised to herself with a smile. Soon it was Moniri's birthday. She invited all her friends and had a party. Her parents had brought a chocolate cake for her. As she took a slice she remembered how she had fed Gred a slice of chocolate cake for when he first came. After eating, Moniri took her friends outside to play. As they ran and danced with joy, a variety of birds joined them. Moniri looked at all of them. "Gred must be watching me from somehwere, making sure I don't get into trouble" she thought.
author: Riddhima Banerjee

title: The Deal of a Lifetime
text: Gattu are you again day-dreaming?” This yell from his mother brough Gattu back to his life but why, he was having so much fun with Jaggu. They both were exploring the depths of the Marina Trunch of the Pacific Ocean. Why did he have to return to read this monotonous history book, anyway who cared about Babar and Akbar? “No Mom, I am studying History,” lied Gattu. “You wait, I am coming to see what all you have studied, useless boy.” his mother shouted from the kitchen. This was how a usual weekend, bickering over Gattu’s studies, was spent at the Khanna’s residence. The Khannas were a middle class family, they lived in the Pink Colony in a small flat. Mr Gaurav Khanna was an engineer and worked in a nearby factory. Mrs. Meena Khanna was a teacher at the local school and earned quite well. And then there was Mr. Gattu Khanna, the boss of all, the day dreamer in paradise and his parents worst nightmare. It was not that Gattu didn’t want to study, the case was that he simply couldn’t study. Whenever he opened the book and tried to read the letters, they started to dance in front of his eyes. No matter how much he pleaded with them, they always made fun of his foolishness. So, Gattu was just helpless, but also hopeless when it came to academics. But there was just one thing in the whole world that Gattu loved, Art. He could sit all day and draw the odds and ends, twists and turns, ups and down of anything! He loved painting, splashing colours on a blank white sheet was the best task, it made him feel so alive! All day, all night, he imagined himself being a big artist who painted on large canvases and had huge bottles of all colours of paint. Oh! I almost forgot there was one more thing that Gattu really loved, or no, no, there was a person whom he dearly loved, Jaggu, his imaginary friend. Jaggu was Gattu’s best friend, they both spent hours talking about Art and painting and Jaggu always assured Gattu that one day he would become the best artist in the world. “So, show me your textbook, what have you studied?” “Ma, can you just give me some more time, I am not clear with this topic.” “You say you are not clear with this topic, then what you been doing the whole day?” “Ma, please, I was just trying to understand it but it’s really tough.” “Gattu, at least stop lying to me, I know you were not studying.” “I was Ma, seriously, why do you pester me so much?” “ Because I care for you, dear, if you don’t study, I am afraid you will end up like Ram Kisan, have you seen him, how hard he has to work for a single day’s roti, all because he did not study an alphabet at your age.” “Alright, Alright Ma, I will study hard, I promise.” “Pakka Promise.” “Pakka Promise.” Gattu really tried hard to somehow manage to learn but he always failed, until one night when Jaggu and Gattu were talking, “Gattu, I have an idea, why don’t you try drawing out all the scenes in the history book and then maybe you’ll understand them?” “Oh my God! Why didn’t that ever occur to me?”“ Cause you are not smart like me.” “Oh, just shut up!” The next morning when Gattu had drawn out all the scenes from his history textbook, he remembered the story like a movie. He confidently strode over to his parents room and announced that he had completed his syllabus to which there were frowns and scoffs but it didn’t matter to Gattu now for he had really studied hard. The exams were approaching and for the first time in his life, Gattu was not tense but he was eagerly awaiting for the question paper. So, as you might have guessed, Gattu passed with flying colours, his parents were ecstatic but Gattu was calm because he knew all along that if he studied he would do well and that’s what happened! “My Raja beta, tell me what do you want?” asked mother. “ What do I want but why?” replied Gattu. “Because you have done wonderful in your examinations, you deserve a gift”, added Father “Tell me, what you want, a new bicycle, a chocolate, a party, a picnic or a day out.” “Dad, I think you won’t get me what I really want”, replied Gattu. "Don’t be a fool, son, I promise I’ll try my best to get you what you want”, said father. “Fine, Mom and Dad, I study by drawing because it helps me to remember the things but what I really love is Art, please Mom and Dad I want to become the best artist in the world, and that can only be possible if I have proper training, so I request you two, can I please, please, please go to the Art School nearby, please, that’s what I really want.”’ There was stunned silence for some time during which Gaurav and Meena had conveyed their feelings through their eyes and their nod to each other was Gattu’s whole life. Dad heavily exhaled and then spoke the magical words, “Ok beta, if that’s what you really want, we will send you to the Art School but if it hinders your academics, we will not give it a second thought to take you out.” Yippee, was the squeal that escaped Gattu’s mouth at the prospect of going to Art School. “Thank you, Thank you, Thank you Mom and Dad, I love you both so, so much!” Gattu started going to Art School from the following week onwards, he worked hard and tried to learn all that he could. He practiced by drawing scenes from his textbook, which further improved his academics as well as art performance. Gattu regularly conversed with Jaggu, who was now becoming fainter day-by-day. Until one night when Jaggu said, “Gattu I will have to leave you now, I have other important people to meet and help.” Gattu was astonished, he managed to say, “But why weren’t we best friends forever?” “Yes, but you have now become what you want to be and trust me, you will be a truly great artist so, I have to leave you know, I have other lost kids to help, to help them find a purpose, like I did for you, so bye Gattu.” Bye, dear friend, was all that Gattu managed to speak as a tear trickled down his cheek. He is today a renowned artist but he will never forget his best mate.
author: ANVESHA RANA
illustrator: Brad Cuzen; Gieve Patel; Gwendolene van der Merwe; Herminder Ohri; Kripa B; Nguyễn  Minh Hải; Rai; Sudhir Patwardhan; Sunaina  Coelho; Trần Lưu  Đăng Nguyên; Upasana Mehndiratta; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: A kind boy and a dog
text: Once there was a dog and his master.The Dog's name was buzo. One day buzo and his master were at the airport. They were about to go on a flight.Then buzo's owner said him by showing a ball "go and Fetch the ball". He goes and Fetch the ball but When he comes back his owner has already board the plane and left Buzo at the airport only. Buzo was looking for his master in desperation and stayed at the airport. Buzo was so attached with his master that he stayed at the airport for so many days and checked all the passengers coming from different flights.But no luck buzo didn't found him. One day a little boy came down from the plane, he saw buzo there and he really likes Buzo and he took Buzo to his home. One day Buzo's original master came back and demanded his dog back from the little boy. Little boy with sad heart gives Buzo back to him. Buzo also felt very sad. So,when his owner took him on the plane buzo ran away to his new friend. Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
author: Aarav Walia

title: A Mother's Love
text: Ravi and Maya had their eyes glued to the television screen until their mother switched it off. "Mom! You can't do that!", protested Ravi, "We were about to get to the climax of the whole story!" "Yes", said Maya, " Can you please let us watch it for the next few minutes?" "Come here", said their mom. They both cuddled up next to her on the bed. "Do you want to listen to a story?" she asked. "Yes! Is it about superheroes?", asked Ravi. "Oh yes", smiled their mother, "In fact, in this story, the superhero is not Superman or anything. It's my mother". "But she isn't a real superhero, is she?", said Maya with a confused look on her face. "Oh, I bet you will call her one, once the story ends", said her mom. And so, she began. Once upon a time, there lived a happy couple in a village. They were very poor, but that never came in the way of their simple and happy life. They had a daughter, who was the joy of their life. Her name was Radha. One unfortunate evening, her father died. Radha was heartbroken. She cried, and cried, and cried. "Oh, mom", she would sob, "what are we going to do now?" But her mom, Radhika, wasn't going to give up. If she didn't work hard, she would fail to be a good mother. She could not bear the sight of her daughter in such a condition. And so, she bravely took the decision of moving on and getting a job. Since she wasn't educated and came from a very poor family, finding a job wasn't easy. Radhika used to work as a domestic help in many houses earlier. Her husband was a fisherman. Together, they managed to make enough money to feed themselves and Radha. They were able to afford for Radha's schooling in some local school nearby. But now, the circumstances were different. Sending Radha to a nice school for her studies needed lots of money. Radhika decided to carry on with her previous job, as a domestic help. She eventually started to enjoy her job. The people she worked for had a daughter who reminded her very much of her own daughter. The very kind people she worked for gave her more wages. But she knew it was not enough. Paying for a nice school and, most importantly, money for getting enough food was needed. One day, while she was in deep thought, an idea came to her. She knew how to stich very nicely. Well, she thought, I should do what I'm good at! She started stitching clothes at a very low price compared to what others would normally sell at. She started gaining popularity and was known for her amazingly nice nature and talent. At last, one day, she managed to get enough money in order to send Radha to a very nice and well-known school. That day they had a little, simple celebration party. Radha was a very determined little girl. She made up her goal to study hard and make up a nice career to pay off all the hard work her mother had done for her. She knew she owed her a lot. Years passed, and Radha grew up to become a very pretty and studious girl. She was the topper of her class, and everyone knew her mom by her name. One day, her daughter came into the house with a very blank face. "What happened, dear?", asked Radhika, fear seeping into her voice, "Did you pass the exam?" Radha didn't reply. She held out a paper with trembling hands. Radhika took it. There, she saw the words, clearly printed in bold: PASSED She said nothing but simply hugged Radha. Her eyes filled with tears. There they were, just savoring the moment. Her tears of happiness found their way down her cheek. They looked at each other and smiled. Radha was even happy to see her mother this happy after so many years. A huge lot of weight had been lifted off their shoulders. Maya clapped, "Now that, was amazing". Ravi said, "So, after that, you got a job in Canada and moved in with your mom?" "Yes", smiled their mother, "You know, I'm lucky to have such a mother. And of course, you two", she added. "And we're lucky to have you", Ravi and Maya hugged their mother tightly. Suddenly, the doorbell rang. Maya darted towards the door, knowing that her Naani had come back from shopping. The door opened, revealing the face of a very old Radhika. "Oh Naani!", she hugged her, "You never told us how much you struggled". Radhika looked up to her daughter's face questioningly, " What do they mean?" "Oh well...", Radha smiled, "I thought they should know our story too". "Oh that, ", Radhika pulled them all in a ginormous hug, " I love you so much. Oh yes, that time was very hard for me, but did I give up? No. Always remember that, after the darkest and cloudiest of days, even after a thunderstorm, the next day will always welcome you with its warmth and fill your life with happiness and love."
author: Samaira Tanwar
illustrator: Alice Toich; Edwin  Irabor; Jano Strydom; Jesse  Breytenbach; Karmacharya K.K; Shamim Ahmed; Sonali Zohra; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: THE ORPHAN CALF
text: It was a cold morning in the early part of the seventeenth century,and sleet was driving across.The hills when jam,the herder made his way down the track that led to farm building.Jam was an old man with straggly white hair and a weather-beaten face. he had looked after cows and buffaloes all his life. This morning, He was feeling tired,for it was the cold season,and he had been up all night with the cow.she had died,poor beast, but her calf was alive,and jam was carrying it,wrapped in a dry sack,held under his cloak. The distance from where he stopped seemed longer than usual in this bad weather,and the sleet stung,the herder's face,but he pulled his hood well over his face for protection.After sometime the sleet stopped. at last he arrived at the farm building and knocked at the farm door. ''Come in'' Cried a woman's cheerful voice and jam stepped into the warmth of a large low-ceilinged room where a fire burned on a grew open hearth. It flames lit up the pots and pans on the shelves. The dried herbs and salts meat hanging from the beams overhead.At a long table down the middle of the kitchen sat a plump,pleasant-faced woman the farmer's wife -and his little daughter about ten years old.The farmer's wife was serving the food.They were just finishing their breakfast. The farmer and his wife had already left the table and went for their work. but penny the little farmer's daughter was slower. farmer said his wife. I have brought you a new born calf stepping into the room and unwrapping his sack to disclose a thin. leggy animal,that seemed half asleep.''Its mother is dead.so, it will have to be fed by hand for a while. ''Poor little beast'' said his wife, bustling forward ''penny go to the linen room and ask for old blanket and the biggest wicker basket,The farmer's wife quickly warmed some milk and poured it into a pitcher with a narrow neck.This she stopped up with a piece of cloth that acted as a sponge. jam set the calf on its wobbly straddling legs. His wife put the neck of the pitcher to its mouth,and at once the little animal began to suck greedily,wagging its tail with enjoyment.When penny came back and saw that she dropped her burdens and ran across the kitchen.'Oh' mother,may I really? I have always a pet calf.what shall I call it? This w as important,she felt,and when her father came home to dinner along with the man and the maids gathered 'round the long kitchen table she put the question to the company.and they named him 'Honey' A lovely name! It is exactly right for him! Said penny delightedly,and her mother agreed. NAME- SHWETA BAGHEL CLASS - VI A SCHOOL NAME- SAINIK SCHOOL REWA(MP)
author: SHWETA BAGHEL

title: As Clear As A Crystal
text: Fifteen-year-old Prashant threw the pebble viciously into the pond. He did not care that he could have hit the fish his father loved to watch when he sat outside on the rolling lawns. All that luxury and the old man was turning into a skinflint! thrice this month he had refused to give him more than fifty rupees when usually he just handed over his purse to Prashant to help himself! What could he do with fifty rupees? He had promised the gang a treat at the movies. He looked at his watch. Just another half-hour before the booking opened and no way to put together the cash for five tickets. What should he do? Suddenly,a fragment of his mother's conversation with a friend ran across his mind. "I have collected this crystals from all over the world and it is my pride and joy." What a great idea! Prashant jumped up and sneaked back into the house. There was no one in the living room. He picked up the first place of crystals he saw-a tall vase-and made off with it. Prashant arrived at the theatre after the other four boys. Panting, but pleased, he grandly pulled out the four hundred he got for the vase and peeled off a hundred rupee note for the tickets. Akash, Arjun, Rohit took it for granted that he should pay. Only Gaurav, whose father supplied steel to Prashant's father's factory, felt a bit awkward. he would have preferred to buy his own ticket but he had seen how annoyed Prashant got if he suggested it, so instead he bought two packets of chips to pass around as they watched the movie. Prashant was relieved that he did not need to spend any more money. The remaining three hundred would see him through the next few days. The missing vase was not noticed for almost a week. By then, Prashant had helped himself to an ashtray and a three-cornered bowl as well. "That is strange," commented Mrs. Khanna. Where did I keep the gladioli vase?" She questioned the household staff, but no one seemed to know anything and Prashant, who was listening, just pretended he was reading. When the sixth piece disappeared, Mrs. Khanna could no longer take it lightly. "You must call everyone and question them," she said to her husband. "I have no time for that," he replied. "My hands are full with the factory and the staffs there." his father had not mentioned it at home, but he had big problems at work. Huge payments(for items his factory had manufactured and supplied) were held up because a defect had come to light, and he was finding it difficult to keep going. The manufacturing process had to be looked and fresh supplies made. Staffs had to be payed or they would go on strike. He did not share his worries with his family because he did not want them to think that the business was collapsing. Prashant did not ask his father for more money for an entire month, but Mr. Khanna did not give much thought to that.Mrs. Khanna,was not going to let go of her crystal that easily. she kept searching it over the whole house. Prashant did not have a chance to pinch any more of his mother's collection to acquire spending money for himself. "Let's go for Darshan Raval concert next Saturday," suggested Akash and Arjun,when the gang was together. They were confident Prashant would,as usual manage to get them these expensive tickets.Rohit's eyes shone at the thought. He fancied himself as a singer and wanted to become another Darshan himself! Gaurav shook his head"no,i cannot come,my parents will not allow me to go for a late night concert show like that." Hemant did not say anything. He knew he could never ruffle up the money for the tickets. Gaurav saw the look on Prashant's face and suddenly recalled the conversation he overheard between his parents a couple of nights ago. "Arrey" replied Akash. "Prashant's father always gets such things for us.He can afford it.What is a couple of thousands for him?" Prashant glared at Gaurav."Yes,spending om tickets and such stuff is chicken feed.If you ask for return tickets for London then he might think twice...." He walked away and gaurav ran after him. "Prashant, wait!" He waited for them to be out of earshot of the others, then he spoke rapidly. "I know things are not good at the factory, Prashant. You can always tell the others to pay for their own tickets. You do not have to treat them." "Why don't you mind your own business?" Prash ant snapped. He headed home, putting Gaurav's words firmly out of his mind and concentrating on a way to get some money. Ma's crystal was out of the question. The silver was not. He went straight to the side- board and opened the drawer where the six heavy, silver mugs lay. He dumped them in his backpack and headed for the lane of silver shops his mother often visited. He did not know that Gaurav was on his trail, determined to reason with him. When Prashant dumped the silver mugs on the Jeweller' counter, Gaurav rushed into the shop and confronted his friend. "do your parents know what you are doing,Prashant?" he asked. "Get lost!" snarled Prashant, pushing Gaurav away. "What is this? What are you boys up to?" asked the Jeweller, pressing an alarm under his table. A siren went off and an armed guard rushed in. Hemant panicked. He left the mugs on the counter and ran into the market-place with Gaurav close on his heels. When they were at a safe distance,Prash ant stopped and turned on Gaurav. "Why did you interfere? Now look what has happened! I don't have the silver and I don't have the money for it either!" "You can get the silver back," said Gaurav. "Oh sure. I just walk back to the sweet, helpful jeweller and tell him that it was all a mistake and that I want the mugs back, "Well, not exactly. You may not be able to pull it off on your own, but if you got your father or your mother to go with you.." "Brilliant!" growled Hemant. "I may as well handcuff myself and go to the cops." "I will come with you," persisted Gaurav. "You don' have to face your parents alone. I will tell them how it is in our group. How everyone expects you to pay for everything..." Prashant shoved Gaurav aside. "You have done enough damage for one day. Just stay away from me. I do not need your so-called help." Prashant decided that he would forget about the silver mugs and just hope that his mother did not think of using them.She had not taken them out in months anyway.But luck was against him.That very evening,when his mother's chacha,Prem, came over,she insisted that lassi be served in the silver mugs. Prashant cringed in his sofa,waiting for the uproar when the drawer was found empty.But there was none.When at least he found the courage to look up,Uncle Prem,Papa and Ma,were all helping themselves to their favourite drink-from the silver mugs! Prashant looked at the tray as if it was going to bite him.'How? How did the mugs get back into the house?Who brought them? he looked at his mother.'What was she hiding behind that smile? And Papa? What would he do to him when they were alone?' Prashant sat like a robot until Uncle Prem left.then he tried to move away,unobstrusively,but his mother called out to to him,"Prashant! just bring me the flowers chacha brought! Prashant picked up the bouquet that was lying on the coffee table.His legs trembled and he felt sick. She didn't say anything but took the flowers from him and began to arrange them in her tall,crystal vase. 'Wait a minute.The tall vase? that was the one he had sold! How did it get back into the house?' Prashant looked around wildly. The ashtray was back, and also the three-cornered bowl! It was too much for him. He crumpled on the floor and began to cry. "I am sorry, Ma, I'm sorry. I'll never do it again." Mrs Khanna bent down and smoothed Prashant's hair back from his forehead. "Why, Son?" she asked, "why did you do it?"Prash ant sobbed out the tale of his friends and the money all of them had needed to have fun together. As he tried to explain, he heard himself for the first time. How lame his excuses were! What foolish aims he had! Trying to buy friendship with his father's money and robbing his own parents to do it! "Gaurav told me everything," Mrs Khanna said, "but I was waiting for you to talk to me."Prash ant wiped his eyes and as he did so, he saw his father's feet next to him. He waited fearfully for the blow to fall on him, but nothing happened. "I should have taken you into confidence, Prashant," his father said, "but I was always far too busy. I did not credit you with the ability to understand that there are hard times as there are good times and we must know what to do in each. "Prash ant stood up. "I was selfish, Papa. I thought only of myself. I thought Gaurav was interfering. But now everything is clear to me. Now I know that he is the only true friend I have!,Prashant hugged his parents and went to Gaurav's house to apologize to him.Gaurav forgave him and they lived happily forevermore.
author: Zainab Fatima
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; David Yambem; Fahad Faizal; Rai; Seat Sopheap; Tanvi Bhat; Zainab Fatima

title: The wise owl and the birds
text: Once upon a time, there was a farmer who was sowing hemp seeds. A wise owl saw this and flew down to the birds, "Beware, the farmer is sowing dangerous seeds." The birds asked why are the seeds dangerous? The owl said these seeds are hemp seeds. Before they grow, pick each seed or you will regret. The birds ignored him and flew away. As some days passed, the hemp seeds grew and the farmer used them to make nets. In the evening,he laid the net and put dome grains on top. As the birds came to eat the grains, their feet got stuck in the net. The owl came and said," I told you to pick up the hemp seeds but you ignored, now you are regretting your mistake." The birds realised and said sorry to the owl. The owl called his mouse friends. The mice cut the net and the birds were free Moral:- Better safe than sorry
author: Divyanshi Kang
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Bi Cha   Ryea; Padmanabh; Partho Sengupta; Sain Thuokna

title: The Magical Garden
text: Mira loved fairytales. She had a whole bookshelf of fairytales and she read them every day. She wished that magical things would happen, but they never did. After a long time of waiting, she got bored. She stopped reading and spent all her time watching TV. Her mother was not pleased. She said "Go to my cupboard and bring my sewing box. I will teach you sewing." Mira went and opened the cupboard, and she was shocked. Inside was a magical garden. A lion came to her and said, "Welcome to my garden." Mira asked, "How did I get here?" The lion said, "Your mother sent you here to play." Mira was so happy. She never stopped believing in magic ever again.
author: Saanvi Sabareesh
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Lavanya  Naidu; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Rijuta Ghate; Shailja Jain Chougule

title: THE BOND
text: NARRATOR- The main character of this story is Gopal a 10 years old boy. SCENE 1- Two kids Ahana and Gopal playing in the garden. AHANA- Gopal,do you know last week, I went to my grandpa’s house I call my grandpa Dadu. So, Dadu and I had so much fun together we ate candies, played football and even made a drawing but yesterday my mother got a message from uncle’s side in that message h mentioned “Dadu is very sick doctors even said he can go to god at any moment” I am scared. GOPAL- If that would happen to my grandpa I will totally be fine AHANA- Ha Why....Gopal!! GOPAL- Because my Dadu is different from yours we don’t eat candies together or play foot ball instead he just write his boring stories. AHANA - Oh sad!Anyways it is time to go home. Bye Gopal see you tomorrow! GOPAL- Bye!! SCENE 2- Gopal sitting in his room *Gopal in his mind* Why just my Dadu is like that everyone’s Dadu play with them and he, just scold me…….. NARRATOR- It’s not like Gopal don’t obey his Dadu it’s just he thinks if Dadu will not be here nothing would change for him. day’s and day’s passed everything was normal but until one day, when Gopal came back from school he saw his parents crying. *Gopal in panic* WHAT HAPPENED MOM!!! DAD ARE YOU OKAY?... His dad in low voice Your Dadu….he….he is no more For Gopal it was a Nightmare. Even though he taught nothing would happen to him when his Dadu will not be in this world…..but he was in shock, he was upset, frustrated,stunned every single word for disappointed The other day he didn’t went to school. He cried and remembered every single moment he spent with his Dadu. *He said in regression* Why I didn’t spend time with Dadu WHY? Dadu, he scolded me every time, but still he cared for me. Day’s and day’s passed. Gopal and his parents went to Dadu’s house without Dadu for the first time. Gopal saw Dadu’s bed, chair, comb and clothes. He became sobbing and regret not sitting with Dadu. Then his mother came and gave him a book “Gopal dear, your Dadu made this book for you before passing away” GOPAL- Really…..mom. MOM - Yes dear. Gopal saw the title of the book and it was “Gopal My Child”by seeing that only he cried and remembered the deep voice of his Dadu.He began reading “Dear Gopal, if you are reading this…it means I have passed away.I made this for you so,whenever you feel lonely just read this “I am with you….always” Why I never played with you like other grandpa’s. Let me tell you a story about my childhood when I was your age “I also loved playing games like you but whenever I win I get so excited that I called other kids loser. So, no one was wanting to play with me at that time and I was worried that if I will play with you, you will fall apart from me and one more thing why I always write books and do nothing else I expressed my words and feelings to books because I felt lonely when no one was wanting to play with me so I played with books. Now, remember if there is a life after death I will love there also My Dearest………..son Gopal cried softly and hugged the book “Love you to Dadu” Since that day Gopal realized that “ we should spend time with everyone we don’t know what’s going to happen tomorrow” “Sometimes it is hard to understand the “Bond” but remember once the bond flew away it is over forever. THE END.
author: Saad Habib

title: My Family
text: I am 7 years old. I have one brother, named Joseph. Joseph is 3 years old. Hello! My name is Lucy. I am Marco's sister. I am 8 years old. I like painting. This is my dog. His name is Caramel. He is very smart and funny. They are my parents. My mother is Julia and she is 37 years old. My father is Javier and he is 43 years old. They are my grandfather and my grandmother. My grandmother is very smart, her name is Angela. My grandfather is a teacher, his name is Julio.
author: Terresa Alicia

title: Limelight
text: She had spent more than enough nights working on the role, making sure that she, too, would ace this role on stage. The director of the show walked up to Antonia. She handed her a cup of coffee. “Jealous of my daughter?” she asked. Antonia scoffed “Why would I be jealous? Arty deserved that award! Plus, she is the lead, I am just the understudy.” “What if we make you the lead for one season, see how that goes?” Antonia looked up from her cup. “How would that work?” she asked. “Just like any other casting” was the answer. “What about Arty?” she asked. “You don’t need to worry about her. She has enough to do.” The cast and crew of the queen of fire met at the theatre the next day to discuss the next season. Artemisia was there, gushing about her award, talking to fans among the cast. Antonia was very much one of them. Artemisia’s acting was what inspired her to enter the theatre industry in the first place, and she would have been no one without Arty’s guidance. Still, she was no one; an understudy, who barely got the time to shine on stage. “Welcome everyone. Before we go on to new costumes, we have a very important change to announce.” The director took a seat. “We have a new lead actress.” Antonia could see Artemisia’s fallen face. She could see her, barely breathing, waiting to know more. “The person playing the queen...” the director announced “...is Antonia Allesto.” “What!” Artemisia said “Toni?” Her face was hard to read. Antonia could already feel guilt churning inside her, even though she wasn’t a part of the decision making process. “Yes. Antonia” her mother said. “She hasn’t been on stage a lot, so maybe you can help her with everything?” “Mom...”she started, with disbelief. “Yes?” the director replied, making it clear that she had all the power in the room. “...Alright” Artemisia said, in a meek, almost silent voice, and left the room in a hurry. It was clear she was trying hard to not cause a scene. Antonia felt really bad about the whole situation, but it wasn’t as if she could do anything. She hadn’t made the decision. The director had planned this long ago. She had only given Antonia a hint of what was to come the previous night. Antonia found Artemisia in the dance studio later that afternoon. Arty was dancing, and once she finished her routine and sat down to open her shoes, Antonia joined her. “Hey,” she started, nervous to talk “I am really sorry about...” “Don’t be” Artemisia said. Her eyes were red. It was clear that she had been crying. “You didn’t do anything, right?” she managed a weak laugh. “Why did they change the lead at all?” Antonia asked. “I think it was my mother’s doing, though I’m not quite sure. She has been pestering me for a few days to branch out into movies, because they are more profitable, and I have been turning down all the offers I keep getting because of the show, so, maybe...” Artemisia trailed off. “Arty, will you help me with the show? I know it’s not right of-“ “Of course! No matter what, you are my friend, right? I’ll always help you” A few days of training later, Arty got Antonia into the empty theatre. One of the queen’s dances was a hard, show stopping number, and they decided to practice it before the cast met up for rehearsals. After about an hour of breathless dancing and singing, the two girls collapsed on the steps. “I can’t believe I’ll have to do this live!” gasped Antonia. She stood up and locked the stage door. “I know, it’s scary, but it’s fun to perform, right?” Artemisia said. “Right! Thanks a lot, Arty; I really don’t know what I would have done without you.” Cast rehearsals came and went, and thanks to Artemisia’s advice, Antonia learnt how to grasp the spotlight and shine in it. The costumes were altered to fit Antonia’s frame, and Artemisia felt a pang of sadness upon seeing her friend getting the attention she once had. But she pushed it down and moved on, determined to be happy for her friend. The night before opening, the cast and crew gathered at a small restaurant for a party. Antonia’s nerves had begun to kick in, and she already felt jittery, so she decided to talk to Artemisia. The latter however, sat in the corner of the room, barely speaking to anyone. Her mother, the director, was busy chatting with her colleagues, and Artemisia not only felt left out, but also unwanted. “Hey, Arty” Antonia started, hoping for a conversation. “Hi” came the reply. “So, now that everything is done, what are your plans?” Antonia immediately regretted saying that. “Done?” Artemisia stood up, tears suddenly streaming from her eyes “you can’t expect me to just be happy with everything and move on! My own mother fired me from this show, that too, after I won her five whole awards!” “That’s not what I meant... please, calm down!” Antonia tried to say. “Of course you didn’t. You can’t just come along and replace me just like that, and then ask me to be calm! I gave this show five years of my life. I created the characters myself; this show is everything to me! And then, mom fired me, because she wanted me to move on to other things, when I was clearly not done with it! So forgive me, if I wasn’t sure if the character would be left in good hands!” Everyone in the restaurant was staring at them, even the cast and the crew. Artemisia shakily sat down, her breaths heavy and laboured, her eyes darting from one corner of the room to the other. Antonia was scared. She didn’t know what to do, what to say. Artemisia looked up into Antonia’s black, void-like eyes, which were consuming all of her happiness. “You used me” she said, quietly. “No, Arty, listen, I would never...” “YOU USED ME!” Artemisia screamed. “I WOULD NEVER!” Antonia shouted back “I have admired your work since I young! I dreamed of meeting you ever since I first saw your show! Getting to work alongside you has been the best thing that ever happened to me!” Antonia continued, “You have a mother who can give you opportunities! In our family, when they learnt I was going to do theatre, all I got were disapproving looks and disappointed faces! I only continued because, when I succeeded in that audition, I knew I would get to work alongside you! For once, Artemisia, please...” She broke into tears. “We can share the limelight, can’t we? Or is it my destiny to always remain in the wings?” The next night, Antonia stood backstage in her red and gold dress, her hair laced with gilded ribbons. The show had been pretty successful, and as far as she knew, Antonia hadn’t messed up even once. And it was all thanks to Artemisia. All throughout the show, Antonia could see her, in a loose, grey-green suit, leaning against one of the wings, silently watching the show. She had left the previous night in a hurry, without even finishing her drink, and Antonia figured that it was definitely her own fault. The musical cue rang out for the final bow. Antonia entered the stage to huge applause, and out of habit, turned to Artemisia to see what she thought of it. To her surprise, the girl was smiling, her hands applauding Antonia’s performance alongside the audience. Without a shred of doubt, Antonia rushed into the wings and dragged Artemisia into the spotlight. She was confused, blinded by the lights, but she too, bowed with a smile. In front of the audience, Antonia embraced her, and whispered “I’m so sorry” “No, I am. I shouldn’t have shouted at you!” she said. “I shouldn’t have made you shout.” They stood in the light for a while until the curtains dropped. “All I know,” Artemisia said “is that I have left the character in wonderful hands. You, Toni, will make a great lead.” “You didn’t finish your milkshake last night because of me. Wanna go and get it?” Antonia asked. “I guess we can be friends again, Allesto” Artemisia laughed after a long time “you have a deal.”

title: Sanskrit-i
text: Wake up Sanskriti! It's 8'oclock! I am going to office. Breakfast is on the table. Sanskriti lazily trudged to the bathroom to brush her teeth. Yes! Meet Sanskriti Sharma, a 9 year- old girl full of curiosity to learn new things. She lived with her parents and her 5 year- old little brother named Roshan in Delhi. Her mother owned a boutique and worked there. Her father was a manager in a bank. Sanskriti and her brother studied in one of the best schools in Delhi. Their school holidays were going on after which they were going to be promoted to the next class. So, they stayed in the house with their cousin sister who was 18 years old. Sanskriti brushed her teeth, took her bath and went to the living room to have breakfast. Now, there was one thought that kept occurring into Sanskriti's mind " Which extra language can I choose?" As she was going to be promoted in fifth grade she had to choose a language out of the three- Spanish, French or Sanskrit. All of her friends used to say "Choose any but not Sanskrit as it will not help you in future." But her Hindi teacher used to say " Choose what you want not what others want." Even her parents used to agree with her Hindi teacher. But Sanskriti still remained confused. After a while she washed her hands and went to help her brother and to do her own holiday homework. In the evening, Her parents came and said "Kids, we have bought some gifts for you! Roshan got a new toy car and Sanskriti got a novel of 200 pages. Since they still had 1 month Sanskriti decided that she will start reading the novel and complete it till the school reopens. The next morning she started reading the book. Day by day as she kept reading the novel, a strong desire to choose Sanskrit as her third language was growing in her. This continued till the whole month was over and school was about to be opened after a week. Her parents asked her "Today is the last day to buy the third language books. So please tell us your choice quickly." Sanskriti replied with a smile on her face" I choose our India's ancient language because I am proud to be an Indian. I choose SANSKRIT" said Sanskriti. Her parents and sister were proud and they bought her the Sanskrit books. Her friends of course said, that it was the wrong decision but Sanskriti knew that her decision was right. And most importantly she also spread the message that- " Learning other languages is fine, But for that, first learn your own language." When she started learning Sanskrit she enjoyed it and was good at it. She got full marks for all the tests. But after some time she realized that it was not to easy to learn Sanskrit. Since, Sanskrit teachers are not easily found, her teacher was a bit aged and could not come up to teach her. All the Sanskrit students had to go down to study the language. Also, when it was her final exam and she could not understand a question her teacher could not come up to explain her. Nevertheless, she still scored full marks in Sanskrit. But there was another problem, since Sanskrit class happened only once in a week for one hour, the syllabus was also not complete for tests. And it was also challenging to find a Sanskrit tuition teacher. But, even after all these difficulties, Sanskriti with the support of her parents, became the Sanskrit topper in all of the sections.

title: Kaali and Buddy
text: Hello! I am Koi and I love dogs. I can do anything for them. Do you know that in our world, there are 200 million homeless dogs? When I was ten, one man named Kaali lived in my neighborhood. He was desolate, his family had left him because of his addiction to drugs. He worked in a hotel and served food. This was his life until a dog came into his life and changed everything. One day, on Holi, while everyone was enjoying and playing with colors, a dog, actually a little puppy of breed (beagle) of about 8 weeks with little white mark on tail, a small nose, big ears and light brown and black shade on his body, looked upset as everyone was playing with colors and dog, they are allergic to color, it looked like he was abandoned. The celebrations were over and in the mid-night, the puppy started making noises as if he was weeping out of hunger. Because of this, Kali's sleep was disturbed. Kali woke up in anger, went out and picked up the puppy and threw him in the dustbin. It was callous but it turned out to be beneficial for both, the puppy and Kali because the puppy got his food and Kali could sleep. The next morning, after toil and moil, the dog tried and succeeded to come out of the bin. When Kaali was leaving for his job, dog started following him. This was not for once, he followed him every day. Because whenever he used to make noise for food and Kali got disturbed, he used to throw him in the dustbin where otherwise the puppy could not get in to get his food. One day Kali was inebriated and he stumbled his car upon that puppy and the puppy was hurt badly. When he came to his consciousness, he realised and felt pity for the little puppy and decided to take that puppy to his friend's brother who was a veterinarian. Upon seeing the condition of the puppy, the doctor urged Kali to take personal care of the puppy for a few days until he was healthy again but Kali was not interested in keeping a pet dog. He told the doc that the puppy did not belong to him and that he had no intention and money to afford a pet. Kali started arguing with the doctor, mentioning how busy he was. The doctor urged that without your care, the puppy might not live long and made Kali realize that God was watching him. Surprisingly, Kali had a change of heart and promised the doc to take puppy home and kept him until he was healthy again. It took him time to learn about taking caring of a puppy but he was doing the best he could. He just wanted to get rid of the puppy as soon as he can. Kali would put ointment on puppy's bruises, which was not an easy task for puppy would run in all directions, to avoid it and was hard to be caught. Since the puppy would live with Kali for a short time, he started calling him Buddy, All that Kali used to spend on alcohol, now started to save that money to buy dog food for Buddy. Now, Kali was never late for work, Buddy would wake him up early in the morning to ask for a morning walk. When Kali used to come back from work in the evening, Buddy could be seen waiting eagerly for Kali sitting in the balcony and a loud bark could be heard as soon as Kali's vehicle used to approach near by, as if the puppy waited all day to see Kali only which Kali started noticing. The puppy was recovering very fast now and once, as they visited the doc for regular checkup, the doc appreciated Kali for his caring for the puppy. In the mean time, two months had already passed now and doctor was also convinced that buddy was healthy. Kali decided to abandon him. While that evening, when Kali returned from work, Buddy was waiting eagerly as usual. Kali called Buddy, preparing his evening meal in his bowl. This time, there was a change, Kali took the bowl and put it outside the house near the garbage bin in which Kali used to throw Buddy before. Buddy innocently followed Kali and started eating from the bowl. Kali quitely tried to get in the house which buddy noticed, and ran quickly behind Kali but Kali had already closed the door. Kali was not feeling good inside in abandoning the dog but he was telling himself that he could not keep the dog, now that he was fine, it is no longer his reposibility. Buddy did not eat there after and sat at the door waiting for the door to open. Kali had his dinner and was about to go to bed when he was filled with the thoughts of Buddy running all around in the house. He laid on the bed, restless, he thought to check once if Buddy had slept. He went into the balcony and could not find Buddy anywhere, only the bowl that too unemptied was lying next to the garbage bin. Kali decided to find Buddy. Kali wore his slippers and got the keys of his car and opened the door. While he was locking the door, he was alarmed by something that touched his feet very softly from behind. Kali turned around and was surprised to find Buddy who was sitting there for all the time. Kali got Buddy in his arms patting him and asking why he left his food. The answer was evident, Buddy missed Kali and Kali could not sleep that night because Kali, unaware also missed Buddy's presence who had been a part and parcel of Kali's life now. Since that night, Kali had been a pet lover, wherever he used to go, he used to take buddy along. This is how loving and caring for an animal changed a person and his repute in the society completely.
author: Vigyani Negi

title: The Ring Of Luck
text: 'Mother, I will be back at 6!' He called back as he ran towards the open lawn to play cricket with his friends. This was Ranjits daily routine he would wake up at 6am, go to school at 8:30am, return at 3pm, go to play at 5pm and he would return at 6pm. He also did his studies and homework till 8pm then his mother would call him for dinner and he goes to sleep at 9pm. Ranjit liked his perfect life and he didn't want anything to change.Everyone liked him,he was really popular at school because of his exam marks. He was also the teacher's pet. Everything was going well until a new boy joined his class. His name was Arun. The teacher introduced Arun to the class. On Arun's first day, he sat next to Ranjit. Ranjit was not very good at starting conversations but he noticed that Arun was trying to speak to him but hesitated so, Ranjit started first. 'Hi Arun' he said, My name is Ranjit, Its very nice to meet you. Then Ranjit smiled at him. Arun smiled back and said 'Hi Ranjit, Its very nice to meet you too...Can we be friends? Ranjit wasn't used to being friends with someone who he had just meet, but he noticed Arun's friendly manner so he agreed. From that moment, They were the thickest of friends. Ranjit treated Arun as his own brother because, Arun was a few months younger than him and they both preferred the same thing and they would always get the same idea. Ranjit slowly realised that Arun was getting more and more popular in school too. Now the teacher liked and praised Arun more than Ranjit. Whenever there was a competition Arun was called to participate instead of Ranjit. The change was so sudden that Ranjit felt as if he had been completely ignored. Ranjit knew this was bad and first of all Arun is Ranjit's best friend, Ranjit should actually be proud and happy if Arun is getting more popular and well-known between teachers but he couldn't help getting jealous. His head told him that he should always be the best and he shouldn't let go of his place even for his best friend. His heart told him to stop worrying and do his best as usual. Ranjit couldn't choose between the two,but one thing was certain in his mind Arun was his best friend and he would never betray or do anything that will hurt Arun. Ranjit became very depressed. His parents too noticed that it had been weeks since he smiled and at school Arun asked him if anything was wrong but Ranjit would always say 'nothing'. This resulted in low grades and suddenly his exam marks dropped, his parennts asked Ranjit if anything is bothering him, but Ranjit didn't tell them anything, instead he told them that it won't happen again. That night, he was really tired so he fell asleep immediatly. Ranjit had a really strange dream. There was a fairy wearing a long gown and she had a wand with a star in the tip. 'Hi Ranjit' she said, I am crystal,I have been watching you since last week. You seemed to be very disturbed so I thought maybe I can help you, This is actually my job, I help children who have mind related problems. So, here take this. She handed him a transparent crystal box inside there was a ring with a tiny star on top of it. Look Ranjit, this is the "Ring Of Luck". If you do anything while wearing this ring you will definitly succeed. Saying this she vanished into thin air. The next morning,Ranjit woke up early. He still remembered the dream from last night. He almost thought that the dream was real, he found it very silly to believe a dream like that so, he got up and was about to leave the room when he noticed something on the nightstand. He went over to take a better look. He exclaimed in shock as it was the same crystal box from the dream! He quickly opened the box and took out the ring. It looked exactly the same as it was from the dream. He looked around if anyone was there and then he quickly slid the ring through his ring finger. Then he hid the crystal box in his room. He didn't hide the crystal box just because he would be in trouble.Even if he told the story to his parents they wouldn't believe him and there are absolutly no chances that his parents are not going to notice the ring on his finger. So someday he will definitly be asked about the ring, but for now he kept all his problems aside and he went to school. That day was very successful just as the fairy had said. After weeks of worrying he felt free. Even Arun noticed it. At home, his parents also noticed the joy in Ranjit's face that has been missing for weeks. Ranjit was also happy to return to his normal life. He thought about the past few weeks and felt really silly to worry about such a small matter but now he had overcome it so he didn't need to worry about it anymore. At dinner, just as Ranjit had expected his parents asked him about the ring he was wearing. He didn't want to lie so, he told the truth. He even showed them the cystal box. He wasn't so sure that his parents understood or even believed the story, but to his surprise they agreed to let him wear the ring in his finger. Ranjit's parents were too relieved to find that Ranjit was back to normal so they didn't care much about the story which Ranjit told. But the ring has a secret in it which only Crystal knows..... THE END Dear Readers, I am Crystal and i'm here to tell you the secret. Actually the ring is a normal ring it does not have any magic in it. I made it to give Ranjit the faith,will power,confidence and hope which he wasn't having at that time. The ring wasn't the reason for being successful in school that day, It was because of Ranjit himself. Everything is within yourself, magic doesn't exist, but faith,will power,confidence and hope does exist within you so the next time you want to succeed in something, do not sit and worry, be jealous or blame others if they are better than you. You have to try the best out of yourselves to acheive something and remember challenges are what makes life exiciting and fun and we should know how to overcome it. - Crystal
author: Shalupritika Muthukamaraj

title: The Infinith
text: ﻿ The Infinith is a one of a kind starship. It is quite similar to the Millenium Falcon YT-1300 Lightspeed Freighter in Star Wars. It uses the same fuel unstable liquid metal. This spaceship is scheduled for its test drive on 3042 July 28 th. This Spaceship's maiden voyage marks the 8 th anniversary of SSA (Staridian Space agency) Days passed quickly, now it is 6 years after the first test drive of the Infinith. It is currently stationed in the parking slot 7, for an important meeting. It is about the bankruptcy that happened in SSA recently. A lot of expensive satellites have been sent into the MEO orbit (Medium Earth Orbit), this costed a lot leading to bankruptcy. These satellites are being used to detect tornadoes thunderstorms,sending television signals etc. So, SSA cannot send satellites for another 10 years. It has money only for giving fuel and electricity to quarter of its starships. All Ark ships are parked in their respective parking slots because they cannot run without ion fuel. Ion fuel is very expensive. So, only electricity can be supplied to the spaceships.Without ion thrusters the ship is useless. Then, SSA got an idea to recover from the bankruptcy within a year. They started their own website called "Getyourspaceride.com" This website allows anyone to travel around the solar system on a vacation in space in just one month! Each and every planet in the solar system has its own price depending on the distance from the launch pad. Gas giants, ice giants, dwarf planets and moons are in the package - Travellers cannot land there but can stay in orbit for a few hours or dock to any facility near the planet they are heading to. In one year, SSA estimates to produce 12 million dollars. This is enough to power all the spaceships and produce two more cargo freighters. SSA was successful and flooding with profits! --- 11.3 years after the Infinith's first test drive--- Infinith is going for an important meeting on Earth. It has almost completed its journey from Cerus(an asteroid) to earth. It is near the GEO synchronising orbit also known as the GEO orbit. Just two minutes after, a large meteorite was detected coming at a speed of 700 miles per hour and Infinith was testing its new Ski-landing legs. The Asteroid hit landing gears 6 & 8 and broke them off. The Infinith couldn't land for another 2-3 hours until the new landing legs arrived from Earth. Part of the landing gear was broken. This was removed with the inbuilt crane facility in Infinith which took around 20 minutes. Finally, the spaceship which had the new landing gears arrived. The spaceship had its own mobile crane. The mobile crane lifted the new landing gears and put them into place. After that, The Infinith safely returned to earth with the shiny new landing gears. Adventures of Infinith and imagination of author keeps continuing!!!
author: Hemanth Swain
illustrator: Isha  Mangalmurti; Seat Sopheap; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: Vindicta
text: As the monsoon faded away, autumn was slowly creeping into Ketterdam. Melanie opened the windows, wind rushed right into her lungs, cold, sharp and crisp. She wondered whether it was her 15th autumn in Ketterdam or 16th. Melanie was a girl of 22 living in the suburbs of Ketterdam while her parents were in london. Originally an intern in the Bretton Woods law firm, she had a strong desire to work at the museum. Melaine was stranger than the other girls of her age. Very strange. One could find her sitting by the willow by the lake or visiting the abandoned churches. This year, her best friend Bertha Jorkins' body was found by the lake with a pair of Viking coins placed on her eyelids. Melanie couldn't digest the grief of the loss of her dear Bertha. The night before Bertha's death, Melanie had spoke to her. Bertha seemed to be very enthusiastic bout visiting the Coin Exhibition which was scheduled to take place on the 29th of the next month. After putting herself up together, she decided to visit the Exhibition in her loving memory. The coin exhibition held at the Victorian Cross Mueseum was the most classy and sophisticated exhibition she had ever seen. Elegant ladies hailing from lavish families, Handsome men possessing riches beyong her wildest dreams and Wealthy estate owners flooded the museum halls. Alongside the exhibition, the phoenix coin had to be auctioned. Phoenix coin was a royalty in itself. The figure of a blazing phoenix was engraved on the coin along with a strange word ' VINDICTA' on it. The coin was believed to be found in Via Dolorosa or the 'way of Suffering', the path in jerusalem which jesus took while walking to his crucifixion. As Melanie paved her way through the crowd, the sight of a stranger caught her eyes. He was a tall man, probably in his late 20s with deep blue eyes. He wore a lean black suit with an overcoat and possessed a walking cane with a golden raven on it. His face felt like moonlight falling on white jade. With the cane in one hand and a glass of wine in the other, he seemed to be walking towards her. There was something about, something magnetic. Judging from his attitude, he seemed a ruthless man with cold demanour. His voice was deep but charming and his eyes felt distant. He surely was a cunning man and wore a sarcastic smile, like a thousand secrets were hidden behind it. He was a coin dealer and was accompanied by an acquaintance, Pekka Rollins. While Kaz Brekker walked towards her, Rollins held up his watch chain. A turnip was hanging from the fob where his diamond studded timepiece should have been. 'That little bastard!' whispered Pekka. Seeing this sight, Melanie realised that Kaz had already walked past her. Melanie reached for her purse. It was gone. So was her gold hairpin, the Kaelish Coin pendant she wore for luck and the gold buckles on her boots. Melanie angrily approached him and exclaied, ' You are a pick pocketer! Kaz calmly replied, his sarcastic smile intact, 'That isn't something pleasing to say on the first meet. I am Kaz Brekker, a business man and a coin dealer. Nothing more, nothing less'. 'You are a thief, Kaz. Greed is your God' 'Isn't that what I just said and let me correct you miss, greed is NOT my god, its my servant and lever, it bows to me'. replied Kaz. As he turned to walk away, Melanie blocked his way and asked, 'What you possess is mine, but I will let you get away if you answer a few questions of mine.' Kaz nodded coldly. 'You told me you are a coin dealer.' 'Young lady, I am not in the habit of repeating things twice.' 'Well, then tell me about the Viking coins.' The word Viking made Kaz's eyes glow. 'I am sorry. That is something not concerning your business.' Melanie smiled slyly and replied, 'True. I believe my business is just calling the cops.' 'What do you need to know about Viking coins?' 'Anything and Everything' replied Melanie. 'Well, the Viking coins are believed to be a token to hell. Viking coins were used by the Mayans in dark Rituals.' replied Kaz. 'And what does Vindicta mean?' she asked Kaz felt a choke in his throat. It felt strange because it was the first time a stranger had brought up Vindicta. Still, he replied coldly, ' Vindicta is a latin word which means.....' 'Which means what?' asked Melanie 'Revenge'. Melanie stood blankly. She felt numb. What did revenge mean to Bertha? Judging from her look, Kaz asked, ' Anything wrong?' 'Why would someone keep a coin with revenge engraved on it? I mean on someone's eyelids who died? My friend Bertha Jorkins was murdered, her body was found by the lake, a viking coin was kept on her eyelids. It means Revenge?' The smile on Kaz's face vanished. He felt blood rushing in his cold veins. Flashback seemed to play in front of him. Nevertheless, Kaz answered, ' I am sorry but I need to leave before nightfall'. With these words, he walked away towards the museum door. As Melanie stood there, she felt her purse in her hand. She hurriedly opened the purse. The world seemed to crash in front of her as she held something shakingly. It was Bertha's photograph by the lake, her throat split an coins on her eyes. Besides the photograph, the same Viking coins lay in her purse with Vidicta on it and a note which stated, IT WAS FOOLISH OF YOU TO BRING UP THE DEATH OF BERTHA JORKINS. YOU'VE MADE A GRAVE MISTAKE AND NOW THE PRICE NEEDS TO BE PAID' Just then the clock struck 7 bells and a half chime. Someone announced that the coin dealer couldn't make it due to heavy downpour hence the auction will be held at midnight.
author: Adyanshi Tiwary

title: OBSTACLES ARE THE PATHS
text: Once there was a boy named Rahul. His father had died before he was born due to a serious disease. His mother was very kind lady and wanted to keep the child but her family pressurized her to remarry. Rahul's granny who loved him even more than his sons denied to send Rahul along with his mother. She took care of him. OBSTACLES ARE THE PATHS Then it was his younger paternal uncle's wedding. Rahul's grandfather admonished his granny to gave the child to the new couple, but Rahul being the apple of her eyes she refused it. After few months the lady (his aunt) gave birth to a daughter. So, his granny antipathly gave his son to her daughter-in-law. After some years she gave birth to a second girl. Being Rahul his step son, the lady didn't love him as much as her own daughters. She taught them separately in a room and overlooked Rahul. But Rahul was a star child, he was an expert at Maths, playing cricket was a child's play for him, he was skillful at computer and altogether an all rounder. The only obstacle in his life was no resources to achieve his goals. One day, his coach offered him to attain leadership in his team being the best player. But the match was out of his city that needed a fees to go there that was only 50 rupees but only for us it is only at that time it had a great value. His elder paternal uncle who was very rage denied to give money and go out. He too had a son who wasn't an all rounder like Rahul was. So, he was jealous of him and always kept him busy in playing and other time-wasting quadrants. Soon he grew up, and passed in his board exams with difficulty. His father cum uncle encouraged him to do some job in Computers. But he had a deep love for cricket and even any other sports. So, he wasn't happy with the words of his step-dad. At last he had to go to a computer class unwillingly. But had being no interest in Computers failed at his classes, his career shattered had to live a life of a shopkeeper which was rather very difficult. His life was full of obstacles, a boy with no parents, all rounder but no facilities, not allowed to follow the path that he wanted to walk on. But being a positive mind he never left scope and worked hard, got married to a caring, loving and gorgeous lady with the blessings of her granny. After his granny died his step-mother became more mean. She was always, till now was busy with her daughters, kept everything they got. But Rahul had never bothered much. He was a calm and a beautiful soul. He had two children a boy and a girl. He always looked his dreams to be fulfilled by them. He worked hard for his kids day and night, provided them the best education, best place for study, best clothes etc. Because he didn't want his children to face whatever he had faced throughout his life. His children proved themselves and the hardwork of their father. His daughter had made a national record by achieving 100% in her exams, more than his step-sisters. His son who wasn't interested in studies had but had become a world Olympic swimmer. He was as proud as peacock that day and has a luxurious life today. Moral: Hard work always pays off whether later or now.
author: TAVISHA 6515
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Alice Toich; Avishek Sen; Dhiman  Sarkar; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Manisha Naskar; Marleen  Visser; Neeta Gangopadhya; Partho Sengupta; Sunando C

title: The sibling's thought
text: Once upon a time, in a city lived a boy named Prem with his sister Prema. Prem was elder and Prema was younger. They lived with their mother, father and grandma. They always watched television, so that their parents was scolding them. One day while they were watching television they saw a cartoon where the king went to heaven and enjoyed his life. The brother got shocked and asked his sister " Is this true? Is the heaven really enjoyable?".The sister too in shock said " I am not sure but I think this is true,a real story ". Then the brother said, "Oh fine, I have a idea we'll ask our friends and teachers regarding this ",on hearing this Prema nodded her head. At the school, in the classroom they started speaking about this. After hearing this all the students were wide eyed and breathless. All the students said I have no idea about this. They were sad on hearing this so the sister planned to ask this to parents. At the home these kids were waiting for their parents who went to job. When the parents stepped inside the home the kids asked this to their parents and, their parents said "First of all, you must stop watching the television. These are just cartoons which are imaginary not the real one don't believe this start to study." but, the kids did not accept this and wanted to see heaven. On hearing this, the grandma in anger called these kids and said how does a heaven looks like. On hearing this they got a idea about heaven and asked their parents for money. His father in anger asked and said “Are you a mad? All of us are suffering for money but you are asking for money. Ok fine now if you want money then you have to work for us,get money,save it and without wasting the money you can get your needed money. For this they worked for three months and got Rs.1700. They called their father for nursery, he did not know why they have to go to nursery,though he went with them.They bought plants for Rs.1200 and had Rs.500 with them. So they bought paint from the shop for making a heaven. First they cleaned their garden and planted the trees. Then, they painted the gate and wall, wrote it as heaven in the gate. They made compost at their home and made birds’ house and a bird feeder. They watered their plants all the day and finally it was like a heaven. All the friends came to their house. The birds chirping,fine breeze and the plants seems to be a heaven. All the friends said wow! And their parents gave Rs.500 to Prem and Prema. They were very happy. Teamwork makes dreamwork.

title: Golu Grows A Nose
text: One time, there was a baby elephant named Golu. In ancient times, elephants had short noses, so Golu also had sharp noses. He was curious to learn new things, so he asked various questions about all the animals in the jungle. So, all the animals in the wilderness were disturbed by the questions asked by Golu. One day, while Golu was roaming in the jungle, he saw a giraffe. A question arose in his mind, and he asked him, “Why do you have a long neck?” Giraffe did not have an answer to this question. While Golu was on his way, he was thinking about some new things when he saw an owl. Again, a question clicked in his mind, and he was eagerly waiting to ask him. So, he quickly asked him, “Why can you see only at night and not during the day?”. Owl was troubled by the question because he didn’t know the answer. He continued towards his way, whistling with his bulgy nose. He saw an ostrich coming towards him, and once again, a question came to his mind. Without waiting, he asked him, “Why you and other ostriches can’t fly?” Ostrich grimaced at this question. Golu was sad as no one was answering his questions, so he could not learn new things. After some time, he started playing and once again, a question came to his mind, “What do lions eat for dinner?” He hadn’t seen a lion before. He went towards his home to ask about this while he met mynah on his way. He asked him, “What do lions eat for dinner?” Mynah did ‘t know the answer, so she directed him to a cave near a Limpopo River. Now in place of his home, he went towards the cave to ask the lion his question. Golu had no experience with a lion. He had never seen a lion before, so he was confused about what it looked like. On his way, he met Chotu, a snake, so he asked Chotu what a lion looks like. Chotu answered that they have short rounded heads, hairy tufts at the end of their tail and a mane of hair around their neck. Thanking Chotu, he went towards the lion’s cave. After some time, he reached the cave situated near the Limpopo river. He saw one animal with a mane on his head which Chotu had said, and he came to know it was a lion. Without waiting, he asked him, “What do you eat for dinner?”. The lion then tried to trick Golu. He said, “Please come near me. I will tell you what I eat for dinner”. As Golu went near him, the lion quickly grappled him by the nose. The lion then said, “You would be my dinner today’s dinner”. Golu requested the lion to let him go, but the lion did ‘t leave him. Chotu, who was following Golu quietly, told him to pull hard. Chotu also helped him by calling himself around Golu and hurting him. During tug-of-war, Golu’s nose became 5 feet long, but he was free from the lion and safe. Golu tried to make his nose shorter by wrapping it with a banana leaf and hanging himself in the Limpopo river to shrink. But it did ‘t shrink. This long nose had many advantages too. Like plucking large bundles of grass, sprinkling water using his long nose to pull his head and many more. Thanking Chotu for his help, Golu went back to his home. Moral: Curiosity may be beneficial but sometimes dangerous to us. But no matter what the experience, he always plays the role of an excellent teacher.
