title: The Essay Competition
text: It was a perfectly normal day in the life of Ravi Ahuja. He woke up with the noise of his alarm clock, brushed his teeth, had a bath, wore his uniform and marched to school. On the way, he thought about the scoldings he’d receive for not completing last day’s homework. He got tensed with the fear of failing his science test as he hadn’t prepared for it. After the prayer and Bible-reading in the assembly hall, Ravi and his classmates gave their science test. He obviously failed as he never took his studies seriously. Somehow, he also escaped his second period of maths by mumbling a lame excuse of having headache. During the third period of IT, he did not pay attention and ended up missing the key points of coding. And the fourth period went as a free period for Sr. Ann was absent. Before telling you about Ravi’s day at school, you should know who he really is. He is just another average student with a short height, dark brown eyes, tanned skin and a mop of unruly black hair that refused to settle down at one place. He is someone who does not pay attention during lessons, forgets his homework and fails his tests. It was after lunch break that his day took an interesting turn. “Good day, students!” boomed the Principal through the microphone just as Ravi had finished his lunch. “I want to tell you about an upcoming essay writing competition. In this competition, you have to write an essay on the topic - ‘What will I become when I grow up.’ So get writing...” Before the Principal could finish her words, Ravi’s thoughts wandered off. During all the lessons that followed, he kept thinking, making him pay even less attention than he would’ve earlier. Even after reaching home, he kept thinking. But it was not long before his thoughts drifted away. He began thinking about Shankar Tau, who was coming over for dinner. Shankar Tau was a police superintendent. A nice person with a huge, bushy moustache and an aura that made goons flee at the sight of him. Ravi thought that he could be a policeman. He would be really honest and catch the bad guys to put them in prison. But for that, he needed to be brave and fearless, which was quite impossible as he was a coward. A few minutes later, Shankar Tau arrived, and the family had a hearty meal together. It was late when Ravi went to bed. The next day was a Sunday so he woke up late. He got dressed and went with his father to meet Harsh uncle, one of his father’s friends. Harsh uncle was a lawyer. He had a huge bungalow and an even larger chamber. The chamber was full of clients. “So many clients...he must be quite popular”, thought Ravi. It was not long before Ravi got the idea of becoming a lawyer. But when he found out that lawyers had to read huge books about previous cases, Ravi sighed out of sheer disappointment. Later in the day, Ravi met his English teacher, Ms. Rosaline. She was his favourite teacher, as she was so nice and Ravi found her more approachable than his other teachers. While talking to her, Ravi wondered if he could become a teacher like her. A nice and fun teacher loved by all the students. But then, it dawned upon him that for being a teacher, he needed to have a rich vocabulary and a deep knowledge of his subject. Looks like I have to study for being anything in the future, sighed Ravi. At night, when he was having dinner, he thought of becoming an entrepreneur like his father. Then he would be rich and well-known in the city. But as an entrepreneur, he would have to be really patient to deal with different kinds of people. After a huge yawn, he went to sleep. He slept on...on...on... Suddenly, Ravi woke up in the morning with a jerk. His head was spinning from the thoughts of the previous day. But he felt something different inside himself. A spark of hope. A new confidence. A strong yearning to learn and study the very subjects he used to hate earlier. His perspective of life had changed. In his heart he knew that he wanted to be wise and great like each of the people he had met. He was willing to study if that meant jumping out of his boring world and being known for something beside his faults. He studied with dedication, knowing that it was the only and true path for becoming capable like the wonderful people of this world. A single day had changed him completely. Earlier, he remained absent-minded during most lessons, but now he was an active participant in the class. From that day onwards, he never gave a single chance to his mother and teachers to scold him. They felt immense pleasure after seeing his dedication and passion for studying to become a capable person in the unforeseen future. He was really inspired by this incident of his life and wrote his essay based on these experiences. And guess what? He won the first prize! You never know when even a small competition may play a major role in your life, helping you to change your outlook of life.
author: Ira Kapoor

title: A POACHER HAS A CHANGE OF HEART
text: Hello! I am your narrator. Before I start with the story, I would like to introduce myself. During my childhood days, I often stayed in the lap of nature and enjoyed it. Neither my parents nor I were worried about studies. So, I could experience a lot in and around nature. I used to stay near the Kaziranga forests and my father was a staff there. The people who stayed there had to be very conscious about everything. This was because of different types of animals, harmful or harmless. Animals could harm anyone at any moment. People also said that here were poachers. I didn't know the meaning of that. So, I asked my mother and she said "Poachers are people who kill animals and sell their body parts in return of a huge sum of money. For them, animals are getting endangered day by day". I still remember an incident about a poacher. I really found him interesting. His name was Mohanlal. He had lost everything of his life when his wife passed away due to tuberculosis. He really loved his wife. After the death of his wife he got disheartened and started his job as a poacher. One fine day, he killed a young deer and was stalking away from the place with the deer. But suddenly, he realized that someone was following him. He turned back and saw a deer. He felt that it could be the mother of the young deer whom he killed. Mohanlal ignored her and started to move again. Still the conscious of doing a sin was hitting him hard. He went to his house and turned back again. To his surprise, he saw, the deer had him up to his house. He didn't have the heart of moving the deer away from its place, he was very tired too. So, he went inside his house and went for a sleep. The next day, when he stepped out of his house again, he saw the deer still sitting there. This time he really thought what he did was wrong. Since Mohanlal had lost his wife he could understand the feeling of losing a person who is very close. He felt guilty and took the deer inside his house. What actually happened he didn't know, but he could surely relate to the pain of the deer. He felt like if the deer was in tears. He took an oath without thinking twice to protect all animals from that very day. I wrote this story for everyone to read and understand the fact that God have created human beings for helping others and not for destroying. Human beings are the most capable of everything. If now we are not conserving anything, our next generations would be left with nothing. We are recklessly harming our environment. We should protect plants and animals. VERY SOON, WE WILL FACE GREAT TROUBLE IF IT GOES ON LIKE THIS. - STORY BY AISHIKA KHAN CLASS: VII SHRI SHIKSHAYATAN SCHOOL

title: The bond of love
text: Tina’s little brother Tim had grown up. He is now 3 years old. Tina used to play with him as he was a lovely, kind and nice boy. But they never shared things with each other. Tina had taught him all the English alphabets and Tim was very smart for his age. But once Tim grew up, they were always fighting. Tomorrow is his first day of school. Tim was excited but a little nervous too and. Tina said that school was bad. She read Tim bullying story books at breakfast to make him uncomfortable. When it was time to go to school, Tina got in the car with him. Her mom drove the car to Tim’s new school and Tina tried to make him afraid, all through. At school, Tim saw a little boy who was also nervous like him. He went and said hi to him. The boy’s name was Sam and they both became friends. Their teacher showed them shelves to put their things. Then Tim and Sam sat next to each other, learning their letters. When the first class was almost coming to an end, suddenly Sam started to cry. “I want my brother,” he wailed. Their teacher Mrs. Herret comforted him not to cry and that they will all go home soon. Then Sam was teased by a boy called Matron, who was a big bully. Matron said Sam was Sam Bam. He teased Tim too, calling him stinky pig. When school got over, Tim ran to Tina and hugged her. He told her how he was being teased. Their mother took them to the park. While their mother was talking to a friend, Tina heard Tim cry. She saw big boys bullying him and ran to stop them. But it was too late. The boys had already pushed Tim down. Their mother immediately, took him to the doctor. The doctor said he has a broken leg and will have to stay in bed for two months, as the fracture was very severe. He couldn’t go to school. The next day, Tina met her friend Sandy in school who was terribly upset because her younger brother had got Covid-19 and will be quarantined. When Tina came home, she saw Tim was sleeping. She started thinking what to do over the weekends. She woke him up and took care of him and wheeled him to the garden in his wheel chair and slowly but steadily their sibling jealousy turned into affection and they had the best days. Soon, they became the most loving siblings in their community.

title: Age Of Adolescence
text: Once there was a girl named Lalita and she was 10 years old. As usual, she woke up in the morning and started getting ready for school. She was feeling nauseous since morning but she tried to ignore it, trying not to bother her mother so early in the morning as she was making Lalita's breakfast and lunch. Lalita wore her school uniform, trotted downstairs, had her breakfast in a hurry, kissed her mom goodbye and something happened....her stomach gave a painful lurch but Lalita stuck to her plan of not bothering her mother and boarded her school bus. not to bother her mother so early in the morning as she was making Lalita's breakfast and lunch. Lalita wore her school uniform, trotted downstairs, had her breakfast in a hurry, kissed her mom She reached school and while she was climbing the stairs she felt as if her stomach was being squeezed like a sponge! She somehow reached her class and sat down. Her lurches felt as if someone was trying to pull her stomach out! She again tried to ignore it and started talking to her friends. By the end of the first class, Lalita's entire body felt sore. Her friends noticed her face and asked her, 'Hey! Are you okay?' Lalita replied, 'Yeah, ow! I'm o-okay.' They argued, 'You don't look okay, do you want us to tell ma'am?' 'NO!', Lalita exclaimed. someone was trying to pull her stomach out! She again tried to ignore it and started talking to her friends, When the first class started, Lalita started to feel that her whole body was sore. Her friends noticed her That's when the teacher noticed the commotion and asked, 'What's going on over there?' She instructed the students to resume reading the chapter, came to Lalita and asked 'What's going on? Lalita! You've gone so pale!' Lalita's eyes were rolling up because of the pain and before she could feel it, her hands and legs were numb. Suddenly her friends looked at her seat and shrieked. The teacher became alarmed and saw BLOOD on her seat! Lalita fainted. She opened her eyes to see the school medical room. There she saw her class teacher and mother beside her bed. Immediately she launched a series of questions at he r mother, 'What is happening?' 'Why am I bleeding?' 'Why does my tummy hurt so much?' She freaked out bursting to ask her mom, "What was happening?", "Why was she bleeding?", "Why did her tummy hurt so bad?" and "Mom! I think I have a bad illness! I' m scared! Take me home!" Her Her mom answered in a comforting voice 'Sweetie, your tummy hurting and blood leaking, it's a good sign!' Lalita asked 'Mom! How is it good?' Her mom said, 'See, your symptoms tell us that you have reached Puberty' 'Pu-what?' Lalita said, 'Puberty, It's a change which comes to our bodies, be it boy or girl. It's called 'Hormonal Changes.' It makes our voice sound different, and in a girl's case, your breasts also start forming. What is happening to you right now, that tummy ache and bleeding is called 'Period' and it will happen to you every month for a week. Lalita's mom replied. Lalita asked, 'Why do girls have periods?' Her mother replied, 'It's a sign, that you now are a big girl who has the power to be a mom in the future!' Lalita asked, 'Why do girls have periods?' Her mother replied, 'It's a sign that you now are a big girl who has the power to be a mom in the future!' Lalita said 'Oh! Stupid me! I was so scared but I'm happy I have my period!' Her mother smiled. Lalita took the rest day off and went home. Next day, she came to school and told her friends what happened to her and what her mother had explained there. Her friends said 'Um, okay, but we have you whom we can call a bit experienced to guide us about this but the other girls don't!' Lalita's face lit up and she clapped her fist to her palm and said 'AHA! We can start a 'Girls Help Forum'!' 'What's that?', one of her friends enquired. 'Forum means organisation and in this forum we can help girls in need and we'll hold meetings for girls with the permission of teachers, so that, we can tell them about this good thing which will happen to them, when they will be nearing the age of 10-11!' Lalita exclaimed. start a 'Girls Help Forum'!" "What's that?" One of her friends interrogated. "Forum means organisation and in this forum we can help girls in need and we'll hold meetings for girls with the permission Then, the girls started working as the 'Girls Help Forum' and they had helped, warned and educated numerous girls about periods. Later, Lalita dedicated her life to educate young girls about periods, sexual abuse and women rights. She soon opened an organisation and went from school to school spreading awareness among young girls. and went from school to school doing her job. - The End

title: photograph and a ticket
text: rina was visiting her grandfather's house during her summer holidays. the house was located in her mom's hometown.the place was very quite there were not many people that lived in that village, just a few houses but a lot of trees. rina got bored. all her friends were enjoying their holidays but she hadn't done fun over the holidays to tell her friends about it once the schools opens there were no parks or badmintion court or swimmimg pool she could go to. she couldn't find any video games or toys in the house. she searched the house to find something fun to do. she went upstairs and found stairs beside her grandfather's room leading upto the attic. she climbed the stairs and entered the room which looked like it had not been used in quite a while. it was dusty, dark and had a strange smell. rina pulled the curtains to let some light enter. she looked around the room and saw that it had old,damaged furniture she notices on the middle of the room there were book shelves. the shelves were filled books of different width, size and colors. she went there and picked up one of the books. ' ﻿all about meditation' ﻿was the title of the book. " who does meditation these days? that's boring" Rina kept it back and went to pick anothe book. ' ﻿ yoga guide', ' build good habits', ' manage time' ﻿none of those books interested Rina. suddenly one book caught her attention. it was an old book with its covered weared out. its was on shelf that was a bit hgh and out of rina's reach so she grabbed a stool and climbed on it to get the book the book looked as if it was older than any other stuff in the room. ' a small town ' said the title of the book. Rina flipped a page and found that it had a picture of the exact place she was staying at. '' isn't this the same place'' she said. she started flipping pages and got to know about the the town. she didn't realized when she had fallen asleep reading the book. she was found herself laying on the floor with the book infront of her.it was closed.'' how long was I asleep?'' rina picked up the book and found something inside it. she found a a yellow envelope. she opened it and found an old, black & white photograph. the photo was of a group of kids playing. rina wondered who it belonged to. she went downstairs and decided to ask her grandma. mom was busy in the garden while grandma was sitting on the verandah knitting a cap. she went over and asked grandma of the photo. '' oh my! where did you found this? '' grandma asked when she looked at the photo." i found it lying around " rina lied afraid to get in trouble for sneaking in the attic. " who's this in the photo?''she asked. " that's your grandpa, the one who's sitting in the right" grandma said. "really? i didn't recognized him at all!" rina was surprised to she her grandpa as a little kid. grandma looked at rina with a warm smile and said'' of course you wouldn't recognize him dear, he was only around 12 years old at that time"."is he playing with his friends? what are they all doing?" " they are playing kho-kho" said grandma. "i have heard about that game before how do you play it?" rina asked. "well' there are 2 teams one player goes to the other side and has to come back to his side after touching a player of the other team while everyone from that team tries to stop him from going back to his side".grandma explained to her." so that's how you play kho-kho.''rina quickly understood.she looked at the photograph of other kids playing kho-kho."grandma, what other games did you used to play when you were a kid?" rina was fascinated how kids played kho-kho and wanted to know more." in those days, we used to play hopscotch, gilli-danda, aankh-micholi, hide & seek and lots of other games too" grandma told rina. "oh! I've played aankh-micholi and hide & seek with my friends before but how do you play the other ones?" grandma explained to her how to play gilli-danda and even showed her how to play hopscotch. rina was very much delighted. " when i go back I"ll tell my friends about all these games and show them too!" rina decided. " that's a wonderful idea dear" grandma said to her with a smile." also i had something else that i also wanted to ask you about" "what is it, dear?" grandma asked. "what's this ticket for? I found it with the photograph" Rina asked holding up the ticket. grandma looked at the ticket for a little while and then said" oh, that's for village fair. It's an old ticket, they don't setup those nowadays "."what happens in a fair?"Rina got more curious now."there were shops that sold various kinds of clothes,sweets,toys all kinds of things. there were rides like merry-go-around, the giant wheel like the ones you see in an amusement parks. we used to save our pocket money for the fair.''grandma told Rina. mom was now done with watering plants and came to grandma and Rina."mom i wana go to a fair too"rina said to her mom."they don't setup fairs nowadays " mom said."but i wanna see those rides"rina said."alright, we'll take you to one only if you promise to do your studies" mom said with a smile. ''ok! i promise I'll to well in my studies" Rina said with confidence. at the beginning Rina thought her stay would be boring at her grandparent's house but it turned out that she learned a lot of things and it was fun. Rina now cannot wait to tell her friends.

title: Enigmatic Abduction
text: It was a beautiful Monday morning. Sarah was heading to catch the bus to go to her school. She was very excited because that day her friend Sana and she were going to receive their badges as they were assigned as head girls. On her bus, she heard some people talking about children vanishing into thin air on the way. She thought it was a rumor so she ignored it and kept walking. She reached her school and out of excitement she started searching for Sana. She asked everyone and searched every nook and corner of the school but to her surprise, she could not find her anywhere in the school. She also called Sana many times, but there was no reply, so she decided to ask about her from her mother. Her mother said she left her home long ago. Now Sarah become a little anxious about her friend. Sana's mother got worried and came to school enquiring about daughter and she was told that Sana didn't turn up that day. with the help of the school administration, she checked for camera footage but no trace of Sana was found. Ultimately a missing complaint was filed at the police station. Police started their investigation and all students and teachers were interrogated by police to find Sarah’s friend but no trace of her was found. Days and weeks passed but there was no news about Sana. Sarah locked herself in a room always thinking about her friend. She was like a body without life. She went into memory lane where she got stuck in their beautiful memories, like a visit to a park where they went deep inside and saw a beautiful mansion where ultimately, they got a scary feeling and they went back home. She was also evoked by their visit to the arcade where they had a lot of fun. Her tears rolled down her cheeks when she recalled the day they went to the mall with their moms and brought a lot of things like their favorite anime t-shirts, friendship bracelets, same phone covers, and many more she also recollected the memory of that morning when they went to the movie, they ate a lot of things and enjoyed a lot the whole day. As she was so very much attached to her friend, she ultimately lost interest in everything, she started missing her classes, she did not go to the park neither she used to sit and enjoy herself with her family and friends. She felt lonely as only the view of her friend could only help her bring a spark to her eyes. Her parents and teachers were now more worried about her so they tried to console her in every possible way. Once in school when she was in her English class, they were reading a story about a child becoming a detective to find his small cat. By that story, she was encouraged and she was determined that she would surely find her friend so she started her research about kidnappings. After a whole lot of searching, she got many clues. She got to know that many children who were 16 to 18 years old were getting kidnapped. All those missing children had something in common, they all were grumpy and all the children were kidnapped in the evening. Only Sana was the one who was kidnapped in the morning and was not at all grumpy instead she was as sweet as honey. Then Sarah got an idea. She knew a grumpy boy who was 17 so she started chasing him and observing him at school. She was sure that the boy would be the next target who would be kidnapped. She planned that she will follow the kidnapper and to her surprise when he was playing in the park suddenly, he disappeared without leaving a trace. Sarah was bewildered because she lost a chance of reaching her friend. She went to her home and one of their memories was haunting her mind again and again. She got stuck somewhere with her memories with Sana in that scary Mansion. That mansion was suspicious. So, she went there and checked. When she entered, she saw a lot of paintings and sculptures that were creepy. She decided to go deep inside. She entered a room and saw a wall that had pictures of many missing children. Sarah started to hear weird noises. She got scared. The noises were like they are asking for help. They were crying and screaming. Sarah got astonished and fainted. The next moment when she woke up, she was in a hospital. With her mom next to her tearing up while seeing her wake up. She asked her mom the reason she was there. Her mom said “Sarah I was so worried about you. You are here because we found you passed out in the park. You are here for the last 2 days. Thank God you woke up. Sarah was trying to recollect what happened after she was in the mansion but she couldn’t. When she was discharged from the hospital. She went home and tried to recall what happened in the mansion, suddenly some thoughts hit her mind, a flashback where she saw a reflection of two people with covered faces in the mirror hanging in front of her. She reminded that the girl was standing still without any moment while the boy came toward Sarah and she passed out. while she visualized that scene once again, she fell fast asleep. She woke up all sweaty and scared. She had a nightmare about the mansion she saw that a girl was crying and asking for help and a boy forcefully closed her mouth and took her into a spooky room. The girl was trying to escape. The girl reminded Sarah of Sana Sarah was getting ready for school when she saw a picture of her and Sana her eyes got teary. Then she was reminded of her cousin who was in the police she thought of taking his help to find Sana and solving the mystery of the missing children. She visited her cousin after her school. She told him everything she knew, and he agreed to help Sarah. Then he along with Sarah went to the mansion. They searched the whole mansion for some clue but unfortunately, all went in vain. That night Sarah screamed while sleeping and her mom came running into her room. Sarah woke up as she saw a nightmare again but it was different this time. She saw the boy going behind the mansion and entering a secret entrance. She saw that the man is approaching her with a knife to stab her and all in sweat she woke up. Sarah told her cousin about what she saw in her dreams. They decided to go there once again in the evening and this time Sarah’s cousin thought to take some of his police friends for help. As they entered there was smoke all over the place, it was coming from a room. They went into that room and saw the boy doing some prayers and all of the children’s hands and legs were tied with ropes including Sana’s their mouth was sealed shut with duct tape, and the police officers got their guns out and pointed them out toward the guy. The guy was in jail, all the children were in the hospital and their parents were informed about them. When the guy was inquired, he said that he was doing black magic on the grumpy children to make them sweet and that’s why he kidnapped Sana so that he could steal all her qualities and put her qualities in the all-grumpy children to turn them nicer like Sana. Now once again Sarah had a smile on her face as her friend Sana was standing beside her. Everything was back to normal but something was weird. Sana was not the same girl now. She was acting uncanny and ghostly. She was not like before. What happened to her? Why was she acting strange this thought is still troubling Sarah………
author: TANISHKA SACHDEVA

title: The Elephant and a Farmer
text: Long ago, a beautiful baby elephant was born in a forest. He was white in color. All the elephants of the forest came to see and bless the baby.Every elephant said that “this baby is as white as the moon. The elephant herd was happy to see that a new member had come in their family. Soon, the white elephant grew up. But He was often sad to see that other calves of his age were selfish, greedy and cruel. They would hurt the weaker animals and even steal their food. Getting dismayed by all this, the white elephant decided to leave the herd. Then he settled in a faraway forest where he began to live a peaceful life, helping and caring for other animals. Soon the white elephant became friend to many animals. One day a farmer lost his way and wandered into the forest. Suddenly he heard a noise. It was the white elephant. The farmer was frightened and began to run for his life, he thought “He is chasing me and my end is near”. Then the farmer hid in a cave after that the farmer heard the elephant say,” O friend don't be scared, tell me why you look so worried. Then the farmer came out of the cave and said,”Friend, I have lost my way and am feeling hungry and tired. Then the white elephant says that his home was close by and the farmer can stay there for a while.The white elephant then carried the farmer to his house.When both of them arrived,the farmer was hungry. So the elephant gave the farmer some fruits to eat.When the fruit was finished the elephant and the farmer slept in the cave where the elephant lived. On his way to the home of the farmer there was a market where he saw a model. He asked the shopkeeper about its price.The shopkeeper said,’’two hundred gold coins ‘’.The farmer asked,’’why is it so costly?’’. The shopkeeper replied,’’ because it is made up of elephant tusk. Now the farmer was thinking,’’Can I go back and ask my friend for his tusk? I can become very rich ‘’. I must go back to the forest.So the next morning, the farmer left his home and reached the forest. When the farmer reached the elephant’s cave. He said,’’ O’ friend, please help me, I am under a huge debt. If you can give your tusk i would be able to pay off my debt.’’ The kind hearted elephant agreed and let the farmer chop off his one of the beautiful tusks with an axe. When he had chopped off the tusk,he went straight to the market and sold off the tusk at a very high price. He then brought expensive clothes and jewels and all that he wanted for himself. Soon all the money was spent but now the farmer wanted more.So the next morning, the farmer again went to the elephant and the generous elephant allowed the farmer to chop off his other tusk also though he knew it would be painful. Without a care for pain that elephant was going through, thee greedy farmer chopped off the tusk and after that he left the forest. He was so blinded by greed and selfishness that he didn’t even turn around to see the poor elephant. Suddenly, the farmer felt the ground under his feet quaking and then there appeared a crack in the earth. The farmer fell in it and huge hot flames he tried to escape but in vain. Soon he was pulled inside and disappeared into the earth. I will tell you a secret that white elephant was none other than lord Ganesha.
author: Anushka Patil
illustrator: Anushka Patil; Meenal Singh; Swathi Sambasivam

title: My Home Holds Us All
text: My home is a pile of boxes and so many doors and windows. A door belongs to our family, too. But my home is spread all around. It is so much larger than our little flat. My home is bright, sunny, dark and damp. Dry sometimes, and sometimes wet. It is yellow, red, pink and all kinds of green. My home is quiet sometimes, but mostly loud. It barks, chimes and sings, too! Can you hear Kaalu the dog, Pakya and his cawing lot, Maaya and her kittens? Aaji’s pickles, a whole chatter of squirrels and the dusty afternoon sun — my home holds us all. My home is Asmi, Falak, Roshan, Samay, Jhilmil. And so many doors and windows. My home is perfect for hide-and-seek!
author: Siddhi   Vartak

title: The Lost Friend
text: The Lost Friend Zoya had an argument last night. His argument slowed down the very next day when she saw a teddy on her bedside given by his/her parents to mat her happy. But, one day she lost that teddy. She used to live alone and always be sad. Now, Zoya was not going to be alone anymore as someone very special was coming to her home. It was her younger sibling. Few months later, When Zoya came back from school. She saw her mom lying with a new-born baby girl. Her father had brought many sweets that day. When she touched the baby’s cheek she was reminded of the soft fur of her teddy. This time, she didn’t become sad and was very happy. Few years went on... Now Zara was two years old. The family went to an amusement park. Zoya was supposed to care of Zara. There was the world’s highest slide and only adults were allowed for it. So, their parents went for it and Zoya and Zara were standing and waiting for them in that huge crowd. Zoya held Zara’s hand tightly. But, suddenly she realized that her hands became empty and the wrest moment of her life came true when she lost her sister. Zoya just suffered from a mental attack. Her family tried every way to find Zara out. But they were unable to get Zara.God wanted something else to happen. After a treatment of four years. Zoya became normal. Zoya became very awful at her studies due to this. All her classmates were in grade 10 th and she was demoted to grade 5 th. One thing was there that her parents never blamed her for anything, they never wanted to see Zoya sad. Zara just knew her own name and Zoya’s name to pronounce. Few years went on in constant search. Now, Zoya was in her college, 3 rd year, her heart was still her sister but it almost seemed impossible. Still her hopes werealive. One day, she saw a new girl coming to her college and she started getting flashbacks of her own lost sister. Her hopes were now getting higher and higher to find her sister. She made that girl her best friend.Her name was also Zara. Zara told that she was separated from her family in her childhood and was taken to a hostel. She was unknown to the people who took her to a hostel in other country and now she was sent back here to sustain on her own. Zoya was now confirmed about her sister but she kept quiet. It was Zoya’s birthday. Zara came up there with an old-looking teddy and it was almost similar to zoya’s lost teddy. While giving that teddy to zoya, she said few words to her, “I am giving you my most precious thing as you gift as you totally seem like my own sister. Even you name is similar tohers. This teddy is only the things which is with me from the day I was separated from my family. Whenever I look up at this teddy, I never feel alone. Today I am giving you this, please always stake care of this.” Zoya’s eyes got filled with tears and she told Zara the whole story from her childhood till the day. They both hugged each other and finally got reunited!

title: Imaginary night became true
text: One day a girl who was only of 4 years old. Her father was an army person and her mother was a microsoft engineer. She was not cute as her brother but her dreams was at another level. When in every morning her father gets ready for office she liked to see him as her dream was to become like her father. She like to see her father in army uniform. Every night she slept and thought about that what she will become in future. Years by years and days by days passed but she continued her seeing dreams to be an army person. Now she was of 8 years old and she started study and working hard like an army person. One night she was thinking that '' if I could be really as my father then I will be able to complete my father's dream. MY father's dream was to became an army person because he was belonging from a very poor family and couldn't afford sufficient food to his family but he wanted to be in a high post but unfortunately he retired and his dream stayed as a dream only but now I will do that''. after thinking she slept. There were some similarities between her and her father like - to stay silent, to play outdoor games, to watch news, to work for a long time and more. Her mother told her that she is a girl and she was not suppose to work like a boy but she thought that there is no difference between boys and girls and she did all the work which a boy is suppose to do. From that day she began to wrote her own diary in which she has wrote her dreams which she thought at the nights. Years passed and she grown up she was very good in her studies and chose science after class 10th. She worked harder and more harder and finally after 4 years she got a chance at the best university of that state. She loved to read books and write by her own imagination. Now after getting her certificate in which she was certified as an army person she went for training. Now after her hard working since 4 years till now gave a result that she became a commanding officer and earned much more money then her father. Now she has completed her dreams and built a bungalow in which her whole family could live happily. This how her imaginary nights became true. THANK YOU I HOPE YOU LIKED IT

title: Ammu Goes Missing!
text: It was an early Sunday morning. The sun blazed brightly and the birds were singing their sweet melodies. Manu was fast awake. He went to his sister, Ammu's room to wake her up but found that she was not there! "Ammu, where are you?" cried Manu as he searched for her. Hearing Manu shout, his mother woke up. "Manu, what happened? Where is Ammu?", she asked him. Manu, what happened? Where is Ammu? Manu was very worried. He couldn't find Ammu anywhere in the neighborhood. He decided to call his friends and search for her outside the village, near the border of the village to the city. Amma, she is missing! Radha and Ramu were playing cricket, but as they heard manu's shocking message, without a second thought they ran with the bat to find Ammu. Ramu and his friends asked everybody in the Bellflower park if they had seen a little girl with a curly hair anywhere, but none of them had. As they were about to go to the next place in search of Ammu a little girl approached them. She asked in a sweet voice, "Are you looking for a little girl with curly hair, a pink skirt and a blue dress?" Manu immediately replied in a joyful voice, "Yes,yes,yes! That is indeed Ammu, do you know where she is?" The girl replied, "Yes, I do, she went to the Lorance Library!" "Thank you very much!", sighed Manu and went in search of Ammu to the Lorance Library with his friends. There they asked the librarian if she had seen Ammu by telling her about Ammu's hair and dress. The librarian was quiet and thought for a while, then she asked, "Hmmm...There was a girl like that who came today morning, well, does she love books about city life?" Manu replied, "Yes,yes,yes! She loves them very much! It is indeed Ammu! Do you know where she went? "Oh yes! She took a book on city life from the library and said that she was going to the city for an adventure and would write down her adventure in her own words and publish it as a book. She also promised me that she will give a copy of the book to the library. Most probably she has reached the city by now." said the librarian. Hearing this, Manu and his friends ran to the vast city! "New people, big houses and many vehicles! How will we find Ammu in this very big place?" exclaimed Radha. "Don't feel hopeless Radha, we will find a way" said Ramu. "Manu, Ammu loves sweets, am I right?" continued Ramu in a very hopeful voice. Yes,yes,yes! She can't pass a day without it! She must be in a sweet shop nearby! "Yes,yes,yes! I know what you mean Ramu! To the sweet shop! The three of them ran to the nearest sweet shop! Manu shouted, "Here is Ammu! As said by the librarian, she was writing a story about the city eating her favorite sweets - Jalebis and Gulab Jamuns! The four of them gave a copy of the book to the library and reached back to the village. Ammu recited the whole story to her mother but rather than scolding her, her mother praised her for her courage and story writing skills after she read Ammu's book. Not only her mother, but all the villagers were proud to have a little author within their village! If you are thinking about Manu, he is fast asleep after the tiring journey.
author: Adithya Pradeep

title: Motherhood
text: It was mid-afternoon, around 3 o'clock. It was a moderately hot day. She had four hours to go before she would reach her destination, Bangalore. Reena was a professor at Gauhati University. She was travelling to Bangalore to present a seminar on the topic ‘The Masks of Majuli’. She had a good job as an anthropology professor and was an independent woman. She loved exploring new things and learning about the depths of the world and beyond. “Peace at last!” Reena uttered to herself. She had two children, Arvind aged 14 and Sohan aged 6. Her husband, Narendra was a supportive husband and a doting father. But since he was away mostly away on official tours, it was she who had to manage her home, work and children. She tried her best, but many times she felt overwhelmed by the task of managing her two misfits! Arvind being the teenage lad, often sulked at his mother’s choice. Reena often found it difficult to judge his mood and cope up with his tantrums. Like last week, she had selected a bright blue shirt for him to wear to his friend’s birthday, but he just sulked at his mother’s choice and wore another one to the party. Sometimes she would cook up his favourite ‘mac and cheese, but he would not touch the meal. He would also be constantly at odds with her and argue about literally everything. Sohan, on the other hand, was a different ball game altogether. Being the younger child, he was very stubborn and he reacted at the slightest pretext. He always wanted to have his way and Reena found it difficult to handle him with tact and patience all the time. At the slightest scolding from her, Sohan would call up his father to complain about how his mother mistreated him! Arvind, being the teenage lad, often sulked at his mother’s choice. Reena was rarely able to judge his mood and cope up with his tantrums. Like last week, she had selected a bright red shirt for him to wear to his friend’s birthday. But Arvind just sulked at his mother’s choice and wore another shirt to the party. Sometimes she would also cook up his favourite ‘Mac and Cheese ', but he would not touch the meal. He would also be constantly at odds with her and argue about everything! Sohan, on the other hand, was a different ball game altogether. Being the younger child, he was very stubborn and he reacted at the slightest pretext. He always wanted to have his way and Reena found it difficult to handle him with tact and patience all the time. At the slightest scolding from her, Sohan would call up his father to complain about how his mother mistreated him! “How I wish they would grow up fast! ” Reena muttered to herself for the umpteenth time. Reena walked down the aisle to find her seat. “21 F” she muttered to herself. It was a window seat and she was quite fond of window seats. It was not because of the window beside her seat, but because she wanted to be the farthest one away from the aisle. She quickly walked beside everyone and found her seat. She had only bought a handbag with her, and she kept the bag underneath her seat. In a few minutes, the other two co-passengers came. They were an elderly couple. The flight attendant demonstrated the safety instructions as Reena rested comfortably and the flight began to take off. Reena walked down the aisle to find her seat. “21 F,” she mumbled to herself. It was a window seat. She was quite fond of window seats because she liked enjoying the scenery that came into view as the plane flew. She quickly walked down the aisle and took her seat. In a few minutes, the other two co-passengers also came and took their seats beside her. They were an elderly couple. The flight attendant demonstrated the safety instructions as Reena rested comfortably. The plane then took off. A slight sobbing sound coming from near her broke her reverie. The elderly lady sitting next to her was looking at a photograph while wiping away her tears. The elderly man was trying to console her. Reena gently held the lady’s hand and asked “Is something wrong, mam? Why are you crying? Here, take this tissue and wipe away your tears.” Reena said as she took out a tissue from her bag and gave it to the lady. The lady wiped her tears and thanked her.” I have a son who is now settled in Bangalore with his family” she said. “We, me and my husband, raised him with much love and care. But now he is so busy. He rarely picks up our calls or calls us himself. I haven’t even heard from him in so long. I miss him so much…” She added, weeping uncontrollably. The elderly man had to take her to the cabin washroom, as she couldn’t control herself. Reena watched on in shock, trying to digest the situation. As the couple came back, the man sat her wife next to the aisle and he sat in the middle seat. The man continued the lady's words, “You see, if you have children, cherish their childhood and the moments you spend with them. Once they can stand on their own feet, things may be very different from what they used to be. They grow up very fast, and nobody knows what the future holds in store.” He pointed to the photograph of a five-year-old girl, who was the couple’s granddaughter. The words of the elderly couple completely shocked Reena. She began to rethink her views, regarding her children. She wanted them to grow up very fast, but what if they have no time for her in the future? Will they find ways to move away from her? Will they even remain in contact with her? What if she was in the same boat as the elderly couple? Reena was deep in thought throughout the remainder of the flight, trying to comprehend the situation. When she landed in Bangalore, she immediately collected her suitcase from the conveyor belt and called up home. A light smile played around her face. Arvind was on the other end of the call. Reena exclaimed “Hi dear! I miss you both already. I will get you your favourite spiderman video game that you wanted and asked me to bring when I get home.” Arvind replied gleefully “Thanks mom, you are the best!” Reena then asked him to pass the phone to Sohan. “Mom, have you reached Bangalore? How big is the city?” Sohan asked. Reena replied with a slight giggle "Yes dear, Bangalore is huge. By the way, I will make you your favourite pizza as soon as I get home, ok?" “Do you promise?” “Yes beta, I promise. I will also bring you your favourite hot wheels set.” Reena then asked Sohan to put the phone on the loudspeaker. “Ok boys, I promise that I will be back as soon as possible, and bring you your goodies. I love you both!” “We love you too, Ma!”, Arvind and Sohan’s voices echoed over the phone, which was soothing to Reena’s ears. She then made her way out of the airport. She was feeling very happy and light-hearted. She made a promise to herself that she would cherish every moment with her kids and never regret not spending enough time with them. Yes, she had done something special today to cherish her motherhood!
author: Ariz Zaman
illustrator: Ajay Hembron; Anjali Kamat; Diya Ullas; Google India; Krupa Thakur-Patil; Nyambura Kariuki; Sachin Pandit; Sadhna Prasad; Saheb Ram  Tudu; Sanjay Kisku; Sheshadri Mokshagundam; Swathi Sambasivam; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya; Visvesvaraya National Memorial Trust

title: Our Imperfections
text: This story introduces the flaws of the existing education systems worldwide. Each character is given a role of personification reflecting how society treats them because of the standards they have set for each individual. Tashi, the Koala, is brought up in the system based on an animal setting. Discover how she turns the system and how she inspires all. In the lush green forest of West Siang, Arunachal Pradesh lived a family of gleeful and scholarly koalas within the animal community. They were the key advisors of the Lion King. Among the Koalas, lived Tashi a not-so-intelligent Koala. It was humiliating for the family that she dreaded going to the forest school. "C'mon Tashi, get going, it is time to go school." "But Ma...", said the young Koala, "I hate school" Her dad filed in, ''The idea of sending you to school is discomfiting, we live in constant fear of the reputation of our family... please don't be such an embarrassment to us" Tears of humiliation filled her eyes, but she dared not to cry, she was brave. "I'll get going them" she managed to say. Her parents chimed in"Have a great day in school" "Whatever, Ma and Pa, Bye," she said calmly. She murmured under her breath."What a pain in the ass" Well, her pessimism was valid. You see, her school was rather uncanny. Here every animal had to climb a tree, whether it be a monkey or an alligator and every animal had to swim, whether it be a fish or a snail. And not to mention, everyone had to study animal science. Seldom did anyone ace this curriculum, but many animals were doing okay. The fish was a great swimmer. The Monkey was quick while climbing trees, and the owl and the fox were the wisest of all. Birdies could fly, and the tiger and lion were the most affluent hunters in school. Only Tashi could not fit in. "I am so lame," she thought. Her friend was a limbless platypus, Tsering.I bet he thought the same. The duo was called, "Dumbos, perfect for each other", by others. They did not bother as they had a talent of making things and advertising it. The teachers didn't mind the bullying, Nevertheless, they pushed young Tashi in their ideas of perfection, as Tashi came from a glorious family of intellectuals. As for Tsering, the platypus, they gave up hope as his family was considered to be absurd. Tashi's grades in swimming and Tsering's grades in climbing were helpless. On one occasion Mr Tenzin, their Science teacher played a fundamental role in breaking their friendship. When asked what was his reason for his action, he simply replied, "You have to ask yourself young Tashi, would you rather be comforted by a lie or strengthened by a truth?" He continued. "Tashi you can only do better if you dispose off defective friends from your life, if you stay with a rotten fruit, you will rot, and look at you you are already rotting." Tsering and Tashi were sick of the treatment. The people they knew since their childhood were judgmental of them. They were hurt, but they could not do any thing about it. They faced their Principal Mrs Dorjee, as the name suggests, she was like a diamond to them. She could only understand their potential. They cried bitterly about their pathetic situation. "My lovely kids, just wait for the right time and you shall shine", she comforted them. They thought she was bluffing as they knew they were outcasts of this society, they were imperfect for this society. Years passed but nothing changed, the mates were seen as flawed in the forest and Tashi knew she let her family down. But in this serene forest, came a muscular hideous hunter who poached an excess of animals, including the Lion king as well. Followed by this monstrosity, there was an episode of acid rain in the forest. The rich canopy, became depilated and bald, near the Yomgo river many animals' flesh rotted and was exposed. The river had a dark apparition of bloodish red. Life for the animals in West Siang got despondent. Everything got destroyed, shelters, food stock, and even the school were shown no mercy. Every establishment was shattered. Loved ones died and their partners suffered the most. Their King left them. No one had high hopes for the future. But Tashi was not going to back down. She contacted other Arunachali forest animals for support conditioning of shelter and food. With her gaining popularity, she brought all the animals together and in unity, they established their academic institutions. Her mismatched eyes which were once a target for bullies now gleamed with heroic intuition. She stated, " Tough times never last, but tough people do and now quit being sad " ''You understand that life is meaningless but we must take pleasure in the moments we live in. And for you that is on this blue blanket" she said while tucking a fawn. "It is not how much you lived, it is for what you've lived for," she added. And the fawn nodded, she did not understand but she was drawn to the tranquil tone of the sermon. Mrs Dorjee gave her a reassuring look. Tashi braced herself, it's been over a year and now she was the principal of her very own school. There needs to be no guesswork that the school's curriculum is really commendable. Here, just birds fly, just monkeys climb trees, only the tigers and lions hunt, and only platypuses and alligators swim. And not to forget the animals of this school study animal science, as they did back in the day. Many animals aced in this curriculum and in no time Tashi's school was the most prestigious in the forests of Arunachal Pradesh. The animals who treated Tashi poorly in school apologised to her. Can you think how she reacted? She was a nice Koala, she forgave them, as to forgive is divine. The animals wanted to apologise to the wide-eyed looking, limbless platypus. But she informed them that, he visited the harpies of the pristine fountains in his teen years and never coming back with the help of a local fox. They felt more guilty than ever and cried. After a month, the hunter, who poached the animals of West Siang was curious about how the forest was re-established without any human help. The hunter became lean, his teeth were crooked yet clean and carried a positive aura, unlike before. Many animals shivered with fear upon his arrival but they were valiant. This time pride of lions and lionesses made a circle around the hunter. The monkeys with their sharp teeth were ready to attack. They were working in a united group, unlike when the poacher came before. But Tashi understood the man meant no harm, she dispersed the crowd and thanked them for believing in unity. The hunter was going to pass out. Tashi took him into her office and asked him why he had returned. He innocently answered that he was inquisitive about how the animals re-established the forest. Tashi calmly clarified, "We've got some help from others" He apologised for his questionable acts. "Save it for later, Sonam sir" she directly addressed him."What's going on in life? You've changed" He explained that since childhood he faces hatred, people called him, a "defect of society", good for nothing" He wanted to prove them wrong, he wanted to do something brave. But this is where he went wrong. In order to show off, he destroyed lives of numerous beings. He wasn't brave, he was terrible and nasty. He explained after he disrupted the forest, he was all over the news. The government fined him a huge amount of money and to pay that his back nearly snapped, he had to sacrifice half of his life to pay for it. T ashi thought about how same their childhood was, but they now had a very different present. She was loved but the latter was still detested. She felt genuinely pitiful for him Some days, the peace of the forest was broken again. This time a group of youth entered. The animals gathered and were ready to attack. But in time among the people, she identified Sonam. She ushered to the front of the pride, and expressed boldly, "What is this all about? ","Sonam kindly justify this act." He smiled, exposing his jagged teeth and calmly stated that he was truly sorry and he meant it, he had called these enthusiastic youth to plant trees in the canopy of the exquisite forest. The animals were quite thrilled. "But at what cost?" asked an owl dubiously. "At no cost deary owl, we are grateful about how essential this forest is for the state." And just to prevent any future man-made disaster, they signed a declaration which forbade any human to poach or pollute any wildlife being and forest resources. And so the youth grew trees and provided additional food. But Sonam was not done yet. Inspired by Tashi, he created a school where athletes were separately honed properly. Only debators were provided with articulation training, artists were encouraged for their artefacts, and mathematicians were educated. Every student had a scholastic and/or a co-scholastic club tailored for them and their talents were polished. He was despised by the common masses for his ways, as they stuck to the slow way of modern learning, but that did not deter him at all. He tried much harder to make a better curriculum after much time he finally got the recognition of India's education minister. His school was deemed the best in India. The school even made it to the national news. Enrollment was quadrupled within months. The school soon became a co-ed boarding school for all and was considered to be the most prestigious. Sonam earned fame and quickly became a millionaire. Look how the fortune turned. He lived a pauper life, but now he could be clad in luxurious fur. But he was modest, he dressed simply but thought in a rich way. The school's walls were clad in slogans. After a week of the animal and human school's anti-bullying campaign. Sonam got a call from the animals of West Siang, that Tashi was no more, she died in her sleep peacefully. He dropped his cell phone and rushed from his cosy, neat office to the forest. Sonam made it to the forest, breathing heavily and pickled with thorns, barefooted, for he admired Tashi. He steered to the front, knelt and hugged the coffin she was in. He was the only one to do so, as no one touches the dead. The animals hugged him. And that was it. The path was concluded there. But he was glad that he could share his infinity with her. ﻿ ﻿Sonam was anxious, it was his first time addressing such a big gathering of dignitaries. He was the fastest-growing billionaire. He started by citing Ken Kessey, "We get so tuned in that we can ride the waves of our existence and never get tossed because we become waves", remembering Tashi. He went on about how is he in this position to address them all. The gathering was awestruck. They were enlightened by him. But do you know who was the most inspired? Little Yobin was. He etched he would want to work with the academic sector of the country Once he finished, the hushed room boomed with life. Everyone gave him a standing ovation After the elite assemblage, he went home and connected with his mumma via an online medium. His mum was a biologist. A splendid one. He shared."Mumma, Mr Sonam is a great man, he talked about Ms Tashi the Koala I want to be like them one day. Will I be able to?" "Why not honey?" What would have become of Sonam if he never stepped into the forest of West Siang after his scandalous hunting act? What would have happened if Tashi and the animals wouldn't forgive him? Well, one thing is for sure, compassion is met with compassion, and whatever you do, accomplish it with no doubts! IMAGE COURTESY,

title: MY UPSIDE DOWN DAY, WHEN I WENT TO WORK AND MY MOM WENT TO SCHOOL (IN MY CLASSROOM)
text: I am Prakriti.I live with my parents and grandparents. My parents love me a lot. Getting all my wishes fulfilled without throwing slightest of tantrums, I got spoiled. I would live like a princess and would not listen to my parents. I grew old and so my wishes. I would not care whether my parents have the resource or how they had to arrange for my needs. One day I was awaken by the screaming alarm. Rubbing my eyes as I came out of the room still sleepy. My mom was in my school uniform so was my dad. Grandmother had taken a nursery rhyme book and was reciting it loudly. Laughing out loud, I asked my parents what it was. Since when have the offices started organizing fancy dress competition for their employees? I asked. To my surprise my mother came up to me and asked for the lunchbox. Her hair was untied. My father was polishing his pair of black shoes. They again asked for food. I couldn’t process whatever was happening so I asked what the matter was and why were they behaving out of the blues. I got the biggest shock of my life when they told me that they had always been going to St. Martin’s School and that the school bus is about to arrive and that I still have not prepared lunch. I thought it was a nightmare, so I pinched myself to confirm but it would not work. The school bus arrived but there was no sign of my uniform. My parents ran and boarded the school bus. To my amazement, the bus had students of my parents’age.I got an unknown phone call. My boss, as the person on the other side of the call would call himself told me to come to the office. Am I in coma, what happened to me, the world? I was trying to recollect all the memories before losing my senses. Taking the address, I reached the office in my casuals. My boss appeared to be an adult. He briefed me about the tasks. Having no idea about it, I somehow managed to complete the work and came back home. It was a tiring day. My parents were back home. I gave them bread and butter. They started throwing tantrums. I had to clean my home as my parents made it messy. I didn’t even get time to drink a glass of water. It was dinner time and we had fruit salad. I must have lost my mind or would have woken up from the coma. If it’s the case, I would want to stay there. I began to accept the fact that children work outside and elders study at school. This happened for many days. I began to realize that I had been very wrong in the first place. I had never cared to ask my parents about their feelings and help them in domestic chores. I would spend all the resources given to me without a second thought and would misuse it. My parents would work hard every day and I never valued their efforts. I began to repent and cry. My sobs start to get louder and louder. Someone shook me up and was caressing my hair. Wiping away the tears, I hugged my mother and said, don’t do this to me please....’what did we do? Why are you crying? We are not forcing you to go to the school. It’s Sunday today, you can sleep. Did you see a nightmare? My parents asked. And indeed it was.
author: Ananya Agarwal

title: The Value of Family
text: There was once a family who wouldn't stop quarreling. On some days when Akshay, the man of the house would come home from work, he would take all his frustration and exhaustion out on his wife by snapping at her and ordering her around. On other days, when his wife, Harita was tired of cooking and cleaning, she would yell and thunder at her husband. Almost every day they would yell at their son, Laksh for mistakes he hadn't made or for no reason at all. Laksh would often come home from school to see his parents fighting. He would walk straight into his room and slam the door shut without even greeting anyone. It was a normal Saturday morning, Laksh’s parents were furious, and he went to play with his neighbors. He lived in a huge apartment complex in Bangalore and had many friends who lived there. He was walking through the corridor when he spotted a man dressed in an Army uniform with a nametag. Laksh looked him up on the internet and found out that he was a warrior from the famous Kargil War. His name was Colonel Vir Singh. Who is he? And why is he dressed in an Army uniform? Laksh introduced. As Laksh spoke out his mind to Colonel Vir Singh, he felt a weight being lifted off his shoulders. The understanding officer offered to try to help Laksh improve his relationship with his parents. The only time Laksh’s parents weren't fighting was when one was sleeping and the other watching the television. Um... Hi! Would you mind talking for a second? Hi dear! Of course is there anything in particular you would like to talk about Laksh was very lucky when he walked into the house when his father was sound asleep, and his mother was enjoying her favourite series on the T.V. With crossed fingers he asked his mother if he could invite the officer home and without a thought, his mother agreed! It was the happiest he had felt in an eternity. Later that day the officer arrived. He introduced himself to Laksh’s parents and took a seat. After talking for about half an hour he brought up how the officers bonded with one and other. He explained how everyone there missed their families and hence treated their corps and regiment as their family. He said that he didn’t understand how some families treat own family members as dirt as in the army the people who you aren’t related to are your everything. At first, they didn’t see any connection with themselves in the words he spoke, but they soon realized how they had been treating each other and their son. They sprang out of their seats and thanked him. They quickly excused themselves and ran to their Laksh! They apologized to him and for the first time they meant it. Laksh went to thank the officer, only to see the seat empty.
author: Avyaya Vepa

title: Shruti's New Home
text: Memorial Trust Today was a new and fresh start for Shruti. She had recently moved from her little house in Palampur to Delhi. Indeed it was a massive change for the little seven-year-old girl to call a new place her home. When Shruti reached her new house, she noticed some children playing in the park. They seemed to be that of her age, and Shruti, being the ecstatic little girl she was, got out of the car and ran to meet the new children. One of the five children, Arti, introduced herself to Shruti and they quickly became good friends. Little Shruti had to leave all her friends, family, teachers, pets, and neighbors at a very young age. There was a seating area near the window on the wall to the right of the fireplace. As she went further she saw the beautiful kitchen with stairs leading to the second floor in front of it. Shruti entered her new room in awe. A bed in the middle of the room and a desk beside it. In front was a dressing table with a wardrobe door next to it. She slowly walked on the stone path leading to the door of her new house and scanned the living room carefully. While on the way to her new school, she was excited but also anxious about all the new things she would have to experience. As she entered the massive building, she was already planning everything she was going to do. It was the first period. Shruti struggled to answer simple questions she could quickly answer at her old school and sat alone during lunch break. Shruti pushes open the wooden door to enter her brand-new classroom. On the wall facing the door was a well-built bulletin board with drawings the children had made. There was a big window on the left wall and cute hangings on the right. After all, the little seven-year-old girl missed her old life, friends, and school, in Palampur. Anjana elucidated to her daughter that change is always hard at first, messy in the middle, and gorgeous at the end. After this, Shruti was motivated and decided that she would improve herself and won't give up. When Shruti reached back home, she was unhappy. Her mom, Anjana, asked her how her day went. Shruti explained to her mom how she had no friends to sit with and was hesitating while answering questions. Slowly and gradually, Shruti changed. Now she had started to socialize and was more confident. She was now the girl she wanted to be, and although Shruti was no longer at her older home, it always remained in her heart as she grew up. The next day, Shruti entered her class and introduced herself to the other children instead of being shy and introverted. She studied hard and quickly caught up on all the curriculum she had missed. Shruti tried her best to go from being a quiet and meek little girl to a confident and outgoing person.
author: Vanessa Kaul
