title: Humanity Changes With Time.
text: The earth is round in shape. In various parts of this round shape various different things are happening. Today, I am going to introduce my readers to a very small portion of this round Earth. The place was in Asia, if we go deep enough, it is in India and deeper to it, it's in West Bengal and the deepest part is Padyanagar village. This whole story is about a family who had recently shifted to Padyanagar village. It was a Brahmin family. This story is of a long time ago. The Brahmin had a son named Gopu and his name was Ramesh Banerjee. His Wife's name was Sriti Banerjee. Many many years back, people used to respect Brahmins a lot. In this Padyanagar village there was no Brahmin before him, so when Ramesh came into the village all the people all the people started to welcome him and his family and also started giving many gifts to him. All the villagers arranged a new home for this family. They started living there happily. He was given importance by all. All the women came to Sriti to gossip. All of the women came to Sriti because they wanted blessings from a Brahmin woman. In those days Brahmins were believed to be same to be God. People believed that touching the feet of Brahmin was same as touching the feet of God. So, this family in one word was kept in the throne of the villager's hearts. Gopu loved to make baskets out of bamboo but his father didn't allow him to do such things because he thought that if a Brahmin son starts doing this type of work then he will become inferior caste. People will no more respect them. But his mother allowed him to do so. So, when his father was out Gopu used to make such baskets and planted trees on them. Various types of trees were there like brinjal, parble, potato etc. Once, in a far away area in lived a group of people. They faced some issues, so they came to the village headman named Sitaram. I think my readers are eager to know what problem the group was facing? Wait I would tell. The group came to the headman and said that their area had become impure because of evil power. The village headman asked them what he can do for that problem. The group of people replied that they wanted to talk with Ramesh ji because he was the one who could help them. The village headman assured them that he would meet. He also added that Ramesh was busy so after three days they had to come to Sitaram's place for the discussion with Ramesh ji. He also told that Ramesh ji is the most important and valuable person of this village. Then they went back. After three days they came. Ramesh ji was also present. Ramesh ji very solemnly said" What's the problem you all are facing? Tell me. I would surely get you out of it". They explained him the whole story. Ramesh ji thought a little and said that it was a serious issue and to come out of it they had to do yajna which would destroy the evil power. Ramesh ji also added," For the yajna things like 2 towels, 4 sarees, planks of wood, 3l of oil, 4kg rice, 2kg of ghee, kg dal etc etc". Then he came to home and told his wife that he had arranged a lot many gifts for her and their son. Then after taking their dinner, they slept. The next day Ramesh went for the yajna in that part of the village. The people welcomed him and he started the yajna and performed many rituals which the people thought could free them from the evil power. After the yajna Ramesh told them that he would take the remaining things because donating such things to Brahmin would be virtue for the villagers. In those days people had a blind trust on Brahmins. Then he came to home and informed her wife about the gifts. They were all happy. After few months Sitaram came to Ramesh and said," Ramesh ji, we need your help. In this village there are not so many literate people. So, if you take the responsibility of teaching our children then it would be very helpful for us. They would be able to write or read something. I along with others am requesting you to open up a school for our children." Ramesh replied that he doesn't have so much money for opening the school. Sitaram replied, "No worries. I and others would pay. We will give you money (Gurudakshina) for teaching." Ramesh agreed to the proposal. So, Sitaram arranged money for building the school. After the school was made, teaching of Ramesh ji started. More students were getting admitted in the school. The nature was the audience of their classes. Every day, the students brought different things for the teacher. One brought coconut, others jaggery, etc. No, the students didn't really do this by own. Ramesh demanded these things so, they brought. One particular morning there was an arrival of a guest. As usual the classes were going on then Satish Mukherjee came and requested for a glass of water. Then Ramesh gave him the coconut water which one of his student had brought. Then Ramesh gave the students an early an holiday. Then Satish babu introduced himself by saying that he was a teacher in a primary school from a far away village and also he was paid Rs 30 for this which was not enough for the five members in his family. Then Ramesh ji advised him to do pujas as he was a brahmin. To this advise Satish babu replied that there a lot of Brahmins from before hand so, he cannot start puja. Then after an interaction Mr. Ramesh took Satish babu to his home. There Sriti arranged lunch for him. He was given many food and Satish babu admitted that he ate this type of food after a long time. Then the years fled away with the passing clouds. Then one rumour circulated among the mouths of folk that there was a war going between two countries. There is a proverb, " That what spreads somehow makes." So, then it became a famous news that a war was going to happen between East and West Pakistan. Then after few months it was reported that the war started. A group of unscrupulous business men intentionally started hiding the most common essential commodities. As a result within a short span of time people found black out in the market. The real struggle for both ends meet had been found largely in the society. In some places people were found sharing food with the beasts. Somewhere fights were taken place even among the family members. The society on stake in the question of survival of humanity. I think the readers are eager to know what happened in Padyanagar village. Here also the scenery was more or less same. Mr. Ramesh went to Sitaram and asked him for some rice. At first he denied then he gave a small amount of rice which was like half filled stomach for them. One woman named Mita came to Sriti and said," Didi, take this rice. You eat it." Sriti asked Mita from where did she got this rice. Mita didn't will to answer. She also said," Didi you are a Brahmin, you should not listen from where I got." Sriti told that she was like Mita's elder sister, she should tell her. Mita took Sriti under a tree where a young man was standing. Sriti understood everything. She was shocked to see that Mita can go down to such a level. Mita asked for forgiveness from Sriti. Sriti came back home and gave the rice to her son and husband. Next day, Mr. Ramesh went again again to Sitaram, he said no rice is there. Then from there Mr. Ramesh went far and wide for search of a a hand of rice but wherever he has gone the answer came as no. Then at last at a shop he got very low quality rice. Whwn he came back home, he saw Satish babu with other four members sitting in the veranda of his home. Satish babu told Mr. Ramesh that Mr. Ramesh could only help him, and Sriti was like Ma Annapurna, that's why they landed there. Mr. Ramesh was very angry from inside. But her wife didn't listen to him. Then after few days, the scenery worsened. No rice, nothing. Mita came and said that she had found one lake where there are lots of shrubs. No one has gone till. So, they both went and plucked kalmai, helencha, and many other Bengal specialized shrubs among which some were not even fit for animals. They just boiled and ate. Then after a long journey Ramesh arranged vey little rice. That same day Sriti's friend came to ask for food. She was looking very weak. Sriti told her to sit under a tree. When Sriti sent the food through her son, then one shocking incident happened. His son touched the woman and she fell. After that it was seen that the woman died. this was the first death of this village. Sriti never thought that a famine can take an innocent person in such a way. History has witnessed many previous famines before. I hope that there is no more artificial famines before is caused. As corruption is increasing, the chances of artificial famine is increasing. The End
author: Suktika Saha

title: White Ball
text: Raj were playing in the garden. They had a small ball. They lost it. Riya and Raj ran to a frog. They asked him, "Dear Frog, have you seen our white ball?" "Yes, I threw it across the sewer," said the frog. Riya and Raj saw an elephant across the sewer. They asked him, "Brother elephant, have you seen our white ball?" The elephant said, "Yes, children! I threw it on the tree." Riya and Raj climbed the tree. There a sparrow was sitting sadly. The children asked, "Sparrow, why are you sad?" The sparrow said, "Children, I had laid four eggs. All have hatched. But one egg has not hatched yet." Riya and Raj said, "This is not an egg. This is our white ball." Both of them took the ball and started laughing, " Ha, ha, ha, hi, hi, he, he...."
author: Veena Bhambhani

title: Am I Ugly?
text: The crackling sound of trains echoes in my ears as I hesitantly wander around, looking for my train. It is eleven in the morning, the rain is pouring, and I'm...lost. Hello, I'm Kriti, a typical Bangalorean: and I'm standing in a vast Railway Station- wholly lost and alone. I ran away from my home. I can't really figure out where I should be going. I lean at a rod and ask for a cup of tea, paying for it from the coins in my piggy bank. Look, I don't hate my home. I love Amma, and even though we fight tons, I still love her very much: but there are things I cannot tell her. She is self-occupied with her household, and my problems looked far less significant in front of her challenges. I often think, 'Are my problems real?'. I tap my foot on the ground. The shopkeeper scrutinizes me with his glinting eyes. Another train arrived at the station. I cross-checked my ticket, which I had secretly booked, and I checked if the three five-hundred rupee notes were still in my pocket. And finally, when the debate in my mind concludes, I step onto the correct train. I sit on the comfortable seat, now fiddling my toes around. Looking around, I wonder how much time it will take to reach Shivamogga, where my grandparents live. I've written a letter already, and my aunt has acknowledged that she would be waiting at the Railway, and then she'd talk to me. Perhaps she'll scold me, but I just don't want to see Bangalore again. A few hours later.. My aunt is the one to start the conversation. She asks me everything at once, and I know my time is up: I would have to tell the truth to someone. As we sit in the rickshaw, I decide to begin, and tell her the secret I've been hiding for months together. 'Tell me, Kriti, what happened in Bangalore that triggered you to run way, hm? Does your amma not know?' 'Aunty, it all began when I first scrolled through the comments of my 'Travel Video' that I had uploaded on the net, only to find horribly mean remarks about my looks. I had always considered the internet to be a boon. 'The comments hurt my pride very badly. Self-doubt took over me, and I wanted to change EVERYTHING about myself. Although I was used to racist comments from my fellow classmates- I thought the outer world was humble and understanding. But, alas! I was wrong..and probably even ugly.' She's darker than the wood! Her face, is out of the question! Ew! Look at her hair! It has a bottle oil poured on it! Ugly Ducklings are allowed at tourist spots? I wonder. 'I browsed all day and night, looking for ways to fit myself into the moulds that society set. I sacrificed my liking and befriended the net. I found ways to look better and thought I was tackling my insecurities. I thought things would get better...but I was mistaken. I wasn't tackling my insecurities, but developing them.' "You will look beautiful after following these instructions..." 'In order to change, I realised, there would be innumerable procedures that I'd have to do one by one, carefully. I convinced Amma to cut my hair down, I fought with her to not oil my hair. I bought all kinds of skin treatment products to change my complexion- and now, I regret all of it with all my heart. I should have loved myself, for, the incident that took place after that, shattered my soul.' 'It happened on a Monday. I was walking to school when I met a girl at my school, Aisha. She was very famous, and I had heard that she was incredibly generous and humorous. 'How're you, Kriti?', Aisha had asked, initiating the conversation. As we talked, Aisha had said- 'You look good today!'. I had been overwhelmed, and it was my best day: to receive a compliment from her!' You look gorgeous today! You're so bright and fresh! 'You could say, in a figurative and metaphoric way, I was on the moon: I was the moon that night, aunty! Hearing such encouraging words after a tragic incident made me feel incredibly better. 'Later that evening, I was walking back home after playing kanche (marble game) with my cousin, who lived next street. I come across a mansion, that I recognised to be Aisha's, and peeked into the window: checking if she was there. She indeed was, and her school friends were also sitting with her and they were talking. I didn't eavesdrop, but by chance, I ended up hearing one remark that Aisha declared to them all. The words she said shattered my self-love. That's it aunty, that's all of my story...' What a nerd, Kriti is! I mean, look at her complexion! My aunt looks at me with utmost care. 'Oh look what you've done to yourself!', she says with pity. She glances at me for another moment or two, and finally responds. 'There is one thing you must always remember, Kriti. Our healthy body is a gift to us. One's complexion isn't capable enough of defining one's worth.' I nod, showing my approval. 'And of course, there is a famous saying: Don't take criticism from someone you wouldn't take advice from. You cannot trust anything on the internet, Kriti. This world is meant to explore!'. I smiled whole-heartedly. 'Okay, it's time to go back, aunty. I've learnt my lesson. I'll go book a train.', I utter hesitantly. 'Of course not! You're coming to our house now, have a whole-hearted meal and go back safely to Bangalore with your uncle. He has a work in Bangalore, anyways.' I agree. She smiles, and slips in- 'I've made ladoos for you! You must eat them before your uncle does!'
author: Arathi Vishwanath
illustrator: Imile  Wepener; Niloufer Wadia; Parmita Mukherjee; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: Emergence, When Wings Unfold
text: I was terrified. Butterflies filled my stomach. But I took a deep breath and finally stepped out onto the stage. The stage somehow seemed to resemble the wide-open mouth of a hungry monster. I could hear my heartbeat racing and with one final, heavy sigh, I took a leap of faith, and stepped onto the massive stage. I glanced at the school auditorium packed with students. The feeble voice in my head, which was encouraging me to move forward, somehow started getting louder. One peek at the humungous screen on the stage, and I could see the magnificent virtual background that I had designed for the “Health Day Assembly”. Suddenly in a matter of split seconds, like a whirlwind, I could experience the love, sweat and excitement behind the entire planning voyage. Today was the culmination of endless days and nights of preparation for the “Big Day”, the very first “Offline Assembly” at school after two and a half years of Online schooling. My mind wandered into the domains of the past few years of my life. Introvert, quiet me, had aced all the tests and performed well throughout junior school, but never had I developed the confidence to speak like my self-assured peers in front of large audiences, nor had I been trusted with an opportunity to lead the pack, and spearhead the show, until now. It was true that while the world was engulfed by the Coronavirus and caged behind the confines of homes, something magical, something unexpected had happened for me. Earlier, I had lived a life of mere existence in the shadows of my peers. However, as I had entered middle school, a completely unknown arena, where everyone started with a clean slate, online schooling came as a “Blessing in disguise” for me. My teachers’ constant encouragement to speak and participate while learning online, somehow gave my life a new purpose and I commenced interacting with them. Little did I know that it was the “Beginning of a New Chapter” of my life. Unexpectedly, after years of no participation in competitions nor public speaking forums, my new, middle school teachers started giving me opportunities to participate and showcase my talent. To my pleasant surprise, I actually emerged victorious and brought back laurels for my school even during Inter-school contests. Coming Back to the Present Moment from my wandering thoughts... I felt a slight nudge on my shoulders and realized it was my teacher telling me it was time. Yes, it was indeed “Showtime”! I could feel a slight smile begin at the corners of my mouth. I closed my eyes for one last time and could clearly visualize my mother’s smiling face. I could swear that I heard her whisper into my ears,” You can do it My Girl! It’s your moment. Go conquer them with your confidence, win them with your smile!” The occasion was momentous in essence and soul, due to being the “First ever Middle School Assembly” which was being conducted offline, right on the second day of the schools reopening. Hence, all the practices had been conducted online. The enormous stage was a stranger to me. I did not get an opportunity to befriend it prior to our introduction today. However, as I approached the podium, magically all my fears and apprehensions disappeared literally into thin air. This was the moment that I had been waiting for, all my school life, the moment when I was the lead coordinator and compere for a School Assembly, the moment I was stepping out of the cocoon of inhibition and coyness. This was the final moment of truth. Before I knew it, I could hear my confident voice welcoming everyone to a Landmark Assembly indeed, post the pandemic. Yes, it was my Day to shine, finally! The butterflies in my stomach had taken flight, and I was soaring high! High on confidence, high on happiness, high on my dreams finally mounting for ascend! The show progressed like a grand celebration. All my peers had brought on their “A-Game” after all for this milestone assembly. Like an icing on the cake, my principal walked onto the stage right before playing the “3-D School Logo” video that I had created and designed. I couldn’t believe my ears when I heard her sing praises about the Logo, video and my self-confident compering skills. The thundering applause was like music to my ears. The journey had been long and tedious, but it was well worth every effort. My teachers were my Heroes. ‘They had discovered the hidden abilities of this lost, introvert girl and changed her life forever!’ I knew that I had finally arrived. The stage and I were going to be best friends! My smile finally reached my eyes! Everyone battles with fears of dreams that they dread are impossible to achieve but they still pray for a realisation of their aspirations. All one really needs is a little sprinkle of the fairy dust of faith, just like what my teachers provided for me, and a dash of “Self-belief”. Though I had many a fall while learning to “fly”, perhaps I always had wings. My determination to embrace new challenges eventually helped “My Dreams” unfold and become “My Wings.” Maybe, this little bird, called “Me”, was destined to “Fly High”, all along! This is “My Little Story”. Never be afraid to write yours!

title: Live-Laugh-Love
text: “Some rule breakers can turn out to be pretty successful, and therefore it is not always necessary to follow the same path that everyone else does. Create your own!” Let’s check the accuracy of this statement. “Study hard! Become an engineer”, said his mother as she brought a glass of milk to him. He was born into a middle - class Indian family. So - ‘he’ had an elder brother, and his parents in his family. His father had a remunerative Government job and let me tell y’all, in India, it is considered fortunate and blessed to have one. He is now retired with a decent amount of pension. His mother was a teacher in a government school too. His older brother was employed as a doctor in the Indian Army. So eventually, as the whole family was employed in the Government sector, the same was expected out of him. His parents wanted him to become an engineer as they thought that there were only two kinds of professions that were successful - a Doctor and an Engineer. The eldest child of theirs was already a doctor in a very reputed organization. What harm could there be in making the other an engineer? Well, there was negligence on their part (if you haven’t already figured it out), they hadn’t even discussed this with their child and did not even ask him what he wanted to do; even if he was interested in this. Let’s get back to this part in a few moments. It’s time to give some introduction about him. He loved going to the gym and exercising since he was about thirteen. Who is ‘he’ you ask? His name was Aman and one thing that is necessary to know about him is that he had a vague mindset. He jumped back and forth between things, so whenever he kept doing something for a long time - he was most likely to continue with it till he felt fully satisfied in what he did. Even though he didn’t have much of his goals clear at the time, he knew whatever he would do would be for money. He considered that money could bring all the happiness. He could do anything for money as he thought and that he could do anything with money. The ultimate goal was to earn a fairly good amount of money and live his life happily. He understood that this could be done only through studying and then getting a good job. Now getting back to the story where we left - There was huge pressure on him for being a good student, get good grades, a good job and further have a good life. And under pressure a person either blossoms or breaks. Aman broke here. Though he did his engineering with 71%, he did not feel confident and felt satisfied in what he did. And he realized that feeling satisfied was important, he was done pleasing other people all his life and doing whatever they told him to. He realized this later on in his life that - “Even if you do ‘n’ number of things to please ‘n’ number of people, there will always be this one person who is dissatisfied and unfulfilled. You are here for yourself and are only responsible for achieving satisfaction for yourself. Live your life and DO NOT let anyone have its remote.” This was the first time he was ready to make a big decision for himself. If you look at the past - his stream, his school and college had already been decided by his parents beforehand and he did not have a role in this decision. Anyways, he went against his parent’s will here and did what he liked. He liked going to the gym, exercising and also liked teaching. Therefore, he combined two of his interests and went on to become a trainer. His parents were unhappy and not pleased with this action, but they couldn’t do anything except pushing him, which they had already been doing for a while now. This had no impact on him whatsoever. He became too stubborn to listen to anyone. He didn’t want to live up to anyone’s expectations anymore. He figured that life was too short for this and therefore continued what he was doing for himself, though it caused constant friction between him and his parents. He went on from being a general to a personal trainer. Graph of progression went uphill from here on..A job with a good amount of money and he had a control over what timings he had to work. There was another thing he had interest in – surfing around the internet and looking at technologies. He himself took initiative to learn certain languages but he knew that he couldn’t specialize in this field by himself. He came to know about an IT training that a company provided for 6 - 7 months and after that he would be employed in the same company with a good salary. He would get the best of both worlds. Alas! What could go wrong? He was happy and, on a path, to achieve the goal he had planned out for himself. But spoken too soon - “Forever is a lie, even Romeo had to die.” His happiness also lasted for a short duration. He had gotten into a car crash, where the other person died. He was not at fault, but according to the Indian law, a case is going on. But despite all of this he keeps on smiling every day and performs both of his jobs with full effort, daily. Therefore, one of the many lessons to learn from his story is - “Sweet are the uses of adversity, which, like the toad, ugly and venomous, wears yet a precious jewel in his head; and this our life, exempt from public haunt, finds tongues in trees, books in the running brooks, sermons in stones, and good in everything. Always keep smiling despite what life throws at you because problems are the only thing which can turn you into a better person in life. Life is a rollercoaster and will continue going up and down a lot of times, therefore the only thing we can do is let go of the past, deal with the present and wait for the future. While waiting, we might as well smile!” THE END by- Jessina Singh

text: The first day of picnic It was a sunny day Anu was going picnic with her parents,grandparents,5 cousins and their parents. They all were going to a forest for a picnic in a bus. She likes to keep her bag with her.The most important thing is she always carries her glasses cleaning cloth It was almost night the adults decided to do a barbecue Anu was checking the book her mother called her for the barbecue. title: My Aunty Savita
text: What am I going to do? Aunt Savita is everything I have, I don't want to lose her. I have to collect the money but how?! I don't have a job. Nineteen-year-old Anaya had just got the terrible news from the family doctor that her only relative, the person who raised her after her parents died, Aunt Savita is suffering from cancer and needed to be treated immediately. Feeling lost, Anaya finished her cup of coffee and decided she has spent enough time crying. She wiped her tears, paid for her coffee, and walked out of the coffee shop. She was walking to her home on the road which was empty besides a few cars, marveling at the fact th at it was so quiet in the usually busy city. She reminisced about the number of times she and her aunty walked on this very road, recalling the conversation they had. They were coming back from school. The atmosphere was tense. The reason was Anaya's final exam results. She has not received good grades. Anaya quietly asked her aunt, "Are you disappointed in me Aunty Savita?" "Who said that? I am not disappointed in you.", said her aunty, confused by the sudden question. "I performed poorly in my exams," said the little girl and hurriedly added, "But I promise it will not happen again." Her aunt chuckled and said, "It's not your fault, sweetie. You helped me with the business when you should have been studying for your exams. You can prepare better next time." Anaya smiled as she remembered the memory. She got full marks in the next exam and Aunt Savita was smiling for the next 2 weeks. Aunt Savita always knew how to motivate her like the time when she was scared to ride her bicycle after falling and getting hurt but Aunt Savita said that everyone falls at least once from their bicycle and told her own experience. Anaya wanted to repay her Aunty for everything she has done for her and decided to always be there for her and take care of her. She knew that she has been inattentive towards her Aunty recently as she had been busy with her studies and friends. Wanting to mend her relationship with her Aunty, she bought Aunt Savita's favorite ice cream to make her feel better as she knew her Aunt would be feeling upset at this sudden and unwelcome change in her life. As expected, Anaya heard the sound of soft crying coming from her Aunt's room as soon as she opened the front door. She went and knocked at the purple door. "Aunty Savita are you there? Please open the door and talk to me. I understand you are upset, but there is no reason to act like a child", said Anaya pleadingly with tears about to fall down her own eyes. The response she got was, "Anaya, you must be hungry. There are leftovers in the fridge from lunch. You should heat them up, sweetie", all this was said in a shaky voice. Anaya sighed, irritated as Aunty started doing what she always does when she thinks Anaya is too young to know her problems, shut her out and pretend there is no problem. "Aunty Savita please open the door. Let's talk about it. Ignoring the issue won't make it go away. You have to deal with it. We have to deal with it and we will. You're not alone", Anaya said with tears in her eyes. The door unlocked from inside and her Aunt came out. She looked awful with tears running her eyes. "When did you became so good at finding words?",said Aunty Savita with a small smile. "Well, I have an aunt who has taught me and believe me when I say she is great with words too", Anaya replied with a big smile seeing that she is not crying anymore. and they both started laughing uncontrollably as they knew everything will be fine as long as they had each other.

title: Report of life
text: One fine day, Rohan of grade 5A, was playing on the new laptop his father got him, he was playing on the laptop for so long. He used to download all the new games until he had full memory. But he bought a new memory card and played again. He was obsessed with the laptop. His parents asked him a goggle of times that not to play on the laptop as the exams are commencing from next week but he ran to his room shut the door and played on the laptop. A week later, Rohan was seated in the third row, forth bench, trying to copy the answers from his friends at the same time trying not to get caught, he thinks about the answers but can't even guess, somehow he finished a paper and finished all the exams too. He got the exam results the next week and shown the report card to his parents, he failed in every subject except computer exam which he was playing on it for days. But he promised to get good marks next exam. He started to concentrate on books but his mind was the one which would flicker away, his mind would think about the new game or the new car that came out recently. However, he realized his mistake after a few days. His favorite subject was Maths and Science. Final exam started, he had doubt in none of the questions. He was well prepared for the exam. He got very good marks in the paper, 100 out of 100 in Math and 97 in Science. His parents were very happy about his marks and behavior. His parents still didn't allow him to play on the laptop so he went out to play outdoor games. He liked football the most he used to play games like volleyball, cricket, basket ball and football. He joined the best football academy in the town. From then he realizes that he must balance between playtime and study time. He made his report of life A++.

title: Bonhomie
text: My heart skipped a beat when I heard that; the phone dropped from my hand and tears rolled down my cheeks. I felt humiliated that time. My best friend Yujin died in an accident. It felt unreal; it was like yesterday, we were laughing and enjoying; now she’s gone in a blink of an eye. I kneeled down on the floor; I was shattered into pieces. I felt layers of unsettling emotions. I held the half heart-shaped necklace in my palms. March 2011 These memories play in my head. And now, I’m here with my mum in the United States. My thoughts got interrupted when the doorbell rang. ‘I’m surprised you managed to set all this up.’ said my mom, entering the kitchen. ‘Eomma! I’ll come back till’ you prepare the dinner. ’ I took my earphones and went downstairs. The cool night breeze whistled softly, blowing lightly through my hair. I was glad to be free of the hot and stuffy classrooms in school; light music playing in my ears and I felt relieved. But still nothing caught my interest; the empty road seemed dull and boring and only a few people around me. The bright city lights were all I could see. I closed my eyes for a moment; remembering the good times spent with Yujin. I sighed; suddenly, I bumped into someone. I opened my eyes and panicked when I saw a girl laying on the road, laughing and smiling like an idiot. I was standing there, dumbfounded until I also chuckled seeing her being so weird and fruitful. I gave my hand to her, and she got up, still giggling. ‘I’m sorry.’ we both said at the same time. ‘I’m Eva Pa- ‘I got interrupted when she spoke. ‘Are you from South Korea?’ she asked, hoping for yes. ‘Yeah, I’m Eva Park.’ hearing that she bowed to me like people there do as a polite gesture. I chuckled seeing her being so cheerful. ‘And you?’ I asked her. ‘Amelia Davis. Well, that’s your English name, right? What’s your Korean name?’ ‘Park Minji.’ ‘Oh my god! It’s such a cute name.’ I felt so comfortable with her. This was the first time after Yujin died, I found someone so cheerful and bright. We both talked for a while and lost the track of time. I looked at my phone and it was already 9:01 p.m. I was heading to my apartment, but I turned back and said, ‘You’ll be able to try the authentic Kimchi stew!’ ‘I’m so excited! We should totally hang out sometimes. I live nearby your building.’ And that night while having dinner, I thought; Amelia wasn’t like Yujin but she still made me feel a sense of deep connection between us. Few months passed away; Amelia and I used to hang out every day. Amelia is trustworthy, not only my secrets are safe with her but so is my fear and weirdness. She always had my back, and I could rely on her. We both were becoming good friends but that doesn’t mean I would forget Yujin. 11 years later ‘This was how I met your mom. This was us, Eva and Amelia.’ I said to Amelia’s son, Oliver. It was currently 11:09 p.m. Amelia had flown to Korea to meet me after years. The doorbell rang and she opened the door; a lady standing there, wearing a half heart-shaped necklace. ‘Hi! Who are you? May I help you in some way?’ I approached to the door and my eyes couldn’t believe what I saw, ‘Y… Yujin? It can’t….be!’ My hands were trembling, and my eyes were watery; I couldn’t even speak a word properly and suddenly, everything blacked out as if I fainted. I open my eyes and find myself laid down on my bed; I looked around and saw someone similar coming towards me. It was Yujin! My mind was filled with questions while I sit on the bed. Why is she here? How is she here? Am I seeing a dream? Is she really Yujin? If yes, then how? I was tensed at that moment when she spoke up, ‘Hey! Feeling any better?’ I kept silent for a while; her low voice made me relax a bit. ‘Yujin, you died?’ I asked her. ‘I did but I rose from the grave.’ I chuckled. ‘I had an accident that night.’ That night, My arm was bruised badly, and I had injured my head. I was in a serious condition that time; I had a mild heart attack too, and I was unconscious, but everyone thought I died because of the heart attack. I was in coma for two years but then I recovered after that. ‘I could never tell you this because you had cut all the connections with us after I DIED. A few months back, the book shop lady told me you had shifted back here, and I came running to meet you.’ ‘I missed you so much, you wouldn’t believe how I was at that period of time.’ I hugged her tightly. Amelia walked inside the room, ‘Thank you so much Amelia for taking care of her’ said Yu-jin to Amelia. What had happened that night was just unbelievable. I had spent almost half of my life thinking my bestie died and she’s suddenly back. It was shocking, but a true serendipity for me. And now, I have two best friends by my side. "There are many who come in life but only some stay with you forever." - THE END
author: Vrishti Chejara

title: Lara Becomes a Mermaid
text: Once there lived a young girl named lara who lived in Queensland located in Australia. She was really an inquisitive girl. One day, she read a story about marine life and the mermaids. Just after this she started knowing more about mermaids and marine life and wished to be a mermaid. The next day, when she was on her way to school, she met a fairy. The fairy asked Lara, “Lara do you want to be a mermaid?” “Yes” she said. “I wish I could be a mermaid and could see the beauty of ocean.”The fairy replied, “I can make you a mermaid but for that you need to come along me to my house”. Lara went with the fairy and asked her to transform her into a mermaid. The fairy made a powder and took Lara to ‘Whiteheaven Beach’, one of the prettiest beaches in the world. “I will sprinkle this powder on you and after 3 seconds, you would transform into a mermaid” said the fairy. “After 3 days you must come here again, because after that you would transform into a human”. As said, the fairy showered the powder and Lara transformed into a mermaid. Lara jumped into the water, she found that she can easily breathe in water, and her tail was really pretty. Lara first suffered while swimming but later she learnt dolphin kick, the way mermaids swim. After swimming a little she reached Merland, the place where mermaids lived. She started talking with the mermaids and was really happy. She made a friend. Her name was Anna. Anna went with Lara and showed her the oceans, fishes and aquatic plants. At some distance Lara and Anna decided to play hide and seek in the coral reef. There were lots of places to hide and they had lots of fun. Lara found a dark cave, she thought it is the perfect place to hide. Suddenly she saw a shadow above her. It was a shark! She was as still and calm as she could be and tried not to make any sound. The shark was getting closer! The terrified Lara closed her eyes and started praying. The shark came closer. “Hello, can I play too” asked the shark to Lara. Lara later knew that the shark was friendly to all the mermaids. While playing Hide and Seek they reached a place, even Anna didn’t knew existed. The place was really pretty. There was a large castle built by the king. He had a son, his name was Rawn. Rawn was just swimming around the castle and playing Hide and Seek with his friends. Then he met Lara and Anna. After some talks and games they became friends too. While playing Hide and Seek they reached a place, even Anna didn’t knew existed. The place was really pretty. There was a large castle built by the king. He had a son, his name was Rawn. Rawn was just swimming around the castle and playing Hide and Seek with his friends. Then he met Lara and Anna. After some talks and games they became friends too. The second day Lara was near the shore and found the fairy who transformed Lara into mermaid. Lara asked the fairy to do something so that Lara can stay a mermaid for her lifetime. After many requests, the fairy agreed to transform Lara into mermaid. The fairy moved her wand and now Lara was a mermaid for her lifetime. Lara went back to Anna, prince Rawn, and her other friends and told them about this. But after a month Lara was missing her family so much. Her family thought the Lara losted or was kidnapped. The next day Lara was going to meet prince Rawn. Anna wasn’t well that day so, went alone. When she was on her way to go she saw a shadow above her, but this time it wasn’t that friendly shark but a boat with some people on it. The people were finding a mermaid for their show. Unfortunately they saw Lara and she didn’t knew that they are going to catch her. She was taken with four other mermaids. They were trained for a mermaid show. Lara was now missing everyone. It was the show day, during the show while showing some tricks she saw something she was so surprised for! She saw her family and was so happy. But could not meet them and Lara’s family didn’t recognized her. She was so fed up of being a mermaid and wished not to wish to be a mermaid for lifetime. She was so down-hearted and depressed now. She started crying loudly with sorrow. Suddenly she hear a voice saying, “Dear, what’s the matter? Why are you crying? Wake up from sleep and get ready for school.” She was so astonished and could not understand what was happening. Then all of a sudden she woke from her and realize that all this was just a dream. Later, she went to her mother and gave her a tight hug. “What happen why are you crying and now giving me a tight hug?” Lara told her mother about her dream and her mother said, “Oh poor Lara, there are no mermaids or fairies. It’s just an imaginated and fantasy character. Stop dreaming now and go to school on time today.”
author: TANU ♡

title: Role model
text: It’s a fact that people like and take inspiration from someone who is in any way like them but it at a limit is good. Blindly trusting or wanting to be just like them isn’t good. But I’ve a friend who is the prey of this ideology and it all started because of me. Yesterday he finished the novel I suggested to him. And, there was a character named Sebastian in it and he found him so interesting that he wanted to be just like him. He knows that becoming like him is impossible because it was a creation of writer’s mind and hence not real. And I also wanted to correct him but his enthusiasm stopped me. Today, at school I found him on the last bench of the second row, lost in thoughts and that was surprising because it wasn’t his seat. The teacher Mr.keshav, allotted him the seat beside me. In my curiosity, I asked him “Sachit why are you not at your seat?” “Do I look like Sebastian, Vaibhav?” “No.” I said while knowing his desire to hear yes. “But I even dressed like him.” This is the reason behind all of this. Sebastian’s dress looks totally like our winter uniform. “I am not getting that vibe from you, by the way, answer my question.” I answered trying to change the topic. “The boy who sits here is absent and this is the seat on which Sebastian sits in the novel so I sat here.” “kay, just come quickly. The bell already rang and I saw keshav sir coming.” It had been only a few seconds after we settle down when Keshav sir came and started taking attendance. When Keshav sir came to his name Sachit didn’t say present. He was a well-behaving student and topper of our class. So this astonished sir. Sir wanted to mark him present but we have a strict rule in our class that if you forgot to say present at the time of attendance then you will be marked absent. So that day for the first time Sachit was marked absent. He was looking forward to maintain his perfect attendance. But I don’t know why he missed it today but I expected it to be Sebastian. The attendance was over and sir ordered Sachit to collect the trip form and fee from the students. He started collecting them and I helped. Tomorrow was our trip to a picnic park near our city. And I was very excited about it but I forget about it due to these recent matters with Sachit. The rest of the day was like a normal day except him trying to be Sebastian. He went to the roof to eat his lunch in recess leaving me in the class. It had been only a few months since he started reading that novel and it had been only two days from when he finished it. And its effect on him was noticeable. The next day was trip and we have come to school at 6 o’clock so we decided that we will not play today instead we’ll complete our work so we have less work to do after the trip. Next morning I woke up earlier than usual because today we have to go to school by ourselves. When I reached Sachit ’s place I saw him standing outside. He joined in the walk to school. We was chit-chatting when the topic of our work come to light. He asked “ Did you finish your work?” “Yes, why, did you not?” “well I was busy.” “Busy in reading about Sebastian ” I replied sarcastically. “Yep, how did you know?” “Just a guess. But that will gonna affect your image in sir’s eye.” “Don’t worry I will complete it.” When we arrived at school. We found our class standing near the bus so we joined them. “Look it’s Vaishali.” he teased me. “I can see that too, I also have eyes” I replied to shut him up. Vaishali is a girl in our which I kind of have feelings for but as I know that these feelings doesn’t matter so I only told Sachit about them. And now whenever he gets chance he tries to tease me. “ok, sorry but look” he had a smart phone with him. “But the sir had prohibited us to bring phones and do your parents know about it.” “If I will be careful sir will never get to know about it and today is trip so I am sure that my parents don’t mind.” “But still…” The sir’s voice interpreted our conversation. He ordered is to make a row near bus’s entrance. He said “We are going to leave soon but before that tell me the truth did anybody brought there phone. If you tell me now I wouldn’t do anything but if I found it later I’ll.” Just after that I looked at Sachit ’s face. I am his best friend so I can judge his face and that time it was chaotic like he wants to tell the truth but he also doesn’t want it. However, he stayed silent. I think he had rotten luck that day because a student told sir about Sachit’s phone while we were entering the bus. Sir stopped Sachit and I heard sir scolding him for few minutes. After that Sachit entered the bus. “What happened?” “I hate him, why did he told the sir about the phone?” It was probably because of jealousy. Sachit is a ideal student as such many students harbor jealousy for him. So he tried to ruin Sachit ’s image. “leave it.” I said trying to refresh his mood. “Kay.” Sir allowed Sachit the use of his phone only in emergencies. In two hours we reached our destination. Sir said we are free to enjoy the park but we have to come back under the banyan tree in two hours for lunch. After that we went to enjoy the park. There was one another school with us. It was a boy school of our city. I was with Sachit. We enjoyed many rides together. During the bull ride we had a friendly competition about who will stay on the bull longer,Sachit won. The two hours was going to be over soon so we went back. We were sitting under the tree. When Sachit handed his phone to me and left for bathroom. The bathroom for both boys and girls was at the opposite side from the tree. We were sitting under the tree. When Sachit handed his phone to me and left for bathroom. The bathroom for both boys and girls was at the opposite side from the tree. Time flew by and most of the class and sir arrived near the tree. The last one to join was Vaishali and her friends. But Sachit wasn’t there. Then something unexpected happened. The teacher of that other school with three boys was coming towards us. That teacher screamed “How shameless your student are!” Keshav sir replied “ Sir what happened?” “Your Student was peeping in the girls bathroom and when my students tried to stop him he hit them.” Then Sachit entered the scene. He looked a little beat up. Three boys said “Sir, that boy.” “Vaibhav, where was he?” “In bathroom.” I answered sir. “Sachit, did you beat these boys.” “Yes but...” “Shut up!” sir screamed furiously. “Go to bus, there is no lunch for you.” “Sir but…” “Go” Sachit left in frustration. But something was wrong. Sachit’s personality is not like that he accept his punishment if he is in the wrong. Sir apologized on the behalf of Sachit and they left. Then I tried to investigate however I was unable to talk to Sachit. I remembered, the last to come was the Vaishali and girls and they came from the same direction as bathroom. That helped me speculate that the boys was peeping while Vaishali and her friends were there, Sachit tried to stop them and a fight broke. Now I needed proof. I was brainstorming on it when my luck shined on me and I heard those boys from the other side of the wall talking about how they falsely blamed Sachit. I was furious but I calmed down and thought about how to catch them. And then it struck me, Sachit ’s phone. In the end, it saved him. I recorded their conversation and ran to sir who was depressed. I played the recording. Hearing it made sir cry of joy. He thanked me and he told me to bring Sachit. He took the recording and went to that boy school’s group. I found Sachit depressingly looking outside. He didn’t even reacted when he saw me. I told him the entire situation. Hearing that he started crying. I had never saw him cry before. “Thanks. I realised how annoying I had become in these few days. And how you tried to tell me that before. Sorry for not understanding you before, the truth is you are my everything. You are my best friend and my one true role model too.”
author: Om Goswaami

title: The Missing Cinnamon Rolls.
text: Winston’s tiny legs trickled along the crosswalk. Late for his first case as an official, he rushed across the Halloween crowd and into Purramid to get his favorite ‘Bunmousse’ for good luck. He went up to the counter and ruffled through his wallet, “Hi, I’d like one Bunmouse, that’s 45 Pawllers right? Here-” He looked at the dumbfound owner. “-Sir?” A slight touch of Teki’s elbow sent the tip jar tumbling. He sunk to his knees in despair, and as any simpleton could’ve guessed by now the recipe had gone missing, the same formula that- Boltie [ Pushing up her glasses, frustrated]: Wait-wait–wait. What cinnamon rolls? What recipe? We have to start from the beginning. Sniff Sniff The aroma of freshly baked goods filled the air. It swayed around Teki, the peppy siamese cat, who held the tray of scones he had baked. This is a good batch!; He thought. Tring! The bell rang and the door of the cafe opened. “Hey, Boltie!” Teki waved at Boltie, the border collie, who was a regular at the Purramid cafe (previously owned by Teki's Grandpa Whiskers) since she started her college semester. “How’s the photography going?” asked Teki as he placed an espresso and a grilled sandwich on her table. “Oh, same old, same old, haven’t gotten much time since my exams started.” She replied. She was an exceptional photographer, so much so that her photos were featured in The Beagle Times, which is a big deal for a novice such as Boltie. Teki even helped her out by displaying her pictures in the cafe. Tring! “Teki! Sorry I am late today.” Yuki, Teki’s snowshoe best friend helped him with the cafe in the morning. In return, Teki served at her ramen shop ‘Eumsig’. Teki waved his paw up and down, giving her an ensuring smile. “How is the banner coming together?” he asked with shimmering eyes. With a special event coming up, the following month would be essential for the cafe. Everyone had put every bit of their soul into keeping it picture-perfect. They worked on banners, pamphlets, and even personalized invitations for some VIA’s [stands for Very Important Animals] Until now, they had kept it a surprise, which meant not working on banners in public or even talking about them outside the cafe. Teki glared at the safe behind the counter, it had the secret recipe they were going to reveal. It was like a sting operation. Boltie however, was an accomplice. Her marvelous photography skills in addition to Yuki’s exceptional calligraphy made for amazing posters. Boltie pushed down her thin-rimmed glasses and raised her paw, “No, I wasn’t able to complete it. I took extra shifts at the library,” she tried to explain, "I am… a bit behind on rent.” Yuki gave her an understanding smile and offered to help with her projects. CLANK! CLANK! “Good lord! They’re back at it again!” Teki grumbled under his breath. Everyone else tried to ignore it as this had become a frequent affair. About a year ago, a new cafe started across the street. At first, they gathered quite a bit of a crowd but soon the people realized that they were nowhere close to Purramid. Ever since then, each day they try to pull off a new stunt to steal Teki’s customers. “Today is their last day on this block!” Teki threw his apron on the floor and stormed out of the cafe. Boltie and Yuki tried to ignore everything, thinking Teki would clear his head and forget about it as always. But today, Teki was taking a long time to come back. “Teki, no!” Yuki yelled. “Ms. Yuki…” the vexed store manager asked Yuki to take care of the situation. Boltie bolted to apologize to the cafe owner Mochie, the old turtle, who had run her cafe for 85 years in Shelloise, her hometown. But due to the pandemic, she had to close down. Finally, all these years later her grandson had opened ‘Hardback’, a library cum cafe, as a gift for Mochie on her 151st birthday. A vast, scary storm brewed in the cafe and there they stood without an umbrella. Yuki had no choice but to drag Teki and the big thundering cloud outside. Boltie bowed quickly to apologize and followed Yuki out. “Hey! You left this!” a euphonious voice reached Boltie. “You left this in there.” He repeated. “Oh, thank you.” She replied restlessly. Winds blew, carrying the blossom leaves away. The air around them twinkled. At that moment, for Armi, only the two existed. Armi, the armadillo, handed her the pen. “So, say….tomorrow evening would you like to hang out with me? We could perfect our bakery skills, talk about every book there is-” At this point, Boltie once again, felt like living up to her name. “-we could file a thesis about every single book in binders, alphabetically and oh! “ He kept going on, “Even color-code them! I could even help you with the banners and poster or we could just watch a documentary about humans!” Boltie stood there with red cheeks, longing to say yes, but blurted a rather alarming ‘NO SORRY!’ and booked it back to Purramid, leaving Armi dazed. Mochie shuffled to the wide glass window and watched everything unfold. She thought, “That recipe isn’t safe…” Our hard-working trio decided to call it a day and spent the night back at Eumsig. At this point, it was either losing their sanity or messing up and forfeiting credibility with their customers. The quadrupeds awoke from their slumber with a frisson of excitement. Still, in their night suits, they groggily dragged themselves back to Purramid. Wake up. Wake up. Boltie slapped herself as Teki opened the safe for a routine check. I can’t believe this. How- A slight touch of Teki’s elbow sent the tip jar tumbling. He sunk to his knees in despair, and as any simpleton could’ve guessed by now the recipe had gone missing, the same formula that Teki worked hard on, the same formula which was passed on from generation and was a culmination of all the different procedures of making the PERFECT CINNAMON ROLLS had vanished! POOF! Just like a student in a magic school with an invisibility cloak...gone. Winston stared in confusion, “Are you, alright sir?” Teki’s eyes went soulless, “Yuki, call the cops.” Yuki signaled Boltie to call the authorities quickly while she pulled Winston to the side served him his Bunmousse in a takeaway box and sent him away with a smile. Tring! Winston preoccupied with his phone, carelessly bumped into another customer entering the store. Ring! Ring! “Hello. Yes?” He spoke on his phone rather seriously. “At the Purramid, are you sure? I’m here already.” He promptly kept the box on a nearby table and spoke with cadence, “Hello, Mr. Teki. I am Winston and I am probably the youngest detective of all time.” Boltie and Yuki tugged him by his paw and explained everything that took place. He asked, “So let me get this clear. You check the safe every day and today it was gone?”. Teki nodded in response. “After the fight?” he counter-questioned and threw the stack of papers on the table, “Interesting.” “It’s the turtles, isn’t it?” Teki shouted accusingly. Winston explained that it isn't always the big purple monster just because legend says so, one has to read between the lines to gain the legitimate truth. Upon reviewing the neighbor’s statements he commanded, “Boltie empty your bag.” and placed down his documents and took a sip of his tea with a content look. Boltie looked around confused but soon acted on the command. “I-I don’t know anything about this. I would never betray you guys.” her paws shook with fear though knowing full well she did not steal it. “I did it,” Armi confessed, tears flowing down his eyes as he stepped up to save Boltie. “I-I wanted to make Mochie proud. I am sorry Boltie, I never intended to hurt you.” He clasped her paws. The air sparkled. Grandpa Whiskers? Teki thought aloud. “I had Armi steal it for safekeeping.” Grandpa Whiskers resonated. “Kind of ironic don’t you think?” Mochie silently snuck in to witness everything. “\Mochie, my lady.” he bowed. “Don’t act cheeky.” Mochie tried to playfully smack him across the arm, inevitably making her hand go through his opaque body. Yuki, Boltie & Winston looked back and forth almost telepathically, Mochie picked up on the confusion and tried to elucidate with an understanding smile, “We were best friends all through our unconventional childhood.” she smiled at her friend insolently. “Mochie warned me, saying that your recipe isn’t safe-” he turned to Teki,”-couldn’t let your hard work go down the drain kiddo.” He smiled Yuki, Boltie & Winston looked back and forth almost telepathically, Mochie picked up on the confusion and tried to elucidate with an understanding smile, “We were best friends all through our unconventional childhood.” she smiled at her friend insolently. “Mochie warned me, saying that your recipe isn’t safe-” he turned to Teki,”-couldn’t let your hard work go down the drain kiddo.” He smiled Winston looked around with a Well-that’s-it-I-guess expression and a little optimistic look. The muddled laughter that filled the room slowly turned into a genuine one. And that is how, just like the sweetness of cinnamon rolls on the day of their reveal to the happy citizens, Halloween magic spread across town.
author: Mahee Puri

title: The Last Dream
text: "Seetha..." a familiar voice called out,it sounded so sweet and comforting,almost like her father."father?.."Seetha called out,her voice seemed worried and was slightly creaking,she ran round the infinite searching for the source of voice,and finally she had found him,her dearest father,with elegantly combed hair consisting of strands of white hair here and there and a bright smile that could make the darkest corner of one's world bright,dressed in a neatly ironed white shirt and mundu with it's golden border emitting a divine shine.His face had started to wrinkle but any imperfection on his body could be unnoticed with his godly affection.There he stood,holding his long arms out to embrace his one and only dear Seetha,he called out again more softer "Seetha...."it made Seetha's heart seem to bloom a thousand flowers...she felt just so ecstatic.She jumped into his arms seemingly crying tears of joy,"father..."her voice was quavering and she held onto him quietly,she embraced his scent to her heart,the smell of sweet jasmine and the grassy earth.She suddenly felt the whole word shaking,or was it that she was being shaken?either way,she was separated from her lovely father. In a sudden blink accompanied with a jolt, Seetha Lakshmi woke up,from her nap at her class.Her eyes were sunken in and dark circles surrounded the sparkling orb of her eyes.Her hair was tied in a twisty and messy braid,she had created it herself,she had no assistance for her mother would be gone for work before she would wake up.Her uniform looked pale,dull and wrinkled,it was washed for sure but it was not new.It was her last year's uniform and the skirt was ever so short that it could only go as far as her tiny little knees.She was a beauty to behold nevertheless. Mr. Rakesh,her math teacher was the one who shook her 'world',she felt her cheeks turn a tint of red as she looked up at the tall and kind man,for a moment,she felt that he was her father,and so she asked in a little astonished voice if he was her father.He gave her a stare of confusion,deep inside though he wouldn't in the least mind if she was his daughter,for she was kind,understanding and obedient.Even if she didn't know,he had always had a soft spot for her.The whole class cracked up laughing and wheezing. "Your mom's here child,oh and also,you have to write this note.And you better write an explanation as well as an imposition for what you have done,young lady" "yes Sir.." she murmured,looking down in embarrassment and guilt. Mr.Rakesh too had felt like he could have not said the imposition part and see a smile of relief escape Seetha's lips.Little Seetha tilted her head over to the classroom door to see her mother,smiling at her,she wasn't at her best at all,after all her mother was now working herself out for a lot and it had took a seemingly well amount of difference on her body and appearance,she was disheveled and pale,her century old saree hanging from her shoulder,so pale that the once indigo dark violet had turned into a pale mauve.She had dry flower on her hair and a small touch of sindoor on her forehead. "Seetha..."she called out,which reminded Seetha again of her lovely dream,only her mother and father could call her so lovingly in the whole world,she thought. Mr. Rakesh signaled the girl to walk to her mother.Holding on to her satchel which had holed everywhere,she got up and walked over to her beloved mother,who by now was holding her arms out to embrace her child."Swetha,how's your husband doing?" "oh,we were going to visit him,Rakesh" ""I see,I hope he would be doing well soon" "Us too! it's really tiring to take care of the house and studying!" interrupted Seetha who now seemed to have been bored by the adult's conversation"well then,we'll take our leave"said Swetha politely.She firmly held Seetha's hand and led her through,Seetha skipping beside her. Rakesh watched them walk beside each other away from the school,he saw how gradually Swetha lost her pretty smile,her desire to look good,and of course the blazing passion in her eyes to make the best out of anything.Afterall,he knew her better than her husband.He had been her friend since they were kids.He loved her and she loved him,but she didn't feel the butterflies he felt when she smiled,nor did she care to acknowledge it,she saw him merely as a friend, he nourished this one sided love forever,only for it to be put down when his friend,one of the dearest, Ram confessed his feelings to Swetha while Rakesh was busy picking flowers for his one and only. Rakesh didn't in the least feel hurt,he knew beforehand that she would not marry him anyway,and Ram was way brighter than he,they had a good future together,he had speculated.And he watched his only true love sail away from the shore,far from his reach.That was how love was,as twisted as ever. There was no happy ending as he thought, for Ram soon got into an unfortunate accident that would make him paralyzed. It only got worse and they didn't have the money to give him the treatment he needed.Soon Ram was welcomed into the sorrowful white rooms of the hospital and Swetha's only available solution to make up for his gap was to work every single bone of hers to ashes,she didn't want others to feel sympathy or pity to her,she wasn't powerless,she thought.So off she went to nurture her family on her own as she faced a lot more hardships than before. Rakesh smiled at himself for being so nostalgic and think about the past,his class was still going on,and the children were walking about talking to one another in the class."stay quiet!Back to page no.98 kids!!"He shouted and off he went to teach the little flowers in his lovely garden. As the sun climbed higher and higher into the sky,Seetha and her mother were kept walking faster and faster.They couldn't afford to lose money on rickshaw nor a bullock,they couldn't dare lose a penny,they could only do with their legs. Seetha was starting to sweat uncontrollably,she thought she would faint any second,she looked up at her gracious and loyal mother,who was so engrossed at the thought of being able to meet her husband again.She had completely forgot about the little bud he had left for her to nurture. "Mamma....My legs hurt,can we rest for some time?"Seetha asked finally,when she felt her heels hurt so worse as it turned red as blood.Without even looking down at her daughter, she picked the little girl up and started to run.Why was mother running?Is dad that severely ill?these kind of horrible thoughts swarmed Seetha's mind. People gave them judgmental and skeptical stares,but they gave no mind to it.All that was in their mind was Ram.To see Ram,to make sure he's well,that's what they'd fight the whole world for.They reached the hospital soon and off they went to stand in the winding line in front of every normal government hospital.It seemed as if they were waiting for what seemed like eternity.Though after half an hour,they were successful in reaching near Ram's room. It wasn't the brightest welcome that they got,with their relatives standing on all sides of the hallway with worried looks,Seetha's maternal grandmother was weeping.Suddenly Seetha saw how her mother's face change rapidly into a face filled with melancholy.Something's wrong,Seetha's heart recited,while pounding heavily."oh dear god don't tell me..." Swetha trailed off.Seetha was let go of soon after,and her mother knelt down with a thud.Her maternal grandmother arose and held Swetha tight in her arms to defend of the prying eyes to see Swetha crying.Still,Seetha didn't get the slightest idea.She walked over to her loving aunt who was worried and markings of dried tears were found on her cheeks."It's nothing dear,your-" she was interrupted by the doctors sharp voice,"it happened at about 11-11.30,that is-" he stared at the clock,"around 2 hours before" The doctor made the room feel intense and the air circulating in it grew colder.Soon he left and the family stayed there,at least for some time till they all decided to go to Swetha's small house.The house was too small for all the people to be in,so some sat on the veranda and some on stools and chairs scattered here and there.While they all mourned in silence,and Swetha weeping,Seetha was wondering about the dream lingering in her mind. She had seen her father smiling ever so clearly and looking at her in the greatest of affection.Her aunt found her nephew look dreamy and lost in another world.And so she inquired'what are you pondering about,dearest?" "I saw my dad in my dream,at school while I accidentally slept" Her aunt was rather surprised and her eyes grew wide,later she gave a little grin to Seetha and looked at her in a loving way and said "So he visited you at last" "Indeed" she felt someone say.But no one there would dare open their mouth.Perhaps the wind, she thought for it carried the words of the dead. ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧ ✧
author: Meera S

title: Our People Are Fighters
text: 18th August 2003 Dear diary, The planes came back today, we are stuck in this hole for the past two days. We have tried to contact the rescuers; their helicopters just ignored us and flew overhead fighting the red planes. Sania is hungry and crying. Abba is trying his best, but the planes bombed every greenery and storage house in our town. I don't know what will happen to us. I just hope I get to know that I will be saved soon.... Mohammed Major Imran looks at the diary entry of a suspected 10-year boy, we're still to be rescued from the remote town of the Dhi Quandir. " Any news of the boy or his family?" asks Imran," no, Sir, but our rescue teams are flying over it as we speak." replied Basheer, the subedar from Prophet Gully. One of the few surviving police officials of the Dhi Quandir. " The Americans have gone too far this time, bombing civilian residential areas." said the pained major." the world is watching, but nobody dares to oppose the Americans strongly." replied Basheer. Major Imran sighed" anyway, where did they find this thing?". "Near the village of Sikandrabad." conveyed the subedar. " Get me a record of the people living there." ask the major." yes, Sir." CHAPTER 2 THE BITTER TRUTH Mohammed looked at the tone pages of his diary, waiting when the rescue teams will come to save him and his family from this building. They had been constantly moving, fearing the red planes. Abba says that the rescuers will come at any moment. It has been five days since they've told us to take shelter. They said that the whites have invaded our home. He is scared. His little sister Sania is just five years old; she has been crying. Ammi has had fever, but she's still trying to find food. They had not eaten anything for two days. He thought of the times before his house was engulfed in flames from an explosion a few houses down. The red planes came every day, sometimes they just flew overhead but sometimes they dropped green things that went BOOM!! It was the same thing that destroyed their house. He thought of all the good times when he used to go to school, play with his friends and lived a carefree life. Now he realized the bitter truth.... He might never see his friends again.... CHAPTER 3 - WHAT DO WE DO? Mohammed looked out of the broken window. An old man that he knew quite too well was out there waving his hands like a maniac. "Suliman! what in prophets name are you doing?" shouted Mohammed. Suliman was a shepherd from Mohammed's village. He was dear to Mohammed as he has spent a lot of time with Suliman." can't you see son; I'm calling those American jets So that they can save me. what about you?" replied Suliman." are you mad Suliman? They will blow you up, wipe you off the face of this planet. Come here fast." What are you doing? Do you wanna die?" angered on Mohammed. Finally, after what seemed like hours to Mohammed, Suliman reached the building." what do you want little boy?" asked Suliman." I just want you to not die." replied Mohammed. Mohammed's Father and his mother, hearing Mohammad yelled earlier, stepped into the room with Mohammad little sister in their arms. " Suliman, why were you roaming around? Because we are trying to contact the government headquarters." exclaimed Mohammed's mother." OK, if that means safety, then count me in." replied Suliman nonchalantly. Suddenly, they heard a loud bang. They looked up in the sky. 3 red planes followed by 4 green planes were flying in the sky. Mohammed could see his country's flag on the green planes. Suddenly bullets started firing from the planes. One of the Green Plane's wings caught on fire and the plane crashed just a few kilometers away from them. Abba shouted," Mohammed come here, we have to go to the next room." Abba started running with Mohammed. Just then they heard a sickening sound. It was a sound they knew all too well. KABOOM! The house just next to them exploded, sending Mohammed and Abba flying. They had just sustained minor injuries. Mohammed looked ahead, he saw his sister and his mother running towards them. He looked back and what he saw made his heart stop. Suliman lied sprawled across on his back. Blood gushing out of his legs and arms. He was aghast by the site. He Tried to move towards Suliman, but his father dragged him away and started running away from the building.." He's gone" was all abba said simply, trying to hold back emotions. The red planes showered the green planes with bullets, one after another. The green planes dropped like flies blasting their own city. Mohammad watched in horror as the scenes unfold. He asked abba " What do we do?".... " anything on that boy?" asked Major Imran." yes. So his last sightings were at Muquadarabad." replied Basheer." ready a squad for Muquadarabad. We are going for a rescue." Imran said with confidence. Mohammed's sitting in a rugged shop with his sister in his arms, sleeping. " I'll protect you whatever the circumstances are." his sister woke up with a start." I am scared moh" replied his sister." don't worry, we'll be fine." though deep inside, Even Mohammed was not sure if they'll be fine. All they had was a glimmer of hope." what is the red planes come again?" asked his sister." we'll be safe, don't worry." replied Mohammed.. Suddenly, they heard a loud siren." that's the air raid siren." said abba. They looked out of a crack in the ceiling, Both red and green helicopters filled the sky. A green helicopter broke formation and started flying towards them. The helicopter landed a few meters away from them. A man started running towards them, then bang! He got struck right in the chest by a bullet. Imran shouted from the helicopter "What? No,Basheer!!" he started running towards the fallen soldier, Basheer was still breathing. Basheer looked at Imran, "Tell my mother, I am sorry, she wanted me to buy a house in the city, but I couldn't, tell her I'm sorry." with that, Basheer left for his second life in heaven. "You god forsaken Americans!" Imran raged with anger. Leaving Mohammed and his family for someone else to rescue, he got in his helicopter and mowed down every red plane in existence there. He was unstoppable. No mercy was shown to the Americans. They dropped like flies. In the end, when there was no red in the sky, the red in his eyes disappeared too. He landed near Mohammad and his family." come on, let's get you to a safe place." said Imran, with the fire smoldering inside of him. They boarded the helicopter and left. Chapter 5 THE NOT-SO-DISTANT FUTURE... A couple days later.... "The war ended yesterday with withdrawal of American troops." the TV crackled and switched off. Mohammed ran out of his tent. The helicopters were ready to take them back to their town of Dhi Quandir. They stepped onto the helicopter." we'll rebuild a town better than ever before." declared Mohammed to his sister Sania. They reached Dhi Quandir. Ahmad Anas family walked out into the Sunset, ready to rebuild and towards a new life. 2 years later… Mohammed was now 12. His town of Dhi Quandir was even better than before. It took them six months to rebuild their town back to it's former glory. He saw a shepherd. It reminded him of Suliman... He turned sad. He saw a car roll into his driveway. Major Imran stepped out and rang the bell to their house. He stepped inside " I just wanted to invite you all to Basheer and other martyr's medal ceremony." we'd love to." replied abba. The war left an everlasting effect on Dhi Quandir but the town rebuilt itself. The people are the town, not the buildings. Mohammed sat in the corner and smiled. His people were fighters.
