title: THE CANNY SCIENTIST
text: After graduating with my degree, I began working in the Center for Cellular Molecular Biology in Hyderabad under the supervision of Dr. Lucas Urquhart, a renowned scientist in the whole country. He was a chubby amiable man with a witty humor in his 40s. It was another frenzied morning in the maddening traffic of Hyderabad; replete with honking and swearing all around helping very little to reach my destination. Science has always been the base of life for me. To know the facts and science of things around us and still be fascinated upon the creations of Nature. From the moment I read about the famous Marie Curie to the moment i am about to live 20 minutes from now; Being a scientist for a middle class woman like me was a dream turned into reality. As Curie once herself said, “One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.” Today was my first experiment upon the use of pancreatic islet cells to treat patients with Type 1 Diabetes without transplanting the whole pancreas. If succeeded it would be the next step towards the path of curing Type 1 Diabetes. When I entered my laboratory, Dr. Urquhart had already invited himself to my chair and casually reading about my new theories to add to the experiments. “You are sitting in my chair doctor,” I accused, “and those are my ideas. One might take this as content- theft which when i last checked was not allowed in this Institution.” I told him sneaking to snatch my notebook from his hand. “And you are quite a canny young scientist. Great ideas you have here Dr. Elias.” He sighed as if bored. “And regarding your accusation it is not theft if you work under me.” “Sadly, Yes but let us keep the gloating for the rest of the day it is only 7 in the morning.” I informed him taking back my notebook with all the respect I could gather this early in the morning without a cup of coffee. He rolled his eyes and began walking behind me towards the refrigerator to collect our first sample of cells for the experiment. The board of director only allowed us access to rat cells. Alas! beggars cannot be choosers. Our first experiment is to use the new bio-hybrid device to trick the immune system into not rejecting the transplanted islet cells of the donor without the use of immunosuppressive drugs. I took the rat cells and proceeded towards the laboratory. Starting the experiment, I caught Lucas from the side of my eye starting the recorder. “DR.VERA ELIAS. EXPERIMENT 1. SUBJECT MOUSE J. INJECTING RAT ISLET CELLS TRANSPLANTED FROM MOUSE A.” I said into the recorder waiting for any results, any hope. After 2 days of observing the test results and countless problems MOUSE J died from diabetes-related cardiomyopathy, taking my first ounce of hope with him. I did not lose hope working day and night for the next 4 months, experimenting with 16 mice not one of them living more than Day 10. Presence of DR. Urquhart helped but each mouse took piece of my willingness to work on this experiment, my dream from university. Lucas walked into the laboratory on day? I do not even remember which day it is quite frankly. He looked tired and sick but i did not had the energy to discuss other people`s problems when i could not solve my own at the moment. “You need to take a break Vera. Your days are filled with taking care of these mouse`s and experimenting every possible variant of islet cells. When did you last sleep? ” 3 days ago, I think. I need to theorize this variant in my papers. Would you mind keeping an extra eye on MOUSE O tonight? She seems to be showing possible recovery signs. ” I answered adjusting the microscope length. I had to examine too many ideas to count in the next couple of days so i could present my experiment, if it even succeeds in the next “Medicine Invention summit”. I had little to no time for old boring small talk. He smiled at me as if he just got some life changing idea coughing as he threw my coffee cup in the dustbin and moved the papers from the desk, responding “Take a day off. Think about the possible solutions instead of trying to correct the same variant cells again and again. Move forward and stop dwelling in the past.” I agreed that it was a pretty unhealthy lifestyle, packing my bags to leave for my apartment biding goodbye to Mouse O and Dr. Urquhart. Since it was only 1 mile away from the laboratory, I reached home showered and quickly went to bed. The next morning, I woke up to a strange mail in my mail box that read - “ A message for Dr. Elias from Mr.X. I heard about your experiment from a friend. I started a similar experiment years ago but stopped it recently after diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes, in almost the last stages. The Irony of life. The disease that i was fighting to cure from such long years had finally caught on to me. I have attached my ideas for the modifications in the device and variants in the next page. I will not be able to save my own life but I hope you save the lives of million others with your upmost knowledge and my ideas. ” I was astonished with the ideas in the next page. It suggested severe modifications in the device that i would not have thought about in hundred years. There was no sender`s address in the mail and the name was anonymous too giving me little to work in knowing the identity of this mysterious scientist. I wondered what it was like studying a nightmare for years only to get defeated by it in the end with the worst possible way. I went to the laboratory next morning returning in a way better mood then i was way before. I shared my ideas with Dr. Urquhart both of us starting to work on MOUSE R with a bright will. I modified the device adding my own brain to the ideas provided by the mysterious Mr. X. Mr. Urquhart left in between after looking sick for a while. I continued my work, starting the recorder. “DR.VERA ELIAS. EXPERIMENT 2671. SUBJECT MOUSE R. INJECTING RAT ISLET CELLS TRANSPLANTED FROM MOUSE Q AFTER MODIFICATIONS MADE IN THE BIO-HYBRID DEVICE. ” I injected the device inside the mouse starting the clock. “00:00:00” Waiting for a little while i looked back on the clock. “00:14:56” The mouse had still been sleeping not showing one sign of movement. “06:47:22” Mouse R woke up after 6 hours. He is still showing signs of drowsiness. “20:07:25” He has started jumping around the mouse cell. The other mice were never this full of energy. After 20 days, Mouse R was still alive and more healthy than he ever was. The idea of finally reaching the breakthrough in my dream experiment crossed my mind at this exact moment making me more happy than i ever had been. “ I did it. “ I whispered making myself aware of the extent this result here could bring to the lives of countless patients out there. Dr. Urquhart was one of the first person to congratulate me on the success of the experiment after Mouse R showed 4+ months of speedy recovery. The experiment got published in the “ National Magazine of Medical Sciences ” getting me calls from the United States and many other countries to work in the next phase on humans. This was the next step and i was more than ready to take it to the next level. Before moving to Delhi to work in AIIMS for the next phase, I attended the Medicine Invention Summit as a Chief guest. During the ending speeches, Dr. Urquhart took the mike. “Vera Elias is one of the promising scientists; I have worked with in the last 22 years of my career. Her research is a starting feat for the promised cure of the nightmare disease known as Diabetes for all the patients out there and men like me. ” I could not understand his last words after more than three months of when it was spoken. A week later, I moved into my new apartment in Delhi started working with many doctors in the laboratory of AIIMS and continued my research. Three months later, I got the call. “Hello. Is this Dr. Elias? ” “Yes. Who is this? ” “I am daughter of Dr. Urquhart. My father had been suffering from Type 2 diabetes for a while and had been bed ridden from the last month. ” “What?” “He died this morning and one of his last wishes was to inform you that the ideas were his but all the hard-work and smartness, it was you. It has always been only YOU. ” The call disconnected. I was so taken back that i sat in the chair beside with a shaken body. Flashbacks of the last year showing in front of my eyes like a cheap movie and it all clicked at once. Dr. Urquhart being sick all the time, his confidence in the project and his last words to me. “Patients out there and men like me.” MR.X WAS DR. LUCAS URQUHART. HE CALLED ME THE CANNY SCIENTIST BUT IN THE END HE WENT DOWN AS ONE.
author: Pratikshya Mallick

title: KINDNESS IS ALWAYS WORTH IT
text: It was 12 am and suddenly Mr. Nelson's phone rang. That's when little Summer woke up and saw her parents rushing out of the house. Summer's parents were doctors by profession and helped people all around the world. Sometimes they even fell ill themselves but they never stopped helping people. Growing up Summer just wanted to be as kind and helping as her parents. Once when she was 6 years old, she went to a park with her nanny. There she found a boy her age crying under a tree. His name was Tanner and he had lost his dog Coco. They spent 3 hours to find his dog and Tanner thanked Summer for her help. Summer was glad to find a new friend and soon she got to know that Tanner was also in her school. Both became best friends and started hanging out together. Years went by and both, Summer and Tanner, were in high school. One afternoon Summer saw that her parents had came back from a trip to Texas. She opened the door for them and saw a thin, beautiful girl wearing big headphones and a walking stick in her hand stood behind them. She looked kinda bored. "Oh sweetheart! We are back and look who's here....Your sister Nicole." said her mother joyfully. Summer was shocked to hear this and of course this was a lot to digest. That's when Nicole came forward and said something to her. ﻿Summer was not able to understand a bit because Nicole could not speak English. On the top of that Summer had to share her room with Nicole cause there were no extra rooms available. Nicole was a headache for Summer because she snored so loudly that Summer didn't sleep the entire night. Due to all this she slept in her class and got scolded by the teacher. The next day Summer's parents enrolled Nicole in her school. Summer had to babysit her for the entire day. Summer told her condition to Tanner and he offered to translate the language or her because he knew that language very well. Then once at 10:00 pm Summer walked into her room after coming back from a party and saw Nicole fast asleep. She saw some papers lying under Nicole's bed. She picked them up and saw that Nicole had worked upon some very advanced math equations. Summer was impressed and thought to register Nicole's name for the upcoming math quiz. She thought of this as piece of kindness and a way to extend help towards Nicole for her better future. The next day after giving Nicole's name, Summer was searching for Nicole to tell her the great news. She found Nicole sitting in the park and Tanner was standing beside her. "It's good that you both have met each other." said Summer joining them. after that Summer told everything to Tanner so that Tanner could translate it for Nicole. But just as Summer stopped, Nicole burst out and said,"How could you do something like that without my consent? Can't you mind your own business?" Both, Tanner and Summer, were shocked to hear Nicole's perfect English. "Why have you been lying to us this whole time?" asked Summer. Suddenly Nicole's face looked so mean. 'Just to bother you because I can and how dare you sign me up for something without even asking me?" replied Nicole. "I was just trying to do something nice for you." Summer explained. "Well then stop! I don't need anything from you." snapped Nicole. With that, Nicole stormed off and Summer was shocked. She tried to tell her parents that Nicole had lied about not knowing English. But they were so in love with Nicole that they didn't even believe Summer. Nicole was so mean and cunning that in front of Summer's parents she acted all innocent but as soon as they left for some work, she was a totally different person. Later at school, Summer noticed that Nicole would sneak off during lunch. So, she decided to follow her one day and see what she was up to. She found Nicole sitting in the music room by the piano. She was playing a soft tune and was really good. "That's beautiful" Summer said. Nicole turned around and asked "What do you want?" "Answers mostly. An apology would be nice too." Summer said. "You're not getting one so just leave." Nicole said. "Why are you hiding out here?" Summer further asked. "It's quiet and people don't stare at me or pity me." Nicole said rubbing her leg. "Does it hurt a lot?" Summer asked Nicole. "All the time! But I don't wanna talk about it." replied Nicole. "Okay fine! and I am sorry for butting in this competition but I've seen your work." said Summer. "You could actually win this thing." "Why do you care?" asked Nicole. I don't know, I just learnt it from my parents- to be kind." Summer replied. "I doubt it but I guess getting some independence won't be that bad for me."Nicole smiled. When the competition came Nicole aced it and received her reward. Later at home, she even confessed about lying to everybody. Although Summer's parents were shocked but they accepted her apology happily and also apologised to Summer. The next day at school, Nicole was on cloud nine. She was getting compliments and attention. Summer was so glad to see her happy. Then once Summer noticed that Nicole had been limping more lately but she ignored it. Everything was going smoothly until one day summer saw a guy in a class and he was talking about Nicole. "Being with Nicole is so cool. She is so good at everything but the best part is that she is doing all my homework for me and I am getting straight A's" said the guy. After listening to this Summer went to find Nicole. Summer was shocked to see that Nicole was doing that guy's homework. "Nicole you need to throw that away right now. That guy is just a good for nothing jerk. He is using you." Summer said. "Oh stop it Summer. You just think that he's too good for someone like me." Nicole replied. Like this both Summer and Nicole got into a fight again. At last Nicole started crying and stormed off. After some time when Summer had cooled down she went to find Nicole. She searched a lot but couldn't find her anywhere. She started panicking and called Tanner. They both started searching for her. Soon it started raining and finally Summer found Nicole sitting in a park fully drenched. she was shivering like crazy. Summer took her home and sorted out everything. "I love you sis." said Summer. "Me too" replied Nicole smiling. The next day Summer took Nicole to a doctor. After having some tests they got to know that Nicole had a rare muscle condition which may take 3-4 months to recover.The treatment started and Summer was always there with Nicole during her hospital days. Soon it was time for Nicole to return home. As soon as Nicole opened the house door, she was surprised to see such a big welcome. Even Tanner and some other friends of Nicole were there. That's when Summer walked towards Nicole and said" I know being kind is hard but worth it."
author: Miloni Jain

title: The Crystal Radio
text: My nephew Ernest Wood was a student at Oakland University. Delia, Ernest’s mother, told me about Ernest’s journey as a detective. How did he become one? Ernest joined the club, “Crystal Radio” formulated by his university. This club trained students to become detectives. When Ernest was in Crystal Radio, he quickly surpassed his fellow detectives. As a result, the officials of the club planned to give him a test. But there was one terrible flaw in him: He was so scared of the dark that he could not go on midnight searches or detective missions. This narrowed down his chances of taking the tests before he left the university. The day came for him to hear the board’s decision. After the evening study shift, Ernest was called to the board. The board put up a vote to decide whether he should write the examinations. And the results were that 10 abstained, 4 voted for him and 6 voted against him. Ernest was so sad that he did not realize that some people were just behind him. This fright jolted him out of his sadness, and he began to think quickly. If he tried to run away, the gang would go after him and not leave him alive. So, he decided to hide. Being the amazing detective he was, he hid in the shadows and noted down all the conversations. It goes as follows: Jim: Poe, we need some cash. And now! Poe: Jim, I wish I could make the sky rain with dollars. But I don’t know how to get that kind of money. Coop: I know how to get us some money. Poe: What?! The cops would get us before we mugged a single piece of candy. Coop: No stealing’s involved, chicken-heart. We’ll break into that university ‘round the corner and the next morning, rob the kids of their phones, call their parents, make up some excuse, and get money. We’d be the richest thugs in California! Jim: Never knew you had such a brain. We’ll do it tomorrow. The meeting broke up and Ernest was so happy he could save his university that he suddenly wrote down, “I am not afraid of the dark. It gives me opportunities to save people.” Ernest ran to the nearest police station where the deputy commissioner was just coming out of his office only to run back into the office again with Ernest and deployed policemen to sneak in through a special trap door and heavily guard the gates of the University. What a surprise the burglars would get tomorrow! The next morning, the three thieves broke into the university and stationed themselves at the gates. And, just as the first batch of students walked into the campus, the thieves found themselves surrounded by blue uniforms and pistols on all sides. They surrendered themselves and were duly arrested. When the board found out about Ernest’s involvement in the mission and his extraordinary detecting skills, he was immediately inducted to the highest rank of detectives, given a radio, and was even awarded the vice-chancellor’s award for “extraordinary acts of service from an ordinary human.” Ernest is the head of the FBI Intelligence Branch and now does detective work for a living but always but he carries a certain piece of paper wherever he goes which contains, “I am not afraid of the dark. It gives me opportunities to save people.” And Ernest always does something wonderful in the worst of circumstances and helps others in the darkest of circumstances.
author: Philip  Chummar

title: The Trip to the Pacific
text: “It’s Easter Holidays again! Yay!” yelled 13-year-old Rose as she entered her home after the last day of school. “Yeah! We’re going to have a blast with Jake and Julie!” replied her twin brother Rob. Jake, a 14-year-old, and Julie, a 12-year-old, were Rob’s and Rose’s cousins. Rob and Rose had gone to their cousins' house in the summer vacation, where they had their first adventure with the Pegasi. The four cousins were given watches by their Pegasi friends- Sky, Storm, Sunshine and Heather, with whom they defeated a witch called Sheila. Sheila had robbed the 'Crystal of Life' from the Queen of Pegasi, Aeria to make a potion of immortality. All four of the cousins wore their watches, anticipating a call from their Pegasi friends. Suddenly, the watches started tinkling. It was a pleasant sound, and Rob and Rose sat listening to it for a minute before they came back to their senses. Shaking out of the ‘trance’ of the tinkling, Rob picked the call from Sunshine. When he picked the call, he saw Sunshine standing on a seashore. Rob asked, “Hey Sunshine! What’s new?” Sunshine replied, “Rob there’s a problem. Heather is waiting for you and Rose outside your house. She will bring you here. You don’t need to tell your mother anything because time will stop this minute until this mission is over. Quick!” she said and her image faded away. At the same time at Jake’s and Julie’s house…… Jake and Julie were packing up to go to their cousins’ house when Jake’s watch started chirping. The siblings exchanged looks. “Yes… Another adventure!” Jake whispered. “Yay!”, Julie whispered back as her brother picked the call from Sky. Sky popped up in a space in the air where the light from the watch projected her image. Julie and Jake notice that Sky looked a little worried. Without giving them a chance to speak, Sky said, “Guys, Storm’s waiting outside your house. He will bring you here. You have no time to lose!” and her image faded away. “What was that all about?!?” asked Julie. “I have no idea.” replied Jake. “But it did sound urgent. Come on, let's go!” Just then, Julie’s watch chirped. “What now?” huffed Julie. “Just pick the call,” said Jake. Julie picked the call, and once more, Sky’s image was projected into the air. “Hey, don’t bother telling your mum anything. She won’t notice you gone. Time will stop and everyone will be frozen except you four and us,” she said. “Cool.” said Jake. “Sky, Rob and Rose know about this right?” “Yes. Sunshine would have told them by now. Oh, and wear your adventure suits. They are waterproof right?” “Yeah.” Said Julie. “Why?” “Storm will explain. I’ve got to tell Rob and Rose; I didn’t tell Sunshine to tell them. So, don't waste another minute. Change and come quickly. See you here!” She said, as once again her image dissolved. Both of them changed quickly and went outside, where they found Storm waiting for them. He smiled at them and said, “Boy! You kids do take a long time to do things!” “Hey! We came as fast as we could!” Said Julie defending herself and her brother. “Cool down! I was just joking. Climb on!” Storm replied. “So, what's happening and why did you tell us to wear our adventure suits?” Jake asked. “Well Jake, your second adventure is not going to be with us. We’ll drop you at the Pacific and a few of our cousins will take over after that.” Replied Storm. “Sky will clear everything else for you.” He added. “The Pacific! Wow!” Exclaimed Jack and Julie together and they looked at each other and laughed. Storm remained silent for the rest of the journey. Soon, they reached a beach where there was no one except Rob, Rose Storm and Heather. Jake and Julie ran towards Rob and Rose as soon as they saw them. They were all excited as they turned to Sky and asked her what their mission was. Sky replied “As Heather and Sunshine told you children, we will not be accompanying you for this adventure and I am not the right Pegasus to tell you what your mission is. Children, meet Cyclone, Tide, Coral and Oceana. They are our cousins who live in the seas and oceans; they are the Water Pegasi. Coral, explain the problem please.” The Water Pegasi were horses who looked like their friends, but they had scales instead of fur! A colourful horse then started speaking. Her voice was sweet and cheerful, “Hey guys, my name is Coral. My friends and I are going to assist you on this mission. The problem might sound like a minor one to you, but it is a life or death situation for the sea creatures. Humans like yourself, except of course, adults, come diving every day. We Water Pegasi can turn invisible with the help of our magic scales. On one of her daily rounds, Oceana here, saw them communicating using sign language. They were measuring the length of the coral they wanted to dig out. We don’t know why they need it yet, but it will definitely affect the lives of the creatures living there. For us Water Pegasi it won't be a problem because we can move fast but for the creatures who live there, they can lose their families, homes and lives.” The four children listened in spellbound silence. “Why should we help though? We would be going against our own people by doing that.” Julie finally said. “Yeah, maybe they’ll just take a little piece for research purposes.” Rob spoke up. “Although corals are mistaken for non-living things, they are live animals. And we knew that a question like this might arise, that’s why we asked you to bring your suits,” said Tide. “We’re going to take you to the reef and show you why this is so important to us.” Rob started protesting, but Rose said, “There’s no harm in going, Rob. We’ll come with you, Tide.” The Pegasi provided snorkels and oxygen tanks to the children and they set off to the reef. After a good amount of swimming, the children and the pegasi reached the reef. The image they saw there was mesmerising. The children swam around and realised how much damage would be caused to the beautiful creatures living there even if only a small piece of the coral was to be dug out. Suddenly, they saw some figures swimming towards them. “Quick, follow me! I know the perfect hiding spot” said Oceana. Everyone followed Oceana into a hollow cave-like structure behind the corals which held the children perfectly. The Pegasi went invisible and all of them held their breaths in excitement and anxiousness. Jake, having attended a sign-language course at school the previous term, could understand what the gestures meant. Once the men had departed, the kids and the Pegasi swam back up to the shore. “What were they gesturing?” Rose asked “They were talking about how the coral could get them good money if sold as jewellery,” said Oceana. “Yes, I can confirm that’s the truth” said Jake. “They are definitely not good guys.” “What can we do to help you?” asked Julie. “We’re only children” “We need you to contact a coast guard and convince them to take appropriate measures.” said Cyclone “But will they believe us though?” asked Rose “Yes. They will. We can show them these pictures as proof. I got these on my watch while we were down there,” said Rob. The children found a coast guard and explained the situation to him. Once they showed the proof, he assured the children that measures would definitely be taken and got Rob to forward the pictures as proof to show the higher officials. The Pegasi thanked the children and said this was all they could do and that they would let them know when the fraudsters were caught. Sky and Sunshine dropped the children back to their respective homes. Epilogue A few weeks later, the cousins were in Rob and Rose’s home talking about their latest adventure, when all their watches started buzzing. Jake picked up the call and they saw all eight of their Pegasi friends smiling at them. “Hello kids! We called to tell you that the fraudsters belonged to a large group of Coral smugglers and have finally been arrested. And thank you so much for your help.” said Cyclone “You’re welcome guys! We’re glad we could help catch the bad guys and are happy that all the creatures are safe.” said Rose The cousins had lots of fun during the rest of the holidays and waited for their next adventure!
author: Anishka Jagannivas

title: A Rainbow Tryst
text: Is it possible that a single person can change your life? Can they erase the darkness of aimlessness with the candle of purpose? Would you ever be willing to put them before yourself? Such questions always puzzled Aditya, but he never anticipated finding any answers. But little did he know that one rainy July afternoon, he would meet the answer to every question of his. Aditya worked as a delivery boy for a small kirana store. He just managed to make ends meet but was satisfied with life. Every day was the same - pick up groceries and deliver them. His life was 'perfect', except he didn't have a dream. A dream that makes you go to any length. A dream that does not let you sleep. A dream that gives your life purpose. As usual, he was on his way to deliver groceries, this time to an orphanage. He was on his way when suddenly the Sun hid behind heavy, grey clouds, and it started to pour. With his bike, he took shade under a banyan tree. That was when he saw her. In the distance was a girl struggling to navigate her way with a stick. Holding a packet of milk in one hand, she was getting drenched in the rain. Aditya ran and put his hands around her shoulders, so she didn't get wet. He took the packet of milk from her hands and led her to the shade. "Thank you," she said. "I am Navya. I stay in the orphanage nearby." "Really? What a coincidence! I was going there to drop some groceries when it started to rain. Well, I am Aditya. It was a pleasure meeting you!" Navya continued to talk about her life. Aditya found out she was an orphan and was abandoned by her parents when they found out she was blind. She had grown up in this very orphanage. Since then, she dedicated her life to serving all the children there. With every passing moment, his respect and admiration for Navya grew. Suddenly, the Sun reappeared, but it did not stop raining. In no time, a rainbow graced the sky. "This is the most enchanting rainbow I have ever seen! " exclaimed Aditya with wonder. Navya chuckled. "It is my dream to see a rainbow. I can't even imagine how beautiful it must be with all those colours!" Aditya offered to drop Navya on his bike, who readily agreed to this proposal. Once they reached the orphanage, all the students came running towards Navya. They were happy that their didi was safe. Aditya smiled at this. Since then, he started to drop by the orphanage regularly and help with the chores there. His relationship with Navya drastically improved and they became closer. Aditya's life had changed. Being around Navya made him happier than ever. He enjoyed his time spent with the children. But most importantly, he now had a purpose. He wanted to fulfil Navya's dream. He was willing to do anything to show her a rainbow. He was no longer satisfied with his meagre salary. "Even if I do manage to save my entire salary, it would take me at least twelve years to save enough money for her surgery," he thought. Aditya needed to do something more. He wished for Navya on every birthday, every shooting star, every lost eyelash, every penny in a fountain was dedicated to fulfiling her dream. And perhaps it all paid off. He got the opportunity he wanted. But he still had to pay the price. "No! This will not happen!" screamed Navya in anger. "I will never let you go there!" Just about a week ago, Aditya saw an advertisement in the newspaper. It was for labour recruitment in a mica mine. The mica mined is of the best quality, but the miners must pay a heavy price. Being near the fault zone, it is said that not a single miner ever came out of that mine alive. On the bright side, they did pay well. And that was all he cared about. "You needn't worry about me, Navya," said Aditya reassuring her. "It's for the best that I will go." Once Aditya made a decision, not even wild horses could hold him back. He took the job and left. Navya was inconsolable. She could think about nothing, but Aditya. She spent the next many weeks crying. She refused to eat and grew weak. The children were worried about her. It was their love and concern that forced her to put her misery aside and take care of them. No, she did not forget Aditya. He left a void in her life that no one could fill. Whenever she found time, she wrote him letters but never received a reply. Still, she did not lose faith. Days turned to weeks. Weeks to months. And in no time, it was more than an year since Aditya was gone. Navya still did not hear from him. Her friends requested her to forget about him, for he might have perished in the mines. But Navya was certain that he was safe and will return for her. About three months later, she received an envelope filled with money. Her friends counted and told her it was just enough for her surgery. There was no name on the envelope, but Navya was certain Aditya sent it. Her friends were afraid that he passed away, and that the money was sent by the mining company to compensate for the loss. But seeing Navya so happy, they decided to keep it to themselves. Navya underwent the operation. When she opened her eyes, tears streamed down her cheeks. It was such a beautiful world that she had never seen. She looked around like a child with newfound excitement. Then suddenly it hit her - she might never be able to see the person who gifted her vision. He sacrificed everything for her. He loved her more than anyone. Her tears of joy were now tears of pain. Still, she gathered the strength to get a grip on herself. This was the least she could do for Aditya. The children in the orphanage were very happy to see her. Navya was overjoyed to see the faces of the children she knew for so long. Aditya gave her a new perspective on life. She would be forever grateful to him. It had been about six months since her operation. Navya enjoyed life more than ever. She still didn't forget Aditya, perhaps she never would. She was inside cutting vegetables for dinner when one of the children called her. "Navya didi! Look! There's a rainbow in the sky!" Navya left everything and ran. It felt surreal - about two years ago, she wouldn't have imagined seeing a rainbow. Yet here she was, running towards the terrace with childlike excitement in her eyes. And then she saw it. Indeed, it was the most beautiful thing she ever saw. The way so many colours blended in one ribbon across the sky! Navya was awestruck. The raindrops mixed with her tears. A dream finally fulfilled. Suddenly, the void Aditya left in her life felt more profound. The first time she met him was on a day just like this. He changed her life in every possible way. He made it the purpose of his life to show her a rainbow, but he could never see his goal accomplished. Her tears were now flowing for Aditya. That was when she heard a voice from behind. A voice she knew better than any other. A voice that guided her when she was all alone. A voice she loved dearly. "This is the most enchanting rainbow I have ever seen!" said the voice. Navya's face curved into a smile.
author: Aratrika Basu
illustrator: Aindri C; Ariful Islam; Deepa Balsavar; Edwin  Irabor; Greystroke; Helga Parekh; Jagdish Joshi; Jesse  Breytenbach; Manisha Naskar; Offei Tettey  Eugene; Phan Thành  Đạt; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Priyankar Gupta; Shambhavi Singh

title: The Chef's Daughter
text: Once upon a time, a daughter complained to her father that her life was miserable and that she didn’t know how she was going to make it. She was tired of fighting and struggling all the time. It seemed that just as one problem was solved, another one soon followed. Her father, a chef, took her to the kitchen. He filled three pots with water and placed each on a high fire. Soon the three pots began to boil, and he placed potatoes in one pot, eggs in the second pot and ground coffee beans in the third pot. He then let them sit and boil without saying a word to his daughter. The daughter moaned and impatiently waited, wondering what he was doing. After twenty minutes he turned off the burners. He took the potatoes out of the pot and placed them in a bowl. He took the eggs out and placed them in a bowl. He then ladled the coffee out and placed it in a cup. Turning to her, he asked. “What do you see?”. “Potatoes, eggs and coffee,” she hastily replied.“Look closer”, he said, “and touch the potatoes.” She did and noted that they were soft. He then asked her to take an egg and break it. After pulling off the shell, she observed the hard-boiled egg. Finally, he asked her to sip the coffee. Its rich aroma brought a smile to her face. "Father what does this mean?” she asked. He explained that the potatoes, the eggs and the coffee beans had each faced the same adversity – the boiling water. However, each one reacted differently. The potato went in strong, hard and unrelenting, but in boiling water, it became soft and weak. The egg was fragile, with the thin outer shell protecting its liquid interior until it was put in the boiling water. Then the inside of the egg became hard. However, the ground coffee beans were unique. After they were exposed to the boiling water, they changed the water and created something new. "Which are you?" he asked his daughter. "When adversity knocks on your door, how do you respond? Do you become weak, like a potato, hard on the inside, like an egg, or do you change the circumstances, like the coffee beans?" MORAL: There are different ways to react to hardship. Don't be weak or suppress things - change circumstances from within. THE END
author: Viha  Ashar
illustrator: David Chisha; Navika  Kharbanda; Viha  Ashar

title: Struggling To Survive
text: Most parents wish their children to grow up to be a doctor, a lawyer, or a successful businessperson, but not Esther’s parents because all they want their little baby girl to be healthy always. One sunny day at a hospital, “She’s not going to live. But if she did, she would be a vegetable,” was only answer that three-months-old baby girl’s parents could hear. Esther’s parents were very excited when they heard they’re expecting a little girl and couldn’t wait their children to tell they’re going to have a new baby sister! Their children told to be very careful not to hit their newborn baby sister, and change the diapers when it’s dirty, or smells bad. WhenEsther’s parents arrived home with their newborn baby, their children immediately knew their new sister came home. They did everything what they told to do, and even gave her a bath! They were very excellent with the baby. One sunny day as usual, she played with her brother and sister, but suddenly she threw up and got a fever and felt stiff all over her bodies. Somehow, she felt it and cried, cried, and cried. Of course, her parents didn’t know what to do and slept on it. Hoping next morning she would feel better, but guess what? She was still sick and she really had to go to her family doctor and examine her thoroughly. After one visit, they were relieved to hear that all the babies go through the same routine. During that night, Esther was so sick, and fainted. Her parents, her sister, and her brother, too, were shocked and surprised. All of her relatives and friends were prayed that she would be all right and just be cold and nothing more serious At a university hospital, a doctor told them to get ready for the worst, and that night might be the last night to see her alive. Esther’s parents, of course, fell down to the ground, and cried uncontrollably. ‘All I wanted her to be a healthy baby girl, and grow up. Are those such crimes?’ Esther’s mom cried, cried, and cried to the Mother Maria’s statue. Next morning, the doctor came with a tragic news. The news was that Esther’s not going to live, so they’d better get ready for a funeral. Esther’s mom insisted that she would come alive, and she couldn’t go to funeral, she couldn’t, wouldn’t let her go because her mom somehow believed she would wake up. A few tragic weeks had passed and as if God heard the news, Esther was alive again, but she was like a newborn baby because she couldn’t talk, let alone walk. After the survival, her struggling to survive, and the difficult paths have just begun because no one said that was easy for her to stay alive, and she had to fight all her mighty to maintain. As she saw the obstacles, it was like these: the obstacles are like very high mountains, so all she has to do was climb, climb, and climb and if you fall, get up and climb back again. And because of the sickness, the side-effect had left her crossed-eyes, and her teeth were like rabbit. ‘But that’s ok,’ her mom thought. ‘Because she could and would learn everything, it just takes time to learn them. That is all,’ and she did. One by one, step by step, she learned to walk, and talk. Esther still remembers how she and her mom went to a “special school” to learn to speak forcefully. Especially one day, when she was about to learn to speak a sound “Zzzzzzzzzzzzz,” the teacher made her to speak by putting a chocolate chip on her tongue, and made her say the sound “Zzzzzzzzzzzzzz.”That was the most difficult thing to do and a nightmare to her. If someone asks her if she would go back and learn, she would run away from them. Esther still remembers how she and her mom went to a “special school” to learn to speak forcefully. Especially one day, when she was about to learn to speak a sound “Zzzzzzzzzzzzz,” the teacher made her to speak by putting a chocolate chip on her tongue, and made her say the sound “Zzzzzzzzzzzzzz.”That was the most difficult thing to do and a nightmare to her. If someone asks her if she would go back and learn, she would run away from them. One day, Esther and her mom got on the subway and on their way to “special school” and she was quite as a mouse as always, but suddenly she burst into tears. The reason was that one kid who sat across to Esther was teasing about her crossed-eyes. Hearing this, Esther’s mom was so upset and started to look for a eye doctor who could perform a miracle on her eyes. And luckily she did after the two painful eye surgeries, she was able to see the same way as the normal children do. After many years later, she has some crossed eyes left on her eyes if you see her closely, and carefully. Finally, Esther got into her first kindergarten. Unfortunately after one year, the kindergarten that she went to had to close, nowhere to go. Plus, her best friend’s son’s mom said to Esther’s mom that her son couldn’t play with Esther anymore because the path is going to be so different and that was that. Esther’s mom couldn’t believe what she was hearing. ‘Wasn’t that her who forced my daughter to be his best friend, and wasn’t that her who pretends to be friendly and nice to my daughter?’ After what she had heard, Esther's mom was goddamn mad at her, she started to look for a s econd kindergarten, she was so happy, and couldn’t believe her eyes because they were all wearing a uniform, and the place was so huge. One week later, she was excited because she made some new friends, and she was fitting in there perfectly. One day, her teacher called the whole class, telling them they’re going to have annual recital, and she and her classmates were going to have Spanish dance, so please let their parents to sign a form saying, ‘My daughter,---- is going to participate this dance, and must pay the dance uniform.’ Esther’s parents did, and the annual recital went perfectly. After few years later, she went to an elementary school and graduated. During her last two years of elementary school was a nightmare. She was always picked on, and teased because at times when she speaks, she couldn’t say the word or sentence correctly, and that made everyone laugh, and that got her into tears many times. And so, she survived and had to go to another obstacle. Esther was a brave little girl in front her parents because immediately after Esther graduated from the elementary school, she immigrated to Canada. Soon after she landed in Canada, she went to Canadian high school, and started to adapt a new world prepared for her. During her high school years, she was obedient to finish her high school. But the grades weren’t that good, so she had to go to Communications, and graduated with Comm. 12 with a C. After Esther graduated, she went to Capilno College, hoping that she could somehow get English 12 degree, but she couldn’t. After few years later, she got a certificate with ASL (American Sign Language).Still studying, hoping to get English 12 degree, and still struggling to stay alive.
author: ADITYA  PRATAP

title: Raju's Best Friend
text: It was 8’o clock in the morning and Raju was getting ready for the school. It was getting late and so he hurried to the school. But he was not on time. Let me introduce Raju. He is 12 years old and is studying in 7 th std. He is always late to school and made to stand out of the class in the first period. He recalls the homework given in the previous day only in the second period and again he gets the punishment. Like this he gets the punishment every day. After school hours he goes to play with his friends and there also he doesn’t play well. He gets beaten by his friends and returns back home late and gets the scolding from his mother. This is his daily routine. But that day it was different. As usual he came late to the school and was made to stand outside. Next period it was the test and teacher gave the test paper. Raju was shocked. On the paper it was written “Science test”. Actually, Raju had prepared for the Maths test and so he was shocked. He was the only student who used to score less marks in all the subjects. Raju had an enemy in the school who used to tease him every day. His name was Aahan. He was fat and very strong. He was not so good in studies but better than Raju. He would always use to beat Raju whenever he talked against him. That day Aahan teased Raju very badly and Raju was very angry. He challenged Aahan that “I will beat you in all the sports and become stronger than you”. He went home saying this. Raju sat in his room and thought for some time. He said to himself “Can I do this? This is impossible”. He simply sat for a while. After that for the first time Raju took his answer papers and showed to his mother. To his surprise the mother didn’t scold him and instead consoled him. He narrated the whole story and Raju’s mother told him “Don’t worry, everything will be fine. Nothing is impossible in this world. Work hard and achieve your goals.” Mother’s words inspired Raju and started working hard. In 2 weeks, it was sports day and Raju was preparing for that. His friends Harshit, Ullas and Kavan helped him. Finally, it was sports day. The first sport was Marathon. They had to run for 2kms. Aahan was the champion for 4 years. The marathon would start in half an hour. But Raju was not at all seen. Aahan said to Raju’s friends in a loud voice “Scary boy Raju. He is scared of me. Ha ha ha”. Raju’s friends were disappointed. It was the time for Marathon and the sports teacher gave the signal for the race. All of a sudden Raju was seen from the back and joined the race. Aahan was in the lead and Raju was just behind him. Aahan did cheating and kept his leg across and Raju fell down and got hurt. As usual Aahan again won the race. He again started teasing Raju. Raju was sorrowful. He lost his hope. But he remembered his mother’s words and got ready for the next competition. It was the long jump event. It was Aahan’s chance and he jumped 4m long. After his friends’ it was Raju’s chance. He got slipped while running for the long jump and missed the chance. Raju again lost his hopes. It was end of the day. Next day Raju’s friends asked the teacher to keep Cat’s cradle game. The teacher announced on the stage that the Cat’s cradle game would be there for the competition. All were ready. It was Aahan’s chance first. He didn’t know about Cat’s cradle game at all. He was doing some nonsense. Next it was Raju’s chance. He was bit nervous in the beginning. He started with a simple one. Then he continued showing some amazing tricks. Judges were impressed and Raju was declared as a winner. Aahan was ashamed and went to Raju and asked him to teach the Cradle game. Aahan said sorry to Raju about the past. Raju taught Aahan the Cat’s cradle tricks. Aahan was very happy. After that they both became best friends and helped each other. Raju became punctual and started scoring good marks in all the subjects. Showed good improvements in sports also with the help of Aahan. Thus, Aahan became Raju’s best friend.
author: Suchit B K

title: Shivani saves the ocean
text: Shivani was a young girl from Chennai. She is a 6th grader in middle school. She was a kind and a generous girl. She used to help out poor people around her society by teaching children and providing them things from her home. Once she arranged a fund raiser event in her society for education of poor children in slum near her society. Her parents too were supportive and supported her event. Shivani was going on a school trip to the beach tomorrow. She was very excited, so she quickly packed an umbrella, snacks, a pink hat, a basket and shovel, magazines and her huge earth- shaped beach ball! My beachball! The next morning was going to be a great day of Shivani's life. She got ready, and went to school. From there, they boarded the bus and set off! Soon they reached a calm, sandy, green and a watery beach! She and her friends were eating packaged food and had juices. They played beach games with ball and danced. The ocean waves were so beautifully blue green, that Shivani decided to dive in. She dressed into her swimsuit she had packed in the morning and SPALSHHH! What an amazing dive!!! Shivani went swimming and splashing and having a lot of fun in the water. She saw her friends building a sandcastle. She decided to come out. Just as she was about to head back, a wave dumped her in and she went far away in deep water. She tried to escape, but she couldn't. She was drowned! Shivani looked here and there, but there was nothing but water! She started weeping. And just then, hearing her cry, a golden seahorse popped up. "Hey you, I am Savea. Why are you crying?", she said in a sweet voice. Shivani looked up and gasped, "A talking seahorse?!. How can you speak?" she asked. "Yes girl, I am a magical creature! I have flying powers and I can also speak to any living being in their language. I save my aquatic friends from the sea garbage people like you dump in seas and oceans", Savea said. "We!, Shivani asked. "Yes, let me show you", it said. Thanks, Savea! Thanks, Savea! She took her deep into the sea singing her melodious song. The song starts.... "Down in the waters, I live helping animals like fish I give them gift of clean water filling them with joy and bliss. This gives me powers for the things I do Help to keep water clean from the dirt you all do. We don't like to fight, we like you all a lot Please stop making our home dirty, and the problem will be sort. Because we are true friends, that's what we thought" "Wow, I didn't know this hurts you so much Savea! I better tell my friends about it. We do not realise the harm we all cause by throwing away garbage in water. I am extremely sorry for this behaviour", said Shivani tearfully. "Well then, what are we waiting for? Let's go tell your friends!", Savea said happily. She unfurled her wings and flew into the sky and onto shore! As Shivani's friends and her teacher looked up into the sky, they gasped. Shivani was in the air and what was she riding on? A shark, monster sea creature. Shivani landed. She got off Savea. The teacher asked tearfully about where she had been. She smiled and told about her story that how Savea saved her and opened her eyes. She said "Dear all, we should not be selfish. We make oceans dirty for our convenience without caring about sea animals. We all forget that, they are important for ourselves and our ecosystem. So let's all pledge to pollute water." Everyone was astounded and ashamed by their behaviour. They quickly starting picking up all the garbage from the beach. Just then, Savea transformed into a goddess!" Oh my goodness, what is this? exclaimed Shivani with an open mouth. "Shivani, you are a kind soul and that's why I chose to save you and wanted you to learn the importance of clean oceans. Also, I knew you would spread this to others", said the goddess. From then on, Shivani continued her campaign for clean environment.
author: Navya Kiran
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Jemma Jose; Jessica  Bosworth-Smith; Jupiter  Pradhan; Lê Thị  Bích Khoa; Mamun Hossain; Muniza Shariq; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: The Last Flea
text: The girl crouched in the shadow of a building, her dog, Flea, at her side. The earth trembled as three search copters roared overhead, blades cutting the air with dreadful thwacks. The girl buried her face in Flea’s black fur and shivered. It smelled musty like dirt and mildew and dried pine, yet it comforted her, and her nausea passed. The copters rumbled into the distance and faded away. The girl and Flea were safe for now, but the copters would be back. They always came back. “Let’s go,” the girl told Flea. He tilted his head and scratched vigorously behind his ear. She tugged at his collar and they sprinted across the clearing of the village square back into the bordering forest. It was the safest place to be because it offered the most cover, but it was also the worst because it was cold, dark and wet, and there was no food. Which is why they had to venture into town to steal scraps. She had tried to get the dog to wait for her in the safety of the forest while she infiltrated the village, but he was loyal to a fault. He wouldn’t leave her side. At first, it was hard to avoid the people in the village, any of whom would turn them in without hesitation. But the population had dwindled since the virus hit. There was less danger of being caught now, but less food too. That night, as they lay beneath a copse of trees, the girl thought about how the night used to be alive with the sound of barking and howling dogs. Sometimes it got annoying, but she would have given anything to hear that cacophony again. “Are you sad?” she asked Flea. “Being the last one left?” The dog let out a heavy sigh and laid his square head on his enormous paws. “They won’t get you,” the girl said firmly, scratching him behind the ears. “I promise.” The dog arched his neck against her hand, begging to be scratched harder. She shuddered, feeling ill, but tried to ignore it. That night the copters returned, their white searchlights piercing through the trees like knives. The girl sat very still and prayed Flea would do the same, as the leaves trembled around them from the force of the copters’ blades, shaking startled birds awake. “We know you’re down there,” a voice barked through a loudspeaker. “Give him up now!” The dog curled his lip and growled. “Shhhh,” the girl hissed, clamping her small hand over the dog’s muzzle. Under her touch, the dog turned placid and rolled pleading brown eyes toward her. Suddenly, there was the sound of crashing brush. Several armed men in hazmat suits leapt into view. The girl wailed and wrapped her thin arms around Flea who snarled menacingly as the men pointed guns at them. “Release him or get shot!” one warned her. “You can’t have him!” She screamed. She could feel her blood’s temperature rise as a change began to overtake her. She trembled as her nails sharpened into points. “Shit! She’s got the virus!” One of them cried. “Of course she’s got it! The dog is a carrier for the last infected flea, idiot.” “But it’s mutated!” The girl had turned into something else. Red rage clouded her eyes. The men fired, but she was faster. Bodies littered the ground, slick with blood. “We’re going to need a new hiding place,” the girl told Flea. Panting, he scratched behind his ear.
author: Jaya Sri

title: Haunted School
text: I was around 8 or 9 at that time, when this adventure of mine began. At that time, I really did not understand what went on in this head of mine. It's the kids around the age of 8 and 9 that I do not understand, for they seem to be lost in a world completely of their own. Still, I consider that time to be the golden era of my mishaps and adventures. My parents always told me that I was spending too much time on the mobile and the television and they still tell me this, they always compare my childhood and theirs. I would always be annoyed that my parents kept singing songs of their past. But it was true that the tales they would tell and the experiences they would share were much more intricate and interesting than the one's I would have to offer. So, I eventually got jealous and was determined to go make some memories of my own so I could keep bugging my kids in the future. After all the tradition must be kept alive! So I met few of my friends and we started searching for what adventures to go on. We held a meeting in the clubhouse lawn and one of us said that we should investigate the abandoned school behind our society. Despite of staying quite a few years in the society none of us had ever heard about it. But when we were led to the school, while the rest were struck with fear and overwhelmed with the mystery of the place, I suddenly realized...... I have seen this place before, yes! it's the same old building I see from my friend's balcony. So, I decided to inform the rest of the group about what I knew related to the place and now that I look back at it, exaggerate every single word. So, it was decided to keep this a secret. Before I knew it, a plan of action was decided, half of us including me would go around the society gathering information while the others would prepare equipment for us, and we would meet up again next week ready to conquer this school. Well, I for one did not do my job seriously, half the week I sat at home watching cartoons and the other half was spent roaming around aimlessly in the society But when we did meet up again on Monday my friends were telling me the craziest of stories, the ghost of a headless lady or the giant 3 dog who was the king of all dogs and lived here with his army. I just sat on the bench of the lawn agreeing to all what they told me and then I looked at the stuff they brought, there was a cardboard box with chips and soda cans, and someone got a plastic sword and a two toy guns to kill the ghosts with while another got a homemade medical kit. I was very sure that her grandma needed those.... I looked at my friends in disappointment, while they seemed rather proud of their work, I told them we should get moving and once we reached the entrance of the school the iron gates were wide open. I thought we should head back since someone was already there, but the leader of our group claimed the ghost opened the gates as a way to show that they accept our challenge, so we continued. As we moved on, a chill ran through my spine despite the fact that it was broad daylight I was scared. The cool wind blew and the school building, which was only half complete with its iron framework sticking out and the bricks not plastered. By now we were halfway into the school ground and those eyes which were once watching us started to materialize in the form of stray dogs and monkeys. I noticed that the gaze had shifted from all of to just one person, the fat kid holding the cardboard box full of snacks and goodies. As the fat kid lacked behind the dogs came to surround him from the front and the monkeys providing support from the trees. When they came to close for comfort I ran off to a safe distance, while our brave heroes with the plastic sword and toy guns went to break the enemy siege of our supplies. As soon as our forces came into combat range and the fat kid finally got a glimmer of hope. One crucial question was asked "Bro we have the guns but... where's the ammo" and our brave commander replied, " I forgot the ammo!". The two gunners freed themselves of their duty and ran off. The leader was now alone and had to protect our supplies and our comrade. He swung the sword so hard it flew right out of his hand and landed near a tree where the monkeys where sitting. Finally, having lost hope the fat kid threw the box of snacks as far as he could and ran away. The rest of us quickly followed. Once we ran back into the s afety of our clubhouse, the mood was grim, and we had suffered enormous losses. Our commander was sad that we could not be an effective fighter or rather he was scared what would happen to him when he told his mother the major general that he had lost all the weaponry. However, our leader was quite optimistic and did not let us admit our defeat. He said that the same plan as last time would be followed. This time for me there was one change. I was in charge of handling the supplies and logistics. So, I started by giving my friends a few bright ideas. The leader had decided that our next mission was to be conducted at night. Two weeks passed and the day of the operation came. In the evening the doorbell rang and to my surprise it was my friends. We gathered in the same old lawn and the leader made us go through the plan. It took quite some time to get ready and make a battle formation. This time it was completely dark and the route to the abandoned school was dimly lit not only that but there had been jaguar sightings in the jungle surrounding the school. As we came near to the gates, we pulled out our weapons, our leader had a wooden stick, someone had a bag of stones and the others had household utensils like a pan and a bowl. I carried my toy nerf gun as a symbolic weapon. As soon as we entered the school grounds a blue light suddenly lit up in one of the top windows. Seeing this one of our members got scared and ran back, while another pulled out a picture of hanumanji and nervously started muttering something. As we moved forward, our visibility started to decline so the leader pulled out a flashlight in order to help us see better. But rather than helping us it made us even more scared. My hands shook uncontrollably out of fear. I looked up and saw that another light source lit up in the building with a shady figure looking at us from the window. Fear coursed through our veins. When we came near the building a large and fierce howl echoed in the building breaking the silence. We were all startled, one of us said" It's the king of the dogs he will eat us all!". The leader told him to calm down. My finger which was on the trigger of my gun slipped and I accidentally fired a bullet. Swoosh, it went and was lost in the sea of darkness. I knew I had to get it back. So, everyone spent the next ten minutes searching for my bullet. Once we found it, we came to the front of the school building we took our first step in and then Bam! a brick fell right in front of us. Before we could go any further, the army of dogs in the building was now aware of our presence and was barking at us. We all braced for a fight and just then a shady figure came in sight and the barks stopped. This was enough to break my resolve and I screamed in fear " RUN FOR YOUR LIVES!". All of us started to run and the shady figure chased us. We all ran as fast as our little legs could take us. After this second incursion it was decided that some places are best left unconquered. Though I had kept quiet about this incident my friends caused a huge panic and their parents did some investigation of their own. As for the shady figure that chased us, it was actually an old woman who kept feeding the stray dogs of our society. So, the dogs started to stay there.
author: Kartikey Pundir

title: Turn the Tables
text: Meet the Characters 1. Thomas Henry: A 67-year-old man who owns a major company. Despite having many luxuries, his life lacks joy. 2. Deepta: A small bundle of joy who immigrated from India. She lives in Thomas' care, usually spending time with him by learning new things about the world that she must face. 3. Mrs. Patel: Deepta's social worker, who tends to her every basic need. She might seem to have a stone-hard shell, but within that hard exterior is a heart of solid gold. She sat next to me, the young girl who asked me so many questions. "No, Deepta, you can't reach Neptune yet. You can try to when you're older." I told her when she said she wanted to see the brilliant blue land. She ecstatically nodded and ran off to her room, giggling. Her curiosity amused me and yet managed to create a spark within my brain as well. She was always bright and when I wasn't around to show her the many wonders of the world, she would seek company in the welcoming arms of a book. It was normal for me to come home to her elfish figure huddled in my large armchair behind the pages of an encyclopedia, surrounded on all sides by stacks of books bigger than herself. Her large, marble-like eyes glittered from reflecting the warm hearth of the fireplace she was cooped up next to. When she wasn't reading by the fireplace, she would be stargazing through the telescope in my study, eagerly looking out the window, with maps of the night sky and its many constellations and star clusters laid out before her. She was such an energetic little girl, that I find it quite a shame that she had no parents who would experience the positivity that she spread to those around her. I discovered that little elf of joy observing a bee in my garden. I took her into my care, but never as her official parent. I am going into my stages of old age, and though my roots are steady, my leaves have begun withering away. So I hired a social worker for her, Mrs. Patel (she calls her Pat for short, the cheeky little imp), in case she requires a new parent. Mrs. Patel calls me up quite often, usually to complain about Deepta playing a silly little prank on her. The most recent one was while I was at work when she yelled at me through the telephone that Deepta had slipped tadpoles from the garden pond into her filing cabinet. Although I found the prank quite hilarious, I acknowledged the fact that it was a wrongdoing and gave Deepta a little pep talk about pranking limits. Having been brought up to be a fine young lady, she obediently listened, her glassy eyes staring at me, and agreed to behave. One day, Randall from work, "Mr. CEO, stocks have been declining! Our income rates have declined by about 30 percent!" I was devastated and gave him orders, hoping to revive our financial stability. I wished to not only pay my workers their promised salaries, but to provide for the said angel that was in my care till the end of my days, and die a man at peace and in harmony. Deepta's future is something that I have grown to think of greatly and care about. Showcasing her brilliance cannot be restricted by poverty. The next week, Mrs. Patel came to meet me while Deepta and I were going through my insect collection. She grimly said, "Mr. Henry, could I please speak with you in private?" I accepted and left Deepta with a warning about the fragility of the insects she was handling. Inside my study, Mrs. Patel began fiddling with her pen, which clearly wasn't a good sign as for her, it was a symptom of worry. She handed me a folder of important-looking documents, which I opened to find Deepta's medical report. She only said, "Check her diagnosis." My knuckles went white and with shaking hands, I turned to the page, only to have my heart shattered. There, in the doctor's stereotypical almost unintelligible handwriting, it was scrawled 'Potential bronchogenic carcinoma'. Lung cancer. NO!... I knew that there was always the chance it was false, so I remained calm and quietly stepped out of the study. Deepta looked at me questionably and I asked her, "Want to go see your own skeleton?" She remained brave while the scanning took place. Once we were asked to wait outside, she came out frolicking and sat next to me, still swinging her legs. I was frantically waiting, and my heart skipped a beat when they called us. The staff member showed me the X-ray and there it was: a cloudy area covering most of her left lung. I held back the tears and took Deepta home. I bitterly tightened my grip on the packet containing the life-changing X-ray, along with all my hopes of a happy life to come. I gave her the news gently, so as to not knock her out immediately. She took it understandably and replied with a mere, "I'll be okay, Uncle Thomas." I sure hoped she was right. A few months into chemotherapy and plenty of drugs, the girl that I had met who changed my perspective of life was now quite a different sight. I could no longer stargaze with her at night, instead I could only read to her before bed, letting her laboured breath deepen through the cannula until she finally drifted off to sleep, where this harsh reality wouldn't harm her. Mrs. Patel called me once again and gave me a cherry on top of my heap of sorrow: I was too financially depleted for Deepta's medical bills to be fulfilled. My little girl was to have a new home, new parents who, despite all the love they would shower upon her, would never truly understand her like I did. She would once again endure the feeling of being a stranger. On the day she was to meet her new parents, she made a labourious effort to put a smile on her face, which looked like it hadn't slept in years. A limousine pulled up and out stepped a woman who was the spitting image of Marilyn Monroe. She was quite gentle with Deepta and had a heart of gold. I hoped that this was true affection for the child, for I wouldn't see Deepta again to console her. I had imagined that at my wrinkling age, I would be the one leaving her. But I realise that Fate has a lot in store for every person and does the unexpected, for she is the one leaving me, hopefully for a better life. Oh, how the tables have turned.
author: DIYA MEHNAZ J

title: The Time Traveller
text: The sun was shining through the leaves of the tree. A boy was roaming around in the woods according to his usual schedule. He used to venture new lands of the forest every evening. It was a sunny evening and the boy was enjoying his lone walk. Suddenly, a chirp from a bird broke his attention from the path. He was always fascinated by beautiful birds. Without a second thought, he decided to follow the bird around. Little did he notice, the scenery around him was changing. The sun was setting near the horizon and it started to get dark. This caught the boy’s attention and he stopped in his tracks. He had ventured beyond his knowledge. He shifted his sight to see a boy with identical looks to himself, although he was much younger. “Are you lost little boy?”, asked the older. “No, I am not lost but lonely”, said the little boy with gloomy eyes. “Oh, dear boy! You must know that you are never alone for there always will be someone to accompany you. You must never lose hope.” The trip was cut short when he remembered he had to be home for supper. On his way back, he thought of the boy’s face as he had seen that face somewhere before. Little did he know, he talked to his younger self in the woods. For in the woods he wandered, there was magic.
author: Anushree
illustrator: Barkha Lohia; Gerhard Van Wyk; Linh Chi; Nyambura Kariuki

title: Reverse The Clock
text: It is surprising how much life can take away from you and not feel guilty. I lost my best friend. My support. My comfort. I lower my head to my desk. Tears start pouring out of my eyes. I shouldn’t be crying. Emma wouldn’t want that. She would want me to stay happy. Live life to the fullest. Be grateful for the memories and time I spent with her. Yet, I wasn’t over her death. How could I be? She was a great part of my life. Eliza pats my head. She also lost Emma. We all were awesome friends, who had been through so much together. We had plans. Splendid plans for both the present and future. Yet, all of them were crushed the moment Emma died. The worst part, no one had informed us. While Emma had faced a severe car accident and had to be taken to the hospital. Both of us were laughing, waiting for Emma. We didn’t even get to say goodbye. We both were basically enjoying while she was dying. I look at Eliza. She smiles at me. I stare at her, confused. I know that smile. She always smiles like that when she has a plan up her sleeve. “Excuse me, ma’am. Can we please be excused for a moment?” Eliza confidently asks. The teacher gives us pitying looks and nods her head. Since Emma’s death, the teachers have allowed us a free pass for any time we need. Whether it be in the middle of an important class, or even an inspection. They allow us anything. Eliza grabs my hand and leads us out of the class. She drags me to the school garden, right where us three would hang out. All the memories came flooding back in. All the times we would share a laugh, a cry, or even a moment or weirdness. Nothing was unusual with us three. I stared at the grass. It was cruel to know that none of that will ever be back. I stare at Eliza. She sits on the grass and opens a Ouija board. I sit next to her, trying to figure out what she is trying to do. “It’s easy. We call Emma with this board. Since she is a spirit and recently died, she will easily come to us.” Eliza speaks, with a slight happiness in her voice. I stare at her even more confused. Her family believes in ghosts and spirits. They have a high opinion in them and would do anything to see them. Yet, I never imagined Eliza being a fond of it too. Although, both of would do anything to see Emma again. As much as Eliza believed in ghosts, it never convinced me. Yet, in this moment, I was willing to try anything. Anything to get my friend group back together. “Let’s do this!” I spoke with enthusiasm. We placed our hands on the plank. Eliza didn’t hesitate and asked the first question. “Spirits beyond this world, can you hear us right now?” We looked at each other, hoping for some time of response. After some seconds, the words “yes” started to fade into the board. We squealed with joy. This could actually work! “Spirts beyond this world, we would like to summon Emma.” We waited, hoping a message would appear. After several minutes, a strange message appeared. “The key to recreating the past, is for you to accept your own.” We stared at it blankly. What did it even mean? What did it have to do with Emma? A flashing light appeared from the board, nearly blinding us. The light slowly vanished. We opened our eyes, unable to process what was in front of us. “Emma” we spoke in unison. There she was, smiling at us. She looked the same, as if the car accident hadn’t happened at all. Like her death didn’t eat us alive. She ran up to us, opening her arms wide. We hugged her. Tears poured out of my eyes. I wish we would have brought her back earlier. I wish she never died in the first place. However, none of this matter, she was back! Suddenly, another flashing light appeared. Ghosts started spiralling out of the Ouija board. We stared at it in horror. Consequences. We hadn’t thought about it. We hadn’t even expected it. We casually assumed Emma was going to come alone. I stared at the ghosts. They had burnt faces, dark eyes and an evil smile plastered on their faces. My eyes widened. Ghosts were entering our school like they owned it. There was nothing stopping them from destroying it completely. Realisation hit me. I leapt towards the board, closing it tightly. The flashing light stops. Stopping any other ghost from entering into our world. I sighed in relief. “Rosie. Rosie! Look up!” I looked above me. Ghosts were carrying many students, laughing and mocking them for being weak. They were torturing the students, dropping them from high levels, scaring them, playing tricks with their minds. Young children were getting destroyed, they were crying out loud, yet, there was no one brave enough to help them. Moreover, this was all our fault. We had suffered the consequences to bring Emma back. We let these ghosts traumatize innocent children that had no partake in Emma’s death. We had to do something. I picked up the board and swung it at a ghost. It looked back at me, its dark eyes staring into my soul, wondering if I was foolish enough to try and kill a ghost. It turned its hard upside down. Its smile widened, covering most of its face, and started laughing into my face. I backed away. The ghost followed me, walking with its dark, skinny legs. Its eyes started to change colours, as if it figured out, I was weak enough to be scared. Someone pulled me. I looked around. Darkness. “Hey, Rosie. You are okay.” Someone spokes. “It is me. Eliza.” She turns me around. I instantly hug her. “What are we going to do?” I whisper. “I figured it out.” Eliza spoke. “You remember the riddle that popped up before Emma came. ‘The key to recreating the past, is for you to accept your own’. We need to accept Emma’s death.” I gasped. My face started to redden. I didn’t want to deal with this again. I couldn’t live with these ghosts, however, life without Emma seemed impossible. As if someone drains the life out of me. It was heartbreaking to even think of it. How did Eliza even expect me to do it? I want to accept her death, yet, there isn’t a path made for me to do that. I was supposed to spend my whole life with Emma and Eliza. Losing one of them is terrible. It messes up my whole life. I stare at Eliza. She looked down. It was obvious she wasn’t happy with the plan either. However, Eliza always put everyone before her. She wasn’t going to let anyone get in between her morals. I hugged her. None of us wanted to lose Emma. Yet, we were given no choice. Emma appeared in front of us. We ran up to her and hugged her. All of us knew what had to be done. What the right thing was. However, the thought of it still ate me from the inside. We walked over to the Ouija. Not fearing if any ghost comes near us. After facing the hard truth ghost didn’t seem scary. They felt like soulless creatures who wont ever experience true pain. I gently open the Ouija board, hoping every other ghost would go away, but emma wont. Obviously, this fantasy didn’t come true. Emma started to walk towards the flashing light. She look behind at us, blessing us with her smile one last time. We smiled back at her. I finally got to say goodbye. I should be happy. Emma walked into the flashing light, disappearing into it. Soon enough, all the ghosts were sucked into it. A smile stretched across my face. I was glad to see those heartless creatures go. 3 Years Later We got over Emma’s death and chose a different path in life. A path
author: Sehaj Kaur
