title: An Unbreakable Bond
text: Long Long ago there lived two sibling named Kang-Sujin and Kang-Suho. their bond was so strong that it was unbreakable. Want to know why? Well, let's find out! Kang-Sujin was a gentle girl. She had the eyes of the colour of hazel which would shine brightly in the sun. Her hair was as brown as chocolate, which she would always tie up in a bun. She wore a blue kimono with a floral design on it. She was kind-hearted and very pretty according to the people of her neighbourhood. She was the younger sibling. On the other hand, Kang-Suho was cold and short-tempered. He had dark ruby eyes which always looked like as if he was angry. His hair was chestnut brown with some streaks of rusty red hair. He wore a black checkered kimono. He was always jealous of his younger sister because of how kind and pretty she was. One day, they were having a walk around their neighbourhood when suddenly, a group of people started to gather around Kang-Sujin. Everyone was giving her compliments of how pretty and kind she was and showering her with blessing. Hearing all this, Kang-Suho got jealous and furious. He immediatally held his sister's hand and rushed home. When they reached, they broke into a huge fight which just kept on going on and never stopped. This continued for days and days, which resulted in creating a huge wall between their love. One day after a fight, Kang-Suho decided to have a nap as he was very tired. While he was resting, Kang-Sujin was crouching in the corner thing about how much she hated her brother, as some tears of anger rolled down her cheeks. After a while, some robbers had broke into their house. The siblings had no clue about it. One of the robbers saw a gold necklace with an emerald shaped like a heart attached on Kang-Sujin's neck. Kang-Suho had gifted this necklace to her long back to show his love to her. The robber told the others about it. They decided on stealing it. Without thinking, the robbers snatched the necklace off of her neck. Kang-Sujin felt it and let out a big shout. This made Kang-Suho wake up. By the time he woke up, Kang-Sujin was chasing the robbers. On seeing this, He got up and ran after the robbers too. Kang-Suho caught up with her sister and asked her what they had stolen. Crying, she replied that they had stolen the necklace which he had given her when they were young. This made him tear up and angrier than ever. He took his sister's hand and sprinted as fast as they ever could. Eventually, the robbers had stopped near a pond. The sibling were tired and out of breath. They quietly went to the pond and cupped some water in their hands. They drank it as if they had not tasted it in years. After drinking it, they hid behind a big tree and peeped to see the robbers. One of them was chanting something when suddenly, the ground started rumbling and a big enterance opened, which led down to a cave. Right after they went in, the siblings sneaked in without them noticing. Inside the cave, they saw lots of gold coins and jewlery. The robbers went straight ahead, leading them to a bamboo door. The siblings followed them and hid behing a huge rock. Instead of opening the door, the robbers hit it three times. A small wooden box came out of an opening in the wall. They kept the necklace in it and pushed the box back in again. They then left the cave, forgeting to close the enterance. Making sure no one was there, Kang-suho came out and imitated what the robbers had done. He stole the necklace back and informed Kang-Sujin about it. They both ran towards the enterance and escaped the cave. Luckily, none of the robbers saw them. Both the siblings were delighted and happy. They safely returned back home and hugged each other as tight as they could. They cried and apologized to each other and told how sorry they were and how much they loved each other. Kang-sujin put on the necklace back again and held it tightly. The wall which was made between their love was broken and they grew so close to each other that their bond was unbreakable and they lived happily ever after. The End Fighting with your siblings can create a big wall between each other which will make us find ways to prevent each other. It will be better off without that wall between each other as it will remove all the hate and anger between each other So, its better not to fight with your siblings! Always be positive and happy:D
author: Ada Hussain

title: Leo and the leopard cub
text: It was a dry, sunny summer. In a local village near Shimla lived a boy named Leo. Leo was a 9 years old. He liked to help people especially his dad whose name was Anderson. He helped Mr. Anderson by taking the water out from the well everyday in the evening. One day it was so hot that the water in the well had dried up. Leo ran to his dad and said, "Dad, all the water in the well has dried up." His dad told him that the water had dried up because of the sun. It was so hot that even the crops had died. The village was in serious trouble. They had neither crops nor water. Leo, in sadness took off to a nearby forest. There he kept thinking," What to do?" Then suddenly as he was walking he heard a growl. Leo took off to find the sound. He ran and ran until he saw a leopard cub. It was adorable. It was so small and full of black spots. Leo could tell by the looking at the leopard cub that it was thirsty and hungry. Leo could not see its mom anywhere and that's why he took the cub in his arms and ran back to the village. He sprinted to his dad and told him," Dad, I found a leopard cub in the forest. It is really thirsty and hungry." His dad replied," Leo! What are you doing with a leopard cub? You could get arrested for this." Leo got scared. His dad told him that he was going to call the forest officer. Leo looked at the cub, seeing how thirsty and hungry he was. Suddenly a sound came, "CRACKEBOOM!" Leo looked up and saw rain. He was so happy and said to the leopard cub," Don't you worry. You are gonna be okay." Meanwhile his dad called the forest officer and told her about the leopard cub. The forest officer told him that he was going to be there asap. Mr. Anderson ran to Leo as fast as a lightning bolt when he saw rain. He was so glad because of the rain, the crops would grow back and the well would be filled up with water. After a couple of minutes the rain stopped. There was water everywhere. A pond had been made by the rain. The leopard cub dashed out of Leo's hands and happily drank water. After a few minutes the forest officer arrived. He said," Hello everyone. My name is Jake. I am here to pick up the leopard cub. I am gonna feed it and then take him. When suddenly a massive roar came out from the bushes. A leopard jumped out from there. "It must be his mom." said Jake. The leopard cub dashed to his mom. Leo was happy for the leopard cub but sad for himself. He went to the cub and said," Well, I guess this is goodbye. I hope you have a nice life. I am gonna name you Leo jr." "I think it's time for him to go now said his dad." Goodbye, Leo jr. I will dearly miss you." said Leo. Then the cub went to his mom and they went in the forest. Leo cried. His dad said," It is okay. If you need me I'll be here." After a few years in that village while Leo was working he saw something in the bushes. Then leaped a leopard out of there and started licking Leo. It was Leo jr. Leo was so happy. Then came out three leopard cubs. They were Leo jr's cubs. Their names were Bite, Sharp and Spot. Leo showed him his children whose names were Emelda, Jack and Max. Suddenly all the kids ran to each other. All of them liked each other. Then Leo jr. called his cubs and they went into the forest. They happily lived ever after.
author: Shaurya Gupta

title: A Carriage Ride to the West
text: Every morning he left for school only after touching her feet. “Bless me Dadi.” “Let the almighty give you all that you desire and more.” And off he ran away to the cold plains of Shimla. He knew these frosted plains like the back of his hand. Green grasslands flushed under the colossal mountain ranges. A valley formed around urban lands. Now, at present, it was covered with white crystal snow with the weather so cold it turned your ears pink. Cottages were constructed close to each other to preserve heat. A road crisscrossed through the snowy plains. Cars rushed onto the road. People saw a slight boy of seven walking to the nearest school four Kilometres away. He jumped onto the sidewalk and started skipping about. He stopped to admire the children skiing along the snowy flatlands. “Rich brats”,Satpal said “ They love showing off,” Lakhan replied. “Aren't we getting late?” “I guess.” And off they ran, reaching school just in the nick of time. Their school was a huge building distempered in turquoise. It did not have a proper roof which often caused the canopy to leak. After the morning assembly, they had mathematics. As they entered the class, the sky changed into a hoary black canvas. Their Maths teacher was a short, round man with very little neck. He had a mean face with wispy hair and was always seen with his trusted cane. He could quieten the class with his mere presence. “Did you all finish your homework?” he asked assertively. Homework? Oh no! Lakhan had completely forgotten about it. He had spent the whole day playing cricket with Satpal. Five strokes later he was asked to stand outside the class for the first two periods. There was a break after the first period. Students from all the classes came out to either use the washroom or to meet their friends. Ranbir, a fat-good-for-nothing boy of twelve years was having a very bad day. He had gotten detention from his English teacher for not finishing his homework assignment and so he decided to make someone's day horrible. He started looking for Lakhan who was an easy prey for his antics. “Oye Lakhan, getting punished already?” “Stop it, Ranbir bhaiya.” “You are just like your father, a complete loser.” Lakhan hated it when people talked about his father. He hadn't seen his father since his mother's death two years ago. Lakhan started crying. Seeing this, Ranbir ran away. He didn't want to get into any more trouble. As Lakhan stood sobbing, there was an announcement in the school. A monotonous voice was heard. “Attention to all students and teachers. A huge storm is expected to hit within the next hour. You are asked to leave home. The same applies to the teachers.”Huge cheers were heard throughout the school. Lakhan was ecstatic. Shouts of “Free holiday” were heard throughout the campus, as teachers tried to contain the crowds of students justling towards the door. From the glass windows, Lakhan and Satpal were seen hopping about with no fear of the upcoming storm. The entire sky had turned stygian. There was a cold, pleasant breeze blowing about, trying to scatter the clouds. The friends were dancing and singing all the way that they almost missed a wounded rabbit lying on the road. Its eyes were watery and it had a deep cut along its forelegs. Blood was oozing out, dampening the snow around it. It almost camouflaged with the surrounding snow. “We have to save it Lakhan,”Satpal said “It won't survive” Looking defeated, the rabbit let out a final snort. Satpal bent down and touched the rabbit. It lay there lifeless.Tears came down Satpal’s eyes for he had lost his pet dog Toto, just three days back. Lakhan looked down expressionless. Teary-eyed Satpal dug out a hole, pushed the rabbit inside and covered it up with snow. Just then a tall man cycling came up to them. He had a pale face, blue eyes and a hooked nose, just like Satpal. “Namaste uncle,” Lakhan said “Namaste beta. What happened, Satpal? Come here.” Satpal ran towards his father and hugged him tightly. “What happened beta?” “ Uncle, when we came …..” As Lakhan narrated Satpals cries came down. “Don't cry beta. Just like Toto, the rabbit is taking a carriage ride to the west.” Hearing this Lakhan stood there stunned. His legs felt weak. He wanted to cry but the tears wouldn't flow. “Don't play outside Lakhan, the storm is approaching and convey my respects to Dadi.” Lakhan started running. He ran and ran and just didn't want to stop. Memories flashed before his eyes. A short man with a thin face and large eyes was shouting. “What have you given me? You gave everything to that wretched daughter of yours. She ran away with that cunning broker, disowning you. I need money to take care of him.”He pointed towards Lakhan. “Everybody calls me a loser. I feel ashamed to show my face in public. Savitri would have understood me. You know what, I don't want to live with you.” He pointed towards an old man with a skeleton face and a large broken nose, his Dada. “You can take care of Lakhan.” And off he walked away into the abyss. From the corner of his eye, Lakhan could see Dadi standing in the corner crying. He hadn't seen his papa since that day. The next morning there was a huge bang on the door. Satpal’s dad came rushing inside. He showed Dada the newspaper. As Dada was reading he collapsed in his chair. “Baba, have you taken everything,” Dadi asked “Yes, Dadi” “Don't stay up late. Remember to brush your teeth and don't trouble Mausi.” “Yes, Dadi.” Hot tears came out of Dadi’s eyes. “Come, say bye to Dada.” She took Lakhan inside the house. Dada was sleeping on a mattress. He appeared frail. His pillow looked wet. “Bye, Dada.” There was no reply. “He is asleep,” Dadi said. Mausi came inside. She was a fat woman with heavy make-up wearing a pink lehenga. “The taxi is waiting. I have to pay for it.” Dadi choked, “I am helpless. That is why I called you. Take care of Lakhan” “Nobody cared for me when I stood helpless. Anyway, take care of your husband. Send me a telegram when all of this is over ”, Mausi said bitterly. “Remember, we gave you everything we had,”Dadi lamented. “Really?" As Mausi replied with spitefulness, Lakhan found the newspaper near Dada’s mattress. He was about to open the newspaper when he found himself in the air. Mausi lifted Lakhan and carried him out of the house. As their taxi took a turn, Lakhan saw a police van speeding past them. The front cover of the newspaper lying near Dada’s mattress read-The body of a 34- year- old found near the banks of Giri. Police identify him as a resident of the Dahanu village. Lakhan came back home after spending two months with Mausi in Rajasthan. He had missed Dada and Dadi. He missed Dadi's stories. He missed Dada carrying him on his shoulders. He missed playing with Satpal. Mausi dropped him outside the house with his luggage and sped off in the taxi. Dada was a retired headmaster in the state government school. He always had his former students come and seek his blessings for future endeavours. But now, the house looked quiet and empty. Dadi came out running and hugged Lakhan. She carried him inside and asked him how his trip to Rajasthan had been. “Where is Dada?” Lakhan asked Dadi turned downcast. Her eyes turned wet. “Dada is taking a carriage ride to the west, ”Dadi stuttered. “When will he come back?” Lakhan asked innocently. “He won't come back. When you grow old, we will go there.” Dadi looked strange. She was not her usual self. It looked as though all the happiness on her face was drained. She was wearing a very simple sari and not her usual bright salwar kameez. “I don't want to go to Rajasthan ever again,” he said “I will never send you away ever again,” Dadi replied. Lakhan was now sprinting. It had been two years since that incident took place. All this made sense now. He wanted to talk to Dadi. Lakhan took a sharp turn and came to a stop. He had reached home. Dadi was in the backyard tending the gooseberry trees. He ran to her. “Baba go inside. I think there will be a downpour.” Lakhan just stood there, speechless. “What happened Baba?” Lakhan stared blankly. He felt something heavy in his throat. “Tell me, What happened? ” She couldn't bear seeing tears in her grandson’s eyes. “Dadi, where is papa?” Dadi’s face turned pale. “He is with Dada.” Lakhan’s vision turned blurry. His breathing became fast. He caught Dadi’s arm. “Don't leave me Dadi. Don't take a carriage ride to the west.” Dadi had tears in her eyes. She hugged Lakhan. Lakhan couldn't stop himself. He burst out. Lightning flashed, and thunder shook the Earth. It started pouring …..
author: adithya v

title: Brave sister
text: It was the day when a man lived with his family. In his family there were 3 members, his mother, father and a sister. The name of a man was Lokesh. He did not have any work and he belongs to the poor family. Hsi dream was to become an I. A. S officer. But suddenly his mother died due to illness. T hen he decided to do part time job. Suddenly, he injured and lost his both legs. He went in depression, his sister who was very brave. She did the part time job and studied in very well mannered. Along with studying she takes care of her brother and do every works. When such a day comes that she became an I. A. S officer by her will power and determination. She did not loses her hope that what will she do now after losing everything. B ut she stands and fight with every difficult situation. Now, his brother also wins over his depression and started studying for fulfilling his dream of becoming an I. A. S officer. After few years he also cracked the UPSC exam and became an I. A. S officer. Now, both started living a happy life.
author: Bhavini Dwivedi

title: Interchanging roles with my mom
text: One evening while my mother was cooking dinner, we had a conversation about who's having more work to do, more pressure, and stuff. She was counting her work of management and lecturing etc. and I was counting mine of homework, studying etc. The conversation lasted till our dinner. Then we watched television and went to bed. That night when I and my mom were sleeping peacefully, then a sudden flash of light appeared from the window which woke me up, I was scared to respond so I decided not to react and act to be asleep, a couple of seconds later a voice came "I know you aren't sleeping, it's an order stand up" I continued my act. "Looks like you are not going to respond, here you go with malediction... I am leaving a note about it". I jumped quickly out of my bed to stop him but he disappeared within a fraction of second, I ran quickly to the paper to read it. There I saw "I am your guardian angel, I came here to clear your mom's point of view of being correct about having more work and pressure" but you didn't respond and pretended not to be wakened up by light, so I am giving you malediction of interchanging your works with your mom's for the rest of your life" But... (I whispered) Next morning "It's 5:30 already! Why didn't you wake me up?" shouted mom. "WHAT!? You're the one supposed to wake me up, why would I wake you?" I exclaimed. I was shocked to see her being depend on me. "You have to cook food and send me school, why aren't you awake already?" I didn't understand but still, I ordered food early morning and sent her school in rush as we were late. I was so tired. Then I remember that I have to leave the office at 8:00 a.m. soon as possible and started because I didn't know what I had to do but I started the car and went to her college there some random strangers students came and touch my feet and ask me if I new them I said yes and the ask if I remember their name. I was in dilemma as I didn't know their batch year name or anything else I was just standing there being numb then someone called me from behind and thankfully I was safe but no there she called me to give a lecture to students again I was in a fix and then I saw principle coming with the new professor for me to show him a demo. I ran out of the room being all frustrated, took the car and went straight to (mom's) my school. There I picked her up and and on the way back home she was talking about how boring her day was, she didn't knew what to do and her friends weren't present to help her and so on... I scolded her because I stressed out too, she was almost tearing up I didn't know how to respond. We reached home, she was still upset with me and I started sobbing too. Then our Guardian angel appeared once again and asked what happened. I told him everything. He smiled and replied "Today you aren't understanding what she (mom) is going through, she just told you had a bad day and there you were being all flustered from the work. Did you paid attention to her? Weren't you stressed out? Were you able to do all then work easily? Then you were saying to have more work than your mom? Listen, more or less we all have work to do, its all about how you handle and react to it. Now it looks like you have got your lesson. So I am taking my malediction back" I nodded and lived happily ever after.
author: Adviti Kumari

title: SALLY'S PARENTS
text: Everything was going as usual until the phone call. It was around 7 o'clock in the evening when my phone rang. I picked up the phone. There was a woman's voice. She wanted me to meet her the next day if I wanted further information. Perhaps before proceeding further, I should give you my introduction and a brief recount. I am Sally Johns. I lived in a mansion that I inherited from my father until there was a fire due to which the mansion burnt and nothing remained of it. I ran in order to save my life with only a backpack in my possession that my father had given me and made me promise to open it only after he died. At that time, I didn't take it seriously, but now, well, I still did not have the courage to open it. According to the police, this was not an accident and they are still investigating. But then, I had another problem to worry about. Where would I live? I had nowhere to go. I took refuge in my best friend, Jacqueline's house. So back to the present. I told Jackie (short form for Jacqueline) about my conversation with the woman and my decision to meet her. Her reaction was as I expected. She didn’t want me to go. At last, after much pleading, she agreed but insisted she’ll also go. When we reached our rendezvous spot, I spotted a woman standing under a streetlight. We approached her. Her face was covered and her eyes were strangely familiar. ‘I'm very glad that you have come,’ she said. I nodded. 'You might be wondering,' she said 'what information I had that I wanted to share with you.' I again nodded. 'I'm sure that you are aware of the formula that your father was working on when he died.' With much courage, I replied, 'No'. My father never shared his professional life with me. 'I see,' The woman replied, 'I suppose I should tell you from the beginning. Your father had been working on a formula for a very long time. But unfortunately, when he reached the completion of his lifelong hard work, he died. He must have realized that he might not live long enough so, he made arrangements.' 'First of all, who are you? And what do you mean by "made arrangements"?' I asked her. But she ignored my questions and continued. ‘The formula your father was working on is very important. Many scientists have worked on it but none of them reached as far as your father did. Some of your father’s professional enemies are trying to get the formula into their hands. What do you think, the burning of your mansion was just an accident? They will again try to get the formula into their hands. Do you want this to happen?' 'What do you want me to do?' I asked. 'You'll find a box in the backpack your father gave you. There's an address given. You must go to the address. The only copy of your father's work is on the computer of your father's office there. You must print that out. You'll find all the security keys of the computer in the box. After printing, submit it to the Government. The rest of the things will be taken care of by them. Your father will get the honour that he deserved.' The next morning, we set out early. On our way, I was thinking about the millions of unanswered questions that were muddling in my brain. The more I grew proud of my father, the more I was angry with him. He never ever gave me a hint about his project, yet that woman, who is a stranger, knew. She must be a stranger. Thinking about all these things, we finally reached our destination. By looking at the building, nobody could tell that such an important formula lay there. We went inside. My father's office was on the fourth floor. I opened the apartment and we went inside. There was a living room that was littered with files and a small kitchen. There was only one room which was my father's office. It had a computer in one corner and the rest of the space was covered with files and there was a big photo on one of the walls. In the photo, I was a newborn baby. There was my mother cradling me and her eyes twinkled. The same way as the woman’s did last night. I switched on the computer. After unlocking all the locks, I finally opened the file. Then I set the document to get printed. The formula started getting printed. When the woman said that I have to print a formula, I did not expect that to be 1024 pages. But in reality, it was. After all the pages of the formula got printed, we got out of the apartment.' A few friends of my father's helped me to submit the formula to the Government and after performing several big procedures, I could finally submit it. Within a month, my father's work was recognized. I was very happy that my father finally got th e honour he deserved. I wanted to thank the woman. But I wasn't sure whether it would be the right thing to do. Finally, I called her. I asked her to meet me at the same spot that evening where we'd met the first time. I saw her standing when I reached there. This time her face was not covered. She was smiling and her eyes had the same twinkle. And my suspicions were right. She was my mother. I had never seen my mother. My parents got divorced when I was one year old and since then my father took care of me. My mother was still standing there. Tears rolled down her cheeks. At last, after regaining her composure, she said, 'I'm sorry, Sally. I never could take care of you. But trust me, it hurt me more than anything else to be away from you.' 'Why were you away from me, then?' I asked. I tried to control my anger. All my life I waited for my mother. But she never came. 'I am sorry, Sally', she said. I had so many questions to ask her. But I just stood there processing everything. 'Well, Sally,' she said, 'I know I've been a terrible mother, but can we live together in my apartment? I would not force you. But if you want-' I know, I should have been angry with her. But when she asked me to stay with her, I lost my composure. I started crying and gave her a bear hug. Since then, my mother and I are living together in her apartment. I miss my father sometimes (which is most of the time). But I am not sad. He had completed his life's goal before he died and he must be living happily in heaven, proud of his success.
author: Kasturi Thakur

title: The Hidden Treasure
text: It was the time of recess, when I was playing football with my friends in the school playground. Suddenly the ball went to the ground of the building behind us. It was all alone there, me and my friend went to pick the ball. There came the sound of leaves moving and my leg fell into a pit. My friend helped me to get out from it. Suddenly my leg touched a box. I tried to lift that box. That box was very heavy. There were probably some valuables in it. There was dust on it. I cleaned the dust with a Clean cloth. A key was required to open that box. The key was buried under the soil. Me and my friend dug the soil. I was shocked because there were so many coins of gold. There was also a map. Finally I found a bundle containing some jewellery. We came back leaving all those things there.We were panicked. The first thing we did is to call our teacher. They informed the authorities about this. We call them because if it’s illegal, the authorities have a legal right to seize the treasure and keep it for themselves. Afterwards we were awarded for our honesty by our principal in the assembly. It was a memorable day for me.

title: Oh Well, Jess
text: , Illustrators: Abhinav Balachandar, Clyde Beech, Kalyani Naravane, Louwrisa Blaauw, Minu Nandakumar, Sarah Rose de Villiers, Smitha Shivaswamy, Sunaina Coelho, Swathi Sambasivam, iaman_ y Great, it’s morning again- a brand new day. I get off my bed, and rub my eyes, everything in a blur with a hint of black; I grab my toothbrush, brushing my teeth while still dizzy. I throw on my school uniform, and put some books into my bag, unaware of which books I put in, I shoot to my school. I won’t say it’s the best morning routine, but trust me- there is plenty more who do the same. Not trying to justify me though. After a couple of kilometers, you could very well spot the super formal colors of our school buildings. “School hasn’t been the best place for me since a couple of years back, around the end of middle school; I’m a high school sophomore now. The reason I didn’t enjoy school is not piling homework or keeping up with extracurricular. It is the anxiety that I have; all the people around you, and you have no idea what they might be thinking or people talking and talking and talking, that you can’t fathom your thoughts. Above all, you feel lost in everything. A continuous restlessness is working inside you.” I said. Melanie gasped, kind of in a concerned manner. “What! Why don't I know it already, am I that not approachable to you?” “No, it’s not that.” “Then what is it?” “I didn’t want to bother you.” “It’s the same thing Jess...” She only took my name when it was undoubtedly serious. She didn’t know any of it in all these years of our friendship. We are best friends. She was upset; I wouldn't have told her about it ever actually. But my condition is falling. I think I know where all her anger is coming from. It’s legitimate. “I need some time alone. I know you’re my best friend, and I shouldn’t probably say this. But, I can’t stay with you just now. I know nothing about you. You need to sort out your anxiety thing.” She said. I said, “It’s not easy, but I'll try. And I can.” “No you can’t”, her voice shook as she said it. “How do you say that a person is healthy?” I asked. She said that a healthy person will do well in their primary activities, which for me are school and hobbies, and then she added, “I don’t know, win trophies? I mean you loved music, but you stopped being how you were. It's like there's no 'You' left in you.” I took a deep breath, and said, “Okay.” She didn’t believe me by the way. She left. But I was determined to change myself, maybe not from the inside, but put out a show I guess. I started working harder day and night. My intervals of anxiety attack increased. But the show I must say was nice. Didn’t think I could do that. I am the school's Cultural Secretary now; people admire and envy me. Who knew that one hit could make me come so far in a such short time? I lost consciousness the other day. It was getting too much. I wasn't supported in my musical journey in the beginning. But that day when you asked why I stopped, it got me thinking deeply. I didn't have an answer to it. I, then let myself loose into music, but somewhere there was an unaccountable pressure. I promised that I will do it. Look at me, I did it. She isn't here to see, doesn't need to either. And maybe I should stop talking to the wall now as well, it's been quite long.
author: Sanchari Pore,

title: The reunion
text: Once there was this 10 year old young boy named Rishi. He belonged to a small town. His father worked as a coolie at railway station and he earned only 70 rupees per day which wasn't a sufficient amount to provide his son education. Rishi was a very smart and kind boy, he was not ashamed for being illiterate instead he happily helped his father at the station. Both father and son would buy 3 egg rolls for 20 rupees each everyday after work. Even though he never showed his willingness to study but his father could see it whenever he glared at the University students going to different cities by train everyday to study. The boy would also see gentlemen with briefcases going to their offices in a smart looking suit and finely polished shoes. He, with a small, confident smile would look at his father and say, " Pa! When I would become taller like you, I would also hold a suitcase in my hands and wear bright and polished shoes just like these men. You will be stunned and every dear woman wouldn't stop looking at me". His father would cherish at his words and proudly get back to his work. One day a young boy similar to the age of Rishi made it to the railway station. He was a strong and fit looking boy. Rishi saw that he was wearing a medal but still was crying. He couldn't resist himself from asking the boy that why he was crying even after winning a medal. The boy didn't respond and kept moving forward towards the railway track. It was almost time for the train of Panipat to arrive. Rishi said, "hey brother, please stop, it's almost time for the next train to arrive and it's dangerous for you to stand near the railway track. Come back!" but the boy didn't listen and stood at the edge right next to the railway track. A lady passing by came and accidentally stepped on the boy's foot and her bag hit him. It was a bad timing as the train also arrived. The boy was about to get crushed by the train but Rishi held his hand and saved him in time. Boy's parents also came after collecting the ticket unknown to the incident. The crowd gathered and people started talking to each other about what happened, his parents also became aware about this tragic incident. The cold blooded boy didn't even thank Rishi for saving his life. His father frowned at him and said, " Rhonny! you careless boy it's time to get on the train come on let's go". Rhonny stared at Rishi and did as he was told. Rishi didn't care that the boy was not thankful but he was happy that he saved a life. His father was also proud. His father got another job and earned enough money to provide his son education. He succeeded to get enough money to get him admitted in a new school. Rishi respected his father's efforts and studied hard to pay him back his hardwork. He graduated and became a well known business man. His family lived happily together in a large pukka house. Years passed and Rishi turned 35 that day. He decided to visit the same railway station where he and his father used to work. He reached there and found the station in the same condition just the way it was. His father with a great sigh said, " Oh dear, some things never change. You remember you used to say about being a powerful gentleman wearing a suit, well polished shoes and holding a suitcase. And here you are just as you wished. I'm proud of you son." All their memories came alive. His father went to buy those old egg rolls they used to eat after work while Rishi had a nice gaze around the station. He stood near the railway track and saw coolies carrying luggage, University students going to different cities to study, gentlemen going to their offices and young children working hard. He got lost with the thoughts of his past life and a strong blow of wind arrived. He fell on the track and came back to his senses. "Stand up and run!!", he heard. He looked behind and saw a train coming. A coolie dropped his luggage and lent him a hand. Rishi stood up, held his hand and came back to the surface just in time. He couldn't digest the past few minutes of his life and was still processing. The coolie asked, " Sir, are you alright?". " I don't know" replied Rishi. " I got so lost in my thoughts that I didn't realise I was so close to death. Thank you sir for saving my life". The coolie with a blank face, having tears in his eyes stood still. Rishi asked him what suddenly happened to him. He replied, "Once when I was young, I was in the same situation just as you were a while ago and a son of a coolie rescued me. He really saved my life and I didn't even thank him. I regretted that all this time and see my destiny brought me to the same post of work. I wish I could thank him before dying." Rishi was shocked listening his words. He first asked his name to confirm, "Rhonny" he replied. Rhonny's answer solved all his doubts and he gladly said," Hey Rhonny brother, no need to regret this anymore, it's great that you realise your wrong doing and think that you paid him back by saving my life today." Rishi's father came with the egg rolls and he left Rhonny with a cheerful goodbye. Both father son enjoyed their visit to the old workplace and went back home happily.

title: The Curse of The Dead
text: ﻿ Once there was a boy named Peter who studied in high school and was extremely fond of books. He was really good at studies and thus his 'History teacher' asked him to write a long and details assignment on the 'Greek mythology'. Peter was thrilled as he got a great opportunity to learn about Greek traditions and culture. The assignment was due today. Peter went to the library and started searching for some information, but he found none. The librarian also gave up. Frustrated, Peter by mistake, push a thick book and to his surprise there was a secret door leading to the basement of school. Peter was flabbergasted but also a bit afraid but, He was really anxious and really wanted to go in there Finally, Peter decided to step in the secret basement. He stepped his foot very carefully at every single step. The place was creepy, filled with spiders and grasshopper all around a place. Then suddenly, he heard series of footsteps cracking towards him. Peter got scared, but he gathered up courage, remembering the fact that there are no ghosts unless we believe in them. finally, he reached the bottom of the basement. He saw a torch lying nearby and took it in case he wants some light to see. At the basement, he saw an enormous and well-equipped library. Peter was excited as he finally got a place to find resources about his history assignment. But the library was so big that finding such a book was next to impossible. peter lost all his hopes and sat down on the chair near one of the bookshelves. But by chance, peter got attracted to that book instantly Suddenly he saw a brilliant flash of light. Peter followed it. Next, he saw a book glittering and shining just the way a diamond does. He read Its title name 'The Curse of the Dead' and in smaller letters it was written ' A true story regarding Greek Mythology.' Peter thought," Finally, I got an interesting book related to this topic. Now let's read it." He started reading the book that had intrigued his interest. He was completely into the book and got a lot of information about the life of kings, people and culture of Greece and that time. At the last page of the book there was a small, but an effective verse written which read 'Zombie's Zombie's Come along'. As soon as he chanted the verse, he felt a cold hand on his shoulder. Peter's heart stood still. He turned around and he saw his best friend Mike calling him. He told Peter, "Peter the bell already rung, it's break time. Let us eat our lunch." Peter left the book right there at the library. On their way to the cafeteria, they saw that the whole passageway, which was earlier buzzling with students, was now silent and unexpressed. Peter Asked Mike" Where are all the students." Just then somebody called them from behind. It was Tony, there common friend. They went towards him. Tony told them" I was playing basketball along with other friends but suddenly all of them disappeared. I got scared and ran towards the classroom but found no one here. Talking you two gave me some courage" Peter replied, " Guys this is extremely unusual, and we should find a solution to this problem." " First let's try to find out the cause. Something weird might have happened. " Asked Mike. "Oh, I know what might have happened. You see when I was in the library I found a glittering peculiar book regarding the topic of Greek mythology. At the last page, there was a verse and when i read it something queer happened. This might be the reason. "What was the book about. Was there anything strange or like scary (Ghosts or something)?" asked Tony. " Yes, But the book was not of Ghosts. It was of ZOMBIES whose plague occurred in Greece 600 years ago." exclaimed Peter. J ust then they heard a weird and scary sound as well as a stinky smell like that of a dead man. " What is this sound and disgusting smell? It is making me feel dizzy" asked Mike. Peter replied, " We just need to stay calm and relaxed. You see, nothing lasts forever" But eventually the smell grew more and more stinky making the boys dizzy and uncomfortable. " I just can't bare it any longer," said Tony. As soon as the boys started to cough and dizzy, they saw something scary and impossible through the translucent gas in the passageway. They seem to have seen a man with large eyes, thin body just like a skeleton in green skin. " What are those creatures?" asked Peter. Then they heard a petrifying sound with the creatures speaking in deep-hollow voice "Humans Humans Come here, your flesh is what we will tear." The boys ran at top speed trying to escape the school. The school had 8 floors. There was gas spread everywhere except the 8th floor. Thus, the children rushed there, skipping stairs and in no time, they reached the top floor. They decided to hide in the washroom and as a result quarantined themselves there. Eventually the zombies following them also reached there but unable to find the kids, said in a horrifying manner, " SOLOVAR WANT YOU TO BECOME INVINCIBLE AND RULE THE WORLD. COME TO US AND YOU SHALL BE SAFE." Peter replied" Hey and I read that these zombies are allergic to 'Methyl Blue' "It's a type of element found in the ink of blue pen." replied Tony. "Wait what, we could use the ink of blue pen as an antidote to the disgusting smell of the zombies." Guys bring all the blue pens here." Who is Solovar" asked Tony. "He is the king of zombies. Maybe when I read the verse, it led to the reborn of Solovar which in turn built a whole army of zombies" answered Peter. " So does that mean that all our friends, our teacher and staff members in this school have become zombies." asked Mike "Yes, and solovar wants to kill us so that he can establish a kingdom and make the whole world, including our family, zombies. He has already made our friends zombies" replied Peter. "We won't let that happen. We would defeat Solovar and make this world safe." said Mike. So, are you guys ready for 'Mission Save The World' "Hey so any ideas how we are planning to do so?" asked Tony. "I think the only way to do it is my getting the book and reading it's reverse verse. But the book will be with Solovar and would be almost impossible for us to get it back." answered Peter. "For that first we need to get out of this little music room" interrupted mike. "But how are we going to do it guys" "Oh, I have an idea" told Tony." Oh, what is it" said mike out of excitement. Pointing at the boxes, Tony answered, " What if we hide in those boxes and escape out of this place." Everybody agreed with Tony's Idea ﻿ Let's go get the book of wizard from Solovar. All the children quickly search the whole room and found loads of blue ink. Then they laid them down on a utensil. They had almost half a litre of ink and each of them poured in their water bottle. They could now use it as a gun. They pulled them tightly into their socks. Then Mike interrupted, The three boys silently got off the room crouching bending and hiding them from the zombie guards searching for them. Finally, they reached the second floor. Now they just needed to find in which room he actually is. They saw a number of zombies going into the Computer Lab carrying some boxes filled with fruits. " I think solovar is right there" whispered mike. Carefully holding their guns, they secretly replaced their fruit boxes with their own boxes." I think we shall be quite over here. When solovar opens the box, we will jump scare him and attack the zombies with ink (methyl blue)" ordered peter. And so, did happen When The boxes reached solovar, the three boys jumped up spraying ink on the zombies. The zombies became unconscious, and their mind seemed to be spinning. Tony quickly got hold of the Cursed book and ran away. But wait there was always a twist: The ink had gone into the eyes of mike making him blind for a moment. But his friends were so out of excitement that they forgot about him, and they ran up the stairs to their original hiding place. "Oh No! Mike is missing." Just then there was a queer sound of the walking dead. " If you read the reverse verse, you friend shall no longer survive and also no more planning of escaping cause we will now find you in every room and every corner of the school, HAHAHAHAHA Good Luck." Peter and tony sneaked out of the washroom, and saw various zombies, searching each and every room. There was almost no way for them to escape. But the worst part was that all the ink had been used against Solovar. But they gathered up courage and very quietly got out of the washroom. They reached the floor where solovar was ruling and suddenly they had an idea. " Pull out your mask" said Tony, "Why" asked peter, "Remember the only weapon of those zombies are their disgusting smell. What if we withstand the smell by wearing the mask. " "Brilliant Idea." " And what if I go in front of Solovar wearing a mask and dislocate his mind. Then you could secretly rescue Mike and then will run away" replied Tony They did exactly as they had planned. As Tony came in front of Solovar, He replied," Hey Solovar, don't dare to touch my friend mike or else suffer the consequences." Meanwhile, Peter sneaked in and set Mike free. As soon as Tony came to know that his plan has been successful, He ran away. Peter and Mike followed him. The zombies roaring and spreading smell also followed them. The three boys reached the place where they had hidden the book. Quickly Peter chanted the Reverse verse: ﻿ ﻿ As soon as he chanted the verse, all the zombies turned into human. It seemed as if nobody remembered anything. "Well, that's that." Said mike. "We did it". "YES and see the book has also turned into ashes" exclaimed Peter. But just then the school bell rung, indicating that the school was over. All the students were astonished as they had not studied anything, and the school had been dispersed. "Anyways It was a wonderful and adventurous day today" "Maybe it's now time to go make home" exclaimed Tony

title: Ducks in Space
text: I find it best to stop for a moment and have a particularly strong beverage. Decaf coffee for example. (Don’t judge me, I’m 10!). I am Khanduri, Fern Khanduri and I’m a member of the first ever Bluebells School detective club. We haven’t had any murder mysteries yet, but I think we might be close! Our group has three people including myself. There’s Hilda, my bestie, and Sarah, my good luck charm! So, let’s start the oddest case you have ever seen! My dad owns a waffle shop, small and cozy; it doesn’t attract a lot of attention. But one day, everything changed. It was a Wednesday morning. As I got up for breakfast, I heard a terrible shriek. "Dad!?" I yelled. “Did you see a spider in the shower again, Honey?” said mum. “My shop! There has been a burglary!” he cried. Everything was still. The police did an investigation, but nothing was found except for some ugly square footprints. “Aha! Our first case! ” yelled Sarah. It was the next day, and we were heading to class. Before we could solve our first case, we heard a loud sound from down in the garden. But we couldn’t leave the class. “Never follow anyone else’s path,” said Hilda, “unless you are stuck in the woods without food and water”. It sounded quite silly to me, so I excused myself to go to the washroom. Instead, I went to the garden. There I saw Ms. Godzilla – I mean Ms. Gladin, crying her eyes out. “What’s the matter?” I said. But soon I understood. Last year we had buried a time capsule with our most prized possessions. Ms. Gladin had put in a solid gold necklace. Next to her was a pile of dirt and no time capsule meaning that someone had stolen the necklace! Next to the pile of dirt, were twenty odd square footprints. “Maybe it was the ducks!” said Sarah. “That is the silliest thing I have ever heard you say,” replied Hilda, “I shall pretend I didn’t hear it”. The following week was full of more and more thefts, even one of a cat. “It probably just wandered off.” I thought. One night, next week, the rest of the club and I decided to hold a stakeout at my dad’s waffle house. Sure enough, at 1:23 AM we heard a sound. “Quack”. Then another “Quack - quack”. It kept going on until the shop was filled with “Quacks”. And there we saw them, the ducks! But these were not ordinary ducks. They were wearing black suits and had square feet. Wait what?! “We are a part of ADSFD – The Alien Duck Society for Ducksss…,” said the ducks. The drama was increasing. Hilda fainted and Sarah lost her voice. With nothing left to do, I threw a waffle at ducks. To my surprise, they started eating it. I threw another and another, and another until the ducks resembled a fat thanksgiving turkey. Then, I quietly slipped away and informed the police about the ducks. They didn’t believe me, so I dragged them to the shop. But lo, the ducks had disappeared! Had it been a hallucination? But on the floor lay one feather. So, it was real! It has been a year, and nobody noticed that the ducks are missing from our school garden. Two Years Later My world is over. As I realised the tragedy, my heartbeat slowed down. His last word, “Fern,” and then it happened. He died, collapsed. My father… is dead. “NO!” my mother lashed out. “No..” said Hilda. “No” said Sarah. Blood spurting out and a knife by his side, lying face up on the waffle shop floor, was Dad. I only remained silent. Grief, had struck again.` ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The case is now of murder, and I am ready. My father won’t be the only one to die this week. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- “Hilda, Sarah, we’re skipping school,” I said. Hilda gave in but Sarah protested, “No way, we’ve got a test toda-" “I’m not suggesting, I’m telling you,” I said. “You’re telling me?” asked Sarah, her voice cracking. “I’m ORDERING you,” I burst out. “Be quiet or just GO AWAY!” And she did, sobbing and pushing past us. “I didn’t… I didn’t like her anyway,” I lied. Hilda put her arm around me. “Don’t worry, it’s alright," she said. “DON’T YOU SEE,” I cried. “EVERYTHING IS NOT ALRIGHT! I JUST LOST MY BEST FRIEND AND MY FATHER IS DEAD!” Comforting though it felt to scream at others and blame them, it was no one’s fault – and that was the hardest part to understand. “Let’s go look at the shop – the now ‘murder scene’," said I. Gruesome though it was to look at the place my father had died, I stood my ground and found something interesting. A single feather and row of SQUARE FOOTPRINTS. But little did I know that this week would be full of surprises. The next day at school, I saw what I feared, the ducks were back. Quacking like maniacs, they flapped their feathers and swam in the lake. “They act so innocent,” Hilda muttered, her rage clearly visible. “Let’s take them in for questioning!” I joked. My mood was getting better since I found out that my father after being hospitalized had normal vitals! Hilda stopped in her tracks, “YOU. ARE. A. GENIUS.” she said. I merely stared back at her, confused. “We will do that!” Hilda explained. And so, at the end of school, we finally managed to strangle a duck and kidnap it. We took it home and put it in an enormous cardboard box and climbed inside. It started to flap its wings and QUACKED like it had never seen us before in its puny, little, miserable LIFE! It made me angry to look at them now, in the dark. “WHY ARE YOU HERE? WHO REALLY ARE YOU? WHAT DO YOU WANT?” Hilda’s voice echoed like gunshots. The duck looked at her. She looked at the duck. "AAAH!" She screamed. "AAAAAH!" I screamed. There seemed to be a humongous ugly tick on the duck's back. It scuttled towards us. We quickly backed out of the box but then the insect stopped. It was actually some gadget! Sudden realization flooded me. My dad has a necklace that he always wears, and the charm on it looks exactly like this tick! It started speaking, “Unplug the wire, unplug the wire, unplug the wire”. "What?" said Hilda and I at the same time. Soon we realized that it was my dad’s voice. And then we heard crackling, “Fern, listen, I don’t have much time, LISTEN, the man in the hospital isn’t your father, I am, he’s an imposter, or should I say it is....", “DON’T UNPLUG THE WIRE, DON’T UNPULG THE WIRE, DO NOT UNPLUG THE LIFE SUPPORT SYSTEM IN THE HOSPITAL” interrupted the duck. And then all was silent as the duck disappeared, along with the insect. “What are YOU doing here?”, I said with a look of disgust. Just minutes later, as I entered my room along with Hilda, I saw Sarah sitting on my bed. “I know what happened,” she said. “I’M NOT DOING IT!” I yelled. Sarah said, “You don’t have to. Your father, or whoever was in the hospital, he’s declared dead." And then just as I was about to cry, I heard a sound. “Dad?” I called. “Where are you?” Sarah and Hilda looked as shocked as me. We all rushed to follow the voice. It came from the basement. “The deep, dark, scary basement?" said Sarah, her voice quivering. I shot her a look as I opened the door. I was forbidden from entering the basement because, well, I don’t know, and it looked like no one had entered into it in years! “Dad?” I called. And then, I saw him. “DAD!” I yelled. And I hugged him. “How? And, more importantly why? Why did you disappear?” asked Sarah weakly. My father shoved some papers with CIA written on them into my hands. “Life undercover?”, said Sarah in a state of utter shock But I didn’t care. There was a lot I didn't know. There was a lot I wasn't supposed to know, but it didn't matter. What mattered was that I was part of one, complete family again. All was well. By Akira Khanduri 5 - A Bluebells School International
