title: A Mouse travels the world
text: One day after eating cheese for dinner, little mouse decided to sneak out of the house and catch fire flies, so she quietly tip toed past her big sister and her parents. She takes a net box and runs along the road to get to the swamp. After a while she finds herself at the bus stop, there was a bus with Mr Nick the mouse who was a professional driver but could never get his stubby little feet to get to the brake pedal so he got a personal bus to let the whole rodent community across town. “Well, I must hurry or else he will tell mum and dad!” she said hurrying alongside the road. Beep! Beep! The bus was finally heading out of town! But, there came a problem… The petrol in the bus was down to ZERO! There ran Mr Nick the mouse hurrying to get the petrol tank. Little Mouse got curious, so she went inside the bus when no one was watching, she sat underneath the last seat so that no one could see her. In front of her sat Mrs Rose who was a lemming, she would usually get her fur straitened or coloured but today every other rodent saw her tangled cream coloured. She also had a very strong sense of smell so Little Mouse had to crawl very far from her. “Off to the Swamp Kingdom! Screamed Mr Nick with petrol drops on his whiskers. As they got there it was almost sunrise! “Huh! Will I never get a chance to be able to reach the swamp at night?” Little Mouse sighed. When they reached there, the whole rodent community squished together out the door bus to get to the Swamp Kingdom first. But why? Well all the rodents knew that during sunrise the Frog Queen would hop along her garden and see who had the best bit of bread, it was quite weird but it was the tradition so it had to stay alive. The Frog Queen came hopping along her orchard and started to taste all the different types of bread everyone had. “I have a baguette, I baked it fresh and the yeast is from Paris.” Said Mrs Allison. “I’ve got some Ciambella, It’s from Rome and my uncle bought it.” Said Mr Giovanni wearing a chef’s hat. And hundreds of other mice showed off their beautiful and cold breads. “Disgusting! All of you rodents know nothing about the perfect type of baked bread! Just Quit and go Home!” The Queen Screamed. But then in the crowd, Little Mouse got the perfect Idea. She had a small piece of the loaf with her. “Miss! Miss! Can you taste this please? My mother baked it with love! Will you please just have a crumb!” she cried. “Well, I shall take it whole. Let’s see what you got little Mouse.” The Frog Queen said raising her black spectacles. As she took the first bite… “Delicious! I did not expect that! Your mother must be an angel to bake such bread! Here, come give me a hug!” The Frog Queen said with glee. “Thank you so much Frog Queen!” The mouse said. The Frog Queen hugged her tightly, mouse got a little bit wet for The Queen had moist skin. All of the passengers sat in the Rodent Tourist Bus (RTB) including Mouse and went to their homes. It was truly a wild adventure for the mouse.
author: Aarvi Singh

title: Trouble In Paradise
text: My name’s Stephie, and I’m 14. I live with my parents, sister and brother. Most people including my family think I work part time at a candy store although I am actually a sidekick- ‘Augur Girl’ to super heroine and my best friend Megan whom the world knows as ‘Thunder Woman’. The most difficult part about my job is to keep it a secret, so I have my own lair to store all of my secret weapons. My lair has a key, and it needs to be with me all the time! During an emergency, Megan would call me, I would get changed by shooting myself with a laser beam in the flash of a second and take the weapons I needed, and run off to the candy store through the secret exit in my lair. Megan was the ‘owner’ of the store and all our missions were handled and sorted out inside her lair. I was freshening up after school one day, when Megan beeped about an emergency. I rushed to get the key but couldn’t find it! Amidst the frenzy, I heard Stephen yelling out, “Laundry…laundry, if anyone has any laundry to be done, give it to me or else I’ll have to yank it away from you because I’ve got other places to be!” My parents believed in ‘division of labor’ and so assigned Stephen to do the laundry this week. But sometimes, brothers can be really fussy. Sophie was having a silly tea party, so she did not care about laundry and was only concerned about making ‘Limbo’ her stuffed elephant feel at home. I threw my school clothes into the laundry basket which was in Stephen’s hands and asked him to calm down but he just wouldn’t listen. He was so mad at Sophie, that instead of asking her twice about laundry, he just popped everything in and turned the washing machine on. He immediately left for his concert. I called Megan hoping she was in a good mood to tell her I’d be late. But apparently, she had gotten into a fight with her mom about trivial matters and was so annoyed that she did not even pay attention to what I was saying. I took the chance and told her I would be late because there were some ‘technical issues’ at home and that I’d try to get there as soon as possible. I felt really bad for being irresponsible and was walking back and forth when I noticed something shining in the washing machine…the key! I recollected immediately that I had put the key in my uniform pocket and had forgotten to take it out before throwing the uniform into the machine. How in the world could I be so silly? The washing machine would take at least 40 minutes to finish, and I had to pause the machine to get the key out, but without anyone noticing! Sophie wouldn’t be a problem because she was busy with her tea party but mom…she would be the real problem. Although mom knows that the machine beeps once it’s done, she still loves peeping in every five minutes just to make sure it is running smoothly. Another problem is, mom has the ears of an owl so she might hear me opening the machine in between. Nobody in the house knew about my lair and the key. If someone caught me sneaking in and pulling out the key, I would have to answer so many questions about it and that would mean my cool life as Augur Girl would be over. I was actively seeking ideas in my head- my powers would definitely not work, because they could only be activated with the power ball in my lair. My only problem to a successful mission was mom, but if I could somehow distract her, then taking the key out would be as easy as a slice of pie! I soon realized that the bathroom was the perfect place for me to cause trouble in paradise for mom. I slowly went over, opened the door without making a sound and shut it behind me. I took my mom’s favorite shampoo bottle, opened it and let it spill all over the place. I put the bottle on the ground as if it had fallen down and sneaked out of the bathroom. Then, I casually walked into the bathroom and shouted, “Mom, your shampoo has spilled all over the floor! How in the world did this happen?” By the time I had finished these sentences, mom was already in the bathroom because a life without her favorite shampoo was not a life for her. She was quite upset and told me, “You go on honey, let me clean up this mess!” I felt bad about what I had done but it was part of my job and although I felt guilty, I knew I had to do it. I quickly took the chance and went over to the washing machine and paused it, then waited for a couple of minutes before it would open and once it did, I slowly pulled the door and was about to slide my hand into it when Sophie popped out of nowhere and yelled, “Mom…Stephie is opening the washing machine!” I asked Sophie to keep her mouth shut and go back to her tea party but this angered her and she screamed out even more loudly, “Mom…Stephie is opening the washing machine!” My mom heard Sophie yelling and asked, “Sophie…why are you yelling, I am coming in a minute!” I knew there was nothing I could do, and as promised, mom came after a minute to find me looking helplessly at her. Mom immediately said, “Stephie, why is the washing machine open?” I stuttered, ‘Um…uh…I was just…putting my top in the machine! Uh…I forgot to do so when Stephen brought in the basket.” Mom replied, “Stephie, how many times have I told you to put your clothes in the machine before whoever’s in charge turns it on? Go to your room now!” I obeyed but was determined to get the key before anyone saw it twinkling in the machine! I was getting ready to attempt the mission once again when my phone rang and it was Megan. I knew she would be mad if I didn’t pick up the call so I did, “Hey…Megan!” I said with a slight stutter. What I heard next was, “How long does it take to reach the store from your home that’s just three buildings away?” I froze and felt guilty for being such a terrible friend and sidekick. I knew I had to tell her the truth, and so I did. She responded, “If you don’t reach the store in the next twenty minutes…you’re fired!” I was more shocked than ever! I felt worthless, and irresponsible! Was I going to lose my job because I could not get a silly key out of a washing machine? I did not want that to happen, and that call gave me more motivation to get the job done. I slipped out of the room, went over to the machine and paused it again. After a few minutes, I sneaked my hand in, got the key and walked back to my room as if nothing had happened. I went over to my lair and attempted to slide the key in, but lo and behold…it wouldn’t fit! I looked closely at the key and realized that it was actually the house’s spare key which must have slipped into the machine from Stephen’s shirt pocket because he had taken it to school today. What was I to do now? I was tired of thinking and decided to at least reach the store on time. Constantly brooding about how I was on the verge of losing my job, I walked to the store and met with Megan in her lair. She was glaring at me and asked, “Where is your uniform?” The silence spoke for itself and Megan realized that I had not found the key. The fact that I wasn’t looking at her face-to-face helped her realize that I had done my best. I was just about to leave when Megan said, “Wait, you’re not fired! Please, don’t leave, you’re my best friend and the best side kick I could ever ask for, so don’t fret over a key! We’ll just make a spare.” I hugged Megan and apologized to her and we decided to go out for ice cream. I put my hands into my jacket-pocket and…when I pulled it out, there was the key to my lair glimmering in my hand. Megan and I looked at each other and laughed at my forgetfulness. But, what about me recollecting that the key was in my uniform…I realized that I had put the key in my school uniform yesterday, not today and that I’d taken it out today and put it into my jacket instead!
author: GABRIELA  GEORGE

title: Those were the days...
text: 24 March 2015 Dear Diary, Today, I have completed 16 years of adventures, 16 years of blissful and joyous moments and 16 amazing revolutions around the bright sun! I wanted to share with you an experience that has been strange yet fun. ……….……….……….……….……….……….………….……….……….……….……….….. The school near the outskirts of the town looked so scary in the evening, na? When I saw it for the first time, I was with Appa, walking to explore the beautiful scenes of that place. But the school was the thorn of the rose. The place is a dense jungle, and in the middle of the jungle, lies the way to go to the abandoned school. It has been abandoned for years and now the school is a spot for ghostly spirits to live. And, if it wasn’t so difficult to guess, it is actually haunted. Yesterday I heard Appa and uncle talking about the same. Appa said that the school is haunted by a ghostly spirit of the History teacher of that school. It is a very popular tale that one morning the people of our locality, including Appa, found the body of that old fogey lying halfway across the library. Some say it was a heart attack, but no one really knows what had happened the night before. Anyway, Appa said that his last wish was not fulfilled and hence his atript atma (dissatisfied spirit) is still roaming inside the school. By the way, his last wish was something next to impossible, it was building a Taj Mahal similar to the one far in Agra, here in Kazhakkoottam. I mean, what an old fogey he was! He was probably the most hated teacher in history, as he used to live in the subject he used to teach, HISTORY! Now this conversation was all what I heard from the window of our house, when Amma was cooking delicious Rasam for me on the occasion of my birthday. 24 March 2015 Dear Diary, Today, I have completed 16 years of adventures, 16 years of blissful and joyous moments and 16 amazing revolutions around the bright sun! I had a brilliant plan going on in my mind, the time to execute it was in the evening. The evening was full of celebration and glamour, it was the birthday of the only son of the tehsildar of Kazhakkoottam. All my friends had come, in new and beautiful clothes. Gopi and Bhola were also cordially invited, as they are my best friends. After having food, we decided to have some fun. Gopi is the most talkative girl of our class, but today she was talking at a different pace. She was explaining her relation with the most popular subject of our school, HISTORY! She said, "Oh my Goodness! How I wonder can there be any subject as boring as history? What’s really the point of learning something which is of no use in the present?" I argued, as a part of the plan, “But, Gopi, we learn from our roots, our past…” “I am not opposing that buddy, but what do you learn from that boring master. He teaches history as if he has to rush somewhere by the train in the morning, I mean it doesn’t feel like learning. History should be taught like a story, like drama, like an emotion, like a tale, like a…” “Ok, ok I got your point.” I mean, what an old fogey he was! He was probably the most hated teacher in history, as he used to live in the subject he used to teach, HISTORY! Now all this conversation was what I heard from the window of our house, when Amma was cooking delicious Rasam for me on the occasion of my birthday. I had a brilliant plan going on in my mind, the time to execute it was in the evening. Today's evening was that of shine and glamour, it was the birthday of the only son of the tehsildar of Kazhakkoottam. All my friends had come, in new and beautiful clothes. Though she said so, everyone knows how badly she hated history. But today her being talkative was a big advantage for me. It was time for the execution of the plan. I narrated the whole story in front of them and Gopi started laughing, but Bhola was very serious, as he was expected to be. He said, "Gopi, are you laughing? Seriously?" As he said this, Gopi turned silent. She then said, "You tell me what to do? The people of the village are scared of the dead history master, I am scared of the one who is still alive and teaching me daily!" Bhola continued, "Don't you think that this village needs a change? We are the future of our nation and we should be the ones to open the eyes of our people. We should bust this myth, what do you say Robin?" "But who will go?" He quickly replied, "I will go!" Gopi and Bhola were cordially invited, as they are my best friends. After having the food, we decided to have some fun. Gopi is the most talkative girl of our class, but today she was talking at a different pace. She was explaining her relations with the most popular subject of our school, HISTORY! She said, "Oh my Goodness! How I wonder can there be any subject as boring as history? What’s really the point of learning something which is of no use in the present?" I argued, as a part of the plan, “But, Gopi, we learn from our roots, our past…” “I am not opposing that, buddy, but what do you learn from that boring master. He teaches history as if he has to rush somewhere by the train in the morning, I mean it doesn’t feel like learning. History should be taught like a story, like a drama, like an emotion, like a tale, like a…” And that was what I wanted. I warned him, actually just acting like I was warning him, "But Bhola, Appa was saying that whoever goes inside, never comes back. Please don't leave us alone!" Bhola, as he was expected to be, neglected the warning, and, acting like a hero, spoke a very heavy dialogue, "Why to fear, when Bholaram Rao is here!" And he jumped and dashed towards the school. I gave a loud clap to Gopi and both of us went to our homes. Well, I am so excited about tomorrow. What will happen next is so much awaited. Bhola is the most innocent child of my age. He is the only person who acts as he is expected to. I am way too excited to see how brave he is. Robin 25 March 2015 Dear Diary, Do you know what happened today? As soon as I came out in the morning, Appa called me with an angry voice, "Purushottam!" After hearing 'Purushottam' (my full name), instead of 'Robin', my excitedness dropped suddenly from its peak to as deep as the Mariana Trench. I went out and the only thing I thought of was, no matter what Appa asked me, I just have to answer with a simple no. But, for me it was a true adventure, and adventures are not that easy. "Tell me where is Bhola?" Appa asked, in a super angry mood. And before I heard it, I started crying, "Appa, I have not done anything. Trust me, I am your only child. It was he himself who went to that haunted school!" The moment I said HAUNTED SCHOOL, Appa immediately shouted, "Purushottam, do you even know what you have done? You didn’t even think of the prestige of your father. Are you no more scared of my rage? Your mother has always shielded you from me and my rage, that is the only reason for your mischiefs increasing consistently. Do you know what happened last night? All of us heard Bhola's scream. His father has come to me begging to help him find Bhola." And then Appa and Rao uncle ran towards the school. Gopi and I also decided to follow them. What we found was even more hilarious than the gossips of Amma and the neighbours. Bhola was lying on ground, in the backyard of the school, with his pant tucked at the branch of the tree. He was snoring and sleeping! We took him and came back to my house. When Amma made him drink some water, he woke up, screaming, "Please don't eat me, not me. I am a small child. I love history. Please leave me." Then, after a little while, he calmed and narrated the whole story. Last night, when he reached the school, he lit a lamp and proceeded further. He didn't find anything except dry leaves and old stuff. When he was returning from the backyard, he felt as if someone held his pant and he screamed as loud as he could. Then the lamp fell from his hands, his legs jumped out of his pants, and he lay on the ground, unconscious. Then all of us laughed louder than ever before. Appa said, "You see Mr. Rao, this was the ghost of our history teacher, the tree in the backyard!" So once again, Gopi, I, and our innocent buddy Bhola, busted this myth and were praised for our bravery. Now, maybe I will visit the school again and this time, flee with my friends to nature’s masterpiece. That was how my adventure ended, this time, after solving the age-old mystery of the ghost of the history teacher. Let's see what tomorrow unfolds for me! title: Father Christmas ?
text: Christmas. A joyous and merry festival celebrating the birthday of Jesus Christ. Christmas isn’t just about him, though. Known and loved by all, he is dear to us. He is known as Santa Claus to some, and St. Nicholas to others. In this particular story, he is affectionately referred to as ‘Father Christmas’. The holidays have always been Anna Turner’s favourite time of year. There was nothing she loved more than magic. Although she didn’t have any siblings, she never felt the absence of one. For as long as she could remember, her life had always been filled with magic. In her life, magic wasn’t brought by the Easter Bunny or tooth fairy, it was in the seemingly everyday things she sensed. She could feel it behind the curtains, in the glint of the light, the pages of her books, the eyes of her dolls, the rustle of leaves, and in the smell of the food her mum made. The Christmas season was especially special to her. A month full of all the fuzziness magic can offer. During the first week of December, Christmas carols and jingles would start playing on radios, lights would be hung, and Christmas trees... Oh, the Christmas trees!! Bright and colorful, filled with bobbles and tinsels and lights and ornaments, and the tree skirt surrounding the trunk with little gifts on them. She could go on and on. She could never describe the joy she felt while opening gifts. This is her last proper Christmas, she’s seventeen now. They say, he stops visiting when a child turns 18 since they are no longer a child. Almost none of the kids believe in him anymore. In their minds, he doesn’t even exist. Rather, their parents keep the gifts under the tree. Anna knows better than to believe all that hogwash. Those kids don’t even deserve Christmas. Their childhood ended when they ceased to believe he existed. Typically, kids would ask her for evidence to back up her claim that he exists. But she didn’t need any, especially not for kids like THEM. On the last Christmas of her life, she poured every ounce of energy into decorating the tree, baking the cookies, and hanging the lights. In preparation for Father Christmas’ last visit, she handcrafted gleaming ornaments, iced all the sugar cookies and prepared the trees. Nevertheless, she had other things on her to-do list, besides preparing for Christmas. She intended to do something she had refrained from doing all these years. This year she intended on seeing Father Christmas. It would be her first and last encounter with him. This will be her last chance to see the embodiment of magic. Her lack of a desire to disturb Father Christmas prevented her from doing so all these years. If he didn’t want to be seen, then she wouldn’t see him. Maybe he’s insecure about all his facial hair or perhaps delivering gifts could be hampered by meeting kids. But once in seventeen years shouldn’t hurt. Or so she hoped. Finally, Christmas Eve had arrived. Despite that it had been snowing for almost a week now, her home was as warm as it could be. With the smell of hot cocoa and gingerbread cookies in the air and the warmth that their heater provided, Anna could feel the festive spirit of Christmas flowing in her blood to her fingertips. Now that it was around six in the evening, it was tradition for them to begin their movie marathon. The family will stay up late watching all the hallmark Christmas movies until ten in the night, snuggled in a single blanket on their couch with caramel popcorn and eggnog in hand. The movie session was over, and Anna was supposed to be heading to bed, at least according to her parents. Having made sure that the lights in her parents' room were off, Anna sneakily tiptoed into the living room and hid behind the sofas. Two hours went by yet nothing happened. Anna was slowly dozing off now. She tried keeping herself awake by fiddling with her beaded bracelet. A sudden sound of footsteps woke her up. As Anna’s sleepiness gave way to anticipation, her heart pounded Ka-thump, Ka-thump. She could see the shadow of him as well! His approach to the room grew closer and closer, and he finally entered. But... he was not Father Christmas. This was her father! But what about Father Christmas? He never existed.. Her entire life had been spent believing lies. By now, her father had left the room. As Anna walked to her bedroom, her shoulders slumped, she was drowning in pain. In an attempt to console herself, she tucked herself into bed with tears streaming down her face. Sleeping was difficult for her as she tried to shut her eyes but she twisted and turned in bed, trying to fall asleep. It had all been a waste of time to argue with her friends when they were right all along. The next morning, she wasn’t sad anymore. She felt grateful. Her parents had worked hard for seventeen years trying to keep the magic alive for her. Her father was Christmas. Father Christmas. So when she was opening her gifts, she didn’t feel like the magic was lost, for her it was more alive than ever. It was the magic of love.

title: Luna: The Lost Dog
text: Once in the city of Seattle, lived a girl named Kira with her parents. It was her last exam. Once the exam finished she planned to go on a picnic with her friends Ava and Grace. The next day each of them asked for permission to go for a picnic from their parents. The parents allowed them to go for the picnic. Ava got the food and drinks, Grace got all the supplies needed like, picnic mat, cutlery, and plastic plates. Kira was in charge of picking the games. The next day, they were all set to go for the picnic. They bid goodbye to there parents, took out their bicycles and started from their houses to meet at Kira's house. They finally reached the picnic spot, after resting for some time, they started to play. Suddenly, they heard a sound. It was from a little distance away. Kira exclaimed "Where is that sound coming from? Come lets go and see". Ava and Grace said to Kira, "I don't think that it will be safe to go there; there could be something dangerous out there. Kira was very curious to know from where the sound was coming. She followed the sound and found a dog whining and howling. She went back to Ava and Grace and said to them, "There is a dog there. I think we should give it some food and water. The dog did not eat the food or drink the water; it continued whining and howling. Kira saw a thorn pierced in the dog's paw, and she said to her friends, "I'll stay here with the dog; you go call a vet. Grace and Ava went to the veterinary doctor and told him everything that had happened. The children then told the vet to come with them. The vet followed the children to where the dog was. The vet saw the dog and said to the children, "We must take the dog to the hospital, this thorn must be removed as it may be poisonous". The dog was taken to the veterinary hospital, where the vet started the treatment. The children visited the dog often, all of them fell in love with the dog. Kira wanted to keep the dog, so she asked her parents if she could do so. The parents were proud of what she had done, and let her adopt it. Kira named the dog "Luna". After a few days, the children planned to go for a picnic again. The plan stayed the same and they started their journey. On the way, Grace saw a poster on a tree. Grace said to her friends, " Guys, look at the picture on this poster. It looks very familiar". Kira read the poster "MISSING!" IF YOU FIND MY DOG, PLEASE CALL NO. "1234567890" Ava sadly said to Kira and Grace, "I think that the dog on the poster 'Sofia' is Luna. Kira replied, " We can't be that sure. I think we should take this poster and show it to our parents. They took the poster to Kira's parents. The parents read the poster and said, "The dog in the poster looks like Luna; maybe it is Luna." ” Ava said to Kira’s mother, “Mrs. Wood I think we should call the number. We found Luna near the picnic spot. She must have run away from her home. Mrs. Woods called the number. She told Mrs. Willow what had happened, and Mrs. Willow said to Mrs. Woods, “Sophia ran away from the house a few weeks ago, and I have been trying to find her since then. Thank you". Mrs. Woods replied, "Sure, Mrs. Willow". Mrs. Woods told the children to go and give the dog to Mrs. Willow the next day. “ Kira said to her mom, But that is not fair!! We found her and it’s ours now!! Mrs. Woods replied, “Don’t be selfish, Kira. That dog is not ours; we don’t own it. You are going to give the dog to her tomorrow. I’m sorry. The following day, the children went to Mrs. Willow’s house to give her the dog. Mrs. Willow said to the children, “I have grown old, and seeing you with Sofia, I feel that Sofia belongs with you now. You should keep her. The children jumped with joy, thanked Mrs. Willow, and bid goodbye to her. THE END

title: Two Friends, Two Spilled Secrets
text: The hallways of N-Blossom academy were as lively as ever. Students chattering, teachers scolding, and the chaos never stopped unfolding. “Katy! Give them back please, I won’t be able to attend the next class without them!” As usual, Katy was messing around with Andrew but it was nothing out of the ordinary. They were always bantering so it was a daily routine for the teachers by now. Most people knew about how they always teased each other (most times it was Katy poking fun at Andrew) but few knew about how deep was their friendship. They were childhood friends and had never left each other's side since they became friends. Those who knew thought about how someone like Andrew could became friends with someone like Katy. They were complete opposites, it just seemed impossible. “C’mon Drew it was just a joke! Plus, you always overreact, drama queen!” Katy beamed. Their friendship was like any other, but every good thing has its end. Katy started despising Andrew for every little thing and they started arguing a lot. “He’s such an egoist, who would even want to be friends with him?” “He thinks everyone likes him. What an idiot!” Those words felt like daggers stabbing him through his chest. Andrew was on the verge of tears as his best friend just double-crossed him. He couldn’t believe it, it was just too cruel to be true. He was devastated, how could she? How could the person he trusted the most do that to him? “How could you, Katy? Why? Why did you do that?” Andrew asked the next day bitterly. He had stayed up the whole night thinking over it and couldn’t think of anything else to do but confront her. “What do you mean? If this is about yesterday, I already told you I was playing around! You can’t still be mad about that. Tch.” Katy retorted. “No, this is about what you said. You could’ve just told me you know…” “I don’t get what you’re talking about…?” “I heard you talking to Jake yesterday, you could’ve just told me that you didn’t like me.” Jake was their classmate, he always followed others like a dog and did everything they asked. Andrew did not expect him out of all people to say such mean words. “Andrew, look, sometimes you can be a handful and I didn’t want to sound rude to you. I’m sorry.” Andrew turned around and walked away. He realized how he always forgave everyone for everything, he couldn’t handle it anymore. She just expected him to forgive her like that? It wasn’t going to work like that now. Andrew headed to his class deep in thought. He didn’t have any other friends except her and, well, it was embarrassing to admit but he always depended on her for everything. At least he had his sister, Eleanor. “Come on, Andrew! She does not deserve your forgiveness anyway.” Eleanor was always there for Andrew, she helped him through everything. “I know El, but after everything I did for her. She still said all that…” “What did you do for her? You never told me anything like that before.” “I, well… I comforted her when her mom died. I promised her not to tell anyone though.” “Oh, didn’t expect that to be honest.” “Yeah. But please don’t tell anyone!” “Sure, whatever…” Andrew was so thankful to have a sister like Eleanor, but he regretted telling her. She could never keep anything to herself and he wasn’t thinking at the time so he told her anyways. Andrew was so thankful to have a sister like Eleanor, but he regretted telling her. She could never keep anything to herself and he wasn’t thinking at the time so he told her anyways. Andrew was so thankful to have a sister like Eleanor, but he regretted telling her. She could never keep anything to herself and he wasn’t thinking at the time so he told her anyways. “I-I didn’t d-do anything!” He was stuttering, he was scared. What if this would affect their friendship even more? “You’re the only one who knew!” Eleanor barged into the classroom. “Katy, wait! It was me, I told one of my friends. I didn’t know she had a grudge against you!” Katy questioned both of them and concluded that it was all Andrew's fault. She said she would never forgive him and a few other things that are better left unsaid. Andrew was devastated, how could he let this happen? He was very cross at Eleanor but they made up in the end. Although Andrew was sad about Katy, he felt his life was less frustrating and a lot happier. Maybe her words were polluting his mindset? After all this, he realized that he should never depend on others.

title: MERCY
text: This is an account of the circumstances that have haunted me to this extend that I’ve decided to press the trigger of the little black thing lying beside me. I’m Venus a simple 20 year old girl.I’d everything that a girl could think of.I’d the best parents in the world. My father died when I was fifteen and since then my mother Athena Bursa had looked after the finance of our lives. Though now both of them are my past.I never believed in ghosts or Gods but I was proved wrong, about gods I can’t say but ghosts – yes they do exist. Three months ago a very strange but insignificant thing started happening at nights. My bedroom lies on the extreme left near the lavatory in the upper floor. It was my custom to study at night but on one of my usual seeming nights the empty flower vase stirred; naturally I didn’t pay any attention. But, night after night the stirring continued getting more intense and long lasting. At first I thought it might be air as it lied just in front of the window. Finally one night I decided to check myself what’s wrong with it. But what waited for me there was, terrorizing. I went up to that vase bathing in the silvery moonlight. I put my hands on the edges of its mouth and felt something warm and wet. I looked at my fingers there was – BLOOD. I’d been reading an email in the moonlight so quickly switched on the lights. There was nothing. I concluded that stress caused me to imagine such things. I started feeling giddy and retired to bed. The following morning my whole body was aching. My next shock followed closely. While bathing I realized that I’ve a deep cut on my back, quickly I came out, and went downstairs to have breakfast. Unable to control my thoughts I asked out my mother. “Mom?” “Yes, dear” “Where did you get that vase from?” “Which vase, the one in your room?” “Yes” My mom turned around and gave an unusual look. “Umm--from an auction of late Sir Alexander Rogers’s possessions.” “That means some 20-25 years ago?” “Yes 10 years after his death when you weren’t even born. I’d a stupid……” The words faded into background as my thoughts shifted to Sir Alexander Rogers. I gobbled up my breakfast and went straight to my friend’s house. Robert was reading a book on ghosts when I entered. “Hi Venus” He greeted as he laid down the book “Hi” “What’s the matter?” I sat on a chair, drank a glass of water and tried to explain myself. “See I don’t know what it is, from past a week the vase in my room kept stirring. Fed up when I checked it had blood on its edged and--and today I realized that I’ve a deep cut on my back and the funniest thing is, there was no blood on my shirt or bed sheets. My told mother me that she bought that vase from an auction of Sir Alexander’s possessions. I don’t know what to do, it sounds so silly but Rob I’m truly scared.” He sat motionless for a span of few minutes, staring at the back of my chair. “See doing anything as quickly as that might not turn out to be justified. Because it’s just been a few weeks let’s see for a little while, till then wear this-” and he took off the crux shaped pendant from round his neck and gave it to me. “This will help you to prevent any physical harm but only physical mentally you’ll have to deal.” I looked at him and nodded. I was lying absent minded on my bed when I heard whispering sound. I sat up and looked about but there was no one. The whispering got nearer, louder and clearer with every second passing. I started precipitating. I wanted to run but wasn’t able to. My mind was getting saturated, my head ached terribly, and it seemed it would burst at any moment. I was screaming like mad at the top of my vice. I was bemused; it felt like hundreds of people were whispering at once. From this crowd of words those words of Rob came at me, “mentally you have to deal” and I tried my best to block the voice, I succeeded a bit, it was working and then suddenly the voice stopped. I ran downstairs and called my mother. “Venus? What’s the matter” it was my sudden impulse but then I felt stupid. “No-nothing, mom called you by mistake.” I kept the receiver down and leaned against a wall, eye closed and bathed in sweat. After that I remember nothing. This series of sufferings continued for months but during that time I learnt to block away the whispering. Sometimes at night I would feel as if something heavy is trying to crush me. I started going to church. Mom was evidently surprised with this sudden change. Rob suggest me ways to deal with the spirit. So eventually I’d an answer to his every call. There was always liberal amount of time when I was alone at home. One day Rob arrived late morning. We were chatting in my room when suddenly I felt as if something fell on my back but it did no harm, whispering started followed by hallucinations. This time I gave up; enemy attacked from three sides. Unable to undergo I screamed- “Who are you? Come out!” Nothing appeared, the pressure decreased, hallucinations ceased and whispering grew fainter. “Come out you coward.” My challenge was answered by a loud, clear, whisper. “I was the one who needed no introduction, everybody knew Alexander Rogers but now I’m more than dead and less than alive. My soul withered, body withered and now this spirit is withering too. Help me Venus Bursa to be accepted by Almighty. Look in that mirror to see me.” I mustered up courage and approached the mirror hanging beside my bed. The reflection of the man I saw was breath taking, elegantly dress, refined face, hair neatly made into a ponytail but one thing he lacked- he was no more than silver mist. “What kind of help you want?” “Sacrifice one of your loved ones.” “Never.” “Think about it.” “Thinking about this cannot take ages.” “It might not be a request next time.” “Are you threatening me?” He said nothing just smirked and vanished. For weeks nothing happened I thought life has gained its old momentum but that smirk haunted me. I wanted to predict his next move. I stared being extremely absent minded, dropping things, leaving them at unexpected places. My greatest comfort was Rob helping me enormously. While cleaning my chest of drawers I found a knife gifted by father. In the second one there was a rope and the third contained a yellowish, decayed piece of paper, those things I didn’t remember keeping there. Next day, I and Rob planned a visit and a two days stay at a distant friend’s house. Those moments were memorable. When I came back I found everything alright. Mom was out. I was tired so i retired to bed. At night, half-awake I hear my mother calling me. I went downstairs, had dinner, answered some general questions and went to bed again. Next morning I woke up late and went downstairs. Everything was just as it was last night. The door was closed that meant mom was in her room which was unusual. I smelt a rat; my heart started beating fast, I was scared and hurried upstairs, opened my mom’s door and saw what I expected. Her lifeless pale figure was hanging from the fan, a knife stabbed in her neck. Blood had dripped down from there. I could see several blood stains on the floor. I moved forward and touched the stains they were dry that meant she was murdered last night but the question was by whom. The windows were closed, door was locked, and mother couldn’t have performed two fatal acts at the same time so it couldn’t be suicide then that left two people me and Sir roger’s spirit. He wouldn’t do it as that wouldn’t get him god’s mercy then the only answer remained was too impossible but I knew the power of that spirit. My eyes caught the decayed piece of paper lying on table. On it with blood it was scribbled: “I told you it won’t come as a request the next time. You gave the sacrifice of your mother unwillingly.” -----Alexander Rogers I looked at my hand, blood covered them. I couldn’t think of a way out and made a phone call and sat down to write a few things. Rob would arrive in a few minutes. He has been my greatest comfort through my hardest times. May God bless him. I’m coming mommy. AFTERMATH Police officials were done tired on reading this account. It seemed fantastic and impossible at the same time. Robert Roderick was traumatized to such an extent that he remembered nothing. He was a complete blank who could throw no light on the matter. Thus, the war ends in a tie were God helped one to save herself but ghost took a life she loved besides her.
author: Pratika  Gupta

title: Near the Stream
text: I attended school, attended tuition, and then came back home. After tuition, at 6 o’clock, I went outside to play. Keira, Avika, and I went to the stream near our street. It was not that far from our homes, just a fifteen minute walk away. It was already dark by the time we reached. It was quite a desolate place. We spent some time talking as we usually do, about school, our classmates, teachers, and anything else. Of course, the usual conversation about the time of April also took place. We noticed the house nearby. We heard bottles breaking. That frightened us and we immediately decided to go back home. The next day, we went there again but this time, earlier. We met at around 5 o’clock. The house near the riverside looked normal except for the windows being broken. The gate was open too, which is odd because Amita aunty, the woman who lives there, prefers to remain alone. Out of curiosity, the three of us decided to investigate. The house was empty so we didn’t see any harm in entering. There were many broken photos on the walls. They were Taashvi’s (Amita Bhatnagar’s daughter’s) childhood pictures. Other than the cracked photos, the rest of the house seemed well maintained. We found Taashvi’s diary as well. Of course we read it, I mean, why wouldn’t we? It was human nature to be curious. Taashvi wrote about how Amita aunty had schizoid personality disorder and her father died only a couple months after she was born.Taashvi wrote about how she felt neglected and for much of her life, felt lost. We felt sad for both Taashvi’s mom and Taashvi herself. We all remembered how sweet and kind Amita aunty was before developing SPD. She had not spoken to anyone in months. Even if anyone tried to get close to her or offer help, she pushed them away. That does not mean she was not able to interact with others at all though. She was always reasonable and careful with her words. She did not bring her emotions into any conversation. She spoke less but when she did, it was always something practical. The last page Taashvi wrote in her diary was three days ago. We decided to go home and ask our parents later about Amita aunty and Taashvi. No one saw them after December 12th. The three of us asked our mothers about the Bhatnagar family. They all told us basically the same thing. Amita aunty came to this town in 1998. She was genuinely a very kind and benevolent person who never hesitated to help others around her. In 2000, after Taashvi was born, Amita aunty began showing signs of SPD. She stopped talking to people and even if she did, it was just with her daughter, Taashvi. She closed herself off from others and rarely left the house. It was around this time that her husband died too. Taashvi has been very alone for her entire life. Most of her time went into dealing with her mom’s silence. Our mothers were close friends of Amita aunty’s. They remember her saying that she had a surprise planned for Taashvi on her 12th birthday. However, they did not know what Amita aunty meant by that. This was a bit creepy because Taashvi’s birthday fell on the 12th of December, the same date both of them were last seen. Before contacting any authorities, Keira, Avika, and I decided to ruminate about this on our own. We remember playing with Taashvi when we were younger. Taashvi seemed like any other normal kid but she always avoided talking about her home life. So, we could always sense that something was wrong. But since we were kids, we didn’t give it much thought. “Thank you. It wasn’t easy on your end. But I don’t see a reason to let you go. Amita Bhatnagar” All three of us were in shock and we did not have any clear idea of what to do. First, we informed our parents. They then called the police. It took a few hours for them to reach us as we live in a remote town. Regardless, when the task force did arrive, they began interrogation. They questioned my friends and I, our parents, and Amita aunty’s maid. She stopped working there years ago. There wasn’t much any of us could tell them. All we knew is that Amita aunty had SPD, Taashvi had a troubled childhood, and her husband died a couple months after Taashvi was born. This incident happened 3 years ago. To this day, all we know is that the body was Taashvi’s. This has been declared as a cold case.

title: Nature's Treasure
text: I shouted. Taylor and I were both ready to leave, our luggage already loaded in the jeep, waiting for the carefree fashionista, as usual. "Okay, okay, I'm here", she said stumbling down the front steps while running her hand through her freshly washed and blow-dried hair. "Please don't tell me you made us wait for half an hour just to fix your hair", I lamented. "No... Okay.... maybe, but not everyone has maintenance-free hair like you Sofia ", She said pointing to my dirty blond cropped hair. T aylor silently rolled her eyes, knowing full well that she couldn't stay mad at the cute and gentle puppy-faced girl for longer than a few minutes. Taylor herself was the no-nonsense girl who could be extra intimidating and was, befittingly, a cop. And me, well I was a nature scientist and conservation enthusiast. The three of us have been as thick as thieves since High School and though life had taken us different ways, we had kept up with the tradition of an annual holiday. So, over the last ten years, we'd gone scuba diving in Australia, bungee jumping in South Africa, hiking in Thailand, camping in Scotland and had our fair share of Paris and Milan fashion weeks. Each of these experiences had been wonderful and thrilling, all the more for the company of my two friends. This year, it was me and my love for both nature and adventure that brought us all here, to this cabin in a remote village of the Himalayas, thousands of miles away from our home. Here, we had spent the last three days, rejuvenating and acclimatizing for the high altitude climb. “Come on. Let’s hurry!” said Taylor, rousing me from my reverie. “Yes, we should get a move on if we want to reach the Palda campsite before nightfall”, I agreed. I took the wheel as we drove towards the base camp while Taylor rode shotgun and Kiara lounged on the back seat for her beauty sleep on the three hour drive from Bhuntar to Rumzu base camp. We reached the clearing, parked the jeep, lugged our bags out of the boot and stretched our limbs getting ready for the six hour trek. The hike was pretty easy till the Malana river bridge and we enjoyed the serenity of the surroundings, the magic of the chilly wind, the lush greenery and the snow-capped mountains in the background. At the bridge, we found some hikers huddled together, deep in discussion. The bridge was closed due to some damage it endured during a storm last night. The river water was rough and rapid and there was no alternative route so they planned to turn back. We were disappointed but refused to turn around without some serious thought. We were a little tired as well, so we sat down to rest for a while. Unsure of what to do next; I was contemplating some options when Taylor declared, “We should continue the trek.” She was looking intently at the old washed out map I had stumbled upon during a 'Save the Turtles Campaign' at the Kamilo Beach a few years ago. "I think the map shows an alternative route. See the map shows another trail a little farther from the bridge. We've got time to explore." As we geared up, Kiara bundled the plastic wrappers of the big packet of crisps and the pound cake we had devoured earlier and threw them in a nearby ditch. “Oh Kiara, don’t do that! Being an environmentalist’s best friend hasn’t changed you a bit”, I said exasperatedly, and picked the wrappers shoving them in my backpack. For an hour, we walked in search of the trail, but in vain. There was no way we could cross that raging river without a bridge. I searched the map again for some clue but most of the markings were faded beyond comprehension. Disappointed, I closed my eyes and let out a long sigh. That's when I heard someone whisper. “She’s here.” “She’s got the map”, another voice added. “Who said that? Did you guys hear it?” I asked looking around. “What?” Taylor said, narrowing her eyes at me. “ We’re the Prahiri. Follow the trail. Look for the signs ”, the voice said again. “Enough, guys”, I said suspecting the girls were playing a prank on me. And then, I perceived the branches of an oak tree rustling in the wind, its leaves falling off, and maybe I had actually gone crazy but I thought they made an arrow pointing north. Impulsively, I started walking northward. When Taylor and Kiara started following me, I was already a few metres ahead of them. After about 10 minutes, I noticed some tree branches swishing in the wind, only there wasn’t the slightest breeze. I went closer and pulled back a branch to witness one of the most beautiful sights I had ever laid my eyes upon. The colourful blossoms went on for miles and miles; dots of red, yellow, orange, blue, purple and pink as far as the eye could see. I stood spell bound, rooted to the ground. “What are you staring at Sofia?” Taylor asked moving a little closer. She too was speechless as she witnessed the breathtaking view in front of us. “Oh My GOD!! This is just gorgeous”, Kiara jumped with joy, nudging me out of the way. We sat there in silence, mesmerized by the beautiful spread of colours. The sun was setting on the horizon, painting the sky a million shades of hazel, golden and red; giving the blossoms a warm ethereal glow. We couldn’t go back now, so we quickly found a clearing and set up our tents. Before turning in for the night, we sat gazing at the stars when a streak of white shot across the sky, followed by another and then another. So we sat there together under the heavens, watching the magical meteor shower. Reluctantly, we climbed into our sleeping bags, still awestruck, to catch some z’s before tomorrow’s journey. “Sofia… Wake up Sofia…”someone whispered softly in my ear. I woke up with a start and saw a swarm of fireflies hovering over me. Impulsively, I followed them towards the hill behind us. They suddenly seemed to disappear behind a rock. On a closer look, I realized that it was the entrance of a cave. I was a little skeptical at first, but my curiosity got the better of me. Besides, the Prahiri hadn’t led me astray yet. The inside of the cave was bathed in a shimmering blue light; glow worms illuminating the path. I could hear water falling somewhere nearby. The winding passage led to a huge chamber with a pond in the centre. Ghost lilies flanked the edge of the pool, which was filled with huge lotus flowers. Moonlight peaked through a hole in the roof creating an ethereal atmosphere. There was a stone pedestal in the middle of the pond and water trickled onto what looked like an altar. Entranced, I looked for a way to reach it. “ Step on the leaves. They’ll hold your weight. ” I took a careful step, and surprisingly it held. I stepped on leaves like they were stepping stones and reached the pedestal; just as a beam of the full moon touched what I realized was a plant on the altar. The huge bud opened to reveal a majestic white bloom. To say it was beautiful was an understatement. It was mystic, magnificent… almost sacred. “This is the Night-blooming Cereus, one of the few left. It blooms only once a year”, the Prahiri whispered in my ear. “It is… ”, I started but my words failed to describe the scene my eyes beheld. " Why me?" was a question lurking in my mind. "You care for us. You are our savior. It's our way of thanking you for the work you are doing", my unspoken query was answered. It was true, for the past five years, I’d toured the world, launching initiatives to help rejuvenate our environment, stop the incessant plunder of its resources and conserve habitats of rare flora and fauna. The flourishing nature and it's miracles like this one were my reward. So I sat there and marveled at 'The Night Queen' until it shed its petals and folded its leaves. As the first rays of sunlight dawned, I headed back to our tent. The girls were sleeping peacefully, oblivious to the treasure I had discovered in the lap of nature When Taylor roused me from my slumber the next morning, I wondered if I had really witnessed the spectacle, because if truth be told; it sure felt like a dream. But then a light breeze fanned my face whispering "It wasn't a dream."

title: THE RED SHOE
text: There lived a small girl Malli in a village playing with her pet dog named Jacky. While playing saw a beautiful butterfly and followed it. Following the butterfly they reached a thick forest. The path led to a beautiful palace, where Malli found a treasure box. She carried the box to her home. She informed her mother Anamika about the incident and opened the box to check. There found a beautiful RED SHOE inside the box. Suddenly a genie came from the shoe, Malli and her mother were scared seeing it. Genie consoled them and made them comfortable. Genie Narrated her story. Her name was Alexandra, princess of the palace and favourite of her parents which made jealously among her siblings. Her parents gifted her RED shoe on her birthday. Siblings always hated her because she was the favourite of her parents. On the way to kingdom Alexandra's parents were killed by the robbers. Due to which Alexandra became sad and even her siblings started to hurt her and made her sick After some time she was not able to bear the pain and died and her soul departed and rested in her favourite RED SHOE. Listening to the story Malli and her mother felt sad and wanted to do something. After that they took care of the RED SHOE as a treasure. Malli and her mother learnt a moral to love each other. And they spread the message to the whole village, the importance of caring, love and affection.

title: Growth
text: Sometimes I just want my kids to stay the same, and never grow from what they are now, not that I don't want them to grow up, I just want them to be my little infants, like how they were. Even if they grow old, I would still see them as newborns. Saying this I feel like it was just yesterday when I became a father, I have such vibrant memories of the good times, the best of the times. But time will never stay the same, the good times will pass, the new times will come, and so on, and as time has passed my children have grown up, grown up a lot. But sometimes I feel that this growth has stolen away my kids, stolen away the childhood from them. Growth is like the middle name of childhood. Even the oldest person alive was once a child, maybe a child with a snot nose. This growth is inevitable and may be a good thing. But does this growth mean that we have to become distant? I don't know why, but it feels like we have drifted slowly apart. It's as if we have become distant as time has passed. I got married almost twenty years ago and being from a hidebound family, I almost had no say in my marriage and neither did my wife. I was still working under someone who practiced law. I worked as a trainee when I got married, in those times not having a good job wasn’t a hindrance in one’s marriage, all that mattered were the characteristics of someone, whether external or internal. Eventually, we got married, and now I had a family to raise, become stable enough to support my newly built family became my goal. And I worked towards it. Two years later I completed my studies and I became an advocate in the very law firm i used to train. We moved away, it was a two-room apartment and I felt ashamed, ashamed of letting my kids grow into such closed spaces, what if they didn’t like it? What if they grew up feeling little of themselves, feeling little of me? But thankfully I was wrong, thankfully. I had thought it was a small house, as my family consisted of me, my wife, and my twins. “Just two rooms for four people?” this is what I used to think all the time. I was proved wrong as my kids grew up, actually, they never complained, we lived in that house for six years. When they were kids they used to play a lot, with me most of the time. There was one part of the house that even I liked and it was the balcony, and from there you get a clear view of the neighborhood park. On this side of the balcony, there was this sliding glass window, and through that, the sunlight made its way every day. My daughter hated the sunlight when she was little, she’d always shut her eyes tight. But as she grew she got used to it, back then she couldn’t open her eyes in the sun and now she could, she got used to it. I noticed this subtle growth and felt proud. But maybe I ignored the most visible form of growth. Our interactions. As they grew older, our interactions became more formal, briefer, and straightforward. As kids, they used to share everything with me, everything. And whenever they did, I got assured that they had trust in me. But as they grew there came secrets, things they thought couldn’t tell me. Now that I think of it, I hate it. Like what’s there in a friend that one can confide in but not with their own parents. I feel like me and my wife were so busy securing the future of our kids that we forgot to nourish their present, we played, traveled, and enjoyed together, but never ever confronted our kids about this lack of correspondence. They say that you can relive your childhood through your kids and let me tell you, it is true, you relive your entire childhood through your children, and I could feel everything that they felt, or maybe most of it, the joy when having something good or when on a stroll, the excitement on festivals, even the pain they felt when they got hurt and yes, the crying part. There’s one thing that no parent can stand and that is the sight of their kid crying. When they cried I used to feel powerless and scared and wanted to do anything in my power that’d them stop from crying. It's just I was never good at it. When you reach your home, late from work you don't expect your kids to stay awake, but at our home, it's a common sight. The sight of my son doing his random things has become a habit, and that too to such an extent that now it doesn’t bother me as long as he wakes up early to catch his bus. Yesterday, knowing that I would be getting late I got some ice creams. I went up to him and said “Look I got you to ice crea-” He cut me by saying “I am studying, not now.” “Oh, you and studies.?” I scoffed and as I said this I prepared myself to face the wrath of my son but surprisingly he didn’t say a thing. “Come on just eat it and go,” I said, persuading him as if I were a trickster and as soon as he’d follow me to get his ice creams I would kidnap him. “No, I can’t,” he said. It felt as if I was talking to a calm monk or something and not my own son, not my childish son who’d get angry over anything. ﻿﻿ What an irony as a father. I was waiting for my son to get angry with me, and when he didn’t, it somewhat saddened me, maybe my kids have really grown up, “have they matured already?” I watched the tv wondering this, absent-mindedly eating my ice cream in a cup and then I passed out. I woke by a warm breeze on my face, a certain someone’s breath, it stank. It was my son sitting beside me, scooping out the melted ice cream I had in my hand. My kids still haven’t grown up.
author: Vibhu Tanay

title: Adorable LYRA - The dog
text: Emma is a sweetheart, who brings the family joy with all of her adorable small victories. She became 4 years old. Her father enrolled her in school. She was attending school regularly and taking pleasure in her education. After a few days, Emma developed a fever and was unable to continue living. Mother suffered from sadness and became quite depressed, avoiding her socializing. To get the mother out of her sadness, the father once brought a charming small puppy, whom he called Lyra. Mother, however, did not first like Lyra. She used to only carry out her obligation to feed the dog, But Lyra used to show her parents such adoration. It frequently played with the father, but when it tried to play with the mother, she would ignore and keep away of it. However, Lyra used to be kind to her mother and would always sit next to her, even when she was working in the kitchen. As the days went by, one day, Lyra was laying in a garage corner, as mother was cleaning the garage, father walked outside. In an instant, Lyra jumped up and began to look about curiously. It began barking vigorously to warn the mother of the threat. But mother ignored it and told it not to bark. With the purpose of bringing the mother out of the garage, Lyra began to tug the mother's clothing. In an effort to get rid of Lyra, Mother began to beat her. However, Lyra persisted, and it began acting as though it were about to bite its mother. She believed Lyra became enraged and was angry towards it. Mother rushed from the garage in an effort to protect herself from Lyra. The garage suddenly collapsed as soon as she exited the room. Mother observed this and realised Lyra acted in that manner to safeguard her. She gave Lyra a grateful embrace after feeling deeply sorry for how she had treated her. When her father returned, she went through everything with him. They both continued to live happy lives with Lyra.
author: Chadalavada Devasuvarshini
