title: THE CAMEL AND THE FOX
text: The camel and the fox were very good friends and very good thieves. One day, the two friends decided to cross the river so that they could travel to a nearby farm to steal food. The small fox could not swim so the camel said to his friend, "Climb up onto my back and I will swim across the river". And so the fox climbed up onto the the camel's back and the strong camel swam across the river to the other side. When they had crossed the river, the camel and the fox made their way to the farm. When they finally arrived at the farm, the fox caught himself a chicken while the camel dug up some lovely fresh vegetables. The greedy fox quickly gobbled down his chicken and then said to his friend the camel," when I finish eating I am accustomed to singing". " do not sing just yet",said the camel as he was chewing his dinner of vegetables. "I have not yet finished eating and if you sing then farmer will hear you". "Let me first finish my dinner and then you can sing as we make our way back home". But the fox did not pay any attention to his friend and began to sing at the top of his voice. The farmer soon heard this singing and came running out of his house waving a large stick. " I will teach you how to steal from me!" exclaimed the angry farmer. Because the fox was so small and nimble, he was able to run away from the farmer. But the poor camel was very slow and still in the middle of eating his dinner and so he did not see the farmer until it was too late. The angry farmer sat upon the camel with large stick and the poor camel received many blows to his legs and back before he was finally able to escape. When the camel reached the river, his bones ached and he was very upset with his friend, the fox. " Why did you sing when you knew that farmer would hear you and you can see that I was still eating my dinner?" asked the camel. "Because it is my custom" replied the fox in his matter-of-fact way. "Now let me climb upon your back so that we may return to our home across the river". Then the camel walked slowly down the river bank into the water and began to swim across to the other side with the fox upon his back. When the camel was halfway across the river, at the point where water was at its deepest and current as its fastest, he stopped swimming and said to the fox, "When I have finished eating I am accustomed to taking a bath". "Do not take a bath" said the fox. "I cannot swim and if you take a bath I shall drown!" I am very sorry," said the camel,but I always take a bath after I have eaten." It is my custom". And with that the camel lowered his back into the deep water until the fox lost his grip on his back and began to splash around helplessly against the fast current. "Help me!" cried the desperate fox. " I am drowning, I am drowning!" the camel asked the fox,"Are you sorry that you were so selfish and caused to be beaten by the farmer? "." Yes, Yes, I am truly sorry!" cried the fox just before her head disappeared once more beneath the surface of the water. The camel did not had the heart to watch his friend drown in the river and so he pulled the little fox out of the water and placed him upon his back. Then the camel swam the rest of the way across the river and climbed up the bank and onto the warm grass. The fox realized that he had been very selfish and said to his friend, "I am so sorry for what I did and I promise that you can trust me forever". "and I am sorry that I had to teach you a lesson today,but many times in life it is often a case of tit for tat". Then the two friends began to laugh and roll around the warm grass while the sun dried their wet fur. The fox had learnt a valuable lesson that day. He had learnt that it was not good to betray a friend, and that if you do wrong by somebody then somebody might will do wrong by you MORAL:As you sow so shall you reap.
author: mannat manchanda

title: Animal Bullying
text: I am an animal lover. All my life I have loved and have brought home animals to save, keep and nurture. But this particular story is about the dark hearts of human beings that torture and tyrannize animals. This story is about Darsy, a four year old Indian that I saved from wretched owner. Darsy lived on the street over from mine. My daughter was friends with a heavy, shy girl who lived in a dysfunctional environment. My daughter, Olivia, noticed that there family dog was in horrible condition. She was dirty, ribs showing and scratched non - stop. But the worst thing was her eye. Darsy was viciously attacked by the family's cat who clawed her eye. The cat's claw dug deep into Darsy's eye,not only causing excruciating pain, but blinding her as well. Olivia also learned that they were not feeding her. Darsy was dying. Her one luxurious fur fell out until you could see her blotchy, red skin from her constant itching. Infested with fleas, she was miserable. She also had a raging ear infection, adding to discomfort and pain. Despite this all this, the little sweetheart craved affection and just a little love. When I learned that the poor dog was living in this kind of pain and suffering. I was livid. How could anyone do this to another living creature? I told mu daughter to go over and ask if she could have the suffering animal. She was told in these exact words," Take her, no one here wants her anyway." So, here she was, in my house with my three dogs and when I looked at her, I couldn't believe what I saw. Darsy's ribs were standing out and her hipbones were just about jutting through her skin. Her eye, bulging out to point of falling out, was horrid. Fleas crawled on just about every inch of her. I held her to my chest and cried. I decided to give her a flea bath right away as not to infest my healthy, clean animals and her skin feel better. I put flea medication on and immediately made an appointment with Ney vet. Considering the urgency of the situation, she was able to be seen that day. I was given meds for her eye, her ear and skin and told that she needs immediate surgery. I couldn't afford such a surgery. I put Darsy's picture and story on Facebook in hopes to find a sponser for the expensive operation. I got so lucky! A woman contacted me with a picture of Darsy when she was healthy! Dog feces and vomit everywhere, and the smell alone was not enough to make anyone sick. She said that she spent the night there when was needed to care for the woman's daughter and she was so bitten up by the fleas the next day, she vomited. She had no clue that shew was being starved to death or that her eye was injured beyond repair. She made some phone calls and behold, we hooked up with the right people and found a vet about fifty miles away willing to not only do the surgery for half price. But do it before he got paid. He told us that never had he seen a dog so close to death. He couldn't believe how heartless some pet owners could be. Darsy not only had her eye surgery but she also sprayed dewormed, nails cut and medicine given to me for her eyes etc. It's price could be of rupees 30,000 but this big hearted vet only charged us rupees 5,000. Now,Mollie has been with me for last five months. She has gained weight and her fur looks better. Today Mollie is a healthy, happy' pain free dog. All pets deserve a chance to be loved and taken care of. Mollie was lucky, but there are others out there who are unlucky. Be a hero today and save dogs' life.
author: MANAV SHARMA

title: PETER WITH HIS GRANDMA
text: "PETER!Come here and help grandma to feed the birds dear..."said Peter's grandma with a smile. He was spending his summer vacation with his beloved Grandma. Every year he spends the summer vacation with her but this year his mother didn't accompany with him to go Grandma's house.. He ran to Grandma and grabbed the bowl of grain.He enjoyed feeding the birds and the birds also enjoyed while eating. 'Why were you looking sad?'his Grandma asked. "that's because I was thinking about my mom''said Peter with a down voice. '''Come on!She'll come here after two days... She had work in her office,that is why she is not here now..I'll tell you some interesting stories!Grandma smiled saying.' ''YES!I am eagerly waiting to hear the stories Grandma! She told him the stories of animals,plants and many many other stories which contained the moral ''how to be a good living being''. Hea ring the stories,made the boy feel that he had to chan ge a lot to become a good boy. He hugged Grandma and kissed her.He also thanked her and asked her if she can make him some toys using bamboo.She smiled and nodded.She made many toys for him.He played with the toys happily. When the sun was about to set,they watched a mother bird giving food to her babies. PETER murmured''When will Mom come?Who knows?''. Two days later h is Mom came. When he heard her car's sound,he rushed to the front door. His Mom opened the car's door and hugged him and Grandma. ''Hurray! now we can enjoy the vacation with Mom.Right Grandma?''said Peter. ''Yeah!Absolutely!!!!! Peter,his Mom and Grandma went inside the house happily.....
author: Aamina  PM
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Jayesh Sivan; Nirzara Verulkar

title: HELP! I'M ALONE!!
text: During the 1950s, when India announced that they were independent and were not under British rule, India also reported the extinction of Wild Asian Cheetahs from the country. This was a great loss for the Indian Society and Ecosystem. And since all stories must perforce begin with a ‘once upon a time, so too does this one. Once upon a time, there was a Cheetah named Sandy. He was among the last few cheetahs left. The other cheetahs lived in other parts of India. He was the only Cheetah who was left in his entire state. If he died, the entire population of Wild Asian Cheetahs would get extinct in India. He was kept in a Biosphere Reserve so that he could be protected. One day, As Sandy was walking alone on the path of the grassland, a memory struck his mind. He was thinking about how he and his siblings would fight for nothing and would complain about each other to their parents. They would get a good scolding from their parents for doing such mischiefs, but they would still be happy with each other. They had a competing mind, that if one of the siblings got the punishment, he/she will make sure that all other siblings get the same punishment or a bigger punishment than theirs. Sandy also starts remembering how he got separated from his happy family and happy life. He was one day just simply playing (or we can say fighting) with his siblings. He was very young; he did not know how to hunt animals. He and his siblings saw a butterfly, that was flying above their heads. The butterfly was having fun making the cubs run behind her. She continued playing with them until they all unnoticeably went too far away from Sandy’s parents. Their parents were very worried. They informed everyone they knew to look out for their children. But it was too late. Till then Sandy and his siblings had gone too far. As they were mere children, they did not even know how to return home. The butterfly was very guilty for making the cubs lose their way home. She ran away. The cubs were left all on themselves. They were very scared. They started praying to God to take them back to their parents. Suddenly, they heard a herd coming near them. It was the cackle of Hyenas. Hyenas usually feed on baby cheetahs or cubs. The children started panicking. Soon, they were surrounded by hyenas. They started shouting and screaming for help. One of their uncles was passing from a distance when he suddenly heard the cries of the children. He hurried to the place with some more cheetahs and started attacking. While the big fight was going on between cheetahs and the hyenas, a group of humans arrived with rifles and guns for hunting. This was a significant threat, even bigger than that of the hyenas. Even the bigger Cheetahs could not handle the situation. All the animals fled for their lives, including Sandy and his siblings. All the animals went in numerous directions. All the siblings got separated in this chaos. Sandy was all alone now. He found himself near a cave with no one around. He took shelter there. He found some plants and herbs, on which he fed and lived there for nearly 1-2 months. Time passed. Now he was grown enough to be ready to hunt and arrange his food. He took his steps out of the cave and this was a bold step toward his new journey. HE went a little further, he found A FEW animals drinking water and talking about the hunters who had come 1 month before and how they had killed several animals. Sandy was shocked to hear this news and ran towards the animals and asked them what had happened. They told HIM ABOUT THE INCIDENT. They also told him that the hunter had killed all the cheetahs in the forest and said that they were surprised to see Sandy. Sandy was heartbroken after hearing all this. He kept walking in a straight line without looking here and there. HIS MIND was TOTALLY blank and did not know what to do. He kept on walking and walking until he reached his home. He was overjoyed hoping to see his parents and siblings. He jumped and went inside but found no one there. He then realized that all his family and friends had also been killed by those ruthless and stonehearted humans. Sandy was enraged but helpless. He could not do anything. If he took a step against humans, they would kill him too, so he decided not to do anything. He never talked to anybody. As soon as he would get his prey, he would take it back to his original home, eat it, and weep day and night. One day, while Sandy was eating his lunch, he saw some humans coming. He got infuriated, but then, he had a second thought. He calmed himself and kept himself indoors only. Even by doing so, he could not be saved from the humans. This time humans had come to his home to take him to a Biosphere reserve so that he could be protected. While Sandy was being transported to the Reserve, he overheard the humans talking to each other. He heard them talking that how because of the carelessness of humans, the wild Asian cheetahs got endangered. Even after sending the cheetahs to the endangered species category, humans did not get satisfaction. They kept hunting them illegally, and now we are in such a crucial stage that only 1 cheetah is left in the entire country. Sandy was flabbergasted on hearing this. After reaching the reserve, he would not treat normally. He would rarely be seen out of his house. He would only come out of hunting and then take the prey back to his home. He would often get ill. He would not even meow. He would only get enraged when he would see humans, who would come to treat him. He needed to be given medicine which would make a fall asleep for some time, during which he would be treated. By seeing this dullness in Sandy and the anger he had when seeing humans, the people working in the reserve got a little tensed. They thought that this behavior is not at all a good sign. The authorities tried hard for making the cheetah happy but failed miserably. Sandy would not budge even a bit. But slowly, Sandy also started feeling that all humans are not the same. Some are cruel, but some are light-hearted as well. Sometimes, Sandy pitied himself. He remembered all the sacrifices he had made, how he learned to become independent. All these things made him proud, but also made him very sad. So, he started giving a positive reaction to the authority's efforts. He started playing a little with the workers. This brought some hope to the workers. They played with him every day. They could also see a lot of changes in Sandy’s behavior. They could see that Sandy would not stay inside his house the whole day, he would go out and try to be friends with the other fellow animals. He was successful, but still, he couldn't share all his feelings with his new friends. But he never complained. While thinking these incidents in his life, he reached home. He was not feeling quite well that day. So, he went to take rest. But after some time, he started having severe stomach pain, he was feeling great difficulty in breathing. After calling the authorities by meowing, he fainted. He was immediately taken to the vet. The vet told them that the cheetah was no more. He had died. When they asked the reason, the vet told them that the cheetah was depressed. He had faced so many problems in the past, that now he was not able to take care of his health. The authorities were dejected and downhearted after hearing this, but they had to accept the fact that their friend was no more. But to have his memory with them always, they built a small statue of him in their office. CHEETAH REINTRODUCTION IN INDIA Reintroduction of the cheetah in India involves the re-establishment of a population of cheetahs into areas where they had previously existed but were hunted into extinction during and after the Mughal Period, Rajput and Maratha Indian royalty and later by the British Raj, until the early 20th century when only several thousand remained.
author: Niyanta Shri
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; André Kieswetter; Jagdish Joshi; Kishor Joshi; Maithili  Joshi; Marion  Drew; Partho Sengupta; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Rajasee Ray; Raju Babu Shakya; Rob Owen; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Sweta  Roy Choudhury; Thanuja Dilhani; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya; Vishnu  M Nair; Wiehan de Jager

title: Best Friend's Secret Magic
text: Aaisha and Aayna were best friends. Really best friends!! They had one other friend. And that was an apple tree! Yes, they both really loved the tree and also the apples from it. And they spent all their free time under it. Both Aaisha and Aayna were really shy and often stayed away from other kids. But they were very bright so, some children were jealous of them. Those kids tried to demean the two besties in every way possible, which included stealing their notebooks, breaking their pens, throwing their tiffin and many other horrible things. But they still had each other to lean on. And, of course, their apple tree!! One day, the bullies thought of a plan to hurt their apple tree! They broke the branches, injured the stem and stole the apples. Oh, how devastated the two were! They planned to take revenge the next day. But little did they know that the tree had already done it! They had planned to confront the bullies and complain to their class teacher. But they found out that all of them had been seriously injured. Turned out, the broken branches of the tree had beaten and injured them. Add the complaint, and their revenge was done!! They had really paid the bullies back. The bullies were silent for a few days but eventually, the bullying restarted. Poor things, they did not know what to do! They decided to meet under the apple tree. It was six o' clock. Aaisha had already arrived and was waiting for Aayna. Suddenly, she noticed a bully throwing a stone at a squirrel and knocking it down. She quickly picked it up. By that time, Aayna had also arrived. "Hi Aaisha!", she said. " Hi Aayna! Do you know what those awful bullies did? They knocked this poor squirrel down with a stone.", said Aaisha. "Oh! Poor thing. Let's help it.", Aayna replied. They took it to Aaisha's home and bandaged its leg. The apple tree (yes, the apple tree) was really enraged by the actions of the bullies. The girls named the squirrel Arcana. Arcana soon became the pet of both girls. One day, the teacher divided the class into pairs and announced a poetry competition. She said that they would have to write about their pet and that the best pair would be selected for the inter-school competition. Aaisha and Aayna wrote a poem on Arcana. They were really happy about their poem. The day of result came. The two besties were eagerly waiting for their results when the teacher announced that they had been selected!! It was great news for them, but not so much for the bullies, who were more jealous than ever. The teacher told them that the topic for inter-school competition was 'Friendship'. They decided to meet under the apple tree with Arcana and discuss. Looking at Arcana running around, they got an idea! "Why don't we write a poem on our friendship with Arcana and the apple tree?", suggested Aaisha. "Great idea!!", exclaimed Aayna. They finalised the poem and had written it when one of the bullies threw paint on it and laughed loudly. But the paint did not reach the poem. There was a magical shield around it. But neither the bully nor the girls could understand what had happened. Surprised, the bully went away. Aaisha and Aayna were really relieved. They submitted the poem to the teacher and she praised them for their effort. She read their poem out in class, which the bullies didn't like. The bullies then decided to hurt the girls' dearest pet, Arcana!! They kidnapped her when the girls were at school. But Arcana was not hurt. Rather, the bullies could not even touch her. Defeated, they returned Arcana to her tree. At first, when the girls found her missing during recess, they completely panicked. But they were relieved to find her scampering up to them after school. They hugged each other and petted Arcana lovingly when she was found. The next day, the teacher announced the results of the inter-school competition. And guess what! Aaisha and Aayna's poem had won the first prize!! They had a party under the apple tree to celebrate their success. The tree was really happy for them. But a bully sneaked up on them and was about to break their jar of apple jelly when he tripped, fell and got hurt. The girls didn't even know about this. They continued making their apple pie. The tree protected them yet again! Likewise whenever they were bullied or someone tried to hurt the tree or their pet, the apple tree always took care of the bully. Aaisha and Aayna continued to read great books, write great poems, be great pet lovers and great friends!! And they didn't know about their tree's secret magic!!
author: Anuska Nandi
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Chathurika Jayasooriya; Ketan Raut; Lavanya  Naidu; Sanjay Sarkar; Srija Preethi

title: The Unusual Switch
text: "This maths problem is so tough! How am I supposed to do it!", I grumbled as I glared into the problem written in my book. "I can't form the equation!", I got angry as I threw the pen on my desk. I was trying to solve the maths problem, but every time I tried, I failed miserably. I felt that the Goddess of Luck was probably sleeping as I tried to form the equation. I came to the conclusion that I would never solve this problem in this manner- I had to ask Amma for help. I raced to the kitchen. "Amma, can you help me do this question?", I asked. "Let me see, oh this is simple..." and within just 15 minutes, I knew how to do the question. She made everything clear and when I did similar questions, it was like a cakewalk. FINALLY! I felt like conquered the Mount Everest. "Amma, you know, being a student is hard... you have to do so so many questions, and get so many home works!", I began. "Well I was a student before doing my job, right? But you should know, that student life is so easy, compared to the life of adults", Amma said. "But adults don't have to study, and life would be so simple!", I said. "You feel so as you don't know the pressures faced by adults", Amma said sternly. "I want to be an adult!", I shouted. You cannot just BECOME an adult!", Amma yelled back. Look, I started a heated debate with my mother, but I had to retire soon, as it was past my bedtime; and you know what, I am pretty obedient when it comes to rules. "I wish I was an adult", I said quietly as I drifted off to sleep. I woke up with the sound of my alarm going off. I did my morning chores and went to the dining room. "Amma, can you please give me my breakfast, I'm hungry", I called out. "What Amma? YOU give me MY breakfast", a familiar voice replied. I looked behind and I was horrified. My own mother was standing there, in my uniform. "Aren't you supposed to be my mother?", I asked. "No, you're my mother, and give me my breakfast NOW!", yes, now I see where I got my stubbornness from! It was at this moment I realised, that I was an adult. "Oh god, what should I do!", I shrieked. On one side, I'm an adult, and on the other side I have my own mother, who claims to be my daughter, just standing there with a confused expression. I ran to the kitchen. "Okay, Dosa batter is all I need", I thought as I looked in the fridge. I took the thing out, and tried to make a Dosa for my mother. Every time I tried to make it, it either got burnt, or stuck to the tawa. And I ran out of batter. Again, the Goddess of Luck was sleeping as I tried to make the Dosa. "Okay, calm down me", I motivated myself. By the utter motivation, I made a sandwich. To be honest, it's not due to the motivation. It is merely because, the only thing I know to make properly, is a sandwich. After the battle in the kitchen, I took my mother to the bus stop to board the school bus. I got curious, was this change only for me? Out of doubt, I looked inside the bus. The parents of all my friends were in the bus instead of them. Ah, yes, I'm not the only one having this change! I felt better. "Oh god, I almost burned down the kitchen", I sighed. "Wait, as I'm an adult, I'll have to go to Amma's office!", well, now, the problem is this job. Amma is a software engineer. "Oh no! I don't even know how to do a simple code in Python!", I yelled. "I will probably destroy her laptop!", I yelled again, like a mad person. Well, I'll just call her manager, and tell him that I'm very very sick. Okay, I can just add on little lies, like, I can't even stand up. I was very satisfied with my plan, only to be disappointed in the end. It turned out that Amma and her co-workers had a very important meeting, with an even more important client. I was in trouble. Such big trouble, from which not even my ancestors could save me from this messed situation. I had no other way out. So, I took my mother's laptop and the necessary items, and set off for the office. In the office, I saw the children of all the employees. Again, I felt relieved that I wasn't the only one who is going to get in trouble. All of us were panicking. However, we had no other choice. We got into the meeting room. We started the presentation, we fumbled, and most importantly... we had no idea what we were telling. You can guess, well, we messed up really well. The client got very angry and went away, telling that he would never ever consult this company. The manager got even more angry, and he started yelling at us. Every single one of us got an earful, to be more precise, more than an earful from him. He punished us, and also told that he would cut our salary. I got very sad. I sat down on a chair... and cried. Because of me, my mother lost an important client, and got her salary cut too. I cried, and cried, and cried.. "Oh my good god!", I screamed. I looked around and around... okay, I was in my room. Is it a dream, or reality? Should I go to school, or to Amma's office? As I sat pondering, Amma came into my room. "Amma, tell me, are you going to school?", I asked. "What? Have you gone mad in the morning itself?! This 40-year old me should go to school? Stop saying stupid things, and go get ready", Amma scolded me. "Amma, I'm so sorry that I argued with you yesterday. I now understand that being an adult is tough", I said, hugging Amma tightly. "Well, good for you", Amma said smiling widely.
author: Anadya Prashanth
illustrator: Aakanksha Mittra; Smitha Shivaswamy; Yuvaka  Srestha; Yuwak  Shrestha; Zaheer Merchant

title: The Pocketmoney
text: Vicky was a 11 year old boy who lived in Pune with his parents and his younger Nicky. Vicky and Nicky both used to fight but they loved each other. They both were very fond of remote control toys. When Vicky saw that his friends had more such toys than him he felt very bad. They both wanted to buy such toys but he was confused how he would convince his parents for that. When he started following his friends, gradually his unnecessary wishes increased day by day. After thinking a lot he came to this conclusion that instead of convincing his parents he should fulfill his demands by his own. Still, he was puzzled..because he didn't know where to arrange money from. He could only see one way which was - if his parents should grant him pocket-money every month. He decided to talk to his parents about pocket-money. He didn't waste a single minute in thinking and directly went to his parents. When he asked them, they agreed. Their reply brought a mischievous smile on his face. Then he asked his father how much pocket-money per month he would get. After thinking for a short while his father said, "You will get rupees five hundred." Vicky's happiness knew no bounds. Now he had started purchasing toys like his friends. But his friends were always two steps ahead of him. His desire to match their life style led to increase in his expenses even more. Now he had spent all of his pocket-money only in 15 days. So, he required more pocket-money to fulfill is unessential desires. Then he asked for more pocket-money from his father. After hearing this his father got shocked and speechless. His father didn't reply. Vicky gloomily left from there. His father and mother thought about this matter. Next day, his father deposited some more pocket-money in his piggybank. Their act supported his bad spirit. After 10 days he again asked for more pocket-money. But now his father got filled with sudden anger and rebuked him because Vicky's spendthriftness affected their monthly budget. Vicky felt very bad by not receiving the amount and confined himself to his room.. His father and mother decided that they would teach a lesson to him as he was no more a responsible child. Next day, his parents said to him l, "We will give you some tasks everyday and if you would complete them only then you would get pocket-money." Vicky only wanted pocket-money so he agreed happily. His mother asked him to do the household chores like cleaning of house, dusting, watering plants along with self care tasks such as going for a morning walk, studying for 6 hours daily etc. during his summer vacations. He said, ''I will''. His father said, "You would get pocket-money in every 10 days but you need to complete the tasks everyday." Vicky nodded. Only for the sake of pocket-money he completed all his tasks with honesty, for the next 10 days. But in these 10 days he got very sick due to tiredness. When his parents came to him to grant him pocket-money then he instantly refused them to take it. Now he had realised that the hardwork he was doing for pocket-money was the same hardwork that his father had been doing everyday to earn money, which he only was wasting in purchasing needless things. His mother told that he had to complete tasks like cleaning of house, dusting, watering plants, go for a morning walk, study for 6 hours etc. during his summer vacations. He said, ''I will" sadly. His father said that you would get pocket-money in every 10 days but you need to complete the tasks everyday. Vicky nodded. Moral of the Story: Life is not a bed of roses, we all must pay the price!
author: Kamakshi Verma

title: It'll be Okay
text: ” Why do you worry? Papa hai na* (I’m here). It'll be okay.” Something her father used to tell her, whenever he saw her anxious about anything. The person who told her everything would be okay had been gone for seven months and she still wasn’t sure if things would ever be okay. Yet she made herself pseudo promises that it would be or maybe deep down she hoped, that he would walk in the faded teal door and all these months would have been a slow nightmare. “Breathe’’ “Don’t worry Amber it would be okay” Amber said while holding her arms, begging herself to breathe ‘ It’ll be okay' Repeating that had pulled her out from countless panic attacks, but still, every once in a while the same words brought tears streaming down. In her thirteen years of existence, she had felt grief - of losing her favourite toys, of her pet rabbit running away, of losing friendships and plants drying up. All these things felt so trivial looking back, these losses were just a drop from the ocean of grief and losing her dad was a rogue wave she wasn’t prepared to deal with. That left her drowning, and the one to tell her that it would be alright was gone. She was told to be strong, whatever being strong meant. Yet, at times she didn't want to be strong, she wanted to cry and even more Amber wanted the hollow feeling to go away. Flipping through the pages of her diary, she found the day on which she learnt how to count the knots of a carpet, and also the day she chose a carpet for her room. Carpets were something that Amber’s father was very fond of, and as Amber grew older her admiration for them was instinctive. Dear Diary, Today dad took me to an exhibition and the carpets there were magnificent. Now he has finally agreed to teach me how to count their knots, after all, I’m a big girl now. Although I enjoyed painting my room's door teal with him, now I get to choose a carpet for my room. Dad was a little disappointed to see me lying down on a carpet, 2 minutes into our search. Silk on silk, he said, Ambi you have expensive taste. I have learnt from the best, I replied. I think I'm good at convincing him that he agreed to buy me the turquoise carpet I wanted, only after teaching me how to count the knots. So now I can say, the carpet in my room has 720 x 680 knots and I have counted them myself. Sweet dreams Amber It had been three years that the carpet had been in her room yet the years did not show on it. After being in denial, Amber was finally coming to terms with her father’s constant absence. People were there for the big moments - for her birthday, report cards, and festivals and she did miss him a lot on those days. The times she missed him more were the insignificantly significant ones like when she entered the living area to wish him good morning and him not being there and parent-teacher meetings where her friends got their fathers. Amber was annoyed at others for expecting her to move forward but more so herself for being stuck. She understood that grief came in waves, that she would have to let them roll in and leave salt as they receded. That she could not block them out, all she could do was find the seashells of the memories she had with her dad, and keep them safe. Amber after taking a deep breath entered her dad’s room on his bedside table, was his notebook which he did not let anybody but his dear Ambi see. Amber used to call it his Grimoire of Carpets. Though a software engineer by profession, he was no less than a magician for her. Amber while keeping the letter found a note. A note he wrote a week before he fell ill, she had a vague memory about the special parcel she had kept in his trunk, that dad would open once he got better, she had forgotten about it amidst everything. She ran towards the old rusty trunk, next to her father’s almirah. The trunk made a screech as she opened it, there it was the special packet, carefully with the keys she cut through the layers of tape, and finally, the wait was over. 2 weeks left: for Ambi's gift to arrive Amber could not hold herself back as the tears streamed down her face, as she saw the leather tag on the side of the carpet, in front of her were signature Iranian carpets, the same ones she and her father had seen in an export exhibition. How the stall owner mentioned his shop in Abu Dhabi and refused to sell the masterpieces. She remembered being sad about it, and also recalled the urgent trip her dad took the same week to Dubai, he had bought them for his Ambi. Wiping away her tears Amber started to unroll the carpets, she closed her eyes and all that her father had taught her played in front of her. She was sure of what she had to do, for the first time in her life she was going to count the knots of a carpet all by herself. She was sad that her father wasn't here to see her, though deep down she knew he would have been very proud of his daughter. Hours later she was exhausted, and along with it, she had a gratified look on her face, something that was seen after a long time. Her grandmother always told her that one heals with their hands and for the first time she felt it. Amber had hope, that she could move forward and live with the grief of losing a parent, and she understood the hollowness she felt. The years in front of her were many, and growing up was scary, but now she actually believed that it'll all be okay.
author: Areebah Chaudhary

title: Holding On
text: into that day—the sun set behind the massive tree at the entrance of the park. I sat on the corner of the bench as my 7-year-old self, hugging my legs. I tried to hold back my tears but as soon as I tasted the salty water on my tongue, my cheeks heated up with warm tears streaming down my chin. I looked up when a girl sat by me. I sniffled into my oversized sweater as she looked at me with her big brown eyes. I didn’t know her then, but she was going to become a big part of my life. We talked for hours as she consoled me. Nightmare. What would appear in your mind if I said this word? Monsters? Ghosts? Your best friend? Not the last, I’m sure. After reading my story, your views might change. I sat on the rusty bench in the city park next to my best friend, Cindy. The bench was a memorable part of our lives. It held many special memories between her and me. As a matter of fact, it was the spot where I’d first met her. As I thought about our first meeting, the setting gradually Millions of thoughts crashed into my mind. Voices. Loud beeps from a hospital monitor. And then a long sharp sound. I breathed. The dark turned into the park like a light switching on. Broad daylight radiated off of…nothing. The sun had vanished, leaving behind its light. I lifted my hand and surprisingly, I could. I’d acquired control over myself. I scanned the surroundings. It was the present-day park. I could tell because of the chalk doodle at the corner. Everything went black. The sound of laughter filled my ears. Cindy approached me from the dark, smiling. Slowly, she walked toward me, flickering like crazy. I reached out to touch her as she neared me but only the essence of a ghost was left of her. A long, shrill sound entered. It filled the air, growing louder until it became deafening. In the middle of my distorted thoughts came a word- alarm. It was the sound of my alarm. Is this a dream? Another thought messed up my mind. Why can’t I wake up from this dream? How could I mistake someone else for her? I should’ve recognized it wasn’t her. A hand touched mine. I relaxed, thinking about how Cindy would scold me for overthinking if she was here right now. Thoughts about her gave me strength. I opened my eyes to look at the person sitting by me. Her eyes matched Cindy’s. Even the shape of her face resembled hers. She looked at me with understanding, while she clapped me on the back lightly. I sat down, stroking the slats. Seeing the doodle, I recalled Cindy drawing it with a broken piece of chalk a day before she died. Tears welled up in my eyes but before they could fall, a hand rested on my back. My eyes lit up thinking it was Cindy. I turned around to fling my arms around her but disappointment washed over me before I could reach her. I slumped back. Millions of thoughts raced through my mind at once— How can it be her when she’s dead? Why would she appear before me when I’m so miserable? Moreover, I felt angry at myself. "You know," Maddie said. "I've also been down since her death. My memories with her keep playing inside my head. Every little word reminds me of her." She paused, taking my hand in hers. “But you’ll get through it. I'm also learning to live without her. It will hurt at the start, but you’ll learn to cope with it.” Hearing this, a tear slipped down my cheek but it wasn’t a tear of sadness. Instead, it was one of comfort. Anyone could mistake that person for Cindy. It was her elder sister, Maddie. But one thing about her stood out. The paleness on her face was familiar but it wasn’t Cindy’s. The paleness matched my face. Maddie was also undergoing what I was— losing someone precious. She understood what I was going through. Through the chaos, I thought about what had comforted me when Cindy was gone. And till now, the only time I’d felt relaxed was with Maddie. Talking to her and airing out my feelings had lifted the burden off my shoulders. I had found someone else to whom I could relate to. Only one word came out of my mouth. “How?” “Find out what comforts you, hm?” She looked into my eyes once again before shimmering away into thin air. I was back in the darkness. It seemed to eat me up. Little by little I disappeared into it. The only voice I could hear was Maddie’s, saying her last words to me over and over. Find out what comforts you. Find out what comforts you. Find out what comforts you. The echo drifted away as the pieces fell into place. The only way to cope with losing someone is to talk. To get through it, I had to let someone know what I’m going through. And I had the perfect person in mind who could share their feelings with me. Till I finished my thinking process, another sound entered my dream. The long, shrill sound was all too familiar. The sound of my alarm.
author: AISHNI GUPTA

title: The Disloyal Dog
text: Once upon a time there lived a dog in a village. He lived in a small cottage. His wish was for to go to an training school. The next day he got a post from the post office. It says that he got an admission for a training school. He got excited. The next day he woke early and started to get ready for his training school. After a few minutes he reached there. Then he saw many dogs. He made many friends at the first day itself. He became really happy. But suddenly the friends started to dislike him. The reason was of his behaviour. He acted like an disloyal dog. So a dog name Bruno named him as disloyal dog. The disloyal dog reacted to everyone in a rude way. The dog bruno said an Idea. The idea was that what if we react the same way like the disloyal dog reacted to us so that he would understand the pain that we felt when he did that. It was the next day. When the right time came everyone was ignoring the disloyal dog. He felt that something fishy is going on. This started to hurt his heart. So he ran towards Bruno and said that sorry I understood what my mistake was but first I thought it was your mistake but then realized it was my mistake. Sorry please forgive me I am pleading you!!!!! He said okay dear friend now you understood the lesson that being rude to others hurts them a lot. Now they all lived happily. The End
author: Saranya Menon
illustrator: Balaram Mandal; Candice  Botha; Marleen  Visser; Shadrach Munene; Siddhartha Tripathi

title: Overthinking
text: "Shweta!", Ritika called out. Shweta turned around, perplexed. Why did Ritika want to talk to her? This was unusual. Nobody had ever bothered to talk to her, so why would the person who was constantly surrounded by people, suddenly want to talk to her? Was she looking dishelmed? Did Ritika want to make fun of her because of that? Shweta had these thoughts under a minute as she nervously made her way to where Ritika was standing. "What is it?" asked. Ritika said, "I've noticed, that you're always present in class, and you always complete your work on time, right?" Shweta nodded. "I've been unwell for the past two days so could you please lend me your science, social science, and English notebooks for the weekend?" Ritika requested. As it turns out Shweta was only overthinking, Ritika wasn't planning to make fun of her or anything but she only wanted to borrow something. Shweta handed her the notebooks and walked away. This was an everyday tale. Even the slightest creak of the window or door could make her lose it. This was Shweta. Tanya, her classmate was the exact opposite. Tanya doesn't have a care in the world. She does as she pleases, walks wherever she wants and says whatever she likes. The only similarity they had was that neither of them had any friends. What seemed like a typical summer morning to most people was an absolute nightmare for Shweta. On that day she had a mathematics class test that was scheduled before recess. She hadn't been able to study the previous night. On top of that she overslept. She had never been late before. If that wasnt enough, being in a hurry she forgot to take her lunchbox. During recess, she sat alone in the classroom as always. The test went badly and she was famished. She wanted to sob loudly. Out of the blue a steel, tiffin box appeared in front of her. The tiffin box contained two laddoos and a sandwich. Shweta looked up to find a girl with straight, short hair and bangs falling on her forehead. It was Tanya. Shweta shook her slightly to tell Tanya that she did not want to eat, though she was starving. At once, her train of thought started. Why was Tanya offering her lunch? Was it some sort of mean prank? Did she put something in the food? As if reading her mind, Tanya broke her train of thoughts by shoving a laddoo into her mouth and said "Don't worry, I haven't added poison to it." When she was finally done with the laddoo and opened her mouth to say something, Tanya shoved half of the sandwich into her mouth. Tanya started making light jokes. And for the first time, Shweta wasn't worrying and instead, was joining in. Thus began a n ew friendship (a friendship over a laddoo and a sandwich.) Being under the influence of such a carefree person as Tanya, Shweta began to become more confident and social. Overthinking wasn't a problem for her anymore. If there was a problem she could simply talk it out with people she trusted.
author: Srishti Kashyap
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Harshika G; Neeta Gangopadhya; Rhea Nandy; Shivam Choudhary; Srishti Kashyap; Swathi Sambasivam

title: THE BATTLE OF REZANG LA
text: Chusul Valley,Ladakh February 1963 It was just like another day in the month of February 1963. The Chusul valley had regained its serenity post the recent war with China. The panaromic view of snow covered mountains and vegetations on them could make one feel like being in heaven. However a delegate of Indian military and civil officials were walking without a word, oblivious to this beauty of nature. From their somber mood, one could predict something offbeat lay ahead. They were trekking laboriously to a remote location. After a long and tiresome adventure, they finally reached the destination and witnessed a marvelous sight. They saw a group of soldiers performing their duties stoically with firm grip on triggers of their guns, they were ready to finish anyone who would cast an evil eye on their motherland. However, something was unusual which made everyone look in awe and horror..... Their bodies were without souls.... The memory of the strange conversation they had with a soldier the previous month flashed in everyone`s mind.  Army Headquarters, New Delhi Nov-Dec 1962 The officials looked Puzzled when they saw the men claiming to belong to the Charlie Company of 13 Kumaon Regiment. The same company which was asked to retreat but didn`t and was thought to be missing or perhaps having been taken as prisoners of war. What these soldiers narrated was even more queer. The soldiers tell a tale:  Rezang La 18 Nov 1962 "Gentlemen! we have been asked to retreat owing to our unpreparedness for an action. However as a soldier I feel, its my duty to fight and fight for my country, no matter what comes over.Those of you who want to go back can do it without any objection from my part" This was the short yet impetuous message from Major Shaitan Singh, Company Commander of Charlie Company,13 Kumaon Regiment. Surprisingly no one was going back. It was evident that this group of mere 120 men was unflinchingly waiting for the storm to come. Be it lack of ammunition or the blood- freezing weather, nothing could deter them. Soon in the pitch dark hours of morning, they valiantly fought back the Chinese offences. The second attack came soon after followed by the third. The ammunition got over but their Josh was high as usual.. They fought till their last bullet and till the last breath of the last man. February 1963: Tears rolled down the eyes of everyone.Emotions swamped their hearts.A feeling of guilt overtook their minds for dubbing the stories narrated by the soldiers as implausible and baseless. AFTERMATH Though the war could not be won but the way a handful of soldiers faced the well equipped and prepared large number of enemies, and fought the battle with nothing but raw courage,continues to exhort the Indian soldiers and equally astonishes the world population.Had those bravehearts not countered the enemy, the scenic Ladakh would not have the privilege to adorn the head of mother India. Data says, 300-400 Chinese soldiers were killed in this face to face combat. UNESCO attributed it as one of the eight most gallant acts done ever in the human history. 114 bravehearts moved to the heavenly gardens of the almighty in the unforgettable battle. People could not believe their eyes when they saw one thing.Each warrior had received hundreds of bullets in their bodies..... AND EACH BULLET ON THEIR CHESTS.
author: Keshav  Raj
illustrator: Amar Soni; Bhubaneshwar workshop  for children; Deepansh  Mishra; Greystroke; Jeyanthi Manokaran; Keshav  Raj; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Priya Krishnan Das; Priya Kuriyan; Ruchi Shah; Shruti Sunil; Siddhi   Vartak; Students of  Himalayan Public School; Suvidha Mistry

title: No Escape
text: NO ESCAPE “Having the opportunity to study abroad with fulfilling our dreams looked like heaven, but it took only seconds for it to transform into hell.” I was never a bright student but rather a hardworking one. The dream of becoming a doctor has been in my heart since childhood. As a result, after completing class 12, I took the NEET exam to gain admission into a government medical college in India. The exam didn't go as well as I expected, but I got enough marks to study abroad and achieve my dream of becoming a doctor. While doing some research, I came across a website showing some Ukrainian medical universities. The next day, my father gave me some recommendations for good universities in Ukraine. He told me how tuition fees were affordable and quality education was provided. It was better to go to these institutions rather than pay a large fee to study at a college in India. I did some more research and talk to some students who were already studying in Ukraine. After talking to them, I finally made up my mind and decided to study abroad in Ukraine. And finally, the day arrived to say goodbye to my family at the airport. I was going to fulfill my dreams and come back home as a doctor. I said a warm goodbye to my family and boarded the flight to Ukraine. After 8 hours of journey, we landed in Ukraine and went to the hostel of our university. As that country was new to us, our biggest helpers were our seniors and colleagues. It didn’t take much time for us to adapt that new life in Ukraine. Well, I have to say that Ukraine is really beautiful, and I had made a lot of good memories there. Every moment spent in that city, whether it be experiencing the first snowfall, or rushing from one department to another for classes. In Ukraine, we don’t get Indian food, so we also learned to cook some delicious food. Everything was going perfectly. We were attending the lectures and classes regularly. Our usual day probably would look like going to university in the morning, returning in the evening, having our food, and studying till it was dark. We Indians never really got involved in Ukrainian politics, but it became a worldwide affair when the Ukrainian government appealed to let Ukraine join NATO, which Russia totally opposed to. Russia and Ukraine had some conflicts, but we never thought that this would transform into a full-blown war suddenly. We got the news that Russia had started to send troops to the border, in what it says are training exercises. We knew that something was going to happen, so we all booked our tickets to travel back to India. A couple of days went normally and then one day I woke up to the loud thuds of bombs and I got to know that Russian forces had begun missile and artillery attacks on major cities, including Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine. They completely shut airports down after there was a missile attack on the runways and all our flights got cancelled. The war started to expand vigorously when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The President of Ukraine imposed Martial law which meant no one was allowed to step outside. And it didn’t take much time when we could see the Russian tanks on the roads. We saw the news that there were missile attacks on so many buildings and we always feared that it could be us next time. It was strictly ordered that whenever the sirens screamed we had to rush to bunkers and stay there till the sirens goes off again. These bunkers were hugely crowded and suffocating. There was no proper heating system and electricity, and the temperature there was around -12 degrees Celsius. I never thought that I would face such a situation in my entire life. There were no proper food and water supplies for us. We had some packs of chips and biscuits on which we survived for so many days. The local people of Ukraine were very helpful and kind. They helped us with edibles and drinks, even when they had very little for themselves. We were gradually becoming hopeless and spent many sleepless nights in the bunkers. I was really scared and so were my parents. We did not get enough chance to talk to them as our phone's battery was not charged enough and we also did not have connectivity in the bunkers. We had no clue when we would be able to go back home and were in constant fear that we would even be alive until the very next morning. The Indian Embassy issued an advisory that asked all the Indian citizens in Ukraine to leave the country as soon as possible. So we all planned that we would try to reach the Poland border by train. It was an enormous challenge for us to reach the railway station, as there was no proper transport service. We had no option other than to walk miles through the missile attacks and firings to reach the railway station. Somehow we made it to the railway station but unfortunately, we could not get on the train because it was immensely crowded as people were fighting to get on the train. It was a do-or-die situation. We became hopeless and returned to our bunker on the same day and decided that we would try again the next day. The next morning, we woke up early, packed our bags, and walked toward the railway station. As the streets were empty and some dead bodies lay on the roads, it was very scary for us, but we somehow summoned the courage to reach the railway station. There was a lot of scuffling and some of my friends got injured too. Luckily, we managed to board the train this time and were relieved when the train departed. We finally arrived at the Poland border and thought that the struggle was over, but it wasn't a simple task to cross the border because of the enormous crowd trying to flee Ukraine. It took us two days to cross the border and reach on the other side. In Poland, we stayed in the refugee tents arranged by the Indian government. Every workable arrangement like food, water, etc. was made for us. It was unbelievable that we made it out of Ukraine and were ready to go back home safely. Our flights were booked and we flew back to India after two days. When I saw my parents tears rolled down my cheeks. I am grateful that I am back in India safe and sound but I want to go back to Ukraine as it is my second home to finish my studies when the war ends.
author: Vratika Shakya

title: True Friendship
text: Once upon a time, there lived two friends named Rahul and Mehul. They have been friends for three years, their friendship is powerful. They both were kind to each other and cared for each other. Rahul was kind, soft-hearted caring, and joyful on the other hand Mehul was kind but made fun of others, bullied others and was cold-hearted. Even though they were totally opposite to each other they had a strong friendship. One day they both decided to go out on a dessert trip to enjoy their holidays. They both were enjoying their trip but suddenly Mehul asked Rahul to give him the bottle of water he had. Rahul denied, because the water in the bottle was finish ed. Mehul burst out in anger and was shouting at his friend. After sometimes they both stayed silent and realized that they lost therye way. Suddenly Mehul slapped Rahul in anger, because he was very thirsty and could not control his anger. Rahul didn't said anything and stopped for a while to write - "my friend slapped me" on the sand. After sometimes both the friends were very tired as they were walking in the lonely dessert and suddenly Rahul got dumped into a hole, but at the right time Mehul saved him. Even though Mehul was angry on Rahul, he helped his friend. When Rahul was saved by him, Rahul quickly took a stone writing "my friend saved me". Seeing that Mehul asked Rahul - Why did you write "I slapped you on the sand" and "My friend saved me on the stone" Rahul replied - " Let all the bad memories fade out from your life and the good memories always be a reminder and a great memory fo your life."
author: Ashna Chand

title: Escapism
text: Lucy was a little princess in her small family. She had loving parents and caring grandparents. Ever since Lucy was born she got whatever she wanted, had many friends and was loved by everyone because of her fun energy. Lucy always wear clean clothes and her hair was always done neatly. Moreover she had a face of goddess, pretty big eyes, soft red lips, a little cute nose. Her grandmother would always tell others that Lucy would be an actress when she grew up and everyone did agree with that because Lucy was also dramatic which made her perfectly fit to be an actress. Lucy grew up receiving all the love from people around her. It was Lucy's 12th birthday. Her parents were coming home with her birthday cake but luck was not on their side, they got into an accident and died at the spot. Due to the shocking news her grandfather had a heart attack and was paralyzed. All her family's saving had been used up for her grandfather's treatment and their finance was in crisis. They eventually became poor so her grandmother had to go to market to sell vegetables. Lucy was no more the energetic little girl, she became a bland person. She was less seen with her friends. Her friends left her after knowing she had become poor and now that she won't treat them to delicious food. Lucy no longer wear clean clothes and her hair was always messy except for the days she wash it. Her bright big eyes had become dull. Lucy was no longer the person she was before. Her life had changed completely after her parents died. When Lucy turned 14, she told her grandmother that she would drop out from school and help her grandmother in earning money for her grandfather's treatment. Hearing that her grandmother broke out in tears and tells Lucy that she had a whole life ahead and that she should not give up just because of some difficulties. The both cried in each other's arms. That night Lucy had an unusual dream. She knew she was dreaming but the dream felt so real. She saw her parents, they were calling her name and she ran towards them. She told them how things had changed, how grandfather had been struggling, how her friends treat her, how she had become not interested in anything. Her parents were hugging her and told her to stay strong and that they were always with her by her side. When Lucy woke up she was already in tears but she knew that those words were the only thing that could help her keep moving forward in her life. The next day at school Lucy was humiliated by the kids who once used to be her best friends. During recess the kids started mocking her old grandmother and badmouthed her in front of Lucy. They called her an orphan and said horrible things to her. Lucy felt angry but she was move sad. All the mixed feelings were inside her. She was ready to punch those kids in the face and also she was already crying inside like a child. That night, while she was dreaming she was able to control everyone. There she made the kids who humiliated her apologize to her and she even scolded them in her dreams and the kids were crying. The next morning when she woke up, she felt more relieved and she was in a good mood. She had the best dream ever. And Lucy was curious how she was able to control the characters in her dream. So she did some research and found out she was lucid dreaming. A type of dream in which the dreamer become aware that they were dreaming while dreaming and were able to control the dream characters and the environment. And surveys show that roughly 55% of adults have experienced at least one lucid dream during lifetime and 23% of people experience lucid dreams at least once per month. But for Lucy it had become a habit whenever she had a bad day she would just dive into the dream and make the people say what she wants to hear and the next day she would feel completely fine. Just like that Lucy had been dealing with her daily problems by dreaming. As time goes when Lucy became 19 both her grandparents had passed away due to old age. After her grandparents died Lucy was left all alone. She had another huge breakdown but this time she does not know how to deal with it. While she was dreaming she was in a forest and she fell asleep in her dream and every inch of her life, it flashed back. She went back to the day her parents died. She was about to blame the other driver who was also in the accident with her parents. But suddenly everything stopped and a man with wings was coming towards her and Lucy was not able to control him. She was about to ask who he was but the man starts speaking, "My dear, you seem to be struggling. What wish do you have?" Lucy didn't even take a second to think she answered, "My family, I want my family back." The man whispered, "Okay!" and then he vanished. Lucy heard her mother's voice calling her. Lucy woke up, she saw her mother beside her with a cup of milk. She doubted if she was still dreaming but there her father came inside her room and asked, "Did my princess have a good sleep?" Lucy smiled and heard her grandfather calling her and saying that she should get dressed to go out for a walk. Lucy asked where her grandmother was. Her mother said, "She's reading newspaper." Lucy started laughing and burst out in tears. She couldn't figure out if she was still dreaming or if it was the real world. She hugged her mother and asked her, "Mom, Am I still dreaming?" Her mother replied, "No, sweetie." Lucy wondered if she got stuck in her dreams but she didn't care if she was dreaming or if it was real. At that moment she was happy that she finally got her family back again.
author: Usha Namram
