title: A RIDE PAST RESTRAINT
text: Nei-ohh-gghh…! I stretched my jaws as much as I could, and closed my eyelids firmly, trying to fall into a deep slumber. But.. Oh come on! Not again! This has probably been the thousandth time I’ve forced myself to sleep. I was just too exhausted from my work, my surroundings, my life, myself- just everything. I started feeling more and more redundant. ‘Excess of anything is poisonous’ they say- it became my steadfast belief over time as I realised that I was surfeited with life itself. I took a glimpse of my surroundings yet again, just the same brownish green stripes of grass brushing each other until my horizon below and flocks of birds hovering intermittently above. And as always, I could hear the gurgling of the puddle that was beside. The place was aloof, visited by visitors very rarely, not even another kind like me would venture here. It was serene outside of course, but well inside- not really. I wanted to walk away from this zone and find some friends. There was always some hindrance to it, perhaps the nostalgia (of my fellow herd mates) I associated with the place, perhaps my reserved nature or perhaps just my fate. Nevertheless, I feel like I should probably set forth and find a new environment. I’ve always had a small intuition of venturing out elsewhere and exploring, at least to get rid of this unvaried food. Though this thought has arisen multiple times, I’ve somehow never had the thrust to do so. As I kept thinking, suddenly I heard a rustle of leaves. I immediately opened my half- closed eyelids to see the light brown skin of a lion camouflaging behind one of those tall grasses. But it had aimed at some other prey. Completely struck blank by fear, I seized the bridles and ran as far as I could. This was completely unprecedented for it is the first time that someone has ventured here after four long years. Thus this time, I really felt the need, the need to move out of my comfort. It was now or never. I took refuge under a peepal tree over the night. As the dawn broke, I set off. I took the bridle, and remembered the times when my brothers raced each other while I’d sit timidly watching them. They always competed to finish off at the good old peepal tree. I bid goodbye to the peepal tree too and promised to return with new friends. I walked and walked to come to a fork. I was perplexed on which path to take, and which one would lead me where. While I contemplated, I heard some sound. I peeped through the bush to see a deer and a fox quarrelling over who was more intelligent. I thought I could use this as an opportunity and went over to them. Both of them looked puzzled at me, and the deer asked ‘What species are you supposed to be? Wild, huh? Because I don’t think this jungle belongs to any horses’. While the fox replied with a smirk, ‘I doubt so. As much as I could recollect, horses don’t belong to any jungle.’ Annoyed by the statement of the fox, I retorted, ‘Um…I am one of the rare species..of hh-horses. My brothers have been c-cc-aptured and taken to town for reasons I am not aware of. I need help to go out of the jungle. So..’. The deer continued, ‘So? You need our assistance, right? I nodded. The fox thought for a while and said, ‘Mr. Rare Horse, It would be my pleasure to help you out but on one condition. You must answer my three questions, three very witty ones.’ If the answers are accurate I’ll show you the way. The deer stared and immediately responded, ‘No, no. I am better aware of the ways of the jungle. I could show you the way more rapidly only if you can keep pace with me.’ Uh-oh! Where have we landed now?! I questioned myself. In an attempt to escape from a fork, I got struck hard by another. Nevertheless, recalling the cunning nature of a typical fox, I accepted the deer's condition. The deer and I started going ahead while the fox gave a crafty look. Then, I galloped high, cantered sprightly with the deer but in vain. The deer had run far ahead and I could only cover one fourth of its speed. I soon got exhausted because I’ve never run this much in my whole life! I continued to walk in the same path for some time, relaxing though frustrated at first, until I heard a loud growl. Quite startled, I reversed to see a tiger hunting a monkey! I galloped silently but with speed in order to not reveal my presence. Then after taking refuge, I saw the tiger pouncing on the mammal, but fortunately the monkey climbed to the pinnacle of the tree and with the help of its long arms and gripping tail flew to the other trees. The ability of the monkey proved to be the weakness of the tiger- obstructing it from aiming further. Naturally after sometime the tiger cooled down, chewed a mouthful of small insects he could capture and left the place. Still in doubt, I walked noiselessly as far as the suspicion went away from me. Then, I came to a halt to see the tall trees shrinking into small strips of grass, shrubs, and herbs. The sun shone brightly on my face, there was no more canopy. It was the edge of the jungle. ‘Yay! I made it!’, I thought. I guzzled down water from a small pond in the town to refresh myself. Then, I carried myself more confidently towards the town in search of my brothers. Initially, I kept out of sight as I did not want anyone to notice a strange creature walking on the road. But I later realised that animals kept in pace with human beings in the modern world. Infact, many humans had a box sort of thing in their hands, which they kept looking at constantly. Few held it close to their ears and spoke too. Wait.. I remember from my vague memory that it was called a ‘phone’. The last time I came to the town with my family, I had seen them too but not this much in use. Well, so I set off again. This time I observed that the small town had sky scraping buildings that grew out of vicinity amongst the mass of clouds. It was present at every nook I saw. Later, I could see a small lake which I remember, along with my herd mates, I had come here for a picnic about five years back. I galloped in the pathway while suddenly a white, polished, small, metal like thing flew past my head making me unstable and eventually making me slip and fall on the water in the pathway. A small girl came out of it, along with her parents. They pressed some random button which made the vehicle compress itself and fly away. I was intrigued by what that vehicle was, while the girl exclaimed, ‘The ride in the flying car was amazing, mom and dad!’ The girl noticed me, and without a second thought started shouting at her parents, ‘I want to ride on that horse! It looks so beautiful, mommy. Pleasee, let me ride.’ I was taken aback and turned to go in the opposite direction unsure of my ability to ride while another horse stopped me. My heart skipped a beat, for it was my brother!! I tiptoed and cantered and exclaimed at his arrival. He too embraced me back. He was proud of my migration, he said, ‘I knew, one day, you would come in search of us past your diffidence.’ I smiled and questioned about the whereabouts of the other brother, and he answered that he too was initially a therapeutic rider but now is in the profession of training horse-like-robots to perform riding and other activities in a finer and more desirable way. I was astonished and asked, ‘Are these robot stuffs replacing animals too?’ ‘Yes’, he said. ‘But do not worry, we’ll ultimately be given more freedom, we can go back to our homes.’ Consequently the girl climbed on my back and I rode and rode and stopped after my brother did. The girl tapped my back with pleasure, thanked me and gave me a fleshy green leaf to eat. ‘At last, I can satisfy my hunger!’ I thought. But as I bit it, the bitter- rusted metal like smell and taste sabotaged the impression I had on it. My brother laughed at my innocence and said, ‘This is a modern currency that is given as a token of gift to the horses that ride- which must be ultimately handed over to our riding instructors; ‘tis not a real leaf!!’.
author: Sadhana Sakthivel

title: The Nights On The Grass
text: “Lakshita, are you sure we are best friends forever?” asked Roohi from her best friend on a starry night lying down on the carpet of soft green grass. “Of course, silly. We are besties forever”, said Roohi. “I know but is it true that you will never betray me?” “Yeah, I won’t betray you ever in my life.” They both stood up and hugged each other tightly. Both said, “Good night” to each other and left home. The next morning in school, Ms Rashmi announced, “Children the annual day is approaching. Who would like to join?” Many students raised their hands in excitement. Roohi and Lakshita were two of them. “Great”, said Ms Rashmi and took all of them to the stage. Lakshita and one of her friends, Yamini got selected for the speech.. On the other hand, Roohi and another friend of hers, Christie, were selected for singing Lakshita and Roohi’s bond got weaker day by day because most of the time, Ms. Rashmi was holding annual day practice. Lakshita and Yamini soon became best of friends and Roohi became insecure. As a loyal friend, she tried to strengthen the bond between her and Lakshita. But Lakshita became way too fond of Yamini.. Roohi tried to move on but it was very hard to leave her best buddy of eight years. She thought of the nights they were looking at the stars and laughing and talking. They had never thought they would leave each other after eight happy years. Roohi felt heartbroken but she had no other choice. Yamini would give her an evil look each time their eyes met. She tried to have Yamini leave Lakshita but now, they were She wrote songs to distract her mind and to continue her life in a happy way. But, she felt lonely after Lakshita left her. She let her go and let her live how she wanted. She thought she would make new friends and she did but never felt loved. A few days before the annual day, Lakshita fainted in the sun. Yamini continued her practice not bothered by Lakshita’s condition. Roohi came to the rescue and took her to the nurse’s office. When Lakshita was conscious, she thanked Roohi for being by her side and went to Yamini straight away. Roohi was shocked to see Lakshita act this way but somehow, she knew this was going to happen. After the annual day, the school announced a break for students of all classes. All the students were very happy after all the hectic work of the annual day. At dispersal, all children wished each one “happy holidays”. Lakshita couldn’t stop herself and went to Roohi. She wished her “happy holidays” with a loving smile. Roohi was filled with tears and hugged Lakshita tightly, remembering the nights on the grass.
author: Saumya Singhal
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Helga Parekh; Imile   Wepener; Shirley Chan; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja; Taposhi Ghoshal; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: Ruthless king, Jake
text: Once there lived Jack, a ruthless king of a big empire. His great, brutal army had helped him in conquering any land coming his way, resulting in extending his empire to far places. People used to call him, the invincible King as no one had ever defeated him. Whenever his huge army moved, either the rival kings ran away to save their lives or surrendered their monarch to save their people from the merciless army of Jack. Those days every king used to pray to god to save their kingdom from coming to the notice of Jack. One day Jack was getting ready to go on a quest of invading a smaller kingdom hidden behind a mountain range.Then, something unexpected happened which was going to change the fate of the invincible Jack.Jack’s beloved daughter Lina suddenly got severely ill.She wasn’t opening her eyes and was struggling for every breath.Jack had never cared for anyone except his daughter. Brutal Jack was unexpectedly a good father and loved his daughter a lot. But, now the only person whom he loved was dying in front of his eyes.Lina was suffering from an incurable disease.Jack couldn’t watch his daughter struggling for his every breath. But, now the only person whom he loved was dying in front of his eyes.Lina was suffering from an incurable disease.Jack couldn’t watch his daughter struggling for his every breath. Jake's wife and queen Ezina blamed him and said that it was the result of all his sins which had now come as a curse for their child. She believed that God was punishing him for all the bad deeds he did in his whole life. Soon, he ordered his guards to abduct all the best physicians from other kingdoms and present them before him. Later, after four days the guards presented before him the twelve best physicians. The abducted men were the most proclaimed physicians from other kingdoms, famous for saving many lives. Jack said if his daughter dies, then he will kill every physician and asked if they want to leave the place alive, then they had to save his daughter’s life. Every physician was given a bag containing all kinds of herbs to prepare any medicine. Soon those miserable and scared magicians of medicine started preparing something to save Jack daughter’s life as well as their own. At night they all presented before him some medicines except one physician named, Toby. Toby didn’t come with any medicine. King Jack got extremely angry to see Toby with empty hands and said, “so you are not interested in saving your life, but don’t think I will give you an easy death”. King Jack I have seen this incurable illness earlier, Toby replied, I want to tell you a harsh truth, no medicine prepared by my fellow physicians or anyone is enough to save your daghter’s life so I felt worthless to prepare anything. Oh!, you know everything about my childs illness, so tell me where you had seen this disease earlier and what happened to your patient, did he died like my son is dying right now?, Jack asked in his angry voice. No, he survived, and right now that patient is standing in front of you, Toby replied. What do you mean?,Jack asked. I was that patient who had suffered this disease when I was a young boy and my father had saved my life, Toby replied. You knew everything about the cure and now you are telling me all this, Jack got very angry at Toby and continued, I will take your life right now for your idiotic behaviour, just tell me how did your father save your life and where is he now. Toby replied, King Jake, my father is no more, but what he did to save me? I think you wont do that, that is why I thought it worthless to tell you and accepted my fate of death by you. Jake shouted in his heavy voice, explain to me everything clearly how your father had saved you otherwise I am barely holding myself to take your life at any moment. Toby replied, King Jake I know you will not kill me at least until something happens to your daughter as I know, right now my life is more valuable after your son. Yes, Jake said, you are right, this is the reason you are still alive and talking to me but not so long. If one more time you tried to puzzle me, I will take your life right now. Im not here to puzzle you, Toby said, so you want to know how my father saved my life, then listen he sacrificed his life to save me. What sacrifice? Jake asked, but this time in a dull voice, What are you talking about? Tell me clearly? Toby said, outside this kingdom in the jungles of Onuma, grows rare red mushrooms, which can save your child’s life from this incurable disease. Listening to this the king promptly ordered his guards to bring every black-looking mushroom present in the jungle. Toby said, King Jake, wait, “I have to tell you something else.” Yes, Jake replied, what do you want more, just tell me?. Toby said, King Jake the rare mushroom only will not save your daughter but you or the queen. As anyone from the blood relation of the patient has to eat that rare mushroom and then has to give some drops of his blood in the ill persons mouth for five days. But on the sixth day the person who had eaten the mushroom dies because of the poison present in it, but the patient gets cured completely. Oh! "So this sacrifice you were talking about", the King replies to Toby and asks his guards to call the queen. Toby again elaborated everything to the queen. Queen Ezina said, Dear king Jake have you forgotten, Im not your child's actual mother, you had killed his mother many years ago for deceiving you. For the first time, the king felt he was not invincible and God was really punishing him for his bad deeds. He soon ordered his guards to release everyone and went to Lina’s room. The abducted physician hurriedly left the place except Toby, who followed Jake to his daughter’s room. Toby saw him crying, regretting, confessing all his sins and blaming himself for his child’s sufferings. At night the guards came with those rare black mushrooms. Jake ate those mushrooms and dropped some of his blood into his daughter’s mouth by cutting his hand. Lina soon started getting better every day and opened his eyes on the fifth day, but on the sixth-day Jake died leaving all his great empire for the future king. Finally, the brutal king got defeated by his own fate, but a great father won. For the first time, the king felt he was not invincible and God was really punishing him for his bad deeds. title: My Non-Biological Brother
text: There are some people who come into our life uninvited, then they change our lives forever. The same happened to Ankit, who was an average student who was not very bright in either his studies nor in extracurricular activities. He was the only son of a farmer who worked all day to feed his family. His mother helped his father in his agricultural activities but she also did the household chores. They were a struggling middle class Indian family who were trying to make both ends meet. Ankit used to go to the neighboring government school. As said earlier, he was an average student. He was planning to take over his father's occupation as a farmer when he completed his senior secondary education. But when he was in 5th grade, a crucial turning point occurred in his life, a new student came to his school. He was from the nearby town who settled into Ankit's village so that it would make it easier for his father to go to his work in the panchayat office. He was from a middle class family. His name was Aarush. He was excellent at his studies, and he was also good at extracurricular activities. In the school, Ankit did not have many friends. But when Aarush appeared, everybody was fascinated by the way he talks and behaves. It was the first time most of them were seeing a boy from the town. They all looked up to him like he was the perfect student, and in fact he is. But this so perfect Aarush was more interested in Ankit, who was weaker than he in almost every aspect. Aarush went ahead and introduced himself to Ankit. Ankit was almost shocked as he did not have many friends and was happy to see someone like Aarush talk to him. You can call Aarush friendly, but he was just curious about Ankit. He wanted to know more abut the boy who did not talk to anybody. He wanted to be a friend of Ankit. Aarush asked Ankit, "What's your name?", Ankit replied,"I'm Ankit, nice to meet you Aarush". Both of them continued their conversation for some time until the lunch break was over. Aarush understood that Ankit was a struggling student from a struggling family and need some help and support from somebody. As time went on, they both were at the first turning point of their life; they were at 10th grade and now both Ankit and Aarush were good in studies and sports. Just as Aarush predicted, Ankit needed a good friend who could support him in times of need and help him as much as he could. One day, after completing their 1st semester exams, Aarush asked Ankit, "What's your ambition, Ankit?" Ankit, who was planning to take over his father's job, was hesitant to say anything and said that he did not have an ambition. Aarush was shocked and said, "Wow, you don't have a goal in your life, well that's interesting! I have one goal in my life, and that is to become a world-famous doctor who loves, cares and cures everybody of their illness", Hearing this, Ankit was also thinking that about the dream he had when he was a child and saw men going around here and there in luxurious cars. He, too, wanted to ride in those cars and own them. He wanted to become a rich and successful businessman, but he left that dream a long time ago since his parents did not have any money, and he thought that only kids with rich parents can reach such heights. He was too afraid to talk about his dream to anybody, as he thought that many of them would make fun of him for thinking such nonsense. But he trusted Aarush, so he told about his long gone dream to him. Aarush was surprised to hear such a thought from Ankit, even though they had known each Aarush, being a good friend, encouraged Ankit to work hard and reach his dream. They both challenged each other that they both would reach their dreams and come before each other only after doing so. After this incident's occurrence, both of them started to study like they never did before. They were way more concentrated than they ever used to, did not participate in any other events, they just kept studying on and on and on. On the day of the result declaration, both their hearts were racing as they were eager for the results. But the results were absolutely fantastic. Both of them scored excellent marks and got position in the top 50 ranks in India. They were one step closer to achieving their goal. Unfortunately, they had to part ways here since both their ambitions were significantly different. But they promised each other to meet someday in the future after achieving their goal. Both of them continued on with their own path, Aarush got admission on AIIMS, Delhi, his dream college and the the dream of many students who pursue medicine as a career. Ankit, on the other hand, was helped by many kind people because they believed that a boy with this much potential should be nurtured. Ankit continued on with his business studies abroad in the USA. After 10 years, Aarush became a doctor who was a well respected and honoured man in his society and got married to Hannah, a doctor in his own hospital and got settled in the US. One day, Aarush decided to have dinner with his wife in a fancy five-star restaurant. As he was driving through the streets of LA, he noticed a man in a black suit going to the same restaurant as he was in a luxurious black Rolls-Royce car. When they both reached the restaurant, Aarush was shocked to see a very familiar face emerging from the car, it was Ankit! He could not believe his eyes as he saw dozens of people coming around the car, greeting Ankit as he was going inside the restaurant. Aarush rushed to meet his beloved friend, but was stopped by Ankit's bodyguards who did not know about their deep relation. After talking to his wife about how he knows Ankit and he was his best friend during their time in the school, Hannah was shocked. She told Aarush that Ankit is the owner of one of the most successful enterprises in the world, which mainly focuses in educating children all around the globe. Ankit was shocked as he did not know the fact his friend was the owner of a multi-million dollar company which was famous all around the world. While having dinner, Aarush head a familiar voice calling his name from a distance, it was Ankit! The people in the hotel were shocked as to see a businessman roaming about here and there in a restaurant. As Ankit's bodyguards were struggling to keep up to his speed, Ankit ran, jumped and hugged Aarush who was preparing to leave the restaurant. They both share their stories to each other and talked for the whole night about how they had reached their dreams. They were overcome with joy. Both of them were single children for their parents, but At that moment, they realized that they were non-biological brothers.
author: Parthiv Prasanth

title: Intelligence Of Raju
text: Once upon a time, there was a small village near a very big city whose name was Sitapur. The number of people in that village was about 1500, a man of 24 years of age lived among them whose name was Raju. He was very famous in the village just because of his intelligence. He often used to go to his farm, he had a very old bicycle, due to which he used to go to his farm. There were many goons living in the town near the village, one of whom was robust, stout and active goon, whom people called by the name of Munna bhai. He had alleged that the police had just got the hand behind him, but he had run to the village. Raju was his childhood friend. So one day, Munna bhai coming to the village after doing a crime, in the way to bunker, he met Raju. Seeing his childhood friend, Raju became happy. He said to him, " Friend you met me after a long time, How are you? Then munna bhai said that, " I am fine, How are you? Raju - I am fine too. Where are you going this way? Munna bhai - Nowhere, I was just going towards your village for some work. Okay Listen, I want to give you a work, Will you Do? Munna bhai was actually coming with a theft and Raju did not know that he was talking to a goon. Then Raju said - Oh somewhere - say! Even my life is present for you. Munna bhai - So you keep this bag with you for a while. If you do this then I will give you a big reward. Raju - ok. But when will you take it from me? Munna bhai - I will take the bag from you from this place after about 2 days. You meet me after 2 days at 4 o'clock in the evening. Raju - Okay brother. I walk. Raju - All right. See you after two days. Raju keeps the bag at his house and goes to the farm and Munnabhai goes to hide. On his way to his secret house, the police follow him. To ignore the police, he sneaks into small alleys. He knew every bit of this village, so he knew that after leaving this street, a huge highway comes. As soon as he came out of the street, the police was standing in front of him and the IPS car behind him. He was surrounded by police from all sides. The police arrested him and made him sit handcuffed to a chair in the interrogation room in the police station. And started questioning him where is that bag full of money? He told them - I have not stolen this. I am innocent. IPS - So who has done this theft? Look, don't even dare to lie to us. You are imprisoned in CCTV. Munnabhai - Yes. It was me but I was told to do this by Raju, who lives in a nearby village. This is Raju's home address. He said while writing his address on the paper. Some police officers left to go to that address. Then the IPS said - although you were made to do this, but you have made a mistake. You will get punished for this. Then the officer came there with Raju. Raju - Sir, what have I done? Why have you brought me here? IPS - You are asking what have you done. You have robbed such a big bank. Raju - Sir, what are you saying? Me and the thief? Not at all IPS - So tell me do you know it? Raju is surprised as he has found his friend arrested. Then an officer says that Sir, a bag of money has also been recovered from his house. IPS -Where did you take this bag from? Raju - This bag was given to me by him. By saying that you give me this bag after 2 days and also said that you do not even open this bag and see it. IPS - But how do we listen to you? Raju - There is a pillar at the intersection near it. A CCTV is installed on it. We did the same thing. So you will start believing in me after watching his recording. Seeing the IPS recording, he said - you are telling the truth. You are abandoned. But you will have to leave this bag here and yes you will also get the reward of honesty from the government. Raju - Thank you sir. IPS - And yes I will get you the harshest punishment. I already said don't lie to me. Munnabhai - Excuse me sir. The next day after Koti's hearing, Munnabhai is sentenced to 7 years in jail.

title: Journey to Confidence
text: “I would often get nervous about my presentation or speaking and there were moments when I had to screw up my courage to raise my hand or make a point, rather than hanging back.” This was Christine Lagarde, If this name sounds familiar or has taken you to a trip down the memory lane, most people know her as a former managing director of the Monetary Fund and as the incumbent President of the European Central Bank. There was a time when this silver haired, six feet tall French lawyer struggled to find her voice, when her boss filled her in, that as a women she would never become partner at a firm. Lagarde in fifteen years not only cemented herself as a partner at Baker & Mckenzie, a Chicago -based company but also its first female chairman. Even after defying all odds and exhibiting grace under pressure, she constantly battled the fear of not measuring up, screwing things up or having pit in the stomach before a presentation. She was not the only struggler, for famous leaders like Angela Merkel and Hilary Clinton too, struggled with their confidence, over prepped and embraced perfectionism. If these well accomplished and awe-inspiring figures had a hard time maintaining their self-confidence, then what about the common people? Let’s walk through the story of a twelve year old, black haired, R Bonney, who lived in Jaipur. Her life was nothing more than solitude and shyness, with books as her only companion. She went to school and sat mutely in a corner chair. As the gong struck the bell, came home, again only to be lost in her own world and company. R Bonney lived in an isolated four bedroom apartment and had her milk teeth. It seemed as if she was han kering at all times to speak up but the terror of being inaccurate or inappropriate, the fright of being a hoaxer and the horror of being left behind, wolfed her down. As time passed by, so changed her life. She moved to Delhi, her permanent teeth replaced milk teeth and she started sitting in the front row, at school. She made a couple of allies and became quite popular amongst her teachers as well as peers. She went ahead with participating in plenty of school events and evolved into having a pleasant vibe and a vibrant personality. But how did this transition took place? How did prominent figures such as Christine Lagarde, Hilary Clinton, Angela Merkel or R Bonney, a twelve year old girl from an ordinary household managed to gain confidence and attain the strength of making ironclad and firmly grounded decisions? “She was afraid of losing but more afraid of never trying.” R Bonney was not at ease moving to Delhi and was dubious if she could ever get used to. Albeit her conduct was the same, she couldn’t deny that the time for change had arrived. She sailed to conquer the inner fright that wiped out the chances, she hence missed. Her voyage was driven by the triple A’s, aspirations, appreciation and assurance. Her aspirations were to touch the sky and open herself up to a world which she had turn down on. She started off by enrolling herself in a public speaking club and grabbed hold of every opportunity to speak in front of the attendees and stand up against her worries. In addition to this, she chatted with her peers and had her parents to converse with. R Bonney took tiny steps to make unhurried progress. Her journey as a writer was anew and she began exploring different genres and the creativity that her weary soul carried. While hard criticism hits hard on an individual appreciation does wonders and results in rapid improvement. The tiny bits of appreciation and encouragement that was offered to R Bonney by the people around her, gave arousing results and a boost to her self-assurance. As frightening as the yells and outcry of horror, knocked her door an opportunity disguised as an obstacle. R Bonney’s first chance to represent the zeal and the light that she carried was one that involved her speaking in front of thousands of people. As she affirmed her participation, she gobbled, took a deep breath and said to herself, “ can I really do this? Am I prepped enough? What if I fail?” As doubts filled her mind, she paused for a second to reaffirmed and recollect herself,” The right time never comes, it’s time to show what I have got.” Don't be afraid, you will do wonders. After days of tedious preparation, hard work and consistency, the day had finally arrived, as R Bonney climbed up the stairs, she reiterated to herself, “She was afraid of losing, but more afraid of never trying.”
author: Aditri Khanna

title: Finding Unity
text: Once upon a time there lived a girl named Neha. She was 10 years old. She was very beautiful. She had completely black hair, brown eyes, soft cheeks and a small nose. She was very slim. Neha lived in Ghaziabad. She lived there since she was born. She was fond of playing Basketball, reading and had a beautiful voice. She was a very modest girl who never had a fight with anyone, helped everyone and most importantly never expected herself to be a hero. Her father was a Businessman and her mother was a Police officer. Neha studied in Delhi Public School which was in Rajnagar Extension. She really loved her school. She studied there since she started her schooling. Everybody was good friends with her except Swati and her friends. Although, Neha never won a prize, Swati was jealous of her because she knew that Neha had the capability to win one. Neha was really happy with her school, her friends and her current life. But, things were soon going to change. After sometime her mother got a transfer to Andaman & Nicobar Islands. They waited for her school term to get over and then moved. Andaman was a very beautiful and a peaceful place but, Neha still missed her old school and friends. Two days after arriving Neha got admission in one of the best schools there. She saw that her class was united just like her old school. She soon made some friends. Her first friend was Riya. She had brown hair, blue eyes and a medium size nose. She was very beautiful. Sometimes, she was a little showy but, she always realised and accepted her mistake and apologised for the same. She was the topper of her class. Her second friend was Rivaan. He was a tall person who had black and brown mix hair, black eyes and a long pointed nose. He really struggled in studying. His best quality was that he never hurt others feelings on purpose and by mistake if he did, he felt so guilty that he started to cry. After sometime Neha’s sadness started flying away and she was happy once more. One day she and her friends saw two students had broken into a serious fight. None of her friends had ever seen anyone fight in their class! Because of that fight the class became divided. Whenever the two groups faced each other, they were always ready to fight. But at that time Neha and her friends jumped between and told them to “Mind their own business”. But, one day the two groups got so mad that neither Neha nor her friends were able to stop them. So, they broke into a fierce fight. All of the students got suspension for a week except Neha, Riya & Rivaan. Riya observed that the situation had started getting worse. Because of the division the behaviour of the students was very bad which was spoiling the reputation of the class in the school. Riya told Neha & Rivaan all of this in the lunch break. After thinking for hours Neha came up with an idea. She discussed the idea with Riya and Rivaan the next day. Her idea was to bring back old memories, the moments the class had spent and enjoyed together. Her friends really liked the idea. So, the next day they wrote an old poem that they had learned in third class which was everyone’s favourite at that time, on the black board. They also found the collage photos of them having fun together and pasted it on the board. After seeing all those photos and reading the poem children started to realise their mistake and understood the importance of unity. Everything was back to normal and everybody was very happy. But, one question remained unanswered “Why did their class broke apart in the first instance?”.
author: Vidhi Chaudhary

title: When the Rains killed the Spring
text: When the Rains killed the Spring The village of Dhudhulia was in a flush of colours. Yellow, Brown, Red. Leaves crunched under the feet. The blossoms of marigold, krishnachuda flowers enthralled the cuckoo into a pleasant melody. Holi was in the air. In the morning, Akash was gulping down stale rice in a hurry. His sister Rakhi was sitting on the veranda, gazing out vaguely. She was not at all excited by the spirit of joy outside. Holi was just like an ordinary day for her- sulking around the shadowy hut all day long. Akash knew this. His sister never moved out of the house. He asked tentatively, “Rakhi, why don’t you go out with me today? It’ll be fun” She looked disbelievingly at him. “I’m fine here. I don’t want to go.” Akash disliked this indifference. “Do whatever you want. I won’t nag you.” He jumped up and ran out on the road. Outside, he felt so carefree chewing on the gum bought from Ramu’s shop. Then he got hold of Deep lazing on the wall of Shyam uncle’s house. They had stocked their colours in a secret place. Akash had to argue a lot with his irritable mother to get the money. “Oi, let’s get the colours and find the other boys.” Deep skipped down and joined him. The boys were reckless that day, mad in the festival of colours, soaking each other with bright shades. They wreaked a terrible havoc on the innocent passers-by. Then Akash retired against the Banyan tree with the boys circling him. He took a deep breath from his cigar and watched the smoke spiralling upward. The boys looked with fascination. “It’s boring. Let’s do something.” He said. Deep suggested, “I’ve an idea Guru. We can bring our mobile phones and play a game of Freefire.” Akash scoffed. “Who wants to be defeated by me?” At that moment they heard a stern voice from behind. “What are you doing here boys? Don’t think yourselves to be oversmart. Stop smoking immediately and go to your houses or this information will go to your parents. Mind it.” A young woman carrying buckets was standing in front of them. The boys were awestruck by her personality. “I warn you against this type of behavior. It should not be repeated in this locality again.” She directly looked at Akash. The boys shook down their heads and departed. Akash stood there alone looking at the receding shadow of the woman. Akash got acquainted with Nalini Boudi that day. She was Sunil Da’s newly married wife. Akash tiptoed into their house and found her cooking. “Hi, Boudi. I am Akash. What are you cooking?” Nalini glanced at him once and returned her gaze towards the sizzling curry. “Potatoes and Pumpkin.” “Wow! Won’t I get a chance to taste?” Akash smirked. Nalini gave an icy stare that numbed Akash. For the first time, he felt the contempt of Nalini stabbing his inner self for his conduct. He fumbled, tried to say something. “I don’t tolerate spoilt boys who disgrace their parents as well as their neighborhood.” Nalini turned away from him. Akash couldn’t sleep that whole night. Something changed in him from that time. Nalini Boudi had cast a spell on Akash. Rakhi was surprised to find her brother at home in the evening. He was unusually quiet and grave. Rakhi herself had little pleasures in her life. When her brimming happy life turned into a nightmare, she only found solace in the corners of her house. Apart from that, she loved to stitch. Akash, to everyone’s surprise, refrained from going to fishing and instead joined his mother for working at the factory. But this was a totally transformed Akash. Even though it was a heavy drudgery at the factory, Akash was in tears when he got his first income. Thirty rupees. Back home, he went flying to Nalini Boudi. She smiled earnestly and patted Akash on his head. “Well done Akash. I knew you are a responsible man.” Akash was elated at this encouragement. But he was again lured to waste his money on a tattoo. Nalini felt sorry for the boy. She saw the conflicts raging inside Akash. She saw how he suffered to control himself from temptations. Nalini was just twenty. Her husband, Sunil worked at the Andamans and seldom came home. After marriage, he couldn’t come till then. Nalini spent a lonely life in the remote village. She had a determination to do something. In this isolated place, she tried to inspire Akash into a good person. They slowly became a habit of each other. Akash would bring flowers for Nalini’s daily worship. Nalini would complain, “You’re making me invalid, Akash.” Akash would laugh and sit down for a cup of tea. Nalini Boudi’s tea was nectar. Akash looked on as Nalini Boudi stirred the tea carefully adding a bit more milk so that it was a rich creamy colour. The two unlikely friends gossiped happily during the course. Akash never missed the vulgar gatherings with the boys at the teashop. In the evenings, they would go for their odd strolls to the river. Precisely, Nalini went to wash dirty clothes and Akash accompanied her. The river flowed serenely. Nalini loved rivers but she couldn’t swim. “Akash, do you know to swim?” “I can swim to the other side. I’m the best swimmer here. Do you want to see?” “No, no. You’ll catch a cold if you swim now.” The sun set slowly painting the sky with an orange-pink tinge. The river water turned liquid gold. Birds flew overhead calling to each other. Nalini’s unlined face was softly illuminated by the last sun rays. Akash breathed slowly as the crickets started to chirp. Nalini Boudi’s eyelashes were pruned, her nose was elegantly curved and she had pale red lips. He had to refrain himself from an unknown instinct. They returned to their homes. Akash had surrendered all his marbles, playing cards and his most treasured fishing rod to Nalini. She used to say, “ There’s nothing a man can’t do. You can mend your ways if you try hard.” Akash said, “You have a beautiful heart, Nalini Boudi.” Nalini often came to their house. When she came, her cheerful presence lit up the gloomy hut. Rakhi also loved Nalini very much. Nalini’s optimism would heal her burdened soul. She could chat freely with Nalini, relieving all her internal torments to her. Nalini was distraught to see the plight of Rakhi. A rural Indian girl who was driven away from her husband’s place lived a meaningless life, crouched under humility. Nalini kindled the extinguished fire in Rakhi to live a dignified life again. Rakhi slowly became as jolly as earlier. One day Akash brought dainty blue bangles for Nalini. She was winnowing grain on her courtyard. Akash swiftly drew her hands into his and slipped in the bangles. Her slender hands looked even more prettier. Nalini was absolutely heartfelt. She had a childlike craze for bangles. And pickles. Akash had caught her stealing a bit of achaar from the neighbour’s house at times. She giggled in an ashamed manner on being caught. One afternoon Akash came with a large new kite. Nalini loved to watch him fly the kite while she sat relaxing in the open green field. But that day Akash found her slumped on the bed absorbed in thought. He cleared his throat. She was startled, “What’s the matter?” “Won’t you go to fly this kite? But what’s up Boudi?” Akash saw her eyes sparkle up. A deep pink blush coloured her cheeks. She wrung her hands nervously. “Sunil’s coming tomorrow.” She ran away flustered. Akash stood there rigid as an inexplicable pain clotted in his throat. A complicated string of emotions flooded him. He went back silently, subdued. Sunil returned with interesting days in Nalini’s life. Her monotonous schedule seemed as fresh as ever with some naughty youthful pranks in the breaks. Nalini would brew a black sugarless tea for Sunil. He would blurt out in disgust but then Nalini would escape out, suppressing her outbursts of laughter. In late afternoons, the two would sit for a quiet lunch. Sunil mixed the rice with dal and a spicy vegetable curry. It was his favourite. He missed these very much in the faraway islands. Nalini waited expectantly as she glanced at her husband. “This is delicious, Nalini. You won’t get these homely flavours back there, you know. It’s been so long I haven’t eaten anything with such satisfaction.” The strain to cook the food in front of the blazing fire seemed to dissolve in a blink. Nalini listened wide eyed to the curious stories of Sunil- the coral reefs, the forests, the funny tribals and the vast inky blue SEA! Her adventurous spirit drifted across these lands through her husband’s eyes. She also recounted the stories to Akash excitedly. She had so much to tell about Sunil, his loving nature and his wonderful experiences. But Akash seldom came nowadays. He tried to avoid Nalini. Nalini noticed that Akash was very sober, very absent minded. He listened to Nalini with a faded smile, but they were not the intimate friends as earlier. There was an abrupt barrier, a solid one, between these two. Aakash’s life was suddenly empty, a lingering void consuming him slowly. In his harsh teenage years, he had entwined around Nalini, who was like the ambrosia of his life. His singular devotion to Nalini had transformed him from a ruffian into a human. Akash realised, he had drained all his emotions and eagerness for Nalini. When he no longer had a presence in her life, he could not bear it. No one scolded him anymore for losing his savings in a bet with the bad guys next village. Akash desperately tried to continue a decent life, living each and every moment just as he had learnt from Nalini. Strolling alone in the scorching heat, collecting feathers, running wild in the green fields and licking the sour ‘kul achar’ with delight. Nalini always told, “There’s a lot of tiny things you can do to enjoy your life. There’s a lot more to explore yourself! You never know, life holds such wonders!” He pulled on the shell of his body during his daily factory hours. He worked hard dripping with sweat. Nalini’s laughter echoed in his ears, her sweaty face loomed in front of him, her jingling anklets very often disturbed him in his sleep. Nalini was a busy house-wife now. But she was delighted. Akash saw her engrossed in preparing home-made sweets for Sunil. She just didn’t need Akash’s help to break the coconuts. Sunil was an expert about coconuts and retrieving their juicy flesh. Though Nalini offered Akash sweet once, he bit his lips determinedly and denied. Then his suppressed tears would stream down his cheeks, hot and salty. He couldn’t understand, couldn’t explain. Everything was so normal. His mother was bothered as always, muttering under her breath while she washed the utensils. Rakhi was sewing clothes in her new sewing machine. She had sold her gold bangles and bought it. She was no more a living corpse. She was enlivened. Rakhi had herself thrown away her veil of hesitation, she had come out in the open to live an independent life. She again cherished thousands of dreams in her glimmering eyes. She has emerged victorious in the challenge of life. Nalini Boudi was her good angel who taught her to stand up, to look straight into the tyrant eyes of the society and proudly reveal one’s true self. But Akash had failed. He looked gloomily at a bunch of strong creepers climbing around a huge tree. The yellow leaves of the Swarnalata has carpeted the canopy completely. It was a parasitic plant. It could die instantly without the tree. It was maybe like Akash. He was smoking once again with Deep in the bamboo thicket. Deep was devastated to see the pathetic condition of Akash. He stood by his side and pressed his hands warmly. “Guru, let’s go away from here. Far away. You and me. Nobody will know. We’ll do anything we want.” “Better say, nobody will care, Deep.” Akash sighed. Deep was lost for words for a minute. Then he felt a twinge of pain in his heart as Akash hadn’t even considered him as someone who cares for him. When Akash was all enchanted by Nalini Boudi, who had ever given a thought about him? Deep was ignored by his friend day after day. But he never left him alone. He never left Akash in his time of need. From their childhood, Deep had always fulfilled his demands. Akash could share everything with him, they were partners in criminal. Deep loved his obstinate friend very much. He was secretly proud of possessing Akash. But, it was he himself who had turned away from Deep. But he had truly forgiven Akash. How could he remain angry with him? The two boys embraced each other passionately. “I love you, Akash. Believe me. I really do.” Deep whispered in a shivering voice. He called Akash by his name for the first time. Akash felt a chill crawling down his spine. He ruffled Deep’s brown hair. “Yes, I love you too. We’ll catch the train tonight.” The existence of the two boys was erased from Dhudhulia totally. They were forgotten like fallen leaves as they roamed forever in a labyrinth of dark worlds. But Nalini felt restless sometimes. She felt a slight pang of guilt. Then she said to herself, “It was just that the rains kept on and killed the spring. I’m sorry Akash.”
author: 01 Anupurba
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Ankita  Thakur; Krishnagopal Shreshtha; Maithili  Joshi; Priya Kuriyan

title: Symphony of Solitude
text: I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. I yawned widely, as I said, “Hello?” I pushed my dry hair aside, when Alyssa’s highly pitched, bird-sweet voice squeaked in excitement, “I got it, Audrey, I got it!” I gave her a confused look. She continued, “I got the email, my biggest wish in life has finally come true.” I stared at her, still thinking. “Bridgeton Academy reached out to me! I’ve been enlisted to attend the 2-year course in Design!” she screamed, deafeningly. “Wow, that’s great! I am so-“, before I could move further, she popped again, “And get this, it’s starting this November! I’m going to the UK!” She’d been waiting for this since forever, this was her chance. Alyssa was my only friend, and I enjoyed her company through both happy and dismal days; naturally, I was proud of her. “I’m speechless! I’m so happy!” I said in delight, grinning. “Thanks, thanks! Okay then, see you at school - I’ve got to tell everyone else too!” she promptly said, and hung up. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. My once pleased, cheery face turned off; that smile slowly faded. I started feeling uneasy at heart, like I’d lost the excitement for her achievement. What was wrong? Was I jealous? “No, never!”, I thought. Then what was it? That saddening feeling killed me. I glanced at the clock, and decided to get ready for school. I looked at the mirror, and thought to myself, “Alyssa sounded thrilled and eager. But she seemed to be missing a tiny detail…once she moves, we’re done. Would we still be as close? It maybe tolerable for her - she has such an extroverted personality, she can mingle with anyone. But what about me? I’ll be forlorn..I have to face those rude students again..all alone.” I realized it was the fear of loneliness that made me feel so overwhelmed. I remembered how I was no one without Alyssa. But I decided not to confront her about our long-distance friendship, considering she was excited. “She’ll give it a thought.” I somehow rushed into my school bus. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. Alyssa was gleaming in ecstasy. Well, that’s explainable; it was a momentous achievement of her life. But the fact that she’d leave me soon didn’t hurt any less. I stared out the window, sighing, when Alyssa shrieked, “Audrey! Earth to Audrey!” I didn't realize that I zoned out through the journey. “You there?”, she asked, giggling. “Oh, yeah! I’m here. I’m just uh..tired.” I said confusingly. “It’ll be alright, perhaps that’s why Alyssa hasn’t spoken about it yet. She knows we’ll figure it out.” I thought, and instantly joined Alyssa’s conversation. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. The next 60 days were the fastest of my life; I relished Alyssa’s company, and there was just a week left before she moved. I hushed up about my discomfort, because I thought she would bring it up first. But it was surprising to me, that all she cared about was how she planned to make new friends. The next morning, I went to Alyssa’s house to help her pack. Alyssa always left the door open when I was visiting; she thought my skinny hands would hurt attempting to twist the knob; She was humorous! I entered her room, and she yelled,”Books!” I exclaimed,”Hahhhh?”, “No, No!!! Don’t step there! Sharp nails!” she went on. “Woah, okay! This is an utter mess!” I somehow leaped onto her bed, crossed my legs over her suitcase and began to talk. “Alyssa, there’s something we need to discuss; I hope you don’t take it in the wrong sense. This is mere planning for what is ahead.”, my dull, thin voice shivered. “Yep! Go on!”, she gracefully signaled. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. “So..uh..it’s just that I was thinking about our friendship over the next few years, since you’ll be away. You think distance communication will work out for us, eh?” I hesitantly began. Without a second thought, still with that immense smile on her face, she said, “Yes, yes! Why will it not? My friends in the UK would love to talk to you, too!” I nervously chuckled. “Now come on, hold this up for me, I’ll get it out!” She jumped onto the packing swiftly. I thought she didn’t bother too much. That fear of loneliness still resided in me. I grew quieter near her, disturbed. The day drew closer; November 6th. Alyssa was to leave that night for her flight at 10:50 PM. I had dinner with her. We spoke awkwardly in the car as the airport approached. I hardly realized my face turned pumpkin red. We got out; I went in for a cozy hug. Her tears covered my spiky hair, and I held her as tightly as I could. It was time; She had to leave. “Wherever you are, you shall forever remain in my heart.” I said, and turned away. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. Over the coming days, I hardly spoke to her; we texted away for a while - she was caught up unpacking boxes, filling forms for school…I gave her the time she needed; a week later, we finally video called. I had realized by then that Alyssa was such a huge part of my life that I couldn’t carry it out fulfillingly in her absence. It was different to talk to her again; I was outcast at school, once everyone found out my social skills were underdeveloped and that I felt uncomfortable with topics they discussed; yet, Alyssa was so busy making new friends that she soon forgot about me. She shared pictures of her new companions, spoke about her school and disregarded my issues. At one point, I stopped trying. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. Two months passed, my bond with Alyssa had totally broken apart; she didn’t return my texts or calls, she uploaded pictures with her new friends, and it seemed like her personality took a total turn. I noticed over time, that our relationship turned out to be more fake. Yes - I was happy she had a new life, but my introverted personality made me feel for things like ignorance, and that’s when I lived in loneliness. However, I was extremely focused in class since I didn’t care about my social life; I started sinking in too much - I gave up on myself. I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. One fine January morning, I was in English class, and something hit me. It made a difference to my mindset. My teacher was talking about how her roommate made up a huge part of her daily life, and now that she settled in a home of her own, she felt lonely. She said, “The roses that bloomed in the terrace today kept me company through my correction spree instead of my roommate. You don’t need to be in someone’s company to feel fulfilled. You, yourself are enough. Daily life is so eventful that the subtle things embedded in them often slip off sight, but it’s those things that support you more than ever.” That struck me rapidly. “Anyway, that’s what I remembered when the poet spoke about the ‘red-red roses’. Let’s not deviate now!” I sank into the sea of thoughts in my mind. “Was that what I needed? Can this loneliness ever turn into solitude?” I woke up to an abrupt pop music blaring at my ears. The rising Sun’s beaming lights poked my dreamy eyes to awake, while I cleared my blurry vision. I picked up my phone; It was Alyssa, video calling me at 6AM, when the morning hardly awoke. While I walked home that day, I smiled radiantly. I realized that just me, making the most of myself, is all I needed. I just needed to know myself better and help my heart have control over what made me happy. “It doesn’t even hurt to try. It’s not a big deal.”, I thought. Obviously, it wasn’t as easy as I assumed to change, but I soon began to notice so many small things that occured on a daily basis. I drank my cup of tea with nature’s company; the chirping birds sat over the grills of the window pane to greet me. The color of those balloons the kid in the basement flew all day splashed brightness onto my empty day’s canvas. The music I heard on my way home from the house next door helped me dive into my imagination. That cool breeze the trees chose to play calmed my perplexed mind, that cycle ride every evening helped me recollect the day. I started paying gratitude to things I never imagined I would; to every sip of water, I thanked God. I spoke to the plants in my garden; often, the leaves would gently fly to, perhaps, regard my experiences. I can’t believe this, but I think all I needed to realize was that I was enough to do great things. I enjoyed my own company; I spent time honing my skills. I figured what writing meant to me - a medium for expression, and here I am - my first story, out to the world - my journey of believing in the ‘Symphony of Solitude’. I can’t believe this, but I think all I needed to realize was that I was enough to do great things. I enjoyed my own company; I spent time honing my skills. I figured what writing meant to me - a medium for expression, and here I am - my first story, out to the world - my journey of believing in the ‘Symphony of Solitude’.
author: Divya Satish

title: The Seasons of Life
text: I t was a bright day. The sky was a blurry concoction of pale blue and creamy swirls, and the air smelled as sweet as honey. The mustard fields of Sarnagar were resplendent. Delicate golden sunlight showered gentle kisses of warmth on the dainty blooms. There was cheer in the atmosphere. Bright yellow cheer that did not match the dull grey shades of Vasanti’s despondence. She was lost in a world of gloom, oblivious to the exuberance in the air. She only saw blue sorrow and hopelessness. She wanted to escape this sadness, so she recalled the sweetest, most delightful memories of her elder brother, Karan. How they had enjoyed sips of frothy, sweet and wholesome lassi together! She thought of the day she’d turned thirteen, and how happy Karan had been. He had said that his little Vasi had become a big girl. Vasi. Only he had ever called her that. She remembered that day as the brightest one that year. How badly she missed those days she spent with her brother- her joy, her world, her everything; who was not with her anymore, who had gone to Samargarh to fight for their country. Noble, idealistic Karan, who joined the Raja’s army so that little children-and his dear sister Vasi- would never have to live in fear, who assured her that everything would be fine; that no matter what, he will always be there at her side, watching over her. But how could she not face the reality? A rough peasant-turned-foot- soldier could only get so far, and he and his brothers-in-arms were shipped away like livestock. Vasanti was dwelling upon memories of Karan when her friend, Khushi, suddenly came up to her. Khushi was like the sun at dawn, she always brought light and bliss to the ones around her. She could not bear to see Vasanti sad, and tried to console her by telling her that wherever Karan was, he wanted his sister to smile and be satisfied with life. Khushi endeavoured to tell her that with time, things change just like the cycle of seasons. We are not fond of changes and are scared to replace the old and accept the new. Everyday, the Sun sets but the hopeful Earth knows another dawn would break after the slumber of night. Vasanti really wished that she could be as hopeful as Khushi. But she knew that everyone did not care about Karan like they did. For the Raja, he was just another soldier. Vasanti just could not sail her boat in a sea of hope like Khushi. She once had faith that Karan would survive, but then she woke up from her dreams and learned to embrace the reality. The odds did not seem to favour him. Vasanti abjectly regretted letting her brother leave. She received no news of him. But when some weeks passed by, the dreary shades of hopelessness in Vasanti’s life started gaining colour. It was nearly spring, and she had to work at the mustard fields. Mustard flowers were Karan’s favourite, so the blossoms which she always associated with exuberance welled up bittersweet emotions. It was Vasanti’s birthday the next day. She missed Karan’s enthusiasm to celebrate her birthday every year. The next day, as she rose up from sleep and started working on the field, Khushi went running towards her. The expression on her face, which was always so composed and cheerful, looked far from peaceful. “The-the Raja….has surrendered … nearly the entire force was -”, she could not say anything further, did not even need to. Vasanti knew that this would happen someday, yet she fell down, shocked that Khushi had declared Karan deceased. The tiny spark of hope planted deep down inside her heart that Karan would survive, extinguished. She wanted to say something, but no words came out. It was as if all the colour she finally regained was getting drained away from her life again. She frantically ran to her hut, as if it would rid her of all her misery. She no longer cared about what was happening in the world. Pounding on the door in bright red urgency shook her out of her melancholy reverie. She opened the door. The voice that spoke was pained, yet heartbreakingly joyous. “Vasi.” it said. Though the winter had lasted too long, truly, it was spring now.

title: The Caking Disaster
text: Holly lived with her father in the city in a comfortable house. They looked almost identical, with the same black hair, nose, face shape etc., except Holly’s eyes were brown instead of black. She loved her father very much. One day, she decided to bake a cake for her father’s birthday. She needed flour, eggs, butter, sugar, salt, milk, baking soda, vanilla essence, some bowls, a whisk and a tin to pour the cake batter into. She tied up her hair before gathering the ingredients. She got out the bag of flour, and kept it on the kitchen counter. She felt a breeze on the back of her neck. While pouring the flour into the bowl, it slipped from her hands and coated the kitchen floor! POOF! She didn’t notice her hair-tie had fallen to the floor. But there was still enough flour needed, so she dumped the remaining flour in the first bowl, which was for dry ingredients. Then she added some sugar, but she put her hand in the jar to taste it (because she had put salt instead of sugar once) and now her hands were very sticky! CHIP-CHIP! She sighed and washed her hands. She added a pinch of salt and some baking soda next. Now, in the second bowl she had to add eggs. She tapped them lightly but they wouldn’t crack! So she applied more force but still no cracks. In her frustration, she applied so much force that the eggs cracked within moments, but there were pieces of eggshells everywhere. CRACK! Ugh! What a bad day this was turning out to be! She put the sticks of butter in the microwave to melt, but burnt her fingers because she touched the small bowl of melted butter while it was still very hot. She blew on her fingers to soothe the burns. FOO-FOO! She waited for the bowl to cool down, and poured the melted butter in the bigger bowl. She poured the milk, but poured it from too high a height and it splashed everywhere! SPLISH-SPLASH! Lastly she added the vanilla essence. Just two or three drops were enough. She then put all the ingredients of both the wet and dry bowls in possibly the biggest bowl ever made! It was so big that at-least two newborn babies would fit inside comfortably. She mixed and mixed and mixed with the whisk until her arms were sore. She coated the baking tin with some butter so the baked cake wouldn’t stick to the tin. Then she poured the cake batter into the tin. The batter looked a bit weird to her. She almost put the tin inside the oven but then remembered that she forgot to preheat the oven. She waited for almost twenty minutes and then put the tin inside the oven. She thought, “What a disastrous day this is turning out to be! But at-least Father will be happy when he sees the cake I made for him.” She cleaned the kitchen while the cake baked, but only managed one half when the oven bell rang. DING! She put the mittens on and carefully removed the cake out of the oven. She cleaned the other half of the kitchen while the cake cooled down and then took the cake out of the tin. It was perfect! She waited until her father came home from work, and wished him a “Happy Birthday!” and showed him the cake. Her father said, “Thank you!” and hugged her very tight, but the only thought that came into her head at the moment was ‘PHEW!’

title: Which stream?
text: Namaste, I am Shobu, a teenager who loves exploration, quizzing, and studies. I know, I know, you might wonder how a person can love studies, you know once you start focusing on subjects, you will feel they are interesting, and quizzing helps me add more to my studies. It's a happy bright Monday morning, and I have to get ready for school. Today is going to be an exciting one as we going to have a career-building workshop. As it's my first time, I wonder what we are going to learn! After having a yummy meal, I am off to school. On my way, my best friend Gauri joins me. We discuss today's workshop. I asked her if she had any idea about it. Nodding her head she said, "Yes, my sister had this once, but after the workshop, she was in great confusion." This left me curious. I couldn't help myself as I wanted to know more about the workshop. So, I went to my class teacher miss Reeta(She is the sweetest and the best teacher I ever had), and asked her more about it. She said," This workshop helps you to know which career you want to choose in your future and how to work on it." Well, now I started to get a brief idea of what was going to happen. We had our workshop after recess. WORKSHOP IN PROGRESS... We all gathered in the auditorium(A grand room that looks just like a movie theatre). The workshop started. The teachers explained the importance of studying and working hard. We enjoyed many brain-puzzling games like checkers and lights out. But then, came a serious part, the teachers provided us with many options for having a career in different fields and said us to choose one of them. At first, I thought it would be easy but in the end, my thoughts were hijacked as there were more than 50 options and we had to choose one of them. The teachers then said that it was just a mini-test and we had nothing to worry about. Now, they explained to us thoroughly about many career options and the trending career options like Artificial Intelligence. In the end, they said," We are going to have another workshop but first you'll have to choose a stream in your class 11th and this is where you'll begin to focus more on career building and the profession you want." Stream! Now, what's that? Oh My God! There are a lot of things we have to think about before choosing a profession!! But we are Gen Z kids and the first thing we do to know about something..... GOOGLE! So I searched what is a stream and which stream to choose after class 10th. I got to know that these are particular subjects we choose and further we deep study about them in college. Well, the second question was the toughest of all, Which stream to choose? Some sites said to science streams like PCB(physics, chemistry, biology) or PCM(physics,chemistry, math's) as they had a variety of professions to choose from, while others said to choose a stream from your strongest subjects. Well, I was strong in many subjects (as I said earlier I love studying) and was curious to know each subject. Thinking about this further made me feel irritated and confused so I just shut the phone. Mom was watching all this from a distance. She made me calm and said to ask my teacher about this. The next day, I asked Gauri about this. She said," Let's do a thing, my parents said me to take commerce, why don't you take the same stream as mine, like that, we'll always be together." I felt happy hearing this but my confusion didn't go away. I wasn't able to focus on my lessons as I was stressed out about which subject to choose. Even madam Reeta was absent that day. The next day, madam Reeta noticed that I wasn't focused on my lessons. She asked me," What's wrong dear? Where have you lost your focus?" I replied "Ma'am I can't figure out which subject to choose after class 10th. During the last workshop, all my friends were able to figure out their dream stream. I feel like an odd one out." Miss Reeta smiled and said," Dear you don't need to get to know your stream within a jiffy. You are in class 8th. You have two more years. Take your time, think thoroughly, and then come to a conclusion as this is one of the most important decisions. For now, focus on the current lessons. "fewww" with a sigh of relief and happiness, I thanked miss Reeta. 2 years later... Namaste again! I am back after two years and have figured out which stream to choose. After two wonderful years of great exploration, I found out that I was a science buff and loved to help people. So I decided to choose PCB(physics, chemistry, biology) stream and have decided to become a doctor. Well, I am still curious to know in which part of the human body I will do specialization. But the answer to this question...only time will tell. Moral- Some decisions take time. So just take a pause, think thoroughly, and then conclude.

title: Beauty is within
text: It was a long time ago, when a baby girl was born. There was only one problem this baby had been born with an unforgiving face. she was ugly, brutal, dull and truly the most hideous looking child in the world. When her parents saw her ugly face they were ashamed and angry that they have given birth to a monster. They hid her in their house for days, until they realized that they couldn't hide her forever. No child wanted to play with her, the only creature that was forgiving was the pig her parents had bought her for Christmas. her mother had just finished breaking a mirror. At that moment the girl was confused. Why had her mother broken all the mirrors? Why had she never seen her reflection? Why was her only friend a pig? One day she went to church and began to walk. Her eyes searched the church trying to find her reflection and something at the front cau ght her eye. After seeing her reflection, a scream ripped out of her lungs. She heated her appearance. She cried and cried and slept. Next morning she spent the whole day in her room. She heard the pig crying from the window because it hadn't seen her since morning. As soon as the pig saw the girl it started jumping. She realized that if her pet can love her so much then why can't she her self. That day she decided to accept herself as she is and live her life happily without thinking about other people. We should always love ourselves no matter what because no one is born ugly we are just born in a judgemental society.
