title: The Invasion Of the Ghosts
text: In this story you will be reading about the adventures of a girl who defeats an army of Ghosts which was summoned by mean and selfish man for his benefits. The spell was taken from Wikipedia which is in Sanskrit and is for summoning the Ghost 'Preta'. Hope you enjoy.:) Anandi Dhapase It was the night before Halloween, me and my 5 friends were having a sleepover and what better way to start it than a horror story, wrapped in blankets and hot cocoa in our hands the agony began. “Hey Aarna, I have a really cool story that would knock your socks off,” said Annu. “I’m all ears.” said Ira. “It is said that there was a mysterious Book, nobody knew what it does. It was said to be in a cottage surrounded by haunted woods. Surprisingly it was so close to our school.” “Annu, I wanna hear more, quite fascinating,” said Tania. “My grandma told me that when she was a little girl, she and her 3 friends- decided to go on a camping trip. My Grandma and her friends packed the essentials and left, they reached the camping site and started a camp fire and fixed the tents. Arvind said that they decided to look around a bit in the woods. My Grandma refused and she thought it was dangerous but their curiosity carried them away, even after warning them they didn’t listen. They made up my grandma’s mind, she took a diary and a pen and they all went deeper into the woods. ‘We found a cottage but saw nothing special’, wrote my grandma in her diary, There were just some basic wood furniture, few torches. To their amaze, the hut looked clean inside as if someone had been there. Just then Arvind accidently flipped a switch that was disguised as a torch and fell in a pit, then in an attempt to save himself he grabbed Shyam and Vinod’s hands while falling but they lost their balance in an attempt to save Arvind. My grandma ran toward the camping site to get some rope but when she got back Shyam said that it was no pit but seems to be a secret passage, light was seen at the end, following it they found a small library, all books covered in dust except a book half-open on a reading table, 3 words were written. Arvind said “Hey its written in Sanskrit, let me spell it – Aaiyyani Lavalian Gatisaman, nothing happened, oh well it was fun.” Shyam said “Hey Anjali can you check on the camping site and make sure it is safe we will catch you later”. My grandma left back for the camp and waited, but after that my grandma heard nothing from them, and she was never able to see them again. We all were so engrossed in the story that we lost track of time. It was 5 in the morning. “Wow, I’m, I’m speechless” I said. “Too bad we don’t know what happened to those kids.” said Priya. “Anyways, thank you for coming it’s been a really pleasure hanging out with you guys.” Said Annu. I got on my cycle and went home, got dressed for school and stood near the bus stop waiting for my bus to school. I replied. “Where is it?” He asked. “It is in the woods near our school.” I spoke. Our conversation was stopped when my bus arrived, “See yah Mr. Akash”. “Bye” said Mr. Akash and left for the office. “Sir, I just found a perfect plan to destroy that school,” said Mr. Akash. “Hmm go on and better make it snappy,” said Mr. Mahendra. “A girl told me that there is a book that can summon ghosts,” said Mr. Akash. “You are very gullible, instead work on the design of my golf course”, said the bossy Builder, “I’ll bulldoze the school. The people were protesting a lot, not to take the school down.” Mr. Akash was so upset that he went off in the woods to find the book. After a while he found the cottage, saw the book lying on the floor half open. The spooky cottage scared him to death. He took the book and ran for life. “I got it, Builder Mahendra,” he showed the book excitedly. “It’s useless, ghosts are not real,” said the Builder. “We will see about that, why don’t you do the honor.” Mr. Akash said. “Fine, anything to get you out of this ghostly venture, 'Aaiyyani Lavalian Gatisaman', see, nothing happened.” Just then the book started glowing, hovering in the air and POOF! The lights went off, all the windows and doors closed abruptly. “Who woke me up, you better have a good reason, if not, get ready to be vanished.” Said the Ghost like an angered lion. Out of wits, gathering courage, the Builder muttered, “I have summoned you to ask a small favor, we want you to destroy the school that is near the haunted woods.” “But what will I get in return” thundered the Ghost. “Hm, whatever your heart desires,” said the Builder. “I will ask that later, I need time to gain my full power, midnight to be exact.”, “Well, fine, do it as soon as possible.” Said the Builder and hurried to find his assistant. “Oh, there you are, good job on finding a solution to our problem”. “Why thank you, don’t you think? the school is special, there is a reason that it is still standing for 60 years and it should not be destroyed for your luxuries, it’s not a wise choice.” “Oh! you have to sacrifice somethings to get few things, besides, we have many better schools.” “But they are not like this one.” Said Akash, “Do you want this job or not.” said the bossy builder, “Yes, I am sorry.” Said Akash, “I’ll go and check whether the ghost is ready.” Said the Builder. “Are you ready,” Builder asked. “Yes, Aaiyyani Lavalian Gatisaman! ”, roared the ghost and suddenly there were hundreds of his kind marching to the school. “Ok, my minions, now gain your physical form and start creating havoc.” I heard some noise of something crashing but I was half asleep. But the noise grew louder and louder so I got up from my bed and went outside. The noise was coming from the direction of my school, I thought maybe my ears were ringing. Although, I knew that everyone were sleeping, I called my friend Ira. “Hello, Aarna.” said Ira. “Hey, by any chance do you hear crashing noises, strange sounds.” I spoke, “yah I do, it’s coming from our school.” said Ira, “should we go and check.” I asked, “yah, I’ll call others”. Me and my 5 buddies rode our bicycles to the school. Though we were scared on what our parents would say curiosity pushed us. When we reached there, we hid behind a rock and watched. We were astonished to see huge giant like figures breaking our school and the Builder and his assistance standing and the Builder gladly directing the destruction. I noticed that the Builder had some kind of book lying beside him. I told this to my friends. Annu said that this is the same ghost summoning book that my grandma told me about. “Ok, I’ll go and get it.” I went silently and ran away with the book as Builder was busy with monstrous work. I opened the book and read the first page, first line. ‘Where there is darkness, let there be light’, “What does that mean” asked Priya. “I heard; Ghosts are afraid of light and it’s only 15 minutes till dawn.” I said, “that means we have to distract them for 15 minutes till the sun comes up, they will pass out.” Said kaya, “Ok, I have a plan, Ira and Tania, figure out a way to destroy the book, Annu and Kaya, take care of the Builder and Priya and I will lure the ghosts “Do you think we can do this as they are more in number”, said Priya. “United we can. Alone we can do so little but together we can do so much.” I and Priya teased the ghost mob and started running when they followed us in the wood. Tania destroyed the book by ripping the pages out of the book. There were only 5 minutes till dawn and the ghosts lost their power the moment the book got destroyed. The sun came up and they vanished. in I was so happy we saved our school. My friends left for their home and while I was leaving. I saw last page of the book lying on the ground, I picked it up, it read……. ‘Evil things are coming in your way only you can save the citizens, Aarna.’
author: ANANDI  DHAPASE

title: Piku's Little World
text: In a village called Pinchak, there lived a boy named Piku. He was quite an adventurous guy and mostly loved summer afternoons. He was very kind to the animals around him. He played with the cats that laid down the window ledge. He chased the sparrows off the balcony as he thought it was a hobby to do it. He took care of the little squirrels that lived on the mango tree. But, the most awaiting thing is that Piku loved the stories her mummy narrated before going to nap in the afternoon. The afternoons heat made the cats to curl upon The sparrows to slip into their nests and the squirrels slipped to hid in the leaves. The stories read by mummy gave Piku great sleep, but sometimes mummy just snores in the middle of the story, but Piku was awake listening to her loud snores go ' khhhh, khhhh, khhhh' He was afraid to even shut his eyes to get some sleep as there were some scary faces on the wall, that made him terrified. Piku doesn't like summer evenings when the lights went off. Piku huffed and puffed to get the precious lantern. As soon as the lantern was lit, mosquitos sang 'pnn... pnn...pnn', the geckos ran fast as flash like 'tut..tut..tut' and the crickets called it's friends by 'crr..crr..crr'. During the night, Piku always goes to the terrace with his father to see the black sky. It was enormous, they counted the stars in the sky and spotted animals like lion, bear, horse etc. that occur in the sky. When the lights come back they were like 'aaaaah'! One fine day, a saddest thing happened to Piku. When he returned from the school in the afternoon mummy was not seen anywhere in the house. He asked the cats, squirrels and sparrows, but had no reply. The cat licked Piku's hand and purred as if it was sad. The house which was usually filled with joy and happiness was now silent as a snail. Piku saw mummy's spectacles and his favorite book and saw his father sitting in a corner, depressed. He hugged his father and asked "Where is Mummy?". His Father with a sad face said she will not come forever and ever. Piku did not understand and rushed to the balcony with his favorite book. Everyday he played with his friends and waited for his mummy to narrate a story. There was no one to read a story for him during afternoons. The shadows became even more terrifying that he could not sleep for days. There were ants crawling around, creepy cockroaches, big spiders and horrifying ghosts. One afternoon, Piku turned a page from the book and 'oh........', kings, queens, fairies and witches suddenly came in front of him. The words made to do actions like laugh, sing, cry and dance. Since that day he read new stories all alone and now his dreams were filled with happiness again. In the dreams there were soft and fluffy rabbits, beautiful golden trees with tasty looking apples. The most beautiful and mesmerizing thing in the dreams was his mummy's biggest smile. Piku missed his mummy so much that tears flow in his eyes on seeing his mother's smile. I, as a narrator feel sorry for Piku and I am sure that his confidence would make him a good man in the coming Future.
author: RUTHVIK VENKATA

title: A Journey into the Past
text: A heartwarming sight greeted me once I opened the car door. My home. I'm back to my roots in Kolkata. I mean, Seattle is nice, but to be back in your hometown, that's a feeling in a whole other universe. I'm John, a regular 15 year old living in Seattle. I was born and brought up here, in Kolkata, before we all moved overseas when I was ten. I remember being so excited to leave five years ago. Now, I feel a little guilty. My mother then stepped out of the car and took a deep breath. "Aah!" She exclaimed. "It feels so nice to be back. So many memories, I just can't believe-" She didn't finish. I could tell my mother was overwhelmed with emotions. "Come on Mom" I said, giving her a bear hug. "Now's not the time to get emotional. Let's go inside." Then, I heard a voice which made my heart leap with joy. "You promised me a tour, remember?" Said Jennifer from behind me. I wheeled around and threw my arms around her. "You're here?" I exclaimed in surprise. "When? How?!" "It was a surprise!" She replied with a smile. "What matters is I'm here now. Kolkata is my home too." Jennifer. My best friend since I was three. We went to the same school together. We still do now. She too moved when we did. She's rather short for her age. But her beauty, intelligence and attitude makes up for it. She is by far the sweetest and kindest person I know. "Come on then" I said, leading her onto the front porch. My old home, a treat to the eyes. A massive, three storey tall building, topped off with marvelous engineering. Weather had taken its toll on it however, some portions of the walls being covered with moss. To my eyes, it did not do anything to mask its beauty. My mom unlocked the door. It opened quite easily, which was a bit suspicious. A house which was left locked up for five years should at least take a little effort to open. I pushed open the old wooden door, and was greeted with a bang, a shower of confetti and a bright light. I saw a table, already set up with a huge cake right in the middle. Going closer, I could see the words 'Happy Birthday John' written in red across the top. Then it hit me. "Oh my!" I squealed. "I thought you forgot." "We would never." Said my mom. "Happy birthday my darling." Saying this, she kissed me on the cheek. I returned a kiss and thanked her. Turning towards Jennifer, I asked "Jen, did you know?" "Everything!" She said with a smile. "Me and your parents were planning this for months. Happy birthday!!" "Thank you" I said. "We came in here earlier today." Explained my mom. "Jen decorated, I baked your cake. Speaking of the cake, you better cut it now." Mom handed me a knife. I cut the cake while she and Jennifer sang 'Happy Birthday'. I took a slice and fed it to my mom, then Jen and I ate the rest of it. The cake, we're going to take home. After a while, we all sat down to chat about our times here in Kolkata. I got to know a lot of interesting things about Jennifer. Surprisingly, even my mom shared incidents she had never told me before. It was nearing noon. A few minutes, and a million funny experiences later, mom spoke up. "Jen, why don't you go with John and see the upper floors? I'm sure you'll find it quite nice to be back there." "Sure, why not?" She replied. I took the keys and led her upstairs. There was a locked door at the top of the stairs. Unlocking it was quite a challenge, since the lock had rusted over the years. Once I managed to open it, I stepped onto the floor. There was something very unique in our house. The floor plans of the second and first floor were exactly alike. This was a specimen of the excellent planning in the 1960's. I couldn't help let out a laugh. It just felt so good to be back there. Without any delay, me and Jen went to the balcony. "I missed this view." Said Jennifer, taking a deep breath. "I did too" I replied. We made our way back indoors and entered my old room. "Remember this room?" I asked Jen. "Of course" She replied. "I've attended every birthday party of yours in here." She laughed. "It's funny how it all changed." "Yeah" I said. That was when something caught my eye. Something shiny was lying on the floor. Naturally, there was no power in the house. I had to switch on my phone's flashlight to examine it closely. Upon lighting it up, I realised what it was. It was a round brooch. The kind that can be worn with fancy, colourful clothes. This particular one was made of metal and had a decent size. It was painted with an eye-catching shade of brilliant blue. Artificial diamonds were lined across the rim. A missive green gem was placed in the middle and was surrounded by more diamonds. It had an enchanting look to it, like it was just there, waiting for something to happen. It seemed to be willing me to pick it up. I called Jennifer over. "Have you seen this before?" I asked. "No. It's my first time coming up here since we left. We were just in the living room downstairs. I didn't come up here." "So it's not yours?" "No way." "Can it be my mom's?" "It may as well be." "I better pick it up then." I bent down and picked it up. In a matter of seconds, there was a blinding green light. I felt a vortex form around me, sucking me up into the air. A cold hand slipped into mine. It was Jen's. Her scream was the last thing I heard before I blacked out. I don't know how long I was out, I don't know. When I woke up, I saw light. It took a while for my eyes to get adjusted. I saw Jennifer, sitting quietly near a bed. I lifted my head, alerting Jen that I was awake. She walked up to me. "Good morning sleepy head" She said. "Ha ha" I said, unamused. I got up. Suddenly, I noticed something. The brooch was neatly pinned on my shirt. I could see Jennifer had noticed it too. We both stayed quiet. We stepped out of the door, a bright red one. Something felt unnatural. Something unnerving. I found a balcony, right outside the room. Bright paint and polished grills. Still, something just felt wrong. I was seeing it in Jen too. "You okay?" I asked. "No" She said. "Something is amidst." "I know, right?" I said. The view from the balcony was stunning. But, it was familiar. Too familiar. Then, the realizstion came to me. I was at my house. But, it was suddenly brand new. Completely painted, shiny glass windows and polished grills. But, how? The possibilities were endless. Jen was as pale as a ghost. There was no doubt she had realised the truth. Terrified, but at the same time intrigued, we ran out of the balcony and down the stairs. A calendar was hanging just down the hall. The circled date made our heart drop down from our chest. The 28th of October, 1984. Exactly forty years ago. There was only one answer to this. We had time travelled. The brooch has to be the one responsible. Jen suddenly put her arms around me. We both needed support. Suddenly the door burst open. We darted out of sight under stairs. Outside the door stood a young teenager, in professional sports gear. On her back was a badminton kitbag. I had no problem recognizing her. It was my mom. My mom, as a teenager. I was in a state of physical shock. My mother was here. My mother was a professional badminton player. She's a teenager! I couldn't believe it. At that moment, she spoke up, in Bengali. "Maa, I'm hungry. Can I have a snack?" A woman's face peeked out from the kitchen door. She too was very familiar to me. I've seen her in all the photos around our house. My grandma, but just about forty years old. I never knew her. She died when I was just a baby. "Chicken patties dear" She said. "But if you want to eat, go and freshen up first." "Okay maa" Said my mother and went into the bathroom. The coast was clear now. "I don't want to stay here any longer." I said in a small voice. "Agreed" Said Jennifer. We ran out of the front door, onto the road. Not bothering to move, we sat down right there. "We travelled back in time!" Exclaimed Jen "My mom was badminton player" I said breathlessly. "You didn't know!?" Asked Jen. "No" Suddenly I felt a vibration in my chest. Looking down, I saw the brooch lighting up again. Green light exploded out. "Jen?" I called out. "Right here" A voice called back. That was the last thing I heard before an excruciating noise filled my ears. The sight of my house became smaller, smaller and smaller. I slammed onto a concrete road. This time, I saw a more reassuring sight. My house was in front of me, but it was worn out. I was back in the present. A moan came from behind me. It was Jen. She had fallen in an awkward position. A small trickle of blood was coming out of her head. I kneeled down beside her. "I'm fine" She said. "No, you're not" I said sternly. My mother was in the front yard. I called out to her. She came running over to us. Noticing Jen's injury, she yelled. "What on earth are you two doing here!? How did you get hurt Jen? John, what were you thinking? " I might ask you the same question. What we're you thinking when you left badminton?" "I- How" She said, really confused. She gulped. "How did you know?" "Long story" Said Jen. "Come inside. We'll talk. Together" Said my mom in a stern tone. Not saying another word, I helped Jennifer to her feet and followed my mother inside the house.
author: Dripto De

title: I - The Woman
text: This was the age where I began experiencing the girliness in myself, the curves, my body and lastly the attention of boys in the school and nearby. My 8 th grade sessions had just begun, and I was in my own fairy world. Everything was going fine, and it hit me – PERIOD. I remember, I was a typical girl like you all, staying in the locality of Parel, a middle class crowded area of Mumbai. Life here was always running with the tickling sound of the watch – every minute mattered. In this hustling city, me Payal, a 13-year-old school going girl was living her life carefree. Making my way through the weekly market rush – I finally reached school just in time. With prayers done I finally settled down in my bench. The first 3 sessions passed with a blink and we all started gearing up for the weekly assembly – we were about to leave for the assembly hall and suddenly I felt huge pain in my stomach. I started late today for the school. It was Friday – means HOUSE Day, I wore by white house uniform, hair nicely combed with white ribbons, white socks and shoes. Never ever I had experience anything like this. I held my stomach with hands and just sat down. I cried with loud noise, which made few girls in my class stop. Pratibha asked everyone to go ahead and she helped me sit on my bench. She handed over the water bottle, asking me to sip some water. She was asking me lot of questions; did I eat properly? What I ate? Was it acidity and they were a lot. I completely lost her voice as my pain intensified. Never ever I had experience anything like this. I held my stomach with hands and just sat down. I cried with loud noise, which made few girls in my class stop. Pratibha became clueless and asked Savita and Jyoti for help. I was suddenly in middle of staring eyes. Everyone was trying their best to console me, pacify me – but it was not working. Still struggling with the pain, I started feeling some wetness in my private parts (Vagina). I held Pratibha’s hand tightly and stood up from my bench. The girls were still grazing at me with confusion – I mentioned about the wetness. Jyoti was quick to notice and found some blood on my bench. I thought that I have hurt myself, there was some wound which opened form now where and now the blood I was going to fall – I panicked. Jyoti whispered in my ears – you have got your PERIODS – Congratulations. I pushed her back, requesting her to focus on my wound and not make fun. Everyone was quiet except me going through the turbulence of my mood – shouting for bandage, asking cotton, checking my bag and what not. I was crying non-stop with all smiles around me. Finally, Jyoti put her hand around me and asked me calm down. This time I was listening to her. She was loud and clear this time – Payal you have got your periods – no worries. This is normal, we all have gone through this – only you have got them late. So, trust me and just follow what I say PERIODS – were never discussed in my family – it was always so called a woman thing. My mom never uttered a single word outside of kitchen. I was her sole assistant when she used to ask to fetch a cloth initially and later get a sanitary pad. I had to ensure that it need to brought home wrapped in newspaper without a single person in our chawl noticing it including my dad and brother. Then, it never occurred that one day I will be going through the same and was never prepared for this, hence the panic Jyoti pulled me out of my flashback – lets get you clean. She was the multitasker and at that moment my savior. First, she sent Pratibha to inform class teacher. I was holding my skirt with my hands. It was slightly covered in blood. We had to quickly make to the bathroom. Jyoti formed a group, she was in my front, me in the middle and Savita and another girl behind me. Slowly we moved to the bathroom. This was my learning moment – Jyoti requested me to handover my skirt and asked me to clean myself. I went in inside, and in next few minutes I heard a knock on the door. I slightly opened the door, Jyoti handed over a sanitary pad to me. While leaving the classroom, she had quickly taken it from her bag and slipped it in her pocket. With hands and some clear instructions, she explained me how to wear it. I was still in a state of uncertainty as to what exactly was happening to me – am I supposed to afraid or happy about this? Why today – why not on weekend when I was sitting at my home with my mom near to me. The cursing continued and again I was disturbed by another knock on the door. Jyoti asked for confirmation and asked me to come out. With little shy, I came out from the bathroom trying to cover myself as much as possible – it was of no use. Those smiling faces were still staring at me as I walked out of the bathroom. There was some cheering and Hi-Fi’s around. Looking me little calmer, Jyoti handed over my skirt back. She had washed it and tried to make it clean and dry. It was still wet but better than what it was few minutes ago. I quickly dressed up and started thanking everyone. Jyoti pulled out her mobile and googled about periods and showed it to me. Today for the first time, I was seriously thinking and talking about the periods. When my friends mentioned, I realized that this is something very natural for any girl – this is never a taboo which I should be ashamed of. My whole misunderstanding around the periods came crashing down – I felt sorry for my mom at that moment – feeling for her that how she was alone going through this without discussing it with my father. Amita maam was quick to say – Payal you have become a WOMAN today – and that engrossed on my mind and heart permanently. We all walked out of the bathroom. In a few minutes, I was totally changed with what had happened with me – my heart reached out to thousands and millions of girls in the world who must be going through same experience and there was no one to help them. By this time, our class teacher Amita maam came there – she hugged me; checking on with my health. She was relieved looking me at that moment. She appreciated Jyoti and the girls for handling that situation with maturity.... By the time I reached the school gate, Jyoti was with me holding my hand as true friend. I hugged her at the gate and said good bye. Today, while stepping out of the gate I was a totally different person – As I put my first step outside the gate, I had a loud shout – Congrats – to me – THE WOMAN and I am proud of it. Amita maam requested me to skip the assembly and go home. She informed all the concern members in the school and made sure that I get all the necessary permissions. How important small things are for a girl like me, to get all the attention and support when you needed it the most. How would I have handled this alone – may be or may be not? Moral: Period is not a taboo – don’t be ashamed, it’s a mark of becoming a WOMAN – carry it with PRIDE. I - THE WOMAN: Moral: Periods is not a taboo – don’t be ashamed, it’s a mark of becoming a WOMAN – carry it with PRIDE.

title: Colours on a Canvas
text: You work fervently; your strokes show urgency and your brush works in haste. You have no destination and yet you keep running towards it. What you have in front of you -your artwork, your career- is all a show; a pretense. You do not know where you are headed. A void of emotions swirls inside you. The cheap paints you use are worth nothing compared to the ones you drown in. Your passion is like the ocean; it retreats, letting you pick the mesmerizing shells and before you realize, it comes back, washing you away with everything you worked hard for. Paint is splashed on the canvas. It drips down, drop by drop, forming a pool of muck on the floor. A mess of colors; a mess of an artwork; a mess of emotions; a mess of you. The blaring Shostakovich string quartet in your workshop does nothing to heal your wound. It drives the blade deeper and lets all the thorns sink in. Your shattered emotions are broken mosaic; once dazzling and incandescent and now, a sorry mess on the floor. With each stroke, you cut yourself again and again and again. Your hands shake against the canvas. Everything is too bright, too loud, too dark, too silent. Everything is overwhelming. It is probably the culmination of everything that leads to your brush falling down. It has never been easy to grasp it. Your emotions have you in a chokehold. They cannot be contained inside and yet you can’t seem to let them out. You’re afraid of what will happen if you were to let go of the leash; they would spill far more than you could fathom or clean up. So you suffer. You stay put, stay silent, and let the torment consume you away. Refusing a helping hand seems the only option. You lean against the nearby wall, chest heaving. You gasp for breath as you slide down the wall and pull your knees close to you. Your whole body shudders. You should have never come here, you decide. You're wasting money, wasting expectations, wasting his time with your stupid company, wasting, wasting, and wasting. Tears stream down your face as you make yourself smaller, curling up on yourself. You shouldn’t have followed him here. He showed you stars and you believed that you could aim for them. He brought you to the shared fantasy among the two of you and you believed that you could succeed. A foolish thought, you should have known better. He could do it all; you could never. You should have stayed home, supporting him from the sidelines and chosen an entirely different field. If you don’t know what to express, how will others hear you? You’re not coming back next year. You can’t make it. You’re going home after finishing this semester. You’re done. You want him to explore the world, seek all opportunities, and get all the appreciation that is rightfully his. Because he deserves it. And you don’t. “Eddy?” his voice fills the room. You didn’t even realize he came in. No, no, no. He shouldn’t see you like this. He should be- “Why aren’t you at the exhibition?” You ask, voice muffled and still not looking up. But you do peep a little. And God, he looks ethereal as always. “Everything finished up half an hour ago. Everyone was looking for you.” You scoff softly. You know he was the only one looking for you. He doesn’t need to hear your scoff to know that you don’t believe him. Good, he knows you that well at least. Maybe you can cherish some last moments with him before you let everything slip out of your hands, like sand grains escaping your paint-stained fingers. He pushes on further, “Ms. Sumina was also looking for you. You know that this is one of the most important events of the year.” You stay silent. He continues when you give no response, “I hope you had the opportunity to-“ “Talk to Mr. Jean, the adjudicator?” You finally speak up. “Yeah, I did. It wasn’t enough.” “You can’t be the judge of that Eddy,” he says, sounding frustrated yet hauntingly soft at the same time. “I know you, your artwork. Anyone would be foolish to let all your potential go untapped and wasted.” Wasted, you think of the word ironically. As if you haven’t wasted yourself already and exploited everything. There is nothing left now. “They would be foolish to select me.” You reply in a monotone, as if stating a universal truth. You hear a sigh from the other side of the room. It resonates well in the now silent room. He speaks up, “I don’t know how to explain it to you. You... you are amazing, one of the best artists I’ve had the opportunity to work together with. Your artistry inspires me and your determination and passion is so, so powerful.” A small pause and then, “You’re my best friend Eddy, and there is not a single day that I am not grateful about it. If only you would stop being so harsh on yourself and see yourself the way I do.” His voice becomes incredibly soft by the end. You straighten your back against the wall and lean your head against its coolness. You still cannot see why he chooses you over and over again. Maybe it is senseless to even ponder on the thought when he just poured his whole heart out to you, but you can’t help it. Your insecurities trap you; the vines of self-doubt wrapped around you are simply too tight. He comes and sits down next to you on the floor. He scoots himself towards you. You can already feel his body warmth encompass you. You let out a shuddering sigh. And before you realize it, you are sobbing while he wraps himself around you, as if shielding you from all negative forces that keep trying to break you down. He whispers sweet words of reassurance to you. They wash over you, leaving the sweet taste of honey in your mouth. When you finally calm down, he tightens his embrace around you. You feel like you don’t deserve this tenderness but it feels fulfilling. Like you have finally found the component of you artwork that you had been missing all along; like you are finally home. He grasps your hand, squeezes it and whispers, “Even if you don’t believe in yourself, let me have enough faith for the both of us today.” And for now, everything is sufficient.
author: Varnika  Baveja

title: A Day in the Life of a Cat
text: I prowled around the table’s leg, I wanted to get up and smell the delicious food up there but I could not. The last time I did, I got a light smack on my bottom. It was like a slash to my pride. I walked towards my food bowl to see if anything was left. There was nothing. I was starting to feel hungry. The humans were sleeping, and it did not make sense to me. There was no point in wasting a perfectly good afternoon. ‘So many things could be done in those hours’ I thought, pulling a string out of a yarn ball. We cats utilise so much time in practising battle moves or doing battles. ‘Well not real battles,’ I thought, ‘atleast house cats don’t have real battles.’ Stalking my shadow to the washroom, I rethought my thought. The roll of thin, white paper beside the loo, loomed up in front of me. ‘Hmm, Maybe I do have battles, and get tangled up in them, only to be freed and smacked (lightly) by the humans.’ I thought So many thoughts... Yet there are so many things to think about. For example: I love to play with human things like the feathery duster or the white roll in the washroom, but the humans think otherwise. Sometimes I felt like stretching my paws and walking out in the streets in the golden sunlight. I want to meet other cats like me if there are any. I want to stalk some mice but of course, never kill them. My humans feed me and that is enough. Sometimes I feel too energetic and want to bound and spring like anything. However I do not bound and spring even when I am full of energy. Maybe I feel self-conscious at times, maybe all cats are like that. The humans were still asleep and I was bored. I went to my room which had all the charming things a cat would love. The scratching post was made of soft wood and string. I started scratching my paws thinking if having a battle with the white roll would be nice to end the boredom. I went to my cat bed and had a cat nap. If the humans sleep all day long then I might as well have a nap too. I woke up with a lot of noise going around the house. The humans were up and awake doing their work. That means that my battle would not have commenced after all. I went to the sitting room, expecting to be gently pet on the head by my humans. I heard a lot of commotion and looked up. ‘Mroowww!! RUN FOR YOUR LIVES!!’ I yowled, dashing into my room and seeking refuge under the cushions. The most horrifying sight I saw in my entire life: There were five children on the sofa. One child screamed at the sight of me, one child scrambled up the sofa like a monkey (very much like a monkey) and the other three loomed over me. They wanted to hug me, cuddle me, pet me and who knows what. I did not want any of those gifts to be bestowed on me. I kept my ears pointed to the door waiting for the children to go. Soon the commotion ended and normal sounds began to emerge. I also emerged from beneath the cushions to the living room. This time I was more careful, but to my relief, there was no one except me. This is how most of my day goes, humans, food and sleep, all mixed up.
author: Reeha Hossain

title: THE RAINBOW BUTTERFLIES
text: Once upon a time, a butterfly laid three eggs which hatched into three little caterpillars. The mother butterfly named them as Filly, Tilly and Milly. They were quarrelling with each other. So the mother butterfly said that they will get same colours and look like triplets if they don’t quarrel, and different colours if they quarrel and taught them to say ‘love others’. But they were still fighting with each other. Just then a strong wind came and separated the three caterpillers in an orchard where there were many trees. The three little caterpillars searched for trees to place their cocoons. Filly found out an apple tree, Tilly a mango tree and Milly a coconut tree. Few days later, when it was time to go into their cocoons, they wriggled towards the places where they had reached and started building their cocoons. After building them, they gently hopped into their small little cocoons and rested. After a few months, they all woke up at the same time and revealed their beautiful wings. Filly’s wings were red as the freshest apple in the whole orchard. Tilly’s wings were yellow as the sunshine on the beach. Milly’s wings were plain and white as a coconut’s kernel. Now they wanted to find out their siblings. They fluttered in the orchard saying their mother’s words ‘ love others’. Soon they were united but they were shocked to find that they were in different colours. They thought that it was because of their fighting only as their mother said. So they flew away together with tears in their eyes and sat on the branch of an oak tree. After sobbing for a minute or two they saw something amazing and colourful in the sky. “A Rainbow”. They flew together towards it and asked in unity, “Miss. Rainbow, you are so colourful and bright. You have seven colours on you. You look very beautiful. We promise that we won’t fight hereafter. Can you make all of us in the same colour now. The rainbow replied, “I know how you feel right now. You can have some of my colours if you want”. They were excited to hear this. The rainbow gave some of its colours to all. All the three became RAINOW BUTTERFLIES. They loved each other and lived happily ever after.

title: Salsa's Journey
text: UGH! They're telling me this story again! This is the fiftieth time I've heard it. Oh hey! I'm Salsa, a little blue hummingbird. I have a survival story to tell you, and how my caretakers found and saved me... This story began on a summer Saturday afternoon. My caretakers, Alexis, Delilah and Romeo were playing together. Suddenly ~ "Delilah! Romeo! Come out fast! Look at what I have found!", Alexis exclaimed with joy as she pointed towards a huge green Crabapple tree that stood in the middle of the backyard. It was the children's favourite tree and today Alexis had found something interesting on it. They were having a playdate. "Alexis was supposed to collect the flowers that had fallen from the tree but why was she shouting all of a sudden?", Delilah wondered as she rushed towards the backyard. Romeo, Alexis' small brother, was cycling on the pavement. He got really excited as he saw the two girls running happily under the tree. He too rushed to the scene. "Alexis, what happened? Why are you two dancing?", Romeo asked curiously. "Oh Romeo! Look up on that branch! Do you see that little nest?", Delilah said while picking up some fallen flowers from the grass. On a branch, Alexis had found a nest which had some eggs. This nest belonged to my mother. The eggs were incredibly small, and the three kids wondered the species of the bird we were. 'Hmm..I haven't seen anything quite like this. this looks very small to be an egg of a bird." Alexis said. "I don't know maybe it's just the egg of another animal" Romeo added. "Hey! my mom is a vet! Maybe we could ask her." Delilah suggested. "Yeah, okay! We might do that, but we have to play first and then will think about the eggs of this bird." Alexis said. And so, they all continued the playdate, but they kept thinking about my mother's nest. The next day, they went to school and on the way back, asked Delilah's mother about the size of a normal bird's egg. Delilah's mother was turned to see the curiosity of these little kids and decided to take them on a bird watching trip. They all became very excited, and they visited a nearby park. "Mom, what is that funny looking thing you have in your hand?" Delilah asked. "Oh, you mean these? They are called binoculars.", she replied. "But aunt lily...why would we need them to watch the birds?" Romeo confusingly inquired. "Actually, these will help us look at the birds better. It is not easy to observe a bird from a far sight therefore we might need these if we want to see the eyes, the feathers or if they go too far away", Aunt Lily said as she handed them their binoculars. "Oh my god aunty! Look at that small little bird sitting on the branch" Romeo immediately pointed. "Wow that is really tiny bird. Do you want to look at it through the binoculars?", she replied with. And so, they went on to observe many birds and the kids were very excited to visit the nest that they had found earlier They went to the nest only to find out that one of my mother's eggs had fallen. "Oh no! What has happened? How did this happen?" Delilah pointed to the floor sadly. They were all heartbroken and wondered who could be capable of doing such a thing. They rushed to Aunt Lily and told her about the incident. She too rushed to the scene and found out that those eggs belonged to the smallest species of hummingbirds. Then she said " It's very possible that a predator, such as an eagle might have wanted to eat this egg. it might have dropped it on its way..." "Oh no! Bad eagle! See there! There is the bad eagle!" Romeo pointed towards an eagle which was sitting on the opposite branch. They all went inside and observed the eagle from a window. In a little while, the eagle had left, and my mother had come back. They then noticed that my mother had purposely dropped another egg. "What! why did she do that?!" they all asked and were too shocked. "Oh no! this is a common phenomenon of some birds. If they find something wrong with the egg, they will abandon it before it hatches...maybe those eggs had been touched by another bird." Aunt Lily explained. They all rushed outside and just then; my mother flew away. She didn't come back after that day. I was the only bird remaining in the nest. My caretakers rescued me and decided to take good care of me. Although it's hard to explain why my mother had left without me, I'm glad to say that I've been raised just like I would've been if my mother was here. They have taught me to help others whenever I can! Surely there's nothing to lose in helping others, but we can gain a strong bond with them by doing so.
author: Maulika Pandey

title: Beauty is within
text: It was a long time ago, when a baby girl was born. There was only one problem, this baby had been born with an unforgiving face. She was ugly, brutal, dull and truly the most hideous looking child in the world. When her parents saw her ugly face they were ashamed and angry that they had given birth to a monster. They hid her in their house for days, until they realized that they couldn't hide her forever. For many years the child's parents hid her distorted face from her and tried to raise her like a normal child. No child wanted to play with her, the only creature that was forgiving was the pig her parents had bought her for Christmas. Her mother had just finished breaking a mirror. At that moment the girl was confused. Why had her mother broken all the mirrors in there house? Why had she never seen her reflection? Why was a her only friend a pig. One day she went to church and began to walk. Her eyes searched the church trying to find her reflection, and then something caught her eye. After seeing her reflection, a scream ripped out of her lungs. She hated her appearance. She cried and cried and slept that night. Next morning she got up and spent the whole day in her room itself. She heard the pig crying from the window because it hadn't seen her since morning. As soon as the pig saw the girl it started jumping around her happily. She realized that if her pet can love her so much then why can't she her self. That night she decided to accept herself as she is and live her life happily without thinking about other people. We should always love ourselves no matter what because no one is born ugly we are just born in a judgemental society.
author: siya pungalia
illustrator: Aindri C; Marleen  Visser; Mary Anne Hampton; Salim  Kasamba; Yuwak  Shrestha; Zainab Tambawalla

title: The Siblings
text: Once there lived a girl named Natasha.Her dad left her just the second she was born.She also had two other siblings Carter and Jonathan they were always kind to her. Then when Nat was five years old her mom Alice decided to get married to another man. His name. was Sam. Sam was not kind to the children. He would beat up the children when they failed to get straight A's on their tests. Jonathan along with Nat was not so good at studies, but Jonathan was a good athlete and Nat was a pretty good artist. Carter was best in studies. After one month of their marriage Sam started drinking and when he was drunk he would beat up Alice with his belt or sometimes even with glass plates and steel bottles. Alice had scars all over her body, She fell sick but Sam did not let her borrow even a penny for her treatment. Carter as the eldest one had to work for four part time jobs, but still it was not enough.Soon Alice started to loose her hope, so did her children. One day the kids noticed that Alice was turning cold like ice and was not waking up. The kids rushed her to the hospital but the doctors was not able to save their beloved mother. After Alice's death the kids life turned into nightmare. Soon Sam kicked them out of the house, making them lonely and homeless.The only way end this difficulty they thought was to up on their life, to attempt suicide.They could not do it because of the promise they kept to Alice to be strong and independent even after her death. In these circumstances Nat and Jonathan was not able to concentrate on then studies and soon got expelled. Every night the kids would pray to god to end their lives.The three of them thought that they were living the worst life possible. They were slowly losing their hope to live. The next morning when the kids woke up Nat noticed a letter in Alice's handwriting. She was shocked but decided to read it. It said "My children, you guys made a promise please don't break it. Even though you can't see me I am still there watching over you and protecting you like any mother will. Even though I am locked in here doesn't mean I am locked from loving you guys.Study well even if you don't attend school. Please don't cry while reading this. I know the past few months have been very hard for you guys but don't forget to be cheerful and playful as always. I feel so lonely here, hope you guys will come and visit me sometimes by your mom Alice." Nat said weepingly "Mom we will never break our promise."Carter along with Jonathan cried "Yes mom we too". The siblings hugged each other and cried.They expressed their love towards their mother. After this incidence the kids decided to visit Alice in her grave.The three of them talked to her for a long time even though there was no response, they felt their mother's presence and her love. After spending some valuable with her Jonathan got some flowers and placed it near her grave and proceeded to leave. The next day when they woke up there was a letter again. It said "The" flowers are beautiful and so is the perfume. You guys can live in the house we lived before. There is no one in there, the keys. is buried under the plum tree. It's plum season take some to me. Love you forever from your mom "Alice". The kids were confused as they never kept a perfume there. They became curious and was determined to find out who kept the letters. They decided to stay up at night. They hid in a bush near, then they saw a man approaching.Carter shouted with happiness"Dad!" Jonathan questioned "Dad? He is just an ordinary man."Carter replied "Just an ordinary man?you were only three years old when he left us you so probably you won't remember him."I was seven" Jonathan replied. Their dad James said "kids your mom left a lot of letters for you all.Come home". They were astonished.Then they decided to go home. When the kids along with their dad reached their house they felt safe and cozy. They all went to their own rooms. But Nat's room was very tiny as she was a newborn when they left that house. Nat decided to sleep in their maid's room, as the maid was on a leave. The next morning when they went out for a walk they saw a stray dog and decided to p et him. They named him Warewolf and sweetly called him wolf. Wolf was a good girl. After a few days James showed them the letters.The visited their mom ate food and slept. Next morning Warewolf was gone missing.They checked the whole house but failed to find her. Then they heard her bark from Alice's room. Nat went there, the room was full of Spider webs, cockroaches and rats.Werewolf was barking. Nat could hear other dogs barking. When she approached them she saw baby dogs. She stream "Dad, Car, John you want to see this." They all rushed over there. Carter told "Oh! Werewolf you have babies now, so that why you were barking loudly yesterday night. John and Nat asked him if they can keep the babies. Dad told "but we got a problem what will we name them?".Carter insisted lets name one of them Peggy?". Nat continued yeah! that is a good name. I have one mo re name Oliver! John,"well Melon is a good name they decided that the names were Peggy, Oliver, and Melon. They all led a happy life until one day Nat overheard James Speaking,he was talking to his friend Ted. Nat heard James telling "I am not talking care of them because I want them its because I want their money. After I get my money I will kick them out of my house!" Nat was surprised, she could never even think about such a cruelty. Nat shouted, "Dad how could you? How could you do this to us? we don't even have a single penny". James told "your Mom had left all her money and things for you all.I love you guys but I have another family to feed! two children and one wife.Please give me the money and the place and the house. John and Carter soon found out. Carte told James with a hot temper -"Dad! We loved you as a dad. You cheated on mom right and I am 23, John is 19 and Nat is 16 you ever told such a thing. John said "Dad? He doesn't deserve to be called as dad,not a single penny of ours is yours. By the time James new wife Luna came to tell him that its over and the kids was going with her. James was heartbroken he lost his both family over one family's greediness. They soon knew that James was the one who was making the letters.Carter, Jonathan and Natasha took their money and lived happily ever after.
author: Naurish Naushad
