title: A Letter
text: There was a huge crowd of people, the vendors were crying to sell and earn a living. The bus started and the engine added a low noise. There stood an old man with a bag which he was carrying like a hump, on his back. There was desolation spread all the way in his face. The bus to Chennai was about to start. The conductor of the bus came shouting for passengers to get in. As he saw the old man in front of the bus he enquired “Where are you going? Chennai?”. The old man was in a deep thought, that, he didn’t notice even the conductor. “Sir, sir”. The instance the conductor patted on his shoulder, the old man fainted and a letter fell out of his pocket. Soon a crowd gathered around him. The old man was none other than Nagarajan, a resident of 12th street in the town. He was always a wonderful father rather than any other mentions. He was so, maybe because his son lost his mother at an early age. But he took care of him without the feeling of having lost his mother. He was a father who gave freedom to his son in all means, but he was particular over what he has to become when he grows up. It’s very much common among parents to decide their child’s future profession and so, was Nagarajan. He took up each step in his education. He made him study in a good school, college and now, he even completed his degree. It was the time for him to find a job. It was early in the morning, When Nagarajan and his son left home to the bus stand. Nagarajan was very much concerned and was all the time enquiring on whether the bus has arrived. A little later the bus arrived and his son got on to the bus. The conductor kept calling out for the passengers and when the bus was full, the driver started the bus. Nagarajan stayed at the bus stop and waved his hands until the bus was off his sight. Two days later he received a letter that read the safe reaching of his son. Later, there were frequent letters that got exchanged between them, until one day, when as usual he received a letter from his son. This time, the matter, written inside was quite serious. His son wrote a confession letter, where he confessed of joining the Military Force. He knew that his father never liked it, but he wrote with a hope he would accept. Unfortunately, there was a sign of rejection from Nagarajan. He felt of losing the greatest happiness in his life. From then, he was never found with a smile on his face. There were only letters that came but, none of return from Nagarajan. Till a certain time, he kept reading them but as time went, he lost his appeal over it. Now the letters came from the post office to the hands of Nagarajan, and went straight into a steel trunk. This, was what was happening for the next few months. It was his routine to get the letter on Monday. But on a certain day he felt that something was wrong. It was Monday and there was no letter. He waited till the evening but nothing happened. He went to the post office and enquired everyone, but, in vain. Each day, he rushed outside the house when he heard the sound of the postman’s cycle but never returned with the letter. Days went by, and for once, the post man stopped in front of Nagarajan’s house with a letter in his hand. He shouted “Letter”. Nagarajan came out of his house hoping for the letter but, the post man delivered to the house on the opposite. Nagarajan turned back with a heavy heart. He couldn’t wait anymore for the letter to arrive. His concern over his son grew day by day. And one day, he decided not to wait for the letter and rather go and visit him at once. He packed his bag and got ready to leave. He locked the house and left to the bus stand. While he was waiting for the bus to arrive, he heard a voice from far off, calling for him. The postman called out “Nagarajan, I have been searching for you from the morning. There is a letter for you.” “For me?” he asked in astonishment. “Yes, here it is”. “Thanks a lot, sir” he said as he got the letter from him. “I have to leave now. But don’t forget to let me know what’s inside.” said the postman as he went on his cycle to continue his work. The letter seemed a little different this time. He for this time surely wanted to read what was inside the letter. He opened the letter as carefully as he could, took up the letter and started reading it. Instead of happiness, there was a shock on his face. Suddenly drops of water rolled down his cheeks. He couldn’t believe his eyes. The letter read “Respected sir, We, with great sorrow, inform you the demise of your son on the account of a mission that was underway, which was mentioned in the previous letter. We express our sincere condolences.” That was something truly unexpected and more for Nagarajan’s heart to hold. He stood as such to be a statue with no way nor anyone to express his worry.
author: Yuthika Mannem

title: Holidays
text: The bell for dispersal, rang and all the students with an unusual whoop of delight, ran back to their home and it’s all because the Summer Vacation had commenced for them. It was joyous days for all except for me, Tom. I was a student of the same school with both my parents working. I never got chance to revel the holidays as others did. I spent most of my time in the school, because I had someone to spend time with but during the vacation the loneliness came back to me. It was one Saturday when I came to school, hoping I could find someone. But there was no one except the old peon. He in a soft tone asked me what I was doing here. I told him why I am here. At the same time, I asked him why he was here. He told in a desperate voice “We people don’t have holidays such as you” he paused for a second “Do you like to join me in cleaning the playground?” I, with the pleasure of finding something interesting to do, nodded my head. I started cleaning the playground when I suddenly found a box buried in the ground. I dug it out and searched for the peon but as far I could see, I couldn’t find him. I thought for a little and later I slowly opened the box. There was something interesting in it. An old pen that looked royal and a piece of paper. There was a note too, that read “WRITE ANY FOUR WISHES THAT YOU WISH TO COME TRUE”. It may be enthralling to happen in movies but hard to believe in reality. With a laugh of disbelief, I, wrote on paper “I wish it rains now”. I looked at the sky and said ‘Is it going to rain on such a sunny day?” It was not that I even completed saying, but, a tiny droplet of water fell on my face. With incredulity, I looked back at the sky and saw the black clouds coming closer and I, well heard the sound of the thunder. The rain started pouring and the peon called out for me and as I reached inside the school, I was partially wet. The peon looking outside the window told me “The weather out is not good. You might have to stay here till the rain stops. You might sit under the fan so that your clothes dry up soon. We will continue the work later.” Though I was shivering in the cold weather and wet clothes, my whole thought was all about the magical pen and the paper. Then I thought, “If the pen and paper have the power to make my wishes come true then, my next wish would be for sure to solve the problem of my loneliness”. So, I wrote’ “My next wish is that the school reopens tomorrow". And it happened as told. The school was reopened for all the next day, but none liked it except me. I cherished the day. I, too found few cursing, for reopening the school and interrupting their holiday plans. I didn’t take it into a serious account after all, whatever I wished has come true. I was happy by my own side. But there was something that disturbed me. My friend seemed quite unhappy, more than what one could feel for losing holidays. Once I decided to speak to him. After the school, when he was getting ready to go home, I went up to him and asked “What makes you much sad? You don’t seem normal!” He refused to answer. Later after a quite many times of compelling, he told the truth “It’s all because my plan to go to London has been cancelled. I wanted to visit my grandmother. Not for spending my holidays, but that she is old and sick now. I wanted to speak to her at once.” Later that day I felt really bad than I ever felt. “I, have been much selfish for myself. For the happiness of mine I have destroyed others’. All will be angrier on me if they get to know the truth.” I realized my mistake and for once, I decided to correct back what I have done. And hence I made my third wish “I wish that the school closes back tomorrow for Summer Vacation”. And my loneliness came back to me. It didn’t worry me much for that, it’s used to me. As my routine, I went back to the school on the next day and found none. And it was only the peon who was there again. But this time, he seemed unwell. His health didn’t seem good. I went to him and asked “You seem ill. Why do you have to do this job even in this age? Why don’t you take rest at home, for a day at least?” He, with a light smile on his face replied back “That’s not possible for peons like us.” Those words touched my heart and there was something waiting for the old gentle man. In a few minutes, the peon was called by the principal to his room. There was a great silence for some time and later, the peon came out with a letter in his hands. He came close to me and said “The world has changed; there are holidays even for us!” And with a fulfilled heart, I kept back the treasure box at the same place, in which there was the paper with four wishes on it.
author: Yuthika Mannem

title: Starvation of Food for the Monkeys
text: It was the second week of lockdown, due to the increasing impact of Ebola virus in Democratic Republic of the Congo. Martin and his family lived in a community which was near a reserve park. Before pandemic almost 50 people visited the park in day. The people also fed the troops of monkeys in the park. But due to lockdown no one visited the park. One evening, while Martin was communicating to his friend through the window, he saw around twenty monkeys roaming in people’s balconies But this didn’t stop that day, the next day he saw thirty plus monkeys roaming this time. He did not understand what was happening. It was dinner time, Martin’s dad, John, was very much worried as he loosed his job due to pandemic. His parents were talking about how to earn money even during their dinner time. Two days later, when Martin looked out of the window he found few monkeys dead in his neighbourhood. Then he realized that those monkeys died because of hunger. Martin really wanted to feed the monkeys but, he hesitated he knows that his family don’t have enough food or money to feed themselves itself. But he couldn’t bear to see those poor creatures starving in hunger. So, Martin thought about it for the whole night and h got an idea. The next day he exclaimed his idea to his dad. Martin started, “Daddy, I wanna tell you something. For the past one week, I saw troops of monkeys starving in hunger, and you loosed job to. So, I came up with an idea, I will message the government regarding the starvation of food for the monkeys, and will request them to give you the job of feeding the monkeys”. He said. Martin’s dad was amazed to hear an amazing idea from his son. John said, “try it out it will succeed “ Martin started typing the letter and posted it in a website through which people can communicate to the government. The whole family was looking forward for the government’s reply. And after days of waiting there was a reply it said, Measurements would be taken and Mr. John is hired. The family was very happy. And finally the day came all the monkeys were fed and John got his first salary of this job.
author: Kaavya Dharshini

title: Thanks to an Accident
text: Everyone was trying to make the best out of the weather, going on picnics and long drives. But Adam felt cold. His brother, Jake, was going to Germany today, where he’d be staying for a year and a half. He sighed, pulling a carton of milk from the refrigerator. There was no use being huffy. He might as well make these last few hours the best, to make up for all the birthdays and Christmases that they’d be missing. He heard footsteps. Hands covered his eyes. “Guess who?”, a cheerful voice rang out. “Let me see. Oh, are you the monster under the bed?” Adam laughed. Jake laughed, and removed his hands from Adam’s eyes. He leaned against the kitchen island. “So, dear brother, when are you taking me to the airport?” “I was thinking we could leave in an hour. That way we could comfortably reach there by 10 AM.” “Okay”, Jake said, plucking an apple from the fruit basket. “What are you making?” “Waffles”, Adam simply replied, watching Jake’s eyes widen with excitement. Jake has always loved waffles, ever since he was little, and Adam was not going to let him go without a proper ‘send-off breakfast’. Before they knew it, they were in the car and speeding down the busy New York lanes. In the airport, Adam was only allowed to go with Jake till the check-in point. As he saw Jake’s retreating figure, the tears came. He tried to keep his composure, and walked back to the car. He sat down and strapped his seatbelt. And then, he let his tears fall. ∞ ∞ ∞ As he woke up the next day, Adam found the house very hollow. Without Jake constantly rambling, everything was very quiet. So to fill the silence, he turned on the television. He was greeted by a pallid news-reader, reciting the morning headlines. “…There have been multiple robberies in Chicago recently. Viewers, please remember to padlock your doors and windows at night. Yesterday, a plane BX-7470-A11 headed to Germany crashed into the Atlantic. Approximately, 11 passengers sadly lost their lives, over 120 people have been injured, with varying levels of severity, and 9 passengers are missing. Authorities are doing everything they can to find the missing passengers. Viewers, if anyone you know was travelling on this plane, kindly get in contact with the Federal Aviation Administration…” All the blood drained from Adam’s face. He dove for his laptop, and opened the copy of Jake’s ticket. ‘BX-7470-A11’, it proclaimed in bold. His knees buckled. “No, no, no, no, no! Oh my god, Jake…” He pulled himself up and sprinted up the stairs to get his phone from his nightstand. He immediately dialled the helpline for the FAA. A friendly female voice greeted him. “Hello, FAA, what can we do for you?” “My brother, Jake Wilson, was a passenger aboard the flight BX-7470-A11. It crashed in the Atlantic”, he said frantically. “Okay, just give me a minute, sir. Jake Wilson…” Adam heard the clacking of the keyboard. “Sir, your brother’s name is not on the list of injured.” Adam’s legs gave out. He started crying. “Sir, please calm down. Just give me a minute.” More clacking. “His name is not on the deceased list either. He must be one of the nine missing passengers. We are doing everything we can to find them. We’ll note down this number and get in touch with you as soon as we find anything.” “Thank you”, Adam managed to choke out, before he disconnected the call. ‘Jake may not be dead yet,’ he thought. But somehow, his heart said differently. ∞ ∞ ∞ The whole day, Adam sat on eggshells, with his phone next to him. He had received no calls from the FAA. He let other calls ring out. He could not afford to miss the FAA’s call. The next day, he stared at the phone till midday. Then he got tired of waiting. He had already come to terms with the fact that Jake may not have survived the accident. But he had to keep trying. He owed at least that much to Jake. He picked up his phone and dialled the FAA landline. This time, a different woman answered. “Hello, FAA, how can we help you?” “Hi. Yesterday, I had called you regarding the crash of the plane BX-7470-A11. My brother was aboard the plane. He is one of the nine missing passengers. I wanted to know if you had found something.” “Oh, I’m afraid not, sir. We have sent several search parties. We think they will be found soon. We will let you know as soon as we find something.” “Okay, thank you”, he replied, resigned to his uselessness. He heard the unease in her voice. It was beginning to creep into his judgment too. If they had not found them yet, will they ever? ∞ ∞ ∞ The next day, they called. Adam steeled his nerves. He would accept either possibility. There was no use in being in denial. He accepted the call. “Hello, this is the FAA. Is is Mr. Wilson?” “Yes, that’s me. Have you found something?” “Yes sir, that’s what we are calling you for. A few fishermen whom we had recruited found three people. We are positive that they are a few of the missing passengers. Could you please come to Edenbrook Hospital? “Oh, okay definitely! Are they okay?” “Yes sir, they are alive. They have not woken up yet, but the doctors believe that they will come out of this alive and well”, she replied. “Okay, I’m coming over right now!” He grabbed his keys and coat, and raced outside. He got into the car, and it was when he turned on the ignition, that he let himself hope. He might be getting his brother back. ∞ ∞ ∞ The hospital was blindingly white. He had never been to this one. It was bustling with activity. He walked up to the reception and said, “Hello, this is Adam Wilson. I am a relative of one of the missing plane crash passengers…” “Oh, of course. Second floor, ward three. It is on the left wing”. Adam thanked her and went into the elevator. It was as it started moving that he started feeling scared again. He didn’t think he could bear it if his brother was dead. He entered ward three. It was supposedly full of the plane crash victims. He went up to a woman in a suit, and said that he was there to identify the missing passengers. The woman led him to a row of beds at the end of the ward. “Are any of these passengers your brother, sir?” He approached the beds carefully. He opened the curtains around the first and looked at the man on the bed. He had blond hair and a Mediterranean complexion. Not his brother. He opened the curtains around the second, and found a middle-aged woman. Definitely not his brother. He was almost scared to open the last. He took a deep breath and opened the curtains. ∞ ∞ ∞ There he was. His brother. Jake. He almost looked peaceful, sleeping on the bed with his head heavily bandaged, and his leg in a cast. Adam gave out a cry. He fell to the floor on his knees, and started letting out all his tears – tears that he had been holding on to, for far too long. He put his head against Jake’s chest. The steady thump-thump of his heartbeat reassured him. His brother was really here. He was alive. And Adam would never let go of him ever again. “This is him. This is Jake Wilson”, he told the lady. “Thank you. Thank you so much.” “It was our pleasure sir”, she smiled and walked back to the entrance of the ward. Adam sat on the visitors’ chair and held on to Jake’s hand. And he finally slept. ∞ ∞ ∞ After staying at the hospital for six weeks, Jake was deemed healthy and sent on his way. Adam had visited him every day, whenever he could, and spent the nights there. Jake got into the car, next to Adam and smiled, “What a roller coaster, huh? Whatever I was expecting from that flight, this was not it.” “Agreed”, Adam chuckled. “Will you be going to Germany again?” “After what happened last time? No thanks”, Jake grinned. “But seriously, my company decided that I was not a plane-person and let me continue here.” “That’s great! No more flights. And I can always keep an eye on you now.” “Yeah. Now our biggest concern is replacing my wardrobe”, Jake joked. “Oh god, yes. But I’m happy everything worked out. And it was all thanks to an accident.” ∞ ∞ ∞
author: Shravya Sriram
illustrator: berenice terzi; Ellen Heydenrych; Janan Abir; Keo  Phunphalla; Meenal Singh; Ndumiso  Nyoni; Nishant Gopalani; Pallak Goswamy; Shamim  Ahmed; Sharanya Singh; Veeransh .; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Through sickness and health
text: In a small village in Sydney, Australia, lived a small, frail boy named James. James was going to be turning twelve the day after, and he was over the moon with the thoughts of all the goodies he was going to be receiving from his grandma, his one and only best friend and all that was left of his family. James’ parents had died when he was just a toddler, leaving his grandma to provide for him. The grandma had served as a civil servant, so she got a pension and was able to provide for both of them. She made sure that all of James’ needs, and wants, were fulfilled. She spent most of her free time playing with James or talking to him, as she really enjoyed it. James attended the Sydney Middle School. He was a bright pupil with the kindest of hearts. Whenever he saw an opportunity to help someone in need, he took it. He had a great outlook on life and always seemed to be gung ho about everything. Almost everyone who had once talked to him, or had been helped by him, wanted to be his friend. Any bully wouldn’t dare come within 6 feet of him, as there were always people around him, ready to return the kindness he had shown them. This Kindness was not limited to his own school or home. If he saw a person struggling to replace a tire by the side of the road, he helped. If he saw a cat stuck in a tree, he helped. He was really popular all over town- with the children, the adults and even the teachers. Sometimes, he had to give up time for leisurely activities to be helpful. He had been so kind that he was expected to help now, instead of it being a kind gesture on his part. He often fell ill because he overworked himself. Once, he came back home looking as sick as a dog, His grandma, thinking he just overworked himself again, told him to lie down while she gave him medicine and prepared tea. However, by the time she came back from the kitchen, James had fainted. He was lying on the floor out cold. The grandma screamed in horror, and the neighbors came at once and called an ambulance. He was taken to the nearest hospital, where he was admitted in the emergency ward. The grandma sat outside of the ward for 3 hours, holding back tears and trying to be strong. When the doctors came out, she rushed to them in hope of good news. However, she got anything but that. James was diagnosed with leukemia. He had 3 months to live. Hearing this, the grandma broke down. So did most of the town, seeing as to James was loved by all of them. James was in the hospital for another month, during which he constantly had visitors bearing cards, flowers and gifts. After a month in the hospital, James decided that he wanted to spend his last moments enjoying life and helping others, not on a bed, lying helplessly as others cried around him. He expressed this to his grandma, who immediately got to work on his withdrawal. When he got out, he spent the the first month living it up with his grandma and visting all of his friends- both adults and children. He then decided to spend the last month of his life helping others. So, he helped and helped. He was often asked-“Why would you want to waste the little time you have left on others?” to which he would reply, smiling- “My cancer did not tell me to not help others!”. James grew weaker and weaker but continued helping people. One day, a very feeble James was helping a traveler change a tire while his grandma watched form a distance when he suddenly collapsed. His grandma came running to him. “Worth it!” he said, as his eyes rolled into his head. He had helped everyone, through sickness and health. Moral of the story- Kindness has no restrictions. Being kind is hard, but worth it.
author: Tanmay Joshi
illustrator: Ashok Rajagopalan; Jesse  Breytenbach; Megha Vishwanath; Meghna Menon; Melany  Pietersen; Rohit Bhasi; Sharanya Singh; Shirish  Ghatge; Suvidha Mistry; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya; Wahyu Tri Nabella Putri

title: A PYRRHIC VICTORY
text: ﻿ ﻿Today, I am on cloud nine as someone very close to me has received the award for the Best War Story. That someone has dedicated this prestigious award to me. I felt extremely honored and delighted. Talking about war, is there anything good done by war? War destroys the mean of livelihood in every possible way ever. It takes away people shelters, families, will to live and what not. Leading a life after war is not so easy but being human we are ought to live. I still remember the day very clearly when the army of Imber invaded our town; Fulminare in order to capture it. They had also attacked some other parts of our country. On a sunny morning where the sun shone ever so brightly in the clear blue sky and streets were filled with daily commotion, shopkeepers were setting up their shops, parents were taking their kids to school, and people were rushing to do their daily jobs. No one can ever expect to have a bombing, can anybody? But this was what exactly happened. The news was out that the neighboring nation; Imber has bombarded few of the famous spots of the country. An announcement was made and the people were requested to find a safe spot and hide. There were numerous rumors spread that militants of Imber will soon invade the country. And yes the rumor came true. The troops invaded the town and soon the sound of bombings became deafening. They killed everyone who came in front of them no matter how much they begged for their lives, no matter how innocent they were. I, myself, witnessed them almost killing a family of three but the young boy, fortunately, ran away and saved his life. Nobody knows, if he survived or not. Two militants had gone behind to kill him. Clouds of dust asphyxiated the people. The Fluminare militants, our militants fought well with a strong determination and the spirit of ‘DO OR DIE'. The people did everything they possibly could to save their lives. This scenario went on and on for the next fourteen days. In those fourteen days, the number of innocent people who had lost their lives, mothers who lost their children, children who lost their parents, families who lost their shelters, or someone who had no one to call a family became uncountable. The situation was out of control. My family was also dying of hunger and I was not in the situation to wait for the things to get normal as we didn’t have any food, not even a single packet of snacks. I was not able to see my children dying from hunger. I hugged my wife and children as I was about to leave to make arrangements for food. I left without thinking about the consequences. Once again there was a bombarding and the only thought that came to my mind was my family. Out of fright, I started running towards my house and as I was running, something hit me and blood started to ooze out of my arm. At that moment I did not bother to care about it. I was just about to reach my house when I heard someone crying for help. ﻿ I thought to leave but my heart did not allowed me to do so. As I followed the sound, I reached a boy who maybe was of fourteen years.He seemed badly injured and half of his body was trapped underneath debris. I somehow freed the boy from the debris and took the boy along with me. As I was badly injured and was bleeding for quite a long time, I fainted. The last thing I remembered was the sound of bombing and the screams of people. And when I regained my consciousness, I learned that I had been unconscious for three days. But that time the only question running on my mind was if my family was safe, were they alive? Since the time I became conscious I was dying to see and embrace them. Thankfully, they were alive and alright. I felt remorseful when I learned that the boy whom I had rescued had lost his parents; his only family. I knew I had to help him. If I won’t then maybe no one else will do so. Meanwhile a news that came as the relief of human peace and life was that the invaders had left and Imber had decided to step back and stop the fight. Not so soon a deafening silence prevailed. The sounds of bombing, firing and cries of people disappeared like they were never there. Maybe the cries of help stopped but the cries of grief were always there. Everybody had lost someone dear to them. How can anyone expect them to act like nothing has happened? A sudden incursion about which nobody ever had any idea; A war which they never really wanted to fight, they fought and even achieved a pyrrhic victory. But for people, the victory lost its value every single time as they looked at the splashes of blood, corpses, and their destroyed surroundings which were once a beautiful town. I was determined to help the boy and so I adopted Axel; the boy. He was very creative. I motivated him to take this situation as his rebirth and I and my family will always be there for them. Over time he started bonding with my family and soon their bond became unbreakable. Due to the war I had lost my business and had to start all over again. I started a small yet cozy new bookshop. Similarly, others were healing too. People knew that things cannot remain the same as they were. They needed to rebuild their town, lives, and hope so that everything can go back to how it had been earlier. They first started by rebuilding the town. Across much of the city, only the basement, low walls, and occasionally ground floor section of a building remained. The remains of the town were utilized in the reconstruction process. While much of the work was done by construction workers, all people helped to clear the vast debris. Everyone worked together to rebuild their town. From the schools to the shops, churches to the houses, people built it all. They worked hard. It was never easy going back to the charming city it had always been. With time everything got back on track. Everything became as it was supposed to be. The charming, beautiful town was back. People had smiles on their faces. Those who never left the city despite the worst condition fought devastation and came back stronger than ever. One morning someone came to my shop to buy a puzzle. He was trying to solve it but failed. Suddenly a little girl who had been watching him for a long time took the puzzle from his hands and solved it in a minute. I was surprised to see that talented girl. I wished to give her another puzzle as a reward. But I noticed her blank dark beautiful eyes looking at the food stall nearby my shop. It didn’t take me long to understand that she was just another victim of that war and was hungry too. I quickly signaled to the vendor to give her something to eat. Without delay, I understood the purpose for which I was living the life after the war. I decided to help other children who had lost their families during the war and became orphans. Our new home was now a home for everyone who had lost theirs. Other day Axel came to me as he got a chance to write a war story for a movie. He started to write a story with tears in his eyes. We both recalled every moment of our life we faced during the war. What we lost could never be made up but still, he zealously wrote the story of his new life after the war. And today he won the prize for the Best War Story. He announced my name from the stage and dedicated this award to me, his war-born father. This makes me proud as I successfully saved some lives from the Horrors of War and was able to be hope for all of those who had lost the will to live. BY:- AYUSHI GOYAL
author: SEEDLING MODERN

title: Monkeys appear in lockdown in a building society
text: Mahesh was a constructor. He was very honest, polite, intelligent and animal-lover person.So, he thought very wisely and he doesn't want to harm anyone, that's why he was loved by everyone.Without doing any harm to monkeys he wanted that the monkey group should leave the society thereself [you will see it later in the story].Few days,before lockdown Mahesh was given a contract to build a society.As he was not aware of Covid-19 or Corona,he started the construction work.In few days, the laborers have tied and engaged the bamboos.After completing their work in the evening Mahesh and the laborers went home. After going home, taking bath, and doing dinner, all of us see the news daily. Mahesh opened the television and saw the news that a very terrible infection had come from China. We all have to take some precautions like using sanitizers, wearing masks, washing hands properly before and after eating, etc. The government of India has declared a lockdown which will cause less infection. Don't come out of your houses and many other things. But till then the laborers had tied the bamboo. Mahesh was very worried, he called the laborers. He asked, "Have you all seen the news". Then Sonu, Gopal, Govind, and the other laborers replied"No, sir".Then Sonu asked, "What happened sir? Why have you called us". Mahesh told "One very terrible infection has come it is called Covid-19 or Corona. That's why the Government has declared a lockdown. So, we will not be able to continue the work of the society." All the laborers were worried. A few minutes later, Gopal said, "But sir today only we had tied the bamboo." Then Govind said, "Sir monkeys can come there and destroy the bamboo because there are fruit trees nearby". Sonu said, "but now we can't do anything, sir"." Yes, you both are right. We will wait for some time." Mahesh said. Then the laborers replied, "Okay, sir". "I will think something and call you all", Mahesh said. Now, after some months lockdown was extended as so many cases of Corona were coming. During the lockdown, there were so many fruit trees near the building society. So, the monkey group came there and started living there. Monkeys have set up their camp in the building. They used to hang on the bamboo. They broke the bamboo by hanging on them. They did it very much dirty. After the lockdown, when Mahesh and the laborers went to the society. They saw so many monkeys. Some were sleeping, some were eating, and some were hanging on the bamboo. They saw that the monkeys have made the half-finished society very much dirty. This was a great problem. Now, what should they do? They were in great trouble. Seeing this Mahesh was in shock. It would be a very big task to remove the monkeys from there as there was an army of monkeys that will attack. As Mahesh was an animal-lover so, he adopted fair methods for removing monkeys from the building. Then the next day they went to the society. Then, when the monkeys were hanging on the bamboo, and one of them fell down and was injured. That time Mahesh and the laborers were also standing there. Mahesh was standing there quietly. Then seeing this Sonu asked Mahesh "Sir you are an animal lover and you are not going to help that monkey. Mahesh said, "I really want to help that monkey. But I can't because I have studied about the monkeys on google in precautions it was written, "If you are helping an injured monkey ensure that the monkey group is not nearby. Okay sir I understood" Sonu said. But till then Govind(another laborer) has gone near the monkey to help it. Sonu and Mahesh saw him and shouted together, " stop! Govind, stop!". They can attack you because they are in the group. Govind came back and Mahesh told him that fact about the monkey. Mahesh told the precautions the laborer about the monkeys and the environment: *. We should not use plastic bags while going to the market and anywhere else because the monkeys can snatch them from us. *. there must be dustbins near the construction area to keep the environment clean and safe and by keeping the lid tight so that monkeys could not open them. Mahesh told the laborers about their fear of the monkey so that they can save themselves from the monkey: * Baboon (Langur), they are afraid of the ﻿baboon too much even if they see the picture of baboon they run away. *. Toy snake So after telling precautions and fear of the monkeys, they decided to keep the cut-out of the baboon around the building. Due to the fear of monkeys, the laborer harvested all the fruits from the trees and distributed them to the beggars and poor ones so that they could not harm anybody by climbing up and down the trees again and again. I want to share an incident that happened with my Nani when she was holding plastic bags in Vrindavan. As you know there are so many monkeys and when we were walking in the market and my Nani was holding a plastic bag. the monkeys snatch it from Nani.and ran away, which little bit hurt Nani. I want to share another incident that happened in our street a few days before: Every day the monkey group comes to our street. they hang on electric wires, and sometimes they enter the house and pick up things and throw them in other's houses. A few days before, when the monkeys came, two people bring a big picture of a baboon and were roaming in the street, the monkey's group see the picture and got afraid very much and instantly left the street. A few days later, the army of monkeys had left the society permanently, and Mahesh and the laborers harvested fruits regularly. In one year the society's construction was completed.
author: Sanvi Goyal

title: Ajjubhai Mithai Waala
text: Situated in the bustling town of Berhampur in the vibrant Indian state of Odisha, is a small sweet shop owned by the patriarch head of the Sahu family. It rests in the middle of a busy marketplace, distinctive with its catchy bright pink walls. Here sits Ajju, endearingly known as Ajjubhai, on the shop’s cash counter, giving his workers instructions on how to arrange the stack of fresh sweets in the display counter. Ajju Sahu is an honest and easy-going man in his early thirties. After working at his father’s sweets business, he eventually decided to open his very own shop and thus came into existence, ‘Ajjubhai ki Mithai’. To his luck, the business was a great success and soon became a household name in all of Berhampur! Summers were essentially the busiest times of the year, and this summer was going to be no different. Ajju drove his yellow TVS scooter, swerving between the swarming lanes of ‘Sanno Bazaar’ which though directly translates to a small market, is a huge and popular market, famous for its wide range of shops. From the luxurious jewellery stores to bargainous wholesale businesses, Sanno Bazaar got it all! Ajju finally reaches his shop and after a thorough lookout for empty spaces and adjustment of the scooter into the cramped parking lot, he enters his shop and is greeted by his workers. Life seems to be going for him and he feels the same. However, he isn’t the best when it comes to his family. Being a workaholic man, wanting to earn a good livelihood and provide well for his children, somewhere along the lines he forgot his responsibilities as a husband, a father and a son. He was not really present in his life, and so weakened his bonds with his family. His parents were not in good health, and just wanted love from his son, and so did the rest of the family. Ajju never felt bad about not being able to spend time with them due to his busy schedules, because to him, he was working to give them a better life, which he was, but at what cost? Ajju amidst his billing and accounting work, receives a call on his cell phone from his wife, Kamla. “Dear, what do you want me to cook for lunch today? You’re coming home right?”, said Kamla. Ajju replied by saying he would not mind anything. Kamla insisted for him to answer her question and they reached a conclusion that the lunch would be his all time favourite – fish curry. Time passes by… and soon it’s 1:15 PM, the time for lunch break. Ajju rarely goes home to have his lunch, but today was different as he had plans to eat his wife’s cooking. As he was getting ready to leave, his employee reminded him about his visit to one of his other branches for some documentation work. Needless to say, he was gone once again without a second thought. He returned 2 hours later at 3 and checked his phone only to see 4 missed calls from Kamla. He called back. “Sorry Kamla… I had to go out urgently.” Ajju said. He continued, “I might return late at night, so don’t make dinner for me. I have work.” Kamla retorted with an upset sigh and said, “Whatever. We’re used to it. You can do what you want.” Angered by her remark, Ajju got defensive of himself and they had a short fight. Listening to his conversation was Kanhu, a 10 year old boy who came to buy a sweet. As the scorching light of the sun hit the sweets in the display counter, he stared at them with both his hands placed firmly on the glass. After a worker ushered him out of his brief reverie and asked him what he wanted, Kanhu pointed towards gulab jamun. Immediately, “30/- per plate.”, said the worker. “I just wanted one piece though…”, said Kanhu. He was told he cannot buy just one gulab jamun and had to pay for one plate. He frowned and looked visibly upset, for he had wanted to eat one since so long. Right when he was about to head out, “Hey, kid!”, Ajju shouted out loud. Kanhu turned around and Ajju gestured to him to get a plate. Kanhu, with his head low, told him he had no money to pay him. Ajju replied, “It’s okay kid. You don’t need to pay.” On hearing this, Kanhu’s face lit up at once! He rushed to the counter to receive the plate of sweets and started gobbling them up promptly with a wide and radiant smile on his bright face. Ajju lovingly asked him his name and where he came from, the boy said it was Kanha and that he resided in a children’s orphanage in Anand Nagar. What about your parents? If you don’t mind me asking. Kanha’s smile vanished and Ajju immediately apologised for overstepping. It’s okay. My parents passed away last year in an accident. I don’t have a family anymore. I’m very sad to hear that Kanha dear, but what about your relatives? They did not want to take me in, so I was sent to an orphanage. That’s horrible, you’re a very strong young lad. You can come to my shop any time you wish. That means a lot to me uncle, you're so kind! Once Kanha was done, he thanked Ajju graciously. “If you don’t mind me saying…”, he continued. “No no, go ahead. What is it?” Ajju interrogated. “Uncle, I know I’m a young kid and I don’t mean bad but, I overheard your conversation with aunty and I just wanted to tell you that a family is the greatest possession one can have. Give them time and value, we never know when they’ll be taken away from us.”, Kanha said. Ajju was out of words to describe what he was feeling. All this while he could only think of what he would have gone through if he were in the shoes of Kanhu, now it all hit him. Kanhu left the shop and they both waved each other goodbye. At that very moment, Ajju made up his mind and informed his employees to manage the shop for two weeks as he will be taking a break. They agreed and he rushed home. Naturally, his family was out of words to express their immense surprise upon seeing Ajju so early. Ajju goes to Kamla and gives her a hug, she could not help but squeal in joy. He lifts up both his kids in his arms playfully. He sits with his parents and the whole family gets back together for a fun dinner. After this small incident that quite literally changed Ajju’s life, he understood the importance of the role his family played to shape him into the successful and happy man he was. A family is where life starts and love never ends, it is the greatest blessing one can have. Behind every man, is a loving family, just as sweet as a plateful of gulab jamuns. — A story by Rahini Mahapatra
author: Rahini Mahapatra
illustrator: Aindri C; Hayley  Alonzo; Kalpna Choudhary; Kruttika Susarla; Lavanya Karthik; Mukti  Jha; Puja Jha; Sanika Phawde; Shanti Devi; Shreya  Sen; Studio Babakiki; Swathi Sambasivam; Zainab Tambawalla

title: ALWAYS AND FOREVER
text: That was the notion about city life, no matter the hour the people would always be bustling about. I sighed as I sat down at the table, only a few hours for my flight, back to my childhood home. I was feeling impatient, the haveli where I had resided as a child proved to be quite a nuisance, it was hard and stressful, trying to manage a mansion the continuous effort to maintain its grandeur, hiring workers to care for it, to keep it clean while simultaneously being a leading force in the business world. Finally, one day I received an offer from a contractor who was interested in my property, who wanted to introduce a new high-rise culture. The money that he offered was too good to refuse. So, I accepted the offer. All that was left was to dot the I’s and cross the T’s. The contractor would be meeting me at the haveli itself in a week’s time with the final documents. The sooner I get this over with the better. It has been a while since I took a break from my busy schedule with the back to back meetings and deals, like I said the city people never sleep.. The next morning as my flight takes off I sit back comfortably going through the contract once again, they will demolish the mansion, everything present till the property’s perimeter. I run my hand through my hair, “It’s the right thing to do there is nothing left for me, nothing to go back to, I have a life here in the city” I shake my head as I snap out of my thoughts mumbling “Dot the I’s and cross the T’s.” There lies a sense of familiarity in the air as I drive through the roads entering my hometown. My last visit was almost a decade ago, it feels the same yet everything has changed. Where once stood beautiful houses designed in such an intricate manner now are empty with just a sign displaying the visions of high-rise buildings. As I take a turn heading inside the familiar gate now looking worn out, my breath hitches as I take in the sight of what was once my home. I didn’t expect the wave of nostalgia that hit me. everything else may have changed but this didn’t, the haveli stands as it stood decades ago…but of course that wouldn’t be the case soon. Before I became the successful businessman that I am now, before my move to the city, I used to be a small-town boy living in the manor which used to stand proud and filled with life. Reminiscing about all the memories that was created here, I felt overwhelmed. As I walked past the halls and into the yard I was pulled into a memory lane. Me and my mother crouching on the yard with a makeshift box containing a small injured bird, “Is she going to die amma?” I asked frowning. “No beta, the myna has a minor injury, she will live.” My mother assured me, smiling gently. Oh! I remember the myna, my mother was indeed right, the bird did heal, how I had begged her to let us keep it. “The bird has to explore the world too we shouldn’t restrict her from doing so. the bird may not be physically present but that doesn’t mean that we would forget the memories created, they will always remain with us.” My mother replied in a soothing tone. “Do you think she will visit us?” I asked, still filled with sorrow on the bird’s departure. “Everyone returns home eventually.” she replied as she engulfed me in a warm embrace. Only later did I realize how true that had turned out to be. As a comforting gesture, my mother had planted a Shisham tree to commemorate the bird for when it returns. “The bird needs a place to build her home, doesn’t she?” She chuckled softly. My sweet, dear mother. I was snapped out of my thoughts as I heard a knock on the door confused I opened the door. Standing there was an old man dressed as a security guard. " Hello?” I asked, the man in turn looked at me with suspicion. “You don’t look like a squatter.” he rasped. “What! No, no I am the owner of this Haveli.” I replied spluttering. He looked at me as if assessing me then to my surprise broke out a smile, “You have your father’s nose, exactly crooked as his.” He chuckled. Upon seeing my confusion, he continued “I have been patrolling this town since a very long time, I know every face. It has been a while since your last visit. I don’t blame you for not remembering.” “Oh! I apologize, but it has been a while, everything is so different.” I replied embarrassed. His expression grew somber “Yes, everything has changed. Boy, you must realize that this is one of the last Havelis remaining in the town. The rest as I’m sure you noticed have either been broken down or destroyed in the attempt to ' modernize’ the town. Nonsense I say! They are cutting down the very roots that connect us to our heritage and replacing them with malls, multiplexes. Our ancestors have maintained the property for generations, passed it to us to preserve the history, not to erase it all away.” He stopped his heated tirade, letting out a tired sigh. “If this continues we will have nothing to remember our familial generation by.” I didn’t know what to say, I felt a surge of guilt flow through me. After a minute of the sudden gloomy silence he bid me goodbye with a weary grimace, saying that he had to continue his patrol. That night, sleep evaded me I finally gave up and headed out into the garden, the old man’s words a constant echo in my head. I stopped short, for in front of me stood the tall, sturdy Shisham tree, grown over the years. I felt a sense of loss overcome me as the memory of my mother and the myna invaded my mind. All I could think of was 8 year old me wondering “What of the myna?” I shook my head, that was long time ago, there was no time, the contractor would be here the following morning. Surely, the contractor had reached on time along with a few workers to examine the property. After he was done he spoke “The Haveli is good to go for the demolition. But there is a slight problem,” he continued “The tree that stands in the garden must be taken down, It is interfering with the design of the building, it’s no big deal the woodcutters need to just size up the tree” I was yet again speechless, I knew that the Haveli would be broken down, I just assumed that maybe the tree could have been salvaged. Wasn’t that the plan, sell the Haveli, receive the money and return to the bustling city life. Suddenly I heard a sound so faint that it could be easily missed, had it not been familiar to my ears. Straining my ears, I listen as yet another faint cry arises from the branches. I stride forward, searching for the source of the voice, I stop short, I couldn’t believe my eyes, after all this while there it was. A small uneven hole was hollowed out in the tree, I knew it, the sound felt familiar, the high-pitched cry that could only be produced by a myna, as I drew closer I saw the slight fluttering of the nestlings. I felt paralyzed, my chest tight as I struggled to breathe, letting out uneven gasps of air, I felt my eyes burn as tears welled up in my eyes. the workmen l ooked confused about my reaction on such a simple sight but as I stared at the little mynas I was back in the garden except this time only my mother was present. Her eyes softened as she stared lovingly at me. “Everyone returns home eventually” she spoke, her voice echoing and I knew that she wasn’t just referring to the myna. Startled by a hand on my shoulder I jerked back. “Is everything alright?” the contractor asked looking concerned. I didn’t answer, consumed by my profound realization. All this time I thought t hat there was nothing left for me here, when it’s been there right in front me. My ancestors, my mother left this for me and today they might not be here but that doesn’t mean that they’re gone, for they have left me the memories that I would hold close to my heart and cherish them. Looking at the tree, I realize that my mother has left a part of her in this tree, the tree that she cared for, the tree now commemorating the myna’s return. My forefathers who built this Haveli decades ago have left a part of them, like a signature, signing off before leaving. I cannot destroy that, I refuse to erase away what’s left of my family, of my heritage and no amount of money can ever account for these treasured memories created. " So, I guess the deal is off right?" startled I turn back, it was the contractor who spoke smiling wistfully at me. Standing upright, a happier man I replied "I guess it is." The end
author: DHRITEE BHARDWAJ
illustrator: Gieve Patel; Kripa B; Shivam Choudhary; Sudhir Patwardhan; Suvidha Mistry

title: THE MYSTERY OF THE NEVER RAINING PLACE
text: That day, I was very excited because my parents were going to Yemen for a few days. They were going on a research mission on something. They were both scientists. They had already decided to leave me in the loving care of my aunt. However, I was determined to accompany them this time. After begging multiple times, my Dad finally yielded to my wish. Wow! I was going to accompany my parents on a research mission in a foreign land. I was very happy. I took a quick shower and wore my favourite dress. After a short drive to the Bir Tikendrajit International Airport at Tulihal, Imphal, we were seated in the plane. Aboard the plane, I noticed that my parents looked very tense and worried. I even saw them discussing something in a very low voice. But, I was too excited to be worried by anything. I occupied the window seat. And my parents occupied the adjacent two seats on the left next to the aisle. The last flight was pleasant and there was no air turbulence. The Pilot made a smooth landing. In hushed voice I screamed, “ Yes finally! ” Soon, we were seated in a waiting car. Our road journey started. My eyes were fixated in the surroundings trying to absorb everything in sight. My excitement level was very high. Suddenly, I was jolted out of my excitement when our car screeched to a sudden halt. I saw a luxurious car blocking ours from a distance. I next saw my father calming down my mother. They reluctantly alighted from the car after they where signaled to do so by two thug-looking men. My mother put her forefinger on her mouth, signaling me to be quiet. And, she also nudged me to hide behind the bush nearby. Then, she ran to join the conversation between my father and the two men. Trembling in fear, I hid myself behind the bush nearby. Then, she ran to join the conversation between my father and the two men. Trembling in fear, I hid myself behind the bush nearby. I was very curious and concerned about my parents. So, I crept up towards the place of their conversation. But, I couldn’t hear anything. I sighed and was about to creep back when I heard one of the men say, “Everything is prepared ma’am and sir, we are eagerly waiting for you to manipulate the weather.’’ My mother uttered something to our driver, who was standing nearby. Then, my parents left with the strangers. Our driver called me out, “Come out kid, and get into the car.’’ Still trembling, I came out and sat in the car. He started to drive. I meekly asked, “What is happening, sir?’’ He didn’t answer. Then, I sternly asked again, “Where are you taking me?’’ He finally answered, “To a guest house in Al Hutaib village.’’ I further asked, “ Why?’’ He said, “Because your mother told me to do so’’. I stopped asking further questions on the way to the village. It’d been a week since I arrived in the guest house. I had been waiting for information about my parents. But, no one in the guest house had any idea about them. I decided to ask somebody outside. So, I asked a girl of my age, “Do you hear any news about a scientist couple from India who had gone missing?’’ She said, “Yes, I have heard my parents talking about a scientist couple who were chosen to manipulate the weather of Al Hutaib. You know, It has never rained here.’’ “ Never rained?’’, I said in a shocked voice. “Yes’’, she answered. After sometime, I came back to my senses. My parents were trying to play the role of Rain Gods of Al Hutaib. Or, were they forced to take those roles? They might have been prevented from leaving that place until they succeeded in invocating the sky to weep in Al Huitab. Or, they were too engrossed in their experiments completely forgetting me. But, I never saw them again. It’s been ten years now. I am intensely working on my research on artificial rain and cloud seeding. I miss my parents’ critical and expert guidance. Last heard, Al Hutaib village is still waiting for its first shower of rain. And, I am still waiting for my parents to return and guide Lily, their only child. - THE END -
author: Ningthithoi Yumnam
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Jitendra Thakur; Jupiter  Pradhan; Lavanya Karthik; Nicci  Nathanson; Nikhil Gulati; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Rayika Sen; Sukhada Rahalkar; Wiehan de Jager

title: FORESTER
text: Once a forester who went into the forest to hunt, as he entered he heard a sound of screaming of a little child. He followed the sound and at last came to a tall tree, at the top pf the tree a little child was sitting for the mother had fallen asleep under the tree. The forester climbed up, brought the child down and thought to himself: " you will take him home and bring him up with your daughter rina." he took him home. Therefore, both of the children grew up together. The one who had found on a tree was named rahul. Rahul and rina loved each other. When they didn't see each other they will become sad. They become the real brother and sister. The stayed together always forester had an old cook. He doesn't like rahul. On a spring evening he took 2 pails and began to fetch water. Rina saw this and followed him. He entered into the kitchen and began to talk to his wife, who is also a servant there. Rina overheard them. "why are you fetching so much water?" wife asked " if you will never reveal to anyone, i'll tell you why" cook replied. Wife promised she won't do that. " tommorow morning, when the foster is out, i'll boil this water and throw on rahul and hurt him. " cook said his plan next morning forester went hunting in the early morning. Rina told everything that she knew to rahul and promised him she will be always with him to protect. Both of them got dressed up quickly and went away. When the water was boiling the cook went into the bedroom to throw water on him. But they were not in their room. Both of them were escaped. " what will i say when the forester comes, i have to get them back. " the cook sent 3 servants after them. The children found themselves in a forest after an hour of running. They were tired enough to run further. That was a rose flower garden. They saw 3 servants coming after them. They began to cry and pray. Suddenly a fairy appeared before them. Fairy suddenly made them into a rose. Both of them became rose and the servants couldn't find them. They returned back in disappointment. The cook scolded them after hearing the news. The cook himself went for the searching. This time rahul became a pond and rina a duck in it by the magical power of the fairy. Cook couldn't find the children but he thought of catching a duck for the night. While trying to catch the duck he drawn into the pond and died. Rahul and rina again become a boy and girl as fairy chant the spell. They lived happily ever after...

title: Friends for Granted
text: Riya,an eleven year old girl used to stay with her family in a small town. Riya grew up with Mona who was as the same age as her. They would often spend their days together chatting,playing and learning things. One day, Riya's father bought Riya a new laptop, Riya and Mona really enjoyed surfing the internet together for the first few days. After a few days, few of riya's school freinds invited her to join a social media app. Riya enrolled herself in these apps and started to spend most of her time on these apps. She started making new online freinds. Many times Mona would call Riya for playing & chatting but Riya would ask her to wait but never got back to her. Many days passed and Riya kept spending more time with her online freinds and began ignoring Mona believing that Mona would always be there, whenever she wanted. In few days, it was time for Riya's birthday. Riya was very excited and invited all her online friends. As her birthday approached, Riya planned a lot of activities online with her friends for her birthday. It included online games, videos and clicking photos. The night before her birthday as Riya was doing last minute preparations, the laptop slipped from the table and broke. This became Riya's worst nightmare. She believed that her entire special day would be ruined. In the afternoon, as invited, many of Riya's online friends started to come to her home to celebrate her birthday. They started to talk amongst each other that how boring Riya's birthday party was since there were no online games, photo clicking etc. as planned. Riya became more sad. She kept thinking that how happy her earlier birthday celebrations with Mona were for so many years. She looked outside the window towards Mona's house, but it was locked. Suddenly Riya's mom called Riya and said "Riya sweety.. look who has come to meet you..come here". Riya walked towards the door with dropped shoulders and a sad face as she knew her party was not at all as she had planned it to be. On the door was her friend Mona. She wished Riya with a big smile and said "Happy Birthday Riya, I have a surprise for you.. cheer up!". Mona opened her bag and brought her laptop out. Seeing this, suddenly Riya's face lit up. Mona said "Lets start the party Riya, what are you waiting for.. online games, photo clicking...". Riya surprisingly asked "Oh my god.. how did you know?". Mona said "Taruna, your online friend is connected with me also online. I saw her and some of your other friends messaging and making fun of how boring your birthday party was due to no online activities. I couldn't see that, so decided to come and help..." Hearing this Riya immediately hugged Mona tightly. Both smiled and began hosting the party together on Mona's laptop. Everyone began having lots of fun. In a short time, everyone started complimenting Riya that this was the best party they had ever attended. As the party finished, Riya said to Mona "Thank you so much my best friend. I have realized my mistake and will never take any friend for granted ever!!". The both gave eachother a high-five and became close friends again.
author: Diya Chopra

title: Brahma's Chronicles of War
text: Chapter 1 Greetings reader, I’m Pri. It's not important what you think of or know about me, all you need to know for now is that I’m a bipartisan force and the impacts of the tales of the battles ensuing don’t affect me. This is not my story, I just narrate the books that my father writes to you. The one I’m holding right now is about a brave warrior of the Terra tribe on planet Terraqua, named Dharti. Here we go! Terra is a three and a half billion year old tribe that ruled Terraqua since it was first inhabited by humans.. until very recently. Twenty-three years ago, Dharti was an itsy-bitsy, tiny little baby when her mother was killed by a karthog king, she died fighting for the foremost Terra battalion that clashed with the most pesky species on Terraqua, the karthogs. They were filthy rodent-like creatures that destroyed the fertility of land everywhere with their broad, venomous incisors and the stinger of a scorpion. Dharti’s mother’s squadron was unprepared for a king's presence at a minor karthog outpost and she succumbed in a successful heroic attempt to save the entire squadron from a tooth-strike. Dharti lived with her home and hearth focused father who loved and cared for her and her little sister, Mitti. His heart's greatest desire became for both of them to grow up to be powerful, independent women. Now, back to the present day. Chapter 2 The barren, damp desert under the moonshine’s dim glow, seemed to radiate a fresh preparedness to be regrown, but there was no one to tend for it yet. It was razed to the ground, burnt to a crisp in the battle that had ensued just moments before. Across from her, out in the distance, Dharti saw a masculine figure, glowing a light, neon shade of blue. She couldn’t pay attention to that right now, she had had enough of the bloodshed. She had never wanted in her life to grow up to be like her mother, she was… almost ashamed. Her poor father had to concede the significance of his life, he should’ve been the one to defend the nation, he should’ve been the one given the opportunity to protect her mother, but her mother was selfish, her mother never cared for her or Mitti, she left them alone. And father was left with a miserable life. And now, because of Dharti’s incompetence in war, compassion, empathy and love, she had failed to protect her dying old father and Mitti from harm's way, an Aqua mercenary had injured Mitti and as Dharti looked out into the horizon to avert her eyes from Mitti’s gaping wound, while tying a fabric swab of wet sand around it to prevent blood loss, she realized an important thing. She realized she was wrong about her family. She realized that everyone plays different roles, and sometimes life comes at you at supersonic speed and not everyone gets to choose what role they play. She was trained by her father to be a strong warrior, inside her, she knew there was a warrior somewhere and it was time to embrace it, be proud of her heritage, both sides, for being phenomenal players of their roles in crisis. As Mitti rose up, wincing in pain, Dharti darted forward toward the blue glow, she was going to play her role. Chapter 3 Greetings reader, I’m Varu. It's not important what you think of or know about me, all you need to know for now is that I’m a bipartisan force and the impacts of the tales of the battles ensuing don’t affect me. This is not my story, I just narrate the books that my father writes to you. The one I’m holding right now is about a Karthog conservationist of the Aqua tribe on the planet Terraqua, named Jal. The Terra tribe is the most oppressive group on the planet, for three and a half billion years, Terra has had their way about the planet. After all, nearly 87% of the land is land, they don’t care for animals except the ones that look pretty, but Jal does. Chapter 4 Karthik is his favourite Karthog, he grumbles when he's hungry, squelches when he’s thirsty and groans when he needs a cuddle. What else could you want from the poor animal, he would protect Karthik from any Terra folks with his life. But he couldn’t think about that now, his gronth (Karthik’s favourite grassy flowers) planting and growing abilities had finally found a use for themselves. Invading Terra forces had ruined a desert of land and it needed healing. His father, a man of horrible temper but true heart, had just assigned it to him, and he was going to listen because the barren, damp desert under the moonshine’s dim glow, seemed to radiate a fresh preparedness to be regrown, but there was no one to tend for it yet. It was razed to the ground, burnt to a crisp in the battle that had ensued just moments before, and Jal was going to regrow it. Oops reader, I think I’m going to have to take your leave, dad is calling Prithvi and I for lunch, Brahma doesn’t take too kindly to being left unanswered… and to us using his magical storybook collection to narrate too many human stories.
author: Hitansh

title: THE MYSTERY OF THE NEVER RAINING PLACE
text: That day, I was very excited because my parents were going to Yemen for a few days. They were going on a research mission on something. They were both scientists. They had already decided to leave me in the loving care of my aunt. However, I was determined to accompany them this time. After begging multiple times, my Dad finally yielded to my wish. Wow! I was going to accompany my parents on a research mission in a foreign land. I was very happy. I took a quick shower and wore my favourite dress. After a short drive to the Bir Tikendrajit International Airport at Tulihal, Imphal, we were seated in the plane. Aboard the plane, I noticed that my parents looked very tense and worried. I even saw them discussing something in a very low voice. But, I was too excited to be worried by anything. I occupied the window seat. And my parents occupied the adjacent two seats on the left next to the aisle. The last flight was pleasant and there was no air turbulence. The Pilot made a smooth landing. In hushed voice I screamed, “ Yes finally! ” Soon, we were seated in a waiting car. Our road journey started. My eyes were fixated in the surroundings trying to absorb everything in sight. My excitement level was very high. Suddenly, I was jolted out of my excitement when our car screeched to a sudden halt. I saw a luxurious car blocking ours from a distance. I next saw my father calming down my mother. They reluctantly alighted from the car after they where signaled to do so by two thug-looking men. My mother put her forefinger on her mouth, signaling me to be quiet. And, she also nudged me to hide behind the bush nearby. Then, she ran to join the conversation between my father and the two men. Trembling in fear, I hid myself behind the bush nearby. I was very curious and concerned about my parents. So, I crept up towards the place of their conversation. But, I couldn’t hear anything. I sighed and was about to creep back when I heard one of the men say, “Everything is prepared ma’am and sir, we are eagerly waiting for you to manipulate the weather.’’ My mother uttered something to our driver, who was standing nearby. Then, my parents left with the strangers. Our driver called me out, “Come out kid, and get into the car.’’ Still trembling, I came out and sat in the car. He started to drive. I meekly asked, “What is happening, sir?’’ He didn’t answer. Then, I sternly asked again, “Where are you taking me?’’ He finally answered, “To a guest house in Al Hutaib village.’’ I further asked, “ Why?’’ He said, “Because your mother told me to do so’’. I stopped asking further questions on the way to the village. It’d been a week since I arrived in the guest house. I had been waiting for information about my parents. But, no one in the guest house had any idea about them. I decided to ask somebody outside. So, I asked a girl of my age, “Do you hear any news about a scientist couple from India who had gone missing?’’ She said, “Yes, I have heard my parents talking about a scientist couple who were chosen to manipulate the weather of Al Hutaib. You know, It has never rained here.’’ “ Never rained?’’, I said in a shocked voice. “Yes’’, she answered. After sometime, I came back to my senses. My parents were trying to play the role of Rain Gods of Al Hutaib. Or, were they forced to take those roles? They might have been prevented from leaving that place until they succeeded in invocating the sky to weep in Al Huitab. Or, they were too engrossed in their experiments completely forgetting me. But, I never saw them again. It’s been ten years now. I am intensely working on my research on artificial rain and cloud seeding. I miss my parents’ critical and expert guidance. Last heard, Al Hutaib village is still waiting for its first shower of rain. And, I am still waiting for my parents to return and guide Lily, their only child. - THE END -

title: THE  PRECIOUS  GIFT
text: Once upon a time there was a cute little girl named "rani'' and her dad. She was seven years old. Rani's dad was the only one who was her own. They both were af fectionate with each -other. Now she was growing up and even her birthday was also coming interestingly she was turning to 8 years. One day she asked from her dad ''when i ''ll get, my birthday present dad ''? '' oh that is so far, six months are left for it ''! Replied her father. Few days past, slowly rani was feeling dizzy and even suffering from several diseases. Dad was worried for her. He thought that now medical check-ups are so important to get done. After the medical check -up he saw in the report there was written she has heart problem. Her heart is defected. Even she is in the last stage of the heart problem and the only way to save her life was the heart transplant but no one was ready for it as it was so quick.dad was broke out and nothing was left in his life. The problem was so serious and critical. Day-by-day she was becoming weak and again she inquire '' when i will get my birthday present, you know that i am turning to 8 years. Her dad was so sad and he started crying a lot. He decided to save her life. After some time, she got the treatment as well as she opened her eyes and did'nt saw her father, when she asked from the nurse she said sadly ''your father is no more. To save your life he donated his own heart but he had left a message for you and in the message, it was written '' dear you were asking about your gift. I had given you the most precious gift of your life my heart, an organ. I hope that you are fine and don't be sad because i am always in your heart''. Family members and mom, dad are the most important person in the life. We should never hurt them. Written by-janvi kandari
