title: A BAD DECISION
text: Once upon a time, there was a 12 year old boy named 'Samie'. He was a poor child and had no mother. His father was a laborer & about 48 years old. Samie polished the shoes for pay his school fees & assist his father in such a tender age. His school use to start at 7:30 a.m. & end at 2:40 p.m. so he waked up at 5:15 a.m. & go to his work at 5:35 a.m. Then after he go to school at 6:40 a.m. as it was far away from his home & took 30 minutes. His life was full of difficulties but somehow he & his father managed to maintain a pretty smile on their faces. One day, Samie was at his school & his neighbour Kiara rang the telephone at school's reception and speak, "Hello, good morning Mam, can I please talk to Samie Sinha? I am his neighbour, Kiara. His father suddenly fainted & there is no one to take care of him even I am going for some urgent work." Kiara was so much close to them but that day she might have been gotten some very urgent work. Besides, the receptionist was in hurry and called Samie from his class. He was so much worried that he driven his cycle as fast as he coul. When he reached his home, he found his father on bed and he was looking so much ill. Samie worridly asked his father, " Dad, What happened!? are you not feeling well?", his father muttered,"Son, I wanna tell you that.....", until he complete his sentence, he fainted again. Samie asked for help to many people but no one helped him. What a pity, he took his father to the hospital after facing so many difficulties, but even the doctor was not available because he was busy playing football. Samie couldn't do anything; he burst into tears and was crying out loud but still not even a single person was ready to help him. All of a sudden, his father said," Sam, son I can't live anymore and one thing i wanna tell you that....", before he finishes he again blacked out and his heart stopped beating and wasn't able to breath, he died! Samie was sobbing and he was feeling sorry that he couldn't take care of his poor old father. After a few months, Samie started forgetting what happened in the past. He determined to work hard and become a doctor. It was Wednesday morning, Samie was getting ready for his school. He reached there and in his class there was a new student. Samie was excited to do friendship with him. In the first period their class teacher introduced the new student to everyone. During the food break, he went to the new student and asked his name but that child was feeling shy; Samie asked him not to feel shy and talk to him freely. Finally, the child replied," Ab- Abhimnyu my name is Abhimnyu", Samie replied," oh! that's really a good name A-B-H-I-M-N-Y-U, nice! By the way I am Samie, nice to meet you." Few days later, Abhimnyu was not shy anymore and he was a bindaas boy, One day, Samie started getting jealous of him thinking that why Abhimnyu abused and I could not?, why he was naughty and I could not?, why he was rich and I was not?. Samie decided to become the naughtiest boy anyone had even seen, he started abusing, fighting etc. He was no more well- mannered. Inshort, he was in a bad company. Every teacher was fed up of him and Abhimnyu even the students were. All strictness and efforts of the teachers was in vain. Monday morning, all teachers decided to complain about both of them to the principal and they meant it and both got suspended for one month. Samie was showing to Abhimnyu that he don't care if he got suspended but deep down he was unhappy. At night, he cried out loud! Few minutes elapsed, there was a sound of knock at his home's door. He asked from inside,"Who's there?" a voice came,"Hey Sam, here's me Kiara", he opened the door and asked Kiara to come in and sit. He brought a glass of water and Kiara asked him while taking the glass" I heard the sound of crying, what happened? you can share with me.", she said very wisely. He explained the whole story to her that what happened in school and why? Kiara said," Oh Sam! you were in a bad company. It was not your fault but tomorrow you must clean your house.", Samie replied,"okay" and she moved to her house. Next day, Samie started cleaning his house. "So much dust oh god! how I will clean it all by myself!?", he said and sighed. When he went to clean his cupboard, he found a letter in it. He opened it and it was his father's handwriting. He started reading it & in it was written, "dear Sam, I don't know when I will pass out but the dates are not so far. I wanna tell you that please when I will leave, never ever be in a bad company and don't become naughty as others. I know you want to become a doctor so work hard on it. I hope you will find this letter soon...," then, he realised that being in a bad company is the biggest mistake. He made his mind to never talk to Abhimanyu again & started going to school after one month of suspension. He worked harder. After many years, he became graduate and got his success after struggling. Now, he was rich, had a big bunglow in Mumbai & did job in one of he most popular hospital. He thanked Kiara for what he was today & god for what he had. The secret between you & me is that Kiara herself sent Abhimanyu in Samie's school so that she could see if he fell in a bad company & then realised so that he could get more confidence to become a doctor & fulfil his father's wish. Indirectly, Kiara played the main role.
author: GEET MITTAL

title: A conservation
text: Introduction The story is about conservation between a student and a school bus driver. The protection between them mainly revolves around education. The driver shares his fair experience with teaching, even though he is uneducated, and the student shares his. Normally we think that the knowledge we get from books is a main part of life, but this story says otherwise. The conservation between these 2 characters is full of details about what many have the privilege to do but take for granted, education. The driver shares his childhood stories related to education. The name of the student is Nikhil, who is having this conservation. "Ring! ring! ring!" rang his alarm. He raised his arm to turn it off, his face was shivering due to the cold weather. It was mid-November, and Nikhil was not ready to go to school during such cold weather. He wanted to wrap himself in his cozy warm blanket and fall asleep. But a cold breeze ran across his face, he felt as though a hundred tiny needles were poking his face. "Nikku! get up and get ready fast, it's already 6:12, hurry up!" his mother screamed at him. "Ok", he groaned. He got up and started walking on this cold floor. Why go to school he thought in his mind, I could fake a cold and it would also be the believable cause of how often I get sick. But he knew his mother wouldn't believe him. He got into the washroom and started brushing his teeth with cold water and thought that this is what frozen hell feels like. He got ready as quickly as possible, he wore a sweater to counter the freezing weather. By the time he got ready the bus was already waiting for him. He packed his bag so fast that many of the books fell over the bed. his mom was calling him, "Nikhil! the school bus is waiting for you.". He ran out to the bus with a couple of books in his hand. Nikhil was a normal student like many others. He was an 8th-grade student, who got average marks, he had some friends who had their level of quirkiness. Nikhil was not as social as his friends, he thought if he would get nice marks his life would be nice. His parents were very strict when it came to education, so he knew he had to get good marks or else he was in for a beating. He sprinted into the bus with his bag hanging onto one of his shoulders and books in his hand. By the time he came, the other students at his stop had already arrived, They were a couple of 4th graders, and they already began chit-chatting about their class rumors and other events that happened in the school. Nikhil went and sat in the second to last row and started arranging his books in his hand into his bag. The bus started moving, the time was 6:50 when they reached the next stop, which was 5 minutes away from the last stop. Two children got on the bus with one of them was crying that they don't want to go to school, the bus attendant tried to console them. The bus went on swiftly so that they can avoid traffic. There were about 5 children on the bus but still, there was causing a ruckus. Nikhil told everyone to keep quiet, he felt that he had to take responsibility as he was the most senior on the bus. The bus attendant was sitting in the passenger seat beside the driver. The bus was divided into two compartments with a wall. The bus went on until it reached a batch of cows that were crossing the road, they had to wait for two to three minutes for the hoard of cows to clear the road. Once the cows were gone, the driver started accelerating at full speed, this was until they reached a bumpy road. The road was narrow and filled with potholes. One of the kids from the back shouted, "Why doesn't the government fix these roads.". Nikhil also had the same thought as them. The bus was finally off the bumpy road and was headed fast toward the next stop. The next stop arrived and there were 3 students already waiting. The students got on and the bus took off to the next stop. The bus was so noisy that Nikhil couldn't control them, his shouts got lost in their loud shouting and bickering. Two students had begun a fight which he had to separate. Afterward, they reached their next stop. This stop was crowded with at least 13 students, and the attendant also informed us that three new students will also be coming on the bus so we had to make space for them. We arrived at the next stop, and all the students including the new students had arrived at their stop. They all got on, but there wasn't enough space because many students had brought projects which had to be kept in the driver's compartment. Everyone was packed tightly, there was hardly any room left on the small bus and they had one more stop to go. The bus attendant told Nikhil to sit in the passenger seat next to the driver. He listened and went and sat on the seat next to the driver. The driver greeted him with a hello! and then the bus took off to there final stop before heading towards school. The drive was going smoothly, the driver asked Nikhil was that project meant, it was a project on grains made by a first grader and it had rice grains and other pulses glued to a chart paper which was around the word "GRAINS" written in bold letters, Nikhil said that it was a chart on grains. As they approached their next stop, there was a women's medical school on the side of the road and the driver asked Nikhil, "What is that? a hospital or a school? ", to which Nikhil replied," It's a medical college". The driver said, "Sorry that I am asking you these questions, You see I don't know how to read English", Nikhil said, "It's fine". "I never went to school, my parents never sent me," he said, Nikhil nodded as he didn't know what to say. The driver continued, " In my childhood, I cried to my parents to send me to school, and children nowadays are crying to not go to school" he said amiably. The driver was a good person with a short personality and a round figure. The bus slowed down to a crawl when the next stop arrived. The driver picked up the conservation from where they had left it, "Where was I? Hmm, yes, I wanted to school." Nikhil nodded as the conservation went along and the driver continued, "I know a few letters in hindi and I had learned all the letters in English, My parents didn't give me that, I earned it myself. In my childhood, I and my friends had to walk about a kilometer to go to a school and write two to three letters on a slate with a chalk piece to learn the letters. At that time we had a bet to see who will learn all the letters including their pronunciation first. ". Nikhil thought in the back of his mind that people in the olden days were so excited to learn and to go to school and nowadays children take education for granted. He thought that the privilege of education is being taken for granted and shouldn't be treated that way. The driver said, "I know what letter is what but I still don't know how to spell out the entire word, anyways, as I grew up I learned what knowledge meant and how one attains it. ", Nikhil eagerly asked him, "What does it mean", To which he replied, "True knowledge means knowing how the world works and one attains it as they age and gain experience." Then Nikhil asked the driver, "What is your name sir?", to which he said, "My name is Nayak ". Nikhil thought about the conservation he had with Nayak for the entire day and finally understood what he meant by it. Conclusion The knowledge we gain from books isn't a fraction of the knowledge that's out there in the world, and this knowledge can be written in words, it can only be experienced when we put ourselves out in the world and gain experience and knowledge about it.
author: Nikhileshwar Reddy

title: Block Agonizing Animals
text: Five friends, Tina, Grace, Rani, Rahul and Amit were close friends. All of them studied at Mount Carmel school in sixth grade. All of their parents worked for the Wildlife Protection Act. They were all family friends and were also animal lovers. All of them had pets like Tina had two dogs and a rabbit, Grace had two cats, Rani had an aquarium and a rabbit, Rahul had two bull dogs, and Amit had a rabbit, a cat and a parrot. They also had animals in cages at their school for educational purposes, and were also well taken care of by the school. The friends visited the animals everyday during break and one day, they noticed the senior boys pulling the tails of the dogs and throwing stones in their cages. The seniors enjoyed torturing and bullying the animals. The friends got very upset. They walked towards the seniors and told them to stop hurting and bullying the animals, but they didn’t listen to the friends, and instead walked away. The students decided to tell the teacher about this, but by the time they got to class, the home bell had already rung and they had missed their chance. So, when the friends got home, they told their parents everything that had happened. The parents visited the principal the next day and told them about the students bullying the animals. The principal called the students to his office and also made an announcement about the purpose of the animals. “The animals we have are taken well care of by the school. They are fed properly and their hygiene is also well taken care of. These animals we have in cages are not for your fun, but for educational purposes, like explaining about their habitats, what they eat, what do they look like, their behavior etc. But I have found out that a few seniors of our school have been bullying and hurting the animals, and then, laughing and enjoying at the sight of them being tortured. Animals are not supposed to be treated like that. I am going to be punishing these students, and I don’t want any other students treating the animals harshly. I am also very thankful to a few students, Tina, Grace, Rani, Rahul, Amit and their parents for pointing out to this problem as some people may ignore this but it is very important to pay attention to this problem.” The senior boys had realised their mistakes and promised to treat animals properly. The senior boys had regretted what they had done and were punished. Whereas, the five friends were applauded by their friends and teachers. We should not treat animals harshly. They are also living beings. They also feel pain. They should be treated well as human beings expect for themselves. Animals are useful for different purposes and activities and also give a smile on our faces. Animal abuse should stop if we want to make our world better. We should stop anyone who is abusing and bullying animals for our future and theirs.
author: Ayana  Fatima
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Canato Jimo; Ouk  Ratha; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Santosh Pujari

title: Ramu asks to many questions
text: A boy named Ramu is a by who would ask to many questions. Whatever was in front of him he would question. "Why did you score second place?" Asked Ramu to his friend Risha. "Should I have not?" Asked Risha back. "Why did you not get first place?" Asked Ramu. "What do you mean? At least I got second place." Replied Risha. "But isn't first place much more better?" Asked Ramu. "I thought you would be proud. Ill just go home now" Said Risha back to Ramu. "Okay" He replied back. Later that day Ramu joined his mother to go to the store. "Mother" Said Ramu. "Yes Dear" His mother replied back. "Why is Mr Nihal's face Curved? Why does it look like that?" Asked Ramu while pointing to a Mr Nihal. "Dear! We do not say things like that" Said Ramu's mother. Mr Nihal walked up to Ramu. "Hey Ramu. Why do you always question everything? Its not always good. Sometimes the people you question get hurt." Said Mr Nihal to Ramu."Oh. I did not know. From now on wards I will try to stop questioning everything. Thank you Mr Nihal" Said Ramu. The next day Ramu went to Risha's house. "Risha I am so sorry for questioning everything." Said Ramu. "Thats alright" Said Risha. "Even sometimes I get too curious." Said Risha. The moral of the story is, before you ask make sure its not hurting anybody. Always questioning everything wont be the answer.
author: SHAIKHA MUQADDAS  MAHABOOB
illustrator: Aakanksha Mittra; Jean  Fullalove; Parth Nadkarni; Phạm Hoàng  Giang; Sam  van Riet; Smitha Shivaswamy; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Vũ Thị  Thùy Dung

title: The Missing Currency
text: Prologue Naina It is often said that the smoke from a fire is more destructive than the fire itself, and this turned to be true in this case too. I really hoped it worked out for her this time. Watching her flail around like this, screaming and crying, broke my heart into a million pieces. The memory of the fire, however, threatened to turn everything to smoke for her. Chapter 1 I woke up with a start, gasping for air into my lungs. I had the same nightmare I did every once in a while: a woman, all clad in white, taking my sister away. "Same nightmare?" asked Sia, already making breakfast. "Good morning. These pancakes should cheer you up. Besides, we're going to be late to that coin show." "Oh my God, to think I almost overslept! I don't think I have time for breakfast." I said incoherently, half dazed by the nightmare. I avoided the mirror, knowing I'd find a pale, skinny girl with dark circles around her dark eyes. By the time I got ready, Sia had already packed the pancakes for me to devour on the way to the show. Despite being younger than me, she was more responsible and took care of me, often accompanying me everywhere to make sure I didn't cause a ruckus. We quickly hopped into a cab, hoping we wouldn't be too late. It turned out that all our hurry was for nothing, since the dealer was running late. "Remind me why we're here you thought this would be a good idea again? This whole 'mythical coin dealer' sounds like a scam to me." asked my twin, her voice heavy with sarcasm and disbelief. She was the complete opposite of me, and so naturally didn't believe in the concept of mythical currencies. She had reluctantly agreed to come after I promised her I would do the dishes for a week. "It isn't! I'm sure his running late is just a coincidence. Besides, he's Arnold Wellington. He's the world's most famous coin collector. Each time a new mythical coin is found, that mythical world is saved from a catastrophe. You can see the mythical coins for yourself today. even my favourite ones like Scronium and Prolucium." "Good to meet another coin geek like me" said a deep voice from behind. I whirled around to see Arnold Wellington, smiling. I apologize for the delay. We will begin shortly" Now was my chance. I smiled and was about to ask him for an apprenticeship, my dream job, when he whirled away, as elusive as the coins he deals with. The show that followed turned out to be the best i had ever been to. He let us in on the secret to tracking down magical coins - namely finding the corresponding magical symbol and tracing it onto glass at 4.44 a.m. Even Sia was wowed by the beauty of the coins, despite still being unconvinced about their magic. Towards the end, however, Arnold dropped a bomb on us. "You all know that each world has their own currencies. However, the oldest currency of all, Scronium, has vanished. There is no trace of it. We only have two days to find it, or else all hope of ever recovering it may be lost. So, as an incentive, anyone who finds it gets to have an apprenticeship." I immediately jumped up, volunteering to find it. So did Sia. Soon, there were throngs of volunteers ready to help save the currency, and we all left after making plans to cover different areas to find the missing currency's symbol. Chapter 2 The following Saturday was a blur. Willing to give up a rare Saturday holiday, Sia and I had spent hours scouring out each nook and cranny to find any relation to the missing symbol. It seemed to be as slippery as an eel. But how could we find something mythical? The answer, as it turned out, was we couldn't. It found us. As we sat down to take a break at 8, it seemed like there was a flash of light against the night sky near a telephone booth. We walked by to investigate further, where we found the symbol - a rose. We found it! I was about to search for the source of light, I saw a blind lady who was about to walk into a bunch of live wires. She and her dog were about to get electrocuted. "Look there, Ria" Sia said. I saw a kid trapped under a rock. With an unspoken bond, we somehow were on the same page. Finding the currency could change your lives and make us rich. It could launch my future career off into heights, but really, it was like there was no choice. I lifted the heavy rock off the kid while she guided the blind woman to safety. Just then, a note landed into our hands. Chapter 3 Only you are worthy of saving the ancient magic. Wait for something that breaks and never falls, and perform the ancient ceremony. We stared at each other in surprise. What breaks and never falls? We decided to go home and ponder on it after a good night's sleep. We woke up within a few hours of when we fell asleep. I had the nightmare again. This time, the woman clad in white poked a huge needle into me, talking about some fires. The next thing i knew, I was screaming again. This woke Sia up. After i had calmed down, she asked, "What time is it?" "Some where around daybreak" "DAYBREAK!!" we both screamed in unison, as we realized the answer to the riddle posed to us in the note. We quickly ran outside. It was just 4.40. We still had time to perform the ritual. The dry leaves cackled beneath our feet as we ran to find find the missing currency. Chapter 4 As we ran through the forest, an unknown person suddenly walked to us. It was Arnold! He walked towards us, grinning. "Well done, girls! Now perform the ritual quickly. You have found the symbol and have been proved worthy. All you need to do is trace it onto class in 4 minutes. And then, everyone would know about my - er I mean your feat." He realized his error - the fact that he had accidentally revealed his plan to steal the credit of discovering the missing currency from us - a second faster than us. Aaron grabbed Sia, holding a knife to her throat. "Do as I say, or your sister will pay for it." "Leave her alone. What do you need me to do?" "Draw." he commanded. I did the only thing I could. As I was drawing, I realized that we weren't the first ones to be a victim of his plagiarism.. His discoveries were as fake as plastic. At exactly 4.44, I finished tracing the symbol onto a nearby shop's window. Just then, the missing currency appeared. The light produced by it was so brilliant that it almost blinded me. Aaron walked forward, dragging Sia along. The atmosphere was hot within seconds. But the light produced by the coin was too, too bright. The dry leaves nearest to the coin caught fire. Aaron coughed due to the smoke and let go of Sia. I ran toward Sia, into the fire. I dragged her before she could be harmed. She kicked Aaron in the face and somehow managed to grab the coin too within seconds. We ran to home and collapsed onto the couch. Miraculously, we had saved the missing currency. The smoke was making me cough. Fatigue took over. Tired but content, I closed my eyes. Epilogue - Nina She opened her eyes. She had been having these hallucinations for 2 days straight now, and the doctors had only now agreed to up the dosage on the antipsychotics. Ria Sharma. I read the cause and her medical history of delusions and hallucinations. She was probably the most traumatized patient here of all, and as a nurse, I thought I had seen some pretty bad cases. She started having hallucinations after her twin, Sia Sharma passed away in a tragic fire. Her mind could not cope, and so it made alternate scenarios where she wasn't dead. I often wondered what her hallucinations were all about. I wondered if she resented us for taking away her sister from her once again. But most of all, I wondered when the damage done to her by the smoke would fade away.
author: Aditti  Durgani

title: Alive for a day
text: " What if I die before I ever get the chance to live? It's 11 pm on a sunday night, while all kids my age are sad that they have school tomorrow, here I am willing to do anything to go to school. I spend my days thinking about the most mundane things. I won't ever go to school, I won't ever graduate, I won't ever be like you. If I were you; I would take risks because life is short, I would dance at every party just because I can, I would make silly faces in photos, I would sing at the top of my lungs even if people stared, I would do everything I want, even if people thought I was embarassing myself. You have no idea, the things I would do to be you." I stared at the text message from my best friend, Asha. Asha is the strongest person I know, but Asha is sick. She has been sick ever since she was a baby. She'd spent her entire life inside the hospital. I knew that Asha was living on borrowed time and I was dreading the news that she was gone. I wanted to help my best friend. I wanted to help her do the most seemingly mundane things, because this might be the last thing I get to do for her. Without a second thought, I started running towards the hospital. I knew the road like the back of my hand, thanks to the countless trips to the hospital to visit Asha. Soon enough, I saw the big gloomy hospital. The hospital had become mine and Asha's biggest enemy. I walked into the hospital and was greeted by the tired receptionist. I said a quick hello and rushed along the hospital hall. I entered the room and saw Asha looking out the window.I called out her name but she was so lost in her thoughts that she didn't hear me. I tapped her shoulder, she turned around and her face lit up. " Oh my God Carol! " Carol wasn't my name, my name was Caroline but Asha loved calling me that, So I just let her. She hugged me and I hugged her back tightly, just in case this was the last time I got to hug her. " It's almost 1 am!! What are you doing here? Don't you have school tomorrow?" she asked " What's with all the questions? I just wanted to take you somewhere!" She gave me a confused look " What? Where? " I gave her a sly look and told her to go to sleep. She was wondering what I was up to, but she did what I asked. In the morning, I woke her up " wake up!! you have to get ready for school" She looked at me in disbelief but when she realized I was serious she burst out laughing. She put on my spare uniform and we were ready to go, but first we had to sneak out of the hospital. While we we were sneaking out, the receptionist saw us. I was sure our plan had failed and now she was going to send Asha back to her room as usual but instead she looked right at me and smiled, I smiled back awkwardly. My heart started beating faster the closer we got to school. This was very risky, but I knew this would make her happy.Can we really pull this off? What if we got caught? What if we got in trouble? I didn't even want to know the answer to those questions, but I knew it was all worth it if it meant Asha would get to live the life she wanted, even if it was just for a day. We entered the school and Asha sat beside me. I had brought my camera with me to take some photos so I could look back at these memories once I was older. Asha made silly faces in almost every single one of them. She wasn't worried if she looks stupid as she was having fun and that was what mattered most. As we continued walking home we sang. From nursery rhymes to pop songs, we sang our hearts out. After singing for some time we got quiet. I knew our friendship had a timer. " I loved everything about today! " she said while smiling. I realized that I did too. I learned that you can love everything not just people. I loved how kind the receptionist was, I loved how loud music was at parties, I loved that we could capture our favourite moments with a camera To my surprise no one even asked who she was. She wished everyone a good morning and smiled sweetly at everyone, she got excited everytime she heard the school bell ring, she loved how everyone greeted the teacher together and she loved how people would share their lunch with their friends. The bell rang once again, signalling the end of the school day. After school we went to a party, I had no idea who's party we were at but we were having fun. The bright lights, the loud music and the sound of people talking was like a whole new world compared to the boring and dull hospital, Asha danced as if there was no tomorrow, we were so busy dancing we didn't even notice if people were staring, and if they were we didn't care. But I loved my best friend the most. We had reached home by now. Before I could say anything to Asha, I turned around and she wasn't there. As I looked for her my mother came out of the house sobbing. "Where were you?" she yelled. I realized i didn't come home the entire day and didn't tell my mother where I was. "Sorry mom, I was with Asha. " My mother looked at me and started crying even more. She hugged me and said " Sweetheart Asha died this Sunday night. I stood there not moving for what felt like eternity. I ran back to the hospital. I burst through the doors and looked for the receptionist. As soon as she saw me she gave me a sympathetic smile. "Sorry for your loss, Caroline. I know how close you and Asha were." "What do you mean! You saw her leave the hospital with me" I yelled. "I am not sure what you mean dear, you left the hospital alone " The receptionist replied. I asked the people in school and sure enough no one had seen her and everyone said I was sitting by myself. I checked the cameras and she wasn't in any of the photos I took of her. Years later I'm still not sure what happened but Asha taught me to appreciate the mundane things in life. I still think of Asha everytime the school bell rings, everytime the school bell rings and at every party. Asha said she would do anything to be me but I wish I always live like Asha. I smile at everyone now, I take risks, I dance at every party, I make silly faces in photos, I sing at the top of my lungs and I do things I enjoy because that's what matters the most. I will forever thank Asha for teaching me how to live and forever tell the story of how my dead best friend was alive for a day.
author: Vaishnavi  Singh

title: The Greatest Time of my Life!
text: It was a Saturday night and my dad asked us if we had a holiday tomorrow because we were thinking of going to Ramoji Film City and having a blast and also spending the night until tomorrow after lunch. He added on and said “but you guys have to wake up early tomorrow or else I will not be taking you guys”. The next morning I woke up at 12:37p.m. “Hmmm.. why is the house so quiet? Mom, Dad, Karthik?” I Screamed to the top of my throat 4 times. No replies, so then I checked all the rooms but no one was there. ``So, does this mean that I’m home alone!! Whoooooohoooo!” I screamed, then suddenly I heard the bell ring nooo is the end to the GREATEST TIME OF MY LIFE??? As I peeked through the peephole…… It was my neighbors, but when I tried to open the door I realized that I couldn’t open it because it was locked! Oops.. a little too loud I Guess. Anyways it’s time to PARTY!! The first thing I did was to have breakfast and by ‘breakfast’ I mean to eat the best Flavor of Ice Cream, which is Cookies and Cream and also some Doritos which are also arguably the best chips in the world. It's about 1 o’clock now. It's Lunch time, but I ain’t feeling hungry. “Yeah I’ll skip lunch today” I said. “It's Time for the next activity”. Which is to play Minecraft and Fortnite for an hour or two. Time really flies, because it's 3 o’clock now. I’m super bored right now. I know what to do,“I am going to watch a Movie with some delicious buttery popcorn”. Now Let's decide on which movie to watch, which is the hardest part. “There are no good movies anywhere”. I guess I’ll have to rewatch a movie. My Favorite genres of movies are comedy and action, What's yours? Now it’s between RRR, KGF 2, and Thor Love and Thunder. I was deciding for 27 minutes, and decided to watch KGF 2. It was about 3 hours. I finished the popcorn in the first 20 minutes of the movie. Well now it's about 6:30pm. Now I’m kind of hungry, and I'm also feeling some pasta, but I don’t know how to make it. I've got an idea, I'm going to search on YouTube on how to make some delicious pasta. Long story-short the pasta did not turn out too good. It's about 7:30. I’m getting super bored and tired. I really like drawing. I might just try to draw myself, as I got ready to draw myself......... Ding dong the bell rang. “Yes, they're finally home”. With my hair half combed, I was sprinting to the door, “ouch”!! I stubbed my toe against the wall. Ding dong I heard the bell again, as I was hopping toward the door to open it “I forgot I can’t open the door”, so then I decided to peek through the peephole. “It’s my friends” as it was a sunday my friends call me to come play cricket with them. “Oh come on I missed this one too”. As I went wining to the couch. It’s about 8 o'clock, and suddenly I remembered that my cousins gifted me a lego set in which you have built a mini globe which took me about an hour and half to finish building. It's about 9:30 and I'm still full from the dreadful pasta. I guess it's time to sleep (the best part of the day). The next morning I woke up at about 6:45 am thinking it was a weekday. I was thinking to myself “I could have woken up like this yesterday and had the best day ever”. This morning I was craving Oreos and milk for breakfast. It was mouth-watering. I felt way better after that. I also decided I had to take a bath, a long one. I was in the bathroom for about an hour singing songs and bathing at the same time. It's about 8:30 now. I felt like playing lawn tennis but I could not go out so instead I just used the wall as my opponent. Just as I was getting the hang of it…… crash!! “Oh No, my mom’s favorite flower vase, I broke it”. I wondered and wondered what my mom would say. Until…… I heard the keys unlock the door. “Yes you guys are finally back”!! As I gave them all a big hug, I was sad and happy at the same time. Then I started to have a big interview with all of them. And when I heard them talking about how much fun they had I was super jealous of them. “Hey Jagannath, where's my favorite vase?” asked my Mom. What I learnt from this was to never wake up late or to never be late, And also NOT TO BE LAZY!! By -Jagannatha Datta Rajanala

title: Lost Passion
text: It was Monday morning and as people would say, a fresh beginning. The sun shined brightly and illuminated the white halls buzzing with excited chatters. Students flooded the entire building, a colourful rainbow of diversity. I walked to my classroom with a heavy bag on my shoulder. But it wasn’t the bag that weighed me down. It was something else. I took my usual seat at the back of the room nodding towards the girl who sat beside me, Amaira. She seemed lithe and petite, fragile like glass. She stayed silent most of the time which made me enjoy her company. It wasn’t like we knew each other. Of course, we didn’t. I hadn’t made the effort to get to know her, or anyone in this class. Why had I not made the effort? It was because I was still hung up on my past, my old friends. My mind had betrayed me and still not crossed them out. It still gave me hope to wait for their arrival, as if by some magical bus they would appear in front of me. But deep inside I knew all of us had already missed that bus. I was now in a new place, a new state and a new school. My father was a young dreamer with various ideas. He still had dreams for himself and had dragged his family into it. He was a workaholic, never having time for his family. He never told me the reason we moved. He just told me, “It’ll be better for all of us, I promise.” I didn’t really believe him but I had no choice left when my parents had already decided that we would be moving. Two weeks had passed and I still hadn’t found a place for myself. I would constantly zone out during class and try my best to remain invisible during lunch. Since school had already begun, everyone had started filling various forms for their co-curricular choices. I too had to join a club. Without thinking much, I signed up for the cricket team. Cricket, for me, had sweet memories attached to it. Since I was a little girl, my grandfather would take me to play cricket every morning in the local ground beside the lake. We would play with his friends and their grandchildren. It was one of the fondest memories of my childhood. However, 7 years ago he started getting extremely sick. I knew I had to let go of him, and with him, my fond memories. I stopped playing after he left for the place unknown. I filled the form and went to the drop box where I saw ‘TRIALS START ON TUESDAY’. I was confident in my skills but not confident enough to actually make the team. After school ended, I walked home. It wasn’t large and luxurious. It was small and tiny. But it was home. I greeted my mother and went upstairs to my room. I could finally be myself when I was surrounded by those four blue walls filled with posters of my favourite teams and cricketers. No one in my school knew about this hidden passion. I wondered whether anything would change if they knew. My mind was the most dangerous place for me to be in. It never helped. All it did was create more confusion and ask questions I didn’t know the answers to. I did my homework and tossed my cricket ball a few times. I thought about grandpa and what he would think when he saw me try out the next day. I fell asleep in the comfort of my bed, drowning in the covers falling into a deep dream. I was woken up by bright rays of sun falling on my eyes and my mother’s cheerful voice, “Breakfast’s ready! Come down.” I brushed my teeth and took a quick shower before rushing down. I greeted my mother. My father was yet again busy and didn’t come out. I then walked to the large sea of students once again filled with chatter and headed towards the cricket ground. holy guacamole! It was huge. I change into my cricket attire and walked towards the group of students gathered around a man who I assumed was the coach. He was tall and well built who seemed like he could uproot a tree and throw it across miles. What surprised me even more, was seeing Amaira beside the coach dressed up in her uniform. But that was just the beginning. The man introduced himself as coach Verma and introduced Amaira as the captain. I was shocked, but awestruck. I knew there was something about her. She was like a hidden warrior, hiding her fangs from everyone. Coach made us do a few rounds of catching and then we started getting ready for a practice game. I focused all my attention towards the twenty-two-yard-long cricket field embellished with short green grass. I felt a chill run down my spine, a chill of thrill. Our team won the toss and chose to bowl first. We did our best and the opposite team scored a hundred and twelve runs. As I ran around the field, the wind blowing my hair and the sweat glistening on my skin, I felt my heart beat faster and faster. I could feel the adrenaline coursing through my veins. I interacted with my fellow team members, shaking hands with people here and there when we got a wicket. I felt happy for the first time since I had been there. I felt lively and enthusiastic. It was then our turn to bat. However, halfway through, our situation wasn’t looking too good. We had already lost six wickets and still had forty eight runs to make. I was next. I wasn’t nervous. All I felt was thrill and excitement along with a will to prove myself. I performed well. No, we performed well. I kept hitting the ball from the centre of my bat, making it roll across yards, crossing boundaries I never thought I could. Amaira and I formed a partnership of forty eight runs and led our team to victory. Victory, oh sweet victory! How I missed this feeling of winning. I ran to Amaira and moved my hand forward to offer a handshake. She didn’t take my hand. Instead, she pulled me towards her offering a warm, friendly hug. It felt like home, small but warm. The rest of the members joined us. It didn’t feel like I had just met them. It felt like I had known them since years. But none of that mattered. We were a team and we were celebrating a common victory. When coach announced the results, I felt happy to know I had finally found something precious again. I was proud of myself and I knew grandpa was too. The newly selected team spent a few minutes talking to each other. I finally felt like I could be myself again. I learned more about Amaira and we walked home together. On the way she suddenly started speaking, “I know it’s hard to move on. It’s hard for anyone to get accustomed to a new environment. Trust me, I have been there. Don’t let this define who you are, though. Don’t let this scare you. Make it your strength. Turn it into a chance to prove to everyone who you are.” Just one hour and this girl had me all figured out. She could see right through me. It should have scared me. This vulnerability should have scared me. But somehow, it just made me feel even more alive. Since then, I started attending practice every morning before school and every evening after school. Amaira and I started growing closer, spending more time together. In the blink of an eye, the strangers I once ran from became brothers whose company I yearned for. I performed better in school and started trying to mend the broken pieces of my relationship with my father. It wouldn’t happen in one day, but as I tried, I could see him trying too. I started enjoying life. And all it took for me to enjoy, was to find my hidden passion. Somewhere along the way I had lost the thing I enjoyed the most. I hadn't realised how much I missed it and the happiness it brought. Nothing would remain permanent forever, but we should try to find the best in each moment, each situation. Just because life changes doesn’t mean that your deepest passion should change too. You should follow it and never let go.

title: A Day In Space
text: During the Covid lockdown in the year 2020, my family and I had an opportunity to watch a splendid movie called ''Zathura: A Space Adventure''. After dinner, we had an engrossing chat related to the movie. Around 10pm, I went to bed with a book called ''Space and its Mysteries''. Soon I fell asleep. Suddenly, I heard a very loud noise with a massive fire breakdown. I opened my eyes. What a surprise! I along with my dad, mom and brother were holding firm enough the railings of our seats. The place was extremely strange for us. It was my brother who first realized that we were on a Space shuttle. We all couldn't believe it. We all four were in Astronaut outfits. What an amazing speed... My dad who was the pilot of the Space shuttle, revealed us that we were about to land on the Moon - the Earth's Natural Satellite. Wow! What a silvery shine, it was a delight for our eyes. We were very proud to step on the Moon as our names would be marked in the history of Moon-landers. We all took a selfie there and sang Vande Mataram. From there, we pursued our voyage in the Space shuttle. Next came the innermost planet of our solar system - the Mercury. The surface of the Mercury was very much like the surface of the moon - with lots of craters. We were taken away by the beauty of Mercury. My mom jogged our memory about our time limit for the trip. We planned to view all the other planets by sitting inside our Space shuttle. And we endured our journey from there to the next planet - the Venus, the twin planet of our Earth. My mom said that it was the brightest and the hottest planet in our Solar System, that even metals would flow like a river in Venus. Next came the Red planet - Mars. According to Scientists, if there were life anywhere else on the Solar System other than Earth, it would be on Mars. We too observed some frozen water like places at its poles. Then followed the largest planet - Jupiter with lots of Natural Satellites around it. Then came the ringed planet - Saturn. It was a visual treat for all of us. It too had more number of moons around it. Then we came across Uranus - one of the coldest planets. And ultimately the windiest planet - the Neptune. Finally, we planned to return back to our Earth. On our return, we saw lots of Comets, Asteroids and Meteoroids, Stars and other unknown Celestial bodies. Space Travel has been a fascination for many centuries. We had an electrifying and stunning escapade in our journey into space. We all agreed to one point, yes, that nowhere in the Universe we could find a place like our Mother Earth. The water, land, atmosphere and sun together provide the vital, life supporting energy for our planet. Finally, we landed on Earth. The first thing that came into my mind was to change my Astronaut outfit which was very uncomfortable throughout the day. I was shouting Hurray! What an Adventurous trip we had to the Space. By that time I heard my brother saying please move Agshi! Give me some space to sleep. Also, my mom was calling me to gear up for my Online classes. I suddenly sprang up to realize that I was still in my bed sleeping with my brother next to me. In spite of the lockdown all over the world, we had an opportunity to travel into the space through my dreams... What a dream! - A day in Space, Hurray!

title: Little Mimi's big dreams
text: Changing the world, it was a big challenge. " ﻿how can anyone possibly do it ﻿?" These were the thoughts of an 11-year old girl, who wanted to save the earth from the most dangerous event which could possibly end the world; ﻿ Global warming ﻿. Mimi was always curious about inventions, machines & researches. Nothing could get in her way! One summer day, Mimi's class teacher, Ms. Deepa, announced a science exhibition which would take place next month. "Attention, children! now i will be announcing the details of the science exhibition, which is happening after a couple weeks." While Ms. Deepa was listing down some important things, Mimi's head was somewhere else, far away in her thoughts. The week for the final registrations were coming closer & Mimi was still not sure if she wanted to join the event. As she ate her breakfast, many ideas of models were flowing into her mind. "Maybe you could give it a try" Mimi's mother said. "I still have time, so i will think about it" She replied. As Mimi left in the school bus, she saw someone new. "Who is that?" Mimi thought. "Goodmorning students, today we have a new girl who has transferred from another school. Please, introduce yourself." the teacher said while looking at the girl. "Hi, my name is Diya. I am sure that we can get together well. My hobbies are to collect new objects. I also aspire to be a scientist one day!" 'She seems very nice', Mimi thought. "Tomorrow is the final date for us to give our names!" Mimi told Diya. They both had become good friends by few days. Surprisingly, they shared many common interests too! "We both can be a team right?" Diya asked. "Ofcourse we can! But, what do we make?" Mimi questioned. "I know, we can make a project about how we can save the earth from global warming!" "Yeah, that's a great idea! We can make giant air filters to clean the air!" "And a machine which cleans the oceans, like giant nets!" "Maybe even some islands made out of the ash of burnt waste!" Just like that, they talked for ages. After she arrived home, Mimi told her whole family about the project. She'd participate a 100% for sure now! "Best of luck!!" her sibling, Bebo, wished her. "Thanks! i'm so excited!" Mimi said. "Ok everyone, today is the final date for registrations. That means the names for the exhibition will be finalized now. So, who wants to participate?" Ms. Deepa asked the class. One by one, all benches had given their names. "Wow, Diya you're taking part? that's great!" Ms. Deepa exclaimed. Everyone else was shocked too, as Diya was still new to the school and she was quite shy too. "Alright students, you can start making your projects. You will all be given the first two periods everyday until the competition to complete your works. So use your time wisely and no useless talking! i'm only giving you permission to discuss the models.";the principal came in the class and said. "For those who haven't participated, you have to study." Days passed by even sooner than Mimi expected. The exhibition was in a week. The duo had high hopes they'd win. "This is a nice model, now we just have to explain it." Diya said. Mimi already had a plan on what they would say. "I do have an explanation speech, but you have to help me improvise it a little." Mimi said. So they did. They wrote their speech. It was finally time. The science exhibition. Many groups had presented and by the looks of it, Mimi and Diya were nervous. Very nervous. Once the competition was over, the judge was announcing the winners. "Do you think we'll atleast get 3rd place? i'm a bit unsure if they liked it." Diya mumbled. "Don't be so tense! i'm sure they liked it. So what if we don't get a prize? We worked hard and i'm proud of it! I know the project might not be as good, but its ours!" Mimi assured her. No one expected what happened next. "The winners for this year's science exhibition are: Rohit and Sanju at 3rd place! Loud claps were heard. Meera and Ardra at 2nd place! The claps were even louder. And at 1st place,.... Silence. Are Mimi and Diya!!! The claps were even louder than a roar!! Oh how happy Mimi and Diya were! "This is so huge! We did it, Diya!" Mimi smiled with joy. "This really is the best achievement i have so far." Diya said. What Mimi didn't know, was that this small prize would bring her closer to the goal of her life. 10 Years Later Now Mimi was one of the most well-known person ever. She had saved the earth. How? All those ideas which were flowing into her mind when she was younger. That's what helped her! She had no idea that making a small model of her ideas would enhance them even more! She achieved her dreams! Diya was always her friend. She still is! She and Diya, side by side had become the best scientists ever! Her sister Bebo, was now one of the best doctor lab expert! This was all done by their hard work!! No one could have thought Mimi would have gotten this far. But she did!

title: The Celestial Connection
text: Woof! Woof! Bruno sniffed the fresh Swiss air and barked in glee. His master, Mr. Hans Wegner looked back and smiled. Bruno was a youthful Saint Bernard dog who was about 7 years old but still as active as a pup. He was here on a trek to the Swiss Alps with Mr. Hans. I-A Day in the Alps- We say that dogs have a sixth sense about disasters. Well, if anyone was in doubt, this fact would be proven right this moment. Mr. Hans thought that Bruno was probably just barking at the snow, but, l ittle did he know that Bruno was barking at the impending danger. Ka- boom! A blast shook the mountain. There was a swift cloud of snow coming down the peak towards the pair. The avalanche just came closer and closer until it filled the view. Mr. Hans reversed his skis and tried to go back but the avalanche caught up and Splash! Mr. Hans toppled face first in t he snow. Bruno along with some other creatures ran down the mountain in top gear. That very moment, Bruno realized that his master wasn’t behind him. He looked back to see that t he avalanche had stopped. There was just snow and an eerie silence. Bruno ran back to the mountain. He sniffed the air. Sniff! Sniff! And then grunted. Distinct smells of… a dead woodland animal, a raw apple and then the familiar smell of Mr. Hans! The dog reached the top and started digging at the spot the smell was the strongest at. He spotted Mr. Hans lying in the snow. Bruno gently nudged the still man and to his relief the man grunted. A few local farmers appeared and saw the man in the snow. They hoisted him and carried him down t o the village where the doctor could help the stricken man. Somehow, nobody noticed the poor d og. Bruno tried to follow the men, but soon got lost in the village. The men had gone into one of t he houses and they all looked the same. The village did not have many attractions to boast about except for a royal water fountain. Bruno just lay there in front of the water fountain waiting for his master… Mr. Hans got up and found himself to be in a clinic. Dr. Max peered over him and said, “Good Afternoon, I see you have had a rather nasty fall in the avalanche. Some local farmers have brought you here. Thankfully, you have neither broken bones nor any grave injuries so you are fit to go.” Mr. Hans nodded and then asked in a somber tone, “Did anyone bring my dog?” II-A Sorrowful piece of news- The doctor looked rather sorry and muttered, “No sir. He must have perished in the avalanche.” Mr. Hans was overwhelmed with grief and with the complete formalities, left the clinic. He was so sa d and so convinced that he did not even look around for his dog. He had loved Bruno truly as he had been a great companion. The next day, Mr. Hans left for Bern but Bruno, continued to wait in the village for his master. He had t o be on the roads, sometimes without food and water and when he was lucky, he was fed by some empathetic tourists and some friendly villagers. This did not stop him from waiting religiously for his master. It had almost been a month since the avalanche and Mr. Hans sat in his house in Bern opening the mail he had received. He had received a somewhat thin envelope from his brother Victor stating that he had been to a certain village in the Swiss Alps and had taken a picture in front of a great Prussian fountain. III- A Ray of Hope- Mr. Hans smiled and took out the photograph enclosed. He examined the photograph and his eyebrows rose up. Behind his brother Victor was a fountain which looked somewhat familiar. There were some houses and tourists as well as it seemed to be a busy spot. The highlight of the photograph was the Saint Bernard dog at the back that distinctly l ooked familiar. Mr. Hans was missing Bruno and had a strange feeling that this was him considering he had the similar birthmark on the head as Bruno. Mr.Hans quickly packed his duffel bag with his clothes and caught the first train to the Alps. Mr. Hans arrived in the village and immediately made a beeline to the Prussian Fountain. He took out Victor’s photograph and compared the two fountains. Yes, the horse and chariot design, the gold plating and the background…it all matched! It was the same village. He looked around and found a local photographer standing with his antique camera and a few lenses. IV- United once again!- Mr. Hans requested him for some pictures taken by him over a month. There were pictures of different tourists; American, French and even British. Most importantly, it was something else that intrigued Mr. Hans. Behind each of them was a Saint Bernard, conveniently photo bombing each photograph. Mr. Hans looked around the fountain but, couldn’t find the dog. He sat on a bench and waited till it was dark. He decided not to leave even when it became unbearably cold, still holding on to the hope t o find the dog. After a long wait when his patience was dipping, suddenly Mr Hans jumped out of his seat with excitement to see a huge, frail Saint Bernard standing right in front of him. He looked at the dog and s houted “BRUNO”! And being a perfectly trained dog, he gave the expected three short barks. ”Woof” “woof” “woof. Bruno had recognized the old man and limped as fast as he could towards him. Mr. Hans hugged him with teary eyes and was overjoyed to find him. Bruno gave a powerful affectionate leap on his master to celebrate the celestial connection between them. Finally the magic of the celestial c onnection of the two friends had begun forever. THE END

title: The Invasion of The Ghosts
text: It was the night before Halloween, me and my 5 friends were having a sleepover and what better way to start it than a horror story, wrapped in blankets and hot cocoa in our hands the agony began. “Hey Aarna, I have a really cool story that would knock your socks off,” said Annu. “I’m all ears.” said Ira. “It is said that there was a mysterious Book, nobody knew what it does. It was said to be in a cottage surrounded by haunted woods. Surprisingly it was so close to our school.” “Annu, I wanna hear more, quite fascinating,” said Tania. “My grandma told me that when she was a little girl, she and her 3 friends- decided to go on a camping trip. My Grandma and her friends Packed the essentials and left, they reached the camping site and started a camp fire and fixed the tents. Arvind said that they decided to look around a bit in the woods. My Grandma refused and she thought it was dangerous but their curiosity carried them away, even after warning them they didn’t listen. They made up my grandma’s mind, she took a diary and a pen and they all went deeper into the woods.. ‘We found a cottage but saw nothing special’, wrote my grandma in her diary, there were just some basic wood furniture, few torches. To their amaze, the hut looked clean inside as if someone had been there. Just then Arvind accidently flipped a switch that was disguised as a torch and fell in a pit, then in an attempt to save himself he grabbed Shyam and Vinod’s hands while falling but they lost their balance in an attempt to save Arvind. My grandma ran toward the camping site to get some rope but when she got back Shyam said that it was no pit but seems a secret passage, light was seen at the end, following it they found a small library, all books covered in dust but there was a book half-open on a reading table, 3 words were written. Arvind said “Hey its written in Sanskrit, let me spell it – Aaiyyani Lavalian Gatisaman, nothing happened, oh well it was fun.” Shyam said “Hey Anjali can you check on the camping site and make sure it is safe we will catch you later”. My grandma left back for the camp and waited, but after that my grandma heard nothing from them, and she was never able to see them again. We all were so engrossed in the story that we lost track of time. It was 5 in the morning. “Wow, I’m, I’m speechless” I said. “Too bad we don’t know what happened to those kids.” said Priya. “Anyways, thank you for coming it’s been a really pleasure hanging out with you guys.” Said Annu. I got on my cycle and went home, got dressed for school and stood near the bus stop waiting for my bus to school. A few minutes passed, when the Builder’s Assistant-Mr Akash walked up to me and asked, “What’s the matter Aarna, not in a good mood”, “No, nothing.” I spoke. “You look like you haven’t slept.” Mr Akash said while trying to hold on to a stack of paper. “Oh, it must the sleepover, you know staying awake the whole night listening a horror story.”, “What was the story about?” He asked. “A book that can summon ghosts." I replied. “Where is it?” He asked. “It is in the woods near our school.” I spoke. Our conversation was stopped when my bus arrived, “See yah Mr Akash”. “Bye” said Mr Akash and left for the office. “Sir, I just found a perfect plan to destroy that school,” said Mr Akash. “Hmm go on and better make it snappy,” said Mr Mahendra. “A girl told me that there is a book that can summon ghosts,” said Mr Akash. “You are very gullible, instead work on the design of my golf course”, said the bossy Builder, “I’ll bulldoze the school. The people were protesting a lot, not to take the school down.” Mr Akash was so upset that he went off in the woods to find the book. After a while he found the cottage, saw the book lying on the floor half open. The spooky cottage scared him to death. He took the book and ran for life. “I got it, Builder Mahendra,” he showed the book excitedly. “It’s useless, ghosts are not real,” said the Builder. “We will see about that, why don’t you do the honor.” Mr. Akash said. “Fine, anything to get you out of this ghostly venture, Aaiyyani Lavalian Gatisaman, see, nothing happened.” Just then the book started glowing, hovering in the air and POOF! The lights went off, all the windows and doors closed abruptly. “Who woke me up, you better have a good reason, if not, get ready to be vanished.” Said the Ghost obviously angered. Out of wits, gathering courage, the Builder muttered, “I have summoned you to ask a small favor, we want you to destroy the school that is near the haunted woods.” “But what will I get in return” thundered the Ghost. “Hm, whatever your heart desires,” said the Builder. “I will ask that later, I need time to gain my full power, midnight to be exact.”, “Well, fine, do it as soon as possible.” Said the Builder and hurried to find his assistant. “Oh, there you are, good job on finding a solution to our problem”. “Why thank you, don’t you think? the school is special, there is a reason that it is still standing for 60 years and it should not be destroyed for your luxuries, it’s not a wise choice." “Oh! you have to sacrifice somethings to get few things, besides, we have many better schools.” “But they are not like this one.” Said Akash, “Do you want this job or not.” said the bossy builder, “Yes, I am sorry.” Said Akash, “I’ll go and check whether the ghost is ready.” Said the Builder. “Are you ready,” Builder asked. “Yes, Aaiyyani Lavalian Gatisaman! ”, roared the ghost and suddenly there were hundreds of his kind marching to the school. “Ok, my minions, now gain your physical form and start creating havoc.” I heard some noise of something crashing but I was half asleep. But the noise grew louder and louder so I got up from my bed and went outside. The noise was coming from the direction of my school, I thought maybe my ears were ringing. Although, I knew that everyone were sleeping, I called my friend Ira. “Hello, Aarna.” said Ira. “Hey, by any chance do you hear crashing noises, strange sounds.” I spoke, “yah I do, it’s coming from our school.” said Ira, “should we go and check.” I asked, “yah, I’ll call others”. Me and my 5 buddies rode our bicycles to the school. Though we were scared on what our parents would say curiosity pushed us. When we reached there, we hid behind a rock and watched. We were astonished to see huge giant like figures breaking our school and the Builder and his assistance standing and the Builder gladly directing the destruction. I noticed that the Builder had some kind of book lying beside him. I told this to my friends. Annu said that this is the same ghost summoning book that my grandma told me about. “Ok, I’ll go and get it.” I went silently and ran away with the book as Builder was busy with monstrous work. I opened the book and read the first page, first line ‘Where there is darkness, let there be light’, “What does that mean” asked Priya. “I heard; Ghosts are afraid of light and it’s only 15 minutes till dawn.” I said, “that means we have to distract them for 15 minutes till the sun comes up, they will pass out.” Said kaya, “Ok, I have a plan, Ira and Tania, figure out a way to destroy the book, Annu and Kaya, take care of the Builder and Priya and I will lure the ghosts in the woods,”. “Do you think we can do this as they are more in number”, said Priya. “United we can. Alone we can do so little but together we can do so much.” I and Priya teased the ghost mob and started running when they followed us in the wood. Tania destroyed the book by ripping the pages out of the book.
author: ANANDI  DHAPASE

title: Ramu asked too many questions
text: A boy named Ramu is a by who asked too many questions. Whatever was infront of him he would question. "Why did you score second place?" said Ramu to his friend Risha. "Why? Was I not supposed to?" said Risha. "I got second place atleast." Risha r eplied. "Yeah, but isn't first place better?" said Ramu. "I tried my best." said Risha. "It's getting late. I should go home now." Said Risha again. The next day, Ramu went to the store with his mother. "Mother" Called Ramu. "Yes Dear?" Replied Ramu's mother. "Why is Mr Nihal's face curved?" Asked Ramu. "Dont say that!" Said Ramu's mother. Mr Nihal walked up to Ramu and said " Ramu why do you question everything? Sometimes it hurts people's feelings." " I am sorry" Said Ramu to Mr Nihal. "Its okay" Said Mr Nihal. Later that day Ramu went to Risha's house. "Hello Risha" Said Ramu. ''Hello Ramu" Said Risha. "I am sorry about what I said yesterday" Said Ramu. ''Its alright'' Said Risha The moral of this story is to think if it would hurt people before you say.

title: My Last Chance
text: It was 11:43 PM. Iris was at her desk, head in her hands, fingers massaging her temple. ”How could I have let this happen?” she scolded herself. Everything was spinning around her. The usual fade-into-the-background ticking of the clock seemed a million times louder and more pronounced. She got up and rummaged through every drawer, cabinet, cupboard, and backpack thrown carelessly to the back of her closet. She racked her brain for any recollection and retraced her steps until they stopped making sense. A little backstory, Iris was a 12-year-old girl living in San Francisco. Quite fond of books and using her imagination to its full extent, Iris was the ultimate daydreamer. Someone could be in a life-threatening situation and she would just zone out into a land god knows how far away. Iris also had an older sister, Phoebe. Phoebe was the opposite of Iris. Grounded, realistic and logical. She was a Math genius and super into computer programming. However going against the stereotypical smart kid or ‘geek’ persona, Phoebe was quite the popular girl. She knew everyone, was extremely nice, and got invited to every party. Of course, she usually declined since she had software to develop and mathematical problems to solve. Now coming back to what was troubling our dear Iris. She had misplaced an extremely,and I cannot stress this enough, extremely crucial piece of paper left to her and her sister by their mother, who had passed away about 11 years ago due to reasons unknown to them. If you’re wondering how the paper made its way to Iris’ soft and curious hands, she found it in her mom’s favourite book (title indecipherable due to the old, tattered condition), smooshed between pages 63 and 64. If you’re wondering what was written inside that was so important, I’m sad to say that I can’t answer your question for it would seem wrong to tell you before the sisters got to know. Iris hadn’t read the paper, afraid of what was waiting for her. So she had hastily shoved it somewhere that morning. As poles apart her and her sister were, she would much rather read it while holding her stiff yet reassuring hand. Due to the jumpscare the note had given her, Iris didn’t know where the note was. She searched the whole apartment. Nothing. Nil. Zilch. Her eyes begged for rest, her back on the brink of giving way. Nevertheless, she would not cease until the note made it back into her careless care. She could not afford to let her sister see the note, let alone read it. And then, as if all the stars aligned into a bullet shooting straight towards Iris, her sister stood in the doorway of her room. Her shadow loomed over her with the hallway light making her seem ten times larger than she actually was. “Iris…” her tone calm but threatening, “ are you looking for something?”. Iris didn’t dare try to lie, Her sister knew her, so naturally, she knew how she lied. Her sister had both her hands behind her back. She slowly brought one of them out to her younger sister’s sight. In her palm sat the creased and faded piece of paper, looking like it didn’t cause Iris twenty panic attacks. Phoebe walked to her sister’s bed and sat down. She then lightly patted the spot next to her, gesturing for Iris to sit. Iris took each step with a sense of dread and took her place. Phoebe took her hand in hers and spoke, “ Baby sis, no matter what’s written in here, we’re gonna get through it, yeah?” Iris nodded hesitantly and motioned her to open the note. The note went- My darling girls I’m sorry. I’m sorry to leave this way. I’m sorry for all the pain I caused your father. He must’ve told you that I died, which is true to an extent as a part of me has been lost forever, though I am very much alive as of right now. Don’t be mad at him. It was the best choice at the time. I was sick. Both mentally and physically. I was taken care of for the latter, but my mental state was deteriorating at an alarming pace. Nobody believed what I was going through. At the time your father and I were drowning in bills so he couldn’t provide me the support I needed. My condition was completely out of my control. I was doing terribly in almost every aspect so I resorted to drinking and with drinking comes turmoil. I couldn’t bear the thought of you being raised in an environment so toxic. But I was the toxicity. I had to go. I hope you dears can find it in you to not forgive me but to reach out to me. Hear me out. To do so you can contact the number of a friend (written on the back), the one who slipped this note inside My Last Chance. You might never find this, but I’ve got all of my fingers crossed. Love The Mom who lost her way so she got away At the end of the letter both the girls were in unglued states. Iris had waterfalls gushing down her cheeks while Phoebe’s eyes let out two stray tears. They sat with words trapped inside their mouths yet never coming out, reluctant to ruin the silence of discovery. Iris was the one to speak first. Instead of letting out all the sentences she wanted to blurt, she pulled out the most important one from her chest where her heart sat. “We’ve got someone to call”.
author: Shreya Arora

title: Back To The Future.
text: A sigh left his mouth as he kept aside his shoes and opened the door into his house. The very minute he entered the house, he was engulfed by the smell of samosas and then the tight grip of his son. Zain was a man in his late thirties, who worked as a clerk to a lawyer. He lived very happily with his wife and his seven year old son in the cornering streets of Piccadilly. Even though a dark cloud of poverty remained above their heads,they lived happily and cosily. Zain and his wife never let their son feel the struggle they were going through to make both ends meet. Zain was a kind of an ambivert also, who didn’t speak much, but he kept a few contacts in and around the city. While taking his usual route to his workplace, Zain had noticed almost every day,a man, in a large coat, and a cigar in his hand, who routinely stood leaning on a tree on the pavement. He noticed him everyday, and he has been seeing him at the same spot for ages now, and the maximum contact they’ve had was a frequent smile when Zain passes by. But through an acquaintance, he found out his name though," Ramsay". Zain had borrowed a little sum of money from a close friend of his, to get his son a comic book series on his birthday. Even though his friend told him that he need not pay the money back, the thought of returning the money went round and round in Zain's brain. That day as he settled down on his office table, which was cluttered in files, his eyes fell upon a box- a parcel. It didn’t have any sort of whereabouts on it, which piqued his curiosity and he tore open the package to see an Iphone and a letter. Zain had no clue on what it was all about and he caught hold of the letter and read along, “i shall meet you outside at 11:23 in the morning. You miss the Time,then you Miss Me” He chuckled as he read the peculiar time and since his interest was at its highest he decided to give it a go. Exactly, at the given time he walked out of the door and he caught sight of a familiar tall figure, Ramsay. He walked towards him and asked: ”Were you the one who sent me the package? Hey, how did you know that I worked here?” “I know everything”, came the reply. “Well uh that’s interesting, but tell me though, how did you manage to get one of these”, Zain asked, lifting up the Iphone in his hand, “I have not seen an iphone in ages, haven't seen them around after college” “Oh! Are these outdated now?” Ramsay questioned. “See, that's one thing you didn't know”. Ramsay decided to ignore that comment of Zain and continued. “You wouldn’t have ended up in this dire strait if you used that sharp brain of yours in your youth days Ramsay: “I know everything” A light gush of cold wind made Zain tighten the grip on his jacket and look around as Ramsay went on.. “Have you ever wished you could change your past?” “Every single day ” Zain blurted out in dismay. “Ouch- W ait..How do you know about my ‘dire strait’ or whatever you just called my poor condition” RAMSAY: ”What if you could actually change it? ZAIN: “Yeah you’re funny, Wait oh! You’re being serious” “I could help you,” Ramsay shrugged his shoulders. ZAIN: “Do I look like a seven year old who believes in all those magic worlds and houses made of candies?” he asked monotonously. Again, Ramsay decided to ignore Zain's taunts and carried on: “That iphone isn’t exactly, something one could use to make calls, connect and all that? Actually, press the side button-” “Hey no offence but you're really wasting my time i should get back before they show me the door” Zain responded in a hurry trying to avoid the other man as fast as he could. But Ramsay pressed a button on the phone and everything froze. Zain,the wind, the dog which was shagging its tail a second a go, the passersby, literally everything and everyone got frozen, except Ramsay. After a minute or two, he pressed the button again, and everything rewinded and started back to its normal pace Zain was too shocked to process what just happened and turned around and walked back to Ramsay and through all that bewilderment within him, he said “So you were serious indeed.” To which he got a nod, as a reply. “You can alter time?”.he questioned again and Ramsay nodded. “I can help you regain a better life by taking you back to the past” ZAIN: “What's the catch?” RAMSAY: “Nothing, but a promise.” “A promise as in…?” Zain trailed on RAMSAY: “I’ll only reveal it the minute we step into the portal.” ZAIN: “Portal? Woah this is crazy.” “Deal?” Ramsay asked, raising an eyebrow. Zain hesitated for a while, but then grabbed Ramsay’s hands into a firm handshake and looked into his eyes, and was slowly getting lost in his web of thoughts. But he was dragged back to the present when he started to feel the chills of electricity and magic through his veins. He didn’t actually believe what was happening, when Ramsay pressed the unique Clock Icon on the old Iphone. They heard the wind whooshing and they took a big leap into the Black hole which emitted a radiant Gold light around it. Feeling as though gravity had a big grip on him through the pitch back tunnel, as they were dropping off ‘into the past’, Zain yelled.. “What’s the promise, Ramsay?” Then came a calm reply as though he’s so used to the whole time travelling thing. RAMSAY: “Promise me you’d change everything you regret today, promise me you’ll find your potential and follow your dreams” It took Zain a while to process whatever he just heard, through the fizzes he was surrounded by. He managed to yell back an agreement when- THUD!!!!!!! He fell on his back and looked forward in astonishment, as Ramsay walked through the air and landed down perfectly, safe and sound. THUD!!!!! Ramsay lent his hand to help Zain get on his feet and spoke again, “Hold on to your promise and keep in mind, to grab ALL the opportunities you can because once you let it go, it's gone FOREVER" There will be a point in your life, where we will meet again. "After our next meeting, you should tell your children - that a chance, once gone, will never come back.By the way, by then, you’d know the value of ‘a chance’ more than anyone. Goodbye, Zain.”. Ramsay took a few steps backwards and leapt back into the portal and was gone within seconds. Zain stared into the empty space before him, he had only seen these in sci-fi movies, Zain felt a bit of a pain on Ramsay's parting. He exhaled and closed his eyes. Soon he got himselves up in mind and affirmed that this time, he was going to grab all those opprtunities once which had slipped for life: thus to lift the TROPHY OF LIFE and make it, a successful one, at par a DREAM "BACK TO THE FUTURE" by Bhadra Ravisankar. This is a motivational story knitted well with a thought of science fiction concept. Opprtunities in life will come only once. Go and embrace Life.
author: Bhadra  Ravisankar
