Ali and Shiva went to King Akbar and said " king Akbar I want to show my friend Ali the temple of lord Shiva which is in the hills but the saints are not allowing Ali in they are throwing Ali and beating him I think this is not fair they are talking about regions and all, you are the only one who can slove this please help us! " But the king don't know how to slove this problem How do you think the king can slove this problem?
author: amulya chitturi

title: WISE OVER GREEDY
text: Once upon a time in a village known as Basotha, there lived a Tribal king who lived a life everyone dreamed of. He has two sons, Diallo and Faraji. They both led a very peaceful life, living and enjoying each and every moment of their life. As they were from a rich family they never faced poverty or shortage of basic essentials throughout their teenage. As the King grew old and weak day by day he worried about giving away his assets. He discussed this with his well-wishers and one of them suggested to share the properties equally among the sons. But one of them replied, "Test both of your sons and give the properties to the wise one, so that your assets wont be misused". Talking about the brothers, Diallo was a spoiled kid who lavish his resources for partying and his own selfish reasons but Faraji was a polite and well mannered kid who was kind to everyone. As Diallo was the eldest he always scolded his younger brother on negligible things. The king called them and told about the tests they have to do, both were facile. The villagers were astonished by the kings demand but most of them felt it as dumb. The challenge was to fill a room completely, they would have given a room and they should fill it with anything available in this world, but it should be completely filled without leaving an empty corner. As Diallo walked over the streets he did not wanted to spend his money on stuff to fill his room as if he spent less money on stuff he would be able to keep the money left with him and can use spend it on him. Trash wont be expensive and can be used to fill the room without leaving a space. He bought all the trash. The room were stinky and smelled awful making the people run out of it immediately after someone entered to it. The king and villagers were disappointed to see this act of Diallo and went to check on the other room of Faraji. Faraji had thought a lot about this summon, he set his eyes on the sun and said "Hooray!" He had got an idea about filling his room in the best way ever someone could. When the king opened Faraji's room he was mesmerized by the light coming up, He was doubtful and entered inside to see what his son has done in this room. The villagers and king saw nothing in that room but a single light bulb hanging on the ceiling of that room. The king uttered "hum.. The competition was to fill the room completely and not empty it. Diallo was furious on his failure and started to shout,'' hey what have you done here don't you have any sense''. Faraji smile and said, "Abba, you told me to fill the room, and here I have filled it with Light, according to your conditions all corners of this room is filled, and not any space is left out. The king knowing that every masses of that room is filled by something and it is light proudly appreciated him for his knowledge and sage. After a few days the king passed away leaving the whole village in Faraji's hand. The power and position was wisely utilized by the young king and the kingdom was well maintained. Everyone in the kingdom was happy to get him as a ruler. King Faraji amazed the people by wise decisions everyday.
author: shada shanu
illustrator: Bronwen Heath; Maithili  Joshi; Michael  Sagikwa; Rajiv Eipe; Rob Owen; Seat Sopheap; Shadrach Munene; Wiehan de Jager

title: MY WILD FRIEND
text: “We have run out of petrol!” exclaimed the driver. He was longing to get some fuel in the tank. “Can’t we walk down the jungle to our resort?” asked Ankush. “So do we have to” said their guide. They took their bags and rug sacks out of their canter and began to walk down the river in the dense jungle. All of their throats were parched, leeches all over their feet. They were going to fill their bottles with fresh river water. Ankush was one of the seven in the group who had special compassion and affection for animals. “We will top up our bottles and then proceed” said the guide. He and the others went down to the river. Ankush went near to fill his bottle when his bottle slipped out of his hand and fell in the river. He ran past the river to fetch the bottle but slipped over the crumbling soil into the murky river. Everyone tried to rescue him, but in vain. He slipped down a tall waterfall. Because of the high force of the river, Ankush fainted and was unconscious. He got up a few hours later with an elephant by his side. Ankush first shrieked, then limply lifted his hand feeling the trunk of the mammal. The elephant bowed down to Ankush. Then Ankush stood still allowing the elephant to adjust with him. Then the elephant sat down, accessing Ankush to sit on its back. Ankush climbed on the elephants back only to see the chains tied to it and understood that it was tamed. He could break the chains with a thick wooden branch because they were rusted. Then he signed the elephant to go down the river and to his surprise, he followed the commands. They walked past the river for what seemed hours. On their way, they saw many animals in herds and packs and groups crossing their way. Ankush was very happy to see them all and decided to call his new friend by the name Ranjan. After a few hours, when the sun decided to break for the day, they saw an animal… orange colored with black stipes, it was a tigress! They both were both surprised and frightened. Ankush fell off from Ranjan’s back and that was the time when the tigress decided to leap over Ankush. Ranjan, as was aware of these much anticipated moments in the jungle, lifted Ankush the next moment and ran away as fast as he could, leaving the tigress confused. After sometime, they had berries for dinner together. They both then fell off to sleep with Ranjan sleeping on three legs and Ankush lying on his back. The next morning awoke to show Ankush and Ranjan a hope of getting out of the jungle. They both had some wild mangoes and bath in fresh river water. Ankush was missing his family but was soon back in action by Ranjan spraying water over him and expressing his love with trumpets. A pack of wolves tried to fiercely interact with them. They together with a good spirit managed to drive them away with a big branch of a rain tree. The pair then continued their mission only to find footprints of humans and reaching the river bank the next moment. They saw a forest of gleaming torches and knew they had reached their goal. But it was a sad moment for both of them since they had to part their ways. Ankush decided to go alone the further distance to keep his best secret of being great friends with Ranjan.
author: Arha Ganapule
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Alyssa Pachuau; Kavita Singh Kale; Ninoshka Dias; Partho Sengupta; Rob Owen; Robert McEwan; Tanish Yadav

title: The Dark Woods
text: I Jumped over a tree stump eager to escape this forest and go back home. I was alone with no one to take care of me. I was completely lost and did not know what to do. I made my way through the trees each time hearing the sounds of creepy crawlies and animals in hide. With my torch light in hand, I shown the way ahead finding some sort of pathway leading out. An eerie feeling fell on me as something wove past my legs. I showed the torch down and peered to see what it was. A snake made its way calmly around my legs urging me to stand frozen. Heeding to its request, I waited until it went. As soon as it went past, I ran like the wind without a care in the world head-first into a tree. I lay on my back for a while with my eyes closed until I felt a wet slobber on my cheek. I slowly opened my eyes to find a hungry eyed tiger peering over me. I could not imagine if it would eat me or ignore me. I froze in fear seeing the deadly animal looking at me. After a while which looked like eternity, I woke up finding daylight creeping its way through the trees. The birds started chirping and the yawns of several animals were heard, awaking from their slumber. To my relief, the tiger had disappeared but had left paw prints on the mud that surrounded me. I ignored the prints and stood observing what all nature had to provide. Suddenly I heard a cry of joy coming from within the woods. A police man followed by my parents appeared from a hollow space between two trees. Overjoyed to see me, my parent rushed forward to embrace me in a tight hug. They grabbed my hands and we hurried to our house. My adventure has come to and and I will be sure never to wander in the woods ever again.
author: Adwitha Vinu Kumar
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Angie & Upesh; Maryam Kakar; Proiti Roy; Rohan Dahotre

title: TRUE FRIENDSHIP
text: Once upon a time, there lived friends named Jack and Ron. They were very good friends. They had many quarrels, but they didn't give up their friendship. One day, they began a journey. They passed through many villages and towns. They had a very long journey; they supported each other throughout the journey. After a while, they reached a desert. They had limited water and food.. Ron wanted to eat and drink just right there, but Jack said they should save the water and food to consume later. They had long quarrels but couldn't find a solution. In the end, Ron slapped Jack. Upon that, Jack didn't do anything. But he was asking for his goods, but Ron didn't want to listen to anything. He went on another way. Jack was very upset. After a while, by chance, they met each other at a river bank. There was no boat to cross the river so they had to swim. He did not know how to swim, but he still went to swim because of his pride. While he went swimming, he's started drowning. When Jack was tense, he jumped into the river to save the life of his friend Ron. He saves him from drowning. He saves him from drowning. Ron was thankful to Jack because he saved his life. Ron promised that he would never leave his friend Jack alone in any situation. Moral of the story: 1. If someone is speaking to us, then we should listen and not be argued with any reason. 2. We can never be happy because of quarrelling with our friends.
author: Tanushree Rout
illustrator: Selina Masego Morulane; Ajay Hembron; Aphisith Souphavongtay; Huynh  Vu Tuong; Promina Shreshtha; Shadrach Munene; Suresh  Mohli; Tapas Guha; Vusi  Malindi

title: One Enchanting Day
text: It was a happening night, without any stars or the moon, as they were sleeping under the blanket of clouds. Diya was scuttling behind every person she saw to sell her home made diyas. Even if anybody stalled for her poor diyas, they were only willing to give two rupees for them. Everybody was busy taking phone calls, talking to their relatives, putting candles and beautiful diyas on their doorstep... Diya was nostalgic. Her eyes were filled with tears. She sat on the sidewalk and sniffed. ‘My diyas, not a work of art, but does no one, not even one, have any feelings for a little lonely girl?’ She felt extremely sorry for herself. She just wanted to relax in her home, but homeless, stretched her legs, but they were too numb to do so, talk to someone, but her lips wouldn't move, as the excruciating pain kept on increasing as the day passed by. She wanted a lot of things, way more than she could afford at the moment, but something, just something, she could barely have any money for... was a small slice of cake. Any cake, be it chocolate, strawberry, butterscotch... her heart needed some cake rather than her stomach. She moaned, but in her mind. She sprawled on the sidewalk, a little afraid to be trampled by someone, but mostly, she didn't care. But as she laid her head on the stone path, she saw something unexpected... It had glass doors, a table full of wonderful sweet delicacies,chocolate chip cookies and free ice cream! ‘What a delight!’ she grinned. She was immediately on her feet and ran inside the bakery. Inside was an old man, busy but happy, lonely but cheerful, a man who resembled a kind person exactly. She went inside with her little bag full of diyas. ``Dear old man, would you like to have my diyas?” She looked at him with hopeful eyes. The old man looked at the staring girl, full of expectation. He was going to deny the little girl, but oh, those eyes, how they swelled to the brim with tears, how can he deny this poor, homeless girl? It was almost impossible, he thought to himself. “Yes, my dear, how much does it cost?”, he asked. The girl smiled a bit. “ten rupees for one diya, five for the small ones!” she said, suddenly all bubbly and cheery. The man, though, wasn’t sure what to do with them, as he was a Christian. “Give me two big ones”, he said, ignoring the fact he will not use them ever. The girl, very happy, gave him two big diyas. The man kindly gave thirty rupees, as he had sympathy for the poor girl. She then looked at him again with her large eyes, but now, more cheerful. He gave the money back to the baker for the chocolate cake on the table. The man was surprised, as she was his first customer, and even though this exchange of money didn't make any sense, he cheerfully gave away not one, not two, but three slices of the cake to show how ecstatic he was. The girl looked at him one last time, upset that she has to go away from the kind old man. The old man thought for some while. He walked to the girl, smiling, as he asked “Little girl, would you like to live with me, a lonely person myself?” The girl, surprised, said only four words to him: “You are an angel!” She embraced the man, her rosy cheeks and eyes moist. The man couldn't control his emotions either. It was the beginning of a new chapter in both of their lonely lives.
author: ADRISHA SAHA

title: The Lion Queen
text: It w as a peaceful day in the Pride Lands. All the animals inhabiting this lovely Kingdom were standing outside Simba's cave anticipating something. Or was it someone? they were about to find out in just a few minutes. Muffled cries were heard and then Simba slowly came out of the cave followed by Rafiki, whom Simba knew since the day he was born. And in Rafiki’s hand, he held the little bundle of joy that everyone was anticipating, that’s right! it was Simba and Nala’s child! Rafiki swung the baby in his arms toward the crowd of animals waiting for it. As soon as the entire jungle caught a view of the king's little one and their possible future ruler, it was filled with ear-piercing cheers and applause. But all the happiness and hoorays lasted only for about a second until they found out that the baby was, well, a girl! It was a deafening silence. Simba was confused. Just a second ago, everybody was so happy they could cry! but now all he could see was thousands of faces with a look of disapproval on each one of them. “What's the matter? Why has everyone gone silent?" asked Simba. Rafiki replied with a concerned look on his face, “well… she is a girl… and you know what that means…” Simba understood the charades. In fact, he knew very well what Rafiki meant. So Simba took his daughter inside the cave and handed her to Nala. He told her to keep the baby safe and stepped out of the cave once again to the crowd where the animals stood. First he bellowed out a huge roar to assert his dominance and to silence the hushed whispers of the animals. Then he took a deep breath and asked, “well, what's the problem? Why do you all look like you’ve just seen a ghost? Sivan, the Macaw, was the first one to speak. “She is a girl! she can't rule the Kingdom after you're gone!” “He's right!” said Kiono, the elephant. The rest of the animals chimed in and agreed with them. Simba sighed and quietly went Inside his abode. He didn’t say anything to Nala. She was overjoyed with the birth of her first baby and Simba didn't want to take that joy away from her by telling her what just happened. Simba and Nala named their cub Astrid. Years passed, Astrid grew strong and smart. She was a very independent lioness. She was so strong that she could take down ten fully grown lions! She was so smart that she would sometimes outsmart Simba himself! Simba and Nala loved the girl that Astrid had grown up to become. But of course, the animals still didn't trust a girl to run the Kingdom! One particular day, when Astrid was taking a walk across the kingdom, she came across Moses. Moses was a lion who was once Simba's close friend and confidant. But they broke off ties when Moses' growing jealousy almost led to him killing Simba. He was later banished from the Pride Lands and was never to be seen again. Upon seeing Astrid, Moses immediately recognized that she was Simba's daughter. He could tell by the way she looked, by the way she walked and just by the way she carried herself. She was almost like Simba's twin! “You've got your dad's eyes” called out Moses. Astrid was startled by the sudden remark coming from behind her. she turned back to see who the voice belonged to. Upon seeing Moses the first thing she noticed about him were the scars that he had on his face. They clearly indicated that he had been in some pretty serious fights and that he was someone to stay away from. But curiosity got the better of her. "Who are you?'" asked Astrid. Moses snickered and replied, “I'm the one who’s going to replace you, so you better watch out.” Puzzled by the mysterious stranger and his strange reply, Astrid just walked away from him. She went back home and narrated her interaction with the mysterious lion to her father. After Astrid described Moses to Simba, he immediately understood that the ‘mysterious lion’ that his daughter was talking about was Moses. Simba was perplexed. He was a bit scared as well. Why would Moses return to Pride Lands after all these years? Why would he say that to Astrid? He knew Moses would come with one purpose and one purpose only and that was to kill off Simba and his family and capture his kingdom that he had always wanted to rule. Another thing that added to Simba's fear was that Moses was one of the strongest lions Simba knew. When they were younger- when they were not sworn enemies- Simba and Moses never could defeat one another. That was because both of them were equally strong. But now, defeating Moses would be harder than ever as Simba had not practiced fighting or been in a fight in a long time! But if anyone could do it, It would be Simba. The following day, Moses finally showed himself to his nemesis and challenged Simba to meet him alone on the cliff in the far east of the kingdom in two days time. Simba knew Moses was planning to kill him, but as the responsible and courageous king that he was, he accepted Moses’ challenge. Two days later, the day arrived and Simba felt ready to take on Moses. Off he went to the cliff on which they were supposed to meet. Astrid heard about the fight between Simba and Moses from Timbo, Timon's son and Astrid's childhood friend. Astrid was horrified! She hadn't heard a word of anything that was happening! Simba had done his best to keep it from her as he didn't want Astrid to interfere and get hurt. he knew Astrid would come and try to help him. And he was absolutely right. Now that Astrid knew about this fight she couldn't just stay and wait for her father to come back! She had to do something! So she quickly followed Simba to the cliff without making sure he didn't see her. Upon reaching the cliff, knowing Simba would never allow her to be there, she hid behind a rock and watched as Simba and Moses were giving each other a tough fight. Simba was losing. He looked like he was about to give up. Finally, after multiple strikes, Moses had Simba on the edge of the cliff. Astrid saw that Moses was about to push her dad off the cliff. Without thinking twice, Astrid instantly sprinted from behind the rock and saved her father from Moses just in time. Moses clawed at Astrid multiple times. She cried out in pain, but still she fought on. She gave Moses a tough fight and finally managed to deeply injure him, but she too was badly Injured. Astrid, badly hurt, walked back home with her wounded father. On seeing her condition, all the animals of Pride Lands thought that Moses had defeated her and everyone blamed Simba for trying to make her the ruler. "How can she be a ruler when she cannot protect her kingdom?" thought the animals. Astrid was exhausted because of the fight and so was Simba, so they didn't pay attention to their mockery and contin ued to walk back home. Nala, aghast at how horribly wounded Simba and Astrid were, quickly put them to bed and called Rafiki to treat them both. Rafiki treated their wounds and relayed to Nala that it would take at least a month for them to recover What Simba and Astrid didn’t know was that Moses didn't die, he was Injured, but he didn’t die. Moses vowed to himself that his struggle to attain the throne of the king of Pride Lands would not end here. he started training himself to fight again. this time, he wanted to win no ma tter what it took. After about a month, when Astrid had fully recovered, she spotted Moses when she was crossing the jungle. Luckily, she didn’t let him see her. She knew Moses would try to kill her again. This time, before fighting him, she wanted to be properly trained and ready for the fight. She wanted to defeat him no matter what. The fate of the kingdom and its animals was now in her hands. She started training intensely. She wouldn't sleep. Wouldn't rest. Wouldn't stop. She had devoted herself entirely to winning the fight. Finally, the day came when Moses showed himself again and challenged not Simba, but Astrid this t ime. Astrid was ecstatic as she was absolutely ready and couldn't wait to take Moses down. She gladly accepted but Simba interrupted. “There's no way I'm letting you fight him! it's too dangerous!” Simba roared in anger. Astrid calmed him down and reassured him saying, "Dad, I am Astrid! the firstborn of Simba the great warrior! The warrior who promised he would take revenge for his dad and he did! I have the same burning fire inside me which you had when you were young, It’s in my blood!" Hearing this, tears rolled down Simba's face. They both rubbed their foreheads against each other and cried. After pacifying themselves, they got up, ready to fight. "There's no more time to spare!" said Astrid "let's take that moss down!” Simba snickered after hearing his daughter refer to Moses as ‘moss’. The following day Astrid showed up to the same cliff on which her dad and Moses had previously fought, the same cliff to which Moses had challenged her to come to if she dared. Moses snuck up behind Astrid and clawed her on her back. She roared in pain. she clawed back at him, right on his face. They both fought tirelessly until sundown. This time, Moses was the one who was losing. Astrid was much more stronger than him now. Moses didn't stand a chance against her. Finally, all of Astrid’s hard work had paid off. Moses was finally dead by the end of the fight. She roared so loudly that all the animals in her forest heard her. it was her first victory and boy was it a sweet one! Simba instantly ran to the place where Astrid was and hugged her tight. He felt so proud of Astrid and knew he did the right thing by believing in her. “You did it kid! you beat him! that's my daughter!” Simba rejoiced. Astrid then proudly walked around the Jungle telling everybody who had doubted her, everybody who had berated her that this time she was the one who had won the battle. She had saved everybody in the kingdom, including the king himself. “Now that isn't too bad for a girl now is it?” Astrid said jokingly. The animals of the Pride Lands had learnt their lesson. Never would they ever think less of a woman ever again. Astrid had earned the trust of everybody. Everyone in the forest bowed before her and Hence was the birth of THE LION QUEEN! THE END.
author: Sruthi Balaji**

title: Two snakes that changed my life
text: I live in a city in a gated society with 11 storey building, club house, swimming pool, CCTV cameras, security guards and play area. One evening, in the full moonlight while we were walking beside the club house, in a slightly dark corner, we spotted something shiny. S ome people put on their mobile torch lights. "Oh my! it is a snake's skin!" someone shouted and the crowd gathered there. It was in goldish yellow color, one meter long and had a scaly texture on it. People in the crowd around me were feeling unsafe. Quickly some people took photograph and posted it on whatsaap group. And some people advised not to send children there. And out of all that feeling of being unsafe, they decided to kill the snake. After a few days, I noticed blood stains on a nearby place where the skin was found. I rushed home and asked my dad to check the whatsaap group.And there was a photo of a dead snake. Now everyone felt secured. Everytime I passed by that corner I used to feel scared and I thought that we have to kill something to save lives of society members. Many months passed by, then after in diwali vacation, I went to my native place. My native place has lots of farms and greenery. And beside each farm there is a home. Some farms are harvested while others are ought to. I was helping my grandfather winnow their rice harvest when a tan brown colored, Indian Cobra came into our neighbour's home. Lady living there shouted,"Snake! Snake! Snake!" and the crowd gathered there. It's head was elliptical, the snout was short and rounded with large nostrils. One of the gentlemen proposed to kill that snake but the crowd refused and called ' sarpa mitra' (snake catcher). He carefully caught the snake with a special stick and put it in a bottle and left it in a forest. Suprisingly, he didn't took any fee. With this experience, I understood that there are two perspectives of people -: one of city-- Live and if required do not bother about others life and one of village-- Live and let live happily Two similar experiences (snakes)and two different reactions motivated me to adopt the second perspective of " Live and let live happily" for my life. This is the turning point of my life let's see what is next exiting there.....
author: Kavyanjali Mangal
illustrator: Aaryama Somayaji; Adonay Gebru; Deepa Balsavar; Imile  Wepener; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Madhuri Srinivas; Priya Ranganathan, Dincy Mariyam; Rajiv Eipe; Rohan Chakravarty; Suvidha Mistry; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Magic Island Named Love
text: The human mind is truly the scariest thing of all. It tells people they are not good enough, it can convince you things are real when they are not, it can convince you to kill and lie and do all the bad things you can imagine. So it is the scariest thing of all and it knows that. Have you ever wondered till what extent can the human mind go to? Well, a lot more than we can imagine. This story is one such of a thing where a girl imagined a lot, a lot more weirder. This is the story of a world where life is different. Every person had one superpower that they possessed. Hands in her pocket, looking down while she walked down the way to her classroom. Looking up, her eyes fell on the popular girls group. Sighing, she muttered,” would have anything changed if I was perfect like that? Would I have been happy if i had a perfect body, fair skin and slim legs?” this is Eleena, a seventeen year old girl. At night of the same day, she, being bored, tried to teleport in her room, all alone. But she wasn’t able to, the only possible reason to that was that someone was watching her. Turning back after feeling someone’s gaze on her, there was indeed someone watching her, the imaginary friend she had made 9 years ago, but she had forgotten about him soon. He, whom she had named Sirius, stood there emotionless. He was just like Eleena, the exact same personality and appearance but in male form. He dropped a note, she picked it up. It said,’ get me out of here, she’s killing me’. Confused, looking back at him, he already disappeared. What did it meant? who was killing him? Where did he want to get out from? she thought for a week and decided on helping him but how? She tried to teleport at the same place and time as she did a week ago and there he was again. As soon as he appeared, they teleported to a different world before she could even blink. Where was it? Nobody knew. She was clueless but the world they were in was totally different. It was a dark place with barely a few lights. But they were shining brightly, for her name literally meant the one shining brightly in dark and his name meant shining brightly, just like stars. All the confusion that had built up in her head finally came out in words, ‘ who are you seriously? Why are you real? And where am i? will you just speak up?’ she said while looking straight into his eyes. He replied while cupping her face, ‘you hold so much sadness in your eyes, I can almost touch the scars of your soul and cry. Would you help me? There’s a monster in here who’s torturing me, killing me. Please help me.’ Not getting the answer to her questions, she sighed, ‘lets go’ she said. Walking along the roaring sea, while the voice of the sea spoke to their souls. He glanced at her, she was just like the sea, so beautiful and calm, yet so deep. She broke the silence,’ how will I help you though?’ he replied looking back to the path’ your presence will help me, you’ll just need to realize something. Walking a long distance, they reached a huge castle like place. It was like the mansion that the rich people owned. They entered the place and went to the room that belonged to the ‘monster’. The room was enormous and magnificent. There came the monster. She was expecting a real monster with giant teeth and a bulky body but the monster was gorgeous. She was so perfect. Long slim legs, thin hips, slim waist, petite body, long blonde hair, thin high bridge nose with plump lips and big doe like eyes, wearing a stunning short dress with high heels. She was like a fairy. Eleena whispered to Sirius’ are you sure she is the monster who’s killing you?’ “ yes she is” replied Sirius. Indeed she was the monster. eleena greeted the monster. The monster said,’ you must be confused aren’t you? Well let me make this quick. I am the perfect girl image that you have had in your mind. You had portrayed the perfect girl image that you thought you had to be in order to be happy, to fit in the society but you did not know you were torturing herself during the process of fitting in. Sirius is actually you, eleena, the image of what you thought you are and your true self and this place is your mind. You are letting me, the monster, who is the perfect girl, to torture your real true self. The beauty standards are killing you, the need to be perfect is killing you inside, Eleena. Our mothers tell us that there are no monsters under our bed, or hidden inside our closets but they don’t warn us that sometimes monsters are just us, dressed in pretty clothes.don’t let anyone rule your state of mind You deserve to be happy and live your life and not just survive everyday. If I could change the way you look at yourself, you wouldn’t wonder why they say they don’t deserve you. Don’t let me kill your soul, my darling. You are beautiful just the way you are. You always wanted to go to the magic island right? You’re there already, my love. I think you’ve already realized what you needed to by seeing that you’re already weeping.’ The monster chuckled Eleena said, ‘I’m sorry. I never knew I was the monster myself. The monsters were never under the bed because the were inside my head. I fear no monsters now, because all this time the monster has been me. I let my nightmares force me into the need to fit in. they’ve promised that dreams come true but they forgot to mention that nightmares are dreams too. If it was a piece of paper, I would tear it, if it was a bottle, I would break it, if it was a wall, I would punch it- but it was my heart. I was breaking myself apart, it felt like I tried to scream but my head was underwater. It felt like everyone’s happy but me. But now, its different.’ She smiled and continued while facing down, wiping the tears‘ ive learnt to love myself, it’ll change the way I look at the world. It will make me admire other’s beauty without comparing it to mine. Thank you’ she said and looked up but to her surprise there was no one there. The monster had gone and only Sirius was there next to her. Perhaps she indeed accepted her real self. Sirius said, ‘lets go?’ eleena smiled and nodded. Reaching outside, he faced her and said, ‘thank you for helping me. I am really grateful for your help.’ She replied ‘I wanted to go to the magic island named ‘love’ but now I know the magic island is within us and the magic is us. Thank you Sirius, my friend from when I was 8 years old, I’ll forever be thankful to you, goodbye.’ Before she could look back at him, there was a bright light that itched her eyes and once she opened her eyes, she was in her room, where she had teleported from. She checked her phone for the time and to her surprise, it was still the same day she had teleported and it was the exact same time. She smiled and looked out the window. The world seemed much more beautiful now.
author: Priti Makwana

title: MY UPSIDE DOWN DAY
text: My Upside Down Day “Why does the eye see a thing more clearly in dreams than the imagination when awake?” Leonardo da Vinci Everyone dreams, but we don’t always remember our dreams the next day. Perhaps because of their elusiveness, dreams have interested people throughout history. In ancient cultures, dreams were thought to contain messages from the gods. I too had a dream yesterday. It was not a mere dream, but proved an eye opener to me because it carried an intense meaning. But at the same time, it was a hilarious one too. Last night, I dreamt that my mother and I exchanged our work. My mother is a housemaid and I am a student of class 8th. So I had to go to somebody’s house for household chores and my mother went to school in my classroom. When my mother entered in the classroom, everybody stood up and wished her morning. She was little surprised but she made it clear that she was not a teacher. So she sat beside a student. The very first lecture that she had was English. My mother was bewildered when the teacher asked about the homework assigned the previous day as she was illiterate. Unfortunately, the teacher made my mother stand and assigned her some sentences to translate in Hindi. The teacher asked, ”You rock the world.” My mother replied, “Tum meri duniya patthar kar rahe ho.” The class giggled. Then the teacher said, “Are you feeling down?” My mother answered, “Kya tum neeche mehsoos kar rahe ho?” All the students burst into tears. The teacher was irritated. She shouted, “Get lost” My mother did not understand what the teacher meant. She again translated it as gum ho jao. The whole class roared. The teacher was mad with anger. She commented “Are you nuts?” My mother innocently described, “Kya tum moongfali ho?” The teacher got frustrated that time and went out of the class. My mother could not comprehend the situation. Second lecture was of Maths. As the math’s teacher entered the class, the students wished, “Good Morning! Ma’am”. My mother was unfamiliar of these words, so when she tried to speak, she said “Goda Marungi, Mam” The teacher scolded her and started explaining the chapter”Division”. Meanwhile, she asked, “What is the half of 8?” My mother stood up and answered, “If we cut it horizontally, then get 2 three and if we cut it vertically, then we will get 2 zeros.” Some students chuckled. Rest also followed them. The teacher and my mother couldn’t resist and guffawed. It was such a hysterical moment. Afterwards, Hindi period was held followed by Social Science period, Science lecture. Most of the lectures passed with a lot of amusement. My mother enjoyed much in school. It was a strange but pleasant experience for her as she came to know many new things. On the contrary, I, who had to work hard, felt weary because I swept and mopped the floor, washed utensils and cleaned the furniture. I prepared food and completed all the household works. After such a tedious drudgery, I was absolutely fatigued. But I had to go back to my home. I didn’t have enough money to hire a taxi, so I went by foot. I stumbled when I was moving like an intoxicated patient and cried out ”Maa!”. By the time, I got up and found myself sitting on my bed. My mother rushed towards me anxiously, “Are you ok? My dearie!” Recently I realized that it was a mere dream, not a reality. But at the same moment, I cognized the significance of parents in life. I embraced my mother and started crying. Tears flew down my eyes. There was a stream of questions, “What happened? Have you seen a nightmare? Why are you scared?” I just replied,”Nothing maa,Thank you for everything. I love you, maa!”
author: Harsh Dhingra

title: The Adventure of Tanya
text: The Adventure of Tanya Tanya is a 16-year-old girl who lives in a middle-class neighborhood in the city. Her father is a high-wage worker who makes much more money than other parents and Tanya always has all the latest gadgets, like her phone or laptop. Tanya is at the age when she is looking for freedom to explore the world outside of her family home. The only thing she wants to do is to explore the woods behind their house. The problem is that she’s too afraid to go alone so she decides to ask for help from her friends. On a Friday afternoon, Tanya goes over to her friend Lalit’s house and asks if Lalit wants to come with her on an adventure in the woods. He declines because he has football practice that day, but gets excited when Tanya elaborates on what they might do, such as having campfires. Tanya continues inviting all of her friends over but they all have their things going on. So, at last, she decides to go alone even though she’s skeptical about it. In the following hour, she packed her things and started her expedition into the unknown. While on her way, Tanya saw a beautiful rabbit looking at her. The rabbit looked so beautiful that Tanya decided to catch it. Tanya followed the rabbit blindly until she realized that she now stood in a strange place. The adventure soon changed its course when Tanya lost her way inside the jungle and had to figure her way out. Everything looked strange and weird inside the jungle as if they were staring at her. Although terrified, Tanya took her bag and decided to explore the jungle until she finds her way out. After walking for a while Tanya reached the same place again. There was no view of the sky because of the trees surrounding it. The place was dark and cold. Losing all hope Tanya started crying for help. While crying she saw the same rabbit again which she followed into the deep jungle. She started cursing the rabbit saying “O beautiful rabbit, your beauty is nothing but an illusion as you use your beauty to lead me to this strange-looking place, I’m now lost and this is all because of you.” To Tanya’s surprise the rabbit replied: • The Rabbit- “it was you who followed me out of your greed and not me pulling you here” • Tanya- “How can you, a Rabbit talk??” • The Rabbit- “You humans know nothing about the world yet you think yourselves to be above all species.” * Tanya (Still surprised by a talking rabbit)- “If you know so much why don’t you lead me out of this jungle just as how you led me into it?” * The Rabbit: “You still don’t get it, It was you who followed me here not me pulling you into this place. But it’s human nature to commit mistakes and blame others.” * Tanya (worried): “I’m very sorry rabbit, please forgive my greed and help me find my way out of this jungle.” * The Rabbit: “Fine, I will give you your way, now listen carefully to what I say – the darker it is, the brighter it gets, remember to see the star but not the sky” The Rabbit left saying these words. Now Tanya was scratching her head as she understood nothing that the rabbit had just said. But she understood the part, she had to look at the stars so she looked up but the tree blocked her view. So she thought of going to higher ground and started her journey once again. On her way, she found a fox that looked beautiful, but she did not follow the fox this time. In the same way, she also found a beautiful butterfly that glowed in the dark but again she did not try to catch it. After hours of walking in the unknown woods, she finally found a small hill. She quickly tried to climb up but fell down as she stepped into a puddle. When she stood up again, the ground started shaking. She was terrified, thinking it was an earthquake, and tried to run, but to her surprise, it was not an earthquake but the mountain moving. When she looked carefully, the mountain seemed to have legs. The mountain turned out to be a giant tortoise and the puddle Tanya stepped on was the tortoise’s eye. Tanya then heard a loud voice asking her: “Who are you?” Tanya was terrified and looked up to find that it was the tortoise talking. • Tanya (Terrified and shaky voice): “ O mighty tortoise forgive me for I didn’t know your existence and stepped on you thinking you a mountain” • The Tortoise (laughing): “What does a little girl have to do in my jungle?” • Tanya: “I came to the jungle to explore it but I lost my way out and so I am looking for a higher ground to see the star as according to the Talking rabbit, the star will show me my way back home” • The Turtle (laugh) – “O little poor girl! You can call me ‘Daara’. Get on my back and I’ll take you to the highest mountain of this jungle” • Tanya (afraid): “No sir, I can manage” • Daara: “Don’t be afraid, I will not eat you” (And Dara started laughing) Tanya with no choice left sat on the back of Dara, the giant tortoise. Daara and Tanya started their journey together. Daara was very friendly to talk and started giving descriptions of the jungle to Tanya. This made Tanya feel relaxed and soon started talking. Both of them enjoyed the conversation. Just before the mountain, Daara stopped by a foothill; • Tanya: “Why did we stop here Daara” • Daara: “You will be leaving the jungle soon so let’s think I’m giving you a farewell party” Tanya got excited hearing about the party. Daara then called the monkeys from around along with deers and raccoons. The place was filled with animals. The monkeys made a flower garland and gave it to Tanya and made her seat on one of the rocks nearby. Tanya was overwhelmingly joyed by this gesture. Daara then started singing in a loud voice and the other animals joined him in dancing. Tanya enjoyed every bit of this party and then Tanya thanked everyone and started her journey again with Daara. Daara then took her to the highest mountain of the Jungle but it was already dark that nothing much was visible. Looking up in the sky Tanya found no star, this made her cry and while crying she saw a bright light coming from a far distance. Looking carefully she found that the light was coming from an artificial Star which happens to be the same star that was above a hotel in her town near her house. This made Tanya jump with joy. She completely forgot she was on the back of a giant tortoise. This sight made the tortoise laugh and started saying “Your joy seems to be even bigger than me.” And headed straight towards the light. In no time they reached the outskirts of the jungle. • “The time has come for you to leave the jungle,” said Daara. Tanya was in tears at finally seeing her town again. With a very loud and shaky voice, she screamed “thank you Daara, my savior, I’ll miss you” and started towards her home. Just then she thought about looking back at the jungle the last time, but when she turned, Daara seemed to have vanished. With astonished surprise, she looked back just to see a large pit in front of her. In no time, she fell inside with a loud scream just to wake up on her bed. • “So everything was a dream?” Tanya questioned herself and went to her mother to tell her about the dream. It was an adventurous dream. But was it a dream???? The End
author: Paku Riba

title: The Most Marvellous Christmas Present
text: Mother mouse climbed up the rusty staircase quietly. Her little lantern flickered as the cold Christmas wind blew in hard, choking its gentle flame. She felt like she was walking in a dream, for darkness reigned, making the passage feel unreal. An old attic lay at the landing of the stairway. Mother mouse turned the handle of whatever was left of the ruined door, and stepped in. The attic didn’t have much of the cheer and air of youthfulness which a children’s room must always possess. But then, a farmer’s old boot isn’t much of a home either, especially when it is by a windowsill which lets in bitter drafts. The little darlings, to whom the attic served as nursery and bedroom, lay cuddled up in a heap. They were pretty young mouselings with sweet smiles. But each was as pale as snow. The dark melancholy of the room not only reminded one of spiders, but it also brought about a feeling of sorrow. Peter, Mirabelle and Ann weren’t really having the best of times. Life had been hard for these mouselings, ever since they had moved into the antiquated boot which they tried to call home. The frequent unwelcome winds gave them nasty colds, and poor Ann’s nose was redder than a tomato. The children were quite weak by now, for an year of illness had been too much for them. They seemed like frail shadows, awakening to blackness and misery. Mother mouse, standing at the doorway, felt her eyes brimming with tears. Wasn’t Christmas meant to bring joy to every sorrowful soul? She couldn’t bear to think of her dear children doing their best to smile as they find empty stockings on Christmas morning. She looked at Peter, fast asleep in his grand spread-eagle fashion, and smiled. Mirabelle wasn’t even seen, for she was wrapped up like a neat parcel, under the blanket. Ann held on to her doll tightly, as though she would never let go. Mother mouse closed the door gently. The day before Christmas is dear to every little boy or girl, and young, audacious mouselings are surely no exception. “Wake up you two. You know today doesn’t come everyday,” whispered Peter, as a faint ray of sunshine pierced through the snow. Ann rolled away from her big brother and promptly landed off the bed and onto the floor. “Oh Mirabelle, how can you bear to sleep?” asked Peter, poking Mirabelle. Mirabelle, enraged, stuffed the end of her blanket in her infuriating brother’s mouth and fell fast asleep. But Peter wasn’t going to have that! He dragged Mirabelle out of bed triumphantly. “You mean thing!” cried Mirabelle in despair. “Do you have to make yourself such a nuisance? It's ever so early.” “After all, what are brothers for? I’m only keeping up my reputation, you know,” Peter replied, placidly. Mirabelle sniffed, and sadly decided to forsake her precious sleep for the sake of her even more precious dignity. Ann giggled as Peter grinned with great satisfaction. “Don’t expect to have any presents Peter, you haven’t been very good, for your kind information,” Mirabelle said, irritated by Peter’s contented expression. “Santa Claus considers teasing sisters a very naughty thing, and you have done quite a lot of that.” “I rather pride myself in that,” said Peter. “Besides, we aren’t going to have any presents either way. And I don’t think you should keep reminding us about that. Even though you consider yourself quite old to hang up Christmas stockings, me and Ann still can’t help wishing we could still have presents.” “Well, it was rather fun when Father used to dress up as Santa,” admitted Mirabelle. “Little Ann really believes in Santa.” “Well don’t you go and tell her about Father’s antics in Santa’s costume. Let her believe in Santa as long as she wants to,” Peter began fiercely. “Come on downstairs, Mother is calling. Ann, come along, don’t you start dreaming into space like Mirabelle!” Little Ann sniffed forlornly. Evening was drawing close, and soon it would really be the night before Christmas. And while all other mouselings hopped and skipped about, dying to go bed, Ann only wished Christmas wasn’t coming this year. She looked down at her plump little hand, which held a pencil. “I might just tell Santa. Peter says Santa is very kind,” thought Ann to herself. Ann stuck her pencil into her mouth, endeavouring to get in a good bit of thinking. After swallowing nearly half her pencil, Ann was finally done with the implementation of her little idea. She made a crumbled aeroplane with the piece of paper on which she had so religiously scribbled on something. Ann stood upon the window sill, glanced at her contraption and gently set it off on its maiden flight. Setting all her hopes on it, Ann whispered fervently, “Go to Santa.” Christmas came along, just as it ought to. Ann opened her eyes and immediately began to investigate the interiors of her holey stocking. Ann’s face fell, she couldn’t feel anything inside it. But oh wait, what was that? Ann drew out a little paper aeroplane. In quiet excitement she unfolded the paper. Pretty rainbows shot out of it in colourful streams. Whatever they touched didn’t look the same as before. In just a minute, the dark attic had lit up in the most beautiful colours. It was quite a delightful spectacle, but the greatest pleasure was in the face of the little girl holding the paper aeroplane. Ann looked all around her. She couldn’t believe what she saw. The attic was now just like the charming nursery room she had always dreamt of. Great windows with darling curtains smiled at her. The finest toys lined cupboards which never existed before. Even before Ann could take a moment to get lost in the myriad of fancies which danced around her, Peter and Mirabelle rushed in like hurricanes. “Ann you wouldn’t believe what we’ve just seen,” shouted Peter, nearly out of breath. “We’ve got a simply enormous Christmas tree downstairs and it's got ever so many presents under it,” cried Mirabelle, joy lighting up her face. Sitting about the Christmas tree, Ann looked around her. Peter and Mirabelle were overflowing with delight and rapture. Mother was smiling, a simply humongous handkerchief in her hand. Ann looked lovingly at her doll. It had a dear face with golden curls and a blue pinafore. The old boot wasn’t a boot anymore. It was now a pretty cottage with a front yard, exactly like the one Mother mouse had always wanted. The mouselings now had a bedroom all to themselves with nightstands and soft bunks. The kitchen cupboards were stuffed with cakes and pies and all sorts of sweet treats. Lavenders and golden sunflowers peeped in at the kitchen windows. Ann still held fast to the piece of paper which came like a Christmas blessing. Ann now noticed writing on it. The plump letters on the paper said, “Dear little Ann, Merry Christmas! Lots of love, Santa.”
author: Grace Mathews

title: Ajjubhai ki Mithai
text: Situated in the bustling town of Berhampur in the vibrant Indian state of Odisha, is a sweet shop owned by the patriarch head of the Sahu family. It rests in the middle of a busy marketplace, distinctive with its catchy bright pink walls. Here sits Ajju, endearingly known as Ajjubhai, on the shop’s cash counter, giving his workers instructions on how to arrange the stack of fresh sweets in the display counter. Ajju Sahu is an honest, workaholic and easy-going man in his early forties. After working at his father’s sweets business, he eventually decided to open his very own shop and thus came into existence, ‘Ajjubhai ki Mithai’. To his luck, the business was a great success and soon multiple branches were open around the city, with this, it became a household name in all of Berhampur! Summers were essentially the busiest times of the year, and this summer was going to be no different. Ajju drove his yellow TVS scooter, swerving between the swarming lanes of ‘Sanno Bazaar’ which though directly translates to a small market, is a huge and popular market, famous for its wide range of shops. From the luxurious jewellery stores to bargainous wholesale businesses, Sanno Bazaar got it all! Ajju finally reaches his shop and after a thorough lookout for empty spaces and adjustment of the scooter into the cramped parking lot, he enters his shop and is greeted by his employees. He takes his seat on the cash counter and begins reviewing the accounts of the previous week. A soft smile crawls across his lips as he notices the significant rate of profit. Upon sharing this with his staff, they all rejoice and treat Ajju to a special sweet dish. The day continues as any other usual business day for the shop. Customers are coming and going, many buying sweets in bulk to take back to their cities after a long summer break. Life seems to be going for him and he feels the same. However, he isn’t the best when it comes to his family. Being a workaholic man, wanting to earn a good livelihood and provide well for his children, somewhere around the line he forgot his responsibilities as a husband, a father and a son. He was not really present in their lives, weakening his bonds with his family. His parents were not in good health, and just wanted love from his son. Ajju never felt bad about not being able to spend time with them due to his busy schedules, because to him, he was working to give them a better life, which he was, but at what cost? Life seems to be going for him and he feels the same. However, he isn’t the best when it comes to his family. Being a workaholic man, wanting to earn a good livelihood and provide well for his children, somewhere around the line he forgot his responsibilities as a husband, a father and a son. He was not really present in their lives, weakening his bonds with his family. His parents were not in good health, and just wanted love from his son. Ajju never felt bad about not being able to spend time with them due to his busy schedules, because to him, he was working to give them a better life, which he was, but at what cost? Ajju amidst his billing and accounting work, receives a call on his cell phone from his wife, Kamla Sahu. “Dear, what do you want me to cook for lunch today? You’re coming home right?”, said Kamla. To which Ajju replied by saying he would not mind anything. Kamla insisted and they reached a conclusion that the lunch would be his all time favourite – fish curry. Time passes by… and soon it’s 1:15 PM, the time for lunch break. Ajju rarely goes home to have his lunch, but today was different as he had plans to eat his wife’s cooking. As he was getting ready to leave, his employee reminded him about his visit to one of his other branches for some documentation work. Needless to say, he was gone once again without a second thought. He returned 2 hours later at 3 and checked his phone only to see 4 missed calls from Kamla. He called back. “Sorry Kamla… I had to go out urgently.” Ajju said. He continued, “I might return late at night, so don’t make dinner for me. I have work.” Kamla retorted with an upset sigh and said, “Whatever. We’re used to it. You can do what you want.” Angered by her remark, Ajju got defensive of himself and they had a short fight. Listening to his conversation was Kanhu, a 10 year old boy who came to buy a sweet. As the scorching light of the sun hit the sweets in the display counter, he stared at them with both his hands placed firmly on the glass. After a worker ushered him out of his brief reverie and asked him what he wanted, Kanhu pointed towards gulab jamun. Immediately, “30/- per plate.”, said the worker. “I just wanted one piece though…”, said Kanhu. He was told he cannot buy just one gulab jamun and had to pay for one plate. He frowned and looked visibly upset, for he had wanted to eat one since so long. Right when he was about to head out, “Hey, kid!”, Ajju shouted out loud. Kanhu turned around and Ajju gestured to him to get a plate. Kanhu, with his head low, told him he had no money to pay him. Ajju replied, “It’s okay kid. You don’t need to pay.” On hearing this, Kanhu’s face lit up at once! He rushed to the counter to receive the plate of sweets and started gobbling them up promptly with a wide and radiant smile on his bright face. Ajju lovingly asked him his name and where he came from, the boy said it was Kanha and that he resided in a children’s orphanage in Anand Nagar. What about your parents? If you don't mind me asking. Kanha’s smile vanished and Ajju immediately apologised for overstepping. It’s okay. My parents passed away last year in an accident. I don’t have a family anymore. I’m very sad to hear that Kanha dear, but what about your relatives? They did not want to take me in, so I was sent to an orphanage. That’s horrible, you’re a very strong young lad. You can come to my shop any time you wish. That means a lot to me uncle, you're a very kind man! Once Kanha was done, he thanked Ajju graciously. “If you don’t mind me saying…”, he continued. “No no, go ahead. What is it?” Ajju interrogated. “Uncle, I know I’m a young kid and I don’t mean bad but, I overheard your conversation with aunty and I just wanted to tell you that a family is the greatest possession one can have. Give them time and value, we never know when they’ll be taken away from us.”, Kanha said. Ajju was out of words to describe what he was feeling. All this while he could only think of what he would have gone through if he were in the shoes of Kanhu, now it all hit him. Kanhu left the shop and they both waved each other goodbye. At that very moment, Ajju made up his mind and informed his employees to manage the shop for two weeks as he will be taking a break. They agreed and he rushed home. Naturally, his family was out of words to express their immense surprise upon seeing Ajju so early. Ajju goes to Kamla and gives her a hug, she could not help but squeal in joy. He lifts up both his kids in his arms playfully. He sits with his parents and the whole family gets back together for a fun dinner. After this small incident that quite literally changed Ajju’s life, he understood the importance of the role his family played to shape him into the successful and happy man he was. A family is where life starts and love never ends, it is the greatest blessing one can have. Behind every man, is a loving family, just as sweet as a plateful of gulab jamuns. — A story by Rahini Mahapatra
author: Rahini Mahapatra

title: Luna was lost
text: There lived a beautiful family in Colybra town. There was a 10 years old girl in that family. The family was amiable and they never fought for anything. The family consists of 5 members; they were a father, mother, a small baby boy, an elder brother and a girl named Luna. Her father’s name was David and her mother’s name was Alice. Her brother Kevin doesn't like Luna but Luna likes him a lot. The small brother could not talk because he was so small. One day, Luna was lost when she was there in the market with her family. Her mother, Alice cried a lot but she was not found. They informed the police but the police didn't take it seriously. So, Alice remembered her old friend Daniela. She was an investigator of Colybra town. They met her and told about all the story that happened in the market. Daniela told that it was hard but if they try it may be possible to find her. So, they started their quest. First they went to the market where Luna was lost. They searched a lot but there was no use of it. But Alice and Kevin found a spray bottle which can make a person unconscious. Then Daniela said it was a planned kidnap and also she said to check the fingerprints. Those fingerprints were sent to testing. The reports came after three days. So, they started searching for the person whose fingerprints were found on the spray bottle. The family and Daniela searched in different directions. But Daniela went in the dangerous direction and that was North side of the Trinity sea. On her way to the sea, an unknown person attacked on her. However, she missed the attacker. Finally she found an lonely place where Luna was held. She tied to a chair and Daniela saved her. She took her to her house. The family was very happy but wanted to find out who was the kidnapper. Luna was now scared to go out alone, she always wanted to go only with her family members. Her family members were worried about Luna's weird behavior. In one instant Luna's life turned upside down.
author: Kancherla Akshaya

title: Compassion
text: A heartfelt story of a girl who was full of compassion for those around her. A fierce sense of loyalty is what this story tells us. Once in a busy city lived Anamika with her small yet loving family in a society The people residing there had a very cheap and cruel behaviour which reflected in the way they treated the street dogs there. No one cared about this but Anamika was different. She used to speak up against those people even her own family. “Do not hurt them” “Why are you hurting them?Don’t you have other work?” With her allowance she used to secretly feed the dogs though it was prohibited by her family. One day her elder sister Prachita caught her feeding the dogs and was furious. She was about to convince their parents to ground her for a month. Anamika replied “Wait Sis!first listen to me.They are just so sweet and kind.They are the absolute opposite of what you all think. Just see it yourself, meet them once” Since Prachita possessed the same qualities as Anamika. Her heart melted at the first glance of the dogs. Both of them decided to convince their parents.They did not know that their parents was going to be such a difficult nut to crack. At this point of time everybody was convinced, they started getting familiar with the dogs. Anamika bought about 6 packets of biscuits for all the dogs she would give extra biscuits to three of the dogs- Caramel, Buttercup and Dusky. Anamika’s mother used to provide those three proper meals like pet dogs. Other people of the society started going against them. They even wanted to throw the dogs out. “Such disgusting creatures! they should not live here.” When Anamika's family prevented her from doing so, they started their evil plan-They planned car accidents for the dogs. Fortunately, most of the dogs were safe but one of their favourite dogs- Dusky had to suffer because of it. She was just 9 months old when she passed away. Anamika's family decided to take revenge as justice for Dusky Though they had no evidences for the car crash, they registered a case against the society management in regard to animal abuse. After doing so today prepared for the case- collecting evidences and hiring the best possible lawyer. Things were way too complicated for the 11 year old Anamika. She was full of rage in her heart. She was just so into her emotions that she could not even have a peaceful sleep. The day of the decision came where both sides present their evidences.And yet again, the good registered a win over the bad. All of them were sent to prison for three months. After getting older, Anamika understood all of this was karma. According to the Indian society,Everything about dogs is awful. She thought about it and came to a conclusion that it it is all about the thoughts of the people. When she grew up, she convinced people to change their perspectives and thoughts towards animals. She believed to treat all creatures with compassion. She said it is not just a word,it is a feeling.
author: Farheen Zaman

title: The Adventure of Tanya
text: THE ADVENTURE OF TANYA Tanya is a 16-year-old girl who lives in a middle-class neighborhood in the city. Her father is a high-wage worker who makes much more money than other parents and Tanya always has all the latest gadgets, like her phone or laptop. Tanya is at the age when she is looking for freedom to explore the world outside of her family home. The only thing she wants to do is to explore the woods behind their house. The problem is that she’s too afraid to go alone so she decides to ask for help from her friends. On a Friday afternoon, Tanya goes over to her friend Lalit’s house and asks if Lalit wants to come with her on an adventure in the woods. He declines because he has football practice that day, but gets excited when Tanya elaborates on what they might do, such as having campfires. Tanya continues inviting all of her friends over but they all have their things going on. So, at last, she decides to go alone even though she’s skeptical about it. In the following hour, she packed her things and started her expedition into the unknown. While on her way, Tanya saw a beautiful rabbit looking at her. The rabbit looked so beautiful that Tanya decided to catch it. Tanya followed the rabbit blindly until she realized that she now stood in a strange place. The adventure soon changed its course when Tanya lost her way inside the jungle and had to figure her way out. Everything looked strange and weird inside the jungle as if they were staring at her. Although terrified, Tanya took her bag and decided to explore the jungle until she finds her way out. After walking for a while Tanya reached the same place again. There was no view of the sky because of the trees surrounding it. The place was dark and cold. Losing all hope Tanya started crying for help. While crying she saw the same rabbit again which she followed into the deep jungle. She started cursing the rabbit saying “O beautiful rabbit, your beauty is nothing but an illusion as you use your beauty to lead me to this strange-looking place, I’m now lost and this is all because of you.” To Tanya’s surprise the rabbit replied: • The Rabbit- “it was you who followed me out of your greed and not me pulling you here” • Tanya- “How can you, a Rabbit talk??” • The Rabbit- “You humans know nothing about the world yet you think yourselves to be above all species.” * Tanya (Still surprised by a talking rabbit)- “If you know so much why don’t you lead me out of this jungle just as how you led me into it?” * The Rabbit: “You still don’t get it, It was you who followed me here not me pulling you into this place. But it’s human nature to commit mistakes and blame others.” * Tanya (worried): “I’m very sorry rabbit, please forgive my greed and help me find my way out of this jungle.” * The Rabbit: “Fine, I will give you your way, now listen carefully to what I say – the darker it is, the brighter it gets, remember to see the star but not the sky” The Rabbit left saying these words. Now Tanya was scratching her head as she understood nothing that the rabbit had just said. But she understood the part, she had to look at the stars so she looked up but the tree blocked her view. So she thought of going to higher ground and started her journey once again. On her way, she found a fox that looked beautiful, but she did not follow the fox this time. In the same way, she also found a beautiful butterfly that glowed in the dark but again she did not try to catch it. After hours of walking in the unknown woods, she finally found a small hill. She quickly tried to climb up but fell down as she stepped into a puddle. When she stood up again, the ground started shaking. She was terrified, thinking it was an earthquake, and tried to run, but to her surprise, it was not an earthquake but the mountain moving. When she looked carefully, the mountain seemed to have legs. The mountain turned out to be a giant tortoise and the puddle Tanya stepped on was the tortoise’s eye. Tanya then heard a loud voice asking her: “Who are you?” Tanya was terrified and looked up to find that it was the tortoise talking. • Tanya (Terrified and shaky voice): “ O mighty tortoise forgive me for I didn’t know your existence and stepped on you thinking you a mountain” • The Tortoise (laughing): “What does a little girl have to do in my jungle?” • Tanya: “I came to the jungle to explore it but I lost my way out and so I am looking for a higher ground to see the star as according to the Talking rabbit, the star will show me my way back home” • The Turtle (laugh) – “O little poor girl! You can call me ‘Daara’. Get on my back and I’ll take you to the highest mountain of this jungle” • Tanya (afraid): “No sir, I can manage” • Daara: “Don’t be afraid, I will not eat you” (And Dara started laughing) Tanya with no choice left sat on the back of Dara, the giant tortoise. Daara and Tanya started their journey together. Daara was very friendly to talk and started giving descriptions of the jungle to Tanya. This made Tanya feel relaxed and soon started talking. Both of them enjoyed the conversation. Just before the mountain, Daara stopped by a foothill; • Tanya: “Why did we stop here Daara” • Daara: “You will be leaving the jungle soon so let’s think I’m giving you a farewell party” Tanya got excited hearing about the party. Daara then called the monkeys from around along with deers and raccoons. The place was filled with animals. The monkeys made a flower garland and gave it to Tanya and made her seat on one of the rocks nearby. Tanya was overwhelmingly joyed by this gesture. Daara then started singing in a loud voice and the other animals joined him in dancing. Tanya enjoyed every bit of this party and then Tanya thanked everyone and started her journey again with Daara Daara then took her to the highest mountain of the Jungle but it was already dark that nothing much was visible. Looking up in the sky Tanya found no star, this made her cry and while crying she saw a bright light coming from a far distance. Looking carefully she found that the light was coming from an artificial Star which happens to be the same star that was above a hotel in her town near her house. This made Tanya jump with joy. She completely forgot she was on the back of a giant tortoise. This sight made the tortoise laugh and started saying “Your joy seems to be even bigger than me.” And headed straight towards the light. In no time they reached the outskirts of the jungle. • “The time has come for you to leave the jungle,” said Daara. Tanya was in tears at finally seeing her town again. With a very loud and shaky voice, she screamed “thank you Daara, my savior, I’ll miss you” and started towards her home. Just then she thought about looking back at the jungle the last time, but when she turned, Daara seemed to have vanished. With astonished surprise, she looked back just to see a large pit in front of her. In no time, she fell inside with a loud scream just to wake up on her bed. “So everything was a dream?” Tanya questioned herself and went to her mother to tell her about the dream. It was an adventurous dream. But was it a dream????
author: Paku Riba
illustrator: Arindam Dhar; Bhavya Kumar; Godwin  Chipenya; Huynh  Vu Tuong; Marleen  Visser; Mbongeni Fongoqa; Sanjay Sarkar; Sarthak Sinha; Shadrach Munene; Shivam Choudhary; Taposhi Ghoshal; Zaheer Merchant

title: AN ENCHANTING DAY
text: It was a happening night, without any stars or the moon, as they were sleeping under the blanket of clouds. Diya was scuttling behind every person she saw to sell her home made diyas. Even if anybody stalled for her poor diyas, they were only willing to give two rupees for them. Everybody was busy taking phone calls, talking to their relatives, putting candles and beautiful diyas on their doorstep... Diya was nostalgic. Her eyes were filled with tears. She sat on the sidewalk and sniffed. ‘My diyas, not a work of art, but does no one, not even one, have any feelings for a little lonely girl?’ She felt extremely sorry for herself. She just wanted to relax in her home, but homeless, stretched her legs, but they were too numb to do so, talk to someone, but her lips wouldn't move, as the excruciating pain kept on increasing as the day passed by. She wanted a lot of things, way more than she could afford at the moment, but something, just something, she could barely have any money for... was a small slice of cake. Any cake, be it chocolate, strawberry, butterscotch... her heart needed some cake rather than her stomach. She moaned, but in her mind. She sprawled on the sidewalk, a little afraid to be trampled by someone, but mostly, she didn't care. But as she laid her head on the stone path, she saw something unexpected... It had glass doors, a table full of wonderful sweet delicacies,chocolate chip cookies and free ice cream! ‘What a delight!’ she grinned. She was immediately on her feet and ran inside the bakery. Inside was an old man, busy but happy, lonely but cheerful, a man who resembled a kind person exactly. She went inside with her little bag full of diyas. ``Dear old man, would you like to have my diyas?” She looked at him with hopeful eyes. The old man looked at the staring girl, full of expectation. He was going to deny the little girl, but oh, those eyes, how they swelled to the brim with tears, how can he deny this poor, homeless girl? It was almost impossible, he thought to himself. “Yes, my dear, how much does it cost?”, he asked. The girl smiled a bit. “ten rupees for one diya, five for the small ones!” she said, suddenly all bubbly and cheery. The man, though, wasn’t sure what to do with them, as he was a Christian. “Give me two big ones”, he said, ignoring the fact he will not use them ever. The girl, very happy, gave him two big diyas. The man kindly gave thirty rupees, as he had sympathy for the poor girl. She then looked at him again with her large eyes, but now, more cheerful. He gave the money back to the baker for the chocolate cake on the table. The man was surprised, as she was his first customer, and even though this exchange of money didn't make any sense, he cheerfully gave away not one, not two, but three slices of the cake to show how ecstatic he was. The girl looked at him one last time, upset that she has to go away from the kind old man. The old man thought for some while. He walked to the girl, smiling, as he asked “Little girl, would you like to live with me, a lonely person myself?” The girl, surprised, said only four words to him: “You are an angel!” She embraced the man, her rosy cheeks and eyes moist. The man couldn't control his emotions either. It was the beginning of a new chapter in both of their lonely lives.
author: ADRISHA SAHA

title: Emma and the Painting
text: Europe has now landed." Detective Emma rushed to the flight with her best friend Lily, who was a famous painter. "Are you sure about this?" asked Lily. "Well, I have been waiting for this day." Emma's happiness lasted till she came to her senses after her hunger ruined her dreams. Feeling extremely hungry, she realised that she had woke up at the devil hour, 3 am. "C'mon Emma, ghosts don't exist...UGH, but hunger does!" thought Emma.''GHOSSTT!! Wait, it's my own reflection. Oh I forgot to tie up my hair, nevermind." Emma took up all her courage to go to the kitchen while chanting names of all the hundreds of Gods she knew. Her situation couldn't get worse until she heard a scream from her little brother's room. She barged into his room to find him laying on the floor, "Ray, wake up! Though you're the naughtiest brother anyone has ever got, but you're still my dear one." cried Emma. Being worried about her brother, she started weeping for the sake of showing her sadness. Seconds later, "Mission accomplished!" laughed Ray, "Prank me and my ghost will come to haunt you," said Emma with a red face. "That's embarrassing that you still believe in ghosts. C’mon, don't act like a 7 year old. Besides, you wanna be a detective," giggled Ray, "Then explain me how NOT to act like a 7 year old?" questioned Emma. "Good question but how do I know because I am a 7 year old myself!" Emma decided to ignore Ray. She took her snacks and slammed her room's door shut while Ray tip-toed to Emma's room and said with a terrific voice, "GhoOoOsts are real my dear, so be careful!" laughed Ray. Seconds later, Emma sighed with relief after hearing Ray's footsteps leaving. She sat beside her window and admired the moon, which made her feel happy. Looking around the sky, her eyes suddenly met Jill's room, who was her neighbour and classmate. She became suspicious as she found that the lights were still on. Emma took out her detective binoculars and took a sneak peek. "It's detective time to find some clues!" Emma saw that Jill was taking out a painting and did the weirdest happy dance. "Not a clue but a beautiful painting! Just like Lily's." thought Emma while having her snacks. She then slept trying to continue her previous dream. Emma woke up at 6am. The nature made her feel more excited to go to school but when she reached her school, she found Lily very tensed and asked if anything had happened. Lily said how she had spent weeks making a painting for a big exhibition, but now it was not in her house and was probably stolen. Lily also mentioned that she suspected Jill as Jill had visited her house recently and always had her eyes on that painting. But neither Jill nor her mom were accepting that she had that painting. "I had seen Jill opening a painting and I have a feeling that it's yours but I will need to be sure," said Emma and asked several questions to Lily about the painting. After investigating for a while, she was sure that the painting she saw last night belonged to Lily. "Now, she surely isn't gonna accept right away, but I have an idea," said Emma. Next evening, when no one was present in the house except Jill, there was a knock on the door. Jill went to open the door and saw two rich men and a tiny assistant having a weird mustache, wearing black suit and hat with the fanciest accessories. "So where's the painting?" asked one of the man with the grumpiest voice ever. "Who in this planet are you all?!! Tell me or I will call the police!" screamed Jill. "I am sorry; they can be a bit stupid at times. Your mom had called us and we want to see your painting," interrupted the assistant, "Oh! I am sorry, please come in! You would love the painting which I have made recently," flaunted Jill. The assistant whispered to the other men, "I told you, she is easy to get fooled." The two men were no other than Lily and Emma with Ray as the assistant. "Here's my painting," said Jill. "WOW, so beautiful! I will buy it in 100k dollars and keep it in a big exhibition. Give me the painting and take this suitcase of money. Enjoy!!!" ran off the three men. "Wait, have some-!" By the time Jill could offer them something, they had already left. She thought to open the suitcase the next evening in front of her parents. Three of them took off their mustache and wigs and were laughing thinking about revealing Jill in school. The event day had arrived, Lily had submitted her painting to the event and met Emma at school. Jill was also there with a smile in her face. Emma and Lily slowly revealed the truth to Jill informing her about the fake money in the suitcase and laughed. Jill's reaction was epic as she felt such a fool. She was angry for a minute but surprisingly later realised her mistake and said sorry. Later on, Lily and Emma hugged and forgave Jill. Jill smiled broadly and they all became good friends.
