title: Zombies in the School
text: I have many fond memories of my childhood days spent in Shimla. I was an enthusiastic girl with a curious mind, and I attended Pride Public School Shimla located just a few steps away from my house. My best friend Kayra and I would walk to school together every day and spend our days playing and learning together. She was also a curious girl but very sweet-natured. The happy memories I have are bittersweet because they also include that cold day in December 2001. It started like any other day, but by the end of it, everything had changed. The whole class was looking forward to their sports period, but when it came we were all laughing and running in the playground. The sky was clear, but something hung heavy in the air. We loved playing Zombie Burst, so we all hid behind the big tree trunks in the corner of the playground to escape from Kayra, who was pretending to be a zombie. All of a sudden, I heard some weird noises. When I looked out from my hiding spot, I saw an ugly green creature scaling our school's walls! "Come out, everyone!" Kayra shouted. "You won't believe your eyes!" We started running towards the school building, our hearts pounding in our chests. When we got there, our mathematics teacher Mr. Nitin took us into a classroom and locked the door behind us. "Was that a zombie?" I asked immediately. "It looked like one from the movies." "I agree with you, Kayra," Anya said before they were interrupted by a loud crash. Zombies spilt into the room and they both froze in fear, unsure of what to do. It felt like death was knocking at their doorsteps. But then a boy - who couldn't have been more than 19 - wearing a brown coat burst through the doors and fought bravely against the zombies until they caught on fire and died "I'm Dome," he said calmly. "Follow me if you want to stay alive." We trusted him implicitly and he led us to the old school library, which was now in ruins. He opened the door with an ancient, rusty key and we went inside. Once we were In, he locked the door behind us. The room didn't look anything like a library should; it was filled with eerie sculptures cast from iron all around. Dome explained that this place would be safe from Zombies because they couldn't break through the iron door--all of this happening because of a witch called Swain. I asked Dome: “Who is Swain, and what does she want from our school or us?” He replied: “Swam is only here to search for the 'Treasure of Immortality,' which supposedly is hidden somewhere in this city. Nothing else matters to her-- not even her own son." Just then, I saw a quick flash of purple light and the door opened. A lady wearing a purple gown and hat entered the room silently Dome said to us quietly: “That's Swain. Everybody stay back." She looked at Dome with an intimidating gaze and spoke sternly: "What a traitor you are my son-- how could you turn against your mother?" Dome angrily replies: "Oh! A mother is the one who killed one of her sons to gain the power of his soul. How can you even consider yourself a mother?" Kayra whispers to me: "Dome is the son of this witch. Is it right to trust him? What if it's a trap?" I reply in a low voice: " He saved our lives. We must trust him. It’s better to trust a friend than fall into the hands of a witch or some Zombies. And, remember,..the witch herself said that Dome isn't on her side." Dome brandished his sword and attacked Swain to no avail. He couldn't even braid her hair. Swain attempted to cast a spell on him. Dome bellowed, looking at me: "Pass that bottle". I saw a pink-hued liquid in a shard of glass on the table before me and tossed it to Dome; he caught it and threw it towards Swain's eyes. Her pupils grew white--she looked terrified. Dome seized her magical wand from her grip. She said: "Do you think it's right to kill me? I'm your mother, the one who brought you into this cruel world." Dome stopped. His complexion paled as if he had seen a ghost. It was a tough decision for him to make. And then he said: "I'm sorry, mom," before breaking the wand in half and ending Swain's life--and with it, the tyranny of the zombies. Dome sat down on his knees, looking relieved but also sorrowful at what he'd been forced to do. We cheered him up and thanked him for saving our lives from certain doom." "Zombies are no more!" I shouted out ecstatically. All the teachers and students emerged from where they had been hiding in rooms behind locked doors. They all seemed happy and relieved. Kayra and I went home together, arm in arm. When I told my parents about it later, they refused to believe me; can you imagine? The school authorities never even told the truth about what happened - they kept the entire incident a secret from the world at large. Life went on eventually... but, trust me, I will never forget that day."
author: Charu  Thakur
illustrator: Ankita  Thakur; Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Carlos Amato; Chaaya Prabhat; Clyde   Beech; Godwin  Chipenya; Heather  Jenkins; Jacob Kono; Jayesh Sivan; Lavanya Karthik; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Linh Chi; Ruchi  Bakshi; Sourav Sarkar; UK Nhal

title: The Inevitables
text: I never had an ordinary life after discovering my Inevitability at ten. At sixteen, I worked as a waitress at a local coffee shop for a living and was used to being overprotective of my sister, Dua. My name is Esther Jackson. To understand the story I'm going to tell, you must understand what an Inevitable is. We are a forgotten species, sworn to protect Time, to hide the memories of a treacherous past. It all started with a book, an ordinary book that I didn't know could change the whole course of my life. One day, Dua came to me and handed me a book as if she was hypnotised. I didn't even have time to open it when I was sucked into it. The sensation was similar to a paper being ripped into a thousand pieces. I landed in a place, a cross between a classroom and an attic. A tall and skinny boy with blond hair and blue eyes stood in front of me. I was sure I was seeing him for the first time, but his face was oddly familiar. He just said, "So she's the third one?" "Seems like it." came the reply. I looked around to see who had spoken, only to see the same face staring back at me, only with green eyes instead of blue. He was christened Adrian and the blue-eyed one took the name of Oliver. "You've been assigned your first mission, Esther, and now I am going to explain everything to you," stated Oliver. I nodded vigorously. "We're here in Brooklyn to seize the Chain of Time and destroy it. It is an immensely powerful object, that can be used to go to the past, see the future and even bring time to a standstill. If we don't find it, hell will break loose." "We don't even have to go anywhere for the Chain of Time. It is hidden in the Shadow Chamber. It is one of the most dangerous places in the world. Let's just say that it is a combination of one's worst fears multiplied twenty times over." continued Adrian. "Why does trouble always come and get me? Do I have a 'kick me' sign on my back?" "You've been chosen for one of the most dangerous missions ever Esther. Try not to be sarcastic." As strange as it sounds, we were sent into the Shadow Chamber to 'explore the most terrifying place mankind had ever seen,' as they called it. I could see the Chain of Time in front of me, but when I moved forward, my worst fear appeared. Dua. Her face was contorted with pain and blood covered her pale skin. As I looked at her in horror, she just fell to the floor and uttered my name. I could not lose Dua for a trifle such as this. She means everything to me. And her name jolted me back to reality. I had to do this for her, if not anyone else. I walked to where she was lying, took a deep breath and crossed over her to the other side of the room like that illusion was nothing but just an artefact decorating the worst of my memories. And here it was: The Chain of Time. Adrian and Oliver were already standing there, looking at me like I had just returned from the dead. Then, an alarm blared. "We have only twenty seconds," screamed Oliver to be heard over the noise. "Just grab that Chain," Adrian screamed back. I picked it up. And then, like the words just came out of my mouth out of their own accord, I said, "Vivimus," and we were transported back to Brooklyn. Three years later, I have all I want. A job, an education, my sister, two great friends and people who care about me. The Inevitable's motto does hold after all, "To peace, for peace and with peace."
author: suryakanta mohanty
illustrator: Bhavya Kumar; Canato Jimo; Gieve Patel; Karmacharya K.K; Kavita Singh Kale; Kripa B; Sanskruti Jitendra; Siddhi   Vartak; Sudhir Patwardhan

title: TREATED
text: There was a boy named Deepu he recently got admitted into a new school due to the transfer of his father. He made two friends there Raghav and Alisha.There were Deepu's classmates as well. The three friends used to hang out together completing their homework together, play together and do much more. One day a Monkey randomly and took the lunch boxes of the students near the corridor in which the fruits were mainly in. Some children were scared and ran away and some were crying and getting hit because of it. Some of Deepu's classmates Divya, Rohit and karishma were there, when they heard the screaming and shouting voice of the children they ran as fast as they could to reach the corridor. Deepu and his friends followed as well. When they reached there, they saw that the monkey was dancing and eating also throwing the fruit feels one by one. But a serious incident happened when Divya threw a big rock that hitted the monkey so badly that it fainted The monkey started to bleed and the corridor was filled with crowd, everybody was pushing themselves to see the monkey, when the Deepu notice the crowd, he also went there to see what was happening. After a while when Deepu saw the monkey lying on the ground he immediately took him to the medical room. Raghav and Alisha called the veterinary doctor with the help of their class teachers, Mrs.Seema's phone. After a while there the Rescue Team arrived and the Vet healed The Monkey. Later Divya and her friends give the monkey some fruits and apologized for the whole incident. Moral of the story:- Be Kind to every Kind, not just Mankind.
author: Abira  Maji

title: World of atoms
text: If we look down and see the ground, I see a tile. If I become smaller, I can see dirt on the tile. If I'm even more smaller I se the structure of the tile. If I'm even more smaller, then I see the molecules of the tile. If I multiply the word small with a trillion smalls,I can see atoms. BUT WHAT are atoms?That is what Riya did not understand. Riya was very apprehensive. She had a ginormous science test and she was definitely not ready. She was reading her textbook again and again but it just buzzed around in her head and came out. She was trying to memorise in a very short time what should be learnt in a slow and long time. This tension made her snappy, irritatable, snappy, mad, depressed, annoyed and guilty for wasting so much time.Her parents were worried for her. Riya was getting a bad headache because of her tension. She was excellent at long jumps and was selected for clusters in her school. But as her performance in science was terrible, her science teacher forbid her from representing her school which made her mad and hate science even more. With a scary temper she went for a walk unable to stand the pressure. She was kicking pebbles regardless of their size. Her feet ached but she didn't care, she just had to vent out her anger. She hit a large stone and the moment she touched it, she went into another world!!!! The moment she opened her eyes, she was floating in something. She couldn't understand what it was. It wasn't wet like water or cool like wind or grainy like soil. Yet she was floating in it it. But she was not able to walk on it. She saw a big sign floating which said 'Welcome to the land of pudding also known as Thomsontopia founded in 1903 '. This did not make sense to Riya. Anyway she moved on.As she floated by, she saw big black balls which looked kind of like raisins. They looked dark and negative. She saw nothing else. Then she finally concentrated on the spot which made her feel positive. The suspension she was floating in made her fell positive. She accidentally collided with on of the dark balls which made her go into something else. Now she found herself on the middle of a road. At a far distance, she was able to see an orb which had a beautiful glow. Then suddenly zooming towards her was a ball. It was zooming towards her soo taste that she had to jump above each ball to not get hit. Like that she jumped constantly. Then one ball after the came towards her with a short word on each ball. The message said " Welcome to the land of Ruthless Fords. The land where the electrons will Ruthlessly trample you like the Ford cars if you don't jump." But wait, Riya didn't understand a small point. If the electrons were anything like cars, shouldn't they run out of fuel? Sooner or later another message came by. WARNING: BEWARE OF EXPLOSIONS AT FAILURE OF ELECTRONS. No sooner did she think about the failure of cars, one by one, the big cars fell into the glowing orb.The glowing orb bubbled violently and exploded! The orb gases reached Riya and now she was transported to somewhere else. She now entered the world of Bohremia. This time, she was sitting on the black orb. Like the previous two worlds, these black structures were not floating g not moving but were stationary. It was peaceful. Before her were roads with stationary black structures. There were two on the first road, 8 on the second road, 8 on the third road and 9 in the road she was on. Then suddenly, another atom was coming near her. The black dot she was sitting on was moving out into a dangerous gap. Riya knew that if she wanted to survive, she had to reach the center of Bohremia. As she was a good jumper she took a looooong breath and jumped onto another black dot. And again and again. Finally she jumped into the center and was back near her school just in time for her test on atoms. Few days later, with a thumbs up from her science teacher, Riya joined the clusters and jumped the farthest in the completion. She won first place in her championship. And she was the class topper for her school. From that day on, Riya loved science.
author: Ruchiraa ranga
illustrator: Aditi Kakade; Adrija Ghosh; Angie & Upesh; Godwin  Chipenya; Nicola Smith; Seat Sopheap; Swathi Sambasivam; Taposhi Ghoshal

title: Friends and Friendship
text: Teen age is not just an age that is to be counted in one's life span but an age which is the most beautiful part of one's life. So, here is a story of a young girl who is now going to turn 16. She knows all about the age of adolescence but she can't understand what is good for her and what is not so good for her. Her family is shifting from the city because of her father’s transfer. What does a teenager think about friends? Teenagers are always concerned about expanding their friend circle and the same happened with Nancy Park. She was a really bright child who knew how to lead. Her friends were amazing. Everyone considered themselves egalitarian, whether it was a boy or a girl. Nancy’s friends were Lily 15 years, Tony 16 years, Bruno 16 years and Darcy 15 years. They all were really good friends. They all enjoyed each other’s company a lot but sometimes, they fought too. ﻿ One day when Nancy came back home, she got a shocking news. It was a surprise for her parents but a shock for Nancy. Nancy's father told her that he has got a promotion for which they have to go to another city. He told Nancy that they have to leave the house early in the morning. She was speechless, still in shock. Though she was a strong girl, she cried just because of her friends. “I can't leave my friends”, Nancy said. She cried a lot but had to leave. Next morning, Nancy's mother said to her, “Wake up dear!!! We have to leave”. Nancy was not in her bedroom. “Nancy, Nancy! Where are you?” Nancy came out of the bathroom looking very upset. “What happened Nancy? Are you not happy?”, said her mother. “How could I be happy! You already know how much I love my friends!!!” Nany said. Her mother said, “I know very well but you should be happy for your father and you can always make new friends”. On the way to the new city, she was thinking about her new city, new house and most importantly new friends. She got admitted to a new school but her new school was totally different. No one tried to make friends with Nancy. Everyone was busy with their own friend circle. Nancy turned into a very under confident girl from the most confident girl in her previous school. She became really quiet. The time came when it was Nancy's 16th birthday. She remembered how she celebrated her birthday with her friends from the previous school. She thought that her new friends would celebrate her birthday but this didn't happen. She invited all of her classmates and thought they would bring gifts but no one came to her birthday party. She felt very lonely, missed her old friends and cried a lot…… To be a good friend, one needs to be understanding, helping and caring towards others. Friendship is a very big responsibility. Friendship is like a flower Glowing in its own glory Each and every seed Telling its own story And once in a while You come across a friend Who is as beautiful as a flower With a good heart to lend….. ﻿
author: priyanshi dhanai

title: Mutual Bond of Love
text: Amay was still in his bed leaning towards his pillow, the sun rays were reflecting on his face, he slowly opened his eyes and turned his eyes towards the tree, whose few branches were very close to the window of his room. Amay was constantly staring at the green branches of the tree. The tree was shining, with sun rays falling on it and had a little silver and golden background effect. Birds were chirruping in the tree, the branches were making a twist in their positions. The sound of birds’ chirruping disturbed Amay’s sound sleep and he got irritated but when he saw the birds sitting on the tree in the sunny morning seems to him as the beauty of nature. He removed his quilt and got up from the bed and went close to the window to see the bird. When he saw the bird, he noticed that the bird is feeding her children with grains. The baby birds were crying because the grains were not enough to satisfy their hunger. The mother bird felt sad to see her babies crying and she herself remained hungry too. The bird covered her babies in the nest and went in the search of food again. At this time Amay’s mother was serving him with food and he shared the incident with his mother and asked “Mumma will the mother bird be able to get food for to satisfy her hunger or she will remain hungry for the whole day”. His mother replied “Amay the mother will find food for herself as she is a hardworking and never giving up mother and if she fails so you can keep water and food grains for the bird near the tree”. When Amay went back to his room, he saw that the mother bird has not returned yet, he waited for the mother bird to return. And after some time the mother bird returned with few grains on her beak, she went to her nest where she was just about to eat the grains when suddenly her babies again started crying. She thought that her babies were still hungry and she again fed her babies with her share happily. Soon the sun was set. Now the mother bird couldn’t go to search for food for herself and felt asleep because she was tired the babies were not mature enough, they slowly and gradually developing their wings and will soon learn the art of flying. One of the baby birds saw her mother sleeping hungry and the baby’s eyes were filled with tears. After few days their mother taught them flying, the art to search for food and how to save oneself when in danger. Amay used to watch the bird family and got motivated from baby birds and started helping his mother in her work. The mother bird daily use to go in search for food and slowly her babies also started accompanying her. One day the mother bird was searching for food grains and ate some poisonous and felt ill. The baby birds were worried and started crying, they brought food grains for their mother to eat. Whenever Amay wakes up in the morning and goes to bed at night, he always checks for the birds and observes their activities. He used to care for his mother. When his mother felt sick, he helped his mother in her work and became an obedient child. His mother loved him a lot and cared for him as every mother does. Both the families of the bird and Amay had a beautiful bond of love. One morning when the birde as well as Amay and his mother woke up, they saw that one of the baby birds was still asleep and didn’t wake up because she was dead. Her mother and siblings were shattered at her loss. Amay was also sad to see and felt bad for the bird’s family. That day the birds didn’t make any chirrup as usual. All day they consoled their mother and never made her feel the absence of one of her children. After seeing all this Amay also tried to become an ideal son for his mother.
author: khushboo aneriya

title: The Intelligent Lamb
text: One day, a lamb was eating sweet grass away from her flock of sheep. She didn't notice a wolf walking nearer to her. when she saw the wolf she started pleading, " Please, don't eat me. My stomach is full of grass. You can wait a while to make my meat taste much better. The grass in my stomach will be digested quickly if you let me dance." The wolf agreed. While the lamb was dancing she had a new idea. She said,"I can dance faster if you take my bell and ring it so hard." The wolf took the bell and started to ring so hard. The shepherd heard the sound and ran quickly to save the lamb's life MORAL: WE SHOULD NOT BE AFRAID OF SITUATIONS BUT THEM FIRMLY
author: Manavi Miracle
illustrator: Marleen  Visser; Siddhi   Vartak; Vongsavanh Damlongsouk; Wiehan de Jager

title: Wolf's Child
text: *Crunch!* With every step, the freshly fallen snow crunched loudly under my feet. This wasn’t going to work. I would have to be quieter. Slowly, I laid down on the ground with my back to the moonlit night sky and the snow-covered conifers. I began to listen for prey. But the bitterly cold, howling wind was too loud. I started commando crawling in order to make as less noise as possible. As I inched forward, it felt like my limbs were going to fall off from the cold, but I had no choice. I had to keep going, as I hadn’t caught any game in two days. I was crawling for hours now. Every part of my body ached, and my fingers were purple. I knew that if I didn’t stop now, I might not make the journey back home. But my pride as a hunter wouldn’t let me. I had been poaching since I was a kid, and nothing will stop me now at my prime. I crept onwards, until I heard a slightest something. It was a sound different from what the wind was making, and that was enough to put me on guard. I must have found my prey. I slowly I raised my head and looked around. In the distance I saw a white hue that was different from the snow in the background. It was a pure and immaculate white, whiter than snow. An arctic wolf. I had seen and killed many of them before, but each time I was dazzled by their magnificence, which only made hunting them more rewarding. The wolf was about 50 metres away from me. This would be too risky a shot for the average poacher, but I was better. I had never missed my shots before. I reached for my rifle and tried not to make any unnecessary movements. Slowly, I placed the rifle in front of my eye and took aim. I held my breath, then pulled the trigger. "Wow, a headshot!" I praised myself as I approached the dead she-wolf. Her beautiful white fur still shone after her demise. "Awoo!" a small voice whimpered. I immediately turned around in surprise, gun in hand. It was a small wolf pup, just looking at me with its sad eyes. He ran toward me, then past me, to his mother. He gave her a nudge, then pulled her by the ears, but she didn’t move. She didn’t look at him. She wouldn’t hug him to protect him from the cold. The puppy nudged its mother for a few more minutes, then began to howl frantically. My mind went blank. It was the first time I really felt compassion for anyone or anything. The little wolf lunged at me and began tearing at my feet with its claws, but I did nothing. I just stared at the child who had lost his mother at my hands. Before I knew it, I had dropped my rifle, and perhaps a single tear, for the first time in my life. That night I returned home depressed. I couldn’t believe that I had been doing this for years. I realised that up till that point, I had no real feelings. I had grown up without my parents in a foster home where all I ever experienced was hate. Eventually I had run away from there and had been living in an abandoned cabin right on the edge of the woods on Melville Island ever since. I knew what I had to do. That very night I turned myself in to the authorities to atone for my sins. I began to pray to God. I prayed daily and asked for forgiveness. Even in prison, where I was surrounded by corruption, I did not break the promise I had made to myself. When I was released 3 years later, I was still overcome with guilt every time I saw a mother holding her child's hand. I realised that praying alone would do nothing, I had to speak with my actions. Hence, I decided to become a forester, to be able to protect the animals from poachers.
author: Rishit Bhattacharjee
illustrator: Brian Wambi; Jean de Wet; Ram Kol; Rishit Bhattacharjee; Suvidha Mistry

title: The Obedient Wife
text: She was a docile and obedient wife, with not many expectations, shouldering the responsibilities of the household willingly keeping in mind the welfare of her husband and all his family members. She was quite pretty, kind and an agreeable wife. She was a little educated but she was a real lady. Her name was Allison Mora. She was married to a man who worked hard and earned and saved a lot of money. He was a real miser when it comes to money. He was quite rich but stin Allison had wanted to get a job before she got married but her mother had gone on and on about how important it was for a woman to get married so she could raise her babies early. Her mother had said she would find a job later. Besides, her husband was a rich business man. She wouldn’t have to suffer. Allison was married to a man who loved his money more than anything else. Life with such a kind of man is not easy, it’s like living your life on a budget. It can be very suffocating when you have to limit your every desire and wish as per his spending capacity. The only luxury you have is to dream because it costs nothing!... When they got married first, he told her that there was no need for a honeymoon and that it was better if they channeled the funds into acquiring assets as a new family. Next, he told her that he couldn’t continue to subscribe for the full bouquet of cable TV so they had no choice but to watch about six channels only, only three of which were actually worth watching. In the earlier days of their marriage, she had always made a fuss about his behaviour and had wondered how she ever ended up with such a man, but soon she learned to adjust.If she ever happened to overindulge or go beyond the budget, he would never let her forget that. She would become a legend who dared to overspend and her stingy husband never missed an opportunity to remind her about what she once did. When she seated herself for dinner opposite to her husband he would give her only a piece of bread no bigger than a hand, with a piece of cheese on it. There is a thin line between being careful about money and being stingy. While it’s always good to spend money wisely but being too thoughtful about parting ways with money can be a very painful experience. He never bought her jewelry or flowers or treated her to a fancy dinner but Allison was so adjusting that she never questioned or argued with him. She would do whatever her husband asked of her without any questioning. One day he told Allison, "When I die, I want you to put all the money in the casket along with me. I want to take my money to the afterlife with me. " And so he got his wife promise him, with all of her heart. The time came when he got sick, after some time the stingy old man died due to kidney failure….. He was stretched out in the casket, while Allison was sitting there, in a black dress, with her friend sitting next to her. When they finished the ceremony and the undertakers were about to close the casket, Allison stopped them and said, "Just a moment." She had a small metal box in her hands, she came over with the box and kept it in the casket, then the undertakers locked and rolled away the casket. Then her friend asked her, “what’s in that metal box?” She replied,”I remembered that he told me to put all the money in the casket along with him as he wanted to take his money to the afterlife with him.” Her friend freaked out and asked her,"Girl you are not that foolish to keep all the money into that casket, right?" The loyal wife replied "Listen, I am a wife, I can't go back on my word, I promised him." "You mean to say, you kept all the money in that casket?!?!" "I sure did," said the loyal wife, While Allison was having this conversation with her friend her brother heard all this and had a malicious idea. He came back to that place after 2 days, he dug that grave but for his astonishment he found an empty box, he got a little confused and scared, he believed that the dead body used up the money, he rushed to his sister and explained what he did. Allison was very angry and disappointed with her brother’s action, she berated him and shouted at him, but all his brother wanted to know was about the money. He asked her,” where did all the money go, where did you keep it?” "I got all the money together, put in my bank account and wrote him a cheque; I kept that in the casket along with him, now it's up to him to encash the cheque. If he can cash it, he can spend it."
author: Sanskriti  Kaushik
illustrator: Ashika Singh; Deepa Balsavar; Jacob Kono; Kavita Singh Kale; Sahitya Rani; Sonal Gupta Vaswani; Tanvi Bhat

title: A Dawn Of Life
text: Orphanage Varanasi Sonali was sitting in the corner of her bed. She was a 9-year-old orphan and was upset. Anvi, her friend in the orphanage. Those who were of the same age were best friends. They always slept together, walked together, and ate together. Their relation was like that of siblings. But that day was the worst day of Sonali. Her best friend was not with her anymore Anvi was adopted by a family. Though it was a happy moment for Anvi, at the same time Sonali was sad. She was all alone now. She had lost her sister. A month passed but she was sad. One day she saw a lonely girl in an orphanage as sad as Sonali. She went to the girl and asked her name. She introduced herself as Sindhu. They both became friends. Sonali had a new best friend. One day a young couple came to the orphanage and they saw Sonali there they decided to adopt Sonali. Sonali felt sad that now her friend will be lonely. She realized that Sindhu is also going with her. At the same time, she felt happy that she would also have a family. She went with Mr. and Mrs. Joshi. Both of them were doctors, and Mrs.Joshi was a Psychiatrist. Mr.Her Father Dharmendra Joshi Bought her new bags, books, toys, and everything else she needed. Her mother Kriti Joshi gave her the true love that she needed. Sindhu was there to accompany her. They played together and lived happily. But Dharmendra bought only one piece of the item. Sonali asked “Papa, Why you had bought only one piece what about Sindhu" Dharmendra asked Sonali “who is Sindhu Dear? I have only one child you,” “Where is she?” Sonali said, Papa are you joking she is here, beside me! But there was no one. She adds, looking from the first time we met she is wearing the same cloth, the same long braid. Dharmendra was shocked but he didn't react because his wife was a Psychiatrist, so he thought maybe she was imagining Sindhu. He said to Sonali, “Sonali, can you tell where you met Sindhu for the first time?” Sonali said, "Yes, papa we met in the orphanage and she came here with me.” Dharmendra later discussed this with Kriti. Kriti was upset but asked Dharmendra to act as if he could see Sindhu. Next Morning Kriti laid the breakfast for four people, ensuring that Sonali doesn't feel anything that problem she has. Kriti called Sonali for breakfast. Sonali came and said “Mumma shall I show you a drawing I made last night” Kriti now confirmed that there is no Sindhu. Her daughter was just imagining a girl. As she was a Psychiatrist so, she started talking to her about Sindhu. Kriti started giving her medicine and consulting with other doctors. A year later Sonali was now 11 years old. And had healed completely. Kriti decided to tell her about her imaginary sister. Kriti explained to her all the things she said when Sonali was 9. Sonali said, "Mumma how is it possible that anyone can imagine a person so well that she/he sleeps, talks, and does all things with that imaginary friend". Kriti said it happens when a person has no friends or if he/she is lonely. Sonali decided to become a child Psychiatrist in the future. Mr. and Mrs. Joshi, Sonali lived peacefully after. Sonali studied well. And was the topper of the class, in college. Further, She became a successful lady in life, not a Psychiatrist but she became a Scientist.
author: KHYATI MAURYA
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Debasmita Dasgupta; Kavya  Bagga; Madhuvanti Anantharajan; Priya Kuriyan; Sahitya Rani

title: The Butterfly Yet to Bloom
text: "You're beautiful" is what Eden, the butterfly heard from most animals while passing through his glade to which he always replied "No I'm not.”. Eden was a beautiful butterfly, his wings mostly jet black except for the unique tennis ball coloured spots.. He had big, deep blue pearl-like eyes which shone brightly in the sunlight. His antennae looked like a golf club, long and thin in the middle but ended in a thicker lump. Once, basking in the sunlight with his wings out-stretched Eden was contemplating about his parents, whom he hated because they were prone to abuse him at any small mistakes. They often called him a caterpillar, which felt very offensive because his caterpillar stage had been quite traumatic. His thoughts were abruptly interrupted by the very butterflies who he had been thinking about, informing him of some guests who had to come to their home later that day. Eden started sweating, or the equivalent of that for a butterfly. He did not like elder butterflies, and meeting them was a very daunting task for him. His day fluttered past him, and he did not realise when it was time for the guests to arrive. When he heard the guests’ wings approaching, he folded himself up involuntarily, which he assumed was a defence mechanism. His father, Sal, with his burgundy and black wings was the first to come into Eden’s room. The angry red winged butterfly called him out of his room. When he denied, his mother, Margarette, with her despicable chocolate and pansy coloured wings came into his room.. He was scared the most by his mother. She threatened to poke and jab his wings if he didn’t come out and greet the guests. With mounds of strain and anxiety he went out onto the flower where everyone ate and sat with his wings upright above his head. He was lost in his thoughts and didn’t realise when the guests had left. He was pulled out of his head when he realised his parents hovered above him, glaring at him with their bulbous eyes. “Why do you humiliate us like this, you caterpillar?” shrieked Margarette, enraged by his behaviour in front of the guests. “You’re a disgrace to all butterflies.” Her voice sounded soft, yet her words embedded with malicious intent. “You should’ve died as a larvae. Would’ve cost us less trouble.” Sal seethed. Eden’s parents had been doing this since he was a delayed flier and till date wasn’t an elegant one. He could never build up the confidence to fly properly as he was tired of being criticized at every step of his. The next day, the black and neon coloured butterfly headed out into the swamp flapping his wings clumsily, as one might see an aged butterfly doing. His movements seemed lethargic and out of sync. This was probably because he was exhausted and frustrated with his life. Slowly, he reached the marshy lands which looked like mounds of wet grass with streams of dirty water flowing between them. He was looking for Oswald, the frog who was commonly known among butterflies for his ferocity. Eden spotted the amphibian from far away.. Looking at him and his slimy pickle coloured skin glinting like, a pickle in the harsh sunlight really put things in perspective for young Eden. The giant frog’s eyes bulged out of his sockets like two bright yellow coloured bouncy balls with black spots in between them. These allowed him to see in all directions except behind, which is where the timid butterfly was approaching from. “Uh, hello”, Eden said in half buzzes, half whispers and half language. “I would like to die, please.” Oswald, considering not devouring the creature, turned around and got a look at the quavering butterfly. “As much as I would like to consume you,” the seemingly gigantic frog boomed, “I would first ask you why it is that you wish for death, young one.” Eden did not expect empathy from the deemed devourer. Quivering, he explained the best he could with his limited social skills to the frog the events of the previous evening and the emotional trauma he had been going through for the majority of his life. He did this with quite a lot of stutters and pauses in between so he could process what he was saying but Oswald was committed and did not lose patience. He was a good listener. While Eden spoke, Oswald was lost in a train of thought of his own. He remembered his young days, when he had been in a situation not dissimilar to what the socially anxious butterfly was in. He had visited a notorious serpent of the woods to get himself killed. The large emerald coloured serpent had been like a father to the young frog at the time. Oswald concluded that it was time he paid the favour back to the universe. Pulled back into reality by the sound of the butterfly crying, he comforted him as best he could. “Why aren’t you killing me?” Eden sobbed. “Death is not what you wish for, my dear. You wish for absolution” “Absolution how?” “I will try approaching those detestable parents of yours.” “No! Please don’t, I don’t know what they’ll do to me if they find out I came to you” “They won’t be able to hurt you in my presence.” And so the duo headed back to the most dreaded place on earth for Eden- his home. Looking at the huge slimy frog next to his small, butterfly sized home was surreal to him. He had never thought he would be bringing the ill-famed Oswald the Frog to his home. Eden’s house looked the same it had one evening ago. To any normal butterfly this house would look like a dream but to Eden it was a nightmare. He called for his parents at the doorstep. As Margarette and Sal must be proceeding towards the door, Oswald said in his booming voice “Let me deal with them.” As the door creaked open, a mouldy smell filled the air. Eden looked to Oswald and realised he had his mouth open, about to eat the two elder butterflies. Hundreds of thoughts flew in and out of Eden’s mind in a fraction of a second. He was conflicted- these butterflies had caused him pain for all his life. But, he did not wish death upon anyone. “NO!” he yelled and sped towards his parents. But, what was he afraid of that is what he had wished secretly so many times. “I never wanted you to kill them.” Eden said, confidently, for a change. The open mouthed frog’s eyes widened as much as they could in his bulged sockets. With a snap, the amphibian’s tongue rolled straight back into his skull. “They abused you, did they not?” the frog mused. “They did, but I’m better than that. I would never wish death upon anyone. Tia, a woodpecker overlooked the scene from an elevation on a tree. She had been a great admirer of Eden’s beauty always. She had always seen him get emotionally abused which made her frightened of the poor butterfly’s parents. This was the first time she had seen him with a supporter. She was rooting for Eden to finally overcome his parent’s tyranny. Lost in her thoughts, she faltered and pecked a beehive on instinct causing it to fall in the butterfly family’s house porch. The whole hive horded out behind the queen and overwhelmed the scene. All of Eden’s problems were invisible. All he could see were bees. Eden scanned the scene. He saw Oswald, all okay with what looked like a full stomach of bees. He had been stung a bit, sure, but despite that he looked okay. He placed Sal and Margarette, lying sprawled on the floor. They were hurt. They had hurt him all his life but he wouldn’t hurt them. In a swift movement Eden took off towards his injured parents and flew astutely evading all the bees. Eden scanned the scene. He saw Oswald, all okay with what looked like a full stomach of bees. He had been stung a bit, sure, but despite that he looked okay. He placed Sal and Margarette, lying sprawled on the floor. They were hurt. They had hurt him all his life but he wouldn’t hurt them. In a swift movement Eden took off towards his injured parents and flew astutely evading all the bees. He gathered his brown winged mother first and took her into their home and laid her on her bed. He did the same with his father. Their wings were hurt. He applied some sap to them and let nature take course. In a few hours, Sal started to stir. “Son, thank you” he croaked. “I’m prou-“ “Save it.” Eden cut his father off. Eden had all his things packed. He could see the regret in his parents’ pearly eyes. Perched with his wings upright, ready to fly, Eden uttered his last words to his parents, “I’m leaving to live on my own. I’m not a caterpillar anymore.”
author: Atharv Chauhan

title: Hungry Rabbit
text: One day, there was a rabbit. He was speaking to himself that:- "Always, everyday I eat raw carrots. ". Now he was tired of it. "What can I do to taste these for better and different?". On that afternoon she went to a farmer's house. Looking from a window, she saw a claypot boiling over the fire. After sometime she had an idea but the farmer's dog saw her and started barking after her. Then the rabbit thought deeply. "Ahh!! What should I do now?" Rabbit tried to leave the carrots in the hot sun. But the carrots remain same raw as before. Then she put them in fire. After sometime she tasted them. It tasted bitter!!! She thought thought and thought to think about what to do now. Then, finally after thinking long she had an idea!! Then, first she found an old tortoise shell. After that she collected some sticks with including three stones. Wow!!! Rabbit found the way to cook her carrots. Then, she was so much excited that she thought to invite her all friends. And atlast, they all enjoyed the meal and all the carrots. Name - Aarjav Naik, DPS Vadodara
author: Charmee Desai
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Chamath Prasanga Lokuliyana; Padmanabh; Sanatan Juanga; Tanaya Vyas

title: Growth
text: Sometimes I just want my kids to stay the same, and never grow from what they are now, not that I don't want them to grow up, I just want them to be my little infants, like how they were. Even if they grow old, I would still see them as newborns. Saying this I feel like it was just yesterday when I became a father, I have such striking memories of the good times, the best of the times. But time will never stay the same, the good times will pass, the new times will come, and so on, and as time has passed my children have grown up, grown up a lot. But sometimes I feel that this growth has stolen away my kids, stolen away the childhood from them. Growth is like the middle name of childhood. Even the oldest person alive was once a child, maybe a child with a snot nose. This growth is inevitable and may be a good thing. But does this growth mean that we have to become distant? I don't know why, but it feels like we have drifted slowly apart. It's as if we have become distant as time has passed. I got married almost twenty years ago and being from a hidebound family, I almost had no say in my marriage and neither did my wife. I was still working under someone who practiced law. I worked as a trainee when I got married, in those times not having a good job wasn’t a hindrance in one’s marriage, all that mattered were the characteristics of someone, whether external or internal. Eventually, we got married, and now I had a family to raise, become stable enough to support my newly built family became my goal. And I worked towards it. Two years later I completed my studies and i became an advocate in the very law firm i used to train and we moved away, it was a two-room apartment and I felt ashamed, ashamed of letting my kids grow into such closed spaces, what if they didn’t like it? What if they grew up feeling little of themselves, feeling little of me? But thankfully I was wrong, thankfully. I had thought it was a small house, as my family consisted of me, my wife, and my twins. “Just two rooms for four people?” this is what I used to think all the time. I was proved wrong as my kids grew up, actually, they never complained, we lived in that house for six years. When they were kids they used to play a lot, with me most of the time. There was one part of the house that even I liked and it was the balcony, and from there you get a clear view of the neighborhood park. On this side of the balcony, there was this sliding glass window, and through that, the sunlight made its way every day. My daughter hated the sunlight when she was little, she’d always shut her eyes tight. But as she grew she got used to it, back then she couldn’t open her eyes in the sun and now she could, she got used to it. I noticed this subtle growth and felt proud. But maybe I ignored the most visible form of growth Our interactions. As they grew older, our interactions became more formal, briefer, and more straightforward. As kids, they used to share everything with me, everything. And whenever they did, I got assured that they had trust in me. But as they grew there came secrets, things they thought couldn’t tell me. Now that I think of it, I hate it. Like what’s there in a friend that one can confide in but not with their own parents. I feel like me and my wife were so busy securing the future of our kids that we forgot to nourish their present, we played, travelled, enjoyed together, but never ever confronted our kids about this lack of correspondence. They say that you can relive your childhood through your kids and let me tell you, it is true, you relive your entire childhood through your children, and I could feel everything that they felt, or maybe most of it, the joy when having something good or when on a stroll, the excitement on festivals, even the pain they felt when they got hurt and yes, the crying part. There’s one thing that no parent can stand and that is the sight of their kid crying. When they cried I used to feel powerless and scared and wanted to do anything in my power that’d them stop from crying. It's just I was never good at it. When you reach your home, late from work you don't expect your kids to stay awake, but at our home, it's a common sight. The sight of my son doing his random things has become a habit, and that too to such an extent that now it doesn’t bother me as long as he wakes up early to catch his bus. Yesterday, knowing that I would be getting late I got some ice creams. I went up to him and said “Look I got you to ice crea-” He cut me by saying “I am studying, not now.” “Oh, you and studies.?” I scoffed and as I said this I prepared myself to face the wrath of my son but surprisingly he didn’t say a thing. “Come on just eat it and go,” I said, persuading him as if I were a trickster and as soon as he’d follow me to get his ice creams I would kidnap him. “No, I can’t,” he said. It felt as if I was talking to a calm monk or something and not my own son, not my childish son who’d get angry over anything. What an irony as a father. I was waiting for my son to get angry with me, and when he didn’t, it somewhat saddened me, maybe my kids have really grown up, “have they matured already?” I watched the tv wondering this, absent-mindedly eating my ice cream in a cup and then I passed out. I woke by a warm breeze on my face, a certain someone’s breath, it stank. It was my son sitting beside me, scooping out the melted ice cream I had in my hand. My kids still haven’t grown up.
author: Vibhu Tanay

title: The Lark and Her Chicks
text: In a large wheat field, lived Mamma Lark and her two pretty chicks. They lived happily in their nest in the field full of wheat. Early every morning, they thanked God for taking care of them and they praised Him by singing sweet songs. Mamma Lark would fly away to a distant place in search of white worms and red berries for herself and her chicks, while her chicks remained safe in their nest. Mamma Lark was aware that the wheat crop had turned yellow and was ready for harvesting. One day, she told her little chicks, "Soon we'll have to vacate our home and move to another field, because the crop is going to be harvested." "Now, my dears," she went on, "listen to what I tell you and watch out carefully. If you see the farmer with his men, pay attention to their conversation and let me know what they said." At noon one day, when Mamma Lark returned to her nest and chicks at noon, the chicks started, "Oh Mamma! The farmer and his son were here. And they've decided to reap the crop soon. The farmer has told his son to collect all the neighbours for harvesting and asked them to come tomorrow at daybreak." Mamma Lark told her chicks that there was nothing to be afraid of. The crop she said, would not be harvested the next day and so, they had their lunch comfortably and went about singing happily. The following day, the chicks were eagerly waiting to tell their mamma that the farmer and his son had come and that they went away sad. The neighbours did not heed their plea so they could not harvest the field. The farmer told his son to invite all their relatives, the following day early in the morning to help them with the reaping of the crop. Quite certain, Mamma Lark told her chicks, they need not be troubled as the crop would not be harvested the following day also. The next day, the chicks quite excitedly told their mamma, that the farmer and his son had come again but none of their relatives had turned up. They waited for a long time and then went away sadly. Finally, the farmer told his son that the following day at sunrise they themselves would start reaping the crop, without seeking help from other people. Then Mamma Lark said, "I knew for certain that the neighbours and relatives would not come to help them. This time the crop will surely be harvested because the farmer and his son have decided to start the work themselves. Let us be quick my dear. The time has now come for us to shift to an unknown place. God will provide a nest for us. We can trust in His help." With these words, Mamma Lark and her chicks flew to their new destination.
author: Shweta Sales

title: Never Lose Hope
text: NEVER LOSE HOPE (A motivational story by Nupur Bhardwaj) Spring arrived early this year. The soft rain when tickled Chinmoyee’s head, she sang even more gracefully. She chattered for hours with trees and squirrels whom she considered magical. She was nine anyway. But at a tender age of seven, she learnt to weave silk like her elder sister. It is an obvious thing for Sualkuchi settler located in the northern banks of the Brahmaputra river in Assam. Silk ran in her family’s blood and every Bathan villager. Her friends called her Chin or Chen. Everybody loved Chen except her neighbor Aditi, a young girl in her early twenties. She was a grumpy, prickly girl often who disliked Chen. Why, for once Chen secretly tasted the pickle prepared by Aditi’s mother and Aditi smacked and insulted her badly. It was the first and last time Chen spoke up rudely to an elder. But she turned little argumentative after this incident. One day, Chen’s father received a letter from his brother for some urgent work. The very next day, Chen’s father left to meet him for Singimari, a nearby village. It was merely a 20 minute walk from Sualkuchi. A whole day passed on. Chen’s father returned the next morning. He told everyone about the meeting. “Your uncle told me about a big textile company in Dispur. They are looking for fine quality, hand-woven silk. We can get a big order for that. We have two months to weave the silk and send it to a village called Ambari from where they will get it transported to Dispur.” – He said - “Ahh! That’s a longer route. It will take approximately 6 hours to reach Ambari.” - Chen said in excitement. Her father said with concern “We must start working as soon as possible.” From the next day, Chen, her sister and her father started collecting silkworms and made silk from it. Even though Chen was not experienced enough, still she worked hard round the clock with family. Two months eventually passed. The day before travelling to Ambari, they loaded the silk into carts and with the help of some villagers, they were able to pull the carts towards their destination. They started long awaited wishful journey with packed food and water along with them. Along the route they took some halts to rest and moved on. Finally!! they reached their destination Ambari. It was evening until then. Her uncle came to receive them and took them to a rest house. Everyone was tired so they slept early in the night. Next morning, they passed on Silk bundles to her uncle. Uncle promised her father that they will get a good amount of money once he receives payment from the textile company. After reaching back to home, Chen told everything about the journey to her mother. A few weeks passed on and there was no news from her uncle. Later, they got to know through a family friend that uncle left for Karnataka and settled there with family. This made them realize that uncle had fled away with their money by selling the silk. Chen's father put all his savings to prepare that silk and his brother cheated on him. Their hard work was wasted and there was no hope of getting the money back. This resulted in financial lose for their family. They had only food available in the house for few weeks. Aditi came to know about her condition. She felt very helpless and tried to find a way to help her family out. But nothing seemed to be helpful. Despite the altercation in the past; Aditi took the courage to speak with her although she knew that Chen might not accept her easily. However, after her persistent efforts, Chen started listening to her ideas to try new ways to earn more money for family. Aditi’s help and Chen’s efforts become helpful and in a matter of some time, their family situation was stable. It was the result of hard work and dedication showed by each and every member of the family and off-course, Aditi’s moral help! Chinmoyee's family did not lose hope and once again started their family business. Moreover, Chinmoyee and Aditi's bond grew stronger over the time, and everyone lived a happy life after then! - Moral of the story – “Hard work brings perfection to results. Losing hope destroys a man’s life and last but not the least, true friends never let you down.” THE END
author: Nupur Bhardwaj
illustrator: Selina Masego Morulane; Ajit Narayan; Cathy Feek; Debasmita Dasgupta; Priya Kuriyan; Raju Babu Shakya; Seat Sopheap; Tanvi Bhat

title: A Carriage Ride to the West.
text: Every morning he left for school only after touching her feet. “Bless me Dadi.” “Let the almighty give you all that you desire and more.” And off he ran away to the cold plains of Shimla. He knew these frosted plains like the back of his hand. Green grasslands flushed under the colossal mountain ranges. A valley formed around urban lands. Now, at present, it was covered with white crystal snow with the weather so cold it turned your ears pink. Cottages were constructed close to each other to preserve heat. A road crisscrossed through the snowy plains. Cars rushed onto the road. People saw a slight boy of seven walking to the nearest school four Kilometres away. He jumped onto the sidewalk and started skipping about. He stopped to admire the children skiing along the snowy flatlands. “Rich brats”,Satpal said “ They love showing off,” Lakhan replied. “Aren't we getting late?” “I guess.” And off they ran, reaching school just in the nick of time. Their school was a huge building distempered in turquoise. It did not have a proper roof which often caused the canopy to leak. After the morning assembly, they had mathematics. As they entered the class, the sky changed into a hoary black canvas. Their Maths teacher was a short, round man with very little neck. He had a mean face with wispy hair and was always seen with his trusted cane. He could quieten the class with his mere presence. “Did you all finish your homework?” he asked assertively. Homework? Oh no! Lakhan had completely forgotten about it. He had spent the whole day playing cricket with Satpal. Five strokes later he was asked to stand outside the class for the first two periods. There was a break after the first period. Students from all the classes came out to either use the washroom or to meet their friends. Ranbir, a fat-good-for-nothing boy of twelve years was having a very bad day. He had gotten detention from his English teacher for not finishing his homework assignment and so he decided to make someone's day horrible. He started looking for Lakhan who was an easy prey for his antics. “Oye Lakhan, getting punished already?” “Stop it, Ranbir bhaiya.” “You are just like your father, a complete loser.” Lakhan hated it when people talked about his father. He hadn't seen his father since his mother's death two years ago. Lakhan started crying. Seeing this, Ranbir ran away. He didn't want to get into any more trouble. As Lakhan stood sobbing, there was an announcement in the school. A monotonous voice was heard. “ Attention to all students and teachers. A huge storm is expected to hit within the next hour. You are asked to leave home. The same applies to the teachers.”Huge cheers were heard throughout the school. Lakhan was ecstatic. Shouts of “Free holiday” were heard throughout the campus, as teachers tried to contain the crowds of students justling towards the door. From the glass windows, Lakhan and Satpal were seen hopping about with no fear of the upcoming storm. The entire sky had turned stygian. There was a cold, pleasant breeze blowing about, trying to scatter the clouds. The friends were dancing and singing all the way that they almost missed a wounded rabbit lying on the road. Its eyes were watery and it had a deep cut along its forelegs. Blood was oozing out, dampening the snow around it. It almost camouflaged with the surrounding snow. “We have to save it Lakhan,”Satpal said “It won't survive” Looking defeated, the rabbit let out a final snort. Satpal bent down and touched the rabbit. It lay there lifeless.Tears came down Satpal’s eyes for he had lost his pet dog Toto, just three days back. Lakhan looked down expressionless. Teary-eyed Satpal dug out a hole, pushed the rabbit inside and covered it up with snow. Just then a tall man cycling came up to them. He had a pale face, blue eyes and a hooked nose, just like Satpal. “Namaste uncle,” Lakhan said “Namaste beta. What happened, Satpal? Come here.” Satpal ran towards his father and hugged him tightly. “What happened beta?” “ Uncle, when we came …..” As Lakhan narrated Satpals cries came down. “Don't cry beta. Just like Toto, the rabbit is taking a carriage ride to the west.” Hearing this Lakhan stood there stunned. His legs felt weak. He wanted to cry but the tears wouldn't flow. “Don't play outside Lakhan, the storm is approaching and convey my respects to Dadi.” Lakhan started running. He ran and ran and just didn't want to stop. Memories flashed before his eyes. A short man with a thin face and large eyes was shouting. “What have you given me? You gave everything to that wretched daughter of yours. She ran away with that cunning broker, disowning you. I need money to take care of him.”He pointed towards Lakhan. “Everybody calls me a loser. I feel ashamed to show my face in public. Savitri would have understood me. You know what, I don't want to live with you.” He pointed towards an old man with a skeleton face and a large broken nose, his Dada. “You can take care of Lakhan.” And off he walked away into the abyss. From the corner of his eye, Lakhan could see Dadi standing in the corner crying. He hadn't seen his papa since that day. The next morning there was a huge bang on the door. Satpal’s dad came rushing inside. He showed Dada the newspaper. As Dada was reading he collapsed in his chair. “Baba, have you taken everything,” Dadi asked “Yes, Dadi” “Don't stay up late. Remember to brush your teeth and don't trouble Mausi.” “Yes, Dadi.” Hot tears came out of Dadi’s eyes. “Come, say bye to Dada.” She took Lakhan inside the house. Dada was sleeping on a mattress. He appeared frail. His pillow looked wet. “Bye, Dada.” There was no reply. “He is asleep,” Dadi said. Mausi came inside. She was a fat woman with heavy make-up wearing a pink lehenga. “The taxi is waiting. I have to pay for it.” Dadi choked, “I am helpless. That is why I called you. Take care of Lakhan” “Nobody cared for me when I stood helpless. Anyway, take care of your husband. Send me a telegram when all of this is over ”, Mausi said bitterly. “Remember, we gave you everything we had,”Dadi lamented. “Really?" As Mausi replied with spitefulness, Lakhan found the newspaper near Dada’s mattress. He was about to open the newspaper when he found himself in the air. Mausi lifted Lakhan and carried him out of the house. As their taxi took a turn, Lakhan saw a police van speeding past them. The front cover of the newspaper lying near Dada’s mattress read-The body of a 34-year-old found near the banks of Giri. Police identify him as a resident of the Dahanu village. Lakhan came back home after spending two months with Mausi in Rajasthan. He had missed Dada and Dadi. He missed Dadi's stories. He missed Dada carrying him on his shoulders. He missed playing with Satpal. Mausi dropped him outside the house with his luggage and sped off in the taxi. Dada was a retired headmaster in the state government school. He always had his former students come and seek his blessings for future endeavours. But now, the house looked quiet and empty. Dadi came out running and hugged Lakhan. She carried him inside and asked him how his trip to Rajasthan had been. “Where is Dada?” Lakhan asked Dadi turned downcast. Her eyes turned wet. “Dada is taking a carriage ride to the west, ”Dadi stuttered. “When will he come back?” Lakhan asked innocently. “He won't come back. When you grow old, we will go there.” Dadi looked strange. She was not her usual self. It looked as though all the happiness on her face was drained. She was wearing a very simple sari and not her usual bright salwar kameez. “I don't want to go to Rajasthan ever again,” he said “I will never send you away ever again,” Dadi replied. Lakhan was now sprinting. It had been two years since that incident took place. All this made sense now. He wanted to talk to Dadi. Lakhan took a sharp turn and came to a stop. He had reached home. Dadi was in the backyard tending the gooseberry trees. He ran to her. “Baba go inside. I think there will be a downpour.” Lakhan just stood there, speechless. “What happened Baba?” Lakhan stared blankly. He felt something heavy in his throat. “Tell me, What happened? ” She couldn't bear seeing tears in her grandson’s eyes. “Dadi, where is papa?” Dadi’s face turned pale. “He is with Dada.” Lakhan’s vision turned blurry. His breathing became fast. He caught Dadi’s arm. “Don't leave me Dadi. Don't take a carriage ride to the west.” Dadi had tears in her eyes. She hugged Lakhan. Lakhan couldn't stop himself. He burst out. Lightning flashed, and thunder shook the Earth. It started pouring …..
author: adithya v

title: THE BEST FRIEND
text: THE BEST FRIEND Diya was a 4th grader. She was a brilliant student. She always used to be excellent in academics and other extracurricular activities. She always used to be teacher's favorite and this made her classmates jealous of her. They used to tease Diya in every way possible. She was worried about this. She realized that she had no friends who would help her or play with her. She always used to complain this to her parents. Her parent's advised that there was no point in being sad about it and that she would one day make a friend who would become her BFF(Best Friend Forever). Diya used to belive in those words and make herself cool Years Passed. The 4th grader Diya now became a 7th grader. She was still friendless. But now she was not sad about that. One Day, during her Physical Training period at her school, she was reading one of her favorite story book and did not play while others were playing. Diya was so engrossed in reading her story book that she was shocked to hear someone crying loudly behind her. She turned to see Neha, one of her classmates crying. Neha used to one of the people who used to tease and make fun of Diya for fun. Diya, seeing that Neha was crying loudly thought that she got a wound while playing. And indeed when Diya approached Neha, she saw a big wound on her knee. Though many people were standing around Neha, none of them came forward to help. Diya, who was now feeling pity for Neha exerted her maximum strength to lift Neha from the ground and helped her to the sick room. Diya looked after Neha till their class teacher came. Their teacher informed Neh'd parents and they took her to the hospital. A few days later Neha came to school fully cured. The first thing that Neha did was to apologise to Diya for teasing her a lot. She also thanked her for helping her even though the former used to tease the latter and said that she was indebted to Diya for helping her when not even her best friend came forward to do so. Diya was happy to hear it and forgave her. Diya now got a new best friend i.e. Neha. Diya and Neha continued to be best friends for their lifelong. Thus, Diya's parent's saying came true. From this story we can clearly understand that the saying 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' to be very true. -- THE END --
author: M VISHNUPRIYA  .
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Manasi Parikh

title: Types of Nouns in English
text: Noun: A noun is a word that represents a person, place, thing, or concept. Examples of Nouns: Person: Nalini Place: Delhi Thing: Bat Concept: Friendship Proper Noun: A proper noun is a specific name for a particular person, place, or thing. Proper nouns always start with a capital letter. Examples of Proper Noun: Kamal India Qutub Minar Tinkle Common Noun: A common noun is a noun that describes a type of person, thing, place or a concept. Common nouns don’t start with a capital letter. Examples of Common Noun: Father Church Box Cricket Abstract Noun: Abstract nouns refer to intangible ideas we cannot touch or see. Examples of Abstract Noun: Love Beauty Time Science Collective Noun: Collective noun is a count noun that denotes a collection of things or a group of individuals. Examples of Collective Noun: Collective noun for fish is school. Collective noun for ants is colony. Concrete Noun: Concrete Noun refers to physical objects in the real world and not to abstract concepts. Examples of Concrete Noun: Biscuit Butterfly Fridge Tree Uncountable nouns or Mass Nouns or Non-count nouns: Uncountable nouns are nouns that cannot be separated and counted. Examples of Uncountable Noun: News Rice Water Luck Progress Pronoun: A pronoun is a word or a group of words that one may substitute for a noun or a noun phrase that has been mentioned earlier. Examples of Pronoun: She It Myself Who That Compound Nouns: Compound nouns are made up of 2 or more nouns. Examples of Compound Noun: Tablecloth Son-in-law Swimming pool Washing Machine Possessive Noun: Possessive Nouns show ownership, and we use apostrophes to create them. Examples of Possessive Noun: Mom’s motorbike Kishore’s parrot Mala’s book Singular Noun: Singular nouns refer to one person, place, thing, or idea. Examples of Singular Noun: Cat Burger Ship Plural Nouns: Plural nouns name more than one person, place, thing, or idea. They end with the letter s. Examples of Plural Noun: Birds Rocks Heroes Activity 1: Match the nouns with the noun types mentioned. 1. Manisha 2. Lunchtime 3. Affection 4. Sister 5. His Common Noun Pronoun Proper Noun Abstract Noun Compound Noun Activity 1 Answers: 1. Manisha – Proper Noun 2. Lunchtime – Compound Noun 3. Affection – Abstract Noun 4. Sister – Common Noun 5. His – Pronoun Activity 2: Identify the nouns in the following sentences. 1. The bridge is clean. 2. He never listens. 3. Tinu cried. 4. The bedroom is big. 5. Beauty is skin deep. Activity 2 Answers: Identify the nouns in the following sentences.
author: Anitha Selvanathan
