title: THE MADDENING MYTH OF MAD MANUEL
text: He picked up the parcel that was lying on the floor. He was so ecstatic that he immediately opened the brown box. A SIM card, which is used in phones, was included in the package that was addressed to him. He excitedly put his SIM card into his phone and viewed a video from his uncle Manuel. “Uncle? Was this sent by him?” There was a video recording, and it started playing on its own. "Hello, Sam... This is a wonderful gift that I'm giving you. Hehehe...” Sam just froze right there and collapsed on the floor. When he awoke, he discovered himself imprisoned in a glass cage. He noticed a shadow and said- “Who is there?! Where am I?” “Hi dear Sam, you must know who I am. Don’t you...?” Sam's heart began to pound as the darkness approached him. Sam exclaimed out of astonishment as he noticed it was his uncle Manuel! “Hello Sam.” “AHH!! What do you want from me uncle? What is this nonsense? And why are you dressed up like a psychopath?” His uncle was not offended, instead he grinned. He patted his grey hair and remarked- “That is rude, but fair. MUAHAHAHA!!”. The classic demonic laugh echoed all around the white room. “So, Sam, how is your mom with her federal work?? Oops... I said too much.” Manuel smiled as Sam looked confused. “Agent work?” “Oh, you don’t know. Your mom is a secret agent who works for the government. Tell your mom it’s now my time to shine.” "Am I missing something? What was the purpose of that spooky video? And you're dreadful! Is it a joke? Is this a dream?" “No Sam.” He said, as he put his hands behind his back and walked over to the metal machine in front of Sam. “ You see this machine, Sam? It’s remarkable. It’s finally my turn. Let me explain. Many years ago, my sister-your mom now, and I lived in the same house where your mom was the favourite child because she excelled in everything she did while I was completely opposite. I was only good in Science. And so, I produced an experiment. When I saw how people would always be obsessed with their mobile phones and use them all the time, I decided that it was time for a change and this time, instead of humans having phones, phones would have humans. I used so many technologies and strategies to make it work and when I was so close to finishing my invention, your mother, along with the government ruined my plan completely!! We fought and one day, I had enough. I left the house.” “I’m sure you’re up to no good uncle.” said Sam. “Urgh. Like mother like son. Just know that from today, you will be working for me. And you’re powerless. YOU’RE MY LAB RAT SAM. MUAHAHA!!” Sam was frightened and started pounding on the door. Sam had always suspected his uncle to be a mad guy because that’s what he had heard. His mom and uncle had lost contact ever since Sam was born. Manuel simply wasn’t thinking and was now trying to make the universe his slaves, which was wrong… I’m sure you must feel lost, but things will make a whole lot of sense now. What will happen to Sam? Let’s find out…. When his uncle touched the large button on his control panel, he took out a tiny SIM that was identical to the one Sam had received in the mail. The glass compartment opened, and Sam fell out, on the floor. “You’ll not get away with this.” His uncle laughed and he held the SIM in front of Sam’s head and suddenly the whole room started shaking. Sam yelled in pain. Some light got sucked out of him, and SWOOSH!!! His eyes blackened as he raised his head. Manuel dropped the SIM and it stuck to Sam’s head like a magnet. “Hello Master.” said Sam. “What would you like me to do for you?” “HAHA MUAHAHAHA!!! It’s finally working. Now I have power! MUAHAHA!” "PSYCHOPATH! WHAT HAVE YOU DONE WITH MY SON?!?” The door opened abruptly. “Oh, Hello Linda! How have you been?” asked the mad Manuel. Sam's mother-Linda was standing at the entrance, her face red from rage. When she first saw her son, she realised something was wrong, “HOW COULD YOU?! HOW DARE YOU?!” Before she could say anything else, her brother ran towards her, and as he was about to put another SIM in his sister’s head, something happened. But hold on! I skipped an important part. Let’s go back in time- REWIND- Exactly when Manuel attached the SIM in Sam’s head, Sam switched the SIMs right before it fully took control of him. He switched the one Manuel attached, with the one inserted in his phone. He just took it out and put it in its place as soon as his mother entered and when Manuel wasn’t looking. Back to the present- As Manuel was about to put the SIM in her head, Sam ran in front of his mom and held his SIM in his hand, right before Manuel’s. BZZ!! Lightning zapped the SIMs and it appeared that they were destroying each other. “WHAT!?!? How did you...?” “I switched the SIMs when you attached it to me.” Sam exclaimed with delight. “PUT YOUR HANDS WHERE I CAN SEE THEM, PSYCHOPATH!!” 3 armed agents crashed into the room. Manuel raised his hands up and said to his sister angrily. "You always knew about my technology! One day, I will have what’s mine!" “You’ll finally learn your lesson now Manuel!” said his sister. “Sam! You have such courage, and I couldn’t be prouder! Well done son!” “Mom, why didn’t you tell me that you worked for the government?” “Some things are simply too painful to share Sam... However, let’s ignore that.” They hugged each other and walked back home while Manuel received the punishment he deserved- a long time in jail! Modern technology has engulfed us so much, that even the younger generation is addicted. But we should be aware of the purpose for which we use technology. Do we have Mobile Phones or do the Mobile Phones have us?
author: SIYONA ABBEY
illustrator: Alicia Souza; Hitesh Sonar; Jesse  Breytenbach; Joe Werna; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lara Berge; Marleen  Visser; Proiti Roy; Radhika Tipnis; Shreyas R Krishnan; SIYONA ABBEY; Wiehan de Jager

title: Liliac's Soul
text: "We'll get you in no time, dad" shouts the little girl swaying her bell sleeved bright yellow dress with white ribbons and polka dots while chasing her father down the beach. Her dog barked in agreement. Her dress seemed to complement the location. The bright yellow sun radiated joy while snow spray like waves tingled the mother's feet as she captured the moment in her camera but much more deeply in her heart. Snow sprays always freaked the girl out. She believed it was the devil's instrument to put her pretty hair on fire. Her parents had no idea where she picked the notion from. In the morning, she was horrified when she saw her mom put whipped cream or what she believed was snow spray on the cake which coaxed her to get out of bed. It was followed by a tantrum on styling her hair for the day. She was enraged at the fact that her tiny hairs couldn't be made into a bun like her mom. It took an ice cream at nine in the morning to make her agree on pigtails. Such frequent tantrums got her father into calling her Rupunzel. By Liliac This was what the city's most sought after model wrote in her journal while looking lovingly at a kid on the train. A glance out of the train window meant to see her grinning billboards which she avoided at all costs. Seven months ago the idea of her travelling by a train would be scoffed upon by her manager. Her fans called her the 'limelight' and her manager believed that her posters were enough to light up the life of the grey people on the grey platform boarding the cold grey train. But colder than the grey train was now the model's heart. But to her fans she was still the ever-young and charming Liliac Blackwell now Liliac Morgan who seemed to be concealed in a bubble of glamour, they failed to realise her concealed emotions. How could they for she knew how to mask her emotions behind her deep red smile,since,the day she attended the teen beauty pageant to fulfill her mother's dream but at the cost of burying her poems and feelings all together. Seven months ago, the pregnant model left the award function with three awards. The paparazzi was swooning over her bold black dress as she sat in her jet black car. Black for her had always signified confidence and elegance or what her mother said were 'model quirks' but black became the colour of misery and bleakness the moment she opened her eyes in the dark ward of the hospital. A doctor rushed to her bed and said, "You're out of danger, Mrs. Morgan but I'm sorry to info rm you lost the child. It was an early delivery and we couldn't save the baby." The words shattered her heart along with all her aspirations. Her dreams crushed again like her fourteenth year in this unfair life. She had always been a dreamer. Dreams can't be confined. Dreams rise in slums as well as in skyscrapers. For neither the sky nor land can limit dreams. Dreams are the language of the soul. Countless souls rise and die each day and so do dreams. There has never been a time without souls and so there will never be a time without dreams. The day little Liliac's dream of writing was buried; a new dream rose in her heart to be a mother; her mother could never be. Poor thing had to mature too soon and so she wanted to let her child live their childhood, to pursue what their heart yearns for and to never face the blinding lights of the stage which blinded them from seeing their true self. But life again was unfair to her. The fate was never in her favour. Couldn't the fate see her experience the touch of her little angel which would heal all the wounds she carried? She tried recalling what happened but all she could remember was the unbearable pain and her screams echoing in the car before she blacked out. Her husband, Noah was soon let in the ward, he tried his best to comfort her heart but she had no heart or soul to be comforted for it was snatched from her along with the baby. The miscarriage meant her heart, her self, Liliac being taken away from her. "A Princess doesn't cry" said her mom on the call. The sentence made her already overwhelmed heart overflow with emotions. She lashed out and said "Who said I am a Princess,mom? You never understood me, the crown of the beauty pageant never made me a princess. Why couldn't you see me happy sondering and pondering as I tried to play the notes of the 'Swan Lake' on my piano? Oh for my crown was made of the wit of Nancy Drew, music of Haydn and the ink of my fountain pen, I was the princess, the princess of my words, my imagination, my dreams, my soul." Few months after she again took over the town with her signature looks. She dreaded using cars. After an argument with her manager she was allowed to use trains on the condition of being disguised. She sat alone, cold and quiet at the end of the grey train compartment but her eyes set on the nosiest family, the one with a kid, the one which for her was fulfilled, the one which was her dream. Seven year old Lilac was fascinated when her older cousin told her about 'sondering' or realising that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as her. Since then every time she felt sad, she confided her feelings into stories, stories about people she sees, stories about strangers. Her journals were filled with heartwarming stories about families she saw on the train. The stories were warm but the hands crafting them were numb and frozen like the writer, Liliac who sat for hours at an end in the corner of the nursery she designed grieving for her baby; her heart. The sad and bleak winter came to an end.The spring brought with itself scent of motherhood and fulfillment for Liliac. She was pregnant again. But this time Liliac was scared, she didn't want the ruthless fate to steal her soul again. This forced her into gatekeeping her emotions but how could a mother not endear her child. She suppressed every urge to talk to the baby or think about them. She dug a grave in her heart and tried to bury all her feelings but afterall it was still a part of her heart and her feelings were engraved in the core of her heart. After months which seemed like eternity, the day came when all unspoken feelings could be said and all unfulfilled wishes could be fulfilled. But Liliac was in too much pain to rejoice. The turquoise scrubs, white lights and red blood filled the operation theatre. The doctors looked restless and whispered among themselves or Liliac's screams made their conversation sound like a whisper. Soon the screams subsided but the panic did not. Little Willow Morgan snatched the pen from her father, Noah Morgan. She made him run circles around the table where he sat writing the ending scene of the story of his late wife, Liliac Morgan. Noah stopped and pulls out another pen from his drawer. Willow was dumbfounded. "That's not fair. Everytime I take your stuff, we settle it with an ice cream and a drive." said Willow. "Same old tricks don't work everytime. Brainstorm another idea while I prepare breakfast." said Noah kissing the freckled skin of his daughter who held great resemblance to her mother. Her honey coloured eyes, black hair and dark skin reminded Noah of his wife. But if the appearance was ignored no one could tell she was Liliac's daughter. Being raised by her father and his friends, she had great interest in cars, sports and video games. She often said that she would make a career in gaming and football. Noah's reply would be "Sure sweetheart, you can be anything you want. Just make sure to hustle. Your mom's wishes and I will always be there to support and cheer you on." Everyday after putting Willow to bed, Noah would talk to Liliac or the stars about how Willow is on her way to become a strong woman just like her and he'll make Willow experience every story Liliac wrote in her journal. But on somedays he would break down and let his tears talk. He would think of how bravely Liliac chose her baby over her own life. She sacrificed herself to give him the gift of Willow. She chose a soulful death over a soul less life. Fate really was never in Liliac's favour.
author: Mrinalini  Singh

title: MAGICAL GARDEN
text: Priya, was a school going girl who lived with her mother in a small city. Priya was a helpful girl, a brilliant daughter and a smart student. She daily went to school with her mother. Her mother tried to give her everything she can, only one thing was missing, Priya’s father. He works in the US, so, he could never meet Priya for a long period of time. This made Priya sad. One day, when Priya was sitting in the classroom, his friend Aryan asked for her English notebook. Priya was kind so she gave her notebook to Aryan. While taking the notebook Aryan replied “ Thanks a lot Priya, you are my true friend.” Priya giggled and said “Oh come on by giving just a notebook I have became your true friend!” Yeah, no one gave me his/her notebook apart from you, Only you know how important this work is for me.” Replied Aryan. After a few minute Aryan thought to tell Priya about the gift brought by his father on his birthday. After telling this, Priya felt sad and told about his father to him. “Oh my god, you haven’t met your father for so long.” exclaimed Aryan. “Yes” replied Priya. Knowing this Aryan told Priya about the magical garden “Magical garden? Is this a joke.” said Priya. “Please, I am serious.” said Aryan. He told that who so ever wishes for anything in that garden, the wish comes true. But Priya did not believe in magic. Aryan advised her to visit the garden.. When the school got over. Priya was waiting for her mother infront of the school gate but she saw her neighbour, Miss Sen. Miss Sen told Priya that her mother is not well. “What! I need to go home” exclaimed Priya. Hours passed but the condition of Priya’s mother doesn’t improve. Priya was so sad, she only have her mother. And suddenly she remember about the magical garden. She don’t believe on magic but she had an hope. At this time she was missing her father the most. So Priya asked Miss Sen “ Miss Sen please stay with my mom I am just coming back” Miss Sen replied “ Yes sure ”. Priya run to the garden, she was sad but she had an hope. When she reached the garden. She was not able to control herself and started crying. She said “ Please magical garden if you have a pinch of magic also please return me my healthy mom, I can’t live without her. Please I request you.” She thought to go back but then a thought came in her mind that she would also wish to get her father also back. After a few minute she thoughts again that there is no magic in the world! She muttered herself “What am I doing, I don’t believe on this, I have to go back home.” At the way to home, she was passing the road, but suddenly someone pushed her beside the road. When she opened her eyes she saw her father, she was not able to believe on her eyes. Then she came to know that the person who pushed her was her father, he did it to save Priya as a truck was coming and Priya didn’t see it. As Priya’s father came from US to meet Priya. After this Priya and his father took Priya’s mother to a good doctor. Soon her mother get well. AND THEN THEY LIVED A HAPPY LIFE. –MEDHAVI SHARMA • --MEDHAVI SHARMA THANK YOU --MEDHAVI SHARMA (GRADE 7)
author: Medhavi Sharma

title: The Best Friends Forever
text: It was the only luxurious hotel in that town. Four friends after the SSLC exam decided to go to that hotel and have tea and breakfast. The four of them deposited a total 80 rupees. It was a Sunday. At ten thirty they reached the hotel on a bicycle now Binesh, Santosh, Mahesh and Akhil started talking while having tea and breakfast. They started talking about how after 35 years they will touch 50? Then they talked about their moustache, their hair, their clothes and the way they would walk and laughed loudly. The sound of their laughter made the place melodious. It was April 1. All four decided that they would meet on April 1 after 35 years in the same hotel. Till then they decided that they would all have to work hard. "It would be interesting to see how much progress is made in ourselves", said Akhil. The waiter, who was listening to all this gave them tea and breakfast. He Said" If I stay in the same hotel for 35 years. I will definitely wait for you in this hotel" and handed them a bill of 75 Rupees. The waiter's eyes were impressed with the scene of them flying away on a bicycle after telling him to keep remaining 5 rupees as tip. The four of them, separated for higher studies. Binesh had left the town due to his father's transfer. Santosh went to his uncle for higher Studies, Mahesh and Akhil got admission in different colleges of the city. Finally Mahesh also left the city. The days moved on, Months rolled by. Many years passed. It seems in thirty five years there has been a rush of changes in that city. The Population of the City increased and the roads widened. Flyover proliferated. The industries near the city gave the air a metallic smell. Big buildings changed the look of the city. The hotel now was not any ordinary hotel. It was transformed into a five star hotel; the waiter now became the boss and the owner of the hotel. After 35 years, April 1 afternoon, a luxury car arrived at door of the hotel. Binesh got out of the car. He was very happy that he was the first of the four and didn't have to pay the bill. Santosh came up a bit later, He became a big builder. He looked like a senior citizen with age. Now both of them were waiting for Mahesh and Akhil. Mahesh came a bit later. The eyes of three friends were repeatedly going to the door ‘When will Akhil come?' they thought. At the same the hotel owner said; “I have received a message from Akhil Sir. He will be a little late". All three were happy to meet other after 35 years. Praising, despising, boasting and mocking made the pleasant place more pleasant again. Akhil did not come. After several hours Akhil's message came again. He said that he will come to settle the bill after the meal. A sorrowful message was also shared along with them to wait till 8:00 pm. A handsome young came out from the car and went to the three friends. The young man's smile brought back Akhil's memory, I am your friend's son Ravi, my father is Akhil the young man started saying. My father told me about your visit today. He waited every year for this day. But he died due to a lung disease caused by industrial pollution and the lack of clean air 3 months ago. At his deathbed my father requested me to meet you all today. He also made me promise that I would only meet you at the end of the day so that you all could be happy for sometime. The three friends now were Sad. They knew that they had to do something for his friend.out of all three of the Akhil was a brilliant student. They also knew that Akhil would stop at nothing to save nature. The scene of Akhil once hugging a tree near the hotel so as to stop it from being cut flash-backed in their mind. The hotel owner tried to consolidate them as he knew about Akhil's death. The three friends and the hotel owner were determined to honor Akhil's memory by saving nature. they were determined to plant one tree everyday and also created an arboretum in his memory The friends now decided that they will meet every week as they wouldn't know when someone's turn might come.
author: Bejieish P
illustrator: Annada Menon; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Maithili  Joshi; Niloufer Wadia; Prabha  Mallya; Rai; Sadhna Prasad; Sahitya Rani; Shivam Choudhary

title: INSPIRATION INSPIARING AN INSPIARER
text: CHARACTERS: Grandmama Evangeline Iris Grandmama's father 27.03.2050,grandmama was narrating a story to her grandchildren and was providing them information about the earlier generation. She began by narrating that, 'the lifestyle of our generation have no similarities with that of the old generation '. there were no robots, the technology wasn't as highly improved as of now'. Evangeline and Iris were listening to the tales of grandmama. Grandmama was never as old as of her age.She was always in her 'forever young' era with her extremely good looking and adept characteristics. While others followed the very modern means to grow,grandmama always preserved the old culture and raised up her grandchildren by the previous means of culture. Evangeline meant "good news", she was a six year old girl with a undistinguishable look. Her red cheek flaunted with her dazzling smile. Her eyes contained the ability to make anyone fall for her beauty. Meanwhile Iris meaning "rainbow" was a ten year old with her thin, five- foot- tall body. Her eyes were wide apart, her brown skin and black eyes made her more charming. Her affinity for bright colors resulted into making her the most colorful child among the whole family. Both of the girls were interested to know more about the old days. "Todays tele books were replaced by printed paper books " informed grandmama. The books had original paper, where words were printed, the pages were turned out and the books were read at any time. The pages of the books were either white colored or sometimes even colorful. The books consisted of information about many historic events, many heroic characters and what not. Evangeline asked her granny if she could tell her about the heroic characters that the old books held. Grandmama's reply was in affirmative. That night, both the children knew about the stories of "Evelyn Glennie." Grandmama told them about the hurdles that they had to face to become an inspiration to many. The children seemed to have great enthusiasm in what grandmama said. Grandmama gave an extreme brief description of the heroic characters. She began by narrating the life story of Evelyn Glennie. "Dame Evelyn Elizabeth Ann Glennie, was a Scottish percussionist. Born on 19 July 1965, she was a normal child just like others. At the age of eleven, she was confirmed to be deaf. But Glennie never thought of quitting. By meeting a girl playing a xylophone, Glennie once had a wish to play that too but she knew she couldn't as she won't even be able to hear anything. On the other hand her grades were deteriorating. There was even a lack of support from her friends and her teachers. Glennie even said by herself that suddenly everything went black. By fortune, Ron Forbes - a percussionist spotted her potential. Forbes even encouraged her and suggested her by saying that,' Don't listen through your ears, try to sense music through the other part of your body'. Evelyn followed his suggestion and there was a turmoil in her life. She could even feel music through every part of her body. Later, she marked her name in the top list of musician. She was the one to score one of the highest marks in the history of academics. She was also selected as one of the two laureates for the Polar Music Prize of 2015. Despite being deaf, she managed to learn music even that in a better way than others. Her deafness was never her weakness instead it was her strength. Evelyn was world famous and was an inspiration to thousands " narrated Grandmama. ''what was her road to success?" asked the children. " It was her hard work and determination " replied Grandmama The children were delighted and motivated by hearing the life story of Evelyn. "I have heard this story from my father, he read it when he was probably in his 9th or 10th class" added Grandmama. "This is the best story that you have ever narrated, granny" said Evangeline. Grandmama put the children to sleep. It was 14th birthday of Iris, she had grown up as a teenager. Life was the to all- with both hurdle and ease. Even Iris had to go through a lot of sufferings at her teen ages as everyone else did. Though the habit of listening to Grandmama's stories every night had not change. Later, it was found out that Iris was gradually losing her ability to see. At the age of 15, Iris was completely blind. She was even on a verge to give up. Evangeline, though being younger than Iris remembered the tale that Grandmama had once made them listen - it was the story of Evelyn Glennie. Evangeline said, "Dearest Iris, remember the tale of the life story of Evelyn that Grandmama once narrated? Even she had to go through a lot but did she give up? No, right! If she can achieve her goal despite of being deaf, why can't you? If you put the equal amount of hard work and determination, even you can overcome your weakness." Evangeline's words touched the heart of Iris. She realized that even she can if Evelyn had. From that day onwards, Iris never looked back. She was focused into her aims and later even she could face the hurdles. Iris could learn and feel things without even watching them. For her success she was always thankful and grateful to her granny and her little sister- Evangeline. THE END. THANK YOU FOR READING.
author: Bidisha  Nag

title: The Mighty Adventures of Best Friends R&M
text: The bell rang, ending the last of the classes for the day. Students filed out in groups: chatting, laughing and making plans for the weekend. Rachel, walked to the first floor library to start her homework project. She was determined to finish her first project at St Thomas as soon as possible and make a good impression on the class. She had already looked through the main library but without success so she decided to look through the other library. You never know where you might find inspiration. She moved to the first shelf of the library, where she came across a blonde girl going through the racks. “Hi! My name’s Melody Walters. What’s yours?” asked the girl turning towards her with a smile. “My name’s Rachel Callidus. I’m a new student here.” Rachel quickly registered the girl’s copper curls, eyes which were the softest hazel and her warm smile which brightened up the room. Setting her bag down on a chair, Rachel turned her attention to the books. “Adventure stories….Adventure…” she muttered under her breath. She wanted to inspiration for her homework project: writing an adventure story. Her eyes fell on a particular spine with no name. No wait, there was a name.. Strange, surely this book didn’t have a name a minute ago. She picked it up. The Mighty Adventures of best friends R&M. How convenient! It was exactly what she was looking for. She took the book and decided to leave a note for the librarian at the front desk. She picked her bag and walked to the front door. It was locked. Strange, The library door is never locked. Maybe it was just stuck. She didn’t believe so, but there was no other plausible explanation. She pushed at the door with all her might. It remained shut. Just as she was trying to understand the strange happenings, her eyes fell on the book of adventure stories. On a impulse, she picked it up and opened the book but the pages were all blank. Puzzled she went back inside and found Melody on the floor, holding her head. Rachel left the book down on the table and went over to her. “What is going…?” “Calm down.” Rachel interrupted her. First tell me what happened with you. “Nothing much. I…was looking for a book on adventure stories… when something hit me on the head.” Suddenly a soft breeze passed by gently turning the pages of the book and words appeared on the pages as if they had been born from the breeze itself. My dears, if you wish to be freed In answering my riddles you must succeed If you fail, you shall stay here forever, guaranteed Fear gripped their heart but they had no choice. The girls exchanged a look. The fact that they were not alone gave both of them some courage. Then, two voices spoke out in unison, “We accept.” Another page turned. New words broke out on the pages. Has a mouth but cannot talk Can run but cannot walk Has no money but has banks Does all jobs without any thanks “It has a mouth…and banks…can run…thankless job.” Melody thought for a minute. “I know, it’s a river! “Nice work Mel!” Rachel said enthusiastically. A gust of wind turned the page and a new riddle rippled out. I can be very calm, I can be rough However, without me all season would be tough “Wind” said Rachel confidently. “It can be a breeze and a storm. During summer, monsoon and winter months wind helps to distribute heat and rainwater equally throughout the earth.” “Great job, Rachel!” Mel said giving Rachel her sweetest smile. A final puff of wind turned the last page revealing the last riddle. I can surf without the sea all day I can help you with your homework or with an essay And if you’re bored I have games to play The friends paused. This one was hard. After a few minutes, they said the answer together “The Internet!” They held their breath waiting for the final gust of wind. The strongest gust of wind which felt the most refreshing to them flew past and closed the book. In the distance, they could hear the door opening. Finally, they were free! Rachel walked towards the table and picked up the book. The Mighty Adventures of best friends R&M. She opened the book and was surprised to find a story in the book. She flipped through it and stopped at a portrait of the two main characters, R&M. It was a portrait of them! “Mel, look! It’s…us.” Melody glanced at the book, surprised. “R&M must stand for us…Rachel and Melody!” The girls carefully put the book back in the shelf and walked out of the library, glad to be friends, glad to free and glad to have a topic for their adventure story.
author: Charu Gupta

title: Hero with No Cape
text: Jagdish was feeling faint on the hot summer afternoon. The blazing sun and the hot blowing wind were making it worse for him to stand there. His feet were burning on a Coal tar road. There was no tree to offer him any shade. He looked around and all he could see were a few houses and shops here and there. Jagdish was on his way home after buying some medicine for his wife. It had been three days since Seema, his wife was of Suffering from fever, with the packet of medicine hanging in one of his hands and in the other he was holding the piece of tire, flung on his back. Those were the cheapest source of firewood for him. This piece of rubber tire caught fire easily and saved a few pennies of firewood for him. But the smoke and its smell were terrible. In this New Sinduri Village, life was difficult; as he had to pay for everything - Medicines vegetables, firewood, and even the fodder for the animals, everything Cost money. Thinking of all these Jagdish walked inside his tin shade, which had become like a hot oven. He looked at his ill wife sleeping on the bed with her back turned towards him. His daughter Jhlimil sat in the other corner, rocking her baby brother, trying her best to put him to sleep. Jagdish always missed his parents. "If only they were here." He often wished. His decision of shifting to this Sinduri Village had saddened them and died before he left his old khedi Village. There were hardly eight to ten families who he could call his own, as they were the ones who had accompanied him from Khedi Village. The entire village was forced to leave their land, house and all their be longings after the massive flood a few years ago. The government had allotted Some piece of land for each family as a compensation and what they got in their share was never enough for their families. Life here was difficult. Not what Jagdish had imagined. There was electricity but only for six to eight hours a day. And the bill was always rocketing high. The tin shade over his head was for a single room. The land he was allotted was barren and filled with stones and pebbles. To sow a life on it was next to impossible. Jagdish and his family did try but they could not grow anything on it. But they never gave up hope. Jagdish and the people who walked away from their village struggled to survive, the only thing that kept them going was their hope." One day, we will be able to get everything we need" this was what that helped them work hard: every single day. With a smile Jagdish entered his house, placing the packet of medicines next to his wife’s pillow, ruffled his daughter's hair, pulled out an orange toffee from his pocket, and extended towards to his tired-looking Jhilmil. It always amused him how that one 50-paise toffee lit up the little girl's face with a million-dollar smile. For the little soul, her Hero never failed to Cheer her up.
author: Chetna Thakur
illustrator: Nicolene  Louw; Ana RoGu; Deepa Balsavar; Iddi  Marumba; Lavanya Karthik; Priya Kuriyan; Ruchi Shah; Shadrach Munene; Vusi  Malindi

title: The Vain Peahen
text: Long, long ago, all peacocks and peahens were very beautiful. They were truly the pride of the jungle. They mesmerised everyone by their beauty. Whenever the rain came, they would spread out wide their colourful tails and dance elegantly. One day, Queen Peahen looked at her image in the water and thought, “Wow! I really am beautiful! No other animal is as beautiful as I am. My tail is so attractive and colorful. Everyone is captivated by my looks and my dancing. I am special and should be treated that way. All other animals deserve to be slaves of our tribe. They must follow my orders and do whatever I say.” The next morning, she shared her idea with all the other peacocks and peahens. The peahens agreed with her and thought it was a great idea. The peacocks, however, were sensible and opposed her folly. They disagreed and said, “Oh! How vain and senseless! We are loved and admired by everyone in the jungle. Every animal is special in its own way. If we act haughtily, we might lose their respect for us." Sadly, the peahens did not listen to the peacocks. From that day, the peahens completely changed their attitude toward other animals. They started bullying and teasing the smaller animals. They would move around in a group and would give orders to anyone who happened to come in their way. They troubled those who disobeyed by playing mean tricks on them. One day, the animals thought they had had enough! The Eagle went straight up to the king of the jungle- The Mighty Lion- and told the whole story to him. He sighed and said, “Dear Eagle, I am getting old and feeble. I am not sure if the peahens will listen to me. But I can tell you this- on the next full moon night, if all the animals pray together, the Guardian Angel of this jungle might appear and do something about this.” The Eagle thanked him and flew back. She conveyed to all the animals, except the peahens, about what the Lion had said. The animals waited eagerly for the next full moon night. It was half past seven. The full moon shone brightly in the sky. All the animals prayed for the Guardian Angel to appear. Sure enough, a few minutes later, a small angel appeared. She had a kind look but her eyes were serious. The animals told her what had happened and then the Eagle spoke up, “Dear Angel, please do something so that the peahens stop bothering us.” No sooner had the Eagle finished speaking than there was a flash of thunder and the Angel disappeared. It started raining heavily and everyone ran for shelter. Meanwhile -unaware of all this- the peacocks, who loved rain, spread out their beautiful tails and started dancing. The peahens, eager to show off their beauty and talent, came out to join them too. But much to their surprise, they could not spread out their tails which were now dull and ugly! They understood that God had punished them for their bad behaviour. They even lost their will to dance as they had no beautiful tails to show off now. The peahens regretted it but nothing could be done. From then on, only the peacocks have beautiful tails and they dance whenever it rains- but not the peahens!
author: Ratnakshi Prasad

title: lucid dreams
text: The dreams started when she was seven. At first Nora was not really sure about what they were or how it happened. as when she slept she could feel herself slipping into another dimension; a parallel universe. That day she cried to her mother but the more it happened the more she got used to it and at one point she went as far as to enjoy it. I'll be brief about the ordeal. Here is what happened / happens every time she starts to drift. In the dream she sees herself with crooked front teeth and brunette hair. The next thing she knows she is falling into another when she wakes up and she sometimes sees a friend, sometimes her sister, sometimes an unfamiliar face. it was not a coincidence Nora realized as the people she saw in her dreams told her how she appeared into theirs too. It took a very long time to accept the fact that she, Nora seed, was a dream walker. She could waltz into anybody’s dream whether she liked it or not. she soon got used to her abilities and started to control whos dream she wanted to go into Quantum mechanics talk about multiverses but not much about (for the lack of better terms) dream walking Nora read books watched movies did her fair share of research but it went to vain as she could not quite find anything that accurately describe their abilities Dream walking had its benefits as much as it had disadvantages. For example, she could make the lives of the people whom she hated miserable. the con is that they got suspicious when she started to occur in their dreams too often In the start of spring, Nora was by herself at the park sitting on a bench and reading a book when she first met Alexis. Alexis was looking for a place to sit when Nora shifted and offered a seat for her to sit. It was quiet at first and while Alexis was looking at her phone Nora was looking at her. She had something of a bruise near her cheek bone but she was pretty nonetheless. Nora figured that the best thing to do was to start a conversation. After a while of them exchanging words Nora found herself connecting with the other quite easily. Their conversation flowed smoothly and they had similar interests. Nora decided then that she really really liked Alexis at that moment– she thought about what it would be like to waltz into her dream and make the moment last longer. That night, Nora went to sleep with a determination like never before and leaped into alexis’ dream. It was oddly dark and different from what she used to, when she realised that this wasn't a dream, but a nightmare. After the smoke cleared out, she spotted Alexis sitting on the same park bench and sobbing her eyes out. At that moment she felt like an intruder. That was when she realised that she is an intruder. She hogged up people’s comfort places and sometimes made it hell. People, despite everything, deserved some quiet time away from everyone. At that moment though, it looked as though Alexis could use a friend to rely on. So Nora ended up staying a little longer, holding Alexis as she cried and swore to herself that she would never be this person again. and wouldn't cross universes to be where she didn't belong. That night, she slowly faded back to reality with a heaviness in her chest. The next following week, Alexis had been waiting at the same park just as nora had expected. That moment she realized that she was very much obligated to come clean if she ever wanted to be something with Alexis. After going over the whole crisis, Nora expected Alexis to laugh at her or call her insane but instead, she gave her a lopsided grin and intertwined their fingers together. This whole affair had been a curse, as much of a blessing it was. The trick, which Nora hopes to learn, is to get a grip. Everything in the end comes down to this, Nora thinks as she walks around the park with Alexis. And if she is lucky, the end of this sentence is where she might begin. This time though, with the help of a new companion.
author: Manya vivek

title: The Yeti
text: It was a chilly day at Mount Everest, in January. Some might even say the chilliest anyone had felt in years. Nonetheless, five brave explorers decided to try and start to scale this magnificent peak on the coldest day experienced by any local. Rahul, Gopal, Mala, Sita and Ravi decided that with light backpacks and two lamas, they could reach the top of Mount Everest. All of them were bold, courageous and wanted to experience thrill. For a few days, they trekked to the peak of Mt Everest, passing trees and shrubs as they went along. They camped in a large tent every night, and ate canned food for every meal. Soon they neared the snowy and icy parts. The view along the way was beautiful, but compared to now, it was nothing. As they approached, the strong winds blowing down seemed to warn them to not climb, but they slowly and steadily climbed. Soon they reached a small cave in the mountain side. All of them decided to rest and call it a day. As Rahul lit a campfire with a few twigs which were cut from a pine tree, Mala spread five extremely fat sleeping bags on the cold hard stone floor of the cave. Gopal was walking around the cave looking at all the walls of the cave. “Hey guys, I think that we shouldn’t be here.” he called out nervously. The others walked up, their curiosity at bursting point. Gopal pointed to some paintings and text on the bare stone walls. It was made with what looked like fruit juice. The text read ‘ BEWARE THE YETI ’, ‘ GO IF YOU VALUE YOUR LIVES ’ and ‘ THE YETI DOES NOT SPARE THE BRAVE NOR THE COWARDLY ’. The pictures depicted a white bearish animal which was three times the height of any man, feasting on what looked like human limbs! No one was prepared for this. It was night, and it was colder than ever. “I don’t know where we will find the next shelter, and the wind won’t ever die down at night. I think we should stay here. If the ‘Yeti’ finds us, if it even exists, we all agree that we all we go down together. Right?” Rahul asked. “If we stay there is a chance that we might survive, but outside, chances are less than zero. I agree with Rahul” Sita declared. The others nodded, all rather scared. They all got into their sleeping bags and everyone snuggled closer to conserve body heat. When everyone woke up in the morning, to their horror, Mala was missing! They got up and looked around to see if she was anywhere in the cave; she was not there. “Hey, there is a “Hey, there is a rather large opening here. Do we go in?” Rahul asked nervously. “I guess so...” Ravi responded. They went in rather scared. It was a long passage, sloping upwards sharply. As they scrambled along, they noticed that it was not getting any colder and the oxygen levels were not dropping. They soon reached a narrower passage sloping downwards sharply. After some time they reached a half broken wooden door. As they approached, they heard some voices behind the door! “Shush” Sita said quietly, as he stepped closer to the door. She peeked inside and gasped. “G... guys, the Yeti!” rather large opening here. Do we go in?” Rahul asked nervously. “I guess so...” Ravi responded. They went in rather scared. It was a long passage, sloping upwards sharply. As they scrambled along, they noticed that it was not getting any colder and the oxygen levels were not dropping. They soon reached a narrower passage sloping downwards sharply. After some time they reached a half broken wooden door. As they approached, they heard some voices behind the door! “Shush” Sita said quietly, as she stepped closer to the door. She peeked inside and gasped. “G... guys, the Yeti!” she whispered! Everyone inched closer to see. Everyone was pale. Everyone gasped, the ‘Yeti’ was just about a foot taller then an average person. But what is more, it was smiling and talking English to Mala! They opened the door and stepped inside. “Hello there, I suppose you all are Mala’s friends! Do come in!” the Yeti called out in a jolly, British accent. Shocked they all stepped further inside. “My name is Small Foot, if you were wondering.” He spoke. “Do have some hot cocoa, it is quite good. Have a seat by the way.” He continued, gesturing at some colourful woolen mats. A bit confused and befuddled, they all sat on mats. “Small Foot was just about to tell me how he came here.” Mala said cheerfully. “Now I will tell my tale. You see, I am from Britain, but when I was young, there was an attack on my home from another tribe of yetis. I was scared, so I ran away. I hid on a ship that brought me to Mumbai. Small Foot walked with them to the cave outside the passage. “Bye Small Foot, we will never forget you!” Mala said. “Yeah, bye.” Said Rahul. Small Foot waved and disappeared into the passage Somehow, I managed to get to the Himalayas unseen. Snow and mountains are my natural habitat, so I could not go anywhere else. And here we are now.” said Small Foot. “Whoa, is all that true?” asked Ravi. “All true.” “What about the warnings outside the passage? Who wrote those?” Gopal asked curiously. “I painted that myself. I am a bit shy, and I don’t like many people here. Because of the warning, most people go away. The few that come are a kind of nice surprise.” Small Foot responded. “Now you must keep this encounter secret, and also you must leave now, okey?” “Alright” said everyone. nice surprise.” Small Foot responded. “Now you must keep this encounter secret, and also you must leave now, okey?” “Alright” said everyone. Small Foot walked with them to the cave outside the passage. “Bye Small Foot, we will never forget you!” Mala said. “Yeah, bye.” Said Rahul. Small Foot waved and disappeared into the passage. They all packed the thing that they had left in the cave and loaded them onto the lamas. Five Weeks Later – “Hello, here we are with breaking news, truly breaking this time!” hollered a news reporter into a mic. “We are in the northern most part of Ladakh waiting for a group of five hikers to arrive from their successful journey to Mt Everest’s peak in the middle of Winter! Very few have returned successful from this famous peak, but this group did it! The hikers in this group are Mala, Sita, Rahul, Gopal and Ravi. And here they come now!” a large jeep with the hikers inside pulled up beside the news reporter. After everyone got out of the jeep, the news reporter interrogated them for nearly an hour. Dozens more interviews awaited as the little group of hikers rattled away in their jeep.
author: Prajna Kiran  Rajarathna

title: ALOO POORI OF LIFE
text: ALOO POORI OF LIFE In the holy town of Haridwar, there lived a girl named Seema. She was different from other children. She always wanted to be the best in each and every field, whether it is studies or extra- curricular activities. She was not very good at managing her time and she would always get irritated very quickly. She always used to compare her life with her classmates and other children. Slowly and gradually, she developed a belief that everything bad happens to her and no one loves her. One day, Seema came to her mother and started crying. Her mother asked her why she was crying. She told her mother that she had burnt her favourite dress while ironing. She continued sobbing and told her mother that she had failed in the examination too and no one talk to her in her class. She said that she has no friends in school. She complained to her mother aggressively that she has so many problems in her life and no one loves her. Her mother smiled and said "Quit this sadness and stop crying, let's make your favourite aloo poori". Seema looked at her mother and was confused that instead of consoling her, her mother was asking her to join her in cooking. Then she joined her mother and said with a smile, "aloo poori is my favourite dish. How long will it take to cook?” Her mother thought of teaching her life lesson through aloo poori recipe. She asked Seema to pick the flour box and asked her to eat it. Seema said while making her face, “who eats maida”. Her mother smiled at her and said "If you do not want to eat ‘maida’, it is fine then you eat two spoonful salt, two red chillies and some baking soda too” Seema was shocked at her mother’s behaviour and got irritated. She said to her mother angrily, “Mother! Don’t you love me as you are asking me to eat maida, salt, red chillies?” Her mother embraced her and responded, “My love, aloo poori is made by using all these ingredients but not in raw form. These are mixed in right proportions and are cooked for a certain time at a certain level of heat. Same ingredients turn out be delicious aloo poori when everything is in right proportion and right time is allotted to each ingredient. Same is the recipe of Aloo Poori of Life, which is made with ingredients of various sweet and sour events and we have to keep the right proportions of all these ingredients in our life. We must manage our limited time in a proper way so that neither it is overcooked nor under cooked” Her mother continued, "If you have failed, then convert your failure into success by working hard. If you have no friends, then introspect yourself and change your behaviour, which can help you make good friends. You burnt your dress due to depressed mind, keeping a good state of mind is very important for successful completion of various activities in life. We do not need to get validation from anyone else, we have to learn to love ourselves. If you can love yourself, you will get love from around you" Seema was overwhelmed with all the things her mother told her. She realized that life is not difficult, it is easy and lovely. But one has to recognize one’s abilities and the best way to do so is to love self. Moral of the Story: Life is made of bitter and sour events, enjoy all, that is life. BY: MANSEJAL KAUR CLASS: VI DELHI PUBLIC SCHOOL PATIALA ﻿
author: MANSEJAL Kaur

title: THE LOVE OF A MOTHER
text: long long ago a hunter named sohab was sitting under a tree he was a kind of lazy hunter he saw a large herd of dear grazing in the lush grade meadow. He said to himself,"These deers are really wonderful but I have to run a lot to catch one of them can't there be an easy way to get one?". Suddenly, he saw a female tigress coming slowly to the deers. she leapt and caught a deer after sometime her two small cubs come out of the bush they all enjoyed thier meal. Sohab's eyes brightened. They sparkled with an idea.He envied the cub's "can I be lucky as these cubs? they got their food withut any effort. Can I have a hunter like there mother?". He thought. He decided to catch a young cup and train it to hunt for him. Then I shall only say "O my dear go and kill a dear for me "my life will be very comfortable then he was very happy with his own idea. At night the mother Tiger cried so loudly that she was heated by a wise man living in the village. The old man understood what had happened. Everybody of our tribe will hate you because you are too lazy and wicked also. We all know that a hunter must hunt with his own strength and skill. But you are a lazy hunter. you are a thief. You have broken the rules of our tribe. You have brought dishonour to whole our tribe. " All the members of the hunter tribe got together. They decided to drive away hunter from their family as well as from village. Shanno took the cubs on his shoulders and carefully returned the kids to their mother. He loved the happiness of tigress. The motive of the story is to tell the love of a mother and animals too have emotions like us.

title: The Birthday Present
text: It started when a kid named Jojo whose best friend Yulu recently assembled a robot. The robot could talk, play and work. Hi, I am a robot. I can talk, play, dance, sing, work and do anything you want. Yulu handed his robot to Jojo as a surprise gift on his birthday. Jojo was very, very happy, when he saw it. He decided not to keep it for himself but give it in an orphanage as the children needed it more than him. The next day, Jojo went to an orphanage and gave it to the children as small gift for his birthday. The children were head over heels and thanked Jojo by all their hearts. Jojo also felt very obliged after doing the grateful work. Suddenly, he caught site of a boy who was acting weirdly, he asked him his name and the boy answered 'My name is Roy' in a weird way. Jojo did not give attention to him and went to the other children. He said them goodbye and promised them that he will meet them again. After Jojo left, the children started playing with the robot. They decided to keep a name for it and kept the name as 'Mika'. Mika also helped them bring their food and drinks. He narrated stories to the children. Mika also used to iron their clothes and kept them nicely. In faraway land of Scotland lived a fairy.She used to help everyone... One night when everyone was asleep, even Mika, Roy changed the robots chip. The new chip was controlled by Roy himself. The next day when the children asked help from Mika, he did the opposite that they said. One time they asked Mika to play with them, but instead of playing he scattered all the toys and broke them. These incidents repeated several times. All the students were irritated by Mika. Roy, enjoyed it while seeing it happen. But a day came when Mika didn't even listen to Roy and Roy didn't understand the problem. He used to scatter all his things and didn't follow his orders. Mika also tore Roy's clothes. That day Roy understood that how the other children felt when he used to disturb them. He felt guilty and apologised to the other children. As Jojo promised to come to meet them again, he fulfilled it and came with his friend Yulu. The children confessed their problem to Jojo. Jojo asked Yulu, if he could correct the problem as he had only assembled it. Yulu added a new chip and the robot started working like before. Everyone was on the cloud nine and thanked Yulu. Roy promised that he would not repeat it again. Everyone was happy and had a happy dinner.
author: Mishka Yadav

title: Feel
text: Hey, I'm Raya. I'm also a messy, lazy, chatty teenager. ﻿ Here's one thing you must know about me- I have always wished for someone to help me in my work,and to keep me company. Let's go back to the very beginning. It all began a few months ago, when my best friend Abby gave me a toy Robot as a birthday gift. At least I thought it was a toy. Until... well, it spoke. ''Hello, Miss Raya! Pleasure meeting you", it said all of a sudden, making me jump a feet in the air. I should've seen that coming, because Abby was a techie, a science-lover, and a super genius! I watched in amazement as the little robot took the pen and spelled out the letters R-A-Y-A on the paper. "I made it for you.Have fun!",Abby said with a huge grin spread across her face. ''You made this?!!"I asked her. "Yep", she answered, "It can even help you do your chores!". She must've noticed I looked very surprised, because just then she grabbed a paper and a pen from my drawer and told the robot; "Can you write Raya's name?". I slowly began to learn more about the robot. I didn’t realise it, but I was really starting to depend on it. It did my homework, folded my clothes, played badminton with me. Whenever my friends called me to play, I never went, I already had my robot to play with. During weekends, I sat in my room all day with it. Until one day, 3 months after I got my robot,something happened. Abby said that I had changed. I was confused, but then she said that she felt she should keep the robot with her for a while. I was very cross at her. But she was the one who made it in the first place, so I was forced to return it. Now that I didn’t have my robot, I had to get back to my old ways. But a day after Abby took the robot back, it was my father’s birthday, and I forgot about it. My mother was disappointed with me and I was upset myself. That’s when I felt a pat on my back. I turned, hoping to see my robot, but it was Abby. "A robot would never be by your side during your hardest times, unlike a friend", she said. Then I realised the truth myself. When the robot came into my life, I turned into a completely different person. Turns out, I'm better off without much technology. There is a major difference between machines and us humans. We have emotions, we can feel, and that can never be replaced by any fancy device.
author: Sruthika Murali

title: Aru and her little friends
text: Aru was at her grandma's house for the holidays. She always enjoyed staying at her grandma's house. She loved the smell and the sights of nature. But, most of all, she loved going down, with grandma, to the garden. There were so many interesting things there. Aru was only in 3rd grade but she was able to help out in many ways. However, she got distracted often. There were also some things that grandma insisted on doing by herself. Some of these tasks included weeding and harvesting ripe crops. One day, little Aru was walking around the garden when she noticed small wiggly things in the soil. She bent down to take a closer look. "They look like miniature snakes..." she thought, "And they're adorable!" Aru watched as the little creature wiggled about minding their own business. Suddenly, an idea popped into her mind. Aru placed her hand, palm facing upwards, on the ground and lured one of the little creatures onto her hand. Then she slowly placed it in her favorite bright yellow bucket. She repeated this until the bucket was half full with the adorable little creatures. Aru, then, stood up, grabbed her bucket and made her way to grandma's cottage. Once inside, Aru placed her bucket on the dining table and eased the creatures onto the table. The creatures wiggled around, getting to know their new environment; they finally decided to settle in the pot of a bush which was on the table. Aru watched these events with a smile on her face and fascination in her eyes. Soon enough, all the little creatures disappeared into the potted plant. Aru was disappointed that she couldn't see them anymore. In her despair, she remembered the magnifying glass grandma had got her last Christmas. She ran to her room and came back with the magnifying glass. Carefully, she peered into the thick bush through the magnifying glass; only to be disappointed. The little creatures had completely disappeared into the soil! The next day, Aru woke up to see grandma making breakfast. On her grandma's instruction's, she goes to brush her teeth and freshen up. Once grandma is done preparing cereal for Aru and soup for herself, she picks up the dishes and walks over to the dining table only to be shocked by the scene in front of her! There were earthworms crawling all over the table. After recovering from her shock, she sets down the dishes on the kitchen counter and calls Aru over. Aru, ecstatic to see her little friends again, leaves her poor grandma in complete confusion and disbelief. Aru then narrates yesterday's events to her grandma. Grandma is intrigued by the whole story. She then tells Aru about what the little creatures were and why they didn't belong in the potted plant. Aru, sorrowful but understanding, agrees to free the earthworms from confinement in the potted plant. Grandma and Aru carefully pick out the earthworms and place them in Aru's yellow bucket. Then, go outside and let the earthworms back into their habitat. Aru goes out into the garden everyday to watch her little friends as they go about their business, making the soil more fertile for plants to grow.
author: Ananya Naik

title: A Story of a hardworking Boy
text: Once upon a time there was a village named sathyapuram where all the workers farmers were very poor. author: Abdul  Ahad

title: THE JOURNEY OF A BRAVE WARRIOR
text: THE JOURNEY OF A BRAVE WORRIER Long ago, there was a boy name Jackson. He lived in a small village named Mirica village. He was a cowered person that he was even scared of a small spider. So, because of these, his father was very irritated with him. For that reason, his father decided a plan to make Jackson brave. So, during dinner Jackson’s father told him, “My boy I know you are fond of sweet mangoes. If you want to eat them then go to the Sansi Garden. He thought of it for sometime and decided to go. And here his journey begins…………… While travelling Jackson thought to ask the address of Sansi Garden, so while passing from the forest, he saw a man, pretty much of his age and was looking very depressed. So, Jackson asked him, “what is your name? “At first, he stared at Jackson and then answered in a sad mood “jack”. Looking at Jack, Jackson thought to introduce himself and ask the reason to him for bring sad “I’m Jackson well……. why are you looking so sad? “At first Jack didn’t reply, but after a minute he said “my house, my family is no more due to fire” and tears crawled out till his cheeks. Jackson told him to travel with him to the Sansi Garden.. As they were passing, Jackson asked the address of Sansi Garden to Jack in hope he knows. And the address given by him was ---“After passing the forest we will reach the crystal town, then we will pass the black sea, next we will reach the town of witches, named Blacktown and at the end of that town Sansi Garden is situated. They travelled and travelled until they reached the crystal town. In there in one of the notice boards, they saw that “black monster was a dangerous monster living in the Black Sea. Jackson and Jack decided to talk to the king and get a ship and in return they will defeat the Black monster. The king agreed. Travelling in the ship for many make them exhausted so, they decided to take rest in a nearby island. When they were taking rest, a pirate from another ship came and said “this is my island, so now as a punishment anyone of you have to do a sword fight with me. If I win you have to give me your ship”. Jackson agreed. And as expected Jackson won. The pirate thought to join them, travelling and travelling, they at last reached the castle of the Black monster. They fought bravely and won but Jack broke one of his arms. And then they started travelling towards the Black town. After reaching there all the witches stared at them as they were the odd one. At last, they reached Sansi Garden, Jackson with tears of happiness ate a mango. After having some mangoes Jackson took mangoes for his family also. And then they returned to crystal town. Everyone welcomed them in joy that they killed the monster. From there everyone started to make away towards their houses. When Jackson reached his house, he got to know that his father passed. Jackson realized that his father wanted to make him brave. Moral---We may face many challenges in our life, but we should know to solve them.
author: Prajukta Darshini
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Jean de Wet; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Rijuta Ghate; Sangeeta Das; Shadrach Munene; Vinayak Varma

title: Reflection!
text: There was once a cat named Toby, he used to live in a jungle, he was known as the coward of the jungle. All the animals used to tease him and tell him that he was a small and weak looking animal and that he had no courage. He was very brave before, but gradually because of the other animals continuous teasing, he started believing their words. One day Toby grew tired of the teasing, and to prove to the animals that he was not a coward, he announced that he was going to go deeper into the jungle. All the animals laughed and didn't believe him, no animal would go that deep because that area was where the lions, tiger, panthers and all the scary animals lived, but toby was too angry to see the risk and he ran off to the deep jungle. All the animals laughed and didn't believe him, as no animal has ever gone that deep because that area was the lion's territory, but toby was too angry to see the risk and he ran off to the deep jungle. He soon started to regret his decision as, He was terrified of the shadows that loomed around the trees and the fact if he met a lion. It soon started raining and toby looked for shelter and found a house. It was a really creepy house with spider webs and tall trees around it, but it started raining more heavily, and Toby decided to go in. It turned out that the house was abandoned. Toby was examining the house when he saw the most bravest, ferocious, courageos looking creature he had ever seen in his life on the floor. He stood there frozen with fear and started to move around the creature but when he did so did the creature, it was then when he realized that the creature was none other than himself. He was looking at his own reflection in a puddle! Toby looked at the reflection once more and realized that he looked quite big, ferocious and brave not weak and small at all. ' Now I know that I look fine, but I know one more thing too, it is that I was dumb to ever take their teasing seriously. I am fine just the way I am everyone is.' Thought Toby. Feeling dumbfounded but wise he went back to his part of the jungle, and because of his newfound courage he didn’t even bother about the lions or the shadows that were looming around. Once Toby reached home, all the animals were surprised to see him alive. They all started asking him questions like, " how did you survive? ", " did someone help you survive?" How did you survive? Did someone help you survive? “No” said Toby, “But I taught myself something very important. Everyone is fine just the way they are, and you should never let someone’s teasing affect you” After his small but wise speech all the animals started whooping for him, and started respecting him, and the king of that territory, the peacock appointed toby as the Mantri. Toby was delighted, and he promised that he would be the best Mantri ever and help the king in making decisions and educate the animals. Toby was saying the truth, he did follow his promises on being the best Mantri. After a few years he himself became the king. The moral we learn here is that we should always believe in ourselves and not let anyone’s teasing affect you. All of us are fine just the way we are.
author: Anveeka Borah

title: The Two Perceptive Cats
text: There once were two poor but witty cats. Their owner, Big Joe, abandoned them because they were nothing but two big bundles of clumsiness and responsibility. They had been living on their own for nearly three years now! They had nobody but each other. One day as they were trying to find something to eat from the trash cans, they heard a mouse squeaking from the other end of the alley they were in. And what do cats love more than anything? Mice! As they followed the squeaking, they reached a filthy and unused cottage. Neither Genevive (the blonde cat) nor Felicity (the black cat) could find the mouse. But there was one thing they found which amused them! It was a colony of ants carrying a pizza slice! As they followed them, they were led to a very posh-looking hallway. Felicity noticed that the ants were carrying the pizza to two fancy-looking mice and were serving them at the price of their lives. The two mice said, together "Well, well, well, look who finally showed up." Jessi, the mouse with the frock, said, "Ew, you pathetic little creatures again with your meaningless lives! Oh, brother, can't we just kill them right now? They brought pizza even after knowing about my gluten allergy! I can't eat pizza and this is what they get?! Kill them!" As they leaned towards the ants to eat them up, Genevive came and stopped the mice. She told them, "Before you eat them and sleep peacefully, could you guys have a look at our teeth? we heard you are famous dentists" "Yes indeed we are!" said the mice. As soon as they came close, the two cats gobbled them up and did not have to worry about that night's dinner anymore. They also became the new bosses of the ants as they saved them.

title: A help well returned
text: 10 year old Chintu was helping his father in harvesting the crops. He had to help his parents earn money, or else they would have to starve like they usually do. " Father, can I go play now? " Chintu asked his father after some time. " Yes, you can go now. But be back before dusk! " his father told him and continued doing what he was doing. Chintu was walking along a stream when he heard a voice which sounded like a dog whining. He walked towards the sound with curiosity and finally reached a pit. He looked inside the pit and to his shock, there was a puppy inside! So he got inside the pit as it didn't look that deep and saved the dog. Chintu successfully took out the dog and took a good look at it. One of it's legs was injured. "Aww, don't worry. I'll take care of you. " Chintu said in a sweet voice as he took up the puppy in his arm and walked home. After he reached home, the tired boy kept the puppy on the warm haystack. " Mom, can I have something to drink?" Chintu asked his mother. Chintu's mother brought him a glass of milk to drink when she saw the dog. " Where did this dog come from?" she asked Chintu. " I found him in a pit. He's injured so I brought him home." Chintu replied. " And how will you feed him? His mother asked him again. " I'll give him a bit of my food and my leftovers to him. Please?" Chintu pleaded to his mother. "I suppose. But you have to take very good care of him, Okay?" She said. "Yay! Thank you so much mom! From today, his name is Rocky!" Chintu exclaimed with joy and hugged her. As promised, Chintu took really good care of Rocky. But sometimes, he had to share his own food with the dog so that it could heal better. After about 4 days, the dog became comfortable with Chintu and his family and was also healing. One day, Chintu was going home from school with Rocky when he saw a man in fine clothes who looked troubled. So, he went near the man. " Excuse me, sir. You look troubled." Chintu told him. The man suddenly shouted with joy as he looked towards the dog. " Oh, Riki! I searched everywhere for you! Where were you?" He exclaimed. "Is he your dog?"Chintu looked at the man feeling a bit sad. " Yes, he is my dog. Where did you find him?" he asked in return. " I found him injured inside a pit. So, I took him home." Chintu replied. " Well thank you!" said the man. " I would like to thank your parents for letting you keep him" he spoke again. To this, Chintu nodded and leaded the man to his home while the dog followed. When they reached home, Chintu's mother asked the boy who the man was. "I am Martin. Your son took care of my dog when I lost him. I even heard from him that he shared his own food with the dog so that it could heal soon. I have come to reward him in return" Martin said. " Well, that's true. Chintu really loves the dog." Chintu's father said and hugged the boy. "But, what kind of reward?" " You see, I own a company. So, I was thinking that I'd offer you a job as a manager there. You will be paid enough to move to a completely new house in the city near my house and little Chintu can get to meet Riki too. " Martin offered the job to him. " But what about the farm?" his father asked. " I can hire some people for taking care of the farm and you can visit sometimes." Martin said. "Really? Wow!" Chintu's father exclaimed. The father accepted the job after few days and the family moved to the city where Chintu could meet the dog daily. They both now play together every day after school.

title: Abandoned
text: “We have to move out!” said a hesitant whisper. “Then what about Tom? He can’t possibly live alone,” spoke another. “Oh come on! He’s a dog! It can live for long enough on the streets. Please. We really cannot lose this opportunity, let’s just leave it on the street and go!” There was a long pause as if they were considering abandoning a friend as an option. “Do you not think of Tom as something more than an animal?” replied a cracking voice, breaking the long silence. “Of course I do!” The other replied. “It’s just for a year. And when we come back I promise you, we’ll take him back,” came another entreaty. “Do you think he’s going to be in one place for a whole year?” the other person replied, sending the sense of reality back to his kin. “We’ll get him attached to one place, he won’t move then,” the other said, still trying his luck. “I’m done arguing with you. Do whatever you want!” And so the following day on the cold, cruel streets far from home, was Tom, all alone and abandoned. Ever since he was a puppy, he was in the warm comfortable home of the two brothers. He didn’t know the ways of the world. Now, he sat down helpless and hungry. From the corner of his eye, he spotted a possibly blind man, wearing glasses, with a hat outstretched in his right arm. The hat was filled with coins that people gave him out of pity. Tom looked at the money with hopeful eyes. Perhaps they would give him food if he sat there helplessly too, he thought. He approached the man, seating himself right beside him, barking in a whimpering tone, hoping that someone would give him a meal. Soon, a man extended his arm, revealing a half-eaten bag of chips as his meal for the day. Throughout the day, many people stopped by to give him leftovers. By the time it grew dark, Tom had collected enough food that would last him a week! He was so amused that he didn’t notice that the blind man took off his glasses, and looked straight at Tom into his eyes, showing pure anger towards the creature. “You’re stealing my meals!” He said in a condescending tone. The man then reached for a stone close to him, and within a matter of seconds, he threw it at Tom. The rock hit his eye, making it bleed instantly. He groaned in immense pain. Running away as quickly as he could, he left his hard-earned food and the scammer behind. As the sun shone on Tom’s golden-brown fur, a new day began, with barely any food, or water to drink. Tom woke up with excruciating pain in his eye. The dirty stone had infected the eye, eventually blinding it. It was noon and he hadn’t eaten anything since the previous night. He was still dazed and had lost all his energy while running away from the scammer the previous day. He was sure he didn’t run out of the city, but he had never been to this place before. From a distance, he spotted a small bakery with a red door and a bell attached to it to notify the entry of new customers. “Maybe, he could steal some bread?”. He carefully waited till a woman entered the shop. He quietly followed her and entered along with the woman to not bring any attention to him. “Welcome! How can I help you?” The shopkeeper asked the woman. “One loaf of bread please,” the woman replied. Seizing the moment of engagement of the shopkeeper, Tom quickly grabbed something off the first shelf from the right, and ran as fast as he could, not seeing where he was going. The shopkeeper chased him with a stick in his hand. “Oi! Stop right there you thief!” he screamed, as an attempt to stop him. Yet, Tom kept running until he could no longer see the shopkeeper behind him. Tom looked around himself, trees, bushes, flowers, and the sound of a river flowing somewhere near him. He ended up running deep into a forest. He was injured and lost, but at least he had food. He quickly munched down the bread leaving nothing for dinner. Soon, the sun went down, and the night began to fall. Tom slowly found a place to sleep for the night. Days turned to months, and months turned to a year. Tom lived his life in the forest, coming to the city every day to steal a meal for himself and making his way back to the forest. To him, the forest provided a safer place than the city, where people were much crueler than the wild lions and tigers. On the other side of the city, the two brothers returned to the comfort of their old home. Days passed swiftly and yet they were least bothered about searching for Tom. One fine day while taking a stroll on the streets, they happened to enter the bakery that Tom got kicked out of. Suddenly there was a soft whimpering sound of a dog behind them, and as they turned around they found Tom, looking at them with tears of happiness filling his eyes. Yet, that happiness was not seen in the brothers’ eyes. Instead, they felt disgusted to look at the disheveled state of Tom; one eye blinded, one leg damaged to the point that it had to be amputated, dirt and mud covering the one majestic soft fur of the animal, cuts and bruises decorating his body. “I think we shouldn’t take him back. He’s too used to the streets now, it will be a disgrace to have him now. Look at him,” one of them said, as the other agreed with a nod. Just by looking at them, Tom seemed to have understood them. Anger, disappointment, and despair filled his eyes. In an instant, he sank his teeth into the neck of one of the brothers, and ran away deep into the forest; a place he called home now. As he walked towards the forest, taking struts filled with pride, Tom reflected upon the two greatest lessons he learnt in his life, never to depend on someone, when you can take care of yourself, and to never trust a person who had already betrayed you. He reached back, resting himself on a cool rock, waiting for the night to fall, happy that he would never have to set foot in that home again.
