title: Friends
text: Two friends met after many years and decided that they will spend an entire day together some place. They both agreed to go trekking in search for a place to rest and spend the night. When they started walking, they found a place surrounded by trees and decided to spend the night there. As the night fell, the mosquitoes gathered around and started biting them and one of the friends started to get irritated and in order to kill the mosquitoes started to smash them by clapping with both hands. The other friend suggested the first one not to make any sort of loud noise since it would attract any wild animals if they were close by. However the first one could not resist and continued to do so since mosquitoes were all over him and were biting him. Because of this the other friend got really upset and kicked the first one. The first friend felt bad about this but didn't react instead he wrote something on a leaf and threw it away. At dawn both the friends started walking again and wanted to come out of the jungle as soon as possible. While on the way back, the first friend noticed a scorpion on the other friend who was about to sting him. The first friend shove the scorpion with the help of a stick and saved him. Again he wrote something on a leaf and threw it. The other friend was watching him doing this since last night and out of curiosity asked him,"why do you keep writing something on the leaves and later on throw them away instead of keeping them with you?" To which the the first friend replied that when you kicked me the last night I felt bad so I wrote my feeling on the leaf and threw it away instead of keeping the grudge within myself. I let the feeling go instead of letting it cling to me for the rest of my life.I know I value our friendship very much and didn't want these small differences to drift us apart. The other friend was moved by this feeling of the first friend. "Time change with life, life change with time, time doesn't change with friends, only friends change with time."
author: Mahak Patel

title: A Never-ending War
text: Veena was flipping through the pages of a photo album. It wasn't like the ones that she had previously seen — all teemed with her photos. This one was quite different, as it hosted her mother's pictures, growing up. Veena was surprised to see that her mother looked very much like herself as a child. But amongst those several photos, one looked strikingly odd. She ran up to her mother, asking what the photo was about. The picture that Veena sees... "Oh that," her mother said, laughing. "It's a very old picture, isn't it? I suppose... It would be about twenty years back. Do you understand it, Veena? No? I'll tell you about it then. So, Veena, haven't you learnt about bacteria in biology?" Veena's mind immediately went back to her biology lesson. They had learnt about bacteria, of course they had. "Yes, the teacher told us about bacteria. She said they are organisms that we cannot see but are present everywhere." "Yes," Veena's mother replied. "Are you also aware of antibiotics?" When Veena shook her head, certainly perplexed, her mother began to explain to her. "Veena, about a century ago, a man named Alexander Fleming found a way to kill bad bacteria. This was an excessively big invention, and it saved many lives. But with time, this invention began being useless. I'll help you with an analogy. You know that Polar Bears have learnt to live in the very cold poles of the earth. The same way, antibiotics began being a regular thing for bacteria." Veena nodded. She understood what her mother was trying to say. Her mother continued, "This shook the entire world. The terrible time when people died of paper cuts was going to come back. Everyone feared what dismal thing they should expect next. All they could do was pray for themselves and their families." "What happened next?" "Well, realising the urgency of the situation, a team of very renowned scientists was set up to help with the problem." "And did this team also include you?" Veena was intrigued now. The photo in the album had quite a few scientists from around the world, working in lab coats with their eyes fixed on the lens of the microscope. "Were you the leader of the team?" Veena's mother smiled. "I was certainly not the leader of the team, but verry instrumental in finding the solution. We would work all day and night, frantically trying to introduce the bacteria to newer environments. We figured out that the bacteria might fail to survive in environments they were not familiar with. "Apparently, we had been wrong, because there was not a single thing that could control these tiny rascals. We were all living dead, we had decided. It was then that a very exemplary scientist thought of trying to use the simple concept of food chains. I'd love to introduce you to her one day, she was all that I'd want to see you grow up to be." "Now, her idea was simple. It was something that none of us had thought about because all the time we were conducting complex experiments, we hardly ever thought that the solution to the problem was present right in our laboratory. Veena, do you know that there are wars going on around us every day, your body itself is the battlefield." Veena was taken aback. Wars going around every day? Veena's mother laughed. "Oh dear, aren't you thinking too much into it? It's just a war between bacteria and a particular virus that's been going on for ages. Now this virus is called bacteriophage, or you can also call it a phage, if its name is mouthful. They are serial killers; they'll kill a bacterium when they see one. These viruses are also quite choosy, they'll prey upon bacteria and bacteria only. Now phages are the deadliest organisms, and we decided to pair them up with the second deadliest organisms, the humans." Veena laughed. Of course, humans were the second deadliest animals. "So, we decided to do what was evident, we began injecting phages in our bodies to kill the tiny monster bacteria." Her mother added. Veena was still in deep thought. Her mother asked if she had a question. She indeed did. She did not have 'a' question, she had several. Mom, I was just thinking, how can injecting viruses in our body ever be a good thing to do? And mom, how can we say that the bacteria would not evolve again like they did for antibiotics? Veena's mother was delighted because of her daughter's thoughtful questions. "Veena, the thing is that bacteriophages are very particular about whom they attack. So even if one of those viruses sees a human cell, they'll simply ignore it. This makes them very safe for humans, but not so much for the bacteria. And about whether bacteria would evolve against these viruses, nothing can be said for sure. But when we apply scientific reasoning to this question, we can deduce some speculation. Anyhow, it would still just be speculation. Most scientists believe that the war between phages and bacteria is one going on for ages, and as bacteria have evolved so have the phages, which means that even if the bacteria do get a cutting edge soon, they'll soon be overpowered by the viruses again. The second reasoning is that, to get resistant to even a few types of phages, bacteria must give up their resistance against antibiotics. So, even if the bacteria do evolve to elude the virus, we can always go back to using antibiotics." Veena was baffled by the information she had received. She kept pondering upon it the entire day. Viruses and bacteria, a never-ending war. She was so amused by it. The next day, Veena managed to surprise everyone with her newfound knowledge. The teacher was quite impressed, which made Veena feel enormously proud. When she came back home, she told her mother all about how the teacher praised her.
author: Ananya Kharade

title: Apoorva The Lioness
text: Once upon a time there was a small forest by name Rampurvan in Mysore, Karnataka. This forest was indeed ruled by the lion breed but not as usual as any other forest. In this forest, female lions called lioness ruled the animal kingdom. There were nine ministers, a princess and a queen. The queen's name was Tulsiana and her daughter's name was Apoorva. Tulsiana 's ministers were Diya, Maya, Shreya, Soundarya, Nithya, Mega, Neha, Arya and Avani. Apoorva grew up in her lovely animal kingdom and was always told not to go out of the forest circumference. Years went by and now Apoorva was 14 years old. One she heard her mom talking with one of her ministers Arya. She overheard Arya murmuring to her mom Tulsiana "Its the time to test Apoorva". Although Apoorva had heard something strange, she decided to pretend like she does not know anything. One day Tulsiana asked Apoorva to check if all the animals were safe and happy in the forest, so Apoorva left her habitat and started walking in the forest. As she continued walking, she couldn’t find even an ant in the forest. She ran back home and there were no one at her home. She was so confused. Suddenly she found a map with a route to a different forest, so now she believed that her family must be in the new forest. She had a goodnight sleep and on the next morning, she got ready for her journey. She had never crossed the forest before, so it was so exciting for her. her.. As she came out of her forest, she saw a really big city ahead of her. When she stepped into the city, it was deserted. As she started exploring the new place she heard a dog crying out for help. As she approached the dog it introduced itself as Lisa. Lisa the puppy told her that it had stolen its owner’s diary, wrote something in it and buried it under a tree.. Apoorva quickly started digging the diary out as Lisa did not have nails. Apoorva took the diary out and Lisa barked happily. Following Lisa Apoorva also roared loudly and caught the owner’s attention. Before Lisa could say thank you Apoorva ran away out of the city and entered a village where lionesses were really rare. As Apoorva walked into the village the villagers started chasing Apoorva.. At last Apoorva got caught and was put in a cage. As one of the villagers tried to kill it pounced on the villager and set itself free.. Now Apoorva was indeed tired of all the running and finally reached the forest. In the forest, it met a lioness by name Sia. Sia said to Apoorva that she was the princess of Rampurvan. Apoorva giggled and asked her to take her to the queen. As she met Tulsiana or her mom, she hugged her tight and told her about her tragic at the same time fun filled journey.. She asked her mom what was the purpose of leaving her a map and making her find that place? Her mom told that she wanted Apoorva to come out of her comfort zone. Then Sia begged for an apology for showing off that she was the princess. Apoorva forgave her and they lived happily ever after….. BY B V SKANDDHAPOORVA GRADE 6A
author: PAULIN SHARMILA
illustrator: Imile   Wepener; Ntembiso  Velemane; tapan sheth; Wiehan de Jager

title: LITTLE THUMB
text: Once there lived a poor woodcutter and his wife. They had no child. The wife sadly thought, "Even if I have a baby, no bigger than my thumb; I would never complained, I would be happy." Later they had a child, the size of a man's thumb. So they named him "Tom Thumb". One day, Tom's father got ready to go to the forest. As he sat on the seat of the cart, he told his wife " If only I had a bigger child to drive my cart". When Tom heard these words he told his mother "Please pit me in the horse's ear, I'll tell him where to go". On the way,two men were surprised to see the cart going along with a driver. They followed it to the last point, where the cart stopped. They were even more surprised when they saw a man sitting in the cart carrying a little fellow out from the horse's ear. They asked the woodcutter (Tom's father)to sell Tom to them for a large sum of money. Tom sat on his father's shoulder and whispered into his ear, " take the money, father,I'll come back to you soon". At last, Tom's father sold Tom and returned home with a large sum of money. A man put Tom in his pocket and said to his companion, "we'll soon become rich,when we take him from town to town and put him on a show.Tom asked the man to put him down so that he could take a rest.When the man put Tom down, he ran and hide in the bushes. The two men could not find Tom and returned looking sad. Tom found shelter in an empty snail shell. As he crept into the shell to sleep soundly, he heard some men planning to break into the Parson's house.He understood that they were thieves.Tom appeared before them and said, "I can help you to steal". The thieves agreed and joined him. Tom entered the house easily and asked them loudly,"How much money do you want?" The cook woke and the thieves ran out of the house. Tom went to the barn and slept on the hay. The next morning the cow was fed with a bundle of hay on which, Tom was asleep. As he went into the cow's stomach he shouted, "Please let me out". The cook cried,"Master this cow is talking". The parson came and was astonished to hear the cow talking. He thought that the cow was surely bewitched and ordered her to be slaughtered. The cow was slaughtered and thrown on to the dunghill. Tom tried to come out of the cow's stomach. But unfortunately a hungry wolf was there and swallowed Tom in one gulp. Tom said to the wolf,"If you want to eat more fresh and delicious food, I will tell you where to get them".The wolf agreed and Tom from inside the wolf's stomach directed him to his own house. Tom's father rushed into take his axe when he saw the wolf. Hearing the commotion Tom shouted,"It's me,father, inside the wolf's stomach". Tom's father attacked and kill the wolf with his axe. He cut open the wolf's stomach and got Tom out.The wood cutter, his wife and Tom were united and they lived ever after.
author: AYUSH   TIWARI
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; AYUSH   TIWARI; Greystroke; Horn Samon; Rohit Kelkar

title: MY CHILHOOD SUPERHERO
text: Well, not every superhero wears a cape right?! When i was born, i was blessed with a superhero who will always stay in my heart rent free. He was none other than my paternal grandad. I get flashbacks to those days when he would carry me on his shoulders during monsoons and wait for me till i reach from school. I would not sleep at night without listening to his stories, those were days when i had nothing to do but only soend time with him. During the summer holidays he used to tell me how he used adventure with his friends when he was my age and taught me climbing a tree, ride a bicycle and so much more. Usually my parents did not make it home at afternoon so i used to have my lunch with him, it was not the best food of our lives but were surely the best moments of our lives we had shared with each other. He would then read the newspaper sitting on the chair in our balcony and make me listen to what's going on in the world. All these good years with him and suddenly one day he left us. I miss him more than anything in my whole life.
author: Aarangan Phukan

title: The Labyrinth
text: GHOST Contrary to what the humans believed, being a ghost was as ordinary as a wooden stick. Even though there are inordinate speculations revolving in the human world about ghostly creatures being “evil spirits' ' and plotting the demise of humanity for the sake of revenge, in actuality, life as a ghost could get pretty boring. And Dawn was no exception in the paranormal world. She, like all others of her kind, lived amongst oblivious humans and showed no signs of existence Life as a ghost was like a perennial blur, faded discreetly into the background of the hustling and bustling lives of human beings. She was slowly getting used to existing only through the lens of her own eyes and not the others. She could walk into restricted areas, overhear other people’s secret conversations, commit a felony and yet nobody would suspect anything. As exhilarating and enjoyable the idea of being a ghost sounded, it was exactly as lonely and tedious. She didn’t have many friends in the paranormal world. All of the other ghosts were either way too old for her to have any sort of camaraderie with or they were not interested in socializing. So that meant that she would have to entertain herself and wander aimlessly to pass her days. PAST LIFE She remembered her old life as a human quite vividly. She replayed those days like a film reel over and over again and yet she could never find herself getting bored of the memories. She lived in a small house with her parents and her dog, Frodo. Her parents were both doctors and were rarely home but nevertheless, found time to accompany her. Frodo was more like a sibling to her than a pet. She adopted him from an animal shelter on her sixth birthday and then they immediately became inseparable. She remembered those days in the summer, when she would visit her grandparents and they would bake cookies, solve puzzles and pluck out mangoes from the mango tree in the backyard. Her grandfather used to tell her stories from his childhood and how he would go on scavenger hunts with his friends, walk around labyrinths, and prank his grumpy neighbor However, she did not remember the cause of her death. When she first came into the after-life, she was convinced that it was all a dream and she would wake up anytime. However, her deduction was proven to be fallacious, eventually. She felt sorrow at the fact that she had died so young and was unable to live her life to the fullest. She had many aspirations as a teenager. But, now she was stuck, aimlessly walking around different streets and watching people eat with their friends and families from outside the restaurant windows. A GHOSTLY CHRISTMAS Today was Christmas eve. It was her first Christmas Eve as a ghost. She walked into the church and quite surprisingly, it was empty. She closed her eyes and prayed. She knew there was only a brief possibility that her prayers would get answered, she still prayed. It was also a widely known fact that god was particularly fond of ghosts. He felt empathy towards their forlorn nature he had cursed them with. “Hello Dawn” her eyes shot open as she heard an unfamiliar voice speak. She saw an old man, standing in front of her. He was reasonably tall, with a gray beard and kind eyes. He was smiling ear to ear. To her immense surprise, she wasn’t in the church anymore. She was sitting in an office with several portraits of cats hung up on the wall. “Hello…” she replied with uncertainty, “I am sorry, have we met before?” “I assure you, we have” the man replied, “but please, take a seat” Dawn jumped as one of the chairs beside her pulled itself backwards from the desk. She stared at it, shocked. The man looked at her with a knowing glint in his eyes. She gulped nervously and sat on the chair. “Well, It is certainly quite rude of me to have not introduced myself yet” the man began, “Hello Dawn, it’s a pleasure to meet you, I am God...I suppose you wanted to go over a few things with me?” Dawn’s jaw was left hung open at the revelation. She failed to comprehend the situation. How could the almighty be sitting in front of her with cat portraits on the wall? The man, who was apparently God, let out a throaty chuckle, “This is a little confounding but I know why you came to me...you want to see your family again” Dawn gulped nervously and nodded. “I do.. but I know that is not possible” “Everything is possible, Dawn, if you have a little faith” God smiled, “I can allow you to meet them for one day, however, you won’t be there in your own disposition. You will have to take form as something else” “Yes!” Dawn exclaimed, elated at the idea of meeting her family once again. Her face lit up with joy. God smiled at her, with a strange glint in his eyes and snapped his fingers. The next thing Dawn knew, she was transported back to her childhood home. HOME SWEET HOME ﻿There was silence in the house and the walls were still covered with portraits of her and her family. There were similar scruffs on the floor and the fruit bowl was filled with green apples, her favourite kind of apples. It seemed as though nothing had changed. She was so caught up in tracing back all of the memories, she didn’t notice the form she had taken. She looked down at her feet, however, there weren’t any. She had furry paws and instead of feet and instead of skin and hair, she had fur. She had turned into Frodo! She heard sounds of people talking and so, instead of stressing the fact that she was now a dog, she walked into the living room and saw her family sitting together. Everyone looked massively dull. Dawn noticed her mother sniffling and her father comforting her, with a frown on his face. Her grandparents looked reasonably quiet and crestfallen. She noticed a picture of her was placed on the coffee table. She suddenly felt a cloud of melancholia take over her. She didn’t realize that it wasn’t only she, dreading the fact that she was not alive, it was also her family. They were probably feeling much more miserable and dejected than she was. Maybe that’s why God, so willingly, sent her as Frodo back home. She had to make this Christmas special for them. THE SECRET OF THE LABYRINTH She found it quite hard to climb the stairs as Frodo, and after slipping two times and almost hurting her head, she finally reached her room. Everything was exactly the same as she had left it. Nobody had moved a single thing. Her chipped wallpaper, thousands of strange paintings and artifacts, they were all the same. She found it easier to take out boxes from under the bed as a dog than a human. Before she had passed away, she had made paintings for her family as presents for Christmas. She had hidden them well enough for her family to not find them. She quickly ran down the stairs with the bag full of boxes between her teeth. She entered the living room and kept the bag beside her mother’s feet. “Frodo, what’s this?” her mother asked her dog-self quizzically. She opened the bag and found the paintings inside. A heart-wrenching sob came out from her mother’s face as she looked at the painting. Dawn had painted herself and her mother, sitting together and eating ice cream at night in the kitchen. It was something that they did quite frequently. They would talk about each other’s day while eating chocolate ice cream, both their favourite. Her dad’s eyes became welled with tears as he saw his present. The painting was of him and Dawn playing chess on a Sunday afternoon. They loved to play chess and they both were quite competitive. Although Dawn claimed she was better than him, she knew he let her win on most days to make her happy. Next her grandmother opened her present. She whimpered and held it close to her chest. The painting was of her grandmother and her licking the chocolate of the bowls while baking cookies. And finally, her grandfather opened his painting. He smiled and sighed. The painting was of the two of them standing before a labyrinth, hand in hand as they were preparing to go inside. Dawn knew that her presents had turned their Christmas right around. They looked considerably happier than they were before. She could go back to her life as a ghost, with much more relief and happiness. Something about this visit changed her perspective on the after-life. Although she was alone and her days seemed incessant, she knew that she had overcome the labyrinth, which was life. And even as a spirit, she wasn’t alone. She had her family who were constantly thinking of her. She was never alone. THE END
author: Trisha Gupta

title: A Rascal is Always A Rascal
text: Once upon a time, there was an old tiger, who was very ill. Due to his illness and his old age, he could not go for hunting. But the tiger was very clever, hence, he thought of hoodwinking people and then, killing them. One fine morning, while wandering, he found a gold bracelet, which was like a blessing of God for him. He started showing everyone, who passes by him, the gold bracelet so as to capture them in the trap of avarice. But people did not trust him and hence, ignored him. He started losing all his hope and then came a greedy man, who could do anything to get money. He was allured by the reference. He stopped and said to himself, “This looks like a good piece of luck. I want to get this bracelet at any cost.” Then, he said to the tiger, “Where is the gold bracelet you speak off? I want to get it.” The tiger figured out that he was caught in the trap of avarice and said, “ Follow me to my cave. I have kept it in my safe custody. I will give you the bracelet there only but I want some food in return.” The man agreed and bought some beef and meat for him. Midway, he was met by his friend, who consulted him not to fall in the trap of greed. But, was completely unaffected. He went to forest where he saw the tiger first. He found the tiger and showed him the food. He said to the tiger, “How can I trust you, given that you are a predator.” The tiger started, "Listen man," and went on to say, "I admit, in my youth, I was wicked and killed many cows, goats and human beings. My wife and children died because of my evil deeds. Then I consulted a holy man who advised me to give alms. So, now I take a bath and give away things for the sake of charity. Besides, I've grown old. My teeth and claws have fallen off. So, why do you fear me?" The man was taken in by his clever talks and followed him to the cave. He blindly trusted the tiger. When they reached the cave, the tiger asked him to enter his cave and the man did so. The tiger comforted him and gave him the bracelet so that he became happy and stop overthinking. The man was overwhelmed and gave him the meat. Seeing his good mood, he waded towards the man and attacked him. When the man was on the brink of death, he shouted, “Ah! This villain's talk of holiness completely took me in. A rascal is always a rascal. Like a fool I believed him. I must have not fallen in the trap and must have considered my friend’s advice. Now I must pay for it. Soon after, the tiger killed the greedy man and ate him up.
author: Manya Mittal

title: Memory Lane
text: The night is cold. I can feel the gushes of wind blowing in through the window. It’s hitting the glass panes hard and making a whooshing noise. There’s a hubbub of activity going on around the house. Everyone’s busy packing up because we are shifting away to a new house tomorrow and not only a new house but a new country altogether. It feels strange. The place I grew up in is going to become a stranger to me in a few days time. I’m leaving behind, the past, the memories, the people I grew up with are all appearing in my mind through flashbacks. I lie down on the hard marble floor- this feels closer to home. My mind drifts… Sun is about to set. My friends and I are riding our bicycles through the mustard fields past the highway that is when we suddenly notice hundreds of fireflies flying about glittering like gold amongst the pink sky… “Roo?” my mom calls out. I am jilted back from my pleasant reverie. My mom is calling me for dinner. I go through the motions. I do everything that is told to me without really putting my mind into it. I feel nauseated. I remember my school days. Going to school, making friends, laughing, talking, learning and playing…what a time it used to be! I feel myself dozing off…I decide to go to bed early tonight. It’s hard. I find my mind recap the memories of the ‘good old days’. It is strange how even the mind has a filtering technique- how it remembers only the happy memories cutting out the unhappy parts of life. Suddenly the images of the Durga Puja festival starts to take hold of my mind…I can see the Goddess Durga in front of me, the streets filled with colourful lights and people making merry. The tangy smell of fast food is in the air and people are joyously moving around with family and friends…I remember how I had spent my evenings with my dearest friends- chatting, eating and riding the giant ferris-wheel! My heart is aching. I find my cheeks wet with tears. I’m crying? I didn’t even realize it! I didn’t get time to even bid my close ones goodbye because my dad’s transfer took place on a very short notice. In addition to that, he informed me about this much later thinking how I would break down…But he didn’t understand that a little before or a little after didn’t matter- this was ought to happen either now or later! I had dozed off for a while. I wake up with a jolt! What time is it? I look at the wall clock in my room- it’s past 01:30am. I’ll run away I think. I don’t want to go to a new country and start all over from scratch when I have a whole life waiting here, at ‘home’. I get up from bed and as my bare feet touches the cold floor I realize the emptiness and foolishness of my thoughts…I have to accept what is happening to me. In the end of the day that’s all what life is about- accepting change and going on. I’m not an escapist. I take out my school photo album. The very first photo there is of me receiving a trophy for an essay writing contest. I remember that the topic given to us were-“the purpose of my life.” I remember having written about how I would want to bring about a change in the Indian education system. It feels like a lie to me now. I feel myself running away from my dreams, my aspirations. I flip the page of the album. Next is a group photo of my class when we were studying in nursery. I try to identify the names of everyone in that photo and as I proceed doing that I find myself laughing thinking how much they have changed now and what they had looked like once! I see myself standing at the edge of the photo with two ponytails and large curious eyes. The way I was glaring makes me laugh out loud. I flip over the page again. This time there’s a photo of some of my classmates and me hugging onto each other and crying. My mind goes to a flashback. It was the summer vacation I remember and we were parting from each other for almost more than a month- which made us all cry. But now I’m parting from them forever! What about My head is throbbing. Clinging into the album I fall asleep. “Wake up Roo” my dad calls out. “It’s already past ten. We need to leave by twelve” he says. that? Rubbing my eyes I get up thinking that there’s just two more hours to go. As I go through the motions of taking a bath, packing the last minute essentials etc., I realize the folly of life and how every destination reached is a temporary one. As the car honks outside the gate and as I take my bag and take a last look at ‘my home’, I feel myself choking. My mind goes blank. As the car turns round the crossroad, I take out a letter from my purse- a letter I had written as a seven year old about how my homeland is the best place on earth on the occasion of Independence Day. I throw the letter out into the air. It flies for a while and I see it fall down in the middle of the road as our car speeds away. I hope someone reads it. I hope someone remembers that I exist with all my unrealized dreams. I make a pledge to myself that I will come back one day.... I take out my smart phone and Google about my new ‘home’- Florida. I want to know a little about the place I’m going into. Life’s not about accepting what comes our way- it is to make those unfulfilled dreams and desires come true that you think might never happen in your lifetime!
author: Ahana Datta

title: Fun With Books
text: Meera didi loves books. She has many children's books. Koki, Sona, Khushi and other children visit her to have fun with her books. Babloo, the pet dog barks, "woof! Get the ball, or other toys to have fun!" "We can have a lot of fun with books too!" Chorus the children. "How can that be?!" Babloo asks. He is thinking of a rubber bone! "We can read stories, about fairies, flowers, animals, trees, birds, boys, ghosts, girls... oh what fun!" Koki says happily. "Books have activities too! We can color, draw or do a puzzle! How nice!" Khushi claps cheerfully. "May be, I can chew the book," Babloo smiles. He likes this activity! "Books help us to make things. It is so much fun to read craft books and make something!" Bebu says. He had come with his craft box! "Oh! Yes! Please make me a soft toy to play with,"Babloo wags his tail. 'I find books fun when someone reads aloud to me!" Coco smiles. And all the children nod. "Yes, Yes, when someone reads from a story book, it is fun!" says Sona. Babloo likes to listen to the bedtime stories. So he agreed and even pretended to sleep! And so, Koki, Sona, Khushi and her friends have a lot of fun with books. They read stories, color the pictures in the book, do puzzles and crafts and read aloud too. Now Babloo too feels books are fun. How do you have fun with books?
author: Shahin Ashraf Ali

title: Dogs Day out
text: Mono is the name of a dog. He had been a homeless dog. He used to look for food here and there. However, he used to sleep without meals sometimes. Lolo, one of his dearest friend was also a homeless dog. They both used to play, swim in the river, try to catch fish, and do a variety of other activities. One day, when they were playing in the garden, a child named Pranav came. He felt quite lonely. He desired to communicate with someone. Then he noticed some barking. He noticed two dogs playing with each other. He, too, desired to play. When Mono noticed the child, he said to Lolo, "I suppose that child wants to play with us." So Mono gave that boy a stick. Pranav tossed the stick, and Mono followed. This was the start of a friendship. So, from then on, Pranav would come every day. Pranav then asked his father if he may adopt two dogs. His father immediately agreed. Pranav 's joy knew no bounds! Lolo and Mono were delighted. They will not be sleeping on the streets. They will be equipped with appropriate food and water. Mono and Lolo then headed to Pranav's. They were delighted. Pranav's friend Krish used to make visits from time to time. ﻿ A fantastic ending

title: The Courageous Mr. Bread
text: Narrator: Out of the oven, came an ordinary loaf of bread but what it was holding, a big surprise, Mr. Bread. He was sliced and forced into a packet where he felt suffocated and trapped and couldn't understand anything. He felt alone and scared. Suddenly, he heard someone, it was Mr. Fluffy. Mr. Fluffy: Hello Mr. Bread. I’m Mr. Fluffy. Mr. Bread: Hello, what is this! Why are we in this packet? Mr. Fluffy: It is our bad luck that we ended up here. I have heard that even the softest breads can’t escape from these packets. These monsters will eat us whole and there will be no trace of us in the history of the breads. Narrator: Both of them tried together and got it open in one go and came out of it. Mr. Bread: Hey, that’s a piece of cake! I’m over the moon. Mr. Fluffy: Yes, you’re right! I never dreamt so. Narrator: Then both of them heard a footfall of steps coming towards them. Mr. Bread: So, what should we do? Mr. Fluffy: There's only one way I can think of, we'll have to use all our might and tear this packet open. Narrator: Then came the baker. Frightened by him, Mr. Fluffy jumped into the packet and Mr. Bread lay still on the kitchen counter. The baker sealed the packet in which Mr. Fluffy was, took a plate, snatched the packet and left. Mr. Bread was devastated that he couldn’t do anything for Mr. Fluffy. Mr. Fluffy: Hush! Mr. Bread! Let’s get back into the packet quickly or we’d be caught. Mr. Bread: No! I'm not going into that prison cell again because I want to see this beautiful world. Mr. Bread: What do you mean? Mr. Grand: It means that I'm the superior one. I escaped from a packet yesterday. Mr. Bread: Wow! Could you suggest me how I can save my friend from that baker. Narrator: Mr. Bread was alone, walking on the kitchen counter thinking about how he could save his friend. Then suddenly, bumped into someone Mr. Bread: Who are you? Mr. Grand: There was a time when I was known as 'The Bread of all Breads'. Mr. Grand: Sure, but first let me take you to a Safer place. Mr. Bread: So nice of you. Thank you very much. Mr. Grand: Listen now. You'll sneak into the baker’s sleeping place when he's fast asleep. You’ll open the packet in which your friend is trapped and will escape quietly. Mr. Bread: Nice idea Mr. Grand. Thanks a lot. Mr. Grand: Now go and save your friend. Narrator: It was night-time and the baker was fast asleep. Mr. Bread reached and saw that only Mr. Fluffy was left in the packet. He got frightened and rushed towards the packet. He whispered, "Mr. Fluffy! Mr. Fluffy! I'm here." Mr. Fluffy: Mr. Bread, you came just to save me. Mr. Bread: Now let's get you out of this packet. Narrator: A s soon as Mr. Bread got Mr. Fluffy out of the packet, the baker woke up. Both of them shouted, “Run!”. The baker grabbed Mr. Bread and put him into his mouth. That was the end of Mr. Bread. NO OO OO OO OO OO OOO oo oo This was the journey of Mr. Bread. He was devoured by the baker in saving his friend’s life. Since that day his name was engraved in the history of the breads. The sacrifice of his dream along with his life to save his friend’s life made him ‘The Bread of All Breads’.
author: Uddesh Gadge

title: THE GENEROUS KITTEN
text: Mia, the kitten lived in a garage with her parents and grandma. It was very cute, furry and pluffy. One day, Mia came whimpering all the way to grandma cat. ﻿ Grandma cat was sitting there idle when she saw her granddaughter. She got dumbstruck and asked Mia, "Why are you crying? Did you fell down somewhere?" Mia shook her head saying "No" but continued to cry. Grandma asked again but she again got the same reply from Mia. Grandma grumbled and said, "Then what's the matter? I can only help you when you tell me the reason of you crying." Teary eyed Mia said, "I saw lots of mice roaming freely outside the garage but I couldn't hunt even a single mouse." Grandma sighed and then asked, "Why? Why couldn't you hunt?" Mia replied, "The mice were just way too fast for me, grandma. They quickly ran into their holes." "Oh my dear, who cries like this for just that? Can you get a mouse just by crying?" Said grandma cat, patting Mia's back. She hugged the little one. Mia desperately cried, "I want to hunt the mice." Grandma consoled her by saying, "Don't cry dear. I promise that I'll bring the mice to our house." Mia was excited and asked grandma if she could really do that for her. To his grandma nodded and said yes. That very evening at Mia's door, a notice board hung saying, "Let's listen & play....come, here the mice are told virtuous stories." All mice were staring at this board. Most of the mice were scared after reading this but still some mice came there hesitantly. When grandmother cat saw this, she told them, " Don't be afraid, little ones. Come in." With a warm smile on her face, she further said, "I'll tell you moral and virtue stories. Also, I'll teach you some exciting games." Only three mice came that day. Grandma cat told them a beautiful story, which was liked very much by all three of them. A little game, a little song-that one hour didn't seem to pass. The mice went home overjoyed. Mia was watching all this from her room. "Just wait for two more days. If you start hunting right away, no mouse would ever come here anymore." Said grandma. Mia nodded happily. Next day, the three mice brought their friends with them. Now, there were many mice in the house. Watching grandma narrate so many thrilling and exhilarating stories, Mia too wanted to go closer and get the experience. Not being able to control her wish, she started listening to grandma's stories along with the mice and played with them happily. This went on and on...until a week passed. Mia ate with them, played with them. She enjoyed the company more than anything else. On the eight day, grandma told Mia, "Mia, the mice will come today also. As soon as I finish the story, you start the hunt." Mia agreed. The title of the story for that day was-'Never disappoint those who trust you.' Grandma told the story and then closed the doors and windows of the room. She said to Mia, "The game has begun. It's your time. You hunt now." The mice shivered after hearing this. Grandma stared at Mia. "Grandma, forgive me. The story you just told has changed my mind. You said that we should not betray those who trust us. In the same way, these mice trusted us and came here fearlessly. I've also become a good friend to them. I can't hunt my friends. I can't..." Grandma, shocked by Mia's speech, thought for a while and then spoke in a sweet voice, "Mia, even though you are young, you compared the stories I told you with your life. But I, the one who told the stories, never did. This is my mistake. Everyone please forgive me. From today onwards, you are like my grandchildren, just like what Mia is to me." From that day onwards, many more mice came to listen grandma's stories and to play with cute little Mia.
author: C.B. SRI SRUTHI

title: Grandma's Love
text: Once in a village there lived a grandma. She was a very kind person and showed her love towards many animals. She loved squirrels very much. One day it happened that a tiny little squirrel lived in a huge neem tree near right next to grandma's house. Grandma was very delighted to see the squirrel nearby. so she decided to keep a small piece of guava and a piece of idly near the window. The next morning when grandma woke up the squirrel had eaten up everything. From that day onwards grandma was happy to feed the squirrel everyday. After a few days grandma made a house for the squirrel with twigs, cotton and newspaper near her window. She didn't like the squirrel always coming from a far off place to eat food. A few months passed, the squirrel and the grandma became friends. Later two more squirrels were born and grandma was overjoyed. From that day, grandma took extra care of the baby squirrels. One night whe grandma was preparing dinner, a cat managed to sneak into grandma's home with the help of the huge neem tree.When grandma was in the kitchen, she heard a loud noise coming from the squirrels home. Kee! Kee! Kee! they shouted. Grandma was stunned to see a cat struggling to get inside. She scared the cat and drove it away. The squirrels showed their gratitude to grandma by bowing to her. From then, the squirrels and grandma lives happily ever after.
author: Madeeha Fathima

title: My friend elephant.
text: Once in a forest, there was a family who lived in the forest their whole family and one day the wife gave birth to a boy they named him as anand, Anand grew up in the forest and was a little familiar with the forest he was really fond of it and wanted a pet animal, not dogs and cats but some wild animal as his pet, One day his family went hunting but he stayed back with his grandmother by the time they came back it was dark and Anand went to sleep, his parents found a baby elephant so they took it and kept it beside Anand On his birthday the elephant ran away their parents searched everywhere and he was sad from that day on wards one day he was really sad he ran away deep in the forest and got lost somewhere And suddenly he heard a roar and he saw behind him there was a lion but it was in the air and when he saw on his other side he saw a elephant lifting the lion with it's trunk and threw it away Then he saw that it was his tomy his baby elephant but now it was big a fully grown adult elephant it picked anand up and kept him on it's back and rode him to home and they both lived ever happily. THE END.

title: DUMA THE PET CHEETAH
text: Duma the pet cheetah Just few years ago on thehills of Alps lived a happy family.The family members are Thomas, his father Henry Carter and his mother Andrea Carter. They were farmers but lived a happy life.Henry always tries to teach Thomas how to ride a bike because Thomas is now 14 years old. One day while Henry and Thomas were on the way back to their house after catching 10 fishes from the river nearby at the same time in the nearby jungle a cheetah gave birth to 3 cheetah cubs. After this within seconds the mother cheetah saw a lion coming towards its cubs then it decided to save her cubs. Soon she ran faster and attracted the lion. But the lion caught the cheetah but without knowing these things her cubs came out in search for their mother in that a cub came to a remote road. The same time the father and his son were returning fastly back to home. While Carter was driving the cheetah cub came in front of the road and in a fraction of a millimetre the cub has escaped and in a rush Thomas and Carter ran out of car saw what happened to the cub luckily the cub was fine. Thomas asked to his father “dad can we keep this cheetah cub with us?” His father answered yes. Thomas named him Duma. 5 months passed awaythe father and his son I mean Henry and Thomas were trying to find the highest capable running speed of Duma their bike were at 80kmph bu the Duma’s speed was more than that, that it overtook them by running itself and Thomas was recording this incident. After sometime at their house garden Thomas and Duma were playing at some distance they saw Hendry getting down and then fell down. Soon they called ambulance but doctors couldn’t save Henry as it was a massive heart attack. The happiness was all over but his mother tries to keep Thomas happy but Thomas is still unhappy. Her mother informs to Thomas that the Duma is going to zoo in 3 days and we areoving to city. But Thomas opposed to send Duma to zoo and he wanted to stay here but his mother didn’t listen him. He then decides to send Duma to forest as his father wished and wrote a letter and went. When Andrea cam house she saw the bike tyre prints in the sand and saw the letter and read it and started crying. She then complain to police but police said he is not in city he must be in desert so we must search him there only with the helicopter. The same time they were on their way to the jungle across the desert. This time nearly 1 hour after the travel starting the fuel of the bike gets over and he saw a crashed plane down and went there and slept there as it became night. Morning when he woke up he saw a man tryingto ride in his bike and then he put a plan and went to the man and said if you give me your water I will say how to on this bike and the stranger also accepted it. The stranger gave the water and asked the way to on this bike the Thomas said “I don’t know”. The stranger said you itself fooled me and intro himself. His name is Steve and he came from West and going to North and Thomas said I’m too heading to North and asked can we join and travel? Steve accepted it and Steve said he ran from his family and village in search of money and wealth but everywhere he was dominated and treaten unequally and then he came to know that family is everything and after that he is returning back to his village. At this time the beetles started chasing them, in this time Thomas went one way with Steve another way a different type of animal which Steve was keeping as pet and Duma went. Duma and Rimba(Steve’s pet)went to safe place whereas beetles were chasing them bu Steve covered Thomas with his shirt and all the beetles stung him and went because of this Steve became sick. Thomas tied Duma there and lied down Steve near him. He made a bornfire near them and took Rimba with him and went in search for help for Steve. The same time Duma noticed that lions went back of Thomas and Duma tore the tie and attracted all the lions and it also escaped and made Thomas also to escape. Thomas found some villagers and used sign language and called them for help and all the villagers rescued Steve but Steve’s face was unrecognisable and the villagers took him to village and gave treatment. The same time Thomas was searching Duma bu Duma found another cheetah and became friend for it and came near Thomas and hunt the nearby wild bull and ate together with its new friend. Emotionally Thomas said bye and gave a last kiss to Duma and came near Steve and saw that it was his village and his family members were hugging him. Seeing this Thomas missed his mother. After sometime came Steve and gave a stone and said you have fuel for bike but don’tforget me if you want to remember me you can see this stone. After this his mother did not sell the land and house instead she stayed there as her son and husband stayed there and was un comfortable with city. While she was ploughing the land with tractor she heared the bike sound with the voice of her son saying “ I fullfilled dad’s wish and I missed you very much mom” Andrea gets down from tractor and hugs her son. Thank You By M.NarenSathya
author: NARENSATHYA cp

title: Meg in Nevada
text: Megan hates change. Being in a new place, away from her friends, with a whole new bunch of people and new school life — she was just not ready to accept. She’d spent all her life in California, and moving to Nevada was going to be really challenging. She looked out the window, eyes filled with tears. “Mom, Why did we have to move? I’m gonna miss my friends and school, you know that.” She said with her breaking voice. Her mother looked at the rear view mirror sympathetically. “Dear, you know this is a better opportunity for us if I had this job. This is life. You have to learn to adjust and accept changes. You can talk to your friends everyday, you have your own laptop. And I’m pretty sure that you’ll meet new friends there.” “No! – I won’t, okay? There aren’t any better friends than Lily and Sam!” Her mother was silent. She didn’t know what to say. It was a silent ride. Even Tim, her dog didn’t make a sound. As the evening sky darkened, they had reached their destination. Megan’s uncle Dan, was waiting for them. “Hi Delphi! How was the trip? Oh, Meg, how are you?” Tim jumped out and circled him but Meg ignored and sat inside the car. “The trip was fine. But Meg’s still upset.” “Oh. I’m sure she’ll be okay soon. Here, these are the papers of the house. And these are the keys. I’m leaving now. If you need anything, just make a call. I live just across the street. Goodnight.” “Goodnight Meg!” “Thanks Dan. Goodnight.” “Meg, c’mon, let’s go inside.” Meg was too exhausted to argue, she just followed her mother inside. Tim also followed. It was a tiring journey, so she slept soundly. The next morning, there was a guest at the breakfast table. “Hi Meg! I’m Avory. I live next door. I’m also going to the same school as you. D’you wanna hang out?” Avery had a round face and brown hair tied with a ribbon unlike Meg who had black hair and a darker skin. Meg was confused, still, she agreed reluctantly, “Yeah, sure.” “ Okay, great. I’ve already asked your mom. So don’t worry about her. I’ve also bought food. I’ve got an old bike in the garage. You can have that.” “Mm.” Soon after the breakfast Meg, Tim and Avery were ready to go. “Mom I’m leaving. Taking Tim with me.” “Okay dear, have fun.” replied her mother with a hope that it might change Meg’s mood. Avery was delighted. She didn’t have many friends to play with. “Let’s go to a hill today. It’s nearby. Your bike’s outside” They got on their bikes and set off. Tim ran behind them. “C’mon Meg! You’re a bit slow” She stopped and looked back. “We’re almost there!” Meg struggled to keep up with Avery. They parked their bikes and went uphill and descended from the other side. “Wow, it’s so beautiful.” It was the first time Meg smiled after they moved. Tim was wagging his tail with excitement and sniffing all around. It was noon. They had their food and rested for a while. After a while, they set out exploring again. When the sun spread its colours in the sky in the evening. The two of them held hands and started walking back. Of course, Tim was there, ahead of them. It was a wonderful day. They had lots of fun. Avery and Meg decided to hang out again the next day. They rode their bikes back home and departed to their own homes. Meg and Avery went out again the next day. This time, to a lake. They had so much fun that Meg realised an important thing -- that changes should be there in life. Later, at dinner Meg was sharing her day with her mom. Her mother was happy for Meg. “Meg, I’ll have to go to work starting next week. Still, you’ll have a friend when you join school next week right? So I don’t need to worry.” “Yeah, I guess. And, you were right, mom. I think we do need to accept changes and things can’t work as I want them to. Me and Avery are friends now. But Lily and Sam are, too.” “That’s great, Meg. Did you call Lily and Sam?” “Uhh, no. I’m gonna call 'em now.. By the way, Avery and I are going out again tomorrow. We couldn't see the lake completely. So can you make us food?” “Yeah, sure dear, and be careful on the lake.” Meg finished her dinner and excitedly went to her room. She made a group call with her friends. They talked a lot about each other's day and discussed their meeting. They all were sad, but they promised each other that they’ll remain friends forever and call each other every night, no matter what. “Goodnight mom, Goodnight Tim!” As Meg laid down to sleep that night, several thoughts were racing through her mind. She saw Avery, Lily and Sam, Tim and her Mom. She thought how lucky she was to have such wonderful friends, a great friend: Tim and a lucky mom. She was thankful and happy laying there thinking. She closed her eyes, for tomorrow she has to go for a new adventure! School started, and life continued. Meg shared her happiness and sadness with her friends, Tim and mom. In the summer vacation, Avery and Meg went to California and had an amazing time with Lily, Sam and of course our Tim! Meg was also a great role model for others who couldn’t accept changes and find friends.

title: The Forlorn Survivor
text: It was one fine autumn evening, although there was something eerie and spooky in the air. The winds were blowing with the leaves along with them. The leaves were creating a rusty noise. There stood a small house in the vicinity, the lights of this house was very dim. Meanwhile, the phone rang in Kai’s grandparent’s house. As soon as the news broke, they ran towards the garage and took their car along with them. In full speed, they drove their car. In about one hour, they reached Park Street. Then quickly, Madison and William came out of the car and rushed towards the house. They heard a crying noise near the porch and the neighbors had surrounded their house. As they went closer towards the porch, they saw their grandson, Kai, crying in agony as he had lost his mother that evening. His father had ran away with all his belongings and had left the child behind. The scene made Madison extremely vulnerable and she fell on her knees. Tears gushed down her eyes. Kai’s mother had committed suicide and left her son behind. All William did was stare at the baby boy who laid down crying. As it was a self-committed suicide, they could not compliant an FIR. Hence, they called up the mortuary van and then, with great grief they called some close family members and performed the funeral rituals. Alas! The baby was just an infant, unaware of the depth of the situation which had taken place. Kai’s aunt couldn’t help much at the time as she was eight months pregnant at the moment and her husband had just come out of coma due to a car accident. Kai’s legal documents were soon changed and his maternal uncle, Cris, became his legal guardian. As Kai grew older, he never questioned any of this but deep down he knew that he was an orphan. His father had died on the same night as his mother, for him and his new family. He had dark brown hair and the color of his eyes were hazelnut. Earlier, Cris was a young lad when he adopted Kai but as he grew older, he knew that even he had to settle down in life and get married someday. As Kai was an intelligent boy with good looks, many barren parents wanted to adopt him. Even his aunt, Lorelai, wanted to take Kai but Cris was very fond of him and could not imagine separation from his nephew, now son. Years past, Kai got into football and became very passionate about it. He was an average student but with a very high IQ level, although he didn’t pay much attention to his studies. His prime focus was sports. He was very devoted towards football. When Kai was about 16 years old, his uncle married a very selfish and manipulative bride. Then, they were not aware of her behavior. Years went by and her grasp on her husband increased and she left no stones unturned to brainwash her husband against Kai. After one year, they were blessed with a baby girl and she used her was a weapon to completely get hold of her husband. The baby girl’s name was Rory, named after her great-grandma. Rory was earlier a very sweet and kind kid but as she grew under the influence of her mother, she became self-absorbed just as well. Lily and Rory always wanted to disown Kai. Cris’s wife, Lily, never loved Kai, she never offered him any food neither did she take him out for vacations nor outings nor functions with them. Madison and William grew old and because of this they didn’t have any say in all these. Lily was even against Kai’s education and his football coaching. She always thought that spending even a dime for him was waste and useless. Cris slowly had started to change. Lily constantly nagged Kai but in front of her husband she was an ideal wife and mother who loved both of their children equally no matter what. Lily always told Cris extremely bad things about the young fellow. Soon, a very bad image of Kai was created in front of Cris. Kai had realized everything but he knew that was the only and only near and dear friend of himself so he always kept shut. On 8 th of October, the day his mother has passed away and coincidentally his birthday, he woke up and just like the past years, no one wished him nor did anyone cut a cake or gifted him anything. Kai, as humble as he was, said nothing. That day, Lorelai, his aunt called him and cooked his favorite delicacies and also gave him some money to enjoy with his friends. This did make him happy but he was expecting a little something from Cris but unfortunately that did not happen. That was his 19 th birthday. After some days past his birthday, he started a conversation about his college at the dining table at dinner. Lily was trying to convince Cris that his education was going in vain and that he was an unfortunate chap who had nothing but destructive motives and always brought disgrace to their family. After hearing this, Kai had it. All these years he heard every nonsense of hers but that day he spoke and stood for himself. After enough humiliation and taunting, Kai put some essential things in a backpack, rode his bicycle and went away. He didn’t even carry his cell phone along. Two weeks passed by, they complaint a FIR but that was of no use as Kai was nowhere to be found. The only person who was happy was Lily. All her planning had finally paid off. Meanwhile, Kai had left his studies and had started a part time job in an entirely different city. He had been working at a library and a hotel reception for some time and with the money he earned, he started his football coaching again and living a very minimal lifestyle. Five years passed by and everyone lost hope of Kai returning and at the same time karma had hit them and their business got insolvent. Their printing press went into extreme loss and they fell into debt. Somehow, Kai was very lucky for them and their family. Whereas, Kai, now twenty-four years old had settled into his sports profession and at the same time, he started his very own football coaching center. At the same time he fell in love with his previous coach’s daughter and got married and they started their very own family and were blessed with a baby girl and they named her Blair, after his own mother. Finally, the spot in his heart which was always empty, fulfilled. His family was small but always happy. They loved each other and Kai had adopted another boy from an orphanage whom they treated just as their own daughter. Kai was quite well to-do now. One day after a lot of convincing from his wife he agreed to meet his family. Madison and William had passed away and Rory was married off to a CEO. Cris and Lily were old now and were filled with shame and guilt. He finally forgave them as to sin is human but to forgive and forget is divine. Rory had left for UK with her husband. So, Kai took his uncle Cris and his aunt Lily along with him to his house. Just like this, they grew older in Kai’s house where they were a reformed version of themselves and loved their children a lot. And this was how Kai’s family completed.
author: bindu Cristy

title: A Special Gift
text: Hmm… What should I buy for my sister’s first birthday? Candies? A plushie? Yes! That’s a great idea! I decided to go and look in the toy store. I took out all the money I had been saving in my desk drawer, and headed out. It was a dull, cloudy day. The weather forecast said that it would rain soon. I couldn’t find anything that might be a good present for my sister at the store. As I headed to the exit, I felt as if someone was watching me. Feeling a bit scared, I looked around and saw a cute teddy bear. It was so adorable and cuddly that I was sure my sister would love it. The teddy bear seemed so real that I could imagine it moving. I glanced at the price. Yippee! I could pay for it! I lifted the bear carefully from the shelf, and took it to the cashier. The lady looked at it with a frown and said, “I’m sorry dear, but this toy is reserved.” I sadly took the bear back to its original position. But I still wanted to gift it to my sister. I looked around, not a soul in sight. Without thinking twice, I quickly grabbed the bear and shoved it into my bag. I burst out of the shop. It was raining already. When I reached home, I opened my bag to check if the bear was still dry, only to find the bear shouting, "Hey! Hey! Oliver!" "Aaaaaaaaahhhhhhhhhh!" "Don't scream! I'm the bear that you stole from the shop!" "...How come you can talk?" "I don't know! Don’t ask me! But I have something very important to tell you! Right now!” "...What is it?" "Actually, tomorrow, I am supposed to be a present for a girl," the bear said. “That’s why I was reserved.” The bear looked me straight in the eye. “Oliver, please stop this. I appreciate your love for your sister, but what about other people's feelings? Would you truly be happy giving your sister a stolen gift? We should go back to the store." I was speechless, I just stared at the bear, and nodded. Then I heard my mom knocking at my door. "Oliver? Are you there?" "Mom?" I looked down and saw an ordinary teddy bear smiling up at me from inside my bag. It didn’t utter a word, leave aside a twitch. "You’re soaking wet! Do you want some hot cocoa?" my mom asked. "No… no, thanks! I need to go to the toy store! Right now!!" I said and zipped my bag. “Oliver? It’s still raining! Go back tomorrow!” called my mom, but I shouted back, “It’s urgent!” and dived into the pouring rain. I ran all the way back to the store, which was just about to close. I rushed in, panting, and went straight to the cashier. The woman looked surprised at my entry, but quickly smiled warmly at me and asked, "How can I help you, young man?” "Actually, I… s… stole this teddy bear earlier today to give it as a present to my baby sister," I explained hesitantly. I thought she would scold me but she didn't. "Hmm… Thank you for telling me,” said the lady, smiling gently. But then she dropped her smile and added, "it is very kind of you to think so fondly of your little sister. But you know you should not steal." "...Yes" "Can you hand me the bear, please?” she asked. I handed the bear, still smiling blankly ahead, to the woman who said, “I can't give this to you. But you can buy something else. The store is open just for you now.” I chose a regular stuffed bunny, took it to the cashier who kindly wrapped it in pink paper. When I headed out of the store, the rain had strangely stopped. Next day, my parents went shopping. “Oliver, I want you to keep an eye on your sister. We will come back soon!” said my mom. When my parents came back, they were carrying a package wrapped exactly in the same pink wrapping paper as the one around the bunny I had bought. We opened the package excitedly and to my surprise, there was the bear! Suddenly, everything fell into place. My parents were the people who had reserved the bear, and the ‘girl’ the bear was talking about was my sister! I looked at the bear in my sister’s hands. It might have been my imagination, but I could swear that the bear winked at me. Not even once since my sister’s first birthday, I saw the teddy bear move ever again.

title: Droplets of Happiness
text: Once in a city named Atlances,there lived a little girl named Riana. She is a silent, little girl with short hair, chubby cheeks and freckles.She lives alone with her father as unfortunately her mother '' Maria'' passed away in a car accident.She and her father lives a tiny cottage where she is provided with a own room for herself which has an old table, old bed,old book shelf and a window where she spends most of her time watching and talking to the rain.The sound of the rain that went '' drip drop'' reminds her the lullaby her mother used to sing when she was just a year old.Rain brings smile to people's face' helps the people in need and is always pure which reminds her mother while talking to the rain Her father however is often worried about her because she never connects to people except him and the rain.She doesn't have someone who she can call a friend at her school or near her house. She goes to school, sits silently in her place, comes back home, does her homework and goes to sleep,she never really plays outside with her friends like the other children. It was one fine morning and she got up five in the morning hoping to see some rain but to her disappointment it was a sunny and hot day so she prepared to go to school, had her favourite breakfast 'pancakes 'and her father walked her to school.When her school arrived, her father waved and said ''have a good day honey and try to get a friend atleast today'', as usual she nodded her head but well knew that wouldn't happen because even if she tried to talk to her classmates, they would get away from her and start gossiping saying her as 'weird, 'dumb' and so on. Today their teacher, miss Catherine made an announcement saying that there was a science expo to be conducted and so asked her students to pair up, and as usual Riana was left alone. '' riana is left alone does anyone want to pair up with her? '' asked her teacher, as usual there was a silence for a minute and in the next second they started making some weird noise that made her feel so embarrassed and sad,tears started rolling down her eyes when suddenly the rain started drizzling ' Drip Drop ', as if it came to console her. The bell rang at 3'o clock' she took her bag, greeted her teacher and started walking on her way back home. While she was walking on her street she found something unusual, at the park near her home, she found a little girl seemed just as about her age,dancing and playing in the rain. From distance she could see that she a had long straight hair with a cute ribbon on and Riana felt some unusual connect with her Riana slowly walked towards the girl with a lot of hesitation but managed to push herself and talk to her. She stuttered at first but introduced herself saying that her name was Riana and asked the girl's name but, the girl replied saying she likes the name Pinky and so can call her by that name if she wanted. Even though Riana was confused by her answer she started playing with her as she was the nicest girl she has ever met Both the girls played a lot in the rain and Riana had the best day she had ever had in her life, and their meeting in the park continued for months. '' Since we're best friends,can you now atleast tell me your name? '' asked Riana, '' mm i would love if you call me by the name Pinky although its not my real name '',replied the girl. Riana wasn't satisfied with her answer but yet continued to call her by the name pinky and usually brings Pinky to her home after playing. Days passed and news spread that Pinky was actually an orphan and an young couple adopted her the last year but it seemed that they were too busy for taking care of her and have planned on returning pinky to the orphanage from where she was adopted. when Riana heard this news,she ran as fast as she can without her slippers to find pinky.After few hours she found Pinky in the park and hugged her tightly, she held her hands and ran towards her father and pleaded him asking whether Pinky can stay with them. Father thought about this and talked to pinky's adopted parents and to the orphanage about this. soon the papers where pinky was to come and live in Riana 's house forever were getting ready, and the day arrived where Pinky was to enter Riana's house. Both the girls were standing in tears. As soon as Riana 's father called her in,she ran towards Riana and hugged her tightly and whispered into her little ears saying that her real name is ''Maria''.

title: Inari
text: A long and in a faraway mountain, a mild yet a long-drawn-out yawn echoed with a subsequent sound of a fall and cry. It turned out that a 7-year-old child with azure blue hair and pitch-black pupil was crying her eyes out on the floor with a big lump on her head. An old man who was in his 70s, soon came to pick the girl up and quieten her up he said, "Oh was our little princess startled", it turned our little princess startled", it turned out that he was her grandfather who was a hill person (a person who live in the rugged land) named Ishiki Shasha and liked to live alone in the woods but this time he had his granddaughter accompanying him this spring because of her parents being busy. Ishiki Shasha also called old man Ishiki lovingly by other, he lived in a fairly higher place even in the village, he worked as a hunter and was more energetic then most his age. He had golden pupils and smooth voice. Being in an unfamiliar place, the girl had bumped her head by falling off the bed. The old man, after calming his granddaughter, took her for breakfast and then the bath. After freshening up the little girl was full of energy. She played in the snow for hours but reluctantly went back. While coming back the grandfather was shocked to see a Vulpes lagopus (a white fox) in the little girl's hand. the old man did not want to raise a wild fox but could not help but 'yes' after seeing the twinkling eyes of his granddaughter. A week had passed by since then the fox had started to open up and no longer felt as a threat to his precious little girl so he, so he welcomed the furry creature in the house and told his granddaughter to name it and officially accepted in the family. the fox was named Celtic Shasha, Cel for shote by the little girl named Celtica Shasha. This was the new beginning of a new journey

title: The Old Man and The Little Angels
text: Once upon a time, there was a girl named Samanvi. She shifted to Delhi with her parents due to transfer of her father. She was new to the place. However, she managed to make some friends in her street. Her friends were Paras, Radhika, Ankita and Umair. They often used to play on streets in the evening. Cycling, screaming, shouting, and playing football and gilli danda were their favourite activities and games. Their parents often used to instruct them not to shout or make noise in streets as it created disturbance to other residents. One day while they were playing football, their ball fell inside the lawn of an old man. They waited for him to return their ball but he did not return. The old man often used to give angry looks at them when they used to play in front of his house. Again, on a sunny day when the children were playing gilli danda, their gilli fell inside the lawn of the same old man but again there was no response from him. With a lot of courage, one evening the five of them jumped over the wall. They wanted to get their items back. Listening to the noises, the old man came out and stared at them. " He looks angry", said Paras. "Idiot!", Samanvi whispered. They all ran back as they were little bit scared. From that day they stopped playing in front of the old man's house. One day the children saw a doctor entering the old man's house. They got excited and started peeping into the house from the window. They listened that doctor was wishing "Happy Birthday" to the old man. When the doctor came out children were eager to know that what happened to the old man. Doctor told them that the old man had nobody to look after. He had no friends who could make his day special. "Oh! so he doesn't have friends who could gift him a card?" Samanvi wondered. "Imagine, no one in the street wished him for his birthday. How sad!" Ankita said. "Why don't we make his day special by celebrating his birthday?" said Umair. "Yes, we can wish him." Radhika replied. " I also want to do the same. But if he shouted at us then?", Samanvi asked. "Nothing like this will happen. Let us create a beautiful card for him," said Ankita. "Good idea!" Paras replied. "We will give it the shape of a football and also draw a gilli on it." Samanvi said "No! this is not fair, replied Umair. Everyone was so cheerful and excited. They decided to make a card at Samanvi's house. Her parents did not care if they made a mess in the room. But all they had to do was to collect money from their piggy banks for buying the material required for making of card. When they had bought the material, they chose a beautiful birthday card from Google. The room had become a mess with papers and cuttings of decorative items. "Wow! It's so beautiful", Samanvi's mom said. The children packed the card in a beautiful envelope. They walked down the road. Everyone was nervous. What if he did not accept the card? "Yes, we can wish him." Radhika replied. " I also want to do the same. But if he shouted at us then?", Samanvi asked. "Nothing like this will happen. Let us create a beautiful card for him," said Ankita. "Good idea!" Paras replied. "We will give it the shape of a football and also draw a gilli on it." Samanvi said "No! this is not fair, replied Umair. Everyone was so cheerful and excited. They decided to make a card at Samanvi's house. Her parents did not care if they made a mess in the room. But all they had to do was to collect money from their piggy banks for buying the material required for making of card. When they had bought the material, they chose a beautiful birthday card from Google. The room had become a mess with papers and cuttings of decorative items. "Wow! It's so beautiful", Samanvi's mom said. The children packed the card in a beautiful envelope. They walked down the road. Everyone was nervous. What if he did not accept the card? They knocked the door and waited for the old man to come outside. He appeared at the gate. "What's it?," he asked them sharply. "HAPPY BIRTHDAY UNCLE!", they all said together. He opened the gate and let them in. They looked around the lawn. Their football and gilli were lying down there. The children sat on bed. The old man went to kitchen and bought neembu pani and sweets for children. With a lumped throat he said, "Thank you my little angels for making my day special." The old man said, " You can take your football and gilli from the lawn. " From then, the old man watched his little friends playing in front of his house. He also enjoyed with them. Finally, he was not alone. He had got the "LITTLE ANGELS" sent by God for him. Moral of the story is: " We should promote fraternity and love in this world. Only love can bind us together forever."
author: samanvi Gupta
