title: Light In The Shadows
text: Annie had a party with her friends. " Ron, I'm leaving, laters gators...". " Sissy, why don't you take me with you? I feel scared" cries, Ron. " Bro...come on, we've been in this home for over a month. Why do you get scared all of a sudden? Don't try to make fools of me. The party is only arranged for our classmates. Even if you come there, you'll have to starve to death. So... take care, will reach home by tomorrow morning" saying this, she waved bye to her brother. Ron walks to his room upstairs, his footsteps saying ' tup, tup '. ﻿ /2010 He started reading his favorite book ‘ The Ghost Of The Well ’ which he found near the backdoor when they moved into this house. He got deeply immersed in it that he was completely unaware of the reality. He heard someone calling his name in a creepy, low-pitched voice. He did not care or scare either. Instead, he walked downstairs reading the book towards the backdoor. He kept on ignoring everything around him with each word he read. ‘ Creak ’, he opened the old, rusty backdoor and found himself near a haunted well. He didn’t know what he was doing. He slowly went near the well staring at the book. ‘Hundreds of snakes were slithering and hissing his name in and around the well’ spoke a raucous voice suddenly from the book. Ron now stepped out of his imaginary world and became alert. “Wait, what was it?” he asked himself. Then… ‘BOOH!’ came a pair of eyes from the book. Ron screamed and fell into the well along with his book and his death remained a mystery forever... Many months passed and Annie shifted to a new house on Bitterston street. She lived in guilt every day thinking she was responsible for her beloved little brother’s death. After her brother’s death, she lived with her grandma who was also paying for her high school. Unable to bear her grandmother’s words about Ron’s death, she moved into a new house and worked part-time. In her new school, she spent time alone because she thought going to a party with her friends was the reason for Ron’s death. Annie was fed up with making friends anymore. But still, there was someone who cared about her. 2011 One evening, she was walking in the streets and was about to slip and fall when a pulling force took over her. She stood up steadily and turned back to look who it was. She found nothing, just an empty street with a few crows cawing. She was puzzled. That night, when she was walking down to her home after work, she heard a voice similar to Ron’s. She stood frozen for a moment and wondered if it was a ghost. “ Hey, sissy…look here, here ” someone called her out. She turned everywhere but found nobody, just a voice. “ Look down to your shadow, ” said a black figure with a pair of eyes and a mouth. “ Aaahh… ” screamed Annie. “ Who the hell are you? ” she yelled. /2011 “ Sissy, it’s me, your Ron ” the mouth appeared to move with a sound. “ Hey, Ron…how, how come this happens? ” she asked with a staggering voice. “ Don’t worry, Annie. I’ll be staying with you here for a month. I’ve sent a leave letter asking for my Shaktis to my Lord. Jesus, may there be no grammatical errors… I fear no man, but the grammar, oh gosh…it scares me. ” said the figure in a euphonious voice. The girl shed tears of joy, jumping, and screaming. Ron went along with her wherever she went hidden in her shadow. They became even closer than before when he was alive. They talked and talked all day long. The people in the streets thought she was kinda lunatic or something else. Her classmates and teacher found her acting unusual; they saw her smiling for the first time... After a heavy dinner, she was rambling in the garden and chatting with Ron. “ Sissy, have you ever wondered what people become after they die ” questioned Ron. “ Mm…I guess they turn into ghosts ” she answered. “ Well, so close to that but ghosts aren’t real, they are just an illusion. Dead people get hidden in the shadows of their loved ones. Only if they can activate their Shaktis, they will be able to speak with humans like me. ” He explained. “ Then what about Pennywise, Bloody Mary, Annabelle, and Veronica? Are they all fake? ” she doubted. “ Bitter but that’s the truth ” Ron convinced her. Their conversation grew deeper and deeper over time. By midnight, Annie fell asleep on the garden bench under the shimmering white light of the moon. “ Caw, Caw …” came a crow carrying a small paper roll. Annie didn’t respond so the bird dropped it on the corner of the bench and flew back. The next morning, Annie went to school and the roll was left unseen. /2011 EVENING After a heavy dinner, she was rambling in the garden and chatting with Ron. “ Sissy, have you ever wondered what people become after they die ” questioned Ron. “ Mm…I guess they turn into ghosts ” she answered. “ Well, so close to that but ghosts aren’t real, they are just an illusion. Only if they can activate their Shaktis, they will be able to speak with humans like me. ” He explained. “ Then what about Pennywise, Bloody Mary, Annabelle, and Veronica? Are they all fake? ” she doubted. “ Bitter but that’s the truth ” Ron convinced her. Their conversation grew deeper and deeper over time. Annie didn’t respond so the bird dropped it on the corner of the bench and flew back. The next morning, Annie went to school and the roll was left unseen During the first hour, she got her ‘ period ’ unexpectedly. She felt cramps and started acting strange. Everyone was looking at her now, she seemed to be uncomfortable. She went to the restroom to check for stains. When she returned, she found a sanitary napkin under her table written ‘ Your Friend ’ on it. She was dumbstruck. That day was a half-working day at school, so she returned home by 12pm. /2011 MORNING Annie was walking down the road feeling worried, and was the reason? Any guesses? Just check the time. Its mid-noon and the sun was right above her head and her shadow disappeared. She missed Ron. My sincere apologies to physics haters! As she crossed the road, she kept on pondering about the magical napkin unaware of the car that was coming towards her with a loud beep horn. A young boy with a mask on his face came running, pulled her aside, and vanished in just a few seconds. Annie called him. “ Excuse me…thanks for saving me, may I know who you are?” The boy just replied ‘ Your Friend ’ without turning back and went. /2011 NOON That night, she was walking in a dark alley chatting with her shadow. There was nobody around them as far as they could see. The only sound was that of the cool breeze and the ‘bat clicks’. “ Wait.. something is happening to me, I feel a magnetic field around this area. I guess it’s the ship of my Lord…Gosh! he is taking my powers back… ” shrieked Ron. “ But didn’t your promise me that you’ll stay here for a month? It’s not even been a week…how can you leave me like that? please don’t… ” Annie begged /2011 EVENING A spotlight fell on her shadow and Ron’s Shaktis were taken back by the ship. Now Ron was merely an ordinary shadow of Annie just like others’. Annie fell to the ground and cried so hard tearing her throat. She felt as if she was trapped in a maze, poor little thing… NOW HAPPENS SOMETHING… She heard loud footsteps advancing toward her with a familiar scent. “ Who are you? ” she asked in a weak and frightened voice. ‘ Your Friend ’ answered a familiar low-pitched voice. “ Your friend? The sanitary napkin…my life savior, isn’t it you? ” Annie asked. “ Well, I’m happy that you came to know about me making my speech easier. And your shadow…sorry, your little brother told me everything about the past. Annie…Still don’t you recognize me? ” he asked getting closer to her. Annie had a good sense of smell and this scent seemed so familiar. “ Oh! Chris, is it you? Long time no see ” she said in a bittersweet tone. Chris’ eyes started tearing up. “ Hey, come on Chris…at this scenario, you should be comforting me, but see what’s happening…cheer up bro ” she convinced Chris. “ You know what? I’ve been living with the same guilt that you have had. I should have also invited your brother to the Halloween party, and I’m not worthy enough even to apologize to you ” sobbed Chris. “I’ve always wanted to apologize and become friends with you again, so I followed you everywhere. Your brother noticed me and understood my intention although you didn’t so he talked to me when you were asleep. I also made a promise to your brother that we will never part ways again.” he said. Annie said “So let’s not break our little brother’s trust dear elder brother” and hugged her old but new friend tightly. Chris visited Annie’s home often and looked after her. He, as a scientist friend, bought many gadgets and devices to pull her away from the ROOM OF SOLITUDE. But still, she tries to remain in her old state of living. Hope he invents a new device to bring back Ron too... He also brought her a new pet dog and named it ‘ Draky ’. One bright morning, when Annie and Chris were watering the plants in her garden, Chris found a paper roll near the bench. “ Hey, fool...what’s in this paper roll? Any recipe for your new ‘out of the world’ dish? ” roasted Chris sarcastically. “ Hey, just starve if you don’t like my food. By the way, I’m not sure what it is.” Annie replied. Chris opened it and the letter went like this: /2011 Day: Pizza day Dear Shadow No.1465432957, GREETINGS! Hope you are doing well. As you have committed 3 grammatical mistakes in your requisition letter, as per Article No.92 in the Shady Land Constitution, we forbid you to use your Shaktis on Earth. We’ll be taking your powers back by the Doughnut Day. Get ready...Have a good time until that. ~ Lord of Shadows “ I didn’t know my brother took English this lightly in his school ”. Chris and Annie giggled and laughed till their stomach ached with drops of happy tears that showed their love for Ron. And YES, they were heartsick for their dear little brother who is unknown units of distance away from them…Let's see when Ron learns English well and gives a rambunctious return! My sincere advice: Never skip English classes ~ Ron

title: A Helping Hand
text: A Helping Hand Once there was a rich family. The family consists of father, mother and a son named Rahul. Rahul helps everyone and after so many years, he got married. The name of his son was Mohan. But he doesn’t like to help everyone. Rahul wrote a letter to his son to understand the importance of helping others. One day I was going to my friend’s house. On the way I saw an old man who was lying on the bench near by the road. I said to my driver to stop the car. I asked to the old man “Why are you lying here?” After a few minutes he slowly woke up and he started narrating the whole story. He said that “He had four sons but his four sons drove him away from his house. But he had raised them without any hunger, he had brought them whatever they ask and he made them study whatever they ask and he made them study whatever they wished to but they forgot the mercy and they had drove him away from his house.” Listening to this story I started crying. Then I said to the old man that “ I will take care of him.” The old man replied that “ My sons itself drove me away then why should you get into trouble for keeping me at your home.” I explained that I don’t have grandparents and have always longed for their love. However I convinced him. He too accepted to come with me. I took him to my home. I introduced him to my parents. They both were happy on seeing him. My father said that “His father died, so he will take care of him thinking of him as his own father.” My mother said that “She will take care of the old man with great love.” Therefore we four lived happily. Through this incident I would like to say that we should always help others. Do you know the importance of helping others. Let me tell you. Helping others improves social interaction, distracts people from their own problems and improves self-esteem and competence. Physical Well- Being helping others leads to increased social integration which allows people to lead more active lifestyle. It helps us to feel good about ourselves and it helps us to connect with others. When we help others we feel like we are a part of something bigger than ourselves and this will make us feel good. Helping others also gives us a sense of purpose, and it helps us to feel needed and appreciated. Helping others is the greatest quality of a human being. There are several ways and numerous styles to aid people who are in need of help. It costs nothing but the person who receives it, gets everything. If you help somebody surely someone will help you. We should at least try our best to help someone. Great people like heroes, scientist and so many people become famous through not only gaining knowledge about their field but also by helping others. Everyone should help each other. This means not helping for bad cause but to help for good cause and people who really need our help. Helping is a quality that everyone should possess. Helping others really gives us happiness and contentment. Helping others means helping about studies, social works and sometimes of you can help innovation way. Everyone makes mistakes we must help them to recover from their mistakes. These are the messages I wanted to convey to you my dear son. I hope you will follow these things in your life. Well wishes Your father After reading this letter, Mohan realised the importance of helping others and the helping tendency of his father. His outlook on life changed and he acted as a helping hand for many years wherever, whenever possible.

title: The Old Ceramic Plate
text: Once in a village in India, three young children were adopted by an old lady, Urmila, from an orphanage. The kids called Urmila, ‘Amma’. She sent two of them, Shruti and Deepak, to school and dressed them in good clothes. However, the third little boy, Shantanu, was blind, and she treated him as a servant. She thought he was of no good and kept him out of pity. She dressed him in old, ragged clothes and fed him the leftover food. Shantanu wasn’t sent to school and ran errands for Amma. One day, Amma sent Shantanu to bring some vegetables. On his way back, he met an old man, who tried to help him. The old man asked Shantanu “How can your mother let you come alone?” Shantanu replied “Don’t worry, I’m used to it. Moreover, I only do most of the household chores.” The old man was astonished to hear such an answer. He said “Oh! It must be very difficult. Don’t you have a problem with doing hard labour all day?” Shantanu smiled and said, “It is sometimes troublesome but I am sure that one day my mother will realize that I am not worthless and I too can be very useful like my siblings.” The old man smiled and walked away after helping Shantanu on his way back home. One night, when a deadly fire broke out in the room where they stored food, Shruti and Deepak ran out of the house to escape the fire. Shantanu risked his life and went inside to help Amma escape the fire. He carried her on his back and saved her. Seeing how brave and selfless Shantanu was despite his blindness and ill-treatment, Amma gave him an old ceramic plate that could grant wishes before her last breath. She told him that the ceramic plate could grant one wish a year, two wishes every two, and three wishes every three years. She also said that all the wishes would be revoked if the ceramic plate broke. So, she told him to wish wisely. When Shantanu wished for his vision to see Amma one last time before burying her, the plate granted him the same. Shruti and Deepak soon got to know about the ceramic plate. The two children wished for a house, food, and good grades in school without studying. After three years, it was time to make wishes again. While Shruti and Deepak wished for houses and gold, Shantanu wished for a library loaded with books. Every three years, they continued to want mansions, gold, spouses, sons, and high-rank offices in the village, without working for any of it. On the contrary, Shantanu wished for more books to replace his old ones and went on to read them. He gathered a lot of knowledge over nine years. Years later, when all the three siblings came together to make wishes yet again, Shruti and Deepak asked Shantanu “Why do you keep wishing for more and more books? What good are these books? Why don’t you wish for wealth like us? We’re so successful without even working hard and you, on the other hand, are still stuck in the same situation reading books as if they will help you to get rich!” Shantanu replied, “You think that these things will help you but in the long run knowledge and development is much more important than materialistic wealth.” They started laughing at such a silly thought and said, “Well, then see for yourself who will be better off 10 years from now.” And went on to ask for more money from the ceramic plate. After nine years, when they came together again to make wishes from the ceramic plate, Shruti and Deepak wanted to keep the plate to themselves. They did not want to share their wishes with anyone else and wanted to grow richer as soon as possible. During their fight, they tried to grab the plate and accidentally dropped it. Immediately, Shantanu lost his vision, and the other two lost all their possessions. Shruti and Deepak learned the lesson of their stupidity and greed and their wealth was gone as none of them worked for it and asked the plate for everything. However, Shantanu did not lose the knowledge he gained from the books, and he was known to be among the wisest people in the village. Even though the old ceramic plate lost its magic, Shantanu glued its broken pieces and kept it on his desk as a memory of an unforgettable life lesson.

title: My dad is DEAD
text: "Sabina come soon", called my dad for dinner. While I'm lost in my imagination, peering at the backyard. After some minutes. ''Sabina, what's wrong with you", bellowed Alexander, my dad. "Oh, Sorry dad, I'm coming" "Dad where are you going today?...um...tight schedule?" I got no reply from him as he was so engrossed having his dinner. Alexander is not a tiny man or someone we can make fun of. his eyes were large more like a murderous eyes with hefty shoulders. he's working as the CEO of AMP Technology company. Yes we are not lacking of anything, but just that I feel like I need more love and care. He usually go for work at 7 AM and back at 8:30 PM. Sometimes he did not even return. Dad stood up suddenly, cleaned himself up, and said 'Bye', and he went for office. The house feels so empty and miss my mother's presence and everything about her. Her name is Screna. She passed away five months ago. She was a doctor, a cardiologist. She is indeed a caring and kind loving woman. I'm sure, I indeed have a great memories and contented life when she was present and always stays besides me. She left me without a word. "Oli..umm...sorry I'm not feeling well today you go ahead, have fun". "What! Hey bud, atleast open the door. Let's talk, What's your problem. Do you need help?" "No..No..No.. I'm fine, I need rest and I don't wanna be out of my bed..Olie. Good day ahead" "Ok then...whatever...Bye. " She went and indolently I lay in my bed. I collect some of my dirty vest for washing and make myself busy with something in my room. Unexpectedly I saw my mom's blazer which she like the most among all. I became plaintive again and I decided to keep it in her room.I went up and noticed that dad's room is full of papers scattered around.I clean up abit and out of nowhwere I saw a picture. It's a woman picture. She is pretty,her smile is perfect,peering the picture I was indignant.But I don't take it seriously and keep going with my work again.I keep my mom balzer in the closet and went back to my room again. "My smile lost in some where I wish you were here by my side Someone take me home Someone take me home" I whispers the sing emotionally. Dad's back and he said "Sabi, I already ate at restuarant.You prepare for yourself ". '' Uh.... dad but.... Before I could say a word he shut his doors. I never see him talking to me with ecstatic ever since my mom left us. He is boors,agression and always in a bad mood.What can I do? He don't cooperate with me anyway. '' I won't eat today, I'm full today'' I whisper and went back to my room again. As I lay down,I heard a very weird laughing voice from dad's room.I heard it about four times and then I frantically went and knock his doors. Dad what's wrong are you okay? Oh,Sabina i'm okay don't worry I just read something funny.Go to bed,good night. Ok dad good night.I love you dad. Dad's room is rustling the whole night which I couldn't cease my eyes so easily. I woke up earlier then usual and make light breakfast.Dad,dad? I shouted. Dad's off to work?.. Why so early. It's just 5:am,trifle fret,but I say to myself that it's not a big problem and I go to school. It's a bright sunny day,everyone looks great and happy with their life. Christ College situated at Osaka,I'm in 12 grade under science stream.I wanted to become a cardialogist like my mom. Olivia and I were in the same stream,we indeed enjoy and have fun in the colledge. "Sabina,let's have dinner tonight, My treat.'' "Oh! Ok sure that's perfect thank you '' I smile. We agreed to meet at 7:pm at Day and Night caffe and went on our separates way. I call up my dad and ask for the night out. I dress decently and went,we met.She ordered food to eat.I went to washroom alone and when I'm about to heed back someone pull my hand and said "Don't scream '' sofetly to my ear. Hearing his voice and heartbeats I can say that he's not ok. I turn away to see him.His eyes were blue,His black hair, his suits were perfect. But he's in pain,His left arms were bleeding continously and I can feel his scourge.I took out my handkerchief and tied to it immediately so,it could somehow stop it.He said thank you look around and disappear. There's four miss call from Olivia, I rush and went to her. ''Sorry Oli,something happen so '' Olivia is showing her long face and say's I'm full. I apologize again and I said ''Oli simon loves you'' As i said Oli started blushing and laughing.Whenever she's angry I would tease her using simon's name.Simon is our class topper and Oli has a crush on him. We are good again. She pays the bill and we went back. ''Bye Oli'' ''Bye ''. As I knock the door,a woman open the doors,the woman whom I saw in my dad's table. ''Oh! you are........ ummm... I'mm...... ''She is my co CEO.Good friend of me ''.Dad reply. I see,have fun then.Saying this I went to my room and I noticed that Dad's looking weird and getting closer with his friend.Seeing this I'm broken deep down. ''Bye Alex'' ''Bye ''. I went to my dad and said ''Dad why do you bring her in our home? Do she need something,why are you two so closed? ''Sabina,mind your own work.'' He shut his door making a loud noice. I feel like I'm nothing to my dad. Each night passed by missing mom terribly. In my dream I saw my mom weeping terribly and saying ''Dear take care of yourself,I'm worried U'll get hurt.Trust him he is meant for you.'' I feel like something presentiment is going to happen.I'm lost in mom's words,why did she say I might get hurt,who am I gonna trust? I had no idea. Then,the next day my dad went to office again and I went to dad's room to see the woman pic as I was so insecure.I found that mom's blazer was no more.I search to and fro but I couldn't find it.Not long Rebecca come in,Rebecca is my mom's best friend. ''Oh nanny Rebec what's up?'' ''Dear Sabi,I wanted to say something but I'm afraid that I might hurt you so I have been keeping this for many months and I think today is the day. Sabi,are you not curious about your mom's dead? I became suddenly alert after hearing this.''Nanny Rebec what are you talking about?Can you explain?''I asked fretly. Screna noticed that her husband is very closed with the woman and also heard unfair about them.Unfortunately she saw the woman in Alexander room.Screna scream out loundly and cried out saying ''Hon you yourself did this to me '' Alexander come and strangle her to death after strangling her she lay her on the bed,while on the other hand the woman stay there smiling.So,Sabi this is the secret I have been hiding.The real case is that, the murderer is your father himself,he is a playboy.''Nanny Rebec sobbed helplessly. Hearing this I'm completely feel with unutterable concepts in my mind.I'm lost again. And now I realized why my dad never likes me after the absence of my mom. Now I know who really is the woman. ''why dad?why?'' Am I still worth living?What is the propose of my life?Mom I miss you.... I cried. I keep asking many question to myself. Nanny Rebec tried consoling me but it wasn't working.She went. I cried continously.I decided not to live together with my dad again.Now I no one except my friend Olivia. And I run weepingly to Olivia house and tell about the strange things.I made an earth saking decision that I would now on stay with her.My eyes were all swallowed and I'm completey famish.I did't eat for three days,not even a single mouth.I'm eagerly waiting for my happy ending and besides dad never come for searching me. ''Oh! dad's happy without me. ''I whisper. Olivia took me to the green park to freshened my mind. The universe guide us back again like fate must have met.I saw this guy who is very familiar. ''Hi,It's me again'' ''Sorry you are.......'' ''Oh! I'm the man who who help me on the washroom.Do you remember?''He asked. Then,I realized.Seeing his blue eyes,perfect smile and his handsomeness makes me fall, we talk and bacame friend.I asked his name ''Felix''he said. ''wow perfect'' I wisper. Being with him was indeed the best,after being lost I feel like I'm now found again.I finally get to wear my real smile after all. It's unbelievable that he is also interested in me.He persuaded me. I don't know what am I gonna do or what reply should I give. Looking at me I feel like I'm being adopted,ugly which will brings problem. I refused him. Yes,I do have feelings for him but he's not my stage.That was what I thought. Plaintively I turn back and within a minute Felix grab my hand,pull me and said ''Sabi trust me.'' title: Brinda With Grandma
text: It was a sunny evening at Brinda’s house. Brinda is a cute little girl and had a mother named Swetha and a grandma in a village. Her grandma’s name is Laxmi and she is very kind and caring. She has many animals in her farm and Brinda loves them. Brinda always waits for Summer holidays to go to their grandma’s house. She likes to hear stories from her grandma. Not long after her holidays were declared, Brinda packed her bag and was getting ready to go to their Grandma’s house. Brinda’s mother Swetha and Brinda started off at their grandma’s house at 8:00AM. Brinda took a small nap as it took them 5 hours to get to their grandma’s house. Brinda was very excited and was tired. As soon as Brinda got down the bus she ran towards her grandma and gave a toy chick to play with. Grandma jumped out of happiness and hugged her granddaughter. After a long time, Brinda was happily having her dinner with her grandma. Brinda was eagerly waiting for Laxmi to come and tell her a real story. Brinda shouts, “Am'mam'ma”. Laxmi started to tell her childhood story. Once upon a time I was returning from play and I saw a beautiful bird on a tree. I was an expert in climbing trees when I was 5 years old. I started to climb the tree with a frisson. When I was about to catch the bird an animal also joined to attack the bird. Ps s s s s s Ps s s s s s comes the dangerous and threatening wild snake with anger. I shouted for help but the snake was not allowing me to and it made a sound like Pssss Psssss Psssss. HELP HELP HELP HELP After some time, the villagers were trying to save me using a rope, ladder etc etc but the snake was furious and fuming and it was refusing them. Soon the bird was tensed and the bird flew away. The snake was looking at the bird flying and intelligently I jumped down the tree. Life is full of risks and you should always be strong to face any challenge that comes up. Brinda and grandma were spending time together joyfully. After a few days, Brinda and her mother packed themselves to get back to their house. On top of this, Grandma packed GOL GOL Ladoos, CRISPY CRISPY Mixture and TASTY TASTY Mango pickle and mein of the food items which Brinda loves. Grandma felt sad as they were leaving very soon. But to grandma’s surprise, Swetha and Brinda gave grandma a mobile phone so that they can always be in touch with each other. Soon after a few days when Brinda's school reopened she told how she spent her time with her grandmother in the village. Everyday after Brinda is back from her school she calls her grandma and speaks about whatever happened in her school. Days were happily going on…..

title: Finding A Friend
text: Bengal, before partition was a richly cultured state. It showed diversity in all forms, be it in religion, culture, or practices. In spite of the differences, different societies embraced each other. In such a harmonic society, lived 3 friends- Ashutosh, Armaan and Durga. Close friends since childhood, they still shared a bond, long after, now well into their teenage. But, teenage is also a period of mental turmoil, a time when the body releases societal notions and tries to create its own way of life. The way of life sometimes creates paths to disaster as well as discovery. But, these friends had other things to worry about. Rather than turmoil in their minds, political turmoil was what they had to experience. Such a topic is alien for children. But, a situation so great cannot be unseen. The partition had left the great state of Bengal in tatters. People were scurrying from both sides of the borders to either state. West Bengal was left in India, while East Pakistan was created as a state for the Muslims. After, a long time, the friends had felt alone even in each other's company. Soon, a rumour of a little thief overexaggerated as a ' Devil child', was spreading in their community. The children were set for an adventure, to bring back fun and wonder in their life through this 'Devil Child'. Durga, mastermind of this operation, along with her friends, devised a plan. They started searching in their allotted directions and, at night, they would search together to "Protect them from the dark" suggested by Ashutosh due to his obvious fear of the dark. Armaan is a very calm and versatile young person who was guiding them through the dark. They were, but, searching aimlessly, navigating through the dense village. Ashutosh was well aware of his shortcomings, but, his eyesight was much sharper than others, thanks to his extreme concentration. Perhaps it was this ability of his, that along with the path laid down by Durga and navigated by Armaan, helped them to finally be able to catch the little 'Devil'. As it turns out, the little thief was nothing similar to his descriptions. It was in reality, a weak little boy searching for food in the lawn They were shocked to see the little boy. Durga asked: "What are you doing here all alone?" The boy replied feebly: "I.... wa... was j... just..." Before he could say anything, Armaan asked: "Where are your parents?" The boy replied hesitantly, on the verge of crying: "I.. Don't... know." The friends consoled him. they took him to Ashutosh's house. They gave him some food. He was feeling a little better and confessed that he tried to steal food from his house as well due to hunger. But, Ashutosh forgave him and so did the people gathered there when they found out the 'Devil' was caught. Durga concluded that he must have lost his parents to the violence evolved in the partition and was orphaned. Feeling pity, they tried to understand his situation and help him in whatever way possible. They soon got to know about him well and befriended him. A smile rose upon his face and his lost soul found a path to traverse. His name was Bejoy but, he was given the nickname Bejju out of love by his friends 'Bejju' was elated and was finally feeling happiness. Though, he always missed his parents, his friends and the new family of theirs would try to fill that gap. He felt that God has sent his friends straight from heaven, as the angels who resurrected from his extreme sorrow have made a special part for themselves in his lives. Now the group of '4' friends never felt alone and would go on to support their combined lives as ' 4 ' strong pillars would a ' Palace Of Wonders', the exact synonym to the lives of discovery, for the 4 friends. THE END
author: Sathvik Narayanan

title: The greatest Reunification
text: A two months old dog, lost in the streets of Denver finding food and her mother.Harry a sixteen year old boy, walking back to school found a little puppy sniffing his leg.He found the dog very cute and held it in his hands. He wanted to play with the dog so he rushed to the park with the puppy in his hands. After having a beautiful time the dog in the park, not knowing what to do with him because his parents would not let him in the house. He sneaked the dog to the house and hid him in the back house. However, after realising that the dog would just grow more impatient, e just took it back to the park. There he lay down next to think thinking about how he could explain his parents about the dog He was phasing through stages of grief as he did not know how to help this dog. Either he could tell his parents or he could leave the dog and go away. The thought of leaving it hurt him. As he walked back to his house, he felt a rush of past memories of him with his previous dog, Tricki. He used to play with her everyday in the very park where he no tread. He realized that without even asking there is no point, therefore he braved up some courage and went home with the dog. The dog in fact was very similar to Tricki, to the point where it even responded to calls. This made the boy extremely suspicious. Tricki had one day wandered away when she was a pup therefore the boy had some hope inside him that this dog was Tricki. He checked for a very familiar birthmark which sure enough was on the dog. He was now in tears. Seeing the joy in his face, Tricki jumped onto him, the boy was in extreme glee as one of the greatest reunifications had occurred right before him. He was no more afraid of telling his parents about the dog, He was just happy to get his pooch back.
author: Somayajula Raam sashank

title: The Imagicaa Excursion
text: It was a chilly morning in October. I woke up around 5:50 AM. I got up from my bed with no difficulty, as waking up early had become my daily routine, except for some Saturdays and Sundays. I had woken up thinking it was a normal school day, but suddenly it popped up in my mind that today was the school excursion. Recently, our school organized a picnic at a famous park in Maharashtra, known as Imagicaa. The students who were attending the excursion had to assemble in school at 7:00 AM on the 18 th of October. The bus wouldn’t reach in time, so my dad decided to drop me and one of my friends in CME to school. I packed up, got dressed, and re-checked if I had taken the required food items. I reached the school by 7:00 AM, along with my friend. I bid goodbye to my father, and I walked to the class. My friend and I also had to depart, because sadly, he was in another section, which was a terrible tragedy. I found a few of my friends waiting in front of the class, and I joined them. According to the timings, we had to leave for Imagicaa by 7:30 AM on our semi-luxury buses, but due to a slight delay, we finally left at 8:30 AM. There were around 17 children attending the picnic from our class, and our class teacher had formed groups. There were 5 people in my group, and I was appointed the leader. We boarded the bus, which was neither big nor small. There were around 50 seats in the bus, windows beside each seat, and 2 electronic speakers. My group rushed to the seats at the far end, and to my surprise, there were exactly 5 seats, as if someone had already reserved them for us. Sadly, I couldn’t get the window seat, but one of my friends took it. We enjoyed our snacks, and someone also started playing songs in the speaker, and the children started dancing. After a long journey of almost 3 hours, we reached the park. It was a hilly region, and as the bus drove up to the park, I saw the huge board of Imagicaa. Imagicaa Theme park Water park Snow park Novotel This is what was written on the board. I was surprised that there was even a Novotel here. The bus suddenly stopped. The children started exiting the bus. No bags were allowed inside the park, so I could only take my bottle inside. We waited some time outside the park, in a line, and there were many, many students there. Not only our school but even 2 or 3 other schools. After the security check-in, our class teacher said, “Ok students, now each one of you stays with your group. Never, ever leave your own groups and listen to what your leader says. At sharp 1:00 PM, meet at Roberto’s food banquet for lunch. At 4:30 PM, exit all rides and come back to the main exit. Enjoy!” And the teachers departed, to enjoy among themselves. I was listening carefully to the teacher’s instructions, and I thought that I and my group should probably find Roberto’s first, so I should tell my group. As I turned around to tell my group, there was not a single person from my group visible. I ran in a random direction and found my group. As I had expected, all of them were inside the washroom. I said, “Let's find Roberto’s”. I received a scornful look from each one of them. “No, let us do this ride.” “NO! NO! LET’S DO THE ROLLER COASTER FIRST!!!”. “Let's do Alibaba and challis chor first”. And they all started arguing. At this moment, I understood why the people in the world were so ruined. They could never agree upon something. As we walked, arguing, all of us saw something. IT WAS A RIDE! In a hurry, we got in. It was something like a lake, in which there were 5 or 6 boats, which contained water shooting guns inside. We just had to shoot at the other boats. I found it amazing. That was the first thing we did. Later on, we found something else. It was more like a movie. Me and my group sat down, and there was a huge screen in front of us. The seats suddenly started rising. We went upto 90 feet. And then, the movie started. It was not something related to my interest. It just showed many helicopter-view shots of Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and other monuments and famous sculptures in India. After the second ride, we straightaway went to Roberto’s and had lunch. By this time, I could only see me and one of my best friends beside me. God knows what happened to the other idiots in my group. After this, we mainly did only one major ride, which I enjoyed the most. It was a river like structure, through which a boat would go at a slow pace, and there were many dinosaurs on the land, electronically controlled. In the end, there was a steep fall, and I felt like everything in my stomach went up. It was really awesome. These are only some of the major rides we did, I won’t be exaggerating my story a lot. Finally, after a tiring day, we all went home. And as I slept, and went into oblivion, the various incidents at Imagicaa kept repeating in my mind.
author: Kevin  Thomas Alex

title: Until Next time
text: "Do you like my rosary Rose?",I ask my sister as I shake my wrist."A black beaded rosary just like the one you wear." She smiled and said "It's beautiful Lily."I remember that day like the back of my hand.I was quite young at the time,I remember how Rose's eye were glowing when grandma gave it to her.I continued talking,"It's been so long since I've talked to you.I must say,its quite boring without you. ”. She laughed and responded, “It’s only been a while. Besides it wasn’t like we saw each other all the time before too. We were both busy with our lives.” “We didn’t spend a lot of time with each other, but it must’ve passed by like a breeze for you right? You make friends so easily; you always know what to say and what to do to make people comfortable. “I said as I recalled the days, I sat on my bed thinking about what Rose would be doing alone in her dorm while I, despite being surrounded by all my family was left alone with my thoughts. Rose was sent to boarding school when she turned 10. My parents realized they couldn’t take care of their five children on their own, so they sent their eldest two to boarding, Rose and Emory. We had a significant age gap, yet she was the one I related to the most. “I know a lot of people Lily but that’s just the kind of hospitality you pick up when you’re the eldest sibling. Even you know your way around people quite well. You’re Lily Peter for goodness’ sake, The golden child of the family. “, she said cutting my train of thought “Do you like my rosary, Rose?”, I asked my sister as I shake my wrist.” A black beaded rosary, just like the one you wear”. She smiled and said,” It’s beautiful Lily”. I remember that day like it was yesterday. I was quite young at the time, but I remember how Rose’s eyes were glowing when grandma gave it to her. I continued talking,” It’s been so long since I lasted talked to you. I must say it’s quite boring without you”. She laughed and responded, “It’s only been a while. Besides it wasn’t like we saw each other all the time before too. We were both busy with our lives.” “We didn’t spend a lot of time with each other, but it must’ve passed by like a breeze for you right? You make friends so easily; you always know what to say and what to do to make people comfortable. “I said as I recalled the days, I sat on my bed thinking about what Rose would be doing alone in her dorm while I, despite being surrounded by all my family was left alone with my thoughts. Rose was sent to boarding school when she turned 10. My parents realized they couldn’t take care of their five children on their own, so they sent their eldest two to boarding, Rose and Emory. We had a significant age gap, yet she was the one I related to the most. “I know a lot of people Lily but that’s just the kind of hospitality you pick up when you’re the eldest sibling. Even you know your way around people quite well. You’re Lily Peter for goodness’ sake, The golden child of the family. “, she said cutting my train of thought. I laughed and said” You’re the golden child, exemplary at everything you do, the perfect student, perfect woman, perfect daughter and of course the perfect sister. Sometimes I feel pressured you know, to do just as good as you, to be you. You’re the one I look up to.” Rose shook her head and said, “No Lily you’re prefect the way you are. Don’t try to be me. Don’t try to be anyone but you because you just can’t. It’s a suffocating feeling. Its ok to look up to someone but not to be them. At the end of the day, it’ll always be yourself that you see in the mirror. So, learn to accept that person, love that person and be only that person.” “People are such confusing beings though. One moment they want you to be your authentic self and the next they’re offended when you show even a little bit of your authenticity. They’re nice. They’re mean and sometimes excruciatingly painful. They can make you feel unworthy, selfish, guilty, lonely,not enough and sometimes all the above. It’s never like that with you. You’ve always made me feel safe, seen, at peace and most importantly, loved. Things are so much easier with you” I told her, tears slowing forming in my eyes thinking about all the times I gave people all my heart and they did all they could to rip it apart. It was so easy for them to do that while I was the one who had to glue the pieces back together carrying the scars with me for the rest of my life. Rose tried to console me saying,” Humans are like that Lily, sometimes they just can’t bother to think twice before they hurt you. But then again, you’re that human too. You too could make someone feel unworthy, selfish, guilty, lonely, not enough and so on. Whether you realize it or not. And besides, people also have the power to make you feel good, loved, happy, beautiful and like the precious being you are. People are coins Lily. There is always two sides to them. They’re just as much an angel like you and you’re just as much a monster like them.” “Do you remember our family reunion we have every year? We used to have so much fun. You always brought everyone together to play a game of charades, share stories, laughs and it used to be such a bliss. Mom and grandma always team up to make the best food. Can’t forget our private gourmand, dad.” I said smiling as Rose added” Of course how could I? It was the only time I got to see the whole family before I left for boarding again. I always wanted to make sure everyone was included and was having a great time. As the eldest child should. They say the oldest sibling is a second parent you know.” “But you weren’t there this time. Everything felt different, it wasn’t as colourful, there wasn’t as much laughter. Only you know how to bring people together like that. It got me thinking whether you ever had any fun yourself or were you too busy keeping all of us happy? So, this time I’m going to make sure of that. You’re coming this year right- “ “Lily! It’s time to leave!”, our mom called out to me. “Coming!”, I responded wiping my tears. I stood up from the grave I sat beside that said In loving memory of – Roselle Peter (1978-1997) I placed the roses I brought for her on the grave, her favourites; roses I should’ve place behind her ear if she was still here and said “Until next time Rose. I love you “. But today I said that in an empty graveyard and walked away. Not knowing whether she heard me. Not knowing whether she heard anything I said since she left. But knowing that from somewhere, she’s still looking out for me.

title: An unexpected guest
text: I It was Christmas.It was snowing very hard outside. Lavender was sitting in her room and was staring out of the window with some kind of admiration. ''Honey could you come down please''?asked her mother. She went down and her mother said,''I'm going out, so lock the doors and study for your exams''. Lavender knew this was coming, her mother had already told her about this yesterday. '' Mom can I come with you please?''asked Lavender trying the best to put an innocent expression on her face. ''Absolutely not, dear, should I remind you about your last exam's percentage''. ''No thanks '', replied Lavender and her mother went out and disappeared into the crowd. II Lavender was seventeen. A beautiful girl with blue eyes like the Atlantic ocean.She was very kind, and had long ginger hair. But she was constantly bullied by her classmates. She hated school very much. She didn't have any friends. There were times when she felt lonely, she felt extremely sad when she saw girls at her age laughing and talking with each other, but now she was used to it. She studied for five hours, and she suddenly heard a doorbell. She ran downstairs and opened the door. But it was not her mother t was a girl. It was snowing very hard and the girl was drenched in. ''It's snowing very hard, would you mind if I stay here for an hour or two, please? asked the girl. Lavender invited her in and offered her a blanket.She was very pretty. She had green eyes and blonde hair. She lit the fireplace and asked, ''What's your name? ''. ''Hazel. What's your name? ''. '' Lavender. I've never seen you before ''.''Oh I'm from Manchester, I came to visit my aunt who lives here in London. I was going to the railway station, but I couldn't see anything, and I was soaked in water. Well thank you'', said Hazel. ''Welcome'', replied Lavender. '' Umm....Are you alone?''. ''Yes I am my mom went to her friend's house''.'' Oh I see''. She beamed and Lavender beamed back. ''Would you like a cup of tea?'', asked Lavender.'' No, thanks''. What's your favourite book? asked Hazel after a while. ''Wuthering heights, by Emily Bronte'', replied Lavender. '' Oh mine is Jane Eyre, by Charlotte Bronte '', said Hazel.''It is amazing. But I love Pride and Prejudice too''. '' What do you do in Manchester ''? asked Lavender after sometime.'' Well, I am an architect, I graduated from college last year. It's snowing very hard isn't it''? asked Hazel.'' Yes it is snowing very hard since two days, it's not slowing down.''.''You're house is very beautiful '', said Hazel.'' Well it was my great aunt Victoria's house but it was given to mom after she moved to France. She is very rich''. ''Well it's obvious, isn't it?'', said Hazel. ''I'm very boring aren't I?'' asked Lavender. '' No, you're not, you 're a fun person to be with''. replied Hazel. ''Well, you're the first person to say it, you know, no one really thinks I'm friendly''. '' Who said these kinda things to you? People say many things and compares you by not knowing who you really are. That's the simple thing and just avoid them and be who you really are. That's it''.'' You're a very big motivator '', said Lavender. '' I know I am '', said Hazel and they laughed at it.''You're very kind'', said Lavender. No I'm not it's just responding to people who are kind. Lavender beamed. She had never seen a person like Hazel before, she was extraordinarily kind and she was very calming. ''I wish the snow would slow down '', said Hazel. ''Well if it's too late you can stay here. I would love that'', said Lavender.'' ''Oh thank you but I can't stay for too long my family will be waiting for me '', said Hazel.'' Oh, ok'',, Lavender replied.'' Well, do you want some Christmas cake? It's so tasty'' and Lavender rushed to the kitchen and gave it to her.'' Oh, it's delicious''. ''My mum made it, she is a very nice chef, you know '',said Lavender. ''She is, said Hazel. They talked for so long. She never had a friend like that. She found out that she and Hazel had a lot in common, they were obsessed with books, Harry potter, Twilight, Star wars and many more things. After a while Hazel said,'' Well,the snow is slowing down. I better hurry up'', and she stood up and put her jacket on. She hugged Lavender and turned to leave. ''Well thanks, I never had a friend like you. You're the best person I've ever met in my entire life''.'' No, I told you, we start to like a person because of their behavior and you are a wonderful human being. But you'll never understand it now but one day you'll find yourself and understand who you really are Lavender, I really hope you do, no, I know you will. I was a complete stranger but you invited me in and offered me help. ''I'll never forget this moment or you''. And she left. She glanced back once and waved, Lavender waved back. And that day in the midst of Christmas, Lavender found two things, two wonderful and amazing things, '' TRUE FRIENDSHIP AND AN AMAZING FRIEND. '' THE END

title: Three keys
text: Radha Rangarajan It was the chilliest day of the year, Hallow family was shivering with cold. "Brr. It's very cold here," Tom's mother shivered. "We should move to another place ",said Tom's Dad. "I don't want to leave", shouted Tom. "Sorry Tom, this place is too chilly and will possibly turn into ice",said Tom's mother,still shivering "Fine",said Tom Then they packed their stuff and went to their second house. While driving to their second house, Tom saw a minor path with a sign saying, "Welcome to Woodies" "Let's drive that way" Tom shouted in a hurry. "No it looked strange!" Mother replied anxiously. In just a few minutes they arrived at their destination. "The house didn't change",Tom's mother said when they stepped in. "Yes",said Tom's Dad. Tom didn't say anything. Tom was thinking about the sign "Welcome to Woodies". He felt a little weird and it seemed something was attracting him. He wondered what on earth was going on in that place. After Lunch, he walked to Woodies without telling anybody. There was no house on either of the side of the path. No people, only trees, tall and big. He was little scared. When he was sneaking into the forest, suddenly, he slithered down a long slope. "AHHHH!"shouted Tom until stopped at the end of the slope, painfully. "Wow" cried Tom, surprised. He saw an interesting chest in front and opened it without any hesitation. Suddenly a voice came out of the chest, "To get out of here,you need three keys,I will give three hours,or you will stay here forever. Here's the riddle for the first key: IT SHINES VERY BRIGHT,BUT IT DISAPPEARS AT NIGHT. Tom couldn't believe what he saw. He thought mother was right and he regretted coming here, but now what he could do was trying best to figure out the riddle. "It shines very bright,but it disappears at night", Hey, it is the sun!, He exclaimed. "But,how can I get up there?" Then he saw a bird. "Maybe that Bird will help me,"Tom thought. He pleaded with the bird for the sun. Believe it or not, the bird actually understood him and soared to the sun. "What a fascinating bird!" Tom thought. The bird was very tired of his journey but still got a piece of the sun for Tom. "Thank you, bird!" said Tom kindly. Then the part of the sun became a chest. Tom opened the chest and the loud voice came again, "Great job for solving the riddle, the first key will appear after the second key: "HYDROGEN IS MY FATHER, OXYGEN IS MY MOTHER,WHAT AM I?"Then, appeared a small key. "hmm.... hydrogen is my father and oxygen is my mother, what am I? If I combine hydrogen and oxygen it is equals to water!,said Tom excitedly. The suddenly a river appeared in front. Tom scooped some water with his hands. It immediately turned into a chest and again, he opened it. "Congratulations, you have solved the second riddle, you will receive your key after the last riddle. Ok, the riddle for the third key: "WITHOUT THE SUN AND WITHOUT THE WATER, I CAN'T GROW." Then, the second key appeared. "Ok, I think it should be a plant!" Said knowledgeable Tom. He then grabbed a plant by pulling it very hard, but instead of transforming into a chest, it transformed into a door, which had three key locks and one of them with a key inside. "Uh-oh it's nearly thred hours!" Said Tom worriedly. "I must put the other two keys into the key locks." At that moment, he placed the other two keys into the other two keyholes. The door opened successfully and Tom was free again. Tom was so happy to see his parents again when he got home. "I learnt a lesson,"he said, "It is important to consider your parents suggestions!".

title: It's Just a Burning Memory
text: Where am I? Memoria thought. She knew where she was, it was the same hallway she’d been to so many times. When she needed a nice escape from reality, she would just come here, her own personal space. Actually, this wasn’t even an escape from reality. It was actual reality. It was Everywhere at the End of Time. All of her memories, the good ones and the bad ones, she could see here, whenever she liked. But they had told her she had dementia, and that she’d lose her memories. What nonsense. She could perfectly remember all of her life. From her childhood, through her teenage years and adulthood, to finally her old age. It was all clear, her entire life in front of her. She even had these convenient doors to look at them any time she wanted. Well, since she seemed to be leaving this place soon, might as well have a look at everything before she left. Though Memoria was sure she remembered there had been more than 4 doors before… Well, these four would have to do, for now. There was not much else to do here. She moved towards the first door. It opened with a groan and a creak, as the rusty joints strained under the pressure. She walked into the chilly, dusty, and cobweb-filled room… It was the beach. How long ago was it? She was a child back then, just like she is now. Father is here. I haven’t seen father in years, where has he been? It was a bright, warm, sunny day, the waves were roaring, and a light cool breeze was blowing against her skin. There wasn’t anything much special about this day. It was just a trip to the beach. But it was beautiful, for some reason she didn’t understand. Special sceneries like those stick in the mind till the end, those are the good memories. Her father, her brother, and Memoria were playing with a beach ball. Smiling and laughing, as they ran around in the sand. Moments like those never die. But this one did. First, the blue sky was gone. It was a dull grey now. Then went the cool breeze, it became an eerie chill that made her uncomfortable. Her father and brother burned away. The memory was gone, reduced to nothing. She was back in the hallway. What had happened? Where did it go? That was a great memory, one of her favourites, but it had just burned away. She didn’t know how this was happening. She didn’t like this. It's just a burning memory. What was she thinking about? Must not have been important. She has a door in front of her. She can reminisce about one of her memories. She opened it. It swung open with a low groan. The door had seen better days, it was pretty old. She entered the dusty but warm room. It was a winter evening. Memoria was a teenager, and was in her room, studying. She looked up from her book, outside the window and let out a sigh. After she had been staring out the window for a few moments, her mother called her to the living room. She went downstairs and her family was sitting there, around a fireplace with cups of hot cocoa in their hands. “You’ve been studying for quite a while, have a break, come sit here with us,” said her mother. She took a cup and sat down, but then this memory started fading too. First the generous warmth of the fireplace. Then the taste of the hot cocoa, it went bland. Her family withered away, and she was left in the dull greyness. It was a warm memory, it was special to her. But it was gone in an instant. She grew worried. She didn’t like this, she didn’t like it at all, she wanted it to stay. It's just a burning memory. There were two doors. Were there always two doors? It felt like there used to be more than these. But she could only see two. So through the third door she went. The door gave a slight creak as she opened it. It was fairly new. It was a summer afternoon. Memoria was an adult now. She had just finished all the work around the house. She sat down and decided to have some rest. Then she heard her kids giggling in the next room. Then a few moments later, they came into the room. They were both holding a colourful card that they had made themselves. It said Happi Mothars Day. She laughed and thanked them both. She herself had forgotten that it was Mother’s day. She kissed them both on the cheek and told them to go play. But they just stood there, blankly staring at her. The card lost all its colour, turning a dull grey. Right after, the children faded away into the greyness. Everyone was leaving too fast, she couldn’t even stop to talk to them. The memories were burning faster. This was not good. This was bad. This was very bad. She wanted it to stop. She wanted all of it to stop. She wanted them to come back. Come back. “COME BACK!” It’s just a burning memory. There was one door. Nothing else to do. She went through the door, not knowing what to expect or what had happened before that. There was nothing before and nothing after. As she opened the door, it felt smooth. Like this door had been recently added. She went through the door, and suddenly she was in her old rocking chair, knitting some sweaters to send to her lovely grandchildren. While she was doing that, the door opened, and her children walked in with her grandchildren. They had decided to pay her a visit during vacation. The grandchildren e xcitedly ran towards Memoria. She had a big surprised smile on her face. But before they could reach her, they burned away. She desperately reached out into the air as if she could catch them and stop them from leaving forever. Her grandchildren, children, the sweaters, her rocking chair. It was all gone in an instant. She was left in the dull greyness, on the floor. She sobbed and wept. There was nothing left. Nothing at all. All that mattered, it was gone. There was no point. She could cry there till the end of time, but it was all gone, everything she had. It’s just a burning memory. It’s just a burning memory. It was just a burning memory. The End? There was nothing left. It was an empty expanse of just clear nothingness. The little girl Memoria ran around, desperately trying to find something, anything. She found nothing. She fell onto the floor once again. She lay there, not knowing what to do. She did not know who she was, where she was, when she was, why she was, how she was, she did not know anything. It suddenly dawned on her. She understood what it was. They had already told her what was happening. She had the thing… the demen… whatever it was. That was the cause of all this. It had been slowly stealing her life from her, mercilessly destroying every memory she ever had. She had no idea what was going on, but was also understanding everything that was happening. She did not have much time before she lost it all. She flailed around hopelessly, trying to collect the scattered ashes, as if doing that could bring it all back. She knew she could do nothing, it was all gone already, before she could even say goodbye. It was unfair. Very unfair. Too unfair. Her Everywhere at the End of Time was left as Nowhere at the End of Time. She let out one last pathetic cry of despair, before she was silenced by the darkness. It did not matter. Now she had nothing left. The hallway came back. The four doors reappeared. They were all locked shut, painted with beautiful colours. Looking at this made her happy for reasons she couldn’t comprehend. Now she remembered that she had had a happy life, and that she was content with it. She was finally done. She had nothing to regret anymore. The hallway faded, and she started falling into the endless void. As she fell, she saw the faces of so many people, she didn’t know who these faces belonged to but Memoria knew she loved them as soon as she saw them. After seeing these people, she was happy again. They faded away, but the smile on her face stayed. It was time for her to leave this world. She kept falling into the nothingness, but this time she did it willingly. She gave herself up to the emptiness filled not with regret, but with joy. Little Memoria faded away, like the leaves off a tree in autumn. Good bye.
author: Pulkit Chauhan

title: The School Mystery
text: "There! they are", "The one and only twins" kids whispered as Rita and Sita walked in. They are the two perfect twins or at least what they showed. Rita climbed up a chair said in her high pitched voice "Listen here everybody! today at 4, we all are going to find out what is the school mystery." The school, Rita and Sita go to have no strict rules but the only one rule is that they can never enter room "308", but the kids are very curious about it... Tina, who is a shy girl and always follows all the rules, said "We are not doing this! we could all get into trouble, and Rita get down from the chair! you know its against the rules." Before Rita could say something, her sister Sita spoke "Who are you to stop us? are you the teacher?" All the other kids laughed and booed Tina. Tina cried as she ran out of the school. By now, you must have guessed why the twins are not perfect, they obviously think that they are better than everyone. What do you think? but apart from that, they cause trouble at their house and constantly fight their parents and each other, the only time they stick up for each other is when they get a chance to pick on someone else. Rita smiled and said loudly "Who ever does not come.. Will face consequences." "Is that loud and clear? " Sita added, all the kids nodded their heads in fear of the consequences. As the clock ticked, TICK TOCK! TICK TOCK! It was finally 4 pm. All the students gathered around the "ROOM 308". Sita clapped her hands and said in deep and cold voice "Let me make sure everyone is here, 1..3...8..10..16..22.. and 29" Rita said in her high pitched tone "Only Tina is not here! she will regret this." Rahul, the class clown said as he giggled "Oh come on! lets get in already! will there be infinite gold? or money? or the test answers? or makeup for your faces? or-" He was cut short, as Sita said "Quite! now knock on the door" Rahul knocked on the door, THUD! THUD! THUD! From the inside came an old man's strong voice "Go away you kids! I can hear you, and I can tell you are breaking the rules!" followed by a loud scream, AHHHHH!! ROOM 308 That left everyone shook.. Everyone ran away in fear. Everything was fine for a couple of days but the class could never forget to find out what the mystery is. Once again, Rita and Sita told everyone to come, but this time Tina decided she would come.. her friend Meera had finally convinced her, with Tina's help the class would easily break in and find out what is the mystery. What do you think is the Mystery? Continue reading to find out. The whole class again met up. Rita said "Hurry up! Rahul! KNOCK ON THE DOOR!" Rahul replied "Geez! have patience Rita!" Rahul then knocked on the door, THUD! THUD! THUD! This time a loud beep came from a small crack in the door. Tina rushed to pull it open, they realized that it was numerical code. Tina said "I can easily crack the code! I've been studying the school's whole data base, from the school's dark secrets to the passcode of the exam cell." Everyone was surprised and shocked, especially the two twins. Sita stepped up and said "Ha! as if." But 5 seconds later, Tina yelled out loud "65850, that's the code!" As she pressed enter, BOOM! the code was cracked. Everyone looked at each other nervously, imagining what was behind the door? Rita said "What you all waiting for? Huh? Open that door!" Rahul nervously chuckled and opened the door. Everyone's eyes glanced across the room. Rita said in the most annoying tone "What in the world is this? Darkness? Are you serious?" Sita replied "You should know that we have to turn on the LIGHTSWITCH." Rita said "Duh! I knew that." Rahul's finger made way to the light switch. He said "3.. 2... 1.." And in the blink of an eye, everyone yelled "Disgusting" You may ask Why? that is because the room was filled with insects and animals.. Tigers said ROAR! Crickets said CRK! CRK! Mosquitoes said BRR! BRR! but behind those insect was a bright light of hope, without thinking Tina began walking and the rest of the class followed right behind. To their utmost shock there was a tunnel that led to the under side of the world.. Tina closed her eyes and jumped in, instead of seeing a new world, all she was the ultimate source of life... GOD! It was mentioned on a huge placard surrounded with GOLD and MONEY! "GOD is the creator, He has created us, He has given us JOY! RESPECT GOD!" Tina was touched as she climbed out she told everyone "Go in turn by turn and read the message that leads us to happiness." As Rita climbed out she muttered "What kind of rubbish is that?". A few days later Rita and Sita walked up to Tina and said "Hi Tina.. do want to hang out with us? like at the mall or something?" Tina said "Oh! I would love to.. can I bring along Meera?" Rita and Sita exchanged awkward looks but said "Yes." As the kept hanging out, Rita and Sita would always find ways to make a fool out of Tina, but she never realized it but Meera did. She tried to warn Tina, but Tina never believed her true friend Meera.. and kept making a fool out of herself. What do you think happens next? Does Tina realize it or not? Keep reading to find out Eventually, Sita realized that Tina was never their enemy but now it was too late.. she tried to tell her sister "Rita, you know Tina is actually very nice." but now Rita had blamed everything that was not PERFECT on Tina.. but weren't the twins perfect? Their life was perfect but the word WAS is used for the past... Their life is still amazing, their perfect reputation, their perfect faces and so on but the thing that bothered Rita and Sita most was their FAMILY LIFE. It turns out that as the twins and their parents kept fighting and arguing on the smallest things, their parents got a divorce.. and their father managed to get full custody of them because he had all the money from the family business and their mother had nothing.. not a single penny.. The twins dearly loved their mother.. but now they were missing her.. and ever since then, Rita and Sita have stopped believing in the existence of GOD. As they kept hanging out with Tina.. Sita very soon realized that she was wrong to blame anyone for this.. and Sita kept trying make Rita understand.. One day Rita said "Can you stop! It's all because of Tina!" Sita replied "How? Why? Tina was never there when we fought and when our parents got divorced and she never did anything wrong to us." Rita thought for a long-long time then said "I think you might be right.. You are right.. she never harmed me... or you or anyone.. it was always us." They now hung out with Tina and Meera with no intention to harm them... Over time.. Tina made them believe in the existence of GOD.. now these 4 girls are living their best lives.. not fighting anyone and always supporting the truth. Now this is the TRUE DEFINATION of "From an ENEMY to a BESTIE".
author: Amal Zakir

title: The Leaves Can Sing
text: I often wonder what pain is. Agony. Torment. suffering. They are merely synonyms. They don't express how you feel. But ever since the passing of my grandfather, I think I have an idea of what the word is trying to convey. But then again, I was never a good writer who knew how to put her thoughts into words. It's ironic, really, how I had a million ideas on "pain", until I was actually feeling it. I'm a writer, just like my grandpa, but funnily enough, right now, I'm at a loss for words. It's autumn, and the weather is making me feel that the environment decided to change its colours just to sympathise with what I'm feeling. For some reason the yellow fall very aptly describes my blues. As if it knows I'm grieving and it decided to help me out. This thought alone provides a sense of comfort to me, a warmth, that I never thought the chilly winds of October could make me feel. But I guess it's not the same for everyone. Some people need to be consoled in the form of human touch and communication. So my family and I decided to spend some time at my grandmother's, to let her know she is not alone. After a 6-hour journey in our rumbly old car that my father had bought as a birthday gift to my mother, we finally reach my grandmother's house. It's the same. Funny how you expect the entire world to crumble down when your world shakes. The flowers in her garden are still as colourful as ever and grandpa's old car, that he probably loved more than dad, is still parked near the driveway. Forcing a smile on our faces, we ring the doorbell, and the door opens to the kindest smile we've ever seen. It is not the most genuine one, I can tell, but the strength in her eyes dares you to question it. "Aadhira". It is the sweetest voice in the world. It has to be. The way my grandmother calls out to me, with her arms stretched outwards, asking for a hug, I know that the 6-hour journey to her house in the hills, with the repeated stops on the way because of my motion sickness, was worth it. It was all worth it. "Aadhira". It is the sweetest voice in the world. It has to be. The way my grandmother calls out to me, with her arms stretched outwards, asking for a hug, I know that the 6-hour journey to her house in the hills, with the repeated stops on the way because of my motion sickness, was worth it. I leap into her arms and never let go, and I can tell she doesn't want me to. Something about her embrace is always so comforting, as if, ensuring me that I never grew up. I never matured enough to feel complex emotions. But I did. I grew up. I grew up to into a 20-year old woman, who has recently lost her grandfather. It's okay. It'll be okay. It's okay to feel the complex emotions I'm dealing with right now. " Are you hungry? I baked a cake ". Yes, I know that it's not a celebration. A cake would be the farthest thing from one's mind when they are grieving, but she has told me before that she finds solace in seeing people enjoy the food she makes. So I nod with a smile to her question, even though I think I lost my appetite 2 weeks ago. I feel like a little girl again. I place my handbag on the dining table and have a look around. The interior is the same as well. I find my grandmother in the kitchen, washing the utensils she used, to cook us lunch. I tell her that I'll wash them later, and we should instead sit down and talk. On all my previous trips to this house, I rarely initiated a consversation. I'm not good at talking and find it easier to answer questions instead. But today was different. I was asking her to talk to me. Thinking of all those times she would've felt lonely and I let her feel lonely, I take her by the hand to the front porch of our house. I was ashamed to not have done this sooner. We step out of the house and sit down on the porch. I hear some rumbling back in the garage, which was probably my dad looking for things that belonged to my grandfather. He said that both grandma and grandpa loved listening to music, and he would like to try repairing the old radio that belonged to my grandpa, to gift it to my grandma on her birthday. I remember grandpa showing me the old radio which was dear to him. He wouldn't let anyone even touch it, but he trusted me with it. It was the first time that the 7-year old Aadhira was trusted with something. It was just a radio, but it meant a lot to her. "Aadhira, where is Chiku's bag of warm clothes?", my mother calls out to me. "In the guestroom", I answer back. In the midst of all the noise, my grandma sits quietly, looking at the leaves as they fall off the trees, one by one. I want to say something, but I don't know what. My phone vibrates in my pocket. It is a message from my colleague, asking for the deadline of the article we had to submit. The company I work for had been considerate enough to let me take a breather; clearly she was not. I put my phone back in my pocket, deciding to answer her sometime later. Now was not the time for work, which I had clearly always prioritized over my family. I came here for my grandmother. After sitting there without saying a word, for what felt like years, I hear my grandmother humming a melody, that sounded like some bollywood classic, I was too young to know. She stops and then closes her eyes. Swaying with the blowing wind, she lets out a giggle and shakes her head, probably laughing at her own thoughts. She seemed like a child with an innocent smile on her face and I didn't want to question it. "It was your grandfather's favourite song ", she says. I didn't know what to say to that. " Was it your favourite too? ", I ask. " Not quite ". I was surprised. I believed since they both liked to listen to music, their taste in music would be similar. " I think I like the song these leaves are singing better ". I didn't know what that meant. The song that the leaves are singing? What song do they sing? "But leaves don't sing", I said. "Yet there was no way I could make your grandfather agree with it." It was getting colder and I suggested grandma that we should go inside. She didn't reply but the smile on her face made it clear she wanted to listen to the song for a while longer. The song of the leaves. "You know, when your grandfather was still with us, he would sit like this on the porch each day and ask me if I could listen to the song. I never did, but now I finally hear it." "But, I don't hear anything." The wind gets stronger and the leaves begin to rustle. I feel droplets of water falling down on me. Grandma wanted to stay. I hold her hand and put my head on her shoulder. "You think music is a bunch of notes that form a melody? It's the ability of the heart to see beauty in mere sounds", she said. I think I knew what it meant. I closed my eyes and thought of all the pain I was feeling. Being in a place that was once full of happiness, broke me. Suddenly, that pain was taken over by something. Something sronger than the pain I was feeling. A sense of gratitude and relief, which was different from the emptiness I was experiencing since the past few days. The light drizzle that I could feel falling down on me, felt as if the darkness surrounding me was being washed away. Before I knew it, I was thinking of all those moments I spent with Grandpa; all those times when I was truly happy. All those times when I could just be a carefree little girl, whose grandpa loves her a lot. I felt a smile sneaking onto my face and suddenly, everything was silent. No. Peaceful. So peaceful that I could hear it. I could hear the leaves singing.
author: Shresta Sharma
