title: A Wish for Santa
text: O ne very cold morning, Emma woke up rubbing her warm, brown eyes. She gazed at the calendar and suddenly a faint smile came across her rosy lips. It was the day before Christmas Eve that day. She had turned nine this autumn and was patiently waiting for Christmas to arrive. Emma and her family would always stay at her grandmother’s house in winters and celebrate Christmas together with her. This year too Emma and her family were spending their vacations at Emma’s grandmother’s house, but this year was special. Every year, she would wish for a wonderful gift for herself from Santa, but this year, she wanted to do something special. She rushed out of her bed to her grandmother, for advice. Grandma Jane was an old, wrinkled woman, but young at heart. She too was a mischievous child in her childhood days maybe deep inside, she still was. Being a believer of Christmas she always stood awake and waited for Santa to come through the chimney to deliver gifts. In today's world where chimneys have taken a new form, Jane never agreed to demolish her beautiful red bricked chimney. She took great care in repairing it and also keeping it clean at Christmas time. Each year, she would decorate the fireplace with little twinkling light bulbs, ornaments and she never forgot to hang her handmade stockings. Emma said softly "Grandma wake up, it's Christmas Eve tomorrow and we have a lot to plan." After a while Jane woke up. In spite of having a good night sleep she seemed to be quite tired. Emma was confused so she asked eagerly "Grandma Jane, why do you seem so tired?" Jane replied, "It's just a matter of age my dear, now a days, I start feeling tired, even before completing the tasks I set for a day.” “My old body does not allow me to do work continuously for long hours." Listening to Grandma, Emma drifted away into deep thinking, concerned about Santa who seemed even older than Grandma Jane. Now this was something to worry about. Jane noticed her tension and inquired Emma about it. "What's the matter sweetheart, where is your mind lost?" Emma replied hastily, "Grandma Jane, if you are having so much of trouble at this age then what about Santa, how does he manage to do all his tasks? Moreover when does he get time to do what his heart desires?" Jane's eyes got filled with tears with the thought that her granddaughter's heart was filled with so much of love and care. She hugged Emma tightly and said softly, “How thoughtful of you, my dear." Emma interrupted, “I know what I want to do this Christmas! I will fulfill Santa's wish, a wish which would make him happy!" “But that is not a simple task to do my darling” said Jane. Emma's eyes were gleaming with confidence; her mind had already formed a picture of Santa surrounded by happiness. Jane's heart pounded at the near impossible idea of her grandchild, because she didn't want Emma to be heartbroken if she didn't succeed but, Jane also believed in doing and failing rather than not making any efforts. So that was it, both of them decided to go along with Emma's idea for a special Christmas. Meanwhile Jane was figuring out the solution for one problem Emma threw another question at her. "What might Santa's most cherished wish be?” “Oh! I know the answer to this one!” said Jane promptly. “I have been listening to Santa all these years mumbling all by himself, about not having the time to enjoy a delicious warm Thanksgiving dinner, with Mrs. Clause” Both Emma and her grandmother knew the feeling of enjoying a delicious Thanksgiving meal with their loved ones, very well. They could imagine that the feeling of being left out of a family dinner would be very sad. They had made their decision about helping Santa, and now they would not back off from it. Both of them put their thinking hats on and discussed about each and every possible way there was, to fulfill Santa's wish. Soon, they were called for breakfast by Emma's mother, they thought about it at lunch, at teatime and then till dinner. Now it seemed like a race against time. Sitting at the dinner table they both felt lost, now the ideas had also stopped crossing their minds. They sat at the table with empty expressions. Even Emma’s mother and father were curious and concerned at such behaviour. They had neither heard the clock ticking so loud in their house, nor experienced a moment of pin drop silence, ever since Emma was born. Emma’s mother was a professional chef before Emma’s birth. She had retired from her job to take care of Emma but, she never lost her culinary skills. She would always prepare the most delicious food for the family and even desserts after dinner at festive times. Emma’s father was a music composer who loved to make new tunes from day to day items. He could even use to bowls kept in the kitchen to make harmonious songs! In spite of all his efforts to cheer up Emma and her grandmother, they were both lost in deep thoughts and the room continued to be filled with utter silence. However, the silence was broken when Emma's mother shared the good news with everyone. She said “Oh my! Dad's new Christmas song is being liked by People across the country. He has received fifty thousand likes on the social media already!” This was it. It cheered up both of them. They both Knew that they were thinking of the same idea. They both figured that they could take the help from children, all across world who believed in Christmas and Santa through the internet. That was exactly what they did. They circulated a message which stated: Hello everyone! I am Emma, a nine year old girl and I request all the little believers of Christmas such as me, to wish for Santa's most cherished wish to get fulfilled, which is to get some spare time to enjoy a warm and delicious thanks giving dinner with Mrs. Clause! All these years he has been fulfilling our wishes but, this time it is our turn to fulfill his wish. Waiting for your support, Emma Now, it was time to wait and watch the likes to increase in number. After sometime, a like popped up, and then another two, and then another four and so on! It truly felt as if the likes were pop corns popping in a hot pan! This meant that all these people were consenting to help make Santa’s wish come true! The next morning it was Christmas Eve. Emma rushed to the fire place but, there were no gifts kept waiting for her under the Christmas tree. Emma jumped with happiness and rushed to bring the news to her grandmother. She said, catching her breath “Grandma Jane, our wish has finally come true! Santa took a day off to enjoy some precious moments with the ones who matter the most in his life, his family!” Grandma's eyes were filled with tears of joy. She spoke in a heavy voice “My dear Emma, you have learnt the true meaning of Christmas at such an early age.” The End
author: Rashi Bathmi

title: From: Sour To Sweet
text: Sitting on a table Ramen searched for another interesting book to read. While surfing on Internet for suggestions of a good book, one book caught her attention "Cooking: the real magic of life”. She pleased her father to buy it, and wala!, It’s a yes, as we know daughters are the princesses of a father, right? And within 3 days, the book got delivered. And to Ramen’s surprise, the book was a story of 5 friends with magical recipes in it. She was surprised as, she loved cooking. She was a girl who also watched cooking shows in Television. Even that was the reason for her getting the nickname Ramen, her actual name was Ramona Oliver. She completed the novel with great amusement. The novel was written by, Mary Fox, she loved the novel, as it was all about friendship and the love for cooking of the 5 friends, with a lot of magic. She was unable to hold her tongue, without talking about the story to her besties for the resties (It’s what the group of friends of Ramen address each other). Her eagerness made her rush out of the house to the place where they usually meet, it's the garden of one of her friend named Monica Fox. Everyday they spent time there in the evening, usually playing and cooking in the weekends. In the afternoons they usually cycled. As she said about the novel and how the five friends used magic ingredients to cook, all the concentration of other three friends Moni(Monica Fox), Prissy(Priscilla Brooks) and Winnie(Winifred Kinsman) was on the excitement and her love for the book. Suddenly she started screaming with excitement pointing Moni, saying that,“You know what, the author’s name is similar to your name, Mary Fox” But to everyone’s surprise, she acts normal, and didn’t show any excitement, but they didn’t bother much about it, as in their opinion she was not interested in Magic. After Ramen leaves, all the three decided to arrange a surprise birthday party with the book’s theme. The next day, they brought seeds of the plants which look similar to those in the book. Soon, they made all the ingredients ready for Ramen’s favorite recipe in the book Glide By Cake, and, on Ramen’s birthday they surprised her by setting a mini kitchen with the magical look alike ingredients. After everyone wished her and gave her their gifts, they started to cook. Finally, they’ve made the cake which looks just as the cake in the book, with the same flavour too! And it was so tempting that they couldn’t even wait till Ramen blows the candle. And just before eating, Ramen informed all “In the book, this recipe is used to travel back in time, so are you guys ready to travel in time!” They all know that it was not real magic but surely, a fake one, so all started eating. Bizarrely, Moni shouted "Yes, I’m ready, are you?” For everyone, it was a bizarre moment, as I said you earlier that Moni didn’t show much of her interest in such things. So, everyone enjoyed eating the cake, just after they finished eating their part of the cake, they all began to be aware of the change in their surroundings. They actually did travelled through time. Yes, it’s Moni who did everything, she used real magic ingredients, which all others thought to be fake. Then she told everyone, that they were in the time, when their parents were of their age. Then, suddenly Ramen observed the five friends who were just similar to the people in the book. Moni told Ramen “Actually, the book is the diary of my mother, who did magic with cooking,” Moni continued to say “The reason for bringing you all here, is to take a helping hand from you all to save my mother and her friends from magic” So, were our three friends helping Moni in saving her mother and other four friends of her? Yes, they were ready as they were all benevolent. But the only question in their mind was why they had to save Moni’s mother and why not any other people. Then Moni said that they have to prevent her mother and her mother’s friends from making “Dwindlaeon.” She explained everyone “This recipe reduces the age of the person who cooks or eats this recipe by 50years” She gets a bit emotional as she said “And even this is the reason of my mother expiring at a very young age as 30” Just then Ramen got a doubt, was this the reason of my mother also expiring at the same age as Monica’s mother, but she didn’t share this doubt of her to anyone. Then they searched for a recipe which can prevent a person from doing an action which harms them that was “Nip in the Bud” Ramen had an idea about this as she read about it in the book Alias diary of Moni’s mother. Then they all cooked the recipe and prevented the five friends from cooking the recipe, by delivering the recipe to each of the five kids, they were such a whip-smart that, they delivered them with the names of the five friends itself! They again ate Glide by cake and had a drink, and they returned back to their present time. And everyone went back to their home. And Ramen as usual slept with her mother and so did Moni. It was usual for both of them, even everyone in the city as well, the drink which they drank in the last was “Obliterate” which made everyone to forget a change that happened in their life, and for Moni and Ramen is their mother’s presence. How then did Monica came to know about her mother’s death, if it was by the diary, why then didn’t Ramen, it’s pretty simple, she tore the pages from the diary, which have a clue about each of their mother’s death. And I guess you have understood quite well that Ramen’s doubt was true, Ramen’s mother was also one of the five friends. Then did magic exist after that? "Nip in the Bud” as mentioned in the diary prevents us from doing action which harms us; therefore, it had also put an end to Magic which led to several problems. Ramen held a helping hand in saving Monica’s mother from death which in turn also helped her mother from death. So, let all of us lend a helping hand to a person in need.
author: Vuyyuru Sreesaranya  Reddy

title: The Mystery Of The Cyber Friend
text: They are very happy as she uses computers. The computer is now her friend. She uses the computer for the images and knowledge she needs for school projects and for sending e-mails Shree's aunt lives with them. Everyone calls her 'akka'. Sleeping while watching her favourite old movies is a habit of hers. Akka is the one who makes shree's favourite hot dosas and noodles. After eating, shree likes to play games, but not the old kind of games akka prefers. She likes computer games. The computer doesn't only provide games. It has a website called FriendsNet. Shree joined FriendsNet on her thirteen birthday, two months ago. After having chai and snacks, she goes on FriendsNet to chat with her school friends. They tell each other what they did since they met last which was on the school bus. Shree says that she got more sugar in her chai. One friend says," You get that everyday." Shree also says she got mutton flavoured noodles with her dosa. Another friend of Shree poked fun at her by saying "Do you do anything besides eating." Shree gets provoked. She decided to unfriend them. After some time, she misses them. But before she told them sorry, she received a new friend request. Her name is Chaitra. She looks very pretty, like a film star You have a Friend request from Chaithra Accept Block Shree pressed accept,. After a click they became friends. Chaitra asked if Shree had many friends. Shree says, "No. And I did lose a few friends today." With a sad face emoji "So what? It doesn't matter how many friends we have- it is how friendship matters. And u do have me now." Says Chaitra. Shree liked it. "Which school do you study in?" typed Shree. "Next to your school." Types Chaitra. Shree asked how she knew her school "Because its next to my school" typed Chaitra. "That's nice. Then we could meet," types Shree. Chaitra says bye. 'Yes we can and we will be best friends forever." Next day while going to school, Shree looked for schools nearby But she didn't see anything. She hasn't even heard of a school nearby. But she felt like Chaitra was nicer than her friends. Chaitra was Shree's special friend and no one else's. Shree loves chilli chicken noodles. But she didn't eat it today. Akka thought what was wrong. 'Are you feeling okay?' She lied saying too much schoolwork. "Then go do your homework while I take a nap." says aunt But she didn't do her homework. Instead she goes to FriendsNet and waits for Chaitra to come online. Soon, she gets a message from Chaitra. "Hello friend, how are you?" 'I am fine but I didn't eat my tiffin," typed Shree "Why?" asked Chaitra "I wanted to talk to you today. So I quickly finished my chai and came here.". said Shree "Great!, could you send me your selfie and your phone number?" types Chaitra "I don't have a camera phone." types Shree and gets sad. "I'll give you my old camera phone" said Chaitra "Let's meet this Sunday. Then I will take your photo. And give you my old phone." said Chaitra. Shree always wanted a camera phone. "Where shall we meet?" typed Shree. "We'll meet at the railway station" said Chaitra "What time?" typed Shree. Chaitra tells when the Bengaluru train reaches there. Akka comes to the room to clean it "What are you doing Shree?" "I got a new friend "says Shree. Akka looks at Chaitra's Photo. "But that's Madhoo, I like that film actress so much. Is she your friend?" Yes, but that's Chaitra Akka laughed and shakes her head. "That's Madhoo, I have seen most of her movies. She must be vey old now" Shree says that she was the same age as her "Not at all, she's as old as I am, That picture was taken when she was in school, from her very first movie." said akka Shree felt angry towards Akka. "Why is Chaitra using someone's else's photo, that too a film star's?" Wondered Shree How old are you?" typed Shree. "I told you, I'm thirteen, the same age as you." replied Chaitra "That's nice. Best friends should be the same age. Hey, the earrings in your profile looks really pretty. 'Thank you. I made them myself'. says Chaitra. Wear them when we meet tomorrow." types Shree. "Okay, but I will only wear them if you come alone." said Chaitra Shree asked why Chaitra said that she was coming alone too, to their secret meeting. Shree typed okay when she suddenly remembered something. She told Chaitra that she hadn't seen any schools nearby, but Chaitra went offline. Was something of about her new internet friend? Was she lying? Shree got puzzled and couldn't focus on her Homework. "Akka?" she asks "Yes dear. Tell me, what is worrying you?" She told the whole truth to her akka about her new friend who is lying. "Akka, what should I do now?" The next morning, Shree and her aunt reached Katpadi Junction very early before the arrival of the Bengaluru Express. They had executed a secret pan to find out if this friend was honest or not. Akka said that she would go to the station manager to seek for help. The train from Bengaluru was coming. Shree looked all around.... She couldn't remember whether Chaitra had told her to wait outside or inside. Where did Akka go She can't see her anywhere A lot of people were coming out of the train. No one looked like Chaitra. A man who was Shree's father's age approached her. He was smiling and said "hello Shree" Shree got perplexed. She did not know this person. 'It is so good to meet you" he said ""Who.. wh- who are you. You are not Chaitra" Stuttered Shree. "No but I am an uncle who would like to be your friend,Shree. I like making friends with young girls." said the man who was not Chaitra. "Eeeeeeee" shrieked Shree In the next second, her aunt and the station manager came to her. The man was shocked. He hadn't expected Shree with two grown ups. Akka hit him with her handbag. Then she yells at him "Don't you ever dare come near my niece." "Ouch!!" he cries Just then the train moves. He runs towards a bogey door. The station manager rushes forward to catch the man, But the man disappears into the crowded train. They all went to the Police station. "You truly are a brave pair." says a policewoman. Thank you for informing us about this fraud pretender. Shree, you were very clever to pass on this information to a trusted adult!. Would you mind putting up a poster about cyber security in your school? We would very much like to conduct a cyber safety class in your school." An expert from the Cyber Crime Cell would need to check Shree's computer On the next day, an officer from the Cyber cell went through Shree's computer. Within hours, they were able to find the man who pretended to be Chaitra. They nabbed him from his office in Bengaluru and and from further speculation, it was found that he has been trying to befriend many young boys and girls on social media. She decides to only have friends from her own school She couldn't wait to tell her friends about her petrifying adventure with her cyber 'friend.'
author: Mahesh Kumar

title: The Wise Monkey
text: Once upon there lived a monkey on a Jamun tree. There was a lake near the tree. Crocodile families use to live in that lake. Everyday monkey use to eat sweet Jamun from the tree. One day monkey gave Jamun to a crocodile for his wife. She loved the Jamun and told her husband that monkey eats those Jamun every day so his heart must be sweet too. He would be a delicious dinner. She asks her husband to invite the monkey to their place for dinner. The crocodile invited monkey for dinner and he agreed. Monkey sat on the crocodile's back and reaching the middle of the river. Crocodile began to sink and monkey got scared. He ask why are you doing this? Crocodile told him that his wife wanted your heart. Monkey was shocked and started thinking fast. He told crocodile I would happily give my heart for your wife but I left it behind on the tree so the stupid crocodile took the monkey back to Jamun tree. when they reached, monkey climbed the tree quickly. The wise monkey saved his life. Moral: The person who wants to cheat others will be cheated and lose everything.
author: Rajveer  patel

title: THE SELFISH GIANT
text: This is a story written by Oscar Fingal O'Flahertie Wills Wilde was an Irish poet and playwright. He was born on 16 October 1854, Westland Row, Dublin, Irelandand Died on 30 November 1900, Paris, France. After writing different forms throughout the 1880s, he became one of the most popular playwrights in London in the early 1890s. NOTE: Oscar Wilde intended this story to be read to children. Every afternoon, as they were coming from school, the children used to go and play in the Giant's garden. It was a large lovely garden, with soft green grass. Here and there over the grass stood beautiful flowers like stars, and there were twelve peach-trees that in the spring-time broke out into delicate blossoms of pink and pearl, and in the autumn bore rich fruit. The bids sat on the trees and sang so sweetly that the children used to stop their games in order to listen to them. 'How happy we are here!' they cried to each other. One day the Giant came back. He had been to visit his friend the Cornish ogre, and had stayed with him for seven years. After the seven years were over he had said all that he had to stay, for his conversation was limited, and he determined to return to his own castle. When he arrived he saw the children playing in the garden. 'What are you doing here?' he cried in a very gruff voice, and the children ran away. 'My own garden is my own garden,' said the Giant; 'any one can understand that, and I will allow nobody to play in it but myself.' So he built a high wall all round it, and put up a notice board. TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED He was a very selfish Giant. The poor children had now nowewhere to play. they tried to play on the road, but the road was very dusty and full of hard stones, and they did not like it. They used to wander round the high wall when their lessons were over, and talk about the beautiful garden inside. 'How happy we were there,' they said to each other. Then the spring came, and all over the country there were little blossoms and little birds. Only in the garden of the Selfish Giant it was still winter. The birds did not care to sign in it as there were no children, and the trees forgot to blossoms. Once a beautiful flower put its head out from the grass, but when it saw the notice-board it was so sorry for the children that it slipped back into the ground again, and went off to sleep. The only people who were pleased were the Snow and the Frost. 'Spring has forgotten this garden,' they cried, 'so we will live here all the year round. 'The snow covered up the grass with her great white cloak, and the Frost painted all the trees silver. Then they invited the North Wind to stay with them, and he came. He was wrapped in furs, and he roared all day about the garden, and blew the chimney-pots down. 'This is a delightful spot,' he said, 'we must ask the hail on a visit.' So the Hail came. Every day for three hours he rattled on the roof of the castle till he broke most of the slates, and then he ran round and round the garden as fast as he could go. He was dressed in grey, and his breath was like ice. 'I cannot understand why the Spring is so late in coming,' said the Selfish Giant, as he sat at the window and looked out at his cold white garden; 'I hope there will be a change in the weather.'
author: Hritik Varindani
illustrator: Jayaprakash Bojan; Nimret Handa; Partho Sengupta; Polina Marandi; Priyanka Agarwal; Rohan Chakravarty; Rupa Prakash; Sangeetha Kadur; Sanjay Sarkar

title: FRIENDSHIP
text: FRIENDSHIP Once there was a boy named Sohail, he lived in Chennai. He was really obedient, playful, cheerful and virtuous child. His parents were blessed having a child like him. He was also doing great in his school. He was also really healthy. One day after school,he found an old box on an unknown street.In that box, he found an innocent puppy inside. He took that sinless puppy with him,to his house.He christened that pup Browny. It took him ages to convince his parents for petting Browny. But ultimately they were convinced. Everyday when Sohail came back home after school,the first thing he did was to cuddle Browny. He was really faithful towards his master. They walked together,slept together, and even ate together.They both shared a special bond. One day Sohail’s cousin visited his house. Mrs. Goswami, his mum also visited his home. That day, Browny and Sohail’s cousin, Rishab had a lot of fun together. But they didn’t invite Sohail in their amusement.This made Sohail a little jealous. After Rishab went back to his home, Browny went in Sohail’s room, and licked him, and hugged him, he even tickled him, all these things made Sohail laugh and they again became Best Friends Forever. One unfortunate day, Sohail took Browny for a walk. They were on a busy road as it was evening time and everyone one was as returning home. The pace of vehicles was very high. One car hit Sohail and was dragged along by it across the road. He was bleeding profusely and the car passed out within seconds. Browny was very restless and barking at every car to get help.He was witty dog. As he saw no car was stopping, he came in front of a car and was reluctant to get away. One car stopped and fortunately and it was Sohail's aunt, Mrs. Goswami. She took Sohail to hospital. Sohail was out of danger now. Brownie stayed near unless Sohail gained consciousness. Even after returning home Browny didn't leave Sohail's side. Earlier Sohail's father was reluctant to keep Brownie but after this incident his father was very much delighted. Ultimately, all’s well that ends well. It 's really true as they say love and compassion if given, it reverts to you in some or other way.
author: Paridhi Lakhwani
illustrator: Marleen  Visser; Natasha  Mehra; Seat Sopheap

title: The Robo Dog!
text: Once upon a time there lived a kid named Ronit, he lived in a residential area of Kolkata. He had everything in his life except of a companion which he wanted, as he was the only one child in his house. So, today he was having his birthday, and he was sitting on beach thinking about the gifts that he would be receiving today. He wasn't expecting a big thing, because on most of his birthdays he received a pencil, pen, eraser and a sharper, but there was something special this time, which was coming of his dear grandma to his house. His dear Grandma was already to his house 1 hour ago, before Ronit could actually come to his house. When he saw her, he couldn't stop him from chatting with his dear grandma. Then he dressed up, called his friends and began to cut his cake. Everyone had a gleam on their faces. After everything was completed, he went to his grandma and asked, "what gift did you bring for me". Grandma said "Oh! I forgot to give it to you". And she brought a cardboard box which had many punch holes, and it was covered with a gift wrapper. On getting his birthday gift he was very happy as, this time he was receiving something different. Then, he couldn't wait more time to open the gift so, he tried to open it and to his surprise there popped out a cute little dog, it was having white fur all over his body and it had a belt in his neck, which contained a name plate as "Robo". The next day his dear grandma was in a hurry to leave, as her husband, Ronit's grandpa was ill. So before going, Ronit gave a warm hug to his grandma, said thankyou and gave some of his favorite snacks which she could consume during her travel... Today, Ronit was a having holiday, so he completed his H.W as fast as he could a went to the Garden with Robo, he taught him all the tricks which all the other dog masters were preparing their dogs for, because a few weeks later, International trained dogs' championship (ITDC) was to be held in their own state Kolkata. Ronit had a good time while teaching Robo, and as he cared for him their boundness between they increased very soon. As well as they kept on practicing till, they didn't receive any perfection... So, at last the day came when their names were found in the ITDC championship list. There were many other dog trainers, but Ronit's case was different from them, as he was the only youngster in that championship, and he was having a fine breed of Dog. After so-many tries of others, their name was announced, and they did really very well! They could do such tricks that previous year's champion and runner up wasn't able to do. After few months, he a received letter from ITDC organization, which was a kind of promotion for his little Robo, although it was a promotion it made Ronit sad, but he could feel happiness in the corner of his mind. The letter mentions that Robo has been ranked 1st in India and Robo was called by Indian Army for any further training and military operations. Then after few days Ronit met with his little Robo for a last time in Military department.... And years went by, and they never met again. After 8 years, Ronit was big enough to travel alone, so he thought of meeting Robo. He took train tickets and went to military department. When he went inside, he saw Robo eating food and he ran towards it. Before he could even reach towards Robo, it came from backside and began to lick Ronit. It was one of the best views in the world. Then, he began to feed it with his own hand. Later, there was an alarm in the department, after investigating they found that there was terrorist who was hiding in a residence. The active relief force was ready to take Robo on mission, as Ronit was also present he too wanted to come with them to see the work which Robo does, so they made him to sit in a different specially armored car. When they reached there, army got the news that the terrorist was on the 3rd floor. Robo's work was to go to 3rd building and harm the terrorist to an adverse extinct. As Robo goes to the 3 rd floor, the terrorist noticed him and started to fire, as he was wearing bullet proof jacket, as it was trained, it wasn’t hurt, but that house had an inverter and some the fired bullets pierced the inverter and there was a big bang, with a lot of smoke which accumulated in the room. Here outside the residence, after seeing the smoke and hearing the noise Ronit was scared, but he had a hope that Robo would kill the terrorist with the help of army and would come back soon. But neither of this happened after the noise the was electrical fire inside, firefighters were called, and now Ronit couldn’t stop him from going to 3 rd floor. He ran and he noticed Robo there who was coming towards him. Then he gave a great dash to Ronit and pushed him back, and suddenly and log of wood fell from up and hurt Robo’s brain in such a bad way that, he couldn’t survive… Ronit was greatly shocked after this, as Robo gave his life form him!....... 10 years later, Ronit was sitting on a bench of his office, and remembering the incident that happed 10 years back, which he couldn’t forget. And whenever Ronit thinks about him, tears just starts to fall form his eyes. Now, Ronit it is IT world, a computer scientist. He just stays silent, in a deep world of sadness. Just 10 days after that his dear grandma passes away, but before going she said something to Ronit, which could ask him to follow a new way of life. She said “My boy, see now you are grown up, and you are one of the greatest computer scientists of this era, so go forward and try building a new mechanized Robo” So, this conversation ignited his creation and the same day he made a team to work on… After many unsuccessful tries their first Robotic dog, which was the exact copy of his dog Robo was made. Ronit was also given a noble prize for his achievement, but his dream wasn’t still completed because he wanted his new Robo to be used in any of the Socially useful work. As time passed by, the whole earth was facing shortage of diamonds, so ISRO planned his new mission to send Robo with someone to Uranus, to bring back some 350kgs of diamonds. For this mission Ronit was selected as he was the one who could understand Robo in the best way. So very soon their spacecrafts were made and meanwhile Robo and Ronit completed his education about space. At last, the day came when the found themselves in the spacecraft. The spacecraft took off the earth's surface and due to advancement on technology it was so fast that it reached the surface of Uranus within 4.78662 hours. When they came out of their spacecraft, they were so shocked that the surface was made of pure diamond and many different jewels. They both had a great time there and picked up a required boulder and kept it in their spacecraft, after that they took many photos and start to come back. While coming back they got a radio signal from ISRO that they would be actually hit by a big asteroid which would come on their path! But the chances of dying were very less as the spacecraft was made up of such a material. The same thing happened, but the things which was predicted was very different in real situation thought they were saved their spacecraft wasn’t anymore and now Ronit and Robo were left only with two small space craft which were installed in their suites and this would take nearly 9.65416 hours to reach earth, but the problem was that the space suits were only made to carry any two things either two persons or 1 person and 1 object. So, who would remain there! According to the statement given by ISRO in such adverse conditions, Ronit would come to earth and Robo’s space suit would be used for transportation of diamond. But Ronit wasn’t ready to leave Robo, but when Robo said “Master! You always did good for me and it’s my turn to do good for you, and don’t worry just chill, I will be there with you for every, don’t think about me think about India and the mission”, Ronit with heavy heart said Good bye to Robo. When he reached India he was given many prizes and awards, but the not in a mood to life in this world, he was planning for a suicide, but he thought of rewinding a his momories by seeing photos and to open all the the gifts which he received after his travel. There wasn’t any big thing in those gifts as it only contained gift vouchers, signature pens etc. But the last box changed his life, When he opened the box, he saw the chip which was inserted in Robo and it contained all the information, so the only things which was left was to make body. And from that day Robo was being used in many social works…….
author: Siddhesh nandanwar
illustrator: Khin Zar Chi Oo; Megan Lotter

title: Thirteenth birthday
text: My thirteenth birthday started well. I woke up at 12 am sharp due to the noises and rumbling from the kitchen. I wasn't expecting such a surprise from my parents. There were exactly thirteen gifts all neatly laid out on the table. I started opening the gifts one by one. There was food, jewelry, an electric toothbrush that I wanted so badly,clothes and nail polish. These were the perfect gifts any thirteen year old girl could ask for. I thanked my parents and went back to sleep. But I couldn't sleep because I was very excited for the rest of the day. My day started off on a good note.I left for school at 7 am sharp, I didn't want to be late on my birthday. As soon as I entered the bus my friend gave me a birthday card. It was so cute, I couldn't help giving her a hug. It was a Tuesday and a busy one too, so I wasn't expecting much fun and only studies, but to my surprise we had a special assembly on the occasion of children's day. It was one day ago but our school couldn't celebrate because of the picnic for the 9th, 10th and 11th graders. It was a wonderful sight! The teachers danced and sang to their heart's content which made the students really happy. Everyone of us was enjoying it a lot!! After the assembly we went back to our classes. The rest of the day was fun, we didn't have to study much and we got to play a lot. After coming home my mom surprised me with my favorite dish and dessert, pasta and macrons. I was so content, I gulped the whole thing down. After some time I left for my tuition. I distributed chocolates to all my fellow classmates. They all wished me and then we sat down to study. After the tuition ended I went home. We decided to have dinner at my favorite restaurant. When we left my dad told us that he is going to come to the restaurant with my grandparents. When we reached I was shocked and at loss of words when I saw my Grandma. Her face was covered in blood. I was so scared. I asked my dad what had happened. He told me that she had met with an accident, but she insisted on coming to the restaurant because she didn't want to miss my 13th birthday dinner. I was so sad. None of the family members uttered a single word for the rest of the dinner. Her love for me left me speechless.I couldn't help it anymore. I insisted that we go home or to a nearby clinic. But she kept saying that she was doing fine. The food that we ate was suddenly tasteless. Luckily it was only a minor injury. But I will never forget this birthday as it was like one I never had before. From this experience, I realized that things don't always go as per plan and we should always be prepared for whatever comes ahead of us even though we can never predict it. We should remind ourselves that this too shall pass and this phase is only temporary. We should also try not to keep our expectations too high so we don't disappoint ourselves.
author: Parineeta Ranade

title: Love, Amir
text: I think of my childhood, my first thought is always Zaafirah. The faces of my parents come later, their images crude and grainy. Her long, curly blonde hair, her high cheekbones, straight nose and green eyes are crystal clear in my mind. The downside to remembering Zaafirah is the gut-clenching feeling of guilt, shame, anger and sorrow that always seem to accompany thoughts of her. I remember everything about her which is more a curse than a blessing. The emotions in her eyes when I looked at them last, still give me nightmares. To atone for all that I have done wrong in my life and every bit of hardship I caused you, this is for you, my brave and beautiful sister. February 1980 (22 years back) Our family lived in Kabul, back in the days when it was a haven of the educated and the rich. We lived in a big house, too big for our family of five – my sister Zaafirah, my brother Abdul, my mother and father and of course me. It was a happy family, and I spent the first years of my life in bliss. When Zaafirah was sixteen years old and I was ten, she came home bursting with pride. “I’ve been selected for the finals of the relay race”, she proclaimed, her head held high and her cheeks flushing with pride. My parents, who had been talking in worried tones and hushed voices about ‘Soviets’ and ‘Communism’ instantly brightened. My feeling of elation increased when she picked me up and swung me about laughing and saying, “Aren’t you proud of your amshira, Amir? She’s going to make you proud! Oh! Life is perfect!” April 1980 When the day of the competition finally arrived, it was with a sense of gloom. Just the image of the Soviets with their Kalashnikovs, and the distant sound of gunfire and bombing by the mujahideen were enough to dampen our spirits. In those two months, my parents seemed to have aged ten years, the anxiety of caring for their family during a war catching up with them. But they still smiled brightly along with Abdul as Zaafirah and I left for the competition. The only thing I remember about the competition is Zaafirah’s joy at winning before a person pulled us both aside to tell us our house had been bombed. When Zaafirah saw the charred remains of our house, she screamed like I had never heard before, one filled with rage, grief and terror. She screamed and screamed until her throat was so dry, that no sound came out. But throughout all this, she did not drop me from her arms. She hugged me closer as her knees buckled with the realization that we both were the only ones of our family left alive. We stayed there all night in confused agony, clutching the only other person in the world we loved and were left with. November 1980 Zaafirah stepped up to the role of becoming my guardian. We both refused to be parted from each other even after reaching the over-crowded and under-funded orphanage. The corridors became our refuge, since we couldn’t enter each other’s dormitories. The condition of the orphanage was pathetic with rats and insects everywhere, hardly any protection from the cold nights of Kabul and a piece of mouldy bread to eat if we were lucky. War had come to Kabul. Children who were turned away from the orphanage by the warden, Hafiz Khan, starved on the streets. Hafiz Khan was taken in by Zaafirah’s charm and let us both do whatever we wanted. She spent her days teaching me English, Russian and Pashto, Maths and Science, all the while hiding the anxiety and emptiness she must have been feeling. After all, she was only a child, trying to survive in a brutal world while taking care of another. On Zaafirah’s seventeenth birthday, I scavenged the entire orphanage for anything I could give her. I finally found an old and worn copy of Rumi’s poems and gave it to her with an inscription on the inside. When she read it, she cried for a long time. She looked at me with anguished eyes and gave me a watery smile as she said, “Tashakkor Amir. Thank you so much.” April 1981 The situation in Kabul only became worse as time passed, and soon the anniversary of our parents’ death had arrived. Zaafirah craved solitude, preferring to spend long periods of time slowly rifling through the pages of the book I had given her, rather than in the company of others. One day, she left me alone and knocked on Hafiz Kaka’s door, asking for an audience. She talked to him for a long time. When she came out, she told me to pack my bags and get ready to leave. Even though I was confused, I had complete trust in Zaafirah and did what she asked. In her hand, she held a set of papers. She hid it in her burqa, something I had never seen her wear. She grabbed my hand and we left with Hafiz Kaka in a hurry. I didn’t even look back at the orphanage, not knowing I would never return. We ran all the way to the train station and then it hit me. We were leaving for Pakistan, something Zaafirah had long wanted to do, but I believed would never happen. “Come on, Amir, faster. Be careful here. You have to be quiet.” I nodded. Hafiz Kaka stepped in front of me to show our papers. He picked me up and began walking but I heard a cold voice behind us, talking to Zaafirah, “Why exactly are you carrying drugs with you?” My blood ran cold. She must have offered to transport drugs for money to afford going to Pakistan. We continued walking and suddenly I heard the same scream I had heard a year back. I tried to run back towards her in a panic, but Hafiz Kaka held me tightly, saying, “Amir, no! Don’t do it!” My sobs and calls of “Amshira, amshira!” mixed in the air with Zaafirah’s scream of “Amir! Go! RUN NOW!” She was being dragged away by the soldiers. I met her eyes and saw the intense pain in them. She screamed one more time and was lost to me forever. July 1992 (11 years later) Hafiz Kaka and I had lived in Peshawar for eleven years till I became twenty two. After years of searching, I finally received news of Zaafirah. It felt like somebody was ripping my heart out of my chest. For the past eleven years, I had heard nothing of Zaafirah. In my darkest moments, I even considered the idea that she was dead. However, I persevered, using Hafiz Kaka’s money and paid people to search for her. I couldn’t even begin to imagine the horrors they were about to tell me of her life. Till the arrival of the Taliban in Kabul, Zaafirah worked as a teacher and spent her time in various shelters as she had no home. However, after the Taliban arrived, they banned women from working and closed down the shelter. She became homeless, foraging for food wherever she could find it. Unable to bear this situation, she had tried to escape again but she was caught and sentenced to death for stealing and going against the inane laws of the Taliban. I listened to all this and worse with barely controlled agony. In a moment of clarity, I lied to Hafiz Kaka and left home, hiring a car to go back into Kabul. I would not leave Zaafirah alone anymore, knowing she was alive. Kabul had changed completely. I couldn’t reconcile this place with the happy memories I had of my past. Each day, I came and watched all the executions hoping against hope that I would find Zaafirah. It was sickening but I was willing to endure anything to save her. And then, a day before I was due to leave, I saw her. Her golden hair no longer shone and her nose seemed to be broken. But her eyes had remained the same. She was holding a book in her hands and she looked down, opened it and smiled. She mumbled, “Tashakkor,” as she was shot in the head. It felt like I couldn’t breathe. It was too quick, too fast. I didn’t even get a chance to say goodbye. I ran over, pushing through the crowd, images of Zaafirah filling my head. I picked up the old, worn book from her hands, still warm and opened it to see the inscription I had written one cold October, twelve years ago- “To my Amshira, mada-jaan, baba-jaan, Zaafirah. I love you so very much. - Amir, your brother” Suddenly, there were droplets on the book. It was a beautiful day.

title: A Disastrous Passion
text: A Disastrous Passion - Abhijith Sujith Krishna This is Mahila Bhavan, a place full ecstasy, joy, vibrancy and loads of extravaganza. In this mansion, located at the divine town of Rameswaram, lives an old man. He is Aadinathan Iyer. Next to him sits his frail, old yet humble wife, Savitri. They gave birth to 3 twin sisters. These wonderful triplets were named Kaamakshi, Meenakshi and Vishalakshi. Kaamakshi and Vishalakshi later gave birth to 2 fabulous children each Vishalakshi’s daughter was named Samudra Rani, while Kaamakshi son, ME, was named Aditya. Though my mother and aunts were born together, they have very different likes and hobbies. Aunt Vishalakshi, whom I fondly call Aunt Vi, has a passion towards ophthalmology. She always loves to treat people, and that too free of cost. When I asked her why, she replied, that the grateful smile of her patients is her payment. She is a successful ophthalmologist and owner of Vishalakshi ophthalmology centre, Rameswaram. Then comes my Mother, Kamakshi. My mother is an expert when it comes towards chemistry. She knows all kind of things related to chemistry and has even won national level debates and quizzes on sciences. She now teaches Chemistry at Rameswaram Public School. Finally, comes my aunt Meenakshi, and she is the person who pesters me the most. Aunt Meenu has a disastrous passion towards Ayurveda. Her main job is now lecturing on the family members to support her experiments. The first time she proposed such an idea, I and Samudra sprang to action. The rest of the family tried to stop us but we were too adamant. Now, we both wish that we had listened to their warnings. We went to what Aunt Meenu called an ayurvedic lab. There we found a shelf containing a collection of most famous medicinal plants like ashwagandha, muleti, neem, tulsi and what not. “I am going to make a medicine” she proclaimed, and ran off to a cellar. She came back with a bottle containing a bright brown liquid. She crushed up a bit of medicinal herbs and put it into a pot almost brimming with water. She then added the brown liquid to it, turned the heat on and told us, “It will be ready after 5 minutes, everybody wait for my wonderful elixir to set.” After 5 minutes, a huge noise came from aunt’s lab. We went there to check and to our horror found that droplets of that brown liquid were exploding all over the room. The lab was a mess. “My plants!!!!” Aunt cried. Suddenly a voice came from the terrace, “Aditya, did you see the bottle of undiluted alcohol I kept in the old cellar. I saved it up for an experiment.” Everybody froze with terror. Well, you can guess what happened after this incident. About a month later, Aunt Meenu came again, this time with what was a nuclear bomb in her hand. She handed everybody brochures that said “Inauguration of Mahilaropyam Ayurveda Ltd. on 4 November 2022, MD – Ms. Meenakshi Aadinathan” This was bad news already, but it was 10 seconds later that I realized that huge trouble was afoot. Aunt Meenu had made me in charge of assisting her! “What about Samudra? I asked. She told that she forced Samudra a lot of times to support but she did not want to assist me. “.Please, Aadi, you are my only hope.”, she pleaded. Finally I gave in. I have to admit, but nowadays, Mahilaropyam is working out loads better than I expected. We are having a lot of business nowadays. Though my Aunt Sometimes makes stupid mistakes, like giving manchaneel apples to customers instead of gooseberries, we daily have a fresh crowd waiting for our medicines. Yesterday, Aunt Meenu bought me a bicycle for assisting her for so long. I saw Samudra’s eyes glow green with envy. Now Aunt Meenu is working as an Ayurveda specialist in the Raghava Ayurveda Centre, with a salary of 15,000 rupees per month. She also is conducting webinars and classes on Ayurvedic benefits twice every week. And guess what? Samudra joins in every single one of them! The entire family is also in great support with Aunt Meenu. My mom often talks about us and our achievements in her class. Aunt Vi recommends our medicines for patients with eye problems. And my peers treat me like a VIP in class. Aunt Meenu says that I should learn and experiment more to create wonderful medicines like those of hers. Any way, when I am planning to conduct an experiment, I am going to look out for bright brown liquids.
author: Abhijith Krishna

title: Believe in yourself
text: Long long ago,there was villagenamed Tulsimukh. Everyone in that village were happy and lived a happy life. There was a festival called 'Bihu' coming. All were busy in the preparations but two children were alone. They both wanted friends but none of them had any. One of the children named Golu was a ten year old boy and the other named Sovik was an eight eight year old boy. On 'Uruka' (the day before Bihu) Golu was walking in the Pothar (harvested crop field),suddenly he slipped in the mud and got injured. There Sovik was walking too, Sovik saw that a boy slipped in the mud, he suddenly went near the boy and asked him 'Are you OK?' and helped him to get up.Golu was injured so he couldn't walk properly. Seeing this Sovik helped him to walk. Sovik said that 'I will help you to get home'.Golu said yes please help me,I am in a bad condition. Sovik asked him so many things like - What he was doing there? Where he lived? etc. Sovik asked him to introduce himself. Golu said " I am Golu a ten year old boy and I live in this village. Sovik told him about himself that his name is Sovik, he lived in this village he was eight. On reaching Golu's home Sovik told all the things that had happened to golu's mother. Hearing this Golu's mother thanked him for saving her son. Sovik said that Golu is injured and that he should be taken care. Then he came back to his home and shared all his experinces with his mother. His mother asked him if he had invited them or not to their home for the festival? He said yes The next day Sovik went to Golu's house and asked him how was he feeling now. Golu said he was feeling good. So Sovik asked Golu's mother to come to their home. They went to Sovik's home and enjoyed the festival. Golu and Sovik became best of friends and always played together after their school. One day, both of them went to a jungle near their village. Golu accidently fell into a well and started to shout for help. Hearing this Sovik came near the well and shouted 'Where are you Golu?' Golu said the whole story. Hearing this Sovik started searching for someone who could help them but no one was there. Sovik found a bucket and a rope, he tied a knot between the bucket and the rope and threw that to the well and said to get into the bucket. Golu got into the bucket. Sovik started to pull the rope, he pulled the rope as hard as possible and at the end Golu finally got out of the well. They then went back to the village and told their whole story to everyone. No one believed their story but a wise man did. Everyone believed that the man was really wise. So, everyone asked him how an eight year old boy can lift a ten year old boy. The man said, as the two boys said how Sovik had done that. People said that the question is not that who done that. The question is that how a little boy can lift a bigger one by himself. The man said, imagine the situation and now listen to me, there was no one to tell Sovik that he can't do that not even Sovik said to himself that he can't do that. Thats how Sovik lifted Golu. MORAL: Don't listen to anyone who demotivates you,listen to those who motivate you and always trust yourself and believe yourself. No matter what the situatio is.
author: Riki Das

title: Journey To A New Planet!
text: It is the year 2355. A new planet was discovered! Riya, who loved everything about space and astronomy wanted to explore it. “But the thing is,” she muttered to herself “How do I get there…?” She laid on her bed, thinking for a way to go there. Until, she remembered her elder brother, Aditya was an Astro physician. “Ah I can ask my brother to take me there in his spaceship.” Riya says to herself. She goes to his lab and as expected, he was doing his research on stars and other stuff. She tells Aditya how she wants to explore the new planet. “Please,” says Riya “Please just this one time!” “But it may be dangerous, it still hasn’t been proved that its safe.” Aditya explains. She kept requesting him to go. At last, Aditya hesitantly agreed. Both of them flew off the earth on a cold night. Riya jumped in excitement. On reaching the earth’s atmosphere, Riya looks out the window, stunned. “Why do stars look so tiny from the earth?” questioned Riya “The stars aren’t actually tiny,” replies Aditya “They’re big balls of fire and hot gases. They’re just very far away from the earth, this is why they look tiny.” She was quite astonished hearing that. “Oh, we’re almost there.” Aditya says. The planet had a greenish blue colour and had a giant, I mean a very giant spot on it. It was almost the size of the Earth. The spaceship landed, they got out and looked around. Riya’s dream finally came true! He looked for things to research on, while she just wandered around. On a distance, she saw something coming towards her. “What’s that?” she says in her mind and begins to slowly walk towards it. As she went on and on, she realised it was a storm, travelling at a great speed. She was petrified to the core of her heart. Riya runs to her brother, almost in tears and shaking with fear. Aditya who was examining the soil and stones of the planet, looked sceptically at Riya. But as the storm was fast approaching, Aditya quickly got up, held Riya’s hand tightly and rushed to the space ship. He started the spaceship, as his hands trembled. Unfortunately, the spaceship takes time to initiate.. Riya covered her face with her hands, frightened that the storm would hit them. Riya can’t recall how long the moments of fear went by, but when she opened her eyes, the storm was gone and everything was silent as before. Fortunately, the storm couldn’t hit them. “Sister!” Aditya exclaims, “Are you alright?”. Riya nodded with a sign of relief, “Yes, luckily it didn’t hit us.”. “But, what just happened right now” She asked after calming down. Aditya took a deep breath and explained that a storm just occurred. It was so strong that if it hit someone, they would have flown away with it. Not all the planets have storms, like the Mercury, whereas planets like Jupiter and Saturn have huge storms. Finally, the spaceship gets started and Riya, Aditya zooms towards the Earth. “I just want to go home.” Riya sighs. A sign of relief appeared on their faces as the screen announces, ‘ Landing on Earth now… ’ The doors of the spaceship opened, the both of them rush out and realised that they landed on a field. “Where are we?” Riya asks as she looked around. “I guess this is a field.” Aditya replies. “Ohh, what a nice and safe feeling to be on Mother Earth, no place is better in this Universe than our own Earth”, mutters Riya. “I’m really tired… Lets go home.” She said. “Alright then, lets go home now.” Aditya smiled.
author: Doreina Choudhury

title: Chess A Game Of Life
text: And to her surprise it was her grandfather who came from Bhopal to visit her. She was very happy to see her grandfather and she hugged him. After having their lunch, Labdhi's grandfather and her father were playing chess. She went to them and asked them about what they were doing. Her father replied,"We are playing chess". She was in wonder and wanted to learn about the game of chess. Her grandfather taught her how to play chess. She practiced for days and days and finally one day came when she had went to a tournament and won her first gold medal in chess at the age of only 6 years. After getting encouragement by her parents and coaches, she went to many tournaments and won many prizes. Her parents were overwelmed by her performance. For tournaments, she visited many places like Hyderabad, Udaipur, Ujjain, Bhopal and may more. Soon she was filled with a feeling of haughtiness and started behaving rude to everyone and was left alone. She had abolished her good memories. Her parents helped her to get out from this phase of her life. There came a new virus which affected Labdhi's two years of excellence. She had lost hope in the game of chess and decided to dock it from her life. After covid-19 her coach motivated her to come back and play chess again. Labdhi was influenced by her coach's motivation. And soon she again started playing chess and just as the earlier days she started winning a lot of prizes and found out that her true talent was chess.
