title: Escape to the Past
text: Today John is leaving his mother, Linda, in an old age home. He had been planning this for a very long time and was finally relieved to do so. He was financially struggling and his mother had started growing old. She would get sick very often and had to be taken care of constantly. Not only that, John had plenty of other worries and he was extremely busy with work. John felt it was best if he left his mother in a safe place where she would get the care she needed, and at the same time he would be able to focus fully on his job. Ever since John’s father passed away, Linda had started feeling the shadow of solitude, but now that her own son was leaving her, she couldn’t feel more lonely. Not wanting to pick fights with her son, she agreed to go to the old age home without even a single complaint. Linda waved her son a final goodbye before he drove off in the distance. She could see the car vanishing into the narrow road and that made her feel like her only source of happiness was vanishing too. Shortly after, she headed to her assigned room and sat down on the bed. She looked at the family photo she had taken with her before coming, and started to wonder how far life had taken her. She never had thought this day would come. She had imagined spending the last few moments of her life with her loved ones, but now she had been left to spend it all alone. All those simple wishes of her going to a beach with her family or eating dinner together after John had come home from a long day of work shattered into pieces in front of her teary eyes. As days passed, Linda started becoming tired of staying in the retirement home. She didn’t want to spend the little time she had left in this life here, in this place thinking of all the things that could have been. She wanted to make those wishful moments true. So, she came up with a plan. She would escape this place. She remembered going to the beach with John when he was little. John loved the sea and loved to swim. He would build sandcastles and catch crabs with his bare hands and stare at them with awe while she would take pictures of him doing all his usual antics at the beach. This beach truly held a lot of special memories and Linda wanted nothing but to relive them all. However, escaping this place wasn’t going to be an easy task and moreover, she would definitely need some money. Linda planned that first she would have to lie to the caretakers by telling them that she was going out for a short walk. After that, she would take a train to the town where the beach was. Finally, her wish would be fulfilled. The following day came and Linda was ready to put her plan into action and everything went as she had envisioned. Although the caretakers were a bit hesitant at first, they let her go thinking it would bring her a bit of joy. Linda took her belongings and escaped the retirement home. Finally, after a long time she felt free. Free of all her burden and worries. All her sadness turned into hope for a better end. She withdrew some money from a nearby ATM machine and bought a train ticket. The conductor was a bit shocked seeing an old lady like her traveling alone, but this didn’t matter to Linda. She was lost in her imagination where she was already enjoying and reliving the best moments of her life at the beach. However, back at the retirement home, Linda’s disappearance worried all the caretakers. They remembered Linda telling them that she would be going out for a short walk and that she would be back in a few minutes, but now hours had passed and she was nowhere to be found. They called the police and they immediately started searching. This news reached John who became furious seeing the negligence of the caretakers. He could not believe how they would simply let a woman of her age go off to the streets without sending someone to look after her. He went to the retirement home and confronted them about their actions. They explained how all her belongings were missing, so they all suspected, including the police, that this had been carefully planned by Linda. They continued explaining how it was actually common for people in old age homes to escape due to the extreme loneliness and helplessness they experience after staying away from their loved ones. Now John had started to feel guilty. He loved his mother immensely, there was no doubt in his heart about that. The thought of never being able to meet his mother again terrified him. He couldn’t think of any good reason as to why his mother would decide to suddenly leave everything to go somewhere all by herself, and if she did go somewhere, where could that place be? At that moment, he remembered her mother telling him about how she really wanted to go to the beach one day. To the beach where they used to go when he was little. John had refused to take her there, as it was quite far from where he lived now and he didn't have enough time to go for any kind of vacation mainly because of work. This conversation had taken place just a few weeks before he had left his mother here. John who previously thought of his mother to be a burden, regretted every of his actions. He wanted to correct his mistake and the only way he felt he could do so was by finding his mother and bringing her back home, their true home. That’s when something tells him to go to that beach. The train finally halted at her destination. She got off the train and looked around. Nostalgia engulfs her and thousands of emotional and old memories flood her mind. This town holds a special place in her heart as this was the town where her family once lived together, happily. She wanted to experience again the moments she had once spent with her loved ones, even though at present nobody was there by her side. With a heavy heart, she walked towards the bus stop. On the bus, looking outside the window, she couldn’t help but think about how she was all alone in this world and how time had changed everything around her. It was a strange feeling. She was feeling helpless but she also felt calm and peaceful. The bus stopped at the beach which she had longed to see for so long. She slowly got off the bus as she became very tired due to the long journey. As soon as she saw the beach from a distance, all her tiredness faded away. The light ocean breeze hit her face bringing her back to the past. The bright blue sky and the emerald ocean left her feeling relaxed and calm. She felt free and happy as she walked near the shoreline. Feeling the cold ocean water with her hands, she couldn’t have felt more alive. The emotions of awe invoked a feeling of connection with the beauty of nature and with her beautiful past. She felt blessed to have lived such a joyful life. She thought how stars couldn’t shine without darkness. Although the feelings of loneliness and helplessness managed to bring darkness to Linda's life, her old memories of spending time with her family and doing the things she loved the most were always there in her heart. Memories had the power to light this haunting darkness. She was reliving her past and enjoying the present moment. Hours passed and she decided to go back to the old age home. Her wish was fulfilled and she felt much lighter than before. She had accepted her present and was finally happy to go back when she saw a young man running towards her. Linda stared in shock as she recognized the man to be her son. John stopped and stared at her mother. They locked eyes and silence set in. “Mom, let’s go back to our true home, where we truly belong,’ said John.
author: Sakura Saha
illustrator: Julie  Smith-Belton; Aaryama Somayaji; Manjari Chakravarti; Parmita Mukherjee; Rajiv Eipe; Siddhi   Vartak

title: Dear Monkey
text: It was summer I guess when mom bought me you. A day lit with the scorching sunrays but it doesn’t affect me with sunburns, so I find my pleasure in this weather. Me, accompanied with my boater, and my mother were on the way to the street markets for buying the starters of summer season. While she was busy haggling with the vegetable seller, I saw you sitting at the corner of a very old shop, by the way it looked so, filled with toys like you. I started pulling on my mother’s last piece of kurta to get her attention towards you. After the contention, I showed her you and she agreed to buy me you in one go since I was not like the ‘always needy children’. But I doubt if my decision was good enough now. My father hung you high in between the two sides of a door. While you were meant for hanging, I used to watch you closely all the time. Having the resemblance of half a monkey, half a bear, with a nose like that of a beak of a bird. Brown colored but without any fur, with big round eyes and a hanging tie behind your neck to hang you. You were all simple, but the thing my mother found weird was that you spoke while you were stuffed with fur from within, you weren’t porcelain. But I saw you more like a monkey. Mother figured out that when we make a sound with the sole of our foot, you ask to say something. One day I found an exciting thing about you, and hence while mother was out, I used to say to you to sing me the lines you rhymed. I even remember some which you sang all the time as- “See the rising sun, see the sunshine, See me looking at you, from the void of lies, See the rising king, whose queen is Miss Nine, As she ate all the nine monkeys in her dine.” At that time I couldn’t even make the meaning out of it, and guess I never can too as I wonder why you were always like this, singing things, telling whom? You didn’t talk back but you wished us the good mornings and good nights. I wasn’t a much fan of figuring out stuffs which are hard to understand, but mom did. She felt it was weird of you of the timing when you spoke. The way she calculated when you talked wasn’t much of a help because you started talking whenever you liked. It wasn’t a sound or a tick to make you start or any buttons in you to stop it, and I still wonder how you were able to rock the sales in markets. Everything was going good but after few weeks, days started getting odd. One night, I woke up to watch a video playing in your belly. I still don’t know if it was a dream but I feel like it wasn’t. Hazy buzz on busy streets, where people were walking down the aisle to do chores, while in the back, as I saw, shops were flooded with toys like you. You were singing the ‘Money’ poem, one of the few present in your mind cassettes, while I slept watching the tape. “Money, money, money, what a wondrous chime, But watch what it brought you, a harbinger of crime.” I never fancied a shut down on the things which were unusual, but those things didn’t stand a chance in front of mom. She threw you inside the drawer of bed after facing an irritation of your inevitable talking. But as the house went silent in afternoons, she used to hear a scratching sound echoing in the hollow drawers. And as she went to check, it was a sight of horror for me too, as I saw the scratched marks on the inside walls, when I knew you had no nails. We didn’t throw you away early because we thought all these happenings were very much normal for we didn’t liked wasting money, for any hypothetical reason. But you know the neighbors, they know everything. The thing was that our neighbor had also bought a similar monkey like you and she also experienced the same with you. As a result, she did throw you out in the backyard ditches of our apartment, for she was very much concerned about bad things. I eavesdropped on their conversation with my mom one day from behind the curtains, when I got to know another poem which you sang in their house which was unfamiliar as you never sang this one for me- “Sun feeds a desert, same as time feeds you, Truth is buried under, to reap a tree of lies in you.” The lady was so scared for she witnessed an eye-wrenching episode of you. At night, in her house, while she was standing in the hallway, drinking a glass of water, she watched your eyes gleam with a red light as you sang these to her. Maybe she understands much more than me the words of you for she threw you out the other morning. They talked that afternoon, when I stood there staring deep into your eyes for the red lights. The time was not far when you would leave this city. Mother dumped you the next day in the backyard but guess what? You cling to the fence as mom reached her full height potential. It was no wonder that you certainly were an unusual toy to be kept. The next day the city cleaning van came and they took you to a different place, a place much out of my thinking area. But I still try to think about your presence in this world, because somewhere I still do want to hear your poems again. This doesn’t have any roots to begin with but if I am being honest, I think my summer was also gone with you.
author: Shwetanjali Shrivastava

title: The Mystery Of The Hidden Stream
text: It was 6 a.m. on a fine Sunday morning in the quiet, hilly town of Bareilly. Meera, Sonu, and Manu were seated in their usual hideout – the garden near the guesthouse - planning their Sunday routine. “Hey!” said Meera, pointing to the hilltop in front. “Did you hear any rumors about that place?” Tara jumped in, “Oh yes! I heard my mother discussing a weird sound coming from the hilltop during the night.” Sonu said, “Why not try and find out what this is all about? Are you both game for this?” “Of course. Let’s go. Maybe we will get to meet a ghost,” retorted Meera. “Interesting. But maybe, it is a wild hyena lost from its pack (just like in fairy tales!),” said Manu. Sonu jumped up saying, “Let’s get moving folks! We don’t have any time to waste. We must use our Sunday to investigate.” After readying their supplies, the three musketeers set out to the hills to unravel the source of the mysterious sound. Within a few hours of their fruitless search, Manu started losing interest. He said, “Meera, now this is getting boring. We have been trekking and searching for some probable source, but no clue yet… Don’t you think we better run home?” His suggestion was immediately rejected by his two siblings who were adamant. “No way, Meera. I am sure we will find something interesting,” said Sonu. So, they continued... It was nearing noon. With no luck in sight, exhaustion started creeping in. They decided to break for lunch. Manu and Sonu seized this opportunity to doze off. Suddenly a loud shout shook them up from their sweet slumber. It was Meera calling out to them. “Manu, Sonu, come near the hedge fast! Hey, be quick!!” They sensed the excitement in her tone and immediately ran in the direction of her sound. The hedge was surrounded by beautiful flowers, tiny shrubs, and lush green grass. Meera was seen lying with her ears pressed toward the ground. Surprised, Manu said, “Meera, what in the world are you trying to do there?” She replied in a hushed voice, “Shhh… Look! I think I have found the cause of that mysterious sound. Press your ears here and listen silently.” Sonu and Manu followed her instructions. They could not believe their ears. They were thrilled to hear a faint gurgling sound coming from the shrubs. They pushed the shrubs aside and found a lovely, little stream flowing down the slope, singing its sweet tune! Sonu yelled, “Meera, we found it. Yayy!” They looked in wonder at each other. Meera proudly exclaimed, “It is a hidden stream! And guess what, we, the three musketeers, are probably the first to discover it!” The three tasted the water. It was sweet! Fresh and pure water! They stayed for a while near the hedge, relishing the surroundings and splashing their legs in the running stream, watching the last rays of the sun disappear behind the hills. “Let’s get back home now before someone comes looking for us,” quipped Manu. “Yes Manu, you’re right. We will reveal the source of the sound to the whole world tomorrow morning. Just imagine, what a discovery we have made,” said Sonu. “But why did no one find it till now?” wondered Meera. “I remember mother saying about someone having tried investigating but the fear of the ghost had taken the better of him. Since then, no one, I think, dared a repeat attempt,” said Meera. Sonu immediately chipped in, “The reason why the stream was not heard by the nearby villagers, all these years, remains a mystery… Probably, it was waiting to be found by us THE THREE MUSKETEERS!” Manu proudly corrected him “We – the three brave musketeers… Yahoo!” Guys, when’s our next mission coming up?” Meera and Sonu burst into laughter…
author: ANJALI MENON
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Amalendu Kaushik; Krishna Bala Shenoi; Maithili  Joshi; Maya  Ramaswamy; Sangeetha Kadur; Shivam Choudhary

title: A TRUE FRIEND-DAISY
text: On a cloudy day, sparkling eyes gazing from the window were on me as if were in a need of favor. As I approached the window, I found a very cute fairy white puppy with soft and tender paws and was of fear- shivering and was in search of warmth to comfort his tender soul. So, I decided to take her under my care and then me and my little one decided to share our home together. Gradually, my routine started fixing in her mind. whenever I used to eat, she also used to sat by me and ate whatever I offered her. And, w henever I used to go to sleep she would lay down on the furry golden blanket which I specially got for her. All this was going like a perfect fantasy dream where I had a friend to share all my joys and sorrows to her and she would sit down patiently listen as if she could understand what I was talking about. Suddenly after a month Daisy fell ill. Now, she would not eat for hours just would sit next to the window looking outside seeing the sky as if it was calling her. I told my parents about the liable condition of poor Daisy. They immediately, rushed towards the doctor. After running some diagnosis- he came to a conclusion that Daisy was infected by viral infection and from now onwards some days are left for little life to live. Coming out of the clinic, as I was upset and I cried a lot. But my father tried to comfort me and told me the truth of life that 'a being who comes to life with happiness has to leave his loved ones crying behind'. These words got stuck in my mind forever but now I started observing the positive moments with daisy- her eating habits, her restful face, her happy eyes while playing, her tail flying in the air with joy. This made me realised whatever time I spent with daisy not even a single second got wasted of her and simultaneously not mine. But in my hearts pf heart i still prayed for her recovery and parents didn’t left any stone unturned to save her life. A week later, when I went to the clinic, Daisy with her tearful eyes gazed towards me as if was in a need of hug. For me this moment became disheartening as I saw my favorite creature in pain. The doctor told there were no chances of her survival but this was a miracle which happened to her by god’s wish. He also mentioned that Daisy’s one leg got paralized due to her illness. But I only was worried about her survival and went to my lovely and beautiful daisy who was in pain and was scared to the core as she was in pain. I lifted her up and hugged her with tears dropping from her eyes. After returning from clinic, I sincerely took care of her. And simultaneously my father consulted tons of doctor for getting her leg recovered. But our hard work felt as if going in vain as there were no signs of improvement in her leg. We started loosing our motivation and got disheartened. Then one day my father was reading through the daily paper and he found about a very nice specialist for the matter – “heads up for tails”. Our faces lift up with happiness and hope for her recovery. Then for a month or so the treatment continued when her leg showed about 40 percent of movement. Another asteroid hit us up - Daisy haf got into an accident with a bike. When I left the door opened so she just went for a walk but the fate had written something else for her. Then again we rushed towards the clinic where her treatment was going on but this time the doctor told us that the condition of her leg had become more worse and there nothing anymore left he could do for her. This incident disturbed me alot, I started gazing only about her and in my school. When lectures were going on and this also resulted in a huge drop in my academics. On a very fine day, my younger brother was playing football with his friends. Suddenly, their ball got stuck inside a wheel. Looking at this playful scene, my little Daisy came running towards them to help them to get their ball free from the wheel. But I wasn’t concerned about my ball because my eyes were stuck at Daisy’s run with her three legs and this made me happy and jolly at the same moment because her charm and playfulness was back. At night when I was preparing my bed my mind was engrossed with multiple thoughts but in hearts of hearts I was happy at the fact that she was able to walk back and play with full energy despite her hurdles. On 21st 20XX, my mom got promotion to a very nice position. So, her work commitments require us to transfer to another city. And then when we went to see our new home in a government society, dogs were not allowed there due to safety reasons. My mom told me we could do nothing but had to give our precious Daisy to our neighbours. This made me really upset but because I had seen Daisy since she was just a little creature to a fully grown dog. I had so many emotions attached to her as she was my only best friend. Then after this talk with my mom, days went by when I started noticing change in Daisy’s behaviour in terms of her daily routine including how happily she used to eat her dog food and how she used to disturb me to grab my attention. I was confused whether I was leaving behind my best friend or my adopted child. Those moments were really difficult for me as my heart was in pain seeing my lovely dog with tearful eyes. The bond and emotions with which we connected was tough and all memories and moments which were happy and sad were running through my mind as a fresh picture. I can say those were the hardest moments in my life as saying goodbye was not easy and put me in a lot of pain which made me realise how much I was attached to this lovely being. When I came to my new home, I was missing her a lot. So, I decided to put a photo frame filled with me and Daisy’s memories to make me feel a little better. I somewhere knew that as much pain I was experiencing, Daisy was going through the same. After 2 years, when I graduated high school, I asked my parents that if I could go to our old home town to spend some time in peace. While I was coming back, I thought how Daisy would react after seeing me in so many years? When I went to my neighbours I greeted them with a bouquet of flowers and chocolates and they welcomed me in. After sometime, I noticed Daisy was not there so I felt insecure. So I instantly asked where was she. They told me with a sad face that Daisy waited for me outside my house for every single day in hope of my return until she passed away by a heart attack in her sleep 6 months ago. Listening to this I could feel nothing but just thought of her pain she had gone through because of me. I could never ever forgive myself for this but the words of my father made me realise once again people come and go so do animals. But she was like my own child. "A dog is the only thing on earth that loves you more than he loves himself."
author: Yana Tanwar
illustrator: Ajanta Guhathakurta; Anupam Arunachalam; Barkha Lohia; Jess  Jardim-Wedepohl; Kalyani  Ganapathy; Madhuri Purandare; Preetam Dhar; Rajiv Eipe; Shamim Ahmed; Shivam Choudhary

title: A Lucid Dream
text: Thomas never grows out of his pranks. Yes, today Sam got a whole big pail of cereal on his head again. No one dares to step up for Sam and talk against Thomas and his gang or famously known as ‘The Undertakers’. Sounds scary, isn’t it? You do not want to experience that. I, Juliet Adams, have never been prone to his pranks because I am invisible to other eyes. You guessed it right; I am that short green girl who will never make friends. I was just so done with my life. My drunkard dad does not care any less about me, all that runs through his mind are young girls. We live in a small dormitory near my university. I am 22 and it’s just been my dad and I for seventeen forlorn years. I had a humdrum routine, which made me lose belief in God and even in living. I do not care much about my life either and so I went to bed. Strange figures, loud shrieks and darkness. A black figure is in front of my eyes. It’s a lady. “Who are you?”, I said to myself not knowing that she could hear me. “I am rosa” “That’s my mother’s name" “I am your mom”, said the black lady figure. We were both sitting on two steel chairs facing each other with a round table before us. Being seated in a dim light, dark color wall room which seemed to be endless, made me perceive this as a haunted experience that I am going to have. With shivers running down my spine I replied in disbelief, “You are not”. She told me things which only my mother and I shared when I was just a toddler. I was too stunned to speak. Having a loss of words all I could do was sob and sob, till it all ended and I could see a ray of light. As I go closer, I find myself waking up as the sun rays pierce through my blinds. ‘It was all just a dream?’, I thought to myself. ‘How could it be so real?’. Another day at college. Another prank. He doesn’t get enough. Does he now? As I made it through another meaningless day. I went to bed, tired of doing nothing and questioning my existence. The same black figure is before my eyes. I believe this is a dream again. In the dark room, with the candles flame burning intensely, silence everywhere. “You do remember me?” she asked. “Yes, I do. What is the meaning of this? Why are you here? What am I doing here?”. “You are here to know your worth dear”. “My worth?”, I asked curiously. “I know what you have been through and what made you question your existence in life. You have to grow out of it. I am here to help you, my child.” I asked her what she knew about me. We talked for hours straight. When the candle melted, I see her no more. I seem to wake up again. This time I noticed that a wax candle was kept on the table which worked as a stopwatch. As it melts the timer runs out and I wake up. I was running late for my college. I pack up and run without brushing my hair or showering. But this time I woke up happier than before. After a long day at college, I was rushing to get home. I realized that I felt better and better every time I encountered my ‘dream mom’. I jump onto my bed with delight and try to fall asleep. All of a sudden, there is a loud thud in the hallway. I turn white. Just then my dad opens my room door and yells at me while he is drunk. I was frightened and threw my books at him. He then slams the door as he leaves. After a while, I finally fall asleep in tears. As I meet my mom, I tell her about the incident. She does everything to console me and says, “Child, forgive me for I could not watch you grow. But you have to promise me this; you will always live your life to the fullest and forget every negative thing around you.” “I will mother, I promise. You do not need to apologize for anything.” And as I say these promising and true words, I wake up to see another bright day I felt energetic, optimistic and a spark of zeal lit inside of me. I was ready to face another day and did not care for anything God threw at me, I was ready to face it all. A few more days passed like this. I felt healed day by day. My grades got better and I started making friends. I enjoyed being a new version of myself. I felt overjoyed to have left the past and move on. Guess what? I got popular. Everyone in college knew about me. Every guy liked me. Every girl wished to be like me. But as great fame paves the way for trouble, my fame too got me into fights. Remember how I told you that you would not likely enjoy experiencing pranks by ‘The Undertakers’? Yes, I do remember being clear about it. Well, my fame made me face that too. The boys glued my pants to the chair. I managed to get up without letting my pants tear. I was pissed off by these pranks! So I decided to do something no one would ever dare to. I spoke up for myself and all those who got pranked and bullied by them. I said ….. “Thomas, I am done with all these pranks of yours. And if you do not stop with this, I am going to have to take a serious action. I am warning you.” “What would you do little brat?”, he replied. Just then I threw a glass of milk at him and left him soaked in it. Everyone applauded as I walked out of the canteen. Thanks to my mom for transforming me into a whole better person. -Naisha R Pawar
author: Naisha Pawar

title: The Greedy Framer
text: The Greedy Farmer Once upon a time, not so very long ago there lived two farmers in a village named Ram and Shyam. Ram was a kind and helpful man to everyone. He was never arrogant and greedy. He had two cows in his shed which was in his field while Shyam was a greedy man and never helped anyone. He ran after money. One day they both met each other at Ram`s field and after some days they became friends. Their fields were next to each other`s field. They started to prepare the field, sowed the seeds and started looking after the crop where Ram showed more attention towards the production of crops and Shyam did not even spare his time properly towards the crop. After some time it was the time of harvest but when they sold their crops in the market they noticed that Ram`s production of crops is more than Shyam. When Shyam saw that the production of crops of Ram is more than his production, he started developing jealousy towards Ram and made him think that he would sell Ram`s cows and burn his crops at night. After he stole the cows and later on he sold them, he got a lot of money. The next day Ram saw that his cows were not there in the shed but the field of Shyam was fully burnt. After a while, Shyam came there and started crying after watching that his field was completely burnt while Ram`s field was completely fine. Shyam realised that he burnt his own field in the dark. This sadness and disappointment made him realise that he was wrong and he said sorry to his friend. At last, Ram forgave Shyam and they both became best friends.
author: Archi Aggarwal

title: Second Chances
text: They say experimental learning is the best. I for one most certainly agree. One such incident that took place during a certain period of my life taught me a valuable lesson. So, here’s how the story goes~ This event took place when I was 9. In my school bus, there was a 10-year-old girl named Anya. You might want to remember her, as she’s the villain of our story. So, this Anya was a bully who liked manipulating other people and playing with them like toys. I know, a little too harsh for a primary school kid, but trust me. She was nothing short of pure evil. Most of the kids in the bus of around our age were part of her ‘gang’ whose life goal was to target one person and make their lives miserable. See what I mean? Rotten to the core. Anyway, I was never in their good books. This was because, I refused to submit to their ‘supremacy’ and was never afraid to shoot back to any snooty remarks thrown my way. One other girl of my own age, named, umm, Ira, was the target of their ruthlessness. You might want to remember her too, as she is the deuteragonist our story and plays a very important role. So, this Ira, was never particularly a bright lamp. Once, she misspelled ‘Audi’ as ‘Ody’ and the others ridiculed her for it. So much so, that she was almost on the verge of tears every time they mercilessly mocked her. One day, when they were being particularly nasty, I put down my book (I often read in the bus), and decided to put an end to this cruelty. I turned to them and told them to buzz off. They glared at me and asked if I was Ira’s bodyguard or something. I told them so if I was and they scowled at me unpleasantly but left us alone anyway. Like this I stood up for Ira three to four times and they eventually stopped bothering her. Ira and I became good friends thereafter. But then something happened that totally shook me. Me and Ira were chatting normally about school life, when suddenly Anya interrupted us and said, “Oh look, it’s the nerd, Gauri!” The others snickered. They often liked to call me that because I was always on top of my class and always had a novel with me. But I wad anything but a nerd. In fact, I was extremely well liked and had tons of friends. Anyway, Anya continued, “Aren’t I right, Ira?”. I started. What was with all the favoritism towards Ira? I glanced at her. She looked hesitant for a moment, and seemed to contemplate the situation, and then nodded somewhat unsurely. I felt as if all the blood was drained out of my body. I was so shocked you could have knocked me down with a feather. That backstabbing, double faced swine! This was how she repaid me for my support? I don’t even remember what happened after that. I don’t remember what I said to Anya or what I did. I was so hurt! So now Ira was part of Anya’s gang. Even though she never actively took part in the vocal bulling, she still never stood up for me. I vowed that I’ll never speak with her again. Things went on like this for some time and I mostly ignored them, only occasionally loosing my temper. Then one day, when Anya had said something to me, before I could retaliate, Ira told Anya sharply, “Shut up Anya, you’re crossing the line now.” And stood up and sat next to me. I was too dumbfounded to react in any way. She smiled at me and apologized to saying that she couldn’t find the strength to stand up to Anya and her minions. I forgave her and we became very close friends. We still are. Later, she revealed to me that she and her mother were going through domestic violence at their home by her father and were in a very rough patch. I was astounded. Everything looked so normal from outside. I was at a loss for words, but this secret brought us even closer. That day I learnt a very important lesson. To always take time to form my judgements about people, because you never know what the other person is going through. And to this day, we remain the closest of friends.
author: Gauri Saxena

title: The Curious Elephant
text: One day, a mother elephant and a baby elephant were drinking from a river. The mother elephant’s name was Lotus and the baby mangrove. The baby was staring at the river curiously. He asked his mother ‘ Where does all this water come from? ‘. His mother answered ‘ it comes from the mountains far away. ‘. Mangrove asked again ‘ and where does all of it go? “. This time the mother said ‘ I will not tell you that for you will be curious to go there and may get hurt. Never try to find out, or else you will get hurt. Mangrove was a very curious elephant. He did not heed to his mother’s warnings. After a long number of activities, he found a way to get away from his mother; ‘mother may I go and get those blueberries you really like’? His mother said yes and off he went. Instead of going to get the berries he followed the river until he heard the sound of falling water. And Mangrove went on until he saw water gushing over enormous rocks. The careless elephant stepped into the river to feel the water - slipped - and down, he fell! Lotus kept searching for Mangrove. She just couldn’t seem to find him anywhere! She called out “ Mangrove! Mangrove, where are you?!” A monkey called Mausam, who witnessed what had happened to Mangrove, heard her and came to Lotus. He told her “I saw a baby elephant fall down the waterfall - is that who you call out for?” “Oh no! I told him not to go there!! Show me where this happened!” cried Lotus. Mausam went to the place where it happened and Lotus cried out “Mangrove!! Mangrove!! Are you there??” Mangrove cried back - from far down the cliff - “here I am! But I’m hurt and need your help!” Lotus tried to find a place where she could climb down the cliff - she found a steep set of rocks where she could climb down and started to descend. Meanwhile, Mangrove, anxious to see his mother - kept calling out “Mummy!!” As she descended, suddenly she saw a bengal tiger spring from behind a bush and began to near Mangrove. Lotus yelled out “Mangrove!! Mangrove!! Behind you… RUN!!” Mangrove looked behind, spotted the tiger, and immediately tried to escape. But, his leg was stuck between two sharp rocks! He cried to his mother… “Help!! My legs are stuck and I can't run!”.The tiger started to growl ferociously. Just before it was about to pounce, a giant eagle swooped down and scratched its’ eyes. The tiger yowled in pain and started to go for the eagle instead of Mangrove. By now, Lotus had already freed Mangrove from the rocks and was starting to back off quickly. Meanwhile, the eagle was starting to win the fight with the tiger and - seeing that Mangrove was safe, and flew away. Lotus yelled out after him - “Thank you kind Eagle for saving my son today!” The Eagle yelled back “Its my pleasure, please don’t worry.” The tiger, by now, had already rushed into the forest, afraid of the eagle. As Lotus and Mangrove slowly made their way back home, Lotus said “This is why I said, you should never try to find out where the water goes. Never be too curious in the jungle.” THE END
author: RAAM HARIHARAN
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Lavanya Karthik; Partho Sengupta; Rohan Dahotre; Ruchi Shah; Seng Visal; Vidula Nene; Wiehan de Jager

title: The Pianist
text: Dear Mahira, I still want to play it with my whole heart, But there’s no one who didn’t tell me it’s hard I would love and learn it, As it’s your last sent gift, It’s the closest to my heart, As you are DEAR BESTFRIEND, I’ll learn it I promise, even if it’s damn hard. Yours truly, Tarz I looked down at her grave, I didn't want to leave; just for another moment let me be there. But the time was short, and the list was long. I had no chances to stay there for five more minutes, so I sat down beside the grave, kept the letter with someone’s favorite shiuli flowers and I prayed to the god, who never heard “D ear god, may her soul rest in peace. And I'll once again ask for something I've been asking for since the last few years. I want to. I really want to play the piano. She gave me.” I walked back without turning around for a moment, tears filled my eyes, like always. Emotions are a human’s all time worst enemy. They kill you inside and make you lonely outside. Four years ago, Mahira died in a car accident. Cars were new at that time and a man who didn’t know how to drive, was driving, and hit my dear Mahira and my right hand was injured. On the day of my birthday, ninth October nineteen fifty. Mahira gifted me a piano. She always told me that my hands were pretty, and they would look so nice playing an instrument. All over these 4 years I tried to join many piano classes, but everyone just told me it’s not possible to play piano with only my left hand. Some of them kept me for money and I was sent in many competitions when I didn't know how to play a single note. I lost every time, and they all insulted me. And I lost my confidence. But for Mahira I wanted to play... I moved to Los Angeles a year ago. This place shares a great relation with me. My dad died here. Seven years ago, he left a 17-year-old girl alone. That girl was me of course. My mother divorced my dad, I lived with my dad and grandmother. But most of the time I stayed with Mahira and her family, my grandmother was a wicked woman, she never thought good of anyone, even of her own son. She poisoned her own son. Imagine a 75-year-old woman poisoned her 47-year-old son. That’s so shameful. Mahira was like my mother, my sister, my aunt, my best friend; she was everything I had. My childhood was pitiful. I was depressed for a long time but then Mahira helped me out. So today, after searching for such a long time, I decided to visit another, pianist, whom I’ve heard of nothing. 'What if she can teach me?' Possibilities and endless! ‘Hello?’ I politely knocked on the door. An old woman with gray hair, blue eyes, an oval face and wrinkles all over the face opened the door. She was a few inches taller than me. She glared at me for a few seconds and said… ‘Black hair, light brown eyes, Pink lips and a bright smile. Small face with a sharp jawline, You must be Tarz? oh dear! darling’ I laughed ‘yes madam, good afternoon! I am here for piano sessions'. She bowed down and welcomed me- ‘Come in! Come in!’ I smiled a thank you, and waited for her to lead the way. She led me to her basement, which was perfect for this cold season. She sat on a chair and offered me- ‘Tea or coffee?’ she asked. ‘Nothing.’ ‘Alright so Tarz, am I pronouncing it right? T-A-R-Z? ‘Yes, Tarz.’ She looked at my hands ‘take off the gloves show me the beauty of your hands!’ I did as she said. I took off the gloves. And I was waiting for her reaction, she smiled politely and took off her gloves and showed me her right hand. ‘My-oh-my! YOU DON’T EVEN HAVE FINGERS?’ I said. I was glad, shocked, excited and worried about what that was! A pianist who doesn’t have fingers in one hand. ‘Well, I lost my fingers when I was ten and I learned the art of playing piano when I was thirteen. I was demotivated and not confident but then I thought of being a different person. And that thought made me this.’ She pointed towards her records and achievements ‘what’s your story?’ I smiled ‘four years back, today on my birthday I lost my best friend and my hand. Her name was Mahira. Mahira always wanted me to play a musical instrument because she told me my hands would look so pretty playing them. And after that I wanted to learn piano. No teacher accepted me. No mentor taught me. But I didn't lose hope, that’s why I am here’ She held my hand and told me ‘I’ll teach you. And I am sure you’ll be a great pianist one day.’ And that’s how it started and made me someone who won life, someone who is a great pianist, someone who made it to the end.
author: Pushti Maini
illustrator: Audrey Agnier; Shivam Choudhary; Tanvi Bhat

title: Roars and trumpets of the jungle.
text: Raj was relaxing by the banyan tree near the river. His herd had finished grazing and were falling asleep or wading into the river for a quick wash. As he watched his father, Aarav, leader of the herd wade into the river, he thought "Why does dad despise the tigers? Does he have any bad history with them? And who is this Talwar?" And with that thought, he dozed off in the cool shade of the tree. Rohan yawned, his parents had gone hunting and he was left in charge of his younger siblings. It was afternoon. They had dozed off and Rohan was a bit drowsy too. His tired eyes sighted the elephant herd, he thought "Why are the elephants cold to us? Have we done anything wrong to them? I wonder how life is, as an elephant." Then he saw his parents dragging the kill and ran to help them. When Raj felt thirsty, he decided to go to the river of fun. Nothing but a secret spring hidden behind a clump of bamboo deep in the jungle. When he reached there, Rohan was already there, but scampered away on seeing him. Raj shrugged it off and entered the spring to cool down and play. On the way home, Raj thought about why Rohan runs away and never speaks with him. He decided to ask his mom. When he voiced his query, she disclosed that Talwar and Aarav were friends earlier. One day, both of them were fighting the jackals. During the fight, their parents were killed. They thought the other was responsible. Since then, they have been rivals. That day, Raj went to search for Rohan. Instead of finding Rohan, he found Rohan's mom. He asked if she knew about what happened on that day. She told him Talwar and Aarav do not know it, but their parents were killed by the Hyenas, who were also present that day. They blamed it on the two, causing them to fall out. Rohan thanked her and went. Rohan ran down the hill towards the river to meet Aarav. When he reached Aarav, he asked about what happened between him and Talwar. Aarav said that the jackals and hyenas came and waged war on them. In the war, their parents were killed. The tusk and claw marks made them assume either the tiger or elephant were to be blamed because no one else could have done it so we fell out. Rohan thanked Aarav and departed. On the way back after visiting the elephants and tigers respectively, Rohan and Raj encountered one of the largest buffalo herds from the village had escaped to the jungle. When Rohan and Raj saw the stampeding herd, they ran but the herd was still on their tail (literally). When Aarav and Talwar saw them, they ran there and scared away the herd. When Ro han and Raj saw how powerful their two fathers were together, they smiled and got an idea. The sons decided to tell their fathers the truth. So they met at the river. They told them that the Hyenas had access to bones of various animals since they lived in the graveyard. That way, they were able to frame you for your parents death. Aarav said that since they knew the truth, they could work together like the old days. Talwar agreed. And that is how Rohan and Raj brought peace and security to the jungle and also re-united old friends.
author: Immanuel  Kakde
illustrator: Barkha Lohia; Kalp Sanghvi; Nancy Raj; Noyonika Banerjee; Partho Sengupta; Rob Owen; Sanjay Sarkar; Siddhi   Vartak

title: Un- Family Ties
text: Niyati was stunned when her aunt mocked at her parents saying “Don’t you guys have any brains? What on earth were you thinking when you decided to adopt a girl. Look at the way you’ve raised her. Gosh! Never seen a girl, so assertive, so outspoken. I am sorry to say she lacks manners Aman.” “But bua, what wrong have I done to protest against them? How could they ask for dowry when it is an illegal act? Gifting him a Mercedes for marrying your daughter, is she so unworthy of getting married to?” said Niyati in her defense. “Enough, Niyati! You've already tarnished our social reputation.” yelled Neelam, Niyati’s paternal aunt, before storming out of the room. It was Niyati’s cousin’s wedding. A typical big fat Indian, wedding, with chandeliers dropping from the ceilings, magnificent showpieces were propped at almost every step., there was an array of food options, from snacks to desserts. As loud music played in the background, her aunt’s words were clear to her ears. The incident was incessantly playing in her head as her eyes welled up and she darted out of the palace. The moon was already out.The wedding and the reception were to happen in a Rajasthani palace. The palace, from a distance looked as if it was set ablaze in a golden fire, with lights all around. She sat near the pool, questioning her existence. She always felt betrayed by her own parents for abandoning her. More than love, she respected and was gratuitous to her foster parents for adopting her and giving her the life she lived. She was adamant to one day epay everything they had to spend on her. Niyati was a very lively girl, full of inquisitiveness and always ready with a “why?”. “Why does the moon change its shape? Why is the sky blue? Why do chocolates not grow on tree?”. Her parents, as patient as they were, even answered her most innocent questions patiently. On her thirteenth birthday, the first birthday after she was diagnosed with vitiligo, her aunt taunted her mum for adopting a girl with vitiligo, who apparently brought misfortune to the family. The next question she asked was the toughest one she ever asked her parents about. “Mumma, daddy, why did bua say I was adopted?” With much reluctance, they revealed how they adopted her when she was barely 6 months old. They told her how much she meant to them and how they loved her more than they could ever love their biological child. Since then, she has been extremely reserved and felt abandoned. As much as her foster parents tried to make her feel secure, she isolated herself from the world. She devoted herself to academics and found a new hobby, fashion designing. She was a brilliant student academically and easily got admission in a well reputed fashion institute in New York. Back home, upon her return, her father offered her a good position in his company, but the strong and self-respecting woman she was, she firmly refused his offer. Within five years of entering the industry, her company became one of the most sought after and established company in the fashion and manufacturing industry. Fame and success came thick and fast after that. She was reflecting upon her life when suddenly, she felt a gentle hand on her shoulder. She looked around to see her parents standing behind her, like all these years, they still had her back. “Bua was harsh, honey. But we understand and agree to your stance.” said Madhuri. She was a generous lady and liked to see the world through rose tinted glasses. “But my dear,” said Aman Advani, “the society still expects the bride’s family to fulfil the demands of the grooms’ family.” Niyati’s eyes welled up. She got up and was about to protest when her phone rang. It was her secretary. She seemed appalled upon receiving the call. She quickly went online and the social media was filled with news of Trending Vogue, her company, partnering with child traffickers to manufacture clothes at a lower cost. She was reflecting upon her life when suddenly, she felt a gentle hand on her shoulder. She looked around to see her parents standing behind her, like all these years, they still had her back. “Bua was harsh, honey. But we understand and agree to your stance.” said Madhuri. She was a generous lady and liked to see the world through rose tinted glasses. “But my dear,” said Aman Kapoor, “the society still expects the bride’s family to fulfil the demands of the grooms’ family.” Niyati’s eyes welled up. She got up and was about to protest when her phone rang. It was her secretary. She seemed appalled upon receiving the call. She quickly went online and the social media was filled with news of Trending Vogue, her company, partnering with child traffickers to manufacture clothes at a lower cost. She received messages and mails one after the other, of clients and partners and investors who refused to work with her. The shares of her company dropped drastically. All this happened in a flash and she had very little time to react. “Dad, I’ve to go to Sumit’s office immediately. There’s a huge mess I’ve to clean up. But before that, I have to confront Sumit.” “But what..” before Aman could finish his sentence, Niyati sprinted towards her car and drove out majestic gates of the palace. But halfway through, she received a phone call from Sachin Patel, the senior inspector at Vasant Kunj police station. She was immediately called at the police station for interrogation. Upon reaching, she found Sumit already there. “Ms. Kapoor, your factory manager, Sumit Saraf has been in continuous contact of child traffickers. Till now, we haven’t found any concrete evidence against you but we suggest you come along with us in the factory and have a look for yourself.” By then the news had spread like wildfire and her parents rushed to Delhi. As they were heading towards the factory, media surrounded them. “Mr. Kapoor, what do you have to say upon the scam your daughter’s company is a part of? Sir, sir!” The media bombarded them with uestions and with great difficulty they reached the police station. Upon learning that Niyati went to the factory, they too rushed towards it.” Sumit knocked on the factory’s door, and hesitantly said “Betty Botter bought the batter, may our bundle of money get fatter and fatter.” The door opened and the man was taken aback to see the police. The factory smelled of chemicals. It was dark and only the sound of machineries could be heard. It was raided and there were around hundreds of children sitting in a dark room, hungry but overworked. They were all escorted outside safely. Upon learning that the factory will not be employing them anymore, the children’s faces withered. Niyati was taken aback, contrary to what she had expected, the children protested to let them work. A little girl held her hand and begged “Please don’t throw us out. Our parents will hit us if we don’t work here. That uncle pays them if we work here. We won’t even get food there, here we at least receive a meal. Please let us stay. We promise to work harder and make prettier clothes.” Niyati’s eyes welled up. She knew she couldn’t let matters be as they were. She couldn’t send these children back to the torturous places. Just as she was trying to figure what could be done, her phone rang. It was her secretary. She had called to confirm a meeting with an investor who was willing to invest in her dream project. She suddenly felt the lump in her throat go down, as she said “Cancel the meeting. Cancel the project, rather. I will now be working on an NGO with the capital I raised for the project. Everyone there was taken aback. “I’m proud of my girl.” said Mr. Kapoor, as he and his wife walked towards Niyati. “We are proud of you, Niyati.” said her mother. The little girl still held onto her hand. She bent down and planted a gentle peck on her forehead. “You will not be sent back home. I will send you to a safe place, where you’ll get food, toys and lots of books.” The girl had the widest smile on her face, and so did all the other children. “Why don’t we shift them to our farmhouse till the time the NGO is made.” suggested Mr. Kapoor. “That’s a great idea, dad”. So, all the preparations were made to shift the bunch of kids to the farmhouse. Niyati and her parents shifted there too. It was more like a housing complex with loads of greenery and a pond and a few horses and dogs. The air there smelt sweeter to the children, who were used to the smell of harsh chemicals. They spent about a month in the farmhouse, playing games, knowing of their dreams and aspirations, teaching them how to read and write. Playing with them revived Niyati’s childhood with her parents. After a month, when the NGO was ready to welcome the children, a client of hers came and conveyed their wish to adopt a child. “We don’t have a child of our own, then why hesitate to adopt one. Anyways, any relationship isn’t measured by DNA, but by emotions.” said the client’s wife. “And the population is rising, as responsible citizens, it is our duty to control it.” the client chuckled. Niyati witnessed the entire process. How the couple came with hopes of raising a child and how the child beamed at the very thought of having a family who loved and cared for one another. Niyati regretted at misinterpreting her parents’ love for sympathy and was pondering over how to apologize to them when a media portal requested her for an interview. She thought the best way was to herself adopt a child and honor her parents’ sacrifices which they made for her. A week later, when Anaya, the girl who held Niyati’s hand during the factory conflict, was adopted, a media portal wanted to interview Niyati. When asked about why she chose adoption she proudly said “Today I want to confess something extremely private about my life to the world. I, myself, am adopted. But the amount of love and support my parents shower on me, I am sure every child deserves that. Well, to address the fact, yes, I am single parenting my daughter and I am self-reliant enough to raise her by myself. That is how my parents have raised me. Anyways, I have been criticized for my vitiligo and people have mocked me saying who will marry her? Well, I’d say let no one marry me. I am self-independent and do not need a man to complete my life. My daughter and parents complete me.” Her interview went viral on social media and thousands of people, especially youth and childless couples thanked her for bursting the prevalent taboo on adoption and she was ecstatic when she saw how adoption was a growing alternative for natural pregnancy and biological children. It was Anaya’s first competition. She was dressed up as her mother and proud to be her daughter. She said she wanted to be like her when she grew up and idolized her in every aspect. Seeing the little girl perform on stage, Madhuri said to Niyati “This is definitely a befitting answer to everyone who questioned your adoption.” "Afterall," said Niyati, with a content look on her face, " any relationship isn’t built by DNA, but by emotions.”

title: Bhim and Raju's Friendship
text: Once there was a village named Dholakpur. A boy named Bhim resided there. Bhim was a brave and a kind boy. Raju, another boy from the same village, was jealous of Bhim as Bhim was always ahead of him in the class. Raju always secured 2nd rank after Bhim. Once a big competition was organised in the village by the Gurukul. All the boys of the village were allowed to participate. Some rules were announced prior to the game. The reward for winning the game was 2500 rupees and 100 kg of rice. After the announcement, the boys all around the village started registering themselves for the competition. Bhim and Raju too gave their names. Soon the teams were created, and it was shocking for Raju to have Bhim as his teammate. The competition started, and the first game was SACK RACE. Out of 25 teams, the first 10 teams would be considered as qualified for the 2nd round. Raju and Bhim qualified for the first round. Meanwhile Raju thought, “In this round Bhim and I qualified together but it may happen that in the next round Bhim qualifies first. If it happens everyone would consider Bhim stronger than me. I should do something to make him lose next round. The next round was of chess. In this round all the players would play individually and if even one of them loses, the full team gets disqualified. First Bhim started playing and he was about to win but Raju could not digest his victory so, while the match was going on he turned off the lights of the Gurukul. It was dark as the colour of Black Panther. In the darkness, Raju made changes to the game that made unfavourable conditions for Bhim, and he was on the verge of losing the game. But the light was repaired quickly. Then the match continued, and Bhim saw something suspicious on the board and then saw a bracelet of Raju on the floor and inferred that Raju was behind all the stuff. But somehow Bhim managed the situation and won. Next turn was of Raju, and he too easily won. 5 teams out of 10 got qualified for the last round. The last round was the most difficult. In this they had to kill the monster which lives in the lake. The match started and both of the teams started aiming their bows towards the monster. ﻿ But suddenly the monster attacked Raju with his friend, but Bhim pushed Raju to save him and got hit by the monster. He was very injured and had many wounds. Raju, after seeing the care of Bhim towards him, realized his mistake. He said worriedly “oh! My friend, I kept hating you; I wanted you to lose in chess; I wanted you to be weak, but you don’t even have a little hatred for me”.” I know all this my friend, it’s good that you have realized your mistake, but now it’s the time to show that we are the best. ﻿ Pull me up and let’s finish off this beast”, said Bhim. But suddenly the monster went into the lake for a few minutes. Then suddenly the monster came out with double its size, shocking everyone. But, as now Bhim and Raju were together, they easily killed the deadly monster. They became the “Masihas” of the village. Ayurvedic Medicines were applied on the body of Bhim for the recovery of his injuries. From that day all lived happily in peace, harmony and friendship.

title: Awakening
text: Once an intelligent, sharp boy who loved sports. He spent most of his time studying and playing soccer with his friends. He was a state champion, self confident, disciplined boy and his parents were very proud of him. He was doing really well in school. One day when he was coming back from school, he told his mother that many of his friends have a play station. He also wants one. He requested his mother to get him a play station. His mother agreed as he was doing well in his studies and sports. The day Kabir's parent bought him a play station, his life revolved around his favourite video games. He loved gaming PC more than anything in the world. He refused to play outside or interact with his friends. Violent gaming, made him anxious, Sleep deprived and aggressive. He got addicted to gaming. He became physically inactive which eventually resulted in health issues. He lost interest in studies and sports. He didn't eat well and got dark circles. Due to prolonged gaming, he started getting headaches and discomfort in eyes. His parents were concerned about him. His granny was also very worried. She was missing her grandson's giggles and gossip. She used to see the previous pictures and medals won by him in soccer which she had kept safely in a beautiful box. But Kabir only wanted playstation and his idiotic games. He started getting scoldings from his parents and teachers as his performance in school got affected. Kabir's teacher told his parents to consult a doctor. The doctor told his parents that, he is suffering from gaming disorder and advised him to stop playing games as his eyesight, health was getting affected badly. But Kabir was addicted and he didn't stop. He played continuously, even failed in his exam and lost his friends as well. One day his mother got fed up and badly scolded him and said, " One day you will lose your eyesight because of gaming. " That night Kabir had a nightmare in which his mother's prediction came true. He lost his eyes and the doctor tells him there is no cure. Kabir awakens shaken and scared. He realised that he has neglected his family, health, studies, friends as well as his favorite game soccer. He went to his mother and narrated the whole dream and promised his mother that he will never play games on the playstation and asked his mother to throw his gaming PC away. So from that day Kabir got back to his old self. This was the lesson he took to heart and became a winner. When he kicked the ball it flew high into the air like beautiful butterflies taking flight and finally landed in the net.

title: Hope
text: A normal another day at school, which for me, was my only ray of hope. It was the day of announcing the results for an olympiad I had taken part in. It may not the the best performance I had ever done but on the basis of efforts I had made, my expectations were high. I had always been taunted for acting like I made most efforts but the results for not at all similar. So, this was the only way to prove myself. Even though I have faced so many difficulties before, I still believed in myself. According to ranks, names were called out. “5: Conrad, 4: Aneesa … and 1 st rank goes to Fabiola.” Where was my name? Hadn’t I worked hard for it? Where was the result? I agree that marks or ranks don’t define us, but it is the only way to prove ourselves, show our worth and that we deserve it. It also boosts our confidence and makes us believe in ourselves. It was a small matter of marks and ranks, but what mattered at that moment was faith and belief, trust and not losing hope. We all need a light of hope to keep us moving in the darkness and for me, it was just some reasons I wanted to keep moving. Being in the race was not what I wanted, neither was being the best meant something. It was the satisfaction and touching the peak of my expectations. We want to feel proud and make our loved ones proud, and what I was doing was just disappointing them. I returned home, after a tiring day from school and directly landed on the bed, thinking about myself. About my future, all the possibilities that could happen and brightness turning into gray, I could imagine them all. My mom noticed I was back, she looked hyped, and asked,” So, how was it?” I smiled and asked, confused,”What?” “The results?” The silence took over. The talk continued with the stare of our eyes. Hers, with excitement and expectations and mine, with disappoint and grief. Her expression suddenly changed from expectant into comforting. “Do you think you deserved it?” “I don’t know, maybe I did?” “Think about it and let me know later. I believe we always get what we deserve and what we think we are. So first, you should believe in yourself and find out the reason behind it. The positive thinking is what keeps us going and come on, there’s always a next time. You’ll do better next time, I know that.” She left with a smooth gesture which said ‘I am always there for you’. Few weeks passed by, and the examinations had started. Again the hope had knocked on the door, along with hidden doubts. I was writing the answer sheet, and in the small corner of my mind said “What if I can’t?” All the exams passed by and it had everyone on knees. My results were even poorer than before, maybe for, I wasn’t focused. My mind said it was my worth, I didn’t deserve it and it was out of league. Getting what I wanted, had never been easy, most of the times, I felt the urge to do something extraordinary and make everyone believe in me. This day, I realised our positive thinking doesn’t come from other beliefs but ours. Till the moment we don’t have our souls to believe in us, no one can inspire us to keep moving. I had a last chance now, doing my best in finals. It was near and this time I pointed out everything which I thought I didn’t have and was required for achievements like self-confidence, focus and self-belief. Along with these, I also worked hard and the faith came crawling by. Today was the day, again the expectations high, but this time, belief of achieving it. It was the results of finals, the names started being called out. Heart beating fast, mind in a whirl, and me assuring myself “Even if you don’t get what you want, that’s alright, you did great. You worked far more than before” “10th: Richard … 2nd: Fabiola..” Before the teacher could continue, students started gossiping about how could Fabiola not be first, she was the best student in our class. My heart had already been broken, in a despair, how couldn’t I make it. Not even in the top 10 list? Was I that low? Did I not make efforts? I did. I can proudly say I did, but where was the result? Why wasn’t I worth it? My thoughts were interrupted by the teacher saying,”The 1st position goes to Stella.” I had done it! My name was at the top! I couldn’t believe it. After a short moment of hiding the bottom, I had risen, I got even more than what I wanted. I realised everyone was looking at me, they looked disappointed but this time, I didn’t feel bad. I had proved myself. I had justified it. After I was back home, I ran over to my mom. After telling her the whole story, I felt proud. I felt that I had made her proud. She looked as if she knew this was going to happen, but still happier than ever. I believe, at the back of our minds, we all have doubts for ourselves. We feel alone, sophisticated, always wanting to do something more. We often feel disappointed but our hard work and belief is what keeps us motivated. Maybe we don’t always get what we want. Maybe sometimes we get something far greater than anything we could've ever hoped for.

title: Tara - A Rising Star
text: A little bundle of joy entered Mr. and Mrs. Jone’s life. Tiny red cheeks, small hands, big black and bold eyes were mesmerizing. A very cute smile increased her beauty. She was always happy and so were the people around her. Her parents named her “Tara”, a small, short and unique name in itself. As time flew, Tara grew up. She was very attractive and calm. Her eyes spoke more than her mouth. It was spring season; she was enjoying with her father. Her father was driving the car following all the instructions. And! Here was Tara, who was looking outside the window, admiring the green bushes and all of mother nature’s magic. She was happy to see so much greenery around her. Her father asked her, “Tara, what do you want to do ahead in life?” Tara replied in nick of time, “Papa! I really want to become a writer and inspire little students and children like me. My school is also ardent supporter of me. It’s my dream to become a writer”. While conversing with her, her father lapsed his concentration for a fraction of second and unexpectedly, a tragedy took place. A big truck bumped into their car. Both the father and the daughter held each other’s hand tightly. Tara was scared at that moment. Her father got heart on his hand. He had a bad bruise on his hand after accident. The front mirror of the car broke into small pieces. Some of the glass particles went into Tara’s eyes and she lost her vision. They were taken to the hospital for timely treat. From that day, Tara was hurt badly. Her parents and friends helped her walk and overcome the obstacles in her day-to-day life. Suddenly and independent girl became dependent on others for her basic needs. After the doctor’s treatment, Tara sounded very upset. Each passing day, Tara turned into impatient, angry little girl. She started avoiding people. She started living an introvert life. She started spending most of the time alone. She was not able to accept the fact that she lost her vision forever. Her parents were also in shock. They were making every possible effort to heal her pain. One day while having dinner to make Tara cheerful, Tara’s mother broke the ice and asked her, “Tara, have you added any story in your collection? How will you become a writer if you don’t think of any ideas for your stories?” Tara said, “Ma, I am really sad and lost all my hopes. All my previously written stories are now in vain. I wanted to become a writer but see my fate! How will I write now?”. Tara’s father said, “Tara, don’t worry, time heals all wounds. We will surely come to a solution as soon as possible.” He gave Tara hopes. That night, Tara didn’t have dinner properly. She ran to her room and locked the door. Little Tara was broken. She couldn’t even sleep properly that night. It was the worst night she had ever experienced. She threw everything here and there and made the room untidy. Tara had to stop her previous schooling. Her parents took admission for Tara in a blind school nearby. It was a right decision for Tara as now she could start learning to write braille. She made new friends there and also got adopted to the new environment very soon. When Tara started going to blind school, she realized the importance of six senses of body gifted by God. She thought to herself that when I was able to see the whole world with my eyes, I had not taken the significance of all senses seriously. But now, I came to know that every little thing of nature is important. With my remaining other senses, I can still explore the world in new way. From that day, she started working hard to fulfill her dream of becoming a writer. Every night, her parents used to read a new story for her before going to bed. Her parents tried to keep going. All the people around her emboldened her in every way possible. Tara felt every small task challenging at first. But she knew that in the long run, all this will be beneficial for her. Her attitude changed drastically. She started taking things positively. Time flew like running water and Tara passed all her exams with flying colors. After a couple of years, Tara became a renowned writer. She was being invited at many programs and inspired little budding authors. She received one such invitation from her own previous school. She was eagerly waiting for that day. She was ecstatically happy. Her school wanted to felicitate her for her achievements. And finally the day arose. Tara reached the venue before time. She recollected all her beautiful memories which she had gathered there. She had a fruitful reading session regarding her first published book named “Vision”. It was her autobiography itself. Soon she became an inspiration for the youth. Her fan club started increasing. Now, cherry on the top was that, she had started her own portal of her stories where she put new stories for written books. Really, Tara was herself an idol of inspiration where she messaged everyone never give up in life whatever situation arise. She became the face of the city.

title: Why is he sad all the time?
text: Aarav was excited about returning back to the new session of class 8C. He hadn’t seen his friends for a long time. Reaching up to the classroom, he saw all his friends sitting around on different benches, gossiping and planning out the session. Aarav sat beside his best friend, Rohan and looked around. They talked over the phone most days during the session break, so they started talking with other students instead. Aarav noticed a new student, sitting away from the rest of the students on a bench by the window. He asked Rohan, “Rohan, who’s that new student?”. Rohan replied,”I don’t know his name, but for some reason, he’s sad all the time! Go sit with him and he’ll just stare out the window and stay quiet. ”. Aarav, however, wanted to make friends with him. He picked up his bag and sat beside Subham. “Hi, I’m Aarav. What’s your name?”. “I’m Subham and I’m new to this school.” replied Subham sadly, staring out the window, looking at a crow cawing loudly atop a tree. “That’s great! I’m assuming you haven’t made any friends yet. I could be your friend if you’d like!”. “Hmm.” he replied. The maths teacher arrived at the class and started teaching linear equations. “Ugh! Algebra. I’m never going to be good at this.” Aarav thought while trying to solve an equation. He looked at Subham and noticed his face, all downcast and woeful, solving equations quietly. Aarav wondered, “I’ve never seen anyone so sad, especially on the first day of school! Everyone’s cheerful and excited for the new session but I can’t understand why Subham’s sad all the time.”. He quickly forgot about Subham and got lost in learning Mathematics, Science, English and History. During the tiffin break, Aarav took his tiffin box and water bottle and sat with Subham, despite Rohan dragging him towards the bench where all the students had gathered to have tiffin together. “Hello! I couldn’t help but notice how sad you’ve been all day. May I ask why?”. “Honestly, I don’t know myself. Ever since mom passed away, I’ve always felt sad like this. It feels like I’m stuck inside invisible bars keeping me away from being happy. I try to smile and laugh freely but I just can’t be happy.”. “I’m so sorry for your loss. But what do you mean, you can’t be happy? How is that even possible? Everyone can be happy or sad. However, I think your mood might be better tomorrow.” replied Aarav. “I wish. Thanks for sitting with me though,” replied Subham. Aarav was confused after talking to Subham. He had never heard of this before. A person who can’t be happy? How is that even possible? Rohan dragged him towards a bench where he saw his friends. He soon forgot about Subham and continued with school. Over the next few days, at school, Aarav sat beside Subham. They would share their secrets, talk about their problems with each other and over time, Subham and Aarav became best friends. Aarav noticed how Subham wasn't sad all the time the way he was at the beginning of the session. On the day of the report card distribution, Aarav and Subham both got good marks on all their subjects. They sat on a bench together after receiving the report cards and Aarav asked Subham, “Have you noticed how you haven’t been sad all day like the way you used to be? On the first day of the session, you weren’t cheerful and happy like others, instead you were staring out the window with a woeful face. But now, you aren’t sad all the time. I wonder what brought about this change in you.” Subham replied, “Well, you were right, my mood did get better later. I think this was because I enjoyed talking to you and that’s how slowly my mood got better.”. “That’s great. Come on, we have a lovely session break to spend!” said Aarav cheerfully. When we catch a cold, we have medicine and we eventually get better. However, sometimes our brain can also have a disease, however, a mental one. Because of such diseases, we might feel sad, we cry, we feel angry or hurt. In this story, Subham feels sad all the time and doesn’t feel like doing anything. This is because he has depression. Depression is a mental disease which causes people to feel sad all the time. They feel woeful and feel tired all the time. It is natural to be sad, however, the sadness feels like it will never go away. In the story, Subham feels better by talking with his friend, Aarav. Depression among teenagers is common during adolescence. If you find any of your friends or classmates suffering from depression, you can talk to them and let them know that you want to help. The best way to help someone with depression is to talk with them. Talk with them about their life, their problems and help them feel better. Talking with a therapist can also help. Remember that depression is not a physical disease, it is a mental one. You don’t have to be a doctor to help them, you can help them just by talking. THE END
