title: A Trip Worth Remembering
text: It was a bright, sunny, and scorching day in June when my family decided to go on a trip to Jaisalmer, the Golden City of Rajasthan. As I was checking and rechecking that I packed everything needed, Dad called from outside- “It's time to go.” With my thoughts uplifted by the idea of a road trip, I took long strides toward the balcony, but as soon as I opened the door, my thoughts sank at a greater speed. God! It was boiling outside. Sweat dripping off my face, I helped my parents heave the suitcases into the car boot and all of us immediately retired to the inside of the car. My dad switched on the AC. Ahh! That felt a lot better. There were four of us: Mom, Dad, Grandpa, and I. To begin our journey with a sweeter note, we popped a toffee each in our mouths and were soon smoothly cruising down the Sagar Mala road. It was a new project, at the time. Trust me, the road was beautiful. From the closed windows of our AC car, we could see the sand blowing with the wind. And the wind, as if playing some kind of game, was lifting heaps of sand from the dunes and dropping them on the road. There were times when we felt like we were driving over sand dunes. After a while, we saw a board in green that showed us that we were going the right way. Happily, we proceeded, but soon we realized that something was wrong. The road abruptly stopped ahead into a sandy path. We thought it to be a stretch of road covered with some benign sand. My Dad pressed the accelerator and the vehicle roared forward. Then suddenly our car gave a groan and stopped. Dad, bewildered ran out and checked the tires. He came back panting, and sputtered, “It’s stuck". “What do you mean it's stuck?!” Mom cried. She too quickly opened the door and ran to see. Later when she came back, she too, with a long face said, “It's indeed stuck”. I gave a groan and Grandpa and I too climbed out of the vehicle. My parents checked their phones, there was no signal. We looked out into the distance for any help. Not a single person was there. Only three definitely undernourished goats, grazing on whatever grass was there, were our local company. I looked at them in despair and said, “Those things can definitely not help us, can they?” For some time, all four of us tried to rack our brains, but when nothing seemed to work, Grandpa was the first to give up and went to sit under a Babool tree. I tried giving a hand with the car. I tried to push it. OUCH! red, hot hands, grabbed a cloth, and tried again. But it was in vain. That’s when Dad saw a man in a parrot green kurta-pajama driving a jeep. We became hopeful. My parents started waving frantically at him. That could have caught anyone’s attention! The man came towards us and when he saw our car, he clicked his tongue in dismay. “ Bhai sahib, why did you drive here?” he said to my Dad. He talked to my father for some time, went back to his jeep, and left. All my hopes shattered like glass. We continued with our attempts but failed miserably. Mom recalled an incident when she saw a little puppy dig its way into our garden at home. It made a tunnel and then slid through it to cross the fence. That thing had its brains! My mom tried to copy that. She literally started to dig into the sand with her hands! After some time, she gave up with nothing but disgustingly dirty nails. Tired, I too decided to retire to the cool shade of the Babool tree to join my Grandpa. After half an hour, we saw the man with the eye-catching kurta again, this time with two jeeps, each full of people. They brought with them a kind of wire. They attached one end of the wire to the front of our car and the other to the back of their jeep. They started driving. Alas! The wire broke! They told us to wait while they came and brought stronger material. By this time, even my mother was with us under the tree. My grandpa had found a nice large rock to sit on while I and Mom were standing. After another twenty minutes, the men came back, this time with a tractor and rope. They attached the rope to the tractor and our car and finally, the car was out! The four of us, totally drenched in sweat, thanked the men earnestly and were about to leave when they invited us to their place. After much persuasion, we were in the car following a tractor to a nearby village. We saw a huge Haveli and we came to know that it was their house. We went inside and they, with a lot of hospitality, served us water. My mom went to chitchat with the ladies there and I too tagged along. They saw me and asked if Mom had any more kids. When she said no, they all started saying something in Rajasthani. There was only one thing that I understood. “ Chora ko ni?" which meant ‘No boy?’. The idea of having just one girl was obviously strange to them. Or perhaps they had never encountered a girl in shorts, with disheveled hair, mud, and sweat on the face. My mom was laughing her head off trying to tell them that girls are just as good as any boy. But they definitely were not convinced. Some more conversation and many pics later we were on the road again. “Well, this definitely was a trip worth remembering,” my mom said. She turned to look at me and teased, “ Chora ko ni?”

title: THE FIRST PATIENT
text: “Saba, come let’s have dinner!” mom called out from the kitchen. I came down from my cosy little bedroom situated on the second floor. Dad and mum were already waiting for me on the dining table. “Shh! Shh! Speak softly, your dad has just returned from a long night shift and is trying to rest.” This, was a daily instruction that I used to get from my mom when I came back from school. My dad was a cardiologist who worked at the city hospital in the night shift. Soon after finishing our dinner the three of us headed towards the lake. It was our daily routine to do so. Also, it was during this walk that I could pour my heart out in front of my parents. Even though dad had a very hectic schedule he always made it a point to visit the lake for some family time. “Dad it feels as if a puppy is crying. Can you also hear it?” I asked. “Yes, it seems as if a newborn puppy is crying. But the mystery is that there is no such animal to be seen.” Answered dad. We reached the river shore. I, mom and dad kept on walking, carefully surveying the place to find the source of the squeaks. But no one could spot it. After about 20 minutes of searching, both mom and dad gave up. As we were walking on our usual path, the sound became louder. With a ray of hope I started looking again. I wanted to help the puppy, desperately. “Saba come here along your mom, fast, see, whom have I found.” Dad screamed out standing between two rocks. Mom and I headed towards him and to our surprise, dad had found a golden retriever. It was stuck between two rocks. We carefully took out the puppy. It looked frightened. It was trembling with fear. One of its paws was badly bleeding. I wrapped my handkerchief around the wound. It seemed he felt better but still was afraid. I did not feel like keeping the puppy down or leaving it. He was trying to say something that I could not understand. “It feels somebody has abandoned the dog because of which it is suffering from malnourishment.” Dad told us while I looked in the eyes of the pup. They had an unusual spark. The way it was staring back at me, I felt attached to him. Standing still, mom and dad were witnessing the silent conversation of ours. I was about to keep it down when the puppy gave a cry. I felt as if I was abandoning him and he would be all alone again, maybe for forever. I gave mom and dad a questioning kind of look. I did not dare to ask them freely. Mom got my point and asked dad if I could keep it. Please Pa, I cried. “I’ll take care of it myself. Feeding him, taking out for a walk all would be my duty. Pa we cannot abandon him, he’s helpless.” I requested. Mom too supported me, unexpectedly, she had sensed my bond with the golden retriever. After a long struggle I finally succeeded in convincing dad. We took the puppy home and I named it Suba after myself. I enjoyed taking care of it. Feeding it, taking it out for a walk and dressing its wounds made me feel better. Suba helped me realize my love for animals. Today, I am 32 years old and a successful veterinarian. I still clearly remember my meeting with my FIRST PATEINT.
author: Sunidhi Bhutoria

title: Teen Love
text: "Woahhh, did he see me?" she asked her friend. "Yeah as usual he acted as if he didn't but he obviously did." replied her friend. Everyone has a school love story which is basically known as infatuation, but unlike any other teen - love story, this is the story of Nayna and her one and only crush It all started during the annual exams. Nayna had joined the school with an objective which was not to fall in love but all of it had gone for a toss after seeing Krishna. Nayna was an outgoing girl who couldn't conceal her feelings so she decided to tell him about her feeling, knowing that it was going to be a "NO". The rejection had hit her hard but she still decided to give up her self respect and keep loving him just with the slightest hope that someday he'll understand her love. Nayna used to run to the exit as soon as the bell rang so that she could reach before he does and see him go home. This was an a daily affair, yearned for. Time flew by and came Nayna's birthday, she was really excited to go to school in civil dress and also to go to his class,of course. Krishna is a great boy but can be really annoying at times like he was talking to somebody and didn't even see Nayna when she went to his class on her birthday. Nayna wanted to give Krishna chocolate, just that she didn't have the courage. So, she gave Akash (Krishna's friend) chocolates and asked him to give it to Krishna as well. It seems as soon as Akash gave the chocolate, Krishna smiled and said "8th right?" and had it. She had also given his brother chocolate.Then later that day while going home his brother literally pointed at Nayna and said "this akka only gave me chocolate", Nayna was petrified imagining Krishna's reaction but all he said was " I know, I also got a chocolate" and went home. One day Nayna was absent and her friend called her saying while going home Krishna didn't speak to his friends, was upset, his eyes were red and was desperately looking for someone. Nayna was happy but angry at the same time because she thought it was his ego which was stopping him from admitting the fact that he likes her too. She was irritated with herself for loving an idiot like him. It had been a year and now it was time for Nayna to move out of the city, that means change of school! Nayna was used to this because of her father's profession but this time it wasn't the same. Nayna had written a letter for Krishna and gave it to Akash asking him to give it to Krishna only if he looks for her. Three days passed, Krishna was upset and was not revealing the reason. So Akash decided to give him the letter. Krishna opened it and read it out loud ---- Dear Krishna, So, after this I won't be loitering near your class unnecessarily, I won't be bunking my music class just to see you play football and most importantly I won't be waiting at the gate just to see you! For you I might not even be a small part of your school life but for me you were my whole life at school. A piece of my heart will always be with and this school. I'll miss you a lot. Krishna bursted out into tears after reading the letter and said "I loved her too", Akash said "you deserve it, why this ego bro?" Krishna said "Not ego, I had thought about this a thousand times. I don't hold hands to leave in between, if I hold I don't leave and this could've never worked out out because of our religions, my dad would never agree and you know how afraid i am of him. Besides this, I may not be able to give her the lifestyle she is used to, I wanted her to be happy that's all. i didn't want her yo get attached to me and that's the only reason I suppressed all my emotions and gave a stone faced look but I loved her too with all my heart. I really did, I hope she finds a better guy". Krishna's grief was valid, after all he had lost a girl who loved him with all her heart, who never gave up on him, who tried her best leaving no stone unturned to tell him,how much he meant to her. Nayna on the other hand was shattered into a million pieces, crying and hating herself for loving such a guy with all her heart but little did she know that what she considered ego was love, ignorance was care and whom she now considered villain was her ‘knight in shining Armour’. Only person capable of clearing this misunderstanding is Akash. Will he do so? Will Krishna and Nayna who loved each other dearly in their own ways cross paths again? What will happen if they do? Will Krishna and Nayna who loved each other dearly in their own ways cross paths again? What will happen if they do? Both had lost the energy to love. Will they ever find tre love again? If they do, wiil it be the two of them again? Will it be a bed of roses or a bsh of thorns? Will they come together? Will their tale have a fairy tale ending or will it end with a sad note of 'Better luck, next time'?

title: A Beautiful Name
text: My name is Ethan. I was born in a middle-class family in a small town near the coasts of Hawaii. I was very clumsy and notorious when I was young. My dad worked at a bank office, and my mom worked as a nurse in a nearby hospital. They both earn enough money for our daily lives. When I was at the age of five, I was admitted to a school near my house, which was about three miles away. I was a naughty boy and a clumsy one in the whole class. I scored good grades on my tests and exams, and once I scored top in one of my exams in the mid-session. My parents were proud of me. It was one of the happiest moments in my life. At the age of eleven, I was studying in 6th grade. It was one of the hardest and most unforgettable years of my life. I studied and scored average in my class. My mom told me that I should study hard and get a job like being a doctor or an engineer, but I had no interest in any of them. And my dad told me that I should do what I liked and follow my dreams. That is when I got meaning in my life, but I never knew what I could do or be. Soon I passed 6th grade and was promoted to 7th grade. I also changed my school, which was now 7 miles away. I had fewer friends in my new school than in my old school. I was not properly fitted for the new school and had many problems with my classmates. So, I usually got into fights and arguments with them. I didn't talk much or didn't have fun at all. I would do my school chores and focus on my grades. One day when I was attending my daily classes, one new student came into the class. It was a girl, and her name was Sarah. The day she came into the class, I was flattered when I saw her. I soon started to make a good friendship with her. And soon, we became good friends. And this is when she gave me A BEAUTIFUL NAME ''LUCAS''. It was the new year, and I was in 8th grade. Most friends stopped talking to me, but it was not a big problem as I had a good friend to talk with and focus on my studies. I still remember that Sarah and I used to talk and make fun of my other classmates as I didn't talk to them. As I was enjoying my school year, I learned that my grades were degrading, but I didn't give much importance to them because I thought I would study and recover my grades soon. Finally, at the end of the school year, I told Sarah how I felt for her. It was sad but fine to know that she said we should be friends and not more than that. I was never ready for this day, but my friendship with Sarah soon weakened daily. I got sad and anxious and tried not to overthink, but it was useless. It was the next year, in 9th grade, I was a lonely boy in the class who was wondering about things in a different world in my mind. Still trying to know what I will become in the future. I couldn't focus on my daily chores and work. A few months later, Sarah found someone who could take good care of her and help her during her bad times. I felt bad for a moment and realized that she was happy. So, for me, if she was happy, then I was happy too. At the age of 16, my family and I shifted to California. My dad got a better post in the new bank he works, and my mom also got a job in a nearby hospital. The best feeling was that I also shifted my school, so I got rid of all my old friends. But I was still curious about my new school, like what my new friends would be like or will it be the same as my old school. All these years, I thought only studying was the key to success. I spent most of my time studying and a bit of recreation by watching TV or reading comics. The day I went to my new school, My teacher told me to introduce myself to the class as a new student. For the first time, I felt I was in the comfortable environment I always wanted. Everyone was humble and polite as I talked and made friends with them. A month later, I made many friends and a best friend named Aiden. I enjoyed it a lot, and also my grades went up. My parents were also happy to see me happy. But after getting everything I wanted in my life, I was still not satisfied; it felt like my life was empty, and something was surely missing. I still wonder what I shall do. And sometimes, I also think about my past and get anxious when I imagine the flashbacks of my past. I still remember that I still remember the time my parents were so proud of me and appreciated me for scoring top in my exams for the first time. The times when I played with my friends and when I was free of struggles and anxiety. The best memory I still remember is the BEAUTIFUL NAME given by Sarah. The name ''LUCAS'' was important to me, as it means the ''bringer of light.'' When Sarah gave the name to me, I thought it was just a simple name just given to me. But when I started to spend time and got to know more about her. I got to know that my name, which was given to me by her not just a name; it meant something to me. I asked her why she gave me this name instead of any other one. Sarah told me that she didn't know what would happen to us in the future or what we would be when we grew up, but she said that when I worked hard and grew up, I would bring light to the things I do. I didn't understand at first, but later she said I could do anything if I worked hard and focused. She also said that many ups and downs might come in my life, but if I surpass them, nobody can stop me. she said the fire grows beneath me as I work hard and become a great person. I soon passed 11th grade by scoring 3rd rank in my class. I felt a bit bad for not scoring top but by remembering the old words that I shall never stop trying until I succeed. My loneliness was also gone over time as I had many friends and had fun with them. Soon, when we graduated in the final year of our school. We celebrated and had farewell, and we promised each other that wherever we go or whatever we become will never forget each other and the memories we spent together. That was when I realized that this is a part of a person's life and how life works. Ultimately, I am still trying to figure out what may happen to me. Life has many ups and downs, but we should still forget about them and focus on what we do. The name given to me motivated me a lot to get to where I am now or where I will be. But I can only become a great person if I work hard with dedication and focus and keep going. Most youths try different things and may be good at some things, but they still keep wondering what they could do. We should do what we have been doing, what we should be doing, and what we are supposed to be doing. Well, that's my life of what I may be; now it's your turn to stand up and find out why you were born on this beautiful earth. Note: Ethan is a character that came to the mind of the narrator/writer of this story.
author: Bidyasagar Kshetrimayum

title: SITA'S DILEMMA
text: Sita was a helpful 7 year old girl. She lived with her parents and her little brother. She liked to help her parents, but her parents scolded her many times due to tiny misunderstandings. She assumed that she is not important in the family! On a peaceful morning, Sita woke up early. She wanted to wake her family up with a gentle song. She started singing loudly, but she did not think about her younger brother waking up. Her dad woke up to her song and scolded her! This time, her intention is correct, but she didn’t think about her brother and got scoldings. On another night, her dad just returned from work, with his laptop in his hands. Sita got really excited when she saw him and ran to hug him. When she did so, the laptop in dad's hands fell down and almost got broken. Again, she got scoldings! A few days later, she was convinced that she was not important at all and one morning, she wanted to sit inside her room all day instead of being with her family. She passed time all day in her room by reading, sleeping and singing songs. That evening, Sita turned around hearing a voice. It was her brother. He gave her a card. Suddenly, she heard her mother call her for dinner. She left the card in the room and started walking, thinking something. ‘Why did my parents scold me when I sang songs in the morning? Did I really disturb their sleep? I only wanted to wake them up with a song. Am I really important to my family?' Just then, she entered the dining room. There, she saw that all the toys were scattered around and the room was very messy. She thought-‘ I help out at home and if it weren’t for me the house is like this? Just then, she realised something and ran to her room. Then she opened the card and found the it was a picture of her. Now she got a doubt if she was important in the family, or not. The next day, mom called Sita's dad and asked him to get something from the shop, but dad was on a call and could not hear mom. Sita decided to prove to her parents that she was just trying to help them, and she went to shop all by herself. But soon after she started walking on the road, she found that she was lost! Later, her parents realised that she was not at home, and they were extremely worried. They began searching for her. Mom and dad soon reached the road Sita was walking in. They were so close! Suddenly Sita was crossing the road, but she did not realise a truck driving very quickly. Was she about to get injured very seriously? Was she in danger? Suddenly, she felt being pulled away. It was a stranger. Just then, her parents came running towards Sita. They were grateful to the stranger and relieved that their daughter was safe. They squeezed Sita in a tight hug. To show their gratitude, mom and dad offered the person dinner dinner at their house with the person's family. Now, Sita understood that to her family, she was an important, equal and special member of the family. From that day, Sita understood that if her parents scold her, it does not mean she was wrong or she did something bad. She understood that scoldings were just to improve her and make her a bit better. THE END
author: Sita Tejasvi
illustrator: Kalyani Naravane; Kavya  Bagga; Saheb Ram  Tudu; Sanjay Sarkar

title: Quest For Love
text: I raced down the stairs, almost galloping, as I picked up the front of my gown to avoid tripping. I was ready to start my day with a big bright smile on my face. I mean, if I smile, the world will smile, right? However, I brought a sudden halt to my speedy descent when I met my sister at the foot of the staircase. I took a quick step back as she looked to be bothered by my presence. “Watch where you’re going. Don’t want you ruining my dress.”, she frowned at me and continued walking forwards. I uttered an apology which I don't think she heard. “Good morning, mom!”, I chirped. “Hmm.”, she looked deep in thought, “Have you finished inspecting the armory?”, she questioned, finally looking at me. I drew in a breath, “I…..I’ll complete it by today.” She inhaled sharply, beginning to frown. “Avery, must you always delay work to the last minute?” “Mom, I was told to do this last night, at 10! I couldn’t do anything at that hour.”, I shrugged. “You’ve had the whole morning. So stop making excuses.”, she shook her head. “That’s-”, before I could even explain, I was silenced by the rising of her hand, “Enough! Go… and do your work.”, she looked away from me and left. All the while I stood there in an expression of disbelief. I dragged myself to the nearest sofa and plopped down on it. Looking up, I scoffed at my own fate. This was my life. The life of Princess Avery Vaughn of Cerulean Court. The state’s name is inspired by the huge amounts of Sapphire that are found in this part of the world. My sister, Elle Vaughn, was adopted when I was seven and she was five. My parents wanted to provide a home, a lavish lifestyle and loads of love to another child and hence, they took her in. I don’t know what happened after that but my mother began despising me. She started loving Elle a lot, more than me. Of course, I didn’t mind Elle on the receiving end of so much love. She deserved it. But I didn’t like the fact that I no longer existed in my mother’s eyes. I don’t blame Elle for that at all and I can’t bring myself to blame my mother either. So, since long, I’ve been lambasting, criticizing myself for being a bad daughter. I have developed the belief that it’s because of my actions and behaviours that my mother has become so distant towards me. I remember being a lazy child who didn’t really want to do much work. I would always get scolded for not helping out. Then, two days after a good earful, I would have a sudden burst of energy and finish everything I had to in time. My mother would, at the time, praise me with the least appreciation and interest. But, for me, even that was enough. Things changed after I turned 18, a full adult. I became entirely responsible and my mother started hating me even more. I realized no matter what I do, how responsible I become, she’ll never be proud of me. I was never appreciated for anything I did, even if it was the toughest I did. Still, I had hope. Hope that one day she won’t have any reason to be unhappy with me and finally love me. So far, the evening was like any other day. However, we had some guests over. It was the King and his chancellor from Advent. They had come about to make relations between the two empires through the means of a business deal and contract, as far as I had known. I wasn’t allowed to sit in the great hall where my parents and our foreign guests were, as it was a confidential interaction. But, just how I was always a victim of prejudice, Elle was allowed to move in and out of the room. Soon enough, a grand feast of dinner was served in the dining hall. We ate in silence, with only the two Kings having a bland conversation. Royalty seriously is just living a monotonous life with a rich title. I wanted to know more about Advent’s ruler. Surely there had to be tons of information about his family, kingdom and lifestyle on the internet. So, I quickly booted up my laptop and began surfing through the web. After all, I wasn’t your typical princess with bounded hands and a tied tongue. I was always up for an adventure. I opened every single article I could find and read through his biography. At the end of one article, which I was near to closing, a suggested article’s heading caught my eye. ‘Finally - the missing-person poster Advent put up for its future heiress.’ So the king of Advent had a daughter? The image of the poster contained all the details about the little girl that went missing almost two decades ago. Given by how torn and yellow it was, the poster was put up around that time too. The face of the young girl really struck me. She resembled Elle so much. ‘Has the emblem of Advent on the back of right hand.’, read the poster. It was in tradition that every heir would have the emblem of their respective state inked onto their skin from a very young age. It was to make them stand out from the crowd; signify they were the future ruler. I wanted to test my theory. I dashed to Elle’s room, pulled down the glove from her right hand that she had since forever worn. Not to my surprise, the emblem was indeed there. “Can’t hide it from you now, can I? Yes, I’m the future heiress of Advent. Yes, I pretended to be an orphan so I could come here and execute my plan.”, she admitted her crimes. “I haven’t even accused you and you’re already surrendering yourself.” “I’m saving you time, Avery. You’d figure it out anyways”. “Why did you do it?”, I frowned. She scoffed, “ Greed. Wealth. Power. Territory. That’s exactly why I did this. What? You thought I did this for your mother’s love? Please!”, she rolled her eyes. “Why don’t you just leave?” “After investing so much time into this? No way! All those years I pretended to love your mother- only to achieve this, Avery. Trust me, I can’t wait to earn this place and leave.”, she squeezed my hand. “I won’t let you.” “Fine,” she seated herself on a chair, “since you’re so adamant on getting rid of me, I challenge you to a battle tomorrow.” I held my head high. “I promise I'll defeat you and you’ll leave this place, alive or dead.” In no time, it was morning. Early in the dusty fog at 6am, I got my armor ready for battle. I picked up my sword, the heavy metal that soon was going to be stained with red, and marched to the training grounds. The audience was ready, they were informed. Elle was standing relaxed, until I walked in. She gave me a sweet smile. I don’t know how she narrated the events to my mother but she seemed very concerned. Soon, it began. The sounds of our heavy blades clashing echoed throughout the arena. It was intense. The urgency to gain victory among us soon followed. Unfortunately, for me, Elle was able to slash through my arm with one swift motion of her blade. “Argh!”, I grunted but still pushed myself to vanquish her. My vision blurred and the sting of my gash got worse, mixed with the fact I was losing blood. She grabbed the opportunity to strike me but I halted her sword with my own, its sharp end cutting through the skin of my palm. “Just give up already, Avery. Nobody cares about you anyway.”, she mocked. “You’re right. Nobody loves me.”, I finally pushed her backwards, “but I love them!”, and charged towards her, the iron piercing through her stomach. Time seemed to halt. Her breathing narrowed and she slowly looked down. She became still, as though holding on to whatever life was remaining in her. “How could you?”, she whispered. “You’re my sister. You taught me this.”, she fell to the ground and my mother rushed towards her. I dropped on my knees. I knew I was going to die. Her blade was laced with venom. But here I was, smiling because I saved my parents from her, danger. “What have you done?!?” - Saved you, mom. But you wouldn’t know that. My limp body could no longer stand, so I fell to the ground, breathing through the tears and smiling through the pain. In due time, it would all be forever gone. I looked at my mother one last time, that stubborn smile plastered on my face, “Maybe one day, in another world, you’d love me.” I hope I made you proud, mom.
author: SARAH ANIS
illustrator: Bipasha  Bhattacharya; Ethan Sen; Hetansh Shah; Swathi Sambasivam; Urvi Prakash

title: Amiable Paws
text: Today I will tell you a true story. We have heard ourselves saying do not judge a book by its cover but we always find ourselves doing the same. Once I found myself in the same situation. There once used to live a stray dog in my neighbourhood called Casper. Though he was energetic, he had dirty fur and looked ferocious. I used to be quite afraid of him. He used to live beside my friend’s house. She too was quite afraid of dogs. As soon as she came outside her house, Casper would jump on her and she used to get scared. She would always describe Casper as a very dangerous and harmful dog and us being children used to accept how she would describe Casper. And we used to be very afraid of him whenever we would see him. One day while I was returning from school with my friend I noticed that Casper was sitting in front of the door staring at it blankly and the house in which Casper used to live in, was vacant. It was empty and the door was locked. I asked my friend “Why is that house locked and empty?” She answered “I heard that the people who used to live in that house have shifted somewhere else. They had gone to another place and left the dog behind”. I did not see any sight of them coming back soon. I felt bad for the dog but since it was getting late, I went home. The next day while I was coming back from school along with my friend, Casper was still lying there and staring at the door blankly. It looked like he was still waiting for the house owner to return. He looked sad and weak. My friend and I thought of taking a close look at him and anxiously went near him. The dog who used to jump at us when he saw us, now just took a little glance at us and again laid down appearing absolutely heartbroken. After having looked at him for the last time, I went home. I could not get Casper out of my mind. I was worried about him. I then asked my Mum for some bread and milk and went outside to give him some. When I came back again to the empty house, I again saw Casper lying there looking weaker then before. I went near him hesitantly and put bread and milk in front of him and ran away from there, as I was a little scared of him. I looked at him from afar and saw that he was not eating the food that I had just given him. I went away to my house hoping that when I come back the next day the food will be finished. The next day we had a holiday and as soon as I woke up the first thing that came to my mind was Casper. I quickly went to freshen up and asked my Mum for some more bread and milk and marched outside my house to go and see Casper. As soon as I came near the house, a big smile appeared on my face. I saw that Casper had finished the food that I had given him the day before. I went towards him to give him milk and bread that I had brought. He came towards me wagging his tail and sat near my feet. I fell in awe at his cute action. I can’t explain the surge of affection towards this cute little thing that I felt for the first time.As it started getting dark, I patted Casper's head for the last time and went away from there. I kept giving him food daily but then, one day while I was returning from school I looked towards the empty house and I could not see Casper anywhere. Feeling sad, I continued towards my house. Soon I heard some steps behind me and as I turned back to look who it was, I found it was Casper who was following me all along. As soon as I turned back, Casper came running towards me enthusiastically and jumped on me. I was very happy to see him. He followed me all the way back to my house. That day onwards Casper started staying with me in my house, of course with the permission of my parents. I took very good care of him. The whole day we used to play together. I loved the way he followed me everywhere wagging his cute tail. It was a cold December month, in the middle of the night, I heard a crackle of window from the sitting room. I saw Casper immediately waking up and barking towards the door. I could feel that something was there behind the door. I froze. I saw Casper with his small paws was able to move the door of my room aside and just ran towards the sitting room from where the sound came. In the faint ambient light, I could see a huge figure jumping out of the drawing room window. Casper kept barking towards the window restlessly. I immediately ran towards my parents room to wake them up who were fast asleep unaware of what was going on. I told them all that had happened and how Casper scared off the burglar. We all went downstairs to meet Casper. He came towards us wagging his tail. My parents started patting his head and gave him treats for the brave action he took to save our lives. We were all very happy. He saved us from getting robbed. We were very proud of him. “ A dog is the only thing in the world that loves you more than he loves himself” — Josh Billing
author: Adrika  Dubey
illustrator: Anupam Arunachalam; Candice  Botha; David Yambem; Deepa Balsavar; Preeti Krishnamurthy; Sarthak Sinha; Siddhi   Vartak

title: The Magical Goat
text: Once a up on time there lived a girl named Rupa. Their family used to get pets and tame them. She had a small goat named Pari as a pet and she loved Pari as she loved herself. As soon as she came home from school she used to spend time with Pari. Rupa doesn’t have any siblings. So, she treated Pari as her sister and spends more time with Pari. The time spent with Pari makes Rupa relaxed and removing the rope tied to it, she used to roam around the garden, where her Pari used to have its lush green grass. It tasted good for Pari. As Rupa liked Pari so also Pari liked Rupa. 2 - Years Passed... The Pari has grown into an adult it’s flesh increased and Rupa lived in a big joint family. It was the time of Bonalu (festival celebrated by Hindus). They wanted to offer the goat to the goddess Kaali. This was revealed to Rupa but she thought that they will offer another goat bought by her uncle but however she came to know that her lovely goat Pari with white and black fleece was about to die. Rupa wanted to save Pari and left the house along with the goat. She went into the forest and left the goat Pari there and came back home as her parents will be searching for her. She felt very happy by leaving the goat in the forest. People in her family started scolding Rupa for her behavior even though she felt happy listening to the scolding of people. Then she stopped eating non-veg. A YEAR PASSED The Pari returned to the Rupa’s house and gave her divine blessing that Rupa could talk to any animal with this blessing Rupa start protecting animals from all these silly customs and rituals. Her loyalty towards animals made her compassionate women and a conservationist. After becoming a billionaire she started purchasing hundreds of birds and freed them. Her true happiness was found on her face while freeing the birds. Therefore she lived happily with animals around her.
author: Samriddhi  J

title: The Enchanted One
text: What did i get myself into? What just happened? Hi, this is Harley Williams, and my family is so called to be magical. Since the day i was born I had never seen the broad daylight. My family always thought that I was the one who had the magical powers, but the last to acquire them was my aunt Dayala Grange. All of this started when my great great great great grandma passed on the powers from generation to generation, but that slowed down inbetween. She was the one who began it, she was profoundly known as the evil witch. She wasn't exactly what we call evil, people just thought that because she had magical powers. My grandma was actually known for her kindness inside the family. Her bloodline started to get the magical powers until Aunt Dayala found a curse to stop it. Since then no one seemed to have the powers. Because of all this I'm not even allowed to leave the house. I've always begged my parents to send me to school, I was fed up of being homeschooled all these years. After so many requests, my parents finally agreed to it, only because they saw no signs of magical powers in me. I was over the moon and filled with joyfullness. My mom and dad warned me not tell anyone about the long line of our history, or else I would have to face the consequences. Oh! Wait! I entirely forgot to tell you all about our Golden Family Rules. 1. Never tell anyone about the family. 2. Never wear colourfull clothes. 3. Always wear a mask. You may be wondering why I have to wear a mask all the time, well it's not because of the virus, but it's because of all this fuss in my family. I've always believed that this is just fictional and that none of it is true, but thanks to my parents, I have to listen to them. After this messed up curse of my Aunt, she formed the Golden Rules of the family. If any outsider looked at my face, the curse will be broken and the powers will re-gain. I thought these were silly rules but my parents were strict about them. So of course, I had to go by them. My first day of school went pretty bad. I got teased for wearing a mask. Even the teachers asked me to remove it, but I couldn't do such a thing or I'll be grounded for the rest of my life. I made one good friend, Avery Wills. She always asked me if she could meet my parents but I refused and I even refused to go to her house. One day I was super tired in class, that I fell asleep at school. I suddenly felt my mask fall off while I was sleeping and everyone saw my face. I was searching for my mask everywhere but I couldn't find it. Anxiety rushed through my body and my mind was crowded with what will happen to me. Will our family regain the powers? I got called into the principal's office because I accidentally slept inside the classroom. All of the students along the corridors stared at me. I realized that I didn't have any power until now, because nothing unusual was happening. But as soon as I entered the principal's office, I found fire everywhere. I finally came to the conclusion, that my power was the power of igniting flames. I didn't know how i felt about it, because I broke the rules, caused destruction to the school and above all, my school life ends here. " Harley Williams?". My mind clicked when the Principal called my name. That's when I realized that it was all a dream. I was unconscious the whole time, but that didn't change me from getting grounded. He proceeded to give me a last warning and I left the place, still not knowing what my powers were. When I was walking back home, I saw dry land, I've always thought of looking at that place with green all around, loads of trees and plants, pretty flowers, fruits in bushes and so on. I closed my eyes and thought about it for a while. I slowly opened my eyes to see what I imagined had come to real life. That's when it hit me, I had the power of 'Mother Nature' the rarest power of all and it was also the so called evil witch's power. No, not the evil witch, she was actually known to be called 'Mother Nature'. I knew exactly what I was going to do. I educated my parents on this issue, and they were happy with it, they let me do whatever I pleased with my powers, after all, they're from Mother Nature herself. I began to develop every part of the world grow to become surplus of greenary. No more global warming, no more scarcity of water. With my powers, I could do anything! Moral of the Story: Trust in yourself, everyone has a power within you. Learn to accept it, and maybe the future might benefit from you
author: Shameera KS
illustrator: 211 Studio; Joanna Davala; Ravi Ranjan  Goswami; Ruchi Shah

title: SOME MISUNDERSTANDING
text: Once upon a time in a small village of Nagaon, there was a boy who was brilliant in his academic career. His family was not economically sound, but he wanted to become an Army officer. He also wanted to enroll himself in National Defence Academy (NDA). At the age of 5, his parents admitted him in Don Bosco. The name of the boy is Saksham. Saksham took his dreams and studied hard from class 1. He received many awards and topped in his class. For these reasons, he faced some problems from his friends. Also due to some unavoidable circumstances and bullying from friends. At class 4, his parents take T/C and transferred him to Kendriya Vidyalaya. At starting days of his school in Kendriya Vidyalaya, he enjoyed the days and become the monitor of the class. He was the teacher’s favourite student. He became class topper enemy. His friends were jealous, and his happy days becomes bad. One day, a discussion moulded to big fight. In this case a middle person is involved. George made conflict between Saksham and Anil. That time, Anil was a big celebrity for the class. Anil was a rule maker of the class. George said to Saksham that Anil says bad things about you. George spoke ill of both Anil and Saksham. But there is nothing between them. At that time Anil and Saksham were best friends. But George wanted to break the friendship between them. According to case Anil make a rule that no one should talk to Saksham. If anyone talked to him then he will be treated as an enemy of the class. This made Saksham depressed and stressed all day. Saksham became bad in his studies. This case happened in class 4. In class 7, George got transferred to Denmark because his mother got job there. One day in the flow of talk a friend asked Saksham about the case that why he said that to Anil. Saksham said that he said nothing to Anil. Similarly, the friend asked same question to Anil and Anil said that he too said nothing to Saksham. This shows that George wanted to make a conflict between the two best friends. At last Anil and Saksham becames best friends and also became the topper of the class. This friendship made Saksham to recover from depression and stress. MORAL: - We should not listen to other’s talk. Otherwise believe whatever we hear with our own ears.
author: Tanay Madhab Saikia
illustrator: Nidhi  Ranjalkar; Sarah Rose de Villiers; Shlok Yagnik

title: The Haircut
text: I are best friends! We love doing everything together! Sometimes, our mom takes us to the hair salon. Meena likes her hair long, so she doesn't cut off much. On the other hand, I like my hair short. That's how I always have it! One afternoon, Meena and I were super bored. "I don't feel like drawing today," said Meena. Suddenly, an idea occurred to me. "Meena!" I yelled. "Let's play hair salon!" "Uh, are you sure, Dhani? I don't want Mom to get me in trouble." "It'll be fine! Wait here." I grabbed a pair of scissors from the kitchen and cut Meena's hair, snip by snip. Of course, I know how to cut hair! Oh no! I forgot Meena prefers long hair. I hear outside footsteps nearing the kitchen. Mom must be home! Mom arrives and sees Meena screaming at all the hair on the floor. "What happened?" she worriedly asks. "Dhani cut my hair, and now it's way too short!" Meena cries. I realized then that this was all my idea from the very beginning. I was selfish and didn't listen to what my sister wanted to do instead. "I'm sorry, Meena. I only thought of myself and what I wanted to do. I didn't listen to you." I say. "Everything's fine, Dhani. My hair will grow out again soon enough," Meena responds. "But now, YOU have to let YOUR hair grow out too."
author: Leslie Plascencia

title: The Five Friends
text: We were five friends. Usually, we were under the big tree in the park near our house. We lived in a small village near Barcelona, in Catalonia- a region of Spain. We would talk about our hobbies, what we did at school, or what we had been reading lately. It was a fantastic friendship; we were inseparable. I was always timid with strangers, but outgoing with my friends: especially the ones from my friend group. I loved reading; my favorite books were detective stories. Sofia was shy like me, but she was shy with everyone. She read books too, but she liked romance and drama books. Often times she would be on her own while reading one of her sentimental books. Ana was her best friend; they'd often go clothes shopping together. Ana was very outgoing and always seemed too hyper around us. Alvaro was also very lively, but a bit less than Ana was. He was very friendly and popular. Everyone called him the class clown. Finally, there was Julio, who was neither shy nor outgoing. He loved animals and would watch the sparrows perched on the big tree in the park. He also loved studying and always got good grades. One day we discovered that, in the distance, there was a jungle. Julio bolted towards the jungle to find out if there were any wild animals. We chased after him but lost sight of him. We searched for him for hours and hours. Until finally, we found a trail of his footsteps, but they were heading in the direction of a river. Deciding to cross it, we were now all drenched, but we continued following the marked footsteps. Suddenly, a tiger appeared, covered in blood because of the deer in its mouth. It was very aggressive and even attacked Ana! She managed to escape and fled far away. Alvaro found and grabbed a walking stick, and the tiger ran away. We went in search of Ana, but we took too long. Day turned to night, so we lit a campfire to keep away aggressive wild animals. We set up our tents, which we always carried around for emergencies. Then, we noticed another campfire and checked if it was either Ana or Julio. At that time, we heard a high-pitched scream. We ran to investigate if that person was okay. We arrived and found the tiger that previously had the deer in its mouth, and to its side was Ana, who was crying. We returned to our campsite, and Ana filled us in on everything that had occurred. The blood on the tiger did not come from the deer, but from Julio. We went back to the tiger's lair to rescue Julio. Sofia picked up the walking stick and led the tiger away. We found Julio's body, and Sofia checked whether he was still alive. He was breathing. We could return home thanks to the trail we had left behind. We called an ambulance and went home. The following day, the doctors informed us that Julio's injuries were not critical. However, he'd still have to stay at the hospital for a few days. We all felt sad and worried in those days because Julio was missing. When Julio returned, we could finally revisit our tree and talk as we used to.
author: Leslie Plascencia
illustrator: Alyssa Pachuau; Angie & Upesh; Barkha Lohia; Rohan Chakravarty; Tapas Guha

title: Isabella the Star
text: There live all the stars, and when the sky darkens, their Mother Moon tells all her children to shine their lights. Every morning before sleeping, Isabella would ask her mother to tell her a bedtime story. These stories would always be about Earth. One day, Isabella asked, "Mother, what is that gray blob with a tube on its face?" Mother Moon said it was an elephant and told her stories about them. Then one day, Isabella saw the sea and fell in love. Since that night, she only asked to hear stories about the sea. She would watch it all night, looking at her reflection on the surface, and imagine what it would be like to live there. One day Isabella leaned over her balcony and fell like a shooting star. She fell into the sea and became a starfish. She saw fish, turtles, whales, seahorses, and everything her mother had mentioned. Her dream became reality, and Isabella has reminded us that we should never give up on our dreams.
author: Leslie Plascencia

title: Out Of The Box !
text: Saksham Arora This is Mr Pathak, a stingy, punctual buisneissman, who was a typical miser too. He was a good man but got stuck between the hands of the clock and his own ego. It was his birthday and he had to crack a very big deal with a client. So he left his house in hurry and drove his car on his own as his driver was just 2 minutes late. When he reached his office, the person he was about to meet had not reached yet.That's why he got irritated. After a while, their client, Mr Desai arrived. Both of them finalized the deal. After that they both went for lunch and discussed more. Mr Pathak got even more irritated as M.r Desai was a talkative person.As though that was not enough.Mr Desai asked for Mr Pathak's car. Poor Mr Pathak! he wanted to say no but he thought it would be rude. Forcefully he said yes. After the lunch, Mr Desai went with Mr Pathak's car. Mr Pathak had to walk as all the taxis and cabs were closed after 2 pm While Mr. Pathak a rich businessman was walking on the road, with an ego of his, people laughed at him as he was walking weirdly and he found it really awkward as he was not used to walk on roads with such a big traffic jam. The next moment his childhood friend, Santosh bumped into him. Santosh looked a little poor guy by the way he dressed but by the way he smiled it seemed like he was a billionaire. Mr. Pathak wanted to know more about Santosh. He wanted to talk with Mr. Pathak while having some tea. Within minutes, Mr Pathak came to know about Santosh's salary,it was 10 times lesser than him,still he was very happy and satisfied with his life. After the tea, Santosh said Mr Pathak a goodbye and left. Still Mr Pathak was very angry and fraustrated at the situation. After a while he saw very poor families on the road. They did not have any good house to live in, and no proper clothes to wear. They lived by entertaining other people. Still they were laughing, enjoying their life. Seeing this Mr Pathak was regretting that he is spoiling his life by running after money and time. He saw the real meaning of life in every situation that we enjoy life in every situation we are in.We just need a smile to start. After that day Mr. Pathak saw the real joy and pleasure of life.Life is the same we just need to change the way we see it. We always look on the bad and negative side of life. Try to look at the good and positive side of life to enjoy, laugh and smile in our life That's why we should leave our routine and come " Out Of The Box! " to see the real meaning of life!

title: The Bond
text: This is the beginning of Treta yuga, goodness was flourishing and demonic powers were constantly trying to conquer the world. A girl named Vatika lived in jungle with her parents and with her pet dog. In the same jungle there lived a demon, who made a spell to see people in terror.He then used the spell to spread a disease which would kill people instantly. People were terrified so were Vatika and her family, unfortunately her parents were caught in the spell and were affected by the the disease.Her parents death crashed her totally. Vatika prayed to the local demi-god Prungala-Gog of happiness, she prayed till she was at the verge of death. This impressed Prungala and appeared in front of Vatika. Prungala asked Vatika for a boon, Vatika answered," I don't want any boon, I want happiness" Vatika answered, Prungala said,' Tathatsu," He then vanished into thin air, suddenly the door of the house opened, light coming from the door blinded Vatika for a second, Then a man appeared in front of Vatika, he was glowing with charm, he had a heavenly and a soothing aura and a smile which would make anyone feel comfort.His name was Matsya. He then treated Vatika and during the treatment of Vatika they both fell in love with each other. After Vatika was cured, both Vatika and Matsya cured the village together. Matsya, Vatika lived very happily for few years. But then the demon reappeared and now was in search of Matysa and Vatika as they cured the whole village which brought happiness back to the village. This led the the demon to get weak as he ate on the sorrow of people to become more strong. The demon later found Vatika's dog in the jungle. The dog was following a butterfly, but the dog was unable to catch the butterfly so the dog went back to his house. He was followed by the demon. The demon later found the place were Matsya and Vatika lived. Demon stayed their till Matsya returned, when he arrived demon used his sword and stabbed him from the back. Matsya was now in the hands of Vatika, she was weeping as her loved one bleed, Matsya stood up and said," Fool demon, you did a wrong thing. This is going to be your last mistake," Matsya now murmured a mantra, he turned a blade of grass into a magical sword. He then faught the demon and left the demon half dead. The demon was unable to regenerate his parts of body which were cut off. Matsya was also on the verge of death, Using his last breath he gave a boon to Vatika," you shall have three children with magical powers", he then said that he was an avatar of Prungala. He later vanished into thin air to get merge into Prungala. The demon also ran away leaving behind no trace of himself. Vatika then had two boys and one girl child. The elder most named Megnath, He had magical powers. The middle child named Mahisha, she had strength of 100 tigers. The youngest one named Mastka, he had the knowledge of the gods.They were interconnected - which means that if even one of them were away from each other, they would loose their power and would become powerless. One day they were training in the jungle where they were seen by the demon,he had the intention of killing them as he wanted to take revenge to Vatika. Demon knew their weakness as he earlier heard it from Vatika when she was talking with her children when they were toddlers, the demon was unable to attack them when they were small kids as they protected by a mantra which protected them from anything which could cause any harm to them. This was also a gift from their father.As they grew older the mantra also grew weak. Now demon has shifted the shape to Mahisha who was at home helping her mother, he acted as if Mahisha was arrogant of her powers, the demon told Mastka,' how weak he was," this hurt pride of Mastka and they started fighting, Mastka used mantras to attack Mahisha (the demon), Megnath then interfered to stop the fight. This all led an inter fight between the siblings. The demon left and now came the true Mahisha, she was confused because she was ill treated by her brothers. The demon returned back in the form of Vatika, the demon told the siblings while being in the form of Vatika," I saw a dream in which your Late father's soul was calling you all to the cave were he was trapped. The siblings rushed to the cave, they separated themselves as they did not want each others help to save their father. This was what the demon wanted. The demon used his powers to make the distance between them more vast, this made them to loose their powers. There was no way for them to get their powers back or to escape. Suddenly there was a ", Wolf," there appeared Vatika's dog, who had the power to find anyone and was able to speak human language and was also able to shape shift himself to anything which he wanted to,gited by Matsya. become. He then spoke that he was commanded by Vatika to find you three. He then made three of them to come to a common place where he told three of them about their father. They were shocked by the truth. Vatika's dog also told three of them about the truth that it was not Mahisha who started the fight earlier and it was also not their mother who told them to come to this cave. It was the demon who took shape of your mom. Then the siblings apologized to each other and started breaking walls to find the exit. Then Mastka said," I think that the demon has used some sort of spell which has made the cave a place with infinite walls,"Then Megnath said," Mastka, You should recite a spell which could counter the spell of the demon. Mastka agreed but he said that the spell that I am going to recite quite long and when recited other demons would attack us. Megnath and Mahisha said,"leave it us," Mastka started reciting the spell, the demons started to ambush on Mastka but Megnath and Mahisha saved Mastka. He was able to break the spell and were able to escape the cave.Now they were in search of the demon. They found the at the lake, he was going to eat Vatika at the center of the lake. The siblings ambushed him and were able to save their mother, now Mastka told the other two to hold their hands together, Mastka then cast a spell, he named it "the spell of BOND", this spell made the demon weak and was unable to regenerate his body, Then Mahisha threw the demon in to the lake, then Megnath used his magic to freeze the water. Three of them now coming with a combo attack punched the demon and he was converted into shards of ice. The family hugged each other, Mastka asked Vatika about the dog of hers. Vatika answered that her dog died when he was 4 years old. Vatika then said it must have been your father's LOVE and power of your BOND.

title: THE JOURNEY OF HAVING A SHIH TZU
text: It was a rainy day. I was 4 years old at that time.One day I woke up and thought that why not keep a pup. As I am a single child, I feel quite lonely. I ran this idea to my parents and they said darling, my sweet child you are too young, not responsible enough to keep a pup.I was really mad at their response. I kept trying again and again but they continued filling my basket with no, no and NO!I decided to show them how responsible I was. At the age of 6, I did a lot of research on Google about the different dog breeds and their habitats.I wanted to find a dog breed suitable enough for my family.Two years later on my birthday when I turned 8, I told my parents about the research which I did. Then finally the hunt began to look for a suitable companion.I first suggested to get a Labrador,it got cancelled because of its big size followed by a golden retriever which couldn’t make it to our house because of too much hair fall. One fine day my father bought beagle but oh! My lord he was too much for us to handle. The beagle kept us up entire night. My mom was up so was my father and beagle whom I named Biglu was chewing drawers handles, pulling sheet, eating carpet and what not. Next morning my mom took a decision which shattered all my dreams.I am sure you all must be eager to know that.My mom returned my Biglu they said he was too much to handle.Again my begging began for a puppy and finally shih tzu they agreed on. One fine day my dad got his friend’s pup.She was a shih tzu when I met her after I returned from school she started barking at me. I got so petrified that I wore my mother’s pyjamas to get close to her.I went inside with a scared face but surprisingly she was loving me a lot. Next day when I woke up I saw her pulling my mother’s pyjama, I laughed a lot. I gave her breakfast just to figure out what she liked the most and turns out she loved chicken.I played with her day, night forgetting one day we had to give her back to my father’s friend. I was devastated and cried the day my father returned her back.The next day my father woke me up in the morning and said,”Wakey-wakey! It’s a brand new day we are going to buy a shih tzu. I was overjoyed and got dressed up. We left our house at 11 in the morning.When I reached there the dog dealer showed me 2 pups the 1st one was black and white and the second one was of tri colour. I decided to go for the tri colour one. My parents also agreed with me. We bought my very first pup. We took him home and set his first bed which was a padded crate and we put a light bulb to give him warmth.Since it was the month of December and he was just 40 days old.I fed him baby food and looked after him well.Three days later,to our surprise, my father had received orders for transferring to Jhansi. I panicked and did not know what to do now because we had recently bought a pup and he was just 41 days old and we couldn't carry him on a train. So you won’t believe me what we did. We decided to sneak him in the train in a vegetable basket. Everything was going perfectly as per plan until 4 in the morning when he started to cry because he needed to pee and to make things worse the ticket checker had just entered our train cabin. I thought we will be apprehended, so my mother took him to the front door and tried to calm him down. We finally reached our station.I put him down at the exit and so that he could pee. We reached our new home and he was very fascinated to discover it.The next day when I woke up I noticed that he was playing with my mother’s pyjama and also that he was very fond of eating chicken and his treats.We spent a week and finally decided to name him, Fluffy. We evenyually started calling him ‘Fufu’ as an affectionate nickname.Two months later we gave him his very first bath and after that he was sent to the groomer. He was crying constantly but we couldn’t figure out the reason,so we took him to the vet and found out that he had a virus effecting him on his rear end. The doctor told us to clean We really got worried but the next day he was fine and back to his regular routine.His walk includes walk by my dad at 4 in the morning. The moment he gets back, he rushes inside the house and bangs his front paws on the bed so loudly that my mom wakes up.I pity my mom as she doesn’t get to sleep because every day Fufu wakes her up. My mom gives him breakfast and then I play with him outside for an hour.In the evening he goes to the park and comes home at exactly 7 pm. If you want to look for Fufu then the place to look is in our kitchen. This is my Fufu’s schedule and one thing more, he loves barking at random strangers! Regardless, I love Fluffy and hope that he lives a long and happy life for days to come.

title: A Group of Frogs
text: A group of frogs was travelling through the woods. Two of them fell into a deep pit. The other frogs crowded around the pit and saw how deep it was. They told the two frogs that there was no hope left for them. However, the two frogs decided to ignore what the others were saying and they proceeded to try and jump out of the pit. The group of frogs at the top of the pit was still saying that they should just give up. They would never make it out. They were discouraging the two frogs despite their efforts. Eventually, one of the frogs took heed to what the others were saying and he gave up, falling down to his death. The other frog continued to jump as hard as he could. Again, the crowd of frogs yelled to stop the pain and just die. He jumped even harder and finally made it out. When he got out, the other frogs said, “Did you not hear us?” The frog explained to them that he was deaf. He thought they were encouraging him the entire time.
author: Shivam Kumar
illustrator: Aindri C; Jane Taylor; Marco Tibasima

title: Saudate
text: Saudade (n.) A nostalgic longing to be near again to something or someone that is distant, or that has been loved and then lost. T he sun sinks as the evening arises. The bright day drips away as the musky red sky overlaps with the gray night. As the moon peeks to check on the night that is to come, the waves play with each other and people play along with them. A lone figure stood amidst this, inhaling the ocean's salty breath. Her curly red hair followed the wind as her hazel green eyes stared at the sinking sun. She had freckles that peppered her rosy cheeks. Her eyebrows were scrunched together as if she was lost in thought causing her to purse her cupid bow lips into a thin line. She came out of her thoughts as something startled her by hitting her. "Sorry!" a male voice shouted as she turned her head from the rolling volleyball that had hit her to see a male with auburn brown hair and blue eyes running up to her with an apologizing look. "Sorry about that." He stated as he picked up the ball, rubbing the back of his neck as he asked if she was hurt. "No, I am fine. It's okay," she assured and smiled politely at him. He apologized again before turning to head back to the game. He froze and turned around " Hey, do you want to join us? You have been staring at the sun for so long." She turned to face him " It's alright. I have some things to think off and let go along the waves." "Is everything alright?" "Don't think it's any of your business," she muttered as she quirked her eyebrows in annoyance. "Carlos! Bring the ball!" they heard someone yell. The blue-eyed stranger turned to the voice where a bunch of girls and boys were standing and threw the ball at them. "You guys continue the game I will join you later." He yelled and threw the ball back at them before facing the curious green-eyed girl as his friend curiously left with the ball. "I don't mean to pry. Sometimes talking about it will help you let go easily." He said as he faced the ocean. "You know....not all storms come to disrupt you. Some come to clear your path" "I think you have come to cause puddles in the calm water Carlos," she said not even trying to hide the annoyance in her voice. Hearing his name called by her fazed him a bit but he came out of it quickly as he replied to her " Someone once said if you follow the footstep of a stranger you will find something new. " He noticed her mumble something under her breath and her face clearly stated that he was a bee on her bonnet. " Seems like you don't want to find something new, I will leave saying that one can't hold their breath for more than two minutes" He turned to join his friend in their game and snickered about how bad they were at hiding the fact they had been curious about what was happening with these two as he saw them throw the ball while their heads were tilted to where these two were talking and side-eyeing them. Before he could leave he heard her ask "What do you mean?" "Quise decir que no puedes aferrarte a nada por mucho tiempo." He said as he turned to face her to see her look at him in utter confusion making him chuckle. "Excuse me?" she quacked. "That was Spanish. I will tell you what it meant if you could tell your name seeing you know mine," he said cocking his head knowing he had opened the door of her curiosity. She stood taken aback and thought for a minute before answering, "I am Anne. It's nice to meet you" and stretched her arm out for a handshake. "Well Anne, let's see where this path leads us," he said smirking cockily at his victory, before shaking her hand "What I said before meant you can't hold onto anything for so long. " he said as he let go of her hand. "Care to elaborate?" Anne asked as she took back her hand. "You can't hold onto anything, let it be an emotion, people, or things. Everything changes with time, meaning you would be holding onto something already gone." "So we have to just forget the value and the place it held in our hearts and just let it go?" "No, I am not asking you to forget but to accept that it is gone. The oyster gobbles up the raindrop to make pearls. We don't care about the gobbled-up raindrop, do we?" "No..." she stated and turned to face the sea as she hugged herself and stared at the head of the sun that was peeping out of the sea. The sky looked as if an artist had mixed gray and blue paint with black paint on her pallet. She turned her head from the fleeting albatross to take a look at the boy talking to her. Feeling her eyes on him he turned his head and raised a brow "What?" He questioned her. "Nothing." "You can ask me whatever you want." He stated facing her and giving her a reassuring smile. "It's just- I mean it was even hard to imagine my life without him, but now he is just....gone." She started with a shaky breath. "I had watched him grow and he was there with me through my highest and lowest point of life. I just am having a hard time comprehending the fact that he is no longer in my life. It annoys me to the death that I just can't bring him back to me." "You can just talk to him?" "You can't talk to someone dead Carlos," she muttered looking away with a rigid look on her face. "Oh Anne! Uh, I am umm…. sorry for your loss." he stuttered wide-eyed as he was a bit flustered by the sudden revelation. "It's okay." Anne sighed and looked down and started drawing patterns on the sand. Carlos still embarrassed looked at the moon welcoming the night. After a few minutes of awkward silence, he pulled himself back together and said "Must have been pretty rough huh? Losing someone dear to you." "Mmm yea. But everyone says it's stupid that I am still missing him considering he has been gone for months. My family and friends are tired of seeing me down in the dumps. But I just can't help it, I am trying to get over it. It's not easy to accept that you can't see that person that you saw every day is just gone and you can never see them again." she said back to see the stars waking up to join the moon in welcoming the night. "Well...remember what I said? The raindrop becomes the pearl. I am sure that he is in a much better place and misses you very much. Think of it as a transformation rather than thinking that the person is just gone. And I am sure wherever he is he doesn't want you to sit and mop around for him." he replied to her after trying his best to empathize with her. " I know...I know that he wouldn't want me to sit around like this. That makes me feel like an idiot." she said sighing. " You are not an idiot just cause you miss him, Anne." He said his voice serious. He looked at the sky and said " When you miss him look at the stars. That would be him staring at you and watching over you." Anne looked up as she stared at the night sky. The two strangers stood there in comfortable silence letting the night sink in. Many people had left as it got dark. The night had sunk in and it had become dark. The sea looked a bit spooked out trying to match the sky but the ﻿stars decorated the sky and were scattered everywhere so that it could shine a bit for everyone. The moon had been awoken fully and shone with all its might brightening the night. Anne looked up at this sky with new hope and wondered how many found a new reason to look up the sky that night. She found herself smiling as she saw fishes leap out of the water to get a glimpse of the night, wishing the stars goodnight before disappearing underwater again. She turned and eyed the stranger she met. His hair was being messed up softly by the wind as he stared at the shrieking seagulls fighting for their dinner with a hint of amusement in his eyes with his arms crossed. "Thank you." Sh e said softly to him that he almost missed what she said. "What?" he asked her. "I said thank you." She said and gave him a small smile. He just smiled back at her. "May I know who this person is? That is if you don't mind." He asked. "Oh! Well, you see it's my pet cat caramel. I have had him for over 14 years. Want to see a picture of him?" she questioned him. "As much as I would love to continue our chat. I have to get going. Or I would probably reach my house at dawn after breaking my knees." He joked as he jogged toward his friend waving to her after yelling "You should also get home,it's getting late. Have a good night Anne. It was nice meeting you. Goodbye!" "Hope to see you around Carlos. Goodbye." She said waving back at him. ~END~
author: Bersheba  Anointus

title: The Monkey and Crocodile
text: This story tells us about the famous monkey and crocodile story in which the monkey lives alone in a tree. The tree is on a riverbank and is laden with fruits. The monkey eats the fruit of his liking to his heart’s delight. The monkey is happy but something still feels incomplete. He does not have a friend to talk to and share the fruits with. So, he longs for one. However, one fine day, a crocodile comes there. The monkey offers him fruit to eat. The crocodile accepts and finds the fruit to be really delicious. Thus, he begins visiting the monkey regularly and eat fruits with him. Now, their bond turns stronger and they become close. While the crocodile eats the fruits himself, he also carries some of them for his wife. The monkey and crocodile talk about everything from birds to animals. Further, they also talk about the villagers nearby and the difficulty they have in raising good crops because of the lack of rain. One day, the crocodile’s wife asks him about his friend. The crocodile tells her that his friend is a nice monkey who send her fruits every day. Thus, the wife expresses her wish to eat the heart of his friend, monkey. She orders him to bring him over someday but the crocodile does not agree to it. He cherishes his friend and does not want to kill him. However, she finally manipulates him to invite him for dinner. He goes to the river bank and invites him over for dinner for a meal. The monkey happily accepts and rides the crocodile’s back to reach the middle of the river. However, the crocodile cannot lie to him and tells him about his wife’s plan. Soon, the monkey realizes the situation and fools him. He tells him he has left his heart at the tree so he must go back to get it. When they reach the riverbank, the monkey quickly jumps back on the tree. Then, he bids the crocodile goodbye. This saddens the crocodile as he has lost a dear friend and he starts crying. So, we see how the crocodile never got to taste the sweetness of fruits again. Therefore, we learn how this story teaches about different human traits through animals. Traits like friendship, betrayal, wisdom and estrangement. Conclusion of The Monkey and the Crocodile Summary The Monkey and the Crocodile Summary teaches us that we must never underestimate ourselves just like the monkey. Even though he did not have the upper hand, he saved himself from the situation by being wise.
author: Aditya Sharma
