title: OBSERVERS IN LOVE
text: The night was dark, and it was raining cats and dogs. Mr. Sharma huddled close to his cat as all the thoughts of his day flooded in. This had been the routine for about 3 months since that period of darkness had passed through his life and helped him more than ever. The focus they had to give to each other helped him more than ever. And did his cat, Linda, want attention? All those times when he used to drift off to his thoughts that brought tears to his eyes it was Linda who used to scratch him to death to make him remember and know that she was the only one that mattered and no one else. Though he was the only person overqualified, there seemed to be no one even trying to give him the work that required his qualification and promote him like they are supposed to. He was also known as the nicest guy but did it earn him any help or even a stable partner? NO, nothing. He was just seen as a too high a level guy whom no one could even reach and hence never tried to. He had done it again, drifted off to his own land. She allowed anything but that, well she was really possessive. Scowling, Linda scratched off his arm and mewed. That was all the signal he needed to come back to his own world, to his Linda, the black cat who had been the only stable thing in his life since that incident involving his parents as he cuddled his face closer so that she could feel him through each and every inch of her body just the way she loved. There was only one formula in her life, she wanted everything and the best. If she became a human only she knew how easily all this nonsense could end and how easily— She tries her best to pick herself up and more than that all that pride that had been scattered on the floor along with her. Jay was standing bewildered looking at the floor. A monkey had fallen from the adjoining tree and blood was flowing continuously from his mouth and to Linda’s bafflement, it was ruining, had ruined all of the carpets. She scrawled and scratched and cried for the absence of him as he took her back and cuddled harder than before. His eyes were wide open in fear but noticing how calm and cute Linda became he couldn’t help but get back onto the window side and try his best not to care about the situation. Because both knew that it wouldn’t matter even to them if death came and takes them the very next day. He was almost asleep without a sound but mewing of Linda on seeing the black cat woke him up. There was a total of 5 blooded creatures on the mat and the monkey and a bat were trying their best to climb through the other window. The next time they woke up all of them had vanished leaving a lot of remnants behind. Jay stood up trying his best to put it all back together and close all the doors and windows. They soon found out that they were one of the few alive and unaffected by the virus which had spread in the whole city killing people or turning them into monsters the next day.

title: Not Just A Scar
text: It was a chilly winter afternoon, and looking around all I noticed was a white, blanket of snow covering the trees, ground and posters. There was a crowd of people waiting for the bus, but there was one pupil whom I couldn’t take my eyes off. He had a peculiar scar on his right arm, curvy at the start, then slowly sliding with another design starting below. Although this scar was very odd I was pretty sure I had seen it somewhere else, but where? This thought of my mind had a abrupt end when the bus going to my home arrived. I wanted to stay there a little more and brainstorm fantasy stories about the scar but it was the last one to go to my residence so I reluctantly boarded the bus. Upon reaching home I heard sobbing voices from my mom’s room she was holding my father’s picture like everyday and that’s when I checked the date… Oh no that’s the day my father, he died. How could I even forget. I opened the door to check on her and I couldn’t believe my eyes. At first all I see is her wailing, but as I notice closely, I saw the same scar like the man on her elbow too.. I gathered my courage and asked my mom about the scar and she wiped her tears, went silent for a second or 2 and just told me that it was because of a car crash. PLEASE TURN THIS PAGE I could clearly tell through her expressions that she was lying bu decided not to bother her.There was still a feeling in my mind that these scar and the man and my mother are related. The next morning I saw that man at the bus stop and he, out of nowhere, came to me and asked for my buisness card. Me, being surprised by his request decided to fulfill it. He sees my card and his expressions change, and all he does is mutter something under his breath and and just walked before I even could say a word to him. Thinking of it again I seem to remember it as a apology. I was searching for this man at the evening and after finding him, I demanded the truth. After a series of interrogation he continued- I, Daniel was orphaned at the age of 3, and growing up my matron always told me how I got my fathers deep, blue eyes. I called her madam vinnie. Such a sweet woman she was. Anyways, soon after I got adopted but by a abusive dad. There I found your dad, Charles and we became good friends. Then the police came to know about my dad and then I got adopted again. My new family was very sweet. My parents didn’t like your dad that much though. They always told me how something was wrong with your dad, and, I, of course ignored it We still were good friends. Soon I started school and there is where we met olivia, your mother. We three started hanging out together. After completing school olivias parents got her married with your dad. Every thing was fine until one day olivia told me about the camping trip with your dad. I decided to surprise them but saw your dad hitting olivia. As I had gone through the trauma, I couldn’t tolerate it and pushed your dad and he went sliding down the hill. I soon was arrested for this and your mother got distanced from me. After coming from jail I tried to trace your mother’s number but in vain. And when I saw you I decided to apologize. I was fuming with anger and hardly noticed the tear in his eyes. Just because my father hit my mom a little, he would just kill him. I was not ready to hear a word from him and just leaving was the only thing I could think of. Upon reaching home I decided to confront mom and as soon as I was entering the room, I saw my mom with a photo in her hand and the photo was not my dad, he was Daniel. I told her the entire story and her eyes widened. You……Met….Him?? Did you said thank you? I couldn’t believe my mom and said Thank you for what?, killing my father? My mom lips curled into a small smile which looked more like sadness, she said that she needed to tell me something and continued- I met your dad and Daniel at school. We became good friends and your dad was always sweet and kind but sometimes he was a little irritating. After college, My parents forcefully made me marry your dad. Sometime later he became stressed due to his work and became abusive.My intention of camping was to tell Daniel about it but never got a chance to. Can you please bring Daniel here she requested. The next day I found him and asked him to come with me and surprisingly, he agreed. My mother and he talked for a long time. They then put their elbows together. It looked like a incomplete flower with heart. They both felt silent. Their still was someone left to complete it.
author: AVIKA MAHESHWARI

title: I Quit
text: "I quit!" yelled Zach as he flung the agreement papers on the office table. He was ferocious and a red shade of frustration covered his neat, straight face. The cause of his anger was quite fair. His deal got cancelled with a renowned industrialist. (story background) Zack's father, Edward started up his own business and succeeded with flying colors.He had worked really hard, put in lots of efforts and time to bring Zach up right.He provided him with everything he could. Eventually,Zach started taking his parents for granted, disobeyed them and misbehaved.His formative years were a tough deal for his parents to handle him. He was average in academics, a total bully and behaved carelessly. Since childhood, he disliked holding a pen or pencil in his hands to write, but little Zach never knew that this pencil one day would entirely transform his life.Yet, somehow his parents managed to deal with him as they knew he was a teenager and needed considerable time to get aligned with high school. Years flew by and he completed his education. By 'completed', I mean -in his final year of college, he couldn't even afford to pass, so somehow he pulled up some strings and managed to pass in an incorrect manner.His father was absolutely clueless about this incident. Now was the time for Zach to choose a career path and start getting a clear vision for his future.He was confused, yet in no ways concerned. Zach tried hard for a job for almost a year, but could not get expected results. Mr.Edward was quite an intellectual and a respected man and when people started seeing his son - a jobless, idle man in his almost 30's, they started mud-slinging. Poor Edward, out of no choice and mercy for his irresponsible boy, gave him a job at his own company. (back to the scene) This deal was like a do or die situation for him.He had been warned by his father that if this deal doesn't get finalized, he would fire Zach.The deal was cancelled because Zach's presentation was not professional and good enough.He was tensed for the very first time in his life and decided to flee from the office.He secretly fled, such a coward of a man! He decided to take a stroll around to calm his temper.As he was walking past the glowed-up, fancy streets of Berkshire Square, his mind was flooded with negative thoughts.He was lost in his own thoughts and lo! he unknowingly took a train!.He was completely annoyed, stressed as well as unaware of what he was doing and just boarded the train.After a while he realized it when there was a group of children creating chaos around him. He looked around, he was astonished! The train had started moving already and Zach broke out in sweat and was extremely panicked.He had no idea what he would do with a meagre amount of money with him, he didn't know where the train would go, no idea at all!. He got off at the next station and drank a little water.He tried to keep calm. He sipped a few sips of water, he sighed -the sigh had an immense amount of relief as well as tension in it.That is, when he saw a poor old man with old, shaggy, rigged clothes with a drawn face selling a bunch of pencils. Zach found it strange that an old man was selling pencils on a railway station and why wouldn't he feel so?, he had never seen poverty before.He approached the man and asked him the reason behind him selling those pencils. The man replied,"Sir,would you like to buy some pencils?".Zach didn't get the asnwer to his question and again asked. The man said, "My son, I couldn't make my own future with these small yet strong weapons called pencils - I always kept being lazy and now here I am in front of you repenting for it and trying to aid others in brightening their future." When he said these words, Zach was speechless, "How?" was all that he blurted. "You see this pencil? it's not just a pencil it's a pathway for students to reach their aim, they will read,write and learn with this and then they will make their aim a reality." Zach did not speak a word. In almost 30 years of his life, this was the first time he had ever gotten so concerned about his future, that he started realising that unless and until he won't make efforts to achieve something in life, it won't happen. He was overwhelmed and a huge wave of inspiration and motivation ran through him and he purchased the pencils. He took a train to California.He decided that he had to make effective use of these pencils in future. He made a firm decision to complete his education, this time in an appropriate manner.With all the money he had, he took admission in a college in California and studied Arts with complete dedication. That is, when he found out about his passion and interest towards the teaching learning process, he decided to become a teacher!To teach students, to nurture the future and to make it bright.He studied hard, after years of hard work, he got a degree-this time a real one! He qualified to become a teacher and taught students in a reputed institute. At that moment in his life, he realized that these words -" I quit." can often be the beginning of some remarkable and unpredictable tasks. "Those who know, do; those who understand, teach." -"Aristotle"
author: Shivani Mane

title: The Tale of Alexandra Jones
text: Alexandra had always known she could do everything. It didn't matter whether she was black or white, male or female. She was so smart and hardworking, that when she skipped a few classes, she didn't find it that hard to catch up with all the work. Alexandra was living happily, minding her own business, but there were just two problems. Two tiny problems. First, she was a girl. And second, she was black. She, her mother and sister faced extreme racism. Alexandra was also at times humiliated because of her tomboyish looks. She had very short, straight black hair. She also called herself Alex. She was told that she could never follow her dreams, which were becoming a writer and a poet, and that too, a famous one. Whenever anyone said this, Alex responded, "I can be whoever I want, and whatever I want. That will not change just because I am a girl or if I am black!" Alex had always been brilliant at writing stories. Her sister, Sadie, too, wrote stories and introduced her to writing in the first place. Their mother, Scarlett, was a teacher and taught them history in their school. They lived with their paternal grandparents but their father had passed away around the time Alex was born, so she didn't really know much about him except for the fact that he and their mother fell in love and that he was an excellent cook. Alex didn't have more than two friends, but there two she did have were very faithful. They were very kind souls, and didn't care about the fact that she was black or that she was a girl. They definitely didn't care about the latter because they were girls themselves. And for the former, well, they were open minded and smart girls. They understood that anyone can do anything if they worked hard enough and if their cause was good. As Alex was turning sixteen and her sister (Sadie) nineteen, Sadie was going to go to college. They were living in Canada, and Sadie was going to go to America (Harvard University). She was going to pursue her love of literature. Alex knew that she was going to truly miss her sister, so she decided to visit her as much as she could. Little did either know, both would go to the very same college and pursue the very same career with the very same love of writing. Over the next few years, Alex excelled at her studies more than ever. She wasn't sure what she wanted to become, a writer or a poet, or maybe even both. And also, at this time, she faced more racism than she ever had. But still, Alex did not lose hope. She was a very, very strong willed girl after all. Alex's favorite hobby was writing poems. When she was writing, it was like she was in a different world altogether. A world of her own. A world, full of imagination, creativity, beauty, and people who didn't care at all about the way a person looks, or their gender. But, the problem was, this was just Alex's world, made of her imagination. It was not reality. But, Alex knew that she would make her imagination world a reality. She would do anything in her power to make this world a better place, and of course, follow her dreams at the same time. Eight years later "Ms Alexandra Jones, the world famous writer of the trilogy 'The Years of my Life' and many other books has…" "Ms Jones, one of the best writers in the world!" "Ms Sadie and Ms Alexandra, the most successful writers…" Alex smiled, reading the headlines of the daily newspaper. She was twenty-four now, living her life happily. Alex was remembering all the times she and Sadie (who lived just across the street) had dreamed of the times when everyone would respect them. But now, Alex happened to be a very famous writer. She happened to be a very famous, black, female writer. It was pure talent and determination and creativity that got her there, not her race or gender. She had not given in. She didn't have limits in her mind. And that's what really matters in the end.
author: Medha Sharma

title: All That Glitters Are Not Gold
text: As I was sitting on my study table thinking what stream I should take for my studies, My younger sister came to me and said “Let’s play Hide and seek! I said “OK” I will take a break. My younger sister started counting and I went to the basement to hide. I opened a cupboard which looked very old and it`s color was vanished, I sat in it to hide. But I noticed It was very huge from inside. It was like a passage to somewhere. I started walking and it was endless! I kept walking but there was no sign of anything. I started crying and did not knew what to do and I slept. When I opened my eyes, I found myself in an another world! I did not knew where I was but there was everywhere drones, holograms and big buildings. I was amazed by seeing the high technology. There I saw a big screen on a building where a lady (30 to 35 years) was receiving an award. When she introduced herself, the earth under my feet slipped. Her name was “AMBER DREW”. The shocking thing was it’s me! A strange question came to my mind “How come it was me?” Then I asked a girl what date and year it was and she said “28 November, 2060. I nearly fainted. So that lady on the screen was…… I was really happy and decided to meet my future self. But as expected, The guards did not let me in. But I got inside the house through a window. I saw my future self and she was beautiful! She has dyed her hair brown and was wearing blue coloured contact lenses. She was about to scream but I stopped her. I said “ I know it’s impossible but I am here from past.” I told her everything that had happened. I even showed her our birthmark and she finally believed me. Then I asked her about her life and she seemed sad answering that. She said “ Yeah, It’s alright. Nothing’s new. Everything's just boring" the older me said. "Are you not happy? You are rich!" I said with an astonishing voice. "NO! I just want to live my dream. A normal happy life! Without any stress and business problems!" the older me explained. "But everyone has problems in their life!" I said. "But they do what they like! We wanted to be an artist and work in a NGO to help others. But, as we grew older, we forgot our dream! And as time passed by we lost confidence in our dream too. Being rich and being happy are not the same thing. All that glitters is not gold!" That line touched my heart. I noticed the shine in her eyes to live her dream and how she was dying to do what she wanted and here I was stuck at being rich. She calmly rubbed my back and said "It’s your time! Do not regret in future, like I do. There’s nothing in being rich! Go decide your future! And remember your dreams come first. Go Amber, choose the best for yourself!" After our consoling and warming introspective conversation, I entered the door I came from and started running. This time I knew I would reach my world! At that moment, I knew exactly what to do in my life. Today, I am an artist and work in an NGO to help others. I am living my life the way I want! I learned from my life that being rich is not important, the thing important is to live your dream! We should be kind enough to make our dream to help others and we should have confidence on our dream too. NAME – SHIVANGI VERMA CLASS – 7M SCHOOL – SHIVALIK PUBLIC SCHOOL, MOHALI
author: Shivangi Verma

title: The lives of victorious girls
text: Once, there was a village that was filled with happiness and compassion. In that village, there was a girl named Kalpana, aged 12. She was a brave, honest, and kind person, but they were poor. Her parents decided to settle in Chennai. For that, her father borrowed money from someone he knew. Kalpana was sad because she was leaving her house, farm, pets, friends, and everything. After some days, they went to Chennai. They decided to live near a coastal area. One day, Kalpana went to her father and asked if she wanted to continue her studies. Her father replied that he didn't have a proper job to spend money on her studies. She was sad upon her father’s reply, and sat near the stairs. There were two girls playing near her house. They saw Kalpana and went to her, realizing she was sad. They asked her, "Why are you looking sad?" At first, Kalpana hesitates to talk to them as they are new to her. Then, after a few minutes, she opened up and told them why she was feeling sad. They consoled Kalpana and asked her to be their friend. They introduced themselves to each other. Their names are Maha and Kanika. One day Kalpana went to Maha’s house to check whether they were there because they hadn’t come to play with her since the morning. Kalapana saw Maha’s mother and asked about Maha. Maha’s mother replied that she is inside her room, go and visit her there. She went inside and went to talk to her. Kalpana: Why didn't you come to play with me from the morning? Maha: I went for hill climbing training. Kalpana: Are you going for the climb? From when? Maha: Yes Kalpana. Me and Kanika have been going for hill climbing training for the last two years. She was very eager to join them for climbing training. She went to her father. Kalpana: Father, I want to join hill climbing training. My friends are also going there. Father: But you only joined the school a few days ago, right? You can join later. Kalpana: Please father, I want to join now itself. Father: Ok. Let’s go and see the training area, and I’ll talk to the trainer. She jumped in happiness and told her friends that she was also going to join the climbing training. After a few days, she joined the training. At the training place... Kanika: I didn’t expect that we were going to attend the training in the same class. Maha: Yes, I also didn’t expect this. This is going to be fun. Kalpana felt more comfortable there. But after some days, her trainer's attitude changed. She told her friends about their trainer’s behavior. Kalpana: Kanika, I am feeling very uncomfortable here because I feel that our trainer's behaviour has changed. Kanika: Why are you feeling this way? Kalpana: A few days ago, I came here alone. I felt the trainer's touch was bad. Maha: I know we also experienced this. Kalpana: Why didn't you tell anyone about this kind of action? Kanika: We tried but couldn’t tell anyone. Maha: Kalpana, Can you go and tell this to your mother? Kalpana: If I tell this to my mother, she will not allow me to attend the training again. Your parents will also be aware of this, and they will not allow you to attend the training. Your two years of training will be wasted. Maha: Then what will be the solution to this problem? Kanika: We can do one thing. We’ll never come alone. Always try to come together. Days passed by. On one Sunday, Kanika hurt her leg while practicing. Her trainer asked her to come with him. Kanika: Maha and Kalpana, please come with me. Three of them followed the trainer. Trainer: Why did you two come here? I didn’t ask you two to come. Kalpana: We wanted to help Kanika.That’s why we accompanied her. Trainer: You two can go. I’ll take care of her. Maha: It’s ok, sir. We’ll wait here and take her home because she is not able to walk because of the wound. After that, they all left together. Like this, they faced many difficulties and managed to get out of every problem. A few days later, the trainer became aware that they were acting differently as a result of his actions. Then he started to ignore them by not giving them proper training and behaving rudely toward them. One day they came to know that there’s going to be an international competition, but the trainer didn’t inform them. They knew he didn't inform them on purpose and didn't even include their names on the list of participants. They asked him, but he didn’t answer them properly and refused to add their names. But they managed to get their names on the list of participants and challenged the trainer that they would definitely participate in and win the match. The international competition day came, and they were ready to participate with full energy and confidence. in their journey. Match begins…. They performed very well and won the match. Their parents and friends were very happy about their achievement. While the judges ask them to speak on stage, they want to talk about how much they struggled to achieve in this match. After that, there is no limit to their success. MORAL: Like those girls, every person should succeed in their dreams, even though they face many struggles in their journey for their victory.
author: Hasini Jayashankar

title: Vindicta
text: ﻿﻿As the monsoon faded away, autumn was slowly creeping into Ketterdam. Melanie opened the windows, wind rushed right into her lungs, cold, sharp and crisp. She wondered whether it was her 15th autumn in Ketterdam or 16th. Melanie was a girl of 22 living in the suburbs of Ketterdam while her parents were in london. Originally an intern in the Bretton Woods law firm, she had a strong desire to work at the museum. Melaine was stranger than the other girls of her age. Very strange. One could find her sitting by the willow by the lake or visiting the abandoned churches. This year, her best friend Bertha Jorkins' body was found by the lake with a pair of Viking coins placed on her eyelids. Melanie couldn't digest the grief of the loss of her dear Bertha. The night before Bertha's death, Melanie had spoke to her. Bertha seemed to be very enthusiastic bout visiting the Coin Exhibition which was scheduled to take place on the 29th of the next month. After putting herself up together, she decided to visit the Exhibition in her loving memory. The coin exhibition held at the Victorian Cross Mueseum was the most classy and sophisticated exhibition she had ever seen. Elegant ladies hailing from lavish families, Handsome men possessing riches beyong her wildest dreams and Wealthy estate owners flooded the museum halls. Alongside the exhibition, the phoenix coin had to be auctioned. Phoenix coin was a royalty in itself. The figure of a blazing phoenix was engraved on the coin along with a strange word ' VINDICTA' on it. The coin was believed to be found in Via Dolorosa or the 'way of Suffering', the path in jerusalem which jesus took while walking to his crucifixion. As Melanie paved her way through the crowd, the sight of a stranger caught her eyes. He was a tall man, probably in his late 20s with deep blue eyes. He wore a lean black suit with an overcoat and possessed a walking cane with a golden raven on it. His face felt like moonlight falling on white jade. With the cane in one hand and a glass of wine in the other, he seemed to be walking towards her. There was something about, something magnetic. Judging fro his attitude, he seemed a ruthless man with cold demanour. His voice was deep but charming and his eyes felt distant. He surely was a cunning man and wore a sarcastic smile, like a thousand secrets were hidden behind it. He was a coin dealer and was accompanied by an acquaintance, Pekka Rollins. While Kaz Brekker walked towards her, Rollins held up his watch chain. A turnip was hanging from the fob where his diamond studded timepiece should have been. 'That little bastard!' whispered Pekka. Seeing this sight, Melanie realised that Kaz had already walked past her. Melanie reached for her purse. It was gone. So was her gold hairpin, the Kaelish Coin pendant she wore for luck and the gold buckles on her boots. Melanie angrily approached him and exclaied, ' You are a pick pocketer!" Kaz calmly replied, his sarcastic smile intact, 'That isn't something pleasing to say on the first meet. I am Kaz Brekker, a business man and a coin dealer. Nothing more, nothing less'. 'You are a thief, Kaz. Greed is your God' ' Isn't that what I just said and let me correct you miss, greed is NOT my god, its my servant and lever, it bows to me' As he turned to walk away, Melanie blocked his way and asked, 'What you possess is mine, but I will let you get away if you answer a few questions of mine.' Kaz nodded coldly. 'You told me you are a coin dealer.' 'Young lady, I am not in the habit of repeating things twice.' 'Well, then tell me about the Viking coins.' The word Viking made Kaz's eyes glow.' I am sorry. That is something not concerning your business.' Melanie smiled slyly and replied, ' True. I believe my business is just calling the cops.' 'What do you need to know about Viking coins?' 'Anything and Everything' replied Melanie. 'Well, the Viking coins are believed to be a token to hell. Viking coins were used by the Mayans in dark Rituals.' Melanie wondered why would someone keep a Viking coin on a murdered persons' eyelids. ' And what does Vindicta mean?' Kaz felt a choke in his throat. It felt strange because it was the first time a stranger had brought up Vindicta. Still, he replied coldly, ' Vindicta is a latin word which means.....' 'Which means what?' asked Melanie 'Revenge' Melanie stood blankly. She felt numb. What did revenge mean to Bertha? Judging from her look, Kaz asked,' Anything wrong?' 'Why would someone keep a coin with revenge engraved on it? I mean on someone's eyelids who died? My friend Bertha Jorkins was murdered, her body was found by the lake, a viking coin was kept on her eyelids. It means Revenge?' The smile on Kaz's face vanished. He felt blood rushing in his cold veins. Flashback seemed to play in front of him. Nevertheless, Kaz answered,' I am sorry but I need to leave before nightfall'. With these words, he walked away towards the museum door. As Melanie stood there, she felt her purse in her hand. She hurriedly opened the purse. The world seemed to crash in front of her as she held something shakingly. It was Bertha's photograph by the lake, her throat split an coins on her eyes. Besides the photograph, the same Viking coins lay in her purse with Vidicta on it and a note which stated, IT WAS FOOLISH OF YOU TO BRING UP THE DEATH OF BERTHA JORKINS. YOU'VE MADE A GRAVE MISTAKE AND NOW THE PRICE NEEDS TO BE PAID' Just then the clock struck 7 bells and a half chime. Someone announced that the coin dealer couldn't make it due to heavy downpour hence the auction will be held at midnight.
author: Adyanshi Tiwary

title: Value of learning
text: In Maindha village, there lived an old man named Lingam. Lingam had three children named Ram, Shaam and Prem. Ram and Sham had found a good job and settled well, though Prem was educated but was not so good in his studies. He lived with his father in their village. Prem is 16 years old, a kind and thoughtful boy. Prem was not too much interested in school education, but he was good in arts and extracurricular activities. One day, his father called Prem and said “You should go to the city and achieve either money or name by some way. I will give you some money only to meet your final expenses”. Prem travelled to Mumbai to fulfil his father’s wishes. He was attracted towards the city life, and he spent half of his money in lavish way. One beautiful morning when sun was shining, Prem was walking in the park. He saw some children learning chess from their teacher Giri. He requested Giri to teach him chess. Giri accepted this and Prem gave rest of his money. He learnt chess and became a grandmaster. As he spent all of money on travel and chess, to earn his livelihood, he started working in the beach. He was selling bottles there and earned enough money to meet his daily needs. One day, he came across an advertisement regarding a chess competition in their city. The winner will get a cash prize of rupees 1,00,000. Prem participated in it and won the chess competition. One evening when sun was red, he was selling bottles in the beach. While selling bottles, he found a boy named Hari crying. He asked Hari the reason for crying. The boy said “My mother is ill, and I can’t treat her, as I am poor. Prem gave all his money which he earned in the competition to him. The boy asked him what to show his gratitude in return to Prem. The boy thought and said, “I know swimming and I will teach him the swimming”. Prem learnt to swim. One evening when birds were returning to their nests, he was doing his business of selling bottles. Then, he saw a rich person named Jay’s child drowning in water. As he had expertise in swimming, without a second thought, he jumped into the sea and saved the life of the child. The rich person was so happy and was ready to give half of his property to Prem. Then Prem said “if you are ready to give half of your property, you should build a school in Maindha village. The school should not only have the formal education, but also it should teach arts and music. As children were forced to study, there were few dropouts from the school, and they were working on the beach along with Me. They are more interested in arts and other cultural activities”. The rich person was very happy and took Prem to his father and said, “Your son is very thoughtful for others”. His father was happy, and the rich person built a school in their village. The key point of this story is that 1. Only formal education is not important, but we should also learn arts and music. It can be useful one or other day and will be of good value. It’s more important in everyone’s life. It may be difficult to practice but not impossible 2. If we determine to learn any new act, we can do it-however difficult it is. 3. Experience is the best teacher for a man to learn new things in life and to make new friends.
author: Vibudhendra Nadgir

title: LEGENDARY STORY OF MONKEY AND HIS LAZY FRIENDS
text: There was a time in animalia, an animal kingdom situated in the far east land of anilionchi which was famous for its island of nikumbhchu. Where there lived the three friends the monkey, the cat, and the fox who happily with one another for years together. Their friendship was a remarkable one as they shared an unbreakable bond together as friends. They used to share both their joys as well as sorrows and together used to resolve their differences among themselves. Throughout the day, the three of them used to enjoy by travelling trips, fairs, and picnics, while having many different kinds of cuisines. So they decided and planned that they too can prepare a mouth-watering bread for the next season of winter. Now, it was time for a very bone-chilling winter to present them with the perpetuity to prepare a mouth-watering bread for their dinner. So, three of them had purchased wheat grains and sowed them in their fertile fields. While the monkey was extremely hardworking, the fox and the cat didn't extend their helping hand to the monkey as they were very lazy and were sitting idly. By the end of the growing season, their crops were not harvested but were rather dried and the land too becam e barr en land as it had lost all its fertility. After a long season of the sweat and toil of the monkey, it was the season of harvesting, the wheat crops were finally ready to make the wheat flour. Soon after, the festival arrived in the kingdom of animalia, the great festival of nikumbha! The festivity of crops! All the animals had started preparation for the crop festival by gathering the seeds. Unfortunately, the fox and the cat had lost all their valuable time by procrastinating. Even there had reminded them to utilise their time for the harvesting of crops. But these two did not pay any attention and went on wasting their valuable time. Finally, the day of festivity had arrived! All the animals had harvested their and prayed to their god, lionchi as he had given them everything to live their life happily. Later, the fox and the cat realise their mistake.so they wanted to apologize to their friend in the form of a helping hand. So, one day, the monkey went to a cliff for some groceries in the shop of gongcha. That shop was the most famous shop for fruits, vegetables, pulses, cereals, and dry fruits. On the way to home, the monkey had a tough time job for climbing down the cliff as the cliff was steep and the groceries was very hefty. This whole scene was keenly observed by the cat and the fox. So they thought of giving a helping hand. So they had climbed to the top of the cliff and had helped their true best friend, the monkey by sharing the weight while returning home down the cliff. Later in the evening, the monkey tightly hugs its friends and says " my dear friends, you have helped me in adversities and in tough times. You both are my truly dearest friends and i promise that we shall stay for each other throughout our life won't break our friendship bond". Finally, the monkey and her friends rejoice in their life happily and everlastingly.so the monkey, the cat, and the fox realise that being in a group, not even the strongest of strong can break them. So this was the story that was narrated throughout the centuries in the land of animalia. There is a temple of suosanga situated in the middle of the island, in which there are statues of the monkey, the cat, and the fox are built. These statues are often addressed as the statues of fortune as they bless the citizens of animalia in the times of natural disasters and their citizens problems. Thus, the moral of the story is '' hard work is the key to success"," as you sow, so shall you reap, '' and "true friends are those who help you when you are in adversities".

title: Maya's monstrous night
text: There was once a little girl named Maya. She was a good girl who always did her homework and kept her room clean. She studied in 6th grade at Anne high school. She played sports at school and received lots of praise from school as well as family. Her parents loved her and were happy to see her progress in school and sports. One day, Maya came home happy as her exam results was out and she had topped the class. She rang the doorbell once and waited, but nobody answered. She rang the doorbell for the second time and waited but nobody answered. She got scared as her parents were always at home. Then she remembered that they had gone to the hospital to visit her unwell grandmother. She was worried about her grandmother as she was very close to her and was always there when her parents were busy. She looked for the keys and found them under the doormat. She opened the door and pushed it open with a feeling of dread. She was Nyctophobic which means she was afraid of the dark. As she went in, she saw that the usually brightly lit living room was pitch dark. There was a dim light coming from the kitchen that created a shadow on the wall. She let out a shrill ear-splitting scream. The shadow seemed to have sharp claws, long fangs, pointy ears and a big humanoid body. She was sure it was a werewolf! She ran to her room scared out of her wits and slammed the door shut. She told herself that she was seeing things. But her mind knew that she had seen the shadow. She tried to divert her mind in every possible way. She listened to music, but all she could hear was the growling of the werewolf coming closer to her room and scratching on her door. She knew she was imagining things but could not stop her fear. She tried reading a book but all she could think of was the werewolf. She even tried to sleep but all she dreamt was nightmares on werewolves. She decided to call her parent, but they did not answer her call. She tried to calm herself, but the werewolf- it had taken over her mind. A couple of hours had passed since she had come from school. She had found a note from her mom that said that they would be back home only late at night. Her fear had now compounded and had consumed her. She tried to sleep again, but couldn’t. After spending a sleepless night the next morning She was relieved the see her parents were back home. She was very upset with them for having left her alone at home when they knew about her fear of darkness. When she confronted them and told them about the werewolf, they calmed her down and explained to her that as per the psychologist exposing yourself to the fear it will help you overcome it so they had purposely left the house pitch dark, and it was just a cardboard cut-out of a werewolf.
author: Aditi Aivalli
illustrator: Nissy Saji; Partho Sengupta; Wiehan de Jager

title: Croaky's Adventure To a Big City.
text: Croaky's Adventure To a Big City. "Once upon a time, there lived a frog named, Tira. She had a baby named Croaky, she was new born". One day her mom Tira and dad Tom advised Croaky not to go anywhere. The next day Croaky asked her mother that she wished to visit the big city. But her mom warned Croaky that "You are too young to go to the big city. So you wait till you grow up." The next day Croak Croak.... Croaky woke up and while her mother and father were sleeping, she went out. She saw a big forest.This was the first time Croaky came out, she was little scared. Instead of going back to her home, she started to walk inside the forest. Croaky saw some ants marching away, some birds, some insects and so on... After walking for sometime, Croaky saw the king of the forest who was big, strong and bold and can you guess who it is? "The Lion". The big lion told, " Iam going to eat you roar rrrr "...... The lion gave a big roar. Croaky ran away with fear and it suddenly fell into a puddle. Croaky was covered in mud and the lion couldn't see her anywhere. The lion went back saying, "I am never going to find a prey. Ooh! Iam starving roarrr r r r r r r..... Croaky said, "phew", and started to walk but she was covered in mud. Do you think Croaky will survive in this big forest? Croaky was scared and she thought to go back but she didn't know the way.. After walking for sometime, Croaky saw a big snake. She was really scared seeing its big fangs, tongue and so on... This time as Croaky was in green colour she camouflaged and jumped into the greeny bushes to conceal her identity. Meanwhile, Tira and Tom were searching for her everywhere. But Croaky has reached the city. There were so many buildings and so many people. Croaky looked so confused. Croaky would have been stamped by people but luckily she escaped. Croaky went into a hotel. Looking at her, the girls working in the hotel screamed. "Oh! Look at this green ugly froggy". Hearing this Croaky got shocked and thought "Do I look ugly? But my mom always says, that I look pretty and beautiful ". Now with great sigh, Croaky badly wanted to go back to her home. A sweeper at the stairs, had a big broom in his hand. Seeing the big broom, Croaky's eyes popped. With the big broom the sweeper pushed Croaky down the stairs. As the hotel floor tiles were very slippery. Croaky fell into the sink and went down the drain - down - down and down. Somehow it managed to find the way out. There she met a bird. The bird carried away Croaky and put it on the middle of the road. The wild animals who were Croaky's enemies came on the left side. Seeing that Croaky got scared. At that time, she heard some croaks sound on the right side. Her mother, father and all her froggy family members crowded there. She leaped fast and joined them. Croaky hugged her parents firmly and said " I will never be disobedient again". Croaky apologised to her parents and lived happily ever after. Moral: DisObedience Lands One In Trouble!

title: Quiet
text: In a small town lived a cute little boy Aadi having fair skin with pink cheeks and brown hair. He was a quite boy who never spoke, he had no friends to talk or play with. In school also he sat alone and didn't talked to anyone also didn't answered any questions. The class was same with him and without him as he didn't played any role. Anybody didn't know about him how he is or how is his personality. In his home also he always stays in his room and didn't come out,he even didn't talked to his sibling. His parents were worried about him that what he did alone in the room. It felt like he didn't existed in the world. One day in his school he met a teacher who wanted to know about him. She wanted to know about him,about his talent. So she called her parents and asked them to tell about him. His parents told that in home also he is alone in his room.Now the teacher asked them to know what he does alone in the room. His parents were shocked to know that he read books alone in his room. But still she didn't knew about his real talent. His teacher took his class to the ground and made them play many games.He wasn't good at any sports or any co curricular activity like art,music or sports. one day his school organized a story writing competition in which he got 1st position. All of his classmates were jealous of him. In half early exams he topped and everyone teased him topper, topper and said you are a nerd. In the story writing competition judges liked the story very much and wanted him to come up with the story.His school arranged extra classes for him for writing a story. He was selected from his school for inter school story writing competition. Many students were jealous of him and wanted to beat him,they tried many ways to beat him but were unsuccessful. He got fist position in the inter-school competition and was selected for state level competition for which he has to practice a lot. His teacher took him to a big city Hyderabad where he can get proper education for writing a story. There he joined anew school where he made many friends and spoke to them. Now he wasn't a quite boy.HE prepared very hard for the competition and got 12th rank he wasn't happy about it so, he participated again in the competition. At the day of the competition his hands were shivering before writing a story. HE took 1hr to write the story and at the result day this time his story got selected for national level. NOW he need to practice a lot for getting selected. HE practiced day and night for getting selected.He joined many classes for getting perfect in writing a story. The day came when the competition was held. He was very confident this time anHd completed his his story in just half hour. This time his story didn't got selected. This was all because of overconfidence.He cried a lot and again participated in the competition this time he got selected between thousands of students and became one of the best writer of India. He was the youngest writer of India and answered his haters back. He got awarded for writing the best story amongst many students. His parents were very happy about him that from a quiet boy he became one of the best writer. THIS WAS THE POWER OF SILENCE.

title: The King and His Complaints
text: The King and His Complaints Story by: Ms.V.A. Sarada, Class 7C, Shiva Niketan School, Tirupur, Tamil Nadu Once upon a time there lived a King named Raja Vishnu Vardhan. He used to keep complaining about his role as a King. He was tired - of attending the Royal Court, to meet his subjects on a daily basis, to practice at the artillery, etc. He was even tired of going for a daily horse ride. His mother, Rajamatha Annapoorni Devi explained the duties of a King, time and again. But, all was in vain. Rajamatha Annapoorni Devi went to a saint named Swami Sadananda. Swami Sadananda requested the Rajamatha Annapoorni Devi to advise the Raja Vishnu Vardhan to meet a weaver name Ajapalan, in disguise and observe his daily activities. Raja Vishnu Vardhan, as requested by his mother went to meet Ajapalan in disguise. Ajapalan was a person of simplicity. When Raja Vishnu Vardhan came Ajapalan gave a warm welcome, offered him a cup of hot gruel and asked him the purpose of his visit. Raja Vishnu Vardhan said that he was a traveller and wanted to stay at Ajapalan’s residence that night. Ajapalan agreed, and started his work for the day. Ajapalan started his job of weaving in the loom. Raja Vishnu Vardhan noticed a rope tied in between Ajapalan and the loom. Raja Vishnu Vardhan inquired about the purpose of the rope. Ajapalan replied that it is to rock the cradle of his little baby boy. Near the loom, there was a long stick with a piece of black cloth tied at its end. Ajapalan said the stick was to scare the crows that feeds on the grain that is dried a little outside. Ajapalan was wearing a belt of bells and then kept weaving the clothes in the loom. Ajapalan said that there are many rats around the house, and the sound of these bells kept the rats away. Raja Vishnu Vardhan noticed a few children standing outside the house. Ajapalan said that he used to teach them a few lessons in Tamil grammar, which he has learnt. The children standing there keep listening to lesson, and also keep stamping the clay with their feet.Weaver Ajapalan has a hobby of making clay toys and then sell them in the market. Raja Vishnu Vardhan asked how he manages to do all these jobs without complaints. Ajapalan said that he does all these works out of passion and disposes the earnings into four parts – One Fourth for his dues, One Fourth for his duty, One Fourth for his saving and One Fourth for himself. Raja Vishnu Vardhan asked him to explain. Ajapalan said he spends – First One fourth to his parents to whom have made him what he is today – to whom is indebted for life – the dues Second One Fourth to his wife to whom he has duty for taking care of her and her wellbeing – the duty Third One Fourth for his son who will take care of him when he becomes old – the saving Last One Fourth for charity – good deeds protect him in life and death – for himself Raja Vishnu Vardhan understood the importance of earning and prudential spending. He stopped complaining. Not only stopped complaining, but also became an expert administrator, especially tax and revenue, for the country. He also made Ajapalan, one of his ministers. All his subjects were happy about their king. THE END
author: Sarada V

title: WAR AND PEACE
text: OPENING SCENE OF RUSSIS AND UKRAINE WAR:- Ukraine has long played an important, yet sometimes overlooked, role in the global security order. Today, the country is on the front lines of a renewed great-power rivalry that many analysts say will dominate international relations in the decades ahead. PRESENT:- Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 marked a dramatic escalation of the countries’ eight-year-old conflict and a historic turning point for European security. After six months, many defense and foreign policy analysts cast the war as a major strategic blunder by Russian President Vladimir Putin, and one that has put his long-time rule in jeopardy. Many observers see little prospect for a diplomatic resolution in the months ahead and instead acknowledge the potential for a dangerous escalation, which could include Russia’s use of a nuclear weapon. The war has hastened Ukraine’s push to join Western political blocs, including the European Union (EU) and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). ﻿ Conclusion of Russia and Ukraine war 2022:- W hatever be the cause of War but the result is always the same thousands of words are known to push Nations back years such Nations have to struggle for new development that leaders of world need to access them if they keep this source of in mind and raised above personal self-interest then it is possible that the horrors of War can be avoided.

title: Come Back Soon, Mira
text: Today is Mira’s last day at home. She will soon be leaving for boarding school. Arav follows her around until she makes him curl up in her empty suitcase. “Stop playing around!” Papa says, lifting Arav out. “There’s so much packing to be done!” Arav wants to go away with Mira, although he secretly wishes she wasn’t so bossy. Like now. She is at the table doing Arav’s homework. “I can do it, didi!” Arav says. “You are too silly,” says Mira, batting his hands away. “I just spoke to your tuition teacher. She says you poured the juice she gave you into a potted plant!” calls out Papa from the other room. “It was green and tasted muddy…” Mira tries explaining. Arav slips under the table to laugh. “Another one of your pranks,” Papa sighs, as he gathers the toys strewn around. “I hope you’ll behave better at the new school.” At this, Mira feels sad. Later Arav wonders, “What shall I make for didi as a goodbye gift to make her happy?” Mira loves playing in the park every evening. So Arav draws a picture of a girl sitting on a swing, and colours it neatly. A cold splash on his shoulder makes him jerk upright. “Oops!” Mira giggles. Arav takes a glass of sharbat from her before she spills any more. “Is that me?” Mira asks, looking at his drawing. Arav nods. She sits close to him. “Too neat. I’m not neat,” she says. “And I’m always in trouble, am I not?” In the evening, Arav and Mira meet their friends Rehan and Hardeep and walk to the park. Mona and Leon join them. Punyam, Sonu and Ayisha also run up. And so do Piggu and Brownie, the naughty dogs of the park, and then the cats from the sports club next door. They are a happy mix of hair, fur, legs and tails. Mira gets everyone together to play hide-and-seek. Whenever any two quarrel, Mira tosses a coin to decide who should back off. Arav slips into a puddle and Mira dries him off with leaves. When he gets tired of being the ‘den’ at catch-catch, Mira lets him grab her sleeve and she becomes the den instead. “Come back soon, Mira!” all her friends say when it is time for them to go home. Mira walks home slowly, looking at the shops and the people around. It will be a while before she comes this way again. It’s late evening, almost time to go to the station. Papa helps Mira pack the last of her things. Arav brings her his gift. “Look at it when you get to school,” he says. “But I can’t wait!” Mira unrolls the drawing. The drawing shows Mira on the swing, surrounded by all their friends. Arav is there too, peeping between them with his usual grin. “That looks like a frog, but it’s Leon!” Arav says, pointing at the drawing. “And Piggu looks like a cow here! Mooggu!” Mira giggles. “Let’s stick this drawing on the wall right here so I won’t really be gone,” Mira says. “Come back soon, didi,” Arav says. His heart feels as though it might burst. “I will miss you,” says Papa. "I will come back soon for the holidays," Mira says softly. ﻿ Arav and Papa hug Mira like they would never let her go.
author: Chatura Rao

title: The dog lover called Grace
text: "You mean it? A real puppy" said Grace smiling broadly.She had been asking a puppy for ages but now on her 12th birthday her wish has been fulfilled."No please! No" begged Nixie, Grace's big sister. " come on Nix please " begged Grace. "Yes Nixie this is her birthday you can't decide what she wants " retorted her mom. The next day Grace was in her room looking through her 'woof' magazine which was all about dogs, the cover had a gorgeous Golden retriever. Grace thought to herself " hmm should I take a Golden retriever or a Jack Russell, she wondered. Mom shouted "Grace, dinner's ready". "Coming mom " she replied in a rather exhausted manner. She went down stairs where Dad,Mum and Nixie were munching their food. Mum and Dad had a slight grin on their faces. Grace sat down with a suspicious face, then finally she said "come on, why are you smiling, spill the beans". "Nothing, we just wanted to ask you what breed of dog you wanted"? Dad questioned. " hmm don't know maybe a Golden Retriever or a Jack Russell" said Grace." Woah those are some big dog breeds there, maybe you could adopt a poor street dog that would help those poor animals" replied Dad sadly. " Gross, no way" retorted Grace. " hmm" Dad replied scornfully. Then he switched on the T.V and showed a video, it was all about street dogs without food, it was rather emotional. By the end of the video Grace could feel tears stinging her eyes. " Woah never thought a video would change my decision, I'm sorry Dad, I really should think before speaking " replied Grace wiping her tears. " I'm glad you understood my point, there are many people to adopt a gorgeous breed but a street dog will be adopted rarely, I'm sorry if you had any high hopes, but you'll thank me later" Dad replied poetically. The next day, they were travelling to their native when they saw a poor puppy sitting, Grace immediately told Dad to stop the car and adopt the dog. Dad smiled and put the puppy into a box and turned to return home. So you see there are enough people to adopt a fancy dog but those street dogs have no one. Please show some kindness to those poor creatures. THE END.......

text: It was speaking skills that day, where everyone have to tell about their dreams and something inspirational about it. title: Sneha and Neha
text: Sneha and Neha were 2 best friends. They both had most things in common. They both liked BlackPink songs, BTS, Cadbury, Drawing, and Painting. One time they even had the same writing. They both were like sisters and they always wanted to be together and they never thought that there will be days in which they fight. They never thought that the days will exist. One time, while they were playing, Neha went to the kitchen to get something to eat. Suddenly, she heard some laughing from her brother, " Ramu " 's room. She went to get a closer look. She saw Neha and Ramu playing. She went to her room and when looking a the condition she was so angry that her head turned red. Then, Neha quickly remembered that she had to blackmail Sneha to her become her friend and so it is not a true friendship. She was very sorry. Then she called Sneha to her room, ' SNEHA! title: Raju's First Flight
text: Paris is definitely a difficult place to fly a plane", he thought, while his heart beat rapidly. All of a sudden, he heard a noise coming from the cabin. *BEEP BEEP BEEP* What was that? Maybe he was in enemy territory? Maybe the motor had a problem? *BEEP BEEP BEEP* Raju woke up suddenly when his alarm rang. "It was all a dream", he sighed. But, wait. There's no time to be upset! It was a big day. "I'm going on my first trip on a plane! Mom, I'm awake!" His mother was closing the luggage. "Good morning, Raju!", she said. "I'm so excited to see your sister. It's been many months since we've last seen Arya. Get ready quickly." Raju was in the airport for the first time in his life. He helped his mom lift up the luggage over the luggage conveyor. The conveyor transferred the luggage over to a big machine. A lady dressed in a uniform was watching a small screen behind the machine. Raju was surprised when he saw the screen. It showed, not only his luggage but everything that was inside of it- his new sports shoes, his binoculars, everything! "X-ray vision! Just like Captain Raju!," said Raju. Raju opened his mouth to ask the woman something, but his mother held him back. "Raju, the lady works on the security team. She has to make sure the passengers don't carry any dangerous items like explosives or guns. It's better to not bother her." Finally, Raju found himself an ample room. The walls were made of glass and he could see dozens of planes outside. One of them was getting ready to take off. "The pilots have an important job, don't they? Right, mom?" "Of course. Just like bus drivers, they are responsible for the security of a lot of passengers." "Chechi is really lucky. She's been on a lot planes! I can't wait to get older". His mom laughed. "Oh yes, without a doubt Arya has been on a lot of planes. But you're only nine years old. You have a lot of time, Raju". Raju looked at the people making a line in Terminal 8. "That's our terminal, mom. It's time to board the plane!" Ten minutes later, they were in their seats, with their seat belts on. Raju looked out the window when the plane started to move. In the beginning slowly, but in a couple seconds, it was moving so quickly that Raju felt his seat vibrate. Suddenly, the vibration stopped. The giant plane was in the air! "Mom, we're flying!". "That's right! Listen, Raju. They're giving an announcement. Shhh!" A voice was heard over the speakers. A familiar voice... "Ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain Arya speaking. Welcome aboard!" "Chechi!" "That's my daughter!"
author: suzanne vazquez

title: Finche's Ridiculous Adventure: Where are you, Ms. Giant?
text: He is a little birdy bird with unique ribbon around his neck. Finche lives in a lovely massive house with Ms. Giant. Finche loves her so much. She has such a big heart. She likes to give Finche lots of toy. Finche loves to play with Ms. Giant, so he would be sad whenever Ms. Giant is away from home. Feeling lonely, Finche fly-off to an adventure finding Ms. Giant. Finche soar high in the sky, so high that he can see the Earth completely. He has to find Ms. Giant Where are you, Ms. Giant? Suddenly a twinkling glimmering light appears in his sight. He dashes off. Only to discover the light was coming from the jewelries inside a deep forest. But to no avail, Ms. Giant is still nowhere to be seen. Finche did not stop his journey until he sees a wide field of white and soft snow. Getting distracted, he is happily rolling around on that cold field. Recatching his senses, he continued to his adventure finding Ms. Giant This time, Finche soars even higher to the sky. He is flying between the stars and galaxies. He can also see the moon and comets. But still, where is Ms. Giant? From the high, his sharp gaze caught something. What could that be? Finche dived down, down, and down that his white ribbon spinning around Just like what he guessed, Finche lands perfectly on Ms. Giant's arms. He is thrilled to meet her again. "I really love you Ms. Giant" He chirps. Ms. Giant hug him tightly, "I love you too," she replies back.
author: Herlyna Nuraini

title: How old is Muttajji?
text: It was Muttajji's birthday and they had a train to catch! ﻿ Muttajji, the mother of the mother of the mother of the twins, lived with Mysore with Ajji, who was the mother of the mother of the twins. Nobody knew when Muttajji's birthday was; but Ajji always used to celebrate it during the vacations of Makara Sankranthi. "Amma, will there be cake?" -Putti asked. "A big cake that's fluffy with pink frosting and a rose on top?" "Noo" -said Putta. "Older people don't have birthday cakes, and 200 candles don't fit on a single cake." "Muttajji isn't 2oo years old, dummy", said Putti. "How old is Muttajji, Amma?" Amma smiled. "Why don't you ask her when we get there?" The moment that they arrived at the old green house of Mysore, the twins exploded into Muttajji's room. "Happy birthday, Muttajji, how old are you today?" Muttajji hugged both of the twins. "How old am I? Who knows, why, does it matter? "Yes!", yelled Putta and Putti together. Muttajji smiled, "Well, I know around five years before I was born, our Maharaja went to a big party for India Maharajas and Maharanis in Delhi. A British king and queen went to visit, and our Maharaja got a gold medal". "Oooh! A party! There should've been lots of cake!' said Putti. "Who was this king, Muttajji? If you know, maybe we can guess in what year he visited, if we add five years to that, we'll know when you were born". Muttajji crossed her elbows. "I've forgotten, Putta." Putta's face fell. "Wait", said Muttajji. "When I was nine or ten years old, my uncle from Bombay visited us and talked to us about the clean trains". Clean trains? "Yes!", Muttajji was very excited. "They were starting to run in Bombay the other year, you never had to travel while being dirty in them, there wasn't any black powder in your clothes or on your face, no dirty, no nothing". The twins looked at her. Why would someone get dirty traveling on a train? "Some years later", Muttajji continued, "I got married, the law was that a girl should be at least 15 years old before getting married, and my dad never enforced that law, so I should have been 16 years old. My marriage, your Muttajji got a job in Bombay, and we left Mysore". "Did something important happen in the year that you got married, Muttajji?", asked Putta. "Yes", said Muttajji, sadly. "Our Maharaja inaugurated our huge dam, and the beautiful gardens next to him, during the festival of Dasara that year, but I missed it, I was in Bombay". "A big dam?" Putta sat down. "It's still there?". Muttajji yelled with laughter. "Of course! It was also the solid rock, it was the dam that the dominated the Kaveri, there were no more floods in the monsoon and enough water for the camps in the summer". Ajji stuck his head around the corner of the door. "Are you talking about KRS, Amma?" "KRS", said Muttajji, looking affectionately at Ajji. "Your Ajji was my fifth son, the youngest, but always the most intelligent. Did you know, kids, that my kids came like a clock, one every two monsoons. The day that your Ajji decided to leave, your Muttajji couldn't find him. They told us that he had decided to go see Gandhiji give a speech in the Gowalia Tank Maidan, I was so excited. He was yelling the whole day, foolish man, bothering the baby. "Leave India!" Putti's eyes filled with emotion. "We studied that in history, Putta! The movement started in 1942. That means 1942 was the year that...". "....Ajji was born", said Putta. "Not Muttajji". "That's a start!" said Putti. "In what year were you born, Ajji?" "I'd be 74 this year", said Ajji. "So I was born in..?" Putti quickly did his calculations. "1942!", he said. Ajji nodded his head. "Now, Ajji is Muttajji's fifth son and all her sons were separated by two years!", said Putta. "So that means if Ajji was born in 1942...". "...Muttajji's fourth son was born in 1942-2=1940, the third in 1940-2=1938, the second in 1938-2=1936, and the first in 1936-2=1934." "So that means Muttajji got married in 1932!" Putti exclaimed. "Not necessarily", said Putta. "Muttajji didn't say that her first son was born two years after her marriage, only that a dam was constructed in Mysore that year that she got married". "Maybe this will help, kids", said Ajji, carrying bowls of vermicelli payasa, Muttajji's favorite dish. "KRS is the dam of Krishnarajasagar, the gardens of Brindavan are the gardens next to it, we went there last year to see the musical fountains, remember?" The twins agreed. "Mmmm", said Putti. "Your payasa is the best, Ajji!" "When was KRS constructed, do you know Ajji?" Ajji shook his head. "I'm not sure, but you can go with Ajja to the central library after lunch and find out". ﻿ In the library, Putti found a book about the history of Mysore. "Here it is!", she whispered. "Two of the most visited locations in Mysore by tourists, the KRS dam and the Brindavan gardens, were opened to the public in 1932". The twins smiled - that means Muttajji was married in 1932, 84 years before! In the library, Putti found a book about the history of Mysore. "Here it is!", she whispered. "Two of the most visited locations in Mysore by tourists, the KRS dam and the Brindavan gardens, were opened to the public in 1932". The twins smiled - that means Muttajji was married in 1932, 84 years before! "Muttajji thought she was 16 years old when she got married", said Putti, "But she could've been 15 or 17 or 18". "She also said that she was 9 or 10 years old when her uncle from Bombay told her about the clean train", said Putti. "Ajja could know what that means". Ajja was sitting the lecture room. "Ajja", Putti whispered, "in the olden times, did people get dirty when traveling on the trains". Ajji nodded. "There were vapor motors, that functioned with carbon, not electricity." he said. "The black carbon powder used to fly outside the chimney and land on everything". "That's right, Putti!", Putta hissed. "The electric trains were the 'clean' trains". He took out a book about the Indian railways. "It says here", he points out, "that the first electric train from India arrived in Bombay in 1925!" "And Muttajji says that she was 9 years old", said Putta. "If she's right, Muttajji was born in 1916". "But she could be wrong, you know", Putti frowned. "There's only one way to find out", said Putta. "We have to figure out if that big party for kings and queens in Delhi, that Muttajji said happened five years before her marriage, occurred in 1911". They began to run towards Ajja. "Ajja, was there a big party for a foreign king who visited India around 1911?" Ajja frowned. "Why is that date so familiar?" "yes, it was the year that the Door of India was constructed in BOmbay and yes, it was constructed in order to welcome the British emperor of India, George V. There should've been many big parties, not one". Ajja touched his forehead, impressed with himself. "Not bad for an old brain, huh?" "Not bad at all!", the twins yelled. "Thanks, Ajja!" They knew exactly how old Muttajji was! Five minutes later, the twins were running home. "Muttajji", they gasped, running directly into the room, "The Mysore Maharaja got his gold medal from George V?" "Aaaaaaaan", said Muttajji with joy. "That's it, George, how intelligent you boys are!" "That means to say, Muttajji, that you were born in 1916. You are exactly 100 years old today!" "That's big detective work, kids!", Amma smiled. "I think you - and Muttajji- deserve a special treat, big, fluffy, with pink frosting and a rose on top". "Hurrayyyyyy", the twins clapped. The Big Maharaja-Maharani Party (and other fun things about the history of India) Remember all the important historical events that Muttajji talked about in the story? All of that really happened! Here's a bit more information about those events. The Big Party: Maharaja-Maharani (1911) - When the British emperor George V and his wife Queen Mary visited India for the first time, they organized a big party for more than 400 kings and queens of India. It was called Delhi Durbar. In order to feed 200,000 people, the bakeries brought out 20000 pieces of bread a day and more than 1000 cattle and sheep were sacrificed for every meal. A lot of Indian rulers received gold medals from the emperor, including the Maharaja of Mysore, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV. The Clean Trains (1925)- On February 3rd, 1925, the first electric train from India left Victoria Terminus of Bombay for the Kurla station. With that, India converted into an Asian third world and the 24th in the world to introduce the electric railway. The Dam that Domesticated Kaveri (1932) - The Kaveri river traverses the south of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The river was always a blessing, it used to flood the monsoons and dry up during the summer. All of that changed when a dam was constructed through the river and it created the reservoir Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS). The deposit still provides the majority of drinking water to the city of Bangalore. Ghandhiji's Big Speech (1942) - The "Quit India speech" was a speech done by Ghandhiji on August 8th, 1942, in the Maidan of Gowalia tank in Bombay. Ghandiji asked the people to fight against the British government without using violence, without disobeying the laws. Five years later, August 15th, 1947, the nonviolent war obtained results that Ghandiji desired: The British left and India became independent. Today, the Gowalia Maidan Tank is called August Kranti Maidan in memory of the peaceful revolution.
author: suzanne vazquez

title: Megha makes Pooris
text: Megha asked her mother, “Mom, what are you making for breakfast today?” Her mom told, “I’m going to make fluffy pooris.” Megha said, “Pooris, Oh Yummy!” Megha tagged along with her mother to watch her making pooris. Megha asked, “Mom, can you please teach me how to make pooris?” Her mom said, “OK. I’m planning to make 8 pooris today. So, I will take 3 big spoons of wheat flour first.” Her mom continued, “Now, I’m going to mix the flour with a little salt and water to make a thick dough ball. Sprinkle water little by little to make the ball. Don’t pour all the water into the bowl in one go. Now, I will knead the dough ball well to make it soft.” “Megha, now you make eight small dough balls from the big ball,” said her mom. Megha made 8 small dough balls. Her mom said, “I will use the chapati board to make the small flat circular dough for the pooris.” Megha asked, “What are you going to do next?” Her mom said, “I’m going to pour oil into a frying pan and heat it. Then, I will put the flat circular dough one at a time and fry them.” Her mom said, “After you fry it on one side, you should flip the poori so that the other side touches the oil.” Megha said, “Wow. Look how they expand when fried in oil. Like how a balloon expands when we blow air into it. " Megha asked, “What side dish did you make for pooris?” Her mom said, “I soaked chickpeas or chana yesterday night. Morning, I cooked it with spices and made a curry.” Megha smelled the pooris and ate them with chana side dish. Activity 1: Arrange the steps to make poori in the right order. a. Fry the pooris. b. Use chapati maker to make small circular flat dough. c. Make small dough balls from the big dough ball. d. Knead flour with water and salt. e. Serve poori with side dish. title: A Strange Voice
text: Once, there were two siblings, Jeff and Paulina. They both studied in class V. One day, after the science class, Jeff heard a strange voice. He decided to follow it during the break with his sister, Paulina. They followed it and reached the entrance gate of the School.No Kids were allowed to leave school Premises.Hence the School guard was standing there. Then, Jeff whispered to Paulina that " the guards will stop us, but we have to find another way to follow the voice. The Guard will stop us.. After dispersal, they heard it again which attracted them to follow it. Finally after two days, they got a chance to unveil this mystery. The school announced the winter vacation. The voice could be heard even at their home. Both were now very curious to know more about it. They set off with their supplies and began the adventure to find out the mystery. Suddenly, a tragedy struck them. They had to pass two obstacles: a jungle and a canyon with a fast-flowing river. They managed to get through the jungle. However, the canyon was dangerous as well as difficult to pass through. From a distance, it was visible that a precious gem was emitting the sound and scattering light all around. But, the canyon was actually two miles away. However, the canyon was dangerous as well as difficult to pass through. From a distance, it was visible that a precious gem was emitting the sound and scattering light all around. But, the canyon was actually two miles away. A wonderful idea strikes suddenly in Jeff’s head. Jeff said, "We can use the river!" Paulina surprisingly asked, "How?" "By creating a raft from the sticks and six little bits of vine that I found on the ground," answered Jeff. They made a raft and reached the other side. They got the gem. It was a great achievement. The gem had inscriptions in an old Egyptian language that chanted mantras. The kids learned to decode the enchanted mantras, which led them to a puzzle. The voice from the gem came to a halt after solving the amazing puzzle. They succeeded in completing their curious adventure. They never gave up, even in a difficult situation.
