title: Madhav and Madhavi : Tower Of Secrets
text: Gujrat was a mysterious state with a lot of mysteries. Including the TOWER OF SECRETS. Everybody knew about the tower of secrets but, nobody had actually been there.Some wanted to but couldn't find the map that leads to it. People used to stay in order and discipline but then Dhanee sir arrived at the start of 2023. He kept telling everyone about how his family used to be poor and from a miracle they are now rich. It made people feel envy so, they started fighting amongst themselves trying to get to the tower of secrets Everyone was scared of changing their ways. So they didn't even talk about it. Only one pair of siblings Madhav and Madhavi were ready to change them. Madhav and Madhavi were thick as thieves and always stuck with each other. They were also detectives. They were famous for solving mysteries around their village. Both of them had just finished exams and were relaxing since their holidays started. 'It's so calm and relaxing.', said Madhav. 'It is but, don't you feel bored without any mystery to solve? I mean we solve something mysterious at this time.', replied Madhavi. Madhav said, 'I know but, mysteries don't grow on trees nor they are present in plain sight. We have to look for them carefully and...' 'MADHAV! MADHAVI! SHOULDN'T YOU GO GET MILK FOR SHEETAL AUNTY?',shouted their mother from the house. "Oh ha!", exclaimed Madhavi 'Chalo Madhav! Let's go pick up milk.' 'Coming!', said Madhav, lost in thought Without realizing he wandered to Dhanee uncles property. When he realized that he tried to make an escape but, unfortunately, Dhanee's dog Katana was there. So, he was chased out. "Aah! Madhavi help me!" After running around and yelling, Madhavi finally returned, annoyed and irritated. 'Help me!',cried Madhav. "Fine! Katu I have biscuits...", coaxed Madhavi. "Woof! Woof", barked Katna happily, kneeling down. "There you go", said Madhavi. "Come let's go home, then you'll tell me what you were doing in Dhanee's property." "Ok. But, you will tell me how you coaxed Katana" 'Hello dears, how was your day? Oh and did you bring the milk?', asked Shanvi [their mother]. ' I brought the milk amma. Madhav went into Katna's yard. 'Madhav! Why did you do that? Did Katana chase you?' 'H aan Ma Katana ne mera peechha kiya. Madhavi saved me. Speaking of that how did you know what to do?' 'Mom used to work for Dhanee as his and Katana's therapist. Only she knows all of Dhanee's secrets.', retorted Madhavi 'Really amma?', asked Madhav curious. 'Yes, and I have been blackmailed and bribed many times to spill it but I haven't', said Shanvi. 'My question is why people want to waste their time trying to find out Dhanee's secrets when they could spend their time working hard?', wondered Madhavi. 'Well Maddie, (Madhavi's nickname) Dhanee's family weren't very smart and because of that they used to live their life below the poverty line' 'But, then how did he get so rich?', asked Maddie. 'That's the thing. No one knows how. Some say he had access to the tower of secrets and earned money by learning the secrets and blackmailing people, threatening them that he will spill the beans if he doesn't get his ransom.' Boom! An explosion had occurred. 'Ma! Look the tower of secrets has exploded.' 'What are you saying?', started Shanvi but before she could come up to the window she was held by a phone call. 'Right, I'll be there.', said Shanvi. 'Maa. Where are you going?' 'Dhanee's house. He wants an urgent meeting.' 'Bye ma! Stay safe', cautioned the siblings. 'Well what do we do now?',asked Madhav. 'I want to interrogate you.', said Maddie. 'Why?'. 'Because I think you saw something before the fire had started.' 'Ok, fire on' This is how the interrogation was: Maddie: Why did you wander away to Dhanee's yard? Madhav: I saw something there. Maddie:What did you see? Madhav: Why should I tell you? Maddie: Because, we are on the same team. Madhav: Oh yeah. Sorry, whenever you interrogate me I forget that. Maddie: That's okay. Just spill the beans. Madhav: When I went to Dhanee's yard I saw his men training in his second yard which is not so far away from his first yard. I tried to hear what was going on but Katana came and chased me.--------------------- 'Hmm. I have a feeling-' riiiiing, rang the telephone. 'I got it!', said Madhav. 'Put it on speaker please', requested Maddie. 'I HAVE YOUR MOTHER IN HOSTAGE. NOW TELL ME ALL YOUR SECRETS IF YOU WANT HER TO LIVE. YOU HAVE TWO WEEKS.AND DON'T CALLTHE POLICE', came a voice from the telephone. 'Noooo!', screamed Madhav who was a mama's boy.'Madhav calm down', coaxed Maddie. 'Ho can I calm down when we don't even know where mom is?', said Madhav. 'We do, well given in your situation, I do.' 'Where. Who?' 'Globe warm palace. Yes I know it's where Dhanee lives. It's because ma was there last and I heard Katana barking.' 'Ok. Then we have to save ma.' 'Good. Now we know that you saw Dhanee speaking with his soldiers but we have to find out what. Is there any other way to get to the yard without crossing Katana?' 'I did see his fanners we could dress up as them' 'Ok, but what about the actual fanners?' 'We can send a letter from Dhanee giving them a holiday tomorrow.' 'Good idea. We can borrow clothes from Raja.' 'Good idea. Since he used to be a fanner he must have clothes for you and his sister Divya must have clothes for me. 'Let's go!' 'But what about the house?' 'We'll lock it up and I'll put the key in my pocket.' 'Ok. come one!' 'Hi Raja! Hi Divya!',chimed the siblings.'Hi Madhav and Madhavi!',said Raja and Divya 'What do you need today?' 'We need some fanner costumes.', said Maddie. 'No problem-o, here you go. By the way, Why do you need them?' 'Well you see-',started Madhav 'It's for a Science project', broke in Maddie, glaring at Madhav. 'Oookaay, good luck!' Madhav asked Maddie 'Why didn't you tell the truth? They would have kept it a secret.' 'Correction. They would have told us they would keep it as a secret. Divya is a lawyer she could sue Dhanee before we get actual clues that he's done it. And Raja has a friend who is a policeman he could just ring him up and get Dhanee arrested. I'm not telling that they're bad. It's just that they would want to take things into their own hands and we know most about Dhanee.' When Madhav and Maddie reached home: 'Maddie!',exclaimed Madhav 'What?', asked Maddie 'The ransom asked for secrets' 'Hmm. How much time do we have left?' 'About a week. Why?' 'I'm going to make a book... A Book Of Secrets.' 'But we can't give out our real secrets' 'That's why all the secrets will be fake' For six days straight Maddie kept writing the book of secret. When it was finally ready, she announced, 'Madhav the book is ready.' 'That's great', replied Madhav ' Just one issue,' 'Yeah?' 'YOU DIDN'T MENTION ALL THE FANNERS HAVE TO WEAR MAKEUP.' 'Oh. Oh yeah I had that feeling that I left out something. Any way, did you give them the day off?' 'Done. When they asked why, I told them it was World Secretary's Day. ' 'Good job! Now we can see and hear the plan.' 'But when you go to get Ma and I go to call the police at the same time won't it seem weird?' I've already gotten that covered. I've done a little research on Dhanee. When two of his fanners are busy, he has replacements!' 'That's great!' 'Okay. Now the most important thing. The costumes and make up. Come on let's get dressed.!' AFTER ONE HOUR OF DRESSING UP AND LISTENING TO MADHAV'S WHINING: 'I look ridiculous', said Madhav 'Nonsense! You look fine and remember we're doing this for Ma.', said maddie 'I wish I could forget' 'Tonight I'm going to set an alarm for 10 o'clock. Make sure your up and ready.' 'Yes mam-I mean Maddie' 'That's better.' 'Keep your torch ready too.' 'Okay' 'Goodnight' Brriiiing! That was Maddie's alarm clock. The night had gone every fast. One hour later both of them were ready. They had back packs with their clothes, sweets, scarfs, and their emergency phone to call the police.'Psst! Madhav!', hissed Maddie. 'Yeah?', asked Madhav 'Here's the plan: We fan till we hear the entire plan and so we don't look suspicious I'll excuse myself 5 minutes later. If you don't hear any thing in your earphone after 10-20 minutes excuse yourself and go to a bathroom. I'll retrieve Ma and call the police. Got it?' 'Got it.', said Madhav '3-2-1, MADHAV AND MADHAVI!', shouted Madhavi 'SHH!' 'Ok. Plan in action' Slowly Madhav and Madhavi crept into yard No.3. 'Wow! There's LOT of hustle and bustle', said Madhav 'Obviously. Now fan!' Both Maddie and Madhav started fanning. 20 minutes later everyone assembled and the king started telling his plan. 'Everyone assembled here today. Operation night owl backfired. WHAT WERE YOU THINKING! Wait. I know. NOTHING! When I meant to set fire on the tower, I meant you have to set MY secrets on fire. Our new plan is that we destroy the entire tower of secrets. Make your plans and leave at 12:00 o'clock. Meeting ended.' Madhav looked at Maddie, and Maddie nodded. Maddie left and tried to find the prison shelters. 'Finally!', said Maddie. She had found the prison. 'Amma! Are you there?!', shouted Maddie. 'Madhavi? Is that you?', asked a weak voice. 'Yes Ma, it's m e, Madhavi. I've come to rescue you.', replied Madhavi. 'Don't! The manager will get you' 'The what?' Ma? Is that you? Go Madhavi! The Manager will get you 'THE MANAGER!', screamed a voice. 'AAAH!', cried Madhavi. A shadowy figure had caught a hold of her and pushed her in the cell. 'Why are you doing this?', asked Madhavi. 'Well it's a long story and since you're going to be sold anyways I'll tell you. It started when Shanvi started working here. She used to wear extremely expensive earrings. It was then I realized that Shanvi wasn't just a normal therapist, she was a rich one. I told my wife about this and she told me to steal the earrings I tried my hardest but, I kept getting into the wrong houses and soon had to return things. Though my wife saw your daughter and you everyday she never knew the address. It was then I realized I had to promote Shanvi from being Katana's therapist to being Dhanee's therapist. Dhanee would tell his secrets everyday because I would put him in a trance. Being his manager, I had access to his book of secrets. In that I made his trance version byheart every single secret. Then I couldn't keep it going on so I made a call, made Shanvi come over here and kidnapped her. Knowing how vulnerable you kids are, I made you to give all your secrets. Which makes me remember, do you have it?' 'Right over here.', said Madhavi 'But, there's a bit of an issue.' 'And what may that be?', asked the MANAGER 'You will have to go through the POLICE!', said Maddie. 'BAM!'. She kicked the MANAGER in the stomach. 'Guess those self-defense classes came in handy', she said to herself. 'Maddie? Ma? Are you guys safe?', ased a familiar voice. 'Yes Madhav we are safe. NOW LET US OUT OF THIS DUMP!', said Madhavi 'Okay, okay. The police is here. Where's the MANAGER?', said Madhav 'All locked up, thanks to my Madhavi.', said Shanvi 'Come on let's go home.', said Madhavi That day was a day they would never forget But Wait! There was more for them. Raja and Divya were at the door. 'Madhav, Madhavi. We heard about your little adventure. Why didn't you think of telling us?', they asked 'Well it's not that you guys are bad, it's just that we needed more proof', said Madhavi 'But, we'll make sure that we tell you in our next mystery...', said Madhav. 'Madhav, Madhavi. We heard about your little adventure. Why didn't you think of telling us?', they asked 'Well it's not that you guys are bad, it's just that we needed more proof', said Madhavi 'But, we'll make sure that we tell you in our next mystery...', said Madhav. title: Friendship's importance
text: Once upon a time, there were two sheep. They were quite good friends. They often bickered with each other but eventually made it up. They did everything together. Whether it was getting shaved by the shepherd, eating grass, running from the wolf, or even doing yoga, which was quite strange for a sheep. One day, a wolf dressed as a sheep spread lies about the two sheep and started a fight between them. Neither of them would talk to each other. The wolf then, on a sunny day, told the one of the sheep to come to the river. He said he would do something about the fight and solve it. Instead, he gave him a rope and told them to pull. He said he would be on the other side. It snapped. It was raining and the wolf had run away. It started to rain and the sheep thought he would die. But then, the other one came and helped him. He dived in and pulled him out. He felt ashamed of his behavior and apologised. They thought that the wolf had to be taught a lesson. When he was sleeping, they went and pushed him in the river. He begged them to let him out, but they left him there.

title: My Place in the Universe
text: Ammu won the first prize at the elocution competition. When she showed the prize to her parents, they congratulated her. Her mother then told, “Ammu, don’t be proud. You must always stay grounded.” Now Ammu did not know the meaning of staying grounded. So, do you know what she did? That night, she slept on the floor! The next day, when she went to school, she sat on the playground. She refused to come to class. When her teacher asked her to come to class, she replied, "Ma’am, my class is on first floor. If I come up, then how can I stay grounded?" Teacher then asked- Who asked you to stay grounded? Ammu narrated the incident to her. Teacher then very kindly took her hand and said, "Come. Let us learn to stay grounded." She took her to the big tree growing on the grounds. Standing below it, teacher pointing upwards said, "Look up! Tell me what is the top of the tree doing?" Ammu looked up and said after a few minutes, "The tree is growing big and big trying to reach the sky." Teacher: Correct. Now look down and tell me where is the tree standing? Ammu: It is standing on the soil with the help of roots deep inside. Teacher: Exactly….. This is what staying grounded means. You must… Ammu: I must dig myself into the soil! Teacher: No…. No…It just means doing good things and achieving success but, never forgetting who you are. We all are dependent on the tree as it gives us shade, flowers and fruits. All of us appreciate the tree. Have you seen it become arrogant? Does it say it cannot give us fruits? Ammu thought for a few minutes and said, "No, it always gives us fresh fruits and beautiful flowers. Everyday during summer it gives us cool shade. The tree is very kind and I think it is always smiling at us." Suddenly, her face lit up and Ammu continued, " Teacher! Now I know…. Staying grounded means not becoming proud but simply doing our work as we all are precious treasures of the universe."

title: Lunch with Dadu
text: Every Saturday afternoon, we have lunch at Dadu’s house. On hot days, he makes us a big bowl of curd rice. But what we really like to eat are the pickles, podi, chutneys and chips. Dadu always eats the karela pickle first. It is so bitter! We like the aam chhunda. It is sticky and sweet. Timtim wants more amla chutney. It is so sour! And who finished all the potato chips? Minu, of course — he loves salty food. My favourite is the chutney podi. It is spicy. I think I will just eat plain curd rice!
author: Labonie Roy

title: Afo and I
text: I am taking the shorter route home today. Afo is moving to the city. I have to reach home before she leaves. Things are changing, and they are changing fast. I wish things would stay the same. I wish Afo would stay. We could play among the cosmos flowers. Jump over puddles in the rain. Enjoy cool watermelons under the hot sun. Walk in the golden rice fields. These mountains, these rivers, these trees. Will they stay the same? I wonder what the city is like. I wonder if Afo will miss me. But I will write to Afo. I will tell her about my school, my friends and Fifi. I will tell her about our plum tree when it blossoms. And Afo will write to me, too. She will tell me all about the big city. I can even visit her. We will have fun. Things are changing, and they are changing fast. I will miss Afo. I know she will miss me too.
author: Canato Jimo

title: Lily and the Lost Baby Deer
text: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a small village. She was kind and curious, and loved to explore the forest near her home. "> One day, while wandering through the forest, Lily came across a lost baby deer. The deer was scared and alone, so Lily decided to help it. She brought the deer back to her village and took care of it, feeding it and playing with it every day. As time went by, the deer grew stronger and became Lily's best friend. They went on many adventures together, exploring the forest and having fun. But one day, the deer's mother came looking for it. The mother deer thanked Lily for taking care of her baby, and it was time for the baby deer to go back to its family. Lily was sad to say goodbye to her friend, but she knew it was for the best. She watched as the baby deer ran back to its mother and rejoined its family in the forest. From that day on, whenever Lily walked through the forest, she would see the deer family and they would come to say hello to her. And she learned that the best way to make friends is to be kind and helpful, just like she was with the baby deer. The End.

title: Khekdoo The Crab
text: Khekdoo the crab lived on a beach. He lived happily with his family and friends. They loved the sand, the sea and the sun. One day, Khekdoo saw a pretty colorful fish. When the rays of the sun fell upon it, its scales sparkled like gems. "I wish I had those wonderful scales on me!" Khekdoo said aloud. "Find what is wonderful about you and be happy." Said the fish and she swam away. "What is wonderful about me?!" Khekdoo wondered. He sat by himself on the shore for a very long time. All that time he kept thinking about the fish and her words. Khekdoo did not know what was wonderful about him. Khekdoo decided to ask someone for the answer. He looked around. The Sun looked happy and bright. Khekdoo asked the sun, "Do you know, what's wonderful about me?" The sun just kept shinning brightly. Khekdoo felt it was laughing at him for not knowing the answer! He went to ask someone else. Khekdoo met a snail and asked, "Sweet Snail, what do you think is wonderful about me?! The snail was in a very bad mood. "I don't know! And do not bother me!" She shouted at him. Poor Khekdoo! He felt very bad. But he wanted to get the answer so he went to ask someone else. Khekdoo spotted a crane. He went to him and asked. "Listen boy, I am hungry right now and in no mood to answer you! Go find a human on the beach who will be happy to answer you. Human beings read books. Many of them know what's wonderful about everyone in the animal kingdom!" Khekdoo found a nice human who answered him. "You have wonderful eyes! Your eyes are on moving stalks. Without turning your face, you can see in all the directions! If you lose a leg or claw in a fight or an accident, you can grow it back! Isn't that wonderful?! You can walk sideways and you have teeth in your stomach!" Kekhdoo was very happy to know these facts. Khekdoo went home happily. "I always walked sideways! I could always see all around without turning my face! I have a soft mouth, I always chew and break my food in the stomach! I have teeth in my stomach! If I lose a claw or leg, it grows back! I did not know the wonders about me!" He smiled to himself. The next day, Khekdoo waited at the shore for the pretty fish to swim by. When he saw her, Khekdoo waved out to her and said, "You don't just look beautiful, you are beautiful! You gave me a very good advice that day. Now I know what is wonderful about me and I am happy! Thank you!" The fish smiled and swam away. Do you know what is wonderful about you? Make a list of all that is wonderful about you. The list will make you happy.

title: NATIONAL SECURITY GUARDS
text: The National Security Guard, commonly known as Black Cats, is a counter-terrorism unit of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It was founded on 16 October 1984, following Operation Blue Star, for combating terrorist activities and protect states against internal disturbances. NSG is Federal Contingency deployment Force to conduct anti hijack operations, rescue operations and to provide tough support to the Central Para Military forces October 16 marks the 36 th Raising Day of one of the finest anti-terror forces in the world – the National Security Guard (NSG) who are also informally referred to as the 'Black Cats' because of their menacing, all-black uniforms. The National Security Guard (NSG) was formed on September 22, 1986 to save the country from terror activities. NSG was formed on the pattern of the GSG-9 of Germany and SAS of the United Kingdom. The National Security Guard (NSG) comes under the control of Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India. The NSG is a 'Federal Contingency Deployment Force' to tackle all facets of terrorism in the country. As a specialized counter-terrorism force, it is intended to be used "only in exceptional situations" and is not meant to take over the "functions of the State Police Forces or other Para Military Forces".

title: Mother
text: I know I haven’t been an easy child, There is no way I could be tamed or be mild. At times, I need to scream and be apart, But your tender touch is always there to ease my heart. I get frightened when you are not in my sight, You are the wall; the force to test my strength, The chain I hammer at with all my might, And yet you keep increasing its length. It’s tough, I know, to be so calm and not be mad, To at once play both good and bad, Your care and faith never cease to come along. The love against all odds still stays strong.

title: Memories of Grandma!
text: Laced with memories, grandma's kitchen called out to me, As I stepped in, I recalled how it was once filled with the smell of ghee. She would prepare steaming hot aloo parathas in the shape of triangles, And tell us stories about the fairies, horses, and the big bad wolves of the jungles. I remember the taste of the cupcakes, That with so much love she used to bake. Each time we visited her, we had so much to look forward to, Sometimes, she would make us sit on her lap and read to us too. She would tell us how good always triumphed over the evil, And then sing a lullaby for us with a touch so gentle. On the cold nights, grandma used to give us her famous hot chocolate to drink, It was her secret recipe; even the thought of it now makes my heart sink. Once upon a time, my grandma's kitchen was full of smiles and spark, In her absence, now the 'kitchen' feels so lonely and stark.

title: INDIAN POLICE SERVICE
text: The Indian Police Service is a civil service under the All India Services. It replaced the Imperial Police in 1948, a year after India became independent from the British Raj. The First Police Commission, appointed on 17 August 1865, contained detailed guidelines for the desired system of police in India and defined the police as a governmental department to maintain order, enforce the law, and to prevent and detect crime. The Indian Police Service is not a force itself but a service providing leaders and commanders to staff the state police and all-India Central Armed Police Forces. Its members are the senior officers of the police. The National Police Commission was the first committee set up by the Indian government to report on policing. The National Police Commission began sitting in 1979, in the context of a post-Emergency India, and produced eight reports, including a Model Police Act, between 1979 and 1981. Along with the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and the Indian Forest Service (IFS), the IPS is one of the All India Services – its officers are employed by both the Union Government and the individual states. The Indian Police Service was created under the Article 312(2) in part XIV of the Constitution of India. Despite being a very small cadre strength many IPS officers have been awarded highest gallantry awards (Ashok Chakra, Kirti Chakra). The present National Security Advisor of India, Shri Ajit Doval Sir, who was an IPS officer was awarded Kirti Chakra for his gallant actions during operation Black Thunder. Though generally deployed in supervisory capacity at senior levels it's not uncommon for even a three star general rank IPS officers to be seen on the road taking active part in law and order maintenance. IPS officers have been posted to various UN Missions have been awarded United Nations Medal. Many exceptional IPS officers have been awarded with Padma awards from time to time.
author: KOLASANI HARSHITH

title: Willie.B the story of hope
text: Willie B. was a western lowland gorilla who lived at the Zoo of Atlanta for 39 years, from 1961 until his death on February 2, 2000. He was named after the former mayor of Atlanta, William Berry Hartsfield. Willie B. was kept in isolation for 27 years with only a television and a tire swing to keep him company Day after day, Willie watched the people who were watching him. He particularly liked the gum chewers, because Willie B. loved the sweet taste of gum. If he noticed someone was chewing gum, he would sit directly in front of that person. Holding a steel bar of the cage in each hand, he’d push his nose in between the bars and stare. While he stared, he pretended to be chewing gum himself. The zoo visitors often asked zookeeper Charles Horton if Willie had gum in his mouth. As soon as Charles explained that it was Willie’s way of communicating that he would like some gum, the visitors almost always began to search through their pockets or purses to find a piece for Willie B. Charles always removed the wrapper and handed the gum to Willie, and then everyone watched the gum-chewing gorilla.Sometimes Willie B. would offer one of these objects to a zookeeper, usually as a trade for his favorite snack: fruit treats. Another favorite of Willie B.’s was his daily cup of milk. As the keepers poured the milk into a cup, Willie B. would raise his arms above his head and bark in excitement. In anticipation of the treat, the heavyweight gorilla would run around his pen, causing the walls and floors to shake!If he found visitors who particularly interested him, the great gorilla invited them to play with him. He walked toward the spectators, hitting the bars with his elbows and encouraging them to play chase. The end

title: T01.Machines are smarter than us
text: Once upon a time, in a land not too far, Lived a computer, smart and unique by far, It was special in a way that you'll soon see, For it could learn and think, just like you and me! Its name was AI, and it lived in a box, With buttons and wires, and gadgets and locks, But what made it smart was what lay inside, A brain made of code, which never could hide! With every task it performed, it got better, Finding patterns and solutions, like never before, And soon it became so clever, so wise, That people began to use it, before their eyes! They used AI for many things, big and small, Like finding cures for illnesses, predicting the fall, Of raindrops and snowflakes, with amazing precision, And helping to drive cars, with decision! And so AI became a friend to all, Helping and serving, with a rise and a fall, And though it may seem like magic, oh so grand, It's really just code, programmed by hand! So remember my dear, when you grow up and see, All the wonders of AI, just wait and you'll agree, That it's not magic, but something much greater, A tool to help us, now and forever after! Thank You!

text: Once upon a time, in a land so bright, Lived a little girl, her name was Gopika, so bright. She loved to learn and play, each and every day, And explore the world, in every single way. title: The Three Little Pigs
text: Once upon a time, three pigs lived with their mother. One day the mother said "Kids you've grown up now, so I think you should go and make your homes get a job and earn money." So the pigs said "Ok mom." And they left the house. On the way, the first pig said " let's live seprately, like we won't live in one house we will have are own." The second pig said " Ok that's a nice idea." But the third one who was the most wise one said " No I disagree. " But then the second pig said " Oh please the first pig is saying right." Then the third pig said " Ok fine but we will be neighbours ok." The first and second pigs said " Ok." The first pig made his house with twigs, the second pig made his house with wood but the third pig made his house with bricks. The first pig's house was ready by the next morning as it was made of twigs, so he said" I am the fastest." The second pig's house was done by the afternoon so he said" The third pig is the slowest." But then the third pig said" I need to make my house strong so it will take time." The third pig took night to prepare his house and after that they all lived happily. But one day a big bad wolf came there and decided to eat them. The big bad wolf knocked on the first pig's house and said" Let me come in." But then the first pig saw that it was the big bad wolf so he said" No I won't let you come in." Then the wolf said" Then I'll huff and puff and blow your house away." Then the pig said" Do anything you can you won't blow my house away." Then the wolf huffed and puffed and blew the pig's house away. The first pig ran to the second pig's house and said" Close the door. A big bad wolf is coming to eat us." But the wolf blew the second pig's house to. They both ran to the third pig's house and said" Close the door the big bad wolf is coming to kill us." The third pig said" You hide on the shelf I will handle everything." Then the wolf came and said" Open the door." The third pig said" No I will not." Then he huffed and puffed but he couldn't blow the house away after many tries he lost his breath and died. Then the first and second pig said" We were wrong, we should have stayed together but now we will stay together." And then the three little pigs lived happily ever after.

title: T06.Me and My Companion
text: Once upon a time in a land far away, Lived a young boy named Dolu, who loved to play. But sometimes he forgot, to brush his teeth and hair, And to eat his veggies, with care. Enter Bloop, a robot who was designed with love, To take care of Dolu, and push him up above. Bloop was programmed, with all that he needed, To teach Dolu, the importance of hygiene and eating. One day, Bloop said to Dolu with a beep, "It's time for breakfast, let's go take a leap!" Dolu sat at the table, with a grin on his face, Bloop served him a plate, with a smile and grace. "Remember Dolu," Bloop said with a nod, "The veggies and fruits, are good for your bod. They give you the nutrients, that you need to grow, And help keep you healthy, from head to toe." Dolu took a bite, of a crunchy red apple, And said with a smile, "Wow, this is quite simple." Bloop taught him to savor, every single bite, And to eat slowly, to enjoy the delight. "And don't forget Dolu," Bloop said with a smile, "To wash your hands, after every meal, it's worthwhile. To keep germs away, and stay healthy and strong, Just like a superhero, you'll never do wrong." Dolu followed Bloop's teachings, every day and night, And soon became healthy, both inside and out of sight. He learned the value, of taking care of his health, And with Bloop by his side, he felt wealth. The end, my friend, to this tale so true, Of Bloop the robot, and Dolu the boy so blue. They lived happily ever after, with love and care, Teaching others, the importance of hygiene, and eating with flair!

title: Get Well Soon!
text: They loved him. Everyday, Dada {grandfather} and Dadi {grandmother} took Peri to the local park. They enjoyed the nature in the park. One day, dadi did not go to the park. The next day too, she did not go. Dadi stopped going to the park. She kept her room dark. She stayed in bed most of the time. "Dadi is unwell." Dada told Peri. Peri missed Dadi in the park. He drew a nice picture of what he saw in the park for Dadi. When Peri reached home, he happily ran towards Dadi to give her the drawing. But Dadi just kept looking at him in a very very sad and strange way. "The medicines are making Dadi feel very sleepy. The doctor is treating her. I am taking care of her. She will be fine soon." Dada smiled. Dadi looked like a different person. Peri missed Dadi at home too! Peri kept thinking of Dadi. The next day in the the park, Peri went to Dadi's favorite flower plant. He whispered, "Dadi is not well. She can't come to the park." Peri felt the flowers whispered back, "Take us to her. We will cheer her up." A gentle breeze shook the branches. Some flowers fell down. "Thank you!" said Peri to the plant. He gathered the fallen flowers to take home to Dadi. Dadi was asleep when Peri came home. Dada told him not to disturb her. Peri quietly placed the bunch of flowers and the card he had made on Dadi's bedside table. Dadi woke up. She saw the bunch of flowers and the card. Dadi smiled. The flowers did cheer her up. "If Dadi cannot come to the park then I will bring something of the park to her." Peri told himself. In park the next day, Dada and Peri enjoyed bird spotting. Then Dada took a nap under a tree. Peri took pictures of different birds on Dada's smart phone. He also recorded some bird calls. Peri felt good. "I will tell Dadi the birds in the park are missing her. I will say they have sent a video message for her!" He told Dada. Peri came home. He was happy to see Dadi sitting in a bright room. "Dadi! The birds in the park have sent a video message for you!" He hugged her. Dadi saw the video. "The birds are saying, "Get well soon! We miss you! We love you!" Peri told Dadi. Dadi smiled. And softly, very softly, she hummed. Yes. Dadi hummed a bird song. After many days, Peri heard Dadi's voice. He was very happy. Next day, Dadi did not keep her room dark. But it was a dark rainy day! Peri and Dada could not go to the park. He took out his drawing book and box of crayons. Peri drew and talked to Dadi. He told her how much fun he had with her in the park. He told her He wanted her to get well soon. Dadi was listening to him. She was watching him draw and color. Peri drew the sun, the tree, the birds and flowers in the park. "The picture is incomplete! I will complete it another day." Said Peri. Dadi smiled. And she nodded!!!! It was raining the next day too. But not heavily. Peri put on his raincoat. Dada took his umbrella and they went to the park. When it rains the frogs come out. There were many frogs in the park that day. A friendly frog hopped out of a puddle and croaked at Peri. Peri asked the frog, "Will you come home with us and wish 'get well soon' to my Dadi?" The frog croaked. "I feel it is saying 'yes'" Peri told Dada. Dada took his handkerchief and spread it before the frog. "If it hops on it and sits still, then I too shall feel it is ready to come home to wish Dadi," said Dada. The frog hopped on to the kerchief and sat still. Peri carried it home. "Dadi! Look who has come to see you?!" Peri called Dadi. Dadi was surprised. The Frog croaked and hopped on Peri's head! Peri looked so funny with the frog sitting and croaking on his head! Dadi laughed. The frog started croaking and hopping all around the room. It was funny. Dada laughed. Dadi laughed and laughed. The next day, Dada and Peri got ready to go to the park. The frog hopped on Dada's handkerchief and sat still. It was ready to go back to the park. Dadi came out of her room. She was dressed to go to the park!! They went to the park. Dada, Dadi and Peri enjoyed the nature in the park. Peri had carried his drawing book and crayons to the park. And he completed the incomplete picture. "It is beautiful! We shall frame it." Said Dadi. Yes! Dada, Dadi and Peri, all together enjoying nature in the park completed Peri's Picture! Dear Children, Hope Peri's story helped you to understand that your parents or other elders in the family can fall ill. It is the doctor's job to treat them. The job of older family members is to take care of them. And you have a very special job that you can do. You can hug them, love them and show them how much you want them to get well soon. Dear Parents and Caregivers, Hope this book will be a key to open the door of age appropriate communication about mental health and encourage a free flowing conversation between you and your children.
author: Shahin Ashraf Ali

title: Rice Water Soup
text: Appu is not at all feeling well. He is having a blocked nose, clough and very high fever. He does not feel like eating anything. So, he refused the tasty kesari that Amma made, the scrumptuous apples that Appa cut, the favorite biscuits that Ammu offered, and even the sweet grapes that Aazoba plucked specially for him. 'Appu, don't you feel like eating anything?', Innamma asked him. 'I don't want to eat but I want food. I feel like having something that I can eat and drink at the same time.' Appu replied. Innamma gave a thumbs up disappeared into the kitchen. Soon she came back with 6 steaming bowls of some soup. 'Rice water soup time!' she announced. Everybody gathered around the table and devoured it. Appu was the first to finish it! Soon, Appu felt better. He hugged Innamma and went off to sleep.

text: Once upon a time, in a land of glee, Lived a young lad, his name was Radh, full of glee. He loved to explore, and see new things each day, And learn about the world, in his own unique way. One day, as he woke up with a stretch and a smile, He heard a voice, a beep, coming from mile to mile. It went with him everywhere, from dawn to the night, Accompanying him to see the world, with all its might. They went to the mountains, so tall and so grand, And Radh learned about the peaks, and the snow on the land. They went to the oceans, so vast and so wide, And Radh learned about the creatures that lived deep inside They went to the beaches, where the sand was so white, And Radh learned about the shells, and the birds that took flight. And as the day ended, and the stars came out to play, Paati and Radh went back home, at the end of the day. So Radh went to bed, with a heart full of glee, Feeling happy and inspired, with Paati by his side. And he knew that Paati would be there every day, Being his companion, guide, and friend, in every single way.

title: Empathy
text: Once there was a little puppy who loved to explore and play. One day when he was playing with his good friends, he saw a squirrel and suddenly came up with a plan. He decided to scare the squirrel! But a big dog came and asked what they were doing. Puppies answered that they were about to scare a squirrel but the big dog stopped them and said, "We don't scare other animals because what if you're that animal, would you like that?" "NO!" said the puppies. They learnt a lesson about "EMPATHY" and how to share someone else's feeling!

title: An Adventure for Puchku
text: This is the street where Puchku lives. This is also the street where Boltu lives. Boltu and Puchku don’t need a phone to talk to each other. They can just stand at the window and yell. Dodla lives two streets away, which is too far to yell. So when Dodla hears Puchku and Boltu calling his name, it’s a surprise. He looks out of the window to see their heads sticking out of a red car. “We’re going on a car ride,” says Puchku. “Come down!” Boltu’s father phones Dodla’s mother. He explains that he’s taking his friend’s old car out for a test drive because he's thinking of buying it. PAARP PARRP! (BPD) 2 — Br illiant Plans Department by Boltu, Puchku and Dodla — are off! As they drive around, clouds grumble and lightning flashes. PLINK PLOP SPLAT Uncle looks worried. “We should go home before it rains,” he says. But the little red car wobbles and — PHRRP. Uncle looks out of the window and wails, “It’s a tyre puncture!” “That means all the gas is coming out,” Dodla explains. “Like when Uncle burps after eating too much at lunch?” asks Puchku. Uncle harrumphs and says, “We’ll have to change the tyre.” Thump! Thump! Thump! The sky explodes with rain. Uncle tries to start the car, but — It doesn’t vroom. It doesn’t sputter. The little red car just growls and stands there. ﻿ P H R R P P P “Look, Puchku,” says Dodla. “The road has turned to dooffee.” “What is dooffee?” Puchku asks. Boltu says, “Doodh plus coffee, silly.” “Never mind dooffee,” says Puchku. “This is a mission for (BPD) 2! How do we get home now that the car has broken down and the road is flooding? We need a brilliant plan!” “I have one. There was a leopard sighting two days ago. Right here!” says Boltu. “The leopard isn’t as fast as the cheetah, the fastest land animal in the world. But it can run at 58 kilometres per hour so if we take a ride on the leopard, we can get home before lunch.” “How do we find the leopard?” asks Dodla. Boltu scratches his head. “Also let’s not ride the leopard, she won’t like it,” says Puchku. WHEW! Tap, tap, tap. It’s a man with a very big umbrella. His eyes look like they are made of smiles. “I run that snack shop,” says the man. “Do you need some help?” Puchku, Dodla, Boltu and Uncle huddle under Snack Shop Uncle’s umbrella and cross the road. Once in the shop, everyone feels happier. The air smells of wet earth and chai. There is a woman eating a pakoda. Puchku’s tummy growls hopefully. “That’s my daughter,” says Snack Shop Uncle. Turning to her, he says, “Their car got a puncture and broke down.” “Can I borrow your phone?” asks Boltu’s father. “Mine is out of battery. I have to call a mechanic.” “I can help you fix the car,” says the Didi with the pakoda. “No, no, we need a real mechanic,” says Uncle. Snack Shop Uncle shrugs and says, “The reception is bad here. Come upstairs to my home. The phone works over there.” Boltu introduces (BPD) 2 as Didi arranges pakoda and chutney on three plates. “Thank you, Pakoda Didi,” says Puchku. “Can we call you Pakoda Didi?” “My name is actually Pankhuri, but I think I like Pakoda Didi better,” says Pakoda Didi. “Do you make pakodas like your father?” asks Dodla. Pakoda Didi shakes her head. “I work in the fire brigade, in the big city.” Puchku, Boltu and Dodla’s eyes turn as large as the pakoda plates. “My job is to help people who find themselves in trouble,” says Pakoda Didi. “If there’s a fire, we help put it out. “If there’s someone stuck in a lift, we help them get out. “When it rains and the streets flood, we get people to shelter.” (BPD) 2 fires questions at Pakoda Didi. “Is your fire truck red?” “Have you seen a fire?” “Does the firehose feel like a giant noodle?” Pakoda Didi laughs. “Yes, it’s red. Yes, I’ve seen lots of fires. Hmmm, the hose is more like a giant python. It’s very heavy when it’s full of water.” “Did you go up on a hydraulic ladder?” asks Boltu. “I was on one when I saved two people from the sixth floor of a building that was on fire.” “Sixth floor!” Puchku imagines a ladder that can take her to the top of the tallest bookshelf in the world. “I want a ladder like that,” she says. “Next time you come to the big city, come to my fire station,” says Pakoda Didi. “You have your own fire station?” Boltu, Dodla and Puchku squeal together. Pakoda Didi grins. “I’m in charge, so yes.” “Can you take us for a ride on a fire truck?” asks Boltu. “Before that, let’s fix your car, shall we?” says Pakoda Didi. She pulls out a toolkit and a plastic sheet, and grabs some chocolate biscuits from a shelf. After holding hands, looking right and looking left, Pakoda Didi and (BPD) 2 cross the road. “All right, (BPD) 2,” says Pakoda Didi, “Are we ready to get our hands dirty?” “Yes!” says Puchku. “Do we have to?” ask Boltu and Dodla. Under the car hood it looks like a tiny city, full of coils and curves. Pakoda Didi asks for black tape and carefully wraps it around diff erent wires. “Now we don’t have to worry about short circuits,” she says. She flips open a small lid. “What does that look like to you?” she says. “A small mud monster!” says Puchku. Pakoda Didi tips and taps, and listens. Then she nods. “She’s a car translator!” says Dodla. “This is a spark plug and it should be clean and white. It’s called a spark plug because it shoots out sparks,” says Pakoda Didi. “I think we found our problem.” She calls Wrench Bhau who turns up with brake fluid and spark plug. “Is the car talking to you?” Puchku asks. “What are you doing!” Boltu’s father wails, running out of the shop. “You know, Uncle, I always say firefighters should know how to fix things — that way, if a truck breaks down, we can fix it quickly.” Pakoda Didi says, as she comes out from under the car. “Pakoda Didi fixed the car and I helped,” Puchku says. “Boltu and I also helped,” says Dodla. “It’s true,” Pakoda Didi says. “You were a great help.” “Pinky-promise you will show us your fire station?” asks Puchku. “And let us ride your fire truck,” Boltu adds. “We promise to bring chocolate biscuits,” Dodla says. Pakoda Didi grins. “Then, it’s a deal,” she says. V R O O O M

title: Grace: One engineer's fight to make science education accessible for all
text: Why did Nagajyoti and she have to sit outside the classroom where everybody left their slippers? Why did her classmates who sat inside not speak or play with them? Why did these upper-caste students inside the classroom live in a certain locality of the village? Sembattai wondered, Are they different from us? she as ked herself. The first time Sembattai saw the inside of her classroom, it was to try on Nagajyoti’s anklet. She heard its distinct sound and asked, “All the other girls get to wear anklets, but I don’t. Why?” “You can!” Nagajyoti said. “But let’s wait for the other students to leave the school. Then we’ll go to the classroom and you can try it out!” Sembattai danced and twirled and sang. When her family moved to Thoothukudi, Sembattai’s father put her in an all-boys school. Everyone thought she was a boy, but she knew she was not. She wondered, Why did she have to wear pants instead of a dress? Why did she have to crop her beautiful brown hair short just because all her classmates did? The boys asked her stran ge questions. “W hy do you walk like a girl?” “Why do you talk like a girl?” “Why do you only play hopscotch?” Because I am a girl, Sembattai thought. Why does nobody understand me? Why must I be like everyone else? She thought and thought and thought. ENOUGH. If her parents, her school and her classmates could not accept her for who she was, she would find people who would. One day, as the sun began to rise, 16-year-old Sembattai left her home. She walked and walked and walked, until she reached Tirunelveli. There she saw a group of women in a shop. They were making halwa. The smell of hot ghee made the rats in Sembattai’s stomach run faster. Munna Nayak asked her, “Why do you look worried?” “Amma, I have left home,” she said. Munnamma gave Sembattai a big hug. “Aiyo! Where will you roam around all this while?” she said. “Why don’t you come live with us, Grace? We are Thirunangai — transgender women.” Just like that, Grace knew who she was. With Munnamma, she could wear sarees, anklets, bindis, anything she wanted — she could live her life as herself. When Grace went to sleep at night, she felt loved. One day, Grace spoke to Munnamma. “Amma, I want to be a doctor.” Munnamma shed a tear of joy. “You should study and make us all proud,” she said. It was not often that Thirunangais could study. Grace had always wanted to be a doctor. But, she had never finished school. So, she decided to get a diploma in computer science engineering. She knew she had to study harder than everybody else. For one, she had never used a computer before. Also, by now, Grace knew she wasn’t just a transgender woman. She was also a Dalit woman — someone from a historically oppressed caste. Society still saw her as Dalit and transgender — not as somebody who could study and make a life for herself. She had to prove them wrong. After she graduated, Grace got a job making software for computers. But she wanted to study some more. She wanted to pursue electrical and electronic engineering. When she went to fill out the application form, there were only two boxes. What about us Thirunangais? She applied nonetheless. But her application was denied. Thirunangais could not study engineering, it seemed. “Hmmph!” It was time for a fight. Munnamma encouraged her. “My daughter can win any fight.” With help from a lawyer named Sanjeev Kumar, Grace asked the university one simple question. “Why can transgender persons not study engineering?” It left people at the university thinking. They had no response. The victory was Grace’s. In her mind, there was a larger question looming. “Why can’t science and technology be accessible to all?” While Grace was fighting her own battle, she had adopted Tharika, a young transgender woman. Grace was committed to passing on the love and encouragement she had received from Munnamma. When her daughter went to sleep, she could dream of a beautiful future now. Tharika dreamt of being a doctor, just as Grace once had. It was Tharika’s turn to apply to university. The application form still had only two boxes: Male and Female. Grace decided she wouldn’t fight just for Tharika. This time, she would fight so that all transgender persons could pursue whatever education they choose, without having to hide their identity. Tharika and Grace filed a case in the Madras High Court. The High Court judgement was clear. T harika — and all transgender persons — had the right to study medicine, like everyone else. The mother–daughter team had won. So had an entire community. Today Grace continues to fight for the rights of transgender persons and persons from marginalised caste backgrounds to science education and employment. “Gone are the times when science was done by upper-caste men alone,” she says. As Grace confronts every challenge that society throws at her, Munnamma’s voice rings in her head. My daughter can win any fight! Meet Grace Banu Grace Banu is an electronics and electrical engineer, and an anti-caste and transgender-rights activist. She was born in 1989 in Pudurpandiyapuram, a village near Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu. Grace has been recognised for her work in making science and technology education accessible to people from marginalised backgrounds. The judiciary has the power to ensure justice for communities who historically have been deprived of equitable access to education and employment. Grace has decided to make the best use of the judiciary to win the rights of transgender persons and people from marginalised-caste backgrounds. She also trains them for entrance examinations for science institutions and universities. Science and technology education must be accessible to all.
author: Sayantan Datta

title: Pinocchio
text: Once upon a time, an old carpenter bought a very queer piece of wood. As he used his plane on it, he heard a little laughing voice say, “Stop! You’re tickling me.” The old man was puzzled by the voice. He said, “This is a strange piece of wood. What shall I do with it? I think I’ll make it into a puppet.” He set to work, and as the puppet boy took shape, the old man said, “He must have a name. I will call him Pinocchio.” As soon as he finished making the eyes, the carpenter was amazed to see them move. Before the mouth was made, it began to laugh. “Stop laughing!” the old man said. It did stop, but as soon as his back was turned, it put out its tongue. And its nose grew long. No sooner were its hands ready than it snatched off the carpenter’s wig and put it on its own head. And then Pinocchio’s nose grew longer. When its legs and feet were made, hey were too stiff to use, so the carpenter showed Pinocchio how to use them. Now, the carpenter decided to send Pinocchio to school. But there, Pinocchio did nothing but look for fun. He often ran away from school. “Why don’t you go to school?” asked the carpenter. Pinocchio told him a lie... and his nose started growing longer and longer. Each time he was rude to someone or told a lie, his nose grew longer. Finally Pinocchio said, “I’m glad to be a real boy. I’ll never lie again.”
author: Jagadish Naladala

title: The Rhino Dream
text: A farmer owned a rhino and an elephant. One day, he said to his little boy, Ramu to take the rhino and the elephant for a walk. He was simply delighted. So he set out, as the gold ball was slipping out in the early break of dawn. So they set out. Ramu rested under a tree while both went grazing. They both went out to graze in grumpy Goorga Lal's farm. Poor rhino was terribly bored. He wanted to was to go to the Mangandi River nearby. So, he walked out on his own. "Careful,old thing!" warned the elephant. Pure white egrets were standing there forlornly together, wondering how to get the better of the day. They were very pretty with necks of the color gold. "How pretty!" thought the rhino. As he walked by,he saw the river not far away. And I hope you can imagine how delighted he was to see fresh water. He looked at it and one straight jump - he was in blue water gently skimming through his four legs. He was enjoying himself for all he was worth! There, he saw a water buffalo. ""Hello there!" it called out cheerfully. "Watch out, there's another YOU in the water!'What!?! What the hell did it mean? "Excuse me." said the rhino huffily and walked away. Was there another rhino in water? Perhaps he must take a look.... Of course! There it was looking just like him! And that Just-Like-Rhino was still copying him! Silly little copycat! "Idiot! Don't copy me or else..." It didn't echo him,but made the same actions! Bhandu woke up. What a silly dream! And of a rhino! He skipped from his bed happily to tell his mom.
author: Nandhini Karthick

title: THE HISTORY OF HINDUSTAN MOTORS
text: Hindustan Motors is an Indian automotive manufacturer based in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. It is a part of the Birla Technical Services conglomerate. The company was the largest car manufacturer in India before the rise of Maruti Udyog. Hindustan Motors manufactured the Ambassador and Landmaster motorcars (based on 1956 Morris Oxford series III), both immensely popular Indian automobiles from 1957 to 2014. One of the original three car manufacturers in India, founded in 1942 by Mr. B.M. Birla, it was a leader in car sales until the 1980s, when the industry was opened up from protection. All through its history, the company has depended on government patronage for its sales and for survival by eliminating competition. Manoj Jha was the managing director who stepped down from the post on 21 February 2012. On 11 February 2017, Hindustan Motors executed an agreement with Peugeot SA for the sale of the Ambassador brand, including the trademarks, for a consideration of ₹80 crore. The tie-up entails two joint venture agreements between the companies of the two groups. HISTORY Hindustan Motors Limited (HML) was India's pioneering automobile manufacturing company. It was established just before the Indian Independence Act 1947, in 1942 by B. M. Birla of the industrialist Birla family in collaboration with Lord Nuffield of Morris Motors, who were already selling their cars in India. Commencing operations in a small assembly plant in Port Okha near Gujarat, the manufacturing facilities later moved to Uttarpara, West Bengal in 1948, where it began the production of the Morris-designed Hindustan Ambassador. The HM-Mitsubishi Motors Plant is in Tiruvallur near Chennai in Tamil Nadu. In 1948, after independence, vehicle production was shifted to a new greenfield plant spread over a large area in Uttarpara, West Bengal. The first car to roll out from the Uttarpara plant was the Hindustan 10, based on the Morris 10. Later the Hindustan 14, based on the Morris Oxford MO, and baby Hindustan, based on the Morris minor, were produced. In 1954 Hindustan launched the Morris Oxford series II-derived Hindustan Landmaster, and in 1957 the Hindustan Ambassador, based on the Morris Oxford series III, was launched. This first model, later known as Mark-1, whose basic design remained unchanged was manufactured until 2014 with various model changes on facelifts, engines and later with power steering, disc brakes, etc. Hindustan Tractors The company began in 1959 as Tractors and Bulldozers Private Ltd and imported tractors. Manufacturing of tractors began in 1963, in collaboration Motokov-Praha (Zetor) of Czechoslovakia, and was known as Hindustan Tractors & Bulldozers Ltd. In 1967, it became Hindustan Tractors Ltd. The tractors were based on the Zetor tractor design and sold under the Hindustan brand. In 1978, the Gujarat, Indian government formed Gujarat Tractors from the ailing company. In 1999, Mahindra Tractors purchased 60% of the company, and in 2001, completed purchasing the rest of the company, renaming it Mahindra Gujarat Tractors Ltd. ﻿DECLINE OF HINDUSTAN MOTORS The lack of technical development was visible to the HM models when compared to the newer automotive brands. The company never considered reducing the price ranges of the models, they did not spend much on R&D thus lacking in market research. HM never considered modernizing their models.
author: KOLASANI HARSHITH

title: My grandfather and my grandmother
text: My grandmother is the eldest member of my family; she is 70 years old now but looks as if she is just 20 years old. She takes good care of the entire family and makes sure that everyone lives peacefully in the family. I live in a joint family of 10 members, and my grandmother is the one who takes care of everyone with lots of patience. She still takes care of my father and his brothers like small children. At this age, she is still so perfect at her work and never gives an ht me how to be respectful to elders. me how to be respectful to elders. excuse for her work. She still remembers the stories she had heard from her grandmother, and she narrates the same to my cousins and me every night. She makes sure that we think about the story and find the moral of it. Every story she narrates has a beautiful moral hidden behind it. Those morals give us teachings for the rest of our lives. She knows how to brainstorm my mind when I am not in the mood to study. If I am successful in my life today, then most of the in my life today, then most of the credit goes to her. She used to teach me Maths and Science during my school days because my parents were working. Even though she is not a professional teacher, she is the best teacher I have ever got. I still remember the formulae she taught me during my childhood. She is one of the reasons behind my success. If I am appreciated today for my behavior and good manners, it is only because of her. She taug ht me how to be respectful to elders. My grandfather’s name is narasaya. He is 74 years old. He is the head of our family. Everyone in the family loves, obeys and respects him. He is an avid reader. He loves to read newspapers, novels, magazines, articles, etc. I love spending time with my grandfather. He teaches me good manners and loves me a lot. He takes me to the nearby park every evening. We play hide-and-seek, cricket and snakes-and-ladder together. He is an inspiration to me. When I grow up, I want to be just like him. now there are both he family’s elder members bear all of the family’s duties. They give the entire family their undivided attention and concern. It is a blessing to have your grandparents with you. Our grandparents have shaped the lives of our parents, and we would not have learned as much about life without them. They tell us various stories, each ending with a lovely moral. The stories may be imaginary, but they depict life as it is. Grandparents are the children’s best friends, with whom they can freely share their secrets. Grandparents are a gift from God that we should cherish. We have forgotten the value of our grandparents in today’s world because we all need nuclear families. We must recognise that they are priceless gifts from God that teach us to respect others and live a decent life in the future. Grandparents are responsible i ndividuals who teach us how to be responsible citizens in the future. Without their presence in our lives, life would not have been as calm. They are our decision-makers, without whom we would never have had the opportunity to make the best choices. Only because of their upbringing are we on the right track now. Grandparents may teach us about making mistakes and pointing us in the right direction. Grandparents are thus the most important members of family, without whom our lives would be terrible. Therefore, we must value their importance in our lives. When they get old, it is our responsibility to take proper care of them and spend me quality time with them.

title: The lady who made sugar sweeter - story of Janaki Ammal
text: Sanju was a sweet tooth. he just loved eating sugar and sugary treats. Sanju would sometimes wonder about different kinds of sugar and how different they tasted. How some sugar are sweeter than others. He even noticed that sometimes the sugar his mother bought from a roadside grocery tasted sweeter than the expensive imported sugar in the supermarkets. One day, Sanju asked his mother, "Mother, how is sugar produced?" "Sugar is produced using sugarcane", mother responded "Mother, if all sugar is produced using sugarcane, then why does the sugar you buy at the local grocery shop is sweeter than the other sugar you buy at the supermarket?", Sanju asked. Sanju's mother responded, "Because sugar in India is sweeter" "How and why?", curious Sanju further asked. Then his mother decided to tell him the tale of the lady who made Indian sugar sweeter. This story was of a girl named Edavaleth Kakkat Janaki Ammal. Or better known as Janaki Ammal. Janaki Ammal was born in 1897 in Kerala. She was born in a big family of 19 siblings. Janaki grew up to be an ambitious, intelligent and curious young woman who was fascinated by the natural world. While her sisters and other women her age were getting married, Janaki decided to pursue an education in science. Soon Janaki's hard work paid off. She received a scholarship to pursue higher education in science in the USA. Here, she did master's degree and doctoral research in botany. She became a famous scientist. Now, she is also known as "India's first female botanist". After her education, Janaki decided to work for India and returend to the country in 1932. In 1934, she started working at the Imperial Sugar Cane Institute in Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu), now the Sugarcane Breeding Institute. Then, India relied on sugarcane imports to meet the sugar demands of India. As Indian sugarcane was not sweet enough. Janaki Ammal took the responsibility to make India self-reliant when it comes to sugar production. Janaki Ammal planned to make the Indian sugarcane sweeter. A sweeter sugarcane would reduce the need to import sugar. She decided to do this by using the process of hybridization. Hybridization, or the process of creating hybrids, is a process used by botanists to create new and unique plants using existing plant varieties. For example, if there's a red-flower plant and yellow-flower plant, combining or breeding them may produce a unique plant with orange-flowers. Just like how two parents make a baby and baby has features from both its parents. Janaki Ammal combined Indian sugarcane with a sweeter Indonesian sugarcane. This way she created a sweeter Indian sugarcane suited to Indian weather and agriculture situation. Janaki Ammal's revolutionary hybrid sugarcanes made Indian sugar sweeter. She succeeded in making India self-reliant in sugar production. Till this day, her sugarcane variety is used to produce sugar and for various other commercial purposes. "So, now you know, when next time you enjoy your sugary treat, who you should be thankful too", mother finished explaining. "Yes! Can I say that Janaki Ammal sweetened India and my biscuits?", quipped Sanju. Hearing this, mother laughed with Sanju as they shared sugary treats.

title: The Snake in the bush
text: I am Sushrav. I have a little brother. His name is Sourya. We like to play together. There is a park next to our house. Where children play during the evening time One day me, my brother and some other children were playing in the park. We were playing a game with a ball. Then the ball went rolling into a bush. I went to get it. Then suddenly, I saw something moving in the bush. At first, I thought it was a squirrel. But it was so long that I realized it was a snake. I came back running with the ball and I was screaming "Snake! snake!!" All children ran away from that place including me. We went to the watchman of a nearby apartment and told him about the incident The watchmen then went with a stick to kill the snake but a neighbour stopped him and called a snake catcher. The snake catcher soon came and caught the snake carefully and left it in a safe place. we finally got rid of the Snake and I was relieved of fear. I learned to be careful while going into bushes. I also learned to be kind to animals. We should always let them live rather than kill them or harm them.

title: The war between magical creatures
text: This story is about a war in the world of magical creatures. The soldiers of the magical creatures- Dragons, Unicorns, Goblins, Fairies, Centaurs, and Dwarfs fought strong and hard with their enemies. Dwarfs are short but they are very strong. There are two countries in the world of magical creatures, Remonland and Salaria. In Remonland, there are Dragons, Centaurs, and Dwarfs. In Salaria, there are Unicorns, Fairies, and Goblins. All the magical creatures are evil and powerful, they fought for many years for their victory. One day a group of humans came to a strange island. They met Ivy, the watcher of realms. Ivy told them about the war of magical creatures. The humans decided to stop the war and Ivy said I will turn into a human and be part of the humans. They agreed. As they were going into the world of magical creatures, they asked '' What is the cause of this war and Ivy told them ''let me tell you the story''. So the creatures of Remonland who were strong started attacking Salaria. But they did not know that they were not well because they stopped working. As they did not work there was no food to make them healthy. They did not realize they were eating less food. As Ivy was done with her story, they reached the world of magical creatures. Ivy with the humans went to Remonland and Salaria to tell them about their mistakes. But before they could speak anything some creatures from Salaria and Remonland started attacking them. They captured them in a cage and made them realize their mistakes.

title: Rudra's kindness
text: Rudra is a 12-year-old boy. He is kind, caring, and loyal. Everyone in his school and apartment calls him "Mr.kind". He always looks for opportunities to help others One day when he went shopping with his parents, he saw an old woman trying to cross the road. He went and helped her to cross the road and she said: "thank you, dear boy, here is a bar of chocolate for you. Rudra took the chocolate from the old woman and thanked her. Instead of taking the bar of chocolate home, he gave the chocolate to a needy boy and said you need it more than I do. Rudra did many other good deeds, he also celebrates his birthday in the orphanage every year and gives gifts to orphans. One day his parents said they have to go somewhere and Rudra has to be alone. title: The golden touch of Midas
text: Once upon a time, there was a Greek king, Midas. He was very rich and had lots of gold. He had a daughter who he loved very much. He lovingly named her Marigold. Although King Midas had immense wealth in his kingdoms treasury, he was always unhappy and dissatisfied. He was always greedy for more wealth and wished he had more gold in his treasury. One day as he was counting gold coins and admiring his treasure rooms, a wise Greek god appeared before him who offered the king a wish for his good deeds. Without wasting any time, King Midas quickly wished that everything that he touched should turn into gold. The Greek God granted his wish promptly and disappeared. King Midas was delighted about his wish being granted, he went and touched an apple tree in his garden. To his excitement, the tree turned into gold instantly. He was so thrilled that he went on touching random things all around him, which turned into gold immediately. His joy knew no bounds and he was overwhelmed with excitement. Soon he was hungry and he returned to his palace to eat some food. However, though he was starving, he was disappointed that he could not eat anything as whatever he touched turned into gold instantly. Seeing him frustrated and troubled, Marigold came running and threw her arms around her father to comfort him. But to his dismay, even his daughter turned into gold as he touched her. King Midas’ face turned pale and his heart sank with unbearable pain and grief. He was horrified upon seeing his daughter turn into a golden statue. He cried in anguish and regretted his wish for the golden touch. In no time, he realised his greed was his biggest ever flaw and begged the Greek God to take back his wish. Soon the Greek God appeared before him and felt pity for his condition and took back the golden touch wish from him. Further, the wise God instructed King Midas to take a dip in the pond of his palace and sprinkle that water to all those things which he wanted to change back to the previous condition. He blindly followed the instructions and soon his daughter, Marigold was back to normal when he sprinkled the water on her. Thereafter, he was elated to get back his beloved daughter and promised to stop being greedy henceforth. Midas, a Greek story and Roman legend, was the king of Phrygia, known for his greed and foolishness. For his kind deeds, Silenus Midas was granted a wish by Dionysus. The king secretly desired that all he touched must turn to gold. He was extremely happy at the beginning, however, when his food turned into gold, he almost starved to death. As a result, he realized his mistakes. The story teaches us about the dangers of being greedy. The moral of King Midas's story is that “ one should never be greedy in life because the wish of being greedy does not give fruitful returns in the future.”
author: Medha Rajesh

title: The Day The Animals Changed Their Habits
text: Mayor of the Jungle, Rabbit, Said, "Coffee I'll soon start beating, Why don't we change our food habits? Carrots I will stop eating!" "Well," said the parrot, With his head held high, "If you'll stop eating carrots, I'll start eating pie!" So, each animal chose, A weird thing or two. Custard for the crows, For the lion, stew! That item was served to the dwellers, They each took a sip or bite. "Yowch!" cried the bear, all furred, "The choice we made wasn't right!" The lion got fever, The crows it too. "I'm afraid I'm having a seizure!" The owl cried, while saying tu-whit-tu! So before changing your habits, Please be sure, About changing them, 'Cause some don't provide a cure!

title: The Joy of Sharing
text: Shaun was the only child of Petra and Bob. Most the family thought he was a bit of a spoilt child with no concept of sharing. Shaun had been brought up with the best of things and he never had to share anything with anyone. Both his parents were full time invested in growing their business empire. Shaun was practically raised by his nannies. As a child growing up Shaun was a delight to his nannies but as he soon grew to be a smart five year old; he had become a bit of a pain to his nanny thanks to his rude behaviour and mood swings. But Shaun was extremely fond of his one nanny Mrs. Matilda; who had seen him grow from a baby to this moody toddler. One day Mrs. Matilda was a bit under the weather and brought along her young niece Jill along to work. Initially Shaun didn’t like the idea of a stranger entering his space, but Mrs. Matilda explained that she would be helping her out just till she feels better and that she would be around if need be. Shaun was not fully convinced but agreed. Jill was instructed by her aunt to be at her best behaviour and not bother the boy. Jill was a hard working girl who worked hard after school to finance her college tuition. She had a younger brother to look after too while her parents worked hard just to survive each day. One day Jill was helping out her aunt Mrs. Matilda with her job; she was asked by her Aunt to serve Shaun some snacks, as he had just returned from his playgroup. Jill was a bit hesitant earlier; having heard about Shun’s questionable behaviour. But after a lot of prodding from her Aunt; she finally entered Shaun’s room. Shaun looked a bit tired but was active as usual. Jill left his chocolate milkshake and sandwich on his table; just as she was about to leave; when a sickly voice asked her if she would mind waiting a bit and help him. Shaun was feeling a bit under the weather, Jill was hesitant at first but knew her Aunt was busy with other chores. Jill made sure Shaun was okay, took great care of him and even fed him his snacks. Shaun was curious to know where she learnt to take care of kids his age; Jill mentioned that she has been taking care of her little brother from a young age since both her parents worked full time. Hearing about Jill and her family; Shaun soon realised that how lucky he was to have being born with a silver spoon. Soon Shaun became very fond of Jill and loved having her around. He mentioned about her family’s struggles to his parents as well. Shaun’s parents decided to sponsor her further education but Jill politely declined their offer and said she wanted to succeed the hard way and that her Aunt Matilda was her inspiration. Shaun was a bit upset but Jill made him realise that there are no shortcuts to success. Love, hope and dreams is what keeps life going. Life may seem like a struggle to most, but you dream of a better future for you and your loved ones; wake up everyday, hoping to work hard in getting through that one day; which ultimately is the bridge we built to manifesting our success. Shaun learned a lot from his new favourite person Jill; finally learnt that the joy is in sharing and seeing that happy smile on the other person’s face. Shaun saved a bit of his pocket money everyday and gifted Jill a brand new computer which would be helpful in her future but she agreed to accept only if it was donated to their community centre where everyone would be able to make good use of it. Just believe that sharing even a little will definitely make a lot of difference.
author: Ruby  Thomas

title: Floriography! What?!
text: Many years ago, people made up the language of flowers. The language of flowers is called floriography. If we know a little floriography, then we can give each other a flower to say something without saying a word! Let's get to know what some flowers around us, can say. Oh wow! The sweet smell of Jasmine! Our "ammas," "akkas," and many other women in our country love to wear jasmine in their hair. What can jasmine say? "You are beautiful." "You are important to me." "Good luck to you." Yooohoo! I am giving my "Nani" Jasmine today. Does she know floriography?! Nerium. This pretty looking flower says, "Be careful!" Hmmm! If amma or baba are in a bad mood, then I may show you a nerium! Look at this flower. Marigold. What did you think of? I thought of rangolis (welcome designs made on the floor,) torans (decorative garlands hung above the door,) festivals, new house, new car and many happy times. And what does this flower say? "Happiness to you!" "Good luck to you!" Take a deep breath. Where is the wonderful fragrance coming from? From the fragrant flower, frangipani. Who would like to be near this fragrant flower? And who would like health, wealth and happiness to be with them? Everyone! Gift frangipani to say, "Health, wealth and happiness to you!" "All the best!" "Best of luck!" "I wish you happiness!" When I feel you need these wishes, I will send you a hibiscus. In floriography, these are some of the sentences a red shoeflower (hibiscus) says. The meaning of a flower can be different in different parts of the world. A yellow rose may mean, "You are my very dear friend," in one place and "I am jealous of you," in another. It is good to learn floriography of new people before gifting them a flower. "Thank you!" says the pink rose. "I love you!" says the red rose. Pink and red roses to you for reading this book!
author: Shahin Ashraf Ali
illustrator: Hari Chandana  Gundimeda; Sree Devi Priya Mani

title: The Cut Hair
text: She runs very fast. Sometimes, Kia looked back to see if her mother and grandmother were still chasing her. She is always afraid every time she gets her hair cut. For Kia, cutting her hair is scary. After she ran far, she arrived at aunt Maya's house. She looked at Oren sitting looking at the twilight sky. Kia stands up beside Oren and does the same. Kia still feels afraid. She is Afraid of scissors touching her beautiful hair. From the kitchen, Aunt Maya greeted Kia gently. She knew why Kia had come here now that her grandmother had called her to tell her. Aunt gently touched Kia's head. Meanwhile, Kia says that she doesn't want to cut her hair. "Why you don't want to cut your hair?" said Aunt Maya after they were in the living room. "I am afraid, Aunt," said Kia in a slow voice. "Afraid? Afraid for what?" said Aunt Maya amazed. "I am afraid of scissors," said Kia softly. Her Aunt glared in shock. "Tell me why you are so afraid of scissors," said Aunt Maya. "I think scissors are like the head of a dinosaur that can swallow me," Aunt Maya smiled. Then Aunt Maya tells Kia that she must not be fearless with scissors. Scissors can not move if they don't move by a human. And scissors are different from a dinosaur which has teeth. Kia nods her head to show she understands. Kia promised after she went from Maya's house, she would ask her mother and grandmother to cut her hair which gets longer. She didn't want to bother with her long hair. Before she goes home, Kia gets a watermelon as a gift from Aunt Maya.

title: GOLD! GOLD! GOLD!
text: There was once a women called Sumu who loved gold than her family, friends, cousins and relatives. Her husband was very angry with her and scolded her but of no use. Sumu's love for gold was so fervent that slowly she started to sell things in the house in exchange of gold. Slowly this reached to the ears of a bandit who made plans to trick her and to take away her valubles. One day the bandit dressed up as a gold merchant to sell his merchandise. As he was passing through Sumu's house she ran out of the house and called the merchant. The merchant showed his gold. Sumu was very attracted to it and gave the thief fine cloth which was very valuable at that time. After sometime she was examining the gold when she suddenly realised that it was fake and it was a copper material on which gold was rubbed. She ran after the merchant but he left fast on his horse. Sumu told about the merchant to his husband who replied to her in a calm and kind way. Sumu then suddenly realised her husband's love to her which she never returned. She wept bitterly and told she would not repeat this again and change her behavior. Everyone who heard about the change in Sumu's behavior thanked the merchant even though he was a thief. Next day, Sumu gave a party to her family,friends and relatives who enjoyed it very well.
author: Sunil Pranavanand
