title: The Coconut
text: It was a bright sunny day in the fields of Haryana. Farmers had taken out their cows and buffaloes for grazing. Ram's mother came into his room with a glass of milk and started to wake him up. Ram sleepily said, "Maa please let me sleep 5 minutes more." But, his maa did not listen to him and asked him to quickly wake up and eat breakfast. Saying so Ram got up happily after listening to the name of food and went to the bathroom to brush his teeth. After that the boy went into the kitchen and asked his maa for food. He also asked for a cup of milk for the kittens that lived in the garden outside his house. Ram gave the milk to the kittens outside and started eating his hot 'Poha' while watching the kittens drink the milk happily. There were two kittens living in the garden. One was a brown and white one which he named Aamir and the ginger coloured one Adil. Even after eating his food Ram began to feel more hungry and went into the kitchen to look for some food. Just then his grandmother came in with a coconut and asked, "Ram my dear child what happened?" Ram answered while moving one of his hands on his stomach, "Daadi maa I am feeling very hungry even after eating my breakfast." Grandmother laughed out loud and said to this response, "You must be feeling more hungry if you were dehydrated. Here I have brought a coconut let me open this and give the fresh and tender coconut water to you." Ram's Grandmother broke the coconut and collected the water in a small steel utensil. She added it in a cup and gave it to Ram. After drinking the water Ram said, "Wow Daadi maa I don't feel hungry anymore is this magic?" Grandma laughed out loud and said, "No this is not magic but a blessing from the coconut farmers of South India!" THE END!
author: Samaira. Singh
illustrator: David Yambem; Isha  Mangalmurti; Jemma Jose; Rajiv Eipe; Samaira. Singh

title: Should I go there?
text: Today, while Anitha was going to school with her father, she heard a news from her dad. "Anitha, as I have to shift to a new place for work, you have to change your school" after hearing this Anitha was sad all day long. she told her friends about what her dad told. First Anitha was very sad. she would miss her friends. Yet she can still meet. during her holidays, she can go to Kanyakumari. Kanyakumari is her native place. Now she is going to Bangalore. Anitha is very sad that she is not even talking to her mom and dad! After sometime dad started a game. "let's play word building game!" said dad. Still Anitha didn't talk. the game went interesting and Anitha also wanted to play! so she joined them. she felt sleepy, so she decided to sleep. in the train an announcement was held. it said "please take you stuffs and be ready. the train reached Bangalore." after hearing this Anitha woke up. she got ready and got down from the train. she walked, walked and walked till the end of the train. she saw the train driver in the front. Soon, Anitha went to her home. do you know tomorrow is a special day for Anitha? Guess why? because she is going to meet new friends in her new school! As Anitha is a new student, in her new school, she has to dance. everybody is cheering for her. also few people become her friends. she felt happy and was no more shy to go to her new school!

title: The messy work we had done
text: We know that at some point, we did something crazy by playing or by accident. Like breaking the flower vase while playing football or flooding the house with water......We know, that after we do anything similar to that, we are very very worried. Why? Well, cause our parents will scold us now... So, most of us are afraid to tell our parents. but something terrible again happens... Well, something similar happened just yesterday... Go Ahead and read on... Read my story and find out, in such a situation should we inform our parents or not...... Whoa!!! so, terrible. Wonder what? Well, the paintbox of white paint tribbed over the carpet and got wet but my brother tried to clean himself without telling us and everything goes kazoos!! Confused?? Let me tell you the whole story... So it all began with......................... So, it all started a week ago... I was very fond of painting, I spend hours and hours on a single painting. it so happened that we had to go to our grandpa's house because he was unwell. that very morning I just finished my new painting when Mom called me to pack my bag. I kept all the things back in their respective places but I carelessly left the white paint tin open; well it wasn't open but half closed... We enjoyed the week in the village. Now we are back home. Now, on the other hand, my young brother Prateek was fond of making towers. He would make a tower on top of the bags or keep the toy cars on top of each other and whatnot. I think some of you can guess it, no, not that, yes you guessed that right! Prateek made a tower on my study table where the white paint was kept and started building a tower on top of that paint... Soon after that, It was dinner time and we were having our dinner suddenly we heard a loud noise of bang boom and bash!!! Prateek understood that the tower he made had tumbled down and made that noise. I said " I'll go and check on it. " Prateek got furious and said, " No no, no need didi... I can handle that." Then he ran into the room he entered the room to find out that something even more terrible than he thought had happened.. Know what?.... The thing is, he made the tower on the paint that was half closed fall on the carpet but that is not the problem. the paint had spilt at a large area of the carpet. Brother got nervous... Prateek came back to the dinner table and said " It's not a matter... The tower I made earlier had just fallen over no big deal. Let's eat" Then suddenly I noticed something white on Prateek's elbows knees and some on his toes... I asked him immediately " What is that white thing on your elbows?" Prateek replied, " Oh, I just had a little scratch so I applied some cream." I answered " Ok, now eat " but I knew he was hiding something so I remained silent. After dinner when I came out of the bathroom I saw Prateek getting scolded. As soon as I entered the room I was shocked! The carpet had been submerged in the white paint. Mother even scolded me. Know why? I'll come to that at the end. Dad didn't come to know about it. Soon, when we all came together in the living room, the talk about the carpet came out, and Dad learned about it. After Dad heard this, Dad and Mom explained to us that if anything bad happens then we should inform our parents about it whether they are at home or outside we can just call them up. This can be explained by another story about when I was little... When I was little, suppose 3 years old or less, then brother was born, he was only a few months old when my mother and father went on duty and I took care of my brother. One day my brother saw a glass vase with artificial flowers which he thought as candies in the showcase. Prateek wanted me to give him those flowers. but as I was little, I worried for my brother and that is why I didn't give him. It was our nap time, I was hardly awake but I finally dosed off. Then Prateek woke me up to show that same candy. I was surprised! I turned around near the mattress to see that the vase was broken and the fruit toys were on his hands I got so worried that I started crying, I lifted Prateek and took him to another room he was finally satisfied to get these things so he didn't tease me anymore. Luckily there was a phone in our house, I cried and called Mom for help. She got worried and said, " Good girl you informed me or else something could have happened to you as well as Prateek. It's almost time for us to leave we will come back soon dear.".... And So, Mother and Father told the story to Prateek to remind him... Now I come to the part, Why did mom scold me in the first place? Yes, that is right!! It is because I was the one who was careless and left the paint half closed...And for Prateek? Because he didn't inform all of us about the mess... The End... ---So remember--- i) Never be careless, always keep things in place. ii) Always inform parents or elders about everything bad that has happened.
author: AHAMTEERTWAA MAITY

title: Anku's Happy Sunday!
text: My name is Ankita. Everyone calls me Anku. I live in Himtal. It is a hilly village in Garhwal. I live here with Mummy, Papa and my little sister Soni. Sunday is my favorite day because there is no school. I can do many other things on Sunday. Sunday is my favorite day because there is no school. I can do many other things on Sunday. SUNDAY FINALLY! I go out to play with my friends Sakki and Akki. We play ‘Train Train’. Papa got me this toy train from Dehradun. Today our train is going to Almora. ‘Choo choo choo choo!’ Sakki Akki and I say as we play. I love my friends. I have so much fun with them. CHHOO! CHHOO! CHHOO! CHHOO! After playing, I go to the forest to get sticks for fire. I have to go very far. Sticks are not easy to find. When I come home I feel tired. I take a short nap. When I come home I feel tired. I take a short nap. SO TIRED Then I give my pet rabbit Guddu an orange carrot. I love to watch Guddu eat. ‘Crunch crunch crunch! Then I give my pet rabbit Guddu an orange carrot. I love to watch Guddu eat. ‘Crunch crunch crunch!’ CRUNCH!! CRUNCH!! On Sundays Mummy makes Halwa for us. Mummy asks me to comb Soni’s hair. I am very excited! Halwa: a sweet Indian dish consisting of carrots or semolina boiled with milk, almonds, sugar, butter, and cardamom. On Sundays Mummy makes Halwa * for us. Mummy asks me to comb Soni’s hair. I am very excited! * Halwa: a sweet Indian dish consisting of carrots or semolina boiled with milk, almonds, sugar, butter, and cardamom. OK! Her hair is long and curly. I start combing. ‘Ouch ouch ouch!’ she screams. When I grow up I want to be a hairstylist. OUCH! OUCH! LOOKS NICE YAY Every Sunday, I try new hairstyles on Soni. Soni looks most beautiful wearing a Sagar Choti. * I make one long Sagar Choti. Mummy looks pleased. *Sagar Choti: French braid Just like that my Sunday comes to an end, I feel happy and proud of myself. How do you spend your Sunday? SUNDAY FUNDAY Just like that my Sunday comes to an end, I feel happy and proud of myself. How do you spend your Sunday?
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: I Feel Safe When..
text: Anku and Soni are ready for school. It is a rainy day in the village. Mummy is worried about them. Her heart is beating fast. ‘Anku! Soni! Walk slowly and be careful today.’ ‘ Yes Mummy, do not worry we will take care,’ says Anku. ‘Ritu is also coming with us. We will be careful,’ says Soni. Ritu meets them outside. ‘Drip-drop drip-drop!’ The rain falls on their umbrella. ‘I always feel safe when I am with you two,’ says Soni. After school Anku, Soni, and Ritu are milking the cows. ‘What happened Ritu?’ asks Anku. ‘I was finishing my homework but Pranav, my younger brother, wanted to play. He asked me again and again. I got very angry at him. My chest felt heavy. Now I feel bad.’ ‘Sometimes I feel upset when Anku does not have time for me. Then she tells me the reason and I understand,’ says Soni ‘Soni is right, talk to him. If you tell him why you were busy he won’t be angry,’ says Anku. ‘Thank you Anku and Soni for listening. I feel loved when you listen to me. I can share everything with you two,’ says Ritu. Rohan never goes to the gaderas * alone. He is scared of falling. His body feels tight and he cannot swim. Mummy and Papa say that he can get hurt because of the big rocks. Today Rohan is with Sunil and Mohan. He is not scared. They swim and play in the river. ‘Splash splash splash!’ Rohan feels safe and his body is relaxed when he is with Sunil and Mohan. * Gaderas: small canals at the foot of the mountains Sunil comes home from school. Mummy has gone to the forest and Papa to work. Sunil waits for them to come back. Sunil does not know when they will come back. He feels alone and sad. His body feels tight and heavy. Suddenly his dog Tikki comes running at Sunil. 'Bhau Bhau Bhau!' barks Tikki. Sunil feels safe and his body feels light when he is with Tikki. In the evening Rohan, Sunil, Anku, Soni, and Ritu go to the forest. Rohan brings his goats and donkeys. Sunil brings his cows and Tikki. Anku and Soni come with their cows and Guddu with the rabbit. Ritu comes with a buffalo and goats. They talk, laugh, jump, and play with their animals. The forest has many wild animals but they feel safe together. What makes you feel safe?
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: We Have Grown so Much!
text: Ankita, Ritu, Rohan, and Sunil are sitting in class. Asma Madam is announcing the exam results. Ankita takes the papers from Madam. She is scared to check her marks but she tells herself, ‘It’s okay I will not make the same mistakes next time.’ ‘Yay yay yayy I passed!’ she happily tells Ritu. Asma Madam calls the students who are selected for Sports Day. Rohan really wants to play for the school team. He tells himself ‘I tried my best, it is okay even if I am not selected.’ Then Asma Madam calls his name and Sunil’s name. ‘Hurray hurray hurray!’ says Rohan feeling excited. Asma Madam calls the students who are selected for Sports Day. Rohan really wants to play for the school team. He tells himself ‘I tried my best, it is okay even if I am not selected.’ Then Asma Madam calls his name and Sunil’s name. ‘Hurray hurray hurray!’ says Rohan feeling excited. Harsh rushes to Ritu. Trr trr trr ‘Harsh Bhaiya, why are you so excited?’ asks Ritu. ‘Ahaha, I will be helping our school students for the Art for Change competition in Almora,’ says Harsh excitedly. ‘Wow that is great!’ says Ritu. Ritu is proud of her brother. When Harsh Bhaiya first started painting he would drop colours everywhere. He would not finish any paintings, but start a new one everyday. Now Harsh Bhaiya knows what he likes to paint and enjoys painting more. Anku is happy that she passed but she wants to study harder for her next exam. She tells her mother about her plan. ‘Mummy, I have decided to study every day from 3-5 in the afternoon,’ says Anku. ‘That’s a good plan Anku. Remember Anku you can always ask for help,’ tells her mother. ‘Sunil, will you practice with me everyday?’ asks Rohan. ‘Yes Rohan, we are good but we can do better. We need to practice to win,’ says Sunil. ‘Okay then I will meet you at 6 o’clock tomorrow morning outside your house,’ says Rohan. In the next month, Anku and Rohan both work very hard. Anku studies for two hours. Sometimes when she does not understand something, she asks Mummy, Ritu, and Asma Madam to help her. Anku now knows a lot about India’s history. After studying, Anku practices different hairstyles on Ritu. Now Anku knows how hairstyles can look very different on different types of hair. Everyone hears the Thak thak thak of Rohan’s bat before the Coo coo coo of the hens. Sometimes when he does not want to wake up, Sunil knocks at his door and pulls him out of bed. Knock knock knock knock Practicing everyday has helped Rohan. He does not get tired even after making 50 runs. He is sure that they will win the match. Anku and Rohan learnt so much by practicing. What steps have you taken to grow?
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: What Can Rohan Do?
text: Pranam, my name is Rohan. I am from Timki, a village on the banks of Ganga. This year I started grade seven. As I am growing older, I am learning many things about myself. Does this happen to you too? Today is Tuesday. On Tuesdays, I have Math classes. All my friends are good at Math but I find numbers very confusing. When I add two and two and when I multiply two into two the answer is the same funny four. But when I write five into five equals ten, a teary ten looks at me confused. Why is ten sad? Did I do something wrong? In class Rana Sir gives us test results. I only get. I can’t understand Math. I never want to do Math again. At home, I try to solve the test again. The numbers look sad and tired. I give up. Mohan, my brother, asks me to show him how to hold the cricket bat. Our friend Sunil throws the ball. I show Mohan the right way to hold the bat. Thak Thak Thak. I hit one six and two fours. ‘Yayy! Bhaiya you are so good! You have to practice with me everyday,’ says Mohan. ‘Rohan you have to be in my team this Sunday. Please please please,’ says Sunil. ‘Okay okay,’ I tell both of them. They were right. I can’t do Math but I can play cricket. What are some other things I can do? I can also swim in the Ganga. Woosh Woosh Woosh I can also take care of our cows and goats. Moo Moo Mehh Mehh I can climb the mountains quickly. Zoom Zoom Zoom I can grow Rajma for my village. Thud Thud Thud I feel very proud of myself. If I can do so many things then I can also ask for help. Tomorrow I will ask Rana Sir to help me with Math. Then when we play cricket I will count my own runs. Tell me what are the things you can do?
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: What Did You Learn about Your Friends?
text: Today, in Art class Asma Ma’am divides the class into groups. Anku, Rohan, Ritu, and Sunil are in one group. ‘You can make anything you like. You only have to work as a team,’ says Asma Madam. ‘What do you want to make?’ asks Rohan. Our School What do you want to make? An airplane A Flower ‘I want to make a big flower,’ says Ritu. ‘But I want to draw our school,’ says Anku. ‘And I want to make an airplane. What will we do now?’ asks Rohan. I listen to all my friends and makes sure they are comfortable to share their ideas. ‘Let us make everything!’ says Sunil. ‘Great idea! Sunil always finds a way to accept everyone’s ideas,’ says Rohan. Everyone removes their brushes and colours except Anku. She gave them to Soni. They share a box of colours. Anku feels shy to ask for colours from others. ‘Here Anku, take this. Do you want to paint?’ says Ritu. ‘Thank you Ritu for sharing your colours. You always understand what I want,’ says Anku. ‘I am your friend, don't feel shy to ask me,’ says Ritu. I am not afraid to ask for help from my friends! I like to share things with my friends! ‘Hahaha what is this?’ says Veer. ‘I am making flowers,’ says Sunil. ‘These look like snakes,’ says Veer. Sunil feels upset and angry. Veer always laughs at everyone. I believe in my friends even when they don't believe in themselves. ‘Rohan, my flowers look like snakes. I cannot draw them. Will you draw flowers for me?’ asks Sunil. ‘They don’t look like snakes,’ says Rohan. ‘I can teach you how to draw flowers,’ says Ritu. ‘Remember Asma Madam said we have to do this together’ says Anku. Anku, Ritu, and Rohan all motivate Sunil to draw flowers. Ritu teaches Sunil. They make many flowers around the school building. ‘What did you learn about your friends today?’ asks Asma Madam. ‘I learned that Sunil adjusts and brings our ideas together,’ says Rohan. ‘Ritu is always ready to share. I can ask for her help,’ says Anku. ‘My friends support me. They teach me new things,’ says Sunil. ‘I feel confident and safe when I work with my friends,’ says Rohan. What did you learn about your friends today? They all feel loved after today’s art class. They give each other a big group hug. How do you feel when you work with your friends?
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: There's a way
text: We couldn't forget that moment of pandemic due to corona. Many of us lost our near and dear ones. Some lost their parents also. That time was very crucial. At that time there were two girls who lost their parents. And now they don't have any other person in their life. They were studying well but due to they lost their parents they couldn't continued their studies. After some days. All the money of them were also finished. They couldn't eat twice in a day. They asked for money from some people, but no one helped them because they are not able to return to them. Then suddenly one day they got a gold ring of their mother in the house. They want to start a business by which they can earn some money to save their. But they have no idea to start from where and how. One day, both off them went to the jewellery shop and sold that ring of their mother and got some money. They buy grocery items for the house and little sister said didi I am very hungry please make something for me. Then the elder one said wait a minute I will make some paratha for you After making paratha they both sat to eat those parathas and then suddenly younger sister thought of selling parathas and she said that idea to her elder sister. She became very happy by listening her idea. Then they thought where they can sell paratha. They thought in their village all are making their foods by their own, and no one will buy from them. One day they went to a railway station near to their village. They saw there are only two shops which are selling some biscuits and other one is selling some samosas. They asked those shopkeepers can start a new shop near to them and they both said yes you can start. Although this place is government place. By taking permission you can open you shop. Then both sisters went to government office and took the permission and started their shop of variety of parathas with tea and some snacks. After selling tasty parathas they became famous in their area. They earn a lot of money and started continuing their. They lived hapilly.

text: Di suatu rumah di tengah hutan, hiduplah seekor beruang bernama Bean. Ini orang tua Bean, sudah meninggal beberapa tahun lalu karena wabah penyakit. title: The Mean Lion
text: Once a lion a very mean lion wandered in to a jungle and saw a rabbit. He asked" Who is the king of this jungle?" "Nobody." The rabbit said worriedly. "Great. I hereby declare my self king. "You can't just do that." said the rabbit. "I just did!" said the lion. The next day he went to a cave and told the fox "Get out! I am the king I need a place to live!" and threw the fox's cubs out the cave and ate the meat the fox collected. The fox went to the rabbit he thought of a plan. One day he saw the rabbit crying and the rabbit said "There is another lion and he says he is the king of the jungle." "Show me who is it!" said the lion He pointed in the well. The lion went to check he saw his reflection but he didn't know so he went into the well to fight him and tried to find him. But he couldn't swim and he drowned. Moral of the story: No bad deed goes unpunished

title: How Do I Grow from My Mistakes?
text: Everyone in school is getting ready for Annual Day. Asma Madam works on the decorations. ‘Sunil, you make red and blue flags. Anku, can you make a big poster that reads ‘Annual Day’? ‘Yes Madam!’ says Anku feeling excited. ‘Okay bring it to school tomorrow morning!’ says Asma Madam feeling proud of her students. At home Anku paints the poster. Anku works on it all afternoon. She keeps the poster out in the sun for it to dry. In the evening, Anku comes to take the poster. She finds Guddu the rabbit sitting on it. ‘Oh no Guddu!’ she says. The poster has Guddu’s footprints on it. Anku starts crying. She feels worried. ‘I should not have put it out. What will I tell Asma Madam tomorrow?’ Anku is upset with herself. After some time Anku stops crying. ‘I made a mistake but I can make the poster again. Ritu and Soni will help me. I should be kind to myself and ask for help,’ thinks Anku. Anku asks Ritu and Soni to help. Together they work faster. The new poster is more colourful and bright. They all feel proud when the poster is complete. ‘Thank you Ritu and Soni,’ Anku says feeling grateful. Rohan comes home late from school. Mohan is playing with the goats. ‘Bhaiya bhaiya, will you play cricket with me?’ asks Mohan feeling excited. ‘No Mohan, stop asking me everyday! Go play with other friends. I am tired,’ shouts Rohan. Mohan feels surprised and leaves. Mehh Mehh Mehh Rohan sits with his goats. ‘Oh no! Why did I get so angry at Mohan?’ Rohan asks himself and his goats, feeling sad and tired. ‘I am busy but I should have told Mohan that. He must be feeling angry. I don’t want to hurt anyone with my actions. I will talk to him,’ thinks Rohan. ‘Sorry Mohan, I should not have shouted at you. You just wanted to play with me but I got very tired after dance practice,’ says Rohan. ‘It’s okay Bhaiya, I understand,’ says Mohan. ‘After tomorrow we can play cricket every day!’ says Rohan feeling happy. ‘Yayy! We can play tomorrow!’ says Mohan. On the Annual Day, everyone feels excited. Asma Madam loves Anku’s posters and Sunil’s flags. All the parents have come to school. They enjoy the children’s dance. Anku, Rohan, Sunil, and Ritu feel very proud after the Annual Day.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: Favorite Pastime
text: What activity do you enjoy doing whenever you are free? Tanu's didi loves to read books. Her favorite pastime is reading books. If you call and she does not answer, then know she is lost in some book! Tanu's bhaiya and his friends love folkdance. Their favorite pastime is learning, practicing and doing different kinds of folkdance. Tanu says, "Bhaiya sings folksongs and dances in his sleep!" Tanu's ma loves growing flowers and herbs. Her favorite pastime is gardening. Tanu says, "When the flowers bloom, ma is very happy. Ma uses the herbs to cook tasty food. The flowers and herbs at home smell so good. We all feel happy." Tanu's baba runs a bakery. When he was young, baking was his favorite pastime. Today baba's favorite pastime is his business! Young Tanu's favorite pastime is helping baba in the bakery. Don't be surprised if Tanu comes to deliver the cake you ordered from her baba's bakery. Tanu says, "You will not hear me say that I am feeling bored, any time. Because, I have a happy pastime!" I agree with Tanu. Do you?
author: Shahin Ashraf Ali

title: The Lonely Octopus
text: I'm a little octopus and I'm sad in my reef. I see dolphins have friends. and seals also have friends. Even turtles swim together in the ocean. whereas I always swim alone. Why am I the only one lonely? I'm currently swimming alone and Oh! Look! there were several octopuses huddled together. It is the coming together of octopuses from everywhere, they are telling stories of exciting experiences. they tell many stories. like the story of one octopus who once talked to a really old sea turtle. or the story of an octopus who once saw a group of beautiful starfish. there was even an octopus that was almost attacked by a shark! I should have realized that actually I am not alone because there are many fish that I meet. Whether on the reef or in the open ocean. I have met a group of seahorses. I have also met a very shy squid. I even once met a very big whale! i am a little octopus, and i am not so sad anymore. For even though I travel on my own, I am never truly alone.

title: Did You Decide?
text: We make decisions every day. We decide what actions to take to achieve our goals. We decide to stop doing unimportant activities. When there are many paths in front of us, we decide and choose the path that gives us happiness and success. Let us look at a few decisions that people take. Neela was getting late to the office. She will not reach the office on time if she takes the public bus. So, she decided to go by auto. Manju could not decide which colour dress to wear to the party. Red, blue, pink, or yellow? Finally, she decided to wear a pink dress. What to do this Sunday evening? Shall we go to a restaurant or go for a picnic? We decided to go for a picnic in the nearby park. Mom decided to cook pooris for breakfast on Mondays. Shall we go to the theatre to watch an action movie or a cartoon film? We decided to watch a movie at home. Is Mallika a nice girl? Yes, she is. So, I decided to be friends with her.

title: The Helpful Dolphin and the Selfish Shark
text: In the ocean, there lived a helpful dolphin who was known for his kindness and generosity. One day, a selfish shark approached the dolphin and asked him for help. The shark said, "I have injured my fin, and I can't swim properly. Can you help me reach the other side of the ocean?" The dolphin agreed to help and carried the shark on his back. As they were swimming, the shark started to attack the dolphin, trying to kill him. The dolphin was surprised and asked the shark why he was doing this. The shark replied, "I am a predator, and you are my prey. I only asked for your help to get closer to my next meal." The dolphin was disappointed and hurt by the shark's betrayal. He realized that not everyone is kind and helpful like him, and he learned to be more cautious and mindful of the people he helps.

title: A Call
text: He has been thinking a lot about and is unable to understand why cell phones take over the attention of adults. It is as if they hipnotize them, being unable to detach the device from their hand. He can’t see all the drawings that he would like. They also don't allow him to touch his parents' tablets or cell phones. They tell him over, and over, and over again that being in front of screens for a long time should be avoided, because it will be difficult for him to focus later on, since he is so small. Additionally -they insist- "the best things in the world happen off-screen." It is true that he would also be stuck on others' cell phones, especially when it came to those cool videos that Uncle Miguel would put on, until Mom set schedules for Luna to watch them. "When will there be schedules for the grown-ups?" he thought, annoyed. A few days ago in class, his teacher had explained what coherence meant. Lu, very attentive, then remembered some moments that lacked logic and led to him to the conclusion that what adults say -and later do- with respect to screens is not coherent. "Luna, when in front of a traffic signal we are to be very attentive to the color so we know if we can cross. Not doing so would be very dangerous" said Dad while going for a walk through the city. Well... w hile walking hand in hand on the way back to school, Luna alerted: -"Green Dad, it's green!" Dad was looking at his phone and had not paid attention. "Luna, we don't play at the table. Mealtime is a time to sit down, eat, and talk as a family." His parents taught him one Sunday while with his nana and poppa. Well… the other day at lunch, Luna had to ask: "Can we start eating?" His parents were teleworking from their cell phones. "A game at the stadium is an incredible thing, honey. It's nothing like watching it on TV. The atmosphere, the excitement, seeing the field from another side...everything is special" Mom told him enthusiastically. Well… yesterday Luna went to the stadium for the first time and had to tell his mom how the first goal had been, because she was posting a story. Today is Sunday. After all this, Lu has decided to take matters into his own hands: he snuck into his parents' room and grabbed their cell phones, also grabbing recycled paper, scissors, tape, a ruler, markers and with a lot of patience and care has made paper glasses. But he has not stopped there, on another paper he has drawn many cell phone screens with an open chat window and has written messages within many important 'notifications'. His parents have just woken up, they missed their little devices and while looking for them have found the crafts Luna made. They read the notes left in the form of notifications and realized that they got a call, a wake-up call. Luna worried that they might have gotten upset or taken it the wrong way, but it was far from that. His parents hugged him TIGHTLY between the two of them and have also, humbly, given him a nice lesson. Parents sometimes make mistakes too.

title: Nobody Cares But I Do
text: In a village called Manthra, there lived a sweet girl called Roopa. She loved nature. But sadly in her village nobody knew the significance of plants and animals. They just thought of them as a way to make ends meet. They did not know that even plants lived like human beings. Rupa knew it, so she cared. Her cottage was near a plant field. She loved to take care of the plants there. One day, she saw some naughty kids come to the field. They started plucking flowers. She didn't like it so she told them to stop, but they didn't listen. She started yelling at them, but again, no effect. The children went with a bunch of flowers for throwing at each other. Roopa became very sad. When Ramu came and saw the flowers missing, he blamed Roopa. She could not say anything but just hear the scoldings of the farmer. Roopa went home crying. Her mother consoled her. She knew it wasn't her fault. After eating dinner Roopa slept. The next day Roopa woke up with a new start. She'd forgotten all about yesterday and was ready to head towards the field for a walk. Later she watered the plants in the area and also in her garden. Soon the scorching heat arrived in mid-summer. Ramu was too lazy to even take care of his field. But as always Roopa was the saviour for the plants. Even in such hot weather, she used to go to the field every day to water and take care of the plants. Ramu just sat back at home. Roopa was full of tans. Her parents always stopped her but she wouldn't listen. Nobody even looked at the hardworking from the corner of their eyes. When summer came to an end, Ramu came to finally work in the fields. To his surprise, the field was full of green, healthy plants. He'd expected to find the field with the scorched plants. He was very happy but also curious to know who did it. He felt a bit thirsty so to quench his thirst, he went to Roopa's cottage. After drinking a glass of water, he asked about Roopa. Her mother led Ramu to Roopa's room. Roopa was lying in the bed. So weak. She was not even able to open her eyes. She was sick because of dehydration, and the hotness of the Sun. Roopa's mother told about how she got sick by taking care of the field. Ramu felt very bad for the girl. There was no food to feed the girl. He couldn't see his savior so weak. Ramu gave half the product of his crops to Roopa's family. soon, with enough nutrients Roopa recovered. She went to thank Ramu. Ramu was happy to see her again. When Roopa thanked her, Ramu said "Don't thank me, thank yourself instead it is your hardwork which helped you in your bad times." Everyone was happy as there were more crops this time. It was because of their savior Roopa!

title: A tree of stars
text: Once upon a time, there was a seed in a forest that was barely about to sprout its first leaves. It was profoundly excited to finally meet the world. One day an ant who was building his tunnel came by and the seed asked him: " Little ant, you know the world up there, tell me what is the most beautiful?" The ant excitedly told him: There are many beautiful things in this world. Flowers exist, blueberries, acorns. But what I like the most are the stars because they shine like little diamonds." The illusioned seed answered: -When I grow I want to be a tree of stars. "Little seed, the stars don't hang from the trees but from the sky."- The ant explained From that day on the seed, spent its days imagining excitedly, how life would be if it could be a star. As time went by, the seed sprouted from the Earth and became a small plant. Anxiously, she waited for the arrival of the night to meet the stars. When she saw them for the first time, her small leaves trembled. "Theyre beautiful!" She exclaimed in wonder. A beetle who was trying to sleep in a bush nearby woke up from the big commotion. " Is everything okay, little plant?" Asked the scared beetle - I apologize, today is the first time I see the stars and now that I have met them, I know that one day I will be a tree so tall that I will be able to caress the stars with my branches- The somewhat incredulous beetle explained to her- " The stars are beautiful, they always make me happy in the darkness of the night. But they live very, very high in the sky. No matter how high I've flown, I have never been close to reaching them. The beetles words did not discourage the little plan. Every day she struggled to grow and grow. With her roots she looked for the best nutrients and little by little she grew bigger until she transformed in to a young tree. One day, a bird began to create its nest in the branches of the young tree. As she watched him build his nest, the young tree asked him: -Bird, you who flies higher than the pines, have you ever met a star? -No, young tree I have never flown that high, but the stars always guide my flight at night, they help me not get lost at night._ With each new thing the young tree learned about the stars, she wanted to know more and more about them. Months passed by and although the young tree struggled to grow, she no longer grew taller. She would stretch her branches, move her roots but couldn't grow more. One day, something surprising happened, apples began to grow from her branches. They were bright red, in all the forest, all the animals came to see such beautiful apples. The rabbit and the caterpillar said they were the best they ever tasted. But the young tree who discovered was that she was an apple tree was not happy about the surprising event. He wanted to be a tall tree so she could meet the stars. But to the surprise of everyone in the forest, He was an apple tree. The only apple tree in all of the forest, the shortest tree in the entire forest. The traveler's who were crossing the forest, noticed the beautiful red glow of the apples and their rich flavor and began to take short breaks under the branches of the apple tree. Even so, every night the apple tree looked at the sky and was full of sadness gazing at the stars. One night the ant, worried to see his friend the apple tree so sad, he told him: -"Dear apple tree, don't be sad, your apples are a beautiful gift. They are the brightest red color I have ever seen and their flavor makes everyone who eats them happy. All the animals in the forest love you and take care of you. You even help humans not get lost along the way through the forest and give them a comfortable place to rest." With the ants words, the apple tree rejoiced. Although she was disappointed that she was not taller and could not meet the stars, she decided to strive to make the richest and most beautiful apples possible. One day a traveler and his daughter sat down to rest under the shade of the apple tree. The girl after eating with her father, began climbing the branches. While playing among the branches, she picked apples to continue their journey. Suddenly an apple fell to the ground and broke in half. The girl hurried down from the tree to see the apple that had fallen. Surprised, she ran to show her dad what she had found inside the apple. -" Dad, look a star, the apple has a star inside!" The apple tree that was listening carefully could not believe what she was hearing and seeing. All her life she had struggled to meet the stars without realizing that within her, beautiful apples there were stars. Stars that shone, that cheered and guided travelers on their way. In the end the apple tree had managed to be a tree of stars. Short story based on "The apple that wanted to be a star"
author: Jasmine Negrete

title: A Call
text: He has been thinking a lot and he still cannot understand why cell phones have taken over adults’ gaze so much. It is as if they were hypnotized, unable to peel the device out of their hands. He cannot watch all the cartoons he would like to. His parents do not let him touch their tablets or cell phones either. They repeat, repeat, repeat that he should avoid spending too much time in front of screens because, being so young, it will be hard for him to concentrate in the future. Additionally, they insist, "the best things in the world happen outside of the screens." It is true that he also used to become absorbed in other people's cell phones, especially with those cute videos that Uncle Miguel used to play, until his mom scheduled times when Luna could watch them. "And when will there be scheduled times for adults?" he thought very upset. A few days before, the teacher had explained in class what consistency meant. Lu attentively recalled some moments that did not make much sense and came to the conclusion that adults are not consistent with what they say, and do, about the screens. "Luna, in front of the traffic light we are very attentive to the color to know if we can cross. Not doing so would be very dangerous," said his dad walking through the city. But hey! Walking hand in hand back to school Luna warned: "Green, Dad, it's green!" His dad was looking at his phone and was not paying attention. "Luna, there is no playing at the dinner table. Mealtime is for sitting, eating and chatting as a family,” his parents had taught him one Sunday with the yayos. But hey! The other day at lunch, Luna had to ask, "Can we start?" The parents were working from their cell phones. "A game at the stadium is an amazing thing, honey. It's nothing like watching it on TV. The atmosphere, the excitement, seeing the field from a different angle... everything is special," his mom had told him enthusiastically. But hey! Yesterday Luna went to the stadium for the first time and had to tell his mom about the first goal because she was posting a story. Today is Sunday. After everything, Lu has decided to take matters into his own hands: he snuck into his parents' room and took their cell phones, he took recycled paper, scissors, tape, ruler, markers and with a lot of patience, care, and dedication, made a pair of paper glasses. But he had not stopped there, on another piece of paper he drew several cell phone screens with a chat window open and wrote messages inside as several important “notifications". As soon as the parents woke up, they missed their small devices and when they looked for them, they found Luna's craftwork. They read the notes, in the form of a notification, and understood that they had a call, but it was a wake-up call. Luna was afraid that they might get angry or take it the wrong way, but far from it, the parents hugged him STRONGLY between the two of them and humbly had taught him a nice lesson as well. title: The angel
text: I GHOSE, Jayesh Sivan, Mitrarun Halder, Nivong Sengsakoun, Srishti Sharath Once upon, there was girl named Radha. She was from a poor family. She was dumb. She lost her mother after few hours of her birth. When she was 2 years old her father died in a bus accident. After her father's dead she lived with her Mamu and Mami. They did not have any child. Her Mami was very miser and selfish. She did not like Radha. But, her Mamu treated her like his own daughter. Her Mamu usually go out for his job. In the absence of Radha's Mamu, her Mami used to do all the house hold work by Radha only. Radha did all the work that her Mami tells to do. She thought that Mami is like my mother, then how can I disobey my mother. In the age playing with friends she used to do the household work. Her friend's also did not like her because she cannot speak. They insulted a lot against Radha. Sometime they used to make fake complains against Radha to her Mami. Her Mami became angry and lock her inside the store room. After few days, Radha's Mamu shifted to another place with his wife and Radha. There they got a house in rent. One day when Radha was flying her kite in the sky her kite falls at her neighbour's terrace. There was girl in the terrace of her neighbour. The girl returned it to Radha. By showing gesture Radha asked the girl about her name. The girl can understand that what Radha is trying say and answered that her name was Anushka. By writing on the floor by the use of a stone Radha tell her about herself. They became very good friend. They treated each other like sisters. Anushka had no problem that Radha is dumb. They usually go out for a cycle ride in the morning. They both enjoyed a lot with each other. One day like always they both where riding the cycle. Radha went ahead and Anushka left behind. After some time when Radha looked behind and search for Anushka. A man came and closed her mouth with the help of a cloth and put her into a sack. Radha became sense less. When Radha opened her eyes she was in a dark, locked room and her hands and legs were tied with ropes. She was scared a lot. She shouted a lot "help, help". Then suddenly a man come and told her not to shout. If she will shout he will shoot her with his gun and went away. After some time she got a piece of glass in the side of her. She tried to get it to her hand which was tied to her back. Somehow she cut the ropes and Get out of that place. She ran and ran. And in the mid way she realized that she can speak. Not making delay she reached directly to Anushka's house and knocked at her door. A lady came. Radha asked her in hurry that "where is Anushka? And who are you?” The lady answered that I am Anushka's mother and told that "Anushka! She is dead since five months. I think you did not know about her death". And Radha was looking at the lady surprisingly and went to her home. When her cute Mamu and miser Mami get to know that Radha can speak now, they became very happy. And they all lived a good life. But Radha's only question that is in her that "who was Anushka? Is she was a human or an angel." The moral of the story is good deeds can change our life
author: Tanaya Tripathy
illustrator: Dakshata Singh; Iddi  Marumba; Jayesh Sivan; JOSMI GHOSE; Mitrarun Halder; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Srishti Sharath

title: Name Your Age
text: The number of years that have passed from the date of your birth is called age. A person in a particular age group has a name or term. Let us learn about them. Birth to 1 month old – Neonates or Newborns 1 month to 1 year – Infants 1 year to 12 years – Children 13 years to 17 years – Adolescents or Teenagers 18 years or older – Adults 60 years and above – Senior Citizens 80 years and above – Super Senior Citizens

The raven asked to the swan how are you? the swan told no many tourist are disturbing by taking pick and some of them are stealing my eggs and making them as pets, but you raven is so free. The raven smiled little and went. Then the raven asked peacock asked how are you? the peacock told no many tourist are disturbing by taking pick and some of them are stealing my eggs and making them as pets, but you raven is so free. title: PANDA
text: We are in china. This is the barrier of china [The Great Wall Of China]. Pandas live in china. We will see the bamboo forest and meet panda. Now let us see the bamboo forest. Let us go deeper and meet P anda. He is an annoying but cute panda. Here is Panda. Panda will show you the way to the village. Have fun with him. You will be here for one day. First Panda will take you for a tour in his village. He will tell you his friends and introd uce you to them. First, Panda will take you for a tour in his village. He will tell you about his friends and introduce you to them.. First let us see Pluffy. This is my friend Pluffy. He is my neighbor, we play all day play play play. This is Rose and Love. You can always understand between Rose and Love. Rose holds a rose flower and Love holds a heart. This way we can understand anyone. This is Taby. He is addicted to phones. We play video games. It is so fun. Now I will show my house. First is the bedroom,I have fun there. Next is the kitchen, I cook food there. Then is my washroom. I bath, brush and wash my hands there. Last is the living room, I watch TV and there is a dining table too. Okay what should we do now.... I'm hungry. Oh we should make some food for lunch. Let us see on the menu. Do you want noodles or pasta? okay noodles and bamboo soup or masala? Okay so you selected bamboo soup and noodles.... superb. This is a cooking manual. It has recipes in it. let's cook noodles and bamboo soup. I love them, you will like it too. Now we can eat noodles and soup. Oh...., I forgot to tell you about the lantern festival, it is today. Did you notice the paper lanterns hanging in the village and at my home. Yayyyy..., we can celebrate now. Here is the plan. Lets go down and have some fun with friends. In the evening there are lion and dragon dances. In the night we will eat dinner by watching TV and then we sleep. The next morning you will go home. The celebrations have not started yet. Let us play video games with friends and play play play play play...all day. Its celebration time.... see the colorful and wonderful lion and dragon dance. It is night time,let us eat dinner and sleep. it is early in the morning.Bye bye visitors see you next time.
author: Meher Anvita
illustrator: Barkha Lohia; Ketki Bedekar; Meher Anvita; Shivam Thapliyal

title: Nikhil and the One-eyed Timor truck
text: Paru and I love going to school. We have amazing teachers and good friends. Then one day, there was a big storm. Our school building was old. The storm was strong. A part of the wall and the roof fell down. We could not attend classes there. My friends and I were sad. Our teachers were sad too. They said, "We will build it up again, but we need to build it up soon." A builder started building up the school. "Will it be ready in time for our classes? " "Yes, of course!" said the builder to Preethi ma'am, " We can work night shifts too." That was when we had a problem....from the construction vehicles.... The vehicles helped us build the school. They zoomed to and fro, bringing tons and tons of bricks, loads of cement and wood to the school building site. Then the builder told them, " We need to build faster! Will you work at night too?" They looked scared. They refused to work at night. They chorused, " No! No! Never! The One- Eyed Timor Truck will get us!" We were puzzled. " Who is that?" asked Preethi ma'am. ﻿ " He is a huge Monster!" squealed Rocky, the forklift. "He comes out at night. He has but one eye, and when that eye falls on a poor vehicle, he smashes him to pulp." said the tempo, shivering. " Please do not make us work at night," the construction vehicles begged. We were worried because we saw that the builder and Preethi ma'am were worried too. Then I had an idea! " Paru, why don't we get Nikhil to help us?" "Who is that, Tarun? " asked Preethi ma'am. "Ma'am, Nikhil is in II standard. He loves everything on wheels. Let us ask him to help us." So we asked Nikhil to help us to talk to the One- Eyed Truck. " Isn't he the one who stays at the old shed near the tracks?, " he asked, "His name is Timor. I will go and see him. My Dad will help me too." We saw Nikhil open the gate of Timor's shed and slip inside. He carried a bag with him. We waited and worried. 'Would Timor agree to be good? Or would he hurt Nikhil too? ' From within the shed came loud noises. Clang! Bang! Scrap! Then we heard the truck start!!! The gates flew open! We opened our eyes wide in fear! Timor, the huge and scary One-eyed trunk drove out with Nikhil and his dad. Surprise! The truck was not One-eyed anymore. Two bright yellow headlights blazed ahead into the night. "Come along and get in!" called Nikhil from within the truck. We tiptoed up to him. The other vehicles were watching us too. They were puzzled. " How did you do it, Nikhil?" I whispered. " I knew he wasn't bad" said Nikhil, fondly patting the truck. Timor hooted his horn in response. " You see, he was One-eyed because his light was not working. He could not see where he was going. He got into accidents" We gasped. " Yes. Dad helped me to fit in new headlights and he is not 'One-eyed' anymore. Timor is sorry and eager to help us." The construction vehicles tooted in glee. And so, Timor helped us in bringing building materials. All the vehicles were delighted too. They built us the school, just in time for our classes. Wasn't that just great? Preethi ma'am was happy. We were happy too. She said, " Good work, Nikhil. You remembered that what we fear might not be scary at all, when we face it." "Good thinking, Tarun and Paru. You thought of a way to get our school ready on time!" Wasn't that wonderful of her? Now it is time for school. Oh! What fun we will have! Trring! Trring!
author: Ilavenil Karunakaran
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Jesse  Breytenbach; Jupiter  Pradhan; Marleen  Visser; Melany  Pietersen; Mohith O; Ntibile Zonke  o hweditše; Rob Owen; Siddhi   Vartak

title: Noni learns to read !!
text: Welcome! to Noni's house her real name was Ankita but when she was little, she can's spell her name correctly, so that's why everyone call her noni, she love every physical activity but doesn't like to study because she can't read properly so how she will understand that? She loves open and fresh air,To at least understand what's written, anyone reads it and she understands. ﻿One time her parents took her to the doctor they thought that it was a disease, but that wasn't, whenever noni sits to study she can't. This problem every time increases, then one day her father thought that I have to teach her to read or how she will be able to manage when she grows up and study in bigger classes. One day her father took her in her bedroom and sat on the bed with noni's books, and called her to come into the bedroom of hers. Then her father told her that if you can't speak the word and if it seem to be difficult for you then break the letters and then read and try to speak that word. Always remember this pattern Word = Sentence = Paragraph = Reading. Or if you are not able to read in closed environment then go to the backyard. Now when she applied this trick it worked and now she created her own trick to remember and read things by fresh mind and she learned and pronounced animals, insects and the names of birds too. Her father was also happy to teach her child how to read. Now noni can Read and learn and understand herself even without going to the backyard even!! All is well, that ends well!!!
author: CHHAVI GUPTA

title: Dolphin is a good friend
text: I am a dolphin, and I have many friends like me. Look, some of my friends are over there, I'll be right over to them. We are animals that like to be together, swimming through the sea. When we were swimming together, we suddenly heard a cry for help. Then we immediately approached the source of the sound. Then we found a fisherman with a broken boat. We immediately helped him by lifting the boat and swimming together to bring the boat and fisherman to the shore... and swimming together to bring the boat and fisherman to the shore. After reaching the seaside, we said goodbye to the sea by flapping our tails as a sign of farewell.
author: Adinda Nuril

title: The terror of the lion
text: One day a big tree fell in front of the rabbit’s hole. The rabbit started thinking about how to remove the tree. Just then, he saw an elephant and walked up to it. The rabbit said to the elephant, “O elephant, my brother! I have heard you have a lot of strength!” The elephant replied, ‘Yes, so what?” To annoy the elephant the rabbit said, “Yet you are not as strong as I am.” "Prove it then!", the elephant replied. The rabbit said, “You pick up the tree and keep it by the side. Then I will keep it back where it is now.” back where it is now.” The elephant effortlessly moved the heavy tree to the side and said, ”Now it is your turn”. The rabbit pretended to move back the tree and said, “O heck! This is too heavy! I will not be able to move it. You are really strong.” The elephant was pleased to be praised. This is how the clever rabbit got the job done by the elephant. A few days after this, a fierce lion came to the jungle and was pleased to see so many animals. He said to himself, “Wow! Such a lovely place! It seems to have many animals!” Then the lion leapt up and hunted a baby fawn. The next day the lion killed a buffalo. In this way he started killing all the animals one after the other. The animals of the jungle called a meeting to discuss how to save themselves from the lion. They decided to collectively go to the lion to speak about their problem. All the animals collected in front of the lion’s den. The lion laughed and said “Hahaha…why are you all here together? I will not hunt so many animals all at once.” The rabbit proposed to the lion, “We want to be free of the terror you create. We will send you one animal every day but in return you will have to stop hunting in the forest.” The lion agreed to this. Since then, each day one animal was sent to the lion. The lion hunted it and lived happily in the jungle. Fifteen days just passed in this way. Now it was the rabbit’s turn to be sent to the lion. The other animals went to meet the rabbit for the last time! The rabbit said, “Do you think the foolish lion will be able to eat me?” The rabbit started thinking about how he could save his life as he moved towards the lion’s den. The lion was waiting for its food. The delay was increasing his hunger. In the meanwhile, the rabbit hopped to a well and said to himself, “ Let me look at myself for the last time.” On seeing his reflection in the water, he suddenly got an idea! On seeing the rabbit the lion growled angrily, “They have sent such a small animal today and so late!” The rabbit told the lion, “Maharaj! I would have reached on time had I not been stopped by the second lion.” The lion got furious. He said, “You are lying. I am the only king of the jungle.” The rabbit said to the lion, “Come I will take you to him. There is really another lion in the well.” The rabbit took the lion to the well. On reaching the well, the rabbit told the lion, “ Maharaj, didn’t I say there was another lion in the well?” The lion peeped into the well to see the second lion. He saw his own reflection and thought it was another lion The angry lion jumped into the well to kill the other lion. The well was deep and the lion began to drown. The rabbit said to the lion, “You fool! Till now you have scared everyone. You must die now!” “Save me!” the lion kept shouting. The lion drowned in the well while the rabbit and his friends were saved. The rabbit killed the mighty and fierce lion with his brains. That is why it is said, “Use your brains rather than your might.”
author: Sriparna Tamhane

title: The world on my finger tips
text: Once upon a time there was a boy called Minu. He loved bossing others around. he would tell everyone to get him things and to do his homework he even bosses his parents. Then this day came that he got so happy that he could boss the full entire world. Then he saw the full meaning of what it is to be a leader because everyone started coming to him about 12 billion. Then he got so tired then was happy doing his chores.

title: Girisha, the mountain girl
text: She lives next to the waterfall. The wild cock wakes her up. She runs along the mountains. She stretches her hands and plays with the floating clouds. All the birds and animals of the forest are her friends. She sings and dances with them. They love garlands strung with wild flowers. One evening Girisha was stringing a garland. Suddenly she heard some noise. A wild elephant had come by. Everyone got scared and ran away. Girisha slowly went ahead. She told her father, " The elephant is hungry. Get a bunch of bananas." She threw the bananas to the elephant and asked it to leave. Everyone was surprised to see how brave Girisha was. The elephant used his trunk to spray some water. Girisha gave the elephant the garland she had strung. The elephant returned to the dense forest. People near the waterfall started playing drums. Everyone danced with joy.
author: Sriparna Tamhane

title: The day Ruminya got lost
text: Rumniya was very little, Grandfather and Grandmother had taken her for a wedding. There were many people there. Many people flocked near the food. That day somehow Grandmother lost Rumniya. Grandmother was very hopeful. She didn't worry if something was lost. She thought everything would be well again. Grandmother therefore, wasn't worried even after losing Rumniya. On the other hand, one and half year old Rumniya got worried. She was not as hopeful as Grandmother. However, unlike other children, she decided to do something about it instead of shedding tears. It was not easy for a tiny little girl like her to spot Grandmother in the crowd. Because she was so little, she couldn't see people's faces. It was easier for her to look at the feet, shoes and slippers of people, to find the right person. Ruminya did just that. From one end of the room, Ruminya started lifting the sarees of everyone and looking at their feet. In the end she came to a familiar saree and she could recognise the pair of slippers too. Grandmother's face matched the saree and the slippers. Yes, Grandmother was there! Granmother lifted her up. Rumniya heard her grandmother telling her friends, "Look, I told you there was nothing to worry about. If you lose something you find it again."
author: Sriparna Tamhane

title: Tara and the Cloud Festival
text: Today is a Big Festival, All schools are closed for the day. So, Tara is going to help didi Organize everything and cook Strawberry flavoured cupcakes!. "Didi! What can I do today?" Tara asks. "Tara, We should make preparations for The festival in the village today! come fast!" She says. "Yay! Am finally old enough!" Thinks Tara. "Didi I know how to make cupcakes! How many?" Tara asks, Anxiously. "Oh Tara... Are you sure? You might wanna think-" "Please didi? Pretty please?" "I do not-" "Pretty please? with dash of Butterflies on top? didi?" "150 Strawberry cupcakes with rainbow Sprinkles!" Says didi. "Didi- How can I make so, so, so much?" Tara asked, Stunned. "Hey Tara Just a minute... My Friend, Chiku is calling me... Hello?" "Oh no! What do I do now? 150 Cupcakes!!? in about 2.5 hours? HOW COME!!!" Tara thought to herself and burst to tears. Her Friend, Kicchu came and Asked "Ayyo! Tara! What happened? is everything fine?" "*Sigh* Hi kicchu, I literally have to make 150 cupcakes!! What to do?" "Am sorry Tara..." Kicchu said. "But I have 215 cupcakes to make! 65 cupcakes more!" Said Kicchu. "Gotta go! Byee!" "Umm Tara?... Tara? what happened?" Asked didi, Appearing out of the Veranda. "Oh Didi!" Tara Sniffles "I have to make 150 cupcakes... HOW CAN I DIDI? HOW CAN I?" Tara says, Crying Softly. "See Tara, You have been finishing all homework since last week so fast. Why? You wanted to play. See? You came at the top of class! Work has stressed you so much you need a Break Tara!" Didi Inquires. "*Sniffle* How Didi? I have a List of work to do, And I have to finish them by!---" "Shhhh!" Didi Comforts Tara. "Now close your eyes and Just Focus on your Breathing... Inhale... Exhale... Inhale... Exhale... (x2)" Didi Comforts Tara Quietly. "Now Tara, Get the Flour, Milk, Food color, Rainbow sprinkles, Bubblegum Candy and Eggs. Let's do it!" Didi says. "Yes! Let's Do it!" So Tara Gets 15 of The 10 spaces Plate for the Cupcakes. "Yay! WE DID IT DIDI!!!!! WE DID IT!!!!! YAY! YAY! YAYYYYYYY! HOOORAY--" "shhhhhhhhh!" Didi says. "Quiet." Tara And Didi Finished the work and decorated the house with Garlands to Celebrate the festives day! Now Tara Feels happy! Happier than you can Imagine... ﻿VALUABLE LIFE LESSON MORALS FROM THE STORY *You shall Try the best you can to reach your goal! * Accept sadness first. Realize that Winning doesn't sound like a very big deal if you never put your Efforts and fail. *You always know the best you can do when you feel unstable * No pain, means, No gain
author: Tsunami >_<

title: Buying books
text: One day Grandfather gave some money to me and my brother and said, "Go and buy books of your choice." We were very happy. We both love reading books. Should we go now? Or later? Should we go today or tomorrow? We decided to go at once. Should we go to a big market or a small shop? Should the two of us go or should we take someone along? We decided the two of us would go to a small shop. We like the small shop. Even though the sop is small, it has many books. The uncle who runs the shop likes us. He always helps us. Should I buy a book with many pictures? Should I buy a book with many stories? Or should I buy a thin book? I was not being able to decide. We didn't know which book would be good for us. The uncle at the shop smiled sweetly at us and said, "Come with me. Those books are on animals and these are on machines. These are on wars. You choose what you want." I chose a few books. My brother chose a few books. I sat on the floor. My brother sat on the chair. We read and read and read. It was quiet all around. There was no noise anywhere. An hour passed. Two hours passed. Finally we could make out which books to buy. The uncle at the shop was laughing at us. I have found a thick book with many stories. My brother has found a book with many pictures. We ran home with the books to Grandfather. We climbed on his bed. Grandfather hugged me and then we read and read and read.
author: Sriparna Tamhane

title: Chocolate - a birthday gift!
text: Tutul went to her mother and said, "Please buy me a chocolate." Mother said she would buy later. Tutul went to her father. She asked him to buy a chocolate. Father said, "I will buy tomorrow." In the end Tutul went to Grandpa. She said, "Buy me a chocolate please!" Grandpa said "I don't have any money!" Tutul was sad yet she wanted the chocolate somehow. After this.... Tutul went to the shop. She told the shopkeeper, "I am Tutul's mother. Please give me a chocolate." The shopkeeper said, "Really? Tutul's mother wears earrings. Where are your earrrings?" Tutul went to the shop again. She said to the shopkeeper, "I am Tutul's father. Please give me a chocolate." The shopkeeper smiled and said, "Tutul's father has a moustache. Where is your moustache?" This time Tutul dressed up like Grandpa. She told the shopkeeper, "I am Tutul's grandpa. Give me a chocolate, please!" The shopkeeper laughed loudly. Then he gave Tutul a chocolate. Tutul's friend got a chocolate. She was happy to get a chocolate!
author: Sriparna Tamhane

title: True praise
text: He used to spend all his time with his books. He sat in one corner of the school and studied while the other children played. He was good in studies. His friends teased him by calling him studious. All the teachers liked him. However, his English teacher, Mr. Tiwari always found some fault or the other with his work. Mohan tried a lot to hear some praise from him but he felt Tiwari Sir was always finding fault with his work. Mohan started working even harder, thinking some day Mr. Tiwari would surely praise him. The results of the annual exam were declared today. Mohan proceeded to the Principal's room to seek blessings. He overheard a conversation between Mr. Tiwari and the Principal and stopped at the door. Tiwari Sir was saying Mohan was really very good. Ha started saying... "I have found fault with him many times so that he could shine. Today he has topped in the entire state. A lot of hard work has gone into this. He is truly very bright." When Mohan heard this praise, his respect for Tiwari Sir grew. When he went in to touch the feet of Principal Sir and Tiwari Sir to celebrate his success, they patted him on his back to encourage him. Today Mohan understood the meaning of true praise.
author: Sriparna Tamhane
illustrator: Andres Mendez; Aneeta Salaria; Cornelius Wambi Gulere; Deepa Balsavar; Jacob Kono; Kirthi Jayakumar; Ouk  Ratha; Saransh mangla; SIDDARTH MARIMGANTI

title: my sister  and her friend
text: my sister and her friend were playing on a brown colour swing my sister is wearing a blue top my sister is wearing a blue top her friend is wearing green top. next they went for cycling with a black colour cycle with a flashing light.my sister was helping her friend. she fell down.my sister was shocked she immediately helped her. they happily enjoyed their day.
author: VV Karthikeya

title: Angry Sophie
text: There was a girl named Sophie. She loved drawing. She drew a lot! All her pictures were hanging on the wall. For her birthday mother brought her a set of crayons and a sheet of paper. She was very excited and she started drawing right away. Her grandma who meanwhile was taking a walk in the garden slipped on a puddle that had formed during the rain last night. she was rushed immediately to the hospital. The doctor said she needed a plaster immediately or else she would not be able to walk. The mother tried to make her mother in law feel comfortable but without success. The only way to make her comfortable was to send her daughter to school because Sophie never cared about anyone but her drawings, her mother never sent her to school and it would teach her some manners. Her mother said ok for Sophie's grandma. Sophie meanwhile was thinking about her drawing being incomplete but not her grandmother who was now in pain. As she was getting ready her pet porcupine jumped on the chair and poked her water bottle without her noticing. In school she put her water bottle in her mouth to drink at recess but the hole had drained it all and no one around helped her out instead were busy playing. So she got angry on their behaviour and decided not to play. After school was over she walked home sadly thinking about the bad things that happened today. She went into her room and started crying. Her mother came to her room after some time and consoled her. She gave Sophie a new set of crayons and a paper and she started drawing. Hey guys, Sophie here, I learned a very valuable lesson that drawings don't matter that much even if you get to complete them or not, its feelings of people around us that matters. Make them feel special and comfortable and then carry on with your work.
author: Aashi Jain
illustrator: Elizabeth Sparg; Godwin  Chipenya; Kenneth Boyowa Okitikpi; Lavanya  Naidu; Pia Alizé Hazarika; Vinayak Varma; ជឿន  ប្រុស

title: Kibow and football
text: She loves to play football She really wants to be a football player Then, her parents decided to send her to a football coach many of his friends had doubts about a woman who became a football player but Kibow didn't care and she continued to strive to become the best football player like her father. Now, Kibow is one of the best female football players in her school.

title: The dancing queen Sharanya
text: Once a beautiful baby girl named, Sharanya, was born into a loving family. Sharanya grew up to be a bright, energetic, and curious girl who loved nothing more than dancing. Her mother often joked that Sharanya danced even before she learned how to walk. Sharanya would sway to the music and tap her feet to the beat, even when there was no music around. Sharanya trained herself at home and danced like no one is watching. One day, Sharanya's school announced that they would be holding a dance competition. Sharanya was overjoyed. She had been waiting for an opportunity like this for a long time. The day of the competition arrived. Sharanya wore her favorite pink lehenga and braided her hair. She was nervous but excited at the same time. When Sharanya's turn came, she walked up to the stage and took a deep breath. The music started, and Sharanya began to dance. She danced with all her heart and soul, moving gracefully to the beat of the music. At the end of the event, prize distribution ceremony was held. Sharanya held her breath as the judges announced the second and third prizes. She was hoping to hear her name being called out for the first prize. "And the first prize goes to..." the judge announced, and Sharanya's heart skipped a beat. "...Neha!" Sharanya's heart sank. She felt like she had let her family down. She tried to hold back her tears, but they started to flow. Sharanya started bawling and went home. Sharanya felt sad and dejected for days. She even stopped dancing. One day, however, she looked at herself in the mirror. The brave girl decided that she would not let a single failure come in the way for her love of dancing. Sharanya loved dancing and wanted to share her love and joy for dancing with the world. She decided she would learn dancing. Taking the matters in her own hand, Sharanya asked her parents to enroll her in a dance class. Sharanya became a diligent student and her dancing skills improved. Many years passed. Sharanya grew up to be beautiful young woman. She worked hard and practised dancing everyday. She became a professional dancer. Sharanya became so famous in the world for dancing that she was getting requests to perform from all over the world. Sharanya's life came to a full circle when her school called her back to perform and teach dancing to kids. Who used to be once her teachers, were now her fans. They wanted their students to be motivated by Sharanya. Sharanya obliged and performed at her school. To claps and cheers. Sharanya went on to become a world-famous dancer. She learned the value of hard-work, diligence and determination. She now lives her best life globetrotting and sharing her love for dancing with audience around the world.

title: Rima - the brave girl
text: It is the 'Baisakhi fair". It is colourful. Red and white. Uncle loves red. There are many shops with many things. Rima was looking at everything with wonder. Suddenly she found her uncle missing. Where was Uncle? He was nowhere near. Rima was a bit sad but she wasn't afraid. She said to herself, "I know how to find people when they are lost.". I will look for Uncle while going around the fair. Many people had gathered under a tree. They were watching a snake dance. However, Uncle was not to be seen. Is Uncle buying a doll for me? Rima went to the doll shop. No, he wasn't there either. Then where was he? Oh! there is the red giant wheel! He could be there. No, he isn't there either. Rima saw a man near her. He was wearing a red shirt like Uncle. "Uncle!" Rima called from behind. The man turned around to look at Rima. He said, "Oho! Your uncle has got lost, has he?" A balloon was flying above the tree. The moment Rima stepped towards it, she saw a boy standing alone and crying. "What happened to you? Why are you crying?", asked Rima. The boy kept on crying "Mummy, Daddy" Rima hurried up. He took the boy to the mike. They made an announcement through the mike. Soon, the boy's parents were found. They came and took him away. But where was Uncle? Oh there he was! Uncle came running and said, "Where were you? I went on looking for you. " Rima said "That's alright but is it god for children to be lost?
