title: The Little Runner
text: "Look who wants to run the Marathon?! "Little Runner! Little Runner!" Amu wished to take part in the kid-marathon. The older children felt it was a joke. Kaveri didi who trained the children to run long distance, did not feel it was a joke. "Quiet! Amu is younger than everyone here. Yet, she can take part in the kid-marathon. Stop making fun of her!" Kaveri didi spoke firmly. "Okay didi," The children said. They all exercised as didi told them to. Oh! Oh! Little Amu could not run fast enough and long enough as others. But she did not give up. Kaveri didi was very pleased with her. "Keep practicing and doing the exercises I teach. I feel you will be able to complete the run." She told Amu. Kaveri didi's words encouraged and inspired Amu. Even at home she did the exercises and ran around!! "Aaaammuuu!" Bhaiya yelled when Amu ran into him in the room. "Sorry Bhaiya!" Amu said and ran away from the room. At the kid-marathon, every other participant completed the long run. Amu was still running far behind. The loudspeaker blared, "Just look at the little girl doing her best!" The crowd began to cheer her. Amu ran. And ran. Amu reached the finishing line and sat on the ground. She was tired but very happy. Bhaiya and the other older children ran towards her. Their "Little Runner" showed them that everyone can do their best at anything they wish to do.
author: Shahin Ashraf Ali

title: Mislead Mischief!
text: Chapter 1: A Gift Well Deserved Anannya, a 10-year-old girl from Bangalore, was sitting in her balcony and looking at all the kids gliding and sliding on the board on two wheels. How they looked like they are gliding on the waves on that board she thought. “So that’s why it is called a WAVEBOARD”! All her friends, except her, had these waveboards and they used to ride on it every evening. She wanted it so badly and she just knew how. Her birthday was coming in 3 weeks and this would be a perfect gift for her. That evening she went to her parents and asked “ Aai-Baba, can you get me a waveboard for my birthday this year ”? Her parents knew that she was very careless and this will become just another toy in her cupboard and it will all be a waste of money. So, they said “Anu, we think that you want the waveboard just because your friends have it and you are not actually interested in doing anything with it”. Anannya felt bad and wanted to prove her parents wrong. That day she decided not to ask her parents for a waveboard until she masters it. So, she asked her friends if she could borrow their waveboard when they are not playing with it and she started practicing from that day onwards. Anannya practiced waveboarding daily, she fell many times but she never gave up. All that practice had finally paid off. She had learnt waveboarding, not just learnt, she had mastered quite a few moves on it. It was 3 days till her birthday, and she decided it was time to show her parents how well she does waveboarding. So called her parents in the court and started waveboarding. As it had rained the previous day, the court was wet and slippery. As soon as she started waveboarding, she fell hard. But she got up, dusted herself and continued waveboarding. Her parents were amazed at her determination and were proud that she did learn the waveboard in spite of not having it herself. On the morning of Anannya's birthday, her parents surprised her with a latest waveboard in her favorite color. This was the most precious gift for her as she had earned it. Chapter 2: The Mystery Once Anannya had gotten her waveboard she and her friends would waveboard daily. ﻿ One day Anannya and her friends decided to waveboard in the basketball court. Anannya got ready and as she was leaving, she noticed that her waveboard was missing. She thought that she must have left it at a friend’s house, so she went to call her friends. First, she called Rudra, her neighbor and asked “Hey Rudra, have you seen my waveboard anywhere?” Rudra replied puzzled “no, in fact I cannot find mine either”. They both decided that they will look for their wave boards together. Once they reached down near the play area, they saw their friends Shreyan and Shashwat looking for something and she before she could say anything, they asked her “hey, have you seen our waveboard anywhere?" All of them look puzzled. Just then Aarav and Neel come running and said “our wave boards are missing, have you seen them anywhere”? Anannya wondered, “This is not a coincidence that everyone’s wave boards are missing”. Shashwat replied “good point, but who would want ﻿ to steal children's ﻿ wave boards?” Just then Shreyan interrupted “Hey, you know that painting work is going on for our building and do you guys remember when we used to waveboard in the corridor, the painters scolded us”. Aarav tagged in “yeah, they said …… if you waveboard in the corridor you will face consequences”. Neel says “oh yes! both of you are correct”. ﻿ The kids decided to start their own investigation. They divided themselves ﻿ in teams. Anannya and Shashwat were good in asking questions and finding clues. Shreyan and Rudra were good at drawing and spying. Aarav and Neel were good at running so they would help by running around if needed. First Anannya and Shashwat went to the security cabin and interrogated the security guards. They asked “have you seen anything odd lately”? The security guard looked puzzled and replied “no, nothing” Anannya puts a small cross beside the word "security" in a notebook. Everybody met at the park. Anannya said “nothing from our side”. Shreyan replied ﻿ “I found something; we all have seen those big barrels of paint with the painters, maybe the wave boards must be hidden in them.” Everyone nodded in agreement. Hearing this Rudra said “ leave this to me. I will sneak into the terrace and check the barrels”. Alas, he found nothing but paint. He said that the barrels were full of paint but there was no waveboard. Anannya put a cross beside the word "barrels" ﻿. Suddenly, Shreyan remembered that there was a tall person with the painters, instructing them to do their work properly. That must be their leader. He must know something. Shreyan told this to his friends but they couldn't recall seeing this person. So Shreyan drew his portrait. He was really good at drawing and when the kids saw the portrait, they realized that this was the same person who had scolded them for waveboarding in the corridors. They all decide to confront him. Chapter 3: The Face-Off Anannya, Shashwat, Shreyan, Rudra, Neel and Aarav were furious and were ready to face-off with the culprit. They approach this person and here starts the most confusing conversation... Aarav steps in and says “do you know why we are here? and do you see anything different?” The "leader" looked puzzled and answered “I don’t know what are you kids talking about?” Shreyan now getting angry, questioned him “can’t you see anything missing here?” The painter, now getting annoyed said “Tell me clearly what’s the matter?” The kids start yelling together “WHERE ARE OUR WAVEBOARDS?" "WHY DID YOU HIDE THEM? NOW HOW WILL WE PLAY?”. The painter, realizing what is happening started laughing and said “it’s not what you think it is” The painter said “that day, you all were waveboarding for some time and then and you left your wave boards in the middle of the road to see something in the park. Later on, it started raining and you forgot your wave boards and went home, so me and my painters saw your wave boards and kept them in the shed behind the pool. You see, we did take your waveboards, but not to hide them but to save them.” He also told them that the only reason the painters scolded them for waveboarding in the corridor as the corridor is full of wet paint which can be dangerous for kids and they can get hurt. Hearing this, the children felt ashamed for having screamed at the painters. They apologized and promised that they would not trouble the painters during their work and would waveboard only in the park. After this incident, the children learn to take care of their things and listen to elders. ﻿
author: Anannya Kudtarkar

title: Happy Mother's Day
text: One fine Sunday morning, when I was only six years old, I observed my mother as she did all the household chores. The cleaning, the cooking, the washing, the drying, they almost seemed endless. And so I hugged my mother calling her the best mother in the world. My mother was happy to see that I had acknowledged her hard work. Later that day, my mother gave me milk to drink and I spilt it all. My mother scolded me because I was roaming around with my glass of milk and ended up spilling it. I asked my mother why she was scolding me because I thought the best mothers in the world don’t scold their children. Only bad mothers do. My mother told me that mothers scold their children for their own good and so that they can learn from their mistakes. And I quite frankly understood what she was saying. The best mother in the world is not the mother who doesn’t scold her children. The best mother in the world is the mother who genuinely loves her children and will do anything to help her children achieve their goals. Happy Mother’s day to all the mothers across the globe, taking care of their children I am Ananthajith,an ambitious 10 year old who wants to show people the world through his stories. I believe that if you want to achieve your goals, you will have to start working towards it from a very young age. I want to help people and show the world from different perspectives through my stories. And so I am practicing my writing skills from a young age and read lots of books. I encourage you to set your own goals and work towards them. I wish you luck on your journey towards your goal and would request you to wish me luck on mine. Thank you & Hari Om
author: Ananthajith Guruprasad
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Fahad Faizal; Sonal Gupta Vaswani

title: The Unicorn Story
text: Once upon a time, in a faraway kingdom there lived a beautiful white unicorn as shiny as the moon. He was very pretty and even kind towards everyone that all the other creatures of the kingdom used to love him. The unicorn has a magical horn that could make rainbows which made him an extraordinary unicorn! He can use his horn to make the dirty water clean, he could fix the injuries or cute and broken bones. But, the unicorn didn’t care much about his magic horn. Instead, he always wished and deeply desired that he had unicorn wings to fly freely like a bird or butterfly. One day, the unicorn went to the castle in his kingdom. The beautiful castle had a garden filled with adorable flowers and greenery which was the home for the butterflies. The unicorn talked to the butterflies and said “I wish I had wings like yours” but the butterflies told him that their wings are too tiny for him Later, the unicorn went to the forest and looked up to the trees and saw the colorful birds sitting on the branches. He said “I wish I had wings like yours” to a bluebird. But the bluebird told him that the color of her wings aren’t the right match for him. He didn’t stop searching and went to the pond where he saw the frogs were jumping, and gorgeous white swans were swimming in the water. He then said the same thing to the swan “I wish I had wings like yours”. But the swan just shook her head as a no in the answer. He was sad as no one wanted to give up their wings. The unicorn felt disappointment after not getting the wings from anyone so he walked and went to the sea and he fell asleep soon after laying down. Suddenly the unicorn felt a touch on his nose and woke up. After opening his eyes he saw a white horse with unicorn wings! The unicorn went ahead and used his magic horn to heal the white horse’s wings and the wings apparently grew strong and didn’t droop anymore. The white horse thanked him and flew away. The unicorn said “I wish I had wings like that”, as he was amazed by her wings as he flew towards the rising sun. Then he looked down sadly and saw himself in the water of the pond. He was surprised to see that he had big beautiful white wings, he stretched his wings out wide and flew after the white-winged horse as he wanted to say “thank you”Finally, he was happy to fly into the sky and he was now known as Rainbow Unicorn with Wings!

title: The Monsoon Party
text: Rain is a very important aspect of our lives, it helps us survive by giving us water to sustain ourselves. It teaches us how to live without certain things and helps us create ever-lasting bonds with our families and friends. I wanted to share an experience of mine, in which the rain played a crucial role. O ne afternoon after all the school periods were completed before me, my mother and my brother went home my mother was talking with my friends’ mothers. And I was playing with my friends. It was one of my friend’s birthday and so we all wished him a happy birthday. My brother took the house keys and went home early whilst me and my mother decided to drop my friends and their mothers at the back gate of the school (Through which they were going to go home). And there I discovered that we were going to have a party there. We had the cake, the plastic plates, chips, etc. Right there and so we had a roadside party. And then suddenly it started raining, luckily most of the mothers had brought umbrellas and so we didn’t get too wet. At that moment I felt very happy, I was happy because I had finally found some true friends. Up until that moment I didn’t feel one hundred percent part of the group, but it all changed that day. Everyone started going home until only me, my close friend and our mothers remained. And that was because me and my friend had not yet finished eating the cake, chips and puffs. That day both of us found out that both of us were slow eaters. After we finished eating, we decided to wash our hands in the rain by keeping them out of the umbrella as we separated paths and went towards our homes. Written by Ananthajith Guruprasad A True Story I am Ananthajith, an ambitious 10-year-old with many goals to achieve. I want to help people and show them the world from different perspectives through my stories. And so, I am practicing my writing skills from a very young age and read many books. I believe that if you want to achieve your goals, you must start working towards it from the day you set your goals in life. I encourage you to set goals and work towards them. I wish you the best of luck on your journey towards your goals and would request you to wish me luck on mine. Thank You & Hari Om
author: Ananthajith Guruprasad

title: Pomegranate Fruit
text: The pomegranate is a red and round fruit that grows on a shrub. In Latin, pomum means apple; granatum means seeded. So, the name pomegranate. The thick, red outer covering is known as the pericarp. Inside the red covering is a thin white spongy inner wall. This white wall is known as the mesocarp. The small round red arils attach to the white inner wall. Each aril has a red flesh that covers a seed inside. Pomegranates are used to make juice and are mixed in fruit salads. Pomegranates have few calories but are rich in fibre, vitamins, and minerals. Pomegranates were known as wine apples in Ireland.

title: The Dark Chevalier
text: A gang of masked criminals robs a mafia-owned bank in Gotham City, each betraying and killing each other until the sole survivor, the Joker, reveals himself as the mastermind and escapes with the money. The vigilante Batman, district attorney Harvey Dent, and police lieutenant Jim Gordon ally to eliminate Gotham's organized crime. As Batman's alter-ego, the billionaire Bruce Wayne, publicly supports Dent as Gotham's legitimate protector, believing his success will allow Batman to retire so Wayne can romantically pursue his childhood friend Rachel Dawes, despite her relationship with Dent. Gotham's mafia bosses gather to discuss protecting their organizations from the Joker, the police, and Batman. The Joker interrupts the meeting and offers to kill Batman for half of the fortune their accountant, Lau, concealed before fleeing to Hong Kong to avoid extradition. With the help of Wayne Enterprises CEO Lucius Fox, Batman finds Lau in Hong Kong and returns him to the custody of Gotham police. His testimony enables Dent to apprehend the crime families. The bosses accept the Joker's offer, and he kills high-profile targets involved in the trial, including the judge and police commissioner. Although Gordon saves the mayor, the Joker threatens that his attacks will continue until Batman reveals his identity. He targets Dent at a fundraising dinner and throws Rachel out of a window, but Batman rescues her. Wayne struggles to understand the Joker's motives, but his butler Alfred Pennyworth says some simply relish destruction. Dent claims he is Batman to lure out the Joker, who attacks the police convoy transporting him. Batman and Gordon apprehend the Joker, and Gordon is promoted to commissioner. At the police station, Batman interrogates the Joker, who says he finds Batman entertaining and has no intention of killing him. Having deduced Batman's feelings for Rachel, the Joker reveals she and Dent are being held separately in buildings rigged to explode. Batman races to save Rachel while Gordon and the other officers go after Dent, but they discover the Joker has switched their positions. Rachel is killed in the explosion, while Dent's face is severely burned on one side. The Joker escapes custody, extracts the fortune's location from Lau, and burns all of it, killing Lau in the process. Wayne Enterprises accountant Coleman Reese deduces Batman's identity and attempts to expose it, but the Joker threatens to blow up a hospital unless Reese is killed. While the police evacuate hospitals and Gordon struggles to keep Reese alive, the Joker meets with a disillusioned Dent, persuading him to take the law into his own hands and avenge Rachel. Dent defers his decision-making to his half-scarred, two-headed coin, killing the corrupt officers and the mafia involved in Rachel's death. As panic grips the city, the Joker reveals two evacuation ferries, one carrying civilians and the other prisoners, are rigged to explode at midnight unless one group sacrifices the other. To the Joker's disbelief, the passengers refuse to kill one another. Batman subdues the Joker but refuses to kill him. Before the police arrest the Joker, he says although Batman proved incorruptible, his plan to corrupt Dent has succeeded. Dent takes Gordon's family hostage, blaming his negligence for Rachel's death. He flips his coin to decide their fates, but Batman tackles him to save Gordon's son, and Dent falls to his death. Believing Dent is the hero the city needs and the truth of his corruption will harm Gotham, Batman takes the blame for his death and actions and persuades Gordon to conceal the truth. Pennyworth burns an undelivered message to Wayne from Rachel, who said she chose Dent, and Fox destroys the invasive surveillance network that helped Batman find the Joker. The city mourns Dent as a hero, and the police launch a manhunt for Batman.

title: When Crocodile craved Chocolate & Chips
text: Once upon a time, in a river very clean, there lived a Crocodile who loved to eat. His favorite food was frogs, sea snakes, crabs and fishes! But... he secretly dreamed of eating Chocolate and Chips! You may wonder, where and how he had tasted Chocolate and Chips?!! Have you seen? Sometimes, children and adults on a picnic, throw them into the river. That is how he had tasted it. He liked it so much, he ate them all...... including their wrappers and packets! Soon, his craving* for Chocolate and Chips grew in a big, big way... So big, he started to pray. One night, he prayed and prayed to the River Fairy to grant him a wish. To fill the river with Chocolate and Chips...and take every little fish away! (*wanting & wishing) That same night, the kind, magical River Fairy came in his dreams to grant him his wish! With a wave of her wand, she said a magic chant: " Google, doodle, poodle, noodle, noodle, poodle, doodle, google, fill the river with Chocolate and Chips and take away all the fish" Lo and Behold!! Crocodile woke up the next morning to find the river filled with what he wanted. He jumped with joy! He gorged and ate, till his stomach was close to bursting! "Chocolate and Chips, Chocolate and Chips. I cannot get enough of it" he said. Alas! Very soon h is stomach rumbled, his stomach grumbled. Oooo...aaaaa...hummaaa...happaaa...ouch! He felt he had a volcano waiting to erupt inside him. He floated on his back with a tummy that hurt. A pain that made him so scared, he knew he had to find a doctor to visit. The next day at the doctor's office, Dr.Turtle peered at Crocodile and said; "What have you been eating to make it so bad? Looks like there is too much plastic in there as well". With tears in his eyes Crocodile mumbled, "Just Chocolate and Chips in their packets " That night Crocodile could not sleep, for Dr. Turtle had given medicines but he did not feel better. Ooooo 'No more' he thought of the Chocolate and Chips he had eaten! Aaaaaa 'That is enough' he said to himself. His craving went away. He called the River Fairy at once and begged her to make the river clean. To bring back his favorites, the snakes, the frogs, the crabs and the fishes. She heard him carefully and then said, "A wish once given cannot be taken back with magic. So... You will have to pick up all that junk while chanting, " No more, no more, make it like before. Only then you will get what you asked for" Then Crocodile did just that. He chanted: "No more, no more, make it like before" and picked up each and every packet and each and every wrapper. He made sure he sent all that plastic for recycling. S oon the river was clean! No more, no more, make it like before Slowly all his favorite creatures came back. Soon the river was clean and so was Crocodile's tummy. For he now eats sea snakes and frogs, crabs and fishes and all that makes Crocodile 's tummy go Yummy! Yummy! Yummy! P.S: As for Chocolate and Chips, he may eat a tiny one at times...but he always remembers to say a big "No" to all that plastic!
author: Sowmya Srinivasan

title: MS Dhoni: biography
text: MS Dhoni, a popular Indian cricketer, was born on July 7, 1981 in Ranchi, Bihar. The full name of MS. Dhoni is Mahendra Singh Pansingh Dhoni. MS Dhoni made his ODI debut on December 23, 2004 against Bangladesh in Chittagong. Dhoni always played wearing with Jersey no. 7.He got a special preference for his birth date. MS. Dhoni played as a captain in all three cricket formats from 2007 to 2017. Under the captaincy of MS. Dhoni India,won the Cricket World Cup against Sri Lanka in 2011. MS. Dhoni married Sakshi Singh Rawat on 4th of July 2010. MS Dhoni has now retired from all three formats, but continues to play for an Indian cricket franchise Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League. MS Dhoni also received the Padma Bhushan, the honorary rank of Lieutenant Colonel and many other awards for his contribution in the field of cricket. Bollywood had made a film on Dhoni's life 'MS. Dhoni: The Untold Story'. A web series named 'The Roar Of A Lion' is based on his life journey in cricket.

title: THE LOST SHOES
text: One Saturday morning Mr. Gopal was watching news. The breaking news was single shoes were being stolen from the locality. This news was watched by his 9 year old daughter Nivya, who was getting ready to go to school. She was having her delicious breakfast. Nivya Gopal was a smart and brave girl. She always liked adventures. On the way to school with her dad, she was curious about the news that was disturbing her and was chatting about the lost shoes. Her dad told that the police were doing their duty and they would solve the mystery very soon. Mr. Gopal dropped Nivya at school and went to office. Nivya entered the classroom and found that her friend Christine was sobbing. Nivya confronted Christine and asked what the matter was. Christine told that she had lost one of her favorite and expensive shoes. Nivya was surprised to know this. Seeing Christine sobbing, many of her classmates came to her to find out what the matter was. Hearing the reason of Christine crying, few of her classmates told that their single slippers and shoes were also missing from their home some time back. Nivya, Christine and all the girls decided to solve the mystery of “STOLEN SHOES”. Nivya and Christine spoke about it and decided to meet in the evening after they finished their school work and discuss further. When Nivya reached home she told what happened at school to her mother. Nivya’s mother told her to finish her school work and they will discuss about it when her father is back from office. Nivya’s dad Mr. Gopal was back from office. After he refreshed and had his cup of coffee, Nivya and her mom told him about what happened at school. Mr. Gopal instantly refused to the plan and scolded Nivya. His concern was that Nivya and Christine were too young for all this. Nivya pleaded and convinced her dad that she would definitely concentrate on studies and only some time she will spend for investigating the matter of stolen shoes. Nivya’s dad also agreed to help them. Christine came to Nivya’s house that evening. Nivya’s parents greeted her. They all sat together in the lawn and had some snacks and coffee. They were discussing about various issues like school, studies, outing, shopping etc. Nivyas ’s parents asked Christine how she found that her shoes were lost. Christine told that everybody in her house would keep their shoes and slippers in the shoe rack in front of their house. Christine had to attend a birthday party. She got dressed up and when she was about to leave she wanted to wear her favorite pair of shoes, but she couldn’t find one of them. She was getting late for the party so she wore some other pair of slipper and went for the party. She thought that she must have misplaced it somewhere and after returning from the party she would search for it. But seeing the news the next day in the television she realized that her shoes had been actually stolen. Nivya’s parents asked if there was anything suspicious in and around their house. Christine tried to recollect and told that as it was a rainy season, she had seen some large footprints with mud, some vehicle tyre marks and some animal footprints. Next day being Sunday Nivya and Christine decided to start early to investigate about this in the neighborhood. Nivya and Christine went door to door in the neighborhood and enquired if they had lost any shoes. Many in the neighborhood had lost single shoes from a pair or single shoes from two pairs. They all were very worried who thief was and why he was stealing only single shoes and slippers. Everybody in the neighborhood was also curious to know whose footprints were they. On the way, they met Mr. Ravi, the investigating police officer. Mr. Ravi was very proud of these children, as at this young age they were curious to solve the mystery. Nivya and Christine accompanied Mr. Ravi in their neighborhood investigation. On enquiring in houses were the shoes (or) slippers were lost Mr. Ravi came to a conclusion that the postman of the locality had visited their houses to drop letters. This was very common in many of the houses. Mr. Ravi took Nivya and Christine in his jeep to the postman’s house. It had started raining again. They reached the postman’s house, got down and ran towards the house so that they don’t get drenched in rain. They rang the doorbell. The lady of the house came and opened the door. She looked astonished to see the policeman and two girls in this rainy season on their doorsteps. Mr. Ravi told not to worry and they had just come for some enquiry with the postman. By this time the postman had also come out of his room to see what was happening. They invited the children and policeman to come inside and he would cooperate in whatever way it was possible for him in their investigation. All of them sat together and had a general chit chat about the locality, people etc. Postman’s wife went to the kitchen to bring some hot tea and pakodas for all as it was raining and everybody would enjoy it. Everybody had their tea and pakodas and were feeling comfortable to talk to each other. It was still drizzling. Mr. Ravi asked the postman about the society were many shoes were missing. The postman told that society was a very peaceful one with all good people, but the roads were not in good condition due to rain and there were many stray dogs, so he always preferred to go by a mailvan in that area. “Stray dogs”, Mr. Ravi and children looked at each other. Being a rainy season, everybody would be inside the house spending time with the family. These stray dogs would pickup some slippers or shoes lying in front of the house and play with them or tear to pieces and roam about here and there. After enquiry with the postman, Mr. Ravi and children left the postman’s house. It was still raining. Mr. Ravi dropped the children at their house and told them not to worry anymore and peacefully go to school the next day. The next day being Monday, Nivya was getting ready for school. Nivya’s father was watching the news and the news channels were showing Mr. Ravi talking to media and press people, about the mystery of Lost Shoes and how the case had been solved. He was asking the public not to worry, and all necessary help will be done by the police department and the corporation. Nivya reached the school and was very excited to share her and Christine’s experience with her classmates that they had the previous day. All classmates and teachers appreciated them. The principal of the school arranged a special assembly meeting and congratulated both the girls. She encouraged all other students also to be bold and brave and have some social responsibility and work towards the upliftment of the society.

The wrestler slipped once again and fell with a thump!!! "You pull up good stunts. You should work in the circus," said Gappu while laughing. The wrestler started running yet again. This time around, Gappu flung all the banana peel. Srr... the wrestler fell near Gappu's feet. "I forgive you this time. Do not throw the peels on the road henceforth." The wrestler does not throw the banana peels on the road anymore.

title: The Mysterious Island
text: Once upon a time, in a small costal village, there lived a young boy named Oliver. Oliver was a curious and adventurous soul who always yearned for excitement. One day, while exploring the rocky shores near his home, he stumbled upon an ancient map tucked away in a hidden cave. With his heart pounding with anticipation, oliver unfurled the map. It revealed a mysterious island that was said to hold unimaginable treasures and secrets. The island's location was marked by an "X", and the faded parchment whispered tales of hiddrn temples and buried riches. Unable to resist allure of unknown, oliver resolved to embark on a daring adventure to find the island. he packed a small backpack with essentials and bid farewellm to worried family and friends. Setting sail on a creaky old boat, Oliver navigated the vast ocean, guided by the ancient map. Stroms roared and monstrous wave crashned against his boat, but his determination and courage never wavered. Finally, after days of treacherouds sailing, the young explorer caught a glimpse of land on distant horizon. The island as described in map, was shrouded in mist, making it even more mysterious and alluring. As Oliver stepped ashore, the damp earth clung to his boots, and the scent of adventure filled the air. He ventured deep into the dense jungle, hacking his way through thick foliage and listening to the distant cries of exoitic birds. Suddenly, he stumbles upon a overgrown stone path leading to a hidden temple. The air grew still, and a eerie silence enveloped the surroundings. With a mixture of trepidation and excitement, Oliver stepped through the temple's ancient stone doorway. The interior was bathed in a soft golden glow as sunlight filtered through the cracks. Intricate carvings adorned the walls, depicting stories of mythical creatures and forgotten civilizations. As Oliver ventured further, he discovered a chamber adorned with gleaming jewels and golden artifacts. His eyes widened in awe as he marveled at the incredible wealth that lay before him. However, he knew the true treasures he sought was not material wealth, but the knowledge and wisdom that the island held. Continuing his exploration, Oliver stumbled upon a hidden library within the depths of the temple. The shelves were lined with ancient scrolls and dusty books, each containing untold stories and forgotten wisdom. He gingerly picked up a weathered book, its pages filled with faded ink. As he delved into the writings, Oliver discovered that the island had once been home to a wise and peaceful civilization. They had left behind their knowledge and teachings, hoping that one day, someone worthy would find them and carry their legacy forward. Days turned into weeks as oliver immersed himself in the island's secrets, diligently studying the ancient texts and unraveling the mysterious of the lost civilization. He learned about their customs, their beliefs, and the importance of harmony with nature. Finally, the time came for Oliver to bid farewell to the island and its hidden wonders. Armed with newfound wisdom, he set sail back to his village, his heart filled with gratitude for the extraordinary adventure he had experienced. Returning home, Oliver shared his stories with his family and friends, igniting their imagination and inspiring them to pursue their own dreams. The village transformed as the village embraced their own sense of adventure and curiosity, fostering a community built on exploration and knowledge. And so, Oliver's adventure on the mysterious island became a legend passed down through generations. The island remained a beacon of wonder, waiting for other brave souls to discover its secrets and carry forward its legacy.

It was a long haul until she reached a short hill where she figured out there was a shortcut to the cottage She hiked up and down the hill and eventually was only a few feet away from the house she was ready to drop.Although she was motivated. title: Ali and Ginger
text: Ali was an 8-year-old, chubby and caramelled hair playful boy. It was a bright summer's day. Ali woke early and smiled at the sun. He felt the sun smiled back at him and the golden rays kissed his chubby cheeks. The birds on the nearby date trees chirped and reminded him to hasten to the fields with his dad. He loved to play in the maze of the palm date fields. Merrily, he hopped to the fields with his dad. the palm trees waved and swayed at him.The cool afternoon breeze lulled him to sleep. Suddenly, he was woken by a knock on his head. Ali angrily shouted, "What's that?" He twirled and looked around clockwise and anti clock wise but saw no one but his dad working, sweating and digging labouriously. What could it have been? Just then, he heard 'Mew, mew, mew'. He followed the sound and looked up and saw a tiny kitten perched on top of the palm trees. The kitten's whiskers moved to and fro as though they pleaded for help. A sudden realization dawned and he quickly tried to climb the tree to rescues the kitten but in vain. The tree was too tall to climb for Ali. He called out to his dad for help. His dad immediately came to the kitten's rescue. Ali took the kitten home with him and named him ginger.

title: The Birds' Blessing
text: A flock of birds were eating grains on the ground. Some children saw the birds. What did the children do? They threw stones at the birds! Throwing stones at birds or at anyone, is so unkind! The birds got scared. Two birds got injured. The injured birds could not fly away. the other birds flew away. Aliya and her friends were passing by. They saw what happened. Aliya and her friends shouted, "Hey! Why are you hurting the birds?! Stop it!" Those who were throwing the stones got scared and ran away. Aliya ran towards the two injured birds. Aliya's friends helped her catch the injured birds. They gently put them in her arms. Aliya and her family loved animals. She carried the birds home in her arms. Aliya told amma and baba all that had happened. Amma and baba were very pleased with her. Baba knew how to treat some wounds with herbs. 'We will take care of the birds and soon they will be fine." Amma said. Aliya, amma and baba took very good care of the birds. Their wounds healed. One day, Aliya felt, the birds were asking her to open the window and let them go. Aliya told amma, "I feel the birds are telling me that they are fine now. They wish to be free... to fly...to be with their flock...They are asking me to open the window." Amma nodded and opened the window. Seeing some birds flying in the sky, the birds in the room began to chirp. They flapped their wings, flew and perched upon the window. They chirped loudly. "They are calling their family and friends!" Said Aliya. Yes. The birds were calling their family and friends. Some distance away, their flock heard their call. They started flying towards Aliya's house. "Amma, they say, their family and friends are coming to take them!" Aliya spoke with joy. "Yes!" Whispered Amma as she saw the flock comming. The birds perched on the window, saw their flock in the sky. They turned their heads towards Aliya. They looked at her and flapped their wings. Then, turning their heads towards the sky, they flew out of the window to join their flock. "Aliya! My child! The birds gave you a special blessing for your kindness. You can now understand what the birds and animals are trying to tell us." Said Amma. Aliya smiled. Soon, animals, birds and insects started calling or visiting her when they needed help. And with the birds' blessings, Aliya lives happily, helping the animals in need.

title: What is that smell?
text: I am hungry too!" "There are milk, eggs, bread and vegetables in the fridge", says mum. "I'll prepare dinner", says dad. "Daddy, can you make fried rice for us?" says Tara. "Fried rice!" exclaimed Madhav. Once Tara, Madhav, and parents entered the living room, they sensed that something was strange. Very strange. "Ew! What is that smell?" says Tara. "This is strange!" shouts Madhav. The living room is hot, dark and smelly. The whole house smells strange! Where is this smell coming from? Mum looked under the bed. Madhav checked the pail in the bathroom. Tara checked the dining room. Dad checked the kitchen. Dad pointed to the fridge and said "I think it's coming from there!" "Could it be that there is a smelly monster hiding in the fridge?" Tara asked. Madhav hugged his mum and said "I am scared!" "Let's open the fridge and have a look" says mum. Everybody pinched their noses and covered their mouths as mum opened the fridge. She reached into the fridge, "The fridge feels warm, and the light is off!" Tara asked "What happened?" Dad mentioned that the fridge has been broken for quite a while. "There is no cold air, every has turned bad", mum sulked. Tara asked "Has the milk turned bad" "Yes, can you smell how sour it has become?" asked mum. "Milk needs to be refrigerated to stay fresh" advised dad. "Has the bread gone bad" Tara asked. "Yes, do you see the green spots on the bread? That's mould and it is growing on the bread." said dad. Madhav curiously exclaimed "It's hairy!". "Don't touch it! If you eat it, you will fall sick" said dad. "How about the vegetables? Have they gone bad too?" Tara exclaims in horror. "Yes, all the vegetables have gone bad, we can't eat them!" said mum. Madhav picked up an egg and dropped it on the floor. "Madhav, now it smells worse!" Tara exclaimed. Dad said "Oh no, the egg has gone bad too" Tara never wants to eat an egg ever again. " How gross! How disgusting!" Madhav screamed and ran away as dad picked up the broken egg. Dad collected all the rotten food and threw them into a trash bag, and cleaned the fridge. "Why would the food go bad" Tara asked. Mum says "Overtime, all the food will eventually go bad. The cool air from the fridge helps to keep the food fresh for a longer time." Tara asked "Does all food go bad?" "Rice and beans do not go bad. They can last for a longer time" says mum. "This cabbage and butter too!" says dad. "Let's have butter and cabbage for dinner!" exclaimed Tara. Invisible monster Tara and Madhav thought there was an invisible monster in their house. While they didn't find the monster, they weren't wrong, there were unseen things in the house. When food becomes "bad" meaning it cannot be eaten by humans, it is because something we cannot see is eating it. These invisible creatures are called microbes. Microbes aren't completely invisible: they're just very, very, very tiny (smaller than the tiniest insect you'll ever see). You need a machine called a microscope to see them. They look like this. When food goes bad Some foods go bad faster than others, and some go bad very slowly. Wet foods, like many fruits and vegetables, spoil relatively quickly. Dried foods, such as undercooked dal and rice, spoil more slowly. Eggs, meat and cheese go bad quickly. Pickled foods like kimchi and ghee go bad very slowly. Packaged foods, like cookies and candy, are the slowest to spoil.

title: Invisible Monster!
text: Mama said "It's great to be home isn't it?" Tala nodded and replied "I'm hungry, mama!" "I'm hungry too..." Little brother Mata exclaimed while rubbing his belly. "There's milk, eggs, bread and vegetables in the fridge." Mama said. "I'll prepare dinner." Papa replied. "Can we have fried rice?" Tala asked. "I would like fried rice too." Mata echoed. As Tala and family entered the house they were overwhelmed by a strong stench. Something is not right. "Yuck, what is this smell?" Tala screamed. "It must be a monster!" Mata shouted. The living room was hot, dark and smelly. The entire house is filled with the stench! Where is this stench coming from? Mama checked the bedrooms. Mata checked the bathroom. Tala checked the dining room. Finally, papa checked the kitchen. Papa exclaimed pointing at the fridge "The smell is from there!" "Could there be a smelly monster in the fridge?" Tata signed. "Mama, I'm scared." Mata added. "Let's peek into the fridge." Mama said. Mama opened the fridge while everyone held their breath. Mama reached into the fridge and sighed, "it's warm inside and the light isn't on as well." "What happened?" Mata asked. "Seems like the fridge has stopped functioning for a while." Papa explained. "All the food has rot without the coldness." Mama said with much displeasure. "The milk too?" Mata asked. "Yes, it's giving off a strong stench." Mama replied. "Milk especially, needs a low temperature to retain its freshness." Papa commented. "Is the bread spoilt as well?" Tala asked. "Yes, can you see the bread is covered by green stuff? It's mould." Papa said. "Mould has multiplied on the bread." "It looks hairy." Mata stared curiously. "Don't touch it, you fall sick if you eat it." Papa said. "Is the vegetable spoilt as well?" Tala asked in concern. "Yes, they are all spoilt and cannot be eaten." Mama replied. Mata picked up an egg and accidentally dropped it. "Mata, the stench has gotten worst." Tala shouted. "Seems the eggs has turn bad as well." Papa said. Tala believes she would not be able to eat eggs for the rest of her life. "That's disgusting!" Mata screamed and ran away while Papa was cleaning up the mess. Tala and family cleared the fridge and threw all the rotten food into huge trash bags. "Why did the food turn bad?" Tala asked. "All food turn bad over time. They stay fresh for a longer period at a lower temperature and spoils faster at a higher temperature." Mama responded. "Does all food turn bad?" Tala asked. "Rice and potatoes last longer." Mama explained. "Cabbage too." Papa added. "Seems like sesame oil as well." Mata chimed in. "In that case we can cook rice with potatoes." Tala happily suggested. Invisible Monsters! Tala and Mata thought there is an invisible monster at home. Although they did not find the monster, they are not entirely wrong. There are micro-organisms at home. When food turns bad, they humans can't consume them any more. That's because there are microscopic organism multiplying on the food. These micro-organisms are known as bacteria. These micro-organisms are not entirely invisible. They are just very small (smaller than the smallest insects). Humans will need a microscope to see them. And they look like this in the picture. When food goes bad... Some food spoils faster while others take a longer time to go bad. Moist food such as fruits and vegetables go bad faster. Dry food such as uncooked grains turn bad slower. Eggs, meat and dairy products turns bad especially fast. Fermented food such as kimchi, soya sauce turn bad much slower. Processed and properly packaged food such as biscuits and sweets takes a longer time to go bad.

title: Gideon and the Golden Key
text: Once upon a time, in a beautiful forest, there was a little rabbit named Gideon. He had soft white fur and slanted eyes. Gideon loved exploring nature and all its wonders. One sunny day, while hopping through the forest, he found a magical golden key. Gideon was so excited! He held the key in his paws and wondered what it could unlock. With a leap of excitement, he began his adventure. Each time Gideon used the key, it opened a door to a new and amazing place. He met talking animals, flowers that could dance, and even a playful fairy named Maya. Maya became Gideon's guide. She led him to a secret glen where a wise and ancient oak tree stood. This tree was known for its wisdom. Gideon approached the tree gently and asked, "Dear tree, how can I find everlasting happiness?" The tree swayed its branches and whispered, "Happiness lies within you, dear rabbit. Be kind, love others, and always be grateful for what you have." Gideon was amazed by the tree's wisdom. He said goodbye to Maya and went back home, filled with joy in his heart. He shared the tree's wisdom with his friends in the forest, and something magical happened. The animals started helping each other, and new friendships blossomed everywhere. Gideon's story spread through the forest, reminding everyone that happiness comes from being kind and loving to others. And so, the legend of Gideon, the friendly rabbit, lived on, inspiring all the creatures to create a world full of love and kindness forever and ever.
author: Wiji Kholifah

He wanted to make friends with them. But whenever he went to someone to befriend them or to talk them, everyone used to run away that makes Ratty feel alone in the world. He had no one to play with no one to talk to. Even other baby rattle snakes used to laugh at him and will not play with him and often called him a Coward. But Ratty knew that his kindness and friendliness will one day give him a life long friend. So one day he set off on a journey in search of someone who will value his kindness and will be his friend Ratty slithered and crawled and faced many obstacles while crossing the dessert alone. He was almost eaten alive by a hawk but managed to escape. After days of travel and solitude, he entered a small beautiful town and was mesmerized by its beauty. He entered a garden and sat in a lush green bush. A small girl came to play in the garden and noticed the little ratty in the bush. Instead of being afraid, the girl smiled at ratty and ratty smiled back at her. From that day on, the little girl came daily to the garden to meet with Ratty. Ratty was way too happy and it was his favorite time. Ratty finally found a friend who liked him despite that he was a snake. Time went by and Ratty grew big and strong still their friendship never changed. the girl was not afraid of Ratty and Ratty never meant any harm to her. One sunny day, the girl was playing in the garden and Ratty was enjoying the sunny afternoon in the bush when suddenly a wild dog came running attacking the girl. Ratty saw it and immediately came out of the bush to rescue and protect his friend. However, seeing a snake in the garden the residents complaint to wild life reservation Centre. The team from the Centre came and pick the Ratty and went away. Ratty was so sad that he lost his only friend but he was sure that just like him the girl will come to his rescue. The next day, to Ratty' s surprise, the girl came to the reserve Centre to adopt Ratty. This was the happiest moment of his life.

title: Scatter the Rice Clouds
text: “Look Bor,” Iba pointed at the deep blue sky covered with fluffy white clouds. “It looks like blobs of rice pudding!” Little Bor laughed at his sister. “It does, Kong kong! They look like ja-shulia, my favourite sticky rice!” Iba and Bor grew up among lush forests and paddy fields. Their village was famous for rice. They often saw elders making delicious putharo rice cakes and rice drinks with jarut. A soft meowing sound appeared from behind them. Kemnai, their cat, had crept in. “Kumno, Kemnai!” Iba said, picking up the fluffy creature. “What do you think of the clouds?” “Purrrrr,” Kemnai answered, running out of Iba’s arms. Off they went after Kemnai, following his lead. Swoosh! They ran past the elders and the rice field. Suddenly, the sky began to change. It grew darker and thicker, changing from rice cakes to grey dust, casting a shadow over the village. Iba and Bor grew worried. “What is happening, Kong kong?” Bor asked, looking up at the sky. “I’m not sure,” Iba said, watching the clouds intently. “But it looks like a storm is coming.” As soon as she said those words, a thunderous sound echoed through the fields. Pitter-patter, large raindrops had begun to fall. Iba used her apron to keep them dry. “Bor! Kemnai has led us close to the shed where the elders work. Let us go there,” Iba yelled, pointing at the shed in sight. They quickly ran inside to escape the rain. Lo and behold! Mama, their uncle, was there. “Oh, children!” Mama said, “I was just taking the rice inside. Come, come, help me before it gets soggy from the rain.” Iba and Bor sprang to help. “Yes, Mama. Come Bor, we must save the rice from getting spoiled,” said Iba. They were able to take the rice drying on the shylliah inside. “Thank you, children,” Mama said while he lit a lamp, shining a warm glow on their faces. “Looks like we’ll be waiting here till the rain stops,” he said as they looked out of the window. The children noticed the items that were lying around Mama’s shed. “Mama, can you show us what you are working on,” they asked. Thud…. ﻿ Thud…. Thud…. “Of course. We are going to grind the rice to make a fine powder,” Mama said, taking out his synrei in hand and thlong, starting to pound the rice. Thud-thud-thud, he pounded the rice. The children marvelled at Mama’s strength and the way the grains danced in the thlong. Thump! A loud sound filled the room. Kemnai had gotten onto the pdung and scattered the rice everywhere. “Oh no! Catch him children! I hope the rice is not spoilt!” Mama shouted with alarm. The children grabbed the little feline by its fur. “Meowww,” he resisted. “He’s made a mess,” groaned Iba. But Bor noticed something else. “He’s made rice clouds!” he gleefully pointed out. “See Mama?” Looking down at the scattered rice, indeed they saw specs of grain merged into clouded clusters. “You’re right Bor!” Mama’s concern melted into a smile, struck by his nephew’s imagination. “You’ll see many kinds in the sky. But only these will be made by a cat’s paws,” he chuckled. Just then, the clouds began to scatter and break apart, just like the rice. Soon, the clouds cleared up, painting the great big sky with the colours of a rainbow. "Are you sure Kemnai isn’t a magical cat?” smiled Mama looking at the clear open sky. Iba and Bor laughed and hugged Kemnai, grateful for his playful spirit that had scattered the clouds and brought a joyful sky to their village. From that day on, whenever the sky was filled with clouds, Iba and Bor would look for Kemnai and rice to play with, hoping to scatter the clouds once again and create more rainbows for their village to enjoy. Spot the Hidden Animals! There are many types of clouds. The clouds Kemnai made are called ‘Altocumulous’ clouds because of their shape in the sky. Can you spot the animal shapes in the altocumulous clouds? Try to find all of them!
author: Samanda N Pyngrope

title: We Are Making a Book
text: We are making a book! For Silverfish The Book Makers Paper wasps build their nests out of wood pulp. They chew wood into a paste which hardens as it dries, making the nest solid and waterproof. A fresh pile of animal dung is both a home and a meal for dung beetles! Some dung beetles, also called rollers, shape the dung into a ball, roll it to a safe place, and lay their eggs in it. Ants may be tiny, but they can carry things that are 50 times their own weight, or more! They tap their antennae to communicate, and work so well together that they are often called a ‘superorganism’. Leafcutter bees cut semicircular pieces out of leaves, which they chew up and use as nesting material for their eggs. Leaf rollers are moth caterpillars that live on plants. When disturbed, they drop down from the plant on a silk thread. They also use this silk to make a tent out of a rolled leaf, inside which they transform into adult moths. Signature spiders build large webs with a characteristic X-shaped ‘signature’ in the centre. The signature may attract insects towards the web, or warn birds and other animals to stay away. Tailorbirds use their sharp, needle-like beak to make nests by stitching leaves together with strands of grass, spider silk and plant fibres. Snails and slugs have soft, moist bodies and secrete a sticky slime. This helps them stick to vertical surfaces, and even move while upside down! Fireflies talk to each other using flashes of light from their behinds! They come out in the dark, when their light glows the brightest. Silverfish are small, fast-moving insects that are most active at night. They often hide in old books to eat their favourite meal: paper a nd book-binding glue.

title: The Robin And The Peacock
text: Once upon a time there lived a peacock in a jungle. The peacock's name was Samuel. He was not like the other peacocks because he was born in colorful feathers while the others were having white feathers. Samuel was very happy and active but the others were dull and serious, Samuel loved playing games but the others hated playing games. Samuel was feeling left out and he decided to move to a new home and he set off to find a home. He walked for several days and he still did not give up. At last on the eighth day he finally found a much larger jungle to live in. He was so thirsty he quickly ran and found a watering pond and started drinking water from the pond and he made lots of new friends! Samuel was enjoying his time and made his home in a tree until he saw a robin just nearby his home. He went towards the robin and asked her name she said her name was Sally and she was very kind. One day Samuel and Sally heard screaming and quickly flew high in the sky to check what was going on. Shocked they saw some large yellow glowing light in the distance. It grew more and more brighter but they realized it was not the sunrise but it was a... "FOREST FIRE!!!", cried Sally. "We have to save the animals NOW!!!", shouted Samuel. They both swooped down to see what was going on. The saw the animals in danger and they used all their strength to take out the fire and rescued the animals from the fire safely. As they saved all of them, the animals cheered, "All thanks to Samuel and Sally!". The animals took them towards their king a tiger whose name is Daniel. He said thank you for saving us but where should we live? Samuel took them a forest he passed by while he was searching for the Jungle that got burned down so he and the animals went to the jungle and they lived happily ever after. Written By Eva Abigail Sakki

title: The Mysterious Time Loop
text: Hello to everyone. I hope everything is going well for you. This is the story of Pavani, a teen who faces the same daily struggles that everyone does. The character's descriptio n Pavani is a talkative and intelligent young girl. She's also a good athlete. She is presently in tenth grade. She has also received the class monitor badge ten times in a row. Nobody could ever beat her. She is every teacher's favorite kid. however, she can get easily distracted. Everyone wishes they could wake up to the sound of birds chirping. Ohh! What a lovely sensation. However, the lead character Pavani awoke to her mother's scolding "Ahh! "I am awake; please stop shouting," Pavani cried tiredly. Pavani awoke as usual, brushed her teeth, and bathed. When she looked in the mirror, she noticed she didn't have any earrings or a necklace on. She suddenly remembered that she had taken it off since her body ached from dancing so much at her best friend's birthday party the day before. After intense searching she discovered her necklace in the drawer, but she couldn't find her earrings anywhere. She looked under her bed, under her table, and everywhere else she could think of. She had forgotten where she had kept the earrings. She dashed downstairs and asked her mother if she might have one earring for the day. Amrita, Pavani's mother, had an extensive jewellery collection. Her earring collection impressed her. She came across a small old box while skimming through her's mom's collection. She opened it because she was curious. A stunning earring with white pearls attached. She was drawn to the elegance of the earring and decided to wear it. Then she heard a bus horn and realized taht her bus was waiting for her outside. She then went away and said, "Bye Amma," to which her mother replied, "Bye dear." On the bus, she sat next to Apoorva, her bestie who had hosted the party the day before. How was the party? Apoorva inquired It was euphoric! Pavani responded. They were speaking the entire time. When they arrived at school, Apoorva discovered that it was dance class today. "Oh no!" Apoorva shrieked. She hated the dance teacher because she used to teache all the most difficult moves and scolds all frequently.{Expect Pavani}. "You will manage it " replied Pavani. Math was the first class they attended. Pooja ma'am conducted a surprise test. Except for Pavani, everyone was depressed. While the ma'am was distributing the paper, the principal declared over the loudspeaker, "Students and Staff, The government has declared all schools to be closed." Everyone was overjoyed. "No dance class today," Apoorva exclaimed. All of the pupils boarded the school bus and drove away. Pavani shouted "Amma, Amma" as soon as she walked in her house, then realized her mother had gone to work. She freshened herself, put on some new clothes, prepared pulav, and ordered an ice cream with her monthly budget. She then went to bed and slept comfortably. ''Wake up Pavani, " her mother yelled. Pavani awoke and walked downstairs to embrace her mother. Have you brushed your teeth? "Yes," Pavani replied to her mother's question. Pavani, don't lie and get ready for school. Pavani was taken aback. She looked at the calendar and noticed that the date had been repeated. "How," Pavani exclaimed. She rushed to her room to get dressed for school, convinced that her mother was playing a prank on her and that she had overslept. Pavani sat beside Apoorva while waiting for the bus this time. "How was the party?" Apoorva inquired. "Why are you asking me this again?" informed Pavani When did I ask you this question? Apoorva inq uired. "Yesterday" Pavani quickly responded. My father dropped me off yesterday, and you came to my party last night. Remember? Apoorva inquired. The same thing occurred in math class. The same goes for the unexpected holiday. After she came home, Pavani proceeded to make some more Pulav and then fell asleep. This time lapse was repeated at least ten times. She couldn't take it anymore. And then Pavani tried to figure out why this was happening. Why do you think Apoorva is facing this again and again. 1. Is her mother and friends playing a prank on her. 2. Or is it a dream. The 2nd part will be uploaded on 12th August Meanings 1. Skimming - reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 2. Euphoric - characterized by or feeling intense excitement and happiness.

title: Koo's lost song!
text: He was everyone's favorite in the village- his family, friends! Pintu loved all kinds of mischief, but his one inseparable partner was his catapult! He would never let it out of his sight! Wherever Pintu would go, the catapult would follow! In front of Pintu's house, stood a magnificent mango tree! Every day, he would aim at the tree and gobble at least two, even three mangoes! On another such day, Pintu, eager to eat mangoes, aimed at the tree with his catapult! crashhhhh! Something fell from the tree! Pintu panicked! When he went closer, he saw a fallen cuckoo! Poor bird was badly injured! The cuckoo had slowly closed its eyes! Pintu was silent! But goodness me!...what was this? The moment Pintu turned around, he saw the cuckoo's nest! He looked closely at the nest and found a tiny cuckoo chick! He gently picked the chick up and ran home as fast as his legs would carry him! He entered home and loudly declared... "Look what I found, Ma!" Ma gave Pintu one of her looks and said - "What is this you have brought into the house? This will take up all your attention now! Another nuisance!" Pintu was hurt by Ma's words but he had decided to look after the cuckoo chick! Day or night, Pintu would not leave the chick's side! He would feed the chick every few hours! He would take such good care of it! Pintu lovingly called it 'Koooooo....'. All day, he would play with Koo!!" But when Pintu looked closely, he saw that Koo hardly ever looked at him. It barely ate or drank and never made the tiniest sound! people around Pintu said - "What kind of a cuckoo is this? It never sings! You should leave her!" Pintu wondered what kind of people these were, who won't even love a bird if it did not do something for them! People's words disappointed Pintu but he did not give up. He had faith that he would help Koo and one day, it would sing! When nobody would be in the room, Pintu would go to Koo and gently whisper "koooo...kooooooo...." in koo's ear but koo never answered. One day, Pintu's father got transferred. Everyone got busy packing and moving to the new house. Ma asked Pintu - "Would you like to take the chick along? I suggest you leave it here beta!" This made Pintu very sad. The night before they had to go to the new house, Pintu sat next to Koo's cage all night. Trying a last time, Pintu said "Koooo....koooooooo... " but Koo did not look at him! The next morning, Pintu cried as he gathered his things from the room! This woke Koo up! It opened its eyes to see that Pintu was leaving the room with his things! Koo was frenzied!! Koo saw Pintu's red shirt and a bag in his hands as far as its sight allowed! And then, all of a sudden, Pintu disappeared from his sight! Koo got so restless! "Koooo.....Kooooooo...kooooo!", it loudly said! When it did not see Pintu coming, it chirped in distress again! "koooooooo.........koooooooooooooooo!" And this is when Koo saw Pintu running towards it! It became so happy! Pintu wiped his tears, picked up the cage and Koo and Pintu started for their new home!!! kooo.....kooooooo!

title: The Curious Kitten's Adventure
text: Once upon a time in a cozy village, there lived a curious little kitten named Whiskers. Whiskers had bright, sparkling eyes and a coat as soft as a cloud. Every day, Whiskers would watch the birds flutter by and dream of exploring the world beyond the garden. One sunny morning, Whiskers decided it was time for an adventure. With a confident leap, he ventured beyond the garden gate. His heart raced as he discovered a forest filled with tall trees and mysterious sounds. Whiskers tip-toed through the leaves, discovering new scents and sights at every turn. As he wandered deeper, Whiskers met a wise old owl named Oliver. Oliver shared tales of distant lands and enchanted forests, sparking Whiskers' imagination. Eager to experience more, Whiskers asked if Oliver could be his guide. Oliver agreed, and together they journeyed through meadows, crossed babbling brooks, and climbed rugged hills. They met friendly squirrels, playful rabbits, and even had a splashy encounter with a mischievous river otter. One day, Whiskers and Oliver stumbled upon a hidden grove where fireflies created a magical dance of light. Whiskers was mesmerized, but he also missed home. Oliver assured him that adventures were wonderful, but there was a time to return. With a heavy heart, Whiskers bid farewell to Oliver and his newfound friends. He followed the stars back home, where his family and the garden awaited him. Whiskers returned to the village with a heart full of stories and memories. He realized that while adventures were exciting, the love and comfort of home were just as precious. From that day on, Whiskers cherished his adventures in his heart and shared his stories with the other kittens. And as the sun set over the village, Whiskers would curl up by the fireplace, knowing that there was always magic in both the world beyond and the warmth of home.
author: Mukesh kumar
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Priya Kuriyan; TAKI team

title: The Story of Happy
text: Dedicated to my lovely daughter and all the dolls of the world This story is a true story. It serves as a source of inspiration and motivation for children, encouraging them to care for their toys, while also offering parents insights into the significance of quality time spent with their children. The story is imbued with emotions, creativity, and a wealth of love, showcasing the happiness derived from appreciating life's uncomplicated pleasures. It's a beautiful illustration of how something as simple as a toy can become a vessel for love, growth, and lasting memories. Ri owned a doll, one among the many in Ri's collection. This particular doll had pink hair and a slender body. As for its name? Well, it didn't have one. It was simply known as "just a doll," blending in with the rest. Interestingly, this specific doll had only one arm. It had lost its other arm during playtime or some unknown interaction with another toy. The exact circumstances of the arm's disappearance remained a mystery. This "just a doll," often referred to as "the doll with one arm," was adorned in a tattered dress that hung loosely from her slender shoulder. Ri possessed an abundance of dolls and toys, and this specific doll held no noteworthy presence among them. Toys indeed possess lives, hidden lives! The instant Ri stepped into her toy room, numerous eyes peered from shelves, cupboards, toy boxes, and even beneath the table, yearning for her attention. If only every child could be aware of this enchanting reality. This one-armed doll, once taken off the main shelf, now rests scattered in various corners. You might stumble upon her anywhere, anytime – be it tucked under a table, nestled within a box, along the bookshelf, or any peculiar spot. Occasionally, she even finds herself beneath the feet of children, inadvertently kicked aside as they move about. Crafted from plastic, this one-armed doll didn't bear the emblem of any renowned brand. Yet, the mention of plastic often diminishes a product's value, both in tangible terms and ethical considerations. After all, plastic lacks eco-friendliness. In the event of plastic damage, it's imperative to promptly deposit it into the recycling bin. Mummy had observed this doll strewn about haphazardly – underneath and atop things, subjected to rough handling, being hurled, kicked, and even used for various experiments. Ri has lots of friends and they loved to play in Ri's toy room. There were instances when Mummy sensed that the doll might have something to convey. However, mummy, always bustling with tasks, rarely found the opportunity to pick her up and attend to her. Shanti, the household helper, had inquired a few times, "Madam, should I discard this doll? It's broken." Mummy's response had been, "Just set it aside," as she immersed herself in her tasks. With a project deadline approaching that very Sunday, Mummy found herself engrossed in her hectic schedule. This morning, as mummy was engrossed in her work, she made her way to the garbage can to dispose of something. To her surprise, her heart sank at the sight of a plastic hand protruding from the side of the can's lid, appearing as though someone sought assistance to escape. Taking a deep breath, mummy retrieved the doll from the bin. However, what she found was a doll without its head and an arm! It was only due to the dress still hanging on that mummy recognized this to be the "one-armed doll." A thought crossed her mind: should she discard it? After all, it was a mere plastic form with fractured limbs and a missing head, and they had a plethora of other dolls. However, she couldn't shake off the image of the hand emerging from the bin. Compelled by that memory, she placed the damaged doll on her worktable. While Ri was at school, mummy swiftly made her way to the toy room, determined to retrieve the missing head of the doll. After a five-minute search, she spotted the head perched atop a pencil. She carefully reattached the head to the doll's body. One day, in the midst of her work, mummy picked up the doll. The doll's gaze met hers, and as mummy stared into its eyes, a sense of amazement overcame her. It was as if the doll had finally been acknowledged. Mummy was uncertain whether this was truly happening or a figment of her imagination. She gently ran her fingers through the doll's hair, sensing a tender smile emanating from it, and then she embraced the doll in a hug. In that moment, it seemed as though both were taking a deep breath, sharing a profound sense of connection and compassion. Mummy planted a gentle kiss on the doll's forehead, offering a warm smile as she spoke, "I'll look after you; just stay here." Over the next few days, the doll remained on mummy's worktable. Whenever mummy found a spare moment, she pondered how she could mend the doll's arm. As mummy gazed at the doll resting on her table, a sense of childlike wonder blossomed within her heart. Picking up the doll, she would hold her close, caress her hair, and in return, the doll seemed to bask in the affection, recognition, and care she was receiving. The presence of the doll on the table became a reliever of stress for mummy, a cherished fragment of her innocent childhood. Sunday arrived, and mummy successfully completed her project. Now, the challenge remained: how to mend the doll's arm? Mummy, lacking expertise in such matters, pondered this new task ahead. After careful consideration, mummy assembled a collection of crafting materials including fabric glue, scissors, cotton, paints, and cardboard pieces. Just as she was contemplating the method, Ri returned from school and found mummy engrossed with the doll. Witnessing parents engage in play or activities with their children always brings joy, and it's a wonderful experience for kids. It serves as a reminder that all parents should dedicate some time to play with their kids, reliving the joy of childhood together. Ri gently held the doll in her hand, and just then, mummy spoke in a playful voice, mimicking the doll, "Hello, Ri." A spark of excitement lit up in Ri's eyes, and she smiled, looking at mummy with amazement. She responded, "Hello, Doll. How are you doing?" The doll's voice (mummy) replied, "I am doing well, Ri. I'm hoping that mummy will mend my arm so I can play with you." Ri enjoyed this whimsical conversation and assured the doll, saying, "Don't worry, doll. My mummy is quite skilled; she will fix you." "Isn't she pretty?" mummy asked Ri. Ri replied, "Yes, mummy. I like her pink hair. I wish I had pink hair." Mummy could sense the affection Ri had for the doll. Ri then asked mummy, "Could you please fix her? I think I haven't taken care of her properly, and that's why her arm got lost. I'm sorry, doll," she said with regret. Mummy comforted her, saying, "It's okay, Ri. I know you love your toys. You must take care of them like how mummy takes care of you." During our childhood, children often had fewer toys. I had only a couple of small dolls, and I would treat them with great care. Each one had its own name, and I never referred to them as just "dolls." I always used their individual names when talking to them. They felt more like companions to me rather than just toys. As I grew older, I had shared most of my toys with my younger cousins, except for one doll named Reena, which I had kept for you and eventually gifted to you. Ri was enjoying mummy's childhood story, Ri loves story afterall she is just a 5 year old child. She told mummy, "I will also take good care of my toys and I'll remind my friends to treat them gently. We'll make sure to put them back in their proper places after we're done playing." "Very good," Ri said, and mummy smiled in response. Everyone fell silent as mummy gazed at the doll, lost in thought. The doll itself seemed to reflect a sense of contemplation, uncertain whether it would be repaired or end up in the recycle bin – God forbid. Out of nowhere, mummy's hands sprung into action. She grabbed a piece of paper, carefully rolling it into a thin tube. Then, using the other arm as a reference, she measured the tube length against the doll's forearm, taking note of its proportions. With delicate adjustments, she matched the pipe's dimensions to the doll's arm, considering the nuances of its thickness and the contour of the shoulder, and skillfully bending it at the elbow. She said, "not bad". Mummy proceeded to use cotton and a special adhesive to craft the shoulder. After coloring it to match the doll's complexion, she created a hand using cardboard, carefully attaching it with the same specialized glue. The result was nothing short of remarkable. Ri's face beamed with pride for her mom. She exclaimed, "I love you, mom!" Mummy rewarded Ri with a new dress for the doll and meticulously cleaned her up. And then, with a flourish, the transformation was complete. The doll looked resplendent. Ri joyfully pointed out, "Look, mummy, the doll looks so happy!" Mummy playfully suggested naming her "Happy." Ri's eyes lit up, and she wholeheartedly agreed, saying, "Yes! I love Happy!" Ri disappeared briefly and returned with a pair of shoes. Mummy added a pair of earrings to Happy's attire. The doll's radiance truly matched her newfound name. Ri suggested adding a handbag and a hair clip for Happy, which sparked a new round of crafting fun. The hours passed delightfully as mummy and Ri worked together. Now, Happy the doll had her identity and a little family. She was no longer the one-armed doll. Ri planted a kiss on Happy's cheek and gently placed her on the doll bed, whispering, "Good night, Happy." In the quiet of the room, whether heard or imagined, Happy softly replied, "Good night, Ri, and thank you, mummy," as she drifted into peaceful slumber, eagerly awaiting another day of play ahead. Activities 1.Do you have any broken toy at your home? can you and your parents together think about a way to mend it? 2. What you do with your old Toys? Teaching kids the value of taking care of their belongings, especially toys, not only instills responsibility but also helps in fostering appreciation for what they have. Encouraging creativity and imaginative play with toys not only enhances a child's cognitive development but also makes their playtime more engaging and enjoyable. Parents can play a crucial role in guiding children to find unique ways to play with their toys. By introducing storytelling, role-playing, and even involving them in crafting or modifying their toys, parents can unleash their children's creativity. Spending quality time together not only strengthens the parent-child bond but also sets a positive example for how they can cherish and use their possessions wisely.
author: Rituraj Mishra
illustrator: CClaire Ingram; El  Marto; Greystroke; Hari Kumar Nair; Jagdish Joshi; Kalp Sanghvi; Kobie Nieuwoudt; Melany  Pietersen; Nyambura Kariuki; Phùng  Nguyên Quang; Rituraj Mishra; Rohit Karandadi; Shamim Ahmed; Sharanya Singh; Tawfiq Ahmed  Anwar; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: The Pink Bird
text: Once upon a time, on a hot summer afternoon, Isabel's mother was working hard. The little girl asked to her if she could go out for a walk. Her mother agreed. During the walk, Isabel saw something on a tree branch. She approached and she saw that it was a little pink bird. Isabel called her mother to show her the animal. They decided to call it Cip. Cip saw them and flew over them happily. At first Isabel got scared, but then she calmed down. Then, they said goodbye to him and they went home. The following day Isabel and her mother went to the well to fill the jugs with water. In the moment when they started to fill in the jugs, Cip appeared. Cip followed Isabel and her mother, flying over them, whilst they were coming back home. The next day Isabel and her mother found Cip flying out of their house and they followed him. Cip flew to a tree branch near Isabel's house. This branch was his new home and he wanted to show it to his new friends. From that moment, every morning, when Isabel was waking up, she could see Cip out of her window waiting for her. Every time that Isabel's parents were working the flour, Cip waited for Isabel to give him some food. Indeed, the little girl was always giving some crumbs to him, as soon as her parents finished to work. One afternoon Isabel was getting bored and she was looking out of the window: Cip flew to her, making her smile. Thanks to Cip, Isabel decided to go out and sat down under a tree. The little bird began to sing a sweet song. Isabel began to dance by hearing such a sweet melody. Later that afternoon Isabel's parents went to the garden and they saw their daughter dancing happily. They decided that Cip could stay with them. From that moment, Cip became part of the family.
