title: Forgetful Dida
text: Dida forgets everything. Ma says she has a forgetting illness. When Dida and I went to the grocery store, I put on my red sandals. Dida put a sandal on only one foot and walked out of the house. I found her other sandal and helped her put it on. “How silly I am,” Dida said. “What would I do without you?” Dida kissed the top of my head. At the grocery store, instead of asking the shopkeeper for bananas and bread, she asked for a blue Maruti car for Ma. I laughed. The shopkeeper laughed. Grocery stores don’t sell cars. Dida smiled and scratched her head. It is not her fault that she has a forgetting illness. Ma was waiting at the door when we got home. She was upset. She said we shouldn’t go out without telling her. My mother worries too much. Like yesterday, when Dida asked Ma what her name was. Ma shook her head and looked at her feet. “Don’t be funny, Dida,” I said. “She is your daughter. How could you forget her name?” Dida smiled and said, “How silly I am. How can I forget my daughter’s name?” Dida looked a little sad. If she didn't have a forgetting illness she would never have forgotten her daughter's name. Never, ever. Dida wanted to go out in the rain today and Ma wouldn’t let her. “I want to go out now,” Dida said and stamped her foot. I giggled. Dida was behaving like a naughty little girl. “It’s raining cats and dogs,” said Ma. She was tired and upset. “Cats and dogs?” Dida asked in a small voice. Dida has forgotten that cats and dogs don’t really fall from the sky when it rains. Ever. Ma felt bad for Dida. She asked her if she wanted to read a book. “Yes,” Dida said, and clapped her hands. Ma gave her a fat book with lots of words and no pictures. “You will love this.” Dida opened the book. “La la la,” she said. She turned the page and said “La la la” again. “Finished,” she said. Dida had forgotten how to read. I looked at Ma, who looked as worried as she had that time when I put a crayon up my nose. “She used to love reading so much,” Ma said. “She is not well. “She is becoming a difficult person. “She is forgetting everything.” Ma looked at Dida, who was counting the bunch of bananas on the dining table, “One-three-ten!” “She will forget all of us one day,” Ma said. “So what if she forgets us, ” I said. “We will never forget her, Ma, will we?”
author: Himanjali Sankar

title: Sringeri Srinivas Keeps His Promise
text: It was the weekly hair wash day for Sringeri Srinivas. He had made a promise not to cut his hair until scientists had learned to manage the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which had caused the terrible pandemic. In three years, his hair had grown so long that he would sometimes trip over it. His hair had grown so long that birds would try to nest in it. His hair would get so dirty that the whole family had to help wash it. Today, as usual, Parvatamma had collected many buckets of water in the courtyard. Homemade herbal shampoo was kept ready. Shiva and Shankari began to scrub their father’s scalp. Just then little Uma came running, waving a newspaper. “Appa, Appa,” she shouted. “Look, look, the government says the pandemic is over!” Sringeri Srinivas got up suddenly. Soapy water got into his eyes and dripped on his clothes. The news was so good that he forgot to get angry. Wiping his eyes, he turned to Parvatamma. “Thank God it is over. And thanks especially to all the scientists for the vaccines and the medicines they quickly made. So, Devare,” he said, lifting up his hands to his Gods, “I have kept my promise. Now I can cut my hair at last.” Parvatamma was very happy. Three years of living with Sringeri Srinivas and his long hair and itchy head had not been easy. The children, too, felt great relief. Months and months of making fancy hairstyles for their father had been hard. And yay! No more family hair wash days! Other families in Chikkooru village were also happy. Many villagers had followed Sringeri Srinivas’s example and their hair was too long and too dirty as well. No one was happier than Bhimanna. Soon, he would be busy cutting people’s hair again. But how could one person cut so much hair? The villagers held a meeting to discuss the problem. “Why not have a hair-cutting festival?” asked Naganna, the carpenter. “We can invite all the barbers from nearby villages to help. We can have a grand feast, too. ” Everyone thought it was a great idea. “OK, but I will be their barber-in-chief,” said Bhimanna, firmly. Soon, barbers from many villages came along with their tools and their families, happy to get some business at last. People gathered in every corner to have their long manes cut. Some wanted to look like popular film stars. Some like cricketers. Youngsters wanted the latest styles. Snip, snip, snip, went the scissors. Ooh, ooh, aah, went the relieved villagers. Just then, little Uma came running, looking worried. “Appa, Appa, maybe COVID-19 is back. There are thousands of new cases everywhere. Our Chikamma has just tested positive too!” “ STOP! ” said Sringeri Srinivas to Bhimanna, who was busy chopping off heaps of his hair. “Now what shall we do?” Everyone fell silent. Scissors stopped moving. Combs fell to the ground. “Relax,” came a booming voice from under a cloud of shaving foam. It was Dr Ashok, from the nearby village. “Yes, the virus has not gone away, but it is less dangerous. We must be careful, but there is no need to be afraid.” Everyone started to talk at once. There was much confusion all around. Suddenly, Sringeri Srinivas stood up from his chair. His hair was half long and half short. Bunches of his cut hair were all over his clothes. The children started to laugh at the sight. He glared at them with his famous frown. They became quiet as mice. “I have an idea,” he announced. “Let us all keep one lock of hair but cut the rest. This lock of hair will remind us that the virus may be down, but it is not out. It will not let us forget that we have to be always alert. What do you think?” Everyone started to talk again. The barbers gathered in a group to decide whether they could agree to such a strange plan. Dr Ashok gave a hearty laugh. “What an original idea! I like it. Manianna,” he said to his eager young hairdresser, “keep some of the hair on the back of my head long. It will remind my patients to take care of their health!” Once the doctor had approved it, everyone decided to accept the proposal. One by one, the hairdressers returned to their customers. Each one wanted a different part of hair to be kept long. The barbers had to be very creative. By the time all the haircuts were done, each villager looked very special indeed. Sringeri Srinivas was very proud of his long single strand, which Bhimanna had curled down to his waist. “Thank you all,” he bowed to the talented barbers, who were busy packing up. Everyone joined the villagers for a grand feast. Byrappa sang his new song, praising the scientists and the Gods. All the cut hair was collected to send to wig-makers, for cancer patients who often lose their hair during treatment. News about this new hairstyle spread far and wide, right up to Doddooru, the big city. Sringeri Srinivas became even more famous than before. Suddenly, hairstylists everywhere had to learn new ways to cut hair. “Now we will all learn to be careful, no matter which virus comes along,” laughed Sringeri Srinivas, twirling his long strand of hair. “I too want a haircut like that,” said little Uma. “Shush,” said Parvatamma, “One in each family is really quite enough!”

title: Mystery of Petunia
text: ﻿Minie and Nenya loved their little puppies. Coco and Chase. They would spend their entire day playing with them and giving them yummy treats. They loved going on nature walks with Coco and Chase. The puppies had a magic power: they could TALK; just like us. They would observe beautiful flowers and often smell them and dance with joy. It was like a perfect life! One day, Coco and Chase started to bark loudly. BHOW! BHOW! BHOW! BHOW! Nenya asked, "Coco, what happened? Why are you barking?" Coco said, "I see my friend Petunia feeling sick and unhappy." On hearing this, Minie and Nenya immediately ran to the gardener. Coco and Chase stood near Petunia and took care of the flower. Butterflies also came and sat next to the flower. Both the sisters called the gardener, "Sankit bhaiya we need your help, our friend is really sick." Sankit and both the sisters ran towards the garden. Suddenly on seeing a new person, Chase asked a series of questions: Who are you? What are you doing here? Can you save our friend? Is this an emergency? Sankit immediately said, " Don't worry, your friend is in safe hands." As per him, plants need three things: We can make simple homemade fertilizer for your friend and it will be like magic. All you need is an egg shell and banana peel. Minie suddenly said "Oh bhaiya, you forgot the most important ingredient. It is love. " Nenya asked, "How can an egg shell make Petunia happy?" This is confusing! Sankit bhaiya said, "Egg gives us Calcium and Potassium. Our plants also love those nutrients While Minnie and Nenya were still thinking, Sankit bhaiya further added, "Oh, banana peel also gives them potassium." Minie snapped her fingers and said, "hurry up pups we need some egg shells and banana peels." The pups ran fast and got the required materials. Sankit bhaiya crushed the shells and put them on the top layer of the soil. He said, "The soil will absorb the shells. Everyone was happy to see Petunia get some help. He chopped the banana peel and soaked it in water. He told the girls, "after 3-4 days you can spray this magic water on your friend." Nenya said, "Thank you so much for all the help! We really appreciate it." After some days, both the girls along with the pups went to spray the magic water. Something happened! The egg shells and banana peel did its magic. Petunia giggled and said, "Thank you my lovely friends. I feel strong and healthy. I hope you all keep visiting me." The mystery was finally solved!

title: The Tunes of Kongthong
text: It is a bright and pleasant day at Kongthong. Kyrpang is excited and eagerly awaits the arrival of his friends to go on a picnic with them. “Bye, Mei!” Kyrpang calls out to his mother as he runs with his friends. Shida smiles as she looks at him and calls out, “Don’t be late, Kyrpang!” Kyrpang crosses the root bridge with his friends Shemphang and Pyndap. Discussing the adventure that lies ahead, Kyrpang says, “since this picnic route is so beautiful, I wonder how lovely our picnic will be!” “We are finally here!” Krypang says, while Shemphang and Pyndap excitedly jump into the stream and say in unison, “We haven’t played in this stream for a long time!” After playing for sometime, Shemphang decides to search for shiny water stones nearby when he suddenly notices something. He points towards a small cave next to the waterfall, “Look! I have never seen that before!” Once they get inside the cave, Pyndap is amazed to see white fishes. “Wow! Look, fishes!” he points. He is followed by Shemphang who suddenly shrieks in excitement, “A crab too!” Enjoying their outing, the boys lose track of time while playing… …when they suddenly realise that they have lost their way. Shemphang, looking worried, remarks, “I think we came this way!” to which Pyndap replies, “No, it was this way!” I n the midst of the confusion, the boys hear a familiar tune coming from outside the cave… They listen intently to the tune as Kyrpang cries out, “Listen, I think I hear someone!” Pyndap, looking relieved adds, “someone is nearby!” Kyrpang responds to the familiar tune by humming his own tune, while his friends look on…hopeful for a response. Suddenly, Krypang hears his own tune being hummed back. “I think someone is very close now,” he says, eagerly looking towards the direction of the sound. Shempang and Pyndap look in the same direction cheerfully. The boys then slowly make their way towards the tune to find Kyrpang’s Uncle emerge before them. “It’s you boys! Why are you still out here?” says the uncle, shocked to see them out in the forest late in the evening, As they walk back towards the village, Kyrpang’s uncle tells them, “Your voice is like the sound of the river nymphs. My grandmother used to tell me stories about nymphs staying in the caves and the rivers singing beautiful melodies. I’m glad you sang your tune and I heard you calling.” “Mei!” cries out Kyrpang as he sees his worried mother waiting for him. “Your son got lost in a cave near the waterfall. Luckily I heard him singing his tune,” Kyrpang’s uncle tells Mei. “I told you not to be late,” Mei reprimands Kyrpang. She then embraces him. Kyrpang hugs his mother back and tells her, “If not for Kongthong’s tunes, my friends and I would have lost our way today!” Shida hums her son’s tune and says, “Our tunes are always there to help us. That is why we sing. They are songs inspired by our ancestral mother – our clan mother. She always protects us. Never forget that and never forget your tunes – your ‘ Jingrwai Iawbei,’ the tune of Kongthong. " “I think I understand Mei. I want to call out to my friends too, we had such a tough day together!” says Kyrpang. Jingrwai Iawbei It is tradition in Kongthong for mothers to compose tunes for their children. The tunes are their unofficial names! Every member of the village has a tune composed by their parents. It is called the ‘Jingrwai Iawbei’. Everyone has their own unique tune, which is sung by others, while calling them, or sung by the person to whom the tune belongs, to inform others that they are nearby. The members of the community are said to be able to recognise each other’s tunes making it the preferred method of calling people. Activity Would you like to have a tune as your name? How about you try composing a short tune for your loved ones, similar to how the people in Kongthong create melodies for each other?
author: Auswyn Winter Japang

title: It's Okay!
text: I can't just forget it.' She smiled but it didn't last long. "Shylie, are you there in the class", she startled and replied. "Call me once you are free." A little frightened, she nodded again. It was three in the afternoon. All were asleep, except for Shylie. "The current across the resistor R1 is 12Ampere...", 'that bird on the branch is so cute, yaar. Wish I would've been a bird. See, how nicely she's preening herself', she chuckled. That chuckle too, didn't last for more than a few seconds. "...and the final answer is 5V. So, that's it for the day. I'll continue tomorrow and don't forget to join at 8 today for the test. Shylie, make sure that you don't miss this one. Ok, See you all, bye.", and her coaching classes ended for the day. "Didi aapka to college me selection ho hi jayega, aap sara din padhte hi rehte ho", Davesh said to which she didn't reply and hushed him. She remembered that she had to call her teacher. "Good evening ma'am", she hastily spoke. "...it has not been that good this year. Your marks have gone low, you're irregular with your classes too...", 'those days when teacher said," the first position is bagged by shylie, congrats." I wish I would've been doing that good', and gradually she grew more and more despondent. She heard her father saying, "she's intelligent, she'll do it. I know she'll make us feel proud. Studying all day, not everyone can do that." 'Everyone has so many expectations from me. While, on the other hand,' she said to herself, later that night, 'I feel very low. My marks are not increasing, nor I've been able to concentrate properly. This pandemic...' she sighed. 'Why is that everyone is able to do, but not me?' She lied her head down, lost again, reminiscing memories of the olden times. Not later did she realise, a solemn tear fell down her cheek; her body looked calm compared to how tangled her mind was.

title: the magic garden
text: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in her garden and exploring nature. One sunny morning, Lily went outside and spotted a beautiful butterfly. She chased after it, but it flew away. Lily was disappointed, but she didn't give up. She decided to plant some colorful flowers in her garden to attract more butterflies. She worked hard, digging holes and carefully placing each seed and she watered them every day and patiently waited for them to grow. After a few weeks, Lily noticed sprouts peeking out of the ground. She was thrilled to see her hard work paying off. The flowers grew taller and brighter with each passing day. One afternoon, Lily was in her garden when she saw a familiar butterfly fluttering near her flowers. It was the same one she had seen before! Excitedly, Lily watched as more butterflies started visiting her garden. They danced in the air, going from flower to flower, spreading joy. Lily was overjoyed. She realized that her efforts had attracted these beautiful creatures. She and her best friend spent time in the garden watching the butterflys. years have passed since then, but Lily's love for nature remains strong. She has planted different types of flowers and even has a small vegetable patch. Lily's garden has become a haven for many insects, birds, and butterflies. The sweet smell of flowers fills the air, creating a lovely atmosphere. Children from the neighborhood often visit Lily's garden, learning about the importance of taking care of nature. Lily's passion for gardening has made a positive impact, not only in her life but in the lives of those around her. She continues to inspire others to appreciate and protect the environment. And so, the story of Lily and her magical garden continues to flourish, just like her beloved flowers.

title: dreams can be true
text: Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lucy who loved to dance. She had been dancing since she was three years old and had always dreamt of becoming a professional dancer. As she continued to pursue her dreams, Lucy joined a prestigious dance academy. She started taking intense dance classes and pushing herself to new limits. The teachers saw great potential in her and encouraged her to audition for a dance company. Last year, Lucy finally got the opportunity of a lifetime. She auditioned for a renowned dance company and was accepted. The excitement she felt was overwhelming She had finally achieved her dream to become a professional dancer. She had worked so hard for this moment and it was all paying off. Currently, Lucy is performing in her first major production with the dance company. Her days are filled with rehearsals and performances, but she couldn't be happier. She knows that this is just the beginning of her journey as a professional dancer, and she is determined to continue working hard and reaching new heights in her career. Every step she has taken, every leap she has made, has brought her closer to her dreams. title: NAVIGATING THE UNKNOWN
text: In the bustling city of possibilities, I found myself at a crossroad, torn between two paths that held equal allure and uncertainty. It was a turning-point in my life, where every decision I took was to determine my coming years. The path of equilibrium, ease, and experience was on one side. It enticed my attention to the promises of tranquility and a well-traveled path. Taking this path appeared to be the most viable one given that it was trustworthy and well-known. But deep within me, an adventurous spirit yearned for something more. The path of drive, adventure, growth, and discovery shimmered on the other side. It teased me with whispers of extraordinary experiences, growth as a person, and dreams comprehended. This path was uncharted with no shortage of unknowns, but it offered infinite possibilities for exploring oneself. Questions encompassed my thoughts like a thick mist as I stood there exploring the possibilities. The fear of failure crept in, taunting me with thoughts of what could go wrong if I chose the unconventional path. I was compelled to follow the well-beaten path by the pressure of societal expectations that weighed heavily on my shoulders. But a smoldering ember of bravery and determination burned deep within me. Life is too short to dwell on regret or hypothetical scenarios, I came to realize. I mustered the courage to make a decision after taking a deep breath and invoking every ounce of the courage that I had.With unwavering resolve, I chose the path less traveled - the path that reverberated with my true wants and desires. As I took a bold step into the unknown,I felt a rush of adrenaline coursing through my veins. Obstacles arose along this new path, putting my perseverance and drive to the test. However, each difficulty offered a chance for growth and learning. I unearthed previously dormant abilities in myself with each step I made. With the passage of time, I realized that taking the uncertain path was the best decision I could have made. It led to encounters with remarkable people, unexpected opportunities, and magical moments. I grew in ways I never imagined possible and discovered a profound sense of fulfillment. In retrospect, I am grateful for the moment of uncertainty that led me to this extraordinary journey. It taught me that sometimes in life, we must take risks and embrace the unknown. Because it's in the midst of uncertainty that we truly find who we are and discover our full potential. So, if you ever find yourself at a crossroad and aren't sure which path to take, remember that your heart has the answer. Be brave enough to step into the unknown, and watch as life unfolds its wondrous tapestry before your eyes. “Embrace the adventure, for it is in those moments of hesitation that greatness is born.”
author: Oishee Banerjee

title: A Nervous Day For Priya
text: It was a nervous day for all the students of Chang's Independent Studies School. Every Body was getting ready for the Math Exam. RRRRRRRRRRRRRRiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiinnnnnnnggggg Rang the bell. Everyone back to the classrooms now said the teachers. It was very quiet and silent in the classrooms. As the teacher handed out the papers and the students looked through them. No Cheating! Said the teacher. Priya was worried and frantically asked her friend Mia who was beside her. "Will the properties of multiplication come in exam " asked Priya, " Yes, Teacher told yesterday said Mia". " Oh No I did not study it what will I do ". "It's okay we can study it, Teacher will give us five minutes" Said Mia. "Ok" said Priya. They both studied and wrote the exams. Priya was so nervous about her answers, But she felt okay when she finished on time. Priya and Mia were so exhausted after their exams especially Math. "I'm so glad that exams are finished "said Mia. "I know right" said Priya. They thought the hard part was over, But it was just getting started. Both of the girls went home happily. The day came where all the parents went to school to see their kid's marks. Everyone was exited, scared for their parents to see their marks. Priya's parents were shocked to see her marks, she got full in all the subjects. "She got 1st Rank in the School". Everyone was surprised that such a small girl like Priya could get such a high position in the school. Priya grew up to be a math teacher just like she had imagined. As the saying goes " HARD WORK LEADS TO SUCCESS "
author: Adithi Preeth
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; Google India; Jemma Jose; Jesse  Breytenbach; Karmacharya K.K; Mohith O; Ouk  Ratha; Sarthak Gautam; Vusi  Malindi; Wiehan de Jager

title: Turtle Timmy is Punctual
text: Once upon a time in the animal kingdom, there lived a young turtle named Timmy. Timmy was a very friendly and helpful turtle. But, he had a little problem. He was always late. One sunny morning, all the animals gathered in the meadow for a special picnic. Timmy was excited and promised himself that he would arrive on time. However, he got caught up in watching a beautiful butterfly and lost track of time. When Timmy finally arrived, all his friends had already finished eating and were playing games. Timmy felt sad and apologized to everyone for being late. They forgave him but explained how important punctuality was. They told him that being on time showed respect for others' time. Timmy felt determined to change his ways. He started setting an alarm and reminding himself about important events. Slowly but surely, he improved. He arrived on time for gatherings, meetings, and even helped his friends when they needed him. Timmy learned that punctuality not only made him feel good. But, it also made others trust and rely on him. From that day forward, Timmy the Turtle was known for his punctuality. And he lived happily ever after, never missing a moment with his friends.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: A Friend in Need
text: Once upon a time in a peaceful village, there lived two best friends named Babu and Gopi. They did everything together, from climbing trees to sharing their secrets. Their friendship was as strong as the sturdy oak tree in their village. One sunny morning, disaster struck the village. A fierce storm blew in, and rain poured down relentlessly. Houses started flooding, and the villagers rushed to save their belongings. Babu's house was one of the worst-hit, and he felt lost and helpless. Seeing his friend's distress, Gopi didn't think twice. He raced to Babu's side, helping him move his belongings to higher ground. Gopi's selflessness warmed Babu's heart, and he realized the true meaning of friendship. As the rain continued to pour, Gopi offered Babu a place to stay in his own home. They spent the night talking, laughing, and keeping each other's spirits high. The next morning, the storm had passed, and the villagers began rebuilding their homes. Babu and Gopi worked side by side, helping not only each other but also their neighbors. Their friendship had grown even stronger. From that day on, everyone in the village knew that Babu and Gopi were true friends indeed, always there for each other in times of need. Their friendship remained as unshakable as the oak tree in their village, a shining example of what it means to be a friend in need. A friend in need is a friend indeed.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The girl who can't find friends
text: There was once a girl named Srishti. She was specially abled. She was very shy. She had a disorder where she could not walk and had to be moved around in a wheelchair. Her father's job required him to transfer here and there. She was a 7 year old with a passion for singing. She learnt many languages and visited many places and was an expert in chess yet she did not have any friends. This year, her father got transferred to Thane, Maharashtra. She moved to an apartment complex with lots of kids. She was very excited to move but she was also nervous to meet new people. During her first week in her new house she felt very bored. The next day, her father told her, "My dear sweetheart, why don't you go out and find some friends to play with! ". Srishti was feeling very awkward to meet new people. Yet she gave it a try. Her father encouraged and helped her to find new people. As she was roaming around in the complex, she met a girl around the age of 8. She was shy and nervous about how people would think of her as she was on a wheelchair. She got the courage anyways and went to talk to that girl. Srishti went to the new girl and introduced herself. The girl was very rude to Srishti but forced herself to introduce who she was. Her name was Haneesha and she was 8 years old. She called Srishti names and was really mean to her. Srishti couldn't handle it, and burst out crying. Haneesha called her a crybaby and left. Srishti went to her home crying. Her mother consoled her. She told her to find some other friends another day. Srishti decided to find new friends the next day. She roamed around her complex. She saw a girl who seemed very nice. She was flying a kite. Srishti went to talk to that girl but before that the girl came to her and asked her name. HI! Who are you? You look new here! She introduced herself and asked Srishti's name. The girl's name was Sahana. Sahana was so sweet and kind to Srishti. Sahana asked srishti to join her for a game of chess and she readily agreed. They were playing in the sports room when haneesha and her gang came. Haneesha came and said, "Sahana! why are you playing with this stupid wheelchair girl?". Sahana said, "She is not stupid. Being in a wheelchair does not make her stupid!" Haneesha kept making fun of Srishti for being in a wheelchair. Srishti pulled herself together and tried not to cry. She continued the game calmly and won. Haneesha was astonished. Sahana was very proud of Srishti. Haneesha and her gang stormed out of the room in embarrassment and rage. Sahana and Srishti laughed and had fun the whole day. The next day, the whole complex got to know about Haneesha being mean to Srishti. They all totally ignored Haneesha. Sahana was very happy. All the kids supported Srishti and played with her. Soon, Srishti was popular. She was the center of attention. Everyone loved and admired her, including her parents. Wow! Srishti is so amazing and cool! I Agree!! Haneesha soon grew very jealous of Srishti. One day, Sahana and Srishti were going out for a round when they bumped into Haneesha. Tears were flowing from Haneesha's eyes. Srishti knew that she was obviously crying. Sahana asked, "What is the matter?". Haneesha said, "Why are you caring about a person like me? Shouldn't you be happily playing with all YOUR apartment friends?" I don't have any friends!!! Sahana and Srishti soon realized what the matter was. Srishti felt very bad. She wanted to help Haneesha in any way possible. She told Haneesha that she could join them for a game of carrom. Haneesha was overjoyed. "You really mean it, Srishti?" she asked with delight. Srishti smiled and nodded her head. Haneesha, Srishti and Sahana grew up to become great friends. They grew up and explored the world together with Srishti. A new future was forged for Srishti, a new world with friends!
author: Bookheart Brave
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Nguyễn  Minh Hải; Partho Sengupta; Pia Meenakshi; Shivam Thapliyal; Sue Beattie; Swarga Bhattacharya

title: The lion
text: Once upon a time, there lived a lion. His name was Alex. He thought that he is the most powerful in the jungle. One day, another lion came. He was more powerful than Alex. The animals appointed him as the king of the jungle. Alex wanted his title of the king of the jungle back. He was thinking how to kill the lion. Then he thought it would be easy to kill the lion at night. In the night, he went to the lion running. The lion heard the rumbling and woke up. He saw Alex coming to kill him. When Alex entered the lion attacked at him and killed him. Moral- Don't think you are the greatest.
author: Vaishnav Thakur

title: Anya's Birthday
text: In just a week it would be Anya's birthday! She was so excited! She had planned a big birthday party and had invited all her friends! Anya told her parents she wanted a pretty dollhouse with many dolls inside. She also wanted new color pencils and paintbrushes. She also wanted a scrumptious chocolate cake from Mia's Cakes, all her friends said Mia's chocolate cake was the best! It was finally Anya's birthday! She ran to her garden and her family sang her happy birthday. They told her she would get her presents in the evening at her party. Anya was upset she couldn't get them now but she thought how fun her party would be. ﻿It was Anya's birthday party time! She and her friends all happily sat around in the garden. They played games and had fun. But, when Anya opened her presents she was upset! She didn't get the gifts she wanted! She felt very sad and went away. Her parents folllowed her. Anya's parents told Anya that she should be grateful that she was able to get any presents as some people don't get any. Anya realised that her parents were right and that she should be grateful. She went back to her party. Everyone asked her if she was okay, and Anya realised she was lucky to have people who care about her. Anya blew out the candles on her Mia's Cakes chocolate cake which was decorated so prettily! She loved her birthday and everyday was thankful for everything! THE END
author: Nayantara N

title: A cat in the jungle
text: ﻿The creatures of the jungle were having a peaceful day when suddenly they heard " MEEEOOOW". Suddenly the tiger said " Who do you think made such a noise ". "I don't know" said the hare. Who do you think made such a noise? He called all his friends the Lion, Puma, Jaguar and last but not least Lynx they ventured through the forest and finally found a CAT The tiger went up to it and said " Where could such a little thing have come from? " Later that day the tiger had decided to keep the cat and raise it like one of the jungle cats His friends agreed to help him. ﻿Everyday the cat would learn to hunt with Lynx ﻿Learn to get used to the jungle with Lion and also learn how to climb with Puma and Jaguar One morning about 2 months after the cat moved in. Someone came into the den where all of the tiger and his friends were staying. It was a cat the cat screamed out loud " MY BABY " and the cat who had been staying with the group ran to stand snuggled it The mother said " Thank you all so much for taking care of my kitten " "What can I do to make it up to you"? The tiger responded "nothing we all had so much fun teaching and playing with him " "Well then we must be leaving now and thank you again" said the cat The tiger and his friends said their good byes The little kitten went up to the tiger and snuggled him and went along with his mother Since then once every week the mother cat took it's kittens meet the tiger and they all lived happily ever after Author's Note:- Hello Readers I hope you enjoyed reading this book Yours Only, Ethan

title: A day in the sea
text: Down below in the sea lived a turtle named Tory Now Tory was just about 8 years old and he was going to go and look for fish to play with. He swam around and found Sally the Seahorse "Hi Sally" said Tory Are you free to play? " Not right now " said Sally Miss Dolphy gave us a lot of homework we need to make a book on seaweed " "OK bye" replied Tory sadly Next he found Octo the Octopus who was resting on a rock "Hi Tory " said Octo " Can you come to play?" said Tory " No " replied Octo I have hurt my tentacle and can't swim well Next he met Goldy the Goldfish " Hi Goldy " Tory said " Hi Tory " Goldy said "Can you come to play?" said Tory No " said Goldy I am still very ill He decided that he was no going to find anyone On the way home he met Mr. Star who was a starfish " Tory why are you all alone " he asked Tory explained everything and said in the end "So today I can't swim around with my friends" So then why don't you swim around alone" said Mr.Star I can't swim around like you but you can can't you? "Yes I can, I never thought of that" said Tory Tory said his goodbyes to Mr.Star and swam all around the place alone
author: Ethan Gojer

title: Ambi's Little Things
text: Ambi passed away last night. She was unwell for a long time. Chimik knows it is time to say goodbye. She holds Ambi’s hand tightly. Leading her out of the room, Ai gently tells Chimik, “It’s okay. She’s finally free of all the pain now.” Chimik nods. She can’t stop crying. In the yard, they see Baba and other men building a delang for Ambi’s final rest. Baba brings out the fire as everyone gathers around the delang. As the delang starts burning, Chimik holds Ai’s hand tightly. She whispers, “Goodbye, Ambi.” Notes of t he bangsi gently fill the air. It seems like the entire village has come to say goodbye to Ambi. With the beat of the drums, people sing and dance. As the sounds of the bangsi and dama surround her, Chimik’s mind fills with confusion. Why is everyone h appy right now? Chimik turns away from the scene and hugs her mother tightly. “Come, Chimik.” Ai leads her away from the delang. The distant celebrations fade into silence. They sit underneath a tree as Ai asks, “Feeling better?” Chimik wipes away her tears and murmurs, “A little.” Ai gently strokes her head and takes out a wooden box. Ai opens it and says, “Look what I got!” Chimik looks inside the box curiously. “Ambi’s little things!” “Ambi wore these bangles everyday!” “These earrings were a gift from Atchu!” Chimik unfolds a cloth. She is surprised to find clipped nails inside. “Are these Ambi’s nails?” "Yes," Ai says. "Keeping Ambi's nails is a special way for us to remember her. We have done this since our great-great-grandmother's time! "But what are we going to do with them?" "We're going to take them to the riverside so Ambi can be with nature before her spirit flies away," Ai gently says. ﻿ “We are keeping the rest, right?” “Yes, we are. Ambi’s little things will help us remember her.” “But I’m not going to forget her!” “I know, Chimik. But when we cannot see her or hug her, Ambi’s little things will make us feel she’s close to us.” Chimik's eyes grow big with wonder. She imagines the little things as a magical thread between Ambi and her. There is still one more thing on Chimik’s mind though. “Why is everyone dancing? I only feel like crying!” Ai gently tells her, “It’s okay to cry. It is sad when we lose a loved one. But we remember the happy times, too. That is why everyone is singing and dancing for Ambi.” “So, I can be both sad and happy when I miss Ambi?” she asks. “Of course, you can miss her in any way you want,” Ai tells her. Chimik finally smiles, feeling Ambi’s presence in the little things. Activity How Do You Feel Today? Could you point to the expression that describes your feeling? Would you also like to share what’s making you feel this way? Surpr ised Happy Confused Excited Bored Sad Angry
author: Eleanor  Sangma

title: A Teacher's Prayer
text: In the land where rivers gracefully flow, In the heart of a nation, with history to show, Lies a classroom of dreams, young minds at play, In the eighth grade, where they learn and sway. Oh, students of class eight, so eager and bright, With dreams in your eyes, like stars in the night, You embark on a journey, an adventure a new, In this world of knowledge, so vast and true. With textbooks as sails and pens as your guide, You'll sail through the oceans of wisdom so wide, Mathematics, Science, and History's lore, In your hands, the future, you shall explore. As you gather the gems of knowledge each day, Remember, my dear students, along the way, It's not just the facts, but the lessons you glean, Of empathy, kindness, and values unseen. So, dear students, as you spread your wings high, Soar towards your dreams, reach for the sky, In the pages of books and in friendships so dear, May your journey be joyful, free from fear. Pride of Jharkhand, so vibrant and strong, You may face hurdle, but you'll right every wrong, For you are the future, the hope of our land, In your hands, our dreams shall stand. In the tapestry of life, you weave your own thread, With perseverance, hard work, and dreams well-fed, Embrace each challenge, for they make you grow, In the heart of your efforts, let determination flow. My students with hearts pure and bold, May your stories be legendary, your futures unfold, As you step into tomorrow, shine brilliantly bright, Jharkhand's future, you are our pride and our light.
author: Sangeeta Kumari
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Karmacharya K.K; Ruchi Shah; Sangeeta Kumari; Students of  Himalayan Public School; Zaheer Merchant

title: The Stray
text: Once upon a time, there lived a stray dog near the streets. Having to steal food everyday and running from animal control was rough. There were marks and bruises all over him as sometimes, he got hit by the shopkeepers or people. No matter how hard he tried, he couldn’t fit in. Every dog pack would just growl and bark at him but not accept him. He lived in a cardboard box close to the streets. One day, he tried to enter a meat factory that was pretty far away from the streets he was familiar to. He went there and soon got lost. He looked around but could not find anything he could remember. Now, his only helpers were humans. Since the only humans he knew always hit him, he was very scared. He tried sniffing people only to hear, “Shoo! Bad dog!”. One person even kicked him on the streets where he got hurt badly. A person named Max passing by noticed him and rushed him to the vet. Thankfully he was okay but now the problem was where he would go. The adoption centers wouldn’t accept him as he had not gotten shots. Max got the dog shots but they still didn’t let him in for who knows what reason. He knew that if he let the dog on the street again something, anything could happen to the dog. The dog still needed a little bit of recovery so max took him in and named it Bella. After Bella was fully recovered, Max decided to keep Bella as they had formed a great bond over time.
author: Sahiti Shrivastava
illustrator: Neeta Gangopadhya; Sahiti Shrivastava; Siddhartha Tripathi; Sunando C

title: A gift of Bhaidooj
text: It was Bhaidooj. My sister and I were very excited. My sister, Moni, wore a beautiful, old fashioned saree, but she looked really cute. I wore a smart beautiful kurta and pyjamas. She said,” You are looking good”, but I said,” You are looking quite the opposite.” She got angry but I laughed at her. Mother quickly got the plate for the ritual ready. We sat down and Moni applied ‘a tilak’ on my forehead. I forcefully forced a rasgulla in her mouth. She was anxiously waiting for a gift. I said, "What gift! No gift!" She said "What! But I gave you a gift. Its cheating. You can't do that." I said, " Ha ha ha. Take this egg”, and saying I handed over a box to her, with an egg in it. She left the box on the floor and ran after me yelling, “An egg!” I said, "Check the box!”. She checked and her joy knew no bounds. I was confused. She ran all over the house She danced all over the house with the box. She said "Thanks brother! This is the loveliest gift I have ever seen’. I asked her, "You liked an egg?". I was surprised, the egg had hatched and a chicken was popping out. What started as a joke finally ended as a real loveliest gift. This is the best Bhaidooj I have had so far.
author: Biswarup Bhattacharjee

title: Adventure with Adverbs
text: Adverbs are words that describe or modify a verb, an adjective, another adverb, or even a whole sentence. Here are a few examples. Describe a verb – He spoke quickly. Quickly is an adverb that describes the verb spoke. Describe an adjective – She is very thin. Very is an adverb that describes the adjective thin. Describes another adverb – Kavya finished her test somewhat hastily. Somewhat is an adverb that describes another adverb hastily. Modifies a whole sentence – Fortunately, the rain stopped. The adverb fortunately modifies the sentence – the rain stopped. Let us learn more about adverbs through an adventure of Ruby and Bunny Roshan. Once upon a time in the colourful town of Grammarville, there lived a curious young girl named Ruby. Ruby loved exploring and discovering new things. One sunny morning, she decided to go on an adventure to learn about adverbs. As she skipped along the cobblestone path, Ruby met her friend Roshan the Bunny. Roshan hopped excitedly and said, "Ruby, let's explore the forest together!" Ruby agreed, and off they went. 1. Quickly, they reached a beautiful meadow with tall, swaying flowers. Ruby said, "Roshan, look how the flowers dance!" "Yes," replied Roshan, "they dance gracefully." Adverbs: Quickly Gracefully 2. As they continued, they encountered a river. Roshan leaped over it easily, while Ruby jumped carefully to avoid getting wet. Adverbs: Easily Carefully 3. They found a tree with a hidden door. Roshan knocked gently, and a wise owl named Oliver opened it. Oliver spoke wisely about the secrets of the forest. Adverbs: Gently Wisely 4. Later, they stumbled upon a squirrel named Sammy, who chatted excitedly about his nut collection. Adverbs: Excitedly Ruby learned that adverbs are words that tell us more about actions and qualities. With their newfound knowledge, Ruby and Roshan continued their adventure with adverbs. They described everything they encountered with adverbs, making their day of exploration even more fun.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Artist
text: Once upon a time in a small village, there lived a young girl named Lily. She had a great passion for painting and dreamed of becoming a famous artist one day. Lily is attending art classes every weekend to improve her skills. Lily will participate in an art competition, and she is determined to win. She wants to impress the judges Meanwhile, her parents are supportive and encouraging. They believe that Lily is going to become a renowned artist in the future. They often hire private tutors to help her develop her artistic abilities. She regularly practices painting different portraits. Her determination inspire others in the village. One day, Lily will show her art in an international exhibition. She will show her unique style and creativity to the world. Lily's ambitions and dreams will change her future, and she will achieve success through her passion for art.
author: giulia origgi

title: The Magic in Pottery
text: In a village far away, lived little Aski and her Ambi in a small house on top of a hill. “Ambi is busy every day,” observed Aski. Like clockwork, every morning, Ambi fetched a basketful of Dilka Asta, dug from the shores of the Simsang river. A curious Aski looked out of the window and wondered, “What is Ambi doing today!” Aski watched her Ambi under the scorching sun, as she pounded and hummed at the Dilka Asta … “1, 2, 3 we pound, 3, 4, 5 we ground, and 6, 7, 8 till you’re found.” “Till what is found Ambi?” asked Aski as Ambi peered into the grounded Dilka Asta. “The unwanted bits, little Aski. These little things can cause cracks in a pot while baking, you know,” explained Ambi, as a curious Aski peeked into Ambi’s palms. Growing more curious, Aski asked, “But, what’s the point of all of this, Ambi?” “There’s magic in remembering what our ancestors did, little Aski!” said Ambi. “Come, I’ll show you!” said Ambi, as she led Aski by the hand to a little shed beside the house. Ambi opened the little shed and Aski was transported to a world of pots! Aski gasped, “You made all of these pots, Ambi?” There were pots, cups, and vases of all shapes and sizes lined up across shelves. Everything seemed larger than life. “How could Ambi make everything that is in this tiny little shed?” wondered Aski. "I made all the pots and vases with these," said Ambi, gesturing towards her hands. "These hands hold the knowledge of your great-great-great Ambi…And it shall pass on to you." “We must give thanks to the Simsang River for Dilka,” explained Ambi, handing a blob of wet clay to Aski. “Roll it like this to build the walls of the pot.” Aski heard Ambi whisper under her breath, and her ears perked. “Are you talking to me Ambi?” she asked. “No little Aski, I’m talking to the Dilka,” replied Ambi. “How strange,” Aski thought. Ambi then took a gilarong to smoothen the edges of the pot, all the while speaking to it.. “You have to speak to the Dilka, tell her a story. I always find that the better the story, the stronger the pot!” shared Ambi. “And that is the magic of moulding Dilka, passed down from your ancestors, little Aski.” As Aski attempted to make a pot, she wondered, “What story should I tell the Dilka?” Aski did not know what story to share… She could only think of a time when she was the happiest. “I hope you like my story, dear Dilka, ” whispered Aski, as she started moulding the clay. “The final test of pottery is firing the clay pots,” explained Ambi, as she took both her and Aski's pots to the fireplace, where she placed them on top of wood logs. She set the fire ablaze and whispered words of blessings. Together, Ambi and Aski sat and watched the pots glow. “What did you whisper to the Dilka?” asked Ambi Aski gazed into the fire and shared, “I told her about the time Sisa and I went to Simsang. She was trying very hard to catch a firefly, and she ended up falling right into the mud. I couldn’t stop laughing!” “It is one of the last memories I shared with Sisa before she left for the city,” Aski recollected. Lost in her thoughts, the fire crackled and it brought them back to the pots. “Aanndd…they are done!” Ambi said as she stoked the pots out of the ashes. Aski watched carefully, her breath held as Ambi took the hot red globes from the fire. As Ambi splashed cold water on the pots, the steam rose and an oddly shaped pot revealed itself! “It didn’t break, little Aski!” said Ambi with glee. “I did it, Ambi. I made it!” exclaimed Aski, proudly looking at the smoke rise up. “Does this mean I now have magic in me, Ambi?” asked Aski, hugging the pot she had moulded. “You do, Aski” Ambi responded. “Also, now you carry history in the palms of your hands!” whispered Ambi. Activity Can you help Aski pick out the unwanted bits from the Dilka Asta, and sort them out? You can follow the steps given below. 1. Look at the colorful dots on the Dilka Asta on the left side of the page. 2. Differentiate the colours, count, and make a note of them on the right side. One has been done for you.
author: Nida Hynniewta

title: The magical vada pav
text: If you ever go to Mumbai, deep into its streets, you must stop to eat Dhagadu’s vada pava. Well it is easy to find his shop even in the rustling and bustling of this busy city. Dhagadu is a simple villager who migrated to the city years ago in search of a better life. Dhagadu came from a small village in Maharashtra. He grew up watching his mother cook delicious meals for the family, and over time he seemed to inherit her culinary skills seamlessly. As a child, he had always been fascinated by the magical way his mother transformed simple ingredients into flavorful dishes. Little did he know at that time that this talent would be useful one day. His vada pav do sell. They are a symphony of flavors and textures, carefully crafted with time, love and precision. Every day he gets up at four in the morning to boil potatoes and prepare masala for his vadas. Vadas are potato patties made of boiled potatoes, mashed and mixed with finely chopped onions, green chillies and species. They are then rolled into small balls and finally dipped into chickpea batter before getting deep fried. Pav is the square shape soft bread bun and while serving fresh vadas Dhagadu applies special chutney sauce to the pav before neatly placing the vada in it. People from all walks of life; school students, college students, office-goers, shop and factory workers, hungry passerby's and anyone else who would have it on chance to visit the nearby market would flock to his stall. Dhagadu made sure that he himself served every vada pav with authenticity, warmth and care. Soon, his stall became a popular destination for food lovers in the vicinity. One hot day, while serving customers as usual, his phone rings and its urgency is evident. On the other end of the line, a voice from his ancestral village delivers a message laden with gravity. Dhagadu's heart sinks as he listens carefully, knowing that duty now calls him home for its his mother, his dearest and most important family member, lies at the village hospital in the clutches of illness, and as a dutiful son he has to go. Without a second thought, he gathers everything, shuts down his stall and heads home. Days pass into weeks, and his mother gradually but steadily begins to regain her strength due to her only sons’ loving presence and care. Her eyes, once weak and clouded with illness, now shine dimly with gratitude and a longing for him to stay, but Dhagadu with a heavy heart knows that he has to leave as all his savings are gone and in the village there is no way to earn a decent wage. Dhagadu once more as countless villagers, embarks on his return journey and is back to his street. As usual he gets up early in the morning and prepares vadas and waits for his daily customers. However, to his surprise and disappointment, this time he notices that his loyal customers; who once would gleefully wait in long lines in front of his stall had apparently deserted him. Instead, they were now visiting other vendors who had sprung up around during his absence. After some uneasy days of waiting and watching he meets one former customer; a student whom he occasionally provided free vadas in the past for his family was going through a rough financial period. This student recognizes him in the busy vegetable market and stops to greet him. In their ensuing conversation Dhagadu asks why he does not visit his vada pav stall now that it is open. The boy explained, "Oh, Uncle Dhagadu, I missed you so much” but he continued, “in your absence we all started visiting other vendors as we did not know where you were and when you would return”. However, the boy promises to help him revive his business once again. He makes a call to his friends and narrates how he met Dhagadhu and why he has promised him help. "Guys, what do you say we give Uncle Dhagadu's stall another shot? It would mean the world to him, and we could relive those amazing vada pav moments together. Let's all go there after school and spread the word to our other classmates too" After school, the friends get together and start preparing colourful and vibrant posters. They decide to make ads and print posters. Each poster was original, adorned with vivid designs, mouthwatering illustrations of vada pavs, and heartfelt messages that resonated with their shared memories of the stall. Some of the posters boasted slogans like: Rediscover the Magic of Dhagadu's Vada Pav! "Taste the Tradition, Feel the Love!" The school boys get together and start pasting their hand made or printed posters on the street walls and in the nearby shops. Looking at the enthusiasm of the school boys, a few college students too join them. And they decide to help Dhagadu. Hence they begin posting messages on social media. The following morning, as the sun bathes the city in its warm light, Dhagadu gets his vadas and pav ready. He waits and surely his vada pav stall this time starts getting busy - old and new customers students and workers line up outside while he happily greets and serves them personally. These days Dhagadu is very busy, not only because of his visiting customers but also because he is posting his vada receipes on social media. Moreover, he knows that he has some very faithful student customers to thank for reviving his business. They come often and enjoy his vada pavs made with all the love and care ever imaginable. Would’nt you too?

The Meeky Monkey, the Cheeky rabbit, Jumbo elephant, blackly bear, petty pig,Sally squirrel and a duck. They go to school and love to play together in the school playground. All these animals,often meet a boy Sunder who reside in a small house. He is a good friend to Meeky,Sally, jumbo and other animals. The monkey, the cheeky rabbit, Jumbo elephant, blackly bear, petty pig,Sally squirrel and duck go to shopping to buy breakfast ingredients. bread, butter, berry jam, eggs, yogurt, fruits waffles, cake powder etc. They grab the shopping cart and attempted a small adventure with the help of a shopping trolley. The Meeky Monkey tries to eat bread and bananas on its way.The Dodo duck said " Meeky the items need to be billed, don't open the packet". Each of them was in extreme playfulness and said "Hurray! Hurray! Hurray!. The blackly bear, petty pig, Sally has shacked there hands finally drove the trolley to the billing counter and little boy "Sunder" paid the bill In meanwhile, the Meeky, the Cheeky, Jumbo and a little boy Sunder have clapped,laughed, giggled, chattered and stomped. Breakfast is cooking in the kitchen. La la la -a-la … Monkey is all set on its mark to prepare w affles and muffins. Monkey prepares by baking the waffles with buttermilk. It opens the microwave oven door and gently puts the tray inside full of waffles and muffins. A happy monkey has a blush on its face, feels great about itself and closes the door and sets a timer of oven. Nobody was lazy and unfriendly to make breakfast for themselves. Here comes the Meow furry cat chosen to prepare a butter toasted bread and jam. It calmly switched ON the bread toaster and finished applying butter and berry- jam on its sides with a spatula and topped on it with chopped nuts. They SING A SONG and prepare food for King Lion and to themselves. "Breakfast is something to eat in the mornings. Do -do- Dudu- do. Wake up early in the morning. La la la -a -la … la la la.. It is cooking on the stove and in oven. Do -do - Dudu-do. Breakfast is cooking in the kitchen. La la la -a-la …la la". The petty pig and Sally squirrel prepares sausage patties, bacon and a ham. The Jumbo elephant makes fresh fruit salad and a coffee cake.The Sally squirrel, first turns off the running tap and puts eggs into that container and lifts carefully and puts on the stove. After partially boiling it strains the water and place each egg in a single cup and serve on the table. Cheeky rabbit makes eggs fried sunny side up with an ease. The Dodo duck serves simply yogurt smooth as silk. Each of them had their favorite and hearty breakfast. AH! "Is it so"? questioned the Cheeky. The Jumbo brought the box placed on the table, and on the other side, the boy closed the box and made ready. Now, the Jumbo carried a special, mouth watering box full of food with it's trunk to school. They all are fun, naughty and hardworking animals.

title: Chako Chaki Tales - A Hungry Panda
text: It was their cozy little home. One night, it was raining heavily with thunderstorms and Chakko was sitting in the tree house and was watching the rain from the window. It was almost dinner time and Chakki asked what she should make in dinner. Chakko said, I want to eat the tasty porridge that you make. Chakki said, I want to eat that too but we don't have enough rice to make it. Chakko said, let me go to the nearby field and get some rice then. Chakko flew under the shade of the trees to avoid the rain as much as possible. It was too dark and Chakko could not find the way to the rice field. He stopped and looked around to see if there was any help available. Suddenly, he heard sound of something breaking. He turned and saw a large animal in that direction. Chakko got scared at first but wanted to check out who it was. Chakko went closer and the big animal turned around. Chakko started to fly back but the animal stopped him. Don't worry - I am a friendly Panda, said the animal. Chakko had never seen a Panda before. He asked the panda, what are you doing here? Panda replied, I live deep in the forest but I have come here in search for food. I am breaking these bamboo sticks which I can take home for my dinner. Chakko said, even I am here in search for food - I need to find rice fields so that Chakki can make some porridge. Panda said, I can help you with that. I know a rice field just outside the forest. Sit on my shoulder and I will take you there. Chakko happily agreed and went to the rice field with Panda. Chakko quickly collected the rice that he needed and Panda brought him back to the place where they first met. Chakko thanked his new friend. Panda said, Welcome! I will now get back to gathering bamboo as I still have to go a long way to my home and I am very hungry. Chakko wanted to help his new friend. He said, why don't you come with me to my tree house. It is nearby and Chakki makes the best food. Take your bamboo sticks and come with me. The hungry Panda immediately agreed. Chakko and Panda both went to the tree house. Chakki was preparing the porridge when Chakko and Panda came. Chakko explained how Panda helped him in collecting rice. Chakki thanked Panda and invited him to sit. Chakko gave the bamboo sticks and rice to chakki. Chakki said, I will make a new type of porridge today - Bamboo Porridge. Chakki prepared the meal while Chakko made dining arrangements in their cozy little tree house. They all ate the delicious porridge and shared their experiences about the forest they live in. Chakko thought - "What a wonderful rainy day!!"

title: Continents of the World
text: Our world is a colourful place, and it has seven continents. A continent is a single large continuous mass of land. Let's embark on a journey to explore these continents. Our first stop is North America, a land of vast forests and mighty rivers. It's home to the United States, Canada, and many friendly animals like bald eagles and beavers. The Statue of Liberty is a historical landmark in North America. Next, we'll travel to South America, a place of lush rainforests and the Amazon River. Colourful parrots and jaguars play here. The Machu Picchu citadel is an important landmark in South America. Now, we're off to Europe, a land of fairy tales and historic castles. You can visit the Eiffel Tower in France and eat delicious pasta in Italy. The Colosseum in Rome is one of the seven wonders of the world. You may spot one among the 17,000 Brown Bears in Europe. Our adventure continues to Africa. You'll meet magnificent lions, African elephants, and explore the Sahara Desert. Mount Kilimanjaro and the Great Pyramid of Gaza are in Africa. Next stop is at Asia, the largest continent. You'll discover the Great Wall of China, the Taj Mahal in India, and so much more. The oldest civilization in the world, Mesopotamia, was in Asia. And, you can’t miss the peacock dancing. Australia, the land Down Under, is our next destination. Here, kangaroos hop and the Great Barrier Reef hides beneath the sea. This continent is also known as Oceania. Oceania includes several small islands in the Pacific Ocean and the largest island Australia. Finally, we reach Antarctica, a land of ice and snow. Here adorable penguins slide on icy slopes. Did You Know? Eurasia = Europe + Asia America = North America + South America Quiz Time: 1. How many continents are there in the world? 2. Which is the largest continent? 3. Which continent has kangaroos? 4. The Eiffel Tower is in which continent? 5. Canada is in which continent? Answers - Quiz Time: 1. How many continents are there in the world? - Seven 2. Which is the largest continent? - Asia 3. Which continent has kangaroos? - Australia 4. The Eiffel Tower is in which continent? - Europe 5. Canada is in which continent? - North America
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The Ghostly Prankster
text: Once upon a time, in the small town of Spooksville, four kids named Tim, Lucy, Alex, and Sarah decided to spend a night at the town's legendary haunted mansion. It was said to be the spookiest place in town, filled with tales of eerie occurrences and restless spirits. As the night fell, the moonlight bathed the haunted mansion in an eerie glow. The kids huddled together in the dimly lit living room, their flashlights casting long, haunting shadows on the walls. Tim: [Whispering] Are you sure about this? This place gives me the creeps! Lucy: [Nervous] Don't be such a scaredy-cat, Tim. We're here for a spooky adventure! Alex: [Bravely] Yeah, we're not afraid of a few ghost stories. Sarah: [Excited] And I heard there's a real ghost here! Little did the other kids know, Sarah had a mischievous plan up her sleeve. She had arrived at the mansion earlier in the day and had prepared to give her friends the scare of their lives. As the kids ventured further into the dark mansion, strange things began to happen. Creaky doors opened and closed on their own, ghostly moans echoed through the hallways. Tim: Did you hear that? I swear something's here! Lucy: [Nervous] I don't know, but we need to stick together! Alex: This place is way spookier than I thought. Sarah: [Suppressing a grin] We're in for a night of thrills! The kids moved deeper into the mansion, and the ghostly activities became even more bizarre. Objects floated in mid-air, eerie faces appeared in mirrors, and cold gusts of wind sent shivers down their spines. Sarah: Guys, I think we're getting closer to the ghost. Unbeknownst to her friends, Sarah slipped into a ghost costume she had hidden in her backpack and put on a translucent mask to complete her haunting look. She waited for the perfect moment to reveal herself as the "ghost." Sarah: [In a spooky voice] Boooooo! I am the ghost of Spooksville Mansion! The other kids screamed and stumbled over each other in a frenzy, desperately trying to escape the supposed ghost. Tim: It's real! It's real! Lucy: Run for your lives! Alex: We're trapped! Sarah (as the ghost): [Bursting into laughter] It's just me, guys! It's Sarah! Relieved and then slightly annoyed, the other kids stopped and stared at their friend, who was now holding up her mask and laughing hysterically. Tim: You scared us half to death! Lucy: That wasn't funny, Sarah! Alex: Okay, you got us good. Sarah: I couldn't resist! I wanted to make our haunted house adventure unforgettable. In the end, the kids couldn't help but laugh at the absurdity of the situation, and Sarah's ghostly prank turned their spooky night into a hilarious memory they would never forget.
author: krishna rai
illustrator: AVNI MAHESHWARI; Kaustubh  Kamat; Kaveri Gopalakrishnan; Lavanya  Naidu; Shamim Ahmed; Sheena Deviah; Shruti M; Tapas Guha; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: The Ingenious Adventures of Professor Quillen
text: In a world not too dissimilar from ours, there lived a remarkable individual known as Professor Algernon Quillen. He was a man of science, and his extraordinary mind was brimming with knowledge and innovation. Professor Quillen was passionate about the wonders of physics, and he ardently believed that understanding force was the key to unlocking the secrets of making work easier. One sunny day, Professor Quillen embarked on an extraordinary journey. Armed with a collection of mysterious gadgets and an insatiable thirst for knowledge, he set out to unravel the profound mysteries of force and simple machines His destination was the remote village of Mechanovalley, a place steeped in tradition, where villagers toiled tirelessly, oblivious to the wonders of science that could make their lives easier. Upon arriving in Mechanovalley, Professor Quillen was met with a mix of curiosity and skepticism. The villagers couldn't comprehend why a man of science would be interested in their humble lives. Nevertheless, Professor Quillen began his quest by setting up a makeshift laboratory and classroom in the heart of the village. With unparalleled zeal, he introduced the villagers to the principles of force and simple machines. He taught them about the significance of levers, pulleys, inclined planes, and the marvelous mechanics of each. Professor Quillen used words like "mechanical advantage" and "efficiency" as he explained how these concepts could make their daily tasks easier. Questions Time Question:1 What inspired Professor Quillen to visit Mechanovalley? Question:2 What are some examples of simple machines that Professor Quillen introduced to the villagers, and how did they help make work easier? Question:3 How did the villagers' lives change after learning about force and simple machines from Professor Quillen? Question: 4 Can you think of a real-life situation where understanding force and simple machines can be helpful? HARD WORDS (a) Ardently With great passion, enthusiasm, or eagerness. (b) Intrigue: Arousal of curiosity or interest by something unusual or fascinating. (c) Skepticism A doubting or questioning attitude, often towards something unfamiliar or unproven. (d) Profound: Having deep meaning or significance; very great or intense. HARD WORDS (d) Profound: Having deep meaning or significance; very great or intense. (e) Zeal: Enthusiastic and eager interest or enthusiasm. (f) Ignited: Set on fire; sparked or triggered strong emotions or actions. (g) Mechanovalley" is a fictional place created for the story. The term is a combination of "mechanical" and "valley," suggesting a place where mechanical or engineering principles play a significant role.
