title: Geeta Goes to the Railway Station!
text: My Baba works as a Station Master at the Nagpur railway station. Every morning, he wears his white uniform and goes to work. He has a very important job at the railway station. When he waves a red flag, the train stops. When we waves a green flag, the train moves! When Baba comes home every evening, he uses sign language to explain what happened at the railway station that day! If Baba forgets any sign, Aai always helps him. One day, I asked Aai if I could go with Baba to the railway station. Aai shook her head from right to left and left to right. When Aai makes her eyes big and shakes her head two times, it means I need to take Baba's help. I sat on Baba's lap and begged him to take me to the railway station with him. Baba put his fingers on his chin, made his eyes small, and looked up. When Baba did this, it meant he was thinking deeply. Aai looked worried. She tapped my shoulder and said, "Geeta, there will be many people at the railway station. If you are not able to see Baba signing, you will get lost!" Suddenly, I got an idea! I took a white piece of paper and wrote: MY NAME - GEETA. MY BABA - STATION MASTER. With a safety pin, I put this on my dress. Aai and Baba laughed. Aai said, "My Geeta is a smart girl!" When Baba promised Aai he would look after me, I was allowed to go. The next day, I wore my new purple frock and skipped with joy all the way to the station! When I reached the station, I saw: Coolies balancing bags of all sizes on their head and shoulders. Travellers running from one platform to another to catch their train. Hot tea and samosas being sold at different stalls. After some time, a train stopped by the platform. An old Uncle got down from the train to buy oranges. While choosing oranges from the big pile on the cart, Baba waved the green flag and the train slowly started moving like a caterpillar! I quickly ran to the cart, tapped Uncle's elbow, and showed him my card. When I pointed towards the train, Uncle got very worried. He paid the fruit seller, ran towards the train, and jumped inside! Just before the train started moving quickly like a snake, he took an orange out of his bag and made me catch it. It was his way of saying thank you to me! When Baba and I got home that evening, we shared stories of our fun-filled day with Aai and ate the orange together! Now every time I eat an orange, I think of my day at the railway station!
author: Gayatri Gulvady

title: A Junglee Helpful Monkey
text: Once, there lived a monkey in a jungle. The monkey's name was Sam. He was brown and fluffy. But, he was very mischievious and junglee. He liked to jump from the ropes of one banyan tree to another. But, he was very kind and helpful. Once, Sam was jumping from one banyan tree to another. But, then he saw a sorrowful sight. He saw that a small bird was lying under a banana tree, wounded. Sam thought, "I think I should help this little bird. Let me the take it to the wise owl." Then Sam picked up the little bird. He started to jump from one tree to another. After few minutes, he and the bird reached the house of the wise owl. There, the wise owl examined the little bird carefully. He then put some herbs on the wounded area of the bird. After few minutes, the bird opened its eyes. The bird said, "Thank you wise owl and Sam. You both saved my life." The wise owl replied, "You should not thank me. You should thank Sam because he brought you to me just in time. If Sam would have been late, then the situation could have been worse." The bird said, "I would like to ask the king of the jungle, the lion, to make Sam his chief minister and give him the title 'The Junglee Helpful Monkey'." The bird went to the lion with Sam and asked the lion to give him the title 'The Junglee Helpful Monkey' and make Sam his chief minister. The lion did so. That is why Sam was given the title 'The Junglee Helpful Monkey'. This is the End of the story
author: Aadvika Pandey
illustrator: Ashok Rajagopalan; Daniel Shin; Guru Khanna; Joanna Davala; Seng Visal

title: Lilly Has A Rainy Day
text: Meet Lilly, a 10-year-old girl who lived in a cozy little house on Maple Street. Lilly was known for many things, but one thing she didn't like at all was the rain. Rainy days made her grumble and frown. She'd often cross her arms and pout as the raindrops splattered on her window. On this particular rainy day, Lilly's frown was even bigger than usual. She had planned to have a picnic with her friends in the park, but the rain had spoiled everything. Lilly sighed as she stared out the window at the rain. She wished it would stop so she could play outside. Her mom, seeing her disappointment, suggested, "You know, Lilly, sometimes when friends get together, they can make magical things happen. Maybe if you play with Rose, the rain will go away." Lilly's eyes lit up with excitement at the idea of magical rain-repelling powers. She grabbed her colorful umbrella and rushed to call her best friend, Rose, on the phone. "Rose, Mom says if we play together, we can make the rain go away!" Rose thought it sounded like a fantastic idea. She grabbed her raincoat, and they met at Lilly's house. With their raincoats on, Lilly and Rose ventured outside. They stood beneath the gray clouds, ready for action. Lilly held her colorful umbrella like a superhero's weapon, while Rose had a toy fan that she thought would help blow the clouds away. They chanted, "Rain clouds, go away! Sun, come out to play!" and twirled around, hoping their efforts would work. But the clouds just laughed and sprinkled more rain. Determined not to give up, the two friends decided to make the best of it. They splashed in puddles, drew pictures with rainwater on the sidewalk, and even made a game out of counting the raindrops on their umbrellas. Then, just when they least expected it, the clouds began to part, and a warm ray of sunshine broke through. Lilly and Rose jumped with joy, their hearts filled with happiness. The sun had listened to their pleas, and it was shining brightly now. Lilly and Rose learned that sometimes, even on rainy days, a lot of fun could make the sun come out in the end. They had created a little magic of their own, and they celebrated with a sunny dance in the backyard, proving that sometimes, friends and a bit of fun could change the weather!
author: Annette Francis

title: Vinu's Snack
text: It was time for Vinu's afternoon snack. His empty shining plate awaited a mouth-watering treat. The aroma of melting cheese wafted through the house. Vinu gasped with delight when he beheld four neatly sliced triangles of grilled cheese toast. The beautifully browned bread contrasted with the creamy cheese and golden corn. "Wash your hands first", reminded Amma. With clean hands, Vinu grabbed the first triangle. Something green dropped on to his plate. "Ugh! Spinach. Why did you put it in my favourite toast?" Vinu sulked. "It's good for your health. This will be a better way to include it in your food", Amma reasoned. "It's the worst. I don't like it at all", argued Vinu. "Try it first" Amma coaxed him. "Why?" "Well, because Amma knows best". Resigned, Vinu sunk his teeth in it prepared to hate it. The mild spice of pepper or the usually weird taste of spinach didn't bother him. It was delicious. That was the miracle of cheese. With all four triangles done, Vinu couldn't believe that he actually enjoyed this spinach toast. But something was bothering him. He ran his tongue over his teeth and felt a small corn kernel lodged between his molars. He pushed with his tongue a few times, but that piece did not budge. Using his jaws, tongue and fingers, he waged a battle against that kernel. All he did was make funny faces. "Brush your teeth and gargle well", Amma suggested. Vinu squeezed some paste and thoroughly brushed his teeth. The stubborn kernel popped out. "Aaha!" Vinu exclaimed in satisfaction. Amma did know best.
author: Neeraja Hari

title: Sarah's Special Friend
text: "No one wants to play with me. Why did we move to this new town?" Sad Sarah asked her mom. Her mom comforted her, "It's normal to feel sad, honey. Just be yourself and be kind to others, and you'll soon find your place here." That day When Sarah was coming back from school, she saw a wounded squirrel. The squirrel had been hit by a car and it was lying near the tree. She was shocked and scared, but she can feel his pain, Sarah decided to help the little squirrel. Sarah gently picked up the squirrel, put it in her bag, and ran as fast as she could to her home. Sarah's mother helped her clean and bandage the squirrel's wounds. Sarah cleaned and fed the squirrel every day. With all her love and care, the squirrel became healthy and Sarah's best friend. They played together every day, and Sarah was happy to have her new little friend. All the other children also wanted to be friends with Sarah and play with her squirrel. Soon, Sarah had many new friends from this new town. She was no longer lonely. Sarah understood that it is important to help those in need, even if they are animals. Sarah's mom hugged her and said, "I'm so proud of you. See, even small acts of kindness can make a big difference. Everyone deserves to be treated with kindness and respect."
author: Shreeya Singh
illustrator: Dỗ Thái Thanh; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: Eina explores the world
text: Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Eina. She planned to explore the world, so she started thinking. She was thinking about her thinking. She wanted to travel the world & meet new people. She wanted to see new buildings and new roads. She was excited and started making plans. "I want to see the world." "I want to make new friends." "I want to click so many pictures at different places." "I want to try new food!" "I want to see mountains, rivers, desert and beaches." Now, she started to think how to travel. "Maybe by a bus, or a car?" "Maybe, I should take a train or a plane." she thought. "Oh! I need to pack. I need to put everything that I need in my backpack!", she said. "What about my food? What will I eat?". "Who will cook for me?" "Maybe I need money for the food when I travel." she said with puzzled thoughts. "What if I meet bad strangers when I travel?" Now, Eina started getting worried and scared. Because she has not thought about everything. Her food, her needs and her safety. At home, her parents are there to take care of everything. Thought of not able to travel the world made Eina sad. Finally, she decided to ask for help for her wish to explore the world. The most reliable people to ask for help are parents. And that is what Eina did. She went to her mom and with puppy eyes she said, "Oh my lovely mommy, I have a wish to explore the world." "I want to make new friends." "I want to click so many pictures at different places." "I want to try new food!" "I want to see mountains, rivers, desert and beaches." The Mom saw big dreams in her little eyes, she smiled and said, "Of course, we will!". "We will see beaches, desert, rivers and mountains." "We could try new food." "We will definitely click many pictures at many new places." "We will meet new people." Eina became so happy and excited again. She danced with joy. She need not to be worried about other things while she travel the world. She will be loved, cared and be safe around her parents. Also, she could have loads of fun and enjoy without worry. Few weeks later: Eina is getting ready. Her Mom and Dad is making sure that all the necessary things are packed. And the tickets and documents are collected. At last, Eina will explore the world. THE END.
author: EINAKSHI RAJESH
illustrator: Bhavana  Vyas Vipparthi; EINAKSHI RAJESH; Jayesh Sivan; Zaheer Merchant

title: Lily Shaw
text: Once upon a time, in the bustling city of New York, there was a young girl named Lily. Her parents had reportedly died in an earthquake, or so her aunt and uncle had told her. However, Lily never believed their story, finding it unconvincing. Despite her doubts, she kept them to herself. Lily's aunt, Mrs. Sharma, was a small woman with black eyes and hair that was almost starting to turn white. She was very demanding and made Lily do all the housework, even though Lily just turned five today. Yes, today was Lily’s birthday. Lily longed for some free time to play and have fun, but she was thankful to her aunt and uncle for taking good care of her all these years. Lily was a pretty girl with brown eyes and black hair, and her skin was as white as snow. However, she was self-conscious about the unwanted hair on her body, including her neck, and she often thought that she was not worthy of anything. She was a kind-hearted girl who never refused to do any work and never argued with anyone. But how could a five-year-old girl do everything alone and perfectly? Her aunt used to yell at her a lot. As usual, Aunt Linda was shouting at her. "Are you done, you little twit?" Aunt Linda barked at her in annoyance. Lily had been washing the dirty dishes and cleaning the kitchen, which was Aunt Linda's mess from the night before. Aunt Linda had been watching her favorite cooking channel and made a mess. Of course, she could not cook the food properly, but Lily had to eat the burned food anyway. "Why do you look so droopy? Didn't you sleep last night? I do not want my work to be messy, like you are a piece of trash. I want my work to be perfect, especially today.” said the crooked aunt. “Are there any guests coming?" Lily asked, feeling happy and excited. She loved being around new people, even though she did not speak much to them. “Yeah, wouldn’t you like to know, mind your business, girl and do the work properly? See, there’s a stain? Don’t you know how to clean? What have your parents taught you? Oh! Yeah, you didn’t even have any parents to teach you how to do anything, just like your mother. You are a burden on me. Your mother ran off with a guy; how could she even leave this hairy white monster on my doorstep, and this girl doesn’t even know how to work properly?” This made Lily feel a storm of tears coming; she couldn’t control it, especially when someone was insulting her parents. Lily was very disappointed. “Of course, Aunt Linda wouldn’t remember my birthday." She thought while she was crying. If my parents were here, they would have celebrated my birthday,” Lily thought while crying. “Yeah, here comes a downpour. I’ll get a bucket for you. I don’t want my house to be flooded,” Aunt Linda said carelessly. But still, Lily didn’t say a word. After doing a big insult to that poor little girl, Aunt Linda makes a dirty expression at the poor girl while going to her bedroom to sleep. That’s her daily morning routine: waking up, taking a bath, eating, insulting Lily, making Lily cry, making a mess, and going back to bed. Now let me introduce you to Uncle Leonard. Lily’s uncle had red eyes with silky smooth black hair, and he was tall and handsome. Uncle Leonard was out for a few weeks, which was a relief for Aunt Linda because, as you see, Mr. Sharma loved kids; he loved Lily more than anything. If Mrs. Sharma shouted at Lily, he would always take Lily’s side, but unfortunately, Uncle Leonard was out for work half the time. Uncle Leonard, or no, Uncle Leonard Lily was calm, sensitive, and lonely, but very smart. Uncle Leonard was out for a few weeks, which was a relief for Aunt Linda because, as you see, Mr. Sharma loved kids; he loved Lily more than anything. If Mrs. Sharma shouted at Lily, he would always take Lily’s side, but unfortunately, Uncle Leonard was out for work half the time. Uncle Leonard, or no, Uncle Leonard Lily was calm, sensitive, and lonely, but very smart. She was missing her parents a lot. No one was there to wish Lily a happy birthday, not even his gay and funny uncle. Just then the telephone rang, and Lily ran to pick the phone up she didn’t want Aunt Linda to wake up. Lily picked up the phone, and then someone said, “Happy birthday, my dear child." It was Uncle Leonard. Lily was surprised. "What, uncle Leonard, is it you?” “Yes, my girl, it’s me.” Uncle Leonard replied. “Oh my god, uncle, I am so surprised. I can’t believe my ears. Oh, thank you very much, uncle. You are the first one to wish me, and I am so happy,” Lily said happily. Just then, Lily realized she wasn’t meant to say that. "I am the first one to wish you didn’t your aunt wish you to, or she is again making you work all day, wait till I come back,” said Uncle Leonard angrily. "No, no, no, no I said that mistakenly, I meant to say that you are the second one to wish me. I was so excited that I even forgot what to say anyway. Why wouldn’t Aunt wish me? She is so nice and sweet. She never tells me to work. Why would you think such a thing? Aunt would never make me work. I am so lazy. I sleep all day, and then also, Aunt never complains.” As usual, Lily was telling a lie to his uncle. “Are you sure, kiddo, she never makes you work?” Mr. Sharma said curiously “Yes, I am sure. Why wouldn’t I be sure she never makes me work?" Lily assures his uncle. "Ok, then I have a surprise for you. I am going to tell you when I come back home." “Oh, uncle, you always leave me confused. Please tell me this time, please, please,” Lily said, being excited and curious. “Wait till I come back. I’ll tell you then, sweetheart. Now bye, see you soon, and one more thing: don’t tell a soul about it. Bye.” “Ok fine I’ll wait till you come back. Bye, wait.” "Lily, I am in a hurry; please tell me quickly.” “Be safe; bye again. See you with my surprise.” “Oh, Lily, what would I do without you? Bye, my girl. Don’t make too many mistakes, or your aunt will scold you.” Lily just started thinking about what the surprise would be, and then her aunt started shouting because the AC was making the room too cold, and she wanted Lily to decrease the coldness even though the remote was just near her bed. Lily was saying to her uncle that she was lazy when her aunt is super lazy.
author: Manasi Singh

title: Mini, the sad caterpillar
text: This is a story of a sad caterpillar called Mini. She lived on a dry brown leaf. There were many insects who were troubling her. There was a cricket who used to eat all her food. Poor Mini was very sad because she did not have any special powers like all other insects. One day Mini went in a big jungle. She saw something sparkly. "Wow!" said Mini. She went near it. WAY TO MAGIC DOOR She entered it and saw many animals. Some of them could fly, some walk, and some dance and swim. But Mini couldn't! She met a nice dragonfly with fluttering wings. He said, "Hello, what is your name?". She wanted wings like that dragonfly. ﻿Hi, I am tini-tiny Mini. She saw a colourful ladybug. She wondered if she could ever have such pretty colours. She met a spider. He was making a web. Are you busy? No. How can I help you? I want to learn how to make web. Can you teach me? The spider taught Mini how to make the web. Yes﻿, I will. Mini tried to make the web but she made a cocoon. The next day, Mini broke the cocoon and started to come out. And she was very happy because she was flying. She had colourful wings. title: Hopper Settles Down
text: Appu and Ammu have a pet rabbit called 'Hopper'. They got it as a gift from their parents for topping the exams. Hopper was a very meek, scared rabbit when he came home. Soon, however, he became a member of the family. Everyday, in the morning, he would eat breakfast with them. While the children ate idli and chutney, Hopper ate grass or dry hay. Sometimes, he was given carrots for breakfast. While the children went to school, Hopper would sit with grandma and listen to her stories. In the evening, when the clock chimed four, Hopper would wait for Ammu and Appu at the gate nibbling at the garden grass and eagerly looking out for the children. He would start hopping as soon as he heard their footsteps. He would then run inside the house and alert grandmother by nibbling around her feet. He would not stop till grandmother got evening snacks ready for both of them. Similarly, as soon as father and mother were home from their work, Hopper would once again jump around and alert grandmother. He would also hop to the children's room and made a sound like a growl. Hopper seemed to say- 'Amma and Appa are home. Tidy up your room! Else they would scold!' Isn't Hopper a really clever rabbit? Do you have a pet like Hopper/ have you seen a pet like Hopper? What's special? Share it with your teacher, parents and friends. You can also write them to Hopper on nrutyadhyeya@gmail.com

title: National Birds
text: National birds are birds that are chosen to symbolize a country's identity, values, or culture. They represent the nation’s characteristics, strength, beauty, or uniqueness. Here are a few national birds in the world. The Bald Eagle is the proud and powerful national bird of the United States. With its snowy-feathered head, fierce gaze, and majestic wingspan, it represents freedom, strength, and bravery. The Peacock is India's national bird, known for its colourful vibrant long feathers and dance before rain. It represents beauty, grace, and pride. The Barn Swallow is the national bird of Estonia. It is known for its sleek, forked tail and long migration journeys. It represents the arrival of spring and good fortune. The Green Pheasant is the national bird of Japan. It is a colorful and resilient bird. It symbolizes longevity, good fortune, and beauty. The Harpy Eagle resides deep in the forests of Central and South America and, it is the national bird of Panama. With its striking appearance and powerful build, it symbolizes freedom and strength. The Gallic Rooster is the national bird of France. It is known for its courage, strength, and vigilance. The Kookaburra is Australia's national bird. It is a fascinating and friendly bird known for its laughter-like call. It embodies a sense of joy and is a symbol of the country's unique wildlife. The Bald Ibis is the national bird of Morocco. This unique bird with a featherless red face and long, curved beak symbolizes good luck and is considered sacred. Each of these national birds holds a special place in its respective country. They symbolize various qualities that make them unique and beloved symbols of pride and identity.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: Zach & Spot
text: Once there was an intelligent boy called Zach. He lived in Abu Dhabi UAE with his parents & brother Duke. He loved robots a lot and spend most of his time reading & studying about robots and their programming. After few years, he started building his very own robot dog. He faced lots of challenges while building his robot dog, but he kept at it to fix the problems and move ahead. Finally, he successfully completed his robot dog and was one step away from powering it on. For a Moment he thought of the name he would give to his invention and finally he decided on calling his robot dog "SPOT". After he powered on his robot dog, the dog's big blue eyes lit up and came alive. Zach jumped with joy and excitement. The Robo dog then said... "WOOF WOOF,MASTER... I AM SO HAPPY TO SEE YOU!!" Zach took Spot to his family in the living room to show them his wonderful creation. When Zach family saw spot, they gathered around him and praised him. Spot was curious and asked Zach who these people were. Zach introduced his father, mother and brother to Spot. Spot wagged his tail and said WOOF WOOF when Zach father patted him on the head. Zach told Spot this was his family and he loves spending time with his family. Eagerly Spot asked Zach if he could join his family. Zach was elated and said "OF COURSE", YOU ARE PART OF MY FAMILY NOW AND I LOVE YOU SO MUCH " This made spot happy as he has a family now to care for him and play with him. Spot rolled on the ground like a real dog feeling excited. This made Zach and his family burst out into a big laughter. THE END
author: Miles Gibin

title: THE POWER OF TEAMWORK
text: THE POWER OF TEAMWORK Once upon a time, there was a little ant named Andy. Andy was always busy collecting food for the ant colony. One day,he came across a big piece of bread. Excited, he started pushing it towards the colony all by himself. Andy filling proud and independent, refused their help and continued on his own. Along the way, he met a group of ants who offered to help him. But as he struggled to move the bread, he realized that teamwork would make the task much easier. He humbly accepted the help of the other ants. Together, they successfully brought the bread to the colony. MORAL OF THE STORY Teamwork and cooperation can lead to greater success than trying to do everything alone.

title: Have you seen my shoelaces?
text: In a beautiful tree house lived a cute bear named Bogy. Bogy bear loved swimming and running. He had a pair of red shoes which were his favourite. One morning Bogy Bear wanted to run. Bogy ran to Minny Mouse’s house and asked “Minny, have you seen my shoelaces?” “No Bogy Bear, I have not seen your shoelaces. I was eating my yummy cheese”, Minny mouse said. He saw his shoes and decided to throw them away. When he picked up the shoes the banana peels fell down and there they were his favourite shoes with the shoelaces. Bogy jumped with surprise “hey! My shoelaces were under the peel! Silly me!”, and Bogy laughed and laughed.

title: Ellie and Her Friends
text: Once there was an elephant named Ellie. She lived with her mother. One day, she went somewhere and got lost. Ellie looked for help. After walking for a minute, she met a giraffe named Jaggi. After a few hours, Ellie met a mouse deer named Shawn. Ellie asked Shawn, 'Did you see a big elephant come through?'. Shawn said, 'Yes!'. Ellie asked which way. Shawn said left. Ellie said thank you and goodbye, and went left. After a day passed, Ellie saw something in the distance. So she went that way and she saw a bear's home. She met a baby bear named Jasper. Ellie asked, 'Did you see an elephant pass through here?'. Jasper said, 'I saw one on the hill. But our cave is a quicker way to get there]. Ellie said thank you and goodbye, and went through the cave. Soon, Ellie saw something in the distance. She went that way. She saw her home and saw her mother. Ellie was happy and gave her mother a big hug. THE END.

title: Deepavali - Festival of Lights
text: Diwali or Deepavali is a festival of lights. Diwali symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. People light diyas in their home and burst crackers. People wear new dress. They give sweets and gifts to neighbours. Some draw rangoli designs on their floors. The Diwali date of a year comes anywhere between mid-October and mid-November. In 2017, it was on October 19. In 2023, it is on November 12. Diwali is celebrated by Hindus to mark the victory of Lord Krishna over demon Narakasura. For some it also signifies the return of Lord Rama to his kingdom Ayodhya after defeating Ravana. You can celebrate Green Diwali to reduce the pollution caused by crackers in the atmosphere. You can minimize the use of crackers that emit too much smoke or are too loud. Happy Diwali to all of you! May you sparkle as bright as the festive lights.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The magical signs of Nature
text: Once upon a time, in a small village nestled amidst rolling hills, lived a group of curious children named Maya, Nita, Dev. They loved spending time outdoors, playing in the meadows and exploring the nearby forest. One sunny morning, as they ventured into the woods, they noticed something different about the trees. The leaves that were once lush and green had now transformed into a palette of vibrant reds, oranges, and yellows. Intrigued by this magical transformation, the children decided to embark on a journey to learn more about the changing seasons. They carried notebooks and coloured pencils with them, ready to document their discoveries. As they strolled along the forest path, they observed how the temperature had begun to drop, and the air felt crisp and cool. They made a game out of collecting fallen leaves, trying to find as many different colours and shapes as possible. As they continued their exploration, they stumbled upon a small stream flowing through the woods. The children watched in awe as the water transformed from a glistening blue to a frozen surface, creating a winter wonderland. They marvelled at how the changing seasons affected not only the land but also the water around them. While walking along the stream, they spotted a family of squirrels diligently gathering acorns. Nita pointed out that the squirrels were preparing for winter by collecting food to store for the cold months ahead. The children realized that animals too were influenced by the changing seasons and had their own unique ways of adapting. As they reached a clearing in the woods, they noticed a patch of brightly coloured flowers blooming. Maya, always the curious one, asked, "How can there be flowers in winter?" Dev, being an avid reader, remembered reading about evergreen plants that stay green throughout the year. Together, they learned that some plants, like the ones they were observing, were called winter bloomers and brought color to the otherwise barren landscape. Inspired by their findings, the children sat down on a fallen log to draw and write about their nature discoveries. They sketched the changing leaves, the frozen stream, the busy squirrels, and the vibrant winter flowers. They were amazed at how much they had learned about the changing seasons simply by observing the wonders of nature around them. As they headed back to the village, the children couldn't help but feel a newfound appreciation for the beauty and intricacy of the natural world. They realized that nature was the best teacher, constantly guiding and enlightening them about the wonders of the changing seasons. They couldn't wait to share their knowledge with their friends and family, eager to inspire others to connect with nature and learn from its ever-changing rhythm.

title: Gauri's Nature Walk
text: Once upon a time, there was a girl named Gauri who had always been fascinated by the beauty of nature. Her curiosity led her to explore the enchanting wonders of the world around her, and she spent most of her free time outdoors, discovering new places to appreciate nature. One summer afternoon, Gauri decided to take a nature walk in a nearby forest she had never visited before. She packed a small backpack with a water bottle, a notebook, and a pencil, ready to document her observations and thoughts. As she entered the forest, the air felt fresh, and the sun's rays filtered through the tall trees, creating a magical atmosphere. She noticed a narrow path and decided to follow it deeper into the woods. The ground was covered in moss, which felt velvety under her feet. Around her, different shades of green painted the scenery, from the ferns to the leaves of giant trees. The orchestra of birdsong filled the forest, and as she walked further, she began to notice various creatures joining in harmony. Suddenly, she heard a rustling sound. She stopped in her tracks, trying to locate the origin of the noise. To her amazement, a family of deer appeared from behind a thicket of bushes. The mother deer, tall and graceful, gently nudged her fawns, teaching them to navigate through the forest. When they spotted Gauri, the deer froze for a moment before bounding away in graceful leaps. Gauri stood still, grateful for the rare encounter. Continuing her walk, Gauri came across a small stream babbling its way through the forest. She kneeled down beside it, observing the crystal-clear water. Small fish swam against the current, while dragonflies glided gracefully above. Further down the path, Gauri stumbled upon an enchanting clearing. The sunlight poured through the treetops, illuminating a patch of wildflowers swaying gently in the breeze with butterflies danced around them, creating a kaleidoscope of colours. As time went by, she realized the light began to fade, signaling evening's approach. Gauri reluctantly left her newfound haven and started to make her way back. With each step, she discovered something new, from the intricate pattern of a spider's web to the magical melody of a hidden creek. Finally, as she emerged from the forest, Gauri carried with her a heart filled with gratitude for the beauty and wonders she had witnessed during her nature walk. She promised herself to return to this place, knowing that there was always more to explore and appreciate in the embrace of Mother Nature.

title: The Gift
text: Appu and Ammu were very excited. They were eagerly waiting for their father to come home. He had promised them a surprise gift for topping the class. Soon they heard the familiar footsteps. They raced and opened the door even before the doorbell sounded. Their father stood by the door smiling at them with a basket in his hand. He entered the house and very gently kept the basket down. As soon as Ammu and Appu opened the basket, out popped a pair of long, fluffy ears. It had a pink nose too! Can you guess what is it? Yes, it's a rabbit. Appu and Ammu wanted to hold the rabbit but it kept hopping here and there. So they named it 'Hopper'. 'Now, now, don't you both keep chasing it. You will trip and fall over it,' said Mother. 'Ma, I want to hold it and keep it on my lap,' said Ammu, 'But it seems scared.' 'That's because all of us are new people for Hopper. Hopper is in a new place with new people,' explained their grandma, Innamma. 'Isn't Hopper being silly?', asked Ammu. 'Remember the first time you went to school, Ammu? Did you sit in the class properly?', asked mother. 'Mmm... I began crying and ran to you, Amma, as soon as I saw you,' replied Ammu thoughtfully. 'And why did you do that, my princess?' asked Grandma. 'Because I was a bit scared. I don't know why,' replied Ammu truthfully. 'And what did your teachers do to help you overcome the scare? Do you remember?' asked father. 'Yes, my teacher hugged me tight, cuddled me and sang a song for me. I felt nice after that.' 'Exactly. In a similar way, do you think you can make our Hopper feel nice too?' asked Aazoba, their grandfather. 'O yes! I will cuddle gently and sing a song.' So saying, Ammu very gently picked little Hopper and held it close to her heart. She began humming a little song and gave him a carrot. Hopper sniffed it and slowly began nibbling it.

title: The Wise Elephant's Tale: Learning to Live in Harmony
text: In a big jungle, there's a smart elephant named Guru Hathi. He's very wise and likes to teach good things to everyone. One day, Guru Hathi sees that the animals in the jungle are not getting along. Lions, monkeys, birds, and insects are not friends, and the jungle is not happy. Guru Hathi decides to help. He wants to tell the animals a story to teach them about being friends and working together. Guru Hathi gathers all the animals near an old tree. He tells them a special story about clever ants who faced a flood. The ants helped each other and made a leaf boat to stay safe. The animals listen carefully and understand that when they help each other, they become strong, just like the ants. They learn that working together is important. After the story, the animals start becoming friends. Lions, monkeys, birds, and insects decide to work together and help each other. Now, the jungle is full of happy sounds. The animals are friends, and they work together to make the jungle a better and happier place. Whenever there's a problem, the animals face it together with the strong power of unity. They help each other and make the jungle a wonderful home for everyone. Guru Hathi is happy to see the jungle filled with friends. He smiles, knowing that his story taught the animals the importance of being friends and helping one another.

title: Whispers of the Forest: A Day with Geezaga at Aranya Learning Center
text: ﻿ ﻿ In the heart of a small, picturesque forest lies the Aranya Learning Center, where children from various villages gather to embark on a journey of knowledge and discovery. ﻿ With excitement bubbling in the air, the children embark on a journey into the lush forest. Vibrant flora and the soothing sounds of nature surround them as they take in the magic of the outdoors. ﻿ Under the shade of a majestic mango tree, the group pauses to absorb the serenity of the surroundings. Suddenly, a mysterious sound captures their attention, sparking curiosity among the kids. A friendly voice speaks, and the source reveals itself – a magical bird named Geezaga. Intrigued, the kids engage in conversation, learning that this enchanting bird has a name and a story to share. Amidst the chatter, the children, led by the inquisitive Manu, inquire about Geezaga's identity. The bird playfully encourages them to look up, leading to a joyous revelation as they spot Geezaga perched above. With a mix of excitement and respect, the kids listen as Geezaga imparts wisdom about life in the forest. The bird, unfazed by the commotion, shares tales of building nests and raising its young. ﻿ Mani, inquisitive as ever, seeks to understand the differences between their homes and Geezaga's nest. The bird explains the purpose behind their unique abode, emphasizing the importance of keeping their babies safe. As the children absorb the fascinating details, they learn about Geezaga's diet – small seeds, worms, and fruits, get their hydration needs from natural water sources such as ponds, rivers, or puddles. They may also consume fresh fruits or succulent plants that contain water. Filled with gratitude for the enlightening encounter, the children express their appreciation to Geezaga. The magical bird encourages them to continue their journey of learning and bids them farewell as they excitedly head back to school. The echoes of laughter and newfound knowledge linger as the children return to Aranya Learning Center. Inspired by their forest adventure, they carry with them the magic of Geezaga's wisdom, making every lesson a journey of discovery in the enchanting world of education. Moral of the Story: "Wisdom resides in the simple wonders of nature. Stay curious, ask questions, and find valuable lessons in the world around you."

title: Where did the grasshopper go?
text: Once upon a time, in a small town filled with beautiful gardens and colourful flowers, two little girls named Gauri and Radha loved to explore and learn about nature. One sunny afternoon, they decided to go on an adventure in their grandma's garden. As they wandered through the garden, giggling and chasing butterflies, Gauri spotted a grasshopper perched on a bright red flower. "Look, Radha!" Gauri exclaimed. "It seems like the grasshopper is eating the flower petals. "You're right, Gauri! I wonder why the grasshopper is eating the petals. Let's stay quiet and observe." Gauri whispered, "I think the grasshopper might be finding something delicious to eat." Radha nodded and said, "Yes, Gauri. Grasshoppers are herbivores, which means they eat plants. Those flower petals must be like a yummy snack to the grasshopper." As they continued their observations, Gauri and Radha noticed something interesting. "Look, Radha," Gauri said excitedly. "See how the grasshopper uses its long hind legs to leap from one flower to another? It's like a little acrobat." Radha smiled. "Yes, Gauri, grasshoppers are incredible jumpers. Their strong hind legs help them escape from predators or quickly move from plant to plant." Just then, a bird flew by and landed on a nearby tree branch. "Hey, Gauri, do you think that bird might eat the grasshopper?" Radha asked with concern. "I'm not sure, Radha, but birds like to eat insects, so it's possible," Gauri replied. "This shows us how everything in nature is connected. The grasshopper eats the flower petals, and birds might eat the grasshopper. Look! how nicely it has camouflaged itself in the leaves." They sat silently, watching the grasshopper hop from one flower to another, aware that the bird was still watching. Suddenly, the bird swooped down but the grasshopper was swift and it quickly leaped into the cracks in the rocks nearby. "Oh, that was a narrow escape for the grasshopper!" Gauri said. Radha nodded, but then she smiled and said, "But Gauri, that's how the food chain works. The bird needs to eat insects like the grasshopper to survive. It's nature's way of balancing things. " Gauri thought about Radha's words and agreed. "You're right, Radha. Nature has its own way of working things out. It's all part of the cycle of life." With newfound knowledge about insect behaviour and the food chain, Gauri and Radha continued their adventure in their grandma's garden. They marvelled at the wonders of nature, appreciating the beauty of the flowers, the acrobatics of grasshoppers, and the importance of every creature, big or small. And from that day on, Gauri and Radha became even more curious and eager to explore the world around them, knowing that there are always amazing things to discover and learn through nature-based adventures.

Tiny, weak Superheroes?” It was the voice of the village bully, Bor. “What do you want, Bor?” Melam’s voice trembled. “Huh, how childish!” Bor sneered at them. “Do you know what my friends and I do to weak creatures like you?” “Bor, Bor, they are here!” Everyone turned to see Bor’s friends approach him. They were all excited. “The Amur Falcons have come again, Bor! Remember your plan to catch them once the sun sets?” “We will catch as many falcons as we can today!” Bor announced “NO!” shouted little Melam, “You cannot hurt those birds. They are our guests in the village. They’re beautiful and …and …” But Bor and his friends ignored him. Melam went home feeling defeated. Seeing him upset, Mei asked, “You are back early today. Did something happen?” “The Amur Falcons…” Melam sighed. “Mei, is it alright for someone to hurt the Amur Falcons?” he asked, turning to his mother. His mother tried to explain how everyone in the village has learnt that these birds are a blessing to them and should never be harmed. She said: “These birds help to eat all the insects that eat our crops.” “Tourists from all over visit our village to see the birds and because of this we have so many different people visiting us!” She told him how their Rangbah Shnong had been training some very special geese to attack anyone who went near the place, where the falcons usually are at night. “If Mei finds me outside at this time, she’ll really be angry but I’ve got to warn Bor not to go near the Falcons. He might be a bully but I’m a Superhero,” Melam mumbled. On reaching the spot, he saw the special birds in action! “Oww! He got me on the leg!” “I’m sorry! I’m sorry Goose! I promise never to hurt anyone again!” “Did you come to laugh at me?” Bor asked in disgust and anger, as he saw Melam the next day. “No, Bor. I’m so glad you are okay. I’m also glad that the Rangbah Shnong came in time to chase away the geese,” Melam said. Bor was silent. The wounds looked very painful. After a while, Bor spoke up. “I should not have harmed the birds. I never realized how special they are to our village.” “My mother told me how important the Amur Falcons are for our village. The Superhero squad will also let everyone else know about this,” Melam said. “Melam, can I also be a part of your Superhero squad?” Bor asked. “ I’m going to be a Superhero just like you, Melam,” Bor said. “Of course Bor, anyone in the village can always join the Superhero Squad.” Activity Fellow Falcon Superheroes! You have a mission to complete. Could you help this falcon regain its beautiful colours?
author: Mebanda Iaka Blah Dkhar

title: The monkey and the cap seller
text: Once, there was a cap seller who used to go from town to town to sell his caps. He had a big bag in which he carried the caps. His caps were of good quality and inexpensive too. People appreciated his caps a lot. The cap seller earned enough to support his family. He led happy and simple life.One day, in the afternoon,it was very worm. The cap seller sat under a big shady tree and had lunch. After having food, he decided to rest for a while as he was feeling tired. He kept his bag by his side and went off to sleep in the cool shade of the big tree. He covered his face with the cap to escape from the heat of the sun. A group of monkeys lived on that big tree. The monkeys got curious to see a man sleeping under the tree. Quietly, they climbed down and and stood around the sleeping cap seller. The cap seller was fast asleep and unaware of the monkeys around him! Deep sleep,the cap seller was snoring. One of the monkey imitated him but the cap seller kept sleeping. Another one went to the the bag and opened it.He put his hands inside and took out a cap.He turned around the cap as if trying to understand what it was. The other monkey also went and joined him. They also took out the caps from the bag and started playing with them. They all seemed to to be fascinated by the colorful caps. One of them accidently put a cap on his head and was thrilled to find it fitting his head properly. With the cap on his head, he jumped here and there feeling excited. The other monkeys were watching him. One by one, they all took their caps and imitated him. Soon all the monkeys had caps on their head!!! After jumping and playing around on the ground, the monkeys then climbed up the tree and sat on its branches wearing the caps. After some time, the cap seller woke up from his sleep. He was surprised to see the bag open and some caps scatter here and there.Who has taken out the caps from my bag? he thought. He picked up all the caps lying on the ground and counted them. There were five caps missing. The cap seller looked around for the missing caps. On hearing the monkeys chatter, the looked up and was astonished to see the monkeys wearing his caps. They were making merry. They made faces at him and teased at him. He asked the monkey to return the caps by waving his hands at them. Instead of giving back the caps, the monkey started imitating him by moving their hands. The cap seller was a wise man. He knew that the monkeys would not return his caps easily. Thought for some time and then he came up with an idea. He took off his cap and threw it on the ground. They also took of there cap and threw them on the ground. The cap seller chuckled and picked up all his caps. He put them in the bag and went off.
author: Mohit Paul

title: Kartik the Naughty Boy
text: Animator: Swathi Sambasivam Illustrators: Debasmita Dasgupta, Manisha Naskar, Milan Nayak, Vridhhi Chaudhry Kartik is a really naughty boy. He always irritates people and does pranks on them with his friend Shivank. He never consentrates on his studies, instead he bunks the classes many times. He wants everyone to respect him but he never respects any of his classmates. Then his mother said to him, "Why are you disturbing and disrespecting other people". Suddenly mom got the grades of Kartik and she was shocked. She said, "I don't want to see these grades again in your report card". Then Kartik replied, "I am really really sorry mom for all that and I will improve". After that day Kartik improved a lot. He started to respect people and focused in his studies. After that he got the highest marks in the whole class and he was really happy. Then the whole class cheered him really much.
author: Aaron Anu
illustrator: Debasmita Dasgupta; Manisha Naskar; Milan Nayak; Swathi Sambasivam; Vridhhi  Chaudhry

title: Sringeri Srinivas learn to laugh
text: Sakthivel Sringeri Srinivas was a great farmer. He planted the best banana trees which bear banana halwa. But he also has the most terrifying facial wrinkles in the world. When he gets angry, his forehead becomes full of lines. His nose turned red. His eyes became extremely sharp. When Sringeri Srinivas wrinkled his face, everyone ran away from him. His wife, children and friends tried to hide from him. The cow and the dog also ran. Until the crows in the field also flew away when Sringeri Srinivas wrinkled his face. And Sringeri Srinivas often wrinkled his face. When the plants don't grow well. When the barber doesn't have time to shave his hair. When the TV can't be turned on. And many more. Once, Sringeri Srinivas went to his field to see his banana harvest. His feelings also became bad. Not a single person knew why he was so angry. He walked very quickly towards his biggest banana tree. There was a very large bunch of bananas. Soon he set out to make his banana halwa famous. His frown turned into a small smile. Suddenly, a troop of monkeys came hanging from the trees nearby. The biggest monkey with its fiery red bottom, jumped right on the tree that Sringeri Srinivas admired so much. This made him scrunch his face again. The wrinkles on his face grew more and more. That's the biggest wrinkle on his face. It started from his forehead and spread to his big toe. The monkeys with their evil tempers were shocked. He had never seen such a frown. He dropped half the banana on the ground then dropped the other. Quickly, he jumped to the next tree and so on. Soon, he was far away and safe from that frown. Sringeri Srinivas saw monkeys jumping from one tree to another. He chased the monkey. He also wanted to teach the monkey a lesson. On the way, he slipped on a banana peel. Swoosh, he fell and his sandals got stuck in the mud. Sringeri Srinivas sat up and tried to chase the monkey again. Swoosh! He slipped again. This time he fell with his face slumped. However, he tried to sit up again, his mouth full of leaves, mud and twigs. When he looked up, the monkey had disappeared. Sringeri Srinivas sees him. His nice clothes are brown. His hands were dirty and scratched. He couldn't find his feet. Everything was covered in mud. Suddenly, it occurred to him that he was seeing something funny. Sringeri Srinivas, the famous farmer. He now sits alone on leaves, mud and bananas. It's all very funny. And Sringeri Srinivas started laughing. That was the first time he laughed a little. Hee Hee. Then it got bigger. Ha ha! He laughed and Sringeri Srinivas couldn't control his laughter. His laughter became very big. HA HA HA. And big! Immediately, he immediately clutched his stomach and rolled around in the mud. HA HA HA HAAAA! Tears came out of his eyes. His laughter became so melodious that the birds nearby came closer to him. His laughter was so loud that the monkeys came back. His laughter was so cute that several children came closer. Her laughter was so novel that her extended family came to listen too. Sringeri Srinivas laughed so much that other people started laughing too. The birds are chirping. The crow groaned. The monkeys chattered. The kids started giggling. The banana tree began to sway. The barber grinned. The tailor started to chuckle. Even the tiger sleeping deep in his cave smiled with his mustache. Suddenly, Sringeri Srinivas stopped laughing. Everyone and the people around him looked at him happily. He also felt happy. "Come on, let's go home," he said, holding out his hand to the children. Sringeri Srinivas still scrunches up his face sometimes. But now, he also likes to laugh. And he had the biggest laugh in town.
author: Raghav Sakthivel

title: Obey Your Parents: it's good for you!
text: Once upon a time, there is a boy who lived with his mother and five siblings named Jack. He is the third son in the family. He has two sisters and two brothers. He was raised in modest farming family. One day, when he was in childhood, he played with his friends. In that time, the rain came heavily. Jack and his friends searched grasshoppers to cook. He collected them as side dish. After he finished collecting them, he went home and gave them to his mother. His mother was really happy at that time because they did not have any side dish at home. In the next day, his mother asked him and his brother, Jimmy went to the rice field. They are asked to plow rice field. Unfortunately, in the middle of their work, his brother left him and played football with his friends. Jack was so exhausted because there was nobody who helped him. In the afternoon, he went home lonely. Every instruction from his mother, he never refused. He knew that his mother would be angry with him if nobody wanted to obey his mother's instructions. Jack always helped his mother in the rice field. The other siblings rarely helped their mom. He did not have a heart to make his mom work lonely in the field because there was only his mother taking a care rice field. It was due to his father who had passed away. One day, when Jack had been adolescents, he went to school. After school, He usually went to the rice field. When he was plowing the rice field, he saw his friends who played and had a date with some girls. He thought that he wanted to be like his friends who could play without working hard in the rice field like that. When he did not have money at all, his mom rarely gave him some money. Jack realized the he was not from rich family. Finally, he earned the money by collecting plastic bottles. After he got a lot of them, he went to collector to exchange them with the money. The money which he got he gave to his mom and some for buying snack. One day, Jack's mother had passed away. Year after year, He grew up became a strong man. He could earn the money by himself. He was a creative and smart man. He became hard working man. He really mastered on farming. He became a rich merchant. His siblings who were lazy did not have any knowledge to make their field grew well. They lived in poverty. In the other hand, Jack who always helped his mom when he was childhood got much information about how to farm well Hard working is never lie. He got what he had been working for all this time. ﻿ Finally, He got married and had a beautiful wife. They lived happily ever after.
author: shinta sartika
illustrator: David Yambem; Hari Kumar Nair; Jonathan  Field; Krishnagopal Shreshtha; Michael  Sagikwa; Phạm  Thu Thùy; Rijuta Ghate; Samanda N Pyngrope; Shreeya Wagh; Thea   Nicole de Klerk; Viplov Singh

title: Home is Where You'll Find Me
text: Woof! Woof! My name is Bouncy. You're asking why the name? Because... I bounce, I jump, and I leap! Every morning, my dear Maggie sets off to school. "Bouncy, keep good watch of the house," she'll say. "Woof, woof," I'll say. I am keeping my house safe! It's a peaceful place where we live. No thieves around I can see... I'm feeling a bit bored. "Woof, woof!" My buddies next door seem to be having a blast! So on this sunny day, I bounce, I jump and I leap! Meet Spotty and Dotty! They are the best runners you can have a race with. "Spotty! Dotty! Time for lunch!" I bounce, I jump and I leap again, into the garden where another of my friends lives. Meet Goldie, my quiet kitty friend. We sit together and keep each other's company, but today I'm feeling sleep...sleep... sleepy. "Bouncy, where are you?" Ooh, the voice I've been longing to hear! "Goldie, see you tomorrow!" "You're back!" Home is where you'll find me... at the end of the day.
author: Cathy Tang

title: The Fox Meets The Drum
text: One day, a fox was walking through the forest and he saw a drum. He lended a paw at it and it made a loud sound. The fox kept on beating the drum and soon the fox thought that there was food inside and that it was a gift from God. So the fox tried to break the drum to get the food inside. The fox opened the drum but soon found out that there was nothing inside. Now the drum was stuck to the fox's head. It turned out to be a battle drum and the soldiers came and killed the fox. The end. Moral: Think before you act. Credits All the images in this story were done by the new AI generator, Microsoft Designer. Storyline written by Arihanth Nirmalkumar.
author: Arihanth Nirmalkumar

title: Dizzy Python
text: There is a dense forest near it. There are many burflower trees in the jungle. On top of a tree, there is a bee. Afraid of bees, Vadan's heart goes thump! thump! One time, There was a big accident. During the burflower festival, a huge python climbed the burflower tree. Vadan's house became crowded with people Catch the Python! catch the python! O Vadan, catch the python! Near the tree Vadan stood motionless, He was not afraid of pythons, but afraid of bees. Bee above, Near the python, People under the trees. The python became dizzy surrounded by people pet! pet! Don't catch the Python. Dizzy Python rushed towards the jungle. But the bee stayed on the tree. And the people began indulging in the festival, in Badan's house.
author: Annie Baruah

title: Homecoming: The Journey of a Tiny Turtle
text: Once upon a time, on the beautiful Konkan coast of Maharashtra, there lived a curious and nature-loving young boy named Appu. Appu was always eager to explore and learn about the wonders of the world around him. He and his friend Manu would spend hours watching the waves crash against the shore. One day, while Appu was exploring a secluded part of the pristine Velas beach, a female Olive Ridley turtle emerged from the depths of the Arabian Sea. She had traveled thousands of miles, exhausted yet determined, the turtle started digging meticulously deep nests in the warm sand, delicately depositing the precious eggs. The turtle covered the nests with utmost care, ensuring their safety until the time came for them to hatch. Once the arduous task was complete, the turtles made their way back to the sea, leaving behind a future generation to continue their legacy. Weeks turned into months, and one starry night, the eggs began to crack open. Appu and Manu noticed a group of people gathered around something. Curiosity piqued, they hurried over to see what was happening. To their astonishment, they discovered tiny Olive Ridley hatchlings emerged, with their flippers flapping with enthusiasm guiding them towards the distant horizon. Among them, he noticed one little turtle struggling to keep up with the rest. Appu's heart melted, and he decided to help the little turtle. He gently picked up the tiny creature and named it Speedy. Every day after school, Appu and Manu would rush to the shore, where Speedy & other hatchlings scurried across the sandy shore. They followed the rhythm of the crashing waves and the distant call of the ocean. Their tiny bodies trembled with excitement as they approached the sparkling waters. As the turtles grew, one fine day the turtles navigated the vast ocean, relying on their innate sense of direction and the earth's magnetic fields to guide them to an incredible adventure journey into the deep sea. The hatchlings bravely navigated through the crashing waves and swam tirelessly, using their flippers to propel forward. The tiny turtles faced numerous obstacles on their path. Seagulls swooped down, hoping to snatch a quick meal. However, the tenacious little hatchlings managed to evade their hungry beaks, slipping into the safety of the water. The journey was far from over, though, as they encountered treacherous waves, strong currents, and lurking predators such as sharks. The sea was a vast & awe-inspiring surrounded by vibrant marine life that Speedy and other hatchlings began to explore. The deeper they went, the darker and colder the water became. Speedy's journey took him through underwater canyons and ridges, where he encountered mesmerizing creatures such as graceful sea turtles, majestic whales, and playful dolphins. Curious starfish reached out with their delicate arms, tickling the turtles' shells as they passed by. The hatchlings marveled at the beauty of the coral reef, with its bustling fish community and mesmerizing patterns of underwater flora. They darted through schools of shimmering fish, their scales reflecting the sun's rays like precious gemstones. The fish greeted the turtles with playful spins and twirls, accompanying them on their quest through the ever-changing currents. The hatchlings learned to ride the currents and glide effortlessly, reveling in the freedom of the open ocean. It was a world of endless wonder and discovery. Finally, after days of swimming tirelessly, the hatchlings reached a magical sight—the bioluminescent zone. The water around them lit up with an enchanting glow as tiny organisms emitted their ethereal light. Speedy and his siblings danced among the shimmering particles, creating a mesmerizing trail. In the deep sea, the turtles encountered unique ecosystems such as hydrothermal vents, where hot, mineral-rich water gushed from the ocean floor, sustaining a variety of unusual organisms. The hatchlings marveled at the wonders of nature, witnessing first-hand the resilience and adaptability of life in even the harshest environments. The turtles learned to ride the currents and glide effortlessly, reveling in the freedom of the open ocean. It was a world of endless wonder and discovery. In the deep sea, the turtles encountered unique ecosystems such as hydrothermal vents, where hot, mineral-rich water gushed from the ocean floor, sustaining a variety of unusual organisms. The hatchlings marveled at the wonders of nature, witnessing firsthand the resilience and adaptability of life in even the harshest environments. As Speedy's adventure continued, he and his siblings faced challenges like strong currents and unpredictable weather, but he pressed on with unwavering determination. Guided by his instincts, they followed the ebb and flow of the ocean, exploring new depths and encountering breathtaking sights along the way. Ultimately, after an arduous but fulfilling journey, Speedy found himself in a tranquil and fertile feeding ground, abundant with nutritious sea grass and bountiful marine life. The adventure to the deep sea had not only shaped him and his tribe physically but also filled them with a profound sense of wonder and appreciation for the ocean's beauty and complexity. It was the perfect place for him and his tribe to grow and thrive. Days turned into weeks, and the baby turtles grew stronger and wiser with each passing adventure. However, not all encounters were as friendly. Along their voyage, the turtles came face-to-face with a mighty shark, its sharp teeth glimmering in the sunlight. Fear struck their hearts, and they quickly swam away, seeking refuge in the depths of the ocean. Upon discovering the hardships turtles endure to survive, Appu was determined to protect these tiny creatures of the vast ocean. Besides reading books, he attended workshops to further his understanding of Olive Ridley turtles and their habitats. Inspired by the turtle's resilience and beauty, Appu and his friends joined a local conservation society to protect the delicate marine ecosystem of the Konkan coast. Through their conservation activities, locals were informed about the importance of preserving the marine ecosystem, protecting nesting beaches, and regulating fishing practices. With each passing year, the number of Olive Ridley turtles visiting the Konkan coast increased, a testament to the successful conservation initiatives undertaken. Their presence brought joy to the hearts of locals and tourists alike, reminding everyone of the fragile yet resilient balance of nature. And so, the Olive Ridley turtles continued their timeless journey along the coast of Konkan, their adventures serving as a reminder of the beauty and diversity that exist beneath the waves. Their story became an inspiration for future generations, teaching them the importance of coexistence and the wonders that lie within our oceans. Together with the community, Appu actively participated in beach clean-up drives to ensure the nesting grounds remained free from plastic and other harmful debris. He along with his schoolmates even organized awareness campaigns, where he showcased his drawings and paintings of the Olive Ridley turtles, capturing their grace and vulnerability. During the nesting season, Appu and the volunteers patrolled the beach during the night to protect the nesting turtles from predators and poachers. They set up barriers and signs to mark the nesting sites, urging people to keep their distance and not disturb the turtles. Appu's enthusiasm and passion for the cause inspired others to join in, and soon the community efforts gained momentum. As time passed, Appu witnessed the positive impact of their collective actions. The number of Olive Ridley turtle nests began to increase, and the survival rate of the hatchlings improved significantly. Appu's heart swelled with pride, knowing that their dedicated efforts were making a difference in the lives of these endangered creatures. The adventures of Little Appu and the community's relentless efforts to protect the Olive Ridley turtles became a source of inspiration for people far and wide. News of their success spread, and other communities along the coast started adopting similar conservation practices, creating a network of guardians for these magnificent sea turtles. Years later, as Appu walked along the beach, he could see the legacy of their efforts. The once-endangered Olive Ridley turtles were thriving, and their conservation had become an integral part of the community's identity. Appu knew that the work was not over yet, and he continued to be a champion for the environment, inspiring others to take action and protect the natural wonders that surrounded them. The community's tireless dedication to protecting the endangered Olive Ridley turtles became a tale of hope, resilience, and the power of collective action in safeguarding our precious wildlife.
author: Preeti Swaminathan

title: The Squirrels home
text: This is Peehu and Doobi-Doobi's new home. It's name is The Squirrel's Home. Squirrels are here, there -everywhere. Sweet sweet squirrels It is a big Peepul Tree. On the tree lived birds and squirrels. Branch to branch jump the squirrels. Nuts and water collect the squirrels. The Squirrel admires its tail. The squirrel grooms its whiskers. Catch me if you can the naughty squirrel plays with the leaves Sometimes standing only on 2 feet, It does appear as if the squirrel prays. Quietly entering the room the squirrel chatters away when it sees cats and dogs the squirrel runs and hides to save its life. The stars and the moon in the sky is what the squirrel dreams of.

title: Chako Chaki Tales - A Hungry Panda
text: It was their cozy little home. One night, it was raining heavily with thunderstorms and Chakko was sitting in the tree house and was watching the rain from the window. It was almost dinner time and Chakki asked what she should make for dinner. Chakko said, I want to eat the tasty porridge that you make. Chakki said, I want to eat that too but we don't have enough rice to make it. Chakko said, let me go to the nearby field and get some rice then. Chakko flew under the shade of the trees to avoid the rain as much as possible. It was too dark and Chakko could not find the way to the rice field. He stopped and looked around to see if there was any help available. Suddenly, he heard sound of something breaking. He turned and saw a large animal in that direction. Chakko got scared at first but wanted to check out who it was. Chakko went closer and the big animal turned around. Chakko started to fly back but the animal stopped him. Don't worry - I am a friendly Panda, said the animal. Chakko had never seen a Panda before. He asked the panda, what are you doing here? Panda replied, I live deep in the forest but I have come here in search for food. I am breaking these bamboo sticks which I can take home for my dinner. Chakko said, even I am here in search of food - I need to find rice fields so that Chakki can make some porridge. Panda said, I can help you with that. I know a rice field just outside the forest. Sit on my shoulder and I will take you there. Chakko happily agreed and went to the rice field with Panda. Chakko quickly collected the rice that he needed and Panda brought him back to the place where they first met. Chakko thanked his new friend. Panda said, Welcome! I will now get back to gathering bamboo as I still have to go a long way to my home and I am very hungry. Chakko wanted to help his new friend. He said, why don't you come with me to my tree house. It is nearby and Chakki makes the best food. Take your bamboo sticks and come with me. The hungry Panda immediately agreed. Chakko and Panda both went to the tree house. Chakki was preparing the porridge when Chakko and Panda came. Chakko explained how Panda helped him in collecting rice. Chakki thanked Panda and invited him to sit. Chakko gave the bamboo sticks and rice to chakki. Chakki said, I will make a new type of porridge today - Bamboo Porridge. Chakki prepared the meal while Chakko made dining arrangements in their cosy little tree house. They all ate the delicious porridge and shared their experiences about the beautiful forest they live in. Chakko thought - "What a wonderful rainy day!!"
author: Abhi Shah
illustrator: Archana Sreenivasan; Barkha Lohia; Jacob Kono; Jayesh Sivan; Linh Chi; Nilesh Gehlot; Shivam Thapliyal; shreeja majumder; Sourav Sarkar

title: Wonder Woman
text: It was a rainy Saturday afternoon. Asha emerged from her room and settled on the veranda. The air had cooled down and the scent of freshly bloomed Jasmine tickled her nose. Pappa was seated in the corner with his laptop, squinting at the screen and typing something - oh, he was working from home! She had learned this from Mommy during a phone call with Leyla Aunty the previous day. Mommy had instructed her not to disturb him while he was working. So, it wasn't a good time to ask him about superheroes! She realized. Asha moved closer to him anyway, hoping he would notice her. Mommy had instructed her not to disturb him while he was working. So, it wasn't a good time to ask him about superheroes! she realized. Asha moved closer to him anyway, hoping he would notice her. It all began the day before when Ruby brought her shiny new bag to class. It was red and blue with lots of pictures and patterns, but what captivated Asha was the vibrant print of some unusual-looking characters in unusual clothes on the front. They were armed and positioned as if ready to fight someone. Ruby told her that they were superheroes, each with unique superpowers to rescue the world from the bad guys. How amazing! Asha listened to Ruby narrate the stories of each superhero until lunch break. Ruby rattled out a long list of names, but Asha's mind only recalled Spider-Man. " How do we get to meet them?" Asha asked while savoring her bread toast. "I don’t know; I only watched them in movies," Ruby replied while chewing on her veggies. "Asha! Are you awake already? Come, sit with me." Pappa noticed how the six-year-old Asha seemed deeply lost in thought, her face swollen from her afternoon nap. He lifted her up from the floor and placed her in the chair next to him. "Are you hungry?" he asked. "Shall I make something for you?" Asha shook her head. "I will eat with Mommy when she comes back from the office." "Alright!" He gave her a forhead kiss. "Let me know when you're hungry; Pappa has learned a new recipe from the YouTube. An absolute stunner!" He chuckled and typed faster on the keyboard. However, Asha didn't want to leave. She wanted to tell him about Ruby’s bag and her superhero stories. "Pappa, who is a superhero?" Asha asked. Looking at her with a full smile, he said, "Superheroes are people who have powers and can do extraordinary things but are also kind enough to use their power to save others.” "Do you know any superheroes? Have you ever met Spider-Man? He can shoot spider webs from his fingers and fly across buildings. Ruby told me," Asha beamed with pride. "Pappa, who is a superhero?" Asha asked. "A superhero"? He paused for a moment and looked at her. "Ha Pappa, I saw their pictures on Ruby’s bag"! her eyes were gleaming with curiosity. " Haha, yes. There are lots of superheroes. Only some of them are on TV though, like Spider-Man. But plenty of other superheroes like us do exist out there. They save the world little by little, every day, through their good deeds," he continued. "Like us?" Asha raised her eyebrow. "But I cannot be a superhero, Pappa! Only boys can!" she said slowly. "Who said that? everybody can be a superhero. Remember how you helped grandma with little chores around her house and how kind you were to your friend when she needed your help with homework. My little one is already a superhero." Pappa turned and looked at her with a sweet smile. Still not fully convinced, Asha retorted, "But I didn’t see any girl superhero on Ruby’s bag!!" "Oh, I see, that’s what it's all about. Come here; I will show you." Pappa opened the search browser and typed something. A colourful image popped up on the screen. Asha looked closely, anxiously biting her nails. It really was a girl superhero, dressed beautifully in a skirt with a confident smirk on her face. She tried to read the name given below the picture. "Wonder Woman" it is, Pappa said. "Wow Pappa! she looks incredible! So, she will beat the bad guys like other superheros, right?" Asha asked while scanning the picture. Pointing at Wonder Woman’s high-heeled shoes, without waiting for his answer, she murmured, "But Mommy always complains how painful it is to wear them. How does Wonder Woman chase bad guys in those?" Their conversation broke off abruptly when a white scooter entered the porch. Mommy parked the vehicle and collected her things from the back seat. Pappa took her bags, and they went inside the house together. Only then did Asha notice that Mommy was carrying something in her hands, and it was moving slightly. She couldn’t quite tell what it was since it was covered by her dupatta. "Mommy, what is it in your hand?" Asha couldn’t conceal her curiosity. "Come and see for yourself." With a slight smile on her face, Mommy slowly removed the dupatta. It was a puppy! Too thin and small, slightly shivering as its body was wet from the rain. Asha couldn’t believe her eyes. She had always loved animals, and having a puppy at home was definitely a dream. "Dear, where did you get this puppy from? It seems like he had a rough time before he met you," Pappa, too, took a special interest in the little guest. "I rescued him. He was drowning in the canal nearby the office. It was filled with water from yesterday’s rain. Poor thing, he was so scared when I took him in my hands. The mother was nowhere to be seen. I didn’t have the heart to leave him there." Mommy put him down on the kitchen table. He licked her fingers as a token of gratitude. Asha’s eyes lit up as she watched her Mommy with the puppy, and she felt a wave of admiration wash over her. "Superheroes are people who have powers and can do extraordinary things, but are also kind enough to use their power to save others." She remembered what Pappa said. It was true. Mommy had used her superpower to save the puppy from a bad fate. Indeed, kindness was her superpower! With her heart overflowing, Asha rushed to her Wonder Woman, who was feeding the puppy in the kitchen, and gave her a tight hug. The End
author: Diana Nadira Puthusseri

title: The Stomach Tiger
text: Abi patiently waited for the clock to tick one. His stomach grumbled from hunger, making the sound of tiger’s growl. "There's a little tiger in our tummy. If you don't feed it when it gets hungry, it may come out and eat the whole food in the kitchen," his Ammumma (Grandmother) used to say when he was a little boy and hesitated to eat. Now, as a grown boy capable of completing his math homework independently, he no longer believed in this tale. "Grrrr"... the stomach growled again. "Oh, the tiger has quite the appetite, I see," Abi tittered. Finally, only ten more minutes to go! But what might Appa have packed for lunch? Abi wondered, attempting to recall the morning scenes in the kitchen. Amma was washing dishes while Appa made dosa. Kingini, the stray cat that they adopted, scolded a crow attempting to steal a dosa through the window. The pressure cooker whistled, signaling that the Sambar was ready, and the mixer produced a rhythmic noise while grinding coconut in the corner. Abi loved having Dosa and Chutney for breakfast, but with the Sambar, lunch could be rice with some side dish, maybe mango pickle. His mouth watered at the thought. Then he remembered Rumaiza Aunty bringing a pot of biryani for him, when he was getting ready for school. So, perhaps it was biryani today! Abi's stomach tiger seemed to grow even more impatient at the mention of biryani. Regardless, Appa would have definitely packed some sweets, as there were leftovers from Ammuma's visit yesterday. He rubbed his hands together with excitement. As the clock struck one, and the school bell rang, Abi jumped from his seat. With his stomach tiger growling "Hurray!", He eagerly reached into his bag, searching for the lunch box. To his surprise, it was empty. Disappointment and sadness enveloped him. The happy images of Dosa, Sambar, pickle, rice, and golden-coloured Laddo slowly vanished from his mind, leaving him with an empty bag. "Abii, Abii...come here," he heard Smita teacher's voice from the corridor. Walking towards the door, he realized it was his Amma speaking with her, holding the lunch box in her left hand. A wide smile spread across his face as he rushed out the door, and the stomach tiger made a happy growl.
author: Diana Nadira Puthusseri

title: The Coconut Barfi's.
text: Sooraj was a young 5-year-old boy. He used to live with his Ammachi. Every summer they made coconut barfi. They both loved Coconut Barfi's. But it was very difficult to make it. He loved helping his Ammachi in the garden, field, or wherever they went She loved telling him about her childhood. She would go on telling new stories if Sooraj didn't remind her about making Barfi's! Ammachi and Sooraj went to the feild where there were many coconuts. Then she sat on a lift kind of thing that Ammachi and Sooraj had made so that it would be easy to get the coconuts. It was fun for both of them as it was like a game of throwing coconuts in the net. After they got the needed amount of coconuts, Ammachi cut them though Sooraj insisted on doing so. Ammachi said "Sooraj Coconuts are hard to cut open. So I will do it. Sooraj agreed. He was surprised as his Ammachi took no trouble in cutting it open. While Ammachi was boiling the milk Sooraj started grating the coconuts. He had expected it to be hard but this time it was a lot harder than he expected it to be. Sooraj could smell the beautiful aroma of the milk mixing with the coconut. He could say that Ammachi was quite a chef! After putting them in the fridge for an hour, Ammachi cut them out and Sooraj put them in the jar. Sooraj by then started feeling hungry. Ammachi laughed and said "Don't worry, Don't worry, After going to the field and Giving Sunitha Aunty a few Burfi's we can eat them while listening to the radio. Finally, they left her house and Sunitha Auntie thanked them and gave them coconut milk as a token of gratitude. Sooraj was happy they were leaving and could finally eat the burfi's with coconut milk. They reached home and ate the coconut burfi's with joy and delight. They enjoyed the flavour of their hard work and success. Now all they had to do was wait for the rainy season to make its own seasonal delight.

text: For Our Dearest Khushmeet, On Her 5 th Birthday 16th December,2023. ' May you forever sparkle and shine like the star that you are. Happy birthday our princess! With lots of love and blessings.
