title: The Litte Tree
text: A little tree looked lonely in the middle of a lush forest. Heavy rain began to fall, and the small tree had to stand the cold air. A big tree protects a small tree from the rain. "I will protect you, my dear little tree," he said. The little trees grow bigger and develop. The little trees now provide shelter for plants and other small animals.

title: Kilbe
text: “Go away! Go away! Don’t come near us! ” “You go away! Don’t come here.” Kengkong kengkong women beating the rice, Sripsrek sripsrip men making bamboo baskets, Ushers the dawn of the Cotton Bazaar season upon the village of Tekarachu Takilkila gre The sun rays on her face riprap riprap Wakes our dear Otse from her sleep She walks towards the balcony as she trips tap… tip To a sight of a beautiful foliage. And the mountain and Kil Oljomas travelling to the bazaar like grai grai grai grai. A semal tree steals her gaze. As the wind blows srisri sra sra... As tears trickles down her cheeks. Toktak toktak, s he asked the tree, “ Bolchu, why aren't you picked by the Kil Oljomas? ” She cradles the bolchu dikdik dikdik “ Bolchu! Bolchu! I will love you from now on!“ Even after the passing of many ‘ dilip dilip’ and ‘gogarek gok ’ Otse kept picking up the bolchu in its season through all the moments of her life. Otse was now wrinkled and old. Due, her grandchild, with a twinkle in her eyes squeezes the bolchu Otse gathered po’om po’om She asks, “Why do you collect bolchu, Ambi?” “Oh beloved Due, it taught me about love better than any one, didori didorido, ” replies Ambi Otse One day, Otse didn't make it past the day. With bolchu in her hand she breathed her… Oang Oang Apai apai amai amai m ourn fills the room As Due’s first tears fall on the basket Where bolchu was collected As though Ambi Otse had something to say A creature rolled out of it Muttering “imbeng imbeng” The ‘Imbeng’ was without a language but loved so faultless As Due bonded with it, she named it Kilbe, They bonded like the beautifully woven reking, taktak taktak Due and Kil went on an errand for uncle Pintok to collect herbs from the forest… As they journey, the Forest was filled with life. Mai jing jing jing jing of the cicadas and crickets, Distant waterfalls roaring dai dai dai dai, The bamboos going wapepe pepe, And all kinds of birds sing choruses. Kil and Due on their search for herbs Saw a cave from afar, As they walk further and further towards it, it drizzles, then it rains heavier and heavier; and as they reach the mouth of the cave, a storm hits, going grimgrim graw graw. “Go away! Don't come here,” a voice rages against the storm, But Kil with the water in its body sprouts flowers all over itself and points a bouquet at the voice squealing, “ imbeng imbeng. ” A voice fell to light, revealing Tongte Gongge whose feet gongge. Sure, its tears turning to flowers made it feel understood, Prompting her to ask, “Do you want to play with me?” And Kil, “imbeng imbeng” Kilbe, Tongte, and Due played and danced after the storm. ♫Drengchak Jenggitchak Drengchak rakichak, Drengchak Jenggitchak Drengchak rakichak ♫ Activity Just like how Tongte Gongge was misunderstood and feared by people, is there something you feared but then after interacting with it further you realised that it was just a misunderstanding? Let’s do this! Can you reimagine and draw your fear, not as something fearful but as something adorable like Kilbe in the story. You never know, maybe this can help you face your fears?

title: Amira and Her Super Mom
text: Amira and her mom always spend time together. Amira always learns many things from her mom, and her mom always takes the time to teach Amira. They love each other and really enjoy every moment they spend together. Amira is accompanying her mom to cook food for breakfast. Amira is also learning to add spices to her mom's cooking. After breakfast, Amira helped her mom to wash their clothes. She really pays attention to how her mom washes the clothes properly. After washing the clothes, Amira asked her mom. "Mom, can I try putting these clothes on the clothesline?". Her mom said,"of course Amira, you can try it." Then, Amira dried the clothes and put them on the clothesline. Amira was very happy because she could reach the clothesline to dry the clothes. Amira and her mom then laughed together because Amira could do it. Amira can't ride a bicycle yet. She asked her mom to guide and teach her to ride a bicycle. Amira said "Mom, can you guide me to ride a bicycle? Her mom said "of course, with pleasure, Honey". Then, Amira excitedly learned to ride a bicycle but she had to be careful and still be guided by her mom. A fter learning to ride a bicycle diligently, Amira was finally able to ride a bicycle without being guided by her mom. Amira feels very happy because she can finally ride a bicycle. Amira said excitedly, "Mom, finally I can ride a bicycle!. Then her mom smiled at her and she was so proud to see Amira riding a bicycle. At night, before going to bed, Amira is used to listening the stories that read by her mom from a story book. Tonight, her mom read a story about a kind turtle and an arrogant rabbit. From that story, the turtle was challenged by an arrogant rabbit to compete a running race with him. However, at the end of the story, the competition was won by the kind turtle and the rabbit lost because of his arrogance. Amira was very happy to hear the end of the story. Then, her mom asked Amira to learn a lesson from the story. Her mom said, "Amira should not be arrogant like a rabbit, because arrogance will definitely have bad consequences. Amira answered, "Alright mom, thank you for a nice story." After listening to the story about a kind turtle and an arrogant rabbit, Amira then went to her bed and she was accompanied by her mom. Amira gets ready for sleeping. Her mom put a blanket on Amira while saying "have a nice dream, Honey". Then Amira answered, "thank you mom, good night!". Then her mother smiled and said "my pleasure Honey, good night!". Amira's mom made sure that Amira was sleeping in a comfortable position. After that, her mom came out from Amira's room and went to her own bed. Today, Amira was asked by her mom to accompany her to water the flowers in the yard. They have extensive flower plants of various types and beautiful colors. Amira was very excited to walk to the flower garden with her mom. After arriving at the flower garden, Amira enthusiastically watered the flower plants. She was very excited and her mom was happy to see her. After watering the flowers, Amira and her mom then walked back to their house. They took home some flowers that they had picked from the garden. They walked happily while occasionally telling their memorable experiences and then laughing together. Amira is very happy because she has learned many things from her mother. Amira said to herself "I am very grateful to have such a great mom!".

title: The Green Revolution: A Boy's Journey from Rio to the World
text: A boy named Thomas, lived near the coastal area of Brazil in the city of Rio de Janeiro. He was 11 years old and was in Grade 6, in Escola Vitoria school. Whenever he was on the way to school, there were construction sites. Everyday, they cut trees and built buildings. He asked his dad, why they were doing so. His dad, completely clueless, decided that it would be best to keep his mouth shut. Weeks and months went by, he was so sad about the cutting of trees. So, one day he decided to carry all his courage and went to his dad and asked him to take him to the construction site. They decided to go there that evening. After they reached, he asked them... Why are you all cutting trees We are doing what the local authorities tell us to do Thomas was curious about who the authorities were but he decided to ask his dad and tell him about what they said. His dad said "Authorities are persons or bodies of persons who have the power or right to make decisions, enforce laws, command, or perform certain functions." Then his dad swiftly replied to himself saying "My cousin, works in the local authorities". The boy asked "Can we go there?". His dad replied "Why not, let's go!". They quickly got dressed and went to the authorities. The boy asked "Why do you cut trees". The people replied "We want to make Rio de Janeiro a developed city and a worldwide attraction, by cutting trees we can build more buildings." Thomas went away sadly. He wanted to stop deforestation. He only knew one last way to stop trees being cut, this would take his goal worldwide! He decided to make a social media campaign! He decided to make a social media campaign! At the start, no-one saw his post, people thought it was just an ordinary kid. He did not lose hope, he made documentaries, drawings, everything he could. And one day, the unthinkable happened. Everyone took notice of his posts, documentaries, and everything he was doing in the past few weeks. Then, came a message from the government of India: "We will help you implement your idea." Thomas was shocked; he didn't expect anything like that! He asked them, "But how will India help Brazil?" The next day, a reply came: "We will handle that; just come and visit us for a conference!" Thomas asked his dad if they could go; his dad thought that they could go to India for their winter holidays. Thomas was waiting for his holidays, researching about India too. Thomas spent every spare moment researching India, learning about its culture, technological advancements, and commitment to sustainability. As his winter break finally approached, he found himself boarding a plane with his father, his mind waiting with anticipation. Upon arriving in India, Thomas was greeted by a team of officials eager to hear about his initiative. They took him to meetings and discussions, where he shared his concerns about deforestation and the importance of preserving the environment. The representatives were impressed by Thomas's determination and his creative approach to raising awareness. In the days that followed, Thomas was introduced to innovative eco-friendly initiatives implemented in India. He visited sustainable architecture projects, green spaces within urban areas, and educational programs promoting environmental conservation. During one of the meetings, a high-ranking official handed Thomas a proposal. It was a collaborative effort between India and Brazil to create a global campaign for reforestation. Thomas couldn’t believe it! He was jumping in joy!! After a few days, a problem arose. The authorities were angry that Thomas had approached other countries, thinking that India should not have poked their finger into Brazil’s business. Thomas was angry and sad at the same time. He thought that the Brazilians would listen to India as they had good relations. He never expected anything like this! Thomas found himself caught in diplomatic tensions. The authorities in Brazil were upset that he had sought help from India without their permission, viewing it as interference in their internal affairs. Despite the problems, Thomas was determined to find a solution that would benefit both Rio De Janeiro and the environment. He decided to organize a meeting with the local authorities in Rio de Janeiro to explain his intentions and the potential benefits of the collaboration with India. With the help of his dad, Thomas secured a meeting with his dad's cousin and his colleagues, who worked in the local authorities. He researched for days on how to integrate buildings with plants and the environment. He came up with ideas like green walls, vertical farming, courtyards, sustainable landscaping, and urban agriculture. As they sat across the table, Thomas passionately explained his vision for a global campaign for reforestation that could make Rio de Janeiro a model for sustainable development. To his surprise, his dad's cousin listened attentively and acknowledged the importance of environmental conservation. However, he also expressed concerns about the political problems of involving foreign countries in Brazil's environmental policies. Thomas, with newfound happiness, proposed a joint effort where Brazil and India could work together under the guidance of international environmental organizations. His dad's cousin saw the idea in this suggestion and agreed to present the proposal to higher authorities. Weeks passed, filled with uncertainty, as Thomas anxiously awaited a response. Then, one day, an official letter arrived at his doorstep. The local authorities had reluctantly agreed to the collaborative effort, realizing the potential benefits for Rio de Janeiro. Jumping in joy, he screamed, “Let’s gooooo”. Your Idea is agreed on Excited, Thomas quickly contacted the Indian officials, expressing his gratitude and informing them of the positive development. The Indian representatives were pleased with the outcome and assured him that they would provide the necessary resources to make the campaign successful The collaborative effort began with a series of initiatives aimed at raising awareness about deforestation and promoting sustainable practices. Thomas, now a symbol of environmental activism in Rio de Janeiro, found himself leading tree-planting events, organizing educational programs in schools, and participating in media campaigns. India's involvement brought international attention to the cause, and environmentalists worldwide lauded the joint effort. As the campaign gained momentum, Thomas and his team worked closely with experts from both Brazil and India to develop comprehensive reforestation plans. They identified suitable areas for planting, selected native tree species, and implemented measures to ensure the long-term survival of the newly planted trees. The campaign also focused on engaging local communities, encouraging them to take an active role in preserving their environment. Green spaces emerged amidst urban developments, and the once barren construction sites were replaced by thriving ecosystems. Thomas's efforts had not only halted deforestation but had also set an example for sustainable development that other cities around the world began to follow. The success of the campaign turned Thomas into a global environmental ambassador. He continued to work with international organizations, sharing the lessons learned from Rio de Janeiro's transformation and advocating for sustainable practices on a broader scale. The collaborative effort between Brazil and India became a model for cross-border environmental initiatives, proving that when nations unite for a common cause, the impact can be profound. As Thomas entered his teenage years, he reflected on the journey that had started with a boy's concern for the trees outside his school. His determination, coupled with international cooperation, had not only saved the forests of Rio de Janeiro but had contributed to a global movement for a greener, more sustainable future.
author: Adrian Caleb

title: A big boy finds sincerity
text: "Arya, let's play" "Don't you want to go to the cafeteria with us?" "Arya, let's eat together." "Arya, why do you always sit?" Today is Arya's fifth day of school. However, Arya always refused all his classmates' invitations to go together. Arya was afraid that if he stood up, they would laugh at his big body. "My legs are very stiff" - Arya Because his legs were too long, he had to bend them under the table. The table and chairs were too short for him. "Arya, we want to go to the library, come with us" again and again, his classmate invited him to the library. "Should I go with them? I'm tired of sitting all the time," Arya thought to himself. After thinking for a moment, Arya finally decided to stand up and go with his new frien ds for the first time. Arya closed his eyes for a moment, afraid of his friends' reactions, but they didn't give any reaction. He felt very relieved that his friends did not make fun of him. After arriving at the library, Arya's friends immediately looked for books they wanted to read. "Arya, can you get this for me?" Since the book was placed on the top shelf, his friends asked his help to get the book, and he was happy to do that. Thanks to his long legs and big body, Arya easily took books from higher shelves. Likewise, his other friends also asked for his help to get books they couldn't reach. "Arya, help me too." "Please get me the book." "That one too." “That green book, please.” This was quite tiring, and Arya wondered if his friends were just taking advantage of him because his legs were so long, but he quickly dismissed his negative thoughts. After the school bell rang, the students immediately went home. While on the way home, Arya saw his friends climbing a tree. "What are you doing here?" - asked Arya "We're trying to get some wood. Can you help us?" Said his friends "Of course." Without a ladder, Arya picked up large and small pieces of wood from the trees. "Enough, Arya." Said his friends "Okay." - Arya “Thank you Arya, we will go home now, see you tomorrow" - After they got the wood they said goodbye to Arya and left After back from school, Arya immediately ate and changed his clothes caused his mother asked him to buy bread near the field. After arriving at the bakery, Arya saw his friends playing on the side of the field, carrying wood that he had taken this afternoon. After buying bread, Arya rushed home ve ry sad ly, thinking that his friends weren't sincere about being friends with him and only wanted to take advantage of his long legs. He cried, he didn't want to be friends with anyone anymore. The next day, Arya came to school with gloomy feeling, When he entered the classroom, he was surprised to see his chairs and desks. They were new, much bigger than before. So, he doesn't need to keep folding his legs while sitting. It turned out that the chairs and table were gifts from his friends for Arya They knew Arya's previous chair and table were too small for him, so they took the initiative to make new ones for him. They went to the library to find out how to make tables and chairs. They also collect wood to make the chairs. Arya was very happy that his friends really care about him, even though he misunderstood their intentions. Since then, Arya promised that he would never feel inferior again. He is grateful for his long legs and promise to use them to help his friends.
author: NADIATUL IKHSANIYAH

title: The Adventures of Lord Hanuman
text: Once upon a time, in the mystical land of Ayodhya, there lived a brave and mighty monkey god named Hanuman. Hanuman was a devoted follower of Lord Rama, the noble prince. One day, Sita, Rama's wife, was kidnapped by the evil demon king Ravana. Rama was sad and worried. Hanuman decided to help his beloved Lord Rama. Verse 1: Praise to Hanuman In the heart of the forest, Hanuman knelt down and began to pray. "Hey Hanuman, the son of the wind, You are brave, strong, and kind. With a heart full of devotion, You'll cross the ocean with unwavering emotion." Verse 2: Blessings of Strength Lord Hanuman prayed for strength and courage to leap across the vast ocean. "Grant me strength, O Lord above, To find Sita with pure love. Bless me with the power to soar, To bring her back forevermore." Verse 3: Hanuman's Mighty Leap With a powerful jump, Hanuman soared across the ocean, reaching the island of Lanka. "Jumping high and flying far, I'll reach Lanka like a shining star. To find Sita and bring her back, I'll stay on the righteous track." Verse 4: Meeting Sita Hanuman found Sita in Lanka and reassured her that Rama was coming to rescue her. "Sita, dear, don't you fear, Rama is near, so wipe that tear. He'll defeat Ravana and set you free, Together again, a happy family." Verse 5: Hanuman's Devotion Hanuman then returned to Rama and shared the news of finding Sita. "Hanuman, the brave and true, Found Sita and gave the news to you. With devotion strong and love so deep, In Rama's service, my promises I keep." Verse 6: Lord Rama's Blessings Lord Rama, grateful for Hanuman's devotion, blessed him with eternal life. "Hanuman, my truest friend, Your devotion knows no end. Blessed you are with life so long, In everyone's heart, you belong." And so, the tale of Hanuman's devotion and bravery spread far and wide, inspiring all to be courageous, loyal, and true. title: Melody March
text: As the melody maiden’s tune begins to play, People from near and far come her way, Happiness spreads, and sadness goes away. I’m the Illep, short and neat, With my pep-pep-pep-peeeeee, I can't be beat, Children come close, tapping their feet. Behold! I am the Otekra! long and thin, I sing tweee-tweeee-tooo in the wind, Like a bird's song, making children grin. Step aside! title: Christmas Eve
text: I woke up in the morning. I was excited, it was Christmas Eve! I go downstairs and gaze at the tree. I was thinking of all the presents that there could be in those big and little boxes under the tree. I thought that it was okay to take a sneak peek into the boxes, but my mom found out. Whatever it was, i still had a big day ahead of me! We had a great breakfast and my mom called me to write a letter to Santa! I wrote a letter to Santa and asked my mom if I could bake cookies and give it to our neighbours. My mom allowed me and she taught me how to bake cookies! It was really fun. At night, we wrapped around the cozy fire. We were telling stories about Christmas and Santa Claus. It was the best Christmas Eve ever!
author: Arihanth Nirmalkumar

title: Johnny and his dog!
text: Good morning mom! Hey Johnny! What's up? The Sky! Ha Ha. Why are you in a bad mood?? I AM NOT!! YIKES!! After some time.... Johnny! COME HERE!! OH NO! Does she know I broke the vase?? BROTHER BROKE IT!! It's not that! But know I know who broke the vase! Then, what is it?? Did you see our puppy?? He's lost and I can't find him!! Oh NO! I left him in the street! YOU IDIOT!! WHY?? You only told me to take him out with the trash!! I meant for a walk, stupid! So, you threw him in the dustbin??!! Johnny!!! Sorry mommy!! Johnny was never found again as his mother took him for a walk while taking out the trash.
author: Bookheart Brave
illustrator: Bookheart Brave; Deepa Balsavar; Megan Vermaak

title: MEG THE CAT
text: This is about Meg, a kind-hearted stray cat. he would always walk through the doors to find a good shelter, but alas, no one wanted her as he was a black cat. he always saw beautiful cats impressing people, and he felt sad that no one needed him. But he was confident that his day would come. One day, Meg entered a beautiful house full of plants. He was happy that he could hide in the outhouse between the plants and have a safe shelter. he did not go too much inside the house, as he was afraid that he could be caught and thrown out. On a rainy day, Meg could not go outdoors; he felt bored, so he decided to slowly go inside the house. On entering the house, Meg was left amazed. The house was kept neat and clean, and Meg was wondering whether she was in paradise. Thinking so, Meg slowly tiptoed to the inside of the house. Suddenly, she heard a sneaky sound. A small, adorable little dog was looking at Meg and smiling. He had a lot of hair that was brown in colour Meg knew that dogs and cats are enemies and was afraid that the dog would attack her. Meg was afraid that he could lose her shelter forever. But to his surprise, the dog did not bark. He was wagging his tail at Meg. Meg took a long breath and smiled back. The dog came near Meg and introduced herself. His name was Teddy. He was the pet dog of the house owner’s little son. Meg told her sad story and the manner in which people used to throw him out of their house. Teddy pacified Meg and told her that he would not tell anyone about this. They became thick friends. Teddy began to share his food with Meg. Meg’s life became cheerful and happy. Teddy came to Meg whenever nobody was around, and they played in the outhouse. Life was going on happily until vacation time came. The daughter of the house owner came on vacation. She was not alone; she came with a big, heavy cat. Meg saw the cat and was terrified of it. Even Teddy was afraid of the cat. Meg knew that the fat cat would bite her if it found out that she was staying in the outhouse. Meg decided to go out of the house. Her life was again the same old story. She came back to the outhouse during the night, as she knew that the fat cat would be sleeping early in the night. She and Teddy had a long discussion, and both of them were very annoyed with the big fat cat. The next morning, while walking through the market, Meg overheard a Shakespearean quote: "Cowards die many times before their deaths; the valiant never taste of death” Meg gained courage she had never had before after hearing this. She decided to face the big, fat cat. She knew that Fat Cat was much stronger than him, but she was confident that with her speed and guile, she could defeat him. Meg came inside the house. The owner’s daughter, Sara, was sitting with the big, fat cat. Sara looked at Meg and said, "Wow, a charming little black cat." Meg was very glad to hear this; this was the first time she had heard somebody praise her. The fat cat did not like the attention Meg was getting. He decided to give a bite to Meg. The fat cat growled. Hearing this, Sara told him to keep quiet. But the fat cat was very livid; he jumped out of Sara’s lap and flung himself towards Meg. Teddy told Meg to run for her life. Meg ran with all her might and, upon reaching the end of the wall, slid towards the other side. The fat cat could not slide as he was very fat, and he hit the wall. Meg was very thin, and he could run at high speeds. The fat cat could not match the speed of Meg and became exhausted. After some time, he fell to the floor, tired. Meg felt like a proud lion, and she jumped and slapped the big cat. The fat cat ran away without looking back. Meg was very happy, and he could see her best friend laughing his heart out. But he knew she couldn't stay in the house any longer because everyone had discovered her secret hideout. he was very sad to part with Charlotte. Both of them hugged each other for the last time. Meg began to walk away from the house. Someone suddenly lifted him off the ground. Meg assumed it was the big, fat cat.. He looked up and saw Sara cuddling him. Meg could not believe her luck. he looked up at the sky with gratitude. Seeing this, Teddy winked at Meg and said, "Luck always favours the brave."
author: Keerthana Krishnamohan
illustrator: Catherine Groenewald; Debasmita Dasgupta; Gwendolene van der Merwe; Marion  Drew; Nirzara Verulkar; Rohan Chakravarty; Sahil Shaikh; Vusi  Malindi; Yuvaka  Srestha

title: Snow the little goat
text: Once upon a time there lived a little goat, who was lonely and sad until a boy named Kailash found her while walking back from school. Kailash took the little goat to his dad who is a farmer. His dad agreed to have the little goat in the farm. Kailash named the little goat as Snow. Snow was happy in the farm but the animals in the farm do not want to play with her. Snow sat under a tree gazing at the sun where she found a new friend. Yummy yummy. The new friend was a bird named Chirp.Snow was very happy to see her new friend.Chirp and Snow played and played till they were tired. Hello. Hi. The next morning the Sun was shining bright. Snow woke up to the cheerful chirping of her friend Chirp.The two friends started playing again and they enjoyed being together.
author: Samiksha Sai

title: Bunny Finds a New Home
text: Once upon a time in the cozy town of Carrotvillae, Jenny the bunny faced a big challenge when a storm destroyed his burrow. With a positive spirit, Jenny and his family set out on a journey to find a new home. The path was tough—rivers to cross, thickets to navigate, and a steep mountain to climb. But Jenny stayed strong, encouraging his family to face each obstacle together. Along the way, they discovered a beautiful meadow with friendly animals willing to help. Jenny's family, along with their new friends, worked together to build a new burrow. J enny's boundless energy and positive outlook inspired everyone. Through resilience and teamwork, they created a haven of joy. In the end, Carrotvillae not only found a new home but also formed a stronger, more caring community. Jenny's journey taught everyone that even in the face of challenges, a positive attitude and helping hands can turn tough times into opportunities for growth and friendship. And so, the meadow of Carrotvillae became a symbol of hope and togetherness for all.
author: Diana Nadira Puthusseri
illustrator: Imphir; Joanna Davala; Katrin Coetzer; San srei nou ch nou ch; Sonal Goyal; Sumit Sakhuja

title: Amina's Journey
text: Once upon a time, in a faraway land, there was a little girl named Amina. Amina lived in a peaceful village with her family and friends. They played together, shared stories, and laughed under the warm sun. But one day... something unexpected happened. A big storm came, and it brought not only rain but also trouble. Amina's village was no longer a safe place to stay. Their village was flooded, and everyone had to leave. Amina's family, along with other families from the village, became refugees. Being a refugee meant they had to travel to find a new home where they could be safe and start anew. Amina was terrified, but she trusted her parents. As they journeyed through unknown lands, Amina and the other children met new friends who were also refugees. Together, they made the best of their situation, playing games and sharing stories to lighten the difficult journey. Along the way, Amina's family faced challenges, but they also found kindness from people who helped them. They were given food, water, and a place to rest. Amina learned that kindness and helping one another made their journey a little easier. Finally, after many days of walking, they arrived at a refugee camp. The camp was a temporary home where many families like Amina's stayed until they could find a more permanent place to live. At the camp, there were schools for the children, and Amina was excited to learn new things and make more friends. Amina and her family worked hard to build a new life. They learned the customs of their new home, made friends with their neighbors, and soon the camp felt more like a community. Amina's parents found jobs, and she went to school, where she discovered the joy of learning.
author: Diana Nadira Puthusseri

title: zombies in school
text: I pressed against the door lest they should try to break it down. It can sound silly and desperate, but I did not want to test their intelligence. I looked over at Shalini, who was whimpering in the corner of the classroom. I reflected on what had happened two hours ago. We had been playing by the old, abandoned grave. It was always our favourite place. Vidya ran towards the boundaries as I ran to catch her. She stopped for breath as Shalini caught up with us. She had shown us the crystalline green salt that she had apparently stolen from the chemistry lab. That was when she had accidentally dropped the salt. It had simply dissolved into the soil and a moment later, the shaking had begun. We saw slimy grey hands protruding from underneath the soil and ran to the school. Vidya’s voice jarred me out of my flashback. “I’m sorry. This was all my fault. I never should have taken that salt,” she sobbed. ‘It’s okay, Vidya. We’ll find a way out of this.” I looked around our physics classroom. Shalini was staring into space. I heard some scratching. I could hear heavy feet being dragged towards our room. I gave out a weak sound. I peeped through the keyhole and saw one of those awful creatures. I resisted the urge to scream as I sat back down and signalled to my friend to be silent. After some time, we heard the feet dragging themselves back down the corridor. I opened the door a little and saw an empty corridor. I immediately signalled to my friends to follow me as we tiptoed down the corridor to the stairs. On reaching the stairs, we climbed down quietly and reached the lowermost floor. We walked across the field at a fast pace and fled up the street on reaching the school gates. Shalini’s immediate suggestion was to go to the police station. We ran up the street until we reached the main road. A kind woman riding her car in the opposite direction, on seeing our dirty uniforms and messed up hair, asked us if we were alright. We immediately replied in a cheerful tone that we were quite alright, but Shalini said, “Actually, ma’am we’d be happy if you could let us hitchhike. You see, we really need to get to the police station right now.” The woman was happy to let us hitchhike. She rode her car to the nearest police station and escorted us inside. There, a man was sitting on a chair next to a desk that held a name card that said “Mr. Rakesh”. On seeing us, his eyes opened wide as he looked down at us. Shalini spoke first. “Sir, there is an abandoned graveyard near our school. When we were playing there, my friend here… she dropped some-uh-salt.” “Immediately the ground shook and we saw zombies coming up. We ran into the school and hid from them. We managed to escape and come here sir. We’re afraid they’re on the loose,” Vidya provided. “Why, this makes no sense whatsoever! But I shall come with you to check, of course.” We went in a police car back to the grounds. There, the policeman asked us to wait in the car and went to check the school out for himself. Some ten minutes later, we saw other police cars coming in the distance. Policemen ran up to the school and returned shortly with the creatures themselves. When my friends saw them, they cried out loud. I assumed they had done so because I was the only one who had actually seen them. The zombies were forced into the cars and there were about 8 of them, I observed. The policeman came back with a grin of satisfaction. He gave some instructions to the other policemen and came back to the car. “What happened, sir?” I asked. “I’ll explain everything later,” he promised. We drove back to the police station in silence. When we reached, the policeman beckoned us to sit down. Since there were only two seats, I remained standing. “The men we caught just now were not zombies. They were criminals who had broken out of prison,” he explained. ‘But they didn’t look human at all!” I protested. Vidya said, “they looked very much human, sir. We had previously believed what our friend here had said,” looking at me in disgust. “Ah, yes. As for the slimy hand you had seen- that graveyard had once been used to make a horror film. The hand had just been a prop.” I could not believe this at all. However, I realised Mr. Rakesh did know more about the world than me. ‘We are sorry for wasting your time, sir. We will take your leave now,” Shalini said. “Oh, not at all! You helpe d us capture some mass criminals, didn’t you? Ill drive you home,” Mr. Rakesh said. “It’s alright, sir. We prefer to walk home all the time,” Vidya said. And so, we began our journey back home. “I still can’t believe this. Those criminals didn’t look human at all!” I complained. Vidya said, “Aditi, you sit in the first row and yet you complain of not being able to see the board. Don’t you think its time you got glasses?” I realised what she had said made sense. I still did not give up my case, tough. “What about the ground suddenly trembling? You can’t deny that” I reasoned. Shalini sighed. “Didn’t you listen to what the kind lady was saying? She had said that their ha been a slight tremor that shook he house along with many others.it was a small tremor experienced not just by us, Aditi.” I sighed. This was another argument I had lost. We reached the street where we had to part ways. I said my goodbyes and walked home, thinking of what colour I would like my glasses to be.
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: Untold Story Of Village Lohari
text: Today I’m going to tell you about a beautiful village,Lohari. The village is located at the foothills of a mountain.There are many beautiful and memerizing place in the village that are not less than tourist attractions. Village is surrounded by high mountain peaks from all sides and the river Yamuna flows near village where I, with my friend and elder swim during summer time. Villager made a temporary bridge out of bamboo that connects village to the other side. There is a large piece of land for farming in village. Villager follows traditional method of farming. The village is affected by the two Hydroelectric Projects, namely Lakhwar and Vyasi of 300 and 120 megawatt. The completion of these project will benefit the residents of Uttarkhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, UP,Rajasthan and Delhi. But these project will affected 334 families and six villages. The Lohari is manily affected by Vasi Hydro-electric project,as Lohari is upstream and the nearest village to this project. But. Many year ago in1972,a land acquisition agreement was signed between the government and the villager for the construction of a dam on the river yamuna. The agreement specifies that in future,land is to be given in compensation for land acquired under the project. But in a cabinet meeting in July2021, the Uttarakhand government backed away from their decision. In 2017 the government had offered a payment to Lohari villagers that would bridge the difference between how much their predecessors had paid in 1972 and the land rate currently. This offer was refused. The villagers also refused to take part in assessments valuing their properties, so officials took rough measurements from outside the houses of villagers to estimate the compensation to be paid. The villagers also said that it is not possible to buy replacement farmland and build new homes with the money the government is giving. Therefore, for four months last year, from 5th June 2021 to protest (Dharna), demanding rehabilitation and land in compensation for land. On the early morning of 2nd October 2021 at the site of dharna (sit-in-protest) 4 AM police arrived at the spot and forcefully arrested more than 11 people of the village and put them into jail.when I was around 5 year old I used to hear that village is going to drown I thought that it’s just a joke but when this happened in front of my eyes I couldn’t believe that. With very heavy heart I have to tell you people that on 5th April 2022, 48 hours notice was sent to Lohari village to evacuate their homes otherwise JCB’s and bulldozer would be used. So the villagers broke their houses themselves with a heavy heart and carried their essentials and belongings to the nearby closed and barren Govenment Primary and Junior High School building. In name of compensation very small amount was forcefully sent into the villagers account without their consent. Now all village families (about 30 families) are homeless and are forced to live in the campus of barren and damaged three room building of Government Junior High School. With very less space, villagers are sleeping outside with heavy risk of wild animals, snakes, mosquitoes etc. It's really heartbreaking that they left their homes for the country's upliftment and development. The government doesn’t bother about anything, they didn’t realise the pain of village people at the time, everytime they only saw their profit and benefit. By the time I reached to the village everything was destroyed. It was all finished. The doors of the dam were closed, slowly the water level began to rise and all houses wereflooded with water. Till next morning the village was fully logged with water and the people of village looked on helplessly as their homes, farmland and cowsheds got submerged in the water. Everthing was finshed, everyone was crying and sitting quietly. Now none could help them. 5th April is the black day of lohari.
author: Sakshi Tomar

title: When it was flooded
text: We had never seen such a flood before. The flood that occurred on /2008 forced us to face many difficulties. Due to the flood, our homes and belongings were washed away. There was also damage to farming, and grains were not available even in the ration shops. Many people started dying of hunger due to the flood, and many were swept away. The laps of many mothers and sisters became empty, and many mothers and sisters became widows. Even brave individuals, big and small, were swept away. Wherever there was higher ground, everyone went, and snakes and insects were also there. In our village, on 28-08-2008, the flood came at 12 o'clock. We left our homes and had to walk 12 kilometers. Still, we faced a lot of difficulties in reaching Saharsa. Here, we get flattened rice and sugar for breakfast. Rice, lentils, and vegetables are available for meals. There haven't been any difficulties in education. Children's Anecdotes In an age when children should be playing, learning, and understanding the world around them without any hindrance, the children of North Bihar had to endure a dreadful calamity like the flood. In this calamity, countless children lost family members, witnessed their homes being swept away, and observed their domestic animals flowing in front of their eyes. These harsh scenes have somehow left an indelible mark on their minds. It will take them time to forget. And forgetting is not easy. Reading the thoughts of children in this collection makes it clear how suddenly this flood has affected the hearts of these children. At an age when children from other places write about flowers, butterflies, rivers, and mountains, children from North Bihar, when they sit down to write, cannot escape the scenes of the flood tragedy. The older generations, having grown up, have a duty to this tender generation. That duty is to ensure that when this generation grows up, it never has to face the crisis of a flood like this again. The older generation must decide today that it will work patiently in this region of North Bihar to prevent the recurrence of floods. They should refrain from any activity that poses a constant threat of floods. To save tender hearts, to save the tender generation, the older generations will have to make some tough decisions today. We must revisit the environment, accept rivers and forests as integral parts of our society, and progress in the direction of establishing harmony with nature. The stories that emerge from the tiny pens of children are just a clarion call for this. 2 June 2009 Anupam Mishra Gandhi Peace Foundation
author: Jaison Rebello

title: Leech!
text: There were only two things that Shanbor enjoyed doing– bossing around and lazing away. “Yaaaawwnnn!! Another day to watch over my people working!” While he loved bossing around, he enjoyed lazing around even more. So lazy was he that he didn't even want to go to his paddy field to supervise his workers. "Let me take a peek through my window." “Are they even working? I can’t see. Yaawnnn. I don't want to go and check now. Maybe tomorrow.” "Maybe tomorrow," he said. And he said this everyday! Then one fine day, Shanbor thought of a BRILLIANT idea! “Aha! I just know what to do! I am so so smart!” “Hello Ding Ding and Mon Mon! I have an important job for you two.” “Go watch over my fields and workers for me. Report everything to me in the evening. Don’t be late!” As Ding Ding and Mon Mon left, Shanbor went back to sleep. “ Now I can go back to sleep. Ding Ding and Mon Mon will do all the work. They will be back in the evening.” As Shanbor snored away to glory, Ding Ding and Mon Mon began their adventures. “Ding Ding, let’s go look for the tallest tree to climb!!” “Mon Mon, this one here is the tallest!” “No, Ding Ding, that one over there is the tallest!” "Adididi! Adadada! Aninini! Hurry Mon Mon, I can't keep an eye on your side of things!" “We have to be diligent and report everything to Master!” “M-mm-master, we are back.” “Ding Ding! Mon Mon! What took you both so long? Report everything to your Master, now!” “Yes, yes Master!” Pleased that he can sleep all day, everyday, Shanbor puts Ding Ding and Mon Mon back. “Time to get back inside, Mon Mon, Ding Ding!” The same cycle continued everyday. One fine day as Mon Mon and Ding Ding were watching over their Master’s fields… …a crow comes and swoops them up… “ Masterrrrrrrrr…!! HELLLPPP!!” …and flies away! As the sun went down and it got darker, Shanbor started wondering where Ding Ding and Mon Mon were. “I can’t see anything! Why are Ding Ding and Mon Mon not back??” A few days passed by and Shanbor managed to crawl out of his house into the dark night. So deep into the night it was that everyone was shut up in their houses. There was no one to help him! “Water! Water! Somebody give me some water!” “Thirsty... I am so thirsty! Maybe I can quench my thirst if I suck my own blood.” “Somebody! Anybody! Deliver me from this misery!!” It seemed like someone had heard Shanbor’s plea. He was turned into... a LEECH! Activity Shanbor is thirsty! Could you guide Shanbor to the water source to quench his thirst?
author: Lanu Tsudir

text: I SHARMA, SEEDLING MODERN, Sayan Mukherjee, Suvidha Mistry This story is about a 10-year-old boy Naman, one boy Naman was weak in studies he got scolded from his teacher and mother everyday he was always late in submitting the copies he can't understand anything in studies one day when he looked in the sky, he decided to become a scientist now slowly he started improving one day he got full marks in the test now he awaited to get back home to show his test his patience was going and suddenly the bell rang. When he reached back and showed his test paper his mother praised him very much and made his favorite food he was now getting better in his studies. 5 years later, he was now in 12th standard and lived in a hostel he was worried because tomorrow was his Final Exam he studied till late night. title: Where is Timmy?
text: Timmy, Katie's puppy was a naughty one. He always kept running around to have his food. One morning, Katie woke up finding Timmy. Where did he go? Mysterious.... She checked the whole house but there was no trace of Timmy. She started crying. "Katie, set up the dining and brush up yourself...Breakfast's ready!". "Coming..."sighed Katie. "What's the matter honey?" mom asked. Katie explained everything about Timmy to her mom. "Oh no!!" exclaimed her mom. "You lost him". Both of them started finding but couldn't so they sat at the dining for breakfast. Something felt soft under the table. Guess what they saw under the table? TIMMY!! "Oh, here you are "both of them sighed of relief. "Naughty boy" Katie said.

title: A DAY WITH BAMBI
text: One cold winter morning, Bambi wakes up and is sleepy. Then, Bambi eats his breakfast because he is very hungry. At 9 o'clock in the morning, Bambi goes to school because he wants to learn. At noon, Bambi is hungry and goes to eat meat. In the afternoon, Bambi goes out to play with his friends in the park. Bambi goes to visit his grandparents, but he falls on the way and seriously injures his leg. At night, Bambi goes to the hospital and the doctors treat his wound. Later, Bambi comes home very tired and in a lot of pain. Finally, Bambi falls asleep and dreams that tomorrow he will be healthy.

text: Good Morning Mom and dad said Sita and Rima. The breakfast is ready! said mom. Dad after i come from school can we go to the food stall that has come to the city. title: The Wise Young Morgan
text: “I despise you both! And your happy, seemingly perfect life. How could you ever understand what I could’ve gone through and not blame me for everything? In a quaint little town, lived a 13-year-old girl who was affectionately called Mellie by her family. It was a nickname chosen by her mother that everyone began to use. But she was the one who was most proud of the nickname she chose… She felt it was the perfect name for a sweet little child like Melissa. From that day on, she yearned to be called Mellie just one more time.She was at that age where emotions ran high, and conflicts with her family seemed inevitable. One stormy evening, after a series of small fights with her parents,Mellie, unable to contain her anger, rushed to her room and slammed it shut. Seated on the floor with her head down and eyes closed, she screamed and cried out of frustration. Harsh and unforgivable words had been exchanged, leaving a bitter taste in the air. In Mellie’s mind came a hurricane of emotions but not a tinge of regret! As she raised her head, expecting the comforting glow of her room's lights, darkness enveloped her. Assuming it was a power outage, Mellie sighed and put her head back between her knees. However, when she looked up again, seemingly having slept for a long time; the entire town was plunged into darkness. Confused, she wandered out of her room to check with her parents. To her surprise, their room was empty. Puzzled, she checked her dining room and even the living room, but her family was nowhere to be found. Panic set in as she called out their names, but only silence answered her. It was as if her family had vanished into thin air. In a state of bewilderment, Mellie realized something was amiss. The air felt different, charged with an eerie energy indicating someone’s presence in the room, even though there seemed to be no one around. She could feel it though, that somebody had entered her house without her knowing and that something somewhere had gone very wrong. As she frantically searched the house for any trace of a living person beside her, she stumbled upon an open window, a subtle hint that someone had entered into the house, or better put, something unusual had occurred. Then, she no ti ced a faint trail of golden dust leading outside. Curiosity and concern arose in Mellie's heart as she followed the trail into the quiet night. The darkness outside was profound such that it was a pitch black night with no sign of the moon, and no sign of her mother who used to tell her to look out the window when a beautiful crescent moon lit up the night sky. Although that darkness,was broken only by the mysterious golden lights flickering like distant fireflies. Mellie hesitated but pressed on, her curiosity overpowered her fear. The trail led her to the outskirts of the town, where the golden lights coalesced into a shimmering portal. The door that outwardly seemed to be an outline made by a large group of fireflies was looking beautiful in the night. At the portal's threshold stood a shadowy figure, barely visible against the darkness. Mellie's heart raced as the figure turned towards her;there stood an adult man who looked young yet sage. “A good nap you seemed to have there, eh? Well I’m glad you seem rested, I had to put you to sleep briefly for the mission I needed to accomplish.It’s no biggie since you woke up just a second after, Plus you got enough rest for the adventure you’re about to go through. Don’t worry! Your parents are safe, I’m just hoping to teach you a lesson.” “And, Since, I don’t want you to blame me later for not giving you enough hints, leaving you completely flabbergasted Blah! Blah! I will give you a clue just this once;” And he stepped closer to the young Morgan and whispered in her ears, “Dear Melissa, Words have power, and you must learn to wield them wisely." Mellie, bewildered and frightened, demanded answers. The figure seemed eccentric and the words didn’t make any more sense either. Still annoyed by the anonymous figure that appeared before her and his unbothered yet wise way of speaking; Mellie felt she had to get her parents back, and so she embarked on a quest to rescue her family from the apparently otherworldly realm. Mellie's journey took her through mystical landscapes that each presented a unique journey of their own that tested her patience and conscience. The mysterious figure, who seemed to be both a guide and a guardian, occasionally appeared to offer cryptic advice, pushing Mellie to dig deeper into her own soul. The golden trail first led Mellie to a library where the very words she had spoken during the fights were recorded in shimmering books. She read through the volumes, reliving the pain she had caused from a perspective she had overlooked. Her parent’s emotions and need to care after their only child who was the apple of their eye was immense. At the same time, they were deeply hurt. They wished to give her child a happy and perfect life, but she seemed to hate them for that! “The writer is cruel.” she said as a tear fell and rolled down her cheek onto the book. The sound of the drop echoed as she realized the intensity of the silence of the library of reflections. And soon the Landscape changed leaving behind only the chair she was seated on. In a realm of illusions, Mellie then confronted mirages that tested her patience. These illusions aimed to deceive her into speaking words that echoed her past mistakes. But when Mellie would not utter a single word without conscience, The mirages changed to portray her with her family, happy moments of simple bliss! Oh! How she yearned for her family… Yet another tear dropped from her eye and she was transported to an entirely different landscape… The culmination of her journey brought Mellie to a serene garden. There, she found her family, encased in a large orb that mirrored the bonds they shared. The mysterious figure appeared once more, revealing that the crystal orb represented the fragility of those connections, easily shattered by thoughtless words. In a final trial, Mellie had to find the key to unlock the crystal and free her family. The key, she discovered, was a simple phrase: "I understand." As she uttered those words, the crystal began to dissolve, releasing her family from its confines. Tears of remorse and gratitude filled Mellie's eyes as she embraced each family member, apologizing for the pain she had caused. The mysterious figure, its purpose fulfilled, nodded approvingly. With a wave of its hand, the golden lights enveloped Mellie and her family, transporting them back to their home. Back in the real world, Mellie awoke in her room, the first rays of a new day casting a warm glow. Her heart was heavy with the weight of the lessons learned, but also lighter with her new understanding and conscious personality. The experience transformed Mellie into a wiser, more compassionate person who would grow up to become an adult like Sammy who had gone through adventures alike Mellie when he was a silly teenager. “Mellie dear, I cooked some pancakes for you for breakfast! I hoped you’d come and eat with pa and me…” Mellie smiled at the call of her nickname and replied “Sure mum! Let’s have a good breakfast together. I’m starving!”
author: Aishani  Chauhan

title: Do you like online games?
text: I like to play online games. Do any of you have the same hobby as me? When I was at school, I was always looking forward to going home so I could play games. "It's taking so long to go home from school, I still haven't finished playing the online game from yesterday," I said to myself. I often don't focus on my studies at school because I'm thinking about games. At home, I keep playing games until I forget the time. "Yay... I won," I said when I won. One day, my mom called me while I was playing a game. I was so focused on the game that I didn't hear her. My mom got mad at me. Nat.. Mom forgot to buy salt at the market. Can you buy it at the corner shop? Hemm.. Oh, by the way, the sugar is running low. Since that incident, my mom banned me from playing games. I even need her permission to open the computer to do my homework. I feel sad when I look at the computer. Sometimes, I get mad and argue with Mom. One week after that, Mom talked to me, "Nat... too much of anything is not good. You spend too much time playing games that you can't focus on your studies and you often daydream. Your grades are not good enough. I know this from your teacher at school through the phone." Nowadays, when I need to use the computer for homework, Mom will always be there with me. She always tells me, "Playing online games too often can lead to addiction, also known as gaming disorder. It can cause changes in the brain's function and structure, especially in the parts that control pleasure, learning, and motivation." I listened to Mom's advice and stopped playing games. I help Mom with chores more often. I spend time with my family and friends in the neighborhood. Hi friends, I hope you can learn from this experience. Keep up the good work, obey your parents' advice, and love them!
author: Victoria Abigail Prabowo

title: Let's Dance with Ainam
text: Hello, I am Ainam. I am practising the dance steps for the Shad Suk Mynsiem festival. Mei taught me these dance steps. Mei says that this is one of the oldest dances of the Khasi people. Ka Pahsyntiew, the legendary Chieftess of the Khasi people, taught us the dance. First, you must stand straight, raise your right foot like this then move it forward. Then move your left foot slowly. Move only your feet forward. Do not move your body. Do it again! Right foot, left foot - like a crawl. Be slow and steady. It is tricky but be patient. Very nice! You and I are doing so well. The Ka Shad Suk Mynsiem is a dance to thank God for blessing us. It's a way for us to say "thanks" through movement. Now! Let's get ready to dance at the festival. Come join me. See you at the Shad Suk Mynsiem!
author: Auswyn Winter Japang

title: I can create!
text: I am a big boy now. I can draw and create. Amma sits still. I draw a picture of her. I am drawing a painting of my sister. She keeps moving. I am drawing many pictures. But, they have told me not to draw on the walls! I can create. I can make a picture of a cat. It's a fatcat. I am making a picture of a fish. It's a small fish. I am making boats,birds and planes out of paper. I am drawing houses and trains. My sister is creating a chaos! I can create many things.

title: Rainbow Sambhar
text: What can we cook for lunch today?" asked the grandmother. “Today we can make rainbow sambar, grandma!” said Bhavya. “Rainbow Sambara! How do we do that?” Grandma wondered. “I'll show you, Grandma!” said Bhavya. Purple 'Karu Muru' onion Dark blue colored eggplant With a blue-handled knife, Chop them into small pieces. Green skinned, elongated drumsticks Yellow circle Split Gram Lentil Orange colored 'Karuk' bitten carrot Tomatoes rich in red color juice Wash all these well, chop and dice Put in a pan. It dissolves leaving a slightly sweet brown tamarind, spicy and aromatic Add yellow sambar powder and salt. Everything should be sauteed. Mix well. Keep it on low flame and let it boil. This is how it is Rainbow Sambar have to do!

title: The Great Poet Bharathiyar
text: Bharathiyar is perhaps one of the most well-known. Commonly referred to as "Mahakavi Bharathi" (The great poet Bharathi), he was a key player in the Indian independence movement. In the struggle for independence, Bharathiyar employed an unconventional weapon: the pen. One that would prove to be much mightier than the sword. He dreamed of an independent India. He wrote poems inspiring people to join the struggle and make that dream a reality. He believed that this new independent India should be based on equality. Throughout his life, he advocated for women's rights, and his poems reflected these beliefs. He wrote in detail about the great women of the new nation. Bharthiyar also wrote poems about other topics as well. Including but not limited to Patriotism, Female equality, Spirituality, and the caste system. His name has been engraved in the pages of history, and his poems have left a long-lasting impact on Modern-day India. The image above is a quote from Bharathiyar: "Did you think I would give up alike many other people foolish people?"
author: Akshay Chandramouli

title: aloo-maalu-kaalu
text: Grandma said, “Well done Malu! Go and get some potatoes also.” Malu saw all the trees, vines and plants. Potatoes were nowhere to be seen. Grandma, the potatoes haven’t grown yet.” Malu kept the empty basket. “No dear, there are many potatoes growing, look carefully.” Grandma explained. Malu went back to the garden. Kalu also started following him. Malu was searching for potatoes when he heard, “Bhaun, bhaun, bhaun.” “Oh ho! Wait, Kalu,” Malu ran. “Don't spoil the garden.” Malu saw that Kalu had dug a pit. There were big potatoes in the dug soil! Wow Kalu! Find potatoes,” said Malu after filling the basket.
author: Yohit Dev

text: She sees a cow chewing grass. No, it's not the cow that makes the noise. A monkey in a tree? No, it's not a monkey. A monkey in a tree? No, it's not a monkey. Is that a frog? title: My cute little kitten
text: My Kitty's name is Elsa. I love her a lot. She is funny, elegant, beautiful and cute. She is a little ball of fur. She is warm to touch. She always gets over excited and happy. She is very adorable. I love you. She is also very mischievous and small in size. She loves to drink milk. I love to pat her. She is a smart kitty. Elsa also sleeps beside my bed in a blanket specially for her. Her fur is soft and silky. Cute kitty. When I do yoga, she also starts doing yoga with me. She is a smart kitty indeed. title: Water Bodies
text: These people would often collect water from these bodies of water. For their convenience some of the townspeople built wells so they could so they could get the water easily. For the townspeople this fresh water tasted sweeter than honey. A few years later, it gradually began to rain less. Many of the town's lakes, wells and other bodies of water dried up. Many of the area's wildlife, which relied on this source of water suffered. To avoid such a situation from happening to us, let's all conserve rain water.
author: Akshay Chandramouli

title: THE PAST
text: Ivy was walking in the muddy roads of Warrington hopelessly.Suddenly a truck pulled in front of her realising that the truck was her uncle’s (Mr. Silvio) she asked him for a ride. ‘Did you go to meet your mother in the hospital?’ asked uncle 'I was so busy with my job and handling the bills and payments i forgot to visit her I’ll surely go today’ said Ivy. ‘ They reached Ivy's house and Mr.Silvio gave her some food from his truck and left Later that evening, Ivy found an old walkie.When she called on her number a girl picked the call demanding money in return of the phone. Ivy was devastated as well as furious at the same time. The next day the walkie was ringing when Ivy picked it up she heard a girl saying ‘Lyra you haven’t called me from many days you forgot me after I CHANGED YOUR LIFE’, confused Ivy asked ‘What? Who are you trying to call I am not Lyra’ ‘what? Is this not the sung-ho store? Don’t you remember me? I am Natalie Alexandra from D-67 sector-81.’ Ivy horrified hung up the call in shock ‘D-67 sector-81!? This is my address.’ Ivy calmed herself and called on that number again no one picked up. The next day, the walkie rung again Ivy expeditiously picked up ‘hello? Who are you and how do you know my address?’ asked Ivy ‘okay relax I’ll tell you everything. I am Natalie Alexandra. Do you know those genie that come into someone’s life and grant them some wish, well I kind of have the same power. ‘What.?’ said Ivy in astonish. ‘Look I know it may sound weird to you but we both are living in the same house but 20 years apart. In my timeline it is the year 1997 and let me guess in your timeline it is 2017?’ ‘You think I’ll believe you? I mean I don’t even know you’ Ivy said and was about to cut the call when ‘Your father, Am I right? Mr. Ethan he passes away in this house. Look Ivy life gives us many choices but it is up to you whether you choose the bad one or the right choices' That night Ivy couldn’t sleep thinking whether to trust Natalie or not. The next day Ivy went to the hospital to meet her mother. ‘Her health is critical, Tumors in the left side of the brain can result in motor deficits on the right side of the body. ‘But there need to be another way please doctor’ said Ivy with a little hope. ‘well there is a way, this brain tumor is only on the left.Chemotherapy tablets can be used to treat brain cancers but this is very expensive. It’s price starts at 12 lakh’ said the doctor. ‘I will arrange the money you just start her treatment doctor’ said Ivy and left in a hurry (What was she thinking? Why did she left in a hurry?) ‘Hello?’ said Natalie ‘Money, I need money make me successful. If you are telling the truth this is your chance to prove yourself. MAKE ME SUCCESSFUL!’ Ivy burst in tears asking Natalie for help. ‘Ivy of course stop bawling your eyes out’ Natalie hung up the call. Natalie only had one option for giving Ivy a successful life.' This is not right but I must do this for Ivy' That night Ivy was sitting in front of the walkie waiting for a call from Natalie. Suddenly it was complete darkness Ivy heard some weird sounds like dripping water vacant sound and then suddenly her room changed she went out her house changed completely she heard some familiar voices from downstairs a tear rolled down Ivy's face 'could it be.....my dad,my mom are they back?' Ivy rushed downstairs to see them but her parents weren't there instead there was a girl around the age of 19-20 'Good morning Ms.Marie seem like you woke up.I have arranged your schedule for today you have a meeting with the head today at 12 noon' said the girl 'What? Who are you?' asked Ivy 'I beg your pardon miss,I am Samantha Greenwhich your personal assistant.' said Samantha, Ivy said with a chuckle 'What do I need a personal assistant for.' 'because you have the most successful brand' Samantha said in confusion ' Yea of course I knew that' (Ivy didn't) Ivy had a blast for couple of weeks she went to meet her parents once but then got busy with work. She didn't even called Natalie for once. One day Ivy got a call from a hospital 'Hello? Am I speaking to Mr.Ivy Marie?' 'Yes' replied Ivy 'Ma'am I request you to come to the hospital as soon as possible' Ivy was worried and went to the hospital leaving her meeting in between. When Ivy reached the hospital the nurse took her to the doctor.'What's going on?Why am I here?' asked Ivy 'Miss Marie I am very remorseful to tell you this but your parents got into a terrible accident and we couldn't save them. We are extremely sorry' Ivy felt like she was shattered to pieces and burst into tears. She realized that she was so into the success in her life she forgot about her parents and friends Ivy felt guilty about her actions Ivy thought of calling Natalie but she was scared of something that even she didn't know about but she remembered the talks she had with Natalie and how she always said 'No matter what we both will be there for you.No matter what we won't hesitate to talk to each other' Ivy finally gathered up the courage to talk to Natalie. 'Hello? who is this?' 'Hey Natalie it's me,Ivy' Ivy said with an awkward chuckle 'OMG! Ivy its been so long how are you?' 'I am fine.Look Natalie I am extremely sorry that I haven't called you for 1-2 months I got so lost in my life I forgot to meet all important people in my life and it is weird that I am calling you after so long for help' before Ivy could finish Natalie said 'Ivy.. come on it is okay you know what i used to say "No matter what we both will be there for you.No matter what we won't hesitate to talk to each other" So tell me how can I help you?' Ivy started gave a warm chuckle and said 'I want my old life back' Natalie was confused 'But why? I thought you were having a great life' Ivy replied 'I was having my best life but as it says "no matter how high you are, There is loneliness at the top." I think that it is best that instead of running away from my past i should learn from it and make my future better'. 'You got some great motivation Ivy' 'I learned from the best' they both started laughing. Ivy got her old life back and started a small business and saved up enough money for her mother's treatment. Even though it was hard for her she worked hard and she even had great help from her friends and family The past might hurt but it is up to us whether we run from it or learn from it ~Navya
author: Navya Choudhary
illustrator: Maithili  Joshi; Navya Choudhary; Swathi Sambasivam

title: The Tortoiseshell Beetle
text: There’s a boy in school Who sits near the blackboard every day, Squinting at the chalk-words To get his spellings right. Rohith tries hard to fix himself With his small, blunt pencil, Which won’t stop inverting his letters. One monsoon day as he sits alone, Staring at the margins in his notebook, Uneasy to the noise within the school’s four walls, Sudha Ma’am calls him outside. With his small, chequered handkerchief She wipes away the dejected faces of other adults And takes him on a walk along the lake nearby. She shows him the waving trails of procession ants on the sand Moving up the bund where the water had risen. Looking for a new place to nest after the rains. They follow the ants’ paths Right until the dense, thorny cane bushes. Sudha Ma’am and Rohith watch the skittering frogs As they run on the water’s surface. When they walk close to them, the frogs plop into the tea-brown lake, Which grows lily pads for the frogs to rest on. Palm swifts make long ribbons with their flight, then settle among the palm fronds. Under the heart-shaped leaves of the morning-glory plants, Rohith finds strange black hairy specks Nibbling little paths on the leaves’ laminae. He shows them to Sudha Ma’am and asks who they are. She says, “No one would ever guess that, months later, these small, slowly crawling creatures... “Transform into tortoiseshell beetles. The only creatures that shine like golden star-glitter By this lakeside.” Rohith’s face brightens like the morning sun rising over the palmyras. He says, “Let’s go find the beetle.”
author: Yuvan aves

title: Rajiv tries Non-veg food
text: Rajiv was a 8 year old boy. His father was a politician so he didn't spend much time with him, or his mother because his mother was a housewife and had a lot of household duties. So one day Rajiv came back from school, after he kept his bag on the living room sofa, he began revising what he had learnt today. Today he learnt about how much harm you do to the animals when you hunt them down. So from that day onwards Rajiv didn't even touch Non-veg food and that's the reason why Rajiv doesn't eat Non-veg food anymore. After his parents finished their work and came back home. For dinner it was eggs, sausages and roti. Rajiv's mother served some eggs and sausages to his plate when everyone started praying for the food, Rajiv gave the egg and sausage to his dog Zoro, Zoro gulped it down by the time the prayer ended. Rajiv quickly smeared some egg yellow onto his face, his mother said Rajiv it's not nice eating between or before the prayer, I should not see this behavior tomorrow, Ok Rajiv. Ok ma replied Rajiv. Rajiv got scared that what should he do tomorrow, So then Rajiv called his grandmother to come over tomorrow and she said Ok. So then Rajiv stopped worrying and went to sleep. Rajiv woke up surprisingly early at 7:00, he usually only wakes up at 8:00 and his school begins at 9:00. Then he got up from his bed and got ready for school, he had 1 hour remaining so he started playing on his Ps5 for 1 whole hour. Then went to school for 6 hours. And then when he came back he hugged his grandma and then continued playing on his Ps5 until dinner time. Dinner time had finally struck it was the moment of truth. Dinner was Chicken, Rajiv's grandma turned out to be a vegetarian, But she said there is always a first time and they started praying, but this time Zoro was eating his food, So then Rajiv closed his eyes and slowly started eating and then realised a chicken's life was taken for me to eat this food so from that day onward Rajiv ate Non-veg.
author: Joshua Cherian
illustrator: Anjana Krishnamurthy; Joshua Cherian; Pratham Content Group; Rae  Zachariah; Sarah Bouwer; Soumya Menon; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: Zola's Day
text: Zola goes to school in the morning. She likes to go to school. She learns to read and write. Zola comes home from school in the afternoon. In the afternoon she has lunch. title: Full of Light
text: Shakthi darted through the schoolyard. She had great news for Amma! It was evening. The day slid behind the clouds. Night purpled the corners of the sky. Shakthi burst into her house. “Amma,” she yelled, “I won the art competition!” “Always so loud,” Amma said, wrinkling her nose. She was filling a brass lamp with oil. She shook her head. She sucked her teeth. She didn’t look up. In a quieter voice, Shakthi said, “Sorry. But I got a medal. See?” Amma turned to Shakthi. But she didn’t notice the award. She noticed Shakthi’s uniform. “Another pocket stain?” Amma asked, rolling her eyes. Turning back to the lamp, she muttered, “This child. Sure, she struggles with marks. But can’t she at least stay clean?” Then Amma sighed. The sigh howled through Shakthi like a cold wind. Shakthi dragged herself to her room. She changed her clothes. Her shoulders sagged. Her mouth felt dry. Amma always complained about how Shakthi never won anything. Today, she’d won a prize. Just as Amma wanted. But Amma wasn’t proud. She was disappointed. Again. On her way home, Shakthi had felt bright with joy. Now, she felt lightless as a shadow. Outside, Shakthi’s neighbour was making a kolam. Shakthi couldn’t tell what it was. If Shakthi made a kolam like that, Amma would tell her to stop making a mess. To stop wasting time. To stop being so careless and sloppy and useless. A kolam like that would make Shakthi feel terrible. But this girl was humming to herself. She was smiling. Doesn’t she know she’s not good enough? Shakthi thought. Darkness glided from Shakthi’s chest to her throat, and onto her tongue. “That kolam looks like bird poop,” Shakthi said. Surprised, the girl sat back on her heels. And studied the design. Then, she burst into laughter. Shakthi was confused. Why was this girl laughing? She was a disappointment. She was supposed to be ashamed. “It’s a peacock!” The girl said between giggles. “But you’re right. It looks like poop. Ocean-coloured poop. So, maybe from a mermaid?” Shakthi snickered. Some of the darkness fell away. “I’m Tejas,” the girl said. “Shakthi,” Shakthi said. “Can I help?” “Yes, please!” Tejas said. Shakthi smoothed the kolam with sure, steady fingers until the mess became a peacock. “Wow!” Tejas said. “Are you an artist?” Shrugging, Shakthi said, “Well… I won an art contest in school.” “That’s amazing!” Tejas squealed. “You’re amazing!” “ You’re amazing,” Shakthi said. “I was mean to you. But you’re being nice to me. Why weren’t you mean back?” “I have a trick,” Tejas said. “When people try to make me feel bad, I remind myself of all the reasons why I’m great.” “Like, I’m the best kozhukatta folder in my family. I have excellent handwriting. I’m fantastic at standing on one leg!” Tejas sprang up. She posed like a heron. Shakthi clapped. “It’s like each of my good parts is a lamp inside me,” Tejas said, her body straight and steady. “When I name them, they light up, one by one. Before long, I start to shine.” Shakthi glanced at the house. Amma was lighting the lamp. Her perfectly pleated sari shimmered. She looked smart, graceful, beautiful—everything that Shakthi was not. “What if I don’t have any good parts?” Shakthi asked. “Impossible!” Tejas said. “You’re an artist. You’re helpful. You’re a friend to animals.” “I am?” Shakthi asked. “You saved my peacock!” Tejas said. Shakthi laughed louder than she had in days. No one had ever told her any of this before. When Shakthi laughed, Amma’s head whipped around like a cyclone. Storm clouds blackened her forehead. Lightning flashed through her eyes. “Shakthi, is that you, bleating like a goat? And covered in kolam powder? Can’t you stay clean for five minutes? Go change. Again.” "Yes, Amma,” Shakthi said. To Tejas, she said, “I’d better go.” “Remember the trick,” Tejas said. Then she waved goodbye. Amma’s words stormed through Shakthi. They dragged the darkness closer and closer—but not close enough. This time, the darkness wouldn’t get in. Shakthi wouldn’t let it. “I’m an award-winning artist,” she said, pulling on clean clothes. "I am a champion at cutting straight lines." “I’m helpful. I’m creative. I’m funny. I’m kind.” Tejas was right! Inside Shakthi’s chest, lamp after lamp caught and blazed. Before long, her whole body glowed, cosy and bright. Shakthi opened her window. The warm wind smelled of camphor and jasmine. The stars winked and shimmered like a million tiny flames. Inside and outside, Shakthi’s world was full of light.
author: Mathangi  Subramanian

title: Haimati's Birthday
text: Haimat i, a girl living in Kolkata is going to Delhi for her birthday. She is very excited! She zoomed away on a flight two days before her birthday. She was going to enjoy this trip with her family! They toured around Delhi for a day. They went to Qutub Minar, Red fort, Jantar Mantar and a lot of other places... They ate the famous foods in Delhi, danced to the famous songs and tried to live the Delhi way! On the second day, Haimati asked her mum to play a game of chess. It was Haimati's birthday. "Mommy! Will you play chess with me?", she asked excitedly. Unusually, her mother said, "Sorry Beta! I have to go to the restroom! Ask daddy." Haimati was sad. Next, she went to her dad. "Daddy, will you please play ludo with me?", she asked. "Sorry dear! I have to take a bath! Ask your little brothers.", he replied. Haimati was sad again. Next, she went to her little brothers. "Ramu and Somu, will you play with me?", she asked desperately. "No didi! Don't interrupt our sword fight!", Ramu said. "Yeah!", agreed Somu. Haimati thought that her whole family acting weird. Why would they not play with her? She wondered. This was very unusual. She was definitely upset now. Haimati's father asked her to go fetch a bottle of water from the front desk. Haimati agreed and went down. She was still disappointed that her family forgot about her birthday. Haimati returned to her room with the bottle. The room was dark. Her whole family suddenly popped out. "Surprise!" They all yelled. "Happy birthday!" Haimati was happy beyond her dreams. She was very delighted that they did not forget her birthday. They spent the whole day laughing, playing the games she wanted, dancing and eating cake! THE END

title: Rohan And The Magnet
