title: The Bull Comes Home
text: Beneath August's warm gaze….. Bram’s hands hold a jackfruit leaf, folding and unfolding until… …. a creature comes to life. A leafy bull awakens. It locks eyes with the young boy, and they share a soft smile. “I’m home,” the bull thinks. The creature becomes Bram’s little friend. Floating in leaf boats during Bram's bath, it watches the clouds pass slowly by. And listens as Bram shares his dreams. The bull meets Bram’s friends. They tell their own tales using jackfruit leaves… Windmill blades dance in the wind, birds take flight in dreams and boats sail imaginary seas. Bram and his friends create and share joy, while the bull quietly watches.. As the days roll by, the children grow older. Laughter of the playgrounds fades away. The leafy friends start to disappear… one by one. The windmill quietly twirls away in October. Dreaming of distant skies, the birds fly off next. And then, the boat follows… By December, dust settles on the bull in the corner of Bram’s room. Hopeful, it waits, as Bram enters. He only picks up a cardigan and leaves again. The bull goes out to the jackfruit tree where it was born. It waits.. and waits.. but Bram doesn’t come. The bull grows tired, its eyes drooping. “I’m so sleepy….” it murmurs. And so it curls up under the tree and sleeps.. and sleeps.. Seasons change, and in its slumber, the bull becomes something new and fresh — a jackfruit leaf falling gently into waiting hands. A child gazes at the green leaf, tracing its delicate patterns. Her hands start to fold and unfold, following a secret map hidden in the leaf. Slowly, a familiar shape appears — the bull, born again. The child skips over to Atchu * Bram with the bull in hand. Bram's eyes twinkle with recognition. He traces the familiar grooves and patterns with his fingertips. * Atchu: A Garo word for grandfather. The bull locks eyes with the old man, who was once a young boy. Delighted, it lets out a heartfelt sigh and says, “I’m home." Activity Hey, there! Ready to create something magical? Let's make our own special bull using a jackfruit leaf. Just follow the steps given below. 1. Take a jackfruit leaf. 2. Make cuts along the first row of veins on each side to make the horns. Then, cut off the end leaving the middle vein intact for the tail. 3. Fold and tuck each side under the horns. 4. Flip the leaf to the other side and gently fold one side on top of the other. 5. Pin the two folded sides with a small twig or toothpick. 6. Make a small hole below the horns and insert the stalk in it. Ta-da! Your leafy bull is complete. About 'The Bull' 'The Bull,' is the signature piece of designer Arak M Sangma, who has illustrated this book. The creature holds a special place in his memories. He fondly recalls a happy time from his youth, crafting a bull with his friends under a jackfruit tree. Through his art, he aims to bring back that joyful feeling, honoring the special moments spent with friends in the lap of nature. Crafting bulls and other shapes from jackfruit leaves is a cherished part of childhood for many who grew up in the Garo Hills. It's a core memory, a thread woven through people's past, connecting them to the joy and laughter of those early days. The artist has infused personal touches from his own memories into the illustrations — wisps of smoke connecting the pages, a toy cart, and a shelter made of banana leaves.
author: Eleanor  Sangma

title: The Unbroken Promise to the Elephants
text: Aditi was a ten-year old girl, with a lively spirit. She lived with her parents in a remote village in Tamil Nadu. The village was called Yanaigal Medu Malai, meaning, the steep hill of the elephants. There were more than a hundred elephants living in the dense forests surrounding the village. The village was situated on the edge of a vast forest, on top of a hill. The place was known for rainfall almost throughout the year. It was always moist and cool. Aditi grew up seeing elephants whenever she went into the forest with her parents. Her parents were native healers. They often went into the forest to pick up small plants, leaves, flowers, seeds and roots for preparing native medicines. The family also practiced agriculture in a small piece of land near their home. Being a hilly region, their home was built on a big piece of rock for stability. Aditi has always been in awe of the huge elephants. She had often seen them from a distance in their natural habitat. Big tuskers, young elephants, cute calves - she had seen them all. Whenever she saw them, she would immediately become silent. She would then hide behind a big bush or a tree, and watch the elephants eat or walk along with family, sometimes for hours together. When Aditi became ten years old, her parents took her into the forest through a different route. Along the way, they told her that she was soon going to see a beautiful sight. Aditi’s interest was piqued, but she did not show it. They went a bit deeper into the forest. Since it had rained the earlier night, it was a bit slippery. However, all the three of them were adept at managing themselves. Soon, they came to a curve, and after that the path began to go up. Holding on to the trees on sides, Aditi and her parents carefully climbed the path, till they reached the top of a small hillock. Aditi wanted to climb to the top of the hillock first, but it was fairly steep. Her parents climbed first, and pulled Aditi up. Once on the top, the trio softly pushed the shrubs aside, to see a deep, dense valley below. At the centre of this valley, was a clearing. A small stream of river flowed effortlessly. The glistening water could be seen from above. While this sight was definitely worth remembering for its natural beauty, what made Aditi gasp with wonder was the delightful sight of magnificent elephants drinking water, young elephants playing inside the stream, babies moving around the place restlessly, and big tuskers staying guard by looking around. The clearing was the elephants’ most loved place, Aditi thought. How come she never heard of this? Her parents said in an hushed tone that one of the most guarded secrets of the inhabitants of the Yanaigal Medu Malai was that no outsider should be able to find out the place where the elephants rested and drank water. This was for two big reasons. One is that if the elephants’ regular visiting places were not encroached upon, they will never harm people. Elephants and the inhabitants have mutual respect for each other, and this was a promise that has remained unbroken for many years. This is the only reason why elephants have never attacked the village. The invisible boundaries were well marked years ago. None of the parties has ever crossed those boundaries. The second reason for the secret is that outsiders were not bound by the promise to respect elephants and may very casually leak this information. This can cause havoc to the herds of elephants and to the villagers. There was also the possibility of elephants being hunted down. The whole place will become uninhabitable for the elephants and the villagers. Aditi shook her head in understanding. She also came to appreciate the fact that all the villagers in the Yanaigal Medu Malai were respectful of the elephants. Never once did any of them speak about the dangers of living so close to the big animals. Never once did the villagers attempt to cross the paths of the elephants. Aditi realized then why her parents and her neighbours never expanded their land for cultivating more crops, why they never went ‘sight-seeing’, why they never used loud musical instruments during celebrations, why they never burst crackers during festivals, why they never believed in animal sacrifice, and why they never entertained outsiders. As they kept watching the elephants down below, Aditi knew that something was going on in the minds of her parents. She was sitting on one corner, while her parents were standing behind her. They were holding here tight. Aditi noticed that her parents were lost in their thoughts and shook both of them gently. At that moment, both her mother and father exchanged a glance with each other. They were thinking if the next generation will safeguard this secret. Will Aditi and her friends in the village understand the importance of peaceful co-habitation with the elephants? Will the next generation keep the promise unbroken? Time will tell!

title: The scaly creature -- A mosy Nair adventure
text: Mosy, a male Chinese Chow Chow, was a very furry pup. He was on an exciting adventure that began with a train journey, accompanied by a rather nice gentleman, named Mohan. They had left the cold wintery regions of Sikkim and were headed for the warm, tropical climates of God’s own country, Kerala, where Mosy was to join his new family, The Nairs. Col. Sabari Nair, a war veteran, was known among his peers as a fierce warrior and a renowned Veterinarian. The colonel and Mosy settled in Punalur, a district of Kerala, where this story is based. Mosy, was a rather friendly fellow, who was always ready to make friends. He loved the family cat, Cookie, who was afraid of Mosy, at first, but grew fond of him as well, over time. At first, the dog’s neck was so furry that the local people called him “Simham-Kutti-Patti”, which meant, ‘Lion Cub Dog”, in Malayalam. As his body got used to the climate, after a month or two his body gradually shed most of the fur. "Simham-Kutti-Patti As a puppy, Mosy was always curious about everything and everyone around him! Once, he was playing in the backyard when he saw a strange looking creature. It had no legs, its tongue flickered in and out, it was very long and had scales on its body! Mosy thought, “Hey! What a strange looking creature! It has no legs! I have four! Its tongue keeps coming out! I only do that when I am feeling hot. Is it feeling hot too? Why doesn’t it have fur on its body? I am covered in fur!’’ Yes, it was a King Cobra, but Mosy did not know what it was. However, something about it did not smell right! At the same time, he was also curios about the snake, so he went towards it. The Cobra started to attack him! When the snake was about to bite, Mosy jumped clear and slapped it on its head. He kept doing that till the Colonel‘s mother, came. Mosy was now done with the snake. Today, was not so much fun for the snake, because he was beat up by a puppy! However, the day was quite interesting for curious little Mosy! The colonel’s mother was very glad that he was there to protect the family. She said “Mosy, thank you for keeping our family safe, I love you!’’ Mosy grinned! He loved the words “Thank you ’ since he loved helping "Mosy, Thank you for keeping our family safe!" Mosy had many more adventures in his lifetime. Once, while at a beach, Mosy even helped a lost little girl find her family. He was a real hero! He also became best friends with a German Shepherd named, Jasper. Mosy and Jasper would very often team up and tease the mice in the yard Where is that Mosy? we still have a few more adventures! One would man the entrance of their hole while the other would locate the escape hatch and be ready to scare any mice who tried to use it. Oh yes, Mosy led a very interesting, adventurous and most of all, very happy life. Next time, I will tell you about the Mice’s great plan. See you next time!

title: The Living Book
text: "Hey, where are we going?" asked Abhay. "Let's head to the newly opened library in the nearby town," added Riya. Abhay, Riya, and Rohan, three friends from the small town of Criewige, decided to visit the newly opened library. Inside the peculiar bookshop named "Mystic Pages," they discovered an old book titled "Ghosts' Unseen Stories." As they opened the book, a soft shimmer surrounded them, and suddenly, they found themselves in a place where shadows whispered stories of long-forgotten spirits, a world they had never seen before. "Where are we going?" asked Rohan. "I think we have forgotten our way. There's a house that way; let's ask for directions," suggested Riya. While moving, they stumbled upon an old palace. The haunted palace sat surrounded by ancient trees, looking sad and abandoned, with broken pillars and vines covering the worn-out walls. The windows resembled empty eyes, indicating the passage of time. Rohan and Riya were scared, reluctant to enter, but Abhay displayed courage, leading Riya and Rohan inside. As they opened the door, the street lights went out, the wind started blowing at a high speed, as if ghosts were approaching to haunt them. The doors creaked, carrying the whispers of ghosts. Riya, terrified, ran inside without looking. Rohan and Abhay called out to her, but she didn't respond. Concerned, they entered to find her. Moving forward, they encountered numerous ghosts, all attempting to frighten them. Finally, they entered a small room filled with toys, where they found Riya fainted on the floor. As they rushed to her, a witch appeared, attempting to harm them. Despite their pleas, she refused to let Riya go. Rohan addressed her as a mother and explained that Riya was their friend; they couldn't leave her alone. The ghost, pleased by their politeness, began reciting her story. "Many decades ago, I gave birth to a baby girl. My husband didn't want a girl, so one night he decided to kill me and our baby. When I learned of his plan, I took my baby and started running, but he shot both of us with his gun. The whole room was filled with blood. Since then, I've sought revenge by killing anyone passing through here, hoping to encounter a girl who can reunite me with my baby. Riya is the only one who can fulfill this prophecy. When we died, my husband cursed me that I would only get my child if a little girl came to this haunted palace. I must kill that girl to reunite my child's soul with her." Rohan and Abhay expressed sadness, arguing that she couldn't harm someone else's child, as it would also make Riya's mother sad. The ghost agreed, revealing an almost impossible alternative. Riya suddenly woke up and joined her friends. Rohan inquired about the alternative, and the ghost explained that if they could find a golden key in the palace and place it here, it could help her find her baby. The key would grant her the powers needed for the reunion. She had been finding that key since decades but was unable to find-so it seemed impossible. Though it seemed impossible, the friends embarked on a quest to find the key. In the kitchen, they discovered a map outlining a specific route to the key's location. This journey took about two days, and upon reaching the destination, they had to sacrifice the most precious thing they possessed to obtain the key. Abhay initially offered his bag filled with chips, but the key wasn't there. Riya gave her earrings, and Rohan sacrificed his watch, yet the key remained elusive. Finally, Abhay recalled the most precious thing, a bracelet given to him by his grandmother when he won his first race in school. As he offered the bracelet, the golden key emerged. They rushed back to the haunted house and handed the key to the ghost. A thunderstorm ensued, magical powers struck her, and with the help of her newfound abilities, she summoned her baby's soul. A baby appeared in her lap, and the clouds vanished. A wave of motherhood engulfed them all, and they found themselves back in the bookshop, sitting in chairs where they had started. The book closed, and they realized they had experienced the story within the book. It was an adventurous memory for all of them. The bond between Abhay, Riya, and Rohan had deepened, The bond between Abhay, Riya, and Rohan had deepened, and t hey pledged to keep the magical book and its story a secret. When Rohan checked his hand, he found the bracelet safely in his hands. The extraordinary adventure became a cherished secret, a testament to the enduring magic found in the simple act of friendship. title: The Root Bridge
text: I was born a Morning Root. The first thing that I heard was chirping. Later I found out this was the sound of the birds singing the arrival of the morning sun.” “Some days later, I felt a cold sensation for the first time. Later I found out that these tiny droplets of water are called rain. I felt my tiny being getting stronger every time the rain would touch me. The rain always made me feel at ease.” “One day, I heard sounds that I had never heard before and saw some unusual figures that I had never seen before.” ‘ Why do we build bridges, Pa? ’ I heard the smaller figure ask. ‘ Watch carefully and learn, dear Pynn. We do this so that this root bridge can help us cross the river to help us get to our paddy field safely, ’ came the response. ” “ ‘ Why do we build bridges, Pa? ’ I heard the smaller figure ask. ‘ Watch carefully and learn, dear Pynn. We do this so that this root bridge can help us cross the river to help us get to our paddy field safely, ’ came the response. ” “The older roots told me that these creatures are called human beings and they help shape young shoots like me to become a part of the mighty root bridge! Ever since that day, I longed to be a part of the root bridge as I also wanted to be helpful.” “The older roots told me that these creatures are called human beings and they help shape young shoots like me to become a part of the mighty root bridge! Ever since that day, I longed to be a part of the root bridge as I also wanted to be helpful.” “Many summers and winters came and left. I grew steadily as I watched my friends start their journey of being a part of the mighty root bridge.” “Many summers and winters came and left. I grew steadily as I watched my friends start their journey of being a part of the mighty root bridge.” “I waited patiently each year to be picked, but Pynn’s father would say, ‘this one is not strong enough yet.’ I felt embarrassed that while my friends made it, I still was not good enough to join the mighty root bridge” “I waited patiently each year to be picked, but Pynn’s father would say, ‘this one is not strong enough yet.’ I felt embarrassed that while my friends made it, I still was not good enough to join the Mighty Root Bridge” “One day, there was a huge storm. It was by far the strongest storm I had witnessed. The root bridge took a lot of damage. Some of my friends came loose and others drifted away because of the wind and the rain.” “I was heartbroken. The always calm mother nature, whom I loved dearly, had destroyed the bridge and taken away my friends.” “The next day after the storm had passed, I heard Pynn making her way towards us with her father, carrying bamboo. I watched as they started repairing the bridge.” “The next day after the storm had passed, I heard Pynn making her way towards us with her father, carrying bamboo sticks. I watched as they started repairing the bridge.” “As Pynn and her father repaired the bridge, Pynn came close to me and held me up to her father and said, ‘Look, Pa! This root withstood the strong storm, it is a strong root in my eyes.’” Smiling, I heard the father reply, "You are right. I think it is time for it to join the bridge." “As Pynn and her father repaired the bridge, Pynn came close to me and held me up to her father and said, ‘Look, Pa! This root withstood the strong storm, it is a strong root in my eyes.’ Smiling, I heard the father reply, ‘ You are right. I think it is time for it to join the bridge. ” “I had never had anyone tell me that I was a strong root, ever! Despite the storm, Pynn’s words that day made me feel warm and accepted.” “I had never had anyone tell me that I was a strong root, ever! Despite the storm, Pynn’s words that day made me feel warm and accepted.” “I was finally a part of the mighty root bridge!” “I was finally a part of the Mighty Root Bridge!” “As I look back on the decades that have passed by, I am a strong root, a part of the Root Bridge, because Pynn saw the strength in me that day. I help hundreds of people each day to cross the river, and serve a purpose.” “Today, Pynn visits with her child and grandchild to repair this bridge and help hopeful shoots like I once was, become a part of the mighty Root Bridge.” “Today, Pynn visits with her child and grandchild to repair this bridge and help hopeful shoots like I once was, become a part of the Mighty Root Bridge.” Living Root Bridges Pynursula, Meghalaya, India Photographs taken by The Forgotten Folklore Project Team, Pynursula, Meghalaya. title: My Sister and Me
text: Anu is my sister. She helps me do my homework. Some days I do not like to do my homework. But Anu makes me sit down. Anu has a big cycle. She teaches me to ride it. When I fall she comes running to help me. Anu also fights with me. Then I get angry. But after some time she is sorry. That is why I love my sister Anu.
author: Kanchan Bannerjee

title: Exam Fever
text: Dadi made a soothing drink, She sang a calming melody. But the exam monster Just would not let us be. Papa laid a wet cloth On Ma’s burning brow. He combed her hair, Fed her khichdi somehow, Because… While notes and studies filled the days, Fast and frantic, forever more, Ma’s fever Did soar and roar! Bhaiya read chapters From a textbook, out loud. He talked about standing first, “Ma, won’t that make you proud?” “Don’t be scared,” I said, Prancing like a clown. Telling funny tales till A smile replaced Ma’s frown. Because… No one can visit— Neither neighbour nor friend, When Ma’s fever Burns without end. Finally the exam day came along. Ma woke up well and strong No more fever, no more worry. And you know what? My Ma got her BA degree!
author: Shabnam  Minwalla

title: Yellow
text: "Lin Lin!" "Yes Bei?" "Linlin, Bei is leaving. You be a good girl and listen to your Beipun, okay?" "Okay, Bei. Bye bye!" "Why are Bei’s hands so yellow but not mine?" "Heh…heh…heh…" "Let’s see where Bei is headed and find out why!" "There she is!" "Whoa! What is this?" "Hey there, little girl! Did I just hear a question?" "Who are you?" "I am the one and only Ma Lakadong – the only turmeric with a curcumin content of 6–12% in the whole world! Have you heard of me?" "No!" "No? Wha-wha-what about the story of the magic spice and cows then?" "Magic…?" "Yes! Let me tell you." "A long time ago, during your ancestors' time, a herd of cows were attacked by tigers!" "Your ancestors, looking for medical herbs, found me in the forest with my peculiar smell…" "…they took me and applied my magic yellow paste on the injured cows." "And of course, I healed them! That’s how I was discovered! Didn’t I tell ya? I’m magic!" "Whoaa. Magic! Ma Lakadong, are you also the reason why my Bei’s hands are yellow?" "Oh yes, I do leave a beautiful shade of yellow on the people I fancy." "I want my hands to be yellow like Bei!" "Leave it to me!" "Linlin! What are you doing here?" "Bei! I was just talking to Ma Lakadong…Huh?" Ma Lakadong was nowhere to be seen. …but when she looked down to her hands, she was surprised to see that her hands were a beautiful yellow… …just like her Bei’s! Take half a spoon of turmeric in a bowl Add two spoons of water and stir Apply the paste on your palm. Make sure your hands are painted yellow like Linlin and her mother! Lay your hand on a color paper of your choice. Press down for a minute. Activity Let's meet Ma Lakadong! Wait for it to dry Draw eyes for Ma Lakadong Cut along the shape And you have your very own Ma Lakadong! ● Lakadong Turmeric is renowned for its exceptionally high curcumin content, ranging from 6-12%, making it one of the varieties with the highest curcumin levels. It has a darker shade and is grown organically. ● On December 2023, Lakadong Turmeric received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, signifying its unique qualities and origin in the West Jaintia Hills district of Meghalaya, India. ● Around 14,000 farmers, in West Jaintia Hills, are currently engaged in cultivating Lakadong turmeric on 1,753 hectares of land. ● It was traditionally used for its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects, and still has high medicinal values from treating cancer to enhancing cognitive health. ● It is used in local cuisines for its distinctive flavor and aroma. ● It is used extensively in cosmetics as well. Facts about Lakadong Turmeric ﻿* *Information extracted from Mission Lakadong 2018–2023, Directorate of Horticulture, Department of Agriculture, Government of Meghalaya.
author: Alemchila Tzudir

title: How old is Dadu's house?
text: There was once a boy named Avi. One day, he went to his grandfather's house. He used to visit it every two to three months. Now it was time to go there again. He went with his parents on a plane. When he reached the house, he saw his grandfather. He was always happy to meet him. He had lunch and then rested. When he woke up, he asked his grandfather, "How old is this house". His grandfather said that his father became the head of a construction business in the year 1920. He used to build a lot of thing. "Do you want to know what he built? He built the Umaid Palace (1928-43), The gang canal (1933-36) and a lot more. He left a old paper stating the age of the house. Where is it? Asked Avi. Grandfather brought it a said "It states that it was built in the year 1937, alongside the neighbor house". Avi was very happy. Avi stayed with the grandparents for 6 days, when he found more about his family and their origins. He had a lot of fun. He went home happy.

title: Happy to Go to School
text: Here is our cute 4 years old Golu. He likes to play all the time. Mom and dad are thinking to send him to school now. Golu is also excited for new school. But he is afraid too. How does a school look? What is a book and note-book? Golu loves to play with his mom. Golu is thinking" who will play with me at school?" Oh!! I will get bore there..... Mumma.... you please come with me in school. Golu's mom smiles at this. Today is the first day of Golu's school. He is feeling happy as well as nervous. Mom and dad took him to the school. There was Ms. Geeta, Golu's class teacher waiting for him at the gate. As soon as mumma gave Golu's hand in Ms. Geeta's hand, he started crying with fear. The teacher took him to the classroom. Golu was surprised to see so many children in the classroom. Few were playing in a corner. Few were eating. They all were looking happy with each other. Ms. Geeta introduced Golu to all the children. All were happy to meet Golu. And so was Golu to meet so many friends. What do children do at school? How did you feel on your first day to school? How can we make friends at school? Did you cry when your parents left you at school on the ﻿ first day?

title: Bei Rym-aw
text: “What are we going to wear to the festival, Waka?” Kiru asks. “ I will be wearing my muka and thoh saru!” says Waka. “I also want one! I also want one!” Kiru jumps up in excitement. Waka laughs and says, “Oh, Kiru! I’m so sorry but they don’t make attires for squirrels.” Kiru looks up at Waka with a pout. “But I want to look nice for my first Chad Sukra.” “What if I make you a matching turban? It'll suit you perfectly!” The day of the festival, Waka and Kiru excitedly run up to the festival grounds, all decked out in their new attires. Kiru is bouncing around, trying to take all the festivities in. “Wow, there is just sooo much to see!” Kiru cries out. “That man is called a Daloi. He is praying for a bountiful harvest” explains Waka to a curious little Kiru. “Is that why we celebrate this festival?” Kiru asks. “Yes, the Chad Sukra is a festival where we pray for good crops and blessings from Bei Rym-aw!" “Is it celebrated only by the Pnar people?” Kiru asks. “Yes, Kiru. The Chad Sukra is a special bond between the Pnar people and Bei Rym-aw.” As they move further, Waka and Kiru come across people dancing with plates. Kiru's eyebrows furrow in confusion. "So, why do they use plates during their dance?" Waka chuckles, "The plates are part of Ka Chad Pliang dance, showing how we all come together as one.” Strolling through the bustling grounds, they spot a lone figure in the corner. “Waka, do you see that Kong?” Kiru asks. “Yes, Kiru. I wonder why she looks so sad? Let's go and see if she needs any help.” The two slowly approach the lonely figure wrapped in tattered rags. “Hi, Kong. Are you looking for someone?” “Hello, little ones. I didn’t realise people could still see me.” “What do you mean?” The old lady sighs softly before revealing her disfigured body. “I am not just a Kong. I am who they call Bei Rym-aw herself. I’ve watched over the land and its creatures for long, but I’ve grown tired now.” “My beloved body does not feel like my own anymore,” says Bei Rym-aw to a bewildered Waka and Kiru. “But…. but, you are worshipped every year,” Waka mumbles sadly. Letting out a sigh, Bei Rym-aw says, “Humans worship me, but they have also failed me. The air, the land, and the water are all polluted, making me weak.” Their shoes go crunch-crunch on plastic wrappers scattered on the ground, making Waka frown. After the encounter with Bei Rym-aw, Waka and Kiru stroll through the festival feeling a bit sad. She suddenly stops walking. “Kiru, do you want to do some cleanup today?” Kiru chuckles, “Like the nature cleanup crew?” “Exactly! And you're my trusty sidekick.” Kiru strikes a pose. “The Super Squirrel Cleaner-upper, reporting for duty!” Waka giggles and they start cleaning up the ground. Holding up a shiny wrapper, Kiru says, “Waka, look what I found! So shiny and crinkly, it's like squirrel treasure!” Waka smiles. “It might look cool, but it's not good for Bei Rym-aw. We can put it in one khoh with the other dry waste.” “And what about the banana peel?” “Ah, this will go in the khoh for wet waste.” Kiru nods and says, “Aye! Aye! Captain!” After cleaning up for a while, they decide to take a break. “Look at that, Waka. Our ground looks so much better already.” Waka smiles warmly. “It sure does, Kiru.” “Do you think this will help Bei Rym-aw feel a little better?” Activity Join the nature cleanup crew! Find things like wrappers and plastic bags and collect them in one basket/bag. Then, look for things like food scraps, fruit peels and put them in another basket/bag, just like Waka and Kiru did.
author: Mayanka Chyrmang

title: The Rabbit and Tortoise
text: Once upon a time, there lived a tortoise in the jungle who lived life on his own terms. He was calm, polite and non-interfering. In the same town there lived a rabbit who loved to talk about the many prizes he had won for always standing first in a race. One day he came to the tortoise and said, “Why don’t you learn to walk fast?” If you do that, we can have a race someday.” The Tortoise only smiled at him and moved on. The Hare was in a bad mood. Every day, he would go to the Tortoise at the same place and make the same remarks. One day When the hare challenged him again, the tortoise replied, “Okay, I accept the challenge.” He looked around and saw the other animals in the forest clapping and cheering him on. After a few days the race started! The whole forest stopped to see the result of this great challenge. When the race started, the hare overtook the tortoise in no time. His speed was remarkably fast, which required him to cover a considerable distance on the track. When he looked back and saw how far he had left the tortoise, the hare decided to stop running and rest for a while. He lay down under a huge banyan tree on one side of the track. The enchanting shade of the leaves lulled him into a deep sleep. Meanwhile, the tortoise ran at its slow pace without giving up and stopping. As time passed, he slowly caught hold of the rabbit who was still sleeping. The tortoise passed by him and continued towards the victory line. Slowly but surely, the tortoise reaches the finish line and wins the race. The whole city started clapping for the turtle. The loud cheering woke the rabbit from his deep sleep. He woke up, he did not understand anything about what had happened. He rubbed his eyes and thought to himself, “God, the tortoise must be still struggling.” The rabbit got up and ran towards the victory post. When he reached there he saw, to his surprise, the tortoise wearing the crown of victory and all the other animals congratulating him. The tortoise saw the hare from afar and smiled at him. The rabbit sat down, regretting his actions that caused him to lose the race against the slowest animal in the forest. Moral story:- When you work hard and with passion, you can achieve your goal. The person who is slow and steady wins the race.
author: Ayaan Rashid
illustrator: Arayana nalwa; Kishor Joshi; Padmanabh; Sri Snigdha Akella

title: Dare to Dream: Embracing Passion and Potential
text: Chapter 1: Nikitas' Resolve "Nikitas didn't let the tough times hold him back. He was determined to get that school clock up and running," Uncle Muzungu recalls. "Even when funds were scarce, he kept pushing forward with his plans. That's the kind of determination we need more of." Chapter 2: A Different Path "I wasn't a failure just because I didn't make it to university on my first try," Uncle Muzungu reflects. "The system failed me, but I found my own way. Makerere University taught me that there's more to success than just passing exams." Chapter 3: Rethinking Success "I told the youth group, 'Grades don't matter if you can't apply what you've learned,'" Uncle Muzungu shares. "We need to focus on skills and creativity, not just memorization." Chapter 4: The Art of Opportunity "Joachim and Necta showed me the power of art and creativity," Uncle Muzungu says with a smile. "Imagine an economist who's also a dancer! That's where the real opportunities lie." Chapter 5: Influencing Change "Persuasion and advocacy are key," Uncle Muzungu explains. "When we needed funding for the office in Gayaza, it was all about convincing people to support our cause." Chapter 6: Seizing the Moment "My time with SPW- Students Partnership Worldwide, opened my eyes to new possibilities," Uncle Muzungu shares. "Volunteering showed me the importance of leadership and activism in making a difference." Chapter 7: Nurturing Tomorrow's Leaders "We need to give our children the chance to explore their passions," Uncle Muzungu insists. "It's not just about education; it's about empowering them to pursue their dreams." Chapter 8: The Heartbeat of Change Nikita stood tall amidst the crowd, his eyes gleaming with determination. "I refuse to let obstacles hinder my dreams," he declared, his voice echoing with conviction. "We have the power to shape our future, to redefine success on our own terms." Chapter 9: Finding Purpose Uncle Muzungu leaned in, his gaze intent as he addressed the gathered audience. "Education is not just about acquiring knowledge; it's about discovering our purpose," he proclaimed. "Let us guide our youth towards their passions, towards a future where they can thrive." Chapter 10: Breaking Barriers "I want to see barriers shattered, stereotypes challenged," Nikita declared, his passion igniting a fire within the hearts of those around him. "Let's embrace diversity, let's celebrate individuality. That's where true innovation lies." Chapter 11: A Symphony of Voices Uncle Muzungu raised his hands, gesturing towards the vibrant tapestry of talents before him. "Imagine a world where every voice is heard, every talent cherished," he mused. "Together, we can create a symphony of change, where each note contributes to a brighter tomorrow." Chapter 12: Empowering Futures "We are the architects of our destiny," Nikita proclaimed, his voice resolute. "Let us empower our youth to dream boldly, to chase their passions without fear. For it is in their hands that the future truly lies." Chapter 13: A Legacy of Hope As the sun dipped below the horizon, casting a golden glow upon the horizon, Uncle Muzungu smiled, his heart brimming with hope. "Our journey may be challenging, but it is also filled with endless possibilities," he whispered. "Together, let us forge a legacy of hope, one that inspires generations to come." Epilogue: The Journey Continues With each step forward, Nikita and Uncle Muzungu embraced the unknown, their spirits buoyed by the promise of tomorrow. For in their hearts, they knew that the greatest adventure was yet to come. A Call to Action "Let's dare to dream and support each other along the way," Uncle Muzungu concludes. "Together, we can create a world where everyone has the opportunity to shine." Through their shared experiences and unwavering resolve, they had discovered the true essence of life: to dream, to inspire, and to never lose sight of the boundless potential that lay within each and every one of us. And as they journeyed into the future, hand in hand, they carried with them the belief that anything was possible – as long as they dared to dream.
author: Gulere Wambi

title: Mai Jingjing
text: Jingjing' Mai Jingjing is a fun game played by children in the Garo Hills. They pinch their left hand with their right hand and say “mai jingjing, mai jingjing,” mimicking the flight of cicadas. They sing “ambi mikki” and “atchu mikki” and playfully tease each other. This rhyme, which has been reimagined and extended upon by the author, paints a picture of joy, keeping alive the memories of childhood for those who grew up in the Garo Hills.
author: Eleanor  Sangma

title: Krishna's Hand Writing
text: Krishna is a seven-year-old school going boy. He is studying in Grade 2. Krishna is teacher's favourite student because he is always attentive in the class. The only problem is Krishna's poor handwriting. It's hard to understand what he writes in his notebook. Krishna's class teacher Ms.Sanjana really wanted to improve his handwriting. She thought a plan. The next day, when Krishna came to school, Ms. Sanjana gave him a pen. Ms. Sanjana told him that it is a magical pen, and he has to write two pages every day with this pen in the evening. Krishna was very happy and promised his teacher to do the same. After ten days, Krishna happily enters the classroom. Looking forward to showing Ms. Sanjana his lovely handwriting. He is very excited. Ms. Sanjana is quite happy to see Krishna's notebook with beautiful handwriting. She said that practice makes a man perfect. Do you think that Ms. Sanjana gave Krishna a magical pen? How did Krishna's handwriting improve? Do you want to try the same magical pen from your class teacher?
author: Sanjana Kashyap

title: The proud peacock
text: He looked at the peacock and said, "People are looking for you to see the beauty of your dancing feathers". "But look at the cuckoo, how beautifully she sings." The cuckoo goes to the place of people in the morning and entertains them by singing with its sweet voice. " It goes back to its nest in the evening." Thats said the monkey and laughed. On hearing this, the peacock went to the place where the people were and screamed hoarsely. Hearing the voice, the people beat the peacock and chased it to the grove.

title: Let's restore nature
text: This year my mother and I had gone to my grandmother's village for the Diwali festival. My grandmother's village was a beautiful village. When my mother was young, she told me that the place was very beautiful and that the trees, fields and gardens were beautiful and green. Here is a story about my experience in that town. The day after Diwali, my mother, my uncle and I went on a tour of the village. Then my uncle pointed to me and said that this is our village tank. The whole tank was rubbish. The tank had not been desilted and no one was using it. When my mother was younger, your uncle and I used to bathe in this pond and play. It was also an excellent source of water for the villagers. But now, in this situation, it is painful to see the tank. I asked my uncle, why is this tank like this? I asked. He said he was in such a state of limbo with no one to take care of the tank. I had an idea, why don't we desilt this tank and protect it? I asked. It's not easy, but what can we do about it? Uncle asked. I said that if we are like that, then we and the people of this village. I told my uncle that I wanted to make the villagers aware and understand. We spoke to the people of the village that evening. I explained to the villagers about the effects of dumping garbage in the tank, such as land pollution and water pollution. All the people of the village agreed to get involved in this work. The next morning, the villagers joined us in cleaning the tank. I also explained how to conserve groundwater and control air pollution by planting and maintaining trees and plants. Google Story-A-Thon Story-a-thon was an online contest launched on 8th September 2020, International Literacy Day, by Google, for little authors from 5 - 11 years to explore their creative writing skills and share their own original stories. From the over 10000+ entries received, 11 stories were shortlisted by the judges. This is one of the winning stories. You can read many more engaging and fun stories on the Read Along app.
author: sai s

title: The Essence of Geeta
text: Sudhir Patwardhan Harshita was feeling sad from quite few weeks as she recently lost her grandmother. She and her granny spend alot of time together playing and reading books. Her granny used to read her stories and tell her all about life and her experiences. She was missing those stories and her talks. She was feeling sad, depressed and lonely. She went to find solace in her mother. "Mommy", she said to her mother Geeta " How are you able to cope up with loss of granny? " Geeta calmly replied, "I read a book, GITA, your granny left for us, that helped me overcome the grief and understand the mysteries of life in a much simpler manner. I will try to explain it to you. Gita says, " Everything that happened is okay ". Try and understand, your grandmother lived her life to the fullest, had a happy and wholesome time with her daughter and granddaughter. Everything that happened is okay since she was in no pain or misery. "What's happening now will be okay...", whatever emotions you are going through now is expected and soon you will be okay. Don't run from this emotion, accept it, embrace it and live it. This will help you move on... What's happening now will be okay It continues, " And what will happen in the future will be okay too. " In future, she will be our guide and mentor for every important event in our life, we will always cherish her in our hearts and our memories. Gita asks you, " What have you parted with that makes you cry? " If you've lost something, don't be sad since everyone which comes has to go. T his body is not forever but the soul continues its journey with the karma earned in that lifetime for which they will be remembered. Gita frees us from bonding by saying Nothing belongs to us, everything is borrowed. " What did we bring with us that we have lost? What did we create which is now destroyed? " Just like the toys you borrow from friends, everything taken must be given back. Gita makes you realize that whatever you call yours today, it belonged to someone else yesterday and tomorrow will belong to someone else. It teaches you to have no attachments or pride towards the worldly possessions you have acquired or gained in this life. Gita teaches us to live our life keeping in mind that " Change is the Law of the Universe, ". Harshita then hugged her mum and wiped the tears off her face. Death is an unfortunate part of life which we all have to face someday. But its acceptance helps us in coping with their loss of dear ones and understand the true meaning of life. This dedicated to my beloved mother whom I recently lost. Her loss made me realize how the loss of a family member can make you whole life turn upside down. In order for us to live life to its fullest, we should not ignore the one constant part of life, Death, we all will meet once. Gita verses has helped me in coping with the loss. I have tried my best to summarize it for others who might find solace in it too.

title: Adventurous Tomato
text: She jumped into the sink... I mean into her space basin. She thinks she is an alien from outside planet Earth. The adventurous Tomato set off after boarding their spaceship, until they arrived on a wonderful planet full of various colorful creatures. She turned to them one by one. The person with the fit, Orange body is the Carrot. as for the one with the long neck, it is celery. As for the lettuce and cabbage, they walked proudly with their bright leaves. There were a lot of other friends. I wonder what was the name of this planet? Of course, it's the planet of vegetables. The Tomato thought and said: “Let us be useful, my friends. Let us introduce everyone to us and the benefits we offer.” We will come together on one plate and create a colorful and delicious meal. Children will enjoy choosing their own dish and eating. And so the adventurous tomato returned to the earth with all her vegetable friends. The mother started preparing the most delicious salads from vegetables. But every time she presents a plate of vegetable salad to her child, he refuses to eat it. The adventurous tomato started talking to him and said: “Hello, my dear.” The boy could not believe what was happening as he looked and listened to the tomato talking to him, but she did not care and continued... Do you know how much trouble we went through to reach you? Did you know that your body needs us? We provide your body with vitamins and fiber. You must eat from us every day. After the boy rubbed his eyes in wonder and listened to the tomato, he ate the salad and loved it very much. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ As he was raising the last spoonful of salad to his mouth, the adventurous Tomato said to him, saying: “Don’t forget to thank your mother for making the salad.” For you every day.” The Health Benefits of Tomatoes Tomatoes are a good source of several vitamins and minerals: Vitamin C. This vitamin is an essential nutrient and antioxidant. One medium-sized tomato can provide about 28% of the Reference Daily Intake. Potassium. An essential mineral, potassium is beneficial for blood pressure control and heart disease prevention. Vitamin K1. Also known as phylloquinone, vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health. Folate (vitamin B9). One of the B vitamins, folate is important for normal tissue growth and cell function.

text: There is a big lake near Begusarai - Kanwar Lake. There are many birds here. Some belong to this place while others come from far-off places. Ali Hussain Sahab is a native of this place. title: Uncle and the Magic Tree
text: An uncle is lying under a lame tree. Suddenly, "What's up, Uncle?" asked the tree with a whispering voice. "Tre-tre-tree can speak!?" Uncle shocked. "That's right, Uncle, I'm a magic tree! Uncle sits under the tree, tears flowing." "I lost my job. I don't know what to do," she replied sadly. "Don't worry, Uncle. What if you started your own business? Uncle can use his skills and experience to help others." "Hmmm, that's a good idea, Magic Tree! Thank you for your advice." Uncle stood up and smiled. "I'll soon find an idea for my business. Thank you, Magic Tree; you've helped me." "Together, Uncle. I'm glad to help."

title: The Smile of Muskanpur
text: In Muskaanpur, there lived a king called Hasmukh. He had a little sister called Punchiri who was the queen of the land. All the subjects of the land always smiled. Once, however, there was a time when Muskaanpur lost its smile. It all began like this....... Punchiri's birthday was approaching and Hasmukh wanted to give her a special gift. Now Punchiri was very fond of animals. She had an entire sanctuary that housed a variety of animals beginning from deer and bisons to rhinos and cheetahs. Hasmukh noticed it did not have penguins. So he decided to gift a few penguins to her sanctuary. Hasmukh took a ship, travelled all the way to Antarctic and got 3 penguins for Punchiri. Once home, Hasmukh eagerly showed it to Punchiri who was beside herself with joy. She hugged and welcomed each of the penguins and released them into her sanctuary. The penguins were initially happy but gradually....... they stopped waddling, stopped flapping their flippers, dropped their heads, sat in a corner of the sanctuary- huddled together. They would not eat, nor play in the pond. The sunshine that warmed the deer and cheetahs only made the penguins pant and close their eyes. Queen Punchiri was the first one to notice. “These are not happy penguins,” she whispered sadly. King Hasmukh called the royal animal caretakers. They tried everything — they built a bigger pond, fed them the finest fish, even painted a snowy backdrop on the rocks. But nothing worked. Punchiri quietly sat beside the three penguins. She placed a bowl of fish near them and gently said, “Tell me, little friends… what do you miss?” Of course, penguins cannot speak human language. But one of them slowly stood up and looked toward the north. Another gave a soft cry. The third tried to glide on the floor. That was when Punchiri understood. “They miss their home,” she said softly. “They miss the snow and the ice. They miss their habitat." Punchiri told this to Hasmukh and he suddenly felt guilty. In his excitement to give the most special gift, he had forgotten something very important- the habitat. It is the natural environment where plants, and animals, live, grow, and reproduce. It is difficult for them to survive when they are not in their own habitat. The next morning, the king made an announcement across Muskaanpur. “True love does not mean keeping someone close. It means letting them be happy.” The people listened quietly. Many of them stopped smiling- but this time, it was because they were thinking. On the same day, the king arranged for the royal ship to take the penguins back to their homeland. The penguins were gently placed in cool enclosures filled with ice and fresh fish for the journey. Punchiri hugged each one. “Thank you for visiting us,” she said. “Now go home.” King Hasmukh himself sailed with them all the way back to the icy shores of Antarctica. When the penguins were released onto the snow, something magical happened. They waddled. They flapped. They slid on the ice! Soon, other penguins gathered around them, calling joyfully. The three penguins joined their families, hopping and diving into the icy waters. Hasmukh watched with moist eyes- but a peaceful heart. When he returned to Muskaanpur, he told everyone what he had seen. Queen Punchiri and the subjects smiled again. From that day onward, the sanctuary welcomed only those animals that belonged to their land and climate. Instead of bringing faraway creatures, Punchiri decided to support the protection of animals in their natural homes. And slowly… The smiles returned. The markets laughed again. The flowers seemed brighter. The deer pranced happily. And Muskaanpur once again became the land where every face carried a warm, thoughtful smile. Because now they knew...... Happiness is not about owning something rare. It is about doing what is right.

title: THE NAUGHTY BOY
text: Once upon a time there lived a boy named Rahul. He was the naughtiest boy in the village. Every day he would get lots of scolding from all of his teachers especially from Ram sir. But that didn't stop him from playing tricks on other people. His classmates, teachers, neighbors, even random people. Once he got a candy from a boy saying he would give him Jalebi's but did not give him anything. Nobody liked Rahul he had no friends. He didn't want to play with anyone because he wanted to plan new schemes but, the boys had so much fun they did not even care that Rahul was there. Soon it was time for the big celebration of the village. All the boys were wearing turbans in different color's so was Rahul. That same day his father scolded him saying that everybody had complaints about Rahul and said that's why he doesn't have any friends. The celebration went by fast everybody had fun with their friends, but Rahul did not have any friends. Every single day the boys would gather around the playground and eat fresh Kesari from the pots but would give nothing to Rahul. Rahul soon started to wish he had some friends that he could play with and share stories with so he made a plan. He asked an older boy named Neeraj to help him change. The first thing he did was apologize to everybody especially his friends, second, he had to start working harder on his studies, third he had to promise that we would never play pranks on anyone. So, he went and apologized to everybody and told them he would never repeat what he did. At first, they had a hard time believing him but finally the agreed. He helped his Neighbours by taking care of their pets. Soon he became a completely different boy. He gave back the candy he had stolen from the boy and gave him an extra one. When he saw a boy stealing Kesari from a shop, he forced him to give it back. The shopkeeper was so impressed. Soon he had many friends and very good grades. Everybody loved the way Rahul had changed. And so did Rahul.

title: the tangled web of friendships
text: The Tangled Web of Friendship I was heartbroken when I found out about the betrayal that had been brewing in my friend group. It all started innocently enough, with laughs shared over inside jokes and secrets confided under the guise of trust. Little did I know, beneath the surface of our camaraderie, jealousy and envy were festering, ready to erupt like a dormant volcano. As the days passed, whispers began to circulate, and I sensed a shift in the dynamics. Suddenly, loyalty was questioned, and alliances were tested. I watched in disbelief as friendships crumbled like a house of cards in a gust of wind. Caught in the midst of the drama, I struggled to navigate the treacherous waters of deceit and betrayal. Who could I trust when even the closest of friends proved to be wolves in sheep's clothing? Amidst the chaos, I found solace in the company of those who remained true, standing by my side through thick and thin. Together, we weathered the storm, emerging stronger and wiser from the ordeal. In the end, I realized that true friendship isn't measured by the length of time spent together or the number of laughs shared. It's about standing by each other's side, through the good times and the bad, and weathering the storms of life together. As the days stretched into weeks, the weight of the betrayal settled like a heavy stone in my chest. Sleepless nights were spent replaying conversations in my mind, searching for clues I might have missed. Each revelation cut deeper than the last, leaving behind a trail of shattered trust and fractured bonds. I longed for the innocence of our past, where laughter flowed freely and smiles were genuine. But now, every interaction felt tainted, clouded by the knowledge that beneath the surface lurked ulterior motives and hidden agendas. Yet, amidst the turmoil, there were glimmers of hope. Friends who had once stood on opposite sides of the divide now came together, united by a common desire for truth and reconciliation. Slowly but surely, the rift began to heal, bridging the gap that had threatened to tear us apart. In the quiet moments of solitude, I found myself grappling with conflicting emotions. Anger burned hot like a raging fire, fueled by the sense of betrayal that gnawed at my insides. But beneath the anger lay a deeper, more profound sadness – a mourning for the loss of innocence and the irrevocable changes wrought by betrayal. Yet, as the days turned into months, I began to realize that perhaps, in the grand tapestry of life, betrayal served a purpose. It forced us to confront uncomfortable truths, to reassess our priorities, and to cherish the bonds of friendship all the more fiercely. And so, as I stood amidst the wreckage of broken trust, I made a silent vow to guard my heart more closely, to treasure the friendships that had weathered the storm, and to emerge from the crucible of betrayal stronger and more resilient than before. Letting people in and breaking my heart was the cycle I had grown all too familiar with. Each time, I convinced myself that this time would be different, that this friendship would be the one to defy the odds and stand the test of time. But time and time again, I found myself back at square one, nursing wounds that ran deeper than any physical pain. But amidst the pain, there was a flicker of resilience – a stubborn refusal to let the darkness consume me entirely. I clung to the memories of happier times, using them as a lifeline to pull myself out of the abyss of despair. And slowly, almost imperceptibly, the jagged edges of my heart began to soften. I learned to forgive, not for the sake of those who had wronged me, but for my own peace of mind. I released the anger and bitterness that had threatened to consume me, replacing them with a newfound sense of acceptance and understanding. In the aftermath of betrayal, I discovered an unexpected source of strength – the unwavering support of those who had stood by me through thick and thin. Their love became my anchor, grounding me in moments of doubt and uncertainty. And so, as I navigated the treacherous waters of friendship, I did so with a newfound sense of clarity and purpose. I understood now that not every bond was meant to last a lifetime, but that didn't diminish the value of the connections forged along the way. I emerged from the crucible of betrayal not unscathed, but wiser and more resilient than before. Armed with the lessons of the past, I ventured forth into the unknown, ready to embrace whatever the future held in store. For in the end, it was not the pain of betrayal that defined me, but the strength and resilience with which I rose from its ashes. With each passing day, I found solace in the simple pleasures of life – the warmth of the sun on my skin, the gentle rustle of leaves in the wind, the laughter of children playing in the distance. These small moments served as gentle reminders that despite the darkness that threatened to engulf me, there was still beauty to be found in the world. And as I opened my heart once more to the possibility of friendship, I did so with caution tempered by hope. I understood now that while the risk of betrayal would always loom on the horizon, so too did the potential for deep and meaningful connections that transcended the pain of the past. So I embraced each new friendship with an open heart, mindful of the lessons learned but unafraid to take a chance on love once more. For in the end, it is the human connection that sustains us through the darkest of times, binding us together in a tapestry of shared experiences and emotions. And so, as I moved forward on my journey, I did so with a renewed sense of purpose and determination. No longer defined by the hurts of the past, I forged ahead with my head held high, ready to embrace whatever the future held in store. For I knew that no matter what trials lay ahead, I would face them with courage and resilience, secure in the knowledge that I was not alone. or so I thought, when the loneliness kicked in with a vengeance. Despite my best efforts to fill the void with new experiences and friendships, there were moments when the ache in my heart threatened to consume me once again. I found myself haunted by memories of the past, replaying moments of betrayal and heartache in my mind like a broken record. The walls I had painstakingly built around my heart began to close in, suffocating me with their suffocating embrace. In those dark moments, it was easy to lose sight of the progress I had made, to succumb to the overwhelming weight of despair. But even in my darkest hour, a glimmer of hope remained, a tiny ember of resilience that refused to be extinguished. I turned to the familiar comforts of solitude, seeking solace in the quiet moments of introspection. It was there, in the stillness of my own thoughts, that I found the strength to confront my demons head-on, to acknowledge the pain that lingered within me and release it once and for all. Slowly but surely, the darkness began to recede, replaced by a newfound sense of clarity and purpose. I emerged from the crucible of my own suffering, reborn and revitalized, ready to face whatever challenges lay ahead with courage and grace. And as I looked to the horizon with renewed optimism, I realized that the journey towards healing was not a linear path but a winding road, filled with twists and turns, peaks and valleys. But with each step forward, I grew stronger, more resilient, more alive than ever before. For in the end, it was not the pain of the past that defined me but the strength and resilience with which I faced it. is asking for a true friend too much? Is it too much to long for someone who understands you, accepts you, and stands by you through thick and thin? As I grappled with these questions, I realized that the answer was simple: no, it wasn't too much. True friendship is a rare and precious gift, one that can't be measured in material wealth or superficial connections. It's about finding someone who sees you for who you truly are, flaws and all, and loves you unconditionally. Someone who laughs with you in times of joy, and holds you close in times of sorrow. Someone who knows your heart better than you know it yourself. And while the search for such a friend may be long and arduous, it's a journey worth taking. For in the end, the bonds of true friendship are forged not in the fires of convenience or obligation, but in the crucible of shared experiences and mutual respect. So I vowed to keep my heart open, to remain vulnerable in the face of uncertainty, knowing that true friendship was out there, waiting to be found. And as I set out on my quest once again, I did so with hope in my heart and a renewed sense of purpose, confident that one day, I would find the friend I had been searching for all along.

title: Phila in the Sacred Forest
text: The day Phila wore her shiny boots She made Chaos all around. Stomp, Stomp, Stomp, Stomping her feet everywhere she goes. " Tamsneng!” * her mother says. “No, I’ll never stop stomping!” Phila cries. *Tamsneng: willful Full of anger, she stomps away. Stomp, Stomp, Stomp To the nearby Forest, she marches on. Without a thought in mind, Phila tramps through the bush into the thick of the Forest. Stomp, Stomp, Sto….. Until she trips and stumbles down a mossy mound! Hurt and bruised, she kicks the root that tripped her. Instead, she misses and her boot goes flying into the air. “Arrrggghhhhhhhhh!” cries a frustrated Phila, breaking the silence of the forest. Birds shriek, monkeys clatter, insects buzz, frogs yelp, and bats click.” Having screamed, she suddenly realises something. She needs her boot! Without it how could she go Stomp, Stomp, Stomp? She runs in search of her boot! But it was nowhere in sight. Phila slumps by a Stonehenge in despair, when she hears a soft deep whisper. "Is this what Chaos look like?” She opened her eyes to see a snake staring back at her with bright yellow eyes. Phila jumps on the stones, terrified! “You can speak?” shocked, she asks. “Of course, I can!” says the Snake. “I’m not just any snake, I am the protector of this Forest” “What do you protect?” asks Phila. “The sacred forestssss,” hisses the Snake, " f rom disruptors like Chaos. " Phila, embarrassed, tries to hide her foot. “Who are you calling Chaos? I just lost my boot” she says, pointing back. " Is that so?” says the Snake. “Well, I happened to see a boot flying past my head when I was on top of that tree. It looked more like it was flung, than lost.” Upon hearing that, Phila’s breath hitched and she runs, leaving the snake behind. She searched and searched for the boot until the sun had gone down. Tired and hungry, all Phila could think of was her mother’s hot bowl of soup. Unaware that a Leopard, the Forest’s deity had crept up behind her. “How did you end up here?” asks the Leopard. "Wahhh!" Phila shrieks as she edges backwards, terrified. “You can speak too, like the Snake?” " I can speak in many tongues, for you to understand,” the Leopard replies lazily. “Will...will you eat me up?” Phila asks, hesitating. The Leopard smiles and says, “Oh no no, I cannot harm. I only protect and provide guidance to those who need it the most. And you are looking for...? " “My boot.” Phila replies before the Leopard could finish his question. “Oh!” says the Leopard. “So you're the one causing the angry stomps everywhere today." " I don't know what you're talking about, " Phila cries stubbornly. “Really?” the Leopard asks again, “They were some very loud stomps. The whole forest heard it.” Phila opens her mouth to respond, but she could say nothing more. She looks down, dejected. She really did go Stomp, Stomp, Stomp. " Your boots, why are they important to you?” the Leopard asks. Still scared, Phila thinks about the question. “I like them! I can go anywhere with them.” “Even if stomping around is hurting everything around you?” " What? I didn’t cause any harm…I…,” She couldn’t finish her words as she recalled her attempt to kick the roots. “Follow me,” says the Leopard as he turns to walk through a dark path. " Today marks the bloom of this flower. It stabilizes the forest’s harmony. It blooms every fortnight as a way to keep the balance between people and nature,” the Leopard declares. Looking at the pitiful flowers, a sudden realization washes across Phila's face. " They are dying, aren't they? " she whispers. “ “Mmm…” the leopard says gently. “That's what Chaos does, causing a ripple effect throughout the Forest. The trees can tolerate it. standing firm. But these flowers bear the brunt of it all. " " If you carry anger in your heart, it disrupts the harmony around you.” Phila’s eyes fills with tears. After a while Phila softly says, “I think I understand now. I don’t want to be Chaos anymore.” The Leopard smiles and shows his gnarly teeth. " Come now, I'll take you home, " he says. “Wait!” Phila takes her remaining boot off and feels the warmth of the Earth beneath her bare feet. Placing the boot on the side, she looks up at the Leopard and smiles. “Now we can go.” The Leopard leads Phila to her own doorstep. There, her mother was waiting, with a hot bowl of soup. Activity Can you spot the following things in the image? Hat | Cat | Dog | Yellow Boots | Kettle | Broom | Firewood | 3 Muras | 3 cups 'Phila in the Sacred Forest,' is part of the 45 Meghalaya-contextual storybooks curated under The Forgotten Folklore Project (TFFP), an initiative of the Sauramandala Foundation. The TFFP team is grateful to Mr Tambor Lyngdoh and Mr Arkie Nelson Wankhar, for sharing their wisdom and knowledge on the Mawphlang Sacred Forest, without which this book would not have been possible.

title: Adventure in Alphabet Ville
text: Once upon a time, in a magical land far, far away, there was a place called the " ALPHABET VILLE". In this wonderful land, each letter had its own unique personality and home. A curious little boy named ARYAN found himself magically transported to Alphabet Ville. As he roamed through the lush green forests and sparkling rivers, he met each letter of the alphabet. He was eager to meet and greet everyone. " A is for Apple Tree!", letter A shouted with glee while pointing towards a tree laden with shiny red apples. " B is for Bear!" said the letter B, as a friendly bear came humming along from his den. Aryan journeyed through Alphabet Ville, meeting new friends and learning about the alphabets along the way. " C is for Castle," proclaimed the letter C proudly, showing off a magnificent castle with blue flags. " D is for Dragon," whispered the letter D mysteriously, as a playful dragon stood like a statue, blowing gentle puffs of fire. As Aryan walked further, he came across challenges and puzzles, each one requiring the help of a different letter. With the help of his new friends, he learned the sounds and shapes of each letter, unlocking the secrets of Alphabet Ville. " E is for Eagle!" cried the letter E, as a majestic eagle soared overhead, leading the way to the next adventure and giving Aryan ride on his back. " F is for Friendly Fox," sneezed the letter F, as a fox scampered by, its tail swishing in the breeze. Together with the letters of the alphabet, Aryan embarked on an unforgettable journey, exploring the wonders of Alphabet Ville and discovering the magic of language. Finally, as the sun began to set, Aryan bid farewell to his newfound friends, grateful for the incredible adventure he had experienced. As he returned home, Aryan carried with him the memories of Alphabet Ville, along with a newfound appreciation for the power of words and the beauty of the alphabet. And so, with a smile on his face and a heart full of joy, Alex drifted off to sleep, dreaming of the endless adventures that awaited him in the magical world of letters.

title: Murugan and his dog
text: One day it rained heavily. Then a boy went fishing. The boy's dog fell into the water. The boy took his umbrella and stepped into the water. Then the dog was dragged away by the water. title: The Growing Up Book
text: Here’s a little secret about growing up. The path to becoming an adult has a fair bit of hair. One day soon, you’ll find hair sprouting from all kinds of places: under your arms, above your lips, all along your legs, and even in between. Maybe you’re already there. Hair in new and unexpected places is totally normal during puberty. Puberty is when your body goes through all kinds of incredible changes. Before you know it, your arms and legs become longer. Your clothes get shorter, tighter. New and unusual smells emerge. Your body surprises you in all kinds of strange ways. For some of you, this means that your breasts grow, and you begin to get your period (yes, there will be blood). You might even start wearing a bra. And for some of you, your voice deepens, and the beginnings of a moustache start to show. You might even start to experience erections. While these changes are exciting, they can also be quite embarrassing. There will be days when it might feel like your body isn’t on your side. A gigantic pimple in the middle of your face. Something in your body seems bigger, or smaller, or stickier, entirely against your wishes. A horrible hair day. A bizarre smell! When this happens, remember that it will pass, and that part of what makes you so uniquely you is this amazing body. Even if it sometimes makes you want to scream. Which is why being curious about your own body is wonderful. As your body changes, it becomes even more important for you to get to know it. Don’t be afraid to explore every inch of your body. The truth about puberty, though, is that while everyone goes through it, our experiences of it vary. So, whether it happens to you sooner than others or later, don’t let it worry you. But puberty isn’t only about your body. It also changes how you feel, and think. You might notice that you suddenly feel angry, or sad. While this can be difficult, these feelings aren’t here to stay. You may also feel the need for a little more space, to be on your own for a while. After all, you are moving into adulthood, which is an adventure. And as with any adventure, there are some ups, and there are some downs. Mood swings are common during puberty. Your friends are likely to be going through them too. So be kind to them, and to yourself. It’s also around this time that you may start developing feelings for others—love, attraction, and that kind of thing. As you make your way through puberty, there will be times when you feel misunderstood. Remember then to turn to something that makes you happy. Listen to that song you love, go for a long cycle ride with a friend, watch a snail glide—do what it takes. Growing can be both joyful and scary. No matter how you feel, remember to listen to your body, and treat it lovingly—after all, your body is yours. I’M GROWING, AND SO IS MY CURIOSITY Understanding the science behind how your body works— especially during puberty— will only help you take better care of it. Why does puberty happen, and when does it happen? Puberty is really just the process of becoming an adult, and it’s caused by hormones in our body. Beginning anytime between the ages of 8 and 14, puberty can last till you’re around 18. So, it’s not something that happens overnight, it takes a few years. What are hormones, though? What do they do? Hormones are chemicals in our body that are vital to how we grow. So when your body is ready for puberty, your pituitary gland (a tiny gland in your brain) releases specific hormones that travel through your blood to different parts of your body, telling them to change. Some of the hormones that are at play during puberty are gonadotropin-releasing hormone: testosterone and oestrogen. What happens when I get my period? A common sign of getting your period is finding blood in your underwear. This sounds scary, but it’s normal. A period (menstruation) occurs when your uterus—for those who have it— sheds its lining. When this happens, you bleed through your vagina. The reason this lining gets thicker is because of hormonal changes in your body. While it can get uncomfortable and sticky, you feel better when you wear a pad or a menstrual cup, or a period product of your preference. Your period will happen every month, and the bleeding usually lasts for three to seven days. Other things you might experience a couple of weeks before and during your period are pain around your abdomen and lower back, headaches, mood swings and acne. Is it true that women on their period can’t enter the kitchen? Why are there so many weird rules around it? There are too many myths and beliefs around menstruation, and unfortunately, most of them aren’t rooted in any logic or science. Thankfully, these beliefs are slowly changing. Sometimes, all we need to do is to ask rational questions. Relying on science to understand the human body is also crucial. You should be able to do anything you want while you are on your period—play, exercise, eat what you like, and go wherever you like. This is your right, and don’t let anyone tell you otherwise. All my friends have facial hair, and many of them have started shaving. Why is it taking me forever? Waiting is hard, isn’t it? While we all go through puberty, remember that our journeys are different. It doesn’t matter whether you develop early, or late—you will become an adult, too. Until the stubble appears, hang in there. There are also other changes that you can expect: you’ll get taller, your voice will change, you may even get erections. When an erection occurs, your penis gets harder and bigger than usual. This happens when blood rushes into your penis, and is caused by the hormones in your body, mainly testosterone. I feel so sweaty, I have acne, and I get bullied! Will it get better? It’s very natural to feel self-conscious about these changes in your body. While this is because of hormonal changes, it’s important to take care of yourself during this time—both physically and mentally. Get enough sleep, eat nutritious food, and make sure to bathe every day. Being bullied is never okay, and you should know that it’s not your fault. It always helps to find someone you trust to talk to about what you are going through. But if the bullying gets too hard for you, talk to an adult whom you trust.
author: Yamini Vijayan

title: The Great Train Journey
text: Our great train journey started with the day we boarded our train. We were finally going to Vishakhapatnam!!...... can you imagine we are going to such a far place with train. It will be obviously fun. On 5 th December, 2021 we reached Howrah Station at about 8 p.m. to catch the train. My father had out seats already reserved in advance. We took our seats in time. I was lucky to get a seat by the window. In our compartment, there were people from different parts of India. The train started after the green signal and soon it picked up speed. the train was running at top speed. I forgot everything of the world and only looked outside through the window. Then, after some time we had our supper and slept. When I woke up I saw that I was 10:00 am. I asked my father that where we were. Then my father told me that we were at Brahmapur. There was only one station left to be crossed. It would take half an hour to reach the staion. I was very excited. As time passed the train became to be emptying. Vendors came to us to sell their articles. ﻿ ﻿ At last!! We reached our destination - Vishakhapatnam. Then we took a taxi and reached our already booked hotel by the sea.

title: Diengsong
text: 1…2…3… 15…16…17… Whoa! Whoa! The earth is shaking again! Ah ha ha ha! …98…99… What comes after 99? 166…167… Uff I know too many numbers....499...500!! Hep-hep, do you know how many more numbers you need to count to reach 2000? Mei! 501…502…503… About 'Diengsong' Diengsong is a small village at the bottom of a hill, in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya. One has to descend over 2000 steep steps to reach the village. With a population of 364 people, and 83 houses (as of June 2023 when the TFFP team visited the village), agriculture is one major activities of the village, with broom cultivation being a major part of the villagers' lives. ‘Diengsong’ is a story very close to the author’s heart because of the sheer joy she experienced on her visit to the village. Each page in the story reflects a personal experience that left an impression on the author. The little girl Hep-hep was inspired from the children of the primary school the TFFP team visited. During their visit on a rainy day, there was a tremor in the hill. While the members of the TFFP team got to rush out of the classroom, the children outside danced with the tremors, their laughter enveloping the rain and the fog. These 2000+ steps are integral for every ‘Diengsong-ian.' From matters of birth to death, these steps are deeply intertwined with the villagers' lives. They would have to climb up the hill to access the nearest PHC (Public Health Centre) or to reach the village cemetery at the top. The author hopes that this story embodies the resilience and simplicity of the village.
author: Lanu Tsudir

title: A DOG LOST IN ALORA TOWN
text: It was a pleasant Sunday afternoon last winter. A group of five friends named Emma, Ruby, Jenny, Nancy and Eli were having a fun time while playing in the park. Suddenly they saw Femma Aunty who lived in the neighborhood and was looking worried. The children asked the reason for her tension. Then they came to know that Aunt Femma had lost her puppy Benge somewhere. All the friends decided to help her. Emma suddenly remembered that one day she had seen Benge eating cake with great interest. All the friends started the search operation to find Benge by looking around at places where they could find him eating cake. Fortunately, they saw a birthday party nearby and went inside in the hope of finding Benge, and their hope turned into reality as they saw Benge inside there enjoying eating the cake calmly beside the cake table. It was a cheerful moment for everyone, especially for Aunt Femma and even the puppy too was happy to be reunited with Aunt Femma. Found my Benge She heartily thanked all the children and gifted them candies for their help. MORAL The moral of the story is that helping others makes everyone happy. Q&A time 1. Who were the main characters in the story? 2. What did Aunt Femma lose, and why was she worried? 3. How did Emma help to find Aunt Femma's lost puppy? 4. Where did the friends find Benge eating cake? 5. How did Aunt Femma express her gratitude towards the children for their help?
