title: Neelu the Unicorn gone back to The School
text: Once upon a time, in a magical land filled with rainbows and sunshine, there lived a little unicorn named Neelu. Neelu was special because her fur was as blue as the sky on the clearest day. Neelu was not just any unicorn; she was talented and kind. She sang beautiful songs, chatted with friends, and was loved by everyone around her. But there was one thing that Neelu found tricky – going to school. Every day, Neelu would trot off to school with a big smile on her face. She loved seeing her friends and her lovely teacher, Miss Mili. But when it was time to practice writing, Neelu felt a little bored. Writing was hard for her, you see. Sometimes, she would get so bored that she couldn't pay attention in class. Miss Mili, being a wise teacher, noticed that Neelu was finding it tough to focus. So, she talked to Neelu's mommy and daddy. After much thought, they decided that Neelu should take a break from school At home, Neelu had lots of time to play and have fun. But deep down, she missed her friends and the adventures of the classroom. So, one day, Neelu told her mommy that she wanted to go back to school. She was missing her craft class, games, stories and friends. Mommy hugged Neelu tight and said, "Of course, my dear! But first, let's practice at home together." And that's just what they did! Every day, Neelu and her mommy worked on writing and drawing. They made beautiful crafts and read wonderful stories. Neelu was so happy to learn new things with her mommy by her side. From that day on, Neelu listened carefully in class and asked for help when she needed it. She worked hard and never gave up, and soon enough, she was writing like a pro! Neelu's mommy and daddy were so proud of their little unicorn. To celebrate her bravery and determination, they gave her a shiny pink heart sticker. Neelu put it on her closet as a reminder of how much she could achieve when she believed in herself. And so, with love in her heart and a smile on her face, Neelu continued her magical journey of learning and growing, surrounded by friends who cheered her on every step of the way.

title: Family wars
text: Hi, everyone my name is Mira welcome to my family, my family and I live in Mattur, Karnataka. One day my father set out for an investigation because he was a police so until my father returned manjula aunty would stay, manjula aunty is my mom's big sister she has one boy named lalith saho he is always stupid I mean he is one year smaller than me he is in 10th class and I am in 11th class I am doing master science isn't great ok lets continue...... Manjula Aunty always loves pets a lot so she brought Sundar, mithai, Sanya and last but not least anusa to our home, we were happily eating lunch, That moment someone knocked at our door my mom wondered who was it and went near the door and opened it, it was none other than a police officer I was scared why a police come to our home instead of our dad? For at least half an hour my mom and the police lady talked in a room that they locked so that nobody could open it, after an hour my mom came out crying and went to her bedroom the same news was shared with my aunt she was shocked nobody couldn't tell me and my cousins a word for this day, next day my mom was sitting on a table She was crying even when she was drinking hot water, so I asked Amma, ninneyinda yake aluthiruve? means- mom why are you crying whats the matter, she said wait dear I will tell you but don't tell to small one's please Your father has met an accident while investigating in Kurnool he is dead I was shocked after listening The next day my mother told me to go to school I was still in that trance Now students let's start Mira and Balu will be the class monitor from now onwards Oh!the bell rang bye children I came home ma, look who came my mom said! DADDY DADDY! you came home police aunty said you died no I wasn't I made them believe so they wouldn't come near us they are betrayers ra aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa! i big noice came from the room dad lets go and see what happen hurry Manjula Aunty was fallen she is not breathing call the ambulance TO BE CONTINUED!

text: A boy with no toy. His name is Pickloo. Pickloo found some paper. He found many happy things to do! Pickloo can do drawing. Pickloo can do drawing and coloring. title: Milo and the Shadow Monster
text: " Milo is not at all speaking these days!" " He is always gloomy!" " He even failed his mid-term, what is going on with him?" Milo was a bright-eyed, curious child with a heart full of dreams and a mind full of wonders. However, something was lurking in the shadows of his mind—an invisible monster that no one else could see but him. This monster was an unknown sadness that crept into his days ruining his peace and happiness. Milo could not figure out how this monster had managed to captivate him, as he had always been a joyous child. Even Mira, Milo's younger sister with whom he was close, could not help him get out of the situation. The monster remained ever-present, hidden from everyone except Milo, following him like a looming shadow. It was there at the dinner table, occupying his thoughts and turning his dinner into a cold mush. " Milo, why are you not eating your food?" It even tagged along when Milo visited his grandparents, numbing his mind and making it hard for him to enjoy their stories. " Milo, are you even listening to us?" It would shamelessly slink around his study table, leaving him wondering why the lessons were not at all getting into his mind. He no longer played the crossword with Mira or read her the storybook. " Milo, can we read this story together please?, it has been a long time!!!" The shadow monster wouldn't stop troubling him even while he slept. He would spend all nights overthinking and impatiently awaiting the dawn to come. He hoped to wake up without its frightening company, but each morning brought disappointment. " Milo...your eyes are red. Are you not sleeping well?" "Milo..look at this toy train, it is soo fun!" "Milo...do I look like a mango monster?....haha!" Poor Mira relentlessly tried her best to cheer him up. Mira always stuck by Milo's side, even when the shadow monster made him act grumpy. She knew Milo was struggling. Day by day, the monster grew on him and he was barely able to get out of his bed and live his life. Mira too noticed the situation and she decided to do something about it. She urged Milo to keep his promise and see the doctor whom their grandfather recommended. Milo had been avoiding it, feeling like nobody would understand his struggles and fearing judgment. “what if they think I am making up stories? ” “What if they think I am crazy?” However, soon Milo found out that meeting the doctor was not a bad idea after all. The way Dr. Shakkira listened to him made him feel seen and understood. The doctor did not laugh it off or call him crazy when he shared his experience. She promised him that the monster was an uninvited visitor in so many people's lives and if we took the necessary steps we could get rid of him. Milo was completely relieved to know that he was not alone. Following the doctor's guidance, and multiple counselling sessions later, Milo found the courage to confront the shadow monster. The monster, completely taken aback by Milo's newly found self-love, tried to threaten him with self-doubt and pessimistic thoughts. However, Milo now realized that all these negative illusions were
author: Diana Nadira Puthusseri

title: Muthu and Kappu
text: For as long as the Muthanna family of Kottageri, in Coorg, could remember, Gangu Muthanna and Raja Muthanna had wanted a pet. But their father Muthanna did not. “It’s too wild. No!” “It’ll dirty the house. No!” “Who knows where it has been. NO!” One day, Muthanna (whom we shall call Muthu) found that his children had brought home a kitten. A tiny BLACK kitten. “Where did you find this thing?” Muthu asked. “Don’t you remember what happened to Machu Uncle? He was enjoying his evening walk when a black cat crossed his path. The next day he was dead!” “But Pappa, he was 93 years old.” “NO! Just take it back before something bad happens!” Aiyo. The children begged and pleaded, but he refused to budge. So they took the kitten back... to their room, where they secretly started to take care of him. But soon enough, Muthu found out. He was very, very angry. “NO!” he thundered. “We cannot keep it! Take it back to where it came from.” Gangu and Raja were very, very sad. They refused to talk to their pappa or eat their favourite dinner of noolputtu and koli curry. That night, Muthu tossed and turned. When he finally fell asleep, he dreamt of black, furry blobs. The next morning, he awoke to loud sounds coming from outside the house. GRRR GRRRRR Pappa! “Muthu!” “Pappa, come fast!” Muthu ran out. “Pappa, it’s the kitten! He’s in the tree! We have to help him.” Muthu lo oked up. Gangu, Raja and Muthu’s wife Poovi stared open-mouthed as Muthu took off his chappals. He then climbed carefully up the tree. The kitten looked into his eyes and mewed softly. M E W Muthu gently scooped the kitten into his sweater and climbed down. “We need to take care of him, Pappa. He is so scared.” Muthu paused. Finally, he said, “OK. But once he gets better, you’ll have to find a home for him. A different home.” Over the next week, Muthu watched the kitten from a distance. He was wild. He left fur everywhere. He even stole dosas right off their plates! But Muthu had never seen Gangu and Raja this happy. And sometimes, even he could admit that the kitten was rather funny. KAPPUUU KAPPU Then, one day, as he was reading the morning paper, the kitten jumped up onto the chair and settled into Muthu’s lap, purring loudly. Muthu opened his mouth to say NO. But he said nothing.
author: Sheena Deviah

title: Once Upon A Night
text: It was a very beautiful full moon night. Everything looked magical. Tanni stood at the window. I wish some magic happens! When Tanni opened her eyes and looked at the sky, she saw a fairy!! Hello Tanni! Wow! The fairy sitting on a star greeted Tanni! Then, she saw some more faries! Tanni could not believe her eyes. She closed them. Is this real?!! Am I imagining it all?!! Magic is Real. Tanni's young heart was beating fast. In her heart was a wish for baba. He had lost his job. He could not get a new job. He wanted to set up his own small shop. But Baba had no money to do that. For a long time, Tanni stood at the window. She kept opening and closing her eyes. The faries kept looking at her. They waved to her. The next moment she closed and opened her eyes, they were gone!! Tanni felt magic had happened. She went to bed feeling baba would get the money he needed. The next day, Tanni found dadi in a very good mood. Tanni! Come and sit here. I want to talk with you. Tanni went and sat near dadi. Child, your amma and baba always got annoyed with one of my habits. You know what it is, don't you? Tanni told dadi, "Your habit of keeping old things safely and not giving them away." Hmm! And I always said, "Old is gold." Late last night, your baba's friend came to meet us. He works abroad. He asked me to show him the 'gold' I have. I did. He purchased my nana's pocket watch and some old coins from me! Now baba has the money to set up a shop! Tanni closed her eyes. The magical sky came to her mind. She saw the fairy upon a star. Tani flew to her. Magic is real!
author: Shahin Ashraf Ali
illustrator: Audrey Agnier; Niloufer Wadia; Proiti Roy; Thea   Nicole de Klerk

title: Labor is luck
text: He was worried about his children's lack of responsibility. Once he called his children and divided the land. He also said that there was a treasure in one of those lands about a foot deep. He told them to find it and died. The three children did all the last things that needed to be done for their father. Then they began to dig the ground to retrieve the treasure he had mentioned. First the eldest son started digging his field. Then the three of them started digging the other fields together, but they were disappointed The land was suitable for cultivation after excavation. The three deceived, though angry with their father, watered their fields and sowed their seeds. At the end of the year they are on the land They reaped and sold a bumper harvest and made a huge profit. The three children understood that the fruit of this labor was what Father called a treasure.

illustrator: Anandee Vaidya; Ayushi Sharma; Divit  jain; Jayesh Sivan; Olivia Fraser; Srikrishna Kedilaya

title: Red Rice
text: “Bei!!! I’m so huuuunnnggrryyy!!” “Oh, Khon! You’re home! Look at your clothes! Go clean up. I’ve just put the rice on,” Bei replies warmly. "Bei, Bei, guess what! I scored a goal today! I shot it from waaayyy back, and it went right into the net! Everyone clapped so hard," Dap exclaims with a smug smile. “Awww, congratulations, " Bei smiles. “Ah, it's red rice! Why have you cooked red rice today, Bei?” asks Dap. “Oh! Since you have your football practice tomorrow, the red rice will give you the strength that you need,” says Bei. " But how? " Dap asks. “Well, firstly, red rice is rich in fibre and proteins, which makes you strong and is good for your tummy. And the second reason is……a secret!” “A secret? Tell me, please!” Dap eagerly asks. Bei tells him, “Well, red rice is very special to us, khon. We work tirelessly to get the fields ready because red rice grows best in well-prepared soil.” “And when the field is ready, they are then sown into each of the muddy beds that have been prepared for them. You have seen Kong do it, haven’t you?” asks Bei. “And as you know, water is like magic for plants, especially for rice! People would consistently keep the water in check.” “Then we wait four to six months to harvest the rice. That is when the 'rashi' and 'khoh' are used to collect and separate the rice from the plants. It's like a big harvest party for the rice!" “Since everyone in the village puts so much effort into making it, our red rice gives back strength to us!” “Ready to eat? The rice is all done!” exclaims Bei with a smile. “ Thank you, Bei!” says Dap, taking in the aroma of the hot red rice. “Mmmmmmm! Thank you, red rice! I’m going to score more goals tomorrow! " Activity Separate the red rice from the husks. You will need: A small amount of red rice or white rice Bowl/Chalani Clean Hands Take a bowl or winnowing tray. Pour red rice on it. You can gently rub the rice grains together to remove husks. Pick out any loose husks. Repeat until most of the husks are removed. Your rice is clean and ready to cook!
author: Nazarene F Jyrwa

title: Snowy The Puppy
text: Snowy the puppy woke up and started barking. “BOW BOW BOW BOW”. Because she heard a lot of noise outside and it was already night time. So, she decided to stay awake and look out at the interesting world during night. Outside, she looked at a bunch of grasshoppers chirping and snowy came and barked “ Bow Bow, dear grasshoppers please stop chirping”. The grasshoppers stopped chirping. She then saw bee and barked at it “ Bow Bow, dear bee please stop buzzing” people are sleeping around this time. The bee stopped buzzing and left. After a few miles reaching to her home she then saw two monkeys shrieking. She barked “ Bow Bow, dear monkeys please stop shrieking the others are sleeping”. The monkeys stopped shrieking. Snowy went back home to sleep. But, she woke up and heard a pleasant sound outside. She decided to go look what was there. When she looked at it she was surprised. She saw a flock of humming birds playing their melodious tune. Snowy became amused by how these birds make this pleasant sound. She then barked” Bow Bow, dear humming birds can you please sing a lullaby so that me and the others can go to sleep”. The humming birds agreed and chirped. They created their melodies tune and slowly it made snowy feel happy to hear this sound. After hearing it, she went back home and realised that nature can be both noisy as well as pleasant. She then, fell asleep.
author: Prateeksha Hariganesh

title: The adventures of Panda and Friends
text: In the serene bamboo forests of China, there lived a panda named Panda. Now, Panda was unique from his peers. While they excelled in their studies of bamboo munching and napping techniques, Panda struggled to keep up.Panda struggled a lot losing one of his eye. In fact, he was known for his lack of academic prowess, earning him the nickname "Notty Panda (Naughty Panda)." Among Panda's closest friends were his fellow classmates from bamboo school: Pinky the Monkey, Onie the Bear, Pengu the Penguin, and Lola the Koala. Each brought their own unique talents and personalities to the group, making them an inseparable bunch. Pinky the Monkey was the smartest and most talented creature in the entire forest. With an intellect that challenged even the wisest elders, Pinky excelled in every subject at bamboo school and was known for her impressive problem-solving skills. Like her name she is very pink and bright. Onie the Bear was the life of the party, always ready with a joke or a prank to lift his friends' spirits. With his infectious laughter and boundless energy, Onie could turn even the gloomiest day into a wild adventure. Pengu the Penguin was the second smartest in the class, but her true talent lay in her storytelling abilities. With a vivid imagination and a talent for weaving tales, Pengu could transport her friends to far-off lands and magical worlds with just a few words. Pengu is a unique penguin, unlike others she can fly. And then there was Lola the Koala, the loveliest and cutest creature in the entire forest. With her big, soulful eyes and her gentle nature, Lola was adored by everyone who knew her, and her presence always brought a sense of warmth and joy to any gathering. One day when Pinky and friends were sleeping, a grey monkey named Harsh entered their room. He took Pinky as enemy as she always used to destroy his mischievous plans. He want to take revenge,so he found out Pinky's whereabouts and took Pinky and friends into a cage with bamboo key. He owned a whole town called Banana crills. He took the cage to his town. They were left in a room full of soapy suds, traps and the door is also a trap door with a bamboo key. The thing is that the many trap doors lead to mazes with soapy suds with the exit back into the room. Pinky knew banana crills very well and always used to found out Harsh's plans. So she used her thinking skills to make a plan to get out of there. Pinky discussed the plan with others. Pinky said '' the lock is made of bamboo, bamboo isn't too hard to snap, we need an iron rod to break it. Lets search the room for an iron rod, if found, lets break the lock and pretend that we still were locked.At night Let's escape by digging a tunnel to our home, because naughty monkeys team are very alert. Be careful and we shall be aware that this room is full of traps. Everyone agreed and carefully went looking for iron rod.As Lola was walking trough one of the mazes, She saw a bunch of laser rays passing all over that path. she was scared to take a step forward but suddenly she saw that the Laser switch was right beside her! Lola switched off the laser and finally found iron rod, she grabbed the rod and went to Pinky. Pinky called others back and Pengu broke the lock with iron rod with great force. Pinky made a map to make an underground tunnel and Panda started to dig the tunnel without any noise. As they made their way through the tunnel Onie made up many jokes and acted as a stress buster., then Onie made a barrier with soil so Harsh could not come back Panda piled the tunnel with soil and grew a plant at the exit. ''All these arrangements just for a barrier! '' Onie said. They finally reached their home safely. After that they all started their daily works like normal and always awaited adventures.
author: Meher Anvita

title: Our Beautiful Earth
text: Pontu is suffering from a disease which is so common nowadays, yes.. you guessed it right...its no other than boredom. Pontu’s summer vacations are full in swing and he has not gone on any trips yet. Because his mom and dad are too busy in their professions. So the chances of their out station visit are miniscule. Pontu is feeling all alone as there is no friend left to play with. All his friends have gone some place or the other to enjoy holidays. Devoid of any sort of entertainment he stares at the ceiling of his bedroom while fiddling with the remote of his T.V. thinking about what to do next. Just like many other kids of his age, Pontu’s brain is filled to the brim with questions. When he asks his mom and dad to reply his questions, they hardly have any time to satisfy Pontu’s constant why’s and how’s. But there is one exception in the family and that is Pontu’s elder brother Montu. He is always ready to spend his time with his younger brother. Pontu’s brain is filled with number of questions and Montu is always happy to answer those. Montu’s brain is a treasure of knowledge. He spends hours of time in reading books and surfing through internet. Today Pontu is curious about the world that he lives in. Pontu only knows that he lives on a round planet and that it is enormous with many unique places in it. He has no idea about the specifications of different parts of the earth, so he went to Montu to ask about it. Pontu requested Montu to tell him about the world. “What will I get in return for answering all your queries” Montu asked. After careful thought Pontu replied “your little brother’s heartfelt thanks.” “Well……. fair enough.” said Montu. Pontu- Well…. what do you want to know about the world? Montu- Just give me a general idea about it. Montu- Do you know that our world is 71% water and 29% land. “Wow..... is that really true” Pontu interrupted. Yes, most of our world is made up of large water bodies called oceans. Montu- The world is not just plain and circular but it has different elevations and depths, so you can say that the earth looks more like an uneven rock rather than a sphere. We call elevation of land as height above sea level and the depths of ocean as land below sea level. MONTU- This difference in elevation creates different types of landforms like Mountains, Hills, Plains and plateaus. Pontu- Whoa, whoa...please slowdown. I need to process this information in my brain. Montu- Ok, for better explanation, lets see this map of India that I have. Montu- The green areas in the map are the plains, the pink areas the plateaus, the yellow colour shows the areas with hills. Orange ones are small mountains, the black ones medium sized and purple ones being tall mountains like Mount Everest. PONTU- Oh, what is this brown area in Gujarat. MONTU- That is a lower area near sea level better known as salt planes in Rann of Kutch. MONTU-I hope, you are clear now about these geographical specifications. PONTU- Yes, most of it. This is all amazing. Thank you soooo....much for sharing all this. Let me process this information in my brain and I will come back to you with more questions. You are always welcome my younger bro.....
author: Gurnoor Singh

title: THE TIGER
text: Once there lived a tiger in the jungle. One day when the tiger went outside, it saw a deer nearby. The tiger decided to hunt the deer. The tiger chased the deer. The deer escaped from the tiger. After the deer escaped, the tiger was roaming and growling very loudly with an angry face. Rrrrrrrrrrrr..... A hunter went inside a forest in search of a tiger. The hunter saw the tiger. The hunter shot the tiger. Finally, the tiger was hunted by a hunter. When we think of destroying others, we will be destroyed.
author: SUJAI RAAJ
illustrator: Jagruti M; Kalp Sanghvi; Kavita Singh Kale; Mugdha Kapri; Nancy Raj; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Rohan Chakravarty; Rohan Dahotre; Sudarshan Shaw

title: Our Half-Asleep Teacher
text: One day, the teacher, in an attempt to get rid of his nickname, told his students "Whenever I fall asleep I meet ancient philosophers and sages in the world of dreams." The students listened carefully as their teacher explained. The next day when the teacher came to class, he saw all the students trying to sleep. Believing that they were making fun of him, he became very angry. He asked the students in an irritated tone, "What are you doing?" They replied that they wished to talk to great philosophers and sages in their dreams. They wanted to experience the land of dreams as well. They wished to be just like their teacher!
author: Akshay Chandramouli
illustrator: Fahad Faizal; Manisha Naskar; ROSH; Ruchi Shah; Students of  Himalayan Public School

title: Rain
text: This rhyme beautifully captures the nostalgic essence of growing up in a place where the elements become part of cherished memories. The clouds are a part and parcel of people’s regular lives in the hills and with that, rain and thunder are inevitable. The author recalls how while playing in the rain and getting wet was a joyful activity, the rain also kept people inside to avoid catching colds. And there would be stern warnings from elders about the wrath of thunder and lightning. Rhymes and stories often serve as comforting companions, bringing joy even in the midst of gloominess and dullness, and the contributors to this book intend to share this comfort with those reading it. 'Rain,' is part of the 45 Meghalaya-contextual storybooks curated under The Forgotten Folklore Project (TFFP), an initiative by the Sauramandala Foundation. This book is a collaboration between the MLCU (Martin Luther Christian University) Shillong, and the TFFP. The TFFP team is grateful to Careen J Langstieh for sharing and helping document this “almost-forgotten” rhyme.
author: Esther Syiem

title: THE FARMER AND THE SNAKE
text: One day a farmer was working in the field but what do you see a snake was in middle of the field the farmer was frightened and he run away And then what the snake attacks the farmer he was so deadly that the bite made the farmer's health down the farmer cried for help
author: parjanya Mahajan

title: Happy Hands
text: I want to try some pottery too, Miss Lari,” says Lana. “Today we will learn how the black clay from the Sung V alley helps make these beautiful black pottery pieces.” “Look, the clay is soft!” says Tori. “Did you add black paint to it?” asks Lana. “I have never seen black clay before,” says Iba. “These are so beautiful,” says Janai. Miss Lari smiles at the excited children. “Yes, they are beautiful indeed, aren’t they?” “How did the clay harden, Miss Lari?” asks Lana. “Where can we find the black clay?” asks Sam. Miss Lari tells them that the the black clay is dug out from the Sung Valley. A serpentine stone is crushed until it turns into a green powder. The women then mix the green powder with the clay and it is sticky! They form different shapes with the sticky clay and then leave them to dry in the sun. The dry pottery pieces are dipped into the dye made from the bark of Sohliya trees. The hardened pottery pieces are then sold. People come from far away places to buy them. “How come we don’t see these pottery pieces in the shops near my house?” asks Janai “Maybe because Larnai is too far and not many know about it,” Lana answers him. “Miss Lari, look at my bowl!” says Iba “What do you think of Larnai pottery?” Activity Ready to make your own pottery piece? Using simple ingredients found in your kitchen, you can create different shapes! 2 cups of flour 1 cup salt 2 cups water 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil 1. Mix all ingredients into a dough. 2. Enjoy making your own hand pottery piece. 3. When the piece is dry, you can colour it with water colours.
author: Mebanda Iaka Blah Dkhar
illustrator: Elmer Renato; The Forgotten Folklore Project

title: The Porcupine and Elephant
text: My oh my! What a lovely day for a bath. Huh? Who dares anger a mighty creature like me, the Elephant!! If you dare, show yourself! Who are you to question what I do? Fear me, as I am mightier than you! Hah! Mightier than me? Not a cha nce! I am sending a strand of my hair. See for yourself if you would like to face me. Ahhhhh!! Hmmmm? Hahahahahaha! Whoooaaa! Thud! And that is why rats have very prominent front teeth. Activity Can you spot the rat in the following images? About the Story An amazing thing about oral traditions is the fact that there are different variations of the same story. Stories narrated orally are passed down from one generation to the next and variations appear because people/regions adapt a story, add or subtract plots, characters, etc. based on their need and understanding. This particular story was pieced together based on two people’s narrations–same story with variations in the endings! 'The Porcupine and Elephant,’ is a part of the 45 Meghalaya-contextual storybooks curated under The Forgotten Folklore Project (TFFP), an initiative of the Sauramandala Foundation. The TFFP team is grateful to Rufus Pangrak G Momin and Bikramjit A Sangma for sharing their versions of the folktale without which this book would not have been possible.
author: Lanu Tsudir

title: We Are Months
text: January is the first month of the year. Then comes February, telling us “Spring is here!” March is a month that is so very windy, But April brings rain to keep us all busy. May is for picnics under skies so blue, June has sunny days, rainy days and happy rainbows too. July is for dancing in the rain, In August you can do it all over again. September skies are for starry wishes, October is for catching a bucketful of fishes. November’s cherry blossoms bring in good cheer, And December is the last month of the year. Every month is different but together they make up one year.
author: Mebanda Iaka Blah Dkhar

title: NO MORE SCHOOL!
text: Once upon a time, in a land far away, there lived a little girl who hated school! This boy's name was Ria. Ria hated school, the idea of children sitting in a room just learning for hours was terrifying to her. Ria would much rather go out and play with her dog, Kabir. Ria loved the outdoors, she wanted to spend every single moment in the day in nature. But much to her sadness, her father decided to send her to school. Some days Ria would act sick and get her mother to let her stay at home. She would lie in bed acting ill, asking her mother for ice cream and other delicious sweets. Her mother, a sweet woman, would do anything her daughter asked her to do. One day, she was forced to go to school. Sitting in her classroom, her teacher knowing she was upset suggested that she should try applying what she learns today in nature. "Maybe, you will find that everything is connected." Ria agreed, focusing fully in classes hoping to see some sort of connection. That evening when Ria and Kabir went out to play in the river by her house, she noticed how the plants by the riverbed were extremely green. She remembered how in her science class they learned about chlorophyll, and she applied that to how the leaves were green here. During that evening Ria realized that learning might actually come in handy. From that day forward, Ria enjoyed going to school and learning. Every evening, her family and her spoke about what new things they learned that day and Ria always was eager to share. Ria and her family lived happily ever after.
author: Nayantara N
illustrator: Shamim  Ahmed; Shamim Ahmed; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: The Capseller and The Monkeys
text: Once there lived a capseller who went house to house selling his magnificent caps. As he walked down the road he began to feel tired and searched for a place to rest. Soon enough he found a huge tree and went into slumber,as he slept a troop of monkeys came and looted all his caps. One of the monkeys passed each cap to the other monkeys. After all the monkeys got the best caps on thier heads, they slowly and quitly climbed back the tree. As they waited for the capseller to wake up. Once he woke up, he was very worried about his caps. He looked up the tree,there he saw all the monkeys wearing the caps and sitting majestically. He thought why not throw it down and the monkeys follow me! As this thought came to the capseller,even the monkeys kept thinking what the capseller is going to do!! As soon as the capsellert threw his cap all the monkeys threw down thier caps,and the capseller thought how great he was. As the capseller collected the caps and put in the bag, the monkeys wondered why had they just thrown down the best caps in the world. As the capseller walked back home happily, his mind flew across the incidents that took place that day. And he learnt to always be aware of the surroundings.
author: Saanvi  S Dabade

title: A women goes to a picnic
text: One day a women plans to go for a picnic on the hills. The next day she went to the hill she stopped next to a tree and started to prepared for the picnic after preparing she ate and slept for sometime then she woke up and started to explore the hill she saw a puppy it was very hungry. She took the puppy to the car and feeded it and she and the puppy to the house
author: Sasrith Krishav

title: Emily's Mother
text: Emily sat by the window, her fingers tracing the delicate patterns of frost on the glass. Memories of her mother, Margaret, flooded her mind, bringing warmth to the chilly evening. Margaret was a beacon of love and guidance in Emily's life. From her tender embrace to her words of wisdom, Margaret shaped Emily's understanding of the world. As a child, Emily would often seek refuge in her mother's arms, finding solace in the soothing rhythm of her heartbeat. Margaret's gentle voice would weave tales of courage and resilience, instilling in Emily a sense of hope and determination. Through the years, Margaret remained a constant source of strength, her unwavering support guiding Emily through life's triumphs and trials. Whether it was a comforting hug after a heartbreak or a reassuring smile before a daunting challenge, Margaret was always there, her love unwavering and unconditional. Even as time passed and Emily embarked on her own journey, Margaret's presence remained ever-present, a guiding light illuminating the path ahead. Her words echoed in Emily's mind, serving as a source of comfort and inspiration. As the years went by, Emily cherished the moments spent with her mother, treasuring each laugh shared and each lesson learned. And though Margaret was no longer physically present, her spirit lived on in the memories they had created together. With a fond smile, Emily whispered a silent thank you to her mother, grateful for the love that had shaped her into the person she had become. And as the stars twinkled in the night sky, Emily felt Margaret's presence surrounding her, a reminder that a mother's love knows no bounds. In the warmth of her memories, Emily found solace, knowing that her mother's love would always be her guiding light, leading her home.
author: Cerena D'Cunha

title: Who am I?... A short riddle
text: I am your friend, I have been with you through thick and thin. Who am I? I live in your backpacks, bags, and desks. I am there for you at school, I am there for you at home. You use me in so many different ways! You have used me to create different universes through your drawings, and yes I have helped you to learn a lot as well. When you use me, never shall you fret about your mistakes! Do you know who I am? Surely you must recognize me by now. Yes! I am indeed your faithful friend the PENCIL and I send my regards.
author: Akshay Chandramouli
illustrator: Abin  Shrestha; Darsh Shahdadpuri; Mlungisi Dlamini; Rajiv Eipe; yulin zhang

title: Rita's adventure
text: The girl named as Rita was tired of doing her homeworks. She thought of an idea to leave the house and immediately went to jungle to explore herself. In the jungle, Rita saw bright flowers and heard birds singing. It was so pretty and fun! She danced around and said, "I'm going to stay here forever!" Initially she really admires the nature and started dancing with peacock. But then, Rita heard a loud "ROAR!" It was a lion! She felt scared. The jungle wasn't just fun and games; it could be scary, too. Rita missed her home and her family. She ran back home as fast as she could. When she got there, her family gave her a big hug. Rita was happy to be back. She realised that even though homework wasn't always fun, being safe at home with her family was the best. That night, Rita went to bed feeling happy. She now understood that adventures can be exciting, but there's no place like home. "Adventures are fun, but being home with family is the best fun of all."
author: Sumbul Khan
illustrator: Arindam Dhar; EBERECHUKWU BLESSED; Kavita Singh Kale; Pratham Content Group; Priyanka Kumar; Rob Owen; Rohit Karandadi; Wesley   van Eeden

title: Sentences with Lily
text: Lily was in the room waiting for her brother and mom to come back home, she was bored and started playing with her ball, she kicked it hard and alas! it landed on one of her mother's Ceramic plates, which were reserved for guest, crashing it came down and fear came down on Lily, she hid the evidence. Mom and Brother were back home, Lily looked scared so, her mom questioned her "What is going on did anything happen?" "We learned grammar in School today!" Brother interrupted, Lily tried to hide but, eventually let it out, "I broke the Glassware......" "That's a simple sentence.", her brother said. "Why?", Lily tried to distract her mom. "The subject is you and predicate is the glassware you broke, so, 1 Subject and 1 predicate make a Simple sentence." Brother said proudly. "Your Sister broke glassware." Mom; "Another Simple sentence." Brother; "Quiet, will you? " mom said, "and you, how did it happen?" Lily failed in distracting her mom, " I kicked the ball a little too hard and the ball landed on the cupboard." Lily was scared and her brother found a chance to intervene, "That is a Compound sentence!" "Explain, I know you won't sit still if I don't let you.", Mom was tired, "There are two Main Clauses joined by a Conjunction, two or more main Clauses joined together by a conjunction it is a Compound sentence." "He is done now, where are the Shards?", mom enquired, "They are hidden under the Cupboard." "Why did you Hide them?", mom was worried, "I broke the Glassware hence, I was scared that you might scold me so, I hid them." Lily explained, here comes the grammar guy, "That's a Complex Sentence!" Mom was surprised with his interest, "You should not touch broken glass on your own so, you should wait for an adult as it might hurt you, understood?" "Yes", answered Lily and her brother. Later Mom found out that, the Boy's interest in grammar was his homework, he was supposed to write and example of Simple, Compound and Complex sentence so, he wrote what he heard! Let's Revise! Simple sentence- A simple sentence consists of a subject and a predicate. Compound sentence- A compound sentence is a sentence that has more than one main clause. It should have at least two main clauses and they can be combined using a coordinating conjunction. Complex sentence- A complex sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause. The two clauses can be combined using a subordinating conjunction. Quiz I Identify the Simple sentence- a) I did not know that this food was meant only for the staff. b) She is innocent, so she has appealed to the court. c) The young students enjoyed the game. Identify the Compound sentence- a) The cat purrs softly. b) Even though the cat was very hungry, he still refused to eat the food. c) The cat was sleepy and it was hungry. Quiz II Quiz III ﻿Identify the Complex sentence- a) I wish I ran well. b) The cat ate the food and started to run. c) Although the cat ran away, it came back for food the next day. Answer key- Quiz I- c Quiz II- c Quiz III- c Answers! Well Done!
author: Esther R.  Nadar

title: Eat Healthy, Be Happy
text: On ce upon a time, in the suburbs of Bombay, there lived a little chubby girl named Riya. She was a junkfood addi ct. Her exams were on, and she had studied well. However, it was a bright sunny Sunday when she got invited for her bestfriend Urfi's birthday party. There, she ate heavy amounts of cho colate cake, potato chips, deepfried chi cken, cold drink, i ce cream, et c. She could not control her cravings and hen ce overate. Her mother had warned her to not eat too mu ch of junk. This led to an up coming trouble... That very night, Riya suddenly felt an a che in her belly. She tried to turn right and left, but to no avail. Her pain was gradually in creasing. Hen ce, her worried mother called up the do ctor. The do ctor che cked her up, and diagnosed her with food infe ction. He advised her to not attend s chool the next day. Hen ce, she missed her exams even when she had studied well. This made her realise that junk food can affe ct one's entire lifestyle, so we must always eat healthy. This was a valuable lesson for her lifetime.
author: Chelsia D'cruz
illustrator: Aditya Agarwal; Jigyasa .; Kakoli Bhattacharjee; Saheb Ram  Tudu; Soumya Menon; Subi Bosa; Supreetha CK

title: Colorful Chameleons
text: Once upon a time, a girl named Ritu who is very fond of animals, on her way to home finds a chameleon. As soon as she sees that chameleon in rainbow color, jubilantly she picks it up and takes it home. She thinks,'why is this chameleon in multiple colors?' So decides to change its color. She immediately goes into her room and take out her color box and start coloring the chameleon in yellow color. A little later, she gets hungry so she goes into the kitchen and search for fruits, there she finds a chameleon sitting on a banana basket. She thinks chameleon is in yellow color, banana is also in yellow color. "How will I identify which one is banana or chameleon? " So she decides to recolor it. She begins coloring the chameleon in orange color. She finds that the chameleon now blends in among oranges. Ritu picks the chameleon from the orange basket and start coloring it in red color. Once she finishes with coloring, she finds that chameleon is now among apples. She recolor it in green color and finds that chameleon is hidden among green leafy vegetables. This time she colors the chameleon in blue color. Now the chameleon hides itself in painting which is in blue color, Ritu searchs for the chameleon in every corner but couldn't find where is it hidden. She gets very furious and irritated. When her mother finds Ritu angry and irritated she asks the reasons. Ritu tells, when I color the chameleon in yellow, it sits on Banana. When I recolor it with red it sits on apples. Now I don't understand why is it happening so? I am not able to find it where is it hidden since I colored it blue. Ritu's mother starts laughing and tell her " My honey don't worry, let me make you understand this." It's the chameleon's ability to change its color according to their surroundings and this color changing ability knows as chromatophores. And it is their unique and remarkable feature. Let me tell you something more. Their eyes can be moved independently of each other due to which they have 360 degree vision which means they can see what is in front of them, behind them and sideways simultaneously. Chameleons have long, sticky tongue that can capture insects with incredible speed. Ritu understands everything about chameleons and her doubts gets solved.
author: Rukaiya Ansari
illustrator: Clyde   Beech; Kalyani Naravane; Karthikeyan S.; Kingshuk Chaudhary; Michael  Sagikwa; Offei Tettey  Eugene; Rupa Prakash; Sandhya Prabhat; Tvishi Nagpal

title: Helpful Jay
text: One day Jay woke up early in the morning. He was going on holiday he remembered. He had to pack his suitcase by himself his mother ordered him to so. He told himself that he will pack his suitcase now and he surprise there's. He started packing his bag he added all his favorite clothes. Jay saw that he had made a mess due to packing as some of his toys were missing. When he cleared his mess he saw his favorite toy truck and many other toys. So he tried packing everything together but he relisted that everything won't fit. He tried his best to fit everything in the bag. His mother woke up due to all the sound and she came in the room to wake him up but she was surprised to see what he was doing. His mother said to him that she is very happy with him. title: A Friend In Need Is A Friend Indeed
text: There was a girl named Priya who had two friends,Sania and Simran.They all studied in the same school.They used to play,eat and study together. But Priya considered Sania as her close bestfriend because Sania was beautiful and rich whereas Priyas used to avoid Simran as she was ugly and poor. One day they all were playing hide and seek in the forest. So Priya went behind the tree to hide whereas Sania, Simran and others were hidding far from her. Suddenly Priya heard a voice of roaring and when she turned back to see who was it, she saw a tiger coming towards her. She got scared and started screaming loudly. When everybody heared Priya shouting they ran towards her and as soon as they saw a tiger, they all ran away.Simran also ran away.Sania was also scared but she didn't ran as she wanted to save Priya's life. As she was thinking of some idea,she saw a man with a gun who was basically a hunter, passing through the forest.She ran towards him and asked him for helped.He told Sania not to worry and he went towards the tiger with the gun. As soon as the tiger saw the man with a gun he ran back in the forest.Sania came runningly towards Priya and hugged her as she was scared. Priya thanked Sania for helping her and even asked her to forgive her for not valuing her friendship.Sania and Priya hugged each other and return back to their home.

title: The Brave Adventurers.
text: ﻿ Once upon a time, there were two friends, Lily and Ben. They loved exploring the forest near their house. One sunny day, they found a mysterious cave hidden behind tall trees. Curious, they ventured inside. It was dark and spooky, but they were brave. Suddenly, they heard a faint sound. Following it, they discovered a baby fox trapped in a hole! Working together, they rescued the scared little fox. Grateful, it licked their hands. Lily and Ben smiled, happy to have helped. From that day on, they became known as the brave adventurers of the forest.
author: Serena  Dsouza

title: What Words Mean
text: As the family sat down for dinner one day, Jade asked her mother while she served some rice. 'Mummy why do we call this salad and this a table?' Mother replied, 'My girl that is because a very long time ago, the people decided to name these things as rice and table'. The next day Jade and her brother Jaden went with Grandma to buy groceries for lunch. Jade, 'Grandma, like rice and table, do these vegetables too have a name each?', 'Yes, my child, just like how your name is Jade, each creature and thing in this world is given a name.', said Grandma. Jade was still confused about why each thing was given a name. So she asked her father, 'Daddy, why is it that all things and creatures given names?' Father replied, 'Baby that is because each person, creature, and thing is unique, we cannot call everyone and everything by the same name.' 'It is why we named you Jade and your brother Jaden.' said Mother. Grandpa said, 'Jade now that you have been promoted to grade 5 you will learn about how words are categorised and used differently. All these names are words created to understand the world better.' 'And when you understand the concept of words, I will play this interesting game called Name, Place, Animal and Thing with you.', replied Father. 'Yay, I am so excited to go back to school tomorrow! Mummy, could you please serve me some of that yummy-looking soup.' 'Yes darling. Eat well, you have a long way to go and grow.' That evening Jade and her family enjoyed a delicious meal cooked by mother.
author: Caroline Pereira
illustrator: Catherine Groenewald; Debasmita Dasgupta; Nan Hom Noon; Sahitya Rani; Vusi  Malindi

title: GENEROSITY
text: Henry was born to a wealthy family. Even when he was a child, he shared his wealth with those in need. He and his wife continued to be generous to everyone. Once Henry ran out of all his money. he was worried about as to how he would feed his family. Both of them decided to trust God and be generous. One day Henry managed to get some rice and vegetables for his family. The family thanked God and started eating. At the same time a beggar came knocking at the door asking for some food. Even though there was not much food, the Henry and his wife offered some food and some other essentials. The beggar thanked them for their generosity and left. After some time a traveler stopped at their house and asked for some food. Henry and his wife offered a seat to the traveler in the house and offered him dinner followed by water. The traveler felt grateful for their generosity and gave them blessings. Later a farmer came asking for some fruits as he was hungry. Henry had one mango left with him and without giving it a thought he gave the mango to the farmer, and the farmer left happily. Henry and his family were left with half glass of water. He was worried about how he would feed his family for the rest of the days. A monk appeared at that time and asked for some food. Henry offered all that he had left with himself. Henry was worried as he was left with nothing. He still had faith in God and said he believed that God is good and he would help him. After sometime, the monk revealed himself as God, the creator. Henry bowed to him and he was blessed with a lot of wealth for his generosity toward everyone. ﻿ Moral: If we help others others will help us too. In addition to making other people's lives better, our generosity in time, money, and compassion spreads throughout the entire planet.
author: Shreya  Falcao

title: The Brave Penguin Blink and the Warming World
text: Once there lived a baby penguin who's name was Blink. He lived with his parents on the ice berg island that place was known as the Glacier Haven. Blink was a good baby and did all his work. He helped his mother with household chores and also played on the ice with his friends. "Blink noticed that his mom had been very worried and upset for the past few days, so he asked his mommy penguin, 'What's wrong, Mom? Why are you upset?'" His mom replied, "Baby, I'm not upset, but scared." Blink exclaimed, "Scared? What are you scared of? Is your health alright?" His mom said, "I'm fine, baby. I'm scared about the melting of the iceberg." Blink replied, "Melting of the iceberg? But how?" Mom replied, "Yes, the iceberg is melting due to global warming." Blink asked, "What is global warming, Mom?" Mom said, "Global warming is like when the Earth gets too hot because of things humans do. When they burn things like coal, oil, and gas for energy, it releases something called 'greenhouse gases' into the air. These gases trap heat from the sun, acting like a big blanket around the Earth. Over time, this makes the Earth warmer, which can cause lots of problems like melting ice, rising sea levels, and changes in weather." While Blink and his mom were discussing, his dad entered and overheard the conversation. Blink noticed his dad and became curious to learn more about how global warming poses a danger to their livelihood. His dad calmed them down, saying that even if the ice is melting, it is a problem that has a solution. Blink asked, "What solution, Dad?" His dad replied, "Humans can help with that." Blink said, "How? What is the solution to this?" His dad said, " Save energy by turning off lights and appliances when not in use. Use less plastic to reduce greenhouse gases from its production. Plant trees to absorb carbon dioxide from the air. Recycle paper, glass, and metal to reduce energy needed for making new things. These simple actions done by humans can help protect our planet and stop the ice from melting." Blink and his mom breathed a sigh of relief, hoping that humans wouldn't let their home, the iceberg, melt. Blink said, "Humans need to stop global warming to prevent further damage to the Earth's climate and melting of ice."
author: Ruth D'silva

title: The Best Moments
text: A long time ago, there was a boy named Ray who was loved by all his teachers and classmates at school. He was good at studies as well as other school activities. One day during the recess, Ray was sitting among in friends while they were having their lunch. Subi asked, 'Ray, what are you going to do after school today?' 'I am going to go for piano classes and then I will go swimming class.' said Ray. 'Do you not get tired from all of these classes and studying?' asked Kia. Ray said, 'No, I don't' Subi said with fatigued voice, 'I would have no energy for all of this. I need to play with my friends to recharge from all the homework and studies.' 'I am too tired to get out of my bed for any other activities.' replied Kia. Ray said with concern, 'Are you not worried about your grades and about what you want to become in life?' Subi replied, 'No. Because I want to just enjoy my time with my friends and have sweet memories to cherish later.' 'Yes, I too agree with Subi', said Kia, 'The moment we step out of school things will change so fast that we will always look back at these days.' Subi, 'Ray, it is good that you are part of so many activities and you have different skills and talents. But my friend, enjoy this time of your life. Live in the present because "time once gone, never comes back", so cherish every moment.' Ray, 'You do have a point Subi. But what if my grades drop in the next exam?' Kia, 'What is destined to happen, will eventually happen. Remember to live life to the fullest and do the things that make to happy and not worried.' Subi said, 'Yes! We must study as well as play and spend time with our loved ones.' Ray, 'I am so lucky to have friends like you! I suggest we meet at my house this Friday after school for some board games. Will you both come?' 'Of course we will!' said Kia. The bell rang and the children quickly moved towards their classroom.

title: An Adventurous Day
text: Once there were three best friends playing outside their huts. Suddenly a bright light came towards them them. They closed their eyes. When they opened their eyes they found themselves inside a forest. They were so confused. They were hiding behind a tree. They were also so surprised that when they were playing outside the huts it was morning but inside the forest it was night. They were coming inside the forest. It was so dark. The parents of the children were so worried about them. They called the police to find the three girls. They found that the bright light led them to the forest. Also, some of the villagers helped them to find those girls. The three girls found a cave to stay for the night. They were very scared because they heard the voices of wild animals. But they had no other option than staying there for the night. They were so scared because it was dark inside the cave. They were also hungry but there was nothing to eat. Morning inside the forest the three besties were walking in the path way. Then suddenly they heard rushing water.They were happy because they finally found food. They were happy and ran on the way where the sound came. They found a big river. They held hands and ran together as fast as they could. They first drank some water and washed their faces. They felt much better than yesterday. They also started to play inside the river. They were enjoying the day together. The police and the villagers were trying their best to find the three girls. For some time they were resting inside the same cave where they slept yesterday night. They started to worry about their parents. The three besties woke up in the evening and went to play in the river. So they went there to play. They were also walking on the sand talking to each other. They were bored so they climbed up a tree to see the view. They were holding the branches of the tree. When they looked down they saw many fireflies flying. So they came down to see those. They saw them and they were so happy. The light coming from them was a little bright. They also touched them. One girl was also counting the stars on the sky. They went back and climbed the tree and suddenly someone touched them. They were scared and looked down, it was their parents. They were happy to see their parents. They came down from the tree to hug them. They hugged them and told the whole story about how they survived. Everyone were proud of them because they were brave survived for one day. They were also hungry so they went home and ate. The three besties lived a happy life from then on......
author: Harshini Thiagarajan

title: The Family Picnic
text: It was a bright summer morning. Mini woke up excited and happy as she and her family were going to leave for their annual picnic today along with some of her cousins. After getting ready in her new dress, Mini and her brother sat at the table with their parents to eat breakfast. They had a delicious meal of omelette, bread and milk. Once they were done with breakfast, Mini's mother began packing food and clothes they might need for the picnic. She packed a few sandwiches, five bananas and juice. Soon, they left for the picnic. On the way, Mini observed the beautiful scenery of the open fields, the cows grazing and enjoyed the cool wind as they drove by. Mini and her family were the last to arrive at the picnic. They met with all her cousins and they all greeted one another. Full of excitement, Mini and her cousins set out play games. Tired from playing all afternoon, each one of them was hungry and they returned to their parents to eat snacks and rest for sometime. After resting, Mini and her cousins changed into their swimming costumes and went to enjoy the cool water of the nearby pond. In the evening, after enjoying themselves thoroughly, Mini bid goodbye to her cousins and they all returned to their homes from the picnic. Once Mini was back home, she quickly brushed her teeth and got ready for bed. In her bed, she fell fast asleep dreaming about the next family picnic..

title: Chandra discovers 'Ugadhi Pachadi'
text: Little Chandra is playing with her new radium ball on the verandah. She hit the ball too hard. It bounced into the house and disappeared. She went in search of it. She looked under the table. "Chandra, don't touch the coconuts. They are for Ugadhi Pachadi." Grandfather said. She searched for it on the table. "Chandra, don't touch the bananas. They are for Ugadhi Pachadi." Father said. She looked for the ball in the basket next. "Chandra, don't touch the mangoes. They are for Ugadhi Pachadi." Mother said. She went to her grandmother. "Did you see my ball come this way, Grandma?" she asked. "No dear, I didn't." "Why don't you have some jaggery powder while you search for it?" " It's for Ugadhi Pachadi tomorrow." Just then her sister returned home with a small bag. She tried to search the bag for her ball. "This bag contains neem blossoms for Ugadi Pachadi", she said. Chandra is confused. "How many ingredients are needed for Ugadi Pachadi?" she wondered. "And what would it taste like with so many ingredients?", she thought. That very moment, Mother said, " I can't find the tamarind jar. I need it for tomorrow. Chandra dear, could you please help me find it while searching for your ball? Chandra is curious about the Ugadhi pachadi. So she set to work and searched every corner of the house. And she found the jar and her radium ball hiding behind the big bag of rice. The next morning, Chandra was dressed in her new Pattu Parikini* for Ugadhi, eager to taste Ugadhi Pachadi. She took a a mouthful of it and.... * Pattu Parikini - A dress with a longskirt and blouse made of silks worn by girls during special occasions, more prominently in South India....all the six delicious flavors of food exploded in her mouth.
author: Vasudha Rani Vejandla

title: The Magical Garden
text: Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little girl named Elle. She loved spending time outdoors, especially in her grandmother's garden. Elle's grandmother had the most magical garden in the village. Every flower, every tree, and every bush seemed to have a story of its own. One sunny morning, while exploring the garden, Elle stumbled upon a tiny door hidden behind a rose bush. Curious, she opened it and stepped inside. To her amazement, she found herself in a magical world filled with talking animals, sparkling streams, and colorful flowers that danced to the rhythm of the wind. Elle spend hours playing with the animals and exploring every corner of the enchanted garden. From that day on, Elle visited the magical garden every day after school. She would listen to the stories of the wise old owl, dance with the playful squirrels, and help the busy bees collect honey. As time passed, Elle grew older, but her love for the garden never faded. Eventually, she became the guardian of the magical garden, ensuring that its beauty and wonder would be preserved f or generations to come. And so, the magical garden remained a cherished secret, known only to those who believed in the power of imagination and the magic of nature.

title: A Riddle a day
text: Long time ago in the far away land of Trickland there was a small town named Tinsel. There were lush green trees and small houses. The people in the village were intelligent, loving but conservative. The people living here were very intelligent and generally spoke in riddles and this made it very difficult for other people who did not belong to the village to understand what they spoke. There were several travellers who came from far and wide to visit this village to witness the wisdom of these people. However no one could ever decipher the way the villagers spoke. The villagers were very proud that they were something different than others. Once there came a traveller who visited this town and was astonished by the way they spoke. He admired their intellect and wit. However, just like the other travellers he too was not able to understand whatever they were speaking because of their manner of speaking. He felt very sad and rejected because he couldn't get involved in the villagers jokes. He was then determined upon learning the different riddles and enriching his knowledge. He was determined that come what may he would learn the way they speak. In the beginning the villagers were hesitant about teaching him several riddles, however after observing his consistent efforts they were amazed by his determination to be a part amongst them and to join them in their jokes and daily conversation. Slowly the villagers began teaching him several techniques to form different riddles and through that he understood that wit and wisdom are not extraordinary virtues but can be attained even through daily conversation. As time passed the traveller became more fluent with his riddles and his knowledge about various things improved. He also learnt to view things through different viewpoints. He was very happy and content. Through this story we understand that language is not the only requirement for communicating with a person but there should also be a common understanding among people to understand each other better. We can also learn that by persistence and consistence one can achieve any goal in life however small or big it may be.

title: Language across borders
text: In a faraway land somewhere around the Venice of the Gulf, lived a girl named Sophie. In a faraway land somewhere around the Venice of the Gulf, lived a girl named Sophie. She was a journalist and she often dealt with the Historical column of the Taaza Khabar newspaper. It was winter and Christmas was just two days away. It was winter and Christmas was just two days away. One day as usual, Sophie boarded her metro train heading towards her workplace. However, she noticed something very different. She saw a group of people speaking a strange language that she had never heard all these years. They seemed to be Indians but they weren’t speaking Hindi. She knew a little bit of Hindi as she had struck conversations with many Indians in her workplace. Sophie knew a little bit of Hindi as she had struck conversations with many Indians in her workplace. Being a curious person, she decided to approach these people. She greeted them saying, “ Namaste, kya mai aapki koi madad kar sakti hoon? ” One of the younger boy said, “ Namaste ”. Since Sophie was also to get off at the same metro station, she asked the young boy what his name was and inquired about which language the rest of the group was speaking in. The young boy responded saying, Sophie was taken back as she was aware that many dialects have become extinct over the years as well as the importance of several regional languages are dwindling which in turn impacts the age-old heritage of one’s country. Sophie, in order to make Ved aware about the importance of languages said, Ved, it’s really nice to hear them speak in their native languages. Although English is important to acquire jobs, you should also follow their footsteps by speaking in your regional language. In this way, you can contribute towards preserving the rich heritage of your culture. Ved gave Sophie a blind stare at first because Sophie was a modern and up-to-date woman conversing in English and not having any Indian roots but yet, she recommended him to speak in his regional language. Ved gave Sophie a blind stare at first because she was a modern and up-to-date woman conversing in English and not having any Indian roots but yet, she recommended him to speak in his regional language. However, Sophie had good knowledge about Indian languages as she had carried out research on the regional languages of India during her initial years in the Journalism industry. She told Ved that English has indeed gained a lot of importance but it is also important to know one’s own mother tongue as well as the regional language of the region where a person resides as it helps an individual to understand their culture and traditions. Not only that but it also fosters cognitive growth. Ved responded, “ I see you have a point but in what way could I preserve my regional language? ” Hence, Sophie put forth many constructive ways. She said, “ I hope you are aware that the New Education Policy, 2020 that is to be implemented in India aims at imparting education in regional languages. This move also focuses on preserving regional languages and ensuring that students are familiar with their mother tongue. ” Since Ved wasn’t aware about the incorporation of regional languages in the educational curriculum, he stated, “ Oh….Wow such a progressive move indeed! So you mean multilingualism? ” In agreement to him, she nodded her head. After pondering for a while on what Sophie had just said, Ved with amazement replied, “ Sophie indeed these are such wonderful ways of keeping one's culture alive even in our modern world. I didn’t realize that by doing little, I can help my community preserve its cultural roots and also play an active role in handing it over to future generations. Thank you so much for opening my eyes. ” That day, Sophie had a wonderful experience and began writing an article about the preservation of regional languages and how they make society more inclusive as well as lead to the preservation of one’s rich cultural heritage. It also included various ways that one could adopt to develop their linguistic skills and knowledge in their respective regional languages. Her happiness knew no bounds as she was very glad on helping Ved take up a constructive step towards safeguarding his rich linguistic heritage amidst the tide of modernization.

title: Let's learn about calamities
text: Seema was surprised, by the torrential rains and the turbulent flowing of the river. She told Sia " The rain does not seem to cease, How will we play in the garden? We may get drenched if we try to.. " " rain rain,go away, come again another day, Seema and Sia want to play Rain, Rain GO AWAY!!" chanted Seema sadly. Just then Seema heard a crashing thunder and bright lightning hit the ground. The electricity went off!! Seema couldn't see a thing. She only heard Lachu paati and Raju at a distance. " Be careful Raju; the rain doesn't seem to cease. Don't follow me, I'll go and get some kerosene for the lamp. " Raju got startled by his own flashlight he went, "Ooooh!! that was scary Grandma, I almost thought there was a ghost." " Raju, I think there is going to be a heavy downpour. That may even cause a flood." said grandma. "A FLOOD!!! " what is that grandma. " Do You know, A flood is a frequently occurring natural disaster in most parts of the world, due to excessive and untimely rains in the same place, a river overflows its banks causing floods" " You mean the ADAYAR river may overflow!! " exclaimed Raju. As grandma took him to Seema's house with each step Raju became excited to know what happens during a flood. "Paati you said that flood is a natural disaster, are there any other forms of disasters." ''Yes Raju, those are called manmade disasters, you remember Revathi Aunty's house caught a fire last month you remember why that happened?" a sked grandma borrowing a coconut. " Aunty left the stove on and went for Girish Anna's wedding" he said. "My boy this is a calamity caused by humans,so what do you call that? " He exclaimed " A MANMADE DISASTER " " Does Rinku the spider like heavy rains? do they get washed away in floods " asked Raju. " Does 'Rinku the spider 'like the rains, does he get washed away in the floods? " Raju asked. 'I'm sure he doesn't like rain, and he may get washed by the floods " replied Grandma grinning. "But you know what he will definitely do. He would anchor himself to any leaf or branch well attached to the tree. You may also do the same in times of crisis." Just as they were speaking the downpour got worse and the river broke out. " Grandma what do u mean by a crisis? I'm scared!" screamed Raju. " There is nothing to be scared of Raju, Do you know 90 % of the natural disaster occurring in the United States of America involves some sort of flooding " said grandma calmly. "There are few steps that we need to follow before, during and after floods. First let us switch the radio on and assess the risks and warnings." As they were speaking Shiva's Appa put the community radio on. ' A FLASH FLOOD IS INCOMING IN FLOOD PRONE ZONES AND OTHER ZONES AS WELL. RESIDENTS ARE REQUESTED TO MOVE TO A HIGH GROUND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. REQUESTING PEOPLE AROUND ADAYAR RIVER TO BE SAFE TILL ASSISTANCE COMES YOUR WAY CALL THE NATIONAL DISASTER MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY VOLUNTEERS A THE HELPLINE NUMBER - 011-1078. " Everyone in the neighboring area started running towards the high point of the village. Seema was worried as their house was also in a flood prone zone. Soon, the flood broke into Seema's house; Raju and Seema were terrified. Grandma instructed Seema's mother to collect the non-perishables and switch off all the electrical appliances in the house and asked Raju and Seema to stay close to them on a higher platform. Everyone in the village left their houses. And so did Seema's family, Grandma and Raju. As they were moving out Seema got anxious and scared, she clinged onto Grandpa and kept asking Amma questions. "AMMA, is'nt this dangerous?" " It is Seema do u know even today in Mumbai people shudder at the memory of JULY 2005. When many people lost their lives in the deluge caused by heavy rains " her mother replied. "So people lose their lives during floods?" exclaimed Seema. " Yes dear it is dangerous! People lose their lives, property and even their beloved livestocks too during these events." ﻿Amma replied. " Are Giddu and Minnu safe? " Seema asked about her baby goats. Appa said, " I left them with Shiva's Appa at his terrace with his other animals,They are alright, need not worry about them. " Within a very short span of time the area looked like a lake. Seema observed everything as they were moving through the waters. They even saw people travelling in boats. "Thatha I dropped Sia!!" Seema started to cry and whine trying to get Sia back. Just then She met the assistance that was provided by the Disaster Management authority. "Who are they Appa? They have Sia with them " asked Seema." They are volunteers from the disaster management cell, helping and supporting each other in these times is our moral responsibility " said Appa. With their help they were all moved to safety. "Why are you loitering around on your own" scolded Amma. " I was only trying to look at the boats, Amma." said Seema. "You were walking around the foot of the mountain, it is not safe; there are chances of landslide due to the heavy rains." said Amma. " A landslide, what is that now!? " asked Seema. " Yes child, a landslide may occur and wash off the soil from the foot of the mountains and other high places." said Thatha. AT THE RESCUE CAMP.... " Thatha can we not play or go back home,I don't want to stay here, " said Seema unhappily. Thatha decided to indulge her in an activity. He gave her a paper and asked her to collect what would each one in the camp do to stop the calamity. " This seems interesting I can do that, could I have your pen too? " asked Seema. " You may go,but be safe and take care of yourself. "Thatha said with delight. "Appa how will you stop the floods?" Seema asked curiously. To this Appa answered "It is not for us to stop the floods Seema, it happens during a cloudburst,We can only prevent it. " " A Cloudburst! is that a disaster too? " asked Seema. "Yes,it is. Sometimes the water coming down from clouds does not reach the land in the form of rains. Instead due to high temperature near the land, it vaporizes and goes back to the cloud which results in a heavy downpour " said Appa. "Appa, now I don't like rains we can't go out and play. Minnu is afraid of the loud thunders; Amma asks me to stay indoors and do my homework instead!" asked Seema. "We can do nothing about it,last year when you didn't get Mangoes to eat how did you feel? " asked Appa. " I felt bad,Thatha said it happened because of a Drought " said Seema. "A drought is caused because of the lack of rain Seema, a drought for a long period leads to a famine." " A drought is caused by no rains!! No rains means no mangoes. Let there be a lot of rain so I can have a lot of mangoes!" said Seema. "We had extreme downpour this year and what happened because of that Seema?" asked Appa. "A FLOOD" said Seema. "This may also lead to a famine; did you notice how our trees are? " asked Appa. "They are submerged inside the water." said Seema. "You are right, the flood might wash away all your mangoes " said Appa. Seema gasped as she didn't want her mangoes to go. " What can be done to prevent all this from happening Appa? " asked Seema anxiously. "To prevent floods the Government has established the'National Flood Commission' which takes special efforts towards the control of the flood." said Appa. "So what do they do for us Appa, do they save our mangoes?" Seema asked Appa, "They can't save our mangoes or animals Seema but they help us by establishing rescue zones during floods and by building Dams. They try to connect rivers which helps to prevent the floods " said Appa. After the conversation,Seema began to worry; wanting to go and visit her friend Reema in the neighboring camp. But Seema's father was afraid about her safety.. Though upset, Seema understood that it was not safe and found Ravi uncle helping repair the boats. "Uncle, have you experienced a natural disaster before?" asked Seema curiously. " Yes, Seema I have, but why do you ask about it?" asked Ravi uncle. "Appa and Lachu paati told me about various disasters; What disaster have you experienced uncle? asked Seema. " Before that may I know What disasters do you know about Seema?" " Appa told me that floods happen due to a cloudburst, but we cant avoid it because otherwise all the mangoes would be gone; leading to a famine " said Seema. Ravi uncle explained " You are right Seema, We cant avoid Rains but do you know that cloudbursts these days are not at all natural " "S o are they manmade too?" gasped Seema. " They are! " said uncle Ravi frowning. "It happens due to the excessive cutting of trees and pollution caused by us; humans. " said uncle Ravi. "Can we do something about it?" asked Seema. " We can definitely try to avoid excessive cutting of trees, protect and plant more tees; try to adopt more efficient waste management techniques to reduce pollution " said uncle Ravi. Later during the day the people started noticing that the rain had stopped and there was a beam of sunlight reaching the ground; ' Mackerel sky, mackerel sky, never long wet, never long dry.' said Lachu Paati as everyone took a sigh of relief. Within some time the floods subsided,and everything came back to normal. Seema, looked back at all she had learned in the time of crisis and decided to do her best to plant more trees and try to educate everyone about the various effects of these calamities. ﻿ AFTER FEW DAYS...
