title: Lets Be Hygienic!
text: Living a hygienic life involves maintaining cleanliness in various aspects of daily living to promote good health and prevent the spread of illness. Educating ourselves and others about the importance of hygiene is key to making informed choices about our diet and lifestyle. So let us see a story why is hygienic life so important. In the vibrant town of Green Grove, where the streets were lined with colorful flowers and the air was always fresh and clean,there lived a young girl named Riya. Riya was a adventurous girl,known for her love for exploring the nature's beauty and outdoor. She was helpful and caring toward others. She was up to date,responsible sensible girl and hygienic girl. On the other hand in the vibrant town of Green Grove,there lived another young girl named Tania who was lazy,irresponsible careless and unhygienic. Riya and Tania were school friends.They used to go to school together and spend most of the time together. Though they were bestfriend, they were opposite in nature. Riya was more matured than Tania.She was aware of Tania's unhygienic and careless nature.She used to tell her always to improve her daily habits but Tania didn't show much interest in such topics. It was the day of final examination. Riya and Tania were all set to appear for the exams. Riya had reached the school and was waiting for Tania before entering the class. The bell rang but still Tania had not come. Riya was worried but she couldn't do anyting. As soon the exam got over, Riya rushed at Tania's place to see what was the matter. As she reached her place,she saw Tania sleeping on bed and crying. She asked her why didn't she come for the exam. Tania told her that she was not feeling unwell, so she had visited a doctor and her reports were bad as she had stomach infection which led to severe stomach pain and she wasn't sure why. Riya understood that Tania's poor eating habits and unhygienic habits might be the cause for her illness. She knew about Tania's unhygienic habits. She told her that the it was because of her carelessness. Tania used to sometimes forget to brush her teeth after food or before going to bed,even she used to often forget to wash her hands before eating.She also used to eat most of the time junk food and eat less home cooked good. Tania was guilty as she understood that if she would have listen to Riya she wouldn't have fall sick and miss her exams. Riya decided to help her and teach Tania about the importance of good hygienic practices and healthy balanced diet.She explained Tania the importance of washing hands regularly before and after food as it will prevent germs and bacteria entering the stomach. She also told her the need to brush teeth twice a day to maintain oral health. She even told her to stop eating outside food and start eating healthy food cooked in her house especially green vegetables. Listening to Riya's advices,Tania decided to follow the steps and adopt healthier hygiene habits. Riya decided to gift a hygiene kit for Tania which included toothpaste,toothbrush and colorful soaps.She also made a chart for Tania so that she can track her daily hygiene habits.Tania started washing her hands before and after her meal,she began to brush twice a day. She also began to eat green veggies regularly. She followed this practices daily without skipping and doing it regularly for a month. After a month she visited the doctor again and this time her reports were pretty good without any infection.Tania was very happy as her stomach pain was disappear and her health improved and she felt more happy and energetic.Tania thanked Riya for her kindness and knowledge. They both decided to spread the awareness of hygiene to others in town and to make everyone understand the importance of healthy and balanced diet. They both together visited schools and community centres to teach children and adults the importance of hygienic life. The organized campaign to spread awareness of a good hygiene. People of all ages understood the importance of hygienic life and soon their efforts paid off and people started adopting hygienic habits which henceforth lead to decrease in illness and increase in overall well-being. Riya and Tania were super happy to see that how a small act of education and kindness can have a big impact on a community's health. Good hygiene and good health boots self-esteem and confidence by making individuals feel clean,fresh and improving mental well-being.Overall, maintaining good hygiene and proper balanced diet is essential for protecting your health,preventing the spread of disease and promoting a clean and healthy environment for yourself and others.

title: The Echoes Of Freedom 1857
text: Once upon a time, in the heart of a bustling city, lived a young girl named Aisha. She loved to listen to the stories from her grandfather, who often shared tales of India's struggle for independence. One evening, as they sat together under the old banyan tree in their backyard, Aisha's grandfather began to recount a particularly poignant story, The freedom Struggle of 1857. He spoke of a time when India was under the grip of colonial rule, oppressed and shackled by foreign powers. He narrated the sacrifices made by brave men and women who dared to dream of a free India, despite the odds stacked against them. Aisha listened intently, her heart swelling with pride and admiration for those who had fought for their country's freedom. But as the story unfolded, she couldn't help but feel a sense of sadness and despair. "The village system shifted. Landownership changed, creating instability. Farmers felt insecure." said dada. "Why did they have to suffer so much, Dada?" Aisha asked, her voice tinged with emotion. " Not just that dear, Taxes burdened farmers, collapsing agriculture. Local industries suffered too, handicrafts ruined, artists unemployed." said Dada with a heavy heart. "That sounds horrific Dada", said Aisha worried. "It indeed was Aisha! Do you know the British meddled with our culture, traditions even the temples desecrated and sacred beliefs dismissed." said dada. "That was truly unfair! If I would have born than, I would have never taken that" said Aisha angrily. "Easy for you to say my dear" said dada smiling. "Why didn’t we have any soldiers dada, why was it so difficult for them?" asked Aisha curiously. "My dear, everything was under the control of the britishers. Sepoys were ill-treated and given low status. They were paid less than the British soldiers. Their allowance slashed." " That’s so messed up!", said Aisha angrily. "Yes dear not just that, In 1856 the British issued Enfield rifles. News spread that cartridges greased with cow and pig fat by which Religious sentiments of Hindus and Muslims were hurt". "Was there a time were we tried to win freedom before 1947?" asked Aisha. "Yes dear, there were constant struggle that took place. Once our Brave soldiers captured Delhi, yet couldn't retain it due to limited supplies and no tactics. The struggle shook British rule. The East India Company dissolved. The Crown took direct control through the Government of India Act 1858," said dada. We were so close, weren't we? asked Aisha sadly. Her grandfather smiled gently and replied, "Their struggle may have been arduous, but it was not in vain, my dear. Through their courage and determination, they paved the way for a brighter future for generations to come." He went on to explain how the echoes of their sacrifices still resonated today, reminding every citizen of the importance of unity, resilience, and freedom. As Aisha listened to her grandfather's words, she felt a newfound sense of purpose stirring within her. Inspired by the stories of India's heroes, she vowed to uphold their legacy and contribute to the progress and prosperity of her beloved nation. And so, under the shade of the old banyan tree, amidst the echoes of freedom's call, Aisha embarked on her own journey—a journey fueled by hope, fueled by courage, and fueled by the unwavering belief that a better tomorrow was within reach. For in the tapestry of India's struggle, woven with threads of sacrifice and perseverance, lay the blueprint for a future where every dream could take flight, and every heart could soar free. Here's a fun crossword for you to solve. All The Best! Let's put your knowledge to test: (Umaji Naik, War of Independence, Lord Dalhousie, Secretary of State, Tatya Tope) (1) V.D.Savarkar named the struggle of 1857 as............ (2)............ united the Ramoshis to rebel against the British. (3) After the struggle of 1857 the post of............ was created in the British Government to look after the affairs of India. (4)............ was the Governor General who annexed the princely states. Let's check your answers: 1. War of Independence. 2. Umaji Naik. 3. Secretary of State. 4. Lord D alhousie. Good to see you here at the very end. To gain more knowledge about the freedom struggle, there are 2 projects assigned: (1) Search for the book written by V.D. Savarkar entitled ‘The Indian War of Independence 1857’ and read it. (2) On an outline map of India indicate the regions where the freedom struggle of 1857 took place.

title: The Jungle Story.
text: Once upon a time, in the area of a jungle, there lived a wise and majestic Eagle. He flew high above the huge trees, but despite his power, he longed for companionship. The Eagle chose a clever jackal as his adviser, a Deer as his protector, and a wise Owl as his messenger. In return for their loyalty, he promised them food and shelter. One scorching day, as the sun beat down relentlessly, the Eagle expressed a curious desire. "I have heard tales of the taste of Camel meat," he mused, "but I have never had the pleasure of sampling it." Intrigued by the idea, the jackal suggested they embark on a journey to find a camel. Guided by the owl's sharp eyes, they set out into the vast expanse of the desert at night. As they journeyed, the night passed and it was the next morning,heat became unbearable. The Deer not used to such harsh conditions, struggled to keep up, and the Eagle grew tired. So the Eagle suggested to return back to the forest. The Eagle's advisers were frightened because they did not know the way back home. The Deer wanted to run away. The Owl wanted to eat the lion later on. But the clever Jackal thought of a plan and ran off into the desert saying he would bring help. The Jackal soon found the camel and said that their king wanted him. The surprised camel asked who this king was. The Jackal said that, the Eagle had killed the camel’s master. So, he was free and the Eagle had invited him to live at his court. The camel agreed to serve the Eagle in return for a home at his court. The Eagle, the Jackal and the Deer jumped on to the camel’s back to get back to the forest. The Owl flew ahead as their guide. They were all tired and hungry when they reached the forest. The courtiers looked at the camel with hungry smiles because they wanted to feast on it. But the Eagle called the camel to him and said, he wanted to thank him for saving his life. The Eagle was hungry, so he told his courtiers to bring him food. However, the courtiers planned to make the camel ask to be eaten instead. They went back to the king and offered themselves as his meal. The camel listened to their offers and thought he must do the same. He offered his life to the Eagle and said he should eat him instead of his old friends. This was what the others had been waiting for. They prepared to attack the camel but the Eagle stopped them. The Eagle said that he had been touched by their offers and would eat them in order. The Deer, the Owl and the Jackal were shocked and ran away. The Eagle laughed and told the camel that he had been loyal and good. So, he would be his friend and provide him home in his court. The camel was happy and grateful. The Eagle thought to himself that it was good to be king, but it was better to be kind.

title: Sandy's Sacrificial Courage
text: Once upon a time, in a noisy hustling city name Macaria. There lived a spirit filled dog with great joy and love within him called Sandy. His Black textured fur sparking under the glowing sun and his eyes full of innocence was undoubtedly loved by everyone around him. Every single day Sandy's boundless energy of joy with each individual in the society never stopped his this nature to be unloved by people. He would sit beside elderly, play along with the little kids and greet every passerby with his cute little wagging tail along with a joyful bark. But suddenly, one fine day Sandy was missing and wasn't to be seen as usual in the society. Immense tension and worry emerged among the people in the society. Many of them went asking about around the area trying to find out if anyone notice Sandy going out anywhere. This created a greater tension among the people especially children and the elderly because there was no news about him and they were quite attached to Sandy and his presence. Finally few hours later few of the members of the society reported Sandy's missing case in the police station. After filing the report investigation began, where almost all the members of the society were called in to be questioned by the police. The CCTV camera were also checked in detail along with outsiders being questioned too, with all the inquiry that took place, Police got to know that Sandy was seen moving out of the gate around 4:30 am in the morning. And also that Sandy wasn't legally a pet to anyone in the society nor was adopted by the society. Few days later, a news spread across where people were heard speaking about a dogs death that took place around few kilometers away from the main city. While the news began to spread widely, one of the elderly from Sandy's society overheard this news from a passerby near her, Finally to confirm the news about the rumor some of the elderly of the society and the society secretary of the building together reached the police station to inquire about the news heard, where police and its team went in depth to confirm the given information which concluded that the dog which died was Sandy himself. According to the police source, information that was confirmed and collected by the police team was that Sandy's death took place in a unexpected event. In which Sandy got killed unexpectedly saving a little girls life from an accident underneath a truck, where Sandy took up a courageous step to save that little girl and sacrificed his life. After knowing the news about Sandy kids and elderly were extremely sad but yet proud od Sandy for his courageous act. Hence they decided to not mourn about his death rather remember Sandy in their memories throughout their life.

title: The Childhood of Shivaji Maharaj
text: In the tranquil hills of Maharashtra, amidst the whispers of the winds and the rustle of the trees, a young boy named Shivaji spent his days exploring the rugged terrain of his homeland. Born into the Bhosle clan, he was destined for greatness, yet his childhood was steeped in simplicity and adventure. From an early age, Shivaji displayed a spirit of courage and curiosity. He would roam the forests with his companions, learning the ways of the land and the secrets it held. His keen eyes and sharp mind absorbed the teachings of his mother, Jijabai, who instilled in him the values of honor, integrity, and love for his people. But it wasn't all play and exploration. Even as a child, Shivaji was aware of the challenges facing his people under the oppressive rule of the Mughal Empire. He listened intently to the tales of valor and resistance told by the elders, his heart swelling with the desire to one day liberate his homeland from tyranny. As he grew, so did his sense of responsibility. He trained rigorously in the arts of warfare and governance, honing his skills for the battles that lay ahead. Yet, amidst the preparations for the future, he never forgot the joys of his youth – the laughter of his friends, the beauty of the natural world, and the warmth of his family's love. And so, in the quiet moments between his lessons and his adventures, Shivaji dreamed of a better tomorrow for his people. Little did he know that his childhood days of exploration and discovery would one day shape the destiny of an empire, and inspire generations to come with tales of courage, resilience, and the unwavering spirit of a young boy who dared to dream of freedom.

title: Never Giving up is the Key to Success
text: There were going to conduct sports in Reema's school. Before even participating Reema started loosing her confidence, by thinking that she won't won in the sports and started giving up. As she was sitting in the corner of her room, Mommy asked her "Reema what happen why you seems to be so sad"? Mommy, there going to be held sports day in the school, says Reema Wow! Then there will be so much of fun in the school says her Mommy. No Mommy, I won't be participating because I know that i am not good at sports. Why? My dear Why do you think that you won't won before even trying? You should always think positive that, "I CAN AND I WILL" it motivates you to reach your goals. And on the other hand my dear, we should not always participate to win rather we should always think that, "No matter if I win, but I will participate for my happiness". Yes Mommy, You are absolutely right! "Sorry Mommy that I was giving up before even I tried by thinking negative", says Reema No problem my dear. But don't give up on things not only on participating in sports but also in life. And always remember that, "Always keep trying and giving your best till you reach your destination". Sure Mommy! Thankyou for motivating me by your magic words. Mommy, "You are simply the best". Now don't worry and actively participate in your school sports and I know you will definitely give your best. Sports Day arrives. All the childrens along with Reema are very excited and happy to participate in various sports. Reema took participation in running race. She was very nervous as well as energetic to take a part. As the race starts, everyone started cheering Reema. Reema was 4th while running, later as the running race was about to reach the winning point, Reema came 1st while running the race. Reema started yelling "Hurry, Hurry, Hurry, I won!" After going home Reema told her Mommy, Mommy I won 1st prize in Running Competition, I am so happy. Reema remember I had told you that no matter what, 'You should never give up before even trying or giving your best' Says Mommy Yes Mommy, I will always keep this in my mind Thankyou! Love you Mommy! title: THE BUS TICKET
text: Rohit a grade seven student used to travel by bus everyday to his school. He had a habit of collecting bus tickets and keeping it in his bag. Travelling daily by bus going to and fro he had collected many tickets which he had kept in his bag. One day while washing his school bag, mother got to know that he had collected so many tickets. Curious mother wanted to ask Rohit why he had collected so many tickets and she waited for Rohit to come back from the school. Once Rohit was back mother asked him, " Rohit, why have you collected so many tickets?" and his mother showed him a pile of tickets that she had removed from his bag. Rohit was himself surprised as he didn't knew those tickets he had been collecting everyday had entirely filled his bag. He explained to his mother that collecting tickets and keeping them fascinated him. His mother looked happy but now Rohit was faced with a dilemma of what he should do with those tickets. Seeing the confusion on his face mother suggested, since you are interested in it why don't you keep it in an orderly manner and create a collection where you could keep adding onto it. when you grow older this will be an amazing childhood memory that you could look up to. Rohit became excited and decided to take his mother's opinion. Next day at school, in the history class the teacher taught them about hobbies and different collections that people have. The teacher told them, some people like to collect old coins, stamps, pictures and many more. And all of a sudden Rohit was taken aback to his ticket collection that he had made and felt happy about it. The teacher ended the class with giving them a homework to work on a collection of things that you like and to bring it to class to show it to your classmates. After hearing this Rohit's happiness had no bounds. He wanted to show his ticket collection that he had done, eagerly to his class. For the next few days he kept on adding on to his collection. On the day of presentation at school, everyone had brought different things that they had collected, some children brought some old coins that their parents had handed to them.Some brought old stamps given by their grandparents. And some children brought a collection of different cars that they had done. Finally it was Rohit's turn to present to the class and he opened his collection of bus tickets. Surprisingly it was not the reaction that he expected. Some of his classmates started laughing and giggling looking at his collection. Rohit became nervous. However his teacher was amazed to see his collection. She appreciated Rohit because his ticket collection was something that he had done on his own, with his own interest rather than depending on his parents or anyone else. The teacher came forward and explained to the students that whatever things that you have collected today, possess a great historical importance even if they are the simple bus tickets collected by Rohit. She further explained, the history that we study today or know about, the information we have is because of such sources and that we get from the past period such as collection of coins, collection of books, different ornaments, different kinds of pots, and many more. These are called the sources of history. The teacher explained, we have three different kinds of sources namely the material sources, written sources and the oral sources. These sources give us information about the different events and significant aspects of the culture. So it is very important to study these sources, before beginning with our study of history. The first is the written sources which are in the written form and help us to know about the past historical events. They also give us information about different languages, food, attire, conventions and rules of conduct for the people. Examples of written sources include biographies, autobiographies, books, newspapers, foreign accounts, travelogues etc. Next we have the material sources which are the tangible sources of history. It includes memorials, buildings, coins, forts, cave sculptures and many more. They help us understand about the culture, rulers, period, governance, personal details etc. The last type is the Oral sources. These include folk songs, myths, legend, powadas, shlokas etc. We get to know the various aspects of folk life and these sources are traditionally passed on from one generation to another. All these three sources have greatly helped us to get information and facts about history that we study today. The teacher explained, all that you have collected today is going to be an important source of history. Now students after understanding about sources, tell me which category or type does Rohit's tickets fall under? the entire class shouted, 'Material sources'. That's right the teacher exclaimed. The tickets that Rohit has collected is going to give us information about the period, type of material used, the language and script which will be an important source a hundred years later and is similar to the collection of coins and pictures. The class ended with a big smile on Rohit's face, he was happy after hearing to the teachers explanation which gave much more meaning to his collection. A crowd of students had gathered around his place to see his bus ticket collection. Going back home with his collection, Rohit was happy, he was excited to share with his mother that his simple bus ticket will be a source of history in the future. He had already started to plan of how to make these bus tickets into a huge collection which will be useful in the future.

title: Make Your Choice: The Wisdom Woods Adventure
text: You find yourself standing in the depths of the mysterious Wisdom Woods, rumored to have been a home to a magical moringa tree that grants wisdom to the one who discovers it. It's time to make your first choice as you step deeper into the forest: 1. Follow the shabby route, you encounter a fork between the road. A signpost is posting to left and right. 2. Venture off the beaten path into the unknown. Following the shabby route, you encounter a fork in the road. The signposts points in two directions: 1. Shortcut to the Magical Moringa Tree 2. A path with hidden dangers If you choose the shortcut: You arrive at the Magical Moringa Tree quickly but discover that the knowledge it offers is shallow and fleeting. Saddened, you realize and learn that true wisdom cannot be rushed. However, if you choose the other option on the signpost,: You steer through a treacherous terrain, battling challenges that test your braveness and resilience. You manage to escape from a dangerous encounter with a lion and save yourself from the dark, deep woods. Hence, you learn valuable lessons and gain a deeper insight into yourself and how you deal with unknown surroundings. As you reach the Magical Moringa Tree having battled all the difficult situations, you encounter a wizard who presents you with a tricky riddle: " It cannot be seen, cannot be felt, Cannot be heard, cannot be smelt. It lies behind stars and under hills, And empty holes it fills. It comes first and follows after, Ends life, kills laughter, What am I?" Choice 1: Darkness Choice 2: Sadness Make your wise choice- be patient and think twice! If you answer "Darkness": The wizard nods in approval and lets you approach the Magical Moringa Tree of Wisdom. Having touched its archaic bark, you experience a rushing current of knowledge flowing from within your veins, giving you the clarity and insight you need in your life! However, if you answer "Sadness": The wizard shakes his head in disapproval, having disappeared into the dark void. This makes you realize that real wisdom cannot be attained without listening, thinking clearly and understanding properly. Carrying the wisdom of the magical tree in your soul, you prepare for your return journey back through the forest. Along the way, you meet fellow travelers who, just like you, are on their venture to the Magical Moringa Tree of Wisdom, facing their own challenges. You take this opportunity to enlighten them about your newfound wisdom and help them on their paths. As you exit the Wisdom Woods, you cherish the lessons that you've learned along the way with you. You understand that true wisdom comes not from shortcuts, easy answers or quick choices but from adapting to the journey and facing all the challenges it throws upon your path with courage and resilience. And who knows? Maybe one day, you'll encounter the forest again to seek wisdom once again! So keep exploring, keep venturing. Take the long roads with life-changing experiences, rather than shortcuts with shallow experiences!
author: Criselle Gonsalves

title: How Do I Feel
text: Everyday I walk to school with her. Today we have a History exam. I ask Ritu many questions. " "Pranam, my name is Ankita. I am in grade eight. My friend in school is Ritu. She always helps me. I feel happy and loved when I am with her. " When we reach school, the bell rings. ‘Tunnn Tunnn Tunn’ How will I remember so many dates? I’m worried but I close my books and run to class. " " During the exam, I write two long answers but I forget the date of First War of Independence. I think and think but I can’t remember. Was it 1847? Was it 1857? Was it 1897? " " Just then Rana Sir switches on the fan. Ritu’s answer sheet falls on the floor. I look at it by mistake. I see that she has underlined 1857. " ‘Two more minutes left’, says Rana Sir. ‘Tick tick. Tick tick.’ I am scared I will fail. I change the date and give my paper to Rana Sir. After exams, Ritu tries to call me but I run out of class. " Oh no! What if Ritu finds out I cheated? What if I get more marks than Ritu? What if she does not want to be my friend? I am sad and scared. " " I walk home alone. When I reach home, mummy asks me how my exam was. I start crying. " ‘Wahh Wahh Wahh’ " Mummy is confused so I tell her everything. Mummy listens carefully. She smiles at me. " ‘It is okay Anku, you looked at it by mistake. If you tell Ritu yourself she will understand.’ " " In the evening I go to Ritu’s house. I tell her everything and say sorry. First, she makes a serious face. Then she smiles. ‘It is alright Anku, it was a mistake I understand. Do you want to tell Asma Madam?’ asks Ritu. ‘I am scared to tell her. What if she thinks I am a bad student?’ I ask. ‘Anku, Asma Madam will understand. You were scared to tell me but don’t you feel better after saying the truth?’ ‘Yes, I feel better I can be honest with Madam too. Tomorrow I will speak with her after class.’ " ‘Asma Madam, I have to tell you something.’ ‘Yes Anku, tell me,’ says Asma Madam. ‘In the History exam, I forgot one date. Rana Sir switched on the class fan and Ritu’s paper flew toward me. I saw the date on her paper and gave my answer. I feel bad about cheating. I am sorry Madam.’ ‘Anku exams are to understand your learnings to provide you the right support,’ says Asma Madam. ‘I understand ma’am, this time I also learnt to ask for help and take responsibility for my actions.’ ‘Yes, today you learned from your mistakes,’ says Asma Madam. ‘Yes Madam, this will not happen again,’ I tell Ma’am. ‘Thank you for sharing this with me, I trust you,’ says Asma Madam. I walk back home with Ritu. ‘You were right Ritu. Asma Madam understands and forgives me. Thank you for encouraging me.’ I smile and hug Ritu. What makes you experience so many feelings?
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: How Do Actions Change Me?
text: Rohan loves to cook. Today he is cooking Rajma. He packs an extra tiffin for his friend Sunil. After school, Rohan and Sunil eat rajma chawal. " Mmm mmm mmm, Rohan, this is so yummy. I feel so happy! " says Sunil. " Hehehe… Sunil, you have some chawal on your face, " says Rohan. Veer, comes to the ground. " Parnam Veer, try some rajma, Rohan made it, " says Sunil. " Hahaha... no I don’t want anything from this little boy who cooks like girls, " shouts Veer. Veer always makes fun of his height and his cooking. Rohan feels sad and leaves the ground. " Rohan are you okay? " asks Sunil. " I swim and cycle but my height does not grow. " says Rohan. " Rohan you don’t have to change how you look. Veer has to change his thoughts. " " Why can’t boys cook? " " Rohan boys can cook. Everyone from school loves Ramu chacha’s chow mein. Don’t listen to Veer, " says Sunil. ﻿" You’re right. I like how I look and everyone can cook. Veer can change his thoughts, ﻿" says Rohan. ﻿" Mmm mmm mmm, now let me finish your yummy rajma chawal ﻿." ﻿ ﻿" Hahaha… Sunil, you are the best, ﻿" says Rohan happily. Rohan and Sunil are going back home when they see Ankita, Ritu, and Soni. Ankita is trying new hairstyles on Ritu and Soni. Ritu’s hair is long Anku makes two beautiful plaits out of them. " I love these long plaits I am excited to show this to everyone! " says Ritu. Ankita has never made a hairstyle on curly hair. She is excited to try a new puff style on Soni’s hair. " Wow! This looks wonderful! " says Soni looking in the mirror. Soni wants to show this hairstyle to everyone, but as soon as she gets up, the puff falls. " Oh no Anku! Look the clip came off, " says Soni. "Let me try again, " says Anku. ﻿" Anku I want to play, I cannot play if the puff falls. Can you try this next time? ﻿" asks Soni. ﻿" Okay Soni, ﻿" says Anku sadly. Soni goes out to play. " Why could I not make the puff hairstyle? How will I become a hairstylist now? " says Anku. " No Anku. Look, you made my hair look great! " says Ritu. " But it did not work on Soni’s hair. I should be able to style everyone's hair. Maybe I should not be a hairstylist, " says Anku. " Anku, this is the first time you tried a hairstyle on curly hair, right? " asks Sunil. " Yes, it is the first time. I feel so sad. I don’t want to give up my dream, " says Anku. " You don’t have to give up your dream, " says Rohan. " What should I do? " asks Anku, feeling confused. " My aunty is a hairstylist in Rishikesh she can help you, " says Ritu. " Yes, and you can try again tomorrow, " says Sunil. " You think my dream will come true? " asks Anku. " Yes, it will we all are here to help you, " says Rohan. " Thank you, everyone, I feel very loved. I will ask Ritu’s aunt and try again tomorrow, " Anku.
author: Dhyanvi Katharani

title: Life of Sant Dnyaneshwar
text: Once upon a time there was girl name Rita who lived in a small village called Shampur. Summer vacation was going on and Rita was getting boared so her mother took her to her Nani's house. Nani asked her if she wanted to hear a story. Rita said she is always ready to listen to a story. Nani said that it is a story of Sant Dnyaneshwar who was a great Sant in the Varkari movement. He wrote the Bhavartha-deepika' or Dnyaneshwari' which elucidates the meaning of the Bhagavad Geeta in Sanskrit. He also composed the 'Amrutanubhav'. He preached the importance of the path of devotion through his works and compositions. He showed a simple way of workship and conduct which the common people can follow. He never lost his calm during any situation. Rita was so happy listening to the story. She thanked her Nani and the next day she told her friends about it.
author: Jeena Bandya

title: The Adventures of Lucy- The AI Dominance_chapter 1
text: Lucy woke up. It was going to be an exciting day because she was going to witness her first sunrise that coincided with her birthday. She removed her dreamglasses from her eyes. She remembered that once upon a time people did not need dreamglasses to dream when they slept. That was so peculiar. Her head started hurting. She realized she was thinking too much and sat up. Belinda said “I sense that you are awake, Luceeliya. Would you like a smoothie this morning?” “Oh, I’ll just have my usual, Belinda, thank you,” lucy said as she was carried off in a mechanical chair to the washroom. She opened her mouth as her teeth were brushed and closed it as her face was washed by a mechanical human-like arm. She was carried to the closet room of her small quarters, and she chose to wear a pink fur coat and a skirt over her warmer. The chair hovered over to the living room and her strawberry smoothie pill was delivered. She popped the pill into her mouth and savoured the taste of it. She put on her thinking cap (literally) so she would not have any headaches thinking about anything. She generally did not think too much and if she did want to, she’d just ask Roberta or Belinda, her AI assistants about it. She lived in the Arctic, where living was now made possible. She was meeting her family for brunch that day. Most people said she had a very huge family. It was true; her mother actually had a real sister, and she herself had a son so that meant there were actually 5 members in her family. That was a lot. She said to Roberta, “it’s my birthday today and it’s also the first sunrise of the year. Can you take me to the place where I can see the sunrise most clearly?” “You are thinking too much. Don’t strain yourself,” Belinda warned. “You could see the sunrise from Mercury, Luceeliya,” Roberta suggested. “Oh, no, Roberta! I want to see the sunrise from the Arctic!” Lucy cleared. Suddenly, there was a beep in Belinda’s screen. Roberta read, “you have been invited to Feliciaki’s enlightening ceremony.” Lucy sighed. Of course it would be today. An enlightening ceremony was the day when all of the knowledge that must be known to man would be permitted into the child’s brain. It usually happened when a child was 5 years old. Belinda cut into her thoughts, “You have a call from Sillinova.” A holographic image of Sillinova appeared before lucy. “Hey Silli! How’s foreign?” “Oh, Mars is just wonderful. A bit cold, but its almost the same as the Arctic” “Oh, that’s wonderful! I’ve got a job offer at Saturn. Do you think I should accept it?” “Oh, it will be very chill there. Anyways, why think of a job at this age? You’re only 29! Enjoy your childhood days!” “I guess you’re right. I only have to worry about jobs when I’m 40. Still, I’m thinking I want to work more than just 10 years. Maybe be a… prentista and invent something new.” “I have to go, Lucy, I have a call from Sahrathik. By the way, how’s your mom?” “Oh, hard days. She’s 62, you know. She’s struggling to stay alive. It’s a miracle she survived this long.” “Well, anyways. Have you finished your dream series?” “Oh, yes I’ve been watching the littelanders for a while now, but I’ve gotten bored of it.” “Well, watch Harry Potter. It’s an old series and its quite funny and strange. My mother said it was written in the 20’s…” “That’s not very long ago…” “By 20’s, I mean the 21 st century”. “Wow that’s quite a long time ago.” “Well, I have to go, bye!” “It is time for brunch now, Luceeliya,” Belinda declared. Lucy sighed. Time flies when you’re with old friends. Luceeliya willed her mechanical chair to move towards the trancellint. She stood up with difficulty and sat in the cell like structure. There was a comfortable armchair, a t-watcher, and a lot of snacks in there. Belinda and Roberta got in after her and stood in a corner. She switched on the tw and started watching her favourite videos-how people lived in the 21 st century. She watched funny videos about something called school in the videos and watched as little children walked about with their friends and laughed at one another because one of them had a Mustache drawn on her face. “Roberta, what’s…. Skool?” “It was the old way of giving knowledge to a child.” “Oh… did it hurt? It says here that most children hate school.” “Education was not imparted in one day. It was imparted on a daily basis.” “You are thinking too much. Relax,” said Belinda. It was true. Lucy did not understand a thing. She just tried to relax and brace herself for the upcoming brunch- you just never knew what mood your mother will be in when she’s in her 60’s.
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: Eid-AL-fitr celebration
text: "Ramadan is over and Eid al-Fitr is tomorrow! I am so excited for Eid! I started the Eid day by cleaning the house. Then, I took a hot shower and wore my new clothes. We went to the Mosque for the Eid prayer, and I met my friends there! After... hmm, let me think... oh yes! I ate some delicious candy that some people gave me. After finishing the prayer, we started exchanging Eid greetings together." "My friends and I decided to go for a walk. So, I went to ask my father if I could go outside for a walk, and my father said, 'Yes, my dear, you can go.' I said, 'Thank you, Dad, I love you. Bye.' I went to my friend's house and rang the doorbell. Her eldest brother opened the door, and I asked him for my friend. But in a loud voice, he said, 'No, she doesn't want to go out,' and closed the door in my face. He is not respectful. It's true! I went home and I was sad. My father noticed and asked me, 'What happened, my dear? Why are you sad?' I said, 'No, I'm not.' My father said, 'Did someone speak to you in a bad way?' I said, 'No, Dad, nothing happened. Don't worry.' My dad said, 'Okay, dear, let's decorate Eid decorations.' Then I decorated with my dad. When I finished, I went to walk with my little brother, Adam, who is 2 years old. While walking, I met someone called Farah, who was the same age as me! We became friends and played together. Don't be surprised—I'm still a kid, 12 years old! Yeah, that's true, and this is the first story I have written. After half an hour, her mother called her, and she went home. I went to my house and watched TV. I fell asleep, so I slept. I woke up and went to play outside again with Farah. After playing, I went back home and ate a delicious dinner with my lovely family. Then we went to a playground. After that, we went home. Later, I kissed my parents' hands, and they gave me Eid money. (The first day ended)" "(THE SECOND DAY STARTED) We cleaned the house, and I put on my Eid clothes. My parents took us out. We went to a restaurant, and then we visited the museum park. After that, we went to the toy market for my little brothers and sisters. Then, we went to the mall to buy a handbag, because, of course, I was not going to buy toys. And we ate some ice cream, yum! Finally, we went home after a long day. We ate a burger, watched TV, and my parents told us to sleep. So, we went to sleep. (THE SECOND DAY ENDED)" "(TODAY IS THE THIRD AND LAST DAY OF EID) Like every day, we started by cleaning the house. Today, we had plans with my friends: Mayar, Aya, Omar, and Amir. When they came, we ate, and then we went to the garden to play 'police and crime.' We decided who would be the police, and Amir was chosen. I was the 'crime,' and guess what? I won! I was faster than him! I couldn't believe it—I won! He was frustrated and said, 'But in the end, I am the strongest.' Then I said, 'Let's see who is stronger.' So, we played a game to find out who was stronger. Everyone started using the excuse that their right hand was stronger than their left, and vice versa. Then Omar asked Amir, 'Do you have six bags?' Amir replied, 'Yeah, I have, but maybe you have six layers, not bags.' Omar said, 'No, I am just 59 kg.' Everyone started laughing. Then we heard the Adhan sound for the Al-Maghrib prayer. Everyone made Wudu, and all the boys wanted to be the Imam. I counted, and Amir was chosen as the Imam. After praying, the boys went out to play football, and the girls played UNO. Then, everyone went back to their houses, and for the second time, we cleaned the house. I took a hot shower and went to sleep. (EID DAYS WERE SO SWEET, AND EID MUBARAK TO EVERYONE.)"
author: Judy Raed alhour
illustrator: Aakanksha Mittra; Abhishek Choudhury; Nikita B

title: Little Birdy Tutu
text: One morning,I woke up and went out in my garden I saw two birds building their nest, they were continuously bringing leaves twigs branches to make the nest and working all day Finally, some days later the nest was completed, and the pair was living happily,they took care of each other. Some days later, the bird layed an egg, they took great care of the egg, the father went to search for food and the mother sat on the egg to keep it warm, and they did this turn by turn each day. Soon after, the egg hatched and out came a beautiful birdy, I named it Tutu I daily fed it seeds. One day it was raining heavily, I put a polythene above the nest to protect them from the rain. I every day, looked in the nest and took a photo of Tutu of him growing up. His parents taught him to fly, sometimes he fell off and sometimes he flies for a short time, as the time passed, he learnt to fly and flied fearlessly. So the day come the bird family went away, I was crying and missed him very much. I wish that wherever he would be he will have a good life.
author: Ayaan AR
illustrator: Julie  Smith-Belton; Aratrika Choudhury; Gouri Katdare; Hari Kumar Nair; Megan Vermaak; Priya Kuriyan; Rajiv Eipe; Samit  Shrestha

title: A boastful rabbit and a mature tortoise
text: Once upon a time, in a serene meadow nestled between rolling hills, there lived a swift and agile rabbit named Remy and a wise old tortoise named Tobias. Though they were as different as night and day, their friendship was as strong as the roots of the ancient oak tree that shaded their meadow. Remy was known throughout the meadow for his boundless energy and love for racing. He would dart and dash across the fields, leaving a trail of dust in his wake. In contrast, Tobias moved at a leisurely pace, taking each step with deliberate care and wisdom gained from many years of life One sunny day, as Remy was boasting about his speed to his friends, Tobias chuckled softly. "Speed isn't everything, my young friend," he said, his wise eyes twinkling with amusement. "There is much to be said for patience and perseverance." Remy scoffed at Tobias's words, dismissing them as the ramblings of an old tortoise. Determined to prove his superiority, Remy challenged Tobias to a race. The other animals of the meadow gathered eagerly, buzzing with excitement at the prospect of seeing the speedy rabbit face off against the slow tortoise. And so, with great fanfare, the race began. Remy shot out of the starting line like an arrow, his legs a blur as he raced ahead with confidence. Meanwhile, Tobias plodded along at his own steady pace, his wrinkled face calm and composed. As the race progressed, Remy quickly left Tobias far behind, his heart pounding with excitement at the thought of victory. But as he reached the halfway point, a sense of fatigue began to creep over him. His breath came in short gasps, and his legs felt heavy with exhaustion. Meanwhile, Tobias continued on his steady course, undeterred by Remy's lead. He knew that slow and steady wins the race, and he remained focused on the path ahead, inching closer to the finish line with each step. As the sun began to dip below the horizon, the animals of the meadow watched in amazement as Tobias crossed the finish line, his pace unwavering and determined. Moments later, Remy stumbled across the line, panting and exhausted. With a humble smile, Tobias approached his friend and placed a gentle paw on his shoulder. "You see, my dear Remy," he said softly, "sometimes the greatest victories come not from speed, but from patience and perseverance." From that day forward, Remy learned to appreciate the value of slow and steady progress, guided by the wisdom of his dear friend Tobias. And as they watched the sunset together, their friendship stronger than ever, they knew that some races are won not by rushing to the finish line, but by taking one step at a time. The moral of the story of the rabbit and the tortoise is that "slow and steady wins the race." This timeless lesson teaches us the importance of patience, perseverance, and consistency in achieving our goals. It reminds us that rushing ahead without proper planning or endurance can lead to mistakes and exhaustion, while staying focused and steadfast, even at a slower pace, ultimately brings success. Additionally, it highlights the value of humility and respecting the strengths of others, as the rabbit learns from the tortoise's wisdom and determination.
author: Atharva Kalalia

title: A mouse in the house
text: There was a mouse in the house. Grandma saw it first. “Mouse:!” she screamed as she jumped onto the couch. The flour dressing fell on the ground Where:?” the father asked, climbing up the window. He pulled the curtain. "here!" Mother screamed as she jumped on the bench. The plate fell and collapsed. Take him in your arms.” Gemini: He told Marzar. Marzar saw the mouse and hid under the bed “Mouse:!” Gemini screamed as he ran after the cat. I will surely run after him and bring him out.” Mother said boldly. She took out the wiper and beat the mouse everywhere “Mouse:! In the country behind you,” the father shouted. The mother saw the mouse and hid under the bed. “I know what to do,” Grandma said, jumping off the couch to the floor. She rolled up the magazine and beat it everywhere. Dad climbed up to an even higher window and shouted, “Mouse! “In the back country.” Grandma saw the mouse and hid under the bed. The father said softly, “Oh! nope". He couldn't go upstairs. He went downstairs and hid under the bed so that the fly could see him. The mouse is at home.” Everyone screamed. The scream that awakened the baby. She sat on the knife and rubbed it in her eyes. What was on that outfit? It has two eyes, four legs, and a hanging tail. “Mouse:.” The baby speaks happily, giving him a palm. The baby saw the mouse and the mouse followed him and took his baby. author: Saanvi Yellajosyula

title: SECRET SEVEN MYSTERY OF THEATER GHOST {CHAPTER 1}
text: It was the first Secret Seven meeting of the school holidays and Barbara had some exiting news to share with other members. As she raced down the garden towards the secret seven's shed Peter, the head of the society, appeared in the doorway, blocking her entrance. What's the password? There's no time for that now. I have some amazing news! Peter didn't say anything. He just stood there with his arms folded. You are so annoying about passwords, peter. Do you know that? said Barbara, crossing her arms too and sighing. Fine. It's Scamper. Scamper barked and jumped up, knocking the biscuit Jack had in his hand on to the shed floor. Jack rushed to pick it up before Scamper could get it and shoved it into his mouth. Colin made a face. You didn't even blow on that before you ate it! Jack shrugged and kept on chewing. I think we need to change the password, said Janet. Scamper gets too exited every time he hears it. Just then Pam rushed into the shed to join her friends, shouting, SCAMPER! Sorry I am late. Scamper gave a loud bark. Don't yell at pam! said peter. It's supposed to be a secret password. He closed the door and took out the official secret seven notebook. Now everyone is here let's start the meeting. I think Janet is right about the password. Any suggestions for a new one? Wait! let me tell you my news. They are here! Everyone looked at her blankly and she rolled her eyes. The travelling actor people I told you last week? I saw their van past just now. They're on their way towards the old theater in the town to set up their show! It's for 1 week only-and my mum says they are looking for local people to appear as extras in the play. They are holding the auditions today. Lets go! Pam jumped up. Can we go? I want to go. Peter looked annoyed. What about the meeting? You just got here and now you want to leave! And you were both late! What's the play about? asked Janet ignoring her brother. Peter had been in bad mood all morning and Janet was sure it was because he'd been given the smallest crumpet at breakfast. No idea said Barbara. But I hope it's got vampires and witches and werewolves in it. Jack laughed. Doubt it! It's probably one of those one's where they all wear big dresses and cry loads. It'll be boring. Barbara pointed her finger at Jack. I bet it's not boring. My mum said that it's a professional theater company and they usually only go to the big cities. So why are they coming to our village? asked Jack. I didn't even know we had a theater! Exactly! said Barbara. That's why they're coming. That old building with the boarded-up windows in the town used to be a theater. And my mum says someone bought it and fixed it up inside and that they've convinced the theater company to visit our village as a part of the grand opening! I'm definitely going to the audition. Anyone coming? Everyone looked at Peter. Fine said Peter closing his notebook with a THUMP. I guess all this meeting stuff will just have to wait until the next one. Janet smiled she knew that there was no way her brother would let them leave if there was was anything really important to tell them. Peter are you coming? she asked. Maybe he said, huffily. I need to clear up the snacks first. Let me help you with that said Jack, stuffing 2 biscuits into his mouth and putting the rest in his pockets. Janet grabbed her brothers hand and pulled him towards the door. But then all of a sudden Barbara said, wait. There's something else I should probably tell you. Barbara's face suddenly had become serious and she wasn't blinking. She put her hand on her chest and took a deep breath. Oh no said Pam. It's bad, isn't it? What is it Barbara? Is it your heart? Tell us. TELL US! Barbara's eyes went even wider. Yes Pam, she said. It's bad. But it's not my heart. Whose heart then? asked Pam. It's not anyone's heart. said Barbara. It's a ghost. This book is written by Enid Blyton Enid Mary Blyton was an English children's writer, whose books have been worldwide bestsellers since the 1930s, selling more than 600 million copies. Her books are still enormously popular and have been translated into ninety languages. As of June 2019, Blyton held 4th place for the most translated author. ﻿ 100 VIEWS FOR CHAPTER 2 ﻿

title: Mika and Peeku
text: Once upon a time, in a small forest, there was a friendly squirrel named Mika. Mika loved to explore the big, tall trees. One sunny day, as he ran around, he found a shiny nut. Excited, he picked it up and showed it to his friends. On his way back, he met his rabbit friend, Peeku. Peeku was sad because she lost her favourite carrot. Mika was kind. He said he would help her. He showed her the shiny nut to cheer her up. Peeku's eyes shone with joy as she thanked Mika. Together, they searched and found Peeku's carrot. She was so happy that she shared her carrot with Mika. Mika felt warm inside. He had made his friend happy. From that day on, Mika and Peeku were the best of friends. They always shared and cared for each other in the big, tall trees of the forest.
author: Radhika Misquitta

title: Brave Little Bunny
text: Once upon a time, in a cosy burrow deep in the forest, lived a little rabbit named Bunny. Bunny loved hopping around and exploring. But one day, she heard a loud noise. It was thunder! Bunny felt scared. She huddled in her burrow, shaking with fear. But then, she remembered what her mother had told her. "Thunder is just nature's way of singing a song," she said. Bunny took a deep breath and peeked outside. The thunder sounded like drums in the sky. She thought of her mother's words and felt a little braver. She hopped outside and watched the rain fall. With each clap of thunder, Bunny clapped her paws and sang along. She felt strong and brave, just like her mother. From that day on, whenever Bunny felt scared, she remembered the thunder's song and knew that she could be brave too.
author: Radhika Misquitta

title: Apu's Big Heart
text: Appu the elephant had a big, kind heart. She loved to play with her friends and explore the jungle. But one day, she felt very sad. Appu's favourite tree had fallen down in a big storm. She loved that tree and all the shade it provided. She walked through the jungle, feeling lonely and upset. Her friends noticed her looking sad and stood around her. "We're here for you, Appu," they said, hugging her tightly. Together, they found a new tree to play under. It was not as big as the old one, but it was still cozy and shady. Appu wiped away her tears and smiled. She realized that even in such a sad time, she had her friends by her side. With their love and support, Appu's heart felt light again. She knew that she could get through anything with her friends by her side.
author: Radhika Misquitta

title: Jojo the Talking Frog
text: In a muddy pond, lived Jojo, a little green frog with a special gift – he could talk! One sunny morning, Meera, a curious little girl, discovered Jojo's pond. She heard a voice and looked around, surprised to see Jojo. "Hello!" said Jojo with a big smile. Meera's eyes widened in surprise. "You can talk?" "Yes, I can! Would you like to be friends?", replied Jojo. Meera giggled with excitement. "Yes, please!" From that day on, Meera visited Jojo every day. They talked about their adventures and shared stories about their lives. Jojo taught Meera about the wonders of nature and his friends in the pond. Meera told Jojo about the world beyond the forest. Together, they explored the pond, chasing butterflies and watching the fish swim. With Jojo by her side, Meera's days were filled with laughter and friendship. And jojo was happy to have found a friend who loved him just the way he was.
author: Radhika Misquitta

title: The Dog And The Crow
text: Once upon a time there was a dog. His name was Zoro. He had a treat in his mouth. That time one crow reached there. The crow wanted that treat. The crow decided to trick him. The crow reached Zoro and said," Hello! King of Dogs." When Zoro heard this, he did not fall for that trick. He decided to make a plan. The plan is: Zoro will dig a hole, but Zoro will not put any treat in the hole. So Zoro will say like this to the crow: Did you see that hole? In that hole there is a treat. Then the crow will get tricked by Zoro. Zoro did the plan, and the plan worked. The crow reached there. And the crow said," Sorry. I tried to trick you, but you got me. Then Zoro forgave the crow. And now Zoro and the crow became friends. And they lived happily ever after. THE END.
author: Emy  Jenu
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; Kamal Narayan Yadaw; Marleen  Visser

title: Farida plans a feast
text: I Elementary Farida sets out every evening. With an empty lunchbox and a big bottle of water. The first stop, the kitchen. "Can I take some grains of rice?" Outside, a vegetable cart is set up. "How many ripe tomatoes can I take today?" The next three steps lead to a tea stall. "Will I get some broken biscuits?" Three steps further, she's at the seaside. "Is the most pungent smelling fish kept for me?" And five leaps away is the potter's shop. "Are there broken edge bowls kept for me?" Grains of rice! Ripe tomatoes! Broken biscuits! Pungent smelling fish! Bowls with broken edges! What is Farida going to feed? "Meow! Meow!" Cat's meal! "Woof! Woof!" Dog's breakfast! "Caw! Caw!" Crow's feast! "Chirp! Chirp!" Sparrow's food! The lunchbox is now completely empty......just for tomorrow! How to feed animals and birds near your houses? If you want to feed the animals around you, you need to keep a few things in mind. Are you ready to feed animals for a long time? - Find an open space away from other houses. -Try to feed at the same time every day. -Feed at the same time daily to keep the animals' feeding instincts intact. -If you want to take care of animals, take care of their health. Get them vaccinated from the nearby animal clinic. -Feeding some animals, like pigeons, monkeys, or rats, can create problems, so don't feed them. -Provide water as much as necessary, especially in the heat. Water in clay pots will remain cool. -Don't feed spicy food. -Don't feed oily, salty, sweet, or spicy food as much as possible.
author: AASTI Elementary

title: Lazy Leela
text: In a peaceful pond, lived Leela, a little fish who loved to relax all day long. She was known as Lazy Leela. While other fish swam and played, Leela floated lazily in the water, enjoying the warmth of the sun. Her friends often invited her to join them for a swim, but Leela always refused. "No, thanks. I'm too tired," she would say with a yawn. One day, as Leela was dozing off, she heard a loud splash. Curious, she peeked out from her hiding spot and saw her friends having a race. Leela felt left out. She wished he could join them and have fun too. With a quick flip of her tail, Leela swam out to join her friends! She may have been lazy, but she did not want to miss out on all the fun! From that day on, Lazy Leela became Lively Leela, and she joined in all the underwater adventures with her friends.
author: Radhika Misquitta

title: Arun's struggle for justice
text: In a bustling city, there lived a young man, Arun. He works in a factory. He is a very hard-working man. One day, Arun was working and suddenly thought of his dream. He lives in a rented house; his lifetime goal was to buy a small house with basic appliances like a TV, sofa, bed, etc. But he said to himself that this salary wouldn't be enough to save and fulfill his wish. That's when his friend Prabhat asked Arun, what are you daydreaming about? Arun replied, I'm thinking of doing another part-time job. Prabhat replied, But why? Arun said, because with this salary alone, I won't be able to achieve my dream. His friend said, "Okay, that's a good idea, but when will you work? We start our work at 8:00 a.m. and finish it at 10:00 p.m. The whole day we spend at the factory. Arun replied, yes, you are right. Maybe we could leave early, and I would earn more. Prabhat replied, Now stop daydreaming. The manager might be coming for supervision, then he will cancel today's wage, and then you can neither dream nor achieve. Imagining about this, he dropped the big box that he was carrying mistakenly. The manager was on the rounds, supervising the work. When Arun dropped the box, the manager started yelling at him in front of all the other workers. Arun felt very humiliated. But he could do nothing. because if he goes to explain about the incident, the manager will get angry and might cancel his one-week salary. So, in fear of that, he just apologized and begged not to cut his wage, and this mistake won't be repeated. The merciless manager replied, how can you command me? Your one-week salary will be cut now. If you still give orders, you will be thrown out of the job. Given that this was the first time for him, Arun felt deeply offended. In an attempt to comfort Arun, Prabhat said, "Just forget it; we already know and have witnessed this behavior from our manager." Arun was sad, though. That day, as soon as he got home, he began crying nonstop. Sunday was the following day, and it was often a half-day shift. Since Arun had dropped the box the day before, the manager called and instructed him to work the entire day. Arun was really disappointed because he had intended to go out with his family. He almost said this, but changed his mind because asking for a leave of absence could result in him losing his job. After finishing the entire task, he left for his house. He felt deeply let down by his life. He let out a cry and exclaimed, "Goddddd!" Are you present? Do you consider that I'm speaking? Why am I experiencing this? Listening to him, God appeared in front of Arun. Arun was very furious. God asked Arun, What happened, my child? Why do you call me? Arun replied in a harsh tone, "Don't you know why I called you? Why do I only have to face all the struggles in life? God replied, "Are you the only one suffering? What about your other colleagues?" Arun replied, "Yes, I know that even they face the same situation. But what can I do when I myself am helpless? You are the only one who can save us from this." God said, No! I can't help you all. You are the one who can help you and your colleagues. Arun asked, How? God said, I will give you a manual that contains solutions for your problem. God hands over the manual to Arun and cautions him, "Use this wisely and only for the good of people." When he uncovers the manual, the title is written as PIL. He was puzzled by looking at it, and he started reading the manual carefully to understand it. He discovered that PIL is a legal tool through which individuals or groups can seek justice for issues affecting the public interest. As he read through the manual, he got answers to all of his questions. He found the best solution to his problem. He meticulously followed the instructions written in the manual. With determination and newfound hope, Arun filed a PIL against his factory manager's unjust practices. He sought the guidance of a lawyer who specialized in PIL cases, and together they prepared a comprehensive petition highlighting the violations of labor laws and the rights of the workers. Through the legal proceedings, Arun not only sought justice for himself but also for the entire workplace, advocating for fair treatment, dignity, and respect in the workplace. As the PIL gained momentum, Arun became a beacon of hope for his fellow workers, inspiring them to stand up against exploitation and injustice. Ultimately, Arun's courageous act of filing a PIL not only transformed his own life but also paved the way for positive change in the lives of countless workers throughout the country.

title: Coral Reefs in the Sea
text: Corals are marine invertebrates. They form colonies to create breathtaking underwater structures in the sea called coral reefs. Coral reefs are known as 'rainforests of the sea.' Coral reefs are formed from coral polyps. Coral polyps are a few millimeters in length. They have stinging tentacles to snatch food and protect themselves. They have a single opening that acts as both mouth and anus. Coral polyps deposit calcium carbonate. Over many years, these deposits build up, harden, and form coral reefs. Corals come in a variety of colours like pink, red, green, purple, brown, orange, and blue. The Zooxanthellae algae, fluorescent proteins, and chromoproteins present in the corals are the reasons for the different colours. There are many diverse coral species, each with unique shapes and colors. Here are a few examples. Staghorn Coral: Staghorn coral features finger-like branches that provide shelter for various reef creatures. Mushroom Coral: Shaped like flattened discs, mushroom coral often has vibrant colours and textures. Star Coral: Star coral has a star-shaped polyp structure and comes in various colours. Uses of Coral Reefs: Coral reefs provide vital habitat for countless fish and sea creatures. They form natural breakwaters and protect coastlines from erosion. They provide us with medicines and building materials. However, coral reefs are under threat from pollution and climate change. Quiz: Coral polyps secrete a. Magnesium Carbonate b. Calcium Carbonate c. Barium Carbonate d. Cadmium Carbonate

title: The One And Only Bullet And Boxer
text: Preface Ashwika Rana This is the author of this book. Right now in 2023 she is 12 years old. She lost her dog Bullet at the age of 10. Bullet never returned. She misses him and cries every day. Bullet was a hybrid sepia. She also lost her paralyzed dog Boxer in 2023 September but was not informed till November. This photo is from google. It is a picture of hybrid sepia dog. This is not bullet but looks exactly the same and I feel it is bullet. There is not even a single whisker difference. Read to know more. This story is of a lost dog named Bullet in a village of Himachal Pradesh, India. The name of the village was Badhera. A girl had this dog as her brother. The name of the girl was Ashwika Rana. She got frazzled about the lost Bullet and in 2023 she got more frazzled as she lost Boxer too. I do not have any pictures of Boxer as they are deleted. The Beginning Once upon a time, a girl named Ashwika Rana came to her village Himachal Pradesh from Chandigarh due to Corona-virus - Covid - 19 in 2020 on March 18 which was me. Then in July two twin puppies came to my house. I saw them behind a room outside my house. I felt very quaint and said to my father “There are two puppies over there”. He checked it and he was taken aback like I was. First of all I thought one was a female and one was a male. But they both were male. I kept their name Bullet and Boxer. On the first three to four days both were playing, my grandfather decided to leave one. But, the day we had to leave Boxer he got stagnant. For some days we gave him some medicines and tried to elixir him. But he didn’t get cured. So we called a doctor. The doctor said to give him a medicine called Neurobion Forte and then see what happens. We started giving medicine to him but he didn’t get cured. So we again called the doctor and he said “Now, he cannot ever walk!” I felt very cataclysmic. Me, my grandparents and my parents gave him the best we could have. I still remember those days when Bullet used to play hide ‘n’seek with me and Boxer used to try to get up. Even on those stormy and spooky nights when I used to be asked to bring the water bottles left upstairs to refill, I used to be very scared. But, Bullet always used to accompany me and from that day onwards I never felt scared or crept out. I used to cry because I wanted to return to Chandigarh but when Bullet and Boxer came, I felt like the best in my entire life. I still feel bad that why didn’t I took Bullet along with me? Well, I always felt as I’ve met Bullet and Boxer before in my life. It feels as if they had the soul of someone who I lost but loved the most. Bullet and Boxer were extraordinary. They beforehand only knew how to shake hands and how to eat properly. Whenever I fed Bullet in bowl, he always used to start eating it from the corners to the middle. They used to handshake very well. Bullet and Boxer even while being playful, never hurted me, not even by a scratch. Sometimes I used to hold the food up in the air, and ask Bullet to get it, so he always used to carefully take the bit without hurting my hand. They felt like heavenly souls. In, 2021 with some of our furniture we came to Chandigarh to find a new house. We didn’t know that will we find a house or not. When we found a house we visited my village couple of times. For a few months when the house was getting overhauled, we stayed at my family friend’s house. Before shifting when I had to come to my village the the last time for goodies, I met Bullet when I came. But, while going back to Chandigarh he was not there. So, I didn’t meet him. In April 2021 I got a phone from my grandmother that Bullet is lost for 4 – 5 days. I was sad but then my father told me that he will come soon. One month went by but he didn’t come. I eavesdropped the conversation of my grandmother and my father. When I came near to my father I was in traumatized. I heard that my neighbours in the village who were my relatives that they heard and also saw vestige of a tiger and bullet on their roof. They even found Bullet’s hair. Everyone believed that Bullet is dead but I didn’t. Bullet is still missing. I still pray to god that please give him back to me. I will always love him and will wait for him for my whole life. But there is still some hope. In 2023 Ashwika got a unicorn pony from one of my favourite toy store. The name of the pony is Chelsea. She loves her like Bullet but Bullet and Boxer are exceptional. I see Bullet in Chelsea. In 2023, in the month of September I lost Boxer. As Boxer was growing and he became hefty, it was difficult for my grandpa to hold him. As my grandpa already had back pain we were always in fear that his back pain might increase. So we left boxer at a dog center for better care and my grandpa would go and visit him every three months. He started becoming very weak. The last time I met was June or July. After that in September, 2023 he passed away but I didn’t know. In November month during Diwali when my cousin twins had also arrived, I asked my grandma that “why didn’t they bring Boxer with them? "She said that “He passes away in September but we didn’t wanted you to feel sorrow so we didn’t informs you”. I cried a lot, like I didn’t’ get the last chance to meet Bullet. I couldn’t meet Boxer also. I miss my best friends and brothers. At last I would just say that life is very unfair. It always tries to succumb you. You can mostly never dodge death but until you are alive always try to keep your loved ones happy so that they live for many years. I really miss them though I show everyone that I am very happy and funny from outside but I only know what’s killing me slowly- slowly from inside. I love you Bullet and Boxer. You both will always remain my best pets and “BEST BROTHERS”. I really wanted to share this story with people outside to tell them that yes, heavenly souls like this exist which love you by heart, and the pain of them leaving you is like a knife in the heart. Even if a soul is an animal never forget that it can love and protect you even better than a human sometimes. Sometimes you don’t realize that the end of your loved ones is near so always spend every moment of life with peace and your loved ones. Life is very short and no one knows when it will end so be nice, good and helpful. Always spend time with you loved ones because once you loose them you’ll regret for your entire life just like me not meeting Bullet and Boxer for the last time.

title: The Dragonfly and the Frog

As the afternoon approached, it was time for Mak Otek and her children to enter the cage. But suddenly, a ferret came. He wanted to catch Mak Otek's children. Mak Otek was shocked and shouted trying to chase the ferret away. But unfortunately, the ferret was not afraid of Mak Otek. "Please... help my child!" shouted Mak Otek in fear. title: The Hat Seller
text: One day a hat seller came to a village to sell his wares After a long walk, he felt tired. So he sat down under a tree to rest. He was so tired that he quickly fell asleep. While he slept, a flock of monkeys watched him from the top of a tree. Then they came down to have a closer look. The monkeys opened the Hat Seller's sack and examined the contents. They were overjoyed to find that there were so many hats and so many different colors, all according to the size of their heads. Soon, every monkey was wearing those hats! They danced happily while wearing hats of various colors: red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple and red. Suddenly, the Hat Seller woke up from sleep, and the monkeys immediately ran back up the tree. When the Hat Seller got up a moment later, the monkeys looked at him and waited to see what he would do. The Hat Seller checked his bag. He felt very sad when he saw it was empty. There was not a single hat left. Then, the Hat Seller looked up and found that the monkeys had put on his hats! For a moment, he wondered how to get his hat back. He took off the hat on his own head and threw it at the monkeys. The monkeys thought the Hat Seller intended to hurt them, so they were furious. Then, the monkeys also took off their hats and took turns throwing them at the hat seller. The hat vendor quickly picked up all the hats and put them back into the sack. The monkeys were stunned, and laughing, the Hat Seller walked away to sell his hats.

title: Clever Mouse
text: Puspita Sari There is a fat cat. And there was a little mouse The cat chases the mouse. However, the agile mouse always escaped. Until one day, the cat managed to corner the mouse. She asked “Since when did I become your aunt??” The mouse replied, you have a sister, right. The cat thought for a moment then agreed. The mouse said that his sister had adopted him. title: Panda's Journey
text: This is their first time on a plane. The funny thing is, they just realized that Korea is so close to Tiongkok. Koreans call them Aibao and Luhbao. Once out, Aibao and Luhbao immediately became famous and the center of attention in the amusement park, especially for children. Many Korean children see pandas for the first time. They immediately became friends. The pandas love to dance with the children. Aibao and Luhbao always go to play when Everland is off. Pertama-tama, they went to Myeong-dong which many tourists liked. There are many people and shops. Aibao and Luhbao saw a lot of cosmetic ads, then bought cosmetics to disguise their panda eyes. Aibao and Luhbao felt hungry while looking around, then bought odeng and tteok-bokki. It's delicious. In the afternoon, they went to Hongdae and saw the show together. Aibao and Luhbao went to a cafe scattered in Hongdae. In the cafe, there are people who chat, also study. Campuses are also widely spread near Hongdae. Aibao and Luhbao looked at Hongdae, then followed the students into the library. There, there are many books as well as computers, and everyone is studying. They really liked the place and were determined to read a lot later on. Next, they went to the famous Gyeongbok Palace in Korea. The buildings there are very beautiful, different from what they see in Tiongkok. Aibao and Luhbao borrowed two pairs of hanboks and took pictures at Gyeongbok Palace after seeing tourists wearing hanboks and taking pictures, then uploaded them on their blogs. Their friends saw and praised their photos. Aibao and Luhbao are satisfied to have fun. While in Everland, Aibao and Luhbao had heard from monkeys that K-pop was very famous. The first song they heard in Hongdae was Don't Wanna Cry which was sung by Seventeen. They heard from the young people around that they like to go to the club and can have fun there. So, Aibao and Luhbao went to the club. They dance cheerfully to the rhythm of the music. Then they went to SM Town in Gangnam-gu, according to a friend's advice. As soon as you enter, there is a cafe. Aibao and Luhbao eat ice cream and pasta. They went upstairs and looked at the clothes and photos of K-pop groups. The staff explained to them that many K-pop lovers look around there because SM has a big influence on K-pop. On it again, there is a small cinema. The members of the K-pop group appeared here before they debuted. K-pop is also a Korean culture that Aibao and Luhbao only discovered after arriving in Korea. According to them, it is very interesting. Aibao and Luhbao then went to Lotte World because they liked the playground. They buy a lot of candy and pretty stickers. Aibao and Luhbao can't ride a terrible ride like kora-kora out of fear. They met many children and greeted them. Lotte World was too big to try all the rides even though it had been around all day. Aibao and Luhbao have heard for a long time about the beauty of Jeju Island. They went there on a plane. Their inn is close to the beach, so they can see the sunrise on the beach, as soon as they wake up. Aibao and Luhbao saw the sea for the first time in their lifetime. They ran to the seaside cheerfully. The sand and sea beaches make them happy. Korean friends Aibao and Luhbao took them to Seongsan Ilchulbong (Peak of the Rising Sun) which is a famous tourist attraction on Jeju Island. Seongsan Ilchulbong is to the east of Jeju Island and close to the beach. The place consists of large and small volcanic stones. Although much different from the golden sand beach in their memory, the special seaside view left a very good impression on them. Aibao and Luhbao can see the sea and grassland from the top of the mountain. Aibao and Luhbao are pandas in the hearts of children. They go to the Teddy Bear Museum they dream of to find friends and see which bear is the most adorable there. The Teddy Bear Museum is full of childish feel. Aibao and Luhbao took a lot of photos there. They were sad because no one answered when Aibao and Luhbao greeted the bears at the Teddy Bear Museum. Why didn't the bears say hello? That's because the staff are watching them.
