title: Daddy, Let's Go Home!
text: Vishakha is really happy because all of her friends come to her birthday party. "Aunty, this party is really amazing", Rohit said. After hearing that, Vishakha's mother embrace Rohit's shoulder. Vishakha's mother really give all of her attention and love for all kids there. All the kids and their mothers also love them. They always be there if someone need for help. And of course Vishakha's mother do the same. "It is the most beautiful party!", when Vishakha and her friends watch a film together. A film about tiger and cubs playing in the jungle. But.. this film makes Vishakha sad. Why? She does not know why she is sad. After the film is finished, Vishakha's friends leave her home. Rohit still prepare his-self to go home. "That film was very good, right?" "Right. I really like it", Vishakha said. "Daddy? Daddy? Daddy?, Where is Daddy? Mom, Where is daddy?" Her mom yawned. "It is time for sleep". "But, but mom.. I need father like the cubs on the film!" "Vishakha, c'mon.. mommy is already tired. Come here and kiss mommy". "But mom??" "VISHAKHA!!!!!" her mother shouted at her. The next day is holiday. Vishakha and Rohit read a book together. "Where should i look for it, Rohit? Where do you look for a father when you can not see him?" "In the bathroom. That is his favorite place to hide. I look for him there". " I already checked it, but my dad was not hiding there. Do you know where is my dad?", "Hmm, i dont know where is he. But from this book, a parrot can talk and know everything". "NOOOO!! Is he cute like me?" "I dont know, Vishakha. That is why i asked you". " Ki-Ki-Ka-Ka". "Rohit, what does it mean?" "Hi Vishakha, How are you today, honey?", Greeting from Rohit's mother. " Aunty, do you know where is my father? I asked Mirchi, but he did not want to answer me". "Haha! Mirchi was so cruel. You should ask your mother. Of course she knows it." "I did, aunty. But she doesnt know it too." "Hmm. It is getting dark, Vishakha. You should go home." "Okay, aunty. See youu." Questions like that keep coming in her mind. She will ask her mother about daddy. Her mother looks different. Vishakha does not know what happened to her. "Mommy, are you okay?", asked Vishakha slowly. "Vishakha, come here. Look at the stars. Look at the light." "So beautiful, mom. I wish I were a star..." "One day, you will be a star. Like your daddy." "Is daddy a star?", Vishakha asked excitedly. " Yes, honey. Do you see that star? The brightest star!" "Yes." "That is your daddy, He is smiling at you." "Hi, daddy. Mom, can he hear me?" "Loudly, Vishakha!" Vishakha smiles at the stars while closing her eyes, trying to calculate the distance between her and the stars. Then she shouted loudly, "Dady, let's go home."

title: New Planet

text: I want to eat cake for breakfast! Mother: You can't. You have to eat healthy food. Child: Why? Healthy food doesn't taste delicious. Cake tastes very delicious. Mother: No problem. Then I'll eat scrambled eggs as protein and bread as carbohydrate. I'll also cut up a banana and strawberries. Bananas and strawberries are my favorite fruits. Mom: If you do this every day, you'll grow up to be a strong child. Question: What do you eat for breakfast? Did you eat a healthy breakfast? Why is it important to eat healthy food? title: Ms. Dani and the Whispering Forest
text: Today we are going on an adventure to the Whispering Forest!" The motorcycle buzzed merrily. Upon entering the Whispering Forest, strange sounds filled Bu Dani's ears. The leaves rustled as if whispering, the river rumbled as if singing, and even the birds chirped rhythmically. "Strange," Ms. Dani muttered with a frown. "It's not usually like this," she said again. Suddenly, a tiny squirrel jumped in front of Ms. Dani, wearing a necklace. "Hi, Ms. Dani," it greeted in a soft voice. Mrs. Dani was surprised. "A-a-are you able to talk?" The squirrel nodded. "Of course! In the whispering forest, all creatures can speak the language of nature." Ms. Dani was fascinated. She talked to the squirrel, whose name was Roro. Roro told her that their forest was sad because the flowers were losing their color. "Can I help?" asked Mrs. Dani. "Of course!" replied Roro. "But, we have to find the Butterfly Queen who can restore the color of the flowers." Bu Dani followed Roro's orders deeper into the forest. They passed giant trees that whispered ancient stories, crossed rivers that sang cheerful songs, and avoided cobwebs that chanted funny songs. Finally, they came to a field of flowers. In the center of the field, a beautiful butterfly with white wings was pensive. "Queen Butterfly," greeted Roro. She introduced Mrs. Dani. "This is Dani, who wants to help us returning the color of the flowers." Queen Butterfly smiled sadly. "My wings lost their magic power due to pollution from the outside world. Without my magic, the flowers cannot be colored." Ms. Dani also told about her vehicle, a magic motorcycle, which uses clean solar energy. The Butterfly Queen gasped. "The sun's energy is what I need!" she exclaimed. "Perhaps with its light, I can restore my magic!" Mrs. Dani turned on the bright lights of her magic motorcycle. The light slowly enveloped the Butterfly Queen. Her wings began to glow and her color returned. Queen Butterfly flapped her wings gracefully. The flowers on the field began to bloom with beautiful colors. "Thank you, Ms. Dani," said Queen Butterfly. "You have saved the Whispering Forest and our flowers." Ms. Dani smiled. "You're welcome, Queen. I'm glad I could help." Bu Dani said goodbye to Roro and Ratu Kupu-Kupu. She left the Whispering Forest, which was once again filled with cheerful colors. Mrs. Dani went home with a happy heart. She was relieved to have helped the people of the Whispering forest and the Butterfly Queen.

title: The Hat Seller
text: One day a hat seller came to a village to sell his wares After a long walk, he felt tired. So he sat down under a tree to rest He was so tired that he quickly fell asleep. While he slept, a flock of monkeys watched him from the top of a tree. Then they came down to have a closer look. The monkeys opened the Hat Seller's sack and examined the contents. They were overjoyed to find that there were so many hats and so many different colors, all according to the size of their heads. Soon, every monkey was wearing those hats! They danced happily while wearing hats of various colors: red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple and red. Suddenly, the Hat Seller woke up from sleep, and the monkeys immediately ran back up the tree. When the Hat Seller got up a moment later, the monkeys looked at him and waited to see what he would do. The Hat Seller checked his bag. He felt very sad when he saw it was empty. There was not a single hat left. Then, the Hat Seller looked up and found that the monkeys had put on his hats! For a moment, he wondered how to get his hat back. He took off the hat on his own head and threw it at the monkeys. The monkeys thought the Hat Seller intended to hurt them, so they were furious. Then, the monkeys also took off their hats and took turns throwing them at the Hat Seller. The hat vendor quickly picked up all the hats and put them back into the sack. The monkeys were stunned, and laughing, the Hat Seller walked away to sell his hats.

title: Grandma, what is Ghatasthapana?
text: Today is the day of Ghatasthapana: Aarav woke up with just one wake-up call from his mom, and he quickly got dressed to help his grandparents in the altar in their house. Usually, Aarav and his parents would celebrate Christmas with Aarav's grandparents in India - however, this year, they decided to celebrate Dasara and Diwali together instead. Aarav and his parents flew to India from overseas to do so. There is nothing comparable to the joy of celebrating Indian festivals in India. Aarav was excited to see how his grandparents celebrated Ghatasthapana. So, he woke up early. Aarav and his grandma went to the garden to collect soil. Grandma spread the soil evenly in a bamboo woven basket and sowed seeds, one-by-one, in that soil. She then spread another layer of soil evenly on top of this first layer of soil. Then, she filled a clay pot with water and placed this clay pot on top of the soil. Aarav had previously seen plants being sown in pots of soil in the garden, but these woven baskets, clay pots were all new to him. He then begun asking his grandma, "Grandma, what are you doing?" "What is Ghatasthapana?" "What will you do with this clay pot and the soil?" His rapid-fire questioning began. Aarav had lived overseas: he was very curious about these new objects that he was seeing. However, Grandma was answering Aarav's questions just as enthusiastically as he was asking them. "Wait, I will tell you a story from my childhood," Grandma said. "A story!" Aarav exclaimed, eyes twinkling with excitement. "Please do tell, I love listening to stories." "My dad also tells me a story every night before I go to bed." "Awesome, you must listen then", said his grandma. "My parents were farmers, and we lived on a farm. You know what I am referring to when I say "farm", right?" Grandma explained with patience in a way that Aarav would understand. "Yes, I have seen a farm before, they are large and spread out - my parents and I went to a pumpkin festival, which is where I saw what a farm looks like", said Aarav. "Yes, that is exactly what a farm is. Your grandpa and I saw a photo from that pumpkin farm - the one you guys took of that enormous pumpkin", Grandma said, laughing, and continued her story: "As October begun, my parents always seemed to be in a rush - here are some sentences I would hear all the time:" "The days will get colder soon!" "And no crops grow in the winter." "Because, the day is short and the night is long." "Crops don't get enough sunlight." "It doesn't rain either." "Hence, my parents had to make preparations for what crops to grow in their fields." "Grandma, what are crops?" Aarav asked. "Crops are what we use in the kitchen to cook everyday!" "Pulses, vegetables, oils, mustard, chillis, coriander, and much more - these all were grown in the farm before they reach our plate - these are all crops." "Anyway, what was I saying? Oh right, preparation for the farm before winter," Grandma continued on with the story. "My parents would examine the soil - they would test it! This way, they could see what crops would grow well in that soil." "My mom would take a bamboo basket - just like this one - and she would put some soil in the basket. Then, she would sow seeds in this soil. She would plant wheat, coriander next to it, and fenugreek. She would also plant chickpeas, millets, and other types of grains." "Then, you keep a clay pot filled with water on top of this soil - this is the "Ghat" in question." Grandma said to Aarav while holding the "Ghat" in her hand. "Everyday, water from this clay pot drips slowly into the soil, thus watering the seeds planted into the soil. Even with such minimal water, many plants sprout - we can see which plants sprout in 10 days: the day of Dasara." "How come, Grandma?" Aarav asked, with a questioning look. "This is because, the plants that have sprouted the most in the "Ghat" will be the crops that give the best yield in the farm." "The practice of Ghatasthapana worked as an experiment that farmers conducted in the olden days." "After Dasara, work on the farm begins again." Grandma's face shone with joy while saying so. "Aarav, dear, did you like the story?" asked Grandma. "Yes!" Aarav exclaimed, but it seemed that he still had more questions. "But, Grandma, we don't farm anymore, right? Why do we still do this?" Aarav inquired. "Yes, but this is a tradition - we pay gratitude to the grains that we eat, we pay gratitude to the farmers who have painstakingly cultivated these grains." "We pray that nature helps these farmers." "In order to do so, I offer a prayer." "You can also pay gratitude by planting a tree." After saying this, Grandma lit a lamp, held the lamp in her hand while circling the bamboo basket, and everyone did as Grandma said - they all prayed. On Dasara, Aarav's excitement grew further after seeing the sprouts that had emerged from the bamboo basket. He said to his parents, "When I grow older, I will also become a farmer." Grandma was overjoyed after witnessing Aarav's excitement and enthusiasm.
author: Netra Joshi

title: The Foolish Crow
text: Once upon a time, there lived a very foolish crow. One day while he was passing by the forest, he suddenly saw a piece of cheese. Even a fox saw it. They both raced to catch the cheese. "I've heard that you sing very well!" said the fox to please the crow. "Yes, of course I do!" the crow agreed. "Can you sing a bit?" asked the fox. As soon as the crow opened his mouth to sing, the cheese fell down. The cunning fox took the cheese and ran away.

title: Story Chikkappa
text: Dedicated to the Gram Panchayat Librarians of Karnataka Uma rings the big bell at the entrance. All the children rush inside for their favourite time of the day — the story hour. Vidya Akka draws a circle on the floor with a piece of chalk and all the children sit around her. Today is Uma’s turn to pick her favourite book from the ones strung across the room on a rope. Uma S..T..R..E..T..C..H..E..S her hand, goes on her tippy toes, picks the one which has a picture of many books on its cover, and hands it over to Vidya Akka. “Will you read us this story, Akka?” “Of course Uma, but first you must tell everyone what made you choose this book.” Uma points to the mysterious title and says, “THE LAND WITHOUT STORIES!!! I can’t imagine what it would be like to have no stories in my life. I love stories!” Vidya Akka asks the other children, “Can you imagine what it would feel like to live in a land without stories?” All the other children look at each other and, almost in chorus, repeat: “THE LAND WITHOUT STOOORIES?!!!” They look surprised! Vidya Akka tries to get their attention. “Now, now, children, who would like to know more about this?” She says, “1, 2, 3... (ONDU, ERADU, MOORU),” and they all respond by saying, “SHURU MAADI!” “shuru maadi!” “shuru maadi!” Vidya Akka’s voice suddenly dips and the chatter in the room settles down to make way for the story. SSSHHHHHHHH! “Imagine a place far far away. Everyone would wake up in the morning and spend their day working silently." “The farmer silently tilled his land… TAK TAK TAK." “The postman silently opened the mailbox at home and slipped in the letters without saying a word. The only sound that was heard was when the mailbox closed... FLAP FLAP FLAP." TAK TAK TAK FLAP FLAP FLAP “Even the animals and birds in this village were mostly silent. The children wandered around from street to street, looking bored and confused." “When they went back home in the evening, they just ate their dinner quietly and went to sleep." “Their parents were too tired after the day’s work and had no energy to remember any stories. And ajjas and ajjis too would just sit quietly in a corner of the house. It was as if someone had cast a spell on the people of this land.” Guntu interrupted Vidya Akka, “Akka, Akka, I know! Like when we press the MUTE button on the TV remote control.” “Exactly Guntu, that is an interesting connection you made!” said Vidya Akka. “Srinivas, the village librarian, also lived in this land. And, like the others, he too would wake up every morning and go to his library which was next to the panchayat office. He would SILENTLY dust the big shelves of storybooks and arrange the new books that arrived neatly on them." “During the afternoons, he sat at his desk and looked outside the large window hoping that someone would come inside to read those books. And he would do that till evening. Then, at 5:00 p.m., he would put the big lock on the library office door and go home." “One night, just before falling asleep, he thought to himself, ‘IT WOULD BE SO NICE IF CHILDREN CAME TO MY LIBRARY and listened to all those stories lying still inside those hundreds of books.’ “That night he had a dream. In his dream, he had become an eight-year-old child. Around him, there were many other children. They were looking at someone. But who was this?" “She looked old. She was wearing a colourful robe and a strange looking conical hat with a bell hanging from its top. DING DING DONG! Her hands moved up and down in the air, and the look in her eyes changed every few seconds. All the children listened to her. Some giggled, others looked shocked. No one seemed bored or restless." ding ding dong “The next morning, Srinivas woke up and looked puzzled. It seemed like he was trying to recall his dream. He got ready for work and spent his morning dusting books and writing something in his big fat notebook. Then, after lunch, he sat down at his desk and looked at the empty window. " “He saw children wandering past the window. One of them came close to the window and peeped inside." 'COME! COME!' “His mother stood a few steps behind him. Srinivas immediately called this boy inside, ‘COME! COME!’" “The boy was a little scared to go inside the library room but he was also curious. He looked back at his mother and called her close. They both entered the library." “Srinivas asked him, ‘What is your name, little boy?’ ‘Appu,’ said the little one. Srinivas remembered the parcel of new books that had arrived in the library that morning. He asked Appu, ‘Would you like to listen to a story?’ Appu did not know what that meant but looked excited at the thought of something new to do. He nodded his head. ‘Come sit here, Appu,’ Srinivas said and began reading. ‘Once upon a time…’ “For the next thirty minutes, Appu could not take his eyes off Srinivas. Appu watched his hands move and sway as he narrated the story." “His face had so many expressions. His voice changed in so many different ways. I t was all so interesting. Appu had never heard or seen something like this before!" “For some time, he actually felt like he was a part of the story. And the story was about a little boy like him. At the end of the story when Appu was leaving, Srinivas told him, ‘Come again tomorrow.’" “The next day in the afternoon, Appu was back at the library window. This time, along with him, four other faces eagerly peeped inside." “Srinivas called them in. Appu led his friends confidently. They enjoyed the story reading and promised to return the following day." “On the third day, there was a crowd of children at the library entrance. Appu pointed to Srinivas and said, ‘Look! That is Story Chikkappa.’ Srinivas was delighted. The silent library room was filled with the laughter of children." “Soon word spread in the Land Without Stories. All the villagers heard about Story Chikkappa and were curious to meet him." “Mothers brought their little babies along to listen to stories. The local school invited Story Chikkappa to the school to narrate stories to children and, for those children who could not come to school, Story Chikkappa would go to their homes with a bundle of storybooks." “Life in the Land Without Stories looked different The farmer’s wife told the farmer the story she had heard from Story Chikkappa." “The crow heard the story being told and went and cawed to the other crows. JUST LIKE AIR, THESE STORIES WERE TRAVELLING EVERYWHERE." “Children were no longer wandering around in the afternoons. Older children started making up short stories on their own, after listening to so many from Chikkappa, and narrating them to younger children. By listening to these stories, children learnt how to laugh at themselves, fight imaginary monsters, and the secrets of life." Just like air, these stories were travelling everywhere! “The Land Without Stories transformed into a LAND FULL OF STORY TREASURES, told by the children to their children, and later to their grandchildren.” Storytime at Shaanta Graama Library ends. Vidya Akka closes the book and asks Uma to put it back on the shelf. She asks the children, “Tell me what did you find most interesting in this story?” Uma says, “I like that STORIES NEVER GROW OLD and, like air, stories can travel anywhere and everywhere. When I grow up, I also want to be like Story Chikkappa and spend my day telling stories to little children.” The state of Karnataka has over 5600 gram panchayat libraries in rural areas. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Smt Uma Mahadevan-Dasgupta, who is the Additional Chief Secretary of the Panchayat Raj, saw the potential of these libraries to provide the children of rural communities with quality literature and reduce the learning loss that the pandemic had brought in its wake. She initiated the “Oduva Belaku” (The Light of Reading) program across Karnataka to revive rural public libraries. The objectives were to help children stay connected to reading and build a library culture within communities. Membership to the library was made free and children were issued library cards. Many libraries received a makeover and some were even given new spaces for better access. Digitization of the libraries was also taken up and many libraries were provided with computers, smart TVs and mobile phones as well. Ms Mahadevan-Dasgupta, who loved to read, was aware that only changes to the library facilities would not attract children. The librarians who ran these libraries also needed to learn new ways to make them child-friendly spaces. In order to do this, civil society organizations like Adhyayan Quality Education Foundation and others were invited to provide to help the librarians learn strategies to increase membership of these libraries and get more children to come to them. Adhyayan Foundation trained the librarians to conduct read-aloud sessions in their libraries for the children. This programme was a huge success — it started in two districts and, was quickly adopted by four more. It is now all set to expand to all the districts as it has helped both children and librarians discover the magical world of stories. About the Oduva Belaku Program
author: Reshma Bachwani

title: AFRAID
text: Sleepy Natalie woke up from a buzzing sound, it was her alarm. Her mother went to her room to wake her up and remind her what day it was, It was her first day of school! Her parents were enthusiastic but well Natalie, not so much. She was bullied everyday by her classmate Chloe a.k.a the mayor's daughter. Even her best friend, Alya, couldn't help her too. As she walked across the hallway of her school, She couldn't help herself seeing Chloe picking other people's leg so she hid herself in the library, burying her tears in her arms. She felt an arm pat on her shoulders, it was a boy with blonde hair. He introduced himself as Adrien. "Why were you crying?" He asked. Natalie just found herself telling him everything. After hearing this, He comforted her and encouraged her to stand up for herself. It had been ages since she felt better. On the following day, Chloe pinned Natalie to a wall. "Whom were you talking to, imaginary friends?? Ha ha ha" Chloe said. She started mocking her. Natalie confidently responded "Are you blind or stupid? Can't you see he is my friend?" Chloe was shocked with Natalie's new personality. Nobody had ever stood up for themselves before from Chloe. From that day onwards, Natalie started protecting anyone who was getting bullied by Chloe. Several months had passed since the incident of Natalie's confidence, she also thought that today would be just like any other day but except it wasn't. Natalie was strolling through the school hallway when she was called to the principal's office. She was shocked when she learned that she was accused of stealing exam papers and was caught on CCTV camera. She was furious when she saw Chloe and Adrien grinning at her. This sight made her blood boil. She started screaming their name and was about to punch them in their faces when she suddenly blacked out. She was immediately taken to the hospital. Her parents were called. As soon as Natalie woke up, she found her mother and ended up telling her mother everything. "I got a call from you school 2-3 months ago. They told me that you were friends with a boy who never existed. I knew it was because of Chloe and no real friends. I consulted a psychologist about it." Her mother explained. As her mother continued " He told me you had been in a trauma for several years so you just created an imaginary friend of your own." Natalie burst in tears after hearing so. All this friend thing was just a fake scenario. Natalie was sent to therapy center for a while to calm herself down. One day, Natalie found Adrien in her room apologizing to her for his earlier mistakes. She snapped out of it and started telling herself that it all wasn't true. Over time, She recovered from her trauma. She decided to move on and have a fresh start with her life. She became a strong girl over time and swore to never look back again. Causes of children/teenagers having imaginary friends (getting themselves into trouble)= * - Getting bullied at school or getting cyberbullied. * - Parents Fighting environment at home. * - Traumatic events in the past. * - When child feels unnoticed everywhere. Having an imaginary friend for children around 9 years is completely normal. Children have imaginary friends to practice their social skills. They should be treated if they are getting themselves into trouble because of imaginary friends. This story was an example to tell everyone that if this is happening to someone you know, you should help them by making them feel better,
author: Kaira Kaushal

title: That Diwali Eid
text: Once it so happened that Diwali and Eid were just 30 days apart. The moment I got to know it, I ran to Amma and asked her to buy me one beautiful shimmering sharara. The next moment I went to Geeti’s house and saw her beautiful lehenga choli stitched by her mother. That entire day Geeti and I discussed our Diwali feast menu and who gets to invite friends first. The matter was for those past couple of years we enjoyed eating lots of sheer korma at our friend’s house on Eid. So, we thought, why not host a Diwali feast for our friends at our homes? You see, meeting friends during festivals is so much fun. As we shared our plans with our friends at school, everyone got so excited that our discussions knew no end. Washroom breaks, recess, breaks in between the classes, and even when classes were going on, we discussed, discussed, and discussed until Mehrunisa teacher caught us disturbing the class. A week before Diwali we all got busy helping our moms to prepare snacks. That day, I felt Diwali is festival of light and lots of yummy food too. Well, Eid is the festival of food too but what made these festivals more special was meeting my friends. Look, this is how we celebrated our Diwali that year. Geeti and I cleaned our front yards, decorated the pathway with colourful rangolis, and lit several Deepams. You know it takes a lot of effort to beautify something. That day we skipped our evening playtime. Usually, it never happened. We loved our playtime a lot yet we were okay to let it go and decorated our houses. And just when the sky turned dark, the glitters and shimmers of our firecrackers lit it back. The next day our plan was ready to execute. We first decided to visit Sonali’s house, followed by Rashmi’s, Shweta’s, Shilpa’s, Ashwini’s, Geeti’s, and then finally my house. At every house we all circle up for the delicious bites and enjoyed the snack we loved the most. When we reached Geeti's home, we ate some of the finest Dhoklas. Done with food, we looked for firecrackers as Amreen, Firdous, Shabnam, Phalak Naaz, and Uzma wanted to burst some. I quickly picked a few crackers kept on the roof to dry. Geeti too bought a few from her house. We all enjoyed bursting crackers in the daylight. That day we were busy hosts receiving our friends and turned guests by visiting them. The next 30 days were the holy days of Ramzan and many of us were fasting. Our lunch circle shrank. The other half of us quickly finished our lunch and joined the rest to play. We loved walking around the school premises. Sometimes, a few of our friends felt sleepy and tired as they woke up early to observe the fast. During such days, we would just sit in the class and chat. Finally, it was Eid. Usually, we would first visit Amreen’s house but that Eid we visited Safiya’s house first followed by Uzma’s, Amreen’s, and Firdous’. We had lots of sheer khorma. Our stomachs were full-fed. We needed to rest so we relaxed at Firdous' house but just for a while. As the day progressed I was not ready to go home and neither were my friends. I do not remember whose idea it was suddenly, we decided to visit Mehrunisa teacher. But how could we go empty-handed? It was Eid after all. So, we quickly gathered some 20 rupees from our pockets. We dropped by the only gift shop in the town and picked a flower vase for our beloved teacher. With our heavy stomachs, we decided to walk across the town in the hot sun. It was exhausting but who cared? The excitement of meeting our teacher and the long walk with friends kept us walking. That is the power of happiness! In no time we made it to our destination. We stood outside our teacher's home with the gift. None of us dared to knock on the door. We whispered as to who would knock on the door but in no time our whispers were heard. “Hello, students! Why don’t you all come in?”, our teacher smiled as she opened the door. She was warm and welcoming which comforted us. We were finally at ease and presented her with the gift. As we stood up to leave she asked us to sit and walked into the kitchen. We all looked at each other. We knew what was coming and rounded up for a quick discussion. Although we had no space for food in our stomachs anymore, we all decided to taste the food just a little. What if she feels bad? How could we offend our beloved teacher on Eid? Our teacher came back with a big tray filled with delicious food. One of the sweets was double ka meetha. Many of us did not know this delicacy at all. Then and there we all gave up our idea of tasting just a little. The food was so yummy that we could not help ourselves. We ate it all as our teacher served with love. ' That Diwali Eid' is truly memorable!
author: Ujwala Krishnaraj

title: Visit to Grandmother
text: Aanya are two twin sisters living in Mumbai. Manya is a curious girl who has curly brown hair. He likes to go on adventures. Aanya also has curly brown hair. He has big eyes and is good at riddles and quizzes. They were excited as they were about to go to their grandmother's house in Bangalore. Their father's friend, who was also going to Bangalore, suggested that the father take the children with him. The journey is long but very enjoyable. They stopped at a nearby dhaba for lunch. Manya and Aanya ate parathas, sabzi and huge glasses of thick and creamy lassi so they were full for the rest of the journey. When they reached Bangalore, they looked at the houses with joy. When the father's friend stopped the car, the children saw the house. Grandma's house was a spacious bungalow with a garden behind it. The cement was cracked and they could see the maroon bricks inside. The terrace has a small swing where grandma sits. He is in his late 70s but as active as a 10 year old. She has dusky skin and long gray hair pulled into a tight bun. The kids ran and hugged grandma. He was very happy to see them. They changed clothes and grandma went to the kitchen to prepare snacks. That's kheer! Aanya and Manya devour the food. The house is big and very spacious. There is a large bedroom and a kitchen with everything grandma needs to throw a party. For several days, Manya and Aanya went out and played with other children in the neighborhood. They played hide and seek and cycled on the bicycles that grandfather had bought them. Every day, they used to collect vegetables and fruits from the back garden and in return, grandma cooked delicious food. At night, they usually go to their grandparents' room. Their rooms are brightly lit and have high ceilings! There were several windows and filled bookshelves. They go there to look at old photos of their parents and listen to interesting stories told by grandmother. Sometimes, Manya and Aanya used to prank grandfather by taking the newspaper and hiding it somewhere. Things like this always keep the house cheerful. After about a week, the children had become a large group. There is Rohit, their neighbor's son, Amit, Reena, Krishna, and Harit. They always go on adventures together. One afternoon, Rohit rushed in, excited and happy. He was thin, dark, and tall. When Manya asked Rohit what was happening, he said, "The circus is coming to town! They will be performing this weekend!" Children squealed with joy and begged their grandparents to take them to the circus. After much pleading, grandfather and grandmother finally gave in. After dancing for a few minutes, Grandpa finally spoke, "I'll only take you all to the circus this weekend if you do extra work around the house and don't be naughty." The kids promise not to get into any trouble all week. The whole group finds out about the circus and is excited to go together. The days passed and the weekend was just hours away. They waited all day and night. The day of the circus has finally arrived. Rohit, Manya and Aanya are the most excited. Grandpa drove his car towards the circus field. They saw large red and white tents towering above them. The shining lights and food fascinate the children. Before the show started, grandpa bought them buttered popcorn and baked beans. As they sat down, a very heavy rain began to fall. All the spectators ran out, rushed to their cars in panic and left. All the children were devastated. They had been waiting for this circus for a whole week and now there was no way to watch it. When their car arrived home, the children got out slowly. For several days, the children were sad. They didn't go out to play much and didn't listen to any stories either. Grandpa tries to take them to the park every day, but it doesn't make a difference. Children stop helping with homework and sit in bed all day. Before the circus left, grandfather begged them to perform once, but the circus master refused because he had to go to another city to perform. The circus truck drives off and grandfather returns home disappointed and tired. Their sadness increased gradually, day by day. One day, grandma decided to make their favorite treat. He works all day to make coconut barfi, pasyam and kheer. But the kids just put the plates away and went to their rooms. Grandma and grandfather are very worried about the children. Grandparents start to get tired and children get bored quickly. All they do is sleep and sit. They watched television with grandfather, but it only entertained them for a few hours. Their friends quickly recovered from their grief and even tried to cheer them up. Sometimes grandmother took them to the terrace to see the twinkling stars, but thoughts about the circus always kept ringing in Many and Aanya's heads. Grandparents began to worry that the children would no longer visit Bangalore and that their behavior would reflect their actions at home. They had to do something before it was too late. Grandfather and grandmother did everything they could but to no avail. Soon they too were fed up. One morning, grandma came in happily. He said that he got a brilliant idea. He decided to create a circus in an empty lot. Grandpa was so excited that he called a meeting and explained his plan. Every week, the community meets to discuss plans. Grandpa and Mr Sumit are the group supervisors. The committee members decided to organize everything the following week. But there is one big problem. They organize meetings and take care of everyone. They don't have enough money to make all this happen. This news really saddens the community. Just as the project was about to close, unexpected help arrived. The principal of a large school, who was a friend of grandfather's, agreed to provide the necessary money. When grandfather heard this, he thanked his friend wholeheartedly. By the time the project was finished, Grandma had assembled a team of women to help her cook the food. They each have a special job to do. One cooks popcorn, another makes baked beans, and the rest make drinks and snacks. All the people work hard to make a big circus. There are a variety of stalls, a large circus tent and a kitchen for preparing food. The circus is finally ready! Everyone is very excited to surprise the kids. In the morning, Manya and Aanya wake up due to Rohit's encouragement. Sleepily they got up and quickly got dressed. The house was empty and the grandparents were nowhere to be found. When they go out, they see Rohit's mother calling them to the car. They sat down and Rohit's mother started driving. When they looked outside, they were shocked to see a huge circus. Mr. Sumit is the clown, Mr. Mahesh is serving popcorn, grandfather is the ring leader and grandmother is making the food. Everyone is in the circus. Manya and Aanya met other friends near the entrance. They looked around the stall. There are fun games like hitting the target and tapping the pin. There are also amazing prizes. Aanya knocks down all the pins and wins a cute doll. When it was time for the main action, the kids rushed in and took their seats. Before the show started, grandpa bought them popcorn and baked beans. When everyone was seated, the tent became dark. Then suddenly an elephant trumpet was heard. Dancers dance around elephants, Trapeze artists fly through the air, and grandfathers perform magic tricks. The funniest part is when the comedian comes. He makes hilarious jokes that make people roll on the floor laughing. When the show ended, they all scattered from the tent. All the kids laughed and smiled as they came out. Grandpa and Grandma were so happy to see the smiles on their faces!
author: Salsa

title: Appu's search for nectar
text: Appu is very excited. For the first time he is going out to search for nectar for the hive. Appu is so excited that today he woke up early in the morning and got ready to go out. Appu went with his elder brother Gappu who has long experience of collecting nectar. But where should we go? Asked Appu. Let's go to the Sunshine Apartment. I have heard that people grow beautiful flowers there. Replied Gappu. Appu and Gappu flied to the Sunshine Apartment. Buzzzzzzzzzzzzzz........ They GO! Awwwww It's SO BIG! "It will take us a whole day if we search here together." said Appu. "Okay, let's divide the area." s uggested Gappu. "You can search in the B-Block and I will go in the A- Block." said Gappu. Appu then flied to the B-Block and Gappu in the A- Block. Whoooooooosh!!!! Shouted Moti uncle when he saw Appu on his beautiful red roses. Buzzz... Buzz... Buzz..... scared Appu flied away. Appu tried to get nectar from roses, lilies, Jasmine Hibiscus and may more but Appu could not get nectar from anywhere. Whoever saw him shooed him again and again. Appu was very sad and he did not want to search for nectar anymore. Soon he went towards Gappu. Gappu was sitting on the Hibiscus flower in Sharmila aunt's garden. "Were you able to find nectar?" asked Appu. "Yes, I found nectar in Sharmila aunt's garden." Replied Gappu. "She did not shoo you away?" Asked Appu. "She is my good friend. I always come to take nectar from her." Said Gappu. "So why did you send me in the B-Block?" Asked Appu. Because I wanted you to understand that life is not as easy as you believe, you would have to face difficulties. Oh! Bhaiya you troubled me today. I know you would have a lot of trouble but don't worry from tomorrow you can come to Sharmila aunt's garden. She is a nice woman. She always welcome bees, butterflies and many more insects like us to take nectar. Oh! we are late today, mother and father would be waiting for us. "This time I will reach first at home before you bhaiya." Said Appu.
author: drishti bansal

title: The Hungry Fox And The Grapes
text: A fox lived in a forest. One day, he was very hungry. It was a hot summer day. He went out of his place and wandered here and there. He is looking up for some food. He visited many places in search of food. Finally, he found a vineyard a mile away. He ran and reached there. He saw a chubby bear near the vineyard. The chubby bear asked him politely, ''Where are you going?'' The hungry fox glared at him. The chubby bear again tried to ask him the same but before he could complete his question, the ravenous fox entered into the vineyard. He saw the multi coloured bunches of grapes in the vineyard. He was amazed and became very happy. His mouth started watering. He wished to eat all at once. He jumped to catch the grapes and tried to eat them. But he got nothing, not even a single bunch. He was not close enough to any branch. He jumped high again and again but failed to catch all the time. His all efforts were of no use as the grapes were far away from his reach. He went away from the vineyard. On his way, he again met with the chubby bear. Now, the chubby bear asked him, ''Have you eaten the grapes?''. He said, ''The grapes were sour. If I eat them, I might fall ill.'' Moral of the story We should accept our incapabilities. If the situation is difficult or uncontrollable, we should use our minds to solve it. Also, we should not hesitate to seek help from our friends and elders. The most important lesson of the story is that it is easy to despise what you cannot have.
author: Vishwadeep Pawar

title: The Clever Rabbit and the Foolish Lion
text: Terro Lion was a very proud lion. He was a real terror in the jungle. He often just roared and killed animals, even when he was not very hungry. The terrified animals of the jungle one day called for a meeting. “We must put and end to this menace,” Forro fox cried. “But how,” wondered the other animals. “Terro is so big and strong, none of can even touch him. I guess we will have to just live with this, more likely die with this!” But Buns Rabbit was not the kind to give up. He thought of a plan. The next day Merry Monkey went to the lion and said, “My majestic lord! You are so mighty, you are lord of us all. But you know what? Buns Rabbit says he has seen someone even more powerful than you.” Upon hearing this Terro Lion roared. He asked Merry to go and send Buns Rabbit to him. The clever Buns came up to Terro. “Hey Buns, you puny fellow," roared Terro. "What’s all this nonsense about a more powerful lion than me in the jungle?" Buns said, “My lord, you are indeed mighty. Forgive me, I am just telling what I saw. I saw a huge lion yesterday.” Terro roared aloud, “Where is he? I will have him for breakfast today! There is no one more mighty than me. Take me to him.” The clever Buns took Terro to a lake. He then pointed to the water in the lake and said, “My lord, I saw the huge lion cooling off in this lake.” Terro peeped into the water. He saw his own face in the water. He roared loudly. He saw his image in the water roaring back at him. He was so angry, that he forgot everything, even that he didn’t know how to swim. “How dare you roar back at mighty me. I will finish you.” He cried and jumped right into the lake. Terro drowned. Buns Rabbit happily took the news of Terro’s end to the other animals. There was joy in the jungle. Moral of The Story: Focusing on solutions rather than problems is the key takeaway from this story.
author: Vishwadeep Pawar
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Avishek Sen; Mahbubur  Rahman; Padmanabh; Princy Rawat; Rob Owen; Robert McEwan; Sanjay Sarkar

title: Meera and The Rainbow Rat: A Tale of Kindness, Forgiveness, and being Organised
text: Once upon a time, there was a six-year-old girl named Meera. She was a happy-go-lucky and playful child. Meera was smart and loved talking to people. However, she wasn’t very good at keeping things tidy. Her wardrobe was often messy, and when she took food from the fridge, she would sometimes leave crumbs, which attracted ants. Meera's mother, who was usually very loving, would get upset about this and sometimes scold Meera, which made her sad. Behind their garden, there was a small jungle. One night, a rat came to their garden looking for food. But this was no ordinary rat it was a beautiful rainbow-colored rat. It was a cold and wet pre-monsoon night. The rat was very hungry and searched everywhere for food. Meera's mother often fed birds in the backyard, but the crumbs had become wet. Desperate for food, the rat looked towards the house. It climbed up a pipe to a window and slipped inside the kitchen. But the kitchen was clean. Then, the rat sniffed the air and found the fridge. It tried several times to jump up to the handle but kept slipping off. Finally, with one big jump, it managed to grab the handle and open the fridge. Inside, the rat found mangoes, cheese, bread, cake, chocolate, milk, and more. It ate everything it could find, spilling food everywhere. Now looking like a plump rainbow ball, the rat struggled to move. It dragged itself to the adjacent room, Meera’s toy room, and made a mess by jumping on the toys and nibbling on a small blanket. Exhausted, it fell asleep on the couch. In the morning, the family woke up to a huge mess. Meera’s mother was very upset. Meera was sad to see her favorite cookies, cakes, and chocolates gone. They followed the trail of crumbs and found the mess in Meera’s toy room. Meera was angry and upset to see her favorite blanket in pieces. Then, she noticed a rainbow-colored ball of fur on the couch. She touched it, and to everyone’s surprise, it was a rat! The whole family was amazed to see a rainbow-colored rat. The rat was terrified and shrank into a corner. Meera’s mother wanted to hit the rat and throw it out. But Meera, looking into the rat’s eyes, said, "No, Mummy, we must forgive the rat. Look at him, he’s just a rat. He must be playful like me and very hungry. Let’s not punish him. Punishment makes people feel hurt and sad. I don’t want to do that to this cute rat. I never feel good when I get scolded for my mischievous behavior." Meera’s mother understood what Meera meant. Her heart melted, and she said, "Meera, I’m sorry. Sometimes I get too upset when I see the mess and scold you. I shouldn’t do that. I love you, my daughter." Meera hugged her mother and said, "Mummy, I also understand now how it feels when someone makes a mess. I will try my best to be more organized." Daddy said, "That’s wonderful, Meera. We will help you." Meanwhile, the rat felt safe when it saw that the people were not going to harm it. Meera gently approached the rat and said, "Dear rat, we will keep some food for you under the tree." Daddy caught the rat in a basket and released it into the backyard. From the next day on, they kept some food outside for the rat, and Meera often got to see her rainbow rat. The rat became fearless and looked at Meera with love. Meera also started keeping her things tidy and stopped spreading food mess. Mummy became more loving and forgiving. She even got Meera a soft toy rat made of rainbow colors, which became Meera’s favorite toy. And so, Meera and her family lived happily, always remembering to be kind and forgiving.
author: Rituraj Mishra
illustrator: Deepa Balsavar; El Huyno; Kabini  Amin; Ketan Raut; Partho Sengupta; Rituraj Mishra; Sujan  Chitrakar

title: The Adventures of Lucy- The AI Dominance_chapter 2
text: She sat on the chair uncomfortably. Lucy’s mother had wanted a simple brunch at a simple restaurant, so they had only hired a yacht and ordered simple dishes like herbed vegan mushroom pate and absheron saffron rice sweets. The world had become health conscious in the late 90’s, so most people had converted to vegetarianism. Another reason for the increasing number of vegetarians was that most animals had gone extinct. Lucy, her aged mother, 50 year old aunt and 17 year old cousin sat at the table and ate in silence. Lucy was quiet enjoying the silence, before her mother broke it by saying, “So, as soon as you get your job, you’ll be assigned a child.” “Yes, mother. Everyone knows that,” lucy said unenthusiastically. Prentista Fizzorlemy had invented a way to create children. This way the humans did not need to worry about their children not doing what they were told or having bad manners. When one turned 30, he or she simply walked into a child centre and chose a child to raise. When the child turned 18, he or she no longer needed a parent and moved away. “So, Derrinmet, are you excited to be moving away? After all, your birthday is next month.” “Nah, not really.” An AI assistant came up to them and said, “anything else you would like, ma’am?” “Oh, I’m stuffed. Eating real food is a real bother because we have to diges t it,” my mom said with a disgusted face. “I’ll have a chocolate smoothie pill please,” my aunt said. “Ooh, can I have a salad pill?” Derrinment asked. “Most certainly not, Derrinment, since you did not have any breakfast this morning even though I insisted,” His mother replied without any mercy. The AI assistant took down her order and went away to get the pill. Lucy turned to Derrin and whispered in his ear, “is it just me, or did that assistant have red eyes?” “I’m sure it was just you, lucy,” he whispered back. The AI assistant came back and lucy was determined not to look at her; she seemed to be having a hallucination. But finally, she couldn’t stare at the plate anymore and looked up at the assistant’s eyes. They were the standard blue issued to all AI assistants. The three you ladies walked off board the yacht along with the teenage boy. They parted with hugs and kisses and lucy walked over to her trancellint with difficulty and sat down, relieved to rest her legs from the 5-metre-long walk. The trancellint glided over the path to her home and lucy was just starting to relax when Belinda said, “you have a mest from Derrinmet.” It read: “you were right. The assistant’s eyes were red, they changed colour to blue when two people were looking at it.”
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: How not to be cold
text: It was a very cold winter day. I didn't want to go out on a cold day Grandma! Can we not go outside? It's so cold. I want to stay in a warm house today. It was a very cold winter day. Oh, you can't. Today is Thursday and you have to go to school. Be patient even if it's a little cold. It's warm inside. It was so cold on the way to school that my teeth were pounding. My hands looked like they were going to freeze. I was annoyed with my mom all the way to school. It was so cold that I felt like I was going to become a snowman. Grandma, it was really cold today. Grandma is bad! Haha, it gets colder when you think it's cold. If you think it's not cold, it doesn't get cold. You're lying! Seriously. If in doubt, try it on your way to school tomorrow. It'll feel less cold really. The next day was also very, very cold. Maybe it was colder than yesterday. I also thought of a way she taught me, looking down on my annoyance. Every step I take, “I'm not cold, I'm not cold.” I murmured. Like a lie, it really felt less cold. I was able to go to school with lighter steps than yesterday.

title: Dream
text: In a small village, there was always a child who dreamed of traveling around the world and experiencing different cultures. After the child grew up a little over time, the child decides to leave the journey. However, the child knew that need money to travel. So, the child start working hard to save money by itself. title: Benny the Brave Bunny
text: Once upon a time, in a sunny meadow filled with colorful flowers and tall, swaying grass, lived a little bunny named Benny. Benny was a fluffy, brown bunny with big, bright eyes and a tiny pink nose that wiggled when he was curious. Benny loved to hop around the meadow and play with his friends, the other animals. But sometimes, Benny felt a little scared of new things. He always stayed close to his cozy little burrow, where he felt safe. One morning, Benny woke up to a strange sound. "Hoo-hoo! Hoo-hoo!" It was an owl named Oliver, who had just moved into the big oak tree at the edge of the meadow. Benny's friend, Sally the squirrel, scampered over to him. "Come on, Benny! Let's go meet Oliver the Owl. He's really nice!" Benny felt a bit nervous, but he took a deep breath and decided to be brave. "Okay, let's go," he said, hopping along with Sally. When they reached the oak tree, Oliver the Owl looked down with his big, friendly eyes. "Hello, little friends!" he hooted. "Would you like to play a game with me?" Benny's nose twitched with curiosity. "What kind of game?" he asked. " To eat both of you". The Owl answered in a scary voice. He started to catch Sally first but he lost his grip and the squirrel fell on the ground. Benny and Sally ran from the Owl's Oak tree and hid in their houses. After that day neither of them nor the Bunny nor the Squirrel had seen the Owl and they lived happily ever after.

title: The Story of a Cricket Lover (part-1)
text: Chapter 1:- The Rise from Betrayal:- In the bustling city of Hyderabad, where the streets echoed with the fervour of cricket, there lived a young boy named Vicky. Cricket wasn't just a sport to him; it was his passion, his dream, his escape from the mundane realities of life. Vicky's father, a hardworking man, recognized his son's love for the game. Despite their modest means, he saved every penny he could to buy Vicky a cricket kit. When he presented it to his son, Vicky's eyes sparkled with joy and gratitude. Excited to hone his skills, Vicky planned to attend the selections at the prestigious cricket school in Hyderabad. He shared his enthusiasm with his friend Arjun, who shared his love for the game. Together, they envisioned practicing side by side, their dreams intertwined like the stitches on a cricket ball. However, fate had a different plan in store. As the day of selections approached, doubts crept into Arjun's mind. What if they didn't allow them to share the kit? Fearful of missing his chance, Arjun succumbed to temptation and stole Vicky's cherished kit, leaving his friend behind. Heartbroken and crestfallen, Vicky watched as Arjun disappeared into the distance, carrying not just his kit, but a piece of his dream. The weight of betrayal crushed him, shattering his confidence and leaving him doubting his worth. Unable to muster the courage to face the selectors without his kit, Vicky stayed home on the day of the selections, his spirit bruised but not broken. While Arjun's name was among the chosen thirty, Vicky's dreams seemed to slip further from his grasp. But amidst the darkness, a glimmer of hope emerged. Determined not to let adversity define him, Vicky scraped together his meager pocket money and bought himself a cricket bat—a symbol of resilience and determination. As he practiced alone in the quiet corners of his neighborhood, a stranger's eyes fell upon him. Intrigued by the dedication and skill displayed by this young boy, the selector approached Vicky and struck up a conversation. Moved by Vicky's story and impressed by his talent, the selector saw something special in him—a spark that refused to be extinguished. Without hesitation, he offered Vicky a place among the chosen few, his own money buying him a brand new kit, a beacon of hope in a world fraught with disappointment. And so, against all odds, Vicky's journey continued, fueled by passion, perseverance, and the unwavering belief in his dreams. For in the game of cricket, as in life, it's not just about the trials we face, but how we rise above them, emerging stronger, wiser, and ready to conquer the challenges that lie ahead. The Rise Of A Young Talent:- As Vicky grew up and became the best cricketer in the camp, he turned 13 and his coach suggested that he could try his luck in the Hyderabad Ranji Team. The selectors were shocked by his skill. Vicky was sure he was going to get selected in the team. But fate had something else in store for him. He wasn’t even named in the 30 probables. Confused and disheartened, he went to the selection committee to confirm whether there was a printing mistake. But they said if he could arrange 5,00,000 by the end of the day, he could get a spot on the final 15-member squad. Vicky was shocked by this; he hadn't expected such a demand. Unable to gather the money as his family was poor, Vicky had no choice but to return to his school in Hyderabad. That Ranji season, Hyderabad came last, losing all matches. Most of the members in the cricket board were suspended, and new selectors were given the job of selection. This time, Vicky was selected in the 15-member squad. But the coach always harbored a bias against him since he was poor and never gave him a chance to play in the 11 or in the nets. The only task assigned to him was cleaning the players' shoes and handing them water bottles during the matches. However, times changed for Vicky when he got a chance in the 11 for the last group stage match against Andhra Pradesh. This was an important match to qualify for the semifinals, especially since the team’s batting star Sunil Yadav (the highest run-scorer in the tournament) was injured. Vicky had to open the batting with the team’s captain Vikram Sahid. In the first over, Vikram Sahid hit 18 runs, displaying his exceptional skill. Then it was Vicky's turn in the second over. However, it didn't go as planned; he was clean bowled in his first Ranji innings. Despite Hyderabad being bowled out for 195 in the first innings, Andhra Pradesh managed to score (declared), leading by a big margin of 410 runs. In the second innings, Vicky was demoted down the order to no. 6. Hyderabad was struggling at when Vicky walked in. Determined to prove himself, Vicky went on to score an incredible 300 runs, the highest score on debut. Despite his remarkable performance, Hyderabad managed to secure only a 38-run lead, and Andhra Pradesh won the match by 10 wickets. Even though they lost this marked the spark of a young talent Vicky. The next season turned out to be Vicky's best season, both with bat and ball. He became the highest run-scorer with 2008 runs and 21 wickets in 12 innings, leading Hyderabad to victory in the tournament. Vicky was awarded the player of the tournament, marking a significant milestone in his career. Everything seemed to be going well for him, and he even got selected for the Indian team. However, tragedy struck on the match day when his father passed away. It was a tough choice for him to choose between his passion and his family, but he decided to play the match in honor of his father. With determination in his heart, Vicky scored a century and kept his bat near his father’s photo, a tribute to the man who had supported his dreams despite the odds.
author: KOLASANI HARSHITH

title: Getting Better
text: Once upon a time, there was a young girl who had no interest in books and studying, but instead loved to play. when she graduated from elementary school, Her father said, "Next week, we are leaving for England." And so, due to her father's job transfer, Jiwon's family moved to England. ﻿ Woooooow! It's England!!!! While the new scenery brought her joy for a moment, Jiwon was soon faced with the reality of a new country... language... and school. This made her think, "Can I really do this?". Jiwon felt uncertain and lacked confidence. During class, Jiwon couldn't understand what the teacher was saying. She was unable to write down the assignment given by the teacher. Her classmates made fun of her pronunciation. They avoided being paired up with her because of her poor English skills. "Mom, I wanna go back to Korea!" Jiwon said, crying. "Oh Darling… it's okay. This is just because it's new to you." her mom said. "Is that so?" Jiwon replied. "Don't worry. Time will ease your pain." her mom said. A year passed... "Mom! I can now understand English!" Jiwon exclaimed. Another year passed... "Mom! I can have conversations with people!” Jiwon exclaimed. Another year passed... "Mom! I became a translator for my new Korean friend!" Jiwon exclaimed. Jiwon is no longer afraid. Jiwon had now become someone who could comfort and support others. Jiwon has become proficient in English!!

title: The Story Of A Cricket Lover(Part 3)
text: As the euphoria of India's World Cup victory settled, Vicky's battle with cancer entered a new phase—one fraught with uncertainty and fear. Despite the triumph on the cricket field, the harsh reality of his illness loomed large, casting a shadow over his newfound fame and glory. For Vicky, the days blurred into a haze of hospital visits, chemotherapy sessions, and the constant struggle to find solace amidst the pain and uncertainty. Yet, even in the darkest of moments, he refused to succumb to despair, drawing strength from the memories of his father's unwavering support and the countless messages of encouragement from fans around the world. As the months wore on, Vicky's resolve was put to the ultimate test. The toll of his illness was evident in his gaunt frame and weakened body, yet his spirit remained unbroken, a beacon of hope for all who knew him. In the midst of his battle, Vicky found solace in the game that had been his lifelong passion. Despite the physical toll of his illness, he continued to follow cricket with unwavering devotion, cheering on his beloved teammates from the sidelines and offering words of wisdom and encouragement whenever he could. But as the months turned into years, the toll of his illness became increasingly apparent. The once-fierce competitor was now a shadow of his former self, his body weakened by the relentless onslaught of cancer. Yet, even in his darkest moments, Vicky's spirit remained indomitable. With each passing day, he found new reserves of strength within himself, drawing inspiration from the countless battles he had fought and won on the cricket field. And then, just when it seemed like all hope was lost, a miracle occurred. Through the tireless efforts of his doctors and the unwavering support of his loved ones, Vicky's condition began to improve. The cancer that had once threatened to consume him now receded, like a distant storm dissipating on the horizon. In the months that followed, Vicky's recovery defied all expectations. Slowly but surely, he regained his strength and vitality, his once-feeble body now infused with new life and vigor. And then, in a moment that seemed almost too good to be true, Vicky received the news he had longed to hear—he was cancer-free. The weight that had hung heavy on his shoulders for so long now lifted, replaced by a sense of joy and gratitude that seemed almost overwhelming. With his illness behind him, Vicky set his sights on a new challenge—the opportunity to give back to the game that had given him so much. Through his foundation, he worked tirelessly to support young cricketers from underprivileged backgrounds, providing them with the resources and opportunities they needed to pursue their dreams. And as he looked back on his journey—from the dusty streets of Hyderabad to the pinnacle of cricketing glory—Vicky knew that his greatest victory was not on the cricket field, but in the resilience and strength of the human spirit, a lesson he would carry with him for the rest of his days.

title: The frog who could not jump
text: Once upon a time, there was a frog who couldn’t jump. He was depressed because everybody else could jump but him. Other frogs used to tease him because he couldn’t jump. So he walked instead… While he walked, he found a witches hut, but he did not know it belonged to a witch. But then the witch returned home… The frog got frightened by the witch he saw. When he was running from the witch, he fell into the pond, but thankfully, landed on a boot. He slowly drifted into the centre of the river. So he slowly leaped to nearby lilly pad. So he bravely leaped to the end of the river, and found out that he could jump all along!! so he was extremely happy. The end.

She dominates the diving board, she tromps the trampoline, At lifting weights and wrestling, she's the best you've ever seen. She's highest in high jump and a champ at hammer throwing, Magnificent in marathons, remarkable at rowing. title: Diving
text: We set off on a small boat, expecting a big adventure!!! When we arrived at the dive site, we carefully checked all our equipment and put on our frog shoes and masks. Once in the water, we were greeted by a school of yellow-backed fish. What a variety of creatures can be seen around this large coral: oriental grunts, parrot fish, bat fish, and large beautifully patterned water snails. To learn more about the creatures in bold, turn to the back of the book. The trumpet fish changes color to blend in with the yellow tang shoal, but you should be able to spot it easily, right? We should keep our distance from lionfish. The spines on its back are quite poisonous! These clownfish guarded their anemone home carefully, but eventually they let me take a few photos. We saw a honeycomb moray eel whose teeth were being cleaned by two cleaner fish, and another pair of fish even rubbed our hands! There are also fish chickens and sea urchins, We even saw coral grouper and coral octopus playing hide and seek. (English) Ada juga ayam ikan dan bulu babi, Kami bahkan melihat ikan kerapu karang dan gurita karang bermain petak umpet. (Indonesia) Octopuses win the game. They are good at hiding. Pipe fish are too. Can you find the two pipefish in this picture? We met a pair of reef sharks resting near the seabed. They were harmless, so we swam closer for a better look. We follow a hawksbill turtle as it searches for sea sponges around the reef for its lunch. when returning to the boat, we were surprised by a manta ray "flying" through the water with two remora fish in tow. And when we thought this dive was impossible to continue, we spotted a dugong feeding on seaweed. What an amazing experience! I can't wait to dive again! Coral reefs are both plants and animals. Thousands of tiny algae live inside corals, giving them energy to grow. Coral reefs have a hard exoskeleton and grow in many different shapes. Plankton is the main food of many marine animals. Plankton is a combination of algae, bacteria, small animals and their eggs, and the larvae of larger animals carried by ocean currents. Sea lilies may look like plants, but they are actually animals. Sea lilies use their feather-like "arms" to catch and eat plankton carried by the currents. Parrot fish have strong teeth shaped like a parrot's beak, which they use to scrape algae off hard corals. Some species eat a little coral too, and they discard it in the form of fine sand that is washed ashore, forming beautiful white sandy beaches. Clownfish and sea anemones live together and help each other. Clownfish help clean the anemone's tentacles and attract other fish to feed on the anemone. In return, the anemone lets the clownfish hide among its poisonous tentacles without stinging them. Cleaner fish are small fish that keep larger fish clean by eating parasites and dead skin on larger fish. Larger fish recognize cleaner fish by their color and the way they move. The reef octopus can hide by changing its own color and texture. Reef octopuses make nests in holes in the reef, or bury themselves in the sand. Pipefish can be found in pairs, swimming with their heads down and hiding among seaweed, coral, or sea lilies. Like the reef octopus, pipefish can change color to blend in perfectly. White-finned reef sharks have slender bodies, broad heads, and white patches on the dorsal and caudal fins. They hunt at night, and sleep throughout the day. Hawksbill turtles have flat bodies, jagged shells, and sharp, curved mouths like an eagle's beak. The manta ray is a large fish with wing-like fins on both sides of its body. These wide fins help the manta ray swim fast in the water. From tip to tip, the fin length of some manta rays can reach seven meters! Dugongs are plant-eating marine mammals. Its favorite food is seaweed, which it can chew with its distinctive snout. Mermaids are also often called sea oxen.
author: raihan syadid

title: how far is it?
text: It would be strange to say that the ceiling of a room is as tall as 3 baby elephants. So we make the reasonable choice to say that the height of the ceiling is 3 meters. Step 1: 10 meters Now that you've gotten a feel for the one-meter step, we're ready to move on to the next staircase, the 10-meter step. A three-story building or a mannga tree is about 10 meters tall. A cricket pitch is about twice that length. Can you think of anything else that is about 10 meters long or tall? 2:100 meter step Have you noticed that with each step, we add a zero to the right of the number we had before and the number of steps matches the number of zeros? Stay focused as we climb. If you've taken part in a 100m race on sports day at school, or watched sprinters do it on TV, you know how far it is. Now imagine if a 100m track stood! It would be about the height of two Gumbaz*-es goals. Step 3: 1000 meters A thousand meters has a special name - it's called 1 kilometer or 1 km. You would cover this distance if you ran a 100-meter race 10 times - wow! You would have to hike about 9 km to reach the top of Mount Everest. Step 6: 10,00,000 meters now let's skip 2 steps and go to step 6, which has six zeros to the right of the number 1. The distance from the northern tip of India at Khasmir to the southern tip at Kanyakumari is about 4 times this distance, or 4 times 10,00,000m or 40,00,000m. since 40,00,000m is a hassle, we usually say 4000km, which means the same thing. Step 8: 10,00,00,000 meters How far away is that bright, beautiful moon? It's there on step 8 of our distance ladder at about 4 times 10,00,00,000 m, or 4,00,000 km from earth! step 11: 1,00,00,00,00,000 meters let's skip two more steps and continue to the blazing sun. how far is that? About 10,00,00,000 km ADDED to another 5,00,00,000 km. That's VERY far indeed! But the far, far away sun still lights up the world and makes us sweat in the summer. Amazing, isn't it? Last step? Is there a last step on the stairs? We don't know yet! but with powerful telescopes, scientists have been able to see far beyond the sun. the farthest object they could see was on the 26th step which is 10,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,000 m away! that's SO FAR away! Maybe when you grow up, you can find something further away, at the 28th or 29th step. Isn't that an interesting thought? Fun with measuring activities The following classroom activities are a great way for children to understand long distances by involving children in a group, or in teams. 1. Ask children to cut long strips (each one inch wide) from old newspapers. 2. Ask them to attach the strips end-to-end with tape or glue to make longer strips, until they get a strip that is 1 meter long (they can use a tape measure). 3. Now ask the children to use this 1 m long strip as a measure and make 10 similar strips and stick them end to end to make a 10 m long strip. They can lie next to these strips, head to head and foot to foot, and see how many of them it takes to make 10 m. 4. They can then stick ten 10m strips together to make a 100m strip that goes around the classroom many times. 5. What about a 1 km strip? How many times can it be done around the classroom? Which team is able to create a 1 km strip the fastest? Note to Parents & Teachers: Point 1 - When writing large numbers with many zeros after the number 1, it is very easy for children - and adults! - to make mistakes. That's why 'Magnitude 10' notation is so useful. Through this book, children can be taught how to use it - all they need to do is count the number of zeros to the right of 1, and write that number as a power of 10. For example, 1000, which has 3 zeros after the number 1, can be written 103. And 10000000 (7 zeros after the number 1), can be written briefly as 107. Simple! Point 2 - In this book, we limit the 'How far is far?' game to the level of the sun's distance. If you want to play further, perhaps you can determine the closest star after the sun, Proxima Centauri, which is 1016m away from the sun. Or the distance from one end of the Milky Way to the other, which is 1,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,00,000 (or 1021) m! Point 3 - One thing you should know is that the distances given in this book are approximate, not absolutely accurate. For example, 3984 km is shown as 4000 km. This does not mean it is 'unscientific'. Rough estimates are very useful in science! Perhaps you could do an activity with the children to emphasize this point. Is the length of a pencil closer to 101 cm or 102 cm? Is the weight of a school bus closer to 103 kg or 104 kg? Let the children come up with their own questions for their classmates too.

title: The Boy who Dreamed
text: Chunnu is an eight yearold boy who lives in a village with his parents. He is an expert at sleeping and dreaming. No matter what time of the day it is; Chunnu can fall asleep. Even when he had just woken up, he could fall back asleep within the next ten minutes. Even his mother has given up on his dreaming habit. While, many people call him lazy, but Chunnu knows he is not lazy. He just likes to dream. In his sleep, he has the most beautiful dreams. Chunnu found his dreams very marvelous. He could do many different things in his dreams and he always felt happy. One day, he dreamed that he was a brilliant magician who could turn a wild school mouse into a wooden plank. He saw himself surrounded by his classmates who admired and praised his talent. Even the cleanest Didi, who was always upset with the children, smiled at his magic. In another day, he dreamed that he was the best drummer in his region. He could play drum beats to different songs, even the ones people saw on TV. Chunnu dreamed as if he was a hero in a movie who could easily drum, sing, and dance at the same time with a whole group of small children from his neighborhood dancing to his song. Chunnu never dreamed the same dream. One day he dreamed of having a stallion like a king. This was not ordinary stallion. The stallion in Chunnu's dream was his best friend and would only listen to Chunnu's instructions. Chunnu dreamed that he would travel around the whole city on his stallion and never feel tired again. One day, Chunnu forgot to wake up from his sleep. He continued his dream for a long time, where he walked out of the house in his sleep. He didn't realize that he was still wearing his nightshirt. Every child along the way laughed as Chunnu sang loudly with his eyes closed. But Chunnu didn't know because he was busy dreaming. With an unseen miracle, Chunnu's feet carried him to school. Chunnu's teacher who was a very nice girl, knew Chunnu's dreaming habits. She woke him up and gave him a spare shirt to wear. That day, the teacher taught the children about how important to dream and at the same time taught how important to strive to make dreams come true. Chunnu was very concerned in class that day. His teacher said, "You can dream of being happy, but by doing good things for others, you can be truly happy." Chunnu understood what his teacher was saying. That day while back from school, Chunnu saw a boy without a shirt. He was shivering and sad. Chunnu took his nightshirt which was still kept in his bag and gave it to the boy. It was not a dream and Chunnu felt happy. The next morning, Chunnu gave a loaf of bread to a poor woman selling pottery on her way to school. Chunnu knew that she was struggling to earn enough money to feed herself and her baby. He decided to bring a portion of food to the woman every day. She asked her mother about it and her mother was happy to help her. From that day on, Chunnu helped people in need. He still dreams but only at night. It was a miracle, Chunnu felt happy even when he wasn't dreaming.
