title: Voracious sparrows
text: This is the story of a sparrow named Gubi. One day, he brought home a big and sweet red guava. When Gubi flew over a field, the fruit slipped from the clasp of his beak and fell into a thorny bush. How upset Gubi was! He was determined to try all means to get her back. Gubi approached the young man working in the fields. "Son, get my guava fruit that fell in the thorny bush," he pleaded pleadingly. "Ah, don't want to!" he replied. "Go away!" Gubi was furious, and complained to the farmer's uncle who owned the field. "Uncle, my guava fell on a thorny bush. I asked the young man to pick it up, but he wouldn't! Punish him!" requested Gubi. "Ah, don't want to!" replied the farmer's uncle. "Go away!" Gubi approached a cow that was grazing in the field. "My guava fruit fell on a thorny bush! The boy didn"t want to take it. I complained to the farmer's uncle, but he wouldn't punish him! Well, you eat whatever is in the farmer's uncle's field!" Gubi exclamation. "Ah, no way!" the cow mooed and moved away. Gubi flies to a fisherman. "My guava fruit fell on a thorny bush! The young man working in the fields wouldn't help me, the farmer's uncle wouldn't punish him, and the cow didn't care. Whip the cow!" Gubi's instigation. "Ah, no way!" replied the fisherman busy casting his nets. Gubi then approached the mouse. "My guava fruit fell on a thorny bush in the field. The young man who worked there wouldn't help me, nor would the farmer's uncle and his cow. The fisherman also refused to help me. Just tear the fisherman's net with your sharp teeth!" "Ah, no way!" squeaked the mouse as it scurried away. Next, Gubi tried to approach the cat. "My guava fruit fell on a thorny bush in the field and no one wanted to help me; a young man working in the fields, a farmer's uncle, a cow, a fisherman, and finally a mouse! You just catch the mouse!" the cat chimed in, "Ah, no way!" Gubi is running out of ideas. No one is subject to his will. Aha! He suddenly remembered the ants. Surely the little bug would help him! He flew to the anthill. "Will you bite a cat, to avenge what it did to me?" the ant replied, "Sure! Which cat are you referring to?" Ants obeyed Gubi's command, biting the cat. The cat runs in pain after a mouse. The mouse escapes the cat and bites the fisherman's net. Fishermen scramble to whip cows. The cow went amok and destroyed the farmer's uncle's field. The farmer's uncle was upset that cows were destroying his fields, so he punished the young man., The young man picked the red guava fruit in the bush with difficulty. Gubi is satisfied because he managed to get what he wanted! The greedy Gubi hurried away, about to savour the guava alone. He perched on a branch to feast on guava. Just after the first bite, suddenly... gubrak! A flop flying past with a branch of firewood in its beak accidentally dropped the branch on Gubi's head. Gubi also fell unconscious and failed to enjoy his guava fruit. That's the reward for a greedy Gubi!
author: Imelda Tasya

title: Gul in Space
text: I want the stars wish for me. Moon and sun too I wake up in the morning. And look! There is rocket waiting outside. I try to hide my happiness. The rocket is all fired up. All my bags are packed an full. "Whoosss!" It roars and shoots up. I`m astronaut Madam Gul!. My cat shakes and trembles in fear. I feel my head spinning around and round In the few of minutes, we are high above the earth. Six hour later, here is my new house in space. They call it Space Station; Hello, Beautiful place! Boing! We jump step by step. I almost could`nt feel my legs Before we realized it, our bodies turned upside down! Then, we start to floating... to the right and to the left We floating in the air, and turning to the side. Oops! My bag turns upside down and two of jelebies came out from my bag. The samosa that i packed so well became a mess. The crumbs of foods and juice are sticky and start to bump around and float. I choose special packed food of space My hair are sticky. My clothes are messy. My cat licks me to clean me. Actually, taking a shower is the best choice. But, there is a little secret: in space there are no water tap. I slightly wet the towel and wipe my face. Then take a bit of shampoo and run it through my hair. Now my hair looks clean. I`m wearing a spacesuit on the special day! come with me to have fun in space! Little by little i crawled outside. It was dark, cold, and quiet outside. The stars were shining brightly. They looked so close and big. The moon smiled at me as if say "Happy birthday my dear, Gul" Now it`s time to me to go back and rest. Walking on the space was exhausting. Terrifying, but very excasting. This is a place where i sleep. My bed for the few time. It`s funny, we lie down while wearing a belt. After a while, i woke up. We dont have to waste the time. Firstly, i brushed my tooth And i swallowed the toothpaste! I want to talk to Ammi. I put the belt on the laptop "Hello, who is this?" she cried from other side "I`m Gul from space!" i told her everything i have done. Also about the wonderful space. About the shape of earth from afar. About the funny of this station. I have been living at space for two whole months. Now it`s time to go back home. From afar we hear children who want to go to the moon. Raise your hand if that's you. Pack your things. My cat and I are going home tonight. Soon, it will be your turn. Did you know? -You have to sit in a rocket to go into space. There are several different types of rockets, but the one that is used most often is the one that Gul and her cat rode in. It took them to the International Space Station (SLAI), where Gul spent two months in space. They used a Soyuz spacecraft to return to Earth from SLAI. -There are spaceships that fly from Earth to SLAI, carrying special packaged food and water, as well as other items that astronauts need during their stay. Gul has to be careful using water on the space station. Every drop of water is precious. - Gul and other things inside the SLAI float like balloons. Anything that is not belted in will float because all objects are weightless in space. When these floating objects approach the earth, they are drawn into the earth's layer called the atmosphere. Friction with the atmosphere causes these objects to burn up, so they do not reach the earth. -In SLAI there are no water taps because water cannot flow in the environment without gravity. So Gul uses a special shampoo that doesn't require rinsing. She also swallows her toothpaste. If Gul accidentally leaves the water container open, the water droplets will float in space, then coalesce to form a large ball of water.

title: My first cat
text: There was a cat. It was thrown away in a box because it was very sick from birth. The cat was too scary and hungry. However, somewhere a girl's voice was heard along with footsteps. Then suddenly, the sound stopped and light came in. It turned out that the girl walking on the street had opened a box. Upon opening the box, the girl saw a baby cat. Realizing that the cat had been abandoned, the girl brought milk and fed the cat. At first, the cat refused, but eventually, being hungry, the cat fell asleep while drinking the milk. Upon waking from sleep, the cat found itself at the girl's house. It was very scared because it was in an unfamiliar place. The girl held the scared cat in her arms, feeling sorry for it. Yelin l: Hi, my name is Yelin. Don't be scared, this is our house. I will be your family from now on. The cat felt relieved and opened its heart to the girl's words. Afterwards, the girl overcame her lonely past like Leon, who became happy by meeting true love in a lonely life under the name of a cat, and named her Leon to live happily in the future. True joy came to Leon as he found his family. He was happy every day. His family believed that Leon would get better. However, Leon was still in pain. And he knew he would soon leave. So he wanted to spend happy times with his family. Leon: I will soon have to leave. I have to make my family happy for the remaining time. On the first day, I sat on the father's lap who was reading a book, sang a song, and told him that I love him. On the second day, I climbed up onto my mother's legs while she was resting from cleaning, and told her that I love her. And on the last third day, I played happily with my beloved Yelin, laid down together, and fell asleep together. When Yelin fell asleep, Leon got up, kissed Yelin's cheek, and told her that he loves her. Cat: Yelin, I was so happy to meet you. Thank you for becoming my family, I love you. I will go first, so let's meet again in the future, I love you. Leon bid farewell to the sleeping Yerin and left this world. Yelin: Farewell, my first cat Leon. We will meet again!
author: 예린 장

title: Neema's Birthday
text: She asked her friends, "Do you have the same birthday with me? Mom said I was born on February 29." It turned out that none of their birth dates were the same as her's. Neema asked her mother, "Ma! Last year we didn't celebrate my birthday. Why does my friend Anna get to celebrate it every year?" Her mother answered, "Be patient, Neema. Your birthday is coming up. We'll have a big party for you. We will invite all your friends." "But, Ma, last year I was looking forward to it. Till the end of the year, my birthday still didn't exist," said Neema. "On Anna's birthday, we gave her a lot of gifts and congratulations. We ate and sang a beautiful song. Everyone was happy. I also wanted to invite all my friends so we could eat, play, and sing together." "Don't worry, Neema," said her mother. "Your birthday is next week, isn't it? Let's make it a big birthday party." But Neema didn't believe it. What if her birthday didn't come like last year? Then, the next week, on February 29! Neema was really excited. It was finally her birthday! "It's my birthday!" she shouted. Neema's friends arrived. Everyone brought gifts. Her parents also gave her a gift, a colorful birthday hat. She looked beautiful! Neema looked at all the gifts. There were so many! Neema's mother said, "Neema, your birthday is celebrated in a leap year, which only happens every four years." ﻿ "Thank you, Papa. Thank you, Mama. See you, on February 29th! I will see you in four years!"
author: Zakiyah _26

title: The Tapestry of Two Brothers
text: Marcus were born. Two brothers, inseparable in childhood, yet destined to diverge as they matured. Elias, the elder by two years, possessed an innate affinity for the land. From a tender age, his hands had learned to coax life from the earth, nurturing crops that sustained their family through years of plenty and scarcity alike. His broad shoulders bore the weight of responsibility with quiet strength, his mornings beginning with the rising sun and ending with the tired satisfaction of a day's labor well spent. Marcus, in contrast, was a soul enraptured by the mysteries beyond the village boundaries. His curiosity was boundless, his nimble feet carrying him over the mossy trails of the nearby forest, where ancient trees whispered tales of forgotten times. The villagers often shook their heads at his wanderlust, marveling at his ability to disappear for days only to return with stories that painted the world beyond in vivid hues. Their childhood was a blend of Elias's grounded stability and Marcus's unquenchable thirst for adventure. Together, they navigated the trials of youth—scraped knees healed with Elias's gentle hands, secret hideouts discovered by Marcus's keen eyes, and dreams shared under the vast expanse of starlit skies. As they grew older, however, the differences that had once colored their bond began to stretch it thin. Elias found solace in the predictable rhythms of village life, content to marry his childhood sweetheart, Anna, and raise a family rooted in the traditions of their ancestors. Marcus, on the other hand, felt the pull of distant horizons calling to him. His insatiable hunger for knowledge led him beyond the hills, to cities where scholars traded wisdom like coins and merchants spoke in the language of opportunity. Their paths diverged, each following the whisperings of their hearts. Elias's days were marked by the toil of the fields and the laughter of his children echoing through their modest home. Marcus traversed seas and traversed mountains, his mind expanding with every encounter, his heart seeking connections that spanned continents. Years turned into decades, and the brothers found themselves living separate lives, their interactions reduced to occasional letters that bridged the physical distance but struggled to traverse the emotional chasm that had grown between them. Elias, weathered by years spent under the sun, watched proudly as his children took their place in the cycle of planting and harvest, while Marcus amassed wealth and influence in distant lands, his name spoken in awe by those who had heard tales of his exploits. Yet, despite the miles that stretched between them, the bond of blood remained unbroken. In times of celebration and sorrow, Elias and Marcus found themselves drawn back to the village that had witnessed their beginnings. Anna's warm embrace welcomed Marcus as readily as it did Elias, and the villagers marveled at how the brothers, despite their differences, remained bound by an invisible thread that time could not fray. It was during one such visit that fate, in its inscrutable wisdom, wove a new chapter into their intertwined tale. The village, nestled comfortably in its routines, was shaken by the specter of drought. The fields that had once yielded bounty now lay parched and barren, and whispers of despair echoed through the streets. Elias, weather-beaten and determined, refused to yield to defeat. Day after day, he toiled under the unforgiving sun, his brow furrowed with worry for his family and his community. But despite his efforts, the land remained stubbornly unyielding, mocking his every attempt to coax life from its hardened surface. It was then that Marcus, hearing of his brother's plight from a passing traveler, felt a stirring in his heart that had long lain dormant. Without hesitation, he diverted his caravan from its planned course and turned towards the village that had once been his home. Laden with provisions gathered from the far corners of the known world, Marcus arrived on the outskirts of the village just as the sun dipped below the horizon. Elias, weary and disheartened, could scarcely believe his eyes when he saw Marcus's caravan approaching. Dust-covered and travel-worn, Marcus stepped down from his horse and embraced his brother, the years and the miles falling away in that moment of reunion. The villagers, drawn by the commotion, gathered around in hushed awe as Marcus unveiled the bounty he had brought—a testament to his brother's steadfastness and his own enduring love for the place they had once called home. In the days that followed, Marcus's presence breathed new life into the village. His knowledge of irrigation and trade, gleaned from years spent navigating foreign markets, transformed Elias's desperate attempts into a coordinated effort that saw water flowing once more to the thirsty fields. Together, they worked from sunrise to sunset, their hands moving in harmony as though they had never known the ache of separation. As the drought loosened its grip and life began to stir once more in the village, Elias and Marcus found themselves sitting beneath the same roof where their journey had begun. The years had etched lines into their faces and wisdom into their hearts, and yet the bond that bound them remained as strong as ever. "We make quite the team, don't we?" Marcus mused, his eyes twinkling with a mixture of pride and affection as he glanced at his brother. Elias chuckled softly, the sound carrying echoes of years spent sharing laughter and tears. "Aye, that we do," he agreed, clasping Marcus's shoulder in a gesture that spoke volumes of the unspoken gratitude between them. And so, beneath the watchful gaze of stars that had witnessed their childhood dreams and the enduring strength of the earth that had shaped their lives, Elias and Marcus found solace in the knowledge that their paths, though divergent, had always been intertwined—a tapestry woven with threads of brotherhood, resilience, and the unbreakable bonds of family.

title: THE NEVER ENDING NIGHTMARE
text: In the heart of a city's forgotten corner lies the Nexus, a place where Emily's nightmares manifest. Seeking answers, she confronts its ominous depths, unaware of the Weaver of Dreams lurking within—a malevolent force feeding on fears, ready to ensnare her in a perpetual nocturnal torment. In the heart of a bustling city, where the neon lights flickered like restless spirits against the midnight sky, there existed a place known only as the Nexus. It was a nondescript building tucked away in a forgotten corner of the metropolis, its entrance concealed behind layers of grime and indifference. To most, it was just another abandoned relic of urban decay, a shadowy reminder of forgotten dreams and broken promises. But to those who knew how to find it, the Nexus was a gateway to a realm beyond comprehension—a place where nightmares took on a life of their own, twisting reality into macabre shapes and feeding on the fears of those unfortunate enough to stumble upon its threshold. Among the few who dared to speak of the Nexus in hushed tones was Emily, a young woman whose life had been scarred by the tendrils of darkness that emanated from its depths. She was no stranger to fear; it had wrapped its icy fingers around her heart ever since that fateful night when her dreams had begun to unravel. It started innocently enough—a faint whisper in the silence of her sleep, a shadow that danced at the edge of her vision. At first, Emily dismissed it as the remnants of a stressful day or the overactive imagination of a tired mind. But as the nights wore on, the whispers grew louder, the shadows darker, until they coalesced into a nightmarish tapestry that threatened to consume her sanity. In desperation, Emily sought solace in the arms of sleep therapists and psychiatrists, hoping to unravel the tangled threads of her mind. They offered platitudes and prescriptions, but none could offer respite from the relentless torment that haunted her every waking moment. It was during one of her sleepless nights that Emily stumbled upon a mention of the Nexus—a fleeting reference in a dusty tome hidden in the depths of an occult bookstore. Intrigued and desperate for answers, she traced the breadcrumbs left by obscure references and cryptic warnings until she found herself standing before the unassuming facade of the Nexus. The building loomed before her like a silent sentinel guarding secrets too terrible to comprehend. Its walls were etched with graffiti that seemed to writhe and shift in the faint glow of the streetlights, words and symbols that pulsed with an otherworldly energy. With trembling hands, Emily pushed open the heavy door, the creak of hinges echoing like a mournful dirge in the stillness of the night. Inside, the Nexus was a labyrinth of dimly lit corridors and twisting staircases that seemed to defy logic and reason. The air was thick with the scent of decay and something more sinister, a palpable sense of malevolence that clung to the walls like a shroud. Emily's heart pounded in her chest as she navigated the maze-like passages, each step taking her deeper into the heart of darkness that had claimed her dreams. Shadows flitted at the edge of her vision, mocking whispers echoed through the empty halls, but she pressed on, driven by a desperate need to confront the source of her torment. It was then that she stumbled upon a chamber unlike any she had seen before—a vast, cavernous space bathed in an eerie half-light that seemed to emanate from the very walls themselves. In the center of the room stood a figure cloaked in shadows, its form shifting and twisting like smoke caught in a gust of wind.. "Who are you?" Emily demanded, her voice quivering with a mixture of fear and defiance. The figure turned towards her, its eyes glowing with a malevolent light that sent a chill down Emily's spine. "I am the Weaver of Dreams," it replied, its voice a hollow whisper that seemed to echo from the depths of the abyss. "I have watched your nightmares unfold, woven from the fabric of your deepest fears." Emily took a tentative step forward, her gaze locked with the creature's unblinking stare. "Why me?" she asked, her voice barely more than a whisper. The Weaver's lips curled into a semblance of a smile, though there was no warmth in its expression. "You are a conduit," it explained, its voice resonating with a strange mixture of malice and melancholy. "Your mind is a gateway through which the nightmares of others manifest. I am but a servant to their fears, a puppeteer pulling the strings of their darkest desires." A chill settled over Emily as she struggled to comprehend the magnitude of the creature's words. "Can you help me?" she ventured, a glimmer of hope flickering within her despite the dread that gripped her heart. The Weaver's laughter echoed through the chamber, a haunting melody that sent shivers down Emily's spine. "Help you?" it scoffed, the sound reverberating off the walls like a twisted mockery of mirth. "There is no escape from the labyrinth of nightmares, no sanctuary from the darkness that dwells within." Despair threatened to overwhelm Emily as she realized the futility of her quest. But then, amidst the suffocating silence, a voice called out to her—a voice that spoke of courage in the face of despair, of hope in the shadow of doubt. " Emily?" She turned, her heart leaping with a mixture of relief and disbelief as she saw a familiar face emerging from the murky gloom. It was Lucas, a childhood friend whose steadfast presence had anchored her through the storms of life. "I've been looking for you," Lucas said, his voice filled with concern as he took in the haunted look in Emily's eyes. "I knew you were in trouble when you disappeared without a word." Emily rushed into his arms, the weight of her fears melting away in the warmth of his embrace. "Lucas, I don't know what's happening to me," she confessed, her voice trembling with the rawness of her emotions. "The nightmares—they won't let go of me." Lucas held her close, his embrace a lifeline in the suffocating darkness. "We'll figure this out together," he promised, his voice steady and reassuring. "You're not alone in this, Emily. I'll help you find a way out." With Lucas by her side, Emily felt a flicker of hope ignite within her once more. Together, they faced the horrors that lurked within the Nexus—the twisted corridors, the malevolent whispers, and the haunting presence of the Weaver of Dreams itself. With each step they took, their bond grew stronger, a beacon of light in the endless night that threatened to engulf them. It was in the deepest recesses of the Nexus that they finally confronted the Weaver of Dreams. With Lucas's unwavering support and Emily's newfound courage, they challenged the creature's hold over their minds and souls. Shadows writhed and twisted as the Weaver fought to maintain its grip, but in the end, love triumphed over fear. With a final, defiant cry, Emily and Lucas shattered the illusion of the never-ending nightmare. The Nexus trembled and groaned, its walls collapsing in on themselves as the darkness that had plagued them for so long was banished into oblivion. As they emerged into the cool embrace of the night air, Emily and Lucas shared a silent moment of understanding. The journey had been harrowing, the challenges daunting, but through it all, they had found strength in each other's presence. The nightmares had been vanquished, their hold broken, but the bond forged in the crucible of their shared ordeal would endure And so, as the first rays of dawn painted the sky in hues of gold and crimson, Emily and Lucas walked hand in hand into the new day—a testament to the resilience of the human spirit and the power of love to conquer even the darkest of nightmares

title: The Magical Dolphin-'Dolly'
text: Mina and her Parents went to the beach during Summer vacation. Mina hated to visit the beach during Summers. She complained about the scorching heat and made faces. Her Parents told her to enjoy the breeze in the beach, play in waters and build sand castles which she could also deck up with seashells. Instead Mina threw plastic bottles and wrappers in the water. While Mina was throwing the chocolate wrappers and bottles in the water, she saw a girl wearing torn clothes and collecting sea-shells in her bag and also the plastic bottles thrown in the sea...Mina was curious to know as why the girl was collecting those plastics and wrappers which people were throwing away. She followed the girl... The girl kept collecting the plastic bottles and reached to the middle of the beach which was not crowded, She took a stone from her bag and threw in the water, Mina was quietly looking at the girl. To Mina's surprise a dolphin came out of the water... Mina shouted with astonishment...The girl saw Mina and approached her, the dolphin went back to the waters. Mina asked her name, the girl said 'Lata'. Lata could not afford to go to school even though she topped and loved studying. She would help her mother by selling ornaments made from seashell and that was the only earning they had. During winters no one would visit the beach and they would sometimes starve...Mina was sad to hear about Lata's condition. Mina asked her about the dolphin... Lata asked Mina to make a Promise to not share about the dolphin to anyone, as Everyone would chase the poor dolphin as she was an unique specie...Mina promised. Lata told Mina, that one day when she was collecting the seashells, she saw Dolly- The dolphin out of the waters and in the seashore, pleading for help. Lata could not drag or push Dolly back to the sea and poor Dolly was crying for help... Lata did not give up and tried her best to save Dolly, she also pour water on Dolly to help her breathe and at last she gathered all her strength and dug out some sand which led to a steep point and finally she pushed Dolly back to the waters... Dolly was a magical Dolphin and could also speak, She would sometimes wantedly grab the attention of the tourists and then disappear near Lata's mother's shop so that they could earn some money by selling the ornaments. Mina wanted to see the Dolphin, so Lata called, " Dolly,O Dolly, bahar aa jao, Mina kuch nahi karegi", Dolly came out and looked at Lata and Mina...Lata asked Mina to sit on back of Dolly and she gave them a ride in the waters...Mina was very happy to explore the unexplored sea. Lata told Mina how people throw plastic in the waters which causes harm for Dolly and other creatures in the water, so she collects the Plastic and tries to clean the beach and the waters. Mina w as upset and shameful on her act of thro wing things onto the w ater making it harmful for Dolly... She promised Lata to come and help her to clean the beach on every summer vacation and she kissed Dolly on her nose and thanked her for the wonderful ride. Mina's Parents were surprised to see her cleaning the beach and enjoying playing in waters and creating sand castles. She also introduced Lata to her Parents and told them about her condition, Since Mina's father was a Govt School Principal, he made arrangements for her to study and Lata was jumping with happiness and thanked Mina and her Parents. There was another Secret which Lata hid from Mina about Dolly... Dolly was a magical Dolphin and when Lata had saved Dolly's life and kept the beach clean, Dolly had given her a chance to a make wish and Lata wished to continue her education and Dolly fulfilled it. Moral: From this we learn that if we help others, we help ourselves too like how Lata helped the Dolphin and got to study in school again and we never know what is a boon in disguise like how Mina was complaining about the heat but she met the magical Dolphin and took a adventurous ride and made a friend like Lata.

title: Why Do Sunflowers Love the Sun?
text: One sunny afternoon, Viveka took a walk in the park near her house. She was eager to draw the sunflowers that flourished in the garden. "Why is this flower called a sunflower?" muttered Viveka to Montu and Bontu, her two faithful dogs. "Is it because it's the color of the sun?" Moments later, the sun began to set and twilight came. Viveka stepped out of her house for a moment to feed Montu and Bontu. Viveka watched the sunflowers in the garden swaying in the evening breeze. "Look, Billi!" she called to Billi, the striped cat. " They curl up like you when you're sleepy!" Viveka sat down and started drawing. She drew a picture of the sun shining brightly in the sky, just as she had seen it during the day. Then Viveka drew the sunflowers drooping to the ground, just as they would at dusk. The next morning, Viveka ran to the park to match her painting to the scene. "Oh, it's not the same!" she complained, "I have to paint it all over again." "The sunflowers looked upright and beautifully fluffy, not drooping like in my painting." "This time, I will draw properly!" he said excitedly to Montu and Bontu. He went to the park at noon when the sun was high, and started drawing the sunflowers he saw. The next morning, Viveka returned to the park to match the pictures. Again, they didn't match! "Ah, how can they change? Are they bewitched?" she lamented. Out of curiosity, Viveka climbed the tallest tree to get a better view of the garden. "I'm going to observe the sunflowers' every move!" Over the next few days, Viveka recorded everything she saw. Every day during the week, Viveka drew a sunflower. On Sunday, she collected all her drawings and took a good look. Finally, Viveka understood what was happening. "It's not magic," she smiled. "Sunflowers do face in different directions. It follows the sun!" Why Do Sunflowers Follow the Sun? The Earth circulates around the Sun while it rotates on its axis. As it rotates, half of the Earth faces the Sun, and we call this "daytime." At the same time, the other half is dark, and we call it "night." We see the Sun rising in the east and setting in the west. During the day, plants use the Sun's rays to process their food, but not all plants follow the Sun's motion. The stems of young sunflowers contain cells that are heliotropic, meaning they are stimulated to move towards the sun. This is why sunflowers move with the sun.
author: Elsa Dwi Sarkiman

text: Once upon a time on a small farm near a small village ﻿﻿ there lived a chick called Daisy "When I grow up, I want to fly high, high into the sky," Daisy said. ﻿ However, the other chicks laughed at her.﻿ "You're so weird," they said. "We don't wanna play with you anymore." "Daisy, we can flap our wings, but it's hard for chickens to fly," said her mother. Daisy never gave up. Every day, she practiced flapping her wings alone. Wus wus wus. She kept flapping her wings, but her feet were still on the ground. When practicing, he imagined himself flying up into the sky and looking down at the chickens below. He imagined himself flying over flocks of sparrows and swallows. "Wow!" the birds exclaimed. "A chicken that can fly!" "Wus wus wus. title: I Love Myself
text: I like to play anything, I'm not afraid to climb trees." The girl looked at Rubina, then pointed at her while exclaiming, "What's that on your forehead, like an outline and hairy?" Rubina likes her eyebrows, what's wrong with that? They were perfect for hiding caterpillars when she went out. Rubina shrugged her shoulders, wishing someone would make friends with her, a new friend who is kind. she walked away while dancing, "Hai, my name is Rubina. Can i play with you guys? I'm good at throwing the ball, as well as being a player on the field." A tall boy who captained the cricket team said, "You have one, two, three, FOUR eyes. Which eye will see the ball?" Rubina loves her round glasses. Because of these glasses, she can see clearly. She could thread her grandmother's needle, and look for lice in Rani's fur. Rubina shrugged her shoulders, she walked away while doing somersaults, wishing that someone would make friends with her, a new kind of friend. "Hi, my name is Rubina. Can I come and play with both of you? We can take turns swinging, and see who can swing the farthest." The two little girls saw Rubina hesitate. They whispered, giggled, and laughed. "We don't want to play with you. You're tall like a giraffe." Rubina likes her long legs. Yes, her legs are really long. But she can save cats and kites that get stuck in trees or thorny bushes. Rubina's face was a little gloomy, her eyes no longer sparkling brightly. She missed Nina, Raj, and Som. If only they were there, the atmosphere would definitely be festive. Rubina shrugged her shoulders, and chose to play alone. In the game she made up, she was the king sitting on the throne. "Hi, my name is Alex. Can I play with you? I like reading and writing and also drawing. If I may know, what's your favorite thing?"
author: Alindia Firda

title: A Book for Putri
text: Where is Putri?" Princess was busy. She was enjoying reading a book. She reads all the time, at home, at school, in the park, even in bed. Page after page, from one book to another, she has read them all. Why do you always read books, Put?" Bayu asked. " Let's watch cartoons with me!" Dodi said "Books are more fun," Putri said. "Do you see a ring? Then, this straight line? Push the line inwards and pull the line outwards, and it becomes a letter. Line up the letters you made, and it's a word. A word. The words can feel wise, funny, sad, or warm to your heart. As you organize the words, they will turn into sentences. Those sentences will turn into stories. Read the story and whoosh! You will enter the world of fantasi!" explained Putri. But Putri was worried today. She had run out of books to read! All the books in the library that her hands could reach had been read from the beginning to the end. "What am I supposed to do? There are no more books for me to read!" Putri sobbed. Wait! What's that up there? Putri looked to the top of the shelf and saw not one or two, but three more shelves full of books. "More books!" she whispered excitedly. But, there was still one problem. She was too short and the top bookshelf was too high. How could she pick up the books on the top shelf? Can Putri use her mother's clothesline or her mother's saree? How about using the chairs and tables in the room? Putri thought it would be helpful if she had a giraffe. A monkey would be fine too, or maybe both. Putri had a plan. She called Bayu and Dodi to help her. As quietly as possible, they climbed over each other's shoulders. "Bayu, you're so heavy!" complained Dodi, "I told you not to finish the sweet potato ball compote." "It's not me who's heavy," complained Bayu, "It's Putri who's heavy!" "Suuut! Almost got it," interrupted Putri. In the end, their plan failed. Aaah! "What's going on? The tall librarian came over to Putri. The librarian put her down from the shelf. Bayu and Dodi had already run away. Putri gazed sadly at the books that she almost reached. "Can I help you?" asked the tall librarian. "I tried to climb the bookshelf. I had no books to read," Putri soobed. "Why didn't you tell me?" asked the tall librarian. "If it was me, you wouldn't have had to climb that bookshelf. Want me to help you get them?" Putri nodded her head in agreement. ' "I want to read this one, this one, and this one too!" Putri exclaimed happily. "Thank you for helping me!" "Get that one too," suggested the tall librarian, "When I was little, I really liked that book." "Were you ever small too?"Putri asked. "Oh of course, even smaller than you, " said the tall librarian. "But I grew up and you will too. Until then, whenever you want to get a book, just ask me, and I'll get it for you." But, did Putri hear what the tall librarian said? Of course... no. She was engrossed in the book and entered a fantasy world through a circle and a line, then a letter and another letter. Then, a word and another word. Forming a sentence and another sentence. Until finally it became a story. All because she had gotten a new book to read.
author: Syva Nurhaliza

title: The river that flows through time
text: They change color based on what is inside them or what is around them. Sometimes it is the color of the rocks in the riverbed. Sometimes they match the color of the sky. The river also changes its direction. If the river was in one place in the past, it might be in another place in the future. Many rivers like the Ganges are thousand of year old. They have seen humanity grow up. People have always loved living an working near rivers. Rivers know how to take care of people. Some of our food comes from rivers and river water is used to grow most of the food. When the food has entered the body, the river comes to the rescue again! If rivers could speak, they might demand that people dispose of their feces somewhere. Humans are not the only creatures that rivers protect. Many birds and plants, animals and fish, insects and flowers depend on rivers. The river even support musical talent. Insects sing strange and beautiful songs underwater that sound like they come from another world. India gets its name from a river. Besides the name of the country, the Indus is home to one of the oldest civilizations in the world. The river helped ancient people build cities. They used the river to travel to lands near or far, carrying everything they wanted to buy and sell. The people of the Indus Valley lived by the river quite happily. Until suddenly they weren't. More than 3,000 years ago, the civilization vanished. Some people think they were too greedy. That by overusing forests and water, they made rivers flood. Floods are scary but sometimes useful. When the flood waters returned to the river, they left fertile soil on its banks - perfect for growing crops! But floods can also destroy lives and buildings. Ferocious rivers scared people. Early humans thought songs, prayers and gifts could calm rivers. Usually it wasn't the best solution. Travel using the river time machine back to the present. Some things from the past will seem familiar. Rivers continue to be used to supply food and transportation. People have also built canals to connect rivers, bring water to those who don't live near them, and make it easier to travel on them. People built dams to control river flow, store water and generate electricity from river energy. But all this human interference is making a mess of the river. Dams and canals make it harder for rivers to nurture all their creatures. Many people do not understand how rivers work, how they live and how they fail. In some areas, rivers are as dry as deserts. In other countries, rivers are treated like trash cans, waste pipes, and plastic dumps. If the river time machine took people on a trip to the future, what would they see? An empty river landscape that only lives in old stories. They will find countries and nations at war over the few rivers that exist. They will wander in the barren desert. Or they will see a world where humans have learned to live with nature and with each other. A world where fresh water is stored, wastewater is recycled, and both are used responsibly. They will find clean rivers and people who protect them. A second future is not impossible. Our skills and technology have brought dead rivers back to life before. Rivers have taken care of us for thousands of years. Now some humans are trying to keep our rivers. Some courts have ruled that rivers have the same legal rights as humans. If one harms the river, one is the same as harming others. Imagine the long list of resentments the river will have against people! GUILTY! Children take to the streets to demand a better future. In 2015, 11-year-old Stella Bowles campaigned to her local government to fix a polluted river - and they did! Adults started listening. The river is contaminated with feces bacteria! All over the world, children are telling adults that they need to be better at taking care of the world they leave behind. After all, it's the only one we have. "AMAZONE" "Sea level rising!" "Climate Attack" The work of cleaning the river never ends. There will be more people, more farms, more factories. Fortunately, there is enough water for everyone. We just need to take care of it and each other.
author: Sulhiya 03

title: A trip to the Wonders of Science
text: The class VI of Crest Wood Valley School, were getting ready to go on a class trip to a Science Complex, Miss. Sophie and Mr. George were in-charge of the students for the day. The students were ecstatic to visit the unreal site. While, some kids were determined on their buffoonery. These are the children Miss. Sophie needs to be alert about. Would you keep an eye on them for her? The class entered the first floor of the complex. They were welcomed by a huge door. That led them into the....... Pradeep Sanjay Delina Trisha Raghav CHEMISTRY LAB The door opened and led them to the Chemistry Complex. The lab assistant addressed everyone and explained that everything in the lab helps 'Study the make-up of all things on earth and How they behave.' The class was buzzing and each one found the place fascinating. The students learnt about the different chemicals and How to identify them, their colours,the aroma. W hen Raghav tried to lift a huge beaker filled with acid and dropped it, t hey learnt about the various safety measures to be followed. After this the students were alert about the risk of the burners, the glassware, and the acids. T hough the lab seemed dangerous,there was magic happening at each table.. While assisting in various experiments, E verybody followed the decorum of the lab to avoid any mishaps. Have you seen these things in the lab? It helps working in the lab easier,let's try finding them! Mortar and pestle Dropper Beaker Bunsen burner Test tube PHYSICS LAB On the second floor was the Physics lab, which had a variety of instruments and various machines decked up everywhere.There they discovered how magnets work, the formation of a rainbow through the prism, how electricity works, different types of cell, working of an electric bell etc. they explored the mirrors and learnt about the various streams in physics. the students were filled with questions and asked the lab assistant about it. They were curious about all the things,including the different uses of a telescope. The kids had a fun time in the physics lab. Did you spot these unique things in the physics lab, what might be their uses? The students after the Physics lab were welcomed by a R obotic arm into the Electronics lab. Magnet Prism Pendulum Telescope Newton's colour Disc ELECTRONICS LAB The Electronics lab felt like, they entered into a ' Transformer world', there were more machines than humans. Here the students acquired knowledge about how drones work, the working of a satellite, how to control a robotic arm etc. and they also took a deeper look inside the computer. Have you come across these things in the electronics lab? I hope you have seen some of them in real life too. Soon, the class moved towards the BOTANY LAB. Drone Robotic arm USB Voltmeter Satellite BOTANY LAB The Botany lab was filled with different kinds of flora and the kids could see a variety of specimens from roots to flowers, leaves,fungus and fruits. The assistants couldn't control the kids due to their excitement. They learnt about photosynthesis (how plants make their food). About the different methods to produce crops according to our desire (genetic modification), how to use a microscope, To differentiate different types of plants, How to take care of various house plants etc. They also created their own theories on making the plants happy. Some of their ideas included giving them a hug, to play some music for them etc. Did you notice any of these plants in the botany lab? Which one of these is used to see things that can't be seen with our naked eye? The students after the botany lab filed up to move towards the last spot on the itinerary that is to the ZOOLOGY LAB. Microscope Watermelon Venus flytrap Cactus Money plant ZOOLOGY LAB The students were astonished to enter the zoology lab. It felt as if they had entered into the 'Jurassic park'. The students were intrigued by the amount of species they could see and spotted various amphibians, fishes,reptiles and birds, they also learnt about different specimens present there and discovered about how it is collected and assembled etc. They all got to learn about various species of insects and also learn about endemic species (found only in India) of butterfly. They made friends with Mr. Anderson the (skeleton of the lab). And took some advice from Mr. Afzal (the bird whisperer) on how to deal with an emergency related to birds. Did you come across these specimens in the zoology lab? Why do you think this insect looks like a stick? With the visit to the Zoology lab the trip to the Science Complex came to an end. Human skull Stick insect Saber-toothed tiger skull Pterosaur skull Monkey Skeleton The trip was successful.I thank you, for keeping an eye on them. The class learnt a lot in the lab visit - how to ask questions, to create theories, to observe, to assist, to operate and remain curious. The trip helped the kids to become little scientists possessing scientific values that would help them make huge discoveries in the future.

title: pranav the pattern detective
text: Pranav looked at the tree, and said, "Okay. I'll climb." "Can you see the ball?" Maansa shouted from below. But something else caught Pranav's attention Look, it's a beehive!" Pranav exclaimed in fear. Maansa looked worried. "What if there are bees inside?" "Don't worry, the nest is empty," Pranav said, looking at her. "There are so many holes! And they all have the same shape..." Why did the bee choose this shape? Why not a circle?" Pranav wondered. He imagined the hive to be circular. "That won't work." Bees are very smart," Pranav told his friends the next day. He had read everything about them. "They managed to find the best shape for their home. Hexagons - or hexagons - that fit together without holes or gaps, like a jigsaw puzzle." Their math teacher, Mr. Das, overheard their conversation. "The six sides of the hexagon give the bees more space," he adds. "Where did they learn to do that?" asked Pranav. Mr. Das said with a smile, "Patterns are everywhere!" The next day at the market, Pranav carefully observed the fruits and vegetables. He looked at the pineapple, the back of the pumpkin and the inside of the orange. So many sizes, colors, shapes... but Pranav could see the patterns! "Are patterns really everywhere?" he wondered. Pranav became a pattern detective! So many things in our nature are made using repeating patterns," Pranav told his classmates the next day. "We use repeating patterns in things built by humans too," Mr. Das said. "Why don't you try creating something It can be your homework. " "What shapes will we use to make patterns? Pranav asked. Mr. Das wrote the answer on the board. Use whatever shape you want. Carpet. Bookshelf. Window. Patterns everywhere! Everywhere he looked, he saw shapes coming together. "It's not just bees that are smart," Pranav thought. "We can use shapes and patterns for many things too!" And then, Pranav got busy drawing his dream house. Rectangular red bricks. Black and white square tiles at the entrance, just like in his grandmother's house. Who knew that a simple shape could make a home - for the bees, for me, and for you! Find patterns Nature has a clever way of combining shapes. Pranav sees patterns in the world around him: the outside of a pineapple, the inside of an orange, the hexagon of a beehive. Some shapes, such as hexagons and squares, fit together perfectly, without any gaps. But not others, such as circles. When shapes in nature match in a repeating pattern, leaving no gaps or holes, it is called Teselasi. Pranav saw that humans also use Teselasi. We lay out shapes repetitively to form patterns, and use this pattern to design bookshelves, build castles, and create works of art. A simpler word for Thessellation is tiling.

title: Flies and Superheroes
text: What have you got so far, Anoop?" asked Sunita. "I have the main character, the boy," Anoop said. "What do you have?" "Mine is a girl," said Sunita. "Let me tell you my idea first," Anoop said. "You criticize my story and tell me how to improve the characters and plot of the story." "Well, after you convey your story idea, you can analyze my story idea," said Sunita. Anoop conveyed his idea first. "My character's name is Ben, he wants to be a superhero." "Okay, that sounds interesting," Sunita said. "Science teacher Ben explained to him that science hasn't figured out how to be a superhero yet." "So, Ben went to his mother, who was ironing his clothes. He talked about the idea of becoming a super giant by eating a secret potion." "And his mother laughed at him," Sunita said. "Don't! His mother just agreed! He can be anything he wants." "Except for superheroes." "Okay," Anoop said. "Okay, so he can't be a superhero normally. Now he has to come up with a better plan to become a superhero. So, what's your idea?" Anita is one of the alumni who always thinks about how birds can fly. Maybe he can learn to fly! Don't, Anoop, have to be more interesting than that. What about space alone? Maybe he could fly through the atmosphere? Anoop, for a moment. So, he loves birds and wonders if birds can fly... in space? What about flies, Sunita? Birds fly... fly... yes! He loves flies and wonders if they can breathe and fly in space. Then, two flies flying in the air, they go on a date. One is male and the other is female, and Sunita loves it because the flies fall in love with each other and... Idh... Sunita, don't do that, ah! Sorry, or maybe they're just flying buddies? By the way, back to your story idea, Anoop.... So in my story, Ben talks to his friends about how to turn into a superhero to save the world from evil. His friends laughed at him, and then they went to the drink stall. There is a bald man and a poster of Khabir Khan in the movie "Kasmir Andai Kau Can". When his friends are drinking mango juice, Ben tells them about his desire to become a superhero and they are knocked unconscious. The bald man was just dumbfounded. So, there is no one believed in Ben. What else is her uncle, Sunita? There are types of flies that mutate and can fly in zero gravity, and Anita studied physics and biology, then became interested in becoming an astronaut. Has India ever had astronauts? I don't know. He, Anoop, maybe she can become the youngest female astronaut in the world! Yes, he had to study diligently and take rigorous tests such as spinning at a speed of 2,000 kilometers per hour. Well, that's cool, Anoop. So, after becoming very smart and graduating from astronaut college and getting a degree in all fields related to space, he officially became an astronaut, then he was told the departure schedule to space on a mission. However, he has to bring something, right? Yes... a specimen of two flies! Does it have to be another fly, Sunita? Why not the ones buzzing around the fruit baskets? Wow, good Anoop! Well, Ben looked out from behind the window. He rarely goes out to play because he is too engrossed in watching superhero TV shows and learning science. He began to think about turning his body into a mighty like an impenetrable robot human. You mean no one can defeat him? Yes! And Ben lives in... in the middle of the forest! Lush trees and foliage surround her house. The environment where he lives becomes a training complex to become a megamighty. There should be a beautiful path from his house to the garden. Yes, it does! Well, at the end of the road there was a creepy maze that could change every time he passed through it. Then, he rushed out and climbed the tree. He felt immeasurably happy because every time he exercised he almost became a superhero. So, he was like changing his skin to become superstrong. Yes, he can transform into a universal hero warrior with an undefeated record of five gold badges! And there was a girl he liked? A girl? Hmm... Yes, why not. However, he is only as a practicing buddy. Then, the girl chased him around a tree and tried to kiss him, but Ben wouldn't want to be kissed so he ran faster. Yes, but it was not suitable, a girl was arrested and forcibly kissed. He's a superhero, not a sissy. What about Anita? Anita dreams about outer space. He was determined to make his dream come true. Why didn't he just go there? Okay, okay. I haven't gotten there yet. So, he finds out about the planets in space and what he will find on his mission. So did the mutated super flies. Yes! The fly also dreams of space! The fly was wearing a helmet, right? He mutated, but couldn't breathe in space. Okay, flies can't breathe in space, we know that from science. However, he can fly, can shoot and soar at will. Superhero Ben wears a helmet, right? No, he wears special smart glasses that can spit out bionic laser light to melt enemies. What kind of enemy? A superhero who turns evil. Like whom? Like a horned man who comes from a mutated rhinoceros trying to seize Africa. Ben meant to fly and slam his enemies. So, have you prepared this story beforehand? Little. I have written some of them. Then, I thought again. I thought again. Then I watched TV to look for ideas. So, this is already airing on TV shows? Not yet, not yet. This is just my story. Your story idea must be more... original, Sunita. Yes, it's very personal because I love space. Well, on the day of the launch, Anita looked cool. He wears a uniform with his hair tied in a ponytail. What can astronauts do that? Anita has a helmet that is specially designed so that her hair can be tied in a ponytail. Then, he prepared to enter the rocket with flies in the jar. Then, they launched into space, right? BLAAAS! Controlled launch, yes. What happens in space? Are there aliens? Hmm... not. However, other astronauts travel in a group with Anita. He released the two flies into space, and to his surprise, they could fly with zero gravity! So, how? Then, everyone made an important note and Anita was officially declared right. He got recognition because it was his idea. Are the flies happy? Yes, but they get a bit sick when they return to earth, because they forget that the earth has gravity. So, they were forced to learn to fly again, but they slammed into the ceiling. Well, Ben knows, there are flies that are attracted to light, so when he wants to learn to fly, he needs bright light to give him strength. It was a secret potion that would turn him into a flying superhero? Light? Well, I don't want to write a long story, Sunita. So, Ben chats with his father and neighbors to prove his theory that light can turn humans into superheroes. And dad is always right, right? Yes, dad knows everything. Then, Ben's father and mother showed him how light works. That's when Ben discovers how to access the power of light and transform his body. Oh, something forgot, Anoop. What? There was damage in the spacecraft so everything was thrown outside. So, they are forced to spend time repairing the plane before returning to earth. What happened to Ben? Did he become a superhuman? Not really. Not? No, he no longer needed his body as a human. He found the perfect body. So, what is it? He became an incredible brilliant fly? Glamorous flies! What? Don’t! Don't be like a girl. He is a mighty male fly. That's how the story ended. Well, Anita went into space again and she found that birds can also fly in zero gravity. They can also breathe! So, they don't need to wear helmets. So finally? Yes. What? What about Anita? Didn't he find a superhero or something like that in space? No, he went back to studying birds and observing flies. Or it can be something else. It could be that he studied cats. What happened to Ben? He thought his room lamp was on fire last month. He lost all his strength. But he keeps trying to be a superhero again, right? Yes, he found a secret potion within the bones that could transform his body. Become what? Dog.

title: Why Do Bees Buzz?
text: They carry pollen from one flower to another like a postman delivering a letter. Pollen is a fine powder in flowers whose function is to help plants produce seeds. Bees are reliable deliverers. Thanks to them, many new plants grew everywhere. How does that tiny pollen stick to the bee's feet? When bees sit on flowers to suck honey, pollen sticks to their legs and bodies. Then, when the same bee flies and dances nimbly near the flower, the pollen is released and hits other flowers. The bee flies again to another flower and leaves the pollen there while also picking up more pollen. This process takes place continuously. Bees are foster parents for new plants that grow far from the parent plant. Can you hear your own breath? Usually not. But you can hear the bees breathing. That's because the buzzing of a bee is also the sound of its breathing. Bees have small, segmented bodies. When he breathes, the air rushes in like a roller coaster over the bumps and produces a hum. Interesting right? Those busy bees are truly amazing, aren't they? Do you know? 1. Bees are hard workers. They can live up to nine months in winter and only two months in summer. Working continuously without playing does not make them bored. 2. Interestingly, when bees did the work of young bees, their brains stopped aging. Their brains work like the brains of young bees. Do you want to be a bee? 3. Bees can recognize faces like humans. At first they saw parts of the face separately, then they put them together and it became a complete face. Remember never to make him angry! 4. Caffeine, a chemical that plants use to repel harmful insects, helps bees remember the location of flowers so they can recognize them when they return. 5. Bumble bees are larger than honey bees and other types of bees. They live in nests and love to socialize. Most bumble bees do not have stings. While they don't produce much honey, they are reliable pollen carriers. Be a bee! 1. Honey bees dance to tell the hive residents where they can find nectar (flower honey). Now try conveying information with dancing, and see if your friends understand what you mean. 2. Try buzzing like a bee. Flap your hands and hear your buzz ﻿ 3. The beehive is recognized as the finest engineering work. Why? Try drawing perfect hexagons like a honeycomb. Or make a hexagon model using regular cardboard. You will find the answer. 4. Try smelling flowers that have different scents. You can imagine why honey from different nectars tastes different.
author: Rasya Almaida

title: Fasten your seatbelts!
text: Arya had seen her in the circus arena. Rosamma was a trapeze artist. Arya wanted to fly and swing in the air. She wanted to wear glittering clothes like Rosamma's and be applauded by hundreds of spectators. Every day she would eat cotton candy and make friends with clowns. The trapeze artist climbs up the grand staircase, walks on the narrow platform, picks up his trapeze and leaps into the air! A partner is waiting to greet him on the other side. When Arya was eight years old, she wanted to be Kalpana Chawla. She changed her orange suit into an astronaut suit and wore it all day. "Arya, aren't you hot in that suit?" her mother asked. "Astronauts have to get used to wearing this suit, mom. Space is different from earth. This suit can protect me." Kalpana Chawla was born in Haryana State, India. As an astronaut, she circled the earth 252 times! Kalpana died on board when her shuttle entered the atmosphere. When Arya was twelve years old, she wanted to be Amelia Earhart. Amelia built a model airplane as part of a school project. Her model didn't fly, but she still won second place. Arya even copied Amelia's haircut Amelia was the first woman to cross the Atlantic. Her dream was to travel around the world following the equator. Unfortunately, she couldn't realize her dream as she was lost somewhere in the Pacific. Then Arya heard the story of Angulia Bai, Kumudammal and Sarla Thakral, India's first three female pilots who are much talked about. Angulia Bai was only sixteen years old! I don't want to wait till sixteen! To drive? No To vote? No So what's it for? To be a pilot On May 30, 1935, nineteen-year-old Kumudammal and sixteen-year-old Angulia Bai became the first Indian women to be granted pilot's licenses. They trained at the Madras pilots' club. When Arya turned eighteen, she wanted to be a fighter pilot. "Who's that, Chechi?" asked her younger brother Raju, looking at the poster taped to the wall in Arya's room. "These are Bhawana, Avani and Mohana, India's first fighter pilots. Mohana, Bhawana and Avani are fighter pilots. Before them, only men could become fighter pilots in India. They protect the country's borders from the air. During natural disasters like floods and earthquakes, they actively participate in rescue missions. Arya saved up some money to pay for her studies at flight school. She spent several years studying. She gained a lot of knowledge in pilot training. She worked very hard and ate a lot of carrots because her mother always told her that carrots were good for the eyes. Until finally she was ready to sit in the cockpit. Today is a special day for Arya. She was in charge and in charge. She was very happy because this morning there were two special passengers on her plane. "Dear Sir, Madam, I am Arya, the captain of your flight. Welcome to our plane." "Chechi!" "That's my sister!"
author: Muhamad Pajar

title: Pishi in the Middle of Storm
text: They feasted on small fish, far from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. ﻿Pishi and her friends were leaping and splashing in the Indian Ocean! When a fishing boat approached, Pishi quickly dove underwater. Her friends scattered. With her large fins resembling a cape, Pishi could swim swiftly and save herself. ﻿ The thunderclap accompanied by lightning strikes disoriented Pishi. The ocean turned dark. A big wave rolled her under the boat. Aaaa, her stomach was injured! Pishi knew what she had to do. She would look for her friends. But first, Pishi would treat her wound. She swam swiftly towards the shore. Pishi's heart was pounding. Her body was very large. If only she wasn't 10 meters long and weighing 900 kilograms, she could have reached the hospital faster! Pishi saw the lighthouse beacon shining on the beach. She leaped for joy. Finally, she arrived at the natural hospital. A school of fish quickly approached her. The fish that sometimes were her prey now became her caretakers. They cleaned the wound on her stomach. The fish nibbled at the peeled skin around the wound. Pishi immediately felt much better. She enjoyed living in the Indian Ocean with 5,000 other living creatures! Hello Readers, the Indian Ocean is nicknamed 'Ratnakara' (in Sanskrit), which means 'the mine of gems'. Stingrays often visit 'cleaning stations' that serve as natural hospitals located in the middle of the ocean. Here, small fish swim between their gills and on the surface of the stingray's skin. They are called cleaner fish because they eat parasites and dead skin tissue from the stingrays. Despite their large size, stingrays are not dangerous. They are hunted by sharks, whales, and humans. #6FrameStoryChallenge: A Carnival of Art The illustrations in this book were created as part of the #6FrameStoryChallenge, an online campaign run by Pratham Books to build a rich bank of illustrations for. The essence of the #6FrameStoryChallenge was to tell a good story using just 6 illustrations. The campaign inspired nearly 70 illustrators to donate their time and skills to India’s first open-source story-publishing platform for children. What started out as an experimental campaign soon blossomed into a carnival of art, birthing nearly 500 new illustrations. These wordless narratives cut across language barriers, opening up a world of possibilies, encouraging ’s growing community to dream up multiple stories around these images. The #6FrameStoryChallenge is a powerful reminder of the need for collaboration, to get closer to our mission: “A Book in Every Child’s Hand.”
author: Amir Hamzah

title: Same or Different?
text: She keeps saying that every day!" "And remember," Mama said. "Stay away from the Snake - he's different." Pipit wished she hadn't said that. Snake was her best friend. But Mama didn't like snakes. "They eat us!" That's what Mama always said. "Birds and snakes are never friends." Elsewhere, Papa Snake is packing lunch boxes filled with bird eggs. "Today's special, son!" he said proudly. "But I don't like eggs, Papa," complained Snake. "We eat them all the time!" said Papa firmly. "Now, let's go. And remember, stay away from Pipit!" The snake left in a huff. "Pipit is different," said Papa again. "You can't be friends with your food!" When Snake met Pipit at school, they understood. "Did your mom say...?" asked Snake. Pipit nodded. "Your father too?" Snake nodded. "Our parents are wrong, Pipit," said Snake. "Let's show them. We have more alike than different." "Great idea!" said Pipit. "Come on!" She took out a piece of paper and drew two circles - like this. "In the yellow circle," Pipit said, "we write 'About Pipit'. In the blue circle 'About Snake'. This shows Snake and Pipit are DIFFERENT." Snake was confused. "I thought we wanted to show that we are the SAME!" "Well, that's what the green part is for." Pipit smiled. "First of all, let's talk about our appearance," said Pipit. "Same or different?" "VERY different," complained Snake. "My body is long, hairless and thin. You are small, plump and soft." "You're right," said Pipit. "I look like a cotton wad." She drew a cotton wad in the yellow section, "and you look like a piece of mine - very rough." She drew a piece of mine in the blue section. "Now," she said. "How do we move?" "VERY differently," said the increasingly sad Snake. "You fly, flapping your wings. I slither along the ground, meandering." "In other words," said Pipit. "I fly like a plane, and you move like a train." Snake sighed. "Cheer up, Snake," Pipit said quickly. "Now what do we eat?" "A VERY different meal." Snake almost cried. "But I don't eat bird eggs." "I know," Pipit said soothingly. But now she looked glum too. "Grains and grass," she mumbled, drawing in the yellow section. "Frogs, and mice," she said, drawing in the blue section. "Preeettt!" Snake and Pipit jumped up in surprise. It was the voice of Mr. Gajah, the school principal. "Why are you gloomy, children?" he asked kindly. "Oh, sir," sobbed Ular. "My father and Pipit's mother forbade us to be friends because we are different." "We wanted to show them that we have more similarities than differences, sir," said Pipit. "But it didn't work." Mr. Principal looked at the two circles for some time. Then he laughed. Snake and Pipit looked at him. "Don't you see, boys?" he said, wiping away his tears. "You're doing it the wrong way. Let me help you." ﻿﻿ The Headmaster sat down on the bench. "Now, Snake," he said, "what do you like to do most?" "Playing and talking, sir," replied Snake. "ESPECIALLY with Pipit. "The Headmaster sat down on the bench. "Now, Snake," he said, "what do you like to do most?" "Play and talk, sir," replied Snake. "ESPECIALLY with Pipit." ﻿ "And you, Pipit?" "Chatting and playing, sir," Pipit replied. "ESPECIALLY with Snake." "Right," said Mr. Headmaster, "you like to do the SAME things." Then he drew something in the green section. "So," he said, "what makes you happy, children?" "When the teacher lets me sit next to my friends, sir," Snake began to smile. "Me too, sir," Pipit clapped her hands. "A-ha!" said the Headmaster. "You two have the SAME fun place. Green! All right, what makes you sad?" "When Papa says I have to stay away from Pipit, sir," complained Snake. "When Mama said I should stay away from Snake, sir," complained Pipit. Mr. Headmaster frowned. "You're both sad," he said, "for the SAME reason - your parents forbid you to choose your own friends. Green again!" "Now," said the Headmaster, "who do you think is the best friend?" "Someone who loves you..." Snake began. "...even though you're different!" Pipit continued. "So you agree," said the Headmaster, "that a true friend loves you for who you are. So there are FOUR similarities and only THREE differences. Similarities win!" "Hooray!" exclaimed Snake and Pipit. "Thank you, Mr. Principal!" "Preeettt!" said Mr. Principal. "Last one..." "Yes, sir?" "Tell your parents you want to meet them in your office tomorrow morning!" And Principal Elephant walked away. He looked great. GROUPING! Choosing and grouping are important skills in math. To group things, you have to ask yourself logical questions, such as: 1. What is the same? What is different? 2. How are they similar? How are they different? 3. Can the same things be selected and grouped in another way? Think of different ways to choose and categorize these toy animals. You could group them: -According to their color - blue animals in one circle, yellow ones in another. -According to their size - small animals in one circle, big animals in another. -According to how they move - animals that walk and animals that fly. Will the group be different every time? Try and see!

title: pranav si detektif pola
text: Arjun said. Pranav looked at the tree, and said, "Okay. I will start it.” “push you to look at the ball?” Maansa shouts from below. But there is something else interesting Pranav's attention. "Look! it's a beehive!” Pranav is scared. Maansa looks worried. “What if there are bees in it?” "Don't worry, this nest is empty," Pranav said while taking care. “There are so many holes! And they all have the same shape…” “Why do bees choose this shape? Why not a circle?” Pranav wondered. He imagined the nest to be circular. “That won't work.” “The bees are very clever,” Pranav told his friends the next day. He had read everything about them. “They managed to find the best shape for their house. Hexagons — or hexagons — fit together without holes or gaps, like a jigsaw puzzle.” Their math teacher, Mr. Das, overhears their conversation. “The six sides of the hexagon provide more space for the bees,” he added. “Where did they learn to do that?” Pranav asked. Mr. Das says with a smile, “Patterns are everywhere!” The next day at the market, Pranav looked closely at the fruits and vegetables. He saw the pineapple, the back of the pumpkin and the inside of the orange. So many sizes, colors, shapes... but Pranav can see the patterns! “Is the pattern really everywhere?” he wondered. Pranav becomes a pattern detective! “There are so many things in our nature which is made using repeating patterns,” Pranav told his classmates the next day. “We use repeating patterns on something built by humans too,” said Mr Das. “Why don't you guys try creating something using a pattern? This can be your homework. ” "What shapes will we use to make the pattern? Pranav asked. Mr. Das wrote an explanation on the blackboard. At home, Pranav thinks about his homework. He dreams of making his own nest, maybe with box. Or triangle. Pranav thinks about what Mr. Das said. “Patterns are everywhere.” Then, he started to see a pattern. Carpet. bookshelf. Window. Patterns everywhere! Everywhere he looked, he saw various shapes gathered together as one. “It's not just bees that are smart,” thought Pranav. “We can use shapes and patterns for so many things too!” And then, Pranav was busy drawing his dream house. Red bricks are rectangular in shape. Black and white square tiles at the entrance, like at his grandmother's house. Who knew that simple shapes could make homes — for bees, for me, and for you! Find the pattern Nature has a clever way of combining shapes. Pranav sees patterns in the world around him: the outside of the pineapple, the inside of the orange, the hexagon from the beehive. Some shapes, such as hexagons and squares, fit each other perfectly, without the slightest gap. But not for other shapes, such as circles. When the shapes in nature fit into a repeating pattern, leaving no gaps or holes, it is called Tessellation. Pranav sees that humans also use Tessellation. We lay shapes repeatedly to form patterns, and use this pattern to design a bookshelf, build castles, and create works of art. A simpler word for Tessellation is tiling.

title: urusan monyet
text: There is a fast-flowing river that flows windingly through the land. Delicious delicious Juicy fruit tastes delicious. Bad bad Bad monkeys are rude and annoying. Abundant overflowing The forest was abundant with mangoes and bananas everywhere. The leader of the gray monkeys was exploring for food when one day he discovered a new area. There are mango trees, various types of fruit, bushes and berries, with fast-flowing rivers winding through the land. It was the perfect place for his tribal flock. The gray monkey leader jumped up and grabbed some mangoes, pulling them off the branches. He clicked one and it was cooked and delicious, fresh and delicious. With plenty of food he knew the monkeys could stay there for a long time. Other monkeys arrived and started eating bananas, mangoes and limes, making bridges with old wood and swimming in the river. They had a lot of fun in their new home, staying safe and being coaxed by the gray monkey leader. Little did the monkeys know that near them lived another tribe of black monkeys. The black monkeys spied on the gray monkeys, observing their behavior. “Look at them,” said the black monkey leader. "Noisy, bad and uncivilized. That is not monkey behavior. We are animals with achievements and pride. We must immediately chase them away." When the gray monkey was drinking by the river, the black monkey launched a surprising attack. They used clubs and started beating the monkeys' backs and pulling their tails. "If you guys want to behave like wild animals, then you deserve to be treated like one!" said the black monkey leader. The gray monkey leader immediately withdrew his group and moved away from the forest and river There is no other place the gray monkeys would go except arid plains and deserts. It feels hotter and more uncomfortable. Almost no humans passed by. Everywhere were scattered the bones of animals. The gray monkey leader left the desert to look for a better place. He skimmed over the rocks so he could get a wider view of the scene. He saw mountains, bushes, and grasslands, as well as many trees. Could there be fruit available there? Turns out there is! The gray monkey got a big bunch of bananas from a tree. The place was abundant with fruits. The place was filled with food! Then the gray monkey returned to the desert where his tribe was, to tell them the good news. When they saw what their leader, the monkeys, were hiding, they threatened and celebrated. He had traveled far just to provide food for them. The monkeys stopped nibbling on animal bones and dead trees because a special treat was available to them. The monkeys distributed the bananas evenly, to ensure each one got a treat. The bananas were ripe and delicious. The gray monkey explains where he got it from – from a faraway place abundant in fruit and vegetables and nuts. The monkeys agreed to go to this new place and live there, because it was full of food and there was a water source that would last a long time. They knew that they could not survive in the desert. The weather is too hot and there is not enough water. At the same time, the black monkeys gathered and protested against their leader. They were very angry. They ran out of food, but the leader wanted them to stay in the forest. There is tension and anger. The leader feels helpless. To their surprise, a herd of gray monkeys came. The black monkeys prepared to fight, and the leader dangled from branch to branch. The gray monkeys spoke to their leader. He tells them of a new place full of food, and offers to share it with them. There will be no more fighting between their flocks. The black monkeys agreed to share their remaining food. They all enjoyed papaya, various types of mango, and bananas. They watched and talked to each other, and realized that they had the same goal. Because everyone promised, the two tribes merged into one and set off together to a new place.
