title: What is that Smell
text: We have milk, egg, bread and vegetables in the fridge," said Ma. "I will cook for dinner!" said Pa. "Pa, can you cook fried rice?" Tara asked. "Fried rice," Madhav replied. When Tara, Madhav, Ma and Pa entered their house, they knew something was wrong. Absolutely wrong. "Cheel What is that smell?" Tara shouted. "MONSTER!" Madhav shouted. It's hot, dark and smelly. The whole house stinks! Where does this smell come from? Ma checking the bedroom. Madhav checking the bathroom. Tara checking the dining room. Pa checking the kitchen. "It is from there", said Pa while pointing to the fridge "Fridge Monster that smelly?" Tara was surprised " I'm scared," said Madhav while hugging Ma. "Let's open the fridge and see what is inside," said Ma. Ma opened the fridge. Everyone covered their noses and mouths. "Hmm, it's warm inside and the lights are off," said Ma while putting her hand inside the fridge. "What happened?" Tara asked. "The fridge didn't work a while ago," Pa explained. "Without cold air, everything is spoil," said Ma with a grim face. "Is the milk spoiled?" Tara asked. "Yes, can you smell how sour it is?" Ma asked. "Milk needs to be kept at a cool temperature to keep it fresh," said Pa. "Does the bread was spoil?" Tara asked. "Yeah, did you see that green stuff? It's mold," said Pa, "It grows on bread." "Fluffy" said Madhav, curiously. "Don't touch it," said Pa. "You'll get sick if you eat it." "Are the vegetables also spoil?" Tara asked sadly. "Yes, that vegetables were spoil," said Ma. " We can't eat it" Madhav grabbed an egg and dropped it "Madhav, now smells worse!" Tara shouted. "Oh no! the smells became worse, "said Pa. Tara was sure she would never eat eggs again "Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Madhav cried, walked away while Pa cleans up the mess. They put all the rotten food in a garbage bag and cleaned out the fridge. "Why does everything rot?" asked Tara. "Everything goes rot over time. The cold air of the fridge keeps the food fresh for longer. When it's warm, food spoils faster," said Ma. Are all the foods rot? Tara asked "This rice is not rotten," said Ma, "And neither are these potatoes, at least temporarily." "And this pickle isn't either," said Pa. "Neither is this butter," said Ma. "We can eat butter rice and potatoes!" said Tara, happily. The Invisible Monster Tara and Madhav thought there was an invisible monster in their house. Although there were no monsters, they were right about there being "something invisible!" When food becomes rot and inedible for humans, the cause is that something invisible starts eating the food. Those invisible things are referred to as microbes. Microbes are not completely invisible. They are just very, very, very small (even smaller than the smallest insect you've ever seen). We need a tool called a microscope to see microbes. They look like this. When food goes bad There are some foods that spoil faster than others and some foods that do not spoil easily. Wet foods like fruits and vegetables will spoil faster. Dry foods like beans and rice do not go bad easily. Foods such as eggs, meat and cheese will spoil faster. Preserved foods like pickles and butter can last longer. Packaged foods like biscuits and candies also last longer than others.

title: Odd one out
text: Amov was busy getting ready. He was in a hurry. Getting ready was not easy when you are only five years old. Usually, you are petted by parents, who help you with things. That is ok. But, Amov was miles apart from ordinary. He was his own boss. He would do things on his own, for example, open the big, old, wooden wardrobe ajar, hunt for his clothes. He kept an adjustable stool to search the shelves on top and he never dropped a single thing! But today was different, he was in too much hurry. He was the captain of his play team. There was a meeting in the park to decide the holiday plan. He was the boss anywhere. Just as he left the house, he could hear his mummy speak over the receiver: “Amov is a little boss!” and it pleased him. At five years, Amov could sing small rap songs in his mother’s parties and all the aunties would praise and cuddle him. Feeling like The lion King, Amov entered the park. There were children all over. Suck ruckus! He thought. Then he spotted his group near the slide. And there was Elle. He disliked Elle, for she was the only one who did not praise him like others and stared as he was just ordinary. As he reached his friends, Elle turned, looked at him from top to bottom and then suddenly uttered something and giggled! His other playmates looked at him and Elle not knowing what to do, but they soon started smiling too. And then he realized the cause. He had worn the wrong sock pair. His left one was blue and right one was red. Other children would have cried and ran back home. But Amov was a boss. He knew how to handle everything. He smiled at his friends and said, “Friends, how did you like the joke? Tomorrow everyone must wear something odd, ok.” With this he glanced at Elle, who knew she no longer had the upper hand.

title: The Curious Caterpillar
text: Once upon a time, in a lush green garden, lived a tiny, curious caterpillar named Pip. Pip loved to explore his surroundings, and he was always on the lookout for new and exciting things. One day, when he spotted a large, flowing body of water, he was curious to know more about it. So, he decided to venture closer and check it out. On the way, he became hungry, so he started munching on a juicy leaf. Suddenly, he spotted a strange, green, slimy creature hopping nearby. "Who are you?" Pip asked, his voice barely a whisper. "I'm a frog," the creature croaked. "And you, little friend?" "I'm Pip, the caterpillar," he replied. Not long after, he encountered another strange sight: a creature with eight legs and a hairy body. A large spider was sitting at its center, watching the world go by. "Hello there," Pip greeted the creature. "What are you called?" "I'm a spider," the creature replied, spinning a web. "Your web is amazing!" The spider smiled. "Thank you. It's my home." Just when Pip thought he had seen enough, he came across a gigantic, red creature with pincers. It was the biggest creature Pip had ever seen! "Wow!" Pip exclaimed. "You're huge! What are you?" "I'm a crab," the creature said, snapping its pincers. As Pip was about to continue his exploration, he heard a strange cracking sound: "Crack, Crack!" He followed the noise and found a chicken egg lying on the ground, about to hatch. Just as the tiny chick began to emerge, a mother hen appeared, clucking angrily. "Stay away from my egg!" she squawked, her beak snapping at Pip. Pip was terrified. He knew he had to do something quickly. He scurried behind a nearby rock and watched as the mother hen carefully gathered her chick and led it away. Relieved, Pip continued his exploration. Soon, he saw a cocoon. Thrilled, he kept observing it for a long time. As the sun began to set, Pip decided it was time to head home. He had learned so much that day, meeting new creatures and experiencing a thrilling adventure. As he curled up on a soft leaf, Pip couldn't wait to see what the next day would bring. That was the time for him to build a cocoon for himself. Soon, he started making one. As he crawled back to his cozy cocoon, Pip couldn't wait to share his stories with the others. Pip had successfully transformed into a beautiful butterfly. He was now wiser and had made many new friends. As he soared through the garden, Pip felt a sense of peace and fulfillment. He knew that his adventures had prepared him for the exciting life ahead.

title: Chotu ran!
text: Chotu ran, he ran very fast that day. His palms tightly clenched in a fist, exerting all the energy an 11-year-old could muster. There were people running behind him. He had no other option, he had to run or else the inevitable would happen. Chotu had the bag fastened to his shoulders, the bag had something very precious. He ran fast, yet was careful with the bag with a box in it... Chotu saw the bus at the bus stop; the bus was about to leave. Chotu ran faster, as he was nearing the door the bus picked up speed. People hanging out from the door, tried to extend their hands to help him get in. Chotu didn’t stretch his hand, he wasn’t interested, he didn’t want to catch the bus...he just ran, faster than ever. "Chor chor catch him catch him” the noise of the people rushing behind him grew louder, Chotu tightened his grip on the bag he was holding and ran...The people got closer and closer. Chotu couldn’t stop to look behind, he continued running. The people got closer to him...they crossed him and chased the thief they were after. Chotu just ran... The sweltering afternoon sun couldn’t stop him, he felt the heat, the dehydration was catching up, he was feeling tired, but to stop was the last thing on his mind. Chotu imagined himself to be a horse, galloping on the race track. His hair flying in the breeze, the air freshening up his face. He had only one thought that the Jockey always has, to leave all the horses behind and to be the fastest and that is what he strived too... Chotu ran, as he was running he heard the school bell ring in the distance, he ran faster, this is the school he attended to, the school he loved, he never liked to miss school. He got closer to the school as the ring faded in the background. He went past the school. He had missed school that day and now it was home time, he had no interest to stop and answer his friends about his absence, he just ran. Chotu suddenly had this thought that he could be the Usain Bolt of his town, world-famous in his own town! He gushed at the thought. Never in his life had he run so much or so fast, but today he was enjoying every moment of it. He mentally made a note to participate in the running race competition in the sports event to be held in school. He was pretty sure that if he ran like today on that day he obviously would come first... The thought energised him to run even faster. Chotu was just a few minutes away from his home now, yet he didn’t slow down. There was a reason he was running so fast, he was in no mood to slow down. He knew that his little sister would be eagerly waiting for him. He knew that he had to reach home fast before it was too late. He had to reach home fast. Before the ice cream could melt! Yes! His sister had wished to eat ice cream and he had rushed out on a summer afternoon, to get her some. He didn’t want the ice cream to melt. He wanted to see her jump up in delight when he gave her the ice cream. He ran fast, he wanted the moment to be perfect.

title: The Fox & the Grapes
text: A Fox one day spied a beautiful bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a vine trained along the branches of a tree. The grapes seemed ready to burst with juice, and the Fox's mouth watered as he gazed longingly at them. The bunch hung from a high branch, and the Fox had to jump for it. The first time he jumped he missed it by a long way. So he walked off a short distance and took a running leap at it, only to fall short once more. Again and again he tried, but in vain. Now he sat down and looked at the grapes in disgust. "What a fool I am," he said. "Here I am wearing myself out to get a bunch of sour grapes that are not worth gaping for." And off he walked very, very scornfully. There are many who pretend to despise and belittle that which is beyond their reach.

title: Almost There...
text: I can't do it, I just can't! Annoyed, I chant. I reach up, with all my might. But no! It's just not right! To lift each other we need encouragement, But all we have now is discouragement. How will we do this? They all ask. My sister tells them,"It's an easy task!" I'm on it! Oh, on this cycle, I am able to sit! Ouch, I crash! Onto the grass I smash, all in a flash. "HA HA!" They all laugh. I was almost there! "I will get up again!" I declare. I didn't know what the others would think and I didn't care! I had success! I knew they were not more and I was not less. They all cheered, and not even one of them sneered. I love riding my bike! It is what I really like. My sister and I, oh, it feels like we fly!

title: The Foolish Lion
text: Once, there was a jungle. There were many animals. They had a meeting of all the animals about Raja the crazy lion. '' Raja has killed my baby.'' said the cow. ''All my friends has killed by that stupid lion" said the Roosters. "My entire family has killed by that lion" said the Dog. All animals were very worried. " I have a plan!" said the goat. '' What plan did you have?" said the Roosters. '' My plan is that one animal will go in the Raja's den everyday" said the goat. "What rubbish plan it is!!" said all the animals. " Yes, We want to live,do not want to die. If you wish you can go and be a food for Raja's Den." said the Dog. " First listen!! The Raja is a crazy lion. He killed with no reasons. So, If we send him an animal on everyday then, He will stop killing us. He will kill and eat only that animal which has gone to his den and then Two Three months he will die or he will become lazy then, We would kill him easily. What you say??" finished the goat. All the animals thought for a while and then agreed. Then, The Dog goes to the Raja's den and he said " Oh Majesty!! You are our king. Please listen to me carefully you have killed our all relatives,friends and family. So, today I have come with a plan which I would like to share with you. Everyday we will send you one animal in your den" said the Dog. Then, The Raja roared loudly. He said " Well, I'm not very happy with your plan. But, Listen to me very carefully If any day you will not send one animal that will be the last day of the animals. Am I clear." said the Raja with a loud voice. "Yes, Yes, My lord" said the Dog. Then, that day starts. Everyday they send one animal to his den. This went for many days. One day, There was the turn of the clever rabbit Crafty. He was very clever. When, All the animals tell him to go Crafty was unhappy. He was very sad. " Why would I go? I don't want to be eaten by that stupid lion. Let me Think." Then, He started walking towards Raja's den. It was a very long walk. When, He was walking he saw a well. " I'm very thirsty Oh! There is a well" said Crafty. When, He looked down he saw that the water was very deep. He saw his own reflection. " No luck!!" He thought. When, He turned back to go. One smile came on his face. "Yes, Yes!! That is the plan." Crafty said. When, He came to the lion he saw that the lion was very angry. He burst out of his mind. "What rubbish!! You rubbish hare. you came so late. Why?? I will kill you." said the Raja. " Oh! Sorry My Majesty. When, I was walking I saw a lion. I thought you are there. But, You were not there so, Who he was?? ''What! You saw a lion. Where??" asked Raja. " You want to know, come I will tell you." said crafty. He took him to that well. "Ah! There is the other lion. You look like a fool." said Raja. The voice echo from the well. The Raja was angry. Then, Raja was very angry he jumped into the water Splash! Splash!! " Help! Help!! Raja cried. He drowned into the water and died. Crafty ran to the animals to tell that Raja has died. All the animals started dancing. The whole jungle started dancing. They thanked Crafty the Rabbit to save them.

title: Little Duckling Andrea quackes naughty
text: Duck Andrea has just climbed ashore, and because the sun was so warm she decided to have a quick nap. She carefully balanced on one leg and tucked her head under her wings. Just before she fell asleep she remembered the time when she was still a tiny, yellow ball of fluff. Andrea the Duckling! Suddenly she sees herself as the tiny duckling in the water. Swimming in the big beautiful world of wind and sun on the water. But also in the dark reeds where you had to swim through as a duckling. And where you know there were rats waiting for little ducklings. They can suddenly pull you down into the water by your legs, and… Andrea remembers how as a young duck she couldn’t control all her muscles like other little ducklings could. She had not yet learned properly how to use her webbed feet. And that became painfully obvious on a terrible day. Right at the moment when she wanted to show mother duck how clever and independent she already was. That became a really awful day! But she found something! In order to show she was different and not just a tiny duckling who was sometimes really scared by the big water world, she had invented something. Something she had discovered quite by accident. She had discovered that she only had to peep ‘Fletch’ or ‘Flatch’ instead of quacking like a normal duckling. If she peeped ‘Fletch’ or ‘Flatch’ all the other young ducks put their heads together and started to quack “Have you heard? Andrea said Fletch and even Flatch!” To Andrea’s astonishment, every time she peeped ‘Fletch’ or ‘Flatch’, all the other ducks quacked about it. So then she made up Flotch and Flutch and that had even more success. It wasn’t until later that she understood that, in duck language, these were naughty words. Duck Andrea was almost asleep in the warm sun, with her head under her wings, but she had to grin at the memory of all this. It was actually very clever of the little duckling Andrea. When she had grown up and become a young duck who could manage her webbed feet perfectly, she had found other ways of expressing herself. Saying ‘Fletch’, ‘Flatch’ and ‘Flotch’ and ‘Flutch’ got lots of reactions but not exactly the reaction she wanted. What did she really want? Was it to make lots of noise with the other young ducks, and to pinch them in their strong little bodies with her beak? Throw mud at them with her webbed feet? Or just to chat with them? To tell the others clearly what she felt and thought? If the slightly older drakes were messing about she wanted to learn to shake off their teasing, in the same way as a duck shakes off drops of water from its feathers. She’d had to learn to do that, shake off all the drops of water, but that had immediately become a great game. Imagine being able to do that with the drakes’ teasing! Just shake it all off! That would make them look up! That was a much better way of getting to them than pinching them with her beak. Andrea thinks back and is very satisfied with her behavior as a young duck – she wasn’t stupid! Not at all! Andrea knows that she can now express herself really clearly, and she wonders how and when she learned this, that clear quacking she can now do? She can’t remember, it must have happened of its own accord. She no longer finds it interesting to use Fletch, Flatch, Flotch and Flutch. Whichever way you look at it they are not clear quacking duck language. But what if she were to use them ….. By now Andrea is fast asleep with her head under her wings. In the big outdoor world where the reeds rustle gently and the birds sing tirelessly. The sun shines warm on Andrea’s head and the rays are mirrored in the rippling of the water. If you see Andrea there in the grass, standing strongly on one leg, then you are so pleased to see that she has grown beautifully! And you understand at once that you can look to her future with great confidence. You can imagine her discovering more of the world every day and each day with more and more self-confidence.

title: An American Mouse In India
text: Once, there was a mouse named Rock. He was very clever but, he was very scared also. He lived in America's jungle in a big hole. Rock loved that jungle. He named it as Loving Balloon. One day, Rock was walking in the Loving Balloon. But, Suddenly, he heard a voice. " This voice is like a vehicle" said the Rock. When, he saw there was a big truck. It was loaded with heavy things " Oh! What's that sound in the vehicle? Is it an animal? thought Rock. Wow!! What a fragrance is coming. I think I should go to see" said Rock. When, he goes to the truck. He saw that there was a cheese over there. He run to eat the cheese. Then, Suddenly, Rock hear a voice Splash! " What's that voice?" Rock said. When, He look, he saw that the truck's gate was closed. " Oh no! The gate is closed! What I do now?" said the Rock unhappily. Then, He heard a sound " Meow! Meow! " What's that sound?" he said. When, he look,he find a cat over there. The cat started chasing the Rock. But, Suddenly, The man open's the truck's door. The cat ran and Rock went out. When, He saw, he was shocked. The place the country where he lived now he was not there. Because, Now he was in India. He walked slowly in the city. Now, It seems to be night. But, he continued walking. He was very sad because he was missing his parents " What fool I'm? Why I went to the truck? Why?" He said unhappily while he was crossing a river. But, Suddenly, It started raining. Rock hide under a leaf. Slowly, Slowly it begins faster. " What a faster rain there is in India. In our country there is no water to drink" said the Rock to himself. But, The rain did not stopped. " Oh! Here it is so cool. I should spend this night here only" said the Rock. He sat down under the leaf and slept. The next morning, When, He got up, he saw that the rain was stopped. He started walking. When, He was on his way, he heard a voice. He looked up in the sky. " Oh! That is a plane" said the Rock happily. But, Then one smile came on his face " Yes! That's the idea! Yes!" yelled Rock joyfully. He ran towards the airport. He was very happy. He took a ticket and saw that in how much time the plane will come. He was standing towards the window. He saw his plane. He ran towards the plane. He ran to see, But, he saw that the plane which has come was not his plane " Oh no! The plane is too late" said the Rock sadly. But, then he saw a jet over there. He took the jet. He went to America. He ran towards the Loving Balloons. He find his hole and entered in. When, His family saw him. They were very very happy. He hugged his family and said sorry to them.

title: CAPPY THE CATERPILLAR
text: Cappy the caterpillar, had no time to waste. He had just hatched. He looked around at his brothers and sisters. All were eating away at the leaves of the plant where they had been born. No sense of adventure, Cappy thought sadly. He saw a leaf ready to drop down. He clung to it, trying to keep his balance. The leaf broke free and sailed down. Cappy got his first free ride. He landed safely on the ground. But it was so hot! Cappy found a small buttercup. He promptly put it on his head. He saw a beautiful flower. He must smell it. He slowly climbed up the stem. Then he poked his nose into the centre of the flower. The pollen tickled his new, sensitive nose and Cappy went ATISHOO! ATISHOO! ATISHOO!!! Cappy sailed through the air and landed in a clump of weeds. An ant took pity on him. ‘Come, I will help you up a bush. You need food and shelter.’ Cappy was happy. He had a friend. But he was doubtful. ‘How can you carry me up a bush? You are so tiny, I can carry you myself.’ ‘ Wait. We ants are intelligent.’ The ant put his antenna into his mouth and gave a piercing whistle. Cappy put his antenna into his ears. What an ear-splitting sound! A whole column of tiny creatures came crawling up. Without waiting for Cappy’s permission, they gathered him up. The ants took him half way up a bush. ‘Here you will have enough to eat. And the leaves will also hide you. Be careful.’ His friend, the ant winked at him and went down. Cappy nibbled many leaves, and ate the softest and sweetest of them. I am sorry to say he was a little wasteful. Cappy looked up at the night sky. Cappy sighed, tired but happy, and soon was gently snoring. Now let us wait for Cappy's next adventure!

title: Appu's Comb
text: Suvidha Mistry Appu was a very obedient and sincere boy. He would complete all his schoolwork on time. He would practice singing lessons every day. He even packed his school bag and kept his uniform ready before going to bed the previous night. However, he had one unpleasant habit that often got him into trouble. Do you know what was it? He would never keep his things back in place. After finishing the homework, his pencils, sharpener and eraser would be lying on the table till his father came and put them away. After his music practice his music book and shruti box would be left on the floor till his sister picked it up and kept it away. 'Appu, keep your things back in place,' his father would say. Ok, Pitashree. ﻿However, Appu never remembered to keep things back in place. One day, he was getting ready for school. He had worn his uniform and was combing his hair. That was his mother calling out to him. Appu, come. We all are ready. Let's go else we shall be late for school. Coming, Matashree! In his hurry, he kept his comb on his mother's pen stand and went off for the day. The next day, after wearing the uniform, he was looking for the comb to comb his hair. He remembered keeping it in his mother's pen stand, but....... it was not there on the pen stand that morning. He looked for it under his mother's desk to see if it was fallen on the floor- but no, it was not there. He searched for it even under the bed by crawling beneath it. That's when his mother walked inside. Appu, why are you hiding under the bed? Amma, I kept my comb yesterday on your pen stand after combing my hair. Now I cannot find it. Is my pen stand the place to keep your comb? No. Then why did you leave it there? Sorry, Amma, my mistake as I did not keep it properly. Ok. Go and look for it in the place where it should be. Appu understood and upon opening the door of his dressing table......... found his comb there! I kept it back in the drawer when I found it on my pen stand, Appu. Please keep things back in their proper place otherwise it will be difficult to find them. Post Story Activities: 1- What do you think? Did Appu change his ways after this incident? Discuss with your teacher and family members. 2- Have you also faced similar situations? What's your story? Share it with you teacher and family members.
author: Ira Periyavallur (aka Indira VMD)
illustrator: Adonay Gebru; ASM Tanvir Hassan Raju; Clyde   Beech; Genevieve Terblanche; Ira Periyavallur (aka Indira VMD); Mahee Puri; Nyambura Kariuki; Priya Dali; Rajiv Eipe; Rhea Sood; Rishabh Goswami; Rutuja Joshi; Sunando C; Suvidha Mistry

title: The little bear
text: Once upon a time, in a distant forest, there was a mother bear with her little cub. The puppy was very curious, but the mother bear always tried to warn him that the forest was is very big and he could get lost. But one day while the mother bear had gone to look for food, the puppy decided to go alone to explore the forest without listening to mother bear. Suddenly the little puppy stopped, and realized that he had moved away, he looked around to look for his home but couldn't find it. The puppy had climbed up the tree because he wanted to see if he could find his home, but suddenly the tree broke and the little puppy had fallen. Mother bear was happy to have found her cub, but also worried about what happened to him, took her cub in her arms and they both went home happy to have found each other again.

title: The Feline Friend
text: Sumi stared out of her bedroom window listlessly. The seven-year-old had just heard that her cousins had cancelled their visit to her house during summer vacation. She had looked forward to a fun time with them, but now it would be a boring vacation alone. Even her friends from the colony were going to be out. “Sumi, cheer up,” said her mother, stroking her hair, “Here, have some ice cream.” Sumi didn’t turn around for she didn’t want her mother to see the tears welling in her eyes. “I’ll leave the bowl here. Eat it before it melts,” said Sumi's mother as she left the room. “Plop!” Something fell onto the window ledge. “Eek!” cried Sumi as she fell back in her chair. “Meow,” came a sound from the ball of white fur that steadied itself after the jump. “You scared me,” said Sumi, smiling. “Meow meow,” replied the cat, rubbing itself against the window grills. “Hungry?” asked Sumi, picking up the bowl of ice cream, " Want to share it with me?" A few minutes later, the bowl was empty, and the friends purred with satisfaction. “Mooli, you need to eat well,” said Sumi, wagging her tiny finger at the bony cat that evening. She held out a piece of paneer which Mooli promptly grabbed in its mouth. Sumi found no reason to tell her family about Mooli as the cat stayed outdoors and came to her window only when hungry. Besides, she always had food to share – milk, chips, curd rice, paneer and Mooli’s favourite ice cream. A month’s vacation went by without Sumi even noticing. She observed that Mooli was no longer skinny. Its fur had grown soft and long. “Too much ice cream,” she told Mooli, brushing its white fur, “I am going to Grandma’s house tomorrow and will return soon. Don’t forget me.” The following morning, Sumi left for a short holiday. A week later, Sumi came back. To her horror, Mooli was nowhere to be seen. Even after a fortnight, there was no sign of her feline friend. Sumi was inconsolable. Luckily for her, her vacation ended, and soon she got busy with school. Two months later, Sumi overheard her mother talking to her father in their bedroom one morning. “That horrible sound... like somebody's scratching metal. I heard it coming from there last night,” said her mother, pointing to the metal wardrobe in the corner of the room. “I hope it isn’t a mouse,” she continued, shuddering at the very thought. “Can't be a mouse … I haven’t seen one around for a while now,” replied Sumi's father. “Aha!” thought Sumi. Somebody had been taking care of the mice in her house. Seconds later, the scratching sound came again. Be fore anybody could react, a figure on four legs emerged from under the wardrobe. “A cat!" cried her father, "With something in its mouth!" “Eek! A mouse!” screamed her mother. Sumi instantly recognized the cat. And certainly, there was no mouse in its mouth. Out walked a nervous-looking Mooli with a fluffy little kitten in its mouth.
author: Rajani Muralidhar

title: Pia Goes to Chandni Chowk
text: Pia misses Nini a lot. Nini moved to Kolkata and hasn’t been to Delhi in a long time. Nini would love to take Pia to Chandni Chowk, the place where she grew up. But she cannot walk around much. Pia has an idea. Off she goes to Chandni Chowk with her Ma. Bright pink, grass green and mango yellow. Are these colours in a box of crayons? “Creamy, juicy and frozen! I know why Nini loves fruit kulfi,” says Pia. “I want some more.” A big black kadhai sizzling with ghee. Bubble, bubble, bubble. Plop goes a twirly orange spiral. “Hot, crunchy and sweet. No wonder, Nini loves jalebis,” says Pia. “I want some more.” Is that a cloud? Oh, it melts in the mouth. “White, fluffy and streaked with the sun. That explains why Nini loves daulat ki chaat!” says Pia. “I want some more.” Are those slippery yellow and pink worms, on top of a creamy white puddle? “Cold, slimy and smooth. I can see why Nini loves rabri falooda,” says Pia. “I want some more.” What does Pia bring home for Nini? Cold kulfi. Hot jalebis. Fluffy daulat ki chaat. Creamy rabri falooda. “The best memories of Chandni Chowk,” says Nini.
author: Shinibali Saigal

title: The little tiger

Morpheus was angry so he decided to show the other animals how bad he could get, so he started hunting furiously. title: A loyal German Shepherd
text: The moon hung high in the ink-black sky, casting eerie shadows on the ground as Max, a loyal German Shepherd, patrolled the backyard. His sharp ears pricked at the slightest rustle of leaves, and his nose twitched, detecting a scent that made his fur stand on end. Max had always been the protector of his human family, and tonight, something felt wrong—terribly wrong. The air was thick with an unfamiliar, metallic scent that made his instincts scream danger. Max's eyes darted towards the old, gnarled oak tree at the end of the yard, where a strange silhouette seemed to flicker in the moonlight. He growled softly, low and menacing, but the figure did not retreat. Instead, it moved closer, revealing a pair of glowing red eyes that bore into Max's soul. A chilling wind whipped through the yard, carrying whispers that seemed to say his name in sinister tones. Max's muscles tensed, and he barked fiercely, hoping to scare away whatever malevolent presence had invaded his territory. Suddenly, the whispers grew louder, forming a cacophony of voices that surrounded Max, making it impossible to pinpoint their origin. The figure with the red eyes advanced, its shape shifting and undulating like a living shadow. Max lunged, teeth bared, but his jaws snapped shut on empty air. The entity vanished, leaving behind only the echo of its haunting laughter. Max's heart pounded as he realized this was no ordinary intruder. He had crossed paths with something otherworldly, and he knew that protecting his family from this darkness would be his greatest challenge yet.

title: The Detective with a Golden Heart
text: There was a school named Ryan Public school in a small town called Nayanpur. The school was famous for its quality education and it used to produce very talented students each year. Once specific year, the school Principal observed the result of one class was deteriorating. He took the input from the class teacher to find out the reason. They observed a peculiar behavior of the class from past few months that majority of the students are feeling drowsy and sleepy most of the day during class hours. So, the Principal called a Parents Teachers Meeting and communicated this behavior to the parents and requested them to take care of their kids. Still Parents were surprised as they used to take care of their kids properly. So finally, the Principal called one detective named John to the school and requested him to find the cause of the situation. John observed few days in the school and found an interesting peculiar reason behind this. There was a student named Babloo who was naughty and used to get scold by the teachers every day for his conduct. As a punishment he was asked to refrain to attend the morning assembly of the school. Babloo got annoyed because of this and planned to take a revenge to the whole class. He arranged some sleeping medicine powder and use to mix with the foods in each tiffin box of all students during the morning assembly, since except him all were attending assembly at the school ground. All students use to take food in their recess time. Soon after that all used to get sleep because of the medicine effect. Detective John called Babloo and narrated the whole findings with him. Babloo thought no one can catch him. He requested John not to complain to School or to his parents. He got worried about his career, and the reputation of his and his parents in the society. John saw a light of realization in the eyes of Babloo. So John advised Babloo not to have a revenge attitude to harm others, rather study hard to make your position and show your value to your school and to the society. Babloo promised to follow his golden piece of advice. In somedays the teachers observed that all the class students became active throughout the class and as the result was great subsequently. The principal called detective John and asked if he found the reason and solved it? John told, yes. When the principal asked about the fact, detective John smiled and said “It’s the magic of realization” and left the premises.

title: A Week in Antarctica
text: I still remember that day when I got stuck on the white continent, Antarctica. We had planned to go to Antarctica and stay there only for 1 day, but our ship's engine stopped working on reaching there. We started calling for help immediately. The rescuers said that it would take them 7 days to reach. That meant we had to live here for 1 week. Luckily, we had brought enough food with us for the journey. DAY 1 We could see snow and large icebergs. We could also see polar bears and penguins. We wanted to explore, but we were feeling extremely cold. It was day time, so it was a little warmer. So, we just went to explore the icy lands nearby. We had also made igloos and shifted our stuff there. We returned in the evening, when it was getting colder. We then had dinner and slept, waiting for help and an another day to explore. DAY 2 We woke up and started to communicate with the rescuers. They said that it would take them 5 days more to reach. We then went to explore the snowy land. I was familiar with the nearby lands. My mom showed me penguins marching on the land. I also saw big and cute polar bears. I had seen a penguin that carried an egg between it legs. Then we came back tired, because today we went farther from yesterday. DAY 3 We woke up after a long nap, but we were still feeling very tired. But we decided to go out and just walk a little. We came back in just 5 or 10 minutes and slept. Our sleep broke in the middle of the night. We were already curious to see the land at night. It was looking beautiful at night! But we were feeling sleepy so we came back in just 5 minutes. DAY 4 We woke up and were ready for a new day. 3 days remaining for the rescuers to come. I went out and played in the snow with my friend that I had made here. I don't remember his name, but I remember that how much fun we had on this day. We also made a snowman, but without a nose. Still it was looking great! We also played snowball fight. In the evening, we were so exhausted and slept in a blink of an eye. DAY 5 When I woke up, I remembered that in the night, fast winds were blowing outside the igloo. When I got out of the igloo, I saw that the snow man was destroyed, as expected. My friend was still fast asleep. I started creating an another snowman. But, I had an idea to prank my friend. I made only the body of the snowman and pilled up a bunch of snowballs right at the entrance of my friend's igloo and woke him up. I called him to help me make an another snowman. And when he came out of the igloo, I started throwing snowballs and every snowball hit him. I laughed at him, but he had other plans. When I was throwing snowballs at him, in that time he made so many snowballs that I had to run from him. I hid behind the half complete snowman watching him look for me. I made some snow balls and threw at him. He shouted "If you have guts, then come in front of me and then throw them". I came out and threw a snowball right at his face. He shouted "AAAAAAAAAA". I laughed and ran away. He was looking for me the entire day. But I was successful in hiding myself till the evening. We were so involved in the fun that when we came back and laid down, we felt that the day was only for 1 hour! I was so tired that I didn't know when I slept. DAY 6 I woke up, excited because there was only 1 more day remaining for the rescuers to come. I thought that my friend must be waiting outside with snowballs to throw at me. So, I made some of them inside my igloo, like 5 or 10 something. I came out of my igloo running so that he could not throw any snowballs at me, and when I turned back, I saw my friend at my igloo entrance looking for me where I had gone. I threw a snowball at him. He got soo angry that he threw all his snowballs everywhere. Some hit me but I dodged some. I came out of my hiding spot, seeing his hand empty without any snowballs, I started throwing them and he ran away, but I caught up to him and continued to throw snowballs at him. After some time, we came back to our igloos and helped the elders to pack the stuff for tomorrow. Till dinner time, we packed all the stuff and slept, waiting for the rescuers to come and take us all. DAY 7 I woke up and ran out to look for the rescuers, but saw none. We contacted the rescuers and they said that it would take them 1 hour more to reach. I went to my friend's igloo and woke him up and I said "TODAY IS A SPECIAL DAY!". He asked me " Now what is special today?". I said "Today the rescuers will come and will take us all. He stood up and went out to see. He said "No one is there. Are you pranking me?". I said "Our parents just communicated with the rescuers and they said that it would take them only 1 hour more to reach. I think only 50 minutes are remining now. So let's help our parents packing the remaining stuff and then play our favorite game, SNOWBALLS!". He said "Ok!" to me and went. After the 20 minutes of packing the remaining stuff, there was 30 minutes left to play! So I called my friend to play and I said "Let's make some heighted barriers for us to hide. He said then said ok and we started making the barriers. I made a large one and said "Should we start the game?!" He shouted "OK!". When I peeked to see his barrier, it was small that I could see his whole face, and you must have guessed where I had threw the first snowball at. His face of course. He stood up and threw some snowballs in the air, that were coming straight at me. I saw only one in the air and not the other ones and shouted "What could only one snowball do to me?". He said "We'll see about that.....". Then all the snowballs came rushing at me. We had soo much fun. Once I sneaked up to him and I threw all the snowballs at him. Finally, it was the time when the rescuers came. They had came on a huge ship. We started loading our stuff and climbed upon the ship, saying a final goodbye to Antarctica. The ship started sailing and reached far, but we could still see the 'White Continent'. We only had 2 hours of network there. So we had to communicate in those 2 hours only. We enjoyed the ship journey and we reached home safely. I still wonder that where my snowball fight companion is now.
author: Darsh Gupta

title: The Backbencher Club
text: There went Rajesh quickly with his bag to his school. His mother shouted "Don't leave your water bottle!" Rajesh took the water bottle and went to school as speed as light. Maya, Vinesh and Kushal were waiting for Rajesh. And, lo! Rajesh was at the class room door. "Well, well. Look who is late!" said Kushal. "I had a deep slumber yesterday" said Rajesh scratching his head. "Anyways, I had an idea of creating a club for us" said Maya. "What shall we name it?" "I guess we could name it the back bencher club!" said an enthusiastic Vinesh. "The main motto of the group is to solve mysteries and chat a little." said Vinesh "Which place would we choose for holding meetings? asked Kushal "I would prefer the backyard of the school." said Maya "I have heard that someone was threatening Karan this weak" said Rajesh " Team we have got a new mystery!" exclaimed Maya. The team scheduled it at recess. They discussed about why it would have happened. They decide to ask Karan about it. Karan said "T he fellow was a middle school teenager. The guy had a red jacket with red shoes." They thought for some while and asked the permission of the principal to see the CCTV footage. They saw the face of the teenager and was surprised as he was the best student of class 8. They called him from the class and asked the reason. The teen went in tears and said that he was always teased by Karan and wanted to take revenge. Now the four friends understood that two of them were the culprits of the situation. The four friends took pity on them and thought of a mild punishment. They asked the Principal that if they could sit together for a week and become friends with each other as a type of punishment. The principal was pleased to hear this and allowed them. Then the two became friends. Maya exclaimed "Case solved!" with a giggle.

title: Kittu's Friends
text: Once upon a time, there was a large and beautiful garden. The name of the garden was Kittu. Kittu was very popular in the city. Many children came and played here. Kittu became happy on watching the children playing in the garden. In the rainy season, peacocks also came in the garden. When it rained, peacocks opened their feathers and danced happily in the rain. The children stopped playing and started watching the peacocks dancing. There were many big trees in the garden. In the summer season, the mango tree became full of fruits. So, when children came from school, they immediately rushed to the garden and climbed up the mango tree and then sat on a branch and plucked and ate the sweet and juicy mangoes. In the winter season, the children would go and pluck and eat the apples from the apple tree. In the rainy season, the children plucked and ate the litchi hanging on the trees. There, many bids came and made nests and also layed eggs inside it and also sang sweet songs. The children loved to hear the songs of the birds. Kittu also loved the songs. There, children also played Holi in the garden. The colours and water also fell on Kittu and he was happy on watching the children play. One day, some people came and started to drive away the children from the garden. They also started to cut down the trees. Then all the children and their parents stood in oppose of this. One person asked "What are you all doing?". Then one of the people who had came said "The government has sent us to make a road here". All the parents and children became angry and said "We will not let anything happen to this garden! It is our play place and the trees inside it give us sweet fruits to eat and also oxygen to keep us alive". All those people were against this decision of the government. One person said "Trees and plants are living beings like us and they also feel pain". Then, a person from the government said "We are impressed by your words and we are feeling sad. Please forgive us". The people there forgave them and all the people and children together sowed many seeds in the garden and after a few years, big trees had grown from them. Kittu was very happy to see all this. Now the children had grown up and suddenly Kittu noticed that the children were not coming to play anymore. Kittu was waiting for the children for some days. Then one day, the mothers of two children were talking about something. Kittu heard that now the children are busy within the fake world of mobile phones instead of playing in the garden. The parents of the children were very sad. Then they thought, why shouldn't we organize a fair in the garden? As soon as the children came to know that there is a fair in the garden, all the children called their friends and went to the fair. They saw that there were many games inside it. Kittu was very happy to see the children after many days playing happily in the garden and the children realized that the real world is more fun than the fake world of 'mobile phones'. They decided that now they will watch their mobile phones only when in need and they will play with their real friends and the children and Kittu started living happily once again. Lesson:- 1. We should protect trees 2. We should use mobiles less.
author: Darsh Gupta
illustrator: Harshvardhan Gantha; Kavita Singh Kale; Nimret Handa; Nirzara Verulkar; Partho Sengupta; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Farmer and the peacock
text: Farmer and the peacock p Once upon a time there lived a farmer in a village called Ramsa.The farmer was a very hardworking man. He used to work day and night in his farm to produce a better yield. But there was a problem. His fields were getting exploited every day. He wondered what could be the reason for it. One day he stayed in the fields for long hours. He found that a group of crows were coming regularly there and exploiting all tha crops. He also noticed that a peocock was also regularly visiting the farm. But that peacock was good and not disturbing the fields. But annoyed from crows farmer decided to teach them a lesson. He then bought a net to catch all the crow. On that day peacock also sat with crows. And on the process to catch crows in the net,peacock was also caught and thrown alway in the jungle. Moral of the story Staying in the company of the bad people wil always get you in unwanted trouble.

title: Gogo: The friend of all
text: In a jungle lived an elephant named Gogo. He was the only elephant in the jungle and had no friends and family. He tried to be friends with other animals, but no one was ready to make him their friend. Mummy, Run! Everyone told him to go and make friends with other elephants. You should be friends with elephants. Moreover, other animals also teased Gogo because he was the biggest and had a trunk. Hehehe!!! He's too big, and see he has a weird nose. Since, there were no other elephants in the jungle and other animals didn't want to make an elephant their friend. Gogo was left alone and always remained sad. He used to watch other animals playing with their friends and felt more said. He used to think, "Why can't I befriend them? Only because I am so big and have a trunk!" Gogo left going out in the jungle and spent his time just sleeping alone all the time in his house. One day while Gogo was sleeping, he saw all the animals running here and there in a rush and shouting. Gogo came out of his house to know that there is a fire in the jungle, and everyone was scared of it. Gogo quickly ran towards the river. He filled water in his trunk and ran back to the jungle. He sprinkled the water over fire and extinguished the fire. All the animals became happy and cheered for Gogo. Gogo, our hero! And, since that day nobody teased Gogo anymore. Everyone became his friend and Gogo lived happily after it.

title: War or Peace?
text: It was a cold, ruthless day. The men were draped in long robes and a thick armor was wrapped around their bodies. They were either sharpening their swords, talking to the people around them or sitting quietly by the fire, drinking a bit of rum or whiskey to keep themselves warm. General Sackings was the commanding officer, leading this troop. He knew what was coming up and also that they cannot win. He had prepared a speech which was to encourage his men, but he did not want to give them false hope with it, as even his men knew who they were facing, but he had to do it. He cleared his throat and said in his great deep voice, “Everyone by the fire, please”. Slowly, they gathered together, keeping themselves close to each other. The General took a deep sigh and started his speech. “ I know how every one of you is feeling right now and I have felt it before I was in your position, maybe 5 or 7 years ago and I was fighting the same opponent that we are fighting now, but you are more capable and better than who I was back then. You are the kind of people who have the abilities to take it to end and maybe even finish it. You guys are fighting not for anyone’s sake, but you are fighting for your families and your destinies. I want all of you to keep these two things in your minds at all times, no matter what the situation. I trust each and every one of you. This will be the hardest fight of your life and you must not underestimate or even overestimate the enemy as a matter of fact.” The General looked around and he finally saw what he wanted. There was a look of courage and fierceness on their faces and he knew that this was enough. He continued, but with his voice a bit louder, “ I want everyone here to fight for their lives, I want every one of you to give their 100% in this fight because it matters Now, let’s go and win this, shall we?”. A roar of hungry men, ready to crush everything that opposed them, was heard in every corner of the forest. It was a cold day still, but not ruthless anymore. General Sackings was leading them and when they reached the open field, they saw them. Nostalgia hit the General, but he asked his troops to remain calm even though it was a atmosphere where no one would like to stay even for a minute. The Corniat clan, the most dreadful, dangerous, wicked and powerful clan, was their enemy. About 300 men were on the field and only 100 of them were the General’s troops. He could see the intimidated faces of his men, but he could not blame them, as he had looked the same way before. He called his second in command, Brisontoe, and told him to tell everyone that they would follow the same plan as discussed. Brisontoe, who himself was scared to death barely gave a reply and walked walked away, talking to the first man in each of the 5 rows, and told them to pass on the message. The plan was that the first row would lead the attack from the front while the second row gave them back up. The third, fourth and fifth rows would attack from the sides. The plan was effective, but it may not work out against an army which was twice of theirs. Moreover, the snow would play a role in this decisive war. It would slow the movements of the warriors and had ordered his troops to attack. General Sackings did the same and the war had begun. If you had a bird’s view of this war, it would look like tiny figures were dashing into each other, but when you looked through the eyes of the men who were fighting, it was hell. You would see a dead body every now and then, some person with a murderous intent would come at you, trying the detach your head from the rest of your body. General Sackings men were greatly outnumbered, both in troops and skills. The situation was so bad that he himself had to come and fight, while he saw the other General jus looking at the war, sitting on his elephant with a half-eaten apple in his palm. Sackings felt infuriated about his situation and he fought harder. He lost count of the number of people he killed but he kept on. The others, looking at their General, got back their courage and followed him. With half of his troops dead or missing, he got back his memories from when he was fighting the same war. It too was a snowy day and they were fighting in the same land that he was fighting in now. His General, General Halking, was a coward and ordered his troops to surrender, even though he had men left who were willing to fight and risk their lives. Sackings never liked his General. Halking was a big fat man, who was given the position because his brother-in-law was the then Commander General, From that day on, he decided and promised himslef to never take a bad decision like this if he ever became General. The world was and is so corrupted, he thought as he stood looking. Why must one suffer while the other enjoys? Why only the weak lose but not the strong? Why was nature so unfair to the weak? As these thoughts ran through his mind, the battle around him was raging, even more fiercely now as both sides had lost a valuable amount of men. He didn’t like being in that battlefield. He wanted to go back home, sit by the fire in his most comfortable armchair, sip some hot chocolate and play with his kids. He wanted to do that the most, but he had to do the most difficult thing and had to face reality. Reality. That one word was the thing that he hated the most right now, even more than this losing war that they were fighting. He wanted to win, but he saw no way. He could not take in the fact that he was going to lose not only this war, but everything he had. All he saw was the doors of death welcoming him to join the rest. He tried to keep his mind in the battle, but his mind would act like child having tantrums and not listen to him and it tries to think about anything but this war. He couldn’t help but be distracted by these thoughts, and they almost killed him a couple of times by now but he kept on going. He never stopped. He couldn’t stop, because the more he thought of going back, the more he wanted to live, and so he kept on. The Corniats were starting to get afraid of Sackings, as he had killed so many of their troops alone and they looked at their General, Geromo Lancer. He merely shrugged and said, “That man is a beast. We can’t do anything about him. We just have to finish off the rest of them gain our control back in this war.” He looked at his second-in-command and said, “Get ready for another offence, we are going to crush the rest of them with this final attack.” Sackings looked at Lancer and he thought, we never met each other before but we are fighting each other for the mistakes of our ancestors. Why must this happen, that we pay for the sins of our ancestors? He looked above and saw an army raining down on him, but they were tiny, and they looked a lot like arrows. They were arrows! He tried to protect himself but got hit on his leg. He was in so much pain that he looked like Achilles when he was about to meet his end. SackingS thought his end was near. He could hear the voices of his family in his mind and he heard the voices of his children calling him “Dad” for the last time. Or so he thought.
author: Vijay

title: the story of Somilaka
text: In a certain town,there lived a weaver by the name of Somilaka. The cloth he wove was so exquisite that it was fit worn by kings. but somehow, he could only earn just enough to make two ends meet. On the other hand, the other weavers, who produced inferior clothes, had become very rich. seeing this, he told to his wife,"Look! other weavers, who produce inferior quality are becoming rich, while I, even though produce good quality, am remaining poor. His wife suggested him to go to another city. He agreed and took leave of his wife. He earned a lot and came back. On the way, he had to cross the forest. In the midway, he fell asleep. In his dream, he saw two men shouting at each other. One man shouted, "Action! why did you allow him to earn so much! " the other shouted," Destiny! how could I stop him? he is the one to decide! so why blame me!" when he woke up, he saw all his money disappeared. He thought to himself, " why lead this life? without money, we will die. suddenly, a voice told " Noooooo! I am DESTINY. I am the one who stole your money. Tell me what you want. Somilaka said, give me a lot of money. Destiny said..."But first, you have to go to two men's houses. The first one has a lot of money but doesn't use it, means a stingy person. He does not share even good food with guests. Guptadhana The other one is Upabhuktadhana. He would serve all his guests with delicious food even though he is very poor and has no money. whom do you choose to be like? asked DESTINY. At that time, Somilaka realised his mistake and said, Forgive me,I have realised my mistake. Make me like the second man that is Upabhuktadhana who was used all his money for himself as well as for everyone around even though he was not very rich. Saying so, he left and lived happily ever after.

title: The hummingbird's journey
text: Once upon a time, in a small garden full of different flowers, there was a hummingbird named Lipzy. She used to fly among the flowers peacefully and taste their nectar. One day she heard some birds saying that outside the garden there was a beautiful world to explore, with many types of flowers, shapes and colors. She made the decision to go out to see the places that the birds commented on. She came out and her eyes never got tired of seeing different types of flowers and colors that were not in her garden. She visited each of the flowers, tasted the nectar and met new friends; a butterfly and a bee. Suddenly Lipzy, without realizing it, was surprised by a snake that wanted to eat her but her speed helped her escape for a while and prevent it from biting her. Being very frightened, she didn't know what to do. So she decided to return to her garden where she was out of any danger and she valued more the importance of being in her home. Even though other places seem more beautiful, there is no place safer than home.

title: The Adventures of Lucy- The AI Dominance_chapter 4
text: Lucy felt faint with fear and surprise. “Derrin? What are you doing here?” she asked. “Exactly what do you think you are doing here?” he asked. “I- I don’t know.” She looked around to see who the others were. Two of them, she did not recognize. But she realised with horror that the others asleep there were none other than her mother, aunt and Sillinova. She immediately started coughing and rasping for air. “We’re a hundred metres below sea level. There’s not much oxygen down here,” Derrin said in a weak voice. “But why?” was all Lucy could say before she fainted from lack of the gas which kept her alive. When she woke up again, it was in the same dungeon. Her aunt, Silli and a girl who called herself Marri were awake along with Derrin. “Oh, she’s up,” Silli said unenthusiastically. Everyone was deprived of oxygen and confused. Why were they here? Derrin broke the silence all of a sudden and said, “if we’re all here, then it must mean that we have something in common. I know that Lucy and I saw the AI assistants have red eyes. Anyone else here who saw something unusual?” “Yeah, right after my call with lucy, I realised that Sarah had brown eyes and I blacked out after asking her about it,” Silli said. “My assistant Horace had a weird static voice all of a sudden and I found myself falling asleep. I hadn’t even asked him why...” Marri added. Her aunt thought for a long time before saying, “well kids, after you walked to your trancellints, my sister and I got talking and we encountered a red-eyed AI assist. Then, I don’t remember what happened.” Lucy tried to make sense of it all. Her head hurt from all the thinking, but she didn’t know what to do. She began recollecting random memories that were stored in her head until she remembered about a secret her mother had wanted to tell her when she was about five. She vaguely recollected that it had something to do with AI and she realised her mom could have the answer to all their doubts. She gently tried to shake her mom awake. But even as she tried, she could feel the warmth escaping from her mother’s skin. “Mom!” she cried as she realised that the oxygen was possibly too low for an old person. Her mom tried to breathe weakly as her eyes half opened. The others understood the gravity of the situation and tried to shake the old woman awake. The world was spinning for Lucy. She did not know why. Most of her friends hadn’t felt much emotion when their parent had died. But Lucy was overwhelmed with emotion as she sobbed. She took no notice of anything around her. The world seemed to have turned black and dark without her mother by her side. She felt her stomach twist as she heard her mother whisper, “call… call out for Mahirdan… just call… he’ll answer…” She was making no sense and lucy knew that her world was collapsing. She withdrew her hand as her mother took her last breath and looked at her knees as her tears fell to the ground. Derrin took her hands into his and looked at her, unsure of what to say. Silli gripped her shoulder and told her not to worry. How could she not? Panic gripped her insides, and she wanted to curl up and hope the ground would swallow her. Weeping at the loss of her sister, Lucy’s aunt crouched in a corner and hid her face. The sad atmosphere lasted for a minute or so, but it felt like an hour to lucy. All of a sudden, the boy who had been sleeping woke up and took in everything that was going on around him. “Woah. What happened here? Oh, my gods, did we lose the basketball match? Oh no, the huskers couldn’t have won. We’re doomed!” he looked up at the ceiling. “Please excuse my brother, he’s a bit stupid,” Marri said. “Hey! Who are you callin’ stupid? I’m Martineer the great and I shall not be called stupid!” he cried. “Shut up Mart.” “Exactly what just happened here?” Lucy could do nothing but stare at him in silence.
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: The Adventures of Lucy- The AI Domination_chapter 5
text: “That’s sad. I’m sorry- I- I didn’t realise the gravity of the situation,” Martin said. “It’s ok. Its not your fault,” Lucy said. The five were sitting in a circle, as far away as possible from the body of Lucy’s mother. “Didn’t she ask us to, like, call someone?” Marri asked. “Yeah, some Marth or something. Didn’t hear what she said.” Lucy admitted. “It was Mahirdan.” Derrin told them. “Well, we should call him. But how?” Derrin’s mother asked. “Oh, like this! Oh, Mahirdan! Oh, Mahiradaaan!” Martin said jokingly. Suddenly, the dungeon started shaking. “Not. A. Good. Idea!” Silli exclaimed. They felt themselves fall through a vortex opening up in the ground. Lucy couldn’t feel anything for a second. It felt as if she were just sitting. The she felt a great pull on her chest as she fell through the vortex. She could see her friends falling along with her. Marri had shut her eyes tightly and looked very sick. Lucy held her hand in hers and shouted over the noise, “it’s gonna be all right!” The pain and the noise stopped abruptly. Lucy found herself and her friends, cousin and aunt in the same dungeon, standing on the floor. But she saw- with horror- two of them all. She saw herself sitting on the floor, holding her mother’s hand and staring into her lifeless eyes. She saw a second Derrin shout, “NO! Stay with us!” She glanced at the Derrin standing next to her and was overcome by confusion. She saw her mother whisper something and take her last breath. Then she felt the same pain in her chest again as she felt like she had been thrown into a tornado. She opened her eyes as the pain faded and saw all her friends asleep in the dungeon- all except for her. She saw a blue light materialise and saw a holographic image of herself- slowly becoming solid and coming to rest on the ground. Lucy turned to her not-so-asleep friends and asked in confusion, “what’s going on?” Marri replied, “I think were in the past.” They stood there, trying to digest the information, when suddenly, Derrin exclaimed, “if we’re in the past, maybe we can change it! We should get my aunt to a safer place with more oxygen!” Lucy and Derrin immediately proceeded to carry the old woman, but their hands passed through her body as if she were a ghost. They saw Derrin wake up- the past Derrin- and look around in confusion. Martin yelped, “hey Derrin, can you see- or- or hear us at all?” The past Derrin gave no notice and was still looking around, trying to process what was going on. In a desperate attempt, Lucy moved forward to touch Derrin’s shoulder- but her hand just passed through his body and flickered out of vision for a moment. “I don’t think this is the past- I think these are our memories,” Lucy’s aunt said. Lucy felt a pain in her chest again and was thrown into the tornado. She found herself in the yacht at brunch his time- but not all her friends were there with her. She was alone with Derrin and her aunt, looking at herself whispering to Derrin about the AI assistants. As the memory-Lucy finished her brunch and walked to the trancellint, Lucy followed her mother, in an attempt to be closer with her at least in her memories. She and her aunt followed the memory-aunt and memory-mother as Derrin followed himself. The memory-ladies suddenly stopped and looked around as if to see if someone was looking at them. “We should tell the kids the truth soon enough…” memory-mom said. “We have another problem at hand. If you didn’t notice, the assists had red eyes,” memory-aunt replied. Lucy immediately turned to her aunt. “What’s this you haven’t told us yet?” Her aunt just looked at her memory-sister with pain in her eyes and gestured for lucy to look at them. The memory-ladies were whispering to one another as, suddenly, they turned into holographic images and disappeared. Lucy felt another sharp pain in her chest and fell back into the tornado- but no one was with her in it this time.
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: Cryptic Message
text: Matilda woke up to the sound of her alarm. An average 26- year- old woman who had to work from 8 to 9 would be exasperated at the thought of waking up this early in the morning at 5. But Matilda was different. She loved her work and wanted to spend as much time as she could in office. She got out of bed, had a quick shower and started out for work. She always reached her office by 6 and had breakfast in the canteen while reading her favourite book and today was no different. She went up to her office table to place her bag there before going down for a meal when a paper caught her eye. It was yellowing and had something handwritten on it. The paper had been placed on her table, and she stared at it for a second. She shrugged it off and went down for breakfast. She was reading a book and eating a muffin when Sandy, another enthusiastic colleague came down to the canteen. For a month now, Sandy had been following Matilda’s routine. She popped down on the same table as Matilda and started reading a book after ordering some cereal. Sandy was interrupted by Matilda saying, “heavy work nowadays, isn’t it?” Sandy casually replied affirmatively and went back to her book. Sandy and Matilda were close friends, but both knew that they couldn’t disturb the other when they were engrossed in a book. Matilda got up with a groan and walked up the stairs to her worktable. She looked at the paper on her desk again. She didn’t know why, but it sent a chill up her spine. She took it up and read it. It was a handwritten note and the person who had written it had quite an impressive handwriting. Sammy was a little boy. He had a little toy. He named the toy Wintyr. Sammy’s syster didn’t like Wynter. She thought he wos very loud and nuisy. Indeed, Wynter was noisy. He was a little monkey who would bang his drums when Sammy wound his key. Sammy liked Wynter verry much but his sister didn’t, so she decided to get rid of hem. She filled a bucket full of watern and put Wynter into the water. But eeven after that, Wynter worked. So, she took him out in the garden and beat him with the stix she found there. Wynter still worked. She was so angry that she threw him in the trash and the trash man took him away to the dump. Sammy was so sad he got a high fever and died. After his death, his sister has always been haunted by the ghost of Sammy and his toy Wynter. Moral: don’t throw toys in the trash because you hatt them. Matilda read the story and frowned. It was dark for a children’s moral story. And the person had made many spelling mistakes. Who could have kept this on her table? She shrugged it off, kept the paper in her bag and started working. Time passed and she realised she was hungry. She went down to the canteen for lunch. There, she sat on the same table as she did every day, with Sandy, Michael and Lily. Today, they were talking about their parents. “My father had been married three times before he married my mother. Each of his wives had died. His first wife couldn’t handle childbirth, the second had typhoid and the third died of lung carcinoma. His fourth wife, my mother was the only one who stayed alive. She took good care of me and my half-sister. She’s still alive but my dad died of old age,” Michael told them. “My mom was very pretty when she was my age. She got married to a family friend’s son and had me, my brother and my sister. One day, my sister went missing and my dad went in search of her. Turned out my sister had been in the back yard playing with my brother’s toy. I don’t know how, but the toy got lost and because it was my brother’s favourite he cried day and night for it, developed a high fever and died at a young age. After that, my sister would scream every night that she was being haunted by her brother, his toy and a man she didn’t know. When my dad went searching for my sister, he was gone for a long time and didn’t come back till late in the night. He’d been searching frantically and was relieved to know my sister was safe. My dad is now working here in this same company and he’s the boss in the accounts sector.” Lily said. Matilda squirmed in her seat and coughed. “Your brother’s toy, Lily. Did it have a- a name?” “Oh, yes, I think he called it summer or autumn or something.” “Weird. Was it a monkey?” “Yeah, how’d you know?” Matilda chose to not answer the question. “You know, it’s weird. My father called me to his study yesterday and told me that there was this tradition in our family where we took revenge on our rival family. He told me that was why he was late that night. I didn’t really understand anything because it doesn’t make sense, but I think his son’s death affected him mentally.” “What about your parents, Matilda?” Sandy asked. “Oh, I was an only child and, well, once when I went with my mom and dad to the grocery store when I was 5, my dad was parking the car, I was inside with my mom and- and,” Matilda started crying at that point. “Hey, its ok… what happened?” Sandy asked with an arm around Matilda. “I realised I’d forgotten my teddy in the car, and I ran back out-and I saw a man hitting my dad in the head with something, glancing at me and then- he ran away. I was too young to understand what was happening- I knew how my dad’s murderer looked but I couldn’t describe him. My mom was overcome with sorrow, but she had to keep the home running, so she got a job as a teacher.” She whispered and started sobbing. After consoling her and finishing their lunches, the other three went back to work while Matilda headed up to her boss’s office. She been promoted the day before and was in the accounts sector and this was the first time she would meet her boss. Something about Lily’s story had disturbed her and she felt as if it was connected to the message she had received through that paper and also her past. Maybe the message was a warning… she had to find out. She knocked and let herself inside her boss’s office. “Oh, hello, young lady. I understand you’ve been promoted to the accounts sector?” her boss smiled. She nodded in the affirmative and seated herself on the chair. She looked at her boss and something about the man was unsettling. He looked familiar- like a part of her past she didn’t want to explore. “So, I’m your boss now. Id like to tell you, I’m very strict. If you make even a slight mistake of matters in work- you may not wake up tomorrow.” He was being creepy and Matilda was spooked out. Something about him reminded her of her father’s death. She recounted the forbidden memory in her head again. They talked about her work and projects, and she went back to her worktable. She tried to focus on her work, but her heart wasn’t in it. She took out the yellowing piece of paper from her bag and began circling all the mistakes. She stared at it for a minute and spelled only the letters that were wrong out loud. She scribbled the letters down on the back of the paper and stared it, horrified for a second. Realisation dawned on her and she began shivering uncontrollably. She immediately went to Lily. “Lily, I need your help. After your father talks to you in your study today, can you please call me and tell me what it was about,” she asked. “That’s a strange request, but sure,” Lily agreed and looked at her as if she knew something about Matilda that she herself didn’t. Matilda couldn’t focus on her work for the entire day. The memories of her father came flooding back into her head and she kept on thinking about Lily and her father, her new boss. She went back home and waited by the phone for Lily to call. Lily called at 10:14 pm and asked Matilda to come to the same department store where she had gone at the age of 5. At 11:47 pm, Matilda Walker was found dead by a young girl of 13, shot by a gun in the heart. The detectives investigated every corner of her home and office and still found nothing. They interrogated everyone except for Lily and her father, who had mysteriously vanished and gone on vacation. Five days after Matilda’s funeral, her mother found the piece of paper in her bag and read what she had written on the back. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ y o u r e n e x t

title: Gaurdian Of the Green: Lucas's Journey
text: Chapter: 1 Guardian of the Green: Lucas’s Journey to Protect Nature In the heart of a spread-out forest, where ancient trees whispered secrets to the wind and rivers wove tales through the valleys, there lived a young man named Lucas. His days were spent wandering the lush, green expanse, a deep respect for nature etched into his very being. From a tender age, he had felt a deep connection to the land, a bond nurtured by his grandmother, who taught him the ways of the forest and its inhabitants As he grew older, he witnessed the gradual encroachment of civilization upon the wilderness he loved.. Trees fell to make way for extensive developments, rivers choked with pollution, and once-teeming wildlife retreated to the shadows. His heart ached for the loss of balance, for the disruption of harmony that he had known since childhood Chapter-2 Lucas Starts His Journey To Save The Environment Driven by a fierce determination to protect his beloved home, Lucas became a quiet yet steadfast supporter for the environment. Armed with knowledge passed down from generations and a deep respect for the natural world, he boarded on a journey to bring about change, one small act at a time. It began with organizing community clean-up efforts along the polluted riverbanks. With each bag of trash collected, he breathed life back into the waters, restoring habitats for fish and birds that had long struggled to survive. His passion inspired others to join him, and a wave of change soon spread through the town. But he knew that more was needed. He appealed to local authorities to enforce stricter regulations on logging and mining activities that threatened old-growth forests and delicate ecosystems. As seasons passed, Lucas's efforts gained momentum. He partnered with conservation organizations to establish wildlife sanctuaries and reforestation projects, transforming barren landscapes into thriving ecosystems once more. His understanding of the interconnection of all living things guided his actions, developing a harmonious balance between human development and environmental stewardship. Yet, Lucas's journey was not without challenges. There were moments of doubt and exhaustion when progress seemed indefinable when the sheer size of the task weighed heavily upon him. Chapter-3 Lucas's Legacy Continues One crisp autumn morning, as golden sunlight filtered through the canopy above, Lucas received an unexpected visitor. A young child, wide-eyed and full of wonder, approached him nervously. "Are you the hero who saves the trees?" the child asked in a voice filled with innocence and hope. Lucas knelt beside the child, a smile spreading across his weathered face. "No, young one," he replied softly, brushing a leaf from the child's hair. "The trees save us. They provide us with oxygen, clean our air, and offer homes to innumerable creatures. We must protect them, just as they protect us."
