title: The Mimic Wolf and the Goat Family
text: They always sang happily and lived happily One day, the mother goat went out, leaving the kids alone at home. The youngest goat hid and did not greet the mother because he did not want to be separated. The youngest was left alone, then waited for the mother goat to come because he felt very scared. As soon as the mother goat returned and heard that her children had been caught, she immediately brought hot water and approached the wolf. Luckily the mimic wolf had not gone far, so the mother goat was able to find it. The mother goat took advantage of the moment when the wolf was off guard, then splashed hot water on it with great courage. The mother goat managed to chase away the mimic wolf. The kids that were caught by the wolf were also successfully saved. Thanks to the brave mother goat, the kids who were saved from the wolf were very happy. They played, sang, and danced together happily. The mother goat warned her kids after they finished playing, “Don’t just believe the fake voice. You have to make sure who it is.” The youngest kid who had gone through a hard day fell asleep on the mother goat’s lap. Since that incident, the kids and the youngest became smart kids. All of that was thanks to the brave and gentle mother goat. May you also become wise people and not be easily fooled by fake news.

title: Miracles Happen
text: In the valleys of Uttarakhand was born Gagan. He lived in a slum with his parents, grandparents and an elder sister. His parents did the work of collecting garbage and with the little money they got was used to run the house. Gagan always had a dream to go to a school and study but due to his family conditions he had to sell balloons at the red light. One day at the red light while he was selling the balloons a young man probably 22 – 24 year old man came and asked him his name, about his family, and about his dream. Gagan answered all the questions. The man then said that he would take the responsibility of him to go to school. Gagan became really happy and hugged him tightly. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿The man then asked him to take him to his house. It was evening at that time and his parents had just come back tired from work. title: can electronics damage your brain
text: Too much screen time may cause physical changes to your brain. The cortex is the outer layer of the brain that processes information. During adolescence, the cortex undergoes critical development. Screen time may affect its growth. Screen time overloads the sensory system, fractures attention, and depletes mental reserves. Experts say that what's often behind explosive and aggressive behavior is poor focus. Another study found that adults who watched television for five hours or more per day had an increased risk of developing brain-related diseases like dementia, stroke, or Parkinson's. This study found that excessive screen time can hinder sleep, especially when looking at screens late at night. Some negative effects that might happen include changes in cognitive ability, problems with social or emotional skills, problems sleeping, and mental laziness. While it's not likely (or realistic) for people to forgo their phones, their are some things we can do to protect our brains from these damaging effects.

title: The Clockmaker's Apprentice
text: ﻿ In the heart of Veriden, nestled between a bakery and a bookshop, stood the quaint shop of Eldridge & Son, renowned for its masterful clocks. The shop was run by Alistair Eldridge, a skilled clockmaker known for his ability to mend not just clocks but also time itself—a secret passed down through generations. One autumn morning, a young boy named Oliver arrived at the shop, seeking purpose after losing his father. His mother suggested he apprentice with Alistair, hoping the craft would bring him solace. Alistair welcomed him warmly, sensing Oliver's earnestness. Oliver began his apprenticeship by cleaning and organizing tools. Over time, he learned the complexities of clockmaking and grew skilled in repairing various timepieces. Alistair, patient and wise, revealed to Oliver a hidden room containing a grand, ornate clock known as the Temporal Clock. “This clock,” Alistair explained, “has the power to influence time—heal wounds, alter decisions—but it comes with a cost: a bit of your own time.” Oliver was intrigued yet apprehensive. The idea of using such a power was daunting. He continued to work diligently, forming a strong bond with Alistair, who became a father figure to him. One winter evening, a young woman named Eliza visited the shop, carrying an old pocket watch that had stopped working. It belonged to her late father, and she was grieving not only his loss but also the fading memories the watch represented. Oliver took the watch, repaired it with care, and felt a pang of sympathy for Eliza’s pain. After fixing the watch, Oliver realized the power and responsibility associated with the Temporal Clock. He knew the temptation to use it for personal gain was ever-present but chose to use his skills to help others rather than alter time. One night, Alistair revealed to Oliver that he was ready to learn the true nature of the Temporal Clock. He handed Oliver an old journal containing all its secrets. “Study this well,” Alistair said. “Remember, with great power comes great responsibility.” Oliver took the journal with a sense of solemn duty. He continued to hone his craft, using the Temporal Clock’s wisdom to mend broken hearts and ease burdens where he could. Alistair eventually retired, leaving the shop and its secrets to Oliver. Under Oliver’s care, the shop thrived, and the Temporal Clock remained a symbol of the delicate balance between time, responsibility, and compassion. Oliver upheld the legacy of Eldridge & Son, ensuring that the art of clockmaking—and the mysteries of time—would endure for future generations.

That is why he destroyed all banana trees. King told Rohit that he did wrong with banana trees. King punished Rohit and ordered him to be put in jail. When princess came to know about this incidence. Princess came to king’s court and told king that he should not have put Rohit in jail. The king told princess that I put him in jail because he destroyed all the banana trees. title: The Big Event
text: Ammu's cousin, Rashi, had organized a huge event at her workplace. People from all over the world attended, representing different countries. Ammu was a bit confused. Rashi was an engineer, after all. Ammu wondered, "E ngineers supposed to only build bridges, buildings, machines, or write code for apps? Then h ow can Didi organize an event?” Rashi Didi had gotten special passes for Ammu, her little brother Appu, and their parents to attend the event. It was exciting, with lots of activities, speeches, and performances from different cultures. When they returned home that night, Ammu and Appu had many questions swirling in their heads. They couldn't wait to talk to Rashi Didi and get answers. As soon as Rashi came home that night....t hey both began prancing around Rashi and..... Didi, can we talk about the event? Of course! But how about we chat over dinner? Let me get freshened up first. “Okay, Didi!” Appu chimed in, bouncing with energy. At the dinner table, Ammu, Appu, and the rest of the family eagerly awaited Rashi. As soon as Rashi sat at the table... Didi, I thought engineers only built bridges, buildings, and machines. Do engineers also organize events? Rashi laughed at Ammu's innocence. Yes, Ammu. I am an engineer by profession, but life isn’t always about sticking to one thing we’ve learned. Sometimes, we have to step into roles or tasks we’ve never tried before. But how did you do it? Wasn’t it hard? At first, I didn’t know where to start. Organizing an event requires creativity, problem-solving, and flexibility. These skills I learned as an engineer, but I had to apply them in a new way. Wasn't it challenging for you? Yes, it was challenging, but also fun! In engineering we are taught to adapt to different situations. That helped here when I came across some difficult tasks. Because in life, opportunities come in all shapes and sizes. If you do just one thing alone, you may miss out on a lot. Trying something new helped me grow and discover talents I didn’t even know I had. Whether it’s organizing events, solving problems, or building machines, it’s all about decision-making, being flexible, and trying new stuff. Exactly! The world is changing all the time. Being willing to try new things makes us stronger. Who knows? One day, you both may find yourself doing something you never imagined, and you’ll be ready for it But, Didi, why did you take up the challenge if it was not a part of your regular office job that you must be doing? So, it’s important for us to learn new skills and be ready for anything in life, isn't it? ﻿Ammu and Appu became thoughtful. They did not have all answer but they were definitely inspired.

Be careful! said their Mother, Evelyn. We will! they said. Sam went as fast as he could but, Charlotte took the lead. They had so much fun but it was time to go back to the hotel. The Next Day, they went to a place called Niagara Falls. It was so cool to watch the water flow, It was calming too! It was considered ' One of the Tallest falls in the World.' It was so mesmerizing and breathtaking! Next Stop! Was to get Maple Syrup! The person there told that maple syrup came from the sap of maple trees. " That sounds delicious! " said Sam. " It sure looks like it too! " answered Charlotte. " Dig in everyone! " exclaimed their parents. They even ate it with pancakes and waffles! So yummy! Then they went to ice skate a bit until they went back home to USA. " We should visit again! " said Charlotte and Sam. THE END Moral of the Story: Travel to somewhere new and enjoy your time there and spend time with the people you love.
author: TANIA BENNY

title: How? Why? What is the difference?
text: “Garam, garam pakodas for everyone,” my father exclaimed as he bought the freshly made mouthwatering pakodas to the terrace, that was overflowing with muddy puddles and the sky above it was filled with roaring grey clouds. “Oh thankyou so much papa,” I replied and munched over the tasty pakodas with my mom. My father and me started singing rain songs, while my mother enjoyed the spectacular scene. When we had finished the pakodas, my father fetched us more. I was completely full & if I was to eat more my stomach would surely burst. But then my father said in an affectionate voice, “My dearest laddoo, won't you taste mouth-watering ladoos. But, no wait I will eat it". He showed the pakoda to me as an aeroplane and exclaimed, "Let's see who's going to catch the areoplane first”. IThat action made me gobbled up two more and then my father put one more saying that it was one with his love. I must say, my father is a genius. One day after, I was having the pakodas at somebody else’s house. They were made of the same ingredients and were ordered from a nearby restaurant but surprisingly I must admit that their taste was actually nothing in front of my father’s lovely pakados. How come my father’s pakodas were way much better than the ones I ate at a neighbour's house? Once my mother ordered some chaat from the restaurant as a treat. There were two pieces of tikkis and we had to mix them with all the chutnis and dahi,. For the first tikki, my mother assembled all the products and handed over to me. It tasted like I was eating the world’s best dish. However, surprisingly when I myself mixed the ingredients for the second tikki, I felt as if I was eating something homemade (I mean not very tasty) and not something made in a restaurant. How come the first tikki was better than the second one? One Thursday in lunch we had kerela (bitter gourd). Our home maid had made it and served it to us. I didn’t like it at all, it was too bitter. I felt like keeping a fast but my mother forced me to eat it. Some days later, our maid was on leave, and so my mother made it and served it to the family. Astonishingly, it turned sweet. I’m not kidding but I just mean that the bitter gourd I had on Monday were much better than the those of Thursday. How at all did this happen? Hmm... so guys, what are you thinking. Don;t you get the same experience. Well, I'm sure you must have. Isn't it time to say to your parents and God for giving you such fabulous parents a big big heartful thank you!!
author: Paraa Baranwal

title: Chik-chik Girl
text: “Amma, why do you make such delicious khichdi?” says Mona. Amma’s khichdi has carrots and tomatoes, peas and potatoes, and a few drops of homemade ghee. “Why, Mona?” Amma asks. “It’s not fair!” says Mona. “It’s too tasty, Amma. I can’t stop eating.” “Don’t complain, then, Mona! No chik-chik!” laughs Amma. “Take a little more.” “Bedtime, Mona,” says Papa. “Time to put away your storybook.” “No, please, Papa,” says Mona. “My book is so exciting.” “What’s the story about?” he asks. “Five children, and their dog. They are detectives. They are cleverer than the policeman.” “Wake up early and read,” says Papa. “It’s not fair!” grumbles Mona. “Why do people write exciting books I can’t stop reading?” Papa laughs. “Tell me, who reads books they want to stop reading?” Dadi hums a song as she massages Mona’s hair with her secret recipe of mustard oil. Sometimes Dadi’s fingers feel like she’s playing a tabla, dham-ta-dham on her head. Other times her fingers feel like raindrops. “Will my hair grow quickly, Dadi?” Mona asks. “Yes. Your hair will be soft and long.” “How long?” “Down to your knees,” says Dadi. “As long as mine.” “It’s not fair, Dadi,” says Mona. “How will my friends’ hair grow strong and long? They don’t have your magic recipe.” “‘Not fair, not fair!’ Always doing chik-chik, chik-chik!” says Dadi. Dada and Mona are walking back from the market. “Dada, it’s not fair! You walk so fast, I can’t keep up with you,” says Mona. “If you climb the trees in the back garden, go swimming, drink milk, and eat paalak, daal, and fruits…” “I will grow up big and strong, I know,” says Mona. “… you will soon walk faster than I do.” “One day my legs will be as long as yours, Dada!” says Mona. “Yes, they will.” Dada smiles and ruffles her hair. “Tee-tee-ti, teeti-ti.” Mona watches the titeeri bird sitting on a branch of the tree outside the window. “Tee-ti, tee-ti, teeti-tee-ti,” replies Mona. A koyal calls out to Mona: “Oo-ee-u, oo-ee-yo.” “Oo-ee-u, oo-ee-yo, koyal!” says Mona. “Did you know we had a koyal in our house?” Dadi asks Amma. Mona swoops around the house singing, “Oo-ee-u, oo-ee-yo, oo-ee-u, oo-ee-yo.” “Chee-chee, chew-chee, chrrr. Chee-chee, chew-chee, chrrr…” “How did so many sparrows fly into our house?” says Dada. “Whee-ta-whee-yu, whee-ta-whee-yu, whee-ta-whee-yu,” sings Mona. “The bulbul in our house sings better than the bulbul outside, doesn’t she?” says Amma. “Shh,” says Mona. “The birds will cry if they hear you. It’s not fair if I sing better than a real bulbul, is it?” “We have a chik-chik bird in our house,” says Dada, laughing. At dinner, Amma says, “Did you know, cooking tasty khichdi is not fair?” “And it’s not fair for anyone to write exciting books,” says Papa. “Or to sing as sweetly as a bird,” Amma goes on. “Or to have long hair,” says Dadi. “Or to have long legs,” says Dada, stretching his legs out under the table. “My Amma makes the best khichdi,” says Mona. “My Papa brings exciting books for me to read. My Dada has the longest legs, and my Dadi’s hair oil is a magic potion! I am the luckiest girl in the world.” “Not fair!” says Amma. “Oh, not fair!” says Papa. “That’s not fair!” says Dada. “Tch-tch, so unfair!” says Dadi with a sniff. “You are all doing chik-chik now,” says Mona. “Yes!” Amma, Papa, Dadi and Dada say together. “We are a chik-chik family!”
author: Komilla Raote

title: HIDE-AND-SEEK
text: Once upon a time, in a big jungle, many animals lived together and were happy. There was a big river flowing in the middle of the jungle, giving life to all, especially the younger ones, who enjoyed playing with each other around this river. All the animals lived in a friendly and peaceful way with each other. One day, the baby animals decided to play hide-and-seek around the river. Multiple trees, rocks, and rivulets made this spot perfect for this game. As the baby animals discussed the rules, the monkey was briefed especially as he was the naughtiest rule-breaker of all. The baby Rhinoceros started laughing at the monkey which made the chameleon angry and said, "If anyone breaks the rule today, they will be out of the game!" So the monkey joked about Rhino and said, "You are too huge to hide so you become the donner and count till we all hide!" They all busted into laughter. As everyone said yes to it, Rhino started feeling very sad! Looking at this the bear said, "Don't mind your friends, everybody will become the donner once!" After hearing this from the bear, their friendship grew stronger. Then everybody said, "Let's start the game!" The monkey decided to hide on top of the tree, as expected. Everyone started rushing towards their hiding spots. Rhino honestly counted to 20 and now decided to go out and try to find them. Some animals hid beside the rock, and some behind the trees. Rhino knew that his friends could hide in these spots, hence it was easy for him to find them all. Rhino found the snail behind the rock. He thought the monkey would hide in a tree, but the monkey was found behind the bushes. Mr. Fox became late and couldn't climb completely and Rhino already found him by touching his tail. Then Rhino set out to find the rest of his friends. But even after searching for a long time, he couldn't find some. After finding a few of his friends, Rhino is in search of the rest. All the animals are cheering and laughing, and the Deer is screaming for help to find other animals. Suddenly, a bird spots the Bear and says, "I've found the Bear!" The Rhino sees the Bear and says, "Found you! Found you!" All the friends started dancing happily after finding the Bear. They then set out to find the Frog and the chameleon. As they all kept on searching, they were shocked to see that the Frog was sleeping! When the turtle saw that the Frog was sleeping in the middle of the game, he was angry and said, "Why are you sleeping between the game?!" The Frog woke up by the loud voice and said, " I am sorry, friends. You know I have a bad habit of sleeping anytime, anywhere." And everyone burst into laughter. Even after searching for a long time, the Chameleon was nowhere to be seen. This made all the animals scared about the Chameleon's disappearance and safety. Everyone was screaming for the Chameleon, and they searched everywhere for him, but still, they couldn't find him. The Chameleon was smartly hiding near the rocks of the pond. When he heard the screams of all the animals, the chameleon was shocked and jumped out of the hiding spot. This made the Rhino spot the Chameleon and he got happy as he found all of his friends now. All the animals were happy, dancing and celebrating for finding the Chameleon. Looking at the immense fun and excitement they had, all the friends decided to play hide-and-seek tomorrow as well. But on one condition: the Frog would not sleep between the games!! And they all laughed! They promised that they would never shame each other for anything, and hence, a usual play day ended in the jungle.
author: shivani jitesh

title: The Last Train Home
text: The Last Train Home One day, I was very tired, exhausted, what ever you want to say but one thing was for sure,I really wanted to sleep. just when I laid, I slept to my dark sweat dreams. I was tired because I argued with alot of people, like alot! So I was not in the mood of talking to anyone. When I was asleep, I had a weird dream. The dream was that I was sitting on the train with all of the people of my past, and I was in a lucid dream (a dream where a person can constol its own dreams) I was sitting at the fifith choach of the train, seat number - 14794027. From the seat number only you can find out how many people where there, there where total of 647285917395038473647583927466829 choaches! Then the train driver announces,"attention please, this is to acknowledge you that the person who is sitting on seat number - 14794027, you are informed that this train is in a infinite loop and your mission is that you have to solve the arguments that you had in the past 16 years, and this is the only was you can come out of the dream. If you solve a agument, then the argument would be solved in reality as real people are dreaming with you, If you want to escape with your friends then you would have to obey my sayings, the red marked people are the people you argued with and the green marked people are people whome with you have relations, good luck! ". The seat number that he called out was me! I then thought to myself, "how would I even travel these many coaches and how would I even talk to them!? " I would feel embarrassed talking to them but I had to take a move to escape this train! So, I started, one by one, I went to the choaches I searched for people who had a red mark on them. Some people accepted my apology and some people where still angry with me, but at the end, I become friends with them too! It took ages to go through all the coaches but finally, I did it!! Then suddenly I heard a buzzer, it sounded like," weeyu weeyu weeyu " some what like this. The the driver announces," Great job Md. Tauhiduzzama, you officially sorted out all the problems in your life! Now the train is moving to the right track because of you! now you can go... " after that the train moved to another direction, and then slowly the dream faded away. When I woke up, everything was normal, it was daytime, birds singing and the sun shing. when I went to my friend 's house, with whom I fighted with, he was happy to see me and then we played video games together. Then I thought, maybe apology is something that is not about embarrassment, It is about repairing relations that could not be fixed....
author: Md.Tauhid uzzama

title: Sharing is Caring
text: Meena is a little girl who was getting ready to school. Meena's amma had made tasty dosa for her and Kutty, her brother. Meena was so happy to eat it! But they were not the only one. Meena's cousins, who came from town also wanted to eat the Dosa. Meena refused to share. They were sad and told Meena "You are not sharing!" Meena was confused, but somehow ate her breakfast, and left for school, with Kutty. Meena was a brilliant student. She got good marks in her studies. At school, Meena sat with her teacher to arrange the answer sheets. She asked her teacher "Miss, what is sharing?" Her teacher said, "Sharing is caring." Meena and Kutty came back home just in time before the rain. Meena's mother called her, while Kutty went to do his homework. Diwali had begun, and Meena's amma was putting the rangoli. Meena asked her amma, Amma, what is sharing? "Sharing is giving what you have, to others who need it. Now, go share your time with Kutty, who needs help. Meena came to see Kutty. He was not able to finish his homework, so Meena helped him. He was so happy and hugged his sister. With Meena's help, Kutty was able to finish his homework fast and help his amma make polis (sweet chapatis) for their thatha. Meena and Kutty helped amma in decorating the house for Diwali. They went to their thatha's house after that. Meena and Kutty had a good time with thatha. Thatha was telling them stories, while she asked him the question, Sharing is Caring because you help someone by giving them something that they need. Thatha, why Sharing is Caring? Thatha was so happy seeing the kids, and shared the hot, sweet polis with them. Meena called her cousin and shared the polis with him and Kutty. The kids were happy. Diwali is all about Sharing. Always give what you have, to someone who needs it. Because "Sharing is Caring"
author: Lakshmi Supriya

title: Marvel Avengers: - Falcon the Captain America
text: (Note: - Continuation of my series of stories The Marvel Avenges. Before reading, Read my 1st story - Marvel Avengers: - Age of Space) The Avengers were having a very great time after defeating Naruto. But these celebrations are short lived, a problem will them. Shang Chi, a powerful Mandarin warrior from Macau. He was sent by his father to conquer the world and make everyone his slave. As usual, the Avengers were stopping him. So, he made a wonderful master plan. According to the plan, when the Avengers were sleeping, Shang Chi's army kidnapped them. But Sam Wilson (Falcon) was not there. He immediately found out that everyone was kidnapped and immediately called Steve Rogers for help. But Steve Rogers didn't return from his mission forever. The committee was left with no option other than to appoint Sam Wilson as the new Captain America, and Sam was compelled to accept the role. Sam immediately flew to Macau and found the Avengers. Then he freed everyone and started to fight with Shang Chi. Shang Chi used his rings to injure Hawkeye, Spiderman, Deadpool, and Bucky Barnes. But Sam used his Vibranium shield and broke Shang Chi's rings. And Shang Chi was instantly defeated and got assassinated.
author: Kotni Srinivas

title: Red Raincoat
text: I wear it now?" Manu asked. "No, honey, the sky is clear now," Mom replied.. Monday the weather was bright and sunny. “WILL it rain today, Mom?” asked Manu. “No Manu, not today. If you wear your raincoat, you will look very strange!” replied Mom. On Tuesday, the sky was blue. “Mom, WHEN will my wish come true?” Manu asked. “Not today, honey, there is only one white cloud in the sky!” Mom said. Wednesday was hot. “Mom, WHY hasn’t it rained yet?” Manu asked. “Son, I think it’s going to rain soon. Maybe even before noon,” Mom said. On Thursday Manu went on a picnic. “Mom, WHAT if it rains? Should I bring a raincoat?” Manu asked. “No honey, it won’t rain today. Those little white clouds are too high Friday was cloudy. “Mom, will it rain today?” Manu asked loudly. “Maybe, honey. There are some dark clouds hanging in the sky,” Mom replied. Saturday started with a thunderous sound! Bang! “Mom, is that thunder I heard? Will it rain soon?” Manu asked. Then finally, the rain came! “Oh, the rain is coming, the rain is coming,” Manu sang as he ran outside. “But Manu,” called his mother as she chased after him, “You forgot your raincoat!”
author: Zahra  Nayla

title: English of majhe mitre
text: I have many friends Some of my friends are big and... And some are small Some of my friends are old, And... some are small babies. I have many friends who are animals And some don't have legs. title: It is time to play
text: He has a round body like a drum. Chhotu is a small rabbit. He looks like a cotton ball. They play together. One day, Golu said "let's try a new game today." Sit down! I will jump on your back in one bound," said Chhotu. Golu sat down. Chhotu jumped with all his might. Thud! He landed on Golu's back. Golu laughed and said, "Now it's my turn. You sit down and I'll jump on your back. You?" "Yes. Me." "How?" asked Chhotu. "Like this!" Golu said while jumping. Thump...thump...thump...some coconuts fell on Golu's head. Because of fear, Golu ran with his big legs. A small coconut fell on Chhotu. I am lucky. It would be better for a coconut to hit my head than an elephant,” Chhotu thought.
author: Andita Keysa

title: Grandma Glasses
text: I put them?" Grandma always asked. Without her glasses, she couldn't find them. So, Grandma needs me. To be her eyes, to find her own glasses! Sometimes Grandma's glasses are in the bathroom. Or on the bed. Or even on top of her head. "Grandma," I called, "they're on top of your head!" "Of course! How silly of me. Thank you, Richa dear," Grandma said with a chuckle. However, this time I couldn't find Grandma's glasses. Not yet. I've been looking for her everywhere. In all the unusual places. On top of Grandmother's head, in the bathroom, in her closet and on top of the puja shelf. I've looked under Grandmother's favorite chair and on the dining table. Nothing. Her glasses weren't there. I wonder where Grandmother's glasses are? Then I'll be a good detective. I'll find out what Grandmother did all day. "Grandma didn't do much today. Only Veena's in-laws came. She loves to gossip! We drank cups of tea. And she spent Raju said, "Grandma is very busy today. She wrote a letter to the Chief Minister about her retirement." Mom said, "Grandma chatted with your aunt for a long time. Then, she knitted a sweatshirt for Raju and went for a walk." I now had many clues. I quickly looked for Grandma's glasses in new places in the house. Aha! I had found the missing glasses! Her glasses were wrapped in woolen thread, near the pen, under the phone, on the table. On top of that, I also found a laddoo that was half gone. For Grandma's next birthday, I'll save up to buy extra glasses!
author: elsa fara

title: grab attention
text: an attention-grabber helps get your audience interested in what you have to say. It's a way to stand out, create a positive first impression, and motivate people to keep engaging with your content. A strong attention-getter sets the tone and lays the groundwork for a memorable message. The drawing that grabbed my attention and stopped me looked different. Over the coming four weeks, rugby league has an opportunity to grab national attention. to cause one to become interested in something. The book's title grabbed/caught my attention and I picked the book up. 7 scientifically proven ways to capture someone's attention Automaticity: Activate the senses.... Framing: Contextualize your argument to appeal to your audience.... Disruption: Break expectations.... Reward: Create desire.... Reputation: Establish credibility.... Mystery: Leave things incomplete. Text Messages to Make Him Obsess Over You Something about you just makes me feel so alive.... You have this way of making everything else seem unimportant.... You're like my favorite song — I just can't get you out of my head.... I just turned down a night out.... You have no idea how much I'm looking forward to seeing you.
author: Darsh Kumar

title: I would have liked it if...
text: I like many things. But Aai doesn’t like some of them. Sometimes Baba does not like some of them. Or nobody likes anything— Aai, Baba, Aajoba or Aaji! See, Aai doesn’t like flowers. I would have liked it if she did. But… “Megh, are you going to go to school wearing this?” says Aai. “Yes,” I reply. “It will be OK. My teacher will not shout at me. Sayali always comes to school with flowers in her hair.” Sometimes it gets very boring at Aaji and Aajoba’s place. Aajoba always wants to play cards. But it is not fun. I would have liked to play with Cookie. But… "Nooo! Aaji, hold Cookie!" “Don’t be scared, sona,” says Aajoba. “He will not do anything.” Okay, forget about Cookie. I would have really liked it if Aaji let me eat anything I want. But… “Aaji, I am hungry. I want to eat something small. Something gooey. Maybe something chocolate-coloured.” “Hmm, shall I give you some dates?” says Aaji. What if every day were Diwali? I would have really loved it! But… “Spinach? Aai, please make shrikhand with chapatis?” “Shrikhand–chapati!” says Aai. “Every day is not Diwali.” I would have loved to sleep alone in my own room. In fact, Baba would have loved it even more. Actually, no. This is so much better.
author: Radhika Shenoy

title: Ananya's Family Tree
text: “Quickly, beta!” Mumma’s voice chimed, “We must leave now to make it on time!” Ananya’s heart fluttered, a special day ahead, Ready for the big wedding, excitement widespread! Ananya hand-knit garlands late last night, Perfect in her eyes, each the same size. With her many garlands, Ananya rushed to the door, Meeting her family, a great adventure in store! Upon arrival, what a lively view, So many familiar faces to give garlands to! “The whole family’s here!” Mumma said with cheer, “Let’s greet them with your garlands, my dear!” “Ananya, look who’s here!” Mumma’s voice near, Aunty Asha from Mumbai, spreading cheer. With Sarah, the love of her life, by her side, Love always wins, far and wide. “Say hi to our pets!” Sarah said with glee. “The cutest babies on our family tree! A dog, a cat, and a little birdie, too.” Oh, what a joyful crew! Ananya tried, “Here’s a garland, hand-knit.” Aunty Asha sighed, “Oops, too heavy, Not a perfect fit!” Mumma introduced cousin Korou, “He’s new to our lives, Adopted by Arjun Mama and his loving wife. With varied tastes and tales to share, This family’s charm fills the air. Ananya tried again, “Here’s a garland, hand-knit.” Korou sneezed, “Oops, my allergies! Not a perfect fit!” Nana and Nani entered from the side, With methai in hand, their smiles oh-so-wide! They caught Ananya in a warm embrace, Across generations, love leaves its trace. Ananya cried, “Here’s a garland, hand-knit.” Nana groaned, “Oops, too itchy, Not a perfect fit!” Ananya looked to Mumma with teary eyes, Alone, Mumma had ensured Ananya lived king size! “Mumma, this garland is for you, hand-knit,” Mumma replied, “Oops, too small, not a perfect fit! “Why don’t they fit?” Ananya’s sadness grew. She sat alone in a corner, feeling quite blue. Aunty Asha and Sarah noticed, they saw it all along. They approached Ananya, their voices gentle and strong. “My dear, everyone’s unique, you see, Our differences make us a beautiful family. Each individual’s special, with their own design. So, let’s remake each garland with each soul in mind.” With not a single second to spare, They sat together, knitting flowers with care. Soon enough, they gathered everyone in their sight, and handed out new garlands, before the wedding rites. Together they stood, each garland a sign, Of a family united, through space and time. Despite their differences, they’ll all agree, They’re entwined by love, Ananya’s family tree! Do you remember everyone in Ananya’s Family? Families come in all shapes and sizes! Uma Nani Amar Nana Freya Arjun Mama Korou Arpita (Mumma) Ananya Yusuf Aditi Mausi Aunty Asha Sarah Mishka Tara Tweety This story is originally published as part of Tales For Tweens: A Compilation of Award-winning Progressive Short Stories for Young Indians.

title: The School Project
text: Meet Suhana, a bright-eyed 7-year-old from Delhi, India. She lived in a vibrant neighborhood surrounded by people from different cultures, religions, backgrounds and ethnicities. One day, Suhana's teacher, Miss Vaishali, assigned a project to celebrate the diversity of their community. Suhana was excited to share her own traditions and learn about others. She started by asking her family members about their favorite festivals and customs. Her mother shared stories of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, while her father taught her about Holi, and her grandmother explained Eid-ul-Fitr, the Muslim celebration of Ramadan's end. Suhana's curiosity led her to visit her neighbors, who shared their own traditions. She learned about Christmas from her Christian friend, Iyana, and the Jewish festival of Hanukkah from her friend, Aaron. As Suhana collected stories and customs, she realized that despite their differences, they all shared a common thread - the spirit of love, kindness, and togetherness. Suhana called all her friends home that day and they all together created a beautiful collage representing the diverse traditions they learned about. They titled it "Unity in Diversity" and presented it to their class. Miss Vaishali was very proud of Suhana's project and encouraged the class to celebrate their differences together. From then on, Suhana's school organized cultural events, where everyone shared their traditions, food, and music. Suhana's project taught her that diversity is what makes their community strong and beautiful. She learned to appreciate and respect differences, and her friends became like a rainbow of colors, each one unique and valuable. Suhana's story was published in her school magazine and it was also spread throughout the city, inspiring others to embrace unity in diversity. She became known as the "Little Ambassador of Unity," reminding everyone that together, they can create a vibrancy of love and acceptance.

title: The Hidden treasure
text: Once upon a time, there lived a pirate named Captain Finn. He was not a typical fearsome pirate; instead of being known for his ruthless raids or frightening crew, he had a gentle heart and a love for adventure that burned brighter than the sun. He sailed through endless blue oceans in search of treasure but didn’t seek gold coins or sparkling jewels. Finn believed that true treasure lay in friendships, stories, and unforgettable experiences gathered along the way. His journey was one of excitement and discovery, where every port he visited brought new friends into his life. These friendships were more than just connections; they were filled with laughter, shared stories, and unforgettable moments that brightened his days at sea. Each encounter painted a vivid picture in his heart, reminding him of the beauty of companionship. As he carefully unrolled it, promising images of unimaginable wealth danced before his eyes. However, along with the thrill came a nagging feeling of worry. What would this treasure truly cost? As waves crashed against his boat, Finn began to reflect on what made life worthwhile. Was it really about chasing after glittering riches, or was it found in the warmth of sharing stories with friends around a crackling campfire? With each thought, he felt torn between adventure and the comfort of meaningful relationships. Ultimately, Finn chose to follow the map—not solely for the allure of gold and jewels but for the experiences waiting ahead. On his quest, he discovered physical treasures and deeper truths about life. He realised that true fortune lies in the bonds we form with others and the cherished memories created together. In a world often obsessed with material gain, Captain Finn unearthed a precious lesson: the hidden treasures of life are often found within our hearts and connections to those we love. title: The Adventure of Benny the Brave Bunny
text: Once upon a time, in a peaceful meadow, there lived a little bunny named Benny. Benny was a curious bunny with soft white fur and big floppy ears. He loved to hop around the meadow, chasing butterflies and smelling the colorful flowers. But more than anything, Benny dreamed of having a big adventure, just like the ones he had heard in stories. “Maybe one day, I’ll be a brave hero!” he thought, looking out at the tall mountains far beyond the meadow. One sunny morning, Benny heard a strange sound coming from the woods nearby. It was a soft rustling, as if someone was calling for help. Benny’s heart began to race. "Could this be my adventure?" he wondered. Without thinking twice, Benny hopped toward the sound. Through the trees, he spotted a small bird stuck in a thorny bush. The bird’s wings were tangled in the sharp branches, and it looked frightened. “Oh no!” said Benny. “Don’t worry, I’ll help you!” Benny gently nibbled on the branches, carefully freeing the little bird’s wings. “There you go!” said Benny proudly. The bird flapped its wings and flew up into the sky, circling around Benny. “Thank you! You’re so brave!” chirped the bird. Benny blushed. “It was nothing. But be careful next time!” he called. The bird flew off, leaving Benny feeling proud of himself. He had helped someone! But little did Benny know, this was just the beginning of his adventure. As Benny continued through the woods, he found a shiny, golden key lying on the ground. It sparkled in the sunlight. “I wonder what this key opens?” Benny asked himself, picking it up. Suddenly, a voice from behind startled him. “That’s the key to the enchanted garden!” said a wise old turtle slowly walking up to Benny. The turtle wore a tiny pair of glasses and had a long beard. “I’ve been looking for that key for ages. The garden is hidden deep in the forest, and only the bravest can find it.” Benny’s eyes widened with excitement. “Can I find it?” he asked. The turtle nodded. “You’ll need to follow the sparkling trail, but beware of the tricky fox who guards the entrance,” warned the turtle. Benny, full of courage, held the key tightly and set off to find the enchanted garden. As Benny hopped deeper into the woods, he saw a trail of sparkles on the ground, just like the turtle had said. He followed the twinkling path until he reached a tall, thick bush covered in vines. But there, sitting in front of it, was a sly-looking fox. Hello, little bunny,” said the fox with a smirk. “If you want to pass, you must answer my riddle!” Benny gulped. He wasn’t sure if he could answer a tricky riddle, but he knew he had to try. “Okay, I’ll do my best,” said Benny bravely. The fox smiled. “Here’s the riddle: What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up, up it goes, and yet never grows?” Benny thought hard. He had heard this riddle before in one of his storybooks! Then, with a smile, he answered, “A mountain!” The fox's eyes widened in surprise. “You’re right! You may pass,” said the fox, stepping aside. Benny hopped through the bush and found himself in the most beautiful garden he had ever seen. Flowers of every color filled the air with sweet scents, and a sparkling fountain bubbled in the center. Benny held up the golden key and unlocked a tiny gate at the far end of the garden. Inside, he found a treasure chest filled with glowing stars! “You are truly brave, Benny,” a voice said. It was the turtle again, smiling at him. Benny realized that being brave wasn’t just about having an adventure, but also about helping others, solving problems, and never giving up. From that day on, Benny was known as Benny the Brave Bunny, the hero of the meadow.

title: Digital data and information: Always be prudent while handling them
text: In the modern world, which is indeed a 'small village', electronic devices and internet have become an indispensable part of our lives. This means that without these facilities, it has become impossible to live because we have become highly dependent on them. After the 3 basic necessities i.e. food, clothing and shelter, internet has become his fourth necessity. Let us now learn how and why internet communication is essential. Computers have become a part of human body. Wherever we are, whatever we do, computers have impacted us. Nowadays, even rising technologies such as big data, artificial intelligence, IoT (Internet of Things) and WoT (Web of things) have become very popular and becoming easily adaptable to our daily lifestyle. But every technology has its own pros and cons. Let us understand this with the help of a simple example. Disadvantages of unregulated cyber usage 1. VIRUS Anny once received a laptop as a gift from her loved one. She was excited about its amazing features. She would never leave any stone unturned while surfing the web - browsers, installing software and apps, downloading or uploading attachments on e - mails, creating audios and videos, messaging etc. One day, as usual, when she tried to turn on her computer, it did not respond to her command. She got worried. What do you think was the main reason? Just as a human body is affected by a microbe called virus when lack of precaution is taken, even computers have their own limit and precautions should be taken while using them. The full form of a computer virus is 'Vital information and resource under seize.' It is a program or a set of instructions given to a software to hamper and damage the functions of an operating system (OS) such as Windows, Mac. Inc, Ubuntu, Linux etc. Each operating system has its own VIRUS program that affects it. VIRUS harms your computer in the following ways: 1) Abruptly stops your system's booting 2) Steals all your personal and significant data 3) Leads to abuse, bank frauds and sometimes permanent damage of your computer system if not addressed immediately. Sources and causes of VIRUS: Hacking is the main cause of VIRUS. They are of 2 types. a) Ethical Hacking This type of hacking is done for the welfare of other devices, individuals and companies. If you receive an SMS or a mail from your registered favourite websites, it is called Ethical Hacking. b) Unethical Hacking This type of hacking is done to corrupt the data, steal it and commit crimes in turn harming victims. Bank frauds, digital data breach, cyber friendship are different forms of Unethical Hacking. Effects of a computer VIRUS: a) Cyber bullying and ransomware Due to a malicious or a malware program of VIRUS, it results in breaching of all your apps, your favourite photos and videos. To recover all that data, you are demanded a ransom amount of money. b) Damage of computer system Computers get damaged when VIRUS gets installed in your computer thus corrupting you hard disk and other secondary devices such as Pen drive, CD etc. ﻿ How can we combat VIRUSES on our computer? 1. We should always install an anti virus software on our computer before surfing any web browser. 2. Always avoid browsing malicious or unsafe websites and social media. The best indication of the safety of a website is the pad lock symbol displaced at the last left corner of the browser homepage. 3. Do not download any unknown attachments from unknown sources in electronic mails.

title: The Bird's Home
text: I watched through the window. A bird arrived. I don't know where it came from. I don't know how it chose that branch. It had grass in its mouth that it knotted and sewn. After that it flew away, and kept on coming back with another grass or a leaf. It did not matter how the weather was. It did not have hands. It used its hands and feet to carry and work. It did not carry the load on its head. It did not carry it on its shoulder. It did not hire a truck or a donkey cart. It did not hire a horse or cattle cart. One day I saw it pampered and looking beautiful. It was happy, and testing its fluffy and comfortable home. It was clear that it has finished making it. Soon the house had eggs laid. The uncle came and cleaned the yard. I cried and stopped him when he wanted to chop the tree, and chop the branch. One morning the nest had lovely chicks. The melody that came there was delightful. I watched the bird bringing food, and feeding them. Oh, the way young ones opened their mouth!

title: Drawings neither Fly nor Dance
text: Ritu was a small girl, who studied in a big school in a big city. Ritu, like every other child wanted to learn, but couldn't because whenever she tried, numbers flied in air and words danced. Sometimes she zoned out and sometimes she suddenly started laughing in class. None of her teacher liked her, and scolded her all the time. Teachers also complained about Ritu to her parents and they also scolded her. Ritu now found school a scary place. But, one day suddenly something happened and Ritu found school a nice place since then. One day, Ritu's teacher took their class to the library and asked them to read whatever they want. Ritu picked many books but couldn't read because words started dancing. She became sad and disappointed. Bimal was sitting next to Ritu, and he was reading a picture book. Ritu observed that there were very less words in that book and even if they were dancing, she could still understand the story. Ritu took the book from Bimal and started reading. She read each page carefully and got lost in the pictures, forgetting the world around her. When she finished the book, she got up and screamed, "Wow! What a story. I want to read more books like this." She went home and told her parents that she enjoyed reading the picture book. Her father got her many picture books the next day. Library became Ritu's favorite place in school. Now, she read picture books whole day. Ritu fell in love with picture books and even started making drawings herself. She drew something daily and narrated the story her drawing told to her parents and friends. Time passed and Ritu is now older. But, she still reads a lot of picture books. And, the most important thing. Ritu now creates similar books she grew up reading. She is a children's book illustrator and draws beautiful drawings for picture books for children.

title: Exam: A humorous satire
text: One who has never faced any test is not worthy of comparison. Today here I am going to talk about a form of examination that I myself face nowadays, and have been doing since childhood. This moment comes in every student's life, it comes and goes. It has to be faced from the age of four. ﻿ ﻿ This time is very difficult. At this time I start to fear books. Think for yourself, what will happen to you if you are surrounded by so many papers and so many words? The depth of examination is felt not only by the student, but also by his parents (rather they feel it more). Papers children have to write, and parents sleep less, rest is taken care of. More numbers are expected. 1) Magu: They are hard working and very quick minded, parents are very happy with them and they get a lot of praise. They come first in every exam, but lag behind in the real life test. Books and their companionship remain for a long time. A complete life rests on education.They cannot be resisted. They are very strange creatures. Industrious: His face always looks nervous, Parents can't say anything after seeing them. At the time of exam, there are many questions in their mind. There is no special attachment to books, but they make friends with books. They work hard but when they don't get the marks, they get drowned in the sea of despair. Mast: This creature keeps the anxiety miles away during the exam, reads a book for one hour and wanders around the market for the remaining three hours. They are not fond of books, but their mind is so much that they can get good results in the exam just by looking at the book. The most amazing are their parents, as they are also known as strays. God is thanked for the results of their examination. Slow: Now what about them, everything they do is done slowly. The love of parents is always with them. Things take a while to make sense. They comfortably spend a couple of years at one level. And feel every joy of life. There are many more species that are being researched There are different ways of studying. For example, I like to hold a book and talk to my friend. There are some who fall asleep after reading a book.Or he starts to feel unwell, otherwise he misses a very important task. There are many who do not digest food without reading the book, and the digestion is not completed (these are found in the Mugu caste). These exams are boring. We cannot ignore them, it is a fact of student life that cannot be ignored. Due to increasing competition in this world, this reality will have to be implemented. While studying some time ago, Dil wanted to write something, and this is the result. "Why don't I understand anything, the words seem like black shadows. My friend sat by my side, eyes deep in his book, Did he read so much? I cried, hey hey."
author: Adiba Syed

title: Aalepak for Tatya
text: It is always fun when he visits us. That night, Tatya and Baba cooked dinner together. Aai got a break. She and I watched a movie. After dinner, the three of them sat and talked. Aai and Baba enjoy listening to Tatya. At dawn, Baba left to milk the buffaloes. Tatya woke up late. We went with Aai to see the calf. Seeing the vest Baba was wearing, Tatya said,“I want that!” “No need to take mine,” Baba said. “We will buy you a new one.” We all went to the town market to buy a new vest for Tatya. I sat in the front seat of his car and played songs. The market was crowded and full of colours. Baba led the way towards a clothes shop. What a grand time I was having. At the shop, we looked at different vests for Tatya. But Tatya couldn’t fit into any of them! “Show us a bigger one, please,” Baba asked the shopkeeper. Tatya fit into the bigger vest. He bought four of them. Then he saw some striped underpants. “Give me those, too,” Tatya said. He spotted some thick blankets. “I’ll take those, too,” Tatya said. When we left home, Tatya was supposed to buy one vest. But once we reached the market, he bought so many more things! Would such a tiny Nano have room for all the things he bought? Phew! Tatya managed to fit everything in his car. Just then, a man passed by shouting, “Aalepak!” “What is aalepak?” I asked Baba. “It is ginger barfi,” Baba said. “It is made with ginger, sugar and cardamom.” “It is delicious,” Tatya said. “Do you want some?” Aai asked me. And she put a ten-r upee note in my pocket. paak le Aaa I ran towards the aalepak-seller. “How much is it for?” “Five rupees!” “Give me one, please,” I said. Walking back to Aai, I read the words written on the packet: ‘Great for journeys’. So I ran back to the aalepak-seller. I bought another piece of aalepak with the rest of the money. Tatya was waiting for me. I gave him one piece of aalepak and said, “Tatya, have a great journey back!” Tatya was delighted. “Thank you, Chingi. There is just enough room in my Nano for this aalepak.” And with the piece of aalepak, Shakil Tatya started his great journey back home.
author: Shreeja Rao

title: the story of the donkey with a tiger's skin
text: In an unknown city, there was a donkey. He had a master who was a washer man. One day, they came across a dead tiger's skin. The master thought, "If I could make the donkey wear the skin, he would be strong enough to create an emotional fear that this donkey would kill them. So, he made the donkey wear the tiger 's skin. He was overjoyed. He thought, " Now, I am going to earn more money." One day, his donkey, went into the garden and was eating everything happily. Whenever anybody came out, they would get scared by the so-called tiger. One night, when the gardeners went to sleep, the donkey happily brayed loudly, and the gardeners realised that the "tiger" was just a normal donkey and killed the donkey with sticks.

title: The Three Monkeys And Their Special Rules
text: Once upon a time there were three cute monkeys called Mikuu, Tikku and Rikku. They were best friends and lived in a big jungle where everyone was always busy. These monkeys had a special rule that they followed every day. Why do you think they followed the rule? One day Mikkuu, the first monkey, decided that she would never look at anything bad. "I don’t like to see anything bad that makes me sad or scared!" she said. That's why she always wore big sunglasses when she walked around in the jungle. "The world is full of beautiful things!" she cheered. What would you wear if you didn’t want to see bad things? The second monkey, Tikku, always covered his ears when someone said something nasty. "Only nice words I want to hear," he said to his friends. "I feel so happy when I hear nice things!" That's why he carried colorful earplugs with him everywhere. "The world sounds better with good words," he laughed. Can you think of a kind word you like to hear? And Tikku, the third monkey, promised himself that he never say nasty words. "I will only speak good words because words can hurt," she explained. So, she always thought before speaking and smiled whenever she talked. "The world is better when we speak kindly!" she said happily. What’s a kind thing you can say to someone today? Well, these monkeys traveled all over the world. They visited big cities with tall buildings, quiet villages with small houses and even places with snow-capped mountains. Wherever they went, they passed on their secret: See No Evil, Hear No Evil, Speak No Evil. Everywhere people began to follow the monkeys’ rule. Do you think people can really follow the monkeys' rule? Why or why not?
author: Poonam Singh

title: An Innocent Boy
text: "When I was in 1st class, I saw him. I thought he was very innocent. If you want to learn how to become a thief, learn from him. One day, I brought my new eraser to school. When I turned back to get a book, he stole my eraser. When I turned around again, I saw that my eraser was missing." "Then I got scared and told my teacher. Suddenly, my teacher said, 'Give his the eraser back.' I was confused, wondering if he had seen him stealing or not. Then I saw my 'robber' friend, Likhithan." "But he is very innocent because everyone beats him without any reason, yet he stays quiet and doesn't tell the teachers. He lives with his sister because their parents are busy with their jobs." "When I was in 5th grade, it was our games period. I was playing with my friends when he came up to me and disturbed my game. Afterward, he would run away. But I felt sorry for him because he had no friends." "When he saw me, he thought I was his best friend. When I realized this, I started sitting with him, and our bond became like that of brothers. But in 6th grade, he got transferred. I asked his neighbor, and they told me he had been transferred." Then I got very upset. I wondered why he didn’t tell me that he was transferred. Then I realized that if he had told me, I would have cried and tried to stop him from going. That’s why he didn’t tell me about the transfer. This is a true story, and it happened to my friend.

She hops on one leg and does all her chores. Hop Hop Hop. One-legged myna explores. Mira, the myna is happy. She loves singing, laughing and flying high above the clouds. Hop Hop Hop. title: Mosquitoes Love Buzzing in Ears
text: Once upon a time, there was a kingdom of mosquitoes. This kingdom was known for its great wealth. The soldiers were very brave, and the knights were very noble. The Queen was very fashionable, her clothes sparkled, and she wore beautiful golden bracelets and earrings, which made her look very majestic. One quiet night, a human sneaked the mosquito kingdom. Unfortunately, the guards on duty were fall asleep. The thief saw his chance and quietly entered the Queen's chamber, were she was sound asleep. He crept closer to the Queen and reached for one of her golden earrings. ﻿ Just as he snatched one, the Queen suddenly woke up began to scream, "Help! Help! Help!" The thief was startled and ran away holding the stolen earring. The guards woke up immediately, but they could not catch him. ﻿ The next day, Queen gathered her soldiers and her people. "All mosquitoes must search for my stollen earring. Check every ear!" she commanded. From that day on, all the mosquitoes searched for the missing earring. Even today, they still look for it, checking every person's ear while buzzing, "Earring! Earring! Earring!".

title: Dive.
text: We set off in a small boat, expecting a BIG adventure! When we arrive at the dive site, we carefully checked all the equipment and put on our fins and masks. Once in the water, we greeted by a group of yellow back fish. ﻿What a variety of creatures can be seen around this large coral reef: oriental sweetlips, parrotfish, batfish, and beautifully patterned sea snail. To learn more about the creatures marked in bold lettering, turn to the back of thee book. The trumpet fish change color to blend with the group of yellow tangs, but surely you can spot it easily, right? We should keep our distance with lionfish. The spines on his back are quite poisonous! This clownfish guarded their sea anemone home carefully, but they agreed to let me take some pictures. ﻿ We saw a honeycomb moray eel having its teeth cleaned by 2 cleaner fish, and a pair of other fish even rubbed our hands! There also triggerfish and sea urchins. We even saw coral groupers and coral octopus playing hide and seek. The octopus won the game. They are good at hiding. The pipefish are too. Can you spot two pipefish in this picture? We met a pair of reef sharks resting near the ocean floor. They are not dangerous, so we swam closer to get a better look. We followed ﻿hawksbill turtle that was searching sea sponges around the reefs for his lunch. On our way back to the boat, we were surprised by manta ray "flying" through the water with 2 remora fish swimming behind it. And just we thought this diving couldn't be any better, we saw a dugong grazing on a sea grass. What an amazing experience! I can't wait to dive again! Coral are both plants and animals. Thousand of tiny algae live inside the corals, and providing the with energy to grow. Coral have hard outer and grow in various shape. Plankton is the main food source for many sea creatures. Plankton is a mix algae, bacteria, tiny animals, and their eggs, also larvae of larger animals that float with ocean currents. Feather stars may look like plant, but but actually they are animal, Feather stars use their feather-like arms to catch and eat floating plankton. Parrotfish have strong teeth shaped like a parrot's beak, which they use to scrap algae from hard coral. Some species even eat the coral little bit, and they later poop out a fine sand that get washed ashore and form beautiful white beaches. Clown fish and sea anemone live together and help each other. Clownfish help clean the anemone tentacle's and luring the other fish for the anemone to eat. Then the anemone allow clownfish to hide among their tentacles without stinging them. Cleaner fish are small fish that keep the larger fish clean by eating parasites and dead skin off their bodies. The larger fish recognize cleaner fish by their color and the way they move. Coral octopus can hide by changing their color and texture. Coral octopus can make their homes in hole in the coral reef or burry themselves in the sand. Pipefish can be found in pairs, swimming with their heads down and hiding among seagrass, coral, feather stars. Like coral octopus, pipefish can change their color to blend in perfectly. White-tip reef sharks have a thin body, a wide head, and white spots on their dorsal and caudal fins. T hey hunt at night and sleep throughout the day. Hawksbill turtles have a flattened body, a serrated shell, and a sharp, curved mouth that look like hawk's beak Manta rays are large fish with wing-like fins on either side of their bodies. These wide fins help manta rays swim quickly through the water. From tip to tip, the wingspan of some manta rays can reach up to seven meters! Dugongs is a herbivore mammals. Their favorite food is seagrass, which they can chew with their distinctive snouts. Dugongs are also often referred to as sea cows.
author: Friska Alan

title: How Far is Far?
text: Kanyakumari is about 4 times this distance, or 4 x 1,000,000 m, which equals 4,000,000 m. Because saying “4,000,000 m” is a bit of a mouthful, we usually just say 4000 km—it means the same thing. Step 8: 100,000,000 Meters How far is that bright, beautiful moon up there? It’s at Step 8 on our distance staircase, about 4 times 100,000,000 m, or 400,000 km from Earth! Step 11: 100,000,000,000,000 Meters Let’s skip two more steps and head toward the blazing sun. How far is it? About 1,000,000,000 km PLUS an extra 500,000,000 km. That’s INCREDIBLY far! And yet, this sun, so very, very far away, still lights up our world and makes us sweat in the summer. Amazing, isn’t it? The Final Step??? Is there a final step on this staircase? We don’t know yet! But with powerful telescopes, scientists have been able to see far beyond the sun. The farthest object they can see is at Step 26, a mind-boggling 100,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 meters away! That’s UNIMAGINABLY FAR! Maybe when you grow up, you’ll be the one to discover something even farther away—at Step 28, or maybe Step 29. Isn’t that an exciting thought? Fun with Measuring Activities The following classroom activities are a great way for kids to grasp these far distances by working together in groups or teams. 1. Have the kids cut long strips of newspaper (each about one inch wide). 2. Ask them to tape or glue the strips end-to-end to make a long strip, aiming for a strip that’s 1 meter long (they can use a measuring tape). 3. Now, have them use this 1-meter strip as a measurement tool and make 10 similar strips, attaching them end-to-end to create a 10-meter strip. They can lie down head-to-toe next to this strip to see how many of them make up 10 meters. 4. They can then tape together ten 10-meter strips to create a 100-meter strip, wrapping it around the classroom multiple times. 5. What about a 1-km strip? How many times would it go around the classroom? Which team can create a 1-km strip the fastest? Notes for Parents & Teachers: Point 1 - When writing large numbers with many zeros after the number 1, it’s easy for kids—and adults!—to make mistakes. That’s why the notation of “powers of 10” is so useful. Through this book, children can be taught how to use it. All they need to do is count the zeros to the right of 1 and write that number as an exponent of 10. For example, 1000, which has 3 zeros after the 1, can be written as 10^3. And 10,000,000 (7 zeros after the 1), can be written simply as 10^7. Simple! Point 2 - In this book, we’ve limited our “How Far Is Far?” journey to the distance to the sun. If you want to go farther, you could add the nearest star beyond the sun, Proxima Centauri, which is 10^16 meters away from the sun. Or the distance across the Milky Way, which is approximately 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 (or 10^21) meters! Point 3 - One important note: the distances given in this book are estimates, not precisely accurate. For example, 3984 km is shown as 4000 km. This isn’t “unscientific”—in fact, rough estimates are quite helpful in science! You might do an activity with kids to highlight this idea. Is the length of a pencil closer to 10^1 cm or 10^2 cm? Is the weight of a school bus closer to 10^3 kg or 10^4 kg? Let kids come up with their own questions to quiz their classmates too.

title: Flower Fun
text: Assalmu alaikum Walaikum assalam "Is my Gudiya ready for school?" asks Dadu. "Yes, Dadu! I'm waiting for my school bus", replies Gudiya. "What are you doing?" title: The Old Man and His Golden Secret
text: Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived an old man named Shyam. Shyam was very rich and owned many gold bricks, but there was one thing about him—he was very miserly. He loved his gold so much that he kept it locked away in his house, never letting anyone see it. One day, Shyam heard some bad news. There had been robberies in the village, and thieves were stealing things from people's homes. Shyam became worried. “What if the thieves find out about my gold? It’s so big and shiny, someone could steal it!” he thought. He paced back and forth in his house, trying to figure out what to do. Finally, his wife, Rajni, had an idea. “Why don’t you break your big gold brick into smaller pieces and give them to our relatives to keep safe? That way, even if someone tries to steal it, they won’t be able to take all of it!” Shyam liked the idea. “That sounds like a smart plan!” he said. So, Shyam took his big gold brick, which was a whole piece of gold, and began to break it into smaller pieces. First, he cut the brick into 10 equal gold plates. Each gold plate was now of the whole gold brick. Next, Shyam took one gold plate and broke it into 10 gold sticks, so each stick was of the gold brick. Then, Shyam took one gold stick and broke it into 10 smaller gold blocks, so each small block was of the brick. Now, Shyam had many smaller pieces of gold. He decided to give some of them to his family to keep safe: He gave 1 gold plate to his wife, Rajni. That was of the whole brick. He gave 2 gold plates to his daughter. That was of the brick. He gave 3 gold plates to his son. That was of the brick. He gave 2 gold sticks to his brother-in-law. That was of the brick. He gave 5 gold sticks to his brother. That was of the brick. He gave 7 small gold blocks to his nephew, Lalit. That was of the brick. After distributing the gold, Shyam sat down to record everything in his notebook. He wrote down each fraction carefully, but it took a long time. He had to write,,, and so on. Lalit, who was very clever, noticed his uncle was taking a long time to write down the fractions. “Uncle, why don’t you use decimals? It will make it much quicker!” Shyam was puzzled. “Decimals? What are those?” Lalit smiled and explained, “Decimals are just a shorter way to write fractions. For example, instead of writing, you can write 0.1. Instead of, you can write 0.2, and so on. It’s much faster!” Shyam thought this was a great idea! He quickly started using decimals to write down the gold amounts: became 0.1 became 0.2 became 0.3 became 0.02 became 0.05 became 0.007 Shyam was amazed! Using decimals made everything much easier. He felt happy knowing that he could keep track of his gold quickly and simply. Shyam decided to share this new idea with the villagers. He showed them how they could break larger amounts into smaller parts, just like he did with his gold, and use decimals to make their records faster and easier. The villagers were very excited and grateful. They learned that decimals were a simple way to represent fractions and that breaking things into smaller parts could help them keep track of their belongings more easily. And so, Shyam not only kept his gold safe but also taught the entire village how to divide and organize things using decimals. From that day on, the villagers were happier and more organized, and they knew that understanding decimals could make life much easier.
