title: Bitcoin: the digital treasure
text: Why can't we just make as much as we want? Money can be coins, bills, or numbers in computers. We use it to buy things like food, toys, or clothes. When we give money, we get what we want to buy in return. When there is too much money around, things in stores start to cost more. This is called inflation. Having more money doesn't make you richer, because if everything gets more expensive, you'll be able to buy less with that money. There is a way to earn money fairly and clearly: it’s called Bitcoin. But how does this special money work? Imagine a team game: computers all over the world solve tricky math puzzles. Whoever solves them wins new Bitcoins, which only exist online and are shared by everyone like a treasure. Each Bitcoin is made by solving tough math problems. To do this, lots of computers, energy, and time are needed. That's why no one can make Bitcoin out of nowhere: you have to work hard to get it! Also, Bitcoin can’t be copied or faked. It takes a lot of computers, energy, and time. Every Bitcoin is recorded in a big public book called the blockchain. If someone tries to make fake coins, the network says no! The rules of Bitcoin aren't decided by a king or a government, but by everyone who uses it. Without the agreement of most people, no one can change the rules! There are only 21 million Bitcoins, and no more can be made. This makes it a strong kind of money that doesn't lose its value, unlike other currencies. Good money should be easy to use but hard to make. Bitcoin is a new idea that solves an old problem. Normally, we need a person or a bank to help us swap money. With Bitcoin, you don't need anyone in the middle. It's easy to use, hard to make, and can't be copied or stolen.

title: Facts about Camels
text: Today I will tell you some facts about camels, I hope you can keep all that in your mind till the end. So these will be containing 'Normal Facts about Camels' and 'Fun Facts about Camels'. Hope it all hops in your brain. Facts about Camels: Physical Characteristics Humps: Camels have either one hump (Dromedary camels) or two humps (Bactrian camels). These humps store fat, not water, which can be converted to energy when food is scarce. Adaptations: Their long eyelashes and sealable nostrils protect against sand, while their broad, padded feet help them walk on sand without sinking. Habitat and Distribution Native Regions: Dromedary camels are native to the Middle East and the Horn of Africa, while Bactrian camels are found in Central Asia. Adaptability: They can withstand extreme temperatures, from freezing cold to blistering heat, making them ideal inhabitants of desert climate. Behavior and Diet Diet: Camels are herbivores and primarily eat dry grasses and thorny plants. Their tough mouths allow them to eat vegetation that other animals might avoid. Water Consumption: They can drink up to 40 gallons (150 liters) of water in one go, and their bodies are extremely efficient at conserving water. Social Structure Herds: Camels are social animals and typically live in groups called caravans or herds, led by a dominant male. Communication: They communicate through a series of vocalizations, including grunts, moans, and bellows, and use body language such as head movements and neck positioning. Domestication and Uses Domestication: Camels were domesticated over 3,000 years ago and have been used as pack animals, for transportation, and for their milk, meat, and wool. Cultural Significance: In many cultures, camels are considered a symbol of survival, endurance, and wealth. Lifespan and Reproduction Lifespan: Camels live for about 40 to 50 years. Reproduction: Female camels have a gestation period of about 13 months and usually give birth to one calf, although twins are rare. Physical Characteristics Coat: Camels have a thick coat of fur that reflects sunlight and insulates them from the intense desert heat. During winter, they grow a dense undercoat to stay warm in freezing temperatures. Legs: Camels have long legs that help keep their bodies away from the hot sand. Their legs are also strong, allowing them to carry heavy loads over long distances. Habitat and Distribution Migration: Some camel herders migrate seasonally to find food and water for their camels. This nomadic lifestyle helps camels to survive in the harsh desert environment. Population: There are millions of domesticated camels across the world, but the population of wild Bactrian camels is critically endangered, with fewer than 1,000 individuals left in the wild. Behavior and Diet Social Behavior: Camels are social animals and often live in groups called caravans. These groups are typically led by a dominant male and consist of several females and their young. Reproductive Behavior: Female camels have a gestation period of about 13 to 14 months, usually giving birth to one calf. The calf stays with its mother for a year before becoming more independent. Adaptations and Survival Strategies Thermoregulation: Camels can raise their body temperature during the day to reduce water loss through sweating. At night, their body temperature drops to conserve energy. Water Conservation: Camels produce very little urine, and their feces are dry, which helps conserve water. They can also tolerate losing up to 25% of their body weight through sweating without suffering dehydration. Importance to Humans Transportation: Camels have been used for centuries as pack animals, capable of carrying heavy loads over long distances without food or water. This has made them essential for trade and travel across desert regions. Agriculture: In some cultures, camel dung is used as fuel for fires, and their hair is spun into yarn for making textiles. Cultural Symbolism: Camels are often seen as symbols of endurance, resilience, and survival in many cultures around the world. I hope these additional facts give you a deeper appreciation for these remarkable creatures! 🐪 Fun Camel Facts: Extra Eyelids: Camels have three eyelids. The third eyelid acts like a windshield wiper, moving sideways to clear their eyes of sand. Kneeling Pads: Camels have thick pads of skin on their knees that protect them when kneeling on hot desert sand. Unique Walk: When camels walk, they move both legs on one side of their body, then the other. This "pacing" gait helps them conserve energy. Spitting Camels: Camels can spit as a defensive behavior. They may not actually spit but rather regurgitate food from their stomachs and fling it at perceived threats. Yuck, but effective! Noise Makers: Camels make a variety of sounds including moans, groans, roars, and bellows. Their vocalizations are quite distinctive and can be heard from far distances. Haircuts: In some cultures, camels are given elaborate haircuts and decorations during festivals and special occasions. Odd Drinkers: When camels drink water, they can gulp down up to 40 gallons in just a few minutes. Talk about a rapid refuel! Nasal Control: Camels have muscular control over their nostrils and can close them completely to block out sand during sandstorms. Camel Racing: In some countries, particularly in the Middle East, camel racing is a popular sport. Camels can reach speeds up to 40 miles per hour (64 kilometers per hour) in short bursts and sustain speeds of around 25 miles per hour (40 kilometers per hour) for longer distances. Modern camel racing often uses robot jockeys to avoid the use of child jockeys. Survival without Water: Camels have an incredible ability to survive without water for long periods. They can go without water for up to two weeks, depending on the conditions, because they get moisture from the plants they eat and can conserve water by reducing sweating and urination. I hope these were enough to keep you thinking all day-night

title: Why does a human shiver?
text: One day, Pratiksh was mountaineering, bustling in excitement to complete it successfully. As for the first time, he was relishing its wonderful experience. But, poor boy, it so happened that he had not covered or wrapped up himself in wool and velvet clothes. He was unable to bear the extreme cold. Hence, he started to wobble, the skin began to develop goosebumps, and he observed that his body liberated a lot of heat, and he was shivering!! It was just involuntary, and one couldn't control it either!!! His friend Raman also happened to mountaineer with him. He was dressed up in layers!!! Seeing Pratiksh's condition, he yelled at Pratiksh. "Pratiksh! You are shivering. Cover yourself up with more sweaters so you can keep yourself warm enough to continue the journey. Else, you would die of frostbite!". Pratiksh did so. He covered himself with more sweaters, tightened his leather boots, and even wore a muffler. They continued their journey until they reached a temporary safe spot. There, Pratiksh lit up a campfire and both were enjoying, taking some warmth. Pratiksh was a born scientist. He wanted to know the cause of shivering in detail and asked Raman, "Raman, by the way, why does a human shiver? It just happened even without my anticipation and control. It was just involuntary!" To this, Raman replied "Yes, it is a natural process bound to happen." He continued. "But I am Sorry. I do not know its cause in detail. You may consult a person who has better knowledge about this." Pratiksh kept this question in her mind. He came back from his mountaineering journey and asked the same question to her parents, teachers, etc. But none of them were successful in providing a suitable and reasonable explanation. Thus, not killing his scientific quest, he dreamt of consulting the world-famous physicist, Isaac Newton one day, one of his childhood dreams. And so, he did. Newton was busy working in his lab when he gave a very surprising entry. Seeing him, Newton replied with amazement. "My good gracious boy, I see you are very excited. What is it all about?" Pratiksh asked the same question. "Newton Grandpa! If you are really an intelligent person, tell me, why does a human shiver?" Newton must have thought this question was quite easy, or silly. But he understood that the boy was not asking a one - word answer but the underlying explanation of the physics principle it had." And so, Newton continued, "Good question. My boy, whenever a human shivers, it means that he liberates heat out of his body in the process." "Where does the liberated heat go?" Pratiksh: Into the surroundings Newton: Yes, of course! So, it means that your body does lose heat which is gained by the surroundings. But how does one know how much heat is liberated by the body in the process of shivering? A law that governs this principle is called the 'Newton's law of cooling' which states that 'The rate of heat liberated by a hot/warm body is directly proportional to the difference of temperature between the body (here, the human body) and its surroundings." Pratiksh: Could you elaborate this law more? This seems quite interesting. Newton: You See, it means that if a body liberates some heat, so it loses heat and is depicted as the system losing heat. Mathematically, it is depicted by the minus sign (-). But the surroundings gain heat. So, it is depicted by the plus sign (+) mathematically. If you would depict this in a form of a mathematical equation, you would model it using calculus and your final equation would be: - dQ/dt = k (T 2 - T 1) Here, - dQ/dt is the heat lost by the body in a given time, k is a constant, T 2 is the final or reduced temperature of the system and T 1 is the initial temperature of the system. Pratiksh (Jokingly): Ah! You are such a brainy grandpa, if I could only understand using an experiment. Your mathematical equation is quite complex. Newton: It's Ok! What you need to understand is not the equation but is application first. Then, this equation is easy. (He continued with the experiment to prove this theory). You take a vessel with boiling water at 100 degrees Celsius. It needs to cool down to 25 degrees Celsius. You put a laboratory thermometer in it, and you wait to take its reading. You observe that it would cool down quickly (in minutes). Why? It is because the room temperature is 25 degrees Celsius. So, your temperature difference is (T ﻿2 ﻿ - T ﻿1 ﻿) = 100 ﻿- 25 = 75 degree Celsius. Wait for some time and the temperature of water would fall to somewhere around 30 degrees Celsius. But now, it takes hours to cool back to 25 degrees Celsius. Why?? Now, your temperature difference (T ﻿2 ﻿ - T ﻿1 ﻿) = 30 - 25 = 5 degrees Celsius. Newton (continuing): So, what did you observe? When the temperature difference was 75 degrees Celsius, the boiling water cooled down in minutes (approx. 5 min) whereas when the temperature difference was 5 degrees Celsius, the boiling water took hours (approx. 3) to cool to 25 degrees celsius. So, it experimentally means that "More the temperature difference, higher is the rate of cooling and less is the time taken and vice - versa." So, the question is "Why does a Human Shiver?" Let's have a biological prerequisite. We know that our human skin contains some heat detectors and radiators called thermoreceptors. These are what are make our skin diathermic (a substance that allows both absorption and emission of heat). The normal body temperature is 37 degrees Celsius. When you go to a mountain peak, the temperature of surroundings is sub - zero say - 40 degree Celsius. Hence, there is a high difference of temperature. Difference of temperature = 37 - (-40) = 77 degrees Celsius. What a huge difference of temperature! Don't you think so? When your 'magical' skin senses this, it sends a signal to your brain through your sensory nerve of the nervous system saying "Hey Brain! The difference of temperature is too high! I'm feeling really cold. Tell me what to do?" And then your brain sends back the message to the motor nerve saying "Thermoreceptors! Liberate a lot of heat from the body so as to reduce the difference of temperature between you and the surroundings." And so, your thermoreceptors liberate heat in large chunks causing goosebumps over your skin and the body vibrates. This is called "Shivering". Pratiksh: Thank You Newton Grandpa! For your amazing explanation. Now, I understand why a frostbite happens. Our heart does a lot of work in the process of shivering. It pumps huge amounts of warm blood to still try to keep human body warm at a constant temperature of 37 Degree Celsius. Gradually, after some time, the heart muscles get tired unable to withstand more pressure to work and hence, they stop the contraction and relaxation, leading to a frostbite death. Frostbite deaths happen when a person fails to cover his body in layers to prevent shivering and excessive energy of heart being spent in liberating heat, especially in snowy and mountainous regions. There is very less probability of survival if provision of immediate medical care is absent or in deficit. Why are sweaters an important invention? Sweaters made of wool are mostly adiabatic walls (they do not allow any transfer of heat). They prevent the heat emission from the body and hence protect the heat flow. So, your body then feels the decrease in difference of temperature and stops shivering or reduces it. Thus, you are prevented from a frostbite death!! So, the next time you go to windy, snowy, mountainous regions or outside on early morning winter days, don't forget to wear a sweater.

title: baby clothing
text: From Playtime to Naptime: Baby Clothes for Every Moment As a parent, one of the most delightful and rewarding tasks is dressing your baby. Whether it’s active playtime or quiet naptime, your baby needs the right attire to stay comfy, secure, and content. Let’s explore the best baby clothes for every stage of the day. A baby’s skin is soft and sensitive, which means their clothes should be gentle and breathable. Also, consider easy dressing features like snap closures, zippers, and stretchy necklines for those fast-paced diaper changes or quick outfit adjustments. Playtime: Comfortable, Durable, and Fun Playtime is one of the most exciting parts of a baby’s day, as it’s when they learn, explore, and discover the world around them. title: Need help ?
text: One day, a Blue elephant, after a long walk, decided to stop by the seaside to cool off. The water was refreshing, and he enjoyed splashing around. Yet, he felt something was missing—someone to play with. He came across a little colorful fish and asked if it wanted to play with him. The little fish replied sadly that their worlds, as close as they might seem, were in reality far too different for them to play together. The little elephant, resigned, continued to wander when he saw a hen followed by a line of yellow chicks. "Do you want to play with me?" the little elephant asked her, but she replied: "Can't you see I have a lot to do?! I'm too busy thinking about my children to play with you. And be careful not to crush us with your big feet!" More and more distressed, the elephant continued on his way and arrived in a village of farmers. "Maybe someone will want to play with me this time!" he thought. But as soon as the villagers heard the terrible sound of his footsteps, they barricaded themselves in their homes, trembling with fear. The little elephant couldn’t understand why everyone was so afraid of him, and he felt sorry about it. He just wanted to be helpful and make friends. So he thought of a solution: a quieter entrance into the village! He said to himself confidently, "In the meantime, I’ll quietly move away a bit. Someone will come out and see that, after all, I’m not mean!" And as he turned around, stepping as lightly as possible......he saw a little girl who was sleeping deeply. She hadn't noticed his arrival in the village; she was busy dreaming that she was eating delicious fruit candies! And when the young girl opened her eyes and saw the clumsy little elephant, who had done everything he could not to wake her, she stood up and said, "Come out, everyone! We’ve finally found the solution to all our problems!" Now it’s your turn: What help could the little elephant possibly provide to this farming village? Imagine possible scenarios and try to create an ending to this story.

title: The Pangolin Protectors
text: POACHERS ARRESTED, PANGOLIN AND SCALES SEIZED AFTER A DARING INVESTIGATION The forest officials involved in the investigation call in the pangolin protectors. Aditya and his team of scientists come as quickly as they can. “It looks like a ball of petals!” says Raju, the youngest forest guard. “The locals call it Salai, it is the Indian Pangolin,” says Aditya. “ Did you say PENGUIN?” “Arre baba! It is a PANGOLIN!” says a senior forest official. “Oh. But where is the face?” Raju has more questions. “See, tucked under her tail. Pangolins curl up this way when they sense danger.” “Does it bite? Or sting?” “No, Raju, she is toothless. Only eats ants and termites,” replies Aditya. Aditya and his teammate Rajesh move the curled-up pangolin to a special box. The box is designed like a burrow, like those where pangolins live. Finally, a safe space for her. With water, and termites for food! The box with the pangolin in it is safely handed over to the Forest Department, until the animal can be released into the wild. After a long and dusty drive, the Forest Department team reaches the busy district court. “Do they hunt the pangolin for its meat?” Judge Veena Roy questions the team. “Yes, your honour, and for its scales. The poachers make huge amounts of money on the illegal market by selling the scales. People in China and Vietnam believe the scales have medicinal qualities,” explains the forest official. “Really? Can the scales cure diseases?” she asks. “Not at all! The scales are made of keratin, just like our fingernails!” The poachers are sent to jail, while the pangolin in the box heads back home—to the forest. But first, a visit to the veterinary doctor, to make sure the pangolin is all right. Next, Aditya and the park veterinarian attach a small device called a radio transmitter to one of the scales near the pangolin’s tail. The transmitter talks to an antenna. The antenna talks to a receiver. Together, these machines will help trace the elusive pangolin once she is back in the forest. But how will the pangolin find a home? Hira and Ace are ready to help. They are intelligent, well-trained conservation dogs brought from South Africa. Their superpower is to find pangolin scents in the forest. With GPS around their collar, Hira and Ace have only one command to follow: “Pingu Soek.” In Afrikaans, “soek” means to search and “pingu” is a word the scientists have made up for the pangolins. That’s how the dogs know they have to look for a pangolin. Today, it’s Hira’s turn to help. Everyone follows Hira into the dense forest. PINGU SOEK Hira suddenly stops by a rock and sits. The rock hides the entrance to a burrow, and it has the scent of a pangolin. Rajesh and the team set up cameras on two sides of the burrow. The cameras will help track not only the pangolin but also her visitors—animal and human. Hira gets a ball as a reward. The team has to wait and observe the burrow for a few weeks, to make sure it can be chosen for the pangolin. The camera trap images show that the burrow is empty. Which means it’s the perfect home for the pangolin! The pangolin protectors go home with smiles on their faces. And the pangolin? She is home at last. • There are eight species of pangolins in the world—four in Asia and four in Africa. • India is home to two species, the Indian and the Chinese Pangolin. • They have long, sticky tongues to feed on ants and termites. • When threatened, they curl up into a ball and are shielded by their armour of scales. • They are nocturnal animals, which means they are active at night. • Pangolin babies, called pangopups, ride on the mother’s tail until they are independent. • The pangolin is the only mammal with scales. Pangolins are extraordinary animals. Hello there Sadly, it is because of these unique scales that the animal is in severe danger. Every ten minutes, a pangolin is poached somewhere in the world. They are the most trafficked mammals on the planet, because their meat is considered a delicacy and their scales are used in traditional East Asian medicine. More than a million pangolins have been poached in just the past decade. MEET THE WILDLIFE CONSERVATION TRUST TEAM In the heart of Central India, scientist Aditya Joshi and his team from Wildlife Conservation Trust, including Hira and Ace—a pair of fearless Belgian Malinois dogs—and forest officials from the Satpura and Pench Tiger Reserves are working hard to conserve the Indian Pangolin. Hira and Ace were trained in South Africa before being brought to India to detect pangolin scent trails in the forest and lead the scientists to burrows. Pangolins rescued from poachers are fitted with a radio transmitter and released in the forest. This helps scientists keep track of the released pangolins, to monitor and ensure their survival. Radio transmitters and camera traps help scientists understand the behaviour of these shy animals about whom we know very little.

title: The most unpredictable phenomenon in the world: Stock market
text: The stock market was accidentally started by the Dutch companies in order to make profits. It was unexpectedly proposed by some traders to gain advantage of colonized countries, such as India, US, Russia, and Germany. Germany was known for its chocolates, Russia was known for its crude oil, India for its spices, and the US, for their color-based labour. Now, it has become one of the most independent factors of this world. The stock market is one of the most influential factors of this world. Stock market is seen everywhere, you listen it wherever you go, and there are thousands of people who have made profits with this. So, let us see what is stock market actually, otherwise we won't understand why it is used everywhere. Stock market is a digital market where you get a set of companies. This is not how you go to the market to buy fruits and vegetables. Stock market means you invest your money into a company, to gain profits. This is how you do it. First, you log into screener and look at what is happening in each company. Then, you have to predict in which company will you get profits. Then, you have to buy the stock and then, when you have profit, just sell it. You will get bonus money because the company is growing hugely and it is influencing almost every independent investor. But the reason I wrote this story is because stock market is the most unpredictable phenomenon that nobody can expect, except god. The reason is quite simple. You cannot see whether the company will grow when you buy and will be the highest price when you sell it. Of course, you can predict whether it will be the highest price when you sell it, but you can never be sure whether the company is going to grow when you buy it, or not. This is why many many independent investors fall into a huge trap of the stock market and lose money, instead of gaining them. But there are some ways you can gain profits even though knowing that the company may go well or not. There are some ways. A few of them are over here. And they are: 1) Please consider taking admission in investment schools. I would recommend any institute that is certified by government. This is because it is very important to learn the risks and the ways of escaping losses and finding out which company is going to grow very hugely. Of course, you might not have time for that, but that is the best thing to do. 2) Be alert do not fall for scammers. Scammers or cybercriminals are using stock market to their benefit. They create a false website that shows you a famous company for example Zerodha, and then taking your money as investments and showing false profits, making you induced to put more and more money into the cybercriminal's app, putting all the money into his account, rather than gaining profits. So, be alert and do not fall for these notorious tricks. 3) Please do not invest carelessly. This might lead to losing money, defamation and many more things that can cause huge trouble to you. So, be cautious, alert, and careful while investing, or you might pay for it. This is why many investors, even gods at investing, sometimes lose lot of money and fame. But the reason why they are gods is they learn from their mistakes. So, make sure to learn from your mistakes and not to repeat that again. So, in this story, you learnt what a stock market is, why is it used everywhere, and why it is so risky to invest in stocks. Now, the solutions are to join an investing school, to stay alert and not fall for notorious hackers who snatch money from everybody, and of course, do not ever take it as a joke and invest carelessly, or you might pay for your carelessness. title: The most unpredictable thing in the world: Money
text: Money has been a part of our body for about centuries, millenniums and even millions of years. It is needed to every single person in this world. And the reason why money is so popular and needed is because we need money to buy food. And farmers grow crops to earn money. This is a cycle that repeats every single time you and the farmer earns money. The The united states dollar has been familiar, I think, with you all. It has been controversially the largest currency in the world. But there were many other currencies like the rupee which were even stronger than the dollar. And even the pound was weaker than rupee. People from Britain invaded us to make our currency weaker and weaker. That's why, we became even weaker than the dollar. This is why money is unpredictable. (This image is taken from Wikipedia) Your enemies will become more stable silently and there is any possibility that bigger countries than us can make us even weaker economically without our knowledge. That is what is happening in developing countries. The developed ones want to show that they are the richest, so they put a lot of pressure on countries like India, Mexico, and many other developing countries. You do not notice this because we do not have technology to make sure That nobody is pressurizing us to make us fall down. This is why money was so unpredictable. India, was the richest country in the world. But the others compensated for it by developing new high-tech weapons to pressurize us which made us fall down quickly and when we got independence, we were so poor that we could not even afford to eat breakfast at that time. If money is that unpredictable, you might think, then why is our salary fixed? Shouldn't it be moving? Well, you'll understand. Your salary is also not fixed. It moves up when you work more, and it comes down when you work less. This is why, many people do not like to play part-time sports. That is because if they work less, they are going to get less money for daily expenses. The reason why they say your salary is fixed is because you work for the same time everyday. So, be careful not to misunderstand salary. When you work more, you get more, when you work less, you get less. Many people do not understand this. That's why they think they get a fixed salary. But, money is not entirely a turmoil, however. There are many pleasures you can have by earning money. First of all, it helps you with your expenses. So, it is important to earn money for basic needs such as food, water and sometimes, even air. That's why many people do not even get educated and go for lower grade jobs. This is because their parents can't afford high-quality or tech education. So, they are forced to go for lower grade jobs. The second thing why money is important, is of course, fun and appliances like televisions, laptops, and even mobiles. They are very costly items. So, it is important to earn money to have a good lifestyle. The third thing is safety. Money helps you with safety in terms of natural disaster, climate change, and many more changes in the Earth's surface. I'll give you some examples. let us say, Your city, because of climate change, becomes colder and colder and becomes a snowy city. You do not have a woollen jacket. So, money can help you buy a woollen jacket so that you can stay healthy and not fall sick. I'll give you another example. Say, there is a flood in your city and that is why, you lose your important things. Money or insurance can help you with recovering all that you lost. Sometimes, it can turn into a turmoil, but sometimes, it can turn into a life-saver. title: The Gift of Chappal
text: ' A Gift of Chappals" is a story from the class 7 English textbook, Honeycomb, by NCERT. The story is about a girl named Mirdu who visits her aunt Rukku Manni with her grandparents. Mridu and her cousins, Ravi and Meena, give away a pair of new slippers to a beggar in need. Mridu notices a pair of large black Chappals with clear toe marks. Ravi pulls Mridu to the backyard to show her a kitten. Ravi hides the kitten and feeds it milk. Mridu sees the music teacher's chappals and gives them to the beggar. The children give the music master Gopu Mama's new Chappals. Rukku Manni laughs when she learns what happened. The moral of the story is to help people in need.

title: Brownie and his new owner
text: Once there was a nice family, a man and his wife with their lovely baby of 9 months old only. They had to move to a new place far away from their own home because of the husband's new job. Once they reached their destination, the village was much smaller than they expected, the wife was a little disappointed as was used to live in a much developed civilization. But being a wise woman, she didn't show her disappointment to her husband. The husband joined his work and both the mother and daughters stayed home all day waiting for him to come home every day. Even though the wife didn't say anything, he felt that she was felling lonely somehow. One day, the husband came home from work and brought a surprise for his wife and gifted her a cute small dog so that she could have more company while he was away. The wife thanked him even though she didn't really like the dog. The husband named the dog 'Brownie". Brownie liked his new owner but the woman never wanted to play with him, instead just gave food to the dog and run away whenever the dog came near her. She never showed any affection to the dog really. One morning, while the woman was busy, she left her baby on the floor, a bee flew in tried to sting the baby. The woman was afraid of the bee so much she couldn't go near her baby to save her. She froze and then suddenly, Brownie ran towards the baby and scared the bee away. ﻿ The woman was thankful to her dog and felt guilty for her feelings towards Brownie, while the all their dog wanted was to be accepted and received affection to his owners. Now, realizing this, the woman apologized to Brownie and hugged him. From that day onwards, the woman, her baby and Brownie spent every day playing together with laughter while the husband had to go for a work. The family felt much happier than before.

title: The resourceful Crow
text: Once upon a time, a crow lived with its family in a village by the sea. He was the youngest among his brothers and sisters and therefore considered a simpleton. Once they wear old enough, all his brothers and sisters flew away to distant lands to find new homes. The little crow also decided to fly away and seek his fortune somewhere else. He realised soon enough that it was not an easy task. He had to stop frequently to east and rest. He saw many kinds of things along the way. However, on the third day, he grew weary and thirsty but could find nothing to eat or drink. he was desperate for a drink of water. He finally sees a pot of water...but he could not reach it! He looks around and spots some pebbles. He picks up the pebbles and drops them into the pot of water one at a time until the water level rises. He finally has a refreshing drink of water by using his intelligence!

title: Brownie helps with Peer Pressure
text: Keerthi is a twelve-year-old girl from Chennai. Keerthi is a shy and introverted girl. She only has a teddy bear whom she calls as Brownie as her best friend. Brownie has been with Keerthi since the time she was a toddler. Keerthi really enjoys her time with Brownie, imagining that Brownie could talk, read books and play with her. Brownie would equally enjoy the time Keerthi spends with her talking, reading and playing. Brownie has played an essential role in the character and the life of Keerthi. Though Brownie talking might be just a figment of Keerthi's imagination, Brownie is an adventurous teddy bear who can actually behave like an alive bear when no one is monitoring her presence. But soon enough Keerthi could not spend her time happily with Brownie just like a few years ago due to her studies. ''Assignments, homework, projects, exams. So much to complete!'', she would go on all the time. She also seemed very sad after coming back home from school. She often also started crying and feeling bad about herself and her shyness. Brownie started getting worried and puzzled by the increasing sadness of her and the reducing amount of her self-esteem. So, one day to find out about what Keerthi is doing in school and what is causing her sadness, our adventurous Brownie jumped into the school bag, planning to spend the day with her best friend in her school. This adventure made Brownie happy as it was bound to help her friend. Once Keerthi reached her school, Brownie used all her might to open the school bag's zip and saw Keerthi beside the school bag. Brownie got a chance to learn and understand a few interesting things like the Pythagoras Theorem and the Newton's laws of motion, which is said to be very hard to learn, making her feel proud of herself. Soon she started to find out the reason behind Keerthi's sadness when she noticed her involved in a conversation with her classmates when suddenly one of her classmates commented about her shyness and the others started laughing and teasing her about the same. This seemed to have her upset and in the verge of tears. ''Keerthi now is handling peer pressure'', Brownie thought to herself when she had an idea to help Keerthi when they both got home. Later that day, after Keerthi came home, Brownie started to execute her plan. First, she found a pack of crayons and using that she wrote a note on a paper that read: It is important that we understand that an opinion expressed by a peer about us is just their point of view based on their understanding and assumptions. We should try to accept our own unique characteristics without judgement and be grateful and happy about ourselves. After writing this note she sat near it with a smile. When Keerthi read this note, she understood the message, cheered herself up and learnt to accept her shy nature. Brownie's efforts are successful now that Keerthi is feeling grateful of herself and has learnt to embrace her uniqueness

title: Curious Kala - 1
text: "Amma, Why do all of them look different? They seem to be thinking about something? " asked curious Kala to her mother. "Yes, each one is feeling different type of emotions dear", Amma said to curious Kala. "What is an emotion Amma?" asked curious Kala. "There she starts with her endless questions!" sighed Amma and silently murmured to herself. "Good question Kala" said Amma with a cheeky smile. Emotions are how you feel inside about something, someone, some place or in general about a situation. "When Amma makes you your favorite food, you feel happy. Sometimes, when you are not getting out of bed in the morning on a school day, Amma feels irritated. At that time, what do you feel? Do you want to give it a try, Kala? " Amma quizzed Kala. "I don't want to get out of bed! ", said Kala to Amma. "You don;t want to get out of bed is a thought and I want to know your emotion at that time?" said Amma. Kala gave a puzzled look. "You feel sad in the morning when I try to wake you up for school! " said Amma to Kala. "This boy is feeling fearful". Its an emotion when someone is uncomfortable or worried or not familiar about something or someone or some place. This lady seems to be anxious about crossing the road! " Can we feel multiple emotions at the same time?" asked curious Kala to her Amma. Yes, you can feel multiple emotions at the same time. For example, when you asked what is an emotion sometime back. Do you remember, I sighed! I was actually getting worried that we were going to move away from our craft work to your endless questions. Yet, I also felt happy that you asked that question. It gave me an opportunity to talk to you about emotions! So, I felt worried and happy at the same time. "Amma, what is a sigh?Why did you say that it gave you an opportunity to talk about emotions. I don't get the difference between thought and emotions. Can you that a little more? " "That is for another day. Lets work on our craft now!", Amma said to curious Kala.

title: Understanding the CompTIA FC0-U61 Certification Exam
text: The CompTIA IT Fundamentals+ (FC0-U61) certification is designed for individuals looking to build a solid foundation in IT concepts. CompTIA IT Fundamentals+ Certification covers key topics such as hardware, software, networking, cybersecurity, and basic troubleshooting. It’s ideal for beginners who are considering a career in IT or want to validate their basic IT skills. The exam assesses your understanding of basic IT concepts like how computers work, the use of operating systems, understanding networks, and recognizing security risks. After passing this exam, you can pursue more advanced certifications in IT, making it a great starting point for a successful career in the tech industry. You’ll have access to high-quality resources that make studying easier and ensure you're fully prepared for the exam.

title: What if something never fell back on to any planet?
text: Earth has an amazing property of the gravitational force. It's not just the earth but every object in this universe possesses the property of gravitational force because they all have mass. Anything that jumps from the earth and flies, rolls or even do somersault must fall back to the Earth, right? Yes. It is a common phenomenon which we have all observed. But have you ever been curious to know what if an object was thrown, but does not return back to the earth? Is it possible? Continue to read the story and you'll get the answer at the end of this book. You must have seen satellites and space missions being launched. Do these satellites and space mission vehicles fall back to the earth the moment they are launched at a high velocity into the space? No! Obviously not! This means that we can actually 'throw' objects in such a way that they can never fall back to the earth!! So, objects must be thrown away from the earth at a very high speed to not fall back to the earth. Such a speed or velocity is called the escape speed or escape velocity. Escape velocity of a heavenly body: To explain, understand and implement the principle behind the launch of an artificial satellites and human space missions, the scientists brought the concept of escape velocity of a planet or in other words, any heavenly body. In physics, escape velocity is defined as: "The velocity required by a body to be thrown from the surface of any heavenly body to escape its gravitational field so as to not fall back." Even though gravitational force is universal and is present between every object in the universe, we don't use the concept of escape velocity for all objects because its value is too negligible to be counted. So, now let us understand how the formula of escape velocity is derived and calculate the escape velocity of the objects on all the 8 planets of our solar system and appreciate its significance. We know that between earth and any object on it, there exists a gravitational force which can be calculated by F = (Gm E m)/r 2 where F = the gravitational force, G = gravitational constant (6.67 X 10 -11 Nm 2 kg -2 ﻿), m 1 = mass of earth, m = mass of object on the surface of earth, r = radius of the earth Now, we know that any object that exerts force also tends to move the object towards itself. So, the object moves and there is some displacement of the object. This is called as the Work done by the earth using its gravitational force. i.e. Work = Force X Displacement When the satellite is launched, it acquires a velocity called initial velocity which is normally denoted by the symbol v i. So, the satellite acquires a kinetic energy. i.e. K = 1/2mv i 2 After some time let's say at time t, it acquired an even higher velocity larger than the initial one. This velocity is said to be the final velocity. The kinetic energy acquired by the satellite then is, K = 1/2mv f 2 Meanwhile, the earth is too selfish!! She doesn't want to let go of the satellite! So, she also does some work on the satellite. The work done by the earth's gravitational force gets converted to potential energy of the satellite because it is still trapped in the vicinity of the earth. Mathematically, the potential energy gained by the satellite due to the earth's gravitational force is given by W = - GM E m/r Why is the work done negative? This is because the earth loses a lot of energy in trying to hold back the satellite! Thus, from the above scenario, we can say that the energy of the satellite when it acquires its final velocity is equal to the sum of the energy it gained in its initial velocity and the work done by the earth's gravitational force in trying to hold back the satellite. So, mathematically it can be written as: 1/2mv i 2 + GM E m /r = 1/2mv f 2 Further simplifying it, we get GM E m/r = 1/2mv f 2 - 1/2mv i 2 We know that v i or initial velocity of the satellite was zero because it was on the surface of the earth. So, the equation modifies to GM E m/r = 1/2mv 2 v = [2(GM E m)/mr] So, finally the equation gets modified to v escape = [2gR E ] because m gets cancelled and GM E m/r 2 = g and power indicates its square root Isn't it interesting? Our scientists have arrived at such a wonderful calculation using their amazing brains! This is a mathematical modelling for finding the escape velocity of a body in general. Now that we know how to calculate the escape velocity, lets calculate the escape velocities of each of the planets of our solar system. Firstly, let's start with the escape velocity of mercury. Escape velocity of mercury: The radius of the mercury is 2439.5 km and its mass is 3.302 X 10 23 kg. So, lets now calculate its escape velocity by first calculating its value of gravitational acceleration g. g = (6.67 X 10 -11 X 3.302 X 10 23)/(2.4395 X 10 6) 2 = (22.02 X 10 12)/(5.95 X 10 12) =3.70 m/s 2 So, its escape velocity is v e = [(2 X 3.70 X 2.4395 X 10 6)] = 4.25 k m/s. If we convert this km/s, the value would be 4.25 km/s! So, did you see how high the value was! If we were to launch a satellite from mercury, its velocity must be 4.25 km/s. We had converted the radius into meters by multiplying 1000. Escape velocity of Venus: The mass of the Venus is 6 X 10 24 kg, and its radius is 6050 kilometers. Let's now calculate the escape velocity in the similar manner. g = (6.67 X 10 -11) (6 X 10 24)/ (6.05 X 10 6) 2 = (40.02 X 10 13) / (36.6 X 10 12) = 10.9 m/s 2 So, its escape velocity = [2 X 10.9 X 6.05 X 10 6 ] = (131.89) = 11.48 km/s Thus, if we have to launch a satellite, it should be at a velocity of 11.48 km/s. Escape velocity of Earth: The mass of Earth is 6 X 10 24 kg, and its radius is 6378 kilometers. Let's now calculate the escape velocity in the similar manner. g = (6.67 X 10 -11)(6 X 10 24)/ (6.378 X 10 6) 2 = (40.02 X 10 13)/ (40.68 X 10 12) = 0.98 X 10 = 9.8 m/s 2 So, its escape velocity = [2 X 9.8 X 6.378 X 10 6 ] = (125.01) = 11.18 km/s Thus, if we have to launch a satellite, it should be at a velocity of 11.18 km/s. Escape velocity of mars: The mass of the mars is 6.910 X 10 23 kg and its radius 3396 km. So, we can calculate the escape velocity of the mars using similar method. g = (6.67 X 10 -11)(6.910 X 10 23)/(3.396 X 10 6) 2 = (46.09 X 10 12)/(11.53X 10 12) = 4 m/s 2 So, the escape velocity is v = (2 X 4 X 3.396 X 10 6) = (27.17) = 5.21 km/s So, if you were to launch a satellite from mars, you have to launch it at a velocity of 5.21 km/s. Escape velocity of Jupiter: The mass of the Jupiter is 1.8987 X 10 27 kg and its radius is 71492 km. So, we can calculate the escape velocity of the mars using similar method. g = (6.67 X 10 -11)(1.8987 X 10 27)/(7.1492 X 10 7) 2 = (12.66 X 10 16)/ (51.11 X 10 14) = 0.25 X 10 2 = 25 m/s 2 So, the escape velocity is v = (2 X 25 X 7.1492 X 10 7) = (357.46) = 18.91 km/s So, if you were to launch a satellite from Jupiter, you would launch it at a speed of 18.91 km/s. Escape velocity of Saturn: The mass of the Saturn is 5.6851 X 10 26 kg, and the radius of the Saturn is 60268 km. So, lets calculate the escape velocity in a similar manner. g = (6.67 X 10 -11) (5.6851 X 10 26)/ (6.0268 X 10 7) 2 = (37.92 X 10 15)/ (36.38 X 10 14) = 1.04 X 10 = 10.4 m/s 2 So, its escape velocity is = [2 X 10.4 X 6.0268 X 10 7 ] = (125.36) = 11.2 km/s So, if you were to launch a satellite from Saturn, you should launch it at a speed of 11.2 km/s. Escape velocity of Uranus: The mass of Uranus is 8.6849 X 10 25 kg, and the radius of the Uranus is 25559 km. So, lets calculate the escape velocity in a similar manner. g = (6.67 X 10 -11) (8.6849 X 10 25)/ (2.5559 X 10 7) 2 = (57.93 X 10 14)/ (6.53 X 10 14) = 8.87 m/s 2 So, the escape velocity of the planet Uranus is [2 X 8.87 X 2.5559 X 10 7 ] = (45.34) = 6.73 km/s If you were to launch a satellite from Uranus, it must be launched at a velocity of 6.73 km/s. Escape velocity of Neptune: The mass of Neptune is 1.0244 X 10 26 kg and its radius is 24629 km. So, lets calculate its escape velocity in a similar manner. g = (6.67 X 10 -11) (1.0244 X 10 26) / (2.4629 X 10 7) 2 = (6.83 X 10 15) / 6.07 X 10 14) = 1.13 X 10 = 11.3 m/s 2 So, the escape velocity of the planet Neptune is [2 X 11.3 X 2.4629 X 10 7 ] = [55.66] = 7.46 km/s If you were to launch a satellite from Neptune, it must be launched at a velocity of 7.46 km/s. Let us now tabulate all the data we have obtained. On the left we have the planet and on the right of the hyphen, we have its escape velocity. ﻿ Planets - Escape velocity (in km/s) ﻿ Mercury - 4.25 Venus - 11.48 Earth - 11.18 Mars - 5.21 Jupiter - 18.91 Saturn - 11.2 Uranus - 8.87 Neptune - 7.46 What are the uses of Escape velocity? 1. Detecting the presence of atmosphere Did you know that the presence of atmosphere is determined by knowing the escape velocity of a planet? Yes. Atmosphere is mainly a mixture of multiple gas molecules. The minimum speed required to control a gas molecule such that it does not escape the surface is 5.6 km/s. But many planets do have lesser escape velocity than this. Hence, these gas molecules escape away and there is no atmosphere on bodies such as Moon, Mercury, Mars, Uranus and Neptune. 2. Launching of artificial satellites Artificial satellites need to escape the gravitational field or pull of the planet to revolve in the orbit or to go on a voyage to the other planet. In such cases, the escape velocity is calculated and the amount of fuel required to exert thrust on the rocket engines is provided. In this way, satellites are even sent to other solar systems. Example: Voyager satellite of NASA, United States is on its way to the neighboring solar system!!! In the next book, we shall come up with some more interesting and mind-boggling phenomena related to the amazing world of physics. Always be inquisitive and think out of the box. SEE YOU IN THE NEXT STORY

title: I am a Kutti Police
text: Last Friday, our Sports teacher called a few of us girls. It was break time, and we were talking while eating our fruits. She said that 5 girls from fifth standard class have been chosen for a very very important task. She would say no more. So, we five students went with the teacher to the Sports Hall. The teacher screened a short video on traffic rules and crowd management. It was very interesting. We learnt the usage of hand signals. We learnt how to manage crowd. After the video ended, the teacher explained that for the next few months, we would be managing traffic and students at our school. We were delighted at first. A few moments later, we were a bit afraid. How were we going to do the task, we asked the teacher. With a beaming smile, she gave each one of us a badge with our individual names. In the badge, it was inscribed that we were Kutti Police – little students on police duty. (Kutti, in Tamil, means small-sized). From that evening, we started to wear the badge with pride. The next day morning was our first day of duty. We assembled at the entrance of the school, near the gate. We stood in a line, and asked all the students to walk on the platform. We diverted the two-wheelers to a different path, and the four-wheelers had to go out on a wider road. In the evening, we ensured that the students left the school in an orderly manner, beginning with very young students. We requested parents to not park the vehicles near the dispersal area. Our first day of duty was over, when all the students left. Our Sports teacher, who was with us all through, was elated with the way we carried out the duty. She said we were truly Kutti Police, but with Periya Responsibility (Periya, in Tamil, means big-sized)!

title: The Penguin Swing and the Basketball Dream
text: Once upon a time, in a land far away, there was a snowy little village nestled between the tall, icy mountains. This village was home to a lively group of little penguins who loved to play and have adventures. The most exciting part of their village was a giant tree that stood in the middle of the snowy playground. With a determined gleam in his eye, Pip set his sights on the towering tree at the edge of the square, envisioning swings tied to its sturdy branches, turning snowball fights into slam dunks and laughter echoing through the crisp air. The village was about to witness a league of its own—a penguin's whimsical dream come to life. This tree was no ordinary tree; it had a sturdy swing tied to its thick, sturdy branches. The swing was made from colorful ropes and a smooth wooden seat that glistened in the sunlight. Every day, the little penguins would gather around the swing, giggling and waddling with anticipation. They took turns swinging high into the air, pretending they were flying like the birds they admired. There were five little penguins who were the best of friends: Pip, Waddle, Splash, Flipper and Snowy. They spent every day together and were always on the lookout for new adventures. One sunny morning, as they gathered at the tree, Pip had a brilliant idea. “Hey, friends!” Pip exclaimed, his black and white feathers shining in the sun. “What if we play a game of basketball while swinging on this swing?”. Flipper, ever the strategist, nodded enthusiastically. “Let’s do it! We’ll need a basketball and a goal. Snowy, can you find something, we can use as a basketball?” Waddle, who was always up for a challenge, flapped his flippers excitedly. “That sounds amazing! But how will we shoot the basketball while swinging?” I have an idea!” Splash chimed in.“We can take turns swinging high and then use the momentum to hit the basketball into the goal! It will be so much fun!” Snowy, with her sparkling eyes, darted off to search for something round. A few moments later, she returned with a bright orange ball that she had found.“Look! I found this! It’s perfect!” she squeaked with delight. The other penguins gathered around, their eyes gleaming with excitement. “Now we just need a goal!” Pip said, looking around the snowy playground. They spotted a pile of fluffy snow that had formed into a small hill, and with teamwork, they shaped it into a perfect snow mound. “This will be our goal!” Waddle declared, jumping up and down. With everything set up, the little penguins took turns swinging on the swing. They pushed off the ground with their tiny flippers, soaring higher and higher. Each time they reached the top of their swing, they would try to hit the basketball into the goal. Pip was the first to swing. He took a deep breath, swung high, and with a mighty flipper flick, he sent the basketball soaring through the air. It flew like a comet and landed right in the middle of the snow mound.“Yes! I scored!” Pip shouted, doing a little happy dance. Waddle was next. He swung back and forth, gaining speed. As he reached the highest point, he closed his eyes and swung his flippers with all his might. The basketball flew up, but it didn’t quite make it to the goal. Instead, it landed in a pile of snow, making a soft poof sound. The penguins burst into laughter.“It’s okay, Waddle! You’ll get it next time!” Splash encouraged, her cheerful voice ringing out. Splash took her turn next, swinging energetically. She focused hard and swung her flippers as she let go of the basketball. It soared through the air and landed just a little short of the goal. “So close!” Flipper cheered, clapping his flippers together. Next up was Flipper, who was determined to score. He swung higher than ever before, feeling the wind against his feathers. With a mighty swing, he released the basketball. It flew straight but missed the goal, landing next to the other penguins. “I’m getting better!” Flipper laughed. Finally, it was Snowy’s turn. She was the smallest of them all, but she had a big heart and a lot of determination. She climbed onto the swing and took a deep breath. “I can do this!” she said to herself. With a determined look, she swung back and forth, gaining momentum. “Here goes nothing!” she shouted as she swung as high as she could. With all her strength, she flicked the basketball. It flew through the air, spinning and twirling, and—Swoosh!—it landed perfectly in the snow mound. The little penguins took turns for the rest of the day, celebrating each other’s successes and laughing at their near misses with their human friends. They were having the time of their lives! As the sun began to set, painting the sky with beautiful hues of orange and pink, the little penguins decided to take a break. They plopped down in the soft snow, panting and giggling from all the excitement. “Today was the best day ever!” Waddle exclaimed, his eyes shining with happiness. We can invite other penguins from the village to join us. Imagine how much fun that would be!” Splash’s eyes sparkled with joy. “And we can come up with teams and have a Penguin Basketball League!” As the little penguins chatted excitedly about their plans, they were filled with dreams of future games and adventures. With their hearts full of joy, they waddled home under the colorful sky, dreaming of their next adventure. The next day, bright and early, the little penguins gathered at the tree once again. They were buzzing with excitement, ready to create their very own Penguin Basketball League. They called their friends from the village and soon, the snowy playground was filled with cheerful little penguins, all ready to play. Pip took charge and explained the rules. “Okay, everyone! We’re going to split into two teams! Let’s have Team Snowy and Team Flipper!” he announced. Everyone cheered, excited for the match to begin. The teams were formed and they decided to play a friendly game. The rules were simple: each team would take turns swinging to score points by getting the basketball into the snow mound goal. The team with the most points by the end of the day would win! As the game began, the little penguins cheered for each other, their laughter echoing in the chilly air. The swings were flying and the basketball was soaring as each penguin took their turn. The excitement was contagious and soon, the entire village was buzzing with the sound of happy penguins cheering for their friends. As the sun climbed higher in the sky, the games continued. Pip, Waddle, Splash, Flipper and Snowy were having the time of their lives, and so were all their friends. They cheered, clapped and even made up silly chants to encourage each other as they swung and shot. With every turn, they learned something new. They learned to work as a team, to cheer each other on, and to celebrate each other's successes, no matter how small. The joy of playing together filled their hearts with warmth, and the snowy playground was alive with the spirit of friendship. After hours of swinging and shooting, the game finally came to an end. The penguins gathered around to count the points.“Let’s see who won!” Snowy said excitedly.As they tallied the scores, they realized that it didn’t matter who won or lost. Everyone had played their best and had a fantastic time. With a gleam in their eyes, they all agreed, “We’re all winners today!” The sun began to set once more, and the little penguins felt a sense of accomplishment. They had created something wonderful together—an adventure filled with laughter, friendship, and fun. They were already planning their next game, excited to see what new adventures awaited them. As they waddled home, tired but happy, they couldn’t stop talking about their basketball league and all the fun they had. They knew that as long as they had each other, every day would be an adventure. And so, in their snowy little village, the five little penguins continued to play and swing, dreaming of new games, new goals and new adventures, forever united by the joy of friendship and the magic of play.
author: Chaithanya Raghavan

title: pengu's first day at school
text: My name is pandu i am 5 years old I am a new student at pandpiss international school my first day at school was exiting. I got up early in the morning. my father took me to school. On the way i met many pandas some with their parents i heard the pandbell ringing tring! tring! tring!. other pandas started running each🐼 panda took his or her place in line.I ran and joined others. When I looked at other students, I felt very small. They seemed much older than me. An older panda took me by hand to where students of my age were gathered. I was with the wrong class! As I stood in line with the pandas of my age,I heard someone yelling ''madam this Panda has wet his shorts! we all turned back.I saw a little panda holding his shorts, looking 😔sad. Both his legs were wet, his eyes were wet with tears. An older panda came and took him by the hand to get help. Then a teacher panda showed us our classroom. It was large and clean. One panda came in late. He was holding his shoes. The teacher asked why. He said that his mom had taught him to always take off his shoes before stepping into a room. We all laughed The bell rang again tring! tring! tring! we rushed outside and stood in lines. A teacher came to us and told us and told us that it was break time. There was no need to stand in lines. It was time to play! after a short while, the bell rang again. All other pandas were rushing into there classrooms. I was confused, I didnt know where to go. I had forgotten my classroom! I saw a classroom in front of me and stepped inside. Two other pandas followed me. None of us knew where to go. One of the panda who was with me started crying. author: Aarohi Munoli

title: The Best Christmas Present in the World
text: It was early nineteenth century, and oak. It was expensive. The author found an old roll-top desk in a junk shop and decided to restore it. Inside a secret drawer, he discovered a letter written by Jim Macpherson to his wife Connie on December 26, 1914 during World War I. In the letter, Jim described a wonderful Christmas truce. A truce where British and German soldiers met in no man’s land, sharing food, drinks and stories. They even played a football match together. Jim bonded with a German soldier named Hans Wolf and they shared their dreams of peace. The author then tried to locate Connie Macpherson to return the letter. He found out that Connie, now 101 years old, was in a nursing home. When he visited her and gave her the letter, she mistook him for her beloved Jim, believing he had returned as he promised in the letter. It was her the best Christmas present in the world!
author: Divya ciet

title: Boli
text: Boli was standing outside her humble home, looking unsure but she was hopeful. Boli was a simple, timid girl living in a small village. She was often teased and underestimated because of her quiet and shy nature. However, she had a kind heart and a curiosity about the world. One day, a new teacher named Sulekha arrived in the village school. She saw potential in Boli that others had overlooked. Sulekha encouraged Boli to read, write, and speak up for herself. Gradually, Boli's confidence began to grow. She started participating in class, asking questions, and helping her classmates. Sulekha's encouragement and support made Boli believe in her own abilities. Boli's actions earned her respect and admiration from everyone in the village. She had transformed from a simpleton to a brave and confident girl who believed in herself and inspired others.

title: A Fun Day with My Cat!
text: Puma are the best of friends. They do many things together. Last summer, Gabi and Puma spent a very fun day together. Since it was July 4th the weather was hot and sunny. Gabi woke up that morning, saw the good weather, and didn't want to stay at home. She wanted to play outside with Puma. Gabi wanted to go to swimming, but cats don’t like water. Gabi went to Puma's room and talked to Puma. "Puma do you want to go swimming?", Gabi asked. "No, I don't want to. I’d rather go eat ice cream or go to the park." Puma replied. "Then shall we eat ice cream at the park?” said Puma. "That sounds fun! let's go to the park together" "The weather is too hot, should we the bus?" Gabi asked. "I don't want to walk." Puma said. "Sure, let's take the bus. I don't want to walk either" said Gabi. Gabi and Puma walked to the bus stop and waited for the bus to arrive. The bus arrived soon, and they took it, riding for 20 minutes. They arrived at the park. There were many people at the park. Gabi and Puma walked to the shop and bought ice cream. Gabi bought chocolate ice cream, anf Puma bought strawberry ice cream. They sat down and ate their ice cream. While enjoying the beautiful scenery of the park, Gabi and Puma were happy. "What should we do next time?" Puma asked. "What's your hobby?" Gabi asked. "I like sports. my favorite is soccer" Puma answered. "So should we play soccer over there?" "Yes! I think it'll be fun!." Gabi and Puma played soccer all day and had a lot of fun. Then, at 6 PM, they went to buy food for dinner. They ate ramyeon by the lake and had a great time. Gabi's friend Elena was also at the park. While having dinner, Gabi saw Elena. Elena told Gabi and Puma, "Since it's July 4th, there will be fireworks tonight." Gabi and Puma were excited. "Elena, do you want to watch the fireworks together?" "I'm sorry, but my family is here, so I have to watch the fireworks with them. But thank you for inviting me!" "That's okay. Let's meet up and hang out next time." "Yes, of course. See you next time!". Elena said goodbye to Gabi and Puma and left. The fireworks started at 9PM. Gabi and Puma watched the fireworks together, and it was really fun. The fireworks ended after an hour. Since the weather was cool, Gabi and Puma walked home. They arrived home and, Gabi and Puma went to sleep. The summer day was very enjoyable. Gabi is happy because Puma is her best friend. Author's Introduction: My name is Gabi. I am 22 years old and live in Washington. I am a university student. I have been learning Korean for 2 years. My hobbies are video editing, and dancing. When I have free time, I enjoy resting at home or meeting with my family.

title: Walk through the Woods
text: Creak. Creak. “Oh, will you stop making that noise, Kayla?” Stephie got up from her armchair and massaged her throbbing head. Her sister, Kayla, looked up at her from the swing. “Sorry… I can’t think straight. Mom’s been sobbing all through afternoon and I’ve been shut up inside this stuffy house all day long…I need a break,” Stephie said. “Yes, you do. Go on out and get some fresh air dear,” Kayla smiled at her younger sister. Stephie came out into the living room and saw her mom sobbing over a piece of paper. Typical. Of course, she would be doing that now. On the paper was a large picture of dad. Above the picture, it was written in big bold block letters- “missing”. Below were two phone numbers- her dad’s and her mom’s. Stephie never understood mom’s logic behind that. If dad was the one missing, why would someone call dad and say, “I found you”? Stephie had asked her mom about it, but she’d said, “you’ll understand when you’re older, dear.” That- that made no sense. Most parents would say that to kids and assume older just meant 16. When their kid turned 16, they would reveal all sorts of magical stuff to them. But nothing of that sort happened to her. In fact, her sweet sixteen had been boring. she was 18 now already- so she wondered, why didn’t mom or my sister tell me? She looked over at her sobbing mom. Considerate Stephie wanted to comfort her, but Selfish Stephie wanted to bolt out of the doors and run into the nearby woods. But she’d dealt with too much that day. Consoling her mom about her dad… it didn’t feel like the thing she wanted to do right now. Selfish Stephie took over and she swiftly walked out of the doors and sprinted into the woods. She replayed that Sunday again in her head. Her coming to these woods. Going to the dandelion fields, playing around in them. But she’d had her dad then and he’d accompanied her. He’d been with her when she skipped through the dandelions. He’d told her idiotic stories about dangerous people who killed others for fun. “Dad! I’m seventeen!” she’d rolled her eyes. That was the day before… before he went missing. When they’d come back home, he’d been really cheerful until that… that phone call. “Yes, Jim… right away… no, no, I don’t think so… what are you saying? No, that’s not possible… not Leonardo! He was the most careful… yes, I think it’s time…” She hadn’t understood a thing. She’d thought it was probably just a work call. Then her dad had rushed around the house packing a bag full of random things and food. He’d then gone up to his wife, kissed her than turned to Kayla and said gravely, “It’s time”. Kayla had asked, “which one?” to which her dad replied, “precaution 23.” He never came back home after leaving that night. He’d been reported missing, and Stephie and her mom were willing to do anything to bring him back. Three days after he was reported missing, his body was found in the woods. He’d been brutally murdered. Stephie’s mom had cried so much her tear ducts must have dried up like the desert. Stephie couldn’t process that her father had died. She cried so hard. Kayla was the only one who seemed unperturbed. But then, she was really good at acting. She probably had been hiding her emotions and cried when she was alone. Kayla was the one running the house now. Stephie was still studying, and her mom was just lying on a bed, crying most of the time. Her soul seemed to have flown up with her husband’s. all that remained was a body which could do basic function and supply salt water through its eyes. Stephie had reached the dandelion field. It was now one year since the day her dad had gone missing. She looked around at the flowers and smiled sadly. She sat down cross-legged and picked up a dandelion. “I wish I could see my dad just one more time. Just once so I can tell him how much I love him,” she wished aloud and blew the petals away. She watched her wish get carried by the wind in front of her. “Hey, Stephie,” a gruff, familiar voice called. She turned back and her eyes widened in horror. “Dad?”
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: The Walking Tree
text: “Hey! Why are you not eating?”, asked Bela when she saw Kuku sitting quietly with her lunchbox during recess. “Oh! When did you come?”, sheepishly asked Kuku. “While you were day-dreaming!”, giggled Bela and opened Kuku’s tiffin. She took one of the soft idlis with a generous dollop of coconut chutney. “Kuku, your mom has made such soft idlis that they are simply melting in the mouth. But why are you not eating? What is bothering you?”, persisted Bela. “I haven’t told anyone, Bela, but I must tell you. Yesterday while having my lemonade, I swallowed a lemon seed”, said Kuku. Bela was shocked to hear this. Her face dropped in grief and her eyes became as round as eggs! “What have you done Kuku! This is so terrible. Now a lemon tree will grow inside you. And branches will come out of your ears, nose and mouth! You will become a walking tree now. Oh! I am so worried Kuku”, cried Bela. “Oh! Bela. I am so scared”, said Kuku with tears rolling down her cheeks. Kuku reached home. She went to her room and slept. She did not say anything to anyone. “Help me, Ma! There are lemons everywhere! I can’t see, I can’t hear! Help! Help!”, Kuku was shouting in her sleep. Her mother came running to her room and gently woke up Kuku. “What happened my dear? Was it a bad dream?”, gently asked her mother. Waaaaahhhhhaaaaaaaaaaaa!!! Kuku was sobbing continuously. Ma hugged her and asked her again about the dream. Then Kuku told her about swallowing the seed of a lemon and that she had a dream that a lemon tree had grown inside her and lemons were growing on her eyes and ears. “Bela also said that I will soon turn into a walking tree” continued Kuku. "What? A walking tree!", said mother, trying her best to hide her smile. She then held Kuku in her lap and asked, “Do you know what a seed needs to grow into a plant?” “Of course, Ma! Air, water, sunlight and the nutrition in soil. We have already done this in our science lesson”, confidently replied Kuku. “Fantastic! You know your lessons well my dear. So now tell me, from where will the sunlight and soil enter your tummy?", questioned mother. AIR WATER SOIL SUNLIGHT "Moreover, the digestive juices in our tummy make it too acidic for the seed to grow. And some of the seeds are so small that we have always been eating them, like tomato, cucumber, banana, grapes, pomegranate and many more”, explained mother in detail. “Wow! I never realized that I am eating cucumber seeds daily”, an embarrassed Kuku said. “Yes, I too have never seen a cucumber plant on your head”, winked Ma. Kuku gave a tight hug to Ma and jumped off the bed. “Where are you going now”, questioned Ma. “Into the kitchen to make lemonade for all. I am not afraid of the seeds anymore. They are our friends who give us life when grown carefully in farms”, cheerfully replied Kuku.
author: Neha Maheshwari
