title: The Big Trouble
text: There was a big Peepal tree in a small garden of the city. Many small animals lived together in the garden. A family of squirrels lived on the peepal tree. Vicky was a very proud member of it. Once his cousin Kato came to visit him from a distant forest. One day as they were preparing to sleep, they heard clattering sounds coming from the adjacent field. ﻿ ﻿ Kato and the other squirrels peeked out and saw that big yellow machines and some men wearing yellow triangular caps were pointing with their fingers towards their small garden. Actually, they were going to demolish the houses facing the garden and build a car park, i.e. a place to park vehicles. Arrangements for other houses were made for the people living in those houses, but who thinks about the animals, birds and insects? The machines were first seen by mole rats. Hawa Singh was the oldest among the mole rats. He told Gulab Singh and he told Makhan Singh. The thing is that when they were children, people used to call them Hawa, Rose and Butter. Hawa Singh told the news to the squirrels, the squirrels to the birds, the birds to the caterpillars, the caterpillars to the butterflies, and thus the word spread to all the inhabitants of the garden. After that it was as if there was a stampede. People were running here and there, flying, running, laughing and crying. What to do? Where to go? Alas, what kind of confusion, what kind of trouble is this? The caterpillars said, “Let’s collect leaves.” The butterflies said, “We want flowers.” The rats were worried about their holes and the moles also wanted holes for themselves. In fact, all the animals knew very well that they would not be able to survive without trees, bushes and grass. They grew up on soft soil. It was not possible for them to live on the hard cement floor. Crying he said, “Where will we get all this? How will we live?” Kato's uncle and aunt were listening to everything silently. The little squirrels were sitting crouched in their mothers' arms. Kato snorted and cleared his throat and said shyly, “I live far away in the forest, why don't we all go there?” Wow, this just happened! There was a commotion. "But how?" And Kato said, scratching his head, “The squirrel 'Super Fast Express' can take all the squirrels, caterpillars, butterflies, spiders and all the insects there. Birds can fly away. The 'Mole Rat Express' can take the mole, rat and snake families from under the ground.” Everyone praised Kato's solution. Hawa Singh ran to Mr. Gintu, the driver of Mole Rat Express, and asked, “Will Mole Rat Express take the mole rats far into the forest?” The driver was first nervous, then shy, stuttered a bit and then said, “Sure!” Hawa Singh felt that he too should show some nobility. “Friends, there is no need to panic. “My great grandfather’s brother’s grandfather’s fourth aunt’s cousin’s third niece and second nephew live far away in the forest,” he consoled. ﻿ Early morning squirrel express and mole rats 'Chhuchunder Express' departed - 'Chhuk-chhuk, chhuk-chhuk' its Towards the distant forest carrying passengers. Towards its trees, flowers, ponds and soft earth.
author: Dan Rebello

title: The roots of an economy: employment Part-2
text: A country is independent when it has enough money to lead the country. A country is put in consideration when it's profits are growing. A country is seen as legendary when it has become the richest country in the world. A country takes attention of geopolitics when it is a rich country. For all this to happen, there is only one thing needed, but for that one thing, you need many things. I am sure you have guessed it, it's money. In the previous chapter, I told you how money works and why it is so unpredictable. Now, we are going to talk about its roots, employment. There is a secret cycle that every country uses to generate more and more profits and therefore get richer and richer. The reason why I put India as the image is because this goes on faster in India than in any other country. The first step is employment. This is the most important step in the cycle and that is why many countries are left dumbfounded by seeing India grow so much. Generating jobs is the hardest step of the cycle. Once you generate employment, you produce more. You create more demand and less supply. And that is when you sell your products and make the country grow. But the country needs the whole country's manpower. With only one person contributing to the economy, what he earns is the economy of the whole country. Does it even make sense? If nobody comes to that man's shop, the country is not going to earn anything. So, if you are contributing to Japan's economy(example) the whole population of the country is needed to make the country rich. Then, whoever gets profits will take home money. As a result, he will also spend money which will bring profits to others. The one who gets the money who had the profit is also going to have profits and therefore, spend. that spending will go to other shopkeeper when he will also spend, this is an infinite cycle, until the whole world gets demolished. So, the country which has more people will have profits, right? Wrong. If you think like this, you are understanding 0.000000000000000000000000001% of economics. The country with more people is harder to develop as you need to create more jobs, if you have more people. The more the population, the more you need jobs. that's why, even though there are very less people in Japan, it is the richest country in Asia. The third step is investments in the stock market. The more investors, the more rich a country becomes. The less the population, the less you need to create employment. That's why Africa is so poor. There are so many people in the country that the government is struggling to create employment. Apart from political violence, what makes Africa very poor is this reason.....With political violence it becomes even worse. So now, that we have completed two steps of the cycle, let's jump on! The third step is generation. This is why many countries, which used to be extremely rich in the past, have become extremely poor. And one example is Africa. It used to be very rich. The rulers of the kingdoms were tight. But after they died, when their successors had to be ruling the kingdom, they did not have any skill that could make them a king. The British and Europeans started to exploit this situation which made Africa so poor. So, it is important to teach the needed skills to your successors to make the country be run safely and wisely. The third step does not end here. Even though you have to teach your successors life skills, you have to choose who will learn what you teach and most importantly, who will follow your wisdom. Because, if you teach a person who does not like you, or does not know what to do after you die, it will be a disaster to your (or the ruler)country. But sometimes, exceptions do take place. When the ruler is not good, and he teaches what he does to his successor, the successor won't follow it if he is a brainy person. But if he is also a fool who thinks that what his master tells is always true, it will still be a disaster to the country. And now, the last step, which everybody aims for, defence. Defence is a very important part of the economy, apart from global geopolitics. It boosts security and helps avoid invasion. Now, let us understand economy as a tree and look at these parts as one of its organs and classify the most important, important and optional. Let's go! Unity: roots, Employment: stem, Generation: soil, Defence: flowers and leaves. So, we have understood that first comes unity, second comes employment, third comes generation and at last, defence. That's why the countries on the screen aren't the richest countries. They do the opposite. They say, first defence, second generation, third employment, and finally unity. Thinking like this says that you know 0.0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000001% of economics. That is all from my side, guys. If you have something else to say,, you can translate my story........ but you should know your own language. That was just the joke of the story. See you again!

title: The hat seller
text: One day, a hat merchant was going to a village to sell his hats. After walking for a long time, he was tired. So he sat under a tree to rest. He was so tired that he quickly fell asleep. While he was sleeping, a group of monkeys was watching him from the tree. They climbed down the tree to take a closer look. They opened the bag and looked inside. They were delighted to find many hats of different colors, just their size. Quickly, each monkey put on one of the hats! The monkeys danced joyfully, wearing hats in red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple, and pink. Suddenly, the hat merchant turned in his sleep, and all the monkeys ran up the tree. When he woke up a few moments later, the monkeys watched him and waited. The hat seller checked his bag. He was very sad to find it empty. There was not a single hat left. Then, he looked up and saw the monkeys wearing his hats! He thought about how he could get his hats back. Then, he took off his own hat and threw it directly at the monkeys. The monkeys thought that the hat merchant was trying to hit them, and they became angry. So, the monkeys took off the hats they were wearing and threw them one by one at the hat merchant. The hat seller gathered all his hats and put them back in his bag. The monkeys watched him in astonishment as he walked away, laughing, to sell his hats.

title: The Realm of Short Stories: I
text: Hi! I Am Sanya. Together, Let’s Strive into the Short Stories Stories have been a part of human life for centuries. They are more than just words written on a page; they hold emotions, experiences, and imagination that transport us into different worlds. Whether it’s a simple fable or an epic adventure, every story has something unique to offer. Short stories, in particular, are like little windows into a vast universe. They capture emotions in a few paragraphs, leaving an impact long after they are read. Unlike long novels that take time to build up, short stories dive straight into the heart of the matter. In a bustling Indian bazaar stood an old haveli. Its grandeur had faded, but its history was alive in whispers. In its main hall, a grand chandelier, once a maharaja’s gift to his queen, hung, dimmed by time but still shimmering in the sunlight. As Diwali approached, homes filled with light and laughter. Among the festivities, a curious girl named Meera wandered into the haveli, drawn to its mystery. Discovering the chandelier, she gathered her friends to clean and decorate the space, reviving its forgotten beauty. Under the chandelier’s renewed glow that night, the haveli came alive with music and joy. The echoes of past celebrations merged with children's laughter, proving that even forgotten places could shine again when touched by love and festivity. As the children danced and sang, the ghosts of the past seemed to awaken, their memories swirling in the air. Laughter echoed and joy radiated through the haveli as the chandelier, once a mere relic, became the centrepiece of a new celebration. The Chandelier The Mehta family argued about everything—what to eat, where to go, even the right way to fold clothes. Their grandmother, tired of the noise, announced, “Tomorrow, no one talks.”The next day, silence filled the house. At first, they made faces and pointed fingers, but soon, they found other ways to communicate—gestures, smiles, even laughter. By dinner, they were playing charades, enjoying each other’s company without a single fight. Grandma just smiled. The Family of Arguments On a lazy summer afternoon, a group of children found an old, dusty trunk in the attic. With wide eyes, they pried it open, hoping for treasure. Inside, they found faded letters, photographs, and a rusty key. Determined, they searched the house until they found an old wooden box in the backyard shed. The key fit perfectly. Inside, they discovered a small note: "The greatest treasure is adventure—never stop seeking it!" They laughed, realizing the real treasure wasn’t gold, but the thrill of the hunt. And so, their summer of endless adventures began. The Treasure The old library stood forgotten at the edge of town, its doors creaking with age. Once filled with eager readers, it now gathered dust and silence. One rainy afternoon, a young boy named Aarav wandered in, seeking shelter. He ran his fingers over the worn books, their pages whispering stories of the past. Curious, he picked one up and began to read. Day after day, more children followed, drawn by the magic of words. Laughter and curiosity filled the library once more, and with every turned page, the old building came back to life. The Old Library Ravi, the town’s laziest bus driver, was famous for his endless tea breaks and slow driving. Passengers groaned as he yawned at every stop, stretching time like a rubber band. One day, a mischievous boy named Kabir challenged him, “Bet you can’t be the fastest driver today!” Ravi smirked. Challenge accepted. That day, the bus zoomed through its route, reaching every stop on time. Passengers cheered, and Ravi, surprised by his energy, grinned. From then on, he still took his tea breaks—but only after the job was done right. The Lazy Bus D river

title: Tokyo Life
text: Tokyo is a very busy city with many people. Mariko's home is in Shinjuku, in downtown Tokyo. Shinjuku is one of the busiest areas in Tokyo. Mariko works at a Japanese advertising company. Her office is in Marunouchi, and it takes about 15 minutes by train. In the morning, there are many people going to work, and the train is very crowded. Shinjuku Station is the busiest station in the world. Every day, 3.53 million people use it. Tokyo has beautiful scenery, so there are many tourist attractions. Right now, it's spring, so the cherry blossoms are in bloom. In autumn, you can see the autumn leaves. Mariko often takes walks on weekends. Mariko lives in the city, but Tokyo has a lot of nature. Mariko likes eating food. Japan has a lot of delicious food. There are many tasty dishes, including sushi, tempura, soba, and shabu-shabu. Among them, Mariko loves sushi the most. She eats a lot, so she is chubby and has no money. Every Friday after work, Mariko drinks with her colleagues. Japanese people often drink at izakayas. Mariko likes drinking Japanese alcohol while eating edamame. Izakayas are very cheap, so there are many young people. Mariko is a kind person, so she has many friends. Nana and Masami are Mariko’s best friends. They have been friends since elementary school. Since April 2nd is Mariko’s birthday, Nana and Masami prepared birthday gifts for her. She got a skirt from Nana and a dress from Masami. Mariko likes watching sumo matches, so she goes to see them every month. Sumo is Japan’s national sport, so it is very popular. Mariko doesn’t like exercising, but she enjoys watching sports. She also likes watching judo and baseball. Mariko often listens to Japanese music. Enka is a music genre in Japan. She loves singing, so she goes to karaoke every week. Karaoke was invented in Japan. That's why there are many karaoke places. Mariko listens to music on a speaker while cooking at home. She often makes karaage. Karaage is a delicious Japanese dish. She likes cooking, but she doesn’t like doing the dishes. Mariko also often reads manga. On the weekends, she reads manga and watches anime. Anime is a famous part of modern Japanese culture. Foreigners also like it. Japan is very safe. People are kind, and the crime rate is low. Tokyo is a busy but convenient city. Mariko likes Tokyo. I’m Ryu Sei, a first-year student at the University of Washington from Japan. I can speak Japanese and English, and I’m currently learning Korean at university. However, Korean is difficult, so I’m not very good at it yet. This summer, I plan to learn Thai. I enjoy learning foreign languages. My hobby is eating, and I love Korean food. I also enjoy watching Korean dramas and study Korean through them. This book is about the life of Mariko, who lives in Tokyo. I also live in Tokyo, so I wanted to write about it. Enjoy!
author: KR EN

title: The Life of a Cat
text: It lived in a very large grassy field. Born in this field, it lived comfortably. It got along well with other cats. This life was fun, but surviving was very difficult. One day, while playing in the forest to find food, the kitten saw a scary person. The kitten wanted to run away, but... That person caught the kitten! Suddenly, the kitten was in a car. The kitten meowed and cried, but no one answered. It wanted to escape, but it couldn’t, so it felt sad. The scary person drove for a long time. A few hours later, the kitten was put inside a box and arrived at a building it didn’t know. Inside the building, there was a kind doctor and other animals. The kitten was nervous, but the other animals were not friendly. Everything was scary for the kitten. The cat caught a cold! For a few months, the kind doctor helped the cat. Slowly, the cat's condition got better. And then one day...... A child that the cat didn’t know entered the building. The child was quiet and kind. The child and the child's father came to the building because they wanted to find the cat. The child said, "I will choose the cutest cat!" The cat had an idea. To get the child's attention, the cat acted cutely. The cat succeeded! The child thought this cat was really cuter than the others. So, the child wanted to play with the cat for a long time. The child liked the cat so much. The child's father said, "Then, I'll adopt this cat next week," but the child replied, "What if someone else adopts this cat by then?" Hearing this, the father immediately adopted the cat. The child took the cat home in a warm car. At the child's house, the cat was excited. It was a big house the cat had never seen before. There were also many people the cat hadn’t met, so it was a bit nervous, but still happy. The cat felt like it could live happily there. The child who adopted the cat is named Avia. Now, Avia is 19 years old, and the cat is over 13 years old. The cat's name is "Honey Pie." Even now, Honey Pie's best friend is Avia, Honey Pie's owner. Avia will love Honey Pie for the rest of their life. Author's Introduction: My name is Avia Oranriwajoo, and I attend the University of Washington in Seattle. I've loved learning languages since I was a child, so I’m studying many languages at university. This story was about me and my cat, "Honey Pie." We currently have four cats at home, and I love animals so much. When I have free time, my hobby is playing with my cats.
author: KR EN

title: The Simpson Family Who Defeated the Tiger
text: One day, Mr. Simpson set off on a journey to the city to sell bananas. On the way to the city, a tiger appeared and said, "If you give me a banana, I won't eat you." Mr. Simpson, startled, gave the tiger a banana, but the tiger kept appearing and ate all the bananas. In the end, the tiger ate Mr. Simpson. The tiger went to the Simpson family’s home, intending to eat them all. However, the remaining Simpson family members joined forces and defeated the tiger. They tricked the tiger by falsely assuring it that they would give it bananas. In the end, the tiger, which had harmed Mr. Simpson, paid the price with its life due to the cleverness of the Simpson family. The remaining Simpson family members helped and relied on each other, living happily ever after.

title: Mel and Moon
text: I dedicate this book to the friends who have been with me from the very beginning. On a dark and spooky night, A little ghost was playing outside. The ghost's name was Moon, and they lived with their family in an abandoned forest. While playing hide and seek with their friends, Moon the ghost discovered a human girl. Curious little ghost Moon followed the girl. The girl seemed to be lost, and Moon wanted to help her. The girl started walking toward a hidden cliff. Moon, who was hiding, called out, "Stop! There's a cliff!" The girl stopped and turned toward Moon. She thanked Moon and continued walking. Moon was surprised and followed the girl. "How can you see me? Humans aren’t supposed to see ghosts," Dal asked. "I’ve always been able to see ghosts," the girl replied. "Wow! Do you know it’s not safe for a human to be in the forest at night?" Dal asked. "I don’t want to see ghosts, and my grandmother said that if I eat Hattri’s elderberries, I won’t see ghosts anymore," the girl said. "What's wrong with seeing ghosts? Ghosts are awesome!!" Dal exclaimed. "No one wants to be friends with a girl who can see ghosts," the girl replied. "Humans are so strange. I’ll take you to Hattri. My name is Dal!" Dal said. "Thank you! My name is Mel! Nice to meet you!" Mel said. Mel and Moon walked through the forest for hours, along the way meeting many forgotten forest creatures. The animals followed Mel and Moon on their journey to find Haltri. "Haltri is just down this path. We only need to cross this bridge now," Moon said. "Great! Let's go quickly!" Mel shouted. As Mel and Moon crossed the bridge, it began to shake. Creak creak! The bridge started to break! Mel fell into the water! The forgotten forest creatures all ran to save Mel. "Thank you so much for saving me!" Mel cried. Mel wanted to repay the kindness of the animals. "My father is the village chief. I will make sure no more creatures from the forgotten forest are hunted!" Mel said. The forest animals cheered and took Mel to Haltri. "Here is Haltri! Are you ready?" Moon asked. "Go ahead!" Mel shouted. Mel took an elderberry from her pocket and put it in her mouth. "Now, let's go home," Mel said to Moon. Mel, Moon, and the forgotten forest creatures all returned to the starting point of the forest. "Goodbye, Mel. Thank you for being my first human friend," Moon said. "Goodbye, Moon. Thank you for being my first friend," Mel replied. After Mel ate the elderberry, she could no longer see Moon. Moon returned home with his friends, and Mel made her first human friend. Every year, Mel goes to the starting point of the forgotten forest, sits, and talks. Moon always comes to meet Mel, but Mel can no longer hear Moon’s words. Though Mel and Dal can't speak to each other anymore, they became close friends, always aware of each other's presence. My name is Michaela Shears, and my Korean name is Ha-eun. I was born and raised in Georgia. My family consists of my mom, dad, three older brothers, and one older sister. I major in International Business at Kennesaw State University, and I will graduate in December 2023. After graduation, I want to work in South Korea. I love different cultures, food, music, and traditional clothes. My dream is to speak multiple languages, and I hope to be fluent in Korean in the near future.

title: Reminiscence
text: Reflecting upon human emotions- It reminds me of one of the best bonds on the earth- the mother & daughter. Honey was brought up as a loving child always been pampered in the family. Whenever she would face a challenge in the world around, she would discuss the minutest details to her mother. Only after her satisfaction she could start studies part. Probably the mother would say," Honey, let's do the homework now, you are getting late" Time elapsed and Honey became a responsible citizen not only in the city but the country too. She brought laurels to the family and and the people associated to her. The mother always would thank the almighty as she was on the best footings. Now, the time was approaching when Honey had to proceed for her research work and she had to leave her mom. Though both were excited superficially but emotions were embedded. Honey was in a dilemma that if she has to leave the mother, can she go & leave her mother behind as she noticed that the mother was getting older and probably the childhood fears were returning and she was trying to put these thoughts away. Whereas, the mother was trying to be composed to allow her to proceed in her mission of research. In both the cases, the fear of not seeing each other were common. But they resolved to go ahead.

title: The tortoise and the hare
text: Once upon a time there was a hare and a tortoise. They were good friends. They used to meet and play everyday. The hare always boasted that he could run faster than the tortoise. The tortoise, one day decided to challenge the hare for a race. The hare laughed at this idea and remarked - "You will never outrun me. ” So they decided to have a race. They chose a starting and finishing point. They both took their positions, and on the first blow of the whistle, the hare started to run. Within a short period of time, it covered a long distance, whereas, the tortoise was taking small steps towards the target. The overconfident and boastful hare took a nap instead of completing the race, thinking that the tortoise would never be able to reach the target before him. Meanwhile, the wise tortoise moved with small steps steadily and crossed the sleeping hare. Hence, the tortoise finished the race while the tortoise remained sleeping. The moral of the story: “ Slow and steady wins the race.”

text: The Rhythm of My Day Tom is a boy of eight years old. He lives in an apartment of a big city with his mum, dad, and little sister, Emma. Tom has a big brown dog. His name is Max. Tom wakes up at 7:00 with his little friend, his dog Max! Then, he washes himself and brushes his teeth. He gets dressed and then Tom eats breakfast. He loves milk and cereals! title: The Power of Truth
text: Once upon a time, in the kingdom of Lumiara, there was a wise and kind King named Arthur. King Arthur loved his people and always told them, "The truth is what makes our kingdom strong and bright. Lies may seem easy, but the truth brings peace and happiness." T he King’s Lesson: One day, King Arthur gathered all the villagers in the town square. "My people," he said, "truth is the most powerful treasure in the world. If you are honest with each other, you will always be strong and united. But if you lie, the light of the truth will fade away, and the world will be filled with shadows." The people nodded, knowing the King was wise. They promised to always be truthful. The Parents’ Lesson: At home, young Elsa listened carefully to her parents. "Elsa," her mother said gently, "we want you to be kind and honest. If you ever tell a lie, it will make your heart feel heavy, like carrying a big stone." Elsa looked up at her parents and said, "But what if telling the truth is hard?" Her father smiled. "Telling the truth can be difficult, but it always brings light into your life. A lie might feel easier, but it will only bring darkness. We love you, and we always want you to be truthful." Elsa promised to do her best and decided to remember her parents' wise words. The Teacher’s Lesson: The next day, Elsa went to school. Her teacher, Miss Rachel, loved teaching her students about honesty. "Class," Miss Rachel said, "when you tell the truth, your hearts will be free and happy. Lies can confuse people and hurt feelings, but truth brings trust and kindness." Elsa raised her hand. "Miss Rachel, why is telling the truth so important?" Miss Rachel smiled. "When we tell the truth, we help everyone understand each other. The truth brings us closer together. Remember, just like the King said, truth is the light that shines in the dark." Elsa felt a warm glow in her heart, knowing that truth made the world a better place. The Friend’s Lesson: That afternoon, Elsa was playing in the park with her best friend, Martin. Martin had found a beautiful bracelet on the ground. "Look, Elsa!" Martin said. "I found this! I’m keeping it." Elsa looked at the bracelet carefully. "Martin, this might belong to someone else. We should find out who it belongs to and return it." Martin shook his head. "It’s mine now. I found it." Elsa remembered what her teacher, her parents, and even the King had said. "But Martin, the truth is always the best choice. Let’s find the owner, so they don’t feel sad. That’s what God, the King, and our parents would want us to do." Martin looked at Elsa and thought for a moment. "You’re right, Elsa. I’ll take it back." They both searched and found the bracelet's owner, who was so grateful. Martin felt proud of his decision, and Elsa felt happy knowing that truth had brought good into their day. God’s Lesson: That night, as Elsa lay in bed, she thought about everything she had learned. She knew that God, who watched over the world, loved the truth. God always wanted people to be honest because truth made everything peaceful and bright. God’s light shone brightly when people chose to do the right thing. Elsa said a little prayer. "Dear God, thank you for teaching us the importance of truth. Please help me always choose to be honest and kind, no matter what." As she closed her eyes, Elsa felt a warm feeling in her heart, knowing that by telling the truth, she was following God’s path and bringing light to the world. Why do you think telling the truth is important to God, the King, parents, teachers, and friends? How did Elsa feel after she helped Martin return the bracelet? What does this teach us about the power of honesty?

title: Cereals Make My Meals
text: Cereals are edible grains from crops. Food for humans is majorly made from cereals that act as a base. The common cereals are rice, wheat, maize or corn, oats, barley, and millets. Rice: Rice is a staple food for over half of the world's population, particularly in Asia. It is grown in flooded fields called paddies, which helps control weeds and pests. Manju had idli for breakfast and vegetable biryani for lunch. These food items were made out of the cereal rice. Wheat: Wheat is a major global crop used primarily to make flour for bread, pasta, and pastries. It is grown in temperate regions and the varieties include durum and common wheat. Ganga had chapathi for dinner and digestive biscuits for snacks. These food items were made out of wheat. Maize (Corn): Maize is a versatile crop used for food, animal feed, and biofuel production. It originated in Central America and is now grown worldwide. Babu had corn in the beach and cornflakes for breakfast. These food items are made out of maize or corn. Oats: Oats are highly nutritious and commonly used for oatmeal and animal feed. They are well-suited to cooler climates and have health benefits, including lowering cholesterol levels. Raju had oats kichdi for dinner and oats dosa for breakfast. Barley: Barley is one of the oldest cultivated grains and is used in brewing, animal feed, and health foods. It is adaptable to different climates and has a short growing season. Roopa drinks barley water to improve digestion and help weight loss. Millet: Millet is a drought-resistant cereal grain used in many traditional dishes in Africa and Asia. It is rich in nutrients and can thrive in arid and semi-arid regions. Karna had millet or ragi porridge for lunch and ragi ladoo for evening snacks.
author: Anitha Selvanathan

title: The Dirty Day
text: Chiku came home after playing for an hour in the evening. Her mom opened the door and she gasped looking at her. Chiku was covered with all kinds of filth. A patch of red stain on her skirt, right foot had dried mud marks, a wrapper of toffee stuck in her curly hair, and the left side of her dress soaked in water. "What games were you playing Chiku? Mummy asked in shock with eyes wide open. "I didn't play," Chiku replied in a low voice glancing at her skirt and feet. “Really, so the mud just jumped on you and the toffee wrapper is a new hair clip, I assume. Go, wash yourself up quickly, the floor is getting dirty" mummy instructed Chiku pointing to the bathroom. Chiku tiptoed to the bathroom, touching just her toes on the floor. While cleansing herself, flashes of all that had happened to her on the street disgusted her. Chiku came out and sighed, settling into the sofa as her mother sat beside her. Her mother placed a gentle hand on Chiku’s shoulder and leaned in closer. "Would you like to share what happened this evening?' she asked, caressing her head. "I went to call Chunni to play in the park," Chiku began. Her voice grew heavy as she recounted her experience." I stood at the front of Chunni’s tall and shiny tower, Waiting for her to finish her shower. Whoosh! A stream of filth falls on my head, slipping through my back, I turned quickly and looked up, The lady looked down, she said sorry, and moved on. I had peels of orange on my head, a gooey goo on my arm, a ball of hair twined in my curls, I tapped and twirled, to shake off the mess from me and my dress. I ran from there to be at home, As fast as I could, dogging the bikes, Swooping by the cars, hopping over the potholes. Wanting to clean up and have a comb. Splat! My foot got sucked by one of those brown holes. Tears streamed down my face, My leg was in the ditches, Warm, lumpy, thick brown mud crawled over my leg, I tried to rise, cleaning the squishy slop with my sleeve, Truly, mom, my leg still itches. I turned onto our street, limping and dragging myself. I was passing an auto, my foot in the air to take a step, and I saw- A man pushed his face out of the driver’s seat, And in a blink of an eye, he sputtered “Phhhht!” A big splash of bright red spit landed on my feet. I stared at him in shock, He looked at me- no emotions, solid as a rock. He waived his hand, motioning me aside, Mumbling words as the red syrup oozed. In horror, I hopped back with a yelp, But coolly, he drove off by himself. I froze for a moment, staring at my feet. I thought it couldn’t go any worse. Now that I neared my house, with dirty sandals, a skirt, and a blouse Eager to clean myself, But just when I thought I was safe, Like a flash, came a speedy bike It zoomed away with a rash drive. Splish! A gush of water flew so high, Left me dripping from shoulder to thigh. Clueless and careless as he could be, He zoomed away without looking back. I waited for a glance, a sign or a sorry, As I stood there like a wet, hanging sack. “Oh Chiku, you’ve had such a tough day. Sorry for all you had to go through." Mummy said, hugging Chiku.“Mummy you know, in my prayers today, I will pray for the people on the road.” I wish that the lady in the fancy house gets a bin, So no one becomes her trash tin. I wish potholes get caps, So no one falls as they take their laps. I wish the men with the oozy mouths wouldn’t make the roads red, And they eat no junk, but bread. I wish the bikers and the drivers show care, Because it’s everyone’s street, and we all need to share.

title: Genetics and heredity with DADI
text: Sakshi knocked on the door.Aadhya’s mother opened the door.”Is Aadhya there” asked Sakshi.Aadhya’s mother replied “ Yes, let me call her. “ Aadhya came and saw Sakshi she got happy and went out with her. They both started swinging. Then Sakshi asked “ Today when I came to call you,your mother opened the door and she looked exactly like you.” “What how is that possible “ replied Aadhya “I don’t know how “ again replied Sakshi.They both were playing but Aadhya was still wondering how is that possible. Then when she went home she asked her grandmother. “Grandma, today when I went to play with Sakshi she told me that I look like my mother “ “ But how is that possible, we both are two different people.” Later grandma giggled and told “This is called genetics and heredity “ “What is that “ asked Aadhya. “ Heredity refers to traits or characteristics that are passed down from parents to their children. Genetics more broadly refers to gene variations that may be inherited at conception or acquired later often due to environmental or lifestyle factors.” “Ohh now I get it.” “But can I look like my father “ asked Aadhya. “ Sure, it does not depend on your gender who you will look like.It could be anyone. “ “ Also you might have the looks of your mother and have the nature of your father. “Told grandma. “So if my mother has the nature of her mother she will have the looks of my mother or the opposite? “ asked Aadhya. It is not mandatory. It could be that you have the nature and looks of your father.” Told grandma. “So genetics is when a person has their mother or fathers or even both ‘s traits, looks or nature.“ said Aadhya. Aadhya continued “ Now I have got it is very easy and very normal.” Yes, now you can tell your friends who don’t know about this. “ Told grandma “ Sure” agreed Aadhya.

title: Playing Under Pressure
text: Once their live a boy named Noah. He loved playing cricket. It was not only his hobby but also his passion. His room was already filled with at least a hundred of medals and trophies. He was 14 but he used to play under 17 district. One hot sunny day, Noah had just received a email from the state cricket association that he has been moved to playing state tournaments and he was his cities team. It was one of his best days of his life and as soon as he read it he sprang up with joy. His first practice had started a day after he got his email and playing with the team was very fun. All of the team members always supported him and encouraged him to do more. He had shifted from playing on dirt to playing on real field. Noah and his team had been playing really well and they had moved to the finals of the state championship. He had been practicing very well and he thought every thing was going right until the championship day. He had got badly injured because he didn't pay attention to the ball as he was under pressure though his teammate had already got 50 runs. Noah was injured and all of their players were getting out one by one. By the time only one player was left who didn't know how to play and as one player can't play alone, their only hope was Noah who was legally allowed to play as hi was not out. The best bowler was bowling at that time, he was very nervous. The baller took the run up and Noah hit a six. Now Noah's team had to do 18 runs for 3 balls. Noah was batting, the fast ball came to him and with all his power the ball was out of the field, 6. Two more balls and again a amazing 6. It was the last ball and if Noah hit a six they would win the championship, Pressure was building up everyone had their eyes on him and and a fabulous 6. They had won the championship his team had won. Despite the pressure Noah had saved the team by the amazing hattrick of sixes. All the pain from the injury had gone only happiness was there inside him. This is how Noah's cricket carrier began..................

title: FACTS ABOUT ADOLESCENCE
text: What is Adolescence? Adolescence is a phase of life between childhood and adulthood from ages 10 to 21. It is a unique devolopment and an important time for body growth. Adolescence is marked by growth, change, emotions and mental growth. Adolecents experience rapid physical, cognitive, and social growth. Why is Adolescence Important? Adolescence is a period of time in life in which a proper change comes and a time to do something new and handle many responsibilities. How to Handle Adolescence? You can try to stay calm and meditate everyday. And feel free to go to any of your friends or family members and express your feelings and talk to them. CHANGES Emotional changes; 1. Your mood swings 2. You feel more sensitive. 3. You feel peer pressure. Mental changes; 1. Your eating food habits. 2. Your feelings change. 3. You have anxiety Physical changes; 1. Height 2. Voice change 3.Weight

title: The Curious Adventure
text: On a sweaty afternoon, there was 10 year old Shreya who lived in an attractive city. She banged the main door forcefully because she was very angry with her sister Kiara. Kiara rushed to the door thinking something was wrong with Shreya. When she opened the door, suddenly Shreya jumped on Kiara and they kept fighting till their rosie the cat scratched them. Then Kiara said “Why did you jump on me, and fight with me!!” 3 days ago, Kiara tore and spoiled a useless pair of jeans but they were Shreya's favourite. She was going to wear those jeans when she planned to go to Paris on her birthday. “Because you tore my favorite jeans which I was going to wear on my birthday to Paris, and you knew that", screamed Shreya. “Sorry Shreya, but it was all stained behind the jeans, so I tore it, by the way it did not even suit you”, explained Kiara. “Ok, but why did you keep it in my cupboard?” shouted Shreya. “Because you should know what happened to your jeans", said Kiara. They still kept arguing for a long time. Then they got ready to go to Paris. When they reached Paris, Shreya and Kiara were looking at the Eiffel tower and Rosie was sticking to Shreya, when suddenly a wicked magician came, took the cat and both of them vanished. “Kiara!! Where did our Rosie go? She was with you” shouted Shreya. Consequently, an unknown man came and said “Excuse me, I saw a magician who took a cat and they both vanished, I think it was your cat, ‘cause it was a yellowish brown colour, right?” “Thank you for informing us, by the way where did the magician go?” asked Shreya. “I heard that the magician is going to perform his show in the China zoo,” said the man. ‘Thank you so much!” exclaimed Kiara. They traveled to the China Zoo, and saw cute pandas. China is famous for pandas. They saw his show but there was no sign of Rosie. Suddenly, another man came and said, “What happened, why are you all worried?” “ Do you know where this magician’s next show is?” said Kiara in a low voice. “I know where the next show is, it is in Australia National park,” said the man. “Thank you so much!” said Shreya. They traveled to the Australia National Park and saw kangaroos. Australia is famous for kangaroos. Again they watched the show and still they did not see Rosie anywhere. Once more, a man came and said “I think you want to know where this magician's next show is, right?” “Yes, yes, do you know where the next show is?” said Shreya sadly. “Yes, Ok, it is in the Canada forest.” said the man. They went to the Canada forest famous for Reindeers, South pole Falkland Islands famous for penguins, New Zealand island famous for Kiwis, Brazil Pantanal famous for jaguars, still no sign of Rosie. But then they went to Southeast Europe, famous for lions. They again saw the show. Shreya and Kiara were shocked to see Rosie with the magician in the show. When the show was over Shreya and Kiara went to the magician and asked, “Hi, did you see any yellowish brown colour cat with anyone or roaming around? And there is a name plate around the cat’s neck, it says “Rosie”. The magician said with anxiety, “Ummm, I saw it going that way.” When they were going through, they saw a tail and the nameplate in the magician's coat. Fortunately, a small girl the same age as Shreya, gave the nameplate and their cat. “ Thank you so much little girl, how did you know we were looking for this?, " said Shreya thankfully. “Hi Shreya, don’t you remember me, l am your friend from the drawing class Disha!” said Disha “Ohhh, yeah, I remember you Disha, how did you know that we were looking for this cat?” “Yes, when I was sitting under a big tree, I saw you both looking at the magician’s coat, because there was a name plate and a cat with him, so I told the magician 'Can you please give me that cat and the nameplate? ‘Cause this is my grandmother’s cat and you stole it'. Then he gave me the cat and ran away.” “I don’t know how to appreciate you, thank you so much.” Then the 4 of them came home and had a wonderful time with Disha.

title: Holiday
text: She hated holidays. Sure, she liked the time she got to spend with her family, but she always frowned a little on the inside when she leaned of a holiday. Holidays meant being away from friends; being away from writing and learning; they meant a day without two joyous bus trips; and most importantly being away from the building she loved and called school. Holidays meant having to put up with family, with an obnoxious young sister. She loved school. She'd wake up, excited, on every school day wondering about the day's possibilities. She was a little ball of positivity who was loved by her family. She was a mischievous nerd who liked popularity just as much as she liked studying. Maybe it was because she got a lot of holidays-she had a fair share of both holidays and school days. But deep down, the little girl knew- she loved school over family any day; books over friends any day; she'd rather write her novel at school then hang out with her baby sister. She'd thought happiness was overrated; who wasn't happy? Only love was allowed to reside in her heart. She carried her self with grace, she was breaking inside, at a young age, but she carried herself with grace, because she wanted to prove to herself she wouldn't break at all the fakeness of everything. She brushed off sad things and she avoided people in general. She just wanted to be in school, the place she most associated herself with if you didn't count the library. She wanted to curl up and read her books, wishing for a life, love and friendship, like the ones she read about had. She was content. But it all changed in a year. One year-her whole mindset had been messed with. She now whoops for joy when she learns it's a holiday-she wants to spend more time with her family. Holidays now mean a day for some me-time; a day away from all the stressful cramming in and note taking; a day at home; a day she could spend with her family, some time with her loving sister. Most importantly, it means a day away from the pathetic building she calls school. She hates school. She wakes up every day filled with dread about the day ahead of her. She craves for love and recieves neglect from her family. She's told she spreads negativity. She craves to get good marks but she's lost the interest she used to have in learning knowledge. It's probably because she barely gets any holidays. School, home, school, and study in every waking second you have. The girl's grown grown up- she'd choose family over school any day; time with friends over fiction; she'd rather hand out with her sister than learn. She wants to experience happiness again. She wants love to eliminate all the other emotions inside her heart. She still carries herself with grace, she's breaking down, she's just revealed to herself the real world, she wants to give up but makes it a point to carry herself with grace to prove to the others that she is strong although she doesn't know if she is. She invited sadness for it is now a friend of hers. It feels good to not carry the burdening tears and let them go- but she can't expose them. She wants to stop acting; stop breaking down; she wants someone to love her, be there for her. She wants more. So much can change in a year. Now, she loves holidays.
author: Sahashri Badhrinath

title: Elephant and friends!!!
text: A lone elephant walked through the forest, looking for friends. She soon saw a monkey and asked, “Can we be friends, monkey?” The monkey quickly replied, “You are big and can’t swing on trees like I do, so I cannot be your friend.” Deflated, the elephant continued to search and stumbled across a rabbit. She asked him, “Can we be friends, rabbit?” The rabbit looked at the elephant and replied, “You are too big to fit inside my burrow. You cannot be my friend.” The elephant continued until she met a frog. She asked, “Will you be my friend, frog?” The frog replied, “You are too big and heavy; you cannot jump like me. I am sorry, but you can’t be my friend.” The elephant continued to ask the animals she met on her way but always received the same reply. The following day, the elephant saw all the forest animals run in fear. She stopped a bear to ask what was happening and was told the tiger was attacking all the small animals. The elephant wanted to save the other animals, so she went to the tiger and said, “Please, sir, leave my friends alone. Do not eat them.” The tiger didn’t listen. He merely told the elephant to mind her own business. Seeing no other way, the elephant kicked the tiger and scared him away. After hearing the brave tale, the other animals agreed, “You are just the right size to be our friend.”

title: 'The Puppy in Trouble'
text: One fine day, on a bright sunny afternoon, Rohan, Aryan and Sonia were playing in the park. They suddenly heard a soft cry. Behind some bushes, they saw a small puppy who was stuck in a hole and was struggling to find a way. "Oh no! We should help the puppy!" Sonia said. Rohan tried to pull the puppy, but it was stuck. Aryan immediately ran to get a basket and rope. Sonia tried to comfort the puppy while Rohan and Aryan tried to lift it out. The three friends tried their best to pull the puppy out. Finally, after repeated tries, Rohan and Aryan were able to pull it out. The puppy felt very free and started licking the hands of the three friends out of happiness. The puppy wagged its tail happily. "We did it!" Aryan cheered. Sonia smiled and said, "Because we worked together and didn't give up" Moral of the story: 'Small acts of kindness can make someone's day and the world will be a better place'

title: The Unusual Fight
text: Vedant was awakened by the wonderful dream, knowing he would smile throughout the day. The sun hadn't arrived till now, making him look towards the clock, “Oh! It's six o'clock in the morning” he exclaimed. He quickly took a bath with hot water, which made his mood even better. He quickly brushed his wild hairs and went to the cricket practice in his school. Vedant reached on the ground, but still the sun hadn’t risen. It was a small but grassy ground. There was a huge school building in front of the ground. It was a five floor tall building. Vedant sat on the ground, but not near the mischievous wild boys. He got the flashbacks - ‘One day Vedant was passing through the group of bad boys having clumsy hairs, bossy look, mischievous hairstyle and wild clothing. They just called him with a impolite manner, caught his neck and made his fun in a group. The heaviness of their words crumbled his heart. They talked about his skin colour, his unusual name, abused him and even physical abuse. This all imbalanced his mentality. The eyes were converted into a sea, and his heart squeezed like a lemon.’ While sitting, he noticed a few boys were beating somebody in a corner. When Vedant observed it closely, he noticed that the boy was known to him, but he couldn’t exactly remember the name. He bravely runs there to help him, but instead they caught him up. Fortunately the coach arrived. “ Huh! I am safe” Vedant sighs in relief. When he asked the boy, he came to know that there were religious affairs. Vedant totally disagreed with this behaviour. He was nervous throughout the day. He couldn't even sleep at night, and kept thinking about the incident. He promised himself, “This is not fair. I have to do something, for myself, my friends and my surroundings. My goal is to stop this discrimination. Stop this!! Stopppp!!” He was totally angry with red chilli eyes, a determination on his face. He was a different Vedant!!! Next day he woke up with the same routine but different plans. He took a hot shower, combed up his hair, and went to school. He gathered Rishesh, Raghav, Sheetal and Rutuja. Everyone seemed confused. Vedant introduces himself “I am Vedant, a grade seven student. I will help you guys because I observed that you all were being bullied.” “That’s true, others always bully us” Rutuja cried. “Everyone hates us”, Rishesh sobbed. Vedant marked "it’s over guys. The bullied ones now have to become the strongest ones” “We will not listen to this!” This became an ideal statement to protest. The team expressed their feelings through act in the weekly assembly. Raghav, Rishesh, Sheetal and Rutuja, everyone gave their best. They all did wonderful acts. Everyone appreciated them. Vedant gave a speech on topic of discrimination and even talked to people who bullied others and convinced others how it feels someone when you make fun of that person’s nature. ‘ Vedant’s efforts couldn’t be counted. They were infinite like the stars.’ The school proudly recognized Vedant’s all efforts to stop the discrimination, he was also honoured and recognized throughout the school. It was his brilliant efforts and contributions, but… Few people continued with this bossy business, still couldn’t understand the importance. But Vedant believed “One day this will change. But …That day wasn’t sure”

title: The Fish with a Plan
text: Once upon a time, there was a fisherman named Ramesh, he was so obsessed with fish, that he could probably tell you what they dream about at night. He loved fish so much; he made it his job. Some days he caught tons of fish, and other days, well. Now, Ramesh had one thing he loved even more than fish his "pride". He would proudly tell everyone, "No one can fool me! I know fish better than themselves!" One bright and sunny morning, Ramesh set off to the riverbank, practically skipping with excitement. "Today is the day!" he thought, "I’m going to catch so many fish, I’ll need a bigger boat!" With grand enthusiasm, he tossed his net into the river and plopped down on the ground, ready to make a * huge * sale at the market. After what seemed like forever, Ramesh decided it was time to pull up his net. He thought, “This is it! The big catch!” He tugged the net with all his might, expecting to find a fishy treasure chest. But when he pulled it out, his face fell. Instead of a boatload of fish, there was just one tiny little fish flopping around like it had just joined a fishy marathon. "This... is it?" he grumbled. "I’ve been waiting hours for this?” He squinted at the fish, which was about the size of his palm. "Well, at least it's not a sock," he muttered, starting to reach for the fish. But just as he was about to grab it, something unbelievable happened. The fish—yes, the tiny fish spoke. "Hey! Hey, fisherman!" the little fish yelled, looking up at Ramesh with wide, pleading eyes. "Please, please, please don't take me out of the water! I'll shrivel up like a raisin in the sun! I'm too small to survive! Don’t you want to see a fish live to its full potential? I could be the next big thing in the fish world!" Ramesh froze, his hand mid-air. "Did you just talk?" he asked, his voice full of disbelief. "Yes, yes, I did!" the tiny fish said, flopping its tiny tail. "I’m special! And I’m begging you let me go! Ramesh scratched his head, and ignored the fish. The fish, in an attempt to save his life, he wriggled in excitement and spoke. "Listen, fisherman! If you let me go, I’ll make sure my fishy friends love you! I’ll tell all the fish in this river about you, and next time you come, you won’t need to wait at all! They’ll jump into your net like they’re going to a party! You’ll be swimming in fish! You’ll be the fish whisperer! Think of the possibilities!" Ramesh thought about it for a moment. "Hmm… fish jumping into my net? That’s definitely something new. The little fish gave him an intense look. "Oh, trust me! You’ll have the best catch of your life. No more sitting around twiddling your thumbs. Just let me go, and I’ll make you the king of fishing!" Ramesh scratched his chin, then smiled. "Alright, alright, little fish, you’ve convinced me. With a tiny fishy grin, the fish darted back into the water swan away happily ‘NEVER TO COME BACK’, leaving Ramesh wondering if he had just made the best decision of his fishing career—or if he’d just let a tiny fish outsmart him. ﻿The next day, the poor fisherman arrived with high hopes, thinking the tiny little fish would magically turn into a whole school of fish, by bringing his other friends. But when he reached the spot where he'd left the fish, he was puzzled. The tiny little fish wasn't there nor his friends! But still with high hopes he tossed the net into the river water, and when he pulled his net back to his surprise there was a note in the water floating. It read: "Dear Fisherman, Thanks for yesterday, but I'm too clever to fall for that again. I have happily swan away never to come back - Your Tiny Fish" The fish with his cleverness saved his life from the fisherman. The Moral of the story is: - you have to be really clever to save your life, from such challenging moments.
author: Annissa Dmello
illustrator: Avika Pathak; Dolly Verma; Lê Thị  Bích Khoa; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Phạm  Thu Thùy; Sangeetha Kadur; Srikrishna Kedilaya; Subir Dey; Thulisizwe  Mamba; Trần Lưu  Đăng Nguyên

title: The Lost Kitten
text: One day, Mia found a tiny kitten in her garden. The kitten was white with little orange and black spots. The cat looked very hungry. Mia ran inside and told her mother," Mom I found a lost kitten! Can we help it?" Her mother smiled and said, "Of course! Let’s give it some milk." Mia gently picked up the kitten and placed it in a small basket. She poured some warm milk into a bowl. The kitten licked it up happily. We should find its owner," Mia said. She made a small sign that read, "Lost Kitten Found!" and placed it near their gate. The next morning, a little boy named Sam came running. "That's my kitten, Whiskers!" he cried. Thank you, Mia!" he added. Mia felt warm and happy inside. She waved as Sam and Whiskers walked home.Her mother hugged her and said, "Helping others is a wonderful thing, Mia." From that day, Mia knew that kindness always made the world a better place. MORAL: ALWAYS BE KIND
author: 43 Jasline Rodrigues
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Karen Lilje Lilje; Lindy  Pelzl; Mary Anne Hampton; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Shailja Jain Chougule; Shirish  Ghatge; Tanvi Bhat

title: THE MISSING BUFFALO
text: In a small village, Granny Lila had a beloved buffalo named Rani. Every morning, Rani would graze near the river and return home by sunset. But one evening, Rani didn’t come back. Granny Lila grew worried. She searched the nearby fields and called out Rani’s name, but the buffalo was nowhere to be found. The next morning, Granny Lila decided to visit the village police station. With trembling hands, she filled out a missing buffalo report. She described Rani’s dark brown coat, the small white patch on her forehead, and her gentle eyes. The kind police officer assured Granny Lila they would help. The villagers also joined the search. After hours of looking, they finally found Rani in a neighbor’s field, happily munching on fresh grass. She had wandered off and gotten lost. Granny Lila hugged Rani and smiled with relief. She thanked the villagers and the police for their help. From then on, she tied a small bell around Rani’s neck—so she could always hear her buffalo, even if she wandered far.
author: Alisha  FY

title: MY DOG
text: One day mama,papa,dada and dadi having dinner. I just came there with a problem I asked papa..... ''why that dog barking at you when you were buying milk??''...... this is not a good behaviour towards others. You only told me this when I shouted at my friend yesterday. eveyone laughs at me hahaha....... ''shibu let me explain.'' said dadi. title: Am I Brave or Not?
text: 9 year old Sukanya peeked from under her sleeping bag. Her eyes wandered to the giant Honne tree. At night, its branches swayed and looked like the arms of a giant monster. She squeezed her eyes shut. Just this morning, Sukanya had reached the beautiful, quiet Honnemaradu (“Golden Lake”) for a camp with her classmates, teachers and volunteers. Seeing the endless blue water and feeling the cool breeze, she exclaimed, “I want to live here forever”. But as the night crept in…she wasn’t so sure anymore. It was too dark and the faint sound of water in the lake made her feel as if a ferocious crocodile was wading towards her. “Are there lions in this jungle?”, she imagined an enormous hungry lion in the dark. She searched for a happy memory to distract her. The big, excited eyes of Vishal Anna, a camp volunteer, came to her mind. During their train ride here, he shared, “Children will set up and run this camp. Volunteers will be there to take care of you. We will swim, trek and coracle. ” “Who wants to do solo camping?”, he asked. “What is that?” Monu, a tiny, energetic 8 year old boy, asked. “During solo camping, you will make your own food and sleep alone in your sleeping bags for one night.”, Vishal Anna explained. “Alone! At night!”, said Monu and laughed. “Sukanya is scared to even play hide and seek in school, I don't think she can sleep alone at night." Realizing that Monu was teasing her again, Sukanya jumped up and said with great courage, “I will! I am an adventurer on the island.” But, at night, the horror stories that her aunt narrated, came into her mind. Maybe Monu and the others were right, “I am a coward”. But Vishal Anna had said that she was very brave to want to do solo camping. That confused her. “Am I brave? Or not?”, she wondered. “If I can spend this night alone in the sleeping bag, I can tell everyone that I am BRAVE.”, Sukanya thought. “That will also keep Monu quiet.”, she smiled, pleased with the image of Monu with zipped up lips that came to her mind. Sukanya counted the stars- some twinkling bright, some fading behind the clouds. “That small group of stars look like a rabbit, and the one far away looks like a tiny jewel”, she thought. Soon, her eyes started feeling heavy and she drifted off into a deep sleep. “Chirp, Chirp”. Sukanya exclaimed, “It’s morning! I did it!”. She hurriedly pulled herself out of the sleeping bag and danced excitedly. She couldn’t wait to tell Monu, Vishal Anna and her friends. She saw someone sitting near the lake... It was Vishal Anna. She announced, slightly out of breath, “Anna! I am brave!” Vishal Anna smiled at her and said “Of course, you are. You are one of the bravest people I know.” He hugged Sukanya and she felt extremely happy. The next weekend, when Sukanya was travelling alone from her boarding school to home, she was afraid, but told herself, “I will try and not give up.” By the time she was 14 years old, Sukanya started travelling all by herself in the big city of Bangalore. Her younger siblings looked at her in awe and asked, “Don’t you feel scared?” Sukanya said, “I feel scared, but I just remember that I am brave too. Whenever I am able to do something which scares me, I feel stronger." "You can be brave too as I am always there for you; just like Vishal Anna was there for me.”, Sukanya told her siblings. They smiled at each other, feeling loved.
author: Saba Ahmad

title: How the Zebra Got it's Stripes?
text: It was a sunny morning, the sky was bright and crystal clear. The joyous chirps of the birds, the buzzing of the busy bees and the sound of running water filled the forest. It was a peaceful day. "Catch me if you can!" yelled the Baboon. "Here, I come!" replied the Zebra. The Zebra bolted across the field, ready to catch the Baboon. BAM! It crashed into a tree. "OUCH! It hit my head!" said the Zebra. Slowly, both of them started laughing. You see, the Zebra and the Baboon were really close friends. They were as close as two peas in a pod! The Zebra got up and said, "Let's meet at your house this evening." The Baboon nodded cheerfully and both of them returned home. I am a Zebra Exactly at 5 'o' clock, the Zebra started walking towards the Baboon's house. When it arrived, it noticed that the door of the house was already opened. Curious the Zebra walked inside to find the house deserted. Baffled it walked out and noticed some footprints on the soil. "These seem familiar," thought the Zebra. It started following the footprints when it heard a sound. It was more of a whimper. It slowly crawled closer and hid behind a bush. A tiger had imprisoned the Baboon! A shiver ran down it's spine. The most daring animal of the forest had caught it's best friend! It was struck speechless, seeing the situation. It had to do something, but what? Suddenly the Zebra had an idea! What is the only thing that tigers are afraid of? Yes, it is fire! FIRE!!! The Zebra took two rocks and rubbed it against each other. But nothing happened at first until a tiny spark of light appeared. In a matter of seconds it turned into a huge fire. The Zebra immediately transferred the fire to the wooden stick and bravely stood in front of the the tiger. As soon as the tiger saw the fire, it ran away! "Whew! That was a lot of work." said the Zebra in relief. As soon as the Baboon saw Zebra it's face lit up with joy. Happily the Baboon came running towards the Zebra forgetting the fire stick that it was carrying. Within seconds the stick fell on the Zebra. "Oh no!" cried the Baboon. The Zebra toppled to the ground due to the fatigue and woke up after some time to see the Baboon laughing at it. Confused, the Zebra went to the nearby pond and saw it's reflection. It was covered in stripes! THE END
author: Anousha Bouthika

title: The Gift Of Nothing
text: We all love celebrating our birthday and unwrapping gifts is even more fun and exciting right?.. So was Max, excited and ready to celebrate his birthday with his friends and family. But there he was thinking about what gifts he would get on his birthday. Max had been counting down the days to his birthday for weeks. The anticipation filled him with excitement as he imagined all the wonderful presents he might receive. Perhaps a shiny new toy, a fun board game, or even a big red bicycle. His mind buzzed with possibilities, and he could hardly wait for the celebration to begin. T he day finally arrived, Max was thrilled. His house was decorated with balloons, and the smell of birthday cake filled the air. Friends and family gathered, each bringing brightly wrapped gifts. Max eagerly opened each present, delighting in the surprises inside. Then, his best friend, Lily, arrived, holding a small box wrapped in colorful paper. Max grinned as he took the gift, excited to see what she had gotten him. He carefully unwrapped the paper and lifted the lid of the box—only to find that it was EMPTY. Max frowned. "There's nothing in here, Lily." Lily beamed. "Exactly!" Max blinked, confused. "But... why would you give me NOTHING?" Lily sat beside him, with her eyes twinkling and she said, "Because sometimes, the best gifts aren't things. They're moments. Like when we laughed so hard last week that juice came out of your nose." Max giggled at the memory. "That was really funny." Lily nodded. "Or when we built that giant fort and pretended we were pirates." Max's eyes lit up. "That was the best adventure!" Lily smiled. "See? The best gifts aren’t in stores. They’re time, laughter and friendship." Max looked at the empty box again, then back at Lily. He began to understand. "So this box isn't really empty, is it?" Lily shook her head. "Nope. It's full of all the fun times we’ve had together. And all the new memories we’ll make." Max grinned. "This might be the best gift ever." For the rest of the day, Max and Lily played together, told stories, and laughed until their sides ached. They chased each other around the yard, imagined they were explorers on a daring mission, and even created a silly dance that had everyone laughing. The joy of their friendship filled the air, more valuable than any toy or game. That night, as Max got ready for bed, he placed the small box on his shelf. But to him, it wasn’t an empty box. It was a reminder- a treasure chest filled with memories, laughter, and the love of a dear friend. As the years passed, Max never forgot Lily’s special gift. Every birthday, he made sure to give someone else THE GIFT OF NOTHING - a simple box that symbolized the most valuable things in life: time spent together, laughter shared, and the joy of friendship. And each time he gave the gift, he saw the same confusion at first, followed by the same warm realization. Because in the end, the greatest gifts aren’t things at all. They are the moments we cherish, the love we share, and the memories that stay with us forever.:)
author: Neha Deshmukh

title: Gray and the floating log
text: Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a curious young girl named Gray. One day, while playing near the river, she saw a large log floating in the downstream. Curious gray decided to push the log and see what would happen. she placed her hands on the log and gave it a big push. To her surprise, instead of just moving the log, she felt herself moving backward! She almost fell but quickly caught her balance. "That was strange!" Gray said, looking at the log floating away. Her grandpa, who was fishing nearby, laughed. "Did you feel that, Gray? " Gray nodded. "Yes! I pushed the log, but it pushed me back. Why did that happen?" Grandpa smiled. "That is Newton’s Third Law of Motion. It means that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. When you pushed the log, it pushed you back with the same force." Gray’s eyes lit up. "Oh! So if I jump off a boat, the boat moves backward?" "Yes!" Grandpa said. "And when you swim, you push water backward, and the water pushes you forward. Even when you kick a ball, the ball pushes back on your foot!" Gray picked up a small rock and threw it into the river. As it hit the water, little ripples spread in all directions. "I see! Everything pushes back!" Grandpa nodded. "Yes, science is everywhere!" From that day, Gray started noticing Newton’s law everywhere. She had learned something amazing, and her curiosity only grew bigger! And so, Gray kept exploring, learning something new every day.
author: Manaki Jyothi

title: Khampai Becomes a Yaopa
text: “Remember, Khampai, to become perfect, one has to overcome the fear of making mistakes.” “I wish you were here, Apu.” “Apu, are you making yanshahbo again?” “Yes, I am. Come, I'll show you how it's made.” “This is nyahrih.” “When it is hot, it turns all soft and squishy, and you can shape it however you want.” “Remember, Khampai, to become perfect, one has to overcome the fear of making mistakes.” “My hands are experienced, because they have made enough mistakes.” “Remember, Khampai, to become perfect, one has to overcome the fear of making mistakes.” “One has to overcome the fear of making mistakes.” “Being a Yaopa is a privilege. I do this work with love for the people and the art. “You know, Khampai, Longwa is one of the only few villages where this art is still alive. It connects us with the rest of the Konyaks.” “Apu, how does nyahrih become a golden metal?” “Nyahrih won’t turn into metal. However, it will help make the mould for brass casting.” “Once the design cools and hardens, we will cover it with clay formed from a mixture of sand aggregate and ash… …then, we will bury it under the charcoal to heat.” “Apu, where is the ball I put inside!!?” “Hahaha, the fire ate it away. But don’t worry, it left behind the shape we need.” “We take the brass scraps and put them in the pot to melt them.” “Once the brass scraps melt, we will pour the molten brass into the moulds to fill its hollow cavities.” “Move away further Khampai......it can be dangerous to be too close.” “We’ll let the brass cool down and solidify before we break it.” “We’ll let the brass cool down and solidify before we break it.” “Tap the mould gently with the hammer to loosen the sand.” “What if I break it, Apu?” “Don’t worry, you won’t break it. Just gently hammer it open.” “It’s there, Apu! My marble has turned go lden. It’s magic! You are a magician!” “The show isn’t over yet. The edges need to be smooth.” “Now the show is complete.” “I miss you so much, Apu.” “I hope I can keep your magic alive.”
author: Longang  Luklem

title: A gift from God
text: John didn't want to go to school today. Yesterday's humiliation still stung. John was from a poor family. He and his mom lived in a small house in a village. On his way back home from school, while leaping over the rickety fence of his home, the already worn fabric of his school pant had ripped. He asked his mom if she can buy him a new one. His mother, with a sad heart, tired hands and a loving smile, stitched it and said, "Dear, I'll buy you a new one next year, for now I have stitched it and see you can't even tell! " That day in school, while playing football with his friends, the stitches gave away, a long, jagged tear exposed his thin leg. The laughter of his classmates echoed in his ears. He felt humiliated and tears welled up. He mumbled, "God please give me a new pair of pants" a desperate plea from his heart. He told his mom what had happened, his eyes red from crying. She comforted him and having no other choice, stitched it again neatly. She assured him that she'll buy him a new one as soon as possible. The next day, when the school bell rang, he picked up his bag to go home. His worn bag felt heavier than usual. He put his bag down and opened it to check. There it was! A neatly folded, brand-new uniform pant lay inside, crisp and clean. A wave of disbelief washed over him, his eyes widened, followed by an explosion of joy. He grabbed the pants, jumped with joy, his voice bubbling with excitement. " I knew! I knew God would give me! " Behind the classroom door, Mr. Anand, his teacher, smiled. He had witnessed the previous day's ordeal, the cruel laughter, and the child's silent tears. He had quietly purchased a new pair of pants, slipping them into John's bag. The pure, unadulterated joy radiating from John was a reward in itself. Mr. Anand's heart swelled with warmth. He knew that sometimes, "God's gifts" came through the hands of those who cared, a silent act of kindness that could transform a child's world.
author: Ann P.

title: The Little Bakery of Dreams
text: Emma’s tiny bakery sat at the corner of Maple Street, filled with the scent of warm cinnamon rolls and fresh bread. She had opened it with nothing but a dream and a handful of family recipes. One dark evening, a young boy named Oliver hesitated outside her shop, his nose pressed against the glass. Emma noticed his tattered coat and the longing in his eyes. Smiling, she opened the door. “Come in, dear,”she said, handing him a warm chocolate croissant. His eyes widened. “But I have no money. Emma knelt beside him. “Kindness is never a debt.It’s an investment in someone’s happiness.” From that day on, Oliver visited daily, learning to knead dough and decorate cakes. As years passed, he grew into a talented baker,he left the town to open his own bakery. 3 years later one morning, Emma found an envelope on the counter. Inside was a key and a note "Dreams shared are dreams fulfilled. This bakery i openend is yours now, just as you once your own bakery with me. Love, Oliver." Tears filled her eyes. She had given kindness, and it had returned tenfold. She couldnt help but be reminded of the nostalagic memories she had when oliver as a small boy started working with her.She will cherish him forever. "A single act of kindness can echo through lifetimes. Never underestimate the power of a good heart."
author: Naeritya Chandola

title: I Am Not a Cat
text: I am not a cat.” “Oh, then who are you?” Meow Meow Meow Meow Meow Meow “I am a LION!” “Wow! What does a lion say?” The two lions walked down the road. There, they saw Jehan. Haaooon Haaaoooon Haaooon Haaoooon “Hello, lions,” said Jehan. “Arre, we are not lions or cats,” said Bir and Aaliya. “Then who are you?” asked Jehan. “We are goats.” “Wow, and what do goats say?” asked Jehan.
