title: The Summer Lesson
text: Alamelu and Keerthi were two interesting thirteen-year-old girls. Keerthi loved thrilling experiences and was extremely adventurous while Alamelu found peace amongst books and silence. They both were complete opposites but best friends. It was March, and all the students wer e busy writing their exams. But Keerthi's mind wandered somewhere else out of the question paper - her summer vacation! She couldn't wait to plan her vacation, forget about school for two entire months and enjoy her vacation somewhere far away from the sweaty city of Chennai. Little did she know two things- her friend Alamelu has been thinking about the same thing, and Keerthi has missed out to write the balanced equation in her science answer sheet! Oops! Soon before Keerthi and Alamelu knew it, April arrived and so did their summer vacations. Both girls decided to travel to and stay in Alamelu's family's ancestral house in Chidambaram with Alamelu's grandmother for their vacation. Alamelu was excited about spending her vacation in the completely serene environment of Chidambaram with books, whereas Keerthi was thrilled to get a chance to visit the mangrove forests of Pichavaram, a village near Chidambaram. After spending an entire day travelling from Chennai to Chidambaram, one thought lingered in the tired mind of Keerthi - when will she visit the mangrove forests of Pichavaram and ride a catamaran, and cruise amongst the mangroves? She had already imagined and pictured how the sight would be next day - small traditionally made catamarans floating in the mild pinkish - red water, tinted by the soft colors of sunrise in the early hours of the day, waiting to be picked by expert boatsman to take passengers and tourists for an early morning cruise around and through the dense and lush green mangrove forests. No one knew why Keerthi was so excited for a simple boat ride. But Alamelu knew the reason - it was for the adventure of course! A few days after their travel, Keerthi had finally convinced Alamelu's grandmother to take her and Alamelu to the mangrove forests in Pichavaram. The trio consisting of Keerthi, Alamelu and her grandmother set out early in the morning to the mangroves and arrived there early. Keerthi was stunned to see the view of the mangroves, which was better than what she had pictured. Suddenly, Alamelu's grandmother mildly shocked the girls by deciding to row the boat herself! As the trio progressed into entering the mangrove forest in a catamaran with their life jackets on, Alamelu demanded a story from her grandmother who was rowing the boat while Keerthi restlessly started scouting for something adventurous. But Alamelu's grandmother was having her focus fixed on the dark and puffy rain clouds that gathered around in the sky. And soon, it was raining, and the trio were at the middle of thick mangroves with no proper shelter. However clever Alamelu had packed umbrellas and towels for extra safety, which came handy for the drenched trio. Alamelu's grandmother anchored the catamaran and pulled over its wood hood to create a small shelter for her and the girls to take cover and dry themselves using the towels. Keerthi was brimming with excitement because the sudden rain amongst the mangroves, the dark skies, the unexplored wildlife and the journey that is unaccompanied by expert boatsmen meant that the three would be navigating an unknown terrain with just a compass and map that Alamelu packed coming handy, eating the lemon rice, gooseberries and millet cookies that Alamelu's grandmother packed. It was going to be an exciting adventure amongst the mangroves! Something that Keerthi has been wanting for days since she travelled to Chidambaram! After the trio had recovered from being drenched, they decided to wait until the rain reduced or stopped. Alamelu stated that the mangroves were similar to the backdrop of her current read, a book about a girl exploring and protecting nature and wildlife, while Keerthi suggested that all the three leave the catamaran and explore the mangroves and its wildlife to make the day more fun. Grandma, who wanted the girls to be safe, decided to distract them for a while by giving them some food to eat and a prompt that the girls both could ponder upon while she silently imparts a lesson through it. So, she offered them food she had brought and gave them the prompt. The girls ate the food while pondering about topic Grandma had given and listening to Grandma expressing her thoughts on the same. ''Imagine you are the sailor of a delicate paper boat, trying to sail in the huge ocean of life. Ocean has tides, waves, currents, storms, tsunamis and cyclones. Usually these are ecological conditions that are influenced by several natural factors such as the wind and tectonic plate movement. Our ocean of life also functions similarly. As the saying goes, ''A smooth sea never made a skilled sailor.'', the ocean of life always tests the boats and its sailors with rough cyclones, tsunamis and storms to ensure and build the resilience of the sailors. As a sailor who is assigned with a delicate paper boat that can get soaked and destroyed easily in the gentlest of the waves, you should think of innovative ways to help your paper boat cope up, while coming across a lot of failures in the process, building resilience.'' This is Grandma's narration Sailing in a paper boat through the vast ocean of life ''At first you would face several failures and come across tough challenges and situations but as you progress further you would gain more experience, confidence and valuable life lessons that would help you navigate through future hardships and struggles. Similar to how a sailor has to shortly handle turbulent weather while sailing through the rough seas to gain proper expertise, the ocean of life briefly challenges you and develops your ability to solve problems, handle tough situations, develop versatile life skills and effectively cope up with hard emotions and feelings to strengthen you as a human being. All the experience, values, confidence and lessons that you have gained in the journey exhibit the true value of you, the sailor, who is exploring the ocean of life in a frail boat '' Sailing in a paper boat through the vast ocean of life This is Grandma's narration As Alamelu's grandmother finished talking about her prompt on the topic of ''Sailing in a paper boat through the vast ocean of life'', both Alamelu and Keerthi had imbibed the lesson that they both had received from Grandma. The girls were reminded and impressed how wise, affectionate and innovative Grandma could get to teach the girls one of the most unforgettable lessons of their life about life itself, which surprisingly had been presented as a simple topic of group discussion! After a while, the rain had stopped, and the trio reached the shore and their house safely. Furthermore, the girls went on to spend a memorable vacation with Grandma by visiting places in and around Chidambaram and having several small adventures together learning more lessons with their favourite Grandma!
author: AKSHARA BALAJI
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Jean de Wet; Kalyani Naravane; Karunya Baskar; Maithili  Joshi; Musonda  Kabwe; Nivong  Sengsakoun; Rae  Zachariah; Sarthak Sinha

title: Cheeku's Cleverness
text: They all worked hard and lived happily. After some days the summer season started. From some other place a wolf entered the jungle. The wolf was very dangerous and cruel. He would kill and eat the small animals of the jungle. One day Cheeku and his friends were playing, Suddenly the bad wolf came there. All the rabbits started running away on seeing him but the mean wolf caught Cheeku's friend Meeku. The wolf killed and ate up Meeku, seeing this Cheeku got very angry and vowed to teach the bad wolf a lesson. All night Cheeku couldn;t sleep and kept thinking of ways to teach the mean wolf a lesson. Finally he came up with an idea. The next day Cheeku went to visit his friend Chunky the monkey and told him his plan. Chunky was happy to hear Cheeku's plan and immediately went to the city and came back with blue paint. Next Cheeku went to see his sister and told her everything. His sister agreed to support Cheeku's plan. Cheeku painted his sister with blue paint who became blue from white colour. Then Chunky the monkey spread the word in the entire jungle that a blue fairy had come to Cheeku's house who has come from the sky. This news spread in the whole jungle like wild fire and all animals started running towards Cheeku's house to see the blue fairy. On hearing this news even the evil wolf came to Cheeku's house. Outside Cheeku's house the crowd of animals collected and then when the wolf also came Cheeku's sister said. "I have come from the sky and I have been sent to serve the strongest animal here, whomsoever will eat me will be crowned the king of the heavens." Hearing this the wolf started drooling and was very happy and said "O, blue fairy, in this small jungle all small and weak animals live. I am the only strong animal here so it should be my privilege to eat you." Hearing this the blue fairy said," O king wolf,only you can eat me but before that you need to dive in the nearby well and then you can eat me." The wolf got greedy on hearing this and immediately without thinking jumped in the well. The well was quite deep and the wolf drowned in it and died. All the animals were very happy to see the dead wolf and picked up Cheeku and his sister and started dancing. This is how Cheeku's clever thinking saved all the animals from the dangerous,cruel and mean wolf.
author: jyoti Tandon Garg
illustrator: Abhra Sengupta; Ajit Narayan; Chamath Prasanga Lokuliyana; Khyati Singh; Shekh Raisuddin Quraishi; Wiehan de Jager

title: The hunt for flowers
text: Every year on her birthday her parents would give her a gift. Her mother had started making a feather hat for her birthday and her father had said he woud get her a singing bird. Sona wanted to surprise her mother on her birthday with a gift. Her mother loved flowers. On her mother's birthday Sona woke up early in the morning and ventured into the jungle to look for flowers. Near a river yellow flowers were blooming. Sona was happy to see and was just about to break the flowers when a voice rang out from behind her - "stop." Sona looked back and saw a wolf standing there. He came closer and said, "break the flowers later, first tell me how do you people clean your teeth? For the last six days I am suffering from tooth pain." Sona was overcome with shame. Her parents cleaned their teeth with a tree twig, but Sona never cleaned her teeth. She said slowly - " I don't know." The wolf got angry on hearing this and growled - "Go away from here right now. If you break even one flower I will teach you a good lesson." Sona walked ahead and came upon a hill surrounded by blue flowers, Sona got ready to break the flowers when a voice rang out from behind her-"stop." Sona saw a lion standing there. His neck hair were all tangled up and there was mud on them. The lion asked Sona - "How do you untangle your hair, tell me." Sona could not reply to the lion's question. She had never untangled her own hair. Her mom always used to do it. The lion said - "if you cannot help me don't touch the flowers." Poor Sona walked ahead. Soon enough she came upon a pond surrounded by red flowers. Sona had never seen such bright red flowers. Sona was even happier than before and was about to break the flowers when she saw a huge crocodile and got scared. The crocodile opened his wide jaw and said - "listen girl, my daughters want to play human games. You teach them how to sweep and light a stove and i will give you many red flowers." But Sona didn't know how to sweep or light a stove, but before the crocodile could scold her she walked ahead. Morning turned into afternoon. Sona was tired from walking. She was hungry also. But she didn't want to go back home without the flowers. After walking for a long time she came upon a place full of white and pink flowers and there were juicy fruits on the trees. Sona leapt towards the flowers but a little monkey held her hand and said, "Didibreak the flowers later, first teach me how to read. The little monkey called her didi but how to teach him to read? She didn't know how to, Suddenly Sona started crying and kept crying till........ her parents came looking for her and found her.
author: jyoti Tandon Garg

title: That 100 rupees that touched the heart
text: There is a high mountain in Kashmir. It is freezing there The mountain passes like a wind. There is an ATM near that mountain. An army officer comes there every day! His name is Arvind sir Every day he comes to the ATM, and withdraws just one hundred rupees. Then he leaves with a smile. There is a grandmother guarding that ATM. Her name is Kannama Bhatti. She was surprised. “Why is it like this, a hundred rupees a day?” she wondered. One day, my grandmother asked, “Why, sir, do you only take a hundred rupees every day? You can take that too in one day! Aravind sir smiled. “I am not for money, Grandma…” He said slowly, “I will send a message to my wife…” “She gets a message saying, ‘Rs. 100 has been withdrawn from your account. ’ That message is a relief for her… A small joy of ‘My husband is alive!’” Grandma's eyes were troubled. Arvind sir is not just a player... A man with a big heart! Arvind sir went… Into the snow-covered mountains. The snow could not stop his mind. Jai Hind! This is a story that will inspire children and instill a sense of patriotism.
author: Suresh Kumar G

title: The Sky Is My Canva
text: I drew a purple flower, It dances in the hour. I drew a blue ball It's big and won't fall. I drew a green leaf, It shows me peace. I drew a yellow sun, It's warmer than a bun. I drew an orange carrot, gave it to a rabbit. I drew a red apple, It sat on the table. I drew a red apple, It sat on the table.
author: Shreya Awasthy

title: Four Friends
text: One day a fox named Fuzz was crossing the jungle.She saw an owl with a broken wing. The owl was about to fall down. Fuzz helped the owl by making a soft nest for the owl to land safely on the ground. The owl is hurt. I must help him. The owl got better and Fuzz and the owl became friends. On the way they met a raccoon. The raccoon was hungry and didn't have anything to eat. Then Fuzz and the owl found some fruits that they gave to the raccoon to eat. I am hungry but I can't reach the apples. We will get them for you The next day the owl, Fuzz the fox and the raccoon continued their journey. Suddenly they heard a sound, it was another owl who had got scared of the rustling sound of the leaves. They reassured the owl there was nothing to be scared of. Then they all became friends. Now we know the story of the four friends, so let's hear one of their adventures. They venture into a bear's cave. The bear gets angry and the four friends start looking for a way out of the cave. Wait look! It's not a bear, it's a teddy bear! Thank you! Have a Happy day!
author: jyoti Tandon Garg

title: Golden Gulmohar
text: It's the season of Gulmohar again. The green trees decorated with bright red, blooming flowers amidst the scorching Sun, the dazzling season of summer. Yet, Gulmohar gives so much happiness to me and fill my heart with red richness. Flowers of all colours are a delight to look at, however, there is something so simple yet breathtaking about Gulmohar that I am unable to stop myself from looking at the blooming tree, over and over......back and forth...back and forth!! I think that if I can pick, not pluck, the beautiful flowers then I will surely make a strong pyramid out of them. Can they survive the test of times....like the Great Pyramids of Egypt. My teacher said that they were made ages ago, yet they stand tall...and live loooong!!!! I know that my dream of Flower Pyramid will never become a reality, but I want my Gulmohar to live a lifetime of ages in the short span of time given by God. I want the butterflies to suck the nectar.......... and make honey out of it. When they will make Honey out of it, then it will live on like the Great Pyramids....for ages. My mother told me that Honey is also known as Liquid Gold.... and Gold Stays Forever!!!! My dearest Gulmohar, you make me happy every year.... And that is why, I want you to live looooong!!!!! Let the bees help us out and you live long...transforming into A Beautiful Golden Entity!!!!
author: BHARTI PANWAR
illustrator: Angie & Upesh; Jayasudha  Bhaskaran; Kishor Joshi; Malvika Tewari; Maryam Kakar; Poornima  Chander; Suvidha  Mistry

title: The Heart of our Home
text: "The smell of pithas made during every Bihu season in our kitchen takes me back to many memories." Biswajit Thakuria Assamese, Assam "No matter how busy we are throughout the day, dinner is the one meal we share together as a family in the kitchen.” Chorovelu Ringa Chakhesang & Angami, Nagaland "The first thing I do when I come home is to enter the kitchen and the last thing I do when I leave home is to enter the kitchen. Kitchen always reassures me of the warmth of my family." H.A Sothing Shimray Tangkhul Tribe, Manipur “Our kitchen is the heart of our home; its hearth brings warmth to our family.” Longang Luklem Konyak Tribe, Nagaland Rildong serves the warmth of broth, enriching the flavour of the rich heritage of the Himalayas. Best known for making “Sisnu and Dehro.” Tashi Chong Sherpa Sherpa Tribe, Sikkim “Kitchens are where life is shared with loved ones and bonds are formed with strangers.” Kemya Yanlem Konyak Tribe and Tangkhul Tribe, Nagaland “These kitchens are a source of a lot of good memories for me.” Moge Basar Galo Tribe, Arunachal Pradesh “The smoky aroma of Rabko, combined with the scent of Ane’s (Mother’s) daily cooking and her presence in the kitchen every early morning, is something I always long for.” Marba Kamki Galo Tribe, Arunachal Pradesh “My kitchen is my happy place, I feel happy when I cook, when I peel, and when I hear the sizzling sounds.” Chalini Basumatary Bodo Tribe, Assam “While most kitchens back home have now transitioned to a modern model, my earliest memory of going back to my village is of sitting by the Sauka (the earthen hearth) and waiting for the elders to make Sunga Pitha, a way of roasting rice inside hollow bamboo tubes.” Kasturi Dev Chaudhury Assamese, Assam “I remember the hymns, the stories, the groundnuts roasting in the khadai and the presence of my loved ones in cold winter evenings. The fireplace knows it all.” Niboli K Chophimi Sumi-Naga Tribe, Nagaland "The kitchen is the heart of the home. In a Mizo household, the 'tapchhak' connects food, love, and memories. Home-cooking, especially traditional recipes, is the ultimate expression of love." Joan Lalramngaihsangi Mizo Tribe, Mizoram “A friend once asked me where one should go in Manipur to truly experience the essence of the place. I told them, a kitchen in Manipur. Our kitchens are sacred spaces. Each community in Manipur has its own unique setting, but as a Meitei, no matter how modern our amenities become, we always dedicate a spot for Phunga Lairu, the hearth, where we believe our Indigenous deity, Emoinu, the goddess of wealth and prosperity, resides. For me, as a passionate cook, my kitchen is not just a place to prepare food, it’s my lab, a space where we gather as a family, discuss important matters, and ensure that it’s always stocked with essentials. The most important of them all? Ngari, the fermented fish, a true staple in our kitchen.” Potsangbam Linthoingambi Chanu Meitei Tribe, Manipur “Home is where my cat is, and my cat is always in the kitchen staring at the smoked meat hung by the fireplace.” Keneisenuo Solo Angami Tribe and Tangkhul Tribe, Nagaland “In the comforting bamboo house kitchen, where ashes drift and earthy scent uplift, I hear echoes of my childhood – Flames of mud oven infused with the aroma of food that shaped my earliest tastes, a space - where I first read and learned; where my earliest joys and achievements found their voice.” Thomas Malsom Hrangkhawl Tribe and Molsom Tribe, Tripura
author: SauraMandala Foundation

title: Meena's stories of childhood
text: Chapter 1 The Beginning Once upon a time, there lived a young girl named Meena who lived in the city of Gurugram in Haryana with her parents, grandparents and a younger sister Divya. Every year both the sisters went to meet their maternal grandparents and uncle aunt in Chandigarh in summer vacation. They always went with their mother and sometimes their father came. One such year, when they went on vacations, after a few days they got a huge surprise. After few days from the day when they reached till the last day they stayed there, the house was full of guests. When they reached, both of them were the only children to play with their uncle aunt and grandparents for the first few days but slowly the population of the house increased, and the space in the rooms got decreased. Let us all together explore the journey of the both sisters because this is just the beginning. Chapter 2 Two But Not Bored The summer vacation was just started but the naughtiness was at level 💯. Sometimes the elders played with them and sometimes they played with each other. Whenever they were not satisfied while playing inside, every evening they went to play outside with their friends & sometimes they went for shopping with their mother and aunt. Every day they followed a routine of playing, doing activities, watching television, eating, sleeping and sometimes to study. Divya was in class U.K.G so she just got the holiday homework of playing, making drawing and craft and as Meena was in class 5th, she got a lot of work but the good reason was that she enjoyed doing those things.Another good reason was that their mother and aunt were expert in craft so they helped the children a lot. Sometimes they went to the temple and to buy fruits and vegetables when the sellers came in the street with their grandmother or aunt while their mother worked at home. Many times they went to the park with all their friends and grandmother. Whenever they were bored they had only one excuse 'Aunt you never play with us, mother and grandmother will do the work but you only play with us, please.' Whenever they asked their uncle, aunt or mother, they always said ' No, we have work to do ' but their grandmother always answered yes. Sometimes their uncle asked ' I am going out for work and I'll also go to the market. Will someone like to join? ' and both of them answered yes. Their grandfather was a police officer, and whenever he had a holiday on weekends or he came back early, he played with them or took them for a ride on the bike. Soon, they got to know that their cousins were coming, they completed their work in hurry. After that, Meena asked their mother ' Mummy, why are we not going to any exciting place as we came here many days ago?' Then mother answered' Meena, we are not going anywhere because we are planning that when your cousins will come, we will all go together. Till that day complete your work' she continued and both kids agreed. Till the guests came, Meena & Divya completed their work and were ready for adventure. Chapter 3 Shivani Didi's Rules It was time for the guests to arrive. Shivani, Raghu, Krishna and Anand came with their mothers. Meena and Divya were delighted to see their brothers and sisters. Krishna was the youngest sister among all of them. Meena and Divya were not worried that if whenever they went out to visit few places and came home late, they were not able to complete their work. ' Completing your work before playing also has many reasons ' said Shivani in an experienced way. Shivani was the eldest sister Everyone was excited to know the reasons and Divya said ' Didi, please tell us what are the reasons'. Then Shivani took out a rulebook from her bag and showed them. The page read - Advantages are - 1 If you quickly do your work before, you will get much time after. 2 You will get extra time to explore. 3 You will not be in a hurry on the last day. After seeing this, both the sisters were overjoyed as they saved a lot of time by completing their work before. While the children were talking, Krishna and Raghu 's mother was calling them. She was saying ' Children, you can play after having your lunch.' All of them went to the dining area for having their lunch. After having their tasty lunch, Raghu said 'I think that we should take a nap now'. Shivani said 'Yes, it's also written in my book and has many reasons too'. Everyone was excited to learn more rules. She took out the book and showed it to them. Again, the page was full of new rules which were interesting and easy to remember. They read and read and read until the words were sitting in their mind. Shivani didi read out the rules for Divya and Krishna. Divya was 5 and Krishna was 4 years old, so they were not able to read difficult words. Then after reading the rules, Anand asked 'Shivani, from where do you get the idea of writing many rules and making a book for them?' Shivani giggled and answered 'Brother, actually this is my holiday homework and I told you all the rules of completing work before,but I missed one point '. Meena excitedly answered 'If we complete our work before, we can use it, especially, if it is a utility item'. Everyone thought for a while and then Anand said 'Yes, this fact is also true.Once I also got a homework to make a pen stand and I made it on the first day of vacation and when my old pen stand broke, I used the one I made' he continued. Then everyone started telling their stories and soon half an hour passed. A sound came from the other room'Now you children sleep' their aunt said. All three mothers and their aunt were talking in the other room but soon everyone was dreaming. Shivani told Meena that it's the first day for cousins but I will tell you new rules every day. Chapter 4 Time For Shopping 🛍️ It was evening time and the children woke up.The afternoon nap made them all feel fresh and energetic. Meena's mother and aunt went to the kitchen.Krishna's mother went out in the kitchen garden to bring vegetables.Raghu's mother was cleaning the floor and their grandmother went to the milk shop to buy milk and curd. Their uncle was going to the market and he asked the children 'Would someone like to come?' All the kids were overjoyed and they were ready to go with him. They took 20 minutes to get ready and 10 minutes just to say their mothers good bye. When they reached, it was 5:30pm and they had time only till 6:30pm. First of all, they went to the grocery store because their uncle had to buy some things for home and all the children were looking for snacks. Then,after buying a lot of stuff, they went to a toy shop.Near the shop, their was another shop in which their uncle had some work, so when he was doing the work the children were buying toys and stationary. Meena and Shalini were planning to do arts and craft so they bought some brushes, paint and stickers because other things were at home. Divya and Krishna chose three soft toys and Raghu and Anand were ready with toy cars. It was a big bill and when their mothers saw the bill,they scolded the kids because they wasted a lot of their uncle's money, but their uncle was not bothered, instead he was happy because the kids were happy. At home, before the kids came, their aunt did craft because she enjoyed it in free time but when the kids came, she enjoyed playing with them. So she gave Meena and Shivani her stationary and said 'Whenever I'm free, I'll do this with you.' They both agreed and took the stationary to their room and kept it in one of the room's cupboard. It was 7pm and their uncle forgot to bring bread and cheese but both the things were sold in different stores so Meena and Anand went to buy bread and Shivani and Raghu went to buy cheese. They bought it on time and gave it to their aunt. Meena's mother and aunt were cooking dinner and Anand's mother was washing dishes. After having their dinner, they went to sleep in their room, ready for tomorrow's adventures. Chapter 5 Tours And Guides (part 1) The kids woke up early in the morning and were ready to go to their first destination 'Maa Mansa Devi Mandir'. Chandigarh's biggest temple with games and carnival inside. Raghu was the first one to wake up and when he was in washroom, Meena woke up. After everyone was ready, they had their breakfast and were in the car. After half an hour long journey, they reached the temple. All the kids were excited and quickly ran inside. There they saw a statue of Durga maa killing the evil monster. Then they saw statues of many other gods and goddesses. Then they went in a huge building where langar (food given in temples) was served. After having a heart and stomach filling lunch,they were all energetic. They quickly ran in the carnival. All the kids were given 100 rupees each to buy their favourite thing. Meena and Shalini ran towards a shop of jewellary. There they bought two same necklaces, bracelets but two different rings. Divya and Krishna bought toy phones, teddy bears and board games. Anand and Raghu bought toy car and had a costly ride which was of no use. They thought that it would be fun but when the ride was going to start, they got to know that it was a ride for the youngest kids like Krishna and Divya and the ride was very slow. Then they went to the park and after some time they were in the car. Soon they reached home and went towards the bed for an afternoon nap. They woke up at 4:30pm and went in the dining area to have their evening snacks and milk. After some time they were ready for going to the park and play. They played in the park for one and a half hour and came home at 7:30pm. Then they had their dinner and went to sleep. The next morning they got to know that they were going to the bird sanctuary in the early afternoon. They had a lot of time so Meena and Divya's mother told the kids to study. After completing their work all the children started playing and Meena and Shalini went to do craft with their aunt. Soon it was time for them to get ready and soon they were in the car. It was a short journey, and it was a beautiful place. The gates were decorated by paintings and flowers. After admiring the beauty of the gate, they went inside and clicked pictures with statues, trees and birds. In one of the tent, their was a long line. The children curiously went inside and saw that a man with a colorful and beautiful bird was standing their. The bird was sitting on the hand of people who were in the line. The children insisted their parents for this. It was a bit painful to keep the bird on hand and it was very difficult for children to control the pain for long so that they can get a photo clicked. After some time they all were hungry and they went to the canteen in the sanctuary. After eating some light snacks, they went outside the sanctuary and bought cotton candy and popcorn. There they enjoyed a horse ride too. Then they reached home in evening at 6:15pm. Everyone decided to order food from outside and after having the dinner, the children decided to watch a movie on the laptop. Then they went to sleep. Chapter - 6 Tours and guides (Part 2) They started travelling after waiting for 4 days. They waited for 4 days because Anand got hurt on his right leg and Krishna was not well. Then in the morning, Meena said 'Mummy, I want to go to the Rock garden'. Her mother decided that they would go to the garden. Then in the late morning, at 11:00, they were all in the car. Soon they reached the destination and the children quickly hopped out of the car and ran inside the big gate. They passed through the stones, saw the flowing water and had a 'Rock puppets' ride. They enjoyed and ate in the canteen which was there only. Then they went back home, played, had their dinner and went to sleep. They travelled a lot for many days, played together, played with their uncle and aunt and enjoyed spending time together. Soon it was the last day and they thought to be at home. The children were getting bored so their uncle took them all for a swimming class. They went there in morning and came back after 2 hour. Then they had the lunch and went to watch T.V. Then in the evening they had milk and snacks and went to park. They played and came back after 2 hours. Then they had the dinner and started talking and after a lot of talks they went to sleep. The next morning they went to their homes. They enjoyed, played, talked and explored together.
author: Anisha Yadav
illustrator: Alankrita Amaya; Catherine Groenewald; Huynh Thi  Kim Lien; Marion  Drew; Mohith O; Noyonika Banerjee; Pallavi Sinha; Rijuta Ghate; Shreya  Falcao; Thansing Verma; Upamanyu  Bhattacharyya

title: Title: Nani's Cooking Competition
text: One sunny afternoon, Nani decided to enter the neighborhood cooking competition, claiming she had the secret recipe to make the world’s best “Aloo Tikki”. Nanu, ever the skeptic, raised an eyebrow. “I’ve had your aloo tikki for 40 years. There’s no world record for it, Nani.” Radha and Arjun were excited to watch the chaos unfold, while Ram was already on standby for the snacks. Nani was determined. “Watch and learn, people. This is how the experts cook.” She threw ingredients into the pan like a tornado. A pinch of this, a dash of that… and a whole bottle of mustard (by accident). Nanu watched nervously. “I think you’ve confused your spices with your cleaning supplies.” Radha whispered to Arjun, “Is that a cleaning liquid bottle in her hand?” Arjun grinned, “Maybe she’s cooking clean food this time.” After 45 minutes, the Aloo Tikkis were ready. Nani proudly presented her creation. The judges took a bite... and immediately ran for the water jug. Ram, looking disappointed, muttered, “This is not the kind of spicy I signed up for.” Nani shrugged, “It’s a new recipe. Just needs some getting used to!” The moral of "Nani's Cooking Competition" is: "Confidence is great, but double-checking your ingredients is even better!"
author: Lavin Patel

title: The Wise Farmer and the Greedy Neighbor
text: In the peaceful village of Sunderpur, nestled between green hills and flowing rivers, lived an old farmer named Hari. He owned a small piece of land where he grew vegetables, fruits, and flowers. Hari was known for his kindness, honesty, and wisdom. Every villager respected him, not because he was rich, but because he was fair and helpful. Right next to Hari’s land lived a man named Gopal. He was younger, but unlike Hari, he was known for being greedy. Gopal always tried to find ways to earn more without putting in much effort. He saw Hari’s small farm flourishing with crops and often wondered how such an old man could manage everything so well. One day, Gopal approached Hari while he was planting marigolds near the edge of his field. “Uncle Hari,” Gopal said, pretending to smile, “You are truly a magician! Look at your land. Everything grows so beautifully. What is your secret?” Hari smiled gently and replied, “There’s no magic, son. Just love the land, work hard, and be patient. Nature gives back what you give to it.” Gopal nodded, but inside, he thought, “That’s too slow. There must be an easier way.” The next morning, Gopal noticed a shiny silver box near a mango tree on Hari’s farm. Curious, he waited until Hari left for the market and then sneaked onto the field to inspect it. He opened the box and to his surprise, found a small sack of shining golden seeds. The seeds sparkled in the sunlight and gave off a faint warmth. “Golden seeds?” Gopal whispered. “No wonder his plants grow so well! These must be magical seeds.” Unable to resist temptation, Gopal quickly grabbed half the seeds and ran home. That evening, he planted them secretly in his backyard, thinking he would soon have the most beautiful crops in the village. Meanwhile, when Hari returned and found some seeds missing, he sighed. He knew someone had taken them but said nothing. Instead, he continued to care for his plants like he always did. Days passed, and Gopal waited eagerly. But instead of golden crops, thorny weeds began to grow where he had planted the seeds. They spread rapidly and started damaging his entire garden. Panicked, Gopal tried to remove them, but the more he pulled, the faster they grew. After a week, his garden was completely ruined. No vegetables, no flowers—just sharp, stubborn thorns. He ran to Hari’s house and confessed everything. “Uncle Hari, I took some of your golden seeds thinking they were magical. But they destroyed my garden! Please forgive me and help me fix this.” Hari looked at Gopal calmly and said, “Those seeds are not ordinary, Gopal. They were a gift from my grandfather. They grow only in the soil of honesty and care. When planted with greed, they become weeds of destruction.” Gopal hung his head in shame. “I’m sorry. I thought I was being clever, but I was only being greedy.” Hari placed a kind hand on his shoulder. “The land teaches us everything. Be patient, work hard, and respect what you have. That’s the real magic.” Gopal learned his lesson. He cleared his field and asked Hari to teach him the right way to farm. Slowly, under Hari’s guidance, Gopal’s land began to bloom again—not with golden seeds, but with honest effort. Years later, Gopal became one of the best farmers in Sunderpur, not because he used magic, but because he had learned the value of truth, patience, and hard work. And whenever new farmers came to the village asking for secrets of farming, Gopal would smile and say, “There are no shortcuts in life. The seed you plant is not just in the soil, but in your heart.” Moral of the Story: Greed leads to destruction, but honesty, hard work, and patience always yield true success.
author: taufiq pathan

title: The unique project
text: Tandon Garg Sunita was very upset for many days. She was the class monitor. For a few days a weird incident was taking place. When all the kids went out of the class for the morning prayer any kid's lunch would get stolen. Someone would steal any kid's lunch and leave the empty lunch box. All the kids were very upset. When the class teacher Miss Amina came to know about this she gave the responsibility to Sunita to found out the culprit. Sunita made a plan. She decided she will not go to the prayer hall for a day or two. Instead she would hide in the class and catch the thief. Sunita had a suspicion about Meera. Meera used to come late to school these days and she also came late to the prayer hall. Meera was from a poor family. A few days ago she had taken admission in the school. She was good in studies. Principal madam was very kind. On Meera's mother's insistence she had agreed to reduce Meera"s school fees by half. Anyways as Sunita had doubts about Meera being the lunch thief, she couldn't prove anything without proof. So the next day Sunita hid behind the Class door during the morning prayer and started waiting for Meera. After sometime Sunita saw Meera entering the class. She kept her bag and then looked around. Then she quickly opened a few kid's bags and took out a parantha from one lunchbox and vegetables from another and kept it in her own lunch box. Then she kept the kids lunchboxes back in their bags. Sunita was watching everything. She didn't say anything. Meera went to the prayer hall. Sunita went and told Miss Amina everything. She didn't say anything to anyone else. The next day again Sunita hid behind the class door. She had asked Miss Amina to hide in the other class. Meera came in and started opening other kids bags. Sunita came out quickly and held Meera's hand and started calling out to the teacher. "Miss come fast." Miss Amina came running. Meera was caught stealing and she started crying. Miss Amina said, "Meera you know it is a bad habit to steal. For this you can be rustigated. I will tell Principal Madam everything. She will call your mother. Hearing this Meera started pleading and asking for forgiveness, "Miss please forgive me. I will not do this again." Seeing her crying like this Miss Amina felt sorry for her. She asked Meera why she steals other kid's food? Meera then said that she was from a poor family. Her father was very ill and her mother sew other people's clothes to meet the household expenses. She had two younger sister brothers. At home there was not enough to eat. Meera would get leftovers from her home to school. When she saw other kids having good food she also wanted to eat it. That is why she started stealing other kids food. Miss Amina got emotional and told Meera, "You are an intelligent student. Don't spoil your future by stealing. Study hard and your future will be bright. She told Sunita not to tell anyone. After that Miss Amina called all the kids of the class and said," Today I am giving all of you a unique project. I am making groups of five children each. The topic of the project is 'sharing,' each group every week will share their lunch with Meera. This project will continue for three months. At the end of three months each group will get a prize." All the kids were happy to hear this. From the next day all the kids started doing this. Miss Amina told principal madam everything. Principal madam praised Miss Amina. When Principal madam found out that Meera's mother was a good seamstress she called her and gave her a part time job to teach basic sewing to the kids. Seeing her good work she started getting the work to stitch the kids uniforms. Gradually Meera's family's economic condition started improving. Meera's father started getting good medical treatment and his health also started improving. The project had passed two months. Meera thanked principal madam, Miss Amina and all her classmates and said that she will now never steal anyone's lunch. With everyone's help her family has overcome tough conditions. She said she will share her lunch with her classmates and requested Miss Amina to end the project. Miss Amina ended the project and gave each kid a chocolate as a prize.
author: jyoti Tandon Garg

title: A wedding with applause
text: There was a good writer in that village. His name is Shankar Thatha. Shankar Dadha is very good at telling stories in a simple way. That is, he knows all the folk tales that his grandmother told him when he was little! He speaks at various special events and captivates everyone's hearts. He is not just a writer… A sweet speaker loved by the people, A good friend! The thoughts, actions, and dreams of the villagers are all Shankar Thatha is a master at creating stories. One day, while telling a story to the children gathered there, a little boy shouted, Grandpa! Grandpa! My grandmother said that your wedding was a “knock knock wedding.” Tell me about i t! To that, Shankar Datha said: My marriage was a simple marriage, meaning no dowry, no pomp, no big pavilion, no ear-piercing microphone set, quality food, none of the food went to waste that's how it happened my marriage, he said. In short, the wedding took place in the green ground of my house, without a temple, without any lavish expenses! Then everyone clapped their hands! "Tell me, Grandpa," the little boy's voice said, picking up speed. Shankar Dada remained silent for a while… Seeing the expressions on the faces of the others, Dada immediately said…… I…. Did I take the thali in my hand? It was then that everyone clapped their hands and cheered. Thinking that this was a good time for us, I immediately tied the talisman. He said happily to the bride who was nearby. There was no Vedas that day! The sound of clapping was the only auspicious sound! The only auspicious sound!… This is my simple wedding!” Do you understand? The little boy said Oh..oh..oh… Is this the clapping wedding? Everyone has caught on to that word! That's why everyone calls your wedding "the wedding of applause" to this day. We learned the truth, Grandpa! He thanked her. We also learned that life is always sweet if it is simple and honest! All the children who heard the story expressed their joy. Later, Shankar Dadha wrote this incident as a short story. That story also came into a book. Now you too are reading it! Lesson: Simplicity and truth If there is life is sweet! ﻿ ﻿

title: Lion and mouse
text: I In the forest, a lion was sleeping with his big head resting on his paws. A shy little mouse unexpectedly appeared and, overcome with fear and panic, ran towards the lion's nose. The lion woke up and, in a rage, raised his huge paw to kill the little creature. ‘Please spare me!’ begged the poor mouse. ‘Let me go, and I will repay you someday.’ The lion was amused at the thought that a mouse could ever help him, but he was generous and finally let the mouse go. A few days later, while following his prey in the forest, the lion got caught in a hunter's net. He couldn't escape, and his angry roars filled the forest. The mouse knew the sound and immediately found the lion struggling in the net. He ran to one of the thick ropes binding the lion and gnawed at it until it broke, and soon the lion was free. ‘You laughed when I said I would pay you back,’ said the mouse. ‘Now you see that even a mouse can help a lion. A kidness is never wasted.

title: Do you like online games?
text: I was at school, I always looked forward to going home so I could play games immediately. "School is taking so long to end, I haven't finished playing my online games yet", I said to myself I often couldn't focus on my studies at school because I was thinking about games. Meanwhile, at home, I kept playing games until I lost track of time. "yay....I did it", I said when I won. Until one day, my mother called me while I was enjoyed in playing games. So, I didn't hear my mom calling me. Then my mother got angry with me. Nat... Mom forgot to buy salt at the market. Can you please buy some at the shop in front of the house! Hmm... ohh yeah, get some sugar too, we almost out. Since that day, my mother has forbidden me from playing games again. Even turning on the computer to do my homework it must requires her permissions. I could only look sadly at the computer. Sometimes, I become angry and argue with my mom. A week after that, my mom called me to talk, "Nat... anything in excess it's not good. You spend so much time for playing games that you don't focus on studying and often daydream. Your grades in school are not good enough. Mom knows this from your teacher at school over the phone. Nowadays, when I need to use the computer for my homework, my mom will accompany me. She advises me, "the effect of playing online games to much is 'addiction', it knows as gaming disorder. A person will experience functional and structural changes in nervous system, especially the system that regulates feelings of pleasure, learning, and motivation." I followed my mom's advice not to play games anymore. I help my mom with housework more often. I spent time with my family and friends in my neighborhood. Friends, I hope you all can learn from this experience. keep up the spirit of learning, follow advice and love our parents!
author: Fitra Auliya Malinda

title: Seed of Success
text: Once upon a time, in a village, there lived a 5-year-old boy named Mohan. He lived with his mother and father, two brothers, and two sisters. He was born into a poor family. His father was a postman. His neighbor, a boy named Sohan, was also five years old. Sohan lived with his mother and father, along with one brother and two sisters. He too was born into a poor family. All the children liked to play together, but Sohan and Mohan were especially close friends! They went to school together, played together, and even shared secrets with each other. One day, they decided to plant seeds so that they would grow over several years and become trees that would produce fruits and vegetables, which they could then sell to earn money. Therefore, they planned to collect seeds from any fruit they ate. However, this was their secret. After a few months, they had collected a large number of seeds. Then, they decided to plant them in the nearest forest on the outskirts of the village because it was very close to their home. After several years, Mohan and Sohan grew up. They found that the trees they had planted had grown abundantly, so they harvested the fruits and sold them at the market. They earned a lot of money over the years, enough to last them a lifetime. They saved all the money in a piggy bank, but now they were wondering how they should tell their parents about it. A few months ago......... but suddenly one day, Mohan's mother found the piggy bank that Mohan had hidden. She was shocked to see so much money inside. She wondered, “Where did all this money come from? Should I talk to Mohan's father about this? However, I don't think this money belongs to him. Did Mohan steal it? I have to find out before I do anything.” A few moments later... When his mother asked Mohan's father about it, he didn't know either. When Mohan came home with more money, he knew his mother already knew about all his money. So, Mohan had to tell his family everything, and he explained what he had done with Sohan. His family was shocked to learn their child had gotten so much money! His family was very happy and proud of Mohan. Shortly afterward, they went to Sohan's house and told his mother about the work they had done as a team. Mrs. Sohan also very surprised and couldn't believe it. Mrs. Sohan likes to make pickles. Her pickles are very tasty, but she couldn't make them because she didn't have enough money. After not making pickles for years, she decided to make tasty pickles that many people would like. Then, she made pickles and sold them. In a few months, her pickles became famous everywhere, and they started a business. Meanwhile, Mrs. Mohan liked to knit. So, she started making winter clothes and selling them to earn money. In a short time, both families had a lot of money. They decided to use all that money wisely so that their children and grandchildren could live a better life. From that day on, both families lived happily ever after. MORAL MESSAGE Everyone must plan for the future by working hard. PLANNING FOR THE FUTURE IS VERY USEFUL IN GUIDING THE PATH TO SUCCESS.

title: My Stubborn Gramps
text: Hi, I would like to share with you about someone very special, someone with a heart of gold and life full of challenges and adventures. This is the story of my grandpa, a stubborn old man whose life taught me that without hardships, one cannot understand the value of life. My gramps worked for a shipping company in the prime of his life but deep-down, was a self-reliant farmer, always clad in khadi. Once he had taken leave in his late fifties, he made a bold decision, moved away from the township, to a small village where his true passions lay. In this quaint hamlet, he reconnected with his beloved farms, trees, and the cozy tile-roofed house that had always felt like home. H ome is where the heart is!! My grandparents used to cherish our visits during summers, in my childhood and looked after us with utmost love and care, feeding us all they could possibly serve. Especially, the so-called ice-apples, or tathi munjulu (as they call in our regional language), sugarcane syrup, tender coconut water etc. YUMM...... The journey to the village 'naava' was an inevitable one especially during Dussehra time. The lake view was spectacular, its beauty enhanced by the shining, pinkish-white Lotuses spread like a carpet all over it. The boat ride in the small lake used to be nerve-wrecking for me, initially. During the boat ride, my mother used to pluck out a few of the Lotuses and make a garland for me. Lovely!! In the warm Summer nights, after our meals, we used to carry folding cots into the backyard of the tiled house and lie down looking at the moonlight and the bright stars while my grandma told stories to us. Those trips used to be exciting and joyful until the many narratives about poisonous snakes lurking in and around the house began surfacing. My gramps had built a small godown inside the house to store the wheat and pulses. There were apparently a couple of instances where snakes hid in the background and barged out scaring the wits out of my grandma. AARGH!!! Those trips used to be exciting and joyful until the many narratives about poisonous snakes lurking in and around the house began surfacing. My gramps had built a small godown inside the house to store the wheat and pulses. There were apparently a couple of instances where snakes hid in the background and barged out scaring the wits out of my grandma. My gramps had specifically carved tools for this very purpose and kept them handy for such occasions. Whenever my grandma raised an alarm,he used to holler and his henchmen used to appear out of nowhere to tackle the snake situation. My mother was scared stiff upon hearing these and unfortunately, our trips to the village became fewer as we grew up. hisssss.... My gramps, what a persistent old man, my juvenile mind thought, never gave up on anything. He once told me that the farmlands which were owned by his adopted father, went into dispute as some greedy neighbours tried occupying a major portion of it, illicitly. He had filed petitions against those, waited patiently for some 30 plus years until the court finally gave the rightful verdict. He, then took over the lands and cared for them until his death. Such was his resolve. I can't even remember when it all started?? Humm.. When I was around eight years old, my big brother and I had the opportunity to live with my grandparents for a short period of time. My brother was very inspired by his principles and his library of books that my gramps maintained in a small room of his house. The books of spiritual leaders and freedom fighters and the philosophical tales he used to recount to my brother, turned him into a bibliophile. Oh! This is very interesting... My gramps, with his unrelenting will, looked after my sick grandmother and cared for her with all his heart and refused any help from his children. Their visits too became fewer over the years as all of us were grown up and parted ways in pursuit of acquiring things in life. One day, we received the news of my grandmother passing away but he continued to live in that house in the village. Independent, patient and bold are synonymous with his character. He was an important person to those around him as he used to advice and help others in need. Such was his presence among the villagers. He was an important person to those around him as he used to advice and help others in need. Such was his presence among the villagers. Cooking and cleaning was a part of his daily chores as he didn't like asking for help. One evening, when he was relaxing in his arm-chair, he fell asleep and something, a poisonous creature, bit him on his leg. He became unconscious. The villagers noticed and admitted him in the nearby town hospital. He survived the incident within a short span even though the poison had spread across his leg turning it blue-black. His survival only proved his courage and mental strength to overcome all odds. ﻿ He was a true free spirit who tried to live his life on his own terms, fulfilling his life's aspirations to the best of his ability but often misunderstood. Even though some of us might be prejudiced about his fundamental thoughts as they were very different from the others, he was an independent thinker and hard worker, who truly adhered to the idea that one must believe in their own strengths and fetch for themselves. This very frame of mind rankled the people close to him as there were expectations. ﻿ He passed away just before his 90th birthday.....and until that day, I too, only thought of him as a stubborn old man. But I sat down and reminisced about all of his life's peculiarities before concluding that he was a true 'Maverick' at heart and in thought….

title: An Old Lady and Her Chicken
text: I BORY TEAM Illustrators: 211 Studio, Ajit Narayan, Aphisith Souphavongtay, Audrey Agnier, Marleen Visser, Ndumiso Nyoni, Proiti Roy, Shadrach Munene, Swati Agarwal Translator: Raihana Hazimah once upon a time in a small village in Goa lived an old lady. Her hut stands in a center of other hut. In the morning, she works in a field and earns maoney for fullfill her needs. The grandmother also had a hen that laid eggs. Every afternoon, she would take the eggs and sell them to the local shopkeeper. Sometimes she would keep one egg for herself. At night, she would boil the egg and eat it with lentil soup. The egg would fill her stomach and give her enough energy. Miraculously, the chicken that the grandmother had was quite smart. ﻿ If the chicken crows once, it means it will lay one egg. If the hen crows three times, it means three eggs. If the chicken crows five times, it means five eggs. The entire village was astonished by this crowing and egg-laying phenomenon. One day, There is a rich man came from the city. He boasted of the big buildings, shiny cars, and big shops that he used to see in the city. Many villagers were amazed at the man's story. "Does the building you live in almost touch the sky?" asked Vilas, the fisherwoman. "Are you go anywhere with this car? So, you don't have to walk at all?" Asked Yeshwant, the farmer, pointing at the man's yellow car. "People in the city don't need to draw water from a well? How fortunate!" said Ratan, the shepherd. "But, do you have chickens in the city that can predict how many eggs they will lay?" ﻿ Hearing the question being asked, all the villagers turned to see who was asking the question. It was Veena, a farmer's daughter. "Shut up!" her father told her. "Don't you know? He is a man from the city. He has many interesting stories to tell." "Oh please don't scold him," said the city man. "But, son, I didn't believe you until I saw the chicken myself." "Okay, come with me," said Veena looking proud. They all went to grandma's house to see her chicken. As they all sat, waiting for the cock to crow, the city man announced - "If this cock actually predicts the number of eggs it will lay, I will pay the old granny Rs.100[1] for each egg." All the villagers cheered! The chicken crowed one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! "It has crowed 10 times, which means it will lay 10 eggs!" shouted Veena happily. [1] Rs or Rupees are the currency of India. Of course the chicken laid 10 eggs. The city man had no choice other than give the money to the grandmother. "But maybe you're just being lucky today," said the city man. "Could it be that this didn't happen by chance?" Finally, the city man stayed in the village for five days, and every time the hen crowed, he predicted exactly how many eggs she would lay. In five days, the old granny had enough money to buy a cow, a hen, and repair her rain-damaged cottage. And what did she do with the rest of the money? She gave it to Veena's parents for school fees, new books, better clothes, and bus fare to visit the city. Activity Use this story to learn numbers while learning different animal sounds: Cow: Moo Moo Moo Moo 4 Donkey: Ngik Ngik 2 Pig: Ngok Ngok Ngok Ngok Ngok Ngok Ngok 7 Cat: Meow 1 Have fun!

title: Live Pharmacy
text: It looks like you have a bad cold, Aditi.” “Yes Grandma, I drank ice yesterday. It was raining anyway,” said Aditi. "Calm down, Aditi. I'll make some tea with lemongrass and ginger for you. You'll feel refreshed," said Grandma as she headed for the kitchen. Aditi followed Grandma into the kitchen and watched as Grandma put fresh lemongrass and ginger root into the boiling water. The smell of tea wafted through the kitchen and Aditi said, “I feel better.” Grandmother laughed and said, "You will feel refreshed after drinking this hot tea. When we were young, there were no doctors in our village. So, my mother always kept herbal medicines for minor ailments like fever, flu and cough." “Grandma, tell me more about these herbal medicines.” "Yes Aditi, but drink the herbal tea first. I'll show you that our garden is a living pharmacy full of medicinal plants. I've even recorded all the plants in this book." Aditi drank the tea and was happy that her throat felt relieved. Then, she and Grandma headed out into the yard. “Look at this plant, Aditi!” "Yes Grandma, this is basil or Holy Basil. We worship the basil plant. Nek, is this plant effective?" "Aditi, basil leaves contain vitamins, and can treat respiratory problems. It is rich in antioxidants and can relieve stress. The juice of basil leaves is useful for treating skin diseases such as itching. Basil is also beneficial for people with asthma," explained Grandma. "Oh... I just found out that there are plants that are very useful in our yard. Nek, what other plants do we have?" asked Aditi. Grandma called out, "Come here Aditi. This is lemongrass or Citronella. I have mixed a few strands into the tea you are drinking. Like basil, lemongrass also contains antioxidants and can flush out toxins from our body. A glass of lemongrass tea can relieve flu. Lemongrass can also treat an upset stomach. People with high blood pressure or high cholesterol should consume lemongrass regularly. If the dosage is right, herbal medicine does not cause side effects." “Grandma, if herbal medicine is safe, is it okay to stop taking other medicines and only take herbal medicine?” "No Aditi, I was just about to explain. Patients with serious illnesses must follow the doctor's advice and take the recommended medicines. Patients should tell the doctor about the herbal medicines they are taking. Herbal medicines are natural and usually harmless. However, sometimes they can cause chronic and dangerous problems. Therefore, patients should consult their doctors and follow their advice. I also take herbal medicine when I'm sick. However, if the pain doesn't subside or gets worse, I go to the doctor." "Okay, Grandma. I'll keep that in mind. Let's look at other medicinal plants." “Come here,” said Grandma. This is ginger for everyday cooking. Ginger is good for digestion. Ginger can also treat coughs and colds." "Grandma, we often use ginger and garlic in our food. Is garlic useful too?" asked Aditi. Grandma replied, "Yes... yes... garlic actually belongs to the onion family. Garlic contains a substance called allicin, which has many benefits. For example, garlic can lower high blood pressure and reduce cholesterol levels so that it can protect the heart. Now, I'm going to show you another special plant. Come here, Aditi." Grandmother took Aditi to see a plant with long, wide leaves. She picked the leaf and asked Aditi to smell it. Aditi said, "It smells nice, Grandma. Mom often uses these leaves for flavoring dishes. What is the name of this plant?" "This is turmeric. The turmeric that we use as a spice is actually the tuber. Turmeric that has been dried and ground into turmeric flour. Turmeric is known for its antiseptic properties. In the past, turmeric was often used as a wound medicine. Turmeric is useful for reducing the symptoms of arthritis. Turmeric can also boost the immune system or be used as an antidote for toxins in the body." ﻿ “Grandma, Mom give me turmeric milk when my throat hurts.” "Yes Aditi. Turmeric milk contains antiseptics, useful for treating sore throats." Right next to the turmeric plant was a plant with thick leaves. Aditi asked her grandmother, “Nek, what is this plant? It has thick leaves.” Grandma explained, "This is aloe vera. Aloe vera leaves are actually succulents that contain water. When the leaf is cut, there is gel inside. This gel is used to make beauty products. Aloe vera is also useful for lowering blood sugar levels. Aloe vera contains many vitamins and minerals, and can be used to treat skin diseases such as acne. You can also apply aloe vera gel if your skin is sunburned. This gel feels cool." Aditi spotted a long-leafed plant and she recognized it immediately. "Grandma, this is also a medicinal plant. It's called Adulsa. My mother gives me adulsa when I cough." "Yes, Aditi, this is Adulsa or Adhatoda. It can be used to treat cold, cough, bronchitis and chronic asthma. Its expectorant properties can remove phlegm. The leaves can be used to treat skin diseases like scabies." Grandmother showed Aditi a big tree and asked, “Do you know the name of this tree?” "Yes, Grandma. This is a neem tree. On Gudi Padva day, the first day of the month of Chaitra, Mother makes us eat some neem leaves. It tastes a bit bitter." said Aditi. Grandmother explained, "Neem leaves are indeed bitter, Aditi dear. However, the neem tree is special. Neem leaves can treat skin diseases. If boiled, the water can be used to wash your hair and get rid of dandruff. Neem branches can be used to clean teeth if toothpaste or toothbrushes are not available. Neem branches not only clean teeth, but also protect teeth from harmful bacteria." “I also saw you sprinkle neem when storing rice and other grains.” "Yes, neem protects the rice from insects. Using neem leaves is much better than adding harmful pesticides to grains. In the past, neem trees were planted in every house. Aditi, we've toured our beautiful garden, now it's time to return home. I'll make breakfast and warm turmeric milk for you. I wish you a speedy recovery." "Grandma, I'm already feeling well. Ginger and lemongrass tea works wonders." "Thank goodness, you're feeling well, Aditi. Walking around the garden was also healthy. Actually, our bodies are capable of treating themselves if they are only mildly ill. Using medicinal plants and herbs is healthy. But if we get sick, we have to go to the doctor." Grandma said. “Grandma, I think the cold drink I had yesterday gave me the flu,” said Aditi. "Aditi, flu is caused by a virus. But it's true that cold drinks, especially with artificial flavors, can cause sore throats." explained Grandma. “If you're thirsty, you should drink water or natural drinks like coconut water, lemon juice, or milk.” “I'll remember, Grandma!” said Aditi as she walked home with Grandma. I hope you like this story. I hope you also learned about a special medicinal plant. Nature provides a huge pharmacy in the form of plants. Our ancestors knew the benefits of these plants and used them appropriately. We should be proud of this knowledge and be willing to learn about it. This knowledge of medicinal plants is part of Indian culture. We call this knowledge Local Wisdom or Lokvidya. We must recognize and explore this knowledge.
author: Nabila Bahiroh Dhiya Shofyana

title: Baingani
text: This story is about a little girl who lived in the village of Ghariya. The people of Ghariya are known to be friendly and live peacefully. Animals and villagers coexist in harmony. ﻿ In this village, there was a little girl named Ragini. She was a kind and cheerful child. Two things Ragini loved the most - going to school and playing with her friends. Ragini had many friends where she lived. Ragini used to wake up early to go to school and after school she played with her friends. One day, there was a giant bird at the edge of the village. Its name was Baingani. It was bright purple and different from other birds! Baingani had traveled all over the earth and was exhausted after a long journey. Baingani intended to take a short rest before continuing to her destination. ﻿ While resting under a tree, Baingani heard the sound of splashing water! What was that? It was Ragini, who was playing on the banks of the river. Ragini had just returned from school and was waiting for her friends. Baingani sneaked a closer look. She had never spoken to a human before! Ragini jumped up in surprise when she saw the giant bird, but she had the courage to say hello. “I am Ragini, who are you?”. Baingani was astonished, she had never spoken to a human before. She used to think humans were unfriendly. “I am Baingani, I come from a distant island. I usually only see humans from a distance.” “Why?” Ragini asked. “Because they look unfriendly”. “Hmmm...maybe because they've never seen a bird like you”. Ragini and the giant bird chatted for a while before Ragini decided to go home. ﻿ Not long after, news of the giant bird's arrival reached the villagers, and they wanted to drive it away. The villagers came to the river with sticks and made noises, which was very scary. Baingani was in a dilemma. Baingani wanted to leave immediately, knowing that interacting with humans was a bad idea. But Baingani also wanted to see Ragini one last time. A fter news of the bird's expulsion spread, Ragini rushed to see the village elders. In every house she visited, everyone said the same thing. “We don't know what kind of creature it is and what it will do to us”. Ragini decided to meet the most respected elder in the village. “Humans are also different fro m each other. And still manage to live in harmony, so why are we afraid of that bird just because it's different from us? Baingani don't deserve to be treated like this”. The elder saw the truth in Ragini's words and ordered the villagers not to hunt the bird. The villagers realized their mistake and released the bird. ﻿ The villagers finally understood that just because something is different, it doesn't mean it's bad or dangerous. Every living thing is unique and has its own specialty. Different does not mean lower or higher. It wasn't long before Baingani built a nest by the river and guess who her best friend was? Ragini, of course.

title: The Ghost In My House
text: There was a ghost that lived in Eric's house. Every evening, it quietly opened the front door and sneaked inside. But every morning, just as the sun comes up, it disappeared outside. Sometimes, the ghost bothers his mom. It shouts at her and makes her cry. It even broke all the things and threw them around the house. When that happens, Eric hid behind mom, and wait until the ghost calms down. At night, when Eric fall asleep, the ghost comes into my dreams. It laughs at him and teases him, making him feel small and scared. Whenever that happens, Eric had to wrap himself in his blanket. But one day, something changed. Evening came, and morning followed, but the ghost did not come to home. Eric looked at his mom and asked, “Mom, isn’t the ghost coming tonight?” Mom waited a little before she said softly, “No, the ghost won’t come anymore.” Eric was so happy to hear that! Eric thought, “Now we don’t have to be scared anymore!" But that night, the ghost came into his dreams again. It shouted at him, asking what I had done wrong!!!!! Eric can not understand, and so scared. The ghost was bigger than ever. And its mouth opened as wide as its body as it screamed. It stomped its feet and made the whole world shake. The next morning, Eric told his mom that the ghost had come back. She hugged Eric tightly. Mom said, "It's OK. It can not bother you anymore." Eric said, "Really?" Mom said, "Sure, you can beat it absolutely." At that night, the ghost never fails to come. It started threatening Eric again. So, Eric screamed to ghost. "GO AWAY!!!! DO NOT BOTHER ME ANYMORE!!!" And then, that ghost really went away. Next morning, Eric met his mom. He ran to her immediately. Mom hugged him tightly. "Mom!!! I Beat it!!",said Eric. "Really? Oh, dear..." Mom hugged him more tightly. After that day, the ghost really did not come to Eric's house anymore. "Mom, I can feel happy now.", said Eric. "I'm really glad to hear that.",said his mom.

title: The Vanishing Vada Pav
text: At Shantiniketan School, Wednesday was just another dull day. Math was the first period. EVS came in second. Additionally, something crazy occurred during third period. During recess, I, Aarav, a proud Class 5B student, opened my tiffin box to discover that my vada pav was gone! Lost. Poof. Not even a crumb. " But I packed it myself!" I shouted. " The largest aloo vada in the world, two tender pavs, and fiery red chutney!" Meera, my best friend, let out a gasp. "Lunch stolen? War is inevitable." Operation PavFinder was initiated. Rohan is the first suspect. He refers to himself as "The Tiffin Terminator" and is constantly hungry. However, he had a lot of dosa in his mouth today. Most likely innocent. Priya comes next. She adores vada pav. I really adore it. However, she opened her box, along with a depressing green chutney and three idlis. We kept a close eye on her. Then we noticed — a chutney stain on the floor … leading to the rear of the classroom. Following the red splashes all the way to the cupboard containing the cleaning supplies, we crept like detectives. Slowly, I opened the door. and a monkey sat there, encircled by tissues and a pencil box. Indeed. A live, breathing monkey. Using my vada pav. He gave me a look. I gave him a look. I got half the pav from him. Respectfully, we both nodded. The principal later claimed that the monkey sneaked from the mango tree But now every Wednesday I pack an extra vada pav, one for me and one for the monkey. Since us students of 5B believe in being kind to everyone!

title: my grandma and grandpa
text: She is now 70 years old, but she looks like she is 20. She takes good care of the whole family and makes sure that everyone lives in peace. I live in abig family with 10 members, and my grandmother is the one who takes care of everyone. To respect older people, she never makes excuses for his work. Grandma still remembers the stories she heard from her grandma long ago and tells them to me and my cousins every night. She always makes sure we understand the stories and find the important lessons inside. Every story she tells has a special meaning that teaches us how to live better. She also knows how to make me feel encouraged. If I am successful today, it is mostly because of her. If I am successful today, it’s mostly because of her. A long time ago, she often helped me with Math and Science when I was in school because my parents were working. Even though she wasn’t a professional teacher, she was the best teacher I ever had. I still remember the formulas she taught me when I was little. She is one of the reasons for my success. If today people appreciate me for my good manners and polite attitude, it’s all thanks to her. She taught me... how to respect older people. My grandfather’s name is Narasaya. He is 74 years old and is the head of our family. Everyone in the family loves, respects, and listens to him. He loves reading—newspapers, novels, magazines, and even articles. I love spending time with him. He teaches me good manners and cares for me deeply. Every afternoon, he takes me to the nearby park. We play hide and seek, cricket, and snakes and ladders together. He is my inspiration. When I grow up, I want to be like him. Now there are both of them. The oldest members of the family take on all the family responsibilities. They give full love and care to everyone in the family. Having a grandfather and grandmother is a blessing. They helped shape the lives of our parents, and without them, we wouldn’t learn so many important things about life. They tell us many stories, and each one has a beautiful moral lesson. Their stories may be full of imagination, but they also show us what real life is like. Grandparents are the best friends for children someone they can trust and share their secrets with. They are a special gift that we must always treasure. In today’s world, many people forget their importance because they live in small families. But we must remember that grandparents are a precious gift. They teach us to respect others and to live a good life in the future. Grandparents are responsible people who guide us to become good citizens in the future. Without them, our lives would not be this peaceful. They help us make good decisions and teach us about right and wrong. Thanks to their wisdom, we follow the right path. They are the most precious. Without them, our lives would be much harder. That’s why we must always appreciate their role in our lives. As they grow older, it is our responsibility to take care of them and spend time with them.
