title: Do you like online games?
text: I have a hobby of playing online games. Do my friends here have the same hobby as me? When I was at school, I always looked forward to going home so I could play games immediately. “It took me so long to get home from school, I haven't finished playing yesterday's online game,” I said to myself. I often couldn't focus on my studies at school because I was thinking about games. Meanwhile, at home I kept playing games until I lost track of time. “Horaiiii... I did it,” I said when I won. Until one day, Mom called me, who was busy playing games. So I didn't listen to her call. Then, Mom got angry with me. Nat... Mom forgot to buy salt at the market. Please buy it from the stall in front! Hmmm... Oh yeah, there's a little sugar left. Since that incident, my mom has forbidden me from playing games. Even opening the computer to do homework now requires her permission. I could only look at the computer with a heavy heart. Sometimes, I became short-tempered and ended up arguing with Mom. A week after the incident, Mom talked to me, "Nat... too much of anything is not good. You spend so much time playing games that you don't focus on your studies and often daydream. Your school grades are not good enough. I found this out from your teacher at school over the phone." Nowadays, if I need to use the computer for assignments, Mom will accompany me. Mom advised, “The effect of playing online games too often is ”addiction", known as gaming disorder. A person will experience functional and structural changes in the nervous system, especially the systems that regulate feelings of pleasure, learning, and motivation." I obeyed Mom's advice not to play games anymore. I help my mom with the housework more often. I spend time with my family and friends in the neighborhood. Friends, I hope you can learn from this experience. Keep up the spirit of learning, obey advice and love our parents!
author: Rini Anggrahini

title: Chipko is starting to grow!
text: Kiki was playing her drum. Her three siblings also climbed the same tree, while their sheep were grazing and bleating in the grassy meadow below. “Kiki!” came Dada’s voice echoing among the chir pine (Pinus roxburghii), pine, deodar (Cedrus deodara), and ash trees (Fraxinus). “Hurry up, we have to visit your grandmother across the river. Kids, bring the sheep along, okay?” “May I come along?” asked Syam. “Not this time, okay?” Dada said firmly. “Kiki will stay there to take care of Grandma. She’s sick right now.” Dada led their pack animals (young horses and donkeys) across the knee-deep river. Kiki lifted her skirt to step over the rocks, her movements nimble like a mountain goat. Her toes tingled the moment they touched the cold water. Suddenly, she slipped and fell. "Be careful!" shouted Cacha in warning. She was wading nearby. Suddenly, a large wave surged forward, and the river roared and churned around them. A flash flood was rushing in with fury. Chacha quickly grabbed Kiki’s hand. Kiki’s left foot got stuck between the sliding rocks. Dada’s figure appeared blurry—his voice drowned out by the roaring water. Trapped in the current, the pack animals tried to swim while whimpering, and the belongings they carried fell and drifted away. Chacha barely managed to keep his balance amid the flood. He struggled to free Kiki’s foot from beneath the heavy rock. Amid the mud, he gathered all her strength to pull Kiki out. His strong shoulders supported Kiki as she handed her over to Ma, who was waiting at the riverbank. Ma nodded, looking at her daughter who was completely exhausted. Kiki’s left foot hurt terribly, as if pricked by hundreds of sharp needles. Kiki shivered and then fainted. Chacha left Kiki with Ma, who was crying loudly. He quickly went back to search for Dada. But Dada never came back. The cold fingers and fear weighed heavily on Kiki’s heart when they brought Dada’s lifeless body home from the river. Kiki heard about a sports equipment company that was cutting down chir pine, pine, deodar, and ash trees to make cricket bats and other sports gear. Were they the ones who cut down our forest? Did they accidentally cause the landslide roaring on the mountain slope? The huge flash flood that swept away poor people? That flood took Dada’s life and Kiki’s left leg. Now her leg is paralyzed. Kiki can no longer feel her leg below the knee. Kiki could never forget the icy cold river water. She still remembered how it covered her ears, flowed down her nose, blurred her vision, and flooded over her head. But no! Chacha said she had to think about good things… think positive thoughts. Hardships would come like the warmth of light that would soften her fear. She still had Ma and her siblings. Chacha and Auntie also took care of everything. They didn’t have children of their own. Kiki loved Chacha as much as she loved Dada, but sometimes she felt tired when she heard Auntie say to Ma, “Chacha was a good man. But his gambling habit can ruin our lives. Look how hard life has become now.” “Chacha a gambler? Oh no, that can’t be!” Time passed. Kiki and her family began to get used to their new routine. Kiki sat on a branch of the ash tree, looking down where two rough crutches lay on the grass… yes, they were made by Chacha from the big ash tree. “My branches are small and stubby, long and short,” whispered the ash tree, “but I am strong.” Kiki climbed higher to peek at the bird’s nest. She moved her fingers following the trail of ants marching, and breathed in the fresh scent of the ash tree’s leaves. “You are my ash tree. Chacha said I am just like you, strong like Yak. With these crutches, I will be strong and fierce like a Yeti.” “Heh, Kiki! Everyone’s gathered!” shouted Syam. Quickly, Kiki jumped down, grabbed her crutches, and followed Syam down the hollow tree where the villagers usually gathered. They sat around Gauri, the village elder. “Maybe we can’t read or write, but we are wise people,” said Gauri. “We won’t allow them to sell those trees to any company. Later, if Chandra, the contractor, comes with his equipment, we will go to the forest and hug the chir pine, pine, deodar, and ash trees. But remember, no violence.” The villagers marched together to the forest, chanting their resistance slogans. Kiki rolled her drum and beat it strongly, accompanied by the singing of the children who gathered and jumped around. Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tak Tak Dung Dung! “What’s inside this forest?” shouted Kiki. “Land, water, and fresh air,” the children cried together, joining Kiki with excitement. However, several men in uniforms were already standing in front of them, carrying axes in their hands. The large contractor Chandra stood tall above them, shouting orders to mark the chir pine, pine, deodar, and ash trees with white paint forming an "X". The villagers angrily gathered around them, shouting out in protest. They yelled at the workers and beat their drums loudly until the sound filled the forest with Chipko resistance songs. “Let’s protect and plant trees. Raise the spirit of the people and drive away those loggers!” Contractor Chandra sneered wickedly as he and his axe-wielding crew boarded the bus and left. The next morning, there was a commotion as the men of the village prepared for a long journey down the mountain slopes. Trucks had been sent by the government so they could watch a movie—a rare treat that couldn’t be ignored, since films were seldom shown in this remote area. The women were busy weaving. The village school was lively. The children were learning new Chipko slogans, drawing chir pine, pine, deodar, and ash trees on the blackboard, beating their drums, and dancing. “This land is ours, t his water is ours, t his forest is ours too. our ancestors protected it, and so must we.” Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tak Tak Dung Dung! After school, Kiki and her siblings took the sheep to the forest to graze. Together with the other village children, they hugged the chir pine, pine, deodar, and ash trees. Their cheerful voices faded as the sun set on the horizon, and the children returned to the village carrying firewood on their heads. Kiki kept her eyes open for a while, then leaned against her favorite tree. Its soft leaves soothed her gently, its smooth bark rested against her cheek, as if whispering to her. “No one is allowed to take my tree!” Kiki thought firmly. Time felt like it stopped. The world felt calm. But the peaceful trees suddenly shook as a flock of parrots flew overhead, screeching loudly. Squirrels darted out from the bushes. The screech of brakes echoed as a bus stopped at the foot of the cliff. The bus was splattered with mud and covered in dust. Kiki peeked through the leaves. A group of men stepped out together. Their uniforms were stiff and crisp, their axes gleaming in the sunlight. They marched into the forest full of chir pines, pines, deodars, and ash trees. Contractor Chandra followed closely behind. Their footsteps echoed across the mountain slopes. “Help, ash tree! They mustn’t cut you down!” Kiki clapped her hands and leapt from the branch, jumping down the steep slope. Panting, she flung away her crutches onto the soft green hillside, then rolled forward to chase after them. Rolling, falling, feeling dizzy! Rolling, falling, feeling dizzy! Kiki’s heart thumped hard, like the beat of her drum. Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tak Tak Dung Dung! “I need help, quick!” Kiki shouted in panic, fumbling for her crutches and limping back with unsteady steps. “Ma!” Kiki gasped. Ma rushed out to hug her tightly and offer comfort, as Kiki trembled like a log caught in a bonfire. “Ma! My ash tree! The... The... They’re cutting it down!” “Who, sweetie? Speak slowly. Here, have a drink first.” “The... They came in a big bus! So many of them! They have sharp axes, Ma!” “Oh no! The contractor's people came to cut down our trees! Quickly! We have to do something.” “Ma, stay here, okay... I’ll gather the people,” said Kiki, catching her breath and squaring her shoulders. The women and children quickly gathered, carrying their drums. “We have to act now. Contractor Chandra tricked us into leaving!” said Ma, angrily twisting the edge of her panthu. “How can we stop them without the men here?” “We’ll resist them! But remember, no violence,” said Gauri, the village elder and Ma’s close friend. Kiki’s heartbeat echoed along with the rhythm of her drum. The forest trembled at the cries of the chir pines, deodars, ash, and other trees. “What does this forest hold?” asked Kiki, raising her fist high. “Soil, water, and pure air!” came the united voices of the women and children. The white X marks painted on the trees to be cut felt like wounds that would never heal. My trees! What can I do without you? Kiki’s fingers trembled as she scraped the tree bark, trying to erase the painted X. “You’re not allowed to cut my tree,” she said fiercely, her small hand pressed against the tree. “Out of the way,” snapped contractor Chandra, yanking her aside roughly. Kiki stumbled away, her crutches thudding. Her sharp eyes scanned the loggers, tired but alert. Then her eyes landed on a figure hiding behind a tree—someone curling into themselves. Kiki's eyes widened in shock, “Chacha??? You too?” Suddenly, a heavy silence fell over the forest. Chacha collapsed weakly, his axe slipping from his hand and hitting the ground with a dull thud. "I’m in deep debt because of gambling... I have no job," Chacha said quietly, his voice full of shame. Kiki and her siblings rushed to embrace him. "Chacha, we will work to help you pay off your debt! I can weave shawls and sell them!" said Kiki. "I will work making soap," said Rama. "I will work at the water mill!" said Syam. Chacha lowered his head, tears shimmering in his eyes. He took off his uniform shirt and picked up Kiki's drum. Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tat Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tat Tak Dung Dung! "What does this forest contain?" asked Chacha and Kiki. "Soil, water, and fresh air!" replied the women and children in unison. "Hey, you foolish child! These forests produce timber, resin, and foreign exchange!" shouted contractor Chandra. "Hey, all of you! Cut down those trees! All of them—chir pine, pine, deodar, and ash trees!" "No! No! No! Help, don’t let them!" cried Kiki while hugging her tree. "These trees are our saviors!" "She’s right," said Chacha. "She lost her father in that flood!" The loggers heard that, and without realizing it, their axes slipped from their hands. Soon, the sound of another axe falling was heard… and one by one, the loggers’ axes dropped to the ground. With their heads hung low, one by one, the tree cutters left the forest. Dung Tak Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tat Tak Dung Tak! Dung Tat Tak Dung Dung! “Chipko! Let’s hug the trees!” shouted Kiki. Her hoarse voice echoed among the whispering wind between the trees. “If you cut down this forest, you’ll destroy our village,” said Ma. Suddenly, a dark shadow appeared as if it covered the sky. Contractor Chandra stood before them, his body towering like a giant. Clenching his fists, he stomped his feet in anger, turned around, and stormed off. Clutching her hands tightly, Kiki took a deep breath. It felt almost unbelievable – all the loggers were gone! Clenching her hands, Kiki took a deep breath. As unbelievable as it felt, all the loggers had left! “We did it!” cried Ma. “We will bring our Chipko Movement across all of India!” “Chipko! Hug the trees!” shouted the women and children. Their feet stomped, their arms stretched out, and hand in hand, they broke into a joyful dance of victory. The trees swayed in the wind. Kiki pressed her cheek against the cool bark of the tree. She felt the soft, furry leaves rustling in the evening breeze. “I am like you, my tree, strong and fierce like a Yeti… steadfast like a Yak,” Kiki whispered to the tree.

title: Dad, let's go home
text: Vishakha was happy that many of her friends were present at her birthday party. “This party is awesome, Aunty,” Rohit said. In return, Vishakha's mother embraced Rohit. Vishakha's mother was attentive and affectionate towards all the children. The children and their parents love her too. They are always there if needed. So is Vishakha's mother. “This is the best party ever!” exclaimed Vishakha as she and her friends watched a movie. A movie about a tiger and its cub playing in the jungle. But this movie made Vishakha sad. Why? He didn't know. After the movie, Vishakha's friends went home. Rohit was still preparing to go home. “The movie was good, wasn't it?” “Yes. I really liked it,” said Vishakha. “Uh, but where's your father? I've never met him,” said Rohit. “Father? Daddy? Dad, where's Dad? Mom, where's Dad?” Her mother yawned. “It's bedtime now.” “But, but... I want you too, just like that tiger cub!” “Come on Vishakha. I'm tired. Come here, kiss mom.” “But mom!” “VISHAKHA!” shouted his mother. “Okay, mom.” The next day the school was closed. Vishakha and Rohit read together. “Where should I look for him, Rohit? Where do you look for Father when you don't see him?” “In the bathroom. That's his favorite place to hide. I looked there.” “I checked, but you weren't there. Do you know where my father is?” “Hmm, I don't know. But this book says parrots can talk and know everything.” “But I don't have a parrot.” “I do. Let's go!” “Mirchi, look who's here.” Rohit called his parrot. “Ki-Ki-Vishakha,” said the parrot. “Oh, Mirchi! Do you know who my father is? Or where my father is?” “NO! Is he as funny as me?” “I don't know, that's why I asked you.” “Ki-Ki-ka-ka.” “Rohit, what does that mean?” “Hi Vishakha. How are you, dear?” greeted Rohit's mother. “Aunty, do you know where my father is? I asked Mirchi, but he wouldn't answer.” “Haha! Mirchi is ignorant. You should ask your mom. She would know.” “I did, Aunty. But Mom doesn't know either.” “Hmm. It's getting dark. You should go home.” “Yes. Bye, Tante.” That night Vishakha kept thinking about his father. How does he look, what does he do, where is he? The questions kept coming. He wanted to talk to his mother. Her mother looked different. Vishakha didn't understand. “Hey, mom. You're okay, right?” asked Vishakha quietly. “Come here, Vish. Look at the stars. Look at the light.” “Beautiful, mom. If I were a star...” “One day, you will be a star. Like your father.” “My father is a star?” asked Vishakha excitedly. “Yes, dear. Do you see that star? The brightest star!” “Yes.” “That's your father smiling at you.” “Hi Mr. Mom, can he hear me?” “Louder, Vish.” Vishakha smiled at the star while closing his eyes, trying to calculate the distance between him and the star. Then he shouted loudly, “Father, let's go home.”

title: Go to the Market
text: There were many sellers and buyers in the market. Some people were busy shopping. Some were just looking at the goods being sold. What about mom? First, Mom and I headed to the grocery store. Mom bought wheat, rice, sugar and dal. Mom and I didn't have to bother carrying bags of groceries. The shopkeeper would deliver the groceries to my house. Next, Mom and I arrived at the vegetable store. Then, I asked, “Are you going to buy vegetables?” “No,” I replied. The vendor offered his wares, “Come, buy. The vegetables are fresh.” Why did you stop at this shop? Oh, this is an oil depot. This place is filled with the smell of oil. Mom protested to the oil seller, “This oil is exorbitantly priced.” The salesman looked grim. Mom and I passed by the fish stalls. Some people don't like the smell of this place. But I love fish. Look how unique the fisherwoman's clothes are. Do you see a fat cat? The cat just sat there, ate the remains of the fish, and got fat. Mom and I stopped at the dairy store. Mom bought butter and cheese. Why doesn't the dairy store sell ice cream? I like eating ice cream. Will mom buy me ice cream? “Are you going to buy a pot and pan?” I asked my mom. There wasn't a single person in the home furnishing store. People usually buy pots and pans when there is a wedding or celebration. “Stop! Don't come into this shop!” I yelled. My mom likes to go to fabric stores. She would hold the cloths that were being sold. The cloth shopkeeper offered her a variety of saris. But Mom didn't buy any. “This is what I've been waiting for,” the toy store! The teddy bear is so big! I've dreamed of riding this scooter. I don't have this toy truck yet either. However, I promised Mom, “I will only look at and hold these toys.” “I won't ask for toys today.” I will ask for toys on my birthday.

title: Jab to myself !
text: Every day, I am tired.. My body was heavy. I had no reason to smile. I was tired of everything... ﻿ ﻿ Little things made me angry. I became sensitive. whenever someone spoke a bit loudly or made a mistake. Everything felt annoying. ﻿ ﻿ I didn’t know how to solve this anger. I kept it inside and that makes me hurt. Even my friends often said, “Are you okay?” One day, I walked past a boxing gym. The sound of punches hitting the sandbag made my heart race. I didn’t wait. I opened the door and walked in on my own. I stood there and said, “I want to learn boxing.” Coach gave me gloves, and I began my first steps. At first, I didn’t know how to punch. But as I punched the bag again and again, my body felt lighter. I also feel like the anger inside me is disappearing. Now, when something made me upset, I didn’t shout or hide. I just punched, breathed, and let it pass. My mind felt clearer. I didn’t get angry as easily and could keep smiling. Boxing didn’t solve every problem, but it helped me face them. It gave me strength not just in my arms, but in my thoughts. Now I know something important. We need to move our body to heal our heart.
author: 익규 이

title: Are We All Different?
text: Little Sia got the opportunity to go on a train journey to her grandmother’s home. It was going to be a long journey so she packed things she wanted. It included a book, a torch, her fav t-shirt and a bag of flavoured candy. She settled in the train and took the window seat, hoping to look at new sceneries and learn about the world outside. Little did she know that she was going to learn a lot more inside the train on this trip. Just before the train moved, a family entered the compartment. The lady wore a dress that covered her head to toe, and Sia wondered why… Appa explained to Sia, that the lady is wearing a hijab & burka. He said, “some people dress differently and they do it because they have been taught to dress that way and they are used to it.” But a dress doesn't define who we are. Inside we are all the same. As the train moved, everyone settled in. In the next compartment, Sia saw a little boy with his hair tied into a tiny bun on his head and wondered why. Amma explained to Sia, that the little boy was wearing a patka & his dad a pagari. She said, “Sometimes people wear their hair differently. For generations their families have covered their hair and it makes them respectful.” But headgear shouldn’t define who we are. Inside we are all the same. The train moved through lovely countryside and Sia observed from the window how little boys were holding sticks and chasing goats away from the tracks. She wondered why they were doing that. Appa explained that some kids don’t get to go to school, but they learn other skills and are good at things like farming & taking care of animals. And though it’s different from what other kids learn, Inside we are still the same. At the next station, a little girl was escorted into the AC 2-tier section on a chair with wheels and Sia wondered why she was not walking like others. Amma explained that she was in a wheelchair. She said, “For some people, some parts of the body may not work exactly like others. But they will be able to do things in their own different ways." Different or not on the outside...inside, we are all the same. Sia’s friend on the opposite seat was now hungry and his mother gave him some food to eat that looked very different from her Idlis. Appa explained that the little boy was eating a chicken lollipop. He said, “some people eat different food as their families cook that and they relish different tastes.” We eat different things, but we all do it to stay alive. Inside we are all the same. Sia walked with her Amma towards the next boogie. She saw a loving family where a little girl called the two men with her Daddy & Pappa. She was confused…. Amma explained that this was a Modern family. She said “Families can be different. Some families have a mom and a dad. Some can have two moms or two dads.” But in any family we all love and respect each other because inside we are all the same. Sia now wanted to have a quick snack before climbing onto her top berth, and dipped her hand into a bag of flavoured candy. Her friend offered to switch on the light so they could pick their favourite colour….. Sia stopped him and said it wouldn't matter because the colours may not define the flavours. Appa & Amma explained to the little boy that Sia was colour blind. They said, “She cannot see colour the way you do, they look different to her. But she still knows what things look like and has her own way of enjoying everything including all flavours of the candy.” The little boy smiled and said, “That's ok. It doesn't matter what we see outside. Inside we are all the same.” Meet the Author, Pooja Sriram When Pooja was a little girl, she loved curling up with storybooks and getting lost in magical worlds. Now that she’s all grown up, she writes her own stories—ones that kids like you can enjoy! She’s also a mom (which means she knows what kids love!) and a content marketer (that’s someone who works with words and ideas). She combines both to create her stories that are exciting, thoughtful, and full of heart. Other books she’s written: Amma’s Work From Home Buddy (for tiny tots 2–4 years old) Hairdresser in a Hairless Town (for curious kids 4–7) Librarian Who Lost Her Books (for book lovers 5–8) The Busy House Diaries (for big kids 7+ and even grown-ups!) Meet the Illustrator, Somya Barpanda A daydreamer and nature enthusiast, Somya tries to capture the magic of this world into her art - one soft stroke at a time. When she’s not drawing, you’ll find her cloud-watching, doodling in the margins of to-do lists, or waving her pencil like a magic wand (because... maybe it is).
author: Pooja Sriram

title: The Magic Fruity Snowballs
text: “Wake up! It snowed outside!” Ollie shouted to his older brother 'Leo'. Then Leo woke up. “Look! It snowed outside,” Ollie said excitedly. “There’s a lot,” Leo said. Then Ollie said, “Right? Let’s go outside!” “No, it's cold outside,” Leo said. “Please..” Ollie said. “Okay, let’s wear warm clothes and go,” Leo said. So Ollie and Leo wear warm clothes and left the house. Everything was covered with snow. Ollie and Leo were excited. They made a snowman and had a snowball fight. Then Leo saw something. “Ollie, what’s that?” “It’s glowing,” Ollie said. “Let’s go there.” Leo said. So they walked toward it. There was a tree. “Is it an apple tree?” Ollie asked. “No, they’re snowballs!” Leo said. “They look like apples. I want to try one,” Ollie said. “No! They’re snowballs,” Leo said. “I still want to try!” Ollie picked one and ate it. “What does it taste like?” Leo asked. “It tastes like apple!” Ollie said. “Really? I want to try too,” Leo said. “Does yours taste like apple too?” Ollie asked. “Yuck! My snowball tastes like lemon! I think each one tastes different,” Leo said. “Really? I want another one,” Ollie said. “This one tastes like grape!” Ollie said. The snowballs tasted like apple, lemon, grape—even peach. They kept eating more and more. They ate almost all of them. “All gone!” Then—POP! A giant rainbow snowball appeared. Ollie and Leo said, “Can we eat this one too?”
author: 이윤 송

title: Think Before You Act
text: Buddhi has a beautiful garden, full of flowers. Looking at it and admiring it makes his heart very happy. It has been a year, and not a single drop of rain has fallen. The flowers are starting to wilt and dry up under the heat of the sunlight. Buddhi visits his friend, Aarti. "My dear friend, this year, the drought has killed the flowers in my garden. Do you know any flower that doesn’t wither or dry out?" Buddhi asked Aarti. "Yes, flowers that made of paper and plastic will never wither or dry out. If it rains, paper flowers will be damaged, but plastic ones won’t," said Aarti. Buddhi goes back home and pulls out all the flowers in his garden. He buys plastic flowers and plants them in another patch of his garden. In the afternoon, as he looks at the garden from the balcony, Buddhi feels a gentle breeze touch his face. But instead of carrying the sweet scent of flowers, the wind brings a strange and strong smell. The next day, Buddhi goes to Aarti's house. "My dear friend," says Buddhi. "My garden is beautiful now, but it doesn’t have the usual scent of flowers. The air even smells strange like the smell of a sewer. What should I do?" "Just spray your flowers with perfume," suggests Aarti. Following his friend's suggestion, Buddhi sprays his plastic flowers with perfume. Nevertheless, his garden still gives a strong, stinky sewer smell. Buddhi goes back to see Aarti. "My dear friend, my garden still smells like a sewer," says Buddhi. Aarti answers, "Buddhi, it’s the wind that spreads the smell. Just place a fan in your garden, so you will only smell the scent of flowers. Therefore, Buddhi puts a fan in his garden so it spreads the perfume scent of the flowers. Finally, Buddhi gets to smell the scent of flowers. But he misses the butterflies, bees, and birds that used to come to his garden every day. Aarti suggests that Buddhi buy plastic birds, bees, and butterflies. Buddhi follows his suggestion and starts flying it in his garden with help from his friends and neighbors. However, it causes a bad accident. The plastic toys crash into each other and fall to the ground. Some people get angry, and a fight starts. Buddhi sighs to Aarti. "The toys you suggested caused a disaster, Aarti! They crashed into each other, fell, and caused an argument and a fight." "Oh no!" says Aarti. "Fighting is wrong! If we see people fighting, we should stop them. And if they don’t want to stop, they should be punished." "But you're responsible for all this mess, Aarti," Buddhi says, getting even more upset. "I have ruined my garden and spent so much money on a fake garden. Flowers, perfume, a fan, butterflies, everything! YOU are the one who should be punished!" "My dear friend," Aarti answers calmly, "We should always listen to other people’s advice. But before doing it, we must think carefully first. If someone tells you that a crow has stolen your ears, will you chase the crow or will you think about it first?" Aarti’s words make Buddhi realize his mistake. "It’s natural for seasons to pass, for flowers to bloom, then wither, dry up, and die," Buddhi says to himself. "I should have never go against the laws of nature." "My dear friend," Aarti asks Buddhi that seem to think really hard, "Do you need another advice?" "Ah, no, that’s enough," Buddhi jokes. "I know what I should do now." The next day, Buddhi removes all the plastic flowers from his flower patch and throws them into the trash can. He also moves the fan. Then, he plants new flowers in his garden, but this time is the real flowers, not the fake one. With great patience, Buddhi waters the flowers and takes good care of them. ﻿ A few weeks later, the garden is full of natural flowers and looks beautiful. Birds, bees, and even butterflies come back. Buddhi feels happy to see the garden come back to life. He is truly grateful to nature for that amazing gift. Not hearing any news about Buddhi, Aarti comes to visit. Buddhi invites him to walk around the garden. He smiles and hugs Aarti, In the middle of beautiful flowers and their sweet scent filling the garden.
author: silvi serang

title: My Grandma and Grandpa
text: She takes good care of the whole family and makes sure that everyone lives peacefully. I live in a big family with 10 members, and my grandmother is the one who takes care of everyone with great patience. She still takes care of my father and siblings like little children. At her age, she is still excellent at her job and teaches me to respect my elders. To respect the elders. She never made excuses for her work. Grandma still remembers the stories she used to hear from her grandmother and tells them to me and my cousins ​​every night. She always makes sure we understand and find the moral message in it. Every story she tells has a deep meaning that is a life lesson for us. She also knows how to lift my spirits. If I am successful today, most of it If I am successful today, it is mostly thanks to him. He used to teach me Math and Science when I was in school because my parents were working. Although he was not a professional teacher, he was the best teacher I ever had. I still remember the formulas he taught me when I was little. He is one of the reasons behind my success. If today I am appreciated for my attitude and manners, it is all thanks to him. He taught me how to respect elders. My grandfather is named Narasaya. He is 74 years old and is the head of our family. All the family members love, obey and respect him. He loves to read, from newspapers, novels, magazines to articles. I enjoy spending time with him. He teaches me manners and loves me very much. Every evening, he takes me to the nearest park. We play hide and seek, cricket and snakes and ladders together. He is an inspiration to me. When I grow up, I want to be like him. Now they are both. The oldest members of the family bear all the responsibilities of the family. They give full attention and care to all the family members. Having grandparents is a blessing. They have shaped the lives of our parents, and without them, we would not have learned much about life. They tell us stories, each with a beautiful moral message. Their stories may be imaginative, but they reflect life as it is. Grandparents are the best friends for children, with whom they can freely share their secrets. They are a gift that we should cherish. In today's world, many have forgotten their role because of the tendency to live in small families. We must realize that they are a precious gift that teaches us to respect others and live a good life in the future. Grandparents are responsible figures, teaching us to be good citizens in the future. Without their presence, life would not be as peaceful as it is. They are the decision makers in the family, ensuring that we make the best choices. Thanks to their education, we are on the right path. They teach us about mistakes and guide us in a better direction. Therefore, grandparents are family members. the most precious, without them, our life will be difficult. Therefore, we must appreciate their role in our lives. As they grow old, it is our responsibility to take good care of them and spend time with them.
author: Shinta Adelia

title: Mini
text: Once upon a time, There lived a small girl named Mini in a provincial town in Assam. She was imaginative and intelligent, but her parents remained oblivious of her gifts. When she came first in class or won a medal in school, unlike most parents who are in awe of their children, Mini's mother never gave importance to her achievements. When she was 8 years old, her mother gave birth to a baby boy, and it was declared that she is a grown-up girl now, who should take responsibility for herself, her siblings and her parents. So, she combed her mother's hair, while her mother never combed her hair. She was taken to a scary fat lady once a month, who chopped Mini's hair in an ugly manner. Tears fell from her eyes looking at herself in the mirror while the ugly lady and her mother laughed with amusement. Her father was a bus-in-ness man because he was always busy. She saw him for two hours in a day. One hour in the day and one hour at night. He never talked to her or played with her. So, she lived in her imaginary world, in the company of mermaids, fairies, princes and princesses. Her favourite story was The Twelve Dancing Princesses. She imagined herself inside the story. A land of the most delightful groves of trees, leaves of silver and gold. She imagined riding on a boat which took her to the illuminated castle on the other side of the lake and the merry music of trumpets. She danced there all night. She remained absorbed in her imaginary world. Days turned into nights, months to years, and the years brought her womanhood. At twelve, it was declared that she had become a nasty creature who bled every month and made a nuisance. She remained like this for the next three years of her life, an ugly girl, neither a child nor a woman. One day, she became a woman. A little woman. Adorable, pretty, beautiful. A spring of cherry blossoms and blooming roses. She became a prized possession. Thus, men from lands far and near – kings, princes, businessmen, poets, writers, goldsmiths and blacksmiths; everybody was smitten by her charm. Her body bloomed like a red rose, with a sweet smell that enchanted kings and servants alike. But she still felt alone. She looked for love everywhere. In distant lands and fields, In kings and knights, In foot soldiers and farmers. But she was disappointed. So, one day, she left her house and started living in a beautiful cottage in a faraway land. The cottage was full of books which she could read all day. She met a little squirrel who became her friend and companion for the rest of her life.

title: He's gone..
text: I woke up in the morning, greeted my parents, had a delicious breakfast and waited for the bus outside with my mom stroking my uniform. Hi, nice to meet you. I'm Avantika, Avanti or Ans, whatever you call me. I'm 12 years old and I'm an Indian girl. Anyway, back to the story, the bus arrived and I got into the bus. Luckily, the seat next to my best friend Aarika was empty and I sat next to her. We chatted with each other all the way to school. Passing the day by helping my friends, playing together and making jokes. I read a book for a while and slept on my favorite bed with my stuffed monkey named Koko. Then, my father gave me a goodnight kiss. “I have an ordinary life and that will change soon.” Sunday was a holiday for dad and he didn't think it was a good idea for me to go out because Vijay had been hanging out with bad guys a lot lately. It wasn't the first time my parents had objected to me going to a party and I was determined to do it my way. But they still said no. I was so upset all day, I didn't even see my father at night. The next day, I went to school with Mishi and Sonu. I arrived home to find my mother sitting at the dining table worried. “Dad is in the hospital, Avanti. I just got a call from them, let's go to the hospital now and mom will explain to you on the way”. “Avanti, move” he said. But I didn't move. I felt as if my body stiffened suddenly. Mom took my hand and pulled me towards the car. Mom told me that Dad had an accident when he was about to take his lunch break. His car hit something and his condition is critical now. 15 minutes later, I looked at my father. HE'S IN A COMA!. I didn't go to school for almost a month and Mama also stayed at home. Days and nights passed in loneliness and despair, maybe even hope. Until one day her vitals dropped and she was gone. Just gone in an instant. I started crying like my world had stopped and shattered. When mom got the news, she was devastated. The next day, the notary came to the house to read out dad's will and said that dad had left all his assets to me and mom. Mom said that Dad's funeral would take one week and after that, I would go to school. Mom knew that it would be hard for me to get back to normal, but she couldn't take my education for granted. The saddest part is that things still go on as usual. No one could stop acknowledging the fact that someone so precious to someone had died. The sun was still rising from the east, people were doing their usual activities, and I was still looking forward to going to school and forgetting everything that happened in my life. The changes in my life hardly had any impact on anyone else. A week later was the day of father's funeral. I just stood there as father's brother began to bury him. I don't remember much about that day, except for the tears of the people as we said goodbye to Dad. It was a good thing that I had a family that always supported each other. On the day I had to go back to school, I was very tired and it showed on me. I got into the bus and sat next to Aarika. It was quiet and awkward between the two of us until she said, “I'm sorry, but I'm always here for you. I just can't imagine it”. I rested my head on her shoulder, looking out the window to see the raindrops and the bus driving towards the school. At school, I had to pass through corridors that looked at me with pity and treated me well. “Avantika take a break, you can lie down”. Those were words of concern from people I didn't even know at all. I know that they came from good intentions, but I hoped that all those words of concern could bring father back to me. I glanced out the bus window, looking at the father who gave his daughter an ice cream and bought her a balloon. I never regret anything, I should be done with this. I could also still recall a very beautiful moment with my father when I was a child. I returned home and thought about today's events. Aarika was the only person who was by my side at school. Many of my friends had distanced themselves from me, and others shared rumors about me, my father and mother. Some said that dad was an alcoholic, and others said that dad was depressed. It was very sad but I had to get used to being the new loser and miserable girl. The three of us could spend time together after school. She thought it was a good idea and she intended to go to this new restaurant and we could go there together for snacks in the afternoon and shopping afterwards. I quickly got ready and after that we were already in the car. We stopped in front of a restaurant and it was a very cute place, more like a cafe. The place was surrounded by plants like in nature. We ate a lot of food and ended with banana ice cream. Then we went to a bookstore, which I asked my dad for recommendations beforehand and he told me that he really liked Hardy as a kid and Roald Dahl growing up. After that we went to a clothing store where we got tons of clothes and had a lot of fun trying on the clothes we had chosen. I bought a shirt for Dad with my savings, then the kits went to the supermarket to shop for dinner. I looked at the shelves full of sweets as my parents went shopping, ending up with a container of skittles and a bag of marshmallows, not forgetting some fruit juice for Sonu. We ended the day by cooking together and watching a movie afterwards. Dad read me a story before I went to bed and it was a perfect day for me. Before going to bed, I made sure that I apologized for our previous argument and that I appreciated my father.

title: Bright Sona help her mother
text: I want to make a pattern too," Sona said. Mum gave Sona a piece of paper and some colouring. The room is full of objects that will be used to make patterned fabric. "Sona, sit outside and try making a pattern. Listen carefully to the sounds when Mum prints the motif" Sona sat at a small table outside the house. When there was no sound coming from the room, Sona knew that Mum was applying colours to her printing press. Then, Sona would also apply colours to the printing press. When she heard the clicking sound, Sona will press the printing press onto the fabric. ﻿ Silence- click, silence- click, Mother and Sona worked together. ﻿ However, there was another small sound that Sona heard, a jingle-jingle-jingle, which made her smile. A few moments later, Mom exclaimed, “Sona, have you seen Mom's keys? I can't find them anywhere.” Sona went to Mother. She hugged her waist. “Sona, this is not the time to play!” said Mom, looking at the things around her. “I need to get the paint out of the closet. I need the key. Please find Mom's key. ” Sona pulled the end of the odhni tucked into her mother's waist. The key was tied to the end of the odhni, and it made a jingling sound. “Oh! How did you know the key was here?” Mother asked in surprise. “Mother, I listened carefully,” Sona laughed. “Silence -click- clink, silence- click- clink!” “You are indeed clever, Sona!” said Mother.

title: A Cloud Full of Trash
text: She is also the unhappiest girl in her class. She might even be the most unhappy girl in the world. Friends? Cheekoo doesn't have any friends anymore. No one wants to play with Cheekoo. Because she has a cloud over her head. A cloud of GARBAGE. Friends? Cheekoo doesn't have any friends anymore. No one wants to play with Her. Because she has a cloud over her head. A cloud of GARBAGE. Orange peels and biscuit wrappers, broken toys and pencil shavings, dented plastic bottles and colourful plastic bags. All surrounded by the buzzing of swarms of flies. No one wants to play with a girl who has a cloud of rubbish hanging over her. What if a rotten banana peel falls on your head? EWWWHH! Cheekoo couldn't even play hide and seek anymore. That cloud will always get her caught. ‘Let's walk to school together,’ she said to Sona. Sona ran in the opposite direction. ‘Can I borrow your pencil sharpener?’ she asked Sweety. Sweety's face soured and she went to sit with Asha. Cheekoo even had to eat lunch alone. Cheekoo knew that she should have listened to her grandmother. Grandma always told her not to litter. "Don't throw banana peels on the street!" "Throw empty biscuit wrappers in the bin." However, Cheekoo never listened. She just laughed and continued to litter. Cheekoo tried to run away. But the rubbish cloud followed her everywhere. Cheekoo picked up a broom to get rid of the cloud. But the rubbish wouldn't go away. Cheekoo tried EVERYTHING. She shouted and asked the cloud to leave her alone. She even tried throwing the cloud into the rubbish bin. But the rubbish cloud wouldn't leave. Cheekoo became very upset. Then something happened! Cheekoo saw Bala throwing banana peels on the road. Cheekoo was upset. Didn't he see the clouds above her head? ‘Hey, you!’ she shouted. "Don't throw the peel on the road. Someone might slip!" Because Bala was afraid of the rubbish cloud, she threw the banana peel into the rubbish bin. The next day, the rubbish cloud became even smaller! ‘How did that happen?’ Cheekoo wondered. Then, Cheekoo saw Reema's aunty throwing away a plastic bag. ‘Aunty!’ Cheekoo said. ‘Please pick up these bags so they can be used again.’ Aunty Reema picked up the bags and left. The next day when Cheekoo woke up, the cloud was much smaller. Cheekoo smiled. Now she knew what to do. When someone litters biscuit wrappers or pencil shavings, Cheekoo stops them. She picks up all the plastic bottle rubbish and puts it in the bin. The village became cleaner and cleaner. And Cheekoo's cloud got smaller and smaller. Until one day, it was gone. COMPLETELY. Cheekoo is now probably the happiest girl in the world. Cheekoo never litters anymore. She actually likes living in a clean village. But she's also afraid that the rubbish cloud will come back, one day. Who knows! Let's Talk About Rubbish Have you ever wondered what happens to the rubbish you throw away? Fear not, it doesn't become a cloud over your head. Rubbish ends up in a landfill near your home. When you litter, rubbish collects on the roadside. Some of it goes into the drains, carried by the water discharged from your house. This clogs the drains and attracts flies that will spread disease! UH! No one likes living in a dirty neighbourhood. Just ask Cheekoo. How to keep rubbish clouds from forming We can start by not littering our neighbourhood. Always, always put rubbish in the bin look around you and find a bin. After eating a banana, don't throw it on the street. Put the peel in a small bag until you find a rubbish bin. - There are many things that you might think are useless, like the bag you put the banana peel in. Not everything is rubbish. So don't throw the bag with the peel! Take the bag home and reuse it. Close the bin so flies can't get inside.
author: Davi Chalid

title: The Dragonfly and the Frog
text: He didn't know what to do, so he stopped flying. He landed on a beautiful leaf. The rain stopped. The sun shone brightly. The dragonfly flew until it was near a beautiful tree. There was a pond in front of it, where the source of the melodious song came from. The dragonfly immediately flew to the pond. There, curiously, he saw a large frog singing. The frog's song attracts the attention of other dragonflies. The dragonfly was puzzled. How could a frog, its enemy, sing such a beautiful song to them? Then the frog told his story. When he was a tadpole, other frogs made fun of his voice, only a dragonfly became his friend. From then on he sang only for them. From then on, the dragonfly decided to stay near the pond for a while and listen to the beautiful frog song.

title: A Special Painter
text: Naya wants to draw a peacock. Tian likes to draw cats. Bintang wants to draw a polar bear. Haura was curious. ‘What animal do you want to draw?’ she asked Teo. ‘I want to draw all the animals!’ Teo replied. Tian was sharpening a pencil, ‘Do you want to use a brush or a pencil?’ she asked. ‘I'll use both,’ Teo said. Bintang took out her crayon box and asked, ‘Are you going to draw with your right hand?’ Teo was confused. ‘I'll try drawing with both hands.’ Naya was mixing colours. ‘What colours are you going to use?’ she asked. ‘I'll wear them all!’ Teo said cheerfully. But Teo could not hold the brush in her right hand because she had no fingers. The brush kept falling over. Teo tried to draw a chicken first. But then, her hands were full of paint stains here and there. Teo was about to give up hope. Suddenly, she noticed a funny pattern that had accidentally formed on her palm. It looked like a duck! Teo has an idea! Teo coloured her hands brown. She laughed happily. ‘Now, I will draw directly with my hands,’ she said. Teo tapped his hand on the corner of the paper. She smiled and added a few more shades of brown. Hey, look. That's a very cute puppy! Teo made two yellow patterns with her hands and arms. Then he added orange dots on top. Look, it's a giraffe! Next, Teo painted her feet brown and stepped on the paper. He drew some lines. Wow, that's great! It turned out to be an adorable bear.﻿ Teo went on to paint her heels with blue and pink colours, and then stamped them on paper. Add a few lines, and, lo and behold, beautiful, colourful birds appear. ‘The train that takes us around the zoo doesn't exist yet,’ Teo said. ‘Does anyone want to draw it with me?’ This was the most incredible painting class! Together, the kids painted the most marvellous picture.

title: The Gold Bars in the chest
text: Once upon a time, there was a merchant named Rahul. He was living in a city with his family. He lived with 2 sons, a daughter, a dog and a wife. He travelled around the world for selling and buying things. Once he went to a small village where their was a fair going on. he went into the fair where many people were selling and buying things. He bought a chest and went home. After reaching home he opened the chest and found a gold bar in it.He was amazed to see the gold bar. He sold the bar and bought some new clothes and other things for his family. He found out in some days that every day an gold bar appeared in the chest. And so, he became lazy and forgot how he travelled around the world and worked hard to earn money. One day the gold bars stopped appearing and he became poor. Thus, he learnt that hard work is the most important thing in life.

title: How the Tiger got it's Stripes
text: They only had an orange mane. Nobody was scared of tigers. They did not look ferocious enough. That is why all the tigers didn't hunt. One day, a generous tiger named Liam was walking by the riverbank, and he saw a tiny rabbit unable to pick mangoes from a tall mango tree. She was there with her kids, whose stomachs were growling loudly. Liam jumped up high and hit the tree with his hind legs. The mangoes fell down with a thud. The mother rabbit turned into the god of animals. Liam was surprised and bowed hastily. The god said to him 'Aha! Liam are you, well boy, I am seeing you for quite a few years and I am glad to say that you have done some good generous deeds, and the time has come to grant you a wish.' The tiger replied, 'I want all the tigers to have magnificent stripes. The God of animals said, ' Oh yes, my child I can give you that wish. But only one condition, that you must show intelligence on your way to gain it. If you don't, well, let's just say you will be in danger. Also, you will have to journey through many lands. Use your wits and conscience along the way. Otherwise, what you want to gain will be difficult'. Saying this, he disappeared. Liam journeyed through deserts and mountains, through snowstorms and sandstorms, until he finally reached the village. He was going where his mind and senses told him to go, because the god of animals had not told him the location where his wish might come true. He was in the village. He didn't know what to do now. 'Well, the god said that I must show intelligence while using conscience.' But unfortunately, he didn't regard the intelligence bit much. Suddenly, his stomach began growling. He hadn't eaten anything for a week. Liam started searching for food. He came near a sweet shop and found a box of fresh and sweets on a table outside the shop. Then he saw a man sitting gazing at the sweets hungrily. Liam picked the box up and gave it to the man. The man said,' Thank you dear tiger, my name is Neeraj. Would you like to have something in return for your kindness?' The tiger told him all about his adventure. The man nodded and said 'I might know where to go. There is a farm not far from here. The farmer might give you shelter for a day or two, then you might have figured out how to gain your wish. But mind you, he doesn't like animals that much.' Liam thanked the man and started heading north. After a while, he arrived. He found the farmer and told him his story. He then asked,' Dear farmer, can you give me shelter for a day?' 'Only if you show me intelligence.' Said the man after a while. 'Hmmm...' Thought the tiger and then said, 'Can you show me how to do intelligence first. 'Okay then. Said the farmer and then brought some matchsticks and a strong rope. He then quickly tied Liam to an oak tree and lit the matchstick. He put the blazing matchstick near Liam's feet. Liam started shouting frantically. He said,' I told you to show me intelligence, not burn me, you complete maniac! Said the angry tiger, roaring.' You told me to show intelligence, and I did. I wouldn't like some tiger figuring out some silly wish and destroying my crop and stealing things.' Said the farmer, smiling. Liam replied, I don't steal things! NOR DO I DESTROY CROPS! Liam quickly started sharpening his claws and scratched the rope here and there. Somehow, he got out. Liam found a lake and jumped into it. Liam came out after a while. Then he stared at his own reflection into the lake. Apparently, he seemed to have escaped from the fire a bit late, and there were burn marks all over his body in the shape of stripes. And, from that day on, tigers had magnificent stripes. Animals were scared of them. The tigers had started hunting.
author: saumya shankar
illustrator: Aashlesha Marathe; Annada Menon; David Yambem; Debasmita Dasgupta; Deepa Balsavar; Ekta Bharti; Huynh  Vu Tuong; Jacob Kono; Jonathan  Field; Narayan Prasad  Bohaju; Priya Dali; rinnie; Rohan Chakravarty; Rohan Dahotre

title: Unnie and Innie
text: Summer has arrived! Kids don’t have to go to school in the summer. They can sleep as late as they want! It’s the first morning of summer break and Unnie wants to go play. “Innie, do you want to come to my house and play?” Unnie asks. “I’m busy reading a book, Unnie,” Innie replies. That afternoon, Unnie is still playing alone. “Hey, Innie, come play with me!” Unnie called. “I already told you, Unnie! I’m busy reading a book!” said Innie. The sun begins to set, and Unnie grows tired of playing by himself. “Come on, visit my house, Innie! I have so many toys!” he says. “I’m busy reading, Unnie!” Unnie gets annoyed. “What’s so interesting about that book?” “I have to find out!” Unnie walks over to the tree where Innie is reading. “What’s in that book?” he asks. “I’m rescuing the princess,” Innie tells him. “Really? Where?” Unnie says excitedly. “Show me!” Now, Unnie and Innie are fighting monsters together. Finally, they save the princess! For the rest of the summer. title: Oci and Oni
text: Pancasila is?" "Pancasila is the five principles of our country, Sis." "That's right! Pancasila is like a foundation that supports Indonesia. There are five principles, namely Belief in the One Almighty God, Just and Civilized Humanity, Unity of Indonesia, Democracy Guided by Wisdom in Deliberation/Representation, and Social Justice for All Indonesian People." "Wow, you know huh!?" "Yes, we just learned about it at school. But, you already know about it, Oni." "Sister, what are the benefits of knowing Pancasila?" "There are so many benefits! Pancasila guides us to live in harmony, respect each other, and work together. Pancasila also teaches us to believe in God, be just and civilized, and love our country." "That's what you want. Come on, let's practice the values ​​of Pancasila in our daily lives!"

title: I want cake
text: I want to eat cake for breakfast! Mother: You can't. You have to eat healthy food. Kids: Why? Healthy food doesn't taste delicious. Cake tastes very delicious. Mother: No problem. But don't you want to grow tall? Child: Yes. Mom: Then you should drink milk and eat vegetables. Milk contains calcium to strengthen your bones. Do you want to be a strong child? Child: Yes, mom. Mom: That means you have to eat meat as a source of protein. If you don't like eating meat, you can replace it with beans. Child: Why is protein important? Mother: Because protein is useful for building muscles. Child: Tell me more about nutrition. Mother: Do you want to have clear eyesight and be smart? Then you should eat lots of fruits and vegetables because they contain minerals that are important for the body. Child: I know carrots are good for the eyes. Mother: That's right. Child: I want to grow tall and strong. Mom: Good but you can't have cake for dinner. Child: All right. I'll drink some milk. Then I'll eat scrambled eggs as protein and bread as carbohydrate. I'll also cut up a banana and strawberries. Bananas and strawberries are my favorite fruits. Mom: If you do this every day, you'll grow up to be a strong child. Question: What do you eat for breakfast? Did you eat a healthy breakfast? Why is it important to eat healthy food? Do you also want to eat cake for breakfast? Can you eat cake? Why is protein important? Why are carbohydrates important? Name the kinds of foods that are healthy to eat? Why do you want to eat healthy food? What health problems will arise if you don't eat healthy food?

title: Saving Plant Life
text: There was a small house with a pretty garden behind it. The garden was full of shady trees and colorful flowers. Beautiful butterflies fluttered there. They, along with small birds, often played around the mango trees and pomegranate trees. In the house lived two brothers, Chandan and his younger brother, Nandan. Every day, Chandan took care of the garden. He watered the plants and cleaned the garden. Chandan always wakes up early in the morning to pick flowers from his garden. Then, he distributed the flowers to his neighbors. The neighbors are happy with Chandan's kindness and often wish him the best. Chandan often asked his younger brother, Nandan, to take care of the garden with him but Nandan never listened. One morning, Chandan saw Nandan in the garden. He thought Nandan was pulling plants. Chandan became very angry. Chandan shouted to his brother, “What are you doing, Nandan?” Nandan was frightened and replied, "Brother, the plants are attacked by pests. I told Father, and he asked me to spray the pest medicine." Chandan was surprised to hear this and said, "Well done, sister! You have saved these plants. These plants will surely grow more beautiful and do you good!"
author: Dea Mustabsiroh

title: Pre-exam Fever
text: She asked, “Mom, does this make you happy?” “Don't be afraid, Mom,” I said, dancing like a clown. I told funny stories until Mom smiled and forgot her fear. No one was allowed to visit, neither neighbors nor friends, while Mother's fever continued to linger. Finally, the day of the exam arrived. Mom had recovered and was cheerful again. Mom was no longer anxious, and her fever had subsided. Do you all know? My mother successfully obtained her bachelor's degree!
author: Rizky Nugraha

title: Why is it hot??
text: He was looking at the sun. Why has it been so hot these past few days? On the other side of the world, there was a camel named Tata. He was looking at the sun. It's hot! I'm already thirsty, why is it so hot? These are Jojo and Dodi, students of SD Bangsa. They just came back from the supermarket. Come on, let's go Jo! I'm getting hot!? Yeah, why does the sun look different, Dodi? This is Alang, an eagle who sees the grievances of the earthlings. Aachh... All right! This can't be ignored. Finally, Alang managed to fly to the sun. Sun, did you know? Right now, the people of Earth are feeling very hot. Hiks... hiks... A ku sakit Lang, demam! The high fever burned the sun blanket. Alang advised the sun to take a dip in the river. Thank you Alang, the fever is finally down!

title: Poni, the elephant with the short trunk
text: Where could he be? Poni?! The elephant with the short trunk? Haha... Momo's right, why is Poni different from the other elephants? True, I think it's really funny, haha!! We shouldn't be like that. Guys... Poni is also our friend. "Oh, how happy I am! I'll come back to play with my friends after yesterday's all-day downpour," said Poni. Poni walked, singing happily, towards where his friends had gathered. He was very cheerful that day. When he was close to the location, Poni walked silently. He planned to surprise his friends and then they would laugh together. However, he didn't go through with it. He overheard his friends' conversation. Poni changed his mind about meeting his friends. He decided to go straight home, taking a different path. He stopped briefly by the river. Seeing his reflection made him even sadder. Yes, I am different. I have a short trunk. Suddenly, Aunt Langlang saw Poni; she wondered why the baby elephant was alone around here. Why are you sad, Poni? Poni told Aunt Langlang about his sadness. She had a clever plan. "Poni, go find the crocodile at the end of the river; he can help you," she said. Happy with the idea, Poni set off to find the crocodile. Okay, Aunt, I'll go find Uncle Crocodile. Thank you! Poni explained to the crocodile what Aunt Langlang had said. Hi, Uncle Crocodile! Aunt Langlang said you can help me. It turned out that Aunt Langlang had lied to Poni. She had tricked Poni so that he would be eaten by the crocodile. she lied to you, kid. Now you'll be my lunch. Haha. What?! No uncle, I'm just going. Poni and the crocodile had a tug-of-war with their trunks. Finally, Poni was able to free herself from the crocodile. But she was surprised, "Hah!? Why did my trunk get longer? How did this happen?" said Poni. Poni immediately went home to see her mother. Poni told his mother about what happened. "Poni, next time you should be more careful and only play in safe places. It's best not to trust strangers. Now, start getting used to your new, longer trunk," her mother advised. "Now I can pick apples from the tree," said Poni happily. Poni has adapted now. she can play in the water with her long trunk. Uncle Danil, hearing what happened to Poni, felt relieved because Poni was fine with her new trunk. "Thank goodness, everything worked out," said Uncle Danil. Children! We often think that physical appearance is the most important thing, and we forget the strengths we and others possess. God created us all different, and each of us has a purpose, making each of us special. As long as you are grateful and have a good heart, God will always protect and love you.
author: Tika Yuniarti
illustrator: Ketan Raut; Wiehan de  Jager; Wiehan de Jager

title: A Mother's Love
text: We never expected a bird to find our balcony a safe haven. She built a nest in an empty flowerpot in the corner, and before you know it, she had laid three shiny speckled eggs and suddenly became overprotective, only flying away to get her food. Soon, two of them hatched and we were ecstatic! It was one of our happiest moments. The baby birds were just little furry bundles of joy. They looked nothing like their mother. They huddled together for warmth and comfort when their mother would go to get food for them. One day, when they were a bit older, their mother went on an especially long trip. She was gone for two days and we were beginning to get worried. On the third day, we were making plans on how to feed them and how to keep them warm, when the next morning their mother came! She fed them and flew away to bring more food for their eager mouths. Soon, the once little pigeons had grown bigger and had started looking more like their mother. They would go and fly in short, clumsy bursts. Soon, their mother taught them the art of flight. We waved a teary goodbye, as they left the nest for good.

text: One afternoon the Samson family was sitting on a couch and were planning for a trip to California. They had a black cat named Minns. One day Minns was climbing on a tree until she fell into a pit. The white cat saw and was very scared for her. She meowed very loudly to tell her family, she also scratched the windows. This noise attracted Pip,the little sister. She saw this and called his elder brother, Larry. title: How to test real friend
text: There was a boy named Mario who had many friends. He was proud of having so many friends. One day, his grandfather told him, "Son, are your friends really true friends?" Mario replied, "Yes, Grandpa, they are all good friends of mine." Grandpa said, "Son, you should test them once." Saying this, Grandpa left the room, and when he returned, he had something in his hands, but Mario couldn't see it. Grandpa told him, "This is an invisible chair; it will help you find out who your true friends are." After hearing this, Mario went to school. During break called all his friends and asked them to stand in a circle while he stood inside this circle. He said to everyone, "Friends, today I will show you something amazing." He tried very hard to sit on that chair, but he fell down. He tried to sit again but fell again. All the kids laughed at him, but Guneet, Deepa, and Manisha helped him. Now he found his friends.

title: Elephant and Turtle
text: "I have to get back to home." For a day the turtle had been trying to climb the steep hole in the dark pond. His heavy eyes squinted against the sun rays hitting his eyes. He pushed himself up, slipping just an inch away from the land. "Help!" A huge silhouette blocked the sun, a trunk swooping the turtle up from the water. A face Turtle was yet to see.. The face staggered the Turtle, the sight of the huge elephant had the power to do such. Especially an elephant with deep wrinkles above a broken tusk. "...There you go." The turtle stepped away, closer back to the pond. "Who..Who are you?" "Hey I am just a friend. I heard your family searching for you and found you here-" "St-stay back-AAAH!" The claws slipped from the marshy grass. The Elephant swooped his trunk wrapping him tightly around his trunk. Covered with old bruises, the pain shot through his trunk. "NGH..not today!" THUD!...Dead silence. From the deep chasms of the grasslands insects crawled to see the quaking sight. The murmurs of the animals surrounded the lingering silence. The turtle opened his eyes. Ones darting all around. He checked himself. No scars. A wince echoed ahead, the animals forming a line, a piece of tusk fallen behind. The pond was about to claim him..and the scary elephant had kept him safe. "........God...." "..God." The elephant laughed, heaving on the ground. "...Crescent moon. The best kind one could watch all night. All night when tired." Really tired. The elephant pushed himself up, just one push more and- "OW!" Crack! Another piece flew, more pain seeping into his broken tusk. A sigh of resignation with heavy breathing. And dead silence all there was... "OI!" "Huh- OW!" The piece of tusk was chucked at the Elephant's trunk. "Who is it...t-turtle!?" He rubbed his eyes. Twice. "....You seem like you have seen a ghost." "What are you doing here!?" "I can ask the same thing to you." The elephant looked away. He couldn't argue with that. "...Look just go to your home. There's no saving an old one like me." The Turtle looked away rubbing his shell..dead silence perhaps- "LISTEN TO YOURSELF. WOULD YOU LISTEN TO ME IF I SAID THAT?" 'T-turtle..?" The turtle looked down, letting his frown shine for this once. "...In the pond when I was stuck, I was thinking that I was done for. Luck came and then I stepped away and you still saved me!" The turtle walked closer, nudging the large trunk. "I judged you by the cover and got the lesson the hard way. And I don't forget my lessons. " ﻿Dead silence. ﻿ ﻿For one last time. A smile formed on the old face. "Oh well. Neither do I." The dawn came, and the lands far away echoed with laughter and none. No place for fear. ﻿
author: Kabir Nair

title: The Werewolf's sacrifice
text: Once upon a time, in Delhi, lived a boy named Rohan. He loved travelling with his friends. He and his friends made a plan to go on a camp in a forest. After some days of waiting, finally the day of the trip arrived. He woke up early, booked his cab, grabbed his luggage & went to the train station where he met his friends. They got on the railway station. After nine hours in the train, they finally reached their destination They met the camp instructor, then in a bus they reached the forest. They set their camps in the middle of the forest and started to cook food. It was a full moon night, but Rohan couldn't see the moon because the trees were hiding it. After cooking they started a campfire and sat around it in a circle. When Rohan sat the moonlight fell directly onto him. He started to feel weird. His body felt like it was burning his & chest felt like growing. His teeth became sharper, fur started growing on his body, his body became massive & his clothed ripped. He was now a massive wolf who stood on two of his legs. The people in the camp started to scream for help but nobody was there to help. They were in the middle of a forest with a werewolf chasing them. They all started running in different directions. The werewolf stayed there. Rohan's friends found a hiding spot & hid there. They settled in the hiding spot, scared, confused & sad because they had lost their friend. They were very confused. They never thought they would be a friend of a werewolf. They started searching for firewood. Suddenly, they heard a tiger's roar. Out of the trees, a tiger appeared They started panicking. They thought they were going to die. They started screaming for help. They thought they had reached the end of their lives, but they were wrong. To their surprise, from the woods appeared the same werewolf that they thought had attacked them, to be more specific, their friend, Rohan. The werewolf started fighting with the tiger. Rohan fearlessly attacked the tiger, in the form of a wolf. The tiger attacked him, but Rohan was no less. after an hour of fighting, finally the tiger lost. It fell on the ground; it was now dead. Rohan was also severely injured. He reached his human form He reached his human form, then fell on the cold grass. His friends had misunderstood him. He was trying to save their life while they thought he was attacking them. His friends wanted to thank him, but he was no more. His friends rushed him to the hospital in their bus, but even after all the treatment, Rohan couldn't make it. The sacrifice he made for his friends was great. Even after dying, their friendship still remained in their hearts.
author: Shreyans Seth
illustrator: Ajit Narayan; Asuki Tachikawa; Elise Elavumkal; Khushi Sah; Rohan Dahotre; Sarayu Manoj R; Wiehan de Jager

title: Simi and the Snake
text: Simi was a little girl who loved to ask questions. One sunny day, she saw something wiggly in the grass. “Hissss!” said the little snake. Simi wasn’t scared. She crouched down and smiled. “Hello, little snake!” she said. Simi asked, “Did you get your name because you move like an ‘S' or because you sound like an ‘S’ when you hiss?” The snake stopped and thought. It slithered slowly into the shape of an ‘S’. “Hissss,” it said again. Simi giggled. “That’s both!” Simi drew an ‘S’ in the dirt with a stick. “S is for Snake,” she whispered. “And S is for Smart,” said the snake, and it slid away.
author: Theodore Cochran

title: Mumma....it hurts!!
text: Anni was a lazy girl. She always had an excuse to skip schools. Sometimes, it would be "Ouch! Mummy my tummy hurts. Mom, won't you give me the sweet lovely medicine?" or "I think so I will fall of headache". Her mother who knew her very well, used to give her the medicine thinking that when the right time comes, she will learn lesson. As soon as the evening turned, she jumped out of the couch and went to play with her friend Charki. Soon the semesters came near and all of them started preparing for it. The school began taking a lot of revisions, but Anni sat in her own dream world. The next day Charki told her about the semesters. " Oh no! I almost forgot that our semesters are going to start the next week. None of my notes are completed. Charki, can you please give me your note books?" That night, Anni sat down preparing her notes. Till the next morning, her eyes reddened. Finally the nervousness struck the students and nothing but the scratching of pens could be heard. Charki was the first one to get out of the hall. She waited and waited for Anni. At last, she came out crying. The paper was too difficult for her. At the result day, everyone got promoted except Anni. From that day on, she promised herself to utilize the education that she was receiving from her school. Activity time! Think of 5 occasions when you behaved like Anni and 5 occasions when you were like Charki. Do you think Anni will perform well at her exams? Find out yourself!
author: Nyra Yadav
