title: The Lost Pen
text: The Lost Pen In a bustling classroom filled with the sounds of laughter and chatter, I, Lilly, sat at my desk, excitedly preparing for art class. My favourite part of the day was when I got to create with my special supplies, especially my sparkly pink pen. It was no ordinary pen; it was a gift from my favourite uncle, who always encouraged my artistic talents. The pen glittered in the sunlight, and I loved how it glided across the paper, making my drawings come to life. As the teacher announced it was time for art, I reached into my pencil case, my heart sinking as I realized my beloved pen was missing. Panic set in. “Where could it be?” I thought, my mind racing with possibilities. I remembered using it during my last art project, but the memory was a blur. Had I left it on my desk? Did it fall on the floor? Determined to find it, I decided to launch an investigation. I approached my friends, who were busy chatting and getting their supplies ready. “Have you seen my pink pen?” I asked, my voice tinged with worry. My friends, sympathetic to my plight, joined in the search. We looked under desks and around the classroom, calling out my pen's name like it was a lost puppy. “Pink Pen, where are you?” giggled Jenny, one of my best friends. But as the search went on without success, I began to feel uneasy.. I noticed my friends were whispering and giggling to each other, and a troubling thought crossed my mind. “What if they took it? What if they’re jealous of my pen?” The idea made me feel uncomfortable. I couldn’t believe I was doubting my friends, but the thought lingered in my mind, casting a shadow over my search. “They might think I’m too attached to it,” I thought, feeling a mix of frustration and sadness. “Maybe they wanted to make fun of me.” Despite these doubts, I tried to focus on finding my pen. As we searched, I retraced my steps from earlier in the day. “I remember using it during math class,” I said, leading my friends to the back of the room where I usually sat. We checked the shelves and the teacher's desk, but the pen was nowhere to be found. My heart sank further. “I should have been more careful,” I thought, wishing I had paid more attention to my belongings. Just then, Sam, a kind-hearted classmate, approached with a thoughtful look on his face. “Lilly, I think I might know where it is,” he said, a smile spreading across his face. Curious, I followed Sam as he led me to the art supply cabinet. “I saw a sparkly pink pen on the floor earlier. I picked it up and put it in my bag so it wouldn’t get lost,” Sam explained. My heart raced with hope. Could it be my pen? Sam reached into his bag and pulled out the sparkly pink pen. My eyes widened with joy. “That’s it! That’s my pen!” I exclaimed, taking it from him. A wave of relief washed over me, mixed with gratitude for my friend’s thoughtfulness. “Thank you so much, Sam! I thought I’d lost it forever!” As I held my pen, I felt a flicker of shame for doubting my friends. “I shouldn’t have thought they’d take it from me,” I realized. It was a lesson I needed to learn about trust and the importance of friendship. The rest of the class gathered around, sharing in my happiness, and the atmosphere brightened as we resumed our art projects. With my pink pen in hand, I felt inspired to create something beautiful. I started drawing a colourful landscape, imagining it as a magical world where my pen could dance and twirl across the page. That day, I not only found my pen but also learned about the importance of trusting my friends and not letting jealousy cloud my judgment. From that day on, I made it a point to keep my desk organized and always check for my pen before leaving class. And every time I used my sparkly pink pen, I remembered the little adventure of finding it and the kindness of my friend Sam.

title: Tuffy and Arjun
text: Arjun’s dog, Tuffy, was enormous — and he had one major flaw: he couldn’t help getting jealous of cats. Little Arjun grew tired after so many attempts to change Tuffy’s mind. Arjun was an orphan. To earn money he used to deliver pots with water to everybody's house. Today he got such less customers, because all of them were mad at his dog for attacking uncle Rajesh's cat. Though it wasn’t easy, Arjun refused to give up on Tuffy. Being the only dog in the village made Tuffy feel terribly lonely, and Arjun couldn’t bear to see him that way. Everybody even made fun of Arjun for having a dog. The next morning, Arjun’s eyes lit up with a terrific idea. He would bring home a cat and get it to play with Tuffy — because if there was one thing Tuffy couldn’t resist, it was chasing a ball. Tuffy was rolling in the mud, his shiny coat turning brown by the minute, and Arjun watched with a smile as he played joyfully with the cat. These days, Tuffy is beginning to love cats. He no longer growls when he sees one — instead, he runs over, eager to play.

title: The hilarious job interview
text: I was in a hurry, my train for Kanpur had already reached the station and I was still at home waiting for my taxi. "My dog is alone at home" I said to the taxi driver on phone. "I came to Delhi for an job interview but it's being my life test" I said to myself. 3 months ago I was peacefully playing with my dog in the lawn. I got a call from one of the big fours of India I was so much happy that I bought a new dog house for my dog. I also booked 1st class ac train tickets. 2 months later I gave my dog p edigree and left for Delhi I boarded my train and safely and reached Delhi. I got off my train and started to leave the station. Due to the excitement I left my phone in the train. My phone was ringing in the train. The TT kept my phone and at the next station gave my phone to lost and found. Meanwhile I joined a car pool till the bus stop. At the bus stop I boarded the bus for the company. When I reached the company A person started fighting with the conductor about money he saw me standing behind him so he asked me to pay online and he would give me the cash. I put my hand in my pocket to take the phone out, the phone was not there. I was terrified my heart beat ran faster than Usain Bolt. I pulled out my wallet and paid the fee. I rushed to the railway station and asked for my phone in the lost and found section. My meeting was fixed for 5 pm and it was already 4:50 pm. I sat and waited for my turn in the lost and found. After many tries I was not given my phone. I called the big fours from the call booth and asked for another appointment. They gave me another appointment. I rushed to the police station and complained. All of my emotions were mixing. I bought a new phone and gave my phone number to police. I walked down the street of Chandni Chowk. I was sweating from the scorching heat. My ears were busted from the noise. I felt dizzy so I walked in the Gurudwara. Inside felt relaxed. I slept there for an hour then I went to a hotel. The next day I got a call from ACP I rushed to the police station and found my phone. I rushed to the office. The receptionist told me to sit. I sat down. Few minutes later the receptionist asked for details. I opened my phone and gave the details 5 minutes later the head counsel came with a security guard "Are you sure that all your details are correct" asked the counsel "y..y...ya you can crosscheck" I murmured I gave all my details again. Soon I found that the details were wrong. I called the on number "Hello, all the details you have sent are wrong" I said the person on the other end hung up. I understood that it was a fraud. 5 minutes later I got a phone from my cousin brother "Hello" a faint voice came "Hello" I said worriedly My brother was silent I asked him what happened. He replied "I am sorry" and hung up. I was totally confused. My brother house was only 5 minutes away. I went there. I rang the bell. The door opened. My brother was in front of me. As soon as he saw me he fainted. I ran to the kitchen and brought water. I gave him and asked what happened He trembled and said "I was the one who said that you got an job" My face turned red "It was only a prank set up by mom and I" said my brother. My aunt came in the hall with fear on face. At once I got very angry. I was about to scream but the doorbell rang and delivery man entered and said "OTP sir" I sat in and my brother gave the OTP My brother slowly approached me and was trying to stop his smile the room was in a absolute silence for a minute. I asked what happened. They both shouted Happy Diwali and showed me a I phone. I was not surprised as I bought the same phone that too pro max. I showed him my phone. His mouth dropped. He sat down on the couch. Holding his head he said "Why... why it only happens with me" I comforted him and said to take the phone. I sat down and had tea with them. We started talking and went on talking, time flew and flew. Until my phone fell down I turned it on to see that its working or not and I saw the time. I was late for my train, I booked the taxi and called the driver. "My dog is alone at home" I said to the taxi driver on phone "Come fast" I shouted. The taxi driver took 15 minutes to come and pick me up. I reached the station just in time. My train was leaving the station it started to moving faster and faster I also ran faster and faster. I did not got first class but I entered the local coach. After getting pushed around, I reached Kanpur and played with my dog

title: Ira's Monsoon Feast
text: Ira stares out of her window. Giant monsoon clouds swim like grey whales above her. “Let’s go gather food for our monsoon feast, Iru,” Aai and Baba say, swinging her up. Off they go, walking past the nachni and the rice crops shooting up from the red earth. Maushi joins them and Ira’s cousins, too. They walk into the forest beyond the farms. They are looking for alambi, the small white mushrooms that grow wild on termite hills. Save one, take one, when our hands are full, we are done, done, done. They sing like they have been taught by Maushi, as they pluck the alambi. On the way back home, they collect wild greens. Ira plucks her favourite long, thin greens, phodshi. Three hands in height, Green leaves in our fields, Growing wild and bright. In their family vegetable garden, air potatoes, elephant yams and pumpkins are growing. The pumpkins will be many colours—orange and bright, green and light. Some tubers will grow as small as Ira’s fists, some as big as her belly. But, for the feast, Aai has saved their harvest of tubers and gourds from last year. Harvested from the rich, red soil, The gourds wait in the kitchen. Some to be planted again, some to boil. Ira, her cousins and their friends sit around with the tubers and gourds. They draw eyes and noses, brows and ears. Everyone has a big smile. Ajji shapes the nachni bhakris with her hand. Each bhakri blooms over the flame. Maushi chops the phodshi. In the pan, the green stems shrink, mixing with the prawns. Ajoba soaks the alambi, and helps Aai to clean it. They cook the onions, grated coconut and tomatoes to make a masala. The alambi sizzles in the gravy. Baba grates the long bottle gourd and stirs in the cardamom. The smell of the dudhi halwa spreads through the house. BOOM! Lightning crackles. Now, it is time to eat! EATING SEASONALLY The Earth’s climate is changing. We have unseasonal rainfall, or it rains too much, too quickly. Sometimes we have heat waves and long dry spells. This means that farming is getting harder. To make sure we are well-fed and safe from some of these climatic changes, we can alter some of our planting patterns and eating habits. Here’s a look at Ira’s family feast: Nachni, called finger millet, grows in hilly areas where the soil is not rich. It can withstand a lot of rain, and does not need many chemicals. Alambi are mushrooms, part of the fungi family, which grow in the Western Ghats during the monsoons. They grow only on termite hills, and are a very important member of the forest ecosystem, so we must harvest them with care. Wild greens like phodshi, gongura and water spinach sprout up during monsoons. These green leafy vegetables offer nutrition when not many other vegetables are ready to eat. Tubers like taro, cassava, elephant foot yam, and arrowroot live underground. They are very good at growing even if there is very heavy rainfall, or a flood. Gourds, like the ash gourd, are full of vitamins and minerals and can be saved for months. This is good in a changing climate because it means we will always have something nutritious to eat. Pumpkins are amazing because we can eat their leaves, flowers and fruits.

title: Pluto...our pet dog
text: I am going to tell a story about my childhood pet. It was a dog. His name was Pluto. Now you might think I’m talking about the former planet Pluto — no, never! We first met him during one of our Christmas holidays. Here, “we” means my younger brother and me. At that time, I was in Class 3, and he was in LKG. Our paternal uncle gifted him to us. Over time, he became a part of our life and family. Every morning before going to school, we usually spent time with our Plutachi. Whenever we felt too much love for him, we called him Plutachi. One day, just like any other day, we were playing with our pet Pluto when something unusual happened. A cat named Pusy from our neighbourhood made a strange hissing sound. After a few seconds, Pusy ran away from the scene. At first, we didn’t understand that she had seen a snake, and that’s why she ran away. Luckily, our Pluto saw the snake and attacked it. When he attacked the snake, it was very close to us. During the fight, the snake bit our Pluto. At last, our grandpa came and rescued Pluto by killing the snake. Because of the snake bite, Pluto partially lost his eyesight. After that, we both supported our Plutochi in everything. We arranged a special place for him in our living room. Whenever he wanted to pee or poop, he made a unique sound, and at the same time, we both rushed to him and helped him. Now, we are grown up, and he is very old and no longer capable of doing much. But whenever he hears our voices, he still raises his head with the utmost happiness. He is our family. We love him very much. ❤️

title: A Day in the park
text: Lucy and Tom are best friends. They live in the same neighborhood, but they are very different people. Lucy is kind, calm, and patient. She always thinks before she speaks. She likes reading books and listening to soft music. Tom, on the other hand, is funny, talkative, and a little careless. He loves adventure, loud music, and making jokes. Even though they are different, they get along very well. Lucy says, “You make me laugh, Tom.” Tom answers, “And you help me stay out of trouble!” One Saturday morning, Lucy calls Tom. “Hey Tom, let’s meet at Central Park today,” she says. Tom replies, “Good idea! But where exactly should we meet? The park is really big.” Lucy thinks for a moment and says, “Okay, come to the big fountain in the middle of the park. It’s easy to find. When you enter through the main gate, walk straight for about five minutes. Then, you’ll see a playground on your left. Turn left there, and you’ll see the fountain next to a tall oak tree.” Tom laughs, “You always give perfect directions, Lucy. I would just say, ‘meet somewhere near the trees!’” Lucy smiles, “That’s because I’m more careful than you.” After thirty minutes, Tom arrives at the park—but of course, he gets lost. He calls Lucy, “I think I’m near some benches and a food stand. I can’t see the fountain.” Lucy giggles, “Okay, turn right and walk past the lake. The fountain is behind it.” Tom says, “Ah, now I see it! You’re better with maps than I am.” Finally, Tom reaches the fountain. He is holding two ice creams—one chocolate and one strawberry. “Here you go, Lucy,” he says. “Chocolate for you, because you’re sweet and calm.” Lucy laughs, “Thanks, Tom. And you’re full of energy—just like strawberry flavor!” They sit down together on the bench near the fountain. The weather is warm, and the birds are singing. Tom starts to feed the ducks, but he drops half of his ice cream. Lucy says kindly, “You’re so careless sometimes.” Tom grins, “Yes, but life is more fun that way!” Lucy nods. “Maybe. You are funnier than me, but I think I’m more organized.” Tom agrees. “That’s true! You always know where we should go and what we should do.” As the sun begins to set, they walk home together. Tom says, “You know, Lucy, even though we’re very different, we make a great team.” Lucy smiles, “Yes, because you make me laugh, and I help you find your way.” They both laugh as they walk down the quiet street, happy to have each other as friends.

title: A Horrible Day
text: There were two best friends living in a town. The girl was named Savita, and the boy was named Ram. They were childhood friends from the start. They knew everything about each other. One day, Savita’s family decided to go on a trip. The trip was to a beautiful place, the beach. She was very excited as her birthday was the day after tomorrow. She and her family enjoyed the scenery of the beach and played many games on the beach. Then in the evening, the beach committee had organised a night party. Savita and her mother went to the party because at midnight, it would be Savita’s birthday. Her friend Ram prepared a gift for her to give after they came home. He did not have money, but he sold his watch to buy beautiful shoes for Savita. While returning from the trip, she and her family had an accident. In the accident, Savita lost her leg. On the other hand, Ram was very happy because Savita was returning home. After she arrived, Ram came to see Savita with the gift he had prepared for her. It was wrapped in paper, but when he saw that Savita had lost her leg, he was shocked. She asked him what he was hiding behind him. Then he showed her the gift, which were the shoes. But the shoes were useless for her because she had lost her leg. Now she did not have legs to wear the shoes that were bought by Ram.

title: See Saw Draw
text: Once there was a boy. And he loved to see and he absolutely loved to draw what he saw. Every evening, from his balcony, he drew not just the living things, but the quiet, non-living ones too. One such evening, he saw, A hand reached for another to cross the road. Anjali pulled a muddy puppy out of a puddle. Chinki and her Dada sprinkled food for ants in a neat row. A man gave flowers to a smiling lady. Peter broke into a dance, headphones on his ears. A sabziwali grinned so big, it spilled out of her face. A tear slid down a small cheek. A person waited for an auto, arms crossed, face scrunched up, angry. The neighbor’s parrot shouted, “No homework!” again and again. The boy had drawn that parrot for 22 days in a row. Clothes flapped on another balcony. A gnat frolicked above a tulsi plant. A wobbly bucket wobbled on a wobbly stool outside the ice cream cart. A lit-up window shone in the building nearby. A pole stood tall with two birds and one stuck kite. A gutter cover over which, a hundred feet tip-tapped each day. A bookstore sign read: “Lost and Found – 1 tooth, 1 tiara, and a slightly stinky sock.” The boy drew and drew. His crayons moved gently across the paper. Almost every evening, he wondered how every drawing was like a small world inside the big one, like a giant never-ending storybook. He might not know them all, but he was part of their moments, just as they were part of his drawings. And, suddenly! A loud honk startled him. A crayon quickly rolled off the balcony ledge. and tumbled… It landed on the shiny head of a man with no hair. The boy’s heart skipped a beat. The man looked up without a smile. The boy blinked. The man bent down, picked the crayon in his hand. He looked at the boy. And threw the crayon back up. The man smiled. The boy smiled back. The world moved. And the boy loved to see, and he absolutely loved to draw what he saw.
author: Krupa  Gedia

title: Brave Girl
text: Once there was a girl named Asha who lived in a small village near the forest.. One day, while walking home, she saw a little boy trapped in a burning hut. Everyone was scared to go near, but Asha didn’t think twice. She covered her face with a wet cloth, ran inside, and pulled the boy out safely. Her hands were burned, but she smiled when the boy’s mother hugged her. The villagers called her “The Brave Heart of the Village.” From that day, Asha learned that true courage means helping others, even when you are afraid.

title: Democratia- I
text: The animals look sad & worried but was it always like this? Long long time ago, The jungle was divided into 2 parts. The left part had all the peace loving animals who worked hard. The right one had lions who pounced upon other's flesh. The animals helped each other. But one mischievous fox was having top much fun. So some animals met and agreed that it would be helpful if a leader is chosen and a government too! They thought different types of governance system. They found democracy to be best. They chose an elephant as their leader. The elephant was powerful and didn't fear lion. Everyone would listen to him because he is big and also makes loud noise. Little did they know, that elephant wasn't morally grounded. Once, he was roaming the left part boundary when he chanced to met a lion. Though he trumpeted loudly. The lion was unperturbed. Seeing this the elephant was shocked because everyone listened to him in his part of the jungle. He asked the lion why he wasn't fearful of the him. After all he is the leader of left part. The lion said you're but an elected leader. You're always on the mercy of your voters. I'm real leader- free and powerful. My teeths (money) give me power. You've to roam all the time to get something to eat, while I spend most of the time resting. Elephant was convinced that lion is the real leader. He asked him to sit on his back so that he can carry him to his country and made him super leader. The innocent animals accepted the elephant and lion duo. They thought elephant (power) and lion (money) are best for them. Monkeys supported them by carrying their message to all citizens. Lion soon started building his empire. Innocent animals became his prey. He found some loyal assistants who would update him about the jungle. All animals were frighten. Initially they thought they are safe though they knew that lion must be eating someone's flesh. But still everyone thought their number wouldn't come. They woke up to reality when king called his friends from the right part. They were in grave danger. Their leader elephant was nowhere to be seen. They began hiding and didn't assemble to protest. Soon democracy was over. They secretly met the old owl who had warned them before. He asked them to unite and fight. Everyone was fearful for her/his life. Yet they decided to follow the advice. But a fox came to lion and told him about the secret plan of other animals.

title: Shampoo Day
text: It is Sunday. Shampoo Day. Rima likes to shampoo her hair. But she does not like what happens BEFORE that. Or AFTER that. Rima eats breakfast. Two idlis and sambar. A glass of milk. She hopes Amma will forget what day it is. No luck. “SHAMPOOOOOO DAYYYYY!” says Amma. Amma massages coconut oil on Rima’s head. She combs Rima’s hair. Rima smells like chutney. Chicken curry. Aviyal. Pappadam. Fish fry. She is HUNGRY. But Amma’s rule is ONE HOUR. One hour of coconut oil. It is yucky. Icky. Slicky. Slimy. Rima is slipping in the oil. She is sliding across the hall. She is a baby seal. A slipping, slippery baby seal. She is sliding across the kitchen. She is a baby hippo. A slipping, slippery baby hippo. She is sliding across the bedroom. She is a baby buffalo. A slipping, slippery baby buffalo. She is sliding across the balcony. ONE HOUR! At last. Rima can shampoo her hair. She smells of berries and flowers. Like a garden, but also a bakery. She wants to shampoo her hair forever. But… There is a knock on the door. She hopes Achan is not waiting for her. No luck. Achan wraps a towel around her head. Like a turban. Rima runs. She is not a slippery baby seal, a slippery baby hippo, or a slippery baby buffalo. Rima is fast. Achan runs, too. Across the hall, the kitchen, the bedroom, the balcony. “Rima! We have to dry your hair,” says Achan. “NOT ANY MORE!” says Rima.

title: THREE LITTLE PIGS
text: Once upon a time there were three little pigs who lived with their parents in their house. The family lived happily together. I LOVE LIVING HERE! Once they were grown up, their mother suggested that they should live independently. She also warned about the BIG BAD WOLF! The three pigs were brave and then, they went on their big journey. The three pigs started to work hard and they were building their houses incase anything happens. They were also going to work fast to have shelter and be protected from the DANGEROUS BIG BAD WOLF! Make it sturdy! The first pig created a house built of twigs and sticks. The pig was impressed by his creation. The second pig created a house built of woods and walls of wood logs. The second pig was too impressed. Then, the third pig created a house made of bricks and cement. The Pig was flabbergasted of its result he got tears of joy and started to dance! One day was the day of the full moon, the wolf was awaken by the moon, he was starving! Growling! To cure his hunger he had a plan... EAT ALL THE PIGGIES!!! Then the wolf came into the first pigs house. Did he survive... nope not at all, he just took a deep breath, and flung away the twigs and the sticks house in just a second! You know what happened after the wolf destroying that house:(... It's DINNER TIMEE!! Now he had replenished his one part of his stomach, but still he had to fill the other two! So he went again on the search and found a wooden house he tried to show off by just vanishing the house from his 1 breath, but that didn't work. So, he tried again, but this time with his foot. He kicked the house apart and yet again the 2nd pig was exposed and was filled in his 2nd part Now to fill his final part he went to the third pig's house. He tried to destroy it but couldn't. Alas, he was trying to go home but suddenly, he saw something miraculous! A CHIMNEY!!! He climbed up through the ladder, hunger going fast and fast but little did he know, that he was about to be steamed in the boiling water and was the food! As right as he jumped in he got really hot and his skin was severely injured. The Pig did not let him escape without him accepting his real mistake. After just 30 seconds, the wolf started to cry out loud and accepted his mistake. From that day onwards, the wolf became a "Friendly Wolf". After he became a friendly wolf he decided, "Why not become friends with the pigs..." Years later from that incident, the wolf still remembered his friends that were almost like family to him. Moral of the lesson:- ALWAYS BE RESPECTFUL AND BE KIND

title: How Life Changes - A Sonnet
text: Change comes to us the way the seasons do, It turns the world in new ways as it moves. It brings new things and takes old things from you, And helps us ask the things that life still moves. It lifts us up and helps our small hearts grow, But sometimes change can make our hearts feel scared. Still we learn things we never used to know, And learn to walk through days we never dared. Each little change can teach us how to be, And show us ways to stand when times are hard. It helps us see the things we could not see, And helps us grow in ways we once found hard. So when change comes, we breathe and say, “It’s fine—” “For in this change, new light will always shine.”

title: A CUCKOO'S EVICTION
text: A crow built a cozy nest on a tall tree, laid her eggs, and flew away to find food. A sneaky cuckoo, looking for a safe place to lay her own egg, secretly removed one of the crow's eggs and replaced it with her own. The crow returned to her nest and sat on the eggs, unaware of the switch. When the eggs hatched, the crow's own chicks and the cuckoo chick grew up together. The cuckoo chick was bigger and stronger than the crow's chicks. As they grew, the cuckoo chick pushed the crow's chicks out of the nest, one by one, and they fell to the ground. The crow, heartbroken, watched her babies fall and die. She didn't realize the cuckoo's trickery and thought it was just bad luck. The moral of the story is that some people might take advantage of your kindness and cause harm to you and yours. Be aware of those who might be hiding their true intentions!

title: The monkey who lost his banana
text: In a sunny jungle lived a little monkey named Momo. Momo loved bananas more than anything. He cleaned them, counted them, and kept them safe like treasure. One morning, he picked the biggest, freshest banana he had ever seen. He placed it on a rock for one second to scratch his back… and when he turned around— The banana was gone. Momo froze. Then he panicked. Then he cried loudly enough to scare three birds out of a tree. He ran through the jungle asking every animal: First, he asked the bees buzzing near the flowers: "Did you take my banana?" The bees shook their tiny heads. “No! Then, he slithered over to the snake lying in the sun: “Did you take my banana?” The snake hissed politely, “No, little monkey.” Finally, he ran to the rabbit hopping near the bushes: “Did you take my banana?” The rabbit shook his head. “No, I didn’t see it!” Momo was about to give up when he noticed something. He looked at his own tail and there it was! The banana had been stuck to his tail the whole time. He had carried it everywhere, crying and worrying, without noticing. All the animals laughed. Momo felt shy for a moment, but then he laughed too. He hugged his banana and promised to be more careful next time. Moral: Before blaming others or getting very upset, make sure the problem isn’t something you already have with you.

title: KRISHNA AND THE CALF
text: KRISHNA AND THE CALF One sunny morning in Gokul, Little Krishna was playing with his friends. Suddenly, a worried cow came running to him. She mooed softly, as if asking for help. Her little calf had wandered away and was lost. Krishna smiled and said, “Don’t worry, I’ll find your baby!” He took his flute and walked into the forest. Birds chirped, leaves rustled, and the wind gently blew. Krishna played a sweet tune so the calf could hear him. After a while, a tiny “moo” came from behind a bush. The calf was stuck in some vines. Krishna carefully untangled them and picked the calf up. “Come on, let’s go home,” he said. When the mother cow saw her baby, she licked Krishna’s feet with gratitude. The villagers cheered, “Yay! Krishna saved the day again!” Krishna giggled. “Always help anyone who needs you. Even if they can’t speak like us.” Moral: Helping others, big or small, always brings happiness.

title: The Magical Garden
text: B Illustrators: Ajit Narayan, Chamath Prasanga Lokuliyana, Preeti Krishnamurthy, Raju Babu Shakya, Tanaya Vyas In a magical garden, a little rabbit named Rosy found a special tiny seed. she watered it with sparkling water, and it grew into a beautiful, talking flower!!! " Hello, Rosy!! " said the flower. " I can grant you one wish! " Rosy thought, " Hmm.... I wish for a big, colorful garden where all my friends can play! " Poof! The garden transformed! flowers bloomed in every color and yummy treats grew on bushes. Rosy's friends - Benny the bear, Sammy the squirrel, and Lily the butterfly - came to play. They had a big picnic, played hide -and- seek among the flowers and danced under a rainbow. Rosy was the happiest rabbit ever!!! As the sun set, the garden sparked with fireflies, and Rosy knew it was the best day ever!!

title: Piko, the smart cat
text: In a quiet little village lived an orange cat named Piko. His bright fur and round curious eyes made him loved by everyone, and he was known as the smartest cat in the village. Piko lived with a young girl named Lala, who always said, “Piko, you’re the smartest cat in the whole world!” Piko would meow softly, as if agreeing with her. One morning, Lala’s mother lost the banana bread she had just baked. The bread placed near the window suddenly disappeared. Lala was confused, but Piko quickly sniffed the floor and spotted small crumbs leading toward the backyard. With steady steps, he followed the trail, and Lala followed behind him. Under the mango tree, they found several little birds happily pecking at the leftover bread. Lala laughed and hugged Piko. “You solved the mystery! You’re amazing!” A few days later, Piko heard a faint cry coming from a bush. He found a small squirrel trapped with a branch tangled around its tail. Carefully, Piko pushed the branch away until the squirrel was free. “Thank you, Piko!” the squirrel chirped happily. Piko simply meowed and continued walking calmly, as if helping others was just part of his daily routine. One afternoon, Lala lost the pencil her grandmother had given her. She was sad, but Piko immediately searched every corner of the house. He eventually found it hidden behind a flower pot. Lala hugged him tightly. “Piko, you really are the smartest and kindest cat!” From then on, Piko remained a loyal friend, always ready to help with his clever mind and gentle heart. Vocabulary List: 1. Clever = Cerdas 2. Village = Desa 3. Backyard = Halaman belakang 4. Crumbs = Remah-remah 5. Mystery = Misteri 6. Squirrel = Tupai 7. Trapped = Terjebak 8. Carefully = Dengan hati-hati 9. Lost = Hilang 10. Loyal = Setia Question: Why did Piko follow the crumbs? A. To find food for himself B. To solve the mystery of the missing bread C. To chase the birds D. To play in the backyard Answer: B Who lost the banana bread? A. Lala B. The squirrel C. Lala’s mother D. A farmer Answer: C How did Piko help the squirrel? Answer: He pushed away the tangled branch so the squirrel could be free. Where did Piko find Lala’s lost pencil? Answer: Behind a flower pot. Match the character to the correct description: 1. Piko A. Lost her pencil 2. Lala B. The smart orange cat 3. Squirrel C. Was trapped by a branch
author: RANI

title: Good Night, Mita
text: Mother peeked into Mita's room. It was late, and Mita should be settling down to sleep. "AAAAH!" Suddenly, Mita screamed loudly from her bed! She had just had a terrifying nightmare. Mother rushed in immediately. She sat beside Mita and hugged her tightly. "Sshh... quiet down, Sweetheart. It was just a bad dream. Mommy is here," Mother said softly. To chase away the remaining fear, Mother began telling a story about a space adventure. The two of them sailed among the beautiful stars and planets in their minds. In Mother's story, they landed in a magical jungle and met a funny monster that only wanted to play! They continued their journey to the ocean, meeting a waving octopus and a shark with a big smile. Everything in Mother's story felt safe and fun. Mita finally drifted off to sleep with a smile on her face. She calmed down and felt safe again. Mother made sure she was sleeping soundly, then closed the bedroom door and smiled with relief. Good night, Mita. VOCABULLARY LIST 1. Ibu (Mother) 2. Anak (Child) 3. Kamar (Room) 4. Tidur (Sleep) 5. Lihat (See/Look) 6. Datang (Come) 7. Takut (Scared/Afraid) 8. Aman (Safe) 9. Cerita (Story) 10. Senang (Happy/Fun) 5 Questions about the Story 1. Why did Mita scream while she was sleeping? 2. What was the first thing Mother did for Mita after hearing her scream? 3. What were some of the places they visited in Mother's adventure story? 4. What was the Mother's purpose in telling Mita a story after she woke up startled? 5. How did Mita feel at the end of the story, when Mother closed the room door?
author: Olivia Inayah

title: The Little Sleepy Bear
text: Once, in a big forest, lived a little bear. The little bear was always sleepy, he was sleepy in the morning, afternoon, and even at night too. One day, the little bear tried to wake up. He brushed his teeth. But he was still sleepy. The Little Sleepy Bear when he was done, Mama Bear came. “Eat your food, dear,” she said. The little bear ate his bread. Yum, Yum, Yum. But he was still sleepy. when he finished it, papa Bear came. He was a cheerful man. “Come play, son!” he said. The little bear yawned. He was still sleepy. Sister Bear came. She brushed his hair. Brush, brush, brush. The little bear smiled. but he was still sleepy. Then, All the bears sat around him. “Little bear,” Mama said, “You sleep late every night. That is why you are sleepy.” The little bear thought, h e nodded. “Yes… I sleep too late.” That night, the little bear slept early. He slept and slept. The next morning, he woke up, h is eyes were bright. His smile was big. “I am not sleepy!” he said. Mama, Papa, and Sister hugged him.
author: Ketut Zidan

title: The Guardian of the Forest
text: In a lush forest high in the mountains, lived a happy little elephant. He lived peacefully with all his friends. They loved to relax and tell stories by the lake in the middle of the forest. One day, rain poured down for many days. The animals stayed together, sheltering under the thick, leafy trees to keep safe. When the rain finally stopped, they looked down and were saddened to see the lower forest and the small homes below covered in floodwater. The elephant and his friends quickly worked together to help. The forest felt warm again. The animals understood how important it was to care for nature, keeping the forest and rivers clean and healthy. From that day on, they protected their forest with love.

illustrator: Jacob Kono; Rob Owen; Sangeetha Kadur; Sanjay Sarkar

title: The lost puppy
text: One sunny morning,I went out to the park.I loved the park because it was big,green,and full of flowers. As she walked,she heard a soft sound."Woof...woof..."It was very weak. I looked around and saw a small puppy under a slide. The puppy looked scared. It was shaking and its eyes were full of tears. ''Oh no,puppy'',My friend said. He slowly went near it. ''Don't be scared. I will help you''.He said. The puppy moved closer to him. My friend gently picked it up. The puppy felt warm and soft in his hands. He gave it some water in a bowl from his water bottle. The puppy wagged its tail again and again. He asked their parents and each and every one's parent to keep the puppy,but no one said yes. At last we all started asking everyone in the park or in the road. Finally,an old man came running.''That is my puppy! His name is Coco.He ran away this morning. I was so worried'' old man said. My friend smiled and handed the puppy to him. The puppy was happy too. ''Thank you,dear children,'' the old man said.''You are very kind.'' My friend felt happy. title: Nana and I
text: My Nana and I have such fun, us two, But there are many things we just can’t do. My Nana and I have such fun, us two, But there are many things we just can’t do. I can’t stretch to the top shelf to reach the sugar jar, He can’t bend to the bottom shelf for his chocolate bar. I can’t swallow spinach without a scowl, He can’t eat ice cream without a howl. His old TV remote I just cannot use, My new mobile game makes him blow a fuse. I can’t climb easily onto his tall dining chair, He can’t crawl into my tent without gasping for air. I can’t name all the capitals of Indian states, He can’t remember important history dates. I cannot drive a car, not yet anyhow, He cannot balance well on his bicycle, now. Sometimes I forget to brush my teeth at night, Sometimes, his medicines just disappear from sight. He can’t see much without his glasses, I can’t see anything with his glasses. There are many more things each one can’t do, But we can do one fun thing together, us two. I can read a little. He can read a lot. I love Nana to read me a book that he’s bought.

title: The Happiness I Found on My First Cycle
text: The Happiness I Found on My First Cycle Suhana was a nine-year-old girl living with her family in Mumbai. She was shy and quiet. Every evening, when the children in her society came down to play, she would watch them happily riding their cycles. Suhana also wished for a cycle, but her parents could not afford one. One evening, as she sat by her window watching the children, she noticed a cycle standing idle on its stand. She wished she could sit on it—just for a moment—to know how it felt. But she was scared that the owner might see her and scold her. Still, her desire was so strong that she slowly stepped out of her house. Suhana looked around to check if anyone was coming. Gathering courage, she sat on the cycle and took a small round. The joy she felt at that moment was beyond words. But suddenly, Ravi, the owner of the cycle, saw her. Ravi lived in the same society. “Hey! That’s my cycle! How dare you sit on it?” he shouted. Suhana froze in fear. She stammered, “I… I was just taking a small ride.” “Get away from my cycle right now!” Ravi yelled. Feeling hurt and embarrassed, Suhana hurried home. She burst into tears. Her mother, seeing her cry, asked gently, “What happened, Suhana?” Wiping her tears, Suhana said, “I sat on Ravi’s cycle. He got angry and shouted at me.” Her mother hugged her and said, “It’s okay, Suhana. Don’t cry. I will talk to your father about getting you a cycle.” At first, her father was hesitant, but Suhana’s mother convinced him. Later, her father called Suhana and said, “If you study hard and do well in your exams, I promise I will buy you a cycle.” Suhana agreed and worked hard every day. She made a study schedule, studied for two hours daily, and still made time to play. After the exams, she eagerly waited for her marks. When the report card arrived, Suhana was delighted—she had done very well! She proudly showed her marks to her father. He smiled and said, “As promised, it’s time to fulfil my word. Tomorrow is Sunday. We will go and buy your cycle.” Suhana could hardly sleep that night. She imagined herself pedalling confidently, feeling the cool breeze on her face. The next morning, her family went to the cycle shop and bought her a brand-new cycle. Her father held the cycle from behind and taught her how to pedal, steer, and balance. He also explained the importance of wearing a helmet and riding only in safe areas. Suhana listened carefully. That day became the happiest day of her life. Now she could join her friends in fun races and play happily with them. Riding together taught her teamwork, cooperation, and communication.
author: Reshma Lotlikar

title: The Song of Luna - Can you Hear the Whale Song?
text: Once, when magic turned the blue sea to silver in the soft moonlight, a little blue whale was born. It was named Luna after the beautiful moon that sometimes weaves its magic deep in the ocean’s heart. As she grew up among the big and wise blue whales, Luna learned the Whale Song. Her voice was deep and beautiful, echoing the vastness of the living ocean. Her song always called her friends and family home and Luna was happy. Suddenly one day, a scream of metal passed over her as if it were a roaring storm of sound. The big ones scattered saying Ship! Ship! Ship! Poor Luna was left all alone. Her song, once bright as the silver moon, went quiet and was then forgotten. Tired, lost and alone, Luna slept. The magic of the silver moon rose again in her dreams and she heard the moon whisper her song back to her. Brave and unafraid, Luna remembered her forgotten song and began to sing. Louder and louder she sang and the big wise ones heard her and joined her in her beautiful song. The fish in the ocean heard them and rejoiced and the ocean itself sang happily deep within its heart. Luna was home again. Sometimes, deep in the silence of the night when the silver moon casts its magic over the whole world, I hear the Whale Song carrying to me. Can you hear the Whale Song?
author: Soumya Mishra

title: The Moonbridge Promise
text: In the gentle kingdom of Lumeria, nights were filled with wonder. Fireflies floated like stars, and the river sang softly as it curved through the land. But the greatest secret of all was the Moonbridge—a glowing path of silver light that appeared only when the moon was full. People said it connected hearts as much as worlds, and only those with true friendship could cross it safely. Aerin lived near the river. She loved quiet things: old books, soft music, and watching the sky change colors at dusk. Many thought she was shy, but Aerin simply listened more than she spoke. One evening, while she sat by the river sketching the moon, she heard laughter carried by the wind. It was Kai. Kai was known across Lumeria for his bright smile and playful magic. He could call gentle breezes with a snap of his fingers and make leaves dance in the air. Where Aerin was calm, Kai was lively. Yet, somehow, they fit together easily. “Waiting for the Moonbridge?” Kai asked, sitting beside her. “Maybe,” Aerin replied, smiling. “I like how the river looks when it appears.” The moon rose higher, turning the water silver. Slowly, a path of light formed above the river—the Moonbridge had arrived. It shimmered, soft and steady, like a promise. Without speaking, Aerin and Kai stood and stepped onto the bridge together. At once, the air grew colder. Dark shapes stirred beneath the water—shadow spirits, born from doubt and fear. They whispered worries into the night. “You’re too quiet,” the shadows murmured to Aerin. “You’ll never be serious enough,” they teased Kai. Aerin’s steps slowed. Kai’s smile faded. Then Aerin reached for Kai’s hand. “I trust you,” she said quietly. Kai squeezed her hand. “And I trust you too.” The Moonbridge glowed brighter. The shadows hissed and melted away, replaced by floating petals of light. With every step, the bridge felt warmer, stronger, as if responding to their bond. On the other side waited a hidden garden. At its center stood the Crystal Tree, its branches shining like glass. Legends said it bloomed only for those who crossed the Moonbridge with honest hearts. As Aerin and Kai approached, the tree burst into soft blue flowers that drifted down around them. Each flower held a promise—a wish waiting to be made. Kai looked at Aerin. “You could wish for anything.” Aerin shook her head. “So could you.” They stood in silence, listening to the gentle chime of the flowers. Kai felt something new in his chest—not loud like excitement, but warm and steady. Aerin felt it too, like moonlight settling inside her heart. “I don’t need a wish,” Kai said softly. “Neither do I,” Aerin replied. They knew then that what they shared was already magic—a friendship built on trust, and a quiet romance growing like the moon itself, slow and bright. When dawn came, the Moonbridge faded. But from that night on, Aerin and Kai returned to the river often. They laughed, talked, and dreamed together, knowing that as long as they believed in each other, the Moonbridge would always exist—if not in the sky, then in their hearts.
author: Hasib Mondal

title: The Generous King
text: Bhagavan-was the name of the Kingdom. The kingdom had a king whose heart always flowed generosity. The king, whose name was, Samrat Danvendra, was a very humble and down-to-earth king who always cared for his people and the kingdom. The people were very happy that they were blessed with such a king. Their king usually always went for a tour in the kingdom, to check whether his people were having any issues financially and health. But during his tour, he always won’t go as king, but as a traveller, stranger, etc. One day when he went for a tour around his kingdom, he found out that some people were struggling for food. He got worried. He did not want his subjects to be hungry and struggle for food. So, he called his ministers and had a meeting regarding the issue. At the end of the meeting, it was decided that food will be provided daily to those who were struggling. So, he gathered best chefs from everywhere. Food was provided for the people who were struggling three times a day. The food was very delicious and there were many varieties. The quantity and the quality of the food was also marvellous. The chefs used to cook at one place and serve it another. So, the serving had to carry the food for a 500 m and then serve it to the people. They usually don’t cover the food with a lid. So, one day as they were carrying the food, there was an eagle flying with a snake it had hunted, held firmly in its beak. Two-three drops of poison fell from the snake’s mouth in the food. The workers didn’t know about it and served the food to the people. The people not knowing anything ate the food. After some time, some started to faint and some started to have fix. Everyone was carried to hospital. The hospital didn’t have enough space to admit and treat the patients. So, many died lack of treatment. And some people who were given treatment also died. The king got really saddened by this event. He couldn’t digest many people dying in his kingdom because of him. When he found out the reason, he was really depressed. He was also depressed because of lack of treatment and lack of hospital facilities. So, he thought of again starting the food scheme. And he also started to build a hospital and buy many facilities and hire doctors from everywhere. Yama, the god of death, was watching all this events and called his assistant Chitragupta. Chitragupta asked Yama “Should I write as a bad deed of the King?”, Yama told him to wait for some time. So, as the king had started his food scheme again. Again, people started to come. This time the food was covered with a lid while it was carried. His scheme got famous and people from other kingdoms also started coming. One day as some people from another kingdom Dholakpur were coming, they asked the route for the place where the food was served by the king to two men. These two men laughed asked the people, “Are you all planning to do a suicide?”, the people were shocked and asked that why they were talking like this. The two men explained the tragedy of how people died because of the food. The people got shocked and they thanked these men. These two men were none other than the king and his minister of Dholakpur in disguise. They got the information of these people going to Bhagavan. They were afraid if these people might leave their kingdom might leave their kingdom if they started liking Danvendra’s kingdom. So, they planned to disguise and send the people back to their home. Yama was watching all this and called Chitragupta again, he said “Chitragupta as you were asking should you write that food scheme tragedy as a bad deed of Danvendra, now write that tragedy and this king and minister of Dholakpur’s atro cities as their bad deed”. Chitragupta wrote everything and asked Yama that why he told him to write like this. Yama answered, “See Danvendra was a humble man and did good deeds. Even though those people died, he wasn’t responsible. But these two men are discouraging good deeds and are not doing any.”. So, Chitragupta wrote those bad deeds in king and minister of Dholakpur. They both were punished. Danvendra continued his scheme. People were happy. Dholakpur’s people also came and settled here. Yama was watching all these. Remember God is always watching you, noting down your good and bad deeds!!

In awaara kutto aur jinse aap is pustak mein mile hain, un sabki dekhbhaal shahar ke hazaron log karte hain. Wo aapke pados ke jute polish karne wale chacha, policewala, sadak par thela lagane wale, sadkon par rahne wale ya bahut hi jarjar makanon mein rahne wale log ho sakte hain. In kutto ke Kalu, Tommy, Julie jaise naam hote hain aur kai baar to filmi sitaron ke naam par bhi inke naam rakhe jaate hain, jaise Aishwarya, Salman aur Shahrukh. The Welfare of Stray Dogs (WSD) naamak ek sanstha pichle 20 saalon se in kutto ke tikaakaran adi ka kaam kar rahi hai. title: The Little Spark
text: Riya loved asking questions. She wanted to know why the sky was blue and how plants grew. Riya loved asking questions. She wanted to know why the sky was blue and how plants grew. One day, her science teacher gave the class a small project. They had to make something using simple science. Riya chose to build a tiny solar oven. She used a pizza box, some foil, and clear plastic. At first, it did not work. The food stayed cold. Riya felt sad, but she did not give up. She read her book again and learned that sunlight needs to stay trapped to make heat. She fixed her oven and tried again. This time, the sun warmed the box. After some time, the food inside became hot. Riya smiled with joy. Her teacher clapped and said, “This is how science works. You try, fail, learn, and try again.” Riya learned that science is not just facts. It is curiosity, hard work, and patience. That small solar oven became a big spark in her heart. She knew that one day, science could help her change the world.
author: Hasib Mondal

title: The mysterious book
text: Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Harry whose age was 11. Harry was a curious little boy to whom it seemed that adventures were just a trip. He lived in a mysterious village where strange things used to happen. He lived with his cheerful parents who loved to travel to new places and explore new culture. They always seemed to be happy no matter what! Harry always wished that he could go on a fun and mysterious adventure. One Saturday morning Harry felt particularly excited as today was his birthday and he was turning 12. He had anticipated that his parents were throwing a party for his friends, but his parents just ordered him a Domino's pizza, a Subway burger and finally a plate of momos along with some juice and cake. His parents told him that they are going out for some work and would be back by morning. As his parents had gone out, he had the freedom to do whatever he wanted except for playing outdoors. Harry was bored so he started reading a book of "Famous Five" but after sometime he started to read his favorite book" "Harry Potter". He felt something unusual in the book but he didn't care and continued reading the book. Suddenly the book floated out of Harry's hand and something from it said "Go have a adventure". Harry didn't understand a word. It was late at night, so he blew out the fire in the lantern and slept peacefully. The next morning when his parents didn't come home, he was worried. Suddenly the voice from the book again said "Go have an adventure to find your parents". He thought the book had read his mind and was telling him to go for it. Harry was very happy. After all, he was finally going on an adventure. He took all the things he used in the previous adventures, but he felt something different about this adventure so he took some extra things like powder and magnifying glasses of various sizes. He left the house with all his things packed, ready to go for the adventure. Then he suddenly realized that he did not know where to start from. Suddenly something appeared out of thin air! It was a letter with a riddle written on it! It said "It is a place where animals dwell in safety until man comes and destroys it." Harry's mind was working quickly to find the place. kkjkjkjpkpoppppop Harry thought about the place. He realized the place was very near to his house, it was a forest! He quickly hurried to the forest and found another note lying on the ground. It was written "It is a place dark and filled with water". He knew it was a pond so, he went to the nearest pond but couldn't see the note. He suddenly saw there he saw a rabbit hole in which he saw a large note and some equipment. All of the equipment was not at all related to what he thought, but there was one thing which was very surprising! He saw his own "Harry Potter" book. Suddenly something surprising happened, the book turned into a rabbit and then into a man! Then the man told Harry "Go to the place where your parents have visited the most and you will find how to reach to them, until then I will be your companion". Harry went to Madhya Pradesh, the place which they visited the most. There he saw a magician named Mr. Big and suddenly the man who had accompanied him had disappeared. His parents had told him that he was their friend. He told Harry this was the trick of changing shape. Mr. Big also told Harry the charm which was "ang dang cing ding min sok lah dhu". When Harry reached Mr. Big's house in Madhya Pradesh Harry suddenly saw 2 items in the hallway a chair and an orange. He immediately thought and said the magic spell " ang dang cing ding min sok lah dhu". Suddenly the figures turned into his father and mother. He was very happy to see them, but during his excitement he did not forget to call the police. The policemen came and arrested Mr. Big. They thanked Harry and his parents for helping them catch the criminal. After all, at the end Harry and his parents travelled back home and lived happily ever after.

title: The Power of Change
text: The days move on, they never stay the same, The seasons turn from sunshine into rain. We learn and grow through joy as well as pain, For change is life, though sometimes hard to tame. A child grows strong by trying something new, New thoughts replace the old we leave behind. Though change may scare, it helps our hearts and mind To see the world with clearer, wider view. The world keeps shifting, people learn to care, New paths appear where none were seen before. We fall, stand up, and rise a little more, And learn that change is growth we all must bear. Though change feels strange, it helps us find our way, And shapes who we become with each new day.

title: Threads Of  Tomorrow
text: In the small coastal town of Mangalore, the air smelled of salt and monsoon rain. Narrow lanes wound between tiled-roof houses, and children played cricket in the streets, their laughter echoing against moss-covered walls. Ananya, a 28-year-old schoolteacher, lived with her widowed mother, Savitri. Their home was modest — two rooms, a courtyard with a mango tree, and shelves lined with old books her father had collected before his sudden passing. Life was simple, but not easy. Ananya’s salary barely covered household expenses, and Savitri’s health was fragile. Yet, every evening, they sat together on the veranda, sipping tea, speaking of small joys — the neighbor’s newborn, the jasmine blooming in the garden. Across town lived Ramesh, Ananya’s childhood friend. He worked as a mechanic, his hands perpetually stained with grease. Though his job was demanding, he carried a quiet dignity. Ramesh and Ananya had grown up together, sharing textbooks, secrets, and dreams. Their friendship was a thread that had endured through years of change. One evening, Ramesh stopped by Ananya’s house. “The school roof leaks again?” he asked, noticing her damp notebooks. She sighed. “Yes. The children huddle in corners when it rains. I keep telling the management, but repairs cost money.” Ramesh frowned. “Education shouldn’t be this hard. These kids deserve better.” His words lingered. Ananya knew he was right. Social issues weren’t abstract — they lived in the cracks of her classroom walls, in the tired faces of children who came hungry, in the silence of parents who couldn’t afford fees. The town was changing. A new highway project threatened to cut through neighborhoods, displacing families. Savitri worried constantly. “What if they take our land?” she asked one night, her voice trembling. Ananya reassured her, though inside she felt the same fear. Development promised progress, but it often came at the cost of ordinary lives. Meanwhile, Ramesh faced his own battles. His younger brother, Arun, had fallen into bad company, skipping work, drinking late into the night. Ramesh tried to guide him, but Arun resisted. “You don’t understand,” Arun snapped once. “You think fixing cars is enough? I want more.” Ramesh felt torn — between loyalty to his brother and the frustration of watching him drift. One monsoon morning, disaster struck. The school roof collapsed during heavy rain. No children were hurt — classes had been dismissed early — but the building was unusable. Ananya stood in the ruins, rain soaking her sari, tears mixing with the downpour. She felt helpless. Ramesh arrived, umbrella in hand. “We’ll fix this,” he said firmly. “How?” she whispered. “We don’t have funds.” “Then we’ll raise them,” he replied. Together, they began a campaign. They spoke to shopkeepers, neighbors, local officials. Some donated money, others offered labor. Slowly, the community rallied. It wasn’t easy. There were arguments, delays, disappointments. But amidst the struggle, Ananya saw something beautiful — people standing together, refusing to let their children’s future crumble. At home, Savitri watched her daughter with pride. “Your father would have been proud,” she said softly one evening. Ananya smiled through her exhaustion. “I just want these children to have a chance.” But Savitri’s health worsened. Hospital visits became frequent, bills piled up. Ananya felt the weight of responsibility pressing harder. Ramesh noticed. “You can’t carry everything alone,” he told her. “Let me help.” His presence was steady, like the lighthouse on the coast — guiding, reassuring. Their friendship deepened, not into romance, but into something equally profound: a bond built on trust, sacrifice, and shared purpose. The highway project advanced. Families were forced to relocate. Protests erupted, but officials remained unmoved. Ananya joined the demonstrations, holding placards, chanting slogans. She wasn’t a politician, but she believed in voices rising together. Ramesh stood beside her. “We may not stop the highway,” he said, “but we can demand fair compensation.” Their fight wasn’t glamorous. It was messy, tiring, often ignored. Yet, it mattered. It was about dignity, about refusing to be invisible. there was over 44 families to find a alternative place many left some helpless some can't find a alternative place Months passed. The school was rebuilt, stronger than before. Children returned, their laughter filling the classrooms. Ananya felt a quiet triumph — proof that ordinary people could achieve extraordinary things when united. Savitri’s health stabilized, though she remained frail. She spent her days in the courtyard, watching the mango tree sway in the wind. Arun, after a heated confrontation with Ramesh, finally sought work in a nearby factory. It wasn’t glamorous, but it was honest. Slowly, he began to rebuild his life. The highway was constructed, but families received better compensation after persistent protests. It wasn’t a perfect victory, but it was something. One evening, Ananya and Ramesh sat by the sea, watching waves crash against the shore. “Do you ever feel,” Ananya asked, “that life is just… endless struggle?” Ramesh thought for a moment. “Yes. But struggle means we’re alive. And sometimes, it builds something worth keeping.” She smiled. “Like friendship.” He nodded. “Like friendship.” The sun dipped below the horizon, painting the sky in hues of orange and purple. It was a bittersweet moment — filled with memories of loss, but also with hope for tomorrow. Life in Mangalore continued. Children studied in the repaired school. Families adjusted to new homes. The town grew, changed, endured. Ananya taught with renewed passion, knowing her work mattered. Ramesh fixed cars, guided his brother, stood by his friend. Savitri watched her daughter with quiet pride. They weren’t heroes in the grand sense. They were ordinary people, carrying ordinary burdens. Yet, in their resilience, in their friendships, in their fight for dignity, they became extraordinary. Because sometimes, the threads of tomorrow are woven not by grand gestures, but by small acts of courage, kindness, and hope. Manglore once again happy peaceful and people with rush.

I was worried about you. " Now Meenakshi understood what the real treasure 🪙 was. It was nature and family... ABOUT THE AUTHOR Daksha ﻿ is a 11 year old girl who likes to read and write ✍️ stories. title: Halloween Party
text: Halloween Party Our family was very excited to go to a Halloween party on 31 October. 2025, at my friend's house. The day was Friday, and we took it easy. We had a good lunch, we ate pizza and drank Fanta. After that, I did my English and my Math homework. After an hour, I went out to play with my friends. My friends and I were cycling while my mom, dad, and my sisters were dressing up for the party. My mom reminded me that we had to go to a Halloween party, so I had to dress up. I dressed up like a vampire, my dad dressed up like a bat, my mom and my sisters dressed up like a witch. After that, my father booked a taxi. The taxi arrived at 18:30. When we arrived at my friend's house, my father realised he had forgotten his wallet. After that, my father wondered if he should go back home or should he borrow the money from my friend’s father. My father wanted to try the second plan. After we reached at my friend’s house, his father paid the taxi bill. My father said to his friend that he is going to pay him back after we get back home. My parents started to talk with others. At 19:00, we. started playing games. We won the first game, and won a toy car in prize. After that, we ate some snacks, like popcorn, peanuts, and chips. After an hour, we started our second game, which was tambola. And we won the second game also. This time we got a marker in prize. After the second game, we started to eat food. It was pizza, Pav Bhaji and Burgers. At the third game, we thought that we won, but it was actually my friend’s family that had won the game. Due to the confusion, the parents started to argue, and the kids were jumping and having fun. After that, my elder sister came and stopped the argument, and divided the gift, which was candies, equally among everyone. After the fun, everybody went home. On the way back, my mom took out her cap and saw my dad's wallet in her purse. She was embarrassed because my dad's wallet was in her purse all that time. As soon as we reached home, my dad paid the money to my friend’s dad. Everyone was laughing about the incident that happened at the party. The party was enjoyable, and we were all very tired, so we slept early. My name is Shivay Sharma, and I’m 8 years old. I live in Sweden with my family. I like to run and play football with my friends

title: Christmas Game
text: It was a snowy day in London, near King’s Road. Tom sat by his windowsill, thinking about Christmas. About gifts. About what he might get. He felt he had a chance of getting COAL because of his antics, which could put him on the naughty list. He shrugged it off. SANTA WASN'T REAL! He had known that long ago. He was ten now. Christmas felt dull. The only good thing about it was GIFTS. Good gifts. Toys, action figures, games. Then came a knock. “Come in,” he said. His mother entered, wrapped in a sweater made by his grandmother. The strings were loose, making it look like a pile of hair. “Tommy!" she said. "Do you want some cookies with milk? You haven’t eaten in an hour.” “Ok, thanks, Mom.” He picked up a cookie, stared at it, and slipped into memory, back to when Christmas meant toys on the floor and plum cake on his plate. He returned to the present. One bite. Sweet. Familiar. Another knock. This time, it was his father: red sweater, a Christmas hat pulled low. He carried a large box. Tom’s eyes lit up. “Merry Christmas, buddy. I got you something I thought you would like.” Tom tore into the wrapping. His hands moved fast. It was an old game. Not the one he wanted. “It’s a classic,” his father said. “I used to play it all the time. I remember every good thing about it. I thought I’d pass it on to you.” “This isn’t the one I wanted!” Tom yelled. “My friends get the new one. Why am I stuck with this piece of junk?!” His father didn't argue. “I’m sorry,” he said softly. "I’ll see if I can get your game in a day or two.” Tom crawled under the covers. He closed his eyes and tried to imagine the game he’d actually asked for. He imagined laughing with friends. He tried to imagine a Christmas that wasn't ruined. He felt alone. Soon, dinner was called. He wiped his tears and went downstairs. The table was full of delicacies with the plum cake placed carefully in the centre. He took roast turkey, a glass of eggnog and sat opposite his father, who laughed with the family. Across the table, his father laughed. To anyone else, he looked happy. But Tom saw the truth. He saw the smile that didn’t reach the eyes. He no longer saw a "bad gift" now. He saw a father who tried his best and a son who had thrown it away. He stared into the fire and thought about the gift. Not what it was. Not what it cost. But the care behind it. The memory. The wanting to share something loved. Christmas had not been ruined by the gift. It had been ruined by him. After dinner, Tom went to his father’s room. “Dad?” “Yes, Tom?” Tom rushed forward and hugged him. “I’m sorry for getting angry at you.” His father paused, then hugged him back. “It’s fine.” Tom pulled away. “So… do you want to play?” His father’s eyes lit up. “Yes. I would love to.” They played the game all night. They laughed. They lost. They won. At some point, the Christmas game did not matter anymore. When Tom finally went to bed, the box sat open on the floor. The old game lay between them, worn at the edges. Tom smiled. Christmas did not feel dull anymore. And that night, Tom stopped being the Christmas Grinch.

title: Ahaan_G7A_Embrace Yourself
text: Jake, on first glance, seems like a normal boy. He studies in the seventh grade. But that "normalness" often goes away. You see, Jake has ADHD and struggles to focus on basically everything. Due to this he doesn't get good grades, he always gets bullied in school for being the "weird kid" and even though they don't admit it, his family despises him for his disorder, and he knows it He was tired of this constant cycle of being hated by almost everyone, so, he decided to pack up his things, take some money, and leave his home for good and to find a place where he could be properly appreciated. Now, you may be asking yourself "Isn't someone gonna stop him?", well, nobody could care enough to even notice. So he was off, a twelve year old boy with ADHD on the crowded streets of New York City While he was on the streets, he bumped into a suspicious looking man. The man quickly grabbed his hand, gave him a peice of paper and whispered "10:45 today". Jake was extremely frightened by this and ran away quickly but he was still holding the piece of paper. Ater he had gotten a safe distance away, he read the note that the man gave him. it said " house 115, 25th boulevard". Now this was obviously a kidnapping attempt but Jake just couldn't see throught it. He trusted the man and started to head towards the address which was given to him. On his way, he saw a tent setup across the road, with a sign that read " Future reading for 50 dollars". 50 dollars was all the money that Jake had but he really wanted to know what would happen to him in the future. He started crossing the road and the because of his ADHD and all the bright lights around him he got distracted and forgot about the address and the tent. Now he was back to square one he spent a few days roaming and eventually ran out of money. He decided to go home but in this span of time he realized something. He finally understood that the man was trying to kidnap him and that the tent was just stealing all his money. He also understood that his disability helped him avoid so much of the horrible things that could have happened to him and he learnt to embrace himself. About the author: I am a young author that makes books to inspire others to make the most of their abilities, skills and want people to feel confident about themselves through my books.

title: Nature's gift: Rugda
text: Jiggi is happy. Grandma says they can go to the forest. They will look for rugda-tasty mushrooms that grow under the soil! Grandma knows the spot well. She digs out the little brown buttons. title: When my mother cooks
text: Once spotless, the kitchen now features a floury floor and parts of ingredients. All drawers open and ransacked shelves. She scolds herself as looks for treasures - long forgotten spice-jars, condiments and recipes cut from magazines curating poems, stories, knit designs & yoga poses. When my mother cooks, we run and get our handkerchief and open the windows. We get ready for dinner with juice and soda, because her food is a little spicy and salty. But we never tell her this. We say its yummy and she smiles so sweetly each time. When my mother cooks I am reminded of my childhood home. An intense longing for my grandmother and her scolding. Her long periods of silence - upset over our misdemeanor and her toothy grin every time she melted. My mother's cooking reminds me of picnics on boat in winters. Of sleeping with cousins on the terrace summers nights. When my mother cooks, sometimes there's not much left for her to eat. She gets too tired to even sit. She looks so alone when she winds up the kitchen. When my mother cooked, I think I should have been kinder and asked her if I could help. When my mother cooks is still a mystery to me, because I only seen her in the kitchen when she bakes. T he house smells different each time she opens the oven door. Sometimes its a sweet and warm aroma like caramel, cinnamon and vanilla. Other times it smells of things that are buttery, garlicky and all things nice. When my mother cooks, she looks a bit lost at times. She stops kneading and stares at her hands that look like giant play dough logs I used to make when I was little. But I don't tell her that. I hug her and tell her that I love her and that brings her back every time. When my mother cooks, we throw a party. S he chops & mixes, grinds and fries. And sweats, sways, sighs and scowls. In evening she puts on a smiley mask. She swings to music and laughs at jokes. And eats from girdle and licks the ladle and stealthily takes a bite from that chicken leg she had hidden in the fridge.
author: pallavi srivastava

title: Chunni, the Ant
text: Chunni is such a sweet-lover; She can eat bowls full of sugar! In the market, Chandulal had a big showroom. You could get everything there, from needle to broom! There was sugar and there was rice; Flour, pulses and spices too, at the best price. Somehow, a hole in the big sugar bag was cut; And Chunni came to know of this top secret! The hole lured Chunni, the sweet-lover! She carefully looked around from one corner to another. She clapped around with happiness; And whistled to signal her friends. Her friends started coming in one by one. And the hole in the bag was now a secret for none! They all formed a queue from west to east. Today there was going to be a grand feast! Ants are a species so amazing; They truly believe in sharing. They build anthills to live together, They firmly believe in 'Unity is Power'! It can lift weight 50 times of its own. The diligence of an ant is well-known. Chunni is so nice, isn't she? How was the story, tell me! - Where did you spot an ant? - Have you ever seen an anthill (the home of an ant)? - Ants are helpful because they eat up dead worms and insects. They sometimes drop seeds on their way and unknowingly plant trees.
author: Neha Maheshwari

title: THE TWO BESTFRIEND RAHUL AND ROHAN
text: Rahul and Rohan had been inseparable since childhood. One day, Rohan's family faced a financial crisis. His father lost his job, and their savings were dwindling. Rohan stopped attending school, feeling ashamed. Rahul noticed the change and approached Rohan. He learned about his situation and decided to help. Rahul gathered their friends and proposed a fundraiser. They organized a small event, and word spread quickly. The community rallied around Rohan's family, donating generously. The fundraiser exceeded expectations, and Rohan's family received enough support to get back on their feet. Rohan was overwhelmed with gratitude. He realized that true friends like Rahul were rare. Their bond grew stronger, and Rohan's family eventually recovered. Rahul's kindness had changed their lives, and Rohan vowed to pay it forward someday.
author: VEDANSH Mishra
illustrator: Leo Daly; Magriet Brinkk; Yuwak  Shrestha

title: THE LION AND A CAT
text: A tiger and a stray cat lived in the same forest. One day, a fierce storm hit, and the cat took shelter in a nearby hollow tree. But the tree was unstable and about to collapse. The tiger, seeing the cat's danger, rushed to hold the tree trunk with his powerful body, shielding the cat from harm. When the storm passed, the cat emerged, shaken but safe. "Why did you save me?" the cat asked. The tiger replied, "I didn't save you for any reward or reason. I saved you because we're both living, breathing creatures, and we need to look out for each other." The cat's eyes welled up with gratitude, and from that day on, the tiger and the cat became inseparable friends, proving that kindness and compassion can bridge even the largest of differences.
author: VEDANSH Mishra

title: The Lost Kitten
text: In a small apartment complex in the bustling city of Mumbattan. There lived a small family, they were Anita & Ganesh the children & the parents Anu & Mukesh. The family was quite content with what they had until the kids started demanding for a kitten. But the parents refused to buy one. Until it was CHRISTMAS-EVE where the children where gifted a kitten and called it Tiger because of it's orange fur and black stripes The kitten was taken care of very nicely. One day the kids were at school, and the parents were out. The kitten was left all alone & jumped out the window to explore the neighborhood. Once the children came home, they wanted to play with the kitten. But they couldn't find it and started searching in every nook & cranny to find it, but no clue. Few days went by; the kids started to put up missing cat posters in the neighborhood cafe, mall & park. But no one even gave it a try, soon the family almost lost all hope. Until a young boy Nitish, from the neighborhood approached them. Nitish longed to be a detective, took up the case. His first idea was to consult the family, but they had no clue where Tiger went. So, his second idea was to ask animal control & the nearby shelter if they knew anything about Tiger. But no clue, this made Nitish clueless. But he had an idea, this was to ask the residents of Tiger's complex. But no one knew anything about where Tiger went, some didn't even know that Tiger went missing! But there was a shimmer of hope when one of the residents said that she saw a kitten of its type heading to the market. So, he left for the market and kept on searching for Tiger, but still no signs. This made him quite disappointed, but still, he didn't give up or even have a thought to give up. That's when, on a busy day, he saw a fish stall with the animal he kept trying to find, the one & only Tiger so he darted to the stall & immediately asked the old lady running the stall. Nitish immediately asked the old lady running the stall. where did she find this kitten, she stated that she saw the tiny little kitten eating a fish from her stall & decided to take it in. So, after taking the kitten from the old lady, he returned to the family. Both Anita & Ganesh started jumping with joy & Tiger was reunited with the family. THE END ABOUT THE AUTHOR I am Aadvik B. and I am 11 years old I live in Bangalore & study 6th grade at The Foundation School Varthur,
author: Aadvik B
