title: Doomscrolling!
text: The screen was the only sunlight in Ajay's room.The curtains were always closed. A 'don't open' sign was stuck on his door. A PS5 was laid on the table as he slept on his bed, staring at his phone... Ajay was a brilliant guy in his teens. He had jet black curls with bright hazel eyes. Ajay loved his cozy room and wished to stay in there all day. He even got a new phone this year on his 14th birthday. On the weekends he used to go fishing with his dad or camp out as a whole family. Ajay loved doing that, especially when he was a kid. But as Ajay grew up, he started to lose interest in family get togethers. Video games were Ajay's life. People next door would always complain due to the loud sounds of his computer. But nowadays Ajay's parents started ignoring him. They thought that he was independent enough. They were always busy because of workload and didn't care what Ajay was up to. Nowadays Ajay was always on his phone...it was like he was glued to it. He had lost interest in camping or any outdoor activities during the weekend. It had been so long since anyone had seen him smile. He thought he was scrolling to take the stress out of his shoulders, but it was doing the opposite. Day by day Ajay was getting weaker and weaker... Whenever Ajay got a reminder to finish his homework or go out for basketball practice, all he cared was to finish the next video. Even at 3 am in the night, he would take his mobile saying "just five more minutes". Wherever Ajay goes he would have his phone in his hand. Whether while traveling or even in the washroom. His neck started bending and his posture was disturbed. Ajay's eyes lost his brightness and even his attention span decreased. He couldn't focus during lectures and struggled to finish a movie as he was so used to those 15 second long videos. His grade was going down and he didn't realize that it was because of his obsession with scrolling. Recently, it seems that Ajay started having a popcorn brain.He feels like the world around him is painfully slow. He thought it would calm him down but all he feels now is anxious and drained. Even in school Ajay is physically present but mentally elsewhere. One day Ajay was walking in his room with his phone in his hand, the thumb moving up and down. As he looks up at the mirror to see himself, it barely looked like him. Dark circles had emerged under his dim weary eyes. That was the day he realized what scrolling had done to him. Ajay couldn't remember what he learnt in school today or what he ate for breakfast. He went and looked into his classwork and saw that half of it was incomplete! "Just 5 minutes" turned into hours and he saved no time for his studies! Ajay didn't know how to undo all this. He tried to consult a doctor on how to stop this addiction towards gadgets and learnt that "unpluging" for a few days wouldn't hurt. He learnt to exercise every morning and drink a lot of water. 'Went for evening walks and never skipped a family weekend. By doing this, Ajay felt more free than ever! All this time he was caught in a digital vortex and didn't realize the fun he had left behind. The silence around him felt calm and for the first time in months, he felt the fresh air enter his lungs. About the author Hello everyone, I am Mohana and this is my first story in this app! I am 13 years old and I am happy with the story I wrote. The phone is this generation's life and we are using it excessively which could ruin our health. I was inspired to create this realistic fiction about how harmful scrolling is, to teach the young readers to prevent from doing so. I really hope this story inspired you and I hope it taught you a lesson too. I once experienced this stress earlier and I learnt a lot from it. I tried my best to stop getting attached to the phone and do something fun! Thank You!
author: Mohana

title: Bear and Hippo
text: It was a hot summer afternoon. Water was drying up everywhere in the forest and very little vegetation was left. Gundu, the hippo was cooling himself in a muddy little pond when he saw Balu, the bear walking by with fish in his mouth. Surprised to find the fish to be fresh and clean, Gundu asked “Where did you find the fish?” Balu replied, “There is a big lake with plenty of fresh water behind the Jwala hills and there is also plenty of fish out there.” Gundu said, “Jwala hills? Where is that?”. Balu replied, “It is a little far from the jungle. I can take you there.” Gundu was tempted by the thought and said, “Let us go there immediately!” Balu replied “But it is getting dark and so it is not safe to venture out now. Let us start at dawn tomorrow.” Next day, Gundu joined Balu and they started walking to the lake behind Jwala hills. Gundu had an idea and he said “Balu, let us have a swimming competition today. We shall swim from one bank to the other. The loser must catch as many fish as possible and feed the winner”. Balu liked the idea as he thought he would win the swimming competition easily and so he agreed. Upon reaching the lake, Gundu counted 1, 2, 3 and both animals jumped into the lake and began swimming. Balu raced away and looked behind to see Gundu. But he could not find Gundu. Puzzled by this, he continued swimming to the other end of the lake. Just as he approached the opposite bank, he saw Gundu standing there smiling. Surprised to see Gundu, he asked “How did you reach so quickly?” Gundu said “Hippos can run under water”. Following the race, Balu started catching fish and Gundu began eating. However, Gundu’s large appetite made Balu very tired. So Gundu took over and started feeding the exhausted Balu. After both had enjoyed the fishing expedition, they left for home.
author: Vamsi Tumuluru

title: The Bond that the time forgot
text: Acknowledgment I would like to express my deepest gratitude to my project supervisor, Ms. Ruchi Namrata, for their invaluable guidance and support throughout the research process. Their expertise and dedication were instrumental in shaping this project. I would also like to thank my classmates for their constructive feedback and encouragement. Additionally, I extend my appreciation to the Pratham story weavers for their assistance in accessing research materials. Lastly, I would like to express my gratitude to my Mother for her love and support during this project. This project truly reflects the collective effort of many, and I’m deeply appreciative of their contributions. About the Myself I am Vishwa Vinayak from grade 7C from the school, The Foundation School in Gunjur, Bangalore. I love to sing and play the flute for my relaxation. And I also have interests on sports like Basketball and Cricket. Chapter-1:Everyday life More than just familial, the father-son dynamic is a rich tapestry woven with threads of admiration, expectation, sometimes conflict, and deep-seated love, evolving from a child's hero-worship to an adult's complex understanding, often mirroring the silent struggles and unspoken hopes passed down through generations. Now enough of those heart-touching words, let's now get started with a courageous, fascinating and an unusual tale of two wise men fighting problems and emotionally clashing their whole life. It's a warm and pleasant morning in a small little home a family of three Chandrakanth an introvert dad very curious on his newspaper, Mayur a busy son who is a therapist by profession and Aasha a dedicated housewife taking care of both Chandrakanth and Mayur. Chandrakanth is the biggest introvert as he never goes anywhere out, always stays home and always reading something or another and guess what he HATES his son the most! Even his son doesn't know the exact reason and this is why he is extremely pissed at his dad! Chandrakanth is the luckiest human being on earth as for his attitude he got the most supportive wife in the world. Whatever he does she supports him! The son is half the time furious at his mom due to this reason. But anyway she continues the supportive mindset. And there's Mayur who has a fixed schedule. he's very perfect on his schedule and the most discipline man on earth! If he takes a work he wouldn't come out without finishing. Hospital, cricket, come home, eat, prepare his day for tomorrow and have a good eight to nine hour sleep and repeat. Chapter-2: uniquely unusual One fine evening Mayur while returning from his workplace he toppled over something looking like a watch as he is a very caring person, thinking a person left it here he picked it up! An unusual voice told that thank you sir and now I must take you to any time in the past as you helped me! Mayur was astonished, he asked that who are you? The voice told i know your problems, your father does not care about you isn't it? oh yeah, i also want to get the fatherly love everyone gets Mayur told to the mysterious voice. i know your problems and I am here to help the most. Mayur tells to the voice but i doubt if you can help me? Zoop! Mayur was teleported to a fierce war in the 1970s of the India-Pakistan war. He was confused, then he saw his grandfather and his grandmother fighting the war fiercely! And his dad was safe in the corner of the military campus sobbing and fearing that nothing bad must happen to his loved ones. But what he feared happened! His dad and his mom dropped to the ground dead, and all his parents comrades who fought along. He was devastated! Chandrakanth was on the ground longing for his parents to return. Instead of his parents the military nurse adopted him. Then he started acting very weird with people. He did not feel secure with humans around but to erase the loneliness the nurse showed him true motherlove. Chapter-3: But unfortunately, she found out that Chandrakanth has a mental disorder a big devil indeed! MISANTHROPY! A huge hatred towards humans. She was legit shocked, and didn't know what to do next. She tried all she could do, but there was nothing she could do! She roamed over temples, churches, mosques but nothing really changed. So he was only kept in his room, and his diary and mirror was his best friends. He couldn't at all interact with humans at his age if he saw anyone else other than the nurse or Mayur he would nearly skin them alive. Mayur was treated like an maternal uncle to him and did not hate him due to at least the little fatherly love left in Chandrakanth. Mayur was with overflowing eyes! He never even though that he would get love from his father like other people got. But his wish finally came true! That's why people say that if your really positive about something and its genuine it will two-hundred percent happen. But it was finally time for the final surgery that the nurse thought she would single-handedly do. But Mayur had a deep intention that if she does it single handedly she may fail. So as he was a professional therapist, he thought of giving it a shot! His approach was, Psychodynamic Counseling is probably the most well-known counseling approach. Rooted in Freudian theory, this type of counseling involves building strong therapist–client alliances. The goal is to aid clients in developing the psychological tools needed to deal with complicated situations. Also was concerned with the impact of early experiences and unconscious drives on behavior. Historically, Psychodynamic Therapy was a lengthy process, it is also applied as a relatively short-term approach. Research has indicated effectiveness for both long- and short-term psychodynamic treatment for psychiatric issues. This was indeed a popular and a interactive way but impactful. So he begged the nurse to give him the surgery and that he'll give his best on it. At first the nurse strictly didn't allow him to even participate but later after hours of pleading she let him take the lead as she had high hopes and believes in him. Chapter-4: The peak intensity The operating room buzzed with urgency. Bright lights shone down on the sterile table where a little boy lay unconscious. His pale face told a story of illness, one that had pushed him into a dark corner of despair. Dr. Mayur, the lead surgeon, adjusted his gloves. He was no stranger to high-stakes situations. But this was different. The boy's life hung by a thread, and the stakes were not just medical. They were emotional, too. “Scalpel,” Dr. Bashir, the phsycologist, called out. He monitored the boy’s vital signs, sweat beading on his forehead. “Heart rate dropping. We need to move faster.” Dr. Mayur nodded, focusing on the task at hand. They had to remove the damaged organ quickly. Time was slipping away. Each second felt like an hour. He remembered the nurse, her tear-streaked face when she had whispered, “He’s losing hope.” As they worked, the boy's life was a fragile thread. Would he come back from this? Would he find joy again? The doctors pushed these thoughts aside, concentrating on the procedure. “Clamp,” Dr. Mayur said, his voice steady. The room fell silent except for the beeping machines. Minutes felt like an eternity. A tense energy filled the air. Finally, they completed the procedure and began to stabilize him. “His heart is responding,” Dr. Bashir said, But the challenge wasn’t over. The road to recovery was long. They had to help this boy rise from the ashes of despair. In the days to come, they would not just be his doctors; they would be his lifeline. As the team prepared to close up, Dr. Mayur made a silent promise. He would do everything in his power to help this boy find joy again. They would fight for him. Chapter-5: Conclusion This was the moment Mayur finally reached his zenith of happiness his first surgery was a success that to with his own father! This is true happiness. Zoop! he was back to his normal world with his dad and mom different with his father love and peaceful. The conclusion usually signifies a fresh start, "shaping from sorrow a new love". This isn't necessarily a return to a childhood dynamic, but a mature relationship built on mutual respect and shared experiences as adults and friends.

title: poem
text: Poem 1: The Last Bus Home The bus was late like always is, Rain tapping hard on cracked glass, I checked my phone for updates And watched another minute pass. A tired driver rubbed his eyes, Said traffic was a mess tonight, We nodded like we’d heard it all And settled in for red brake lights. A kid behind me hummed a song, Off-key but trying his best, His backpack held too many books For someone who needed rest. Downtown slid by in blurry streaks, Closed shops, a flickering sign, Someone laughed, someone sighed out loud, All of us killing time. An old man talked about the past, How buses used to cost a dime, Nobody checked if it was true, We just let him rewind time. My stop came up without a sound, No big moment, no delay, Just wet shoes and a cold walk home At the tired end of the day. The bus pulled off, lights fading fast, Carrying stories I won’t know, Different lives on the same route, All heading somewhere slow. I unlocked my door, kicked shoes aside, Tomorrow waiting like before, Nothing changed, nothing dramatic Just life doing what it’s for. Poem 2: After the Test The bell rang loud, we shut our books, Pens dropped like they gave up too, Some people stretched, some stared ahead, Pretending they already knew. “Did you get number seven right?” Someone asked a little fast, A few heads nodded, others didn’t, Already stuck in the past. One kid said, “I definitely failed,” Then laughed like it was a joke, Another swore they aced the whole thing But wouldn’t say what they wrote. The teacher stacked the papers neat, Face unreadable, calm, Like she didn’t just hold our stress In a slightly crooked palm. We walked out into louder halls, Footsteps echoed as we passed by, The test already fading out, Under jokes and reasons why. Someone said grades don’t matter much, Someone said they do, The truth sat quiet in between Like it usually tends to do. By lunch, we talked about other stuff, Food, plans, the weekend ahead, Still, the test lived somewhere back In things we never said. When I got home, I didn’t check Notes or answers or blame, Tomorrow would show what it showed Life moves on all the same.
author: Amritha

title: My Trip To Pondicherry
text: Introduction Characters: 1.Avni (me!) 2.Meera- My fun loving cousin 3.Paati- My grandma 4.SK chittappa- My uncle 5.Aparna chitti- My aunt DAY 1 We left from Meera's house at around 5:30am and headed straight for Pondicherry. The moment we hit the road, Meera and I fell sound asleep because we had stayed up late the previous night playing around in her room. When we woke up, we woke up to blaring old Hindi music. SK Chittappa was responsible of that. Our first pit stop was at a Starbucks in Shoolagiri for breakfast. I had a blueberry muffin, shared some spinach and corn sanwiches, and had a strawberry milkshake that tasted like melted strawberry ice-cream with extra sugar. After that, we headed straight to Pondicherry, stopping only for lunch at this restraunt in Auroville called Consious cafe. I had spaghetti with vegan meatballs, and for desert I had a strawberry cheesecake. We then got to our hotel. It was a beautiful place called Esperan Heritage. It was built around a central courtyard with a small koi fish pond and a Ganesha idol in the centre of it all. Our room was rather long, with the bathroom almost as long as the room itself. After we rested in the room for a couple of hours, we stepped outside to explore the city. The first stop was the beach. It was full of rocks and people, but had little to no sand. It was a fine view with the waves crashing against the rocks. We stayed there for the rest of the evening and then proceeded to have dinner at a restaurant called Sola. I had tomato soup, and we all shared a pizza which was disguised as garlic bread, and went back to the hotel to end the day. DAY 2 We woke up at around 8:15 am, changed, and went straight for breakfast which was held in the hotel. It had idli, dosa, vadai and bread with jam. After everyone had their fair share, we drove to a handmade paper factory. We had booked for a tour in it. In the factory complex, there were lots of trees, so it was nice and cool. The tour itself ended up being quite underwhelming, because the whole paper making process was just pressing and drying pulp, and we didn't even get to see the dying process. The gift shop, on the other hand, was very nice. It had all kinds of hand made and hand painted products that were made from the paper manufactured in the factory. Our next unplanned stop was the botanical garden. In it was a large playground with plenty of people in it. We strolled around, absorbing the lovely green view. After a while, we came across a mini aquarium inside the garden, and we just had to visit it. There were many tropical fish, including angel fish, who were by far the prettiest. There was also a red-eared turtle which was also really cool. Our lunch stop was supposed to be at a restaraunt called 'The Spot', but it ended up being so crowded that we could not even find a table that wasn't in the sun. The next option was a place called 'Oh Pondi!'. We were lucky to have a table to ourselves, because it was getting crowded fast. It got so crowded that the waiters forgot to give us our order. With the help of some pesuasion, we went to an ice cream place called 'Richie Rich' that had over 15 different flavours to choose from. We had our ice creames by the sea. We ended up staying there for a good half an hour, watching the waves crash against the rocks. Then, we retreated to the hotel. It was decided that we would have dinner in 'Coramandal Cafe', the top rated restaraunt in Pondicherry. Aparna chitti and SK chittappa dropped Paati, Meera and I there and went off to find a parking spot. The cafe was so crowded that we felt like every single person in Pondicherry was in there. People were literally waiting on the stairs to get in, and the staff were issuing waiting time to each family. They gave us forty minutes, so we gave up and walked out. It was then that we realised that Paati's phone didn't have internet. Because of that, we had trouble following the live location that SK Chittappa had sent us. The only thing we knew about their location was that they were at a pani puri stall. We hailed an auto and somehow found our dear relatives. Everyone agreed that we should just go back to the hotel and order something. After a hearty dinner of dosas, we retired for the day. DAY 3 First thing in the morning, we headed to a town called Auroville for our day's activities. Our first stop was at a restaraunt called 'Bread & Chocolate. It was by far the best breakfast of the entire trip. Meera and I had a chocolate croissant, while my aunt had pancakes, my uncle had bread with some kind of tomatoes and egg, and my grandma had a farm fresh sandwich. In addition to this, we ordered a strawberry smoothiewhich Aparna chitti, Meera and I shared. After our amazing breakfast, we went to the chocolate factory that suppliedd 'Bread & Chocolate' their chocolate. It's name was 'Mason & Co'. We learnt how their chocolate was made, from the bean to the bar. First, the cacao beans were cracked to obtain cacao nibs. These nibs could be sweetened and then tasted. From these nibs, cacao powder and butter were separated. The chocolate is made from the powder. We gor samples of all their different types of chocolate, and 5 bars of sea salt dark chocolate free! By this time, we were all ready for lunch. We went to a small cafe in the middle of nowhere. I had a mozzerella that turned out to taste better without the mozzerella. We lingered there for some time before we went to the Auroville guest centre for an instrument making workshop that Meera and I were participating in. We were making a small bamboo flute-like instrument. It turned out to be a big success. After this, there was a long walk up a hill to a view point to view a big golden dome called Matramandir that was built by the founders of Auroville. This turned out to be quite exhausting even though we returned to the start of the 'trek' by bus, so we drove back to the hotel immediately. After our past experiences with Pondicherry and parking, we decided to order food again. With that, we put an end to yet another fun and exciting day. mm kij;jm DAY 4 At long last, it was time for the journey home. We had left early in the morning to beat the Bangalore traffic. Meera and I were pretty much knocked out by the time we hit the road, and woke up in about an hour. After a while of putting up with SK chittappa's annoying music, we finally arrived at 'Shri Saravana Bhavan', a restaurant that I feel is present on literally every south Indian highway. There, we had the regular idli and dosa and whatnot. All in all, fairly boring. After that, we were on the road the rest of the way back to my home. They were dropping me home first and then going th their home. We ended up getting extremely bored on the way, so we decided to play a few random word games. Once we were bored of that too, SK chittappa ended up introducing new songs to us that were actually good! Finally, after a long time, I was coming back home! Although it felt really good coming back home, I still missed Pondicherry more than I had expected I would. This trip is one that I will never forget, and the experiences will stay in my heart for ever. With those thoughts in my mind, I said goodbye to my relatives and retreated to the comforts of my little home.
author: Avni Narayan

title: Through Nizams' Land
text: ﻿ Hyderbad, one the most known places across India. the place is known for its history,culture and its tech. Hyderbad has ﻿ many rulers and dynasties, like the Mughals and the Quth Shah dynasty. the most well known dynasty in hyderbad is the Mughals becuase in the 1687 Mughals got control of Hyderbad after the Quth Shah dynasty. THE TRIP TO HYDERBAD We started from bengaluru at 5:15, the winter fog was so heavy and blurry. Hence, we drove slowly till Chikkaballapur. Then, we passed through Anantpur and Kurnool. then lastly, we reached Telangana and ate tasty biryani to get energy,to reach hyderbad at 3:50, about a nine hour trip. Ramoji Film City: Ramoji Film City is the world's largest film studio complex and a thematic destination located in Hyderabad, Telangana. It shows many film sets, amusement park rides, live shows, gardens, and many entertainment options for visitors.I went there and saw Bahubali film set and many other sets The Charminar is a 16th-century monument and mosque in Hyderabad, India, known for its Indo-Islamic architecture featuring four towering minars. Made by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591 to show the end of a plague, it's a symbol of the city's richness, blending Persian and Indian architectural elements with difficult work and big arches. There are many shops of clothes,ather and bangles because my mother made me go there. The Hyderbad trip was better than expected because i saw the mighty charminar and the massive Ramoji Film City. I will remember this trip forever

title: Athena
text: I just love going to Gujarat as I have already visited Gujarat a lot of times. Their food, religion, culture, tourist attractions and their dances just fascinate me. There were 3 days for our journey and I was just diving deeper or researching about "fun places to visit in Gujarat". Then came a place, highlighted in bold letters" The Gir National Park ". " What place was that? " I wondered. I searched about that place and found out that it was a lion sanctuary famous for it's Lions. Wow! That trip is going to be fun! As this fascination drew me closer to the journey, it was finally time! "Packing done, research about places done, finally everything is done" was a final check done by Mumma. After getting assured that everything is done, we locked our house and reached the airport. After waiting for an entire hour, we boarded our plane. "Papa I'm just so excited" exclaimed an excited me. After a light lunch, having rice, lentils and a sweet desert, we dozed off to a refreshing siesta. Cold AC winds and a soft carpet, as if pulling all tiredness from us, made a soothing Atmosphere for all passengers in the plane. OFF WE ARE TO GUJRAT! As our plane landed, we took our belongings and descended the stairs. We ate some snacks at the airport and left for our hotel. Luckily the hotel was quite close to the airport, so we didn't take much time. After some refreshment, we went to our first attraction to visit, The Modhera Sun Temple! A beautiful, stunning 11th century hindu temple dedicated to the Sun God, Surya Dev. We worshipped Surya Dev, took some family pictures and enjoyed there. It was 7:00 pm when we left the temple to our second place, Rani Ki Vav, which is quite close to the temple. Even though it was a dark evening, we could clearly see the stunning artifact. It is said that this was buit by Rani Udayamati as a memorial of her husband as a water conservation structure. After eating a delicious, finger licking good dinner, we went to our hotel and rested ourselves. That's how our day ended fantastically! The next day, we woke up at around 6:00am. We got ready and hopped into our taxi. Guess where we were going? We were arriving at the Gir National Park! as we reached there, I saw a scary lioness. Probably a powerful one. I was staring at the lioness when Papa called "Deetya, we are going for a safari, come on!". We all hopped in the safari jeep and off we go! We all saw lots of lions and lionesses there, litrally lots of them. But my favourite was the first lioness I saw. Eventhough she might be scary, I just saw the gentleness and goodness in her eyes. The safari was finally over after 3 hours or so. It was lunchtime and we had gone to a restaurant. Lots of delicacies were kept and eaten by us. Yummy food! Ymm... After the lunch, me and my family were quite tired. So, we decided to continue our trip the next day and we returned to our hotel. After a good rest, we woke up in the evening. I watched TV for sometime and went down for a stroll with my family. Down there, we saw a huge buffet being set for all people staying at the hotel. Our dinner was finalised there. After a huge gujrati meal, we went back to our room and enjoyed our slumber (I was quite enjoying my dreams of having a sweet dog). Good Night Gujrat! Next morning, I got ready as quick as possible. So was my entire family ready. We were set for another adventure in Gujrat. We had a few places to visit that day but I requested Papa if we could go to the Gir National Park again. "It was so fun there", I told Papa. And so, he agreed! We reached there as soon as possible because we had other plans for the day too. Papa got a jeep for our safari. Well for me, in the meanwhile I was staring at my favorite lioness again but she seemed quite weak than the previous day. "What happened to her" I wondered. Then I heard Papa calling me. I went close to the jeep and I saw a person at the driver's seat trying to start the jeep. "Sir it is not starting, maybe there is a problem in the engine, it will take sometime to repair" said that person sitting at the driver's seat. So there was a shade quite close to the lioness. I sat there staring at the lioness's move, but what I saw next was terrifying... Two people, their face covered with black masks, got food for the lioness. Before giving it to her, they mixed something it the food. Then, the food was given to her. The people instantly ran of without closing the gate. As the lioness was eating, she suddenly stopped. Then, she fell hard on the ground, as if dead. I quickly ran to her, without thinking. I went to pet and comfort her, also to make her feel better, but she stopped breathing.... Tears rolled down my eyes. I quickly ran inside the shade, where I was sitting before and found a first aid kit for animals. I took my phone and asked google for what medicine should I give her at such condition. Luckily, the medicine google recommended was in the first aid kit. I took it and ran to the lioness. I dropped a few drops in her mouth. After sometime when she didn't seem to show signs of life, I realised she was dead. I got up, turned back, off to go, when I heard something... I turned back to see that the lioness had opened her eyes! She got up and came closer to me. I was quite scared, but she came to me and licked my hand. She had trusted me! I went inside and told this incident to the management team of this santuary. They believed me had were quite impressed. They assured me that they will find and catch the culprit. When this incident reached the ears of my parents, they were very proud of me. I went back to the lioness and gave her a warm hug. We played for hours. I even gave her a name "ATHENA". Then sadly, it was time for me to go back to the hotel. We spent a few more days travelling in gujrat, playing with Athena and enjoying, but then we had to leave... I sat in the taxi, quite satisfied but sad too. We travelled for sometime and I saw the Gir National Park again. I asked the driver to stop the car for a moment and asked my parents if I could go out. They agreed. I went and stood at the edge of the road, from there I saw Athena. I looked at her and she looked at me with tearful eyes. Then I said " Good bye and see you soon, ATHENA".

title: The Little Christmas Tree
text: Once upon a time there was a tiny little Christmas tree named Piney in a Christmas tree farm. This little Christmas tree was very very small. When she looked at the other Christmas trees which were tall and blooming, she felt a little sad. “When will I grow up?" she asked. It was nearing Christmas time, and all the people from the nearby Snowway village were coming to the farm to pick their favourite christmas tree. The trees stood tall and were proud of their green coat as they sparkled and shone under the midday sun. Once upon a time there was a tiny little Christmas tree named Piney in a Christmas tree farm. This little Christmas tree was very very small. When she looked at the other Christmas trees which were tall and blooming, she felt a little sad. “When will I grow up?" she asked. It was nearing Christmas time, and all the people from the nearby Snowway village were coming to the farm to pick their favourite christmas tree. The trees stood tall and were proud of their green coat as they sparkled and shone under the midday sun. Piney saw all this and thought, “Nobody wants me, nobody needs me. I will remain on the farm this year and maybe the next and the next year, until I become that tall”. She started to cry: “Nobody nobody nobody wants, a little tree like me, I will stay here forever, Oh poor me”. Just then she heard a slight rustling behind her. She swayed a bit and looked around. “Hi Piney, how are you doing?, asked granny Mousie Mou. Now everybody at the farm knew granny Mousie Mou. She was the softest, furriest mouse with kindness in her eyes. Piney knew she could tell her the truth. “I feel unwanted granny Mou”, she said. “Everybody will leave the farm, except me and nobody is even wanting to look at me”. Mousie Mou lowered her spectacles and looked at Piney with affection. “Oh dear Piney, never underestimate yourself or the joy that you can bring to another. Wait for the Christmas miracle, as you never know what could happen! Don’t lose hope dear Piney”. And saying that she vanished under the hole near the shed. Piney again started to cry: “Nobody nobody nobody wants, a little tree like me, I will stay here forever, Oh poor me”. Piney sighed. Days passed and the snow fell gently over the farm, making everything look magical. That night Piney looked at the moon and the shimmering tall pine trees that glistened in the moonlight and prayed for her Christmas miracle. The next day, floods of families came to the farm, each one excited to choose a tree of their choice. Piney looked around with awe. “Someday someone would want me too”, she thought, and Piney went to sleep. A few days later, it became very cold and the winds howled through the branches of the tall fir trees. It was an impossible day to be outside, therefore the Christmas tree farm was strangely quiet. Just then a yellow van came hobbling around to the farm. It moved ever so slowly just making it to the gate. A family of three stepped out. A graceful young lady and a tall man who was holding a young child in his arms. The girl looked around five years old. She has the most lovely golden curls that could be seen hanging over her shoulders. They walked into the farm looking around intently at the fir trees. Suddenly Piney felt someone touching her leaf. She opened her eyes and Lo, she saw a young girl standing with her parents. “Mamma, can we take this one?” the girl asked her mother. Piney waited with bated breath. The girl's parents looked at each other and smiled. “ Yes dear, we can take this one, this tree is just as tall as you are!” Piney felt like she would explode and jump out of the soil that very moment. All her tiny roots shook with glee. The next day Piney woke up to a pink colored bedroom with a beautiful golden curly haired girl sleeping soundly on the bed near her. There was a mirror right opposite Piney and when she looked at it she gasped. Piney was decorated with silver bells and baubles of different colours. There were also white feathery angels and mini stockings along with ribbons strung around. And the best part was the topper which was a shining red star. Piney felt like a showstopper. And then she began to sing: I am tiny, but I am fine, I bring happiness to the little one I am tiny, but I am fine, I thank this loving home a ton! From that day onwards, Piney never felt sorry for herself. She knew that however large or small you are, you can bring happiness to another being. So she held her branch high and became the closest friend to the golden haired girl of Snowway Village.

title: Christmas in Ooty
text: Th e Christmas lights of Bangalore still shimmered in my mind's eye as the Nilgiri Blue Mountain train its final, breathless ascent into Ooty. The air, sharp with the scent of eucalyptus and woodsmoke, was a thrilling shock to the system. This was our families escape, a trade of humid coastlines for misty hills, a white Christmas of the soul if not of the snow. Our third day, the sun clear and generous, was reserved for the Government Botanical Garden. Stepping through the arched entrance was like walking into a living, breathing kaleidoscope. The December chill was softened by the sheer abundance of life. But it was the central lawn that stole my heart a vast, emerald tapestry so impeccably manicured it seemed unreal, terraced down a gentle slope, with a star-shaped flower bed bursting with scarlet salvias and canary-yellow marigold, a living Christmas ornament laid at our feet. My parents vanished into the Fossil Tree section, marveling at the petrified echoes of a 20-million-year-old past. I, however, was drawn deeper, following a serpentine path into the heart of the garden. The noise of the town faded, replaced by the whisper of a thousand leaves. I found myself in the Fern House, a realm of pre-historic green. The air here was cooler, moist, and hung with the smell of damp earth. Lacy fronds, some as tall as me, created a vaulted ceiling that filtered the sunlight into a soft, jade glow. It felt cathedral-like, silent and ancient. Emerging, I followed a fragrance-sweet, heady, and utterly unfamiliar-to a section where bushes were covered in clusters of delicate, white, bell-shaped flowers. A small plague read: Daphne. A kindly gardener saw my curiosity. "Winter Daphne, sir," he said with a warm smile. "It blooms only in cold. Its perfume is the ghost of an Ooty Christmas." I inhaled deeply, imprinting that scent into my memory, a sensory souvenir no photograph could capture. I met my family by the Italian-style garden, where topiary shrubs were sculpted into whimsical cones and spirals, like a festival of green Christmas trees. We sat on a sun-warmed stone bench, watching rosy-cheeked children roll down the gentle slopes of the main lawn, their laughter ringing in the clear air. That evening, back in our cozy lodge, as a log fire crackled and the scent of ginger tea filled the room, my thoughts weren't of the boat ride on the lake or the bustle of the market. They were of that quiet Fern House, the surprise of the Daphne's fragrance, and the impossible green of that vast, terraced lawn. The Botanical Gardens hadn't just been a visit; it had been a gentle rearrangement of my inner landslide. It was just a reminder that the deepest magic of Christmas wasn't just in celebration, but in contemplation; not only in the bright and the bold, but in the quiet, enduring green heart of an ancient, walking world. My trip to Ooty was a postcard of mist and mountains, but its stamp, forever fragrant and green, was from the garden.

title: The library of portals
text: It was quite a pleasant day at the library when Piper Page, the librarian, decided to take up the night shift at the library. Though she was excited to start, she was scared as well, as she thought, "What if something goes wrong!?" At night, the time was about 9 pm at her local library. Piper was walking to the library in a long brown coat with baggy jeans and a collar - neck t-shirt, her straight brown hair with blond highlights let down, and her hazel eyes glowing. She walked into the library, and the manager gave her instructions and the keys to lock up after he left. She nodded and went on with her job. First, she roamed around for a while, then she decided to go to a book section, more specifically, the thriller section. She saw this one fantasy book in the wrong section and decided to read it. The book was about dragons, but she couldn't find any pictures of dragons in the book, not even one. As she continued reading for about 5 minutes, she finally came across a page that had a dragon on it. She examined it because it looked like the dragon was about to jump out of the book. She turned around for just 5 seconds as she heard a swift movement from behind, and to her surprise, the dragon in her book was gone and was throughout the library as if it was searching for something or someone. She clicked back into reality, and she started running towards the direction the dragon had gone. She arrived at the edge of the library, where there was nothing but a glowing corner. She stepped towards the corner, and she felt a push behind her. She fell into the corner, which was surprisingly a portal to a very beautiful land with a red and orange sky (sunset) and a beautiful sea of meadows (a sea made of literal grass!), and she spotted the dragon. She came back to her senses and ran towards the dragon, gladly running near the beach and not over the ocean, and she ran towards the direction of where the dragon was running, and she caught him jumping into another portal to another land. As she jumped in as well, tired, she witnessed the most amazing sight: the hills were purple, the sky was blue, and there were sky mobiles everywhere, and the dragon was still running as if it just wanted to make Piper run. On she ran, she kept running through different portals, some with mermaids, some with fairies and some with even flying books and at the end she stopped and stared into one portal...that portal looked familiar like she already jumped through the portal before, but she had no time to waste because she had to catch this dragon before 6 am and it was already 5.40 am. So she started sprinting towards the portal as it was slightly far away. Then she jumped through. As she entered, she realised that she had come back to the library again. Then she started searching through every section to find the dragon. Just then, she heard a movement, and when she saw the thriller section, where the book was, she witnessed the same dragon duplicating itself into colours and then jumping into the book again. When she opened the book. She saw the dragons smiling at the page and she locked up and left for the morning.

title: When warmth is in the winter
text: It was a cold winter morning and Skylar had just woken up. Her parents had gone to visit her sick Aunt for a few days. The only grown up in the house was Skylar's loving and old Grandma, Stella. Even though Stella loved her grandchild with all her heart Skylar didn't have the same approach towards her grandmother. Anyway, back to when Skylar woke up. She got up with a longing to go back to bed. Well, she always did. Stella made masala dosa for breakfast, and of course it was excellent but Skylar always said it was "okay". Skylar ate without telling her grandma something. This something was that Skylar needed permission, from an adult to go to her next field trip. She knew her parents would never allow as the field trip was to a trek. She was too shy to ask her grandma. Even though she knew her grandma wouldn't hesitate to allow her, she just didn't know how to. She practiced in front of the mirrors but she couldn't muster up the courage to ask her. Stella was an independent woman who had learnt to do so with the demise of her husband. Skylar knew this very well but she didn't have time to care of her when she was little and she didn't know how to start now. Skylar was now heading to the school bus in a hurry. Her grandma was going to clean the house starting with Skylar's room. She diligently started and spotted a diary which she knew belonged to Skylar and she also knew that she wouldn't be happy that her grandma read through her very secretive diary. But curiosity got the best of Stellla. She opened the diary going through every page, Then she stumbled upon yesterday's entry. She discovered that Skylar had a field trip and how she felt about telling her Grandma about it. She felt bad about the fact that her grand daughter didn't feel comfy about conversing with her. She wanted to change this. Once Skylar came home she was confronted by her grandma about the truths she hid from her in her diary. Skylar told her that she was sorry but Stella wanted to tell her something before Skylar's parents came the next day. Stella told Skylar to meet her at the swing at 8 sharp and so she did. Stella told her grand daughter stories about her childhood out of the blue. Before they dispersed they both told each other that they should have more sessions like this often and in that flow Stella handed Skylar a note where in she had signed and given permission for the filed trip as well as a yellow sweater. Skylar hugged her grandma and said that she would never desert her. She also told her that she loved her and the yellow sweater she gave. In this moment both the grandmother and the grand daughter felt a warmth in that cold night (this warmth was not caused by the sweater Stella gifted to Stella).A warmth that felt super special to both. They slept with this warmth and lived with it and learnt to cherish it for a life. Both kept in touch until Stella's demise and they lived happily ever after.

title: My Journey To The Cholas
text: Hello, all. My name is Malhar Kulkarni. This book is a journey of mine to the Chola Empire's capital; Thanjavur. This is the most beautiful and scenic journey of mine. But, who had made it more enjoyable? My best friend; Aaron Arun. We know each other for around nine years, so you can tell how our connection was. Anyway, without further ado, lets begin this magnificent journey. Both of us went with our parents, along with Aaron's grandparents. We used two cars; Aaron came in my car, and his family in one more hatchback. Totally, we were eight people. We started from our homes at around seven o' clock, and we met in no time, as our house is just about three kilometers away from each other. Our first stop for breakfast came around at nine o' clock, and we ate dosa, idly, vada, and meals. Me and Aaron were full, but still decided to eat some snacks in the car. When we were on the highway, we were completely asleep. Then, my dad woke both of us up, and we went to eat food for lunch, at around noon. Then, we got on to the service road, as we got into city. then, we started to look for the resort we booked. It was surrounded by just fields, so it was completely a rural backdrop. The name of the resort was Deshadan Chola, which is a resort with around sixteen rooms, and there was a field with grass in the center, with a swimming pool at the back. The name has 'Chola' in it, as each room represents a royal person from the Chola dynasty. Aaron's grandparents were in the room called 'Rajendra', Aaron's room as 'Sundara' and ours as 'Aditya'. We decided to go to Brihadeshwara Temple at evening. When we returned at night, we were exhausted. Then, we just decided to dose off for the night. We had totally enjoyed the temple. There were many things going on, because of the trip to here. The way we were interested in the car to stay up for some time is because of a Spotify playlist that I made, and Aaron added nine songs to collab. What we did after going to the Brihadeshwara temple, is admire those glorious sculptings of it. Once we woke up in the morning,we swam, and we went to the restaurant, after getting ready. There was a buffet, and we quickly ate. After eating, we were playing cards, and other games with the whole family. Then we went to Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple, and spent some time there. The problem was that it was getting hot, and we were about to get baked by the sun, so we ate and explored. We walked everywhere around the temple, and admired its beauty. We found it so overwhelming that this temple had thousands of hand carved architectures! Then, we went walking around after coming back to Thanjavur, and then we ate a lot of street food. The food was mouth watering and yummy, but our stomach did not really enjoy it as such. With an aching stomach, we ate dinner at a restaurant, and went all the way back to our cars, to rest for the night. The next day, we woke up and swam, got ready and ate breakfast. Today was a big day. We started in the morning, and we drove far, to some temples. Then, we stopped at Star Biryani. The venue was not that of a luxury, but the food was first-rate. Then, we went to an ice cream store, and I ate a scoop of Tiramisu and Belgian Chocolate, and Aaron chose a Choco chip, with some other fruity flavour. As Aaron's grandparents were tired, they were called a cab and went back home. Then, we started. We went to a beach, with an old Danish Mansion on the side. we went to the beach first, and made a cool looking sand castle, which got totally destroyed by the wind. Then, we went to explore the mansion. The mansion was huge, with an old bot of the owner, and the things he collected. The house was made in the nineteenth century, but still looked very ahead of its time. We were very amazed to see the fort and the beach. By the time we were done exploring, we saw that the time needed to reach back home was over two hours! That means, we were going to reach by ten o' clock at night! So we rushed backed to the resort, and ate dinner in the resort's restaurant. Tomorrow was the day, the day we were saying goodbye to Thanjavur, and going home. So, we played a card game called 'Pit', which is a game where you have to get a pair of a particular item, by giving off your other cards that you don't need, to get the same amount of cards back. So the game basically worked on trade. Anyways, we finished around five games of pit, and slept our last night in Thanjavur. So, we woke up in the morning, went to swim, and went to get ready and eat our breakfast. After breakfast, we rested for sometime, and then started for home. We kept on driving, and vibing to the playlist. We stopped at a rock museum, and after seeing the exhibitions, we started again. Then, we ate lunch at a restaurant on the highway, and then, we continued. Then, we reached Thiruvanmalayur, and went to Lord Shiva's Agni Temple. By the time we entered, it started to rain. Then, as we went through the temple to seek blessings from Lord Shiva, we headed out. We ran one by one, to reach the other side. Then, we realised, that we left our shoes at the other end of this big temple! As our stress abated, we went outside to call an auto. All of us eight somehow fit into an auto, and we drove to the other end. The mothers and grandparents stayed in the auto, while we got out to bring everybody's footwear with our fathers. Then, we walked all the way to our cars, and again started from the temple, to home. We kept on driving, and then, we finally reached the main highway to our home. After three long hours, we reached home. That was the end of the magnificent trip to Thanjavur. Here, our journey concludes. The End
author: Malhar  Milind Kulkarni
illustrator: Amrita Dasgupta; Clyde   Beech; Lindy  Pelzl; Marco Tibasima; Mohith Mohan; UK Nhal

title: Agustya's trip around India
text: Agustya was walking among the trains at the railway station. It was always his dream to ride one, only his parents never let him do so they had always travelled by car. He had only travelled to school by bus and nowhere except his hometown. It was always the deepest desire of his heart if he had money of his own he'd go for train rides all the time. After one week of begging his parents they allowed him to ride along with them to his hometown. Agustya felt delighted, but alas fate had i's own path for Agustya. When his father got off the train for snacks Agustya went along but got separated from his father and in confusion boarded the wrong train. Agustya was terrified but little did he know that he could experience life as he wished it would be. The conductor(driver) of the train was a kind hearted man his name was Arun. He wanted to reunite the boy with his parents. He first asked Agustya where his parents went. Poor Agustya had never heard the name of his hometown. He and his parents had never said the place's name. Agustya had described how it looked like but that information was vague. So Agustya said that it was a 4 day journey. Arun found out it must be atleast 2000 km away from the city they were in. so they visited Delhi but Agustya said his home town had less pollution and was less crowded. So they went to Jammu and Kashmir but he said his hometown was less cooler. So they then tried Assam but Agustya said the place was absolutely not like his home town. They finally tried Goa and it was Agustya's hometown. They went to his grandma's house. It was locked! Agustya's grandma was away. They then returned home where they started and guess what they found Agustya's parents and his grandma they all looked worried sick. Arun and Agustya's journey came to an end they both vowed hat when Agustya came to age they would go on a year long journey around the world. Arun was thanked, given many gifts and honored. Agustya was taught a valuable lesson be content with what you have. but never stop dreaming keep on dreaming but make sure you make your dreams come true.
author: Dhanvine Krishnan AR

title: Spanish
text: Once upon a time a dinosaur named David was washing his dishes from breakfast. When he finished, he went to drink water and eat fish that was there. When the fish were in his belly, they started to tickle and the dinosaur started to laugh. When he stopped laughing, he got up and became to jump so that the fish would leave. So, the fish then left his belly and David said, "Oh, it is like they were in the water!" So then he ate donuts for breakfast and went to sleep to relax.

title: Dad's Party
text: Once upon a time, in the evening of March 16th, a girl named Ana and her dog named Plato. Ana had started to write a letter to her father for his party and she wrote "Dear dad..." She started to write on her paper and finished after an hour. She had written a lot and had made a drawing of her with her dad. When she finished the letter, she decided to go to a postal service to speed up the letter and surprise her dad, but the postman said that he could not expedite a letter without a stamp. So, her dad decided to buy a stamp from the postman. On March 17th, for her dad's party, she letter arrived at Ana's house. Her dad thought they had made a mistake. But when Ana asked him to read the letter, he understood it all and was very happy.
author: Palak Kundalia

title: WHISPERS OF THE REAL WORLD
text: The river flows, so calm, so wide, Mountains stand with strength and pride. Wind whispers through the trees above, Nature teaches patience, care, and love. A child walks through the forest green, Finding beauty in sights unseen. Raindrops fall, the sun will glow, Life moves gently, steady and slow. Storms may rage, the earth may shake, Paths may twist, and hearts may ache. But every challenge, every trial, Teaches courage all the while. No magic hides, no talking beasts, Yet every moment is a feast. Stories bloom where nature stays, In simple, real, and wondrous ways.
author: monal gupta
illustrator: David Yambem; Dỗ Thái Thanh; Joanna Davala; Sangeeta Das

title: Bebo's Desert Adventure
text: Good morning! I’m Bebo. Did you recognise me? I’m a ladybug, a cute little red beetle with black dots. This is my friend Jewel, the grasshopper. “What’s that?” I asked. A blue and grey truck rolled past us while we were looking for breakfast near the park fence. The driver stepped out and walked into the big vegetable store near the park. “I want to see the truck up close,” I said. “Be careful,” Jewel warned me. I just couldn’t help it. I love seeing new interesting things and learning more about them. I walked closer, but the boy from the vegetable store had kept big crates full of vegetables near the truck. The crates blocked my view, so I crawled onto a crate full of carrots to see better. Suddenly, the driver and the boy started loading the crates into the truck. I had nowhere to go! So I quickly hid among the carrots. The driver shut the door after all the crates were loaded. “Oh no! I’m locked inside.” It was dark, and for a moment, I felt scared. I slowly moved to the next crate and felt soft tomatoes under my feet. I took a deep breath. “Don’t worry, Bebo,” I told myself. “I’ll be alert and will fly out as soon as the truck stops.” But oh dear… The truck didn't seem to stop at all. It kept moving for hours. At first, the ride was smooth, but soon it became very bumpy. Every time the truck jumped, I jumped too! “Oh my!” I cried. “When will this journey end?” The truck stopped for a while, but the doors did not open. Maybe the driver was eating dinner. But what about me? I was hungry too. Ladybugs are farmers’ friends. We don’t eat vegetables. We eat tiny insects that harm plants. So I munched on some aphids stuck on the tomato and brinjal leaves. Tired and full, I fell asleep holding on tightly to the carrots. When I woke up, the truck was still moving. I knew I was very far away from my home now. I was worried. How would I find my way back? I also felt curious. Where was I going? Which new place am I going to see? At last, the truck stopped! The driver unloaded the crates and called a man with a cart to take the vegetables to his village shop. Before anyone noticed, I quickly crawled out. “At last, I’m free!” I cheered. But… where was I? Under my feet was soft orangey sand. All around me, I saw sand, sand and more sand, with a few strange looking plants. “What is this place?” I wondered. I decided to fly up high to see better. I landed carefully on a tall plant, avoiding its sharp spines. Everywhere I looked, there was brown-orangey sand, sandy hills and very few oddly shaped plants scattered here and there. The sun was bright and the sky was clear and blue. The air was warm and dry. I had reached a desert! I felt thirsty. So I flew to a spiky plant with bright red flowers. “Mmm!” The nectar was sweet and refreshing. I also ate a few tiny mites near the flowers. “Now I’m ready to explore!” I said. As I landed on the sand, I noticed something moving. It blended so well with the sand that I almost missed it. It was a lizard! A little farther ahead, I heard a strange rattling sound. I peeked from behind a spiny plant. There was a snake, sandy-coloured like the ground, making the rattling sound with its tail. I stayed very still until it slithered away. After moving a little ahead, I saw something HUGE! It had long legs, flat feet, a long curved neck rising up to the sky and a big hump on its back. I had never seen or heard about anything like that before. It was happily munching leaves. “Don’t be scared,” it laughed. “I’m a camel. People call me the ship of the desert because I can travel easily on sand!” Just then, I saw a scorpion scurrying away, waving its pincers. I watched it disappear quickly across the sand. As the sun set, the sand began to cool. What an interesting day it had been! I felt tired and sleepy. So I searched for a safe place to rest for the night. I found a cozy spot inside a small leafy bush. Soon, I drifted into a peaceful sleep. The next morning, I knew I had to find my way out. The desert plants had thick stems to store water and their leaves had turned into spines. The animals were all sandy-coloured. They were all well adapted to live in the desert, but I stood out with my shiny red coat. It was an interesting place to visit, but I was clearly not meant to live here. After climbing a sandy hill, I saw a yellow truck nearby. Some men were loading stones onto it. “That’s my ride out of the desert!” I smiled. I flew straight to the truck. Quietly, I sat on top of the stones. Soon, the truck started moving. We were leaving the desert! I waved goodbye to the sandy hills, the spiny plants, the lizards, the snakes, the camels… …and the scorpions too. This little desert adventure turned out to be fun after all! I hope to visit a new place soon and tell you all about it. Bye-bye! Let’s Talk About Bebo’s Adventure! How did Bebo feel when she was stuck inside the truck? What can we do if we feel scared or lost? Who can help us? Which animals did Bebo see in the desert? Why do you think many of them looked like the sand? Are the desert plants different from the plants near your home? If yes, then how? Where would you like Bebo to go on her next adventure?
author: Garima Sinha

title: Travel Troubles
text: My suitcase, a black hole where socks tuck deep, One after the other, a mystery to keep, My toothbrush vanished into thin air Probably lazing and sippin’ juice somewhere Packed books for “emergencies” galore But the chips were the treasures, I swore The flimsy map grins with delight As I wander in lunch time fright! Security grilled my gum like it was crime Said “sticky stuff? Nah.” Every time While ketchup packets hid in my sack, Laughing, as they plan their snack-attack! Humidity turned my hair to a wild fuzz Looks like a cactus, caught in dramatic buzz Combed it once and it fought back with glee Now it waves at strangers, free as can be Sand snuck in my socks and formed a clan Holding meetings, as per plan It sits in my bag, like it’s made of gold Planning adventures, both brave and bold! Ordered fancy juice with dramatic flair Got lemonade, not cold, unfair! Mr. Waiter winked “artisan zing!” As my wallet cried with a tiny spring I climbed the dunes like a mighty queen, Then rolled like a pancake on a sandy scene My dignity waved goodbye with a grin, While crickets laughed deep from within The hotel bed looks soft and sweet Like marshmallows tucked in a mighty treat But springs hide like spies underground, They poke and prod without a sound The minibar whispers with glowing pride, Tempting treasures I cannot hide, The prices make my wallet weep, Like dragons hoarding gold they keep The shower roars like a dragon’s breath Hot then cold, such a wicked test I wrestle the spray like a hero would, But it splashes me where I once stood So I conquer beds and showers wild, Snacks that cost more than a child, Travels odd challenges make me grin, I laugh at chaos and take a spin So here’s to travel, goofy and grand, To missing brushes and castles of sand, It’s mayhem with glitter and lemon zest But I still want another quest
author: Dvaitha Prajith Nair
illustrator: Asha Susan  Alex; Pratiti Parmar; Sharath Ravishankar; Sushant Ahire

title: Kabir the curious
text: Kabir was one curious boy. He would take his cat, Moti, and go to the frontal park every single day. Mamma usually says, "It's such a long walk". But by his face itself, anyone can understand that he is trying to ignore it. He calls Deepa and Vignesh, his classmates and best friends and comes from his house in D-BLOCK. One day, Kabir fell from the stairs to the playground. Only Moti came to his aid but all she could do is stay there and wail. But before climbing the steps after overcoming a lot of pain, he saw a bright light from the north side of the gate. He decided to investigate tomorrow after his wound healed. The next day, his wound miraculously healed. He took out his "EAGLEHAWK VISION" binoculars and looked exactly where the light had come from. But by now, the light seemed to have vanished. Suddenly, a bright light blinded him. It seemed to be coming from the layout opposing their apartment. The very next day, he decided to investigate the mystery. So, Kabir took out his ball and took Moti with him w\to the layout. It was a treacherous walk to the layout, but Kabir and Moti remained cheery. After reaching, they discovered that the layout had houses big and small. After going back and rechecking, it seemed to be coming from Villa#18. Then another flash of light rushed into his eye. By now, they had been done with the blinding flashes. But they discovered that all the disco lights have been coming from a tiny supervillain, a pendant with a mirror. They asked everyone about who it belonged to and all the clues pointed to Rishab, a naughty boy just like him who liked to pluck mangoes. It seemed that his loose pendant fell off him while plucking a mango high off the ground. Then, they both became friends The next day, they hosted an event in the layout that let the children's imagination free by imagining daily objects as instruments.
author: Niranjan K

title: ANNA'S TRIP TO DISNEYLAND
text: Anna is a girl who is curious at everything, like when there is any assignement on researching any artifact she gets so interested. It is winter and holidays started and their parents planned on them to go to Disneyland. And if you do not know about Anna, she is such a crazy girl around trips to faraway places. And it is also her birthday in a few days. Anna bought many different chocolates for her birthday and many clothes and dresses also for her trip. NEXT DAY... Anna went to school and imidietly started talking to her best friend right after she reached. She immidietly told about her going to Disneyand. Anna is really fond of travelling to far away places especaily with her family. 2 DAYS LATER... it's been 2 days and there is only one day left for her birthday and 3 days for her TRIP!! But some thing was wrong none of her friends were talking to her especially right before her birthday! Anna did not even do anything wrong but she did not know why everyone was not talking to her. Anna was very upset, really upset than anyone human being would be. Anna continued her day being moody and did not even talk to her parents when they asked her about her birthday plan. The parents ware also upset because they never saw her daughter this sad and that to before her birthday. Anna was thinking why her friends were ignoring her,but anyways she still packed her bag. It was her birthday!! and she silently entered the school premises to lead to a surprise, her friends were not talking to her because they were planning a surprise party for her, her friend screamed out loud "SURPRISE"! and loaded her with many of gifts. She had the best birthday of her life!! She never had a surprise party in her life. " IT WAS TRIP DAY"! shouted Anna loudly while running into her car hood with her luggage. she immediately went and sat in her window seat with her bestfriend, her diary. The trips starts and so does the fun, Anna has her headphones on and she is listening to one of her favourite play lists but Anna found something wierd. the wierd thing was that There was a bird continusely chirping more sounding like the bird was asking for help. When Anna went to check on what it was she saw a bird asking for help because it was stuck on tree branch, Anna's kindness helped the bird to come down. And it was rescued and taken care of from the garden managers and farmers. they have been tavelling for about 6 hrs and it has become dark already. Anna sees something golden in the forward, when they went to close to it they saw a golden coyotee. Anna is fond of animals that are not found in their place. Anna finally reached her destination to her Resort and she directly jumped on the bed, but she does not sleep until she writes in her diary. It is the next day and their day is full of discovery and explorations. Anna straight went to the roller coaster and had a BANG!! Anna loves roller coasters and is not even an inch scared. Anyways Anna had a bang with her disney trip. But all that fun made her hungry so she ate full stomach and explored a little more and did a few more rides. Finally, Anna is done with the disney trip and is travelling back home. But the sad thing is her holidays are over and school starts again. so this was a chaotic holidays, How was your experience of the holidays?

title: Story of Life
text: Story of Life Getting pushed from the light to the dark, wandering aimlessly through it all Too much homework, too less time. Far too busy too even make a call Realising that most people aren't who they claim to be, Two faced friendships are all that's there. Jealousy and envy are always present, This friendship's like a ride, you have to pay the fare Questions, questions are everywhere, about finding who you really are. Classes, sports attend it all, only to be told to raise the bar Behind the dark hides a clear future, that comes once your hardships are over. Pull away the curtain, face the window Walk on the golden path decorated with four leaf clovers
author: Avani Salgaonkar
illustrator: Lê Thị  Mai Phương; Sarah Rose de Villiers; Wiehan de Jager

title: A Republic Day Dream
text: She had to reach school earlier than usual for singing practice. Her class was going to sing the National Anthem for the chief guest on 26 January. But Poonam was not ready for school. Suman had to persuade Poonam every day to come to school, even though Poonam was very good at studies. The reason was that t he school in the village had classes only up to Grade 7, and that made Poonam miserable. For further studies, the children had to travel 15 kilometers everyday. Often, they were not allowed to travel so far and had to stop going to school. The thought of not being able to go to school next year kept troubling Poonam and haunted her everyday. It was 26 January, Republic Day - the day India had got its Constitution. The school was filled with excitement. The chief guest that day was the first woman Sarpanch (Village Chief) of the village. W hen the girls saw her hoist the Indian Tricolour, they felt pleasantly surprised and very proud. The chief guest won the hearts of all the children with a heartwarming speech. She announced that from next year, the school would now have classes beyond Grade 7. Poonam was overjoyed. Next morning, Poonam happily got ready for school before Suman arrived. As the Indian Tricolour flew high, Poonam felt her hopes rise too.
author: Bhavna Gupta

title: Maya's Best Birthday Gift
text: Once there lived a girl named Maya. She used to love dolls. Her birthday was on november 14. She was curius of her birthday gifts. And she was very curius about only one thing which is a doll. She was eagerly waiting that someone give her a beautiful doll as her birthday gift. It was friday. Maya's birthday was on saturday. She was very excited. She said excitely to her mother, '' MOMMY, MOMMY what are you doing '' Her mother said ''Maya I am doing your birthday preparation'' ''So now tell me which flavour cake do you want'' said Maya's mother She was thinking about which cake to choose. After thinking for a while she suddenly said excitedly ''I want a chocolate cake.'' Her mother agreed to Maya. And said OK Maya I will prepare a chocolate cake for you tomorrow. She said ''Thank You Mom'' to her mother. And her mother hugged her. And finally it was saturday the day of Maya's birthday. She woke up early in the morning and ready quickly. And quickly ran to kitchen, where her mother kept her favourite breakfast on the dining table. Her mother invited Maya's friends to come to their house in the evening. All of her friends arrived her home. And her mother bought the cake which she had prepared. Like this they enjoyed a lot. It was the time to give the gifts. No one gave a doll. Then it was the time of mother to giv the gift. She gave a beatiful doll. Maya was very happy. It was the Maya's best birthday gift.
author: Rutu Rutvika

title: The Forbidden Forest
text: Our school was just like any other school, except for one thing. Behind our school, stood a thick and mysterious forest. We were told never to go near it, and no one ever asked why. We always stood staring at the enchanted forest and wondered what was going on inside. Once, there was a kid who tried to go in but when he reached near the forest he heard loud screaming from the forest. He was terrified and ran away In school, I had a lot of friends. I had a big friend group and we all loved to explore. One day we were all hanging out at a park near the school. We were bored and decided to play "Truth or Dare", which never ended well. My friend Jack loved giving people crazy dares such as prank calls and embarrassing dances. Once, he dared my timid friend Lucas something that made him cry.:"I choose dare!!" said Lucas. Jack immediately stood up and said "Alright! I have the perfect one for you!". He continued, "I dare you to run across the playground and scream at the top of your lungs.” Lucas froze and shook his head. The laughter around us slowly faded. That was the moment I realized Jack’s dares were no longer funny. But today felt different. Everyone was bored of the old and repeated dares, it wasn't fun anymore. It was Jacks turn to choose truth or dare, and as always he chose dare as he was the bravest of all of us. Suddenly, Lucas got up with a mischievous smile. He said "Jack, I dare you to go into the forest behind our school." Everyone froze and looked at each other, they could not believe that Lucas would dare him something so extreme. However, I knew this was payback for when Jack dared him. Jack seemed shocked at first, but he laughed and said "You know we aren't allowed to go in there right?". Lucas replied "Hah, just admit it that you are afraid and can't do it." Jack replied "Fine, I will do it!." All our friends left as they did not want to accompany us. So, it was only Jack, Lucas and me. As soon as we reached, Jack decided to run in. I tried to call him but he didn't turn back. Thirty minutes later, we could hear weird noises and screeches. I was worried and Lucas was feeling guilty. "I shouldn't have dared him something like that, now if he doesn't come back, it will all be my fault.", said Lucas. I tried to cheer him up by saying "Don't worry, he is going to come back! Its Jack, he is the bravest person we know!". Lucas still looked worried and said "Maybe, we should call our parents and tell them what we did?" I replied, "I don't think that will help, maybe we should go in and look for him?". Lucas stared at me and said "That's insane! I am not going in!!" After a lot of convincing, I finally got him to say yes. We both entered the gloomy forest and started calling for him. "Jack! Jack! can you hear us?" The moment we stepped into the forest, everything felt different. The noise from outside disappeared, and the air felt still and cold. It was dark and we couldn't see anything. I walked in first, and Lucas stayed close behind me. We kept looking around as it felt like someone was watching us. We walked deeper into the forest and still caught no sight of him. Suddenly, I saw a small figure move. I stopped walking and said "Somethings there!". Lucas shivered and said "Umm, why don't you go check it out, I will stay here and keep watch." I agreed and slowly walked towards the black figure. As i got closer, the figure felt familiar and that's when I called out, "Jack?" Jack turned around and looked surprised and relieved to see me. He ran towards me and started crying. "I don't know what this scary place is! I keep hearing noises! I don't like this." I consoled him and brought him to Lucas. Lucas was so relieved to see Jack and gave him a hug. The three of us followed the footprints left by Lucas's shoe and got to the entrance of the forest. All three of us let out a relieved sigh and started laughing. We promised each other to never give scary dares and to always look out for each other.
author: Nehaan M
illustrator: Alyssa Pachuau; Barkha Lohia; Godwin  Chipenya; Jacob Kono; Shadrach Munene; Vinayak Varma; Vusi  Malindi

title: Tales from an Abandoned Dog
text: I was not always a stray. Once, I had a name. I had a bowl with my name on it which always used to be full, not with food, but with belonging. Back then, love was everywhere. Sometimes the humans would sit on the floor and press their forehead against mine, as if we were sharing secrets. I was not just a dog, I was family. I thought that feeling would last forever. I didn't know even love could forget. I will never forget the time that new scent filled the rooms, the new little human that would replace me. The hands that once reached for my head, now push me away. I watched from the corners of the room as love shifted its shape. I didn't know what I did wrong. I was only a small chapter of their life, but to me, they were my whole life. One morning, they called my name again. My tail wagged so hard it hurt. The leash came off the hook, and for a moment, I thought the old days had returned. I jumped into the car with a heart full of hope, not knowing that hope was the last thing they were taking from me. As we drove, roads thinned, and the world stopped feeling like home. When the car finally stopped, they opened the door and told me to get out. I did, because I always listened. I always trusted. Then the door closed. The engine started. I ran after the car, my paws slipping on the road, my chest burning as I called for them in the only way I knew how. But the car became smaller and smaller, until even my love could no longer reach it. My paws followed the road until the road forgot me, and I found myself on streets that smelled of strangers and sadness. So I curled up beneath a broken bench, tucking my nose under my tail to keep the cold away. S omething inside me quietly broke, and it never fully healed. As the wind whispered through the streets, I understood what it meant to be alone. Days passed, though they no longer felt like days. Hunger blurred time into one long ache. I searched through trash, sniffed at empty wrappers, and licked puddles that tasted of dust and oil. Nothing filled the hollow inside me. My legs grew weak. My thoughts grew slow. I slept not because I was tired, but because being awake hurt too much. Maybe if I slept, the hunger in me would disappear, but t he hunger never left. I slept longer and longer, because being awake meant remembering that I had nothing. When the hunger grew too loud to ignore, I tried to ask for help. I followed people with tired eyes, hoping someone would understand what I was begging for. But the world had no patience for a dog like me. Some turned their faces away. Some shouted. Some lifted their feet and pushed me aside as if I were nothing more than dirt on the road. I wasn’t dangerous. I wasn’t angry. I was just hungry… and afraid. I stopped waiting for kindness, because waiting had begun to hurt more than being alone. I once heard humans talk about getting rid of dogs like me, because a few had grown angry and wild. They put us all into the same small, careless box: dangerous, unwanted, disposable. I wished they could see what I was instead, not a threat, not a problem, just a tired heart that had been left behind. We were not all the same, even if the streets had made us look that way. One day, when I had almost forgotten what it felt like to expect anything, the world softened. I heard small, hurried footsteps and a voice that did not sound afraid. A child came running toward me, not to chase me away, but to kneel beside me. Their hands were warm. Their eyes were kind. For the first time in a long while, someone saw me. Just like that, the long, dark story of my loneliness began to change. I was lifted into gentle arms, and for the first time since I was left behind, I felt safe. Now I sleep on a real bed again. I have a bowl with food. I have a name. But sometimes, when the house is quiet, I still remember the dog I used to be. T he one who waited on the street, believing that love would return, and somehow… it did.
