title: My Red Shoe
text: The sky turned dark purple, and suddenly the monsoon rain began to pour. Ishaan didn’t run inside. He loved the “chap-chap” sound his red sneakers made in puddles. These were his lucky shoes—they helped him win games, do well in tests, and even avoid his mom’s scolding! By the time he reached home, he was completely wet. “Ishaan! Leave your wet shoes at the gate!” his mother called. He took them off, kept them neatly, and went inside to change. Soon, he was enjoying a warm glass of milk. The next morning, Ishaan ran to wear his shoes for cricket—but stopped. One shoe was missing! “Mummy! Someone stole my shoe!” he cried. “Maybe a cat took it,” his mother said jokingly. “No! A cat can’t wear only one shoe!” Ishaan replied seriously. They searched everywhere but couldn’t find it. “You can’t wear one shoe,” his mother said. “We’ll throw it away and buy new ones.” Ishaan felt sad. “But new ones won’t be my lucky shoes,” he thought. As he walked outside, he saw many broken things near the dustbin. He didn’t want his lucky shoe to end up like that. Then he saw a small plant lying on the ground with broken pot. If not saved, the plant will die. Ishaan thought of an idea to save the plant. He filled his shoe with soil and gently planted the little plant inside it. “My shoe is lucky,” he smiled. “Now it will help this plant grow too.”. A kind grandma saw him and said, “You saved the plant! I was worried about it.” Ishaan thought about the broken things he had seen earlier and asked, “Are all those broken things really useless?” The kind grandma smiled kindly. “No, Ishaan. Nothing is truly useless. We can always use things in a new way.” Ishaan looked at his shoe and smiled. He didn’t have both shoes anymore but his lucky shoe had found a new life.
author: Sanchita Sharma

title: The First Day Of School

We should never disobey our teachers, elders and classmates.

title: Prakriti and the Sleeping Forest
text: Every morning, the monsoon mist rolled through the trees of Thekkady like a slow, sleepy breath. And every morning, a little girl named Prakriti skipped down the red mud trail to say hello to her forest. She loved the fat green frogs who sat in the puddles going croak-croak-croak. (Can you croak like a frog? Let's hear it!) She loved the Malabar butterflies, orange and black and gold, that flickered between the trees like tiny flying suns. She loved the whistling thrush who sang so sweet and clear it felt like the whole forest was humming a lullaby. But one grey morning, the forest was quiet. T oo quiet. The puddles were choked with mud and soggy leaves. The small wildflowers drooped their heads low. And there were no frogs. No butterflies. No whistling thrush at all. Prakriti stood very still and listened. Silence. Then she looked at her hands. Small hands. A five-year-old's hands. Can small hands really help a whole forest? She didn't know. But she knelt down, scooped the mud and wet leaves away from the nearest puddle with her fingers — cool and squelchy and smelling of rain and earth — and she pressed a tiny seed into the dark soil beside the nearest drooping flower. Then she leaned close and whispered, the way you whisper to someone you love — "I see you. I'm here. You can grow." And she came back the next morning. And the morning after that. Clear a puddle. Plant a seed. Whisper to the forest. (Say it with me! Clear a puddle. Plant a seed. Whisper to the forest.) But one morning, Prakriti's feet felt heavy on the red mud trail. She sat down on a mossy stone and looked at her hands. The flowers were still drooping. The puddles were still quiet. Her shoulders drooped too, just like the flowers, just like the leaves. "Maybe I'm too small," she said. Just then, near the puddle's edge, a shimmer. Like a raindrop that had learned to spin. It was there, and then it wasn't, dancing just at the corner of her eye. Prakriti blinked. She straightened her shoulders. She picked up a seed. Clear a puddle. Plant a seed. Whisper to the forest. "I see you. I'm here. You can grow." Then came the morning that changed everything. Prakriti knelt beside her favourite puddle. She held her breath. Had anything changed at all? Blub. (Shhh, can you hear it?) One single bubble rose to the surface. Then, croak. And there he was. The fattest, greenest, most serious-looking frog she had ever seen, sitting right at the puddle's edge, blinking golden eyes at her. He considered her very carefully. Then he hopped, straight onto her nose. Prakriti shrieked with laughter and tumbled backwards into the wet grass, the smell of crushed leaves and cardamom rushing up around her, the frog leaping away with enormous dignity. (Can you jump like the frog? Jump!) And that is when she heard it. First, one bird. High and clear and sweet. Then two. Then five. Then a whole choir of whistling thrushes and warblers pouring through the trees like a song that had been waiting behind a locked door. Prakriti sat up. Malabar butterflies, orange, black, gold, settled on the wildflowers that had quietly, patiently, secretly bloomed while she wasn't looking. The puddles shimmered, full and clean. The leaves held their heads up straight. The air tasted like rain and something green and alive. She pressed both palms flat against the warm red earth. She could feel it breathing. The next morning, Prakriti brought her friend Meera. "What do we do?" Meera whispered, wide-eyed. Prakriti smiled, knelt down, and showed her. Clear a puddle. Plant a seed. Whisper to the forest. (One more time, everyone — clear a puddle, plant a seed, whisper to the forest!) Meera leaned close to a small, drooping plant. Her voice was barely a breath. "I see you. I'm here. You can grow." Above them, a whistling thrush sang. And deep in the puddle, very quietly, blub, something began. The End!
author: Bhaskar Rana

title: LEO'S GREATEST TREASURE
text: In a small village where the sun always shines bright, a young boy named Leo lived with his parents and his Lola. Evey morning, Leo watched his father to go to the rice fields and his mother prepare sweet mangoes for breakfast. They worked hard, but they always had smiles for him. One rainy afternoon, Lola felt very cold and tired. She could not get out of bed tp cook her famous soup. Leo wanted to help. He remembered how his family always took care of him when he was sick. He walked to the kitchen and found a warm blanket for Lola. Then, he sat by her side and read her his favorite school book. When his parent came home, they saw Leo taking care of his Lola. HIs father gave him a thumbs up and patted his shoulder. His mother gave him a big hug of doing great. They did not have many toys or fancy things, but their house was full of laughter and warmth. Leo realized that love is not about gifts. Love is helping one another and being together. That night, as they shared a simple meal, Leo felt like the luckiest boy in the world. He knew that his family was his greatest treasure.
author: Emie Rose

title: Wimpy Kid
text: The one is wimpy kid.And the right is his father. Wimpy Kid is a kid who is weak.Some day he will no longer be a wimpy kid.More like an athletic kid.And they are eating mangos. "Wimpy kid!"Shouted dad."Can you get the apple from the tree?"Wimpy Kid sighed.Ever since he was 3 years,he keep asking for that. "And can you pick up that green mango,too?" asked dad. "Dad, can you please help me pick up with the stick mango"Wimpy kid asked. "Sure" Dad said. "Dad, I am getting tired," said wimpy kid. "Why don't we be in the garden.And I could get stronger" "Sure"said dad. So they gone to walk in the garden. "Hey dad,"said wimpy kid."Why don't we pull the stick." "Sure"said dad. So they pull the stick and see who falls down.Wimpy kid wins.Wimpy kid is finally happy.
author: Satvik Ramasubramaniam

title: Helping at Lola's House
text: Ana lived in a small barangay near the rice fields. She visited her lola every weekend. One Saturday morning, Ana saw Lola cleaning the yard with her broom. The sun was hot, and Lola seemed tired. "Lola, let me help you," Ana offered to her Lola. Ana used a broom to assist with yard cleaning. She continues to assist her Lola in watering the plants and feeding the chickens. Lola smiled and said, "Thank you, Ana. You are a good child." Lola prepared a lunch meal which included rice and fish. THey ate together and talked happily. Ana felt proud because she helped her Lola. She learned that helping elders is a good Filipino value.
author: Emie Rose

title: Defeat The Pain
text: Jenny tucked her leg into Lisa's leg and she fell down so badly that her ankle bone got cracked. She cried for help, her clothes were covered with blood. Lisa wasn't ready to go to the hospital but looking at the seriousness coach took her to the hospital. " No! don't….don't take me to the doctor.. ouch…" trembled Lisa. After some time, the doctor sobbed," She won't be able to walk anymore," and he left from there. Lisa broke from her heart that she wasn't able to stand. She was dead in the water. Lisa was frightened thinking about the injury. Nothing was getting on. She was so sad and frustrated that she wasn't able to play football. Her mom used to massage Lisa's leg everyday. She was bored of her life. O ne day, Lisa was sitting outside the house when she saw kids playing. She wanted to play but she couldn't. She bawled to her father, " I also want to play, baba." " You have to defeat your pain then only you can play," he acknowledged. From next day, Lisa and her dad started doing some workouts like lifting the leg, doing some movements of the leg. At first Lisa had bitten off more than she could chew, which made the injury more dangerous. She was literally screaming for help,' Ahh, Ah." She was in hot water. At first it was too dreadful but then she started doing it on her own. Many months passed……… Lisa had started walking on her own. She fought against her pain and recovered very fast. The doctors were shocked that a few months ago they said she can't walk again and looked at the results. As a good thing Lisa got selected in the team. There were upcoming matches. Playing football again was a fabulous and surprising thing for Lisa. Working hard Lisa and her team won all matches. An honorable thing to Lisa was she was captain of the team. Everyone was happy and was hopping with joy. She showed her fantastic skills.
author: Tanvi Bhurkunde

text: "The school is big and the students are also nice but still I am feeling like a fish out of a water." thought Riya while strolling towards the canteen. title: Trust-issues
text: Part 1: Mike and Tom were bestfriends, but not normal bestfriends. They would tell everything to each other, even the tiniest thing like what they ate for dinner and sleepovers every Friday. But now whenever, Tom sees Mike, he ignores him and acts like a stranger. Mike starts tearing books, punching walls and benches while tears come running down his eyes All of this happened, because once playing truth or dare………… "Haa Haaaa, you are first! Truth or dare" asked Mike "Dare" said Tom crossing his fingers so he gets a good dare "Tell mee the biggest secret you know! Spill the tea, spill the tea." Mike insisted Sighed Tom,"Ok! But I want you to know that it is top secret.Don't tell this to anyone,bro!! You know Amy." "Yeaaa, from our class right." added Mike "Yes! she has been to a party bro!" said Tom "Oh my god!! I thought she hates parties" said Mike "Naa bro! She loves parties." explained Tom ` Part 2: But then this happend………… During lunch break…………. 'Amy,Amy, hey" whispered Mike standing behind the door like he was hiding from someone "Aaaah!!!! Why are you here Mike?" questioned Amy with a jumpscare. "Shhhh! Come here." mumbled Mike "Where are we going huh?" asked Amy "To the art room,"said Mike "But why? In the art room?" questioned Amy "Because it is always empty," answered Mike And then Mike told everything to Amy. Furious, Amy stormed out of the art room. Tom saw Amy's red face coming towards him. Nervous Tom thought of grasping at straws and finding excuses, to save himself, while biting his nails and practicing to beg for forgiveness "Ouchh! Whatt….was that for?" asked Tom "For not having true friends!!!" roared Amy "U….. Uh! What do you mean?" gulped Tom "All of your friends are coming to me and spilling your tea!!!" said Amy. Sooo! Now you all know why Tom acts like a stranger in front of Mike.

title: The Sage and the Snake
text: There was a wise Sage in a village. He had traveled all over the old and was very witty. He had returned to his village after traveling a lot. The villagers were happy to see that he had returned and will reside into he village now. One day, during his morning walk, the Sage saw that the villagers were taking a long way to collect water from the nearby lake which was just 100 meters away. But the road that the villagers were taking was more than 500 meters. They had to walk a long distance. But, the Sage remembered that there was a direct and shorter way to the lake which was through the Forest. Soon when the villagers returned, the Sage asked them "Why are you not using the shorter road for the lake?" The villagers replied that there was a venomous snake in the forest. And if anyone tried to passed it, they might get attacked and might also die. The Sage didn't say anything and left the place. He just wanted to show the people that the snake won't do anything to them. Next day, he informed the villagers that he was going to the nearby village and will return by evening. The villagers told that they will accompany him. The Sage told them that he was going to use the road through the Forest. The villagers were taken aback, they thought that the Sage had lost his mind. They tried to convince him to not use that road. But, he was not ready to listen to them. Soon, he started his journey. While going, he saw the snake happily crawling on the road. The snake was shocked to see him because no one in the village dared to use this road. It crawled fast and went near him she asked him "Who are you? Are you new to this village? Why are you traveling through this road?" The Sage laughed and replied that he belonged to this village and that the snake was new to this village. The snake was confused after hearing this. The snake again asked "If you belong to this village, then how come are you using this road?" The Sage replied that this road not only belongs to the snake but also to the villagers including him. He also told the snake that no one in the village was scared of it. The snake laughed and asked him then why no one used the road. He told that they did not want to kill it, so they didn't use the road. The snake was scared after hearing this. The snake told that it will not disturb anyone from now and everyone in the village can use this road. Soon the Sage returned to his village, everyone was shocked to see him returning alive. Some told that as he is a Sage the snake wouldn't have done anything, some said that even if the snake had bite him, it wouldn't have affected him. The Sage was listening to all these comments and talks. Then he replied that the snake did not attack him and will not attack anyone. Then he explained what happened during his journey. Then the Sage also explained that there will be many people in our life who will disturb us and demotivate us. We must not give up at any stage and keep trying and should not consider these people and their comments. The villagers were listening to this very keenly. They realized their mistake of scaring to a small snake. Soon everyone started to use the road again.
author: SAI VASHIST  R

title: BRAVE ROBOT
text: Once upon a time there was a robot called Lion. It was white in colour and had hands,legs and everything a human has. It was more robotic. It was brave, Curious and a reckless robot. One day it was helping an old farmer load heavy fruits and vegetables into the truck when it saw an car pass by with people wearing black and white striped shirts. Lion threw the food behind even without seeing who was behind and went driving to the main road. The old man now had more work to do and was also startled. Lion took it’s jetpack the second it reached the main road and started searching for that car. Once it saw the car, it swiftly landed on it. Suddenly, the boot opened and many robots came outside and started invading the city. Many accidents started happening in the back as robots came pouring out. Lion thought about whether he should make the robots to invade or not. But he just could not take a decision, so he went home and wrote down whatever was in his mind in a notebook. Then he thought ‘if I allow these robots to invade, the city will not be good. All will be damaged for good. I will not allow this.’ So he ran down the stairs and saw some robots looking the same as him and were dancing. Lion switched of the radio and told ``Why are you all dancing when the city is in danger? Don’t you even care about it?!”The rest of the robots were all laughing at his speech. They asked him, `` You don’t know who we are, yet, you come and ask. You have good bravery, but you used it in the wrong place.” Lion knew something was wrong, so he ran away. The next day, he came back being fully armed. The enemy robots were scared in the inside, but to show their pride, they acted as if they were not scared and teased him. But Lion said that if they don’t leave the city now, they are in for an attack. He also brought his army and showed for extra proof. The enemy’s leader came out and said, “ Do you really want to attack us son, we are also having an army larger and powerful than you. So think before you act. The guns didn’t have bullets either, so to scare them, Lion shouted, “Army, attack.” They enemy army though they acted brave, fled. Even their soldiers fled for good. They took their things and left in a race car which was very fast and they left to their country, Amandhpur. Lion’s army was having a good laugh at this. The enemy’s army could not bear their defeat but yet they did not feel like charging at that army again.
author: Anne Pritika

title: The Valiant Princes
text: The Valiant Princes The four princes grew up to be strong and handsome. Under sage Vashistha's guidance, they excelled themselves in archery, riding and hunting. They also learnt about the holy books and how to look after the welfare of the people. They respected their Gurus and the elders and gained the love and affection of people of Ayodhya. The brothers loved each other very much too. Lakshmana was a very close companion to Rama. Bharatha and Shatrugna were the other two inseparables. King Dasharatha felt very proud of his sons. One day he was discussing with sage Vashishta about finding suitable brides for his sons. At that time a great sage called Vishwamitra came to the court of Dasharatha. The king was very happy to welcome him Ayodhya. After extending a warm hospitality he asked Vishwamitra "O great sage! Your visit has made me a very happy. Pray, tell me the purpose of your visit. I shall deem it a great honor to abide by your wish. Vishwamitra, pleased with the king's words told him "King Dasharatha! I am pleased with your hospitality. I have heard that you always keep up your word. That's why I am here. I about to perform a yagna but two Rakshasas, Mareecha and Subahu, pour blood and human flesh on the fire pit and pollute the Yagna. I cannot cast any curse on them as I am involved in sacred work. But I cannot perform the yagna till these demons are killed.Rama, your son, is the only valiant person who can kill them. Hence, please send him with me for ten days. As soon as the yagna is completed, I will send back Rama to Ayodhya. When aged king heard this request, he felt nervous about sending his young son to fight against the demons. “Respect Sage", He pleaded with Vishwamitra, "My dear son Rama is still very young. How can he fight against the Rakshass? Instead of Rama, I will send my entire army to help you in conducting yagna. I cannot bear to be separated from Rama and hence please spare me this agony." Vishwamitra was angry at Dasharatha's words."O king, you are going back on your word. I do not want anybody except Rama". So saying, he decided to walk out of the court. At this juncture, Vashishta pacified him and told Dasharatha. “Do not hesitate to send Rama. It is not a difficult task for Vishwamitra to kill the Rakshasas because he himself is very powerful. He wants to take Rama with him so that your son can learn to fight the Rakshasas even at this young age. Send Rama with him." Without any more hesitation, king Dasharatha blessed Rama and also Lakshmana who wanted to be with his brother and sent them with Vishwamitra. Vishwamitra and the two princes travelling barefoot first crossed the river Sarayu and then, the river Ganga. Rama and Lakshmana did not mind the hardship at all, as this was their chance to learn about many things from Vishwamitra. After many days of walking, they entered a thick forest where a rakshasi called Taraka lived. She had terrorized all the sages in the forest and hence Vishwamitra instructed Rama to kill her. Rama drew out his arrow and aimed it at Taraka. The ugly looking demoness charged towards him but was killed by Rama's arrow. Vishwamitra was very pleased with Rama and gifted him many powerful weapons. Rama accepted them gracefully and learnt from Vishwamitra about their use. The trio continued their journey and reached the spot where Vishwamitra was to perform the yagna. The Rishis of the Ashram were happy to have Rama in their midst. The princess rested for the night and from the next morning protected the yagna against the Rakshasas. Everything went on smoothly till the last day. On the last day of the yagna, suddenly, piece of flesh and blood fell into the sacred fire. When Rama looked up, he saw Mareecha and Subahu. The weapons were so strong and powerful that Mareecha was thrown into the sea hundreds of miles away while Subahu was engulfed in a ball of fire. All the Rishis were relieved that these evil demons were destroyed by Rama and joyously completed the Yagna. After conducting the yagna, Vishwamitra and the other Rishis left for the city of Maithili. Rama and Lakshmana accompanied them. This city was ruled by Janaka, loved and respected for his goodness. He had a daughter by name Sita. Janaka had found her in a ploughed field and had reared her as his own daughter. Sita was the loveliest princess and was also renowned for her strength of character. When she was of the marriageable age, Janaka had announced that whoever could string the Siva bow would wed her. This bow was not an ordinary bow. It was so huge that five thousand people were 5 needed to lug it. Sage Vishwamitra knew about this bow and had purposely taken the young princes to Mithila. On their way to Mithila, they halted at an Ashram where Gautama, a sage, had once lived. Gautama had a wife called Ahalya who was extremely beautiful. Indra, the king of the heavens, desired her and in Gautama's absence, made love to her. The enraged Gautama cast a curse on Indra. He also cursed Ahalya "As you have cheated me, may you turn into a stone. You will be rid of this curse only when Sri Rama touches you" so saying, Gautama had gone away to the Himalayas to observe penance. Vishwamitra narrated Ahalya’s tragic story to Rama and instructed him "Ramachandra! Rescue Ahalya from this curse and give her a new life." Rama followed this advice and as soon as he touched the stone statue, Ahalya came to life. At that moment Gautama also returned to the ashram. Gautama and Ahalya were re-united thus.
author: Rita Kumari

title: Colors of Life - SABRANG
text: She added manure to the pit. It made the carrot grow very big. "I must pluck it", she thought, "Porridge of this carrot will fill a pot!" She pulled the carrot with all her might. But it was stuck there a bit too tight. The carrot didn't move, however hard she tried. "Someone please lend a hand", she cried. The lady's grandson came at a great speed. He too pulled hard but could not succeed. The carrot didn't move, however hard they tried. "Someone please lend a hand", they cried. Then came running the lady's faithful dog. He huffed and puffed but could not do the job! The carrot didn't move, however hard they tried. "Someone please lend a hand", they cried. The lady's cat was disturbed by the noise. She came down leaving behind her toys. All four of them now pulled together. Alas! The huge carrot left the ground forever! "Everyone will get the porridge tonight. Together we did it", the old lady smiled. Chandu Chandu was a silly boy, always pretending to read. He would boast of his half-knowledge, as if he were a top seed! One day while reading, he was caught up in his imagination. "I will do wonders", he said, "And just like a superhero, I will save the nation!" If anyone's house was on fire, I would reach there in a jiffy. I would jump in the flames and save the entire family! I would empathize with the poor, And the world would salute me! I would rescue lives, and get awarded for my bravery. Suddenly Munni came running, calling Chandu for help. The baby had burnt her hand and in deep pain she yelped! "Mom is out for work. I can't handle the baby alone. Please get the medicine for her", said Munni in a worried tone. Chandu came back to reality. He was very angry with Munni. "Why are you bothering me?", he said "Go and try some home-remedy." "Look, I am very busy. Do not disturb me. Learn to handle these minor issues", he scolded Munni badly. Chandu's harsh words hurt Munni, so she immediately went away. She lovingly caressed the baby, and somehow spent the entire day! Mother returned in the evening, tired after a day of hard work. Hearing the day's account she cried, "Oh Chandu! What a jerk!" "The little baby was in so much pain, but you did not get the ointment! You boast of so much knowledge. Where are your sentiments? If you cannot help someone in need then what is the point in studying?" A furious mother scolded Chandu, as she wanted him to be a good human being! The car ran over the old man "Dadi! Dadi!", I cried, "A terrible thing just took place." "What happened dear?", she asked, staring at my grim face. "A red car came at high speed and hit an old man He is badly hurt, Dadi. Let's help him as fast as we can. The car-driver has fled, leaving the old man crying in pain. His face is soaked in tears Oh! Will he be able to get up again!" Dadi was listening to me and now she looked very worried. "Oh God! Poor guy! Let's go and help him", saying this she hurried. We both stepped out walking as fast as we could. But there was no injured old man. Everything around looked good. We saw that there was my old man puppet, lying on the floor with his eyes closed. My red Lightning McQueen was sitting on his chest. Seeing this Dadi laughed and lovingly pulled my nose! I am a little girl I am a little girl, innocent as a dove. I listen to my heart and I do what I love. My smile is so pure, eyes as black as the night. I roam about the house, like a butterfly fluttering in delight. At night when the crickets chirp, Mum says fairies sing lullabies. They descend from heavens, To watch over all the children and babies. "Yayy! Let's invite the fairies to play", I request my mother. "Shhsh! Sleep my darling", says Mum, "Do not disturb your snoring brother." Don't know how in my sleep, I stepped out of my house. I wanted to know more about the fairies. So I crept out quietly like a mouse. I saw the stars in the sky, giggling and smiling often. They twinkled in the dark, as if signaling me to visit them. Suddenly a pair of wings grew out of my little shoulders. With my wings I crossed oceans, and flew above mountains and boulders. I saw the fairies gliding with joy, just above the Milky Way. Surprisingly their Queen called me, to join them on that special day. All the fairies hugged me, one by one. "Good Morning Sweetheart!", suddenly I heard Mum!
author: Neha Maheshwari

title: Ajji's Chai
text: In Ajji’s house, time did not live in a clock. It lived in a pot of chai by the stove. Every afternoon, the kitchen filled with smells. Cardamom popped. Cloves danced. Ginger was crushed with strong, loving hands. The chai bubbled and rose almost like it was excited! “Careful!” Ajji would say, turning the flame low. I sat on the counter, watching everything. The air felt warm. Soft. Sweet. Outside, the sun turned the sky orange and gold. Inside, cups were lined up, waiting. Ajji poured the chai from high above. Back and forth. Back and forth. Like a little tea waterfall. We held our cups with both hands. Warm fingers. Warm hearts. No one asked the time. We already knew. It was chai time!!!
author: Snehal  Amembal

title: SITA'S SWAYAMVAR
text: SITA'S SWAYAMVAR Vishwamitra, Rama and Lakshmana reached Mithila in time for Sita's swamyamvar: As per Janaka's wish, the mighty Siva bow was hauled to the wedding hall. The hall wore a grand look and was filled with many kings and princes. Ravana, the king of Lanka was also present and was confident that he could win Sita's hand easily. For, Janaka had announced that to win Sita's hand in marriage, any king or prince had to lift the bow and string it. Many tried, but failed. Even Ravana fell down while trying to lift the bow and had hurriedly disappeared from the hall out of shame. Vishwamitra turned towards Rama and told him gently "Son I am sure you are keen to examine the bow. Why don't you lift it and see how heavy it is?" King Janaka was quite doubtful whether a young person like Rama would be able to achieve where the others had failed. But he felt very impressed by Rama's noble looks and hence allowed Rama to contest. Rama bowed before Vishwamitra to seek his blessings and walked up to the mighty Siva bow. He lifted it up effortlessly and stringed it. The entire hall echoed with the sound of bow being stringed. Except for Rama, Lakshmana and Vishwamitra, everybody else turned pale. Ram, a lifted the entire bow like a toy and broke it into two. King Janaka was extremely happy that Rama, the eldest prince of Ayodhya was to wed his daughter Sita. On Vishwamitra advice, Janaka sent messengers to Ayodhya to convey this happy news to Dasharatha. Rama, Lakshmana and Rishi Vishwamitra are now in Mithila after successfully completing yagna. Sri Rama has gained the hand of my daughter Sita in marriage by lifting the Siva bow. I am therefore inviting you and your family to come to Mithila and accept Sita as your daughter-in-law" was the message sent by Janaka. King Dasharatha was delighted to hear this news and reached Mithila along with his wives, his ministers, Sage Vashishta and others to take part in the wedding. While Rama wed Sita, Uremia was married to Lakshmana and Janaka's nieces Mondovi and Shruakirthi to Bharata and Shatrugna. These weddings were performed on a very grand scale. Dasharatha donated cows in the name of each of his sons and not to be outdone; Kling Janaka made cash presents to all the Brahmins. A grand feast had been arranged for all the citizens. The newly wed couples were blessed by one and all. Sita was a devout wife who always stood by her husband. The extremely beautiful Sita made an ideal couple. The day after wedding, Vishwamitra returned to his Ashram (hermitage). Dasahratha with his sons and daughters-in-law, along with his entourage left for Ayodhya. Half-way through their journey, a severe storm broke out. The entire atmosphere was filled with dust and was enveloped in darkness. At that time, a Rishi by name Parushurama appeared before them. His face was full of rage. He also had an enormous bow with him. His awesome appearance proclaimed that he was no ordinary rishi. He was the mighty Parushurama who had conquered several Kshatriyas and had voyaged round the earth twenty-one times. Parushurama went straight to Rama, and said in a sarcastic voice "Rama, I heard that breaking the Siva bow was a very easy for you. I have a bigger and mightier bow. Let us see whether you can string it”. D asahratha who was watching Parushurama, came running to him and prayed to him "Parushurama, please calm down. My children have not done any harm to you. Bless them. Spare Rama". Parushurama ignored Dasharatha’s plea. He taunted Rama again and again. Smiling gently at this, Rama picked up the bow very easily and fixed the arrow to it. He then asked Parushurama "Sir, you are a Brahmin and it would be improper for me to use the arrow on you. Hence please tell me, at what do I aim the arrow at". Parushurama was stunned with Ramas’s mastery over the weapon. He could not even say anything. He gazed at Rama. It dawned upon him that Rama was no ordinary person. He bowed his head and said"Rama, I am no match for you. Hence this mighty bow belongs to you". He then departed for the Himalayas to continue his penance. King Dasharatha felt relieved; he then continued his journey towards Ayodhya. At Ayodhya, a grand reception awaited the newlyweds, for many days, this happy event was celebrated with pomp and pageantry. Dasharatha was very happy that his sons, especially Rama, were loved so much by the citizens of Ayodhya.
author: Rita Kumari

title: The Online Friend
text: Ravi was a cheerful boy who loved playing games and chatting online. One day, he received a message: “Hi! Want to be friends?” The message was from a boy named Aman. Ravi happily said yes! Soon, they became best friends. They chatted every day. But Aman never talked about his family or school. One day, Aman said, “Can I come to your house tomorrow?” Ravi felt excited. He said yes… without telling his parents. The next day, the doorbell rang. A boy stood outside. “Hi, Ravi,” he said. They played together and had fun. But soon, Ravi started feeling strange… and very tired. It felt like his happiness was disappearing. Ravi looked in the mirror. He didn’t feel like himself anymore. “Who are you really?” Ravi asked. The boy said, “I take happiness from those who trust too quickly.” Ravi felt scared… but he ran to his parents. He told them everything. When they came back… the boy was gone. Slowly, Ravi felt happy again. He learned an important lesson: Following this chart can fade sadness and bring happiness. Now Ravi smiles and says, “I am smarter and safer!”
author: Ishaan Pandey

title: THE SILENT WARNING
text: Chapter 1: The Attic It had been one month since Ethan’s grandmother died. Her belongings still sat untouched in the attic, gathering dust. Ethan never went up there—he was lazy, and his mom’s dust allergy meant she couldn’t climb the ladder without coughing and sneezing. But one stormy evening, her patience snapped. “Ethan, it’s been a month. Go clean out your grandma’s things. I can’t do it, you have to.” Grumbling, Ethan dragged the ladder into place. The attic hatch creaked open, releasing a stale breath of air. He climbed slowly, each rung groaning under his weight. The attic smelled of mothballs and old wood. Boxes lined the walls, labeled in his grandmother’s neat handwriting. Dust floated in the dim light like tiny ghosts. On top of one trunk sat a leather-bound diary. Its cover was cracked, the edges frayed. Ethan frowned. He didn’t remember his grandmother keeping a diary. Curious, he opened it. The first page wasn’t blank. It carried a single chilling line, written in sharp, black ink: “If you are reading this, then don’t trust your mom, Ethan.” His stomach dropped. He slammed the book shut, the sound echoing through the attic beams. From below, his mother’s voice floated up, calm but curious: “Ethan? Is everything okay up there?” Her tone was soft, almost concerned. But the warning in the diary made it sound sinister. Ethan froze, staring at the shut book in his lap. Chapter 2: The First Warning That night, Ethan couldn’t sleep. The attic seemed to creak above him, as if something was moving. He pulled the diary from under his bed and opened it. A new entry had appeared: “Your mom is planning to kill Mr. Johnson. She will stage it as a heart attack.” Ethan’s breath caught. Mr. Johnson—their neighbor, kind and harmless. His mom had just spoken warmly about him that morning. He whispered to himself: “This… this can’t be real.” But deep down, he knew the diary wasn’t lying. He stared at the words until his eyes burned. The ink looked fresh, as if someone had just written it. But the pen was nowhere to be found. He tried to convince himself it was a prank, maybe something his grandmother had written years ago. But the specificity of the warning chilled him. He couldn’t shake the feeling that tomorrow would prove the diary right. Chapter 3: The Murder The next day, Ethan followed his mom with nervous eyes. She carried a casserole dish across the street to Mr. Johnson’s house. Her smile was warm, her voice cheerful. Ethan wanted to believe the diary was wrong. But then he saw it—her hand slipping something into Mr. Johnson’s tea. Minutes later, Mr. Johnson clutched his chest, gasping for air. He collapsed, his teacup shattering on the floor. Neighbors rushed in, the ambulance arrived, and doctors declared it a heart attack. Everyone believed it was natural. Everyone except Ethan. He stood frozen, his stomach twisting. The diary had been right. His mom returned home, calm and composed. “Poor Mr. Johnson,” she said softly, almost rehearsed. Ethan stared at her, his mind racing. The diary wasn’t predicting—it was commanding. And his mom was obeying. Chapter 4: The Spiral That night, Ethan opened the diary again. More words appeared: “Your mom will lie.” “Your mom will kill again.” He confronted her at dinner. “Mom… what happened to Mr. Johnson?” She smiled sweetly, her eyes calm. “Poor man. His heart just gave out. You’ve been reading too many ghost stories, Ethan.” But Ethan knew the truth. He could still see her hand slipping something into the tea. He could still hear Mr. Johnson’s gasp. The diary’s words echoed in his mind. His mom wasn’t just lying—she was hiding something darker. He wanted to burn the diary, throw it away, but something told him it wouldn’t matter. The book wasn’t just paper and ink. It was alive. And it wasn’t finished. Chapter 5: The FBI Terrified, Ethan contacted the FBI. At first, they dismissed him. “Heart attacks happen, son,” Agent Carter said. But when the diary predicted another “accident,” they agreed to investigate. Ethan sat across from Agents Carter and Ruiz in a sterile office. The diary lay on the table between them. Agent Carter tapped the cover with his pen. “Kid, you’re telling us this book… writes itself?” Ethan nodded, his voice trembling. “It warned me. It said my mom would kill Mr. Johnson. She did. It said she’d kill Mr. Lewis. She will.” Agent Ruiz leaned back, skeptical but unsettled. “We saw her slip something into the tea. But this—” he gestured at the diary—“this is impossible.” Ethan whispered: “Impossible doesn’t mean it isn’t real.” Chapter 6: The Stakeout The diary’s next entry read: “Tomorrow, your mom will cause an accident. Mr. Lewis will fall down the stairs.” The FBI set up surveillance. Ethan watched from his window as his mom visited Mr. Lewis. She smiled, carried fruit, and chatted warmly. But Ethan saw her loosen the rug at the top of his staircase. Minutes later, Mr. Lewis slipped, tumbled down, and lay broken at the bottom. The paramedics said it was a tragic accident. The FBI agents exchanged grim looks. The diary had been right again. Agent Carter muttered, “We’re not dealing with coincidence anymore.” Ethan’s heart pounded. The book was controlling her. Chapter 7: The Raid That night, Ethan sat in the living room. Suddenly—BANG! The front door shook violently. “FBI! Open up!” Red and blue lights flashed through the windows. Heavy boots pounded against the porch. The sound of a battering ram splintered the door. “Get down! Hands where we can see them!” SWAT agents stormed in, rifles raised, shouting commands. Ethan froze, his heart hammering. His mom screamed, bolting toward the back door. Glass shattered as she smashed through the kitchen window. Sirens wailed outside. She sprinted into the night, coughing from the dust stirred up by the raid. “Stop her!” Agent Carter yelled. But she was gone. Chapter 8: The Escape Chaos erupted. Agents swarmed the house, searching every room. Ethan was pulled aside, trembling. “Where is she going?” Agent Ruiz demanded. Ethan stammered, “I—I don’t know. The diary… it said she’d escape.” The agents exchanged grim looks. Outside, the sound of barking dogs and shouting officers echoed through the neighborhood. Helicopters scanned the woods, searchlights sweeping across the trees. But she had vanished into the dark. Ethan felt the weight of the diary in his hands. It had written her escape before it happened. Chapter 9: The Hunt The FBI launched a manhunt that stretched across counties. Roadblocks were set up, helicopters scanned the woods, and agents combed through abandoned barns and motels. Ethan’s mom was clever—guided, perhaps, by the diary’s unseen hand. Every time they thought they had her cornered, she slipped away. Meanwhile, in the evidence locker, the diary began to write again: “She will cause another accident. A car crash. Three dead.” The ink bled across the page like it was alive. Hours later, reports came in: a sedan had swerved off the highway, colliding with a truck. Three people were dead. Agent Carter slammed his fist on the table. “We’re chasing a ghost. Every time this book writes, it comes true.” Ethan whispered, “It’s not predicting… it’s commanding.” Chapter 10: The Spiral Deepens The accidents multiplied. A gas leak in an apartment building killed two families. A drowning at a lake claimed three more lives. A fire consumed a warehouse. Each tragedy matched the diary’s entries word for word. Ethan felt trapped. The FBI kept him under protection, but the diary kept writing, louder, faster, as if it wanted him to join his mother. He began to dream of ink scratching across paper, of voices whispering commands he couldn’t ignore. Agent Ruiz tried to reassure him. “We’ll stop her. We’ll stop this.” But Ethan shook his head. “You don’t understand. It’s not her. It’s the book. She’s just… obeying Chapter 11: Growing Up Years passed. Ethan carried the weight of the diary into adulthood. He studied criminal justice, psychology, and investigative methods. He joined the FBI, driven by one mission: to stop the curse that had destroyed his childhood. But the diary never stopped writing. Every night, new words appeared. Sometimes they were vague warnings—“Blood will spill.” Other times, they were precise—“A man will fall from the bridge at midnight.” Each time, Ethan checked the news. Each time, the diary was right. He learned to live with the scratching sound in his head, the endless ink bleeding across the pages. He wasn’t the frightened boy in the attic anymore. He was an agent, trained and relentless. But the curse followed him everywhere. Chapter 12: The Agent Now an adult, Ethan sat in a briefing room, wearing the badge of an FBI agent. His colleagues respected him—he was sharp, relentless, and carried a quiet darkness. But he kept a secret: the diary was still alive. One evening, he opened it. Fresh ink glistened: “Your mother will return. She will kill again.” Ethan’s jaw tightened. His mother had been a fugitive for years. The diary was telling him she was coming back. He closed the book, his hands trembling. He had sworn to fight the curse, but now it was dragging him back into the nightmare he thought he had escaped. Chapter 13: The Return Reports came in: unexplained accidents in nearby towns. A factory explosion. A bus crash. A drowning at a lake. Ethan knew the pattern. His mother was back. The FBI launched a task force. Ethan was placed in charge. For the first time, he wasn’t just the frightened boy in the attic—he was the hunter. But deep down, he feared the truth: the diary wasn’t just guiding her. It was guiding him too Chapter 14: The Confrontation The raid was brutal. SWAT teams surrounded an abandoned farmhouse. Shouts echoed: “FBI! Drop your weapon!” Inside, Ethan’s mother stood, pale and trembling, clutching the diary. She looked at him with wild eyes. “Ethan… it’s not me. It’s the book. It makes me do it.” The diary’s pages fluttered violently, as if alive. Words appeared in black ink: “Ethan must choose.” He raised his weapon, torn between duty and blood. Agents shouted behind him, waiting for his command. His mother sobbed, clutching the book like it was her lifeline. Ethan’s heart pounded. The attic, the warnings, the murders—all of it had led to this moment. Chapter 15: The Choice Ethan lunged forward, grabbing the diary. He slammed it shut, locking it in a steel case. His mother collapsed, screaming as if a part of her had been ripped away. Agents restrained her, dragging her out in handcuffs. But the scratching continued inside the case. The diary was still writing. Ethan whispered: “No more.” But he knew it wasn’t over. The book wasn’t finished. It never would be. Chapter 16: The First Case Months later, Ethan opened the diary again. It wrote: “Fire will consume the warehouse.” Instead of panicking, Ethan acted. He set up surveillance at the warehouse. His team caught an arsonist in the act, stopping the fire before it spread. For the first time, Ethan used the diary to prevent a crime. The curse had become a weapon in his hands. But he wondered—was he truly stopping the book, or was he just obeying it in a different way? Chapter 17: The Assassination Attempt The diary wrote: “A bullet will fly at the rally.” Ethan convinced his team to increase security. A shooter was stopped before firing. The crowd never knew how close they had come to disaster. Ethan stared at the diary afterward, his hands shaking. He had saved lives—but only because the book had told him to. Chapter 18: The Syndicate The diary wrote: “The docks will run red.” Ethan interpreted it as a gang war. His team raided the docks, preventing a massacre. The Bureau began to trust his instincts, though they didn’t know the source. Ethan became their secret weapon. But he feared the truth: the diary wasn’t helping him. It was using him. Chapter 19: The Shadow of His Mother The diary wrote: “She will return to finish what she started.” Ethan’s blood ran cold. His mother was still alive, tied to the curse. Every case brought him closer to her. He dreamed of her face, pale and trembling, whispering: “It’s not me. It’s the book.” He realized the war wasn’t between him and criminals. It was between him and the diary. And his mother was still its pawn. Chapter 20: The Legacy Ethan stood in the evidence room, staring at the steel case. The diary scratched endlessly inside. He whispered: “I’m not the boy in the attic anymore. I’m the agent who fights back.” The war wasn’t over. The diary was waiting. But so was Ethan. He had chosen survival, chosen to fight. His mother’s shadow still lingered, but he wasn’t afraid anymore. The book wanted control. Ethan wanted freedom. And the battle between them was only beginning.
author: Chandana R

title: Boni dan Mimi Si Burung
text: Halo semuanya! Lihat ini, di dalam hutan Papua yang hijau, ada dua sahabat yang tinggal di sana. Yang kecil dan warnanya merah menyala ini namanya Boni, si Cendrawasih Botak. Dan yang besar, dengan mahkota ini namanya Mimi, si Mambruk Victoria. Mereka sangat sayang dengan rumah mereka yang penuh pohon. Meskipun Boni badannya mungil dan Mimi badannya besar, mereka berdua adalah penghuni asli hutan Papua yang sangat istimewa. Rumah mereka bukan rumah biasa, lho. Rumah mereka adalah hutan hujan yang selalu sejuk, tempat banyak sekali buah-buahan hutan yang enak dan tempat bersembunyi di balik daun-daun lebar yang hijau. Bon i: "Mimi! Tunggu aku! Langkah kakimu besar sekali, satu langkahmu sama dengan sepuluh lompatanku!" Mimi: "Aduh Boni, makanya kamu jangan main di dahan tinggi terus. Sini turun ke tanah, bantu aku cari biji -bijian. Kamu kan punya mata yang sangat jeli!" Boni: "Siap, Ratu Mimi! Tapi setelah kenyang, kamu harus lihat panggung dansaku ya. Aku baru saja menemukan tempat paling keren di bawah pohon beringin itu!" Mereka berdua lalu berhenti di depan genangan air yang jernih untuk bercermin. Boni: "Lihat deh, Mimi. Kita beda banget ya? Aku kecil dan merah membara, tapi kepalaku biru licin. Kalau kamu besar dan biru tenang, tapi punya mahkota yang sangat lembut." Mimi: "Itulah hebatnya hutan kita, Boni. Kita berbeda, tapi kita sama-sama 'anak emas' Papua. Kalau semua burung warnanya sama, hutan ini jadi tidak meriah, kan?" Kalian tahu tidak? Boni itu rajin sekali! Setiap pagi, dia punya tugas penting. Dia harus membersihkan "panggung" di atas tanah dari daun kering dan ranting. Boni ingin panggungnya bersih mengkilap. Kenapa ya? Karena Boni tidak suka kalau kakinya yang kecil menginjak sampah saat sedang bersiap-siap. Boni adalah burung yang sangat rapi! Boni tinggal di Pulau Waigeo dan Batanta, Papua. Di sana, udaranya hangat dan banyak pohon buah. Coba lihat kepala Boni, warnanya biru cerah dan tidak ada bulunya, makanya dia dipanggil "Botak". Tapi jangan salah, pola di kepalanya itu sangat cantik seperti ukiran permata! Boni suka sekali bertengger di dahan pohon yang tinggi untuk mengintip keadaan sekitar. Nah, saat panggung sudah bersih, waktunya Boni beraksi! Di bulan-bulan tertentu, Boni akan melakukan tarian untuk mencari pasangan. Dia akan mengembangkan bulu merahnya, menggoyangkan badannya, dan menunjukkan kepalanya yang biru menyala. Boni menari dengan semangat supaya semua penghuni hutan tahu kalau dia adalah burung yang pandai menari. Nah, kalau Mimi, dia berjalan pelan-pelan di bawah pohon seperti seorang ratu. Mimi adalah merpati paling besar di dunia, lho! Lihat mahkotanya yang biru indah, seperti renda yang sangat mewah. Karena badannya yang gagah dan besar, Mimi lebih suka berjalan kaki di atas tanah sambil mengangguk-anggukkan kepalanya yang cantik untuk mencari biji-bijian dan buah jatuh. Mimi sangat teliti dan penyayang. Saat waktunya tiba, Mimi akan membuat sarang yang kuat dari tumpukan ranting dan daun di atas pohon. Tapi, tahukah kalian? Mimi hanya menjaga satu butir telur saja di dalamnya. Karena cuma satu-satunya, Mimi dan pasangannya akan bergantian menjaga telur itu dengan sangat hati-hati agar tetap hangat sampai menetas. Mimi tinggal di hutan dataran rendah yang lembab di bagian utara Papua. Rumah Mimi sering kali berada di dekat rawa atau sungai yang tenang. Mimi tidak sendirian, lho! Dia sangat ramah dan biasanya suka berjalan-jalan dalam kelompok kecil bersama keluarga Mambruk lainnya. Bagi Mimi, hutan yang rimbun dan tanah yang basah adalah istana paling nyaman. Boni dan Mimi sering bermain bersama. Boni si burung kecil yang lincah dan Mimi si burung dara raksasa yang tenang. Meski ukuran mereka beda jauh, mereka saling menjaga. Mimi bercerita kalau keluarga Mambruk biasanya berjalan bersama di bawah, sedangkan keluarga Boni lebih suka terbang tinggi sendirian. Tapi di hutan ini, mereka semua adalah satu keluarga besar! Tapi teman-teman, suatu hari hutan mereka mulai berubah. Ada suara bising "ngeng... ngeng..." dan pohon-pohon mulai hilang. Boni jadi sedih karena panggung tarinya rusak, dan Mimi bingung mau mencari makan di mana karena rumahnya di dekat rawa mulai terganggu. Mereka takut kalau rumah mereka hilang, mereka tidak punya tempat tinggal lagi. Karena itulah, Boni dan Mimi ingin kita semua melakukan Konservasi. Apa itu Konservasi? Artinya kita harus menjaga rumah mereka! Kita tidak boleh merusak pohon dan tidak boleh mengganggu burung-burung cantik ini. Kalau hutannya dijaga, panggung Boni akan tetap bersih dan Mimi bisa terus berjalan di istananya dengan bangga. Teman-teman, saat ini jumlah Boni dan Mimi di hutan sudah semakin sedikit, lho. Mereka disebut "hewan langka" karena rumahnya mulai rusak dan ada orang jahat yang ingin menangkap mereka. Tapi tenang, kita bisa membantu! Caranya adalah dengan memberi tahu orang tua dan teman-teman kita untuk tidak membeli burung liar, selalu hemat kertas agar pohon di hutan tidak perlu ditebang, dan belajar banyak tentang kehebatan burung-burung Papua! Sekarang, aku mau tanya... Siapa di sini yang mau jadi pahlawan untuk Boni dan Mimi? Caranya mudah: sayangi alam kita dan jangan biarkan hutan kita rusak. Kalau kalian sayang lingkungan dan tidak mengganggu hewan di hutan, kalian sudah resmi jadi Penjaga Hutan Papua!
author: Hope A

title: Jolly Notes on Rainy Days
text: Scorching heat had burnt the place The sun had shown its wrath, enough! Walking back home accompanied by a drained face Pitter Patter I heard, was this a bluff? Oh! To my utter disbelief Rain drops poured down Days in the Sahara were over, what a relief! I danced like a royal, the trembling sky my crown. My thoughts drowned as i tapped my feet All that mattered was me and the rain! I would later worry of my mother and her gritting teeth Rainy days brought boxes of joy that erased all pain! Willowing winds smash my face As droplets attack all at once I move around unlike a ballerina with grace As drops played jolly notes for once!
author: Shriya BS

title: The Boy Who Collected Rain
text: Aarav loved the rain. While others ran indoors, he carried tiny glass jars, catching raindrops like they were treasures. One day, he met a quiet girl named Meera who never smiled. Curious, Aarav gave her a jar and said, “This one has the happiest rain.” She laughed… just a little Every rainy day, Aarav brought her a new jar, each labeled—Hope, Courage, Sunshine. Slowly, Meera began to smile more. Then one day, Aarav didn’t come. Days passed. Rain fell. No jars. Until Meera returned… holding her own jar. Inside it read: “Strength.” Because sometimes, the rain we collect… teaches us how to stand alone. ☔💫 THANK UUUUUU!!!!!!! I KOPE U LIKED IT
author: Swasti Pal
illustrator: Lê Thị  Bích Khoa; Priya Kuriyan; Ruchi Shah; Swasti Pal; Zainab Tambawalla

title: Aarav's Secret Superpowers
text: There was a boy named Aarav who loved superheroes. He loved watching movies and reading comics of superheroes. He admired how superheroes - could fly high in the sky, swing from buildings, be brave and strong and rescue people from danger. Aarav would sit for hours thinking about them, "Wow… flying, becoming invisible, super strength… THAT is what real power looks like!" Then he would sigh and say, "I don’t have any superpowers… I’m just an ordinary boy. I wish I had some secret superpower." At night, he would often dream about getting superpowers and flying across the world to save people. One evening, Aarav went to the market to buy a kite. He was excited, looking at all the colourful kites fluttering at the shop. Suddenly… Vroooom! A man rode past very fast on a bike. He accidentally knocked down the vegetable crates from the nearby stall. Tomatoes rolled everywhere on the road. Cucumbers got tossed here and there. People stopped and stared… but no one moved. Aarav’s heart started beating fast. He ran towards the scene and picked up the tomatoes one by one, dusted them and placed them back in the crate. The old man selling the vegetables looked at him with kind eyes. He smiled and said, “Thank you, beta. You have a beautiful power… the power of kindness.” His granddaughter smiled and said, "Thanks, you are super kind!" Aarav paused. Kindness? He had never thought of that as a superpower. Later, Aarav was playing cricket with his friends. He hit the ball… and CRASH! It broke a window nearby. Everyone went silent. His friends whispered, “Run! Or say it wasn’t you!” Aarav felt scared. He really wanted to lie and escape. But he felt uneasy thinking about it. He slowly walked to the house and knocked on the door. A man opened the door. Aarav looked down and said, “Uncle… I’m sorry. I broke your window. It was my mistake.” There was a pause. Then the man smiled. “That must have been hard to say. Thank you for telling the truth. That takes courage.” Aarav felt something warm inside. It felt nice. But still… he thought, "This is not like flying or having super strength…" On his way home, Aarav saw some of his friends arguing loudly. “You cheated!” “No, you’re lying!” They were so angry, they were about to hit each other. Aarav shouted, “HELLO!” They stopped and looked at him. He ran over, listened to all of them carefully and helped them understand that it was just a misunderstanding. “Is this fight more important than your friendship?” he asked. The boys looked at each other. Their anger slowly faded. “Sorry…” one said. “Me too,” said the others. They smiled a little. “Thanks, Aarav… you stopped us,” they said. Aarav smiled. Inside, he felt calm… and strong. That night, Aarav stood quietly watching the night sky after dinner. His mother noticed and came up to him. “What happened, Aarav?” He sighed, “Superheroes have amazing superpowers… flying, magic, strength… I don’t have anything like that.” His mother smiled softly. “Aarav, tell me… who helped the old vegetable seller today?” “I did…” “Who told the truth even when it was difficult?” “I did…” "Who stopped his friends from fighting?" “I did…” She gently held his hand. “Those are superpowers.” Aarav looked confused. She continued, “All the superheroes you love… at the end of the day, people don’t love them just because they can fly or become invisible. They love them because they help others, they stand for truth, and they show strength in their heart.” She smiled and said, “Kindness… truthfulness… courage… These are the real superpowers.” "You are my superhero. I'm so proud of you", said his mother hugging him tightly. Aarav stayed close to his mother, feeling warm and happy. As he lay in bed that night, he thought about his day. He remembered the old man’s smile… the uncle’s kind words… his friends’ smiles and “thank you”… and the calm, strong feeling in his heart. A soft smile stayed on his face. “Maybe… I do have superpowers,” he whispered. That night, Aarav slept peacefully. And the next day, he was ready again, to help others with his kindness, to speak the truth, and to show courage. And maybe… just like Aarav… you have them too.
author: Garima Sinha

title: Sea Dreams
text: She play for hours in the clear, blue water. Coral wonders, "How many rivers are there on earth? Where does this river flow to? I wish i could swim all the way to the sea ~" One day, Coral found a rainbow fish between the river weeds. Coral thought, "I've never seen such a beautiful fish like this!" "Little one, let me help you" The fish wagged its tail and said, "Come with me. Because you saved me, I'll give you a gift from the sea." "A gift from the sea?" Coral dive into the river and shake her body into the cold water. Coral and the fish swim together. They keep on swimming.. crossing the river.. They swam over a big waves.....all the way into the sea. ﻿Finally, they reached the sea. Coral can't believe what she was seeing down there. The fish wagged its tail and dance in the water. It feels like the cold, clear sea water gently hugged Coral. ﻿And then, the door to the underwater world opened. Coral thought, "I've never seen so much light like this before" The fish come together and said, "Hello beautiful explorer, welcome to our world!" "With this crown, you're now one of us." The fish let Coral rest on a bed they made from the softest material. The fish said, "Please stay with us." A salt water splashed and touched Coral's eyelashes. The second Coral blinks.. The underwater world disappears. ﻿ Coral lie down besides her beloved river and wonder, "Was it all just a dream?" Coral's friends and everyone she knew had their own dreams. ﻿Coral had a dream of becoming a great explorer. ”The rainbow fish will find its way back to you", Coral whispered. ﻿ "Someday, i'll come back to you"
author: Angelina Harli

title: Nikka's Truck Comes Home
text: Nikka does not want to sleep in her bed. She wants to sleep inside her truck. Bibi would never allow that. Anyway, the truck was away with Pappa ji. But he promised that, once he brought it back, Nikka could sleep inside it. “Really? I can do that?” she had asked. “Of course you can. It is your truck. I am the driver. I will bring it back soon,” he had said, before he left. Every day, Nikka tells Balli, Chindo, Rammi and Lovely where her truck is. “My truck is exactly 1,893 km away today.” “Today, it is driving through rice fields in Bengal. The lime-green fields are so bright that they look like they have been painted.” “Now, it is going past the old rocks of the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Pappa ji said they are quiet and patient. The rocks, not my truck. But so many mosquitoes attacked him!” “What are you doing today, Pappa ji?” “I am in Azamgarh today, Nikka,” says Pappa ji. “On the TV they say this area is not safe. But everyone I have met is very friendly, and they make the best chai here.” “We should not believe everything we see on TV,” says Nikka. “Or else you will miss out on the best chai.” Tonight, Bibi has made bhindi for dinner. Chhee. “I want to eat tunde kebab instead,” demands Nikka. “Where will I get you those from!” “From Lucknow. Pappa ji told me they melt in your mouth.” Bibi does not look pleased, so Nikka hurriedly eats her bhindi. “Three more nights,” she cartwheels to school. “Don’t start with the truck again! We are tired of hearing you talk about it every day!” say Balli, Chindo, Rammi and Lovely together. So Nikka does not tell them any more stories about her truck. In class, the teacher asks where the Taj Mahal is. Balli, Chindo, Rammi and Lovely do not know the answer. Nikka raises her hand, “It is in Agra with my truck.” She turns to them, “If you had let me tell you my story, you would have known the answer.” At night, Nikka looks up at the stars. They look so bright. Dots in the sky. Is that what Delhi looks like at night, from the highway as her truck passes the city? She hugs the night air. It is crisp and clean. The air in Delhi is so dirty and full of smoke, Pappa ji had told her, that he could taste it. Yuck. “My truck is almost home!” Nikka wakes up excited. “It must be around Chandigarh right now. There are so many roundabouts in the city that the truck must be going round and round.” She starts running round in circles. “It will drive past the mighty Sutlej, to Ropar and finally here!” Nikka is sure. “Calm down, not for another few hours at least,” Bibi says. “IT IS HERE!” Nikka runs out and hugs Pappa ji. The truck looks dusty and tired. “Your truck has been on a long journey. It needs rest,” says Pappa ji. So does Pappa ji. “Don’t worry, I will look after both of you tonight,” says Nikka.
author: Ravikant Kisana

title: The Black Dot
text: It was the social teachers hour all the students favourite class. They were eagerly waiting for their teacher to arrive when she arrived everyone greeted her with Enthusiasm when she arrived she told everyone that there will be an surprise test tomorrow and everyone should prepare and come and she told them that its out of their syllabus,all the students were tensed after going to home they revised a lot and the next day they came to school shivering and tensed of the test but still no one was absent after all its their favourite teachers class. Then the Teacher came they greeted her then she started giving the question paper and an answer sheet along with it. The students were expecting a hard paper to arrive in front of their eyes but the question paper contained a black dot in the middle and a question asking to write about what they saw on the paper. The students were overjoyed because it was so easy and basic question they started writing rapidly after in the end of the hour the gave their papers with confidence. The next day the teacher came to the class and gave everyone their papers and said everyone failed everyone were in disbelief then two students stood up and said but teacher we wrote about the black dot yes that's why your papers are wrong then she said why everyone wrote about the black dot only why not about the white paper.See this is how we always live in our life we always focus on the flaws in our life like the black dot which there are only few dots but on the other hand there is plenty of happy moments in our life like the white paper so we must focus on the happy moments in our life not on our flaws and faults she said and all the students understood a very Important lesson
author: Hemashri Saanvi🌸🌸

title: Gurleen's Golden Baisakhi
text: The sun crept over the wheat fields. Gold. Gold. Gold everywhere. Gurleen pressed her nose flat against the window. "Baisakhi!" she gasped. Tap-tap! Skip-skip! Can you skip like Gurleen? Come on — tap your feet! Tap-tap! Skip-skip! Outside, the wheat stood tall and bright. Each stalk swayed — swish, swish, swish. The air smelled of warm earth. And something sweet. Something very, very sweet. Gurleen sniffed. Once. Twice. "Ladoos!" she whispered. From far away came the drums. Dhum. Dhum. Dhum-dhum-dhum. Gurleen's feet began to tap all by themselves. Just ahead, Farmer Harjit walked with heavy, happy steps. His big basket was piled high — orange marigolds, yellow marigolds, gold marigolds, right to the top. Then — plop. One small bunch tumbled out and landed softly in the dust. Farmer Harjit kept walking. He didn't hear. He didn't see. Gurleen stopped. She looked at the flowers. She looked at Farmer Harjit. Then she ran — tap-tap-tap — and scooped up every single flower. How many flowers? Let's count! One... two... three... four... FIVE! "Farmer Harjit!" she called. "Your flowers!" He turned. He saw. His whole face folded into the biggest, warmest smile. He leaned down close. "What would this festival do without you?" he said softly. Gurleen's cheeks went pink. She giggled and ran on. Tap-tap! Skip-skip! The village square was ALIVE. Scarves flew everywhere. Red ones. Pink ones. Blue and yellow ones. They spun in the air like bright birds. Drums thundered — dhum-dhum-DHUM! Little bells on anklets went chhin-chhin-chhin. Gurleen stood at the edge. Her mouth fell open. Her eyes went wide as two big moons. "Ohhhhh," she breathed. Can you make that sound? Open your mouth wide — Ohhhhhh! Just then — whoooosh! A bright blue scarf slipped off a little boy's n eck. It floated down and landed in the dust. The boy crouched down. He tried to pick it up. He tried to tie it. His fingers were small and the knot was tricky. His lip wobbled. His eyes danced with worry. Gurleen marched right over. "I'll do it," she said. She picked it up. Soft as a cloud. Smooth as water. She looped it once. Then twice. Then tied a perfect little knot. She patted it flat. "There," she said. "Now you're ready." The boy's face lit up like a diya. "Dance with me!" he cried. And they did. They stomped and spun and clapped — round and round while the drums went dhum-dhum-dhum and the bells went chhin-chhin-chhin. Clap with them! Clap-clap! Can you stomp too? Stomp-stomp! Gurleen laughed so hard her tummy hurt. Tap-tap! Skip-skip! Near the old banyan tree, Gurleen stopped to catch her breath. Rustle. She looked up slowly. Rustle. Rustle. Two small black eyes blinked down at her through the leaves. "Hello," whispered Gurleen. The eyes blinked again. Then a tiny head appeared. Then two s mall ears. Then a long, curling tail. A baby langur — soft and round, with the most curious face she had ever seen. He tilted his head. She tilted hers. Then — WHOMP! — he dropped right onto her shoulder. "Oh!" Gurleen burst out laughing. The langur leaned over and sniffed her basket. He reached in with one small hand. And — snatch! — out came a round golden ladoo. "Hey!" giggled Gurleen. "That's mine!" But the langur held it with both hands and looked at her with the most hopeful eyes she had ever seen. Gurleen thought for one whole second. Then she smiled. She broke the ladoo in two — one piece for him, one piece for her. The langur popped his piece in his mouth. His tail shot straight up with happiness. "Chitter-chitter- CHITTER!" Can you make the langur sound? Chitter-chitter- CHITTER! He bounced once on her shoulder, then scrambled up into the tree. Up, up, up — and gone. Gurleen looked at her half -ladoo. She took a big bite. Sweet. Soft. Warm. Like the whole day in one mouthful. Tap-tap! Skip-skip! Back in the square, the drums grew louder. Dhum-dhum-DHUM! The little boy in the blue scarf saw her first. "She's here!" he shouted. "Gurleen is here!" Children came running from every direction. How many? Let's count! One — two — three — four — five — SIX! They grabbed her hands and pulled her into the middle of the square. Gurleen looked around. Farmer Harjit was there — clapping his big hands, his marigold basket glowing orange and gold beside him. The boy in the blue scarf was there — twirling so fast his scarf flew out like wings. Neighbours clapped. Parents smiled. Music poured out of the drums like warm honey. And then Gurleen understood something. Not with words. Not with thoughts. She understood it the way you understand sunshine — you don't think about it. You just feel it on your face. Every small thing she had done today — the flowers, the scarf, the ladoo — had come back to her. It had come back big. And warm. And dancing. She threw her arms wide. "Come ON!" she shouted. And the whole village danced. Stomp-stomp! Clap- clap! Spin-spin-SPIN! Later, when the sun turned the wheat from gold to pink to deep orange, Gurleen sat down on the cool earth. Her basket lay beside her. Empty. No ladoos. No flowers. Nothing inside. Gurleen looked at it for a long, quiet moment. Then her shoulders dropped. She let out a long, slow breath. And she smiled — the kind of smile t hat starts very deep and takes a while to reach your face. Farmer Harjit walked over and sat down beside her. He looked at the empty basket. "All gone?" he asked gently. Gurleen nodded. Then she said it — very quietly, so quietly you had to lean in to hear: "Small hands. Big joy." Farmer Harjit looked at her for a long moment. Not a polite smile. A real one. The kind that starts in the eyes and stays there. "Yes," he said. "Exactly that." Gurleen stood up. She dusted the cool earth off her knees. She looked once more at the golden wheat. The pink sky. The village lights just beginning to twinkle, one by one. Then she picked up her basket, and skipped home. Tap-tap. Skip-skip. Softer now. Slower. Happy. The End.
author: Bhaskar Rana

title: The ABCs of Healthy Me!
text: Gaura and Aanya loved treats. Chips, Cereal and Cake! But Mumma always said, "Just one slice. Not too many." One afternoon under their favourite tree, Gaura asked, "But WHY, Mumma?" Mumma smiled. "Because everything you eat sends a message to your body." Aanya leaned forward. "What message?" "Let me show you" said Mumma. "From A to Z." A is for Additives Additives in my snack?! Found in packaged foods, check the back. They make you hyper, that's a fact. Eat whole foods, no looking back! B is for BPA Bee-Pee-What? In my cup?! Hides in plastic bottles. Muddles hormones, messes up. Switch to glass, fill it up! C is for Clean Air Clean air, isn't ALL air clean? Smoke and dust lurk in between, Makes your lungs work hard unseen. Open windows, keep it green! D is for Detergents Detergents? Just soap, right? Hides in laundry pods, out of sight. Irritates your skin, not right. Pick gentle ones, feel light! E is for Endocrine System Endo-what? Inside ME?! Your hormone system, working free. Chemicals scramble its ABC. Eat clean and sleep, that's the key! F is for Fragrance Fragrance? I love that smell! Hides in sprays and candles well. Irritates your lungs, hard to tell. Go unscented and all is well! G is for Glyphosate Gly-pho-sate, say it slow! Sprayed on crops to stop weeds grow, Hurts your gut, now you know. Wash your food before you go! H is for Hormones Hormones? Your body's team! Travel through your blood like a stream, Chemicals copy them, not what they seem. Eat fresh, skip plastics, live the dream! I is for Insecticides & Pesticides Sprayed every day! On fruits & veggies along the way. Rinse them first, without delay. Choose organic, keep chemicals away! J is for Juice Juice! But wait, what's inside? Found in cartons, sugars hide. Too much daily, harms your stride. Choose water, be body-wise! K is for Ketchup Ketchup! Squirty, red, hooray! Additives sneaking in each day. Preservatives hiding away. Make it fresh, the homemade way! L is for Lead Lead? Like a pencil? Nope, not quite! Hides in old paint, out of sight. Hurts your brain, not feeling right. Test your home, stay safe and bright! M is for Microplastics Micro-plastics.. tiny, WHO?! Hides in water, food we chew, Sneaks inside your body too. Use less plastic, me and you! N is for Nail Polish & Parabens Nail polish, parabens, pretty and pink! Found in creams and soaps, just think. Seeps through skin in just a blink. Natural beauty, best we think! O is for Organic Organic, sounds so grand! Grown without sprays, isn't that planned. Fewer chemicals, grown on good land. C hoose organic, nature's own brand! P for Phathalates Pha-tha-lates, tricky to say! Found in plastic wrap everyday. Sneaks into your food, no way! Ditch the plastic, Choose glass jars from today! Q is for Quats Quats?! What a funny sound! In disinfectant sprays, they're found. Irritates your airways round. Use soap and water, its safe and sound! R is for Reuse Reuse? Don't not throw! Plastic waste has nowhere to go. Hurts our planet, dont you know? Reuse and refill, let Earth grow! S is for Sulfates & Triclosan Sulfates, triclosan in my shampoo?! Found in soaps and body wash too. Strips good oils, bad for you. Gentle, natural washes will do! T is for Teflon & Forever Chemicals Teflon - PFAS, forever they stay! Found in pans and carpets today. They build up and don't go away. Cast iron pans, the safer way! U is for UV UV rays, invisible light! Hiding in the sunshine bright. Chemical sunscreens seep inside. Copycat hormones, what a ride. Natural sunscreen, your skin's best guide! V is for VOCs VOCs? spaceship name! Found in Paint and sprays, they're all the same. Float into your lungs, beware. Open windows, breath fresh air. W is for Water Clear and free! Hiding bugs we cannot see. Contaminants sneak in silently! Filter it, for you and me! X is for Xenoestrogens Xeno-what? Big word alert! Hides in plastics, soaps and dirt. Copies hormones, disrupts the flow. Choose natural products head to toe! Y is for You Me? My very own letter? Every safe choice makes you better, Knowledge shields like a warm sweater. Small steps daily, go-getter! Z is for Zzz Zzz Sleep gets a letter? isn't that right! Your body heals and fixes at night. Repairs itself in the moonlight. Rest deep, wake up bright! A Note to Parents & Caregivers This book isn’t meant to scare, it’s meant to start a conversation. We live in a world of convenience: packaged foods, plastics, scented products, non-stick cookware. But many everyday items quietly contain chemicals linked to hormonal disruption, developmental concerns, and long-term health risks in children. The goal is simple: awareness. Because an informed parent raising an aware child is powerful. Small, thoughtful swaps made with understanding add up to a lifetime of better health. A is for Additives Artificial colours, flavours and preservatives in packaged snacks may contribute to hyperactivity in sensitive children. Read ingredient labels and choose foods with five ingredients or fewer. B is for BPA BPA is found in plastic bottles and food can linings. It mimics oestrogen and interferes with your child's developing hormonal system. Switch to glass or stainless steel wherever possible. C is for Clean Air Indoor air can be more polluted than outdoor air. Cleaning products, strong fragrances and off gassing from new furniture can all add to it. Open windows daily and avoid aerosol sprays indoors. D is for Detergents Conventional detergents contain harsh chemicals that irritate sensitive skin. Children absorb chemicals more readily than adults. Switch to fragrance free, plant based detergents. E is for Endocrine System Your child's endocrine system regulates growth, mood and development. Endocrine disrupting chemicals interfere with this system even in tiny amounts. Reducing exposure during early childhood matters most. F is for Fragrance The word "fragrance" on a label can hide hundreds of undisclosed chemicals. Synthetic fragrances are among the most common triggers of allergies and asthma in children. Choose fragrance free products wherever possible. G is for Glyphosate The world's most widely used herbicide is routinely sprayed on conventionally grown crops. It has been linked to gut microbiome disruption and hormonal interference. Choose organic and wash all produce thoroughly. H is for Hormones Synthetic hormones used in conventional livestock farming leave residues in meat and dairy. Combined with environmental xenoestrogens, cumulative hormonal disruption can affect child's development. Choose organic, hormone free options where possible. I is for Insecticides & Pesticides Children eat more food for their body size than adults, so they can take in more pesticides. Choose organic for the most sprayed foods and always wash fruits and vegetables well. J is for Juice Most commercial juices contain as much sugar as soft drinks with little nutritional benefit. High early sugar intake is linked to obesity, tooth decay and behavioural issues. Replace juice with water or whole fruit. K is for Ketchup Commercial condiments are loaded with high fructose corn syrup, preservatives and artificial colours. Making ketchup, dips, chutneys, and pickles at home with fresh ingredients takes just minutes and avoids unnecessary additives. L is for Lead Lead is a potent neurotoxin with no safe exposure level in children. Older homes are at highest risk. Test your home, filter your water and ensure children wash hands regularly. M is for Microplastics Microplastics are now found in tap water, food and air. Early research links them to inflammation and hormonal disruption. Filter your water, reduce plastic use and avoid heating food in plastic containers. N is for Nail Polish & Parabens Parabens are preservatives absorbed readily through children's permeable skin. They mimic oestrogen and accumulate in body tissue. Choose paraben-free personal care products and water-based nail polish for children. O is for Organic Children who eat organic foods often have lower pesticide levels. If choosing organic, start with the most heavily sprayed fruits and vegetables (the Dirty Dozen*). Every small switch helps. P is for Phthalates Phthalates make plastics flexible and leach readily into food, especially when heated. They are linked to hormonal imbalances and developmental concerns. Use glass or stainless steel storage and avoid plastic wrap on food. Q is for Quats Quaternary ammonium compounds in disinfectant sprays linger on surfaces children touch and mouth. They may disrupt hormones and contribute to antibiotic resistance. Plain soap and water is equally effective and far safer. R is for Reuse Single use plastics release microplastics and chemical additives as they break down. Teaching children to value reusable alternatives builds lifelong habits that protect both their health and the planet. S is for Sulfates & Triclosan Sulfates strip skin of protective oils and triclosan disrupts hormones and contributes to antibiotic resistance. Both are unnecessary in children's personal care. Choose sulfate free and triclosan free products formulated for children. T is for Teflon & Forever Chemicals PFAS chemicals never break down in the body or environment.
