title: Ami and the Rainbow Ribbons
text: The whole village smelled of sweet rice cakes and marigolds. Drums were beating. Thump-thump-thump! Can you beat your knees like a drum? Thump-thump-thump! Bamboo flutes were singing. Lanterns swayed overhead like little glowing moons. And right in the middle of it all stood Ami, five years old, her eyes wide as festival plates. Today, the children would make the rainbow ribbons for the Hornbill dance. Grandmother Suno carried over a big bamboo basket — full to the brim with ribbons in red, blue, green, pink, orange, and purple. "One colour each," she said with a wink. "And I hear a visitor is coming from the village over the hills. She may bring something new." Ami grabbed the red ribbon. It slipped right out of her hands. She grabbed it again. It slipped again. "Hmph." Her friend Rin came bouncing over, arms overflowing with ribbons. "I have a plan!" Rin announced. "Loop the green over the blue, then under the yellow, then twist the pink — no wait, twice — no, three times, then—" Ami blinked. "Rin," she said carefully. "Even you look confused." Rin looked down. Her ribbons were already in a spectacular knot. A very, very complicated knot. "...Yes," said Rin. "I am quite confused." They both burst out laughing — and can you guess what happened to Rin's ribbons? They got even more tangled! Whoops! Then their friend Tanu sat down, calm as still water, and began to hum. A low, gentle hum, like a song looking for its words. Mmmm-mm-mmm. Mmmm-mm-mmm. Can you hum with Tanu? Mmmm-mm-mmm. Something about that hum made Ami's fingers feel steadier. She tried once. Tried twice. On the third try — the ribbon stayed. But then — whoooosh! — a gust of wind snatched the golden ribbon right out of Grandmother Suno's basket It spun and twirled and drifted and landed — plop — right on top of Elder Bano's head. Elder Bano looked up, very slowly. The children froze. Then Elder Bano smiled the slowest, grandest smile anyone had ever seen. "I have waited years," she said, "to look this magnificent." The children laughed so hard the festival flags shook. But when the laughter settled, Ami looked down at her small hands and hid them behind her back. Her ribbons kept slipping. Everyone else's were coming together so beautifully. She stared at her feet. Maybe my hands are too small, she thought. Maybe I can't do this. Just then, a voice said, "Hello." A girl stood at the edge of the festival ground, holding a single ribbon — deep and shimmery gold, the colour of warm afternoon sun. "I'm Miko," she said. "I came from over the hills. My grandma gave me this ribbon to bring. She said a rainbow always has room for one more colour." Ami looked at the gold ribbon. She looked at all their ribbons together. She brought her hands out from behind her back. "Come sit with us," she said. Miko showed them her special knot — a looping, swirling tie that moved like water when you shook it. They all tried. They got it wrong. They tried again. Tanu hummed. Rin's tongue poked out in concentration. Miko guided Ami's fingers gently over and under and through. And when it worked — when Ami's ribbon finally held its knot and swayed and stayed — something warm and bright bloomed right in the middle of her chest. Tangle, untangle, twist and twirl, Slip and slide — what a whirl! Together we make colours bright, Dancing ribbons in the light! That's the ribbon chant — can you say it with me? Tangle, untangle, twist and twirl— let's remember it, because the dance is about to begin. The drums went thump-thump-thump. The flutes rose high and sweet. The children stood in a circle, each one holding their ribbon, the bamboo-and- lantern-lit festival ground humming beneath their feet. The air smelled of marigolds and rice cakes and something else — something like excitement, warm and buzzy on the back of your tongue. "Ready?" said Ami. And they danced. The ribbons rose. Red and blue and green and pink and orange and purple — and gold, Miko's gold, looping and swirling above them all in that special water-knot that shimmered like sunlight. Together the ribbons made a rainbow. Thump-thump-thump went the drums. Swish-swish-swish went the ribbons. Thump went Ami's heart. Elder Bano clapped. Grandmother Suno pressed both hands to her cheeks. The whole village watched seven children — six from this village, one from over the hills — spin a rainbow into the sky with their own two hands. Ami looked up. Her small hands were still holding on. When the music settled and the ribbons came gently down, Miko stood beside Ami, both of them breathing hard and smiling harder. "I'm glad my grandma sent me," Miko said. "I'm glad she did too," said Ami. And in the warm, drum-quiet air of the festival ground, with lanterns glowing and marigolds under their feet, Tanu began to hum. One by one, the children joined in — not the words yet, just the melody, mmmm-mm-mmm — until even Elder Bano was humming softly, her ribbon crown still perched magnificently on her head. And then Ami took a deep breath, and sang it out, soft and sure: Tangle, untangle, twist and twirl, Slip and slide — what a whirl! Together we make colours bright, Dancing ribbons in the light. The lanterns swayed. The festival sparkled. And somewhere above the rolling green hills, the evening sky looked — just a little — like a rainbow. The End.
author: Bhaskar Rana

title: A cat who doesn't like another cat !
text: I just woke up from my bed. Suddenly I saw Another cat, just like me, plying in side the cardboard box. I first s tarred at her then I SHOUTED get out go out of my house, now! she looked at me then started to play again. I went closer to her and saw that she has many infections on her body. I thought '' Maybe I'll just let her go?, NO I will never ever give my house to any one, even for a small Fly in this house '' With Anger I shouted at her again GET OUT! GET OUT! GET OUT OF MY HOUSE! but she did not listen to me me at ALL. Not even a bit. I shouted at my owner to take her out of the house. he had beaten me for doing such a thing. I BECAME SAD AND ANGRY I went under the sofa in fear and started thinking ''What shall I do?'' one day my owner took the another cat and went out. I wonder why did he take her? I sat quietly, watching him go with a smile in my face. HAA, HAA, HAA. No more worries for me! He came back empty handed. I was sure she was gone out of this house forever. jolly, jolly, jolly, together we read news paper with more fun than we both ever had THE END!
author: Sujatha V
illustrator: Canato Jimo; Catherine Groenewald; JP Brouard; Kalynne Vorster; Karen Lilje Lilje; Preetam Dhar; Priya Kuriyan

title: No Homework Today Because of a Cat in a Tree!
text: Benny, you haven’t handed in your homework! Where is it? I’m so sorry, Miss. It’s all because of a cat in a tree! No Homework Today Because of a Cat in a Tree! Written by Sharan Sagoo, LQM Stories Illustrated by Priya Kuriyan I was about to start my homework when I saw a black cat stuck in a tree. I couldn’t just leave it there, so I went on a hunt to find a ladder. A neighbour lent me a ladder, but it was broken. So I had to go on another hunt to find a hammer and some nails. Another neighbour lent me a hammer and gave me some nails. I made so much noise fixing the ladder that I woke my sleeping baby brother! Mum panicked when she heard my brother cry. She ran so fast out of the kitchen that she didn’t notice that a mischievous hungry monkey had snuck in! The mischievous monkey made a big mess, and he ate all of our food. Because of the monkey, Mum had to send Dad to the local tea shop to buy something for us to eat for dinner! Dad bought steaming chicken and rice for our dinner. It was so hot he could hardly carry it. The yummy smell from the food attracted a greedy dog who chased my Dad home! I was waiting for Dad in the garden. The greedy dog came charging toward me and ate my notebook, which was filled with my homework! So, Benny, what you are saying is that the dog ate your homework? Yes, Miss, but don’t you see, it’s all because of a cat in a tree! THE END
author: Sharan Sagoo / Little Quiet Mind

title: Rahul and His Loyal Friend Rockey
text: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Rahul. He had a pet dog named Rockey. When Rahul first met Rockey, he was just a small street dog—hungry, weak, and lonely. But Rahul took care of him with love and kindness. From that day, they became best friends. Rahul and Rockey did everything together. They ate together, played together, and even slept beside each other. Rockey was the happiest dog in the world because of Rahul’s love. One day, something very sad happened. While Rahul and Rockey were out for their morning walk, an accident occurred, and Rahul died on the spot. Rockey was heartbroken. He couldn’t believe that his best friend was gone forever. Rahul had been a very rich boy. Before he died, he had said in his will, “When I die, everything I own will belong to my dog, Rockey.” So after Rahul’s death, Rockey became the owner of a big bungalow, many cars, twenty servants, a swimming pool, and several companies. But even with all the wealth, Rockey felt empty. He had everything — except Rockey decided to share one of Rahul’s companies with Varun. From that day on, Rockey and Varun lived together, taking care of each other, keeping Rahul’s memories alive forever.
author: Purvi Bhingardive

title: Climbing trees again.
text: When I was small, I loved climbing trees. Near my house, there was a big Gulmohar tree. I used to motivate my friends who were afraid to climb the trees. My friends climbed up and came down fast. But I always stayed on the trees. When I looked down, I felt scared. The ground looked very far. I did not know how to come down. I was brave to come up,but scared to come down I always used to cry while coming down and my friends would call him for me. My father used to come to save and rescue me like a super hero. Even though i get a lot of scolding for climbing trees, I still climb on trees again i still cry but, I will always keep climbing trees again.
author: AANCHAL AJIT

title: Ammu and Raja
text: Ammu was enjoying at home with her family on Sunday. Mom said, “Ammu, get a mug.” Ammu noticed her dog Raja looking sad and very bored. She thought, "Why Raja is so sad?" Ammu got a fun idea! She started dancing with a few toys to make Raja happy. But Raja did not react... She started dancing again with a dog trea t, and Raja got happy! Raja jumped with happiness!! Ammu and Raja danced and played together on that Sunday afternoon!
author: MANDHARA PRABHU

title: Someone has been playing with our toys!
text: It has been raining all week and the back garden became a pond. Verity and I have not been able to play outside. When the rain stopped, we put on our wellington boots and looked at our toys. It looked like someone had been playing with our toys. Who? Someone had sat on the swing. The seat was all muddy. It wasn't me and it wasn't Verity, but who? Someone had used the slide. We could see muddy footprints. Leaves and grass covered the ladder on the slide. The slide was dirty. It looked like someone had sat on the slide and slid down on their bottom! We could hear a noise coming from the treehouse. It was very loud snoring. "Who could it be?" Verity asked. "I don't know," I said. The whole treehouse rattled and shaked. The louder the snore, the more the treehouse moved. We wondered if the treehouse would fall to the ground. Verity and I wondered what we should do. "Better get Daddy," I said. "Yes!" said Verity. So, we returned to the house and called out to Daddy. He wondered what was going on. Daddy put on his wellington boots and went to the treehouse. The three of us stood and listened to the snoring. We looked at one another and laughed. Daddy wasn't sure what was making such a loud noise. He decided to go the shed to collect a net. He thought he needed something to help get whatever it was out of the treehouse. Daddy decided to climb the tree to get to the treehouse. He told Verity and I to stay at the bottom of the tree. We thought this was a good idea. We watched Daddy carefully climb the tree. When Daddy looked inside the treehouse he saw a pair of very large, black eyes. The eyes looked at Daddy and Daddy looked at the eyes. Everything became very quiet. Daddy had found a fox! "It is ok!"said Daddy. Daddy climbed down the tree. Daddy explained that a fox had come into the garden and had been playing with the toys. The storm came and the fox took shelter in the treehouse. Daddy said it was best to leave the fox alone and when the fox was ready, the fox would leave. We went back inside the house and sat by the kitchen window. We waited and waited for a chance to see the fox. It became dark and we still had not been able to see the fox. Verity thought that the fox was so tired that it was still having a sleep. I thought the fox would wait for us all to go to sleep and then it would leave the treehouse. When we woke up th enext day, we could not wait to go in to the garden. We immediately went to the tree and looked uo at the treehouse. It was very quiet. Daddy came to check and told us the fox had gone. In some ways we were glad that we could give shelter to the fox. In some ways wewere sad as we did not get to sy goodbye. The story about someone coming to play with our toys would remain with us forever.
author: Lynne H.
illustrator: Abraham Muzee; Annika  Brandow; Harshika G; Niloufer Wadia; Nyambura Kariuki; Phạm Hoàng  Giang; Princess  Kabeya; Priya Kuriyan; Rhea Nandy; Sam  van Riet; Sourav Sarkar; Wiehan de Jager

title: Mum, You're the Best Ever!
text: Mum, you're the best ever! Your smile is as beautiful as the flowers that grow in our garden. Mum, you're the best ever! When we wash the clothes in the tub, I make so many bubbles by splashing my hands in the water and you splash along with me! Mum, you're the best ever! Cooking yummy food with you makes me feel grown up. I like how you trust me to measure out the ingredients. Mum, you're the best ever! When I ride my bicycle and glide through the wind, you are always there watching over me and smiling. Mum, you're the best ever! Spending time with you makes me happy. Mum, you're the best ever! You make words fun and stories come to life! Mum, you're the best ever! Bedtime is never scary because you always settle me into bed. Mum, you're the best ever! Thank you for being the best ever mum in the world!
author: Sharan Sagoo / Little Quiet Mind

title: The mystery of the special pen
text: I went to school this morning and found a letter under my desk and I was in 6-A. The letter said "You are our detective. You are going to help us find my precious pen. It has a sticker of a lion on it. You have one month as time to find this pen." I showed it to my friends (Ishita,Thasleema and Nonmozhli) and asked who wrote the letter and whether they recognize this handwriting. But Ishita said that she does'nt know who wrote the letter because many people can have the same handwriting but she told to check on our teacher. So I told her to go and check whether it was our teacher who wrote the letter, and so she went. An hour later, she told me that she isn't claiming that she wrote the letter even though I showed the proof. Now we were both confused. But that very second one clue popped in my head.'Our teacher and my friend (Ishita) have the same handwriting so it could even be a letter written by Ishita! So that's why our teacher is not claiming it! So I told her about it. Then she said that if she wanted help searching for her lucky pen, she would've told me. But I wasn't having it so I decided to be sneaky and keep an eye on them. Lately I've noticed that our teacher has been so worried and she has stopped putting her signature and also stopped correcting our books. And each time this happens, my friend was getting happier and happier. Today I found some red ink on the teacher's table. I noted that as clue too but my friend never goes near the teacher's table during school hours, Then something popped my mind. She must've put the red ink on the table when anyone or me was not there so that I will be tricked into knowing that t he teacher has the pen. So I decided to check my friend's bag tomorrow morning in school. The next day, when my friend came to school, I checked her bag but couldn't find the red pen. So I let the mission blow over. But we also realised that Shrinth our classmate was acting weird. So we decided to act like we had a stomach ache during yoga period and check his bag. During yoga period we checked his bag and sure enough we found the pen. Then we gave it to the teacher then she thanked us and left.
author: Anne Pritika
illustrator: Ekta Bharti; Gauri Kathula; Juhi  Agarwal; Neha Bhatt; Ram Kol; Rohit Kelkar; Saksham Arora

title: Creamy Mess!
text: One Afternoon, while Amma was taking a nap, Ahalya finds something Exciting.... She finds Amma's new box of face cream... Ahalya loved the smell of the cream! She starts applying the face cream all over her face... Unknowingly she starts drawing fun things on the mirror using the face cream. She starts exploring different surfaces and starts putting it all over the place. Suddenly Amma wakes up, and calls Ahalya... Amma looks at the creamy mess and instead of getting angry she starts laughing!! Amma and Ahalya clean the creamy mess together!
author: AHALYA A

title: Would you like to come for tea?
text: “Would you like to come to tea?” Verity asked the tiger. “Hmm!” said the tiger. “Mummy makes a delicious chocolate cake!” said Olly. “Well in that case, yes I would love to come, but can I bring a friend?” said the tiger. “I am sure Mummy would not mind,” said Olly. Verity said, “It is agreed then. Come over Friday afternoon at 2pm.” Olly and verity were so excited and told Mummy about their house guest plus one. Olly, Verity and Mummy cleaned the house. Mummy did the grocery shopping and baking. Verity collected flowers from the garden to put in a vase. Olly set the table with a nice tablecloth, cutlery, and crockery. Mummy placed homemade sandwiches, scones, jam and cream and her chocolate cake in the centre of the table. They all sat down and waited for the doorbell to ring. Just after 2pm there was a knock on the door and the doorbell rang. “I will go,” said Olly. Verity and Mummy looked at one another and wondered who tiger would bring as the plus one. We could hear Olly saying, “So good to see you. Come on in!” We could hear footsteps coming down the corridor. Plus, a very odd smell. It was an extraordinarily strong, unpleasant smell. We did not know if it was the tiger or tiger’s friend. When Olly reached the kitchen table, we could see the tiger, but a puff of smoke came from behind him. As the tiger stepped to one side, we could see a skunk! We all looked at one another politely. The tiger introduced the skunk as his friend. He explained that the skunk did not have many friends. Olly, Verity and Mummy nodded their heads. They thought, we know why. Mummy offered the tiger and skunk a seat. Everyone sat at the table and politely smiled. Mummy lifted the plate of sandwiches and said, “Sandwich anyone? I have made cheese and tomato, egg, chicken, and tuna sandwiches. Help yourselves!” The tiger took a chicken sandwich. The skunk took an egg sandwich. Olly and Verity took a cheese and tomato sandwich each and Mummy took a chicken sandwich. “Yummy!” said the tiger. “Delicious!” said the skunk. Mummy then offered tea or coffee. The tiger took a big slurp. The skunk placed lots of sugar in his coffee. They were so thirsty that Mummy had to make another pot of tea and coffee. Everyone enjoyed the scones, cream, and jam. The tiger and skunk licked and licked their mouth and hands. The jam had become caught in their paws and whiskers. Everyone laughed. The tiger’s eyes kept looking at the chocolate cake. Mummy could see that he wanted a piece. She said in a loud voice, “Time for cake!” Both the skunk and tiger sat upright in their seats. Mummy served the chocolate cake, and everyone purred with “Ohhhhhhhhh,” and “Arrrrrrrr!” The chocolate cake was extremely delicious. The tiger rubbed his tummy, feeling very satisfied. The skunk rubbed his ears as the sugar had made them hot. Mummy, Olly and Verity just stared at the animals as they reacted to being so full. The tiger said, “We need your help!” Mummy, Olly and Verity were incredibly surprised. “What can we do?” Mummy asked. The tiger went on to explain that the skunk had an important meeting to attend, but because of his smell, that everyone would walk away when he enters a room. He wondered what we could do to make the skunk smell nice. “Well!” said Mummy. She sat and put her finger to her cheek. This mean that she was thinking. She asked the skunk to come to her so she could understand what was going on with the skunk’s body. As the skunk moved to Mummy, a spray of liquid came out of the skunk. Mummy then understood what was happening. “Ummm!” said Mummy. We all looked. She explained that when the skunk walked the spray provided a scent and it was that which everyone could all smell. Mummy asked did the skunk know he was doing this. The skunk said he did not know. Mummy said, “Well, we have worked out what and need to work our why!” Mummy asked the skunk more questions and decided that the skunk sprayed the scent as a survival mechanism. He did it to protect himself as it happens when he feels threatened. Everyone nodded their heads and agreed. Mummy said we need to make sure the skunk felt confident and strong. If this could happen, the skunk would not feel threatened. Mummy had an idea. She took one of her plates and balanced it on the skunk’s head. She asked the skunk to walk around the room without dropping the plate. The skunk walked and dropped the first plate. Immediately the skunk sprayed a scent. Mummy reassured the skunk that it was ok and that they were using old plates. The skunk saw that Mummy did not get mad so tried again. This time the skunk walked around the room and held his head up high. The plate stayed on his head. When Mummy took the plate off the skunk’s head, she told him that we were all proud. The skunk smiled from ear to ear. Mummy suggested that we give the skunk a bath. She said she would use her magic bubble bath to make the skunk smell sweet. People would smell the perfume and want to be friends with the skunk. The skunk had never had a bubble bath before and so was a little nervous. Everyone stood by the bath and told the skunk he would enjoy it. The skunk took a bubble bath and floated around in the bubbles. Mummy took a nice soft towel and dried the skunk off. She found an old brush to brush the skunk’s coat. It was a little tricky, but Mummy did an excellent job. Mummy found a nice scarf and tied around the skunk’s neck. The skunk looked a million dollars. He did not smell unpleasant and smiled with a welcoming manner. Mummy reminded the skunk of why he came to smell so bad. She told him to remember this day and carrying the plate on his head. She said that this would help him in situations where he needed to be calm. The tiger and the skunk thanked us all and went on their way. The next morning there was a knock on the door, and a delivery man had a huge bouquet of flowers. The flowers were for Mummy from the tiger and the skunk. The card said that the skunk’s meeting was successful and that he had now made many friends. This was all due to taking tea with us. Mummy, Olly and Verity just smiled.
author: Lynne H.
illustrator: Elizabeth Sparg; Lynne H.; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'; Saanvi Pratul

title: Bey the boy who loves adventures
text: A boy named bey and he is eight years old that loves nature and adventure He have a dog names delfin One day he found some something it,s a potato he take the potato One day he found something it full of tiny creatures it,s a beehive run After the chase he collected some vegetables while secretly hiding from the bees Where has you been grandma said i bring you some vegetables for lunch After eating he adventure again
author: Caleb Mannuel

title: A Yak Called Aputi
text: It was early one morning when there was a knock at the door. It was a loud knock. We had no idea who it was. When we opened the door, it was our neighbour, Raj. He told us that the whole village was excited as a yak had come to town! We have not seen a yak in many years so this was a really massive thing. We quickly put on clothing and dashed out the door. Everyone had gathered to see the yak. The yak looked startled and sat and stared. We all looked at one another. She looked magnificent. Her coat shined, her eyes sparkled and her smile made us all happy. We did not know what the yak would do. So, we all waited and waited. What was the yak going to do? The yak slowly started to walk along the pathways towards the market. We all followed. She stopped and smelled the flowers. Some flowers did not seem to bother her, but the sunflowers tickled her nose. She then gave a big, “Achoo, achoo, achoo!” Some of us also sneezed. We all laughed. She walked further and met other animals. She stopped, smiled, and said hello. A rabbit looked and then turned away. The rabbit thought he was seeing things as he had not seen a yak before. He turned back to have another look to check to see that it was a yak that had come to visit. The yak went through the back gardens of houses and passed by the washing lines. Was she looking for something to wear? We wondered if she would take anything from the washing line, but she did not. She just wiped her face on a tea towel. We all looked in amazement. The owner of the tea towel said they would always love that tea towel from now on. We followed the yak some more. The yak followed the path through the rice fields. She stopped to take a drink at the river. Next thing, to our surprise, she had jumped in the river and took a swim. She was a particularly good swimmer and loved the water. When she got out of the river, she gave her body an extremely big shake. All the water came over us. We looked like we had all been swimming! She walked further towards the marketplace. The yak heard music and started to dance. She liked the music that was playing. We did too. So, we all danced with the yak. The yak had a good rhythm, and we all thought she had danced before. She walked to the playground and saw the slide and seesaw. She could not go on the seesaw as you need two people. She looked at the slide and decided to climb the ladder. We were shocked to see her climb. She carefully went up each step and go to the top of the slide. She stopped and looked around and then slid down the slide. We all clapped. The yak wandered into the market and started to look at the stalls. She lifted her head high and started to sniff. We thought that she might be hungry. We did not know what she would like to eat. One person suggested meat, but we thought that would upset her tummy. Another person suggested bread. But we did not think that was a clever idea either. Another suggested grass. We gave the yak some grass, but she was not too impressed. She spat the grass out on to the ground and then she rolled around in the dirt. We all looked surprised. What should we do? She wandered back to the pastry stall. She looked at the pastries. The yak sniffed the air. The stall owner gave the yak a chocolate croissant. We did not think it was a clever idea. The stall owner said, “Trust me, she will love the chocolate croissant!” We gave the yak the croissant and she munched and munched on it. She was incredibly happy. The stall owner thought we should call the yak, “Aputi.” We liked the name and called her Aputi. We thought that Aputi might be thirsty. So, we offered her some milk. We all stood back and watched. She went to the bowl and gave it a sniff and then stepped back. She saw someone in the crowd with a cup of coffee. She lifted her head high and sniffed and went to the person with the coffee. They placed their cup on the ground and Aputi drank the coffee from the cup. We all laughed. Aputi became very tired after her busy morning. She wandered to a big tree in the market square and sat. It was obvious that she was tired. A cool breeze blew and Aputi gave a big sigh. Aputi looked at everyone and smiled. She had brought excitement to our village, and we all fell in love with her. Aputi was content and fell fast asleep. She snored softly and we all loved her for that. She was peaceful and slept soundly. We sat with her until it became dark and then we all went home. A few people decided to sleep close to Aputi to keep her safe. The next day, the sun was shining and clouds were in the sky. We were all happy thinking about Aputi. We wondered what she would do today. We all went to the market to see her again, but she had gone. The people who had slept close to her did not even know that she had woke up and left the village. We all stood still and in silence. One person said, “We were lucky to spend a day with Aputi, and she will be forever in our hearts.” We all agreed. We all thought that our day with Aputi would live on through our stories. Dancers created an “Aputi” dance. Artists painted pictures and made carvings, silversmiths made “Aputi” jewellery. The chocolate croissants became famous. Aputi would be with us forever and maybe one day she would return to say hello.
author: Lynne H.

title: Winter has come and so has Harry!
text: Winter has come and the weather has turned cold. The leaves have fallen off the trees and make a carpet of reds, browns, yellows, and orange colours. The back garden looks bare and lonely. When we go out, we put on coats, scarves, hats, gloves, and our boots. We can only stay outside to play for a short amount of time as otherwise we get too cold. We usually play on our slide, swing, and seesaw. Then we come inside and have a cup of hot chocolate and sit by the fire to warm up. We usually leave our boots outside on the step as they are too wet to bring inside. Verity loves her boots. Mummy bought her a new pair for this winter. They are pink covered with flowers. Verity has a matching pink coat, hat, and gloves. So, when I see her in the garden, she is all pink. It makes it easier to see where she is playing if she has gone into the garden before me. On this one day, she was eager to go outside. We had been in the house for a few days due to poor weather. I was still putting on my coat and hat and then I heard a scream. What happened, I thought. Daddy came rushing to the door and I went too. Verity had tried to put her feet in her boots, but something prickly went through her socks. What was it? Daddy put his hand inside the boot and pulled out a hedgehog. We were all surprised. Hedgehogs usually come into the garden during winter. This hedgehog was a little early. Daddy wondered why the hedgehog was awake. He told us that they are nocturnal and that means they sleep during the day and are awake at night. He said they usually build their nests in hedges and bushes and that’s where part of their name comes from. He said if we listen carefully, we might be able to hear the hedgehog snort. It sounds like a hog. So, people called the animal a hedgehog! Daddy placed the hedgehog on the outside table. We looked at it with awe. I said, “Hedgehogs are amazing! Verity said, “Look at the spikes!” We stopped and moved a little closer to examine the hedgehog more. Daddy told us that the hedgehog as over more than five thousand spikes. He said they act like our hair and fall out after a year. But another spike grows in its place. Verity asked, “Does he have any friends?” Daddy explained that hedgehogs live alone. I said, “We can be his friend and let’s call him Harry!” We all agreed. Daddy put Harry on the floor, and he ran straight to the flowerpot. He jumped inside the pot and pushed himself between the flowers. He bobbed up and down and seemed happy. Daddy thought Harry might be looking for beetles and caterpillars as that is what hedgehogs eat. We did not think he would find anything like that in the flowerpot as Mummy likes to keep the bugs away. Harry then ran across the garden and went to the slide. We were shocked to see Harry climb the ladder and slid down the slide. He looked like he was having fun. We all laughed. He went down the slide a few times. He stopped at the top of the slide and looked around the garden. It is a beautiful view from the top of the slide as you can see all the garden. Hary slid down the slide and went over to the paddling pool. Daddy had forgot to put it away after summer. Rain had fallen and had filled up the pool to the top. Harry jumped in the pool and started swimming. We did not know that hedgehogs could swim. We wondered if he felt cold in the water. Within no time, Harry got out of the pool and gave his body a shake. He ran to the top of the garden. He curled himself up in a tight ball and rolled down the hill. We thought this was his way of becoming warm. Hedgehogs are very curious animals. Harry ran along the shed and then climbed on to the outside table. Harry had spotted Mummy’s watering can. He tried to climb into the watering can but ended up headfirst. All we could see was Harry’s bottom. Harry wriggled and wriggled to try to get out of the watering can. Harry snorted as though he was in trouble. Daddy carefully lifted him from the watering can. Harry moved to a nearby plant pot that had berries on the plant. Harry sat and looked at the berries. He climbed up to the plant where the berries were and started eating them. He made a funny sound when he ate. We thought he must be enjoying them as he ate with his eyes closed. Daddy went inside and brought out fruit. He cut up an apple and Harry ate it all. He peeled a banana and Harry aet it all. He gave Harry a strawberry and Harry ate it all. Daddy placed more berries on the table and Harry ate them all. There was a tiny snail that had also come to eat the fruit, but Harry did not eat that. Daddy thought it must be time for hibernation and that is why Harry ate so much. Daddy explained that Hedgehogs hibernate because it becomes difficult to find food in winter, especially when it snows. Hedgehogs eat a lot of food and then “sleep,” but it is more like resting during winter. They live off the fat they have gained by eating so much beforehand. Daddy went back into the house and cut a large slice of watermelon. He also brought out a bowl of water for Harry. Harry ate the watermelon and drank the water. Daddy thought that Harry had eaten enough food to help him through winter. We all thought that was good. Harry started foaming at the mouth. Verity and I became very worried. Daddy told us not to worry as this is something Hedgehogs do. He said the hedgehog’s take the foam and then spread it all over their body. It gives them an extra protection from other animals. Daddy was convinced that it was hibernation time. If Harry slept and another animal came towards Harry, the strong smell would send the animal away. This was interesting to know. Daddy went to the shed and took out our hedgehog house. He gave it a dust and then we all went to the back of the garden to find a good place for the house to be left. We looked for dry ground and an area where it is sheltered. We placed Harry’s home against a thick hedge and fence so he would feel safe. It was also placed out of the wind so Harry would not get cold. Daddy placed Harry in his new home and he was happy. From time to time, we look out from the kitchen window and into the back garden. We can see Harry’s house clearly. We look out for Harry and wonder if he is still resting. Sometimes we do get to see him scurry out of the house for a few minutes and then scurry back into his house. We are looking forward to spring, when it will be warmer, Harry can find food by himself and we can play together.
author: Lynne H.

title: The Great Lion loses his ROAR!
text: One morning in the Jungle, the mighty Lion tried to roar, but… No roar came out at all! “But who will keep order and peace now?” the animals wondered. The Lion decided to give the other animals a chance to become the next ROARER... We must find… a substitute Roarer! Whoever can roar the best shall guard the forest! So, the Fox stepped up first. Not even a single leaf moved from his roar. Next, the Snake slithered forward. Everyone broke into sneezes! One by one the others tried; But none could shake the forest like the Lion once did. Then came the Mouse, tiny and shy. The others wondered, “What roar could he ever make?” But the Rat roared into a hollow cave, The voice boomed back, LOUDER and LOUDER! And from that day on, the tiniest voice held the loudest honour. What a GREAT ROAR! You’ve proved that size doesn’t matter But the will to do something does!
author: Ever After  Kids

title: Lina and The Amazing Soap King Rescue
text: Lina loves running through the fields chasing after butterflies.......and the birds that soar high above in the sky! On rainy days, she loves to splish and splash with her paper boat in the muddy pond. On hot days, she makes towering sand castles in the wet sand on the beach. Every time Lina comes home from an adventure, she returns looking dirty and messy. Her mother always greets her and hands her a bar of soap to wash herself clean. This makes Lina angry. " Go away, soap, leave me alone. My adventure is not ending. I'm not going to wash you off! " Then one night, Lina dreams of the sandcastle that she built on her beach adventure. The castle is under attack by a swarm of nasty germs! All of a sudden, the nasty germs start chasing Lina. There is no escaping; everywhere she runs, the germs follow. Suddenly, out of nowhere, a fancy-looking Soap King appears. "Don't worry, Lina, the germs won't survive my soapy bubbles. I will wash them away". Splish, splash, bubble, bubble! No more germs ever again! And just like that, the germs vanish. After her scary dream and her amazing Soap King rescue, Lina always washes after every adventure. Splish, splash, bubble, bubble! No more germs ever again!
author: Sharan Sagoo / Little Quiet Mind

title: There is a mouse in the house!
text: There is a mouse in the house. It moves about. All through the night we can hear it scratch and bite. It sounds like the mouse, and the cat always fight. He comes to the kitchen to find cheese. He looks at us to say, “Can I have more please?” We wave our hands to tell it to go away. But it batters its eyes and asks, “Please let me stay!” We put down a box and small blanket so it can make a bed. He crawls under the blanket and becomes a sleepy head. The mouse wakes up early every morning. He hears the milkman and baker make their calling. He sits on the windowsill after nibbling some bread. He would see the postman walk by and call out, “Hello, Fred!” The mouse would join us for morning tea. He eats a biscuit and then sits on my knee. His morning ends with a play outside. When it gets cold, he comes in and sits near the fireside. For lunch he nibbles and chews. At anything he can find and then watches the cockatoos. In the afternoon he sits and takes a nap. He likes to sleep lying on his back. For dinner he sits looking up at the table. He wants to sit with us and asks if he is able! After dining on an exceptionally fine meal. He will sit and eat orange peel. He lies on the couch to rest and relax. He enjoys eating tv snacks. When it goes dark and it is time for bed. Again, he curls up under his blanket and becomes a sleepy head.
author: Lynne H.
illustrator: Ahana Goyal; Amy Uzzell; Aruna Keerthi Gamage; Catherine Groenewald; Herminder Ohri; Kaustubh  Kamat; Nancy Raj; Rajeev Verma 'Banjara'

title: News about Aputi!
text: News has spread around about a yak called Aputi. She moves from village to village and some called her “Tutti!” Everywhere she goes she spreads a friendly cheer. All the villagers want to give her milk that she won't go near. Aputi goes to the temple so she can pray. The monks will try to give her hay. She thanks them kindly and gives them a bow. She tells them she is not hungry exactly right now. She drinks coffee and water and they all know that. She eats a chocolate croissant even though it makes her fat. Aputi likes to swim in a river. When she gets out, she always gives a shiver. She dances and sings to music when she hears it. The villagers join in but some fear it. They all laugh out a loud and have lots of fun. Then they sit with Aputi in the sun. Aputi plays with the children and hop, skips, and jumps. When she falls down, she makes a big thump. She gets up and has a good laugh. The children all love her and give her clap. Aputi smells flowers and walks through gardens. Sometimes she says, “I beg your pardon!” The flowers tickle her nose and she does a sneeze. A villager will offer her a handkerchief to wave off bees. Aputi makes friends with other animals. She knows a rabbit called Annabelle. Everyone loves her as she brings good luck. Some say she runs just like a duck. She becomes tired after having a busy day. The villagers make a model of her in clay. Aputi sleeps and snores. Everyone in the village close their doors. Some sleep with her to keep her safe at night. She is gone however, when the sun shines bright. They do not know when they will see her if ever again. They write stories about her using a blue pen. The villagers are happy when she is around. They think she is the best yak they have found.
author: Lynne H.
illustrator: Adrija Ghosh; Aphisith Souphavongtay; Lavanya Karthik; Lynne H.; Niloufer Wadia; Ogin Nayam; Pallavi Jain; Sheena Deviah; Shrujana Shridhar; Tanvi Bhat

title: Where did they go?
text: Every evening our apartment became a hide and seek playground. We ran through corridors and hid behind shoe racks and squeezed under the stairs. I was the seeker. I closed my eyes and started counting near the lift. "8..9...10.." I finished counting and went to find everyone... but no one was easy to find! I searched and searched and.. searched "Wow.. they're really good at hiding," I thought. My stomach growled. "I'll go home for just one minute," I said. And I went home. One minute turned into snacks, TV and sitting on the sofa. Outside my friends were still hiding... waiting for me to find them!
author: SHIVAHARINI S

title: Ankit and the Sky Ball Quest
text: In a village tucked between green hills — where the bamboo scaffolds caught the morning mist and the mango trees dropped their sweetness into the warm air — there lived a small boy named Ankit. He was five years old. He was not very big. But inside his chest — oh, his heart was enormous. Every evening, Ankit stood at the edge of the Sky Ball field and watched. The balls swooshed down the curved bamboo tracks. They zoomed around the long slope. They flew up — and landed, thud, right into the wide wooden groove at the far end of the field. That groove was the goal. One ball in the groove. One point for your team. Have you ever watched something so wonderful that you wanted to jump right in? That was Ankit, every single evening. "Someday," he whispered, "I will play too." But the villagers only chuckled. "Too small, little one! Come back when you are taller!" Then one morning, he found old Ramu in his workshop at the foot of the hill. Ramu made every Sky Ball in the village — each one shaped by hand, smoothed with river stone, and polished until it shone. The workshop smelled of cedar shavings and beeswax and something that felt, somehow, like patience itself. The balls sat in rows on a low wooden shelf, cool and smooth to the touch, each one glowing softly in the morning light. "Can I help?" Ankit asked. Ramu smiled — slowly, the way old trees sway. "Sit. Count them out for me. One by one." Can you count with Ankit? One — two — three — four — five! Five perfect balls. Smooth and shimmering as little moons. Every morning after that, Ankit came back. He polished. He counted. He listened to Ramu's stories of great players from long ago. And one morning he asked, "What made them great?" Ramu held a ball up to the light. It shimmered. It spun a small golden circle on the wall. "Three things," Ramu said softly. "Roll. Shine. Fly." Can you say it with me? Roll — shine — fly! Ankit said it quietly to himself all the way home, like a song, like a secret, like a promise. In the afternoons, he practised alone in the mango grove. The grass was warm and scratchy beneath his bare feet. The air tasted of ripe fruit and dust. "Swoosh!" he cried, swinging his arms wide. Can you swoosh? "Zoom!" He spun — and tumbled magnificently into the grass. Zoom! "Thud!" He sat up, blinking, with a long mango leaf stuck to his nose. Thud! His best friend Mira peeked from behind a trunk, giggling into both hands. "Finest tumbler in the whole village," she announced. "I am practising," said Ankit, with enormous dignity. The next day, Mira brought him to the field. Taru crossed his arms tight. "He is too small. He will cost us the game." Ankit's stomach dropped like a stone. But he looked at Taru steadily and said, "I know every curve on that track. Just let me show you." He played. His passes were careful and exact. He called out to his teammates — where to stand, when to move, which way the ball would curve. Taru said nothing. But slowly, one finger at a time, his arms uncrossed. Tournament day. The whole village came. Saffron and green flags snapped in the warm breeze. The field smelled of dry grass and festival smoke and something sweet from the tea stall at the edge of the ground. Somewhere, a drum was beating — tuk tuk tuk tuk — steady and low, like an excited heart. Taru pulled Ankit aside before the first round. "The other team is fast," he muttered. "Really fast." His voice had lost its sharpness. What was in it now was something closer to worry — and asking, in its own way, for help. Ankit looked at him. "Then we move faster together," he said. Stand up tall, just like Ankit. Take a deep breath. Ready? He closed his eyes, and whispered it — Roll. Shine. Fly — and walked onto the field. The game was fast. Faster than anything. The balls curved and dipped and surprised everyone. Ankit ran, darted, and sang out to his teammates at every turn — "Mira, left! Taru, now! Hold — hold — go!" The clack of sticks rang through the warm afternoon air like music. Then — a ball broke loose from a scramble n ear the far bamboo track. It rolled fast. So fast Straight down the long curved slope, heading directly for the wide wooden groove at the end of the field. Ankit was closest. He could reach it before anyone else. He could nudge it — just a little, just enough — and the point would be his. No one would even see. His hand stretched out. The drum stopped. The crowd noise fell away. The whole world went very, very still. He felt the smooth, cool surface of the ball beneath his fingertips. He felt the prickle of dry grass under his feet. He felt his own heartbeat — thump. Thump. Thump. What do you think Ankit should do? And then, like a polished ball catching morning light, three words rose up from somewhere deep and warm inside him. Can you say it with him, right now? Roll — shine — fly! Ankit pulled his hand back. He looked up. Mira was two steps away, perfectly placed, eyes wide and shining and ready. He passed. The ball swept through the warm air in one clean, curving arc. Mira caught it sure and smooth. She curved around the last defender — drew back her arm — and sent it, clean and true, right into the wide wooden groove. Thud. For one breath, the field was silent. Then the village exploded. The flags shook. The drum hammered. The mango trees trembled with the noise of it. And Ankit — small Ankit, five-year- old Ankit — felt something burst open in his chest like light. His arms flew wide. His feet left the ground. He laughed the kind of laugh that starts in your stomach and has nowhere to go but up. Taru ran over. He did not say sorry. He did not need to. He grabbed Ankit's hand and held it up high, and the village cheered even louder, and Ankit thought — this. This is what roll, shine, fly feels like. That evening, Ramu sat beside Ankit on the stone steps as the hills turned slowly gold. He said nothing. He simply reached into his pocket and placed a fresh ball in Ankit's hands. They polished together in the warm, settling quiet — the soft scrape of cloth on wood, the first crickets starting up in the grass below, the distant laughter of children still playing in the last of the light. The ball shimmered in Ankit's small hands like a little moon. He was still not very big. The hills were still very tall. But something had grown inside him — quiet and warm and as strong as the hills themselves — and no one, not ever, could take it away. Small hands, he thought, can do the biggest things. He smiled at the stars. And the stars smiled right back. The End.
author: Bhaskar Rana

title: Sheep Shenanigans
text: Autumn in Buckleberry is always hard. The leaves all turn brown, orange, and red and fall off the trees. The wind blows chilly air and makes the leaves swirl around. The rain and black clouds hang heavy in the sky. Storms are frequent. Thunder and lightning take place. Last night when everyone was snuggled up in bed, the wind howled and the rain poured. The roof of the houses rattled, and the trees swayed from side to side. When we woke in the morning, we could see all the damage that was caused by the storm. Trees had been uprooted. The riverbank had burst and water had filled the street. There was no electricity in the house but luckily the water was still coming out of the taps. It looked like it was going to be a difficult day. Verity and I went downstairs for breakfast and sat at the kitchen table. Daddy managed to make a hot chocolate using our camping stove. He made us some scrambled egg and tomatoes too. As we sat and ate breakfast, we could hear a strange noise coming from the garden. It was still raining and therefore it was difficult to see what was going on. Daddy said he had better take a look. Verity was adamant that she wanted to go too. I also thought I wanted to see what it was. So, we all put on our raincoats and rain boots and stepped into the garden. We had to walk to the bottom of the garden and there we could see where the noise was coming from. “Baaaaaaa, baaaaaaaaaaaaaa, baaaaaaaaaaaa!” A sheep had got its head caught in the fence. We were not sure where it had come from. Daddy carefully held the sheep and moved it around so it could be free of the fence. The sheep was glad to be free of the fence. She gave herself a shake and then stood and looked at us all. We looked back at her as we did not know what to do next. Daddy said he had better make some phone calls and see if anyone else knew about the sheep. Daddy said, “Let’s go inside and leave the sheep to roam in the garden.” We went back inside the house and sat near the kitchen window. We were surprised to see a sheep in our garden. Next thing, the sheep started jumping over our toys. It made us laugh. She treated the toys like hay bails and jumped high across each item like it was an obstacle course. Verity thought that the sheep thought she was on the tv show, “Ninja Warrior!” We both laughed. The sheep then went over to our skipping rope and started to skip. It was obvious that she liked jumping. She played with family back home. Then the sheep became a little naughty. She pulled on the washing line and pulled off a tea towel. She started to chew Mummy’s tea towel. We were sure that it did not taste genuinely nice. After a while, the sheep dropped what was left of the tea towel on the ground. She was a nosey sheep as she started to poke her head in all sorts of things. She put her head in a bucket. We thought that she was thinking there was food in it. She got her head stuck and then had to shake her head and body to get the bucket off her. She then sat in the washing basket. We thought it was like abed for her. “Maybe she will have a sleep!” Verity said. “I do not think so,” I replied. The sheep had so much energy, she was not tired yet. But what would she do next? The sheep went to Mummy’s flowers and started eating them Mummy would not be too happy as she likes her flowers. The sheep ate them all. The sheep then made friends with rabbit and Harry the hedgehog. She thought they were other sheep as she chased them around the garden. She moved the rabbit and hedgehog from one side of the garden to another. The sheep then stopped in her tracks. She stared across the fence as she saw a fox. Sometimes foxes come into the garden. They are nosey and mischievous too. We did not want the fox to come in the garden now as it would cause more trouble. The fox knew that this was not the time to come in the garden to play. He slowly moved away. The sheep went and stood next to the rabbit and hedgehog to protect them. She thought they were her children. She brought them closer to the house as that was a safer area. Daddy had watched some of the sheep’s antics and said it was time to go back outside. Daddy had cut up watermelon and gave it to the sheep, rabbit, and hedgehog to eat. They sat and ate the watermelon for hours. Daddy had called farmer Ted. The bad storm last night had frightened all his sheep, and they had escaped from the farm. He had received calls all morning telling him that people had sheep in their gardens. Farmer ted was glad that Daddy had freed the sheep form the fence and it was in our garden playing. Farmer Ted said he would come and collect the sheep. Just before lunchtime, farmer Ted came to the house. He came in his tractor as he had a trailer on the back, and it was already full of sheep. He said there was room for one more and took the sheep and placed it with the others. He said he had secured the farm fence and hopefully the sheep would not escape again. The sheep looked happy to be together again. Farmer Ted said we could visit the farm anytime and see the sheep. We all thought that was a great idea as we had loved watching the sheep in our garden. Buckleberry Newspaper reported the story, and it gave everyone a good laugh. We made a joke about it and said how the sheep had taken a holiday. Verity and I will always remember the day a sheep came into our garden.
author: Lynne H.
illustrator: Avishek Sen; Lynne H.; Maithili  Joshi; Ravi Gupta; Siyasanga  Madyibi

title: The Girl and a Black Cat
text: On the foothills of himalayas lived a beautiful village of uttarakhand. This village was covered by a great no. of green trees. In this village lived a girl named harsita. She was a passionate lover of cat, but due to her family she couldn't a chance to keep one at home. She always thought to convence her parents to buy her one but didn't have courage to do so. She always used to see her friends playing with their cats. She always used to talk to her friends about having a cat. Her friends also encouraged her to talk to her parents to buy her a cat. She always wanted to have a black cat. On the last day of month while she was going with her mother to the market she saw a grey colored cat on the way. She went near the cat but it seemed like it was scared by her. The cat was so cute that she couldn't control herself and took it into her arms and went home with it. On reaching home she and her lil brother tried to convence her dad but it all got in vein. Dad was furios at the cat and threw it out of the home while harsita was not at home. When harsita came home she looked everywhere in her home like under the almirah. under the table and at different places but couldn't find her cat. At last she cried so much on the bed that the bed was all wet. After a day she came to know that the cat was near friends home, she quickly grabbed her umbrella and left for her friends home when she saw her cat she quickly grabbed her and went home. After a lot of disscussion with her parents she was finally allowed to keep it at home. She was very happy with this. She fed the hungry cat with her hands and showed her friends too. And now like her friends she had a cat too.
author: Ronit Khuntia
illustrator: Alison Byrnes; Canato Jimo; Debbie  Faber-Human; Karmacharya K.K; Sheena Deviah; Yuvaka  Srestha

title: The fear of SST
text: SST, a subject that one has the most fear of. I am one of them. This subject how matter hard we study the question still comes out of the world. This is a story about Ravi who studies in grade in grade 9 and his unlikingness of sst. Ravi, a hardworking boy. LIked to study all subjects but after he completed his 5th class and entered in 6th. He saw a monster whose names was sst. Earlier Rohan thought that this was a normal subject. But when he tried to study he was shocked no matter how hard he studied but she couldn't understand a single topic. This was first time in his life that he was not able to understand a subject. He studied day and night and while sleeping too. But still nothing. He went various libraries, studied various book but from one topic another enermous topic would emerge. He was very scared and day by day his grades started falling. Due to sst he couldn't focus on one subject. He would ask his ffriend how they studied but for nothing. He got very sad. His parents very also shocked from his grades. He would study day and night he built his library with 100s of book but still no improvement. This gave a burden on his head. At last he thought that he should other subject importance rather than only on sst. But sst had covered his eyes and couldn't control himself. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ Till now he is still struggling with his subjects. BASED ON TRUE INCIDENTS Disclamer:This is just a thought of one's mind and preferences may vary from one person to another. (i.e. you like sst or not this is your own choice.)
author: Ronit Khuntia
illustrator: Aindri C; Hari Kumar Nair; Joe Werna; Maithili  Joshi; Manisha Naskar; Nidhin Shobhana; Saanvi; Santosh Pujari; Wiehan de Jager; Yusuf Ali Noton

title: I can read My book anywhere
text: Bunny really love to read a book anywhere, even on the floor!! And, Dada just back home!! Dada was shocked!!, "What are you doing on the floor?". Bunny said,"Reading my favorite book, Dada". Dada," Oh my dear!!, the floor might be dirty. Could you, please sit on that chair!." "Yes, Dada." Bunny answered. Now, Bunny is already sitting properly on the chair. Meanwhile, Mama is preparing some cookies to bring to the picnic with Bunny and Daddy. Bunny, Daddy, and Mama are enjoying their picnic. But look! Bunny and Daddy are reading a book while Mama is serving the cookies. They are really enjoying it!!.
author: Diana Devianti

title: The Pink Sheep Mystery
text: Farmer Ted and his wife Matilda live on a farm in Buckleberry. It is quite a large farm, it has a cosy house, a number of barns and plenty of fields. There is a river that flows through the back paddock, and it is home to salmon. Water from the river is used for the orchard, vegetable fields, and animals. The farm has mostly sheep, a few cows, a pig, chickens, and a dog. Farmer Ted loves his farm, and the farm has been in his family for generations. When he is not working, he loves to read, bird watch and do carpentry. His secret skill is singing, but he usually only sings to his animals and plants. He thinks that if he sings to his animals and plants that they will be happy and grow healthy. Farmer Ted is well known in the community, and he is an active member of the Buckleberry Community Club. Farmer Ted is married to Matilda. Matilda was born in a city far from Buckleberry, but she loves famer Ted and the farm too. She is passionate about nature and the environment. When it is winter she sometimes lets certain farm animals come into the house. Farmer Ted loves how kind she is, especially to his favourite, the sheep. Matilda works on the farm but enjoys cooking and making jam. Everyone knows she is great at knitting and people often ask her to knit them a sweater. Farm life starts early each morning. Farmer Ted and Matilda are awake at 5.00am. The cows need to be milked; chickens and pig need to be fed. Hay is given to the sheep. Then comes breakfast. Matilda usually makes scrambled eggs and cooked tomatoes, and this is taken with hot milky tea. The rest of the day is taken up with watering the plants, vegetables, and maintenance. During planting and harvest time the days are longer. Farmer Ted and Matilda make the most of the fresh air and being with nature. Farmer Ted and Matilda have “pumpkin harvest” clearly marked on their calendar. They usually invite the whole village to come along to help collect the pumpkins. Matilda and some of the other farmer’s wives cook for most of the morning so they can give a feast for all the workers. Pumpkin soup and pumpkin scones are always on the menu. Pasta, pizza, and cheese fill the tables. The community love spending a day at the farm. Each year the farmers try to compete with one another to see who can grown the largest pumpkin. Farmer Ted prides himself on growing large pumpkins. He says that pumpkins need watering every day. He places used teabags at the base of the plant and of course he sings to them. Farmer Ted keeps seeds from large pumpkins from the previous year and uses them again the following year. He believes this is what helps make the pumpkins grow bigger. This year, farmer Ted came second. Mr Mosby won first place. Mr Mosby used seeds he got from his travels to Italy. Farmer Ted said he could not compete with such a different breed of seed and that next year he will try something new. He wondered if he could get seeds from Italy too. Farmer Ted also thought he needed to sing different songs and then the pumpkins would grow bigger. Matilda prides herself on her jams. She came first this year in the Buckleberry Jam Competition with her strawberry jam. Second winner made lemon curd and third was an orange marmalade. The jam competition is exciting for the whole village as after the judging, people can eat scones, cream, and jam. Everyone sits in the village square at long tables. People sing and dance after they have eaten. People come from neighbouring villages as they refer to the competition as the “Jam Festival.” After the competition season is over, the farm returns to the seasonal cycle of work. Farmer Ted enjoys moving around the farm on his blue tractor. He often takes some of his favourite sheep with him. The sheep like to cuddle up and go for a ride around the farm. When the tractor goes over bumps the sheep let out a loud “Baaaaaaaaaaaaaa!” Farmer Ted sings to the sheep to calm them down. They usually say, “Baaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!” back. The sheep like to travel together as they feel safe. If one sheep moves to a different part of the field, they all usually move in the same direction. They spend most of their day eating grass. They have great eyesight as their eyes allow them to see behind them without turning their head. They can also detect if Matilda and farmer Ted are happy or sad. They will brush up against Matilda and farmer Ted to make them feel good. The sheep have lots of personality. They love to run, roll, and jump. Matilda will often stand at the kitchen window and see them playing. It is funny to see the sheep jump over objects in the garden. One sheep will say to another, “I bet I can jump higher than you!” Another sheep will reply, “I will jump higher!” And so, it goes on and they compete against each other. When one falls over, the rest of the sheep just laugh. They usually say, “That was a silly jump!” Sheep are very curious animals and will get into mischief. It is difficult to grow flowers on the farm as the sheep eat them. They will poke their nose into the petals and give a sneeze. “Achooo!” They then eat the flower head and then sneeze again. “Achoo!” It even makes Matilda sneeze when she watches them. Naughty sheep will pull the clothes off the line. Not only that, but they eat the clothes as well. Sometimes Matilda and Farmer Ted put clothes on in the morning and find big holes. Matilda then patches the clothes to hide the holes. Their clothing then becomes like a patchwork quilt, so many different coloured patches of material to cover all the holes. Sheep poke their heads in all sorts of places. Their favourite thing is to put their head in the farm buckets. They think the buckets always have food in them. They always seem hungry! The only problem is that they then cannot get their head out of the bucket. They shake and shake until the bucket comes off. It is like they do a dance. Matilda looks and says, “Silly sheep!” It is even funnier to see them trapped in the washing basket. Sometimes they will sit for hours in the washing basket and then when they want to get out, they are unable to. Matilda is the one to pull the basket off their bottom. Matilda usually falls backwards on to the ground. The sheep just say, “Baaaaaaaaaaa!” Matilda shakes her head. They all then laugh. The sheep do not have good memories so when they do it again the next time they go through the same routine. Some of the sheep like to look what is happening in the next field. They poke their heads through the fence and then are unable to get their head out. Other sheep gather around to look at the trapped sheep. They all join in a chorus of “Baaaaaaaaaaaaa!” Farmer Ted comes running to see what the matter is and then releases the trapped sheep. In spring, the sheep are shorn of their fleece. Framer Ted brings in shearers to help gather all the fleece. The fleece is turned into wool and then knitters make clothes from the wool. Special scissors and shears are used to make the sheep feel comfortable. The scissors and shears make a terrible buzzing sound and some sheep do not like the noise. When a sheep has had its fleece removed, it looks like a different animal. The sheep can cope with the hot weather in summer. Their coat grows back and becomes longer in autumn and by winter it is thick again to keep them warm. After they have been shorn, some sheep parade around like they are in a fashion parade and showing off their new spring look. Older sheep just shake their head but then they do the same once their fleece has been taken off. This year sheep ran away from the shearing shed. Farmer Ted thought he had all the sheep in pens and continued to shear. The missing sheep went unnoticed. The naughty sheep heard the noise of the shears and did not want their fleece removed. Matt said, “I am keeping my coat on this year!” Softly said, “If you are going to do it, I am too.” Silky said, “We will need to run away then, let us go to the very back paddock!” The sheep ran away. The missing sheep ran and ran and ran and had found their way through the orchard and into the grape vines. Because they were not at the shearing shed, they did not have any food. One of the sheep suggested that they eat the red grapes. They all thought it was a clever idea and stood and ate the grapes for many hours. Matt said, “I am feeling so much better now.” Silky and Softly agreed. The grapes were easy for the sheep to eat as they hung low on the vines. The red grapes were juicy, sweet, and overall delicious. The sheep devoured bunches of grapes at a time. After they had eaten, they wandered through more fields and went to the furthest boundary of the farm. They had never been this far before. They walked up a hill to see of they could see the farmhouse as they were so far away. Little did they know that farmer Ted had counted sheep and noted that some were missing. Farmer Ted took his tractor and travelled the length of the farm and found the missing sheep. He placed them in the back of the tractor and drove them home. The sheep were relieved as they did not have to walk the long way home. It was late in the evening so, farmer Ted just placed them in a pen and gave them something to eat and drink. The sheep were still full of the grapes, so they had no room for food and drink. When farmer Ted went to see the sheep in the morning, he let out a loud cry. Matilda came running. They both wiped their eyes as they could not believe what they were looking at. It was a pink sheep. “Pink!” shouted farmer Ted. “Pink!” replied Matilda. “What has happened?” they both said at the same time. They then looked at one another and laughed. They had no idea of how the sheep had become pink. “You had better get shearing!” said Matilda. “I guess so!” said farmer Ted. The shearing shears came out of the cupboard and buzzed busily to remove the pink fleece. Matilda quickly turned the fleece into wool. She had so many balls of wool that she thought she had better make something. Farmer Ted and Matilda talked about how the sheep became pink but could not work it out. Matilda spent the next few days knitting and knitting. She made a number of jumpers using the pink wool. The wool was so soft and nothing like she had felt before. She decided to enter one of her creations in the local farmer’s wives knitting competition. Matilda knew that no one else would have pink wool and that it would even surprise the judges. Matilda was shocked when she received a phone call to say that her jumper had won the knitting competition. The judges commented on how soft and silky the wool was and wanted to know her secret of creating such wool. Everyone admired her jumper. The villagers all wanted Matilda to make them a sweater too. Farmer Ted and Matilda only had a few fleeces of pink. They still could not work out how the sheep became pink. Matilda used up the pink wool she had and knitted as many jumpers as possible. She gave them out to people who lived in the village. Everyone in the village all looked the same as the same pink jumper was worn by them all. Farmer Ted and Matilda wear their pink jumpers with pride. They still do not know how the sheep became pink.
author: Lynne H.

title: The Kitchen of Learning
text: Two siblings — a big sister and a little brother. They loved each other very much… but also fought, just like all siblings do! The little brother went to school later because he was younger. The sister also wanted to go with him every day… but their school timings were different. She felt a little sad sometimes. But slowly, she learned something important: Everyone has their own timing in life. Everyone grows at their own speed. After school, they came home and shared everything! What they learned What they played Even their small mischiefs They laughed… argued… and played again! But the moment they heard the sound of Dad’s vehicle… “Vroom vroom!” They instantly became silent and acted like perfect angels. One day, Mom said: “Please bring me a kadai!” The sister tried to help… but brought a plate. Then she brought a bowl. She kept bringing the wrong one. The sister asked: “Mommy, why do vessels have much confusing names?” Mom smiled and said: “They have names so we know exactly what we need for cooking. You just need to learn them slowly.” From that day, Mom started teaching her properly… and the kitchen became a small classroom! Kadai – for frying vegetables and making curries. Tawa – for chapati, dosa, and roti. Pressure cooker – for rice, dal, and quick cooking. Bowl (Katori) – for curry, dal, and snacks. Pan – for shallow frying or making snacks. Step by step, she learned everything. Slowly, she stopped getting confused… and started identifying everything correctly! She realized: “Even kitchen things have names… and learning them makes me more confident!” She realized something powerful: “I may not know now… but I can always learn.” "Say it aloud!" -Don’t compare your timing with others -Mistakes are part of learning -Be patient while learning new things. -Small efforts create big confidence. {Now think of a mistake you made recently. What did that mistake teach you?}
author: Sowjanya Sundar

title: My super bandage !
text: I want to be like my favorite superheroes. I run very fast! I jump… I lose my balance… Ouch! My hand hits the ground. In the distance, I hear laughter. Me, I’m hurting… I stay off to the side. The teacher comes quickly. She sits down next to me. She opens her box. Gently, she takes care of my hand. It stings a little… but it feels better. Then she puts on a bandage. ﻿ She smiles at me. H ere’s a super bandage for a superhero. In class, I show it. The other children come closer. They look at it. They don’t feel like laughing anymore. I want one too. I smile. My heart feels all warm. At the end of the day, Mom comes to pick me up. I tell her everything: my adventure, my fall… and most of all… my super bandage. In the evening, I wash my hands. It foams, it slips… it’s funny. Then I dry them. And then… Poof! The bandage has disappeared. I look at my hand. The boo-boo is gone. In its place, there’s a tiny mark left. Almost invisible. It looks like a sign… My heart skips a beat. What if it was his sign… Wow… my super bandage. I smile. I look at my hand one last time… Then I close my eyes. I whisper: Goodbye, my super friend… I will never forget you
author: Joh Azura
