title: The Humpback Highway is Open.
text: Hello! My name is Sashi and I am a humpback whale. I am one of about 30,000 whales that live in the Southern Hemisphere. I have a remarkably interesting life. I would like to tell you about myself as this time of the year you will see me and hear about me on the television, radio, newspapers, and internet. I am told that I am incredibly special. My giant flippers make me unique. They are only small now, but I am still growing. I believe that they will grow exceptionally long and will be at least five metres in length. The fins help me swim, allow me to feed more easily and give me balance. I can slap my fins on the water to talk to other animals. It is fun to communicate this way. My fins are black, but some whales have white fins. I also have a small fin on my back; this dorsal fin also helps me balance in the water. I have a wonderful tail called flukes. Every whale has their own tail. People who whale watch can tell who we are by our tail. It is a little bit like a human having blue, green or brown eyes. When I swim around and show my tail, people can identify me by the shape of my tail and my markings. I have some scratches and barnacles on mine. My flukes can grow up to five metres wide, and I move it up and down, not side to side like a fish. I slap my tail o the water to make a sound that travels for long distances under the water. I am still learning how to do this. Unlike other animals, my nose is on top of my head. I have a special hole. In fact, I have two holes. My relatives, the dolphins and toothed whales only have one hole. People like to see me when I breathe out. I take in a large amount of air, but then I blow it all out. When I breathe out, I not only blow out air but water and bacteria as well. My spray goes high into the sky. People like to take photos of me when I do this. I need to breathe all the time and therefore it is difficult to sleep. I have ears that are inside my body, and these are especially important to me. When I hear, I hear sounds below the water as well as above. Below the water, I can hear the movement of sea life like fish and krill. When I am with other humpback whales, we make sounds to help us work together to catch krill. This makes feeding time fun. Sounds under the ocean tell me if I am in danger or if I need to swim in a different direction to avoid bumping into a reef. Females can hear the songs males sing and calves can hear the noises their mothers make. Human made noises can often cause confusion. My eyes are quite large and are placed on either side of my head. When I dive out of the water, I use my eyes to look for land and to see if there are any ships and boats nearby. I don not have any eyelashes, but I do have eyelids. My eyes have a greasy film that go over the eyes to help protect them from the salty water and then the air when I am out of the water. I use my eyes when I sleep. I close my right eye and rest my right side of my brain. I then switch to closing my left eye and rest the left side of my brain. My eyes help keep me safe. I have no teeth. I have something else instead. When I open my mouth, you will see something that looks like a fringe. When I eat my food, I use my tongue to push the water out of my mouth, but my fringe traps krill and fish and fish. I then swallow the fish and krill. I eat mostly when I am living in Antarctica but eat extraordinarily little when I travel to the warmer waters off the northeastern coast of Australia. Food helps build up a special layer of tissue around my body called blubber. The blubber keeps me warm in the freezing waters of Antarctica and helps keep me cool in the warm waters off Queensland. The blubber also acts as an energy tank and provides fuel for my body when I go through times of not eating. The blubber helps protect the shape and form of my body. It gives my body a structure so that I can swim easily through water and dive in and out of the water without causing damage to myself. The most impressive thing about me and my kind is that we migrate. We do this each year. Normally around April and May each year, we see changes in the ice in Antarctica. This is a signal for us to move from freezing water to warm water. We travel north and follow the coastline of Australia and travel as far as Hervey Bay. It is an exceedingly long journey, and we travel day and night. We do not all leave Antarctica at once. We take it in turns. Because I am still young, I will leave in the first group. Next comes the males and then the last group to leave are usually females. It would all be difficult to move together as there are tens of thousands of us that migrate. It would be very crowded if we did. They call the route we take from Antarctica to Queensland, the “Humpback Highway!” We use landmarks and sound and follow those who have been before us to take the blue corridor highway from south to north and return from north to south. Some whales head left to go to Western Australia. Some whales head north to swim off Victoria and Tasmania. Many swim north and follow the eastern coastline of Australia to travel to Hervey Bay off Queensland. It is one of the longest migrations by animals. It is impossible to swim non-stop to our destination. We take time to take rest stops along the way. People will come out to see us and stand on headlands, cliffs, and beaches. They use their eyes and binoculars to spot us using our blow hole and the flapping of our tail. We get very playful and dive in and out of the water. Sometimes we like to show off and show how high we can jump out of the water. Sometimes humpback whales are still travelling north in August. Climate and environmental changes have both had an impact on our timing of our migration. Rising sea levels and temperatures have meant that the krill we eat also move. We need to move where the food is. Ocean currents have become stronger, and this means we need more energy to swim to our destination. It is very tiring swimming a long way. Human activity has also impacted on us. Pollution in the ocean means we need to look for safer and cleaner areas to rest and stay. Nets can block our pathway. The light and noise from cargo ships can impact on what we see and hear. This can make us travel in the wrong direction and then we need to travel further to get back on the right route. We love it when we arrive in Hervey Bay as this becomes our playground. We get to do many unusual types of tricks. We like to jump as high as we can and see if we can reach the moon and the stars. We then make a big splash when we land on the water. We like to slap our fins and fluke in the water; it is a way that we talk to one another. We like to sing. Sometimes we swim in circles and blow bubbles, but this is usually done in Antarctica when chasing krill and fish. When we are travelling sometimes people take boats and come out to see us. There are rules in place to keep us all safe. We like to be friendly and say hello. We know that you like to take photographs of us and we love that. Sometimes we will put on a show and demonstrate how we move in the water. Sometimes however, we are not in the mood as we have had a busy day. It takes patience and understanding for us to both live in harmony. In the mornings we usually like to rest, afternoons we play and then we swim in the evening. When September comes, we know it is time to return to Antarctica. We have not eaten very much so we are lighter and can travel faster. Mothers are usually terribly busy as they bring their young babies with them. Babies are called calves. By November we are all back in Antarctica and ready to start the cycle again. When we reach Antarctica, we are ready to eat. We need to build up our blubber so we can stay warm. As the ice melts the krill move. We need to move with the krill so we can feast. Once we have found food, we stay and build up our energy, allow our skin to rest and restore, and enjoy our time before we need to move again. I hope that you now know more about me. If you have an opportunity, come and see me or check me out on the internet. You can use maps on the internet to follow my migration from Antarctica to Hervey Bay. You can listen to me sing and see me do tricks. I think you will be amazed at what I can do. Please take time to protect our planet as it is a wonderful place where we all live.
author: Lynne H.

title: Peachy
text: Winters are cold in Buckleberry. The sun rises later and sets earlier. There does not seem very much sunlight each day. People wear hats, gloves, coats, and boots when they go outside. Everyone wants to stay warm. The chilly wind blows so hard that all the leaves fall off the trees leaving them bare. People shiver and shake and want to be home sitting by the fireside and drinking hot chocolate. Then spring arrives. Everything changes. It is like someone has turned the light on. It is bright, warm and the sun shines. Leaves sprout on trees and gardens come alive. Everyone feels in a happier mood. People spring clean their homes and start the season with hope. The animals are busy too. Butterflies are busy laying eggs, blossoms are starting to bloom, hedgehogs and badgers are coming out of hibernation. In one garden it is a hive of activity. Eggs laid by insects are starting to come alive. Small caterpillars have broken out of their shells and start to explore the leaf that they live on. They start to take their first bite of the leaf that will fill their tummies and help them grow. The caterpillars were too busy going about their business and did not notice that one egg had not hatched. They just kept on eating and eating and growing bigger and bigger. The lonely egg just rested on the leaf and there was no movement whatsoever. As the caterpillars grew, they became more observant. They started to notice that there was a lonely egg. They would go up to the egg and say “hello.” They would go up to the egg and then shout “hello.” They would go up to the egg and scream “hello.” The egg stayed still. The caterpillars could not work out what was going on. It became the chatter amongst everyone. Then one day, a large cracking sound could be heard. The lonely egg broke and out popped a caterpillar. But this caterpillar was different. Everyone came running to see what came out of the lonely egg. They all stared in disbelief as they saw a peach-coloured caterpillar. ‘Oh my gosh!” said one. “Wow!” said another. Someone even said, “She is not like us!” The caterpillars thought that “Peachy” as she became known was a different animal to them. They went about their business and just kept on eating. They always seemed hungry and just wanted more and more food. The caterpillars became so full that they then became tired. They all felt that they needed to rest and sleep and then they would feel better. It was difficult to sleep on the leaf. One of them came up with the idea to hang upside down. They thought that the food in their tummies would go to their tail. “Clever idea!” one said. So, they all decided to hang upside down and tried to rest. As they rested a chrysalis formed around their bodies. It made a cocoon and kept them warm and snug. The chrysalis completely covered their body. When you looked at the leaf there was only one caterpillar that could be seen and that was Peachy. Peachy was shocked to see what happened to the caterpillars. She wondered if the same thing would happen to her. Peachy went on with her life and enjoyed feasting on the leaf. There was no movement from the new caterpillar homes. Peachy did not know what to make of it all. The weather became warmer and the garden was full of noise. Birds were chirping. Bees were buzzing. Daddy was mowing the lawn and Mummy was planting flowers. The chrysalis was cracking. But with all the noise you could not hear what was going on below the leaves. Out popped butterflies. They were so happy and flew around the garden. They could see parts of the garden that they had never seen before. They went back to their original home of the leaf and spotted Peachy. Peachy was still an animal. They did not think that Peachy would become a butterfly and thought she would remain living on the leaf. Peachy became so tired as she walked from one end of the leaf to another. She lay down on the leaf and went to sleep. Magically a pink blanket started to cover her body. She could feel the warmth of the blanket, and it made her dream. She started to dream of becoming another animal. She thought if the caterpillars could turn into butterflies, what could she turn in to? Peachy became covered in the pink blanket. All the animals came to look as the pink blanket was something they had never seen before. The butterflies, the rabbits, the hedgehogs all came and did not know what was going on. The spring rains came. The clouds turned grey and then they turned black. It rained and rained and rained. Then it rained some more. Everything was wet. People looked out of windows and saw rain. They used an umbrella and raincoat and rainboots to protect them from the rain. It just never stopped raining. Then, the sun came out. Everything looked brighter once again. The sun sparkled and made people feel warm. People smiled from ear to ear and were so glad that the sun was in the blue sky. The sun looked down and saw Peachy. The rain had nearly washed away the pink blanket. Peachy was no longer the Peachy that was under the blanket. Something had changed. The sun called the animals to come and take a look. They were all surprised to see a different Peachy sleeping on the leaf. They said, “Hello!” Peachy did not move. They then shouted, “Hello!” Peachy still did not move. Then they all screamed, “Hello!” There was still no movement from Peachy. “We had better get Mrs Ladybird!” one said. They all travelled to see Mrs Ladybird. Mrs Ladybird was wise and knew lots of things. They thought if anyone could help Peachy, it would be Mrs Ladybird. All the animals explained carefully what had go on. Mrs Ladybird nodded her head and moved her hands up and down. She said, “I will need to take a look!” All the animals travelled to see Peachy. Mrs Ladybird moved around the leaf and around Peachy. She inspected every part of Peachy’s body. She said, “I will need to go to speak with Mr Sun. He will know what to do!” Mrs Ladybird flew to see Mr Sun. She tried to get as close as possible without getting burnt. Mrs Ladybird explained everything about Peachy to Mr Sun. He blinked his eyes and said, “I will look after her and keep her warm.” Mrs Ladybird thought this was a clever idea. Mr Sun moved to shine his light on Peachy and watched over her all day. When Mr Sun could no longer look after Peachy, he handed it over to Mr Moon. Mr Moon and stars stayed close to Peachy. Some of the stars sang to her a lullaby and hoped it would make Peachy better. The next day, the sun was shining, the garden was buzzing and all the animals came to see Peachy. To their surprise, Peachy was awake and smiling. She fluttered her wings and showed everyone that she had become the most beautiful butterfly anyone had ever seen. All the animals said, "You are so beautiful. We are so happy you are well. We want you to know we love you and will always take care of you!” Peachy smiled and thanked them by showing off her beautiful wings.
author: Lynne H.

title: The Lost Cute Puppy
text: One day, a small puppy wandered into the forest. He was chasing a butterfly. But soon, he stopped. He didn’t know the way home. The trees looked tall and scary. The puppy felt afraid. Just then, a monkey jumped down from a tree. “Why are you here?” asked the monkey. “I’m lost,” said the puppy. “I will help you,” said the monkey. They walked together. Soon, they met a deer near a river. Follow the river,” said the deer. “It leads to the village.” The puppy thanked them and ran along the river. After some time, he saw his house. “Woof!” he barked happily. His family ran to him. The puppy was safe. And he never went into the forest alone again.
author: Rudra Cheeti

title: Elly and Her Loving Grandparents
text: Elly was a sweet little girl. She loved spending time with her grandparents. Her grandparents loved Elly very much. She was their first granddaughter. Whenever Elly visited them, the house felt bright and happy. Her laughter filled every room. Elly liked helping Grandma in the kitchen. She also helped Grandpa in the garden. She watered the flowers carefully. Grandpa smiled and praised her. Sometimes Elly brought Grandma’s glasses. Sometimes she folded small towels neatly. Her grandparents were proud of her kind heart. They loved having her near them. When Elly fell sick, Grandpa and Grandma felt worried. They stayed beside her all day. Grandma gave her warm soup. Grandpa told funny stories to make her smile. Soon Elly felt better again. Her grandparents thanked God happily. Elly loved asking for her favorite food. She always asked Grandpa to cook it. Grandpa was a chef. He cooked every dish with love. The food was always tasty and yummy. Elly ate with joy. Grandpa was also very disciplined. He woke up early every morning. He ate on time every day. He worked on time too. At night, he slept on time. He believed good habits make life better. Grandpa taught Elly to respect time. He said, “Time is precious.” Elly listened carefully to his words. She wanted to be like Grandpa. She learned to wake up early. She learned to finish things on time. Elly loved her grandparents deeply. Their love and lessons stayed in her heart forever. Grandparents give us love, care, and wisdom. When we spend time with them, we learn kindness, discipline, and gratitude. We should treasure every moment with them.
author: Sowjanya Sundar

title: The haunted library
text: One night Riya went for a walk at 7;00 PM. suddenly she saw a library which is creepy and she wanted to explore the library. Then she went inside the library. after she went inside the library, the door was closed harshly. after a while she got a book called 'The diary of my life'. Then she started to read that book. While she was reading,a skeleton scared her and she ran to her house. The next morning she shared about the incident which was happened in last night with her friend vidya. vidya told ' let us go to the library at 7;00 PM today'. Riya said 'ok let us meet there'. At sharp at 7;00 PM they both met in the library, then they entered a library the door slammed once again. Vidya and Riya heard the sound of someone who is shouting creepily outside they went out to check who is there, but no one is there. but a strange thing happened it was not the entrance of the library instead it was a grave yard. then the went inside library the library. Vidya noticed that 4 members were running inside the library. Vidya and Riya are running fastly to catch them. finally Riya, Vidya caught them they are thiefs and sent them to jail.
author: sai viveha

title: The Underwater Olympics
text: Everyone has been notified in the ocean that the “Underwater Olympics” will take place in a month. The games will begin early morning on the 5 th of May and go all day. A banquet will follow so that presentations can be made. All participants are asked to train so they can be fit and strong to compete. A reminder was sent to eat healthy, exercise and make sure to sleep. In the northeastern part of the ocean the crab community decide to send a participant. But who will they send is an issue. “We need to send our strongest,” said one. “I think the tallest,” said another. “Let’s have try-outs!” said the chief. The next day, the Chief organized for crabs who wanted to compete to attend the try-outs. The chief had organized for large pebbles be placed in a row. The challenge for the crabs was to lift the pebbles high and hold them in the air. This would assess their strength. Each crab took a turn and held the pebble high above their head. It was impressive to see how strong their arms are. The Chief then placed a piece of seaweed across the sand. He then walked and placed another piece of seaweed across the sand. All crabs lined up and were told to run as fast as they could between the seaweed lines. It was exceedingly difficult to see a clear winner as all the crabs ran fast. The final test was to roll a shell. The crabs lined up and took turns in rolling a shell from one place to another. This looked easy to start with but some of the carbs struggled. Eventually one crab rolled the shell from start to finish. The Chief decided that this would be the crab that would represent them. “Hurray for Hermit!” everyone cheered. In the southeastern part of the ocean a different challenge was taking place. The rocky platform community was trying to decide who they would send to the games. Many of the octopuses decided not to try out. They said they did not have the energy. The Octopus King was sad, he said, “If we are not represented, it does not look good for us!” Long Legs and Many Legs volunteered to compete. The Octopus King was incredibly happy. He told everyone else that even though they were not competing, they would need to train with Long Legs and Many Legs. They all agreed. One octopus said he would become their coach. He set up an exercise timetable to make sure that they could build up muscles and increase speed in each octopus. In the western part of the ocean, things were a different matter. All the clownfish wanted to participate. The Clownfish Queen had difficulty in selecting who would participate and who would not. The Clownfish Queen held trials, but all the clownfish could compete with strength and speed. She could not select one clownfish over another. The Clownfish Queen went to the games committee and asked if she could have more participants in the games. She was told she could have five. All the clownfish waited for the Clownfish Queen to announce who would compete. She had no idea of who she would select. As she stood before all the clownfish, she smiled but had to be truthful. She explained about how five clownfish could compete and she wished everyone could, but she found it hard to decide. One of the clownfish suggested that they play “Rock, Paper, Scissors” and this would be a fair way of picking the competitors. They all agreed. It took a long time to play “Rock, Paper, Scissors” as there were so many clownfish. In fact, it took all day. Just before dinner, the last clownfish played the game. Stripey, Little One, Smokey, Polly and Tally were the last clownfish. Everyone was happy with the selection and gave them a cheer. In the northern part of the ocean, the jellyfish had also received the news about the games. They thought that they could not compete as it was time for them to move homes. They would be busy and not have time to train. A dolphin passed through their community and informed them about the clownfish, octopus, and crabs. When the jellyfish heard about the trials and selection processes, they became interested and decided to compete. The jellyfish decided that they would select their competitors by trying to stretch coral. They thought this would be fair as it would assess the strength and speed of each jellyfish. The first jellyfish tried and could not move the coral at all. The second, third, fourth and fifth jellyfish could stretch the coral a little bit. This then went on and on. There was one jellyfish who was very shy and stood back. They looked at the shy jellyfish and said, “You are our last chance, can you stretch the coral?” The shy jellyfish was nervous about trying to stretch the coral. He moved slowly towards the coral and checked the way the current was going. He positioned himself near a rock and then used his tentacles to balance and pull on the coral. To everyone’s amazement, he stretched the coral further than anyone else. Everyone was surprised and a large, “Wow!” came from the crowd. It was settled, that the shy jellyfish would compete for the north. All the animals trained hard. They lifted heavy and heavier things to build up their muscles. They carried smaller sea life on their backs and ran to build up speed. They slept, they ate, they had other animals giving them encouragement and tips of what to do and what not to do. The whole ocean was buzzing with things to do about the games. Finally, the day had arrived. Animals had travelled from the north, south, east, and west to attend the “Underwater Olympics.” Animals gathered to hear the opening speech. Neptune King of the Sea, encouraged participants to try their best, play fair and to enjoy. He also told the crowds to cheer, clap and admire the talents of each animal. Everyone put their hands above their heads and waved from left to right The first game was to roll a shell across the sand. It was an intense race as many of the animals had practiced this. The crab started well but then became tired. The clownfish found it exceedingly difficult to do. The octopus with some many legs found it easy and moved quite quickly. The tentacles of the jellyfish were no match with the other animals, and the jellyfish won the race. The crowd jumped up and down. The second game was digging a tunnel under the sand. The octopus, jellyfish and clownfish could not do this. The crab had instant success and won. Hermit stood proud at the end and pleased he had managed to win something. The third game was moving in and out of obstacles. The shy jellyfish became stuck behind a rock. Long Legs and Many Legs had too many legs and fell behind. The clownfish could dart in and out of objects and could swim under and over things. The clownfish were declared a winner. The final game was a scavenger hunt. The animals were given a list of things to find and collect. The crowd looked on and “ooooooooooo, arrrrrrrrrrr,hmmmmmmmmmm!” could be heard. They were amazed at how many things the animals could find, but it was the octopus that won the game. With so many legs, they could collect many items all at once. It was their time to shine. Everyone was exhausted after the busy day. It had been terribly exciting, and the animals loved being able to meet friends and make new friends. The competitors of course had an amazing day. King Neptune called for people to ready themselves for the banquet. He had prepared a feast. All the animals gathered and sat at a long table. Coral entertained everyone by performing a dance. Sea horses provided music. Turtles helped serve the food and drink. The banquet was enjoyable. Just before dessert, King Neptune gave out awards. He handed out medals for first, second and third. All the competitors smiled and thanked King Neptune for organizing such a wonderful event. They all thought it was a success and something they should do again. The animals travelled back to the north, south, east, and west. Animals that stayed home wanted to hear all the stories and news about friends. Conversations went on for months. Those who did not attend or compete decided that the next time they would become involved. The event was too good to miss. It brought the ocean community together and helped create friendships and harmony. Being able to meet and greet King Neptune was something that everyone said was fabulous. The “Underwater Olympics” is already marked on the calendar for next year.
author: Lynne H.

title: THE GIRL WITH THE UNUSUAL NAME
text: T he dinner table at the Chowdhurys’ buzzed with excitement as everyone spoke over each other, sharing the news of the day. This was a daily routine — family time and food. But that day, Anu sat with her head bowed, two roly-poly tears in her eyes, waiting to roll down her cheeks. Her grandfather noticed her silence and asked softly, “Anu, what’s wrong?” The kindness in his voice broke Anu, and she burst into tears. “Why couldn’t you name me something normal?” “All my friends have lovely names — Ahana, Ipshita, Ruhi! I wish I had a simple name. Why did you name me Anandibai? Such an old-fashioned name!” “They call me ‘Bai, the maid!’ or they yell ‘Baa Baa Black Sheep!’ when I’m close by.” Her mother smiled. “One day, you’ll love your name.” But Anu didn’t believe her. One rainy afternoon, she came home from school with tears in her eyes. “Everyone laughed again,” she muttered. Her grandfather, who was reading near the window, looked up thoughtfully. “Do you know who you’re named after?” Anu shook her head. Grandfather patted the seat beside him. “Come here. Let me tell you a story.” He opened an old book and showed her a photograph of a woman in a saree, wearing striking traditional jewellery, with a large nose ring that immediately caught Anu's attention. “This,” he said, “is Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi. she was one of the first women doctors from India. Long ago, many people did not think girls needed to study. But Anandibai worked very hard and never gave up on becoming a doctor. She inspired many girls in India to study and believe in themselves.” Anu stared at the picture. The woman looked confident and brave. Grandfather continued. “And do you know what people noticed about her when she was young?” “What?” whispered Anu. “They knew she was special.” For the first time, Anandibai smiled a little. That night, she searched online with her mother and read more about Dr. Anandibai. The next morning, when attendance began, Anandibai Chowdhury sat up straight. “Anandibai?” called the teacher. Before anyone could snicker, Anandibai stood tall, proudly. “My name is Anandibai,” she announced, “and I’m named after a famous doctor.” The class fell silent. “She opened doors for women who wanted to become doctors,” Anandi continued confidently. “And my grandfather says people knew she was special too.” Her friends blinked. “Really?” Anandi nodded. “Yes. So, I like my name now.” At recess, Ruhi came up to her shyly. “Your name is actually very cool,” she admitted. “Can you show us her picture?” another child asked. Anandi grinned. “Of course.” That afternoon, she wrote her name carefully at the top of her notebook: ANANDIBAI CHOWDHURY. For the first time ever, she thought it looked beautiful. And from then on, whenever someone asked about her unusual name, Anandibai answered with pride. Because now she knew — Sometimes, unusual names carried extraordinary stories.
author: Vinita Rajeev

title: Harimau yang kekurangan warna
text: seekor harimau yang bulunya kekurangan warna. Bulunya hanya berwarna abu-abu, hitam dan putih. Sampai-sampai harimau itu terlihat seperti sesuatu yang keluar dari film hitam-putih. Harimau itu terkenal karena kekurang warna, hingga para pelukis paling hebat di dunia datang ke kebun binatang untuk mencoba memberikan warna pada bulu-bulunya. Tidak ada satupun yang berhasil, warna yang diberikan ke bulunya selalu luntur. Lalu datanglah Van Cough, si pelukis gila. Dia adalah pria aneh yang berkelana kemana-mana dan senang melukis dengan kuasnya. Ya, lebih tepatnya dia hanya menggerakkan kuasnya kesana-kesini, karena dia tidak pernah menggunakan pewarna di kuasnya dan dia juga tidak pernah menggunakan kanvas maupun kertas untuk melukis. Dia mewarnai angin, itulah kenapa dia dipanggil sebagai Van Cough. Jadi ketika dia bilang ingin mewarnai harimau itu, semua orang menertawakannya Saat masuk ke kandang harimau, dia mulai berbisik ke telinga para binatang, dan menggerakkan kuasnya ke atas dan ke bawah tubuh harimau. Mengejutkannya bulu harimau mulai terlihat berwarna dan itu adalah warna paling jelas yang pernah dimiliki oleh harimau manapun. Van Cough menghabiskan waktu dengan berbisik ke hewan-hewan dan merapihkan lukisannya. Hasilnya sangat indah. Semua orang ingin tahu rahasia pelukis. Pelukis menjelaskan bahwa kuasnya hanya untuk melukis di kehidupan nyata, dan untuk melakukan itu dia tidak membutuhkan warna. Dia melukis warna di tubuh harimau dengan berbisik: "Dalam beberapa hari, kamu akan bebas kembali, kamu akan melihatnya." Melihat betapa sedihnya harimau itu menghadapi keadaannya dan bagaimana harimau itu terlihat bahagia melihat adanya harapan tentang kebebasan, kebun binatang kemudia mengirimnya ke hutan untuk dibebaskan. Sehingga harimau itu tidak akan kehilangan warnanya lagi
author: Andira Revi Astuti
